100110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100110.value: The proposal considers a wide class of error bounds developed in the context of statistical learning theory which are expressed in terms of functionals of the target function, for instance its norm in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space or other functional space. These bounds are unstable in the sense that a small perturbation of the target function can induce an arbitrary large increase of the relevant functional and make the error bound useless. A recent result shows how to recover stability for two important classes of problems using a suitable version of Fano's inequality. The first class includes problems in which the output samples are binary, the second class includes general linear regularization filters. The purpose of the project is to develop mathematical techniques which would allow to recover stability for much more general learning algorithms using information theoretical results, and apply these results to various error bounds available in the literature. On the computational side, the purpose of the project is to develop algorithms which can effectively estimate the "stabilized" complexity functionals from empirical samples, and to implement these algorithms on synthetic and real datasets. 本项目主要考虑统计学习理论中常见的可以表示为目标函数的泛函形式的误差界，例如：再生核Hilbert空间或其它函数空间的范数。这些误差界是不稳定的，也就是说，目标函数的小的扰动可能会导致相关函数任意大的变化。这使得该类误差界变的没有什么价值。最近的研究结果利用Fano不等式的稳定形式，给出了一种重构两类重要问题的稳定性的方法。一类是分类问题，另一类是包含一般的线性正则化滤子的问题。该项目的目的是利用信息学的结果，开发一种对更一般的学习算法的稳定性的重构方法。并把所得到的结果应用到不同的已有误差界中。在计算方面，该项目的目的是从观察样本中建立有效估计这种‘稳定的’复杂性泛函的算法，并把所得的算法应用于人造的或真实的数据。

100110.label: Realisation of objectives
100110.value: The expected wide range generalization of previous results was only partially successful; some results have been published in the journal paper No.1 of Part C; these results are based on a very general information-theoretical technique, Fano's inequality, and can be applied to a large class of error bounds available in the Learning Theory literature. This procedure allows to widely extend the range of application of the corresponding error estimates. Other theoretical extensions, in particular regarding the empirical effective dimension, have not been published yet. In prospective these results would allow to empirically estimate in the semi-supervised setting the empirical effective dimension which in turn would allow to estimate with larger accuracy the error bound. The actual algorithmic computation of the stabilized complexity measures proved to be an over-ambitious challenge. Therefore actual algorithmic application of these techniques has not been proved.

100110.label: Major findings and research outcome
100110.value: The established results, dealing with perturbation of both the marginal distribution and the regression function are summarized in the journal publication No.1 of Part C. These results show that it is possible to obtain stable versions of a wide class of error bounds available in the Learning Theory literature, in the sense that the new bounds are robust under small L2 perturbations of the regression function which would spoil the smoothness conditions assumed in the original bounds. For a suitable class of estimators this procedure has been extended to perturbations of the marginal distribution on the input space. Research regarding the notion of "empirical effective dimension", its computation and role in the stability of error bound has not led to the publication of journal papers.

100210.label: Project Objectives
100210.value: to identify various changes in track and structure (wind and convection distributions) of tropical cyclones before, during and after their landfall to understand the physical mechanisms that cause such changes through diagnostics of observations and numerical simulations

100210.label: Realisation of objectives
100210.value: The project started out with the broad objective to understand the mechanisms responsible for changes in track and structure (wind and convection) as a tropical cyclone is close to landfall. We basically achieved a very good understanding of the track and convection changes, mostly through numerical modeling. However, during these investigations, we found much more that are of significant interest to be studied and hence there was not enough time to (1) perform observational analyses, nor (2) finish the investigation of the changes in the wind distribution although a second PhD student is currently working on it. Nevertheless, our work has resulted in 7 journal articles (one of which is currently under second review), 4 conference papers and a PhD thesis.

100210.label: Major findings and research outcome
100210.value: As a tropical cyclone is close to land, its track is affected by the differences in surface roughness, moisture availability and topography. All these modify the dynamic and thermodynamic characteristics that cause changes in the potential vorticity tendency, and hence changes in the track. The new findings include the development of vertical wind shear that did not exist prior to the approach of the tropical cyclone, the establishment of a pair of counterrotating gyres and/or other circulations in the presence of topography, and the shifting of the convection from offshore to onshore, although such a shift depends on the evolution of the vertical wind shear. These features can be used to explain the changes in the track and convection as a tropical cyclone is close to land.

100210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100210.value: Although our understanding has improved substantially in terms of the track and convection changes, the effect of land on wind changes still needs to be studied, which is the topic of another PhD student. In addition, most of these changes are found based on modeling studies, and more observations are necessary to validate these results. This is the objective of the GRF proposal submitted in Nov 2014.

100210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100210.value: As a tropical cyclone is close to land, its track is affected by the differences in surface roughness, moisture availability and topography. All these modify the atmospheric conditions that cause the movement of the tropical cyclone, and hence changes in the track. The results are useful in actual forecasting of tropical cyclone landfall especially in the representation of the land use in the prediction models, as well as in understanding of the model predictions.

100410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
100410.value: 剛性多金屬框架的拓撲學與協同反應性

100410.label: Project Objectives
100410.value: To design and prepare topologically diverse bimetallic architectures with potential cooperativity. To investigate cooperativity of homo- and heterobimetallic systems with tunable topological properties for binding and activation of small molecules. To develop reactivity and catalytic applications for homo- and heterobimetallic frameworks, and probe the nature of cooperativity in these systems.

100410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100410.value: Inspired by nature, cooperative reactivity between metal centers in close proximity has attracted intense interest. While metalloenzymes have distinct advantages conferred by the surrounding protein envelope, the development of cooperative multimetallic systems displaying desirable reactivity and selectivity remains a challenging yet worthwhile goal. This proposal is dedicated towards the design, preparation, and function of multinuclear assemblies featuring reactive metal-organic subunits in face-to-face geometry that are stacked together by a rigid anchoring group. Such a conformation allows minimal lateral displacement but a degree of rotational flexibility for the subunits. By changing the nature and dimensions of the metal-organic and anchoring components, and thereby varying their relative spatial arrangement (topology) and electronic properties, the capacity of the resultant frameworks for binding and activation of small molecules can be examined and adjusted. It is envisaged that a synergistic and tunable reaction space between the metal centers can be generated. Compared with previous studies in this area, novel approaches are proposed which can modify and enhance the reactivity of bound substrates. The underlying aim is to develop reactivity and catalytic applications for these bimetallic frameworks, for example in the production of biodegradable polymers and chemicals using sustainable resources. 由於大自然的啟發，金屬中心之間在鄰近時的協同反應引起了深度的關注。雖然金屬酶周圍的蛋白包膜賦予其獨特的優點，但開發能展現出理想的反應性和選擇性的協同多金屬系統仍是一個具有挑戰性而值得的目標。這建議書是專注於多核裝配之設計、製備、和功能；裝配的特點為活性金屬有機亞基以面對面的幾何被疊放一起在一個硬性的錨定組。這種結構允許最小的橫向位移，而又給予亞基一定程度的旋轉彈性。通過改變金屬有機物和錨定組件的性質和尺度，從而變更它們相對空間的佈置（拓撲學）和電子屬性，此框架所產生之潛力如小分子的結合和激活便可以被檢驗和調整。據設想，一個於金屬中心之間，有協同作用並可調的反應空間可被生成。與以往在這方面的研究相比，在此提出的新方法能修改和提高結合受質的反應性。其根本目的在於發展這些雙金屬框架的反應性與催化之應用，例如使用可持續資源生產可生物降解的聚合物和化學品。

100410.label: Realisation of objectives
100410.value: The project has been completed and all objectives have been achieved, resulting in several publications. Two research students have been trained under this project. Objective 1: Several families of bimetallic Schiff base complexes have been designed and successfully synthesized. The newly devised bis-(M-salphen) systems, with contrasting rigid linker units (to preclude M–M interactions and conserve coordinative unsaturation) as well as different ‘anchoring’ positions to the salphen moieties, are anticipated to confer varying degrees of rotational flexibility, thus allowing the tuning of (1) relative spatial arrangement and orientation (‘topology’) of the cofacial M-salphen units, and (2) intermetallic distances and geometry, to potentially enhance catalytic reactivity and engender cooperativity. New rigidly-linked dizinc Schiff base and heterobimetallic complexes that can potentially display cooperative reactivity have been prepared, while synthesis of the targeted bis(Co-Schiff base) derivatives proved to be challenging (due in particular to difficulty in purification of reactive products) but was eventually successful. Objective 2: The topology of the cofacial and adjacent bis-(metal-Schiff base) moieties has been modified in order to probe and adjust the capacity of the resultant bimetallic cavity for binding and activation of small molecules, such as carbon dioxide. The mutual positioning of the M-Schiff base units (and the associated intermetallic separation) in the bimetallic complexes are manifestly critical to achieve enhanced catalytic efficiency, and especially synergistic and cooperative reactivity. DFT calculations have been extensively performed to model the molecular structures and possible conformations, and provide insights regarding the said structural parameters. Objective 3: The catalytic reactivity of the binuclear metal-Schiff base complexes towards fixation of small molecules such as carbon dioxide and their transformation into desirable chemicals have been extensively studied. The development of diverse bimetallic frameworks with different topology and rotational freedom has facilitated investigations into the effects of catalyst structure and conformation, as well as the important factor of intermetallic separation and geometry between active sites. In particular, the catalyzed coupling of carbon dioxide and epoxide to give organic (cyclic and/or poly-) carbonates has been examined. Importantly, notable catalytic performance, high efficiencies and exceptional turnover frequencies have been achieved under mild reaction conditions (down to 1 bar of carbon dioxide and 45 deg C). Selected binuclear catalysts are significantly more active than the corresponding mononuclear analogue under identical conditions and concentration of metal sites, thus demonstrating synergistic reactivity between the metal centers and implying bimetallic cooperativity.

100410.label: Major findings and research outcome
100410.value: New bis-(Zn-salphen) assemblies with contrasting rigid linkers have been prepared, which are anticipated to afford different rotational flexibility and orientation of the cofacial Zn-salphen units, thus allowing adjustments in intermetallic separations to potentially engender increased reactivity and synergistic characteristics. The molecular structures of key catalysts have been determined by X-ray crystallography. The binuclear complexes have been investigated as catalysts for coupling of carbon dioxide with epoxides. Saliently, selected dibenzofuran-based derivatives are significantly more active than their mononuclear congeners. Excellent yields of cyclic carbonate under mild conditions (1 bar of carbon dioxide, 45 deg C) and high turnover frequencies (up to 12800/h) are observed. Furthermore, the turnover frequencies observed approach the benchmark literature examples, and compares favorably with previously reported zinc catalysts. These results underscore the importance of tuning the mutual orientation of active sites and intermetallic distances for enhanced efficiency, and imply cooperativity between the Zn centers (Publications 1 and 4). Conformationally rigid binuclear salphen-cobalt(III)-trifluoroacetate catalysts have been synthesized, and the impact of anchoring the salphen-Co moieties to a variety of rigid linker groups and altering the salphen anchoring positions upon reactivity were evaluated. The catalysts are active for the copolymerization of carbon dioxide and propylene oxide to give poly(propylene carbonate) under mild conditions, and display superior efficiencies and enhanced regiochemical control compared with their mononuclear counterparts (Publication 2). The syn- and anti-forms of binuclear cobalt(III)-trifluoroacetate Schiff base complexes derived from a highly substituted p-terphenyl backbone have been prepared, as confirmed by crystal structures of synthetic precursors. These catalysts are active for the copolymerization of propylene oxide and carbon dioxide under mild conditions to yield poly(propylene carbonate). The anti-form of the dicobalt complex displays higher head-to-tail connectivity and molecular weight, and substantially enhanced turnover frequencies (Publication 3). Binuclear Zn-salphen complexes bearing trifluoromethyl substituents have been employed as catalysts for cyclic carbonate formation. The enhanced electrophilicity expected for the Zn centers was envisaged to favor coordination of the substrates. Selected dimetallic catalysts display elevated activities and turnover frequencies, which exceed those for t-butyl and mononuclear congeners, thus signifying synergistic and possible cooperative reactivity (Publication 5). New binuclear Zn-salphen complexes based on a highly substituted m-terphenyl backbone was prepared. Selected catalysts exhibited high activities for cyclic carbonate synthesis from carbon dioxide and epoxide, but polyether was also produced. These results demonstrate that appropriate positioning of active sites and intermetallic geometry in a shape-persistent bimetallic framework can engender unusual catalytic reactivity (Publication 6).

100410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100410.value: The development of catalytic routes to transform sustainable resources such as carbon dioxide into desirable and valuable chemical products continues to attract considerable interest. In this project, the strategy of modifying the structure and topology of these frameworks in order to create bimetallic cavities, as well as adjust their associated reactivity, has been explored, and excellent catalytic performance under mild conditions for coupling of carbon dioxide and epoxide have been achieved. The exceptional turnover frequencies observed are noteworthy, and paves the way for a new design approach towards highly efficient catalyst systems. The development of novel catalytic reactions mediated by shape-persistent bimetallic assemblies with tunable topologies may be envisaged. Related catalytic transformations such as the ring-opening polymerization of epoxide (or lactide) may be investigated. Further efforts dedicated to the development of bimetallic complexes bearing new rigid linker units, and the modification and functionalization of the Schiff base ligands, would be worthwhile. It should be noted that the catalysts developed in this project are not covered by the patent literature.

100410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100410.value: The use of carbon dioxide as a non-toxic C1 building block and its fixation into valuable chemical feedstock under mild conditions are of great interest, due to its potentially inexpensive, abundant and sustainable characteristics. This project has focused on the design, preparation, and function of multinuclear assemblies featuring reactive metal-organic moieties in face-to-face geometry, that are stacked together by a rigid anchoring group to preclude metal...metal interactions. Such frameworks allow minimal lateral displacement but differing degrees of axial rotation for the metal-organic units. By changing the nature and dimensions of the metal-organic and anchoring components, and thereby varying their relative spatial arrangement and orientation (“topology”) as well as intermetallic distances and geometry, the capacity of the resultant frameworks for binding and activation of small molecules was examined and adjusted. The underlying aim was to develop catalytic applications for these bimetallic systems, for example in the formation of polymers and chemicals using renewable resources. Attractive catalytic performances for coupling of carbon dioxide and organic substrate, in terms of high turnover frequencies (per metal) under mild conditions (low pressure and temperature) have been achieved, which are superior to those for mononuclear analogues, thus signifying synergistic reactivity and cooperativity between the metal centers.

100510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100510.value: One of the most crucial challenges for the development of high performance lithium ion batteries for future vehicle is the development of high power durable cathode material. The cathode materials must be robust and stable upon repeated charging and discharging. Furthermore, the allowable charge-discharge rate should also be high, say 10C or above. There should also be no compromise in safety issues. Hence, electron conductivity and ion conductivity are crucial properties affecting the performance. The aim of this project is to develop high energy storage, as well as high power and high charging rate, lithium ion batteries (LIB) for hybrid electric vehicles (HEV) and/or EV based on olivine lithium transition metal phosphate (LiMPO4) nanomaterials. The proposal consists of three parts: (1) controllable synthesis of large-scale olivine-type LiFePO4 and LiMnPO4, and their solid solution LiFe(1-x)Mn(x)PO4 nanocrystallites (<100nm) with ultrathin plate-like morphology and narrow particle size distribution; (2) characterization of the crystal structure, morphology, composition, electronic and ionic conductivity, and electrochemical characteristics of the LiMPO4 nanocrystallites synthesized; (3) design, fabricate, and optimize of LIB based on LiMPO4 nanocrystallites. We will attempt to synthesize ultrafine LiMPO4 nanocrystallites with well-defined plate-like geometry by three simple and inexpensive methods: (i) hydrothermal method; (ii) precipitation in combination with high-energy ball milling and (iii) moderate temperature calcinations, hydrothermal plus ion-exchange. The structure, composition, morphology and particle size of LiMPO4 nanocrystallites will be characterized systematically to provide information for optimizing the processing parameters of cathode powder synthesis. The LiMPO4 nanocrystallites will be used to fabricate LIB. Two types of batteries will be fabricated and characterized: (1) prototype half-cell using LiMPO4 nanocrystallites as cathode and lithium metal as anode, (2) industrial type cell employing LiMPO4 nanocrystallites as cathode and graphite as anode. Properties related to LIB cell performances, such as charge-discharge cycling hehaviour, will be carefully studied to provide detail information for achieving high energy storage capacity, high output power and high charging rate LIB suitable for HEV or EV. 電池汽車未來發展的最關鍵挑戰，可以說是高性能鋰離子電池正極材料的高功率耐用性能。 理想的正極材料必須是儲能量高和穩定的，並可以反复充電和放電千次以上。此外，所允許的充放電率(大電流)也必須很高(10C或以上)；當然，還不應該在安全問題上妥協。因此，正極材料的電子導電性和離子導電性能的影響是至關重要的。 此項的目的是發展高能量儲存、以及高充放電率的鋰離子電池（LiB）正極材料，這些正極材料應適用於混合動力電動汽車（HEV）或電動汽車(EV)。計劃將根據橄欖石鋰過渡金屬磷酸鹽（LiMPO4、LiFePO4和LiMnPO4）納米材料現有的優越電化學性能，進一步改善其高充放電率特性。

100510.label: Realisation of objectives
100510.value: Both objectives are fully achieved and detail understanding of the critical processing parameters controlling the purity, size, shape and morphologies of the electrode materials. Objective 1. Hydrothermal and solvothermal synthesis processes were adopted to synthesize LiFePO4 and LiMnPO4 in the presence of citric acid, ammonium or polyethylene glycol to control the morphology of the olivine micro- and nano-particles. The mechanisms of the formation of the solid sphere, cubic crystals, rhombic crystals, nano-rods, hollow particles and hollow structures were established. The first objective is fully achieved. Objective 2. The purity and complete transformation of the template to the final composition is crucial to the ultimate performance of the cathode and anode particles. The hollow micro- or nano-structures and nano-rods with higher surface area to volume ratio was found to have the best high rate electrochemical performance. In general, the smaller the particles, the better the high rate performance; however, it was also found that the presence of carbon coating can enhance the capacity as well as the high rate properties. The quality of the carbon coating was found to be affected by the pH values of the reactants during the synthesis. The second objective is fully achieved.

100510.label: Major findings and research outcome
100510.value: [#] refers to number of paper reported in Part C. Olivine LiFePO4 (LFP) with different morphologies were prepared in reactants containing ammonium ions and citric acid (CA) as predicted. Platelet shape NH4-FePO4.H2O phase formed and was found important in controlling the final LFP morphology, which was a poorly defined egg shape. The presence of NH4+ ions slows the speed of crystal growth in the c-direction. The subsequent hydrothermal reaction with CA aiding the dissolution of the LFP lead to hollow LFP after 15h of treatment. The hollow structure has led to a dramatic increase in surface area to volume ratio leading to excellent electromechanical performance. The specific capacity of 158mAh/g was achieved, which is very close to the theoretical value of 170mAh/g. [1] The porous structure was confirmed very important in the performance and cycling of the LiMn2O4 at high rate. [9] Solvothermal approach was also employed to synthesize LiMnPO4 (LMP) nanorods by varying the polyethylene glycol to water ratio, reaction sequence, time and pH value. The reaction mechanism was studied and it was found that the reaction rate depends critically on the pH value of the reactants. Smaller particles with higher lithium ion diffusion coefficient with better electrochemical performance was achieved. [2] LiFeSO4 cathode was also synthesized. However, the lithium ion diffusion rate was found low, which had limited its electrochemical performance. [6] Layered LiNiCoMnO2 thin film electrodes was prepared by PLD to investigate the effect of microstructural difference on the electrochemical performance. It was found that the performance depends on the annealing temperature, composition and thickness. These processing parameters will affect the Li-ion diffusion coefficient. [3] Graphene coating was found useful in enhancing the performance of LiF/Fe nanocomposite cathode. The related mechanism was also studied. [7] The anode was also studied. SnNi-C nanocomposite on carbon matrix synthesized by a simple solvothermal method with subsequent heat treatment was found having outstanding performance. Enhanced electronic conductivity, improved crystallinity and higher purity are factors contributing to the improvement. [4] LiTiO nanorod anodes was also found a potential candidate for next generation LiB. The capacity is as high as 136mAh/g at 10C and ~60% capacity was retained after 1500 cycles. [5] Fe2O3 hierarchical anode was found to have increased the capacity from ~200mAh/g to 675mAh/g. [10] The thin film Fe3O4 porous structure also possess outstanding electrochemical performance. [8]

100510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100510.value: Based on the knowledge obtained concerning the control of morphology and particle size of the related cathode materials, we can develop an industrial project to scale up the production of cathode materials for future generation lithium ion batteries. LiMn2O4 is an environmentally friendly cathode and will be considered as the future cathode research direction. This topic is challenging because the cathode dissolution problem at high temperature need to be solved.

100510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100510.value: This project has studied the method of enhancing the capacity of cathode materials to be used in lithium ion batteries. LiFePO4, LiMnPO4, LiMn2O4 and several other cathode materials were synthesized using new approaches. The most successful electrode is particles with hollow structure, which possesses large surface area for rapid charging and discharging. The newly developed cathode materials can be charged up at 10C or 20C within 6 minutes or 3 minutes respectively. The relevant mechanisms were also studied. The new cathode materials can be used by manufacturers in the making of the next generation lithium ion batteries for electric vehicles.

100710.label: Project Title(Chinese)
100710.value: 彈性學邊值問題的新表述

100710.label: Project Objectives
100710.value: The long-term impacts are three-fold (these aspects, which will not be addressed in the present proposal, could serve as themes of later investigations). First, in the linear case, the proposed research could be used for developing and mathematically analyzing new finite element approximations of the intrinsic approach to the (more realistic) displacement-traction problems, thus extending the analyzes of [9, 10], which were restricted to pure traction problems. As shown in [10], the discretization of the intrinsic approach for such problems seems to be surprisingly effective (most likely because the supports of the basis functions are substantially smaller than those found in the finite element approximations of the classical approach); hence it is reasonable to expect that this effectiveness will also carry over to displacement-traction problems. Second, in the nonlinear case, the proposed research would constitute a welcome complement to the landmark theory of Ball [5] which, at least in some specific cases, would thus be completely recast in terms of the Cauchy-Green strain tensor field as the sole unknown. Third, the proposed research could pave the way for similarly extending the mathematical analysis of the intrinsic approach applied to linear and nonlinear shell models. Such an extension could prove in particular to be a welcome complement to the pioneering work of Opoka & Pietraskiewicz [26] on nonlinearly elastic shells.

100710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100710.value: Classically, the displacement vector field of the reference configuration is the unknown (or one of the unknowns) appearing in the mathematical models of linearized and nonlinear three-dimensional elasticity. Yet another approach, called the "intrinsic" approach, is slowly coming of age, where the strain tensor field, or equivalently the stress tensor field (by means of the constitutive equation), is the only unknown. Since the knowledge of the stress tensor field is of primary importance in computational mechanics, an intrinsic approach is thus particularly attractive from a practical viewpoint. It is only recently, however,that the mathematical analysis and numerical analysis of the intrinsic approach have been undertaken. The objective of this proposal is to contribute to its mathematical analysis, in both the linear and nonlinear cases. In the linear case, its mathematical analysis has been so far limited to pure traction problems, i.e.,where no boundary condition on the unknown displacement is imposed on the boundary of the reference configuration. The first objective of this proposal consists in finding explicit expressions of boundary conditions that only involve the strains for pure displacement, or displacement-traction problems, i.e.,where a more realistic boundary condition of place is imposed on the whole boundary of the reference configuration, or on a subset thereof (this means that the unknown displacement should vanish there). It is also planned to establish the existence of a solution of the corresponding minimization problems, which are thus expressed only in terms of strains (or equivalently, only in terms of stresses). In the nonlinear case,it was already shown that the pure displacement problem can be recast as a minimization problem where the only unknown is the Cauchy-Green strain tensor. The second objective of this proposal is to find in this case an explicit formula for the corresponding boundary condition, expressed only in terms of the components of the unknown Cauchy-Green strain tensor. In addition to its mathematical interest per se, the proposed research would pave the way in the linear case for developing and analyzing new finite element approximations of the intrinsic approach applied to the more realistic displacement-traction problems (preliminary computations indicate that such numerical methods seem to be quite effective). In the nonlinear case,the proposed research would constitute a welcome complement to the landmark existence theory of John Ball, which could thus be completely recast in terms of the Cauchy-Green strain tensor field as the sole unknown, at least in some special cases. 在經典的三維線性和非線性彈性學的數學模型中,描述參考位形的未知量（或未知量之一）是位移向量場。 然而在另一種近年來出現的被稱為“本質途徑”的處理方式中，應變張量或等價的應力張量（通過狀態方程）是僅有的未知量。由於關於應力張量場的知識在計算力學中具有基本的重要性，這一“本質途徑”從實用的角度來看尤其具有吸引力。 然而關於“本質途徑”的數學分析和數值分析僅僅只是在最近才開始。本研究的目標集中在它的線性或非線性情形的數學分析。 線性情形的數學分析到目前為止僅限於純粹的牽引問題，即在參考位形的邊界上未知的位移不給邊界條件。本研究的第一個目標是找到純粹位移或位移-牽引問題中僅僅涉及到應變的邊界條件的顯示運算式，即在參考位形的整體或一部分（這意味著未知的位移必須在這裏消失）被賦以更現實的邊界條件。我們也計畫得到相應的僅涉及到應變（或等價的應力）的極小問題解的存在性。 在非線性情形，業已證明純粹的位移問題可以轉化為僅有的未知量是Cauchy-Green應變張量的一個極小化問題。本研究的第二個目的是得到這種情況下僅由未知的Cauchy-Green應變張量的分量表述的相應邊界條件的顯示運算式。 除了數學興趣外，本研究計畫將圍繞發展並分析線性情形下將這一本質途徑的新的有限元逼近應用到更現實的位移-牽引問題中這一研究方向上另闢蹊徑（初步的計算結果表明這些數值方法似乎很有效）。 在非線性情形，本研究計畫是John Ball的里程碑似的存在性結果的一個很好的補充，至少在一些特殊的情形，可以將問題完全轉化為將Cauchy-Green應變張量場作為唯一的未知量的情形。

100710.label: Realisation of objectives
100710.value: Objectives #1 and #2: Using the Legendre-Fenchel duality, the intrinsic approach has been put in a completely new perspective, which allows in particular the consideration of Dirichlet boundary conditions. The boundary conditions for displacement-traction problems in linear and nonlinear elasticity have been explicitly found, thus solving major open problems in intrinsic elasticity theory. All this has resulted in three publications in A+ journals. Objective #3: We have been careful in formulating all these results in such a way that they "pave the way" for shell theory (this is what 50% means), even though this has not resulted in actual publications; the reason is that fulfilling Objectives #1 and #2 took much much longer than expected (as is often the case in Mathematics!), because unexpected difficulties (mostly from the differential geometry of surfaces) were encountered, and eventually circumvented.

100710.label: Major findings and research outcome
100710.value: - Reformulation of the three basic problems of linearized elasticity within a single framework, via Legendre-Fenchel duality. - Explicit expression of the boundary consitions in the intrinsic approach to linearized elasticity, i.e., in terms of the linearized strain tensor. - Explicit expression of the boundary conditions in the intrinsic approach to nonlinear elasticity, i.e., in terms of the metric tensor, also called the Cauchy-Green tensor.

100710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100710.value: These findings have potential for future developments in two directions: - Two-dimensional linear and nonlinear shell theory. - Numerical simulation of elastic structures by means of ad hoc finite element approximations of the intrinsic approach.

100710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100710.value: The numerical simulation of the elastic structures found in contemporary engineering is of great importance. The interest of the intrinsic approach is that it provides directly the state of stress (rather than the deformation) inside an elastic structure subjected to applied forces. This research is thus highly relevant since it is intended to establish the mathematical foundations of the intrinsic approach, an indispensible preliminary before devising approximate methods for the numerical simulation of elastic structures.

100810.label: Realisation of objectives
100810.value: The only objective of this project was completely carried over and some additional work, which was not in the original objectives, was done as well. More specifically, we performed a smoothed analysis of Beltran and Pardo's algorithm (showing smoothed polynomial cost) and designed a deterministic algorithm which provides a near solution to Smale's 17th problem. In addition, we studied the numerical behavior of this deterministic algorithm and showed it is numerically stable. Finally, we used some of the ideas in this work to analyze algorithms for different (but related) problems, namely, the computation of eigenpairs for Hermitian matrices and the feasibility problem for second-order conic systems.

100810.label: Major findings and research outcome
100810.value: The solving of polynomial equations is one of the central problems in computational mathematics. An assortment of problems in various areas of mathematics and applications reduce to solving this kind of equations. It is probably because of this relevance that Steve Smale included (a very precise form of) polynomial equation solving as the 17th in his list of problems for the mathematicians of the 21st century. In this project we came with the closest development (up to now) to a complete solution of Smale's 17th problem. We performed a smoothed analysis of a randomized algorithm and an average analysis for a deterministic algorithm, showing in both cases that zeros of complex polynomial equations can be efficiently found. The paper with these results was published in "Annals of Mathematics", widely considered the most influential journal in mathematics. In a sequel paper in "Mathematics of Computation" we showed that the deterministic algorithm above is numerically stable. That is, that the accumulation of errors produced by the use of finite precision is unlikely to affect the quality of the algorithm's outcomes. Finally, we used some of the ideas in our development to two different (but related) problems. Firstly (in a paper accepted for publication in "Foundations of Computational Mathematics") we proposed and analyzed an algorithm to compute eigenpairs (eigenvalue, eigenvector) for Hermitian matrices. Secondly (in a paper accepted in "Mathematical Programming") we did so for the feasibility problem for second-order conic systems.

100810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100810.value: Probably the most relevant problem that can be further dealt with the methods and ideas in this project is the computation of eigenpairs for arbitrary complex matrices. This is a long-standing theoretical open problem in numerical linear algebra (algorithms up to now are either numerically unstable or defy rigorous complexity analyses). We are presently working on it.

100810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100810.value: Solving equations, that is, finding values for variables that satisfy a given number of constraints, is arguably the most important task in applied and computational mathematics. The form of these constraints (usually refereed to as equations), along with the nature of the values the variables can take, varies, and as a result a variety of families of equations are considered: diophantine, linear, differential, algebraic, ... One of the most basic families is the so called "polynomial equations". Its importance is so high that the problem of solving this kind of equations has been considered a central problem to be solved in the 21st century. In our project we have done substantial steps towards the solution of this problem.

100910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100910.value: The six Painlevé equations are a series of nonlinear second order differential equations with special properties. Nowadays, it has been realized that they play an important role in many branches of physics, for example, statistical mechanics, nonlinear waves, quantum field theory, general relativity, etc.. Moreover, they may be thought of nonlinear analogues of the classical special functions, such as Airy functions, Bessel functions and parabolic cylinder functions. In the meantime, there has been a considerable amount of interest in their higher order analogues, so-called the Painlevé hierarchies. Usually, the solutions to the Painlevé equations, as well as the Painlevé hierarchies, are meromorphic and have poles in the complex plane. However, there also exist some solutions, which are pole-free on certain line or in certain domain in the complex plane. Although breakthroughs have been made in the recent years, there are still many important open problems in this area. In this project, we will focus on pole-free solutions to the Painlevé hierarchies. More precisely, we will try to prove the existence of these solutions and derive their asymptotics. 所謂的Painleve方程是六個擁有特殊性質的非線性二階常微分方程. 如今, 人們已經意識到這些方程在物理學的很多分支裡面發揮著重要的作用, 比如統計力學, 非線性波動理論, 量子場理論和廣義相對論等等. 此外, 它們的解還被看作為經典的特殊函數(Airy函數, Bessel函數和拋物柱面函數)的非線性推廣. 於此同時, 人們也開始重視高階Painleve方程的研究. 通常來講, Painleve以及其高階方程的解是亞純的, 並且在復平面中擁有極點. 不過, 無極點解也可能在復平面的特定的直線上或者領域裏面存在. 雖然最近幾年這方面的研究已經取得了長足的進步, 在這個研究方向上還有很多重要的待解決的問題. 在此研究項目中, 我們將會專注於研究這些Painleve高階方程的無極點解. 更加確切地, 我們會嘗試證明這些解的存在性, 並且推導它們的漸近性質.

100910.label: Realisation of objectives
100910.value: The main objective of this research project is to study properties of pole-free solutions to the Painlevé equations and the corresponding hierarchies. We first considered the third and fourth Painlevé equations. By using the classical asymptotic methods for ordinary differential equations, we successfully proved that these equations possess pole-free solutions in quite large regions in the complex plane. These solutions, which are also called tronquée solutions, are important in the study of the Painlevé equations. The asymptotic expansions of these solutions are also derived. Then we considered a perturbed Laguerre ensemble in the random matrix theory, which possesses an essential singularity at the point 0. We are interested in the limiting kernel as the matrix size tends to infinity. Due to the influence of the perturbed term, the limiting kernel near the hard edge is no longer the Bessel kernel. By using the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method for the Riemann-Hilbert problems, we derived the limiting kernel and showed that it is closely related to the third Painlevé equation with certain parameters. We think this is an important discovery and implies a new class of universality in the random matrix theory. Moreover, because of the relation between our matrix model and the third Painlevé equation, we proved the existence of the pole-free solution to the third Painlevé equation on the positive real axis and obtained the asymptotics near 0 and infinity. The relation with other Painlevé III equations and the Jimbo–Miwa–Okamoto σ-form are studied, too.

100910.label: Major findings and research outcome
100910.value: In this research project, we studied pole-free solutions to the Painlevé equations. It is well-known that solutions to the Painlevé equations are meromorphic functions and possess numerous poles in the complex plane. Usually, pole-free solutions occur when either the parameters or the initial conditions are special. Due to their nice properties, pole-free solutions are important and attract many researchers’ interest. We studied the third and fourth Painlevé equations, and proved the existence and uniqueness of the tronquée solutions. These solutions are pole-free in quite large regions in the complex plane. The asymptotic expansions of these solutions are also derived. We also considered a particular Painlevé III equation and obtained a special pole-free solution on the positive real axis. This solution plays an important role in describing the phase transition near the hard edge of a perturbed Laguerre ensemble. Moreover, we expect that this solution will also appear in many other matrix models in mathematical physics when the potential has essential singularities. This will give us a new class of universality in the random matrix theory. In addition, we notice that the solutions to the Painlevé equations, namely the Painlevé transcendents, are viewed as a new family of special functions in the 21st century and closely related to orthogonal polynomials. So, we also studied several related orthogonal polynomials. By using different method, especially the difference equation method, we obtained the asymptotics for the orthogonal polynomials, which is not characterized by the Painlevé transcendents but some functions related to elliptic integrals. This is an interesting discovery. More importantly, with the development of the difference equation method, we expect to apply it to study the Painlevé equations as well, especially the discrete Painlevé equations.

100910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100910.value: Based on this project, there are several possible research problems in the future: 1. Study other matrix models with essential singularities. There are quite a few matrix models arising from mathematical physics whose potential has essential singularity. With the results and techniques in this project, we hope to study these problems and find the corresponding universality if possible. 2. Study properties of the tronquée solutions when |z| is bounded. The most well-studied tronquée solutions are those to the second Painlevé equations. This class of solutions is shown to be pole-free not only when |z| is large but also when |z| is bounded. So, we wish to know whether our tronquée solutions to the third and fourth Painlevé equations share the similar properties as those to the second Painlevé equations.

100910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100910.value: The Painlevé equations are a class of nonlinear ordinary differential equations with special properties. Their solutions, known as the Painlevé transcendents, have important applications in many branches of modern physics, including statistical mechanics, random matrix theory, quantum field theory, etc.. Because the Painlevé transcendents play a similar role as the classical special functions in the past, they are viewed as a new family of special functions in the 21st century. In this project, we have derived several valuable solutions to the Painlevé equations. Some solutions are pole-free in large regions in the complex plane, which are of interest since the early study of the Painlevé equations. The other solutions are pole-free on the positive real axis and play an essential role in an important matrix model from mathematical physics. This class of solutions may be used to prove the universality results for a quite large class of matrix models in mathematical physics whose potential has similar singularity as that in our problem.

101210.label: Project Objectives
101210.value: To fabricate bottom-up InGaAs NWs with controlled surface morphology, chemical composition, structural quality, and electronic transport properties utilizing catalytic solid-source chemical vapor deposition (CVD). This provides optimized high performance NWs for subsequent integration studies. To characterize InGaAs NWs to assess the role of NW surface, diameter and stoichiometry on the intrinsic transport properties. This finding will be used for careful device design considerations to achieve the optimal device performances. To assemble highly dense, uniform, well aligned parallel arrays of InGaAs NWs on Si substrates in large-scale with the NW contact printing technique. This NW assembly uniformity will be crucial for the subsequent integration of high performance InGaAs NWs at the circuit level. To directly characterize InGaAs NW arrays to evaluate the resulting device performance limits. To explore integrated circuits based on high performance InGaAs NW arrays first assembled on Si substrates. This demonstrates the integration of InGaAs NW arrays into functional circuits which are compatible with the conventional Si technology. Then we will further extend our studies onto plastic substrates to explore the low-cost, large-scale, and flexible electronics utilizing high performance crystalline NW materials.

101210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101210.value: Synthetic nanomaterials, such as semiconductor nanowires (NW), will play an essential role in the future of integrated circuits due to the unique electrical and physical properties arising from their qusai one-dimensional (1-D) structure. Through integration with conventional silicon (Si) technology, they enable further miniaturization of devices, enhance switching speed, and reduce power consumption as compared to conventional planar structures. However, many challenges still remain in controlling the synthesis and assembly, understanding the fundamental properties, detailed device characterization, and establishing the performance limits of the integrated circuits based on these synthetic nanostructures. In this proposal, we will emphasize indium gallium arsenide (InGaAs) NWs which have been shown to exhibit high carrier mobility and low off-state leakage. The aim is to address these challenges through a series of well designed and systematic experiments ranging from NW synthesis to circuit integration studies. Ultimately, we will extend this work to parallel NW arrays assembled on plastic substrates, thereby utilizing high performance crystalline inorganic nanomaterials for low-cost, large-scale, and flexible electronics. 合成納米材料，如半導體納米線將在未來的集成電路中發揮重要作用，由於其獨特的准一維結構和電氣和物理性能。与傳統的器件結構相比，這些納米材料与傳統的矽技術集成可以使進一步器件小型化成為可能，，并可提高器件的開關速度，及降低功耗。然而這一領域仍然有很多挑戰，比如如何控制納米材料的合成和組裝，研究材料的基本性能，納米器件的表徵，及瞭解這樣的納米器件的性能極限等。在這項計劃書中，我們強調銦鎵砷化物奈米線已被證明具有較高的載子遷移率，低關閉態漏電電流。我們的目標是通過一系列精心設計和系統的實驗，從納米線合成到集成電路，來解決這些挑戰性的問題。最終，我們將會把這項工作擴展到塑膠基板上的納米線陣列及器件，從而利用高性能無機納米材料製造低成本，大規模的，和柔性的電子產品。

101210.label: Realisation of objectives
101210.value: In this project, we have successfully achieved all the objectives with 100% of completion. Specifically, we have developed a unique “two-step” chemical vapor deposition technique to synthesize InxGa1-xAs nanowires with controlled crystallinity and morphology. By simply manipulating the source powder mixing ratio and growth parameters, the complete composition and bandgap tunable InxGa1-xAs alloy nanowires (diameter = 25~30 nm) have been attained (Objective 1). Importantly, the obtained nanowires exhibit impressive electrical performances with the electron mobility up to 10,000 cm2V-1s-1, high current on/off ratio and on current density, when they are configured into field effect transistors (Objective 2). Also, the current-voltage behaviors of fabricated transistors, with different nanowire diameters, reveal that the aggressive scaling of nanowire diameter would result in a degradation of electron mobility, while low-temperature measurements further decouple the effects of surface/interface traps and phonon scattering, highlighting the impact of surface roughness scattering on the electron mobility (Objective 2). Furthermore, the device operation can be tailored with the newly developed metal cluster decoration approach, in which this technique can effectively modulate the transistor threshold voltage with minimal changes in device performance by just controlling the work function difference between metal clusters deposited and NWs (Objective 2). All these suggest a careful design consideration of nanowire dimension and device structure is required for achieving the optimal device performances. In addition to the material and electrical characterization, these nanowires are then employed in the contact printing to achieve large-scale assembly of nanowire parallel arrays on conventional silicon substrates for the fabrication of thin film transistors as well as different circuit components (Objective 3). For example, utilizing the metal cluster decoration approach, we have achieved n-channel metal oxide semiconductor (NMOS) inverters which use an Au-decorated enhancement-mode nanowire transistor driver and an original depletion-mode nanowire transistor load with the gate and source/drain terminals connected (Objective 4). The inverters can be operated effectively with a 100 Hz input and a high gain (Objective 5). Notably, the static power dissipation is estimated to be as low as ≈ 4 μW, which is comparable to the lowest NW NMOS reported values and far lower than their planar counterparts (Objective 5). In summary, all these findings have indicated the technological potency of these InxGa1-xAs nanowire arrays for the active channel materials of future high-performance integrated circuits.

101210.label: Major findings and research outcome
101210.value: In this project, there are several important major findings and therefore all these lead to more than 10 high-impact journal publications (2 Advanced Materials, 1 Nano Letters, 4 ACS Nano and others) as well as 10 presentations at various international conferences (4 invited talks). Specifically, as reported in ACS 2012, we have developed a simple but unique “two-step” chemical vapor deposition technique to obtain crystalline and uniform InxGa1-xAs nanowires as compared to the defective ones grown by other conventional methods. These high-quality nanowires exhibit impressive electrical properties, yielding more than 10,000 cm2V-1s-1 of mobility when configured into field effect transistors. Importantly, these nanowires can be assembled into parallel arrays and fabricated as high-performance thin film transistors on silicon. These nanowire thin film devices give superior electrical performances which is better than the state-of-the-art silicon devices. Furthermore, one of the ultimate challenges in practically developing high-performance nanowire thin film transistors is the control of nanowire electrical properties. Notably, it is challenging to control all those electrical properties during the nanowire growth. In this regard, we have developed a simple scheme to modulate the electrical properties of nanowire devices, simply decorating the nanowire channels by metal nanoparticles. As discussed in Advanced Materials 2013, by manipulating the work function of the metal nanoparticles decorated, we can tailor the threshold voltage, carrier concentration and others of the nanowire channels. Importantly, we have later applied this decoration scheme to fabricate several nanowire circuit components and demonstrated all those with high operating performance as well as low power consumption. In summary, all these major findings are significant and bring forward the utilization of InxGa1-xAs nanowire parallel arrayed devices for future electronics.

101210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101210.value: Although there are many high-impact findings resulted from this work, there are still several potentially key areas for the further development of these InxGa1-xAs nanowire devices. One is to investigate the ultimate performance of the optimized nanowire device structure, such as configuring them in the top-gated device with high-k dielectrics. Currently, all the studied devices are fabricated as back-gated transistors, in which the device performance is expected to be restricted by the gate coupling efficiency in the back gate. Therefore, the electrical performances are predicted to enhance significantly once the devices are optimized in the top-gated structures. Another one is to further explore the applications of these nanowires in optoelectronics including the infrared photodetectors, due to the unique bandgap range of InxGa1-xAs nanowires and extraordinarily large surface area to volume ratio. Also, since the electron mobility of these nanowires is significantly higher than the one of silicon, these nanowire photodetectors are expected to yield much higher photoresponsivity and photosensitivity. All these potential works would push further the technological development of InxGa1-xAs for various practical applications.

101210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101210.value: III-V compound semiconductor nanowire materials such as InAs nanowires have been extensively studied for high-speed and high-frequency electronics due to the low effective electron mass and corresponding high carrier mobility. However, further utilizations still restrict from the substantial leakage current in InAs nanowire devices owing to their small electronic bandgap. In this project, we have developed the successful synthesis of ternary InxGa1-xAs nanowires with controlled stoichiometry in order to tackle this leakage issue utilizing the larger band gap material but at the same time not sacrificing the high electron mobility. We adapt a two-step growth method on amorphous SiO2/Si substrates which significantly reduces the kinked morphology and surface coating along the nanowires. The grown nanowires exhibit excellent crystallinity and uniform stoichiometric composition along the entire length of the nanowires. More importantly, the electrical properties of those nanowires and nanowire parallel arrayed film are found to be remarkably impressive with high current ON/OFF ratio, field-effect mobility, and ON current density. It is also noted that the fabricated nanowire circuit components can operate with the high performance and low power consumption. All these have further illustrated the potential for utilizing these high-performance nanowires on substrates for the fabrication of future integrated circuits.

101210.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
101210.value: In this project, we have successfully synthesized high performance InGaAs nanowires utilizing the newly developed "two-step" chemical vapor deposition technique. Importantly, these nanowires exhibit several impressive properties in electronics and optoelectronics. Due to all these unique and interesting properties, we have therefore established several collaboration with other research groups (e.g. Arizona State University, Wuhan University, and National Laboratory for Infrared Physics, Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, etc.) to further explore potential applications of these nanowires in sensors and photodetectors. Furthermore, we have recruited two undergraduate students working part-time for 9 months altogether for this project, in which they were involved in the synthesis of nanowires and the corresponding electrical measurement of fabricated nanowire devices. All these trainings have provided them early research exposure that is at the cutting edge of materials science and at the same time moving the project forward.

101310.label: Project Title(Chinese)
101310.value: 分數階偏微分方程的核近似法

101310.label: Project Objectives
101310.value: To develop the theoretical formulation and mathematical analysis for solving problems in partial differential equations with fractional order. Both well-posed and ill-posed problems will be considered. Particularly in the ill-posed case, we aim at developing mathematical model for the determination of unknown concentration distribution and fluid flow pattern from measurement of scattered noisy data in an accessible media at a particular time. To develop an efficient computational method for solving both well-posed and ill-posed problems in partial differential equations with fractional order. Combining the use of reproducing kernel functions approximation and adaptive regularization techniques, we will provide a stable and accurate numerical approximation to the solutions of the problems.

101310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101310.value: Partial differential equations of fractional order have been the focus of many studies because of their various applications in fluid mechanics, viscoelasticity, biology, physics, and engineering. Fractional calculus in mathematics is a natural extension of integer-order calculus. It has been used for modelling many physical processes arisen from real-life problems, for instance, the modelling on the transport of passive tracers carried by fluid flows in a porous medium under groundwater hydrology. Studies of the complicated phenomena of the interstitial fluid flows are still under intensive researches and are particularly challenging for quantitative analyses and modelling. Some kinds of numerical techniques are indispensable for industrial and engineering applications. The aim of this project is to provide a theoretical background and justification on developing efficient computational methods for solving both well-posed and ill-posed partial differential equations of fractional order. To speed up the time of computations, modern numerical methods, mainly meshless kernel-based approximation methods combined with the methods of fundamental solutions and particular solutions; Laplace Transform and regularization techniques, will be employed and implemented. 分數階偏微分方程在流體力學、 粘彈性、 生物學、 物理和工程的各種應用有很多的重點研究。 在數學中的分數階微積分是整數階微積分的自然延伸。 它已用於許多物理過程，例如地下水的多孔介質的運輸模型中液體流動的複雜現象的研究仍在深入研究，特別是具有挑戰性的量化分析和建模。有效率的數值解法在工業和工程應用是不可缺少的。 本專案的目的是提供理論背景和發展高效率的計算方法，解決合適和不合適分數階偏微分方程組。為要加快計算將採用並實施現代的數值方法:主要是結合基本解，拉普拉斯變換，正則化技術和基於內核的無網格近似方法。

101310.label: Realisation of objectives
101310.value: The theoretical formulation and mathematical analysis for solving problems in partial differential equations with fractional orders had been investigated. Both well-posed and ill-posed problems were considered. Particularly in the ill-posed case, we had developed a new mathematical model for the determination of unknown temperature distribution and heat flux history from measurement of scattered noisy data in an accessible media at a particular time. In general, a complete recovery of the unknown initial temperature and heat flux is not attainable from mere scattered final temperature measurements with noises. We first gave a theoretical justification on the efficiency and convergence of combining the kernel-based approximation method and discretized Tikhonov regularization technique for solving these kinds of highly ill-posed problems. In one of our published papers we had proven that the unknown solution can be reconstructed with stability estimate and regularization control. In real-life heat conduction process, this provides a theoretical foundation to develop practical algorithm to determine the unknown initial temperature profile from final scattered heat measurement. Furthermore, the result of this work can be extended to solve more general inverse problems such as Cauchy problem and inverse source identification problem for partial differential equations of fractional order. The theoretical part had been extended by the PI to solve three-dimensional Laplace problems on sphere via the use of harmonic kernels. The first objective of the project had been realized. Based on the theoretical results, an efficient computational method had been developed by combining the methods of fundamental solutions, radial basis functions, and adaptive regularization. The computational method had been shown to be effective and accurate in solving these kinds of inverse backward heat conduction problems. Furthermore, the method is a truly meshless computational method which can avoid the tedious meshing problem in using some traditional computational methods like finite element or finite difference. The numerical algorithm had firstly applied with good success to solve well-posed problems of various kinds of fractional partial differential equations. We then extended the numerical algorithm to solve ill-posed problems of time-fractional diffusion equation. The second objective of the project had been realized.

101310.label: Major findings and research outcome
101310.value: The major results of this research project are: (i) The theoretical formulation of the mathematical model on solving problems in partial differential equations with fractional orders had been developed. One paper had been published. (ii) A truly meshless computational algorithm based on reproducing kernels and adaptive regularization technique for solving the mathematical model had been developed and coded by using the matrix solver MATLAB. The algorithm was found to be efficient and accurate to solve the highly ill-posed inverse problems. Two papers on solving well-posed and ill-posed problems of fractional order partial differential equations respectively had been published. (iii) A new computational method (Finite Integration Method) that enjoys both the advantages of existing numerical methods, such as finite difference, finite elements, and meshless kernel approximation, had been developed and found to be highly effective and efficient to solve various kinds of partial differential equations. A paper had been published. Furthermore, we also extended the Bell polynomial to determine the exact solutions of supersymmetric equations. A paper had been published.

101310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101310.value: Both the numerical algorithm and the regularization techniques have been proven to be efficient in solving both well-posed and ill-posed problems of fractional order partial differential equations. The theoretical justification and numerical verification on the meshless methods via the use of reproducing kernels will further enhance the establishment of efficient and effective computational methods with potential applications to solve large scale real industrial problems. The newly developed Finite Integration Method will be extended to solve fractional order partial differential equations.

101310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101310.value: It is the purpose of this research proposal to develop the theoretical formulation and computational method for problems in partial differential equations with fractional orders. This kind of numerical computations is very important and in high demand by the engineering industry. For instance, it is important to determine the unknown temperature and heat flux history from measured data with noises during heat conduction and diffusion processes for economical and safe control of plants. The results of this proposal will also greatly facilitate the current research activities in the studies of inverse problems.

101410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
101410.value: 一些正交多項式和正交函數中的問題

101410.label: Project Objectives
101410.value: Develop a conceptual theory of summation theorems and transformation formulas for special functions using contour integral representations resembling the integrals in the Taylor and Laurent series. The techniques used are complex analysis and long experience to know what to look for. Solve the Calogero problem of identifying interacting particle systems whose small oscillations around equilibrium are isochronous. Also provide a q-analogue which is a deformed system. Develop Plancherel-Rotach asymptotics for the polynomials in the Askey scheme and also do the large degree asymptotics for certain q-polynomials when q depends on the degree and the degree tends to infinity. Find an analytic setting for the Macdonald ${}_4 \phi_3$ biorthogonal rational functions [21]. Mcdonald took a whole Cambridge Tract to develop this theory but our preliminary findings shows not only that we get his results but our findings indicate that there are natural companion families of biorthogonal rational functions that were missed. Moreover we believe there are more general ${}_{10}\phi_9$ functions which will be the highest level of generalization. We have already formulated a q-versions of the Freud conjectures [20]. We wish to study the asymptotics of the recursion coefficients and study the nonlinear difference equations satisfied by the recursion coefficients. The recursion coefficients of polynomials orthogonal with respect to exp(-Nx^4 + ax^2) have fascinating properties and there some indications that they will also hold for our q-analogues.

101410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101410.value: We explore several ideas involving orthogonal polynomials and orthogonal functions. These functions are functions that appear in applied problems and in many instances their properties are useful or crucial in solving equations describing explicit models. We greatly simplify the study of biorthogonal rational functions identified by I G. Macdonald and discover natural companions to them. We plan to study these functions in detail. Another problem is to determine the behavior of standard polynomials (of the Askey Scheme) when the degree tends to infinity. Another problem to to identify isochronous systems using biorthogonal rational functions. There are linear operators associated with the orthogonal polynomials and rational functions. They lead to interpolation series which are analogues of Taylor and Laurent series. This answers questions in interpolation and give a fresh approach to the theory of evaluating explicit sums and integrals of special functions. Analogues of the Freud weights are introduced and they lead to nonlinear discrete integrable systems. We plan to study the discrete systems arising from orthogonal polynomials and use them to determine the behavior of the recursion coefficients. We also expect that the initial conditions which come from orthogonal polynomials lead to well behaved solutions while any other initial conditions lead to chaotic solutions of the nonlinear difference equations. 在這個項目中, 我們會研究關於正交多項式和正交函數的幾個問題. 這些函數經常出現在應用問題中. 在求解一些描述數學模型的方程的時候, 它們的性質往往起到有益的甚至是至關重要的作用. 目前我們已經很大程度地簡化了I.G. Macdonald提出的雙正交有理函數並且找到了它們的同類函數. 我們計劃更加詳細的研究它們. 第二個問題是在Askey類正交多項式的階趨向無窮的時候, 確定它們的性質. 第三個問題是要用前面提及的雙正交有理函數去鑑別一些等時系統. 這些系統是與正交多項式和有理函數有關的線性算子. 它們會導出與Taylor和Laurent級數類似的插值級數. 已有的研究已經回答了一些插值理論中的問題並且提供了一個計算一些與特殊函數有關的求和以及積分的新方法. 目前人們找出了一些與Freud權函數類似的函數, 發現它們會導致離散的可積系統. 我們計劃研究與正交多項式有關的離散系統, 並且用這些多項式來確定系統中遞歸係數的性質. 我們也希望證明從正交多項式中得到的初值條件會給我們的非線性差分方程帶來性質良好的解, 同時其他所有的初值條件都會導致混沌的解.

Additional work on approximation operators has been carried out. The research results have also been disseminated at several international conferences. Please see part C for details of the publications and presentations.

The recursion coefficients of polynomials orthogonal with respect to exp(-Nx^4 + ax^2) have fascinating properties and there some indications that they will also hold for our q-analogues.

101410.label: Major findings and research outcome
101410.value: We developed the Plancherel-Rotach asymptotics for a general class of q-orthogonal polynomials. We also proved a theorem for asymptotics of integrals of product of or polynomials times a fixed function. This is applicable to the many combinatorial numbers that have this type of representation involving orthogonal polynomials. We developed a separation of variables approach to combinatorial numbers which are integrals of products of orthogonal polynomials times their weight function. This includes derangements, perfect matchings, weighted derangements and general weighted combinatorial problems. This is done via a difference equations approach We found an analytic approach to the biorthogonal rational functions originally developed by I. G. Macdonald through Hecke algebras. We found new functions and many new interrelationships between four classes of biorthogonal rational functions. We also found several inequalities for n x n determinants generalizing 2x2 cases. Our approach is very general and leads to many other developments. We also found a new approach to finding integral representations for q-polynomials and functions. This led to a large number of new identities for such functions. We continued our research on the J-matrix method in physics and proved that the spectrum and spectral measures of the Hamiltonian and its tridiagonal representation are the same. Physicists expected the spectrum to be the same.

101410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101410.value: The integral representations project is expected to lead to several further developments and applications to orthogonal polynomials with varying weights. The work on Macdonald rational functions is just the first step in a systematic study of these functions. We developed the asymptotics of integrals on unbounded sets but we are currently working on the bounded cases and they are very promising. We have several new ideas about further work on the J-matrix method. We extended the inequalities from determinants to Pfaffians with connection to quaternionic calculus.

101410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101410.value: Special functions are explicit functions that appear in many areas of applications of mathematics. Some of the special functions discovered in the 1980's are now used all over mathematics and physics. We have isolated new functions which have a lot of structure. We also identified techniques to classify and apply quite a few standard and recently discovered functions. We confirmed a concept used by physicists since the 1970's without mathematics proof and found additional properties of the physics technique. Some times one can not get explicit formulas for combinatorial numbers but would like to know what happens when we have a large configuration. We handled several cases of these numbers.

101510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101510.value: The long-lived phosphorescence and rich excited state properties associated with the metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) excited state of the rhenium(I) tricarbonyl diimine complexes have been extensively reported. It has been shown that with rational design on the diimine ligand, this class of complexes can be used as a building blocks for many different applications. However, when the diimine ligand is functionalized with a specific functional moiety for the application, tuning of the physical and excited state properties of these complexes is extremely difficult since the carbonyl coligands cannot be derivatized and are inert towards substitution. We have recently shown that by replacing the carbonyl ligands with isoelectronic isocyanide ligands, a new class of luminescent rhenium(I) isocyano diimine complexes can be obtained. By simply varying the electronic and steric features of substituent on the nitrogen atom of the isocyanide ligands, the properties of the corresponding rhenium(I) complexes could be readily modified. In addition, it would also open up the possibility for the extension of the rhenium bipyridine luminophore towards the construction of highly functionalized molecular systems. In this project, new series of rhenium(I) diimine complexes with two, three or four isocyanide ligands in different conformations will be synthesized and characterized. These complexes will be subjected to detailed spectroscopic and electrochemical studies. Moreover, by slight modification of the substituent of the isocyanide ligands, rhenium(I) diimine luminophores with diverse physical and excited state properties could be readily obtained. Through rational design, water-soluble luminophores, photocatalytic and light-harvesting systems will be developed. In summary, the proposed project should contribute to the basic understanding of the photophysics and reactivity of rhenium(I) isocyano diimine complexes. It should also provide insights into the development of photocatalytic system capable of converting solar energy to chemical energy and carrying out useful catalytic reactions. 三羰基錸(I)二亞胺配合物的MLCT激發態而導致的長壽磷光及其豐富激發態特性已經被廣泛報告。透過對二亞胺的理性設計，此類型配合物能夠用作構造單元作不同的應用。但是，羰基配體不能夠衍生及很難被取代，所以當二亞胺加入功能基團作不同應用時，這些配合物的物理及激發態特性很難被調節。我們於近期已展示了透過等電子異氰基配體取代羰基配體而獲得新型發光異氰基錸(I)二亞胺配合物。還有通過改變異氰基中氮原子取代物的電子及位阻特性時，其相對錸(I)配合物的特性亦會因此而改變。除此之外，這亦可以開拓錸(I)雙聯吡啶發光體在構建可作多功能化分子系統的發展。 在這項目中，帶有二、三或四異氰配體的新系列錸(I)二亞胺配合物會被合成及表徵。這些配合物的分光物理及電化學的特性也將會被研究。再者，透過異氰配體中取代物的微調，更可獲得擁有多樣化的物理及激發態特性的錸(I)二亞胺發光體。透過理性的設計，水溶性的發光體、光催化及光收成的系統亦會被發展。總括而言，這個項目不僅提供異氰基錸(I)二亞胺配合物的光物理及活躍性的基本認知，而且，亦對發展把太陽能轉成化學能並同時進行有用的催化反應之光催化系統提供參考依據。

101510.label: Major findings and research outcome
101510.value: The research was conducted in accordance with the proposed research plan and methodology. Tricarbonyl Re(I) diimine complexes are widely used as building blocks in many applications. However, these applications are limited by the difficulty of tuning excited-state and physical properties. In this context, we have designed different novel classes of readily tunable rhenium(I) diimine luminophores, [Re(CNR)4(N–N)]+ (ref. 1), [Re(CO)(CNR)3(N–N)]+ (ref. 2), and [Re(CO)2(CNR)2(N–N)]+ (ref. 5). In this project, a wide range of isocyanide ligands with diverse electronic, steric and functional properties have been successfully prepared (refs. 1,2,4,5). On the other hand, new synthetic methods have been developed for the preparation of these isocyano Re(I) diimine complex systems. Based on these synthetic methods, most of the isocyanide ligands can be incorporated into these complex systems to give a new series of MLCT phosphorescent Re(I) complexes with interesting and readily tunable photophysical properties (ref. 5). Their application as luminescent probes has also been investigated (ref. 3), opening up possibilities for extending Re(I) diimine luminophores to the construction of highly functionalized supramolecular systems. With the newly-developed photo-ligand substitution reaction, new class of water-soluble dicyano rhenate(I) diimine complexes, which exhibit exceptionally strong solvatochromism and photocatalytic activity for the reduction of carbon dioxide, have been developed (ref. 6). All the new ligands and their metal complexes have been fully characterized to confirm their identity. The photophysical and photochemical properties of these complexes under different micro-environment as well as the electrochemical properties have also been studied. These complexes not only show applications derived from their luminescent behavior such as phosphorescent materials, chemosensors and probes, many of them are also good photosensitizers and photocatalysts. Some of these results have been reported in six articles in internationally-refereed journals including Organometallics, Inorganic Chemistry, Dalton Transactions, Chemical Communications and Coordination Chemistry Reviews. The importance of these works led to a Distinguished Lectureship Award from the Chemical Society of Japan (2013) and numerous invitations to lecture at international conferences, including the 2010 International Chemical Congress of Pacific Basin Societies: “Pacifichem 2010,” Hawaii, U.S.A. in December 2010; the 19th International Symposium on the Photochemistry and Photophysics of Coordination Compounds (19th ISPPCC), Strasbourg, France in July 2011; the 3rd Asian Conference on Coordination Chemistry (ACCC3), New Delhi, India in October 2011; the 7th Asian Photochemistry Conference 2012, Osaka, Japan in November 2012; 93rd Annual Meeting of CSJ, Shiga, Japan in March 2013 (keynote and award lecture).

101510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101510.value: New classes of isocyano rhenium(I) diimine luminophores have been developed in this project. The strong phosphorescent properties, long-lived excited state lifetimes as well as high flexibility in the design and tuning of these complex systems have been demonstrated. Moreover, some of these complexes show exceptionally strong environmental sensitive emission properties and good photocatalytic properties. With these properties, it is anticipated that new classes of phosphorescent materials with enhanced performance and desirable photophysical properties, highly sensitive chemosensors and robust photocatalytic systems can be developed through optimization and functionalization of these complex systems. Since the excited state properties, redox potentials and absorption properties of these complexes are readily tunable, new photocatalytic systems can be readily designed by coupling tailor-made Re(I) diimine complexes with properties suitable for the photosensitization of various electrocatalysts. On the other hand, similar design strategy and concept should also be applicable to improve the luminescent and excited state properties of different transition metal complex systems.

101510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101510.value: In this project, we have designed several new classes of emissive (phosphorescent) compounds. All the newly designed compounds have been prepared with new synthetic methodology and fully characterized. The functional properties, such as the luminescence (light emission), light absorption (color) and electrochemical properties, of these compounds have been examined by different techniques. With these new classes of compounds, compounds with desirable physical and emission properties could be tailor-made. It is expected that the current design concept can be widely applied to enhance the tunability and properties of different families of compounds. The study also showed that these compounds not only lead to light emission-based applications such as the development of new phosphorescent materials and chemical sensors, but they are also demonstrated to be good photocatalysts, which can facilitate the use light energy in the production of useful chemicals. On the other hand, these compounds could also be functioned as photosensitizers to use light in the activation of different chemical processes. The results have been reported in internationally-refereed journals and led to a Distinguished Lectureship Award from the Chemical Society of Japan (2013) and numerous invitations to lecture at international conferences.
