101810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101810.value: This project is mainly concerned with fundamental studies of C-H bond activation by a series of nitrido, imido and amido complexes of ruthenium. Compared to metal-oxo species, C-H bond activation by metal nitrido (M≡N), imido (M=NR’) and amido (M-NHR’, M-NR’R”) species has received much less attention. An understanding of the mechanisms these reactions could lead to new and selective methods for C-H amination of organic substrates, which are involved in the synthesis of many drugs. Nitrido, imido and amido species may also effect dehydrogenation of organic substrates. These reactions usually occur by hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). HAT reactions are of fundamental interest since they represent the initial steps in many important organic transformations in chemical and biological systems. In this project we propose to study C-H bond activation by a series of nitrido, imido and amido complexes of ruthenium bearing salen ligands. The advantages of using salen ligands include ease of synthesis, stabilization of high oxidation states, steric and electronic effects are readily tuned by varying substituents, and chiral salen ligands can also be readily prepared. Our preliminary investigations show that (salen)ruthenium(VI) nitrido complexes readily activate the C-H bonds of various hydrocarbons. A detail study of these unprecedented reactions is of fundamental interest, and could also lead to a novel approach to C-H amination of organic substrates. Our preliminary studies also show that (salen)ruthenium(IV) amido species prepared via addition of various nucleophiles to (salen)ruthenium(VI) nitrido complexes readily undergo HAT with hydrocarbons. An understanding of the mechanisms of these reactions is of fundamental interest, and could also lead to the development of new, selective methods for the dehydrogenation of organic substrates. We also propose to prepare a series of highly active ruthenium imido (as well as amido) complexes via oxidation of readily prepared (salen)ruthenium(III) amine complexes and to study their reaction with various organic substrates. Our studies should result in significant advances in C-H bond activation by complexes containing metal-nitrogen multiple bonds. It should also provide insight into the design of new catalytic systems for the C-H amination and dehydrogenation of organic substrates. 本課題主要研究一些釕的氮化物，亞胺基和胺基化合物啟動的C-H鍵。與金屬氧化物相比，由金屬氮化物(M≡N)，亞胺基(M=NR’)和胺基(M-NHR’, M-NR’R”)化合物所激活的C-H鍵較少引起人們的注意。反應的機理研究表明，這些反應可選擇性胺化一些有機底物。這個過程包含在藥物合成中。同時，金屬釕的希夫鹼的亞胺基和胺基化合物可能使有機底物發生去氫反應。這個反應通常通過氫原子轉移(HAT)來完成。HAT是一個重要的反應，因為在化學和生物體系中它是許多有機物轉化過程中的第一步反應。在此課題中，我們打算用一些含希夫鹼配體金屬釕的氮化物，亞胺基和胺基化合物來活化C-H鍵。使用希夫鹼作為配體是因為它製備方便，能夠穩定高氧化態，可以通過改變它的取代基團來調節空間位阻和電子效應。同時，手性的希夫鹼配體也很容易製備。我們的初步調查結果表明，希夫鹼釕(VI)氮化物很容易活化各種的碳氫化合物。進一步研究表明這些新反應是非常有意義的，因為它提供了一個新的胺化有機化合物的方法。同時，我們的研究證實通過各種親核試劑與希夫鹼釕(VI)氮化物反應得到的希夫鹼釕(IV)胺基化合物很容易與碳氫化合物發生氫原子轉移(HAT)反應。對於此反應的機理的研究是非常有化學意義的，因為它是一個全新的、選擇性的使有機物去氫的方法。我們打算通過氧化希夫鹼釕(III)胺化物來製備一些高活性的金屬釕的亞胺基和胺基化合物，並研究它們與各種有機底物的反應。此外，我們將利用含金屬-氮多重鍵的化合物來激活C-H鍵。這些研究將在C-H胺化和有機底物的去氫的催化體系中提供有價值的見解。

101810.label: Major findings and research outcome
101810.value: 1. C-H activation by ruthenium(VI) nitride complex We have provided definitive evidence for intermolecular C-H activation of alkanes with C-H bonds as strong as those in cyclohexane by a (salen)ruthenium(VI) nitrido species. The initial rate limiting step involves HAT to form an alkyl radical, which then undergoes N-rebound and desaturation pathways that are reminiscent of C H activation by cytochrome P450 and metal–oxo species. To the best of our knowledge, desaturation of alkanes by a metal–nitrido species is unprecedented. Our findings should provide insights into C-H functionalization using metal nitrides. 2. We have done experimental and computational studies of the facile oxidative C−N bond cleavage of anilines by a (salen)ruthenium(VI) nitrido complex. We provide evidence that the initial step involves nucleophilic attack of aniline at the nitrido ligand of the ruthenium complex, which is followed by proton and electron transfer to afford a (salen)ruthenium(II) diazonium intermediate. This intermediate then undergoes unimolecular decomposition to generate benzene and N2. 3. Exploring new reactivity of metal nitrides is of great interests to chemists because it can provide insights to N2 fixation chemistry and provide new pathways for nitrogenation of organic substrates. In this project, reaction of a (salen)ruthenium(VI) nitrido complex with various alkynes was found to result in the formation of novel (salen)ruthenium(III) imine complexes. Kinetic and computational studies suggest that the reactions go through an initial ruthenium(IV) aziro intermediate, followed by addition of nucleophiles to give the (salen)ruthenium(III) imine complexes. These unprecedented reactions provide a new pathway for nitrogenation of alkynes based on a metal nitride.

101810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101810.value: The activation of C-H bonds of various organic substrates by ruthenium nitrido complexes can be further explored. The reaction of aliphatic amines with ruthenium nitride should be investigated. In future we also plan to study nitrogenation of various other alkynes.

101810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101810.value: In this project we mainly studied C-H bond activation of alkanes, C-N bond cleavage of anilines and alkyne functionalization by (salen)ruthenium(VI) nitrido complexes (RuN). Compared to metal-oxo species, C-H bond activation by metal nitrido (M≡N) species has received much less attention. Our work should contribute to a better understanding of the mechanisms of these reactions and could lead to new and selective methods for C-H amination of organic substrates, which are involved in the synthesis of many drugs. We have also discovered the dehydrogenation of organic substrates by RuN. These reactions usually occur by hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). HAT reactions are of fundamental interest since they represent the initial steps in many important organic transformations in chemical and biological systems. In this project we have also shown that (salen)ruthenium(VI) nitrido complexes readily activate the C-H bonds of various hydrocarbons. Our findings are of fundamental interest, and could also lead to the development of new, selective methods for the dehydrogenation of organic substrates.

101910.value: To develop low-cost solution-based chemical processes for synthesizing CIGS nanocrystals with controlled compositions and adjustable energy band-gaps; To design and prepare arrays of CIGS/CdS/ZnO nanostructures on transparent substrates; To prepare and characterized CIGS-based solar cells with the nanostructures arrays.

101910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101910.value: Chalcopyrite Cu(In1-xGax)Se2 (CIGS) has be considered as a promising candidate for solar cell applications. While high conversion efficiency of about 20% has been demonstrated in thin film CIGS solar cell, its wide commercial applications have not yet been realized. This is mainly due to the difficultly in achieving controllable and uniform composition over large area and the relatively high manufacturing cost involved in the vacuum co-evaporation/sputtering processes. One possible approach to alleviate these problems is to prepare CIGS nanostructures using solution based approaches which are typically of much lower cost. Using the CIGS nanostructures for making solar cells can potentially offer additional advantages of increasing the p-n junction area and improving the charge collection efficiency. The present project proposes to develop low-cost solution-based approaches for making CIGS based solar cell. CIGS nanoparticles and nanorods with controllable compositions would first be synthesized by solution-based chemical reactions. Arrays of CIGS/CdS/ZnO nanostructures would then be prepared on glass substrates again with solution-based approaches. Solar cells consisting arrays of ZnO nanorod/CdS nanoshell/CIGS nanoparticles coating and CIGS nanorod/CdS nanoparticle coating/ZnO nanoparticle coating would be prepared and characterized. Key parameters controlling the photovoltaic and charge conduction processes would be investigated and correlated to the solar cell performance.

101910.label: Realisation of objectives
101910.value: In this project, we explored simple and low-cost methods for preparing a series of novel 1D ZnO-based core/shell nanostructures with the realization of composition-dependent properties and structure-dependent properties. Arrays of ZnO/CuSe and ZnO/CuInSe2 nanocables with controllable Cu/In ratios have been synthesized by using ZnO nanorod arrays grown on FTO glass substrates as sacrificial templates. Chemical conversions from hexagonal ZnO to cubic ZnSe, hexagonal CuSe and tetragonal CuInSe2 are demonstrated as a novel means for synthesis of I-III-VI semiconductors. The array of CuInSe2 shells was shown to have an absorption coefficient of 10^4 cm−1 in the visible region which is much higher than that of CuSe shells. We applied these 1D nanocables as effective light-harvesting materials in low-cost solar cells with novel device configuration to pursue high performance. It was found that PCE of the ZnO/CuInSe2 cell was about two times higher than that based on ZnO/CuSe. Furthermore, this chemical conversion synthetic strategy was extended to fabricate other functional nanocable arrays on transparent conducting substrates. Arrays of ZnO/ZnxCd1-xSe, and ZnO/ZnSe/CdSe nanocables with tunable optical properties have been synthesized through the ion-exchange approach using ZnO nanorod arrays grown on FTO glass substrates as sacrificial templates. PCE of 4.74% and 4.54% have been achieved by using the ZnO/ZnxCd1-xSe and ZnO/ZnSe/CdSe nanocable arrays, respectively. Cu2ZnSnS4 (CZTS) has a direct band gap of 1.5 eV, a large absorption coefficient (>104 cm1), and earth abundant composition. Multinary Cu2SnS3 (CTS) and Cu2ZnSnS4 (CZTS) microspheres have also been synthesized by a solvothermal method and used as efficient counter electrode materials for high performance semiconductor-sensitized solar cells (SSCs) using the ZnO/ZnSe/CdSe nanocable arrays as photoanodes.

101910.label: Major findings and research outcome
101910.value: Some major outcomes of this project are summarized as follows: (1) Well-aligned arrays of Cu-rich and Cu-deficient CuInSe2 nanotubes as well as ZnO/CuInSe2 core/shell nanocables have been synthesized using ZnO nanorod arrays grown on FTO glass substrates as sacrificial templates. Chemical conversions and phase transformations from hexagonal ZnO to cubic ZnSe, hexagonal CuSe and tetragonal CuInSe2 are demonstrated. The absorption coefficient of the CuInSe2 nanotubes in visible region is on the order of 10^4 cm-1. Arrays of ZnO based nanocables can serve as promising photoelectrodes for solar cell applications. PCE of the ZnO/CuInSe2 cell is about 2 times higher than that based on ZnO/CuSe. (ACS Nano, 2010, 4, 6064–6070). (2) Arrays of ZnO/ZnxCd1xSe (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) core/shell nanocables with composition-tunable shells have been synthesized via a simple ion-exchange route using ZnO nanowires as sacrificial templates. The lattice parameter and the band gap of the ternary ZnxCd1xSe shells show respectively linear and quadratic relationships with the Zn content (x). The ZnO/ZnxCd1xSe nanocable arrays are demonstrated to be promising photoelectrodes for solar cells, giving a maximum PCE up to 4.74% and EQE as high as 82%. (Nano Letters 2011, 11, 4138–4143). (3) Low Voc is a main factor limiting the PCE of SSCs, even for the few recently reported high performance SSCs with efficiencies of 4–5%. We synthesized arrays of ZnO/ZnSe/CdSe tri-layer nanocables as efficient photoelectrodes for solar cell application, achieving a PCE of 4.54% and a Voc as high as 0.836 V. The high photovoltage is attributed to the ZnSe layer with a high conduction band edge, which reduces carrier recombination by surface passivation and upwardly shifts the conductor band of ZnO. (J. Mater. Chem. 2012, 22, 13374–13379). (4) Besides configuration of the ZnO/ZnSe/CdSe nanocable photoanode, electrocatalytic activity of the counter electrode to the electrolyte also govern the photovoltaic performance. To replace the traditional noble Pt counter electrode, we explore the application of multinary Cu2SnS3 and Cu2ZnSnS4 microspheres as effective counter electrode materials, resulting in significant enhancement in both FF and Jsc. These works were published in Nanoscale (2012, 4, 6537–6542) and J. Phys. Chem. C (2012, 116, 19718−19723).

101910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101910.value: There is a realization in the PV communities that increasing cell efficiency while decreasing cost will be critical if PV technology is to be widely utilized for primary energy needs. Therefore, one of the urgent tasks is to decrease PV cost by exploring low-cost and earth abundant photovoltaic materials, developing simple and low-cost material preparation and device fabrication technologies. In this project, simple chemical conversion approaches have been developed to fabricate a series of 1D ZnO/CuInSe2, ZnO/CuSe, ZnO/ZnSe/CdSe, and ZnO/ZnxCd1-xSe nanocable arrays for solar cell applications. The chemical conversion strategy developed in this project can be further extended to fabricate Cu2ZnSnS4 (CZTS) nanocable solar cell, as CZTS is one of the most promising candidates for low-cost photovoltaic materials, for the abundances of its constituting elements, low toxicity, a suitable energy band gap (~1.5 eV), and a high absorption coefficient (∼10^4 cm-1). Novel configuration of solar cells, such as tandem solar cells, can be designed by using these nanocable arrays to pursue high PCE. Solution-phase deposition processes typically yield lower efficiency solar cells. Much work remains to be carried out to increase the efficiency of such solution processed solar cells to the level of corresponding devices prepared by using high-cost and high vacuum involved vapour based technologies. Effective surface passivation for suppressing surface recombination is required to improve the device performance due to the large surface area of nanostructured solar cells.

101910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101910.value: Chalcopyrite CIGS and related materials (Cu2S, Cu2xSe, CuInS2, CuInSe2, CuIn(SxSe1x)2,) possess various attributes for effective solar energy applications. However, the wide commercial application of CIGS solar cells have not yet been realized, which is mainly due to the difficultly in achieving controllable and uniform composition over large area and the relatively high manufacturing cost involved in the vacuum co-evaporation/sputtering processes. In this project, we worked on fabrication of 1D CIGS/CdS/ZnO nanostructured arrays for solar cell applications. This project offer a low-cost solution processes for preparing high-quality CIGS based solar cell with controllable properties. Arrays of ZnO/CIGS nanocables grown on glass substrates were prepared by using solution based approaches which are typically of much lower cost. Using the 1D core/shell nanocables for making solar cells offered additional advantages of increasing the p-n junction area and improving the charge collection efficiency. Key parameters controlling the photovoltaic and charge conduction processes were investigated and correlated to the solar cell performance. Furthermore, this simple chemical conversion synthetic strategy was extended to fabricate a series of ZnO/ZnxCd1-xSe and ZnO/ZnSe/CdSe nanocables nanocable arrays on transparent conducting substrates with tunable optical properties for high performance solar cell applications. The knowledge we obtained from this project, e.g. solution approach and core/shell nanocable array, would definitely be useful for manipulating and processing other solar cells and optoelectronic devices.

102010.label: Project Objectives
102010.value: • To develop large-scale synthesis of high-efficiency up-converted CNPs via parameter optimization of the electro-chemical method, such as current density, electrolyte composition, and reaction temperature. • To characterize the morphology and structures of CNPs. We will study the morphology and structure of the obtained CNPs with transmission electron microscopy (TEM), high-resolution TEM (HRTEM), and Raman spectroscopy. We will characterize the functional groups on CNPs. • To characterize the optical and up-conversion properties of CNPs, such as photoluminescence (PL) and radiative recombination properties. We will study the relationship between the surface groups, morphology and structures, and the PL of the CNPs. We will optimize experimental parameters (e.g. current density, electrolyte composition, and solvent selection) to achieve CNPs with strong up-converted PL. • To establish the fabrication methodology of CNPs/SNPs composite systems. We will systematically study the experiment parameters (e.g. pH values, reaction time, reaction temperature, aging time) to achieve the optimum CNPs/SNPs composite catalyst. • To investigate the energy transfer mechanisms of CNPs component in CNPs/SNPs composite catalyst and optimize photocatalyst (CNPs/SNPs composite system) design. We will systematically study the interaction of CNPs and SNPs (TiO2, SiO2, ZnO etc) with different crystal phase, sizes, and morphologies. • To investigate the photo-response of composite photocatalyst. 102010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102010.value: High-efficiency photocatalysis systems, especially those operative in the visible region, may offer promising remedy to tackle today's environmental and energy problems.[1-3] Semiconductors are usually selected as photocatalysts because of their narrow gap and strong light absorption in the visible range. [1-5] To perform as photocatalysis, a semiconductor needs to absorb energy equal to or greater than its energy gap to generate exitons or electron-hole (e-/h+) pairs. TiO2 is the perhaps most studied semiconductor and potentially a facile and low-cost catalyst for removing environmental wastes and tainted water due to its physical and chemical stability, low cost, non-toxicity, and superior electronic and optical properties. However, one obstacle hindering its effective utilization lies in the fact that only less than 5% of the sunlight (in UV zone) is absorbed by the undoped TiO2 because of its wide band gap. While other semiconductors with a narrower band gap (such as TiS2, CdS, and ZnS etc.) can capture visible light but they always suffer from photocorrosion. Numerous promising visible-light-activated TiO2 nano-powders have been produced via doping and modification, howeever those photocatalysts ususlly suffer from instability problem, and their catalytic abilities are dependent on morphology, size, crystal phase, and/or doping concentration.[1-5] Consequently, design of catalysts with controlled properties, especially the energy gap, composition, and surface modification, remain the urgent and important challenges. To improve catalyst efficiency, an ideal photocatalyst sytem should be able to utilize the full spectrum of sunlight, photo-stable (i.e. not prone to photocorrosion), inexpensive, and non-toxic. We have recently produced carbon nanoparticles (CNPs) with excellent up-conversion luminescence properties. Significantly, our preliminary results have shown that the up-converted CNPs are potentially a powerful energy transfer component in photocatalyst design. Based on the up-conversion properties of CNPs, we have revealed that the photocatalyst TiO2/CNPs and SiO2/CNPs composite systems are capable of harnessing the use of the full spectrum of sun light. Consequently, we seek in this proposal to further develop the potential of the up-converted CNPs in the design of efficient photocatalysts. Towards this aim, we plan to control the synthetic route for CNPs, understand the mechanisms of the up-converted luminescence properties of CNPs, and exploit CNPs as an energy transfer component in the design of high-efficiency photocatalysts. Ultimately we plan to develop a new general approach to high-efficiency photocatalyst design based on the combination of the up-converted CNPs and semiconductors nanoparticles for environment and energy applications.

102010.label: Realisation of objectives
102010.value: The project objectives have been successfully accomplished in the following ways. We have utilized two approaches for the fabrications of carbon nanoparticles (CNPs). (i) We adopted electrochemical cutting of graphite sheets to fabricate carbon quantum dots (CQDs), using graphite rods as electrodes and NaOH/EtOH as electrolyte. (ii) We developed a one-step hydrothermal synthetic route (e.g., glucose/sucrose/starch as carbon sources) for the fabrication of fluorescent CNPs with diameters of 70–100 nm. We have applied comprehensive characterization techniques to analysis the chemical composition and microstructure of CQDs synthesized by different methods, and studied their correlation with the properties particularly optical and photocatalytic properties of CQDs. We have carried out detailed PL studies of CQDs prepared by electrochemical cutting method under different current densities. It is found that the current density affects the emission colors of CQDs predominantly, showing that lower current density leads to increasing amount of CQDs emitting at longer wavelengths. Our optical experiments also show that CQDs possess clear upconversion PL properties To establish the fabrication methodology of CNPs/SNPs composite systems, we have employed two approaches. To synthesize CQDs/Cu2O composites, we used one-step ultrasonic method. The CQDs/Cu2O composites are shown to be a highly crystallized nanomaterial with the CQDs on the surface of Cu2O. To synthesize CQDs/Fe2O3 composites, we adopted one-step hydrothermal process containing CQDs, FeCl3 and (NH)2CO solutions. For the energy transfer mechanisms of CNPs component in CNPs/SNPs composite, we have proposed a model similar to Forster energy transfer process (long-range effect). When a bunch of low-energy photons excite the CQDs, the electrons transit to a high-energy state (such as the LUMO). The excited electrons are favorable for transition back to a low-energy state, and the up-converted PL of CQDs can excite the SNPs. We have employed UV-vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy to characterize the optical properties of CQDs/Cu2O composite. The results demonstrate that CQDs/Cu2O composite can adsorb significantly more light in the 600-2500 nm regions as compared with pure commercial Cu2O, implying that the CQDs/Cu2O composite has an “infrared-sensitive” structure and is able to form an infrared photocatalytic activity system. We have carried out various experiments to test and verify the applications of CNPs/SNPs composites in photocatalysis. We have successfully demonstrated (i) the use of CQDs/Cu2O composite in the degradation of methyl blue (MB) under infrared light, and (ii) the use of CQDs/Fe2O3 in the degradation of toxic gas (gas-phase benzene and methanol) under visible light.

102010.label: Major findings and research outcome
102010.value: We utilized different approaches to fabricate CQDs. The as-synthesized CQPs have diverse diameters, we successfully purified and separated them into different sizes (1.2–3.8nm) by column chromatography (J. Mater. Chem. 2012, 22:24230). We found that the PL properties vary sharply with CQDs size, i.e., the small-sized CQDs (1.2nm) give UV emission (~350nm), medium-sized CQDs (1.5–3nm) give visible light emission (400–700nm), and large-sized CQDs (3.8nm) give near-infrared emission (about 800nm). These C-dots show photocatalytic activity. We also demonstrated the fabrication of TiO2/C-dots hybrid photocatalyst through a hydrothermal route, which showed enhanced photocatalytic activity under visible light (Dalton Trans. 2012, 41:9526). We synthesized CQDs/Cu2O composite by ultrasonic method. This composite has efficient (N)IR photocatalytic activity based on the combined effect of superior light reflecting ability of the Cu2O protruding nanostructures and the up-converted PL property of CQDs. (J. Mater. Chem. 2012, 22:17470). We demonstrated the use of CQDs/Cu2O composite in the degradation of methyl blue (MB) under infrared light. We also demonstrated that CQDs with diameter of 1–4 nm are effective NIR light driven photocatalysts for selective oxidation of benzyl alcohol into benzaldehyde with high selectivity and efficiency. We successfully synthesized CNP ionic liquid hybrid by microwave method. The hybrid is stable and has unique PL properties, which may offer new photocatalytic applications. (J. Colloid Interface Sci. 2011, 358:146). Besides CNPs, we have also explored functionalized Si NPs for nanocatalysis (Nanoscale 2011, 3:777). We prepared highly water-dispersible graphene quantum dots (GQDs) using hydrothermal method with polythiophene derivatives (PT2) as the carbon source. We demonstrate that the GQDs could be applied as a new photodynamic therapy (PDT) agent that can produce singlet oxygen via a multi-states sensitization process, resulting in a quantum yield over 1.3 (the highest ever reported in PDT agents). Significantly, through in vitro and in vivo studies, we illustrate that GQDs can simultaneously allow imaging and provide a highly efficient cancer therapy (Nature Comm. 2014, 5:4596). Apart from photocatalysis, we have extended the usage of different C nanostructures for lithium ion battery and solar cell applications, such as (i) Ge-3D graphene (Appl. Phys. Lett. 2013, 103:253903; J. Mater. Chem. A, 2013, 1:1821); (ii) Sn-3D graphene (Nanoscale 2013, 5:10599); (iii) Si-graphene composite (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2013, 1:6593; Energy Technol. 2013, 1:77); (iv) 3D graphene supported Si anode (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2013, 1:10092); and (v) N-doped graphene (Nanoscale, 2013, 5:600).

102010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102010.value: UV light only accounts for 4% of sunlight, so (N)IR-vis light sensitive photocatalysts will be a developing trend in photocatalysis. The output of this project shows that CQDs-based (N)IR-vis sensitive photocatalysts may have attractive practical applications. However, the properties of the GQDs depend sensitively on the synthesis method, carbon precursors, and surface modification/functionalization. More effort is therefore required to further understand the relationship of the structure and properties of CQDs with synthesis conditions. Upon that rational design and synthesis of GQDs with controlled properties may become possible. C-dots have also a great impact in biotechnological and environmental applications because of their potential as nontoxic alternatives to traditional heavy-metal-based QDs. The research in this project indicates that C-dots composites have the potential to expand the capabilities of next-generation energy-storage and photovoltaic devices, chemical and biological sensors, and biomedicine. Our work shows that GQDs have excellent singlet oxygen generation capability and could be applied as an efficient PDT agent for cancer therapy. The ultrahigh singlet oxygen generation efficiency may also enable the GQDs to be applied as efficient, environmentally friendly and visible-light-responsive photocatalysts for the degradation of persistent organic pollutants and microorganisms, and further studies on this topic will be interesting.

102010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102010.value: Among various carbon nanostructures, zero-dimensional carbon-dots are an important member due to their distinctive properties. The strong dependence of their properties in particular optical properties on their size, microstructure, surface, and chemical composition etc., and as well the environmental benignity and ease of fabrication, enable their attractive applications in diverse fields of environmental, energy, and bioscience. In this project, we synthesized size-controllable C-dots using different approaches, e.g., simple, low cost, and scalable alkali-assisted electrochemical method. Through comprehensive analysis we showed the properties of C-dots could be tuned by the carbon precursors and synthesis methods employed. Besides normal photoluminescence, C-dots could possess up-converted photoluminescence, which allows the design of high-performance, complex catalyst systems based on C-dots for efficient utilization of the full spectrum of sunlight. The photocatalytic degradation of toxic gases and chemicals by C-dots was illustrated, and compositing C-dots with other nanostructured semiconductors could further extent their applications. Significantly, we demonstrated that graphene dots had excellent singlet oxygen generation capability and could be applied as an efficient photodynamic therapy agent for cancer treatment. Moreover, this project also reveals other potential applications of carbon nanostructures in the devices such as lithium-ion battery and solar cell.

102410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102410.value: The aim of this project is to develop luminescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal complexes as a novel class of PEGylation reagents. PEGylation is the covalent modification of proteins, peptides, antibody fragments and drug molecules with poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG). This derivatization procedure favourably alters properties of the molecules without sacrificing their specific biological or therapeutic characteristics: most notably the toxicity of the molecules is significantly reduced. PEGylated molecules are less immunogenic, more biocompatible and soluble in aqueous solution, and display reduced nonspecific interactions with surfaces and other biological entities. For these reasons, a number of PEGylation reagents have been developed. Although fluorescent organic dyes are commonly used as probes for biological molecules and cellular components, luminescent transition metal complexes are considered to be excellent alternative choices because they offer such advantages as high photostability, large Stokes’ shifts, long emission lifetimes and high structural variation that leads to rich emission characteristics. These complexes also exhibit environment-sensitive emission, which reflects the local environments of the probes. Hence, there is an emerging interest in using these complexes as covalent biological labels. Whilst PEGylation reagents and transition metal PEG complexes have been well documented, there has been no report about the development of PEGylation reagents derived from luminescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal complexes. In this project, we will design novel PEGylation reagents using inorganic and organometallic transition metal complexes with interesting luminescence properties. These reagents will be used to PEGylate a wide range of targets including small model molecules, proteins and macromolecules. The photophysical behaviour and biological properties, including the cellular uptake efficiency and cytotoxicity, of the PEGylated conjugates will be investigated using various approaches. The favourable photophysical properties of luminescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal complexes, together with the non-cytotoxic and hydrophilic nature of PEG, will render the proposed luminescent PEGylation reagents a novel generation of biological tools with extremely high application potential. 這個項目的目的是開發發光性無機和有機金屬過渡金屬絡合物作為新一代聚乙二醇化試劑。聚乙二醇化是指將聚乙二醇通過共價鍵連接在蛋白質、多肽、抗體片斷和藥物分子上。這個衍生過程在不犧牲它們生物學和醫療學特性的同時適當地改變其分子性質：最明顯的是顯著降低了這些分子的毒性。分子在聚乙二醇化之後免疫性變低，生物相容性和水溶性更高，與表面和其他生物實體之間的非特異性相互作用變弱。基於這些原因，很多聚乙二醇化試劑已被開發。雖然有機熒光染料通常被用作生物分子和細胞成分的探針，但是發光性過渡金屬絡合物仍然被認為是有機熒光染料的優良替代選擇。它們的優勢包括高耐光性、大斯托克斯位移、長發光壽命和高結構變化性以至豐富的發光特性。這些絡合物還表現出對環境敏感的發光，這可以反映探針的局部環境。因此，現在使用這些絡合物作為共價生物標記引起了廣泛的興趣。雖然關於聚乙二醇化試劑和過度金屬聚乙二醇絡合物分別都有詳盡的記錄，但是並沒有關於開發發光性無機和有機金屬過渡金屬絡合物作為聚乙二醇化試劑的報告。在這個項目裡，我們將用具有趣發光屬性的無機和有機金屬過渡金屬絡合物設計新型聚乙二醇化試劑，並用這些試劑聚乙二醇化包括小模型分子、蛋白質和大分子在內的廣範圍目標。我們將通過多種方式研究聚乙二醇化的結合物的光物理性質和包括細胞吸收效率和細胞毒性的生物性質。發光性無機和有機金屬過渡金屬絡合物的有利的光物理性質以及聚乙二醇的無細胞毒性和親水性將會使提議的發光性聚乙二醇化試劑成為新一代具極高的應用潛力的生物工具。

102410.label: Realisation of objectives
102410.value: All the objectives of the project have been successfully achieved. In this project, a range of luminescent transition metal complexes functionalized with a PEG pendant were designed, synthesized, and characterized. The electronic absorption, photophysical, photochemical, and electrochemical properties of the complexes were also studied. Additionally, the water solubility, lipophilicity, cellular uptake, and cytotoxic activity of the complexes were evaluated. Our results show that the incorporation of the PEG unit into the complexes perturbs the photophysical and photochemical properties of the complexes. Also, due to the presence of a PEG unit, all the complexes reveal greatly enhanced solubility in aqueous solution and significantly reduced cytotoxicity, which render them to be attractive candidates as biological reagents. Some of the complexes were further modified with a reactive functional group, which can be used to label different biomolecules and interact with specifically designed surfaces. The bioconjugation properties of these complexes were investigated and the resulting conjugates were isolated and characterized. Their photophysical and cellular uptake properties were also studied. The major advantages of these luminescent transition metal PEG complexes include their rich photophysical properties, facile cellular uptake behavior, and more importantly, negligible cytotoxic activity. Also, using different molecular designs, we demonstrated specific localization of these complexes in organelles such as mitochondria and cell membrane. These characteristics, together with the advances of laser-scanning confocal microscopy techniques, render the complexes very useful bioimaging reagents for cells and tissues. The results will be of significant values in the future development of new biological probes and imaging reagents. In conclusion, all the objectives of the project were completed.

102410.label: Major findings and research outcome
102410.value: In this project, we have designed and synthesized many luminescent transition metal PEG complexes with rich photophysical properties, facile cellular internalization behavior, and negligible cytotoxicity: (1) Luminescent iridium(III) nondiscrete PEG complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-CONH-PEGn)](PF6), their discrete PEG counterparts [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-CONH-dPEG24)](PF6), and the PEG-free complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-CONH-Et)](PF6): the PEG complexes showed high water solubility and very low cytotoxicity, and were localized in the endosomes upon uptake by HeLa cells. The aldehyde-containing complexes were coupled to bovine serum albumin (BSA) to form strongly luminescent conjugates, indicating that they can function as luminescent PEGylation reagents. (2) Luminescent iridium(III) complexes [Ir(bsn)2(phen-R)](PF6) (R = NH2, NCS, TU): the phen-NCS complex was conjugated to various proteins and polymers including serum albumins, holo-transferrin, PEG-NH2, and poly(ethyleneimine) (PEI) to afford luminescent bioconjugates. The uptake of the complexes and the polymeric conjugates was studied. The cytotoxicity of the PEG conjugate was much lower than the complexes and the PEI conjugate. (3) Luminescent iridium(III) polyamine complexes [{Ir(N^C)2}n(PEI)](PF6)n and [Ir(N^C)2(en)](PF6): the PEI played a dominant role in the polar nature of the former complexes, rendering them very soluble in water. The cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, and DNA-binding properties of the PEI complexes were investigated. Furthermore, one of the PEI complexes was grafted with PEG to different extents, yielding luminescent copolymers that showed enhanced transfection activity but negligible cytotoxicity. (4) Luminescent rhenium(I) fluorous amine complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-Rf-NH2)](PF6), and the isothiocyanate and thiourea analogues: the lipophilicity, cellular uptake, and cytotoxicity of the complexes were studied. The isothiocyanate complexes were used to label GSH, BSA, PEI, and Poly-K to yield strongly emissive conjugates. The GSH conjugate can be readily purified with fluorous solid phase extraction. Also, the DNA-binding and polyplex-formation properties of the PEI and Poly-K conjugates were investigated. (5) Luminescent rhenium(I) PEG amine complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-PEG-NH2)](PF6) and [Re(bpy-PEG)(CO)3(py-NH2)](PF6): they can be activated with thiophosgene to yield isothiocyanate complexes, which were used to PEGylate BSA and PEI, giving luminescent conjugates. The DNA-binding and polyplex-formation behavior of the PEI conjugate was compared with that of unmodified PEI. Zebrafish embryos treated with one of the PEG complexes at high concentrations revealed delayed hatching as a result of hypoxia. (6) Luminescent iridium(III) DIBO complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-C6-DIBO)](PF6) and their TEG counterpart [Ir(ppy-COOH)2(bpy-TEG-DIBO)](PF6): they were used as the first phosphorescent bioorthogonal labeling reagents. Their reactions with benzyl azide and azide-modified proteins were studied. The membrane of Ac4ManNAz-treated cells exhibited intense emission after staining with the TEG complex, reflecting the bioorthogonal nature of the labeling.

102410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102410.value: In this project, we modified a number of luminescent transition metal complexes with a PEG pendant. Interestingly, the photophysical properties of the complexes were retained after the incorporation. Also, the complexes displayed greatly enhanced water solubility and significantly reduced cytotoxicity. The improved biocompatibility of the complexes allowed them to serve as useful biomolecular probes and bioimaging reagents. This project has established new research opportunities; for example, many metal complexes have been identified to be efficient singlet-oxygen sensitizers upon irradiation. Thus, luminescent transition metal PEG complexes, which have been demonstrated in this project to exhibit negligible cytotoxicity in the dark, are anticipated to display enhanced cytotoxic activity upon photoexcitation. It is likely that work along this line will lead to the production of new reagents for photodynamic therapy. It is noteworthy that the photophysical and photochemical properties of transition metal complexes can be readily tuned by the use of different metal centers, ligands, and substituents, which is obviously an advantage for the development of new reagents. In conclusion, we believe that this project has a strong potential to be further developed into a larger-scale project, which would ultimately lead to new biological and medical reagents for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes.

102410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102410.value: PEGylation is the covalent modification of biomolecules and drugs with poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG). It favorably alters properties of the molecules without sacrificing their specific biological or therapeutic characteristics. Importantly, PEGylated molecules are less immunogenic, more biocompatible and soluble in aqueous solution, and display reduced nonspecific interactions with surfaces and other biological entities. Although fluorescent organic dyes are commonly used as biological probes, luminescent transition metal complexes are considered to be excellent alternative choices because of their rich photophysical properties. However the development faces two major challenges: the low water solubility and high cytotoxicity of many metal complexes. In this project, we have designed and synthesized new luminescent transition metal PEG complexes that show greatly enhanced water solubility and significantly reduced cytotoxicity. Since the complexes exhibit interesting emission properties, they have been utilized as biological probes and imaging reagents. Some of these complexes also contain reactive functional groups for bioconjugation, rendering them new luminescent PEGylation reagents. In summary, the results generated from this project would form the basis of future design of luminescent transition metal complexes as biological probes and imaging reagents for both a range of in vitro and in vivo applications.

102610.label: Project Title(Chinese)
102610.value: 解Fredholm 积分方程的快速多尺度方法

102610.label: Project Objectives
102610.value: In our previous research, we have constructed piecewise polynomial multiscale bases and used them in the development of a general framework for fast multiscale collocation, Petrov-Galerkin and Galerkin methods for solving integral equations defined on an invariant set, such as simplices. We have also developed a general framework for multiscale augmentation methods for solving discrete linear systems resulting from discretization of operator equations. To extend the applicability of these methods, we need to construct special multiscale bases in special contexts that satisfy the requirements of the multiscale augmentation methods. We will give a systematic study on fast multiscale numerical algorithms for solving large scale discrete linear systems resulting from discretization of integral equations when a multiscale approximation is used. Our methodology is to employ the multiscale augmentation method in exploiting the multiscale structure of the coefficient matrix of the discrete linear system aiming at fast stable computational schemes. We will develop fast multiscale collocation/product-integration methods for integral equations of high dimensions. We will also study adaptive multiscale methods for solving integral equations when the solutions are not smooth, by using the multiscale augmentation methods. We will study Fredholm determinants for weakly singular kernels in the context of multiscale methods. We will complete a book on multiscale methods for Fredholm integral equations. Although there has been rapid progress in the multiscale treatment of Fredholm integral equations, there has yet to appear a suitable graduate text on this subject. One of the goals of this proposal is to provide such a text. This will provide interested scientists and engineers an opportunity to make use of this important advance in computational mathematics.

102710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102710.value: The study of blow-up and stability of nonlinear PDEs and reaction-diffusion equations has important practical applications, such as modeling the thermal evolution and stability of chemical components, or the concentration of species in population dynamics. The behavior of semilinear PDEs has been investigated by probabilistic methods using the Feynman-Kac representation formula, which has turned out to be a powerful tool for the treatment of time dependent and non-polynomial nonlinearities with potential terms. This project aims at the study of the blow-up and stability properties of quasilinear and fully non-linear PDEs. In this framework the probabilistic methods will play a major role and in particular we will use the probabilistic representation of solutions via backward stochastic differential equations, which extend the Feynman-Kac formula beyond the semilinear case. 102810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102810.value: Light harvesting, in terms of the efficient collection of sunlight, is a topic of global significance, especially due to the limited resources of fuels, air pollution and global warming. Nanoscience and nanotechnology can provide valuable solutions for an effective design of photovoltaic devices, reducing their cost and increasing efficiency. In this project, we suggest the use of semiconductor nanocrystals as components of efficient light-harvesting assemblies with a potential to be employed as components of third-generation photovoltaic devices. Semiconductor nanocrystals are very efficient absorbers of light, whose morphology, electronic structure and optical properties can be controlled with an exceptionally high degree at the synthetic stage. Based on our long-term experience in the chemical synthesis and optical spectroscopy of semiconductor nanocrystals and their assembly into functional structures, this project aims at fabrication and design of functional assemblies of semiconductor nanocrystals allowing for efficient light harvesting and charge separation, with a perspective of their integration into existing dye-sensitized solar cell technology. Starting from the synthesis, surface functionalisation and basic characterisation of nanocrystal building blocks with strong panchromatic and near-infrared absorption and variable surface chemistry, we will move on to fabrication of functional assemblies of semiconductor nanocrystals and/or organic dyes of desired morphology and tailored spectral characteristics. Advanced optical spectroscopy will be employed to study energy and charge transfer processes in these hybrid structures. The fundamental knowledge gained in this project in terms of materials requirements, chemical fabrication techniques and the underlying photophysical processes in complex NC-based structures offers ample perspectives for an improvement of the performance of dye-sensitized solar cells, making them competitive with conventional silicon-based technologies. 由於燃料資源有限，大氣污染和全球變暖的種種原因，人們對吸光材料，尤其是對太陽光能夠有效吸收的材料的研究是一個具有全球意義的研究領域。納米科學和納米技術可以為有效的設計光伏器件提供有價值的解決方案，從而降低光伏器件的成本和提高效率。本課題中，我們認為如果使用半導體納米晶作為吸光組件，它將有潛力成為第三代光伏器件。納米晶半導體是一種高效吸光體，在合成階段可以實現對其形貌，電子結構和光學性能的高度控制。基於我們在納米晶半導體的化學合成、光譜學研究以及組裝成功能結構等方面的研究經驗，本課題將致力於構造和設計具有高效吸光，分離電荷的半導體納米晶功能組件，並期望將其融合在現存的太陽能染料敏化電池中。我們首先合成納米晶基元，對其表面進行功能化，使納米晶組件可以吸收全色光和近紅外光，並且具有各種不同的表面化學特性。然後，把功能化的納米晶半導體和具有所需形貌和特有的光譜特性的有機燃料組建在一起。我們將採用先進的光譜來研究該複合結構中能量和電子的傳遞過程。通過對本課題的研究，可以獲取材料特性，化學製作技術和復合納米晶材料中的基礎光物理過程等方面的知識。我們從本課題中獲取的知識，為提高染料敏化電池的性能使之可以與傳統的矽技術相媲美提供了廣闊的前景。

102810.label: Realisation of objectives
102810.value: Objective 1. Synthetic protocols providing NCs with high extinction coefficients and absorption thresholds tuneable over the whole visible spectral range and extending in to the near infrared have been identified and optimised. NCs compatible either with hydrophilic (thiol-capped CdS, CdSe and CdTe NCs) and with hydrophobic solvents (mainly CdSe NCs) have been synthesised. Functionalised NCs with desirable surface properties have been prepared by employment of surface capping agents with different functional groups. Objective 2. Hybrid structures of colloidal quantum dots with Ru-dyes have been designed as panchromatic sensitizers for TiO2-based solar cells. A straightforward in situ deposition method has been developed to directly assemble aqueous thioglycolic acid capped CdSe NCs within mesoporous TiO2 thin films by a low-temperature hydrothermal route. This approach integrates linker assisted adsorption and NC synthesis in a single step, due to the use of thioglycolic acid as the capping agent for NCs and tethering agent for TiO2. Electrophoretic deposition of pre-synthesized thioacid-capped CdTe NCs on TiO2 nanotubes (TNT) results in poor charge transfer across the heterojunctions, due to the intermediate layer of bifunctional linkers. For CdTe NC-sensitized TNT prepared by in situ deposition provided direct QD-TNT contact, and hence favorable heterojunction for charge transfer. Objective 3. Steady-state and time resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy and photocurrent measurements have been employed to identify prevailing transfer mechanisms for photogenerated excitons between NCs and Ru dyes deposited on inert glass or mesoporous TiO2 substrates. For the Ir dye in combination with CdTe NCs we revealed the electron-transfer process on the few-ps timescale, which competes with non-radiative processes, such as Auger recombination, which would otherwise act as a relaxation channel for multiply excited NCs. Objective 4. Solar cells co-sensitized with both CdS and CdSe quantum dots demonstrate superior efficiency compared with the cells using only one type of quantum dots. Exploiting the inherent type II heterojunction between layered structures of CdSe and CdTe colloidal quantum dots, we systematically study diﬀerent ways of combining such nanocrystals of diﬀerent size and surface chemistry and with diﬀerent linking agents in a bilayer solar cell conﬁguration. We demonstrate the beneﬁcial use of two distinctly diﬀerent sizes of NCs not only to improve the solar spectrum matching but also to reduce exciton binding energy, allowing their eﬃcient dissociation at the interface. We further make use of the ligand-induced quantum-conﬁned Stark eﬀect in order to enhance charge generation and, hence, overall eﬃciency of nanocrystal-based solar cells.

102810.label: Major findings and research outcome
102810.value: This project focused on fabrication and design of functional assemblies of semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) allowing for efficient light harvesting and charge separation, with a perspective of their integration into photovoltaic devices. It combined chemical synthesis and functionalisation of NCs, assembly of NCs into functional nano-assemblies, advanced optical studies of created hybrid structures leading to a deep understanding of their light harvesting and energy/charge transfer properties on both the nanoscale and mesoscale levels, and finally the exploration of both promising structures in test solar cell platforms. The details are summarized in 7 published papers (2 review articles and 5 original publications). In details, we demonstrated a facile solution growth method of vertically aligned ZnO nanorods sensitized with aqueous CdS and CdSe quantum dots for photovoltaic solar cells; studied photophysical processes of energy transfer and charge separation in hybrid systems of semiconductor quantum dots and Ru-dyes as co-sensitizers of TiO2-based solar cells; compared in situ versus ex situ assembly approaches of aqueous-based thioacid capped CdSe nanocrystals within mesoporous TiO2 films for quantum dot sensitized solar cells; combined the ligand-induced quantum-confined Stark effect with Type II heterojunction bilayer structure in CdTe and CdSe nanocrystal-based solar cells; used CdTe and CdSe quantum dots as photosensitizers of TiO2 nanotube arrays to demonstrate intricate effects of their size-dependency and interfacial contact on photoconversion efficiencies; designed a water-soluble hybrid nanocomposite of CdTe quantum dots and an Iridium complex for photoinduced charge transfer.

Proposed course of action: focus on quantum dots providing the panchromatic absorption over the broad spectral range, and look into the emerging materials systems such as perovskites.

102810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102810.value: Light harvesting, in terms of the efficient collection of sunlight, is a topic of global significance. The nanoscience and nanotechnology can provide valuable solutions for an effective design of photovoltaic devices, reducing their cost and increasing efficiency. In this project, we used semiconductor nanocrystals as components of efficient light-harvesting assemblies with a potential to be employed as components of third-generation photovoltaic devices. Semiconductor nanocrystals are very efficient absorbers of light, whose morphology, electronic structure and optical properties can be controlled with an exceptionally high degree at the synthetic stage. In this project, we designed functional assemblies of semiconductor nanocrystals allowing for efficient light harvesting and charge separation. Starting from the synthesis, surface functionalisation and basic characterisation of nanocystals building blocks with strong panchromatic and near-infrared absorption and variable surface chemistry, we created functional assemblies of semiconductor nanocrystals and/or organic dyes of desired morphology and tailored spectral characteristics. Advanced optical spectroscopy has been employed to study energy and charge transfer processes in these hybrid structures. The fundamental knowledge gained in this project in terms of materials requirements, chemical fabrication techniques and the underlying photophysical processes in complex structures offers ample perspectives for an improvement of the performance of nanocrystal-sensitized solar cells.

103110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103110.value: Gas-phase dissociations of protonated peptides in mass spectrometers are being widely applied for microsequencing in proteomics for protein identification, for de novo sequencing, and for determination of posttranslational modification sites, which are of great importance for deciphering genetic codes in the nature. Large-scale analyzing the mass spectra of the protonated peptides are fully automated with bioinformatics searching algorithms by correlating the experimental spectra with the theoretical spectra of the peptides in standard protein databases. Generating the theoretical spectra relies on knowledge of the gas-phase ion chemistries. Therefore, better understanding of the underlying dissociation mechanisms, energetics, and kinetics are of fundamental importance for improving the efficiency and precision of the current database searching algorithms in order to reduce the rates of false-positive protein identifications. Our research program aims to develop a dynamics model to describe the chemistries of the peptide dissociations in the gas phase at finite temperatures. In this three-year funding cycle, the dynamics effects of the peptide chain lengths and the amino-acid side chains on the proton-transfer and cyclization reactions of the protonated peptides will be systematically examined by means of density functional theory based molecular dynamics simulations. These chemical processes play important roles in the formation of cyclic peptides, a structural rearrangement process that leads to the unpleasant loss of sequence information in the mass spectrometric data. 質譜中質子化多肽的氣相解離的研究對于破解基因密碼有著十分重要的意義，它已被廣泛應用于蛋白質的微量測序鑒定、從頭測序以及翻譯後修飾位點的確定中。基于生物信息學的搜索算法對標准蛋白質數據庫中實驗譜圖和理論預測譜圖的相互關聯，質子化多肽的質譜分析可以全自動的完成。而理論譜圖的獲得依賴于人們對氣相離子化學的理解。因此，更好的理解解離過程的內在機理以及熱力學、動力學過程對提高現有數據庫搜索算法的效率和精度，減少蛋白質的錯誤鑒定的起著十分重要的作用。我們的研究主要致力于發展一個能夠描述有限溫度下氣相中多肽的解離機理的動力學模型。在這三年的資助周期中，我們將基于密度泛函理論的分子動態模擬對肽鏈長度以及氨基酸側鏈質子遷移和環化反應對動力學影響進行系統的研究，以彌補質譜在這些過程中數據的不足。

103110.label: Realisation of objectives
103110.value: The structural dynamics of various peptide ions and their fragment ions at different temperatures have been theoretically simulated by means of density functional theory based molecular dynamics (DFT-MD) methods, performed on a home-built high-performance computing cluster (with a total of 2.3 TGLOPS computing power) managed by the PI's team members. The critical structures predicted from these trajectories and/or chemical intuition have been further optimized, also in the framework of DFT, based on the variational principle approach by minimizing the total internal energy of the molecular geometries. Thereby, potential energy surfaces (PESs) associated with the tautomerization, isomerization, and dissociation of the peptide ions have been constructed. The competitions among these reaction pathways on the theoretically predicted PESs have been modeled with the Rice-Ramsperger-Kassel-Marcus (RRKM) kinetic theory. The theoretical models established in this study have also been ratified by collision-induced dissociation (CID) experiments performed at the University of Hong Kong. The gas-phase structures of some peptide fragment ions have also been characterized by our DFT modeling in combination with the infrared multiple-photon dissociation (IRMPD) spectroscopy measured with the free-electron laser installed at the FOM Institute for Plasma Physics, The Netherlands. A wide variety of peptide models have been examined in this project. They include peptides with length from two up to seven amino-acid residues, which contain aliphatic, aromatic, acidic or basic, as well as phosphorylated side chain. These peptides are ionized either via protonation giving even-electron species or oxidative dissociation giving odd-electron radical cationic species. Both species exhibit mobile protons and undergo facile tautomerization and dissociation along the peptide backbone yielding a-/b- and y-type peptide fragment ions. The 5-memebered oxazolone structures of the b-type ions have always been observed for all models studied, while their 6-membered diketopiperazine structures were not commonly formed. The odd-electron species provide an additional reactive radical to induce peptide dissociations, yielding c-/z-type and a-/x-type ions in parallel with the charge-induced formation of b-/y-type ions. Many of these dissociations involve the amino-acid side chain preformed as a proton/hydrogen atom/electron donor/acceptor.

103110.label: Major findings and research outcome
103110.value: Formation of all b-type ions observed in this project has been suggested to follow the 5-membered oxazolone-ring mechanism [1-6]. Interestingly, the subsequent formed the a-type ions can undergo tautomerization and cyclization [1]. For the conventional linear structure of a2 ions, facile proton transfers between the N-terminal amino nitrogen and the C-terminal iminium nitrogen have been observed within pico-second time scale in our DFT-MD simulations at a temperature of 300 K. Alternatively, the 5-membered imidazolidinone cyclic structure can be formed by a nucleophilic attack of the amino group on the iminium carbon. Its free-energy surface is not affected significantly by temperature ranging from 200 K to 500 K and a particular diastereomer of the cyclic structure is dominant, as supported by DFT and IRMPD spectroscopy [1]. The cyclic a2 ions can undergo ring-reopening to form a non-conventional linear structure containing a C-terminal amide group identified by its characteristic C=O stretching frequency [1]. The critical step for this reopening reaction involves a proton transfer that can be catalyzed by residue solvent molecules [1] or presumably by other polar amino-acid side chains, which also play important roles on isomerizations and dissociations of peptide ions [2-5]. Radical cationic peptide ions contain not only charge (free proton) but also a radical. Comparing with the mobility of protons, radical is less mobile along the peptide backbone [2]. However, in the presence of a very basic residue, such as arginine, the free proton is sequestered tightly by its basic side chain and consequently the energy barriers to the charge-induced pathways are largely increased [2]. With the removal of the free proton by the basic residue, the peptide backbone becomes more flexible that kinetically facilitates the radical migration which involves a cyclic transition structure [2]. A common radical cationic isomer contains an alpha-radical and a mobile proton that can induce the formation of the b-type ions via the 5-membered oxazolone-ring mechanism [2] and the unprecedented cleavages of the Cbetal-Cgamma bond of the side chains [2-4]. Similar mechanism has been suggested for the dissociation of phosphoserine- and phosphothreoine-containing peptide radical cations [5]. Another common isomer contains beta-radical that can induce backbone cleavage via beta-scission mechanism yielding the c-/z-type ions or the a-type ion [2-5]. Selective formation of the a1 ion has been observed via a direct N-terminal Calpha-C bond cleavage induced by a tyrosine radical suggested by DFT and RRKM kinetic models [6].

103110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
103110.value: It has been proposed that the amino-acid side chain may play important roles on the intramolecular proton transfers which are the critical steps involved in the cyclization and re-opening reactions of peptide fragment ions. Thus, it is interesting to examine similar effects for amino acids that contain different polar groups. It has also been suggested that presence of the basic arginine residue can mobilize the radical along the backbone of the peptide radical cations. The mobility of both proton and radical along the peptide backbone is crucial for their dissociations, which have been applied for peptide sequencing, differentiation of isobaric amino acids, and identification of the post-translational sites using mass-spectrometric techniques. Therefore, it is important to further understand the correlation between the location of charge and radical on the thermodynamics, kinetics, and dynamics of these dissociation pathways. Last but not least, we have demonstrated that the dissociation patterns can be qualitatively modeled in combination of DFT and RRKM modeling with energy-resolved CID experiments [6]. It is of fundamental interest to refine the theoretical model and give a better quantitatively comparison with the experimental observations, which will enhance the reliability of mass spectrometry-based protein identification.

103110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103110.value: Dissociations of peptide ions in mass spectrometers have being widely applied for microsequencing for protein identification, which is of great importance for deciphering genetic codes in the nature. Large-scale analyzing the mass spectra of the peptide ions can be fully automated with bioinformatics searching algorithms by correlating the experimental spectra with the theoretical spectra of the peptides in standard protein databases. Generating the theoretical spectra relies on the knowledge of the gas-phase chemistry of peptide ions. In this project, we employed theoretical calculations in combination with mass spectrometric experiments to examine the dissociation mechanisms of some peptide models. It has been demonstrated that some peptide fragment ions can not only undergo facile proton transfer reactions but also undergo ring-closure and ring-reopening reactions. For radical cationic peptide ions with the presence of basic amino-acid residue, the radical migration can be facilitated causing rich dissociation reactions induced both by the charge and the unpaired electron. Better understanding of the underlying mechanism of these peptide dissociations is of fundamental importance for improving the efficiency and precision of the current database searching algorithms for protein identification.

103210.label: Project Objectives
103210.value: To study the closed image hypothesis. With a fixed scale, we shall find general conditions for the image of the co-boundary operator to be closed in the L^2 space. To conduct the related Hodge decomposition. We shall derive some conditions for the co-homology group, the quotient of the kernel of the higher order co-boundary operator by the image of the co-boundary operator, to be finite dimensional. Then we shall study the Hodge decomposition and apply the results to data analysis and learning algorithms.

103210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103210.value: Hodge studied fundamental relationships between geometry, topology, and partial differential equations by extending the harmonic analysis of Fourier to higher order linear differential operators on manifolds. For many new applications of mathematics, as in statistics, data analysis, intelligence and learning, broader setting for a new Hodge theory is needed. The purpose of this project is to extend the classical Hodge theory to the quite general and abstract setting of metric spaces with a probability measure. Compared with some previous advances such as combinatorial Hodge theory, our framework and results are new, relying on integral equations to replace the differential equations and moreover apply at each finite fixed scale. We shall establish conditions for the co-boundary operator to have closed image, and study the related full Hodge decompositions. 通过把Fourier的调和分析推广到流形上的高阶线性微分算子，Hodge研究了几何，拓扑和偏微分方程之间的本质关系。很多诸如统计，数据分析，智能学习等数学的新应用需要更广框架下的新的Hodge理论。本项目旨在推广经典的Hodge理论到一个带有概率测度度量空间的一般抽象框架。与之前诸如组合Hodge理论等进展相比，通过用积分方程代替微分方程应用到每个有限刻度上，我们的框架和结果是全新的。我们将建立协边界算子有闭图像的条件，从而研究相关的Hodge全分解。

103210.label: Major findings and research outcome
103210.value: In a joint paper [1] with Nat Smale, we present the relation of the new data-based Hodge theory and the classical theory. In the case of Riemannian manifolds at a small scale, we construct explicit chain maps between the de Rham complex of differential forms and the L2 complex at scale α, which induce isomorphisms on cohomology. We also give estimates that show that on smooth functions, the Laplacian given in our earlier work, when appropriately scaled, is a good approximation of the classical Laplacian. Much of this support was devoted to establishing a group of young scientists with focus on the mathematical (and topological) foundations of immunology. After 3 years of development, three scientific papers have been produced [2, 3, 4]. In [2] we have accomplished the state of the art predictions for the peptide binding problem. The work and the methodologies involved have potential for aiding selection of vaccines for viral and bacterial diseases. Already we have initiated studies into the H5N1 virus strains. This part of Asia has especially drawn attention to the need for such studies. The science behind the geometry used in this research is a great emphasis on amino acid chains. This geometry comes into play in the vaccines (peptides), the human alleles, and the viruses as well. In [3] we modify the algorithm in [2] and apply to MHC I binding prediction, which we refer to as KernelRLSpanI. We develop a novel consensus method to predict naturally processed peptides through integrating KernelRLSpanI with two state-of-the-art predictors NetMHCpan and NetMHC. The consensus method achieved top performance in the Machine Learning in Immunology (MLI) 2012 Competition, group 2. We also introduce our progress of improving our MHC II binding prediction method KernelRLSpan by diffusion maps. In [4], we present a simple, fast and accurate algorithm for the prediction of residue-residue contacts based on regularized least squares. The basic assumption is that spatially proximal residues in a protein coevolve to maintain the physicochemical complementarity of the amino acids involved in the contact. Our regularized inversion of the sample covariance matrix allows the computation of partial correlations between pairs of residues, thereby removing the effect of spurious transitive correlations. The method also accounts for low number of observations by means of a regularization parameter that depends on the effective number of sequences in the alignment. When tested on a set of protein families from Pfam, we found the regularized least squares algorithm to have performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods for contact prediction, while at the same time being faster and conceptually simpler. All the results obtained in [2, 3, 4] lead to interesting questions for high-dimensional data and hence their geometry including new directions of Hodge theory.

103210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103210.value: This project aims at developing Hodge theory and its applications in data analysis. We have presented some relations of the new data-based Hodge theory and the classical theory and studied properties of boundary and co-boundary operators. We have also applied ideas and methods from Hodge decomposition and learning theory to data analysis, with focus on the mathematical and topological foundations of immunology and bioinformatics.

103310.label: Project Title(Chinese)
103310.value: Hybrid脉冲控制问题及相关的一组Quasi-variational不等式

103310.label: Project Objectives
103310.value: In this project, we will characterize the value function of the optimal control problem as the unique viscosity solution of a system of several Quasi-variational inequalities (QVIs) on general subadditive intervention cost. Based on the characterization of the value function, we can further study the regularity, stability, the existence of the optimal strategy. We will develop a two-component Markov chain approximation method to seek for a feasible computational method for approximating the value function. One of the major concern is that, although the convergence of the value function can be established from the theoretical point of view, the computation cost grows exponentially fast with respect to the the number of discrete events. To reduce the computational complexity in a huge hybrid system, a two-time-scale method will be developed based on a singular perturbation approach. Such a development shall lead to near-optimal strategies by using optimal controls of significantly reduced limit problems. To further demonstrate, we turn our attention to the study of the financial markets with frictions, due to either transaction costs or illiquidity costs. Such a problem has received great deal of attentions from researchers on impulse control theory as well as practitioners in financial industry. We shall study the relation between the path regularity of the optimal trading strategy and the growth of the cost functionals. One particular interesting problem among the analysis is that, the value function of the underlying model fails to be characterized in the usual sense under weaker condition on intervention cost $c(\xi) = O(\xi^\gamma)$ for some $\gamma$ between 0 and 1. The possibility of an alternative characterization will be also studied.

103310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103310.value: Optimal impulse control problems naturally arise in various applications, when a non-zero intervention cost is incorporated into the objective function. The study of such systems has been regarded as one of the important topics in stochastic control theory. Along another line, in many complex systems, in which continuous dynamics and discrete events coexist, the need of successful controls of such systems in practice leads to an optimization on hybrid models, which has become an emerging new area of the study in stochastic control. In this proposal, we consider the impulse control problems on the hybrid diffusion systems. One of the distinctive features of the underlying system is that the corresponding dynamic programming principle leads to a system of Quasi-Variational-Inequalities (QVIs) of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) type. The objective of this project is to exploit the properties of the optimal strategy and the value functions in a fairly large class of intervention cost functionals, and to develop a class of efficient numerical algorithms of the control and optimization problems. It is expected that we can characterize the value function of the underlying optimal control problems as the certain unique viscosity solutions of Quasi-variational inequalities. The expected results reveal the connection between underlying stochastic optimization and related PDE formulations. Due to the nonlinearity and switching mechanism, closed-form solutions are virtually impossible. Continuing on our quest, we plan to furtherdevelop eective computational methods to solve the optimal control problems. Because of the complexity of the hybrid system, the computation cost has in general exponential growth in size of the space of the discrete events. To circumvent the difficulty in dealing with real systems with a huge complexity, we propose to use a two-time-scale approach on hybrid impulse control system to reduce the high dimensionality. In such a way, the limit system of Quasi-variational inequalities with reduced number of discrete event shall preserve the main features of the original control problem asymptotically. For the demonstration purpose, we are planning to implement the numerical scheme with dimensional reduction on various benchmark problems. Furthermore, we consider an applications in the nance market on general transaction costs and liquidity costs, and through the impulse/singular control formulation. We study the relation between the path regularity of the optimal trading strategy and the growth of the cost functionals. 如果非零交易成本计算在目标函数里，即会出现最优脉冲控制问题。这种问题的研究一直被认为是重要的随机控制分支。另外，在连续动态系统和离散系统并存的复杂系统中，控制问题演变成hybrid最优控制模型。这种问题逐渐变成一个新的研究领域。 在此课题中，我们将要研究在复杂hybrid随机系统的最优脉冲控制(optimal impulse control)问题。这个问题的一个很重要的特点是：动态程序原理(Dynamic programming principle)引出的等价形式是一组Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB)类的Quasi-variational-inequality (QVIs)。此课题的研究方向是找出相对广泛的成本函数所相关的最优控制和目标函数的性质，然后更进一步提出有效的数值计算方法。 我们期望用一组QVI的粘性解(viscosity solution)来刻划最优控制的目标函数。这种结论可以用来解释所研究的随机控制问题及偏微分方程的联系。一般情况下，因为问题本身的非线性和hybrid特性，显性解是很难得到的。与之相对应的，我们将要提出有效及可行的数值方法去解决目标函数和对应的最优控制。我们注意到hybrid系统中离散状态的数目直接导致计算成本的指数增长。为了克服在实际系统中存在的这种巨大计算成本，我们将利用two-time-scale的方法来简化问题的维数。这种方法的特性是，简化的系统与原来的系统是渐进相似。最后，我们将通过计算若干例题，分析所提出的方法的可行性和有效性。更进一步，我们会研究此方法在金融领域中的应用，比如最优策略的路径规律特性和目标函数的增长特性。

103310.label: Realisation of objectives
103310.value: With respect to the characterization of the value function related to objective #1, the PI and co-authors have better understandings in different frameworks through the several sequential works. We mainly use a probabilistic approach. We note that the main effort is to find a sequence of continuous functions uniformly converging to the desired value function, utilizing the sample path properties of the diffusion processes. In this procedure, to obtain uniform convergence, Dini’s theorem plays an essential role. However, such an approach is not directly applicable to general settings. The boundary of the domain may be unbounded so Dini’s theorem is not applicable directly. Therefore, one needs asymptotic properties of the approximating functions. We devise an approximation sequence and obtain the continuity of value function by local uniform estimate. Regarding two-time scale computational aspect of hybrid setting related to objective #2, the PI and collaborators focused on devising an efficient algorithm with mean exit time, which is considered to be the essential difficulty arisen from complex problems. In this work, we show that the multilevel approach can be adapted to the mean exit time context. In order to justify the algorithm, we analyze the strong error of the discretization method in terms of its ability to approximate the exit time. We then show that the resulting multilevel algorithm improves the expected computational complexity by an order of magnitude, in terms of the required accuracy. On the application in the financial market regarding the objective #3, we study an optimal portfolio selection problem under instantaneous price impact. Based on some empirical analysis in the literature, we model such impact as a concave function of the trading size when the trading size is small. The price impact can be thought of as either a liquidity cost or a transaction cost, but the concavity nature of the cost leads to some fundamental difference from those in the existing literature. We show that the problem can be reduced to an impulse control problem, but without fixed cost, and that the value function is a viscosity solution to a special type of Quasi-Variational Inequality (QVI). We also prove directly (without using the solution to the QVI) that the optimal strategy exists and more importantly, despite the absence of a fixed cost, it is still in a “piecewise constant” form, reflecting a more practical perspective.

103310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
103310.value: The random noise of the control problem in the current setting is restricted to standard multi-dimensional Brownian motions. In fact, there is a wide open area if the random noise being given by space-time Gaussian noise, which can be deemed as infinite dimensional Brownian motion. However, some of the existing techniques and estimates would be somehow extendable.

103310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103310.value: This project studies the impulse control theory under the hybrid diffusion setting, which is a new model and it extends the stochastic control theory applicable to more realistic problems. Note that, such models widely used in financial engineering management sciences, and other areas, it lacks with solid theoretical foundation. Our result provides a rigorous theoretical justifications through mathematical theory and try to close the gap between theory and practice, although there is no uniform theory applies to this complex system.

103410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
103410.value: Galerkin/collocation型譜方法及Helmholtz方程的數值解

103410.label: Project Objectives
103410.value: The stability analysis with explicit wave numbers for the Helmholtz type boundary value problems with large wave numbers plays a key role in error estimates of numerical methods. However, no stability analysis for large cavity problems has been done although some efforts have been made for interior and exterior Helmholtz problems with certain boundary conditions and geometries. We shall study the stability bound for large open cavity problems with an explicit form of the arbitrary distributed source f, "incident" source g and more importantly, the wave number k. The stability analysis on physical type perturbation, such as plane wave type source $g$, will be also investigated. Based on the stability analysis, we shall develop some efficient spectral Galerkin/collocation methods and provide the corresponding error estimates. Approximations in Besov space and recently developed triangular spectral element methods will be studied for problems with geometric singularities. Implementation and computation for some practical cases will also be conducted. Numerical approximations to cavity models consist of two parts: the approximation to the Helmholtz equation (or Maxwell's equations) and the approximation to the transparent boundary conditions on the aperture. From primary analysis for some simple models, the incident source $g$ plays a more important role in the stability bound. This implies that a more efficient approximation to the nonlocal operator may lead to significant improvement of accuracy. More attention will be paid to the approximation to the hypersingular nonlocal operator. Extend the analysis and methods to three-dimensional models (Maxwell's equations or vector wave equations), in which the stability bound with explicit wave numbers is an essential issue.
