111710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
111710.value: This proposal aims to carry out efficient algorithms design for Binary Neural Networks (BNN) and Cellular Nonlinear Networks (CNN), with basic mathematical analysis on Cellular Automata in general, from the dynamical systems theory approach, targeting potential real-world applications in brain-like computing and new information processing technologies. First, the classical extended one-dimensional Cellular Automata (CA) will be combined with bi-infinite symbolic sequences to perform rigorous mathematical analysis, and the rich and complex dynamics of a class of Elementary Cellular Automata (ECA) rules will be analyzed from the symbolic dynamical systems viewpoint. Then, the behaviors of the perceptron of BNN will be characterized. Moreover, based on biological concepts and methods, several new algorithms will be designed for efficiently performing a huge number of Boolean functions. 111810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
111810.value: This project launches a comprehensive investigation into networked control systems, with a particular focus on the constraints (capacity constraint, quantization error, etc) of communication channels on feedback control performance. Our principal objectives are (1) To obtain analytical solutions and bounds for optimal tracking and regulation performance of multivariable, multi-channel networked systems under information-limited feedback; (2) To develop Bode and Poisson type integral relations for multivariable, multi-channel networked feedback systems; (3) To develop insights and understanding into resource (capacity, power) allocation problems of multi-channel systems; (4) To investigate problems of joint design of controller and communication channel for optimal performance; (5) To develop benchmarks, guidelines, and rules of thumb for the design of multivariable, multi-channel networked control systems. Underlying these objectives is the goal to discover, understand, and quantify the intrinsic constraints, fundamental performance limits, and inherent design limitations and tradeoffs for multivariable, multi-channel networked feedback systems. Built on the PI's expertise and prior success, the project employs a variety of techniques that seek to fuse control theory and information theory. Networked control systems, a setting in which control tasks are executed by exchanging information over wired or wireless communication networks, differ fundamentally from the conventional control systems and present new challenges unexplored in the past. This project tackles one of the most compelling issues facing networked control: the information constraint on control. The proposal outlines a number of key problems, where we believe significant challenges exist and advances can be made. A focused research plan has been delineated, which is supported by concrete, realistic problem formulations and technical approaches. The project will provide benchmarks and guidelines, and will lead to new and better understanding of networked control systems, and potentially to improved design methods and techniques, thus contributing to the advance and application of networked control theories and more generally, to control problems subject to information constraints. The research will also lend insights and thrust to information theoretic problems. 本项目拟对网络控制系统作广泛研究，尤其着重于通讯信道之约束（如容量约束、量化误差等）对反馈控制性能的影响。其主要目标在于（1）对于多变量、多通道网络系统，获得最优跟踪与最优调节性能的分析表达式或下界；（2）发展多变量、多通道网络反馈系统的波得与波松积分关系公式；（3）深刻理解多通道系统的资源（如容量、功率）分配问题；（4）研究控制器和通讯信道的统一设计问题；（5）由此发展多变量、多通道网络控制系统设计的规则、指南等等。 通过以上目标，本项目旨在发现、理解并确定多变量、多通道网络反馈系统的本质性约束，终极性能极限、以及系统内在的设计局限。基于本研究者的专长和前期研究的成功，该项目将采取一系列办法，求得控制论与信息论之融合。 所谓网络控制系统，专指通过有线或无线网络交换信息并执行控制任务的系统。网络控制系统与通常遇到的控制系统有根本的不同，也带来前所未遇的挑战。本项目旨在对网络控制中最重要的问题发起挑战，也即控制系统中的信息约束问题。本报告书列举出数个关键性的问题。我们相信，这些问题既构成严肃的挑战，亦可取得巨大进展。我们在此提出的工作计划，包括问题的提出与技术路线，具体而可行。本课题将给网络控制系统设计工作提供参考性和指导性的成果，引领对网络控制系统新的、进一步的理解以及导致更完善的设计方法，由此推动网络控制及更广泛的信息受限条件下的控制之研究，同时，也对信息论研究工作提供借鉴和参考。

111810.label: Realisation of objectives
111810.value: This project, along with CityU 111511, has provided the essential support to the PI's research into networked control systems, which has resulted in a total of 11 journal papers (published/submitted), 1 book chapter, 1 editted volume, and 20 conference publications. The objectives as proposed have been achieved satisfactorily, with major results and findings summarized in Section 6.1-Major Findings and Outcomes. The project has not only led to the resolution of certain fundamental problems in the networked control research, but also to the developments of new problem areas and solution techniques. In particular, Objectiveds 1, 3, 4, 5 are nearly completely achieved. Objective 2, while partially attained by a large margin, can be further explored to a greater depth, with the promise to lead to a major breakthrough. Section 6.2 outlines a particular attempt in the future research to address this issue. Two Ph.D. students have been trained and partially supported by the project, who are expected to graduate in the Academic Year 2014-2015.

111810.label: Major findings and research outcome
111810.value: • We studied in Outputs [9, 13] (and conference papers [6, 7], [10], [12]) the stabilization and optimal tracking problem over noisy additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels. With respect to this popular channel model, we derived necessary and sufficient conditions for stabilization and explicit relations between a feedback system’s tracking performance and such channel characteristics as channel SNR (signal-to-noise ratio) and channel capacity. For multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems with multiple parallel AWGN channels, for which a fundamental issue is how the channel’s total input power should be allocated to individual channels to optimize the performance, our investigation reveals that the optimal power allocation policy for tracking is no longer the same as Shannon’s renowned “water filling” strategy. This is believed to be among the first available results on optimal performance of networked control systems, which provides fundamental insights that will aid the design of multiple AWGN channels for control performance improvement. Joint channel and controller designs are explored which shows that the stabilizability requirement can be lessened and the tracking performance can be considerably improved. Bode-type integral relations are derived incorporating such new notions as Channel Blurredness and Negentropy Rate. • We studied in Outputs [7, 8] (together with conference papers [1-5]) the stabilization and a number of canonical optimal control problems with quantized control signals. In this formulation, we considered erasure channels subject to random multiplicative noises, which are known to be capable of capturing the essential features of channel fading, random delays, and data dropout. We obtained necessary and sufficient conditions for a feedback controller to stabilize an unstable plant over such channels. These conditions furnish fundamental bounds on the channel noise variances in terms of the plant unstable poles. The cases of state feedback and output feedback with minimum phase plants are completely resolved in this work, resulting in explicit a priori bounds for stabilizability. We also solved the optimal regulation, optimal disturbance attenuation, optimal tracking problems under a mean-square criterion. The solutions to these problems are cast into forms of linear matrix inequalities which can be readily computed using standard softwares. The results constitute a major advance in the study of networked control problems, which have been considered intractable for some time. • While achieving major successes in the core area of networked control as set out in the project objectives, this project has outgrown to related research areas of time-delay systems and multi-agent systems. Small gain stability conditions are developed in Outputs [10, 11], and fundamental bounds on the important notion of delay margin are developed in [19]. Consensus algorithms are developed in [3, 6, 12] (and in the conference papers [8, 11], [13]-[15], [17], [20]) for multi-agent systems with second-order agents and general linear time-invariant agents.

111810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
111810.value: Nearly all objectives are accomplished to satisfaction as envisioned. The development of Bode type integral relations, however, appears to be a truly challenging task. This objective (Objective 2) will be futher explored in the future work. A particular goal will be to develop an MIMO entropy rate relationship which will construe as the cornerstone in our development of MIMO Bode integrals.

111810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
111810.value: This project sets out to investigate fundamental problems concerning networked feedback systems, which seek to integrate communication channels and feedback controllers. This is an area of research that has not been addressed until very recently and one that poses a daunting challenge to both theoreticians and practitioners alike. The project addressed the most common communication channels adopted for feedback control, and led to fundamental findings for stabilizability and performance of such systems in the forms of analytical or readily computable conditions and expressions.

112510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
112510.value: Plasma immersion ion implantation and deposition (PIII&D), a proven surface modification technique encompassing the merits of plasma surface treatment and energetic ion bombardment, has widespread applications in microelectronics, metallurgy, nanotechnology, and biomedical engineering. In spite of technological advances heretofore, conventional PIII&D still suffers from a few intrinsic limitations such as ion fluence non-uniformity when dealing with components with a complex geometry and excessive surface damage in materials sensitive to plasma / ion interactions such as polymers. In this project, we aim at developing advanced plasma immersion technologies and new applications that would be difficult or even impossible with the current technology. One method is quasi-DC (direct current) PIII&D in which a continuous low pressure discharge is maintained in the vacuum chamber above a grid and there is no direct contact between the plasma and sample surface thereby reducing overheating and damage to the materials. In addition, the grid can be made with predesigned patterns to perform direct in situ surface patterning in concert with surface modification. The technique can thus be utilized to produce surface patterns and nanostructures in selected areas to tailor local surface properties and achieve desirable and long-term antibiotics and drug delivery effects. The concept can be extended to three-dimensional (3D) PIII by replacing the planar grids with cylindrical, spherical, or other types of 3D screens when processing components with a complex geometry like spinal medical implants and hip joints. Another novel idea is enhanced glow discharge PIII (EGD-PIII) in which external plasma sources are not required and the plasma with a density reaching 1E9 to 1E10 cm-3 is produced by self glow discharge. An electron-focusing electric field is formed between the small pointed hollow anode and large tabular cathode inside a dielectric cage when a negative voltage pulse is applied to the sample platen. Consequently, electrons including secondary electrons are all focused to the region near the hollow anode and a higher ionization rate of the species through the hollow anode can be achieved. In addition to better process efficacy, ionization of some solid materials with poor electrical conductivity and some semi-conducting materials that are difficult to ionize in traditional plasma sources can be enhanced. The overall objective of this proposal is to develop new plasma immersion techniques that will propel the technology in the coming decades and to cater to the more stringent requirements demanded by modern and upcoming applications. 等離子體浸沒式離子注入與沉積技術（PIII&D），是一項被證實了的集等離子體表面處理和高能離子轟擊多重優點的表面改性技術。已經被廣泛的應用於微電子、冶金、納米技術和生物醫學工程等行業領域。這項技術發展到如今，常規的等離子體浸沒式離子注入與沉積技術仍然由於自身的某些特性而被掣肘。比如在處理具有複雜的幾何外形的樣品時，離子流量均勻性不好；以及在處理諸如聚合物等對等離子體和離子比較敏感的材料時，會對樣品表面形成過度損傷。在本項目中，我們將致力於開發先進的等離子體浸沒技術並探索其新的應用領域，解決使用目前已有的技術很難克服甚至不可能解決的應用技術難題。其中一種是准直流等離子體浸沒式離子注入與沉積技術（quasi-DC PIII&D）。在置於真空室的網柵上維持連續的低壓放電，產生的等離子體不與樣品表面直接接觸，因而減少了過熱現象以及對樣品材料的破壞。除此之外，還可以在網柵上預先設計好圖案，可用於在做表面改性的同時直接實現原位的材料表面圖案化。這種技術能夠運用於在選定的區域進行圖案化處理以及生成納米結構，從而改變材料表面的性質達到所需要的長效抗菌和藥物緩釋效應。如果使用圓柱狀、球狀或者其他三維結構的網柵取代先前平面的網柵，由次可以衍生出三維等離子體浸沒式離子注入技術，用於處理醫用脊椎和髖關節植入體等具有複雜幾何外形的樣品。另外一種新技術就是增強輝光放電等離子體浸沒式離子注入技術（EDG-PIII）。該項技術能夠在不需要外部等離子體源的情況下，依靠自身的輝光放電獲得109至1010每立方釐米的等離子體密度。在絕緣箱中，當一個負壓脈衝作用到樣品盤時，小又尖的中空陽極和大而平的陰極之間會形成一個電子聚焦電場。這樣，包括產生的二次電子在內的所有電子就會集中在靠近中空陽極的區域，通過中空陽極就可以獲得很高的離化率。這種技術除了能夠提高工藝效益外，對於那些很難使用傳統的等離子體源離化的導電性很差的和一些半導體材料，可以增加離化效率。總而言之，本項目的目標就是開發多種新型的等離子體浸沒技術，希望會在未來的數十年推動等離子體技術的發展，並能夠滿足不斷湧現的越來越急迫的應用需求。

112510.label: Realisation of objectives
112510.value: The first three objectives have been fulfilled. (i) A new technique utilizing a moving auxiliary electrode inside the tube to improve the dose uniformity and plasma ion implantation efficiency has been developed. The effects of the moving auxiliary electrode are investigated by 2-D particle-in-cell simulation and uniform ion implantation into a cylindrical bore can be accomplished by physical translation of the electrode, and this technique is suitable for implantation of long tubes without an internal plasma source. (ii) PIII employing hybrid radio-frequency (RF) and high-voltage (HV) pulses via a single feed-through has been demonstrated to be an effective surface modification method. (iii) An advanced plasma treatment process based on quasi-PIII in the presence of a mask has been demonstrated to produce different surface morphology and chemistry on PTFE to direct the adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells. The new technologies developed in this project have been applied to different types of materials, mainly biomaterials such as magnesium, titanium alloys, and polymers and more details can be found in the published papers attached. Concerning the fourth objective, our experimental and theoretical studies have revealed the basic phenomenon and important factors affecting the process. For instance, in nitrogen EGD-PIII, the implantation current increases sharply with the gas pressure when a threshold pressure is exceeded, indicating that the glow discharge dynamics changes with increasing diatomic gas flow rate. The voltage drop rendered by the anode glow produces noticeable N2+ dissociation and electron-atom ionization in the positive column which expands to the cathode. As a result, charged particles reach the cathode more easily, and the larger plasma density and N+/N2+ ratio in the positive column lead to the higher current. Our results clarify the implantation current characteristics. However, although EGD-PIII does not require an external plasma source, ion focusing affects the lateral ion fluence uniformity, thereby hampering its use in high-fluence hydrogen ion implantation for thin film transfer and fabrication of silicon-on-insulator (SOI). Insertion of a metal ring between the sample stage and glass chamber improves the ion uniformity and reduces the ion fluence non-uniformity as the cathode voltage is raised. Two-dimensional multiple-grid particle-in-cell simulation confirms that the variation of electric field inside the chamber leads to mitigation of the ion focusing phenomenon and the results are corroborated experimentally by hydrogen forward scattering.

112510.label: Major findings and research outcome
112510.value: The use of a grounded grid to conduct direct-current plasma immersion ion implantation (DC PIII) evolves from the conventional broad beam line technique but with the target located immediately in front of the extractor. In this project, the underlying principle, factors affecting the process, process improvements, and various applications are studied. A new method utilizing a moving auxiliary electrode inside the tube to improve the dose uniformity and plasma ion implantation efficiency has been developed. We have also extended this technique to perform one-step, non-contact pattern transfer. Complex patterns with micrometer line-widths can be transferred onto a planar sample such as a silicon wafer by placing the metal masks a few mm away from the wafer. Long-pulse, high-frequency quasi direct-current (DC) oxygen plasma immersion ion implantation (PIII) has been used to produce a super-hydrophobic polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) surface in our laboratory. This technique allows the use of a high duty cycle without adversary effects arising from excessive sample heating that frequently plagues conventional PIII. A theoretical model incorporating particle-in-cell (PIC) ions and Boltzmann electron distribution has been adopted to simulate quasi-DC PIII into the S-shape bar inside a grounded cylindrical cage containing a mesh. According to the simulated potential and ion density contour lines as well as retained dose, more uniform ion implant fluence distributions can be attained by using quasi-DC PIII. The simulation results corroborate the experimental data and provide the numerical evidence for further development of 3-D DC-PIII. Concerning enhanced glow discharge plasma immersion ion implantation (EGD-PIII), our experimental and theoretical studies have revealed the basic phenomenon and important factors affecting the process. For instance, in nitrogen EGD-PIII, the implantation current increases sharply with the gas pressure when a threshold pressure is exceeded, indicating that the glow discharge dynamics changes with increasing diatomic gas flow rate. The voltage drop produces noticeable N2+ dissociation and electron-atom ionization in the positive column which expands to the cathode. Charged particles reach the cathode more easily, and the larger plasma density and N+/N2+ ratio in the positive column lead to the higher current. In the application of EGD-PIII to hydrogen ion implantation for the fabrication of silicon-on-insulator (SOI), insertion of a metal ring between the sample stage and glass chamber has been shown to improve the ion uniformity and reduces the ion fluence non-uniformity as the cathode voltage is raised and the results are corroborated by two-dimensional multiple-grid particle-in-cell simulation.

112510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112510.value: The quasi direct current and enhanced glow discharge plasma immersion ion implantation techniques have been investigated systematically both experimentally and theoretically. Our results provide a better understanding of these two processes and open up new applications, particularly pertaining to surface treatment of biomaterials and functional materials. Future developments are expected to be applications oriented because the techniques are suitable for different types of materials ranging from metals, semiconductors, to polymers which are being used in many fields. Our laboratory will continue to find new applications and collaborate with the industry to investigate the commercial potential of the technology. Future GRF and ITF proposals are being planned for the next step.

112510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112510.value: The quasi direct current and enhanced glow discharge plasma immersion ion implantation techniques have been investigated systematically both experimentally and theoretically. For example, a new technique utilizing a moving auxiliary electrode inside the tube to improve the dose uniformity and plasma ion implantation efficiency has been developed. An advanced plasma treatment process based on quasi-PIII in the presence of a mask has been demonstrated to produce different surface morphology and chemistry on PTFE to direct the adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells. Our experimental and theoretical studies have revealed the basic phenomenon and important factors affecting the EGD-PIII process. In the application of EGD-PIII to hydrogen ion implantation for the fabrication of silicon-on-insulator (SOI), insertion of a metal ring between the sample stage and glass chamber has been shown to improve the ion uniformity and reduces the ion fluence non-uniformity as the cathode voltage is raised. The research output has hitherto produced 31 journal papers and 50 conference presentations. In addition, one US patent and one Chinese patent have been issued.

112710.label: Project Title(Chinese)
112710.value: 用圆达曼光栅进行非接触、多功能测量的系统

112710.label: Project Objectives
112710.value: To follow-up the development of the previously supported project on the design and fabrication of n-order circular Dammann grating and to design an optimal CDG so that the integrated optical system would be able to measure multi-functional parameters including distance, angle and area. High-resolution spatial-light modulators (SLM) will be used to model the CDG before it is fabricated. To utilize the fractional Fourier transform in the design of the measurement system so that the set-up can be more compact, without sacrificing the measurement accuracy. To do simulation on the design of the optical system initially using the FRESNEL simulation software and later the more sophisticated ZEMAX optical system design software. The many design features and ray-tracing capabilities of ZEMAX will help to model the system and to optimize the measurement system and to enhance the measurement accuracy.

112710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
112710.value: This proposal will extend the very encouraging research results obtained on the novel applications of a new type of diffractive optical elements (DOE) in our on-going GRF No. 112507 “Potential Applications of Circular Dammann Gratings” which will be completed shortly by the end of June 2010. We have investigated various types of design and fabrication of this novel DOE for optical communications and non-contact optical measurement techniques for various parameters, including focal length of lenses, wavefront collimation, angle, distance and area of distant objects. We called this DOE circular Dammann grating (CDG) as a circular pattern of equal intensities can be produced at different diffraction orders with high efficiency similar to a linear Dammann grating producing a rectangular pattern. We propose to extend this research work to design an integrated non-contact multi-functional measurement system using the CDG's design and fabrication experiences obtained in the GRF No. 112507 project, which provides not only simple, low-cost and compact configuration, but also comparable high-precision measurement capability. In this project, we will focus our research and design effort on the integrated in-situ non-contact measurement of distance, angle, area of distant objects and other appropriate parameters. In addition we plan to utilize the 3 major equipment items only recently installed in our clean room, viz. the Crestec CABL-9510C Electron beam lithography system, the Oxford ICP65 Inductively coupled plasma etching system and the Microtech LW405 Laser direct write system, to design and fabricate the CDGs. We shall therefore be able to effectively make the masks in-house, instead of outsourcing them to an outside company as the previous practice. The new ICP etching machine will hopefully produce better gratings so that the measurement system performance and accuracy can be significantly improved.

112710.label: Realisation of objectives
112710.value: Objective 1 We have succeeded in increasing the diffraction efficiency greatly to over 85% with a uniformity of less than 2% for all seven ports in a 7x high-density grating beam splitter as reported in Appl. Opt. in Part C. Objective 2 We have designed an optical diffractive element which is composed of circular and cylindrical phase gratings, producing a mixed spectrum in a fractional Fourier transform system so that the set-up can be more compact, without sacrificing the measurement accuracy. The result of this compact measurement system was reported in an international conference in part C. Objective 3 The Fresnel simulation software has been very well used in achieving the above design and experimental set-up. In summary A lot has been achieved in improving the diffraction efficiency and uniformity of the grating and the fractional Fourier Transform technique has been used to design a more compact and accurate measurement system.

112710.label: Major findings and research outcome
112710.value: We have designed and also successfully fabricated high-density gratings in the form of three-, five- and seven-port beam splitters. Our experimental result shows all beam splitters has overall efficiency between 85% to 90% with uniformity of less than 2%. The Fresnel simulation software has been very well used in achieving the above design and experimental set-up. This project has been progressing well, resulting in 1 paper published in a top optical journal - Applied Optics, one book chapter and 2 papers presented in international conferences.

112710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112710.value: There is an exciting area on the application side that can be further explored, viz. the design and packaging of a portable distance measurement meters using the circular Dammann Gratings pioneered by our group. Further development- (1) design a more compact and hand-held portable distance meter. (2) improve on the accuracy of the measurements leading to an enhancement of the overall system.

112710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112710.value: We have designed an integrated non-contact multi-functional measurement system using the circular Dammann gratings. This system is composed of a mixture of circular and cylindrical phase gratings to measure the tilt degree, the vertical and horizontal degrees and other parameters simultaneously. We have successfully fabricated high–density Dammann gratings in the form of there-, five- and seven-port beam splitters. Our experimental result shows all beam splitters has overall efficiency between 85% to 90% with uniformity of less than 2%. Fresnel simulation software has been very well used in achieving the above design and experimental set-up. The overall system provides not only simple, low-cost and compact, but also comparable high-precision measurement capability. Distance, angle and area of distant objects can be measured simultaneously. Result of this project: two conferences papers, one journal paper and one book chapter have been published.

112810.label: Project Objectives
112810.value: Analyze the network throughput and multi-hop delay performance based on the statistical network model. The effect of key factors, such as traffic pattern, node distribution, channel statistics and transmission power, on the network performance will be investigated; Examine the traffic scaling laws of wireless ad hoc networks and formulate the optimal rate allocation problem with the constraints of network requirements such as QoS and fairness performance; Develop distributed MAC and routing algorithms based on the above theoretical analysis and evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithms in practical environments. Extensive performance comparisons with the protocols applied in current wireless ad hoc networks will be conducted to illustrate the performance gains.

For Objective 1, a statistical node-centric modeling approach is proposed in [1] based on which the network throughput, delay, and stability analysis of two most representative random access schemes, Aloha [13] and Carrier Sense Multiple Access (CSMA), are unified into a coherent theoretical framework. Effects of key factors on the network performance are analyzed in a series of follow-up papers, including: 1) backoff [2], 2) receiver model [3], 3) power control [3], and 4) availability of channel state information at the transmitter side (CSIT) [4]. 2. For Objective 2, the proposed theoretical framework is applied to practical wireless networks including 1) IEEE 802.11 networks and 2) distributed antenna systems (DASs). It is shown in [5] that the MAC design of IEEE 802.11 networks can be optimized by adjusting the initial backoff window size of each node according to the network size. The optimal network performance, including the maximum network throughput and the minimum mean access delay, as well as the corresponding optimal values of the initial backoff window size, are all derived as explicit functions of system parameters, and extensive performance comparisons to the current standard demonstrate that significant gains can be achieved by the optimal design. The analysis is further extended to study the optimal downlink/uplink throughput allocation [6]; 2) the maximum network throughput in the heterogeneous scenario where different traffic statistics of nodes are further taken into consideration [7]; and 3) the optimal service differentiation of IEEE 802.11e networks [8]. For DASs, by assuming a uniform distribution of both mobile stations and access points, the uplink sum capacity is analyzed in [9] and the downlink sum rate performance with various linear precoding schemes is characterized in [10-12].

112810.label: Major findings and research outcome
112810.value: 1. Unified theoretical framework of random access: A unified theoretical framework is proposed in [1] under which the throughput, delay and stability performance of two most representative random access schemes, Aloha [13] and CSMA, can be analyzed. The network steady-state points are derived as explicit functions of key system parameters including the aggregate input rate and the number of nodes, which enable the characterization of stable regions and performance optimization. The proposed analytical framework of [1] is further extended in a series of follow-up papers [2]-[4] where effects of key factors on the network performance are studied. Specifically, a comprehensive study of the effect of backoff schemes on the network throughput and delay performance of CSMA networks is presented in [2]. In [3], the analytical framework is extended to characterize the maximum sum rate of Aloha with the capture model over fading channels. The comparison to the classical collision model further reveals that despite an overly pessimistic estimation on the network throughput, the collision model could serve as a good approximation for the capture model when analyzing the sum rate performance of Aloha networks. Moreover, the effect of power control is studied, and a uniform mean received SNR is shown to be crucial for achieving a good balance between fairness and sum rate when the network operates at the low SNR region. The analysis is further extended to the ad hoc mode where nodes can transmit to each other, and the effect of CSIT on the network throughput and mean queueing delay is analyzed in [4]. 2. Application to practical wireless networks: The medium access control (MAC) layer protocol of IEEE 802.11 networks, Distributed Coordination Function (DCF), is a variant of CSMA. In [5], the proposed analytical model of [1] is applied to IEEE 802.11 DCF networks, where the stability, throughput and access delay performance with two access mechanisms, i.e., the basic access mechanism and the request-to-send/clear-to-send (RTS/CTS) mechanism, in both unsaturated and saturated conditions are all analyzed within a unified framework. Explicit expressions of the optimal network performance, including the maximum network throughput and the minimum mean access delay, and the corresponding optimal values of initial backoff window size are derived, and important insights are offered for the optimal design of IEEE 802.11 DCF networks. The proposed analytical framework of [5] is further refined to tackle a series of practical issues in [6]-[8]. Specifically, in [6], both the uplink and downlink transmissions are included into the network model, and the optimal initial backoff window sizes of the access point and mobile stations to maximize the network throughput while maintaining the downlink/uplink throughput ratio at a target level are derived as explicit functions of key system parameters. In [7], by taking distinct traffic statistics of nodes into consideration, the analysis shows that to optimize the network throughput performance, the input rates of unsaturated nodes and the initial backoff window sizes of saturated nodes should satisfy a constraint that is determined by the number of saturated nodes. [8] further demonstrates how to maximize the network throughput under a certain differentiation requirement by optimally choosing the backoff parameters of each access category (AC) including the initial backoff window size and the arbitration inter-frame space (AIFS) number.

112810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112810.value: The findings of this project have stimulated a number of interesting topics for future research. From the theoretical perspective, the proposed analytical model assumes perfect sensing for CSMA, that is, all the nodes can perfectly sense the concurrent transmissions, which may not hold true when nodes experience fading channels. How to model the sensing error and analyze its effect on the optimal network performance is a challenging issue, which deserves much attention in the future study. Moreover, the analysis shows that for random-access based networks, throughput maximization and delay minimization normally cannot be realized simultaneously. In many cases, there exists a fundamental tradeoff between throughput and delay (for instance, with BEB the maximum network throughput is achieved when the mean queueing delay is infinite). It is therefore important to further characterize the optimal throughput/rate performance under certain delay constraints. From the application perspective, the proposed theoretical framework can be further applied to various wireless networks such as sensor networks and device-to-device (D2D) networks, where the MAC protocols are usually variants of Aloha and CSMA, but with different system requirements. The modeling and optimization approaches developed in this project may find wide applications in practical random-access based networks.

112810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112810.value: Despite the encouraging success in practical systems, there is a huge gap between theory and practice in wireless ad hoc networking. Most studies have focused on network capacity and traffic scaling laws, yet delay analysis, which is a fundamental issue in data networking, is largely overlooked. Moreover, a central controller is usually required to perform perfect scheduling to approach the proposed scaling laws. Few insights can be shed to the practical protocol design, as all the network protocols must operate in a distributed manner. In this project, random access is assumed to incorporate the distributed nature of wireless ad hoc networks, and a statistical node-centric modeling approach was proposed, based on which the network throughput, delay, and stability analysis of two most representative random access schemes, Aloha and CSMA, are all unified into a coherent theoretical framework. Effects of key factors, including backoff, receiver model, power control and the channel statistics, were analyzed, and the proposed theoretical framework was successfully applied to practical networks such as IEEE 802.11 networks and DASs. The results provide important insights to the practical protocol design. For instance, it is shown that the MAC design of IEEE 802.11 networks can be optimized by adjusting the initial backoff window size of each node, and explicit expressions of the optimal initial backoff window size are derived in various scenarios. Extensive performance comparisons to the current standard demonstrate that significant gains can be achieved by the optimal design.

112910.label: Project Title(Chinese)
112910.value: 离散单调增映射不动点的计算及在超模博弈中的应用

112910.label: Project Objectives
112910.value: Complexity of Determining Whether a Discrete Increasing Mapping Has a Fixed Point: Let f be a discrete increasing mapping. To determine whether f has a fixed point, it is important to study its complexity. To address this issue, we will convert an NP-complete problem into an equivalent problem of determining whether a particular discrete increasing mapping has a fixed point. Let P be a polytope with rational input data satisfying that each row of the defining matrix has at most one positive entry and one negative entry. Determining whether P has an integer point is an NP-complete problem. We will fully exploit the special property of P and apply it to construct a discrete increasing mapping p satisfying that p has a fixed point if and only if P has an integer point. The key technical issue to be tackled is how to construct such a mapping p. (Phase 1) An Integer Labeling Rule and Its Properties: One of the objectives of the project is to determine whether f has a fixed point. To accomplish this objective, we need an applicable integer labeling rule that assigns an integer label between 0 and n+1 to each integer point of the space and yields a 0-complete n-dimensional simplex carrying all integer labels from 0 to n. To address this issue, we will fully exploit the order-preserving property. For any given nonnegative integer vector u, we will use u to partition the space into two parts. To determine whether f has a fixed point satisfying 0 ≤ x ≤ u, we will define an integer labeling rule to assign an integer label based on f to each integer point satisfying 0 ≤ x ≤ u and an integer label based on 0 and u to each integer point violating 0 ≤ x ≤ u, respectively. The key technical issue to be tackled is how to find such an applicable integer labeling rule. (Phase 2) Construction of a Finite Simplicial Path and Development of a Path-Following Method: One of the main issues to be addressed in this phase is how to construct a finite simplicial path that either leads to a fixed point of a discrete increasing mapping or proves no such point exists. Given any starting point, we will use it to partition the space into n+1 cones and introduce a cone-like set with an extra dimension. A triangulation will be adapted for subdividing the n+1 cones and the cone-like set into simplices. Given this triangulation, we will first use the labeling rule in Phase 2 to define almost complete, complete, or 0-complete simplices, respectively, and then apply all these simplices to define an undirected graph with a path that either leads to a fixed point of f or proves no such point exists. A path-following method will be developed to move along the path from one simplex to another. The key technical issue to be tackled is how to continue the path when a complete n-dimensional simplex is met. (Phase 3) An Extension of the Path-Following Method to Approximating Fixed Points of a Discontinuous Increasing Mapping and Implementations: By introducing a discrete increasing mapping, we will extend the path-following method in Phase 3 to approximating fixed points of a discontinuous increasing mapping. The key technical issue to be tackled is how to construct the discrete increasing mapping such that its fixed points yield approximate fixed points of the mapping with a known error bound. The path-following method and its extension will be coded in MATLAB. Numerical comparisons with the iterative procedure will be carried out. Window-based software packages will be made available for applications. (Phase 4) Applications to Supermodular Games: The computation of Nash equilibria plays an important role in the applications of Supermodular games. We will formulate increasing mappings for various supermodular games from applications and apply the path-following method and its extension to compute equilibria of these supermodular games. (Phase 5)

112910.label: Realisation of objectives
112910.value: To show that it is NP-hard to determine whether a discrete increasing mapping has a unique fixed point, we have reduced a well-known NP-complete integer programming problem to a fixed point problem of an increasing mapping on a semicomplete lattice by an application of linear programming. If the integer programming problem has an integer point, then the fixed point problem has at least two fixed points. This leads to the NP-hardness on the uniqueness of Tarski’s fixed point. To compute a fixed point, we have introduced an augmented set. This augmented set plays an essential role in the development of a finite simplicial path-following method. It facilitates the method to continue the search when it meets a complete full-dimensional simplex before a fixed point is generated. By assigning integer labels to integer points in the interested space according to the mapping and artificial integer labels to integer points outside the interested region, a finite simplicial path has been formulated, which starts from an arbitrary integer point and leads to a fixed point of an increasing mapping if such a point exists or proves that there is no integer point in the set. To compute all pure strategy Nash equilibria, we have reformulated the problem as a mixed-integer programming problem and exploited a fixed-point iterative method to compute all the pure strategy Nash equilibria. To approximate a discontinuous increasing mapping, we have introduced a discrete increasing mapping, which is able to approximate the discontinuous mapping to any precision provided that the grid size of the underlying triangulation is sufficiently small. One can apply this approximation to compute an approximate fixed point of a discontinuous increasing mapping with the proposed method. To show the efficiency of the methods, extensive numerical tests have been carried out in the project.

112910.label: Major findings and research outcome
112910.value: Let P be a polytope with rational input data such that each row of its defining matrix has at most one positive entry. It is well known that determining whether P has an integer point or not is an NP-complete problem. As an application of this polytope, we have successfully constructed a discrete increasing mapping f such that f has a unique fixed point if and only if P has no integer point. Finding a Nash equilibrium of a supermodular game is equivalent to finding a mixed integer point in a polytope. To assign an integer label to each point in the space, an applicable integer labeling rule has been formulated. As a result of these theoretical developments, a mixed zero-one integer programming methods has been proposed in [1] to compute all pure-strategy Nash equilibria and a finite simplicial path-following method has been developed in [7] to find a fixed point of an increasing mapping. Numerical experiments have been carried out to show that the approaches are effective and efficient. When the dimension is fixed, it has shown in the literature that Brower’s fixed point theorem is equivalent to Tarski’s fixed point theorem of an increasing mapping on a complete lattice. Online auctions can be formulated as a noncooperative game and consequently a fixed point problem. Online auctions with some special characteristics have been investigated in [2]. This investigation leads to an interesting application of the proposed method in this project. Constrained optimization can be reduced to a fixed point problem and many engineering problems can be formulated as constrained optimization or fixed point problems. The research efforts on communication networks, decision-making evaluation, and constrained optimization have been made in [3], [6], [8], [9], [10], [11], [12]. The research results in this project will provide an alternative solution to these problems. Piecewise-linear systems have been extensively formulated in control design and analysis. As an effective paradigm for modeling piecewise linear functions, linear matrix inequalities have been substantially applied to deal with these piecewise-linear systems. Studies on these systems have been carried out in [4] and [5]. Constrained optimization has been exploited in the analysis. These studies will yield important applications of the methods proposed in this project.

112910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112910.value: The ideas developed in this project can be extended to the computation of an economic equilibrium for an exchange economy with indivisibilities. One can first formulate the equilibrium problem as a fixed point problem of an increasing mapping on a complete or semicomplete lattice. Then a finite simplicial path-following method can be applied for finding an economic equilibrium for the economy.

112910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112910.value: As an effective paradigm for studying strategic complementarities, supermodular games have been extensively applied in supply chain management, wireless communications and economic analysis. In these applications, the computation of Nash equilibria plays an important role. This project establishes an equivalence relationship between the uniqueness of fixed point and integer programming and develops efficient methods for computing Nash equilibrium. The research of the project will further promote applications of Tarski's fixed point theorem and supermodular games in management and economic analysis.

113610.label: Project Title(Chinese)
113610.value: 基於運動感知的視頻縮放

113610.label: Project Objectives
113610.value: To identify the main factors that influence temporal coherence and introduce the concept of motion-aware constraints for achieving spatiotemporally coherent resizing of videos. We will illustrate how existing video resizing methods often fail to retain temporal coherence due to their motion-oblivious constraints, easily causing undesirable flickering or waving artifacts. We will show that temporal coherence can be effectively achieved by preserving the motion information of the input video. To this end, we will study what type of motion is vital to temporal coherence and how to extract the related motion and integrate into a content-aware resizing process. Various related issues and concerns will be discussed and addressed. To develop a more practical content-aware video resizing system. Our idea of motion-aware constraints is largely orthogonal to the building blocks of the existing video resizing methods and thus can be used to improve the existing methods. However, in this project we will integrate our motion-aware constraints with the state-of-the-art image resizing work proposed by Wang and colleagues [Wang et al. 2008], towards a new and more powerful video resizing system. We will show how to strike a balance between spatial content preservation and temporal coherence using a technique of importance map blending. To improve performance and scalability, we will break long video sequences into short overlapping clips and resize the individual clips sequentially while constraining their in-between temporal coherence over the overlapping frames. To evaluate the effectiveness of our method, we will apply our method to a variety of videos that contain large object motion and/or camera motion, which are challenging to handle with previous methods.

113610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
113610.value: Appropriate resizing of images or videos is of high demand nowadays due to the ubiquitous display devices with significantly different aspect ratios and resolutions, e.g., wide-screen TVs and smartphones. Content-aware image resizing, which adapts images to target display devices while preserving important content, has enjoyed a certain degree of success and some techniques have even been incorporated into professional image editing packages like Photoshop. Following the popularity of image resizing, content-aware video resizing has gained significant attention in both research and industry. However, the existing video resizing systems have been demonstrated only on a small set of video examples and are still far from mature. This project aims for a practical content-aware video resizing system. We identify the main problem with the existing systems as the lack of appropriate ways to preserve temporal coherence during resizing. To date, the problem of temporal incoherence has been addressed by constraining temporally adjacent pixels to be transformed coherently. However, due to the motion-oblivious nature of this simple constraint, the resized videos often exhibit flickering and waving artifacts, especially when significant camera or object motions are involved. Since the feature correspondence across frames changes spatially with both camera and object motion, motion-aware treatment of features is required for video resizing. This motivates us to design a motion-aware video resizing framework. To design effective motion-aware constraints for temporal coherence, which have not been studied before, we need to address several challenges such as what type of motion content is needed, how to extract the related motion information robustly, how to effectively integrate the extracted motion content into the resizing process, and how to address the scalability problem for long videos. This project plans to study various issues related to the idea of motion-aware constraints and to build a complete deformation-based video resizing system which will handle challenging inputs that are difficult to handle with previous methods. We are confident that we can complete the project and deliver the expected outcomes. We have had extensive research experiences in the field of interactive shape deformation, which we believe have paved the way for the proposed ideas. We expect that the new project will follow the success of our completed projects and make continuous contributions to both research and industry.

113610.label: Realisation of objectives
113610.value: We have successfully identified the main factors that cause temporal incoherence during video resizing (objective 1) and developed a practical content-aware video resizing system (objective 2), which is based on the concept of motion-aware constraints (objective 1). The preliminary video resizing system, initially supported by the start-up grant from the university, led to a journal publication at ACM Transactions on Graphics. The proposed ideas have been successfully extended and applied to various applications such as content-aware reshaping of human bodies in images and video-based stop motion production.

113610.label: Major findings and research outcome
113610.value: There are in total nine peer-reviewed journal publications arising directly from this project. Among them, 5 papers (No. 3, 4, 6, 7, and 9) have been published in ACM Transactions on Graphics (the most prestigious journal for the publication of computer graphics research) and also been presented at ACM SIGGRAPH or SIGGRAPH Asia (the best conferences in the field of computer graphics). Publication No. 1 and 5 were published in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics, which is the second best graphics journal according to Google Scholar Metrics. These publications contributed solutions to two major problems: content/structure analysis (No. 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9), and content/structure-aware resizing or editing (No. 2, 4, 5, 8). The idea of content-aware resizing has been extended from video retargeting to new applications like structure-preservation of 3D shapes (No. 2) and urban facades (No. 4). The proposed concept of motion-aware constraints has been applied to new applications such as cartoon layer extraction (No. 5) and video-based stop motion production (No. 8).

113610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
113610.value: Our current implementation of the video resizing system used a 2D camera model to model camera motion, which ignored the parallax effect and might cause misalignment for scene points of varying-depth backgrounds. In the future, it would be interesting to see if a more sophisticated camera or object motion detection technique could improve the resizing results further.

113610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
113610.value: The main goal of this project is to design a content-aware video resizing system which is able to change the aspect ratio and the resolution of video data to fit target display devices with different display sizes and aspect ratios. This is able to bring enhanced video-view experience. We have introduced the concept of motion-aware constraints to solve the problem of temporal incoherence, the core problem in the previous video resizing systems, and successfully implemented a practical video resizing system. We have also extended the proposed ideas to new applications such as content-aware reshaping of human bodies in images and video-based stop motion production. Our invented techniques have been published in the best journals and presented in the best conferences in the field of computer graphics.

114010.label: Project Objectives
114010.value: An efficient algorithm will be developed for processing the non-positive definite stiffness matrix in the nonlinear iteration calculation for the simulation of super CNTs. An atomistic-based CA model will be developed to simulate the bending, tension, and fracture behaviors of super CNTs in terms of the interatomic potential. The developed model will be suitable for the simulation of super CNTs, especially defective ones. An effective parallel computing algorithm will be developed using PC clusters. Based on the proposed algorithm, a parallel CA code will be established to explore and gain a better understanding of the mechanical behavior of super CNTs. 114010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114010.value: The proposed project aims to develop a parallel cellular automata (CA) algorithm for the simulation of the mechanical behavior of super carbon nanotubes (CNTs) in a personal computer (PC) environment. By linking the atomistic and continuum mechanics methods, the proposed parallel CA algorithm will be as accurate as the molecular mechanics method but allow much faster simulation. In the atomistic-based CA model, a super CNT is treated as a discrete system in which the interaction between atoms is described using Tersoff-Brenner’s many-body potential, while the solution framework is based on the proposed CA algorithm which ensures the positive definiteness of stiffness matrix. Hence, the proposed parallel CA model will be suitable for the mechanics simulation of large CNT systems, termed “super CNTs”. Based on the proposed algorithm, a parallel FORTRAN code will be established to predict the bending, tension, and fracture behaviors of super CNTs. The proposed parallel CA model, once verified, will provide a comprehensive understanding of super CNTs, which is the key towards achieving practical applications of this new class of materials. 本项目将传统细胞自动机方法扩展用于研究超级纳米碳管的力学性能。基于原子层次上的连续力学模型,拟建立的并行细胞自动机算法和分子力学方法同样精确,但计算效率却高得多.在细胞自动机模型中, 超级纳米碳管处理成一个离散的系统.其中原子间的相互作用通过Tersoff-Brenner多体势能来描述, 但计算是在刚度矩阵分析的框架下进行.因此所提出的算法很适合于分析大型纳米碳管系统,如超级纳米碳管的力学性能. 一旦确认了该算法的正确性,利用该算法有助于全面认识超级纳米碳管的力学特性.

114010.label: Major findings and research outcome
114010.value: A new method is developed for the simulation of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) based on the molecular mechanics and cellular automata algorithms. The proposed atomic-based cellular automata algorithm (ACAA) is as accurate as the molecular mechanics method and much faster for the simulation of CNTs. Specifically, the use of the ACAA effectively avoids the problem of a nonpositive-definite matrix in the simulation of large CNT system because the maximum size of the stiffness matrix is only 30 rows!30 columns. Although we consider the simulation of CNTs, it should be noted that the proposed method covers general topics of other nanomaterials such as fullerenes C60, grapheme sheets and even CNT-reinforced composites. The ACAA simulations illustrate that an initial vacancy lowers 8.1% of bonds rearranging strain of (10,10) SWCNTs with Stone–Wales defects occurring first at the initial vacancy sites, implying that the initial vacancy leads to an earlier advent of plastic deformation. Also, simulation results reveal 3.7% lower critical fracture strain than perfect (10,10) SWCNTs, indicating that an initial vacancy causes a significant damage in CNTs. Also, the ACAA study shows that vacancy defects lower the critical buckling load significantly and the buckling occurs at the defect sites, indicating that a vacancy defect causes a significant geometrical imperfection in CNTs.

114010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
114010.value: The developed atomic-based cellular automata algorithm (ACAA) will be extend to the simulation of grapheme sheets because the potentials to describe the interactions between carbon-carbon atoms in CNT and grapheme sheets are the same. A parallel computing scheme will be developed according to the structural characteristic of grapheme sheets. In the parallel ACAA model, a super grapheme sheets is treated as a discrete system in which the interaction between atoms is described using Tersoff-Brenner’s many-body potential, while the solution framework is based on the proposed CA algorithm which ensures the positive definiteness of stiffness matrix. Hence, the proposed parallel ACAA model will be suitable for the mechanics simulation of large grapheme sheets system.

114010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114010.value: Super carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are particularly attractive for reinforcement materials in nanocomposites due to extremely low mass density. It is found that super-CNTs exhibit some unusual mechanical properties distinctly different from individual CNTs and the rupture strain of super-CNTs reaches more than 30%. Thus, super-CNTs might be used as reinforcement materials with high flexibility and a remarkable capability of force transferring. The current investigations on super-CNTs are mainly focus on the atomistic based methods, but these methods are limited to very small size because the computational time exponentially explodes with increase in the number of atoms. On the other hand, continuum mechanics theories is not applicable to describe the mechanical behavior of super-CNTs because current continuum mechanics is developed based on the theory of continuum media with the materials being assumed defect-free. The proposed atomic-based cellular automata algorithm can overcome the shortages of above mentioned methods because it is as accurate as the molecular mechanics and much faster for the simulation of super-CNTs. The successful development of the computational model will help to study the super-CNTs with defect-free or defects. This is the key towards achieving practical application of this new class of materials.

114310.label: Project Objectives
114310.value: Develop a highly active and stable OCO foam reactor for this proposed study based on the latest nano-material preparation technology. Nano-sized catalysts (e.g., Pd or Pt) will be uniformly dispersed on the surface of hydrophobic substrates (e.g., MCM-41 or SBA-15), which will be coated on the aluminum foam reactor. Study the main effects and possible interactions of the operational variables in the OCO system with statistically designed experiments to achieve the maximum removal efficiency and robustness of the purification process towards nuisance environmental factors. Investigate the toluene decomposition mechanism in the OCO system under various scenarios, including optimal and worst-case scenarios, which were identified based on the aforementioned fitted statistical models. Develop a theoretical model that incorporates mass transfer and chemical kinetics to predict the conversion efficiency of the OCO process for indoor air purification. Develop an accurate bias-corrected predictive model by combining the theoretical model and physical experiments for future prediction and process optimization.

114310.value: 近年來，室內空氣質量已成為香港和許多其他國家共同關心的一個重要問題。室內排放的低濃度甲苯（0.5-3 ppm）會導致不良的健康影響，如過敏性反應，疲倦，甚至癌症。在這種情況下，為了達到政府制定的更嚴格的室內環境質量標準，建築物就需要消耗大量的能源。 可在中溫（300 400℃）運行的臭氧催化氧化（OCO）是一個相對較新的節能技術，可在高濃度甲苯（500-1000 ppm）戶外應用中實現70-95％的去除率。然而，要應用此技術於室內環境室溫下去除甲苯，就必須實現技術突破。這是由於室溫下臭氧催化氧化過程中的甲苯氧化反應速率非常低。因此，發展和優化高性能的反應器使其可應用於室內甲苯去除勢在必行，解決臭氧催化氧化技術中的一些關鍵問題，包括對環境有害的中間產物的形成，釋放的低濃度臭氧，在室溫條件下長時間使用後催化劑的失活等問題。 本項建旨在解決應用於室內甲苯去除臭氧催化氧化技術中的關鍵問題。首先，我們要製造新型的臭氧催化氧化反應器。該目標可通過下列步驟實現。將活度和穩定性高的納米級催化劑（如鈀或鉑）均勻分散並沉積在疏水基體表面（如分子篩MCM - 41或SBA - 15），然後將它們塗在泡沫鋁反應器裡。與傳統反應器相比，這種高活度的泡沫反應器可大大強化傳熱傳質並降低壓損，從而降低運行成本。 第二，設計和開發階乘和響應面試驗，從而建立統計模型以同時研究不同參數的的主要影響及可能的相互作用幾。利用此模型，對應於與環境因素有關的滋擾對各運行參數進行表徵和優化。 第三，基於統計模型的結果，設計最佳和最壞的情況下的實驗條件來研究和理解乾濕條件下臭氧催化氧化過程中的甲苯分解機制，在線分析催化劑表面的中間產物。獲得的結果可用於指導催化劑的設計從而實現甲苯的完全氧化。 第四，利用實驗數據，建立一個包括傳質和化學動力學的理論模型用以描述泡沫反應器中的臭氧催化氧化過程。該模型可幫助研究人員更好地了解臭氧催化氧化過程，指導反應器的配置，並提供必要的全面工程操作數據。 第五，結合理論模型和物理實驗，建立一個精確的偏置校正預測模型，為將來的預測和過程優化服務，實現臭氧催化氧化系統的高能量效率和價格低廉的優點。本研究還將提供更多關於具有高能量效率的室內空氣淨化系統的相關信息，保持一個更加健康的建築環境。

114310.label: Major findings and research outcome
114310.value: The objectives were achieved. In objective 1, we developed a simple method to produce a highly active and stable nano-sized Pd catalysts on MCM-41 which was coated on a nickel foam reactor. PdO catalyst was loaded onto MCM-41 via impregnation. XRD, BET, TEM, FTIR spectroscopy, and TGA were used to examine the physicochemical properties of the PdO/MCM-41 samples. The characteristic hexagonal channel array of the MCM-41 pore system was not destroyed by loading Pd, but the order and surface area of ere decreased. In objectives 2 and 3, the effects of reaction temperature, concentration of toluene/ozone ratio, space velocity, and time-on-stream on toluene oxidation behavior were investigated. The enhanced toluene removal efficiency was attributed to the decomposition of ozone to form atomic oxygen reacting with adsorbed toluene. Higher toluene conversion was observed at lower space velocities under various inlet ozone concentrations. As the inlet ozone and toluene concentration increased, the toluene removal efficiency was limited by the number of available active sites in the PdO/MCM-41, which governs the amount of adsorbed toluene and atomic oxygen available for subsequent reactions. Post-reaction sample characterizations were conducted to determine the cause of sample deactivation. No severe coke deposition was observed on the sample surface. The results suggest that the oxidation of the adsorbed byproduct organic species may have occurred on the catalyst surface in air. In objectives 4 and 5, the mechanism of toluene oxidation was proposed by assuming that toluene and ozone were adsorbed onto the catalyst surface. The toluene active adsorption sites were considered to be different from the ozone active adsorption sites. The process is acceptably modeled by a dual adsorption Langmuir–Hinselwood mechanism after some empirical based simplifications. The proposed model was capable of simulate the tests conducted by varying both the inlet ozone concentration and toluene concentration. The results suggest that with a high catalyst loading, a higher portion of ozone goes through the decomposition into active oxygen species for oxidation of toluene. We proposed a macro-homogeneous model, which does not consider the transport of species between different types of pores, to predict the conversion efficiency of the OCO process. The model as well as the employed parameters could reasonably reflect the physical and chemical process occurring inside of the OCO reactor. At lower temperatures (< 250 oC), the model predictions show an obvious trend that the reduction of toluene conversion fraction is more rapid at higher GHSVs. At lower reaction temperatures, the reaction rates are lower, which leads to longer toluene concentration half-lives. There is a minor effect on the toluene conversion fraction by changing the residence time in OCO process. The results suggest that at lower temperature applications, residence time becomes a more influential parameter for process yield control.

114310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
114310.value: The results of this project provided some important information about 1) how to produce PdO/MCM-41 on Ni foam as a filter for air purification application, 2) modeling of VOCs removal efficiencies of the proposed OCO process. The know-how obtained from this project can support us to produce a large foam filter (8 cm x 8 cm x 0.2 cm) for application in table-top air cleaner. We may utilize the findings from this project to develop a cost-effective commercial air purifier based on the OCO technology.

114310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114310.value: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) have been recognized as major contributors to indoor air pollution which has become an important issue in Hong Kong and in many other countries. When source control and increase ventilation cannot mitigate the indoor air quality (IAQ) problem in buildings, air purification becomes a feasible option to assist in the improvement of IAQ in buildings. In the retail sectors, we have a lot of air purifiers available on the Hong Kong market. However, most of them are using overseas’ technologies for air purification. Huge amount of money actually flow to overseas suppliers due to a lack of technologies/products from Hong Kong companies. In this project, we proposed an ozone-catalytic oxidation (OCO) technology for VOCs removal. PdO/MCM-41/Ni foam was used as an air filter. Ozone and toluene were adsorbed on the filter for subsequent decomposition reactions. This new filter design 1) enhances the VOCs transport and adsorption, increasing the purification efficiency, and 2) decreases the energy consumption (e.g. pump work). Air purifiers, adopting the OCO technology, can be operated at room temperature, which further reduces energy consumption. The outcomes of this project will benefit local engineering contracting companies who will use a local supplier of air purification systems in building projects. Other sectors that can benefit from this project are porous material suppliers, plasma system suppliers and device control companies in Hong Kong.

114410.label: Realisation of objectives
114410.value: For objective 1, we have examined the interactions of the wireless charging pads and the signal transmission and reception of the mobile phones. The research team has tested the effects of the Radio-Frequency Interference (RFI) generated by the electronic charging circuits on the mobile phones and practically confirmed that such RFI could deteriorate both signal transmission and reception capabilities. For objective 2, we have confirmed practically that the EM shield underneath the charging pad could reduce the signal strength in both transmission and reception. The results in Objectives 1 and 2 enabled us to understand the issues so that we can develop solutions in Objectives 3 and 4 to solve the problems. For Objective 3, we have successfully developed a technique based on the Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) to block the RFI emitted from the electronics of the charging circuit underneath the charging pad. The FSS can be fabricated as a thin layer that can be placed on top of the charging surface. The practical results and confirmation of this concept were published in the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics. For Objective 4, we have developed a passive antenna that can enhance the signal transmission and reception of the mobile phones without affecting the energy efficiency in the energy-receiving modules of the mobile phones. Such results were published in another paper in the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics .

114410.label: Major findings and research outcome
114410.value: The major findings of this project are listed as follows: Based on a practical wireless charging pad, we have practically confirmed that the switching actions of the power-electronics based charging circuit would generate Radio-Frequency Interference (RFI) that falls within the communication frequency bands of the mobile phones. Consequently, the signal reception and transmission of the mobile phones would be adversely affected. In the process, we have identified the exact mechanism and magnitude of the problems. Besides the RFI generated by the charging circuit, we also identified the Electromagnetic Shield (placed underneath the charging pad) as another factor that reduces the signal transmission and reception capabilities of the mobile phones. Such EM Shield can reduce the signal strength in both transmission and reception. After practically identifying the issues, we then focused on new solutions to reduce the RFI and shielding effects on the signal transmission and reception. The first invention is a novel passive antenna (repeater) that can be placed on the surface of the charging area of the wireless charging pad. This passive antenna consists of a very thin layer of conducting patterns that act as signal repeaters. It has the effects of enhancing the signal magnitude in both signal transmission and reception. The practically proven results have been reported in the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics (Paper-1). A second breakthrough in the project is the successful design and implementation of a Frequency-selective Surface (FSS) for suppressing the RFI emitted from the charging circuit. the FSS technique has been previously been used in Stealth Technology and for shielding microwave. Our team is the first one who have successively designed a FSS, based on the folded Jerusalem Cross patterns, to block RFI in the communication bands. Such FSS has been proved to be very effective in suppressing RFI that could affect the signal transmission and reception in the mobile phones. These results have been reported in the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics (Paper-2). Upon an invitation by the Editorial Board of the Proceedings of the IEEE, the PI has also published an Invited Paper (Paper-3) on the general development of the planar wireless charging technology and the Qi Standard. 114410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114410.value: We have successfully demonstrated that signal transmission and reception of mobile phones could be affected by the 'noise' generated by the charging circuit and by the electromagnetic shield placed underneath the charging pad. We adopted two approaches to deal with the problems. Firstly, we looked for a technology that can enhance the signal. Secondly, we developed technology to block the noise. In this project, we have pioneered the passive antenna design to enhance the signal transmission and reception capabilities. The passive antenna or repeater can strengthen the signal so that the signal-to-noise ratio will not be severely affected by the noise generated by the charging circuit. The promising results have been published in the IEEE Transactions. We have also developed the Frequency-selective surface to block such noise. The two technologies have been practically proven and published in the IEEE Transactions.

114710.label: Project Title(Chinese)

114710.label: Project Objectives
114710.value: Developing optimal algorithms for placing APs in an area such that clients bandwidth requirement can be met and the total cost of APs is minimized. We consider the case that APs can be equipped with different number of access radios and clients can have different data rates depending on the signal strength it can receive from an AP. Developing algorithms for placing minimal number of gateway in a connected subgraph, such that clients QoS requirements (bandwidth and delay) can be met. We consider system-wide interference when computing effective capacity of links in the network. Developing algorithms for placing minimal number of MRs to interconnect a set of disconnected small subgraphs into adequate sizes such that each of them can be served by one gateway subject to clients QoS requirements. The objective is to maximize the cost saving, which is defined as the cost of reduced gateways minus the cost of added MRs (note: initially each disconnected subgraph requires a gateway).

114710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114710.value: A wireless mesh network consists of three types of nodes: AP (access point) nodes that provide front-end access to wireless clients, MR (mesh router) nodes that interconnect AP nodes and gateway nodes to form a mesh backbone network, and gateway nodes that are connected to internet by wired line to provide internet connection for the mesh network. The principal goal of this project is to investigate the optimal placement of APs, MRs, and gateways in indoor environment such that the clients QoS requirements clients are met and the total financial cost of the network is minimized. The unit prices for AP, MR and gateway are different. We divide the problem into several sub-tasks as the following: 1) developing optimal algorithms for placing APs in an area such that clients bandwidth requirement can be met and the total cost of APs is minimized. We consider the case that APs can be equipped with different number of access radios and clients can have different data rates depending on the signal strength it can receive from an AP. 2) developing algorithms for placing minimal number of gateway in a connected subgraph, such that clients QoS requirements (bandwidth and delay) can be met. We consider system-wide interference when computing effective capacity of links in the network. 3) developing algorithms for placing minimal number of MRs to interconnect a set of disconnected small subgraphs into adequate sizes such that each of them can be served by one gateway subject to clients QoS requirements. The objective is to maximize the cost saving, which is defined as the cost of reduced gateways minus the cost of added MRs (note: initially each disconnected subgraph requires a gateway). The project has great significance of both academic research and industrial applications. The output of the project includes high quality research publications, algorithms and software for solving the optimal placement problems, and training of PhD students. 無綫網狀網絡包含三種類型的節點：接入點（AP），用於爲無綫客戶端提供前端接入；網狀網絡路由器（MR），用於提供AP與網關節點之間的連接，形成一個網狀骨幹網絡；網關（gateway），通過有綫綫路連接到互聯網，爲網狀網絡提供互聯網連接。本項目的主要目標是研究AP、MR與gateway三種節點在室內環境中的最佳擺放位置，以滿足無綫客戶端的QoS需求，並且使得網絡的組建成本最低。這三種節點的單位價格是不同的。我們把該項目分爲以下幾個子問題：1) 設計一個放置AP節點的最優算法，以最低的成本滿足一個區域內無綫客戶端的帶寬需求。我們允許一個AP裝備多個無綫收發設備，同時也考慮由於無綫客戶端與AP間信號強度的不同而帶來的多種通訊速率的情況。2) 設計一個算法，通過在一個連通子圖中放置最少的網關，來滿足無綫客戶端的QoS（帶寬與延時）需求。在計算各個鏈路的有效通訊容量時，我們會把系統級的鏈路干擾考慮在內。3) 設計一個算法，通過放置最少數量的MR節點，把小規模的子圖連成一些大小合適的連通子圖，使得每個子圖由一個網關提供服務，並且無綫客戶端的QoS需求得到滿足。我們的目標是儘可能地節約成本，成本的節約量即是減少的網關的成本減去增加的MR節點的成本（注：初始狀態下每個連通子圖都需要一個網關）。 無論從學術研究或是工業應用的角度來看，該項目都具有重要意義。它的產出包括解決該問題的高質量學術論文、算法、軟件產品，並且可以用於訓練博士研究生。

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114710.value: A mesh network consists of three types of nodes: AP (access point) nodes that provide front-end access to wireless clients, MR (mesh router) nodes that interconnect AP nodes and gateway nodes to form a mesh backbone network, and gateway nodes that are connected to internet by wired line to provide internet connection for the mesh network. The principal goal of this project is to investigate the optimal placement of APs, MRs, and gateways in indoor environment such that the clients QoS requirements are met and the total financial cost of the network is minimized. The unit prices for AP, MR and gateway are different. We divide the problem into several sub-tasks as the following: 1) developing optimal algorithms for placing APs in an area such that clients bandwidth requirement can be met and the total cost of APs is minimized. We consider the case that APs can be equipped with different number of access radios and clients can have different data rates depending on the signal strength it can receive from an AP. 2) developing algorithms for placing minimal number of gateway in a connected subgraph, such that clients QoS requirements (bandwidth and delay) can be met. We consider system-wide interference when computing effective capacity of links in the network. The project has great significance of both academic research and industrial applications. The output of the project includes high quality research publications, algorithms and software for solving the optimal placement problems, and training of PhD students.

115210.value: 通過設施管理模型來提升老年人在香港護理安老院的生活質量

115210.label: Co - Investigator(s)

115210.label: Project Objectives
115210.value: To identify FM components and indicators of the QoL of the elderly. To establish the FM-QoL relationship for the elderly in C&A homes. To develop an integrated FMQoL model for the elderly in C&A homes. To recommend FM guidelines for enhancing the QoL of the elderly in C&A homes.
