115210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
115210.value: Although the birth rate in Hong Kong (HK) ranks among the world’s lowest, life expectancy is among the highest. As a result, the proportion of elderly people in the HK population is increasing and has been projected to reach 24% of the total by 2031. Some elderly people live in relatively poor communities with insufficient facilities, and possibly without adequate family support. Their dilapidated housing implies poor Quality of Life (QoL), with all the associated health and safety problems. Hence, the HK government has announced plans to earmark a one-off tranche of funding of $200 million over the next five years to help improve housing for the elderly (HKSAR 2007). The physical environment in which we live is a recognized dimension of QoL (The World Health Organization Quality of Life Assessment [WHOQOL] Group 1998a), and is likely to be particularly important for elderly persons living in residential care. Due to limitations in their health and mobility, many older people spend most of their time at home and depend on facilities and facilities management (FM), to compensate for their physical and biological problems and also to maintain their psychological wellbeing. ‘Ageing in Place’ was one of the objectives initiated by the HK Chief Executive in his recent Policy Address (HKSAR 2007). However, the HK government only introduced the Residential Care Homes (Elderly Persons) Ordinance in 1996 and the Standardised Care Need Assessment Mechanism in 2002; both include only simple environmental items. There is extensive literature about facilities management, caring environmental design, occupancy evaluation, and QoL for adults and the elderly, but there is a lack of study about the integration of all of these aspects for the elderly. The purpose of this research is to enhance the QoL of the elderly in Care and Attention (C&A) homes through integrated facilities management(FM). The objectives are: (1) to identify FM components in C&A homes and QoL indicators for the elderly; (2) to establish FM–QoL relationships for the elderly in C&A homes; (3) to develop an integrated FM-QoL model; (4) to verify the model by case studies; and (5) to establish FM guidelines for enhancing the QoL of the elderly in C&A homes. It is envisaged that the findings of this study will promote the development of a proactive assessment of FM in C&A homes, and will enhance the QoL of the elderly in residential C&A homes by disseminating the results throughout the industry. 雖然香港的出生率在全球性中相對較低，但其預期壽命也是比較長的，結果造成老齡化人口在整個香港人口的比重逐年上升。在香港的老年人之中，有的人仍然生活在較為貧困的社區，缺少足夠的設施，甚至缺少足夠的家庭支持。惡劣的生活環境降低了這些老年人的生活質量，引致了很多健康及安全相關的問題。作為生活質量一個公認維度的居住實體環境（世界衛生組織 1998a），對於安老院的老人來說非常重要。由於健康和活動能力的限制，老年人大部份時間呆在室內並且需要依賴於室內設施及設施管理的輔助去解決他們生理上的問題和維持心理上的健康。然而，香港政府在1996年發佈的安老院條例以及2002年發佈的安老院服務統一評估機制都僅僅涉及一些簡單的居住環境事項。 大量的設施管理文獻涉及居住環境，使用者評估和成年人及老年人的生活質量，但是將這幾個方面綜合起來的研究還相當缺乏。本課題的目的就在於通過全面系統的設施管理來提升護理安老院老人的生活質量。研究目標包括：（1）確定護理安老院的 設施管理指標以及老年人生活質量指標；（2）建立設施管理和護理安老院老人的生活 質量的關係；（3）提出一個綜合的設施管理 – 生活質量模型；（4）提出設施管理的指導原則以便於提升護理安老院老人的生活質量。研究成果用於護理安老院設施管理的前攝評估，大範圍的推廣運用有助於提升養老院老年人的生活質量。

115210.label: Realisation of objectives
115210.value: Facilities management (FM) in Care and Attention (C&A) homes were categorized into three main aspects: architectural, building services and supporting facilities components. To enhance the Quality of Life (QoL) of elderly in C&A homes, the elderly health and the risks affecting them should be identified. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), health is a state of complete physical, and mental and social wellbeing, not merely the absence of physical disease or infirmity (WHO, 1998). In general, there are 18 common physical and mental diseases which follow from the age-related deterioration of various body systems (Hurley 1991), e.g., sudden loss of balance , dementia, depression, etc. as a result of deterioration in the nervous system (D1-7); arthritis, osteoporosis, and tremor under musculoskeletal system (D8-10); stroke under cardiovascular system (D11); breathing difficulties under respiratory system (D12); diabetes mellitus under endocrine system (D13); difficulty in sensing temperature under touch-sensory system (D14); loss of vision and red eye under vision-sensory system (D15-16); loss of hearing under hearing-sensory system (D17) and tinea infection under skin system (D18). Different elderly people will suffer from different diseases. Even though they may be living in the same physical environment, the risk susceptibility of individuals suffering from different diseases will be different. Based on an extensive literature review, conceptual relationships between health, environment and risks to the elderly in C&A homes were established. a questionnaire survey including 4 parts (background information, 18 diseases, 8 risks, and 13 FM components) were designed and conducted to the elderly living in subsidized and non-subsidized C&A homes. To ensure the cognitive ability of elderly in the study, all respondents were recruited with the assistance of the C&A home staff, and passed a cognitive test before responding the formal survey. Researchers then conducted personal interviews verbally one-by-one. Both Pearson Correlation (FM component: Risk) and Partial Correlation (FM component: Risk | Health) were adopted to analyse the data systematically. The complicated relationships between FM and QoL (Health/Risk) and an integrated FM-QoL(HR) model were established (Leung et al. 2012), while a number of recommendations were suggested to both designers and facilities managers for enhancing the QoL of elderly in C&A homes.

115210.label: Major findings and research outcome
115210.value: 1. Thirteen FM components were identified, including space planning, privacy, lighting, fixtures & finishes, ventilation, noise, temperature, signage, cleanliness, standard of staff, recreation leisure, safety & security and catering. 2a. The Pearson correlations revealed that four FM components, namely space planning, noise, signage and catering are significantly related to the risks of falling, collision, infection and/or behavioural disorder. 2b. The partial correlation analysis further indicated that several diseases, including arthritis, loss of vision, depression, short-temperedness and mild memory impairment, exert significant influence on the relationships between these FM components and risks. 2c. In a specific interview study, the elderly QoL were measured by five dimensions (i.e., overall QoL, physical health, psychological health, social relationship and living environment) based on the scale established by the World Health Organization. The quantitative and qualitative study indicated that distance, space planning, ventilation, furniture, non-slip floor and recreation facilities exert positive impact of the final QoL of the elderly living in C&A homes. 3. A FM-QoL(health/risk) for Elderly in C&A Home model has been finalized in a published paper (Leung et al. 2013). 4. To enhance the elderly QoL and minimize any potential risk, various recommendations are suggested: to enlarge the bedroom for the elderly (with 10 m2 for the single room and 16 m2 for double room), shorten the travel distance between different rooms, centralize the location of dining room and living room, place sound absorption walls in common areas, align pipes and drainage properly, install non-slip floor and windows and arrange recreation facilities

115210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115210.value: 1. It is strongly recommended that further investigations of the specific FM needs of elderly persons with those diseases (i.e., arthritis, loss of vision, depression, short-temperedness and mild memory impairment) should be carried out, so as to explore ways of protecting them from the risks of collision, infection and behavioural disorder. For instance, for elderly arthritis sufferers, further work should examine whether shortening the distance between their bedroom and the various ADL zones can mitigate their risk of collision. 2. The positive relationships between FM factors in C&A homes and final elderly QoL have been confirmed, but there are still other factors influencing elderly QoL, such as the age of the C&A homes, the financial support for both the elderly and the C&A homes, the size of individual flat and the physical condition of the elderly. It is suggested to further investigate these factors based on current research results, in order to understand a really sustainable environment for our elderly. 3. Further investigation into more specific and technical requirements of FM components is also needed. Building information modeling (BIM) is thus recommended to be used in the design and FM of the C&A homes for improving elderly QoL.

115210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115210.value: Hong Kong is a rapidly-ageing society. Elderly population may reach 24.3% in the next 20 years, causing a demand for care services. The study thus aims to investigate the impact of FM in the C&A homes on the residential elderly QoL via both quantitative and qualitative study. Totally, 13 FM components were identified, while 4 components, namely space planning, noise, signage and catering are significantly related to the risks of falling, collision, infection and/or behavioural disorder. The study also revealed that several diseases, including arthritis, loss of vision, depression, short-temperedness and mild memory impairment, exert significant influence on the relationships between these FM components and risks To improve the QoL of the elderly in the C&A homes, the designers and facilities managers are suggested to enlarge the bedroom for the elderly, shorten the travel distance between different rooms, centralize the location of dining room and living room, place sound absorption walls in common areas, align pipes and drainage properly, install non-slip floor and windows and arrange recreation facilities. Moreover, it is also suggested to develop a BIM program for the design of elder-friendly C&A homes in the future.

115310.label: Project Objectives
115310.value: To develop a new and more accurate numerical tool to account for strong coagulation and deposition for nanoparticles. To validate the proposed numerical tool by performing experiments in a scaled chamber, an environmental controlled chamber at CityU and a test house at NIST. 115310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
115310.value: In HK and many countries of the world the control of aerosol emission has a very high priority as scientific evidence has shown aerosol concentration correlates with adverse health effects. Smoking is banned in public places. However there is another combustible source which cannot be ignored. We can avoid the second hand smoke but we cannot stay away from exposure to cooking. One feature of cooking-generated particles is their extremely small sizes (2-10 nm). Common residential hoods cannot remove this size range of ultrafine particles effectively. Cooking-generated ultrafine particles are highly diffusive and they can escape from kitchens and be transported to other places within the residences. Coagulation and deposition are extremely important and dominant for this size range. To assess and control such exposure, we need to gain more fundamental understanding of the physical and chemical properties of the particles generated by stoves (gas flame, electric heating elements) and food. Numerical and experimental approaches will be applied. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be adopted to resolve this complex issue. Current commercial CFD cannot model the growth and loss dynamics for this size range accurately. New numerical kernels will be incorporated to account for coagulation and deposition. Prior to applying the developed CFD tool to model cooking scenarios, the code will be validated. Experiments will be conducted in a research house at the National Institute of Standards and Technology and a small-scale chamber and a full size environmentally controlled chamber in CityU. A modified particle scanning instrument will be used to measure the size distribution from 2 to 100 nm. Gas stoves and electric appliances will be used to generate particles with and without food. The results obtained will gain invaluable information to better model the particles. The particles generated will also be sampled and the composition analyzed. The results will be fed back to optimize the modeling parameters. It is anticipated that the current design of the hoods cannot remove effectively the nanoparticles. Cooking experiments will be conducted to measure the removal effectiveness. With the completion of proposed project, a more accurate numerical model, particularly for coagulation and deposition, will be developed. More chemical and physical characteristics of nanoparticles will be revealed. All these will become very important tools to develop engineering strategies to reduce exposure in residential settling. This will be very important in helping policymakers to review or amend current ambient air standards or policies.

115310.label: Realisation of objectives
115310.value: Objectives 1&2. Particle dispersion and deposition in a scaled ventilated chamber were studied by numerical simulation. The numerical computations are achieved by applying multiple-relaxation-time lattice Boltzmann (MRT-LB) method and the Lagrangian particle tracking method. Airflow and particle dispersion in indoor environments, where LES was used, were simulated. It was implemented by using the MRT-LB method with the Smagorinsky model. Experimental and numerical studies of airflow characteristics and particle dispersion in a ventilated model room with a partition were employed to verify the present model. Good agreement between the present results and the experimental data were observed. Besides, another simulation model was built up to study coagulation. The coagulation decay process of airborne particles were numerically investigated by using the Eulerian mixture turbulence model along with moment form of aerosol general dynamics equation (GDE), which considers the effects of Brownian motion, interparticle forces (van der Waal and viscous forces), fractal nature and convection. All the calculations were performed by employing a commercial code and the coagulation kernels in combination with population balance model of the code via user define function (UDF). The temporal change of airflow temperatures and particle number concentrations at five sampling points inside the chamber were measured. Good agreement between computed and experimental results was found. Objective 3. The size resolved concentration of the cooking activities, water boiling and oil heating, were studied in the environmental controlled chamber. Various chemical compositions have been reported to be emitted during cooking, such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), carbonaceous particles, fatty acids, NOx (NO and NO2), etc. The emission depends on the types of cooking activity and stove. For instance, deep frying was found to generate more chemicals than steaming or boiling; while gas stove has also been studied to be more emissive than electric stove. Besides, morphology of particles generated from oil heating has been studied using SEM in CityU. Even the resolution of SEM is not good enough, suspected particles can be found in the SEM capture. Objective 4. The experiments were conducted as described in Objective 3. The experimental results conducted in environmental controlled chamber were compared with the results in the test house at NIST. Capture efficiency of the kitchen hood was also measured by comparison between the particle concentrations at upstream and downstream of the kitchen hood extract fan.

115310.label: Major findings and research outcome
115310.value: The research outcomes are very encouraging. Two journals have been published while one manuscript is under-review and the other manuscript is ready to submit by the end of Sep-2014. Objectives 1&2. The MRT-LB method is introduced and verified by comparison with conventional N-S solvers, such as FLUENT results. Good agreement between these two solvers indicates that the MRT-LB method has the ability to predict the airflow field in the chamber accurately. For the simulation model focusing on coagulation, five types of coagulation mechanisms have been tested in scaled chamber. The predicted results of particle number concentration, which have been compared with the experimental data, validated the model, which includes a convective term in GDE and a van der Waals/viscosity correction, matches well with the measurement values. Therefore, it can be concluded from the results that coagulation and convection effect should be considered as the prime causes for the variation of the indoor particle number concentration during high concentration periods (>10^6 cm−3). In the environmental chamber cooking case, the buoyancy-driven airflow resulted from the temperature difference between the stove and the ambient air firstly has been thoroughly simulated. The temporal change of airflow temperatures and particle number concentrations were computed and measured. Good agreement between the predicted results and experimental results of the particle concentration changing can be found. Objective 3. In the experiments performed, we focused on the size distribution of particles generated from the cooking process. The particle size distribution was measured for each set of experiment. The concentration profile was found to shift over time from smaller to larger sizes. This could have been mainly caused by coagulation. Coagulation occurs only at high concentrations, which are provided by the high emission rate from the stove. Objective 4. The capture efficiencies of the kitchen hood were determined under three power levels for both water and oil heating. All capture efficiencies at the three hood power levels showed similar high values. However, the experimental results described in Objective 3 indicate that certain amount of concentration was measured outside the hood boundary (space under kitchen hood), in spite of a lower magnitude. This result implies that particles might transport from the source to the side and access other locations outside the hood boundary, instead of moving upward. The capture efficiency presented here may represent the ability of kitchen hood to capture the particles close to the hood extraction inlet.

115310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115310.value: The study indicated that spillage of particles is possible even if the kitchen hood is operated. Therefore, further study could be conducted by evaluating the location of spillage of cooking emitted pollutants. Particle concentration at various locations below the edge of kitchen hood can be measured in order to find out the particles’ transport pattern when the kitchen hood is operated. The results may help to develop a more efficient measure in reducing exposure to the pollutants, for instance, finding an optimum installation of kitchen hood and cooking platform. This is important to improve indoor air quality at home. Besides, the current research project was conducted in environmental controlled chamber, where mechanical ventilation is used. This is definitely impacting on the kitchen hood extract flow. In a domestic unit, the dominant factor of kitchen hood performance is the size of window/door opening (i.e. the amount of air available). This factor can be studied by providing different amount of air into the chamber to demonstrate the natural flow in a domestic unit. The result could indicate how the outer flow influence on the kitchen hood performance.

115310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115310.value: This research project adopted both experimental and numerical approaches to study physical characteristics of cooking emitted particles. As smaller particles are easier to penetrate to lung compared with larger particles, while some of the substances emitted during cooking have been revealed to be carcinogenic, it is important to reduce exposure for such pollutants. Since domestic kitchen hood is the common measure to reduce exposure, the performance of it was revealed. A good practice in use of kitchen hood greatly reduces the risk in exposing to the cooking pollutants. The kitchen hood is suggested to always be operated since cooking starts, while additional protection can be obtained by operating the hood after cooking. It is noted that only operating the hood after cooking is nearly useless. In addition, the results also indicate that the people outside the kitchen (e.g. in living room) can also be exposed to a highly cooking-induced polluted environment. As residential unit in Hong Kong is not big, pollutants emitted during cooking can easily transport throughout the entire flat. Therefore, the risk of exposure is not only limited to the person who performs cooking, but also all people at home.

115510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
115510.value: 道碴軌道系統是鐵路運輸其中一種最重要的系統。 鑒於鐵路安全的重要性，與工業應用的研究工作已正進行。 現在鐵路軌道監測系統是全面，快速而有效地監測軌道平水、線形、方向、軌距及波浪紋等等。 但是，道碴損傷檢測仍然依靠目視檢測及破壞性的鑽芯測試。 雖然對道碴損傷評估的非破壞性方法發展巳進行了廣泛的研究，但是鐵路仍需要一個普遍接受的方法。 香港現行的做法是軌道督察收到軌道故障報告（例如，車長及乘客匯報異常列車振動），便進行詳細的現場勘察找出有問題的地點。 不過這種目視檢查方法卻衹能夠找出軌道表面道碴的損傷、軌道幾何及三角坑問題。 其實要找到會由在混凝土軌枕受力面下或在道碴肩的損壞道碴破壞軌道穩定性及行車平順性是極其困難甚至是不可能通過目測檢驗來探測到。 鑽芯測試是破壞性、 昂貴、 耗時及可能嚴重影響行車服務。 軌道督察可以用快速即時檢測方法及簡單設備來探測道碴的損傷將有有價值的資訊交予軌道工程師，幫助他更有效評估軌道安全及行車平順度。 因此這個提案的主要目的是研發一種基於用簡單錘擊量度混凝土軌枕原位震盪探測道碴損傷的簡便方法。 用來支承軌枕的道碴剛度取決於其大小和搗固平水。 研究證明此剛度的變化會引起可探測到軌枕振動特性的變化。 在這個建議提案中的量度現場鐵路混凝土軌枕震盪探測道碴損傷資料會進行研究。

115510.label: Realisation of objectives
115510.value: The project is satisfactory completed. Several classes of models for capturing the vibration characteristics of the rail-sleeper-ballast system were developed (objective 1). The classes of models are mainly divided into two categories. They are (1) the discrete model class, and (2) the continuous model class. In the discrete model class, the ballast under the sleeper was divided into several regions with equal width, and the ballast stiffness within a given region is assumed to be constant. This model class is simple and easy to implement. However, the artificial stiffness discontinuity at the interface between two regions increases the problem of modeling error. To overcome this difficulty, the continuous class of models was developed. The basic idea is to model the ballast stiffness under the sleeper as a continuous function, which is controlled by several non-parametric parameters. In this study, polynomial with different order was employed as the continuous function. The order of polynomial was identified by the Bayesian model class selection method based on a set of measured data. Full-scale vibration tests on the undamaged ballasted tracks were carried out (objective 3) for collecting vibration data in confirming the performance of different newly developed model classes and identify the most appropriate one for the purpose of ballast damage detection. The experimental case study results are very positive showing that several model classes can be used to predict the dynamic characteristics of the system in reasonable accuracy. Based on the newly developed model classes, several possible methods to detect the ballast damage were developed (objective 2). The most outstanding advantage of the proposed ballast damage detection method is the use of Bayesian probabilistic theory in quantifying the uncertainties associated with the analysis result, which is introduced by the problems of measurement noise and modeling error. Different ballast damage scenarios were simulated in the full-scale test panel, and a series of vibration tests were carried out to obtain the vibration data of the in-situ sleeper (objective 3). The data is employed to verify the proposed ballast damage detection methods and very encouraging results were obtained.

115510.label: Major findings and research outcome
115510.value: Apart from several newly developed model classes and the proposed damage detection method for ballast damage detection, the project also developed a full-scale in-door test panel and the corresponding specification of vibration measurement using impact hammer test. It must be pointed out the dynamic characteristics of the rail-sleeper-ballast system depends on the environmental factors, such as temperature. The in-door test panel allows researchers to control the effects of temperature and humidity. As a result, the damage induced changes in dynamic characteristics will not be altered by the environmental factors. This control is essential in the development stage of a practical ballast damage detection method. The same experimental setup can be employed for the future development of track safety methods. The newly developed rail-sleeper-ballast model classes, the ballast damage detection method, and the corresponding full-scale experimental verification case studies were reported in a series of conferences. It must be pointed out the conference paper “A Study of Detecting Prestressed Concrete Sleeper Damage” received the Best Paper Award in the Annual Conference of World Railway Development and Research Society 2011 (see research output). Furthermore, a journal paper was published in Engineering Structures (see research output). An EngD student (Mr Wong MT) was trained in this research project. The EngD student completed his oral defense at 4 June 2014. The external examiner decided to recommend Wong MT’s work for the best thesis award. However, there is no such award for EngD students. The PhD student targets to submit her thesis at the end of 2014.

115510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115510.value: It must be pointed out that this project opened a new area of research for the railway industry. The idea of using vibration data for the purpose of continuous monitoring of railway track system is very new. Both the theoretical and experimental contributions from this project is essential for the development of other new methods for enhancing the performance of track safety monitoring systems. It is not difficult to list some potential follow up projects (e.g., the detection of cracks under the sleeper based on vibration measurement of the in-situ sleeper, and the health monitoring of rail-sleeper-ballast system). One important example is the nonlinear modeling of ballast. In the proposed method, impact hammer test is employed to collect vibration data and natural frequencies and mode shapes were employed for the detection of damage on the system. This approach is applicable only when the system is linear. It was found that for small amplitude vibration, the system can be accurately approximated by a linear system. However, the system is nonlinear when the amplitude of vibration is not small. Therefore, the study of the nonlinear behavior of ballast is an important research topic for ensuring the safety of ballasted track system.

115510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115510.value: This project aims in the development of a new and practical method for the detection of damaged ballast under the sleeper without lifting up the sleeper. The main function of railway ballast is to keep the sleeper and so as the rails in position. Damages on ballast (the reduction in the size of ballast particles) will reduce the stiffness of the ballast in supporting the sleeper. As a result, the deformation of the track system will be increase. This may result in rail buckling or derailment problem. For busy cities like Hong Kong, it is not possible to lift up sleepers for the detection of ballast damage as this will seriously affect the train schedule. The proposed method allows permanent way engineers to assess the condition of ballast by simple impact hammer test on the in-situ sleeper. The analysis results not only helps engineers to detect damaged ballast but also provide important information for railway company to make decision on re-ballasting of track systems.

115910.label: Realisation of objectives
115910.value: The original project objectives are all 100% completed. More specifically, 1. We have developed a fuzzy ontology based knowledge representation scheme to capture contextual opinion knowledge such as the relationships between entities and entity features, and entity features and sentiments for various business domains; 2. We have successful developed a hybrid lexicon and statistical learning based computational method named Pseudo Labeling for the automatic extraction of entities, sentiments, and the relationships between entities and sentiments from training corpora so that bilingual domain-specific opinion lexicons are built; 3. We have integrated both informational inference and probabilistic language modeling approaches to develop a novel computational method to represent and reason about the uncertainty arising in opinion retrieval from free texts; 4. We have developed an experimental bilingual opinion mining system on our project computer server. TREC-based benchmark opinion retrieval tasks were tested against our prototype system. In addition, usability studies were performed to demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed methodology.

115910.label: Major findings and research outcome
115910.value: In this research project, we have achieved the following outcomes: 1. An expressive fuzzy ontology based knowledge representation scheme was developed to capture the rich semantics in opinion retrieval contexts (e.g., the relationships between entities and entity features, and the relationships between entity features and sentiments for various business domains); 2. A novel semi-supervised bilingual sentiment lexicon learning method named Pseudo Labeling was developed and tested under a variety of business domains; 3. Both informational inference and probabilistic language modeling approaches were exploited to develop a novel computational method to address the uncertainty issue arising in opinion mining; 4. A java-based prototype opinion retrieval system was developed. Based on the developed prototype system, rigorous experiments were performed to verify the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed methodology; 5. The aforementioned reseearch work has been presented in top-tier international conferences such as ACM Annual Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (ACM CIKM'11), and top-tier international journals such as MIS Quarterly and Decision Support Systems.

115910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115910.value: The aforementioned opinion retrieval methodology does not address the noise and spam presented in online comments. Future research work will develop a bilingual deceptive opinions detection framework to filter out noisy comments before feeding them to our opinion retrieval system. This future work forms the integal part of another related GRF project (CityU 145712) that is under way.

115910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115910.value: In the era of the Social Web, user-contributed data is the norm, and there is an explosive growth of the number of user-contributed comments on the Web. Manually browsing through all the online comments has become impractical. There is a pressing need to develop automated opinion retrieval systems that organizations or individuals can use to more efficiently retrieve and analyze the online comments about various entities and services. To this end, an opinion retrieval system should be able to automatically learn domain specific sentiment indicators because constructing sentiment indicators manually is very labor-intensive. The aim of this research project is to exploit ontology extraction techniques, context-sensitive information retrieval, and informational inference methods to develop a cross-domain opinion retrieval system that is underpinned by a novel sentiment lexicon learning method. The practical implication of our research work is that an effective bilingual opinion retrieval technology is developed to support Hong Kong organizations in extracting business intelligence (BI) from online comments to improve the quality of their products and services and enhancing their competitiveness in the global market.

116010.label: Project Objectives
116010.value: We will perform a formal investigation on some representative prediction algorithms for addressing the network latency problem of the demanding DIAs in order to determine the main factors that affect the prediction accuracy of these algorithms. We will then analyze the accuracy profiles of these algorithms against individual factors. We will develop mechanisms for estimating the prediction error bound. We will make use of the accuracy profiles to help determine the error bound. Three approaches to determine the error bound will be considered here, the statistical approach, the feedback approach and the analytical approach. We will extensively evaluate the performance of the mechanisms for estimating the error bound in a simulated environment. We will apply different metrics for the evaluation. Some potential metrics include tightness of the error bound against accuracy of the error bound, adaptability to different users, and adaptability to different devices. Finally, we will evaluate the performance of the mechanisms in a real application. We plan to incorporate the mechanisms to the caching and prefetching module of a streaming-based online game engine and evaluate how the proposed mechanisms perform in such a demanding application.

116010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
116010.value: 虽然已有很多针对网络延迟问题的预测方法被提出来，但是对于预测的准确度，暂时还没有太多的工作。在这个项目里，我们准备研究影响已有预测算法准确度的因素，以解决对"分布式交互应用"要求较高的网络延迟问题。我们将研究现有算法的特征，建立模型来分析影响它们精度的因素。在这些分析的基础上，针对每个预测算法做出的预测，我们将提出估计错误上下限的方法。以下是我们考虑使用的估计错误界限的方法： - 统计方法-记录一系列预测所产生的偏差，计算它们的分布。 - 反馈方法-利用算法在最近产生的预测偏差 - 分析方法-分析预测算法所使用的预测模型的特征 我们的研究会包括对比以上方法的性能以及综合各种方法的可能性。除了使用模拟环境之外，我们还会研究新的错误界限估计方法在真实环境中的性能。

116010.label: Realisation of objectives
116010.value: In this project, we aimed at studying the accuracy of prediction algorithms. As prediction algorithms are widely used in many different applications, understanding how accurate a prediction technique is and what factors determine its accuracy are becoming important issues. In this project, we used the 2D mouse of a desktop environment as an investigation platform and studied techniques for predicting the 2D mouse position. First, we investigated six factors that might affect the accuracy of the prediction algorithms: mismatch of motion model, input noise, input quantization, sampling time precision, network jitter, and update frequency. Second, we developed techniques for estimating the prediction error bounds at various stages of the prediction cycle, by considering the six factors. One technique is based on an analytical approach integrated with a feedback mechansim to estimate error bounds and the other is based on a statistical approach - the confident ellipses. Third, we applied the ideas to two applications, using the findings from this project. One is on multi-server load balancing, where network latency may affect the accuracy of the load balancing solutions. The other is crowd motion prediction, where the error bounds can be used to avoid collisions among the agents. Overall, we have essentially completed the three objectives that we proposed to do. For objective 1, we investigated various factors that affect the prediction accuracy and also studied how each of these factors affects the prediction accuracy. For objective 2, we originally proposed to study three approaches to determine the error bounds, the statistical approach, the feedback approach and the analytical approach. While we were developing the analytical approach, we found that the feedback approach should be incorporated in order to refine the error bounds. Hence, at the end, we focused on two approaches, the statistical approach and the analytical approach. For objective 3, we evaluated the error bound mechanism on two applicants, multi-server load balancing and crowd motion prediction. In both situations, we demonstrated that the error bound strategy could help improve the performance of the applications.

116010.label: Major findings and research outcome
116010.value: In this project, we first identified a number of factors that might affect the errors of a motion predictor as follows: 1. Mismatch of motion model: caused by the use of incorrect motion model to model the motion behavior of the device/object. 2. Input noise: caused by the deviation of the input measurements from the motion behavior of the input device. 3. Input quantization: caused by the quantization of the measurement values. 4. Sampling time precision: caused by the uncertainty of when exactly each input measurement is sampled. 5. Network jitter: caused by the fluctuation of the network latency or processing delay. 6. Update frequency: caused since the predictor needs to use the last received update message for prediction until the next update message is received. By considering these six factors, we divided each motion pulse of the mouse into three stages: stage I – unpredictable stage, stage II – refinement stage, and stage III – predictable stage. We propose to bound the prediction error in stage I by applying acceleration clipping on the mouse motion. In stage II, we considered two situations – when the filter has converged and when it has not. When it has converged, we propose to estimate the error bounds by jittering the current internal state of the predictor. When it has not, which happens at the beginning of stage II as the motion model has just been constructed, the predicted results tend to fluctuate more significantly. We propose to reference the last predicted position to estimate the error bounds, which provides some information on the amount of fluctuation. In stage III, the motion becomes more stable and the model is typically more accurate. Hence, we may simply tighten the error bounds predicted at the end of stage II. Details are discussed in [Lau, Lee, and Wah, under preparation] submitted with this report. Finally, we have applied this idea on two applications. In multi-server load balancing, we investigated the error in the computed load balancing solutions due to network delay and how to compensate for it [Deng and Lau, 2012; Hu, Lau, and Wah, 2014; Deng and Lau, 2014]. In crowd motion prediction, we tried to predict the trajectories of multiple street pedestrians in videos in which the error bounds can be used to avoid collisions among them [Kim et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2015].

116010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
116010.value: Prediction techniques are now widely used in many applications. However, any delay between the availability of the measurement values and the incorporation of the prediction results may affect the performance of the application. This delay may be caused by network delay in the case of distributed applications and/or by processing delay in the case where the computation time for producing the predicted results is not neglectable. In this project, we have found that being able to estimate the prediction error is very important in many applications. We have investigated only two applications, one suffering from network latency and the other from processing delay. Both of them apply the error bounds to determine the prediction frequency so as to improve the performance. In fact, there is another type of applications which may use the estimated error bounds to trigger different actions. For example, in stock prediction, we may use the predicted error bounds to determine if we should perform the predicted buy/sell actions. If we find that the error bound of a particular prediction is too high, we may not execute the predicted buy/sell recommendation, and we only execute the recommendation when the error bound is small than a particular value. This can be an interesting application and worth further exploration as a future work.

116010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116010.value: In this project, we have considered the latency problem in the more demanding distributed interactive applications (DIAs). We have studied two types of applications, one due to network latency – multi-server load balancing and the other due to processing delay – crowd motion prediction. Our results show that the ability of being able to estimate the prediction accuracy can help improve the performance of the DIAs. With the Hong Kong Government’s initiative on the huge West Kowloon Cultural District project, the Hong Kong Government is trying to establish Hong Kong as a cultural, creativity and entertainment center. However, the success of the latter depends not only on being able to fund the constructions, but also on the development of the technological infrastructure to allow people from Hong Kong as well as around the world to share and distribute cultural activities, and to develop and participate in creativity and entertainments. Distributed interactive applications (DIAs), with success in many fields such as virtual museums, collaborative design and online games, provide a good Internet-based technological platform to support various cultural, creativity and entertainment activities. Our results from this project can be applied to enhance the performance of DIA servers, i.e., the infrastructure, and the user interactivity, i.e., the user experience.

117210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
117210.value: Although five-axis high speed machining (HSM) has been in existence for quite some time and has gained in popularity over the past decade, toolpath computation methods for five-axis HSM have not been well investigated. Apart from a very few new techniques, most methods provided by current commercial CAM systems are derived from and similar to their three-axis counterparts. To generate a toolpath for five-axis machining, the locus of the contact points between the cutter and the surface, the so-called cutter contact (CC) curve, and the orientation of the cutter at each point on the CC curve must be determined. For high-speed machining, the CC curves and the tool orientation must be designed so that when the cutter moves along at high speed, the dynamic constraints of the machine tool are not violated, otherwise the tool has to slow down, causing problems to the machine, the cutter and the machined part. Existing research tends to tackle the CC curve planning and tool orientation issues separately. The proposed project will adopt an integrated approach. Based on our previous research experience, we propose to investigate a surface partitioning method that splits the part surface into regions so that any abrupt change in tool orientation in a region is avoided. We will also investigate a new technique that generates a smooth spiral toolpath within each region so that abrupt changes in cutting direction do not occur. The generation of the spiral toolpath within a region requires the determination of the medial axis of the region. We will investigate a novel technique for the rapid computation of medial axes by utilizing the tremendous processing power of graphics processing units (GPUs). In our previous research, we developed a novel GPU-based method for boundary-conformed toolpath computation. Our recent preliminary investigation shows that it is feasible to rapidly determine the medial axes of 2D regions using a GPU. In the proposed project, further investigation will be conducted to extend this method to regions on 3D surfaces. All of the new techniques developed in the research will be integrated to form a new toolpath generation method that addresses the special requirement of five-axis HSM. This new method will enable five-axis HSM to realize its full capabilities in terms of machining speed and surface quality. The developed methodologies and algorithms will also benefit further research and development in toolpath computation and GPU programming. N/A

117310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
117310.value: Complex distributed parameter systems (DPS) widely exist in production industry. Except the complex spatio-temporal nature, the stronger nonlinearity will make the process dynamics change more significant between operating conditions than the traditional lumped parameter system. Since all the previously developed models work only at vicinity of the operating condition, tracking control between operating conditions will be more difficult. Furthermore, the final performance of the process, which is actually a complex function of process variables or other unknown factors, can not be measured directly. All these difficulties make the process monitoring nearly impossible. We aim to develop a novel spatio-temporal multi-models based process control and monitoring for the DPS, with application to the cure process. The model developed should be able to work in a wider range of operating conditions, so that the cure process can be globally simulated. First, the whole operating region will be divided into several small zones, upon which a spatio-temporal Wiener model is developed for the local modelling, and then integrated by the fuzzy system for a global model. Based on each spatio-temporal Wiener model, a low-order observer will be designed to estimate dominant states; then the observer-based local controller will be developed to stabilize the spatio-temporal process at each operating condition. These local controllers will be integrated by a T-S fuzzy system to maintain a satisfactory tracking performance in the whole operating region. Finally, a SPC-based expert system will be developed to work with the global fuzzy multi-models to on-line monitor performance variance and capture any quality drift caused by the fault or aging components during the production. 117310.label: Realisation of objectives
117310.value: The project has been successfully completed and achieved all the planned objectives. Objective 1 – Spatio-temporal fuzzy multi-models First, a time/space separation based modeling approach is developed for the nonlinear DPS at any operating condition. Then, the operating region can be classified into multiple operating conditions. Afterwards, multi-models approaches are developed in first time to work at larger working region. Different methods can be used for the multiple models integration. The methods have been successfully applied to cure oven and other thermal processes. Objective 2 – Multi-models based fuzzy control of DPS A neural observer based fuzzy control is designed for the parabolic DPS. The state observer will reduce the measurement requirement. Due to the spatiotemporal dynamics of the DPS, a set of spatial differential linear matrix inequalities (SDLMI) are designed in the first time for the stability analysis, which leads to a novel proportional spatial derivative (P-sD) control. Finally, the global performance can be achieved by the optimal fuzzy control under multiple objectives. Objective 3 – Process monitoring for quality First, a probabilistic fuzzy platform has been developed for performance modelling and monitoring. Then, different data based learning method can be used on this platform to extract the dominant features of the process. The developed probabilistic fuzzy system has been successfully applied to the prediction of the selected process.

117310.label: Major findings and research outcome
117310.value: 1）Process modeling A time/space-separation-based support-vector machine (SVM) modeling approach is developed for the nonlinear DPS [1], which integrates KL decomposition and the least-squares support vector-machine (LS-SVM) approach.The methods have been successfully applied to cure oven and other thermal processes. For the complex DPS, multi-models approaches are developed in first time based on the probabilistic PCA [17] or kernels [19]. These multi-models approaches can work for the complex DPS at larger working condition. 2）Process design A robust approach is developed under model uncertainty to design the complex process to be inherently good for dynamic performance [2]. Different probabilistic design methods are developed to minimize the model uncertainties [7, 9] when process data are available. Proper design of the process will help reducing the system complexity, and eventually improve the control performance. 3）Fuzzy control A neural observer based fuzzy control is designed for the parabolic DPS [4]. The stabilization condition is presented in terms of a set of spatial differential linear matrix inequalities (SDLMI) [3, 10], which is then solved recursively via the existing LMI optimization techniques. Furthermore, a novel proportional spatial derivative (P-sD) control is developed to control the spatially dynamic process [8]. This P-sD control is an equivalent PD control in the time domain. Further development has been applied for DPS with multiple objectives [20] and the nonlinear hyperbolic DPS [15]. For the real-world application, the output saturation is the bottle neck for implementation of advanced control methods. The saturation of fuzzy control has been studied, upon which a new tuning method has been developed to improve the robustness of fuzzy control [6]. 4）Process monitoring and prediction: A new configuration of the probabilistic fuzzy logic system has been developed for data modelling [12]. The fuzzy inference and probabilistic reasoning are integrated to speed up the computation. The novel design and tuning method is developed to fine-tune the parameters of the system. With the newly designed multi-period estimation window, the probabilistic fuzzy system is successfully applied to the wind speed prediction [18].

117310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
117310.value: There are still lots of room for developing multi-models based approaches for the complex process, particularly for spatiotemporal dynamic system. The recently new method “Deep Learning” would be a potential way to work with the traditional modeling technology to improve the spatiotemporal modeling. Control of spatiotemporal process is always a difficult task as there are limited measurement and actuation means. Reinforcement learning could be integrated for performance improvement in the time-varying environment.

117310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
117310.value: Complex distributed parameter systems (DPS) widely exist in the production industry. These processes are usually described by nonlinear partial differential equations with complex boundary conditions. The outputs of these processes not only vary with time but also vary at different spatial locations. Typical examples include curing ovens in semiconductor packaging plants, where material moving, gas flow and thermal heating interact together to form a nonlinear distributed temperature environment. The production quality relies heavily on the spatial temperature distribution profile that will vary significantly between operating conditions. Monitoring and control of these kinds of processes are not easy due to their infinite-dimensional nature and limited sensors used in the production. A good process monitoring and control has to rely on the effective process model. The strong nonlinearity in the process will make the model developed at one operating condition not working well at other operating conditions. It poses a great challenge to modelling and control of such processes. The research has produced novel results on modelling and tracking control of DPS using multi-models approach. It is the first time to develop multi-models based spatio-temporal modelling, fuzzy control and performance prediction for the DPS.

117510.label: Project Title(Chinese)
117510.value: 利用加入DLC桿的三維方法來改進納米複合硬塗層的摩擦和磨損性能

117510.label: Project Objectives
117510.value: To prepare nanocomposite coatings on steel and WC alloy substrates by using closed field unbalanced magnetron sputtering ion plating (CFUMSIP) technique. The coatings will be studied by a variety of characterization techniques such as XRD, XPS, TEM, nanoindentation, etc. To develop laser ablation technique to fabricate controlled micro-sized patterns on hard nanocomposite coatings at high efficiency and low cost. The effects of the size, shape, depth, and density of dimples on friction and wear properties will be correlated and optimized. Laser operating parameters are varied in order to obtain a surface with the best tribological performance. To deposit solid lubricant DLC film on the patterned hard coatings. The structure and mechanical properties of the DLC coatings prepared at different parameters will be characterized. In addition, guidelines will be developed for the design of the next generation of low friction surfaces. To evaluate the tribological property of hard nanocomposite coatings embedded with lubricating reservoirs by using high temperature pin-on-disk tribometer, scratch tester, and impact tester. The wear mechanism of the improved performance will be characterized and studied by different analytic techniques.

117510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
117510.value: 在現代工業中，納米複合硬塗層在機械加工中已顯示出重要的應用前景，可用於減小摩擦和磨損，延長工具的使用壽命。這樣，其現實意義不僅在於節約我們有限的能源，還能減少有害物質的排放對地球的影響，造福後代。然而，隨著加工水準的提高，例如低摩擦和高切削溫度，單相單層耐磨塗層很快就達到其性能極限。通常，使用多層膜或多相塗層能改善其耐磨特性。最近，在工程表面上進行鐳射式樣處理來改善摩擦和磨損引起了人們的極大興趣。高精度的准分子鐳射可用於納米複合硬塗層的後加工，減小其摩擦係數和降低切削溫度，而對原塗層的品質影響輕微。 本研究中，提出了一種三維方法來改善納米複合硬塗層的耐磨性能。首先，用高精度的准分子鐳射在納米塗層表面上垂直刻蝕出不同尺寸的微凹孔。然後，利用磁控濺射技術沉積類金剛石(DLC)固體潤滑塗層來填充這些凹孔。這樣，連續的納米複合硬塗層中將鑲嵌有很多DLC潤滑桿。在摩擦過程中，這些凹孔將作為DLC潤滑物的儲藏所，並收集在磨擦介面上產生的磨屑，從而降低磨損。這一綜合處理方法簡單而有效，原塗層的性能基本保持不變。本研究將探討鐳射刻蝕和DLC沉積條件對磨損特性的影響。通過優化工藝參數，使摩擦和磨損性能得到最大程度的改善，使之適用於高接觸應力，高速和高接觸溫度的場合。此外，作為一種可靠有效的表面處理方法，我們將研究其改善機理並開發在製造工程領域的應用。

117510.label: Realisation of objectives
117510.value: Objective 1 We have successfully prepared nanocomposite TiAlSiN onto steel and WC alloy substrates by using closed field unbalanced magnetron sputtering ion plating (CFUMSIP) technique. After the optimization process, it was found that the TiAlSiN coatings prepared at target currents of Ti = 6.0A; Al-Si = 1.5A; Al = 4.0A, and a bias voltage of -55V has the highest hardness. Such optimized TiAlSiN coating with 1.5 at.% Si and 9.0 at.% Al reached a maximum hardness of 35 GPa. The optimized TiAlSiN coating was confirmed to be a form of nanocomposite structure. Objective 2 Regular dimples have been successfully prepared on the TiAlSiN coatings with different dimple area densities, dimple diameters and dimple depths. The effect of dimple densities on the tribological properties of the TiAlSiN coatings has been revealed. Under the dry sliding conditions, the results showed that the TiAlSiN coating with dimple density of 10% has an obvious improvement on wear performance as compared to un-patterned surfaces. Objective 3 We have deposited lubricating DLC films into the dimpled TiAlSiN coatings. DLC films were prepared by CFUMSIP technique with different bias voltages (20 to 120 V). It was found that the DLC films prepared at high bias voltages had a higher hardness and a better penetration depth, but the adhesion was poorer. After the optimization process (based on penetration depth and wear performance), the bias voltage was selected to be 80V. In addition, DLC films can be effectively filled into the dimples only if the dimple diameter is ≥ 100 micron and dimple depth is ≤ 10 micron. Objective 4 Surface patterning followed with DLC deposition is an effective approach to improve the tribological behavior of hard nanocomposite coatings. The wear performance of the post-treated TiAlSiN coatings has been studied by using a reciprocating wear tester in dry condition. The results showed that the introduction of regular dimples and DLC film could lead to a significant improvement on the TiAlSiN coatings. The friction coefficient of the post-treated coatings could reach 0.1 and there is at least two orders of magnitude smaller than the TiAlSiN coating. The excellent tribological property can be explained by the formation of lubricating DLC layer and the formation of dimples that can act as lubricating reservoirs and trap wear debris to reduce wear due to third bodies trapped at the sliding interface.

117510.label: Major findings and research outcome
117510.value: 1) CFUMSIP technique was used to prepare the TiAlSiN coatings. It was found that the coatings prepared at target currents of Ti = 6.0 A; Al-Si = 1.5 A; Al = 4.0 A, and a bias voltage of -55 V has the highest hardness with nanocrystalline (Ti,Al)N grains surrounded by amorphous Si3N4 matrix. 2) Regular dimples were prepared on TiAlSiN coatings by a commercial Nd:YAG laser. The surface quality and the drilling efficiency are majorly governed pulse energy and number of pulse. After the optimization process based on the drilling efficiency and dimple quality, the pulse energy was set at 20-30 Jcm2 and the number of pulse at 30-35 pulse. 3) Lubricating DLC films were prepared onto the dimpled TiAlSiN coatings by CFUMSIP technique at different bias voltages (20 to 120 V). It was found that the hardness and the penetration depth of the DLC films increased with bias voltages. After the optimization process (based on penetration depth, hardness and wear performance), the bias voltage was selected to be 80V. 4) DLC films were prepared onto the dimpled TiAlSiN coatings with dimple diameters ranging from 40 to 300 micron. It was found that the TiAlSiN coatings with larger dimple diameter exhibited a thicker DLC film. 5) The tribolgical performance of the TiAlSiN coatings with surface patterning and DLC layer has been studied in dry condition against WC ball. The results showed that the introduction of dimples and DLC coating can lead to a significant improvement on wear performance of TiAlSiN coatings. The friction coefficient reaches 0.1 and there is at least two orders of magnitude smaller than the TiAlSiN coating. 6) The effect of dimple diameter on the wear performance of the TiAlSiN coatings with surface patterning and DLC film was evaluated. It was found that the TiAlSiN coating with 100 micron dimple diameter has the longest duration of low friction (at least two times longer than others). With respect to the wear volume, the TiAlSiN coating with 100 micron dimple diameter also exhibited the lowest wear width and depth, indicating the excellent wear resistance of the sample. 7) The speculation of the mechanical and tribolgical analyses of the TiAlSiN coatings showed that the excellent wear performance of the TiAlSiN coating with dimple diameter of 100 micron can be due to the formation of lubricating layer inside the dimples and the entrapment of wear debris

117510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
117510.value: It has been shown that the post-treatment of TiAlSiN with patterning and DLC deposition can significantly improve the wear performance of the TiAlSiN coatings. High speed cutting and dry machining processes are the main developing tendency in the modern manufacturing technology. It is believed that the drop of friction coefficient can facilitate chip removal, particularly in drilling without coolant participation. In addition, low friction coefficient can provide a better quality of machining products. Normally, the temperature raised at contact points can reach over 1000 oC. Although the thickness of the lubricating layer inside the dimples is just 0.5 micron, the influence of the layer on the cutting test is expected to be obvious. With improved wear life, there is no need to stop the machining operation for tool replacement, which in turn, reducing the machining down time. Particularly, the reduction of friction can provide a better quality of machining products. The improved properties would lead to a long-term significance of the nanocomposite coatings. This results in greater manufacturing reliability and productivity, as well as reduced costs and resource. Therefore, a detailed investigation of the TiAlSiN with surface dimples and DLC layer working in machining applications is highly valuable.

117510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
117510.value: Reducing friction, wear and lubricant are the main developing tendency in the modem manufacturing technology. In this work, we used an integrated approach to reduce the friction and wear of hard TiAlSiN coatings. First, dimples were introduced to TiAlSiN coating by a ND:YAG leaser. Secondly, lubricating DLC layer is prepared onto the dimpled surface. The results showed that a great improvement of wear performance was observed on the TiAlSiN coatings with the post-treatment processes. The TiAlSiN coating exhibited a friction coefficient of 0.5, whereas the friction coefficient of the post-treated TiAlSiN coating could reach 0.1. The specific wear rate of the post-treated TiAlSiN coatings was extremely low, which has at least two orders of magnitude smaller than the TiAlSiN coating. The excellent wear performance of the coating can be due to the formation of lubricating DLC layer inside the dimples and the effectiveness of entrapping of wear debris during the wear process. It is expected that the greatly enhanced wear property of the TiAlSiN coatings can expand the coating to be used in a wider range of modern industries where manufacturing reliability and productivity are important.

118610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118610.value: 為節省夏季空調能耗，全球性的趨勢是提高室溫。東亞各地政府紛紛提倡將室溫顯著提高。在此新條件下，常規的氣流組織方式難以適應新的挑戰—如何使用更少的能源來滿足熱舒適和室內空氣品質的要求。因此必須探索合適的氣流組織方式。層式通風，作為強調頭胸部高度（呼吸區）局部熱舒適和空氣品質的新方式，將為中、小型房間提供解決方案。除風口位置外，層式通風的設備與常規系統幾乎相同。風管將安裝在夾牆內而不是吊頂內或地板下。空調系統佔用的室內空間的體積變化不大。二〇〇五年以來進行的初步的實驗和使用者試驗顯示層式通風能夠同時顧及熱舒適、室內空氣品質和節能三方面的要求。在蘇黎世舉行的二〇〇九年通風會議（Ventilation 2009 Conference）的總結中，層式通風被列為兩項重要創新之一。但是，在基礎和應用層面上，還有很多地方需要認清，包括氣流組織特性，量化熱舒適和室內空氣品質效果，以便為其在建築上的應用制定設計導則。通過實驗研究（包括測量溫度、速度、二氧化碳濃度和使用者實驗）以及計算流體力學仿真，揭示該通風方式的性能特徵。 實驗研究將在我們的大型環境實驗室進行。辦公室、課室和商店的佈局都不難實現。關注局部熱工和氣流狀況的客觀量測和電腦仿真將會開展。針對不同佈局的使用者實驗也將進行。反映層式通風性能的簡化公式將被導出以應用於工程實踐。層式通風在設計、安裝和運行階段的能耗和成本將與常規通風方式進行比較，並徵詢本行業的建築師、設計工程師和供應商的意見。最終將推出一套適用於高溫空調的設計導則。總之，這個新的通風方式有以下幾方面的優點： 一.呼吸區的空氣品質不亞於常規方式； 二.在頭、胸高度的氣流為水平方向但不會導致吹風感風險； 三.夏季熱舒適需要的溫度分佈—工作區適度的逆溫度梯度得以實現； 四.風管和風口安裝安全方便； 五.高能效（比常規方式節能10%以上）。

118610.label: Realisation of objectives
118610.value: All six objectives have been achieved, specifically: 1. The effects of air temperature and air movement of stratum ventilation on thermal comfort and indoor air quality have been understood quantitatively; 2. The thermal neutral temperature over 27°C for 0.6-clo value and 1 met under cooling operation was confirmed by a large set of human subject test; 3. The layouts of air terminal (inlet and outlet) for optimal air distribution have been found; 4. The IAQ in the breathing zone of stratum ventilation has been quantitatively confirmed to be better than the conventional air distributions; 5. The year-round energy consumption of stratum ventilation were found to be substantially lower than the conventional methods; and 6. A set of design guidelines for stratum ventilation has been formulated.

118610.label: Major findings and research outcome
118610.value: Stratum ventilation, a new method emphasizing local thermal comfort and IAQ at the head-and-chest level (breathing zone), could be one of the solutions to the problem elevated room temperatures for smallto medium rooms. The Gaps between partitions, instead of the ceiling/underfloor voids, are most likely to house the air duct and plenums. The space used by the system is more or less the same. The experimental and human subject test results have been obtained, which shows that the new method is able to address thermal comfort, IAQ and energy saving simultaneously. The results have been reported in several refereed journal articles. This study characterizes the performance of the system through laboratory studies (mesurements of the temperature, velocity and CO2 concentration profiles and human subject tests for their perceptions of comfort and air quality) and though CFD simulations. The laboratory study was conducted in our large environmental chamber which allows the configurations of office, classroom and shop to be conveniently realized. Objective experimental measurements and computer simulations emphasizing local thermal and flow conditions were conducted. Human subject tests for different configurations were carried out. A simplified analytical method, the ADPI/EDT method, to predict the performance of stratum ventilation was developed to provide more information for practicing engineers. The advantages of the new method show in the following aspects: 1. IAQ in the breathing zone better than the conventional methods; 2. horizontal air movements at the head-and-chest level (the breathing zone); 3. desirable temperature pattern for thermal comfort in summer: modest and reversed temperature gradient in the occupied zone; 4. convenient installation of ducts and air terminals; and 5. energy efficiency (at least 20% saving based on conventional methods).

118610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118610.value: A thermal environment under stratum ventilation was thought to be non-uniform, but a recent finding suggests that the thermal environment provided by stratum ventilation is uniform. If this is confirmed, the knowledge on stratum ventilation will be fundamentally updated on the following two aspects: (1) the mechanism of thermal comfort under stratum ventilation; and (2) the methodology for stratum ventilation design. Further studies are therefore needed to characterize the thermal environment under stratum ventilation. The future tests should be carried out in the configurations of office, classroom and retail shop. Objective experiments and computer simulations on thermal and flow conditions should be conducted. Human subjective responses on the thermal sensation and comfort should also be collected. For the convenience of practicing engineers,relevant thermal environmental indices should be derived to suit the need for the design of stratum ventilation. Finally, an updated version of design guidelines for the application of stratum ventilation in Hong Kong should be developed.

118610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118610.value: Stratum ventilation, a new method emphasizing thermal comfort and IAQ at the head level, could be use at higher room temperatures for smallto medium rooms. The experimental and human subject test results obtained show that the new method is able to provide thermal comfort, indoor air quality and energy saving simultaneously. The results have been reported in several refereed journal articles. The laboratory study was conducted in our unique environmental chamber. Objective experimental measurements and computer simulations were conducted. A simplified analytical method to predict the performance of stratum ventilation was developed to provide more information for practicing engineers. The advantages of the new method show in the following aspects: 1. IAQ in the breathing zone better than the conventional methods; 2. horizontal air movements at the head level (the breathing zone); 3. desirable temperature pattern for thermal comfort in summer: modest and reversed temperature gradient in the occupied zone; 4. convenient installation of ducts and air terminals; and 5. energy efficiency (at least 20% saving based on conventional methods).

118810.label: Major findings and research outcome
118810.value: We developed an heterogeneous multi-task learning framework in the principles of the proposed random-sets-based higher-order hidden Markov model (RS-HO-HMM) for human pose estimation from monocular image with deep convolutional neural network. We showed that including the body-part detection task helps to regularize the model so to converge to a good solution. We empirically demonstrated that the learned neurons in the middle layer of our RS-HO-HMM network were able tuned to localized body parts which is significant in that we can use this approach to modeling finer features, such as facial expressions and hand movements. Based on the RS-HO-HMM representation for video sequences, we developed novel type-2 fuzzy models to recognize human actions. In traditional models for visual recognition, each video sequence is modeled as a “document” composed of spatial-temporal interest points called visual words. Our method make it possible to convert so video sequence into a mixture of action topics for recognition. Our used type-2 fuzzy sets and MFR to encode the higher-order uncertainties, so to measure the degree of uncertainty that the visual data belongs to specific actions. Experiment results on widely available data sets, such KTH, Weizmann, UCF and Hollywood2 human action data sets confirmed that our approach outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches for human action recognition. As human motions naturally tell stories which play an essential role in communication and social interaction, it is interesting to investigate models such as RS-HO-HMM, the Gibbs energy minimization, and MRF for story. We successfully developed a story co-segmentation approach to automatically extracting stories from multiple Chinese broadcast news documents. Unlike visual tracking and detection, our approach needs not the guidance of well-trained models and can consistently segment the common stories from input data. Following the MRF and RS-HO-HMM scheme, we constructed a Gibbs energy function that balances semantic dependencies, and solved story co-segmentation. Extensive experiments based on benchmark dataset validated the effectiveness of our story co-segmentation approach. In addition, we demonstrated the superior performance to other major the state-of-the-art in story co-segmentation.

118810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118810.value: Since this technique is scalable, flexible and robust and potentially intelligent, my next R&D move will be to develop applications that may be used in mobile applications and benefit average users, commerce, and even government agencies.

118810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118810.value: Human motion and facial expression are essential in communication and social activities. This project uses the theories from the Bayesian probabilistic family to develop techniques for human motion modeling, analysis and synthesis. This will help us develop systems that are intelligent, scalable, flexible and feasible for average users on basic digital devices, specifically, ubiquitous mobile devices so that they may take the advantage of the cloud computing and big-data. For instance, with 4G LTE technology, almost everyone is now online 24/7 (almost), communication has become mostly visual (videos, pictures, emotIcons) with automated motion modeling and synthesis, it is possible to make social interaction more engaging and entertaining, e.g., generating--on the fly and real time--a facial expression animation that synchronizes with the user facial expression, etc. In addition, thanks to its scalability and intelligence (as it can readily generate semantics from data), we can develop systems for online commerce (online shopping) and even government agencies, for security, for example.

119610.value: To research key techniques for rapid localization of near-duplicate clips among a large set of videos. Algorithms for efficient indexing and search of partial near-duplicates will be developed, by jointly considering audio-visual similarity, spatial coherency and temporal consistency. To develop techniques for tracing the migration of a search topic in terms of the changes in meaning, context and perspective. Towards this goal, three tasks will be studied: identification of key near-duplicate clips as the iconic representation of a topic; context enrichment of iconic clips by information propagation; presentation of near-duplicate icons according to the meaning, context and perspective. To research techniques for effective threading of videos, generation and visualization of topic structure to describe narrative themes of a topic. To achieve this goal, two tasks will be investigated: detection of burst events by time-frequency analysis; semantic threading of videos based on partial near-duplicates, multi-modality analysis and external knowledge.

119610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
119610.value: With massive amount of videos available on web, commercial search engines use to return a long list of hundreds or even thousands of videos in response to a query topic. These videos are sorted according to relevance and then presented to users. As a consequence, users often need to painstakingly explore the search list for a gist of the search results, and are subjected to repeatedly watching similar clips which has been viewed previously. This eventually brings out the research challenges of large-scale video browsing and search exploration: (1) How to efficiently browse hundreds or even thousands of videos at a glance? (2) How to navigate videos and efficiently locate the events of interest under a topic? This project addresses the aforementioned challenges from three aspects. First, we consider the unique role of partial near-duplicates (PNDs) in bridging videos. PNDs are similar clips that are manipulated and inserted into videos for serving different purposes. Different from full near-duplicates, mining PNDs requires temporal localization of clips and scalability can become a big problem with huge volume of videos. Our proposed solution for this problem is based upon the search of minimal yet informative local features for scalable indexing. Rapid localization of PNDs by accounting temporal and geometric consistency checking is also addressed. Second, drawn upon the manipulation clues of PNDs, we propose the possible solution of mining iconic clips and their time stamps. The iconic clips, with proper chaining and visualization interface, are expected to provide an overview of search results in terms of topic evolution, and changes of context and perspective. Third, we consider a more granular level of browsing by building topic structures based on burst event detection and topic threading. Clues from PNDs, analysis from multi-modality processing, and knowledge from external sources will be jointly exploited for this task. In addition, visualization techniques which allow efficient navigation of topic structures for search exploration will be researched. The significance of this project is twofold. First, we address the timely issue and challenge of scalable video browsing, which is still a relatively new research topic since the proliferation of social media. Second, we investigate large-scale mining of near-duplicates, which is a hot research topic along the development of Web-2.0. Different from most existing researches which employ full near-duplicates for search diversification, we address the localization of partial near-duplicates in large-scale and the exploitation of PNDs for topical video browsing. 由于网络上存在大量的视频，商用搜索引擎对于用户查询的响应通常是返回一个包含成百上千个视频的列表。 这些视频是按照相关度进行排序之后呈现给用户的。为了得到关于搜索主题的梗概，用户通常需要费力的在返回的搜索结果中查找。另外，网络中大量相似视频的存在使得用户常会碰到之前已浏览过的视频。这就给研究大规模视频浏览和搜索结果挖掘带来了以下的挑战：（1）如何迅速有效的浏览几百甚至几千的视频？（2）如何组织视频以及快速有效的定位出特定主题下的感兴趣事件？ 本项目将在三个方面加以解决。第一，我们考虑了部分近似视频（partial near-duplicates：PNDs）在视频归纳中的特殊作用。PNDs是指为了特殊目的而插入到其他视频中的被处理过的相似视频片段。和完全相似视频不同，挖掘PNDs需要得到视频片段在视频中的时间位置；同时对于大量的视频，可扩展性是个重要的问题。我们提出的方法是基于寻找最小并且有信息量的局部特征来生成可扩展性好的索引。同时强调了通过统计时间和几何连续性验证来快速定位PNDs。第二，依据搜索到的PNDs所提供的线索，我们提出了针对如何挖掘图标片段及其时间戳的可能性方案。通过适当的链接和可视化界面的构建，这些片段可以提供对于搜索结果的梗概，概括出所要搜索主题的演进、上下文和观点变化。第三，基于热点事件的检测和主题趋势的挖掘，通过构造出主题的结构从而实现更加精细的浏览。为了达到这个目的，我们综合考虑了通过多模型处理得到的PNDs的线索，以及外部资源提供的知识。另外，我们还将对可视化技术进行研究，从而可以有效的组织和浏览主题的结构。 本工程的重要性包括以下两个方面。 第一，强调了时间问题以及可扩展性视频浏览带来的挑战。由于多媒体数量的迅速增加，可扩展性将是一个新的研究课题。第二，随着Web-2.0技术的发展，我们针对大规模近似视频挖掘进行了研究。这也是一个比较热点的研究课题。不同于已有的基于完全近似视频的检索结果多样化研究，我们强调了大规模情况下部分近似视频的定位和PNDs的挖掘在主题视频浏览中的作用。

119610.label: Realisation of objectives
119610.value: The project was divided into three phrases inline with the three objectives: partial-duplicate mining (objective-1), extraction and presentation of iconic clips (objective-2), and topic threading and structuring (objective-3). In phase-1, a system (VIREO-VH) for scalable localization of partial-duplicate segments in large video collection was developed. The framework is composed of three major components: feature extraction, near-duplicate detection and partial-duplicate video alignment. The videos are represented using a one million visual vocabulary and indexed with inverted file. For a video collection of 1 million keyframes, the current system consumes 30G bytes of main memory, answers a search query in less than 1 second, and completes the mining in about 250 hours. The current system is still relying on visual analysis. Audio information is found to be less useful mainly due to the low quality audio signal in Internet videos. The audio signals in our datasets are mostly speeches, which do not actually complement visual information much. In phase-2, iconic clips of different news topics were extracted and hyperlinked with information propagated from external knowledge sources, including wiki timeline, Google trends and news, Bing news and video search logs. Different interfaces, including galaxy and celebrity browsers, were developed to visualize the evolution of milestone events from different perspectives. The key problem of this phase is on aligning heterogeneous information extracted from videos and external sources. In galaxy browser, the problem is formulated as an optimization algorithm. A four-layer bipartite graph is established, and the alignment is efficiently solved via a network flow algorithm. In celebrity browser, because query logs for news and video search engines are available, the problem is reformulated as reinforcement learning. A three-layer bipartite graph composed of clicked histories of news articles and Web videos is constructed, and iconic clips are identified by iterative propagation of information from news clicks to video clicks, and vice versa. Finally in phase-3, an efficient algorithm was developed on placing videos into topic hierarchy constructed based on Wikipedia. The main issue is on the mapping of videos into events of different granularities under a hierarchy. Three criterions (relevancy, diversity and uniqueness) are defined for characterizing browsing efficiency. A multi-criterion optimization algorithm was proposed and a greedy version of it was implemented. The effectiveness of this algorithm under the scenario of frequent hierarchy update was investigated. A hierarchical browser was also developed for subjective studies and comparison with different browsers developed under this project.
