119610.label: Major findings and research outcome
119610.value: Under this project, a system (VIRE-VH) for large-scale mining of partial-duplicate video segments was developed [MM 2012]. Algorithms for hyperlinking of videos and external sources were also researched, resulting in different novel interfaces for topical browsing of Internet videos [MM 2011, TOMCCAP 2013, ICMR 2014]. VIREO-VH: Developed with distributed indexing and multi-threaded programming, the system allows scalable video threading. The software, available at http://vireo.cs.cityu.edu.hk/VIREO-VH/, was recently featured by ACM SIGMM Record (http://records.sigmm.ndlab.net/2014/01/vireo-vh-libraries-and-tools-for-threading-and-visualizing-a-large-video-collection/). The software forms the foundations for several video browsers developed under this project, and leads to several research outputs. These include the proposal of dominant curl computation [TIP 2013] for flip-invariant feature extraction and visual word collocation [TIP 2014] for contextual consistency modeling. Both works focus on leveraging of stable features, improving not only retrieval effectiveness but also the online search speed. Galaxy browser: The underlying technique is to mine iconic clips while linking to external knowledge [MM 2011]. Both spatial and temporal hyperlinking methods were studied, where the former links iconic clips with sentence snippets extracted from Wikipedia pages, while the latter chronologically orders iconic clips by aligning to Wiki timelines. Galaxy browser integrates both linking methods, and supports explorative search by showing how videos are inter-related and augmenting them with contextual information from external sources. The user studies indicated that galaxy browser is significantly better than traditional video browsers such as static storyboard and video skimming in terms of browsing efficiency. Hierarchical browser: Assigning videos to a semantic hierarchy is challenging due to the variability of video content and complexity of topic. The three criteria defined in [TOMCCAP 2013] address this problem by balancing the tradeoff between relevancy and redundancy when placing videos. In a user study conducted to compare different browsers, the subjects using hierarchical browser achieved the best performance by finding the most number of video answers with the minimum error rate and search time. The result is significantly better than using galaxy browser. Celebrity browser: Celebrity search occupies around 10% of Internet traffic. Reinforcement learning was studied for mining iconic videos from the news and video search logs provided by Bing [ICMR 2014]. The algorithm successfully extracted the milestone events and videos for 38 celebrities from query click-through of 6-month durations. A browser was developed on Windows Phone 8 to visualize the results for multi-perspective information access. The browser received the highest rating in a user study to compare different systems for celebrity browsing.

119610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
119610.value: The current works can be extended in the following two directions, which are related to Big Data research. Object-level search and hyperlinking: The project considers threading of videos at the frame-level. The work done can naturally be extended for object-level or instance-level mining for applications such as search of objects and discovery of trendy patterns, which are becoming hot research topics in social media. Nevertheless, object-level analysis is challenging due to non-planar and non-rigid motions of objects in 3D space, resulting in large variability in visual appearance. Future research can focus on exploring spatial layout of local features for more robust representation and efficient mining. Dynamic versus static video corpus: The project assumes static video corpus, and hence the mining results only support retrospective view of topic migration. In order to deal with streaming videos and develop browser that reacts to topic evolution, the developed techniques in this project need to be further extended for incremental and real-time mining. To achieve this goal, the speed of visual feature extraction has to be accelerated to cope with large volume of incoming data. Issues on online topic monitoring, such as the detection of emergence events by micro-blog data, are also worth researching.

119610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
119610.value: The project addresses the issues on efficient browsing of large collection of Internet videos beyond list-wise presentation of search results. The focus is on researching techniques for mining partial near-duplicate video content, and developing video browsers, which hyperlink iconic clips with rich online information, for efficient search navigation. The project has succeeded in developing a scalable system framework, which encompasses techniques in video indexing, spatial geometric verification and temporal video alignment, for partial-duplicate mining in video collection as large as several thousands of videos. Based upon the system, techniques in cross-media and cross-source hyperlinking are investigated for topical video browsing. First, a network flow algorithm, which links heterogeneous information among news, timelines and videos, was developed for galaxy browser. Second, a multi-criteria optimization algorithm, which takes into account three criteria (relevancy, diversity, uniqueness) for optimal assigning of videos to semantic hierarchy, was proposed for hierarchy browser. Third, a reinforcement learning technique was studied for celebrity browser, through mining iconic clips from news and video search logs provided by Bing search engines. Positive feedbacks, in terms of browsing efficiency and user search experience, were obtained in user studies when comparing the developed browsers to traditional video browsers and commercial systems.

120310.label: Project Title(Chinese)
120310.value: 應用機器人及光鎳技術實現生物細胞的微操作

120310.label: Co - Investigator(s)
120310.value: Prof Cheng, Shuk Han Prof Leung, Anskar Yu Hung

120310.label: Project Objectives
120310.value: Develop mechanical cell membrane models through optical stretching for cell property characterization. A mechanical model of cell membrane determined through stretching using optical tweezers will be developed based on membrane theory, utilizing nonlinear elastic material models to describe deformation behaviors of the cell membranes. The modeling approach will be used to interpret mechanical responses of biological cells and thus characterize the cell properties. An example application to be conducted in this project will be characterizing mechanical properties of human blood cells in different osmotic (chemical concentration) conditions, which can be applied to medical applications such as identification of diseased (cancer) cells. Investigate cell trapping strategy. A sophisticated model for the mechanism by which cells are trapped in a dynamic environment will be developed, with a particular focus on the relationship amongst the trapping force, cell motion speed, laser power and cell dragging force. A fundamental understanding of this relationship will lead to more effective cell trapping strategy. Our contribution in this area will be the development of a cell trapping strategy by considering the dynamics of the trapped cell in motion under varying cell velocity conditions while incorporating environmental influences in the trapping force analysis. Importantly, this research will help us to model how the trapping force varies as a function of the deviation of the trapped cell from the geometric center of the trap, and how the motion planning affects this position deviation under different laser power inputs. Transport swarms of cells with path generation and network control technologies. Moving multiple cells simultaneously and precisely is a challenging manipulation task, but has great potential to improve experimental techniques, since researchers currently work with a group of cells or even an organ. We will first develop a path generation methodology for transporting groups of cells incorporating cell collision avoidance techniques, so as not to disturb the cell group once in motion. Then, we will develop a synchronization network control technology to control multiple optical traps to move the cells while maintaining the required positional relation amongst the traps/cells, e.g., transporting a relatively large biological cell (i.e., eukaryotic cell) or a cell group which must maintain a pattern when moving (i.e. tunneling nanotubes cells [1]). Perform bio-medical applications. Important biomedical applications, made possible with the proposed work, will be conducted by Drs. Leung and Cheng in collaboration with the PI. These include: (i) Characterization of cancer and stem cells properties, utilizing blood-derived cells or cell lines which have had extra-chromosomal DNA molecule (plasmid) such as GFP (green fluorescent proteins), added to the nucleus (transfected). (ii) Harvesting and sorting cells with green fluorescence from a group of cells. (iii) Studying behavior of phenomenon in which bodily cells, bacteria, and other single-cell or multicellular organisms direct their movements (chemotaxis) and cell-to-cell communication through moving cells.

120310.label: Major findings and research outcome
120310.value: 1. Cell mechanical model We have investigated cell mechanical model through stretching cells with optical tweezers. The cell membrane mechanical model was utilized. We particularly examined the dynamic and static micromechanical properties of hESC and hESC-CM, with both modeling and experimental information. We further developed a new actin cytoskeleton microstructural model based on the semiflexible polymer nature of the actin filament. The relationship between the stretching force and the mechanical properties of cells was examined. Experiments on deforming hematopoietic cells with distinct primitiveness from normal and leukemic sources were conducted via optical tweezer manipulation at single-cell level. The cell modeling research has laid a solid ground for our further research on probing cell functional mechanism and controlling cell biological behaviors. 2. Cell transportation control We developed a robot-tweezers manipulation tool for automatic transportation of biological cells. The dynamics equation of the cell in an optical trap was analyzed. Closed-loop controllers were designed for positioning single cells as well as multiple cells. A synchronization control technology was designed for multicell transportation with maintained cell pattern. Experiments were performed on transporting live cells to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. We further proposed the use of coalition concept to optimize the cell trapping strategy by modeling the cell–optical connection as a coalition. Finally, an automated tool technology for handling batched cells was developed, which could facilitate us to conduct complex cell manipulations process that includes recognition, isolation, assembly, transportation, and deposition of the interesting cells. 3. Biomedical applications We have performed numerous biomedical application with the developed cell manipulation technology with optical tweezers, which include: 1) Cell fusion: We report a study on the laser-induced fusion of hESCs at the single-cell level. Cells were manipulated by optical tweezers and fused under irradiation with pulsed UV laser at 355 nm. Successful fusion of hESCs with somatic cells was also demonstrated. The reported fusion outcome may facilitate studies of cell differentiation, maturation, and reprogramming. 2) Cell-to-cell interaction: We also applied the optical tweezers based cell manipulation to cell-to-cell interaction study. We manipulated adhesions between leukemia cancer cells and stromal cells with optical tweezers, and characterized the adhesion properties, where fluorescence intensity was used as a label to study the Wnt signaling pathway of leukemia cells. The approach verified that the optical tweezers based cell manipulation approach can offer new avenues to investigate otherwise inaccessible mechanisms in cell-to-cell interactions.

120310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
120310.value: Further development of the research will be a Cell Bio-Probe that integrates robotics, optical tweezers, and microfluidics based on micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS) and nanotechnology. The Cell Bio-Probe will include optical manipulation tools that can enable several key manipulation tasks, such as: cell stretching, cell adhesion, and cell transportation. The robotically controlled system will allow either a single cell, or simultaneously many cells to be tested and probed. This will enable the key cell properties to be characterized over a population of cells, further refining our understanding of cell properties. The Cell Bio-Probe will be used to probe the mechanism of cells from the perspectives of: i) characterizing the mechanobiological properties of cells with reference to its link to abnormal differentiation; ii) investigating the molecular mechanism that regulates cell-to-cell interactions; iii) studying the cell migration mechanism.

120310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
120310.value: In this project, we have integrated robotics and optical tweezers technologies to achieve advanced manipulation and characterization of biological cells. Robotics is a promising technology in control and visual processing for object manipulation. Optical tweezers utilizes low power laser beams to trap and manipulate particles and biological cells in the micro and nanometer scales. The combination of both robotics and optical tweezers technologies can open up a new dimension of cellular biology with significant impact on both clinical and biological science. With the robot-tweezers manipulation tool, we have carried out research in four perspectives. First, we developed a cell mechanical model under optically induced mechanical cell stretching, which can be used for cell property characterization. Second, we investigated cell trapping strategies by considering the dynamics of the trapped cell. Third, we extended the networked multi-agent path generation and control technologies to multi-cell transportation. A synchronization control approach was proposed to transport multiple cells while maintaining required formation shape amongst the cells. Finally, we applied the above developed manipulation technologies to numerous bio-medical applications such as cell fusion and cell-to-cell interactions. The ability to manipulate cells with high precision and throughput is an essential component of such new techniques.

120610.label: Project Objectives
120610.value: Design and fabricate small tools for Erf. Understand how process parameters and tool parameters affect the material removal and develop models of the material removal function. Identify ways to use the tools to polish small surfaces uniformly and demonstrate polishing automation.

120610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
120610.value: Small aspheric and complex optical mirrors/lenses are facing an increasing demand in the fields of opto-electronics, communication, project and display systems, life science and automotive applications, etc. Some stringent applications call for the surface roughness of those surfaces to be as low as a few nm. Conventional polishing methods are not suitable due to problems in tool miniaturization and tool wear. This research aims to develop a novel polishing process for polishing small complex optical surfaces based on electrorheological finishing. Tool / spindle systems will be designed, fabricated and evaluated. Process modeling and strategies for using the developed process for polishing will also be addressed. 小口径非球面型及复杂型光学反射镜/透镜应用于光电、通信、投影和显示系统、生命科学和汽车领域中的需求日益增加。对于一些较特殊的使用中甚至要求元件表面粗糙度小于几个纳米，传统的抛光方法不适于解决工具小型化和工具磨损的问题。 本研究基于电流变抛光技术，致力于开发一种新型的抛光工艺用于抛光小型复杂光学表面，将进行工具轴系统的设计、装配及评估，对抛光工艺建模与分析也将深入开展。

120610.label: Realisation of objectives
120610.value: (1) Previous Er polishing tools made use of the work surface as one of the electrodes. In the current research, both the anode and cathode were integrated into the tool. This enabled the use of Erf in the polishing of both conducting and non-conducting surfaces. The tools should be compact to allow the use of Erf in small components. Yet, anode and cathode should be well isolated as the supply voltage in Erf is high. Tool development involved mechanical design, selection of materials, fabrication and testing. Finite element analysis was employed to evaluate the E-field in the vicinity of the tool tip. Two polishing tools were developed and tested. The first one was a pin-type polishing tool with the spindle shaft as the cathode and a concentric hallow shaft as the anode. For further improvement of the removal rate, a wheel-type polishing tool was also developed. The design adopted two wheel shaped electrodes fixed to the spindle shaft which allowed the linear speed of Er fluid to be substantially increased during polishing. Polishing was successfully demonstrated with both designs. Experiments with glass specimens showed reduction of surface roughness to below 3nm. (2) Parametric studies of Erf removal characteristics were done based on the developed polishing tools. Parameters investigated included the supply voltage, working distance and the tool speed. Knowledge of factors affecting the feasible range of these parameters were established. Effects of these parameters on the removal rate were identified. (3) Feasibility of using the developed tool for polishing was demonstrated experimentally. Tool impression on flat specimens were established. A trough was produced on a flat glass specimen when the tool was passed slowly over the surface. In addition, an attempt was made to plan tool dwell / tool path to suppress edge effects associated with polishing.

120610.label: Major findings and research outcome
120610.value: Effects of the fluid composition on Erf were experimentally studied [1]. Experiments showed that among the candidates considered, the highest shear stress was realized using starch as the dispersed phase with silicon oil as the continuous phase. After fine tuning, the composition of 47.62% starch, 47.62% silicone oil and 4.76% ceria was found most effective for Erf. A pin-type tool with integrated-electrodes was developed [2]. The spindle was the cathode and a concentric tube was the anode. E-field was concentrated at the tip of the spindle which extended beyond the tube. A prototype was fabricated and tested on K9 glass. At supply voltage of 3000V, spindle speed of 1500 rpm and working distance of 0.5mm, the surface Ra was reduced from 8.46 to 2.53nm after 30min polishing. Parametric study of Erf was done with the pin-type tool [4]. The field strength was found to vary monotonically with the supply voltage between 1500-3000V. The field strength also decreased rapidly away from the tool tip. At 2000V supply voltage and 0.5 mm working distance, the PV of the specimen was reduced from 59 to 25nm. The achieved surface roughness did not seem to vary with the supply voltage. However, the roughness reduction rate did increase with the supply voltage. A wheel-type tool for Erf was developed for removal rate enhancement [5]. The wheel-shaped anode and cathode were fixed to the motor shaft. Voltage was passed to the anode through a slip-ring. The cathode was earthed through the shaft. Parametric study was conducted by varying the supply voltage (max 4500v), operating distance (max 1mm) and the wheel speed (max 1800 rpm). The removal rate was found to increase with the supply voltage and decrease with the working distance. However, it increased / decreased with the wheel speed when the speed was low / high. The Ra achieved was 0.002 lamda . Work was done to suppress edge effects in polishing through surface error map extension [3]. Here, 4 error map extension algorithms for error map construction were investigated. The construction assumed the tool path was extended to cover a region extended by half the tool width beyond the edge of the surface. Among the algorithms, neighborhood extension was shown to be superior through simulations. Polishing experiments were done to confirm the efficacy of the algorithm.

120610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
120610.value: Future research can be done to increase the removal rate. Analysis shows that the strength of E-field increases rapidly if the working distance is reduced. Thus, if the polishing system (including the Er fluid) can be tuned to enable Erf with shorter working distance, it may be possible to increase the polishing rate. Secondly, it was found that, due to centrifugal force, speed of the Er fluid at the work surface may be slower than that at the wheel surface when the wheel speed is high, leading to reduction in the removal efficiency. It may be possible that the wheel surface can be suitably textured to promote the flow of the fluid so that the speed of the fluid at the work surface can follow the wheel speed more closely at high speed. A potential use of Erf is in the finishing of small components. Future work needs to be done to investigate edge effects associated with finishing small components using Erf. Knowledge of the process characteristics and ways to suppress edge effects need to be further developed.

120610.value: Small aspheric and complex optical mirrors/lenses are facing an increasing demand in the fields of opto-electronics, communications, project and display systems, life science and automotive applications, etc. Some stringent applications call for the surface roughness of those surfaces to be as low as a few nm. Conventional polishing methods are not suitable due to problems in tool miniaturization and tool wear. This research aims to develop a novel polishing process for polishing small complex optical surfaces based on electrorheological finishing. Pin-type and wheel-type tools have been developed. They can be used to polish both conducting and non-conducting surfaces, as both anode and cathode are integrated into the tools. Process investigations were done through finite element analysis as well as experiment based parametric studies. The use of the tools for millimeter scale finishing was demonstrated and nanometer level surface roughness was achieved.

121410.label: Realisation of objectives
121410.value: The first objective was well achieved. We developed a random-effects Wiener process model to characterized observed degradation signal. We also adopted Bayesian approach to account for possible uncertainties and developed an online filtering algorithm to jointly estimate the distribution of the degradation rate and the underlying degradation levels. The second objective was also fullfilled. We developed algorithms and procedures to automate computer models calibration using stochastic approximation. We further considered the calibration parameter uncertainty and proposed an approach to quantify it using asymptotic approximations. The third objective was well achieved. We developed surveillance strategy with consideration of (1) population trend, (2) change magnitude, (3) change coverage, and (4) change time. We also evaluated and compared various monitoring methods for temporal, spatial and spatiotemporal surveillance situations. Methods based on likelihood ratio statistics and methods based on exponentially weighted moving average were both studied. Lastly, the fourth objective is also achieved. We used real examples and cases for testing and evaluation that include application to health surveillance, such as detecting counties with large number of male thyroid cancer incidents in New Mexico; condition monitoring of units with heterogeneous degradation rates and imperfect inspections, anomaly detection and failure prediction of hard disk drives, remaining useful life prediction for Lithium-ion battery, bearing diagnostics with the concurrent occurrence of multiple defect types. Monte Carlo simulations were also used for more structured evaluation of different situations.

121410.label: Major findings and research outcome
121410.value: A random-effects Wiener process model with measurement errors was developed to characterize the observed degradation signals over time. To account for possible uncertainties, a Bayesian approach was adopted to impose a prior distribution on the degradation rates. An online filtering algorithm was developed to jointly estimate the distribution of the degradation rate and the underlying degradation levels [Ye et al. 2015]. An effective and efficient algorithm based on the stochastic approximation (SA) approach was proposed to automate calibration of computer models. We further considered the calibration parameter uncertainty in the subsequent application of the calibrated model and proposed an approach to quantify it using asymptotic approximations [Yuan et al. 2013]. For the advancement of surveillance methods, we extended the CUSUM and Shiryayev–Roberts temporal surveillance procedures to spatial and spatiotemporal [Tsui et al. 2012]. We developed an SLR test for practical use without prior knowledge about incidence rates or under inhomogeneous population sizes [Shu et al. 2012]. We proposed an algorithm based on piecewise collocation to provide robust approximation of the run-length distribution, especially suitable for heavily-skewed process distribution [Huang et al. 2013]. We recommended a probabilistic measure for design and evaluation of CUSUM in health care surveillance when population size changes over time, after a thorough comparison of evaluation metrics [Jiang et al. 2013]. We evaluated performances of spatiotemporal surveillance methods for detecting rate changes of Poisson data considering non-homogenous population sample size. We concluded that changes associated with a small population favored the WLR approach, but those associated with a large population favor the GLR [Han et al. 2014]. An adaptive CUSUM was developed for monitoring drifts in Poisson rates with unknown parameter [He et al. 2014]. EWMA-type methods for surveillance provide an ongoing estimate of the incidence rate. We adopted an adaptive EWMA (AEWMA) scheme for linear drifts in process means instead of step changes [Su.et al. 2011]. The AEWMA method, capable of dynamically updating its smoothing parameter, was found to provide an overall good detection performance when shifts occur at both the first time point and a later time point, after an extensive comparison using the simulated population size and count [Shu et al. 2014]. We also proposed a spatial-EWMA approach that can detect spatial clustering with mean shifts [Lin et al. 2014]. We also proposed methods for various case studies mentioned in Section 5.3 [Wang et al. 2014, Ng et al. 2014a-b].

121410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
121410.value: Two-side surveillance methods can be extended to one-side detection [Su et al. 2011]. Changes in other parameters e.g. from linear drifts in process mean to process variance [Su et al. 2011]; from scale parameter to shape parameter [Huang et al. 2013] can be considered. Methods can be used with other distance measures [Tsui et al. 2012]; other distributions [Tsui et al. 2012, Huang et al. 2013]; other statistics [Shu et al. 2012]; other applications [Wang et al. 2014, Ng et al. 2014b]. We provided recommendation to advance the current methods using more general assumptions [Tsui et al. 2012, Jiang et al. 2013, Lin et al. 2014, Han et al. 2014] and more practical situations e.g. calibration with non-unique parameters [Yuan et al. 2013]; varying operation conditions [Ng et al. 2014a]; nonlinear function [Ye et al. 2015]. Other potneital studies include carrying out a better baseline estimation [Shu et al. 2014, Han et al. 2014] and uncertainty quantification in model parameterization [Ye et al. 2015]. Developing robust surveillance methods that are insensitive to population growth but still sensitive in detecting changes in incidence rate is also important [Jiang et al. 2013, Han et al. 2014].

121410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
121410.value: Computer experiments play a very important role in engineering and science research and have received a lot of attention from industries and research institutes. While the developed methods and results have been shown to be very powerful and promising in many applications, they are largely limited to computer models with single uni-variate output. This research successfully developed systematic modeling approaches that helps computer model developer and users (designers and scientists) to understand the impact and importance of validating the adequacy of functional computer models, and to model and monitor functional computer experiments. We have developed interpretable and accurate meta-models that combine functional physical experiments and computer model output together, computer model validation metrics and procedures that allow model develops to assess the prediction capability and allow designers to optimize engineering designs, surveillance strategies for monitoring the adequacy and accuracy of functional computer models dynamically, and provided practical solutions for model developers, scientists, and engineering designers. By utilizing complex computer models, use of computer experiments has opened a new avenue towards a better understanding of systems or phenomena that are difficult to carry out physically.

122710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
122710.value: 節能与低碳排放已成為當今全球關注的熱點。实现该目标的途径之一便是开展潤滑理論研究，改善機器的工作效率，这是目前摩擦学研究人員的重要工作内容。兩年前，我們开始了彈流條件下固-液界面的滑移的测量研究，這是一个众多研究者尚未探索的领域。合理解釋彈流接觸區的界面滑移，不僅對摩擦學基礎研究有重要意義，而且對實際工程中機械零部件，如軸承、齒輪等實現更好的潤滑从而实现能量的节省有著重要影響。最近，我們已經開發出一種新的實驗技術，可以成功地测量表征滑移程度的重要參數─滑移長度。該新方法是第一次被提出，而且是迄今為止能夠在彈流接觸區测量界面滑移的唯一方法。 但是，由於受當前實驗裝置的限制，测量僅限於低速條件，所得剪應變率也小於1 s-1 。滑移長度对剪應變率的依赖关系一直是一个悬而未决的问题，解決該問題唯一辦法是擴展剪應變率的測量範圍，獲取更大範圍的測量數據。在此基礎建立一個考慮多因素的彈流條件下的滑移模型。 那麼，我們要怎樣開展這項研究呢？在試驗方面， (i) 採用高速攝像機，將目前的滑動速度提升3個數量級，則剪應變率增加到103 s-1; (ii)通过往複運動提高滑移長度的測量精度；(iii) 通過適當地調節實驗裝置，考察不同黏度的潤滑油對滑移長度的影響。在理論方面，數值模擬在界面滑移及高壓流變條件下潤滑油運動的狀態。因為滑移效應已經由測量得到，那麼通過比較實驗結果和理論計算結果可以反推出部分高壓流變參數。 該項目可以完成的成果包括：(i) 彈流接觸區滑移長度测量的新技術；(ii) 壓力及速度對滑移長度的影響；(iii) 建立較合理的高壓流變模型。 我們已經在最近召開的世界摩擦學大會(京都，2009年9月)上初次介紹了該測量方法。我們的報告受到同行的好評，並一致鼓勵我們在此基礎上採用更多種類的潤滑油、擴大測量範圍、獲取更多的測量數據。 對於滑移長度的本質仍然存在大量的問題。這一測量滑移長度的新技術無疑有助於推动該領域研究的進步。

122710.label: Realisation of objectives
122710.value: (Objective 1) The optical EHL test rig was successfully developed to achieve reciprocating sliding motion through a programmable controller system. The glass disc and steel ball were driven by independent serve motors. To get the same stroke at each period, a phase compensation method was employed. The movement of dimple on Cr- and SiO2-coated surfaces was observed under pure rolling and sliding conditions. The influences of period, amplitude, speed and surface energy on boundary slippage were analyzed. The dimple being able to move to-and-fro across the contact area prolongs the measuring period of experiments. (Objective 2) To access the influence of shear rate on boundary slippage, the moving speed and direction of glass disc and steel ball were controlled separately. Different shear rates were generated by adjusting the relative motion of glass disc and steel ball. A relationship between slip length and shear rate was obtained. The experimental results were similar to the numerical prediction of previous researches. By controlling the impact stroke, dimples with different depth were obtained and the central pressure was calculated by surface deformation. Both influences of shear rare and pressure on slip length were assessed. (Objective 3) A new slip model which considers viscosity and shear stress variations across a thin layer adjacent the solid wall was established. By this model, the influence of certain parameters such as layer thickness, velocity and viscosity coefficients on slip length can be predicted. Although this model can largely describe the mechanism of boundary slippage, it is difficult to integrate into the EHL governing equations due to the weak convergence in numerical simulation. In this model, there exists an abrupt change of velocity and viscosity, resulting in a numerical instability. To overcome this problem, a new algorithm should be developed and debugged repeatedly. (Objective 4) To study the high-pressure rheology of lubricants, the film shape and friction of EHL contacts were measured simultaneously with slightly modifying the test rig. Effects of boundary slip and non-Newtonian were largely differentiated. The influencing parameters such as speed, loading and surface properties on the friction force and film shape were studied. To simulate the experimental results, a circular (non-Newtonian limiting shear stress) model was employed. The numerical results of film thickness and friction against with speed were well correlated with experimental data. It is concluded that the high-pressure rheological characteristics of the tested lubricants were governed by the limiting shear stress behaviour.

122710.label: Major findings and research outcome
122710.value: 1. Movement of dimple under reciprocating sliding conditions Experiments were carried out with Cr-Steel and SiO2-Steel contacts. Under disc sliding for Cr-steel contacts, the dimple almost stays at the center. The moving amplitude of dimple core is much smaller than that of the ball surface. By increasing the reciprocating frequency, the dimple moving amplitude decreases. But for the case of SiO2-steel contacts, the movement amplitude of dimple core is about the same of the ball surface. In ball sliding for SiO2-steel contacts, the dimple core holds an opposite phase comparing with the disc movement. Moreover, the dimple core moving amplitude increases during reciprocation, indicating that the slippage effect becomes weak due to the decrease of pressure. 2. Evidence of lubricant slip on steel surface in EHL contact Slip on steel surface was validated by observing the dimple movement under different running conditions. The experiments were carried out by varying the speed of steel ball (disc) in a large range (from negative to positive speeds) and keeping a constant disc (ball) speed. Under a fixed disc speed, the dimple core moves faster than the entrainment speed if the contact surfaces move in the same direction. However, the dimple core becomes independent of the ball surface motion when the contact surfaces moved in opposite. Under constant ball speeds, the dimple core moves close to the disc speed. The experimental data prove slippage occurring on the steel surface. 3. Dependency of boundary slippage on surface energy Surfaces with different surface energy levels were achieved by coating different materials on the glass disc and steel ball, e.g. Cr, SiO2, Al2O3 and DLC. Experimental results show that slippage always occurs on the surface of lower surface energy. Moreover, depending on the surface energy level, the boundary condition may show a variation from no-slip, to partial or full slip. The present studies directly show different slippage behaviours using different contact pairs. 4. Effect of interfacial properties on EHL film shape and friction The study concludes that surfaces with low surface energy promote boundary slip at the EHL contact, leading to a reduction in friction and film thickness. Under certain circumstances, adsorption layer may be formed on the lubricated surfaces, which leads to non-uniform surface conditions. A new type of “abnormal” EHL film shape characterized with three dimples in the inlet of the contact was obtained, which is attributed to the localized effect of the adsorption layer.

122710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
122710.value: 1. This project did not include any thermal study. It is really worth to look into the thermal effect on boundary slip because it is closer to practical engineering conditions. In fact, the effects of boundary slippage and thermal are interrelated. A thermal-slippage model should be built to describe to what extend the boundary slippage can play a role in lubrication. 2. The reciprocating experiments with high frequency which give high shear rate should be further carried out. Present technique has a limitation of reaching a high frequency. This can be achieved using electromagnetic control technique. Also, thermal effect should be considered under high frequency conditions. 3. It is amazing if boundary slippage can be controlled, which probably be realized by surface modification or surfactants techniques. Combining surface modification methods with optical EHL measurement technique, an optimal balance between film thicknesses, friction force and oil film capacity can be explored. The relationship between friction reduction and boundary slippage can thus be deduced.

122710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
122710.value: This project has provided a novel experimental approach for measuring slip length in highly pressured elastohydrodynamic lubricated (EHL) contacts. Mathematical relationships of slip length and pressure and shear rate were established. The dependency of boundary slippage on surface energy was explored. Direct evidence of lubricant slipping on steel surface was given which is helpful for the study of limiting shear stress of lubricant. Experimental and numerical observations show that boundary slippage causes strange EHL film shapes and a reduction in friction. The result of this work enriches the understanding of boundary slippage in lubricated contacts and inspires better tribological design in practices.

123210.label: Project Objectives
123210.value: For single-core processor architecture with software controlled cache, develop write-aware scheduling techniques such that the resulting schedule needs the minimum number of write activities on the main memory (flash memory). Both ILP and heuristic algorithms will be analyzed. Study a novel idea to reduce the total running time and the number of write activities on flash memory through data recomputation. Since write activities are costly, it is desirable to make less writes while taking more reads or recomputations. Recomputation will be analyzed thoroughly on single-core architecture with software controlled cache. Develop joint scheduling and recomputation techniques. Recomputation can be done before scheduling, after scheduling or concurrently with scheduling. We will analyze which approach leads to minimized write activities. For architecture with hardware cache, develop techniques to conduct both scheduling and recomputation to minimize write activities. Extension to traditional architecture will be studied to facilitate the goal of write activity minimization. Analyze how to produce the best data layout for a given program such that the write activities can be minimized with hardware cache. Study the best embedded memory configuration, cache structure, cache consistency policy, cache replacement policy and scheduling techniques on both single-core and multi-core flash memory based systems. Integrate the proposed techniques into compilation tools that can be used to develop reliable and efficient flash memory based embedded systems.

123210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123210.value: Flash memory has the characteristics of low-cost, non-volatility, shock-resistivity and power-economy. As the market grew to 15 billion US dollars in 2008, flash memory is now widely used as secondary storage in mobile and embedded devices. As flash memory consumes orders of magnitude less idle power than DRAM and is twice as dense as DRAM, it is desirable for the embedded system industry to use flash memory not only as non-volatile storage, but also as the main memory. In order to make it possible, however, we need answers to two challenges – the first is the issue of lifetime and the second is the slowness of write activities. By reducing write activities on flash memory, the goal of this project is to develop solutions to these problems which will lead to the practical adoption of flash memory as the main memory in mobile and embedded systems. First, the durability of flash memory, considering the number of erases, is limited. With the current technology, a block of typical NAND flash memory can be erased only up to 1 million times. A block is considered worn-out if the erase count exceeds its limitation. A write operation, except for the first write operation on clean flash memory, will always cause an erase action. Therefore, reducing write activities will extend the lifetime of flash memory. Second, a write is much slower than a read on flash memory. With the current flash memory technology, it takes about 23 μs to read 512 bytes from NOR flash versus 7200 μs to write, which is 313 times slower than read, as shown in Table II. Again, reducing the number of write activities on flash memory will significantly improve the system performance. For systems with cache, a lot of writes into the main memory are caused by dirty evictions. As shown in Table I, about 81% of the writes could potentially be avoided with the set of SPEC 2000 benchmarks that were tested. This project plans to reduce write activities by conducting write-aware scheduling and recomputation on software controlled and hardware controlled cache, on single-core and multi-core architectures. Reducing write activities is crucial in implementing main memories using flash memory in an embedded or mobile device. It is believed that this project will make significant contributions to embedded system research and the results can be applied directly in several vital industries of Hong Kong.

123810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123810.value: Kilovoltage radiotherapy is used for the treatment of skin and subcutaneous tissue cancers as well as palliative bone treatment to help with pain relief. Dosimetry of kilovoltage x-rays is quite difficult at these energy levels as x-rays interact quite differently in various materials such as skin, tissue and bone. X-rays also interact very differently in dosimeters such as low-density film detectors, silicon oxide MOSFET devices and metallic based ionization chambers. These combinations of variations make dosimetry quite complex at kilovoltage energies. This proposal is aimed at studying the dosimetric properties of high-sensitivity radiochromic films using Monte Carlo simulation techniques which will provide specialized information as to how these detectors can accurately measure kilovoltage radiation doses. Monte Carlo is a technique which allows x-rays to be individually monitored to simulate a real kilovoltage x-ray beam and how it interacts with matter such as the detector and human tissue. Once the correct beam parameters and modeling techniques have been obtained, the Monte Carlo code will be used to evaluate the dosimetric properties of the new higher density – high sensitivity radiochromic film products for radiation dosimetry. The Monte Carlo code will then also in conjunction with these new detectors be used to simulate and measure the effects of density variations in kilovoltage x-ray radiotherapy clinical treatments. Specific examinations will include areas such as the effects of beam shields in facial cancer treatments and areas such as effects on limbs from large bony structures located behind the treatment site. It is expected that large variations in delivered radiation doses compared to planned radiation doses may occur due to the presence of high density material in the beam path. The use of lead shields will affect the backscattered doses and thus affect the delivered tumour dose. The same or similar effect is expected for large bony structures. The use of Monte Carlo modeling will allow us to accurately simulate these conditions where measurements may not be able to be performed easily or accurately. Using these techniques, we expect to be able to provide the radiotherapy cancer treatment community with more accurate information about dose delivery around high-density materials using kilovoltage x-rays. 千伏放射治療適用於皮膚和皮下組織癌症的治療，以及用於骨頭緩解治療以減輕痛楚。因為千伏X-射線在皮膚、組織和骨頭等不同的材料會作出非常不同的反應，測量劑量顯得相當困難。與此同時，X-射線在不同的劑量儀如低密度膠片探測器、氧化硅MOSFET儀器和金屬电離室等，亦會作出非常不同的反應。這些變數導致千伏X-射線劑量學變得複雜。本研究計劃將應用蒙地卡羅方法研究高敏感性輻射變色膠片的劑量特性，幫助瞭解這些探測器怎樣才可以準確地測量千伏輻射劑量。蒙地卡羅方法容許監視個別X-射線光子以模擬真實千伏X-射線束及其在不同物質如探測器和人體組織中之反應。有了正確的射線參量和模擬技術，我們將利用蒙地卡羅方法評估新型高密度高敏感性輻射變色膠片的劑量特性。蒙地卡羅代碼與這些新型探測器將會用作模擬和測量千伏X-射線放射臨床治療中密度變化的影響。具體測試範圍將包括面部癌症治療中的X-射線束屏蔽和位于治療點後的大骨骼結構。由於在射線路程中存有高密度材料，實際的輻射劑量與預算中的輻射劑量之間可能出現較大的差異。使用鉛屏蔽會影響向後散射劑量，亦因此會影響腫瘤劑量。大骨骼結構亦會有同樣或類似的影響。蒙地卡羅方法可以準確地模擬這些無法進行簡易及準確測量的情況。利用這些技術，我們期望能夠為癌症放射治療人員，提供千伏X-射線在高密度材料附近的實際劑量之準確資料。

123810.label: Realisation of objectives
123810.value: The first two objectives were (1) to create a Monte Carlo simulation cluster to simulate a clinical kilovoltage x-ray beam for energies of 50 kVp, 75 kVp, 100 kVp, 125 kVp, 150 kVp, 200 kVp and 250 kVp, and (2) to match the spectrums produced by these simulated beams to clinical radiotherapy beams for accurate dosimetry in water based phantoms. In the present project, Monte Carlo modelling was optimized. Our studies highlighted the fact that for these types of Monte Carlo simulations using EGS nrc code, single CPU large core computers provided the optimal method for analysis. That was due to the serial nature of the programming and simulation process. Whilst large multi-core computers would significantly speed up for the simulation runs they were inherently slowed down by the geometry building and other input parameters. As such, using 6 standalone, 8 core hyper-threaded computers provided a similar speed to a single 48 core clustered supercomputer. Utilizing these research results showed that we were better off using standalone – multi-core (8 core hyper threaded) computers for analysis as multiple simulations could be run in parallel. Using the optimized Monte Carlo simulations, beams were simulated to match clinical x-ray beams for x-rays of energies 50 kVp, 75 kVp, 100kVp, 125kVp, 150 kVp, 200 kVp and 250kVp. These beam depth dose results were matched to within 2% to 20 cm depth and were used for simulations of clinical experimental research work. Work has then been performed on the effects of high density, skin dose detectors at interfaces, as well as on other interface and high density materials. Experimental work was also performed on nasal shields and the results were verified against Monte Carlo modelling. These works completed the tasks related to objectives (3) and (4). Finally, we employed Gafchromic film types like XRQA and studied their effects on dosimetry. The XRQA radiochromic film has been designed to have a high response to low energy x-rays to make it more sensitive. Results for both experimental work and Monte Carlo simulations showed that there appeared to be little or negligible effects caused by the higher density base material found within the XRQA film compared to other radiochromic films such as EBT2. These results completed the tasks related to objectives (5) and (6).

123810.label: Major findings and research outcome
123810.value: As described above in section 5.3, Monte Carlo modelling was optimized to simulate clinical kilovoltage x-ray beams with various energies, and spectrums produced by these simulated beams were matched to clinical radiotherapy beams for accurate dosimetry in water based phantoms. With these beams, evaluation of the effects of lead shields placed in clinically significant positions were researched. These were at depths of around 0.5 and 1 cm as would be the case behind areas of treatment like lips, ears or nasal regions. Simulations to theoretically calculate the effect of delivered dose were performed and results found. These results were compared to experimental research results which were measured over an extended period of time with radiochromic films. These results showed that reductions in delivered dose of up to 10% could occur if these small lead shields were not accounted for. Both experimental and theoretical Monte Carlo calculations agreed within 2% for most scenarios. This work was published in the Physics in Medicine and Biology Journal (publication [3] in the Research Output section). Work was continued on measuring the effects of a “higher-density” skin-dose detector called the MOSKIN on skin dose delivered during radiotherapy treatment. This work had been published in the Australasian Physical & Engineering Sciences in Medicine journal (publication [1] in the Research Output section). In performing the work required for calibration of the kilovoltage x-ray clinical beams, we needed to use various new quality assurance (QA) devices. This allowed us to compare and contrast various results caused for different clinical setups. Part of this work was to use a daily QA device for radiation dose assessment. Our investigations found that the use of this device in certain ways could affect the results of the calibration, which would have in turn changed results for comparison of the Monte Carlo simulations and experimental work. As such, further investigations were performed and evaluated. Results showed the size and manner of errors or uncertainties that could occur if the correct approach was not performed. This was published in the Australasian Physical & Engineering Sciences in Medicine journal (publication [2] in the Research Output section). Whilst it was not part of the original objectives, the work needed to be performed to complete the objectives. As described above in section 5.3, we found little or negligible effects caused by the higher-density base material within the XRQA film compared to other radiochromic films such as EBT2.

123810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123810.value: In the present project, we had optimized Monte Carlo modelling to simulate clinical kilovoltage x-ray beams with various energies, and matched spectrums produced by these simulated beams to clinical radiotherapy beams for accurate dosimetry in water based phantoms. This had established the platform for accurate simulation of conditions where measurements might not be able to be performed easily or accurately. Using these techniques, we will be able to provide the radiotherapy cancer treatment community with more accurate information about dose delivery using kilovoltage x-rays under different conditions in the future.

123810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123810.value: Kilovoltage radiotherapy is used for the treatment of skin and subcutaneous tissue cancers as well as palliative bone treatment. Dosimetry of kilovoltage x-rays is quite difficult at these energy levels as x-rays interact quite differently in various materials such as skin, tissue and bone. X-rays also interact very differently in dosimeters. These combinations of variations make dosimetry quite complex at kilovoltage energies. The present project had established a platform with optimized Monte Carlo modelling to accurately simulate the various conditions encountered with kilovoltage radiotherapy. For applications, we found that lead shields placed in clinical significant positions could lead to reductions in delivered dose of up to 10%, and that both experimental and theoretical Monte Carlo calculations agreed within 2% for most scenarios. We also identified the effects of a “higher-density” skin-dose detector called the MOSKIN on skin dose delivered during radiotherapy treatment. We also revealed that the use of a daily QA device could affect the results of the calibration, which would have in turn changed results for comparison of the Monte Carlo simulations and experimental work. Finally, we found negligible effects caused by the higher-density base material within the XRQA film compared to other radiochromic films such as EBT2.

124510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
124510.value: RiskMed: 基於協同智能的銀行業流動資金風險调控法 本项目提出一个基於協同智能的銀行流動資金風險调控法。雖然流動資金風險管理系統已經應用於銀行多年，由于金融事件可能會非常複雜，不穩定，及難以跟踪, 现存系統都不足以有效地管理系统性流動資金風險。因此，香港及世界各地銀行需要新的流動資金風險调控方案。 本項目力圖填補這个技術空白。我们致力于開發一個人類智能與機器智能协同（或簡稱協同智能）處理複雜金融事件，及相关的流動資金風險預測, 分析，決策, 和运营。銀行流動資金風險調控是一個複雜的過程，因為銀行的現金流常常会顺瞬万變。金融机构的償付能力取決於該銀行的客戶行為，各單位財務狀況的銀行，和外部市場環境。因此，許多財務指標需要不斷地監測以估計該銀行的流動資金狀況。當某些金融事件發生時，銀行必須有效地調動分佈在世界各地管理人員来應對風險，特別是大型跨國銀行可能有數百個分支機構。经过2008年的金融海嘯，中央銀行非常強調流動資金指標,以監測和保持銀行的財政健康。因此，銀行業急需有效的流動資金風險監測技術及相关的決策支持方法和工具。 本項目將进行三個階段的研究： 1。 （分析）调查現有的商業智能技術在複雜事件處理，預測分析，決策和協作分析實施的可行性, 并開發一個適合於銀行流動資金風險調解的風險分析技術。 2。 （設計）跟据第一階段的结果, 創建一個工作流程驅動下的協同智能架構和測試平台,并評估在各種金融環境下如何有效性调控銀行流動資金的系统性風險。 3。 （驗證）通過個案研究，問卷調查和實驗，實施和評價RiskMed風險调控法在地方銀行及跨國銀行中的应用。 本項目的研究結果将包括新的流動資金風險的算法和協同智能下流動資金風險的調控解決方案。我們的研究將根據各銀行在香港及大中國地區業務需求。本 RiskMed團隊擁有金融，商業智能，決策支持和過程管理等多方面的專业知識,足以应付管理系統性金融風險的挑戰。我們的研究工作將增加如何在信息經濟条件下控制金融風險的知識，從而幫助避免或减轻某些未來金融危機。

124510.label: Major findings and research outcome
124510.value: We develop a BI-based approach called NARM to support banks in monitoring and mitigating bank systemic risk. We adopt a network view of the modern portfolio theory (MPT) to model bank systemic risk. To do so, we conceptualize the network principle—correlative rankin-network principle (CRINP)—for modeling the impact of interbank relationships on bank systemic risk. By incorporating CRINP and MPT, we developed the LASER algorithm to rank banks according to their relative systemic risk levels. We use discrete event simulation techniques to evaluate LASER in monitoring and mitigating systemic risk in comparison with other methods. The results of our simulation show that LASER outperforms other HITS-related algorithms and the capital adequacy ratio. We claim two research contributions. First, our work initiates a new research direction in the study of systemic risk at the individual bank level with a network perspective for mitigating contagious bank failures. We developed a BI algorithm that incorporates network and financial principles into a systemic risk analysis framework of a banking network. As a result, our work lays the foundation for a practical approach allowing better monitoring and management of systemic risk. Second, our research has potential impacts on the modeling and analysis methods of various business networks. The CRINP network principle we conceptualized has instructional value to research in other domains such as citation analysis. In this project, we further developed an ontology-based bank stress testing approach called BESST. BESST provides the stress testing stakeholders with 1) the capability tomodel “exceptional but plausible” financial crisis scenarios; 2) recommendations of possible scenarios at each time step in a modeled scenario; as well as 3) the plausibility check on the designed scenarios. We claim the following contributions from both methodological and practical perspectives. First, to the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to introduce ontology and conceptual modeling methods into designing bank stress testing scenarios. It provides researchers and practitioners new methods and tools other than probability-based econometric approaches for modeling “exceptional but plausible” financial crisis scenarios without historical data. In addition, we also studied several intelligent banking techniques and decision support systems surrounding liquidity risk management. We hope that our research efforts are making liquidity risk management easier to do in the future.

124510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
124510.value: We acknowledge that our research has some limitations. First, certain assumptions of modern portfolio theory we adopted are simplifications of reality. Second, LASER requires high-quality financial data. For central banks that do not have such data on market risk and interbank transactions, LASER’s performance may degrade. Third, our evaluation study focuses on commercial banking systems mainly because of data availability issues. However, other types of financial institutions like hedge funds are becoming more connected with banking systems and should be included in systemic risk monitoring and analysis. Our future research will focus on improving NARM to allow users to validate various risk management theories and methods for applications in systemic risk management. We also plan to improve the LASER algorithm for experiments with other bank data sets from the European Union and Hong Kong. In addition, we intend to explore other BI techniques for further exploiting the network-related information associated with interbank relationships as sources of systemic risk. In addition, we would also like to 1) integrate the BESST approach with simulation methods into a decision support system for bank stress testing, and 2) explore the possibility of extending the scenario recommendation functions to strong complete and sound.

124510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
124510.value: Overall, this project has made significant impacts in the area of liquidity risk management and intelligent banking techniques. We have developed several new business intelligence techniques for banking network analysis and bank management that are based on both modern finance theories and advanced information technologies. In the process, the project helped train two doctoral students who generated a number of high quality research publications and graduated with Ph.D. in Information Systems. Both doctoral graduates are now working for the financial industry in Hong Kong.

140410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
140410.value: Institutional investors are often perceived as focusing on short-term trading strategies and jumping into and out of the same stocks over the same period of time. This type of trading pattern, or “herding,” has attracted the attention of both academics and practitioners, as institutional investors play a central role in facilitating price discovery and incorporating new information into security prices. Despite the development of several theoretical models that have successfully explained why institutional investors may herd, empirical evidence focusing primarily on the U.S. market yields weak evidence in support of the herding hypothesis. In a recent study, Sias (2004) proposes a new herding measure and documents stronger evidence of herding in U.S. equity markets. Our project aims to provide the first and most comprehensive study to date on herding in international equity markets, covering a period of 10 years from 1999 to 2008. We will explore similarities and differences in herding patterns between non-U.S. developed markets and emerging markets. Specifically, we plan to compare patterns between underlying stocks and global depository receipts (GDRs); between different institutions, such as between commercial banks and investment banks; and between pension funds and mutual funds. Developed and emerging markets have distinct characteristics in terms of market efficiency, risk-return trade-off, level of transparency, degree of information asymmetry, and equity trading costs. It will be interesting to explore what types of investors herd more intensively to each market and what specific stock characteristics each type of investor prefers in the two types of markets. Our project has important implications for investment analysis and asset management on a global basis. 机构投资者通常在一段时间内同时买入或卖出股票。 这种情况被称之为羊群效应。 羊群效应对于股票市场价格发现和及时反映新的信息是十分重要的。 这个项目主要目的是研究国际证券市场的羊群效应。我们会研究1999-2008这十年期间 发达国家和发展中国家之间，商业银行和投资银行之间，以及不同类型基金之间的羊群效应的区别。

140410.label: Major findings and research outcome
140410.value: We will first construct the heading measured based on the fraction of investors increasing their U.S. dollar portfolio value in one particular country, which we refer to as inter-country demand. We will then construct an alternative herding measure based on the weighted average of the fraction of investors increasing their holdings in individual stock within one particular country. The two measures will allow us to answer the following questions: (i) whether inter-country demand in one quarter to lagged inter-country demand for developed and emerging markets, respectively; (ii) whether institutional investors follow their own trades or follow other investors when they heard into and out of one particular country; (iii) whether inter-country demand is related to lagged country returns; and (iv) whether institutional investors follow the trades of institutions of similar type, i.e., banks follow the trades of banks, or follow the trades of institutions of different types. Our major findings can be summarized as follows. First, we document as a strong negative correlation between inter-country demand this quarter and the previous quarter. This negative correlation is driven mainly by professional investors following their own trades in opposite directions. This negative correlation is also much stronger in emerging markets than in developed markets. Second, we find that the negative correlation remains strong in the presence of value-weighted country returns. The lagged 3-, 6-, and 12-months returns do not alter the strong correlation between inter-country demands over adjacent quarters. Finally, we categorize all institutional investors into different types and conclude that all of them follow the “contrarian” strategy when they allocate assets across different countries. They tend to move into a country where fewer investors had increased their positions in the previous quarters and leave a country where more investors had increased their positions in the previous quarters.

140410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action

141110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
141110.value: The HKSE bans insiders from trading in their own firms’ shares in a period immediately before the announcement of financial results. Prior to 1/1/2009, the blackout period is 2 months in a year. In early 2008, the HKSE proposed to extend the insider trading blackout window from two months to a maximum of 7 months. The proposed rule was subsequently approved by the Securities and Futures Commission in December 2008 and was scheduled to take effect on 1/1/2009. However, in approximately two weeks prior to the effective date, 236 Hong Kong listed firms (denoted lobbying firms) objected to the new rule and successfully pressured the HKSE to modify the new rule by significantly reducing the length of the blackout period to 3 months in a year. This proposal utilizes this unique experiment to examine how changing insider trading regulation affects shareholder value. We conduct several types of complementary analyses. Our first analysis assesses the overall effect of changing the insider trading blackout window on shareholder value by conducting an event study of the stock market reactions to the initial new rule proposal and the subsequent reversal of the new rule. We will conduct the event study for all firms as a whole as well as for the 236 lobbying firms and non-lobbying firms separately. Our second analysis examines the economic determinants of a firm’s decision to lobbying against the new insider trading rule. We are interested whether lobbying is motivated by efficiency reasons (i.e., shareholder value increasing) or managerial agency problems (i.e., shareholder value decreasing). Using the years prior to the new rule, our third analysis examines whether the lobbying firms are more likely to delay the announcement of financial results than the non-lobbying firms in order to increase their insider trading profits during the period that would be otherwise banned by the new rule. Our last analysis examines the insider trading behavior of the lobbying firms in the years prior to the new rule proposal. We examine whether lobbying firms’ net insider trading volume (purchases minus sales) in the period that would be affected by the new rule is positively associated with the subsequently announced earnings surprises. In addition, we also examine whether the lobbying firms’ insiders earn a greater abnormal return from their trades in the period that would be affected by the new rule relative to their trades in the period not affected by the new rule. 香港联交所禁止上市公司内幕人在业绩公布之前的一段时间（限制买卖期）内交易所属公司的股票。在2009年1月1日前，每年的限制买卖期共有2个月。香港联交所于2008年初建议将限制买卖期从每年2个月增加到最长为7个月。该提案于2008年12月为证券及期货监察委员会通过并定于2009年1月1日正式生效。然而在正式生效前约两个星期，有236家于香港联交所上市的公司公开对该法案表示反对，并成功迫使证券及期货监察委员会对法案进行重大修订。根据修订后的法案，限制买卖期在一年中只有3个月。 本课题将利用这一独特的实验研究内幕交易之监管如何影响公司价值。本课题将进行若干项分析。首先，我们将研究市场对该提案的提出及修订如何反应，并籍此评判延长限制买卖期是否对公司有利。我们首先对所有上市公司进行分析，然后对比上述236家公开反对提案的公司和其他公司的市场反应。 其次，我们将研究是什么原因促使上述236家公司公开反对提案。究竟是对公司效率的考虑（即为增加股东价值）促使他们公开反对提案，还是因为这263家公司有特别的代理问题（即为侵害股东利益）。 最后，我们将对比上述263家公司与其他公司在法案生效前的行为。我们特别关注上述263家公司是否刻意延迟业绩公告以达到增加在法案所延长的时间内进行内幕交易获利的目的。我们还将研究上述263家公司在法案生效前的内幕交易行为。这些公司的内幕人是否会更对的利用即将公告的业绩信息进行内幕交易，并且是否从中获得更高的超额收益。

141110.label: Realisation of objectives
141110.value: We have achieved all objectives. For Objective 1, we estimate a portfolio return regression of the excess return of the lobbying, where the excess return is defined as the raw return of the lobbying firms minus the average returns of a portfolio of non-lobbying firms matched by propensity score. we find that the market reaction to the events that reduce the perceived probability of enforcing the new rule is more positive for the lobbyers than the non-lobbyers. For objective 2, we find strong evidence that the lobbyers have higher demand to use insider trading to signal private information. We also find some weak evidence that the lobbyers have higher incentives to expropriate minority shareholders. For objective 3, we have changed our research design. Because the lobbying decision is made after the firms have made their decisions on reporting lag in the years before 2008, we believe that it is more appropriate to use the reporting lag as an explanatory variable for the lobbying decision. We construct a dummy variable MOST_AFFECTED that considers both the reporting lags and the insider trading intensity during the period from the fiscal period end date to the earnings announcement date. We find that firms with longer reporting lag and have more intensive insider trading in the period from fiscal year end to announcement date are more likely to lobby against the new blackout rule. This analysis is now combined with the tests for Objective 2. For objective 4, we compare the historical insider trading behavior between the lobbying and non-lobbying firms. We find that there is no evidence that the insiders of the lobbyers are more aggressive in exploiting private information by insider trading. The evidence, if any, actually suggests that the insiders of the lobbying firms are less likely to profit from private information.

141110.label: Major findings and research outcome
141110.value: We have produced a working paper titled “Does Insider Trading Regulation Benefit Shareholders: Evidence from Hong Kong”. This paper is now under review at Journal of International Business Studies. In this paper, we use a unique setting in Hong Kong to examine the effect of extending insider trading blackout period on minority shareholders’ value. Most Hong Kong listed firms report their financial results twice a year. Prior to 1/1/2009, the blackout period is 2 months in a year (i.e., a one-month period before the half-year result announcement and a one-month period before the annual result announcement). In November 2008, the SFC approved a new blackout rule proposed by the HKSE and the rule was scheduled to take effect on 1/1/2009. The new rule bans insider trading in the period from a fiscal period end to the announcement of the fiscal-period’s results. As Hong Kong listed firms have a maximum of 3 months after the half-year end to report the half-year results and a maximum of 4 months after the fiscal year end to report the annual results, the maximum blackout window under the new rule could be as long as 7 months. However, the new rule was strongly objected by many listed companies. Finally, the HKSE under pressure modified the new rule and only extended the blackout period to 3 months in a year. We find strong evidence that the lobbyers have higher demand to use insider trading to signal private information. In particular, those firms that suffer from more severe price drop since the start of subprime crisis, have lower market-to-book value, and followed by fewer financial analysts are more likely to lobby against the new rule. We also find some weak evidence that the lobbyers have higher incentives to expropriate minority shareholders. That is, the lobby firms are more likely to have positive wedge between the largest shareholders’ control rights and cash flow rights. However, there is no evidence that the insiders of the lobbyers are more aggressive in exploiting private information by insider trading. Finally, we find that the market reaction to the events that reduce the perceived probability of enforcing the new rule is more positive for the lobbyers than the non-lobbyers. Overall, our results suggest that extending the blackout period may not benefit minority shareholders.

141110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
141110.value: A potential extension is to examine the change of insider trading behavior after the modified new blackout rule is effective from April 1, 2009.

141110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
141110.value: Whether insider trading should be prohibited is one of the most controversial issues in security regulation. Opponents of regulation argue that insider trading reveals relevant information to the market and thus makes the prices more accurate. However, the proponents of regulation argue that insider trading exaggerates adverse selection in the market, and therefore thus reduces liquidity and increases the cost of equity. Moreover, allowing insiders to trade may induce more agency problem by encouraging managers to make decisions inconsistent with shareholder value maximization. Most recent cross-country studies seem to suggest that restricting insider trading benefit shareholders. Our evidence suggests that this may not be the case.

142010.label: Project Objectives
142010.value: The first part of the research will involve the development of a theoretical model. This model will draw on the international and Chinese literatures, as well as our own experience in Chinese firms. We propose a generic research framework to guide our qualitative and quantitative studies at the beginning of each project. 142010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
142010.value: Chinese firms are increasingly paying attention to the knowledge resources of their employees – and are seeking to leverage those resourses for the greater good of the firm. Based on prior research undertaken by ourselves and others, we aim firstly to develop and test a theoretical model that explains the salient factors determining successful Knowledge Management (KM) practice in Chinese firms. This will involve survey-based data collection and statistical analysis. We have already identified four firms in two different industries (Public Relations and IT Services Offshoring) that are interested in participating in the research. We will follow the theoretical validation with a case-based, action-oriented intervention, working with the same firms so as to improve their KM practices. We will thus discover how specific KM practices influence key dimensions of organisational performance such as financial profits, customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, personal productivity and employee satisfaction. We expect that this two-pronged approach will generate knowledge of significant value to both KM researchers and organisations. The proposed research extends prior work undertaken by the PI and CIs. 如今中國企業越加註重來自員工的知識資源，並且試圖利用這些資源為企業創造利益。建基於過去我們和其他學者所作的研究，我們旨在建立和測試一個有關成功的中國企業知識管理及其主要因素的模型。此項目包括問卷調查和數據分析等研究方法。我們已經確定有來自兩個行業（公共關系和資訊科技服務離岸外包）的四間企業將參與此項目。我們將使用案例分析和以行動介入為導向的研究方法來驗證理論的有效性，並與四間企業密切合作從而保證我們的實踐對企業的業績，例如財務盈余，客戶滿意度，經營效率和員工的滿意度，發揮積極的影響。 我們希望此雙向的方法能夠為研究知識管理的學者和企業創造具有顯著價值的知識。此項目延伸了課題主要負責人和其他研究人員以往所從事的研究。

142010.label: Major findings and research outcome
142010.value: We have made substantial progress in identifying the key dimensions of knowledge sharing in the Chinese context. We successfully collected a large body of evidence from interviews, observations and a thorough review of the literature. From these varied sources, we constructed a research model in which we integrated different aspects of guanxi and different types of technology, considering their combined impact on the knowledge exchange process, with the ultimate dependent variable of performance outcomes at the individual, team and organisational levels. We collected data from 341 individuals across a number of organisations in an attempt to validate this theoretical model. This work has been instrumental in our writing of a number of research papers, as reported in the previous annual report at the end of the first year. This work has also contributed to our ongoing work in the area of KM in Chinese firms, including the preparation of a GRF application that is currently under consideration. Not all of the data we collected has been published to date - we are still in the process of preparing new papers that will acknowledge the source of funding and so constitute significant research outcomes. We list two papers in the research publications that were partially supported by this grant. One paper is in MISQ and one in ISJ. Although the early stages of these papers started before the grant was awarded, the grant was instrumental in facilitating the completion of the research - that was then accepted for publication.

142010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
142010.value: Even when an organisation claims to be interested in research, unforeseen circumstances often intervene and plans are changed. We have no immediate plans to attempt to develop this line of research - intervening in Chinese Private organisations in order to effect changes in the way knowledge is shared. We expect that we may offer advice based on our research findings in an informal fashion, but we do not intend to plan researcher-led interventions.

142010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
142010.value: The way in which Chinese employees share and exchange their working knowledge has, before this project, been little investigated and poorly understood. Chinese researchers have tended to apply and test Western models, while Western researchers have tended to ignore the topic. In this study, we undertook an in-depth and indigenous investigation into Chinese knowledge sharing practices. We noted the critical importance of guanxi-based relationships, and the way employees leveraged guanxi through informal technology applications as they undertook their work, seeking and sharing knowledge in the process. We conceptaulise this as a model of "Knowledge, Guanxi and Technology" - that contributes to the work-based performance outcomes at the individual, team and organisational levels. The model is designed to inform both researchers and practitioners about the way technology, guanxi (relationships) and knowledge interact in the work place.

142210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
142210.value: Online product reviews in review web sites, blogs, and social networks have made significant impact on consumers’ online purchasing behaviors (Lee and Youn 2009). A growing stream of research has begun to investigate how online product reviews can influence product sales (e.g., Liu 2006, Godes and Mayzlin 2009), yet the results so far are mixed. Two major problems can be identified in existing research. First, many researchers conduct their analyses in a cross-sectional design, which cannot control for unobserved differences in product quality (Duan and Whinston 2008). The other problem is that most studies only used the average ratings of reviews in their analysis (e.g., 3 or 4 stars) without taking into account the actual content of the reviews, e.g., what the reviewers say about the performance of various product attributes. This simplification approach may be limiting as scholars have shown that consumers in fact respond to the actual content of reviews, not merely the summary statistics (Chevalier and Mayzlin 2006). An accurate understanding of consumers’ reviews about product attributes has important implications for e-commerce. For instance, firms can pinpoint the specific product attributes that can influence sales outcomes so as to act accordingly (e.g., remedy attributes that receive lousy reviews). In addition, by isolating the longitudinal effects of product reviews on sales, firms can appreciate better the lingering effects of consumer reviews and adopt a systematic approach in managing the impact of such reviews. Using a new text mining tool, the study intends to fill a void in the online product reviews literature by modeling the longitudinal effect of attribute-level consumer review scores on online sales responses. Specifically, we shall extend and make improvements on extant product review mining tools (e.g, Hu and Liu 2004) to fit the Chinese Internet market. Our study will consist of two parts.
