142810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
142810.value: 在當今的知識經濟時代，組織已經越來越多地代表了專門從事快速有效的創造和分享知識的社會團體[46] 。由於有價值的專業知識通常會被保留在個體員工處，壹個組織的每個員工在知識共享過程中都發揮著核心的作用[32，63]。在員工間有效的共享和使用此類知識對於提高整個組織的市場競爭力就變的尤為重要[5，32]。在現代的組織中，雖然已經有大量的文件化的資源比如知識庫來儲存和獲得知識[1，35]，但研究早已表明，人們更樂意直接與其他人互動，比如通過非正式的社會關系紐帶[例如，8]來共享知識[3，17]。 通過社會關系分享知識在習慣上已經被理解為在面對面（F2F）互動的情況下發生的[例如，8，51]，然而對於現代組織員工來說，即使他們經常在壹起[44]，利用各種溝通媒介[例如，8，51]與同事交往卻早已經是習以為常的了。這些員工現有的信息與通訊技術（ICT）的數目正在持續的增加，而且種類變的多樣化。辦公室中最常見的有比如尋呼機、移動電話、即時通訊系統、電子郵件、電話和語音信箱。 因此，通過ICT的使用而形成的社會關系（除F2F互動之外）是在目前現代工作環境中所流行的，並可能對員工間的知識共享有重大的意義。 這個項目的目的是探討以ICT為媒介的社會關系在組織的員工知識共享中的角色。具體來說，我們將回答以下的研究問題： 對比F2F社會關系，以ICT為媒介的社會關系如何以及在何種程度上影響了知識共享。這個問題的答案不僅具有學術價值還具有實際意義。盡管在實踐中以ICT為媒介的社會關系的知識共享普遍存在，但在文獻中有關以ICT為媒介的社會關系的相關研究工作卻非常有限[例如，16，41，67]。 少量關註以ICT為媒介的社會關系的研究推斷，這種關系是薄弱的（基於ICT工具是貧乏媒體以及通過它們的互動很少發生的假設）。 他們是在弱關系理論[30]的基礎上解釋以ICT為媒介的社會關系對知識共享的影響。這曾是壹個社會背景下的理論，後來被采用到企業環境中，然而，當時以ICT為媒介的通訊工具相當有限。 我們註意到，現代員工經常使用ICT工具彼此進行交流，這意味著以ICT為媒介的社會關系可能已經可以被認為是強勁的。 如果事實如此，強關系理論[51，79]也可被運用其中。 鑒於在文獻上的重要差距，我們必須重新定義以ICT為媒介的社會關系的力量以及發展壹個對於這些關系如何影響員工間知識共享的更加全面的認識。 我們會整合計算機媒介溝通（CMC）理論、強關系 [51，79]及弱關系[30]理論來研究這個問題。 首先，我們提出以ICT為媒介的社會關系的強弱取決於通過這些關系發生的互動的頻率的概念。 然後，我們認為以ICT為媒介的強/弱社會關系比F2F的社會關系更加多樣和值得信賴，因此，對於員工間的知識共享也更有價值。 為了測試我們的假設，我們將使用調查的方法從三個組織中收集社會網絡數據。 項目將會在壹個已經建立好的團隊的引領下開展，其中包括兩位學術研究人員（方和庫雷希）和壹位擔任高級研究助理的博士研究生。 在過去的幾年裏，團隊壹直致力於研究知識共享，社會網絡，及其它相關領域，如虛擬環境下的計算機媒介溝通等，並在使用所提出的研究方法下已取得良好結果。 研究人員的資歷在提議書中已詳細列出。

142810.label: Realisation of objectives
142810.value: All the objectives of this research project have been achieved. The first objective has been achieved by finding that the original assumption regarding the weak-tie nature of ICT-mediated social ties does not hold. The second and third objectives have also been achieved in the study. Specifically, through a social network analysis of the employees in high-tech organizations, we find that (a) IT-mediated social interaction (in comparison to F2F social interaction) can provide better support to interactions between individuals with heterogeneous backgrounds, and (b) can better facilitate frequency-based strong social ties that are high in competence based trust. We find that both of these mechanisms support effective sharing of knowledge of ICT-mediated social ties than F2F ties. In particular, we find that IT-mediated strong ties (frequent social interactions that occur through IT) are the most effective in sharing knowledge (Israr, Fang et al. 2013). Given the additional funding granted by the university, we have extended this line of research by investigating the effects of social network ties on employee innovative behavior (Wang, Fang et al. 2013) as well as employee stress (Liu, Fang, et al. 2013). These extensions offer a more comprehensive understanding of the role of social networks in organizations.

142810.label: Major findings and research outcome
142810.value: Research Outcomes Our research project has led to three research articles under different stages of journal review process or under final preparation for submission at major international journals. One research student has benefited from participating in this project. Her thesis builds on ICT-mediated social ties by investigating online social networks and user behavior. Please refer to Part C for specific outputs. Major findings Here we illustrate major research findings specific to the questions we post to address. We examine the effects of F2F versus IT-mediated social interactions on knowledge sharing, by integrating the literature on knowledge sharing, social networks, and information systems. Specifically, through a social network analysis of nearly 90% of the employees in high-tech organizations, we find that (a) IT-mediated social interaction (in comparison to F2F social interaction) can provide better support to interactions between individuals with heterogeneous backgrounds, and (b) can facilitate frequency-based strong social ties that are high in competence based trust. We find that both of these mechanisms support effective sharing of knowledge. In particular, we find that IT-mediated strong ties (frequent social interactions that occur through IT) are the most effective in sharing knowledge. We also examine and falsify the assumption that all ICT-mediated social ties are weak ties. We find that they can also be frequency-based strong ties. By extending this line of research, we examine the relationships between social ties and innovative behavior, which is an important outcome of effective knowledge sharing. Specifically, by integrating social network theory and leader-member exchange (LMX) theory, we explore the effects of three types of social relationships on individual innovation: weak ties outside the group, LMX, and strong ties within the group. The results showed that LMX fully mediated the positive relationship between out-group weak ties and innovation, and within-group strong ties negatively moderated the second stage of this indirect relationship such that LMX was positively and significantly related to innovation only when the number of within-group strong ties was low. Furthermore, we take this project further by exploring how and when employee stress is contagious in organizations through social network ties. Based on affective contagion and the social network perspective, we find that employees with strong friendship ties and with an interdependent self-construal in the workplace share a greater similarity in felt job stress than those with weak or no friendship ties.

142810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
142810.value: Several directions can be taken to further the development of this research project. First, by confining an employee’s social network within the organizational boundary, we may have missed social ties outside the organization that are also important for knowledge sharing. We encourage future research to address the role of IT-mediated ties outside the organizational boundary. Second, given the relative youth of the workforce in our empirical context, we realize there may be some limitations to the generalizability of our findings to organizations with older employees. This new generation of workers’ familiarity and rich experience with IT applications make them inherently suited to working and socializing using IT-based media. However, this specific empirical context also opens up interesting considerations with respect to social ties, IT use, and knowledge sharing among the ‘Millennial’ workers, who will be a significant portion of the workforce in most enterprises in the future. Future research could focus on understanding the role of IT-mediated ties in other important outcomes, such as in the creation of social capital. It would also be interesting to better understand and then design emerging technologies helpful in creating IT-mediated social ties, such as the organizational adoption of social networking sites.

142810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
142810.value: In the contemporary knowledge-based economy, organizational success is increasingly dependent on how efficiently and effectively organizational employees share information with each other, often through social interactions. With the rapid advancement of information technologies (IT), IT-mediated social interaction has become an important alternative to face-to-face (F2F) interactions for the purpose of knowledge sharing. However, little research has been conducted to understand the extent of knowledge sharing enabled by IT-mediated social interactions in comparison to the traditional F2F social interactions. Our project examines the effects of F2F versus IT-mediated social interactions on knowledge sharing, by integrating the literature on knowledge sharing, social networks, and information systems. Specifically, we theorize the ability of IT-mediated social interaction (in comparison to F2F social interaction) (a) to support interactions between individuals with heterogeneous backgrounds, and (b) to facilitate frequency-based strong social ties that are high in competence based trust – both supporting effective sharing of knowledge. In particular, we find that IT-mediated strong ties (frequent social interactions that occur through IT) are the most effective in sharing knowledge. Through a social network analysis of nearly 90% of the employees in high-tech organizations, we confirm our theoretical insights and offers contributions to researchers and practitioners.

142910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
142910.value: With numerous opportunities for business expansion in the global market, an increasing number of Chinese-based business enterprises aspire to transform from national companies to multi-national corporations. Such transformation is accompanied by introduction of new organizational structures and business practices geared toward global market expansion and global talent attraction and retention. Hence it brings about new cultures that champion instrumental rationality and efficiency. From the perspective of senior management, such changes are inevitable. However, employees who have submerged in the customary practices in the local business culture may find the new culture foreign and prefer to maintain the status quo. They may view these changes as threats to their “normal” way of life in the local business culture. This is especially true for employees in many state enterprises in China that are undergoing rapid structural transformations to catch up with global competitions. Research in change management so far has not examined employee resistance to organizational change from a cultural clash perspective despite its important practical implications. For China to sustain its economic growth and strengthen its global presence, companies in China have to resolve the resistance stemmed from the bottom of the organization structure. This research proposal attempts to provide a nuanced understanding of the factors that contribute to culturally motivated employee resistance to organizational change from the cultural clash perspective. Our theory consists of five propositions, which will be tested in five rigorous experimental studies using data provided by white-collar workers in globalizing state enterprises in China. The major hypothesis is that activating a cultural comparison mindset will increase the likelihood of culturally motivated resistance, whereas instituting process accountability will reduce it. Furthermore, once employees view organizational change through a cultural lens, identification with local business culture will further strengthen culturally motivated resistance, whereas instituting accountability to change agents would attenuate it. Our theory will have important practical implications for managing organization change, particularly for national enterprises in Mainland China. 基於在全球市場上許多拓展商業市場的機會，越來越多中國的企業熱衷從國企模式轉變成為跨國模式。因為企業在全球化擴張後需要吸引和保留人才，企業會引入新的組織結構和經營手法來達到理性化和高效率的新文化。從高級管理人員的角度來看，這種變革是不可避免的。但是，當員工已有慣性的工作方式，他們會難以適應新的企業文化，寧願保持現狀。他們可能認為這些變革會威脅到他們在當地的商業文化和“正常”的工作模式。許多中國企業正在經歷迅速的結構轉變， 以圖趕上全球化競爭，對於這些員工來說，企業變革帶來的影響尤其深遠。為了保持中國經濟增長和加強其在全球的地位，中國企業必須解決這些源於基層的阻力。 這項研究旨在從文化衝突的角度去瞭解員工抗拒組織變革的原因。我們的理論包括五個提議。我們會在五項嚴謹實驗性研究中，分析由正在全球化的中國企業內的白領員工提供的數據。我們的假設是，啟動了文化比較的心態會增加員工對新文化的抗拒；相反，實行過程問責制將減少這種抗拒。此外，一旦雇員從文化角度來理解組織變革，對地方性企業文化的認同會進一步加深對新文化的抗拒，反而設立問責制能減低其影響。我們的理論將有助中國國家企業瞭解如何組織企業變革。

142910.label: Realisation of objectives
142910.value: Our project objectives have been fully achieved. We reviewed the literature of organizational change and multiculturalism. Specifically, drawing on the literatures of cultural cognition, intergroup dynamics, creativity and change management, we developed our theoretical framework and derived several major hypotheses. To test the hypotheses empirically, we first designed a number of pilot studies to test for reliability and validity of measurements and experimental stimuli. The measurements and experimental stimuli were then revised and used in the main studies. We employed different samples in our studies to increase generalizability of the results. In some studies, we used real work samples while in others we used undergraduate students and postgraduate professional degree students with work experience (e.g. MBAs). The studies produced promising findings that showed support to our framework. We presented these results and implications in several major conferences (Annual Meeting of the Society of Personality and Social Psychology, Association of Psychological Science, International Association for Cross-Cultural Psychology, and International Association of Chinese Management Research) and afterwards submitted the written-up manuscripts for journal publication consideration. One paper was published in Management and Organization Review (Impact Factor = 3.277) and we are preparing another two papers targeting Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes (Impact Factor = 2.897) and Journal of Cross-Cultural Psychology (Impact Factor = 1.547).

142910.label: Major findings and research outcome
142910.value: Below are the major findings of the studies. The first set of major findings evolved around the basic notion that when individuals cognitively processed information from multicultural perspectives, they were more receptive to changes. Our research respondents showed that when they cognitively processed both local and foreign cultural stimuli, they were more willing to accept a drastic drop in the percentage of the basic fixed component of salary than those who processed only local cultural stimuli. We further showed that this pattern was observed in respondents who were more open-minded rather than the less open-minded ones (Fu, Chiu, & Zhang, 2014; Fu, Zhang, & Chiu, 2014 May). From this research, we concluded that multicultural framing was a condition under which respondents were more likely to accept new and novel ideas, such as a change in human resource management. Further to this finding, we also found support to two possible boundary conditions. The first boundary condition was that how the new change was framed in terms of added cultural value. The enhanced effect of change acceptance from being multicultural-minded was observed when a new business strategy was framed as a cultural exchange rather than as an economic transaction (Hui, Fu, & Tong, 2013). The second boundary condition was symbolic threat. We found that when core cultural values of a society were threatened and might be jeopardized, multicultural-minded people viewed a new strategic move as more negative and showed great resistance to such change (Fu, Hui, & Tong, 2014). The second set of major findings concerned the contextual factors in an organization that affected the change recipients. The first factor was the accountability of the change recipients. Results showed that multicultural-minded participants were more receptive to change and rated higher work motivation when they were not held accountable for the fellow colleagues than they were (Fu, Zhang, & Chiu, 2014 July). This may explain why we always observe large resistance to change in union leaders, who bear high outcome accountability to their fellow union members. The other contextual factor was leader’s interactional justice towards followers. Leaders who showed trust and fairness in their interaction with subordinates could promote creativity and open-mindedness in subordinates (Li, Yu, Yang, Qi, & Fu, 2014). To conclude, our findings showed support to our framework and associated propositions.

142910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
142910.value: Our research findings have inspired further research developments. We found that multicultural framing can lead to two possible arrays of reactions. The first array of reactions is driven by creativity. In this process, individuals become open-minded to changes in which their self-interests might be sacrificed. One possible extension of our framework could be to explore the effect of multicultural framing in promoting citizenship behaviors in organizations. The second array of reactions is driven by perceived cultural clashes. In this process, multicultural framing highlights the differences among cultural groups and hence prompts negative emotional responses toward foreign cultures and rejection towards collaborations with foreign cultural groups. These potential research directions have been discussed in the conference presentations and researchers in the field may explore these suggested new directions. My collaborators and I also have plans to follow up on these ideas and would pursue them when we obtain new funding.

142910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
142910.value: When companies expand or implement new strategies, changes to the existing organizational practices are inevitable. These changes demand learning of new knowledge and procedures, change their work routines or involve rational instrumentality in reward structure. Hence, senior management often encounters tremendous resistance from employees during the course of change. The current research demonstrates under what psychological conditions employee resistance would be high and suggests ways to mitigate the resistance. First, employees who are prompted to be multicultural-minded are more open to new company policies. This behavioral tendency is further exacerbated when they think that they have to make their opinions towards the change known to the public audience. Second, workers who were tasked to be held accountable for their fellow workers tended to follow status quo and were more resistant to new organizational changes compared to those who did not hold such accountability. Thirdly, workers who feel fairly treated by the leader during their interaction with the leader are more open to new ideas. The knowledge derived from this research offers useful and practical advice to managers when dealing with change resistance in the company.

143210.label: Project Title(Chinese)
143210.value: 中国地方政府的腐败治理：动因与困境

143210.label: Project Objectives
143210.value: To examine and evaluate cases of local institutional experimentation and innovation concerning corruption prevention in China and to identify and scrutinize their origins, processes, mechanisms, and effects; special attention will be given to the dynamics and embedded dilemmas in developing local anticorruption strategies and what we can learn from their successes or failures. To demonstrate that beyond the anticorruption “consensus playbook” (Johnston, 1998)—economic and political liberalization, civil engagement, privatization, independent judiciaries, and a free news media—lie rich and diverse local variations that help us understand what works to prevent corruption in a given country or region and why, so that we can avoid attempting to fit ill-suited external institutional blueprints from one place to another.
rows: To examine and evaluate cases of local institutional experimentation and innovation concerning corruption prevention in China and to identify and scrutinize their origins, processes, mechanisms, and effects; special attention will be given to the dynamics and embedded dilemmas in developing local anticorruption strategies and what we can learn from their successes or failures.

To demonstrate that beyond the anticorruption “consensus playbook” (Johnston, 1998)—economic and political liberalization, civil engagement, privatization, independent judiciaries, and a free news media—lie rich and diverse local variations that help us understand what works to prevent corruption in a given country or region and why, so that we can avoid attempting to fit ill-suited external institutional blueprints from one place to another.

143210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
143210.value: This research attempts to identify and analyze local institutional experiments and innovations aimed at corruption prevention in China. Corruption is a major threat to all societies, but success in combating corruption has been far from satisfactory. It is seductive to search for universal recipes or to attempt to follow successful anticorruption “epitomes.” Conventional wisdom considers democracy, the rule of law, civil society, and open markets as prerequisites for corruption prevention. A logical question that follows from this is how should one pursue anticorruption reform in societies where these conditions do not exist? Scholars tend to agree that China has been highly innovative in mastering the complex challenges of economic growth in order to avoid regime breakdown (Heilmann, 2008). But on the issue of corruption, which can topple a regime with equal ease, it is less clear to the outside world how the country is tackling the problem in its various localities, and whether these efforts have been successful or unsuccessful. Following the institutionalist argument that institutions shape human behaviour while they themselves are being institutionalized, reinstitutionalized, and deinstitutionalized, the proposed study examines local institutional experiments in China that attempt to control corruption. Anticorruption institutional development takes various forms, including new rules and procedures, modifications in the existing regulatory frameworks, novel accountability mechanisms, innovative use of public resources, and the broadening of supervisory and accountability relationships. Many local anticorruption efforts are “innovative” in the sense that they are locally conceived schemes that do not follow any imported or imposed ideal “model,” or do so only slightly. The proposed research thus offers an analysis of the contextually embedded patterns and features of institutional development in China with regard to corruption prevention. This research attempts to address several questions: What types of institutional innovation and policy initiative have become visible in China’s recent anticorruption reform? How have they been formulated? How do they work to reform the structural nexus between public power and corruption and to enhance the self-regulatory capacity of the government? Have they encountered any institutional inertia and opposition while being implemented? What explains their success or failure in controlling corruption? What contributes to the success of a particular anticorruption programme? Methodologically, this research adopts an embedded-case-study approach by disaggregating China’s anticorruption experience into various local practices and then carefully examining several major cases to identify distinctive local patterns and to illustrate the dynamics and dilemmas of corruption control. 本项研究旨在分析中国地方政府治理腐败的实践。官员腐败是所有社会的一大弊端，但是，迄今为止，众多的反腐措施都无法十分有效地遏制腐败。因此，反腐败策略成为腐败研究的一项重要课题。多数人认为，民主、法治、发达的市民社会以及开放的市场是反腐成功的前提条件。问题是，如何在上述条件尚不成熟的情况下有效的控制腐败？学者们指出，改革开放以来，中国政府通过体制内政策不断调整和创新成功地应对了经济快速增长带来的一系列挑战（Heilmann, 2008）。然而，就腐败这一严重损害政府诚信，影响管治效率，甚至可能引发社会动荡的社会问题，中国政府又是如何处理的，尤其是地方政府在廉政建设上的作为和实践及其成功与否，都是值得关注的， 而学者们以往在这方面所作的研究甚少。 制度主义学派认为，制度影响人们的行为方式，而制度本身也在不断变化之中，也即所谓的制度化、再制度化和去制度化。本研究从制度主义的视角来分析地方廉政建设的种种创新和实践，包括如何推出新的规章制度、修订以往的规则框架、设计和建立问责机制、合理配置公共资源、以及强化监督等等。地方政府的许多反腐举措具有创新意义，因为它们并不是仿照外来的模式，而是在一定条件下发生和基于实际经验的产物。因此本研究将有助于人们进一步理解廉政建设与社会环境之间的关系。 本研究设定的问题如下：近年来，中国地方政府出台了哪些具有制度创新和政策实践意义的反腐举措？这些措施是如何遏制政府官员以公谋私的行为并增进政府自我管理和控制能力的？这些创新和实践是否遇到制度惯性的束缚和执行过程中的障碍？反腐创新成功与否的原因何在？一个成功的廉政制度必须具备哪些基本条件？ 在方法论上，本研究采用嵌入式案例分析法， 将中国地方政廉政建设分解为不同的创新和实验项目。在通过对重要个案进行细致研究的基础上，本研究将界定一些主要的地方反腐创新模式，并深入研究它们的产生背景，发展原因，政策特点，以及执行过程中的难点和困境。最后本研究将有针对性地提出一些反腐败的应对措施。

143210.label: Realisation of objectives
143210.value: The project has fully achieved its objectives. The PI conducted extensive desk-based analysis of government documents, media reports and relevant scholarly works on corruption and anti-corruption reform in China. Special attention was given to cases of local innovation that dealt with various forms of corruption. This led to the compilation of a database of hundreds of anti-corruption innovation cases at different levels of government and across different regions in China. The database served two purposes. First, it provided a general picture of the scope and variety of local anti-corruption efforts. Second, it gave detailed information on individual cases to allow the PI to identify some significant local innovations for further study. The desk-based documentary analysis was followed by extensive fieldwork in several major Chinese cities such as Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Changsha, Hangzhou, Chongqing and Chengdu. The PI conducted more than 80 in-depth interviews in these cities with local officials and, in particular, those who participated in the making and implementation of anticorruption policies. The interviews revealed not only different anti-corruption approaches and their rationales but also various dilemmas local governments faced in pursuing integrity management. All this information enabled the PI to understand and analyze what efforts were made and how they were carried out at the local levels in China, so the first objective was clearly met. The project was successful in achieving its second objective as well. The empirical data gathered by the PI showed a great deal of variation in anti-corruption reform from different localities. The PI was able to conduct research based on the information to see what worked and what did not in controlling corruption. As an extension of the research, which helped deepen the analysis, the PI also compared the Mainland China experience with what Hong Kong did in order to understand that there was no one-size-fits-all blueprint for corruption prevention.

143210.label: Major findings and research outcome
143210.value: The major findings are as follow: First, despite intensified anti-corruption endeavors, corruption has evinced a trend of acceleration in China. The evidence gathered by this study shows that the number of corruption cases involving high-level government officials has soared and corruption causes a huge drain on the state coffers. Meanwhile, corruption has taken more diverse forms. Corrupt activity has taken place under the disguise of market competition, which makes it more difficult to control. Corruption has even become a collective undertaking as a result of increased collusion between officials and business people. Second, the failure of previous attempts to control corruption has prompted the Chinese leadership to re-calibrate its drive against corruption. Since the last decade, there has been a noticeable change in the focus of anti-corruption enforcement from campaign-based corruption control to institutionalized integrity management. This "turn" manifests itself in the development of many new rules and regulations that aim at promoting government integrity. This research has established a database to collect and analyze these regulations. Third, changes have taken place not only at the central level but also at various local levels, as local governments began to play a more active role in corruption prevention. Burgeoning and disparate local integrity innovations have emerged and are generally encouraged by the Center. A local approach to integrity management serves some practical purposes. It leads to the creation of integrity programs and measures that better suit local conditions and needs. It may also bridge missing links between policy design and execution by facilitating the formation of stronger accountability relationships locally. A further advantage is that by pressing local authorities to come up with innovative measures to combat corruption, some new and effective methods may emerge for possible replication on a larger scale or even at the national level. This research nevertheless also finds that the Chinese local states’ capacity for innovation is highly constrained. Local governments work on the scripts for their officials’ behavior by providing substantive guidelines, but their intended institutional reforms cannot go beyond centrally prescribed policy templates. Local initiatives still need the blessing of higher authorities to be considered valid and appropriate. These findings have been disseminated in various forms of research output such as journal papers and conference presentations. This project has led to the publication of 10 SSCI-listed journal articles, several others in top Chinese journals, and 12 conference presentations (see Part C for detail).

143210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
143210.value: Although the current project is completed, research will continue. First, the data gathered by this project will be further analyzed and more publications are expected. Second, research will be extended to focus on some specific issues related to this completed project. One is to examine the new developments in China's anti-corruption enforcement. Following the 18th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party, the Chinese government has engaged in another drastic anti-corruption campaign. While the drive is still unfolding, it has demonstrated some new features and its effects and implications need to be carefully assessed. Secondly, the rich empirical data gathered through this project should be further analyzed, especially from a comparative perspective. Thus, the anti-corruption approaches taken by Hong Kong and Mainland China may be compared; and it would also be interesting to compare public perceptions of corruption and levels of toleration for corruption across different regions.

143210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
143210.value: In the existing literature, scholarly attention has largely focused on the causes, levels and forms of China's corruption. It is less clear to the outside world how the government has tackled the problem, and whether its endeavor is successful. This research adopts a case-study approach by disaggregating China’s anti-corruption experience into various local practices and examining some major cases to identify distinctive patterns and to illustrate the dynamics and dilemmas of corruption control at local levels. The research finds that there have been many developments in China's battle against corruption such as the making of new rules and procedures, modification of existing regulatory frameworks, adoption of novel accountability mechanisms, and the broadening of supervisory relationships. Many of these efforts are “innovative” in the sense that they are locally conceived schemes that do not follow any imported or imposed “model,” or do so only slightly. The growing local integrity innovation nevertheless has paradoxical roots. It reveals new thinking of the government by encouraging local authorities to play a key role in corruption prevention. However, just as clearly, it reveals the leadership’s deep concern about losing control over individual malfeasance or organized power abuse at local levels due to implementation hurdles.

143510.label: Project Title(Chinese)
143510.value: 谁将在中国法院中胜出？

143510.label: Project Objectives
143510.value: The project will develop a computerized quantitative data set based on 5,000 court judgments. In the developed countries, court documents are normally public records available to the academy. Since Galanter’s seminal paper published in1974, such a source has been the basis for numerous quantitative data sets created by scholars. China has not been in this league and has thus fallen outside the purview of comparative studies on redistributive justice. Our project will change this situation. With the systematic data, this project will assess the state of redistributive justice in the Chinese system. What are the differentiating levels of judicial equality across time, regions, issue areas and social groups? What is the position of China in comparison with other countries, especially those at the same economic development level (Peerenbooom 2007)? This study will add to the existing Rule of Law Index (Agrast et al 2008) with new measures for the redistributive dimension of the legal system. The project will also allow us to develop statistical models to identify the determinants of the winning odds of litigation. These findings will inform policy making in building a more equitable legal system in China. This project is posed to provide research findings that have direct implications for the legal development in transitional China. One of major debates can be characterized as between “form” and “substance:” legal reform leads to an increasingly formalistic system, but does judicial equality grow in tandem with this process? In this study, we will determine whether court rulings have become more and more equitable as the legal reform deepened in the last decade. One hypothesis to be tested is that legal justice is deeply shaped by underlying social forces despite changes on the books. This insight suggests that social justice is a result as much of intra-legal rules as of extra-legal societal forces, and that we therefore cannot achieve judicial justice without addressing the root causes of inequality and injustice.

143510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
143510.value: Existing empirical research on Chinese courts has normally employed public surveys or fieldwork interviews as its method. We propose to develop a quantitative data set to study China’s court system, based on newly available court judgments. The project is an application of the well-established research program originated from Marc Galanter’s 1974 seminal paper “Why the ‘Haves’ Come out Ahead: Speculations on the Limits of Legal Change.” We will compile and then computerize 5,000 court judgments, covering litigation cases across time, issues, regions, social-economic status of the litigants, size of the organizational party and so on. This data set will make it possible to measure the winning probabilities of the opposing parties involved, and to estimate their values as predicted by a host of independent variables. Supplementary data will also be collected through fieldwork research involving interviews with judges and litigation parties, to fresh out and corroborate the insights from the quantitative data. We will test three sets of hypotheses that are in tune of the Chinese reality of the legal system and judicial reform. We will be able to identify significant predictors as to who is more likely to come out ahead in litigation in contemporary China. This study will thus uncover to what extent that the Chinese legal system is equal to all, what social variables may hinder or facilitate redistributive justice, and how to achieve it in a system under transition. This proposal is built on our preliminary data collections, which have indicated the feasibility of the project and shown great promise of findings. 现有关于中国法院的经验研究通常运用问卷或实地访谈的方法。基于新近公开的法院裁判文书，我们将建立一套定量的数据库来研究中国法院。这将是对格兰特1974的论文提出的研究模式的任用。我们将从5000个法院文书中收集数据。该数据库将可以测量案件的胜诉机会与当事人社会特征的关系。其次，我们将通过访谈法官和当事人来检测在定量研究中的发现。我们将辨别出决定当事人胜诉机会的主要因素。本研究将揭示出中国法律制度是否公平、何种社会变量影响分配正义、以及如何在转型过程中获得正义等等。我们初步的收集的数据已经表明本项目的可行性和发现的重要性。

143810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
143810.value: 是項研究旨在探討團隊創意和跨齡團隊在創意工業的關係。研究所提出的新範式，在於提倡跨齡化的工作環境是有利創意工業長遠發展。是項研究包括兩個項目：(一) 以搜集經驗數據的方式，驗證跨齡團隊、多元專業組合及複雜工序對團隊創造力的影響；(二) 以問卷調查的形式重覆驗證跨齡團隊、多元專業組合及複雜工序對團隊創造力的影響，在不同創意工業的影響。

143810.label: Realisation of objectives
143810.value: In Study 1, momentary data of creative professionals during work provided little evidence that team diversity in terms of age, specialization and job function correlated with individual and team creativity. The team diversity also did not influence perception of facilitators and barriers of team process and creativity. The reasons might include that these stable characteristics might not have influenced on momentary variables, such as flow experience, and positive emotion. Previous literature do not employ momentary data to explore the relationship between team diversity and individual or team creativity. On the other hand, momentary variables have direct and indirect effects on individual and team creativity. In Study 2, contextual factors, such as perceived support, reward for creative application, and team processing, can predict individual and team creativity, in additional to creative self-efficacy and conception of creativity among creative professionals. To gain more insights on how creative professionals perceive creativity in HK's advertising industry, an extended qualitative study was carried out.

143810.label: Major findings and research outcome
143810.value: In Study 1, momentary data of creative professionals revealed that perceived support and barriers, team processing, flow experience and positive emotions during work were significant predictors of individual and team creativity. Flow experience and positive emotions also serve as moderating variables in predicting creative performance. Age, specialization and job function did not correlate with employee creativity. It was also found that most of the employees in creative industries were young adults. In Study 2 of professionals from different creative industries, team process (creative synthesis, norm for team, and reward for team creative) and mini-c (social axioms of creativity, and creative personality) were significant predictors of creative self-efficacy after controlling for age, gender, educational attainment, income level and nature of industries. Team processing variables had greater effects on creative self-efficacy. In addition, team processing (creative team strategy and importance of teamwork) and individual conception of creativity (novelty and usefulness) were significant predictors of creative team performance after controlling age, gender, educational attainment, and work experience. Team processing variables mediated the significant relationship between usefulness and creative team performance. In an extended qualitative study of creative professionals in advertising, the findings indicated that in a collective culture, creativity was mainly defined as the modest modification of prior knowledge. Creativity is both a precedent and consequence as a result of a good, health agency/client relationship. Originality and resonance are two crucial qualities defining creativity. Comparatively, clients in mainland China appeared to be more conservative than those in Hong Kong, even though this business segment is growing rapidly.

143810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
143810.value: To further test if positive or negative emotion is related to individual and team creativity, studies with randomized controlled trial on how stress management program, such as mindfulness based stress reduction, can enhance individual and team creativity. Other data also showed that creative industries, such as advertising, mainly employ young adults. The reasons for this age pattern may deserve further investigation. Does it really show that midlife adults or older adults will leave or cannot enter the industries because of age stereotype or inadequate employee assistance program to cope with the work demand and strain.

143810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
143810.value: This research is concerned with an interplay of contextual and individual factors on individual and team creativity. Team diversity (age, specialization and job function) do not relate to creative performance. Both contextual factors (team processing, barriers and facilitators for creativity) and individual factors (creative self-efficacy, beliefs in reward for creative application, conception of creativity) can predict creative performance. Age diversity is not typical in creative industries. Does it indicate age stereotype or a lack of employee assistance program in creative industries to enhance and sustain the creative performance of individuals and teams? The perception of creativity as the modest modification of prior knowledge and different perception of Hong Kong and Mainland clients by the creative directors in advertising industries also deserve more research attention. Organization support is also important to enhance team creativity in professionals. These findings have important implications on policy development in terms of supporting and sustaining the development of creative industries in Hong Kong.

143910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
143910.value: 一个好的运输方案必须将不确定性因素考虑在内。众所周知，运输的可靠性——即准时转运交货的概率——是衡量航空货运代理表现的最重要指标。在此，我们将关注于一个二阶段货运方案问题。在这个方案内，我们将其所包含的全部运输活动分别分配在两个阶段当中。其中，运输的第一阶段（即首阶段）包含了具有不确定性的运输活动，之后在第二阶段（即次阶段）货运代理可以根据首阶段中运输活动的实际表现来对该运输规划进行调整。比如，首阶段中运输活动的实际延误可能需要改变初始的货运规划，从而力求弥补已损失的时间。而针对此调整所带来的实际成本的增加，其将进一步影响到后续运输活动的集成与整合。本研究的贡献在于设计出将潜在风险因素考虑在内的运输方案，并将该规划模型直接应用于香港物流行业。

143910.label: Realisation of objectives
143910.value: Objective 1 We have analyzed the two-stage shipment planning problem and develop a control scheme for monitoring shipment process. Different shipment plan adjustment strategies are examined when the control procedure signals. The two-stage shipment planning with random processing times is formulated to a stochastic programming problem where recourses are made on delayed jobs. The objective function includes the start-up shipment plan processing costs, adjustment costs, job delay costs and shipment plan reliability cost. Objectives 2 and 3 A scenario generation approach is adopted to approximate the randomness in the stochastic programming problem. A heuristic search is established in a two-echelon framework to find the optimal start-up shipment plan.. The searching algorithm consists of a number of modules including: a 0-1 LP module, scenario generation, recourse and tabu search. Objectives 4 and 5 Shipments from Guangdong to Hong Kong are often delayed due to various reasons. It could be severe typhoons/rainstorms in the Pearl River Delta area or the tardiness of cross-border customs clearance. Here we consider the trucking times from Guangdong cities to Hong Kong are random. In the common Free on Board (FOB) practice, the subcontracted agents (airlines and the overseas agents) will be responsible after the cargo handover at the airport. We then assume processing times for other activities are deterministic. The shipping process is divided into two stages with stage 1 including the ground activities from shippers to Hong Kong International Airport and stage 2 includes activities outside Hong Kong. If tardiness is observed for job k, the forwarder will immediately release those jobs waiting for consolidation with job k (breaking the subsequent consolidations involving job k). The delayed job will be processed through the fastest route/agent. Intermodal logistics activity costs in Pearl River Delta are collected. The Pearl River Delta international shipment planning problem is formulated to a two-stage stochastic programming model where trucking times from Mainland to Hong Kong are assumed random. An optimal start-up plan is obtained from the proposed two-echelon algorithm. Our solution outperforms the solution derived from the deterministic approach. Reliability, cost and service level are the most important performance measures in freight delivery. We have examined the performance of the solution on target delivery times, processing time variability, shipment plan reliability cost, adjustment strategy and problem size in a number of simulation experiments.

143910.label: Major findings and research outcome
143910.value: Major Findings This research addresses the shipment planning problem with uncertainties for an airfreight forwarder responsible for multiple intermodal shipments in the planning period. Shipment activities are divided into two stages according to regional settings (or processing sequence). Activity processing times in stage one are assumed to be random while those in stage two are considered to be deterministic. The forwarder first determines a start-up shipping plan and acquires the resources. In case a shipment job delay is observed in stage one, the airfreight forwarder may implement an in-process adjustment on the existing shipping arrangements to reduce costs. The past literature gives little guidance on uncertainty in cargo shipping. Most of the research related to logistics planning uses deterministic optimization models. To emulate the two-stage stochastic problem in maximizing profit, we establish a two-stage stochastic shipment planning model using the scenario generation approach. The scenario approach allows the model to see/experience the good cases and the bad cases. The recommended solution is derived from the likelihood of event occurrence, event outcomes, actions and final outcomes. The two-stage stochastic shipment planning model follows a mixed 0-1 programming model which is NP hard. A two-level optimization algorithm is designed for obtaining the optimal start-up shipment plan. The lower level optimizes the shipment plan adjustment in recourse and the upper level is the global optimization. Tabu search algorithm is adopted at the upper level to find the optimal shipment plan. Case studies with industry data in South China are examined. Performances of the shipment plan solutions obtained from the stochastic approach and the traditional deterministic approach are examined in simulation studies. The performance of the proposed approach is demonstrated from its robustness in target delivery times, processing time variability and processing costs. An important issue in this research is that typical optimization models do not formulate the impact of a recourse behavior. Research Outcome The first three conference presentations address the work in Project Objectives 1, 2 and 3: 08/2011. The 5th Multidisciplinary International Conference on Scheduling: Theory and Applications 12/2011. The 16th HKSTS International Conference 03/2012. International Conference on Applied Mathematical Optimization and Modelling The fourth conference presentation delivers the results from Project Objective 4: 07/2012. International conference on Business and Information The project is concluded in a research paper: A Two-Stage Stochastic Programming for Airfreight Forwarder’s Shipment Planning

143910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
143910.value: We have extensively explored the two-stage shipment planning model with uncertainty in stage 1 and discussed the problem with uncertainty in both stages. Our model framework is based on the common shipping contract FOB (Free on Board). It will be of interest to develop new models on other shipping contracts. This research focuses on the randomness in activity process times. There are other risk factors exist that may affect the processing and execution of shipment plans. An interesting example is the availability of agent resources and routes in the shipping process. For future research, it would be interesting to identify certain practical features where forwarders can adopt when operating under a particular set of risk profiles. Future research could also extend the current model to incorporate the monitoring of shipments in a shipment plan. This means that the stochastic environment would be placed within a control environment involving planning, detecting, and in-process revision of shipment planning.

143910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
143910.value: Good shipment planning, which involves coordinating shipment activities and arranging logistics resources, is required for achieving shipment reliability and cost efficiency. In practice, cargo shipments are exposed to many unforeseen risks. We address an airfreight forwarder’s shipment planning under uncertainty. Shipment activities are divided into two stages. It is assumed that activity processing times in stage one are random while those in stage two are deterministic. In case a shipment job delay is observed after stage one, the airfreight forwarder could have in-process adjustment to start stage two processing. A two-stage stochastic program is formulated and is solved using the scenario generation approach. The scenario approach allows the model to experience good cases and bad cases. The recommended solution is derived from the likelihood of event occurrence, event outcomes, actions and final outcomes. The performance of the proposed approach is demonstrated from its robustness in target delivery times, processing time variability and processing costs. An important issue in this research is that typical optimization models do not formulate the impact of a recourse behavior. This means that forwarders could start with a solution that may seem to be superior but can be an undesirable solution in the face of uncertainty.

144010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
144010.value: 釋放「歌德式娃娃」：華文電子媒體如何挪用日本動畫敘事與美學

144010.label: Project Objectives
144010.value: Our aim is to analyze the cultural-artistic and sociological aspects of Web communities and their discourses of gender. The project will focus on Chinese Web users who share and re-mix "Japanese" content in digital media media environments. The study will make comparisons between Web content generated primarily in the Asian centres of Hong Kong, Taiwan and Mainland China. It will be an investigation of indigenous Chinese creations and reinventions within the larger globalization and online circuits of "J-culture." The study will make an important contribution to the field of Internet studies and Chinese Web communities. There are an increasing number of International conferences devoted to the study of emerging Internet cultures. We want to contribute to this field by providing a unique focus on the Chinese articulation of popular culture and discourses of gender. There is a lack of emphasis on narratives of gender and sexuality in critical studies of Chinese Web cultures. Even though Chinese and Western feminist scholars such as Rey Chow and Sharon Kinsella have laid the foundations for Asian gender studies using Japanese manga and anime texts, for example, we will make a major contribution by carrying out case studies within Chinese Web cultures. The project investigates a renewed political economy of distribution and consumption of Japanese products within different Chinese nation-states such as Hong Kong, Taiwan and Mainland China. Since many of these products are distributed through Web sites and involve forms of piracy or dubbing of original content, there is a new chain of distribution and consumption. We will examine the importance and role of animation fans and Web cultures in nurturing a vital economy of culture products. The project will make a contribution to queer studies by looking at how female and male fans identify with the other gender and with homosexual types of romance. We will find out to which extent such "queer" fantasies are relevant to everyday practices of gender and sexuality in other social environments. Japanese animation stories are not only frequently devoured by dedicated Chinese animation fans, they have also carried over into other media contexts such as commercial porn movies made and distributed in Europe and USA. We would like to investigate how different cultures and creators are projecting cultural fantasies and social habits onto the Lolita figure and the various mediated representations of this character. We will investigate some related phenomena such as "Maid Date Cafes" and "Doll Lover Gatherings" to draw a larger map of more youth based and energetic Chinese subcultures and how they manifest themselves in various contexts. We will find how youth communities use various websites and online agencies to communicate and carry out social activities.

144010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
144010.value: This study is a reception study of Japanese animation in Chinese cultures and Web communities such as social networks, gaming sites, fandom sites, and blogging networks. It will apply ethnographic research methods and develop audiovisual documentation to analyze gender discourses within Chinese Web communities. It will specifically study the cultural dissemination and Chinese adoption of the popular figure of "Gothic Lolita." Gothic Lolita is one of the embodiments of an eroticized "pretty/scary girl" who possesses dark powers and dreams of escaping into old-fashioned decadent life-styles. This Japanese figure of femininity is partly inspired by 18th Century French court narratives, and to a lesser extent by the Western interpretation of Nabokov’s Lolita (1955) as a lustful teenager who desires older men and, as such belies a mixture of innocence and sexuality. In our analysis of the dissemination of the “pretty/scary girl” figure, we will track the production of Chinese narratives and role-models in both real and virtual cultural contexts across space and time. The study will explore the ways in which Chinese Web users develop gender discourses as collective media aesthetics and intelligence in Web communities (Levy, 2001). It will examine how they discuss and develop characters to negotiate cultural narratives and power dynamics (Jenkins, 2001, Pattynama, 2001). It will also analyze mutual influences between Chinese and Japanese Web communities and their depictions of eroticized girlishness, thus investigating novel sexualities within the globalized flows of popular culture. We will use visual ethnographic methods to interview Chinese Web users about their attachment to local and global entertainment and to carry out an analysis of their cross-cultural dialogues and Web behaviors. 這項受眾研究旨在探索日本動漫在中國文化與網絡社群內的具體情境，研究對象包括社交網絡，在線遊戲網站和博客網絡。本研究採取民族志的調研方法並建立記錄了一系列影音材料從而分析中國網絡社群中的性別話語。研究將會特別關注“哥特式洛麗塔”——一個流行的次文化形象， 探究它的文化擴散與傳播，以及它傳入中國後所經歷的本土化改變。哥特式洛麗塔是情色化的“漂亮/可怕女孩”的化身，她擁有著黑暗的力量並總是夢想著能逃離現實進入舊時的糜爛腐朽的世界。這個日本女性形象在很大程度上受到十八世紀法國宮廷敘事的影響，也多少與西方世界關於納博科夫1955年小說《洛麗塔》的詮釋有關。納博科夫小說中的洛麗塔是一個充滿慾望的少女，她希望得到年長的男子，是一個純真與性慾的混合體。在我們對這一“漂亮/可怕女孩”的解析中，我們將會追踪現實與虛擬世界中中國式敘事和角色典範的生產發展過程。 這項研究將會探索中國網民在網絡社群中如何將性別話語作為集體媒介審美與媒介智識來發展演化的(Levy, 2001)。研究將會檢驗網民們如何探討和建立網絡角色，如何集體協商文化敘事與權力關係(Jenkins, 2001, Pattynama,2001)。我們將會運用視覺民族志的方法訪問中國網民，探尋他們對於本土和全球娛樂產業的依附關係。我們還將進一步分析他們在網絡世界裡的跨文化對話和種種網絡行為。 同時，研究更將分析中日兩國網絡社群的交互影響和他們對於情色化的女孩特質的描述，從而研究在全球化流行文化與網絡社群背景中的新奇的性別特質說帶來的社會效應。

144010.label: Realisation of objectives
144010.value: Overall the GRF grant has helped me enormously in fulfilling most of these objectives. Here below are some further observations. # 2 I have noticed that there are more studies devoted to aspects of gender and sexuality within Chinese web cultures and the fandom cultures of Japanese animation. But overall feminist or queer perspectives on these emerging domains are still quite sparse, which is probably due to the fact that queer life-styles or outspoken feminist viewpoints are not encouraged within public cultures and education in mainland China. In this sense we need to make more efforts to set up cross-cultural research platforms between Chinese and non-Chinese institutions, so that the globalisation of emerging sex cultures can be investigated from within a culturally diverse and multidisciplinary platform. # 6 Since I have mostly investigated fans culture and artists in Japan, Hong Kong, China and Indonesia (to a lesser extent) I was not able to devote much time to the growing fan circles of Japanese animation within Western cultures. It would certainly be a meaningful addition to this project if the analysis of concepts of gender and sexuality within East Asian animation cultures could be further examined within Western context.

rows: Our aim is to analyze the cultural-artistic and sociological aspects of Web communities and their discourses of gender. The project will focus on Chinese Web users who share and re-mix "Japanese" content in digital media media environments. The study will make comparisons between Web content generated primarily in the Asian centres of Hong Kong, Taiwan and Mainland China. It will be an investigation of indigenous Chinese creations and reinventions within the larger globalization and online circuits of "J-culture."

The study will make an important contribution to the field of Internet studies and Chinese Web communities. There are an increasing number of International conferences devoted to the study of emerging Internet cultures. We want to contribute to this field by providing a unique focus on the Chinese articulation of popular culture and discourses of gender.

There is a lack of emphasis on narratives of gender and sexuality in critical studies of Chinese Web cultures. Even though Chinese and Western feminist scholars such as Rey Chow and Sharon Kinsella have laid the foundations for Asian gender studies using Japanese manga and anime texts, for example, we will make a major contribution by carrying out case studies within Chinese Web cultures.

The project investigates a renewed political economy of distribution and consumption of Japanese products within different Chinese nation-states such as Hong Kong, Taiwan and Mainland China. Since many of these products are distributed through Web sites and involve forms of piracy or dubbing of original content, there is a new chain of distribution and consumption. We will examine the importance and role of animation fans and Web cultures in nurturing a vital economy of culture products.

The project will make a contribution to queer studies by looking at how female and male fans identify with the other gender and with homosexual types of romance. We will find out to which extent such "queer" fantasies are relevant to everyday practices of gender and sexuality in other social environments.

Japanese animation stories are not only frequently devoured by dedicated Chinese animation fans, they have also carried over into other media contexts such as commercial porn movies made and distributed in Europe and USA. We would like to investigate how different cultures and creators are projecting cultural fantasies and social habits onto the Lolita figure and the various mediated representations of this character.

We will investigate some related phenomena such as "Maid Date Cafes" and "Doll Lover Gatherings" to draw a larger map of more youth based and energetic Chinese subcultures and how they manifest themselves in various contexts. We will find how youth communities use various websites and online agencies to communicate and carry out social activities.

144010.label: Major findings and research outcome
144010.value: I have published one book and a website called "Wandering Dolls" which contains samples of my ethnographic fieldwork. I have given a conference presentation about the artistic and visual culture methods employed in this project and how they can be further applied by other scholars and students. I have also written several refereed essays to further analyse research information that I have received from my ethnographic observations and interviews. More particularly, I have devoted one book chapter and one journal article to a study of queer performativity and cross-dressing within these specific subcultures and fandom groups. My journal article "Impersonating and Performing Queer Sexuality in the Cosplay Zone" was published in November 2013 in "Participations: International Journal of Audience and Reception Studies." This article highlights the physical and digital behaviours of the fans of Japanese ACG (Animation, Comics and Games) cultures in Mainland China and Hong Kong and, to a lesser extent, in Taiwan. It focuses on Cosplayers (costumed players) who frequently engage in acts of cross-dressing and fantasized same-sex relations. The article explores what these performative gestures mean in relation to their sexual identities. Ethnographic testimonies were solicited through interviews, collaborative photography and video documentation. The article postulates that new boundaries of selfhood and sexual pleasure are explored within a ‘Cosplay zone,’ an amalgam of interconnected spaces and augmented realities that allow subjects to morph between fictionalized fantasy worlds, physical gatherings and online appearances. Additionally, I am now preparing a conference paper and publication about "The Art of Failure in Boy’s Love Narratives." The paper will be presented at the Women and Manga conference in Hong Kong, March 2014, which I am co-organizing with Dr. Kazumi Nagaike and Dr. Fusami Ogi. The papers presented at this conference will also be compiled for publication in an international journal. My own paper delves into the worldviews of Hong Kong Chinese and Mainland Chinese women who have projected fantasies of sexual climax and failure onto homo-erotic narratives in Boy’s love animation. It analyzes how productive failure is expressed in collections of fan comics featuring “homme fatale” Barnaby Brooks who seduces an older colleague Kotetsu T. Kaburagi "Wild Tiger" (often nicknamed “the old man”) from the anime series Tiger & Bunny. The paper redefines pornographic depiction as a contradictory impulse towards glorifying sex acts and admitting failure.

144010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
144010.value: The theme of animation fandom and and sexuality/gender has become more developed within several field of arts and humanities. There is also a growing concern in Hong Kong and mainland China about the sexual ideology of these products, as governments and mass media alike are eager to report on aspects of "moral degradation." In this sense it is important for scholars to keep doing in-depth research about actual "sexually explicit" content and the production/reception mechanisms of contemporary youth. I will continue to research the impact of Japanese animation cultures and sexually explicit media on Chinese youth and subcultures. I have become member of international research theme on this topic. This team is coordinated by Japanese scholar-expert Dr. Fusami Ogi who organises an annual conference. This year's conference "Modern Women and Their Comics: Changing Local Identities from the 1960s to the 2000s" will take place in March in Hong Kong. I will be involved as co-organizer of the conference and as presenter of a paper on Boys' Love manga. I will also be authoring a forthcoming book on Chinese women's sexuality and social media which will partially be devoted to animation culture. The book proposal is currently being reviewed by several international academic publishers, one of which has made an offer to publish the book in 2015.

144010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
144010.value: This research study examines the reception of Japanese animation cultures within Chinese subcultures and digital media environments. It focuses on how Chinese consumers use digital media to access and creatively respond to changing roles of gender and sexuality. The study develops ethnographic research methods and audio-visual documentation to analyze participatory Internet culture. It specifically studies the cultural dissemination and Chinese adoption of concepts of gender and sexuality such as the popular figure of “Gothic Lolita” or the home-erotic fantasy stories of Boy's Love (yaoi). Gothic Lolita is one of the embodiments of an erotized "pretty/scary girl" who possesses dark powers and who dreams of escape into old-fashioned decadent life-styles. This Japanese figure of femininity is partly inspired by French 18th century court narratives, and to a lesser extent by the Western interpretation of Nabokov’s Lolita (1955) as a lustful teenager who desires older men and as such belies a mixture of innocence and sexuality. In the analysis of the dissemination of sex and gender roles, the study tracks the transformation of narratives of power and gender from within Japanese and trans-national animation culture into Chinese subcultures in both real and virtual contexts.

144110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
144110.value: This project aims to explore discursive practices associated with food labeling. It takes as its site of investigation Hong Kong, an international city which imports 90% of its food and which has recently passed a strict new food labeling law. The project focuses on how this new law and the legal, political, media and consumer discourses surrounding it have affected the discursive practices of manufacturers, marketers and designers as they produce food labels, and the interpretative practices of consumers engaged in the everyday action of choosing a product from the supermarket shelves. It aims to determine: 1) How the law has affected the ways manufacturers and marketers design food labels for the Hong Kong market. 2) How the law has affected the ways consumers interpret and use food labels. 3) How retailers, consumer organizations, politicians and the media act as discursive intermediaries between consumers and manufacturers, and how their discourse affects both how labels are produced and how they are used. The data collection will span a period of eighteen months shortly after the new labeling law takes effect in July 2010. During this period, three kinds of data will be collected. 1) Textual Data (food labels, media reports, government documents), 2) Interview Data (interviews with manufacturers, marketers, retailers, public officials, specialists in healthcare e.g., nutritionists and dieticians, and consumers) 3) Ethnographic Data (including observation of retailer and consumer behavior, spot interviews with shoppers, as well as in-depth case studies of ten families compiled over the duration of the study including periodic interviews and observations of family members’ shopping, cooking and eating behavior as it relates to label use). The data will be analyzed using tools from the three distinct but complementary traditions in discourse analysis: 1) Critical Genre Analysis, an approach that explores the relationship between texts and the professional practices and identities of the discourse communities that produce them, 2) Critical Discourse Analysis, an approach which explores how media and political discourse can shape people’s perceptions of issues, and 3) Mediated Discourse Analysis, which focuses on everyday practices like shopping and preparing meals and explores the role texts take in the moment by moment performance of these practices. The findings of this research will benefit consumers, corporate stakeholders, and government officials. It will inform efforts in consumer education, health promotion, and policymaking, and will also provide industry stakeholders with valuable information on label design and consumer concerns and behavior, 鑑於香港現時有九成的糧食由外地進口，而政府近期亦通過嚴謹的食物標籤法例，本專題研究旨在探索這國際都市對食物標籤的推論實踐。 這項研究集中探討這法例及關於法律、政治、傳媒及消費者的論述怎樣影響生產商、營銷商和設計師製造食物標籤時的推論實踐，以及消費者平日於選購超市產品時對此的理解及應用。這項研究旨在查明: 1) 法例如何影響生產商和營銷商對食物標籤的設計; 2) 法例如何影響消費者使用食物標籤; 3) 零售商，消費者組織，政客和媒體之間如何充當消費者和生產商的推論媒介，以及其論述如何影響到標籤的製造和使用方式。 由2010年7月新標籤法例實施開始，研究人員會展開為期十八個月的資料搜集，並會在這期間搜集以下三項資料﹕ 1) 文本資料 (食物標籤，媒體報導，政府文件) 2) 訪問資料 (生產商、市場策劃者、零售商、公職人員、消費者和醫療專家如營養學家和營養師的訪問) 3) 人種誌資料 (觀察零售商和消費者行為，與顧客進行現場訪談，以及深入研究共十個家庭，當中包括定期訪談和觀察其家庭成員使用標籤於購物、烹調、和飲食等行為。) 是項研究將會以下列三種不同卻又能互相補足的方法分析收集到的數據: 1) 批評體裁分析 -- 探討文本和專業實踐與其建構群體的身份特徵之間的關係; 2) 批判論述分析 -- 探討媒體和政治話語如何塑造人們的觀念; 3) 間接論述分析 -- 著重於日常實踐如購物和煮食，並探討文本在這些實踐中時刻扮演的角色。 這項研究的發現將會惠及消費者，企業持份者和政府官員。它將會推動社會對消費者的教育，健康推廣和政策制定，並為業界人士提供設計食物標籤與消費者考慮因素及行為相關的寶貴資料。

144110.label: Realisation of objectives
144110.value: This project had five objectives 1) to analyze the key discursive practices of various stakeholders in implementing the new food labeling law in Hong Kong; 2) to examine the communicative strategies used in the design of food labels; 3) to understand how consumers read, interpret and understand labels; 4) to understand how consumers use labels to take concrete social actions: and 5) to appraise how the discursive behavior of consumers is affected by public policy and industry responses to that policy. The first objective was realized through the analysis of a large collection of media texts and government documents dealing with the law, as well as of interviews with government officials, manufacturers, retailers, nutritionists, and customers. The second objective was realized through the collection and analysis of a large corpus of food labels from both before and after the implementation of the law using both traditional tools of text analysis and more recently developed methods of multimodal discourse analysis. The last three objectives were realized through both the structured collection of data in the form of spot interviews with customers in supermarkets and focus group interviews with customers from different demographic groups. and through the ethnographic examination of the nutritional practices of ten families in Hong Kong accomplished through week-long participant observations within these families. This multi-dimensional approach to data gathering and analysis allowed investigators to understand how the production and consumption of food labels is effected by multiple factors beyond the semantic content of the labels themselves, factors that range from the larger social/political conditions in which regulations are formulated and implemented, and more local conditions within families which affect practices of purchasing, preparing and consuming food. This project has demonstrated how labelling and packaging practices arise from complex social interactions among those who sell food products, those who consume them, and those who regulate these transactions. Food labels at all stages of legislation, design and interpretation are subject to various discursive strategies which often have little to do with the actual content of food or whether or not it is nutritious or safe. As a result of this, laws intended to improve the quality of food and customers’ ability to make informed decisions about purchases can sometimes actually increase restrictions on choice and access to information.

144110.label: Major findings and research outcome
144110.value: The findings from this project illustrate how attempts to regulate commercial discourse can sometimes have unexpected effects. While the new regulations were intended to ensure that customers had more information about the food they bought, they instead resulted in widespread confusion among customers and adverse economic consequences for retailers. One of the main reasons for this was that lawmakers, retailers and customers approached the issue of food labeling with radically different understandings of the role that language plays in it. Government regulators focused primarily on the semantic dimensions of language: nutritional labels were seen chiefly as means of conveying information. Among the problems arising from this view was that legislative definitions often diverged from the everyday lay definitions used by consumers. Manufacturers and retailers, on the other hand, focused more on the interpersonal dimension of language on food labels, and consequently worked to develop various linguistic strategies that allowed them establish relationships of trust with customers. Retailers in particular were found to engage in that involved creatively undermining the restrictions on the kinds of information they could provide to their customers. Finally, investigation of the way customers read the new labels revealed a more functional view of language in which information was usually accessed slectively. Most customers reported not reading food labels at all, making their purchasing decisions based not on information but on the reputation of the product or their past experiences with it. The findings regarding the implementation of the law were reported at a number of international conferences and in an article submitted to the Journal of Business and Technical Communication. These led to a wider examination of the more general difficulties of regulating the discourse on food packages using a traditional semantic framework. Analysis of alarge corpus of food labels revealed multiple ways manufacturers are able to circumvent regulations by making veiled claims through the use of implicature and non-verbal elements such as images. In an article submitted to Multimodal Communication, an alternative model for analyzing claims on food labels based on pragmatics and multimodal discourse analysis is suggested. Finally, the way customers use labels on products like food and medicine depends on the complex interaction of multiple linguistic, social and contextual factors. A framework for understanding how label information affects health behavior was developed and reported in the book Health and risk communication: A applied linguistic perspective (Jones, 2013).

144110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
144110.value: Further research will examine how the insights from pragmatics and multimodal discourse analysis gained in this project can be translated into workable public policy regarding claims on food packages. How can regulations be written and enforced to cover claims that are made through indirect means (through implicature) and through non-verbal means like graphics, colors, and fonts? In addition, lessons learned from the difficulties and confusion encountered by retailers and consumers in the implementation of these regulations – and the source of these difficulties in specific communication practices—can inform future efforts in public consultation and education when it comes to nutrition and food safety. Finally, greater attention must be paid to the various new forms of social media marketing food manufacturers are engaging in (thorough social networking sites like Facebook), forms of marketing which are currently unregulated. In the concluding stages of this project, evidence of the linguistic strategies used in social media marketing were collected with the aim of applying for further research funds in the future to explore this issue.

144110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
144110.value: This project examined the implementation of a new food labeling law in Hong Kong from the perspective of government regulators, manufacturers, distributors and retailers, and customers. The new law strictly regulates the nutritional information that must appear on food labels and the kinds of nutritional claims that can be made. The project used tools from discourse analysis and applied linguistics to analyze the linguistic strategies used to make food labels comply with the law, and the ways customers interpreted the new labels and used them to make purchasing decisions. Results revealed that stakeholders developed a number of competing strategies to cope with the new law, and that, in many cases, this resulted in consumers being given less information about the food they bought rather than more, and less choice as to the range of products available. Insights from the case study led to a wider examination of the difficulties in regulating the discourse on food packages due to the numerous ways manufacturers have developed to circumvent regulations by manipulating rules for the reporting of nutritional content and by making veiled claims through indirect statements and the strategic use of images, colors, fonts, and the physical attributes of packages.

144310.label: Project Title(Chinese)

144310.label: Project Objectives
144310.value: To test whether accounting conservatism reduces not only the likelihood of stock price crash occurrences in China but also delay such occurences. To test whether the effect of accounting conservatism on the occurrence and timing of crashes is accentuated (attenuated) when managers have stronger (weaker) incentives to conceal unfavorable information from outside investors. Specifically, we investigate whether and how the conservatism-crash relation in China is more pronounced for Chinese firms with concentrated ownership and high government ownership. To test whether the effect of accounting conservatism on the occurrence and timing of crashes is accentuated (attenuated) when external monitoring is more (less) effective. Specifically, we examine whether the conservatism-crash relation in China is conditioned upon the extent of product market competition or industry concentration and the number of analysts following a firm.
