160810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
160810.value: 前扣帶回區域CaMKII蘇氨酸位自動磷酸化調節大鼠內臟痛 功能性腸道疾病如腸易激綜合征（IBS）患者存在內臟擴張所致的高敏感。這一狀態可能與中樞神經系統某些區域的中樞傳遞異常有關。 近來，我們通過建立內臟高敏感大鼠模型, 該大鼠模型對結腸擴張增強的疼痛反應在7周后仍可觀察到，這種反應不同於粘膜炎症所致的疼痛。本實驗組前期實驗表明前扣帶回皮質神經元的敏感性源自其興奮性依賴的神經元可塑性的改變。前扣帶回皮質NMDA受體的NR2B亞基在調節扣帶回皮質與疼痛反應過程中發揮關鍵作用。然而，這一過程的細胞和分子機制尚不清楚。鑒於鈣/鈣調蛋白依賴性蛋白激酶II（CaMKII）在突觸可塑性，學習與記憶中的關鍵作用，及其與NR2B亞基的高親和力，我們推測這種CaMKII的磷酸化與NR2B亞基的結合調節生物化學的“記憶”過程，進而調節內臟高敏感狀態的內臟疼痛反應。為了驗証這一假設，應用電穿孔技術將小干擾RNA片段轉染入大鼠前扣帶皮質回，使αCaMKII表達沉默，分別檢測正常大鼠與內臟高敏感大鼠的前扣帶回區域神經元的反應及其對結直腸擴張的內臟疼痛反應。採用生物化學分離方法對pACC神經元的亞細胞組分進行分離，以研究突觸后聯合部位αCaMKII與NR2B亞基的遷移特征及兩種分子間的相互作用。αCaMKII在第286位即蘇氨酸進行自動自磷酸化，並且引起這種酶不依賴於Ca2+/CaM結合為特征的持續活化。針對內臟高敏感大鼠，我們將分析磷酸化的CaMKII在前扣帶回皮質神經元突觸后的遷移現象，及其與NR2B增強的相互作用的特征。進一步應用CaMKII抑制肽(CaMKII 281-302)靶向抑制CaMKII 第Thr286位的自動磷酸化，以驗証自動磷酸化的CaMKII的遷移減少，及其與 NR2B亞基結合減少，進而緩解結腸過敏反應誘導的內臟高敏感。本實驗的后期階段，用天冬氨酸替代CaMKII自動磷酸化部位的蘇氨酸(CaMKII T286D)，集中研究大鼠前扣帶回皮質區域神經組織生態表位的遺傳機制。 了解前扣帶回皮質區域神經元的可塑性及慢性內臟痛記憶的細胞與分子機制，可能為我們對功能性胃腸病紊亂的病因學深入認識提供重要線索，為在腦皮質區域治療人類功能性腸病提供可能的手段。

To demonstrate that Thr286 αCaMKII autophosphorylation in the pACC is critical for neuronal plasticity, and mediates visceral pain memory. αCamKII must autophosphorylated to be active and remain active independent of Ca2+/CaM binding. This property of the kinase led to the suggestion that autophosphorylation may function as a biochemical ‘memory’ process that can prolong a sufficiently strong but brief calcium signal into a long-term synaptic change, and memory. This biochemical model can be effectively used to better understand the mechanisms involved in prolong pACC neuronal sensitization, which mediates visceral hypersensitivity after local inflammation in the gut has subsided. To test this hypothesis we plan construct an inhibitory peptide whose sequence is derived from the autoregulatory domain of αCaMKII. Electroporation of this inhibitory peptide to the pACC will be performed, followed by electrophysiological recordings of the pACC and visceral pain response studies.

Characterize the upregulation, translocation of CaMKII to postsynaptic density (PSD), and the enhanced interaction between pCaMKII and NR2B. CaMKII is specifically localized to the cytoplasmic face of isolated postsynaptic density (PSD). Investigators has demonstrated that αCaMKII can bind to several PSD proteins. p-αCaMKII may exert its function at synapses by regulating postsynaptic NMDA receptors. Recent work showed that two different CaMKII interaction domains, residues 839–1120 and 1289–1310, are present in the cytoplasmic tail of NR2B. Interactions with these domains are strengthened by αCaMKII activation and Thr286 autophosphorylation in vitro and in vivo in a Ca2+/CaM-dependent manner. We reasoned that understanding the changes of postsynaptic expression of CaMKII and NMDA receptors, and the alteration of the binding between these two molecules should facilitate identifying the putative molecular mechanisms underlying the pACC sensitization and the memory of visceral pain in the visceral hypersensitive states.

160810.label: Major findings and research outcome
160810.value: 1. The nociceptive abdominal pain response, visceromotor response (VMR) to CRD, was recorded in normal and viscerally hypersensitive rats induced by colonic anaphylaxis. ACC lesions were generated with ibotenic acid. L-glutamate, NMDA receptor antagonist aminophosphonopentanoic acid were microinjected into the ACC. We showed that ACC lesions, and Aminophosphonopentanoic acid significantly suppressed the VMR in VH rats but not in normal rats. Theses observations indicated that the ACC plays a critical role in the modulation of visceral pain responses. This process appears to be mediated by enhanced activities of glutamate N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors. 2. There are multiple downstream signaling pathways linked to the NMDA receptors that may play important roles in plasticity and memory. Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) has been proposed to be critical for its role in long-term potentiation (LTP). To provide irrefutable evidence about the critical role of CaMKII in the mediation of visceral hypersensitivity, we performed pain behavior studies following silencing of CaMKII by local application of specific siRNA into the ACC using electroporation, a technique we have recently established in our laboratory. By silencing CaMKII expression in the ACC we have shown that silencing of CaMKII caused a significant decrease in the VMR in viscerally hypersensitive rats but had no effect in normal rats. 3. CaMKII presented high-affinity binding to the C-terminal tail of the NR2B subunit. Using a biochemical fractionation approach, we prepared ACC all cellular and synaptoneurosomes (SS) fractions. Post-synaptic density fraction (PSD) and extrasynaptic fractions were prepared from SS fractions. The over-expression and synaptic accumulation of NR2B and Thr286CaMKII protein level were observed. Co-immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting were performed to identify the enhanced interaction between CaMKII and the NR2B subunits in PSD. Finally, administration of CaMKII inhibitor, Antennepedia-CaMKIINtide, restored the level of NR2B to control levels in the PSD fraction suggesting blocking of CaMKII binding to NR2B interferes with post-synaptic accumulation of NR2B. This was accompanied with suppression of visceral pain responses in VH rats. 4. Pain contains both sensory and affective dimensions. Using a rodent visceral pain assay that combines the colorectal distension-induced VMR with the conditioning place avoidance, we measured a learned behavior that directly reflects the affective component of visceral pain. We have demonstrated that neurons in the ACC are necessary for the ‘aversiveness’ of visceral pain. ACC activation is critical for the memory processing involved in long-term negative affective state and prediction of aversive stimuli by contextual cue.

160810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
160810.value: In past several years supporting by this GRF project 160810 our study electrophysiological recording showed long-lasting potentiation of local field potential in the medial thalamus (MT)−ACC synapses in VH rats. Theta burst stimulation in the MT reliably induced long-term potentiation in the MT-ACC pathway in normal rat, however, induction of visceral hypersensitivity effectively blocks the expression of LTP at MT-ACC synapses in vivo. It appears that induction of VH produces a change in the ability to induce subsequent synaptic plasticity at the MT-ACC pathway. It seems conceivable that homeostatic metaplasticity is present in the VH state and, perhaps, in inhibitory intracortical circuits. These results imply that chronic visceral pain related emotional and cognitive disorders may typically associated with ACC functional disruption. In continuing and expanding this completed project160810, we hypothesize that the mechanisms of ACC synaptic metaplasticity are involved in the processes of modifying the visceral pain threshold, the aversive responses to pain, and affect the processing learning and memory in chronic pain state. A new Project (CityU 11100914 ) title “Brain astrocytes drive mood and cognitive dysfunction in chronic visceral pain” is current ongoing.

160810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
160810.value: Hypersensitivity to visceral distention has been reported in patients with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Human brain imaging studies have revealed new roles of cortical neuronal networks in chronic visceral pain. Our electrophysiological studies of viscerally hypersensitive (VH) rats have shown that colorectal anaphylaxis resulted in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) sensitization. Measuring behavioral pain responses, we have shown that the enhanced glutamate receptor activities in the ACC were responsible for abdominal pain. Further, ACC activation is critical for memory processing involved in long-term negative emotional state. The hypersensitivity to colonic stimulation could be observed up to 7 weeks following the initiation of colonic anaphylaxis and appears to be independent of mucosal inflammation suggesting an important mechanism for learning and triggering of pain memories in the ACC neuronal circuitry. Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) is enriched at the post-synaptic density (PSD). Localization of CaMKII at the PSD has been proposed to be critical for its role in long-term potentiation (LTP). Our pain behavior studies following silencing of CaMKII by local application of specific siRNA into the ACC showed suppression of visceral pain responses. Our studies further support the therapeutic potential of CaMKII antagonists in treating disorders involving visceral hypersensitivity in IBS patients.

161310.label: Project Objectives
161310.value: The concept of biomedical applications using multifunctional nanocomposites as drug-delivery therapeutic systems and for nuclear or optical imaging has been verified. However, many of the reported nanomedicine platforms are still at the early stage of development, and a number of scientific and technical issues need to be addressed. The objective of the project is to develop multifunctional, heterostructured nanocomposites for targeted imaging and simultaneous photothermal therapy of tumor cells. Specifically, we will focus on the study of three important aspects of nanomedicine, including (1) the establishment of a stable optical sensing system based on fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) with controllable donor-to-acceptor separation distance (2)the establishment of a robust and reproducible method for the assembly of multiple functional components into a nanocomposite (3) the establishment of a stable and biocompatible system with minimal photobleaching for long-term monitoring.

161310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
161310.value: Nanomaterials provide a robust framework in which two or more components can be incorporated to offer synergetic multifunctional nanomedical platforms. The combination of tumor-targeted imaging and therapy in an all-in-one system provides a useful multimodal approach in the battle against cancer. Novel multifunctional nanoparticles thus offer a new avenue in the application of personalized medicine in the near future. In this project, we propose to design and fabricate FRET-based multifunctional heterostructured nano- composites for targeted imaging and simultaneous therapy. Heterostructures consisting of silica nanoparticles which function as fluorescent imaging vehicles, and gold nanomaterials which serve a dual function as fluorescence quencher and irradiation converter, will be assembled using biomolecule-directed strategies. Biomolecules which can specifically recognize cancer cells will be functionalized to gold nanoparticles to serve as targeting molecules, while their complementary pairs will be functionalized to silica nanoparticles for specific assembly of multifunctional nanocomposites. 161310.label: Realisation of objectives
161310.value: The project objectives have been achieved successfully. We have synthesized, functionalized and characterized silica nanoparticles, gold nanoparticles and carbon quantum dots, and assembled them by biomolecule-directed strategy. In the heterostructured nanocomposites, silica nanoparticles acted as fluorescent imaging vehicles, and carbon/gold nanomaterials served a dual function as fluorescence quencher and irradiation converter. The heterostructured nanocomposites have been used for analysis of cell extracts, targeted cell imaging and cellular uptake. Hybrid of carbon quantum dots and gold nanoparticles has been demonstrated for discriminative detection of glutathione in human plasma. Peptide-bridged assembly of silica nanoparticles and gold nanoparticles has been applied for caspase-3 detection in cell lysate. Fluorescent dye-doped silica nanoparticles with different functional groups and/or specific surface markers have been designed and synthesized for targeted cell imaging and therapy. The mechanism of cellular uptake of the nanoparticles in both cancer cells and cancer stem cells have been investigated for better understanding of the cell-nanoparticle interactions.

161310.label: Major findings and research outcome
161310.value: (1) We have designed and fabricated a hybrid of carbon quantum dots (CQDs) and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs), which served as a dual-mode nanosensor with both colorimetric and fluorometric readout. CQDs served as fluorometric reporter, and AuNPs served a dual function as colorimetric reporter and fluorescence quencher. Through controlling the surface properties of as-prepared nanoparticles, the addition of CQDs into AuNPs colloid solution induced the aggregation of AuNPs and CQDs, leading to AuNPs color changing from red to blue and CQDs fluorescence quench. The nanosensor reflects on its simplicity and flexibility, where no further surface functionalization is required for the as-prepared nanoparticles, leading to less laborious and more cost-effective synthesis. (2) We have further synthesized a “satellite”-shaped hybrid nanomaterial consisting of fluorescent dye encapsulated silica nanoparticles (SiNPs) and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) through peptide-bridged assembly in a controllable way. A peptide that contained recognition sequence DEVD specific for active caspase-3 cleavage was employed to bring SiNPs and AuNPs into close proximity through specific molecular recognition. A fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) system with SiNPs as energy donors and AuNPs as energy acceptors has been developed, in which a change in distance between the two building blocks resulted in a change in FRET efficiency, causing a ratiometric change in emission. (3) We have utilized functionalized SiNPs for targeted cell imaging and investigated uptake mechanisms of SiNPs with different surface charges and/or specific surface markers. We have used pharmacological inhibitors respectively to inhibit major endocytic pathways in both lung cancer cells and lung cancer stem cells, and found that SiNPs entered cells via active energy dependent processes, but different pathways involved in the two types of cells. We suggested that SiNPs uptake in cancer cells was strongly affected by actin depolymerization, but it were internalized by cancer stem cells via a different route that involved the scavenger receptors-mediated endocytosis pathway.

161310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
161310.value: The research project has developed a set of multifunctional heterostructured nanocomposites for targeted cell imaging, cellular uptake and analysis of cell extracts. Heterostructures consisting of silica nanoparticles which function as fluorescent imaging vehicles, and carbon/gold nanomaterials which serve a dual function as fluorescence quencher and irradiation converter, have be assembled using biomolecule-directed strategies. The nanohybrid composites assembly is ultrasensitive and highly selective, which could be significant in disease diagnosis with proper optimization in the future. In addition, through tailoring the bridging biomolecules or employing different nanocomponents for the targets, it is feasible to develop different nanosensors using the FRET model. For targeted cell imaging and drug delivery, as the existence of differential uptake pathways for the same SiNP in cancer cells and cancer stem cells, it is possible to design nanocarries as useful candidates for targeted cancer imaging, simultaneous therapy and drug delivery sensing.

The project has emphasized the importance in the areas of material science, analytical chemistry and cell biology, and has direct relevance to the development of nanomedicine. 200210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
200210.value: 在生物或物理現像的數學建模中，模型的狀態（如：種群數量、延伸的聚乙烯片的形狀對於平衡狀態的偏移）也依賴於過去的歷史（‘記憶效應’），因為常微分方程不包含延遲項，所以這時常微分方程已經不能提供可行的模型。因此，考慮到記憶的影響，延遲微分方程和最近的Volterra 泛函積分和微分方程已經在生物和物理科學的數學建模中擔當了越來越重要的角色，這些方程中的延遲函數不僅依賴於當前時刻，而且依賴於未知函數或未知狀態（狀態依賴延遲）。 因為描述這些數學模型的泛函方程非常復雜，並且一般不能解析求解，對於這些數學模型的分析，有效的、精確的數值方法就成為了關鍵的工具。另一方面，這些方法的設計要求深入了解這些泛函方程背後的數學性質（存在性、唯一性和解的正則性）。 狀態依賴延遲微分方程的理論和（可能較小程度的）數值分析目前已經得到充分理解。和Volterra 泛函積分和泛函積分微分方程的當前狀態的鮮明對比是：雖然對於不依賴於狀態的變延遲方程，數值分析和計算解在過去的十年裡已經取得了很大進展，但是對於狀態依賴Volterra 泛函方程卻沒有系統的研究。 這份研究計劃的目的就是朝著填補這個缺陷邁一大步。具體來說，我們將對狀態依賴Volterra 泛函方程的潛在的最有效的方法，即配置方法和（相關的）Runge-Kutta方法的數值解建立收斂性（和超收斂性）理論。我們也研究比如我們前面提到的具體的數學模型的數值模擬的實際應用。在該研究計劃中產生的結果將很大程度地增加我們對如何最好地數值求解狀態依賴延遲Volterra 泛函方程的理解。因此，本工作期望能為研究由這些方程描述的模型的有效且精確的數值模擬的研究者提供一個有力的新工具。

200210.value: 1. The fundamental paper 2 presents a complete analysis of the asymptotic stability properties of collocation and implicit Runge-Kutta methods for delay differential equations with vanishing proportional delays. 2. The above papers also discuss the computational implementation of collocation and discontinuous Galerkin methods for the functional equations described above. 4. Owing to insufficient time, the work on concrete case studies (application of, and numerical simulation by, collocation and discontinuous Galerkin methods to particular mathematical models involving Volterra functional equations with state-dependent delays) is still ongoing.

200310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
200310.value: Many drug-induced toxic effects involve disturbed endogenous metabolites because the metabolite profiles and concentrations in blood and urine may be related to the toxic processes. The toxicity-induced disequilibria are often reflected in the biofluids. Evidence accumulated has shown 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (2,3,7,8-TCDD or TCDD) leads to extreme toxicity mainly through aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). Metabolomics research based on mass spectrometry and pattern-recognition methods has been used to classify the samples as being normal or abnormal, to identify biomarkers of toxic effects, and to evaluate time course of the effects. In this study, we will develop and apply mass spectrometry methods for studying metabolic phenotype associated with toxic effects of TCDD. Liquid chromatography/quadrupole-time of flight mass spectrometry (LC/QTOFMS)-based untargeted metabolomics will be applied to investigate the TCDD toxic effects in AhR high affinity strain-C57BL/6J wild type mice. Mouse urine and plasma will be analyzed by combining the platform of mass spectrometry and pattern-recognition data analysis. Difference in the TCDD toxicological responses between the non-, low- and high-dosed mice will be investigated and compared. In addition, metabolic phenotype of TCDD in AhR low affinity strain-DBA/2J mice will also be analyzed and compared. For the identification and confirmation of potential metabolites, targeted metabolomics approach will be developed by using ultra-high performance liquid chromatography coupled with triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (UPLC/TQMS) in multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mode and gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (GC/MS) in selected ion monitoring (SIM) mode. The obtained results will not only provide useful information for designing novel strategies to investigate toxicity of TCDD, but also contribute to the researches toward our long-term goal of developing diagnostics for TCDD-associated diseases such as the type 2 diabetes. 药物引起的毒性反映可体现在内源性代谢物的扰动，因为血液和尿液中的代谢物轮廓与浓度跟毒性过程相关。毒物引发的代谢不平衡状态也常常表现在生物流体当中, 已有文献报导2378-TCDD（二噁英中最毒的一种化合物）可通过芳香烃受体的作用从而导致极大的毒性。基于质谱和模式识别方法的代谢组学研究已经被应用于区分正常与异常的代谢状态；鉴定毒性相关的生物标记物；以及评估毒性反映的时间依赖性。在本项研究中，我们将开发和应用质谱方法，并用于研究与2378-TCDD毒性相关的代谢表型。本项目将利用液相色谱 - 四级杆飞行时间质谱的全局代谢组学分析方法考察2378-TCDD在芳香烃受体高亲和力的小鼠模型（C57BL/6J）的毒性效果。质谱与模式识别方法将应用于分析小鼠尿样和血浆。通过比较空白组、低剂量和高剂量组的差异，从代谢角度了解TCDD的毒性效果。另外，我们也将分析和比较2378-TCDD在芳香烃受体低亲和力的小鼠模型（DBA/2J）的代谢物组，基于超高效液相 - 三重四级杆质谱的多反应检测模式和气相色谱 - 质谱的选择离子检测模式的目标性分析途径将会被应用到鉴定和确证潜在的代谢物。本项目所得到的结果将不仅为考察TCDD毒性提供有用信息，而且将会为考察TCDD毒性相关的疾病，比如2型糖尿病奠定研究基础。

200310.label: Realisation of objectives
200310.value: Mouse models of high affinity to Ah receptor (C57BL/6J) and low affinity (DBA/2J) were dosed with various levels of TCDD and exposure time. As proposed, urine and blood samples were collected and prepared for LC-QTOFMS analysis. In addition, tissue samples were also analyzed. The mass spectrometric parameters were optimized with QA control in order to achieve the best metabolic coverage and quality. The metabolites were detected from LC-QTOFMS analysis combined with pattern recognition software and metabolome database. The identification was confirmed from the comparison with authentic standard. After the metabolites identification, the disturbed metabolic networks induced by TCDD were described based on KEGG databases. To confirm metabolic networks, absolute quantification was performed on UPLC-TQMS in MRM mode and GC-MS in SIM mode. GC-MS was not only applied for analysis of relatively non-polar compounds, but also for covering polar metabolites after sample derivatization. Instrument conditions were optimized to achieve the lowest detection limits because levels of biomarkers in samples were very low. Mouse blood samples were collected and prepared for the trace analysis of TCDD by using GC/high resolution MS. The obtained TCDD levels were not only compared with those environmental biological samples to evaluate the exposure, but also with the TCDD detection in control samples. The levels were co-related to metabolomics results for investigation of environmental toxicity of TCDD. While the metabolites of TCDD itself were not detected in mouse blood samples, in vitro metabolism study was conducted for data validation. TCDD was detected in the in vitro samples with the proposed detection limit. The metabolic networks were confirmed with the targeted metabolomics approach using UPLC-TQMS and GC-MS. The metabolomics analysis of urine, plasma and tissue samples from the mice with non-, low- and high-doses of TCDD generated many data points. The data interpretation was performed by using pattern recognition and multivariate statistical methods. The PCA algorithm within the MS data package for metabolomics allowed comparison of results. Least squares-support vector machine was used for classification and prediction. The discrimination of TCDD-induced mice from the wild type mice was investigated based on metabolic profiles. The profiles of TCDD-induced toxic effects were found to reflect both normal variation and impact of toxicity. The toxicity of TCDD was related to metabolic changes, such as lipid peroxidation, fatty acid beta-oxidation, fatty acid accumulation and amino acid metabolism.

200310.label: Major findings and research outcome
200310.value: C57BL/6J wild type and DBA/2J mice were fed with TCDD-containing corn oil at various exposure levels and time periods. Biological samples including urine, blood and tissues were collected and prepared for metabolomics analysis. The sample extracts were cleaned up and analyzed by using the developed GC-MS and LC-MS methods. MS/MS analysis with the accurate mass measurement was used for the detection and identification of metabolites. The MS data interpretation relied on pattern recognition and multivariate statistical methods to derive information from a large number of variables. The PCA algorithm within the GC-MS and LC-MS data package for metabolomics allowed comparison of results obtained from the same conditions. Least squares-support vector machines (LS-SVM) was used for classification and prediction. The obtained GC-MS and LC-MS profiles of the wild type mice administrated with non-, low- and high-doses of TCDD were summaired and compared for the investigation on metabolic profiles of TCDD-induced toxic effects through pattern recognition data analysis. The comparison generated information of both normal variation and impact of toxicity. The associations of dose- and time responses, blood TCDD levels and TCDD-induced toxicity from the interpretation of metabolic profiles and metabolite identification were then further investigated. The obtained data indicated that fatty acids may transfer from adipose tissue to liver in TCDD-sensitive mice based on the obtained results. The intermediate metabolites in glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, TCA cycle and fatty acid biosynthesis were identified. It should be noted that in addition to the originally proposed analysis of mouse urine and blood samples, we have also collected and analyzed mouse tissues. Metabolomic profiles based on mass spectrometry delineated the biochemical changes in serum, liver, skeletal muscle as well as hippocampus tissues in mice and rats exposed to TCDD. The toxicity of TCDD showed a wide spectrum of metabolic changes, such as lipid peroxidation, fatty acid beta-oxidation, fatty acid accumulation and amino acid metabolism.

200310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
200310.value: The developed GC-MS and LC-MS methods have extensive significance for other persistent organic pollutants (e.g., dioxin-like PCBs and PBDEs) for their disease-associated toxicity. As food intake is the major dioxin exposure and the dioxin contamination has caused significant public and environmental concerns in Hong Kong, the outcome of this research will have impact on scientific studies on relations between the possible dioxin exposure and toxicity. The outcome of this research may benefit the design of novel metabolomics strategies to investigate TCDD-induced diseases through biomarker identification. Because many data in MS spectra contain signals from metabolites that are associated with specific targets for toxicity, data interpretation may potentially provide information on the discovery of biomarkers. The obtained metabolomics results not only provide useful information for designing novel strategies to investigate toxicity of TCDD, but also contribute to research toward our long-term goal of developing diagnostics for TCDD-associated diseases such as the type 2 diabetes. Because the identified metabolites may lead to a better understanding of metabolic pathways associated with toxicity, we propose to confirm the biomarker identification with other tools of biological sciences and further study the relationship of dioxin exposure with human disease, in particular the diabetes.

200310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
200310.value: Dioxins are persistent organic pollutants (POPs) that have been widely distributed in food chain. Evidence accumulated has shown 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (2,3,7,8-TCDD or TCDD) leads to extreme toxicity mainly through aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). Metabolomics approach has been proved to have the potential for assessing toxicity and disease. In this project, metabolomics research based on mass spectrometry and pattern-recognition methods was used to classify the samples as being normal or abnormal, to identify biomarkers of toxic effects, and to evaluate time course of the effects. Mass spectrometry methods including GC-MS and LC-MS were developed for studying metabolic phenotype associated with toxic effects of TCDD. LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomics was applied to investigate the TCDD toxic effects in AhR high affinity strain-C57BL/6J wild type mice. Mouse urine, plasma and tissues were analyzed. Difference in the TCDD toxicological responses between the non-, low- and high-dosed mice were investigated and compared, and the metabolic phenotype of TCDD in AhR low affinity strain-DBA/2J mice was analyzed and compared. Ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-triple quadrupole mass spectrometry in multiple reaction monitoring mode and GC-MS in selected ion monitoring mode were used for targeted metabolomics, which not only confirmed the biomarker detection but also quantified their levels.

200610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
200610.value: All-optical probes for chemical analysis are long sought after. Two candidate methods are most notable. One is laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) which is wonderfully versatile and simple but has unremarkable sensitivity. The other is laser-excited atomic fluorescence (LEAF)which is phenomenally sensitive but is not user-friendly. Our group recently demonstrated that the best of both worlds was possible. We first created a dense plume with a laser pulse that desorbed a minute amount of the sample mass from the material target. We then excited the multi plume species by 193-nm laser photons. The analytes subsequently emitted their respective fluorescence fingerprints for chemical analysis. We showed that this plume-LEAF technique was hundreds to thousands fold more sensitive than LIBS while preserving its versatility. We now propose to apply our method to tackle three important but challenging analytical problems. First is the nondestructive chemical analysis of the ink of written lines on questioned documents. Second is the three-dimensional chemical profiling of metal-organic interfaces of organic electronic devices to help pin-point failure mechanisms. Third is the detection of trace metals in proteins that are dispersed in two-dimensional gels. This is a key enabling step in metallomics study. Currently, solutions to the three problems are either cumbersome or simply nonexistent. We envisage that the experience gained from these applications can be generalized to other equally relevant and difficult surface analysis problems of our time. 為求以激光作化學分析, 有兩個方法甚俱潛力。一個是激光擊穿光譜法 (LIBS)。它的應用性廣，但靈敏度不高。另一個是激光原子螢光法 (LEAF)。它的靈敏度高但極難操作。 最近，我們發明了 “氣團 – LEAF” 這個新技術。它集 LIBS 和 LEAF 的長處。我們首先把激光聚焦在樣本的表面，將微量的物質蒸發成氣團。繼以 193nm 的激光截擊氣團。其中的多種成份遂發螢光，立可識別。 這方法比 LIBS 要靈敏上百至千倍。操作上又較 LEAF 簡易。我們現計畫用它作三種分折。其一是筆跡的無損化學分折。其二是金屬和有機物的介面分折，以助了解有機電子器件的故障。其三是測量蛋白質內的痕量金屬。 目前，上述三個課題都沒有簡易的解決方案，甚或沒有任何方案。我們的新技術不但對症下藥，而且更可推廣至其他相關的課題。

200610.label: Realisation of objectives
200610.value: Objective 1. We have successfully analyzed the elemental composition of five different kinds of written black ink under non-destructive conditions. The results were reported in Chu 2011. Upon suggestion from forensic chemists, we then extended our work to the analysis of laser printed black ink. We successfully identified four different kinds of toners, again under nondestructive conditions. We were able to profile the ink layers and could differentiate the order of overprinting, as well as being able to tell the 'age' of the ink since printing. The results were published in Chu 2013. We have since extended the analysis to Chinese ink on xuan paper for the purpose of analyzing artworks. A manuscript (Cheung 2014) reporting our results is attached. Objective 2. We did 355 nm ablation and measured the z-profile of ITO-PEN. We found the thermal damage excessive so we switched to 193 nm ablation. We got very positive initial results but the supply of excimer gas was unexpectedly delayed so we could not finish that part of the work before the project deadline. Objective 3. We did PLEAF analysis of lobster hepatopancreas tissue homogenates. Got very encouraging results. We will do more definitive studies before we want to publish our findings.

200610.label: Major findings and research outcome
200610.value: Major findings are 1. PLEAF analysis of inks and pigments was highly sensitive, with relative LOD in the tens to hundreds of ppb and mass LOD in the amol to tens of amol range. We could sort various brands of ball pen inks and laser printed black inks on copier papers, and Chinese black inks on xuan papers without inducing visible damage to the sample. See Chu 2011, Chu 2013, and Cheung 2014. 2. Elemental depth profiling at hundreds of nm resolution with detection sensitivity comparable to dynamic SIMS was demonstrated. However, thermal damage at 355-nm laser ablation was excessive. See Chu 2011.

200610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
200610.value: We developed a material analysis technique using laser excited fluorescence of gas plumes that were produced in pulsed laser ablation. Its major advantages were (1) universal applicability in terms of sample form and elements to be analyzed, (2) high sensitivity in the sub-ppm and atto-mole range, (3) being all optical so it was compatible with air, non-contact and it could reach awkward sites, (4) requiring zero sample preparation, and (5) very fast, producing tens of data spectra per second. We demonstrated the unambiguous identification of various kinds of ink on paper. The damage to the sample was so minuscule that no marks were visible even under the microscope. The technique would find applications in forensic analysis as well as in the authentication of artworks.

200710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
200710.value: This project proposes and studies four different spatial models. For a spatial point process, each point is associated with a non-overlapping polygon containing the point. We start from the polygon containing the origin and then build the first layer, the second layer and so on. The limiting shape of the union of the first m layers, when m goes to infinity, is conjectured to be related to the underlying intensity function of the point process. In particular, if the intensity is invariant under rotation, the limiting shape is believed to be spherical. Ways to construct statistics for testing isotropy are also proposed. Given an initial configuration of particles in some space, such as the d-dimensional Euclidean space, we add particles sequentially according to the following construction rule. We randomly choose one particle from the existing ones and then add a new particle such that the location of the new particle is a random variable the distribution of which depends on the geometry of the chosen particle and its neighbours. Therefore, particles in such a sequential process exhibit a certain local interaction, suggesting the name locally interacting sequential process. The project intends to find weak or minimal conditions under which the support of the limiting measure is bounded. We consider the asymptotic variance of vacancy (AVV) in the high-intensity small-grain Boolean model. Subjecting the grains to rotations or, more generally, linear distortions gives rise to a function which maps distortion distributions to the AVV of the corresponding Boolean model. We would study continuity properties of this function, related optimisation problems, and the geometry of the typical connected vacant region. A spatial process Z is anisotropic if the dependence between Z(x) and Z(x+h) is a function of both the magnitude and the direction of the lag vector h. Consider an anisotropic model with an ellipsoidal covariance structure, characterised by a positive definite matrix Q such that the anisotropy can be “corrected” to the second-order isotropy by transforming h to h’Qh. Such an anisotropic model gives rise to the so-called geometrically anisotropic processes. A doubly stochastic version can be obtained by randomising Q via its representation P’DP, where P is a rotation and D a diagonal matrix. This project aims at developing mathematical or numerically tractable representations for the mean variogram of such a doubly stochastic geometrically anisotropic spatial process. 200710.label: Realisation of objectives
200710.value: Consider a Boolean model, which is a union of iid random closed sets, called grains, centred at germs that form a stationary Poisson process in the k-dimensional Euclidean space. We proposed a model that incorporates anisotropy by applying a random rotation matrix independently to each grain, and then further generalized the model to allow distortion of each grain by applying an independent random linear transformation the absolute value of the logarithm of the maximum eigenvalue of which is bounded by a parameter. The quantity known as asymptotic variance of vacancy has been investigated in details. Optimality, continuity and convergence properties have been established. To introduce anisotropic structure not to the grains but to the germs, the proposal originally suggests a model with ellipsoidal covariance structure. However, because of the need of such anisotropic models in applications, there have been many other people considering the same problem and it turned out the PI has lost the chance to claim the scientific priority for the problem of this geometric anisotropic model, as Jesper Møller and Håkon Toftaker released their study of this model in January 2012. To change the Poisson nature of the germs, the PI considered in particular the one-dimensional Euclidean space, whose topology allows us to replace the Poisson process by a renewal process. Such a generalization has no straightforward analogue in higher-dimensional space. However, if the grains are interpreted as claim sizes, then such a germ-grain model on the line can be interpreted as a risk process, and we studied the complete monotonicity of various quantities of practical interest, such as the ruin probability, the Laplace transform of the ruin time and the density of the deficit at ruin. For statistical estimation and tests, we developed an asymptotic model-free test for testing stationarity and a bootstrap-type but model-free test for testing isotropy of a given d-dimensional point pattern. The test statistic for stationarity is an integral of the deviation between observed and expected counts of points in expanding regions of the sampling window in the d-dimensional and all lower dimensional spaces. The isotropy test requires generation of bootstrap samples without specifying the underlying model; the idea is to shift points in a generated sample in order to minimize the discrepancy between the non-orientation structure of the given pattern and that of the generated pattern. We developed a quick estimation method to estimate Mecke’s morphological function used in this test.

200710.label: Major findings and research outcome
200710.value: For the asymptotic variance of vacancy (AVV), we showed that the AVV is the least when the distribution of the rotation component in QR decomposition of the distortion transformation is the Haar measure, and is a continuous functional of the distortion distribution under the Wasserstein distance; under certain conjugation invariance assumptions, the Wasserstein distance can be replaced by the supremum norm; for a Kac’s random walk of rotations, the AVV converges at an explicitly known rate. More details were reported in [1] and as an invited talk in the 2nd IMS-APRM conference. For the risk process, we proved that the ruin probability, the Laplace transform of the ruin time, and the density of the tail of the joint distribution of ruin and the deficit at ruin in the Sparre Andersen model are completely monotone if the claim size density is completely monotone. The machinery used in the proof is to show that the complete monotonicity is preserved under mixed geometric compounding. The results were given in [2]. We extended Guan’s (2008, Biometrics) stationarity test by incorporating deviations from stationarity in lower dimensional spaces and by constructing wisely the expanding integration domain where the deviations are calculated. The limiting null distributions are expressed as integrals of a Brownian sheet and hence asymptotic critical values can be approximated. Simulation studies showed that our test would be always more powerful than Guan’s. When applied to the longleaf pine data that Guan’s test gave an inconclusive answer, our test indicated a clear rejection of the stationarity hypothesis. The study was published as [3] and presented in the 9th ICSA conference. For testing isotropy, we developed an iterative algorithm that shifts randomly chosen points in a generated isotropic pattern to minimize the discrepancy between the non-orientation structure of the given pattern and that of the generated pattern, without specifying the underlying model. (A similar iterative method was also developed for minimizing the empirical MSE in ridge regression and outperformed 26 existing ridge estimation methods; this has been reported in [4]). Simulation studies showed that our approach outperforms the existing chi-squared test by Guan et al. (2006) in the sense that the latter depends heavily on the choice of the scale and smoothing parameters but ours does not. When applied to real data, our test is able to detect anisotropy in patterns that exhibit some local orientation correlation, while the chi-squared test fails. This will be reported in [5].

200710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
200710.value: This project developed two one-sample model-free tests for spatial point patterns. A very natural further development is a two-sample model-free test for testing equal distribution for two given point patterns. This is very different from the analogous problem in classic statistics because points in a point pattern are correlated in very complicated ways and each sample consists of one pattern only so that no replicates are available for estimation; in fact, working without specifying the underlying model makes it impossible to estimate any covariance structure as there are infinitely many possibilites. However, when developing the stationarity test and isotropy test, we noticed the possibility of having an asymptotic model-free chi-squared test for testing equal distribution of two given point patterns. Some other asymptotic methods have also been inspired. These ideas will be written up as a GRF proposal to seek support for future endeavour.

200710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
200710.value: This project led to five major outcomes. First, a new model for spatial patterns resulted from random independent distortions applied to grains in a germ-grain model was proposed and studied in details. Second, a condition on the claim size distribution for the complete monotonicity property of many interesting quantities of a risk process was found. Third, an asymptotic test for testing stationarity of a given spatial point pattern was developed and was shown to be more powerful than the sole test available in the literature. Fourth, an iterative method for ridge regression estimation was proposed, which outperformed 26 existing methods. Fifth, a model-free test for testing isotropy of a given stationary spatial point pattern was suggested; the new test was better than the existing one in the sense that it would be less sensitive on the user-chosen parameters, without sacrificing its power in detecting deviation from isotropy at the same significance level.

200910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
200910.value: The Richtmyer-Meshkov instability and the Rayleigh-Taylor instability are two major driving forces in the turbulent mixing of compressible fluids/gases. Reduction of the turbulent mixing in the Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF) in experimental apparatus for generation of environmentally clean nuclear fusion energy is important as the turbulent mixing causes a loss of compression of the nuclear fuel. The lose of pressure energy might result in reduction of efficiency or in some case, a total failure of fusion ignition. Design of high order high resolution numerical schemes and the simulations of the 3D large system of PDE are critical in understanding the behavior of such physical phenomenon and in designing experiments. The simulations, however, depending on the setup of the problem, might require computational resources beyond what is currently available. There is an urgent need to reduce the large system of equations (in billions) into a smaller system which would maintain the fidelity of the solution within a range of acceptable accuracy. This is the system reduction problem. Methods for this problem have been studied by A. Chorin and recently further developed by Gottlieb et al. We aim to study, both theoretically and numerically, the new technique of Optimal Replacement Variables for systems of nonlinear equations. The technique if proven successful would significantly improve and expand the scope of simulations of large-scale complicated physical systems. Optimal Replacement Variables (ORV) is a method for approximating a large system of ODEs by one with fewer equations, while attempting to preserve the essential dynamics of a reduced set of variables of interest. An earlier version of ORV [1] had some issues, including limited accuracy and in some rare cases, instability. Here we present a new version of ORV, inspired by the linear quadratic regulator problem of control theory, which provides better accuracy, a guarantee of stability and is in some ways easier to use.

200910.label: Major findings and research outcome
200910.value: The new ORV method introduces a new and more natural criterion for the dynamic accuracy of a reduced system, and develops the machinery necessary to optimize the new criterion. The resulting new reduced system works well on the problems it has been tested against that it has better accuracy for the heat equation and has guaranteed stability, at least in the alpha equal to zero case. Furthermore, it does not require the user provide a suitable-for-all-time probability density on the phase space. Finally, the associated minimization problem has a unique local minimum. We have developed a novel Mapped Hybrid Central-WENO finite difference scheme that is accurate and efficient for simulating multi-dimensional combustion problems. To detect the smooth and discontinuous parts of the solutions, a high order multi-resolution algorithm by Harten is used. A tangent domain mapping is used to cluster grid points near the detonation front in order to enhance the grid resolution within half reaction zone that drives the development of complex nonlinear wave structures behind the front. Several numerical comparisons among the uniformly spaced WENO-Z scheme, the WENO-Z scheme and the Hybrid scheme with the domain mapping in simulations of classical stable and unstable detonation waves are conducted. Results showed that the increased grid resolution in the half reaction zone by the Mapped WENO-Z scheme and the Mapped Hybrid scheme allows a significant increased effiency and accuracy over a highly resolved uniformly spaced WENO-Z scheme. To further reduce the computational cost and to avoid wave reflection from the artificial computational boundary of a truncated physical domain, an efficient and easily implemented one dimensional Perfectly Matched Layer (PML) absorbing boundary condition (ABC) for the two dimensional unsteady reactive Euler equation. Numerical comparisons among characteristic, free stream, extrapolation and PML boundary conditions showed that PML boundary condition is the best choice to absorb the outgoing waves while minimizing the wave reflection from the artificial computational boundary. Also, the larger amplitude of perturbation wave generated more smaller scale structures of detonation wave due to more energy is released when the shock fronts came across the strong perturbation wave. The number of cell structures depends on the wave number of sinusoidal perturbation. Regular rectangular combustion cell, pockets of unburned gas and bubbles and spikes are generated and generally well resolved in the simulations and agree well with the published theoretical and numerical results in the literature.

200910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
200910.value: The improved version of ORV fixes many of the issues of the original ORV, but has some possibly-limiting qualities of its own: 1. It is probably more difficult to extend this version of ORV to nonlinear problems. 2. Evaluating the error function and its gradient is more complex than for the original ORV. Not necessarily in the sense of the amount of CPU time required, but in the sense of the number of equations and amount of software required. This may make it harder to generalize or extend. The stable and non-oscillatory contact interface is still an open questions that is urgently needed to be addressed in some satisfactory ways. The design of approximated Riemann solver based on other relevant adaptive conservative/primitive variables is interesting in term of accuracy and efficiency.

201210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
201210.value: Suralose is an artificial sweetener that attracts a lot of enviromentalists’ attentions in recent years. It is considered as an emerging contaminant, due to its persistence and ubiquitous occurrence in the environment. To date, little is known about the environmental ramifications of this emerging contaminant upon entering sensitive marine ecosystems. The consequences of chronic exposure over an extended period of time remains unclear, where the interaction of sucralose with the aquatic environment is still unknown. This present proposed work, first aims to develop and validate sensitive liquid chromatography-mass spectrometric (LC-MS) methods for the determination of sucralose and its transformation products in the environment. Special emphasis will be put on the study of transformation mechanism and the pathways. Toxicity of the generated degradates will then be evaluated using bioassay methods for preliminary assessment of their possible environmental impacts. The efficiency of catalytic photolysis in the removal of this recalcitrant emerging contaminant is also the focus of this present proposal. Knowledge of the identities of transformation products, their transformation mechanisms and pathways together with their possible toxicity is important for an extension of the database required for a comprehensive environmental risk assessment. The success of the present work would reduce health risks and is particularly important for wastewater that is recycled into a system that will be used as a potable water resource.

201210.value: A comprehensive environmental study was undertaken to evaluate and characterize the environmental fate of the four most commonly used artificial sweeteners acesulfame, cyclamate, saccharin and sucralose. As a start, an analytical method was developed based on ultra performance liquid chromatography triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (UPLC-QqQ) for the quantitative determination of target analytes. To achieve that, a solid-phase extraction protocol was tailored and optimized to obtain sample enrichment and clean-up for all targeted artificial sweeteners. Analyte recovery and method sensitivity were satisfactory and fit for the analysis of all target compounds at trace ppt levels. In this study, we have firstly investigated the occurrence profile in an open maritime system. Sample were analysed at selected locations about the marine environment of Hong Kong to draw linkage between distribution patterns and seasonal/geographical features and the chemical nature of the sweeteners. In order to examine the environmental fate of the two most persistent sweeteners known, we studied the photo-degradation chemistry of acesulfame and sucralose, as well as to systematically evaluate any short-term marine toxicity induced by UV irradiation. An in-house UV-irradiation chamber was set-up for the photocatalysis experiment and UPLC-TQ MS used to monitor and elucidate the transformation profile and structural identities of the degradation intermediates. Photodegradates were systematically fractionated, lyophilized and screened for their combined acute toxicity to bioluminescent bacteria. To our knowledge, this is the first time that the phototoxicity of acesulfame and sucralose were systematically quantified and compared. In long term to alleviate the threat from and sustain a safer use of artificial sweeteners, the application of a more efficient retention/removal barrier in wastewater treatment becomes a necessary task. Nowadays, photo-disinfection by means of UV irradiation has already received recognition in wastewater and drinking water purification works. It is also important to remark that with the use of oxidants, photocatalytic treatment is an increasingly promising way to cope with refractory organic pollutants. For this reason, the present study explored the feasibility of TiO2-assisted photocatalysis to achieve complete mineralization. Results from this aspect of our study offer a practical solution for the problem of developing effective pollution control of artificial sweeteners.

201210.label: Major findings and research outcome
201210.value: As a first step in the comprehensive study of artificial sweeteners, this work elucidates the geographical/seasonal/hydrological interactions of acesulfame, cyclamate, saccharin and sucralose in an open coast system at an estuarine/marine junction. Higher occurrence of acesulfame (seasonal average: 0.22 μg L-1) and sucralose (0.05 μg L-1) was found in summer while saccharin (0.11μg L-1) and cyclamate (0.10 μg L-1) were predominantly detected in winter. Seasonal observations of the four sweeteners suggest strong connections with chemical resistance of each sweetener. Our photodegradation investigation further projected the potential impact of the most persistent sweeteners--acesulfame and sucralose under prolonged exposure to intensive solar irradiation. Real-time degradation profile obtained by UPLC-TQ MS illustrated the formation of new photo by-products under prolonged UV irradiation. Upon photocatalytic treatment in sucralose, a major degradation intermediate with a molecular ion at m/z 216 could be tentatively identified as a fructose moiety, namely 1,6-dichloro-1,6-dideoxyfructose with an empirical formula C6H10O4Cl2, consistent with a bond cleavage occurring adjacent to the six-membered glycoside. Furthermore, the inspection of the base peak at m/z 411 revealed the possibility of monohydroxylation to the parent molecule. Formation of higher mass degradates as observed suggested the presence of even more complex reactions involving oxidation and recombination. As for acesulfame, its photo-degradates could be categorized into two groups based on distinctive kinetic profiles. Group I, which comprised four ions with base peaks at m/z 154, 180, 194 and 212, was characterized by rapid transformation: the presence of acetoacetamide-N-sulfonic acid (m/z 180) due to ring breakage could be tentatively identified. Group II comprised molecular ions with m/z 82, 96, 136, 138, 215, 231 and 328 with much slower reaction response. The appearance of m/z 96 was consistent with aminosulfonic acid. Interestingly, Group II was found to be at least six times more persistent than the parent compound. For the first time, acute toxicity for the degradates of both sweeteners were compared, revealing photo-enhancement factors of 575 and 17.1 for acesulfame and sucralose, respectively. The higher phototoxicity and stronger persistence of acesulfame’s degradates implied that this sweetener renders greater impact to aquatic ecosystems. The feasibility of UV/TiO2 as an effective mineralization process in wastewater treatment was evaluated for both sweeteners. Under an environmental and technical relevant condition, a >84% removal rate recorded within 30 min and complete photo-mineralization was achieved within 2 hr and delivering the best cost efficiency comparing to existing removal methods. All research findings on the artificial sweeteners’ occurrence, photodegradation, toxicity evaluation and attenuation strategy were documented and published in a peer-reviewed journal article (Sang, Z., Jiang, Y., Tsoi, Y.-K., Leung, K.S.-Y., 2014. Evaluating the environmental impact of artificial sweeteners: A study of their distributions, photodegradation and toxicities. Water Research 52, 260-274.)

201210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
201210.value: Further development of the research will be directed towards advanced chemical analysis and toxicological assessment of photodegradation products. Acesulfame, found to be of higher environmental risk, will be a concerning target of research. Identities of individual transformation intermediates and products will be confirmed by comprehensive structural characterizations by different techniques, including LC-QTOFMS and NMR, based on which mechanism and transformation pathways will be established. Results will support better understanding and initial guidelines on the degradation process to mitigate environmental burden due to persistent acesulfame. A thorough study into the ecotoxicological impact of acesulfame degradates is proposed using a battery of biotests. Toxic effects due to short-term and prolonged exposure by crustaceans and aquatic vertebrates will be measured in a variety of biological models using freshwater fleas, seawater shrimps and zebrafish embryos. Integrated with findings on the transformation and fate of acesulfame, the entire set of toxicity data should provide not only a broader database for comprehensive environmental risk assessment, but also novel insight guiding prospective research on improved waste attenuation for a more sustainable environment.

201210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
201210.value: In this work, we set out to firstly investigate the current pollution state of the four sweeteners in marine environment, where acesulfame and sucralose where the most ubiquitous due to their known chemical stability. Comprehensive studies were then launched only to found out that acesulfame presents higher environment risk for it is able to liberate, under UV exposure in the environment, degradation products that are much more toxic and persistent than acesulfame itself. For the first time, acesulfame and sucralose were compared side-by-side for their photodegradation chemistry and toxicology. At this stage, current knowledge of the identities of photo-degradates and the transformation mechanism leading to them is critical for improving attenuation strategies for acesulfame contamination. Especially, photocatalysis using oxidative UV treatment was proven effective in present study. Continuous progress along this line will need to emphasize not only on the elimination of original sweetener compounds but also on the safety of photo-induced by-products. The compilation of degradation and toxicity data forms a solid foundation necessary for a comprehensive environmental risk assessment, and in long term will contribute to an improved environmental management and attain maximum benefit from the sustainable use of these health food ingredients.

201610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
201610.value: 广义变系数模型在很多科学领域发掘动态模式信息中有很重要的用途。申请基金的主要目的是为广义变系数模型发展有效和一致的统计估计和推断方法。我们也会将研究的新的统计方法推广到其它的广义半参数模型。 在我们的计划中，我们将在广义变系数模型框架下研究估计的变系数和真实的变系数最大差异渐近性质。 在此基础上， 我们会讨论在不同途径下如何构造变系数估计的置信域或置信带。 在现实中，有一些变系数函数实际上是一些常系数。如果我们不顾及这样的事实，将常数估成函数， 我们会增加估计的方差， 增加推断的苦难。因此我们系统的研究了下面两个问题，（1）如果确认常系数变量， （2）如果有效的估计它们。 另外，在广义变系数模型中，人们往往假设连接函数有已知的形式，但在实际中我们并不知道。引用错误的连接函数会导致矛盾的结果，以及对结果错误的理解。因此在连接函数未知的情况下， 我们会研究在广义变系数模型下如何有效的估计变系数函数。 现在的科学技术使数据的收集变得更加简单， 大量的海量高维数据不断地出现。要研究这类数据， 对统计学家提出了巨大的挑战。在我们的计划中，我们也将研究广义变系数模型在高维下的统计推断， 特别是如何有效的估计和选择模型。当然，在高维模型下， 如何检测异常观测值， 随机误差是否服从正态假设，都是一些很难回答的问题，需要更多的研究。针对这些问题，对高维广义变系数模型我们会比较现有的方法，提出一些有效的强壮稳定的统计方法。

201610.value: In Zhang and Peng (2010), they systematically stuided the inference problems about generalized varying coefficient models based on the maximum discrepancy, including contructiong simultaneous confidence band for functional coefficients, hypothesis testing problem to determine constant coefficients in the model. The objective 1 is finished by such work. Zhang (2011) studied cross-validation methods for generalized semivarying coefficient models, and used the cross-validation meethod as a criteria to identify the constant coefficients in the model but avoid to computing the CVs of all condidation models. The new methods reduce computation burden, and also keep the consistency of model selection. The objective 2 has been achieved by this work. Making use of the structure of the GVCMs, Zhang, Li and Xia (2013) gives a very weak identification condition for the GVCMs when their linfunction is unknown. Under such identification condition, an iterative estimation procedure for the GVCMs with unspecified link function is proposed. A weighted least squares based algorithm is introduced to implement the proposed estimation procedure. The asymptotic properties of the nonparametric estimators obtained by the proposed iterative estimation procedure are also established. The objective 3 is finished. In the Ph.D disseration of Chen Chi, high dimensional varying coefficient models was systematically investigated. A simple sure screening method is proposed to reduce ultra-high dimensional varying coefficient model to relative high dimensional model. Then a regular model selection method based on SCAD penalty and local polynomial was suggested to select significant coefficient functions and identify significant constant coefficients simultaneously. Cheng, Honda, Li and Peng (2014) considered high dimensional varying coefficients for longitudinal data, a nonparametric independence screening method has been proposed to select significant coefficient fuctions and identify the structure of coefficient functions. The objective 4 has been acheived. Li, Peng, Zhang, and Zhu (2012) proposed a robust screening method to semimparaemtric model to reduce ultra-high dimensional model to relative large model. Li, Peng and Zhu (2011) investigated M-estimion for high dimensional regression model. Lin and Peng (2013) also suggested a regularization robust method based on rank correlation for the model selection. The proposed method can be used to generalized semiparametic model without knowing the link function. Those studied robust methods all can be applied to high-dimensional generalzied varying coefficient models without any difficults though there are still need to make theoretical and numerical investigation for those methods under generalized varying coefficient models, we believe the objective 5 have been almost finished.

201610.label: Major findings and research outcome
201610.value: The PI and Co-PI systematically investigated inference problems for generalized varying coefficient models, including constrcuting simultaneous confidence bands for coefficent functions, hypothesis testing problems to identify constant coefficients. For details, see Zhang and Peng (2010). Yang, Li and Peng (2014) considered measurement errors in the varying coeffciient models with longitudinal data. Some inference problems are investigated based on empirical likelihood ratio in the paper. The PI and Co-PI also considered model selection and identification problems for generalized varying-coefficient models. When the link function of the generalized varying coefficient models is unknown and the model is not identified, Co-PI and his coauthors proposed an iterative algorithm to estimate the function coefficients in the model. The asymptotic properties of the proposed method has been investigated. For detial, see Zhang, Li and Xia (2013). Zhang (2011) also suggested to use cross-validate methods to identify constant coefficients in the generalized varying model to avoid the inconsistency problem of hypothesis testing methods. Based on such work, Peng, Yan and Zhang (2014) also studied the relationship between cross-validation and AIC under generalized varying coefficient models. Cheng, Honda, Li and Peng (2014) and the disseration of Chen chi suggested to identify the constant coefficients by regularization methods. To high dimensional model selection problem, the disseration of Chen chi systematically investigated the sure screening and regularaiztion methods for ultra-high dimensional varying coefficient models. Cheng, Honda, Li and Peng used similar idea to study high dimensional varying coefficient models for longitudinal data. The other researches of PI focuses on models selection by robust regularziation methods and complex statistical model selection problems. Based on the rank correlation, Li, Peng, Zhang and Zhu (2012) proposed a robust sure screening method for ultr-high dimensional regression models. Such method can be used to generalized regression model without knowing the link function. Li, Peng and Zhu (2011) stuided robust properites of penalized M-estimations under high dimensional regression models. Lin and Peng (2013) suggested to use smoothong rank correlation to select significant coefficients in semiparametric regerssion models. Such method can be also applied to semiparametric generalized regression modedls without knowning the link function. Robust numerical properites have been investigated in the paper. To complex statistical models. PI investigated model selection for singlex index model (Peng and Huang, 2011), linear mixed model (Peng and Lu, 2012), additive model (Cui, Peng, Wen and Zhu, 2013) and guassian mixture model (Huang, Peng and Zhang, 2013).

201610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
201610.value: First, we will consider statistical inference for high dimensional generalized varying coefficient models. High dimensional data are araised from different statstical fields. Hence studying inference problems for high dimensional generalized varying coefficient models has wide application in practice. On the other hand, because of spurious correlations between the estimate of the high dimensional model and errors in the model, and endogeneity in ultrahigh dimensional data, there exists some challenges in theoretical investigation and methodolgy application in practice. Second, we will consider to extend our studies to other classical semiparametric regession models, such as single index models, additive models and so on to see if there exists some difference between those models with generalized varying coefficient models, and if there exists some uniform inference methods for generalized semiparametric models. Third, we will consider robust inference problems for generalized varying coefficient models. We have done some research about robust estimates for generalized varying coefficient models. The next step, we wish to see how to apply those robust estimates to construct robust inference procedures for generalzied varying coefficient models. This problem is some interesting, but with challenge, especially when the dimension of the model is some high.

201610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
201610.value: In this project, W systematically investigated statistical inference problem for generalized varying coefficient models. We proposed methods to construct simultaneous confidence band for varying coefficient functions, and used hypthoesis testing and regularization methods to identify constant conefficients in the model. We also studied regularization model selection methods and some robust estimation methods for high dimensional varying coefficient models. Generalized varying coefficient models is a classical semiparmetric regression model, and has wide application in different scientific fields. Especially, varying coefficient models are very useful to discover the dynamic phenomenon. Hence our research has its significance in application. Our research was related many statsitical inference and model selection problems. Little literature sysmetrically investigated those problems before. It would be a special contribution of our work to varying coefficient models analysis. As a toy of semiparametric regression models, our results could be extended to other semiparametric models. We believe that our research also has its theoretical significance in semiparametric model analysis. Especially, we investigated high dimensional varying coefficient models in our project. The proposed methods and theoretical results made contributions to high dimensional data analysis. High dimensional analysis is a very important topic whether in theretical analysis and application.

201710.label: Project Objectives
201710.value: We will develop efficient moving mesh methods to resolve the localized solutions of the Turing-type reaction-diffusion systems on growing domains. Since the moving mesh techniques have been successfully applied to the GM, GS, Schnakernburg, and Brusselator models on fixed domains, we expect that our proposed moving mesh methods will work equally well for those models on growing domains. We will explore a suitable global mesh refinement method. It is important to know under what kind of circumstances that we need to refine the mesh. One possible way is to refine the mesh when new patterns, such as spots and stripes are created. Further study on the global mesh refinement method based on the error estimate will also be carried out. We will couple the global mesh refinement method with the moving mesh methods. We plan to apply the proposed method to some classical pattern formation problems defined on fixed domains to validate our proposed algorithm. We will revisit some important pattern formation models and expect to see improved results and efficiency using our proposed algorithm. We will also implement the proposed method for the pattern formations on realistic growing geometries. Particularly, we plan to simulate the pattern formation process of a growing butterfly wing using our proposed method.

201710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
201710.value: Turing-type reaction-diffusion mechanisms have been widely used to study the biological pattern formation problems. Pattern formation can be seen everywhere in our daily life. For example, the skins of zebra, leopard, and tiger are some of examples of pattern formation. Most of the applications of Turing theory have assumed fixed domains. Recently, it has been shown that the domain growth and domain shape can play a very important role in pattern formation and selection. The nonlinear nature of the reaction-diffusion system coupled with the domain growth means that it is not feasible to obtain meaningful analytical solutions. Therefore, it is indispensable to develop efficient and robust numerical methods to solve these kinds of problems. In this proposal, the key idea is to develop a novel mesh adaptation strategy that couples the global mesh refinement and the moving mesh method to solve Turing-type reaction-diffusion problems on a growing domain. The global mesh refinement is done at some time levels according to the domain growth and the number of patterns, while the moving mesh redistribution is implemented at each time step according to local properties of the solution. The moving mesh method will help us to concentrate the mesh within the areas of large solution variation so that fewer mesh points are needed to resolve the localized patterns. The global mesh refinement on a growing domain is a new adaptive technique and it involves many challenges including indicator functions and interpolations. An indicator function is used to indicate when to apply a global mesh refinement technique. Some appropriate interpolation algorithms will be designed to get the solution information on the newly added points due to the globally refined mesh. The proposed adaptive method is expected to significantly improve the computational efficiency while keeping good approximation accuracy.

201710.label: Realisation of objectives
201710.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved successfully. Under the support of this GRF grant, we have studied numerical methods for resolving localized solutions of the Turing-type reaction-diffusion systems. The main purpose is to understand different types of dynamical behaviors that occur for the motion of a localized solution to singularly perturbed Turing-type reaction-diffusion models. One of the main difficulties for efficient numerical simulations is the existence of large solution gradients in a small localized solution regions. To overcome this difficulty, a moving finite element numerical strategy was developed. Our numerical algorithms can handle many complicated real physical phenomena using only a moderate number of mesh-points, including spots and stripes replication where new spikes are created. This provides a severe challenge as it requires new computational mesh-points to be generated to follow each new spot or stripe. The moving finite element methods we have been developing have been found extremely useful for handling complex pattern formation phenomena. We also developed some high order nonconforming finite elements which could globally increase the accuracy of numerical solutions, especially when new spots or stripes are created. Our current interests are to solve some more complicated reaction-diffusion models that have more complicated physical backgrounds with our developed moving mesh methods and high order finite elements. We will then compare the numerical solutions with the experimental results available.

201710.label: Major findings and research outcome
201710.value: 1. We have developed an efficient adaptive finite element method for solving Turing-type reaction-diffusion systems, which gives high resolution for large gradient solution area. This adaptive finite element method is based on a harmonic mapping framework. It decouples mesh redistribution and PDE evolution. It allows us to use any appropriate PDE solver for solving reaction-diffusion systems which is independent on mesh redistribution strategy. The main work relevant to the development of the adaptive finite element algorithms for the pattern formation can be found in: Moving finite element simulations for reaction-diffusion systems, Guanghui Hu, Zhonghua Qiao, and Tao Tang. Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics, Vol. 4, No. 3, pp. 365-381, 2012. This work also finds out the importance of the boundary grid redistribution which is particularly important for a class of problems for one Turing-type reaction-diffusion model, the Brusselator model. To improve the accuracy and efficency of the finite element method, some high order nonconforming finite elements have been developed in this project. A bubble function method is proposed in designing highly efficient nonconforming finite elements, which could further improve the solution accuracy globally in the adaptive finite element implementation for solving Turing-type reaction-diffusion systems. A paper was published in one of the top numerical analysis journals, Numerische Mathematik: C0-nonconforming tetrahedral and cuboid elements for the three-dimensional fourth order elliptic problem, Hongru Chen, Shaochun Chen, and Zhonghua Qiao. Numer. Math. (2013) 124:99–119. 2. We also considered another strategy, immersed interface method, to solve PDEs with discontinuous or large gradient solutions. This method is proposed for a flow past obstacles problem in the following published paper and could be used for solving Turing-type reaction-diffusion systems. The sensitivity analysis for the flow past obstacles problem with respect to the Reynolds number, Kazufumi Ito, Zhilin Li, and Zhonghua Qiao. Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics, Vol. 4, No. 1, pp. 21-35, 2012. 3. During the study of this project, we found that long time simulations are usually needed for pattern formation problems. So we proposed an adaptive time-stepping strategy for solving a phase field crystal model in An adaptive time-stepping strategy for solving the phase field crystal model, Zhengru Zhang, Yuan Ma, Zhonghua Qiao. Journal of Computational Physics, 249 (2013) 204–215. This method has been also used to solve other types of reaction-diffusion equations for pattern formation, e.g., Cahn-Hilliard equation, which will be one direction of our future work related to this project.

201710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
201710.value: The further development of this research is to develop a better mathematical understanding of complex phenomena arising in Turing-type pattern formations which may be described by reaction-diffusion systems. With the robust and efficient adaptive finite element method and adaptive time-stepping algorithm developed, we may be able to investigate more complicated pattern formations in long time simulations. It can be expected that the adaptive strategies both in space and time will help to improve the efficiency of the simulation significantly. Efficient simulation of complex pattern formations is currently under investigation.

201910.label: Project Objectives
201910.value: Systematic annotation of topological features of the E. coli carbon flow network. This includes classification and identification of accumulation and branching points of carbon flow as well as end points of synthetic pathways and waste production. Compilation of cases of end-product inhibition at entry points of synthetic pathways for cellular components based on BRENDA and literature knowledge, as well as the identification of entry points leading to carbon waste and their regulation. Carrying out analytical and simulational studies of linear pathways in the presence of single and multiple feedback controls. The response of the linear pathway flux to perturbations in the entry and exit metabolite concentrations will be examined to gain an in depth view of the stability of steady-state flow and sensitivity to the choice of model parameters. Analysis and discussion of theoretical issues in systems level modeling, including the interaction between converging and diverging pathways at branch points, the regulatory motifs and strategies to achieve optimal flux partitioning, and issues of regulation that impact on the global stability and sensitivity of the metabolic flow.
