201910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
201910.value: Regulation of enzyme activity through small molecule binding offers a well-known feedback mechanism in the biosynthesis of cellular components. It is believed that such regulations are able to steer the metabolic flow towards an optimal solution that represents the most efficient use of resource such as nutrients in the environment. However, the extremely complex topology of the metabolic network, the large number of regulatory interactions, and the diverse set of regulatory logic have so far prevented a comprehensive understanding of this hypothesis. There are many issues, from both data gathering and theoretical analysis and modeling side, that need to be addressed before decisive progress can be made towards answering this question. In the proposed work, we plan to define and tackle some of these issues through a detailed analytical and computational study of allosteric regulation in the model organism E. coli. Our basic premise is a dynamic view that biosynthesis is carried out by a collection of autonomous units subject to mass conservation, common resource constraints, regulatory control and systems level coordination. To identify and isolate such units, we shall first annotate the topology of the metabolic network to highlight linear pathways as well as branching and merging nodes where units join. Information on the allosteric regulation of these units and their interactions will be collected and classified with the help of online databases and literature. Analytical and simulational studies will be performed to: i) characterize the dynamic properties of individual units or linear pathways; ii) establish scenarios on how two linear pathways interact at merging and branching points; iii) evaluate the necessity of global control and coordination to achieve optimal flux partitioning in biosynthesis. The model study will allow us to develop a physical understanding of allosteric regulation on metabolic flow at the systems level. Interfacing with ongoing experimental studies, although not planned in this proposal, is nevertheless an integral part of our long-term goal to quantify bacterial metabolism and growth, and hence will be given active consideration once the key theoretical issues are clarified. 通過小分子結合來調節酶的活性是在細胞成分合成中一個知名的反饋機制。很多研究者相信，這類變構調控能夠優化代謝流分配，包括環境中營養物質等資源最合理的使用。然而，由於代謝網絡非常複雜的拓撲結構，細胞內大量的監管相互作用，以及多種類型的監管邏輯，這一假說的全面證實還言之過早。在回答觀察到的變構調控能否實現資源有效利用這一命題之前，在數據的收集到理論分析到建模等若干方面都需要取得決定性的進展。在此項研究中，我們計劃通過對模式生物大腸桿菌小分子變構調控數據的詳細分析和計算，將部分有關的問題作出界定和理論處理。此項研究的基本前提是，生物合成是由多個相對獨立的自動單元組成的動態過程，單元之間滿足質量守恆、資源共享、及系統層次的協調等約束。要識別和隔離這類單元，我們將首先詮釋代謝網絡的拓撲結構，包括線性路徑及其分叉與合併節點。下一步是收集網上數據庫及文獻中有關變構調節的數據，對單個單元的調控及單元間的相互作用進行分類。通過分析建模和計算： 一）刻畫單個單元或線性路徑的動態特性; 二）建立兩條線性通路在合併點和分叉點的多種互動模式; 三）評估整體控制和協調在實現系統層次上最佳的代謝流量分配的作用和必要性。 該項模型研究將使我們能夠對系統水平上代謝流的變構調節有較客觀的了解。長遠來說，一旦以上提到的關鍵理論問題得以澄清，我們將積極尋求與實驗研究的合作，最終實現對細菌的代謝系統和生長速率的定量描述。

202010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
202010.value: In recent years, many numerical methodologies have been developed for the computational areodynamics based on the finite difference method, the finite volume method and the finite element method. All these methods can be used to discretize the Euler or the Navier-Stokes equations, which may result in highly nonlinear algebraic systems. Developing robust and efficient solvers for the nonlinear systems is a main challenge in the numerical simulation; this is particularly important for solving the steady state Euler equations. In this project, we will investigate robust high-order numerical algorithms for multi-dimensional Euler equations on unstructured grids, with particular attention to the numerical simulations to the steady state Euler equations. To obtain higher order numerical accuracy, we will extend the reconstruction to the quadratic case, and use hierarchical reconstruction strategy to avoid the non-physical oscillations. We will also use the multigrid technique to speed up the convergence process. The issue of balancing the robustness and accuracy will be also addressed in this project. We will also combine the numerical schemes developed in this proposal and the adaptive grid techniques to improve the efficiency of the numerical simulations. 近年來，很多研究以有限差分法、有限體積法、及有限元法為基礎，建立了針對計算空氣動力學問題的數值方法。這些方法可以用於離散歐拉方程及納維葉－斯托克斯方程，從而得出高度非線性代數方程組。針對非線性代數方程組而建立的穩健有效的求解演算法，是數值模擬的一大挑戰，而且，這些求解演算法對於計算穩態歐拉方程尤其重要。本項目旨在研究應用在多維歐拉方程在非結構網格上的穩健高階數值演算法，特別是穩態歐拉方程的數值模擬。為了得到高階數值精度，我們會把重組擴展到二次的情況中進行研究，採用分層構建的策略抑制非物理振盪，並且使用多重網格法加速收斂。本研究同時會探討平衡穩健性及準備度的問題，亦會結合本研究計劃中提出的數值方法及自適應網格技術，提升數值模擬之成效。

202010.label: Major findings and research outcome
202010.value: To develop robust high-order numerical algorithm for two-dimensional steady Euler equation on unstructured grid is a challenging task. This research project begins with my work with my PhD student G. Hu and a former student R. Li: Guanghui Hu, Ruo Li, and Tao Tang, A robust WENO type finite volume solver for steady Euler equations on unstructured grids, Commun. Comput. Phys. 9 (2011), 627-648. G.-H. Hu, R. Li, and T. Tang, A robust high-order residual distribution type scheme for steady Euler equations on unstructured grids, J. Comput. Phys. 229 (2010), 1681-1697. We then try to extend the above two works to more adaptive level. To this end, we studied two relevant works (which are listed in Part C) H. Dong, Z-H Quiao, S-Y Sun, and T. Tang, Adaptive moving grid methods for two-phase flow in porous media, J. Comput. Appl. Math. 265 (2014), 139-150. G. Hu, Z. Qiao, and T. Tang, Moving finite element simulations for reaction-diffusion systems, Adv. Appl. Math. Mech. 4 (2012), no. 3, 365-381. The above investigation allows us to have better understanding of adaptive grid methods for two-phase flows and reaction-diffusion systems. The difficulty from the coupling systems and the complex solution structures was well understood, and the relevant methods to handle the difficulty are studied. Wuth the preparation of the above works, my former PhD student G. Hu completed the final goals of this research project in the following paper: Guanghui Hu, An Adaptive Finite Volume Method for 2D Steady Euler Equations with WENO Reconstruction, Journal of Computational Physics, Vol. 252, pp. 591-605, 2013. In this work, he introduced the mesh adaptive methods to improve our previous numerical methods for numerical schemes for Euler equations on unstructured grids. The features of this work include: (i) different reconstruction stencils for WENO reconstruction are discussed in detail, including their performance on the convergence of steady state solutions and on the application of h-adaptive methods, and (ii) an effective indicator for generating quality nonuniform mesh is proposed, which is based on the entropy production. The improvement of the numerical methods is demonstrated by many numerical examples.

202010.value: Computing steady state solutions to systems of conservation laws is of important applications; several very recent works have quite close connection with our results or approaches (they also cited our earlier work): including recent research of fast sweeping methods for computing the solutions of static Hamilton-Jacobi equations; see Björn Engquist, Brittany D. Froese, Yen-Hsi Richard Tsai, Fast sweeping methods for hyperbolic systems of conservation laws at steady state, J. Comput. Phys. vol. 225, pp. 316-338, 2013. and also Wenrui Hao, Jonathan D. Hauenstein, Chi-Wang Shu, Andrew J. Sommese, Zhiliang Xu, Yong-Tao Zhang, A homotopy method based on WENO schemes for solving steady state problems of hyperbolic conservation laws, J. Comput. Phys. vol 205, pp. 332-346, 2013. Another very relevant recent work is: Panagiotis Tsoutsanis, Antonios Foivos Antoniadis, Dimitris Drikakis, WENO schemes on arbitrary unstructured meshes for laminar, transitional and turbulent flows, J. Comput. Phys. vol. 256, pp. 254–276, 2014. All of the above three papers cited and commented our works relevant to the present project. In fact, these works open several possible doors for further development and application of the adaptive approaches for steady Euler flows on unstructured grids.

202010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
202010.value: In many applications, it is important to compute the steady state solution of hyperbolic conservasion laws. A natural approach to computing steady state solutions is to use an explicit time stepping or pseudo time stepping technique to evolve the system to steady state, but this procedure may be very slow due to the stability requirement. In order to substantially improve the efficiency, it is desirable to develop methods that solve the steady state equations directly instead of through a time-evolution process. Other two factors affecting the efficiency is accuracy and adaptivity. Higher-order accuracy in space discretization is very important; as low resolution schemes may provide unsatisfactory results in critical areas with physical interests. Adaptive grid methods for unstructure grids can be used, which can cluster more grid points in these critical areas to greatly enhance the resolutions there. The key motivations of this project is to investigate the accuracy and adaptivity for computing the steady state solution of hyperbolic conservation laws.

202210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
202210.value: 光動力療法（photodynamic therapy）由於需要特定波長的光照射才會引發光敏反應而殺傷腫瘤細胞，因而具有高度的選擇性並成為治療癌症的有效手段之一。無毒的光敏劑優先聚集於癌細胞，然後通過特定波長的光進行激發而產生具有殺傷細胞作用的活性氧（例如單線態氧）。 單線態氧在生物體內的壽命一般很短（<0.04us），因此其作用半徑也比較小（<0.02um）。一般來說，光敏劑的聚集範圍就是光損害範圍。 線粒體由於其在細胞凋亡、殺傷細胞中具有非常重要的作用，因此在光動力療法中線粒體是光敏劑最有效的聚集部位。 因而開發線粒體靶向性光敏劑可以大大提高光動力療法的治療效率。 研究表明，雙光子吸收（two-photon absorption）可以提高生色團激發的選擇空間，特別是激發達到能透過生物體內介質的近紅外（NIR）區域時，治療效果好並且光敏反應的毒副作用比較小。利用雙光子吸收來激發所需的光化學以及光物理過程的研究在體內（in vivo）光化學（photochemistry）、生物成像(bioimaging)、氧敏反應(oxygen sensing) 以及光療(phototherapy)中具有非常重要的意義。而且，用來激發雙光子吸收的鐳射，具有凝聚性和單色性，可以精確激發靶點產生單線態氧從而保護健康的組織完整無損。另外，當光敏劑的雙光子吸收的激發能量與其螢光產生的波長在同一範圍，那麼此光敏劑既可用於光動力療法又可用于生物成像。 本課題中，我們主要是為了設計及合成一系列具有較大雙光子吸收截面（two-photon absorption cross-section）的陽離子型兩親性卟啉類化合物。 這些化合物可以通過光譜（UV-vis, IR, MS, NMR and Fluorescence）以及元素分析、X-ray單晶衍射分析來表徵。然後我們進一步測試它們的光化學物理性質，雙光子吸收截面，DNA的結合及切斷，親水及親油性，細胞吸收效率以及光動力療法效率，以及這些性質和卟啉環上取代基以及連接的親水性陽離子基團的關係。 最後，我們將評估他們作為雙功能雙光子吸收-光动力疗法（TPA-PDT）药物的可能性。

202210.label: Realisation of objectives
202210.value: Objective 1: We have developed synthetic routes for the preparation of (i) amphiphilic Ru-P dyads in which a hydrophobic porphyrin moiety and a hydrophilic Ru(II)-polypyridyl moiety were connected with different linkers, (ii) water-soluble porphyrinato ytterbium complexes linked with rhodamine B, (iii) axially-ligated rhodamine-Si(IV)-phthalocyanine conjugates, (iv) water-soluble cationic porphyrin conjugated cyclen-based ytterbium(III) complexes, and (v) YbPor-BODIPY conjugates in which an electron-donor moiety ytterbium(III) porphyrinate (YbPor), was linked through an ethynyl bridge to an electron-acceptor moiety, boron dipyrromethend (BODIPY). These complexes were fully characterized by standard spectroscopic methods. Objective 2: The linear and two-photon induced photophysical properties of the above conjugates have been measured. They all showed substantial singlet-oxygen quantum yields and displayed moderate two-photon-absorption (TPA) cross-sections. The TPA cross-sections of conjugates could be increased via expansion of π-conjugation and enhancement of molecular polarization induced by asymmetrical (D-π-A) structure of the molecules. This is well demonstrated by the YbPor-BODIPY complexes. Flow cytometry studies further demonstrated that it is necessary to have an optimal hydrophobic/ hydrophilic balance in order to achieve a high cellular uptake. Most of the above mentioned conjugates showed low dark cytotoxicity but high photo-toxicity. Cell-based studies showed that conjugates with an appended free porphyrin have a faster cell uptake rate and a stronger photo-cytotoxicity than with an appended metalloporphyrin. Incorporation of a rhodamine B moiety into the complexes enhanced the water solubility of these conjugates. Organelle specificity was also observed via the modification of the appending moiety. Conjugates with rhodamine B and cyclen moiety showed mitochondria- and Golgi apparatus-specific subcellular localization, respectively. Depending on the nature of the linkers, the Ru-P dyads can target specifically at the lysosome, mitochondria or cytoplasm. Objective 3: The potential of the above mentioned conjugates as bifunctional “see and treat” TPA-PDT agents has been assessed. Amphiphilic Ru-P dyads fulfill the major requirements as a two-photon absorption photodynamic therapy (TPA-PDT) photosensitizer in the “see and treat” approach: (i) good solubility and stability in water, (ii) adequate fluorescence quantum yield with high singlet-oxygen quantum yield, (iii) a relatively large two-photon absorption cross-section, (iv) no significant dark cytotoxicty, (v) rapid and high cellular uptake, and (vi) potent photo-cytotoxicity. Our work demonstrates that, in addition to a high intrinsic TPA cross-section, a large cellular uptake is an important design parameter for TPA-PDT agent as well. Furthermore, axially-ligated rhodamine-Si(IV)-phthalocyanine conjugates and cationic porphyrin conjugated cyclen-based ytterbium(III) complexes are found to be potential TPA-PDT agents.

202210.label: Major findings and research outcome
202210.value: A water-soluble porphyrinato ytterbium complex linked with rhodamine B showed mitochrondria-specific subcellular localization and strong two-photon-induced near-infrared (NIR) emissions (emission at 650 nm, porphyrinate ligand π to π* transition; emission at 1060 nm, Yb(III) 5F5/2 to 5F7/2 transitions) with an impressive Yb(III) NIR emission quantum yield (2.5%, excited at 430 nm) in aqueous solution. (J. Am. Chem. Soc., 2011, 133, 20120-20122.) Water-soluble porphyrin-Ru(II) conjugates with different linkers between the hydrophobic porphyrin moiety and the hydrophilic Ru(II)-polypyridyl complex have been synthesized. Their linear and two-photon-induced photophysical properties were measured and their potential application as dual in vitro imaging and photodynamic therapeutic (PDT) agents were evaluated. Conjugate with hydrophobic phenylethynyl linker was shown to be highly promising for further development as a bifunctional probe for two-photon (NIR) induced PDT and in vitro imaging. (Bioconj. Chem. 2012, 23, 1623-1638) An amphiphilic water-soluble ytterbium complex which is Golgi apparatus specific has been designed as a responsive dual probe capable of sensitizing emission within the biological window (660 and 750 nm), generating the singlet oxygen (quantum yield, 0.45) and triggering local cell damage only upon exposure to visible and NIR laser excitation. (Chem. Commun. 2012, 48, 9646-9648) Two axially-ligated rhodamine-Si(IV)-phthalocyanine conjugates were synthesized and their linear and two-photon photophysical, subcellular localization and photocytotoxic properties were studied. These conjugates exhibited an almost exclusive mitochondrial localizing property in HK-1 and HeLa cells. Strong photocytotoxic but low dark cytotoxic properties were observed towards the HK-1 cells. (Inorg. Chem., 2012, 51, 812-821) Rh-SiPc-Rh exhibited strong growth inhibition of tumour xenograft with significant tumour necrosis and limited toxicological effects on the nude mice. (Bioorg. Med. Chem. Lett., 2013, 23, 2373-2376) A series of push-pull YbPor-BODIPY conjugates have been synthesis. Photophysical studies showed that the BODIPY moieties harvest light energy and transfer it to the ytterbium–porphyrinate moieties, which efficiently sensitized the NIR emission of the Yb(III) ion. Conjugate which had a classic pull-push framework, exhibited remarkable two-photon-induced NIR emission and high two photon-absorption (2PA) cross-sections of 2226 GM. (Chem. Eur. J. 2013, 19, 739-748) A conjugate, in which the ruthenium(II) poly-pyridyl moiety is linked to the β-position of the tetraphenylporphyrin via a Schiff base linkage, has been synthesized. Its singlet oxygen quantum yield, TPA cross-section, photo-induced DNA cleavage and cytotoxic activities were measured. The results indicated that the conjugate is an effective DNA photocleavage agent, with potential application in TPA anti-cancer photodynamic therapy. (J. Lumin., 2014, 154, 356-361)

202210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
202210.value: In this work, we have demonstrated a new modality of PDT through the design of truly dual functional PDT and imaging agents. In this design, the location of the administered PDT drug can be monitored by its laser-excited photoemission signal without triggering the generation of phototoxic ROS to the tissues in the light path of the imaging laser. When the PDT drug has reached and accumulated in its intended target, irradiation at a wavelength that can trigger the generation of phototoxic ROS will kill the intended cancerous tissue. This treatment modality opens up a new direction in the development of “precision medicine”. In the long term, we envision the use of these synthesized in-vitro imaging PDT drugs incorporated with different vectors to enhance their target specificity in clinical practice. We purpose to systematically develop several transition metal complexes as fast responsive biomedical probes for targeting and monitoring the disease; in addition, delivering the drug in-vitro, in-situ and in-vivo with a combination of biochemical, molecular and structural modification will be studied.

202210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
202210.value: Applications of luminescent lanthanide/transition metal materials for PDT and NIR imaging are very promising. Lanthanide/transition metal-porphyrin hybrids merit greater attention from the wider scientific community. However, to understand and apply the theories of lanthanides/transition metal and porphyrins is an uphill task prior to any further medicinal applications so the results from this project can seek to give scientists a very quick resume of the key fundamentals and updated literatures, and insights into recent advances in particular exemplified in part by our own work on the potential application of lanthanide/transition metal-porphyrin conjugates as NIR imaging and PDT agents. We have developed several multi-modal complexes systematically as fast responsive biomedical probes for targeting and monitoring the disease, in addition to delivering the drug in-vitro, in-situ and in-vivo through multidisciplinary (biochemical, molecular and structural) approaches. In our publications, we have summarized the very criteria for the development of new modality biological agents and complexes, through the design of truly dual functional imaging agents, which can target particular tumors in vitro specifically.

202410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
202410.value: Developing high-performance organic thin-film transistors (OTFTs) or organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) is one of the key technologies for an extensive market of organic electronics. Increasing demands for inexpensive electronic components for memory, logic and displays have recently driven research toward technologies involving OTFTs. OTFTs are considered attractive alternatives to conventional inorganic transistors in functions that require low-cost, low-temperature fabrication, solution-phase device processing and mechanical flexibility. As the core element of an OTFT, organic semiconductors with high performance and excellent stability are necessary for commercial applications. To date, many organic semiconductors with higher charge mobilities than that of amorphous silicon have been developed. Among these, pentacene becomes the benchmark for OTFTs. Although a variety of organic semiconductors based on acenes, oligothiophenes, C60, etc., have been extensively developed, examples of OTFTs consisting of transition-metal complexes are yet limited, despite their several advantages. In particular, examples of organometallic small-molecule complexes and polymers as active OTFT materials are very scarce indeed. In this project, we initiate a new program of developing novel series of organometallic semiconductors for high-performance OTFTs. Metal-containing complexes and polymers are good candidates owing to the immense structural diversity, range of properties and intermolecular/supramolecular interactions made possible by the presence of metallic elements. The incorporation of electron-rich transition metal centers would be expected to facilitate intrachain charge transport and intermolecular stacking interactions favorable for high-performance devices. With our strengths in synthetic chemistry, polymer and metal complex chemistry, the performance of devices can be fine-tuned through chemical modifications of the organometallic structures. The present work does fill in a relatively under-investigated area of organic electronics and would provide a new impetus to the creation of some technologically useful organometallic semiconductors with higher stability and charge carrier mobilities. Facile manipulation of molecular skeleton allows fine-tuning of the highest occupied and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital energy levels to achieve either p-channel or n-channel or even ambipolar materials. High-performance organic transistor devices can be fabricated from solution-cast films, which will allow large-scale device fabrication from low-cost techniques such as screen or ink-jet printing. The combination of organometallic semiconductors with flexible substrates such as polymer films, paper or textiles can lead to the emergence of soft or plastic electronics and photonics, thus opening the possibility to develop light-weight, low-cost, and eventually low-end products such as intelligent organic (electronic) paper, smart cards, flexible display devices, or radio-frequency identification tags by simple, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly technologies.

202410.label: Realisation of objectives
202410.value: To our knowledge, the use of organometallic molecular compounds for high-performance OFETs is yet very scarce in the literature and there have been few reports of metallopolyyne polymers that can perform well in OFETs. Hence, an innovative class of solution-processable organometallic polymers and complexes have great potential to excel in realizing highly efficient BHJ and OFET devices. In this project, we have developed a new class of solution-processable and semiconducting functional conjugated metal-containing molecules and their structure-property relationships were investigated in details. The data were also correlated to those of the purely organic counterparts. Among these, OFETs based on metallopolyynes with the electron-deficient thiazolothiazole spacer afforded the maximum hole mobility of 2.8 x 10–2 cm2/Vs, which is among the best reported value for related systems. These results demonstrate that metallopolyynes are promising materials for high-performance air-stable solution-processable OFET devices. On the other hand, we recognize that further structural characterization is required for understanding the exact interchain organization at the dielectric interface in the OFET devices. From a broader perspective, it is worth highlighting that these guidelines for achieving structurally more precise narrow band materials are relevant within the context of BHJ polymer solar cells, where balanced charge carrier transport improves power conversion efficiencies. As far as the GRF proposal is concerned, the PI considers that we have addressed in full all the issues relevant to the revised objectives, even though the budget funded is less than that in the original proposal.

202410.label: Major findings and research outcome
202410.value: New platinum(II)-acetylide polymers containing thiophene-triarylamine chromophores of different dimensions were synthesized and their electronic band structures, field-effect charge transport, and application in bulk-heterojunction solar cells were evaluated. Their spin-coated thin films showed p-channel field-effect charge transport with hole mobilities of 1.90x10–5 to 7.86x10–5 cm2/Vs and an improved charge carrier transport was found for polymers with higher molecular dimensionality. The work indicates that multidimensional polymers exhibit a better hole mobility and photovoltaic performance over the linear polymers (paper 1). Four donor-acceptor platinum(II) bis(aryleneethynylene) complexes were synthesized and utilized as the electron donor materials for bulk-heterojunction solar cells. Stronger electron-donating groups significantly enhance the solar absorption abilities of the complexes. Typical p-type characteristics were observed. The charge mobility is dependent on the molecular packing and film morphology. The work illuminates the potential of organometallic complexes in developing light-harvesting small-molecules for efficient power generation (paper 3). The work was extended to platinum(II) aryleneethynylenes with conjugated oligothiophenes (paper 11). Two platinum-acetylide polymers with the electron-deficient thiazolothiazole spacer was synthesized. Their spin-coated thin films exhibited p-channel field-effect charge transport characteristics exhibiting impressive peak field-effect charge-carrier mobilities of (2.1–2.8)x10–2 cm2/Vs and on/off ratios of 8000–100000 for the holes. Such hole mobility value is among the highest reported for metallopolyynes to date (paper 4). Simple ambipolar phosphorescent Ir(III) ppy-type complexes playing trifunctional roles were obtained which can substantially enhance the EL performance through improving the charge carrier recombination efficiency. This system provides a new way to furnish highly efficient phosphorescent OLEDs (see paper 9). π-Conjugated, narrow-bandgap copolymers containing pyridal[2,1,3]thiadiazole (PT) were synthesized. Compared to their regiorandom counterparts, the regioregular polymers exhibit a two orders of magnitude increase of the field-effect hole mobilites from 0.005 to 0.6 cm2/Vs (paper 2). The molecule, with two weakly conjugated chromophores, was synthesized. The data suggests that the overall molecular shape provides a kinetic barrier to crystallization. These findings highlight the importance of molecular topology when designing molecular components for solar cell devices (paper 7). Organic donor-acceptor counterparts consisting of benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b0]dithiophene unit and various acceptor groups were synthesized. Their OFET and photovoltaic properties were examined. These data provide valuable insights to the future investigation of related metal-based organic materials for organic optoelectronics (papers 8 and 12). The PI was invited to contribute Review/Progress Report articles (Coord. Chem. Rev. and Adv. Mater.) on metal-containing polymers and materials for organic electronics and photonics (papers 5,6,10).

202410.value: The following areas of research work can be developed in the future: (1) To further explore the applications of these metal-organic complexes in the advance of high mobility OFETs; (2) To synthesize 3D architectures with more π-conjugated branches in order to reduce the HOMO-LUMO gap according to the known synthetic principles.

202410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
202410.value: Organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) are a cornerstone in the development of organic electronic devices and the utilization of organic materials for OFETs has attracted considerable research attention in low-end electronics market because of their merits over conventional silicon technology. Solution-processable OFETs have become a promising emerging technology for low-cost, large-area electronics on flexible, plastic substrates, active-matrix electronic paper, and simple low-cost memory devices (e.g. smart cards and price tags). Organic semiconductors with high performance and excellent stability are necessary for commercial applications. Among these, conjugated organic molecules that can be incorporated into solution-processed OFETs will hit the focus for up-and-coming OFET research. For high-performance devices, the molecules should possess a high charge carrier mobility. To address this key issue, we have developed a new class of solution-processable and semiconducting functional conjugated metal-containing molecules. It is known that suitable metal chromophores strongly influence the optical and electronic features of the organic materials. Solution processing also offers the potential for much cheaper devices that can be patterned using large-area deposition methods such as ink-jet printing. The work also enables the elucidation and optimization of key structure-property relationships desirable for the new design and improved performance of future materials.

202610.label: Project Objectives
202610.value: For the rank minimization problem with linear constraints, we will present the generic algorithmic framework based on ALM and apply linearization techniques and proximal techniques to solve the resulted subproblems. For some special cases including the matrix completion problem, the resulted subproblems admit explicit solutions. For the sparse and low-rank matrix decomposition problem, we will present the ADM approach where the resulted subproblems admit explicit solutions. We will present the first conceptual model of sparse and low-rank matrix nearness problem and then suggest heuristically its convex relaxation problem to approach the original problem. The generic algorithmic framework based on ADM will be proposed. For some special cases including the nearest correlation matrix problem and box-constrained case, the resulted subproblems admit explicit solutions. For nuclear-norm regularized least squares problem, we will present the generic algorithmic framework based on ADM, and then apply the linearization techniques and inexact techniques to solve those subproblems that do not admit explicit solutions.

202610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
202610.value: Many applications arising in a broad spectrum of fields can be modelled into matrix optimization problems seeking low-rank solutions. In general, these low-rank-driven matrix optimization problems are NP-hard due to the combinatorial feature of the rank-related terms. Recently, it has been discovered that these NP-hard problems can be well approached by solving their convex relaxation problems where the nuclear norm is utilized as the surrogate of rank. This breakthrough achievement hence motivated rapidly the great interest of developing efficient numerical algorithms for solving the resulted nuclear-norm-involved convex relaxation problems. These nuclear-norm-involved convex relaxation problems are still numerically challenging, especially for large-scale cases. Although a few algorithms have been proposed, the literature in this regard is very limited. In particular, for some low-rank-driven matrix optimization problems, existing algorithms treat their nuclear-norm-involved convex relaxation problems as generic convex programming problems, and ignore their favorable structures such as the separable structure in both objective functions and constraints. This project aims at developing innovative numerical algorithms for some interesting low-rank-driven matrix optimization problems capturing concrete applications in various fields. The principles for designing the new algorithms are fully structure-exploited, easily implementable, and thus numerically efficient. 許多應用領域裡的問題都可以轉化為求解一個矩陣優化問題的低秩解。一般來說，由於秩這一數學量的組合性質，這些涉及到低秩解的矩陣優化問題是NP困難的。最近，有學者發現，如果用矩陣的核范數來取代秩這個量，那麼這些求低秩解的矩陣優化問題可以鬆弛為凸優化問題，而且這樣的鬆弛是很準確的。這一突破性的成果迅速地引起廣大學者的注意，并促使大家開始考慮求解這些與核范數相關的凸優化問題的數值解。 從數值上來說，求解這些與核范數相關的凸優化問題並不容易，尤其是當問題的規模很大的時候。有關這些問題的數值算法方面的研究，目前剛剛開始。目前比較常用的辦法是將這些與核范數相關的凸優化問題當成一個一般的凸優化問題， 而忽略了問題本身固有的一些有利結構。例如，這些與核范數相關的凸優化問題的目標函數或者約束條件常常是具有分離結構的。 本項目旨在設計一些新穎的數值算法來求解一些具有實際應用背景的帶核范數的凸優化問題。我們設計算法的原則是充分利用問題本身的結構，從而使得算法容易實現，並且數值效果好。

202610.label: Major findings and research outcome
202610.value: This project has investigated how to develop efficient algorithms for solving some low-rank-driven optimization models. The major finding is that classical augmented Lagrangian method can be perfectly used to design a series of efficient algorithms by applying appropriate decomposition in accordance with the model's structure under consideration. Some interesting applications arising in the image processing and statistical learning areas have been solved by the algorithms developed in this project; and some theoretical results have been analyzed.

202610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
202610.value: The techniques used for algorithmic design in this project have inspired us to consider similar methodologies for other optimization models such as more intensive consideration for more general separable convex minimization models and customized applications of the proximal point algorithm for related models. Some proof techniques developed in this project are beneficial for us to analyze deeper convergence rate results for splitting methods in more general settings. The numerical algorithms developed in this project have the potential to be further optimized toward publicized or commercialized software packages.

202610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
202610.value: This project prompts some novel algorithmic design ideas for solving a class of low-rank-driven optimization models which have wide applications in many areas, a particular one of which is the big-data scenario. The outcome of this project enhances the current set of methodology and domain of applications of splitting methods.

202710.label: Project Objectives
202710.value: Develop a measure of dynamical network complexity applicable to characterize brain states basing on large-scale dynamical activity. 202710.label: Realisation of objectives
202710.value: The project was only partially supported compared to the initial proposal, but has been completed satisfactorily. Objective 1 is fully realized. We have developed a measure of dynamical network complexity that basing on synchronization of oscillators in network. This measure can provide a characterization of the balance of functional segregation and integration in complex network systems and we have found that real neural networks have optimal complexity [1,4]. Objective 2 is fully realized. We developed a mapping that can relate network structure connectivity to functional connectivity and extend the complexity measure to the functional connectivity. We studied the impact of various network properties, especially modular organization and the combination with hubs on the dynamical organization and dynamical complexity [1-8]. We found that the real networks have maximal complexity when compared to rewired networks [1,2], reflecting a trade-off between multiple constraints [13]. We also studied the impact of neural plasticity on the network activity [14] and structure [15]. Objective 3 is fully realized. In close collaboration with the Co-I of the project, cognitive neuroscientist Prof. Werner Sommer from Berlin, we have developed a new method called RIDE (Residue Iteration Decomposition) which can decompose the ERP components for 3 cognitive subprocesses (perception, decision-making and response). The method is based on the dynamical variability of the latency and reaction time in single trial experimental data. The method can obtain the spatial-temporal pattern and electrode networks associated to the sub-processes and obtain the information of latency and amplitude in each single trial. The method has been published [9] and has been applied to various experiments [11,12, 16,17]. Objective 4 is fully realized. With the method RIDE, we can separate the ERP components from the on-going activity. We found that reaction time variability is significantly contributed by the latency of an intermediate decision-making process. RIDE method would allow us to characterize the ongoing activity before and after the stimulus onset using functional network measures and dynamical complexity and study its relationship to the latency and reaction time of the RIDE-separated components. Applying RIDE, EEG data can now be explored in a much broader scope to study brain-behavior relations by using (1) latency-corrected reconstructed ERPs, (2) separated components for different neurocognitive processes in greater detail and specificity, and (3) information about variability in single trials. In the future, we will extract the network underlying the generation of the dynamical patterns using inverse method [10].

202710.label: Major findings and research outcome
202710.value: Brain networks display complex connectivity and activity. This project proposed to characterize the complexity using the approaches of synchronization in oscillatory networks. We established strong collaborations, published 15 papers and trained 3 PhD students. 1). We found that complex connectivity, especially modular architecture (HMN) as in cortical networks has significant impact on dynamical complexity [1-8, 14-15]. We developed a measure of dynamical network complexity based on synchronization of oscillator to characterize the balance of functional segregation and integration in complex networks and found that real neural networks have optimal complexity [1,4]. The maximal complexity is related to a critical competition of intra- and inter-community synchronization [2]. Proper modularity in the real neural network provided the optimal balance. The complex structures of the real neural networks and the functional implications were studied and we were invited to write reviews [3,4]. These features reflect a trade-off between multiple constraints [13]. In realistic neuronal networks, we found that neural oscillations and critical avalanches as observed in experiments can simultaneously organize in HMNs [7]. The HNMS can greatly enlarge the critical region [8] (our work was selected 2012 highlight of New Journal Physics). Introducing neural plasticity, modules [5] and feed-forward network architecture [15] can emerge and can explain micro-saccade-induced neural activity [14]. 2). We developed a new method RIDE (Residue Iteration Decomposition) which can obtain much richer dynamical information in brain EEG data [9,11,12,16,17]. Complex oscillatory activity in brain EEG data from cognitive experiments induces strong variability in the response to stimuli. In conventional analysis, complex activity and response variability is treated as noisy fluctuations and are eliminated by averaging many trials of experiments to obtain event-related potential (ERPs). Our modeling work suggested that complex network activity is inherent in neural networks and should contain rich functional implications. This project developed a new framework of EEG analysis, assuming temporally overlapping components with variable latencies and associated to different cognitive events, and developed new method RIDE to extract the ERP components for particular sub-processes. RIDE can reconstruct ERP waveforms as most probably observed in single trials and obtain the distributions of dynamic latencies and amplitudes of each component among single trials. Applying RIDE, EEG data can now be explored in a much broader scope to study brain-behavior relations by using dynamical information about complex activity and response variability in single trials. RIDE has been published [9] and has been applied to various experiments [11,12,16,17].

202710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
202710.value: We have developed very productive collaboration with Co-I Prof. Sommer from Humboldt University (HU) on the analysis of cognitive experiments using our new method and dynamical approaches. We co-organized workshops and symposium in Hong Kong (Oct. 2012), Beijing (April 2014) and Japan (Sep 2014). We established HKBU-HU Joint PhD program and co-supervised a PhD student, 1 Hong Kong PhD Fellowship awardee and 1 postdoct. We have published 3 joint papers, made one joint US patent application and currently are finishing 4 manuscripts for publication, and have planned several experiments and applications. We have planned and started a large project to study individual difference in cognitive ability (with 250 participants) using the method RIDE, and a grant is under review of German Science Foundation. Prof. Sommer will visit HKBU as Sabbatical Scholar in Sep-Dec 2014 to continue collaborations. We have also developed collaborations with several other cognitive research groups, including Prof. Annekathrin Schacht (Goettingen University), Prof. Rolf Verleger (Luebeck University), Prof. Birgit Stürmer (International Psychoanalystic University at Berlin), Prof. Suiping Wang (South China Normal University) and Prof. Hua Shu (Beijing Normal University). A workshop on the method RIDE was hold together with Hua Shu at Beijing Normal University.

202710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
202710.value: Neural networks in the brain display complex connectivity such as hierarchical modular organization and dynamical activity such as avalanches and oscillations. This project studied the relationship between network structure and dynamics using the approaches of synchronization. We developed a measure of complexity that can characterized a balance of information segregation and integration and found that complex connectivity, especially the modular organization, has significant impact on dynamical complexity. Real brain networks obtain optimal complexity with a proper combination of modularity and hubs. The complex dynamics in neural system should also impact on functional performance. In cognitive experiments, EEG data is highly complex and response times to task stimuli are highly variable. However, conventional analysis of event-related potential regards such rich dynamical information as noise and eliminates it by averaging. In collaboration with cognitive neuroscientist, we developed a new framework of EEG analysis to obtain latency-variable components associated to cognitive sub-processes. The new method RIDE can obtain much richer dynamical information from brain activity in association to functional performance. This highly interdisciplinary research collaboration has built solid foundation for further exploration of structure-dynamics-function relationship in the brain through the integration of bottom-up modeling of network dynamics and top-down analysis of experimental data.

202810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
202810.value: The classic generalized linear model and the single-index model have been extensively investigated and their asymptotic properties have been the standard results in the literature and particularly, existing estimations have been proved to be asymptotically efficient in the sense that the limiting variances attains minimum in certain classes of regression functions. A fundamental question is: Could we have some estimations who are asymptotically unbiased with smaller limiting variances, in other words, who are asymptotically more efficient than those in the literature? It seems not possible. However, in this project, we will find that we can use a constructive approach to construct semiparametric generalized estimating equations (SGEE), and from those SGEEs, we can obtain smaller limiting variances for the classic generalized linear model and the single-index model correspondingly. We will also consider some gemeralized single-index models 经典的广义线性模型和单指标模型得到了广泛的研究，其渐近性结果已经是文献中的标准结果。特别地，现有的估计已被证明是渐近有效的，也就是他们的渐进方差达到最小。一个根本的问题是：我们能不能有一些渐进无偏估计，达到更小的渐近方差，换言之，渐进意义上更为有效？这似乎是不可能的。然而，在这个项目中，我们会发现，我们可以用建设性的方法来构造广义半参数估计方程（SGEE），并从这些SGEEs，我们可以得到更小的差异限制为经典广义线性模型和单指标模型。

202810.label: Major findings and research outcome
202810.value: In this project, we have three outputs. For the single index model, we proposed a new approach and a new algorithm. The estimation efficiency is proved and the variance is proved to be smaller. The paper has been appeared in Annals of Statistics. For the generalized linear model and the transformation linear model, we proposed a new estimation method. The asymptotic properties are investigated and we can see that in high-dimensional cases, its variance can be much smaller and the method is also robust against the heavy tailed errors. For the multi-index model with missing at random, we give the properties of the estimator, and found that with nonparametric estimation for the weighted inverse probability, the asymptotic variance can be even smaller than that without its estimation.

202810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
202810.value: The methods would be used for variable selection because in the second method for the generalized linear model and the transformation linear model, we mainly use a way to transform the nonlinear problem to a linear problem and thus, it provides a way to use existing approaches such as LASSO or SACD. For the method in Annals of Statistics, we may extend it to handle quantile single-index regression models and then perform variable selection.

202810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
202810.value: In this project, we proposed several approaches to handle the generalized linear model, the transformation linear model, the single-index model and the multi-index model. The asymptotically efficient estimations are constructed and proved. This research plays an useful role in these parametric and semiparametric regression analyses in statistics and econometrics.

210410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
210410.value: 能有效運用醫療資源有賴高效率的醫療作業系統.若配合上良好的調度方法,可為病人提供更及時的診治, 而這對癌症病人尤為重要.根據以往研究顯示,醫療作業上延誤的根源多來自醫療單位及醫療人員間之工序未能協調之故.但因現時醫療系統之復離性及不同的處境,找出問題所有十分困難.同時現時的病人調度系統多未能考慮病人的診治旅程因素, 以致病人常面對非常長的等候及診治旅程. 此研究計劃集中如何應用計算機技術以縮短癌症病人之診治旅程,目的分四方面.首先,計劃將預備一套按現有醫療單位的作業程序及預處理過的作業數據及病人旅程數據.其中將需耍開發軟件工具以支援數據預處理過程.二,將開發動態群組挖掘算法以有效分析導致工作流的延遲的原因,將集中於研究在發掘出群組中存在的主題(motif)及延遲原因是有關連.三,將開發一個基於投標方案的多智能體調度算法,以及比較不同資源掉動策略的有效性.四,將開發一個整合的多智能模擬環境,以支援針對流程改善及病人調度作假設分析. 此研究計劃將利用已建立包括醫療及具數據挖掘及多智能計算機專家的優勢,透過對醫療領域的掌握及建基於真實醫療數據,對以上將開發項目作仔細審查,評估及核實.

210410.label: Realisation of objectives
210410.value: As stated in the Mid-Term Project Report regarding the difficulty faced in collecting healthcare workflow datasets needed for this project (which were understood to be possible at the time when the proposal was prepared), plan B can be to develop a simulation tool for the generation of synthetic datasets. However, such generated datasets are to be validated in order for any subsequent analytic tasks to be meaningful. After reviewing the project schedule, we find that achieving Objective 1 is out of our control. We thus decided to make best use of the relatively small patient journey dataset we collected early on, and focus our effort on the other objectives. For Objective 2, given that patient flow can be interpreted as temporally ordered interactions between different units in a hospital (which to some extent is similar to the interactions revealed in social network data sets and smart home data sets), we developed data mining algorithms for studying the structural properties of the network/graph formed based on the data sets storing human interactions. The probabilistic modeling approach is adopted to identify in the “interactions” the embedded community structures and salient stochastic subgraph patterns. The correctness and effectiveness of the developed algorithms has been evaluated quantitatively and demonstrated to be effective. For the relationship between the structural properties and the functional properties of the network (e.g., cause of delay), so far we can only do that qualitatively. For instance, identifying the collective action pattern in a data set indicates that there exist many hubs which could be the cause of the bottlenecks, resulting in long patient journey. For Objectives 3 and 4, we have developed a multi-agent framework with an adaptive bidding mechanism proposed for determining how additional healthcare resources can be mobilized in a nearly optimal manner for patient journey shortening. Different ways for formulating the bid value have been evaluated regarding their effectiveness in shortening the patient journey. A system for integrating Objectives 2 and 3 cannot be developed as the patient flow data needed cannot be obtained. Still a system that can support the what-if analysis based on different resource allocation strategies based on the proposed agent-based approach (Objective 3) has been developed to support our experiments for performance evaluation.

210410.label: Major findings and research outcome
210410.value: We have developed a number of novel data mining methods using the probabilistic modeling approach for detecting salient subgraph patterns (also called network motifs) [Liu et al. 2011, Liu et al. 2012, Liu et al. 2013]. In particular, we have proposed the use of finite mixture model and a component-wise EM algorithm so as to extract the subgraph patterns reliably in network data, even (1) with the presence of many noisy links and (2) without knowing the number of patterns embedded in the data set. Social network datasets were used (but the algorithms can also be applied to the social networks formed by the interactions of the healthcare units established based on patient flow). A conference version of this work received a best student paper award in PAKDD 2012 [Liu et al. 2012]. A journal paper has been published based on that [Liu et al. 2013]. To further demonstrate their applicability, we have successfully applied the developed algorithms to human interaction analysis [Liu et al. 2013] (similar to interaction between healthcare units) and human mobility analysis [Liu et al. 2012a] (similar to patient flow in a hospital). The corresponding journal versions are in preparation. For identifying the community structures, we used the co-citation data set for the network data and proposed an improved probabilistic model that can better model and integrate the node attributes and their links for community identification [Li et al. 2012, Li et al. 2014]. The effectiveness of the newly proposed model has been carefully evaluated to outperform some state-of-the-art methods (again the algorithms can be applied to the healthcare social networks for analyzing the underlying behavior as revealed by the community structure of the interactions of the healthcare units). One conference paper [Li et al. 2012] and one journal paper are resulted from that work [Li et al. 2014]. In addition to the study of patient flow with the hope to increase the efficiency and thus the daily capacity to treat more patients, this project concerns as well how intelligent allocation of resources can shorten the patient journey more effectively. In particular, we have developed a multi-agent framework with an adaptive bidding mechanism for optimal patient journey shortening [Choi et al. 2010]. A comprehensive empirical evaluation has been conducted, which has been documented in a technical report and will be submitted to a healthcare related journal.

210410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
210410.value: Given the effort we spent in collecting patient workflow data, it seems to us that we may still need to wait for a little while before these kind of research (getting more positive support overseas) can be more accepted in Hong Kong. Since the main research challenges are in fact on human interaction and indoor mobility behaviors, related datasets of other domains can be used. Related research directions can still be carried out. We focus on small subgraph patterns and large community structures in this project. We believe that some daily routines of care providers can be better captured as `”sub-flow” which is of size bigger than subgraph patterns but smaller than community. Effective and scalable ways to extract them will be useful as another research direction and we are looking at that at that moment. Establishing the functional properties and dynamic structural properties of a network is important and yet challenging. More in-depth understanding of this problem is still needed. And regarding the agent-based patient journey analysis, we believe that some context-aware, or in other words phenotype-aware, approaches can be considered so as to allow a more flexible model to be considered in resource allocation.

210410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
210410.value: This research project studies how data revealing the interactions of human or healthcare units can be mined for extracting the underlying behavioral patterns causing the overall interactions observed. In particular, a suite of robust pattern mining algorithms have been developed and demonstrated to be effective using a number of real-world data sets. Such extracted patterns (motifs) can then be presented to domain experts as deeper knowledge on the underlying processes for better managing the involved users or healthcare units for efficiency improvement. In addition, the agent-based system developed for intelligent resource allocation has demonstrated a novel methodology to make use of historical patient journey data for healthcare resource planning in a hospital. We believe that, after further evaluation and benchmarking in a related environment, the system can become a what-if analysis tool to be used by health resource allocation body for decision support on strategic healthcare resource planning to achieve patient journey shortening.

210510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
210510.value: Graph/Network data model has been a powerful tool to model complicated structures such as social networks, network traffic, biological databases and XML documents, among many others. Nowadays, there has been voluminous graph data. A typical task on graph data is to retrieve substructures embedded. Formally speaking, given a query graph and a graph database, we want to find the subgraph(s), in the data graphs, that is/are isomorphic to the query graph. Since subgraph isomorphism has been a NP-hard problem, there has been a few recent works on indexing for subgraph isomorphism. The current state-of-the-art methods almost always comprise two phases -- the filtering and verification phases. The filtering phase aims at pruning subgraphs that are irrelevant to the query graph whereas the verification phase checks isomorphism between the query graph and those that pass the filtering phase. Pruning is often performed by specialized or feature-based indexes. The pruning power of indexes is evidently crucial to the overall performance in answering the query, because the verification phase requires checking subgraph isomorphism. Data graphs are often changing or evolving, which may affect the pruning power of indexes in the filtering phase. Unfortunately, maintenance of such indexes receives far less attention. It was claimed that the pruning power is relatively stable with respect to updates of data graphs. However, we demonstrate in the proposal that such a claim may not be sufficient for some emerging applications on graph data, e.g., social networks. This problem calls for a detailed investigation on the maintenance of the indexes in the filtering phase in response changes of data graphs. A closely related problem is that due to the hardness of subgraph isomorphism, the filtering phase is inherently imperfect. Certain queries may lead to poor pruning. To alleviate this problem, we propose to adjust the indexes adaptively, in response to query workloads. The following four tasks list the novelties of this investigation: (A) We study how existing indexing techniques for subgraph isomorphism are efficiently maintained in response to changes of data graphs; (B) We study how the indexes are adapted to query workloads; (C) We study the connection between filtering and verification phases, which may exploit the computation in the former phase; and (D) We consolidate our results by publishing papers in reputable database journals/conferences and developing a prototype for researchers to reference with. The outcomes of these tasks will result in an advancement of graph-structured databases. 图/网络模型是一个对复杂结构，对应用如：社会网络，网络传输，生物数据库和XML文档等，进行建模的强有力的工具。近年来，随着新应用的不断涌现，图数据的数量不断增加，规模进一步扩大。一个迫切需要解决的问题就是快速地从海量的图数据中检索出特定的子图。具体就是给定一个查询图和一个图数据库，从数据库中检索出与查询图同构的图或子图。子图同构问题是一个NP难题。对该问题最近的研究成果是使用索引的方法进行判断。此类方法通常包括两个阶段：过滤阶段和验证阶段。过滤阶段把与查询图不相关的子图过滤掉（或称剪枝），剩余的子图进入验证阶段进行子图同构的验证。剪枝通常是借助于特定的或者基于特征的索引完成。索引的剪枝能力是整个系统性能的关键。 实际应用中，图数据库在不断更新。数据图的更新可以削弱索引的剪枝能力，这要求我们对索引进行更新维护。然而，索引的更新维护目前并未得到应有的重视。尽管有人声称静态索引的剪枝能力在数据图更新时保持基本稳定，但是我们发现静态索引并不能满足某些新兴应用，如社会网络的要求。这使得我们有必要对索引更新维护问题进行更加深入的研究。 另外，由于子图同构问题的复杂性，索引的剪枝性能不可避免的会在某些查询集上表现稍差。针对这个问题，我们提出自适应的索引，以应对不同的查询集。

210510.label: Realisation of objectives
210510.value: Objective 1. We have proposed incremental maintenance of some fundamental graph indexes (bisimulation), which are known to be useful for a wide variety of graph queries such as reachability queries, and path and pattern queries [TKDE2]. The graph (e.g. social network graphs) may change rapidly. We showed that the index can be efficiently maintained as the graph changes. Several optimizations have been proposed. The results show that the index can be almost always up-to-date by paying a small amount of update cost and query performance remains efficient, as the graph evolves. Hence, the objective is 100% achieved. Objectives 2 and 3. We have studied the efficiency of existing indexing (filtering and verification approaches) for subgraph queries (both subgraph isomorphism and subgraph similarity) [TSC, TKDE1]. As we were investigating the problem, we realized that an important issue of subgraph queries is that their processing can be very time consuming (where the worst-case theoretical complexity is exponential to the graph size). A trendy solution is to shift the query processing to a cloud. The party responsible for query processing is now changed to the cloud. We have proposed indexing techniques that are suitable to support processing in this environment. Since the cloud may be hacked or not trustable, our technique can efficiently verify the authenticity of query answers, which is essential to the cloud environment. In addition, users' queries may change. We study the adaptation of the index in the context of GUI for graph databases, developed at the co-I's institute, where we can find some real changes in query workloads. In [VLDBJ, CIDR, ICDE], we have proposed indexing for processing queries as the users are drawing them. The index is aware of the users' actions that change the queries. Our findings are that subgraph queries can be efficient and scalable as the users are changing the queries. For large graphs, we propose new partitioning algorithm which minimizes network bandwidth [SOCC]; and indexing different subgraphs with different indexes [PAKDD]. Therefore, the objective is 100% achieved. Objective 4. We have published our results in reputable journals (please see Part C) and we have conducted empirical studies on all of our proposed techniques. We have implementations (prototypes) of the proposed techniques for researchers to repeat our experiments. Hence this objective is 100% achieved.

210510.label: Major findings and research outcome
210510.value: Objective 1. In [TKDE2], we showed that: - the graph index (bisimulation) can be efficiently incrementally maintained; - the advantages of this approach is that the index is almost always online. That is, it is not necessary to take the index offline for index reconstruction; - the maintenance algorithm can support large graphs; and - a cost model is derived to determine the optimal setting to maintain the index. In [TSC], we found that - the filtering and verification framework for subgraph queries can be efficiently outsourced to a cloud while the authenticity of query answers is guaranteed; and - both the computation at the query client and the communication between the client and the cloud are small and therefore the shift of the framework to the cloud is practical. In [TKDE1], we found that - the filtering and verification framework of subgraph similarity search can be efficient, too; - subgraph similarity can be expressed using the graph metric distance and the metric distances between graphs can be indexed; and - the filtering phase is done at the cloud and the verification is mostly done at the cloud. The work done at the client side is minor. In [VLDBJ, CIDR, ICDE], we found that - it is efficient and intuitive to provide GUI for querying graph databases; - it is efficient to interleave the filtering and the verification phases as the user is drawing queries; and - this approach is further extended to support large graphs [VLDBJ] and similarity search [ICDE]. In [SOCC], we propose new partitioning algorithm which minimizes network bandwidth [SOCC] for large graphs. An extended description of our work is included in a book chapter [Book]. In [PAKDD], we propose the first optimal index prediction model (derived from spectral graph theory). We revealed that the optimal index for graphs may change as the graph itself changes. By using the model, users can quickly determine if there is a change in the optimal index. In [TKDE3], we applied the filtering approach to a fundamental computer science problem, namely the view update problem. Specifically, instead of invoking the costly update view translation algorithm, we proposed a lightweight update filter, where most untranslatable updates are simply rejected. The performance improvement of the filtering approach is significant. We obtain the US patent for the filtering approach (No. 61/863,448).

210510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
210510.value: In this study, we have developed indexing for adapting the change of query workloads in the context of GUI of graph databases. The reasons are that in such applications, we can obtain real evolving query workload and GUI for graph database is intuitive. We have demonstrated the GUI in various research conferences [SIGMOD1, SIGMOD2] and obtained many positive feedback. We have also studied the authentictiy of query answer in the cloud environment, as the complexity of subgraph queries are often high. We foresee there are at least two further development directionsof our research. First, we have not combined the GUI in the context of cloud. We expect that there are adaptive and "authenticable" index for GUI for the cloud. This is expected to be a scalable and usable solution for querying graph databases. Second, we expect that the usability of GUI of graph databases should be further enhanced. We expect that performance is not the only consideration for usable GUI. We plan to investigate query suggestions to subgraph queries as users are formulating queries with our GUI.

210510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
210510.value: In this project, we showed that graph index (bisimulation) can be incrementally maintained. The nice property of incremental maintenance is that as data graph evolves, query performances will not degrade and the index can be online most of the time. The second achievement is that we have successfully shift the computation of subgraph queries (the filtering and verification framework) to the cloud and the computational results of the cloud is authenticated. The third achievement is that we have interleaved the filtering and verification phases of subgraph queries when the users are using a GUI to draw subgraph queries. To support large graphs, we have proposed network bandwidth aware graph partitioning on the cloud. In all, we have proposed a scalable and efficient method to support subgraph queries (both exact and similar subgraph queries). We have proposed efficient algorithms to handle data changes and query changes. We have showed our solution on top of the co-I's institute's GUI for graph databases.

211510.value: 快閃記憶體由於其讀寫速度快和省電等性能優勢，近年來已成為外部存儲設備除了硬碟外的另外一種主要選擇。快閃記憶體上的資料管理應用需求迅速增加。但由於快閃記憶體的物理特性和硬碟有很大差異，如把應用於硬碟的傳統資料庫技術直接轉移到快閃記憶體上會帶來很多問題。特別是快閃記憶體的讀寫速度不對稱，隨機寫比較慢，這使得需要很多隨機寫操作的事務處理性能大大降低。因此我們將從快閃記憶體的物理特性入手，在本項目中提出一系列新的技術和方法來提升快閃記憶體資料庫的事務管理性能。

211510.label: Realisation of objectives
211510.value: The project objectives have been successfully realized. We have developed a novel transaction commit scheme, called FlagCommit, to exploit the unique characteristics of flash disks [Journal/1]. We have also exploited the efficient write patterns of flash devices to optimize the write performance for database applications [Conference/1]. To optimize the buffer management and query processing performance, we have designed FD-Buffer and DigestJoin for database systems running on flash-based disks [Journal/2, Journal/3, Conference/2, Conference/4]. Furthermore, we have developed a novel logging scheme that uses PCM devices for both data caching and transaction logging [Journal/4, Conference/3]. In all the above studies, trace-driven experiments based on TPC benchmarks have been conducted to evaluate the proposed algorithms and schemes. In addition, we have implemented the proposed transaction processing and buffer management techniques in an open-source PostgreSQL database and demonstrated their performance via the prototype system.

211510.label: Major findings and research outcome
211510.value: In this project, we have studied how transaction recovery can be efficiently supported in database management systems (DBMSs) running on flash disks. Inspired by the classical shadow-paging approach, we have proposed a new transaction commit scheme, called FlagCommit, to exploit the unique characteristics of flash disks such as fast random read access, out-place updating, and partial page programming [Journal/1]. To minimize the need of writing log records, the transaction status is embedded into flash pages through a chain of commit flags. Based on FlagCommit, we have developed two recovery protocols, namely commit-based flag commit (CFC) and abort-based flag commit (AFC), to meet different performance needs. They are flexible to support no-force buffer management and fine-grained concurrency control. Furthermore, we have developed a novel logging scheme, called PCMLogging, to exploit PCM devices for both data caching and transaction logging [Journal/4, Conference/3]. Speciﬁcally, PCMLogging caches dirty pages/records in PCM and further maintains an implicit log in the cached updates to support database recovery. By integrating log and cached updates, PCMLogging enables simplified recovery and prolongs PCM lifetime. We have also exploited the efficient write patterns of flash devices to optimize the write performance for DBMS applications [Conference/1]. Specifically, motivated by a focused write pattern, we have proposed to write pages temporarily to a small, pre-allocated storage space on the flash device, called StableBuffer, instead of directly writing to their actual destinations. In contrast to prior log-based techniques, our StableBuffer solution does not require modifying the driver of flash devices and hence works well for commodity flash devices. To optimize the buffer performance, we have designed a buffer manager, called FD-Buffer, for database systems running on flash-based disks [Journal/3, Conference/2]. In detail, we use the average I/O cost per page access as opposed to the traditional miss rate as the performance metric. We have developed a new replacement policy in which we separate clean and dirty pages into two pools. The size ratio of the two pools is automatically adapted to the read-write asymmetry and the runtime workload. We have also designed an efficient mid-tier cache solution that overcomes the weakness caused by the indirect use of flash memory [Conferecne/4]. In addition, in order to optimize non-indexed join processing, we have proposed a new framework, called DigestJoin, to reduce the intermediate result size by exploiting fast random reads of flash disks [Journal/2].

211510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
211510.value: As for further development, we plan to extend the proposed logging schemes with PCM devices in a few directions. First, with PCM as a data buffer, data should be destaged from PCM to the disk when the PCM is about to be filled up. I/O-efficient data destaging strategies will be designed by considering the database workloads and disk characteristics. Second, since flash disks and PCM have the limitation of write endurance, wear-leveling will be considered in space allocation when new tuples are to be buffered. Third, so far we have assumed lock-based concurrency control; we will investigate how the logging schemes can work with other concurrency control mechanisms such as multi-version concurrency control.

211510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
211510.value: Owing to the superiority in access latency and energy consumption, flash memory drives have recently become a competitive alternative to magnetic hard disks as secondary storage. Consequently, flash-based database systems have been receiving increasing attention from the research community in the past few years. However, flash memory drives possess a number of unique I/O characteristics, which make the state-of-the-art database techniques that assumed I/O characteristics of magnetic hard disks suboptimal when implemented on flash memory drives. In particular, flash memory drives have a relatively slow random write speed due to an erase-before-write constraint. This significantly deteriorates the performance of on-line transaction processing where randomly scattered write requests are common. In this project, we have developed a number of optimization techniques for transaction management in flash-based database systems, by exploiting the characteristics of flash memory drives (such as out-of-place updates, page reprogramming, and efficient write patterns). Our performance evaluation based on TPC benchmarks demonstrates the performance superiority of the proposed techniques.

211710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
211710.value: Multiplicative noise removal is a very challenging problem since this kind of noise may contaminate images in a totally different way from additive noise. This research proposal is centered on the development of image restoration models for multiplicative noise denoising and deblurring. The importance of multiplicative noise relies on many aspects. As is well known, they are commonly found in many real world image processing applications, such as laser images, microscope images, medical ultrasonic images and SAR images. Unlike additive noises, these noises are much more difficult to be removed from the corrupted image, mainly not only because of their multiplicative nature, but also because of their distributions which are generally not Gaussian. In this proposal, we consider variational approaches based on the theory of image restoration, optimization and statistic. Indeed, we will first examine a general method to deal with the non-convex model revoked by multiplicative noise. In particular, we are interested in the AA model and RLO-I model. We then derive a new variational method for blurred image with multiplicative noise and study how to effectively solve it. After that, we turn to establishing new variational model that can also capture the texture information in the ideal image. Finally, we study the blind deconvolution problem under multiplicative noise. 乘性噪聲消除非常具有挑戰性, 因為該噪音以完全不同於加性噪聲的方法污染圖像. 本研究項目致力於研究乘性去噪和去模糊圖像復原模型. 乘性噪聲的重要性依賴於許多方面. 眾所周知，它們通常存在許多現實世界中的圖像處理應用中，如激光圖像，顯微圖像，醫學超聲圖像和合成孔徑雷達圖像。和高斯噪音不同, 這種噪音非常難以去除. 這不僅由於它的乘性性質, 更由於它在統計上不服從高斯分佈. 本研究項目考慮基於圖像恢復, 優化, 統計等方面理論的變分方法. 事實上, 我們首先考察乘性噪音引起的非凸問題. 特別的, 我們研究AA模型和RLO-I模型. 我們接下來對乘性噪音和模糊給出一個新的變分模型並考慮如何有效求解該模型. 在此之後, 我們考慮建立更好的模型以捕捉圖像的紋理信息. 最後, 我們考慮乘性噪音下的圖像盲恢復.

240110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
240110.value: This research aims at analysing the drivers that are pushing African countries to develop closer relations with China or, on the contrary, that are complicating these relations. The basic question which this research ambitions to address is the following: Are African nations expecting from China a type of partnership that they cannot build with other big powers, as the US, Britain, France, Japan or India? Or, conversely, are African nations just trying to develop with China the same kind of economic cooperation as well as diplomatic and people-to-people relations as with the other developed or emerging countries that have been present and active for a longer time on the Black Continent? Are they specific problems that affect negatively Africa’s attitude towards China? On the one hand, I will analyse the economic drivers of Sino-African relations. This research will attempt to identify and evaluate the drivers that have pushed these governments to deal with China rather than other countries as well as the new problems both sides have to manage (ex: Chinese immigration). On the other hand, I will analyse the diplomatic, political and cultural determinants of Sino-African relations. I will in particular study whether a closer partnership with China: 1) is promoted as a balancer of Western influences; 2) is stimulated by African governments’ need for external support on a particular international issue in which they are involved; 3) is motivated by a quest for cheaper military procurement and cooperation; or finally 4) is driven by an interest in China’s way of development, culture and language or political system. In order to address these questions, I have selected a sample of a dozen African countries, chosen because of their different size, historical background, economic structures and resources and political nature. In these countries, I will conduct qualitative interviews with the main actors influencing the relations with China and collect data that are not available in Hong Kong or in mainland China. I will in particular study three countries rich in oil and other raw materials: Angola, Gabon and Sudan; four African regional powers that have developed a multi-dimensional relationship with China: the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa; and four smaller states with which China has established a close partnership for reasons that are not mainly economic but rather political: Ghana, Senegal, Tanzania and Zimbabwe. 《日益密切的中國-非洲關係：雙邊合作誘因的比較研究》 本文旨在分析中國和非洲國家發展雙邊合作背後的誘因，同時涉及可能導致關係複雜化的議題。作者想知道的是：非洲國家是不是在中、非交往裡尋求與包括美、英、法、日、印等大國的關係中沒有的獨特原素？還是跟中國建立同別的大國早已有了之經濟、外交和人脈關係？此外，非洲國家有沒有對中國不滿的具體問題呢？ 我們首先想分析中非關係中最重要的經濟因素：非洲各國為什麼那麼熱心地向北京靠攏呢？在密切的交往中，會出現什麼新問題呢？雙方如何處理例如中國移民湧入等問題？另一方面，我們想研究中非關係中的政治、外交和文化因素，尤其是以下各具體議題： 1)非洲國家想平衡西方影響；2) 非洲國家需要借助外力來處理個別國際問題(例如達爾富爾) ；3)企圖向中國購買廉價軍備和爭取軍事合作；4)非洲國家希望仿效中國發展模式和學習它的語言、文化和政治制度。 我們在研究過程裡，據國土大小、歷史背景、經濟結構、資源和政治制度，選擇了十多個非洲國家作為研究對象，跟涉足中非交往的人士進行訪問等質性研究，而搜集到的資料獨特，無論在香港和中國內地都找不到。 我的研究對象計有，安哥拉、加蓬和蘇丹三個盛產石油和天然資源的國家；剛果民主共和國、埃塞俄比亞、肯尼亞、尼日利亞和南非五個與中國建立多邊合作關係的地區大國；以及迦納、塞內加爾、坦桑尼亞和津巴布韋四個中國為了政治而非經濟理由而刻意親近的國家。

240110.label: Realisation of objectives
240110.value: I have achieved all four objectives: I have published five articles and a book review on the major drivers determining African's countries policy towards and perception of China in looking at both the whole picture and specific cases (Ethiopia, Gabon, Cameroon) in refereed academic journals. A sixth article on Tanzania's relations with China is still under review. This research output is based on six fieldwork trips to a dozen African countries: Ethiopia, Djibouti, Kenya, Tanzania, Togo, Benin, Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, The Gambia, Guinea, Gabon, Cameroon and Angola. With the help of a research assistant, I have constituted a large data base on Sino-African relations which is both on my computer and on separate CDs. I have taken part in several international conferences related to China-Africa relations, including two in Washington DC, liaising with other researchers in this field and contributing to the knowledge and understanding of the issue. Conducting fieldwork in Africa is not easy; it requires a lot of preparatory work. Chinese actors (embassies, companies, entrepreneurs) are not always ready to talk. And African data or perceptions are far from being always reliable, compelling me to double-check many of the collected information. Hence the extension of my GRF to four years. In addition, some of the countries that I wanted to visit, as Sudan or the Democratic Republic of Congo, have been too unsafe for me to do research, forcing me to modify the sample that I initially included in my research plan. For these reasons, I have not been able to write a research article on each of the African country where I conducted some fieldwork. I have completed such a research article only on the four countries (Ethiopia, Gabon, Cameroon and Tanzania) where I was able to gather enough reliable data. However, I have used many of the data or information found in every country that I visited in other research outputs, as in a more general article on Sino-African relations or the section on Sino-African relations in the latest edition of my book on China's foreign and security policy (in French). In spite of these difficulties, I think that I have fulfilled the objectives indicated above and have now a much better comprehension of the drivers determining African countries' policy towards and perception of China. These drivers are mainly of economic nature. However, political, strategic and even cultural drivers have contributed to intensifying Africa's relationship with China.
