240110.label: Major findings and research outcome
240110.value: The most important driver determining African's countries' policy towards and perception of China are of economic nature, China having become a major economic power and importer of oil, minerals and other natural resources as timber. China is also today Africa's first trade partner, ahead of the United States and any other traditional (as France or the United Kingdom) or new partners (as India or Brazil) of the continent. However, other drivers, of more political, strategic or even cultural nature, have led some African governments and societies to develop a closer relationship with China: the attractiveness of China's economic and political model, China's growing soft power and cultural activism as well as African countries' willingness to diversify their partnerships and strengthen their hand in their relations and negotiations with their traditional partners. Oil and other raw material exporting African countries have a vested interest in developing closer economic relations with China. Following Angola and the so-called "Angola Model", they are tempted to get more or less advantageous loans from China guaranteed by these exports to finance the construction on their soil of infrastructures and other badly-needed development projects. These projects are mainly realized by Chinese companies, which are often cheaper and faster in completing them, but also thanks to the close relationship that the Beijing government has developed with many African countries. While contributing to speeding up Africa's economic development, this new type of business relationship has triggered some negative reactions from a growing number of African governments and societies that have complained about the tied nature of China's cooperation or assistance, the large number of Chinese workers involved in these projects, the bad practices of a number of Chinese entrepreneurs, particularly in logging or fishing, the poor quality of some of the Chinese construction or infrastructure projects and the growing number of Chinese migrants that have settled in Africa and compete with local shopkeepers or entrepreneurs. These criticisms have contributed to dividing African countries between the China optimists and the China pessimists. To be sure, a majority of African countries belong to the first group. Ethiopia is probably the best example, being also attracted by the Chinese development and political model. At the same time, many of the countries that I visited, do not wish to become over dependent upon China. This is the case of Gabon, Cameroon and even Tanzania that have all diversified in the last few years their external partnerships.

240110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
240110.value: In 2014, I obtained another three year GRF on "The rise and limits of China's influence in Sub-Saharan Africa" that I started to carry out in 2015. My plan is to build on the foundation of the first GRF that I received to explore and better comprehend the scope and limits of China's economic, political, strategic and cultural influence in Africa, looking in particular at China's impact on African countries' foreign policy objectives and priorities. The additional field work that I will conduct in Sub-Sahara Africa will also contribute to a more comprehensive and probably contrasted understanding of Sino-African relations and the major drivers determining African countries' policy towards and perception of China. Expanding the sample studied to another eight African countries (including Mozambique, Burkina Faso, Mali, Congo-Brazaville and Rwanda) will help comprehending Africa's management of China's growing role, the options that they can contemplate and the new areas of bilateral or multilateral cooperation that they can contemplate with China and other players, particularly in the realm of security and cooperation against terrorism. This new research will also attempt at better evaluating both cooperation and competition among Africa's traditional and emerging partners, particularly the US, France, Britain, Japan, China, India and Brazil.

240110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
240110.value: China's rapid economic development and increasing needs of natural resources, as oil, minerals or timber, have directly stimulated its relations with Africa. However, all African countries, including the one that have not much to offer to China (as Ethiopia or Senegal) have intensified their relationship with China, importing more and more cheap products from there or choosing Beijing's attractive loans and Chinese companies to realize much needed infrastructure or development projects. China's growing economic role in Africa has contributed to enhancing its political, strategic and even cultural influence on the black continent. African capitals must now factor in Beijing's diplomatic interests in their own foreign policy decisions. Nevertheless, this closer relationship is not without its problems: the tied nature of China's cooperation or assistance, the important number of Chinese workers involved in Chinese construction projects, the bad quality of some of these projects and the increasing wave of Chinese migrants settling down in Africa have complicated Beijing's relations with many African governments and societies, particularly in Angola, Cameroon, Gabon, Ghana and Nigeria. As a result, more African countries have tried to limit their dependence upon China and diversify their options with partners as the US, France, Japan or India .

240210.label: Project Title(Chinese)
240210.value: 跨國朝聖, 旅遊與身份政治: 媽祖祟拜的人類學研究

240210.label: Project Objectives
240210.value: To introduce a new analytical approach, with special reference to a Taiwan-Macau-China triadic pattern of shared religious traditions, to explore and analyze a complex and multifaceted relationship between pilgrimage, tourism and identity within and across national borders. To complement the current literature on the popular cult of Mazu in Taiwan and China by giving due attention to the role and position of the post-colonial Macau government and the local community in the further development of this region-wide religious cult and its social, cultural, economic and political implications at the local and regional or national level. To contribute to the emerging anthropological study of tourism of “Asian origin” (tourism in Asia by Asian tourists). This research conceptualizes and analyzes the transnational Mazu cult (religious-cultural tourism) as an assemblage of an array of interconnected networks and flows of people, images, culture, knowledge, politics and capital that move within and across national borders. The findings will enhance our understanding of the cultural, economic and political significances of popular religion and tourism in the contexts of: (i) fast-growing and competitive Asian tourism; and (ii) the development of modern nationalisms between Taiwan and China in terms of national unification.

240210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
240210.value: The worship of Mazu (Goddess of Heaven) is the most popular cult in Taiwan and costal China. Macau, a costal city-state whose name is derived from this seafarers’ goddess known locally as A-Ma, has no exception. Built in the 15th century and managed by several ethnic groups, the A-Ma Temple has been a ritual center of the Mazu cult and a major tourist attraction. In recent years, its centuries-old leading role has been challenged by another group which aspires to promote a new form of worship and celebration. In 2001, it started building a A-Ma Cultural Village—a 7,000 square meter complex of towers, temple palaces, a museum and shops, with its architectural design copied from the Mazu ancestral temple on Meizhou Island in Fujian. They also followed Meizhou to organize Mazu Cultural Tourism Festival annually in Macau. The festival includes: pilgrimage to major Mazu temples in Taiwan and Fujian; an elaborate ritual of offerings to the goddess; a grand Mazu procession; and an array of performances and activities organized by an invited mainland city. By 2009, the pilgrimage and the festival had attracted approximately 200 million worshippers and tourists worldwide. This research examines the implications of the above development from a socio-cultural perspective. At the local level, it investigates ways in which the old and new Mazu temples compete for reputation, resources and donations, and worshippers, and how they struggle to (re)define a sacred ritual centre, religious community and collective identity in Macau. At the regional level, it reveals how the new form of worship contributed to the development of Macau sustainable tourism in competitive Asian tourism industry. And, it investigates Macau’s newly-defined mission and role in promoting the cult and culture of Mazu across the Taiwan Strait for the continuity of the civilization of Greater China in modern contexts. At the national level, it explores the political meaning of that sacred transnational cult in the context of complex interactions between China and Taiwan. Focus will be on how such a cult defines a strategic position and role of Macau, particularly in post-colonial era, in helping the Chinese government advocate a modern Chinese nationalism or a national imaginary between China and Taiwan, through the shared religious traditions. In sum, this research aims at revealing a complex and multifaceted relationship between pilgrimage, religious tourism and identity in the context and framework of a Taiwan-Macau-China triadic pattern of religious connection. 媽祖祟拜流行於台灣及南中國， 包括了以媽祖命名的澳門。建於15世紀， 由多個族群管理的媽閣廟， 是澳門供奉媽祖的中心， 亦是當地的旅遊勝地。 近年， 它的地位受到了挑戰， 一新興政商群體銳意建立新的媽祖祭祀及慶祝方式。 在2001年，它們興建了媽祖文化村--該村佔地7，000平方米， 由鐘樓、 廟堂、 博物館和商舖組成， 而且建築設計完全仿照福建湄洲島媽祖祖廟。另外， 它們參照湄洲島的慶典， 在澳門每年舉辦媽祖文化旅遊節。 文化旅遊節包括有隆重的祭祀大典、大型的神像出巡、以及一系列由國內受邀文博團體舉辦的民娛活動。 直至2009年， 跨國媽祖朝聖活動及文化旅遊節共吸引了2000萬來自世界各地的旅客及朝聖者。 這項研究以社會文化的角度來審視上述的發展。 在地方層面， 研究將探討新舊媽祖廟宇在名聲、 資源、 捐款及信徒方面的競爭， 以及如何重申界定它們在澳門的祭祀地位、 與社區的關係、 以及集體認同。 在區域層面， 研究將掀示， 在亞洲區內競爭激烈的旅遊工業當中， 新的媽祖祭祀、 跨國朝拜活動如何促進澳門旅遊業的可持續發展。 研究亦會探討澳門在海峽兩岸中媽祖祟拜作為當代大中華文化延續所擔當的角色。 在國家層面， 研究將探索媽祖跨國朝聖活動在中台互動關係上的政治意義。 研究重點包括:這一新興跨國朝聖活動如何釐定澳門於回歸前後， 在當代中國政府借助媽祖信仰推動中台兩地的現代民族主義或民族想像的政治脈絡下所扮演的角色。 總括而言， 是項研究旨在掀示， 在中-澳-台三地共同的媽祖信仰基礎上， 跨國朝聖、旅遊與身份政治之間的多層複雜關係。

240210.label: Realisation of objectives
240210.value: During the research period, I had conducted participant-observation in a series of festive events (all celebrated a common deity Mazu--Goddess of Heaven) organized by different Mazu cult groups (both local and governmental) in Macau, Taiwan and China. Through anthropological fieldwork, I had observed, and collected much information about the development, operation and management of these events as well as the intricate relationships between different cult groups at the regional and national level. In addition, informal communications with some organizing committee members on various occasions had allowed me to learn about the nature, characteristics and meanings of those events in the context of cross-strait relations. Moreover, I had conducted in-depth interviews with some temple leaders in Taiwan (who had been actively participating in the Mazu cultural tourism festival organized by Macau over the years) about their views on Macau’s Mazu festival and on its organizing committee’s formal and regular visits to them. All these information helped me understand comprehensively the strategic role of Macau and its meanings in promoting the Mazu cult and its related festival (held annually from 2004 onwards) which has been particularly focusing on Taiwanese cult groups and pilgrims. They also revealed the political meaning of this transnational festival in post-colonial Macau (in collaboration with dedicated and designated official organizations from China). The findings complement current literature on the study of cross-strait relations which has missed the role of Macau in bridging official and local Mazu cult groups from China and Taiwan in a new platform as well as promoting cultural exchange (including Chinese culture, history and identity) and dialogues between them. In the meantime, 3 sets of questionnaires (474 pieces in total) had been completed during the festive events held in Macau and China in different periods of time. The respondents were Taiwan pilgrims and Macau local residents. The first two sets of questionnaires achieved to reveal their perceptions of, and views on, the meanings and significance of those events. The third set of questionnaire were completed in the summer of 2013 and 2014 by tourists (largely from China) when they visited A-Ma Cultural Village, Macau. These questionnaires substantially captured the level of attractiveness of the A-Ma Cultural Village and its potential as an emerging popular sightseeing point when the cult and culture of Mazu is now a world heritage.

240210.label: Major findings and research outcome
240210.value: First, this project achieved to reveal the cultural and political implications of Macau’s Mazu cultural tourism festival (in collaboration with Chinese authorities) for Taiwanese pilgrims. After its return to China in 1999, Macau has been playing a strategic role on behalf of the Chinese government to strengthen cultural exchange and interactions with Taiwanese and between Taiwanese and mainland Chinese. Through these, it aimed at providing a platform and opportunities for Taiwanese to learn more about their history, cultural root, traditions and Chinese identity. This explained why the festival has mainly focused on Taiwanese cult groups and why the organizing committee has actively cultivated and maintained its networks with them. The findings of research project suggest a Taiwan-Macau-China triadic pattern of shared religious connection that highlights a new emerging role of Macau in promoting the Mazu cult in the contexts of cross-strait relations, the continuity of Greater China civilization across a region, and a national imaginary between China and Taiwan. Preliminary findings had been presented at the annual meeting of American Anthropological Association in late 2011. Second, Mazu cultural tourism festival has been promoted by the Macau government as a major event to highlight the attractiveness of Macau whose name is derived from the name of Mazu. It was especially after the city has been conferred an UNESCO World Heritage status in 2005. Therefore, this project found that the Mazu festival provides a new force to promote and maintain a symbiotic relationship between popular religion and the development of sustainable cultural tourism in Macau. Besides the festival, the A-Ma Cultural Village (where major rituals and the opening ceremony of the festival are held) is a new tourist attraction. The questionnaires we had collected from the visitors at the Village revealed that the site, albeit new and located remotely, is also attractive compared with the oldest and popular Mazu temple (built in the 15th century). The questionnaires also revealed how to enhance its attractiveness and competitiveness in the field of religious-cultural tourism not only in Macau but also in neighbouring countries. The findings of these questionnaires will be developed into a research article.

240210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
240210.value: Based on the networks and trust relations that I have established with many Mazu cult groups in Macau and Taiwan, I propose to explore further the dominant and hierarchal relationship among them in terms of resources allocation or contribution for organizing the religious activities. In addition, in this project it is found that some Taiwanese cult groups actively invested their huge amount of annual income (mainly from worshippers’ donations) into Mazu-related tourism project in China. It is worthy of studying how this particular type of investment shape the nature and the direction of religious-cultural tourism in China in the long run.

240210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
240210.value: This research project examines the development and meanings of a newly developed celebrating event on the deity Mazu (Goddess of Heaven) and its ritual and heritage center, the A-Ma Cultural Village, in Macau. Since the event is organized by Macau official and local organizations, and particularly in collaboration with Chinese authorities, its cultural, economic and political meanings deserve our attention. By examining the popularity of that event held at a significantly large scale in the past eleven years and that Taiwanese pilgrims have been its targeted participants, this research suggested that Macau, after its return to China in 1999, has been playing a strategic role in providing a platform for promoting and enhancing cultural exchange and interactions between different cult groups from Taiwan and China. Also, this project revealed the attractiveness and competitiveness of the A-Ma Cultural Village in the context of religious-cultural tourism in Macau and its neighbouring countries. It is found that the A-Ma Cultural Village offers various attractions, though its history is short and location remote. For maintaining competiveness and sustainable development, this tourist site is recommended to further develop its unique cultural resources and facilities.

242110.value: 二十世紀香港書法：從文化及社會視角看藝術 本研究擬用一整合的方法，以考察二十世紀香港書法生產和消費的藝術、文化及社會情境。探究書法如何於社曾發展進程中，在人們的文化和社交生活中扮演關鍵的角色。研究範圍函概100名生於本港的居民、外來移民及短期客居於港並有顯著影響力的書法家及其作品。研究目標為完成以下香港書法專著中三章的第一章： 1. 社曾菁英生活中的書法 2. 市場中的書法 3. 公共空間中的書法

242110.label: Realisation of objectives
242110.value: In response to the comment from an external reviewer that the original scope of the project is too ambitious if viewing art from all the 3 cultural, social, and economic perspectives, the PI has narrowed down the scope and revised the first objective as “to offer a theoretical break-through in art history by offering a holistic investigation on how calligraphy played a pivotal role in people’s cultural and social lives in the course of societal development.” Although there has been richly multi-faceted development of Chinese calligraphy in Hong Kong, little research has been conducted that yields a thorough and satisfying understanding of this subject, apart from exhibition catalogues and chronicles pertaining to calligraphic activities, and scattered discussions and critiques on individual calligraphers’ biographies and personal styles. Traditional Chinese art historians largely emphasize the examination of calligraphic works as art objects, and hence the over-reliance on stylistic analysis in academic inquiries. Attempting to fill the gap in the research on Hong Kong calligraphy, the research output offers a theoretical break-through in art history by offering a holistic investigation on how calligraphy played a pivotal role in people’s cultural and social lives in the course of societal development. Moreover, important historical and cultural events pertaining to twentieth-century Hong Kong calligraphy have been examined and embedded in the research output, which in a sense; contribute to a new understanding of history and the history of calligraphy. Addressing the issue of how works of calligraphy in Hong Kong embody a strong sense of cultural identity, the papers listed in Part C enhance the understanding of important aspects of the development of the arts and culture in Hong Kong that ultimately fosters a sense of cultural identity. Hence, the 3 objectives of this research projects have been largely achieved.

242110.label: Major findings and research outcome
242110.value: The PI was invited as Visiting Scholar to present a lecture entitled “Chinese Calligraphy in Hong Kong” at Peking University (北京大學) in 2012. As initial research findings, the lecture presents how Chinese calligraphy was used as a vehicle mapping and interpreting the development of cultural identity in twentieth-century Hong Kong. After further investigation, a conference paper entitled "In Search of Identity: Chinese Calligraphy in Twentieth-Century Hong Kong," was presented and has been revised and submitted for peer-refereeing before publication. Through specific themes, including 1.) A Chinese Intellectual's Encounter with the West; 2.) The Propagandas of the Revolutionaries; 3.) The Pride of Qing Dynasty “Left-over Subject”; 4.) From Erudition to Contemporary Life, this paper presents the research findings on the historic and societal circumstances in which works of calligraphy were produced in a way that calligraphic works were viewed as vehicles projecting a strong sense of social and cultural identity. For instance, Wang Tao’s calligraphy, as existed in the form of the inscription of his portrait photo and letters, reveal the calligrapher’s ambivalent self-image as a miserable fugitive yet intellectual in Hong Kong who was blessed with his proactive encounter with the foreign world. Next, works of calligraphy by the revolutionaries were produced as vehicles for spreading ideological and social ideals, hence effective propaganda to fan the flame of revolution. In contrast, calligraphy by Lai Jixi (1865-1937) and his literati circle often reflect a relatively more subtle sense of elitist and scholarly identity through their use of literary allusions, metaphors and delicate poetic lines as the literary content of their calligraphic works. Moreover, a strong sense of the special identity of Qing Dynasty “left-over subject” or “loyalist” and diasporal sentiments is often projected as an intangible cultural identity. The utilization of ancient script types is a typical approach for some calligraphers to suggest their erudition. To address the change from the traditional literati culture to the pluralistic and multifaceted city life in Hong Kong, other artists’ works reveal various aspects of the dynamic life and contemporary occurrences in Hong Kong. The forthcoming paper “Clerical Script of the Han Dynasty as the Foundation of a Convergence of the Stele and Model-book Studies: The Calligraphy of Han Yunshan,” listed under “other impact” offers an in-depth case study of how a major Hong Kong calligrapher’s artistic philosophy and career were developed in social and cultural contexts.

242110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
242110.value: Based on this project’s established knowledge and theoretical framework, future research can examine calligraphy from an entirely different perspective by investigating how calligraphy transformed from an elitist art, into a more accessible form of visual culture, namely calligraphy as a decoration and an integral part of architectural spaces in Hong Kong. Appearing at public venues, the more accessible calligraphic works, in such forms as engraved couplet (楹聯) and tablet, serve as identity markers of venues of cultural, historical and religious significance such as ancestral shrines, schools, charity organizations, public parks, historic sites, temples, and Christian churches. In fact, this special category of public calligraphy can be viewed as the embodied image of the following four major aspects of local culture: indigenous clan culture, civic culture, political culture and religious culture.

242110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
242110.value: Traditional researches on Chinese calligraphy in the field of art history tend to emphasize the analysis of stylistic lineages and the artistic aspects of works of calligraphy. By contrast, this project examines how Chinese calligraphy was practiced in Hong Kong in the twentieth and pre-twentieth century, and the historic and societal circumstances in which works of calligraphy were produced in such a unique way that calligraphic works were not only viewed as art objects but also vehicles projecting a strong sense of social and cultural identity. Addressing the issue of how works of calligraphy in Hong Kong embody a strong sense of cultural identity, the research project enhances the understanding of important aspects of the development of the arts and culture in Hong Kong that ultimately fosters a sense of cultural identity. This will have a far reaching impact on the recent development of local arts and culture, especially in the midst of the Government’s dedicated effort in the establishment of the West Kowloon Cultural District.

242410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
242410.value: This project proposes to study the “literary extension” of the Salem Witch Trials (1692-1693), namely literary creations that have used the trials, related figures and details as the main setting, in the plot development, in characterization, or in the discussion of themes such as faith, anxiety during crisis, gender relations, and other related issues of the human condition stemming from this historical event. Since John Neal’s novel Rachel Dyer (1820), a novel, play, or short story using the trials has been published in almost every decade, up to the present. While Neal’s historical novel depicts the hysteria and evasion of personal responsibility during the trials in order to expose the injustice and religious bigotry, the other literary works approach the event and the related personalities in genres such as the historical novel, the thriller, science fiction, novels of suspense, and even a cluster of young adult fictions. This continuous creative engagement with the trials shows not only a peculiar fascination with them, but also a keen desire to revisit and rethink some of the enduring human concerns as we move into modern times. The incidents that happened in Salem Village during the years 1692-1693 have been the centre of considerable academic interest, owing not only to the number of people involved, but also to the transgressive nature of the teenage girls’ behaviour which initiated the accusations, and their consequences. The most vulnerable people in that society unexpectedly toppled the local power system and unleashed an outburst of violence for which the authority was wholly unprepared. Although order was finally restored by the colonial government, the event exposed the threat posed by subordinates. In this sense, the Salem Witch Trials – it was to be the last large-scale witch-hunt of its kind - started a process of reflection to which posterity has responded through new literary creations depicting the witch trials, albeit with a view to quite different human dramas. This project will examine and analyze selected fictional narratives of the Salem witch trials, from Rachel Dyer (1820) to The Lost Book of Salem (2008), to study how this historical event becomes a recurrent component in almost two centuries of creative engagement. These narratives are unique cultural documents of our society’s self-reflection on gender relations, identity politics, religious and secular ideology, and feminism and witchery, as postmodernism, postcolonialism, and globalization exert their forces on different aspects of individual identity. 本研究計劃建議研讀1692-1693年塞林（Salem）女巫審判的「文學延伸」，亦即曾使用這件歷史事情的審判過程、有關人物及細節、事件發展、人物性格作為主要骨幹的文學作品，以討論人類的信仰、面對危機的焦慮、性別關係和其他有關議題的序述作為主要研究對象。 自從19世紀初首本有關塞林女巫審判的小說面世後，以這件歷史事實為背景的各類文學作品不絕。有些作品標榜事件中人類的恐懼與逃避責任的心態，有些作品欲以此事件反映不同時代政府內的混亂及造成的不正義狀況。而作品類型方面，包括歷史小說、驚慄、科幻、懸疑，甚至一系列的青少年讀物。這些不絕的文學作品不單顯示多年來作者對這件史實的迷醉，更標誌著進入現代文明之餘，我們對事件所反映的人性本質興趣不減。 1692-1693年間在塞林村中發生的事情一直以來被學術界重點研究，除了因為涉及的人數不少之外，更因為事情的起因──一群少女的指控──重重的顛覆了當時社會的權力制度，引發了一場活於低層人民借故釋放內心對體制、權威不滿的重大事件。雖然最終事情被平息，政府重建了秩序，事件的發生已揭露了這種權力架構下的弱點和其可顛覆性。這個角度看，女巫審判事件（進入現代社會之前最後一個如此大型的捕獵行動）開始了一個後世反思的過程。 這個研究計劃檢視由捕獵女巫事件引發的一連串小說文學作品，試圖瞭解三百年來後人如何反思、回應、重塑這個歷史事件。

242410.label: Realisation of objectives
242410.value: The Salem Witch event was well documented in history. Objective 1 have been well achieved by referring to the full trial documents which contain the court records of the individuals who had been tried then in the 17th century, as well as the many critical analysis of this historical event from various disciplinary perspectives. The records of the trials provide detailed information about the way the individuals faced the accusations and attempted to defend themselves in the face of this mysterious uprise. The later critical analysis which were done by scholars from different disciplines tried to read/interpret this historical event outside of the realm of witchcraft or magic, and see this event as a political, social, economic and cultural manifestation of a particular type of life. The contemporary and later analysis have shown very interesting differences in their focuses, obviously due to the shift in beliefs and the distance from the event. A field trip to the Salem Town had been organized and conducted in the summer of 2012. Objective 2 has been very substantially achieved in the planning, execution and the processing of the data obtained afterwards. With a secular shift in beliefs, Salem the “witch town” then has become a sought after tourist spot after 300 years. The field trip revealed that Salem today is transforming the disreputable past into a marketable identity, by turning witchcraft into modern consumerism, so much so that some local residents protest against this overwhelming image and demand a more visible representation of the local industry. The field trip offered firsthand information about how the history is turned into a consumerist narrative, and how the town is turned into a haven for tolerance of differences in cultural identities (racial, ethnic, sexual, religious differences). Objective 3, 4, and 5 have all been very substantially achieved by the searching, identifying and analysis of the rich collection of literary re-creations using the Salem trials as their subject matter. Different genres from different historical periods, as well as young adult fiction which has been so fashionable in the recent decades, have been read and analyzed. Objective 6 has been partially achieved. 8 paper presentations have been made in international conferences focusing on gender, education, cultural studies, and humanities; and 5 academic papers have been published in refereed journals. The book-length study needs more time for preparation.

242410.label: Major findings and research outcome
242410.value: The project has allowed a thorough understanding of the historical event at the time, and an overview of the modern interpretations of this event. The findings can be divided into 3 inter-related aspects: the literary trend and possibilities, the pedagogical potentials, and the creative potentials. The study of the rich collection of literary re-creations using Salem shows that different historical periods have different literary trends. The 18th and 19th century focused on the presentation of the historical event from different perspectives (the victims, the prosecutors, an objective historical view, etc.), the 20th and the 21st century shift to a personal and highly reflective mode. Publication 5 shows the recent trend is more an attempt to build a kind of continuation of identity from the tradition to the now. This is in line with the current popularity of autobiographical narratives. The Salem experience becomes an opportunity to establish a root of this 21st century “self” in the past. This trend is also found in other productions of popular culture. Publication 3 also suggests that the historical event can easily fuse with the futuristic mode of recent cultural products for new representations of our society’s fears and anxiety about humanness. The second important finding is the pedagogical use of such materials. Young adult fiction is a particularly suitable field for the adaptation of the Salem event, because of the teenagers involved. Together with the sweeping success of Harry Potter, magic and the supernatural become a major element in young adult fiction today, and many new fictions make use of Salem. In view of this proliferation, I have also explored their pedagogical potentials. The result has been publications 1, 2, 4, and numerous conference paper presentations. I have proposed that the drama of the Salem event allows its adaptation for the teaching of creative writing, moral education, critical thinking, and cultural studies, if suitable pedagogical practices were used together with the introduction of the historical event. The third finding is more creative. From the observation of the literary possibilities, it is clear that the drama of Salem can still be used for further creative potentials, given the changing cultural and political environment in the 21st century. In my conference presentations, various possibilities for using the Salem material and its legacy have been explored. The papers have been well received and they have explored themes related to gender representation, ethnic representation, and cultural changes.

242410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
242410.value: As suggested in one of my publications (Paper no. 3), although the Salem event is more than 300 years old, it has good potentials of being revived and used for different purposes because the Salem drama is essentially human drama. It is very likely that the story can revive itself in different forms of narratives which shift with the trend of popular culture. I suggested that the Harry Potter series put magic on the table as the focus of young adult fiction. In the recent years we also see the revival of the Vampire figure, and we already see new literary publications put the vampire side by side with the witches. Therefore it is very clear that the "supernatural" will continued to be employed to refer to the down to earth and realistic human world, but as a symbol to represent our fears and anxieties. The virtual world we live in now poses many problems and risks for humanness, and it is possible that the witch trial story will be adapted into new forms to express the hidden human sentiments in our century.

242410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
242410.value: The research project is a careful study of the historical Salem Witch trials not only in its reality in the form of court records and contemporary narratives, but also later day literary re-creations using the event. This is to understand the details of the event, the responsibility of various parties, and how this event can have an impact on our society which is 300 years in the future. The significance of the project lies not only in clarifying an important event that happened in the past, but also what we can learn from this event. What we learn from reviewing this event, and especially the contemporary literary re-creations, is not the cliche notion of "not repeating history", but the depth of human fear and anxiety about identity. The Salem drama in many ways is a drama of alienated people trying to get their share back, and making use of other people's weaknesses. This is human nature, and it will still be present even if our society is a society of virtual reality. This concern about our fear and anxiety is consistently present in the literary re-creations, and we can expect the same concern to continue its presence in future cultural productions.

242710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
242710.value: This study aims to examine the effect of the hedging cost on market making activities in derivative markets and the illiquidity of derivative securities. The study makes use of the data of derivative warrants traded on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (HKEx), and examines the effect of the reduction of the tick size or the minimum bid-ask spread implemented by the HKEx. As the tick size reduction is applied only to underlying securities with few exceptions, the event is exogenous to the derivative warrants market and provides an ideal setting to examine the effect of the hedging cost on the illiquidity of derivative securities. The hedging cost arises when market makers in derivative markets hedge their positions in derivative securities by trading underlying securities frequently. Thus, the hedging cost may account for a significant portion of the cost to the market makers. By conducting the study, we can better understand the sources of illiquidity of derivative securities and issues related to the microstructure of derivative markets. The study reveals whether the implementation of the tick size reduction reduces the hedging cost to the market makers of derivative warrants, improves the liquidity of derivative warrants, reduces the trading cost to the investors of derivative warrants, and fertilizes the growth of the derivative warrants market. 此課題研究對沖成本對衍生市場的做市行為及衍生証券的流動性的影響。此研究運用香港認股証的數據來檢驗香港証交所實施的減小股價最小變動幅度所帶來的影響。由於此變化隻適用於標的資產，對認股証市場是外生的，因此提供了一個對對沖成本對衍生証券的流動性的影響的很好的研究機會。對沖成本由於衍生市場的做市商應用標的資產進行對沖而產生，是做市商成本的一大組成部分。通過此研究，我們可以更好的理解衍生証券的流動性的來源及衍生市場微觀結構的有關問題。此研究可以說明減小股價最小變動幅度是否降低了認股証做市商的對沖成本，提高了認股証的流動性，降低了認股証投資者的交易成本，並有助於認股証市場的成長。

242710.label: Realisation of objectives
242710.value: To realize the first objective, we compare bid-ask spreads, trading volumes and other liquidity variables of underlying stocks 5-day before and after the implementation of the tick size reduction. The results suggest that the implementation of the tick size reduction improves the liquidity of underlying stocks significantly. In particular, bid-ask spreads are reduced by more than 3/4 on average. The effect is also sustained for at least one year. To realize the second objective, we compare the level and time-series variation of the derivative warrants inventory held by market makers and their level of participation in the liquidity provision 5-day before and after the tick size reduction. The results show that the level of participation in liquidity provision, measured by the ratio between the trading volume by market makers and total trading volume, increases only marginally. There is no significant change in the inventory held by market makers, or the time-series variation of the inventory held by market makers and of their participation in liquidity provision. The results indicate that the tick size reduction does not strongly encourage market makers to provide better liquidity to the derivative warrants market. For the third objective, we find that quoted and effective bid-ask spreads of derivative warrants between the 5-day periods before and after the tick size reduction are also reduced but to a lesser extent when compared with those of underlying stocks. Trading volumes of these derivative warrants are reduced, however. Derivative warrants typically have a time-to-maturity of 6-month when issued, and the characteristics of derivative warrants change quickly in a relative short period of time. As a result, it is difficult to find two comparable derivative warrants at different points in time and conduct a clean test of the long term effects on the liquidity of derivative warrants. The results that the tick size reduction has rather limited impacts on the behavior of market makers and the liquidity of derivative warrants are somewhat surprising given that it improves the liquidity of underlying stocks substantially. To understand the puzzling results, we go beyond the original objectives of the projects and examine the effects of the tick size reduction on the liquidity of stock options. Much stronger results are obtained from the sample of stock options.

242710.label: Major findings and research outcome
242710.value: This project empirically examines the effects of the reduction in tick sizes of underlying stocks on the liquidity of underlying stocks, options and derivative warrants in Hong Kong. The exogenous change in tick sizes significantly reduces the bid-ask spreads of underlying stocks. Derivative warrants / options written on the underlying stocks with a greater bid-ask spreads reduction also experience a greater bid-ask spreads reduction. The effects of the liquidity spill-over from underlying stocks to derivatives depend on the relative costs of hedging in the underlying market and derivative market. For derivative warrants, which are liquid, and whose market makers can manage their inventory by trading in the warrants market at a low cost, the bid-ask spreads are little changed on average. For options, which are less liquid and more costly to hedge in the options market, the bid-ask spreads are reduced significantly. Among individual derivative warrants and options, the liquidity spill-over from underlying stocks to derivative warrants / options is weaker if the trading volumes of derivative warrants / options are higher, and outstanding amounts of derivative warrants or open interests of options are more stable. For derivative warrants, when the number of warrants issued by the same issuer on the same underlying stock is higher, the spill-over effect is also weaker. The results also show that trading volumes of derivative warrants decrease and those of options increase after the tick-size reduction, suggesting that derivative warrants and options in Hong Kong are substitutions of each other. Overall, the results shed light on the sources of liquidity of derivative securities. The detailed results and the empirical implementations are discussed in a working paper entitled “Does the liquidity of underlying stocks affect the liquidity of derivatives? An empirical study”.

242710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
242710.value: Much of the research on the Hong Kong derivative warrants and options markets has focused on the complementary role of these two markets. It is generally regarded that the derivative warrants market mainly serves short-term and individual investors because of the better liquidity, whereas the options market mainly serves long-term and institutional investors. The results derived from the project that the tick size reduction of underlying stocks leads to a decrease in the trading volume of derivative warrants and an increase in the trading volume of options, clearly suggest the competition of these two markets, which is ignored in the literature. The extension of the research in such a direction is interesting and timely as the Hong Kong Stock Exchange recently have started to revamp the stock options market by requesting market makers to better provide liquidity, and a few issuers have quit the derivative warrants market in the past a few years because of the competition from other warrant issuers and the options market. The substitution aspect of these two markets deserves further investigation, and I will pursue the research in such a direction.

242710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
242710.value: This project examines the determinants of the liquidity of derivative securities. The results suggest that the liquidity of derivative securities depends on the liquidity of underlying stocks. When the bid-ask spreads of underlying stocks are low, the bid-ask spreads of derivative securities tend to be low as well. This is so because market makers of derivative securities can hedge their derivative positions with underlying stocks at a low cost, and require a low compensation by quoting a narrow bid-ask spreads. The effect is the strongest when derivative securities are illiquid, and costs of alternative hedging strategies, such as hedging with other derivatives, are high. The results of the project also have important policy implications. The results suggest that, to promote the derivatives market in Hong Kong, in additional to providing better incentive to market makers and imposing more strict requirements on the liquidity provision, improving the liquidity of the underlying stocks market also helps.

242810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
242810.value: We develop a theoretical model on the relationship between symbiotic ownership in joint venture (JV) firms and their performance (See Fig.1 attached). The concept of symbiotic ownership is based on the research by Jeffrey Pfeffer on symbiotic interdependence, which is defined as a mutual dependence between unlike firms from different industries in a value chain. According to this definition, when firms from different industries build ownership joint ventures (JV), we name it symbiotic ownership or symbiosis. In other words, the symbiosis here refers to ownership symbiosis between/among firms from different industries in a value chain. Since Pfeffer, little research has been conducted on the relationship between the symbiosis and firm performance, and relevant theory needs to be developed for the management of such JVs. For instance, as HK firms establish JVs in China, several relevant questions need to be addressed. First, given the choice, should a HK firm builds a JV with firms from the same industry only or with those from other industries? Also, should the HK firm establish a JV with only one mainland firm or with many? Finally, if the HK firm has to establish a JV with mainland firms from other industries, what managerial intervention or strategy may the HK firm adopt to improve the performance of its JV? To improve our understanding of these issues and provide practical guidelines for better development and management of JVs, we develop a model based on research of symbiotic interdependence. While the research by Pfeffer suggests that the symbiotic relation in JV can help firm performance through reducing uncertainties in external environments so that firm performance can be improved, we argue, based on past research, that a positive relationship between the symbiosis in JV and performance can be moderated by several factors, including specialist strategy, trust, coordination with parent firms and participation of all board members in JVs. A theoretical model is proposed covering the relationships among all these factors, and a plan is proposed to test the model. Specifically, we plan to first collect panel data from over 70,000 equity JVs surveyed by the Chinese government in 2002, based on which we conduct questionnaire surveys and interviews to collect additional data. 对企业的共生所有权与业绩的关系，我们提出了一个理论模型， 基于JEFFREY, PFEFFER关于共生依赖的理论， 我们将企业的共生所有权定义为不同行业的企业在合资企业中的共生所有权。 多年来对这种所有权的研究一直不够充分。 许多问题需要通过研究来加以回答。 例如， 如果可以选择, 企业应否从多个行业挑选合资伙伴？ 有哪些情景因素影响这个决定？ 最后，如果一家企业必须在别的行业寻找合资伙伴， 管理层可以采用什么方法来提高合资企业的业绩？ 为了回答上述问题， 我们在共生关系的基础上提出一个理论模型。 我们认为共生所用权会影响企业业绩。 但是， 这种影响会受到一系列情景因素的影响， 例如， 合资伙伴的相互信任等。 我们计划在为数多达7万家的中国合资企业中抽样调查， 用数据证明提出的假设。

242810.label: Major findings and research outcome
242810.value: Based on symbiotic, resources dependency and institutional theories, we test the effect of symbiotic alliances on firm performances. In several studies related to the issue, we also consider the effects of several other variables, such as market orientation, human resource, and social capital. Our results show that strategic symbiotic alliances in China can improve firm performances in terms of growth, financial returns, marketing and other dimensions. In addition, other factors can also have significant effects. For instance, firms’ market orientation has a positive effect on social capital, which, in turn, has a positive effect of the stability of the large-small symbiotic alliances. Moreover, social capital also has a positive effect on the sharing of resources among the partners, which should also influence the stability of the alliance.

242810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
242810.value: For researchers, the symbiotic perspective proposed in this study draws attention to the need to deal with such issues as international joint venture and entrepreneurship using a more dynamic and timely approach with more consideration of three symbiotic processes. For instance, for the development of entrepreneurship, we should further study empirically the important propoersitions (see Li, Young and Tang, 2011). One of which is that entrepreneurial innovation is not only a micro case of long evolution but also a symbiotic process at the macro level by which new types of entrepreneurship are generated or changed, often in a short time period and in a systematic way. This means reconsidering the way that entrepreneurship has traditionally been viewed, and more empirical evidence should be collected. Proposition to be tested in future studies: 1 Entrepreneurship of Chinese ethnic communities is malleable in a symbiotic process, within which it merges and re-merges with cultural elements from foreign societies or other sources. 2 The more the cultural element of the value of family or kinship is present in a given entrepreneurial culture, the more likely is the development or persistence of commensalistic entrepreneurs. 3 The more elements of innovation and creativity there are in a given entrepreneurial culture, the more likely is the development of mutualistic entrepreneurship. 4 The fewer cultural elements of uncertainty avoidance and respect for the law there are, the more likely it is that parasitic entrepreneurs will develop. 5 Through symbiosis, new forms of entrepreneurship can emerge and succeed in a short period without a long period of evolution. 6 Entrepreneurial culture in a given society influences or shapes entrepreneurial activities, but entrepreneurial activities can also create or change an entrepreneurial culture through interaction with other elements in a Gaia system. 242810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
242810.value: In the development of joint ventures or entrepreneur firms, the perspective of symbiosis is a new and interesting perspective. Take the development of joint ventures as an example. Joint venture can be developed through building horizontal alliances as well as vertical alliances. Our research shows that, in an emerging market such as China, horizontal alliances should be more efficient than vertical alliances. Both the symbiotic perspective in our current study as well as the empirical evidence reported support this conclusion. Accordingly, when investing in developing countries, firms from developed societies may need to find partners from the same industry first before doing so for those from other industries. This selection decision should result in more similarities among the partners and better efficiency in performance.

243110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
243110.value: 本研究將評估《骷髏之舞》對伊利沙伯年代 (1588-1603) 戲劇的影響。《骷髏之舞》（又稱《死之舞》）以藝術形式將「死亡」描畫為一具動態骷髏或屍體，它遍遊生者世界，攫走那些生命走到盡頭的人。這種藝術形式甚或其名稱的起源皆無從考究；有學者曾將《骷髏之舞》與中世紀末的戲劇表演拉上關係 (Clark 91-94; Neill 64-65; Oosterwijk 249-287;Gertsman 1-40)。死之舞的宗教意味濃厚，舞者的形象曾出現於16世紀的歐洲各國，或繪在教堂詩班的木板上，或雕畫在大教堂內的支架上，或蝕刻在男修道院的大理石柱上¬¬ ── 目的皆為警醒人們生命之短暫。 死之舞於16世紀及17世紀初的文學曾多次出現。基德 (Thomas Kyd)，黎里 (John Lyly)，格林 (Robert Greene)，莎士比亞 (William Shakespeare)，馬盧 (Christopher Marlowe)，皮爾 (George Peele)，諾頓 (Thomas Norton)，沙克維爾 (Thomas Sackville) 等名劇作家都曾以此形象入戲。他們大多都走一貫宗教道德教化的路子，但亦有開拓新的範疇。以馬盧的《巴黎大屠殺》為例，劇中一眾匪黨連環攫走並殺害胡格諾教派民眾，受害者向兇手乞求時間或憐憫，最終難逃一劫；這情節不免讓人猜想這是否《骷髏之舞》的伊利沙伯戲劇化版本。而在莎劇中，死之舞亦頻頻出現，最明顯例子就在《理查二世》中（「怎麼一回事？『死亡』張牙舞爪地直撲過來！」（第五章，第五幕）），死亡被形象化為人的「典型」（殺人犯），定性為可被擊倒的敵人。在諾頓與沙克維爾撰寫的劇本《高布達克》(Gorboduc)中，死亡則在英國失樂園的舞台上飾演一角。 本研究焦點為伊利沙伯年代的某一特定戲劇類型。此類戲劇並不希望觀眾或評論家將其中《骷髏之舞》的參照當作靜態、學術的表徵，將將其視作具可塑性的動態「符號」，容許人自由詮釋與再詮釋。沃洛希洛夫 (V.N.Volosinov) 稱此種特質為「多音性」(multiaccentuality)，提出每個群體或階級在觀察特定符號時或會賦予該符號不同的重點或「聲音」。本人的研究方向可稱為文化符號學途徑，容許有限度記錄直接的圖像參照，但會嘗試解構並詮釋更多具彈性、動態的《骷髏之舞》符號規律。本研究會集中探討並解釋古代英語劇作家如何利用《骷髏之舞》，使其作品與伊利沙伯年代英國的藝術、文化、社會政治生活建立連繫。 本研究的主要目標為完成長度及質素皆可出版成書的專著。為完成目標，以出版圖詩文學為主的紐約的AMS Press出版社已同意考慮出版本人將會完成的稿件 (已附上出版社高級編輯Dr. David Ramm的信件)；該出版社現正進行本人有關馬盧一本專著的出版工作，該書在本人上一個研究用途補助金(CERG)資助下完成。在過去30年，AMS Press為各國最優秀的中世紀／文藝復興學者提供論壇（其中包括：Clifford Davidson, Peter M. Daly, Michael Bath, Clifford Leech及Thornton Burnett；其中Thornton Burnett為權威的馬盧Everyman系列版本的編輯）。該出版社必定能為此類學術作品提供具影響力的出版途徑。

243110.label: Major findings and research outcome
243110.value: The study has provided further evidence to support the still-contentious view that the danse macabre emerged primarily from earlier dramatic traditions, and that this "ancestry," so to speak, lent itself readily to the semiotic predilections of emerging dramatists in the Elizabethan Renaissance. The essential "performativity" of danse macabre tableaux, reflected initially in the grand murals of medieval secular and religious spaces, and latterly in Renaissance emblem book, made the static, artistic form accessible to a dramatic imagination and its usage in theatre is, in that respect, understandable. However, my study goes further in showing that Elizabethan playwrights theatricalised the form to a surprising degree. For example, in some cases the drama actually mimics the dance of death processional on stage or drawing the artistic form into mythological paradigms of myth and/or anti-myth. What is particularly intriguing is that my research gives credence to the view that the danse macabre underwent a double metamorphosis: transmigrating in the first instance from a dramatic format into a statistic artistic mode; and then emerging from the artistic form back into a dramatic context. The research outcomes have proved very satisfactory and, despite my departure for a senior academic position in Australia, the ambitions of the research have been achieved. I believe the draft manuscript I have produced evidences quality research and opens up new vistas of research into the danse macabre--and I feel confident it will emerge, in due course, as a published and creditably contribution to he field.

243110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
243110.value: There is an obvious lead-in to the Jacobean period (1603 onwards) which fell outside the parameters of the current study. The danse macabre appears in the work of a number of dramatists of this age, and my research (which inevitably has lapped across period boundaries) has already brought to light some interesting areas of further investigation within the work of writers like Marston, Webster and others. The dark intensity of the Jacobean age melds comfortably with the more didactic, menacing intensions of the danse macabre as an art form. This makes it an intriguing area for further study, though it does not suggest that my current study has been too limited in its intentions. The Elizabethan age uses the danse macabre in seminally different ways to the Jacobean period, and on these grounds the disjunction of the two is both reasonable and desirable.

243110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
243110.value: The traditional view of the danse macabre (an art form in which skeletons lead off earthly "types" to the grave, jigging as they do so) is that the gruesome, gaudy disposition of medieval artistry fell into abeyance as the Renaissance age due to changing and more sophisticated tastes. My research argues that the danse macabre, in a sense, "re-invented" itself finding new and sophisticated uses and meanings in the drama of the Elizabethan age. An investigation of these uses and meanings, achieved through the manuscript I have produced and through ancillary articles, provides us with a better understanding of Elizabethan drama and culture.

243610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
243610.value: This research project is an in depth analysis and interpretation of one of the most influential books in the history of the philosophy of religion: Immanuel Kant’s "Die Religion innerhalb der Grenzen der bloßen Vernunft" (1792/1793), most recently translated by Werner Pluhar as "Religion within the Bounds of Bare Reason" (Hackett, 2009). The PI worked closely with Pluhar in 2007-2008, advising him on numerous points of translation and wrote the scholarly introduction to the translation. The current project will examine Kant’s text in a far more detailed manner than was possible in that introductory essay. This will involve three levels of research: (1) the proposal of a creative (yet hermeneutically well-informed) thesis or series of theses indicating how modern-day readers ought to interpret this book and understand its implications for actual, empirical religions; (2) a comparison of the original (German) text with the three complete English translations, in order to highlight key differences and similarities between them and to arrive at an optimal translation of controversial passages; and (3) an examination of how this text has been treated (both in general and with reference to specific passages) by past interpreters, in order to discern interpretive trends and plausible options on controversial issues. The first level will be an extension and elaboration of positions initially argued in the books "Kant's System of Perspectives" (1993) and "Kant's Critical Religion" (2000). The second level has already been done in a cursory manner when the PI worked with Pluhar on his translation, but requires a more in depth study in order to reach the standards of a commentary. The PI is already familiar with much of the literature relevant to the third level, but has not yet systematically related it to the Religion text. When this project is complete, the commentary will be published either as a lengthy one-volume work (tentatively entitled "Baring All in Reason’s Light") or as a two-volume series. Kant's Religion has four main parts, so in the latter case the first two parts (on the problem of human evil and how religion seeks to overcome it) would constitute the first volume while the last two parts (on the need to form religious communities and the proper method of ensuring that the service performed by members of such communities is genuinely good) would constitute the second volume. The overall goal will be to demonstrate how Kant set out to reform Christianity. 此研究項目志在深入分析和詮釋其中一本在宗教哲學史上最有影響力的著作：康德的Die Religion innerhalb der Grenzen der bloßen Vernunft (1792/1793)。最近由Werner Pluhar譯為Religion within the Bounds of Bare Reason (Hackett, 2009)。PI與Pluhar在2007-2008緊密合作，為他提供多項翻譯上之建議，並為譯本撰寫序言。現在此項目將可以作比序言更詳細地研究康德的文本。研究會分為三個層次：(1) 提出有創意 (但詮釋上成立) 的主題指出現代讀者應如何解讀此書並明白其對真實、經驗上的宗教的含意；(2) 將德文原文與三個完整英文譯本比較，從而突出主要相同與不同，對受爭議的段落作最理想的翻譯；和 (3) 調查歷來詮釋者如何看待此文本 (一般和參考特定的段落) ，從而分辨詮釋趨勢和對受爭議的段落作可行的選擇。第一層次會是伸延和詳細闡述書本Kant's System of Perspectives (1993)和 Kant's Critical Religion (2000) 的立場。第二層次在PI和Pluhar作翻譯工作已粗略完成，但需要更深入的研習來達到撰寫評論的水平。PI已對第三者層次相關的文獻，但未系統地與“Religion”關連起來。當項目完成時，評論將會以一冊 (暫名“Baring All in Reason’s Light”) 或連續兩冊出版。“Religion”主要含四部分，所以若是後者的話，首兩部分(人類罪惡問題和宗教如何尋求克服它)會構成第一冊，而後兩部分(形成宗教社區的需要和正確方法去保證社區的人的服務是真誠地好) 會構成第二冊。整體目標是要展示康德如何著手改革基督教。

243610.label: Major findings and research outcome
243610.value: The significant findings arising as a direct result of this research are too numerous to list here. Most are quite technical, as this Commentary is intended primarily as a work for Kant scholars, theologians, and philosophers of religion. However, here is a simplified list of major innovations, discoveries and arguments developed in the book and/or the background journal articles: - Kant's key technical term, "Gesinnung", refers neither to a transcendent, metaphysical "disposition" nor to a psychological "feeling", as others have assumed, but to the volitional act of selecting a "conviction" that grounds all of one's life-decisions. - The PI discovered and co-translated a previously unknown book review that Kant referred to briefly (but misleadingly) in the second Preface of Religion, and demonstrated its influence on the changes Kant made in the book's second edition. - New historical evidence uncovered by the PI reveals that the section of his book entitled "General Comment" to the First Piece should not, in its entirety, be identified as the "first parergon" (i.e., "effects of grace"). Rather, Kant put the text of all four parerga into small type, which previous editions of the book have simply ignored. Attention to Kant's careful typography provides crucial confirmation that grace is a constituent element in Kant's religious system, not just an optional extra. - The PI has demonstrated, contrary to common assumptions, that Kant's religious system permits (but does not require) belief in the divinity of Jesus. - Historical faith (i.e., faith in some historical religious tradition) is not derided by Kant as a useless or necessarily harmful delusion, as often assumed. Rather, new evidence demonstrates that he portrayed such historical traditions as prudent means of conveying rational truths that remain valid, even if considered apart from that tradition. - The technical term, "Gottesdienst", which all past translators have translated as a synonym of "Dienst Gottes" ("service of God"), is actually the standard German term for "liturgy". This discovery has huge implications for Kant's discussion of the difference between true and false religious practices, in the Fourth Piece of his Religion. As such, Kant is not universally dismissing ALL organized religion, but is rather offering specific criticisms of the approach to religion that sees liturgy as an end in itself. - The four "principles of the true church", defended in Religion's third Piece, can also be found operating in Laozi's Daoist philosophy, though Daoism implements the principles differently to the way Christian churches typically do.

243610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
243610.value: The various articles that have been published as part of this funded research are not merely early versions of what later became chapters in the book. Rather, the book consists entirely of new material: the arguments advanced in the articles are often referred to in the book, for readers who want to consult more detailed defenses of certain key arguments. Similarly, during the course of writing the book, the PI had ideas concerning how he might write future articles to give more detailed defenses of various other positions as well. Just to cite one of many possible examples: Kant proposed a specific theory of deathbed conversion, one that has specific implications for how pastors and other religious professionals and/or social workers should proceed when dealing with persons who are near death. In the book, the PI could only devote a few pages to this argument, but it is significantly profound so that a very interesting journal article could easily be written--one that would be sure to have an influence that would extend far beyond the realm of Kant scholarship and the philosophy of religion.

243610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
243610.value: Immanuel Kant's Religion within the Bounds of Bare Reason (1793/1794) is arguably the most influential publication in the history of the philosophy of religion, excluding the scriptures of various world religions. Yet, aside from one dense, historically-oriented book written in German in 1938, no commentary had been written on Kant's Religion when the PI began work on this project, in 2006. Since then, three short commentaries have been published, focusing on Kant's Religion. However, each offers mostly a general overview, without taking seriously that Kant's religious theory is meant to be a guide for real religious organizations. By contrast, this new Commentary is encyclopedic in its coverage of Kant's text, demonstrating without a doubt (and for the first time) that Kant's aim in this book was not merely to supplement his ethics, but that he was developing practical guidelines for how to be authentically religious. And clear thinking on this matter is even more relevant to the twenty-first century than it was in Kant's own day. Thanks to the UGC's generous GRF funding, well-educated religious leaders will soon have access to a guidebook highlighting how Kantian religion provides a non-sectarian Way that all good-hearted human beings can accept.

244210.label: Project Objectives
244210.value: to evaluate the development of union organisation in foreign-invested enterprises (FIEs) in the Pearl River Delta region of mainland China, with particular reference to the extent to which such unions are able to effectively embrace the “representative” function; to investigate employees’ attitudes towards their employer, industrial relations and their union, and in particular to evaluate the factors associated with members’ commitment to and participation in their union in FIEs in the Pearl River Delta region of mainland China; to evaluate the role of individual characteristics as antecedents and moderators in union commitment and participation models. Factors to be examined will include age, tenure, occupation, gender, and individual differences; to evaluate the role of workplace characteristics as antecedents and moderators in union commitment and participation models. Particular attention will be given to industrial relations climate and the implementation of high performance HR practices. This analysis will adopt a multi-level approach to theory and estimation, which has yet to be applied in the union commitment and participation literature; to provide not only a contribution to the academic literature in industrial relations, but also specific policy-related insights for policy-makers, managers and union leaders.

244210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
244210.value: In light of the escalating level of industrial disputes in China and amid concerns about the need to maintain social stability and inward investment, public policy sees a role for unions as a communications channel and as a means of resolving labour disputes. Relatively little is known about the extent to which Chinese unions are able to effectively represent their members’ interests, about employees’ attitudes and behaviour towards their unions, and about the factors shaping such attitudes and behaviour. This project therefore deals with issues of considerable interest to government, employers, foreign investors, and unions themselves. The project will evaluate the development of enterprise-level unions in foreign-invested enterprises in the Pearl River Delta region of mainland China, and the factors associated with members’ commitment to and participation in their union. It will assess the role of individual and workplace characteristics as antecedents and moderators in union commitment and participation models. Factors to be examined at the individual level include age, tenure, occupation, gender, personality and exchange ideology. At the workplace level, attention will be given to industrial relations climate and the implementation of high performance HR practices. Several contributions will be made. First, the project will provide a better understanding of the relationship between members and their unions in foreign-invested enterprises in China. Chinese unions have historically had a dual role, as employee representatives and also as representatives of the broader national interest, by promoting labour productivity and resolving disputes. Market reform and economic restructuring has led to tensions between the two roles, as labour disputes have increased. The study will provide a timely evaluation of the implementation of the representative role in contemporary China. Second, responding to calls from Bamberger, Kluger, and Suchard (1999) and Fullagar, Gallagher, Clark, and Carroll (2004) for research on moderating variables in union commitment and participation models, this is the first project to systematically examine moderators. This is important because it will provide a more developed understanding of the factors influencing, facilitating and constraining union commitment and participation. Third, the project will examine workplace context as well as individual moderators, including industrial relations climate and the implementation of high performance human resource management practices in the workplace. The study will provide the first rigorous assessment of the way in which workplace context influences individual union commitment and participation, enabling us to make a much-needed contribution to cross-level theory in industrial relations. 中國珠江三角洲外資企業的員工對職工會的忠誠態度和參與行為 鑒於中國大陸愈來愈熾烈的勞資紏紛及高度關注社會穩定和內部投資，公共政策認為工會應擔當溝通和解決勞資糾紛的角色，惟對於有關中國工會是否有效地代表其會員之利益、僱員對工會的態度和行為及有何因素塑造他們這些態度和行為等，所知較少，因此本研究所探討的各項題目是對政府、僱主、海外投資者及工會本身皆有益和有建設性。 本項目將研究工會在珠三角外資企業內之發展情況、會員對工會之忠誠態度和參與程度，亦評核員工個人背景和工作場所特色作為前因變量和調節變量去影響會員對工會之忠誠和參與，將會觀察員工個人背景包括年紀、工作資歷、性別、性格和交換觀念，亦探討工作場所之特色包括勞資關係氣侯和實行高表現效能人力資源管理實務。 我們期望本項目有幾方面的貢獻，第一，可讓人更明白在外資企業內的工會與其會員的關係，中國工會歷來履行「雙重角色」－作為員工的代表和國家整體利益的代表 (即鼓吹勞動生產力和解決勞資糾紛)，但因近期勞資紏紛增加，市場改革和經濟架構重整使工會的雙重角色出現張力，此研究正好為近代中國實行的代表角色提供適切的評價﹔第二，本項目是第一個相關的研究去回應Bamberger、Kluger & Suchard (1999) 和Fullagar、Gallagher、Clerk & Carroll (2004) 所提出要求：有系統地研究影響會員對工會之忠誠和參與之模式的調節變量，其重要性在於更深入明白有哪些因素可影響、引導或限制會員對工會之忠誠和參與﹔第三，本項目將探討工作場所之環境特色和個別調節變量，包括勞資關係氣侯、實行高表現效能人力資源管理實務，這是第一個嚴謹的研究去評核工作場所因素如何影響會員對工會之忠誠和參與，為勞資關係範疇中正需要的跨層面理論作出一點貢獻。

244210.label: Realisation of objectives
244210.value: We have addressed all five objectives. Objective 1 relates mainly to the qualitative phase of the project, and is addressed in paper 2. We have examined the developing role of enterprise unions and in particular the opportunities for the union to perform the representative function. Our findings suggest that changes are taking place, but that progress is uneven, so that it is too early to talk in general about the emergence of independent and representative unions. Objective 2, on the antecedents of union commitment and participation, is addressed in the quantitative-based papers 1, 3 and 4, which provide support for the antecedents seen in the Western literature. More specifically, paper 3 addresses objectives 2 and 3, assessing individual-level antecedents and moderators of union commitment and participation. Paper 1 addresses objectives 2 and 4, focusing on workplace-level characteristics in union commitment and participation models, utilising a multi-level approach. The focus is on high-performance human resource practices (HPHRP), and the key finding is that such practices appear not to act as a union substitute, with some evidence of a complementarity between such practices and unions. Paper 4 also addresses objectives 2 and 4, assessing whether union commitment and participation models differ by type of enterprise. This was not mentioned explicitly in the objectives, but it allows us to begin to address the issue of generalisability by enterprise type. In addressing the above objectives, we provide practical insights for policy makers, managers and union leaders (objective 5). Our findings have implications for debates on the development of enterprise unions and collective bargaining, and the provision of channels for employee voice, all of which are key issues for public policy and management. We have addressed objectives 1, 2, 3 and 5 in full in the attached papers. For objective 4, in the papers we have focussed our analysis of enterprise level-factors on HPHRP (paper 1) and enterprise types (paper 4), neither paper dealing directly with IR climate. However, we do have some findings on this and we plan to return to the issue in a future paper. The PI assumed an Associate Vice President position as the project was commencing and continued in that role for the duration of the project, then moving to the UK. This has caused some delay in our publication schedule, but we have been able to meet the objectives of the project in terms of work completed.

244210.label: Major findings and research outcome
244210.value: The qualitative phase of the project focussed on objective 1, consisting of case studies of foreign-invested enterprises, based on interviews with management, enterprise union leaders and workers, and also on interviews with others, such as regional union officials and activists in pro-labour NGOs. Findings suggest that enterprise unions may play a significant role in resolving labour disputes, and in some cases the signing of a collective contract provides an opportunity for the union to influence pay and conditions. However, management policy is still critical in shaping the union’s role, and the “dual role” continues, with the welfare function significant and with the union acting as a communication “bridge” between management and workers. Furthermore, the union role in resolving labour disputes is usually as a reactive “middleman”, mediating in an “impartial” manner, rather than actively soliciting, framing, and presenting workers’ demands to management. Whilst it appears that changes are taking place in the role of enterprise unions, progress is uneven and in general it is too early to talk about independent and effective unions. The quantitative phase involved surveys of management, union leaders and workers in a sample of FIEs. Addressing objective 2, findings confirm the generalizability of the Western models of union commitment and participation to the Chinese FIE context, with organisational commitment, pro-union attitudes, and union instrumentality positively associated with union loyalty, which then at least partially mediates the relationships with willingness to work for the union (our measure of union participation). As in the Western literature, the direct effect of job satisfaction on union loyalty is in some analyses non-significant. Looking at individual-level characteristics (objective 3), neither gender nor age were significant moderators in the model, but there was evidence that a strong exchange ideology was associated with a weaker relationship between union loyalty and willingness to work for the union, implying that those members with a more calculating approach were less likely to reciprocate for instrumental benefits received from the union, instead adopting a free-rider mentality. As in some Western studies, we found that women were no more or less loyal to the union than men, but they had lower levels of willingness to work for the union. In examining the role of workplace characteristics (objective 4), there was no evidence that high-performance human resource practices acted as a union substitute, and we found some evidence of a complementarity between such practices and unions.

244210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
244210.value: There are three main areas for development. First, there is a need to evaluate further developments in the role of enterprise unions. There are debates about this and the potential for collective bargaining. This is a dynamic field and the findings of our paper 2 will need to developed in future. We are already addressing this with additional interviews, reflected in our outline of paper 5. Second, our findings relate primarily to foreign invested enterprises in the Pearl River Delta, so there is a need to assess their generalizability to other enterprise types and regions. We have started to address this by collecting additional data in two companies in Shanghai, one a foreign-invested enterprise and the other a state-owned enterprise (paper 4). Third, there is a need to further examine the impact of enterprise characteristics, management strategy, and the industrial relations context on the role of the union. For example, we touch on the importance of country-of-origin of FIEs in papers 1 and 2, and there is emerging work on this, but more needs to be done. Also, we plan further work on the IR context. We are considering a follow-up project to address some of these research needs.

244210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
244210.value: This project evaluates the development of trade unions in foreign-invested enterprises in China, focusing on the Pearl River Delta. Findings suggest that enterprise unions may play a significant role in resolving labour disputes, and in some cases the signing of a collective contract provides an opportunity for the union to influence pay and conditions. However, many enterprise unions continue to focus their attention mainly on providing welfare services. Management policy is critical in shaping the union’s role, and many employers value the union as a communication “bridge” between management and workers. Enterprise unions’ role in resolving labour disputes is usually as a middleman, expected to mediate “impartially”, rather than actively soliciting, framing, and presenting workers’ demands. Whilst it appears that changes are taking place in the role of enterprise unions, it is too early to talk about unions in general as effective representatives of their members’ interests. The project also identifies the key factors that explain individual workers’ commitment to, and participation in, enterprise unions. Several individual and enterprise characteristics are found to be significant, including attitudes towards the union and the enterprise. There is little evidence that employers are using sophisticated HRM practices as a substitute for unions.
