340010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
340010.value: This research project illuminates a field of contemporary art practice that has been marginalized in relation to the field of collaborative practice known variously as ‘relational’, ‘participatory’ or ‘dialogic’. It explores a range of case studies of contemporary collaborative drawing and painting that involves two or more artists contributing to the same work, successive artists responding to prior contributions. I argue that such processes—and the resulting works—instantiate visual dialogues that are creatively and pedagogically productive. The research method may be aligned with that increasingly recognized field of study that spans theoretical research, artistic practice and pedagogy. It incorporates (1) attention to particular collaborative creative processes and the resulting works; (2) discussion of the specific genres and traditions—for instance portraiture, miniature painting—that pertain to them (3) consideration of other contexts (artistic, historical, cultural, socio-political) pertinent to an understanding of the works in question; and (4) participant-observer accounts. The approach is essentially interdisciplinary and draws upon relevant work from the areas of sociology, psychology, anthropology and philosophy as well on scholarship in the areas art history and theory and aesthetics.

340110.label: Project Objectives
340110.value: To complete the first systematic analysis of Arendt's treatment of the social sciences, with special emphasis on sociology (synchronic dimension of the study). The first part of the study has already been researched and is in press. To complement this with an historical study of the intellectual sources of Arendt's critique. This will detail Arendt's brief involvement in Karl Mannheim's network in Heidlegerg and Frankfurt and, through Karl Jaspers, her introduction to Marianne Weber's Heidelberg salon. A writer's thought is typically formed both by attraction and by antipathy, by emulation (a model) and by collision (an anti-model). This research focuses on Arendt's collision with sociology, based on her view that the sociological attitude was an affront to the ideas of human freedom, personal responsibility, and republican judgment. To retrieve and record the objections of those Arendt attacked. We need to hear as many voices in this dispute as possible. Arendt was part of a dense network of young writers, some of whom were already well established as sociologists (Mannheim), others who became prominent as sociologists later (e.g. Hans Gerth, Norbert Elias). Their counter-positions to Arendt will be delineated. To do the above with the full range of extant sources - books, articles, archival materials, tape and video recordings, interviews - in the three most relevant languages: English, German and French. To examine the relevance of Arendt's early experiences of, and appraisal of, sociology for her later theory of totalitarianism. In formulating this theory, Arendt believed herself to be on terra incognita. She insisted that standard treatments of dictatorship, and the methodologies that underlay them, were redundnant for the Bolshevik and National Socialist cases. To appraise Arendt's contention 5. (above). To examine the parallels, or lack of them, between Arendt's attempt to forge a theory appropriate to the novelty of totalitarianism and post 9/11 attempts (e.g. by Philip Bobbitt) to map the distinctiveness of modern terror.

340110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
340110.value: Hannah Arendt (1906-1975) is among the leading political thinkers of our age. A refugee from Hitler’s Germany, she became the foremost writer on “totalitarian” regimes: National Socialism and Bolshevism. She was also a fierce critic of the social sciences, especially of sociology. Arendt believed that the sociologists of her day had fundamentally misconstrued the nature of modern predatory regimes. More starkly still, she argued that the social sciences invoked theories of causality and ideal-type models that disabled them from comprehending the nature of political life in general. The regimes of Hitler and Stalin, she claimed, were unprecedented. Yet social science commentators stressed their continuity with past regime-types (despotism, dictatorship, Bonapartism). In so doing, they failed to understand totalitarianism’s unique nature, dynamics, and modality of social evil. This research project deepens and concludes work that the PI has been pursuing for a decade: a systematic reconstruction, analysis and appraisal of Arendt’s indictment of social science interpretations of modern politics, especially of totalitarian regimes. The PI is a sociologist and, fittingly, it was sociology that Arendt principally attacked. Part one of this study, to be published by Stanford University Press in 2010, examines Arendt’s disagreements with her greatest post-war sociological rivals: Theodore Abel, Raymond Aron, Daniel Bell, Jules Monnerot, Talcott Parsons and David Riesman. The second and concluding part of this study - the research proposed here - will trace Arendt's rejection of sociology to its historical source: her assessment, principally, of Max Weber and Karl Mannheim. Arendt was introduced to Max Weber's work by her doctoral thesis advisor Karl Jaspers. She also attended the Heidelberg salon of Weber's wife, Marianne. Before Arendt fled Germany in 1933, she took two seminars with Karl Mannheim, founder of the sociology of knowledge. The research will reconstruct these experiences and their impact on Arendt’s later thought. It will entail archival research, biographical detective work, and historical reconstruction. If one arm of the research pursues a detailed historical understanding of Arendt, the other arm is substantive and evaluative; it employs Arendt as a foil to ask and answer a range of broader questions. Does philosophy, as soon as it touches on social questions, entail a covert sociology? What are unprecedented events and how are they recognized? What were Weber, Mannheim and other sociologists able to see about modern political fanaticism that Arendt's hostility to sociology occluded?

340110.label: Realisation of objectives
340110.value: The objectives have mostly - but not entirely - been realized; those that have been realized, have sometimes been so in a somewhat modified form. It is characteristic of the real flow and process of research that things one hoped to find fail to materialize, and other things that one is not expecting turn up surprisingly. This was very true of my GRF research. I was unable (see objective 3) to find anything pertinent on Hans Gerth and Norbert Elias. I also decided to keep the project historical and wished that I had never written down objective 7! It is not that I do not have ideas about the issues stated there; it is more that it now seems forced to mix them with a contextualist account of Arendt and her contemporaries. On the other hand, I found in the Arendt archives some remarkable material on a cognate area of the research: see the translation and commentary on the Arendt-Voegelin correspondence on totalitarianism in the section on Researched Outcome; I have documented a major critique of Arendt (objective 6) by Robert Nisbet from the standpoint of sociology (see Research Outcome chapter on Nisbet); I finished two major pieces on Arendt and the sociology of knowledge, related to objectives 2 and 5. And I made major strides in segueing this GRF research on Arendt with my next research project on "unmasking" (also relevant to objective 6). The first major output of that was the result of a close study of Arendt's rejection of "unmasking" as a proper approach of the human sciences. Again there is project output, focused not on Arendt hersef (that task is ongoing) but inspired by her (see Research Outcome; objective 6 again.) While the project is now largely completed, there are some loose ends which I will continue to tie up. In particular, I plan to re-route my distinction between "unmasking" and "disclosure" - a distinction I adapted from Arendt to apply to modern sociological theory - back to her own work (see objective 6 again). This will entail a systematic article, covering almost the whole span of her books in so far as they deal with this topic. In sum, the research proved productive and, at times, exciting. I am most grateful to the RGC for enabling me to do this work. My ambitions for it outstripped my abilities. But the output was far from negligible.

340110.label: Major findings and research outcome
340110.value: Major findings included: discovering correspondence between Arendt and Voegelin on totalitarianism; identifying a critique of Arendt's writings on totalitarianism by the American sociologist Robert A. Nisbet; recording the extent to which Arendt recapitulated a sociology of knowledge approach in her writings on Jewish intellectuals; developing her contrast between "unmasking" and "disclosure". The research outcomes are best seen in the published deliverables or those that are accepted for publication and forthcoming. Already published (pdfs with express acknowledgment to this grant found in Part C): A commentary (translation by Gordon Wells) on the Arendt-Voegelin exchange, published in HISTORY AND THEORY; an article on Mannheim and Arendt (and Jaspers and Heidegger), published in SOCIOLOGICA: ITALIAN JOURNAL OF SOCIOLOGY; a chapter in a new book on Robert Nisbet which contains a long section detailing his evaluation of Arendt's theory of totalitarianism and her likely response; the book is called A CONSERVATIVE IN ACADEME: CRITICAL ESSAYS ON THE SOCIAL AND POLITICAL THOUGHT OF ROBERT A. NISBET (edited by myself and Bryan S. Turner); an analysis of Arendt's adaptation of a sociology of knowledge approach; to be included in my edition of THE ANTHEM COMPANION TO HANNAH ARENDT; a discussion of the "unmasking" and "disclosure" approach, published in article for the JOURNAL OF SOCIOLOGY. The other main research outcome is that, early on, it led me to the work I will do next and for which I was awarded a Humanities and Social Sciences Prestigious Fellowship.

340110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
340110.value: A key finding of the research - the long debate about "unmasking" - has provided me with a large new set of sources for analysis. I have still to write up a systematic account of Arendt's own work on this topic. But meanwhile the research opened a much broader field to me that I will engage during my year Fellowship, beginning in January 2014. My objectives are: - to provide a systematic, historically informed, analysis of theories of unmasking and their political corollaries since the French Revolution - to clarify unmasking’s relationship to other modes of exposure: notably, satire, muckraking and debunking - to identify the range of unmasking modes (e.g. the exposure of secrecy, conspiracy, bad faith, hypocrisy, character, illusion, ideology, “false consciousness”) and their social targets - to examine the historical conditions of unmasking that make it interpretively plausible to modern people - to describe key modern theorists of unmasking from Rousseau to Bourdieu - to delineate the work of writers (including Max Weber, William James, Edmund Husserl, Hannah Arendt and Raymond Aron) who oppose the unmasking stance

340110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
340110.value: Arendt, a German-American political theorist, wrote innovative work on totalitarianism – the Bolshevik and Nazi regimes. The current research, extending my previous book on the topic, plumbs the sources of her opposition to sociological accounts of totalitarianism and examines sociological responses. One source of her negative view of sociology lay in an intellectual encounter with Karl Mannheim, a pioneer of the sociology of knowledge. Arendt criticized his approach as one that “unmasked” social actors, portraying them as dupes of historical forces they did not understand. It had an intellectual affinity with the violent unmaskings of the French Jacobins and the Russian show trials of the 1930s. I describe the unmasking approach to which Arendt objected but show that Mannheim’s standpoint was far more sophisticated than she allowed. The research also (a) identifies an early exchange of views on totalitarianism between Hannah Arendt and Eric Voegelin; (b) examines the assessment of Arendt’s theory of totalitarianism by the American sociologist Robert Nisbet who adapted her ideas but claimed they were insufficiently attentive to the social dynamics of totalitarian regimes; (d) shows that Arendt was unable, despite herself, to escape a sociological approach (the example given is her study of Jewish intellectuals).

340510.value: 帝國思維中運河前蘇伊士 - 1798至1869年

340510.label: Project Objectives
340510.value: completion of archival research necessary for writing a book

340510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
340510.value: This project investigates the history of French and British efforts to use the Isthmus of Suez to reach their colonies in Asia between the Napoleonic invasion of Egypt (1798) and the start of the construction of the Suez Canal (1859). It is not a study of the Suez Canal, but a study of the idea of a Suez passage and its role in the French and British imperial imaginations. It is a reminder of the double existence of empire—as much an imagined empire in the minds of the men who run it as a real one on the ground. This study focuses on Franco-British rivalry at Suez and the gap between the physical capacity to transport large numbers of men, materiel and goods across Suez, and the hopes and fears that such transportation was possible. Such ideas about Suez often contracted reality. Thus in 1798 the British erroneously feared that French-occupied Egypt could threaten India from Suez. Later, French engineers erroneously reported that differences between the Red and Mediterranean Sea water levels made construction of a canal too difficult. French and British policymakers operated on this premise from the 1820s until the 1840s. Boosterism for (and fear of) a canal in the 1850s over-estimated the immediate changes a canal would bring. At each step, French and British decision-makers perceived the situation at Suez differently than it was: believing a canal possible when it was not and believing it not possible when it was. Yet their imaginations also drove them to alter the terrain at Suez as well: One had to believe Suez could be crossed by canal or rail before one began digging or laying tracks. Similarly, in the 1820s and 1830s, when the French and British assumed the isthmus could not be crossed, their assumption became a self-fulfilling prophecy. At no point did French or British policymakers view Suez on their own: each made decisions about Suez based on expectations about the other. This project thus examines the interactions between the French and British Empires and their mutual imperial expectations at Suez and in the Red Sea, investigating how each drove the other to cross the isthmus. This grant would fund the final stages of archival research in Britain and France for this project. The research will form the basis for a book.

340510.label: Realisation of objectives
340510.value: The project objectives, as originally laid out, were entirely accomplished. I completed the archival research necessary for writing a book covering the Anglo-French duel over Suez and the route to Asia between 1798 and 1859. As indicated in the mid-term progress report, I extended the period of time covered by the book twice, first to 1870, and then to 1885. I have completed the research up through 1885. The book in progress examines the French-British relationship over the Suez isthmus crossing between European and Asian waters, and how the French-British relationship there affected the French-British relationship in maritime Asia throughout the nineteenth century. A number of archives were potentially pertinent to the subject, not all of which could be visited without significantly delaying the book project (and one doubts that there would necessarily be much to gain from visiting each and every local archive). In addition to archives in Egypt and the maritime port cities in Asia (Saigon, Bombay, Hong Kong, Singapore, and so on), there were significant archival holdings in Britain and France. Since archives in the colonial metropole were most likely to cover both Suez and Asian waters at once, PI focused there. PI focused further on naval archives, since the two countries navies were the institutions most directly focused on dealing with the other. While foreign office, postal, colonial office and other archives were consulted, the focus on naval records allowed PI to narrow his search while maintaining the geographic breadth which the project required. (Furthermore, an existing focus on diplomatic archives in the secondary literature encouraged an examination of naval records instead.) Much of the data found at the French naval archives in Vincennes, France has been unexamined by French imperial historians (the papers of the Division d’Egypte, will force us to revise our understanding of French colonial expansion in Southeast Asia significantly). I also conducted significant research in the British National Archives into Anglo-French naval relations as well.

340510.label: Major findings and research outcome
340510.value: The Anglo-French relationship in Asia was complex--but whether they were at war with each other, at peace, or in some nebulous state between these two powers defined their places in Asia in relation to each other. This relationship evolved over time, from one primarily of antagonism in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars, to one of friendly enemies--frenemies, or as the French might say, frère-enemies (brother enemies)--who might passive-aggressively support and undermine each other at the same time. This frenemy relationship was particularly prevalent at sea, where the French and British navies needed bother to counter each other and cooperate with each other in order to project their tenuously thin forces beyond the Indian Ocean and into the China Seas. In the competitive-collaborative relationship between Britain and France, specific matters previous un-examined come to greater light: 1) The role of coal (including collier companies, coal mines, and coal depots) in fostering French dependency on British colonies in Asia. 2) The degree to which the French colonial project in Vietnam was fundamentally reliant on the British base at Hong Kong (and to a lesser extent, Singapore) for its early development. 3) The role of the French Division d’Egypte in pioneering the transport of soldiers en mass between Europe and Asia through Egypt, and the British copying of the French effort. 4) Anglo-French collaboration in mail and transport through Egypt and France in 1840 even as Britain and France came close to war over the ability to interdict the other’s mail and transport in Egypt. 5) The degree to which the function of the Suez Canal was preceeded by the Egyptian railroad network prior to the canal’s completion

340510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
340510.value: Potential for further development is twofold. First, the research needs to be written up in final form as a book. Second, the research has clear implications for the origins of the Anglo-French entente and the origins of World War I. This might be developed by another scholar, perhaps a doctoral student under my supervision. The main course of action from here on is writing in order to produce a book manuscript.

340510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
340510.value: This study investigates French and British use of the Isthmus of Suez to reach their colonies in Asia between the Napoleonic invasion of Egypt (1798) and the 1880s. It examines the idea of a Suez passage and its role in the French and British imperial imaginations. This project examines interactions between the French and British Empires and their mutual imperial expectations at Suez and in the Red Sea, investigating how each drove the other to cross the isthmus and transforms the Asian maritime world. It makes use of previously un- or under-examined archival sources in French and British archives (especially naval archives) to construct a history of British and French rivalry in maritime Asia in the 1800s. The resulting book will interpret French and British imperial histories in light of one another (they are usually interpreted on their own), providing a major addition to the historical literature. The resulting book will also serve not only as a research monograph, but as a general survey of 19th century empire, appropriate for assigning to undergraduate students.

340810.label: Project Title(Chinese)
340810.value: 零售经营面积交换的合作式博弈分析

340810.label: Project Objectives
340810.value: We will investigate a retail-space exchange problem that originates from a novel practice of Woolworths and Somerfield. This problem has not been investigated by academics. We hope that the research project will contribute to the marketing and OM literature, and provide useful managerial insights to practitioners. We will develop a nonlinear, product category-dependent demand model, which is different from extant marketing-related publications (which assumed linear models). We will consider both the two-retailer and the n-retailer (n>=3) problems, and for each problem we will analyze the decentralized and centralized cases. In each case, we will examine whether or not the retailers can benefit from the retail space exchange, and we will use cooperative game theory to find a fair allocation scheme that is used to divide the system-wide profit surplus between two or, among n>=3, retailers. We will provide some numerical examples to illustrate our game analysis. We will consider a more general case for our game analysis, where the retailers may have different bargaining powers; this should be helpful to other cooperative game-related research projects in the OM area. We will propose a new approach to compute a unique weighted Shapley value that satisfies the core conditions and also reflects retailers' bargaining powers.

340810.label: Realisation of objectives
340810.value: We have carefully investigated this project to address five major objectives. To address the first objective, we have analyzed a retail-space exchange problem that originates from a novel practice of Woolworths and Somerfield (and also, Waitrose and Boots). We have proposed two papers in Production and Operations Management (POM, 2013) and European Journal of Operational Research (EJOR, 2013) for the research project---which, we believed, can contribute to the marketing and operations management (OM) literature, and have drawn a number of managerial insights that should help practitioners successfully implement the space-exchange strategy. For the second objective, we have used cooperative game theory to propose a paper---which was published in EJOR (2013)---where we extended Corstjens and Doyle's space-dependent demand function (1981), and developed a general (nonlinear, product category-dependent) demand model to calculate each retailer's sales at his own space and those at other retailers' spaces. Our demand model is different from most extant marketing-related publications which assumed linear models. In another paper that has appeared in POM (2013) we applied the Hotelling model (1929) to derive the demand function for two retailers. For the third objective, we have considered the two-retailer problem in our papers in both POM (2013) and EJOR (2013), and investigated the n-retailer (n≥3) problem in our paper EJOR (2013). For each problem in both papers, we analyzed the decentralized and centralized cases. For each case in our paper in POM (2013), we calculated two retailers' pricing and space allocation decisions in Nash equilibrium; and for each case in our paper EJOR (2013), we employed cooperative game theory to fairly divide the system-wide profit surplus between two or, among n≥3, retailers. We provided a number of numerical examples to illustrate our game analysis in our two papers. For the fourth objective, we have already examined a more general case for our cooperative game analysis in our paper EJOR (2013). In this paper, the retailers may have different bargaining powers, which should be helpful to other cooperative game-related research projects in the OM area. For the fifth objective, we have considered the two-retailer and the n-retailer (n≥3) cases in our paper EJOR (2013), using the concepts of "generalized Nash bargaining scheme" and "weighted Shapley value," respectively. We proposed a new approach to compute a unique weighted Shapley value that satisfies the core conditions and also reflects retailers' bargaining powers.

340810.label: Major findings and research outcome
340810.value: We have two research publications that appeared in POM (2013) and in EJOR (2013). In our paper published in POM (2013), we considered retail space-exchange problems where two retailers exchange shelf space to increase accessibility to more of their consumers in more locations without opening new stores. Using the Hotelling model (1929), we find two retailers’ optimal prices given their host and guest space in two stores under the space-exchange strategy. Then, using the optimal space-dependent prices, we analyzed a non-cooperative game where each retailer makes a space allocation decision for the retailer's own store. We showed that the two retailers will implement such a strategy in the game, if and only if their stores are large enough to serve more than one-half of their consumers. Nash equilibrium for the game exists and its value depends on consumers' utilities and trip costs as well as the total available space in each retailer's store. Moreover, as a result of the space-exchange strategy, each retailer's prices in two stores are both higher than the retailer's price before the space exchange but they may or may not be identical. In our paper that appeared in EJOR (2013), we also analyzed retail space-exchange problems where two or more retailers exchange their excess retail spaces to improve the utilization of their space resource. But, different from our paper published in POM (2013), we considered the space-exchange problem with two or more retailers, and used cooperative game theory to examine the problems from the perspective of retailers' incentives for exchanging their spaces. We first investigated the two-retailer space exchange problem and found conditions under which the system-wide profit increases. In order to entice both retailers with different bargaining powers to exchange their spaces, we used the generalized Nash bargaining scheme to allocate the total profit surplus between the two retailers. Next, we considered the space-exchange problem involving three or more retailers, and constructed a cooperative game in characteristic function form. We derived the necessary and sufficient conditions under which the game is essential and superadditive, and also proved that the core is non-empty. Moreover, in order to find a unique allocation scheme that ensures the stability of the grand coalition, we proposed a new approach to compute a weighted Shapley value that satisfies the core conditions and also reflects retailers' bargaining powers.

340810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
340810.value: For this project, we have successfully proposed two papers to investigate the space-exchange problems with two or more retailers. In the paper published in POM (2013), we used the Hotelling model to consider two retailers’ pricing and space-exchanging decisions in a non-cooperative setting. When we proposed this paper, we found that the informational advantage and the risk reduction should be the two main advantages of the space-exchange strategy. This could not be examined by using the Hotelling model. Thus, in this paper, we only focused on consumers' increased choices and reduced trip costs, which should be the primary advantage for the strategy. The analysis of the informational advantage and the risk reduction for the space-exchange problem would be a future research direction. In our paper that appeared in EJOR (2013), we developed an approach to compute a unique weighted Shapley value that satisfies the core conditions and reflects retailers' bargaining powers. I indeed addressed our fifth objective successfully. But, to use our approach, we need to solve a non-linear problem, which may limit the application of our approach. In future, we may try to find a simpler method for the calculation of a unique weighted Shapley value.

340810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
340810.value: In reality, retailers selling different products may implement partnership strategies that involve exchanging shelf space to improve their operating performance. The space-exchange strategy has been adopted by Woolworths and Somerfield, Waitrose and Boots. To investigate the impact of the strategy on the retailing operations, we need to consider the pricing and space-allocation decisions of two retailers who agree to exchange their space. Accordingly, we proposed the paper that appeared in POM (2013), where the two retailers will implement such a strategy in the game, if and only if their stores are large enough to serve more than one-half of their consumers. Moreover, as a result of the space-exchange strategy, each retailer's prices in two stores are both higher than the retailer's price before the space exchange but they may be identical. To assure the willingness of each retailer to exchange its space, the allocation of the profit surplus resulting from space-exchange strategy must be fair to all retailers. We proposed the paper in EJOR (2013) to find the fair allocation schemes, and also found that all retailers can jointly achieve a positive profit surplus iff at least one retailer allocates a positive excess space to the other retailers.

340910.label: Project Title(Chinese)
340910.value: 一九五○年代的香港文學與文化

340910.label: Project Objectives
340910.value: The primary aim of the project is to recover, evaluate and make available to the public the seminal yet obliterated and under-researched Hong Kong literature of the 1950s to fill the research gap in the studies of Hong Kong literature and modern Chinese literature as no systematic research has been done on the topic despite the historical, political, cultural and social significance and complexity of the 1950s. To achieve the principal objective, the following working directions are set: (i) to thoroughly and comprehensively collect and systematically examine literary works published dispersedly on the newspapers and literary magazines of the decade; (ii) to develop new research methodology for the studies of Hong Kong literature to combine empirical research and critical investigation; (iii) to critically evaluate the aesthetic value and historical and cultural significance of the collected literary works of the 50s so as to illuminate (a) the formation of Hong Kong modernism, (b) the inheritance from and transformation of Chinese cultural and literary traditions, (c) the interplay between literature and other art forms (e.g. Cantonese opera and cinema), and, (d) the dynamics between literature and popular culture; (iv) to situate Hong Kong literature in the context and development of modern Chinese literature, and to raise issues emerged from the complexity of Hong Kong literature of the 1950s to the studies of comparative literature; (v) to investigate the tensions, negotiations and intricacies between various contesting literary, cultural and ideological influences hidden in the collected texts against the Cold War background in order to unravel the perplexity of the decade and to illuminate the Zeitgeist of the 1950s Hong Kong in contribution to the writing of Hong Kong literary history and to the studies of Hong Kong history and culture.

To achieve the principal objective, the following working directions are set:
(i) to thoroughly and comprehensively collect and systematically examine literary works published dispersedly on the newspapers and literary magazines of the decade;
(ii) to develop new research methodology for the studies of Hong Kong literature to combine empirical research and critical investigation;

(iii) to critically evaluate the aesthetic value and historical and cultural significance of the collected literary works of the 50s so as to illuminate (a) the formation of Hong Kong modernism, (b) the inheritance from and transformation of Chinese cultural and literary traditions, (c) the interplay between literature and other art forms (e.g. Cantonese opera and cinema), and, (d) the dynamics between literature and popular culture;

(iv) to situate Hong Kong literature in the context and development of modern Chinese literature, and to raise issues emerged from the complexity of Hong Kong literature of the 1950s to the studies of comparative literature;

(v) to investigate the tensions, negotiations and intricacies between various contesting literary, cultural and ideological influences hidden in the collected texts against the Cold War background in order to unravel the perplexity of the decade and to illuminate the Zeitgeist of the 1950s Hong Kong in contribution to the writing of Hong Kong literary history and to the studies of Hong Kong history and culture.

340910.label: Realisation of objectives
340910.value: Through thorough archival research and examination of the literary magazines and newspaper supplements published in Hong Kong in the 1950s, the Centre for Humanities Research (CHR) has rediscovered a lot of seminal work of Hong Kong literature at the time, for example, the short stories written by Ronald Mar, Evan Yang, and Li Kuang, as well as the poems published in Hong Kong in the 1950s, which were anthologized into a series of publications by CHR and Chung Hwa Books. The archival research also benefited the research of PI’s, Co-PI’s, and participated scholars’ critical investigation in many different levels. After the interim conference held in May 2012, CHR was able to publish a peer-review special issue of the Journal of Modern Literature in Chinese on the topic, ‘Cultural Transformation in the 1950s: From Mainland China to Hong Kong.’ As part of the research outcome of this project, CHR edited a book that collects the articles written about music, visual art, martial art fiction, and cinema, by the speakers of the Project’s seminar series ‘Hong Kong Literature and Culture of the 1950s.’ The the articles collected in former PI Prof. Leung Ping-kwan’s book, Leung Ping-kwan’s 1950s: Hong Kong Literature and Culture, also illuminates the adaptive nature of Hong Kong literature in the 1950s, which anticipates Hong Kong modernism in the late 1950s and early 1960s. The conclusive conference successfully held in May 2013 gathered scholars of Hong Kong literature and culture of the 1950s. The in-depth discussion of methodology, case studies and cultural political context of the Hong Kong literature anticipated a future project on its continuation in the 1960s. CHR also noticed the lack of study in the area of popular culture, and therefore conducted a conference on Hong Kong pulp fiction in the 1950s in December 2013, at the moment preparing a peer-review special issue on this topic to be published in the Journal of Modern Literature in Chinese. During the project period, CHR has successfully filled many gaps in the study of Hong Kong literature and culture of the 1950s, although former PI Prof. Leung Ping Kwan sadly left us in January 2013. I decided to pick up the project, carried it on with my best efforts, and I now believe, completed it with best quality.

340910.label: Major findings and research outcome
340910.value: In 2011, CHR published two books (Part C 8.1 Hong Kong Literature: Legacy and Transformation and 8.2 An Anthology of Hong Kong Short Stories [Two Volumes]) which contain CHR’s initial efforts on the research on Hong Kong literature and culture of the 1950s. Part C 8.2 An Anthology of Hong Kong Short Stories [Two Volumes] was extended into a book the rediscovered stories translated into English (Part C 8.10 In Search of a Flat: Hong Kong Short Stories). As the project became more mature and thorough in 2013, CHR and Chung Hwa Books published a series of six books, as research outcome from the industrious archival research (Part C 8.5 Anthology of Hong Kong Poetry of the 1950s, 8.6 Stories after a Long Night: Selected Short Stories of Li Kuang, 8.7 Half Century Glimpses: Ronald P. Mar’s Fiction Collection, and 8.8 True Lies: Selected Urban Short Stories of Evan Yang) which made available the excellent literary work in the 1950s to the public, and from critical investigation (Part C 8.2 Leung Ping-kwan’s 1950s: Criticisms on Hong Kong Literature and Culture and 8.3 A Decade of Joy and Pain: Hong Kong Literature and Culture of the 1950s). What is more, Part C 8.2 and 8.3 are among the few books that can serve as reliable academic sources for the future study of Hong Kong literature and culture of the 1950s. The peer-review special issue of the Journal of Modern Literature in Chinese on the topic, ‘Cultural Transformation in the 1950s: From Mainland China to Hong Kong,’ edited by me and Co-PI Prof. Sun Yifeng (Part C 8.9), includes articles that study how Hong Kong inherited and transformed Chinese culture and literary traditions in the context of the cultural Cold War in Hong Kong, as demonstrated in the interplay between such art sectors as poetry, fiction, literary translation, cinema and visual art.

340910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
340910.value: Completing the project, I and CHR colleagues believe that the formation of Hong Kong modernism cannot be sufficiently examined within the scope of the 1950s, as its early exponent Ronald Mar and the publishing venue Literary Currents (1956-1959) remained even more influential in the early 1960s. As Quanan’s stream-of-consciousness novel Down through the Limbus was published in 1961, Liu Yichang’s The Drunkard in 1963, and modernists’ magazine Modern Edition in 1963, the temporal gap between Literary Currents and the modernists’ activities in the early 1960s needs to be studied in a larger framework that allows the investigator to examine its making and thrift towards the mid-1960s. Therefore, CHR has established a 2-year research project on Hong Kong Literature and Culture of the 1960s with the focus on modernism and successfully get another RGC GRF grant that starts from January 2015.

340910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
340910.value: Under the leadership and vision of the late Prof. Leung Ping-kwan (Ye Si), the best loved Hong Kong writer and scholar of Hong Kong literature, the Centre for Humanities Research (CHR) of Lingnan University has successfully completed the General Research Fund project ‘Hong Kong Literature and Culture of the 1950s.’ Through industrious archival research and critical investigation, CHR has brought the project to fruition by making the rediscovered literary work available to the public and producing volumes of academic work that can best serve as both academic and public references.

341910.label: Project Title(Chinese)
341910.value: 對因果發現方法的一些重要假設的建設性考察

341910.label: Project Objectives
341910.value: I aim to examine three standard assumptions upon which many causal discovery methods are built, by investigating the testability of these assumptions and the kinds of mistakes that would result when these assumptions fail. The general objective is to gain a better understanding of the consequences of falsely making the assumptions, and to suggest modifications or extensions to the existing methods to cope with the possible failure of the assumptions. More specifically, regarding the assumption called Causal Faithfulness Condition, I aim to further develop the line of work presented in Zhang and Spirtes (2008), especially the attempt to incorporate tests of the condition into causal discovery procedures and the interesting finding that the procedures may satisfy a more demanding asymptotic success criterion with tests of Faithfulness. Regarding the assumption called Causal Minimality Condition, I intend to further develop our preliminary examination of the condition presented in Zhang and Spirtes (forthcoming), and also relate my work to the problem of causal inference in deterministic causal systems (e.g., Glymour 2007), in which Minimality routinely fails. Regarding the assumption called Causal Markov Condition, the assumption that has attracted the most attention from philosophers, I aim to study in detail the implications of its failure for causal inference. Since the condition is essential to the framework of causal Bayesian networks, it will be necessary to slightly generalize the framework of causal Bayesian networks (see the section on Research Plan and Methodology for more information on this issue). A more practical objective is to implement and test the modifications and extensions to the existing causal discovery procedures suggested by the above theoretical investigation. I expect to publish a series of articles based on the research project, in philosophy of science and artificial intelligence journals and conference proceedings. In particular I expect to write at least one more article on the causal minimality condition, one more article on the causal faithfulness condition, and two or three articles on generalizing the causal Bayesian network framework and on the consequences of the failure of the causal Markov condition. These articles will be submitted to quality philosophy journals such as synthese, philosophy of science, and BJPS, etc. Moreover, with the help of a programmer, I aim to also produce several papers on more robust causal discovery algorithms, suitable for artificial intelligence journals and conference proceedings.

341910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
341910.value: The epistemology of causation has received rigorous yet controversial treatment in the framework of causal Bayesian networks (CBN). The main controversy in the philosophical literature is concerned with the assumptions commonly adopted in the CBN framework. In this project I propose to examine the assumptions from a novel perspective. Two central theoretical questions are: (1) to what extent is the failure of the assumptions detectable/testable? And, more importantly for this project, (2) to what extent can we still get correct answers (to certain causal questions) even though the assumptions made are literally false? By asking these questions, I grant the skeptical worry of the possible (or even widespread) failure of the standard assumptions, but resist the temptation to draw a quick destructive conclusion from the worry. The theoretical side of the project has three parts, dealing with three assumptions: Causal Markov Condition (Markov), Causal Minimality Condition (Minimality), and Causal Faithfulness Condition (Faithfulness). First, assuming Markov and Minimality, I will further study the testability of Faithfulness and how such tests can be incorporated into causal discovery procedures, based on my earlier work. Moreover, I will develop an interesting finding regarding how algorithms incorporating tests of Faithfulness may satisfy a stronger asymptotic criterion (known as uniform consistency) than what the current algorithms achieve (known as pointwise consistency). Second, assuming Markov, I will develop my earlier work on the consequences of falsely assuming Minimality, and improve the results on how to control the damage of falsely assuming Minimality. With such results we could argue that it is fine to assume Minimality as if it is true even though it is literally false. The previous two parts both assume Markov. In the third part, I will investigate the consequences of the failure of Markov. Since Markov is essential to the semantics of CBN, this part requires a generalization of CBN, but the basic methodology follows that of the second part. That is, I will investigate exactly what mistakes would result from falsely assuming Markov, how serious such mistakes are, and how they might be detected and suspended. If successful, such results can be used to argue that assuming Markov is still useful even when it is literally false. On the more practical side, I will try to implement and empirically test modifications and extensions to the existing causal discovery algorithms, as suggested by the theoretical investigations.

341910.label: Realisation of objectives
341910.value: We think we have sufficiently addressed the objectives and greatly improved our understanding of the original questions that motivated the objectives. In connection to the first objective, we had both negative and positive findings. The original question was whether the mathematical results on the identifiability of functional causal models could lend support to the thesis that causality is reducible to probability, or more precisely, the thesis that the asymmetry between cause and effect is identifiable from properties of their joint probability distribution. We now think the answer is probably no. First, we realized that an old result due to Hyvarinen and Pajunen (1999, "Nonlinear independent component analysis: Existence and uniqueness results") could be adapted to show that even if variable causation is assumed to be generally representable by a functional causal model, causal asymmetry is still not always determinable from the true probability distribution of variables, unless. in general still not in which the effect variable is taken to be a function of the cause variables and a noise variable that is independent from the cause variables,

400410.label: Project Objectives
400410.value: The main objective of this proposal is to develop useful statistical methodologies for the analysis of processes with jumps such as the Levy process, and to study the empirical likelihood characteristic function approach to the analysis of Levy processes. Another objective is to combine the empirical characteristic function with the jackknife methods to conduct parameter estimation and testing for Levy processes, which will lead to important development in the inference for Levy processes. The results will be useful to conduct goodness-of-fit tests and model validation. Since interval estimation is found to be more informative and useful than point estimation as a risk management device, a related objective in this propoal is to develop methods for interval estimation of value-at-risk (VaR) in higher dimension by means of the empirical copula technique. To this end, the idea of jackknifing the empirical likelihood is most useful. To model the dynamic volatilities structure, constructing novel empirical likelihood for the inference of GARCH models constitutes another important objective. Based on the idea of smoothing, asymptotic chi-squared limits will be developed and different smoothing techniques will be investigated. The evaluation of empirical likelihood involves solving highly nonlinear equations under nonstandard constriants, which is computationally challenging and difficult. This proposal aims at developing efficient numerical algorithms to compute the empirical likelihood procedure in real-time. Comparisions with other smoothing techniques will also be conducted. This proposal also carries an important human resources perspective. Risk management is a rapidly developing discipline as evidenced by the recent financal cirsis, it is crucial to incorporate frontier research into the pedagogical front in a timely manner. As more and more practioners are faced with the challenge of modeling huge jumps, successful completion of this proposal will lead to a deeper understanding of the empirical likelihood method, which in turn enhances the applicability of many commonly entertained models to financial risk management and other disciplines.

400410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400410.value: 金融市場往往表現不連續與跳躍現象。要有效地提高風險管理，風險管理師需要把跳躍與相關現象反映於波幅內。而萊偉(Lévy)過程則提供了一有效的方法去處理跳躍現象。 這研究計劃旨在發展有用的統計方法處理跳躍。命題重點在於利用萊偉過程及特徵函數去作統計推斷。結合經驗似然與大折刀方法，推斷出條件風險值與相關連系數(copula)的置信區間估計。 這研究計劃除了能發展科研外，還能帶出多方面的協同效應，使風險管理能更有效地推廣於研究與教學的領域，在金融財經及統計帶出不可或缺的成果。

400410.label: Realisation of objectives
400410.value: The main research objectives of this proposal have been realized. New statistical techniques for empirical likelihood characteristic functions for heavy-tailed time series such as Levy processes have been established. These methodologies include characteristic functions, goodness-of-fit tests for nonstationary heavy-tailed GARCH models, inference for long-memory, nonstationary and threshold inference for non-linear time series models. The findings of this project cover a wide scope of statistical inference for heavy-tailed and non-linear time series. Together they cover objectives 1-3 to a large extent. In the course of these findings, new numerical procedures have to be developed and some of these methods have been reported in the relevant publications, which addresses objective 4. Finally, during the duration of this project, a new book in risk management was published, which together with the puplished articles reported in Part C constitute the basis of objective 5.

400410.label: Major findings and research outcome
400410.value: The major finding of this proposal is to employ empirical characteristic function techniques to conduct statistical inference for heavy-tailed, non-linear and long-memory time series models. In particular, by making use of estimated empirical characteristic functions, goodness-of-fit test statistics can be constructed and testing the adequacy of the models can be performed. Further, by means of a high-dimensional regression framework, new techniques about inference of non-linear time series were established. Numerical integration methods have also been developed in the course of this project to handle the non-standard asymptotics that involve fractional Brownian motions and Levy processes. The collected research outcomes not only offer an entirely new way to analyze long-memory, non-linear and heavy-tailed phenomena in financial time series, but also to other disciplines such as network traffic, internet data, and e-commerce. Important research findings from this project were reported in major international conferences and published in premiere refereed journals and books, as stipulated in Part C: Tables 8 and 9.

400410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400410.value: As empirical processes techniques are nonparametric in nature, the results obtained in this proposal can be used in many other contexts. In particular, by introducing the idea of empirical likelihood characteristic functions, results from this project offer a novel way to analyze time series with jump behaviors, which is of huge potential interest in financial risk management. The techniques developed in this project can be applied both to the long-memory, nonlinear and nonstationary cases with heavy-tailed innovations. Further, by introducing a high-dimensional framework, this project offers new insight into the inference for the threshold parameter of general non-linear time series models. In particular, with the established theoretical properties of threshold parameters, the pursuit of non-linear time series will be greatly enhanced. Finally, in areas such as financial risk management and network engineering, where heavy-tailed and long-range dependence are rules rather than exceptions, results of this project offer a useful alternative to the traditional parametric methods for conducting statistical inference.

400410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400410.value: All of the major objectives have been realized in this project. By virtue of the empirical likelihood characteristic function techniques, advances in model estimation and calibration can now be efficiently conducted. This will bring significant impacts in modeling important features not only for a single time series, but also for several series jointly such as in the case of portfolio management and network traffic, where the joint effects of different assets have to be taken into account. In particular, the first four objectives achieved in this proposal offer a platform and new direction that will lead to important advances in the pursuit of modeling multivariate financial data. In addition, by developing numerical algorithms in evaluating the limit distributions involving fractional Brownian motions and Levy processes in the empirical processes procedures, many of these methods can now be computed, which would enhance their applications in various disciplines. Finally, by publishing relevant papers and monographs in the field of risk management and statistics as indicated in objective five, important research developments can be disseminated to practitioners timely and effectively.

400510.label: Project Objectives
400510.value: To design algorithms for solving inpainting problems in transformed domains. This includes (i) designing efficient and accurate solvers for edge-preserving and sparsity-enhancing energy functionals by using different variational techniques, such as primal dual proximal method and the splitting schemes; and (ii) developing noise detectors and suitable data-fitting terms for other non-Gaussian noise models, such as the impulse noise model. To build the convergence theory for our algorithms. This includes (i) adapting existing convergence results in image-domain inpainting, such as those of the Douglas-Rachford splitting, to our algorithms; and (ii) using convex analysis and variational inequalities to derive our own convergence proofs for our algorithms. To test the algorithms and apply them to practical problems. These include (i) performing an exhaustive comparison of our algorithms with existing transformed-domain inpainting algorithms in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness; and (ii) applying the best algorithms to JPEP and JPEG2000 inpainting problem, Magnetic Resonance Imaging, and other potential applications such as compressive sampling.

400510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400510.value: Image inpainting problem refers to the correction of corrupted data in images. It is an important task in image processing with a wide range of applications. Typical examples are (i) scratches removal---remove undesired features in an image, (ii) zooming---blow up a part of an image, (iii) impulse noise removal---remove noise when an image is transmitted via a noisy channel, and (iv) high-resolution image reconstruction---construct a high-resolution image from multiple low-resolution ones. Inpainting needs to be done in an image domain or in a transformed domain depending on where the corrupted data are. In JPEG image compression standard, images are formatted and stored in terms of discrete cosine transform coefficients, while in the JPEG2000 standard, they are stored in terms of wavelet transform coefficients. If some of these coefficients are lost or corrupted during storage or transmission, the degraded image may contain some artifacts such as blurred edges or black holes. This prompts the need of inpainting in the transformed domains. This research focuses on the reconstruction of the lost or corrupted transformed coefficients, especially under the wavelet, discrete cosine, or discrete Fourier transform. Inpainting in image domains, such as zooming, is similar to the problem of interpolation where the missing pixel values are approximated by using the pixel values of the available pixels. Inpainting methods in image domains usually exploit the property that the regions to recover are local and hence the corrupted pixel values can be estimated by using neighboring information. Inpainting in transformed domains, however, is different since the corrupted transformed coefficients can affect the whole image and it may be impossible to define the corresponding inpainting regions in the image domain. Image-domain inpainting methods therefore can not be applied directly to the transformed-domain inpainting problems. In this proposal, we will design efficient and accurate variational algorithms for solving inpainting problems in transformed domains. Different energy functions, including the edge-preserving total variational norm and the sparsity-enhancing l-1 norm, will be employed; and different optimization techniques such as the primal dual proximal method and the splitting schemes will be utilized. Noise detectors and suitable data-fitting terms for non-Gaussian noise models will also be developed. We will derive convergence theory for these algorithms, and apply them to some important practical applications, such as the JPEG and JPEG2000 inpainting problem, which are cosine-domain and wavelet-domain inpainting problems; and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), which is a Fourier-domain inpainting problem.

400510.label: Realisation of objectives
400510.value: We have successfully designed algorithms for solving inpainting problem in transformed domains. For these new algorithms we have studied how to choose the regularization parameters in the primal-dual proximal method and the splitting schemes. We have also studied their convergence behavior. As for applications, we have considered wavelet and JPEG2000 compression and inpainting problems. We also have studied image recovery problem in ground-based astronomy. Specifically, related to the objectives in Section 5.1, we have done the followings: Objective 1: We have developed an algorithms [3] that automatically choose the regularization parameter so as to minimize the noise and the data-fitting simultaneously. We have also developed algorithms [4,6] when the images are required to be in a range, e.g. 8-bit images. Objective 2: For the algorithms we have developed, we have proved that they are convergent. We also studied the linearized version of some of these algorithms [8]. Objective 3: We have also tested our algorithms [1] and [2] on robustness and accuracy on wavelet domains using JPEG2000 images. We have considered practical problem in ground-based astronomy, queueing networks, and ODE respectively in [5,7,9].

400510.label: Major findings and research outcome
400510.value: We have developed powerful and efficient methods for solving inpainting problems in transformed domains. The methods we used are either based on primal-dual formulation or splitting formulation. In order that the methods be practical, we also have addressed the problem of choosing the regularization parameters and restricting the images in a box. Linearized version of the algorithms we proposed are also developed. For these new methods we give their convergence proofs and compare them with existing state-of-the-art methods.

400510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400510.value: Many of the methods we proposed can be applied to other image processing problem such as image restoration, image reconstruction and video separation. A graduate student is being trained in this direction.

400710.label: Project Title(Chinese)
400710.value: 多重檢驗中的功效、正確決策以及樣本量的確定

400710.label: Project Objectives
400710.value: Re-examine the concepts of power in multiple testing. Illustrate and discuss the various problems of using popular concepts of power in multiple testing. Develop a new paradigm to evaluate different multiple testing procedures using the probability of correct decision. The concept of correct decision instead of power serves as a better choice in assessing and comparing multiple testing procedures. Both theoretical and simulation methods will be explored to substantiate our arguments. Derive asymptotics to understand the operation characteristics of the newly proposed techniques, including the relationship between the probability of correct decision, and the composition of the inferential family and the structure of the test statistics. Conduct extensive simulation studies to explore small sample behaviour. Since in many clinical studies nowadays, sample size may be very small due to cost or the availability of subjects, the behavior of our proposed techniques in small sample size environment is quite informative. Explore sample size determination methods under the proposed paradigm. Sample size determination is extremely important before the onset of an experiment owing to its impact on the viability, cost, efficiency and validity of the entire experiment.

400710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400710.value: 在多重檢驗中，功效的含義與單一假設檢驗的情形有很大的區別。假設在一族假設檢驗中包含有k個原假設。每一個原假設都有可能是真也可能是假，這樣在這一族假設中就可能有總共2k 種真與假的組合方式。因此，在多重檢驗的背景下，對如何度量檢驗的功效沒有統一的標準。最常見的關於功效的定義包括：全對功效，定義為檢測到全部真的差異的概率；任一對功效，定義為檢測到至少一個真的差異的概率；以及平均功效，它是對拒絕錯誤原假設的平均比例的一種估計。然而，在多重檢驗中所有這些常用的功效的概念僅僅關注于一族假設中的一類錯誤的假設。而且人們似乎已經把功效看作是評價不同檢驗過程優劣的一個唯一尺度，在本課題中，我們將對這一傳統做法發起挑戰。我們將在多重檢驗這一背景下設法展示兩種與功效有類似作用但又有非常不同工作方式的方法，我們的方法將會考慮到被接受的真假設的數目以及檢驗統計量的相關結構。因此，我們將提出一種新的方法，利用正確決策的概率來替代功效作為比較不同多重檢驗過程的尺度，這裡的正確決策既包括拒絕錯誤的原假設能力又包括接受正確的原假設的能力。 除此之外，我們將進一步研究基於這一新準則的樣本量的確定，因為樣本量的確定對於開始新的實驗或臨床試驗是非常重要的先驗資訊。

400710.label: Realisation of objectives
400710.value: The stated objectives have been achieved. There are numerous ways to conceptualize power in multiple testing environments. Common adopted measures include all-pairs power, the probability of rejecting all false null hypotheses; any-pair power, the probability to reject at least one false hypothesis; and per-pair power, the probability to reject a specific hypothesis. The choice of different measure is important, especially in the case when the selected measure of power becomes a crucial apparatus for the determination of the required sample size before the onset of a clinical trial. The formulation of power is further complicated when two-sided tests are involved. For two-sided tests, the rejection of a null hypothesis implies that substantial statistical evidence exists against the null hypothesis. However, it is worth to note that a correct decision requires more than a rejection of a null hypothesis, but also a correct identification of the direction of parameters. In this project, we are able to connect the concept of power with correct decision and sample size determination. The sample size required in a clinical study involving several treatments is computed based on the least favorable configuration of the set of parameters, and at the same time, guarantees a certain level of power with correct directional decision. Both theoretical justification and simulation study are provided to substantiate the use of our proposed method. To ensure the applicability of our proposed method, a very general inferential class of hypothesis is explored, with both one-sided and two-sided hypotheses. The procedure and algorithms required to compute sample size in order to achieve a pre-specified level of power is offered. Sample size allocation among different treatments is also considered. Simulation study indicates that our proposed method would be able to reduce the required sample size of a clinical study.

400710.label: Major findings and research outcome
400710.value: To discuss the merits of different definitions of power, we start with a very general class of families of hypothesis that contain a mixture of one- and two-sided tests. These families are called direction-mixed families. The introduced flexibility allows a wider spectrum of applications since in many clinical trials, prior information or requirement permit some of the hypothesis to be formulated as one-sided. Using all two-sided hypotheses would result a failure to use valuable information to increase the power of the study. The concept of power, modified to include directional decision error besides type I and type II errors, is discussed. Relying on the modified idea of power, an efficient scheme to generate the optimal sample size is provided. This work is accepted and appeared in Computational Statistics and Data Analysis (2012, see Section C). In clinical studies, ordered categorical data are frequently encountered. A popular method for comparing the efficacy of treatments is to use logistic regression with the proportional odds assumption. However, this assumption is often invalid. A better alternative that employs the latent normal model is given. Asymptotic results are derived to enable testing and estimation. With the proposed framework, power and sample size could also be obtained. Extensive simulation studies have been conducted to explore small sample behavior. This research is accepted by Statistical Methods in Medical Research (See Section C). With the developed framework, we also explore multiple comparison procedures for non-inferiority clinical studies. Non-inferiority trials are becoming increasingly popular as a means to assert the effectiveness of a new treatment compared with a standard treatment by demonstrating that the former maintains a substantial fraction of the effect of the latter. The loss of effectiveness should be clinically inconsequential and is outweighed by the gain in benefits such as the lowering of costs, the alleviation of side-effects and the adoption of less complicate regimen. We believe that our findings in this area will offer practitioners in the field of clinical research a useful tool for data analysis. The appropriate statistical procedure is given to conduct non-inferiority trials with multiple treatments. Further, both power and sample size determination are investigated. This work is accepted by Statistics in Medicine (See Section C).

400710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400710.value: This project focuses on responses which are assumed to have a parametric model. An interesting extension of this work is to explore non-parametric settings where less restrictive model assumptions are needed. Further, only univariate responses are considered, but in clinical studies, it is frequent that we encounter multivariate responses. For example, to measure the efficacy of a drug, we might collect both blood pressure and Cholesterol level for all patients. In that case, we have responses which are bivariate and these two variables are definitely correlated. The statistical techniques that are required could be far more complex. This should be a challenging research project for future consideration.

400710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400710.value: Nowadays, data collected in clinical studies are more complex than before and usually involved more than two treatments. Therefore, multiple testing techniques are required in order to obtain valid statistical inferences. However, there is a shortage of appropriate measurement tool that connect the measurement of power (the ability to reject false hypotheses), correct decision, and sample size determination. In this project, we have address this important issue and provided a framework so that practitioners in the field of clinical data analysis would find our proposed method useful. When comparing several treatments in a clinical study, we provide a useful tool for researches to identify the better treatment. Further, we also offer the means to estimate the required sample size before the onset of a clinical study.

400810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400810.value: The use of environmentally friendly reactions that enable chemists to stitch molecular species together in very efficient manner has brought tremendous impact on materials and biomaterials synthesis. In this proposal we seek to use such a method to prepare a new class of polymers containing multiple amide/amine and triazole units. These are chemical entities that have the potential to interact with each other along the polymer backbone and to endow the polymer with unique material properties. Our objectives are to study the effects of the polymer side chains, the spacer component between the above entities, and the number of such entities on the strength of the self association behavior of the resulting polymers. We believe that a thorough study of this type of polymer can generate a new class of materials with many potential applications, and can give us a better understanding of the underlying principles that govern such self association process in a polymer system. 可以让化学家们高效地把各种分子基团缝缀在一起的环境友好反应的应用对材料与生物材料的合成带来了巨大的影响。在这个课题中，我们试图利用这样的反应方法来合成一类包含多元酰胺/胺和三唑基团的新聚合物。这些基团具有沿着聚合物的骨架相互作用的潜力，从而可以赋予聚合物独特的性能。我们的目标包括研究聚合物侧链的效应、研究上述基团之间的空间构成以及上述基团数目对其相应聚合物自缔合强度的影响。我们相信，对这类聚合物的深入研究可以产生一类具有多种潜在应用的新材料，并且可以使我们对控制聚合物体系中上述自缔合作用的基本规则有更深入的理解。

400810.label: Realisation of objectives
400810.value: Objectives 1 and 2: Main chain poly(triazole) 3 with oligo(ethyleneglycol) side chains was prepared from dialkyne 1 and diazide 2 monomers under click polymerization conditions. However, the degree of polymerization (DP) was poor (6−11). Further optimizations of the polymerization conditions by changing the copper catalyst and solvent systems were carried out, but no significant improvement could be achieved. Main chain poly(triazole) 6 with alkyl side chains was also prepared from dialkyne 4 and diazide 5. For the polymerization involving dialkyne diamide 4 (X = NH) and 5, oligomeric products with a very low DP value (<3) were obtained. However, the corresponding polymerization with the dialkyne diester 4 (X = O) proceeded smoothly to afford polymer 6 (X = O) with a good DP value (20). The reason why the polymerization with the ester compound was much better than that of the amide analog was not known. Objective 3: It was found that the cyclization problem encountered in our earlier polymerization studies could be significantly reduced if some structural rigidity elements were introduced into the monomer. Hence, amongst the four dialkyne monomers 7−10, only the one 7 with two intramolecular H-bonds capable of reducing the rotational freedom of the two alkyne units copolymerized with diazide 11 to produce a polymer 12 with a much higher DP value (~53). The other monomers 8‒10 gave polymers with much lower DP values (13−16). Objective 4: Among all the polytriazoles prepared, only the one 12 with two intramolecular H-bonds could form strong transparent physical gels with organic solvents. Based on NMR, FT-IR, XRD and SEM studies, a physical model was proposed to rationalize the finding. This polymer gel also showed stimuli-responsive properties towards halide anions, and could be restored back to the gel state by the addition of Ag+ ion. Objective 5: To investigate the relationship between the number of H-bonding units and the strength of gelation properties, a series of oligo(amide-triazole)s 13 (n = 1−6) with different number of CONH units was prepared. It was found that oligomers with <5 CONH groups were non-gelating, but were good organogelators with ≥5 CONH groups. According to Tgel measurement, the strength of the organogelators increased with increasing number of CONH groups. These results indicated that a minimum amount of hydrogen bonding moieties was required to initiate the organogelating property. A self-sorting between oligomers of different chain length was also identified. (see appendix for structures)

400810.label: Major findings and research outcome
400810.value: 1. The polymerization efficiency of the click polymerization depends strongly on the structure of the monomers. Monomers with bulky substituents tend to possess inferior reactivity towards polymerization, while those with a more rigid backbone structure gave polymers with a higher molecular weight. 2. The supramolecular gelation properties of the main chain polytriazoles also depends on the structure. In general, polytriazoles with more H-bonding groups (CONH) and with a rigid backbone structure tend to form a gel network structure more easily, and hence are stronger gelators. Furthermore, the gels were found to show extremely interesting restorable stimuli-responsive properties towards anions. This result represents one of the rare examples of restorable, stimuli-responsive polymer gel in the literature. The findings were published in two journal papers (publication no. 2 and 4) and also presented in two conferences. 3. The number of H-bonding units in these poly(triazole)s has a critical effect on their gelating properties. It was found that a minimum amount of H-bonding moieties was required to initiate the organogelating property, and that a synergistic self-assembly effect was found with increasing number of H-bonding groups, since the melting temperature of the organogelators was found to increase with increasing number of H-bonding units. A very interesting self-sorting phenomenon between oligomers of different chain length was found. This research result was published as a journal paper (publication no. 4) and in a conference paper. 4. At the invitation of an editor of a book series, we published a review article (publication no. 1) on the gelation property of triazole-based polymer gels, which is related to the work of this proposal. 5. A PhD student was trained based on this original research.

400810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400810.value: This research work identifies key factors which can affect the self-assembly and organogelating properties of main chain polytriazoles. Based on these new findings, our next goal is to design stimuli-responsive polymer gel systems for sensing applications. For examples, we plan to prepare photo-responsive and redox-responsive gels by incorporating appropriate functionalities into these polymers. The advantage of using polymer gels as sensors is that sensing (i.e. gel to sol transition) can be visualized using naked eye without resorting the use of analytical instruments.

400810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400810.value: This research work identifies several new structural factors that can control the strength of gel materials, which are commonly used in our daily life. Many important daily applications, such as those in the food and biomedical industries, relies on the use of such gelating materials. Hence, the design of new and novel gel systems that can cater for different future applications is very important, and the results produced from our research work can provide new design guidelines of such useful materials.

400910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400910.value: One of the most important discoveries in cosmology and astrophyics in recent years is the confirmation that dark matter exists and accounts for the bulk of matter content in the universe. However, little is known about the nature of dark matter, except that it is massive and interacts with matter weakly. The sterile neutrino is a hypothetical particle that is a popular dark matter particle candidate. Its existence emerges naturally in simple generalizations of Standard Model of Particle Physics, and if confirmed, would represent major breakthroughs in our understanding of fundamental physics. Even though sterile neutrinos do not participate directly in weak interaction (hence the name), they would decay into ordinary particles such as photons and ordinary neutrinos, thus giving rise to observable consequences. In particular, we will study possible distortions of the cosmic microwave background - the remnant radiation leftover from the Big Bang - and thereby obtain constraints on sterile neutrino properties. If a significant amount of sterile neutrinos are accumulated into a neutron star, static and dynamic properties of the latter will be altered. We also propose to study the properties of such hybrid compact stars to determine whether they can be used as natural 'detectors' for sterile neutrinos. 近年宇宙學及天體物理學最重要的發現之一，是核實了暗物質的存在並且佔宇宙物質的大部份。但是，除了知道它們質量大但與普通物質只有微弱相互作用之外，我們對於暗物質的物理性質所知甚少。惰性中微子是一種假設性的粒子，是其中一個受歡迎的暗物質粒子模型。它們很自然的出現在粒子物理學標準模型的推廣內。若能證實它們的存在，將是基礎物理學的重大突破。雖然惰性中微子並不直接參予弱作用（故名），它們可衰變至光子及普通中微子，從而帶來可觀測的後果。我們將研究它們對宇宙微波背景輻射的影響，從而規範惰性中微子的物理性質。若果一顆中子星吸入相當數量的惰性中微子，它的靜態及動態性質會改變。我們亦將研究這種物別中子星是否可用作惰性中微子的自然「探測器」。

400910.label: Realisation of objectives
400910.value: Objective 1: We have achieved this object by showing that the existence of a degenerate halo of decaying sterile neutrinos with rest mass of 17.4 keV near the Galactic center (GC) naturally accounts for both the excess 8.7 keV emission observed by the Suzaku mission and the power needed to maintain the high temperature of the hot gas near the GC. We have worked out how the cosmological reionization history depends on decaying sterile neutrino mass m, lifetime tau and fraction f. We can reproduce the ad hoc reionization history assumed in the standard analysis of CMBA data. Objective 2: We have achieved this objective by deriving constraints on tau, f, and m using the WMAP 7-year data. Objective 3: We achieved this objective by adapting a general relativistic two-fluid formalism to calculate the hydrostatic equilibrium configuration of a sterile-neutrino-neutron star. We study its equilibrium structure and oscillation modes. We extended the calculation to sterile-neutrino-white-dwarfs as well. Objective 4: We achieved this objective by developing a two-dimensional two-fluid Eulerian hydrodynamics code for the explosion stage of a sterile-neutrino admixed SNIa. We find that DM admixture can lead to observable changes in the explosion energy, nickel production and ejecta velocity. A preprint has been prepared and will be submitted to Astrophysical Journal shortly.
