400910.label: Major findings and research outcome
400910.value: We developed the equations governing the Hydrogen and Helium ionization and matter temperature, as a function of redshift, given three parameters in the decaying sterile neutrino model: mass of the sterile neutrinos m, decay lifetime tau, and mass fraction of dark matter (DM) that are decaying f. We show that the existence of a degenerate halo of decaying sterile neutrinos with rest mass of 17.4 keV near the Galactic center naturally accounts for both the excess 8.7 keV emission observed by the Suzaku mission and the power needed to maintain the high temperature of the hot gas near the GC [5]. The reionization history, particularly the optical depth, has significant effects on CMBA, which can be used to constrain m and tau/f. We can reproduce the ad hoc reionization history assumed in the standard analysis of CMBA data. Assuming that there are no other sources of reionization and using the WMAP 7-year data, we find that 250 eV < m < 1 MeV, whereas 2.23 x 10^3 yr > τ/f > 1.23 x 10^18 yr. The best-fit values for m and τ/f are 17.3 keV and 2.03 x 10^16 yr respectively [2, 3]. We adapted a general relativistic two-fluid formalism to calculate the hydrostatic equilibrium configuration of an admixture of sterile neutrinos and normal nuclear matter. A new class of compact stars is found, consisting of a small normal matter core embedded in a DM halo [1]. These stars have two classes of oscillation modes, one of which is due mainly to the DM fluid, with frequencies depending sensitively on m [4]. We study white dwarfs with DM cores with m ranging from 1 GeV to 100 GeV. The DM core can be as massive as ~0.1 M_sun and affects the global structure of the star significantly. The radius of a stellar model with DM can be about two times smaller than that of a traditional white dwarf, and the Chandrasekhar mass limit can also be decreased by as much as 40% [6]. We developed a two-dimensional two-fluid Eulerian hydrodynamics code for the explosion stage of SNIa. We find that DM admixture can lead to observable changes in the explosion energy, nickel production and ejecta velocity. Our results suggest that DM admixture may account for a class of subluminous SNIa, and it may be possible to extract DM signals from SNIa observations [7].

400910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400910.value: Dark matter admixture may affect stellar evolution in many stages. We have studied their effects on neutron stars, white dwarfs, and the supernova stages, but it is worthwhile to extend our studies to other stellar evolution stages as well.

400910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400910.value: There has been tremendous advancement in the understanding of neutrino properties in the last decade. We now know that at least one species of neutrinos are massive, and that they can change from one type to another when propagating in free space. We also know that there should be a large number of neutrinos produced in the Big Bang as well as in stars. However, there are still much more to understand in this sector of ubiquitous yet elusive fundamental particles, such as their absolute mass scales and whether there are sterile neutrinos, hypothesized neutrino species that do not participate in weak interaction. If exist, sterile neutrinos may decay with cosmological lifetime to ordinary neutrinos and photons and affect the ionization history of the universe. Furthermore, their admixture into stellar objects, such as neutron stars and white dwarfs, may have significant effects on their structures. We study the possible roles of sterile neutrinos in several astrophysical and cosmological observables, including Cosmic Microwave Background Anisotropies, cluster hot gas distribution, neutron star and white dwarf structures, and the explosion of supernovae. We made use of relevant observation data to constrain sterile neutrino parameters.

401010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401010.value: The aim of this project is to develop and analyze a new class of efficient and stable computational techniques for the numerical approximations of wave propagation problem and convection-diffusion problem. The wave propagation problem and the convection-diffusion problem are a class of linear conservation laws that arises from plenty of important applications. Thus, the topic of numerical approximations to these problems has been an active research area. One crucial aspect common to these conservation laws is that the solutions to these problems satisfy some conservation properties. From the computational point of view, it is desirable to produce numerical approximations to these problems so that the conservation properties are preserved. This is particularly important when longer time simulations are required. There are in literature many computational approaches for these problems. The finite element methods provide a class of techniques that preserve the conservation properties globally. However these type of methods are typically implicit, making the schemes inefficient. The discontinuous Galerkin methods give an alternative class of efficient and explicit numerical methods for the above problems, but they are in general either dissipative, meaning conservation is not preserved, or have severe stability issues, meaning unphysical modes are artificially produced in the numerical solutions. In this project, we will develop a novel hybridized computational method for the numerical approximation of the above problems. Moreover, we will provide a rigorous mathematical justification for the validity of the new method. We will also perform a careful numerical study by plenty of simulations and comparisons to benchmark problems. The proposed method can be seen as a compromise between the finite element method and the discontinuous Galerkin method, in the way that it has the advantages of both finite element and discontinuous Galerkin methods. In particular, it is both explicit as discontinuous Galerkin methods and preserves the conservation properties of the conservation laws as finite element methods. Moreover, the proposed method is both stable and optimally convergent. Thus, it provides a new class of stable and accurate solvers for applications based on the wave propagation and convection-diffusion problems. Due to the non-dissipaive nature, the proposed method is extremely suitable for applications which require longer time simulations. Furthermore, the methodology and mathematical tools developed in this project will provide a foundation for the successful development of conservation preserving techniques to a broader class of problems arising from a variety of important applications. 這個項目的目的是開發和分析一類新的高效和穩定的計算技術。這計算技術可用於波的傳播問題和對流擴散問題的數值逼近。 波的傳播問題和對流擴散問題是一個類線性守恆定律並來自很多重要的應用。因此，數值逼近這些問題一直是活躍的研究領域。面對這些守恆定律常見的一個關鍵是它們的解滿足一定程度的守恆性。從計算的角度來看，可取的數值逼近方法使守恆性被保留。 當需要較長時間的計算，這一點尤其重要。有許多文獻研究這些問題的計算方法。有限元方法提供了一流的技術，保護了全區的守恆性。然而，這些類型的方法通常是隱式的，使方法效率低。間斷有限元方法提供了一種對上述問題明確的和高效的計算方法，但他們是耗散，這意味著守恆性是不保留，或有嚴重的穩定性問題，即非物理和人工製造的數值解。 在這個項目中，我們將開發一種新的雜交計算方法去數值逼近上述問題。此外，我們將提供一個嚴格的數學證明去證明新方法的有效性。我們也將進行仔細研究，並通過大量的數值模擬和比較基準的問題去驗證這方法。 這方法可以看作是有限元方法和間斷 Galerkin方法之間的一種妥協， 它同時具有有限元方法和間斷 Galerkin方法的優點。 此外，這方法既穩定和最佳收斂。因此，它提供了一類新的穩定和準確的方法去求解波傳播和對流擴散問題。由於這方法的非耗散性質，這方法是非常適合去應用於需要較長的時間模擬。此外，這個項目開發的數學方法和工具將提供一個基礎，去開發由各種重要的應用產生的問題的保護守恆性的計算技術。

401010.label: Realisation of objectives
401010.value: We have successfully achieved all the objectives described in the proposed research. Firstly, we develop a new class of discontinuous Galerkin methods for solving the wave propagation problem and the convection-diffusion problem. The method is based on the discretization of some staggered grids. The resulting numerical schemes are able to preserve some of the physical laws arising from the partial differential equation. Secondly, we have successfully proved the stability of the methods. In particular, we have proved that the methods are stable in both the L2 norm and the energy norm. This is achieved by some carefully chosen local approximation spaces. Moreover, some mathematical tools are developed for carrying out the stability analysis. Thirdly, we have successfully proved the optimal convergence of the methods. In particular, we have proved that the methods have a convergence order k+1 in L2 norm and a convergence order k in energy norm when degree k polynomials are used in the local approximation space. Finally, we have carried out plenty of numerical experiments to validate the performance of the methods. Our numerical results show that the methods have the correct convergence order and the required conservation properties.

401010.label: Major findings and research outcome
401010.value: The proposed research has given a new class of discontinuous Galerkin methods for solving wave propagation problems and convection-diffusion problems. The solutions to these equations satisfy some important conservation properties. In terms of numerical approximation, it is well-known that the numerical solutions may not satisfy these conservation properties. One of the important contributions of the proposed research is that the numerical solutions obtained by the new schemes satisfy the required conservation properties. The key to the success of this is the use of a staggered grid. The staggered grid is a new design. There are typically two unknown functions involved in the problems considered in this project. These two unknown functions are approximated by using two different grids, namely, the staggered grid. By using this kind of technique, the numerical solutions satisfy the important conservation properties. Another important research outcome is the construction of a stable pair of finite element approximation spaces. By using the above mentioned staggered grid, there is no guarantee that the resulting method is stable. It is therefore one important task to construct stable pair of spaces. In particular, our pair of finite element spaces satisfy a staggered continuity property. More precisely, one of the unknown function is required to be continuous on a subset of cell edges while the other unknown function is required to be continuous on the complement of the above cell edges. The resulting spaces satisfy some inf-sup stability conditions. Hence, the resulting method is stable. Finally, one more advantage of using the above spaces is that the method becomes optimally convergent. In particular, one obtain convergence order that is comparable to the best approximation error. This property is highly desirable as it will ensure the accuracy of the numerical approximation.

401010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401010.value: The results of the proposed research are highly encouraging, and there are plenty of rooms for further research. In particular, the problems considered in the proposed research are linear problems. There are many important applications that are modeled by nonlinear equations. Hence, it is desirable to develop numerical schemes for nonlinear partial differential equations, that give numerical solutions with the correct conservation properties. The tools developed in the current project cannot be used directly for nonlinear problems. It is therefore necessary to introduce some new concepts in order to apply the staggered grid idea to nonlinear problem.

401010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401010.value: The proposed research has given a new class of numerical approximation techniques for solving a class of partial differential equations with commonly appear in real applications. It is therefore important to develop accurate and efficient approximation strategies to these equations. The novelty in the construction of these methods is that they will produce numerical approximate solutions having the correct conservation properties. These properties are highly desirable in practice. In addition, the approximation properties of the methods are mathematically justified. In particular, the stability and the convergence of the methods are proven mathematically. These results allow one to ensure that the numerical approximate solutions are accurate and will not prone to round off errors. Hence, the results of the proposed research have given an important class of numerical techniques with unique features.

401710.value: 分形上的邊界理論及分析

401710.label: Project Objectives
401710.value: Our investigation will focus mainly on connected self-similar $K$ that satisfy the open set condition. We want to find the admissible Markov chains on $K$, i.e., those chains whose Martin boundaries can be identified with $K$. The related Poisson boundary will also be considered. We propose to use the harmonic structure of the Martin boundary and the Poisson boundary to study the existence problem of the Laplacian on a self-similar set. We will seek additional conditions on the self-similar set or the Markov chain for this purpose. We also propose studying the problem in another direction: Approximate the fractal set with open domains from outside, and use the limit of the classical Laplacians as the Laplacian on $K$. We will apply the above results to study the intrinsic properties of the self-similar sets such as the spectral dimension, the walk dimension as well as the eigen-problem, the Green function, the heat kernel and the energy measure that arise from the Laplacian.

401710.label: Realisation of objectives
401710.value: Our goal was to identify the self-similar sets with the Martin boundaries of transient Markov chains, and to introduce the discrete potential theory on Markov chains to the self-similar sets. We used this to consider the existence of a Laplacian $Delta$, or more generally, a Dirichlet form on self-similar sets $K$. A self-similar set $K$ is defined by the limit set of an iterated function system, and the iteration is addressed by a symbolic space of finite words which form a tree. We introduced different Markov chains on such trees and study their limits (the Martin boundary). In particular, we considered two most basic situations, the Sierpinski gasket and the Hata tree [1,2], which revealed the essential features in this approach, and showed the compatibility with the known theory. We also studied another type of Markov chain on the symbolic space, which extended the Denker-Sato chain on the Sierpinski gasket to the most general setting [3]. These investigations set up a clear direction for the study of the class of post-critical finite self-similar sets. In another direction, we assume the existence of the Laplacian and Dirichlet forms on the fractal spaces, or more generally, on the metric measure space, and consider how the classical theory can be carried over. In [4] we studied the two-sided estimates of heat kernels with finite effective resistance. This setup is different from the above self-similar setting, and so is the associated Markov processes. It brings in another aspect of the analysis of fractals.

401710.label: Major findings and research outcome
401710.value: In [1], we defined a new Markov chain on the symbolic space representing the Sierpinski gasket (SG), and showed that the corresponding Martin boundary is homeomorphic to the SG while the minimal Martin boundary is the three vertices of the SG. In addition, the $P$-harmonic structure induced by the Markov chain coincides with the canonical one on the SG. In [2], we ran the same type of Markov chain on the symbolic space of the Hata tree $K$, a non-symmetric case. In this case, the Martin boundary ${mathcal M}$ is not identify with $K$, it is homeomorphic to the "trunk" of $K$, and the minimal Martin boundary is the three vertices of the trunk. Still, the class of P-harmonic functions on ${mathcal M}$ coincides with Kigami's class of harmonic functions on K. The two special cases in [1], [2] suggested another approach to consider the existence of Laplacian on those self-similar sets for which the problem is still not settled. In [3], we considered a more general Denker-Sato type Markov chain associated with the self-similar sets $K$ with the open set condition. The chain is defined on the augmented tree of a symbolic space. Such tree was introduced by Kaimanovich, it is hyperbolic in the sense of Gromov. We showed that the Martin boundary, the hyperbolic boundary and the self-similar set $K$ are homeomorphic. The hitting distribution of the chain was also obtained. It brought together the probabilistic, geometric and fractal considerations. In [4], we carried out another direction of investigation. We studied certain class of non-local regular Dirichlet forms on metric measure spaces, including fractal spaces. We used a purely analytic method such as the parabolic maximum principle. We deduced an off-diagonal upper bound of the heat kernel from the on-diagonal one under the volume regularity hypothesis, restriction of the jump kernel and the survival hypothesis. As an application, we obtain two-sided estimates of heat kernels for non-local regular Dirichlet forms with finite effective resistance, including settings with the walk dimension greater than 2.

401710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401710.value: Up to now, there are two basic approaches to construct the Laplacian on self-similar fractals: the discrete approximation on the p.c.f. fractals, as well as the probabilistic method on the finitely ramified fractals and the Sierpinski carpet. The approach in [1-3] using the Markov change offers a new way to look for the Laplacian and Dirichlet forms on a fractal set $K$. This is one of our future lines of investigation. On the other hand, by assuming the existence of the Laplacian, Dirichlet forms and harmonic structure, there is a wide scope of topics to be considered. Our investigation in [4] is related to diffusion and heat conduction in the general metric measure space. Some shaper estimate for the more specific cases are to be studied.

401710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401710.value: There is a lot interest to extend and assimilate the classical theories and ideas on analysis and probability theory to the fractal setting. One of the central questions is to establish the existence of the {it Laplace operator} on fractal sets. Another problem is to study the consequence and properties of the operator, for example, diffusion and heat conduction. In this project we identified certain classes of the self-similar sets and the boundaries of Markov chains. As the boundary theory is well connected with harmonic analysis, potential theory, as well as random walks on groups and graphs, we successfully integrated this theory into the study of fractals. In particular, by using this, we brought in a new method to study the Laplacian on fractals different from the existing approaches, which are still limited to small classes of fractal sets. In regard to the application of such operator, we studied the heat kernel on the general metric measure spaces, which include the classical Euclidean spaces and the fractal spaces.

401810.label: Project Title(Chinese)
401810.value: 光耦合機械諧振器的動力學和控制

401810.label: Project Objectives
401810.value: Establish an effective Hamiltonian of optomechanical resonators based on microscopic models of dielectric mirrors beyond the single-mode approximation and linear approximation. Determine the coherent transient dynamics of the mirror subjected to various input light fields. These include the effects of optical pulse sequences and nonclassical light fields. Identify quantum features of the motional states of the mirror arising from cavity QED interactions using atoms inside the cavity. In particular, determine what interaction schemes can efficiently generate non-classical states of motion.

401810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401810.value: Micromechanical oscillators can interact strongly with electromagnetic fields by radiation pressure. Such an optomechanical coupling not only is a key to access quantum effects in macroscopic systems, but also important for building precision measuring devices . We propose a theoretical research to address quantum dynamics and control in optomechanical resonators. Our focus is placed on the foundation of Hamiltonian models, and the dynamical response of movable cavity mirrors subjected to classical laser pulses and various quantum states of light. In addition, by incorporating techniques in cavity quantum electrodynamics, we will explore strategies and mechanisms of controlling quantum states of the mirror and cavity fields, as well as their quantum correlations. We expect our research will bring new insights of quantum mechanical effects of radiation pressure, which could pave the way for testing quantum theory in macroscopic systems. The knowledge would be a crucial step for developing novel applications in quantum information science and quantum limited metrology based on optomechanical coupling. 微機械振盪器可以和電磁場輻射壓力有強烈的相互作用。這種光學耦合不僅讓我們探討宏觀量子效應，也可以建設精密測量儀器。我們提出一個理論研究，以解決在這光耦合機械系統中的量子動力學問題。我們把重點放在基礎哈密頓模型以及腔鏡受到激光脈衝與不同光量子態的動態響應。通過整合腔量子電動力學的技術，我們將探討對控制鏡子和電磁場量子態的機制。我們期望這研究將帶來對輻射壓力的量子效應新的見解，並為量子理論在宏觀系統的測試鋪路。這些知識也將為開發量子信息和量子光學新的應用提供基礎。

401810.label: Realisation of objectives
401810.value: We have realized the three project objectives as follows: For the objective (1), we have established effective Hamiltonians of various optomechanical systems. These include an optomechanical cavity with a dielectric mirror, dielectric membrane, and a dielectric sphere. We have taken the fact that a moving electric dipole processes a magnetic moment, which may not be neglected in the regime of non-adiabatic dielectric motion. We developed a theory to incorporate the effects of such a magnetization into the optomechanical coupling beyond the single-mode adiabatic approximation and linear approximation. Specifically, we first derive the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of the classical counterpart of the system. The quantum theory is then obtained by canonical quantization of the Hamiltonian. To provide a microscopic details of our theory, we have generalized the Lorentz model to moving dielectric, and derived the corresponding optomechanical Hamiltonians. For the objective (2), we have investigated the dynamics of a movable mirror when the optomechanical cavity is driven by various types external light fields. Specifically, we have examined four configurations: (i) A large-detuned classical driving field with a modulated amplitude, (ii) classical chirped pulse, (iii) two classical fields of different frequencies, and (iv) single photon input. For (i) and (ii), we made used of the linearized theory to obtained the fluctuations properties of the state of the mirror's motion. For (iv), the single photon drive is an important example of nonclassical light, and we have solved the single photon scattering problem fully quantum mechanically and exactly. For the objective (3), we have identified the quantum features of motional states of the mirror due to various optomechanical coupling schemes. This is achieved by studying the solutions of the system subjected to various driving schemes as indicated in (i-iv) above. Specifically, the quantum features we focused on included the quadrature squeezed states, motional dark states, and the influence of two-photon scattering. Our study has also explored various effects of an atom inside an optomechanical cavity. We have examined the ways to induce an effective coupling between atom and phonons (mirror's vibration). The very different dynamical time scales between an atom and mirror motion is a key obstacle to achieve a coupling directly, but we find that an indirect coupling can be possible by external driving fields via resonance. The investigation of optomechanics with a two-level atom is a part of the graduate student Mr. Xu Gao Feng's M. Phil. thesis.

401810.label: Major findings and research outcome
401810.value: Our major findings have been published in 7 PRA papers. We provide a summary below: (1) We discovered a mechanism to generate quadrature-squeezed states of a moving mirror in a Fabry-Perot cavity by using parametric resonance. This is achieved by using an external field with a large detuning and a modulating field amplitude at a frequency matching the frequency shift of the mirror. [PRA 83, 033820 (2011)] (2) We found a cooling mechanism based on the response of a harmonically confined mirror to an optical pulse in cavity optomechanics. We showed that when the pulsed coupling strength takes the form of a chirped pulse, thermal fluctuations of the mirror can be significantly transferred to the cavity field. [PRA 84, 053838 (2011)] (3) We formulated an effective Hamiltonian to describe the interaction between a moving dielectric membrane and radiation pressure. Our theory was established without making use of the single-mode adiabatic approximation, and linear approximation and hence, it enables us to incorporate multimode effects in cavity optomechanics. Our Hamiltonian theory has also been generalized to a moving and spinning dielectric sphere problem, and we predict that a geometrical quantum phase can be gained by the sphere moving in a light field. [PRA 84, 023812 (2011); PRA 86, 033807 (2012)] (4) We have calculated analytically the spectrum of single-photon scattering in a cavity optomechanical system. Our solution indicated the relationship between the spectral features and the interaction strength of radiation pressure per photon. In addition, our work also clarify the conditions under which the phonon sidebands are visible and the photon-state frequency shift can be resolved. [PRA 85, 025803 (2012)]. (5) We obtained an exact analytical solution of the two-photon scattering in a cavity optomechanical system. The long-time solution reveals the detailed physical transitions for the two photons in the scattering process. In particular, we characterize the photon correlation by calculating the two-photon joint spectrum of the long-time state, and the equal-time second-order correlation function. We found that photon blockade effect is strongly modulated by the phonon sideband resonance. [PRA 87, 043809 (2013)]. (6) We discovered a class of dark motional states when an optomechanical cavity is driven by two external fields of different frequencies, i.e., the system is decoupled from the external fields. The decoupling is a quantum interference effect arising from mechanical coherence in cavity optomechanics. We have determined the properties of dark states and proposed how they can be generated by optical pumping. [PRA 87, 053849 (2013)].

401810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401810.value: Our work has the potential for further development in the following directions: (1) The Hamiltonian developed in this research has provided an approach to formulate optomechanics involving moving dielectric beyond single-mode adabatic approximation. The Hamilonian can be used to further explore the physical effects of multi-mode problems. In addition, the formalism may be extended to media with finite conductivities, where the noninertial effects of quantum vaccum radiation due to dynamical Casimir effect in a spinning sphere can be studied. (2) Most of our analysis of the response of optomechanical systems to external fields has been applied to linearized regime where quantum fluctuations are relatively small. It will be useful to extend our work beyond the linearized regime. Specifically, the quantum counterparts of nonlinear dynamical features exhibited in the classical systems (such as limit cycles and chaotic motion) at a sufficiently strong driving would be interesting to learn about the quantum-classical correspondence, non-classicality of macroscopic systems, and quantum control.

401810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401810.value: In this research project we have studied theoretically the effects of radiation pressure force on the quantum motion of a dielectric object, which can be a movable mirror in a cavity, a vibrating membrane, or a spinning sphere, and the motion of the dielectric object can in turn affect the properties of radiation. Our work has developed a formalism of optomechanics directly from fundamental physical laws. Such a formalism is important because it generates rigorously the equations governing the motion of the electromagnetic field and dielectric object. With this formalism, we learn more about the nature of optomechanical coupling, and so enabling further investigations of optomechanics beyond the previously studied regimes. In particular, the optomechanical system can help us to understand quantum theory in macroscopic physical systems. Our work has also discovered various interaction schemes that demonstate how light can control the quantum motion of a dielectric and vice versa. This helps us to identify different effects of optomechanical coupling, and the knowledge would be useful to develop hybrid quantum imformational device involving both opto and mechanical degrees of freedom.

402210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402210.value: This project is to study the synthetic methods, structures and reactivities of novel germanium(I) compounds. Germanium(I) compounds will be prepared by the reduction of organogermanium(I) chlorides with alkaline metals. Bulky ligands will be used to stabilized the germanium(I) center and prevent it from oligomerizing or further oxidation. These bulky ligands are currently developed in our group and will be used as supporting ligands in the synthesis of this type of compound. Other synthetic methods to obtain stable germanium(I) compounds will be explored. The bonding interactions and the reativities of this class of compounds are of great interest in this field. We will determine the structures of the germanium(I) compound by spectroscopic methods and X-ray crystallography. The major focus will be on the reactivities of this type of germanium(I) compound. Germanium(I) compound will be acted as an important precursor for synthesis of other novel germanium compounds such as the germanium analogues of carboxylic acid, acid anhydride and aldehyde. 這個項目的工作主要探討鍺(I)有機金屬化合物之合成、結構及活性研究。鍺(I)化合物將從鍺(II)金屬有機化合物及鹼金屬反應還原得到。巨大的有機配體將用於穩定該頪化合物，以防止其聚合或進一步氧化。在我們進行的研究工作中, 現在正用一些大配體作為輔助穩定作用，我們將會研究其他的合成方法，我們對這類的化合物的活性及結構有極大興趣。這工作將會用波譜方法及X光晶體學去找出這些鍺(I)化合物的結構。焦點在於這類鍺(I)化合物之活性。這類化合物可用作合成其他有機鍺的相似物如：羧酸、無水酸及醛。

402210.label: Realisation of objectives
402210.value: This work has developed the synthesis of a bulky ligands for preparing the precursor compound organogermanium chloride. This organogermanium chloride compound served as a crucial precursor for the synthesis of unstable germanium(I) compounds. The germanium(I) compounds have been successfully synthesized by the reduction of organogermanium chloride with alkali metals (lithium or potassium) or magnesium. This germanium(I) compound exists as a dimeric compound and stabilized by the nitrogen-bearing group within the bulky ligand. This work has experienced some difficulties in the isolation of the pure germanium(I) compounds. The isolation of pure germanium(I) compound has led to the investigation of the structures of these compounds by X-ray crystallography and spectroscopic analysis. The reactivity of the germanium(I) compound prepared has been carried out. Some of the results are reported in the published paper. Using the germanium(I) compound, a novel germanium analogue of dithiocarboxylic acid anhydride has been synhthesizes and structurally characterised.

The germanium(I) compounds have been successfully synthesized by the reduction of organogermanium chloride with alkali metals (lithium or potassium) or magnesium. This work has experienced some difficulties in the isolation of the pure germanium(I) compounds. The difficulty is the separation of mixed germanium(I) compounds in the reduction reaction. The structures and spectroscopic properties of the new germanium(I) compounds were investigated by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (proton, carbon-13, phosphorus-31 and tin-119) and X-ray crystallography. The reactivity of the novel germanium compounds has been investigated.This germanium(I) compound can undergo oxidative-addition reaction. The reaction of germanium(I) compound with azobenzene afforded the 1,2-digermylene hydrazinide. It can also act as a two-electron ligand coordinates to compound such as iron-carbonyl. This germanium(I) compound reacts with elemental sulphur to give an unprecedented germanium analogue of a dithiocarboxylic acid anhydride.

By using bulky ligand bearing a pyridyl group, the germanium(I) compound formed can be stabilized. The germanium(I) compound was prepared from the reduction of an organogermanium(II) chloride with alkali metals (lithium or potassium) or magnesium. The reduction reaction produced mixtures of germanium(I) compounds. The isolation and separation of the extremely air-sensitive germanium(I) compounds experienced great difficulty and much effort have been spent on the isolation of the compound. 402310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402310.value: Geometrical frustration appears in a wide variety of solid states and induces many novel and complex phenomena. It is caused by the geometrical properties of the crystal lattice (or the presence of conflicting atomic forces) that forbid simultaneous minimization of the interaction energies acting at a given site. A simple example is antiferromagnetically interacting spins in a triangular arrangement. In order to minimize energy, each spin prefers to align opposite to its neighbors, but if two of them align anti-parallel, the rest one is frustrated. Recent progress in material synthesize of geometrically frustrated systems put them into spotlight again because many fascinating magnetic phenomena, such as ferromagnetism, superconductivity, and magnetic monopole, were observed. The observations manifest a clearly important role played by the geometrical frustration hence call for understanding both the nature of frustration and various (magnetic) orders in these materials. In this project, we plan to carry out a systematic study on the geometrically frustrated systems, and explore the nature of magnetism and superconductivity in these systems. This is a difficult task because both quantum many-body effects and the Coulomb interaction needed to be treated properly, and one must deal with interplay of all interactions in order to capture physical properties correctly. We shall investigate the spin-spin correlation and their corresponding structure factor, spin susceptibility, and pairing correlation by performing extensive numerical calculations such as quantum Monte Carlo simulations and exact diagonalization studies, to determine the phase diagram and compared with structural and spectroscopic information obtained experimentally. These non-perturbative approaches are necessary to clarify some ambiguities and unresolved issues in some challenging novel materials. Specifically, we select four systems as sketched in Fig. 1 to investigate. By varying hopping integral t’, we study the dominant magnetic order and superconductivity during the crossover (or transition) from a fully-frustrated system to a non-frustrated system. Moreover, based on our systemic studies on magnetic orders in different kinds of geometrically frustrated systems, we will try to identify a physical quantity the measure of the frustration. Our recent success in double triangular and honeycomb layers put us in a promising start and our team is confident in completing the project successfully. Our findings will provide important information to condensed matter fields. For example, the investigation on the origin of ferromagnetism may lead to possible controllability of ferromagnetism in novel materials, which is one of the key factors in the application of spintronics. 这个项目对一些几何组错系统进行系统地研究，以探讨它们的磁性和超导性。

402410.label: Project Objectives
402410.value: Formulation and numerical calculation of electron spin resonance signals of an NV center in diamond coupled to a random distribution of nuclear spins. Multi-pulse electron-spin-flip sequences will be considered to elongate the electron spin coherence time by dynamical decoupling so that the coherent fingerprint oscillations of a nuclear spin bond is well pronounced. This part of research will lay the foundation of the imaging and quantum control schemes. Development of a novel scheme of atomic-scale magnetic resonance imaging. A library of oscillation fingerprints will be built for coherent bonds at different positions and orientations, under different magnetic fields, and in the control of different dynamical decoupling sequences. This library will then be used for detection and characterization of coherent nuclear spin bonds embedded in a nuclear spin bath. Schemes of two-qubit gates on single nuclear-spin bonds for scalable solid-state quantum computing at room temperature. The basic idea is: The coherent pair-wise flip-flop of a nuclear-spin bond is conditioned on the center electron spin state, so a desired two-qubit gate can be realized by flipping the center spin at a designed timing. Simulation and understanding of the effects of measurement errors, uncertainty in system parameters (such as hyperfine coupling coefficients), extra decoherence mechanisms, and other uncontrolled factors, on the fidelity of imaging and quantum gates. Such study will deliver experimental schemes feasible under realistic conditions.

402410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402410.value: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is widely used in structure analysis, medical diagnosis, magnetometry, and quantum computing. However, the low sensitivity of conventional NMR limits its application. Magnetic resonance force microscopy (MRFM) can produce nanoscale three-dimensional imaging with single-electron or million-nucleus sensitivity, but requires vacuum and cryogenic conditions and has not reached single-nucleus sensitivity. Optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) can detect single electron spins in molecules or solid defects and in turn single nuclear spins strongly coupled to the electrons. ODMR signals of nuclei not so close to the electron, however, are concealed by noises of nuclear spin baths. In this project, we will develop a scheme of atomic-scale magnetic resonance imaging with single-nucleus sensitivity using ODMR of single nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. The key idea is to sense a bonded pair of nuclear spins instead of individual ones. Under a medium to strong magnetic field, the center electron spin decoherence is caused mainly by pairwise flop-flops of nuclear spins surrounding the center. Our preliminary research shows that a bond of nuclear spins is distinguished from the background by its coherent oscillation imprinted on the electron spin decoherence, even when the bond is well separated from the center. The oscillation fingerprints have atomic sensitivity on the position and orientation of the bond. To distinguish the fingerprint oscillations better, we propose to suppress the decoherence due to incoherent pairs by an in-situ technique, namely, dynamical decoupling through frequent flips of the center electron spin. As a spin-off, coherent nuclear spin bonds will be studied for two-qubit quantum gates, which can be implemented by rotating the center electron spin at a designed timing, since the oscillation of a coherent bond is conditioned on the center spin states. The theoretical tools include the quantum many-body theory for spin bath dynamics and the dynamical decoupling theory, recently developed by PI's group. The theoretical research will be compared with experimental results from CoI's group and deliver new experimental schemes. The long-term objectives are a new direction of atomic-scale magnetic resonance imaging and scalable quantum computing with single nuclear spins in solids (in contrast to ensemble quantum computing by liquid NMR). Moreover, the scheme may be extended to analyze structures of single macromolecules, using isotope-labeled bonds as indicators. The research will have impact on several interdisciplinary fields including magnetic resonance spectroscopy, quantum computing and molecular structure analysis. 核磁共振在結構分析、醫學診斷、磁測量、以及量子計算等領域有廣泛應用。但是傳統技術的低靈敏度限制了核磁共振的應用。磁共振力顯微可以達到對單個電子或數百萬核自旋實現納米尺度的三維成像，但是卻要求真空、極低溫等苛刻條件，而且還遠遠不能達到單個核自旋的靈敏度。光學探測磁共振可以探測到單分子或者固體裡面單個缺陷上的一個電子自旋，也能檢測到和該電子自旋有強耦合的單個核自旋。但是離電子自旋較遠的核自旋卻因為背景噪音的影響而難以被探測到。 在本項目中，我們將發展用金剛石中單個氮-空位中心的光探測磁共振來實現具有單核自旋靈敏級別的磁測量之理論方案。我們設想的核心思想是探測一對核自旋和不是探測單個的核自旋。在較強的磁場下，氮-空位中心電子自旋的退相干主要由配對的核自旋翻轉導致的。我們的初步研究表明，在一對碳-碳化學鍵兩端的核自旋會和其他的核自旋對有非常不同的性質，表現在它會導致電子自旋信號上強烈的具有指紋特性的振盪，哪怕這對核自旋遠離中心電子也是如此。這些具有指紋特徵的振盪對核自旋對的位置和取向有原子分辨率的依賴。為了是指紋特徵更加明顯，我們還建議用和磁共振譜技術直接兼容的動力學去耦的辦法延長電子自旋的相干時間。另外，我們可以利用該核自旋對來實現通過中心電子自旋來控制的雙量子比特邏輯門。 我們將用到的理論工具包括自旋庫的多體量子理論和動力學去耦理論。本研究組對這些理論都有前期研究和準備。理論研究也將和合作者的實驗對比，並提出新的實驗方案。 本項目的長遠目標是原子尺度磁成像技術以及基於單個核自旋的可擴展的固態量子計算（作為對比，此前的液態核磁共振量子計算方案是基於自旋系宗的，也因而是無法擴展的）。進一步，本項目也可能發展出單分子結構分析技術手段。總之，可以預計本研究可能對數個交叉學科產生影響，包括磁共振頻譜學、量子計算、以及結構分析等。

402410.label: Realisation of objectives
402410.value: We have achieved the objectives of this project by developing a novel scheme of ultrasensitive magnetometry of nuclear spins in diamond, implementing the scheme by collaboration with experimental teams, theoretical design and experimental observation of control of nuclear spin dynamics via flips of a central electron spin, and extending the magnetometry to a new concept of detecting many-body physics by central spin decoherence. We have formulated a microscopic theory on decoherence of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center spins in the baths of C-13 nuclear spins. We calculated the microscopic hyperfine interaction between the NV centers and C-13 spins using the density functional theory and then numerically simulated the quantum dynamics of the coupled spin systems. We designed various dynamical decoupling pulse sequences to enhance the signals of nuclear spin clusters and established the finger-print library for different nuclear spin clusters on the decoherence profiles of the NV center spin. Using this library, we performed double-blinded numerical experiments to demonstrate the feasibility of detecting single nuclear spin pairs and single-molecule NMR using NV centers in diamond. We then pushed for collaboration with experimentalists in Stuttgart and in the University of Science and Technology of China to realize the scheme. We proposed the experiments, analyzed the experimental data, and numerically studied the realistic conditions in the experiments. The experiments achieved the world record sensitivity of single nuclear spin detection and demonstrated the first single-nucleus NMR. We further studied the control of nuclear spin dynamics by pulsed flips of the central spins and predicted the anomalous decoherence effect on the NV center electron spin. Then we collaborated with experimentalists in the University of Science and Technology to observe the predicted effect. Furthermore, we extended the scheme of ultrasensitive magnetometry (viewed as probe of few-body physics) to the concept of detecting many-body physics in environments using central spin decoherence. This study led to two important results. One is high-temperature quantum criticality revealed by spin echo; another one is an approach to thermodynamics in the complex plane of physical parameters, especially time-domain phase transitions. These works are of timely influence in the field of quantum coherence control and detection using solid-state single spin systems, as evidenced by publications in high-impact journals (2 in Nature Nanotechnology, 2 in Physical Review Letters, and 1 in Nature Communications).

Multi-pulse electron-spin-flip sequences will be considered to elongate the electron spin coherence time by dynamical decoupling so that the coherent fingerprint oscillations of a nuclear spin bond is well pronounced. This part of research will lay the foundation of the imaging and quantum control schemes.

Development of a novel scheme of atomic-scale magnetic resonance imaging. A library of oscillation fingerprints will be built for coherent bonds at different positions and orientations, under different magnetic fields, and in the control of different dynamical decoupling sequences. This library will then be used for detection and characterization of coherent nuclear spin bonds embedded in a nuclear spin bath.

Schemes of two-qubit gates on single nuclear-spin bonds for scalable solid-state quantum computing at room temperature. The basic idea is: The coherent pair-wise flip-flop of a nuclear-spin bond is conditioned on the center electron spin state, so a desired two-qubit gate can be realized by flipping the center spin at a designed timing.

Simulation and understanding of the effects of measurement errors, uncertainty in system parameters (such as hyperfine coupling coefficients), extra decoherence mechanisms, and other uncontrolled factors, on the fidelity of imaging and quantum gates. Such study will deliver experimental schemes feasible under realistic conditions.

402410.label: Major findings and research outcome
402410.value: We proposed a novel scheme of atomic-scale magnetometry of nuclear spin clusters and NMR of single molecules via spin decoherence of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond under many-pulse dynamical decoupling control [Nature Nanotechnology 6, 242 (2011)]. This theoretical work has stimulated a great deal of experimental investigation (in Harvard, TU Deflt, Stuttgart, etc). In collaboration with us, the Stuttgart group has demonstrated NMR detection of a single C-13 nuclear spin by many-pulse dynamical decoupling control over a nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond [Nature Nanotechnology 7, 657 (2012)]. These works mark milestones toward the ultimate goal of single-molecule NMR, a top challenge in research of magnetic resonance spectroscopy. We studied the control of nuclear spin dynamics via flips of the central electron spin. We predicted [Phys. Rev. Lett. 106, 217205 (2011)]and experimentally observed [Nature Communications 2, 570 (2011)] the anomalous decoherence effect due to such control. Most recently, we extended the concept of magnetometry (as a probe of few-body physics) to detection of many-body physics of environments by central spin decoherence. We found that quantum criticality at high temperature can be revealed by central spin decoherence under spin echo control [ New Journal of Physics 15, 043032 (2013)]. We discovered a deep link between central spin decoherence and thermodynamic partition functions of the environments in the complex plane of physical parameters [Physical Review Letters 109, 185701 (2012)]. This finding makes it possible for the first time to observe Lee-Yang zeros (which were discovered by T. D. Lee and C. N. Yang in 1952 but have never been experimentally observed). We further proposed a new concept of phase transitions, namely, time-domain phase transitions [Physical Review Letters 109, 185701 (2012)], which may have important applications in studying thermodynamics of small systems and quantum quench dynamics in cold atom systems.

402410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402410.value: Two new fields have been opened by this project. One is the study of many-body physics using the central spin decoherence as a probe. In particular, time-domain phase transitions and thermodynamics in the complex plane of physical parameters have a wealth of new physics for further study. Actually, we have been awarded a new RGC/GRF project to investigate these phenomena (Ref. # 401413. "Time-domain phase transitions in environments detected by central spin decoherence") Another important field is to apply the ultrasensitive magnetometry to realistic researches (e.g., on biological systems and chemical reactions). With PI as the Principle Coordinator, a RGC/CRF project has been funded on this direction (Ref. # CUHK4/CRF/12G "Multifunctional Ultrasensitive Sensing with Hybrid Gold-Diamond Nano-Systems").

402410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402410.value: NMR (nuclear magnetic resonance) has been widely used in chemical analysis, medical diagnosis, quantum computing research, etc. The crown-jewel challenge of NMR is to push the sensitivity to the single-molecule level. In this project we invented a novel scheme of single-molecule NMR, based on measuring decoherence of a nitrogen-center spin in diamond under multi-pulse dynamical decoupling. In collaboration with experimentalists, we achieved the world record sensitivity of sensing single nuclear spins in diamond and realized the structure analysis of single nuclear spin clusters in diamond. These works mark milestones toward the ultimate goal of single-molecule NMR, a top challenge in research of magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Then we discovered a deep link between central spin decoherence and thermodynamic partition functions of the environments in the complex plane of physical parameters. This finding makes it possible for the first time to observe Lee-Yang zeros (which were discovered by T. D. Lee and C. N. Yang in 1952 but have never been experimentally observed). We further proposed a new concept of phase transitions, namely, time-domain phase transitions, which may have important applications in studying thermodynamics of small systems and quantum quench dynamics in cold atom systems.

402710.label: Project Objectives
402710.value: We plan to synthesize designed macrocyclic ligands bearing ethynyl functional groups for the generation of a series of heterometal silver ethynide complexes, in which different metallic ions occupy the central cavities of the macrocycles and the ethynide group binds to several silver(I) centers. A systematic study will be initiated to synthesize large silver clusters with encapsulated polyoxometalate anions based on the multinuclear silver(I)-ethynide supramolecular synthon that we had established in our completed project GRF CUHK 402405. We shall explore the controlled assembly of the above multinuclear building blocks in order to construct discrete molecules, as well as one-, two-, and three-dimensional coordination networks. Variation of optimized reaction conditions in aqueous and non-aqueous media will be attempted.

402710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402710.value: Silver Ethynide Complexes Containing Polyoxometalates and Oxometalates Polyoxoanions of the early transition elements (V, Nb, Ta; Cr, Mo, W) in Group 4 and 5 of the Periodic Table, known as polyoxometalates (POMs), exhibit unrivaled structural diversity combined with a wide range of unique physical properties and nuclearities ranging from 6 to 368 metal ions in a single molecule. Based on our recent finding that POMs can be embedded in silver ethynide cages, and smaller oxovanadates (OVs) can serve as templates with phosphonate-functionized OVs as robust structural components for building up multinuclear silver (I)-ethynide cluster shells, it seems feasible to construct new types of silver(I)-ethynide clusters based on a plethora of oxometalates (OMs) and POMs as template anions and/or shell components. For example, the arsonate-functionized polyoxomolybdates [Mo4O8(O3AsC6H5)4]4-, [Mo4O8(O3AsC6H4NH2)4]4-, [Mo5O11(O3AsC6H4OH)5]5- and [Mo4O10(O3AsC6H3NO2OH)4]4- have been used as building blocks for the construction of metal cluster coordination complexes. The reactions of this type of POMs with silver ethynide in the presence of other silver salts will be carried out to generate a new family of heterometallic cluster complexes.

402710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402710.value: The present proposal is concerned with a systematic investigation of the designed assembly of novel high-nuclearity silver cluster complexes by combining the multinuclear silver-ethynide supramolecular synthon and related with oxometalates, polyoxometalates, phosphonates and various ancillary anionic species as structure-building units, and the synthesis of new silver-organic framework complexes that incorporate carbon-rich ethynide ligands and an angular linker such as the 1,3-diphenyl group, a flexible linker such as the methylene group, or a rotary linker such as the 1,1'-ferrocenyl group. The results obtained have significantly advanced our current understanding regarding the construction of argentophilicity-induced organic-inorganic networks in one- to three dimensions, the utility of multinuclear metal-ligand supramolecular synthons in large cluster synthesis, and controlled supramolecular assembly based on the principles of crystal engineering.

402810.label: Project Title(Chinese)
402810.value: 以五元環為特徵的N型有機半導體新材料及其在有機太陽能電池和薄膜晶體管中的應用

402810.label: Project Objectives
402810.value: To synthesize a series of cyclopenta-fused polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, which feature five-membered rings and are rationally designed to function as n-type organic semiconductors. To characterize the electronic structure and molecular assembly of these molecules. To deposit highly ordered films of these molecules and in this way fabricate n-channel organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) with high charge carrier mobility. To fabricate bulk heterojunction organic solar cells using these n-type semiconductors as electron acceptors. To characterize the device performance of the OTFTs and organic solar cells and to elucidate the fundamental links between chemical structures, molecular assemblies and electrical properties for these designed materials.

402810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402810.value: 有機半導體材料在電子及光電器件中具有廣泛的應用。其中，有機光伏太陽能電池直接把太陽光轉化為電能，有希望成為大規模獲得廉價清潔能源的技術，以滿足人類日益增長的能源需求並應對全球暖化的困境。而有機薄膜晶體管則是有機電子器件中不可或缺的結構單元，是製造廉價的大面積柔性電子器件的基礎。有機半導體材料基於不同的電荷載體通常可以分為P型（電子傳輸型）和N型（空穴傳輸型）兩類。有機光伏太陽能電池和有機薄膜晶體管的發展都需要高性能的P型和N型有機半導體材料，但是N型有機半導體的發展卻落後於P型材料。 為應對這一挑戰，我們計劃研究一類新型的N型有機半導體材料，旨在研製出高性能的有機光伏太陽能電池和有機薄膜晶體管。這一類新型有機半導體材料在分子結構上以五元環為特徵。這一獨特的設計是受到富勒烯的結構-性能關係的啟發而來，並得到電化學實驗和量子化學理論計算的支持。由於比迄今為止在有機光伏太陽能電池中表現最佳的N型有機半導體材料PCBM具有更高的最低空軌道能級，我們設計的這些N型有機半導體材料將有可能在有機光伏太陽能電池中實現更高的開路電壓。我們計劃合成這些分子，研究其電子結構和分子組裝方式，並探索它們在N溝道薄膜晶體管和有機光伏太陽能電池中的應用。我們將評價這些新型有機半導體材料在有機太陽能電池和薄膜晶體管的表現，並結合其分子結構及堆砌方式來探討結構與性能的基本關係。 我們提出的這項研究計劃為探索有機半導體材料的結構性能關係提供了有意義的研究對象，它的成功將為設計有機電子材料帶來新的思路，通過這項研究開發出的新穎的N型有機半導體材料將有可能為高性能的有機太陽能電池和薄膜晶體管開闢新的方向，並最終促進有重要應用的新技術的開發。

402810.label: Realisation of objectives
402810.value: We have successfully realized the following objectives. 1. We synthesized a series of cyclopenta-fused polycyclic arenes. To achieve effective molecular packing and better understanding of structure-property relationship, we tuned the original molecular designs by varying substituting groups. 2. We characterized these compounds in terms of molecular and electronic structures as well as supramolecular structures in the solid state. 3. We successfully fabricated n-channel organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) from some of these compounds and achieved field effect mobility as high as 0.1 cm2/Vs. 4. We fabricated bulk heterojunction organic solar cells using some of these compounds as electron acceptors. 5. We characterized the device performance of the OTFTs and organic solar cells and to studied the fundamental links between chemical structures, molecular assemblies and electrical properties. By realization of the above objectives, we have developed a new group of n-type organic semiconductors that have cyclopentadienyl moieties as a key building block.

402810.label: Major findings and research outcome
402810.value: In this project, we developed a group of new n-type semiconductors with a cyclopenta-fused polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (CP-PAH) backbone and achieved electron mobility much higher than that of the recently reported CP-PAH molecules. The most successful organic semiconductor developed in this project is a derivative of cyclopent[hi]aceanthrylene, which functions as an ambipolar semiconductor (both n- and p-type) in organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) exhibiting field effect mobility of 0.1 cm2/Vs for both electrons and holes. The paper reporting this material (Chemical Communication, 2013, 49, 4301–4303) has already been cited for 11 times since its publication in 2013. This cyclopent[hi]aceanthrylene derivative was also applied as a secondary acceptor in organic photovoltaic solar cells, and enhanced the power conversion efficiency of a P3HT:PC61BM bulk heterojunction solar cell from 3.4% to 4.3%. With these findings, this study demonstrates that the cyclopentadienyl moiety is a useful building block for n-type organic semiconductors. This project has led to 2 publications, one manuscript in preparation and 2 presentations at international conferences. Moreover, one PhD student, who graduated in July 2013, was trained in this project. These outcomes are detailed in Part C.

402810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402810.value: On the basis of the findings from this project and recent reports from other research groups, polycyclic arenes containing fused five-membered rings have been recognized as promising candidates for new n-type organic semiconductors. However, the number of this kind of organic semiconductors is still quite limited. In order to explore polycyclic arenes with unprecedented arrangement of five-membered rings, it is necessary develop new synthetic methods for these compounds. Further study on synthesis of such compounds is in progress in our laboratory.

402810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402810.value: With the financial support from the General Research Fund CUHK 402810, we conducted an interdisciplinary study to develop a novel family of n-type organic semiconductors, which are polycyclic arenes containing fused five-membered rings. This project focused on synthesis, electronic structures, molecular packing and two kinds organic electronic devices, namely organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) and organic photovoltaic solar cells. The best organic semiconductor developed in this project led to high-performance ambipolar OTFTs, and enhanced the power conversion efficiency of a benchmark organic solar cell. This project also led to better understanding on structure-property relationship for organic semiconductors. This work together with the recent studies by other groups have demonstrated that polycyclic arenes containing fused five-membered rings are promising candidates for n-type organic semiconductors with high performance in organic electronic devices.

403110.label: Project Objectives
403110.value: To establish separation results applicable to families of both convex and nonconvex sets. To establish approximate Lagrange/KKT rules for optimal/approximate solutions to multiobjective optimization problems. To identify constraint qualifications for stable Farkas Lemma and the total Lagrange duality. To establish the Ekeland variational principle for vector-valued functions.

403110.label: Realisation of objectives
403110.value: In this completed project we have achieved all objectives in full by employing the advanced variational analysis techniques in terms of coderivatives and various kinds of tangent/normal cones in carrying out our study for multiobjective optimization problems especially the problem of minimizing a function from a Banach space (or Asplund space) to partially ordered Banach space (POB) with geometric constraints and conical inequality constraints. We have particualrly extended the Fermat Rule, the Lagrange and KKT (Karush-Kuhn-Tucker) rules in the general context. As fundamental tools and also with independent theoretical interests, we have extended the famous Ekeland variational priciple and the Separation Theorems in Functional Analysis in the vector-valued setting covering the classical convex separation theorems, the approximate projection theorem, as well as the extremal principles developed by Mordukhovich and others. There are eight journal publications solely or partially supported by this project with the majority of them published in Siopt or Math Programming.

403110.label: Major findings and research outcome
403110.value: Embracing all existing convex separation theorems, approximate projection theorems as well as the generalized extremal principles, we have established an unified separation theorem which concerns with n-many closed (not necessarily convex) subsets of Banach space X (or of more special type such as an Asplund or Hilbert space) and we consider a pair of ‘conjugate numbers’ p, q to measure the distance between elements of the product of n-many copies of X or that in the dual. For the sake of simplicity in presentation, we report here only the simplest case: p=1, and A, B are closed sets with a, b respectively from A, B such that d(a,b)= d(A,B). We show that there exists Clarke normal functional a* to A at a, of unit norm such that –a* is Clarke normal to B at b and such that is the norm of b-a. We have shown by applying our results (a special case of which is reported in the above paragraph) together with Ekeland type variational techniques) the existence of $varepsilon$-Pareto solutions in vector optimization, and established rules of Lagrange type and Farkas lemma. To cater for more general situations, our multifunctions F [into (subsets) of a partially ordered Banach space (Y, K) with convex cone K] need not be from a Banach space, e.g., let F be a set-valued function from a complete metric space M to the power set of Y. We have established that, for any pair of a positive number and a convex subset of K missing the origin satisfying some reasonable conditions there exists a nature partial ordering in M defined in terms of this pair together with F) such that dom(F) has the domination property in the sense that each point in dom(F) is minorized by a minimal element of dom(F). This abstract principle has been applied to various situations such as in getting error bound results in connection with inequality/equality systems defined by finitely many and even infinitely many proper lower semicontinuous functions on Banach spaces or some other subclass of spaces. In many important cases, sharp upper bounds can be explicitly then given (in terms of some known parameters and the starting points satisfying suitable conditions such as some approximate solutions) for algorithms of Gauss-newton type.

403110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403110.value: Further applications are being explored especially in regard with the stability and/or global aspect of "fractioanl" or Holder type error bounds.

403110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403110.value: Some well known fundamental results in functional analysis and convex analysis theory are improved and extended in this completed project from the classical smooth or convex case to the nonsmooth and nonconvex case: we established a 'unified separation theorem' for any closed sets in Banach spaces from which one deduced (as corollaries): the classical convex separation theorems, the Bishop-Phelps Theorem, the Approximate Projection Theorem as well as the Extremal and the Generalized Extremal Principles of Mordukovich et al. We have also applied our results in providing optimality conditions for approximate Pareto solutions of constraint vector optimization problems for which we also gave a vairational principle of Ekeland type. For some subclasses of problems including the semi-infinite or infinite programming problems, conic inequality problems, convex-composite problems and convex inclusion problems (involving nonconvex but smooth functions) etc, we have done error bound or convergence analysis. In particular we relax the Robinson surjectivity assumptions in establishing the convergence of the iterative sequences generated by the Gauss-Newton method.

403210.label: Project Objectives
403210.value: To synthesize and characterize functional microgel particles for use as particulate emulsifiers. To formulate the HIPEs stabilized solely by the synthesized microgel particles. To produce functionalized porous materials by templating the structure of microgel particle-stabilized HIPEs. 403210.label: Realisation of objectives
403210.value: There are six objectives in this project and the details of the realization related to each objective are as follows: 1. To synthesize and characterize functional microgel particles for use as particulate emulsifiers. A series of soft particles, including poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM)-based microgels, protein nanoparticles and polyurethane (PU)-based nanoparticles were prepared and employed as the effective emulsifiers for formulation the particle-stabilized emulsions. 2. To formulate the HIPEs stabilized solely by the synthesized microgel particles. We have successfully formulated the HIPEs stabilized solely by the synthesized PNIPAM-based microgels, bovine serum albumin (BSA) protein nanoparticles, polyurethane (PU)-based nanoparticles, or lignin nanoparticles. Furthermore, we have extended our study on the production of HIPEs stabilized by two different kinds of particles, which open a door to make functional materials. 3. To produce functionalized porous materials by templating the structure of microgel particle-stabilized HIPEs. A series of soft particle-stabilized HIPEs have been produced and subsequently used as templates to fabricate three dimensional, hierarchical porous materials, protein scaffolds, Janus microspheres with multihollow structures, and nitrogen-rich carbon aerogel. 4. To characterize the structure, morphology, permeability, and mechanical properties of the porous materials. The structure and morphology including the pore size, compressibility, internal structure and permeability of the resultant porous materials have been well characterized by different techniques to understand the influences of parameters on the HIPEs formation and consequently on the structure of the resulting materials. 5. To test the applicability of fabricated porous materials, particularly the pore walls packed with functional microgel particles for capture of biomolecules. We demonstrated that the as-prepared materials can be used to entrap inorganic particles, dye molecules or to load polymers and the encapsulated substances can be released out and the release profile can be tuned. In addition, nitrogen-rich carbon aerogels (NRC) were also successfully fabricated and used as oil-sorbent materials to absorb oils or organic solvents. 6. To prepare organic-inorganic porous materials by incorporating and dispersing active inorganic nanoparticles to the polymeric films and study the photocatalytic reaction of these hybrid porous materials. We have produced hierarchical porous materials by incorporation TiO2 nanoparticles and the fabricated materials are good photocatalysts, showing enhanced activity in photodegrading of organic molecules. Moreover, we also made polymeric microspheres with a hierarchical porous structure, which possess a preeminent catalytic rate and recyclable, making them good candidates for catalyst scaffold materials.

403210.label: Major findings and research outcome
403210.value: This is a fruitful report led by our group. Four new classes of particle stabilizers (PNIPAM-based microgels, bovine serum albumin (BSA) proteins, polyurethane (PU)-based, and lignin nanoparticles) were designed, synthesized and evaluated in this project. Hierarchical porous materials, protein scaffolds, Janus microspheres and carbon aerogels have been fabricated and used as effective adsorbents and catalysts. Moreover, we also explored some of the particle behavior at oil-water interfaces in relation to emulsions. This project has generated a total of 15 high-quality publications and trained 3 students (one Ph.D and two M.Phils). PI has also compiled a book focused on particle-stabilized emulsions and colloids. The main findings are summarized as follows: 1. Functional materials based on PNIPAM-based microgels. We have developed a facial approach for the synthesis of micrometer-sized, pH-responsive microgels, which can load and release active ingredients via changing pH values. By using both microgels and TiO2 solid nanoparticles as stabilizers, we produced three-dimensionally interconnected porous TiO2 monoliths with macropores and interconnecting throats. This kind of pore materials can be excellent candidate for catalysis. 2. Functional materials based on protein nanoparticles. We have prepared hierarchical porous protein scaffolds from an oil-in-water (o/w) HIPE stabilized by bovine serum albumin (BSA) protein nanoparticles. The resulting materials are suitable for a wide range of bio-related applications. 3. Functional materials based on particle-stabilized double emulsions. We have developed a one-step inversion approach for fabricating multiple emulsions with long-term stability by using a precisely defined amphiphilic copolymer. We also developed a simple method for the synthesis of a novel kind of polymeric microsphere with a hierarchical porous structure, making them excellent candidates for adsorption and catalyst scaffold materials. 4. Functional materials based on lignin nanoparticles. We have successfully prepared nitrogen-rich carbon aerogel based on lignin particle-stabilized oil-in-water HIPEs, which possess highly porous structure and excellent fire-resistant property and thus can be applied in oil-spill clean-up and industrial oily wastewater treatment. 5. Functional materials based on polyurethane (PU)-based nanoparticles. We have designed and used of PU-based grafted copolymers as particulate emulsifiers for the generation of stable o/w or w/o particle-stabilized emulsions. This study develops a new polymeric particle for Pickering emulsification, a technology with widespread industrial applications and increasing popularity in materials development. 6. Particle behavior at oil-water interfaces. We showed that the gradients of surface tension can induce particles to jet towards the oil/water interface when particle suspensions come in contact with the interface.

403210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403210.value: In this project, we have focused on fabricating functionalized porous polymeric materials by templating particle-stabilized high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs). Hierarchical porous materials, protein scaffolds, Janus microspheres with multihollow structure and carbon aerogel have been successfully produced in this project. We demonstrated that materials with bimodal porous structures are particularly intriguing because the presence of macropores allows ready mass transfer, while the smaller pores have a specific large surface area and can be used to control and transform substances that encounter it. This kind of pore materials thereby can be excellent candidate for catalysis. This project also leads to a three dimensional, bimodal meso-macroporous protein scaffold, which can be further used for cell culture and tissue engineering. In addition, we have developed a simple method for the synthesis of polymeric microsphere with a hierarchical porous structure, Janus spheres and carbon aerogel. They possess preeminent properties like highly porous structure and excellent fire-resistant property, which thus can be used for separation of oils and organic pollutants, and have potential applications in oil-spill clean-up and industrial oily wastewater treatment.

403210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403210.value: This project has focused on using particle-stabilized emulsions as the initial templates to manufacture functionalized porous materials for applications in chemical and biological fields. Four porous materials including hierarchical titania porous materials, protein scaffolds, Janus microspheres with multihollow structure and fire-resistant carbon aerogels have been fabricated and evaluated in this project. Titania porous materials containing the bimodal porous structures are particularly intriguing and they show great potential for the development of high-throughput flow-through reactors for applications in water treatment. Protein scaffolds consisting of three-dimensional, interconnected pore structure can be readily applied to biomedical applications such as cell culture and tissue engineering. The fabricated polymeric porous microspheres are excellent candidates for adsorption and catalyst scaffold materials, while the as-prepared carbon aerogels can be used like a recyclable container for oil and chemical clean-up, as the oil/chemical-absorbed aerogels can be readily cleaned for reuse by direct combustion in the air, and thus have potential applications in oil-spill clean-up and industrial oily wastewater treatment. Therefore, this project leads to an important step towards the development of novel high performance porous materials for opening up a number of new applications.

403310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403310.value: 繼光子學和電子學之後，表面等離子體光學業已成為非常重要的研究領域。尤其在實現真正意義的納米級光子器件方面，表面等離子體光學器件被認為是最有希望的候選之一。表面等離子體光學，也稱為表面等離子體激元，產生於導體和電介質界面，涉及到強倏逝場的科學和工程學問題。過去的十年中，世界範圍的大量工作集中于金屬結構表面等離子體基礎特性的研究，比如超常透射，超級棱鏡效應，負折射率，等等。隨著對這些特性的逐漸理解，注意力正在轉移到混合結構的研究，比如，金屬結構和活性材料如光發射體，非線性材料，鐵電材料，等結合在一起。當功能材料集成在被動等離子體光學系統中時，我們可以實現對等離子體的主動控制。在此系統中，我們不僅可以產生和發射信號，同時可以調製、處理、切換和探測信號。例如，在金屬納米結構上結合發光材料，通過控制表面等離子體激元的場強，發光強度或者輻射壽命便可得到控制。然而，由於場強對系統幾何結構具有很高的依賴性，微小的結構變化可能對結果產生巨大影響，因此，全面而詳細的理解幾何結構對材料發光特性的影響就顯得尤為重要。壽命是表面等離子體激元最重要的特性參數，它控制著輻射強度的大小。壽命越短，輻射強度越強。在之前的研究中，由於多個等離子體光學模式和輻射模式同時參與，不同物理機制互相影響或者干擾，難以區分。在此項目中，我們計劃系統地研究各種大小、形狀、週期的金屬納米結構對螢光基團自發輻射壽命的影響。爲了定量描述材料特性，角分析和譜分析螢光壽命成像系統已經設計和建成。這個獨一無二的儀器不僅可以在時間上監控螢光基團的衰減過程和實現300納米以下的空間分辨率，而且可以精確地激發和探測等離子體和輻射模式。最後，大量的理論模擬將與實驗同步進行，我們將得到表面等離子體系統的幾何結構對壽命影響的清晰圖像。在這個項目的結尾，我們將嘗試設計識別理想等離子體光學系統的方法，固態照明、顯示技術、光伏等產業將成為最大的受益者。

403310.label: Realisation of objectives
403310.value: We have fulfilled all the objectives of the project. In general, it is known that two processes work hand in hand to yield the surface plasmon mediated fluorescence and they are excitation and emission enhancements. For the excitation enhancement, the incident light excites the incoming surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) which subsequently enhance the excitation of the fluorophore. The fluorophore then couples energy into other outgoing SPPs before radiatively decaying to far field, yielding emission enhancement. To completely understand the entire process, differentiating and then determining the excitation and coupling lifetimes in two processes are necessary. However, to date, the exact determination of these lifetimes is not yet available, hindering the understanding. We combine the coupled mode theory (CMT) and rate equation model to study the interaction between the fluorophores and SPPs. More importantly, we devise theoretical and experimental approaches to determine the enhanced excitation and emission lifetimes of fluorophores through accessible parameters and measure them one by one by using angle- and polarization-resolved reflectivity and photoluminescence spectroscopy. As a result, we are able to understand how the fluorophores interact with SPPs in terms of the effective mode volume and the radiative decay and absorption rates of both incoming and outgoing SPPs. To the best of our knowledge, we are among the first to decouple the surface plasmon mediated fluorescence and study it in such a quantitative manner. All the experimental results are complemented by numerical simulations such as finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method with good agreement. In addition, based on CMT, we have developed methods to control the plasmonic field strengths so that the fluorescence enhancement can be optimized. In particular, we identify that the radiative decay and absorption rates of SPPs have to be matched in order to maximize the field strength. Our CMT prediction is consistent with experiment and FDTD simulation. Therefore, one now can design the geometry of the plasmonic array to match the rates of SPPs for achieving the most desired local field. For example, we have found the optimized groove width and hole radius in 1D and 2D metallic periodic arrays for maximizing the field. Finally, we have constructed a Fourier-space optical microscope for not only spatial imaging but also momentum- and frequency-resolved intensity and lifetime imaging. This new system has become a workhorse in our research group.
