403310.label: Major findings and research outcome
403310.value: We have prepared different one- and two-dimensional metallic arrays with a wide range of geometries by interference lithography and have characterized their surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) radiative decay and absorption rates by combining temporal coupled mode theory (CMT) and angle- and polarization-resolved reflectivity spectroscopy (Part C, 8(1,5,6,11)). The results agree with finite-difference time-domain simulations. It is found that the geometry of the plasmonic systems has great impact in determining the decay rates. As a result, we can study the decay processes of both nondegenerate and degenerate SPP modes and they are later found to be of importance in understanding the surface plasmon mediated fluorescence. In addition, we develop a simple microscopy technique to image the radiation damping of SPPs (Part C, 8(7)). Based on CMT, we deduce the decay rate matching condition for maximizing the plasmonic field strength. We find for a given wavelength, the field strength is the strongest when the radiative decay and absorption rates of SPPs are equal (Part C, 8(10)). In addition, we find this rate matching condition can be measured by using orthogonal reflectivity spectroscopy without involving any near-field techniques, which are both instrumentation demanding and expensive. As the intense field enhancement is the key advantage in the area of plasmonics, our finding provides a direct means for improving different applications that make use of SPPs such as emission enhancement, surface enhanced Raman scattering, photovoltaics, optical tweezers, and photocatalysis (Part C, 8(3,4,8,9)). We have used CMT and rate equation model to determine the excitation and coupling lifetimes of fluorophores in the presence of SPPs without involving the time-resolved techniques. Our method is simple and effective and can differentiate the excitation and emission enhancement processes individually, facilitating better understanding of the entire fluorescence enhancement. Through the analytical models, we express the dependences of the excitation and coupling lifetimes on several different physical parameters such as the decay rates of SPPs and thus are able to optimize both enhancements by tailoring the properties of SPPs. As a demonstration, we have determined the excitation and coupling lifetimes of quantum dots and molecular dyes on plasmonic systems and the results are found to be consistent with simulations (Part C, 8(4,8,12)). Our method is found to be applicable not only to fluorescence but also Raman scattering, which is of importance in bio and chemical label-free sensing (Part C, 8(9)).

403310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403310.value: Our study has opened a new channel to access to this phenomenon by differentiating the sub-processes one by one, enabling a more quantitative understanding than other methods such as fluorescence lifetime imaging and spectroscopy which provide only the information of the decay process but not the excitation. However, we so far are limited to an ensemble of fluorophores. It is known that the plasmonic field is highly inhomogeneous and each single fluorophore would experience different excitation and emission enhancements. In other words, the fluorophores interact with SPPs differently despite being in the same plasmonic system. The degree of interaction depends strongly on the position and the orientation of the fluorophores. Therefore, the next course of action is to study the excitation and coupling of single fluorophore. By selectively positioning and orienting the fluorophore, which could be done by using atomic force microscopy and/or chemical method, we can then study the excitation and emission enhancement in a single molecule basis. To achieve that, sophisticated optical imaging and spectroscopic techniques are required since the signal from a single molecule is so weak that detection of its presence is highly challenging. Nevertheless, we are moving towards this direction.

403310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403310.value: Surface plasmon mediated fluorescence is promising in solid-state lighting and sensing and it possibly leads to better light-emitting diodes, displays, phosphors, biological labeling tags, etc. However, understanding the process is not an easy task. In this project, we have studied the excitation and emission lifetimes of fluorophores attached on various metallic nanostructures with different size, shape, periodicity, etc. To characterize the lifetimes quantitatively, analytical models and sophisticated spectroscopy and microscopy techniques have been developed. We find the lifetimes are strongly dependent on the plasmonic properties, which can be tailored based on our theoretical models. In particular, the field enhancement can be maximized by matching the radiative decay and absorption rates of surface plasmon polaritons. The experimental and analytical results are consistent with rigorous full field numerical simulations. As a result, it is now possible to understand the mediated fluorescence process thoroughly and to optimize it systematically. Our results point to the direction of developing high brightness fluorescence platform in near future.

403510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403510.value: Modern natural product synthesis has placed an added requirement for the organic chemists, i.e. the target molecules should be harvested in optically active form due to the different pharmacological response of the enantiomers. Chiral bicyclic ring systems are versatile intermediates/starting materials for making optically active pharmaceuticals. Methods for preparing these chiral substances efficiently from simple achiral alkenes are therefore important and of commercial value. The project aims at developing inexpensive sugar-derived amines as efficient organocatalysts (non-metal, small organic molecules as catalysts) for making chiral bicyclic rings via an intramolecular Diels-Alder reaction. The successful research results will provide economical avenue towards optically active bicyclic ring systems from achiral alkenes and will allow the synthetic chemists to devise viable routes to target pharmaceuticals. In summary, our successful research results are (a) important for the advancement of the science of synthetic organic chemistry and(b) useful for the chemical industry that may employ the developed sugar-derived amine catalysts for the preparation of chemicals of pharmaceutical interest or for other industrial applications. It should be appreciated the new amines described in this proposal would be useful for making optically active substances via other organic reactions. 現代合成天然產物對有機化學家提出了更高的要求-----目標分子以光學活性形式出現，而其不同的對映體(enantiomer)則會產生不同的藥理反應。當中手性的二環體是製備光學活性藥物的合適中間體或原材料。因此，從簡單的無光學活性烯烴出發，利用高效方法製備該類光學活性的物質，極具商業價值和符合成本效益。本課題旨在設計廉價的糖源胺分子來開發高效有機催化劑（非金屬，有機小分子作為催化劑），通過分子內 Diels - Alder反應製備手性的二環體。研究成果將提供一條具經濟效益的途徑把非手性烯烴製備成有光學活性二環體，並讓合成化學家制定可行的路線; 從而製備目標藥物。綜上，我們的研究成果（一）是有機合成領域上的大躍進及（二）對製藥業及化工業上使用已發展成熟的糖源胺催化劑來製備化學藥物或化合物極具参考意義。課題中提及的新型胺對於其它用於製備光學活性物質同樣適用。

403510.label: Major findings and research outcome
403510.value: We have accomplished a new synthetic route to chiral pyrrolidines via a Grignard reaction on hemiaminal. A total of 12 new hydroxylated pyrrolidines were synthesized. The stereoselectivities of these catalysts have been assessed by comparing with those of MacMillan’s imidazolidinone on a known intramolecular Diels-Alder (IMDA) reaction of a triene. The results indicated that although the enantioselectivities of our amine catalysts were not as superior as those of MacMillan’s catalyst, satisfactory enantiocontrol could be attained. Two additional IMDA reactions of symmetrical dienals with concomitant desymmetrization further established the potential use of these novel amine catalysts. The ees obtained are in the range of 86-90 and 77-82%, respectively. However, the chemical yields were disappointing and were attributable to the inherent instability of the dienals. This effect prevented us from further investigation of the IMDA reactions on dienals. Our attention was turned to pyrrolidine catalysed intramolecular aldol reactions. 1,7-Dial was synthesized from ethyl formate and was used to study asymmetric aminocatalyzed intramolecular aldol reactions. Pyrrolidine catalysts with a trimethybenzyl blocking group displayed good enantioselectivities from 89 to 94%. These pyrrodilines are valuable catalysts for other synthetic transformations involving enamine and iminium ion activation.

403510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403510.value: We have prepared 12 enantiopure chiral amine catalysts from sugars. These amines are not only useful for Diels-Alder reactions, but they can be applied to catalysing a wide varieties of chemical transformations, namely alpha-allylation, -oxygenation, -arylation, Michael addition, and domino reactions. We have already demonstrated their use in aldol reactions. Research on other chemical transformatons using these new amines is warranted and hence justifies further funding in this area.

404010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404010.value: This proposal is devoted to the mathematical analysis of a class of new partial differential equations that were proposed-relatively recently-as models for certain Micro-Electromechnical Systems (MEMS). In this proposal, even though we deal with much simplified models of MEMS, it still leads to very interesting second and fourth order nonlinear elliptic equations (in the stationary case) and to nonlinear parabolic equations (in the dynamical case). The main new feature of such elliptic problems is that the non-linearity is of an inverse square type, i.e., negative exponents, which--until recently--has not received much attention as a mathematical problem. Numerics and formal asymptotic analysis give lots of information and point to many conjectures, but even in the most simple idealized versions of MEMS, one essentially need the full available arsenal of modern nonlinear analysis and PDE techniques "to do" the required mathematics: the notions of weak and regular solutions, bifurcation analysis and their connection to Morse theory, energy estimates via Sobolev theory and Moser's iteration, compactness via blow--up phenomena and nonlinear Liouville theorems, uniqueness via monotonicity formular and Pohozaev identities, and finally profile analysis via maximum principles and moving plane methods, among others. Indeed, while nonlinear eigenvalue problems are a well-developed filed of PDEs, the type of nonlinearity that appears here, helps to shed a new light light on the class of singular supercritical problems and their specific chanllengs. Furtheremore, these fourth order models for MEMS are also amplifying the need for a better and deeper understanding of equations involving bi-harmonic Laplacian, which remain quite elusive in spite of recent advances. The main objective is that proposal is combine techniques in various fileds, such as method of moving planes, singular perturbations, dyanmical systems, geometric analysis, to give a thorough, rigorous, and unified mathematical analysis for various phenomena related to the simplest proposed models, many of which were observed either numerically or in simple cases. 摘要: 本研究計劃著重於最新才提出的微局部電力系統(MEMS)中的偏微分方程的研究. 雖然我們只是考慮比較簡化了的MEMS模型, 但是也有很多有趣的二階及四階方程. 這些方程的特徵是它們的非綫性項是負平方, 即負指標. 關於這類方程以前有少的研究. 雖然數值計算及非平格的計算告訴我們很多新的有趣的現象, 但是數學上嚴格的研究才剛開始. 很多問題(看起來簡單)至今懸而未解: 弱解的定義, 分歧分析, 緊性, 非綫性Liouville定理, Morse叠代, 單調公式, Pohozaev等式, 極值原理, 等等. 雖然非綫性譜問題有很多的研究, 但是對負指標問題的研究會給一些新的方法去處理超臨界指標問題. 另外, 帶負指標的四階方程需要發展對四階方程特別的工具. 我們的主要的目標和計劃是利用不同領域的方法, 比如移動平面法, 奇異攝問, 動力系統, 幾何分析等. 對負指標問題發展出一套嚴格的數學理論, 從而對實際問題作出新的貢獻.

404010.label: Realisation of objectives
404010.value: We have acheived 100/100 of the objectives. 1. For problems with negative exponents, we constructed and analyzed the rupture solutions. 2. For biharmonc problems with negative exponents or super critical exponents, we completely classified the stability/instability of the solutions, solving long-standing conjectures. 3. For MEMS with fringing fields, we first discovered a transformation and gave complete analysis of the rupture behaviors. Then we constructed solutions with ruptures. 4. For self-similar problems of curve-shortening flow, we proved the existence for 2pi periodic potentials. 5. For Lane-Emden problems with supercritical exponents, we found new nonradial singular solutions 6.For fourth order problems we have analyzed the criticality and its connection with conformal flows. 7. Using techniques developed for negative exponent problems, we solved several outstanding problems: a) we obtained infinitely many nonradial sign-changing finite energy solutions for NLS in dimensions 2 and 3. Previously only dimensions 4 or higher are studied b) we gave a complete classification of SU(n+1) Toda system with singularity.

404010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404010.value: Nonlinear elliptic equations with negative exponents arise in many applied fields, such as MEMS or elasticity theory. A major difficulty is that it is non-standard: first there is no variational structure due to lack of Sobolev inequality second all classical methods of proving existence such as sub-super solutions, Mountain-Pass, a priori estimates do not work here. In this project we have developed a systematic approach to treat such problems and achieved amazing results, including a complete classification of stable solutions for biharmonic problems with negative exponents, complete classification of SU(n+1) Toda systems with singularities, constructions of nonradial sign-changing solutions to NLS--a deep connection with CMC theory.

404210.label: Realisation of objectives
404210.value: We have studied how the copolymer composition, block length and solvent quality affect our discovered nanopore-extrusion induced sphere-to-cylinder transition of polymeric micelles; tried to to fix the shell and the core of long and thin cylindrical polymeric micelles by using several fast chemical cross-linking reactions; explored different extrusion conditions to align and spin these chemically fixed individual cylindrical polymeric micelles (nanowires) into a microscopic nanowire bundle after the nanopore-extrusion; and tested their tensile and breakage strengths and viscoelasticity of individual chemically fixed thin cylindrical micelles as well as microscopic nanowire bundles. We have also hypothesized, for the first time, why RNA and protein chains are linear and not colliding inside nuclear pores; namely, only for linear chains, the critical flow rate for them to pass through a small pore is independent on the chain length and there exists passive breathing motions of the nuclear membrane, which is driven by thermal fluctuation to generate a sufficiently high flow rate to pull or push the chains in or out of the nuclear membrane so that the collision is naturally avoided.

404210.label: Major findings and research outcome
404210.value: We developed a general approach to polymer chains confined by interacting boundaries; i.e., flow through a cylindrical nano-tube, wherein the Laplace-Green’s function methods are extended to describe polymers confined in interacting, impenetrable cylindrical geometries, whose treatment is far more challenging than the slit and box geometries previously considered. The general methods are illustrated with calculations (as a function of the polymer-surface interaction) of the free energy of confinement, the radial density profile, and the average of the drag force in the free draining limit. The calculated values are quantitatively comparable with our experimental results (Refs. 1 and 2).

404210.value: Using theoretically and experimentally established quantitative relationships between polymer chains with different topologies and critical flow rates, one can develop some analytic instruments to separate polymer chains by their topologies instead of by conventional chain sizes.

404210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404210.value: Amphiphilic block copolymer chains contain at least on solvent-like and one solvent dislike polymer block (short chain). In a give solvent, those solvent dislike blocks tend to associate together to form a microphase separation, resulting in spherical, cylindrical or vesicle-like polymeric micelles. This current study was based on our finding that the extrusion of small spherical polymeric micelles through a small pore can lead to the formation of long and thin cylindrical polymeric micelles. In this study, we have studied how the copolymer composition, block length and solvent quality affect our discovered nanopore-extrusion induced sphere-to-cylinder transition of polymeric micelles; tried to to fix the shell and the core of long and thin cylindrical polymeric micelles by using several fast chemical cross-linking reactions; explored different extrusion conditions to align and spin these chemically fixed individual cylindrical polymeric micelles (nanowires) into a microscopic nanowire bundle after the nanopore-extrusion; and tested their tensile and breakage strengths and viscoelasticity of individual chemically fixed thin cylindrical micelles as well as microscopic nanowire bundles.

404610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404610.value: The chemistry of carboranes and metallacarboranes has been dominated by 12-vertex icosahedral molecules for almost half a century, and the knowledge on supercarboranes (carboranes with more than 12 vertices) had been limited merely to the possible cage geometries predicted by theoretical work before 2003. Recognition of the relatively lower reducing power of carbon-atoms-adjacent (CAd) carborane anions over the carbon-atoms-apart (CAp) counterparts offers a very valuable entry point to the synthesis of supercarboranes. Subsequently, several 13- and 14-vertex carboranes and 15-vertex metallacarboranes have been prepared since 2003. We have made significant contributions to this growing research field. Part of our work has been summarized in two recent invited reviews (Organometallics 2007, 26, 1832-1845 and Coord. Chem. Rev. 2007, 251, 2452-2476). These works have laid a solid ground in the exploration of supercarboranes. In this proposal, we plan to enlarge the scope of synthetic possibilities to include carboranes and heterocarboranes having 15 vertices or more, and to explore systematically the rich reaction chemistry of supercarboranes on the basis of our previous achievements. 404610.label: Realisation of objectives
404610.value: The chemistry of carboranes and metallacarboranes has been dominated by 12-vertex icosahedral molecules for almost half a century, and the knowledge on supercarboranes (carboranes with more than 12 vertices) had been limited merely to the possible cage geometries predicted by theoretical work before 2003. Recognition of the relatively lower reducing power of carbon-atoms-adjacent (CAd) carborane anions over the carbon-atoms-apart (CAp) counterparts offers a very valuable entry point to the synthesis of supercarboranes. Subsequently, several 13- and 14-vertex carboranes and 15-vertex metallacarboranes have been prepared. Reactivity studies showed that 14-vertex carboranes have a diverse reactivity pattern toward nucleophiles. It reacted with MeOH/Me3N, tBuOK or LiNMe2 to give 14-vertex nido species [μ-8,9-(CH2)3-μ-11,12-(Nu)BH-8,9-C2B11H11]- (Nu = MeO, tBuO, Me2N), which were converted to a 13-vertex nido-carborane [μ-8,9-(CH2)3-8,9-C2B11H11]2- via deboration in the presence of excess nucleophiles. [μ-8,9-(CH2)3-μ-11,12-(MeO)BH-8,9-C2B11H11]- was also converted to a 12-vertex closo species [μ-1,2-(CH2)3CH(OMe)-1-CB11H10]- in an acidic MeOH solution. The results indicated that substituents on the cage carbons have significant influence on the properties of supercarboranes. To this end, 1,2-(TMS)2-o-C2B10H10 was selected as the suitable starting material after screening many substituents. We have finally succeeded in the preparation and characterization of 15-vertex carborane (TMS)2C2B13H13 and the corresponding 16-vertex metallacarboranes (TMS)2C2B13H13Ru(p-cymene). They represent the largest carborane and metallacarborane known so far, respectively. In summary, this project was very successfully carried out and all objectives were achieved.

404610.label: Major findings and research outcome
404610.value: (1) A series of ether-functionalized 12-vertex carboranes were prepared and fully characterized, which were used as starting materials for the investigation of substituent effects. The reaction of 12-vertex carboranes with NHC carbenes was also studied, which offered important information on the deboration process (Pubs #1&3). (2) The reactions of 13-vertex carborane with nucleophiles are very versatile. A nucleophile-dependent reactivity pattern is observed. 13-vertex carborane reacts with MeOH and Ph3P to give exclusively cage-carbon extrusion product closo-CB11 monoanions, with Et3N/MeOH or PS/MeOH to afford nido-CB10 monoanions, with Py to generate closo-CB10 monoanion, and with bipy to yield exclusive cage-boron extrusion species closo-C2B10 neutral system. The reaction mechanism was proposed after the identification of the key intermediates (Pubs #2&4&8). (3) Several monoanions of 13-vertex carboranes were prepared by deprotonation of C,C’-linked 13-vertex carboranes with strong bases or lithium metal. Their structures were confirmed by spectroscopic data and single-crystal X-ray analyses, revealing the existence of Ccage=C exo-π-bonding. The cage bears two trapezoidal faces with the others being triangulated, giving one five- and one four-coordinate cage carbon atoms. They represent the first examples of 13-vertex carboranes having exo-π-bonding to hypercarbon atom. The results suggest that 13-vertx carboranes are more electron deficient than 12-vertex species as the -methylene hydrogen in 1,2-(CH2)3-1,2-C2B10H10 can not be deprotonated by strong bases. This work also shows that a short carbon-chain between two cage carbon atoms can prevent the cleavage of the cage C–C bond, but lead to the cage C–B bond breaking after the delocalization of negative charge from exo carbon to the cage. The presence of such a short chain may force the monoanions to adopt a closo-like geometry though they should be [2n+4] systems. It is anticipated that a similar phenomenon might be observed in other C,C’-linked carboranes (Pubs #6). (4) Our studies on the chemistry of supercarboranes have been summarized in two account articles (Pubs #5&7). Res. paper, which summarizes the work of this project. We are sorry for such a mistake.) PI was invited to give two plenary and one invited lectures at international/national conferences. Two postgraduate students have been trained.

404610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404610.value: Carboranes are a class of polyhedral boron hydride clusters in which one or more of the BH vertices are replaced by CH units. Their chemistry has been dominated by 12-vertex carboranes for over half a century. In contrast, knowledge regarding supercarboranes (carboranes with more than 12 vertices) had been limited merely to possible cage geometries predicted by theoretical work before 2003. Only in recent years has significant progress been made in synthesizing supercarboranes. Such a breakthrough relied on the use of Carbon-Atoms-Adjacent (CAd) nido-carborane dianions or arachno-carborane tetraanions as starting materials that were discovered in our laboratory. We have further developed the synthetic methods and prepared, for the first time, 15-vertex carborane and the corresponding 16-vertex metallacarboranes. They represent the largest carborane and metallacarborane known so far, respectively. This research can largely enhance our basic understanding of boron clusters chemistry.

404810.label: Project Title(Chinese)
404810.value: 將二氧化碳轉化為燃料的太陽能光催化先進材料

404810.label: Project Objectives
404810.value: To synthesize a series of porous visible-light photocatalysts by using template methods. To study the physical and chemical properties of these new materials. To use the photocatalysts for converting carbon dioxide to fuels under visible-light irradiation. To elucidate the fundamental mechanisms of these transformations and apply this knowledge to improve the efficiency and selectivity of the process.

To elucidate the fundamental mechanisms of these transformations and apply this knowledge to improve the efficiency and selectivity of the process.

404810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404810.value: Global warming is the most pressing issue currently facing mankind. The major greenhouse gas, carbon dioxide, is being released at an alarming rate by burning fossil fuels. To slow down global warming, several methods have been proposed for carbon sequestration including the injection and storage of anthropogenic CO2 in deep geologic formations. Such method requires a huge amount of energy to condense CO2 gas. Moreover, if permeable pathways are present, CO2 may eventually migrate away from the storage site into the shallow subsurface and eventually into the atmosphere. This proposal tackles the problem from a different perspective. The CO2 being discharged into the atmosphere should be considered a vast and cheap source of carbon for the production of fuel. This project focuses on the design and fabrication of advanced porous photocatalysts which will use solar energy to convert CO2 to fuels such as methane, methanol, or even longer chain hydrocarbons. This approach may revolutionize the energy industry. 燃燒化石燃料産生大量二氧化碳等溫室氣體,引發全球暖化,這是人類面對的最大難題。雖然把二氧化碳封存在地底深處可以緩和溫室效應,但是這方法耗用大量能源來凝結氣體。而且儲藏的二氧化碳難免會泄漏回淺層而最終釋放到大氣中。這個研究計劃提出另一個解決問題的方案,將排放到大氣的二氧化碳視作寶貴的碳資源,用來生產碳氫燃料。本項目專注於新穎多孔光催化劑的製備,用太陽光把二氧化碳轉化為甲烷,甲醇或其他碳氫化合物。這個方法會給能源工業帶來革命性的影響。

404810.label: Realisation of objectives
404810.value: A series of porous visible light active photocatalysts, ranging from a single element structure to graphene-based composites, have been fabricated by using template methods. The physical and chemical properties of these new materials (including elemental red phosphorus, hierarchical BiOBr, WO3 nanorods/graphene nanocomposites, P/YPO4 microspheres, WO3/TiO2 microstructures, In2S3 nanosheets/graphene composites, CdS nanorods/reduced graphene oxide nanocomposites, and Pt3Co-loaded CdS) were studied. Their photocatalytic activities for inducing redox reactions were measured. These materials were found to show potential for energy and environmental applications. Explanations and mechanisms for these applications were proposed in the publications. Carbon monoxide and methane were the two major products from the photocatalytic reduction of carbon dioxide. However, the conversion efficiency was relativly low as compared to that for photocatalytic water splitting. It should be noted that we found recently an exceptional SrTiO3 photocatalyst for carbon dioxide reduction but we need to carry our additional experiemnts to elucidate its mechanism.

404810.label: Major findings and research outcome
404810.value: We have reported our major findings in 12 publications listed in Part C of this report. These include a book chapter titled "Advanced Photocatalytic Nanomaterials for Degrading Pollutants and Generating Fuels by Sunlight" published by Springer and a highly cited feature article about "Graphene-Based Photocatalytic Composites" appeared in RSC Advances. Many advanced photocatalytic materials were fabricated including chemically modified TiO2 and CdS, BiOBr, composite materials with graphene and upconversion property, and simple elemental photocatalysts. They were found effective for hydrogen generation from water splitting, and they were explored for CO2 reduction. Recently, we have prepared a novel SrTiO3 photocatalyst from Sr(NO3)2 and TiO2 (p25). It was found that hydrogen evolution over SrTiO3 could be improved by loading Pt or Rh as a cocatalyst. For the reduction of CO2 to CH4 or CO, it was necessary to add cocatalyst Ag or Pd. We are working with a group at UCL to confirm the latest findings.

404810.value: To form an interdisciplinary team to seek industrial support for device fabrication, testing and knowledge transfer.

404810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404810.value: The conversion of CO2 to useful fuels by chemical means not only reduces CO2 in the atmosphere, but also eases our dependence on oil. This project shows that it is possible to achieve that objective by photocatalytic reduction under sunlight. This is a perfect solution to both the global warming and energy shortage problems. A series of photocatalytic materials have been prepared in this project. The design of novel photocatalytic materials with higher efficiency is a perennial subject of interest. These materials may be the key to a sustainable future.

405110.label: Project Objectives
405110.value: We proposed an efficient inexact Uzawa method with relaxation parameters for the most basic saddle-point system (i.e., A is SPD and D=0 in (1)); but its convergence was established only under some restrictive assumptions. We will investigate the convergence of the method in depth and remove some restrictive and practically inconvenient conditions. We will propose some efficient inexact Uzawa methods with relaxation parameters for the generalized saddle-point system (1), including the symmetric case (A, D are SPD), the non-symmetric case (A is non-symmetric, D=0 or non-zero). We will study the convergence of the newly proposed inexact Uzawa methods for generalized saddle-point systems (1) when effective preconditioners are available for both A and the Schur complement associated with (1). We will study the convergence of the newly proposed inexact Uzawa methods for generalized saddle-point systems (1) when effective preconditioners are available only for one of A and the Schur complement, or for none of them. We will apply the newly proposed iterative methods to solve saddle-point problems arising from different PDEs and carry out numerical experiments to understand and find out the actual efficiencies of the proposed methods, and then improve the methods and the convergence theory.

405110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
405110.value: 求解广义鞍点问题的予处理方法的数学分析 摘要 实际应用中, 许多数学模型涉及的边值问题或时间相关的初边值问题的数值求解过程中经常需要不断求解大规模线性方程组的鞍点问题。 如何快速求解鞍点问题是应用数学中一个非常有挑战性的课题。 予处理选代法是求解鞍点问题的一个主要方法，但对予处理矩阵的选取要特别小心以便保证选代的收敛性。大部分现有的方法通过对予处理矩阵作适当的规范化可以达到选代的收敛性，但数值实现过程非常困难。 本申请人及其合作者最近对于简单的鞍点问题提出了多个选代法，通过引进适当的松弛因子可使选代法对于一般的予处理矩阵均收敛。 本研究课题的主要目的就是提出一些新的选代法，对更一般的广义鞍点问题通过引进适当的松弛因子使选代对于一般给定的予处理矩阵均可保证收敛。

405110.label: Realisation of objectives
405110.value: For Objective 1, we have established in [2, 6, 10, 12] the convergence of the inexact Uzawa method and its variants we proposed earlier for the most basic saddle-point system, under several less restrictive assumptions and conditions. These results are mainly based on more delicate matrix factorizations, subspace decomposition techniques and eigenvalue estimates under more appropriate norms. For Objective 2, we have proposed some efficient inexact Uzawa methods for the generalized saddle-point system, including the symmetric case [2, 12], the non-symmetric case [2, 10]. Several other types of iterative methods were also proposed for various nonlinear saddle-point systems from the Navier-Stokes system [9], the stationary, full and time-harmonic Maxwell systems [1], the inverse problem in a coupled elliptic and parabolic system [5], and from the inverse reconstruction of heat fluxes [7, 11]. An iterative method with variable relaxations for finding reasonable regularization parameters was proposed for linear inverse problems [6], and a semi-smooth Newton method with relaxation parameters for the regularized formulation in inverse scattering problems [4], an iterative indicator method for inverse electromagnetic scattering problems [3] and a globally convergent iteration with relaxations for reconstructing the physical coefficients in a wave equation [8]. For Objectives 3 and 4, we have studied the convergence of our new inexact Uzawa methods for generalized saddle-point systems when effective preconditioners are available for both A and the Schur complement or for only one of them [2,10,12], and the convergence of an iterative method with variable relaxations for finding reasonable regularization parameters for linear inverse problems [6]. We have investigated the well-posedness and convergence of various finite element saddle-point systems from the stationary, full and time-harmonic Maxwell systems [1], various inverse reconstruction problems [5,7,11] and the Navier-Stokes system [9]. For Objective 5, we have applied the newly proposed methods and some further developed related methods to solve saddle-point problems arising from the Maxwell system [12] and different inverse problems [6, 7, 8, 11], the Navier-Stokes system [9] and the coupled elliptic and parabolic system [5]. We have carried out various numerical experiments on these methods and observed their high effectiveness, efficiency and robustness compared with some popular existing methods. All the objectives of the project have been satisfactorily achieved. In fact, many numerical methods, their performance and theoretical justifcations are better than expected in the original proposal.

405110.label: Major findings and research outcome
405110.value: In this project, we have proposed various numerical iterative methods for a wide class of important application problems. The following is a list of the effective and efficient iterative methods we have proposed for various generalized saddle-point problems: (1) inexact iterative methods for the generalized saddle-point system for both the symmetric case [2, 12] and the non-symmetric case [2, 10]; (2) iterative methods for many nonlinear saddle-point systems from the Navier-Stokes system [9], the stationary, full and time-harmonic Maxwell systems [1], the inverse problem in a coupled elliptic-parabolic system [5], and from the inverse reconstruction of heat fluxes [7, 11]; (3) an iterative method with variable relaxations for finding reasonable regularization parameters for linear inverse problems [6]; (4) a semi-smooth Newton method with relaxation parameters for the regularized formulation in inverse scattering problems [4]; (5) an iterative indicator method for inverse electromagnetic scattering problems [3]; (6) a globally convergent iteration with relaxations for reconstructing physical coefficients in wave equations [8]. We have studied and analysed in depth the convergence and mathematical behaviors of the most iterative methods we have proposed in this project and have achieved the following results: (1) the inexact Uzawa iterative method and its several variants we proposed before for the most basic saddle-point system converge under much less restrictive conditions [2, 6, 10, 12]; (2) the newly proposed inexact Uzawa methods converge for generalized saddle-point systems when effective preconditioners are available for both A and the Schur complement or for only one of them [2,10,12], and they may converge optimally in various environments. (3) the iterative method with two variable relaxations for locating effective regularization parameters converges globally and monotonically for general linear inverse problems [6]; (4) the saddle-point systems and their discrete forms from the stationary, full and time-harmonic Maxwell systems [1], various inverse reconstruction problems [5,7,11] and the Navier-Stokes system [9] are generally well-posed and converge optimally in terms of mesh size and time step. The newly proposed iterative methods have helped us successfully solve many important application problems. We have applied these new methods to solve various saddle-point problems arising from the Maxwell system [12], different inverse problems [6, 7, 8, 11], the Navier-Stokes system [9] and the coupled elliptic-parabolic system [5]. We have carried out various numerical simulations using these methods. From these experiments we have observed many meaningful mathematical behaviors of the physical solutions to these application problems.

405110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
405110.value: In this project, we have proposed various numerical iterative methods for solving generalized saddle-point systems arising from a wide class of important application problems and have systematically studied and analysed their effectiveness and convergence. Based on our theoretical analysis and numerical observations, we may explore the following further developments in the research direction: (1) we have discussed and studied the inexact iterative methods for the generalized non-symmetric saddle-point system in [2, 10]. But under the most general settings, one may seek more effective preconditioners and explore their numerical effects on the convergence. (2) we have proposed iterative methods for many nonlinear saddle-point systems from various application problems. Some physical systems have a few special physical parameters involved. It would be very interesting to see how these parameters may affect the convergence and stability of the resulting iterative methods. (3) For some model problems with discontinuous solutions, such as the solutions to the regularized formulation in inverse scattering problems [4], we have proposed a semi-smooth Newton method with relaxation parameters. More numerical and mathematical insights and tools may be developed to explore the convergence and stability of the method. It is practically important to develop similar methods for more application problems.

405110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
405110.value: Numerical solutions and simulations of many physical, engineering, industrial application problems involve large-scale saddle-point systems of linear algebraic equations. These systems are mostly indefinite and non-symmetric, so their numerical solutions are much more challenging and time-consuming than those non-saddle-point systems. Preconditioned iterative methods aim at speeding up numerical solution processes of large-scale systems. But great care needs to be taken of the preconditioners in order to ensure the convergence of the resulting iterative methods for large-scale saddle-point systems. Most existing methods require some scalings of the preconditioners to guarantee their convergence. But the desired scaling is usually very difficult to achieve in real applications. In this project we have proposed a class of inexact preconditioned iterative methods with relaxation parameters for the general saddle-point systems. These methods do not require the scalings to ensure their convergence, and converge reasonably well when effective preconditioners are available. We have tested numerically and studied systematically these inexact preconditioned methods, and observed their good efficiency and robustness for a wide class of application problems. This project has made a significant contribution to the numerical solutions of the challenging generalized saddle-point systems, in terms of the developments of efficient algorithms, their numerical analysis and applications.

410110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410110.value: The problem of reconstructing or estimating partially observed or sampled signals is an old and important one, and finds application in many areas of signal processing and communications. Traditional acquisition and reconstruction approaches are heavily influences by the classical Shannon sampling theory which gives an exact sampling and interpolation formula for bandlimited signals. Recently, the classical Shannon sampling framework has been extended to classes of non-bandlimited structured signals, which we call signals with Finite Rate of Innovation (FRI). In these new sampling schemes, the prior that the signal is sparse in a basis or in a parametric space is put to contribution and perfect reconstruction is possible based on a set of suitable measurements. This leads to new exact reconstruction formulas and fast algorithms that achieve such reconstructions. The main aim of this project is triple: 1) To improve over our current FRI algorithms by using a coarse-to-fine strategy (wavelet/pyramid decomposition); 2) To extend the class of admissible sampling filters by using a novel property, the ``Generalized Annihilation Property''; 3) To extend these algorithms to the superresolution of edges in two-dimensions. 這個問題估計部分重建或觀察或採樣信號是一個古老而重要的，並認為在許多領域應用的信號處理和通信。傳統的收購和重建方法是極大地影響了古典Shannon採樣理論，給出了一個精確的採樣和內插公式帶限信號。最近，古典Shannon採樣框架已經擴展到類別的非帶限信號的結構，我們的呼叫信號與有限速率的創新（星期五）。在這些新的抽樣方案，事先該信號是稀疏的基礎或在參數空間的貢獻是提出和完善的基礎上重建是可能的一組合適的測量。這將導致新的公式和快速精確重建算法，實現這種重建。其主要目的是三重這個項目：1）改善對我們當前的星期五算法通過使用一個由粗到細的戰略（小波/金字塔分解），2）擴大受理採樣過濾器類使用一種新的屬性，在“廣義湮沒財產”; 3）擴大這些算法在超分辨率邊在兩方面。

410110.label: Realisation of objectives
410110.value: All the objectives have been addressed and attained: * 1. New Finite Rate of Innovation algorithms have been developed, and shown to be significantly more efficient compared to standard FRI algorithms. In particular, the i-LET framework (journal paper #2 and conf paper #2) has shown how to perform sparse minimization in multiresolution setting. The most efficient FRI algorithm available today is now described in the conf paper #7. Matlab implementations are freely available at http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~tblu/demos/ * 2. New FRI-admissible sampling kernels have been found for non-uniform sampling (journal paper #1), and for solving inverse problems linked to the Laplace equation (conf paper #) or to the wave equation (conf papers #4,5 and 6). More generally, by allowing Strang-Fix properties to hold approximately, it was possible to demonstrate that virtually all arbitrary kernels could be used in an annihilation framework (journal paper #3). * 3. The FRI algorithms have been extended to 2D, and so to images characterized by sharp edges made of a new class of curves "annihilable curves", resulting in a highly accurate super-resolution algorithm (from a single image): see journal paper #4 and conf paper #1. Formation of two MPhil students and visit by PhD student from KAIST Dae Gwan LEE (supervisor: Prof. Kil Hyun KWON).

410110.label: Major findings and research outcome
410110.value: The major findings are in line with the objectives of this project. The most significant achievement is a novel approach to describing the edge part of images, in a way that is fully continuous, thanks the a FRI representation. This approach has also resulted in a new understanding of FRI algorithms, based on a masking equation, compared to the original framework which is based on an annihilation equation in the Fourier domain. In the journal paper #4, we have shown how to use this masking equation to enlarge an image, while being faithful to its edges, and to achieve super-resolution from a unique image. Hanjie Pan, the research MPhil student who developed this research is now working towards the PhD on the same subject at EPFL, supervised by Prof. M. Vetterli (co-I of this research project), and co-supervised by the current PI. Another important achievement is the i-LET framework (journal paper #2) which shows how to generate efficient sparse optimization algorithms within a multiscale or multifilter setting. In particular, we have been able to give very simple rules for these types of iterative algorithms to converge unconditionally to the global sparse optimum. Other achievements that are still under development: new FRI kernels for solving sparse inverse problems arising from partial differential equations (application to photoacoustic tomography and to electroencephalography under development: cof papers #5,6 and journal paper #1), new FRI kernels for non-uniform sampling (con paper #3). We would like to mention specifically a very fast and efficient FRI algorithm (conf paper #7, for which a more substantial journal paper is in progress), able to deal with large data sets, that is now a key tool for our ongoing research in this domain.

410110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410110.value: a) development of a novel approach to sparsity based on a masking principle, that has the potential to address continuous and discrete sparse settings. This approach, currently investigated by Hanjie Pan at EPFL, is even much more promising in that it allows to solve most inverse linear problems (deconvolution, tomographic reconstruction, etc.) under explicit sparse assumptions. This can be compared directly with the other concurrent approach based on non-Euclidean regularization ("compressed sensing") which achieves exact sparsity in only very constrained cases. b) development of a local FRI curve framework, from the current (non-local) Fourier-based formalism c) further extension to volumes of the curve FRI technique d) extension of the fast FRI fitting algorithm to arbitrary sparse parametric representations (currently limited to sum of exponentials)

410110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410110.value: Sparsity, i.e., the property of signals to be made essentially of very few non-zero coefficients, is a very hot topic in signal and image processing. This is an important step to capture the essential part of the information contained in a signal. An image, for instance, can be approximated by a sketch which is "sparse" in a certain way. The current project is about an explicit approach to sparsity ("Finite Rate of Innovation" or FRI framework), by involving few descriptive parameters ("innovations"). The difficulties lie both in the adequate models to use for this description, and how to infer the parameters from the measured signals. Our main achievements in this project are twofold: 1) develop new FRI models to represent not only one-dimensional "sparse" signals (current FRI state of the art), but also multi-dimensional models able to represent the edges of images with arbitrary accuracy; 2) develop new efficient and accurate algorithms for retrieving the parameters or approximating measured signals by FRI "sparse" signals. The applications of this type of theoretical research are typically super-resolution enhancement of images (arbitrary zoom, without blur).

410410.label: Realisation of objectives
410410.value: We have derived the likelihood function, the score functions and the information matrix based on the progressive and adaptive progressive hybrid censored samples assuming the underlying lifetime distribution are two-parameter exponential and Weibull. We also studied the maximum likelihood estimators. For the two-parameter exponential case, exact inference is proposed. For the Weibull case, the estimators are not in a closed form and an approximation of the estimators is suggested and both estimation methods are studied and comparisons have been made. Some suggestions to obtained the optimal censored schemes are made. Sensitivity of the optimal censoring schemes are also studied.

410410.label: Major findings and research outcome
410410.value: In this project, we have successfully developed theories associated with the progressively hybrid censored sampling and adaptive progressively hybrid sampling. The exact inference based on the progressively hybrid censored samples from a two-parameter exponential population is well studied and the results are contained in the research output 4 in Part C. The inference of Type-II progressively hybrid censored data with Weibull lifetimes is studied and the results are published in the research output 1 in Part C. Note that the maximum likelihood estimators of the censored are not in the closed form, an approximate estimators which in closed form are also given. We also develop an algorithm in determining the optimal allocation in regression models (output no. 6 in Part C). We also studied the optimal allocation for multi-level stress testing with exponential regression under type-I censoring and the results are given in the output 2 of Part C. Sensitivity studies are also considered. Finally we have extend the censored schemes to a more flexible scheme and associated inference on the scheme is considered in output n. 5 of Part C.

410410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410410.value: The progressively hybrid censored schemes can be generalized to other flexible schemes. It is good to compare these different flexible schemes in order to determine the optimal schemes. The optimal allocation schemes in this project are obtained by enumeration method. This can be done only when the sample size is small. When the sample size is large, it is infeasible if not impossible. It will be good if we can develop the asymptotic theory on the progressive hybrid censored schemes. The results can be used in determining the optimal schemes when the sample size is large. Comparisons between the finite sample and asymptotic results are of interest theoretically and practically.

410410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410410.value: In designing an experiment, minimizing the cost in conducting the experiment and maximizing the information collected from the experiment are usually the major objectives. However, these two objectives are competitive: longer experimental time will collect more information but more costly. This is why we propose the idea of hybrid censoring. The results of this study provides the practitioners guidelines in designing the experiments. The required inference based on these kind of experiments are also given. The users can easily conduct the analysis.

410810.label: Project Objectives
410810.value: We address inventory management when demand is uncertain but depends on the stocking quantity. We wish to address an open problem in this area: a general demand function by which demand varies with the stocking quantity and a general cost structure that includes both fixed and variable ordering costs. This is the basic model. We then extend the basic model to include non-zero leadtimes and expect to fully characterize the optimal inventory policies (when excess demand is backordered). We also aim to consider the combined inventory and pricing decisions when demand depends on both price and stocking inventory. An empirical study is also proposed to calibrate the results obtained for our models.

410810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410810.value: We will consider a set of problems that address the interface between marketing and operations. Research on retail inventory management has traditionally been based on the assumption that underlying demand does not vary with inventory levels. A growing body of marketing research supports the contention that the validity of this assumption has substantial implications for optimal inventory policies. Indeed, such research provides solid empirical evidence to show that a store's sales depend on the amount of stock displayed on its shelves. In the proposed study, we will investigate how inventory should be managed when inventory affects sales. We will assume inventory levels are monitored and determined periodically. In the basic setting, our concern is with inventory management when demand is uncertain, but is influenced by the displayed stock quantity. Our goal is to answer the open problem of a general demand function by which demand varies with the stocking quantity and a general cost structure. To gain insights into this problem and obtain structural results, we first assume that replenishment orders are delivered instantly after ordering. We then relax this restriction by allowing non-zero delivery leadtimes. We also consider the pricing effect, in addition to the inventory effect, on demand. Building upon the prior experience gained in related inventory-pricing control problems, we aim to establish structural results for general problems. Reports indicate that a lack of attention to the inventory effects on demand is one of the main reasons that store managers often overwrite the automated order advices generated by standard software packages developed by enterprise resource planning (ERP) vendors. The outcome of this research will be a set of inventory models and solution techniques that will serve as useful decision support in the field of supply chain management in general and inventory management in particular. 許多零售商發現提升的存貨量不僅改善服務水準而且還會刺激需求。市場行銷研究者通過實證研究發現許多零售商品的需求會和存貨陳列的數量呈現很強的正相關。大量的陳列可能會刺激需求的原因很多。例如，顧客對商品擁有更多的選擇（選擇效應）；現實中存在很多專業市場，如水果、蔬菜市場等，其需求尤其受此效應影響； 將商品大量堆放陳列可增加其能見度，藉此刺激潛在需求，獲得更大銷售的機率（廣告效應）； 高存貨量也會暗示消 費者該商品質優、暢銷，或是提供消費者一個高度未來的可獲得性的保證（暗示效應）；大量陳列某種商品時，往往減少顧客的找尋成本，增加了顧客服務水準 （服務效應）。 雖然存貨會刺激需求，但是隨者存貨水準的上升，相關的管理成本、持有成本的控管上，顯得更為重要。因此，許多文獻將這種需求類型融入庫存模型進行了深入研究。 但此類研究大多數假定確定性需求函數。 即便假定不確定性的需求函數，其他模型假設卻相當局限。 針對需求會隨存貨量增加的產品，本研究考慮一個連續補貨的庫存系統, 其需求量依賴於這種商品的貨架展示量. 旨在建構出一套具普遍性的庫存模型和進行系統的優化分析。 有行業報告指出，現有的自動補貨的庫存系統（往往包含在ERP系統中）由於缺乏對需求與貨架展示量相依的考慮，使得其實際應用受到很大限制。本研究將為填補這方面的欠缺做出努力，其成果可望應用于完善自動補貨的庫存系統。

410810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410810.value: We have addressed the inventory management problems in which demand is uncertain but depends on the stocking quantity. We successfully solved the problem with a general demand function and a general cost structure. Empirical evidence from retail industry shows that for some types of products, higher levels of on-shelf inventory have a demand-increasing effect (“billboard effect”) while for some other types of products, higher levels of on-shelf inventory have a demand-decreasing effect (“scarcity effect”). This suggests that retailers may use the amount of shelf stock on display as a tool to control demand and operate a store backroom to hold inventory of items not displayed on shelves. Then, retailers face the issue of efficiently managing the backroom and shelf inventories while also considering demand-influencing role of shelf stock level and lower operational costs of backroom storage. We are also able to address such an issue by considering a periodic-review inventory system in which demand in each period is stochastic and depends on the amount of inventory displayed on shelf. Structural results have been obtained and numerical examples show that the existence of backroom, and its joint replenishment with on-shelf inventory, generates significant profit gains under billboard and scarcity effects.

410910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410910.value: This proposal is to request support for research on electronic equalization using diverse optical filtering (DOF) for the mitigation of signal distortion due to fiber nonlinearity and chromatic dispersion (CD). Two electronic equalizers, namely, maximum likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) and combined feed-forward equalizer (FFE)-decision feedback equalizer (DFE), will be employed with the proposed DOF for the equalization in the systems with different modulation formats. Electronic equalization is one of the most active research fields in optical transmission systems. The electronic dispersion compensation (EDC) is one example that has gained wide acceptance in industry. Fiber nonlinearity-induced distortion is an important and challenging issue, especially for long haul dense wavelength-division-multiplexing (DWDM) transmission systems. The distortion not only impairs the transmission quality but also ultimately limits the number of channels and the transmission distance in DWDM networks. Compared to CD, these detrimental effects are more difficult to mitigate. The two aforementioned equalizers have yet to show good performance in combating the distortion due to fiber nonlinearity. In this project, we will investigate the mitigation of fiber nonlinearity-induced impairments and CD using electronic equalization with a novel approach of diverse DOF. Both theoretical study and experimental verification will be conducted to show its performance advances over the original equalizers. 摘要：本計劃旨在進行基於分集光濾波的電均衡方法對於光纖傳輸系統中光纖非線性效應和色散造成損傷補償的研究。對於不同的調製格式，我們研究結合分集光濾波的兩種電均衡方案，即最大似然序列估計和前饋及判決反饋均衡。電均衡是光纖傳輸系統中最熱門的研究領域之一，其中電色散補償技術已經在工業界得到廣泛的認可。光纖非線性效應造成損傷的補償是重要且具有挑戰性的研究內容，尤其在長距離密集波分複用系統中更是如此。光纖非線性效應造成的損傷不僅降低了信號傳輸的質量，更是密集波分複用網絡中信道數目和傳輸距離的限制因素。同色散相比，光纖的非線性效應更難補償。到目前為止，最大似然序列估計和前饋及判決反饋均衡對光纖非線性效應的補償性能還有待進一步提高。本計劃將研究用於光纖非線性效應及色散補償的基於分集光濾波新型電均衡方案，並用理論研究和實驗驗證給出該電均衡方案相對于傳統電均衡方案性能的提升。

410910.label: Realisation of objectives
410910.value: [Obj.1] We have experimentally investigated fiber Kerr nonlinearity mitigation for NRZ-OOK signals with diverse-optical-filtering (DOF) MLSE, in which DOF is realized by a delay interferometer (DI). Experimental results show that while conventional MLSE can hardly mitigate the impairment, DOF-MLSE can enhance the Q-factor significantly. [Obj.2] We have investigated the CD compensation capability of DOF-FFE by simulation [Ref. C3]. When the DOF is realized by super-Gaussian optical bandpass filters (OBPFs), the CD compensation capability of DOF-FFE increases linearly with the number of FFE taps and it does not saturate at least when the number of FFE taps is less than 129. With some penalty the CD tolerance of DOF-FFE is close to that of coherent FFE. When the DOF is realized by DI filters, the parameters of which are much easier to control, the optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) penalty as a function of the CD is small only in a window near the CD at which the parameters of the DI filters are optimized. [Obj.3] For more advanced modulation formats, we have investigated relevant digital signal processing (DSP) algorithms. We have proposed and investigated a hardware-efficient carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation algorithm for 16-QAM signals [Ref. J1]. Compared with conventional CFO estimation algorithms based on periodogram, our algorithm consumes substantially less memory and computation resources. We have also investigated DSP algorithms for coherent fast orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (F-OFDM) receivers, including 1) a blind maximum-likelihood CFO estimation algorithm to enhance the CFO tolerance [Ref. C4], and 2) a least-square dispersion estimation algorithm utilizing the start-of-frame (SOF) symbol, which can achieve near-optimum performance for joint symbol synchronization and channel estimation by using single SOF symbol [Ref. C5].

410910.label: Major findings and research outcome
410910.value: One of the major areas of this research is to improve the performance of short- and medium- range optical fiber communication systems and networks. In such systems a balance between performance and cost is required. For NRZ-OOK signals we have thoroughly investigated CD compensation with DOF-FFEs [Ref.C3]. Two types of optical filters, super-Gaussian filter and DI filter are considered. Simulation results show that the CD compensation performance of FFE can be significantly enhanced by DOF followed by joint equalization. For super-Gaussian DOF-FFE the required OSNR gradually increases with the accumulated CD, thus it can be utilized in optical fiber transmission systems and networks with dynamic links. However, for DI DOF-FFE the ONSR penalty may be small only near the CD value at which the parameters of the DI filters are optimized. Therefore, DI DOF-FFE is more suitable for the case when the transmission link is fixed. In addition, with some OSNR penalty both the two types of DOF-FFEs can compensate larger amount of CD with increased number of taps. Specifically, when the bit rate of the optical signal is 42.7 Gbit/s and the number of taps for each of the two branches is 129, the CD tolerance for super-Gaussian DOF-FFE at 5.8-dB OSNR penalty is 4,200 ps/nm, which is roughly 85% of that for coherent FFE with 129 taps. In related to signal processing to improve the throughput of time-division multiplexing passive optical networks (TDM-PONs) we have proposed and experimentally demonstrated a novel optical physical-layer network coding (PNC) scheme [Ref.J2]. Full-duplex error-free communications between optical network units (ONUs) at 2.5 Gb/s are shown for all-optical virtual private network (VPN) applications. Compared with the conventional half-duplex communications setup, our scheme can increase the capacity by 100% with a power penalty smaller than 3 dB. Synchronization of ONUs is not required for the proposed VPN scheme. We have also conducted a series of researches on DSP for advanced optical modulation formats. For optical QAM signals we have proposed a carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation algorithm based on eighth-order statistics [Ref.J1]. The CFO estimation algorithm does not involve FFT and can be implemented by hardware with little memory and computation resources. Simulation results show that in a 10.709-GBaud optical 16-QAM system, CFO ranging between ±1.25 GHz can be estimated with a uniform standard deviation of 2 MHz when the OSNR is 17 dB and 4^10 symbols are utilized. For coherent optical fast OFDM (F-OFDM) receivers we have also proposed a blind maximum-likelihood CFO estimation algorithm, and investigated its effectiveness in a 12-GSa/s 4-ASK F-OFDM system [Ref.C4]. Simulation results show that the algorithm can accurately estimate a CFO as large as ±3 GHz at 12 GSa/s, which leads to 300-times tolerance enhancement over a system without CFO compensation. The proposed method has low sensitivity to CD and less than 2-dB OSNR penalty can be achieved in the presence of 18,000-ps/nm CD and 2.5-GHz CFO. In addition, we have proposed a least-square dispersion estimation algorithm which utilizes the start-of-frame (SOF) symbol in coherent optical F-OFDM signals, and shown in a 37.5-Gb/s 16-QAM coherent optical F-OFDM experiment over 480-km fiber transmission that the proposed method can achieve near-optimum performance for joint symbol synchronization and channel estimation by using single SOF symbol [Ref.C5]. On the CD measurement we have proposed and demonstrated a novel dispersion measurement scheme with a large measurement range and relatively high accuracy. The scheme preserves the sign of the dispersion and is robust to the pulse broadening effect. [Ref.J3]

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410910.value: This project aims to explore cost-effective solutions for compensating/mitigating fiber transmission impairments in short- and medium-range optical fiber communication systems and networks, in which intensity modulation and direct detection may be preferred for their simplicity. However, in the process of direct detection phase information of the optical signal is lost and the performance of FFE/DFE for compensating/mitigating fiber transmission impairments is limited. Although MLSE can achieve impressive performance with direct detection, its complexity increases exponentially with the channel memory. In this project, we have thoroughly investigated a technique of diverse optical filtering (DOF) to convert part of the phase information of the optical signal into amplitude domain, and thus by direct detecting the optical signals after optical filters with different characteristics more information from the optical signal can be extracted. As a result, the performance of fiber transmission impairments compensation/mitigation can be significantly enhanced by the following joint equalization. DOF is a competitive candidate to compensate/mitigate fiber transmission impairments in short- and medium-range intensity-modulating optical fiber communication systems and networks, in which a balance between cost and performance is desired.

411010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
411010.value: 动态P2P系统的随机建模和优化

411010.label: Project Objectives
411010.value: To develop new queuing models for dynamic P2P systems. On one hand, the models should be flexible enough to capture the individual dynamics of customer and server peers, as well as their correlation. The models should be able to include classical models in which servers are mostly static as special cases. On the other hand, the new models should also be general enough to describe different P2P service systems by using a taxonomy. To characterize the system stability condition and the average customer delay for the new P2P queuing systems, and to investigate how these two aspects are affected by the customer and server peer dynamics and their correlation. These investigations are particularly relevant to P2P storage systems. The average customer delay is the average amount of time for a randomly-arriving customer peer to retrieve a file. Interestingly, our preliminary investigation shows that higher server peer dynamics leads to smaller average customer delay. This indicates that P2P storage systems with high server dynamics may offer better QoE as compared to cloud storage systems with sporadic server dynamics, which is in sharp contrast to the general belief. We plan to further explore the fundamental behind this somewhat surprising observation and its consequence. To explore stochastic optimization technique to optimize different types of QoE for various P2P service systems, by exploiting the peer dynamics captured by our models. As a concrete start, for the P2P video-on-demand (VoD) systems with dynamic user and helper peers, we have begun applying Markov Decision Process technique over the corresponding P2P queuing models to maximize the video quality users experience. Our preliminary results confirm there is considerable gain of optimizing video quality with peer dynamics taken into account. To implement prototype P2P storage and VoD systems, that follow insights and guideline generated from our investigation, over testbeds like PlanetLab [10] and characterize their performance. This prototypes, if successful, can crosscheck our theoretical results and evaluate the performance of our proposed solution in 3.

411010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
411010.value: Peer-to-peer (P2P) systems provide a scalable and cost-effective way to deliver content to multiple receivers over the Internet. The past decade has witnessed rapid evolution of commercial P2P systems providing various types of services, including file sharing (e.g., BitTorrent [1]), TV streaming (e.g., PPLive [2]), video-on-demand (e.g., UUSee [3]), and storage (e.g., Wuala [4]). P2P has become a major type of service traffic on the Internet. The flourish of P2P techniques has attracted a tremendous amount of research efforts to evaluate and optimize the performance of P2P systems. Many of the existing work evaluate the performance of practical P2P systems (see e.g., [5]). Some recent work design static P2P systems with provable quality of experience (QoE) guarantees (see e.g., [6,7,8]). However, P2P systems are dynamic in the sense that peers dynamically arrive and leave. For such dynamic P2P systems, the following fundamental questions were not addressed by existing work and remain largely open: • How to model dynamic P2P systems? • How to optimize QoE of P2P systems in the presence of peer dynamics? These questions are of great practical interest. For instance, consider a P2P storage system where users store files on a crowd of dynamic server peers and retrieve the files at a later time. It is critical to minimize the average delay for a randomly-arriving user to retrieve a file, and to quantify how server peer dynamics affects this delay. This project aims to answer the above two questions. We plan to first interpret dynamic P2P systems as a new type of queuing systems and characterize them by extending classical queuing models. In the new P2P queuing systems, both customers and servers arrive and depart randomly. This is different from traditional queuing systems where customers are dynamic but servers are mostly static. Then we plan to apply stochastic programming techniques to optimize QoE of P2P systems by exploiting the peer dynamics. Our preliminary investigation confirms there is indeed significant gain of optimizing QoE with peer dynamics taken into account. It also leads to a somewhat surprising observation: P2P storage systems with high server dynamics may offer better QoE as compared to cloud storage systems with sporadic server dynamics. We aim to build upon our initial results and further develop a general framework for modeling and optimizing dynamic P2P systems, and to guide the design of practical P2P systems with provable performance guarantees. 对等网络（P2P）系统提供了可扩展性和成本效益的方式将内容传递到多个接收器在互联网上。过去十年，人们目睹了商业的P2P提供各类服务，包括文件共享（BitTorrent），电视流（PPLive），视频点播（UUSee）和存储（Wuala）。 P2P网络已经成为服务的主要类型的互联网通信。 对P2P技术的蓬勃发展吸引了大量对P2P系统的性能的研究。有许多工作评估实际P2P系统性能。也有静态的P2P设计与体验质量保证。 然而，P2P系统是动态的，节点的到达和离开都是随机的。对于这样的动态系统，下面的根本问题没有得到解决： •如何对动态P2P系统建模？ •如何优化动态P2P系统的QoE？ 这些问题都是非常实际的。例如，考虑一个P2P存储系统，用户把文件存储在动态服务器上以便日后检索。系统的关键是要尽量减少一个随机到达用户的平均检索文件延迟，以及如何量化服务器的动态行为对这种延迟的影响。 该项目旨在回答上述两个问题。我们计划先把动态P2P系统解释为一个新型的排队系统。在新的P2P排队系统，客户和服务器随机到达和离开。这是和传统的排队系统不同。然后，我们计划运用优化技术，提升动态P2P系统的QoE。 我们的目标是建立在我们的初步结果上，进一步发展建模和优化，并指导实际的P2P系统的设计。

411010.label: Realisation of objectives
411010.value: For objectives 1 and 2, we have successfully developed queuing models for P2P service systems and taxonomy for different variations of these queueing models. For several basic classes of these systems, we derive the stability conditions and compare them to those results in the classical queueing theory. We also develop upper-/lower- bounds for average user delay. The tightness of the bounds is evaluated by numerical analysis. It turns out characterizing the exact average user delay for P2P queuing models is more difficult than we expected. It requires us to derive a closed-form expression for the steady-state distribution of a 2-D Markov chain even for the simplest model (in particular M/M/(M/M) model according our taxonomy). Deriving closed-form expression for multi-dimensional Markov chain is known to be very challenging. The only scenario that is known to be easy is when the Markov chain is time-reversible, where one can decompose the multi-dimensional Markov chain into multiple single-dimensional one to derive the steady-state distribution in a divide-and-conquer manner. However, the Markov chains we need to study in this project are not time-reversible, which makes the analysis very challenging. Instead, we manage to obtain lower and upper bounds via an involved analysis on the moment generating function of the user delay distribution. We have documented the results and are in the process of submitting the results for conference and later journal publication. For objective 3, we have developed optimization technique, called Markov Approximation, that systematically introduces system dynamics to optimize the system performance. The basic version of the technique focuses on systems with fixed number of entities (e.g., peers), and introduces dynamics for the interaction among the entities, for example adding and removing active connections among peers. The dynamics is introduced in a way so that it can be modeled by Markov chains. We have also extended the technique to leverage the case where the number of entities (e.g., peers) is time-varying and the dynamics is modeled by queuing models. The QoE we optimize for the system is the system-wide user (e.g., peer) throughput. Due to the time and resource limitation, the delay performance optimization is left for future investigation.

411010.label: Major findings and research outcome
411010.value: Recent development of Peer-to-peer (P2P) services (e.g. streaming, file sharing, and storage) systems introduces a new type of queue systems not studied before. In these new systems, both work and server arrive and depart randomly. The server dynamics may or may not correlate to the work dynamics. Motivated by these observations, we develop queuing models for P2P service systems and a taxonomy for different variations of these queueing models. We prove that these models are stable, i.e. all arriving work will be served and cleared in finite time, if the average work load does not exceed the average system service capacity. We also derive lower and upper bounds for the average user delay for these queuing systems. Furthermore, we develop optimization techniques to leverage the system dynamics to optimize the system performance. Overall, we believe that our models and techniques provide theoretical foundation for modeling and optimizing dynamic P2P systems, and also guidelines for the design of practical P2P systems with provable performance guarantee.

411010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
411010.value: Due to the time and resource limitation, we were not able to fully study the delay optimization in P2P systems by exploiting the system dynamics. We believe such study is important and has carried out follow-up investigation on the very topic.

411010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
411010.value: Our developed P2P queuing models are the first ones that enable systematic modeling of dynamics in P2P systems, as well as other service systems where servers and users arrive and depart randomly. Our models allow one to characterize the performance of the systems (such as throughput and delay), as functions of various system design parameters. Furthermore, we develop optimization techniques to exploit the system dynamics to optimize the system performance. We believe that our results are important for the research community as well as the practical system designer to understand and release the full potential of various system dynamics on improving system performance.

411110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
411110.value: The latest financial crisis entails the necessity of strict risk management on asset portfolios of financial institutions, including especially financial derivatives. The common practice in risk regulation is to summarize the portfolio’s risk profile according to a specific risk measure and request the institutions to reserve proportional capital against potential losses. Salient features of the distributions of risk factors and complicated cash flows embedded in the derivative contracts impose serious challenges on the calculation of such risk profile and in turn, make technical obstacles to the implementation of the aforementioned regulation policy. We propose this research to investigate how to make use of Monte Carlo simulation, an innovative numerical methodology, to tackle two subtopics in the broad area of risk management. They are: (1). American option sensitivities. American options entitle the holder a right to choose exercise time at her discretion. Most options traded on the exchanges are in American style and many other highly structured financial products contain American-option features. Price sensitivities provide a vital tool in the risk management of those derivatives and on the other hand, they cannot be observed directly in the market. Therefore, we need to develop accurate and efficient methods to estimate sensitivities. The dual approach by Rogers (2001) and Haugh and Kogan (2004), combined with the Monte Carlo sensitivity estimators studied by the PI, will yield upper and lower bounds for the sensitivities. (2). Nested simulation. Due to the lack of close form pricing formulae, a two-level Monte Carlo simulation is often used in practice to estimate the risk profile of derivative portfolios. The outer level generates different scenarios for the underlying risk factors and the inner level estimates the loss using sample averages under each scenario. Many samples are needed in each inner loop to make sure that the sample averages converge to the true value of the losses. Therefore, this method will incur tremendous computational efforts. We propose to explore how to utilize sequential analysis, a technique from statistical sciences, to screen out the scenarios which correspond to large losses. This will help us to detect the scenarios of interest earlier than a scheme with fixed sample size and to make the nested simulation more efficient. 近期的全球金融危機使得對金融機構所持有的資產組合，尤其是金融衍生品的相關資產的風險管理任務變得十分迫切和必須。在風險管理實踐中通常的做法是利用一種風險度量去衡量資產組合的風險特性，然後要求金融機構準備適當的資本以抵禦可能的損失。風險因素分佈中一些顯著的特性以及金融衍生品所蘊含的複雜現金流使得風險度量的計算問題充滿挑戰，同時在技術層面影響了金融風險監管的實施。 在本項目中，我們建議利用蒙特卡洛模擬方法去解決風險管理中的兩個問題。它們是： (1). 美式期權的敏感度問題。美式期權賦予持有人在他認爲適當的任何時候執行期權的權利。絕大多數在交易所交易的期權均為美式的，許多結構化的金融產品也包含有美式化的特點。價格的敏感度為我們提供了對其進行風險管理的關鍵工具，但是它卻不能在市場上直接觀察得到。爲此，我們需要發展出快速準確的估計方法去估計它。Rogers (2001) 和 Haugh and Kogan (2004), 結合上本項目的主要研究者所研究的蒙特卡洛敏感度估計法，將會為美式期權的敏感度提供上下界估計。 (2). 嵌套模擬問題。由於缺乏顯式的定價公式, 實踐中往往要利用分層模擬的方法去計算金融衍生品組合的風險度量。外層模擬生成風險因素的不同情境，内層模擬提供在各個情景下的損失估計。爲了保證樣本平均能夠收斂于損失真實值，每個内層模擬需要大量的採樣。因此該方法導致巨大的計算量。我們建議利用統計學中序貫分析的方法檢測出對應巨大損失的樣本。這樣會有助於提早發現可疑情形，從而使得嵌套模擬更爲有效。

411110.label: Realisation of objectives
411110.value: The project of GRF CUHK411110 set up two objectives in the proposal. Both of them have been achieved satisfactorily. The first objective is to develop Monte Carlo estimators to evaluate American option sensitivities. The principal investigator, together with one of his PhD student, introduce a generalized infinitesimal perturbation analysis (IPA) approach to resolve the difficulty caused by discontinuity of the optimal decision with respect to the underlying parameter. Our research has been extended to perform sensitivity analysis for stochastic optimization problems with model uncertainty, which has a wide application domain in the area of operations research. The outcome also makes a nice contribution to the literature of simulation: we point out that the pathwise continuity is not a necessary condition to apply the IPA approach. The related results are published in several venues, including the journal of Operations Research, a flagship journal of the area. We complete the initial proposed objective. The second objective of the project is to develop a method based on sequential analysis to improve the efficiency of the nested simulation for the purpose of measuring the risk profile of a derivative portfolio. An approach based on multilevel simulation technique is developed. The main idea is that we use sketchy simulation to obtain a “rough” measurement about the portfolio riskness, and then use some detailed simulation to fine-tune the estimation. Since our estimator consists of a linear combination of several standard nested estimators, it is very simple to implement and universally applicable. We establish computational complexity analysis results for the estimator, which shows that this approach is superior to the existing estimation methods in the literature. The original objective is fulfilled completely. The research outcomes are represented in a variety of scientific conferences. One PhD student was trained under this project. The PI is working together with him to revise his doctoral thesis for publication.
