411110.label: Major findings and research outcome
411110.value: The project makes two major findings. First, we develop a generalized IPA approach for studying the sensitivity analysis of the performance of a stochastic system in the presence of decision variables. Mathematically, we show that in a stochastic optimization problem, the expected value of the optimal performance is typically less sensitive to a change in the underlying parameter than the optimal decision itself. Based on this observation, we can still obtain sensitivity estimator by taking derivative along sample paths. This finding can be applied to establish unbiased estimators for American option price sensitivities. One peer-reviewed journal paper (paper 1 in Part C) was published to report these outcomes. Related to this work, another research paper (paper 2 in Part C) was submitted to Review of Financial Studies. It is now in the second round of review. The PI presented the same paper in the 2014 Western Finance Association annual meeting (see the link of paper 2 for the conference proceedings). The second finding is on efficiency improvement of the traditional nested simulation technique used widely in risk measurement of financial derivative portfolios. To evaluate portfolio riskiness, people typically rely on a two-step simulation scheme: they simulate market scenarios first, and then under each simulated scenario, use inner simulation to value portfolio. Such scheme takes considerable computational efforts and is widely viewed as inefficient in practice. We find that applying a multilevel technique, using a linear combination of a set of the standard nested estimators that have different amounts of inner and outer samples, will significantly save the computational costs to attain the same magnitude of estimation error. At the initial level, we allocate more resource in the outer stage simulation to reduce variance. At latter levels, we generate more inner samples for bias reduction; in the mean while, we combine the knowledge built up in the former levels to construct control variate for variance reduction. One PhD student (Student 3 in Part C) finished a thesis on this topic under the financial support of the project. We presented this result in several scientific conferences (conferences 1 and 2 in Part C) and are preparing to submit it to a journal for publication. Another two students (Students 1 and 2 in Part C) finished their theses under the support of this project.

411110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
411110.value: One particular near-term objective of the PI is to continue to work on prepare one publishable journal paper based on the student's thesis.

411110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
411110.value: Risk measurement of financial derivative portfolios is a challenging research topic in the area of financial engineering. Two types of measures are widely used in practice. One is based on sensitivity analysis, aiming to evaluate the portfolio price change in response to small market perturbation. The other is from some theoretical risk measures, focusing on the impacts due to large market dislocation. Monte Carlo simulation serves as an essential tool in both to estimate the risk profile of a financial derivative portfolio. The complex nature of the cash flows associated with derivative payoffs poses significant difficulties for us to develop efficient simulation-based methods. The current project overcomes the inefficiency of the traditional simulation schemes, and will have a great impact in the applications of financial industry.

411310.label: Project Objectives
411310.value: Building a powerful graph database engine. The primary objective is to build a domain-driven graph database engine that supports storage, indexing, query processing, mining and classification on software execution graphs to address software testing and debugging needs. We will coil program execution traces to form graphs and store them in the graph database. Different functionalities will be provided to facilitate mining and analysis of software executions. Graph classification for failure detection. The second objective is to build a classifier from a training graph dataset representing software executions to predict future software behaviors and detect anomalies. With this technique, it is possible to generalize past known errors to capture future failures and anomalies. We aim to mine a set of discriminative weighted subgraphs as classification features which are able to distinguish correct executions from failing ones. The weighted subgraphs carry weights on the edges to quantify the iteration number of functions calls. Discriminative graph mining for bug signature identification. We propose to identify bug signatures with a graph mining approach. Given two sets of graphs representing correct and faulty executions, we plan to extract top-k discriminative subgraphs which contrast the program flow of correct and faulty executions. The extracted subgraphs serve as bug signatures which highlight potential bug locations and provide informative contexts where bugs occur, which help to guide programmers in finding the source of bugs and correcting them. Graph indexing and query for software testing and debugging. We plan to build index for the software execution graphs to support efficient query processing. A user can express his search needs, e.g., some desirable behavior or a specific path, as a query to search the database. The techniques we will develop include constrained graph pattern matching with imposed node and edge constraints and graph similarity search. The tasks we will study include test case selection, suspicious behavior elicitation and example generation for debugging. Experimental evaluation and case studies. We plan to perform extensive experimental evaluation and case studies on the benchmark Siemens dataset and real, large-scale software systems to evaluate the accuracy, efficiency and scalability of our proposed graph classification, mining and indexing techniques in software testing and debugging applications.

411310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
411310.value: Software is a ubiquitous component of our daily life. Many critical scientific and industrial systems are dependent on the correct working of software systems. Due to the complexity of software systems, bugs and anomalies are prevalent. Bugs and anomalies have caused billions of dollars loss, caused privacy and security threats and even for some cases, the loss of lives. Software testing and debugging are important but expensive tasks to software developers. It is particularly hard to identify, locate and fix a bug given known failures in a system, as the bug can appear far from the point where a failure becomes observable. Therefore, automating part of the testing and debugging processes can substantially help in easing the programmers' effort in locating bugs and reducing the overall cost of software development. A past study has estimated the cost of debugging can go to billions of dollars annually. Given a set of test cases, software produces a massive amount of execution data called program traces. In this project, we plan to collect program traces and coil them into graphs to capture the control and data flow information. We aim to build a powerful graph database engine to support storage, indexing, query processing, mining, classification and maintenance of software execution graphs to address software testing and debugging needs. The graph database system contains three layers. The database layer at the bottom is for the physical storage of graphs representing software executions. The function layer in the middle provides functions including graph classification, discriminative graph mining, graph indexing and query processing. On the top is the application layer which supports various software testing and debugging tasks, for example, software behavior prediction for failure detection, bug signature identification, searching for suspicious behavior, etc. For a testing or debugging task in the application layer, we will formulate it as a graph search or mining problem and process it in the function layer. Through this study, we plan to provide an effective way to manage the repository of software traces. Users can mine the graph database and use the mining results for downstream software engineering applications. Users can also search for suspicious or desired behaviors by specifying their search needs as expressive graph queries. Our goal is to use graph mining and indexing techniques to facilitate software testing and enable automated debugging. We aim to improve the accuracy, efficiency and scalability of several testing and debugging tasks.

411310.label: Realisation of objectives
411310.value: The project objectives have been successfully achieved through our research. The details are as follows. Objective 1. We have collected a rich set of software data, including execution traces of benchmark programs, bug reports of open source projects, and programming APIs. We modeled them as graphs and stored them in a graph database. On top of the database, we have built a graph database engine, which supports various functionalities including storage, indexing, query processing, mining and classification. Objective 2. We have worked out an effective solution to graph classification for failure detection. We first created a training set of graphs modeling open source software projects. Then we mined discriminative rich subgraphs that appear frequently in the successful projects but rarely in the failed projects. These automatically mined patterns are effective features to predict project outcomes. Then we built a classification model to predict the class label, i.e., success or failure, of the software projects. Experimental results on a large open source software development portal showed that our approach could achieve an accuracy of more than 90% and an AUC score of 0.86. Objective 3. We have developed an effective solution to discriminative graph mining for bug signature identification. We first modeled program executions as graphs. Two sets of graphs corresponding to failures and correct executions are then contrasted to extract the most discriminative connected subgraphs serving as bug signatures. To exclude irrelevant components in the signature, we developed a signature minimization technique to capture minimal discriminative signatures. Also, we proposed a technique of signature fusion to fuse disconnected subgraphs so that our method can capture bug contexts spanning multiple locations. Experimental study on Siemens and Space dataset showed the effectiveness of the proposed bug signature minimization and fusion techniques. Objective 4. We have developed various graph indexing and query techniques to support software testing and debugging. We can effectively support API usage query, keyword search query, community query, graph search query, graph reachability query, shortest distance query, etc. Provided such query functions, a user can express his search needs to search desirable software behavior, e.g., suspicious software behavior, and help generate examples for debugging. Objective 5. We have conducted extensive experimental evaluation and case studies on the benchmark programs and real, large-scale software systems/repository/library, e.g., Siemens, Space, SourceForge, Java API library, etc., to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of the above research tasks.

411310.label: Major findings and research outcome
411310.value: The research results of this project have been published in 10 refereed journal papers and 18 refereed conference papers. The major findings are highlighted below. 1. We developed a graph classification approach to predict software project outcome. From an open source software development portal, we created a training set of graphs corresponding to successful and failed projects. A new data mining approach was proposed to extract discriminative rich patterns as classification features. We built a classification model to predict the project outcome. Experimental results showed that our approach could achieve an accuracy of more than 90% and an AUC score of 0.86. Please refer to the publication in Part C/Section 9/No. 9. A related graph classification approach which takes the feature diversity into consideration was published in Part C/Section 9/No. 8. 2. We proposed several algorithms for mining discriminative patterns, which can serve as bug signatures. (1) We developed a diversified discriminative feature selection approach to select subgraphs with high diversity (Part C/Section 9/No. 8). (2) We also designed an algorithm for mining closed discriminative dyadic sequential patterns (Part C/Section 9/No. 6). (3) We designed a semi-supervised approach for mining discriminative subgraph patterns with constraints (Part C/Section 9/No. 1). (4) We developed a signature minimization technique to capture minimal discriminative signatures, and a signature fusion technique to fuse disconnected subgraphs so that our method can capture bug contexts spanning multiple locations (Part C/Section 9/No. 4). 3. We developed various graph indexing and query processing techniques to support software testing and debugging tasks. We can effectively support API usage query (Part C/Section 9/No. 7), keyword search query (Part C/Section 8/No. 5), community query (Part C/Section 9/No. 17), graph structural search (Part C/Section 8/No. 6), graph reachability query (Part C/Section 8/No. 3), shortest distance query (Part C/Section 9/No. 2 and 5, Part C/Section 8/No. 4). We have systematically tested the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed methods. These graph query techniques can be used to support various software query tasks.

411310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
411310.value: The potential for further development of the research includes the following aspects. 1. Increase the expressiveness of the discriminative graph pattern as bug signature: we can further study how to increase the expressiveness of the discriminative graph pattern by incorporating attributes, numerical weights and textual content in the nodes and edges of the graph pattern. Such more complex and expressive patterns can carry more information as bug signatures to reveal the location and the underlying cause of bugs. We need to design a new mining algorithm to discover such graph patterns. 2. Support graph query with rich semantic meaning: we can further study how to support graph query with rich semantic meaning, for example, by combining structure with text. The answer to such a query should exhibit both high structural similarity and textual similarity. Thus the new query type is more expressive and powerful. We need to design an effective way to integrate and balance the structural and textual information in index construction and query processing.

411310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
411310.value: In our society, many critical scientific, industrial, healthcare, and service systems are dependent on the correct working of software systems. Due to the complexity of software systems, bugs and anomalies are prevalent. Bugs and anomalies have caused billions of dollars loss, caused privacy and security threats and even for some cases, the loss of lives. Software testing and debugging are important but expensive tasks to software developers. Therefore, automating part of the testing and debugging processes can substantially help in easing the programmers' effort in locating bugs and reducing the overall cost of software development. In this project, we developed various functionalities to facilitate software testing and enable automated debugging. Our techniques can effectively support various tasks, including software behavior prediction, software bug signature identification, test case selection, suspicious behavior elicitation, API usage suggestion, etc. Through extensive experimental evaluation and case studies, we achieved satisfactory accuracy, efficiency and scalability of these testing and debugging tasks. We believe that our techniques can help reduce the cost of software development, testing and debugging, and ensure the correctness and reliability of the software systems.

411910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
411910.value: In humans, the part of the central nervous system (CNS) responsible for balance control consists of the vestibular system (composed of three semicircular canals) and the cerebellum. However, due to the complexity in their shapes and the lack of specific image computing techniques in the past, little research has been carried out to objectively investigate the morphoanatomy of these complex CNS structures and to correlate them with clinical functional assessments. Our first objective is to develop a novel method to automatically extract semicircular canals images from T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This is technically challenging as the signal intensity of the semicircular canals is usually inhomogeneous, and a portion of it can be contaminated by imaging artifacts. Our second objective is to automatically segment the cerebellum from T1-weighted MRI images by exploiting its texture features and using them to guide the segmenter propagation. The third objective is to develop innovative surface comparison schemes that enable angle-preserving surface mapping for both genus-0 structures (cerebellar hemispheres) and structures with high-genus topology (semicircular canals). In this study, we would use adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) as a clinical example. AIS is a 3-D spinal deformity occurring commonly in adolescent girls. Its prevalence in Hong Kong is relatively high (4%). When untreated or improperly treated, the deformity may deteriorate progressively and cause significant cosmetic and functional problems. Impaired balance control is well known to be associated with this disease. It has been suggested that anatomical changes in the vestibular system and cerebellum might be related to poor balance control, which could be associated with the initiation and subsequent progression of the spinal deformity. This, however, is still a poorly studied area due to the lack of technology and computational techniques to extract, visualize and analyze these structures. In this project, we would like to investigate any statistical morphometric differences in the vestibular system and cerebellum between AIS and controls. In AIS patients, we would further study the correlation between these anatomical variations with clinical postural balance functional tests. Findings from the current study could provide better understanding of the relevance of these anatomical changes and its relationship to the etiopathogenesis of AIS and the progression of the spinal deformity. With further refinement, the technique could potentially provide objective guidelines for predicting the occurrence and progression of AIS – a matter of high clinical significance that would affect the treatment strategy of individual patients. 在人類的中樞神經系統中，前庭組織和小腦為負責平衡控制的器官。然而，由於其自身形態復雜，以及缺乏相應的圖像計算技術，目前對其解剖形態尚鮮有客觀的研究。本項目旨在開發創新的方法從核磁影像中自動提取前庭組織和小腦，並開發相應的統計形態測量學方法。我們將採用特發性青少年脊柱側彎（AIS）疾病作為臨床例子。 AIS是一種常發於青少年女性的三維脊柱形變，在香港的發病率相對較高(4%)。如果治療不當，側彎會進一步發展，嚴重影響病人的功能和外觀。並且，該疾病常引起平衡控制方面的問題。關於AIS的病因，有理論認為前庭系統和小腦的形態異常引起AIS病人在平衡感知方面失調，繼而引發脊柱的形變，並有可能造成形變的進一步發展。一直以來，由於缺乏相應的技術手段提取、顯示、分析這些組織的形態，相關的病因研究尚未開展。在本項目中，我們將致力於開發先進的計算技術來研究AIS病人相對正常對照在前庭組織與小腦之間的統計形態差異，以及解剖形態差異與AIS病人平衡控制功能之間的相關性。這項研究將會揭示平衡感知器的形態異常與AIS疾病發展的相關性，對AIS的臨床治療將有深遠的影響。

411910.label: Realisation of objectives
411910.value: The cerebellum was segmented from the cerebrum using the technique reported in [J07] according to the following procedures: (1) whole-brain normalization, (2) cerebellum isolation, (3) mapping with the statistical cerebellum template, and (4) cerebellum regional volume correction [C13]-[C15]. The cortical thickness was also measured in patients with scoliosis [J01] and [C05]-[C10]. Vertex-wise cortical thickness calculation and regional cortical thickness calculation were completed. The spinal cord is connected to the cerebellum, so a computational system was developed to create panoramic diffusion tensor images of the whole spine [J05], [C11], [C12]. The vestibular system was automatically segmented using a coarse-to-fine mathematical morphology method reported in [J02, J06]. After the segmentation, the cerebellum was statistically analyzed. The thickness of the cerebellar cortices was measured using the method reported in [J07]-[J08]. The shape of the semi-circular canal was assessed in [C01]-[C04] using the best-fit plane best-fit circle, and rotational angles of the morphology of the semicircular canals. A cerebellar template was constructed using the methods reported in [C16]-[C19], [C21]. The morphometry of the vestibular system was analyzed. A technique corresponding to the centerline of the semi-circular canal was adopted to measure the length of it in patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. We concluded that the changed length of the lateral canal of the VS is possibly associated with the postural balance and vestibular dysfunctions [J06] [C20]. In summary, we have successfully segmented and analyzed the cerebellum and the vestibular system. We studied the cerebellar morphological difference between patients with scoliosis and healthy control. We found that the cerebellum regions e.g. right I_IV was significantly larger than the left I_IV in the control group, and right I_IV is significantly larger than its left counterpart in the scoliosis group. For the vestibular system, after the segmentation, the length of the semi-circular canal was measured in patients with scoliosis and compared with the healthy controls. We reported that the lateral canal in scoliosis group is longer than that in the healthy control group.

411910.label: Major findings and research outcome
411910.value: The cortical thickness is measured between patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) and healthy controls. The experiment demonstrated that the cortical thickness declined significantly in almost all cortical lobes in normal subjects but in AIS patients this decline was weakly correlated with age (Spearman correlationN−0.4) and largely insignificant (P≥0.05). In addition, we concluded that the focal cortical thickness was significantly different in AIS patients compared with healthy controls in areas involved in motor and vestibular functions as well as object recognition. The findings from this study imply a different thinning pattern of the cerebral cortex during adolescence in patients with AIS; this may be primary (i.e. etiopathogenetic) or secondary (i.e. adaptation) to the development of scoliosis. [J01] A computational segmentation algorithm is developed and the reliability has been tested. Experimental results demonstrated that it is in high agreement with that from manual segmentation (intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.9892), and with a good correlation with visual scores (R = 0.8442, p < 0.0001) [J03]. After the segmentation of the vestibular system, the length of the semi-circular canal is measured and compared between AIS and healthy controls. Our results suggest that the lateral semi-circular canal in patients with AIS is shorter than that in healthy controls. We have proposed a hypothesis that the altered vestibular system is possibly associated with the poor postural balance and vestibular dysfunctions [J02, J06]. The current technology, due to the limited Field-of-View, can only capture a portion of the spine DTI image. To create a panoramic DTI image of the whole spine, we have developed a computational system based on feature-based registration and adaptive composition to stitch DTI images of the spine. This algorithm has been tested on a patient with scoliosis and a healthy control. [J05] We have successfully segmented and measured the cerebellum and we found that the cerebellum regions e.g. right I_IV was significantly larger than the left I_IV in the control group, and right I_IV is significantly larger than its left counterpart in the scoliosis group. [J07] After completing the segmentation of the cerebral cortices and cerebellum, we have analyzed the cortical network of AIS patients and our results demonstrated that they fully preserve the small-world architecture and organization, and further verify the hemispheric asymmetry of AIS brain with right thoracic. Our results indicated increased central role of temporal and occipital cortex and decreased central role of limbic cortex in AIS patients compared controls [J08].

411910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
411910.value: The segmentation technique can be further applied on different research studies. Experimental results support the cerebellar morphology is different from AIS and healthy controls. The effect of abnormal cerebellar morphology and the body functions should be further investigate. Furthermore, our results suggest that the lateral semi-circular canal in AIS patients is shorter than that in healthy control. The cause of the shorten canal would be an interesting topic to study the etiopathogenesis of AIS. A longitudinal study will provide long term data to observe the development of the canal compared between AIS and normal.

411910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
411910.value: This research project focuses on the segmentation and analysis on the vestibular system and cerebellum. Literature review suggests that the etiopathogenesis of AIS is possibly associated to the vestibular system which it is neurologically connected to the cerebellum. We have observed significant findings in the morphology of the cerebellum and the length of the semi-circular canals between patients with AIS and healthy controls. The results indicated that the shape of the cerebellum is different from patients with AIS and healthy control as well as the lateral semi-circular canal. We have concluded the poor postural balance in patients with AIS may associated with the altered vestibular system and functional study of the cerebellum in patients with AIS will be conducted in the further to enhance the understanding of the abnormal changed caused by AIS. The results obtained from this project are valuable in AIS studies from a neurological approach. The segmentation technique and analysis methods could also be used on other parts of the human body.

412510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412510.value: Regional anesthesia is the process of injecting local anesthetics into the body for nerve block in order to offer operative pain relief. Conventional regional anesthetic techniques that are dependent on anatomical landmarks (such as bone) of skin surface are associated with a relatively high failure rate (up to 20%). In the recent decade, the use of ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia (USRA) is growing rapidly. The success of these procedures is dependent on the correct identification of the neural structures and the surrounding soft tissues in the ultrasound scan. Due to the importance and the complexity of nervous system, it is essential for an anesthetist to possess a firm knowledge of ultrasound-imaged anatomy (sonoanatomy) before he or she operates on a patient. The ability to comprehend anatomic structure under ultrasound imagery is also the common first step in many complex interventional procedures such as biopsy, percutaneous drainage and tube insertion. Virtual reality (VR) based learning of sonoanatomy is feasible when an anatomic correlation of clinical ultrasound images to a database of ultra-high resolution virtual human limb/spinal datasets is available for the learner to interactively scan and visualize in virtual space. Interactive rendering of different ultrasonic characteristics (e.g. speckle, attenuation and tissue anisotropy), vascular deformation and the blood Doppler effect are also essential for the nerve localization on top of the correlated ultrasound imagery. Due to the complexity and deformity of different human musculoskeletal, vascular and nervous structures, it is a great challenge to build a virtual sonoanatomy system that provides realistic anatomic/ultrasonic visualization coupled with physically based deformation. In this project, we propose to build a virtual sonoanatomy system to facilitate physicians in learning ultrasound guided regional anesthesia. One of the main objectives of this proposed research is to develop state-of-the-art virtual environment that facilitates interactive sonoanatomy learning. The research issues to be addressed include image segmentation, 3D anatomical model reconstruction, data fusion of multiple modalities data, realistic rendering and deformation, interactive navigation and visualization as well as multi-sensory human-computer interaction. This training system will provide an actual view of ultrasound images, in real-time, while performing an examination on a life-like mannequin. This is a cost-effective approach to providing standardized clinical education, training and accelerated learning. 412510.label: Realisation of objectives
412510.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a virtual reality simulation system that matches all the original project objectives to facilitate the training of anesthetists and medical students in learning regional anesthesia related sonoanatomy. Key research and development issues addressed in this project include feature detection in ultrasound imagery, ultrasound segmentation, anatomical model reconstruction, human computer interfacing for anatomy learning, and interactive surgical skill visual guidance and training with haptics. In our developed prototype, interactive navigation of huge Chinese Visible Human (CVH) data is presented to user, in real-time, while performing a simulated ultrasound examination of regional anesthesia related scan plane alignment. We have designed a multi-resolution framework for ultrasound image segmentation based on combinative active contours; such an approach is further enhanced to a multi-scale version through the incorporation of speckle reducing anisotropic diffusion. We have also proposed a novel standard ultrasound plane localisation by radial component for image analysis. In order to fully exploiting the rich information inside B-mode ultrasound image, we presented a novel descriptor based on quantized local edge distribution. By utilizing a local phase-based measure call multi-scale feature asymmetry, we have developed a novel phase-based feature detection technique for fetal ultrasound images. Via using phase information and incorporating iterative randomized Hough transform, we further proposed an enhanced ultrasound feature detection for measuring of abdominal contour in fetal images. To enable MRI –TRUS registration, a personalized modelling of prostate deformation based on elastography is proposed. A coarse-to-fine normal filter for mesh denosing based on isotropic sub-neighborhoods is also developed. We presented an interactive high-fidelity GPU-based haptic needle simulation engine; such an engine has been exploited to develop a virtual reality simulator for training biopsy. On top of this, we proposed a serious game based system for learning general ultrasound-guided needle placement skills for radiologists and anesthetists; we also presented a novel needling guidance approached based on the visualization of needle access pathway and we conducted a 5 degree-of-freedom evaluation to prove the effectiveness of our system. In order to facilitate intuitive anatomy learning, we proposed an interactive cross-sectional anatomy navigation system called CVHSlicer – where the whole system can be executed on just a normal personal computer with ultra-fine high-resolution CVH data. We also developed a new tangible handheld device interface, for interactive exploration and annotation of volume data. Futhermore, an interactive web-based anatomy navigation system is implemented via WebGL and Kinect so that navigation can be made user-friendly.

412510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412510.value: In our future work, we aim to annotate the anatomical structure in the virtual sonoanatomy interface, extend the ultrasound feature-detection algorithm, conduct more in-depth system evaluations and extend our system to other body regions. Such a virtual surgical simulator can truly provide an intuitive learning of difficult sonoanatomy based on ultra-fine resolution Chinese Visible Human data. Our proposed course of actions include – • Collaborate with medical surgeons and anesthetists for further evaluation and refinement of our existing prototypes. • Provide software licensing for educational purpose and beta testing. • Search for industrial collaborators for technology transfer in the area of virtual surgery and virtual anatomy learning. • Continue to seek new research grants to further our research in virtual anatomy and surgical simulation.

412510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412510.value: The success of ultrasound-guided regional pain management procedures is dependent on the correct identification of the neural structures and the surrounding soft tissues in the ultrasound scan. Due to the importance and the complexity of nervous system, it is essential for an anesthetist to possess a firm knowledge of ultrasound-imaged anatomy (sonoanatomy) before he or she operates on a patient. However, the ability to comprehend anatomic structure under ultrasound imagery has been very difficult to master through conventional learning-by-seeing approach. In this project, we developed a virtual reality (VR) based learning environment for studying ultrasound guided regional anesthesia related sonoanatomy. Interactive scan and visualization in virtual space on a database of ultra-high resolution virtual human datasets is considered as the most important item to help physicians in learning anatomical landmarks and as well as its relation to the corresponding ultrasound scan features. In the training of anesthetic needle placement, our needle guidance implementation delivers a unique and intuitive learning experience with no need to practice on patients. Our virtual environment can truly facilitate interactive sonoanatomy learning and strengthen existing anesthetic training. This may lead to technology transfer of related virtual reality based anatomy learning systems.

412710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412710.value: Mobile wireless data service is becoming increasingly popular, thanks to the worldwide deployment of high-speed cellular networks and Wi-Fi access points. It has become an important revenue source for wireless service providers. For example, revenue of the US mobile wireless data market reached 45 billion US dollars in 2009. Meanwhile, market competition is intensive as providers try to offer good services and low prices to attract customers. To prosper in the wireless data industry, it is critically important for wireless service providers to implement sound wireless spectrum resource allocation and pricing mechanisms to achieve good revenue and profits. Compared with the traditional wireless voice traffic, wireless data applications are more elastic and bandwidth-consuming; thus these applications require new and different revenue management solutions. However, there does not yet exist a conceptually unifying, mathematically rigorous, and practically relevant framework for revenue management of wireless data networks. The goal of this project is to build such a framework. We will answer the following key questions: (a) how should a wireless service provider allocate and price resources to maximize revenue?; and (b) how should a user choose the service provider(s) to achieve the best performance-cost tradeoff? We will answer these questions under various practical network scenarios, such as differential pricing mechanisms, incomplete network information, competition between wireless service providers, and flexible total network resources. We will also consider the key features of wireless technologies, including heterogeneity of users and the Quality of Service requirements of data applications. The proposed research intends to bridge the gap between the classical economic analysis and the pure engineering design of wireless communication networks. The PI and Co-I have strong and complementary research expertise in wireless communications, microeconomics (game theory and pricing), and operations research (optimization and stochastic control), and thus are in a good position to address the relevant issues. The outputs of the proposed research will lead to a new design and analysis framework for wireless resource allocation to better serve the customers and increase the providers' economic incentives. Its findings are expected to spur the development of new business models for the wireless communications industry, including the latest technologies. 412710.label: Major findings and research outcome
412710.value: The following is the summary of results of this reporting period, i.e., April 2012 - November 2014. (1) We designed contract, auction, and game mechanisms for wireless user cooperations under incomplete network information (journal publications 5, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17, 18, and conference publications 17, 27, and 28). (2) We designed price differentiation mechanisms for wireless network resource allocation, and understood the impact of incomplete network information (journal publication 6). (3) We designed effective spectrum sharing mechanisms and innovative information market mechanism based on wireless spectrum database (journal publication 7 and conference publications 24, 26, and 29). (4) We proposed an auction framework for distributed power allocation in multiuser cooperative networks (journal publication 15). (5) We analyzed the pricing practices of local and global WiFi operators, considering the user behaviors and market coverage (conference publication 18). (6) We analyzed the upgrading timing of cellular network operators, considering the network upgrade cost, the benefits of the new technology, and the network effect (conference publication 19). (7) We provided regulatory suggestions regarding whether to allocate additional spectrum to WiFi or cellular networks (conference publication 20). (8) We characterized the fairness and efficiency tradeoff for user cooperation in distributed wireless networks (conference publication 21). (9) We proposed pricing and incentive mechanisms in user-provided wireless networks (conference publications 22 and 32). (10) We proposed a family of network selection and incentive mechanisms for effective mobile data offloading (conference publications 23, 32, and 33). The following is the summary of results of the previous report period (September 2010 - March 2012). All publications are reported in Part C. (1) We studied how selfish wireless users share spectrum effectively considering spatial reuse (journal publication 1 and conference publications 11, 13, 15). (2) We studied the revenue optimization problem in stochastic cognitive radio networks (journal publication 2). (3) We studied the network bargaining between licensed and unlicensed users in wireless networks to achieve a win-win situation (journal publication 3 and conference publications 2, 4, 6, and 8). (4) We studied the interactions between cognitive virtual network operator and the users (journal publications 4 and 9). (5) We studied how multiple wireless cellular providers set access pricing to maximize the social welfare (conference publications 1). (6) We studied how a cellular service provider allocates and prices resource in femtocell services (journal publication 16 and conference publication 5 and 30).

412810.label: Project Title(Chinese)
412810.value: 持续激励条件,参数收敛,及一类非线性自适应控制系统的稳定性分析

412810.label: Project Objectives
412810.value: Develop a novel approach based on YW lemma to study the global uniform asymptotic stability of a nonlinear uncertain system under an adaptive control law. A direct consequence of this result is to prove that the PE condition guarantees that the estimated parameters can converge to the actual unknown parameters. It is known that the output regulation problem with an uncertain exosystem can be converted into an adaptive stabilization problem of an augmented nonlinear system. This project will show that the PE condition can be made satisfied if the internal model is minimal. Thus it is possible to identify the unknown frequency by employing a minimal internal model. Apply the methodology to solve some benchmark control problems such as the synchronization of an unknown harmonic system with the Lorenz system, and the asymptotic tracking of the FitzHugh-Nagumo model.

This project will show that the PE condition can be made satisfied if the internal model is minimal. Thus it is possible to identify the unknown frequency by employing a minimal internal model.

412810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412810.value: Control systems invariably contain unknown parameters. Adaptive control is an important control approach aimed at accounting for parametric uncertainty in control systems. The basic idea in adaptive control is to estimate the uncertain parameter on-line and use the estimated parameter in the controller design. This idea was conceived in the 1950s and has been implemented in many control problems such as the design of autopilots for high-performance aircraft. One of the most important issues associated with the adaptive control is the stability property of the closed-loop system. For linear systems, various conditions have been established to guarantee the uniform asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. Moreover, if certain input signal satisfies the so-called persistency of excitation (PE) condition, then the equilibrium point of the closed-loop system can be made uniformly asymptotically stable (UAS). As the parameter estimation error is part of the state of the closed-loop system, the PE condition also guarantees the convergence of the estimated parameters to the true parameters. This result is established by applying a quadratic Lyapunov function to the closed-loop system. Nevertheless, the stability issue of a nonlinear plant under an adaptive control law is not adequately addressed. In particular, it is unclear whether or not the PE condition can still guarantee the global uniform asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. In this project, we will develop an alternative approach to addressing the stability issue in a nonlinear adaptive control system. This approach utilizes a key lemma developed by Yuan and Wonham to show that, for a class of nonlinear systems in output feedback form, if certain signal satisfies the PE condition, then the origin of the closed-loop system resulting from a class of nonlinear adaptive control laws is globally UAS. Then we will further study the problem of the nonlinear output regulation subject to an unknown exosystem. It is known that this problem can be handled by using the adaptive control technique. What we will further establish is that if the internal model used for handling the output regulation problem is of minimal order, then the PE condition of certain signals will be satisfied. Therefore, the closed-loop system can be made globally UAS. Finally, we will apply the theoretical result to some practical control problems including the chaotic control of Chua’s circuit, synchonization of the Lorenz system with an unknonw harmonic system, and the asymptotic tracking of the FitzHugh-Nagumo model etc. 控制系统不可避免地包含未知参数。自适应控制是旨在对付系统不确定性的一个重要方法。 自适应控制的基本思想是在线估计未知参数并用被估计的未知参数设计控制器。自适应控制的一个重要问题是闭环系统的稳定性分析。对于线性系统, １９７０年代即已发现若干条件可保证闭环系统的全局稳定性。值得一提的是, 如果系统的输入信号满足所谓的持续激励条件， 则可使闭环系统的平衡点渐进一致稳定，因而持续激励条件可保证未知参数收敛于其真值。然而对于非线性系统, 在自适应控制下, 闭环系统的稳定性问题尚未得到透彻了解。尤其是目前对持续激励条件是否可保证未知参数收敛于其真值这一问题仍然没有答案。 本项目将提出一种有新方法来探讨一类非线性自适应控制系统的全局稳定性。该方法基于Yuan 和Wonham 在１９７７年提出的一个关键引理。我们首先将证明, 对一类输出反馈非线性系统, 持续激励条件仍然可保证闭环系统的全局稳定， 从而保证未知参数收敛于其真值。其次， 我们将进一步研究非线性系统在未知外部系统作用下的输出调节问题。众所周知，该问题可用自适应控制方法来研究, 我们将探讨最小内模是否可保证持续激励条件得到满足。最后, 我们将项目的理论结果应用于包括蔡氏电路，洛伦斯系统等若干系统的控制。 本项目的成功将不仅推进非线性控制系统的自适应控制的研究, 并且将导致前面提到的若干实际系统的全局抗干扰问题及全局渐进跟踪问题的解决。

412810.label: Realisation of objectives
412810.value: This project aims to achieve the following three objectives: 1. Develop a novel approach based on YW lemma to study the global uniform asymptotic stability of a nonlinear uncertain system under an adaptive control law. A direct consequence of this result is to prove that the PE condition guarantees that the estimated parameters can converge to the actual unknown parameters. 2. It is known that the output regulation problem with an uncertain exosystem can be converted into an adaptive stabilization problem of an augmented nonlinear system. This project will show that the PE condition can be made satisfied if the internal model is minimal. Thus it is possible to identify the unknown frequency by employing a minimal internal model. 3. Apply the methodology to solve some benchmark control problems such as the synchronization of an unknown harmonic system with the Lorenz system, and the asymptotic tracking of the FitzHugh-Nagumo model. So far all three objectives have been successfully achieved. The research results have led to several chapters in one book, 5 journal papers, 10 conference papers, and numerous keynote speeches or invited talks. Four PhD students have been supported or partially supported by this project. Additionally, we have further expanded the scope of the research to study the output regulation problem for a multi-agent system via a distributed control scheme. This problem is called cooperative output regulation problem. We have shown that our results include the leader-following consensus problem as a special case.

412810.label: Major findings and research outcome
412810.value: We have successfully achieved all objectives. The main findings are summarized below. 1. For a class of nonlinear systems, we have shown that the PE condition guarantees the global uniform asymptotic stability of closed-loop system under a specific adaptive control law. We have further shown that the PE condition and the minimal order internal model guarantees that the estimated parameters can converge to the actual unknown parameters. This class of nonlinear systems includes the Lorenz system, the FitzHugh-Nagumo model, and the rigid body spacecraft system as special cases. The main findings have appeared in the Conference papers 1 and 7, and also entered Chapters 2, 5, 9 and 10 of the following book: Zhiyong Chen and Jie Huang, Stabilization and Regulation: Robust and Adaptive Approach, Springer, September 2014. The journal version of the conference paper 1 will appear as follows: Z. Chen and J. Huang, “Attitude tracking of rigid spacecraft subject to disturbances of unknown frequencies,” International Journal of Robust and Nonlinear Control, DOI:10.1002/rnc.2983 2. We have studied the cooperative output regulation problem of uncertain nonlinear multi-agent systems, The results have laid a foundation for further studying the same problem under an unknown known leader by adaptive control. The main findings have led to the publications of Journal papers 2, 4, and 5 and conference papers 2-6, 8,10. 3. We have extended our study on the attitude control of a single spacecraft system into the leader-following consensus of multiple spacecraft systems. The main findings have appeared in conference paper 9. 4. We have applied the nonlinear output regulation theory to the control of spherical inverted pendulum system and published the journal paper 1. 5. We were invited to write a survey paper on (Journal paper 3) advanced nonlinear and adaptive control.

412810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412810.value: In this project, we have initiated our study on the cooperative output regulation problem of nonlinear multi-agent systems. We will further pursue our research on this topic along the following directions: 1. Extend our results on the cooperative output regulation problem of multi-agent systems from static communication graph to dynamic communication graph 2. Further consider the leader-following consensus problem with connectivity preservation 3. Study the output regulation problem of linear and nonlinear systems with time-delay.

412810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412810.value: Control systems invariably contain unknown parameters. Adaptive control is an important approach to handle parametric uncertainty in a plant. One of the most important issues associated with the adaptive control is the stability property of the closed-loop system. For the class of linear systems, various conditions have been established to guarantee the global stability of the closed-loop system. This approach to establishing the parameter convergence is called the Lyapunov argument. Nevertheless, the stability issue of a nonlinear plant under an adaptive control law had not been well addressed before. In this project, we have developed an alternative approach to address the stability issue in a nonlinear adaptive control system.. We have shown that, for a quite general class of nonlinear systems, PE condition of certain signals can guarantee the global uniform asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. Then we have further studied the problem of the output regulation problem of nonlinear systems subject to an unknown exosystem. Finally, we have applied the theoretical result to some practical control problems such as the spacecraft system. The results of this project has significantly advanced the research on the nonlinear adaptive control.

413110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413110.value: Extracting high quality moving foreground layers from a video is generally referred to as bilayer segmentation. It is one of the important problems in computer vision due to the necessity of many applications to cut out the captured characters for creating visual effects, such as inserting the foreground into a virtual environment; or for accomplishing nontrivial content-based adjustment in the input video, such as removing unwanted objects and modifying motion in multiple frames. Albeit important and necessary in video editing, high-quality layer separation from a video is very challenging because tightly coupled layering, depth, and motion information introduce a large number of variables and high ambiguities in computation. Previous methods made various assumptions, such as fixed camera and/or simple background color distribution, to make the problem tractable. However, it is very common that a video is taken under the condition that these requirements are not satisfied. In these cases, a more robust algorithm that can relax these conditions is in high demand. It is observed that the main difficulty of layer separation lies in background modeling. If the background image is known (a static or rotating camera makes it possible to construct the background image by the clean plate or image mosaicking techniques), it is relatively easy to obtain the foreground estimate using the color and structure information. Otherwise, both layers have uncertain pixel assignment and there exists a large ambiguity to identify them. The latter scenario commonly arises when using a handheld camera. In this project, we plan to tackle this challenging problem with the input of only a video sequence taken by a freely moving camera. Our goal is the high-quality dynamic foreground extraction, which requires that the foreground estimate is accurate and temporally consistent along the boundary in multiple frames. In the meantime, we will solve the dense motion and depth estimation problems for the extracted layers, which are also considered very important and difficult conventionally. Our plan will be detailed further below in this proposal, wherein our research will advance in several ways to increase the accuracy of bilayer segmentation, especially in texturally complex regions, and will extensively explore the relationship between depth/motion estimation and bilayer segmentation so as to enhance both of their estimates. 從視頻中提取高質素的移動前景層，通常被稱作雙層分割（bilayer segmentation）。這是機器視覺領域的一個重大研究課題之一，因為許多應用都依賴於該技術，或用於提取出拍攝的人物角色，用以製作視覺特效，比如將前景插入虛擬環境中，或者用於實現一些非平凡的基於內容的視頻調整，比如去除不需要的物體和修改多個幀中的運動。 雙層分割在視頻編輯中很重要而且是必須的，但是高質素的視頻分層仍然有很大挑戰性，這是由於層與層之間的緊密結合、深度層次關係、運動信息給計算引進了大量的變量和高不確定性。爲了簡化問題使之易於處理，以前的方法做了各種的假設，譬如攝影機位置固定和/或簡單的背景顏色分佈。但是，經常出現的情況是，一般視頻的拍攝條件不滿足這些要求。在這種情況下，我們非常需要一個更加魯棒而且放寬這些限制條件的算法。 我們可以看出分層的主要難點在於背景建模。如果背景圖已知（靜止或者旋轉的攝影機使得我們可以用純背景（clean plate）和圖像拼接技術來構造背景圖），用顏色和結構信息來估計前景是相對簡單的。否則，前景和背景這兩個層都包含有不定的像素點，並且確定這些像素值存在很大的不確定性。在使用手持攝影機時，後面這種情況經常遇到。 在本項目中，我們的計劃是，在僅輸入一個使用自由運動的攝影機拍攝的視頻序列的情況下，解決這個具有挑戰性的問題。我們的目標是提取高質素的動態前景，即要求提取出的前景必須準確，而且在多個幀中前景邊界有時域上的一致性。同時，對於這些提取出的圖像層，我們還要解決它們之間的密集運動（dense motion）和深度層次這兩個在傳統意義上認為很重要也很困難的問題。 我們的計劃將會在下文進一步詳述。我們的研究，會從幾個不同的方面，增強雙層分割的準確性，尤其是在紋理複雜的圖像區域；同時深入探討分析層與層之間的深度/運動估計和雙層分割這兩者之間的關係，以提高它們估計的準確性。

413110.label: Realisation of objectives
413110.value: For the first objective to develop the dense depth and motion estimation method with the consideration of foreground/background labeling, we have evaluated all existing methods. None of them is enough to tackle our problems. We note Structure-from-motion (SFM) and multi-view stereo matching can be applied to static scenes where global constraints are established through the multi-view geometry. However, it is also not suitable for videos that contain moving or deforming objects. Our solution is nontrivial - it not only estimates its actual disparity value, but also determines the object segment it belongs to. We proposed new chained temporal constraints to make long-range depth-flow estimation less problematic. Our method is to generate consistent depth and scene flow, utilizing pixel correspondence among multiple frames. It consists of main steps of initialization, temporal constraint establishment, and final depth and joint scene flow refinement. To build the robust bilayer segmentation model, we come up with a novel frame-selection scheme - rather than summing the matching cost over all frames, we propose the strategy for multiview geometry enforcement by picking frames where corresponding pixels exist (or are visible). We introduce an effective method to search for frames that contain non-occluded matching pixels for each reference pixel. Based on the fact that occluded pixels generally have small disparity values, we apply an easy but effective algorithm for label map inpainting. This strategy is very useful for pixels near discontinuous boundaries where occlusion commonly arises, and in the meantime does not affect depth estimation for other visible pixels. Finally, to construct a practical system, we propose complete objective functions incorporating all previous techniques. In the first place, the label maps of the whole sequence are unknown. So the energy cannot be directly solved. We introduce a system initialization step to separately estimate a label map for each frame by removing the geometric coherence constraint. To handle textureless regions and make the following refinement easier, we also incorporate color segmentation in the initialization step. We use all terms in the data function and progressively update the estimates by minimizing the energy. The frames are processed sequentially starting from the first one. In optimizing label map, we fix the estimates in other frames. Two passes of optimization is adopted to let all frames be processed with nearly even neighborhood information. In short, our method remarkably improves segmentation and disparity estimation. All objectives stated in the proposal have been achieved with these new techniques.

413110.label: Major findings and research outcome
413110.value: In this project, we have proposed a few important and fundamental techniques for solving computer vision problems. They improve state-of-the-art of motion estimation, bilayer segmentation, to name a few. Our methods are presented in a few high-quality academic papers published in CVPR, ICCV, IJCV, TOG, etc. 1. In the paper published in IJCV in year 2014, we present a depth and image scene flow estimation method. The key component is motion-depth temporal consistency preservation, making computation in long sequences reliable. We tackle a number of fundamental technical issues, including connection establishment between motion and depth, structure consistency preservation in multiple frames, and long range temporal constraint employment for error correction. We address all of them in a unified depth and scene flow estimation framework. 2. We in SIGGRAPH Asia 2011 present a new editing tool, greatly helpful for characterizing and enhancing fundamental image constituents, i.e., salient edges, and in the meantime for diminishing insignificant details. Our objective is to globally maintain and possibly enhance the most prominent set of edges by increasing steepness of transition while not affecting the overall acutance. It enables faithful principal structure representation. This idea leads to an unconventional global optimization procedure involving a discrete metric, whose solution enables diversified edge manipulation according to saliency. 3. In the essential dictionary learning framework, we found s dictionary contains many atoms in general. Its scale is highly variable, ranging from hundreds to hundreds of thousands in different applications. We proposed a Scale Adaptive Dictionary Learning (SADL) method. It is a unified framework to learn the sparse dictionary representation and determine the appropriate number of atoms simultaneously, which has a dissimilarity lower bound for any two atoms theoretically. This paper was published in TIP. 4. In CVPR 2012, we found patch-level linear features do not always work as well as handcrafted features. We alternatively propose a model to greatly improve the usefulness of linear features in classification by introducing covariance patterns. We analyze their properties, discuss the fundamental importance, and present a generative model to properly utilize them. With this set of covariance information, in our framework, even the most naive linear features that originally lack the vital ability in classification become powerful. 5. In this project, we also deal with human recognition for multiple images or sequences. It is a co-detection and labeling (CoDeL) framework to identify persons that contain self-consistent appearance in multiple images. Our CoDeL model builds upon the deformable part-based model to detect human hypotheses and exploits cross-image correspondence via a matching classifier. The paper was published in ICCV 2013.

413110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413110.value: In the current multi-body stereo method for constructing high-quality depth maps and for segmentation of several moving rigid objects from an input monocular image sequence, the new multi-body stereo label representation couples depth and segmentation indices, making it possible to employ optimization to simultaneously compute these two sets of variables. The multi-body plane fitting method is introduced to improve initial estimates in textureless regions, together with disparity hole filling to offer additional matching information for occluded pixels. Our method can handle independently moving rigid objects. Further development will be on handling nonrigid objects in this system, for example, water, changing light, and dancing persons. These objects currently could cause problems in segmentation when they deform in consecutive frames. Possible solutions are on deformable object modeling by non-linear function fitting and new energy definition.

413110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413110.value: Both stereo-based 3D reconstruction and image/video segmentation have been fundamental problems in computer vision for long time, due to the critical need of high quality depth and segment estimates in many applications, e.g., recognition, image-based rendering, and image/video editing. However, these two problems were researched typically along different lines. In this project, we propose a new system to simultaneously achieve dense depth estimation and motion segmentation for multiple rigid objects undergoing different movements. The significance includes a new multi-body stereo representation that couples depth and segmentation labels, and a global estimation method to minimize a unified objective function, which notably extends multi-view stereo to scenes with several surfaces independent in motion. We also proposed an adaptive-frame-selection scheme with a depth and segment hole filling algorithm for effective occlusion handling. The objective function is solved by an iterative optimization scheme. It first initializes labels with a novel multi-body plane fitting algorithm, and then iteratively refines them by incorporating the geometry and segment coherence constraints in a statistical way among multiple frames. Our method can yield spatio-temporally consistent depth and segment maps.

413210.label: Project Objectives
413210.value: Our first objective is to provide an in-depth study on the current state-of-the-art {\em Semi-supervised Learning} (SSL) techniques. Here, we may consider two main approaches typically found in semi-supervised learning. The first approach is based on the clustering assumption which assumes that the training data are well-prepared and fall in a typical distribution. The second approach is based on the manifold assumption which assumes that most data lie on a low-dimensional manifold in the input space. Our second objective is to extend the theoretical understanding of the SSL framework. Since web-based data are unlabeled and contain both relevant as well as irrelevant information, the task of extract useful information from the data set for classifiers to learn is a difficult and important task. We plan to first focus on using kernel-based SSL classifiers, a specific family of classifiers, which are popular and have shown potential effectiveness in classifying web-based data. The third objective is to evaluate the performance of the proposed extensions to the SSL framework and its associated algorithms through a set of systematic and rigorous experiments on synthetic and real-world data. We will define the performance criteria in terms of the accuracy, error rate, and computational resources needed based on cross-validation methodology for our analysis. The fourth objective is to implement possibly one SSL-based applications to validate our proposed SSL framework for social computing: (1) a personalized classification algorithm or (2) a personalized ranking algorithm.

413210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413210.value: With the advent of the Internet, social network mining tasks such as community identification, social page classification, etc. have become a hot research topic. These social data collected from social networks sites are typically voluminous, unlabeled, and embedded with public and hidden social information. Semi-Supervised Learning (SSL) is a machine learning paradigm that handles both labeled and unlabeled data in an effective manner. Although SSL seems to be a good approach to deal with social data crawled from the web, there are some assumptions in SSL that the social data do not satisfy nicely, which often renders SSL paradigm ineffective. The main problem with the data collected from the Web is that although the data contain relevant information, it often also contains, if not more, irrelevant data. In the past, the SSL framework assumes the data are all relevant. Hence, we are now confronted with a new scenario in the SSL framework which not only include labeled and unlabeled data, but that these data can also be either relevant or irrelevant data. Our hypothesis is that by dealing with the irrelevant data properly, we will be able to raise the effectiveness of the SSL approach. Based on these considerations, we propose to extend the SSL framework as follows: (1) to provide an in-depth investigation on the state-of-the-art SSL techniques and social computing applications. In addition, we plan to provide a implement a unified platform to conduct further research, including SSL algorithm comparisons and data collection, data preprocessing on social computing applications, etc. (2) to formulate theoretical SSL models that can learn from both labeled and unlabeled with irrelevant data, (3) to evaluate the performance of the proposed models with theoretical analysis and simulations on synthetic and real-world data sets, and (4) to utilize the proposed novel SSL framework on at least one of the two web applications, e.g., personalized ranking and hierarchical web page classification, in order to validate the effectiveness of the proposed SSL approach, and (5) to produce academically significant research for further strengthening of the high-tech industries in Hong Kong and China. As the PI is an expert in machine learning and social computing, We believe the proposed SSL framework will offer novel ways to extend traditional machine learning paradigms to solve these new issues with not only theoretical results, but also very practical impact to daily life in searching, ranking, and classification of social information on the Web. 由於互聯網的出現，通過社交網絡進行數據挖掘的任務成為一個很熱的研究課題。這些任務包括如社區鑑別，社交網頁的分類等。這些任務從社交網絡收集的數據通常是大量的，未標記的，並且蘊含公開的和隱藏的社交信息。 半監督學習是機器學習的一種模式。它能夠有效的處理已標記的和未標記的數據。雖然半監督學習是一種處理從網頁抓取的社交性數據的好方法，但是社交性數據並不能很好滿足半監督學習的一些假設。這導致半監督學習在這些任務不怎麼有效。 從網站收集的數據主要問題是雖然數據包含相關信息，同时又包含许多不相關的數據。在過去的研究中，半监督的学习框架假设所有數據都是相關的。因此，我們考虑半监督学习框架下一种新的情況，就是数据不僅包括已標記和未標記的數據，而且這些數據可以是關的或不相關的。我們的假設是，通過适当地處理不相關數據，我們將能夠提高半监督学习的效果。 基于这些考虑，我们对半监督学习框架的拓展提出如下： （1）对目前最前沿的半监督学习技術和社會計算應用提供一個深入的調查研究。此外，我們計劃实现一個用于進一步研究的統一实验平台。该平台能够进行各种半监督学习算法的比較，數據採集，和對社會計算應用的數據預處理等。 （2）制定可以從包含不相關數據的已標記和未標記的數據學習出規律的半監督學習理論模型， （3）對提出的模型進行理論分析，並用模擬生成數據和真實世界的數據評估模型的表現， （4）對新提出的半監督學習框架進行現至少一個網頁應用，以驗證所提出的半監督學習是否有效。這些應用包括諸如，個性化網頁排名和分級網頁分類， （5）為進一步加強香港和中國的高新技術產業產生顯著的學術研究成果。 由於主持人是機器學習和社會計算領域的專家，我們相信，我們提出的半監督學習框架不僅能夠為傳統統的機器學習模式解決這些新問題提供新的理論成果，而且也能夠通過對網絡中社會信息的搜索，排名和分類實際影響人們的日常生活。

413210.value: At the completion of the project, all revised objectives have been achieved. 413210.label: Major findings and research outcome
413210.value: This project has generated two journal papers, 17 conference papers, and one patent. Moreover, the grant has helped to train four M.Phil. students and two Ph.D. students by providing them support in various research activities during their study. I will use J for journal entries and C for conference entries as references in the following discussion. I shall highlight some of the more significant output. Objective 1: To provide an in-depth study on Semi-supervised Learning (SSL) techniques. The two assumptions that we are particularly interested in are the clustering assumption and the manifold assumption. In J2 and C15, we have developed graphical lasso quadratic discriminant function in the SSL framework and applied it to character recognition. We also studied whether irrelevant data can help SSL and the results are positive in C1. Objective 2: To extend the theoretical understanding of the SSL framework. We extended the graph-based SSL for processing online social networks in C12. Moreover, we extended the SSL to recommender systems in C11, C13, and C10. Objective 3: To evaluate the performance of proposed SSL extensions. In J1, we used the SSL framework to find out about attack and protection algorithms for online social networks. Objective 4: To implement possibly the proposed SSL framework in applications. We used our research results in C2 for joint information extraction and community Q&A in C3, C4, C7. We also applied our research results in crowdsourcing systems in C5, C6. We have also obtained one US patent on using our research output for web query classification with colleagues from AT&T. Overall, the research project has produced many publications in top venues, e.g., CIKM, AAAI, ACM SIGIR, WSDM, NIPS, etc. It has further helped to train a number of post-graduate students. All in all, the PI is pleased with the outcome of the project.

413210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413210.value: Semi-supervised Learning (SSL) appears to be quite useful and practical in Big Data processing due to its flexible framework and approach. We would like to explore ways SSL can help to reduce process time and increase performance in a number of applications in different domains. We plan to carry on our theoretical developmental work as well as design novel applications based on our research project.

413210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413210.value: Semi-supervised Learning (SSL) is a machine learning framework to process a large dataset of unlabeled data when only a small amount of labelled data is available. In our research work, we studied about extending the current SSL approach by using kernel-based approach. We have done an in-depth study of the literature, formulated the kernel-based SSL approach, conducted a series of experiments to illustrate the effectiveness of our kernel-based extension, and also incorporated the novel kernel-based SSL into a recommendation system. The outcome is significant since it may have great implication to processing large dataset as in Big Data.

413310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413310.value: 癌症的特點是癌細胞不受控制地生長和增殖，影響病人健康。每年世界各地新發的病例約600萬宗。癌病不僅影響病人健康，而且影響其家人及社區。因此，尋找新的抗癌藥物，幫助病人及其家屬有迫切需要。 抗癌藥物殺死癌細胞的主要機制是透過誘導細胞進行凋亡程序。在這個細胞死亡過程中，細胞色素c從線粒體中被釋放到細胞質誘發細胞死亡。釋放細胞色素c是凋亡過程中一個早期發生的事件，並可以在凋亡細胞培養液中找到。因此，細胞色素c是一個有用的生物標記，作檢測抗癌藥物殺死癌細胞之用。傳統測量細胞色素c是透過凝膠電泳和免疫印記法分析。這個過程非常繁瑣和耗時，而且是一個定點的檢測方法。在這個項目中，我們提出發展一個以適體為基礎的表面等離子體共振生物感應器作快速細胞色素c的測定，從而加快開發抗癌藥物的過程。 適體是小的單鏈核苷酸。透過分子內的相互作用，折疊成獨特的立體結構，像個抗體，可與特定的標靶結合。在這個項目中，我們將篩選與細胞色素c結合的DNA適體，並進行測序，合成和定性。這細胞色素c適體將被固定在表面等離子體共振金表面上，作無標記細胞色素c的檢測。相對於傳統的分析方法，我們的生物感應器提供了一種快速，無標記，高靈敏度，高特異性，實時的監測方法。多年來，我們的團隊已建立一個更好的表面等離子體共振技術，作生物分子檢測之用，我們現在有一項已簽發和兩項待發的美國專利技術。 在這個項目中，我們將整合所有知識，如適體技術和我們的表面等離子體共振的專利技術，開發微型光電感應器，從傳統中藥尋找新的有效抗癌藥物。我們希望這新感應器，有助開發香港和中國的中醫藥業。

413310.label: Realisation of objectives
413310.value: The Objectives (1-3) have been achieved. In Objective 1 (To select a monoclonal DNA aptamer and obtain its sequence for binding cyto-c), we obtained 3 aptamer clones by SELEX (Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment) and the best clone (Clone-3) in terms of binding affinity was used for Objectives 2 and 3. To demonstrate the utility of Clone-3 for cyto-c binding, we developed an Aptamer-based Bio-barcode (ABC) Assay, using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and isothermal recombinase polymerase amplification, to amplify the barcode DNA (aptamer) for cyto-c detection. Results are promising and data in this part were published in Talenta (2013, 115:159-65). In Objective 2 (To develop a novel aptamer-based SPR biosensor for the detection of cyto-c based on our patented phase-sensitive SPR (pSPR)), hardware was built and experiments were performed with the common-path spectral interferometry phase SPR (pSPR) technique. The theory part and simulation for the pSPR were published in 2 papers (Ann. Phys. (Berlin) 524, 11:637–662; Opt Express. 2013, 21:20268-73). In Objective 3 (To demonstrate our approach is a viable technology for anti-cancer drug screening and discovery from TCM), candidates from TCM (polyphyllin D, berberine, curcumin, ferutinin, betulinic acid, atractyloside, carpacin, cordcepin and veratridine) were selected after literature survey and their potential anti-cancer effects were first confirmed by conventional biochemical assays. The anti-cancer effect of these agents was then evaluated by our aptasensor using pSPR with reference to doxorubicin, a conventional chemotherapeutic drug used in hospitals to treat cancers. Results indicate that our aptasensor provides a low detection limit (80 pM) and a fast detection process (within hour) for drug screening. Among the drug candidates tested, polyphyllin D is the only agent that can bypass the multi-drug resistance (MDR) in the liver cancer cells (e.g. kill more cancer cells with MDR). A manuscript entitled “An Aptasensor using DNA Aptamer and White Light Common-path SPR Spectral Interferometry to Detect Cytochrome-c for Anti-cancer Drug Screening“ was submitted to ‘Sensors & Actuators: B. Chemical’ for publication. Based on our results in the project, we believed that our aptasensor using pSPR can speed up the anti-cancer drug screening process. Also, with the development in the pSPR technique, part of the work was used for grant application. For this, our group has luckily to obtain one ITF, one CRF and one AoE funding (as Co-I).

Objective 2: Hardware was built and experiments were performed. The theory part and simulation for pSPR were published respectively in (2) and (3). (2) Huan Y, Ho HP, Kong SK, and Kabashin AV (2012) Phase-sensitive surface plasmon resonance biosensors: methodology, instrumentation and applications Ann. Phys. (Berlin) 524, 11, 637–662. Objective 3: A number of candidates from TCM were selected after literature survey. Their potential anti-cancer effects were confirmed by conventional biochemical assays. As mentioned in Objective 1 and 2, the effects of these TCM candidates were evaluated using the aptamer Clone-3. Results are promising and agreed with those from conventional biochemical assays. The TCM candidates in our work included polyphyllin D, berberine, curcumin, ferutinin, betulinic acid, atractyloside, carpacin, cordcepin and veratridine. For a fair comparison, conventional chemotherapeutic drug doxorubicin used in hospitals was employed as a positive control for reference. Results from our studies indicate that polyphyllin D, among the drug candidates tested so far, is the only agent that can bypass the multi-drug resistance (MDR) in the liver cancer cells (e.g. kill more cancer cells with MDR). A manuscript entitled “An Aptasensor using DNA Aptamer and White Light Common-path SPR Spectral Interferometry to Detect Cytochrome-c for Anti-cancer Drug Screening“ had been submitted and positive feedback was obtained from reviewers and editors. 413310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413310.value: Many cancer cells exhibit multi-drug resistance (MDR). To identify effective anti-cancer agents is therefore an urgent need. During cancer killing, cytochrome c (cyto-c) is released from the mitochondria to the cytoplasm. This is a point-of-no-return event in the cell death process. Because of this, cyto-c is a useful marker for anti-cancer drug screening. In this project, we used aptamer to detect the cyto-c release. Aptamers are small single-chain DNAs that fold into unique 3D conformation for target binding. In our project, 3 anti-cyto-c aptamers were selected, sequenced, synthesized and characterized. One good aptamer was then used to detect cyto-c using the common-path spectral interferometry phase SRP technique. After modeling and simulation, we determined the detection limit and fine-tune its utility. For real application, we employed this biosensor to screen anti-cancer agents from the traditional Chinese medicine after literature search. Among the tested candidates (polyphyllin D, berberine, curcumin, ferutinin, betulinic acid, atractyloside, carpacin, cordcepin and veratridine), only polyphyllin D was found to bypass MDR and killed more liver cancer cells with MDR. We believed that this new biosensor and the pSPR technique can facilitate the anti-cancer drug discovery process.
