413510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413510.value: Mining useful and precise information from text documents involves handling high-dimensional and complex text data. It is important for a wide variety of applications such as supporting relational search which aims at retrieving entities that have a given relation with another entity. For example, it can support the query "List the heads of nations in Asia" which requires the extraction of person named entities involving the relation "head" with a country entity. Traditional information retrieval techniques and search engines cannot handle this kind of query with satisfactory precision. Sequence classification models, such as conditional random fields, have been employed to solve a variety of shallow text mining tasks including entity extraction achieving the state-of-the-art performance. However, one disadvantage of sequence classification models is the incapability of handling non-local or global entity-level interactions commonly found in practical text mining problems. Another drawback is the limited expressiveness of attribute-value representation of features. Logic is a powerful paradigm that can overcome the modeling of non-local or global interactions, and knowledge representation problems mentioned above found in sequence classification models. It can capture complex entity-level domain knowledge commonly found in human experts or in practical situations. It provides much more expressive power than attribute-value representation of features. Recently, some approaches, such as Markov Logic Network, have been proposed based on combining logics and statistical learning. They have been applied to tackle text mining problems coping with the uncertainty and fuzziness found in the text data while maintaining the expressiveness power of logics. However, these methods require that those necessary entities are already known or extracted. Hence, they rely on the assumption that the necessary shallow text mining task, such as entity extraction, has been done manually or solved without errors and such assumption is invalid in practice. We aim at developing a new text mining framework that can incorporate non-local interactions and logical inference into sequence classification models. Our framework is able to tackle practical problems which demand solving simultaneously entity-level relation interactions task and related necessary shallow text mining tasks. It can also handle uncertainty in a principled manner. We plan to evaluate our framework using benchmark corpora solving text mining problems such as gene extraction and interaction discovery from biomedical texts. We also intend to develop an application on relational search from online news stories supporting complicated queries for which traditional information retrieval techniques and search engines cannot handle with satisfactory precision. 從文本文檔中挖掘有用而精確的資訊涉及到高維度的複雜文本資料操作。這在諸如關聯搜索支援（目標是檢索與既定實體相關聯的其他實體）等一系列應用中甚為重要。譬如，它可以支援形如“列出亞洲國家的元首”的查詢，這需要提取與國家實體擁有“元首”這一關聯的人名實體。傳統的資訊檢索技術和搜索引擎並不能令人滿意的精確處理這一類型的查詢。 序列分類模型，如條件隨機場，已經被應用於解決各種淺層的文字勘探任務，其中包括實現了現有最佳表現的實體提取。但是，序列分類模型的缺點之一在於不能處理實體層面的廣域或全局互動，而這點在實際文字勘探問題中相當普遍。另一不足是特徵表述時對屬性值表述的局限性。邏輯作為一項有力例證，能夠解決廣域或全局互動的建模以及序列分類模型中提到的知識表述問題。它能捕捉專家或實際應用中常見的複雜實體層的領域知識，提供了比屬性值特徵表述更強的表述能力。近來提出的一些方法，如馬爾科夫邏輯網路，正是基於邏輯與統計學習的混合。它們已經被應用於解決文字勘探問題，如為維持邏輯的表述力而常出現於文本資料中的不確定性與模糊性。但是，這些方法需要事先知道或已經提取必要實體。因此，它們是基於如下假設，即淺層文字勘探任務（如實體獲取）已經人工完成或是無誤解決，但這個假設在實際中顯然不能成立。 我們致力於構造一個新的文字勘探框架，這個框架能夠將廣域互動和邏輯推理融入序列分類模型。我們的框架能夠解決實際問題中需要同步解決實體層關聯互動任務和相關的必要淺層文字勘探任務的情況。同時，它能規範化處理不確定性。我們計畫利用評比樣本來評估此框架處理文字勘探問題的結果，例如，從生物醫學文本中提取基因和發現互動。我們亦打算構建一個基於線上新聞的關聯搜索應用，以支援傳統資訊檢索技術和搜索引擎不能精確解決的複雜查詢。

413510.label: Realisation of objectives
413510.value: To realize the first objective of this project, we have developed a new text mining framework that can conduct information extraction via incorporating non-local interactions and logical inference into sequence classification models. A lot of text documents can be regarded as semi-structured or unstructured text data involving greatly complex and high-dimensional data. These difficulties impose challenges for conducting precise information analysis and extraction. Our proposed framework is designed based on a combination of sequence classification modeling, latent topic detection, and first-order logic. To cope with non-local interactions found in complicated semi-structured text data records found in Web page content, we consider a more global view in tackling the problem using a Document Object Model (DOM) structure knowledge driven detection. This model can conduct global analysis on the Web content structure via logic-based background knowledge as well as statistical knowledge. Non-local interactions between data records and record regions can be effectively captured by logic-based paradigm of encoding the semantics of the labels as well as certain structural constraints among the labels. Latent or hidden topics are useful for capturing semantic content of text documents. We also consider to uncover or detect latent topics found in text documents and user queries. We have also investigated the capability of our framework for entity expansion and entity attribute extraction from Web documents. Non-local interactions exist among the candidate text fragments related to various entity attributes in the domain of the target entity. Our developed framework can handle such kind of non-local interactions effectively. Precisely, this framework is able to conduct discovery and extraction of entities and attribute content from desirable semi-structured data record sets which are automatically detected from the Web page content. A semi-supervised sequence classification model coupled with Conditional Random Fields (CRF) is designed. To realize the second objective, we have developed several methods for tackling the approximate inference and training problem. One method is to employ an inference technique derived from a technique known as generalized expectation. We exploit the inherent structure of complex data records facilitating collective learning and detection. External clues from large-scale linked data sources such as DBpedia are incorporated via a collective detection algorithm based on Markov Logic Networks (MLN). This model is able to consider logical consistency among potential entities as well as header texts in a field column. It also enables uncertain inference on a set of first-order formulae in a principled manner. Another model related to approximate inference algorithm is to develop a Bayesian nonparametric model based on a metaphor called Chinese Restaurant Franchise with Buddy Customers, which can maintain the word order and infer the number of latent topics based on the data characteristic. Such model can discover n-gram words in topics. A refinement on Gibbs sampling has been investigated for posterior inference. To realize the third objective, we have evaluated our framework using corpora involving semantic relation classification learning such as DBpedia, Wikipedia, INEX-XER, SemSearch, INEX-LD, Delicious bookmark data collection, AOL query log, and other corpora. One strategy for improving search quality and user satisfaction is to assist them to issue more effective queries. Query reformulation aims at generating new queries from the current query issued by users. Most of the existing methods heavily rely on context relation of terms in the history queries and cannot maintain the semantic consistency of queries. We tackle this problem using our new model on sequence classification via a graphical model for scoring queries. Our query reformulation method exploits a latent topic space, which is automatically derived from a query log, for detecting semantic dependency. We also consider terms in a query and dependency among topics. We have also investigated an extension of our method which considers users’ history search interests when we conduct query reformulation for different users. This enables our graphical model to conduct better and more flexible candidate query scoring so that the overall performance of the proposed query reformulation can be improved. We have also tackled a related problem on Web page segmentation that can be applied to improve the Web search. The content of a Web page can be treated as a semi-structured text document where free text content is mixed with semi-structured HTML tags. The aim of page segmentation is to analyze the semi-structured texts and segment the content into coherent regions. Our method formulates the segmentation task as a structured labeling problem. The first phase is to conduct a transformation of the text content to a Web page segmentation graph (WPS-graph). This graph can model the candidate segmentation boundaries and the dependency among the segmentation boundaries. To realize the fourth objective, we have developed an application on relational search supporting complicated queries. We propose an entity retrieval framework which aims at searching specific entities to directly answer a user query. Many existing entity search models follow the document retrieval assumption: when issuing queries, users choose the words that may appear in the “entity pseudo-document”. Based on the assumption, these models construct internal query representation by combining various entity descriptions and use these representations for entity search. We propose that an entity query is generated via a two-step process: users first select facts that can distinguish target entities from the others; and then choose words that describe the selected facts. Based on the proposed query generation paradigm, we develop an entity retrieval application. We also develop an application for document retrieval ranking via learning latent topics. While most methods for learning-to-rank documents only consider relevance scores as features, better results can often be obtained by taking into account the latent topic structure of the document collection. Our proposed learning-to-rank framework integrates the supervised learning of a maximum margin classifier with the discovery of a suitable probabilistic topic model. The labelled data that is available can be exploited to identify the most appropriate topics. A unified constrained optimization technique is also developed for dynamically computing the latent topic similarity score between the query and the document.

413510.label: Major findings and research outcome
413510.value: We have also obtained some significant findings from the above research works. Some findings have been published in top tier journals and international conferences. Our text mining models capturing non-local interactions and dealing with complicated semi-structured text data records found in Web page content are more effective than existing works. New inference algorithms and training techniques have been developed. Extensive experiments using various data sets and corpora have been conducted to evaluate our models. Our research findings have been published in ACM Transactions on the Web, Information Retrieval Journal, ACM Conference on Special Interest Group on Information Retrieval (SIGIR), ACM Conference of Web Search and Data Mining (WSDM), ACM Conference of Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM), European Conference on Information Retrieval (ECIR), and other conferences. Our semantic classification learning application considers query reformulation. Our model is shown to be useful via the modeling of latent topic dependency and term context. The research finding has been published in ACM Transactions on Information Systems (TOIS). Our applications in entity expansion, search, and retrieval application have generated encouraging results on handling entities in text documents and queries. More effective retrieval performance has been obtained. Our works have been published in Knowledge-Based Systems journal, ACM Conference of Web Search and Data Mining (WSDM), ACM Conference of Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM), and the Annual Meeting of Association of Computational Linguistics (ACL) which is a flagship conference in natural language processing area.

413510.value: We intend to continue to investigate new text mining models that can capture more semantic and context in term representation. Some models being investigated are word embedding paradigms and neural network models which have been successfully adopted in some natural language processing tasks such as machine translation. In-depth investigation and analysis will be conducted to gain some insights on how they are useful in these tasks.

413510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413510.value: Digesting and extracting useful and precise information from text documents and data involves handling complex and high-dimensional representation. Such mining goals are useful for different applications such as supporting more advanced search and digesting text content. Traditional methods employ sequence classification models, such as conditional random fields, to tackle the mining tasks. However, there are some limitations for these traditional sequence classification models. One major limitation is the incapability of handling non-local interactions. Another limitation is the restriction on traditional attribute-value representation of data. This project investigates and develops new text mining models that can incorporate non-local interactions and logical inference into sequence classification models. Our new models have also been integrated into various text mining applications including entity search, document retrieval ranking, and discovering hidden topics not previously known.

413610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413610.value: A low-latency, accurate RFID counting scheme can be used as a fundamental building block to support more elaborated RFID query operations. Such RFID counting algorithms have been proposed recently. One distinct feature of these schemes is that they do not require explicit identification of individual tags and therefore can preserve the privacy of the RFID users. However, these schemes all assume perfect communications between the reader and the tags which is unachievable in practice. In fact, recent empirical measurement studies have found that the communication between an RFID reader and a set of seemingly ``in-range'' tags are still unreliable and non-deterministic due to the highly varying radio channel conditions. Worse still, given the stringent cost constraint, it is unlikely that typical channel estimation and/or error-recovery procedures can be applied for individual tags. The objective of this project is to design and implement a set of channel-oblivious RFID counting algorithms and the corresponding reader-tag protocols for RFID tag-set cardinality estimation over unreliable, lossy wireless channels. In particular, the proposed scheme can provide accurate estimates while assuming no prior knowledge of channel parameters. It is scalable over a wide range of tag-set size spanning several orders of magnitude, using a small, fixed protocol frame-size, which is critical for low-cost RFID tags with typically sub-par synchronization or timing control. It also self-tunes its algorithm parameters according to the tag-set size and channel characteristics which are both unknown a priori. The proposed scheme can be used to track the membership changes of multiple tag-sets and their stored data across different spatially and temporally-diverse domains. This set of features makes the proposed scheme applicable in a wide variety of situations where the reader is unaware of channel conditions. Besides tag counting, the proposed scheme can be readily extended to support the estimation of SUM, MAX, MIN of data-values stored amongst fields of RFID tags in a privacy-preserving manner. Our channel-oblivious techniques can also be applied to other query tasks such as category identification of RFIDs present in a tag-set. The proposed system requires only simple modifications to standard RFID tags/readers and can be implemented using current technologies with minimal increase in tag/reader cost. We will demonstrate the efficacy of our scheme by implementing it on an existing home-grown active RFID system. This prototyping effort will enable us to better understand and thus address additional challenges in deploying the proposed scheme in practice. 通道不經意的無線標籤(RFID)算法以供大規模應用 準確快捷的無線標籤計數方法可以支持更多其他複雜的查詢操作。 這種無線標籤算法已在最近提出。這些計劃的一個特點是，它不 需要明確的識別個人標籤，因此可以保護無線標籤用戶的私隱。 然而，這些方案都假定無法實現的，完美的通信。但是，實驗發現 無線標籤閱讀器和一組看似“在範圍內”的標籤的溝通仍然是不可靠的。 這是由於無線電頻道的不確定性變化。儘管如此，由於嚴格的成本約束， 典型的信道估計程序是不適用於無線標籤。 這項目的目標是設計一套通道不經意的無線標籤算法和相應讀取器的通訊協議。 就算沒有無線電頻道的參數，這方案仍能夠準確估計無線標籤的數目。 這方案有很高的可擴性，也可降低無線標籤的成本。建議的方案可以用來在 不同的空間和時間上追踪無線標籤。這技術也可以應用於其他查詢任務，如 分類鑑定無線標籤。只需要簡單修改目前標準的無線標籤和閱讀器， 擬議的系統就可以實現使用。

413610.label: Realisation of objectives
413610.value: In this project, we have designed a series of fast probabilistic RFID counting algorithms which can provide accurate estimates of the tag-set cardinality under unreliable, non-fully-characterized radio channels. To understand the behavior of the proposed schemes, we have evaluated their performance via mathematical analysis and model-based simulations established via empirical channel measurements/ statistics. For analytical tractability reasons, we started by assuming an implicitly characterized memoryless channel with identical, independently distributed (i.i.d.) packet losses. We then relaxed the requirement of the 2-moment implicit characterization of the wireless channel and proposed PELOC, a fast estimation scheme which provided a lower-bound on the number of tags in the tag-set without any knowledge of the channel. We demonstrated via simulations that the lower-bound estimate produced by PELOC was remarkably tight under a wide-range of fading conditions and channel parameters of practical relevance. Besides PELOC, we also designed the Union-bound estimator. We showed that the Union-bound estimator performed even better than PELOC except when the tag-set size was very large (> 1000) and the successful responding probabilities of the tags were of impractically small values, (e.g. all < 0.1). We identified that the weakness of the Union-based estimator was due to its lack of projection power: in order for any tag to be counted, it had to show up at least once during the repeated probings of the RFID reader. We then overcame such limitation by a novel application of the capture-recapture-based sampling techniques in the field of biostatistics. In particular, we showed via analysis and simulations that, under a wide range of practical channel conditions, our capture-recapture based estimators is more accurate than the Union-based approach while requiring the same probing latency. The remaining part of our study moved beyond the initial, simplistic i.i.d. lossy channel model. Firstly, we established a detail channel model which captured not only the time-correlated fading but also the backscattering effects commonly found in passive RFID systems in practice. We then re-evaluated the performance and accuracy of all of our previously proposed RFID counting algorithms under this more realistic channel model. Our studies indicated that, depending on the specific estimator and actual channel parameters, the temporal correlation of the wireless channel could cause either over-estimation or under-estimation of the tag-set size. To tackle the inaccuracies caused by time-correlated channel effects, we modified and extended our RFID counting algorithms by adopting seed-interlaced probing, together with adaptive convergence test/ termination rules for the algorithms.

413610.label: Major findings and research outcome
413610.value: Major research outcome of this project include: 1. Our IEEE WiOpt paper (Item#1 of Part C.9) covered the design and performance analysis of a series of RFID counting algorithms which required minimal or no channel characterization. An analytically tractable but simplistic memoryless i.i.d. lossy channel model was adopted. The performance of the various proposed schemes were evaluated via mathematical analysis and simulations using models derived from empirical measurements/ statistics. This work was one of the 3 Best Student Paper finalists in the conference. 2. In our IEEE CCNC paper (Item#2 of Part C.9), we constructed a more realistic time-correlated fading channel model to capture the practical characteristics of the back-scattering operation between the RFID reader and the tags. Based on this new model, we determined the impact of backscattering mechanism and time-correlated fading on the accuracy of all of the proposed Channel-Oblivious RFID counting algorithms. We found that all of these algorithms would suffer from additional estimation errors compared to the case of memoryless channel with i.i.d. packet losses and the lack of consideration of backscattering effects. The extent of performance degradation depended on the time-scale of correlation found in the channel fading. Through careful examination and analysis of the design of each of the above algorithms, we identified the source of the problem. Based on these findings, we modified and extended our previously proposed RFID counting algorithms to reduce the estimation errors caused by more realistic correlated packet losses. We also demonstrated the applicability of those modifications via extensive simulations. To be more specific, for the two-moment implicit approach, we showed that the backscattering and time-correlated fading effects could be accounted for as long as the actual first two moments of the successful responding probabilities of the tags were empirically measured. For the Union-based, capture-recapture as well as the PELOC approaches, substantial under-estimation of the tag-count could be resulted in when the channel coherence time was larger than the frame duration. However, by adopting seed-interlaced probing and adaptive convergence test/ stopping rules, it was possible to control/ avoid the inaccuracy problems caused by time-correlated channel losses. 3. In our journal paper currently under submission (Item#1 of Part C.8), we presented the aforementioned findings in a coherent, comprehensive manner, with detail mathematical proofs, to illustrate and quantify the relative strengths and weaknesses of each of the proposed algorithms under different application scenarios.

413610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413610.value: The channel oblivious algorithms we proposed and studied in this project can potentially be adapted for other applications beyond RFID counting under lossy wireless channel. One application is to leverage our methodologies to estimate the number of hard-to-detect network attacks/intrusions. In the context of this new application, the "lossy behavior of the unknown wireless channel" becomes the unknown probability that an intrusion packet can sneak through the network intrusion detector. The lower-bound nature of the estimate produced by some of our schemes, e.g. PELOC, can be particularly useful in quantifying the residual risks and alert the network administrators about newly emerged threats. During the last phase of our project, we also explored the application of other statistical theories, e.g. the Extreme Value Theory, for the design of alternative RFID counting algorithms. However, we found that those theories required the setting of certain critical hyper-parameter(s) of the algorithm in some heuristic manner. Furthermore, the accuracy of the resultant estimator is very sensitive to such hyper-parameter settings. Going forward, it may be worthwhile to seek collaboration with specialist(s) in those statistical theories to develop more systematic ways to determine the hyper-parameters of the corresponding estimators, making them robust enough for different practical applications.

413610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413610.value: Scalable, low-latency and accurate RFID counting algorithms have recently been proposed as a fundamental building block to support more complex query operations in large-scale RFID systems. One distinct feature of these algorithms is that they do not require explicit identification of individual tags and therefore can reduce latency while preserving user privacy. However, these algorithms all assume reliable communications between the reader and the tags - a requirement which is practically unachievable given the current technology and the low-cost nature of RFID tags. In this project, we discuss the design and performance analysis of a series of channel-oblivious RFID counting algorithms which can estimate the size of a tag-set of interest over unreliable wireless channels. The proposed schemes can provide accurate cardinality estimates with minimal or no prior knowledge of the channel parameters. We first propose a series of algorithms and analyze their performance under a simplified memoryless lossy channel model. We then extend them to handle the impact due to backscattering effects and correlated losses found in practical RFID systems. Our proposed algorithms only require simple modifications to standard RFID tags/ readers and can be implemented using current technologies with minimal increase in tag/ reader cost.

413710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413710.value: 約束滿足問題（CSP）在各行各業的工業應用和計算機科學中皆有出現，如調度、 裝箱、運輸路徑編定、類型檢查、圖表佈局等。在傳統的約束滿足中，約束都是嚴 格的：它們必須得到滿足。但面對過度約束或優化問題的情況時，便需要放寬或軟 化一些約束。加權約束滿足便是在這背景下產生的新興架構，為軟約束問題推展新 的求解技術。加權約束滿足問題（WCSP）的求解建基於分支限界搜索再配合高效的 約束傳播算法以減少搜索空間，但這些解算法到目前為止一般只照顧一元至三元的 約束。在實際應用中，許多複雜的條件性質上都是非二元的，因此缺乏較高元數的 約束大大限制了WCSP解算法的適用性。基於WCSP的組合性質，為解算法引入任意非 二元約束是困難的。在這項目中，我們建議探討有效的算法以處理加權約束滿足中 的非二元「軟全域約束」。軟全域約束有其特定的語義，其中它們（一）在許多問 題領域中是常見的子結構，和（二）可以有高效的約束傳播算法。我們的方法必須 足以使我們可以構建一個約束庫，包含一些常見、有用和能於實際問題應用的軟全 域約束。擬議的研究在加權約束滿足領域中開闢了一個新的研究方向，並對於理論 和算法設計帶來正面影響及實際應用意義。我們期望能對軟全域約束及其特性作深 入的了解，設計及開發高效的軟全域約束傳播算法，並應用到實際生活中的問題。

413710.label: Realisation of objectives
413710.value: In terms of Objective 1, we have generalized the notion of flow-based projection-safety to tractable projection-safety, and given necessary conditions both in terms of flow graph and recurrence equation representations on when a soft global constraint (or global cost function) is tractable projection-safe. We also develop algorithms based on min-cost flow and dynamic programming to compute the minimum cost of tractable projection-safe functions, which is essentially for polytime consistency enforcement. We also differentiate projections/extensions to/from cost functions of arities 0, 1, and k (where k > 1), and give theoretical characterization on tractable 0-, 1-, and k-projection-safeties respectively. In terms of Objective 2, we proved how a number of global cost functions are flow-based projection-safe (thus also tractable projection-safe), and implemented the consistency algorithms for these cost functions. We propose polynomially decomposable global cost functions and show that they are also tractable projection-safe, thereby increasing our reportire of global cost functions. Some cost functions are inherently NP-hard or we do not have polytime algorithms to compute their minimum cost yet. We propose Polytime (Integral) Linear Projection-Safe global cost functions, and give approximate consistency algorithms. An advantage of these cost functions is that their conjunctions are also polytime (integral) Linear Projection-Safe, thus resulting in stronger consistency. In terms of Objective 3, we demonstrate that EDAC* cannot be generalized for global cost functions directly. Instead, we propose Weak EDGAC* and give polytime algorithms for tractable projection-safe cost functions. In addition to the above 3 objectives, we also investigated bringing global cost functions to new variants of WCSPs. In particular, we demonstrate how the same consistency algorithms can be transferred to Minimax Weighted Constraint Satisfaction Problems, which have applications in optimization games, and also Distributed Constraint Optimization Problems, which are situation in naturally geographically distributed systems. We have also applied the theories and algorithms developed to a real-life judge assignment problem, which is a goal listed in the *original* Objective 5.

413710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413710.value: Tractable Projection-Safety is the pillar notion developed in this project. It characterizes theoretically when a global cost function is amenable to tractable implementation. More research is needed to understand and perhaps even generalize this notion to further our reportire of efficiently implementable global cost functions. As such, we have submitted a new proposal for GRF funding in the 15/16 exercise with the following title, aim and scope. Tractable Projection-Safety for Cost Functions Network Revisited: Theory Algorithms and Applications We would like to further our theoretical understanding of Tractable Projection-Safety and investigate possible generalization. Topics of investigation include theoretical underpinnings, new data structures and algorithms, approximation and applications. Such advances will increase our repertoire of efficient data structures and algorithms, and thus additional variety of useful global cost functions, thereby enriching the vocabulary of human modelers in tackling hard combinatorial optimization problems. The impact lies not only in theory and algorithm design, but also has practical implications. We expect to contribute to the deep understanding and characterization of when a global cost function is amenable to efficient consistency algorithms, design and implementation of new efficient algorithms, and applications to real-life problems.

413710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413710.value: Weighted Constraint Satisfaction is important for solving hard combinatorial optimization problems which are ubiquitous in the industry. While the common solving technique is based on branch-and-bound search, various consistency algorithms are incorporated to improve search efficiency. The project makes an important breakthrough by making it possible to enforce generalized consistencies on different classes of tractable projection-safe global cost functions. The contributions give human modeler a library of versatile cost functions for modeling complex real-life applications. The impact lies not only in theory and algorithm design, but also practical implications. We expect to contribute to the deep understanding and characterization of when a global cost function (or soft global constraint) is amenable to efficient consistency algorithms, design and implementation of new efficient algorithms, and applications to real-life problems.

413910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413910.value: Although WiFi networking has become popular among many corporations and home networks, users still occasionally suffer from the poor performance of wireless data transmissions due to the inherently unstable wireless link conditions. One problem that currently deployed WiFi networks suffer is known as the rate anomaly problem, in which stations (e.g., laptops, PDAs) transmitting at lower data rates dramatically reduce the throughput of stations transmitting at higher data rates. In this research, our major goal is to design and implement a practical, deployable opportunistic relay mechanism that "opportunistically" activates higher-rate stations into repeaters and have them relay data for lower-rate stations, with an objective of improving the throughput of all participating stations, including the higher-rate and lower-rate stations. By opportunistic, we mean that our mechanism is activated only when all participating stations receive performance improvements. We use this mechanism to address not only the rate anomaly problem, but also a general class of data forwarding problems due to the unstable wireless link conditions. Designing a practical, deployable opportunistic relay mechanism is always a challenging issue. Currently deployed WiFi networks mainly operates in the IEEE 802.11 infrastructure mode for managing stations and forwarding data. It would be a daunting task to replace existing protocols and hardware with a new wireless infrastructure in order to include the mechanism. Instead, our focus is to design an opportunistic relay mechanism that is compatible with existing protocols and hardware. The major contribution of this research is to provide practical, deployable solutions that can immediately improve the performance and robustness of today's WiFi networks, such as the city-wide WiFi networks deployed by the Hong Kong Government. In particular, our research spans both applied and theoretical sides. On the applied side, we aim to design and implement an opportunistic relay mechanism that works seamlessly on today's WiFi networks and remains robust under various wireless environments. On the theoretical side, we aim to derive various mathematical frameworks that can quantify the performance of our relay mechanism for different traffic patterns and the incentives for stations to activate the relay mechanism. 雖然無線WiFi網絡已經為許多公司和家庭使用，但是用戶偶爾仍然會遇到無線數據傳輸性能表現不理想的問題。其中一個問題為「傳輸率異常」的問題，即低速站點大大拖慢高速站點的數據傳送流量。 在本研究中，我們的主要目標是設計和實施一個實用的「臨機中轉機制」，按需要啓動高速率的站點為中繼站，使它們為低速率站點傳遞數據，以逹致所有參與站點的數據傳送流量有所提高。所為「臨機」，是指我們的機制是只在當所有參與站點的接收性能得到改善的情況下才會被啓動。我們利用這個機制，不僅旨於解決傳輸率異常的問題，亦旨於解決一般由於無線鏈路中不穩定狀況下所衍生的有關同類數據傳送問題。 設計一個實用的臨機中轉機制是一個具有挑戰性的課題。目前使用中的WiFi網絡主要在802.11基礎架構模式上管理站點和傳送數據。如果要取代現有的協議和硬件，並搭建一個新的無線設施來實現我們的機制，這將是一個艱鉅的任務。因此，我們的研究重點將會是設計一個兼容現有的協議和硬件的臨機中轉機制。 本研究的主要貢獻在於提供實際的解決方案，以即時改善現今無線WiFi網絡（例如由香港政府搭建的全市WiFi網絡）的性能和穩定性。我們的研究將涉及應用和理論兩個方面。在應用方面，我們的目標是設計和實施一個可以適用於現今WiFi網絡上的臨機中轉機制，並在不同無線環境下仍有穩定表現；在理論方面，我們的目標是設計不同的數學模式以量化我們機制在不同流量模式上所帶來的性能表現，並計算出有關啓動機制的所需條件。

413910.label: Realisation of objectives
413910.value: As per Objectives 1 and 6, we present a general mathematical framework via stochastic difference equations to model the interaction of incentive mechanisms and various underlying protocols, including shortest-path routing, ETX routing, and back-pressure routing. To analyze unstable wireless link conditions, we model the loss probabilities based on the lognormal shadowing model. We consider how link loss probabilities influence incentive-based routing. As per Objectives 2 and 3, we present a credit evolution model to quantify the expected credit variation of each node. We also propose the use of differentiated pricing that can be used for probing measurements and handshake message exchanges, and show how it can achieve credit equality among nodes, resulting in a more robust network under different traffic loading.. As per Objective 4, we design a new anonymous network-coding-based scheme called ANOC that achieves secure routing between wireless nodes. We show that traditional anonymous routing makes network coding fail, so we design ANOC to make anonymous routing compatible with network coding. The idea is based on session key sharing among neighbors and auxiliary decrypting, so that the neighbors opportunistically decrypt the encrypted packets and mix the transmitted packets via networking. We also conduct security analysis on ANOC to validate its security strength. As per Objective 5, we also prototype ANOC via nsclick (a combination of ns2 and Click Modular Router) and evaluate its performance in different topologies. The use of Nsclick makes ANOC readily deployable in real systems with only minimal interface changes.

413910.label: Major findings and research outcome
413910.value: We mainly explore two topics in the cooperative relay mechanisms in wireless networks: (i) the mathematical frameworks for interaction between the incentive mechanism and the underlying relay protocols in wireless networks and (ii) the security protection for network-coding-based packet relay in wireless networks. In the first work, we observe that in open wireless networks, not all wireless nodes are cooperative in relaying packets for other nodes. Previous work has proposed different incentive mechanisms to provide incentives for nodes to cooperate and relay packets. However, understanding the interaction between an interactive mechanism and the underlying relay routing protocol is non-trivial. In this work, we seek to develop a general mathematical framework to capture such an interaction. Our current results propose a new mathematical framework, based on stochastic differential equations, to understand the relaying incentives of nodes in shortest-path routing, ETX routing, and back-pressure algorithms. We further present a differentiated pricing scheme that can work with link-level scheduling, so as to achieve credit equality and hence the routing robustness in wireless network. Our proposed mathematical methodology opens doors to investigate the sustainability of wireless networks that employ different incentive mechanisms and/or routing protocols. Our preliminary work was first published in the conference IEEE SECON 2011, and the extended work was then published in the journal Computer Networks in 2013. In the second work, we note that in open wireless networks, some wireless nodes may be malicious. These malicious nodes may want to steal the information from any packets that they help relaying. Our goal is to develop an anonymous relay protocol for network-coding-based wireless networks. Our observation is that wireless networks may leverage network coding to achieve higher throughput performance, but its design cannot be easily extended to support anonymity since the cooperative network coding operations are in conflict with the cooperative encryption/decryption mechanism required by anonymity relaying. Our work was published in the journal IEEE JSAC in 2012.

413910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413910.value: We propose mathematical models and algorithms to achieve robust routing in wireless networks. Our results are mainly driven from a theoretical perspective. Future work will be to design new relay systems that can work in real-life networks, and conduct extensive experiments to verify our theoretical findings. Our current results focus on IEEE 802.11-based networks. Given the advent of 3G/4G wireless data networks, it is important to study the robust communication mechanisms in such networks.

413910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413910.value: We mainly explore two topics in the cooperative relay mechanisms in wireless networks: (i) the mathematical frameworks for interaction between the incentive mechanism and the underlying relay protocols in wireless networks and (ii) the security protection for network-coding-based packet relay in wireless networks. First, we propose a new mathematical framework, based on stochastic differential equations, to understand the relaying incentives of nodes in shortest-path routing, ETX routing, and back-pressure algorithms. Second, we propose ANOC, a novel anonymous communication protocol that achieves secure wireless routing, while operating seamlessly on network-coding-based wireless networks. Our findings are published in one prestigious conference in wireless communication, and two prestigious journals in computer networking.

414010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414010.value: Larynx is the most important organ for human speech production. It houses the vocal folds, which vibrate periodically to generate pitched voice. For patients with late-stage larynx cancer, the removal of the entire larynx is the most common surgical treatment, which results in the loss of the ability to speak. Statistical data show that there are over 600,000 laryngectomees in the world. About half of the laryngectomees use an electrolarynx (EL) device as their primary method of speaking. EL is a hand-held device. When speaking, the user presses the device against the neck, and a buzzing signal created by the vibrating membrane on the EL is transmitted to the oral cavity to generate speech sounds. Despite its ease of use, EL speech is known to have several major deficits, including poor intelligibility, robot-like sound quality and lack of pitch variation to represent different tones and intonation. The inability to vary pitch is particularly detrimental to EL speakers of tone languages like Chinese, in which pitch contrast is sometimes the only cue to distinguish words. The broad objective of this project is to develop new EL technology that enables laryngectomized people to communicate with natural speech. More specifically, it addresses the problems of the lack of pitch variation and robot-like sound quality of the existing electrolarynx (EL) devices. We will try to search for tone-related cues from surface electromyography (sEMG) signals and use these cues to generate natural pitch contours for EL excitation. We will also try to identify the characteristics of EL excitation waveform that are most critical to the sound quality and accordingly design the optimal excitation signal. The performance of the new EL system will be evaluated by subjective listening tests. This is a collaborative project between signal processing researchers at CUHK and speech scientists at HKU. We expect that the developed system of EMG-controlled EL will be beneficial to Chinese-speaking larygectomees. Our research will also lead to improved understanding about the human speech production mechanism and related bio-signal activities. 喉頭是人體發聲系統的主要部分之一，其中的聲帶部分週期性振動產生不同音高的聲音。對晚期喉癌病人而言，喉頭的完全切除是最常見的治療手段。手術後病人將喪失說話的能力。目前全世界超過六十萬無喉者，其中有一半左右依賴電動喉頭作為基本的言語溝通方式。電動喉頭，又稱電子咪，是一種小型的手攜式系統。使用者需要將電動喉頭放在頸側或下巴適當位置並向皮膚輕壓，電動喉頭上的振動器產生聲音配合口型和舌部動作產生語音信號。電動喉頭方便攜帶，也簡單易用，但是聲音的質量和清晰度都比較差，只能產生固定音高的聲音，導致說話人無法表達不同的音調和語調的變化。這對說中文的無喉者來說尤其困擾，因為有很多詞語需要依靠音調才能分辨。本項目的整體目標為開發新的電動喉頭發聲技術，讓無喉者能用最自然的語音進行溝通。項目的具體目標為應用信號處理技術解決音高控制和聲音質量兩方面的問題。我們將嘗試在表面肌電信號中尋找與聲調或音高相關的特徵，並利用它們對電動喉頭的振動頻率進行控制。我們也將研究電動喉頭的聲源波形特點，找出對聲音質量最關鍵的部分加以改善，設計出最優的聲源信號。我們會進行主觀聆聽實驗，評估新開發的電動喉頭系統性能。本項目的研究隊伍由香港中文大學電子工程系的信號處理實驗室和香港大學言語聽覺科學系的語音康復專家組成。我們希望研究成果能直接改善無喉者的日常生活，同時也促進對人體發聲系統的構造和操作原理的理解。

414010.label: Realisation of objectives
414010.value: 1) To establish a mathematical model of EL speech production and to develop a software simulator of EL speech production A computer-controlled vibrator system was built using a mini-shaker and a tailor-made plastic head. The system could be used by a human subject to generate EL speech in a similar way to a commercial EL device. With this system, extensive experiments were carried out to measure the neck frequency response functions (NFRF) of different human subjects. Despite the individual differences among subjects, NFRF generally exhibited a high-pass characteristic. It was noted that the NFRF could not be completely separated from the vocal tract frequency response. For different vowel sounds, the measured NFRFs were found to be significantly different. All components in the EL speech production model were represented by linear systems and implemented using MATLAB. Owing to the limited time, we were not able to complete the development of a readily usable software simulator. 2) To analyze sEMG signals from different parts of human body and extract useful cues that are related to the production of lexical tones in Chinese speech A multi-channel desktop EMG system was set up for the acquisition of sEMG signals. Through extensive experiments, we successfully identified two relevant muscles in the neck region that are related to vocal pitch control. These two muscles are the sternocleidomastoid and the inferior belly of omohyoid. Both of them are close to skin surface. Parallel measurement of sEMG and acoustic speech signals was done on 5 male and 5 female normal subjects. The speech materials included pitch-varying sustained vowels and Cantonese isolated syllables that carry different lexical tones. A clear correlation between voice pitch and sEMG signal activities was found in most of the subjects. 3) To design new excitation source signals for producing EL speech of natural sound quality The acoustical signal generated by the computer-controlled vibrator system was found to have a relatively low intensity. We designed a novel strategy of generating the driving signal to enhance the loudness of output speech. In addition, we investigated ten different driving signals, which included periodic impulse train, sawtooth wave, sinsusoidal, Gaussian noise and their combinations. Five best driving signals were selected by perceptual experiments. We also tested with different fundamental frequencies and found the perceptually most preferred one by perceptual tests. 4) To evaluate the performance of the new methods by subjective listening tests In addition to the perceptual experiments on the driving signals (see objective 3), we carried out a subjective listening test on Cantonese tone

414010.label: Major findings and research outcome
414010.value: 1) There exist marked differences between the commercial electrolarynx devices and our experimental minishaker system. In the experimental system, sounds are generated via the vibration of the exciter plate. While this allows easy manipulation of the vibratory characteristics, the signal intensity is unavoidably lower than that of an commercial device, which uses a vibratory plunger. (Refer to Conference Paper No.6) 2) In EL speech production, the neck frequency response function has a high-pass characteristic. To produce output speech with sufficient loudness level, the driving signal is required to have large energy concentration in the low-order harmonic components. This renders periodic square wave an undesirable driving signal. Using multiple short-duration pulses in one pitch cycle is a good strategy for producing better and louder sound. The sound quality can be controlled by manipulating the heights and duration of the short pulses. (Refer to Refer to Conference Paper No.1 and No.6) 3) The exact neck frequency response function depends on the vocal tract configuration. It is not a realistic objective to derive a single neck transfer function that is applicable to all speech sounds. (Refer to Conference Paper No.1) 4) Among the non-laryngeal musles that are close to the neck skin surface, the sternocleidomastoid and the inferior belly of omohyoid have muscle activities that are related to voice pitch. The intensity of sEMG signal captured from the sternocleidomastoid is inversely proportional to the produced pitch level. The sEMG signal from the inferior belly of omohyoid showed simlar behavior to a lesser extent. (Refer to Conference Paper No.5 and No.7) 5) sEMG signals captured from the sternocleidomastoid and the inferior belly of omohyoid are closely related to Cantonese tones. High-pitch tones are associated with low sEMG amplitudes. The sternocleidomastoid exhibits more consistent correlation than the inferior belly of omohyoid. However, the sEMG signals are very noisy. In practice, it would not be possible to differentiate the six Cantonese tones based on sEMG. For Cantonese speech production using EL, three tone categories, namely high, mid, low, can be considered. (Refer to Conference Paper No.7)

414010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414010.value: 1) More studies are needed on joint investigation of the mechanical design of the vibrator and the electronic design of the driving signal; 2) Denoising strategies for sEMG signals need to be investigated. Possible methods include information fusion with multiple sensors; 3) Further investigation is needed to measure the neck frequency response functions of real laryngectomee patients; 4) The use of pitch and tone information captured from sEMG signals is not limited to conventional electrolarynx devices. It is applicable to other alarygeal speech methods.

414010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414010.value: The broad objective of this research project was to develop new technologies of speaking aids for laryngectomee patients who do not have a voice box. The research addressed the problems of poor sound quality and monotonic pitch in the existing electrolarynx systems. Based on both theoretical models and experimental measurements, we have established a mathematical system representation for electrolarynx speech production. We developed new design strategies for electrolarynx driving signals that can produce better-quality speech. We discovered two neck muscles that can be potentially utilized to provide information for pitch control of electrolarynx systems. This makes it possible to generate different lexical tones of Chinese speech and greatly improve the speech naturalness and intelligibility. Our research was a joint effort of signal processing researchers, voice scientists and medical doctors. The findings will be useful to the creation of new speaking devices which enable patients without voice box to communicate naturally and efficiently by speech.

414210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414210.value: Single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) DC-DC converter uses a single inductor to provide independent supply voltages to the circuit blocks inside an integrated system for reducing PCB size and saving cost of external components. Typical SIMO DC-DC converter operates in the discontinuous-conduction mode (DCM) but not in the continuous-conduction mode (CCM). Although the output-current capability can be enhanced by using the pseudo-CCM/DCM, this control method is suitable when all sub-converters provide high output power simultaneously. When only one or two sub-converters are needed to output high power, both the DCM and pseudo-CCM/DCM fail to regulate the sub-converters. In order to solve the above-mentioned problem, the goal of this project is to develop a new control scheme to regulate a SIMO DC-DC converter under different load conditions of the sub-converters. Circuit design to achieve the proposed control scheme is another challenging topic of this project. 單電感多輸出(SIMO) DC-DC電源轉換器使用單一電感器去提供多個獨立的電源電壓給予綜合系統內的電路塊。 這種方法可以減少PCB的尺寸和節省外部元件的成本。 典型的SIMO DC-DC電源轉換器在不連續導通模式(DCM) 而不是在連續傳導模式(CCM) 下運作。 雖然輸出電流能力能夠在P-CCM/DCM增強，但是這種控制方法只適用於當所有子轉換器同時間提供高輸出功率。 當只有一兩個子轉換器需要提供更高的功率時，這種控制方法便不適合使用。 為了解決上述問題，此項目的目標是開發一個新的管制計劃去控制SIMO DC-DC電源轉內的分轉換器換在不同負載條件下的運作。 而電路設計是這個項目內另一個具有挑戰性的課題。

414210.label: Realisation of objectives
414210.value: The project has been successfully completed. All objectives have been achieved. A structure of SITO dc-dc converter to solve unbalanced output power problem of each sub-converter has been developed. The proposed structure has been investigated and the impacts towards the cross-regulation have been studied as well. During the development of the proposed SITO dc-dc converter, a number of required circuit techniques and structures have been investigated, optimized and developed. They are 1. Pseudo-PWM operation based on PLL-based hysteresis control – In order to fix the switching frequency of developed dc-dc converters while accommodate all channels’ operation based on the required output power adaptively, a PLL-based hysteresis control has been developed. The pseudo inductor current is set adaptively by this proposed control. The locking time has been designed to be a small value to minimize the average inductor current for lower power loss by the dc resistance of inductor. 2. Fast high-gain error amplifier based on signal- and transient-current boosting technique – It is known that the transient speed of the error amplifier affects the transient responses of dc-dc converter. As such, a novel structure of amplifier based on proposed signal- and transient-boosting structure has been developed. Moreover, the voltage gain of error amplifier can be significantly enhanced by the proposed high-swing gain-boosting structure. 3. High-accuracy high-PSRR LDOs – The internal supplies of the controller in the dc-dc converter requires LDOs. It is known that supply variations and accuracy are the dominant factors to affect the overall line regulation and transient response of dc-dc converter. Three LDO structures which improve PSRR, transient response and overall accuracy, respectively, have been developed. 4. Energy-efficient charge pump – In the boost-mode operation, the supply voltage may need to be boosted in order to switch on and off the power transistors effectively. The controller may be powered up a charge-pump circuit. An efficient charge pump based on novel gate control strategy has been implemented. 5. A SIMO auto-buck-boost dc-dc converter with auto phase allocation – To optimize the power efficiency of a SIMO dc-dc converter with auto-buck-boost feature in the time-multiplexing mode (TMC), a such dc-dc converter has been developed. The design details including circuit structure, closed-loop stability and cross-regulation have been investigated and developed. Light load condition has been considered. 6. A SIMO dc-dc converter with duty-cycle control – Another dc-dc converter design method to modify the duty cycle for minimize cross-regulation under unbalanced load transient has been developed.

414610.label: Project Title(Chinese)
414610.value: 金融优化时间一致性问题研究

414610.label: Project Objectives
414610.value: To introduce the concept of time-efficiency in efficiency and to prove that time-consistency in efficiency is corresponding to the rational decision-making behavior when trade-off between mean and risk are wealth (history) dependent. To devise revised policies which perform better than the traditional mean-risk frameworks by eliminating irrational investment behaviors caused by their inherent nature of nonseparability, such that to satisfy time-consistency in efficiency. To develop mathematical frameworks for offering systematic approaches in constructing risk measures which are time consistent in efficiency and intuitive enough for investors, by utilizing, for example, the concepts of dynamic risk measure and g-expectation in the literature. To study the relationship between the market completeness and time consistency in efficiency: More specifically, to derive the conditions which the risk measures must satisfy to be time-consistent in efficiency, and to identify the relationship between the properties of (multiple) risk neutral probabilities and the time-consistency in efficiency for incomplete markets.

414610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414610.value: The last half century has witnessed promising applications of mean-risk portfolio selection frameworks in guiding investment practice. Choosing an appropriate risk measure is one of the most important steps in carrying out risk management in investment. When a risk measure satisfies time consistency, stage-t optimal investment policy derived at initial time is still optimal if we consider a truncated problem starting at stage t, thus offering no incentives for investors to deviate from the pre-committed policy. When a mean-risk measure satisfies time consistency in efficiency introduced in this proposal, any efficient portfolio selection policy remains efficient at any time in the process with respect to any current wealth level. When a mean-risk measure does not possess time-consistency in efficiency, following the optimal policy derived from such a mean-risk measure may yield irrational investment behaviors. Unfortunately, almost all widely adopted risk measures in the literature are not time consistent, or even not time-consistent in efficiency. Furthermore, the theoretical frameworks proposed recently in the literature on time consistency are difficult to satisfy and these abstract measures are not intuitively understandable by investors. The overall theme of the proposed research is to develop a framework to identify suitable mean-risk measures which satisfy time consistency in efficiency and can be intuitively understood and appreciated by investors. The achievement of the overall research goal will be attained by carrying out the following four specific research objectives. i) As the best portfolio policy is always sought under a multi-objective mean-risk framework, and time consistency is too restrictive to identify appropriate mean-risk measures, we propose to relax the requirement from time consistency to time consistency in efficiency. ii) We propose to upgrade these well adopted mean-risk frameworks to their revised versions to satisfy the time consistency in efficiency. iii) Utilizing the concepts of dynamic risk measure and g-expectation in the literature, we will develop mathematical frameworks for offering systematic approaches in constructing risk measures which are time consistent in efficiency and intuitive enough for investors. iv) We will study the relationship between the market completeness and time consistency in efficiency, investigate whether or not these well-known risk measures are time consistent in efficiency in complete markets and identify the conditions which the risk measures must satisfy to be time-consistent in efficiency. Furthermore, we will identify the relationship between the properties of (multiple) risk neutral probabilities and the time-consistency in efficiency for incomplete markets. 半个世纪以来，均值-风险模型已被公认为在指导投资组合实践中最重要最有前景的理论框架。为特定的投资者选择合适的风险度量已成为风险管理中的最重要的步骤之一。当风险度量满足时间一致性的时候，在初始时间得到的最优策略仍然是以t时刻为开始时间的截尾问题的最优策略。也就是说，若在后续的时间里采用预先制定的由动态规划求到的最优策略时，投资者绝不会后悔（不存在机会损失）。当均值-风险模型满足我们在该研究计划中提出的有效性意义下的时间一致性时，任何的有效投资策略，在随后的任何一个时点和可能财富水平下，依然是有效的（帕累托最优的）。一旦均值-风险模型不具有有效性意义下的时间一致性时，采用该模型的最优策略进行投资时，可能会出现非理性的投资行为。不幸的是，几乎所有被业界广泛使用的风险度量均不满足时间一致性，甚至也不满足有效性意义下的时间一致性。近年来学术界进行了关于时间一致性的大量理论研究，提出了许多理论框架。这些理论框架的技术条件要求过于苛刻和抽象，不易被投资者理解和接受。在这项研究计划中，我们的主要目标就是寻找合适的均值-风险模型，保证其满足时间一致性或者有效性意义下的时间一致性，同时保证其能被投资者很好的理解和接受。 为了完成以上的主要目标，我们准备从以下四个子目标入手。（1）：首先，均值-风险模型的最优投资策略是在多目标的框架下，通过权衡最终财富的期望和风险两个目标得到的。此时，时间一致性要求太强，一般的均值-风险模型难以满足。我们需要将时间一致性的要求放松为只保证最优投资策略的有效性而不是最优性，即采用有效性意义下的时间一致性要求。（2）尽管一些常用风险度量，如方差和VaR，能被投资者很好理解和使用，但是其函数形式的不可分性可能导致投资者在投资中存在一些非理性的投资行为。我们将尝试改进这些均值-风险模型，以使其满足有效性意义下的时间一致性。（3）利用文献中动态风险度量和g-期望的理论成果，我们将尝试构建一套系统的数学框架，为寻找满足有效性意义下的时间一致性，且能被投资者直观接受的风险度量提供帮助。（4）在均值-方差框架下，市场的完全性成为能够剔除有效性意义下的时间不一致性现象的一个因素。我们将进一步探讨除方差外的一些著名的风险度量，如半方差，VaR，CVaR等等，在完全市场下是否满足有效性意义下的时间一致性。并且，进一步研究在不完全市场下风险中性概率测度的属性和有效性意义下的时间一致性要求之间的关系。

414610.label: Realisation of objectives
414610.value: The concept of time-consistency in efficiency (TCIE) studied in Research Task 1 is to keep the pre-committed policy efficient at all the time instants and at any realizable wealth level. In our revised mean-variance policy devised in Research Task 2, when our semi-self-financing policy takes some money out of the market, it makes the trade-off adaptive to the current wealth level. While the revised mean-variance policy achieves the same mean-variance pair of the terminal wealth as the pre-committed policy, the revised policy enables the investor to receive a free cash flow stream during the investment process, thus offering a better portfolio policy to investors. We go beyond the scope of the Research Tasks 1 and 2 by offering necessary and sufficient conditions for TCIE in a cone-constrained market and identifying its close relationship with the minimum-variance signed supermartingale measure (VSSM) . We further establish a general procedure for constructing TCIE dynamic portfolio selection problems by introducing suitable portfolio constraints. Possessing features of both utility functions and risk measures, the lower-partial moments (LPM) proposed by Fishburn (1977) can be viewed as a utility type of risk measure. The LPM enables us to represent a general form of (downside) risk measures with two parameters, the benchmark level and the order of the moment. Our research in Research 3 has revealed that we can construct an LPM problem with order of moment equal to 2 to replace the original mean-variance formulation, as the LPM model is time consistent and dominates the original mean-variance formulation. Furthermore, our research has also revevealed that we can translate mean-VaR to an LPM problem with order of the moment equal to zero, and translate mean-CVaR to an LPM problem with order of the moment equal to one. In conclusion, LPM formulations can serve as various proxy risk measures which are time consistent and could eliminate some undesireable properties in the original mean-risk settings. Discrete-time mean-variance model, in general, corresponds to an incomplete market. We have proved in Research Task 4 that the existence of the free cash flow stream is related to the market completeness, i.e., the existence of the free cash flow stream disappears in a complete discrete-time market. We have further established a general procedure for eliminating time inconsistency in efficiency by introducing suitable portfolio constraints.

414610.label: Major findings and research outcome
414610.value: The mean-variance framework in dynamic portfolio selection is not time consistent, due to the inherent nonseparable nature of the involved variance term. The trade-off between the two conflicting objectives, the expected value and the variance of the terminal wealth, is time-varying and state-dependent. In some situations where the wealth level exceeds some threshold, the trade-off may change its sign, which implies that the investor changes his/her risk attitude towards the objectives, leading to time inconsistency in efficiency and irrational trading behaviors for the remaining investment periods. By relaxing the self-financing restriction to allow withdrawal of money out of the market, we develop a revised mean-variance policy which retains time consistency in efficiency (TCIE) for all time periods anf dominates the pre committed optimal mean-variance portfolio policy in the sense that, while the two achieve the same mean-variance pair of the terminal wealth, the revised policy enables the investor to receive a free cash flow stream (FCFS) during the investment process. The analytical expressions of the probability of receiving FCFS and the expected value of FCFS are derived. We emphasize that the distribution-free discrete-time mean-variance model in Li and Ng (2000), in general, corresponds to an incomplete market. We have proved that the existence of the free cash flow stream to be related to the market completeness, i.e., the existence of the free cash flow stream disappears in a complete discrete-time market. We have also analytically investigated the effect of portfolio constraints on the TCIE of convex cone-constrained markets. More specifically, we derive semi-analytical expressions for the pre-committed efficient mean-variance policy and the minimum-variance signed supermartingale measure (VSSM) and examine their relationship. Our analysis shows that the pre-committed discrete-time efficient mean-variance policy satisfies TCIE if and only if the conditional expectation of the density of the VSSM (with respect to the original probability measure) is nonnegative, or once the conditional expectation becomes negative, it remains at the same negative value until the terminal time. Our finding indicates that the TCIE property depends only on the basic market setting, including portfolio constraints. This important recognition motivates us to establish a general procedure for constructing TCIE dynamic portfolio selection problems by introducing suitable portfolio constraints.

414610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414610.value: Time inconsistency has been a thorny issue in the multi-period mean-variance portfolio selection and many other stochastic decision problems. We may consider to develop a two-tier planner-doer game model with self-control, in which the planner and doers represent different interests of the same investor at different time instants. In the model, the planner (the willpower to resist short term temptations) can impact preferences of doers through commitment by punishment, while the applied total penalty in turn affects the planner's own preference. Through aligning interests of planner and doers, a degree of internal harmony (measured quantitatively by the expected cost of self-control) can be achieved.

414610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414610.value: The seemingly straightforward mean-risk framework is generally preferred by both practitioners in the financial industry and researchers in academia, when compared to a more abstract, albeit more mathematically rigorous, expected utility maximization approach. However, some of the widely adopted risk measures, for example, the variance and VaR, do not satisfy coherence properties. Furthermore, almost all widely adopted risk measures are not time consistent. We may consider an LPM framework which endows some inherent features associated with a risk measure to a corresponding utility function and solves the primal mean-risk portfolio selection problem by invoking utility maximization. Under a realistic premise that investors only thoroughly understand their investment goals in terms of the mean and risk measures, we assume that investors prescribe their investment targets by setting certain attainable levels for the mean and risk measures. We then translate such investment targets in terms of the mean and risk measures into a corresponding utility maximization problem which possesses favorable properties and is computationally tractable.

414710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414710.value: Two important properties associated noble metal nanoparticles, i.e., the enhanced local electromagnetic field in the vicinity of the particle and the increased light scattering cross section with extended optical path, contribute to enhanced light absorption in semiconductors when plasmonic particles are incorporated, and thus making plasmonic nanostructures very attractive for constructing high-efficiency solar cell devices. In this type of solar cell, the improved device performance is closely related to the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) of the noble metal nanoparticles, which depends mostly on the material parameters including the particle size, shape, and density, as well as on the surrounding dielectric medium. Consequently, novel designs for plasmonic solar cells that make use of the critical material parameters could significantly improve the device efficiency, and would be of great interest and application potential. In the present work, we propose plasmonic solar cells employing novel nanostructured configurations—II-VI semiconductor/noble metal nanocomposite thin films, with noble metal nanorods (of controllable size, aspect ratio, and density) grown in the pores of a semiconductor photovoltaic network. The packing of metallic nanorods within the semiconductor could effectively introduce absorption enhancement in the whole photovoltaic layer with its adequate optical thickness guaranteed; while the adjustable aspect ratio, diameter, and packing density of the metal nanorods in the semiconductor matrix allow the fine tuning on the SPR wavelength for the maximum enhancement effect. In particular, we will investigate optical and photoelectric properties of the nanocomposite film device as functions of the critical material parameters including the composition of the semiconductor porous network, the noble metal nanorod aspect ratio, diameter and density, as well as the interfacial structure between semiconductor and the noble metal. The proposed work will lead to the identification of the correlations between the enhanced device photocurrent and these material parameters, and the determination of possible cell physical thickness reduction for high efficiency solar cell applications. 在此项计划书中，我们提出一种特殊的二六族半导体-金属纳米复合结构薄膜的概念，并研究其在等离子体增强太阳能电池中的应用。在这种纳米复合结构中，贵金属纳米棒将贯穿于有序的二六族半导体多孔薄膜中。它们的引入将提高半导体材料的吸光能力，从而提高太阳能电池的转换效率。

414710.label: Realisation of objectives
414710.value: CdSexTe1-x nanotube arrays have been synthesized using a template based wet chemistry method with x range from 0 to 1. Thickening the wall of the nanotube eventually leads to the formation of continuous porous layer on an ITO substrate with through-thickness pores perpendicular to the substrate. Au can be grown on the surface of the CdSexTe1-x nanotubes in the arrays. In the ultimate case, Au nanorods can be filled in the pores of the continuous porous layer of CdSexTe1-x. The microstructure and the optical properties of the CdSexTe1-x/Au nanocomposite have been investigated, and the correlations between the nanocomposite absorption properties and the material parameters (such as composition etc.) have been identified. Proto-type solar energy conversion devices using the CdSexTe1-x-based nanocomposite with different morphological combinations have been assembled, and their photoelectrochemical properties have been measured.

414710.label: Major findings and research outcome
414710.value: Using ZnO as template, CdSexTe1-x/ZnO nanocable arrays can be formed directly on conducting substrate with x adjustable from 0 to 1. Etching the ZnO core in the nanocable results in CdSexTe1-x nanotube arrays. Thickening the nanotube wall eventually gives continuous porous layer of CdSexTe1-x with through thickness pores perpendicular to the substrate surface. Two different methods were used for the ZnO nanowire array growth, i.e., the thermal evaporation method (TE) and hydrothermal method (HT) . The hydrothermal method allows the nanowire arrays to be prepared on almost any kinds of substrates while the suitable substrates for TE method are limited to high-temperature-stable ones. Moreover, HT samples showed higher electrical conductivity than TE samples, and thus are more suitable for electrical/electronic device applications [Liu Y et al.,ADVANCED FUNCTIONAL MATERIALS, 2011]. In addition, HT nanowires could be totally and easily etched away when used as the sacrificial templates, while the TE ones were found difficult to be removed. The nanocable-array based photoelectrodes were assembled with Pt counter electrodes for photovoltaic performance tests. The photoelectrodes showed seriously corrosion in the iodine electrolyte, while were stable in the polysulfide electrolytes. The cell using the electrolyte composed of 1 M Na2S, 1 M S and 1 M NaOH had the highest efficiency. [Zhu HJ, thesis work] CdSexTe1-x nanotube arrays showed strong visible-light absorption due to their small direct bandgaps and high absorption coefficients. High photocurrent and good photocatalytic performance of MB degradation have been observed,owing to efficient carrier separation and large surface area of semiconducting nanostructures[Zhu HJ et al., Nanoscale Research Letters, 2013; Wang XN et al.,Applied Catalysis B: Environmental, 2013]. Lastly, redox reaction between a Au(III) salt precursor and CdSe nanotube arrays results in formation of Au on the surface of CdSe and at the same time consumption of CdSe. By carefully controlling the growth conditions, one can obtain nanostructured arrays with composition ranging from CdSe/Au composite to Au. The presence of Au nanorods can enhance the absorption of the light absorbing materials, and lead to enhanced conversion efficiency of solar cells [Chang S et al., Energy Environ. Sci, 2012]. When loaded Raman-active molecules (4-MBA) on the Au nanotubes surface, the Raman scattering of these molecules are greatly increased for about 4 orders of magnitude compared to that recorded from their powder form due to the strong local field enhancement of Au nanotube arrays. [Zhu et al., Nanoscale, 2013]

414710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414710.value: The growth methodology of CdSexTe1-x nanotube arrays (and continuous porous layer) directly on conducting substrate can be generally extended to the fabrication of a large family of semiconducting and/or metallic nanostructures with similar configurations [Shi L. JOURNAL OF THE AMERICAN CHEMICAL SOCIETY, 2011]. Most recently, we have further explored the possibility of using ZnO as both the sacrificing and compositional template, forming ternary compound nanotube arrays [Guo X et al; CrystEngComm, 2013]. These semiconducting nanostructures may find applications in photocatalysis [Wang XN et al., Applied Catalysis B: Environmental, 2013 ] and energy storage (such as supercapacitors). When noble metals are employed, the specific geometric configuration would associate with specific plasmonic properties that can find applications in energy and sensing [Zhu HJ et al., Nanoscale, 2013]etc.

414710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414710.value: Nanostructured semiconducting architectures are promising candidates for applications of solar energy conversion. The present work investigate a possible configuration for such nanostructured architectures, i.e., the nanotube arrays (or continuous porous thin films) grown on conducting substrate, as it can directly serve as photoelectrode for solar energy conversion. The present work develops a general methodology that can be applied to a vast base of semiconducting (and even metallic) nanostructures with the proposed configuration, and is not only limited to binary compound systems. These nanostructures may find applications in solar cells and photocatalysis. Incorporation of noble metals to these semiconducting nanostructures leads to the formation of semiconductor/metal composite hetrostructures, when the plasmonic effect of the noble metal bring in many advantages, such as enhanced light absorption, for the composite material system.

414810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414810.value: In recent years, the idea of applying smart materials to structural devices and systems has been studied in various disciplines. In particular, magneto-rheological (MR) fluids are very promising for semi-active control devices by virtue of their adaptive properties. This controllable change of state with other desirable features such as high strength, good stability, broad operational temperature range, and fast response time show great potential in various applications. In this research, we aim to develop MR actuators with three functions as motor, clutch and brake. By integrating multifunctional technologies, size and weight of the MR actuator will be reduced while no external motor is needed. For applications such as assistive knee braces, concurrent designs in motor and clutch/brake are desirable for MR actuators, integrated with signal conditioning electronics. Prototypes of the smart MR actuators will be fabricated and tested. We will evaluate the motor and brake abilities individually, and then their concurrent motor/clutch performances when the operating conditions change. The output torque of the self-contained MR actuators will be investigated. Experimental efforts will be carried out to implement the optimally synthesized multifunctional MR actuators. The scientific knowledge base created through this project will facilitate the full realization of MR actuators for semi-active control devices and stimulate continuing research efforts in this area. The results of this study are essential for advancing the technology of various dynamic systems such as robots, medical applications, exercise equipment, vehicles, and rotary machinery. 414810.value: Innovative multifunctional magnetorheological (MR) actuators were designed. Novel MR actuators with motor/clutch/brake functions were designed and fabricated. Models of the smart MR actuators with torque and current equations were developed as the useful tool for deeper analyses and design optimization. Due to the interactions among motor, clutch and brake functions within the self-contained MR actuator, it would be interesting to figure out how they could work together and/or affect one another. Physical insights have been discussed to have better understanding on interactions among different functions. The integrated MR actuator with motor/clutch/brake functions has been implemented. The proposed ideas and analyses have been evaluated and validated. The project objectives have been fully realized.

414810.label: Major findings and research outcome
414810.value: Multifunctional actuators utilizing magnetorheological (MR) fluids were first considered for assistive knee braces. MR fluids were integrated into a motor to work with multiple functions as a motor, clutch, and brake in order to meet the requirements of normal human walking. [c 8.2, 2011]. In some environments with very limited working space, an integrated actuation device with multiple functions would be desirable. We developed novel MR fluid based multifunctional rotary actuators [c 11 Patents, 2012, 2014]. The configurations and design details of the motor part and clutch/brake part were illustrated, and the operating principle of the actuator was discussed as well. The torques of the motor part and clutch/brake part were derived. The finite element method was utilized to analyze the magnetic circuits, the influence of permanent magnets on the MR fluid, and the magnetic flux distribution. A prototype of the actuator was fabricated and each function was tested. The results showed that the developed actuator is promising for applications which require multiple functions with compact size. [c 8.1 SMS 2012; c 8.3 2013] In addition, we performed optimization of a multifunctional actuator utilizing MR fluids. In our earlier design of the MR fluid based rotary devices, the inner coils are mainly in interior and exterior forms. However, the effect of these two forms of inner coils on output torque was not discussed. To perform optimization of the brake function, models with different inner coils were built, analyzed and compared. Among them, the model with interior inner coil is the best option in terms of output torque. Based on the analysis, optimization of the multifunctional actuator was carried out. The corresponding prototype was then fabricated and each function of the developed multifunctional actuator was tested [c 9.1; c 8.4 2014]. We also studied the feasibility of applying MR fluids in different dynamic parts of a bicycle such as the transmission and braking systems. MR continuous variable transmission (CVT) and power generator assisted in braking systems were designed and analyzed. Experimental results showed that the proposed designs are promising to be used in bicycles. [c 9.2 SPIE 2013]. Furthermore, we proposed a new MR-fluid working operation, in which MR fluids work between gear transmissions. The results of this research would be beneficial to advance the design and multiple functions of MR dampers while not limited to traditional piston-type design. [c 9.3 SPIE 2013].

414810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414810.value: This RGC supported project (CUHK414810) conducted at CUHK has resulted in 2 book chapters, 1 international journal paper (with another one to be submitted), 3 conference papers, and 3 awarded patents. One PhD student was trained, and our team has received the Best Poster Award on CU Energy Day in August 2012. Although significant results have been obtained through this project, research and development could be further conducted to fully realize this technology. Exoskeletons and assistive knee braces using magnetorheological actuators with multiple functions should be further developed.
