415110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
415110.value: 無人水面機器人的自適應視覺伺服控制

415110.label: Project Objectives
415110.value: To develop a new design scheme for robust visual servoing of a differentially driven water surface robot to cope with the nonholonomic motion constraints, uncertain hydrodynamic forces, unknown geometric information of the image features, unknown camera parameters and image errors. To analyze the stability and robustness of the proposed controllers using the Lyapunov theory on the basis of the hydrodynamics and nonholonomic constraints of the water surface robots. To implement the controllers in the water surface robot at our laboratory and validate their performance by experiments.
rows: To develop a new design scheme for robust visual servoing of a differentially driven water surface robot to cope with the nonholonomic motion constraints, uncertain hydrodynamic forces, unknown geometric information of the image features, unknown camera parameters and image errors.
To analyze the stability and robustness of the proposed controllers using the Lyapunov theory on the basis of the hydrodynamics and nonholonomic constraints of the water surface robots.
To implement the controllers in the water surface robot at our laboratory and validate their performance by experiments.

415110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415110.value: Unmanned water surface robots move autonomously on the surface of a lake, or a river and or a sea in order to accomplish tasks such as cleaning, surveillance, and environmental monitoring. In many situations, the robots rely on visual cameras to guide their motion. Visual servoing is a method that directly feeds back the visual information to the low-level motion controller of the robots so that they can respond faster to the changing environments. Compared to robot manipulators and ground robots, there are several new challenges in visually controlling a water surface robot. First, the hydrodynamic forces play important roles in the robot dynamics. Second, most water surface robots are subject to nonholonomic motion constraints. Third, there are various uncertainties in camera parameters due to pan-tilt motion, image errors, and environmental noises. Those issues make it difficult to design a stable visual servo controller for water surface robots, and hence no effective solution has been developed so far. This project proposes to develop new design schemes for robust visual servoing of a differentially driven water surface robot. First, to cope with the nonholonomic motion constraints, we propose to design a two dimensional error function so as to change the position and orientation control of the nonholonomic robot to a problem of controlling two error variables using two control inputs. A new design scheme for adaptive visual servoing will be developed based on the new error function. An on-line algorithm will be incorporated with the controller so as to cope with un-calibrated camera parameters and unknown depths of the image features. In order not to compensate for the uncertain hydrodynamic forces of the robot, we will develop a model-free adaptive controller to regulate the position and orientation of the robot. We will use the Lyapunov theory to analyze the stability and robustness of the proposed controllers while addressing the nonholonomic constraints and the hydrodynamic forces. Finally, the controllers will be implemented on a water surface robot at our laboratory and their performance will be validated by experiments. The results of this project will have many potential applications in surveillance, environment monitoring, and other areas.

415110.label: Realisation of objectives
415110.value: We have fully achieved the objectives of the project. The research activities are detailed as follows: 1) We developed a new estimator for estimating position of a water surface robot and other mobile robots on-line by fusing measurements of the orientation and linear velocity with the visual information. This new estimator employs an on-line algorithm, similar to that for estimating unknown parameters in the model-based adaptive controller, to estimate unknown geometry of the 3-D features and position of the robot. It has been proven that this approach yields asymptotic stability of the position estimation and the errors will not accumulate during the motion. 2) We investigated vision-based trajectory tracking control of nonholonomic water surface robots/mobile robots when the hydraulic drift term is not taken into account, i.e. in calm water. A visually servoed controller has been developed for the robot to trace a time-varying trajectory stably without using GPS sensors for localization. The nonholonomic constraints of the robot are taken into account in the controller design. 3) We extended the aforementioned controller to control of nonholonomic water surface robots with hydraulic terms. This new controller embeds the vision-based position estimator into the low-level control loop and enables the water surface robot to trace time-varying trajectory without direct position measurement. 4) We have analyzed the stability of the proposed visual servo controllers using Lyapunov theory. The controller gives rise to asymptotic stability of the system when the desired velocity of the robot is not equal to zero. (5) We have developed an experimental system for verifying the proposed vision-based position estimator and trajectory tacking controllers. A differentially driven water surface robot has been built. In order to achieve real-time efficiency, a parallel computing system using GPU has been developed so that the processing time for all the image processing can be shorten to 10ms. Experiments have been conducted to verify the performance of the controllers on the water surface of the CUHK lake. The results validated the expected performance.

415110.label: Major findings and research outcome
415110.value: The major findings and research output of this project are as follows: 1) A new algorithm has been developed for estimating the position of a water surface robot and other mobile robots on-line by fusing the orientation and linear velocity with the visual information. This algorithm is of a simple structure particularly suitable for parallel implementation and its performance is guaranteed by Lyapunov theory. The work was presented at the 10th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation and 2012 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Biomimetics, and has been published in IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics (A Simple and Parallel Algorithm for Real-Time Robot Localization by Fusing Monocular Vision and Odometry/AHRS Sensors, IEEE/ASME Trans. on Mechatronics, vol. 19, no. 4, pp. 1447-1457, 2014). 2)A new visually servoed controller has been developed for tracking control of a nonholonomic water surface robot in calm water and ground nonholonomic mobile robot. The nonholonomic constraints of the robot are taken into account in the controller design. It is the first successful work for vision-based tracjectory tracking of nonholonomic mobile robots. The results have been presented at 2013 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation and accepted for publication on IEEE Trans. on Robotics (“Visually Servoed Trajectory Tracking of Nonholonomic Mobile Robots without Direct Position Measurement”, IEEE Transactions on Robotics, 2014). 3) A new controller has been proposed to control nonholonomic water surface robots with hydraulic draft terms. This new controller embeds the vision-based adaptive estimation for robot position into the low-level control loop and enables the robot to trace time-varying trajectory without direct position measurement. This results has been submitted to IEEE Trans. on Control Systems Technology, presented at 2013 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Biomimetics, and accepted for presentation at 2014 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems. 4) Two Ph.D. students: Mr. Kai Wang and Mr. Luyang LI were supported by this project. Dr. Wang obtained his Ph.D. in 2014 and Mr. Li will complete his study in 2015.

415110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415110.value: The controllers developed in this project can be further improved by removing the assumptions on the measurement of the orientation and linear velocity. Ideally, we should control the position and orientation of the robot purely using the visual feedback by estimating the orientation and linear velocity from vision. More theoretical work needs to be conducted on robustness analysis of the proposed controllers. Finally, it may be possible to extend the controllers to formation control of water surface robots and further investigation on this issue needs to be carried out.

415110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415110.value: Water surface robots move autonomously on the surface of a lake, or a river and or a sea in order to accomplish tasks such as cleaning, surveillance, and environmental monitoring. In many situations, the robots rely on vision to guide their motion. The difficulties in controlling such a robot using vision arise in localizing its position and coping with the nonholonomic constraints and hydraulic dynamics. In this project, we investigated the crucial problems in vision-based control of the robot. First, to estimate position of the robot on-line, we proposed a simple and parallel algorithm by fusing vision with IMU measurements. Second, we developed the first controller for a water surface robot in calm water to track a time-varying trajectory using visual feedback. Third, a visually servoed controller has been developed to cope with both the nonholonomic constraints and hydraulic forces. The performance of the proposed position estimator and controllers was analyzed by Lyapunov theory. Finally, we developed a water surface robot and conducted experiments on it to validate the approaches. The results led to publications in the top journals and presentations at the major international conferences in the area. This project supported two Ph.D. students as well.

415310.label: Project Title(Chinese)
415310.value: 關於數學理論與應用滲透和傳播信仰的大型通信網絡

415310.label: Project Objectives
415310.value: Develop a general mathematical theory to analyze influence spreading, belief propagation and percolation for large scale communication networks. To validate the mathematical theory that we develop can be applied to communication networks with tens of millions of nodes, we plan to develop a fluid-like parallel simulator on multi-core clustered machines, which are available in CUHK, so that we can test and validate the theory on different range of network topologies. We plan to apply the theory to several important new services on the Internet, they are: (a) Designing efficient product advertisement strategies for large scale online social networks. (b) Designing effective security investment and pricing policies [8,10,11] so as to encourage participating nodes to adapt and thereby making the whole network more secure and robust. (c) Designing effective deployment policies for new communication protocols, for example, how should one encourage and influence different ISPs to deploy the IPv6 protocol[16]}. Apply the algorithms we develop for online social networks and protocols deployment policies under realistic scenarios. We are collaborating with ``Tencent Inc.'', which has the largest online social network in China (e.g., QQ software), to test out different methods of performing product advertisement. We also collaborate with the China Education and Research Network (CERNET), which has over 30 million users, on how to effectively encourage users to perform security investment and IPv6 protocol deployment. The academic impact of this research will help the computer system and network researchers to gain the fundamental understanding on the issues and tradeoffs of information and influence spreading on large scale networks. This research will contribute to the body of theoretical networking knowledge and give insight to the system implementation in the fields of computer and networking technologies. As stated in our objectives, the industrial impact of this project is in assisting local industry (e.g., Tencent Inc.) on product advertisement in online social networks, as well as how one can incentivize security investment and protocol deployment in CERNET.

415310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415310.value: 世界上沒有任何可以溝通的地理限制。事實上，人們現在相互作用不僅通過電子郵件，而且在不同的溝通類型的虛擬世界，公告博客和在線社交網絡。我們的行為或決定可以影響這些互動，有趣的是，我們的決定可以作為一個 ""催化劑"為其他人作出自己的決定。 為了說明這一點，考慮一個在線社交網絡的其中一家公司要完成的目標廣告。具體來說，這家公司有多少其產品的免費樣品，並希望這些免費派發樣品，用電磁小時間選擇性組的用戶通過 OSN。 該公司的目的不僅是為了吸引這一小部分用戶購買的產品，而且還依賴於這個小設置用戶創建一個梯級口碑影響力給其他用戶，從而觸發一個更大的一套用戶通過 OSN購買該產品。這個傳播時間的影響是很有挑戰性的模型或量化。一方面，不同的用戶可以查看的產品不同，例如，有些人可能喜歡的產品，而其他人可能不喜歡，或甚至可以無動於衷。此外，任何現實的OSN的有幾千萬用戶和國家空間表示所有這些用戶成為在時間維度詛咒建模的問題。 要充分認識影響和信仰傳播的影響，以及如何將這些相互依存的決定，可過濾大規模通信網絡，我們需要制定一個正式的和分析方法，模型和動態行為分析底層網絡的節點，它可以由一個普通連通圖。 鑑於這種方法，人們可以了解用戶（或節點）互動，和一個可以評估信息傳播的速度，率信仰的傳播，以及必要和足夠的條件一小部分節點引發大級聯。更重要的是，數學理論可有助於我們制定更有效的算法來新的服務，例如，優化分配給用戶的免費樣品在OSN的，適當的激勵政策，鼓勵用戶投資安全的措施，或以激勵用戶去適應一個新的協議標準，例如，IPv6。 本研究的目的是要開發一個通用的數學理論'和應用它接獲的新服務的大型通信網絡例如互聯網或在線社交網絡。這一數學基礎將提供基本的認識網絡研究人員和工程師或誰需要設計高效的算法為新的互聯網服務，如產品廣告，或幫助決策者決定實施的有效途徑安全或議定書部署在互聯網，以及取得的諒解動態行為大型團體，例如點對點通信蜂擁 /流系統。

415410.label: Project Title(Chinese)

415410.label: Project Objectives
415410.value: Fault avoidance and fault removal for service-oriented systems. This objective is to model the work flows of complex service-oriented systems. Based on the model, different verification approaches will be proposed to detect the design problems of the service-oriented systems. Moreover, test cases will be generated based on the model, and model-based testing techniques will be investigated for discovering and removing system faults. Fault tolerance for service-oriented systems. This objective is to investigate fault tolerance strategies for masking Web service faults and for preventing faulty service components from causing major system problems. Adaptive and reconfigurable fault tolerance strategies will first be designed to handle the dynamic changes of Web service performance as well as user requirements. Then, we will apply service fault tolerance techniques for the stateful Web services, which are much more challenging than stateless Web services, due to the state dependency between different Web services. Finally, Byzantine fault tolerance for Web services will be comprehensively investigated. Fault prediction for service-oriented systems. Our objective in this task is to design a systematic reliability prediction approach for complex service-oriented systems. Complementary to the existing reliability prediction approaches which mainly focus on system-level compositional analysis, a new paradigm for both component-level reliability prediction and system-level reliability aggregation will be explored. Specifically, we will employ machine learning techniques for investigating a novel collaborative reliability prediction model, which predicts the Web service reliability for the current service user by employing past failure data of other similar service users on the same Web service. A Web service reliability aggregation model will therefore be proposed, where Web service reliability can be well predicted.

415410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415410.value: Service-oriented systems are becoming prevalent nowadays. Service-oriented architecture (SOA) has been widely employed in e-business, e-government, automotive systems, multimedia services, process control, finance, and a lot of other domains. The trend towards large-scale complex service-oriented systems makes it a formidable talk in developing reliable service applications. In traditional software reliability engineering, there are four major approaches in building highly reliable systems: fault avoidance, fault removal, fault tolerance, and fault prediction. However, in the service-oriented environment, most of the traditional software reliability engineering techniques may not work properly due to the immense degree of heterogeneity of Web services, the vastly unpredictable Internet environment, and the fact that the remote service components are provided and hosted by other organizations. We have recently been focused on extending traditional software reliability engineering techniques and designing new reliability techniques for the service-oriented systems. Our preliminary research efforts convinced us that formalizing a systematic and efficient design paradigm for reliable service-oriented systems is not only urgent, but also vital for the future success of service computing. We propose to advance the current state-of-the-art in service reliability engineering by providing systematic and comprehensive investigations on various service reliability engineering techniques. Four research tasks are proposed in this project, which are: (1) service fault avoidance and service fault removal techniques, (2) service fault tolerance techniques, (3) service fault prediction techniques, and (4) a service reliability engineering toolkit and real-world Web service QoS datasets. This project will enable us to build reliable service-oriented systems, whose achieved reliability can be predicted. Practical and systematic service reliability techniques will not only promote the development of service computing research, but also facilitate the establishment of Hong Kong’s preeminent status as one of the world’s major service centers, whose daily operations highly depends on reliable IT service infrastructures. As a tangible outcome, the service reliability techniques will be encapsulated into a toolkit, which will be widely released to industry and academia. 在当今世界，面向服务的系统变得非常盛行。面向服务架构（SOA）已被广泛运用在电子商务，电子政务，汽车系统，多媒体服务，过程控制，金融和很多其他领域。当今系统大型化和复杂化的趋势使得开发高度可靠的面向服务系统变得很困难。在传统的软件可靠性工程领域，主要有四种开发高度可靠系统的方法，它们是：故障避免，故障排除，容错和故障预测。然而，在面向服务的环境中，传统的软件可靠性工程技术很可能无法被正常使用。因网络服务是异构的，因特网环境是不可预知的，而不同的网络服务组件是由不同的组织提供和维护的。最近，我们一直专注于扩展传统的软件可靠性工程技术和设计新的面向服务的可靠性技术。我们初步的研究成果使我们相信，构建一个系统的和高效的设计框架来开发可靠的面向服务的系统不仅迫切，而且也是服务计算在未来能否成功的关键。我们建议，通过对各种可靠性工程技术进行系统和全面的调查来提升目前服务可靠性工程的发展水平。这个项目提出了四个研究任务，它们是：（1）服务故障避免和服务故障排除技术，（2）服务容错技术，（3）服务故障预测技术，（4）服务可靠性工程工具包和真实的网络服务QoS数据集。该项目将使我们能够建立可靠的面向服务的系统，并使其可靠性可以被预测。实用的服务可靠性技术，不仅将促进服务计算研究的发展，也将奠定香港作为世界上主要服务中心的地位。因为香港的日常服务业务很大程度上是建立在高度可靠的IT服务基础设施之上的。作为一种有形的结果，这个项目的服务可靠性技术将被封装成一个工具包，并广泛发布到产业界和学术界。

415410.label: Realisation of objectives
415410.value: All the project objectives have been either completely achieved, or exceedingly achieved. In addition to the proposed reliability engineering techniques for service-oriented systems, we extended the proposed approaches to various applications, which include sensor network systems, recommender systems, social networks, and expert finding systems. In addition, the project enabled us to explore a number of new modeling techniques in machine learning theory for the analysis of complicated scenarios in modern software intensive and service oriented systems.

415410.label: Major findings and research outcome
415410.value: Totally seven journal papers and 16 conference papers have been published, all acknowledging the support of this grant. These publications cover the proposal's research objectives in various aspects. We describe the resulting research outcomes as follows. (We use [J1] label to refer to journal publication [1], and [C1] label to refer to conference publication [1], etc.). In fault avoidance and fault removal for service-oriented systems, we proposed a cloud service redeployment mechanism based on user experience [C5]. This approach considered both reliability and performance for cloud computing service in a holistic scheme. In specific applications, [J4] investigated fault avoidance techniques in underwater acoustic sensor networks with a specific reliability oriented protocol. The conformance testing of the protocol was evaluated in [C9], and its priority scheduling was explored in [C10]. In programming techniques, [C3] established a foundation for managing API complexity with flow-augmented call graph for reliability purpose. Regarding fault tolerance for service-oriented systems, [J2] engaged a new metrics for similarity measurement to identify similar modules in a software system for fault tolerance purpose. [C4] proposed a Byzantine fault tolerance framework for cloud computing and service computing based on resource constraints. In fault prediction for service-oriented systems, we proposed an innovative collaborative Web service Quality of Service (QoS) prediction technique with memory-based approach in [C6] and with model-based matrix factorization approach in [J6]. We further described a clustering-based QoS prediction approach for Web services in [C16], and formulated a systematic personalized reliability prediction for service-oriented systems in [J7]. The reliability prediction techniques formulated in this project was extended to recommendation systems for popular applications in IT era. These extensions include exploring social regularization for recommender systems [C1], employing fusion approaches for quality and relevance for multi-criteria recommendation [C2], applying learning techniques for question suggestion in online forums [C7] and Twitter [C13], engaging question routing schemes in community question answering [C14], using Web service engines for cross-library API recommendation [C8], formulating probabilistic factor models for website recommendation [C12], allowing social recommendation by incorporating social contextual information [J5], exploiting heterogeneous bibliographic networks for expert ranking [C15], and predicting expertise with social and academic communities [J3]. The project also made theoretical contributions in machine learning techniques for prediction. [J1] proposed an efficient sparse generalized multiple kernel learning techniques, which allows the employment of the advanced machine learning technique for analysis of complicated fault interaction scenarios for fault prediction purpose. [C11] explored irrelevant data in helping semi-supervised learning.

415410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415410.value: In this project we have investigated software reliability engineering techniques for developing reliable service-oriented systems with predictable reliability. The techniques applied includes fault avoidance, fault prediction, fault tolerance, and fault forecasting. Further research can be investigated for the design and publication of a service reliability engineering toolkit with a collection of demonstratable datasets. This would allow our formulated service reliability engineering techniques to be implemented and disseminated for wide adoption among researcher's and practitioner's communities. Service-oriented system developers can effectively apply suitable reliability techniques for service computing, while researchers can further investigate with our published data sets for further exploration of service-oriented reliability engineering techniques. We plan to apply the proposed paradigm to a number of research projects in service computing area, collecting real world data for publication and sharing. Some of the new data have appeared in the WS-DREAM site for Web service QoS datasets sharing site (http://www.wsdream.net/) that we have been maintaining. More projects will be incorporated, with their resulting data incorporated.

415410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415410.value: We formalized a systematic and efficient design paradigm for reliable service-oriented systems. Included in this paragidm are service fault avoidance and service fault removal techniques, service fault tolerance techniques, and service fault prediction techniques. The effectiveness of this paradigm in advancing the current state-of-the-art service reliability engineering has been demonstrated through the implementation of experimentation of the proposed techniques therein. This project enables service reliability engineers to build reliable service-oriented systems, whose achieved reliability can be quantitatively managed and predicted. The resulting paradigm is both comprehensive and systematic. It formulates methodical service reliability engineering techniques to modern service-oriented systems, enables efficient, predictable, and reliable service-oriented system development, and promotes research by releasing large-scale real-world Web service QoS datasets. The proposed techniques in this project promote the development of service computing research in general, and facilitate the ongoing reserch in the Internet era, where immense degree of heterogeneiby of Web service with vastly unpredictable connection time and various degree of service quality.

415810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415810.value: This project focuses on the theoretical aspects of a communication problem: determining the set of achievable data rate pairs for a broadcast channel; a classic open problem in the area of network information theory. While special cases such as the Gaussian noise model has had success in the past decade, results in the general case of the discrete memoryless broadcast channels were dated back to the seventies and early eighties. The project proposes to build on a series of notable successes and novel ideas developed by the principal investigator over the period of last two years. The relevance and practical motivation of this study is the following: the demand for data over wireless networks has increased dramatically in the last decade primarily due to two factors. First, the density of wireless users have increased several fold; and second, the data demand per user has also increased dramatically, thanks to the growing popularity of mobile computing devices. Given that wireless bandwidth is a limited, scarce, and expensive resource the need for maximizing throughput in a given communication scenario has increased tremendously. It is in this backdrop that we investigate, from a fundamental theoretical perspective, the maximum possible data rates in basic multiuser communication scenarios. Traditionally there was a huge gap between the rates achievable for practical communication strategies and the fundamental communication limits, even in a point-to-point network. However, remarkable advances in technology(both hardware and algorithms) over the past decade has significantly closed the gap between practical algorithms and fundamental limits in the single user setting. Unlike the single user setting, most fundamental communication problems in the multiuser setting remain unsolved and most of the available tools and techniques date back to 70s and early 80s. Preliminary research, conducted by the author along with some research collaborators, has proved that one can go beyond the communication rates obtained via traditional tools and techniques. This proposal seeks to build on a series of significant preliminary results and ideas in order to investigate the full implications of the preliminary results, and to explore exciting new directions prompted by these results. Researchers worldwide are trying to squeeze more data through a given channel in wireless networks. In identifying the fundamental limits one develops new techniques and understands optimal strategies, which then can be incorporated into practical implementations. This theoretical study intends to enlarge the available set of communication strategies in large networks.

416010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416010.value: The existing video coding standards use Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) or its simplified variants, such as Integer Cosine Transform (ICT), for transform coding. The underlying assumption is that the signal to be transformed can be modeled by a first-order Markov random field with the correlation coefficient approaching 0.95. This assumption has been verified for images. In video coding, where the input of the transform is the intra or inter prediction error instead of the original pixels, the assumption is violated. Based on our study, the correlation coefficient varies from 0.1 to 0.9, depending on the spatial resolution. The reason is that edges become dominant in a residual frame. In a frame to be coded, the energy in smooth areas is greatly reduced by motion-compensated prediction (MCP), but in edge areas, where the prediction is sensitive to occlusion and geometric distortion, the residue’s energy along the edge direction is still strong. When the edges are neither horizontal nor vertical, conventional transforms result in large-magnitude high-frequency coefficients that not only need more bits to code, but also introduce large quantization noise at low bit rates. Actually, the directional transform, which efficiently compacts energy along arbitrary edges, has been a research topic in image coding for many years. It will have a more significant impact on video coding, where efficiently dealing with edges becomes more critical according to the above rationale. The proposed work will be the first attempt to develop a directional transform for block-based hybrid video coding. It will have three features. Firstly, as the name implies, the energy along the edge direction is efficiently compacted to a few transform coefficients. Secondly, the complexity is acceptable for the current software and hardware platforms, on which the video codecs with the directional transform integrated are running. Thirdly, the directional transform implicitly adapts to various local edges, so the side information to indicate the edge direction can be saved. The proposed directional transform will be integrated into the state-of-the-art video codecs such as H.264 as an alternative to the current transform used and both the subjective and objective improvements will be rigorously evaluated. Therefore, the related techniques including quantization, entropy coding and transform mode decision, will be optimized to maximize the benefit of directional transform. The improved rate-distortion (R-D) performance over H.264 will have a significant impact in the development of the next generation video coding standard. 現有的視頻編碼標準使用離散餘弦變換(DCT)或其簡化方案，如整數餘弦變換(ICT)，來減低空間冗餘。這一做法依賴于一個前提假設，也就是輸入變換的信號符合相關系數約為0.95的一階馬爾可夫隨機場模型。對于圖像編碼，輸入變換的信號是原始採樣，這一假設已被驗證是正確的。但是在視頻編碼中，輸入變換的信號是幀內或幀間預測誤差(或稱之為殘差)，這一前提假設未必成立。根據我們的研究，以邊緣為主的殘差信號的相關系數普遍小于0.95，並大致隨著視頻信號的空間分辨率的增加而增加，在0.1到0.9 範圍內波動。殘差信號以邊緣為主是因為：平滑區域能被預測的很準確，殘差的能量相對較小；而邊緣豐富的區域受到遮擋及幾何變形等因素的影響不容易被準確地預測，往往產生和邊緣相關的高能量預測誤差。特別是當邊緣不是水平或豎直時，使用傳統的變換將導致頻域幅值較大的高頻系數，而這些高頻系數需要更多的比特來編碼，在低碼率的時候還會引入大量化誤差。 方向變換能將任何邊緣的能量沿著其方向集中起來，從而達到高效的壓縮效果。這一課題在圖像編碼領域已有多年的研究歷史，對于視頻編碼將有更深遠的影響，因為根據上述分析，殘差信號以邊緣為主導，對邊緣的有效壓縮是具有決定意義的。 應用于基于塊的混合視頻編碼的方向變換是一個全新的課題，本研究方案是對這一課題的首次嘗試，它將具有三個特征。首先，如題所示，任何邊緣的能量都能沿著其方向集中到少數的變換系數上；第二，其復雜度對于現今主流的軟件和硬件平台來說是可接受的；第三，方向變換可以靈活地運用于局部的邊緣，而不需要傳送任何額外的信息。 本研究方案會將設計好的方向變換集成到最新的視頻編解碼器中，如H.264，作為其已有變換方案的另一選擇。我們會對方向變換所帶來的主觀和客觀編碼效果的提升做出嚴格的評估。同時，我們也會優化一些和變換相關的模塊，如量化，熵編碼，以及變換模式決策，將方向變換的好處發揮到最大。由方向變換帶來的率失真性能的提高對下一代視頻編碼標準的制定將會有深遠的影響。

416010.label: Realisation of objectives
416010.value: Objective 1: We adopted two approaches: (a) The Mode-Dependent Directional Transform (MDDT) is the state-of-the-art directional transform for video coding. It is mode dependent, but it does not consider the video content in designing the transform bases. We improved the Mode-Dependent Directional Transform (MDDT) by first defining a video content feature as a concatenation of coefficient magnitude, dominant gradient and spatial activity histograms of residues. Then each KLT basis which is obtained from off-line training is associated with a given feature. Lastly, a histogram-based feature matching algorithm is proposed to select the best transform basis from the provided multiple candidates for encoding a frame. Experiment results showed that an average PSNR improvement of 0.65 dB can be achieved by the proposed Content Dependent Directional Transform (CDDT) compared to MDDT for inter frame coding. Compared to Rate-Distortion Optimized Transform (RDOT), it also has about 3% bits saving with similar peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) improvement. (b) We further designed a two-layer transform structure, where the first layer uses discrete wavelet transform to compact the residue energy to the LL band and then the second layer uses 2-D non-separable directional transforms to deal with the arbitrary edge directions in the four subbands. By doing this, the edges in a macroblock are efficiently compacted to a few coefficients and at the same time the overhead used to indicate the transform directions is affordable. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme provides a PSNR gain of up to 0.46 dB, compared with the H.264/AVC High Profile. Objectives 2 and 3: Transform has been widely used to remove spatial redundancy of prediction residuals in the modern video coding standards. However, since the residual blocks exhibit diverse characteristics in a video sequence, conventional transform methods with fixed transform kernels may result in low efficiency. To tackle this problem, we proposed a novel content adaptive transform framework for H.264/AVC-based video coding. The proposed method utilizes pixel rearrangement to dynamically adjust the transform kernels to adapt to the video content. In addition, unlike the traditional adaptive transforms, the proposed method obtains the transform kernels from the reconstructed block, and hence it consumes only one overhead bit for each transform unit. Moreover, rate distortion optimization scheme is used to choose the best candidate kernels. In addition, a spiral-scanning method is developed to reorder the transform coefficients for better entropy coding. Experimental results on the H.264/AVC Key Technical Area (KTA) platform showed that the proposed method can achieve an average of 0.35 dB gain in PSNR, and an average bitrate reduction of about 7.95% and 7.0% in all-intra and low-delay configurations, respectively. Objective 4: The objective performance is evaluated in terms of PSNR gain and bitrate reduction against the H.264/AVC video coding standard, which are measured by the Bjontegaard-Delta Bit Rate (BD-BR) and the Bjontegaard-Delta PSNR (BD-PSNR) metrics. Subjective evaluation was carried out by informal viewing by the human observers, and the subjective results are shown as printed images in the published papers. Formal subjective tests were not carried out due to the lack of viewing facility (we did not have enough funding to build it) conforming to international standard such as CCIR recommendation 500-3, which specifies the standard visual environment for conducting picture quality assessment. Moreover, in almost all the published papers on H.264/AVC, the BD-BR and BD-PSNR metrics are commonly used to compare performance across different coding algorithms, without giving any formal subjective evaluation results.

416010.label: Major findings and research outcome
416010.value: 1. A two-layer transform structure, where the first layer uses discrete wavelet transform to compact the residue energy to the LL band and then the second layer uses 2-D non-separable directional transforms to deal with the arbitrary edge directions in the four subbands has been developed. The proposed scheme achieved a PSNR gain of up to 0.46 dB, compared with the H.264/AVC High Profile. One journal paper (Section 8, Paper #1) based on the research findings was published. 2. A novel Content Dependent Directional Transform (CDDT) for video coding has been developed. The CDDT adapts to the video content by taking into account the coefficient magnitude, dominant gradient and spatial activity histograms of the residues as features. The transform basis associated with a given feature is obtained from off-line training; and the best basis is then selected to encode a frame. Experiment results showed that an average PSNR gain of 0.17 dB and 0.65 dB can be achieved by the proposed scheme over the state-of-the-art MDDT for intra frame and inter frame coding, respectively. Two conference papers (Section 9, Papers #1 and #2) based on the research findings were published. 3. A novel content adaptive transform framework for the H.264/AVC-based video coding has been developed. The proposed method adapts to the video content by rearranging the pixels dynamically to adjust the transform kernels, and uses rate-distortion optimization scheme to choose the best candidate kernels. In addition, the transform coefficients are reordered according to a spiral-scanning method for better entropy coding. Experimental results on the H.264/AVC Key Technical Area (KTA) platform showed that the proposed method can achieve an average of 0.35 dB gain in PSNR, and an average bitrate reduction of about 7.95% and 7.0% in all-intra and low-delay configurations, respectively. One journal paper (Section 8, Paper #2) and one conference paper (Section 9, Papers #3 and #4) based on the research findings were published.

416010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416010.value: One potential area for development is formal subjective evaluation of the reconstructed video, which will be necessary for performance evaluation of future video coding standards (i.e., H.265 and beyond) which cater for ultra-definition videos. This calls for the establishment of a subjective viewing laboratory conforming to the CCIR recommendation 500-3, which specifies the standard visual environment for conducting picture quality assessment. With the facility, studies can be conducted on the factors affecting the subjective visual quality of videos. It could also be used to test and compare the subjective quality of video displays.

416010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416010.value: Digital media is ubiquitous in our everyday life. Video as an integral part of the digital media plays a crucial role in enhancing the viewing experience in entertainment and communications. Due to the limitation of physical infrastructure, the amount of video data that can be conveyed (or transmitted) is constrained by the capacity of the medium. Video coding (or compression) is used widely to deliver the video data at an acceptable quality, and there are various video coding standards to cater for different applications. Invariably, standard video encoder employs transform coding of fixed bases without regard to the nature of video data to be coded, be it video with nature scene, man-made objects (such as buildings, roads, etc.) or animation. The project investigates a new class of transform with directional properties to exploit the characteristics inherent in the video. The directional transform is adapted to the video content and chooses the best transform kernels using the rate-distortion optimization criterion. It then reorders the transform coefficients to be coded according to a spiral-scanning method for more efficient entropy coding. Experimental results demonstrate that it outperforms the popular H.264/AVC video coding standard.

416110.label: Project Objectives

416110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416110.value: The time-to-digital converter (TDC), a device for time interval measurement, is widely used in laser ranging, nuclear physics, Positron Emission Tomography medical imaging, space science, and test instrumentation. Recently, TDC attracts increased attention for use in phase-locked loops (PLLs), where it replaces the phase-frequency detector and allows the replacement of bulky analog loop filters with digital ones. The resulted PLLs become digitally intensive or all digital, and hence amenable to the scaling of CMOS technologies. A fine time resolution is critical to TDCs in most applications. There are techniques to push the TDC resolution to better than the minimum gate delay that a CMOS technology can offer. However, existing sub-gate-delay TDC techniques inevitably bring problems like excessive power consumption, small dynamic range and large distortion. In this project, we propose to develop a novel type of TDC called “multi-stage sub-ranging TDC”, which has great potential to achieve sub-gate-delay resolution while maintaining wide dynamic range, low distortion level and high power efficiency. We plan to realize the multi-stage sub-ranging TDC in an advanced CMOS process to verify the idea. While applicable to all TDC applications, the first multi-stage sub-ranging TDC prototype will aim for use in high-speed all-digital PLLs. 時間-數字轉換器（TDC）是一種精細時間間隔測量裝置，它廣泛應用於激光測距、核物理、正電子發射斷層掃描醫療成像、空間科學和測試儀器。最近，TDC於數字鎖相環（PLL）的應用更獲關注。它取代了傳統相位頻率檢測器，使得PLL的模擬濾波器可被更簡單有效的數字濾波器所替代。整個鎖相環因此變成數字密集型或全部數字化，更適合不斷更新的CMOS工藝。 精細的時間精度於TDC在大多數應用中是至關重要的。現有技術能夠把TDC的時間精度做到小於閘延遲。但是，這些技術不可避免地帶來以下種種問題：能耗過大、小動態範圍和大失真。本提案提出開發一種新的TDC，稱為“多級分域TDC＂。這種TDC能實現小於閘延遲的時間精度，同時保持寬動態範圍、低失真和低能耗。我們計劃在先進的CMOS工藝上實現電路以驗證這一構想。雖然多級分域TDC適用於所有的TDC應用，我們將將應用鎖定於高速全數字鎖相環。

416110.label: Realisation of objectives
416110.value: The project objectives have been fully realized. First, a multi-stage sub-ranging TDC with sub-gate-delay resolution, wide dynamic range and low power consumption has been developed in a 0.13-μm CMOS process. The time resolution (the size of LSB, least significant bit) it achieved is 5ps, well below the intrinsic gate delay of the CMOS technology. Furthermore, the TDC achieves a measured differential nonlinearity of 0.6 LSB and single-shot precision of 0.4 LSB, a dynamic range of 6 bits while consuming only 1.15 mW from 1.2 V at a conversion rate of 20 Msps. Second, the above TDC is based on our proposed architecture named “Vernier sub-ranging TDC”. Unlike existing sub-gate-delay TDC techniques, the developed TDC do not bring problems like excessive power consumption, small dynamic range, or large distortion. In our TDC architecture, the time input is converted to a digital code in a coarse-fine manner by two stages of parallel delay lines. Both stages have coarse (but slightly different) time resolutions. The effective fine resolution of the second stage is achieved by making it work with the first stage in a Vernier manner. To alleviate the linearity problem caused by random variations of the delays of the delay elements, a differential nonlinearity calibration technique has also been developed. Third, another new TDC with sub-gate delay resolution has been developed. It is a parallel delay-line TDC based on the Vernier principle. A 2-bit TDC fabricated in a 0.18-μm CMOS technology demonstrates a fine time resolution of 2.5ps, again, lower than the intrinsic gate delay. The time resolutions of these TDCs correspond to light travel distances (in vacuum) of less than 1.5mm. They can be applied as a critical functional block in laser ranging systems to make finer measurement over wider ranges and at lower power consumption. They can also be used for next generation PET medical imaging application, improving the resolution of the medical images. They can be used in phase-lock-loops (PLLs) to enable all digital implementation PLLs amenable to the CMOS technology scaling. In general, they can be applied in any time interval measurement systems requiring fine resolutions.

416110.label: Major findings and research outcome
416110.value: First, a novel TDC architecture named Vernier sub-ranging TDC has been developed. Unlike existing sub-gate-delay TDC techniques, the developed TDC do not bring problems like excessive power consumption, small dynamic range, or large distortion. In the new TDC, the conversion is divided into two stages in the same coarse-fine manner. The two stages have only slightly-different unit step sizes, which are allowed to be large. The delay elements in the first stage are reused in companion with those of the second stage to generate fine time scales in the Vernier manner. The overall resolution of TDC turns out to be the difference of the two stages’ unit step sizes. As in other TDCs, a problem of the TDC is the random deviations of the delays, which leads to deviation of time step sizes of the TDC and results in non-linearity. To alleviate the problem, a digital differential nonlinearity calibration algorithm has been developed. Furthermore, a new behavioural model has been developed in MATLAB Simulink for the TDC as a quick way for system-level verification and optimization and for deriving performance specification of each circuit block. The above new techniques have been verified by a prototyping TDC fabricated in a 0.13-μm CMOS technology. In laboratory, the TDC demonstrates a fine resolution of 5ps, which is below the intrinsic gate delay, and a small differential nonlinearity. The results of this work have been submitted for publication (Part C 8.2). Second, a new parallel delay-line TDC architecture based on the Vernier principle has been developed. Two parallel delay-line stages with a slightly different incremental step sizes are cascaded, resulting in a finer resolution compared to the traditional parallel delay line. A 2-bit TDC fabricated in a 0.18-μm CMOS technology demonstrates a fine time resolution of 2.5ps, again, lower than the gate delay (Part C 8.1). Third, the concept of TDC has been applied in a novel resistor-based temperature sensor. Fabricated in a 90nm CMOS, the sensor measures an inaccuracy of −0.6°C/0.8°C over −40°C~125°C range and a peak supply sensitivity of 4°C/V after two-point calibration at 25°C and 45°C. It dissipates 11.8μW at a sampling rate of 5kS/s from a 0.9V supply (Part C 9.1). Last, a new design methodology for self-calibrated successive-approximation analog-digital converters has been proposed (Part C 8.3).

416110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416110.value: The project goals have been accomplished. The following further developments of the research are suggested. 1. To port the TDC design in CMOS technologies with finer channel lengths. With better device matching in more advanced CMOS technologies, it is expected that the resolution of the Venier sub-ranging TDC can be further improved, e.g., finer than 1ps. 2. To integrate the TDC in a larger system for the intended applications like all-digital phase-locked loop, PET medical imaging, or laser range finders. It is proposed to search for interested industry partners to apply the techniques in the real world.

416110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416110.value: In this project, novel time-to-digital converter (TDCs) have been developed, which features fine time resolutions, wide dynamic range and low power consumption. Based on our proposed architecture named Vernier sub-ranging TDC, they push the time resolution of TDC below the intrinsic gate delay of the CMOS technology. Unlike existing sub-gate-delay TDC techniques, the developed TDCs do not bring problems like excessive power consumption, small dynamic range, or large distortion. Two prototyping TDCs have been realized in advanced CMOS technologies, achieving time resolutions of 5 ps and 2.5 ps respectively. The time resolutions correspond to light travel distances (in vacuum) less than 1.5mm. The developed TDCs can be applied as a critical functional block in laser ranging systems to make finer measurement over wider ranges and at lower power consumption. They can also be used for next generation PET medical imaging application, improving the resolution of the medical images, thus helping the physician to diagnose. They can apply in phase-lock-loops (PLLs) to enable all digital implementation PLLs amenable to the CMOS technology scaling. In general, they can be applied in any time interval measurement systems for finer resolutions.

416510.label: Project Objectives
416510.value: Develop a general framework and system for face photo clustering using statistical context information. 416510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416510.value: In recent years, extensive work has been done on face clustering. However, despite the success achieved in well controlled conditions, it is widely acknowledged that even the latest systems have difficulties in processing faces in real world photos due to the large variations of lighting conditions, expressions, poses, and occlusions. In this project, to improve face clustering performance in personal photo album, we focus on three key issues: effective utilization of statistical context information; efficient data clustering algorithm; low quality photo filtering. For the first issue, even though there exist a number of works for general object and face detection using context, we find few works on using statistical context information for face photo clustering. In this project, we propose a framework for face clustering using statistical context. By congregating statistical context information over the whole data set, we can significantly improve the overall performance of face clustering. For the second issue we propose a fast data clustering algorithm. The data clustering algorithms used in most existing systems are mainly based on variations of spectral clustering algorithms. The computational complexity has become a bottleneck for the scalability of the whole system. In this project, we propose a much faster algorithm, with O(n^2) complexity compared to O(n^3) of the spectral clustering, without sacrificing the clustering accuracy. Finally, we propose a novel low quality photo filtering approach by extracting high level photo quality features based on modeling of human artist perception. We use the photo quality filtering algorithm to remove low quality photos before the photo clustering step. It will not only help to reduce data noise for the clustering algorithm, but also help users to search and select better photos from their photo collection. We plan to apply the system on both offline personal photo album and online personal photo sites. 近年来，人脸聚类一直是一个重要的研究课题。但是，大部分研究只能在实验室控制条件下取得成功，目前即使是最先进的系统也会在处理光照、表情、旋转、遮挡等时遇到困难。在本项目中，为提高个人照片集中人脸聚类的结果，我们将集中研究三个关键问题：有效地使用统计上下文信息，高效的数据聚类算法，低质量照片的过滤。 关于第一个问题，虽然存在不少关于使用上下文信息进行一般物体和人脸检测的研究，我们发现很少有研究使用统计上下文信息进行人脸照片聚类。在本项目中，我们将提出一个使用统计上下文的人脸聚类框架。通过集成全部数据库中的统计上下文信息，我们可以大大提高人脸聚类的整体表现。对于第二个问题，我们提出一个快速的数据聚类算法。现在大多数系统中使用的聚类算法主要以谱聚类算法的变形为主。计算的复杂性成为整个系统扩展的瓶颈。在本系统中，我们将提出一个更快的O(n^2)复杂度的算法，而不是谱聚类中的O(n^3)复杂度，同时不牺牲聚类的质量。最后，我们将在对人的感知进行建模的基础上抽取照片质量特征，并以此提出一个新的低质量照片过滤方法。我们使用照片质量过滤算法在照片聚类以前对低质量图像进行过滤。这将不仅可以消除聚类算法中的数据噪声，同时还可以帮助用户寻找和选择相片集中的高质量照片。我们计划将系统应用于离线个人照片集和在线照片网站。

416510.label: Major findings and research outcome
416510.value: In this project, we developed a simple but powerful graph-based agglomerative clustering algorithm. We explore the important yet different roles of two fundamental concepts in graph theory, indegree and outdegree, in the context of clustering. Our clustering algorithm can handle high-dimensional data, and is robust to noise and outliers. It has three main advantages: good performance, easy implementation, and high computational efficiency. We also developed a content-based photo quality assessment using regional and global features. Under this framework, subject areas, which draw the most attentions of human eyes, are first extracted. Then regional features extracted from subject areas and the background regions are combined with global features to assess the photo quality. Since professional photographers may adopt different photographic techniques and may have different aesthetic criteria in mind when taking different types of photos (e.g. landscape versus portrait), we propose to segment regions and extract visual features in different ways according to the categorization of photo content. Therefore we divide the photos into seven categories based on their content and develop a set of new subject area extraction methods and new visual features, which are specially designed for different categories. To apply our work to online photos, we also developed a novel online photo search system. It only requires the user to click on one query photo with the minimum effort and photos from a pool retrieved by text-based search are re-ranked based on both visual and textual content. Our key contribution is to capture the users’ search intention from this one-click query photo. Experimental evaluation shows that our approach significantly improves the precision of top ranked images and also the user experience. Finally, to recognize and cluster face photos more accurately, we proposed a new learning based face representation: the face identity-preserving (FIP) features. Unlike conventional face descriptors, the FIP features can significantly reduce intra-identity variances, while maintaining discriminativeness between identities. In order to learn the FIP features, we carefully design a deep network that combines the feature extraction layers and the reconstruction layer. Extensive experiments on the large MultiPIE face database demonstrate that it significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art face recognition methods. We also proposes a hybrid convolutional network (ConvNet)-Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) model for face verification in wild conditions. A key contribution of this work is to directly learn relational visual features, which indicate identity similarities, from raw pixels of face pairs with a hybrid deep network.

416510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416510.value: We plan to continue the research work on face recognition. Especially, we plan to focus more on deep learning based face recognition study. Based on some of the research findings in this project, we have recently submitted a new RGC grant application focusing on deep learning for face recognition.

416510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416510.value: The clustering algorithm, face recognition method, and photo quality filtering approach developed in this project all have values in real world applications. The clustering algorithm is fundamental to big data processing. The algorithm is very simple and robust thus can be easily applied in real machine learning systems. The deep learning based face recognition algorithm is able to accurately recognition face photos under uncontrolled environment from the internet. Besides application in online and offline photo management system, it can also be used in a wide range of other applications including security and surveillance. The photo quality filtering approach can not only help photo clustering but also help to improve photo search quality of online image search engine.

416610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416610.value: A spatial database manages geometric objects such as points (representing hotels, restaurants, etc.), rectangles (parks, precincts, etc.), and so on. In practice, a spatial entity often comes with a text description: for example, the list of services and amenities of a hotel, the menu of a restaurant, the out-patient specialties of a hospital, and so on. In many applications, users need to search with both spatial and textual predicates. The following are some examples. Query 1: find the hospital that is nearest to my home among all hospitals that offer acupunctural out-patient service. Query 2: find all pairs of hotels and restaurants such that (i) they are within 1 mile from each other, (ii) the hotel has wireless connection, a spa pool, and a gym room, and (iii) the restaurant serves tenderloin and Beaujolais Nouveau red wine. Query 3: similar to the previous query, but find the closest pair of hotel and restaurant (as opposed to all pairs in 1 mile). The results of all these queries must satisfy certain spatial predicates, and must contain certain keywords in their descriptions. Associating objects with texts is a highly flexible approach to capture objects' information, especially when it is difficult to "normalize" such information in a universal relational schema. Thus, the ability of searching the objects by their texts is essential. Keyword search has been extensively studied in document retrieval, web search, and in recent years, relational databases. However, spatial data have many unique features that are drastically different from plain documents, web pages, and relational data. As a result, most of the existing techniques are either inapplicable or inefficient when adapted to spatial databases. Spatial keyword search is gaining attention from the database community only recently. A large variety of problems remain open. This project aims to carry out systematic investigation in this exciting area. Topics expected to be covered include the whole line from query specification to building the end-system. 空間數據庫管理幾何對象，例如，點（即賓館，飯店等），長方形（公園，專用區等），等等。在實踐中，空間實體往往帶有文字說明：例如，酒店的服務和設施清單，餐館的菜單，醫院的門診專科等。在許多應用中，用戶往往需要結合空間和文字來進行檢索。以下是一些例子。查詢 1：找離我家最近提供針灸服務的醫院； 2：找出滿足以下條件的旅館和餐館組合：（一）它們互相在1英里內，（二）該酒店提供無線上網，溫泉按摩池，和健身房，（三）該餐館提供脊肉和薄酒萊新紅酒； 3：與前一查詢類似，但在所有滿足條件的旅館和餐館組合中找最近的一對（而不是對1英里內的）。這些查詢的結果必須既滿足一定的空間條件，又包含某些關鍵字的描述。 為實體添加文本描述是一個高度靈活的辦法來捕獲實體信息，尤其是當實體是很難用一個公用的關係模式來加以“規範”的。因此，有能力通過文本來搜索實體是非常必要的。關鍵字搜索已被廣泛應用于文獻檢索，網絡搜索，和關係數據庫。然而，空間數據許多獨特的性質是截然不同與文本文件，網頁，和關係數據的。其結果是，大多數現有的技術要么不適用與空間數據庫或是完全無效的。空間關鍵詞搜索在數據庫領域中最近才開始受到關注。大量的問題仍然沒有得到很好的解決。本項目將在此領域中進行系統的研究，旨在設計出整套用于空間關鍵詞搜索的終端系統。

416610.label: Realisation of objectives
416610.value: This project's scientific findings have been documented in 6 journal papers (4 in TKDE and 2 in TODS) and 15 conference papers (5 in SIGMOD, 2 in VLDB, 6 in PODS, 1 in SODA, and 1 in SoCG), which are listed in Part C of this report. All the journals and conferences where our work was published are top-tier journals or conferences in databases and/or theoretical computer science. Next, we discuss how the objectives (as stated in our original proposal) have been realized by referring to those papers. Regarding Objective 1, our results have appeared in the TKDE'14 paper entitled "Fast Nearest Neighbor Search with Keywords", which proposed new index structures that can answer keyword-augmented nearest neighbor queries with theoretical guarantees. Regarding Objective 2, our findings have appeared in the other TKDE'14 paper entitled "Range Aggregation with Set Selection", which developed new access methods to answer queries that aim to inquire arbitrary sub-spaces of the data space with theoretical guarantees. Realization of Objective 3 is best illustrated by our SIGMOD'11 paper entitled "Nearest Keyword Search in XML Documents'', where we introduced a new operator called "nearest keyword search", and showcased how this operator can be leveraged to answer a good variety of queries with theoretical guarantees. See also the other SIGMOD'11 paper entitled "On k-Skip Shortest Paths", and the VLDB'12 paper entitled "Optimal Algorithms for Crawling a Hidden Database in the Web". The accomplishment of Objective 4 is perhaps the most mention-able outcome of this project -- our investigation on the theory of keyword search has produced a long string of theory papers: see the PODS, SODA, SoCG, and TODS papers. Most of the theoretical bounds in those papers are still the best even to this day, and pave a solid foundation for further research down these lines. Finally, towards Objective 5, we have implemented all the techniques proposed in our system-oriented papers (the SIGMOD, VLDB, and TKDE papers), and thoroughly tested their effectiveness and efficiency with extensive experimentation. In summary, all the 5 objectives stated in our proposal have been fully achieved. Also worth mentioning is the fact that this project, in addition to its scientific and empirical contributions, has also trained two PhD students. Both students have built up excellent track records. One of them has graduated and is currently working for Google Switzerland (with a lucrative paycheck). The other student is to graduate in 2015 summer.

416610.label: Major findings and research outcome
416610.value: As mentioned earlier, the findings of this project have been documented in (i) 6 journal papers: 2 in ACM TODS, 4 in IEEE TKDE, and (ii) 15 conference papers: 5 in SIGMOD, 2 in VLDB, 6 in PODS, 1 in SODA, and 1 in SoCG. All these are first-tier journals and conferences in databases and/or theoretical computer science. The project has laid down a solid theoretical foundation on spatial keyword search. We have developed algorithms for solving a long list of existing and new problems on this topic. Here we can only briefly mention some examples, due to the space constraint. The SIGMOD'11 paper entitled "Nearest Keyword Search in XML Documents" proposed "nearest keyword search" as a new operator on XML databases. We showed that this operator can be utilized to perform two important tasks on XML data with excellent quality and efficiency guarantees: evaluating XPath expressions and finding approximate group steiner trees. The TKDE'14 paper entitled "Range Aggregation with Set Selection" studied a natural integration of conventional range aggregation and keyword search. It develops a data structure to answer such queries with strong performance guarantees, and proves lower bounds showing that the data structure has achieved the optimal query performance, on condition that the space consumption is linear. The SIGMOD'13 paper entitled "Minimal MapReduce Algorithms" devised a suite of algorithms on the MapReduce framework with good theoretical guarantees. Many of those algorithms serve as fundamental building bricks for spatial keyword search systems. The PODS'11 paper entitled "FIFO Indexes for Decomposable Problems" presented a generic framework for converting static data structures into new structures on first-in-first-out stream data, on which spatial keyword search thus has become a reality. The TKDE'14 paper entitled "Fast Nearest Neighbor Search with Keyword Search" attacks the "de factor" keyword-search version of nearest neighbor search, and gives a data structure that can answer such queries with excellent performance guarantees. In particular, the index structure incorporates new compression ideas in order to achieve a provably minimal amount of space. Please see the research output for our other contributions to the theory and practice of spatial keyword search. This project has produced prototype systems that can be deployed to answer a large variety of spatial keyword search queries. Our source code has been tested by extensive experiments that were designed to scrutinize our algorithms' behavior in numerous tough situations. Our code is both efficient and reliable.

416610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416610.value: Spatial keyword search is an exciting topic. We are very happy to, through this project, have worked in and contributed to this area. In the past few years, this area has expanded vastly, judging from the large number of relevant papers in important venues. These papers have, remarkably, demonstrated plenty of opportunities for further research. Here, we briefly mention two directions. First, it is very interesting to explore new types of queries, in response to the ever-growing information needs of the general public. Indeed, many of the papers published in these years belong to this category. In retrospect, it is fairly surprising to see the astonishingly rich variety of queries that have been proposed in those papers. Second, many problems on spatial keyword search are difficult from a theoretical point of view. Currently, the existing state of the art on those problems suffers from either the inability to produce good results, or the expensive running time required to find good results. Improving the state of the art poses great challenges to computer scientists.

416610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416610.value: Spatial keyword search is a powerful extension of a conventional search engine such as Google. Currently, a search engine is good at "keyword search" (namely without the spatial part) -- or phrased differently, queries based on pure texts. With spatial keyword search, on the other hand, a user is able to input not only texts but also additional geographic constraints. For example, while traditional keyword search allows you to issue a query like "Restaurants with Spaghetti and Red Wine", spatial keyword search allows you to issue more powerful queries like "Find all the restaurants within 1 kilometer from my current location whose menus have Spaghetti and Red Wine. Note that in the latter query, the text part is "Spaghetti and Red Wine", while the spatial part is "within 1 kilometer from my current location". Prior to this project, people already knew how to process the text and spatial parts separately, while doing so by integrating the two parts could only be done in an inefficient manner. Remedying the situation is exactly the primary contribution of this project, which has developed a suite of techniques for answering such queries, as well as many other more sophisticated ones, in real time.

416710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416710.value: In recent years, advanced optical modulation formats such as differential quadrature phase shift keying (DQPSK) have attracted considerable attention for high speed communications systems because of their increased tolerance to dispersion, resilience to optical nonlinearities, increased spectral efficiency and 3dB improvement in receiver sensitivity compared with conventional on-off keying (OOK). These advantages may lead to more cost effective, faster and spectrally more efficient optical communications. However practical deployment of these advanced modulation formats in optical communication systems has been hindered by the extra complexity in controlling the optical polarization and phase in the delayed interference interferometer needed in the conventional optical receivers which demodulate the phase encoded optical signals. In this project we propose to investigate whether novel nanophotonic functional elements may be suitable for integrated optical receivers to provide a practical low-cost alternative to the conventional delayed interferometer based receivers. In this project we will design, fabricate and test innovative new nanoscale functional elements that may be used in integrated optical receivers for decoding optical Differential Phase Shift Keying (DPSK) and DQPSK modulated signals. The proposed nanophotonic functional elements to be investigated include highly compact chirped waveguide gratings for coupling light to the sub-micron sized optical waveguides, polarization diversity frequency discriminators and optical delay interferometers, and balanced ion-implanted silicon waveguide photodetectors. The focus of the project will be in exploring the performance offered by various novel functional element designs and the fabrication and testing of the individual functional elements on a silicon platform. Integrated delayed-interference decoders and micro-resonator based frequency discriminator filters will be studied to assess whether their loss, polarization dependence, optical bandwidth and temperature dependence, are suitable for practical use in high speed optical communication networks. One outcome of the project will be in creating novel silicon nanophotonics which provide lower coupling loss, better polarization performance and with sufficiently robust stability as to allow their use in practical communication systems. The proposed work may in the long term lead to the practical deployment of optical phase-modulated communication systems which offer higher bandwidth/longer reach transmission at lower cost than present day systems. 近年來，先進的光學調製格式，比如差分正交相移鍵控（DQPSK）， 受到了廣泛的關注，因為如果它們應用於通信系統，可以增加對色散和非線性效應的耐受性，提高頻譜效率和改善接收的靈敏度(相較與傳統的通斷鍵控（OOK）)。這些優勢可實現更低成本，更快速，更高效的光通訊系統。但這些先進的調製格式的實際應用，受阻於傳統的延遲干涉儀光信號接收器對光的偏振及相位延遲的高精度控制的要求。在這個項目中，我們將利用新型納米光學的功能元素，研製集成光接收器以提供了一個切實可行的低成本器件，來替代傳統的延遲干涉儀接收器。我們將設計，製造和測試新的納米級功能元素，應用於光差分相移鍵控（DPSK）和DQPSK調製信號的集成接收器。其中包括高度集成的啁啾光柵波導耦合器，亞微米光波導，鑑頻器，集成光延遲干涉儀和離子注入矽波導探測器。該項目的重點是在矽芯片上製成的各種新的功能元件的設計，製造和測試，以及探索它們的表現。集成光延遲干涉儀解碼器和微諧振器鑑頻器都將在研究的範圍內，以評估它們的各項性能是適合實際應用在高速光通信網絡。該項目的成果將包括研發新型矽納米光子器件，提供較低的耦合損耗，更好的偏振性能和足夠的穩定性。這些研究工作將促成各種新型光相位調製的通信系統在未來的實際應用，從而實現比現今的通信系統更高的帶寬以及較低的成本。

416710.label: Realisation of objectives
416710.value: The four project objectives were all addressed. The theoretical design and analysis of subwavelength quasi-period nanostructures (objective 1) was carried out and enabled efficient wideband and polarization independent coupling between fiber and the silicon waveguides. The polarization independent grating coupler is a novel idea which was introduced in this project as an alternative to the already established polarization diversity approach to address the polarization dependence of the waveguide coupling without the need to use polarization splitters, and the related paper (Chen and Tsang, Opt Lett, 2011) was the most downloaded paper online in second quarter of 2011 and now has 22 citations. We also published two papers (Eg K. Xu et al, Opt Lett 37, 4738, 2012; K. Xu, ibid, 3462, 2012)) demonstrating the use of tuneable frequency discriminators for DPSK and DQPSK demodulation respectively (objective 2). One problem we encountered in was the loss of the capability to make ion implanted photodiodes at CUHK and instead we had to rely on a foundry for the integrated photodiode fabrication. We thus had to adopt an alternative approach involving the technology of germanium on silicon phodetectors (objective 3). The detailed photonic device design and mask layouts for the fabrication of micoresonator based receivers for the DPSK and DQPSK balanced receiver were carried out. The devices were fabricated at a photonic foundry and the results were published. (K, Xu et al PTL 24 1221,, 2012). We also investigated the possibility of using the silicon waveguides in the receiver to monitor the optical signal to noise ratio (OSNR) by exploiting the two photon absorption in the waveguide. This approach could lead to additional functionality in silicon DPSK and DQPSK receivers without additional cost. The work resulted in a paper published in the IEEE Photonics Journal. We also used the tuneable DPSK receiver to demonstrate a new system architecture for next generation passive optical networks involving the use of time–wavelength-division-multiplexing and signal remodulation of a DPSK downstream signal. The tuneable receiver was used for receiving the downstream DPSK signal and the results were published in IEEE Photonics Journal (Objective 4). We also demonstrated the use of the silicon Mach Zehnder interferometers as silicon modulators and employed them for low speed multilevel modulation (and reported the results at OFC 2013).

416710.label: Major findings and research outcome
416710.value: The research outcomes were published in 9 IEEE or OSA journal papers and three international conference papers (CLEO, IEEE Photonics Conference and OFC). In summary they included the development of new sub-wavelength nanostructured gratings to make them polarization independent [1], optical monitoring of PSK systems using two photon absorption in silicon waveguides [2], tuneable frequency discriminators integrated with germanium waveguide photodetectors for DQPSK receivers [3], use of sub-wavelength grating structures to increase the bandwidth of grating couplers [4], variable bit-rate PSK receivers using microring resonators integrate with germanium photodetectors [5], OSNR monitoring using integrated microdisk resonators [6] and variable bit rate DPSK receiver [7], use of the integrated PSK receivers in a novel TWDM-PON system [8] and assessing the compatibility of silicon photonic integration with advanced modulation formats such as optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing modulation with quadrature phase-shift keying (QPSK), 8 phase-shift keying (8PSK) and 16-quadrature amplitude modulation(16-QAM) [9].

416710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416710.value: There is potential for further development and commercialization of integrated coherent receivers for telecommunication systems, and this may be a possible topic for future ITF projects in collaboration with industry. Talks with Huawei on possible development of integrated silicon photonics components for telecommunication systems has been scheduled to explore this possibility.

416710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416710.value: The project introduced advances in the use of nanotechnology for coupling and detecting light in advanced optical communication systems. The integration of low cost advanced optical receivers on a silicon platform can potentially enable new architectures for optical fiber to the home communication networks systems which offer more than 40 times the bandwidth than is available with present day networks.

417110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417110.value: The aim of this project is to develop a new intelligent visual surveillance system which will work reliably in large crowded scenes using a distributed network of cameras. Effective and efficient visual surveillance has become one area greatly in need of active research due to escalating demands on security requirements, anti-terrorism measures and traffic control. Hong Kong has tens of thousands of surveillance cameras collecting a huge amount of video data every moment. Existing technology works well when scenes are sparse and the areas being monitored are small. However, they are not reliable for large and crowded scenes of security interest, such as airports and train stations. We now propose to carry out research that will enable us to develop intelligent visual surveillance systems which automatically track and recognize objects of interest, understand activities of objects, and detect abnormalities from extensive video data collected in large crowded scenes. To improve reliability and robustness, low-level tracking and object matching are jointly solved with high-level activity analysis under hierarchical Bayesian models in this research. It is intended that this visual surveillance system will self-adapt to a variety of scenes with minimal human intervention. The requirements for the next generation of video surveillance systems are robustness, reliability, scalability and self-adaptability for crowded, large and complex scenes. There is an urgent need to develop visual surveillance systems which can efficiently extract useful information from fast accumulated data and can self-adapt to different scenes with minimal human intervention. This research will be an important step to fill this gap. 本項目的目標是研究開發一個新的基於分佈式攝像頭網絡的智能視頻監控系統。該系統可以在大範圍的擁擠的場景中可靠地工作。 安全、反恐和交通控制等諸多領域對高性能智能視頻監控系統需求的快速增長，使其成為研究的熱點。香港擁有數以十萬計的監控攝像頭，每時每刻採集大量的視頻數據。現有技術在小範圍稀疏場景下可以良好工作。但是它們在例如機場和火車站這樣大範圍擁擠的場景下工作時可靠性低。 本研究項目研究開發的智能視頻監控系統，通過處理海量視頻數據，可以在大範圍擁擠場景中自動跟踪和識別感興趣的物體，分析物體的活動，以及檢測異常行為。為了提高系統的可靠性和魯棒性，本研究利用分層式貝葉斯模型聯合解決底層目標跟踪和高層目標活動分析兩個密切相關的問題。這個視頻監控系統可以在最少的人工干預下，自動適應各種不同的場景。 下一代智能視頻監控系統對大範圍擁擠複雜場景中的魯棒性，可靠性，可擴展性，和自適應性都提出了很高的要求。迫切需要開發可以從快速積累的視頻數據中高效提取有用信息以及可以在最少的人工干預下自適應不同場景的視頻監控系統。本研究將為填補這一空白邁出重要一步。

417110.label: Realisation of objectives
417110.value: All the objectives in this project have been realized successfully. In this project, we first developed an unsupervised hierarchical Bayesian model, which could automatically learn the transition probabilities across different camera views and the distributions of transition time across camera views. By being integrated with appearance based object matching, such model was used as prior to connect highly fragmented trajectories due to heavy occlusions in crowd and trajectories observed in different camera views. In this way, complete trajectories across multiple camera views on a distributed camera network were obtained from crowded scenes. Such complete trajectories were used to model multi-camera activities. Therefore, multi-camera object tracking and multi-camera activity recognition were jointly solved under a single hierarchical Bayesian model. When the scene is extremely crowded, even short tracking is infeasible. We proposed a hierarchical Bayesian approach to learn the activity models across camera views from the temporal co-occurrence of moving pixels without tracking them. If two clusters of moving pixels in different camera views belong to the same activity category, they should satisfy spatial consistency in the overlapping region of the two camera views. Therefore, both spatial consistence and temporal co-occurrence were used as regularization when learning the activity models. The activity models learned above were used to effectively improve detecting and tracking pedestrians and vehicles in crowded scenes across camera views. With the assistance of the prior on the path models of pedestrians and vehicles, we automatically adapted a generic pedestrian/vehicle detector to a specific scene, and the detection accuracy in target scenes was dramatically improved by 40%. The coherent motion patterns were used to predict the behaviors of objects and continuously tracking them even though they were completed occluded by other interaction objects. A large number of objects were automatically divided into groups with different coherent motion patterns. We assumed that the movement of an object is constrained by its neighboring objects in the same group. All the proposed methods and models were evaluated a large scale database created by us. The new database has more than 100G video sequences from 260 camera views, with annotated ground truth on activity recognition, object detection and tracking. Experimental results show that our new approaches significantly outperform state-of-the-art on multi-camera activity recognition, object detection and cross-camera-view tracking.
