417110.label: Major findings and research outcome
417110.value: Six journal papers and 24 conference papers were published, and two journal papers are under review. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (PAMI), and International Journal of Computer Vision (IJCV) are the two best journals on computer vision and machine learning. We published three papers at PAMI and IJCV. 24 papers were published on the top three conferences on computer vision (CVPR, ICCV, and ECCV). Two awards were received. We found that behavior analysis and tracking in crowd scenes can be well unified under a hierarchical Bayesian model and jointly solved. In crowded scenes, only very short trajectories are available due to occlusions. It is important to add spatial-temporal priors to Bayesian models to learn long-range activity models from highly fragmented trajectories. Along this direction, several papers (Part C.8 No. 1, 4-5; Part C.9 No. 1, 11-13, 23-24) were published. For example, a random field topic model for learning activities was proposed in Part C.9 No. 1. A dynamic agent-based was used to learn the behaviors of pedestrians (Part C.8 5, Part C.9 24). The learned activity models can be used to adapt generic pedestrian/vehicle detectors to target scenes without labeling training samples and dramatically improve detection accuracy (Part C.8 No. 2, Part C.9 No. 2, 4). The motion patterns learned by activity models were used to improve tracking object through occlusions (Part C.8 4-5, 7, Part C.9 1, 5, 13, 23-24). To track object across camera views, effective approaches were proposed to match objects by integrating the information of appearance, spatial and temporal transition (Part C.8 1, Part C.9 8, 9, 16, 20-21, 22). To improve the tracking performance in crowded scenes, robust object detectors were also developed (Part C.8 No. 3, 8, Part C.9 No. 3, 6, 7, 10, 14-15, 18-19 ). The new detectors were robust to occlusions and suitable to crowded scenes. Four datasets were built for evaluation. A traffic scene dataset was used to evaluate recognition of pedestrian and vehicle behaviors in complex environments. A train station scene dataset was used to evaluate the recognition of pedestrian behaviors and tracking in crowd. At the Chinese University of Hong Kong, a distribute camera network was built and a dataset was collected to evaluate multi-camera tracking. 40G videos from 240 camera views were collected from Shanghai World Expo 2010 to evaluate tracking and activity recognition. Our approaches outperformed state-of-the-art on all these datasets.

417110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
417110.value: In the future work, we will extend the methods and models develop from this project to study crowd behaviors and the general underlying principles of various crowd systems. In this project, we detect and track individuals in crowds and analyze individual behaviors. Differently, in the future work we will treat the whole crowd as a unit, track it as a whole, and study its overall statistics instead of focusing on individuals. This requires us developing new models and methodologies. All the activity models developed from this project are scene-specific, i.e. models learned from data of a specific scene can only be used to recognize activities from the same scene. However, scientific studies show that different crowd systems existing in nature, such as fish school, bacteria colony and human crowds, share similar understanding principles. It means that some general properties can be extracted and used to compared different crowd systems. It motivates us to study and quantify such properties from computer vision point of view, and develop some generic descriptors to recognize crowd activities across different scenes. This would be an important extension of the current project. It not only has use practical applications, but also has important scientific values.

417110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
417110.value: In large cities with high population density, public areas often accumulate large numbers of pedestrians, and therefore crowd video surveillance is very important for public safety. However, this is very challenging, because it is very difficult to detect and track objects with heavy occlusions in crowds, and existing activity recognition techniques are based on complete trajectories of objects. More over, there are often hundreds or even thousands of objects in crowded scenes, which makes activity modeling extremely complex. In order to minor the activities of objects in a large area, a large distributed camera network is needed. In most applications, the topological and geometrical relationships of cameras are unknown, and they are important for tracking objects across camera views. As the research outcome of this project, it successfully solves these challenges by proposing novel hierarchical Bayesian models. Under these models, activity recognition and object tracking in crowds are jointly optimized since they have close connections. The topological structure of the camera network is also inferred. It significantly advances the state-of-the-art on crowd behavior analysis, tracking and multi-camera analysis. It also has large impact on the applications of crowd video surveillance.

417910.label: Project Title(Chinese)
417910.value: 分子摻雜石墨烯的研究

417910.label: Project Objectives
417910.value: To construct a controllable doping process for graphene materials using doping species that conform specific charge transfer and charge carrier transport characteristics. We plan to microscopically and macroscopically investigate different graphene materials and dopants, by means of conventional electrical, compositional, structural, and spectroscopic measurements, as well as nanoscopic characterization using scanning probe microscopy. This will unveil optimal electronic attributes that can potentially yield superior device performance. To explore novel n-type doping species and the gated tunable band-gap for novel graphene/dopant materials, e.g., PTCDI, TTF, PTCDA, etc., and the associated transport properties, to improve the understanding of the doping mechanism for manipulating the gated band-gap in graphene. To conduct theoretical investigation of charge transfer and electronic state distributions in doped graphene materials, so as to build a better model system for elucidating transport characteristics. We envisage that the theoretical studies based on first-principles calculations will provide crucial insights into understanding the origins of the effective doping and gated band-gap characteristics in graphene. To utilise the comprehensive understanding in the development of high performance graphene-based devices

417910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417910.value: The remarkable miniaturization of semiconductor microelectronics over the past few decades has profound impact in our daily life. If the miniaturization trend continues for the next 10 years or so, devices are expected to approach molecular dimensions. By that time, electronic devices will no longer function under the current designs, and probably require conceptually novel device structures and operation principles. In addition, new materials, such as low-dimensional materials and spintronic materials, will probably be required. Graphene is an emerging low-dimensional electronic material with unusually startling electronic properties. It consists of a single atomic layer of carbon atoms, and has far superior mobility, higher thermal conductivity, and larger current-carrying capabilities than present semiconductor materials. Moreover, its planar geometry facilitates multilayer device architecture for simpler integration with existing CMOS technology in the development of the next generation of devices. Despite the large amount of research work done on graphene, little effort has been expended on the interplay between graphene and molecular materials in the proximity of the interface. As a result, electronic properties and transport characteristics near the interface in graphene-based devices remain largely unexplored. A predicative model capable of describing the charge carrier behaviors in the devices and the inherited interfaces would be difficult to formulate without a comprehensive understanding of processes at the molecular level. In this proposed project, our aim is to develop a systematic understanding of the molecular interactions between graphene and molecular materials, and in interfacial regions, to model electronic characteristics that will aide in the design of high performance carbon-based devices. The organic-electronics theme and expected outcomes of this project are consistent with one of the major areas supported by the Innovation and Technology Commission and identified by the Hong Kong Government. The project will also provide training of R&D personnel in the lattest semiconductor technology for the development of future devices in the local electronics industry. 半導體微電子器件的微型化對人類產生了巨大的影響。如果人們保持現有的微型化趨勢，半導體微電子器件的尺寸將在十年後達到分子尺度，現有硅基微電子器件將無法勝任其責。人們必須尋找新的電子材料，例如低維材料和電子自旋材料。 石墨烯是一種新型的低維電子材料，具有很多奇特的性質。它由一層或幾層碳沿平面原子周期排列而成。其厚度只有若干原子層，但其機械強度極高，具有金屬般的導電性和導熱性。其平面型幾何結構為多層電子器件結構的設計，以及與已有CMOS半導體技術的集成創造了先決條件。 儘管人們在石墨烯的研究方面取得了很多進展，惟關於電子在石墨烯與分子材料界面附近的行為特征卻獲知甚少。本研究計劃重點研究石墨烯與分子材料在界面附近的相互作用，以及電子在界面附近的輸運特性，以期為高性能碳基電子器件的設計與發展奠定重要基礎。

417910.label: Realisation of objectives
417910.value: In this project, we have actively been engaged in understanding graphene surface and interfacial properties associated with electronic structure, carrier transport and related phenomena on a nanometer scale. We have investigated both experimentally and theoretically the mechanisms of graphene interfacial couplings to different substrates, charge injection from metal electrodes and its interplay with adsorbates. (1) Few layer graphene’s (FLG) electronic properties were effectively adjusted and controlled through functionalizing its top surface. Both n-type and p-type doped exfoliated graphene sheets were realized by virtue of adsorbing organic molecules, e.g., F-TCNQ, CuPc, etc. Additionally, the doping effects induced by electron beam (EB) irradiation and oxygen plasma were also studied. And graphene p-n junctions were constructed by EB irradiation. Ab initio calculations on bilayer graphene doping by F-TCNQ were performed. (2) The crucial roles acted by supported substrate for graphene were systematically interrogated, both for mechanically exfoliated and CVD synthesized graphene. We find that the existence of charge impurities and ripples adversely affects the mobility of graphene on commonly used SiO2/Si substrates. To reduce the electrically deleterious species on SiO2/Si substrates, we developed self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) to passivate SiO2/Si substrate surfaces. We achieved an increase in carrier mobility of the exfoliated monolayer graphene by nearly one order of magnitude (~ 47,000 cm2/Vs) at room temperature. The technique is also applicable for CVD graphene. (3) The electronic properties of the interfaces between graphene and various metal electrodes were systematically investigated. For graphene on SiO2/Si passivated with highly-ordered SAMs, we find that by utilizing voltage bias, the contact can be reversibly altered between high resistance and low resistance. We ascribe the phenomenon to graphene’s cone energy dispersion relationship as well as the vanishing density of states at the Dirac point. (4) We demonstrated that high-quality cm-sized graphene sheets can be synthesized on Cu foils by a self-assembled approach from defect-free polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in a high vacuum (HV) chamber without hydrogen. We tried various molecular motifs, e.g., coronene, pentacene, and rubrene. For coronene precursor, the graphene sheet obtained at 1000 °C, exhibited a carrier mobility up to ∼ 5300-10,000 cm2V−1s−1at room temperature. The underlying growth mechanism mainly involves surface-mediated nucleation process of dehydrogenated PAHs rather than segregation or precipitation process of small carbon species decomposed from the precursors. (5) An ultra-high sensitive photodetector based on graphene/photonic waveguide hybrid configuration has been developed from visible to infrared spectral ranges.

417910.label: Major findings and research outcome
417910.value: (1) We developed a method to modify large area SiO2/Si substrate and produced high performance graphene transistors. By utilizing highly-ordered OTMS self-assembly monolayers (SAMs) on conventional silicon wafer with thermally grown oxide dielectric, we have significantly minimized the intrinsic graphene doping level resulting from the substrate effect. The carrier mobility can reach up to 47,000 cm2/V-s, which is about 10 times higher than those fabricated on conventional SiO2/Si substrates, approaching to the intrinsic properties of suspended graphene. The transport measurements in the new platform have strikingly brought about the observation of reduction in both charged impurities and remote interfacial phonon scattering for electron transport in graphene. Also we theoretically calculated the interaction between graphene and CH3 end-group. See more in Nos. 3, 6, 8, 9, 11, & 13, Part C. (2) We developed a new synthesis technique for high-quality large-area graphene on catalytic Cu foils from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) under high vacuum without hydrogen. An invited review was published. Very recently the technique was further developed by a research group to realize doped graphene with various PAHs as precursors (see more at DOI. 10.1021/nn505913v). More of our relevant findings can be found in Nos. 7, 9, 10, 11, & 17, Part C. (3) We systematically investigated doping effects with various molecular species. Charge transfer processes were experimentally observed. However, the controllability of doping concentration is still a pending issue. More studies are needed for doped graphene on SAMs, in order to minimize the substrate effect. See more in Nos. 1, 2, 5, 6, 13, 15, & 19, Part C. (3) We developed graphene-based memory devices on SAM modified SiO2/Si substrate with cycling number over 1000. An invited review was reported. See more in Nos. 4, & 16, Part C. (4) We meticulously interrogated light beam interaction with graphene as well as hybrid structures, namely graphene/photonic waveguides, graphene/Au nanoparticles, graphene/silicon. Ultrahigh sensitive photodetectors were accomplished in both visible and infrared spectral ranges. Our discovery provides a new technical platform for graphene-silicon photonics, nonlinear graphene optics, as well as graphene-based optical signal processing. One published paper in Nature Photonics was highlighted by Nature (Vol. 501, p.284, 19 Sept. 2013) and Nature Photonics (DOI:10.1038/nphoton.2013.257), which was reported by over 50 news outlets. See more in Nos. 10, 18, & 20, Part C.

417910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
417910.value: Our findings consistently show` that the interaction between graphene's pristine lattice with disordered surroundings plays an important role in realizing its unique properties. And the decoupling itself from SiO2 substrate is crucial to improve the mobility of graphene in electronic and optoelectronic applications. In addition, the facile modification process to place large-area SAMs on conventional SiO2/Si wafer and preserve the high quality optical contrast makes it a promising method for flexible and large-scale electronic devices. (1) OTMS-SAM/SiO2 and ODPA-SAM/Al2O3 are useful active-interface platforms for other newly discovered TMD 2-dimensional layered electronic/optoelectronic materials. (2) These key techniques involved in graphene synthesis, transfer and interface can be further applied to other 2D layered materials for achieving novel electronic and photoelectric devices. Hopefully our findings can be the catalyst for other breakthroughs in 2D layered materials.

417910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
417910.value: We have had advances towards the much improved understanding of the electronic properties at the interfaces of graphene transistors and graphene-based photodetectors via a variety of interface engineering techniques, at either the electrically active or the photonically active interfaces of electron device. We have achieved a comprehensive understanding of the photonic properties at the graphene/photonic waveguide interface and developed two novel platforms to achieve the best graphene-based photodetectors at room temperature. The developed platform paves the way for devising high performance optoelectronic devices based on 2D layered electronic/optoelectronic materials, which is one of the most burgeoning research topics globally at present.

418010.label: Project Objectives
418010.value: Tackle the problem of appropriate Gaussian components per state in a HMM system, with the EM algorithm replaced by BYY harmony learning for automatic determining Gaussian components. Also, a comparative study will be conducted on typical criteria BIC/MDL, variantional Bayes, and recent discriminative growth functions. Proceed to estimate transfer probabilities across hidden states also by BYY harmony learning and to examine whether there is a better number of hidden states for a HMM to describe each phone, which may provide an alternative approach for modeling variable transfer duration. Conduct a comparative investigation on two typical structured covariance matrices, namely by a factor analysis model and by a linear latent model that uses one Gaussian mixture for latent variables and the other for noise, in term of both empirical and mathematical analyses. Extend the studies of Objectives 1&2 to the above two covariance matrices, which becomes much more difficult because we need to determine not only the number of components per state, but also the number of latent factors and the number of Gaussians in a mixture for describing noise. Further investigate discriminatively training all or a subset of HMM models jointly at a level of phones in help of Rival Penalized Competitive Learning (RPCL) in a comparison with the conventional MMI, MCE and MPE, together with analyses on the links and cross-benefits. Extend the above RPCL based studies into the cases of two structured covariance matrices studied in the above Objective 3, in help of a combination of making RPCL learning across many HMM models and implementing BYY harmony learning within each HMM. Controlling the complexity of each HMM model and making discriminative training across many HMM models are two closely related tasks. A further investigation will be made on each of their roles to speech recognition performance and their mutual relations.

418010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418010.value: Automatic continuous speech recognition has many potential applications including command and control, dictation, transcription of recorded speech, searching audio documents and interactive spoken dialogues, ..., etc. As an official language of mainland China and with a vast population of speakers, automatic mandarin speech recognition gets a rapid increasing need as mainland china jumps into an information society in the past decades. Regardless what kinds of languages, almost all present day large vocabulary continuous speech recognition systems are based on Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) that provides a simple and effective framework for modeling time-varying spectral vector sequences. Although the basic framework for HMM based automatic continuous speech recognition has not changed significantly, in the last decade or more, the detailed modeling techniques developed within this framework have evolved to a state of considerable sophistication. These developments arise or renew a number of problems that becomes critical to be solved in order to consolidate these lines of developments. Potential chances for solving these problems also emerge as the advances of machine learning in the past decade. Particularly, motivated by recent efforts on structured covariance modeling and discriminative measure based learning, this proposal focuses on automatic determining Gaussian components per state in a HMM and further on controlling the complexities of two factor analysis based structures. Moreover, this proposal proceeds to explore discriminative learning, along a direction different from those based either on the standard MMI, MCE and MPE measures and recent extensions to discriminative growth functions or on the Bayesian evidence such as BIC/MDL and variational Bayes. The goals will be pursuit in help of automatic model selection ability during parameter learning, which is possessed by Rival Penalized Competitive Learning and Bayesian Ying-Yang harmony learning. These studies will be practically implemented on a large vocabulary continuous Mandarin speech recognition system developed by Peking university, incorporating specific natures of mandarin speech. The possible outcomes will be not only possible improvements of this Mandarin speech recognition system but also new understanding and new techniques that are not only specific to Mandarin speech recognition, but also beneficial to other HMM based speech recognition tasks. 自動連續語音識別有許多應用,例如,指令控制、錄音註解、語音庫檢索、人機對話等等。隨著我國快速進入信息化社會，對官方語言普通話之自動識別的需求也急劇增長。不論語種，當今的大詞彙連續語音識別系統幾乎都是基於HMM模型，因為該模型為時變譜矢量序列提供了有效描述。過去十幾年來，儘管語音識別系統使用HMM模型的基本方式沒有重大改變，技術層次上還是有許多新發展，並導致對若干基本問題的重新關注，而過去十餘年來機器學習的發展為解決這些問題提供了新的機會。本立項考慮對協方差的結構分析和基於判別準則的學習，它們是近年來倍受關注的課題。首先，致力於HMM模型中每個狀態附屬高斯分佈個數的自動判定，進而研究兩種基於因子分析的協方差的結構。然後，既不基於通常的MMI, MCE and MPE 準則，也不同於近年來對判別增長函數、BIC/MDL、變分Bayes的研究，本立項倚賴RPCL競爭學習和BYY和諧學習，具有在進行參數學習过程中能夠自動選控模型複雜度的能力，發展判別學習的新方法。研究工作將在北京大學研發的大詞彙連續語音普通話識別系統上實現，期望的成果不僅是此識別系統的進一步改進，並且不局限於普通話識別，對基於HMM模型的大詞彙連續語音識別，也提供進一步地理解和新的技術手段。

418010.label: Realisation of objectives
418010.value: The first three objectives are targeted systematically in long papers C8.1,C8.2 (Remark: Some studies in C8.1 as well as in C8.6 and C9.3 started before the commencement date of the project in preparing this project). First, the BYY harmony learning algorithm has been developed for learning Gaussian components per state such that appropriate Gaussian components per state are determined automatically. Extensive empirical investigations are made in comparison with criteria AIC,BIC/MDL,variational Bayes(VB) and minimum message length(MML) for learning Gaussian mixture with an appropriate number of Gaussian components. It has been shown in C8.2,C8.4 that the BYY harmony learning outperforms not only the ML based AIC and BIC/MDL but also VB and MML for any type of priors and whether or not hyperparameters is optimized. Second, several covariance structures for Gaussian components have been studied for Objective 3 in 5.2. See Sect.2.2 of C8.2, parameterization structures of factor analysis have been investigated from a co-dimensional matrix pairing perspective in comparison with ML learning, Bayesian approaches, and BYY harmony learning. In term of appropriate controlling the covariance complexity or determining the number of latent factors, the ML learning is incapable to differentiate these parameterization structures, while the BYY harmony learning is better than both ML learning and Bayesian approaches in a good use of relevant information for model selection to improve learning performances. Moreover, both the structure of classic factor analysis and the structure that uses one Gaussian mixture for latent variables and the other for noise are both inferior to one parameterization structure previously proposed by the PI group. Such a promising feature has also be illustrated by empirical studies C8.6,C8.8,C9.2. Much beyond this Objective 3, parameterization structures have also been extended to temporal structures (see Sect.5.2 of C8.1 and Sect. 4.2 of C8.2) and binary structures C8.7, C9.1, also supported by empirical results and other applications C8.6,C8.7,C8.8,C9.1,C9.2. Actually, the above studies not only complete but also beyond the first three objectives. The rest two objectives, i.e.the 5th and 6th, a new discriminative approach has been developed in C8.3,C9.1,C9.2,C9.3 for Gaussian components of HMMs based continuous speech recognition system, featured by embedding the BYY harmony learning and its simplification of RPCL on the level of hidden states. Without the extensive computing burden required by typical discriminative methods, this new approach saves computing costs considerably with better performances than the classical ML learning and improved generalization ability over MMI and MPE.

418010.label: Major findings and research outcome
418010.value: Targeting at improvements of Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) based large vocabulary continuous speech recognition (LVCSR) systems, major findings and research outcomes of this project focus on discriminative measure based learning and structured covariance modeling. For discriminative measure based learning, it has been found that the Bayesian Ying-Yang (BYY) harmony measure provides better discriminative and generative abilities than the classic measures such as MMI, MCE and MPE. On the level of hidden Markov states, Rival Penalized Competitive Learning (RPCL) provides an effective implementation of BYY harmony measure. For every input, the correct identity state, called winner and obtained by the Viterbi force alignment, is enhanced to describe this input while its most competitive rival is penalized by de-learning, which makes Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) based states become more discriminative. Without the extensive computing burden required by typical discriminative learning methods for one-pass recognition of the training set, RPCL saves computing costs considerably. Moreover, the BYY harmony learning algorithm has been developed for learning Gaussian components such that appropriate Gaussian components per state are determined automatically. Extensive empirical investigations are made in comparison with criteria AIC, BIC/MDL, variational Bayes (VB) and minimum message length (MML) for learning Gaussian mixture with an appropriate number of Gaussian components. It has been shown that the BYY harmony learning outperforms not only the ML based AIC and BIC/MDL but also VB and MML for any type of priors and whether or not hyperparameters is optimized. For structured covariance modeling, covariance structures for Gaussian components have been studied either with each Gaussian component replaced by a factor analyses model or with an entire mixture of Gaussian components modeled by a linear latent model that uses a Gaussian mixture for latent variables and another Gaussian mixture for observation noise. It has been found that automatic selection mechanism relates to parameterization of latent factor structures. In term of appropriate controlling the covariance complexity or determining the number of latent factors, the ML learning is incapable to differentiate these parameterization structures, while the BYY harmony learning is better than both ML learning and Bayesian approaches in a good use of relevant information for model selection to improve learning performances. Moreover, both the structure of classic factor analysis and the structure that uses one Gaussian mixture for latent variables and the other for noise are both inferior to one parameterization structure previously proposed by the PI group.

418010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418010.value: For Hidden Markov Models based large vocabulary continuous speech recognition systems, discriminative learning actually involves controlling the complexities of covariance structures for Gaussian components, the number of Gaussian components per state, the number of hidden states, transfer probabilities across hidden states. This project has shown that it is a promising direction of using Bayesian Ying-Yang harmony learning and Rival Penalized Competitive Learning to control these complexities. In addition to the studies of this project on covariance structures, Gaussian components per state, and the number of hidden states, the Bayesian Ying-Yang harmony learning algorithm has been preliminarily developed for learning transfer probabilities across hidden states, efforts towards this direction are deserved. Furthermore, further studies may also be extended to discriminative learning for multiple HMM models, as proposed in the original application while removed in the revised objectives of section 5.2, i.e., controlling the complexity of each HMM model and making discriminative training across many HMM models are two closely related tasks. A further investigation will be made on each of their roles to speech recognition performance and their mutual relations. Additionally, comparative studies may also be used on those existing discriminative learning methods that have not examined in this project.

418010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418010.value: Regardless what kinds of languages, almost all present day large vocabulary continuous speech recognition (LVCSR) systems are based on Hidden Markov Models. In the last decade or more, new developments within this framework arise or renew a number of problems that becomes critical, among which two issues have been investigated by this project. One is discriminative measure based learning, for which a new direction is found. Automatic selection mechanism is embedded on the level of hidden Markov states by RPCL learning and BYY harmony learning, such that the appropriate Gaussian components per state are automatically determined and the resulted states become more discriminative. The new approach saves computing costs considerably and demonstrates better discriminative and generative abilities than the classic approaches. The other issue is seeking good covariance structures for Gaussian components, for which it has been found that the performances of controlling the covariance complexity depend on both parameterizations of latent factor featured covariance structures and the training approaches. The ML learning is incapable to differentiate parameterization structures, while the BYY harmony learning is better than both ML learning and Bayesian approaches. These studies have contributed improvements to a mandarin LVCSR system PULSAR developed by Peking university.

418610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418610.value: Proteins from bacterial surface layer (S-layer) serve as a versatile substrate for templated assembly and organized arrays of molecules and nanoparticles. This proposal aims to interface living bacterial endospores to silicon electronic devices nanopatterned on S-layer protein monolayers along microfluidic channels. In this study, we will use the S-layer protein SbpA of Bacillus sphaericus as our bioelectronic breadboard to study physiological properties of Bacillus subtilis endospores from a novel nanoscale perspective by converting cellular metabolism into electrical signals. Using impedimetric, amperometric and microgravimetric measurement techniques, we proposal to study (1) bistability behavior in endospores as a bioelectronic switching mechanism; (2) endospore inactivation using titanium dioxide nanoparticle ultrafiltration system; (3) supramolecular fusion protein to study endospore germination, and (4) stochastic modeling of the exhibited heterogeneity of endospores. Bacterial endospores are of great research interest because of their extreme resistance, dormancy and longevity, thereby leading to implications in medical sterilization, food hygiene, astrobiology and longevity of life. S-layer proteins are capable of self-assembly to form highly ordered 2D- and 3D-nanostructures under in vitro conditions with well-defined pores. This customizable and fluidic nature enables easy conjugation of nanoparticles, antigens/antibodies and fusion proteins. The microfluidic platform offers additional advantages such as high-throughput, short reaction time, potential for parallel operation and integration with other miniaturized devices. 418610.label: Realisation of objectives
418610.value: Both objectives have been achieved with flying colors. 1. We have successfully constructed a microfluidic bioelectronic breadboard using the surface layer protein SbpA of Lysinibacillus sphaericus. We also tested out the self-assembly capability of two other species, Bacillus cereus and Geobacillus stearothermophilus, in forming a biotemplating platform. This is the first attempt in the literature to optimize the S-layer protein extraction protocol and a comparison of extraction protocols among different species. The isolated S-layer proteins were characterized by Bradford assay and SDS-PAGE. The proteins were recrystallized on gold surface with cross linkers (i.e., 11-mercaptoundecanoic acid (11-MUA) and 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide (EDC)). Atomic force microscopic (AFM) measurement and water contact angle measurement were used to study the surface property. The platform was coupled with microfluidics to allow easy immobilization of S-layer protein on gold. The mechanism of protein recrystallization on gold was investigated by electrochemical measurement. A pair of interdigitated electrodes underneath was fabricated on the platform using a micromolding-in-capillary (MIMIC) technique. The regions were connected with each other by microchannels and microvalves. 2. We have successfully measured properties of endospores, biofilms, proteins and nucleic acids using S-layer biotemplate platform as a rapid prototyping interface for impedimetric and amperometric changes. Electrochemical workstation and impedance analyzer were used to determine the performance and sensitivity of the breadboard. Specifically, we have (1) characterized the bistability behavior in endospores as a bioelectronic switching mechanism determined; (2) deciphered the endospore inactivation mechanism using an ultrafiltration system made of titanium dioxide nanoparticles; (3) investigated the germination mechanism of endospores and (4) carried out a stoachastic model of the exhibited heterogeneity of endospores.

418610.label: Major findings and research outcome
418610.value: Nanotechnology offers a suite of tools to interface with biomolecular processes with matching size scale between nanodevices and biomolecules. Devices for studying biomolecules are of great research interest. Proteins from bacterial surface layer (S-layer) can serve as building blocks for a nanostructured self-assembly system and be able to recrystallize at surfaces of a broad spectrum of materials. S-layer protein based bioelectronic breadboard on a microfluidic platform was developed to provide a rapid prototyping interface for studying impedimetric and amperometric change of magnetic nanoparticles, bacteria and endospores (Wong et al. 2014). Major findings include: (1) This is one of the first studies to optimize the S-layer protein extraction and isolation efficiencies in bacteria. We have tried a number of recrystallization schemes, cross-linking chemicals, dialysis parameters, and freeze drying conditions to achieve a uniform layer of self-assembled monolayer of protein lattice on a gold structure (Wong et al. 2014). Attempts have also been made to compare the S-layer protein purity and self-assembly properties between Lysinibacillus sphaericus, Bacillus cereus, and Geobacillus stearothermophilus. (2) Breadboard built with S-layer protein alone is not enough to fulfill the reconfigurable and plug-and-play properties. We have successfully integrated this biotemplate with a microfluidic platform with full fluidic control coupled with electrochemical measurements (Wong et al. 2014). (3) The bistability behavior sporulation and cannibalism behaviors were first observed in Bacillus endospores. Two discrete alternative states have been observed in Bacillus sporulation and cannibalism for the first time (results to be published). This constitutes the basics of logic-type operations in which bacterial activities can be switched on and off by external factors. (4) The underlying mechanism for the surface sporicidal effect of titanium dioxide has been elucidated. Photocatalytic oxidation due to the formation of OH radicals have been observed in endospores from scanning electron micrographs (results to be published). (5) Germination receptors were fused with S-layer proteins as highly ordered monolayers for a more thorough understanding of germination from a nanoscale perspective. The germination timecourse elicited in surface-associated Bacillus and Clostridium was elucidated for the first time. (6) Single cellular response of endospores towards germination stimuli was studied from a nanoscale perspective, thus providing a more thorough understanding of the inherent heterogeneity associated with microbiology. This study not only cross fertilizes nanotechnology, biology and fabrication, but also initiates innovations in the fields of molecular electronics, nanotechnology, medical sterilization and bacterial engineering.

418610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418610.value: Built on the results achieved, we have the following future plans: • Integration with open microfluidics to create suspended droplets for 2D array printing and spatial patterning. Biomolecules will be encapsulated in individual suspended droplets with a robust fluidic control. • Collaboration with Prof. Ki-Bum Lee from Rutgers University on the use of helium ion scanning microscopy to provide sub-nanometer resolution of biomolecules conjugated on the S-layer protein template. We are specifically interested in deciphering the surface morphology and proteins on the spore coat of Bacillus and Clostridium. • Our group has developed piezoelectric cantilever tips coated with molecular imprinted polymers for near-field scanning microscopy. The marriage between this scanning technique with the S-layer biotemplate opens up avenues for probing nanoscale science. • The surface acoustic wave-assisted atomizer developed by our group will be used as a means of rapid prototyping and surface spatial patterning on the S-layer protein surface. • Collaboration with Prof. Xiankai Sun from CUHK on the integration of optical MEMS and nanophotonics with the S-layer biotemplate substrate. The miniaturization of photonic devices enables in vitro monitoring of biomolecular interaction. Initial attachment of microbial biofilms on substrates will be investigated. • Step up industrialization with transfer and protection of intellectual property rights.

418610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418610.value: Given a battery, resistor and light bulb, the easiest way to check their functionality is to connect all components on a circuit breadboard. Breadboards are reusable and does not require soldering, thus allowing rapid prototyping of various circuit designs. Resistance, voltage and current can readily be measured. Mimicking this idea, our project invents a nanoscale breadboard consisting of regularly arranged surface-layer proteins extracted from bacteria. Cells, nucleic acids, and proteins can be conjugated to this biotemplate in a “plug-and-play” fashion with the help of a microfluidic platform. Electrochemical properties of biomolecules can thus be measured at ease. Interaction of molecules and cells can also be investigated. Biofilm is a surface-association community of microorganisms commonly found in the nature with implications in hospital cross contamination and industrial biofouling. Biofilm appears as slimy molds of microorganisms encased in a complex 3D structure, which presents a great challenge for scientists to decipher for years. We have demonstrated the spatial measurement of biofilm properties by the S-layer protein template. This technology provides a new paradigm for the manipulation, patterning and measurement of biomolecules from an electrochemical perspective.

418710.label: Project Objectives
418710.value: Improve the previous lower bounds for the quantum query complexity of a list of concrete functions, including Graph Matching, Bipartiteness, Triangle, k-Element Distinctness, Matrix Product Verification, Local Search (on low dimensional cubes). Prove strong lower bounds for all monotone graph properties, a class of functions drawing the most attention classically in the query computation model. The current best lower bound is \Omega(n^{2/3}) by the old graph packing method. As a first step of attempt, we plan to reproduce the bound by a totally different method through a complexity measure called influence. Discover new relations between the quantum query complexity and other complexity measures. In particular, we propose to study quantum lower bounds in terms of the classical query complexity, the maximum influence, and the communication complexity.

418710.value: 量子查询复杂性是一个与量子算法和其他经典复杂性度量有很多自然联系的复杂性度量。量子查询复杂性好的下界意味着设计这些问题的量子算法的难度。关于这个专题的研究有助于发现新的技术设计量子算法。证明对量子查询复杂性的下界一直是一个具有挑战性的任务。在这个项目中，我们计划在三个方向上研究量子查询复杂性，重点放在下界证明上。 1。改善一些具体函数的下界。虽然人们付出很多努力，还是有一些问题的量子查询复杂性没有确定。我们希望对这些函数的下界进行改进。我们重新研究这个重要的任务的主要的原因是，一个新的证明下界的方法最近被发现总是能证明最优的答案。这意味着只要我们运用正确的参数，我们的方法总是可以证明最好下界。鉴于该方法和之前的一个方法形式上非常类似，而PI对之前的这个方法有很多一手的经验，所以是用新方法研究这些问题的一个好机会。 2。证明在经典计算复杂性理论中广为关注的所有单调图形属性的好的下界。一个经典的猜测是所有单调图形属性的随机查询复杂性至少\Omega(n)，已经有超过三十年，但是我们还不知道答案。相应的量子版本猜测的证明也卡住了将近十年。任何对这个著名的难题取得进展将导致对对称性在复杂性中的作用上有突破性的新认识。PI和他的合作者已经再联系量子查询复杂性和另一个复杂性度量“整体影响”上迈出了坚实的一步。而那个结果令人惊讶的适用于所有的平衡图属性，一类比单调图属性更大的一类属性。我们还猜测另一个不等式，如果正确，将会对这一个问题给出一个漂亮的解。 3。研究量子查询复杂性和其他复杂性度量之间的关系，特别是经典查询复杂性，最大影响，和通信复杂性。这三个度量都与理论计算机科学中很多其他的研究有着紧密地联系。PI已获得了一些关于最大影响和通信的复杂性的关系，希望改善这些成果，和在于经典查询复杂性的联系上取得进展。 我们所有提出的这些问题都是量子计算中的核心问题。对这些问题的研究会增强我们对量子信息处理技术，以及各种相关的问题如经典计算近似度，阈度，布尔函数的傅立叶分析有关的度量的理解。

418710.label: Realisation of objectives
418710.value: 1. The PI studied the specific functions but didn't obtain better lower bounds. But actually, all previous lower bounds remained the same in the past years; in other words, no one made progress on these hard problems either. Though no publications, the PI got many first-hand experiences during the studies of these functions which could be used in future research on related questions. 2. The PI studied various lower bound methods and gave an alternatively proof of an important lower bound for randomized query complexity in terms of maximum influence. The previous proof was the main content of a FOCS paper. Our proof is much simplified and essentially contains just one-line. The proof was recently found to extend to more powerful computational models of parity decision tree. This shows that our simple proof is very robust and actually yields even stronger result. The work was published in the leading journal Theory on Computing. 3. The PI proved that the quantum query complexity is lower bounded by total influence. In another paper, the PI proved that the communication complexity of formula has a depth-dependent lower bound of sqrt{n} for randomized and n^{1/4} for quantum (COCOON'10). In yet another work, the PI gave tight bounds on communication complexity of symmetric XOR functions in one-way and SMP Models (TAMC'11). The PI also studied the power of existing lower bound methods for quantum one-way communication complexity, and showed that all of them are exponentially weak for some functions (ICALP'11).

418710.label: Major findings and research outcome
418710.value: The PI compared various randomized query complexity lower bound methods and gave an alternatively proof of an important lower bound in terms of maximum influence. The previous proof was the main content of a FOCS paper, and the new proof by PI is much simplified. Actually it essentially contains just one-line. What's more, the new proof has long term impact as well: It was recently found to extend to more powerful computational models of parity decision tree. The work was published in the leading journal Theory on Computing (Part C.8 [2]). The PI proved that the quantum query complexity is lower bounded by total influence. In another paper, the PI proved that the communication complexity of formula has a depth-dependent lower bound of sqrt{n} for randomized and n^{1/4} for quantum (Part C.9 [9]). In yet another work, the PI gave tight bounds on communication complexity of symmetric XOR functions in one-way and SMP Models (Part C.9 [2]). The PI also studied the power of existing lower bound methods for quantum one-way communication complexity, and showed that all of them are exponentially weak for some functions (Part C.9 [1]).

418710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418710.value: More studies on quantum query complexity on certain problems are expected, which will benefit our understandings of those fundamental functions in this and other models. Decision tree complexity has been an important subject of concrete complexity theory. Recently there was an increasingly amount of attention on an extension called parity decision tree complexity, in which a query algorithm is allowed to ask any linear function of the variables. Some results obtained in this project shed an important light on our understandings of this extended model as well. Decision tree complexity and communication complexity are connected by canonical results of Nisan, and Buhrman-Cleve-Wigderson. Whether the two complexities are constantly related is an interesting question.

418710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418710.value: This project studies an important complexity measure called quantum query complexity, which basically measures how fast a quantum algorithm can run. Unfortunately this quantity is very hard to determine, so upper and lower bound methods are important. In this project, the PI studied quantum query complexity of both specific functions and important classes of functions. The results obtained significantly deepen our understandings of how much quantum computers can speedup computation over their classical counterparts.

419010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419010.value: Spare parts or (as it is often called)service parts management is critical in manufacturing and service operations. Without adequate stocks of spare parts, machines will be idle, power plant cannot function, airplanes will be grounded and the resulting costs could be enormous. But holding too much spare part inventory will tie up a large amount of capital and reduce the utilization of assets. This project aims to provide effective and efficient inventory management solutions to balance this tradeoff for complex spare parts supply chains taking into account various practical issues such as multiple supply sources, service-differentiated demand classes, economies of scale in ordering/production, and multiple stocking locations. Different classes of demand could come from replacement requests from equipments with different critical levels if spare parts are for internal use or from external service requests of customers in different priority classes. A well-designed and easy-to-implement rationing policy to allocate on hand inventory to different classes of demand hence needs to be in place to satisfy different service requirements. With the increasing popularity and importance of outsourcing, firms have commonly procured spare parts from multiple supply sources to achieve flexibility in delivery lead times and cost benefits so as to respond quickly to demand while avoiding excess inventory. Economies of scale are always a goal that firms aim to achieve when fixed ordering/production costs arise. And efficient deployment and management of stocks in multiple locations is always a challenge for spare parts supply chain. These practical issues, individually or combined, have not yet been fully explored in previous studies. To tackle these challenges, we develop quantitative models and focus more on examining simple and effective strategies. We further provide approaches to evaluate the proposed policies and optimize the policy control parameters. We compare the performance of different policies and discuss various managerial insights. Guidelines and tactics are provided to support managers' decision-making in controlling spare parts supply chain. Building upon the theoretical analysis and results, we quantify the value of solutions using data from a large petrochemical company in Western China which is keen to improve its current unsophisticated and inefficient spare parts inventory management. We also seek opportunities to implement the solutions to manage some representative parts and compare their performance with the existing practices. We expect the research outcomes of this project will have great potential applications and large impact in various industries. 备品配件管理（通常简称为备件管理）是很多制造业与服务业运作管理中的关键环节。一方面，如果备件库存不足，机器设备将被迫闲置，发电厂将无法运行，飞机将被迫停飞，由此产生的成本可能是巨大的；另一方面，备件库存过多，将占用大量的资金，降低资产利用率。本项目旨在为企业提供高效的库存管理解决方案從而平衡复杂的备件供应链中的这两方面問題。本项目涉及多个相关的实际问题，如多供应源，服务差异化需求，订货/生产中的规模经济，和多点库存。备件需求通常被劃分不同的優先級別。在内部需求的情況下， 需求可能来自于对不同重要程度设备的更换或维修； 如果該備件是用于外部客户服务，則不同客戶有不同的优先级别，例如，优先级别需求和标准级别需求。因此这就需要一个设计良好，易于实施的库存配给策略，将现有库存分配给不同层级的需求，以满足不同服务水平的需求。随着外包的日益普及和日渐重要，企业开始普遍从多个供应源采购备件，以获得交货时间的灵活性和成本上的效益，进而快速响应需求且避免库存过剩。另外，当订货/生产存在固定成本时，企业往往需要考虑到订货/生产的规模经济效益。如何高效地对多地点的备件库存进行部署和管理，也是企业在备件供应链管理中所需要解决的颇具挑战的问题。这些实际问题无论是单独考虑或合并考虑，在以往的研究中都没有得到充分的探讨。这样的系统，在建模和分析的时候通常非常复杂。为了解决这些问题，我们建立了一系列的定量模型并重点研究一些简单有效的库存策略。我们提出准确有效的方法去评估这些库存策略并优化相应库存控制策略中的参数，比较不同策略的性能并讨论各种管理上的启示。最后我们还將給出相应的指导方针和执行策略，以幫助管理者做出备件供应链管理时的决策。 在理论分析结果的基础上，我们使用了中国西部某大型石化公司（该公司正急切需要改善其目前简单低效的备件库存管理方法）的数据以定量地衡量我们提出的策略的价值。更重要的是，我们还将寻找机会在某些具有代表意义的备件上实施我们提出的管理策略，以比较新策略与现行做法在性能表现上的差别。我们希望本项目的研究成果能够在不同行业中都具有很大的应用潜力和影响。具体来说，我们的建议和解决方案将帮助企业提高其备件运作管理的效率，降低库存成本，减少资本占用率的同时并提高资产利用率，维持高的服务水平。这些成果都将最终提高企业的盈利能力和竞争力。

419010.label: Realisation of objectives
419010.value: The four objectives proposed in the project have been achieved successfully. For objective 1, we developed three quantitative models closely related to spare part management: a single-location model with dual sourcing and pricing decision, a single-location model with dual sourcing and two classes of demand; and stochastic one-warehouse-multi-retailer system. These models are rather complicated, for which there is no much existing analysis. For objectives 2 and 3, we proposed, evaluated, and optimized some simple but effective control policies for the models. We also numerically test and compare their performance with other existing policies. For the second model, we further used real data sets from a petro-chemical plant in western China and showed the effectiveness of our policy. For objective 4, we communicated with the manager of the petro-chemical plant (mainly via the collaborator of the PI at Xi’an Jiaotong University) and partially implemented the proposed solutions, which lead to efficiency improvement of inventory management of their spare parts.

419010.label: Major findings and research outcome
419010.value: Through this project, the PI has two journal papers published/accepted and one under revision. The major findings of this project are reported in these papers summarized below. In the paper “Dynamic Pricing and Inventory Management with Regular and Expedited Supplies,” published in POMS, we consider a periodic-review inventory system with regular and expedited supply modes. The expedited supply is faster than the regular supply but incurs a higher cost. Demand for the product in each period is random and sensitive to its selling price. The firm determines its order quantity from each supply in each period as well as its selling price to maximize the expected total discounted profit over a finite or an infinite planning horizon. We characterize the optimal inventory and pricing policies. We further study the operational impact of such supply diversification and show that it increases the firm's expected profit, reduces the optimal safety-stock levels, and lowers the optimal selling price. Thus that diversification is beneficial to both the firm and its customers. A working paper titled “Spare parts management: Anticipated rationing policy and dual sourcing” is currently under revision. In this paper, we develop a multi-period spare part management model, in which a firm has two available supply sources for its spare part. One supply is faster but more expensive than the other. In each period, the firm faces two classes of demand with different backlogging costs. We propose a class of easily-implementable control policies. For inventory replenishment, the policy is base-stock type and is determined by two base-stock levels. For demand rationing, we introduce an anticipated rationing policy. Meanwhile, we also design a simple heuristic to obtain near optimal policies within the proposed policy class. PI also developed and analyzed a distribution inventory system in “Optimizing Reorder Intervals for Two-Echelon Distribution Systems with Stochastic Demand”, which is closely related to and can be applied to spare part inventory management. We consider a periodic-review inventory system in which N non-identical retailers replenish from a warehouse, which further replenishes from an outside vendor with ample supply. Each facility faces Poisson demand and replenishes according to a base-stock policy in a fixed time interval. Fixed costs are incurred for placing an order. We develop an evaluation scheme and provide a method to obtain the optimal base-stock levels and reorder intervals. Meanwhile, we develop a simple and effective heuristic, which can be applied to large systems.

419010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419010.value: Spare parts management is critical in manufacturing and service operations. Without adequate stocks of spare parts, machines will be idle, power plant cannot function, airplanes will be grounded and the resulting costs could be enormous. But holding too much spare part inventory will tie up a large amount of capital and reduce the utilization of assets. By developing and analyzing quantitative models, this project provides effective and efficient inventory management solutions and pricing strategies to balance this tradeoff for complex spare parts supply chains involving various practical issues such as multiple supply sources, service-differentiated demand classes, economies of scale in ordering/production, and multiple inventory stocking points. We further test and demonstrate the performance of these policies and discuss various managerial insights using either real or simulated data. The research outcome also includes guidelines and tactics to support managers’ decision-making in managing spare parts supply chain.

440410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
440410.value: 误价，异质风险和股票横截面收益率

440410.label: Project Objectives
440410.value: Test the competing theories on the role of idiosyncratic risk in asset pricing, by examining whether and how idiosyncratic risk affects the cross-sectional stock returns. Explain why previous studies find conflicting evidence on the cross-sectional relation between idiosyncratic risk and returns. 440410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
440410.value: This proposal explores the potential effects of idiosyncratic risk on the cross-section of stock returns. Competing theories on the role of idiosyncratic risk in asset pricing make different predictions regarding the relation between idiosyncratic risk and stock returns. Previous literatures document mixed empirical findings. Using the limit of arbitrage framework, we test new hypotheses on how idiosyncratic risk affects the expected stock returns. We also seek to provide an economic rationale for the conflicting empirical evidence documented by previous studies. Idiosyncratic risk is an important arbitrage cost. It deters risk-averse arbitrageurs from buying undervalued stocks and short selling overvalued stocks. We expect that idiosyncratic risk, as an arbitrage cost measure, is not systematically priced. However, among undervalued (overvalued) stocks, returns should increase (decrease) with idiosyncratic risk. We further expect that this conditional relation could explain the puzzling finding that high idiosyncratic risk stocks have lower value-weighted portfolio returns. Our project will contribute to the debate on the relation between idiosyncratic risk and stock returns. It will also provide new evidence on the limit of arbitrage theory, which is an important building block of behavioral finance. Our study enhances the understanding of asset pricing and market efficiency within the context of idiosyncratic volatility. 本项目试图探讨异质风险对股票横截面收益率的可能的影响。对于异质风险在资产定价中的作用，比如异质风险和股票收益率的关系，不同理论提出了不同的预测。不仅理论上存在分歧，实证研究的结果也没有定论。关于异质风险如何影响预期的股票收益率，我们将基于有限套利的理论框架来检验一些新的假设。对于目前相互矛盾的实证研究结果，我们也试图提供一个合理的解释。 异质风险是一种重要的套利成本。它不仅阻止风险规避的套利者买入被低估的股票，也阻止他们卖空被高估的股票。我们认为异质风险作为套利成本并没有被系统性的定价。然而，在被低（高）估的股票当中，收益率将随着异质风险的增加而增加（减少）。我们更认为这种条件性的关系能够解释为什么较高异质风险的股票组合会有较低的市值加权的收益率。 本研究将有助于解决关于异质风险和股票收益率之间关系的争论。同时也对行为金融学的基石之一， 有限套利理论，提供了新的实证支持。通过研究异质风险，本项目将有助于更好的理解资产定价和市场有效性。

440410.label: Realisation of objectives
440410.value: 1. We use an EGARCH model and weekly returns to estimate expected idiosyncratic volatility. The main empirical findings exactly support the limits of arbitrage theory and can be summarized as follows: First, idiosyncratic risk is not systematically priced. Portfolio analysis results show that stocks with higher idiosyncratic risk have higher equal-weighted portfolio returns, but also have lower value-weighted portfolio returns. However, neither relation is robust over subsamples or confirmed in the multivariate regressions. Second, as a large arbitrage cost, idiosyncratic risk does matter. Under the assumption that mispricing exists, both portfolio analysis and multivariate regressions results confirm that there are conditional relations between idiosyncratic risk and stock returns. Stock returns increase with idiosyncratic risk among undervalued stocks, while decrease among overvalued stocks. Alternative theories such as CAPM and Merton (1987) can explain these findings. 2. Empirically, AHXZ (2006) document that stocks with high lagged realized idiosyncratic volatility have low value-weighted returns. Fu (2009) finds a positive relation between EGARCH idiosyncratic volatility and returns. We use weekly returns for EGARCH measure, which solves the short sample size problem of monthly returns in Fu (2009), and we find a similar result with AHXZ (2006) for value-weighted returns. It suggests that how idiosyncratic volatility is measured is not the key, but the fact that idiosyncratic volatility stands for an arbitrage cost. We also find that the idiosyncratic volatility-return relation becomes more negative if stocks are held for longer horizons. Short-sale constraints, which only apply to overpriced stocks and have stronger effect in longer horizon, could explain why the relation between idiosyncratic volatility and stock returns changes toward more negative when holding horizon extends. 3. We provid evidence in both stocks market and stock option market that idiosyncratic volatility deters arbitrage. In stock market, idiosyncratic risk itself is not priced, but it affects returns of mispriced stocks. stock returns significantly increase in idiosyncratic volatility for relatively undervalued stocks and decrease for relatively overvalued stocks. In stock option market, idiosyncratic risk increases the relative mispricing between option and the underlying stocks. Dealers charge a higher premium for options on high idiosyncratic volatility stocks due to their higher arbitrage costs.

440410.label: Major findings and research outcome
440410.value: Cao and Han (2012a) reconcile the debate on empirical evidence between idiosyncratic volatility and the cross-section of stock returns. AHXZ (2006) document that stocks with high lagged realized idiosyncratic volatility have low returns. Fu (2009) finds a positive relation between EGARCH idiosyncratic volatility and returns. One potential problem of Fu (2009) is that monthly time-series of firm level return is short and may not generate precise volatility estimates. To address this concern, we use an EGARCH model and weekly returns to estimate expected idiosyncratic volatility, and find no systematic relation between idiosyncratic volatility and expected weekly returns. High idiosyncratic volatility stocks have higher (lower) equal (value) -weighted portfolio returns than low idiosyncratic volatility stocks, and both relations are only marginally significant. However, we find robust evidence that stock returns significantly increase in idiosyncratic volatility for relatively undervalued stocks and decrease for relatively overvalued stocks. It is consistent with the argument that idiosyncratic risk is an important arbitrage cost. Among high idiosyncratic volatility stocks, overvalued stocks are relatively bigger than undervalued stocks, hence the equal (value) weighed portfolio return is very high (low). We also find that the idiosyncratic volatility-return relation becomes more negative if stocks are held for longer horizons. Short-sale constraints, which only apply to overpriced stocks and have stronger effect in longer horizon, could explain why the relation between idiosyncratic volatility and stock returns changes toward more negative when holding horizon extends. Overall, idiosyncratic volatility is not priced, and it does not depend on how we measure it. But idiosyncratic volatility does affect stocks return as an arbitrage cost measure. Cao and Han (2012b) study how idiosyncratic volatility affects option returns. We documents a robust new finding that delta-hedged equity option return decreases monotonically with an increase in the idiosyncratic volatility of the underlying stock. It suggests that options with high idiosyncratic volatility are more overvalued relative to the underlying stocks than options with low idiosyncratic volatility. The results are robust for both lagged realized idiosyncratic volatility and EGARCH expected idiosyncratic volatility. It is consistent with market imperfections and constrained financial intermediaries. Dealers charge a higher premium for options on high idiosyncratic volatility stocks due to their higher arbitrage costs. Reference: Cao, Jie and Bing Han, 2012a, Reconciling the debate on idiosyncratic volatility: An explanation from the limits to arbitrage, Working paper. Cao, Jie and Bing Han, 2012b, Cross-section of option returns and idiosyncratic stock volatility, 2012 Journal of Financial Economics.

440410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
440410.value: Extend the sample for international evidence that idiosyncratic volatility is an arbitrage cost measure.

440410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
440410.value: Idiosyncratic or firm specific risk prevents rational arbitrageurs from buying undervalued securities, and short-selling overvalued securities. So market is not fully efficient due to the limits to arbitrage. We find evidence to support this argument from both stock market and stock option market. In stock market, idiosyncratic risk itself is not priced, but it affects returns of mispriced stocks. In stock option market, idiosyncratic risk increases the relative mispricing between option and the underlying stocks.

441410.label: Major findings and research outcome
441410.value: When properly managed, financial bailout can better facilitate incentives than a blanket-syle financial discipline against all loss making firms. It helps shed light on China's economic reform, especially that since the late 1990s during which China privatized almost all small-and medium-sized state firms while keeping afloat many large state companies. As we will see below, when extending our insights beyond the specifics of China, we are able to understand why some developing countries, for example, are able to succeed with some carefully designed subsidy programs, to support their infant industries for example.

441410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
441410.value: We will extend our argument to a more general context to examine how subsidies can be designed to not only address externality problems but also encourage, rather than compromise, incentives. This may help us understand under what conditions, for example, infant industry policies can facilitate, rather than compromise (as the existing literature often claims), firms' incentives.

441410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
441410.value: This research has shown that by helping out some state-owned companies, China has been able to push through its state sector reform without causing much turbulence in its economy while instead promoting the country's economic growth at the same time. Our study sheds new light in China's state sector policy.

442010.label: Project Objectives
442010.value: To examine the existing documentation of Messiaen’s views and writings about his colour-hearing and to evaluate how well Messiaen’s testimonies fit the terms and conditions accepted by neuroscientists as normative in synaesthesia. To investigate how Messiaen’s comments on the religious experience of 'sound-colour bedazzlement' and his musical realization of the same interacted and evolved over time. To reconstruct Messiaen’s sound-colour materials and techniques with recourse to his writings and music and to explore possible correlation between the aural and visual effects of his sound-colour materials. To examine Messiaen’s theological background with recourse to his references to the scriptures and canonical theological writings for factors that might have fuelled his conception of the 'sound-colour bedazzlement'. To establish how Messiaen’s faculty of sound-colour hearing could have affected his compositional approaches and aesthetics, shaped the way he expressed and communicated his Catholic faith through music, and influenced his artistic development. To develop an interdisciplinary approach to Messiaen’s claim of the musico-religious experience of 'sound-colour bedazzlement' by taking into consideration pertinent scientific research on colour-hearing and theological speculation on bedazzlement. 442010.label: Realisation of objectives
442010.value: As mentioned at the outset of my article published in Rivista di Analisi e Teoria Musicale, a comprehensive examination of Messiaen’s testimonies that pertain to his colour-hearing claims resonate well with the terms and conditions currently accepted by neuroscientists as normative in synaesthesia. Messiaen's musical rendition of 'sound-colour bedazzlement' is found to be intricately related to his cultivation of a chorale-style of orchestral writing, where the factor of rhythmic design is scaled down in order to arrive at an optimal display of the sound-colour material. The technical use of Messiaen’s sound-colour materials as documented in volume VII of his Traite de rythme, de couleur, et d'ornithologie has been reconstructed with reference to primarily two orchestral works: Sept Haïkaï and Couleurs de la Cité Céleste. Excerpts from Transfiguration and Eclairs sur au-dela have also been examined in the light of Messiaen's discourse on sound-colour issues in his Kyoto Conference. Time did not allow fuller examination of Messiaen’s theological background, though I succeeded in establishing a distinct relationship between Messiaen’s religiosity and his use of the 'sound-colour bedazzlement' by unearthing both textual and musical evidence. Indeed, my attempt to combine the research findings of neuroscientists into synaesthesia with the existing musicological and theoretical studies of Messiaen's life and music proves fruitful in affirming his claim as a synaesthete. Since this is arguably the first confirmed case of a contemporary art music composer of canonic stature to be a synaesthete, his writing and music composition assume particular importance in the burgeoning field of synaesthesia research, and will certainly be drawn on by more collaborative research studies to come. The aesthetics of surrealism and French symbolist poets provide ample room for further investigation, since Messiaen’s writing revolves around them, and in the case of the French symbolist poets, sound-colour correspondence had been a major concern.

442010.label: Major findings and research outcome
442010.value: Neuroscientists’ latest findings on how best to verify the claim of a synaesthete is applied to the case of Messiaen by consulting primary and secondary sources about his life and music. This is found to be in support his claim as a synaesthete in the category of colour-hearing mode, and thus helps establish him as the first case of a contemporary art music composer of canonic stature to be proven a synaesthete. In-depth studies of textual and musical evidence reveal that there is a distinct relationship between Messiaen's composition of music that draws on Biblical texts and his use of the sound-colour material. More specifically, parts of Sept Haïkaï and Couleurs de la Cité Céleste that draw heavily on sound-colour materials as documented in volume VII of his Traite de rythme, de couleur, et d'ornithologie are scrutinized to throw light on the ascendency of a chorale-style of orchestral writing in Messiaen’s late orchestral works. The waning of his earlier use of complex rhythm is found to correlate with a gradual move towards the use of immensely slow tempo. These are arguably measures taken to maximize the impact of the sound-colour material. Messiaen’s claim of sound-colour bedazzlement, because of its overly subjective nature, is relatively hard to establish. Inspired by Debussy’s ‘Reflets dans l’eau’ and ‘Hommage à Rameau’, Messiaen’s exploration of the pentatonicized twelve-tone space is found to technically overlap with his use of cascades of chords derivable from the modes of limited transposition and thus, by extension, to his synaesthetic approaches to music compositions. Major research deliverables are book chapters and articles published in refereed journals of international standing: ‘Buddhist Temple, Shinto Shrine and the Invisible God of Sept Haïkaï’, Messiaen the Theologian (Hants: Ashgate, 2010), ed. by Andew Shenton, pp. 241–261. ‘Plainchants as Coloured Time in Messiaen’s Couleurs de la Cité Céleste’, Tempo (Cambridge University Press, 2010), vol. 64, no. 254, pp. 20-37. ‘Culture as Reference in the ‘Gagaku’ of Messiaen’s Sept Haïkaï’. Music and its Referential Systems (Series Specula Spectacula III), ed. by Matjaz Barbo & Thomas Hochradner (Vienna: Hollitzer, 2011), pp. 177-200. ‘Toward a Theory of Synaesthetic Composition: A Case Study of Messiaen’s Sound-colour and Bedazzlement’, Rivista di Analisi e Teoria Musicale, vol. 19, no. 1 (2013), pp. 65-88. ‘“Mirroir fluide”: Messiaen, Debussy and Cyrano’s “Synaesthetic” Bird’, Music & Letter, vol. 95/4 (2014: forthcoming from Oxford University Press).

442010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
442010.value: The research topic of Messiaen’s colour-hearing, given its interdisciplinary nature and the fact that the research area of synaesthesia came to prominence only in the past decade, has immense potential for further development. My presentation of a paper on Messiaen’s synaesthesia at the 2014 Annual Conference of UK’s Synaesthesia Association is an important step taken to explore opportunities of research collaboration. This has taken place in April this year. I shall consolidate the research network before proceeding to map out new and more extensive interdisciplinary and collaborative research projects.

442010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
442010.value: Foremost among the scholarly achievements generated by this GRF grant is the forthcoming publication of an extended refereed article of over forty pages in Music & Letters (Oxford University Press), which is, importantly, recognized as a first-class music journal worldwide. The article is ground-breaking in that it proves in unprecedentedly concrete terms how the legacy of Cyrano de Bergerac, a seventeenth-century French literary figure, and the canonic works of Claude Debussy influenced the course taken by Olivier Messiaen in his exploration of synaesthetic approaches to music composition. In addition, my investigation of Messiaen’s perplexing claims of sound-colour bedazzlement was published in 2013 in Italy’s top music theory journal, Rivista di Analisi e Teoria Musicale.

442110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
442110.value: In The Social Life of Things, Appadurai (1986) mentions that:“Commodities, and things in general, are of independent interest to several kinds of anthropology. ... As valuables, they are at the heart of economic anthropology and, not least, as the medium of gifting, they are at the heart of exchange theory and social anthropology generally.”Here, I would like to pay attentions to the different meanings of one food item in various social contexts in order to understand local livelihoods from an anthropological perspective. Food is one of the most important cultural markers of identity in modern societies, and it has provided a medium for the understanding of social relations, kinship, class, gender ideology, and cultural symbolism. Much scholarly attention has focused on the social and cultural construction of foodways, but a truly comprehensive view of food cannot neglect local politics and power relations among different stakeholders in the mode of food production. It is also necessary to discern how, when, from where and even why different kinds of food are produced, prepared and supplied. These are vivid examples of the global movement of ingredients which travel from region to region and even across oceans from continent to continent. Most importantly, they remind us not only of the changing concepts of food, as well as various eating and cooking styles in different places, but also of how people adopt and reproduce for trade and consumption regarding the local social development. This research project seeks to examine the social impacts brought by the introduction of North American freshwater crustaceans (commonly called crayfish) to Japan and mainland China, and to investigate individual and community responses toward the adaptation, consumption and conservation of this exotic species mainly during the last two decades. By studying different crayfish production in the US, Japan and mainland China, I aim to understand the socio-cultural changes that have taken place in the agricultural and fishery system in relation to the local economic and conservation developments since the 1990s. Finally, questions related to food production have been overlooked by social scientists, as it is commonly believed that they are the province of professionals working in the field of agriculture, biology, and nutrition. However, cultural aspects of food production have a significant impact on how and what we eat, and my focus of this project will help to elucidate the different interests of various stakeholders in the local socio-political context of production. 食物生產的模式，在歐洲船隊發現「新世界」後起了巨大的變化。若我們拿現今食物生產方式與其在殖民主義、帝國主義和資本主義的時代比較一下，或許會得到一些啟示。我們現在日常使用的食材其實很多都是外來進口，而非本地生產的。亦即是說，按其來源及流動，我們清楚得知有多少不同種類的食物是通過帝國主義、殖民主義、跨界網絡及全球貿易而流散的；當然，這些都涉及國際政治、權力關係、文化交流、國內和國外之間的貿易網絡及經濟發展等因素。如果你在過去幾年到過南京的食肆，你一定不會忘記當地的一種流行食物。它是一大盆豔紅的、形態有點古怪，但又飄散着濃郁麻辣香料的潮流小食──「南京小龍蝦」。對於這北美原螯蝦，有人說這是蓮花以外「出淤泥而不染」的君子，但也有人認爲是日本人為破壞江蘇一帶的水稻而遠道帶來的小特工。原產於北美大陸東南部的淡水濕地地區，其親族分佈世界各地，超過五百個品種。至於牠為何會攀山涉水來到南京人的餐桌上，背後卻隠藏著一個到今天仍不大清楚的原因。一方面，我們可能永遠無法知道這北美原螯蝦在江蘇一帶出現的真正原因；但另一方面我們對牠在中國和日本人民生活帶來的影響卻不能忽視。談及以克氏原螯蝦作為路易斯安那州的特色食物時，我們不可忘記牠就是早年非洲和法國勞動移民，在有限的經濟條件和多樣文化生活的交互影響下，所炮製出來的一種叫“Cajun food” 的美國南部地區主要食物。而且，今天的“Cajun cuisine”，不但代表新奧爾良的地區性食物，更反映了美國精神文明中，一種深層的南部文化及其源於移民社區的原動力。至於這種在美國被看成是基層的食物,如何在中國大陸變成美食,帶動農村經濟的發展，則是探討的課題。
