442110.label: Major findings and research outcome
442110.value: The research explains the rise of crayfish eating in New Orleans, United States and Nanjing, China from the global perspectives of food production and consumption. Crayfish used to be a new crop for all these three areas and was successfully created as a local food for various reasons under similar reason of regional development. Xuyi is just a show case of how a third-tier city develop with both traditional and modern aspects, and the localization of crayfish reflected by not only the increase of food consumption but also the establishment of museum and relevant festival. Through tracking down the path of how exotic ingredients were turned into local food catered for outsiders as well as tourists, this study of red swamp crayfish (Procambarus clarkii) both in the New Orleans, Louisiana (NOLA), Hokkido, Japan and Xuyi, Jiangsu (XYJS) provides an interesting case showing the relevant transformations in the three different countries in many parallel ways regarding their socio-cultural development. Based on my recent fieldtrip to New Orleans, Louisiana, I found the rise of crayfish farming only taken place since the late 1960s, and before that, all crayfish was wild, caught from bayou and drainage. When I asked local people about the origin of crayfish dishes and how and why it became popular and boomed in Louisiana, I often got the answer that crayfish eating has a long history and it had become a common dish because crawfish is essentially delicious; therefore, I would like to bring in the emotional attachment of local people to crayfish, which symbolizes an identity as well as a sense of belonging, but more importantly, as an anthropologist I aim to learn how the changing individual taste is related to the social and political environment. In the Chinese context, P. clarkii was brought to Nanjing by Japanese in the 1930s though the reason is still unclear. The Chinese in the Jiangsu area did not welcome it since it ate crops and fishes and did not bring benefits to the people there. For a long time, no one paid attention to it, and the emergence of the dish called ‘Nanjing little lobster’ did not appear until the early 1990s; yet its rapid growth in popularity was not limited to Nanjing but extended to big cities such as Shanghai and Beijing.

442110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
442110.value: I hope to continue the study of crayfish farming in the same three areas so that a longer and better documental of social change regarding the introduction of new crop together with its impacts brought to the local community can be furtherly investigated.

442110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
442110.value: This is an ethnography of crayfish (P. clarkii) farming in three cultures from the socio-cultural perspective. This Louisiana crayfish was brought to Jiangsu province by the Japanese in the 1930s and was not welcomed by local people, as it did not bring benefits to the community but caused damage to crops. However, during the last two decades, because of the farming of crayfish and the organization of international festival, tremendous changes taken place in agriculture and rural tourism development. One might ask if crayfish farming really help the farmers to earn enough for their living expenses, then the social problems arisen from migrant factory workers might be reduced and/or resolved at a good amount. With the study of a Xuyi in Jiangsu, I found out that innovation of crayfish farming is only the way local government makes a third-tier city famous instead of the major vehicle for generating revenues, and the real developmental expectation was attracting manufacturing and real estate investment from outside in order to increase the tax income and employment opportunity. Therefore, with the studies of crayfish farming in China, japan and the US, we are alerted that the understanding of agriculture development should consider how various interests (farmers, investors, consumers, and the government) can work together for the future rural lifeways.

442310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
442310.value: 王念孫(1744-1832)是清代傑出的校勘學家、訓詁學家，他對先秦、秦漢古籍的研究成果，至今仍普遍為學者肯定與採用。目前研究王氏之學的論著雖多，研究範圍卻長期局限在《廣雅疏證》、《讀書雜志》等幾部已經刊刻的著作上，難有突破。本計劃將收集、整理、研究八種經王氏親手批校的古籍校本，包括經部小學類的《方言》、《廣雅》，子部的《管子》、《韓非子》、《晏子春秋》、《呂氏春秋》、《山海經》、《風俗通義》。這些校本收藏在中、臺圖書館的善本書庫，大部分從未對外公布，有待開發研究。本計劃擬將上述校本的材料輯錄，編成《王念孫古籍校本所見校改、校語彙編》（以下簡稱《彙編》），並上載至本計劃的網頁，為學者提供極具學術價值的新材料，解決目前有關王氏之學在研究材料上的局限，開拓研究王氏之學的新里程。 校本直接反映了王氏早年校讀古籍的最初形態，本計劃將具體分析八種校本的校改與校語，並將其與王氏晚年寫成的《廣雅疏證》、《讀書雜志》等著作比對，梳理王氏前後期校讀古籍的成績，全面歸納王氏校讀古籍的條例，藉此探究王氏的校勘、訓詁理論在早期形成的過程與進境。 Wang Niansun(1744-1832) was a Qing scholar distinguished for his studies in textual criticism and semantics, whose researches on pre-Qin, Qin and Han ancient texts have been widely acknowledged and applied by scholars to this day. Present research into the great scholar's studies has been hampered, however, since such valuable materials can be accessed only by gleaning through Guangya shuzheng (《廣雅疏證》) and Dushu Zazhi (《讀書雜志》). To address the problem, this project aims to collect, compile and study the eight ancient texts Fangyan (《方言》), Guangya (《廣雅》), Guanzi(《管子》), Hanfeizi (《韓非子》), Yanzi chunqiu (《晏子春秋》), Lushi chunqiu(《呂氏春秋》), Shanhaijing (《山海經》) and Fengsu tongyi (《風俗通義》) in the versions collated and revised by Wang that are now scattered around libraries of rare books in China and Taiwan and are in closed stacks never opened to the public. Upon exploration and careful examination, these titles will be compiled as entries in a publication to be entitled Wang Niansun guji jiaoben suojian jiaogai jiaoyu huibian (《王念孫古籍校本所見校改、校語彙編》, A Collection of Collation and Interpretation from collated versions of ancient texts revised by Wang Niansun) and will be uploaded onto the internet for easy access. It is our hope that the extremely valuable fresh materials thus made available will open up a new path for researches into Wang's studies. Mindful that these collated versions represent no more than Wang's early findings, we will also compare and contrast them with Wang's other works which were completed in his middle and old age in an attempt to reveal the principles that the great scholar adopted for collating ancient texts and to trace how he developed his theory of textual criticism and semantics.

442310.label: Realisation of objectives
442310.value: 本計劃的主要目標，是抄錄並研究八種經王念孫親手批校的古籍校本。申請本計劃之前，計劃主持人已經從上海圖書館及臺灣中央研究院傅斯年圖書館借鈔了王念孫《方言》、《廣雅》、《管子》、《呂氏春秋》、《風俗通義》五種校本。在為期兩年半的計劃期間，計劃主持人先後三次到北京國家圖書館，借鈔該館所藏的《韓非子》、《晏子春秋》、《山海經》三種校本，將校本原書所見王氏親手用墨筆、朱筆所寫的批校如實過錄。我們聘請了全時的研究助理，將計劃主持人抄錄所得的資料輸入電腦，編製成《王念孫古籍校本所見校改、校語彙編》(以下簡稱《彙編》)。完成《彙編》的編輯工作後，我們隨即對個別校本進行了逐條疏證的研究，考證校本所見文字校勘、詞義訓解、章句分合等材料，比對《廣雅疏證》、《讀書雜志》、《經義述聞》、《經傳釋詞》等已經刊行的著作，同時參考前人對相關古籍的研究成果，藉此梳理王念孫的校改及校語，分析王氏校改的理據並加評騭，最後將研究成果以學術期刊及學術會議論文的形式公布。同時，我們重視學術成果的交流與分享，把新材料盡快公布，正是本計劃的研究目標。因此，我們分階段把已經發表的學術論文等研究成果上載至本計劃的網頁。

442310.label: Major findings and research outcome
442310.value: 在兩年半的研究時間裏，計劃主持人完成了所有抄錄校本的工作，並將資料輸入電腦，編製成《王念孫古籍校本所見校改、校語彙編》(以下簡稱《彙編》)。我們將數量較多，學術價值較大的材料，分別撰寫成三篇學術期刊論文(請參見Part C/Section 8)及四篇學術會議論文(請參見Part C/Section 9)。這些研究成果主要有： 第一、 從校勘、訓詁兩方面具體研究了校本的材料。研究了個別校本所見校改、校語，從而歸納王氏校勘相關古籍的方法與創獲。 第二、 我們將《彙編》的材料先按辨字形、通假借、考異文、明詁訓、因聲求義等訓詁方法分門別類，然後探究王氏的訓詁理論如何體現在這些校本的校改中。 第三、 我們將本計劃編纂的《彙編》與本計劃另一策劃人陳雄根教授主持的「《經義述聞》、《讀書雜志》研究計劃」編纂的《〈經義述聞〉、〈讀書雜志〉訓詁資料彙編》相互比較，梳理了王氏校讀古籍的條例。 第四、 我們利用校本的材料深入探討部分與王氏相關的學術問題，如有關「高郵王氏四種」著作權的問題，校本的發現證明了劉盼遂等人懷疑《經義述聞》、《經傳釋詞》並非王引之所著的說法不可信。 第五、 我們將已經發表的論文分階段上載本計劃網頁，分享研究成果。 第六、 本計劃的階段性成果，將以《新見王念孫古籍校本研究》為題，由上海古籍出版社在2014年出版。

442310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
442310.value: 我們發表論文介紹各種校本的同時，對個別材料較為豐富的校本進行了逐條疏證的研究，比對《廣雅疏證》、《讀書雜志》等已經刊行的著作，同時參考前人對相關古籍的研究成果，藉此梳理王念孫的校改及校語。這方面的成果將由香港中文大學中國文化研究所劉殿爵中國古籍研究中心以「王念孫古籍校本集證」為題出版，並收入該中心「漢達叢書」系列。「集證」共有四冊，首冊《王念孫〈韓非子〉校本集證》將於2014年中旬出版。計劃的研究成果甚豐，證明了新材料在研究方法上開拓了新的方向。本計劃主持人在此期間，繼續收集遺稿，將範圍由王念孫兼及王引之，由校本擴闊至稿本、抄本，並進一步發現了更多的新材料。在本計劃的基礎上，我們在2012年向研究資助局(RGC)提出申請2013/14年度GRF計劃，開展全新的「王念孫、王引之稿本、抄本、校本研究計劃Research Project on the Manuscripts, Copies and Critical Editions of Wang Niansun and Wang Yinzhi」，並成功獲得撥款資助，新計劃(編號442113)將於2014年開始。

442410.label: Project Objectives
442410.value: To explore the extent and pattern of gambling in males and females among married couples in Hong Kong. To formulate a theoretical framework integrating the social mechanisms of control, strain, marital inequality, and the individual beliefs about traditional gender norms and gambling, so as to investigate the correlates of gambling among genders and their implications for gambling and deviance theories.

442410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
442410.value: Historically in the predominantly masculine domain, gambling is becoming a popular activity for woman. Like the West, Hong Kong has witnessed the narrowing of gender gap in gambling in general and problem gambling in particular. Most of the prevailing comparisons between genders in gambling behavior in both the local and international literature are confined to the treatment populations. Relatively little is known if the gender differences apply to the general population. Knowledge on social mechanisms and couple dynamics generating gambling behavior and its gender differences is even more meager. The proposed study will examine and compare the pattern and level of gambling among males and females of married couples in Hong Kong, and assess the strength of various sociological theories of deviance in explaining gender disparities in gambling. A theoretical framework incorporating various mechanisms of social control, social strain and inequality of marital power will be developed. Beliefs about traditional gender norms and gambling will also be included mediating variables. The model will advance the understanding of how the interactions between the broader social milieu, marital setting and individual mentality may shape the gambling behaviors of men and women. A cross-sectional community survey of married couples, both husbands and wives, of 1,620 households selected from a two-stage stratified clustered sampling will be undertaken. The total sample size will comprise 1,620 couples with 3,240 individual respondents. Respondents will be interviewed by an anonymous standardized questionnaire in the absence of their spouses. Dyad data derived from both partners of a couple will facilitate not only the gender comparison, but also a more recent, multilevel dyad analysis to take into account the couple dynamics in testing the explanatory model. 過去傳統視賭博為男性的活動，但賭博在現今女性當中也成了普遍的行為。像西方國家一樣，香港在一般賭博及問題賭博的性別差異上也呈逐漸縮窄的趨勢。大部分賭博行為性別比較的本地及海外文獻只分析治療群體，文獻所提出的性別差異研究結果能否反映社區一般群體的狀況則所知不多，而對有關影響賭博行為的社會性與配偶互動因素及其性別差異的認識更是缺乏。本研究旨在比較香港已婚配偶中男性與女性賭博的模式和程度，並以社會學越軌行為理論為骨杆，檢驗它們解釋賭博行為性別差異的效力。本研究所建立的理論模型引入多樣社會控制形式、壓力模式及婚姻不平等為主要預測變量，亦會包括對傳統性別規範和賭博的信念作為中介變量。此理論模型將提升對社會環境、婚姻處境與個人思維的相互作用及其對男性和女性賭博行為影響之理解。本研究採用已婚配偶(包括丈夫和妻子)的社區問卷調查設計，已婚配偶樣本來自由兩階段的分層、群集抽樣法選取的1,620個住户的已婚配偶，樣本總人數即合共3,240名被訪者。訪問以標準化、不記名問卷進行，且要求訪問期間另一配偶不在場。由夫妻兩者提供的成對資料不僅有助性別分析，並能應用近年始起的跨層成對二元體統計分析模型，令本研究理論模型深入掌握配偶互動性的影響(成對內和成對間的變化)。

442410.label: Realisation of objectives
442410.value: In order to achieve the two project objectives, we successfully conducted a territory-wide cross-sectional survey of Chinese married couples in Hong Kong. The questionnaire items included gambling behaviors, beliefs about gambling, social bonding, reintegrative/disintegrative shaming, gambling peers, various forms of social strain, spousal violence, coping strategies in response to strain, self-control, marital inequality, and beliefs about traditional gender norms. With respect to the sampling, a stratified-cluster random sample of households was selected on the basis of district area (New Territories, Kowloon, and Hong Kong Island) and type of housing (public housing and private housing). The sampling frame of households was obtained from the Census and Statistics Department of Hong Kong Government. For each area stratum, the two types of housing were identified, and then for each type of housing, we randomly selected 270 households. For each selected household, both husband and wife aged 21-50 were recruited for face-to-face interview using an anonymous standardized questionnaire. Formal data collection of the sampled married couples commenced in September 2011 and completed in September 2012. Given that our topic is sensitive and in order that confidentiality of data can be protected, the respondents were interviewed in their homes in the absence of spouse. If the absence of spouse could not be secured, they were invited to come to some venues outside home for interview. Altogether, our sample for quantitative analysis comprised 1,620 married dyads, that is, 3,240 individual respondents, from 1,620 households. Thus far, in addressing the two project goals, we have produced one journal manuscript and two conference presentations. These research outputs mainly (1) present gambling patterns between genders of married couples; (2) apply multilevel dyad modeling to show the relative impacts of the correlates of social bonding, gambling peers, various social strains, self-control, and the couple dynamics of between-partner social strain contagion on gambling pathology in males and females; and (3) and the consequences of gambling strain on couple violence. Our next outputs will work on how inequality in marital power, beliefs in traditional gender norms, reintegrative/disintegrative shaming, and the couple dynamics of these three constructs are related to gambling attitudes and behaviors in male and female spouses by utilizing multilevel dyad modeling.

442410.label: Major findings and research outcome
442410.value: (1) Gambling patterns (N. Cheung’s conference presentation 2013; N. Cheung’s journal paper 2014): - Problem gambling was significantly more pervasive in male partners than in female partners. The classification of gambling pathology is based on the DSM-IV problem gambling screen (scores ranging 0-10). Among male partners, only 26.8% were non-gamblers, whereas 73.2% gambled for money in the preceding year, of which 64.5% scored on the social gambling range (DSM-IV = 0-1), 6.2% on the at-risk gambling range (DSM-IV = 2-4), and 2.5% on the pathological gambling range (DSM-IV = 5 or above). Among female partners, 50.6% were non-gamblers, whereas 49.4% gambled in the past year, of which 47.5% were social gamblers, 1.7% were at-risk gamblers, and only 0.2% were pathological gamblers. - The most popular gambling activities for past-year gambling husbands were legal lotteries, (82.4%), followed by betting on horse racing through licensed gambling operator (47.1%) and mahjong (a Chinese form of gambling, 26.7%). Similarly, the most popular gambling activities for past-year gambling wives were legal lotteries (78%), followed by mahjong (28.8%). - Past-year gambling male and female partners gambled for virtually identical reasons, as 52% to 82% of them cited winning money, the pursuit of leisure and recreation, and testing luck as their primary reasons for gambling. (2) Specific gambling-related problems (N. Cheung’s journal paper 2014): - The DSM-IV problem gambling screen has ten criteria of pathological gambling, which involve preoccupation, tolerance, loss of control, withdrawal, escape, chasing, lies, illegal acts, risked job/education/relationship, and bailed out. In this study, chasing the loss of money gambling appeared to be the most common problem in both male and female gamblers. (3) Multivarite analysis of social strain, social bonding, and social learning correlates of gambling pathology in spouses (N. Cheung’s conference presentation 2013; N. Cheung’s journal paper 2014): - Male and female partners appeared to respond to different social strains in ways that affected their gambling pathology. Stressful life events in childhood/adolescence, household hassles stress, negative relations with offspring, negative relations with peers, and marital conflict were significant sources of strain for male partners, indicating that husbands who were strained through these forms tended to have a more severe level of gambling. For female partners, their exposure to failure to achieve job goals, household hassles stress, and stressful life events in childhood/adolescence were significantly and positively related to their gambling pathology. - Female partners were more affected by stress-specific negative affect than their male counterparts, as it had a significant positive association with gambling pathology only among female partners. - Concerning the social bonding measure, family support was associated with a lower likelihood of gambling pathology in male partners but not in female partners. - For the social learning measure, gambling peers were the strongest significant correlate of gambling pathology across male and female partners, suggesting that association with gambling peers increases the likelihood of severe gambling regardless of gender. (4) Multilevel dyad modeling of couple dynamics of social strain contagion (N. Cheung’s conference presentation 2013; N. Cheung’s journal paper 2014): - Both social strain and stress-specific negative affect encountered by male partner significantly increased his wife’s likelihood of at-risk or pathological gambling. There was also a significant positive relationship between female partner’s stress-specific negative affect and her husband’s gambling pathology, but no significant prediction of female partner’s social strain for her husband’s gambling pathology was observed. The impact of within-couple social strain contagion on gambling behavior was more pronounced in wives than husbands. (5) Effect of gambling strain on spousal violence (Y. Cheung’s conference presentation 2013): - Husbands’ exposure to financial strain due to gambling was not significantly related to husband-to-wife psychological and physical violence.

442410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
442410.value: The rate of pathological gambling is found to be far higher among male partners than in female partners in this cross-sectional study. Future research should introduce a longitudinal study of male gamblers, so as to track the possible changing patterns of their gambling behaviors and to reveal more vividly the social causes and the potential social consequences of their problem gambling. Furthermore, this study applies a dyad-level design to address inter-influence of couple interaction on individuals’ gambling behaviors. Such design can be extended to the treatment sample so as to substantiate how couple dynamics between non-gambling and treated gambling spouses may thwart or enable recovery from gambling problems.

442410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
442410.value: Historically in the predominantly masculine domain, gambling is becoming a popular activity for woman. Like the West, Hong Kong has witnessed the narrowing of gender gap in gambling in general and problem gambling in particular. Most of the prevailing comparisons between genders in gambling behavior in the local and international contexts are confined to the treatment populations. Little is known if the gender differences apply to the general populations. Knowledge on social mechanisms and couple dynamics generating gambling behavior and its gender differences is even more meager. This study represents the pioneer effort to examine the patterns of gambling among males and females of non-treatment, community-based married couples, and to look into various social correlates affecting gender differences in gambling. Findings of the study inform the gender-specific and couple-related gambling prevention and treatment strategies. In particular, our findings suggest that problem gambling is more prevalent in male partners relative to female partners in our Chinese sample, and wives’ gambling behaviors tend to be more affected by their husbands. Intervention should target not only different risk groups of gambling men and women, but also the couple setting that can amplify or reduce the risk of the partner drifting into gambling pathology.

443010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443010.value: This proposed project is an extension of my CUHK Direct Grant (2006-07) project which is focused on the Grand Universal Salvation Rituals (萬緣勝會) celebrated by the Cantonese Chinese in Penang and Singapore. The Ritual was a response to the late 19th and early 20th century anti-superstition movement in China. Instead of pacifying wandering ghosts annually in the lunar 7th moon, the Ritual which shared similar religious function was publicized as a memorial event and organized irregularly by public Institutions. It was adopted by the Cantonese migrants in Shanghai, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia since the 20th century. The Ritual was organized in Hong Kong until the 1960s and is still organized irregularly by the Cantonese Chinese institutions in the former British Strait Settlements, including Penang, Malacca and Singapore. This project will use an historical anthropological approach to reconstruct the history and current practices of the Ritual, from South China to Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. It aims to find out how the deaths are remembered or forgotten by the Chinese overseas from the late 19th century to present day. I shall further discuss how popular religion as a cultural resource facilitates the consolidation of an ethnic community and as a mechanism to solve ritual dilemma of the Overseas Chinese majority of whom cannot afford an ancestral hall to accommodate spirits of remote distance. Ritual is a living tradition, it demonstrates human creative genius, and it is a means of affirming cultural identity of the communities concerned. However, it also encounters rapid changes because of the process of modernization. The objectives of this project, therefore, are three: (1) To document the history of the Grand Universal Salvation Rituals in South China, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. (2) To establish a multi-media collection of these Rituals using digital device. (3) To understand the ritual foundation of Chinese cultural identities in the overseas. This project will produce: (1) A manuscript on the history of the Ritual, its practices and cultural meanings in South China, Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore. (2) A collection of documents, including reports written before the Second World War, religious texts and notices produced by the organizers and ritual experts. (3) An audio-visual databank to facilitate future studies. 本計畫嘗試比較在華南、香港和英國海峽殖民地的廣府人舉辦的萬緣勝會。萬緣勝會是地方社會對１９世紀末２０世紀初風起雲湧的反迷信運動的一種回應。傳統每年七月的安撫游魂野鬼的行為被視為迷信。因此，萬緣勝會雖然在功能上具備同一作用，但為公共團體詮析為紀念活動，並且不定期的舉行。萬緣勝會的很快的為廣府移民所採用。本計畫試圖以歷史人類學的研究方法，重組萬緣勝會從華南傳播到香港（迄１９６０年代仍然舉行）和前英國海峽殖民地的檳城、麻六甲和新加坡的歷史和變化。從而理解１９世紀末以來海外華人如何記憶或忘卻死者。本計畫並且希望進一步的討論作為文化資源的民間宗教如何幫助海外社群的整合，並且作為解決大部分不能歸葬故里或建立宗祖祠堂的海外華人群眾的儀式困境的工具。儀式是活的傳統。它宣示人類的創意，而且是確立社區文化認同的工具。然而，在現代化的過程中，儀式也無法避免的面對急激的變化。因此，本計畫希望達至的目的有三： (1) 紀錄在華南、香港和東南亞的萬緣勝會的歷史，(2) 紀錄當代舉行的儀式，從而(3)理解海外華人社會的文化認同的儀式基礎。

443010.label: Realisation of objectives
443010.value: This project proposed to study the Grand Universal Salvation Rituals celebrated by the Cantonese Chinese. It aims to document the history and development of the Rituals in South China, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia and to understand the ritual foundation of Chinese cultural identities in the overseas. The Grand Salvation Ritual was a response to the late 19th and early 20th century anti-superstition movement in southern China. Instead of pacifying wandering ghosts annually in the lunar 7th moon, the Ritual which shared similar religious function was publicized as a memorial event and organized irregularly by public Institutions. It was adopted by the Cantonese migrants in Shanghai, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia since the 20th century and is still organized by the Cantonese Chinese Institutions in the former British Straits Settlements, including Penang, Malacca and Singapore. In the process of our research, we learnt not only the history and diffusion processes of the ritual from the Pearl River Delta area to overseas Cantonese communities, we also realize the importance of understanding how the ritual is adopted and emulated by other Chinese dialect groups. We realized that (1) the ritual which is related to pacifying death spirits is closely related to how it is used by overseas Chinese as a tool to settle ancestral spirits in their adopted home country and that (2) ideologies such as the “anti-superstition” in the early 20th century and the “intangible cultural heritage” in the late 20th century play an important role in modifying and standardizing the practices. To accomplish the task, we conducted extensive library and archival searches on reports published in newspapers and qiao kan (bulletins published in the emigrant communities) and In-depth field researches. From 2010 to 2013 the PI and his assistant observed and documented a total of 112 salvations and produced a total of more than 4000GB digital records. The PI and his assistant has published five articles, compiled two manuscripts with analytical articles, produced two internet video series, presented their findings in nine conferences (including four in English) and nine public lectures. The PI is also preparing a book manuscript on the Grand Salvation ritual which will be completed by the end of 2014 after observing the once every ten year Jiu Li Dong salvation ritual which is organized in Aug. 2014 in Singapore.

443010.label: Major findings and research outcome
443010.value: We have published five articles, compiled two manuscripts with analytical articles, produced two internet video series, presented findings in nine conferences (including four in English) and nine public lectures. PI is preparing a book manuscript. These articles can be divided into three categories: History and development of the ritual (8.1, 8.6, 8.8, 9.3, 9.4, 9.6): The Grand Salvation Ritual, a new type of spiritual cult that emphasized commemoration (Ji Nian) and engaged priests, monks, and Taoists from institutional monasteries, was “invented” in the urban sector of Southern China and was quickly adopted by the rural population. By the beginning of the 20th century, it was then adopted by the Chinese overseas. This ritual was adapted and interpreted differently by the Chinese in different Southeast Asian countries. For instance, in Penang, Malaysia the ritual was held whenever there was exhumation of a substantial number of unattended graves. It served to forestall any unattended ancestors becoming wandering spirits. In Singapore, from the 1980s when the Cantonese Peck Shan Theng ceased management of their cemetery, there was no necessity to evacuate unattended graves and hence no concern about releasing wandering spirits. The ritual however, continued to be performed periodically once every five years. The main purpose of the ritual has changed from pacifying unattended spirits to commemoration of ancestors. Comparative ethnographies (8.2, 8.4, 8.5, 8.7, 9.9): most of the articles are based on detailed ethnographies. We compared different types of salvation rituals celebrated in different communities. We pointed out that the local government policies as well as changes in the macro-environment determined how the festival was run. In Shantou, for instance, in the late 19th century, it was related to the development of trade. In Kobe, Japan, the changes were responding to immigration and naturalization policies as well as the notion of intangible cultural heritage. Theory (8.3,8.8,9.1,9.2,9.7, 9.8): I have implemented Arthur Wolf’s “God-Ghost-Ancestor” spectrum by arguing that the Salvation ritual is introduced as a “ritual charity” by changing the unattended spirits into collective ancestors. This is especially important for the overseas Chinese as “collective ancestors” are taken care by associations. I also argued that, unlike B.E. Ward’s conscious model, contemporary ethnic boundaries were not conferred by the imperial state but are result of long term process involving people’s narration of their own history, their ritual practices, and their emulation of their neighbors’ ways of living.

443010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443010.value: Ritual is a living experience. Historical records of Salvation Ritual are scattered and memories of old folks are fading out rapidly. The meaning and practices of the ritual have also been adjusted according to different times, places and social groups. Systematic documentation of the Ritual, now and then, is therefore essential for future studies and comparison. This project collected two groups of important source materials that are essential for further research development: (1) the primary sources, including newspaper reports, bulletins, notices and ritual scripts which are not available in local libraries and (2) the ethnographies which recorded detailed contemporary ritual activities in various Chinese communities. If funding is allowed, the large quantity of data collected could be published and put on-line for a wider readership. Salvation rituals organized by the Chinese overseas is closely related to how the Chinese mange spirits of their ancestors. It is also a festival representing the community. This project serves as a foundation for the understanding of cultural hybrdity and emulation through comparative studies of overseas Chinese communal festivals. The PI is applying for the CRF under the title “Reenacting “cultural China” in the twentieth century: communal festivals in emigrant and overseas Chinese communities”.

443010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443010.value: This project applied historical and anthropological methodologies in the study of Chinese rituals and popular religion with focuses on the Salvation Ritual. It studied the history of the Ritual and how it was adopted and transformed in the overseas Chinese communities. The PI and his assistant conducted in-depth participant observation and library research in the Pearl River Delta, Hong Kong and the former British Straits Settlements. They produced a source book, an edited volume on ethnographies, 5 articles, two internet talk series (a total of seven 30 minutes episodes) and presented 9 conference papers and 9 public lectures. Their research covered a period from the late 19th century to the 21st century, and a wide spatial area from South China to Hong Kong and East and Southeast Asia. This project is a detailed and multi-disciplinary study using a particular ritual to illustrate the complexity between cultural and social factors. It complements the cultural diffusion theory and provides a comparative perspective in the study of Chinese popular religion. The data collected by the investigators are invaluable and will benefit many scholars who are interested in the study of rituals and festivals in emigrant and overseas Chinese communities.

443310.value: 領導-部屬關係、心理賦權和創造力：工作部門結構的權變作用

443310.label: Project Objectives

443310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443310.value: Given the importance of creativity in organizations, there is growing interest in better understanding how and under what conditions leaders can stimulate creative work performance among employees. The project proposed herein will investigate the complex relationships among leader-member exchange (LMX), empowerment, and the work-unit structure, as well as how they interact with one another to enhance creativity. Leaders can have a significant impact on capitalizing the creative potential of subordinates and enhancing their self-efficacy, which, in turn, promotes creativity. A high-quality LMX is characterized by respect, affect, contribution, and loyalty, thus allowing subordinates better access to additional information, resources, and opportunities. Moreover, it has a close relationship with emotional support and encouragement, which are conducive to the level of comfort and trust necessary for creativity. Thus, a high-quality LMX is expected to be directly linked to the creative performance of employees. To encourage creativity, leaders need to empower their followers and provide them with intrinsic motivation. Leaders play a vital role in empowering their subordinates by granting them the autonomy and discretion necessary to carry out challenging work, expressing confidence in their work, fostering a participative climate, and offering opportunities for growth and development. Empowered employees are, in turn, more likely to exert the extra effort needed to generate creative ideas. The creative work outcomes of LMX quality may be indirectly derived through the intrinsically motivating experience of psychological empowerment. Therefore, empowerment is expected to mediate the relationship between LMX and creativity. The organizational context contributes significantly to employees’ creative performance at work. Effective leaders foster a working environment that is conducive to creative work. Organic structures provide a facilitative context for psychological empowerment and employee creativity, whereas mechanistic structures provide a constraining context. We plan to examine the moderating role played by the work-unit structure on LMX’s indirect effect on creativity. The proposed study will also examine the mediated moderation process through which LMX affects employee creativity. More specifically, psychological empowerment is expected to mediate the relationship between LMX and creativity, and the work-unit structure is expected to moderate the indirect effect of LMX on creativity (through psychological empowerment), such that the mediated effect is stronger for organic structures than for mechanistic structures. Theoretically, the proposed study will advance our understanding of the mechanism between LMX and creative performance. Practically, it will offer managerial guidelines for nurturing and empowering subordinates and fostering a creative workplace environment. 本研究通過有仲介的調節過程檢驗領導-部屬關係對員工創造力的影響。領導成員交換通過心理賦權的仲介效應對創造力產生影響。同時，工作部門的結構調節領導成員交換對創造力的間接作用：心理賦權的仲介作用在有機式結構比在機械式結構中更強。理論上，本研究加深領導成員交換對創造力的影響機制的理解。 實踐上，本文為如何培養和授權下屬、營造有創造力的工作環境提供了指引。

rows: The main aims of the proposed project are to develop a model that strengthens our current understanding of the relationship between LMX and creative performance, as well as the mechanism of empowerment and the contextual factors that enhance that relationship. Its more specific objectives are:
to investigate the extent to which LMX is related to creative performance
to examine the mediating effect of psychological empowerment on the LMX-creativity relationship
to investigate the moderating effect of the work-unit structure on the indirect relationship between LMX and creativity through psychological empowerment

443310.label: Major findings and research outcome
443310.value: This study proposed and tested an integrated model in which high-quality LMX relationship can exert influences over both employee psychological empowerment and felt obligation that lead to creativity. The processes may be enhanced or inhibited by the work-unit structure. The results of our data reveal that (i) motivation-oriented psychological empowerment and social exchange-oriented felt obligation fully mediates the relationship between LMX and employee creativity, and (ii) work-unit structure moderates the indirect effect of LMX on creativity through psychological empowerment, such that the mediated effect of LMX is stronger in organic than in mechanistic work-unit structure. In other words, LMX can enhance employee creativity completely through psychological empowerment and felt obligation, and (2) the indirect effect of LMX on creativity through psychological empowerment is facilitated in the organic work unit, but inhibited in the mechanic work unit. Results from the present study reveal intervening variables (employee’s felt obligation to perform creatively) that help account for the complex relationship between LMX and creativity to better explain how LMX leads to creativity at work. The findings indicate that relationship with supervisors can influence employee creativity through motivation-oriented psychological empowerment and social exchange-oriented felt obligation. That is, LMX can affect employee creativity through psychological empowerment and felt obligation. LMX plays an important role in stimulating a high level of employee creativity by simultaneously enhancing employee psychological empowerment and felt obligation. To increase subordinates’ creativity, supervisors should provide them with the necessary support including information, resources, authority, verbal encouragement, and consideration of subordinate’s personal well-being. Leaders should know that employee creativity is boosted if their psychological empowerment is increased. Our research results also support that organic structure facilitates the mediating effect of psychological empowerment on employee creativity. The finding suggests that the features of organic structures provide a facilitative context for psychological empowerment and creativity whereas those of mechanistic structures provide a constraining context for the effect of psychological empowerment on creativity. The strength of the mediated relationship between LMX and creativity through psychological empowerment varied depending on work-unit structure, and the indirect effect of LMX is stronger in organic than in mechanistic structure. When empowered employees work in organic structure, the effect of their psychological empowerment is reinforced by the work-unit structure, leading to stronger employee creativity. The research results do not support the mediating effect of felt obligation is stronger in organic than in mechanic work-unit structure.

443310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443310.value: Based on the foundation of this study, two projects on empowering leadership and employee creativity will be conducted in future research direction.

443310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443310.value: This study contributes to the literature in developing a framework by integrating the motivation-oriented psychological empowerment and social exchange-oriented felt obligation in explaining the leader-member exchange (LMX)-creativity relationship and the boundary condition of work-unit structure for the mediated effects of LMX on creativity. It extends previous LMX literature by investigating how to motivate employees to engage in creativity and how to make employees feel obligated to put efforts in creativity. The framework enables a better overview of the process through which LMX impact on creativity. The study of the process by applying multi-level approach captures the rich and complex social context in which the mediating relationship is developed. The current study responds to the call for expanding the range of contextual variables examined that might affect the incidence of employee creativity at work. Work unit structure serves as a moderator that either facilitates or restricts the mediated effects of LMX on employee creativity. It offers new insights on how leaders nurture employee creativity through motivating employees and designing work- unit structure. Results shed new light on the LMX-creativity research and provide primary work for future research to further explore why and how LMX influences employee creativity.

443510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443510.value: In the summer of 2009, teenage delinquency has sparked a new wave of concerns in Hong Kong. It is ‘new’ in a sense that girls are made the center of attention. Sex, drugs, violence and teenage pregnancy present a group of troubled and troublesome girls in media. Instead of being the causes of various social ills, these young girls could, however, be the products of some other notable phenomena. The ubiquity of slimming advertisements, the never-ending calls for consumption and the saturation of mass media in everyday lives are all contributing to a drastically different social environment for today teens. This new social landscape is filled with competing discourses in issues related to sex and gender. Adolescence is a transition period marked with changes and uncertainties. The onset of sexual maturity is an overwhelming experience, which will have deep significance for the teenagers’ views of themselves and others. For teenage girls, while changes in their bodies are seemingly biological in nature, their physical appearances often fall into the gaze of others. Whether girls welcome it or not, female bodies are often turned into objects of desire in the consumer culture. Growing up female is also a social, cultural and ideological matter. Media are certainly one of the forces shaping teenage bodies. In fact, media are also highly gendered. In recent years, there sees a proliferation of gender-related terms created and popularized by mass media. ‘Kong Girls’ (or Gang Nu，港女) is used to describe girls who are greedy, materialistic, naïve and narcissistic. While ‘teen models’ or ‘pseudo models’ (0靚模) appear to be a kind of modeling work, the negative connotations have made them a cause for moral panic and a target of criticism The study centers on two questions: How are teenage bodies gendered in, and gendered by, Hong Kong media? To answer these questions, the study will examine the production and consumption of media. It will identify the forces at work in the production of desire, subjectivities and media labels. It also asks how teenage girls think about (opinions) and feel about (feelings) such media products, and how they perceive their bodies and negotiate their identities in the consumption practices. Instead of seeing teenage girls at risk, or reducing it to another moral panic, the proposed research aims to produce findings that can lead to intervention work in media education and sex education. 近年，媒介上出現愈來愈多「問題少女」，當中有人未婚懷孕、有人參與援交、校園欺凌、吸毒販毒。社會關注青少年問題，除了思索對應策略，亦要探尋問題成因。少女作為社會問題，卻同時是特定社會文化的「製成品」。今天的青少年在成長階段，通過無孔不入的媒介，接觸大量縱情消費、瘦身纖體的信息，其中不乏對性、性別角色、性別意識的論述。媒介對青少年的影響，持續成為大眾關心的課題。 青少年時期本來就充滿了轉變和種種不確定性，身體發育是其中一個最深刻及影響深遠的改變。在一個擅於把女性身體打造成慾望對象和商品的消費社會，少女的身體轉變，卻不僅是個人的事，不管少女是否願意，她們的身體往往成為被注視的對象，甚至是各種力量對壘爭持的戰場，而媒介正是其中一股重要力量。媒介不但參與「再現」女性，近年更生產和普及了不少加諸在香港女性身上的標籤，例如漸被等同為貪心、拜金、無知又自戀的「港女」，形象負面的「0靚模」，經常被嘲弄、鞭撻和批評。媒介上充滿了對女性矛盾的論述，似乎不論高矮肥瘦、品行好壞，女性都很容易變為並品評和標籤的對象。 基於這些發展，本研究旨在解答兩大問題：1)香港媒介如何呈現和論述青少年(特別是青少女)的身體？2) 媒介如何通過他們的報道和創作，生產符合某些性別特質的青少年身體？研究同時聚焦於媒介的生產和消費兩方面，包括探討慾望、主體性和媒體標籤的生產過程，亦會著眼青少女如何評論媒體的表現，以及她們的主觀感受和實質的消費習慣。研究結果可望協助發展和設計相關的傳媒教育和性教育課程。

443510.label: Realisation of objectives
443510.value: The project aimed at identifying relationships between youth gender identities and gender-related labels in Hong Kong media. It examined both the production and consumption of these gender-related media labels, with reference to three notable examples including Lang Mo (teenage models), Kong Girls (Hong Kong girls) and Shengnu (leftover single women). The first two objectives are mainly about media representation and production. This research conducted two separate studies which examined how women being labeled as Lang Mo was represented in photo books in the first place, and how news discourses depicted them in the second. Due to time constraints, this project could focus mainly on the case of teenage models. Another study focusing on the construction of Shengnu in reality television is still ongoing. Considering that teenage models constituted a major example here, it is estimated that both objectives 1 and 2 are largely addressed. In view of the aspect of consumption, two methods were used in addressing objectives 3 and 4. A territory-wide survey of 920 secondary school students in Hong Kong was conducted in late 2011, resulting in a rich set of data that included general opinions, attitudes and feelings of teenagers about media labels, media performance and their general media use. The survey also covered questions on self-image of the youth. These data provided much data for identifying meaningful patterns in media consumption and its relationships with the production of desires and subjectivities among the young generation. In addition to this data set, the study also conducted six focus group interviews with two groups of teenage girls and one group of teenage boys. The findings provided ample data and native perspectives for analysis. They contributed much to our understanding of the preferences and grievances about media among teenagers. In view of the tight time-frame of this study, it is considered that these objectives were satisfactorily addressed at this stage. For the last two objectives, they are mainly about further theorization and design of relevant education frameworks. Since the rich and varied findings are yet to be fully analyzed, these two objectives are not met to the full at this stage. Instead of being perceived as under-achievements, however, they indicate meaningful and useful directions for future research in both youth and gender studies. It is particularly so for objective 7 which calls for long-term planning for possible intervention in education.

443510.label: Major findings and research outcome
443510.value: Two papers have been accepted by two SSCI-journals, with one focusing on sexualities research and another on youth studies. Five presentations related to this research were made in four conferences in the past two years. The findings in the one of the peer-reviewed journal publications looked into how media producers collaborated with teenage models and the readers in the production of erotica. It analyzed over 2000 photos of teenage models who claimed to sell ‘sexiness’, and identified how the set of erotic pictures was characterized by three distinctive features. First, they emphasized a look of innocence that suggested purity, fragility, and delicacy. Second, albeit being sexy and desirable, the girls were often presented as if they were unaware of the sexiness. The implication was that their sexiness was unintentional and thus the girls were not to blame. Finally, a sense of intimacy was purposefully built between the models and readers by constituting a direct gaze and presenting models as ordinary girls-next-door. All these echoed the emphasis of female chastity in Chinese culture. It was found that in Hong Kong, where sexuality issues often provoke debates, the producers of sexy images have benefited from media controversies. Teenage bodies were used to fuel the imagination of curious customers. In another peer-reviewed journal article, the focus was on how the youth perceived two emergent gender-related labels in Hong Kong. It examined how the young population defined and negotiated the meanings of two media labels, Kong Girls (Hong Kong Girls) and Lang Mo (teenage models), which have become a part of daily usage. Moving beyond the debates about misrepresentations in the media, the paper discussed the functions and influences of stereotypes. Despite the youth in study were aware of the circulation of gender labels in media, they did not necessarily take the negative views.To the contrary, there was a marked indifference about these media representations. It was notable that social media played a far more crucial role in shaping gender attitudes. This study also resulted in five conference presentations. They presented major findings that are further developed into journal papers. In a nutshell, they were mainly about the major production mechanisms in use in media representations. In a study about ‘connectivity and prosumption’, the focus was on the new media use patterns of the young generation. The findings raised questions about media literacy programmes in the midst of all these emerging trends in communication.

443510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443510.value: The present study has renewed our understanding of the latest production strategies of media in gender representation. It has also found some emerging patterns of media use among the youth. Future research should ask more specific questions about how such media production strategies are influenced by other social and cultural factors, and whether and how alternative media production is possible to combat the monolithic representation of women in Hong Kong media. This study has inspired two related areas of research. Firstly, with reference to the notions of habitus and embodiment of Bourdieu, a paper in progress is now focusing on the intricate relationships between youth, their gendered beliefs and their media use. Secondly, explorations are to be made so that media and gender education materials can be developed out of these updated findings. Both will continue to address the objectives 6 and 7 stated in the original proposal.

443510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443510.value: The prevalence of mass media has always prompted one to ask: what are their effects or influences on us, especially the “impressionable minds”? This study aimed to answer this question by considering a specific media phenomenon. In recent years, Hong Kong witnessed the birth and circulation of a few gender-related labels in popular media. These labels often contained pejorative and negative meanings against women. Lang Mo, a colloquial expression referring to teenage models, was directly related to teenagers with a sexual undertone. The research project examined how and why media producers chose to represent women as such. It was found that they actually played with societal expectations and cultural norms in order to maximize their profit in selling teenage bodies. The research also looked into how the young generation responded to these images of women. Findings suggested that media were not as all powerful as one expected. The youth negotiated the meanings of these media labels with cynicism and indifference. Social media was clearly playing an increasingly important role. To conclude, the study has contributed to an updated understanding about the complicated dynamics between media producers and consumers in upholding and changing stereotypical gender beliefs in Hong Kong.

443610.label: Project Objectives
443610.value: To demonstrate the central role architecture plays in giving physical and spatial dimensions to 'memory' and the construction of 'place' by thematic and interdisciplinary analysis. To collect basic data on representative 'commemorative spaces' in Japan, and begin to delineate a more complete picture of how the scope and character of commemorative spaces have developed and transformed in relation to its socio-cultural contexts. To analyze the case of Japan and use it as an exemplar to highlight the problematics and paradoxes regarding commemoration in East Asia. To gain a deeper appreciation of how Yasukuni and Hiroshima are situated within the public discourse on war commemoration in Japan by interpreting their architecture vis-a-vis mechanisms of contemporary social memory. To enhance research output by presenting a conference paper, and preparing a book chapter manuscript, and preparations for a future teaching course on the topic.

443610.label: Major findings and research outcome
443610.value: The research examined Japanese commemorative space via the theme of “Myth of Peaceful Country”, as interpreted through the two case studies in question. The contrived peacefulness of Tokyo’s Yasukuni Shrine is integrally connected to the Kudan topography and the Imperial Palace grounds, an apparently vacuous nucleus observed by Roland Barthes which can now be thought of not as empty, but as “mighty full”, the centre in which the shadow of Japanese imperial authority continues to reside and from which the deep-seated spell of the emperor cult radiates. Kudan’s commemorative landscape on which the host of postwar memorial buildings sit, which extends to Kitanomaru and the Imperial palace, is therefore structured by a very precise urban order, an inescapable axis generated by what Marc Bourdier termed the “tennocratic” system” (from tenno as emperor). Ultimately, Yasukuni’s setting within Kudan’s urban form needs to be situated with respect to this “national axis of commemoration” (From Yasukuni’s disused ShokonSaitei, spirit-summoning grounds, through the axis of the National Cemetery for the War Dead’s Hexagon Hall, to the Kusunoki Masashige statue in Plaza before the Imperial Palace - discovery by PI) one that orientates as it mystifies in the midst of encircling traffic, but one that continues to embody the paradox of “Peaceful Country” in ever more unarticulated, serene form. The “Peace” of Hiroshima, if treated as heroic testimony, as perpetual absence of conflict at any price, or as future-oriented well-being, is seemingly beyond controversy. If however, one reflects on the more profound ethics fo peace found, for example in Shinto/Buddhist enlightenment, or the Judeo-Christian Peace of God that locates the highest peacefulness beyond everyday material reckoning, then both the annual Peace Ceremony’s commemorative silence through its perfunctory ceremonialism that is coordinated to through the abstract, pristine form of the Peace Memorials architecture and urban landscape, and the annual Hiroshima Flower Festival’s carnivalesque energy amount to a confusion or disorientation between roots and renewal (using history and morality as the basis of regeneration instead of references to universal tranditions of the natural-divine realms) characteristic of secular modernity. Importantly, the variously mediated re-enactments through Hiroshima’s narrative and concrete spatiality (eg. A-bomb victims recounting, recording and reliving their experiences, or guided mnemonic derives encouraging people to discover alternative sites of conflict and inclusive commemoration) will open up the potential for a better participation and genuine understanding of history and renewal beyond the peace but contrived afterlife of Hiroshima.

443610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443610.value: The integrated research approach on architecture and memory developed through this project is already being applied, extended and refined in another ongoing GRF project (443611: Mapping Urban Culture in Hong Kong) which deals with memory, architecture and urban transformation with respect to the filmic imagination. The intention is to prepare for future research proposals based on similar topics of commemorative space and memoryscapes, but rather than scrutinizing issues of nationalism and regional politics abroad, the focus will be on local Hong Kong and Chinese sites and the emphasis on the everyday vernacular of urban culture. Knowledge gained from this project has informed the course curriculum of the CUHK Social Science Faculty course “Understanding Cities” that has been newly developed by the PI. The PI will seek to integrate research findings within his current teaching; and rather than aiming to start a new course from scratch, the PI will evolve his teaching together with research topics simultaneously to maximize on potential synergies.

443610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443610.value: The research studied how the idea of commemoration (how people remember important events) connects with architecture and the built environment and everyday life, by looking at two controversial examples in Modern Japan. Tokyo’s Yasukuni Shrine and its compound seems to quite peaceful in an everyday context to an outsider. However, if you study the commemorative landscape more carefully, a series of postwar memorial buildings extending from the shrine to the Imperial Palace creates a precise urban order based on the silent imperial authority and emperor cult. There is a “national axis of commemoration” extending from Yasukuni to the Imperial Palace through symbolically important places that continues the paradox of “Peaceful Country”. At Hiroshima, “international peace” surrounds the annual Peace Ceremony, held within the Peace Memorial park with its pristine memorial architecture and urban landscape. Or there is the carnival-like annual Flower Festival held across the city. But both, like the neutral architecture seem to be banal and flat. However, the many ways people talk and relive their experiences or visit actual sites of conflict and disaster will open up the potential for a better participation and genuine understanding of history and renewal beyond the peaceful but contrived afterlife of Hiroshima.

443710.label: Project Title(Chinese)
443710.value: 非消費期的消費者偏好變化研究

443710.label: Project Objectives
443710.value: We aim to understand the evolution of consumer preference over periods of time when they do not consume a product or experience. We examine the joint effects of consumer need and consumer inference making on consumer preference toward a product or experience. Through our analyses of the relation between consumption pattern and consumer preference, we hope to derive managerial insights for marketers to design effective marketing strategies to better meet consumers’ need and increase sales and profits. From individual consumers’ perspective, this may help improve their well-being.

We examine the joint effects of consumer need and consumer inference making on consumer preference toward a product or experience.

Through our analyses of the relation between consumption pattern and consumer preference, we hope to derive managerial insights for marketers to design effective marketing strategies to better meet consumers’ need and increase sales and profits. From individual consumers’ perspective, this may help improve their well-being.

443710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443710.value: In the proposed project, we seek to understand how the absence of consuming a product or experience affects consumer preference over time, which is a relatively unexplored area in the study of preference construction and intertemporal dynamics of preference. We propose that two processes jointly affect the relation between non-consumption duration and consumer preference. The first process is the development of need over a period of non-consumption. The longer one has not consumed a product (or experience), the greater the need one feels for it. As a consequence, his/her liking for that product or experience increases over time of non-consumption. On the other hand, one may infer from the (long vs. short) duration of non-consumption that s/he does not like the product that much. Thus, need state and the inference of liking from non-consumption jointly impact the patterns of preference over time. We further propose that 1) contextual cues at the point of judgment, such as the physical presence (versus absence) of alternatives, and 2) subjective characteristics, such as consumers’ propensity to make inferences, moderate the effect of non-consumption duration on consumer preference. These factors impact the relation between non-consumption periods and consumer preference by affecting the degree of inference consumers make. The project will contribute to the marketing and consumer decision making literature by providing the first systematic analysis of the effect of non-consumption on consumer preference. In addition, it could contribute to various bodies of knowledge such as consumer inference making, self perception theory, and other theories in constructive view of preferences. From a practical perspective, our research will help marketers design more effective marketing programs to provide better services to consumers and ultimately increases sales and profits. 現存關於偏好動態變化的理論大部分研究的是重復消費對消費者偏好的影響。本研究着重于系統研究非消費期長短對消費者偏好的影響，從而填補這個領域的空缺。 我們提出兩個心理過程聯合作用決定了非消費期長短對消費者偏好的影響。第一個心理過程是基於我們的需求(need)。一種產品我們越長時間沒有消費，我們對它的需求越高，喜歡程度也越高。比如説，跟短時間相比，我們長時間沒吃飯就更喜歡食物。這個過程導致偏好隨著非消費期變長而上升。另外一個過程基於我們的推理過程。根據自我感知理論（Bem,1972）,人會通過觀察自己的行爲來推測自己對某樣東西的態度。隨著非消費期的變長，人們越來越會認爲之所以自己這麽久沒有消費這個產品，是因爲自己不太喜歡它。這樣一個通過觀察自己行爲的推理過程會導致偏好非消費期變長而下降。因此，非消費期長短對消費者偏好的影響取決於上述的哪個心理過程更加強烈。 在本研究中，我們提出：1）偏好判斷時的環境因素，比如其它可選消費品的物理存在，以及2）消費者的主觀特點，比如對推理的偏好，會系統地影響以上提及的兩個心理過程的重要性。這些因素對非消費期對消費者偏好影響的作用是通過影響消費者的推理過程而達到的。 本研究通過對非消費期對消費者偏好影響的系統研究，將會極大促進市場營銷及消費者決策研究領域對相關問題的理解。從商業實務的角度來看，它能夠幫助公司設計更好的營銷方案來滿足消費者的需求的動態變化。

443710.label: Realisation of objectives
443710.value: We have conducted a series of studies tested the hypotheses we stated in the proposal. Now we have much better understanding of the effects of non-consumption lengths on the evolution of consumer preference, and how they interact with contextual information at the point of judgments and decisions. For example, for the first objective “to understand the evolution of consumer preference over periods of time when they do not consume a product or experience,” based on our experiment result, we could give a clear answer. For the second objective “We examine the joint effects of consumer need and consumer inference making on consumer preference toward a product or experience,” we also systematically examined the circumstances under which contextual cues (such as presence of substitutes) could affect inferences consumers make and its impact on preference construction. In terms of implications, our research findings could directly inform research in intertemporal choices. Research on temporal preferences typically controlled for the lengths of past non-consumption and focused on choice between smaller-sooner and larger-later rewards. Our model suggests the length of the non-consumption period prior to making intertemporal choice matters and can affect temporal preference and discounting rates by changing the preference for an item that is available for present or future consumption. More generally, the study of preference based on non-consumption suggests consumers learn about their preferences by thinking about what they have not consumed. Given changing trends and fashions and the reintroduction of consumer products every several years (e.g., fashion trends making a comeback), this research can shed light on what makes consumers welcome old favorites and see them as nostalgic, and what makes consumers, at other times, reject these products as “old fashioned.”

443710.label: Major findings and research outcome
443710.value: How does non-consumption shape consumer preference? In this proposal we suggest the length of the non-consumption period and the presence of salient alternatives when making a preference judgment jointly determine consumer preference. In the absence of salient alternatives, non-consumption increases longing for the unconsumed item and increases preference. However, the presence of salient alternatives suggests new tastes have developed. Then non-consumption decreases longing for an item and decreases preference. a series of experiments support this model across non-consumption of products (e.g., food), experiences (e.g., culture), and specific social interactions. Our findings further have implications for how longing and preference are construed, situationally determined, and rather flexible. The outcome of this proposal is a paper in the review process at the Journal of Consumer Research (invited revision). Meanwhile we also used the fund to support several related projects, some of the papers have already been published (see the Part C).

443710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443710.value: We are optimistic that the findings in this project will inspire future research to more systematically study 1) how non-action affects motivation and preferences construction, and 2) how contextual cues affects inference and consequence preference construction at the point of judgment. We will continue to work in this very field and generate more research outcomes that could contribute to the theories of preference construction and intertemporal choices in particular, and decision making processes in general.

443710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443710.value: Understanding preference is critical to the study of decision making. This project systematically studies how preferences change as a function of time if people's regular consumption is temporally unavailable. We find that if people do not think about substitutes when making these judgments, the longer is this period of time, the stronger they miss and desire for the consumption; whereas if people think about substitutes when making these judgments, the longer is this period of time, the weaker they miss and desire for the consumption. These findings suggest the circumstances under which the time of non-consumption has opposite impact on people's preference and desire. It further suggests specific ways for marketers to optimize their marketing strategies in facing with consumers' non-consumption period.

443910.label: Project Objectives
443910.value: (1) Examine whether or not firms employ accounting opacity as a mechanism to attenuate the outflow of proprietary information regarding the firms’ research and development activities. (2) Investigate whether or not managers’ incentives to use opacity to protect proprietary information varies, depending on the level of property rights protections across different regions. (3) Examine the impacts of accounting opacity on firm value, conditioning on the demand for protecting proprietary information.

443910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443910.value: We examine the association between the attributes of accounting numbers, information disclosures, and aspects of the institutional environment in which firms operate. Specifically, we explore how property rights protections across different regions in China affect the flow of proprietary information, and thus managers’ incentives to disclose details of financial and operational performance. In particular, we focus on research and development (R&D) spillovers as a proxy for information leakage to competitors, and investigate whether or not opacity is employed as a mechanism to attenuate such leakage. In doing so, we provide new insights as to institutional factors that influence disclosure policies, and the costs and benefits of information disclosure. We also contribute to the work examining agency problems between managers and outside stakeholders, and how aspects of the legal system affect accounting disclosures to parties outside the firm.

443910.label: Major findings and research outcome
443910.value: We find that accounting opacity is associated with lower firm value. However, once we endogenize the effects of protection of proprietary information, the relationship between opacity and performance disappears. These findings are consistent with our hypotheses, and are robust to various sensitivity tests. Our paper is accepted for publication by Emerging Markets Review. In a second paper, we find that 1) uncompensated spillovers are greater in regions with weaker property rights, 2) such spillovers are associated with lower R&D expenditures, and 3) the latter is exacerbated in low property rights regimes. The paper is accepted by Journal of Multinational Financial Management.

443910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443910.value: We are searching for research and development expenditure data with detailed break down of expenditure types. This will allow us to investigate whether property right protection matter most to certain stage of research and development.

443910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443910.value: The opacity of publicly traded companies in China has a lot to do with institional weakness. When the law and the government do not provide suitable protection of proprietary information which is critical for research intensive firms, firms will underinvest in research and development while focusing more on immitating others' ideas.

444010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444010.value: Like personality traits, personal values have multiple dimensions. Personality profiles have been widely used to describe individual characteristics or predict individual behaviors, employee training outcomes, and personal development. And yet, most researchers examining the influence of personal values on attitudes or behaviors have used single dimensions that neglect the complex nature of value structures (Nonis & Swift, 2001). The few studies that have examined personal value profiles (the configuration of different values) have not established valid profiles that can be used for predicting employment-related outcomes. The proposed research study is designed to: (1) investigate personal value profiles using an innovative method; (2) examine how values profiles change over time; (3) explore factors that may cause changes in values; and (4) examine whether determinants of changes in values vary depending on the socio-economic context, i.e., Hong Kong versus Mainland China. Because values are “a product of the culture” (Parsons & Shills, 1951), we argue that there is a need to develop an indigenous Chinese values instrument that addresses the limitations of the widely used Schwartz Value Survey (SVS; Schwartz, 1992, 1994) and other Chinese values instruments (e.g., Chinese Culture Connection, 1987). We have conducted preliminary work to develop a Chinese Values Survey (Yu, Fu & Liu, 2009) and have sought to identify personal values profiles among Chinese on the basis of cross-sectional data collected over the past three years (N=2088). The proposed study is the second stage in the instrument validation that tests the predictive validity of values profiles for employment-related outcomes. Hence, we aim to meet the four research objectives stated above using longitudinal data from a targeted sample of 700 new employees and their supervisors. In addition, the results of the proposed study will serve as the basis for future research on the use of values profiles for various purposes, including employee recruitment, career development, leadership training, and so forth. This study will be of interest to both practitioners and academics because the results will provide a more systematic explanation and prediction of differences in individual work attitudes and motivations. Further, this project will provide knowledge about factors that change personal values profiles that will provide insights to the development of individual leaders as well as organizations in Hong Kong, Mainland China and beyond. (375W) 个体的人生价值观是人们做选择或评价时采用的标准。这种标准基于不同的价值取向之间的权衡，而非某单一价值取向，因此它和人的性格类别一样，应该有不同的价值观组合来理解价值观对人的行为、态度的影响。但是迄今为止，绝大多数价值观的研究都是在单个的导向基础上进行的，限制了我们对价值观的作用的了解。本研究的目的有4个方面：1）用非传统的方法验证人的价值观的不同组合；2）检验不同的价值观组合是否会随着时间的转移或环境的变化而变化；3） 探索可能导致价值观组合发生变化的各种原因；4）检验导致价值观组合发生变化的因素是否会受社会-经济环境影响。 我们认为价值观是“文化的产物，”由西方学者开发的量表不一定能够准确地反映中国人的价值观。在过去三年里，我们用本土化方式开发了一个测量中国人的价值观的工具，并已开始在2088被试的数据基础上识别不同的价值观组合。此研究将采用我们开发的工具从全国七所高等院校的700毕业生收取他们毕业前和参加工作一年后的数据，通过追踪研究方法探讨他们在职业发展初期价值观组合的变化及规律，检验价值观组合与他们的择业倾向及实际工作的关系，以及其他可能会影响价值观变化的包括职业发展、领导培训等各种因素对他们的影响。我们还准备通过这些学生获取他们的直接上司对他们在公司的表现的数据，并将此作为结果变量来考虑。 我们的研究结果不仅会推动对价值观的研究，为行为理论的发展做贡献，同时也将对高校学生的价值观教育、就业指导和企业的职业引导提供理论支持。

444210.label: Project Objectives
444210.value: Objective 1 To examine whether ideal affect varies by age across cultures: Study 1 will use survey method to examine age differences in global ideal affect and Study 2 will use experience sampling method to examine age differences in momentary ideal affect, among European-Americans, Chinese-Americans and Hong Kong Chinese. Objective 2 To examine the antecedent (i.e., potential cause) of age differences in ideal affect across cultures: Study 3 will use quasi-experimental method to examine whether time perspective accounts for age differences in ideal affect among European-Americans, Chinese-Americans and Hong Kong Chinese. Objective 3 To examine the outcomes (operationally defined as correlates) of age differences in ideal affect across cultures: Studies 1 & 2 will examine whether ideal affect is associated with conceptions of mental health, aging and leadership.

444210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444210.value: Socioemotional selectivity theory argues that as people age, they perceive time as more limited. This perceived time limitation motivates them to prioritize emotionally meaningful goals. Our prior research on social relationships and cognition have documented that although Chinese and Westerners (Germans and Americans) both prioritize emotionally meaningful goals with age, the specific behavioral manifestations of this prioritization differ. For example, although both Chinese and Germans seek to interact with more emotionally close social partners with age, they do so in different manners. Chinese do so by increasing the percentage of family members and decreasing the percentage of acquaintances in their social networks; yet, Germans do so by increasing the percentage of acquaintances and decreasing the percentage of family members. Similar differences have also been found in cognition. Although both Chinese and Americans pay more selective attention to emotional stimuli with age, Americans pay more attention to positive stimuli while Chinese pay more attention to negative stimuli. We argue that these cross-cultural differences may occur because Chinese and Westerners perceive different goals as emotionally meaningful. In this proposed project, we will assess whether Hong Kong Chinese, European- Americans and Chinese-Americans perceive different goals as emotionally meaningful within the framework of the Affect Valuation Theory. The theory postulates that because Chinese tend to adjust to the needs of others, their ideal affect (i.e., the emotions they want to feel) are low arousal positive emotions (LAP) such as calmness. In contrast, European-Americans seek to influence others, so their ideal affect are high arousal positive emotions (HAP) such as excitement. Chinese-Americans’ ideal affect is somewhere in-between. This theory has received empirical support in studies using college samples (i.e. young adults). In this project, we will use survey (Study 1) and experience sampling methods (Study 2) to examine whether these cross-cultural differences in ideal affect persist or even magnify across adulthood (i.e. among young, middle-aged and older adults), and whether they predict conceptions of aging, mental health and leadership. We will also use quasi-experimental methods (Study 3) to assess whether perceived time perspective accounts for age differences in ideal affect across cultures. 社會情緒選擇理論認為，隨著人們的年齡增長，他們認為時間越來越變得有限。而有限的時間促使他們優先定立在情感上有意義的目標。我們先前在社會關係和認知的研究已證據表明，儘管中國和西方人（德國和美國）都隨著年齡的增長而定立在情感上有意義的目標，相關具體的行為表現會有所不同。例如，雖然年紀較大的中國人和德國人會更加和密切的社會夥伴交往，他們當中的表現會有所不同。中國人會增加家庭成員以及減少朋友的比例，然而，德國人則剛剛相反，他們會增加朋友和減少的家庭成員比例。認知的研究上亦同樣發現類似的差異。雖然年長的中國人和美國人更加選擇性地注意有關情緒的東西，美國人更加注意情感正面的東西，而中國人則相較注重情感負面的東西。我們認為，這些跨文化差異可能是因為中國和西方人對情感上有意義的目標有不同的定義。 在此建議的研究項目，我們會以情感價值理論的框架下評估香港人，美籍歐洲人與美籍華人有關情感上有意義的目標。該理論認為因為中國傾向於適應他人的需要，他們理想的情感（即他們想感受的情緒）會是屬於低激發性而正面的情緒（LAP），如平靜。在相比之下，美籍歐洲人傾向試圖影響他人，讓自己的理想情感處於在高激發性而正面的情緒（HAP），如興奮。美籍華人的理想的情感是介於兩者之間。這一理論已經在年輕成年人中得到實證支持。在這個項目中，我們將使用的調查（研究一）和經驗抽樣方法（研究二）檢查理想情感是否存在跨文化的差異，而我們亦研究當中其差異會否隨著年齡增長而放大，以及它們是否能預測健康，幸福感和產生情緒的行為。我們也將使用類似的實驗方法（研究三），以評估時間觀感上的年齡差異會否影響跨文化上對理想情感的看法。

444210.label: Realisation of objectives
444210.value: We carried three studies to address the objectives. In Study 1, we recruited 320 participants from 18 to 89 years old, with 112 young adults (Mage=21.6, 50% female), 98 middle-age adults (Mage=50.1, 55.6% female) and 110 old adults (Mage=71.9, 50% female). We used survey method to examine age differences in global ideal affect (Objective 1) and whether such ideal affect was associated with conceptions of mental health, aging and leadership (Objective 3). Then, we recruited a subsample from Study 1 to participate in Study 2. Overall, 112 Hong Kong Chinese (52% female) were recruited, including 41 younger adults (Mage=21.46), 32 middle-aged adults (Mage=48.34), and 39 older adults (Mage=70.08). They were contacted by phone five times a day randomly for seven days (experience sampling). When they were contacted, they reported their actual affect, ideal affect and their activities. Findings from this study revealed age differences in momentary ideal affect (Objective 1), as well as studying whether ideal affect was associated with conceptions of mental health, aging and leadership (Objective 3). We also completed Study 3, in which we used quasi-experimental method. A total of 371 Hong Kong Chinese participated in the study, including 131 younger adults (60.5% female) aged from 18 to 35, 120 middle-aged adults (36.7% male) aged from 36 to 64, and 120 older adults (55.5% male) aged above 65. The three age groups were randomly assigned into different FTP conditions (i.e. Time-limited, Time-expanded or Control condition), with 126 participants in the Time-limited group, 143 in the Time-expanded and 102 in the control condition. This study examined whether time perspective accounted for age differences in ideal affect, as reflected in their choices of health-related activities that can give rise to the ideal effect (Objective 2). To address the cross-cultural aspects of the three objectives, studies corresponding to the above three studies were carried out among European-Americans and Chinese-Americans in California, USA (supported by a different grant). Finally, to further explore the real-life consequences of ideal affect, the ideal affect scores obtained from this project were merged with similar data obtained from nine countries/regions to predict the facial emotional expressions and leadership styles of the political leaders of countries/regions, ranging from United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, China, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan to Mexico. Please see the next section for results of each study. All three objectives have been realized.
