446710.label: Major findings and research outcome
446710.value: The findings from this project can be grouped into three clusters. With regard to the effects of subjective social status and perceived mobility on health, we find that in contemporary China, subjective social status is an important predictor of individuals’ physical and mental health outcomes, above and beyond the effects of objective indicators of socioeconomic status. Most people felt that they moved up the social ladder as compared with their parents or with themselves from ten years ago. But perceived upward mobility has little effects on health, whereas perceived downward mobility is significantly associated with worse health outcomes. This finding focuses our attention on those who felt that they moved down the social ladder. Moreover, we also find that the health effects of subjective status at a specific time point also include the cumulative influence of prior changes in one’s social status. With regard to the effects of subjective social status on the positive and negative aspects of health, we find that subjective wealth status is a strong predictor of both psychological well-being and ill-being, whereas subjective power status is associated with indicators of psychological well-being such as happiness and subjective cultural status is predictive of experiencing depressive symptoms. Inconsistency between power and wealth status has little effects, whereas inconsistency between wealth and cultural status is related to psychological well-being. Finally, three papers examine various aspects of health inequality in China. One paper reveals socioeconomic gradients in physical health, as well as in depression and happiness, and shows that economic development influences the socioeconomic gradient. Two papers demonstrated that non-cognitive skills, which are associated with socioeconomic status, are significant predictors of both the positive and negative aspects of health. The research outcome of this project includes five academic papers, two of which have been published or accepted by SSCI journals. One is under review at an SSCI journal. Another two are under preparation and we plan to submit them to SSCI journals. We have also presented the findings from this project in four presentations at international and regional conferences. Currently, one PhD student is using the 2010 data to examine the effects of higher education on health in one of the chapters in his dissertation. Please refer to Part C for details. Finally, this project also generates two nationally representative data sets, which can used to address some of the questions arising from this project and to study other topics.

446710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
446710.value: Two lines of research may be further developed: 1. This project finds that both subjective social status and perceived social mobility are predictive of health status. The next step is then to investigate the mechanisms of the health effects of subjective status and perceived mobility. Scholars have posited several psychosocial pathways between subjective status and health, but they have not been systematically examined. We can utilize existing data to assess the possible mechanisms. There is little theoretical or empirical exposition of the pathways between perceived mobility and health. More theoretical development and possible additional data collection are needed to examine the mechanisms of perceived mobility. 2. An interesting question arising from this project is how people assess their social status. The analysis in this project shows that an extensive array of indicators of people’s objective socioeconomic status cannot entirely account for the subjective evaluation of their status. Further analysis will use existing data to assess the effects of other factors, for instances contextual inequality and possible reference groups such as those living in the same community. Qualitative interviews will be used to examine the criteria people use to assess their status.

446710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
446710.value: It has been well established that people with low socioeconomic status tend to suffer worse health, but the gaps in health between the rich and poor cannot be entirely explained by the unequal access to material resources. Recent research has emphasized the role of subjective relative status—those with lower perceived status in the social hierarchy tend to suffer worse health through psychosocial pathways. This research, however, has so far overlooked the dynamic changes in people’s subjective social status and mostly focused on the negative aspects of individuals’ health. Our project seeks to contribute to filling these gaps by bringing perceived social mobility into the analysis of subjective status and health, and by examining both the negative and positive aspects of health. Central to this project are two large sample survey of health inequality in China. China represents a social context that combines rapidly rising social inequality and widespread social mobility from a very low starting point, resulting in large variations in social status, health, and socioeconomic inequality. It is therefore important to examine the relationships among subjective status, perceived mobility and health in China and at the same time, it provides an excellent context to assess these issues.

447010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
447010.value: 勞工條件的企業自我監管及其對越南服裝與鞋業工廠的影響

447010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
447010.value: 透過非政府的機制以監管勞工標準是現今全球供應鏈的新口號。跨國企業與非政府組織為改善勞工狀況共同定下行為準則(codes of conduct)以審查各供應商之生產是否符合標準。此等企業自我監管的行為雖已蔓延全球，然而我們對其成效之了解卻仍十分有限，本研究項目旨在透過探討越南服裝與鞋業工廠的勞工現況以補足我們對此的了解。 本研究項目會對越南的服裝與鞋業工廠進行抽樣，不論有否企業自我監管的經驗，目標是得到150所工廠的樣本。調查方法分別為管理調查(management survey)和與兩位在被抽樣的工廠中工作的工人進行深入訪談(in-depth interview)。本研究項目亦旨在延伸首席研究員於2005年進行的工廠調查(樣本數目為124所工廠)，讓我們能對企業自我監管的成效同時作出縱貫性(longitudinal)及橫斷性(cross-sectional)的審視。現有的實證研究大多是為數最多四間有企業自我監管經驗的供應商之個案研究，它們既未能審視工廠狀況的改變亦欠缺了與其他沒有企業自我監管經驗的工廠比較的部份。本研究項目將會改善過去文獻該等之短處，以更嚴謹的研究設計去評核企業自我監管的成效。 本項目的另一主要目的是要探討帶來改善的因果機制(causal mechanism)。企業自我監管的運作理念原本是希望透過買家的權力和對違規的脅迫性制裁來促使供應商遵循並作出改善。然而，近期研究發現買家的權力其實十分有限，其影響力也不持久。有鑑於此等 “遵循式” 的監管(compliance-focused approach)的限制，企業的自我監管開始轉向一種被稱為 “承諾式” 的監管 (commitment-oriented approach)。此監管模式強調透過糾錯(remediation)及難題梳解(problem solving)以帶來正面的行為改變。此模式雖假定供應商自因身欠缺改善勞工狀況的能力才未能作出改善，然而迄今之研究仍未對如何讓工廠管理層自願作出改善有透徹的了解。本研究項目期望通過對帶來改善的因果機制作深入調查，重塑現時對勞工標準的企業自我監管之激烈辯論。 越南是研究此因果機制的最合適地方。國際勞動組織 (International Labor Organization)為了在越南的供應商開展了一個名為 “Better Work Program” 的計劃，旨在提供糾錯及難題梳解等方面的協助。此計劃正好給予研究者機會去探討有何因素能驅使供應商去作出改善。雖然本項目的研究對象皆在越南，但因本項目旨在透過實證上嚴謹和理論上合理的方法指出有何條件能促使企業自我的監管運作起來，本研究之結論將能推及至越南以外的地區。

447510.label: Project Title(Chinese)
447510.value: 晚清基督教中文小說 (1807-1911)：宗教與文學的跨學科研究

447510.label: Project Objectives
447510.value: To discover and investigate the long-neglected Chinese Christian novels of the late Qing period. To supplement and re-construct the history of modern Chinese literature by highlighting the literary quality and value of Chinese Christian novels. To promote the interdisciplinary study of religion and literature as a field in the Chinese academic contexts. To facilitate further research and teaching in the field by writing four to five academic articles, and reprinting major works of Chinese Christian novels.

To supplement and re-construct the history of modern Chinese literature by highlighting the literary quality and value of Chinese Christian novels.
To promote the interdisciplinary study of religion and literature as a field in the Chinese academic contexts.
To facilitate further research and teaching in the field by writing four to five academic articles, and reprinting major works of Chinese Christian novels.

447510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
447510.value: 在晚清基督教的漢語文本中，不少作品採用中國傳統小說的形式作爲載體，既具有深刻的宗教內涵，也表現出明顯的文學特徵，可視為一類特殊的基督教小說。由於中國特定的歷史原因，這批基督教小說散藏於世界各地，一向鮮爲學界所知，乃中國宗教和文學研究的盲點。近年來，隨著原始資料的逐步發掘，已有學者開始關注這批文本，如韓南(Patrick Hanan)、吳淳邦、陳慶浩、宋莉華等，更有學者認為「晚清基督教中文小說」在一定程度上影響了梁啓超所提倡的「小說界革命」，促進了中國近代文學的改革與普及，對中國文學史的演進具有重要意義。基於前人以歷史考證爲主的研究成果，本研究計劃將整合宗教和文學兩個領域的資源進行多角度的考察，探討「晚清基督教中文小說」異彩紛呈的文本世界及文學價值，嘗試為中國近代文學史補上重要的一章，並促進在華人學術處境中宗教與文學的跨學科研究與教學。

447510.label: Realisation of objectives
447510.value: This project has, to a large extent, achieved most of the proposed objectives by discovering and critically analyzing the long-neglected but nevertheless important corpus of Chinese Christian novels in late Qing China (1807-1911). On the basis of Patrick Hanan’s “missionary novels”, this project has proposed a more inclusive term “Chinese Christian novels” which could be categorized by the following two criteria: first, the identity of the writers, whether Western missionaries or Chinese Christians, and second, the nature of the texts, whether translated or original works. These novels endeavored to cater for the reading habits and aesthetic interests of the Chinese audience, and hence facilitate the spread and acceptance of the associated religious message. The project has contributed to the promotion of the interdisciplinary study of religion and literature as a field in the Chinese academic contexts, and substantiated our knowledge of the history of modern Chinese literature. By integrating the academic resources of religious and literary studies, notably hermeneutics and narratology, this project has investigated such important themes as the inter-religious dialogue between Christianity and Chinese religions, inter-textuality between the novels and the Bible, strategies of cross-cultural translation, and the interactive relationships between the novels’ narrative features and the Chinese literary traditions and socio-cultural contexts. Special attention has been paid to the interaction between the translation and production of Chinese Christian novels with late-Qing literary trends, especially the introduction of western learning and the vernacular movement. This has supplemented our understanding of the rise of modern Chinese fiction in the early 20th century. I have published two annotated volumes of novels, five academic articles, one encyclopedia entry, and presented five conference papers, more productive than my original anticipated output of four to five articles. The in-depth case studies of analyzing representative Christian novels in the articles have helped to draw some theoretical observations for a deeper understanding of the constraints and strategies of the entire missionary enterprise of literary endeavours. The two annotated volumes have made the rarely known yet highly significant works of Chinese Christian novels readily accessible to the academic world. The republication of major primary texts will be of considerable value to scholars of religious studies, literary studies and translation studies.

447510.label: Major findings and research outcome
447510.value: The five journal articles have explored new research themes and approaches by doing a critical textual analysis of several pieces of widely-circulated yet under-researched Chinese Christian novels, as demonstrated by the following four examples. The paper “重構他界想像：晚清漢譯基督教小說《安樂家》(1882)初探” examines the reconstructing the other-worldly imagination through a pioneering study of the translated Victorian children fiction Anle jia (Home Sweet Home, 1882), from Christie’s Old Organ by Mrs. O. F. Walton. This novel demonstrates vivid artistic creation, as shown in the visual, auditory, and psychological representation through image, music, and dream. The protagonists, Treffy and Christie, are homeless wanderers in the world, suffering from poverty, loneliness, fear, and disease. The biblical motif of hope and thirst for heavenly home, as portrayed in Revelation, becomes a strong motivation for their journey of spiritual pursuit. The article “首部漢譯德文基督教小說：論《金屋型儀》中女性形象的本土化” investigates the first German-Chinese translated Christian novel, Jinwu xingyi (1852), from Hermann Ball’s Thirza, oder die Anziehungskraft des Kreuzes . This was a classic example of acculturation and appropriation, with its literary and religious components blended into the Chinese cultural framework. This article focusses on the ways in which the target text has re-presented the female image, with special reference to the formation of Chinese Christian identity, against the late-Qing background of anti-Christianity. The paper “《聖經》的中國演義：理雅各史傳小說《約瑟紀畧》(1852)研究” examines the ways in which James Legge adapted the story of Joseph as recorded in the Book of Genesis into a classical Chinese novel. The most remarkable characteristic lies in the author’s attempt to offer a Confucian interpretation of the biblical story, notably depicting the Hebrew patriarchs as Confucian sages upholding lofty standards of morality. The article "從《勝旅景程》(1870)的小說評點看傳教士「耶儒會通」的策略" investigates the missionary strategy of reconciling Christianity with Confucianism from the perspective of fiction annotation of Thomas Hudson's Shenglü jingcheng (1870), Chinese translation of The Pilgrim's Progress. Demonstrating a vividly indigenized translating strategy, it adopted the literary form and narrative features of traditional Chinese fiction. More prominently, it inherits the literary tradition of fiction annotation to interpret the Christian thoughts of the novel by making profuse references to traditional Chinese religious and literary allusions, especially from Confucian classics. The annotated volume “晚清基督教敘事文學選粹” collects six representative works of narrative literature by six leading Protestant missionary writers, while “贖罪之道傳──郭實獵基督教小說集” is a critical edition of seven novels by Karl Gützlaff, the most prolific, and arguably most important, late-Qing missionary novelist in Chinese.

447510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
447510.value: On the basis of the substantial research outputs relating chiefly to the novels produced by missionaries, I have been awarded another General Research Fund for the project “Rediscovering the Lost Heritage: The Religious Poetics of the ‘New Age Novels’ (1895) and Its Far-reaching Impact on Chinese Literary Modernity” (2013-2015). The new three-year project launches the first critical attempt to investigate the recently discovered Shixin xiaoshuo (時新小說 New Age Novels), some 150 pieces of unpublished manuscripts for the fiction contest organized by John Fryer (1839-1928) in 1895. The project aims to further contribute to complementing, if not revising, traditional accounts about the rise of modern fiction, the development of new literary genres and vernacular language in China. With my research findings in the field, I have been invited to take an active part in the internationally collaborative publication project "Creation and Translation: Re-reading and Re-publishing the Late-Qing Christian Novels in Chinese", headed by Prof. Wallace Sher-shiueh Li of Academia Sinica (Taiwan), the Co-investigator of the current GRF project, together with Prof. Soon-Bang Oh of Soongsil University (Korea). The multi-volume annotated collection of Chinese Christian novels will be published by Academia Sinica.

447510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
447510.value: This project breaks new ground and makes three major scholarly contributions. Previous literary historians might have overlooked that the experimentation with Chinese vernacular modernity originated with the missionaries’ literary engagements. This study fills a gap by supplementing the history of modern Chinese fiction by a critical assessment of the literary value of the vernacular novels produced by Protestant missionaries. Secondly, these novels shed new lights on the process and strategies through which Christianity was contextualized and indigenized in the Chinese literary and cultural milieu. This investigation deepens our understanding on the inter-textual influence between the Bible and Chinese literature, and the interplay between Chinese religious thoughts and Christian culture in the late imperial era. Thirdly, the project makes pioneering efforts to unearth, collect, re-edit, and annotate the missionary novels by consulting the rarely known and hardly accessible extant copies of the late-Qing Chinese Christian novels which are mainly scattered in major libraries and archives in the West. The republication of these long-neglected primary texts will promote the interdisciplinary study of religion and literature as a field in the Chinese academic contexts.

448310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
448310.value: 以往有關教師心理健康的研究主要在關注教師負面性、病理性的抱怨情緒，現在我們有需要從正面的角度來認識教師身心康寧的問題（Lau, Yuen, Chan, Myers & Lee, 2008）。因此，本研究有以下三項目標：（1）在中國社會背景下的教師群體當中，驗證身心康寧模型的結構以及它的測量方法（例如：5F-Wel）以發展一個教師身心康寧模型；（2）研究香港教師的身心康寧的狀況，以及其與教師個人特性之間的關係；（3）研究身心康寧、教師工作壓力和生命意義之間的關係。 在預研究中，通過對資深教師的訪談，收集他們關於教師身心康寧的看法。訪談的結果將作為後續聚焦小組討論的提綱。在聚焦小組討論中，教師將討論和分享他們關於身心康寧以及對5F-Wel項目（Myers & Sweeney, 2005）的看法。在此之後，進一步分析5F-Wel翻譯版本中的同時效度、效標參照效度、因數結構以及其他測量學指標。我們希望通過這些分析，以及對個別項目的微調，能夠獲得具有良好心理學指標的5F-Wel中文版本。 在正式研究當中，從本地小學與中學隨機選取約2000名教師進行調查，調查主要研究（1）身心康寧與教師人口變數之間的關係；（2）身心康寧、教師工作壓力與生命意義之間的關係。然後所有教師將會完成一系列問卷，包括5F-Wel中文版問卷、教師職業壓力問卷（Lau, 2002）、生命意義問卷（Crumbaugh, 1968; Shek, 1988），並收集他們的人口變數。期望能從研究結果中發展出一個關於香港教師身心康寧的模型，能夠較全面地體現中國文化特色下的身心康寧模式的特點。研究結果還將對身心康寧的本質，其影響因素，特別是對瞭解香港教師的身心康寧狀況產生積極的啟示。

448310.label: Realisation of objectives
448310.value: All the proposed objectives have been achieved in the research period. In order to develop a new wellness model, a comprehensive literature review on teacher’s wellness and well-being, stress, purpose in life, and teacher burnout were conducted. After gathering the information, an in-depth interview with a retired secondary school principal, and four focus group sessions with teachers and principals were conducted in the summer 2011. Results of the interview and focus group sessions showed that the 5F-Wel model could be applied to Hong Kong teachers. Participants of the focus groups also revealed that collegial support in schools might be a factor related to teacher wellness. A pilot study was conducted in October 2011 with 243 teachers in Hong Kong to study the psychometric properties of the Chinese 5F-Wel and the newly developed Collegial Support Inventory. The reliability and the structural validity of both the 5F-Wel and the Collegial Support Inventory were found to be adequate. Concurrent validity of the 5F-Wel was also confirmed. After the pilot study, 25 primary school and 24 secondary schools were randomly selected and invited to participate in the main study in March to June, 2012. This was about 5% of the total number of schools in Hong Kong. All teachers of each participating school were invited to fill in the questionnaires comprising the Chinese version of 5F-Wel, Purpose in Life Questionnaire, a simplified version of Teacher Occupational Stress Questionnaire, the Collegial Support Inventory, and items of the demographic information. Altogether 2,546 questionnaires were sent out, and 1,827 were returned. Return rate was 72.76%. Mean replacement was employed to the questionnaires which consisted of small amount of missing data in order to retain as many data as possible for data analysis. As a result, the total number of participants with completed data is 1,763. The subsequent analyses were to study the reliability and validity of the inventories, demographic difference in teacher wellness, the factor structure of each inventory, as well as the relationship among constructs. Therefore, reliability analysis, ANOVA, confirmatory factor analysis and SEM were conducted. The mediating relationship of teacher occupational stress (TOS), purpose in life (PIL), collegial support (CS) and teacher wellness were then tested. The large number of items involved may lead to accumulation of error terms thus affect the accuracy of the results. Therefore, item parceling was employed to reduce the error.

448310.label: Major findings and research outcome
448310.value: Major findings and research outcome are summarized as follows. A five-factor structure of C-5F-Wel (CFI =.91, NNFI =.93, RMSEA =.081, SRMR = .040), a five-factor structure of TOS (CFI =.92, NNFI =.91, RMSEA =.064, SRMR = .062), a single factor structure of PIL (CFI =.93, NNFI =.92, RMSEA =.071, SRMR =.042) , and a single factor structure of CS (CFI =.95, NNFI =.91, RMSEA =.110, SRMR =.041) were confirmed. For teacher wellness, the result implies that the 5-factor model proposed by Hattie, Myers and Sweeney (2004) could be applied to teachers in Hong Kong. In addition, all measuring tools showed good reliability. The Cronbach’s Alpha was .93, .94, .91 and .87 for the total scores of C-5F-Wel, Teacher Occupational Stress, Purpose in Life and Collegial Support respectively. Besides, the reliability of the sub-scales of both C-5F-Wel (ranged from .76 to .88) and Teacher Occupational Stress Questionnaire (ranged from .80 to .89) were adequate. ANOVA was conducted to investigate the demographic differences of C-5F-Wel. Significant wellness difference was observed in gender, teaching experience, religious status and students’ academic ability, whereas no difference was noticed in marital status, subject taught, and school duties. However, the pattern of demographic differences varied in primary and secondary schools. To study the relationship among PIL, TOS, CS and teacher wellness, two structural models were put forth for comparison. With the application of SEM procedure, a direct effect model studying the direct effect of PIL, TOS and CS on teacher wellness was found to be marginally significant (CFI =.90, NNFI =.89, RMSEA =.056, SRMR = .152) accounting for 57.6% of the total variance of teacher wellness. Then, two paths were added to the direct effect model with one from TOS to PIL and the other from TOS to CS, thus forming a direct-effect-mediating model involving PIL and CS as mediators on the effect from TOS to teacher wellness. Results of the SEM analysis showed better fit indexes were obtained (CFI =.90, NNFI =.91, RMSEA =.052, SRMR = .077) indicating the latter model better fit the data. However, the path from TOS to teacher wellness became insignificant. Thus, a complete mediating model was resulted accounting for 62.2% of the total variance of Teacher Wellness, 4.6% better than the direct effect model. The negative effect of occupational stress on teacher wellness would be totally mediated by teachers’ purpose in life and collegial support.

448310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
448310.value: This study aims to examine the wellness situation of Hong Kong teachers with their demographic information and variables of purpose in life, stress and collegial support. Nevertheless, the factors that contribute to teacher wellness may be a lot more. Different approaches should also be considered to study the wellness of teacher,e.g. by adopting the model of Job Demands-Resources (Schaufeli & Baker, 2004; Wang, 2013). Although the study proposed a mediating role of both PIL and CS between TOS and teacher wellness, a clear directionality between the components cannot be confirmed in such a quantitative study. The direction of the path from TOS to PIL could be reverse or both. Likewise, the direction between TOS and CS should be reconsidered as well. It is worthy to explore the relationship of those components through qualitative methods in order to ground a more accurate theory. This research was conducted solely in Hong Kong. However, teachers in Mainland China share similar cultural characteristics with Hong Kong teachers. It would be interesting to conduct further study to compare the findings between teachers in Hong Kong and teachers in Mainland China. This would be able to identify some common variables that affect teacher’s wellness in the Chinese communities.

448310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
448310.value: This project aims to examine the wellness situation of teachers in Hong Kong, and its relationship with teacher occupational stress (TOS), purpose in life (PIL) and collegial support (CS). The study is quantitative in nature by adopting a survey as the major means of study though individual interview and focus group interviews were also adopted to collect data from school teachers and principals on concepts of wellness and factors affecting wellness. The Chinese version of the 5F-Wel was confirmed to be a good measuring tool to study teacher wellness in Hong Kong because of its adequate reliability and validity. Among Hong Kong teachers, the total wellness is composed of five factors, namely Essential Self, Social Self, Coping Self, Creative Self and Physical Self. Significant wellness differences were found in gender, teaching experience, religious status and students’ academic ability, whereas no difference was noticed in marital status, subject taught, and school duties. However, the pattern of demographic difference varied in primary school and secondary school. In addition, teacher stress was found be negatively related to teacher wellness. The more a teacher feels stressful from his/her job, the less wellness he/she experiences. However, the effect of TOS on teacher wellness are completely mediated by PIL and CS.

448510.label: Project Objectives
448510.value: To develop two IATs for predicting the counterproductive attitudes of employees in Chinese context. To verify the predictive power of integrity tests in Chinese context in predicting counterproductive performance.

448510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
448510.value: Counterproductive work behaviors such as poor attendance, gossiping, misuse of work time and resources etc. are serious problems faced by many managers. Each year, billions of dollars are wasted in that kind of organizational misbehaviors performed by employees. While organizational culture and environment is one factor leading to these behaviors, dispositional characteristics of employees may be an even more important antecedent. In the 20th and 21st century, it was a common practice for large organizations to use integrity tests and personality inventories to check the dispositional characteristics of applicants before they were selected. However, there are three problems of these assessment tools. First, faking is an obvious problem. Many applicants tend to present themselves in a favorable way when asked about what they think and who they are. Lie scales may help a little bit, but not that much. Second, many applicants may not do it purposefully. They may not even aware of their tendency of positive impression management. Third, these assessment tools assume that the applicants have good understanding of themselves, which may not be true for those who have tendency of counterproductive work behaviors. Starting from the 20th century, there was a new set of assessment techniques which claimed to be useful in assessing the implicit attitudes of respondents. One of those techniques, the Implicit Association Test (IAT), uses response time latency to capture the possibly unconscious attitudes of individuals. In the last twenty years, many studies showed that IAT might be a useful technique in assessing the implicit attitudes of human beings. While there were numerous applications of IAT in the western social psychology literature, the technique was basically new in the business world. We try to apply the IAT in this study to assessing the tendency of individuals in having counterproductive work behaviors. We hypothesized IAT would have incremental predictive power on counterproductive work behaviors over and beyond that of personality and integrity tests. If this is true, it may open a new arena for personnel selection research in the future. Business organizations may use IAT to screen out applicants who have strong tendencies of performing counterproductive behaviors in the work place. Organizations may also use this result to assess the change in attitudes of employees in some training programs. Other than counterproductive behaviors, implicit attitudes may be used to identify altruistic employees who have a high tendency to perform extra-role behaviors. 反生产行为（如迟到、无故请假、讲同事闲话、胡乱使用工作时间和资源等）是今天管理者遇到的一大难题。在美国，企业每年有数以亿计美元的开支是用在反生产行为上的。在二十世纪，诚信度测验和性格测验是选拔中用来预测应征者反生产行为的一般用具。但是这两种测验都有做假的问题。应聘者可以估计设计问卷者的目的而选择设计者预期的答案。测谎量表也可以估计应答者提供不真实答案的机会。但是这类测谎量表的真实测谎能力也没有完全得到证实。所以，如何在招聘时找出有反生产行为倾向的应征者一直是一个悬疑未决的问题。 从在二十一世纪开始，心理学家提出了用内隐态度测试来测验一个人隐藏在内的态度。內隐态度是相对于应答者对问卷调查所表现的外显态度而言。內隐态度测试是用应答者在计算机上对不同词语的反应的时间差作为內隐态度的表征。我们提出用内隐态度测试来预测应征者的反生产行为的观点。这个研究就是验证上述的假设。如果验证成功，除了反生产行为以外，我们还可以尝试用内隐态度测试来估计员工的其他工作态度和表现。

448510.label: Major findings and research outcome
448510.value: Based on the web survey, we found that IAT was a useful alternative to personality inventory and integrity test to be used in the selection setting in predicting counter-productive work behaviors (CWBs). The IAT test was significantly correlated with the reported CWBs of the employees. This relationship was still true even when we control for personality and scores of a validated integrity test. These results supported our original hypothesis that IAT can be used to predict employee CWBs in the selection setting. Since we cannot find significant results in the paper-and-pencil survey in Beijing, we went back to do follow-up in-depth interviews in the company to understand reasons for the unexpected results in this sample. What we heard from the respondents was that the company was under a major re-engineering program during our data collection. Many of the store managers (raters of CWBs of employees) were new to the store and might not have good understandings of CWBs of employees in such a short period of time. This provided good explanations of our insignificant results. We did another follow-up recently and use our newly developed IAT to predict objective lying behaviors of university students using an experimental design. Results supported our predictions that IAT score was highly correlated with lying behaviors of subjects. This provided additional support of the validity of our IAT scale and further evidence that the Beijing results were only unexpected situational artifacts.

448510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
448510.value: This is the first study to show that IAT can actually predict CWBs in the work setting. We also have hard experimental evidence that IAT can predict lying behaviors of student subjects. When these two pieces of information are added together, we have some evidence that IAT can be used as a low cost and valid alternative of personality-based integrity tests in the selection setting. Other than the selection setting, companies may also think about using IAT to predict the integrity of potential managers when they consider promotion different employees to important managerial position. Given the current trend of serious actions taken by companies on corporate government after the Emron incident, IAT may be a viable assessment tools to be used for managerial selection.

448510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
448510.value: Implicit Association Tests (IAT) are tests to assess the subconscious value and attitudes of human beings. Using timed responses to computerized stimulus, IAT can check the implicit attitudes of individuals. We apply the IAT to test the implicit values and attitudes of employees towards counterproductive work behaviors (CWBs) such as simple matters as taking company stationaries for personal use, to serious offense as thefts in the workplace. Our results in a controlled experiment showed that IAT can predict students objective lying behaviors to get higher rewards. In an online survey, we found that IAT can predict CWBs of employees over and beyond personality inventories and integrity tests. Since an IAT would only take 15 minutes, it would be a very viable alternative to existing predictors which are often accused of having high false-positive, i.e., labeling a person of having high CWBs inclination which is, in fact, false.

448610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
448610.value: This collaborative action research study investigates how English teachers of S1-3 (lower secondary) students in Hong Kong can be supported to bring innovation to conventional feedback approaches in the writing classroom, and how such innovation can impact the teaching and learning of writing. Feedback is a useful pedagogical tool to enhance the teaching and learning of writing. While research has yet to establish the most effective feedback strategies, there is growing evidence that casts doubt on conventional feedback approaches, such as teachers marking single drafts, focusing predominantly on errors, and responding to errors comprehensively. In Hong Kong, however, teachers have for years been adopting such conventional feedback approaches. They spend a significant amount of time marking student writing but there is a tacit awareness that their efforts are not generally effective. Students continue to make the same mistakes, become more reliant on the teacher, and their writing does not necessarily improve as a result of teacher feedback. With a paradigm shift in assessment that puts more emphasis on its relationship with teaching and learning, i.e. assessment for learning, there is a need to revolutionize conventional feedback approaches to bring improvement to the teaching and learning of writing. Much existing research, however, focuses on the act of feedback itself without addressing the issue of how effective feedback can be implemented in real contexts. Specifically, there is virtually non-existent research on teachers’ readiness to implement change in feedback, how they can be supported to initiate change within the constraints of their work contexts, and how such innovation can impact the teaching and learning of writing. The study serves to fill these gaps. The project involves working collaboratively with twelve secondary English teachers in six different schools, relying mainly on qualitative methods including interviews, classroom observations, questionnaires, and analysis of student writing and teacher feedback. Through its collaborative action research design, the study will make a significant theoretical and methodological contribution to the research literature on feedback in writing. It will contribute to the local educational community by providing a highly contextualized picture of how innovation in feedback can be implemented, shedding light on the factors that facilitate and inhibit change, as well as the impact of innovative feedback approaches on the teaching and learning of writing. The study will also result in professional development seminars on effective feedback in writing in support of the government’s education reform that promotes assessment for learning. 是次合作形式的行動研究旨在探討何種元素能幫助香港中一至中三(初中部)英文教師為現行批改寫作及給予評語的方法引入創新的改革，以及此革新如何影響教師教授及學生學習寫作。 批改學生寫作及給予評語是有效的教學途徑，有助於老師教授及學生學習寫作。正當許多研究在確立一套最有效的批改寫作及給予評語的策略時，愈來愈多證據質疑現時教師批改寫作及給予評語的方法，這包括：每次寫作時，教師只批改學生一篇草稿，以及教師批改作文時，主要著重修改及批評學生所有錯誤。然而，香港的教師已經實行上述批改寫作及給予評語的方法多年，他們耗盡許多時間來批改學生作文，但彼此卻存在著一股沈默的體悟：如此的努力批改並不是十分有效。學生依然繼續犯下同樣的錯誤，學生們變得更依賴老師，然而學生們的寫作並不一定會因為老師們的批改及評語而作出相對應有的進步。由於強調教學及學習關係的評估 (即促進學習評估) 的範式轉向，我們有必要為現行批改寫作及給予評語的方法作出改革，以改善老師教授及學生學習寫作情況。 可是，現時很多研究都只著重鑽研批改方法及評語的本質，而沒有提出教師如何能在真正的教學環境中實行有效的批改及給予有效的評語。特別是，現時沒有任何實質研究探討教師是否就實行批改寫作及給予評語的革新作好準備，何種元素能幫助教師們在其限制性的工作環境中作出革新，以及此革新會如何影響老師教授及學生學習寫作。是次研究正好補充上述知識上的漏洞。 是次研究需與六名來自三間不同中學的英文教師合作，並主要採用性質研究的方法，這包括面試、課堂觀察、問卷、學生寫作分析以及教師批改寫作及給予評語的方法分析。由於是次研究是一個合作形式的行動研究，故於理論層面及研究方法論層面上，都將會為現時關於批改寫作及給予評語的文獻帶來重要的貢獻。是次研究亦將會為本地的教育作出貢獻，它不但能就著教師如何為批改寫作及給予評語的方法實行改革提供一個清晰的局面，而且更帶出促進及約束此革新的元素，以及探討此革新如何影響老師教授及學生學習寫作。是次研究更能產生一些主題關於有效批改寫作及給予評語的教師專業培訓講座，以支持政府所提倡之促進學習評估的教育改革。

448610.label: Realisation of objectives
448610.value: Through multiple sources of data gathered from the participating teachers including in-depth interviews, classroom observations, collection of relevant documents, as well as student data gathered from focus group interviews, questionnaires, classroom observations and pre- and post-study writing, the research team was able to achieve all the objectives of the project. Specifically, the above data sources enabled us to investigate the reasons why the teachers determined to undertake feedback innovations, how they went about change, the classroom processes and factors that facilitated the innovations, the impact of feedback innovations on student learning (including both motivation and writing performance), as well as the factors that posed impediments to change. On the whole, the participating teachers were co-operative and data collection was generally smooth. However, the research team was unable to get the teachers to write reflections on their innovative attempts and to interact with other participating teachers through the online platform created for the project. As the participating teachers (typical of secondary teachers of English in Hong Kong) were all swamped with work in one way or another, it was impossible for the research team to make them write reflections and exchange ideas on the online platform. As a result, the collaborative action research component of the project was not realized. However, since collaborative action research was not a major focus of the study, the absence of this element did not affect the quality of the research. We were still able to collect the abovementioned data to explore the teachers’ feedback innovations and gain insights into the research topic.

448610.label: Major findings and research outcome
448610.value: The major findings and research outcome are summarized according to the research objectives. 1. The findings of the study show that through university-school collaboration (Lee, 2013), the participating teachers were helped to think outside the box and bring change to conventional feedback approaches. The strong coalition with the research team helped sustain their motivation and provided support for the teachers’ continuing professional development. In the words of one participating teacher, they “develop a better understanding of students’ difficulties in writing, find feedback less burdensome and more enjoyable, and witness pupils’ gradual improvement in motivation and writing performance”. 2. The findings show that teachers undertook classroom research to improve their feedback practices mainly because they were uncertain about the effectiveness of conventional feedback practices, which diminished students’ interest, motivation and confidence in writing, and made students focus mainly on the scores. Students played a passive role and became reliant on the teacher. Together, these reasons prompted the teachers to undertake classroom research to improve their feedback practices (Lee, 2014). 3. The participating teachers attended a series of workshops held by the research team, selected a few feedback strategies that suited their own context, and carried out change in their classroom. The innovative feedback strategies include: focused written corrective feedback, coded feedback, peer feedback, comment-only feedback (i.e. no scores), and the use of feedback forms. 4. The findings show pockets of success in teachers’ feedback innovations in terms of improving student motivation in writing (Lee, Mak & Burns, under preparation). As for students’ writing performance, at the end of the study, teachers reported improvement in students’ writing, though such self-reported data are not fully corroborated by the post-study writing test results. Nonetheless, in one school, there were significant improvements in students’ internal writing exam results, which according to the teachers were a result of innovations in their feedback strategies. 5. The study demonstrates that systematic efforts to implement new feedback approaches, coupled with relevant changes in instructional practices provide benefits for students by assisting them to understand more explicitly what teachers look for in writing performance and therefore what to self-monitor in their writing. Obstacles to feedback innovation, however, include the lack of a common vision among colleagues, the time constraint, and colleagues’ insistence on marking all errors in writing. The last obstacle actually caused some teachers in the study to revert back to unfocused written corrective feedback after one school term.

448610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
448610.value: One major finding from the study is that although teachers in the three participating schools were aware of the benefits of focused written corrective feedback, some of them were unable to implement it fully. In one school, the teachers started the project by attempting to implement focused written corrective feedback but reverted back to unfocused WCF (i.e. marking all errors) after a few months, for fear that they would be looked upon as different from the other colleagues (Lee & Mak, 2013). The findings suggest that if focused written corrective feedback is to be implemented successfully, teachers need stronger understanding of how focused written corrective feedback can be supported by instructional methodology, and that more teachers (preferably in the whole school) have to be involved so that participating teachers will not be innovating in isolation. In view of this, further research is warranted to focus on written corrective feedback as a pedagogical innovation in specific classroom contexts, looking into its implementation, efficacy and the factors that influence the efficacy.

448610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
448610.value: Feedback is a useful tool to enhance the teaching and learning of writing. While research has yet to establish the most effective feedback strategies, there is growing evidence that casts doubt on conventional feedback approaches, such as teachers marking single drafts, focusing predominantly on errors, and responding to errors meticulously and comprehensively. This study investigates how English teachers of S1-3 (lower secondary) students in Hong Kong can be supported to bring innovation to conventional feedback approaches in the writing classroom, and how such innovation can impact the teaching and learning of writing. Results of the study show pockets of success in teachers’ feedback innovations, particularly in contributing to better student motivation in writing and in enhancing teachers’ professional development in the teaching and assessment of writing. The study has made a significant contribution to current research on feedback in writing, uncovering the sociocultural forces that impact the effectiveness of feedback innovations. It also contributes to the local educational community by providing a highly contextualized picture of how innovation in feedback can be implemented, shedding light on the factors that facilitate and inhibit change, as well as the impact of innovative feedback approaches on the teaching and learning of writing.

449210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
449210.value: Airfreight forwarders are third-party logistics service providers who plan, coordinate and manage client shipments. They acquire airfreight spaces from three major sources: carriers (airlines), partners and subcontractors, all of which are different in terms of cost, flexibility and service reliability. Booking spaces directly from carriers is done several months in advance and is the cheapest. Under most situations, carriers do not allow any changes once the booking contracts are signed. Acquiring spaces from partners would cost more, and the available amount is typically smaller. But partners usually allow forwarders to finalize the bookings as late as one month before shipping time. International freight forwarding is greatly affected by fluctuating economic conditions. When shipping time arrives, forwarders could find themselves in need of additional resources or having surplus resources. For the former, forwarders may subcontract shipping requests to other industry agents; subcontracting cost is the highest, and the service reliability is typically the lowest. For the latter, forwarders may sell surplus resources to other agents. Carriers offer a variety of resource booking schemes (by region, origin-destination, route, etc.), with some having less restriction on the shipping schedule and others more so. A booking that is less restrictive for the carrier would have a lower cost. An important concern of forwarders is whether the mix of bookings is indeed viable when implemented to meet individual shipment requirements. In this research, we provide a two-phase framework for this airfreight planning problem. The first phase is several months in advance when carrier bookings are made. Using the demand forecast at that time, a multi-item newsvendor model first determines, in aggregates, the resource requirements from carriers, partners, and subcontractors. A heuristic is then used to disaggregate the resource requirements into specific bookings. A simulation model simulates whether the bookings are viable during shipping time. The second phase is several weeks from shipping time, when bookings from partners are finalized. Similar to the first phase and based on the latest demand, a multi-item newsvendor model and a heuristics determine the specific booking from partners and the amount from subcontractors. Again, a simulation model studies the viability of the bookings during shipping time. Extensive numerical analysis would be conducted to examine managerial implications in a forwarder’s resource planning.

449210.label: Realisation of objectives
449210.value: We have done a considerable amount of research work to address objectives 1 and 2. We believe the objectives have been achieved. For objective 1, we formulate a two-stage stochastic dynamic program to determine aggregate resource bookings from carriers, partners, and subcontractors. Analytical results are obtained, based on which a heuristic algorithm is provided. A real-life example is used to examine the behavior of aggregate resource bookings. Here, we show several patterns of aggregate resource bookings with respect to different demand variances and cost parameters. The impact of capacity limits of respective resources on the booking patterns are examined as well. For objective 2, we perform simulation experiments to assess the viability of the proposed model based on real-life data. To make specific resource bookings, aggregate resource bookings have to be disaggregated to meet specific needs of shipping requests, which are uncertain and differ in terms of origin-destination, routing requirements, and weight and volume. A simulation model is developed to examine whether a disaggregate resource plan is able to handle different scenarios of specific resource needs. Tradeoff issues within this disaggregate environment are also explored.

449210.label: Major findings and research outcome
449210.value: Paper 1. An Aggregate-Disaggregate Approach to an Airfreight Forwarder’s Resource Planning under Uncertainty Airfreight forwarders acquire airfreight spaces from three sources: carriers, partners and subcontractors. Booking spaces from carriers is the cheapest and is done several months in advance. Resources from partners would cost more, but partners allow forwarders the flexibility to finalize bookings as late as one month before shipping time. When shipping time comes, because of demand uncertainty, forwarders may either have to subcontract or trade-in surplus resources. Since there are many decisions (routes, flight, time, ULDs, etc.), we propose an aggregate-disaggregate decision approach. In this paper, a two-stage stochastic program first determines, in aggregates, resource bookings from carriers, partners, and subcontractors (or surplus). A heuristic is then used to disaggregate the resource requirements into specific bookings. An extensive analysis is provided to examine the relevant managerial issues. Here, based on real-life data, we show several patterns of aggregate resource bookings with respect to different demand uncertainty and cost parameters. We show that resource disaggregation has to balance cost-effectiveness, capacity flexibility and routing flexibility of a resource plan. Submitted to European Journal of Operational Research, revising for resubmission (reviewers comments attached). Paper 2. An Airfreight Forwarder’s Resource Planning and Revenue Management A forwarder’s resource planning decisions and revenue management decisions are related. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between these two sets of decisions. For resource planning, we consider the problem of determining the amount of cargo space to acquire from airlines, partners, and subcontracting agents. For revenue management, we consider the two market segments and determine the control limits based on which a present request (from either a regular or an ad hoc customer) is accepted or rejected. The joint consideration of these two sets of decisions means that we now need to identify the best resource acquisition plan along with the corresponding optimal accept/reject decisions for customer requests. We first consider a customer arrival pattern where regular customers arrive before ad hoc customers. Here, a two-stage stochastic dynamic programming model is formulated. We examine the relationship between resource planning decisions and revenue management decisions. We then consider an arrival pattern where regular and ad hoc customers may arrive in any order. A Markov decision process model is formulated. Similarly, the interactive effects of resource planning and revenue management decisions are investigated and the results of the two arrival patterns are compared. Submitted to Management Science.

449210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
449210.value: For paper 1, the proposed aggregation-disaggregation approach can be augmented by an optimization-simulation approach to plan the aggregate booking. Such an approach has been effectively used in many situations: resource planning, order planning, transportation network design and production scheduling. For paper 2, future research could examine the situations where subcontracting cost and surplus trade-in price are random variables and customer requests are not firm and can be revised. In this paper, we consider the airfreight forwarder’s problem for a specific route and in a specific week. It would be interesting to incorporate the effect of capacity decisions across different routes on revenue management decisions.

449210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
449210.value: In paper 1, we introduce the problem of an airfreight forwarder’s resource planning under uncertainty, where the forwarder may acquire airfreight space from multiple sources and across time. The acquisition costs from respective sources are different and their flexibility differs as well. We also point out that there is a need to address such a planning problem both at the aggregate level as well as the disaggregate level. Based on real-life data, we show several patterns of aggregate resource bookings. It is also shown the key in resource disaggregation is to strike a balance between cost-effectiveness, capacity flexibility and routing flexibility of a resource plan. In paper 2, we articulate the importance of separating customers into regular customers and ad hoc customers, and that a forwarder could apply revenue management concepts to management resource availability for the two customer segments. Here, we show that a forwarder’s resource planning decisions and revenue management decisions are related. The relationship is analyzed with respect to various market characteristics. We find that the use of revenue management decreases resources acquired on average, and the effect of revenue management on expected profit is shown to be less significant with abundant capacity.

449410.value: To understand the dynamic interactive effects of family-relational values, occupational prestige, career interest and choice congruence on the career adaptability and commitment of Chinese university students in regions (cities) with different degrees of exposure and acculturation to Western. To inform counseling practitioners on how cultural and contextual factors influence career choice and behavior of Chinese university students so that culturally-sensitive career and psychotherapeutic interventions could be offered. To provide empirical findings that would contribute to the development of a career development framework with an emphasis on cultural and contextual factors. 449410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
449410.value: This proposed study aims to examine the interactive effects of personal interest, family relational values (filial piety, parental expectations) and social expectations (preference to pursue prestigious occupations) on the career development and career commitment of Chinese university students. Existing models of career counseling and development are influenced by Western-oriented values emphasizing individualism, self-determination, and personal actualization. The career counseling approaches resulting from these models often center on helping individuals to explore their individual self, and to uncover personal attributes (e.g., interest, values, skills) that could be used to identify “matching” occupations. A major limitation of these models and approaches is that they failed to take into considerations the importance of cultural and contextual factors specific to individuals from non-Western cultures, such as Chinese individuals. For individuals from a collective culture such as China, personal career interest is often influenced by cultural-contextual factors such as family relational values (e.g., filial piety and parental expectations) and social valuing (e.g., prestige level of occupations). Hence, in addition to assisting the person to understand their attributes, counseling efforts should also help the individuals negotiate with the social environment so that career decisions that could maximize individual expression and relational harmony could be made and implemented. With the above in mind, this proposed study will administer a number of inventories related to career interest, filial piety, parental expectations, preference for occupational prestige, and career adaptability and commitment. We hope to delineate the complex and dynamic relationship among personal (career interest), family relational values (filial piety, parental expectations), contextual variables (preference for occupational prestige) and career development competence (adaptability, commitment). We propose to collect data from Hong Kong and Chinese Mainland cities representing different degrees of exposure and acculturation to Western cultural values. The findings will help researchers to build theories and frameworks that could further our understanding on the career development of university students in Chinese communities. The findings will also inform practitioners in Chinese communities (e.g., university student counselors and student affairs professionals) on how cultural and contextual variables shaped students’ career choice and aspirations, so that on-target career counseling and guidance services could be offered to students. 本研究的目標擬在檢驗個人興趣、家庭關係價值觀（即，孝道和父母期望）以及社會期望（即，追求高聲望的職業）三者對於中國大學生的職業發展與職業承諾度所産生的重要交互效應。目前，關於職業輔導和事業發展的理論模型都主要受西方主導的價值觀念所影響，即强調個人主義、自我决定、以及個人實現等概念。在這些模型指導下應運而生的職業輔導方式則相應地著重於幫助個體去探索他們的自我世界，通過揭示自我的特徵（如，個人興趣、價值觀、技能等）來發現與他們相匹配的職業。然而，這些模型和輔導方式的主要局限在於它們未能充分考慮到文化與情境因素對放非西方文化的個體，如華人群體，所産生的重要影響。對於生活在集體主義文化大環境下的個體來說，以中國人爲例，個人的職業興趣往往要受到文化-情境因素的影響，包括家庭關係價值觀念（如，孝道和父母期望）以及社會的價值取向（如，職業的聲望水平）。因此，除了要幫助個體去理解他們自我的特性之外，職業輔導也應當努力幫助個體與周邊的社會環境進行協商、平衡。只有這樣，職業决策才能在顯明地表達個人內在聲音的同時，也幫助個人維持、實現人際關係的和諧。基於以上的分析，本研究擬採用一系列與事業興趣、孝道、父母期望、職業聲望偏好、以及職業適應力和職業承諾度有關的評估工具。我們希望能够揭示出個人變量（即職業興趣）、家庭關係價值觀變量（即孝道與父母期望）、情境變量（即職業聲望偏好）、以及職業發展能力變量（即職業適應力與職業承諾度）之間複雜的動力關係。我們計劃從香港、以及中國內地城市中收集數據。對城市樣本的選取會考慮到各城市對西方文化價值觀不同程度的接觸和融合。我們相信，這研究發現不僅將幫助研究者們進一步揭示華人大學生群體的職業發展，建議、完善相應的理論和框架；也將推動在華人社區中的實踐人員們（如，大學的學生輔導員、學生事務專業人員等）理解文化和情境因素如何影響著學生的職業選擇和職業抱負，以便對學生進行有效的事業咨詢與輔導。

449410.label: Realisation of objectives
449410.value: Objective 1 - Research measures on the key variables (e.g., family-related cultural values, occupational prestige, career interest, career adaptability) were identified and the reliability and validity of these measures were examined. - Data were conducted in four regions (Hong Kong, Shanghai, Beijing, and Langzhou). In the main study, university students were participants, even though the instrument development study (on the Personal Globe Inventory) involved senior secondary school students (n=479). A total of 1,412 students participated in the main study (653 female, 778 male; Hong Kong 390 students, Shanghai 394 students, Beijing 351 students, and Langzhou 296). - Data were then entered and analyzed (e.g., analysis of variance (ANOVA), discriminant function analysis, regression analysis, and structural equation modeling). - Findings were presented in major academic conferences, and research papers are being drafted and/or submitted to academic journals (Leung, Zhou, Ho, Li, Ho, & Tracey, in press, Journal of Vocational Behavior). One other paper is in the final writing stage and will be submitted soon. Objective 2 - The conceptualization and counseling implications of finding were examined and discussed in the research articles published or to be presented. - The findings and counseling implications (including culturally appropriate interventions) were presented in academic conferences in Australia, Chinese mainland, and United States, and France. Objective 3 - The findings of this study contributed to the development career development framework, such as cross-cultural career assessment framework (e.g., Leung et al., in press). - The analyses on the complex relationship among individual level variables (career interest congruence), contextual variables (occupational prestige), and family-cultural values (filial piety, parental expectations) has yield findings that would enrich theoretical conceptualization on how cultural factors affect career choice and development. Objective 4 - This study refined a number of career development measures, including career interest measure (Leung et al., in press), measure of career adaptability (Hou, Leung, Li, Li, & Xu, 2012), and measure of parental career expectations and filial piety. These measures are developed to tap into indigenous, cultural-specific elements of the variables, yet allowing for cross-cultural comparisons across different studies from diverse cultures. - The refined measures are made available for use for local and cross-cultural studies and applications. For instance, the PGI (interest measure) refined in this study is now adopted for use by Hong Kong secondary schools via the assessment platform of the Hong Kong Association of Career Masters and Guidance Masters.

449410.label: Major findings and research outcome
449410.value: 1) Effects of Culture-based relational variables (filial piety and parental career expectation) on students’ career adaptability Findings (e.g., from hierarchical regression, structural equation modeling) suggested that career adaptability (control, concern, curiosity, confidence) was associated with parental and self career expectations, especially expectations related to achieving independence/autonomy and professional standing through chosen careers. Filial piety based on reciprocity as opposed to authoritative adherence was also instrumental. Findings also revealed that students’ tendency to make premature career decisions (foreclosure) was associated with adherence to authoritative filial piety. 2) Effects of prestige on career adaptability and career commitment Students with a higher preference for career prestige tended to have a higher level of career adaptability than students with lower career prestige preference. The same was found for career exploration and commitment. 3) Did interest-choice congruence and prestige preference moderated the effects between family-relational values and career choice adaptability and career choice commitment The results suggested that individual-level variables (interest-choice congruence, interest-competence gap) had a much weaker effects than family relational values on career adaptability and career commitment. Findings from structural equation modeling revealed a partial mediating effect of prestige on the relation between reciprocal filial piety and career adaptability. The results under-scored the importance of including cultural and contextual variables in formulating career development models, especially in Asian Chinese cultural context. 4) Regional Differences There were regional differences on the variables but the differences did not result in different conclusions or model relevance. For instance, the strength of parental career expectations for students in Beijing and Shanghai were significantly higher than their counterparts in Langzhou and Hong Kong. The strength of reciprocal and authoritative filial piety was strongest in Shanghai and Langzhou. 5) Research Outcomes a. The development and refinement of research instruments that could be used to assess culture-related variables in Chinese communities (e.g., congruence measures and prestige using PGI, the Parental Career Expectation Scale). b. Dissemination of research findings through presenting in international academic conferences around the world (USA, Australia, France, China; Part C, #9) c. Publications of articles in refereed journal (e.g., Leung et al., 2014, Journal of Vocational Behavior; and one other in progress article; see Part C, #8). d. Development of culture-based career development and assessment models based on the findings of this study to be disseminated through the various presentations and publications. e. Three Ph.D students (Li Xixi, Zhou Sili, Hon Suet) were involved in implementing this research study and they conducted dissertation research studies that were further extension of this study. These students played an important role in assisting the project because the Research Assistant hired had to terminate appointment at the middle of the project due to health and family reasons and only re-joined at the ending part of the project on a fractional-time basis.

449410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
449410.value: Additional research work could be conducted to further understand the effects of Chinese family relational values on career development. First, research studies should obtain career expectation data directly from parents and comparing them to the perceptions of their children. Second, in-depth interviews could be conducted to understand how parental expectations, filial piety, and other contextual variables influenced career choice and development. Third, research should seek to understand strategies that Chinese parents used to influence, shape, and support the career development of children. Studies along these lines could generate new perspectives and frameworks to guide research and practice. The PI of this study is actively seeking to form a research team to apply for funding to conduct the above lines of research. The instruments refined in this study could be further developed and use in career development research and practice. For instance, the Chinese version of the Personal Globe Inventory (PGI) has been strengthened for clarity and language accuracy (e.g., Leung et al., 2014). It is a good research tool for studies in which career interest and self-efficacy are major variables. Additional research and development work are now underway to use the PGI in career guidance in Hong Kong secondary schools.

449410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
449410.value: Western career development theories and research have focused mostly on understanding how personal-level variables (e.g., interest and competence) influence career development. However, in a Chinese cultural context, there has been observation that culture-based relational factors (e.g., obeying one’s parents) are more critical. Accordingly, this study aimed to explore the effects of individual and cultural factors on the career development of Chinese students. Some key findings: - High perceived parental expectations might facilitate the development of adaptive career development competence, especially expectations related to achieving independence, autonomy, and professional standing through chosen careers. - The positive effects of parental expectation were enhanced when students (a) subscripted to a value of reciprocal filial piety (to repay for the love of parents), (b) preferred to pursue high prestige occupations, and (c) had career expectations that were similar to their parents. - Authoritative filial piety (that is, to obey and subscript to parental wishes) tended to contribute to pre-mature career decisions. - The effects of parental expectations, filial piety, and prestige preference on career adaptability and commitment were stronger than personal-level variables (e.g., interest). Overall, findings support the need to include culture-based relational factors in career development research and interventions.

450010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
450010.value: Chinese citizens have made numerous claims about what the government must not do, what they are entitled to receive from the government, and what they can do against the government. Those claims are generally framed in terms of rights. Moreover, rights talk is not simply empty talk. In numerous cases, efforts to claim rights have spurred disruptive protests. Scholars, however, disagree about how to understand rights claims and associated protests. Some researchers argue that the claims represent a nascent rights consciousness and suggest that protests driven by rights consciousness could "evolve into a more far-reaching counterhegemonic project." Harvard political scientist Elizabeth Perry, on the other hand, argues that what appears to be rights consciousness is a seasoned "rules consciousness." As Perry sees it, popular contention driven by rules consciousness can "undergird rather than undermine" the political system by providing "an effective check on the misbehavior of state authorities." The debate raises many important issues. What is rules consciousness? What is rights consciousness? How can we empirically tell one from the other? What factors may affect the growth and decline of rights and rules consciousness? In what ways may rights and rules consciousness affect people's propensity to engage in different modes of political participation and contention? In what ways can popular protests driven by rights and rules consciousness affect the direction and course of political development in contemporary China? The project aims to address these issues. First, it will examine to what extent Chinese people have rules consciousness and rights consciousness. Second, it will examine how individual-level factors such as life experiences and involvement in disputes affect rights and rules consciousness. Third, it will examine how contextual factors such as the local economic structure and the strength of local civil society affect rights and rules consciousness. Fourth, it will examine how rights consciousness and rules consciousness are associated with the propensity to engage in various modes of popular participation and contention. Fifth, it will explore whether popular protests driven by rules consciousness may help to pave the way for building the rule of law. Lastly, it will analyze how the mobilization of rights consciousness may help chart a course toward a more participatory political system. The project will be carried out over three years. It will produce a number of articles in top-tier political science journals and China studies journals and a university press book.

450010.label: Realisation of objectives
450010.value: Thanks to the funding, I have successfully administered a pilot survey on rights consciousness and rules consciousness. The newly designed survey measures of political trust, sense of equality, rights consciousness and rules consciousness turn out to be valid and reliable. Analyses show that the following working hypotheses have strong empirical support: (1) Chinese people have rules consciousness as well as rights consciousness; (2) rules consciousness is associated with the propensity to engage in popular contention that targets local rule-enforcement authorities; (3) rights consciousness is associated with the propensity to engage in popular contention that aims to push central rule-making authorities to change existing laws or policies or to make new laws or policies.

450010.label: Major findings and research outcome
450010.value: The project shows that the following working hypotheses are empirically supported: (1) Chinese people have rules consciousness as well as rights consciousness; (2) rules consciousness is associated with the propensity to engage in popular contention that targets local rule-enforcement authorities; (3) rights consciousness is associated with the propensity to engage in popular contention that aims to push central rule-making authorities to change existing laws or policies or to make new laws or policies. The pilot survey has also generated three new findings. First, Chinese people's trust in the Center is highly resilient in that many people may adjust their understandings about what the Center is and what trustworthiness means when they encounter problems that are thought to have an erosive effect on political trust. I have written an article about this finding, which has been published online with Modern China. Second, urban residents tend to have significantly weaker trust in the central government and stronger rights consciousness than rural residents. However, since the sample size is too small and the pilot survey covers only one rural county and one urban city, I plan to gather more evidence before I write up the finding. Lastly, the pilot survey opens up two new research questions. For one, it shows that in China the commonly observed pattern of having stronger confidence in the central government than in local governments may imply hidden distrust in the central government. I am currently using the China Survey data to explore if this is indeed the case. For another, it shows that the propensity to engage in rightful resistance may have an inverse-U shape relationship with relative distrust in local authorities.

450010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
450010.value: Further development of the research will depend on larger-scale surveys that cover more geographical areas. Given the logistical and financial challenges of doing national surveys, I plan to draw on analyses of the China Survey data to select localities where popular trust in the central government is particularly strong or particularly weak.

450010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
450010.value: Chinese citizens in the reform era have engaged in a wide variety of protest, demonstration and petition to defend or assert what they call lawful rights and interests. This project finds that more often than not Chinese people are demanding that national laws and central policies be faithfully implemented. Such claims about rights are based on rules consciousness, which is characterized by distrust in local rule-enforcement authorities and the understanding that ordinary people are equal with local authorities before the law. In some cases, however, protesters have also demanded that existing laws be changed or new ones made. Such claims about rights are based on rights consciousness, which is characterized by doubts about the rule-making central leadership and the understanding that ordinary people and national authorities are equal before the supra-political principles such as having common ancestors or obeying the Heavenly Way. It is important theoretically and practically to distinguish rules consciousness from rights consciousness. Popular protests based on rules consciousness pose no immediate threat to the existing political system, while popular protests based on rights consciousness call for innovative policy changes and/or political reforms.

450210.label: Project Objectives
450210.value: In order to realize the integrated model for Qinghai-Tibet railway deformation monitoring, four technical challenges and proposed solutions need to be carefully addressed, Geometric shape constraint: the geometric shape constraint is useful information for the railway identification and deformation monitoring. Thus it is valuable to introduce such information into the small baseline DInSAR procedures using a mask achieved from manual interpretation or GIS thematic layer. In the full-resolution small baseline DInSAR procedures, a space-time deformation parameters model will be employed. Phase unwrapping: when the SBAS model is introduced, phase unwrapping and calibration for each interferogram are essential for the following estimation of deformation parameters and residual topography. Taking into account the railway deformations may occur in decorrelation regions caused by seasonal frost, it will be a challenge of phase unwrapping for low quality interferograms. Thereby, in addition to introducing longer wavelength SAR data (L-band PALSAR), our developed ant colony optimization algorithm phase unwrapping method will be employed. GPS observation integration: retrieving reliable point-based deformation information with millimetric-centimetric accuracy, GPS data can be integrated in DInSAR procedures as follows. First, GPS observation provides reference data for phase calibration. And those data are also useful for phase unwrapping to suppress processing errors. Second, GPS data are useful for DInSAR-derived results accuracy estimation and validation. High resolution preservation: In general, the size in width scale is small for LMLFs, e.g. tens of meters for this railway project. As a result, it is necessary to preserve high spatial resolution to provide detailed deformation information. For this requirement, a full-resolution SBAS DInSAR method is developed to overcome this issue. Meanwhile, with the aid of SBAS scheme, ground deformation in limited SAR images circumstance will also be feasible.
