450210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
450210.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research to enhance the capability of monitoring Qinghai-Tibet railway deformation combining Differential SAR Interferometry (DInSAR) and Global Positioning System (GPS) observations. As a bridge between human being and the earth, large scale man-made linear features in modern society have played an essential role in physical distribution and energy transportation. Though with a wide extension, those linear features primarily concentrate upon infrastructure field, including railways, bridges, highways, dams, metro-lines and pipes. Qinghai-Tibet railway, a typical large scale man-made linear feature, passes through permafrost regions with about 550 km. The surface deformations due to seasonally freezing bulge and thawing subsidence have a great influence on the railway stability, resulting in hazards to engineering construction and maintenance in permafrost regions. Consequently, the surface deformation along this railway requires to be well monitored. DInSAR and GPS observations are both capable of providing ground deformation information with millimetric to centimetric accuracy. Such technologies confront with challenges in Qinghai-Tibet railway monitoring because of its large/linear geometric shape. First, the point-based GPS observation is not affordable to monitor a reasonably dense two-dimensional scenario, not to mention inaccessible regions along the railway. Secondly, although prevailing advanced DInSAR techniques have high potential for area-based ground deformation monitoring, applications shift from area-based to linear-based features are still questionable and unproved. In this project, we propose an integrated model taking the advantages of DInSAR and GPS techniques for Qinghai-Tibet railway deformation monitoring. The linear geometric shape and GPS-derived deformations are adequately considered in our model to modify the conventional advanced DInSAR methods. With the aid of our developed model, an early warning before a hazard can be issued to avoid or mitigate severe consequences, which is imperative for policy makers and emergency managers. The railway nearby Beilu River, Qinghai, China is selected as our study site because of the available SAR images and GPS observation data. The scientific significance of this study would also benefit in large-scale man-made linear features monitoring in Hong Kong and Pearl River Delta Region. 本項目擬聯合雷達差分乾涉技術和GPS差分技術，開發新型方法，增強對青藏鐵路地表形變的監測能力。 大型線狀人工地物已在現代生活的交通運輸和能源物流起著不可或缺作用。它們主要集中在基建領域，包括鐵路、橋樑、高速公路，大壩，市政地鐵、輸油管線等。青藏鐵路是一種典型的大型線狀人工地物，它貫穿了550 km的連續多年凍土。青藏鐵路多年凍土區每年都發生季節性融化和凍結，並伴生各種不良地質現象，因此為了保證安全運營，對其路基進行形變監測就顯得尤為重要。 雷達差分乾涉技術和GPS觀測技術都能提供毫米~厘米級的地表形變信息，然而這些技術因青藏鐵路特殊的幾何長寬比及惡劣作業環境面臨挑戰。首先，GPS技術很難在全程550km鐵路上獲取高密度的二維速度場信息，並且在一些人力不可達地區就顯得無能為力。其次，高級雷達差分乾涉技術在獲取面狀地表形變方面具有很好潛力，但當把它們應用到線狀目標監測時仍存在問題和亟待驗證。 在本研究中，針對青藏鐵路複雜實驗區，我們提出了一種集成雷達干涉和GPS差分技術的新模型。模型考慮了線狀地物的特殊幾何形狀及GPS形變信息，改變了常規多基線雷達干涉處理流程，使得災前形變預警成為可能，可有效避免或緩解潛在嚴重災害的損失；為應急管理者作出科學決策提供支撐。本研究的實施，對香港地區大型線狀人工地物監測同樣具有很好的借鑒意義。

450210.label: Realisation of objectives
450210.value: In the research, the major objectives have been realized. All the achieved outcomes as following: (1) Geometric shape constraint: For capturing the more detail and higher resolution deformation information, a space-time deformation parameters model has been proposed in the full-resolution small baseline DInSAR procedures. Preliminary deformation result along the Qinghai-Tibet Railway has been derived, showing that there are some areas with significant deformation. (2) Phase unwrapping: An ant colony optimization algorithm phase unwrapping algorithm has been developed, and used for PSInSAR and SBAS time series phase unwrapping. The experiments using L-band PALSAR data have proven that the new method obtained more robust and reliable phase unwrapped result; (3) GPS observation integration: Calibration of InSAR phase by exploiting of GPS data for retrieving the more accurate deformation of the Qinghai-Tibet Railway. The cross-validation between InSAR and GPS measurements has been performed also, revealing the consistent deformation rates derived by DInSAR has been improved significantly, which can reach millimetric-centimetric accuracy. (4) High resolution preservation: A new full-resolution SBAS DInSAR model has been developed with taking the SBAS strategy into consideration, which has the capability for surface displacement monitoring using a limited SAR images. In general, the main objetives of the project have been accomplished. However, there are some new findings are worthy of further works. Since the SAR platforms are used to right side-look working mode, the InSAR monitoring result is an one dimensional up-left observation. For comparatively analysis or validation purpose, the normal solution is projected the GPS or other 3D ground based observations to LOS direction. But for InSAR result in LOS direction, it is difficult to realize transformation from 1D to 3D, or just another direction. Therefore, the 3D model and relevant algorithms are worthy of further research, which is our long-term goals in the future.

450210.label: Major findings and research outcome
450210.value: For the successful implementation of this project, a InSAR research team has been working from 2010. We have proposed a new time series based InSAR model for surface displacement monitoring using a limited SAR images, and derived deformation result along the Qinghai-Tibet Railway. Additional, the following are the related works have been accomplished in our research. (1) Implementation optimization for the full-resolution SBAS model for capturing the more detail and higher resolution deformation information in time series. (2) Developing method for InSAR phase Calibration by exploiting of GPS data for retrieving the more accurate deformation of the Qinghai-Tibet Railway. (3) Improving the traditional time series based InSAR model and incorporating it to the 3-D phase unwrapping for high-resolution information preservation. Furthermore, we have published a number of academic papers in international magazines and important conferences, including 7 journal publications and 9 conference proceedings. The detail information has been listed Part 8-9 in the following. Two students of PhD full time (i.e. Cheng Shilai and Luo Qingli) have been supported by the project funding, for their thesis. Dr. Cheng has obtained doctoral degree in 30/5/2011, and Miss Luo is about to thesis defense in 31/7/2013.

450210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
450210.value: After synthetic aperture process, the resolution of radar image improved significantly to meters level. Meanwhile, the microwave signals to each target were compressed and recorded in one pixel, with complex format, including distance related phase (like GPS) and material related amplitude value. It means that only the radar line of sight projection of the displacements can be detected. Actually the InSAR monitoring result is an one dimensional up-left observation. For comparatively analysis or validation purpose, the normal solution is projected the GPS or other 3D ground based observations to LOS direction. But for InSAR result in LOS direction, it is difficult to realize transformation from 1D to 3D, or just another direction. Therefore, the 3D model and relevant algorithms are worthy of further research, which is our long-term goals in the future.

450210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
450210.value: Radar satellite remote sensing has been one of the foci of ISEIS, including InSAR methods for monitoring ground deformation of earthquake zone, urban ground subsidence, and stability of transportation facilities. In this research, a new method has been presented for monitoring the stability of the roadbed in the frozen ground zone of the depopulated region, which could be a valuable reference for further studies on the monitoring of deformation of large scale man-made linear features such as high-speed railway and highway networks. In additional, the research team has accumulated valuable experience in this process. Dr. Chen Fulong, Postdoctoral Fellow of the ISEIS won ShunjiMurai Award – the Best Paper Award of the 2011 annual conference of Asian Association on Remote Sensing (AARS 2011).

450410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
450410.value: Archaeological sites are an important cultural heritage. There are tens of thousands of archaeological sites in China, including 12 World Heritage sites. Recently, the Chinese government has made substantial efforts to preserve archaeological sites. Besides tourism, what are the social, political, economic, and ideological impetuses for this phenomenon? As economic development and heritage preservation both demand land and other resources, can archaeological sites survive in the wave of modernization and globalization in China? The government controls the conservation process and often ignores the local community’s interests and voices, so will conservation cause new social conflicts? What are the impacts of conservation upon local communities, their cultures and the local environment? In contrast to mainland China, the management of approximately 200 archaeological sites in Hong Kong has attracted very little attention. As land is extremely expensive in Hong Kong, many archaeological sites face the threat of being destroyed by commercial activities. Can archaeological sites survive in metropolitan Hong Kong? What is the local community’s perception and attitude towards archaeological sites? Further, do the different social, political and ideological structures in mainland China and Hong Kong influence the conservation of archaeological sites? What can mainland China and Hong Kong learn from each other in terms of managing their past in a changing world? This project aims to tackle these questions by comparatively examining the management of two archaeological sites, namely the Mogao Caves in Gansu Province, and the Rock Carving at Big Wave Bay on Hong Kong Island. The project will investigate: 1) diverse interpretations of the archaeological and cultural significance of the two sites by different stakeholders, and the causal factors and consequences of this diversity; 2) the impact of local ecological, economic, social and political structures, as well as modernization and globalization upon the management of the two sites, and 3) the impact of the management upon the local communities and environments. The project will have significant academic, social and educational value. First, it will reveal the academic, economic, social, political, and even ecological rationale for managing archaeological sites both in mainland China and Hong Kong. Second, it will examine the impact of this management upon the local people and the environment, and propose suitable polices for managing archaeological sites not only in China but also in Asia more generally. Third, it will produce new data for liberal studies in secondary schools and teaching in tertiary institutes. 考古學遺址是重要的文化遺產之一。中國大陸有數以萬計的考古學遺址，其中超過10個為世界文化遺產。近年來，中國政府在考古學遺址的保育方面付出了可觀的努力。除了旅遊之外，這一政府行為還有什麼經濟、社會、政治和意識形態的原因？此外，考古遺址的保育和經濟發展均需要大量土地和其它資源；考古遺址是否能夠在中國現代化和全球化的大潮中生存？中國政府全盤掌控文物保育事業，通常忽視社區的需要，這樣的“保育”會否引起新的社會衝突？考古遺址的保育對當地的環境、社區及其文化有什麼影響？ 另一方面，儘管香港也有大約200個考古遺址，公眾對這些遺址的保育卻缺乏關注。香港的土地非常昂貴，相當多的考古學遺址可能因為現代經濟活動而受到破壞。考古學遺址在香港是否可以被保存下來？香港社會對於考古學遺址的保育抱什麼態度？更進一步，中國大陸與香港不同的社會、政治和意識形態架構，又是否影響到考古學遺址的保育？大陸和香港是否可以互相借鑒對方的經驗？ 本研究項目旨在通過對比中國大陸和香港管理考古學遺址的經驗，探討上列問題。本項目選擇了中國大陸的敦煌莫高窟和香港的大浪灣石刻作為個案，探討下列問題： 1.不同的持份者對同一考古學遺址之文化重要性是否有不同的解讀；如是，為何會出現這些不同的解讀。 2.當地自然環境、經濟、社會和政治架構，以及現代化和全球化對考古學遺址保育的影響。 3.考古學遺址的管理對當地社區文化及其環境的影響。 本項目的研究結果將具有學術、社會和教育價值。首先，本研究將反映中國大陸和香港考古學遺址管理的學術、經濟、社會、政治甚至生態原因。第二，本研究將反映考古學遺址管理對當地社區和環境之影響；第三，研究結果可為中學通識教育和大學教育提供新資料。

450410.label: Realisation of objectives
450410.value: The first four objectives have been completely achieved, and some localized policies and managerial approaches have been discussed and proposed. However, as different stakeholders have different economic, ecological and political interests, and some of the interests are conflicting and cannot be negotiated, it is very difficult to find policies and managerial approaches which can be accepted by all stakeholders as "suitable, efficient and sustainable", particularly at the Mogao Caves in Gansu Province, mainland China, where the government and the social elite have a dominating power, while members of the local community have virtually no power in terms of archaeological site management. This problem is a result of the current political, administrative and educational structure in mainland China, and cannot be overcome by merely conducting academic research. The case at the Big Wave Bay, Hong Kong, shows another story. According to our fieldwork, apart from the Hong Kong SAR government, the majority of all other stakeholders, namely tourists, villagers and members of the Hong Kong community, show very little interest in the archaeological site, and are not concerned with the policies and managerial approaches. Only a few local residents who are foreigners have some interests in the management of the archaeological site, and they agree that the current policies and approaches are good enough. In summary, the result of our project manifests that some archaeological sites in both mainland China and Hong Kong are meaningless to the general public today. Consequently, the general public does not have much interest in the management of these archaeological sites and/or are powerless in the process. This is another type of social alienation. Without the participation of the community, it is probably impossible to have efficient, suitable and sustainable policies and managerial approaches. However, to empower the local community and facilitate community participation in the management of archaeological sites in mainland China and Hong Kong, changes must be made in the political, administrative and education sections of the society.

450410.label: Major findings and research outcome
450410.value: 1. We have comparatively examined the construction of the cultural significance of the Mogao Caves in Gansu, and the rock carving at the Big Wave Bay in Hong Kong. The main stakeholders of the Mogao Caves are central and local governments and their agencies, the Dunhuang Academy, local and overseas scholars, local communities (including villagers and urban residents) and tourists. The stakeholders in the Big Wave Bay are HK SAR government and its agency, local scholars, local villagers and residents, and tourists. The significance, authenticity and integrity of the Mogao Caves are constructed by the government, the Dunhuang Academy and scholars with their own agenda and interests, while the significance, authenticity and integrity of the rock carvings at the Big Wave Bay are constructed by the government agency and local scholars. 2. Each group of stakeholders at the two archaeological sites have their own economic, social, ideological, spiritual, political and ecological interests. The interests between members of the same group may also vary. For example, the economic and political interests between the Dunhuang city and the Gansu provincial government are not the same, though both are governments. Some inter- or intra-group interests can be reconciled but others cannot, such as the conflict of economic interests between the local government and some villagers in Dunhuang. However, as the management of the Mogao Caves is controlled by the government and the Dunhuang Academy, while the local community does not have a say, it seems that the conflict and negotiation of interests between different stakeholders have not had significantly negative impact on the management of the Mogao Caves at the moment. No significant conflict of interests has been found in the Hong Kong case. 3. The impact of modernization and globalization upon the management of the two archaeological sites are significant, particularly at Dunhuang, where the conservation techniques and managerial approaches have been much influenced by overseas funding, techniques, expertise, and the internet. 4. The impact of archaeological site management upon the environment and local culture is very apparent at Dunhuang, where tourism has become an economic foundation of the region, with the Mogao Caves being the main attraction. The decline of farming as an economic activity is ecologically more suitable as much less water is required. 5. It is proposed to encourage members of the local community to participate in the management of archaeological sites; however as discussed in 5.3 there are problems.

450410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
450410.value: Based on findings of this project, as well as other projects being done in the last decade, it seems that many archaeological sites in Hong Kong and mainland China are alienated to ordinary members of the contemporary society, while being economically and politically used by the government or/and other powerful stakeholders. Thus, what is the social meaning of preserving archaeological sites in this context? Is it socially justifiable to use public resources (money and land etc.) to preserve archaeological sites just for the benefit of certain social segments? Is it necessary to encourage community participation in the preservation process, and what can be done if the majority of the community refuses to participate (as in the case in Hong Kong)? Should the management of archaeological sites be an empowerment process for the less powerful, or is it OK to let the powerful getting more power and the less powerful be further marginalized since they are not interested in the issue? If not, then what changes should be made and how? These are questions for further studies.

450410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
450410.value: This project comparatively studies the economic, political and ecological impacts of archaeological site management upon the local people, their way of life and the local environment at Dunhuang, Gansu Province, and a village at Hong Kong Island. At Dunhuang, the development of tourism with the Mogao Caves as a main attraction, plus modernization and globalization, have profoundly changed the economic and social structure of the local community and enlarged the gap between the rich and the poor, but tourism is also more environmental friendly compared to farming, as the latter demands much more water than the former, and water is crucial in the Dunhuang oasis. On the contrary, the archaeological site in Hong Kong plays a very limited role in the local economy and has attracted little attention, raising the question of the lack of public participation in heritage management.

450910.label: Project Objectives
450910.value: To investigate the historical, theoretical and intellectual bases of the romantic fantasy; To undertake in-depth structural analysis of three mature fantasies by Schubert (the Wanderer Fantasy for piano solo, D. 760; the Fantasy in C major for Violin and Piano, D. 934; and the Fantasy in F minor for Piano Duet, D. 940); To expand and refine a critical model (‘the lyric-paratactic paradigm’) for Schubert’s mature instrumental style, and to explore its broader generic and theoretical implications; To investigate the hybrid nature of the fantasia genre in the early nineteenth century through examining its cross-fertilisation with sonata and variation conventions; To examine the stylistic, formal and aesthetic differences between the late 18th-century free fantasia and the romantic fantasy towards addressing problems of generic definition; To address critical questions arising from the conquest of improvisation by composition in 19th-century music, as exemplified in the Schubert fantasies; To explore the viability of the lyric as a canonical paradigm for 19th-century instrumental form.

450910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
450910.value: While recent research recognises that Schubert’s formal and harmonic innovations constitute an alternative to the dynamic, teleological narratives favoured by Beethoven, the generic implications of these innovations have largely been overlooked. I aim to explore these implications by studying the generic interaction between sonata and fantasy in the three mature fantasies by Schubert (D.760, D.934 and D.940). The fantasy is chosen for its generic fluidity. Works entitled ‘fantasies’ around 1800 may range from large-scale, sonata-like compositions to variations on popular tunes, and there was also considerable semantic and conceptual overlap between uses of the term ‘fantasy’ to refer to the instrumental genre, the act of improvisation, and the creative imagination. These ambiguities raise critical questions concerning generic definitions and boundaries in the 19th century. Furthermore, whereas the 18th-century free fantasia simulates spontaneous improvised performance via temporal displacements, textural contrasts, adventurous harmonies and affective discontinuities, Schubert’s fantasies comprise sections that are thematically distinct, formally closed, and affectively unified. They allude to the formal conventions of the classical sonata cycle, and thus seem to contradict Romantic aesthetic emphases on freedom and personal expression. Yet these seemingly static sections also often occupy remotely-related key areas, simultaneously creating the impression of foreground stability and the opposite effect of large-scale structural dissonance. What in the free fantasia were ephemeral flashes of harmonic colour now crystallise into aural images, directing the audience to perceive them as aesthetic moments. I contend that, in displacing the interplay between order and disorder in the fantasy from style to form, Schubert initiated a fundamental shift in the fantasia’s aesthetic conception. This shift, in turn, reflects a lyrical conception of musical discourse that offers not only a prototype for later 19th-century tonal practice, but also a strategy for reconciling the conquest of improvisation by composition with the romantic imperative of expression. Key issues and problems arising from this hypothesis will be modelled hierarchically, radiating outward from structural analyses of the three Schubert fantasies to broader generic, theoretical and aesthetic considerations. A paradigm for the lyric mode in Schubert’s instrumental discourse, developed in my earlier research, will be refined and expanded towards addressing these questions. The research outcome will embrace journal articles and conference papers, and likely constitute a substantial part of a monograph on lyricism in Schubert’s instrumental music. It may also provide the groundwork for a broader study of sonata-infused instrumental genres in the 19th century.

450910.label: Realisation of objectives
450910.value: Objectives 1, 4 and 5: Fully achieved through: • Comprehensive survey of primary sources between 1750 and 1850, including (1) published keyboard fantasies, (2) composition and keyboard treatises, and (3) music criticism and reviews, with focus on the fantasy’s generic definition, taxonomy of subtypes, and intersections with sonata and variation conventions; • Comparison of Schubert’s discursive strategies with that in Beethoven’s sonata-fantasy pieces; • Original analyses of selected nineteenth-century sonata-fantasy hybrids, with a view of comparison with Schubert’s practice. Hummel’s Piano Sonata in F# minor, Op. 81 (1819) and Schumann, Fantasie in C, Op. 17 (1836) received detailed attention. • Study of key philosophical and literary texts in the German idealist tradition, with focus on theories of the creative imagination. Objective 2: Structural analyses of D. 760, D. 934 and D. 940 were completed. Objectives 3 and 7: The lyric-paratactic paradigm has been expanded and refined through: • Incorporating Friedrich Schiller’s conception of the elegy from Naïve and Sentimental Poetry and notion of play-drive from On the Aesthetic Education of Man in a Series of Letters; • Adapting the literary critic J. Hillis Miller’s model of ‘linguistic moment’ in Romantic poetry. The paradigm’s broader generic and theoretical implications, and viability as a model for nineteenth-century instrumental form beyond Schubert, have been explored through: • Contextualization within other studies of nineteenth-century musical genre, especially Jeffrey Kallberg’s and Jim Samson’s work on Chopin; • Comparison with other models of nineteenth-century form, especially Janet Schmalfeldt’s neo-Hegelian perspective of ‘processual form’ and Peter H. Smith’s theory of ‘dimensional counterpoint’; • Integration with Schenkerian analytical methodology. Objective 6: A number of critical and methodological issues arise from the apparent absence of improvisatory style in the Schubert fantasies and their displacement of the interplay between order and disorder from within the domain of style to larger, cross-dimensional negotiations. These issues have been addressed through: • Expanding the scope of analytical study to include pieces not explicitly entitled fantasies, as well as chamber music; • Theoretical examination of implications for Schenkerian theory. The main problems I faced were not methodological but practical. As previously reported, publication of two research outputs were delayed or cancelled: • Change of editorship at Cambridge University Press delayed publication of the monograph on Schubert’s late style to early 2016 (see email correspondence included in Part ‘C’;) • An article that compares D. 760 and D. 940 was accepted by the Schubert-Jahrbuch in 2012, but publication of the next issue has been indefinitely delayed for lack of funding. I have since withdrawn my article and will instead include the research findings in my book-in-progress. I also considerably over-estimated the budget for reasons explained in previous reports. The balance has been refunded to UGC.

450910.label: Major findings and research outcome
450910.value: Research outcome constitutes a substantial portion of a book-in-progress (#6). It also yielded 3 articles (#s 1, 2, 4), 1 translation and edition with critical commentary (#3), 1 peripheral publication (#5), and 3 conference papers. Major findings: 1. Fantasies published between 1750 and 1850 were comprehensively surveyed and classified into five subtypes: (1) free fantasy (2) sonata-fantasy, (3) introductions to set forms (fantasy and variation, fantasy and fugue, etc.) (4) potpourri, and (5) fantasy on famous themes. Discussions of fantasy and sonata styles in late 18th- and 19th-century composition and keyboard treatises were also studied. The findings provide the necessary historical context for understanding the generic hybridization between fantasy, sonata, and theme and variation in Schubert’s instrumental practice (see outputs #s 2, 6). 2. Structural analyses of selected works by Schubert reveal that the critical engagement between genres in his music manifests itself through the blending of formal archetypes, the re-contextualisation of Classical formal functions and the repetition of salient sonic gestures, which result in lateral dichotomies across sectional divisions and vertical disjunctions between structural levels. Consideration of the technical innovations in these works and the aesthetic background to their genesis address critical questions arising from the fantasy’s generic fluidity in the nineteenth century (see output #s 2, 4, 6). 3. Close reading of primary texts on theories of the creative imagination, cross referenced with biographical documents pertaining to Schubert, led to the identification of Friedrich Schiller as a major aesthetic influence on Schubert (see output #6). 4. Development of a new analytical paradigm that integrates the PI's earlier work on lyricism in Schubert with two tropes taken from Friedrich Schiller’s Naïve and Sentimental Poetry and On the Aesthetic Education of Man in a Series of Letters. Specifically, I argue that Schiller’s conception of the elegy, which posits the dialectical opposition between ideal and reality, and his notion of play-drive (Spieltrieb), which mediates between the sensuousness of intuitions and desires (Stofftrieb) and the urge to impose order on feelings and experiences (Formtrieb), have multiple resonances with Schubert’s constructions of subjectivity (see output #6). Additionally, the structural opacity and semantic polyvalence resulting from the simultaneous projection of multiple temporal scales in Schubert’s discourse may be usefully modelled by adapting J. Hillis Miller’s notion of ‘linguistic moment’ (see output #s 1, 6) 5. Situation of the early Schenkerian reception of Schubert, and recent theories of nineteenth-century musical form, within the German idealist philosophical tradition (see output #s 3, 5).

450910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
450910.value: Potential for further development: 1. The critical paradigm developed in this project may be applied to the analysis of other works by Schubert; 2. Expansion of analytical scope to include Schubert’s vocal music; 3. Further exploration of Schubert’s intellectual debt to writers in the German idealist tradition, and comparison with contemporaneous literary developments; 4. My methodology, which integrates technical analysis with literary and philosophical considerations, may illustrate the hermeneutic potential of the interdisciplinary approach for other scholars; 5. The research outcome on generic hybridization may provide the groundwork for a broader study of sonata-infused instrumental genres in the 19th century; 6. The identification of structural and form-functional ambiguities in Schubert’s music has strong methodological implications for Schenkerian theory. Proposed course of action: 1. Continual preparation of book manuscript is a top priority. 2. Presentation of new research output at refereed international conferences and journals.

450910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
450910.value: This project studies the interaction between fantasy and sonata in Schubert’s mature instrumental music. Structural analyses of selected works by Schubert reveal that the critical engagement between genres manifests itself through the blending of formal archetypes, the re-contextualisation of Classical formal functions and the repetition of salient sonic gestures, which result in lateral dichotomies across sectional divisions and vertical disjunctions between structural levels. I propose that Schubert initiated a fundamental shift in the fantasy’s development by displacing the interplay between order and disorder that is the genre’s defining characteristic from within the domain of style to larger, cross-dimensional negotiations, and that this shift is informed by the aesthetics of Friedrich Schiller, an author whose influence on Schubert has hitherto received little scholarly attention. After establishing Schubert’s familiarity with Schiller’s writings through biographical documents pertaining to the composer, I propose a new discursive paradigm for Schubert that draws upon two tropes taken from Schiller: his conception of the elegy, which posits a dialectical opposition between ideal and reality, and his notion of play-drive (Spieltrieb), which mediates between materiality and form. I believe that my approach not only informs our understanding of Schubert’s compositional strategies, but may also provide the groundwork for a broader study of sonata-infused instrumental genres in the 19th century.

451010.label: Project Objectives
451010.value: We introduce a new construct, "historical ties". The traditional international business literature has focused on the location-specific attributes of host countries as the key driving force behind FDI. This project focuses on historical ties between countries as additional factors affecting the investment decisions of firms. Historical ties create a unique institutional framework that guides the choices of individuals, policy makers, and firms, and thus reduces uncertainty. They take two general types: informal and formal. Informal ties are those that evolve naturally as a result of geographic proximity, colonization, immigration, or missionary activities. These ties are developed in a path-dependent manner and are strongly bound by a common cultural heritage, such as language, religion, as well as social practices and conventions. Formal ties are created intentionally and usually take the form of agreements, treaties, and alliances aimed at promoting mutual national interests. Both forms of ties create an institutional framework within which economic exchange (e.g., FDI flow) between countries takes place. We make an attempt to “bring history back into international business” (Jones and Khanna, 2004) by examining how historical ties influence the flow of FDI between home and host countries. Understanding the historical background to cross-country relations is of particular importance for the study of international business in Asian countries and in other less developed countries, because many of these countries have complex histories of foreign dominance involving colonization, invasion, occupation, or alliances. Despite the importance of this factor, in the existing literature on international trade and investment, the history of cross-country relations is “treated in a stylized fashion with little concern for the complexities of particular historical situations” (Jones & Khanna, 2006: 460). Adopting a historical perspective brings into focus the role played by past ties in the foreign investment decisions of today and provides additional insights into existing theories of FDI. We provide additional evidence to "distance" research. In examining the effects of cross-country relationship on FDI flows, many researchers have used the "distance" in a certain attribute, such as culture, administrative practices, geographic proximity, or economic development, between the home and host countries. Distance research, however, focuses merely on the static comparison of location-specific attributes that reside independently in these countries. Our study focuses on the ties between countries over and above the distance attributes and examines how such ties influence FDI decisions.

451010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
451010.value: Research of foreign direct investment (FDI) has focused on country-specific factors of independent countries and examined how these factors would influence the flow of FDI across the world. More recently, researchers suggest that the distance in culture, institutions, geographic proximity, and economic development between countries matters for the direct investment decisions of foreign firms. This stream of research assumes that key factors affecting FDI flow are immobile across countries and focuses on the static comparison of location-specific attributes that reside independently in countries. It, however, ignores the effects of “relational” factors that are historically developed between pairs of countries. Our proposed project focuses on the ties between countries as additional factors affecting the investment decisions of firms. Ties are defined in this study as historical relations that are developed intentionally (Formal ties) or evolve naturally over time (Informal ties) between a specific pair of countries. In this project, we argue that historical ties - both formal and informal - between countries significantly influence the world flow of FDI and examine how much the effects of historical ties improve the explanatory power of the conventional models of FDI such as the distance model. 關於對外直接投資（FDI）的研究曾集中於討論單個國家的某些具體因素對全球FDI流動的影響。最近，有學者提出外國公司直接投資決策受國家之間存在的文化，制度，地理位置和經濟發展差異的影響。這類研究通常假定影響FDI流動的關鍵要素是穩定存在于國與國之間的，然後靜態地比較各國的區位屬性。但是，這類研究忽視了國家之間由於長期歷史發展而形成的“關係”因素所帶來的影響。本項目將國與國之間的聯繫作為公司投資決策的額外影響因素。研究定義的聯繫包含國家之間通過長期有意識地發展而形成的歷史關係（正式聯繫）和特定國家之間經長期自然演化而形成的關係（非正式聯繫）。在項目研究中，我們提出國家間正式和非正式的聯繫對全球FDI 的流動存在顯著影響，並檢視這些聯繫對常見的FDI模型，如距離模型解釋力的具體改善程度。

451010.label: Realisation of objectives
451010.value: We believe that we have successfully achieved all of the three objectives proposed. Below are brief summaries of our achievements in relation to each of the objectives. Objective 1 We extended the level of analysis from a single national context to a “relational” national context. Many previous IB studies have investigated the institutional environments in home and host countries separately, and then examined how these environments would affect IB practice. However, few studies have investigated the institutional contexts embedded in both the formal and informal ties that have historically developed between countries. While the “relational” perspective has proliferated in the literature on strategic management, the scope of its application to IB research has been very limited for example, the formation, mode, and survival of international joint ventures and alliances. Our studies have applied the relational perspective at a national level to explain how historical ties circumvent distance and facilitate the flow of cross-border business exchanges. Objective 2 We consistently argue throughout our studies that IB practices are constrained by a number of complex factors, such as the enforcement mechanisms, norms of behavior, and cognitive structures of local constituents. These institutional and cultural factors are developed and shaped in an incremental and path-dependent manner. Our study shed light on the role of history in explaining the impact of institutions on IB practices and regional development. As we will discuss below in detail, we conducted a comprehensive review of the literature on business systems, institutions, and organizations in Asia; developed a conceptual foundation of historical ties and institutional development; and conducted empirical investigations of the practice of IB from the historical perspective. Objective 3 We have done a preliminary analysis, using a small sample of inward FDI in Vietnam. In particular, this study examined three major historical factors that affect cross-country ties in Vietnam, namely, Chinese occupation and conflict, French colonization, and socialist ideology, and the ways in which these historically developed ties have influenced the direct investment decisions of foreign firms in this country. The results indicate that historical ties significantly improve the explanatory power of the distance model. The final version of the study was published in Journal of International Business Studies.

451010.label: Major findings and research outcome
451010.value: The conventional IB research has focused on location, firm, and transactional characteristics as the key determinants of FDI, as exemplified by Dunning’s OLI framework, and political factors have generally been treated as given or exogenous to FDI decisions. However, our findings show that historical ties and events can play active roles in initiating FDI in the process of economic development of the nations. Without an understanding of historical backgrounds in cross-country relations, IB research including distance research may provide misleading implications for IB practices. Below are the key findings of our studies. First, our study published in JIBS shows that firms from Mainland China have tended to be late investors compared with those from Taiwan or Hong Kong. This finding is particularly interesting, because all three regions share the same cultural traits and are geographically close together. The behavior of Mainland Chinese firms has to be explained by the strained relations between Vietnam and Mainland China following the Sino-Vietnamese War. Another notable finding is that, although many of the socialist countries in our sample (i.e., former members of Comecon tend to invest in former Soviet republics. Similarly, and consistent with our prediction, French ties, when defined as a broader group of la Francophonie, had a significant and positive effect on early entry of FDI. Second, our study published in the "Multidisciplinary Insights from New AIB Fellows" shows that a historical development of political ties has a critical influence on FDI flows. In this study, we investigated the record of national political leaders’ visits between 2000 and 2012, and examined two types of information: the number of political leaders’ visits to foreign countries from China, and the number of political leaders’ visits to China from foreign countries. We found a clear increase in the numbers of both kinds of political visits over the years. However, the balance between these numbers varies across countries, depending on China’s political and economic dependence on the host countries. For example, our evidence suggests that foreign leaders from the former Soviet Union visit China more often than Chinese leaders visit these countries, reflecting China’s decreasing dependence on the former Soviet Union countries. Third, our study published in the Oxford Handbook on Asian Business Systems provides (1) a comprehensive review of the literature on business systems, institutions, and organizations in Asia; and (2) an empirical investigation about the long term trend of strategic behavior and performance of Asian enterprises. This study convincingly shows that understanding of historical factors (economic, political, social, and cultural underpinnings) is critical for explaining the long-term changes in strategic behavior and performance of the Asian enterprises. The study under review at GSJ extends the historical perspective to explain different paths of development in the three industrial zones in China.

451010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
451010.value: Foreign direct investment (FDI) research has robustly shown that country- specific factors, such as factor endowments, a country’s capability to innovate, and institutions, play a major role in explaining FDI flows. However, it assumes that such factors are less mobile, if not immobile, across countries, and thus provide few insights regarding how countries can develop particular relation-specific attributes that play a pivotal role in enhancing cross-border economic exchanges, beyond the effects of the comparative advantages of countries. A series of our studies suggest, although preliminarily, that FDI flows can be enhanced by developing close ties between home and host countries, and by avoiding conflicts. In addition, we strongly believe that the IB literature will benefit greatly from work with a historical perspective to advance our understanding of a nation’s underlying social and cultural structures that affect the development and evolution of organization and business systems in an economy. As such, the historical perspective provides new insights to the theories of the firm. Our wish is to continue to shape the conceptual framework of the historical perspective and develop more solid methodologies for analysis of the historical data (both large sample and case-based studies).

451010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
451010.value: The conventional research of foreign direct investment assumes that decision makers are rational, making the investment decision based on the economic analysis of cost and benefit. We argue that the process of such decision can also be influenced by unique historical factors in a region and country. A country’s institutions evolve in a path-dependent manner, with cross-country relations developing as a consequence of a variety of historical events. However, as Jones and Khanna (2006, p. 460) argued, IB researchers have tended to treat history “in a stylized fashion with little concern for the complexities of particular historical situations.” A series of our studies have focused on advancing our understanding how history matters for IB practices and how the historical perspective can complement the conventional economics-based theories of foreign direct investment and multinational enterprises. Jones, G., & Khanna, T. 2006. Bringing history (back) into international business. Journal of International Business Studies, 37(4): 453–468.

451210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
451210.value: In the proposed research, we will develop and test different measures of reading comprehension and writing composition for Hong Kong and Beijing Chinese adolescents ages 12-15 and explore early childhood and concurrent linguistic and metalinguistic correlates of these across three years. The present proposal requests a follow-up of an ongoing longitudinal study (funded by the RGC) that began when the children were 9-16 months old. Those children, currently 160 from Hong Kong and 290 from Beijing, are now ages 10-12 years old. This research began as an early language study and progressed to a focus on early literacy skills, with a strong emphasis on morphological processing. The participants have now clearly progressed from “learning to read” to “reading to learn,” and issues related to their language and literacy skills now center on effective communication, namely reading comprehension and writing composition. We seek to examine longitudinal and concurrent correlates of reading comprehension and writing skills across three years, spanning from approximately ages 12-15 years old (note that the Beijing sample is approximately one year ahead of the Hong Kong sample in age). There are at least three features that make this proposed study uniquely important. First, we have a wide range of childhood reading-related measures across a number of years to examine in relation to both reading comprehension and writing composition. Second, the writing composition skills we plan to tap across the coming three years have rarely, if ever, been explored in Chinese children and adolescents; indeed, there are only a handful of such studies in any language. Third, our aim is, as much as possible, to tap reading comprehension and writing composition skills in both Chinese, the mother tongue, but also in English, a standard second language for these children. This exploration should yield solid data on a) early predictors of reading comprehension and writing composition skills, b) concurrent and subsequent predictors and components of reading comprehension and writing composition in early adolescents, and c) comparisons of such predictors and components in the same children for Chinese and English. 我們將利用三年時間，發展並測量不同的閱讀理解及寫作能力的測驗方法，用以評估香港及北京十二至十五歲青少年的閱讀理解及寫作能力。同時，我們會將這些青少年在兒童時期語言能力上的綜合表現與現時的閱讀理解測驗的表現進行對照，藉以探索兩者的相關性。 此項研究是我們先前的一項追踪研究的延續。先前研究(由大學教育資助委員會資助)的兒童均從九至十六個月大起便開始進行追踪測量，其中香港兒童佔一百六十個，北京佔二百九十個。這些兒童現年已十至十二歲。該項研究由最初集中研究兒童的早期語言發展，發展至後來著力研究兒童的早期讀寫能力，特別著重語素認知方面的能力。參與研究的小朋友，明顯地由最初的「學習為閱讀」，進展成現時的「閱讀為學習」。同時，有關他們在語言及讀寫能力的評估，現時亦集中到有效的溝通上，包括閱讀理解和寫作能力。 我們期望利用三年的時間，探索這些青少年，介乎十二至十五歲 (注：北京的樣本大概較香港的樣本年長一歲)，在追踪研究時及現時的閱讀理解和寫作能力的相關性。此項研究具備三項特點，足以突出其獨特的重要性。首先，我們擁有廣泛的兒童讀物—歷年用以評估閱讀理解和寫作能力的相關素材。其次，我們計劃裏所評估的寫作能力，過去甚少以中國兒童和青少年作為對象。再者，我們不單旨在評估這些青少年在他們的母語—中文的閱讀理解和寫作能力，他們的第二語言—英文，亦是我們評估的關注點。我們堅信上述的探索定能為以下範疇提供可靠的數據：一. 預測閱讀理解和寫作能力的早期要素；二.青少年在閱讀理解和寫作能力上，現時和往後的表現的預測要素及組成部份；三.同一個兒童在中文及英文上，這些預測要素和組成部份的比較。

451210.label: Realisation of objectives
451210.value: We had four objectives for this project (see project objectives). Overall, we achieved almost all of our research objectives of this project. First, we have developed new measures of reading comprehension both in Chinese and in English for Chinese-English senior students aged 12-15. These measures have been successfully used and adopted by several research groups. These measures might be very useful for helping to develop a standardized reading comprehension task for diagnosing and screening those children with reading comprehension difficulties both in Chinese and in English. Second, we have developed an evaluation model of Chinese children’s writing composition which includes seven dimensions. This evaluation model has been validated using data from both Hong Kong and Beijing. However, we also found that the evaluation model for Hong Kong children’s writing was a bit different from the evaluation model for Beijing children’s writing composition. Specifically, the dimension of the organization criteria was more valued in Hong Kong children, but the meaning aspect evaluation of relevance was more important in evaluating Beijing children’s writing composition. In addition, our mechanical and grammatical error analysis of children’s writing composition showed that while Beijing and Hong Kong children exhibited common mechanical and grammatical errors, we also found some differences in spelling and grammatical errors between Beijing and Hong Kong children. These findings suggest that writing is not only cognitively shaped but also culturally-invented. Third, we found some important cognitive- and linguistic-related predictors for Chinese reading, writing and English reading and writing. More specifically, we found that morphological awareness, vocabulary knowledge, tone knowledge and syntactic skills are uniquely and longitudinally predictive of Chinese reading comprehension in Chinese senior graders. Speed, writing fluency, vocabulary knowledge and syntactic skills are significantly correlated with Chinese writing composition, and vocabulary and word reading are important predictors of writing composition in English for Chinese-English speaking children.

451210.label: Major findings and research outcome
451210.value: A number of important findings, leading to several publications in some top journals in education and psychology research (see the papers listed in Part C), have been derived from this longitudinal study. More specifically, the findings and outcomes of this study were the following: 1). We developed measures for reading comprehension in both Chinese (L1) and English (L2). These measures are reliable in testing Chinese children’s ability in reading comprehension in both Chinese and English across Hong Kong and Beijing societies. They have been used in several papers. 2). We also found that some cognitive- and linguistic-related factors were uniquely and longitudinally predictive of Chinese children’s reading comprehension. For example, vocabulary knowledge and morphological awareness and phonological skills were found to be significantly correlated with Chinese children’s reading comprehension. Syntactic skills were also found to be reciprocally related with Chinese children’s reading comprehension in Chinese. 3).Our data revealed that vocabulary knowledge for English as well as phonological awareness, and English word reading were longitudinal predictors of Chinese children’s reading comprehension in English. 4). Writing evaluation models for Chinese children’s writing composition were developed and validated across Chinese societies (i.e., Hong Kong and Beijing). We developed a seven-dimension scheme for Chinese children’s writing composition evaluation. We found that five dimensions consisting of depth, sentence level, paragraph level, key element and overall intelligibility were important for Hong Kong children’s writing composition evaluation. Compared to the model for Hong Kong children’s writing evaluation, one dimension of meaning, which we termed “relevance,” replaced the dimension that we called “key elements” for the evaluation model for Beijing children’s writing composition. 5). The model developed for Hong Kong Chinese children’s writing composition in Chinese also fit well Hong Kong children’s writing composition in English. 6). We also found that Chinese word dictation, phonological awareness, speed of processing, speeded naming and handwriting fluency were all correlated with Chinese children’s overall writing quality. 7). Rapid automatized naming (RAN) and word reading in English were found to be significantly correlated with Chinese children’s English word spelling. Collectively, the findings and outcome of this project are both of theoretical and practical importance for understanding Chinese children’s reading comprehension and writing composition in both L1 Chinese and L2 English.

451210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
451210.value: Although several important findings have been revealed in this longitudinal study, there is still much that is unknown regarding the mechanisms by which children develop reading comprehension and writing composition skills in both Chinese and English in Chinese-English speaking bilinguals as well as associations with some cognitive- and linguistic-related factors. For example, we are interested in exploring more ideas related to poor comprehenders’ problems in reading comprehension in both L1 and L2 and their associated factors, as well as in investigating poor writers’ problem in writing in both Chinese and English. In addition, we ultimately would like to explore transfer between reading and writing skills between L1 reading and writing and L2 reading and writing. We will continue exploring those questions using this longitudinal dataset. Recently, we finished a paper, to be submitted soon, on the association between Chinese syntactic awareness and Chinese children’s writing composition. We found that there was a bidirectional relationship between syntactic skills and writing composition in Chinese children and that this association was fully mediated by children’s performance in reading comprehension. We will do more analyses using the data from this study in the future.

451210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
451210.value: Reading comprehension and writing composition (i.e., writing essays) are two important literacy skills that children have to acquire in their schooling. Several factors may influence the acquisition and development of these two skills. In our study, we looked at what kind of tasks would be effective in measuring children’s abilities in reading comprehension and writing composition in both Chinese and English in Hong Kong Chinese-English bilingual speaking children, what skills might be associated with children’s reading and writing ability, and what criteria should be used in evaluating children’s writing composition in both Chinese and English. We also wanted to examine whether there were some common factors that influenced reading comprehension and writing in both Chinese and English. These questions are important for parents, teachers, and educators. The findings from this study can potentially help teachers, educators, and parents better understand the problems of reading comprehension and writing composition in both Chinese and English. The findings of this study are also useful for psychologists and educational psychologists to build comprehensive models of reading comprehension and writing composition.

451710.label: Project Objectives
451710.value: How do parenting practices around academics differ by culture and immigration background across the transition to formal schooling? (a) What are the patterns of concurrent and longitudinal association between parenting practices and children’s school readiness skills? (b) Do these patterns of association vary by culture and immigration background?

(a) What are the patterns of concurrent and longitudinal association between parenting practices and children’s school readiness skills? (b) Do these patterns of association vary by culture and immigration background?

451710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
451710.value: It is well documented that Chinese children outperform US children throughout the school years. Little is known, however, about how this gap develops. The transition to kindergarten offers a unique window for examining how Chinese and US parents may engage in practices that promote children’s school readiness, thereby potentially setting children on different academic trajectories. Additionally, the transition can also speak to the early emergence and parental antecedents of possible educational disparities between immigrant and native children within a society. The transition to kindergarten represents immigrant children’s first extensive immersion into the host society. Yet immigrant children from low-income families tend to exhibit poor school readiness, possibly because their parents tend to have limited psychological resources for supporting their development. This research will compare families from four populations: low-income immigrants from Mainland China to US and Hong Kong, as well as low-income natives in the two locations. The design of having these two immigrant groups is unique in that the two groups both share the Chinese heritage and adjustments associated with living in a new land, but only immigrants to the US have to adjust to living in a completely new culture. Comparing parents of these two groups will therefore enable us to tease apart the effects on parenting of cultural heritage and immigration adjustments, which are confounded in most research to date. A total of 320 mothers and their children will visit our laboratory across the transition to kindergarten (aged 4 and 5 years). Only low-income families will be included to control for the effect of socioeconomic disadvantage. Demographic variables will be included as covariates in analyses. At each age, children’s school readiness skills in terms of content knowledge in literacy and math, and effortful control (a form of self-regulation) will be assessed. Mothers’ use of instructions in literacy and math, and informative feedback will be coded from mother-child interactions. Group differences in the mean levels, and concurrent as well as longitudinal patterns of mother-child associations of these variables will be explored. Specifically, analyses will compare (a) the two native groups, (b) the native and immigrant groups in Hong Kong, and (c) the two immigrant groups. This will highlight the respective roles of cultural heritage, immigration adjustments, and acculturation in shaping parents’ practices, which in turn may shape children’s school readiness during the critical transition to formal education. 有充份證據顯示，華人學童在各個階段的學業表現均比美國學童優勝。然而，我們對於箇中的原因卻所知甚少。孩子入讀幼稚園的時期正提供了一個難得的機會，讓我們探討中國和美國兩地的家長如何為子女入學作準備，從而使某些孩子在入學時已然佔優。此外，這時期亦能讓我們了解本地和移民家庭的孩子何時出現學業上的差異，以及家長在其中所扮演的角色。對於來自移民家庭的孩子而言，入讀幼稚園是他們首次全面融入主流社會的機會，但低收入移民家庭的孩子卻往往缺乏入學準備，這可能是由於他們的父母沒有足夠的心理資源來支援他們的發展。 本研究將比較四種不同背景的家庭，包括分別移居至香港和美國的低收入中國內地移民家庭，以及兩地的低收入本土家庭。此設計的獨特之處在於這兩類移民家庭均受中國傳統文化影響和需適應新環境，但唯獨移居至美國的中國內地移民家庭才需要面對美國截然不同的文化所帶來的衝擊和挑戰。由於過往被研究的華人移民家庭大都既受中國傳統文化影響，又同時要適應全新的文化，本研究的獨特設計將有助我們了解兩者分別對家長育兒帶來什麼影響。 我們將邀請320名母親及其就讀幼稚園的子女，在孩子年滿4歲和5歲時前來我們的研究中心。只有低收入家庭獲邀參加，數據分析亦會配合，以排除因家長來自不同社會階層而出現的差異。孩子在每年會接受入學準備的評估(包括認字，數學和自我控制等能力)。我們也會記錄母親在進行親子活動時，怎樣在認字和數學方面教導子女和回應其行為。我們將會就母親的教導方法與子女入學準備的關係及其隨年齡產生的變化，在以上四類家庭中進行比較，包括（一）兩類本土家庭、（二）居住在香港的本地和新移民家庭，以及（三）兩類移民家庭。本研究將顯示傳統文化，移民適應，和文化融和如何分別影響家長的育兒法，從而影響孩子在接受正規教育這關鍵時期的入學準備。

451710.label: Realisation of objectives
451710.value: The project objectives were achieved, which was enabled by the large samples that we successfully recruited in both Hong Kong and the United States. In Hong Kong, about 80 native and 100 immigrant low-income mother-child dyads participated in the study at age 4 and 5 years. In the United States, about 240 low-income mother-child dyads participated in the study at these ages, with African American, Dominican, Mexican, and Chinese immigrant families each making up about a quarter of the sample. In both sites, different aspects of children's school readiness were assessed in the lab by the experimenter. Mothers' learning-related practices were videotaped and subsequently coded. Mothers also reported on their parenting beliefs and practices. Analyses have been conducted to examine the mean levels of and associations between children's school readiness and mothers' practices, exploring how such mean levels and associations may vary by cultural and immigration background. So far, a paper that focuses on the link between children's executive function and early math skills has been published in a peer-reviewed journal. Although additional results are ready to be written up for dissemination, the PI's severe morning sickness symptoms during her pregnancy as well as her subsequent maternity leave have resulted in significant delay in this effort. Plans to submit results for conference presentations were likewise affected.

451710.label: Major findings and research outcome
451710.value: One of the major findings concern the relation between inhibitory control and early math skills among young children from different cultural and immigration backgrounds (Ng, Tamis-LeMonda, Yoshikawa, & Sze, 2014; please refer to Part C). Inhibitory control is one of the three major components of executive function, which has received increased attention from investigators given that it is associated with academic skills among children as early as the preschool and kindergarten years. However, prior research on executive function and its relations with academic skills have predominantly involved White non-Hispanic children. When studies involved non-White (e.g., African American and Latino) children, these children were almost always combined with White children for analyses, obscuring possible cultural differences. To date, only a few studies have examined executive function among Chinese children. Moreover, all but a handful of studies in the literature on executive function have adopted a concurrent design, which precludes us from understanding the causal direction in the relation between executive function and academic skills. The paper published from our longitudinal study addressed the aforementioned gaps by examining the executive function of African American, Dominican, Mexican, and Chinese children from low-income families separately. It added to the literature by showing that the inhibitory control of preschoolers from these ethnic groups predicted their subsequent math skills. In addition, it provides evidence that Chinese children's advanced inhibitory control in the preschool years may be one of the factors that underlie their superior performance in math when compared to non-Chinese children, which has been well documented across school grades. These findings highlight the important role of executive function in the development of academic skills among preschoolers of low-income and diverse cultural and immigration backgrounds, which has important implications for designing intervention to support these children to overcome their socioeconomic disadvantage when they first begin school.

451710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
451710.value: Additional analyses will be conducted on the rich dataset yielded from this study. For example, although there is new evidence that mothers' practices may predict children's executive function, it is only based on predominantly White non-Hispanic sample. We will extend prior research by investigating if such a link is evident in Chinese families. There is also plan to follow up on the children so as to better understand their long-term development and achievement (most parents have expressed interest in and consented to be contacted in the future). We have begun to do so with a subset of the sample. Although not part of the original proposal, mothers' adjustment and emotional functioning were assessed in this study. This was because when we contacted NGOs for recruitment, we came to realize that these factors may play an important role in immigrant mothers' learning-related practices. Preliminary analyses indicated that social support is important for buffering immigrant mothers from the negative effect of parenting-related financial stress (Sze, Ng, & Cheng, 2013; please refer to Part C). Based on these pilot findings, we plan to investigate how immigrant mothers' adjustment may shape their functioning, thereby influencing their learning-related practices.

451710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
451710.value: This project was designed to examine preschoolers' readiness for school at the transition to kindergarten and the role played by their family during this critical period. Of particular interest was how young children’s academic and cognitive skills as well as their mothers’ learning-related practices may vary according to their cultural and immigration background. To this end, children from diverse cultural and immigration backgrounds in Hong Kong and the United States were invited to visit the laboratory with their mother when they were in preschool and again in kindergarten. In each visit, children's academic and cognitive skills were assessed. Mothers' practices were assessed through observation during their interaction with children. Among other findings, it was found that preschoolers’ ability to inhibit their impulse predicted their early math skills later on. This was documented among children varying in cultural and immigration background. Moreover, Chinese children were found to exhibit advanced ability to inhibit their impulse when compared to other children, which partially explains why they showed better early math skills. These and other findings from this research will inform practitioners and policymakers of ways to support parents from diverse backgrounds to prepare their children for the critical transition to kindergarten.

452210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
452210.value: How should firms determine top executive compensation? Are CEO contributions to shareholder value sufficient to offset their compensations? Is the market for executive compensation efficient or driven by powerful executives? This project investigates these important questions by studying the extent to which top executives are paid for their contributions to firm value. An efficient labour market for top executives implies a positive sorting between managerial ability and compensation. Managers with higher marginal contribution to shareholder value should receive higher compensation, and any rent from the firm-manager relationship should be shared with shareholders according to the relative bargaining power between the executive and the firm. We estimate the implied marginal value of top executives from stock price reactions to sudden deaths, and regress it on the annual compensation. The intuition behind this approach is that the stock price reaction equals the difference between the deceased executive's value (net of compensation), the anticipated replacement's net contribution, and any switch cost. If executive compensation is efficiently set, managers are expected to receive higher compensation whenever their contribution to firm value is high, the anticipated replacement value is low, and search and replacement costs are high. Using a pilot sample of sudden deaths of top executives in the U.S. between 1994 and 2008, we find that top executives are valuable to firm value. Stock prices drop by 0.83% following their sudden deaths. However, the large variation in stock reaction indicates that they are not equally valuable. The stock reaction is positive for about half of the CEOs and negative for the other half (means equal to -5.60%, and +5.90% respectively). Top executives are not equally paid for their marginal contributions to firm as the coefficient of pay for value is negative, but not equal -1. Entrenchment, independence of compensation committee, governance, and firm and individual characteristics appear to impact top executive pay. Our project contributes to the literature in several lines. First, to our knowledge, it is the first project that investigates whether top executives are paid for their contributions to firm value. It is an important issue since prior literature focuses more on the levels and on the functional form of pay. Second, our study reports factors that impact pay for value such as governance, industry, firm and individual characteristics. Third, by showing that top executives contribute differently to shareholder value, we contribute to a growing literature on the value of top executives. 摘要︰ 行政總裁之薪酬是否足以平衡其對股東價值之貢獻？本研究以突然死亡的高級管理人員對股價之影響，從而識別高級管理人員的價值。我們假設股價變動相等於去世高級管理人員對股東價值之貢獻。若公司能有效地設定高級管理人員的薪酬，其對企業價值有較大的貢獻時，薪酬亦會相應較高。本研究對高級管理人員之價值可在日漸增多的文獻及討論作一分貢獻。

452210.label: Realisation of objectives
452210.value: The project has resulted in the working paper "What death can tell: Are executives paid for their contributions to value?". Using the setting of a natural experiment we measure the contibution of top executives to shareholder value by the stock price reaction to sudden deaths. We then compare the maginitude and sign of the stock price reaction to the deceased's compensation package, and find interesting results. The objectives of the project has been fully acheived as the study gives answers to the question whether top executives are paid for their contribution to value. After having collected comments from seminar presentations and academic conferences we have amended the study. We are now ready to submit the study to an academic journal.

452210.label: Major findings and research outcome
452210.value: The study provides novel empirical evidence on the relationship between executive pay and managerial contribution to shareholder value by exploiting the exogenous variation resulting from stock price reactions to sudden deaths. We find, first, that managers with high contributions to shareholder value obtain higher pay. Second, an average executive appears to retain 70% to 80% of the total rent. Overall, our results are informative about the workings of the managerial labor market.

452210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
452210.value: The study has resulted in a novel dataset containing sudden deaths of top executives. The dataset will be valuable in future studies of the determinants of top executives' contribution to firm value. We are currently developing a new research agenda that will benefit from the extensitve data collection effort undertaken in this project.

452210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
452210.value: Few topics in financial economics rival executive compensation in the degree of interest they elicit from academia, media, policymakers, and the general public. Is executive pay related to executives’ contribution to firm value? Are CEOs’ contributions to shareholder value sufficient to offset their pay? Despite a rich literature on the subject, these important questions remain open avenues for research. Using the stock price reaction to sudden deaths, this paper examines the relationship between executive pay and contribution to shareholder value. We find that managers with high contributions to shareholder value obtain higher pay. We estimate that executives retain 70% to 80% of the rent from the firm manager relationship.

452710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
452710.value: In 2006, Pisapia offered a strategic leadership theory which bridges the ordered world with the postmodern world. He postulated that the uncertainty associated with moving from one era to another requires leaders who are able to maximize their conceptual and behavioral agility, and who are hence better able to build the conditions under which organizational learning, adaptability, and flexibility can flourish. The central tenet of this theory is that leaders who are able to think and act strategically will be able to create more supportive organizational environments and achieve more valuable organizational outcomes. His theory of strategic leadership should not be confused with strategic planning or strategic management. It differs in that leaders at all levels of the organization must possess a strategic mindset that encourages flexibility and the ability to use adaptive leader actions. This study examines the relationship between the ability of school principals in Hong Kong to think strategically and execute a versatile set of leader actions and professional work environment of the teachers. Three hypotheses will be tested in the study: 1. School principals’ competence in strategic thinking and strategic execution leads to more productive schools and professional work environments. 2. School principals who use strategic thinking cognitive skills to help leaders to make sense of the complexities facing the organization create more productive professional work environments. 3. School principals who use a wide array of leader actions, including managing, transforming, bonding, bridging and bartering, are better able to support the development of productive professional work environments than those who do not. This research is important because, if the results confirm the hypotheses, training materials and professional development activities can be produced to improve the thinking and acting skills of principals and aspiring principals. Two instruments, the Strategic Thinking Questionnaire (STQ) and the Strategic Leadership Questionnaire’s (SLQ) will be used to collect data from the principals and from observers on the principal’s use of cognitive skills and leader actions. Pang’s (2004) School Life Questionnaire (TSLQ) will also be used to collect data on the teachers’ quality of school life in terms of their feelings, perceptions of empowerment, efficacy, commitment, job satisfaction and their organizational learning capabilities. The researchers will employ the LISRELL approach to analyze the relationships among the variables from which they will draw their conclusions and recommendations. 我們正處於邁向後現代的時期。面對著這變幻莫測的世界，現今的領袖必須擁有新的戰略思維和行動，才可克服不穩定環境帶來的挑戰。Pisapia在 2006 年提供了一種戰略領導理論作為有序的世界過度至後現代世界的橋樑。現今的領袖在思維和行動上必須有高度的機敏，才能為機構建立更強的組織學習能力和適應能力，為機構創造蓬勃發展的條件及靈活性。這一理論的主張是，假若領袖採取正確的戰略思考和行動，他們將能創建一個多方支援的組織環境，使組織的發展獲取更多的成就。我們不要將「戰略領導」的理論與「戰略規劃」或「戰略管理」互相混淆。它的不同之處，是著重組織內各級的領導都必須具備應有的「戰略思維」以促進組織的靈活性，以及採取相應的「戰略行動」以提高組織的適應力。這兩種的戰略領導能力，將決定現今的領袖能否成功帶領組織從一個穩定時代轉移到一個高不確定性的時代。 這項研究將檢視香港學校校長的戰略領導模式及形態，評核他們在應變時的「戰略思維」能力，和分析他們所採取的「戰略行動」對教師的專業環境產生了甚麼的影響。這研究將測試三個假設如下： 1. 學校校長的戰略思維能力和相應的戰略行動會促進教師的專業環境和提高學校的效益。 2. 學校校長若能應用我們所倡議的戰略思維技巧來面對複雜的問題，這有助促進教師的專業表現和提高學校的效益。 3. 學校校長若能應用我們所倡議的戰略行動來面對複雜的問題，這有助促進教師的專業表現和提高學校的效益。 假若這項研究能證明以上的假設，這研究的結果將有助制定校長或擬任校長專業發展的策略和有關培訓活動的規劃和設計。這研究將以「戰略思維問卷」(STQ)和「戰略領導問卷」(SLQ)收集有關的數據和資料，以了解香港學校校長的「戰略思維」能力和他們所採取的「戰略行動」模式。這研究亦以彭新強（2004）的「教師學校生活問卷」(TSLQ)收集教師的學校生活的感受，以了解校長的「戰略思維」和「戰略行動」模式與他們的專業表現有甚麼關係。我們將使用LISREL方法分析當中變項之間的關係，以繪製有關的結論和建議。

452710.label: Realisation of objectives
452710.value: Basically, the objectives in the three stages of the project have been achieved. The first stage was to develop an instrument to assess school leaders’ perception of the complexity of schools’ internal and external environments, self-reporting of the capabilities of strategic thinking and strategic actions and to examine the relationship among three sets of variables. In total, 706 individual school leaders, from 364 schools (including primary, secondary, and special schools in Hong Kong), at senior management were the respondents of this study. They were invited to respond to the self-reporting versions of STQ (STQ-Self) and SLQ (SLQ-Self). The data set, representing about one fifth of the school leaders in Hong Kong, allowed the researchers to answer the research questions posted in stage 1. The objectives of the second stage of the study were to examine school leaders’ capabilities of strategic thinking and executions from teachers’ perspectives and to determine their impact on organizational outcomes. This stage of research was a follow-up survey based on the results of Stage 1. Seventy schools out from 354 schools in stage 1 were invited to take part in this stage of the study. In total, 1,647 individual school teachers returned their responses to the teacher-perception versions of STQ (STQ-Other) and SLQ (SLQ-Other) as well as the Change Capacity Questionnaire (CCQ). The sample size is large enough to warrant reliability and validity in generalizing the results to the rest of Hong Kong schools. The objectives of Stage 3 were to conduct qualitative case studies of a few selected schools to understand the complexity of the schools’ environments, to describe how school leaders think and act strategically and to explain their effects on organizational outcomes. In this stage, focused-group discussions with 17 principals (from a mix of primary, secondary and special schools as well as government, aided and DSS schools) were conducted. In addition to the focused-group studies, 3 schools (1 primary school, 1 secondary school and 1 special school) were purposefully selected for in-depth multiple-case studies. From each school, a group of five respondents (including the Principal, two deputy principals and two junior teachers) were invited to take part in the case study. The focused group discussions and the multiple-case studies allowed the comparison and contrast of the practice of strategic thinking and executions across schools within a sector as well as different sectors.
