452710.label: Major findings and research outcome
452710.value: This study has been successfully describing the patterns of school leaders’ perceptions of the complexity of environments, their cognitive capabilities using the Strategic Thinking Questionnaire (STQ) and their capabilities of acting strategically using the Strategic Leadership Questionnaire (SLQ). This study has also been able to explore the relationships that may exist among these variables and to examine what were their effects on organizational outcomes, including organizational learning capability. Both quantitative and qualitative information were collected to answer the research questions. The studies of strategic thinking skills and actions of school leaders in Hong Kong show the following significant findings. In Pang and Pisapia’s study (2012; 2013b) shows that (a) the use of the strategic thinking could distinguish between more and less successful leaders, (b) school leaders’ understandings of system dynamics had significant effects leadership effectiveness, and (c) while systems thinking explained much of the variance in the success variable, there was a cumulative impact of the use of all three capabilities. Findings also show that those school leaders that demonstrated a higher use of systems thinking and reflecting in strategic thinking skills also reported a greater use of a range of leadership influence actions (Pang & Pisapia, 2013a). We also attempted to determine if Chinese school principals use leader influence actions differently than United States principals (Pisapia & Pang, 2013c). The findings suggest that (a) managing and transforming actions are universal, (b) relationship influence actions (bonding, bridging, and bartering) are culturally sensitive, and (c) societal values are less important than local values in determining which influence actions principals employ. The above studies would have several practical implications for school leaders and universities since the relationship between cognitive capability and leader actions has been firmly established. In terms of the organization, the results would give organizations further criteria and measurement tools to screen individuals who are being considered for selection. In terms of the school leaders, the data will provide the necessary feedback for their professional development on an important but hereto untouched set of skills. In terms of university based training and professional development, the data would enable them to make changes in their programs of delivery to support the development of new skills. Finally, the study would contribute to a more specific understanding of the theory of strategic leadership within the fields of educational leadership, management and administration.

452710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
452710.value: The research project allows us to advance research and the practice of strategic leadership through the generation and exchange of knowledge by establishing the Strategic Leadership Network (SLN). Further development of the research can be made through of three synergistic groups within the SLN that focuses on research, services, and use of strategic leadership principles and tools. The researcher group may compose of active academic or corporate researchers from education, government, and other NGOs. The task of the research group is to research the paradigm and continue to develop it. The providers group will be comprised of professional developers and executive coaches who take the ideas and consult with organizations to put them into practice. The end-user group will be composed of individual practitioners and/or organizations that are committed to using SL ideas to improve their organizational and personal performance in the workplace. The SLN may meet once a year in different parts of the world to learn from each other, get the latest research, solutions that move the bottom line, and tools to make it happen months before they hit the public domain, and to renew commitments to SLN principles.

452710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
452710.value: John Pisapia (2009) offered a strategic leadership theory which bridges the ordered world with the postmodern world. The central tenet of this theory is that leaders who are able to think and act strategically will be able to create more supportive organizational environments and achieve more valuable organizational outcomes. This study examines the relationship between the ability of school principals in Hong Kong to think strategically and execute a versatile set of leader actions and professional work environment of the teachers. The hypotheses tested and confirmed in the study were: (i) school principals’ competence in strategic thinking and strategic execution leads to more productive schools and professional work environments; (ii) school principals who use strategic thinking cognitive skills to help leaders to make sense of the complexities facing the organization create more productive professional work environments; (iii) school principals, who use a wide array of leader actions, including managing, transforming, bonding, bridging and bartering, are better able to support the development of productive professional work environments than those who do not. This research is important because training materials and professional development activities can be produced to improve the thinking and acting skills of principals and aspiring principals.

453110.label: Project Objectives
453110.value: To determine if chronic differences in the use of procedures depends on culture and age and if the match between the procedure typically used and the information presentation format leads to greater ease of processing and more favorable reactions to the ad. To examine whether the procedures that consumers use to process information can influence expectancies about the characteristics of the product and the evaluation of the product described.

To examine whether the procedures that consumers use to process information can influence expectancies about the characteristics of the product and the evaluation of the product described.

453110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
453110.value: Consumers often use a particular procedure to process information about a product. For example, they may respond to information either quickly or slowly, interpret information either abstractly or concretely, or compute the implications of information using a holistic or piecemeal integration process. Although product evaluation can be influenced by the interpretation of the information and its implications, little has been done to understand whether product evaluation can also be influenced by how its information is processed. We suggest that the use of different procedures might influence not only the ease of processing information but also alter consumers’ expectancies about the target stimulus. As a result, consumers’ judgments of a product may be changed accordingly. We will investigate these issues in two projects. First, we suggest that consumers’ reaction to an ad could be influenced by the similarity of the manner in which consumers process the ad to the procedures that they typically use. We expect that culture and age will be important determinants of procedures that are chronically used. Asians, for example, typically pay more attention to contextual information than Westerners do. Therefore, if they receive advertising material that emphasizes this type of processing, they may find it easier to read and these feelings of ease, in turn, could lead them to make more favorable evaluations. Second, the procedures that consumers use to process information could also induce expectancies about the characteristics of the stimulus. For example, consumers might expect that a dish will take less time to be prepared if they process its name quickly than slowly. Consumers might expect an object to be heavier if it moves slowly than quickly. Such expectancies could bias consumers’ judgment of the target stimulus. Our work will address these issues and their implications for consumer behavior. 消费者经常可以用不同方式处理产品信息。比如，他们看东西的速度可以不一样，可以用抽象或具体的思维方式去理解信息，在总结信息时可以从总体着眼或者从细节考虑。虽然以前的研究表明不同的信息可以影响消费者的评价，但是对于不同的思维或行为方式对消费者评价的影响，这方面的研究还比较欠缺。我们认为使用不同的方式去看一个产品不但会影响消费者处理信息时的难易感觉，而且会影响他们对产品的期待。这些感觉或者期待都可以最终影响消费者对产品的喜欢程度。我们将从两个方面对这些进行研究。 第一，当消费者处理广告信息的方式和他们习惯中的思维方式一样时，他们会对广告更正面的评价。比如，东方人通常更关注事物所处的情境，而西方人会更关注事物本身。如果，广告中更强调情境，就会让东方人看广告时觉得更舒服，从而影响他们对广告的态度。 第二，消费者处理信息的方式有时可以影响他们对产品特点的期待。比如，如果消费者读一个菜名很快，消费者可能会觉得这道菜需要更少时间准备。如果产品图片在屏幕上显示的速度很慢，消费者可能会觉得这个产品的份量更加重。这些期待都可以影响他们对产品的判断。

453110.label: Realisation of objectives
453110.value: Objective 1 was obtained in a series of studies. We showed that individuals who recently employed a particular eye movement, such as scanning information from top to bottom versus from bottom to top, evaluated a product more favorably when that same movement was employed during the evaluation task. Objective 2 was also obtained in a series of studies that examined whether the length of the name of an object could influence their expectancy about the object. For example, we found that people estimate a survey to take a longer time to complete if the title of the survey is long rather than short. They estimate that it takes a longer time to arrive at a building if it has a long name than a short name. Objective 3 was obtained in several studies that investigated whether occupying the dominant (vs. non-dominant) hand leads to lower evaluations of the target object. This effect occurs because restricting the use of the dominant hand impairs the ease with which perceivers simulates holding the target. Objective 4 was obtained in studies that investigate when consumers apply a procedure based on its desirability and when they will apply it more spontaneously based on its accessibility. We showed that when people work on a marketing survey, they typically are not conscious of the speed with which they work on that survey. Therefore, the speed of their actions during a previous experience (e.g. their rate of speaking) can spontaneously influence their speed of completing the survey, and this is true regardless of whether they think it is desirable to do things quickly or slowly. However, desirability matters if people are conscious of the speed of working on the survey.

453110.label: Major findings and research outcome
453110.value: We found that the procedures applied by consumers to process an object can activate different concepts which, in turn, can influence their judgment of the object. Shen and Adaval (2013) found that people process a name of an object more quickly if its acronym (vs. its full name) is used. Consequently, the name of the object can influence the estimation of the amount of time that they would use to deal with this object. For example, we found that people estimate that a survey would take more time to complete if the title of the survey is “a pretest at Hong Kong University of Science and Technology” than if it is “a pretest at HKUST”. We also found people estimate they need to wait longer for a dish to be prepared if its name is long than short. Cai, Shen and Hui (2012) demonstrated that people have learned a procedure of reading or writing numbers from left to right in increasing order of magnitude. Consequently, they estimate a higher price for the product that is presented on the right side than the left side of a display. This effect is reversed if they are induced to process multiple products from right to left. We also found that people may infer their belief from the motor procedure they are using. For example, Xu, Shen and Wyer (2012) showed that people may infer their relationship with others from their motor behavior of approaching others and, therefore, would be more likely to choose products that others are likely to consider socially desirable. Huang et al. (2012) found that couples’ satisfaction with the marriage can depend on whether they commute to work in the same or different directions. Mere similarity in the direction of commuting to work can increase marital satisfaction. The ease with which consumers apply a procedure can also influence their judgment of product. For example, Shen and Rao (2013) showed that if people have previously scanned information from top to bottom, they would feel easier to process a product and like it more if it requires them to reapply the same (vs. a different) eye movement to process product information. Shen and Sengupta (2012) demonstrated that occupying one’s dominant hand could lead one to feel more difficult to simulate reaching toward the target object and, therefore, would decrease one’s liking of the object.

453110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
453110.value: Further research can be done to investigate whether the way in which a procedure is activated can have different effects on consumer behavior. For example, when we activate a procedure of doing things quickly, we can let people actually move hands quickly, or ask them to imagine this behavior in mind, or just let them observe others doing this behavior. Does actually performing a procedure make a different influence on people’s behavior than simply simulating or observing a procedure? We think that although people’s performance of a procedure can be enhanced when they have been activated with this procedure previously, this effect may last longer if they have actually practiced the procedure than if they simply imagine or observe this procedure. We plan to test this idea in the future research.

453110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
453110.value: The procedures that consumers use to process information could influence the judgment of an object. For example, people may process a dish name more quickly if its name is short than long. Consequently, people may estimate that the dish takes less time to be prepared in the former case than in the latter. As another example, people typically read numbers from left to right in increasing order of magnitude. This procedure can lead them to estimate a higher price for a product that is presented on the right side (vs. the left side) of a display. Also, consumers may infer their belief from the motor procedure they are using. They may be more likely to conform to others and choose socially desirable options if they are moving close to others. The ease with which people apply a procedure can also influence product judgment. Consumers who used to move eyes in a particular direction may feel easier to process product and like it more if they are required to make the same eye movement during product evaluation. Consumers who have their dominant hand occupied may feel more difficult to simulate reaching toward the target object and would decrease their liking of it. Our research contributes to the field of knowledge accessibility and provides rich marketing implication for how applying a procedure can influence consumer behavior.

453710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
453710.value: This project proposes a three-year interdisciplinary research program to examine the role of Hong Kong in the birth, growth, and development of an international market in Chinese art over the past fifty years (1950-present). No one will argue that Hong Kong is a major global finance centre in Asia. But few are aware of Hong Kong’s profound impact on the international art market in Chinese art, on the fortunes of personal and corporate businesses in art, and the role its collectors and their collecting activities played in enhancing international understanding and appreciation of China’s artistic and cultural heritage. This research will study the complex inter-relationships between individual collectors, supporters, and dealers of Chinese art, and their background, resources, and the social, political, and economic conditions of Hong Kong under which they lived and collected. Through personal stories of collectors, dealers, members of collector societies, the business developments of international auction houses, and sales of Chinese art in international markets, a picture describing the global impact of art collecting among Hong Kong collectors will emerge. The experiences of these economically powerful and spatially mobile collectors will enable us to capture the historical process in which collecting Chinese art in Hong Kong became a global phenomenon. Moreover, as we examine the network of institutional, corporate, and individual practices in Hong Kong’s art market, we hope to understand the depth of impact these activities had on Hong Kong, the international art business, and global intercultural understanding. A better appreciation of the Hong Kong art market’s role in the development and enhancement of global interest in China’s artistic heritage should have important implications when the government of Hong Kong SAR begins to more clearly define a Cultural Policy for the region. Research methods will be interdisciplinary, using anthropological approaches such as in-depth interviews, archival research, and art historical analysis. Major deliverables will include an international conference examining the research results in broader historical, economic, and social contexts, a major publication that will be the first critical history of Hong Kong as Asia’s art hub with global business and cultural impact; and a data archive based on historical materials collected through fieldwork, and interviews of selected art collectors, dealers and auction house representatives in Hong Kong and abroad. 這一跨度為三年的跨學科研究項目旨在考察香港在過去50年中（1950至今）在興起與發展中華藝術的國際市場的過程中所扮演的角色。眾所周知，香港是亞洲一個主要的國際金融中心。但是很少有人認識到：香港對中華藝術的國際藝術市場的深遠影響、對個人與團體在藝術交易中產生的財富的作用， 以及香港是如何型塑收藏家及其收藏活動並使之提升中國文化藝術遺產的國際理解與鑒賞程度的。本研究將探尋藝術收藏家個人、藝術愛好者與商人的複雜互動關係，以及他們的背景、資源和所處的香港的特定社會政治經濟環境。我們將用敘事的方法記錄收藏家、商人、收藏協會成員、國際拍賣行的商業發展、國際市場上中華藝術的交易， 以此展示藝術收藏對香港收藏家的全球影響的圖景。這些富有的、四處遷移的收藏家可以讓我們瞭解香港的中華藝術收藏是如何成為一個全球現象的歷史過程。 另外，我們將考察香港藝術市場中制度的、團體的和個人的實踐所構成的網路，並且我們希望理解這些活動為香港、國際藝術商業和國際跨文化理解所帶來的深度影響。更好地欣賞香港藝術市場在發展和提升中國藝術遺產的國際興趣中扮演的重要角色，有助於香港特別行政區政府為本地區制定一套更為清晰的文化政策。 本專案的研究方法將是跨學科的，融合了人類學方法，如深度訪談、文獻研究與藝術史的分析。主要的成果將包括：一次國際會議，以在更廣的歷史社會和經濟框架下考察研究的結論；一部首次用評論性的、歷史的角度審視香港作為具有國際商業與文化影響力的亞洲藝術中心的出版物；一個建立在田野調查所收集的材料之上的檔案庫；以及部分香港與海外收藏家、商人與拍賣行代表的訪談記錄。

453710.label: Realisation of objectives
453710.value: 1. Three years were adequate to get the project started and obtain meaningful results, although the methodology employed - using in-depth personal interviews in Hong Kong and abroad - took time to set up and more (and follow-up) interviews could have benefitted the project further, if time was available. An extension of the project completion date from October 2013 to April 2014 became necessary, as interviews were still being set up and carried out in at the beginning of 2014. The unexpected wealth of information collected in the interviews have demanded far more time and effort in their transcription than anticipated. Audiotapes had to be reviewed several times to ensure information such as names, places, and events are accurately transcribed. Some of these required research, since many individuals or events were mentioned when records were minimal. Others should be reviewed and checked by the interviewees, who, as busy professionals, were not always available or willing to do so. Accuracy of information in the transcripts risks compromise, unless additional time and research efforts can be put toward them. Therefore, only a rather broad statement of the findings can be prepared for publication at this point. In-depth articles can only follow after careful sorting, organizing, and analysis of the contents of the transcripts. 2. Research demonstrated clearly that such complex interrelationships existed, but also revealed that there were constant shifts in the balance of these interrelationships. The interview methodology - allowing the individual to speak for him/herself - was ideal in exposing this complex symbiotic relationships between the individuals and the unique political, social, and economic conditions of Hong Kong in which they lived and worked. Research also affirmed the important role of research, dialogue, and exchange in the form of exhibitions, conferences, workshops, and other educational programmes as means of knowledge-sharing among scholars and the greater Hong Kong community. 3. The workshop organized in April 2013 validated the importance of such open dialogues, and the need to cross interdisciplinary, academic and business boundaries. It provided a platform and occasion for scholars, museum curators, collectors, dealers, auction house professionals to meet and learn about each other's perspectives and experiences over the period in question. Almost immediately, it has generated interest in the work of a little-known Hong Kong foundation, initiated by a collector, that has been a key player in the promotion of Chinese art education and collecting.

453710.label: Major findings and research outcome
453710.value: 1. In addition to the well-known economic, political, and legal factors that made Hong Kong an ideal bridge between China and the Western world, this research added an important component by highlighting the previously unknown role of the individuals (private collectors, dealers, auction house professionals) as one of the key drivers toward Hong Kong's leading status as a global market for Chinese art. 2. That collecting Chinese art in Hong Kong began in the traditional context of a 'scholarly gathering' (e.g. the Min Chiu Society) prompted by the desire of immigrants to recover a bit of the homeland lost to Communist rule. Such collector societies played an incubation role for future generations of collectors. 3. That the arrival of the European auction houses in 1970s and 1980s changed the way art was bought and sold, took some of it out of the hands of the traditional scholar elite, and allowed more general participation. Open commercial sales through established auctions became a sort of equalizer that enabled the subsequent mass participation in collecting. 4. That individual collectors and dealers in Hong Kong, including a cohort of women professionals who became active in the 1980s and 1990s, promoted new categories of Chinese art among scholars and collectors, e.g. classical “Ming” furniture, ornaments, textiles, etc. The reframing of Chinese antiques as such generated appreciation for Chinese art among non-traditional collectors. 5. Unlike most international cities with museums, Hong Kong is unique in that its publicly run museums have not played significant roles in the nurturing of interest in art and art collecting. Most of this happened through the efforts of private collectors and businesses, dealers, auction houses. 6. The success of the Hong Kong art market is tied to the rule of law, a favorable tax system, and geographic proximity to the mainland. With the economic boom in the mainland since the 2000s, demand for Chinese art has driven prices to unprecedented highs, making it far less accessible to the traditional scholar collectors who established the field in Hong Kong in the first place. 7. Efforts must be made by the Hong Kong government and society to protect this delicate balance in the relationship to prevent the territory's leadership position from being overtaken by fast-developing PRC hubs such as Shanghai and Beijing.

453710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
453710.value: 1. Focus of research may be shifted away from Hong Kong toward charting similar relationships and their impact in Japan during the pre-war and post-war years in China; toward developments in Taipei, Taiwan during its economic prosperity in the 1980s; and to comparison between Hong Kong, Taipei, Singapore, and Shanghai-Beijing to tease out in greater detail, the unique conditions that have made Hong Kong such a success. Such comparisons can highlight how different interpretations of Chinese tradition have emerged in each respective territory due to individual and institutional circumstances. 2. Post-doctoral research fellow (Chen Ying) has been encouraged to pursue the Japan connection, with her fluent Japanese language skills, and potential access to Japanese material in Japan (as a Japanese resident). 3. Explore in depth the role of women (dealers, collectors) in a traditionally male-dominated sphere of activity 4. Investigate the significance of the dual identity of Hong Kong (predominantly Chinese under British Colonial rule of law) in globalization of Chinese art collecting 5. Examine the factors and impact of the shift in collecting activity as a traditional literati pursuit to the intellectually and knowledge-driven goals of 'modern' professionals, to the cash-rich business 'trophy-hunting' activities of the new Chinese collector.

453710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
453710.value: The role of Hong Kong as a commercial and financial hub in Asia has long been acknowledged. It also had the dubious reputation as a 'cultural desert'. This research hopes to correct this misconception by highlighting Hong Kong's cultural achievements over the past 50+ years by focusing on its unsung heroes - a group of Chinese who chose to spend their financial resources on collecting the varied artifacts of their cultural heritage. Through the voices of these collectors and individuals, this research recovers some of the daring feats, long-term commitment, intellectual engagement, and passionate persistence that made them the catalysts for the global interest in Chinese art we see today. These collectors of Chinese art in Hong Kong, and a few knowledgeable and dedicated professional dealers and auctions experts from abroad, were the driving forces that made Hong Kong the global Chinese art trading hub it is today, poised to overtake the traditional centres of London and New York. As cultural ambassadors for Chinese art and heritage, Hong Kong collectors' contributions should be recognized. Through them and their activities over the past half century, Hong Kong is no longer a 'cultural desert'.

454210.label: Project Objectives
454210.value: To contest putative scholarship that the historicity in Judith is secondary to the story. To re-examine the assumptions concerning the purpose of the story and the conditions at the time of the composition. To highlight the primary political and socio-historical purposes in the story through the application of postcolonial approaches. To apply those postcolonial approaches developed and highlighted by Asian scholars. To proffer another feminist interpretation to the story but with postcolonial interest. To define in more quantitative terms the aspects of the story where it is fictional and factual as it relates to real history. To demonstrate that Judith is the only book in the Old Testament that articulates and struggles with the confrontations of all of Israel’s rulers and colonizers.

454210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
454210.value: The aim of this project is to study the book of Judith, one of the deuterocanonical books of the Old Testament, from a postcolonial feminist standpoint, to offer interpretations how the text resists and opposes the empires which ruled them. The Book of Judith, placed by many Christian churches among the books of the Old Testament Apocrypha, describes how the Jewish widow, Judith killed the Assyrian general Holofernes, thereby saving Israel. The historicity of this particular episode is extremely doubtful, but this does not mean that the book has no historical value. If read carefully the Book of Judith gives a coded account of the Jewish experience under the rule of various empires. As such, theories of postcolonial biblical interpretation when applied to this book have much to offer modern scholarship. In this study we intend to interrogate the narrative of the Book of Judith from a feminist and postcolonial viewpoint. We will deploy with advantage the perspective of Asian women who have experienced colonial and postcolonial rule. Specifically, drawing on an established template for this kind of study, we will (a) set the experience of Jewish subversion by their rulers from the Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians and Greeks in perspective; (b) explore the strategies used by the Jews in their struggles and negotiations for liberation during these epochs of domination; and (c) compare and contrast a range of recent interpretations on the Book of Judith. Previous scholarship has largely neglected the historical aspect of Judith because the historical data given in the story does not add up. This study will address that shortfall and will show that the story in actual fact picks up the epochs of Israel’s history up until the first century BCE. It will explore pertinent issues related to postcolonial criticism, such as hybridism, fragmentation, multiple identities, territorialism and deterritorialism, joint colonization, ethnicity, language, gender and marginalization which are relevant to much of the Asian world today.

454210.label: Realisation of objectives
454210.value: The essays which I had written and in progress have fulfilled the above objectives. All the objectives are achieved satisfactorily in the writings that I have submitted and have also been reviewed. Reviewers have given excellent comments and I have given careful attention to achieve the objectives in my writings. I was not able to fulfill publishing the essays within the project’s time frame, but with the reviewers’ recommendations, I am revising and expanding the essay into at least two or more pieces where I deal with the postcolonial feminist interpretations of the book and also relate it to the SE Asian postcolonial context. The essay is attached.

454210.label: Major findings and research outcome
454210.value: Major findings include there is a threshold of postcolonial ideologies in the book of Judith which scholarship has not paid much attention to. From the reviews of the essays which I had submitted, I have received positive feedback on the ideas and methodologies employed. However, they think my essays are "too ambitious" to put so much ideas in one essay and hope that I expand these ideas to more extensive works. More importantly, I have shown that although the book of Judith is fictional, it is quintessentially addressing historical ideologies such as resistance and postcolonialism. The significance of the interpretations I have proposed for the book Judith sheds new light to consider other similar genres in the Jewish literature.

454210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
454210.value: In the midst of this research, I have also gathered ideas to consider some of the Jewish intertestamental literature as portraying resistance related to postcolonialism as well. In particular, the genre of novellas and wisdom writings - which much scholarship tend to bypass when dealing with postcolonial interpretations. I believe my outputs in future will be able to encourage more studies to apply interpretations of postcolonialism on the above mentioned genre - and to also relate them to the interpreter's contexts.

454210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
454210.value: This research has shed new light on taking the book of Judith which scholarship and churches has taken merely as "story" and appreciating its purpose to nail important issues which occurred in history: how the Jewish community had and could overcome the political oppression throughout their history. Therefore, there could be other similar "stories" in the biblical books that could be read this way. At the same time, it can also to encourage communities today to imagine possibilities of different ways of expressions to overcome oppression.

454710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
454710.value: This project examines the performing arts of the Chinese Cultural Revolution (1966-76; hereafter CR) by taking a fresh look into some under-researched musical traditions from both the Han and minority peoples in China. Music-making was an indispensable tool of socio-political control for the Communist state during the CR. Much research has been done on the notorious "Eight Model Operas" and mass songs. This project engages the topic from an utterly different standpoint. The primary foci of the investigation are musical traditions found on the periphery of China. The term “periphery,” as conceptualised in this project, comprises at least two distinct definitions. Firstly, it refers to ethno-geographical locales that are defined primarily by their physical and racial/ethnic detachment from China proper; Northwest China (music of the Uyghurs), Northeast China (music of the Koreans), and Hong Kong (local musical traditions) fit into this category. Secondly, the term refers to musical traditions - mostly of the majority Han people - that are perceived as ancient and historical, which were considered problematic during this period. The music of the qin belongs to this category. This project will scrutinize such peripheral Chinese musical traditions during the CR through archival and ethnographic research. At the centre in this project is Jiang Qing, whose role as scapegoat has hitherto discouraged serious examination of her input in this formative period of Chinese cultural development. We analyse her understanding of music and its revolutionary function. We then examine how the "centre" was defined in relation to its "periphery" through musical means at this time. Looking beyond temporal and national boundaries, we explore how musical ideologies of the CR were consistent with those before 1949 and still resonate throughout greater China. Although subject to censorship, data on the CR is increasingly available, and more importantly, key participants who lived through this period are aging, making a study such as this one particularly timely. By including a senior Chinese scholar and younger scholars outside China, this project will facilitate scholarly exchange across generations, disciplines and national borders. Musicologists have examined the relationship between music and revolutionary politics in various cultural contexts, and increasingly explore the relationship of musics of the "periphery," and their relationship to the "centre." This project will be the first to address this issue with respect to the CR. The academic issues addressed by this project will be cross-cultural, reaching beyond the field of Chinese music. 本計劃從一些以往缺乏學術關注的中國漢族和少數民族的音樂傳統為切入點，來檢視中國文化大革命（1966-76，此後稱文革）時期的表演藝術。音樂是共產主義中國在文革時期實行社會與政治操控所不可或缺的工具。現有的大量研究主要探討了眾所周知的「八大樣板戲」和大眾歌曲。而本計劃則選擇了一個截然不同的研究角度，其主要關注的焦點為處於中國邊陲的音樂傳統。 本計劃所指的「邊陲」一詞包括至少兩種不同的定義。第一，它指代那些在實際地理位置和種族或民族上都與中國相脫離的民族地理區域，如中國西北部（維吾爾族的音樂）、中國東北部（朝鮮族的音樂）、香港（本地音樂傳統）皆包含在此類別內。第二，它指那些被認為是古老而具歷史的音樂傳統，其中大多數是漢族的音樂傳統。這種「古舊」的音樂傳統文化在文革時期被認為有問題，古琴音樂便屬於此類。本計劃將會透過文獻檔案的查閱及民族志的研究方法，深入探討這些在文革時期處於邊緣化的中國音樂傳統。本計劃以江青為研究重點。由於她成為文革的代罪羔羊，她在這個中國文化發展與成形的重要時期所起到的作用一直不被重視。我們首先分析她對音樂及其革命性作用的理解，進而探討文革時期如何透過音樂手段來定義「中心」及其與「邊陲」的關係。我們將跨越時空和民族界限，去探索文革時期的音樂意識形態是如何成為一九四九年以前的音樂意識形態的延伸，以及其現今在整個中國地區的影響。雖然仍受到資料審查制度的限制，但是文革時期的資料已是越來越開放。更重要的是，文革時期的重要見證人現正逐年老去，如本計劃這類的研究已是刻不容緩。 本計劃包括一名資深的中國學者和幾位中國以外的年輕學者，這將會促進跨越年代、學科和國界的學術交流。幾位音樂學家都對不同文化脈絡中音樂與革命政治之間的關係已有一定研究，並在進一步探討各種「邊陲」音樂文化之間的關係，以及它們與「中心」文化之間的聯係。本計劃將會是首個針對文革探討此議題的研究。當中將會涉及跨文化的學術議題，甚至延伸至中國音樂以外的範疇。

454710.label: Realisation of objectives
454710.value: Due to the unstable circumstances of the departmental management from 1 August 2012 and the subsequent decision made by the PI to depart from his current position, the project has to be closed down on 12 August 2013, although the end date of this project shall be 31 December 2013. As a result, there is insufficient time to refine or improve some project findings and outcomes. If a relief teacher could be appointed (funded from within the unspent balance HK$ 84511.78), and the remaining four and a half months could proceed according to the original proposal, the current report would be enhanced. Nevertheless, after two and a half years’ intensive ethnographic and archival research, the team members have gathered a large amount of oral history data and some critical materials (e.g. programme notes, audio/video recordings, internal reports and musical notations) that were previously unknown to the academic community. This gathered data not only helps us to understand the music-making and its relationship to the political ideologies during the era of China’s Cultural Revolution, but also helps us to make sense of some major musical developments since the 20th century. Sub-projects looking into the musical thought of Jiang Qing, and the tasks of the Zither Reform Committee/ Recording Committee provide fresh perspectives on the relationship between the cultural products (music and opera), central political leaders (Mao Zedong and Jiang Qing) and the political movement itself. The musical activities at the political centre, as suggested by findings of this project, were also very different from activities at the margins of China. To give just one example, in 1973 (or 1974) Jiang Qing set up the Recording Committee to serve Mao’s personal interests in Chinese traditional music and opera although the cultural and musical consumption by the general population were censored. The counter situations in Taiwan and Hong Kong during the Cultural Revolution have been addressed less in the project outcomes, due to the nature of our project focus and its writing narrative as well as large amount of research data that has a huge potential and deserves full investigation. A new project, titled “Cultural Revolution Beyond China’s Borders”, has now been proposed. The findings of the current project will not only serve as an important source for the upcoming project. With the new findings from the proposed project, a comprehensive cross-cultural comparison on music and revolution (or even anti-revolution) will be possible.

454710.label: Major findings and research outcome
454710.value: The major findings of this project can be outlined thematically under the following headings - Underground musical activities and the life of musicians. Several underground musical activities, such as the gathering among qin players, and the lives of influential musicians were documented. - Relationship between modernity and revolution. In Yanbian the researcher found that the Cultural Revolution, though written off as an aberration in musical history, showed many continuities with previous and later projects that modernized music for political ends. Local musicians were just beginning to reclaim this history, which had long been avoided as too sensitive. In Xinjiang, the researcher has found Uyghur “model opera” The Red Lantern during the 1970s sought to theorize the relationship between twentieth-century Uyghur musical modernism and the production of the model opera in the Uyghur context. This final finding has served to support the thesis that the Cultural Revolution was as much a continuation of minority nationalist cultural projects in twentieth-century China as it was a disruption. - Different approaches to transplanting model opera project. We have documented the careful incorporation of local and ethnic elements into centrally approved operas in two key border areas. Using interviews and contemporary reports, we have uncovered the lengthy process by which local musicians negotiated the limits of political acceptability, while trying to create a musically satisfying result. - Mao’s view on traditional music and opera. The study on the Recording Committee reveals not only Mao’s personal preference on traditional Chinese music and opera but also shows how his own personal interest contradicts to the revolutionary ideologies of the era. - Musical performances and diplomatic relationships. In Yanbian, China’s fractious relationship with North Korea was a key musical issue – North Korean sounds were forbidden. Yet, when diplomatic relations were restored, North Korean music was welcomed throughout China as a welcome contrast to model works. The central PRC government used the soft-power - performing arts of China - to enhance its diplomatic relationships with first and third world countries. Any important official foreign visits or state banquets would be complained by China’s performing troupes. - Music as ideology vs music as entertainment. Oral histories collected in Yanbian (as well as other areas of China) amongst participants in the cultural revolution (mainly former red guards) revealed that many found pleasure at the time in the musical aspects of the revolution, recollecting the dances and songs that accompanied demonstrations and meetings. Many songs were felt to be well-crafted musically, although the political ideology was now disliked. - Some rare data (programme notes, audio/visual recordings, and musical instruments) has been collected or identified. The recording of the Zither Reformed Committee and its internal report concert programme, as well as an unpublished book on Chinese music history, previously unknown to us, have been collected. In Yanbian, it was the first time in forty years that the original performers and composers had heard the music. - Relationship between centre and margin. Oral histories and archival research have revealed a changing relationship between centre and margins reflected in music, from imposition, through incorporation of margins, to ‘transplanting’ the music and ideology. During the earliest years of the Cultural Revolution, centrally created and approved music (such as the quotation songs) were imposed on the margins. The incorporation of the border regions into the Cultural Revolution was musically represented in key red songs, approved centrally and published nationally. However, after 1971, there was recognition that the revolution could only take root through the adaptation of local genres – a reaching out to the margins. The research outcome includes (See Part C)

454710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
454710.value: This project was conducted during a very critical time for two major reasons. (1) Participants in the cultural revolution are now elderly and their own point of views (oral histories) may otherwise never be heard; (2) Due to the current climate in China, the new generation of Chinese musicologists show little interest in understanding this particular history and its relationship to music and other performing arts. The project has collected, documented and made sense of these histories - music and data that may otherwise be forgotten - it has also inspired academic interest in this period. The project outcomes - academic publications and conference presentations - have developed our understanding of the relationship between music and the revolution both among the “political centre” and the “marginal minority”, in ways that were previously unknown. We have found that that the experiences of the Cultural Revolution, although repudiated today, still influence the development of modern Chinese music. The large amount of oral history data and some rare materials (e.g.. programme notes, audio/video recordings, and musical notations) collected by the project team members will eventually be made available to the general public by depositing them into the designated archives and libraries.

455010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
455010.value: 香港中英雙語使用者語言能力與注意力控制之間的關係

455010.label: Project Objectives
455010.value: To examine the relationship between L1/L2 proficiencies and components of attentional control within a Cantonese-English bilingual sample, after controlling for other factors (e.g., socioeconomic status). To capture the subtle variation of bilinguals' attention performance with their L1/L2 proficiency by using tasks with varied attentional demands. To tease apart the role of different components of attentional control (goal maintenance vs. conflict resolution) in the "bilingual advantage" by using finer-grained analytic procedures (ex-Gaussian modeling). To track age-related changes on the relationship between L1/L2 proficiencies and components of attentional control by recruiting children and adolescents with a wide age range.

455010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455010.value: In Hong Kong, most students from primary and secondary schools can be regarded as Cantonese-English bilinguals who can operate in both languages at a different level of proficiency. While the abilities to speak, write, read, and comprehend two languages are clearly language skills, recent research has demonstrated that bilinguals outperform those who know only one language (i.e., monolinguals) in attention-demanding tasks. The goal of the proposed study is to examine how this "bilingual advantage" in attention tasks is modulated by bilinguals' language proficiencies. The Stroop task offers a good example. When individuals read aloud the ink color of a color name (e.g., RED) that is printed in a nonmatching color (e.g., green) (i.e., incongruent trials), they need to suppress the irrelevant word and then access the relevant color. No such suppression need occur for congruent trials where the color and the word match (i.e., RED in red). The Stroop effect (slower and less accurate color naming for incongruent than congruent trials) reflects how well one can control attention and ignore irrelevant information. The smaller the Stroop effect, the better their attentional control abilities. Bilinguals often show a smaller Stroop effect than monolinguals. This bilingual advantage has often been reported in children and older adults, although relatively fewer findings have been demonstrated in adolescents who typically have better attentional control. Previous studies tended to contrast between monolinguals and bilinguals, confound some demographic characteristics of their samples, focus on a limited range of ages, group together bilinguals who differed in their language proficiencies and fail to clearly tease apart the advantages of bilingualism in various components of attentional control (e.g., goal maintenance vs. conflict resolution). The proposed study will address all these concerns. Given that bilinguals in Hong Kong have varied levels of language proficiencies, we will examine the effect of language proficiency on attentional control across a wide age range of Cantonese-English bilingual children and adolescents. After taking into account their nonverbal intelligence and other demographics (e.g., socioeconomic status), we will track the age-related changes in the relationship between proficiency in Chinese/English and attention performance. To pinpoint the specific component of attention control systems that is influenced by bilinguals' language proficiencies, we will increase the sensitivity of our measures by using two Stroop tasks with different attentional demands and modeling response-time data down to the level of their distributions. Results will enrich our theoretical understanding of bilingual advantages in attention control. 在香港，大部份學生是雙語使用者（即能說、寫、讀和理解兩種語言），雖然他們的中英語熟練程度各有不同。近來有研究發現雙語使用者在注意力控制的表現比單語使用者優勝。本研究的目的在於考察雙語使用者在注意力控制上的優勢會否受到他們語言的熟練程度所影響。 在斯特魯普實驗中，當被試者出聲朗讀顔色名稱的單詞（例：“紅”）呈現時的顔色時，如果這個顔色名稱和它本身的顔色含義不匹配的時候（例：綠色的“紅”字，不一致組），被試者需要抑制這種與任務無關的單詞含義干擾，而只注意加工單詞呈現的顔色。但當單詞代表的含義和呈現時的顔色一致時（例：紅色的“紅”字，一致組），被試者則不需要這種抑制。這種斯特魯普效應（相對於一致組，不一致組命名單詞呈現顔色的朗讀正確率比較低而朗讀速度也比較慢）反映了我們控制注意力並忽略其他無關信息的能力。斯特魯普效應越小，說明我們更能控制注意力。研究發現，雙語使用者的斯特魯普效應小於單語使用者。這種“雙語優勢”通常見於兒童和老年人，相對較少的研究採用具有更高注意力控制水平的青少年作爲被試。 前人研究有幾點不足之處，例如只比較單語使用者和雙語使用者，在研究樣本中混淆了一些人口學的特質，被試樣本的年齡範圍過於狹隘，忽略雙語使用者語言熟練程度的差異而把他們作爲同質群體，以及沒有明確區分“雙語優勢”在注意力控制系統不同組件上的影響（如：目標維持和衝突解決）。本研究將會一一考慮到這些問題。 因爲香港的雙語使用者對語言的熟練程度不同，我們將會考察語言熟練程度對注意力控制的影響。被試樣本的年齡跨度將會從兒童到青少年。在考慮到他們的非語言智力和其他人口學資料（例如：社會經濟地位）後，我們會繼續追蹤中英文熟練程度和注意力控制能力之間的關係的年齡變化。爲了加強我們測量的敏感度和研究雙語使用者語言熟練程度對不同注意力控制組件的影響，我們會用兩種對注意力控制有不同程度要求的斯特魯普實驗，同時又會探索反應速度的數據分布。這些結果將會豐富人們對雙語優勢在注意力控制的理論了解。

455010.label: Realisation of objectives
455010.value: In Study 1, we tested the bilingual young-adult samples in a Stroop color-naming task. Their data were analyzed by using ex-Gaussian modeling, the finer-grained analytic procedures. The results suggested that both conflict resolution and goal maintenance play significant roles in the relationship between attentional control and bilingualism. The results of this study achieved Objective 3. In Study 2, we tested bilingual young-adult samples in a task with higher attentional demands, that is, the Stroop switching task. The results showed a positive effect of bilinguals' second-language proficiency on the subtle variation of their attention, as reflected by performance in the switching task. The results of this study achieved Objective 2. In Study 3, we tested the bilingual children samples in two nonverbal attention tasks with varied demands (Simon and Simon switching) and a working memory task (operation span). Their data were analyzed by using ex-Gaussian modeling. After taking into account cognitive maturation, we found that conflict resolution plays a larger role than goal maintenance in the relationship between attentional control and bilingualism in the Simon task. However, we did not find any relationship between attentional control and bilingualism in the Simon switching task. This suggests that the relationship between task-set switching and bilinguals' language proficiency depends on participants’ age. Overall, the results of this study achieved Objectives 1, 3, and 4. The conflicting evidence between the Stroop and Simon switching tasks should be resolved by further experimentation. Thus, Objective 2 has only been partially addressed, to date. We conducted Study 4, with the design and procedure parallel to those in our Study 3 (yet with modified stimuli to accommodate task difficulty due to potential age-related differences) in bilingual adolescent samples. However, we found an issue regarding a speed-accuracy tradeoff in the Simon and Simon switching tasks—participants speeded up their responses at the expense of making more errors. This ambiguity made it difficult for us to compare these findings with those obtained in children (Study 3) and young adults (Studies 1 and 2). Given that the funding period was over and it was very difficult to recruit adolescent participants after their school term began in September, we were not able to clarify this in our project. Hence, we could not address Objective 4 to the fullest extent.

455010.label: Major findings and research outcome
455010.value: In Study 1 (Tse & Altarriba, 2011, International Symposium on Bilingualism; Tse & Altarriba, 2012, Bilingualism: Language and Cognition), we tested bilingual young-adult samples in a Stroop color-naming task. Their data were analyzed by using ex-Gaussian modeling, the finer-grained analytic procedures. The results showed that after controlling for other factors, such as socioeconomic status, the shift of the reaction-time distribution in incongruent vs. congruent trials, as well as the tail of the reaction-time distribution, were modulated by bilinguals’ first-language and second-language proficiencies. This suggests that both conflict resolution and goal maintenance play significant roles in the relationship between attentional control and second-language proficiency and echoes the recent view that the bilingual advantage in attentional control may be attributed to more than one cognitive mechanism. In Study 2 (Tse & Altarriba, 2011, Annual Meeting of the Psychonomic Society; Tse & Altarriba, 2014—in press, American Journal of Psychology), we tested bilingual young-adult samples in a task with higher attentional demands, that is, the Stroop switching task. The results showed a positive effect of bilinguals’ second-language proficiency on task-set shifting and updating and reconfiguration abilities (local switch cost) when they switch from a more difficult task set (color naming) to an easier task set (word reading) in the task switching paradigm. This study was the first to report that this task-set asymmetry in local switch costs was sensitive to bilinguals’ second-language proficiency in the literature. In Study 3 (Tse & Altarriba, 2013, International Symposium on Bilingualism; Tse & Altarriba, 2014—under revision, Special Issue “Context Specific Nature of Bilingual Cognitive Advantages” in Frontiers in Psychology: Language Sciences), we tested bilingual children samples in tasks with varied attentional demands, Simon, Simon switching, and operation span tasks. After taking into account cognitive maturation, we found that conflict resolution plays a larger role than goal maintenance in the relationship between attentional control and second-language proficiency in the Simon task. Bilinguals’ language proficiency did not modulate the local switch cost in the Simon switching task. This suggests that the relationship between task-set switching and bilinguals' first-language/second-language proficiency depends on participants’ age. Finally, we found that bilinguals’ second-language proficiency was associated with higher scores in the operation span task. Overall, these results suggest that bilingual children’s second-language proficiency was associated with their conflict resolution and working memory capacity, but not goal maintenance or task-set switching.

455010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
455010.value: In our Study 3, we obtained a relationship between bilinguals’ L2 proficiency and operation span scores. This measure has typically been used to reflect participants’ general working memory capacities. It is important to clarify which aspect of working memory capacities could be modulated by L2 proficiency the most by using working memory tasks with different stimuli (reading span, running span, and symmetry span). Using internal research funds offered by the Chinese University of Hong Kong, we are now running a preliminary project on this topic for young-adult bilinguals. In our Study 4, given the problem of speed-accuracy tradeoffs in the adolescents’ data, we could not clarify the age-related changes in the benefit of L2 proficiency in attentional control. Future research should modify the attentional control tasks to minimize this problem, e.g., using instructions that emphasize speed vs. accuracy and inserting short vs. long response deadlines. Given our cross-sectional design, we could not establish the causal link between L2 proficiency and attentional control abilities. Future studies should use longitudinal designs and follow up the development of attentional control groups in a group of bilingual children to test vigorously whether increasing L2 proficiency would cause bilinguals to develop stronger attentional control abilities.

455010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
455010.value: The current research demonstrates how bilinguals’ second-language proficiency is associated with different aspects of attentional control abilities. Those who have higher second-language proficiency (a) are more able to process information from multiple sources simultaneously because they have a larger “mental workspace” and (b) are less likely distracted by irrelevant information. In contrast, the relationship between bilinguals’ second-language proficiency and their ability to switch between tasks and to maintain the goal of an ongoing task may depend on their age. However, it is noteworthy that the causal link between second-language proficiency and attentional control abilities has not been established. It is possible that second-language proficiency could cause bilinguals to possess better attentional control abilities and those who have better attentional control abilities are more able to acquire a second language. This causal link should be verified by following up on the development of second-language acquisition and attentional control abilities in a group of bilingual children for a number of years, in future research. Nevertheless, the current study clearly showed that gaining proficiency in more than one language has direct, positive consequences on other forms of cognitive abilities, that is, attentional control.

455110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455110.value: An Urban heat island (UHI), defined as an urban experiencing a higher temperature than its surrounding areas, is one of the major concerns in the 21st century. Its effects include increased energy consumption, negative impacts on environmental quality and human health. Combining with the increase in number of urbanization per year and global warming, UHI effects will only be intensified in future. It is extremely important to properly address UHI issues and take immediate action on UHI mitigation. Many countries such as Japan and USA have addressed the significance of the detrimental effects of UHI and proposed various mitigation strategies used in urban planning level to response to UHI. The strategies comprise land use change, increase in green and water surface coverage, optimization of building configurations etc. However, at present, there is limited knowledge concerning the quantitative effects of these mitigation measures. Decision makers face difficulties in choosing the appropriate strategy and/or combination of the strategies among those. A proper mitigation measure should also consider the complex interrelationship between UHI and various mitigation strategies in different temporal and spatial scales. Therefore, there is a urgent need to develop a multi-scale simulation platform for the quantitative assessment of the UHI effects and its mitigation strategies to support decision making. Advanced numerical simulation tools could play a vital role in predicting and assessing UHI effects and UHI related mitigation strategies. This research aims at developing a multi-scale simulation platform based on numerical techniques for UHI related studies. The platform will consider multiscale modeling approach, which is a methodology to couple mesoscale atmospheric simulation model and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). The coupling technique will provide information exchange between the two models, such as the interaction between built environment, land use and atmosphere, improving the accuracy of the model prediction. The two simulation tools are currently used individually to investigate UHI issues but there is a concern that the model simplification in each technique will result in an unrealistic model prediction. This research does not only develop an efficient tool for decision makers to deal with UHI related matters to create a sustainable living environment; but also through case studies in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) region in this study enhance our understanding of the cause of UHI and the effectiveness of the mitigation strategies. 城市熱島是指城區溫度要高於周圍地區的現象。而熱島效應將導致能源消耗增加，並對環境質量和人類健康具有負面影響，它已經成為21世紀全世界所面臨一個問題。由於快速的城市化和全球變暖的綜合影響，城市熱島效應將來會進一步加劇，如何妥善解決城市熱島問題付諸於行動顯得極為重要。 許多國家已認識到城市熱島的不利影響，並在城市規划水平層面上提出了各種減緩城市熱島的策略，包括土地使用的變化，增加綠和水體的覆蓋，優化建築物配置等。但是目前而言，對這些相關緩解措施定量影響的認知還有限，使得決策者往往在選擇適當的戰略或採取什麼樣的綜合戰略時候面臨困難。優秀的城市熱島緩解措施應該能後考略不同時空尺度上熱島和緩解策略之間的複雜相互關係。因此，迫切需要發展一個多尺度的數值模擬平台，對城市熱島的影響及其減緩策略實施定量評估，以對決策過程進行支持。 先進的數值模擬技術，在城市熱島影響和各種緩解戰略的預測、評估過程中起到至關重要的作用。本項目基於城市熱島的數值模擬工具和相關研究，旨在建立一個耦合中尺度大氣模型和計算流體動力學（CFD）模型的多尺度模擬平台。數值耦合技術將使兩個模型在城市建築環境和土地利用、大氣狀態等多方面發生信息的交換，使得數值模擬的精確性提高。過去，上述兩個模型工具都單獨被用來研究熱島問題，但單個模式技術過於簡化，往往使得模擬結果和實際情況並不吻合。 本研究並不僅僅是為決策者解決城市熱島相關問題，創造可持續發展的居住環境建立一個有效的工具，，同時，本項目也可以通過在珠江三角洲個案研究，提升我們對我們對城市熱島成因和緩解戰略有效性的新認識。

455110.label: Realisation of objectives
455110.value: [Realization of objective 1] The multi-scale technologies for UHI monitoring and simulation are investigated. UHI mitigation is considered as an important part of green city planning.The multi-scale experiments are conducted for UHI monitoring and simulation. Remote sensing (RS) and Geographic Information System (GIS) are integrated in the platform. The UHI was monitored with satellite images, aerial images and images taken by the hand-held thermal infrared equipment. The Figure 1 in Appendix 1 shows the result of retrieving land surface temperature through satellite images with Remote Sensing technologies. The Figure 2 in Appendix 1 is the real-time temperature photo taken by hand-held thermal infrared equipment and processed by supporting software. The decision making platform will support the decision making process of urban planning regarding its eco-potential, intensity of development, etc. Comparing with traditional approaches, the systematic approach with different techniques provides the opportunities for conducting performance-based or data-driven decision making process for urban planning. Investigation of combing multi-scale grids were conducted, including the academic exchange with the Key Laboratory of Regional Climate-Environment Research for Temperate East Asia, Institute of Atmospheric Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the cooperation with the Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. [Realization of objective 2] Taking Sanshan, Shenzhen and Hong Kong as experimental sites in PRD area and Hanoi, Vietnam, as comparative study, land-cover change and surface temperature change with remote sensing monitoring demonstrates the relationship between the land cover change and UHI. Applying WRF model and CFD model together facilitates the detection of UHI dynamic along with urban transformation and how the urban development effects the UHI distribution or intensity. Supervised by the research group, some of the MSc. Advanced Environmental Planning Technologies Programme students conducted the thesis with related topics in their AEPT6100/ESGS6100 course. The selected research projects are listed in Appendix 2. [Realization of objective 3] The thermal environment index is included in the Sanshan Low-Carbon Ecocity Index System, which has been handed over to the local government. The guideline is composed of two major factors which are used to illustrate the performance of low carbon city planning in UHI effect mitigation: 1) ecological living environment; 2) low-carbon life style. 54 indexes are finally designed to assess the function of the above 11 indexes. These indexes considered thermal environment mitigation in a broad way that integrated the consideration of social-economic-environment factors. Please see the Appendix 3 for the index system.

455110.label: Major findings and research outcome
455110.value: [Cooling effect of land use patterns and urban textures, especially green infrastructure] With the integration of RS and GIS, the UHI was monitored with satellite images, aerial images and images taken by the hand-held thermal infrared equipment. The satellite and aerial images were used in surface temperature retrieval, and the hand-held thermal infrared monitoring was used to detect the effect from high-density vertical facade. With the staggered arrangement of green space, water and buildings, the city could be cooled down and the UHI could be mitigated. Experiments showed that most of the artificial infrastructures were heating cities while water bodies and vegetation were cooling the cities. From the analysis of the relationship between land use pattern and the formation of UHI, it is indicated that the UHI intensity will be enhanced with the reduction of urban green spaces and the agglomeration of population. Moreover, the urban renewal activities will also contribution to the enhancement of UHI, if improperly implemented. The experiments at Kowloon, Hong Kong, (see Figure 3 in Appendix 1) and Hanoi, Vietnam, (see Figure 4 in Appendix 1) showed that the urban regeneration process will influence on the UHI intensity due to land use change and the development activities. And Kowloon case also indicated the intra-urban migration also correlated to the dynamic of UHI. [Multi-Scale Decision Making Platform] Based on investigation and academic exchange with other research institutes, it was learnt the complexity of multi-scale simulation integration. The simulation technology is processed based on mesh and influenced by the grid size. As grids perform on the real objects, the illustration methods are varied on different objects, eg, wind, heat and light. There will be problems or mistakes, if normalize the different scales of grids in one way. [UHI mitigation guideline] There are two major significances regarding to the guideline. One is to forecast, detect and amend the development pattern and construction activities conducted in the urban area which may positively motivate the formation of UHI effect. The other is to contribute to the standardization of low-carbon eco-city evaluation system for the urban development located in sub-tropical climate zone. Analyzing and comparing the other eco-city evaluation systems, this mitigation guideline was applicable for comparing the performance of different sub-tropical cities and also helped to detect and evaluate the timely ecological environment progress. It focused not only on the living environment but also human lifestyle to guide the UHI mitigation.

455110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
455110.value: Urban developmental activities usually have impacts on the living environments, especially the thermal comfort of residents. Nowadays, people always feel hotter and hotter in the streets or other parts of cities covered by concrete or pitch than in rural areas, which make the urban areas feel like “heat islands”. However, we can cool down the urban areas or avoid it through the urban planning stage. Thus this project wants to collect the factors regarding to the urban characteristics that caused people feel extreme hot in urban areas and evaluate the contribution of each main factors to this heat island and define the influential parameters. Based on the parameters, we want to develop a comprehensive evaluation system to the urban heat island. The evaluation system will support the urban planners or government officers in their decision making on the future urban development mode which can cool down the cities and make the residents more comfortable with the living environment.

455110.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
455110.value: [Prizes] The paper presented by the research team and also supported by this RGC fund, “Applying Integrated and Multiple Scientific Methods in Urban Green Space Planning and Analysis”, was awarded the Best Paper Prize on the 10th China Urban Housing Conference. [Collaboration with other research institutions] Through this research project, the research group built collaboration with the Nanhai City Government in delivering the site experiments in Sanshan and related research seminars in mitigating the UHI effect in future urban development. The research works, including density control, green infrastructure planning, development intensity and all the developmental characteristics, are highly appreciated by the government. The research group also collaborated with Shu-Te University, Taiwan, and Kaohsiung City Government on a Memorandum of Understanding which will be a five-year comprehensive academic cooperation and exchange scheme in Eco-city planning, green industry training, green building development promotion as well as application of high-tech in all urban developmental areas. Some of the professional works have been conduced following the recommended approaches of this research, such as the “Kaohsiung LOHAS Building plan”. Seminar with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, USA, National University of Singapore, Osaka University, Japan and LBNL, NUS, Osaka U and Key Laboratory of Regional Climate-Environment Research for Temperate East Asia, Institute of Atmospheric Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences were conducted on the exchange of latest research findings. [Knowledge Transfer] Leading by the PI, the research group organized the 10th China Urban Housing Conference in Shanghai during July 2013. This conference, supported by the Expert Committee and Science & Technology Committee of Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, PRC, attracted more than 200 scholars, professionals and experts from Mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and overseas institutions. Four sub-forums related to issues of sustainable urban development and living environmental optimization were hosted as platforms for speakers in respective field to deliver their research findings and share opinions with other attendees. More than 120 papers were selected into the Proceeding of the 10th China Urban Housing Conference, demonstrating the most representative research stream and innovative thinking of urban characteristics. Based on the research outcome which were well spread and presented in international conferences and seminars, the research team also build collaboration network to transfer knowledge to students by organizing anural Visiting School @ Winter Break for students to learn the good experience of the eco-city development and urban cooling methods outside Hong Kong and also enhance their understanding of the UHI issue.

455310.label: Project Title(Chinese)
455310.value: 元明道教神仙經傳畫研究

455310.label: Project Objectives
455310.value: to build up an archive of images of Daoist pictorial hagiographies of the Yuan and Ming dynasties; to establish a chronology of Daoist hagiographic illustrations basing it on datable scriptures; to examine the evolution of Daoist hagiographic illustrations with special reference to the relationship between the conceptual approach, compositional structure and format of the illustrations and the religious contexts in which they were produced; to examine the artistic style of major religious book-printing workshops and their relation to patrons; to compare the evolution of Daoist hagiographic illustration with that of Buddhism and consider if Daoism has developed its system of hagiographic illustration.

455310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455310.value: The aim of the project is to investigate the hagiographic illustrations preserved in Daoist woodblock-printed or manuscript scriptures of the Yuan Dynasty and the Ming Dynasty so as to assess their artistic evolution and with particular reference to their Buddhist counterparts. Although the artistic and didactic value of narrative illustrations has been widely acknowledged in scholarship on Chinese art, previous studies have focused mostly on Buddhist and Confucian illustrations, leaving Daoist hagiographic illustrations largely untouched. The neglect may be ascribed to the conventional assumption that Daoist art was influenced by Buddhist art and that pictorial hagiographies of Daoist deities were mere derivatives of those of the Buddha. However, this conventional assumption has lately been challenged, as recent scholarship has shown that Daoist hagiographic illustrations might have been organized in accordance with principles specific to Daoism. The proposed project aims to explore the patterns of evolution of Daoist hagiographic illustration in China and to assess the extent to which a framework for categorizing and analysing Daoist hagiographic illustration, independent of that of Buddhism, can be established. The outputs of the proposed project will include an archive of images of Daoist hagiographic illustrations of the Yuan and Ming periods, and a series of academic papers on the following issues: (1) The evolution of Daoist hagiographic illustration By establishing an archive of images of datable pictorial hagiographies, the study will investigate the patterns of evolution in the hagiographic illustrations of certain prominent Daoist deities, such as the Dark Warrior, the Celestial Worthy of Thunder, Xu Xun (許遜) and Wenchang (文昌), and consider possible correlation between the modes of pictorial representation and the religious motives behind their production. (2) Woodblock-printing workshops and their relation to patrons Focusing on Daoist hagiographic illustrations produced in the Xuande-Zhengtong period (1426-1449) and the Jiajing period (1522-1566), the study will examine how social factors other than religious reasoning, such as artistic style of printing workshops and the taste of patrons, affected the visual characteristics of pictorial hagiographies. (3) The differences and similarities between the evolution of Daoist hagiographic illustration and that of Buddhism With the supply of solid visual and textual materials, the proposed project will consider if Daoism has developed a unique system of illustrating its gods, saints and immortals, and whether the long-standing assumption about the arts of the two religions can be substantiated. 本計劃旨在研究保存於元明道經刊本和手抄本中的神仙圖像，探討它們的藝術發展軌跡，以及與佛教圖經的關係。 在中國藝術史的領域，學界早已承認叙事性插畫的藝術和教育價值。然而，過去的研究大多只集中於佛教和儒家經典的插畫，而道教經典中的神仙插畫則鮮有討論。以往對道經插畫的忽略，部份是由於道教藝術一直被認為是受佛教藝術影響而產生，而道教神仙傳插畫則是佛陀傳的衍生品。但近年一些道教藝術的研究，卻對上述的傳統觀念提出挑戰，並指出道教神仙傳插畫很可能是根據道教獨有的觀念而設計。本研究計劃的目的，是要整理出中國道經中神仙插畫的發展模式，並探討能否建立一個獨立於佛教圖經發展，而可用於分類道教神仙插畫和分析其內容和形式的理論框架。 本研究計劃將建立一個元明道經神仙插畫的資料庫，並發表論文以討論下列專題： (1)道經神仙插畫的發展 本研究通過建立元明道經神仙插畫資料庫，嘗試整理真武、雷聲普化天尊、許遜、文昌等道教主要神和仙的圖像發展，並探討圖像的表現形式與產生該圖像的宗教目的之關係。 (2)雕版印刷中心及道經贊助人的關係 明代宣德至正統（1426-1449）以及嘉靖（1522-1566）朝皆是道教圖經產量較多的年代，本研究將探討在此期間除宗教因素以外，其他可能影響道經神仙插畫發展的因素，包括中國各地雕版印刷中心的藝術特色和贊助人的品味等。 (3)道佛神仙傳插畫的異同 在上述的圖像和文獻研究的基礎上，本研究將探討道教是否有一套用於展示神靈、聖人和仙真圖像的獨特系統，並重新檢視道佛藝術的關係。

455310.label: Realisation of objectives
455310.value: Objective 1: 1. An archive of images of Daoist hagiographic illustrations of the Yuan and Ming dynasties has been established. It contains images from about 80 illustrated Daoist scriptures collected from libraries all over the world. 2. At the beginning of the project, the PI narrowed down the scope of scripture collection to those in accordion binding (format of ancient scripture) due to the sheer amount of extant Daoist books. She acquired the images by visiting the libraries in person or by mail. 3. Object 1 has been achieved. Objective 2: 1. The PI established the chronologies of Daoist hagiographic illustrations for major Daoist scriptures based on datable scriptures. 2. With the help of the chronologies established, tentative dating has also been given to undated copies of individual scriptures based on stylistic similarities. 3. Object 2 has, in the main, been achieved. 4. There are some illustrations bearing too few distinctive features to be dated to a specific period. More study on the artistic style of religious paintings and printing beyond accordion-bound scriptures may help overcome the problem of dating. Object 3: 1. The PI conducted case study on three major scriptures, including Scripture of the Jade Pivot, Scripture of the Jade Emperor and Scripture of Salvation to probe into the relationship between different kinds of hagiographic illustrations and the religious contexts in which they were produced. 2. Images from different editions of a single scripture were drawn from the image archive for study. In the case of Scripture of the Jade Pivot (Yushu jing玉樞經), focus was given to the relationship between different modes of illustrations and the development of a Daoist tradition. The study of Scripture of the Jade Emperor (Yuhuang jing玉皇經)concerned how the choices of deities were related to different liturgical traditions. The study of Scripture of Salvation (Duren jing 度人經) dealt with the function of scriptural illustrations. 3. Objective 3 has been achieved. Objective 4: 1. The PI has had difficulty in pursuing information about Daoist book-printing workshops. For few Daoist scriptures collected in the archive bear places of production. Also, many datable Daoist scriptures were inscribed rather than printed, thus offering no information about the printing industry. Hardly any secondary research has been done on the subject. 2. Rather than focusing on religious printing workshop, the PI turned to investigate how the artistic style of Daoist books was related to their patrons. 3. Objective 4 has been archived in part.
