455310.label: Major findings and research outcome
455310.value: 1. The project discovered a large number of Ming-dynasty accordion-bound Daoist scriptures with illustrations which have never been noticed and published. An image archive was established. A table listing all references of the illustrations has been uploaded to the following website for public access: http://www.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/~fadept/txt/Maggie%20Wan/wan8.pdf (Also see Part C, 11, no. 1). 2. The PI noted that there were multiple traditions of Daoist hagiographic illustrations coexisted and developed in the Yuan and Ming periods. Hence, the term “evolution” mentioned in the project title cannot fully describe the development of Daoist hagiographic illustrations. Case studies to investigate the development of major traditions were, thus, conducted. 3. To clear up the connection between Ming hagiographic illustrations and their predecessors, the PI studied the Sancai dingwei tu, a Song-dynasty illustrated scripture preserved in the Ming Daoist Canon. My research has established that the Ming edition is conceptually and pictorially connected to its Song original. My research was presented in an international conference in 2011 (Part C, 9, no. 1) and a paper published in Taida Journal of Art History (Part C, 8, no. 1). 4. The case study on Scripture of Jade Pivot has showed that the selection of deities as appeared in frontispieces changed according to liturgical traditions affiliated to Thunder Rites in the Ming dynasty. Also the choice of composition for a frontispiece depended on the purposes of scripture production. My research was presented in the AAS and a workshop in Dartmouth, US (Part C, 9, nos. 3 & 4). The paper has been submitted to Artibus Asiae and currently under review (Part C, 8, no. 3). 5. The case study on Scripture of Salvation has demonstrated that successive scriptural illustrations serve to explicate, supplement and draw attention to selected highlights of the text. They offer pictorial aids to the reciters to visualize the essence of the scripture which concerns mostly visions and realms that are invisible and intangible. My research was presented in an international conference in 2011 (Part C, 9, no. 2). The paper will be published in a book (accepted) in 2014 (Part C, 8, no. 2). 6. The case study on Scripture of the Jade Emperor has reinforced my argument that the choices of composition and individual deities in the frontispieces were determined by liturgical traditions with which the edition was associated. My research was presented in an international conference in London (Part C, 9, no. 5).

455310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
455310.value: 1. The frontispieces for the Ming Daoist Canon form an important group of Daoist scriptural illustrations. They represented the imperial standard for Daoist prints of the mid-fifteenth century and an imperially recognized Daoist pantheon. Different editions of the frontispieces can also shed light on how the Ming Daoist pantheon was modified in later periods. The PI is currently conducting a GRF project entitled “Frontispieces to the Ming Daoist Canon: Formation, Edition and History” (GRF reference 451513) to pursue this topic. 2. There are a good number of Daoist illustrated scriptures produced in the last decade of the Wanli period (1610-1620). The Wanli Emperor was seldom considered to be a Daoist believer. A study on his religious belief and the intentions behind his production of Daoist scriptures will shed light on this unknown aspect of his life. 3. The PI plan to author a book on Daoist scriptural illustrations. The book will offer a comprehensive examination of the frontispieces and illustrations for major Daoist scriptures and the Daoist Canon in the Ming dynasty. The proposed study of the Wanli Emperor will also be include as a case for understanding the relationship between patrons and the making of illustrated scriptures.

455310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
455310.value: The project aimed at investigating hagiographic illustrations preserved in Daoist wood-block printed and manuscript scripture of the Yuan and Ming dynasty. It focused on Daoist scriptures in accordion binding, an ancient religious book format. The project has archived the followings. First, it collected Daoist hagiographic illustrations from libraries all over the world and built up an archive of images. The archive offered abundant little known visual materials for the study of Daoist art and culture. Second, it established the chronology of hagiographic illustrations for major Daoist scriptures, including Scripture of Jade Pivot, Scripture of Jade Emperor, and Scripture of Salvation. Third, the project established that Daoist hagiographic illustrations did not evolve from a simple to a complex representation. Rather, many traditions of Daoist hagiographic illustrations coexisted in the Ming dynasty. The selection of deities as appeared in frontispieces for a scripture changed according to liturgical traditions with which a particular edition of the scripture was associated. Also, the choice of composition for an illustration depended on the purposes of commissioning the scripture. This project opened up a new area of study in Chinese art history and Daoism. Also, it lay down a solid foundation for further study on Daoist prints.

455410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
455410.value: 海外独立董事对上市公司的价值

455410.label: Co - Investigator(s)
455410.value: Prof Masulis, Ronald Prof Xie, Fei

455410.label: Project Objectives
455410.value: To examine how prevalent are FIDs on the boards of U.S. public companies. To study what types of firms are more likely to have FIDs. To investigate whether FIDs are effective monitors or valuable advisors; To study the impact of FIDs on shareholder value and firm performance and whether FIDs strengthen or weaken board effectiveness in handling specific corporate decisions and tasks.
rows: To examine how prevalent are FIDs on the boards of U.S. public companies.
To study what types of firms are more likely to have FIDs.

To investigate whether FIDs are effective monitors or valuable advisors; To study the impact of FIDs on shareholder value and firm performance and whether FIDs strengthen or weaken board effectiveness in handling specific corporate decisions and tasks.

455410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455410.value: The board of directors is a critical element of a firm’s corporate governance system, and it has two major functions: monitoring senior managers and providing advisory services. In this study, we propose to investigate an interesting class of directors for whom the very attribute that enables them to perform one function well hinders their ability to carry out the other—foreign independent directors (FIDs) in U.S. corporations, defined as independent directors domiciled in foreign countries. We hypothesize that there are both benefits and costs associated with having FIDs on board. On the one hand, FIDs can enhance the advisory capability of boards to the extent that living or working in a foreign country gives them first-hand knowledge of the foreign market and the opportunity to develop a network of foreign contacts. These resources allow FIDs to provide valuable insights and assistance to U.S. corporations with either existing foreign operations or aspirations to expand internationally. On the other hand, because of considerable oversight costs created by geographic distance and international travel, FIDs may have greater difficulties in fulfilling their monitoring function and thus weaken the effectiveness of boards, leading to questionable board decision making and weaker corporate performance. Given the concomitant benefits and costs associated with FIDs, their net effects on overall board effectiveness, firm value and performance, and corporate decision making represent intriguing empirical questions. We plan to start with S&P 1500 companies from 1998 to 2006. We will first examine the sample frequency distribution of firms with FIDs and then investigate what type of firms are more likely to have FIDs. Finally and most importantly, we will study whether FIDs are less effective monitors than their U.S. based counterparts and whether there are circumstances under which companies benefit from having FIDs. Specifically, we will examine the market reactions to FID appointments, effect of FIDs on firm performance, FIDs’ board meeting attendance records, and whether FIDs strengthen or weaken board effectiveness in handling specific corporate policies and tasks such as the quality of accounting disclosure, executive compensation, and foreign acquisitions. 随着企业发展壮大，所有权与控制权分离，为了保证管理层从股东利益出发、减少代理成本，董事会及独立董事制度应运而生。董事会由股东大会选举产生，是公司治理机制中以保护股东利益为最终目标的重要组成部分。其职能之一是扮演监督角色：聘用、激励、并在必要时解聘上市公司管理层；其职能之二是扮演咨询角色：为管理层的重大战略决策提供专业建议。独立董事制度不仅能够制约管理层，还能制约大股东利用其控股地位侵害外部股东利益，这将进一步强化董事会的制衡机制，保护中小投资者的利益。 海外独立董事是独立董事中一个很特别的群体. 他们是指那些与其担任独立董事的上市公司处于不同国家的董事。而对于上市公司的股东来说，任命海外独立董事可以说是一把“双刃剑”，其“利”与“弊”也经常能够在某些重大问题上得以显现。 一方面，由于海外独立董事与其所属上市公司相距甚远，而行使监督职能最重要的途径——董事会议，一般又是在上市公司总部举行，长途跨国旅行的艰辛及其所耗时间成本会导致海外独立董事经常缺席董事会议。同时上市公司总部所在地会形成本地“网络”和诸多“软信息”，这些都能帮助独立董事更好地了解公司经营状况和监督管理层，可是海外独立董事却无法获取这些资源。加之他们不一定熟悉当地的会计准则、法律制度、监管环境、治理标准和管理文化等，这些因素都使得海外独立董事的监督职能被明显地减弱，增加了股东与管理层之间的代理成本，最终会降低上市公司经营业绩和股东价值。 另一方面，海外独立董事因其所处位置而普遍具有国际视野，当上市公司涉及拓展海外业务（尤其是与海外独立董事所在国家和地区有业务往来）时，他们往往能够提出独到和精准的专业建议甚至直接帮助上市公司建立海外关系、更好地融入国际市场，这时海外独立董事的咨询职能便得到体现，从而会提高上市公司经营业绩和股东价值。 那么，现实中这些扮演了监督与咨询双重角色的海外独立董事们究竟表现得如何呢？是否真如上文所分析的那样“利”“弊”兼备呢？我们将对1998年到2006年间纳入S&P1500指数的上市公司进行系统的研究。我们将首先研究什么样的公司会倾向于雇佣海外董事。进而研究海外独立董事是否尽到了有效的监督职责。我们将研究海外独立董事出席董事会议的频率、付给CEO的薪酬是否过高、是否尽职监管上市公司的会计质量，以及最终对公司价值和业绩的影响。

455410.label: Realisation of objectives
455410.value: We have three objectives proposed in the original application. We have successfully achieved 100% of each of the three objectives. To achieve the first objective, we started with firms in S&P 1500 the period between 1998 and 2006 (around 1500 firms per year). We hired a full-time research assistant to hand-collect the country origins of all the independent directors in this sample. We classify directors whose primary employers are based outside U.S. as foreign independent directors (FIDs). Our summary statistics show that FIDs are present in about 13% of firm-year observations. Conditional on a board having at least one FID, the percentage of FIDs among all independent directors averages about 18%, equivalent to one FID in every 5 to 6 independent directors. Regarding the second objective, we estimate a probit model with the dependent variable being the indicator for whether a company hires FIDs. The explanatory variables include a firm’s financial characteristics and governance variables. The results from this probit model suggest that large firms and firms with more foreign operations are more likely to hire FIDs. More interestingly, we also find that firms are more likely to have FIDs when their headquarters is located within 100 kilometers of one of the top-10 international airports in the U.S. This is consistent with the argument that FIDs may prefer to sit on boards of firms whose headquarters they can more easily reach. To address the research question raised in our third objective, we examine several actions undertaken by FIDs and some major corporate policies and decisions in which they are frequently involved. Specifically, we study FIDs’ board meeting attendance record and the impact of FIDs on (1) the performance of a company’s cross-border acquisitions; (2) a firm’s accounting disclosure quality;(3) CEO compensation policy; (4) board effectiveness on disciplining poorly-performing CEOs. Our analyses produce a set of rich findings suggesting that FIDs are generally less effective monitors than their U.S. based counterparts, but they could be valuable advisors under certain circumstances. Specifically, we find that FIDs display poor board meeting attendance records, and firms with FIDs are more prone to commit intentional financial misreporting and overpay their CEOs and have lower CEO turnover sensitivity to performance. However, firms with FIDs also make better cross-border acquisitions when the targets are from the home regions of FIDs.

455410.label: Major findings and research outcome
455410.value: The research project has produced a working paper. We have presented the paper in a number of research institutions, including the Chinese University of Hong Kong, George Mason University, Tilburg University, and Vanderbilt University. The paper was also presented at the 2011 American Finance Association (AFA) (please see supporting documents attached in Part C), one of the top finance conferences. Below we summarize the major findings of the study. We first investigate how prevalent are foreign independent directors (FIDs) on the boards of U.S. public companies. Our examination of the boards of S&P 1500 companies from 1998 to 2006 reveals that FIDs are present in about 13% of firm-year observations. Conditional on a board having at least one FID, the percentage of FIDs among all independent directors averages about 18%, equivalent to one FID in every 5 to 6 independent directors. Regarding the types of firms that are more likely to have FIDs on their boards, our findings suggest that large firms and firms with more foreign operations (measured by the percentage of total sales from foreign subsidiaries) are more likely to hire FIDs. Moreover, our results also indicate that FIDs tend to sit on the boards of companies that are located close to the top 10 U.S. airports, suggesting that FIDs prefer firms that they can easily reach from their home countries. We also study specific actions undertaken by FIDs and some major corporate policies in which they are involved. These tests aim to provide insights into the channels through which FIDs impact board effectiveness, shareholder value and firm performance. We find that firms with FIDs make better cross-border acquisitions when they pursue targets from the home regions of FIDs, evidence of the value added by FID expertise. However, we also find that FIDs are more likely to miss board meetings than domestic independent directors, and that firms with FIDs pay their CEOs excessively high compensation and are more likely to engage in egregious financial misreporting. These findings point to the monitoring deficiencies of FIDs and suggest that they undermine the effectiveness of board oversight and contribute to more managerial slack and misbehavior. Overall, our findings suggest that there are both benefits and costs of having foreign directors on the boards of U.S. public corporations.

455410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
455410.value: We have discussed one potential extension of our study and plan to develop it into a separate research paper.Specifically, we plan to investigate FIDs' insider trading activities. We have two competing hypotheses regarding the profits from FIDs' trading of their companies' stocks. One is that FIDs may have less valuable inside information about the firms where they serve as outside directors because of the long geographic distance between the U.S. firms' headquarters and FIDs' home countries. On the other hand, FIDs are more likely to engage in fraudulent insider trading activities than U.S. domestic directors. This is because many FIDs are from countries with weaker investor protections and legal systems (e.g. Mexico and Brazil), and as a result, they may be less sensitive to poor corporate governance and managerial self-serving behavior than U.S. based independent directors, who are accustomed to higher standards. We are currently collecting the information on FIDs' stock transactions and we will start the empirical analysis once the data collection is completed.

455410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
455410.value: We study independent directors of U.S. firms who are based in foreign countries, and investigate how their geographic location affects their ability to perform their monitoring and advisory duties. On the positive side, foreign independent directors (FIDs) can utilize their international background and expertise to enhance the advisory function of boards and benefit firms with substantial foreign operations or plans for overseas expansion. On the negative side, the geographic distance between FIDs and corporate headquarters, as well as national borders with passport and custom controls create significant obstacles for FIDs to effectively participate in the governance of U.S. firms. Our evidence indicates that the international expertise of FIDs benefits firms with substantial foreign operations or when making cross-border acquisitions. However, for firms without major operations in the home regions of FIDs, it appears that FIDs’ expected advisory benefits are not large enough to offset the value destroying effect of their weaker monitoring. Appointing FIDs to boards may be a well-intentioned decision, but a potential pitfall is that it overlooks the logistical difficulties and informational disadvantage that FIDs must overcome to perform their duties effectively. Overall, our findings suggest that a careful cost-benefit analysis is warranted when firms hire foreign directors.

455510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455510.value: The aim of the whole project is to translate, compile and publish the Chinese edition of "Major Works of Martin Heidegger" (20 vol.). The current project is the first phase of the whole plan. 12 out of 20 vol. of Heidegger's Major Works would be Published or ready for publication within 3 years. Martin Heidegger (1889-1976) is one of the most important philosophers in the past 100 years of world history. Since the year of 1987, several of the important philosophical works of Heidegger have been translated into Chinese and have tremendous influences on contemporary Chinese thoughts. Both the PI and the Co-Is of this proposed project have participated very actively in the works of translation of Heidegger and thus become major translators and researchers of Heidegger’s philosophy in the Chinese speaking world. Considering that 1) some of the important Heidegger’s works have not been translated into Chinese yet; 2) many of the existing translations have been done for years and need to be revised in order to reflect the new development of Heidegger scholarship both in the West and in China; 3) many of the existing translations have been published by different publishers in different styles and do not fit the standard new German edition of Heidegger Gesamtausgabe (102 vol.), it is necessary to compile the Chinese edition of “Major Works of Martin Heidegger” (20 vol.). The project should not be simply treated as a "transfer" of foreign texts. Translation of philosophical classics must be understood as serious work of research itself. It is dialogue of thinking at the most fundamental level of languages, as well as that of values and cultures. To carry out the project, we will 1) complete 3 new Chinese translations of Heidegger's Major Works; 2) revise 9 existing Chinese translations of Heidegger in accordance with the format of the standard German edition of Heidegger's Gesamtausgabe; 3) draft a series of research articles along the way of preparing the translations. 4) develop some post-graduate level seminars / lectures which would be based on the above mentioned works of translation. 5) cooperate with the project (Project No. CUHK 4559/06H) of "A Trilingual (German, English, Chinese) Lexicon of Heidegger's Philosophical Vocabulary". 6) hold a small workshop. 7) prepare for the phase II of the project which will work on Chinese translation of 5 new vol.; revision of 3 existing vol. of "Major Works of Martin Heidegger"(20 vol.). 本研究計畫的目標在於完成編纂、翻譯中文版《海德格文集20卷》- 第一階段10卷的工作。考慮到海德格在當代哲學思想史上的重要地位以及過去30年來海德格哲學著作在華語地區的出版、研究和影響的現狀，依據德文標準新版《海德格全集》，編纂、翻譯和出版一部中文版的、包括海德格哲學基本著作的《海德格文集》時機已經成熟，這對漢語哲學研究和思想發展也將有著極為重大的意義。雖然本計畫的基本實施方式是翻譯，但思想的翻譯，尤其是經典思想的認真翻譯從來就不是單純的“轉述”，它本身就是一項嚴肅的學術研究，它是一種在語言、文化、和價值層面上的深層次的思想對話過程。 具體來說，本研究計畫(第一階段)準備用3年時間，通過香港學者與內地學者合作的方式， 完成並爭取出版 1) 3卷海德格基本著作的漢語新譯； 2）7卷過去已出版的海德格基本著作漢語譯本的修訂（依據德文標準新版全集本）； 3）若干與此翻譯工作相關的研究論文，包括譯者前言、後記、譯名討論； 4）若干與此翻譯工作相關的課程、研討班、講座等等； 5) 一次關於海德格思想研究和翻譯的小型會議; 6）開始該研究計畫的第二階段（海德格文集11-20卷）的準備性工作。

455510.label: Realisation of objectives
455510.value: Most of the objectives of this project are completed successfully. Within the period of the project, we published three new Chinese translations of Heidegger's major works, i.e., "Kant and the Problem of Metaphysics" (2011);"Difference and Identity" (2011) and "New Translation of Introduction to Metaphysics"(2015); one monograph on "Heidegger and the Beginning of Philosophy" (2015); one edited book on "Heidegger: Translation, Interpretation and Understanding"(forthcoming);12 journal article or book chapters; 11 international or national conference presentations. A workshop was held successfully with more than 20 top scholars in the field participated. Besides courses which are on both undergraduate and post-graduate levels, and are partially related to the project topic, a post-graduate seminar was offered on the subject of the project. A PhD student was supervised and a PhD thesis on the related topic was completed. The PI was also invited by the prestigious universities such as Peking University and Fudan University to give lecture-series on the project subjects. All of these achievements help to establish solid grounds to further and to develop this pilot project into an even bigger one, i.e., completion of "Chinese Translation of Heidegger's Major Works (20 vol.)" as the second phase. The only under-achievement of the project is "the revision of the 7 existing Chinese translations". It was originally the main responsibilities of our Co-Is. Mainly because of the failure of getting the final approval of the publication plan (which was originally approved as part of the budget and again of the revised budget), we cannot use the funding in the budget to fulfill the contract with the publisher and to support the works of our colleagues outside Hong Kong. As the PI, I tried several other ways to solve the problems. For example, I contacted the Hong Kong publishers such as Oxford University Press (HK) and The Commercial Press (HK). The former rejected me because of financial reasons while the latter’s proposal could not be approved by UGC either. Then we had to change the way of cooperation with scholars outside Hong Kong into one with a more looser style and to give up an united publication plan under the GRF project. During the first year of carrying out the project, all of our publications were without giving an acknowledgement. This mistake was due to my lack of experience in handling the GRF grant. We have made full acknowledgement in all later publications since then.

455810.label: Project Title(Chinese)
455810.value: 全球共同基金间的竞争状况

455810.label: Project Objectives
455810.value: To understand the circumstances under which the mutual fund business model succeeds in attracting investors’ flows, by taking country as the unit of observation. To examine whether mutual fund industry is competitive in a broad sample of countries, using our parsimonious measure of overlap in equity holdings. To identify the country factors that are related to competitive forces in mutual fund industries around the world. To evaluate the importance of the foreign mutual funds holding of domestic equity as the contribution to the size and fee difference in mutual fund industry around the world.
rows: To understand the circumstances under which the mutual fund business model succeeds in attracting investors’ flows, by taking country as the unit of observation.
To examine whether mutual fund industry is competitive in a broad sample of countries, using our parsimonious measure of overlap in equity holdings.
To identify the country factors that are related to competitive forces in mutual fund industries around the world.
To evaluate the importance of the foreign mutual funds holding of domestic equity as the contribution to the size and fee difference in mutual fund industry around the world.

455810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455810.value: This paper is to study the competition of mutual funds around the worlds. Establishing a connection between entrants and incumbents requires us to measure the degree to which an entrant competes with incumbents. The unique nature of mutual fund disclosures allows us to bypass the problems, at least to some degree. Knowledge of mutual fund stock holdings entails us to create parsimonious metrics with which to measure the equity overlaps between each incumbent fund and entrant fund. Using our measure, we plan to perform the analysis of economic consequence (price, revenue, cost and profit) on incumbent funds in a set of countries, which can be viewed as a litmus test for a competitive force of mutual fund industry around the world. Skepticism about competition in the mutual fund industry dates back to the 1960’s view that market forces fail to constrain fund advisory fees. It’s been long argued that mutual fund industry featuring a very large “skimming operation” is not a paragon of competitiveness. However, one can easily argue, in the context of the economic forces, that investor’s discipline through capital redemption and redeployment, combined with low barriers to entry shall result in robust competition in mutual fund industry that, among others, constrains the amount of fees charged by an adviser. Our project contributes in three main ways to the current literature. First, this is among the first few papers attempting to examine the competitive force in mutual fund industries around the world. It shall bring substantial, hopefully conclusive, evidence on the controversy about the alleged excess advisor fee practice. Second, different nature of mutual fund competition around the world can also help explain the well-documented cross-country variation in size and fee in mutual fund industry. Third, the study of foreign mutual fund holdings of domestic equity and its impact on domestic mutual funds can also shed some lights on whether foreign investors are disadvantaged due to information, distance and culture differences. 本文旨在研究全球共同基金间的竞争状况。为了建立市场中新进入基金和既有基金之间的联系，我们需要衡量新进入基金在何种程度上和既有基金进行竞争。共同基金所特有的披露原则使我们可以在一定程度上解决这些问题。基于有关共同基金持有股票的信息，可以产生一个近乎完美的指标，以此来衡量每个既有基金和新进入基金之间重叠持有的股票。利用这个重叠指标，我们将分析一连串国家的既有基金所承受的经济后果（包括价格，收益，成本和利润），这可以作为全球共同基金行业竞争力测试的试金石。 针对共同基金之间竞争的怀疑论可追溯到1960年代，它认为市场的力量无法限制基金提高管理费用。长久以来备受争论的议题是，具有大量“隐性操作”的共同基金业究竟是不是充分竞争力的典范。然而，我们很容易得出，在市场经济力量的背景下，投资者具有资本赎回和重新调配的能力，加上进入门槛低，将导致共同基金业的强力竞争，其中包括将限制管理费用。 我们的研究有以下三个主要方面的贡献。首先，本文率先研究全球共同基金业的竞争力问题，并将提供关于超额管理费用这个争议的实质性甚至是决定性论据。其次，全球共同基金业的不同竞争特性，将有助于解释不同国家间共同基金业的规模和收费差异。最后，关于境外共同基金持有境内股票以及其对境内共同基金的影响的研究，也将有助于探求是否境外投资者在信息、距离和文化差异方面处于不利的竞争地位。

455910.label: Project Title(Chinese)
455910.value: 结构性信用市场和公司借贷

455910.label: Co - Investigator(s)
455910.value: Prof Goyal, Vidhan K Mr Xia, Han

455910.label: Project Objectives
455910.value: Examine the effect of banks’ access to the capital from CDO investors on their lending policies. What types of borrowers do banks extend the structured credit to? How loan contract terms are affected by banks’ access to the CDO capital? Investigate borrowers’ investment and financing choices in response to the new supply of capital from CDO investors and the associated shift in banks’ monitoring incentives. How was this new source of credit used in borrowers’ real financing and investment? Do borrowers take more risk and engage more in risk-shifting activities? Do we observe higher default risks associated with borrowing from CDO-active banks?
rows: Examine the effect of banks’ access to the capital from CDO investors on their lending policies. What types of borrowers do banks extend the structured credit to? How loan contract terms are affected by banks’ access to the CDO capital?

Investigate borrowers’ investment and financing choices in response to the new supply of capital from CDO investors and the associated shift in banks’ monitoring incentives. How was this new source of credit used in borrowers’ real financing and investment? Do borrowers take more risk and engage more in risk-shifting activities? Do we observe higher default risks associated with borrowing from CDO-active banks?

455910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455910.value: Bank loans are considered a special source of financing for businesses. Bank lending involves greater monitoring, and bank loan contracts are easier to renegotiate compared to public debt contracts. However, recent developments in structured credit markets, particularly the growth of collateralized debt obligations (CDOs) substantially altered the traditional role of banks. CDOs pool portfolios of loans or other assets, restructure the cash flow, and sell claims in different classes to various investors. This innovation creates additional demand for corporate loans from non-bank investors that cannot be generated from loan sales or loan syndication within the banking system. The new demand creates incentives for banks to originate loans with the purpose of distributing them to non-bank investors. This new incentive for lending has implications for the role that banks play in information production, monitoring, and enforcing contracts. This project examines whether the growth of the CDO market and the consequent increase in supply of credit affected the nature of corporate lending. We will focus on four main questions. First, we investigate if banks’ access to CDO capital shifted lending towards larger, less risky borrowers. With less monitoring associated with loans distributed through CDOs, banks would shift lending to firms with less severe information asymmetries and agency problems. Second, we examine the impact of banks’ access to CDO capital on loan contract terms. A positive supply shock should reduce prices while increase quantities. We expect lower spreads and larger loan amounts for loans by CDO-active banks. We also expect longer loan maturity and less restrictive covenants in these loans. Third, we examine the impact of borrowing from CDO-active banks on firms’ financing and investment policies. We expect borrowers to increase their leverage as the availability of credit increases. We also expect a change in the composition of debt as firms shift from public debt to bank loans. On the asset side, we expect borrowers of CDO-active banks to increase their investment in physical assets and engage in more M&A transactions. Fourth, we examine the impact of reduction in bank monitoring associated with structured lending on borrowers’ risk-taking incentives. Less monitoring provides borrowers with greater incentives to take risks. We will look for evidence of increased risk-taking by examining asset volatility and distance-to-default, two commonly used measures of default risks. We also expect borrowers of CDO-active banks to exhibit higher default rates on their debt obligations and under-perform compared to other borrowers. 银行贷款是公司融资的一种特殊来源。与公共债券合同相比，从银行借贷会更多的受到银行的监控，借贷合同也更容易再次协商。然而，近期结构性信用市场的发展，尤其是CDOs的增长，给这些银行的传统职能带来了实质性变化。CDOs将贷款或其他资产组成资产池，重组现金流，向各种投资者出售不同级别的证券。这一金融创新增加了非银行投资者对公司贷款的需求，这种需求是旧有银行系统凭借贷款出售和贷款银团无法实现的。新的需求激励银行发行以向非银行投资者分发为目的的贷款。这种新的贷款激励对银行在信息挖掘、借款人监管和合同实施方面的角色有诸多影响。 本项研究检验了CDO市场增长及后续信用供给增长是否影响了公司借款的本质。我们集中在四个主要的问题上。第一，我们检验拥有CDO市场渠道的银行是否会将借款转向规模更大且风险更低的借款人。由于通过CDOs分发贷款所受到的监管较少，银行会将贷款发放给信息不对称和代理问题较少的公司。 第二，我们研究了银行的CDO资本对于贷款条款的影响。正向的供给冲击应当降低价格、提高交易金额。我们估计使用CDO较为活跃的银行贷款会拥有较低的利率和较大的贷款金额，并且这些贷款会拥有较长的期限和较为宽松的贷款条款。 第三，我们研究了从CDO使用活跃的银行借款对公司投融资决策的影响。我们预计由于可用信用增长，借款人会提高杠杆。同时，由于公司从公共发债向银行贷款转移，债务构成将发生变化。在资产方面，我们预计从CDO使用活跃银行借款的公司会增加在有形资产上的投资，并参与更多的并购交易。 第四，我们研究了银行减弱对结构性借贷的监管对于借款人风险承担的影响。更少的监管将更大程度上激励借款人冒险。我们通过检验两项通用的衡量违约风险的指标，即资产波动率和违约距离寻找冒险增加的证据。我们估计与其他借款人相比，CDO使用活跃银行的借款人在债务上违约率更高，业绩更差。

455910.label: Realisation of objectives
455910.value: We have fully achieved objective 1. The structured credit has been extended to borrowers with speculative grade ratings. We show that banks' lending to speculative grade borrowers have increased dramatically before the onset of the financial crisis of 2008/2009. Banks that are active in securitization extend credit to firms of larger size and of lower risk (measured before loan origination) than banks that are not active in securitization. Moreover, the securitization-active banks are more likely to lend to B-rated firms than BB-rated firms within the speculative grade spectrum. Related to banks' lending policies, we find that at origination, these banks impose less restrictive covenants on their loans. This would give the borrowers more flexibility in their financing and investment choices. Moreover, after these covenants are violated, these banks are more likely to grant a waiver without change any loan contract terms. The ex ante less restrictive covenants and the ex post less actions to violation collectively support the argument that banks extend easy credit when they can securitize loans. On objective 2, we focus on investment and not so much on financing. We find clear evidence that borrowers of securitization-active banks experience more substantial increase in their default risk (measured with distance-to-default and asset volatility) after loan origination. Furthermore, we distinguish this effect of securitization on banks' ex post monitoring effort from that on banks' ex ante screening incentives. Namely, the higher increase in risk might simply reflect the riskier nature of these firms as a result of lax screening standards of the securitization-active banks. Using instrumental variable approach and a setting where the borrower-lender matching is predetermined, we show a causal effect of banks' securitization activities on their borrowers' risk taking. Borrowers engage more in risk taking investment if they are able to obtain credit from securitization-active banks. We hence conclude that securitization leads banks to put less effort in ex post monitoring in corporate lending. This step we take to distinguish the ex post monitoring and ex ante screening goes even beyond the objective and has important contributions to the banking literature. Our paper documenting these findings are currently conditionally accepted at Review of Financial Studies (see Part C).

455910.label: Major findings and research outcome
455910.value: We examine how securitization markets affect the role of banks as monitors in corporate lending. We find that banks active in securitization impose less restrictive covenants on borrowers at origination. After origination, these borrowers increase their risk taking more substantially than borrowers of non-securitization-active banks. To distinguish the effect of securitization on the banks’ ex-post monitoring from its effect on ex-ante screening, we use several strategies. We first hold constant the borrower-lender matching by focusing on borrowers that have previously borrowed from the same banks before these banks became active in securitization. When obtaining the prior loans, these repeat borrowers were evaluated and screened under the lending standards that had not yet been influenced by banks’ securitization activities. By focusing on these borrowers, we essentially let the borrower-lender matching be determined before securitization takes place. We confirm our results in this setting. Second, we use borrowers’ geographic locations to instrument for borrower-lender matching. We construct region dummies to indicate borrowers' geographic locations. To the extent that firms tend to borrow from banks in close proximity, we expect (and verify) that borrowers located in securitization intensive regions are more likely to borrow from securitization-active lenders. On the other hand, we expect that the borrowers’ locations are independent of their covenant strictness and risk characteristics. By applying these instruments, we further establish the causal effect of securitization on banks’ monitoring incentives. Lastly, we investigate the banks’ actions following covenant violations. At the time of covenant violations, the banks’ screening function and their matching with borrowers are already decided. Therefore, analyzing the banks’ actions following covenant violations provides direct evidence on the banks’ monitoring incentives. We find that securitization-active lenders are more likely to grant a waiver without changing loan terms. Overall, our results suggest that banks exert less effort on ex post monitoring when they can securitize loans.

455910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
455910.value: The banks’ information roles are essential to firms with non-investment grade ratings. When their loans are widely securitized, the value of banks’ special role in lowering various frictions is reduced. However, it is not clear from our results whether loan securitization improve welfare. First, it is not clear whether the level of monitoring devoted by traditional banks is optimal. Too much monitoring can be costly to borrowers, leading firms to forgo good projects. Therefore, the loose monitoring we find is not necessarily value destroying. Second, loan securitization can create a new financing source that is beneficial to some borrowers. Recent studies show that securitization improves the borrowers’ access to credit and reduces credit spreads. Some studies along this line can be interesting. It is possible that this easy credit might come at the cost of less monitoring effort devoted by banks. Nevertheless, this less-monitored capital can be valuable to firms that have limited access to capital.

455910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
455910.value: We find that banks active in securitization impose less restrictive covenants on borrowers at origination. After origination, these borrowers increase their risk taking more substantially than borrowers of non-securitization-active banks. We use borrowers’ geographic locations to instrument for borrower-lender matching to distinguish the effect of securitization on the banks’ ex-post monitoring from its effect on ex-ante screening. We also investigate direct evidence of banks’ monitoring role by examining their actions following covenant violations, and find that securitization-active lenders are more likely to grant a waiver without changing loan terms. Our results suggest that banks exert less effort on monitoring when they can securitize loans. This contributes the large literature on banks' specialness and also contributes to our understanding of the new type of financial instruments--CLOs.

456010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
456010.value: 空間與場所營造：傳媒與資訊及通訊科技在被迫性移民生活中扮演的角色

456010.label: Project Objectives
456010.value: Theory Development: The literature in Communication Studies on forced migrants in general and uses of traditional media and ICTs by forced migrants in particular is in its developmental stages. I am particularly interested in theorizing the intersections between globalization, forced migration, mobility, space, and place and how people living in exile and who are not acknowledged yet as “legal” and part of a diaspora create transnational and transcultural spaces and notions of locality and home. Practical Policy Guidelines: The results can be used to encourage governments and law-making bodies to understand the role of ICTs and the media for the well-being of forced migrants and use them to help people already during the asylum process to develop their potential. The insights could foster the use of certain types of traditional media and ICTs during the asylum process to make the process more productive for forced migrants and society in general.

456010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
456010.value: Mobility is engrained in human history (Peters, 1999) and has yet taken on new meanings through global migration movements (Ong, 1999; Portes, Guarnizo, & Landolt, 1999). Forced migration as one dimension of a globally mobile society is one of the pressing social and political issues (UN, 2006). However, there is a paradox between the notion of global mobility and being frozen in social and physical space, an experience that asylum seekers often have after their transnational move. The study engages with this paradox and examines the role of (new) media to transcend arrested mobility, create notions of home, and engage in social relations across national borders. Lack of mobility was one major theme that ran through the interviews I have had in the summers of 2007 and 2008 with forced migrants in Germany. People talked to me about how they felt “arrested” and “isolated.” Although strict asylum laws often prohibit physical and social mobility, the literature on diaspora and media has shown that migrants can move virtually through (new) media and build a sense of home and transnational interaction spaces (De Leeuw & Rydin, 2007; Drzewiecka & Halualani, 2002). The spotlight in this study is on the social practices that accomplish this task. The study focuses on Germany as this is a continuation of a previous study on migrants and identity building and as Germany is ranked amongst the top asylum seeker receiving countries in Europe (UNHCR, 2009). Moreover, some pilot studies I conducted have provided preliminary results on how and why asylum seekers use (new) media, results which need more insight. The study will focus on three key issues. First, what is the role of media and ICT in the lives of forced migrants with regard to place and space-building, and which places and social spaces do forced migrants find meaningful? The second key issue is how factors like literacy, asylum law, and living conditions affect usage of media and ICTs and enable/prevent space and place-making. The third key issue is providing recommendations for how to improve the lives of asylum seekers through media and ICTs. The study develops theory related to forced migration and communication and policy related to bettering the lives of forced migrants. It is relevant to China as Germany is a destination for Chinese asylum seekers, which begs the question how the people build and maintain transnational relations and spaces between Germany and China. 遷移深植於人類的歷史中(Peters, 1999)，但在全球化移民進程中，遷移有了新的含義(Ong, 1999; Portes, Guarnizo, & Landolt, 1999)。作為一個全球化的流動型社會的維度之一，強迫遷移是一項緊迫的社會與政治議題(UN, 2006)。然而跨國尋求政治避難的人們在避難國常常受到社會空間與物理空間上的限制，這與全球化遷移的概念相互矛盾。這項研究聚焦這一矛盾，研究（新）媒體在突破被束縛的移動性，建構家鄉的新意義以及在跨國界社會關係中所參與扮演的角色。在我對德國的被迫性移民於2007年以及2008年夏天進行的訪問中，移動空間受限是一大主題。人們告訴我，他們感受到“被監禁”以及“被孤立”。雖然嚴厲的政治避難法律常常禁止移民者在物理空間與社會空間上的移動，但是關於移民群體以及媒體的研究顯示移民者可以通過（新）媒體進行虛擬移動，並製造某種意義上的家鄉以及跨國境的互動環境(De Leeuw & Rydin, 2007; Drzewiecka & Halualani,2002)。而達成這一目標的社會行為是此項研究的聚焦點。此項研究著重於研究德國，這是作為先前對移民和身份認知研究的延續，另一原因是德國是歐洲接收政治避難者最多的國家之一(UNHCR, 2009)。此外，我所做的一些前趨研究已經為政治避難者使用（新）媒體的方式和原因提供了初步的結論，這些結果需要被進一步的探究分析。這項研究著重於三個問題。第一，媒體和資訊及通訊科技在被迫性移民營造場所和空間的過程中扮演了什麼樣的角色，什麼樣的場所和社會空間是被迫性移民認為有意義的？第二項關鍵問題是研究文化程度，政治避難相關法律以及生活條件等因素如何影響媒體與資訊及通訊科技的使用，以及這些因素如何幫助或限制空間和場所的營造。第三個關鍵問題是提供通過媒體和資訊及通訊科技來改善政治避難者生活的建議。這項研究拓展了強迫遷移以及傳播學的理論，也拓展了改善被迫性移民生活的政策。這項研究與中國有關，德國是中國政治避難者的一個目的地，這項研究探究人們是如何營造與維持中德跨國的關係和空間。

456010.label: Realisation of objectives
456010.value: The project objectives have been achieved. I have theorized the relationship between place, space, and new information and communication technologies for forced migrants in Germany. I have illustrated through multiple single-authored publications (see publication section) how forced migrants, asylum seekers in particular, create cultural, social, and political belonging and local and transnational networks through new technologies. Related to new technologies, I have illustrated the role of social media and social networking services, websites, and voice-over IP services for creating meaningful localities for asylum seekers and maintaining transnational spatial relations. Despite being arrested in space, virtual practices and platforms enabled people to become virtually mobile. People engaged with virtual practices and platforms to maintain strong ties with family at home and elsewhere in the diaspora and create social, cultural and religious community in Germany. Especially young people used new technologies to create local friendship networks based on shared interests like sports or faith. They also used new technologies to prepare for life in Germany, e.g., by learning German, seeking information on legal and health services as well as education and potential future employment. In addition, new technologies played an important role in mobilizing other asylum seekers in Germany and across Europe for political action against restrictive asylum policies. Overall, new technologies and platforms enabled asylum seekers to resist immobilities created through national and transnational law, the media, and politics of the nation state through digital networking, which was facilitated by NGOs and supporters from civil society. In addition to illustrating the vital role of new technologies for the creation of place and spatial relationships transcending the local, I have also started theorizing important concepts like emotion and how those structure engagement with the digital. One example is shame and how it prevented some women from engaging with the digital, thereby not gaining access to important legal, health, and educational information. Moreover, I have illustrated methodological opportunities and concerns related to research with people with socioculturally and historically different backgrounds (Witteborn, Milburn, & Ho, 2013). I have also outlined a list with policy recommendations related to asylum seekers, space, place, and new technologies, which I am currently developing into a paper. I have not encountered any problems.

456010.label: Major findings and research outcome
456010.value: There are several findings. First, asylum seekers below the age of 45 used new technologies to create local and transnational networks while waiting for their claims to be recognized (see Handbook of Global Media Research, 2012). While the people used social networking sites (SNS) to connect with family back home, they used those sites to engage with or create local shared interest groups (e.g., sports, culture, faith). The people used SNS to find a sense of belonging, either on those sites or in physical places like churches, mosques, community centers, or other mostly public meeting places while waiting for their asylum claims to be processed (Witteborn, 2012). Waiting is a difficult process and increases psychological pressures and a sense of helplessness, uncertainty, and loneliness. Cultural, political, and spiritual networks can alleviate these pressures somewhat through a sense of community. New technologies can help the people become imperceptible as asylum seekers and position themselves as human beings with multiple ways of belonging (manuscript under review in Journal of Refugee Studies). During the time of the refugee protests in Germany, starting in 2012, asylum seekers have used new technologies to mobilize for political support against deportations, residency requirements, and the requirement to stay in assigned asylum seeker accommodations. Social media, social networking sites, and blogs play an important organizing and documenting role in this process, mobilizing for support for refugee issues on a communal, city, national, and transnational European scale. Moreover, the research has illustrated the importance of emotions, an overlooked concept in Communication Studies, and how culturally (e.g., shame) and politically (e.g., fear) meaningful emotions structure engagement with the digital. I have also illustrated how those emotions are gendered (Witteborn, 2014). In addition, I have discussed methodological issues in relation to how to do research with vulnerable groups like forced migrants (Witteborn, Milburn, & Ho, 2013). Finally, I have started theorizing digital practices in relation to border and how practices like social networking, Skyping, or blogging challenge national border practices. The findings strengthen arguments related to the autonomy of migration (Moulier Boutang, 1993) with its own logics and practices tied to information exchange and networking (ICA conference, Seattle, June 2014).

456010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
456010.value: One productive direction is a long-term project to see how new technologies and digital practice shape and change political engagement and protest of forced migrants. The current situation related to forced migration is volatile worldwide. We can see increasing attempts by governments to regulate migration and close their borders for asylum seekers like in the case of outsourcing asylum seekers arriving by boat in Australia to Papua New Guinea or in the case of strengthened border protection through agencies like FRONTEX in Europe. According to my research findings as well as extant research, people will continue seeking asylum, no matter how deep the ocean or how high the fence. Political protest is on the rise, from Australia to Europe and Israel, as asylum seekers find their own voices to mobilize through new technologies and pressure governments to fulfill their obligations related to the Geneva Refugee Convention. Therefore, research related to political protest and digital mobilization by forced migrants is important, especially as there is hardly any literature on the topic. I am preparing a GRF grant related to political mobilization of forced migrants and new technologies, including the role of political organizations in supporting or appropriating the goals of forced migrants for their own purposes.

456010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
456010.value: This project examined how forced migrants use new technologies to create local networks and maintain transnational ones by the example of asylum seekers in Germany. The topic is important as forced migration is a central phenomenon in the 21st century due to ongoing political upheaval and poverty. Loneliness, social isolation, and uncertainty are major challenges for forced migrants in Germany, amplified through long asylum processes and having to live in shared accommodations. This project illustrates how new technologies, especially social media and networks and voice-over IP services, are important for the people to create local social relations to reduce isolation and maintain transnational ones for social, cultural, spiritual, and political purposes. Digital practices enable forced migrants to position themselves beyond an asylum seekers status as family members, cultural community members, political actors, and people embedded in transnational networks. New technologies also help people to prepare for life in a new locale, e.g., through learning the language. The research also shows how emotions (e.g., shame and fear) structure engagement with digital practice. Overall, the project provides insights into how forced migrants create local and transnational networks and a sense of belonging. It illustrates the challenges involved and how new technologies enable the people to mobilize for goals as defined by themselves.

456610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
456610.value: The aim of this project is to conduct comparative research to determine if there is a relationship between the translocal rice-trading networks and state formation in the contemporary Philippines and Thailand. By conducting historical and ethnographic research in and between Manila and Bangkok and the major rice-producing regions, the project will: (1) determine how the translocal rice-trading networks operate in the two countries; and (2) identify the ways that the translocal rice-trading networks connect with the national capitals in the rice-producing regions. Since World War II, the states in Southeast Asia have witnessed decades of social upheavals and political conflicts which coincide with the interchanges of authoritarian and democratic regimes. For instance, in the 1960s and 1970s, waves of public protests and peasant insurgency preceded the imposition of martial law in the Philippines and Thailand. The 1980s saw the instalment of nationwide democratization, but the following decades have been marked by continued unrest and militarist intermissions. Given the availability of a substantial aggrieving peasantry and strategic importance as the state granaries, the rice-producing regions in, for example, the northeastern Philippines and northern Thailand, have been the hotbeds for armed movements and mass mobilization. Food and interior security has therefore been closely connected with state formation in contemporary Southeast Asia. How have the Philippine and Thai states struggled to pacify and include their rice-producing regions? How have they localized themselves in the rice-producing regions? What have been their major policies? How have the local population reacted to these policies? How have the states responded to the local reactions? This project hypothesizes that the translocal rice-trading networks have been performing a crucial role in the state formation processes by connecting the centralizing state and the rice-producing societies together as a whole (Migdal 2001). Using multiple methods to collect data, this project will: (1) compare the strategies that the Philippine and Thai states have used to govern the rice-producing regions; (2) track down and compare the rice production, trading, milling and distribution practices, routes and mechanisms that the rice-trading networks have used to connect the capitals with their rice-producing regions; (3) track down how the studied rice-trading networks have participated in the implementation of state policies in four domains; land reform, counterinsurgency, democratization and the local government. 本研究項目會使用比較研究方法去解答究竟菲律賓和泰國跨省府米糧貿易網絡與其國家形成過程有沒有關係。於馬尼垃和曼谷及其主要產米區進行歷史學和民族學的研究，本研究項目將會： (1)介定兩國跨省/府米糧貿易網絡的操作形態； (2)弄清兩國跨省/府米糧貿易網絡是如何連結國家首都和其主要產米區。 二次大戰以還，東南亞諸國見証了數世紀的社會動盪和政治衝突與不同的專制和民主政權交錯著。於上世紀六十和七十年代，繼一連串公民抗命和農民起義之後，菲律賓和泰國當局相繼實施軍法統治。縱然兩國於八十年代實施全盤民主化，接踵而來的卻是斷斷續續的社會不安和軍事政變。由於擁戴著龐大佃農人口和高度戰略安全價值，主要產米區如菲律賓東北部和泰國北部一直是武裝運動和大規模動員的溫床。於東南亞國家形成過程中，食糧和內政安全一直存在密切關係。菲律賓和泰國當局是如何平定產米區內的動亂？兩國是如何將國家主權地方化？有什麼主要政策措施？地方人民如何反應？當局如何再回應？為了回答這些問題，本研究項目大膽提出以下命提：跨省府米糧貿易網絡一直於菲律賓和泰國國家形成過程中扮演重要角色並將中央政權與地方社會有效連結甚至統合。 利用不同方法去搜集資料，本研究項目將會: (1)比較菲律賓和泰國當局管治其產米區的策略； (2)追蹤和比較連接兩國首都和產米區之間的米糧生產、貿易、練米和分銷的手段，路線和機制； (3) 追蹤和弄清有關跨省府米糧貿易網絡如何參與和協助實施四項政策：土地改革，平定內亂，民主化和建設地方政府。

456610.label: Realisation of objectives
456610.value: 1. To track down the rice production, trading, milling and distribution mechanisms which connect the Philippine and Thai rice-producing regions with the national capitals. To the full extent, this objective has been achieved by conducting field research visiting rice producers, traders, millers and distributors in both the Philippine and Thai provinces and national capitals. 2. To determine if the translocal rice-trading networks are involved in Philippine and Thai electoral politics. To a very large extent, this objective has been achieved by conducting field and documentary research. 3. To determine if the translocal rice-trading networks are involved in the implementation of the Philippine and Thai land reform. To a moderately large extent, this objective has been achieved by conducting field and documentary research. The Philippine part is fully achieved whereas the Thai part is partially achieved. It is mainly because due to leave restrictions, the PI was not able to stay long enough in the field-sites to conduct more thorough investigations but largely relying on ethnographic accounts provided by the local farmers and rice-traders. The PI therefore forged collaboration with local Thai researchers to over the problem. 4. To determine if the translocal rice-trading networks are involved in the implementation of counterinsurgency. To a moderately large extent, this objective has been achieved by conducting field and documentary research. The Philippine part is fully achieved whereas the Thai part is partially achieved. It is mainly because due to leave restrictions, the PI was not able to stay long enough in the field-sites to conduct more thorough investigations but largely relying on ethnographic accounts provided by the local farmers and rice-traders. The PI therefore forged collaboration with local Thai researchers to overcome the problem. 5. To determine if the translocal rice-trading networks are involved in the operation of the local governments. To the full extent, this objective has been achieved by conducting field and documentary research.

457110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457110.value: After the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949, the socialist government implemented the policy on the freedom of religious belief and carried out a number of social and political movements, all of them imposed tremendous impacts on the development of institutional Buddhism. This project investigates the history of Buddhism in socialist China, especially after the end of the Cultural Revolution in 1976 when China opened its door once again to the outside world. By highlighting the profound transformation of Buddhism from 1949 up to the present, the research demonstrates its ups and downs within the contexts of contemporary social and political developments. In an introduction, I will provide the historical background of Buddhism in the early 1950s when the government was formulating its policy on religion in general and Buddhism in particular, and investigate the impacts of social and political champaigns on institutional Buddhism. Having briefly examined Buddhist situation during the Cultural Revolution(1966-1976), I then focus on investigating the formation and development of humanistic Buddhism appeared in the early 1980s as monks and nuns who had left their temples before or during the Cultural Revolution gradually returned and reassumed their monastic identities, while young monks and nuns were ordained and temples were open to the public. In addition, the transforamtion of Tibetan Buddhism in Tibet and Theravada Buddhism in Yunnan will be examined in connection with Buddhist developments nationwide and within the contemporary social and political frameworks. This research explores the theories and practices of humanistic Buddhism which aims at benefiting living human beings and establishing a pure land on earth instead of going to the West Paradise (西方極樂世界) after death. I will explore the modern managements of temples and Buddhist organizations, new life of clergy, Buddhist education, social charities, political and economic activities. Detailed discussion will be undertaken to demonstrate the reactions of Buddhist leaders, particularly Ven. Juzan (巨贊1908-1987) and Mr. Zhao Puchu (趙樸初1907-2003) to the social and political changes, and their contributions to the transformation of Buddhism particularly after 1949 and 1980 respectively. Since the transformation of Buddhism in China is part of socialist construction and modernization program of the state, I will employ different methods, such as historical approach, sociological approach, case studies, and fieldworks in order to carry out thorough and comprehensive studies. 中華人民共和國於一九四九年成立以後，中國政府在全國推行宗教信仰自由政策的同時，亦發動了一系列社會主義改造運動，清除封建迷信，建立新國民形象。頻繁的社會和政治運動給中國佛教的發展造成巨大的影響。本研究將考察社會主義時期中國佛教發展歷史，特別是一九七六年文化大革命 (1966-1976) 結束以後和改革開放以來的佛教狀況。首先，我將系統論述五十年代中國佛教的歷史和特徵，分析中共政權在這個時期出臺的各項宗教政策、特別是針對佛教的政策，檢討宗教政策和社會政治運動給佛教帶來的沖擊。然後，我將介紹佛教在十年文化大革命時期的情況，分析極左政治給佛教帶來的毀滅性破壞。最後，我將重點探討上個世紀七十年代末開始出現的佛教復興運動，即人間佛教。在這個歷史時期，宗教信仰自由政策重新獲得倡導和落實，中國佛教百廢待舉，全國出現了恢復佛教寺院的熱潮。許多早先被迫還俗的僧人重新穿上袈裟、回到寺院；政府允許一些青年人出家為僧，部分寺院也陸續向社會大眾開放。我將以人間佛教理念為主線，以佛教寺院和組織團體的現代化管理、僧眾的宗教生活、佛教教育和慈善活動、以及佛教徒的政治和經濟參與等為重點，深入研究上個世紀七十年代末以來佛教與政治、社會、和經濟的互動情況，分析人間佛教的思想內涵和人間淨土的實踐。在這個方面，我將以巨贊法師 (1908-1987) 和趙樸初居士(1907-2003)的佛教思想和政治活動為個案，具體分析當代中國佛教社會主義轉型以及佛教徒在這種轉型中所扮演的角色和作用。佛教在當代中國的發展是中國社會主義建設和現代化的一部分，與社會和政治思潮以及經濟發展存在著千絲萬縷的關係，因此，我將採用多元研究進路，如歷史學、社會學、個案研究和田野調查等方法，綜合而全面地分析研究當代佛教思想和歷史。

457110.label: Realisation of objectives
457110.value: The project has achieved its primary objectives. It has gone in depth to examining the critical relations between the institutional Buddhism and the state. A special attention is paid to investigate how Buddhist clergy who had undergone political suppress and economic pressure for self-reform, either willingly or being forced, abandoned their monastic life style and readjusted their way of living in accordance with the currency of socialist transformation. To a large extent, the socialist transformation of Buddhism in modern Chinese history would be a perfect example for the theory of the secularization of religion. Nevertheless, my research has proved differently that the secularization in terms of the socialist transformation of Buddhism is perhaps superficial, because the religiosity of Chinese Buddhists has remained unchanged and manifested itself once again when government policy on religion changed in the 1980s. Such phenomena as well as the materials collected throughout the process of research have been extensively examined and discussed in the classes for both graduate and undergraduate students in the last two years.

457110.label: Major findings and research outcome
457110.value: Together with some other articles both in Chinese and English, a comprehensive monograph entitled Socialist Transformation of Buddhism in China is to be published by the Chinese University of Hong Kong Press. The monograph covers a variety of aspects of developments of Buddhism in the early period of the People’s Republic of China, examining in detail the socialist transformation of institutional Buddhism during various social and political movements. Just as one of peer reviewers for the publication of the monograph has put it “this research has filled the gap of scholarship in the study of Buddhism and shed more light in understanding interactions between religion and politics in Communist China.”

457110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
457110.value: Due to the limitation of budget, extensive interviews could not be carried out. I was only able to interview a few Buddhist veterans and record their own experiences of socialist transformation in the early period of the PRC. Oral history is very important for us to understand the development of Buddhism in modern and contemporary China, and hopefully, I will be able to extend and deeped my research to examine the change of institutional Buddhist in current China, and to make extensive interviews of such Buddhist veterans soon as most of them are quite old.

457110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
457110.value: This research project has undertaken extensive and comprehensive studies on the history of Buddhism in socialist China between 1949 to 1980. The examination and discussion focus on the interactions between institutional Buddhism and the state during several social and political movements, such as the Land Reform and Anti-rightists Movement in which Buddhist leaders such as Juzan enthusiastically urged Buddhists to follow the path of socialist transformation. The research has thus adequately demonstrated that the disappearance of Buddhism in public after the funding of the PRC in 1949 was the collective efforts of both Communists and Buddhists, particularly Buddhist leaders.

457210.label: Project Title(Chinese)
457210.value: 後改革期中國區域創新體系：珠江三角洲自主創新與區域轉型

457210.label: Project Objectives
457210.value: To examine distinctive roles and dynamic interactions among various actors, namely foreign and domestic high-tech firms, central and local states, and universities and research institutes in developing an evolving regional innovation system in China and particularly the PRD; To investigate the rise of indigenous technology firms from followers to major global players in their respective sectors and effects on changing the positions of China and particularly the PRD in the global economy; To understand the dynamic interactions between the regional production networks and regional innovation systems in reshaping the trajectories of technological catch-up and regional development in the PRD under the challenges of globalization.

To investigate the rise of indigenous technology firms from followers to major global players in their respective sectors and effects on changing the positions of China and particularly the PRD in the global economy;

457210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457210.value: After three decades of opening and reform, China, particularly the Pearl River Delta (PRD) has attempted to change its roles in the global economy from a low-tech manufacturer to a high value-added technology-intensive producer and quest for a balanced orientation towards export and domestic markets. Previous interpretation of the PRD as a provider of low cost labour for the “global shift” of export-oriented production is not longer adequate to understand the dramatic transition in the PRD, particularly the dynamic technological trajectories. Compared with substantial studies on the contribution of the transnational corporations (TNCs), especially Hong Kong and Taiwanese firms, little has been conducted on the rise of indigenous technology firms and their impacts on technological catch-up and regional transformation in the PRD. Notably, the 2008 global financial crisis has prompted timely theoretical inquiries and empirical debates on the export-oriented development which challenges conventional wisdom of technology innovation in the global era. Taking the PRD as a case, this study explores the emergence and transition of regional innovation systems (RIS) in post-reform China. Through comprehensive field investigations, in-depth interviews and firm surveys, this project examines the distinctive roles of diverse actors, viz. the central and local states, TNCs, indigenous technology firms, universities and research institutes and their interaction with the global forces in developing the salient regional innovation systems in the PRD. Based on intensive firm-level case studies in such high-tech sectors information and telecommunication (IT), biotechnology, optical electronics and new materials and energy, the project sheds light on how and to what extent the rise of indigenous firms from followers to the major global players in their respective sectors has brought about the transformation of the PRD from production to innovation and the balance between export and domestic markets. The empirical experience of the PRD exemplifies the dynamic interactions between the regional production networks dominated by TNCs and the regional innovation systems led by indigenous firms under the interplay between the global and local forces in reshaping technological catch-up and regional restructuring in the PRD. The study will advance the theoretical debates on globalization and enrich the empirical literature on regional innovation systems primarily dominated by the cases in the western developed countries. It demonstrates that policies and strategies for technological catch-up, indigenous innovation and regional transformation should be formulated in a holistic manner rather than (as hitherto) on a piecemeal basis in the changing era of globalization. 經過三十年快速的改革開放，中國特別是珠江三角洲正致力於改變其在全球經濟體系中的定位與角色，由低附加值的製造商提升為高附加值的技術密集型的生產者，同時追求出口與國內市場的平衡。過往的研究多將珠三角作為“全球轉移”低成本出口加工基地，顯然不能充分解釋正在發生巨變的珠三角。以珠三角為例，本研究試圖探究後改革時期中國區域創新體系的形成和轉變。通過翔實的田野調查，企業訪談和調查，研究將揭示在各個主要的動力，包括中央及至地方政府，外資企業，自主創新企業，大學和研究機構在建立區域創新體系中的角色和相互之間的互動關係。研究將特別關注並分析自主創新企業由追隨者成為相關行業的全球領跑者之轉變，及其對區域創新體系的影響。此研究冀望補充現有關於區域創新體系文獻偏於西方發達經濟的實證分析，從而豐富有關全球化趨勢下區域創新的理論分析和探討，並為相關決策機構提供政策性參考。

457210.label: Realisation of objectives
457210.value: Thanks for the sufficient financial supports, I with the collaboration of the Co-I, conducted intensive research activities and successfully realize the objectives as proposed during the period of undertaking of the Project in the past two and half years (Jan. 2011-June 2013). Firstly, intensive on-site field investigations have been conducted in the major cities in the PRD such as Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Dongguan, Foshan, Shunde, Huizhou, cities in Yangtze River Delta (e.g. Shanghai, Suzhou, Nanjing), Beijing-Tianjin metropolitan regions, as well as inland cities e.g. Chongqing, Chengdu, Wuhan, Zhengzhou, to examine distinctive roles and dynamic interactions among various actors, namely foreign and domestic high-tech firms, central and local states, and universities and research institutes in developing an evolving regional innovation system in China. The project has provided evidence of the uneven technological landscape in China with considerable differences in endowments, cultures, institutions, positions in state’s strategies and linkages with global economy. Secondly, case studies, particularly the state-designated strategic emerging industries (SEIs), e.g. LED, LCD-TFT industry, as well as labour-intensive industries, e.g. home electronic appliance, furniture and garment industries have been conducted to investigate the rise of indigenous firms from followers to major global players. Unlike previous studies on high-tech industry in China mainly focus on information and telecommunication sector, this study has extended to the promising strategic industries designated by governments, as well as traditional industries, with particular attention on their changing relations with global networks of production and innovation, and subsequent effects on the evolution of regional innovation systems in China and the PRD in particular. Thirdly, firm-level survey (in overall and specific industries, e.g. LED, LCD-TFT , home electronics industry) and in-depth interviews with foreign-invested firms from various sources of origins and domestic firms in different cities and regions, government officials (e.g. Bureau of Foreign Economy, Promotion Centre for Foreign Investment, Promotion Association of Foreign Trade, Bureau of Science and Technology, Statistics Bureau), business associations and experts/scholars at universities and research institutes, have been conducted to investigate the dynamic interactions between the regional production networks and innovation systems in reshaping the trajectories of technological catch-up and regional development in China. With around 100 firms interviewed in various sectors, cities and regions, the project examined how the trajectories of technological catch-up in China and particularly the PRD have been transformed in the changing business environment in the crisis and post-crisis recovery.

457210.label: Major findings and research outcome
457210.value: As of the reporting date (March 2014), the project has generated considerable outcomes including nine peer-reviewed international journals, including "Review of International Political Economy" (2014), "Cities" (2014), "Environment and Planning C" (2014), "Eurasian Geography and Economics" (2014), "European Planning Studies" (2013), "Habitat International" (2013), "Applied Geography" (2012), "Acta Geographica Sinica" (2011), and "Growth and Change" (resubmitted with minor revisions), five book chapters, and seven papers presented at international conferences. The major findings and outcomes could be summarized as follows. First, this project elucidates the emerging paradigm shift of technological innovation in China, since the mid 2000s, characterized by a policy change from expectation of technological spillover from transnational corporations (TNCs) to an emphasis on indigenous innovation and domestic firms. Drawing upon the institutional and evolution perspective on the RIS approach, the project examine how foreign-invested and domestic firms have adjusted their innovation strategies in changing institutional environment, particularly government policy change, through the cases of light-emitting diode (LED) and liquid crystal display (LCD) industries. It argues that government policy change has resulted in the evolution of regional innovation systems in which technological upgrading of foreign-invested and domestic firms have demonstrated distinctive trajectories. Second, the study advanced the literature on the roles of domestic firms and states in technological upgrading of latecomer cities and regions. Drawing upon the strategic coupling concept of the global production networks (GPNs) framework, the project sheds light on the collective roles of various state authorities ranging from the central to provincial and municipal governments in fostering technological innovation of domestic firms through explicit coupling with global lead firms. The experience in Shenzhen indicates that indigenous innovation focused on domestic firms may unnecessarily exclude the participation of TNCs. The empirical experience in Shunde in the western PRD provides a vivid case of technological upgrading of home appliance industry, through strategic coupling of local firms in the GPNs. Third, the study extends the focal notion of GPNs perspective, i.e. strategic coupling to "de-coupling" and "re-coupling" to illustrate the interaction among technological upgrading, market reorientation and spatial relocation of TNCs in the changing context of global-local dynamics, particularly the aftermath of the global financial crisis and economic downturn. The project has demonstrated the changing power relations among TNCs and concerned regions with the emergence of key supplier-led domestic market-oriented production and innovation in China. Please refer to Part C for details.

457210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
457210.value: A number of valuable and interesting issues have been identified and worthwhile for future research. This project sheds light on the domestic market and rising customers in China as emerging dynamics mediated by institutional transition and changing government policies. Numerous avenues are opened on future research agenda, such as 1) changing dynamics of technological upgrading of various firms in response to the global economic restructuring, 2) impacts of the rising domestic markets in host countries on the national/regional innovation systems, 3) market shifts of production and consumption and impacts on technological innovation of foreign-invested and domestic firms, 4) the rise of indigenous firms in various of sectors and their articulation into the global networks of production and innovation, and subsequent effects on urban and regional transformation. It is hoped that existing comparative study on regional innovation systems in China could be expanded to comprehensive exploration of the interaction among regional innovation systems, spatial relocation and market shifts in other developing countries in a comparative way. These potential issues warrant for further research in future, which could be well developed on the basis of this project with substantial outputs and solid experiences of research activities.

457210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
457210.value: This study examines the evolution of China’s regional innovation systems particularly the PRD region during the transition from a low-tech manufacturer to a high value-added technology-intensive producer. It sheds light on government policy changes from expectation of technological spillover from transnational corporations (TNCs) to an emphasis on indigenous innovation and domestic firms since the mid-2000s. It provides in-depth analysis on China and the PRD in particular. Based on intensive field investigation, case study and firm-level survey and interviews, this project examines the distinctive roles of diverse actors, including various levels of governments, TNCs, indigenous technology firms, universities and research institutes in the dynamic global-local interaction. The empirical experience in major cities of the PRD such as Shenzhen and Shunde, has witnessed the rise of indigenous firms in the global economy through explicit coupling with global lead firms, under the government’s supports of fostering technological upgrading. The research outputs provide valuable lessons for latecomer cities and regions in other developing countries. The study has fundamental policy implications for relevant government and business to work out viable strategies for technological upgrading and market capturing in urban and regional transformation in China.

457310.label: Project Title(Chinese)
457310.value: 國際化、制度改革與中國工資增長

457310.label: Project Objectives
457310.value: This research project will conduct the first systematic investigation of the trends, sources, and causes of rapid wage growth in urban China for the period from 1992 to 2008. The proposed theoretical and empirical analyses will assess how factors of globalization, economic reforms, supply of skill and technological change have influenced the evolution of wage and employment structures during China’s economic transition. Our access to the comprehensive national sample of Urban Household Surveys presents an unprecedented opportunity to investigate the profound changes in China’s labor market since the early 1990s. We will document major labor market trends, including wage differentials by education, gender earnings gap, the decline in female labor market participation, and state vs. nonstate wage differentials. The data will reveal some novel features of the labor market that are essential to future research. The proposed decomposition analysis will provide estimates on major sources of wage growth in China. In particular, it will assess the relative importance of various factors—such as the rise in base wage, the increase in returns to education and state-sector restructuring—in explaining rising wages in China. Based on aggregate production functions, we will formulate a two-sector labor market model that explores a simple, explicit mechanism for understanding the determination of base wage and wage premiums during globalization and economic transition. Our objective is to extend the standard model of wage inequality between skilled and unskilled workers along two dimensions, namely, analyzing the determination of base wage levels and state-sector wage premiums, both of which are important aspects of the Chinese labor market. Structural estimations of the model based on simulated methods of moments (SMM) will help assess the effects of FDI, export expansion, state-sector restructuring, supply of skill, capital deepening and skill-biased technological change on wage changes over time. These econometric analyses will for the first time provide a set of parameter estimates for China’s aggregate production functions with capital-skill complementarity. Our analysis will have important policy implications. Our proposed research can be applied to the evaluation of the impact of changing economic conditions on urban wage and employment structures. For instance, the framework can help assess the wage effects of a dramatic decline in exports resulting from the recent financial crisis, or the effects of depleting rural surplus labor, on urban wages. As such, this research has the potential to support the Chinese government in important decision-making processes.
