457310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457310.value: China’s recent emergence as the workshop of the world and as the largest receiver of foreign direct investment (FDI) has profoundly influenced global trade patterns and the competitive landscape. The impetus for these successes stems largely from China’s comparatively low wages for workers. However, wages in China have risen sharply with globalization: average real wages have more than doubled in the past decade according to aggregate government data. Since soaring wages have started to erode China’s global labor advantage, this phenomenon has drawn increasing attention from the public and policy makers. Somewhat surprisingly, however, a systematic investigation of the trends, sources, and causes of rising wages in China has yet to be attempted by social scientists. The paucity of research on China’s evolving wage and employment structures reflects, in part, the lack of high quality microeconomic data covering a long period of China’s institutional reforms and globalization. Hence, our recent access to the comprehensive yearly Urban Household Surveys collected by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) presents an unprecedented opportunity to investigate fundamental labor market issues in China. We plan to develop the project in three stages. First, we will use the national sample for 1992-2008 to document major trends in wage and employment structures, sorting the labor force by education, work experience, gender, ownership category, industry and region. It is anticipated that the data will reveal novel and striking features of China’s labor market. Second, we will conduct a decomposition analysis to identify major sources of wage growth in China. Third, we will develop an aggregate labor market model that explores a simple, explicit mechanism for understanding the joint determination of base wage as well as schooling and sectoral wage premiums. Our objective is to extend the standard analysis of wage inequality by incorporating into the framework the determination of wage levels and factors of globalization and economic reforms for a large developing economy. Structural estimations of the model will help assess the effects of FDI, export expansion, state-sector restructuring, supply of skill, capital deepening and skill-biased technological change on wage changes over time. As China continues its evolution into a global economic power, enhancing labor market competitiveness is now more important than ever. We believe that our research findings will add significantly to our understanding of major labor market processes in China, help anticipate future wage trends, and provide significant insights into scientific policy making. 本課題旨在研究國際化與制度改革背景下中國工資與就業結構的變遷。我們將採用中國國家統計局城市家庭調查資料，分三個階段展開研究。首先，我們將利用1992-2008年家庭調查資料描述在此時段工資與就業結構的變化趨勢。然後，我們將運用計量分解的方法剖析工資大幅上漲的來源。最後，我們將建立一個宏觀勞動力市場模型，進一步分析影響基本工資以及教育溢價的機制。研究目的在於擴展對工資不均衡的分析，確定在國際化與制度改革背景下決定工資水準的因素。

457310.label: Major findings and research outcome
457310.value: Using a national sample of Urban Household Surveys, we document several profound changes in China's wage structure during a period of rapid economic growth. Between 1992 and 2007, the average real wage increased by 202 percent, accompanied by a sharp rise in wage inequality. Decomposition analysis reveals 80 percent of this wage growth to be attributable to higher pay for basic labor, rising returns to human capital, and increases in the state-sector wage premium. Employing an aggregate production function framework, we account for the sources of wage growth and wage inequality in the face of globalization and economic transition. We find capital accumulation, skill-biased technological change, and export expansion to be the major forces behind the evolving wage structure in China. The most important research output of the grant is an economic article, entitled "Changes in China's Wage Structure." This paper was first published as an IZA working paper in April 2012, which has attracted hundreds of downloads by academics, policy makers and business analysts. Later, we submitted this article to the Journal of European Economic Association (JEEA), one of the top general-purpose journals for the economics profession. Recently, we have received strong support for this paper from the JEEA editorial team and five referees. It should have no difficulty of being accepted for publication after the revision in the near future. To highlight the significance of this paper, the referees have made the following comments: • “This is an important paper. There is a lot of general interest in understanding the structural transformation in China and this paper offers a unique and insightful perspective, including the best measurements to date of wage trends in China. It has the potential to become a major reference in macroeconomics, well beyond the literature focusing on China. Bottom line, the paper would be a great catch for JEEA.” • “After seeing hundreds of papers on returns to education/human capital and wage differentials/discrimination/inequality in China, I feel excited when reading this paper, which, for the first time to the best of my knowledge, aims to address some really fundamental issues about China’s labor market over the past two decades. … In short, my prediction is that this will be one of the most cited papers on China.”

457310.value: We plan to revise the paper based on comments and suggestions made by five referees and two editors. We believe this paper will be published in early next year in a prominent economics journal.

Decomposition analysis reveals 80 percent of this wage growth to be attributable to higher pay for basic labor, rising returns to human capital, and increases in the state-sector wage premium. We find capital accumulation, skill-biased technological change, and export expansion to be the major forces behind the evolving wage structure in China. This is the first systematic investigation of the trends, sources, and causes of rapid wage growth in urban China for the period from 1992 to 2007. The result of this research will be soon published in a leading journal in economics. It represents a significant contribution to the economic literature on evolving wage structures during a period of rapid economic growth.

457410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
457410.value: 监管者还是掠夺者：给券商分配佣金的机构投资者

457410.label: Co - Investigator(s)

457410.label: Project Objectives
457410.value: To demonstrate that the degree of favorableness or optimism in stock recommendations and earnings forecasts by analysts is positively associated with the commission fee pressure faced by analysts. Specifically, for stocks that mutual funds have taken large positions in, analysts from brokerages that obtain commission fees from the fund companies (affiliated analysts) issue more optimistic opinions compared with those from brokerages that receive no commissions fees (unaffiliated analysts). To show that, for stocks that the funds have taken large holdings of, affiliated analysts increasingly shift from downward recommendation revisions to silence and from silence to upward revisions as they face greater commission fee pressure. To demonstrate that the effect of trading commissions on analyst bias is also consistent with the market reaction to, and funds’ holding-change response to, stock recommendations. To identify a paradoxical role that institutional investors play in analyst research. Their preferences for accurate and unbiased research are likely to be different before and after the investment decision. In particular, once they have put the money in the individual stocks, they would rather analysts bias their research optimistically for these stocks to avoid any price drop.

457410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457410.value: Anecdotal evidence suggests that institutional investors pressure financial analysts through trading commissions to issue biased opinions in support of their stock positions. We use a unique dataset that identifies mutual fund companies’ allocation of commission fees to individual brokerages and provide direct evidence in this regard. In particular, we show that, for stocks that the mutual funds have taken large positions in, analysts are more optimistically biased in their stock recommendations and earnings forecasts when their brokerages receive commission fees from the fund management companies. The relationship is stronger when the commission fee pressure is greater. The market reacts less favorably to the “strong buy” recommendations of analysts facing greater commission fee pressure. The funds also respond negatively to such recommendations in making portfolio adjustments. 市场上有传闻表明机构投资者会通过它们的佣金分别来给财务分析师施加压力，从而使他们发表有利于机构投资者的投资意见。本项目利用一个独特的数据库来对这一传闻进行严格的学术检验。我们期待发现，对于那些机构投资者已经大量持股的股票，分析师会发表更偏向于乐观的股票推荐意见和盈利预测， 特别是当雇用这些分析师的证券公司从这些机构投资者出分得佣金的时候。佣金关系的程度越高，这些分析师的意见也就越有偏向性。市场似乎意识到这种偏向性，投资者对那些有发表有偏向性的意见的分析师所发表的“强买”意见的股价反应相对于别的分析师的“强买”意见要低一些。机构投资者对这类意见的投资反应也要相对弱一些。

457410.label: Major findings and research outcome
457410.value: Regulators and the investment community have been concerned that institutional investors pressure financial analysts through trading commission fees to issue optimistic opinions in support of their stock positions. We use a unique dataset that identifies mutual fund companies’ allocation of trading commission fees to individual brokerages and provide direct evidence on this issue. In particular, we show that for stocks in which the fund companies have taken large positions, analysts are more optimistic in their stock recommendations when their brokerages receive trading commission fees from these fund companies. The relationship is stronger when the commission fee pressure is greater. The market reacts less favorably to the ‘‘Strong Buy’’ recommendations of analysts facing greater commission fee pressure. The funds also respond negatively to such recommendations in making portfolio adjustments. These results point to a source of analyst bias that has been little explored in the literature.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
457410.value: Financial analysts depend on insitutional investors for trading fee revenue. As a result, they will bias their stock recommendation opinions to please these institutional investors. The results suggest that institutional investors, instead of playing a monitoring role on analysts for their reports' accuracy and reliability, press analysts to bias opinions so they can benefit.

457910.label: Project Title(Chinese)
457910.value: 慈善網絡：東華義莊與粵、港、北美間的聯繫

457910.label: Project Objectives
457910.value: With a focus on Hong Kong’s pivotal role in networking charity between north America and Guangdong, this project aims at providing us with a case study of the extraordinary and yet under-researched global networking phenomenon centering round TWCH's charitable service of repatriating coffins and bones from all over the world to China from the late 19th century to the 1950s; The project is to examine the changes in Chinese death culture and burial customs as informed by the institution of TWCH which seemed to have facilitated a combination of the customs of delayed burial in north China and secondary burial in the south; The project is to relate TWCH's history to the social and cultural history of Hong Kong and demonstrate how stories of the Home have borne witness to changes in the territory especially in relation to the colonial context as well as conditions in mainland China; The project is to study Hong Kong’s function in facilitating emigration from China and the return of overseas Chinese from abroad, living or dead; The project is to enrich the scholarship of the Chinese diaspora with substantial and detailed, both qualitatively and quantitatively, archival evidence from Hong Kong testifying to its pivotal position in the global Chinese world; The project is to supplement local documentary evidence of the historical international network of south China-Hong Kong-north America with field information collected from research trips to the home towns of the overseas Chinese in Guangdong and sites of Chinese communities in north America; The project is designed to herald a macro study of the global picture of the Chinese diasporic world to which Hong Kong has long been the pivot in one way or the other.

457910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457910.value: 東華義莊於1899年倡建於大口環現址，目的在延續並發展東華醫院始於十九世紀七十年代的的慈善事業。義莊是東華醫院及後來東華三院的重要部門，其慈善工作包括寄存棺木、骨殖以等候原籍歸葬，或在本地覓義山埋葬。東華醫院一向被視為殖民地早期香港華人社會的領袖和華人慈善團體的表率，但義莊所展示的東華醫院特色，仍有待深究。 年前本人為東華三院編集東華義莊文獻資料選輯時，有機會接觸東華三院文物館所藏的大量相關檔案，深覺東華義莊工作性質獨特，在香港史、中國史乃至世界史上的重要性，不容忽視。其研究價值一方面固在於義莊的慈善事業與香港及中國的社會史、文化史演變息息相關。義莊結合了華北停棺候葬和華南二次葬的習俗，我們由此切入，或可重新評價華南、華北的死亡和喪葬文化。另一方面，東華義莊在聯繫海內外慈善團體、每年自海外運送數以千計棺材及骨殖回鄉的工作上發揮了極其樞要的作用。義莊的宏觀研究，有助於了解華人僑居海外的全球性，以及香港在海外華僑與其故鄉的聯繫方面所起的作用。東華義莊可能是全球唯一肩負起如此大規模慈善事業的機構，直到上世紀五十年代中國因禁運而與外界隔絕，義莊的原籍歸葬服務才中止。以此為研究對象的學術論著，至今絕無僅有。 作為個案研究，本計劃聚焦於十九世紀至二十世紀五十年代香港在北美（特別是廣東人視為「金山」的美國和加拿大）與中國僑鄉（主要在廣東）間的慈善網絡中所起的關鍵作用。香港一向是全球華人社會的樞紐，期望這個以慈善網絡為主題的原創性研究，可為全球華僑華人世界的宏觀研究開創先河。

457910.label: Realisation of objectives
457910.value: My previous report was too modest while in fact I achieved around 60-70% of the objectives then already. Now objectives in the following seven areas have all been successfully realized: 1. By focusing on the TWCH’s role in connecting north America and Guangdong through Hong Kong, this project has provided us with a case study of the amazing global networking phenomenon centering round the charitable service of repatriating coffins/bones of the deceased Chinese from all over the world to China through Hong Kong from the late 19th century to the 1950s. The research outputs concerned include items Nos.1,3,4 in Part C:8; No.1 in Part C:9. 2. My studies of Chinese death culture and the homebound burial practice as informed by the TWCH archives and burial records in cemeteries and public archives in north America and south China have resulted in the following research outputs: Nos.2,3 in Part C:8; No.4 in Part C:9. 3. Through relating previous investigation into the TWCH’s history to studies of the socio-cultural history of Hong Kong, the following research findings demonstrate the historical changes of the territory in relation to the colonial context and conditions in mainland China: No.1 in Part C:8; Nos.1,3 in Part C:9. 4. Supplementing source materials collected in Hong Kong with archival and field information from emigrant communities in south China, the following research products address Hong Kong’s function in facilitating emigration from China and return of the overseas Chinese, living or dead: Nos.1,4 in Part C:8. 5. Hong Kong’s pivotal role in the global Chinese world is testified and the scholarship of the Chinese diaspora, enriched, as the following findings show: Nos.1,3,4 in Part C:8; Nos.1,3 in Part C:9. 6. After a series of in-depth field trips to hometowns of the overseas Chinese in Guangdong and sites of Chinese communities in the USA and Canada were conducted to substantiate local documentary evidence, the existence of the historical international network of south China-Hong Kong-north America was testified in the following works: Nos.1,3,4 in Part C:8; Nos.1,3 in Part C:9. 7. With a solid and legitimate case study, the project does exemplify a transnational approach to the global networking phenomenon of the Chinese diasporic world and Hong Kong’s pivotal position in it. To herald a macro study of this global Chinese world, initial research works on the charity network such as Nos.1,3 in Part C:8 and Nos.3,4 in Part C:9 have been produced.

457910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
457910.value: This project is a solid case study to herald a macro study of the global history of the Chinese world. The PI may be continuously invited to present research findings. For example, I have recently been invited to give a presentation on Hong Kong and the Chinese “modern tradition” of homebound burial at the International Conference on the History of Hong Kong to be held next year. More macroscopically, a book workshop organized by me will be held in mid 2015 to follow up the international Workshop on Philanthropy and the Chinese Diaspora, 1850-1949 held in Nov. 2014 in Melbourne. Publishable papers will be selected from the 2014 workshop to be revised for presentation and review at the 2015 workshop in preparation for the publication of the book chiefly edited by me with the title Philanthropy and the Chinese Diaspora on the Cantonese Pacific Rim covering a wider area beyond north America. In the long run, the book series on the list in Part C:8 as item No.4, which is designed and edited chiefly by me, will cover even the world. Indeed, the global Chinese world is the subject that sustains my research interest with high potential for further development.

457910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
457910.value: The Tung Wah Coffin Home in Hong Kong was built in 1899 as an important unit of the Tung Wah Hospital then in making connection between Chinese charitable institutions overseas and those in China for transport of thousands of coffins and exhumed bones of the deceased Chinese from their host countries all over the world to their native towns in south China every year until the 1950s when the embargo problem affected the communication between China and the world outside. This kind of charity work had great significance in the history of Hong Kong, China, and the world. Research in the field can shed light on Chinese death and burial culture as well. As a case study, this project focuses on the Home’s role in connecting north America, especially the USA and Canada, the first “gold mountain” for Cantonese, and hometowns for the overseas Chinese mostly from Guangdong during the time span from the late 19th century to the 1950s. This original study centering round the theme of charity networking can also herald a macro study on the global picture of the Chinese diasporic world to which Hong Kong has long been the pivot in one way or the other.

457910.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
457910.value: In terms of academic contribution, this project has produced research outputs that drew attention from the circles of scholars in the field of studies of the Chinese diaspora. As a result, I was invited by international institutions to present my works and even establish collaborative relationship. For example, the workshop initiated by me to be held in mid 2015 to prepare the publication of the book Philanthropy and the Chinese Diaspora on the Cantonese Pacific Rim, as mentioned in 6.2, may turn out to be a project in collaboration with the Asia-Pacific Centre for Social Investment and Philanthropy of Swinburne University of Technology in Melbourne. It is also through exchange with colleagues in the field from all over the world that I can line up authors for the book series mentioned in 6.1 and 6.2. Titled Gan she chongyang ying xinyu 敢涉重洋營新宇：海外華人新史系列, the series will be a long-term project aiming at exerting paradigmatic impact upon the studies of the global Chinese world. Moreover, impact on knowledge transfer has been obvious all along as I was invited to deliver public lectures on my findings all the time. For example, I had the most successful interaction with the audience when I served as one of the speakers of the History Department’s annual “Public Lecture on History and Business in China” on March 17 this year addressing the topic “度生濟世：從原籍大歸看香港與全球華人慈善網絡.” Outside Hong Kong, I delivered a talk on my research at the Simian Humanities Lecture Series, East China Normal University in May 2013. In March 2012 I spoke on my work in the project to faculty members at Bridgewater State University, Boston during my field trip in the US. Lately I have been invited to be an advisor for an exhibition to be held in Los Angeles on Hong Kong’s role in the Chinese diasporic world and the speaker to address at the pre- exhibition symposium. I may need to speak in San Francisco as well when the exhibition moves there. Having said the above, the PI of this project cannot help being frustrated and depressed at times as the “triple burdens” (heavy administrative duties, demanding research and teaching performance) deem that one needs more time to complete everything perfectly while the local aggressive “research culture” (not the international norm though) pressures us all to produce quick and instant results. I am moved by the comments on my last progress report that “It is admirable that the PI manages to sustain this project with heavy administrative duties, but surprising that there has not been some reduction in duties to allow more time for this grant.” But sometimes support is just too difficult to get. It is beyond imagination, for example, that qualified relief teacher (especially for some courses) can be so hard to find. Failing to recruit one (entailing the large amount of unspent balance of the grant), I have to work round the clock as Department Chair, as well as Division Head at times, while conducting research and teaching. I did not even have time to prepare documents for the reimbursement of expenses for the last several field trips. Some of these trips were made with my own long leaves because the “Research Leave” for “Time-off” for “Individual Research” was just not long enough to cover my many research trips required by this project. As the only RA qualified for this kind of work turned out to be overqualified for hiring, I had to work on my own most of the time. And I am still waiting for response to my comment on one of the university’s strategic and planning documents that “…the university should look into the problem that in quite a lot of cases where good administrators are also good teachers/researchers who may have to break their health in response to the university call (if they are responsible people). In a way the university would suffer too when this happens.”

458110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
458110.value: Press release on corporate scandals such as contaminated eggs and milk, poisonous toys, and corporate financial frauds in China in the recent years have drawn the world’s attention to corporate misdeeds and governance effectiveness in transition economies. It is interesting to note the role of media in these events. In China, the largest transition economy, it is not surprising to hear that media is the most influential actor in the legal and governance system. The widespread report of corporate misdeeds by the media has successfully created public pressure on firms to improve governance control because they noticed that the reputational penalty on corporate fraudulent behaviors could be very great. Over the past decade, media commercialization and increased media editorial discretion have increased media’s incentives to expand their traditional roles. China’s media have become increasingly critical in their news coverage, exposing alleged wrongdoing, and even criticizing officials for failure to address injustice. Media also has the ability to appeal to and create popular opinions, express public thoughts, and offer comments and criticisms on social issues. Viewed in this way, media serves a strong governance role by exerting reputational sanctions on fraudulent firms in transition economies. In this study, we will explore this novel but understudied form of governance in guarding against corporate financial fraud of publicly listed firms in the transition economy of China. Corporate financial fraud is a dominant form of corporate fraud that refers to intentional misrepresentation of amounts or disclosures in the financial statements. We challenge the conventional wisdom that transition economies are lacking an efficient corporate governance system as those that are found in the developed economies. We propose that informal, reputational sanctions serve as an effective governance mechanism that complements the formal governance system in the current state of transition economies. Drawing from social cognitive theories and organizational theories on firm reputation and legitimacy, this study proposes to examine the influence of both administrative penalty and reputational penalty on firms’ likelihood to initiate governance restructuring after committing corporate financial fraud. We argue that the positive relationship between administrative penalty and firm’s likelihood to initiate governance restructuring is moderated by political power of the firm. However, such moderating relationships would be attenuated by media coverage and framing. We use China as the empirical setting and the study takes the time frame from 2000 to 2007. 本研究挑戰傳統學說認為經濟轉型中的企業缺乏一個有效的公司治理制度。在這研究中, 我們提出非正式的聲譽制裁可以在轉型經濟體中作為一種有效的治理機制，以補充正式的治理制度。借鑒社會認知理論和組織理論，我們研究行政處罰和聲譽處罰對違規公司展開治理改制的影響。我們認為，違規公司的政治權力將減弱行政處罰與企業治理結構調整的正面關係。然而，媒體的報導和框架將緩和這種關係。此研究利用中國上市企業的財務違規作為分析。其實, 研究公司管治的學者一直在辯論經濟轉型中的政府是否要採用與全球標準相同的公司治理系統，或是應該制定一套適合自己國家體制的獨特公司治理系統。本研究對此將提供一個答案，就是確定了媒體在轉型經濟體中作為一種聲譽制裁的治理作用。因此, 本研究將擴大我們對非正式治理機制的理解及為轉型經濟的政策制訂者和企業提供了重要的涵義和啟示。

458110.label: Realisation of objectives
458110.value: In all, the objectives listed in the research grant proposal are successfully achieved by the following: First, we developed a theoretical framework of whether and how reputational sanctions are at work in the transition economy of China where conventional internal corporate governance mechanisms are under-developed or their effects are still hindered by the insufficient institutional system. The framework has been presented at the 2012 Strategic Management Annual International Conference, in which we identify three types of reputational governance mechanisms – relational governance, administrative governance, and foreign governance. We contend that these governance mechanisms are complementary to the prevailing institutional framework of transition economies, thus representing useful deterrents of corporate financial fraud during institutional transition. Extending the framework, we conducted several empirical studies, each of which focuses on an alternative governance mechanism focusing on reputational sanctions. We examined the role of foreign governance mechanisms by disentangling their deterrence and detecting effects on corporate financial fraud. The paper is under review at Strategic Management Journal (SMJ). In another paper also under review at SMJ, we identified a unique governance mechanism in the context of China, board secretary (to signal a firm having governance professionals) by examining how role conflicts faced by board secretary precipitate its turnover. In regard to administrative governance and reputational sanction, we examined whether fraud punishment announcements by the regulatory authority can generate deterrence effect to all actors in the stock exchange. In a recently accepted paper at Organization Science, we developed a new perspective on the deterrence effects of vicarious punishments premised on social learning theory. The study sheds lights on the corporate fraud literature by illuminating the inhibitive learning process from vicarious punishments and enriches our understanding of the role of reputational sanctions in transition economies. This, together with a dissertation that studies the process of reputational loss after media reporting of corporate financial fraud incidents from a sentiment perspective, has fulfilled the second and third objectives by illustrating the role of reputational governance played by the media in transition economies where information asymmetry is severe and firm’s reputational stakes are of particular importance in governing firm behaviors. Finally, this research grant also facilitates the development of a rich and unique data set that consists of an enormous amount of textual data of corporate fraudulent news release, content analyzed data, and various governance mechanisms that are salient in the context of China.

458110.label: Major findings and research outcome
458110.value: The research projects have produced four journal papers with one of them being accepted at Organization Science (a prestigious top-tiered management journal) and the other three are under review and to be submitted to top-tiered management journals (AMJ and SMJ). There are also 7 paper presentations at major international management conferences. In the Organization Science paper, we posit that firms vicariously learn from their peers for punishments by picking up modeling, environmental, and social cues in the inhibitive learning process, thus being deterred from committing future fraudulences. Using a matched sample of 604 observations of Chinese listed firms between 2002 and 2008, our findings show that an observing firm is deterred from committing fraud if the peers in its industry are caught and punished. We further find that such deterrence effects are subject to how the observing firm evaluates the possibility of being caught and how likely it will be punished the same way if it violates similar prohibitions. The study contributes to the research stream of corporate financial fraud by examining the deterrence effects of vicarious punishments, an aspect that has been largely ignored in previous studies, and by advocating deterrence as an important, but often ignored, type of learning. Most importantly, we showed the salient roles of administrative, relational, and reputational governance in transition economies. A typical consequence of corporate financial fraud is the reputational penalty levied on the fraud firm. In a paper under review at AMJ, we investigate why different fraud firms receive different levels of reputational penalties given the same level of fraud severity. Using a sample of 468 fraud cases of the Chinese listed firms during 2001 and 2008, we find that public stakeholders have sentiment rigidity toward those fraud firms with higher reputation. However, sentiment deflection occurs when the visibility of the fraud firm increases. This study highlights the impact of media governance and views firm reputation as stakeholders’ sentiments. Other research findings include the effectiveness of foreign ownership, foreign partnership, and the use of foreign auditor in combating corporate financial fraud in China, as well as the unique governance role and effectiveness of board secretaries in transition economies. Overall, our findings indicate the effectiveness of non-legal governance mechanisms in transition economies that can be a cost-effective way to thwart corporate fraud as they are complementary to the existing political and social institutions in the context.

458110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
458110.value: 1. Our project has clearly showed that reputational governance is context-specific and institutionally coherent. The field of corporate governance has been dominated by the examination of the Anglo-Saxon governance systems, while our studies demonstrated that context-specific reputational governance mechanisms are in place and co-evolve with the historical and institutional development of a country. Therefore, future research may explore more context-specific governance and trace the development of corporate governance system in a more path-dependent way. 2. The project also paves a way to examine corporate governance and fraudulent behaviors in a behavioral and socio-psychological way. For instance, we have adopted social learning theory and theories from sociology and criminology in developing our theoretical frameworks. Future research can integrate inter-disciplinary literatures to study corporate governance and fraudulent behaviors. 3. Our project also shifts the perspective of corporate fraud research from focusing on the fraud firm to the interaction between the fraud firm and the observing firm. We highlight that fraud punishment has a more subtle and fundamental function of sanctions that is socio-pedagogical. This may direct future research to enlarge the scope of actors in corporate governance research.

458110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
458110.value: Corporate financial frauds in China in the recent years have drawn the world’s attention to corporate governance effectiveness in transition economies. The widespread report of corporate misdeeds by the media has successfully created public pressure on firms to improve governance control because they noticed that the reputational penalty on corporate fraudulent behaviors could be very great. Thus, reputational sanctions are important in governing fraudulent firms in transition economies. This research project has investigated this novel but understudied form of governance. Using the context of corporate financial fraud of publicly listed firms in China, we proposed and demonstrated that firm reputation can be viewed as embodying stakeholders’ sentiments and reputational sanctions thus would be useful in governing firms. Using a comprehensive data of media reporting of corporate financial fraud incidents of Chinese listed firms from 2002 to 2010, our findings show that reputational sanctions can have both general and specific deterrence effects on the observing firms, and different fraud firms received different levels of reputational penalty due to different political and social mechanisms. Such findings are significant as they enrich our understandings of reputational governance process and outcomes, showing how non-legal governance is at work in transition economies.

458610.label: Project Objectives
458610.value: To construct a large multi-cohort panel data set of students’ academic records with retention value. To clarify the negative bias in the estimates of the peer coefficient from typical regressions that simultaneously control for individual- and peer-level lagged test score variables due to the transitory-common-shock problem and to propose an IV strategy to correct this bias. To empirically implement the proposed IV strategy to the data and to provide credible new evidence on the existence and magnitude of the educational peer effects in the linear-in-means model. To explore alternative nonlinear/heterogeneous peer effects specifications that allow peer influences to operate through other measures of the distribution of lagged peer test scores than the mean or through the interaction between the distribution of lagged peer test scores and a student’s initial achievement. To empirically test the existence of single-crossing property in peer influences: i.e., whether an increase in the average peer ability affects high-achieving students more than low-achieving students.

458610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
458610.value: This project will examine the existence and structure of peer effects on student achievement in middle school using a large multi-cohort panel data set of students’ academic records from Wuhan, China. With multiple cohorts of observations from every school, we will base our identification on the plausibly exogenous variation in peer composition across adjacent cohorts within the same schools, thereby controlling for omitted variables due to unobserved school characteristics and student sorting across schools. The empirical educational peer effects literature has often resorted to estimating peer effects specifications that simultaneously control for both the individual- and peer-level lagged test score variables. In this project, we will clarify an econometric problem in estimating such peer effects specifications arising from the positive correlation between the measurement errors in the individual- and peer-level lagged test score variables. The source of this positive correlation in the measurement errors is the continuing presence in a student’s current peer group of her former peers, whose lagged test scores are subject to transitory common shocks just like her own lagged test score. In this project, we will show that the transitory common shocks on the individual- and peer-level lagged test score variables lead to a negative bias in the estimate of the peer coefficient, which we refer to as the transitory-common-shock bias. An important methodological contribution of this project is to propose an empirical strategy to correct this transitory-common-shock bias by using the lagged test scores of new peers as an instrument for the lagged test scores of all peers. The longitudinal structure of the data set for this project will enable us to distinguish a student’s new peers from her former peers and, therefore, to implement our IV strategy to correct the transitory-common-shock bias in our data. 通过使用武汉市的一个大型的关于学生成绩的面板数据库，本项目将研究影响学生成绩的同群效应的存在及其结构。我们将通过同一所学校内不同入学年级之间的群体组成的变化来识别出外生的群体组成的变化，从而能够控制基于观测不到的学校特征和学生在不同学校间的选择而造成的缺失变量的影响。关于同群效应的实证研究在估算同群效应时往往同时控制学生本人上一期的学习成绩和她的同学上一期的成绩。在这个项目中，我们阐明上述常用的实证方法非常可能导致对同群效应估算的负的误差。这一估算误差的产生是由于学生本人上一期的学习成绩和她的同学上一期的成绩都包括测量误差，而这两个测量误差是正相关的。造成这两个测量误差之间的正相关性的原因是一个学生现在的同学里面往往包括了一部分原来的同学，而这些原来同学上一期的成绩和她本人上一期的成绩受到了短暂的共同因素的影响。在这个项目中，我们会将由此产生的同群效应的估算误差称为“短暂共同因素误差”。这个项目在方法论上的一个重要贡献就是提出了一个新的实证方法来纠正这一“短暂共同因素误差”：使用新同学上一期的成绩作为所用同学上一期成绩的工具变量。面板数据库可以使得我们区分一个学生现在的新同学和旧同学，从而能够应用我们提出的工具变量的方法来纠正“短暂共同因素误差”。

458610.label: Realisation of objectives
458610.value: Objective 1 I collected and constructed a panel data set of about 7,500 students who completed middle school in a school district in Wuhan between 2005 and 2007. The panel data set contains each student’s middle school of graduation, and test scores in the citywide uniform Middle School Exit Exam (MSEE) as well as elementary school of graduation, test scores in a district-wide uniform exam taken right before starting middle school. Specifically, the availability of information on elementary school of graduation allows distinguishing between new peers and old peers in middle school. Objective 2 Using a simple value-added model, I showed that testing noise between lagged individual and peer achievements is likely to be positively correlated because of the continuing presence of former peers in one’s current peer group, leading to a negative reversion bias in the estimates of peer effects. I proposed to correct this reversion bias using the lagged achievement of new peers only to instrument for that of all peers. I also conducted a Monte Carlo analysis to illustrate the mean-reversion problem and the working of the IV strategy. Objectives 3-5 I conducted an empirical analysis of peer effects using the panel data set collected. I started with the simplest linear-in-means peer effects model. The conventional estimates of the peer coefficient were negative and significant, showing evidence supporting the existence of the reversion bias. After applying the IV strategy to address the mean-reversion problem, the peer coefficient became positive but statistically insignificant after clustering. I also explored a heterogeneous peer effects model by interacting a student’s lagged test score with the average lagged test score of his/her peers. The results showed some support to the single-crossing hypothesis that an increase in the average lagged test score benefited high-achieving students more relative to low-achieving students. The imprecision in the IV estimates of peer effects using the Wuhan data set is caused by the small number (15) of schools included in the sample, which results in large standard error after clustering at the school-cohort level. To overcome this sample size limitation, I applied for and obtained access to the National Pupil Database (NPD) in the UK containing panel information of over 2 million students who completed Key Stage 3 between 2005 and 2008. I am currently working on conducting the same analysis using the UK data set, which should solve the small-sample problem in the Wuhan data set.

458610.label: Major findings and research outcome
458610.value: Peer Effects on Student Achievement: An Instrumental Variable Approach Using School Transition Data, Working Paper (8.2 and 9.1-9.5 in Part C) In this paper, I show that testing noise between lagged individual and peer achievements is likely to be positively correlated because of the continuing presence of a student's former peers in her current peer group, leading to a negative reversion bias in the estimates of peer effects in value-added models with lagged peer achievement. I propose to correct this reversion bias using the lagged achievement of new peers only to instrument for that of all peers. To illustrate these points, I conduct a Monte Carlo study and also present an analysis of peer effects in Chinese middle schools. The Mirage of Elite Schools: Evidence from Lottery-based School Admissions in China, under review at American Economic Journal: Applied Economics (8.1 and 9.6-9.9 in Part C). In this paper we use school admission lotteries to estimate the effect of elite school attendance on student achievement in China. To address an imperfect matching problem arising from the lack of a common unique identifier in combining lottery records with Middle School Exit Exam (MSEE) records, we develop a data combination procedure and extend the existing local average treatment effect framework to contexts with imperfect matching following data combination. Despite the large observed superiority of elite schools in student achievement, we find little evidence that elite school attendance improves students' MSEE scores or secondary school admission outcomes. *The elite school paper also uses the same data set from Wuhan.

458610.value: I applied for and obtained access to the National Pupil Database (NPD) in the UK, which contains panel information of over 2 million students who completed Key Stage 3 between 2005 and 2008. I had conducted the same empirical analysis using the UK data set, which overcomes the imprecision in the estimate of the Wuhan data set and yields significant IV estimate of peer coefficient. A new working paper entitled “Beyond Attenuation: The Role of Testing Noise in the Value-added Estimates of Achievement Peer Effects” is currently under preparation.

458610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
458610.value: The peer effects paper contributes to the existing peer effects literature by extending the investigation of the role of measurement error to the commonly used value-added estimation using lagged peer achievements. It is the first to illustrate the existence of a negative reversion bias caused by common testing noise and shows that the reversion bias imposes a serious challenge to the empirical estimate of achievement peer effects than the commonly considered attenuation bias. It also proposes an IV strategy that can correct for the reversion bias. The elite school paper presents new quasi-experimental evidence on whether students benefit from attending "better" schools by exploiting lottery-induced variation in access to elite schools in China. It also contributes to the program evaluation methodology literature by extending the benchmark local average treatment effect (LATE) framework to treatment effect analysis in contexts with imperfect matching, encountered when combining an assignment data set and a treatment/outcome data set in the lack of a common unique identifier. As imperfect matching is commonly confronted in randomized evaluations involving the combination of information from different data sets, the extended LATE framework is applicable to a variety of contexts in which similar observational problems arise following data combination.

458910.label: Project Objectives
458910.value: To use the large-scale rural-urban migration in China as an important unique setting to test the impacts of parental absence on children’s educational and health outcomes. To design a practical intervention program that can assist the “left-behind” children while their parents are away. To implement the program as a randomized experiment to test the effects of the program. To better understand the impacts of family environment on children’s education and health and the impacts of the related policy interventions through careful empirical analyses using an experimental approach, which will contribute to the economics and policy literatures. 458910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
458910.value: This project will investigate two important questions in economics. First, what is the impact of parental absence on children’s educational and health outcomes? Second, how effective will be a remedial educational tutoring program in improving educational and health outcomes for elementary school children, especially for those with parental absence? In many developing countries, parental absence due to interregional and international migration is widely observed in poor rural areas. Parental absence is particularly acute for China due to the large scale of rural to urban migrant workers (estimated to be about 140 million in recent years) and the unique household registration (Hukou) system that prohibits rural migrant workers from acquiring formal city residency and hence limits the access to public education in cities for their children. Clearly, the answers to these questions are of fundamental importance to policy makers as well as to academic researchers who aim to further open the “black box” of the educational and health production processes. However, due to data constraints, there is little systematic research on these issues. The large-scale parental absence in China also presents researchers an important and urgent agenda to observe what happens if children grow up without their parents constantly coresiding. Using data from the Chinese Health and Nutrition Survey (CHNS) and Chinese Population Census, we will first study how parental absence affects children’s educational and health outcomes. We will also conduct a new survey of school children and their family members in a particular county in China to obtain more detailed information on children’s school performance and family environment. This survey will enable us to make a more-detailed examination of the potential effects of parental absence on children’s academic and other performance. Furthermore, we will work with a charitable organization in that county to design and implement a “tutoring scheme” to provide academic and counseling assistance to those “left-behind” children as well as regular children. We will assess the effects of this scheme with a randomized experimental approach. The results of this exercise will not only have significant academic value in adding to our understanding of an important issue, but also provide useful policy recommendations on how to better assist these “left-behind” children who are at risk of suffering life-long disadvantages due to parental absence. 本研究將分析教育經濟學中的兩個重要問題。第一，与父亲母亲分离會對学童的教育和健康狀況產生什麼影響？第二，補救性教學援助計畫對於提高小學生（特別是那些留守儿童）的教育和健康狀況能起到多大作用？在許多發展中國家的農村地區，跨區域人口流動使得小孩與父母分離成為一種普遍現象。在中國，勞動力從農村流向城市的規模逐年增長（據估計，近年來流動人口規模約為1.4億），然而在現有的戶籍制度下這些流動人口的孩子並沒有在城市上學的權利，這導致留守儿童現象在中國尤其嚴重。不論對於政策制定者還是對於研究者而言，這些問題都是極其重要的。然而，由於資料限制，至今為止仍鮮有研究對這些問題進行了系統分析。首先，我們將利用中國健康和營養調查資料（CHNS）和中國人口普查資料，研究留守儿童的教育和健康狀況。其次，為了獲得更詳細的有關学童學習和家庭環境的資訊，我們也將在一個代表性縣市實施一項新的資料調查。利用這個調查獲得的資料，我們可以更細緻地檢驗与父亲母亲分离對学童學業以及其他績效的影響。進一步地，我們將與當地的慈善機構合作，設計並實施一項“教學援助計畫”，分別為那些留守儿童和其他学童提供學習方面的幫助。我們將運用隨機試驗方法評估這個計畫的效應。這項研究獲得的結果不僅有重要的學術價值，而且也可向政府部門提供如何採取措施更好地幫助那些留守儿童的政策建議。

458910.label: Realisation of objectives
458910.value: Objective 1 We used a stratified random sampling method to select a random sample of 23 primary schools in the study county (Longhui County of Hunan Province) and collected both administrative and survey information on all third to fifth graders enrolled in April 2011. We then linked the retrospective information on parental migration history from the household survey to the longitudinal test scores from school’s administrative records, and constructed for up to five, seven, and nine school terms for the third, fourth, and fifth graders, respectively. Finally, we applied dynamic panel methods to evaluate the effects of parental absence on children’s cognitive achievements while controlling for both unobserved individual heterogeneity and endogeneity in parental absence. Objective 2 We designed an after-school tutoring program in which we recruited high-achieving students in grades 4 and 5 to offer one-to-one peer tutoring to low-achieving students in grades 2 and 3. We formed over 700 such tutor-tutee pairs in 36 primary schools in the study county. Objective 3 We implemented the field experiment for two semesters with four 45-minute sessions per week. We also administered two rounds of cognitive tests, a baseline before the experimental intervention and a follow-up at the end of the experimental intervention. Objective 4 In addition to evaluating the overall effect of the tutoring intervention, we also examined the heterogeneity in the treatment effect on tutees by their parental absence status. We found that the tutoring intervention generated much larger test score gains for tutees with both parents absence as compared with those having at least one parent at home, suggesting that family background plays an important role in affecting the effectiveness of such a tutoring program. Our results provide experimental evidence that a targeted remedying educational intervention focusing to students with disadvantaged family background is likely to be more effective than an untargeted universal intervention because of the extent of family substation is more limited for children with poor background. Objective 5 (100%) Given the huge scale of parental absence, our finding of significant adverse effect of parental absence on the cognitive achievements of children left-behind calls for urgent need of policy interventions eliminating the restrictions causing family separation or remedying educational interventions ameliorating negative learning effects of parental absence. Our experimental evidence suggests one cost-effective remedying education in the form of cross-age after-school tutoring targeting specifically to children left-behind by their migrating parents.

458910.label: Major findings and research outcome
458910.value: “Does Parental Absence Reduce Cognitive Achievements? Evidence from Rural China,” Journal of Development Economics, pp. 181-195. Many children worldwide are left-behind by parents migrating for work — over 61 million in rural China alone, almost half of whom are left-behind by both parents. While previous literature considers impacts of one parent absent on educational inputs (e.g., study time, enrollment, schooling attainment), this study directly investigates impacts on children's learning (test scores) and distinguishes impacts of absence of one versus both parents. Dynamic panel methods that control for both unobserved individual heterogeneity and endogeneity in parental absence are used with data collected from rural China. The estimates indicate significant negative impacts of being left-behind by both parents on children's cognitive development, reducing their contemporary achievements by 5.4 percentile points for math and 5.1 percentile points for Chinese. Cross-sectional evidence indicates that only absence of both parents is associated with substantially lower family inputs in after-school tutoring. “Family Background, After-school Tutoring and Student Achievement: Theory and Experimental Evidence from Rural China,” Working Paper. In this paper we develop a simple model in which the effectiveness of a remedying education program on academically lagging behind children hinges critically on children’s family background. Specifically, an outside tutoring program is more effective for children with a disadvantaged family background when the substitution between home-based tutoring and outside tutoring is strong. To test the predictions of the model, we conduct a randomized within-school, cross-age tutoring program in a poor rural county in China, with a high prevalence of “left-behind” children with both parents migrating to work. In this experiment, we recruit high-achieving 4th and 5th grade students to offer after-school tutoring help to low-achieving 2nd and 3rd grade students, and form over 700 such tutor-tutee pairs. Our results show that such a program helps to improve tutees’ math scores but not Chinese scores, and generates no adverse effect on tutors’ academic performance. Moreover, the program generates much larger test score gains for tutees with both parents absent, which account for about 40% of the our tutee sample, as compared with those having at least one parent at home. We also find a substantial reduction in home-based tutoring for tutees with at least one parent at home, but little reduction for tutees with both parents absent, suggesting that family background plays an important role in affecting the effectiveness of such a program through input substitution effect.

458910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
458910.value: Based on the foundations laid out in this GRF project, the PI is planning to launch a longitudinal study of migration and children in China in collaboration with some Mainland partner. This longitudinal study is designed to share some similar features as the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY) in the US, but will pay special attention to those from migrants’ families.

458910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
458910.value: The paper “Does parental absence reduce…” expands the scope of the existing literature in two important ways. First, it distinguishes between the absence of one parent and that of both parents and estimate the effects of both these conditions separately. Second, it examines the effects of parental absence on actual learning outcomes, which is an important addition to previous research focusing almost exclusively on the effects on learning inputs. The findings suggest that the absence of both parents, a common phenomenon in rural China, is a much more serious problem than the usually considered cases elsewhere of the absence of only one parent, and deserves greater policy attention. The paper “Family background, after-school tutoring…” conducts both a theoretical and empirical investigation into the effectiveness of a remedying educational program in the form of cross-age tutoring on academically lagging behind children as well as its interactive effect with children’s family background. As far as we know, it is the first randomized experimental study on cross-age tutoring in China and also the first study examining the interactive effect between a remedying educational intervention and family background.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459010.value: Past research has shown that a physical experience (e.g., warm) can influence metaphorically linked psychological judgment (e.g., friendly). However, the underlying mechanisms have not been formally tested. Our project examines the role of semantic activations underlying such influences, focusing on the effects of a ubiquitous physical experience—“carrying weight”—on consumers’ judgment of importance. We have conducted a number of experiments which provide converging evidence that semantic activation is the primary underlying process for the effect. Specifically, physically carrying a load is neither a necessary nor a sufficient condition for processing the concept of importance. The effect is fully mediated by semantic activation of related weight concepts. Moreover, processing the concept of importance does not necessarily influence the physical experience of carrying weight. An affective state such as mental stress (psychological load), however, does have a reciprocal effect on the physical experience of carrying weight, indicating that there might be different pathways between a physical experience and its metaphorically linked concepts.

459210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459210.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research into the impact of coastal water-quality on Hong Kong’s coral environment using satellite remote sensing. The coral environment in Hong Kong has become seriously degraded since the 1980s due to coastal pollution, environmental and climate changes. Most hard corals have a very small tolerance to the changes in physical parameters such as salinity, temperature, and rate of sedimentation. They need not only light to support the photosynthetic activities of their symbiotic algae, but also a hard substratum on which to settle. Since Hong Kong’s coastal environment is characterized by a limited amount of hard bottom, space for coral settlement is scarce, and competition for space among corals and between corals and other organisms is intense. Additionally, a coral colony could itself be used by boring organisms for their own habitat. They easily settle on the coral surface and attack the corals, especially when the corals are not in good health. Extensive infestation of a coral colony by these borers can cause the coral skeleton to become so weakened that it is easily toppled by strong waves generated during a storm. Corals are delicate and slow-growing marine animals, but of high ecological-value by supporting the biodiversity. They are sensitive to changes in the marine environment and vulnerable to very many kinds of physical disturbance. In this proposal, multi-satellite data will be applied to investigate the changes of coastal environment in the study area during the last two decades. Historical data and the latest advanced high-resolution satellite data will be used to extract water-quality changes and relate these changes to the distribution of coral cover. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time that satellite remote sensing is used to study the impact of coastal water-quality on Hong Kong’s coral environment. The outcome of this proposal includes publications in peer-reviewed journals and reports for Hong Kong decision-makers in coastal-zones management. The findings of this study can be applied in several important fields of research, including the preservation of biodiversity, sustainable tourism and the understanding of global change/climate change, with particular reference to increasing sea surface temperatures and rising sea levels. Hong Kong is typical of many coral areas in the tropics, and therefore the implementation of this project can readily serve as a model for other tropical coral regions elsewhere in the world. 本项目研究目标就是应用卫星遥感调查海岸水质状况对香港珊瑚生长环境的影响。 自1980年代以来，由于海岸污染、环境和气候变化等影响，香港水域珊瑚的生长环境愈来愈恶化。许多珊瑚种类对诸如盐度、温度和沉积过程等物理变化的适应能力很小，他们不仅需要适当的光照条件进行光合作用，而且还需要坚硬的底盘作为支撑的生存条件。然而，由于香港附近海岸环境相对缺乏这种坚硬的底地盘，因此珊瑚生长空间有限，或珊瑚之间的空间竞争就异常激烈。此外，珊瑚群落本身也可以是自身的生长地，结果使得他们在健康不良条件下，易于受到外来物种的侵袭。这就使得这些珊瑚格架或底盘变得脆弱，更易于被风浪破坏或损坏。珊瑚是珍贵且生长缓慢的海洋动物，具有极高的生态价值。但他们对其生长环境及其敏感。 本项目将应用多种卫星数据调查研究区的过去二十年的环境变化趋势。历史数据和新的高分辨率卫星数据将用来提取水质参数，并找出其变化与珊瑚分布的对应关系。就我们所知，这是首次应用卫星遥感数据研究香港水域水质环境变化对珊瑚生长环境影响的研究项目。 本项目的成果将主要包括国际期刊文章和海岸带研究报告。研究的新发现将应用于其它相关领域，诸如生物多样性保护、生态旅游、以及对全球变化的了解和认识，特别是海温升高和海平面上升的影响。香港是热带区典型的珊瑚生长区域，该项目的实施将为其它热带珊瑚区的研究提供一个应用示范，具有十分重要的意义。

459310.label: Project Objectives
459310.value: Examine the joint effects of TQM and brand building efforts on quality, brand performance, customer satisfaction and loyalty by synthesizing the literature on TQM, branding efforts and their effects on performance and by drawing from the contingency theory perspective (Lawrence and Lorsch, 1967; Thompson, 1967, Drazin and Ven de Von, 1985). 459310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459310.value: Although operations management (OM) scholars have shown that TQM positively influences firm performance (e.g., Flynn et al., 2001; Zhao et al., 2004) and marketing scholars have provided empirical evidence that brand reputation influence customer’s choice and loyalty through identification and the differentiations of quality and origin (Cretu and Brodie, 2007), few studies have examined how TQM interact with branding efforts to influence firm performance. While it might be proper to examine the effects of TQM on firm performance without looking at branding efforts in the case of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEMs), it is very problematic for Original Brand Manufacturer (OBM). While the OEMs do not own the brand and often produce products according to the quality specifications and quantity requirements from their OEM customers, the OBMs own the brand and will have to face the demand uncertainty as a result of dynamic changes in consumer’s brand preferences as well as well as quality requirements. For OBMs, the branding efforts can influence the consumer’s choice of products with a specific brand through emotional appeals and thus significantly influence the effectiveness of the firm’s TQM efforts. However, little is known as to whether and how TQM and branding efforts will interact with each other and jointly affect OBMs. The negligence of branding effort in OM literature can potentially under or overestimate TQM’s contributions to firm performance and result in a biased conclusion about how OBMs compete in the market. To bridge this gap, we investigate the joint impacts of TQM and branding efforts on quality, brand performance, and customer satisfaction and loyalty. Drawing from the contingency theory, we hypothesize that these two efforts should fit each other and their interactions will positively influence organizational performances. Using data collected from 560 OBMs in a national wide quality management survey conducted by China Quality Management Association, we propose and test the a number of hypotheses concerning the relationships between TQM, branding efforts, their interactions, quality, brand performance, customer satisfaction and loyalty. The results of the study will show how TQM fits branding effort and how they jointly influence organizational performances. This study will also reveal whether TQM is critical to OBMs in the presence of branding effort and their relative and joint effects on performance under different situations. The findings will shed lights on the roles of TQM and branding efforts in improving OBMs’ performance. 当企业运作和市场营销需要的资源相同时，有限的资源使得原始品牌制造商（Original brand manufacturer，OBM）不得不在两者之间做出投入优先次序的选择。而做出这项选择的依据就来源于原始品牌制造商对于哪项投资能够带来更大的收益，并且这两项投资之间是不是有交互作用的理解。但是，现有的文献并没有针对这类问题提供相关信息。通过对560家中国原始品牌制造商数据的分析，项目研究企业运作中的全面质量管理和市场营销中的品牌建设对产品质量、品牌绩效、顾客满意度和忠诚度的联合影响。研究结果揭示了企业在这两方面的投入对其所关心的各种绩效的影响。其中，我们更特别地研究了二者之中哪一项更值得投入，以及这两项投入的交互作用对企业的各种绩效产生的额外价值。同时，这项研究也证明了全面质量管理和品牌建设是否在影响顾客满意度和忠诚度方面起到不同的作用。

459310.value: 1. Based on literature review and theoretical arguments, we proposed a conceptual model about the joint effects of TQM and brand building efforts on quality, brand performance, customer satisfaction and loyalty. 2. To test the model, we collected the data in collaboration with China Quality Management Association from Chinese manufacturers. 3. We performed the data purification, reliability and validity analyses using the data collected; 4. We performed structural equation modeling to test the main and interaction effects of TQM and Branding efforts on Chinese OBMs’ product quality, brand performance, and customer satisfaction and loyalty. 5. Based on result of the data analysis, we provided guidelines for OBMs to improve their performance: the operations department which implements TQM and the marketing department which is responsible for branding-building should collaborate with each other to ensure better performance. We submitted two papers for journal publications and have achieved all the research objectives we proposed to achieve.

459310.label: Major findings and research outcome
459310.value: Results revealed that brand-building may deserve more resources because of its more prominent role in influencing various performances. TQM and brand-building affect customer satisfaction and loyalty through different paths. Furthermore, TQM and brand-building are positively correlated and their interaction generates additional contributions to the product quality. These findings indicate that although brand-building may deserve more resources input, OBMs should also invest in TQM since investment in both is found critical to the OBMs’ long-term success. On the basis of the above analysis, we have finished one paper “The Joint Impact of TQM and Brand-building on Original Brand Manufacturers - a Chinese Study". This paper was originally submitted to Journal of Operations Management. Unfortunately, it was rejected. Then we revised and submitted it to Production and Operations Management, however, it was rejected again. Now we have finished revising it for the third round and submitted it to International Journal of Production Research. Moreover, using another secondary survey dataset, we tested another model. The results showed that with different level of environment uncertainty, the normative TQM profiles prescribed for manufacturing company will be different and deviations from these normative TQM profiles will lead to lower manufacturing performance. Especially, when the environment uncertainty is low, deviating negatively from the normative TQM profile has more disastrous impact on manufacturing performance than deviating positively. Based on these results, we have written another paper- "Aligning TQM Efforts with Environment Uncertainty Levels: Profiles, Fit, and Manufacturing Performance”. This paper will be revised and resubmitted to Journal of Operations Management.

459310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
459310.value: Another paper “The Impact of TQM and Brand-building Effort on Innovation Performance: Evidence of China” is under preparation. This paper aims at testing the main and interaction effect of TQM and Brand-building efforts on innovation performance.

459310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459310.value: Chinese Original Brand Manufacturers (OBMs) have to decide how to allocate resources between Total Quality Management (TQM) which focuses on operational improvement to make sure that products are designed, produced and delivered with high quality and brand buiding actitivities to boost market demands through enhancement in the brand image of the product. Chinese OBMs will have to address the question of which investment can bring more benefit to the firm and will investment in one increase or decrease the effectiveness of the investment in another one. To shed light on these issues, we investigate the joint effect of TQM and brand-building effort on product quality, brand performance, customer satisfaction and loyalty. Using the data collected from 560 Chinese OBMs in a national wide quality management survey, we test a model specifying the relationships between TQM, brand-building efforts, their interactions, product quality, brand performance, and customer satisfaction and loyalty. The result broadly substantiates our postulation by revealing that the interaction of TQM and brand-building effort generates additional contributions to the firm. More importantly, our study reveals that brand-building effort may deserve more resources because it plays a more prominent role than TQM does to influence OBM’s performances.

459410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459410.value: This project involves an advanced time-series analysis of gender-specific official crime data and markers of development for Taiwan society over the past five decades. It aims to assess the impact of development on female criminal involvement by testing four competing theoretical arguments: liberation, heightened strain, formalization of social control, and opportunities for female-based consumer crimes. There is a contentious debate in criminological literature about whether and to what extent female crime has increased with the process of development. It reflects longstanding attention among sociologists about the effects of development/modernization on the lives of people. It is also corresponding to gender scholars’ upsurge interest in the differential affects of development on men and women. According to the liberation thesis, development improves gender equality and thus leads to a rising female crime trend. Differently, the strain/anomie group argues that development brings more strain to modern women (i.e. economic marginalization, family disruption, and/or role conflicts) so that females may commit more crime to cope with the strain. Other research has suggested the formalization of social control may increase the visibility of female offending. In addition, development seems closely associated with the growth in opportunities for female consumer-based crime. Previous investigations of this topic are hampered by the shortage of suitable data across societies and historical periods. Using Taiwan longitudinal data to test the above four explanations, this study has potential to make ground-breaking theoretical contributions by relating the Chinese experience to heated debates on the development-female crime relationship that have often been based on cross-sectional evidence from Europe and North America. It also generates implications for future gender-specific crime prevention policies in Taiwan and the greater China region. Two major research questions are examined in this study. (1) Does female crime increase with development in Taiwan? If so, in what patterns? (2) How does development lead to rising female crime rates? The four competing explanations will be tested here, considering the effects of development on male offending as benchmarks. Distinctively, this research will apply stringent time series techniques (including Augmented Dickey-Fuller tests and Annual Time Series Regression) in tandem with intuitive trend plot-displays to probe the data and draw conclusions. A variety of qualitative methods, such as archival research and in-depth interviews (with professionals and legal practitioners), will also be used to get familiarity with the special social background, account for the dark figures in official data, and better understand the quantitative results. 本研究試圖應用先進的時間序列法來分析台灣過去50年的分性別官方犯罪數據及社會發展指標， 以評估社會發展對女性犯罪趨勢的影響。四種競爭性的理論觀點因此將被檢驗，包括女性解放，女性壓力增大，社會控制的正式化，以及女性為主的消費性罪行機會增加。 女性犯罪是否隨社會發展進程而有所增加或增加到何種程度？對此疑問，犯罪學文獻中一直存有激烈的爭論。它既反映了社會學家對社會發展/現代化與人類生活之間關係的長期關注，也呼應了性別研究者在社會變遷對男女兩性的影響差異方面的強烈興趣。根據女性解放學說，社會發展促進了兩性平等，進而導致了女性犯罪上升、與男性犯罪差異縮小的趨勢。與之不同，壓力/失範一派的學者認為，社會發展帶給現代女性更多的壓力（例如經濟邊緣化，家庭破碎，以及角色衝突），所以女性實施更多的犯罪以緩解壓力。也有其他研究表明，社會控制的正式化/專業化會增加女性犯罪的可見度，直接造成警方統計數字的上升。此外，隨著社會發展，以女性為主的犯罪機會（比如超市盜竊）也可能逐漸增長。由於缺乏跨文化和歷史階段的相應數據，這一領域的過往研究局限於歐美社會的橫向比較。本課題利用台灣社會的縱向數據來檢驗上述四種理論解釋，有可能在社會發展與女性犯罪的關係這方面做出突破性理論貢獻， 也有可能影響台灣乃至大中華區域的分性別犯罪防治政策。 此項課題包括兩個主要研究問題。 （1）隨著社會發展，台灣的女性犯罪是否有所增加？如果是這樣，以什麼模式增加？ （2）社會發展如何導致女性犯罪率上升？上述四種理論將在這裡被檢驗，同時也會與社會發展對男性犯罪的影響做比較。本研究將應用嚴格的時間序列統計技術（包括ADF檢驗與年度時間序列回歸模型）和直觀的趨勢圖來分析數據並得出結論。定性研究的各種方法，例如檔案研究和深入訪談（針對台灣的司法界以及其他相關專業人士），也將被用來收集台灣社會背景資料，解釋並彌補官方逮捕數據缺陷，以及深入理解定量結果。

459410.label: Realisation of objectives
459410.value: We collected all available and relevant official statistics and then organized them into two data sets for data analysis: (1) Dataset A, which has gender-specific crime rates (calculated based on annual crime statistics and overall population numbers by gender) for six major types of offences (homicide, aggravated assault, robbery, larceny, stolen property, and fraud) from 1961 to 2009. Drug offenses are also included but please note that the consistent definitions on drug offenses only exist since 1978. All important indicators of gender-related social development are further merged into this dataset (available only since 1978). (2) Dataset B, which has records of offence numbers, population numbers, offence rates and PAI by gender and every single age in every year from 1978 to 2009 (because single-age gender specific population numbers are only available since mid-1970s). Offence rates and PAI (age-specific female share of offenses) are then calculated. Object 1: We ran both descriptive analysis (trend lines) and rigorous Augmented Dickey-Fuller tests to check gender-specific crime trends based on the data set A & B. In general, this project objective has been achieved and the analysis shows that female crime trends increased and the gender gap narrowed in Taiwan for both the traditional (robbery and larceny) and the new types of property offenses (fraud), but not for non-property violence and drug offenses. The trends are also varying across different age groups of women. Especially, young women seem more likely to use violent means to gain financial benefits (robbery). Object 2: This objective has also been achieved successfully. Mainly based on data set A (1978-2009), four models have been built to test competing theories of gender-related social change and female crime: liberation, strain/institutional anomie theory, opportunities, and formalization of social control. We used principle component analysis (PCA) to combine a factor based on indicators that measure a same concept and added the factors into the four different AR time series regression models. PI also conducted two field trips in Taiwan (summer 2011 & summer 2012) to use various qualitative methods, such as archival research and in-depth interviews with experts in Taiwan, to further understand the quantitative regression results and systematic fluctuations reflected in the time series trend lines. The results show that the anomie and opportunity theories are supported. The formalization of social control is partially supported.

459410.label: Major findings and research outcome
459410.value: H1: In Taiwan, female crime trends are increasing with development from 1961 to 2009. For total women offense, the answer is yes. But there are variances by age and by type of offenses. Based on data set A, the trend curve displays and the ADF test results all show a general increasing trend for female rates, together with a narrowing gender gap (indicated by the rising Female percentage) for robbery, larceny, and fraud. For drug offenses, both male and female rates increased over time with similar pace and thus the gender gap was not narrowing. The female increasing trends are not found for homicide, aggravated assault and stolen property. We further ran similar analysis using the data set B. The results indicate that the rising crime rates and the narrowing gender gaps for larceny and fraud are across all age groups of women. However, the upward trends of female robbery rates and the narrowing robbery gender gap are mainly driven by the increasing criminality of young women below 18 years old. In general, the main hypothesis is supported for both the traditional (robbery and larceny) and the new types of property offenses (fraud), but not for non-property violence and drug offenses. Moreover, young women seem more likely to use violent means to gain financial benefits (robbery). H2 (liberal thesis): The AR regression model did not find consistent significant effects of the liberation indicators on female property offending and robbery (male-typed violence). The detailed bread-down of property offenses and the in-depth interviews with experts also did not identify the increasing female offending on lucrative forms of property offenses. The young women’s rising robber rates are either not related to the liberation indicators. Thus this hypothesis is not supported. H3 (anomie): The relationship between strain and institutional anomie experienced by females and female offending is positive and significant, especially for traditional female consumer-based offending and girls’ robbery as anomie/strain thesis predicted. H4 (opportunity): both the quantitative and qualitative study supports that development will increase the opportunities (i.e. more available goods) to female consumer-based offenses (including traditional theft and new types of fraud) as opportunity perspective predicted. H5 (social constructionists): our regression models and the interviews with experts indicate that the formalization of crime control and the policy shift in Taiwan increases female arrests for minor theft and also increase the arrests of young female offenders.

459410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
459410.value: Different from sociologists and criminologists, recent economics studies on crime trends mostly use VAR or error correction model. Our research team would like to try to compare the results of this VAR model with our AR models and to see whether we need to adjust our analysis methods. We will also prepare to submit two more papers using the data set of this project: one addresses the different effects of gender development on crime among girls vs adult women; one focuses on the changes of age-crime relationships (by gender) with social development. Both of the papers aim to publish in top journals of sociology/criminology.

459410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459410.value: There is a contentious scholarly debate about whether and to what extent female crime has increased with the process of development. It reflects longstanding attention among sociologists about the effects of development/modernization on the lives of people. It is also corresponding to gender scholars’ upsurge interest in the differential affects of development on men and women. According to the liberation thesis, development improves gender equality and thus leads to rising female offending. Differently, the anomie group argues that development brings more strain to modern women (i.e. economic marginalization and family disruption) so that females may commit more crime to cope with the strain. Other research has suggested the formalization of social control (i.e. standardized law enforcement) may increase the arrests of female offenders. Development also seems closely associated with the growth in opportunities for female consumer-based crime (i.e. shoplifting). Previous investigations are hampered by the shortage of data across societies and historical periods. Using Taiwan longitudinal data to test the above four explanations, this study has potential to make ground-breaking theoretical contributions by relating the Chinese experience to heated debates on the development-female crime relationship that was often based on Western evidence. It also generates implications for future gender-specific crime prevention policies.
