459410.value: Institutional Collaborations and knowledge transfer PI conducted two field trips in Taiwan (summer 2011 and summer 2012) and both trips were hosted by the Institute of Sociology (IOC), Academia Sinica in Taiwan. PI interviewed the relevant experts in IOC to have a general understanding on gender development and social change in Taiwan during the last five decades. Based on the individual-age crime data set collected for this GRF project, PI gave a talk at IOC to introduce the age-crime relationship in Taiwan. Such talks are usually open to both the scholars and the general public in Taiwan. PI also established further collaborations with two professors in IOC: one professor would like to ask her PhD student to help me collect Taiwan data and literature when I am not in Taiwan and the other professor will visit our department and try to co-organize a conference with us very soon. The institutional understandings and collaborations between IOC and our department (Department of Sociology, CUHK) are thus strengthened. The details of the talk: http://www.ios.sinica.edu.tw/ios/E/colloquiaBrief.php?colId=726 Topic： The Relationship between Social Development and Age- Crime Distributions: A Comparison of the US and Taiwan Date： 2012.07.13 Speaker： Associate Professor Zhong Hua (Department of Sociology, Chinese University of Hong Kong) Brief： Abstract: Although scholars agree that crime tends to rise and peak in adolescence or early adulthood and decline afterwards, there is a contentious debate in the criminological literature about whether and to what extent the shape or form of the age-crime curve varies across historical periods, geographic locations, and crime types. The invariancy view, most strongly articulated by Hirschi and Gottfredson (1983), is that the age-crime relationship is universal and invariant across all social and cultural conditions and all social groups at all times. Writers holding the variancy position contend (e.g., Greenberg 1985; Steffensmeier, Allan, Harer and Streifel 1989; Tittle and Grasmick 1998) that there is fact considerable variation across crime types and across countries or historical periods. A central feature of this debate concerns whether development increases youth crime involvement and then changes the age-crime distribution. The present study addresses these issues by examining the age-crime relationship in Taiwan over the period of 1961-1991. Taiwan is a strategic research site mainly because it has undergone considerable development over the past several decades and, in fact, has moved from being classified as a developing nation to a developed nation. Specifically, four hypotheses guide the research: (1) comparing age-crime distributions in Taiwan over the entire1960-1990 time frame, the distributions shift to a younger distribution with development; (2) based on both Taiwan and US arrest data, the age-crime curves in both nations should move to a younger distribution and peak earlier in the process of development; (3) due to cultural differences, there might be variations between Taiwan’s age-crime curves and the United States’ age-crime curves even at similar level of development; (4) markers of development predict changes (if they have occurred) in the age-crime distribution over the 1960-1990 period. Descriptive techniques and advanced time-series analysis are applied to examine these hypotheses. Overall, the results indicate that for general property offenses (except typical adult crime such as fraud), Taiwan’s age-crime curves have shifted to a younger age distribution over this time period as predicted by the variancy position. Moreover, the forces of development are especially useful for explaining these shifts. Such shifts and effects of development are not found for violent offenses and total offenses, which may be at least partially due to the continuity of traditional Chinese culture.

rows: How can investors use foreign currency to manage the risk of international equity portfolio if returns are not normally distributed and investors have positive skewness preference?
Does currency coskewness with international stock market have substantial explanatory power over the respective currency returns?
Is currency volatility exposure, measured by stock coskewness with currency, priced in stock return?

459510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459510.value: The aim of this proposal is to consider currencies as a separate and important asset class and to examine their diversification potential and valuation impact on international equity/bond portfolios beyond the traditional mean-variance framework. Understanding the co-movement between equity/bond and currency markets is crucial to international investment and portfolio diversification, as the choice of currency denomination is an important dimension in the make up of the overall portfolio. Many existing studies typically focus on the correlation between equity/bond and currency markets. However, the co-movement may not be fully captured by correlation. This project proposes a new method to address co-skewness across equity, bond and currency markets (i.e., the relationship between one market’s returns and another’s volatility), which goes beyond correlation (i.e., the relationship between two markets’ returns). Although there is some evidence that co-skewness is important for international equity/bond market returns, cross-market co-skewness between equity/bond and currency markets has not yet been analyzed. We intend to fill this gap in the literature and make the following contributions. With monthly data of ten developed markets and twelve emerging markets, this study will offer new evidence on cross-market co-skewness between equity/bond and currency markets and their pricing effects. These findings should enable us to better understand how investors should select foreign currencies to optimize the risk-return trade-off of an international equity/bond portfolio if returns are not normally distributed. First, the lower (higher) expected return on some currencies can be partially attributable to their characteristic of positive (negative) co-skewness with equity/bond markets. Second, some currencies may offer more diversification opportunities than one would normally expect based on the correlation, or the conventional mean-variance framework, supporting a higher strategic portfolio weight on these double hedging currencies. Third, investors should hedge currencies that are negatively correlated and/or positively co-skewed with equity/bond markets more fully, and hedge currencies that are positively correlated and/or negatively co-skewed with equity/bond markets less fully. 本课题旨在超越传统均值-方差的框架,将货币作为一种单独的重要资产类别,研究其分散性的潜力和对国际股票组合的价值的影响。虽然有证据表明协偏度对国际股票市场收益具有重要性，但尚没有人研究股市和汇市之间的跨市场协偏度。我们试图填补这一空白，采用一种新的方法，并运用约二十个国家的月度数据来研究其股市和外国货币之间的跨市场协偏度及其定价效应，以期更好地理解投资者应该如何选择外国货币来最优化其国际股票组合的风险与收益之权衡。首先，某些货币的高（低）收益可能是因为其与股市的正（负）协偏度。其次，某些货币可以提供更多分散性的机会，因而在资产组合中应占有更多的比重。第三，股票与货币的协偏度，即股票收益与货币波动性的关系，可能体现在股票的收益中。

459510.label: Realisation of objectives
459510.value: For the first objective, we examine the hedging benefits of various currencies in terms of their co-skewness with the international equity market. In the portfolio context, an investor with a skewness preference will examine an asset’s contribution to the skewness of a broadly diversified portfolio, referred to as “co-skewness” with the portfolio. The currency co-skewness is measured by the covariance between currency excess returns and global equity market volatility. We find that over the period 1973 to 2010, the safe-haven currencies, namely, the USD, the JPY, and the SWF, have better co-skewness properties than other developed market currencies – they have positive co-skewness with equity market whereas other currencies have negative co-skewness. The patterns imply that these currencies are a good hedge in a volatile market, because they appreciate when the equity volatility increases. For the second objective, we explore whether currency co-skewness with the world stock market earn ex ante risk premiums beyond conventional risk factors, such as conditional beta with the stock market and currency volatility, as well as currency idiosyncratic skewness. We find that currency co-skewnesses are significantly priced with the expected negative risk premium, after controlling for currency betas, volatilities and skewnesses. The finding suggests that the lower excess returns on these safe-haven currencies can be partially attributed to their desirable hedging properties of positive co-skewness, which differs from time-varying beta, volatility and skewness. For the third objective, we derive stock co-skewness which is the covariance between stock excess return and various currency volatilities and then explore whether stock co-skewness with the world stock market earn ex ante risk premiums beyond conventional risk factors, such as conditional beta with the currency market and stock volatility, as well as stock idiosyncratic skewness. However, there is no clear pattern that stock co-skewness with currency is priced in stock return. Therefore, I do not include this part in the paper but focus on the currency co-skewness and its pricing effect.

459510.label: Major findings and research outcome
459510.value: We keep revising our paper directly from this research project. The current (15th) version of the paper is titled "What Makes Safe-haven Currencies? Evidence from Conditional Co-skewness" with following major findings. We examine the currency co-skewness with the global stock market (i.e., covariance between currency returns with global equity volatility). We document that the three safe-haven currencies (USD, SWF and JPY) have positive co-skewness whereas other currencies have negative co-skewness. Moreover, currency co-skewnesses are significantly priced with the expected negative risk premium, after controlling for currency betas, volatilities and skewnesses. The finding suggests that the lower excess returns on these safe-haven currencies can be partially attributed to their desirable hedging properties of positive co-skewness, which differs from time-varying beta, volatility and skewness. It also extends the recent evidence that the low interest rate currencies are less exposed to global stock market volatility and thereby provide a hedge against global stock market volatility. We argue that safe haven currencies have lower interest rates because investors would flight to the Treasury bond markets of safe-haven currency economies, when global equity volatility increases. It takes some time to publish the above paper on top finance journal. We have received good comments from field experts such as Warren Bailey, Greet Bekaert and Bruno Solnik as well as referees from Journal of Finance on the earlier versions of the paper. We are trying to submit the revised paper to another top Finance journal. Also, two other related papers has been published or nearly accepted. One paper titled "Credit Risk Spillovers among Financial Institutions around the Global Credit Crisis Firm-Level Evidence" has been published in Management Science. The other paper titled "Modeling the Joint Dynamics of Risk Neutral Stock Index and Bond Yield Volatilities" is under minor revision at Journal of Banking and Finance.

459510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
459510.value: There is potential to further examine conditional co-kurtosis, which is measured by the covariance between currency excess returns and equity market skewness. Safe-haven currencie's co-kurtosis with the world equity market is either negative or lower than other currency counterparts, suggesting even higher hedging effectiveness for these currencies during extreme stock market downturns (market crashes). I like to pursue further along this line if the unspent balance could be used or there is additional funding support.

459510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459510.value: Following the Lehman Brothers’ collapse and financial tsunami in 2008, investors around the world have been looking for safe-haven currencies over the last few years. Safe-haven currencies are those that investors flock to whenever there is a crisis, or merely an outbreak of uncertainty, and which give hedging benefits at times when financial markets are volatile. According to conventional wisdom, “When foreign exchange investors felt panicky, they head to, or back to, old faithfuls: the Swiss franc, the U.S. dollar and the Japanese yen,” so that these three currencies – the US dollar (USD), the Swiss franc (SWF) and the Japanese yen (JPY) – are regarded as safe-haven currencies. We find that these safe haven currencies have desirable hedging properties because investors would flight to the Treasury bond markets of safe-haven currency economies, when global equity volatility increases and thus earn lower currency return and interest rates. The findings extends the conventional literature and offers better understanding of global currency hedging.

459710.label: Project Objectives

How to understand the market pricing mechanism on the risk premium associate with equity and credit instruments? Can we reconcile the risk premium associate with equity and credit instruments? rows: How to understand the impact of credit risk of a firm on its equity price?
How to better measure market CDS spreads?
How to understand the market pricing mechanism on the risk premium associate with equity and credit instruments?
Can we reconcile the risk premium associate with equity and credit instruments?
Is credit risk premium consistent and/or justifiable between equity and credit instruments?

459710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459710.value: The aim of this study is to understand whether the prices observed in equity and debt markets reflect the same credit risk on the firm level. The ongoing financial crisis has pushed US economy into a recession that is comparable to the Great Depression. In one measure, the high yield spreads reached record levels over 2000 bps in 2008 and 2009, and the high yield debt market was essentially closed in most of the time in 2008. However, with either dollar-weighted or volume-weighted measure, the real default rate of these high yield bonds, although jumped from 2007, was no more than 5.8% in 2008, not even comparable to that in 2004. This brings up an interesting question. Why the market implied default probability reflected in the Credit Default Swaps (CDS) spreads is so high compared with the realized default probability? Existing studies from structural approach have tried to answer this question from equity and its option. But so far the existing studies have not answered the question: what is the impact of credit risk on a firm’s equity price? With our previous work and recent datasets, we intend to answer: Can we justify the market prices of equity and credit instruments by credit risk? More specifically, we want to know whether the credit risk at the firm level has an impact on firm’s equity value. If so, is the impact of credit risk on the equity side comparable with that on CDS side? This is because equity is a residual claim of a firm’s cash flow. Given existing credit risk, not only should the firm’s CDS spreads show this risk, but also the firm’s equity put option should reflect the same risk. By comparing the risk premium associate with credit spreads and equity put option, we can tell a story whether the CDS spreads are justifiable. The main contribution of this study is to find out the relationship between the sources and artifacts of the risk. Especially, we are interested in how the observed prices in the financial markets reflect credit risk. This is because what pushed the US economy into recession is the 2000 bps spreads not the 6% real default rate. Hopefully, investors and regulators could benefit from the results of this study, so we are in a better position to reduce the cost of a future credit crisis. 本研究的目的是为了探寻股票市场和债券市场对于同一公司违约风险的定价是否一致。

459710.label: Realisation of objectives
459710.value: I started the work on objective two. The results showed that the default probability (DP) implied by CDS market is much higher than the realized default rate. This is not surprise because CDS spreads are forward looking with risk premium. According to contingent claim theory, equity and credit are contingent on firm asset. To understand the risk premium from the equity side (object three), I generated implied DPs based on information from equity and option market. Comparing two implied DPs, I found that they co-moved but the magnitude was different. To reconcile the risk premium in two markets (objective four), I created a DP divergence index. Please refer to Appendix II in the paper attached. Surprisingly, the index at the market level highly co-moved with the S&P 500 index. When the market was normal, the index movement was dominated by the CDS market. From 2004 to 2006, the DP warning from the CDS market became stronger than that from the equity side (objective one). But if CDS is more informative in normal time, why in 2008 crisis the equity side really took over (objective five)? The anecdote evidence suggested the counterparty risk in CDS market may play a role. To investigate the counterparty effect, I started to collect CDS transaction data from SEC EDGAR. After compiling the CDS transaction data, I noticed with surprise that no more than 20 broker-dealer banks traded as CDS counterparty. If the 20 banks are related to the crisis, how risk was generated, and what was the channel of contagion? I enlarged the sample from CDS companies to all companies borrowed syndicate loan or corporate bond. After comparing the return of CDS and non-CDS yet with debt access companies, I had two findings. First, stock returns of CDS and non-CDS companies co-moved yet CDS companies suffered more. Second, the 20 CDS dealer banks have taken a dominant market share of the intermediary service in two debt markets. Following this line, I have answered the question in objective five by Lundblad and Zhu (2013) (paper attached). The equity market takes control in 2008 because it is a systematic crisis, which is a result of systemic banking crisis stemming from bad assets on banks’ balance sheet. 97 large banks are pivotal because they hold illiquid mortgage assets and they dominate the intermediary service in debt markets. Our findings support Diamond and Rajan (2005).

459710.label: Major findings and research outcome
459710.value: The major findings are as follows. The market based CDS spreads are forward-looking, and the implied DP is higher than the historical default rate. Contingent on firm assets, we can imply DP from credit and equity market. The two implied DPs co-move in general. In normal market condition, CDS spreads predict DP relatively higher than the equity market, but in crisis period, equity markets take over, especially in 2008 financial crisis. The endeavors to understand why the equity markets dominate in 2008 financial crisis lead to a paper by Lundblad and Zhu (2013). This is perhaps the first empirical paper, to our best knowledge, that tests 2008 financial crisis against three theories and provides supporting evidence to Diamond and Rajan (2005, DR). Our results show the 2008 financial crisis starts as a banking crisis stemming from bad assets and spills over to thousand non-financial companies. The top 97 banks are critical because they hold bad assets and are dominant liquidity providers. We observe liquidity has reduced significantly during the crisis. Banks that could access more liquidity or banks with alternative liquidity connections, however, could not reduce their systemic risk. The contagion that arises within the banking sector does not require ex ante, explicit link among banks. These findings are difficult to explain by previous theories, yet consistent with the predictions of systemic crisis by DR. For risk spillover from financial to non-financial sector, our findings could be expected from DR yet difficult to understand by the lending channel theory. In addition, we create several measures to identify how non-financial companies connect to the financial system. The measures include short-term financing, number of connections to the financial system, and connection to good/bad banks. Our findings show that the in-crisis risk is higher for companies replying on short-term financing or with more connection to the system. Risk could be reduced if companies connect with good banks instead of bad banks. There are about 1000 companies that report lower in-crisis risk. This is because these companies do not connect to the financial system before the crisis. The bankruptcy of Lehman Brother (LB) may not be social optimal because LB is the top 8 net liquidity provider to the system, and the insolvency of LB exacerbates the liquidity shortages and speed up the meltdown process. Our findings contribute to the empirical literature on banking crises and the contagion mechanism.

459710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
459710.value: Lundblad and Zhu (2013) is the proceeding of this project. We are working on the paper for broader circulation to conferences and journals. In addition, the database on CDS transactions has inspired new ideas on a further research project. In my RGF 2014/15 proposal, I propose to address a question: Why mutual funds trade CDS, especially sell CDS during the crisis period? I aim to test the database of CDS transactions against two theories.

459710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459710.value: Although literature is growing on financial crises, many questions remain unanswered. Carey, Kashyap, Rajan, and Stulz (2012) list over 30 topics calling for proposal on the 2008 financial crisis. This paper aims to address the first one: How could moderate losses from the mortgage market amplify into a systematic crisis? Our findings trace the origin of the crisis back to the bad assets on a small number of large financial institutions, and show the development of a systemic banking crisis and the path of contagion on non-financial companies. Our results provide supporting evidence for Diamond and Rajan (2005). We show novel, direct evidence on systemic crisis in financial sector and contagion effects from financial to non-financial companies. We also show how to reduce spillover effect on non-financial companies. Our study may also be of interest to regulators by showing that large banks providing liquidity service to the system and holding illiquid assets on their balance sheet are important to understand the cause of 2008 financial crisis. Our results also show the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers may not be social optimal as its insolvency exacerbate the situation.

460010.label: Project Objectives
460010.value: To evaluate the physiological tolerance of select Sargassum species in NW Pacific to temperature and salinity; To verify how these differential physiological tolerances of members of the subgenera Bactrophycus and Sargassum could explain their current biogeographical pattern in this region; To project how global climate change could affect the distribution pattern of major Bactrophycus and Sargassum species, and hence indirectly, the biodiversity of their associated epiphytic flora and fauna.
rows: To evaluate the physiological tolerance of select Sargassum species in NW Pacific to temperature and salinity;
To verify how these differential physiological tolerances of members of the subgenera Bactrophycus and Sargassum could explain their current biogeographical pattern in this region;

To project how global climate change could affect the distribution pattern of major Bactrophycus and Sargassum species, and hence indirectly, the biodiversity of their associated epiphytic flora and fauna.

460010.label: Realisation of objectives
460010.value: Temperature and salinity changes are known to affect biogeographical distribution of marine coastal species. The effects of these variables on the distribution of marine algae in the Asia-Pacific region are poorly documented. Recent biogeographical studies on common brown alga Sargassum hemiphyllum revealed two distinct and highly homogenous clades, a China clade and a Japan-Korea clade. Gradients of sea surface temperature (SST) and hyposaline condition in Bohai and East China Sea created by the outflow of freshwater from Yellow and Yangtze Rivers were proposed to be the key physical barriers in halting the gene flows between the populations of this species during postglacial period, leading to its genetic divergence into two varieties. The present study was set up to test this hypothesis and to evaluate main underlying driving forces determining the phylogeographical distribution of the brown alga Sargassum in northwest Pacific. Both field and laboratory based studies were carried out to address the objectives. Field works included bi-weekly to monthly phenological assessment of the representative Sargassum species in Hong Kong, S. hemiphyllum, and integration with long term (>10 years) data available from the past to correlate these with the temperature data also collected within the same period. Laboratory based studies included experiments in which life history stages of S. hemiphyllum were exposed to ranges of temperature (ambient ± 4 to 8C) and salinity (35 to 5 psu) to evaluate their tolerance limit. Several physiological end points were used, including photosynthetic yields, non-photochemical quenching, growth and mortality. Additional experiments involving pre-exposure of growing stages of S. hemiphyllym branchlets to different temperatures, to simulate natural lowering and rising of SST from winter to spring, were also carried out to verify the possible triggering condition for the initiation of reproductive seasonality. On a broader geographical scale to address objectives 2 and 3, multivariate statistical analyses were carried out to evaluate the relationship between environmental conditions and range of distribution of Sargassum species in northwestern Pacific. Different operating geographical units (OGU) were first designated. Major environmental variables, including latitude of the centroid of OGU, the mean annual SST, lowest winter SST, highest summer SST, annual salinity and tidal amplitude were correlated with the diversity of Sargassum species within each OGU. The most important underlying driving forces determining the distribution and diversity of Sargassum species were extracted and their possible roles in affecting the distribution pattern of Sargassum in evolutionary and ecological scales were also assessed.

460010.label: Major findings and research outcome
460010.value: Phenological changes in the life history stages of Sargassum hemiphyllum were followed from August 2011 to June 2013. The data were integrated with earlier data collected from 1998 to 2007 to evaluate the pattern of change in growth and reproduction with pattern of temperature change. Reproduction was found to be strongly correlated with the rising seawater surface temperature (SST) after a drop in winter temperature. Peak reproduction could be delayed by two to four weeks in some years (e.g. 2012) because of delay in the onset of rising SST in spring (Conference 1, 3; Research 1 ). The ranges of tolerance to temperature and salinity of life history stages of the algae, including the holdfast, slow, rapid growth and germling stages, were assessed. For the temperature experiments (Conference 2, 4; Research 2), the ranges tested were ambient (corresponding to each stage in Hong Kong), -4/8 and +4/8 oC below or above the ambient respectively. The parameters evaluated included photosynthetic yield, non-photosynthetic quenching, change in thallus length, wet weight and surface area (for holdfast only). The results revealed that different stages tested were all growing under suboptimal conditions in Hong Kong. The optimal conditions were always lower than the ambient. This suggests that populations of this species are likely to be at their marginal range of distribution in Hong Kong. For salinity experiments (Research 3), a fixed range of salinities (35, 25, 15 and 5psu) was used. A consistent result was observed. Individuals in the different stages under ambient salinity of 35psu exhibited optimum growth whereas lower salinities had significantly impaired their growth and survivorship. The brackish condition of 5psu was always lethal. Photosynthetic rate was the most sensitive metabolic parameter towards salinity stress with significantly lower photosynthetic yield and high non-photochemical quenching recorded in samples exposed to low salinities. Multivariate statistical analysis was used to further evaluate the relationship between environmental conditions and range of distribution of Sargassum species in northwestern Pacific (Research 4). SST (covariate with latitude), especially winter SST, was found to be the most critical factor in structuring the Sargassum phycogeographical patterns. A transitional zone of occurrence between species under the subgenus Bactrophycus and those under the subgenus Sargassum was found. The former were likely to be more recently radiated, especially in the northern part of the northwestern Pacific, and exhibited eurythermal adaptation. In contrast, the subgenus Sargassum likely originated in the Tropics.

460010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460010.value: Sargassum populations examined in the present study indicated that they are not growing under the optimal SST conditions. The evidences point to sites in higher latitudes, most likely around Zhejiang Province where summer and winter temperatures appear to be more appropriate for their optimal growth. There is a need to verify this hypothesis. Samples from areas around Zhejiang should be examined to see if indeed these populations are growing at their best. Another possibility is that this species originated from the north, hence the temperature optima of all derived populations in the south would always be lower than what they currently experience in their local conditions. Yet the populations can survive and propagate, as they remain tolerant to these temperature conditions. In terms of exposure to salinity, current evidence suggests the inability of the reproductive population to tolerate below 15psu. In which case, the outflow of freshwater from the major rivers in central China, as hypothesized earlier, appears to be able to serve as an effective barrier for their northward dispersal. The interactive effects of temperature and salinity should also be considered. These are major questions that remain to be addressed and could be the focus of future works.

460010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460010.value: The brown seaweeds Sargassum are the most dominant canopy forming species in the coastal environment from Southeast Asia to northwestern Pacific, including China, Korea and Japan. Environmental conditions that could affect the distribution patterns of different species of this brown seaweed were examined. The focus was primary on two main factors, temperature and salinity. Different stages of the main Sargassum species, S. hemiphyllum, were examined. Rising temperature in spring was found to be the triggering factor in initiating reproduction and reproductive season could be delayed because of delay in the onset of this rising temperature. Furthermore, laboratory experiments indicate that this species, although dominant in Hong Kong, are not growing under the best environmental conditions locally. This indicates that Hong Kong is likely to be the southern range limit of its distribution. Salinity experiments, however, showed that they are growing best under the ambient salinity condition. This suggests that it is a truly marine species less tolerable to low salinity. Using statistical approach, sea surface temperature, especially winter temperature, was found to be likely the most critical factor in affecting the distribution of different species of this seaweed in northwestern Pacific.

460110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
460110.value: All gastric Helicobacter species possess a prominent feature of flagella-driven motility that is essential for colonization and infection in those tested. Flagellar assembly, export, torque generation and chemotactic induced-switching are controlled by the flagellar motor switch complex typically composed of FliG, FliM and FliN. In some bacteria, FliN is replaced by a protein called FliY that bears a FliN domain fused to a phosphatase domain called CheC. Interestingly and unusually, H. pylori harbors both FliN and FliY. Accumulating genomic, transcriptomic and biophysical studies have shown that the flagellar system in H. pylori differs in interesting ways from other microbes such as having both FliN and FliY. Up-to-date, no structures of any these switch proteins in H. pylori has been solved. We are particularly interested in understanding the molecular basis for flagella formation and switching in this microbe. Recently, we have solved the crystal structures of flagellar export chaperone FliS and its complex with co-chaperone HP1076, chemotactic protein CheY and motor switch FliM. To continue our study on bacterial motility in H. pylori, we have demonstrated the molecular interaction of FliG-FliM and FliN-FliY, and mapped the domains required for their interaction. Furthermore, in vivo FliG, FliM, FliN and FliY and FliN/FliY deletions result in aflagellated phenotype in H. pylori, suggesting that all four switch proteins are required for flagellation and FliY is a structural component of the switch complex. In this study, we will apply multidisciplinary approaches in molecular and structural biology to characterize the structural architecture of the switch complex and the biological significance of FliY and its co-existence with FliN in H. pylori. Specifically, we will study the molecular interactions of FliG-FliM and FliN-FliY, and define the critical binding interface by mutagenesis studies. We will solve the atomic structure of FliG and attempt to determine the complexes of FliG-FliM and FliN-FliY by x-ray crystallography. The findings from the in vitro interaction studies will be further verified and examined using in vivo complementation assays of the null mutants. Our work will generate novel knowledge in motor switch assembly and rotation switching in H. pylori, and also lay a foundation for future investigation of multi-protein components in the switch complex. In the long term, the structural model will reveal key information to understand the diversity of bacterial flagellar systems, especially the specific functions of FliN and FliY, and the export mechanism for secretion of virulence factors in other pathogenic bacteria.

460110.label: Realisation of objectives
460110.value: Objective 1: Our team has successfully purified the FliG-FliM and FliY-FliN complexes. By using a combination of mutagenesis, pull-down, static light scattering and isothermal titration calorimetry assays, we have further mapped their interacting surfaces, studied their stoichiometric ratio and binding kinetics. Specifically, residues 139 YDQ 141 of FliM and 182 EH 183 of FliG were found to be essential for the 1:1 FliG-FliM complex formation. Our results also showed that FliY and FliN formed a heterodimer mediated by hydrophobic patches. Objective 2: To confirm our in vitro findings, we attempted to use the H. pylori FliG-null strain for in vivo complementation. Full length FliG in overexpressed pILL2157 vector and RdxA vector systems were applied, however flagellation cannot be complemented. We considered some other neighboring genes related to flagellar synthesis may be interrupted during the construction of the FliG deletion strain. To overcome the problems, we have applied FliM-null strain to validate the mapping results of FliG-FliM interaction from Objective 1. For FliY-FliN interactions, H. pylori FliY-null strain was used for in vivo complementation. Mutations of hydrophobic residues on the binding interface resulted in non-flagellation. These results are in line with our in vitro findings. Objective 3: By using x-ray crystallography, we have determined, for the first time, the crystal structures of H. pylori FliG, FliM, and FliG-FliM and FliY-FliN binary complexes. The atomic details revealed the underlying molecular basis of switch protein interactions and the assembly of the motor. These structural findings are very beneficial as they provide a solid key to dissect the structure-function relationship of the switch proteins as described in Section 6.1. Objective 4: In vivo assays were performed using H. pylori FliY-null mutant complemented with different FliY truncated fragments in pILL2157 overexpression vector. In conjunction of electron-microscopy and soft agar motility assays, we demonstrated that the FliY N- and C-terminal domains each carried distinct function; the former is required for wild type motility whereas the latter is required for flagellation. This in vivo data was also supported by our binding assays that export apparatus FliH can associate to FliY C-terminal domain in complex with FliN. Despite FliY contains a CheX/CheC like domain, H. pylori FliY is defective in phosphatase activity. The full biological role of the FliY N-terminal domain remains to be addressed. Nevertheless, together with the structural data, the co-existence of FliY and FliN implies that H. pylori exploits a unique flagellar motor system.

460110.label: Major findings and research outcome
460110.value: 1. Structural insights of rotational switching from the crystal structure of FliG Two crystal structures of FliG have been determined to 2.6Å and 2.7Å resolutions. Structural comparisons revealed a two-fold molecular rotation at the C-terminal alpha 1-6 subdomain which bears a charged-ridge for stator MotA-MotB interaction. Interruption of the conserved 245 MFXF 248 motif at the hinge of the alpha 1-6 subdomains resulted in rotation bias, suggesting that conformation flexibility of this subdomain is critical for motor function. The results lead us to propose a model for symmetrical torque generation in motor switching. These findings have been presented in BLAST meeting and published in Structure 20:315-25 (2012). 2. Assembly of FliG-FliM in the motor C-ring We have determined the crystal structures of FliM and FliG-FliM complex at a resolution of 2.3Å and 2.8Å, respectively. We demonstrated that formation of FliM-FliG complex is mediated through the FliG middle domain, but not the C-terminal domain as in E. coli system. Variable residues on the binding interface were also identified that contribute to differential binding affinities across bacterial species. By combining our structural data and previous cryo-electron tomographic data of H. hepaticus, we proposed a FliG-FliM assembly model. These findings have been published in Mol. Microbiol. 88:798-812 (2013) and selected for cover image. 3. Co-existence of FliY and FliN is indispensable for motor function in H. pylori Unlike model microorganisms such as E. coli, H. pylori genome encodes an addition switch protein gene FliY with unknown function. By using different truncated FliY fragments transformed into FliY-null strain, we showed that FliY C-terminal domain is indispensable for flagellation and bacterial motility. Interestingly, FliY N-terminal domain harbouring sequence similarity with CheX/CheC family was required to give full motility, suggesting its role in maintaining proper motor function. We further demonstrated the physical association of FliY with the switch complex, in particular FliN. A 2.1Å crystal structure of FliY-FliN complex has revealed that FliY-FliN heterodimer resemble FliN dimerization in T. maritima. Moreover, we have mapped the residues on FliY-FliN that are important for FliH binding for flagellar protein export. Since the co-existence of FliY and FliN only occurs in H. pylori and its closely related species, our findings provide the first biochemical and structural insights into the divergence of motor switch complex. A manuscript describing this part of work is in preparation. The PI was invited to deliver talks on the flagellar motor in two international meetings.

460110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460110.value: Our work has elucidated the structural basis of the four switch proteins, and the FliG-FliM and FliY-FliN complexes in the upper and lower C-ring, respectively. These findings lay a solid foundation for us to further investigate the mechanics and regulations of this nano-motor. Currently, there are several lines of investigation underway in our team. First, we are studying the assembly of MS-C ring junction, and have recently solved the crystal structure of FliF-FliG which reveals how the cytoplasmic switch complex is anchored to the inner membrane. Second, we are studying the mechanism of torque generation and rotational switching mediated by MotA-FliG (stator-motor). Third, in collaboration with Prof. Zhang Qinfen (Sun Yat-sen University), x-ray crystallography and cryo-EM approaches are applied to dissect the whole architecture of H. pylori flagellar motor. Fourth, we have extended our work to identify the interactome of switch complex that regulates the motor function. Fifth, in collaboration with Prof. Wu Yilin (Physics, CUHK), we are studying the stoichiometry and turnover of FliM that are critical for tuning response and adaptation of the motor. In the future, the assembly of export apparatus onto FliY-FliN and the significance of structural diversity of motor on adaptation will be studied.

460110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460110.value: Flagellar motor switch complex is an important nano-rotary device that governs the rotation of flagellum for bacterial movement. Gastric pathogen H. pylori consists of four motor switch proteins FliG, FliM, FliN and FliY but how they assemble into a supramolecular complex is unknown. This project aims to characterize the molecular architecture of motor switch complex from H. pylori. We have determined, for the first time, the crystal structures of FliG, FliM, and FliG-FliM and FliY-FliN binary complexes by x-ray crystallography. Together with the biochemical and genetics studies, the atomic basis and biological significance of these switch proteins in flagellar formation, rotation and switching are elucidated. Specifically, flexibility of FliG C-terminal domain is associated to rotational switching mechanism. FliY when complexed with FliN mimics dimerization of FliN in E. coli system and forms a docking site for export apparatus, implying the functional role of FliY-FliN co-existence in H. pylori. Moreover, differential binding affinity of FliG-FliM and phosphatase activity deficient FliY suggest that H. pylori exploits a distinct strategy of motor assembly and regulation. Our findings improve our understanding of the flagellar motor and also provide new concepts to dissect the divergence of this nano-machine critical for host cells colonization and adaption.

460710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
460710.value: Tendon connects muscle and bone and transmits force generated by muscle to bone for skeletal movement. Tendon tissue mainly composed of dense fibrous collagenous bundle and endures constant mechanical stress/strain loading. Tendon injuries are common with 3-5 millions injuries annually worldwide caused by sports activities and trauma.. Achilles tendon is one of the most frequently ruptured tendons and counts for approximately 40% of all tendon repair surgery. Tendon injuries are usually caused by a sudden overloading strain or direct blow to the tendon during contraction or age related chronic degeneration. Achilles tendon rupture is preferably treated surgically with immobilization and the complications associated are wound breakdown, adhesion, joint contractures and secondary rupture. Tendon injury is difficult to repair and often leads to scar tissue formation, which is prone to re-rupture. Augmentation of tendon healing is needed to reduce rehabilitation time, morbidity and complications. Injection of anabolic factors, biophysical intervention and stem cell therapy with tissue engineering have been attempted to enhance tendon repair in preclinical studies. In this proposal, we will test the use of tenogenic stem cells with tendon matrix in Achilles tendon defect animal model using tissue engineering approaches. Bone marrow derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) will be induced for tenogenic differentiation by growth differentiation factor-6 (GDF-6) or over-expression of tendon differentiation specific gene, Scleraxis gene. The modified stem cells will be loaded to a novel three-dimensional acellularised tendon matrix. The cell-matrix composites are then implanted into mouse Achilles tendon defect model to test the hypothesis that MSC-derived tenogenic cells together with tendon matrix could enhance tendon healing. The objective of this study are: 1) To investigate effect of GDF-6 and Scleraxis axis on tenogenesis of bone marrow derived MSCs; 2) To fabricate acellularised tendon matrix as bioscaffold for tendon regeneration and 3) To exam the efficacy of tenogenic MSCs combined with tendon matrix for tendon repair. The results will shed light on mechanisms of tendongenesis and tendon tissue engineering. 肌腱連接肌肉和骨頭，傳送肌肉的力量至骨頭作骨骼運動。肌腱主要由一束束密集的膠原纖維組成，能承受機械應力或張力。肌腱損傷十分常見，全球每年約有三至五百萬宗，主要由運動勞損和創傷造成。肌腱損傷通常是由於伸展時突然超出負荷或收縮時直接碰撞所造成，亦可能與慢性退化有關。肌腱斷裂最適宜採用手術加石膏固定療法，而可能的併發症包括傷口破裂、黏連、關節攣縮、及繼發性斷裂。肌腱斷裂較難修補，修補後經常形成疤痕組織，引致繼發性斷裂，其成效往往取決於自癒能力。要減少修復時間、降低病態和併發症的風險，必須促進肌腱癒合。一些臨床前研究表明，注射促進合成代謝的因子、進行生物物理學的干預、或應用組織工程學的幹细胞療法，都能促進肌腱癒合。 在這個提案中，我們將利用組織工程學的方法，在肌腱缺損動物模型中測試成肌腱幹细胞與肌腱基質的治療效果。骨髓間質幹细胞(MSCs)將透過生長分化因子6 (GDF-6)的誘導或Scleraxis基因的過量表達，被誘導向肌腱分化。我們將被誘導的成肌腱幹細胞注入已去除細胞的三維肌腱基質中，然後將之植入小鼠肌腱缺損傷口，藉此測試成肌腱幹细胞與肌腱基質能否促進肌腱癒合。這項研究的宗旨是：(1) 探討GDF-6與Scleraxis在誘導MSC分化成肌腱的作用; (2)製造去細胞的肌腱基質，作為肌腱再生的三維生物支架; (3) 檢驗成肌腱幹细胞與肌腱基質結合後修復肌腱的效能。 研究結果將有助了解幹细胞分化成肌腱的機制及肌腱組織工程學。

460710.label: Realisation of objectives
460710.value: All the project objective have been achieved. Objective 1: We study the effect of GDF-6 treatment and Scleraxis overexpression on tenogenesis of tendon derived MSCs (TDSCs). In this part we discovered that GDF-6 treatment promoted tenogenic differentiation of BMSCs but not TDSCs. We also successfully generated Scleraxis overexpression TDSCs cell line. In this cell lines, tenogenic markers are up-regulated which indicated Scleraxis promoted tenogenic differentiation. These results have been presented in 3 conferences (1. School of Biomedical Sciences Research 2012, 2. 32nd Annual Congress of the Hong Kong Orthopaedic Association and 3. 7th International Congress of Chinese Orthopaedic Assoication). Objective 2: We have successfully fabricated acellular tendon matrices as bioscaffold for tendon tissue engineering. We have culture TDSCs with the acellular tendon matrices; cell could growth on this scaffold. Objective 3: We have used tenogenic MSCs (TDSCs) and Scx overexpression TDSCs with acellular tendon matrices for tendon repair. In this part, we found Scx overexpression TDSCs improved tendon healing in a patellar tendon window injury model at early stage, both in histology and biomechanical properties. These findings have been presented in 2 conferences (1. 2nd CUHK International Symposium on Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine, 2. 2013 Orthopaedic Research Society Annual Meeting) and published in 2 papers (1. 460710.label: Major findings and research outcome
460710.value: In the first part of the study, we found that GDF-6 did not promote the tenogenic differentiation of TDSCs. While GDF-6 increased the expression of tendon-related markers (Col1a1, Scx and Thbs4) in BMSCs in the serum-free condition, the expression of these tendon-related markers remained lower compared to TDSCs and hence BMSCs might not be a favorable cell source for tendon repair even after pre-treatment with GDF-6. In addition, we investigated the effect of Scx transduction on the expression of lineages markers in TDSCs. GFP-TDSC-Scx consistently showed higher expressions of most of tendon- and cartilage- related markers compared to the GFP-TDSC-Mock. However, the effect of Scx transduction on the expressions of bone-related markers was inconclusive. There were significantly higher expressions of tendon-related markers including Thbs4 (post-hoc p=0.006), Tnc (post-hoc p=0.025), Col1a1 (post-hoc p=0.018), Epha4 (post-hoc p=0.047), Eya1 (post-hoc p=0.009) and Six1 (post-hoc p=0.021) but not Six2, Eln and Tnmd in the GFP-TDSC-Scx compared to those in the GFP-TDSC-Mock. There were also significantly higher expressions of cartilage-related markers including Acan (post-hoc p=0.009), Bgn (post-hoc p=0.009), Col2a1 (post-hoc p=0.009), Sox9 (post-hoc p=0.016) but not Col10a1 in the GFP-TDSC-Scx compared to those in the GFP-TDSC-Mock. There was also significantly higher expression of bone-related markers including Runx2 (post-hoc p=0.047) but not Spp1 and Bglap in the GFP-TDSC-Scx compared to that in the GFP-TDSC-Mock. In part 2, we aimed to fabricate an acellularized matrix as a scaffold for tendon tissue engineering. Fresh tendon tissue was immersed in liquid nitrogen and grounded into powder. The tendon tissue was then deceullarized using trypsin/EDTA, DNase I and triton X-100 sequentially and was confirmed by absence of nucleic acid bands in agarose gel electrophoresis. The acelluarized matrix powder was then dissolved in acetic acid and formed a 3D scaffold by adding NaOH. Cell viability was tested, cell seeded on the acellularized matrix was less healthy than control. For the in vivo study, the transplanted GFP-TDSCs could be detected in the window wound at week 2 but not at week 4 in both the TDSC-Mock and TDSC-Scx groups. Ectopic mineralization was detected in some samples at week 8 but there was no difference among different groups. The GFP-TDSC-Scx group statistically significantly improved tendon repair histologically and biomechanically compared to the Scaffold-only group and the GFP-TDSC-Mock group at the early stage of tendon repair. There was significantly higher expression of collagen type I in the window wound in the GFP-TDSC-Scx group compared to the other two groups at week 2. We concluded that the transplantation of GFP-TDSC-Scx promoted healing at the early stage of tendon repair in a rat patellar tendon window injury model.

460710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460710.value: Our results showed that Scx transduction consistently increased the expressions of most tendon- and cartilage- related markers in TDSCs. However, its effect on the expressions of bone-related markers in TDSCs was inconclusive. The fate of TDSC-Scx should be further confirmed by the type of neo-tissue formed after transplantation using the nude mouse model. Further optimization of the acellularized tendon matrix is needed to enhance the healing outcome. The blasticidin selection of transduced TDSCs may be an issue for tissue engineering application as over 85% died during selection and TDSCs age with passaging. As the transplanted cells were seen in the window wound at week 2 but not at week 4 after transplantation, whether transient transduction using an adenoviral system would yield similar or better results compared to the stable transduction of Scx in the promotion of tendon repair needs further research. Ectopic mineralization was observed in some samples in all groups with no statistical significant difference among groups. However, the sample size in each group was small (n=6 per group for the GFP-TDSC-Mock group and GFP-TDSC-Scx group; n=3 for the Scaffold-only group). Further study with larger sample size is needed to confirm the effect of cell transplantation on ectopic mineralization in tendon.

460710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460710.value: Tendon injury is common in various physical activities. While healed, scar tissue is formed with ectopic mineralization observed in some cases. The biomechanical properties of the healing tissue are compromised, which account for the high re-tear rate of repaired tendon. The promotion of tenogenic differentiation of tendon-derived stem cells (TDSCs) prior to transplantation may promote better tendon repair. Our results showed that GDF-6 failed to increase the expression of tendon-related markers in TDSCs. However, Scx transduction consistently increased the expressions of most tendon- and cartilage- related markers in TDSCs. However, its effect on the expressions of bone-related markers in TDSCs was inconclusive. The transplantation of Scx tranduced TDSCs enhanced early stage of tendon repair in a rat patellar tendon window injury model as shown by histology and biomechanical test.

460910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
460910.value: This double-blind randomized trial aims to compare an alternative treatment (H2-receptor antagonist) with a standard strategy (proton pump inhibitor) for the prevention of ulcer bleeding associated with low-dose aspirin in patients with very high ulcer risk. Low-dose aspirin (ASA) is one of the most widely used drugs for secondary prevention of atherothrombotic diseases. However, ASA induces peptic ulcer bleeding that remains an important cause of hospitalization and death worldwide. In Hong Kong, we found that ASA use accounts for about one-third of all cases of peptic ulcer bleeding. ASA users with a history of ulcer bleeding are at the highest risk; up to 15% of these patients develop recurrent ulcer bleeding in one year when exposed to ASA again. Current guidelines recommend co-therapy with a proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) in ASA users with high ulcer risk. Among ASA users with prior ulcer bleeding who receive prophylactic PPI, we have shown in a double-blind randomized trial that the one-year incidence of recurrent ulcer bleeding was 0.7% only. However, there have been concerns about PPIs because of their costs, safety, and potentially serious drug interactions in patients with coronary artery disease (see Background). Recently, H2-receptor antagonists (H2RAs) have been advocated as alternative to PPIs for the prevention of peptic ulcers in ASA users. Comparing to PPIs, H2RAs are much cheaper and have minimal drug interactions in cardiac patients. Results of a recent endoscopic trial indicate that famotidine, a H2RA, reduces gastric injury associated with ASA. However, the efficacy of H2RAs is uncertain at least in the Chinese population. Limited local data suggest that H2RAs are inferior to PPIs in preventing ulcer bleeding associated with ASA. To date, there is no large-scale, clinical outcome trial comparing H2RAs with PPIs for the prevention of ulcer bleeding in high-risk ASA users. Despite the uncertain efficacy of H2RAs, our local health authority has already endorsed this class of drugs as an alternative to PPIs for ASA users with high ulcer risk. In this proposal, we hypothesize that PPIs are superior to H2RAs for the prevention of peptic ulcer bleeding in ASA users with prior ulcer bleeding. Unfortunately, this important clinical question is not a priority of pharmaceutical companies because the results may not favor their products. The outcome of this industry-independent clinical trial will encourage health authorities and international guideline committees to review their recommendations for ASA users with high risk of ulcer bleeding. 研究題目 在有高風險腸胃潰瘍出血的低劑量亞士匹靈服用者中，比較使用H2 受體拮抗劑 或特效制酸劑(PPI)於預防腸胃潰瘍出血的研究(ASP (PPI_H2RA) Study) 研究撮要 這是一項雙盲、隨機抽樣，目的是在有高風險腸胃潰瘍出血的低劑量亞士匹靈服 用者中，比較同時服用特效制酸劑或H2受體拮抗劑以預防消化道潰瘍出血復發 的研究。 低劑量亞士匹靈是最常用來作第二階段預防動脈血栓疾病的藥物。然而，亞士匹 靈仍然是全球性因腸胃潰瘍出血導致需要住院或死亡的主要原因。在香港，約有 三份之一腸胃潰瘍出血的患者都是服用亞士匹靈的。曾有腸胃潰瘍出血的亞士匹 靈服用者是十分高風險的，他們約有百份之十五於一年內有腸胃潰瘍出血復發。 根據現時醫學指引，建議患有高風險腸胃潰瘍出血的亞士匹靈服用者同時服用特 效制酸劑(PPI)。但是，特效制酸劑 (PPI)的費用昂貴、它的服用安全性和對於冠 狀動脈疾病的患者所服用的藥物有著潛在性嚴重的藥物相互作用已被受關注。 近年，亞士匹靈服用者被提倡服用H2 受體拮抗劑以替代特效制酸劑(PPI)來預防 腸胃潰瘍出血。雖然H2 受體拮抗劑比特效制酸劑的價錢便宜很多及對於心臟病 患者服用的藥物只有輕微的藥物相互作用，但是H2 受體拮抗劑的療效在中國人 中還沒有被確定。有限的數據顯示H2 受體拮抗劑對預防亞士匹靈導致腸胃潰瘍 出血的療效不及特效制酸劑(PPI)。直至現在，還沒有大規模以臨床成效作指標來 比較H2 受體拮抗劑和特效制酸劑(PPI)在亞士匹靈服用者中預防腸胃潰瘍出血的 試驗。 儘管H2受體拮抗劑的功效還是不明確，有些衛生管理機構已認可有高風險腸胃 潰瘍出血的低劑量亞士匹靈服用者，服用這類藥物以代替特效制酸劑(PPI)。在 這項研究，我們假設特效制酸劑比較H2受體拮抗劑能有效預防曾患潰瘍出血的 病人再度潰瘍出血。可惜，這臨床相關的問題並不是藥廠優先考慮的事擬，因為 臨床結果未必有利它們的產品。此項研究的結果可鼓勵衛生管理機構及國際指引 委員會可重新探討他們對有高風險腸胃潰瘍出血的低劑量亞士匹靈服用者已作 出的建議。

460910.label: Major findings and research outcome
460910.value: We screened 510 patients for patients using ASA and we enrolled 243 patients. Two hundred and forty three (n=243) patients were included in the intention to treat analysis: 123 were randomly assigned to rabeprazole group and 120 to famotidine group. The two treatment groups were similar in terms of demographic characteristics and baseline parameters. The rate of discontinuation of the medication were similar between the two groups: 23.6% (29/123) and 24.2% ( 29/120) in the rabeprazole and placebo groups respectively (Figure 1). Three patients died in the rabeprazole group and five patients died in the famotidine group. All the events were considered unrelated to the study medication. 94 patients in the rabeprazole group and 91 patients in the placebo group completed the study. There were a total of 21 cases of with symptoms of gastrointestinal bleeding evaluated by the adjudication committee. The committee identified 1 case in the rabeprazole group and 3 in the famotidine group that met the pre-specified criteria for recurrent upper gastrointestinal bleeding. In the intention-to-treat analysis (n=243), primary endpoint being was reached in 1 (0.8%) in the rabeprazole group compared with 3 (2.6%) in the famotidine group (log-rank test p=0.31 (figure 2)). When considering the composite endpoint, in the rabeprazole group, 1 patient had recurrent upper gastointestinal bleeding, 8 patients had asymptomatic endoscopic ulcers or multiple erosions (>=10 erosions), and 1 reported significant dyspepsia with normal endoscopic findings. In the famotidine group, 3 patients had recurrent upper gastointestinal bleeding, 9 had asymptomatic endoscopic ulcer or multiple erosions (>=10 erosions), and no patients reported severe dyspepsia. Eleven patients (8.9%) on rabeprazole and 6 (5.0%) on famotidine had lower gastrointestinal bleeding (p=0.23). Atherothrombotic events occurred in 5 patients (rabeprazole=2 (1.6%), famotidine=3 (2.5%); p=0.68). In the rabeprazole group, the types of atherothrombotic events included: acute coronary syndrome (n=1), transient ischemic attack (n=1). In the famotidine group the types of atherothrombotic events included: acute coronary syndrome (n=1), myocardial infarction (n=1), ischemic stroke (n=1). Out of the five patients who suffered an atherothrombotic event only one patient was taking dual antiplatelet therapy with clopidogrel and ASA. In conclusion, among ASA users with a history of ulcer bleeding, there was no meaningful difference between H2RA and PPI in the prevention of recurrent bleeding. H2RA may be considered as an alternative gastroprotective drug in high-risk ASA users such as those patients requiring dual anti-platelet therapy with ASA and clopidogrel.

460910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460910.value: Since the result showed that H2RA can be considered as an alternative gastroprotective drug in high-risk ASA users, we plan to establish an Asia Pacific Consensus Meeting in near future for the establishment of the guidelines of the widely use of H2RA in patients of regular use of ASA.

460910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460910.value: The usage of aspirin has increased worldwide, and it is now recognized as the one of the most common cause of ulcer bleeding from the upper digestive tract. In those patients presenting with ulcer bleeding, possible management options to reduce risk of recurrent bleeding include stopping aspirin or continuing its use with prophylactic medications. One of the proven prophylactic medications includes a stomach acid suppressing drug called proton pump inhibitor (PPI). But there has been concern of its interaction of with other blood thinning drugs (clopidogrel) and possible increase risk of heart attacks. One of the safer alternative drugs is Histamine-2 Receptor Antagonist (H2RA), yet few studies have investigated their effectiveness in prevention of ulcer bleeding in aspirin users. We conducted a randomized study comparing a proton pump inhibitor PPI (rabeprazole) with a H2RA (famotidine) for prevention of recurrent upper gastrointestinal bleeding in aspirin users with a history of ulcer bleeding. The results showed that in patients with a history of ulcer bleeding there was no meaningful difference between H2RA and PPI in the prevention of recurrent bleeding. This suggests that H2RA may be considered as an alternative drug option to prevent rebleeding in these patients.

462710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
462710.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third most common cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, with a gender prevalence observed in men. Recent studies have suggested that elevated activity of the androgen axis is one major host factor underlying this disparity between genders. The androgen receptor (AR) mediates function of androgens in vital developmental and oncogenic pathways by binding to genomic androgen-responsive elements, which influence the transcription of AR target genes. AR is over-expressed in over 70% of human HCC and decreasing levels of AR protein significantly inhibit HCC development and growth in model systems. However, AR-induced hepatocarcinogenesis is still poorly-understood because little is known about the identity and role of direct AR-dependent target genes in hepatocytes. Using chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by human promoter array analysis of AR-over-expressing HCC cell lines; our preliminary findings suggested a number of novel cell cycle-related genes that are likely under the direct modulation of AR. Cell cycle-related kinase (CCRK), previously shown to promote glioblastoma tumorigenesis, was found to be the most significant AR-bound target (p < 0.0001). CCRK was up-regulated by AR as shown by both ectopic expression and knockdown experiments; and was commonly over-expressed in primary HCC compared to the adjacent non-tumorous liver tissues (p < 0.0001). Ectopic over-expression of CCRK dramatically increased the ability of nontumorigenic hepatocytes to form colonies and attenuated the HCC growth inhibitory effect introduced by AR small interfering RNA. On contrary, down-regulation of CCRK significantly decreased HCC cell growth and counteracted the AR-induced hepatocellular growth. Based on these findings, we hypothesize that CCRK is an essential direct mediator of the AR-induced HCC cell growth and proliferation. In this application, we hence propose to dissect the transcriptional regulatory control of AR on CCRK in HCC cells. In addition, we will elucidate the oncogenic function of CCRK in liver tumorigenesis and determine its significance in relation to clinical outcome and pathological features of primary HCCs. The long term goal of our project is to elucidate the direct AR-dependent target genes and define their pathobiological significance in human HCC. Due to the potential systemic effects of AR modulation on androgen-responsive tissues, it would be more clinically relevant to determine the critical AR-dependent effectors in HCC as they may represent potential molecular targets for development of therapeutic interventions. 462710.label: Realisation of objectives
462710.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the fifth most common cancer and the third most frequent cause of cancer deaths worldwide, occurs mainly in men. HBV is the most important etiologic factor, accounting for most of HCC cases in the developing countries including China. The risk of HCC is greatly increased in chronic viral carriers of the male sex, suggesting that sex steroid hormones contribute to the development of HCC. Previous studies have shown the importance of androgen receptor (AR) signaling in hepatocarcinogenesis, but the molecular mechanisms remained unclear. Our preliminary findings in the proposal have shown that AR can up-regulate cell cycle-related kinase (CCRK), the latest member of the cyclin-dependent kinase family, in HCC cells. To elucidate the upstream mechanisms that underlie the expression of CCRK in HCC (Objective 1), we have employed chromatin immunoprecipitation, luciferase-reporter assays, site-directed mutagenesis, co-immunoprecipitation and expression analyses in both ectopic expression and knockdown approaches. We have elucidated the transcriptional regulation of CCRK by ligand-activated AR and its co-activator, the polycomb protein enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2), in human liver and HCC cells. Moreover, we have investigated the role of a viral oncoprotein HBV X protein (HBx) in CCRK up-regulation in viral-associated HCC. We further delineated the functional properties and biological pathway by which CCRK modulates HCC development (Objective 2). Functional analyses including cell cycle analysis, cell proliferation, colony formation and soft agar assays as well as xenograft and orthotopic models have been employed in both ectopic expression and knockdown experimental settings. We also elucidated the signaling pathways involved in CCRK-mediated oncogenicity using immunofluorescence, expression analysis, in vitro and in vivo rescue experiments. To investigate the role of CCRK with HCC characteristics (Objective 3), we have examined the expressions of CCRK, its regulators and downstream signaling components in primary paired HCC and non-tumor tissues using Western blot and immunohistochemistry and correlated their expressions with clinical outcome and pathological features. In summary, we have achieved all the project objectives. Using the aforementioned methodology, we have delineated the mechanistic and functional significance of AR/CCRK signaling in HCC.

462710.label: Major findings and research outcome
462710.value: Our integrated approach in this project showed for the first time that the direct AR transcriptional target gene CCRK plays a critical role in hepatocarcinogenesis. We demonstrated that CCRK mediates AR-induced cell cycle progression, cellular proliferation, and malignant transformation. CCRK expression in immortal liver cells induced focus formation, anchorage-independent growth, and tumor formation in immunodeficient mice, whereas CCRK knockdown in HCC cells reduced G1/S phase progression, focus formation, and tumorigenicity, demonstrating the strong oncogenic capacity of CCRK in HCC. Our findings further demonstrated that CCRK activated β-catenin/T-cell factor (TCF) signaling through direct phosphorylation of GSK-3β. The functional link between CCRK and β-catenin/TCF signaling was further demonstrated in vitro and in vivo, where silencing of β-catenin in CCRK-expressing cells reduced active β-catenin levels and significantly attenuated cell proliferation and tumorigenicity in both the xenograft and orthotopic models. Therefore, CCRK connects the AR and β-catenin/TCF cascades and provides a mechanistic basis for the aberrant β-catenin activation in human HCCs (Feng et al., J Clin Invest 2011; AACR 102nd annual meeting 2011). HBx is a promiscuous transactivator that cooperates with AR signaling to increase viral load, which is believed to be a mechanism for sex disparity in chronic hepatitis B. Our present findings revealed that HBx induces CCRK expression in an AR-dependent manner. Moreover, CCRK mediates the HBx-AR signaling to form a viral-host oncogenic circuitry that induces hepatocellular proliferation and transformation. Targeting inhibition of CCRK perturbs the CCRK/GSK-3β/β-catenin/TCF/AR regulatory loop to suppress hepatocarcinogenesis in an HBx transgenic HCC model (Yu et al., Gut 2014; Cheng et al., AACR 105th annual meeting 2014). Interestingly, we found that the expression levels of the CCRK/GSK-3β/β-catenin/AR loop in both tumour and adjacent liver tissues of male patients are significantly higher than those of the female patients. These findings extend our previous observation that CCRK is overexpressed in human HCC tissues. The male-predominant elevation patterns indicate that cooperation among transcriptional regulators orchestrates gene expression program in male hepatocarcinogenesis. More importantly, hyperactivation of this new regulatory loop in HBV-associated HCC tissues correlates with poor prognosis of patients, highlighting the clinical significance of our findings (Feng et al., J Clin Invest 2011; Yu et al., Gut 2014). Finally, in two review papers, we have summarized the transcriptional and epigenetic control in HCC and depicted the importance of the novel AR/CCRK signaling pathway in hepatocarcinogenesis (Tian et al., Semin Cancer Biol 2013; Yu and Cheng, Curr Pharm Des 2013).

462710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
462710.value: Based on our identification of the AR-activated oncogenic functions of CCRK in HCC through up-regulation of β-catenin signaling, the novel AR-CCRK-β-catenin axis may represent a major molecular mechanism that drives and maintains the aggressive growth of HCC. By identifying and applying small molecule inhibitors specific to CCRK, there is reasonable potential to interrupt the critical molecular signaling between the initiator AR and the effector β-catenin, and thereby attenuate the consequential HCC development and progression. In this regard, we have developed a high-throughput kinase assay for library screening of small molecules that can abrogate CCRK kinase activity. This high-throughput assay can be complemented with computational virtual screening to identify and verify the specificity of the screened compounds. In the current project, we have demonstrated the significance of AR/CCRK signaling in HBV-associated HCC. Recent epidemiological studies showed that obesity and type 2 diabetes can elevate the incidence of HCC. Since the risk of HCC is greatly increased in obese subjects of the male sex, further study is warranted to investigate the role of AR/CCRK signaling in obesity-associated hepatocarcinogenesis. The high-fat high-carbohydrate dietary and leptin receptor-deficient genetic obesity-promoted HCC models will be very useful for this investigation.

462710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
462710.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the fifth most common cancer worldwide. It is more prevalent in men than women. Related to this, recent genetic studies have revealed a causal role for androgen receptor (AR) in hepatocarcinogenesis, but the underlying molecular mechanism remains unclear. In this project, we used genome-wide location and functional analyses to identify a critical mediator of AR signaling — cell cycle–related kinase (CCRK) — that drives hepatocarcinogenesis via a signaling pathway dependent on β-catenin and T-cell factor (TCF). Functional analyses showed that CCRK was critical in human cell lines for AR-induced cell cycle progression, hepatocellular proliferation, and malignant transformation. Ectopic expression of CCRK in immortalized human liver cells activated β-catenin/TCF signaling to stimulate cell cycle progression and to induce tumor formation, as shown in both xenograft and orthotopic models. In primary human HBV-associated HCC tissues, AR, CCRK, and β-catenin were concordantly overexpressed in the tumor cells. Furthermore, hyperactivation of this regulatory loop correlated with the tumor staging and poor overall survival of patients. In conclusion, our study reveals a novel AR-CCRK–β-catenin–positive regulatory circuit; disruption of which may be highly relevant to the design of therapeutic interventions in HCC and potentially the other male-predominant cancers.

462810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
462810.value: Male fertility is a complex and subtly orchestrated process. Spermatozoa produced by the testis during spermatogenesis are immature and are incapable of undergoing fertilization. They acquire their motility and fertilizing capacity during their passage through the lumen of the epididymis in a process known as spermiogenesis. Normal testicular function is dependent upon hormones acting through endocrine and paracrine pathways. Hormones such as testosterone, follicle stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone are key regulators in deciding germ cell fate. In addition, evidence now indicates the importance of estrogen in sperm maturation by affecting epididymal function. The G protein-coupled receptor 30 (GPR30) is a newly characterized membrane-bound estrogen receptor capable of mediating both the rapid responses and transcriptional events of estrogen. But whether GPR30 is involved in mediating the actions of estrogen on male reproduction is not known. In our preliminary studies we have identified the expression of GPR30 in the rat caudal epididymal epithelium at both the mRNA and protein levels. Moreover, in primary culture of caudal epididymal epithelial cells, we have demonstrated that the GPR30-specific agonist G1 stimulates a sustained chloride ion conductance. Based on these initial findings obtained by us so far, we propose the following hypothesis: that the action of estrogen on male reproduction is at least in part mediated through GPR30 by regulating caudal epididymal secretory functions during spermiogenesis. This proposal describes the initial studies that we have performed to reach this hypothesis. More importantly, this proposal describes a series of logically designed experiments to substantiate this hypothesis. We aim at achieving the following objectives: (1) to clearly define where the receptors are located in the rat epididymis and to study their gene expression at different developmental stages of the rat. (2) To find out what intracellular second messengers are involved in the stimulation of chloride ion conductance through activation of this receptor. (3) To employ pharmacological agents and RNA interference techniques to prove that the endogenous estrogen really acts through this receptor in the epididymis to trigger the observed events. The successful accomplishment of this project will contribute towards understanding the physiological significance of this receptor in male reproduction. In the long run, such information will be useful for the design of approaches in the manipulation of male fertility in health and in disease. 男性生殖是一個復雜而又受到精密調控的過程。在精子發生過程中睪丸所產生的精子是不成熟的，所以不能受精。精子在附睪管腔中獲得活力和受精能力的過程稱為精子形成。正常精巢功能的運行依賴於激素內分泌和旁分泌的調節。睪酮、促卵泡刺激素和促黃體生成素在生殖細胞命運決定中起重要作用。此外，現有證據表明雌激素通過影響附睪的功能而在精子的成熟過程中取重要作用。GPR30是一種新發現的雌激素膜受體，它能夠介導雌激素的快速效應和基因組效應。但是，GPR30在雌激素對男性生殖調控過程中的作用還不清楚。我們的初步研究結果表明，GPR30的mRNA和蛋白都在大鼠的附睪上皮中表達。在原代培養的附睪上皮細胞，我們發現GPR30受體特異激動劑 G1能夠刺激氯離子通道的持續開放。根據以上結果，我們提出以下假設：在精子形成過程中，雌激素對男性生殖的影響至少部分是通過GPR30調節附睪的分泌的作用來實現的。這項申請書闡述了我們提出這個假設的研究基礎及進一步驗證這個假設的實驗計劃。我們擬實現以下研究目標：（1）明確GPR30在大鼠附睪中的表達定位並研究它在大鼠不同發育階段的表達情況。 （2）闡明GPR30激活氯離子通道的信號通路。 （3）利用RNA幹擾技術來研究內源性雌激素是否通過作用於附睪中的GPR30來引起以上觀察到的現象。順利完成該項目將有助於了解GPR30在男性生殖中的生理意義。從長遠來看，這些結果將對男性生育的健康有積極意義。

462810.label: Realisation of objectives
462810.value: All the project objectives have been addressed. In summary, the following studies have been performed: 1. Primary culture of rat caput epididymal epithelium was established. This can only be achieved in epididymis obtained from rats of a particular age (about 5 weeks old). The reason is that when the rats are too young, the epididymis has not reached a sizeable organ for dissection and cell isolation. On the other hand, when sperms begin to appear in the male reproductive system, the swimming sperms would disturb the adherence of the epithelium. Therefore parallel studies on different developmental stages of the rats could not be performed. 2. Immunofluorescence staining of marker and target genes in the primary culture of caput epi-didymal epithelium was established. 3. Measurement of intracellular pH and extracellular pH was established on our primary culture system using a fluorescent pH sensitive probe and a sparklet pH electrode to explore the functional roles of the cultured epididymal cells. 4. Measurement of intracellular calcium was established on our primary culture system using the fluorescent dye Fluo-3 and recorded on a laser scanning confocal imaging system. 5. Expression of G protein-coupled receptor 30 (GPR30) in the epididymal epithelium was investigated by RT-PCR, immunofluorescence and Western analyses. Measurement of short-circuit current was established on our primary cultured epididymal epithelium. Assessment of cAMP level upon activation of GPR30 and perturbation of the intracellular cAMP concentration by pharmacological agents was performed. In addition, the in vivo action of GPR30 in affecting epididymis morphology, function and sperm motility was performed. However, in vivo receptor knockdown by lentivirus was not successful. This could be due to the lenti titre not reaching a high enough value and also to the low knockdown efficiency.
