462810.label: Major findings and research outcome
462810.value: 1. The biological functionality of our primary epididymal epithelium culture system was demonstrated by the regulation of intracellular and apical pH by sodium coupled bicarbonate influx (see item 1 in Part C of this report). 2. The significance of intracellular calcium as a second messenger in regulating epididymal function was demonstrated (see item 2 in Part C of this report). 3. The functional role of G protein-coupled receptor 30 (GPR30) in the epididymis was demonstrated. GPR30 is expressed in the epithelium of the rat epididymis and is involved in chloride secretion into the epididymis lumen. Activation of GPR30 by its specific agonist G1 induced a mono-phasic short-circuit current increase. On the other hand, G15, the specific antagonist of GPR30, could completely inhibit the current induced by G1. The G1-induced current was largely blocked by the non-specific chloride channel inhibitor diphenylamine-dicarboxylic acid as well as by the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator CFTRinh-172, suggesting that the current was mainly mediated through CFTR. This activation of CFTR by stimulation of GPR30 by G1 was demonstrated to act through the cAMP signal pathway. Upon administration of G15 to rats in vivo, the osmotic pressure of the micro perfusion solution from the epididymis increased and the motility of the sperms decreased. The significance of GPR30 in the formation of the epididymis fluid micro-environment thus affecting sperm motility was demonstrated in our in vitro and in vivo studies.

462810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
462810.value: 1. We have demonstrated that sodium coupled bicarbonate influx exists in the epididymal epithelium and acts by regulating the intracellular pH of the epididymal epithelium as well as modulating the epididymal luminal microenvironment. Our present work in this aspect only focuses on in vitro studies and subsequent demonstration of its in vivo significance is highly warranted. 2. Calcium ion influx is vital for many cellular processes including secretory functions. The mechanism of calcium ion influx in the male reproductive tract especially in the epididymal cells is still unclear. Our studies have demonstrated the existence of store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) in the epididymal basal cells and its relationship with intracellular tyrosine phosphorylation. But how this calcium entry is linked to ion secretion and its physiological significance awaits further elucidation. 3. We have demonstrated the existence of GPR30 in the epididymal epithelium and its involvement in regulating chloride ion transport into the epididymal lumen. Our in vivo data also provided support for its physiological significance in the formation of a suitable fluid micro-environment in affecting sperm motility. Apart from publishing this observation, further in vitro and in vivo gene knockdown studies to substantiate the phenomenon is highly warranted.

462810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
462810.value: After their generation in the testis, the sperms enter the tract of the epididymis and therein complete the maturation process. The epididymal epithelium creates the necessary environment in the epididymal tract including the reabsorption of the majority of the testis fluid and sodium ions, secretion of potassium and chloride ions as well as acidification of the microenvironment. This maturation process is essential for the sperms to obtain the capability of approaching the eggs and fertility. This project has established the requisite platform for the detailed analysis of this process by successfully culturing epithelium cells obtained from the rat epididymis. In addition, we have demonstrated how the intracellular acidity of the epididymal epithelium can be regulated so as to modulate the epididymal luminal microenvironment. We have also demonstrated how calcium ions can enter the epididymal cells. Moreover, we have categorically demonstrated not only the existence but the physiological significance of a G protein-coupled receptor in the epididymal epithelium in affecting sperm function by regulating chloride ion transport into the epididymal lumen.

463410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
463410.value: Respiratory diseases, particularly pneumonia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, tuberculosis and lung cancer, are four of the top ten causes of death worldwide. In Hong Kong, according to statistics in 2007, respiratory conditions accounted for 7% of all hospitalisations and were the third and fifth leading causes of death. The respiratory system is also the major site whose function is compromised due to infections by the newly emerged pathogens such as the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus and H1N1 influenza which Hong Kong and many communities in the world had or has been combating. Despite the clinical significance of respiratory diseases, thus far, there has been a paucity of blood biomarkers generic to the respiratory system that would allow an objective assessment of disease burden. Our group has a long-standing track record in plasma nucleic acids research. We have successfully developed organ or disease-specific plasma DNA and RNA markers that are derived from the placenta of a fetus, various tumours, transplanted organs and liver for the non-invasive assessment and management of pregnancy, malignancy, organ transplantation and liver pathologies. In this project, we aim to apply our experience to develop lung-derived RNA transcripts in human plasma as indicators of lung damage for baseline investigation of patients suspected of diseases of the lower respiratory track. Our proposed approach is different from the strategies currently taken by other researchers for developing blood biomarkers for the respiratory system. We have already generated preliminary data to show that a lung-expressed RNA transcript is detectable in human plasma. The research objectives include: 1. To confirm the lung origin of the identified plasma RNA transcript. 2. To assess if quantitative aberrations of the lung-expressed plasma RNA transcript are associated with pathologies of the lower respiratory tract. 3. To evaluate the utility of the detection and quantification of the lung-expressed plasma RNA transcript for the clinical assessment of diseases of the lower respiratory tract. The successful achievement of the research goals may result in the availability of blood tests that allow the generic assessment of lung function and pathologies for the diagnosis, monitoring or prognostication of respiratory diseases. 呼吸系統疾病，特別是肺炎，慢性阻塞性肺疾病、 結核病和肺癌，是全球致死的十大疾病的其中四項。 香港在 2007 年的統計數字顯示呼吸道疾病占所有入院個案 的 7%，是排第三和第五的主要死亡原因。 呼吸道系統也是受到新興病原體打擊的主要器官。 儘管呼吸系統疾病的臨床重要性，至今為止仍缺乏在血液內探測到的相關生物標誌物。這些標誌物可用作有關疾病的客觀評估。 我們的研究組在循環核酸課題中發表了很多文章。 我們已成功研發不同器官或特定疾病的血漿 DNA 和 RNA 標記。標記可用作胎兒、 妊娠、各種惡性腫瘤、 移植器官和肝病的無創評估肝。 在現提出的研究專案中，我們針對利用肺部表示的RNA發展與肺部損害有關的指標。 研究的目標包括： 1. 以確定血漿 RNA標誌物是源宇肺部的。 2. 以評估血漿肺部RNA標誌物的量化與呼吸道病症的相關聯。 3. 以證實血漿肺部RNA標誌物的量化為肺病症作臨床評估的價值。 研究目標的成功實現可能會允許利用血液測試作肺病症診斷、 監測或預測。

463410.label: Realisation of objectives
463410.value: As described in the previous progress report, by studying plasma samples collected from lung or bone marrow transplantation recipients, we have confirmed the lung origin of plasma SFTPC and SFTPA2 mRNA (i.e. objective 1 achieved). We have also presented data in the previous progress report to show that SFTPC and SFTPA2 mRNA were elevated in plasma of patients with lung pathologies (community-acquired pneumonia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer) when compared with healthy controls (i.e. objectives 2 and 3 achieved). We have recruited and collected plasma samples from smokers and non-smokers with no apparent lung pathologies (objective 4 achieved). We did attempt to address objective 5. However, the data showed that both SFTPC and SFTPA2 mRNA had a low dynamic range in plasma even among individuals with lung pathologies. We observed that a proportion of cases had undetectable amounts of plasma SFTPC and SFTPA2. We further observed that there is much overlap in levels of the two plasma mRNA markers between subjects with or without lung pathologies. Thus, we concluded that plasma SFTPC and SFTPA2 mRNA were unlikely to serve as optimal markers to monitor disease progression and predict prognosis. On the other hand, massively parallel sequencing have emerged as a powerful tool for the development of molecular diagnostics. We therefore applied sequencing to directly study the profile of mRNA species in plasma of two pairs of patients with and without community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Interestingly, among transcripts that were statistically significantly different in the CAP and control plasma samples, there were two lung-expressed transcripts, ras-related protein Rab-39B (RAB39B) and Interferon, alpha-inducible protein 6 (IFI6). A summary of these data is appended with this report. We believe that these data will offer a new avenue to develop effective biomarkers for the non-invasive assessment of lung pathologies. These data are appended in Part C.

463410.label: Major findings and research outcome
463410.value: We have confirmed that SFTPC and SFTPA2 mRNA are detectable in human plasma. With the use of samples from lung-transplant recipients and bone marrow transplant recipients, we proved that they are lung-derived. We showed that their concentrations are generally elevated in patients with lung pathologies than healthy controls. However, due to their low dynamic range in plasma, they do not appear to be the optimal biomarkers for the monitoring and prognostication of lung pathologies. We have presented these data at the Human Genomic Meeting 2013 in Singapore. We are also in the process of preparing the manuscript for submission. However, to continue to pursue the goal of developing effective biomarkers for the non-invasive assessment of lung pathologies, we adopted the new state-of-the-art approach, massively parallel sequencing, to compare the plasma RNA profiles of patients with community-acquired pneumonia and controls. Interestingly, we have identified a list of genes that are significantly different in plasma of the patients.

463410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
463410.value: The list of genes with high abundance in plasma of CAP patients as detected by massively parallel sequencing is a valuable resource for the development of biomarkers for CAP assessment. The approach adopted in this study also serves as useful reference to other researchers attempting to develop blood-based biomarkers for other bodily organs. Lastly, the project team will continue to use the sequencing approach to develop biomarkers for lung cancer as part of a Theme-based research scheme project (T12-404/11) (see Part C of this report).

463410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
463410.value: Respiratory diseases, particularly pneumonia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, tuberculosis and lung cancer, are four of the top ten causes of death worldwide. In Hong Kong, according to statistics in 2007, respiratory conditions accounted for 7% of all hospitalisations and were the third and fifth leading causes of death.Despite the clinical significance of respiratory diseases, thus far, there has been a paucity of blood biomarkers generic to the respiratory system that would allow an objective assessment of disease burden. In this study, we aimed to identify genes that are specifically expressed by lung tissues and detectable in blood plasma. We have successfully identified a list of such genes. These candidate markers have the potential to be developed into blood tests for the detection, monitoring and assessment of lung diseases.

463410.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
463410.value: The experience that we have gained in this project helped to formulate some of the research plans described in the Theme-based research scheme (TRS) project, titled "Massively parallel sequencing of plasma nucleic acids for the molecular diagnostics of cancer (project #: T12-404/11)". The PI of this GRF grant is the Deputy Project Coordinator of the TRS grant. One of the goals of the TRS project was to exploit the detection of plasma RNA as a means to detect cancers, including lung cancer. Based on our experience derived from the present GRF project with SFTPC and SFTPA2 mRNA detection in plasma, we realised that the well-characterised lung-specific mRNA targets did not have adequate dynamic range for robust detection in human plasma. Furthermore, in this GRF project, we performed massively parallel sequencing on plasma of patients with and without lung diseases and was able to detect lung-expressed mRNA species. These data encouraged us to propose the use of sequencing to assess the plasma transcriptome of cancer patients. Lastly, we believe that the sequencing data generated in this GRF project would be useful as the baseline data for comparison with data obtained from cancer patients.

463710.label: Project Title(Chinese)
463710.value: 多发畸形而核型正常的胎儿染色体拷贝数变异的检测和结果分析

463710.label: Co - Investigator(s)
463710.value: Prof Lau, Tze Kin Dr Lee, Charles Prof Wang, Chi-chiu

463710.label: Project Objectives
463710.value: Aim 1: Generation of genome-wide CNV data from a well-defined population cohort of Chinese. We will generate normative CNV data from a homogenous cohort of Chinese individuals. Specifically, germline DNA will be isolated from blood obtained from 500 normal healthy un-related individuals age over 60 years-old. Their DNA will then be used to generate CNV data from the Agilent genome arrays which consist of a CNV-focused catalog array of 1 million features for CNV detection. We have already in place a well-established sample operating procedure to carry out this study. Aim 2: Identification of CNVs associated with fetal multiple alformations. The working hypothesis of this aim is that high resolution array CGH platforms will detect micro-chromosome aberrations such as CNVs, which are one of the major factors contributing to fetal malformations. Accordingly, we have already collect 300 study trios including parental DNA and prenatal samples (amniotic fluid, chorionic villus or fetal blood) from fetuses focused on 3 major malformations (high NT; congenital heart defects (CHD) without syndromic malformations; and congenital diaphragmatic hernia). We aim at identify pathogenic CNVs associated with congenital malformations by comparison to the data generated in Aim 1. The Agilent data that we generate will be assessed for quality before any further analyses are performed by using Agilent QC metrics for signal intensity, CNV calls, and inter and intra array variation. Aim 3: Validation of fetal malformations associated CNVs for genotype-phenotype correlations. The working hypothesis of this aim is that CNVs that are found to be strongly associated with fetal malformations in Aim 2 can be validated using independent measures. To accomplish this we will use a real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) assays as well as direct sequencing to confirm the DNA copy number of the pathogenically relevant CNVs. We will prioritize to confirm the pathogenic CNV with similar phenotype and plan to validate the phenotype-genotype correlations with a replicated disease group from another population using qPCR. Aim 4:Construct a Database: to allow data sharing, which will broaden our understanding of genetic-based clinical syndromes.

463710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
463710.value: 染色体拷贝数变异(CNVs)，即超过1kbDNA序列的增加或者丢失，在正常个体的基因组中普遍存在。病理性的CNVs不仅与出生缺陷及肿瘤有关，还与出生后神经发育异常或成人神经退行性疾病有关。不幸的是，对大多数CNVs的表型认识不足导致许多CNVs仅被作为临床意义不明的基因组失衡改变。利用本实验室的Agilent 微阵列比较基因组杂交技术(array CGH) ，我们发现在华人中CNVs常见变异、分布以及频率与国际基因组多态性数据库有明显不同。该全基因组研究数据高度提示本地华人与欧洲人群的CNVs谱有所不同。对华人种群CNVs知识的缺乏限制了医生及病人 对CNVs临床意义的认知。.因此许多CNVs目前被定性为临床意义不明的基因组失衡改变，难以区分病理性CNVs与正常的多态性。因此我们计划对比当地华人种群中生殖细胞与多发畸形的胎儿细胞的CNVs的特点。利用Agilent 的arrayCGH平台全面绘制本地人群CNVs谱，并通过实时定量PCR及测序技术，绘制图谱并估计所识别的CNVs位置及频率，分析其与疾病状态、临床表现的相关性。我们相信对华人种群CNVs的研究与其他种群的研究对全面了解CNV生物学意义具有同样的重要性，有助于辨认与胎儿畸形相关的病理性CNVs。该研究将为遗传咨询以及产前诊断提供帮助。

463710.label: Major findings and research outcome
463710.value: 1. Investigation of the presence of chromosomal copy number variants (CNVs) among our Chinese samples (500 normal healthy un-related individuals age over 60 years-old) revealed a spectrum an frequency difference between local Chinese and Caucasian reported. This data has being reported in one publication ( Zhu H et al., Am J Hum Genet. 2011). 2. We have successfully obtained a good number of prenatal samples (amniotic fluid, chorionic villus or fetal blood) from fetuses focused on 3 major malformations (high NT ); congenital heart defects (CHD) without syndromic malformations ; and congenital diaphragmatic hernia for array CGH analysis. We reported a high incident of pathogenic CNVs among fetus with structural anomalies (Leung TY et al., UOG 2011; Hung et al UOG 2014). We also demonstrate the feasibility of obtaining additional genomic information using aCGH including the first identification of Mowat Wilson syndromes ( Choy KW et al., Obstet Gynecol. 2010; Yan Z et al Prenat Diagn. 2014) and Optiz syndrome (Cheng Y et al., Clin Chim Acta. 2014). 3. We have developed a database of CNVs identified by array CGH analysis in our local population. Relevant clinical-pathological data have been uploaded to public database such as DECIPHER (http://decipher.sanger.ac.uk/)

463710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
463710.value: Those prenatal case with ultrasound structural malformations but normal aCGH and karyotype result are of interest to preform whole exome sequencing to study the presence of genetic variants that might contributed to the pathogenesis.

463710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
463710.value: With advances in molecular-based techniques, several genome-wide screening platforms based on microarray technologies have been developed, enabling the detection of submicroscopic deletions or duplications in segments as small as tens to hundreds of kilobases (kb) in size, which is well below the level of discrimination by conventional G-banded karyotype analysis. At present, arrayCGH is rapidly becoming the method of choice to detect very small chromosomal imbalances associated with postnatal syndromic malformations. By applying arrayCGH in prenatal cases with ultrasound abnormalities and normal karyotype result, we detected an extra 5.6% abnormal chromosomal copy number variant (CNV) among karyotyping normal prenatal cases. The disease causing CNVs detection rate increased to 15.4% among case with ultra-sound detected congenital abnormalities. Compared to conventional karyotype, arrayCGH significantly increases the diagnostic yield of fetuses carrying structural malformations.

463810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
463810.value: The Thoracotremata Guinot, 1977 are defined as those eubrachyuran crabs in which male sexual openings are located on the sternum, as opposed to the fifth pereiopod coxa (Heterotremata). Over the last two decades, this classification has gradually replaced earlier subdivisions of the Brachyura and has found additional support in sperm morphology and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) based molecular phylogenetics. Consequently, the Thoracotremata and Heterotremata have been adopted as subsections within the Eubrachyura in most recent revisions of the Brachyura. According to the current classification, the Thoracotremata are composed of four superfamilies, viz. Cryptochiroidea (gall crabs), Grapsoidea (rock crabs), Ocypodoidea (sand crabs) and Pinnotheroidea (pea crabs). However, in the recent literature, there is growing evidence that these superfamilies are not reciprocally monophyletic and that morphological convergences may be more frequent than the current taxonomy reflects. The phylogeny of Thoracotremata becomes especially interesting considering the incredibly diverse life histories and ecological adaptations that have evolved within this relatively young taxon, with living representatives occurring in a wide diversity of habitats, from hydrothermal vents, on turtles, encrusted in reefs, in all types of littoral habitats, forming symbiotic associations with many marine taxa, in land and freshwater, as well as colonizing pitcher plants and bromeliads. In this sense, the Thoracotremata can be regarded as the most diversified and thus successful taxon within the Brachyura, if not the Crustacea. It is therefore of special interest to reconstruct the origin and evolutionary history (phylogeny) of this taxon and calculate the age of this radiation as a contribution to understanding the processes driving biological diversification, as postulated by Darwin 150 years ago. So far all the evidence is based on morphology (adult and larval) and on mtDNA, but both by itself and combined are insufficient to unravel the entire history of this group, which predates the resolution optimum of mtDNA and is influenced by morphological convergence as mentioned above. The use of nuclear protein-coding genes as recently established molecular markers seems to be the most feasible approach to solve this striking lack of knowledge. These markers have recently been applied with great success for phylogenetic reconstruction of other decapod taxa, and their inclusion and combined evaluation with the already established mtDNA markers promises rich dividends for resolving thoracotreme phylogeny. It is here proposed and described, how this can be achieved during a three year project, involving three internationally recognized groups contributing their specialized knowledge and field of expertise. 胸孔亞派（Thoracotremata Guinot, 1977）被定義為真蟹派一類雄性個體生殖孔著生於胸板，而不是第五胸肢基節（如異孔亞派Heterotremata）的短尾類蟹類。在過去的20年，這一分類模式逐漸代替了早期的短尾蟹類的分類方法，並且得到了其他的基於分子系統學方面的資料支援，如精子形態和線粒體DNA。因此，在最新的短尾類分類學修訂中，胸孔亞派和異孔亞派被接受為真蟹派階元下的亞派。根據現在的分類系統，胸孔亞派包括4個總科，即隱螯蟹總科（Cryptochiroidea），方蟹總科（Grapsoidea岩蟹），沙蟹總科（Ocypodoidea）和豆蟹總科（Pinnotheroidea）。然而，在最近的文獻中，越來越多的證據顯示這些總科並不是相互單系起源的，而形態上的趨同可能比目前分類系統所反映的更加頻繁。胸孔亞派的蟹類可以在相當廣泛的棲息環境中發現，從深海熱泉噴口，到海龜身上，珊瑚礁內，任何沿海的棲息地，和許多海洋生物共生，陸地和淡水中，甚至在囊葉植物和鳳梨科植物上，考慮到這一年輕的類群已進化出如此非常豐富多樣的生活史和生態適應性，胸孔亞派的系統發育研究變得尤為有趣。在這個意義上來說，胸孔亞派可被視為甲殼動物，至少是短尾類中最多樣化和最成功的類群，因此，重建本分類單元的起源和進化史，以及估算其輻射年齡，將幫助我們理解達爾文150年前所提出的促進生物多樣化的發展過程。到目前為止，所有的證據都是來自于形態（成體和幼體）和線粒體基因，但兩者的單獨或者結合分析都不足以解構這個類群的完整歷史，因為胸孔亞派的分化遠早於線粒體基因最佳解析時序，而形態分析又受上述所說的形態趨同性的影響。使用我們最近發展出的細胞核蛋白編碼基因序列分子標記似乎是最可行的解決方法。這些標記最近被非常成功的應用於重建其他十足目類群的系統發育，將這些分子標記與已經建立的線粒體基因標記進行綜合評估，對解決胸孔亞派內的親緣關係提供了一個可靠的途徑。所以，在此我們提出並闡明，如何在這一個由三個國際專業單位合作，歷時三年的專案中達到這一目的。

463810.label: Realisation of objectives
463810.value: Objective 1. A robust phylogeny of Thoracotremata in relation to other groups of Brachyura has been constructed using six nuclear protein-coding genes and two mitochondrial rRNA genes. The analysis includes 140 crab species belonging to 58 families, and represents the most comprehensive molecular phylogenetic analysis of Brachyura to date. We also focused on the relationships within Thoracotremata and reconstruct its phylogeny based on ~100 species from 16 families (out of 18). In particular, we also elucidate the phylogeny the family Grapsidae based on an analysis of 40 species. Part of the funding was also used to complete phylogenetic analysis of two other groups of decapod crustaceans we worked on, namely Anomura and Linuparus. Objective 2: Based on the results of the molecular phylogenetic analysis, we conclude that most of the currently defined superfamilies of Thoracotremata, and Brachyura in general, are not monophyletic and thus not natural groupings in taxonomy. Thus the revision of the classification scheme is much more extensive than we anticipated before. Such a revision is now undertaken by the two taxonomists who are co-investigators of this project. Objectives 3: The molecular phylogenetic analysis indicates that morphological convergence is prevalent in Thoracotremata. Thus, the morphological analysis guided by the results from molecular analysis would be a lengthy process, as many morphological features need to be re-examined in details and new morphological features have to be sought. Such an extensive morphological analysis is in progress but beyond the scope of this three-year project.

463810.label: Major findings and research outcome
463810.value: We reconstructed the most comprehensive phylogeny of Brachyura to date using DNA sequence data of two mitochondrial rRNA genes and six nuclear protein-coding genes from more than 140 species belonging to 58 families (Tsang et al., 2014). The phylogenetic tree confirms that the target group Thoracotremata is monophyletic and the sister group to the other major section, the Heterotremata. The two form the Eubrachyura with the lower crabs (Podotremata) being paraphyletic. We found that freshwater crabs were derived early in the evolution of Eubrachyura and have at least two independent origins. The freshwater crabs separated from their closest marine sister taxa ~135 million years ago (Mya), that is, after the break-up of Pangaea (~200 Mya) and that a Gondwanan origin of these freshwater representatives is untenable. Most extant families and superfamilies of Brachyura arose during the late Cretaceous and early Tertiary. Within the Thoracotremata, the inferred gene trees strongly falsify the monophyly of the two major superfamilies, Ocypodoidea and Grapsoidea, indicating the prevalence of morphological convergence (Tsang et al., in prep). However, the lack of resolution among deeper branches concerning many interfamilial relationships and the divergence time estimate suggest rapid diversification of major groups of thoracotremes in a relatively short period of time through adaptive radiation to different ecological niches. Moreover, substantial rearrangements in subfamily and generic composition are necessary in order to keep the classification in line with the evolutionary history of the thoracotremes as reflected by the present analyses. For example, the polyphyly of the genus Pachygrapsus was observed, as members from this genus are dispersed throughout our gene tree (Ip et al., submitted). Grapsus and Planes were shown to be paraphyletic with species of Pachygrapsus nested within. As stated above, we also completed the molecular phylogenetic analysis of two other groups of decapod crustaceans, the Anomura (Tsang et al., 2011) of which we show that the crab-like forms have multiple origins, and the genus Linuparus (Tsoi et al., 2011) for which the evolutionary history is elucidated with the description of a new species. Our group is invited to prepare a chapter on genetic diversity and evolution (Chu et al. in preparation) in a book on Brachyura in the book series Treatise on Zoology, to be published in 2015.

463810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
463810.value: The robust molecular phylogenies revealed from this project shed many insights on the evolution of the Brachyura in general, including the evolution of body forms, origins of the freshwater crabs and divergence times of the major groups. As the discrepancies between morphological and molecular phylogenies are numerous, our molecular study has initiated many research works on the morphology of different taxa not only now undertaken by the collaborators of this project but also other research groups. All these studies will lead to a complete revision on the classification scheme of Thoracotremata and Brachyura, in general. Further, with a robust phylogeny available, a study on the molecular mechanisms underlying the emergence of different body forms of decapod crustaceans could be initiated. Our research group has just submitted a CRF proposal to pursue this goal.

463810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
463810.value: We studied the molecular phylogeny of crabs and obtained the most complete and extensive dataset to date, based on 140 species and 58 crab families. The analysis using this dataset provides some new important insights into the timing and processes of crab evolution. Our estimates show that most living crab families and superfamilies first arose during the late Cretaceous and early Tertiary (60-100 million years ago), at the same time when dinosaurs ruled the Earth. We also demonstrate that freshwater crabs were derived early in the evolution of true crabs and are shown to have at least two independent origins. They separated from their closest marine relatives after the break-up of Pangaea (~200 million years ago). The study refines many crab evolutionary issues, and provides a new, comprehensive resource for scientists to further investigate the molecular underpinnings responsible for body form shapes and functions among the various species.

464010.label: Project Objectives
464010.value: To determine the role of miR-433 in TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis in vitro. We will firstly determine whether miR-433 expression is up-regulated in three major fibrogenic kidney cells including tubular epithelial cells, mesangial cells, and fibroblasts in response to TGF-beta1 in a time- and dose-dependent manner. Then, we will use gain-of-function and loss-of-function models to either overexpress or inhibit miR-433 to study the functional role of miR-433 in TGF-beta1-induced renal fibrosis. To investigate signaling mechanisms by which TGF-beta1 regulates miR-433 expression and examine the candidate target genes of miR-433. We will employ Smad3 knockout (KO) and conditional Smad2 KO cells, and inducible Smad7 expressing kidney cell lines to dissect as to how TGF-beta/Smads regulate miR-433 expression. Furthermore, we will also identify the specific Smad-binding sites in miR-433 promoter and the mechanisms by which miR-433 mediates renal fibrosis in response to TGF-beta. To validate the functional role of miR-433 in vivo and to develop a therapeutic strategy for renal fibrosis by delivering Pre-miR and Anti-miR-433 microRNAs into kidneys using an ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene delivery technique. This will be performed in a mouse model of obstructive kidney disease. We will firstly examine whether the overexpression or inhibition of miR-433 will alter the initiation and progression of renal fibrosis induced by the unilateral ureteral obstruction in mice. Then, we will investigate the therapeutic potential of miR-433 in established obstructive kidney diseases.

464010.label: Realisation of objectives
464010.value: 1. Specific Aim 1. To determine the role of miR-433 in TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis in vitro. By employing rat kidney tubular epithelial cells (TEC), we demonstrated that miR-433 expression was up-regulated by treatment with TGF-beta1 or Angiotensin II (AngII) in a dosage- and time-dependent manner. We next demonstrated the pathological role of miR-433 in fibrosis. With treatment with TGF-beta1 or AngII, overexpression of miR-433 in kidney cells enhanced the expression of fibrotic markers. However, downregulation of miR-433 suppressed the expression of fibrotic markers. 2. Specific Aim 2. To investigate signaling mechanisms by which TGF-beta1 regulates miR -433 expression and examine the candidate target genes of miR-433. By using stable cell lines and mouse models of kidney diseases with alteration of TGF-beta signaling, we showed that miR-433 expression during renal fibrosis was Smad3, not Smad2, -dependent. Smad7 blocked miR-433 during renal fibrosis via inhibition of Smad3 activation. As we identified two conserved Smad binding sites (SBS) located in miR-433 promoter, we employed promoter reporter assays and chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), and demonstrated that one of the SBS was bound by Smad3 and possessed promoter reporter activity. These results showed that Smad3, but not Smad2, was a key mediator of TGF-beta-induced miR-433 in fibrosis. We also demonstrated that Azin1 was a target of miR-433 during renal fibrosis. As microRNAs can suppress protein expression through translational repression or mRNA degradation, we found that overexpression of miR-433 was able to reduce expression of endogenous Azin1. This correlation was further confirmed by the ability of miR-433 overexpression to suppress the reporter activity of the 3′ untranslated regions of Azin1. To assess the functional contribution of Azin1 to renal fibrosis, we demonstrated overexpression of Azin1 decreased renal fibrosis and polyamine abundance in TEC and these results were reversed by blocking Azin1 expression with siRNAs. Polyamine depletion enhanced TGF-beta1- or AngII-induced expression of pro-fibrotic genes and activation of TGF-β signaling while treatment with polyamine abolished such effects. The reduction of polyamine depletion by overexpressing Azin1 and suppressing either antizyme or miR-433 inhibited renal fibrosis and activation of TGF-β signaling. These results suggested that miR-433 induced renal fibrosis by suppression Azin1-polyamine axis. 3. Specific Aim 3. To develop the therapeutic strategy for renal fibrosis The ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene transfer of a miR-433 knockdown plasmid in mouse models of obstructive and hypertensive kidney diseases ameliorated renal fibrosis, and this revealed a therapeutic potential for miR-433 knockdown in renal fibrosis.

464010.label: Major findings and research outcome
464010.value: TGF-beta/Smad signaling plays a critical role in renal fibrosis in chronic kidney disease (CKD). It is well known that Smad3 is a key mediator of downstream TGF-beta/Smad signaling in renal fibrosis, however, the exact mode of TGF-beta/Smad3 in renal fibrosis remains unclear. In this study, we tested a novel hypothesis that TGF-beta may act by regulating the Smad3-dependent miR-433 to mediate renal fibrosis and that specific targeting miR-433 may represent an effective and novel therapy for chronic kidney disease. By microarray and realtime PCR, upregulation of miR-433 was observed in tubular epithelial cells (TECs) in response to TGF-beta1 and hypertensive condition. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that the upregulation of miR-433 expression during renal fibrosis was dependent on the activation of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling. The functional role of miR-433 in renal fibrosis was investigated by generating stable cell lines with overexpressing or down-regulating of miR-433. In TGF-beta1 and Angiotensin II (AngII) in TEC, overexpression of miR-433 promoted but knockdown of miR-433 suppressed TGF-beta1- or AngII-induced renal fibrosis. The findings demonstrated the pathological role of miR-433 in fibrosis in vitro. More importantly, the therapeutic potential of miR-433 in kidney disease was demonstrated in mouse models of obstructive and hypertensive nephropathies by applying an ultrasound-microbubble-mediated anti-miR-433 gene transfer technique. The ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene transfer of a miR-433 knockdown plasmid into the mouse kidney of two disease models was able to halt the progression of renal fibrosis. The pathological role of miR-433 on renal fibrosis was mediated via the depletion of renal polyamine as Azin1, a key component for maintain polyamine levels, was identified as a direct target gene of miR-433. The restoration of polyamine levels by overexpressing Azin1 and suppressing miR-433 inhibited the progression of renal injury. All these results revealed a therapeutic potential for targeting miR-433 in chronic kidney disease. In conclusion, miR-433 is a downstream mediator of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling and plays a pathological role in the development of renal fibrosis. Targeting miR-433 may represent a novel and effective therapy to combat renal fibrosis in chronic kidney disease. The research work of this study resulted in 13 publications and a manuscript under review, and 7 presentations in international conferences, and training of two doctoral students.

464010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
464010.value: (1) As a biomarker of kidney disease Being excellent biomarkers of kidney diseases may be another potential application of microRNAs. Recently, more investigations imply the circulating microRNAs are potential biomarkers for organ injuries because of their stability and tissue specificity. More studies confirm the fact that microRNAs are released into urine or blood during kidney disease. For instance, circulating miR-433 levels has been demonstrated to be significantly higher in patients with severe interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy. (2) Search of possible target(s) for miR-433 during renal injury Accurate identification of microRNA targets is not easy because one microRNA is capable of regulating multiple target genes. Target prediction programs currently provide us a huge number of potential microRNA targets. However, the overlap between algorithms is so minimal that only a small portion of these targets can be validated experimentally. In addition, the power of microRNAs also depends on their ability to target multiple genes that contribute to a pathway or phenotype. This also increases difficulty to search real targets of microRNAs. High-throughput validation and proteomic analysis may be possible approaches for us to identify microRNA targets.

464010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
464010.value: TGF-beta/Smad signaling plays a critical role in chronic kidney disease (CKD). It is well known that Smad3 is a key mediator of downstream TGF-beta/Smad signaling in renal fibrosis. However, the exact mode of TGF-beta/Smad3 in renal fibrosis remains unclear. In this study, we tested a novel hypothesis that TGF-beta may act by regulating the Smad3-dependent microRNA-433 (miR-433) to mediate renal fibrosis and that specific targeting miR-433 may represent an effective and novel therapy for chronic kidney disease. Expression levels of miR-433 increased in kidney cells after treatment of TGF-beta1 or under hypertensive condition and this increase depended on the activation of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling. Alteration of expression levels of miR-433 in kidney cells demonstrated the pathological role of miR-433 in fibrosis and inflammation in vitro. Enhanced miR-433 expression promoted but suppression of miR-433 inhibited TGF-beta1-induced renal fibrosis and hypertension-induced kidney injury. More importantly, suppression the miR-433 levels in diseased kidneys was able to halt the progression of renal fibrosis. In conclusion, miR-433 is a downstream mediator of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling and plays a pathological role in the development of renal injury. Targeting miR-433 may represent a novel and effective therapy to combat chronic kidney disease.

464710.label: Realisation of objectives
464710.value: Objective 1: We have used a multiple libraries approach to sequence the genome of the Chinese amphioxus, B. belcheri (Gray). Totally, 188,081,589 pairs of reads were generated with throughput of 38 Gbp. By the kmer analysis, the estimated genome size is about 442 Mbp. Thus, the sequencing depth of this library was 86X, which was much higher than the fold coverage we promised in the proposal. After extensive scaffolding and gap-filling, the current assembly result contains 159,509 scaffolds with a size of 472.33 Mbp. Totally, 37,909 protein-coding genes were annotated by the Tophat-Cufflinks pipeline. By using the CEGMA tool, more than 80% of the eukaryotic core genes were identified. Due to the high heterozygosity and repetivity in the genome, we had not put more efforts on scaffolding and gap-filling because several long contigs were already available for the comparative genomics tasks of the Objective 2. Objective 2: Among the top ten scaffolds, the third scaffold contains the hox cluster, spanning 478 kbp from Hox1 to Hox15. We have constructed the first complete hox cluster without gaps in the amphioxus. It is interesting that some conserved regions which might serve as the binding site of transcription factors or microRNAs can be found within the non-coding regions. Moreover, 79 putative long non-coding RNA genes were found within the hox cluster of the B. belcheri (Gray) genome and these genes are also present in similar regions in the B. floridae genome. It is also interesting that there are three isoforms of Hox3 transcripts in the hox cluster, although all of them code for the same protein sequence. Objective 3: A total of 1,796,755 Roche 454 reads and 57,485,189 Solexa pair-end reads were generated from an adult cDNA library and a mixture of cDNA of 13 different developmental stages, respectively (Solexa reads were contributed by Dr. Bingyu Mao of the Kunming Institute of Zoology). After combining assembly results, 44,782 mRNA transcripts of B. belcheri (Gray) were generated and then annotated. Among them, 3,813 genes were detected to be differentially expressed in at least one comparison of male adult stage and other 12 stages. Several genes including Otx2, Lhx3 and GSC were found to be specifically active in the gastrula stage. Moreover, 2,056 genes were activated at some developmental stages and kept on being expressed even in the adult stage. This is the first comprehensive analysis of the gene regulation during amphioxus development.

464710.label: Major findings and research outcome
464710.value: In this project, we have generated a draft genome of B. belcheri (Gray) with a total size of 472.33 Mbp, of which the N50 is 9.6 kb. Totally, 37,909 protein-coding genes were annotated and the genome probably covered more than 80% of the genes coding by this species. At the nucleotide level, the genomes of B. belcheri (grey) and B. floridae are very different. We can speculate that those conserved regions in the two genomes are functionally important and contribute to the very similar, or even nearly identical, morphology and phenotypes of the two species. The first gene cluster that drew our attention is the hox cluster. We have successfully constructed the first complete hox cluster without gaps in amphioxus. Although we may assume that the proteins encoded by the hox cluster should be nearly identical because of the morphological similarity, we did find some significant differences, although their significance remains unclear. Another novel finding is the identification of long non-coding RNA based on the genome comparison and transcriptome data. This will open a new avenue of research on the role of long non-coding RNA in the body plan formation. Last but not least, we have compiled the first experimentally generated transcriptome for the amphioxus. It contains 44,782 mRNAs and many of them are full-length. This transcriptome will be very useful for researchers to clone amphioxus genes, as well as to perform differential gene expression (DEG) analysis in amphioxus. We have also identified many differentially expressed genes during amphioxus development. In the future, we will compare this differential expression profile with that of other model organisms including zebrafish, drosophila and mouse. Moreover, to our surprise, we found that 18.15% of mRNA in our transcriptome cannot map on the transcript set generated from the B. floridae genome but are homologous to genes in related species including Saccoglossus kowalevskii and Strongylocentrotus purpuratus. The re-annotation of the B. floridae genome based on our finding will be an essential task in the near future.

464710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
464710.value: The genome and transcriptome of B. belcheri (Gray) have opened up interesting questions for future investigation. Publishing the results in a timely manner is the most urgent task and we plan to send out all the manuscripts by the end of 2014. For further development of the research, at least there are four major areas to be focused: 1. To study the existence of conserved sequences in the non-coding regions of the two amphioxus genomes in other genomes. This may lead to the advancement in the RNA biology and the role of non-coding RNA in evolution; 2. To study the role of long non-coding RNA genes in the hox cluster; 3. To study the differentially expressed genes during amphioxus development in the collaboration with Kunming Institute of Zoology; 4. To re-annotate the B. floridae genome and investigate the existence of exon shuffling, gene gain and gene loss during the divergence of the two species. Another General Research Fund application will be probably submitted in the RGC 2015 exercise.

464710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
464710.value: In this project, we have constructed a draft genome for the Chinese amphioxus. The genome is composed of around 4.7 million nucleotide pairs and codes for more than 40 thousand pieces of RNA. It is amazing to us that the genomes of Chinese amphioxus and Florida amphioxus are so different, although they have very similar appearance and anatomical structures. Based on the future comparison of their genome sequence, you might find the clues we need to explain how the conserved regions of these genomes shape various aspect of the species and how flexible a genome could be during the evolutionary divergence. In this study, we have also investigated the dynamic changes in gene transcription during the amphioxus development. This might open the Pandora's box of development and show how a swimming amphioxus, a tiny living fossil, could be generated by the temporal and spatial expression of various genes. Special attention has been drawn by the study of the hox cluster which control the body plan of the species. In summary, this project has successfully generated invaluable resources for future amphioxus research and created many interesting topics for further investigation on this evolutionarily important species.

465110.label: Project Objectives
465110.value: Determine the spatial and temporal expression pattern of AaGL3 during A.annua GT development As the first step towards understanding its functions, I propose to examine the spatial and temporal expression pattern of AaGL3 during A.annua GT development using RNA in situ hybridization technology. Such information will provide important clues to elucidating the function of this gene. Finding the interactive partner(s) of AaGL3 In Arabidopsis, GL3 interacts with a WD-40 protein and a Myb factor to form an activation complex, which subsequently controls the initiation of non-glandular trichome. Although AaGL3 and AtGL3 share high amino acid sequence similarity, they may not have similar biochemical property. We will perform a series of experiments to: (1) examine whether AaGL3 interacts with AtTTG1/AaTTG1 in Arabidopsis protoplasts systems using Bimolecular Fluorescence Complementation technology; (2) identify the interactive partners of AaGL3 by pull-down assay. Finding the direct targets of AaGL3 ChIP-Seq experiment will be conducted to identify the direct target(s) of AaGL3. In order to achieve this goal, I also propose a 3-run 454 pyrosequencing of A.annua draft genome. The recent advancement of high throughput pyrosequencing technology has made whole genome sequencing effort efficient and affordable. In fact, we have recently completed the global characterization of A.annua GT transcriptome using 454 pyrosequencing technologies. The generated draft genome will not only facilitate the proposed mechanistic study, it may also bridge the genomic information gap and facilitate further knowledge discovery in this non-model system. Effects of AaGL3 over-expression and knockdown We have established a high efficiency A.annua leaf transformation system, which serves as the firm foundation for in vivo functional study of our candidate gene. Together with the Arabidopsis gl3/egl3 mutant obtained from ABRC, we will examine: (1) whether the AaGL3 can complement the Arabidopsis gl3 mutant trichome phenotype. Because Arabidopsis gl3/egl3 has a trichomeless phenotype, such complementation test will determine if AaGL3 is a functional homolog of AtGL3. (2) effects of AaGL31 knockdown on A.annua GT development. Such systematic investigation will define the role of AaGL3, and reveal the possibly divergent mechanisms underlying GT vs. non-GT morphogenesis and patterning.

465110.label: Realisation of objectives
465110.value: We have successfully completed the project objectives. Specifically: 1. Spatial and temporal expression pattern of AaGL3 during A.annua glandular trichome development has been determined. It was found that AaGL3 was highly expressed in A.annua roots and trichomes. In the root tip cells and protoplasts,AaGL3 showed both cytosolic and nucleic expression pattern. 2. BiFC was used to determine the subcellular localization of the interaction between AaGL3 and AaTTG1. In BiFC experiments, reconstituted YFP fluorescence was observed throughout the nucleus, and no fluorescence was observed for the AaGL3-YFPN alone.To verify whether AaGL3-TTG1 can interact with each other, pull down assay was done with AaTTG1-His as bait. Recombinant AaGL3 carrying Trx-tag was pulled-down by His-AaTTG1, demonstrating that AaGL3 can indeed bind to AaTTG1 in vitro. The in vitro assay confirm the BiFC interaction result. 3.To examine the effects of AaGL3 over-expression, The A.annua AaGL3 gene was introduced into the Arabidopsis gl3 mutant, and genetic complementation test revealed that AaGL31 can rescue the phenotype of the Arabidopsis mutant. Effect of AaGL3 knockout on A.annua GT morphogenesis was also evaluated. Although we have successfully generated A. annua AaGL3 knockout lines, the phenotype analysis unfortunately showed that the glandular trichome formation was not affected. This negative result is not to our expectation and further investigations are still needed to understand the role of AaGL3 plays in A.annua.

465110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
465110.value: Artemisinin is the most prominent drug against the deadly disease malaria. However, low artemisinin content in plants has hindered its wide application. An attractive alternative to improve artemisinin production in plant is to manipulate the density and metabolic activity of glandular trichomes, the sites where artemisinin is produced. In this regards, understanding the underlying mechanism governing GT morphogenesis is crucial. The aim of this research is to study an A.annua AaGL3 gene, which is a homolog of Arabidopsis GL3 gene that play important roles in trichome morphgenesis. We systematically investigate the functional relevance of AaGL3 and its Arabidopsis homolog in A. annua and Arabidopsis model. Unfortunately, this gene turns out not to be related to glandular trichome morphogenesis and development in A.annua. Although this work did not result in any publication, the results highlight the difference in grandular and non-glandular trichome containing plants such as A.annua and Arabidopsis.

465410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
465410.value: 油菜素内脂（Brassinosteroids，BRs）是植物中的类固醇类激素，其在结构上和动物及昆虫的类固醇类激素非常相似而且在植物界普遍存在。BRs调节植物的很多发育过程，包括细胞分裂、细胞伸长、种子萌发、生殖发育、衰老及抗逆反应等。在农业上，BRs还能增加作物产量。 尽管来自模式植物逆南芥的大量分子遗传学研究已经证实，BRs 对植物生长发育至关重要并揭示了一条从BR受体BRI1 到细胞核转录因子BZR1和BES1的信号转导途径，但BRs如何调节植物生长发育这一核心问题仍未得到解答。这主要是因为目前对BZR1/BES1之后引致诸多细胞反应的BR 末端信号途径尚未被揭明。 该课题申请人以前的研究曾引致一个重要的BR信号转导因子BZR1的发现。BZR1作为一种植物转录因子专门调控那些受BR调节基因的表达。BZR1是通过一个遗传筛选被发现的，由bzr1-1D突变体克隆而来。bzr1-1D是一个显性突变，它可以使BZR1蛋白更稳定并引起持续的BR反应（如不依赖BR的细胞伸长）。bzr1-1D有几个很特别的、不同于野生型和其他BR突变体的表型，例如对BR合成抑制剂brassinozole (Brz)不敏感、半矮株形、深绿色的叶片，以及茎干上的打弯现象等。 为了帮助揭明BR信号转导中由BZR1/BES1到各发育过程的的下游途径，我们在拟南芥中开展了一个bzr1-1D抑制突变体的遗传筛选，并且找到了一些部分或完全抑制bzr1-1D表型的新突变体。本课题的研究目标是：（1）挑选几个bzr1-1D抑制突变体并对其进行详细的表型分析；（2） 克隆引起突变体表型的基因， 并（3）研究这些基因在BR信号转导和植物发育中的功能。我们相信这一课题的研究成果将导致有关BR信号转导和植物发育的新调节因子的发现。

465410.label: Realisation of objectives
465410.value: The aim of this project is to identify new regulators of brassinosteroid (BR) signaling and plant development through screening for bzr1-1D suppressor mutants in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. From a T-DNA activation tagging based suppressor mutant screen, we identified several potential bzr1-1D suppressor mutants and two of them, bzs433 and bzs20, were chosen for detailed characterization in this project. (1) Objective 1: 100% completed We characterized the bzs433 mutant phenotypes at both early seedling stage and reproductive stage and young seedlings were characterized under both dark and light growth conditions. Since the bzs20 mutant is an albino mutant with seedling lethality, we only performed phenotype analysis at seedling stage, either on MS medium or soil. For both mutants, the linkage between phenotype segregation and T-DNA insertion, phenotype dominance and inheritance were analyzed. We also examined the responses of bzs433 and bzs20 to BR and Brz treatments. Brz is a BR biosynthetic inhibitor. We have cloned the BZS433and bzs20 genes by adaptor-ligation mediated PCR (O'Malley et al. 2007). BZS433 gene is a novel ORF and encodes a putative Myb-like transcription factor. BZS20 gene encodes a chloroplast-localized unknown protein. The bzs433 mutant phenotype has been recapitulated by overexpressing the BZS433 gene in bzr1-1D background. Recapitulation of bzs20 is underway. (2) Objective 2: 100% completed The bzs433 mutant has a striking phenotype in stem, which makes the plant cannot stand erectly and resemble the nst1-1 nst3-1 mutant that is defective in secondary wall thickening (Mitsuda et al. 2007). To understand whether the BZS433 gene also plays a role secondary wall biosynthesis and whether this function is regulated by BR, we performed histochemical staining and measurements of major secondary wall components, and analyzed the expression of key secondary wall biosynthesis genes by qRT-PCR. Protoplast transient assays were performed to test whether BZS433 can transcriptionally regulate the expression of these biosynthetic genes. bzs20 is an albino mutant, so we measured its changes in chlorophyll contents and chlorophyll fluorescence. We also compared the ultra-structure of its chloroplasts with wild type plants by electron microscopy (EM). The results indicated that the mutant has severe defects in chloroplast development. (3) Objective 3: 100% completed The results from objectives 1 and 2 indicate that the BZS433 is likely a BZR1 suppressor and functions as a novel transcription factor that negatively regulates secondary wall biosynthesis. The BZS20 may define a new regulator for chloroplast development.

465410.label: Major findings and research outcome
465410.value: Major findings: 1. The bzs433 mutant has typical BR mutant phenotypes at early seedling stage, including compact rosette, thicker and more wrinkled dark-green leaves. At reproductive stage, bzs433 is a semi-dwarf with stems that cannot stand erectly. Microscopy studies and measurements of key secondary wall components indicated that the secondary wall formation in the mutant was severely impaired, and interfascicular fibers are completely missing. 2. bzs433 mutant has decreased sensitivity to BR treatment but increased sensitivity to Brz treatment compared to the original bzr1-1D mutant, suggesting that BZS433 is likely a BZR1 suppressor. Unlike bzs433, the bzs20 mutant has similar responses to both BR and Brz in cell elongation with the wild type Col plants, but bzs20 is resistant to Brz-induced seedling greening. Thus BZS20 is unlikely a BZR1 suppressor. 3. BZS433 gene encodes an uncharacterized Myb-like transcription factor with sequence similarity with other Myb factors involved in secondary wall biosynthesis. It is localized in cell nucleus and can repress the transcription of secondary wall biosynthetic genes. In addition, overexpression of BZS433 in Col and bzr1-1D background can reproduce the bzs433 phenotypes and RNAi knockout of BZS433 in bzs433 background suppresses bzs433 phenotypes. All these data suggest that BZS433 may function as a BZR1 suppressor to negatively regulate cell elongation and secondary wall biosynthesis. 4. The bzs20 mutant is an albino mutant with seedling lethality. Supplement of sucrose or different plant hormones in growth medium could not rescue the albino phenotype, suggesting that the mutant is not a cotyledon-specific albino mutant. Chlorophyll content, chlorophyll fluorescence and chloroplast ultra-structure studies indicated that bzs20 has severe defects in chloroplast development, particularly in inner membrane systems. 5. BZS20 gene encodes an uncharacterized expressed protein with putative chloroplast targeting signal. Although our current understanding to BZS20 function is limited, our phenotype and gene cloning data suggest that BZS20 may define a new and important regulator of chloroplast development. Research outcome: 1. Due to the interesting findings from this project, the PI has recently successfully secured a UGC-AoE grant “Center for Organelle Function and Biogenesis” (Project code: AoE/M-05/12, HK$47.25 M) in the capacity of Co-I. 2. Under the support of this project, 7 journal publications and 4 conference publications have been generated. 3 new manuscripts are in preparation. 3. The results gained from this project can be used to apply for other major competitive grants such as RGC GRF grants.

465410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
465410.value: 1. Although we have gained interesting results from study of the bzs433 mutant and the BZS433 gene, there are still many questions regarding BZS433 function to be addressed. For example, how BZS433 regulates secondary wall biosynthesis and what is the position of BZS433 in the relevant regulatory pathway? What are the genetic and biochemical relationships between BZS433 and other transcription factors in the pathway? 2. The bzs433 mutant has altered sensitivity to both BR and Brz treatments compared to the original bzr1-1D mutant, suggesting that BZS433 may function through interaction with BZR1. However, the questions such as what is the nature of this interaction, through protein-protein interaction or protein-DNA interaction remain to be answered. 3. Compared to BZS433, much less is known for the BZS20 function. Further studies are needed to understand what fraction and what step of chloroplast development are affected by the bzs20 mutation and what are the molecular mechanisms by which BZS20 regulates chloroplast development. In addition, bzs20 mutant is resistant to Brz-induced seedling greening but the mechanisms behind this are to be elucidated. We believe that through above studies we will have a better understanding to BZS433 and BZS20 gene functions in BR signaling and plant development.

465410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
465410.value: Brassinosteroids (BRs) are a group of steroidal hormones essential for plant growth and development. Although much progress has been made in understanding BR functions and signaling mechanisms, little is known for how BRs regulate specific developmental pathways. The objective of this project is to identify new regulators of BR signal transduction and plant development through characterization of two bzr1-1D suppressor mutants in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. BZR1 is a key transcription factor in the BR signaling pathway and bzr1-1D is a dominant mutant of BZR1. By characterizing two of the bzr1-1D suppressor mutants, bzs433 and bzs20, in this project we identified two novel genes, BZS433 and BZS20, involved in regulation of secondary cell wall formation and chloroplast development in plants, respectively. BZS433 may also play a role in controlling cell elongation as the bzs433 mutant is a semi-dwarf and partially suppresses the BR response phenotypes of the bzr-11D mutant.

465810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
465810.value: Hypertension is an important risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. Substantial evidence has also shown that prehypertension [systolic blood pressure (BP) 120-139 mm Hg or diastolic BP 80-89 mm Hg] is the strongest predictor of incident hypertension and is associated with elevated risk of cardiovascular diseases. Thus, prehypertension and its progression to hypertension have enormous public health implications. Soybean contains many beneficial components, among which isoflavones have received most research attention. The prominent soy isoflavone components are genistein and daidzein. Recently researchers have investigated their influences on vascular functions but only a handful of studies have focused on BP reduction as the primary outcome. Daidzein, the second most abundant isoflavone (>40%) in soy is a precursor of equol. Equol production is hypothesized to be the key to the clinical effectiveness of isoflavones. The role of whole soy or daidzein on BP is yet unclear. We hypothesize that whole soy (soy flour) or purified daidzein alone could reduce BP, improve EF, and decrease CVD risks in equol-producing menopausal women with prehypertension or initial untreated hypertension. We propose to perform a 24-week double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in postmenopausal women with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension. The primary objective is to verify if whole soy (soy flour) or purified daidzein alone has anti-hypertensive effects at a dosage of habitual high soy intake (top quartile in Hong Kong women) in prehypertensive equol-producing postmenopausal women; and the secondary objective is to test and compare their effects on endothelial function and other cardiovascular risk factors (lipid profile, glycemic control and inflammatory biomarkers). This study will be performed in community subjects. If the hypotensive effect of whole soy (soy flour) and/or daidzein is proven, the provision of whole soy foods or daidzein extracts alone will be an important strategy for the primary and secondary prevention of hypertension and cardiovascular diseases on a population basis. The population control of prehypertension or early hypertension has enormous public health significance. These research efforts will also have significant implications in the industrial segment in the provision of suitable soy products or food fortification for the prevention of hypertension and its related complications. 高血壓是心血管疾病的重要危險因素之一。大量證據顯示，高血壓前期（收縮壓120～139mmHg或舒張壓80～89mmHg）是高血壓發生的最強的預測因子，將會增加心血管疾病發生的危險。因此，高血壓前期以及高血壓進展的防治具有及其重要的公共衛生意義。 大豆含有許多有益的成分，其中大豆異黃酮備受關註。 大豆異黃酮的主要成分是染料木黃酮（genistein）和大豆苷元（daidzein）。近年來，一些研究人員調查了大豆對血管功能的作用，但只有為數不多的研究以血壓作為主要的研究目標。大豆苷元是大豆中第二豐富的大豆異黃酮單體（>40％），也是雌馬酚（equol）的前體。Equol 的產生被認為是大豆異黃酮臨床有效性的關鍵因素。然而，全大豆和大豆苷元對血壓的作用仍未清楚。 我們設想，在能夠產生equol的高血壓前期和早期人群中，全大豆（豆粉）或提純的大豆苷元將有助於降低血壓，改善內皮功能和降低心血管危險。我們計劃在有高血壓前期和早期高血壓的絕經後女性中開展一個為期24周的雙盲，隨機，安慰劑對照的試驗。該研究的主要目的是證實全大豆（豆粉）或純化的大豆苷元在習慣性高攝入劑量下（香港女性大豆攝入的最高的四分位數）有降低血壓作用。次要的研究目標包括檢測和比較大豆對內皮功能和其它心血管危險因素的作用（血脂，血糖控制和炎性因子）。 該研究將會在社區人群中進行。如果全大豆和/或大豆苷元被證明有作用，提供全豆食品或大豆苷元將會對人群高血壓和心血管疾病的初級和二級預防有重要的公共衛生意義。該研究也將有助於為工業部門推薦合適的大豆產品或強化食品以幫助預防高血壓及其引發的合並癥。

465810.label: Realisation of objectives
465810.value: We have fully realized the study objectives as per original application to examine the effect of whole soy (40g soy flour) or iso-caloric purified daidzein (40g low-fat milk powder and 63mg daidzein) on ambulatory blood pressure (BP) ,endothelial function and other cardiovascular risk factors (body composition, fasting glucose and lipids) in 270 equol-producing postmenopausal women with prehypertension or early untreated hypertension. This six-month double-blind, randomized and placebo-controlled trial was performed with strict adherence to the study protocol. The study indicated an effective randomization, blindness, low drop-out rate (6.3%) and good compliance of participants (by 24h urinary isoflavones testing), which ensured the study validity. Participants were screened and verified to be equol producers by the testing of 24h urinary isoflavones excretions after consecutive seven days’ daidzein challenge. Their BPs were screened by 4~6 office BP readings on two different screening occasions. The 3 kinds of supplements were concocted into granule with similar color, odor and major nutrient profiles, which secured good blinding efficacy and eliminated the possible bias due to unbalanced nutrients intake. The primary outcome measures were 24h ambulatory BP and endothelial function assessed by ultrasound determined brachial flow mediated dilation (FMD). In addition to the original outcomes on BP and FMD, we additionally examined the effect on menopausal symptoms (MS), markers of renal function and serum uric acid (UA) by taking the advantage of the existing resources. The hypotheses were based on the review of the literature and our preliminary results. We collected the data on MS before and after intervention using our previously validated questionnaire. Furthermore, according to the protocol, we have collected the data on serum and urinary creatinine, 24 h sodium and potassium excretions. The preliminary analysis on markers of renal function indicated a trend of reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate (by Cockcroft–Gault equation) with whole soy consumption. We thus further examined the change in serum cystatin C by using the remaining budget and found that whole soy tended to have a modest improvement of renal function in women with lowered renal function. We also have interests in the effect of soy on serum UA since there was no long term trial on soy and UA. We therefore conducted a pool analysis by combination of the data from our current trial and previous soy trial among postmenopausal women with either prehypertension or pre-diabetes. Several articles have been published or under review based on above findings.

465810.label: Major findings and research outcome
465810.value: We conducted a six-month randomized controlled trial among equol producing postmenopausal women with prehypertension or untreated early hypertension. 270 eligible women were randomized to either one of the three treatments: 40g soy flour (whole soy group), 40g low-fat milk powder+63mg daidzein (daidzein group) or 40g low-fat milk powder (placebo group) daily each for 6 months. 253 subjects completed the study according to the protocol. Urinary isoflavones indicated good compliance of participants. We found that: 1) Whole soy (soy flour) intake had significant effect on lowering lipids and inflammatory marker (high sensitivity C-reactive protein, hs-CRP) compared with isocaloric purified daidzein and milk placebo. There were significant differences within the groups in changes from baseline to 6 months in LDL-c (p=0.006), LDL/HDL ratio (p=0.006), hs-CRP (p=0.022), triglyceride (p=0.037) and total cholestrol (p=0.038) levels with lower levels in whole soy group compared with the other two groups. (The article was published in journal of Molecular Nutrition and Food Research) 2) There was no significant effect of whole soy or purified daidzein on 24h ambulatory blood pressure and endothelial function assessed by ultrasound determined brachial flow mediated dilation (FMD). (The article was under review by European Journal of Clinical Nutrition) 3) Six-month consumption of whole soy and purified isoflavone daidzein had no significant effect on body weight, body mass index (BMI), waist and hip circumferences, waist to hip ratio (WHR), body fat percentage, fat mass and free fat mass[4]. (The article was published in Journal of Obesity) 4) There was a less decrease in eGFRcockcroft in 6-month change (p=0.044) and %change (p=0.031) with whole soy intake relative to milk placebo. Subgroup analysis among women with lowered renal function suggested whole soy consumption tended to improve markers of renal function relative to milk control. ( The article was published in journal of Clinical Biochemistry) 5) Our pooled analysis including postmenopausal women with prehypertension or prediabetes indicated that six-month soy intake did not increase urate levels, but indicate a significant less decrease of UA than milk products. (The article was published in European Journal Of Nutrition) 6) Whole soy or isoflavone daidzein did not improve menopausal symptoms. (The article was published in journal of Menopause) 7) A cross-sectional study among 648 prehypertensive women who attended screening tests for the whole soy and daidzein trial indicated that equol producers had significantly less body fat percentage, higher sport physical activity, lower blood pressure, inflammatory marker (hs-CRP) and lipid profiles than equol non-producers. (The article was published in journal of PLOS one)

465810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
465810.value: 1. We have found a significant reduction in inflammatory marker (hs-CRP) and lipid profiles with whole soy consumption. Studies have implicated inflammation as primary mediator of the accelerated bone loss at menopause and cardiovascular health has a strong effect on skeletal health. Thus, we hypothesized that whole soy or purified daidzein may have potential benefits on bone remodeling among equol producers. We have collected adequate serum and 24h urine samples for the further bone biomarkers testing, which were stored in ultra-low freezer without repeated thawing. We have submitted a one-year proposal to RGC-GRF this year for a continuous study to examine the effect of whole soy and isoflavone daidzien on bone turnover markers and explore the potential mechanisms. The proposed study would be the first study specifically conducted among equol producing postmenopausal women, a population at high risk of bone loss and fracture and most likely to benefit from soy treatment to examine the effect of soy on bone metabolism. 2. Based on the current findings of whole soy on renal markers, we have great interests to propose a trial to verify the potential effect of whole soy on improvement of renal function among subjects with declined renal function.

465810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
465810.value: In this 6-month trial, although we did not find a significant effect of whole soy or purified daidzein (the potentially effective component of soy isoflavones) on blood pressure and vascular function, whole soy consumption at a dosage of habitual high soy intake in Asia had significant improvement on inflammatory marker and lipids (the important cardivascular risk factors), as well as a restorative effect on renal function suggested among women with declined renal function. The significance of this work lies in the potential of a simple dietary intervention or modification - increased dietary intake of whole soy (less processed soy products including soy flour, soy milk, soy nuts and tofu etc.) to improve cardiovascular health. The dietary strategy with whole soy consumption will offer an additional nutritional approach to the prevention of cardiovascular diseases and will be a practical, safe and inexpensive modality to improve cardiovascular and even renal health. The study will have important public health implications when the findings are disseminated in communities. Future studies using whole soy as replacement diet, among patients with high risk of cardivascular diseases and declined renal function are necessary to substantiate current findings.

466110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466110.value: 血管內皮對血管功能具有調節作用，血管內皮結構與功能完整性的缺失是糖尿病與肥胖症引起血管疾病的起點。在代謝綜合症與心血管疾病中，有關氧化應激的研究很多，但氧自由基 (ROS)在不同疾病中的來源尚未明確。最近的研究指出，線粒體來源的ROS在調節血管功能與糖尿病各種並發症的發展中起了重要作用。線粒體解偶聯蛋白(UCP2)是新發現的線粒體陰離子載體蛋白，參與調節線粒體膜電位與抑制線粒體ROS產生。研究發現UCP2可抑制動脈硬化與內皮細胞凋亡，但UCP2在血管功能上的直接作用仍不清楚。本研究的目的在於了解UCP2敲除促進糖尿病引起的內皮功能失調的作用機理是否與線粒體ROS產生增加從而抑制參與修復受傷內皮的內皮祖細胞的動員有關。本研究將探討1) 在基因敲除與高脂飲食誘導的兩種糖尿病模型小鼠中，UCP2敲除是否會增加內皮細胞功能失調，而UCP2過表達是否能保護內皮細胞功能；2) UCP2敲除對外周血內皮祖細胞的數量及功能有影響；3) UCP2是否參與了過氧化酶增殖物激活受體PPARδ對內皮細胞的保護作用。這些實驗將揭示UCP2在糖尿病血管病變中的功能與作用，為UCP2作為新的靶點治療糖尿病血管病變提供依據。

466110.label: Realisation of objectives
466110.value: We have established for the first time that UCP2 overexpression is effective to restore the impaired endothelial function not only in conduit aortas (acetylcholine-induced relaxations) and also in small mesenteric arteries (flow-mediated dilatation) in high fat diet-induced obese and diabetic mice. The beneficial effect of UCP2 is further confirmed in UCP2 deficient mice. This vascular benefit of UCP2 was associated with the increased NO bioavailability, while UCP2 deficiency exaggerated oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction in obese mice. Our new findings highlight a protective role of UCP2 against endothelial dysfunction in diabetes and obesity. The new results were published in Circulation Research (Tian et al., Uncpuling protein-2 protects endothelial function in diet-induced obese mice, 2012;110:1211-1216). We extended to search for any new anti-diabetic drugs which protects vascular function in diabetes through up-regulation of UCP2 expression and activity and found that a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor, sitagliptin, which elevates glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1, an insulin-sensitizing peptide), and GLP-1 analogue exendin-4 (GLP-1 receptor agonist) can effectively reduce mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) to preserve endothelial function in hypertensive rats and angiotensin II-infused mice and such beneficial effects are largely diminished in UCP-2 knockout mice. We thus elucidate for the first time that UCP2 serves as an important signal molecule in endothelial protection conferred by GLP-1-related agents. UCP2 could be a useful target in treating hypertension-related vascular events. Conclusions: UCP2 inhibits oxidative stress and down-regulates COX-2 expression through GLP-1/GLP-1R/AMPKα cascade. This work is published in Antioxidants & Redox Signaling (Liu et al., Uncoupling protein-2 mediates DPP-4 inhibitor-induced restoration of endothelial function in hypertension through reducing oxidative stress, 2014 Mar 12. [Epub ahead of print]). We also show that PPARδ activation is vascular protective in PPARδ agonist-treated diabetic mouse arteries. GW0742 (PPARδ agonist) augments endothelium-dependent relaxations while inhibits ROS production in aortic wall of db/db mice as suggested by the reduced DHE and MitoSOX fluorescence intensity. GW0742 and GW501516 (another PPARδ agonist) up-regulates the expression of UCP2 in endothelial cells. GW0742 prevents high glucose-induced endothelial dysfunction in wild-type mouse aortas but not in aortas from PPARδ-/- mice. We are now summarizing all data for preparation of a manuscript for submission.

466110.label: Major findings and research outcome
466110.value: 1. Previous studies indicate uncoupling protein-2 (UCP2) as an antioxidant defense against endothelial dysfunction in hypertension. UCP2 also regulates insulin secretion and action. However, the role of UCP2 in endothelial dysfunction associated with diabetes and obesity is unclear. We hypothesized that UCP2 protects against endothelial dysfunction induced by high-fat diet through inhibition of ROS production, and subsequent increase of nitric oxide bioavailability. High-glucose exposure reduced EDR in mouse aortae, which was exaggerated in UCP2 knockout (KO) mice, whereas UCP2 overexpression by adenoviral infection (AdUCP2) restored the impaired EDR. Impairment of EDR and flow-mediated vasodilatation in aortae and mesenteric arteries from high-fat diet-induced obese mice (DIO) was exaggerated in UCP2KO DIO mice compared with wild-type DIO littermates, whereas AdUCP2 i.v. injection restored both EDR and flow-mediated vasodilatation in DIO mice. Improved EDR in mesenteric arteries was inhibited by nitric oxide synthase inhibitor. UCP2 overexpression also inhibited intracellular ROS production in the en face endothelium of aorta and mesenteric artery of DIO mice, whereas UCP2 deficiency enhanced ROS production. This vascular benefit was associated with the increased NO bioavailability, while UCP2 deficiency exaggerated oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction in obese mice. Our new findings highlight a protective role of UCP2 against endothelial dysfunction in diabetes and obesity. 2.UCP2 negatively regulates intracellular ROS production and protects vascular function, its participation in vascular benefits of drugs used to treat cardiometabolic diseases is largely unknown. We also investigated whether UCP2 and associated oxidative stress reduction contribute to the improvement of endothelial function by a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor, sitagliptin, in hypertension. Angiotensin II evoked endothelium-dependent contractions (EDCs) in C57BL/6 and UCP2 knockout (UCP2KO) mouse aortae. Chronic sitagliptin administration attenuated EDCs in SHR arteries and Ang II-infused C57BL/6 mouse aortae and eliminated ROS overproduction in SHR arteries, which were reversed by GLP-1R antagonist exendin 9-39, AMPKα inhibitor compound C, and UCP2 inhibitor genipin. By contrast, sitagliptin did not affect EDCs in Ang II-infused UCP2KO mice. Importantly, exendin 9-39, compound C, and genipin reversed the inhibitory effect of GLP-1R agonist exendin-4 on Ang II-stimulated mitochondrial ROS rises in SHR endothelial cells. Moreover, exendin-4 improved the endothelial function of renal arteries from SHR and hypertensive patients. We elucidate for the first time that UCP2 serves as an important signal molecule in endothelial protection conferred by GLP-1-related agents. UCP2 could be a useful target in treating hypertension-related vascular events. Conclusions: UCP2 inhibits oxidative stress and downregulates COX-2 expression through GLP-1/GLP-1R/AMPKα cascade.

466110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466110.value: Our findings suggest UCP2 can become a useful target for therapeutic intervention. We have published two papers in top journals, Circulation Research (2012) and Antioxidants and Redox Signaling (2014). In addition, we also recently demonstrate that UCP2 is an important signalling molecule in mediating anti-diabetic effects of berberine, the latter is used in mainland China. We are now screening newer chemicals for their potential stimulatory effects on UCP2 and study regulation of UCP-2, hoping to elucidate new cellular mechanisms of vascular beneficial action of UCP-2 in obesity, diabetes and hypertension.

466110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466110.value: Disturbed balance between vaso-protective nitric oxide (NO) and vaso-harmful of oxygen reactive radicals (ROS) in endothelium, a layer of cells lining the lumen of blood vessels, causes endothelial cell dysfunction, a most important pathological event which triggers a cascade of inflammatory response within the vascular wall, leading to occurrence of cardiovascular complications such as heart attack and stroke in patients with diabetes and hypertension. Our recent studies provide novel evidence that uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2), an anti-oxidant protein is an important molecule to limit vascular wall oxidative stress in diet-induced obese and diabetic mice and UCP-2 can act as an effective target for intervention of anti-diabetic drugs such as sitagliptin and berberine in blood vessels and islets, respectively. Our new findings highlight a protective role of UCP2 against endothelial dysfunction in diabetes and obesity.
