466610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466610.value: All eukaryotic cells contain an endomembrane system with functionally distinct organelles for protein transport to their final destination. These membrane-bounded organelles include the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi apparatus, trans-Golgi network (TGN), endosome, prevacuolar compartment (PVC), vacuole or lysosome and plasma membrane (PM), all of which connecting the secretory, endocytosis and exocytosis together. Recent studies in plant cells demonstrate that multivesicular body (MVB) is PVC and TGN serves as an early endosome (EE) merging the secretory and endocytic pathways. However, compared to yeast and mammalian cells, relatively little is known about plant exocytosis in terms of its transport vesicle and regulatory mechanism. In yeast, the exocyst complex, consisting of eight proteins (Sec3, Sec5, Sec6, Sec8, Sec10, Exo70 and Exo84), has been shown to be essential for the targeting and docking process of exocytosis. Interestingly, different from the yeast and mammalian cells, the plant Arabidopsis genome contains 23 Exo70 homologs (AtExo70) with little information about their subcellular localization and function. As a first step to study plant exocytosis, we have recently used a green fluorescent protein (GFP) fusion approach to study the subcellular localization of selective AtExo70 proteins in Arabidopsis cells. When transiently expressed in Arabidopsis protoplasts, both AtExo70E2-GFP and AtExo70B2-GFP fusions are found to colocalize to punctate organelles adjacent to PM that are distinct from all tested known organelle markers. We thus hypothesize that these AtExo70E2-GFP positive organelles are exocytotic vesicles or compartments of plant exocytosis. Therefore, the ultimal goal of this proposal is to use selective members of AtExo70 as tools to study the molecular mechanisms of exocytosis and the nature of the exocytotic vesicle or organelle in plant cells. First, via transiently expressing various AtExo70-GFP fusions in Arabidopsis protoplasts, we will identify AtExo70 members with punctate patterns to be used as probes to study plant exocytosis because they may represent organelles or transport vesicles involving in exocytosis. Second, using confocal immunofluoresence and immunogold electron microscope (EM), we will study the dynamics and identify the ultra-structure of these AtExo70-GFP positive organelles in transgenic Arabidopsis cells. Third, using subcellular fractionation and affinity purification, we will isolate exocytotic vesicles for structural EM identification and proteomic LC-MS/MS analysis. Last, using both loss-of-function and gain-of-function approaches in transgenic Arabidopsis plants, we will study the functional roles of selective AtExo70 members and selective newly identified exocytotic proteins in mediating plant exocytosis. Our long-term goal is to illustrate the molecular mechanisms of plant exocytosis.

466610.value: 1) We have identified and characterized the first AtExo70E2-mediated exocyst complex (components) in plant cells; 2) We have characterized the dynamics and structures of AtExo70E2-positive vesicles in plant cells; 3) We have isolated EXPO for proteomic analysis and identified more than 100 putative EXPO cargo proteins, we have also carried out subcellular localization characterization of these novel EXPO cargos; 4) We have generated and characterized transgenic Arabidopsis plants expressing the EXPO marker AtExo70E2-GFP under the control of the endogenous AtExo70E2 promoter, and demonstrated that EXPO are distinct from autophagosome. 466610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466610.value: 1) EXPO and EXPO-mediated protein secretion represent a less-characterized Unconventional Protein Secretion (UPS) pathway in plants, the findings and publications from this project have served as a very foundation for future study in understanding the underlying mechanisms of EXPO-mediated UPS in plants; 2) Some of the findings can be used to develop further into a new research project in future application; 3) This new research of UPS can be further enhanced and promoted via international collaboration with leaders in both yeast and animal fields. 4) Potential application of UPS in plant defense will be explored in future studies.

466610.value: This RGC-funded project aims to study the nature, function and molecular mechanisms of AtExo70-mediated exocyst complex and protein secretion using a combination of cellular, biochemical and molecular approaches. Such study will provide new insights about the molecular machinery in regulating exocytosis in plants, with potential implications in cell wall biosynthesis and plant defense.

466710.label: Project Title(Chinese)
466710.value: 小儿神经母细胞瘤的机制研究-全新的研究手段

466710.label: Co - Investigator(s)
466710.value: Prof Chan, Hsiao-chang Dr Tsang, Kent, Kam Sze

466710.label: Project Objectives
466710.value: To analyze the biological significance of MYCN in maintaining neural crest stem cell function by using RNAi-mediated knockdown. We will knockdown MYCN expression by an inducible lentiviral- shRNA vector in NCSC to elucidate the function of MYCN in maintaining stem cell properties i.e. self-renewal and multilineage differentiation. To evaluate the consequences of MYCN over-expression on human NC differentiation and oncogenesis. We will over-express MYCN in NCSC using constitutive or NC progeny-directed lenti-viral vectors and determine if MYCN over-expression affects NC differentiation, disruption of which facilitates malignant transformation of NCSC. To compare the gene expression profiles of NCSC, MYCN-over-expressing NCSC, MYCN-over-expressing NCSC progeny, and neuroblastoma stem cells to identify other potential genetic changes that may contribute to the tumorigenesis of neuroblastoma. We will apply genome wide methods to compare unmanipulated NCSC, MYCN-over-expressing NCSC and neuroblastoma stem cells by coding RNA profiling, to uncover gene expression changes and identify potential key genes involved in the neural crest tumorigenesis.

466710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466710.value: 人体胚胎干细胞是全能干细胞，它能分化成人体200多种细胞类型，形成机体的任何细胞、组织和器官，因此在再生医学领域中的应用前景十分广阔。另一方面，人体胚胎干细胞在人类发育和人类疾病中的研究价值日益受到广泛关注。 神经嵴干细胞是胚胎发育过程中从外胚层神经褶顶嵴衍化而来的一种细胞类型。它们是一类具有高度移动性和干细胞多能性的细胞群， 在机体胚胎发育和成熟中发挥重要作用。神经嵴细胞功能障碍可导致多种人体疾病，包括恶性肿瘤， 如小儿神经母细胞瘤，恶性黑色素瘤和尤文氏肉瘤。 小儿神经母细胞瘤是起源于神经嵴的原始多能交感神经细胞的小儿多发性恶性肿瘤。小儿神经母细胞瘤最常见的生物学特征是有MYCN的扩增，MYCN的扩增与肿瘤的恶性表型和预后都密切相关。至关重要的是，神经嵴定向MYCN转基因小鼠具有神经母细胞瘤的表型， 表明MYCN在肿瘤发生中的关键作用。最近，我们在体外成功诱导人类胚胎干细胞快速生成了具有多能干性的神经嵴干细胞，本研究旨在运用人体神经嵴干细胞进一步研究神经母细胞瘤的发病机制。 我们假设MYCN扩增阻断正常的神经嵴分化和发育，从而启动肿瘤的发生。我们的研究内容包括：（1）分析MYNC在正常神经嵴细胞分化和神经嵴发育过程中的作用。 （2）检测和评估过表达MYCN是否导致神经嵴发育障碍和肿瘤发生。 （3） 通过基因质谱分析，寻找其它可能影响神经母细胞瘤发生的基因。 长期以来，由于人体神经嵴细胞来源非常有限，关于神经嵴发育和疾病的研究基本止于动物模型。运用人体胚胎干细胞，我们可以获得大量的人体神经嵴细胞，将对人体神经嵴发育和疾病的研究有极大的帮助。另外，此项研究将有助于我们进一步了解神经母细胞瘤的来源和发病机制， 并为神经嵴发育和疾病的研究提供新的研究手段和思路。

466710.label: Realisation of objectives
466710.value: Aim 1: Analyze the biological significance of MYCN in maintaining neural crest stem cell function by RNAi-mediated knockdown. We have successfully completed this aim. Originally, we used pSLIK-MYCNshRNA to knockdown MycN in NCSC differentiated from hESC and found that the lentiviral vector itself had an adverse effect on NCSC growth, indicating the lentiviral vector we used might have some non-specific effects. To solve this problem, we constructed second lentiviral vector using pGLVH1/GFP-MycN and found the human NCSC could tolerate this viral vector very well. For the first time, we showed that suppression of MycN in hNCSC inhibited cell growth and cell cycle progression. Knockdown of MycN in hNCSC increased the expression of Cdkn1a and Cdkn2b. In addition, MycN is involved in the regulation of human sympathetic neurogenesis. Aim 2: Evaluate the consequences of MYCN over-expression on human NC differentiation and oncogenesis. We have completed this part of project. Originally, we transduced freshly-sorted p75+ hNCSC with MND-MYCN-IRES-EGFP and the control vector. We showed that MycN overexpressing hNCSC could tolerate MycN and expressed the protein in our pilot study. However, we have found later that hNCSC stop to express MycN after passaging, indicating the vector we used cannot stably transduce hNCSC. To overcome this difficulty, we made another lentiviral vector (EF1α-EGFP-MycN) and transduced P75+hNCSC. Our results showed that overexpression of MYCN in undifferentiated hNCSC was readily tolerated and promoted cell proliferation and self-renewal. Aim 3: To compare the gene expression profiles of NCSC, MYCN-over-expressing NCSC, MYCN-over-expressing NCSC progeny, and neuroblastoma stem cells. This part of work has been mostly completed. During the process of sample collection, we have encountered difficulty in getting sufficient number of cells for analysis. To overcome this difficulty, we used two alternative methods: 1) Using PCR focused array. We have already identified MycN target genes which are involved in histone modification. In particular, polycomb genes like BMI1 and EZH2 are dramatically induced by MycN in hNCSC; 2) Improve hNCSC isolating protocol. As a consequence, we have already collected sufficient RNA from neuroblastoma cell lines, control and MycN overexpressing hNCSC and sent the samples to BGI for whole genome microarray analysis. The results will be ready in three months.

466710.label: Major findings and research outcome
466710.value: 1. MycN is critical for the maintenance of human neural crest stem cells We showed that knockdown of MycN prevented cell proliferation in human NCSC in both anchorage-dependent and -independent culture condition. Compared to control cells, which could be maintained for 2-3 months, the MycN depleted cells could only be passaged for 2-3 weeks. Following cell cycle analysis showed that downregulation of MycN dramatically impaired cell cycle progression and arrested NCSC at G0/G1 phase. In addition, we demonstrated that MycN knockdown in human NCSC increased the expression of Cdkn1a and Cdkn2b mostly, which encode the cyclin-dependent kinases p21CIP1 and p15INK4b, emphasizing the critical role of these tumor suppressors in stem cell growth and cell cycle progression. More interestingly, we revealed that suppression of MycN upregulated the expression of Mash1 and Phox2b, but downregulated the expression of Hand2 and Gata3, indicating suppression of MycN expression in hNCSC dysregulates autonomic neuron development. Taken together, these results indicate MycN is critical for the maintenance of hNCSC identity. We have summarized this part of work and submitted to Plos One for publication (Part C). 2.Overexpression of MycN in hNCSC promotes cell growth and initiates transition to neuroblastoma-like cells We demonstrated that overexpression of MYCN in undifferentiated hNCSC was readily tolerated and promoted cell proliferation and self-renewal. Compared to control cells, MYCN overexpressed hNCSC exhibited increased cell cycle progression and more neurosphere formation. In addition, MYCN regulates cell-cycle related genes, such as p16 and cyclin D1 in hNCSC. Moreover, ectopic expression of MycN in undifferentiated hNCSC led to enhanced expression of neural crest stem cell markers, such asp75, HNK-1 and Slug. Together these studies confirm that human NCSC tolerate expression of MYCN and ectopic expression of the oncogene initiates transition to neuroblastoma-like cells. We have submitted the result for conference abstract for oral presentation in ISSCR 2015 (Part C). 3.MycN can regulate polycomb genes in hNCSC Polycomb genes, such as Bmi1 and Ezh2, block the transcriptional activation of differentiation and tumor suppressor genes by epigenetic suppression. Interestingly, we found that knockdown of MycN downregulated the expression of Bmi1 and Ezh2 in hNCSC. On the contrary, we demonstrated that overexpression of MycN significantly upregulated the expression of Bmi1 and Ezh2 in hNCSC. These results indicate Bmi1 and Ezh2 can be regulated by MycN, which could mediate the regulatory role of MycN in hNCSC growth and differentiation.

466710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466710.value: To date, studies of neural crest development and biology have been almost exclusively done using model organisms. With the discovery of hESC, there is no doubt that knowledge of human neural crest development and diseases will be profoundly enhanced by the unique opportunities provided by NC lineage-directed differentiation of hESC. In our study, for the first time, we have demonstrated that MycN governs human neural crest stem cell growth and cell cycle progression. We have also demonstrated that overexpression of MycN is critical for the initiation of neuroblastoma, which could be mediated by polycomb genes. Together, these findings suggest that abnormal induction of polycomb proteins and subsequent deregulation of polycomb target gene expression might be critical early events in MycN-induced transformation, which warrant future investigations into the epigenetic mechanism underlying the regulatory role of MycN in neuroblastoma development. Thus, we have initiated a basic research project studying the role of histone modification in human neural crest development and tumor initiation. On the other hand, we propose that in vitro differentiation from hESC can be reliably used to isolate large numbers of human NCSC for biologic study of human neural crest development and diseases.

466710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466710.value: Human embryonic stem cells (hESC) hold great promise for applications in regenerative medicine, disease modeling, and developmental biology studies because of their capacity of self-renewal and their developmental potential to generate various cell types. Neuroblastoma is a common childhood malignant tumor of neural crest origin, arising in the sympathetic nervous system. Among the genetic alterations identified in neuroblastoma, amplification of the oncogene MYCN is strongly associated with highly malignant behavior and poor prognosis. For the current study, we evaluated the consequences of MYCN manipulation in human embryonic stem cell-derived NCSC (hNCSC). Lentiviral mediated knockdown of MYCN dramatically suppresses cell proliferation and self-renewal of hNCSC, indicating the critical role of MYCN in hNCSC function. On the contrary, overexpression of MYCN in undifferentiated hNCSC was readily tolerated and promoted cell proliferation and self-renewal. MYCN overexpression induced hNCSC genes as well as the PcG proteins BMI-1 and EZH2 in hNCSC. In addition, MYCN regulates cell-cycle related genes, such as p16 and cyclin D1. Together these studies confirm that human NCSC tolerate expression of MYCN and ectopic expression of the oncogene initiates transition to neuroblastoma-like cells.

467210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
467210.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the fifth most common malignancy worldwide. In Hong Kong HCC is the third most common cause of cancer mortalities. Despite its high prevalence and inferior prognosis in general, to date, our understanding of the liver pathogenesis is limited. Treatment of HCC is complicated by the fact that the disease is often diagnosed at an advanced stage when it is no longer amenable to curative surgery, and that current systemic chemotherapeutics are mostly inefficacious. A better understanding on the molecular basis of HCC is therefore urgently required to facilitate development of new therapeutic strategies. Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) is a histone deacetylase that has been implicated in gene regulations and stress resistance. Although SIRT1 over-expression is observed in a number of cancers and is thought to play a role in tumorigenesis, the underlying molecular basis remains largely unexplored. Our studies on SIRT1 in HCC found that, whereas SIRT1 was expressed at very low levels in normal livers, it is commonly over-expressed in HCC cell lines and tumors (70% of cases). To further establish the value of SIRT1, tissue microarray analysis of >140 paired HCC tumor and adjacent non-tumoral liver tissues revealed a profound positive correlation between the expression levels of SIRT1 and advancement in tumor grades (P=0.006). At the cellular level, down-regulation of SIRT1 consistently induced growth suppression and senescence in a panel of HCC cancer cell lines. Remarkably, SIRT1-silencing also caused telomere dysfunction-induced foci that were clearly associated with reduced expressions of telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT), protection of telomeres 1 homolog (POT1) and POT1-interacting protein 1 (PTOP) concomitantly. Given that these genes are well known for their role in telomere maintenance, our preliminary data therefore revealed a hitherto undiscovered role of SIRT1 in telomere maintenance via the regulation of telomeric genes expression. The central theme of this proposal is thus to elucidate the molecular basis of SIRT1 in telomere maintenance and to evaluate the potential value of SIRT1 inhibition as a therapeutic targets in HCC. Our objectives include: 1) Elucidating the correlation between SIRT1, POT1, PTOP, and hTERT expressions in primary HCC specimens; 2) Characterizing the role of SIRT1 in telomere maintenance; 3) Elucidating the transcriptional regulation of SIRT1-mediated hTERT gene expression; 4) Evaluating the anti-tumorigenic role of SIRT1-silencing/-inhibition in vivo. Our proposed studies should provide a better understanding of the role of SIRT1 in HCC tumorigenesis, and development of SIRT1 inhibitors as potential HCC therapeutics. 原發性肝癌是世界上最常見的五大惡性腫瘤之壹，在香港地區肝癌死亡率位第三。肝癌具有發病率高，進展快，預後差等特點，但是目前人們對肝癌的發病機制仍舊不十分了解。由於大多數肝癌患者就診時疾病已經進入晚期，完全失去了手術治愈的機會，並且肝癌的化療效果不佳，因此,現在最為迫切的是對肝癌的分子機制有壹個更好的認識，這樣才能有利於發展新的治療策略。Sirtuin 1 是壹種組蛋白脫乙酰基酶，在細胞中與多個基因的調節及抗逆性緊密相關。雖然人們在多種腫瘤組織中發現SIRT1表達增高，並且認為它在腫瘤形成過程中發揮著重要作用，但是SIRT1發揮作用的潛在分子機制仍然不為人們所知。我們的研究發現SIRT1在肝癌細胞系和人類肝癌組織中表達增高（70%），而在正常肝組織中表達水平極低。為了進壹步研究和證實SIRT1的重要性，我們運用組織芯片技術對140例肝癌組織及癌旁組織中SIRT1的表達水平進行檢測，結果顯示SIRT1在肝癌中的表達水平和腫瘤的病理分級呈正相關性(P=0.006)。在細胞模型研究中，當下調SIRT1的表達水平時，肝癌腫瘤細胞系表現出明顯的生長抑制和雕亡。我們亦發現, SIRT1的沈默能夠導致端粒的功能障礙，這種功能障礙與端粒酶逆轉錄酶(hTERT), 保護端粒1蛋白（POT1）及POT1相互作用蛋白1 （PTOP）表達水平的下調息息相關。 眾所皆知，這些蛋白基因能夠在端粒維持中發揮重要作用，我們的初步結果顯示SIRT1可能通過調節端粒相關蛋白基因的表達從而保證端粒維持，而在這之前，人們從來沒有發現SIRT1在這個過程中發揮著作用。因此，本課題的主要內容就是闡明SIRT1在端粒維持中的分子機制，並以此評估SIRT1的抑制在肝癌治療中的潛在應用價值。我們的目標包括：1）闡明SIRT1,POT1,TERT和PTOP在原發性肝癌組織中的表達相關性；2）闡明SIRT1在端粒維持中的作用。3）闡明SIRT1介導的hTERT表達的轉錄調控。4）在體內評價SIRT1沈默或者抑制對治療腫瘤作用。此課題將有助於我們進壹步了解SIRT1在肝癌發病機制中的作用，從而能夠開發SIRT1抑制劑作為潛在的肝癌治療手段。

467210.label: Realisation of objectives
467210.value: Sirtuins are histone deacetylases. In mammals there are 7 sirtuin members (SIRT1-7). The aim of this proposal is to characterize the role of SIRT1 overexpression in the pathogenesis of HCC. Objective 1 has been completely accomplished. We used paired HCC specimens to determine the correlation between the induction between SIRT1 and hTERT/PTOP respectively. POT1 expression was not determined because it was not consistently repressed by SIRT1 depletion in different cell lines. hTERT but not PTOP was significantly correlated with SIRT1 in clinical samples, suggesting that SIRT1-hTERT regulatory axis may exist in vivo. We have published the above findings. Objective 2 has been completely accomplished. We showed that SIRT1 depletion induced cell cycle arrest, cellular senescence and telomere dysfunction-induced foci (TIF) in HCC cells. We found that SIRT1 depletion also disrupted mitotic checkpoint signaling due to the repression of AURK-A, AURK-B, CENP-A, or/and BUB1 gene expression. We found SIRT1-depleted cells exhibited increased nuclear abnormality characterized by multinuclei and micronuclei formation. We have published the above findings. Objective 3 has been largely accomplished. We explored the role of transcriptional, epigenetic, and miRNA regulation in SIRT1-mediated TERT expression. None of these regulatory mechanisms play a role in the regulation of hTERT. We speculated that SIRT1 might regulate hTERT via acting at a more distal promoter region or via long-range interaction. We are preparing manuscript for the above findings. Objective 4 has been partially accomplished but was extended towards a new direction. We attempted to develop tetracycline-regulated SIRT1 shRNA expressing HCC cell lines for tumor xenograft experiment but failed. To circumvent this problem we collaborated with Senabiotech biotech to evaluate the efficacy of their proprietary SIRT1-specific inhibitor Selisistat on HCC cell growth (this is the only sirtuin inhibitor available for in vivo experiment). However, this inhibitor, even at high concentration, did not effectively inhibit tumor cell growth. Therefore we did not test this compound in xenograft model. During the course of investigation, we have also discovered a role of SIRT2 in HCC tumorigenesis. We showed that SIRT2 is overexpressed in a subset of HCC cases. We found that depletion of SIRT2 suppressed cell migration and invasion of HCC cells that were associated with a reverse epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) phenotypes. We showed that SIRT2 regulates Akt/GSK3-beta/beta-catenin signaling pathway via directly deacetylation of Akt. We have published the above findings.

467210.label: Major findings and research outcome
467210.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly malignant tumor with a poor prognosis. Treatment of HCC is complicated by the fact that the disease is often diagnosed at an advanced stage when it is no longer amenable to curative surgery, and current systemic chemotherapeutics are mostly inefficacious. Sirtuins are class III histone deacetylases that are implicated tumorigenesis. In human there are seven sirtuin members (SIRT1-7). In this study, we showed that although SIRT1 and SIRT2 was expressed at very low levels in normal livers respectively, they were overexpressed in HCC cell lines and in a subset of HCC (Chen et al, Cancer Research; Chen et al, Hepatology). Tissue microarray and western blotting analysis of HCC tissues revealed that the advancement in tumor grades are associated with SIRT1 expression level (Chen et al, Cancer Research), whereas the presence of microscopic vascular invasion, more advanced tumor stage, and shorter overall survival are associated with SIRT2 expression level (Chen et al, Hepatology). Downregulation of SIRT1 consistently suppressed the proliferation of HCC cells via the induction of cellular senescence or apoptosis. SIRT1 silencing also caused telomere dysfunction–induced foci and nuclear abnormality that were clearly associated with reduced expressions of telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), and PTOP, which is a member of the shelterin complex. Ectopic expression of either TERT or PTOP in SIRT1-depleted cells significantly restored cell proliferation. There was also a positive correlation between the level of induction of SIRT1 and TERT in human HCC. SIRT1-silencing sensitized HCC cells to doxorubicin treatment (Chen et al, Cancer Research). On the other hand, depletion of SIRT2 reduced the motility and invasiveness of HCC cells. It also led to the regression of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) phenotypes, whereas the ectopic expression of SIRT2 in the immortalized hepatocyte cell line enhanced the expression of EMT markers, and promoted cell motility and invasiveness. Mechanistic studies revealed that SIRT2 regulates the deacetylation and activation of Akt, which subsequently impinges on the GSK-3β/β-catenin signaling pathway to regulate EMT (Chen et al, Hepatology). Our work on SIRT1 (Chen et al, Cancer Research) was featured as one of the “Key Scientific Articles” in August 3, 2011 issue of Global Medical Discovery (www.gloalmedicaldiscovery.com). Together, our findings reveal novel functions for SIRT1 and SIRT2 in telomere maintenance and invasiveness of HCC respectively, and they rationalize the clinical exploration of inhibiting sirtuins for HCC therapy.

467210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
467210.value: We made pivotal discovery that SIRT1 and SIRT2 is overexpressed in HCC respectively, and their overexpression is associated with tumor progression and dissemination. SIRT1 plays a role in the regulation of TERT expression, but the underlying mechanism remains elusive. On the other hand, SIRT2 deacetylases and regulates the activity of Akt, which in turns regulates beta-catenin signaling, cell motility and invasiveness, suggesting that inhibition of SIRT2 activity is a potential strategy to control tumor metastasis. Therefore, one research direction in the future will be to further elucidate the molecular events responsible for SIRT1-mediated TERT expression, which could provide insights into the regulatory mechanisms and might possibly lead to the discovery of new therapeutic strategies against HCC. On the other hand, it will be important to evaluate, using mouse xenograft model, the efficacy of known SIRT2-specific inhibitors in preventing HCC metastasis. Such information will provide essential information on the possibility of clinical trials of SIRT2 inhibitors in HCC therapy. Furthermore, to design and synthesize SIRT2-specific inhibitors is highly desirable because most of the existing sirtuin inhibitors at present are cross-reactive to different sirtuin members.

467210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
467210.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly malignant tumor with a poor prognosis. Treatment of HCC is complicated by the fact that the disease is often diagnosed at an advanced stage when it is no longer amenable to curative surgery, and current systemic chemotherapeutics are mostly inefficacious. Therefore, there is an urgent need to understand HCC carcinogenesis and to identify novel molecular targets for the development of more efficacious therapeutics. We made pivotal discovery that histone deacetylases sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) and sirtuin 2 (SIRT2) are overexpressed in HCC, and they play essential roles in the progression and metastasis of HCC. Our studies showed that SIRT1 regulates the growth of HCC by upregulating the expression of telomerase and telomere-associated protein, which are important for the maintenance of telomere integrity in tumor cells. On the other hand, SIRT2 enhances the motility and invasiveness of HCC cells by deacetylating a protein kinase known as Akt, leading to its activation. Subsequently, Akt activates downstream signaling cascades and transcriptional programs, leading to tumor metastasis. Our findings reveal novel functions for SIRT1 and SIRT2 in HCC progression, and they rationalize the clinical exploration of inhibiting sirtuins for HCC therapy.

467410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
467410.value: Nutritional intake is essential to human health and a healthy diet is the key to prevention and treatment of obesity. Glycemic index (GI) is a measure of blood glucose after eating a set amount of carbohydrate. Clinical trials suggest a role for low GI diet in the management of obesity and associated metabolic risks including diabetes. Foods that are rapidly digested, absorbed and transformed into glucose have a high GI which causes accelerated and transient surges in blood glucose and insulin, quick return of hunger sensations and excessive caloric intake. Conversely, low GI diet decreases blood glucose and insulin excursion, promotes greater fat oxidation, decreases lipolysis and increases satiety. Modern food-processing technology has produced many food products with high GI which may contribute to the burgeoning epidemic of obesity especially in children/adolescents. Since dietary habit is shaped in early life, adolescence is a critical period to educate our young people to acquire a healthy eating habit to prevent obesity. This is a 12-month randomized controlled dietary interventional trial followed by a 6-month observational study. The purposes of the study are to examine the changes of body mass index, body fat percentage, insulin secretion, insulin resistance and obesity associated cardiometabolic factors; and to explore the underlying neurohormonal mechanisms associated with these changes in both short-and long-term. 健康的飲食對預防及治療肥胖是十分重要的。升糖指數(Glycemic Index, GI)是指依據食物對血糖濃度的影響，來描述碳水化合物類的一種數字方法。 根據臨床研究的數據顯示，低升糖指數飲食對治療肥胖及相關的代謝風險，如糖尿，是有一定的效果。含高升糖指數的食物會迅速吸收及轉化為糖份，提升血糖及胰島素、快速回復飢餓的感覺以致進食過多的食物及卡路里。相反地，低升糖飲食會降低血糖及胰島素的波動，促進脂肪代謝，減低脂肪分解成游離脂肪酸及增加飽足的感覺。現代食品加工製造了很多高升糖的食物，這也許是現代人肥胖，尤其是兒童及青少年人肥胖劇增的一個因素。 我們的飲食習慣在兒童及青少年已建立成形，所以這個時期是培養良好飲食習慣的一個重要時期。這是一項為期12個月的隨機對照飲食臨床研究。我們將有一個6個月的隨後觀察跟進研究期。這項研究是評估低升糖飲食對體重指數，脂肪比例、胰島素敏感度、及肥胖相關的新陳代謝及心血管風險之影響。此外，這項研究會探討這些改變在短及長期的內分泌及賀爾蒙的致病病變機制。

467410.label: Realisation of objectives
467410.value: We completed the study with the objectives achieved. We had recruited 285 subjects (4 subjects excluded because they were found to have psychiatric problems and/or on chronic medications which were not disclosed at entry of the study) with the first subject enrolled on 15 Feb 2011. All eligible subjects were randomized into low GI group (n=139) and control group (n=142) as per protocol. 164 subjects completed 6 months follow-up while the respective figures for subjects completed 12 months and 18 months follow-up were 81 and 37 respectively. We found that subjects in the low GI group had significant reduction in obesity indices including BMI, body weight and waist circumference compared to subjects in the control group at 6 month of intervention after adjustment for age and sex (all p <0.05). The results had been written up and the full paper had been published in BMC Public Health. At 12-month, there was a non-significant trend of reduction of obesity indices and the results at 12-month had been submitted to International Congress of Endocrinology (ICE, to be held in Chicago on June 2014) for abstract presentation. This randomized controlled trial had provided evidence that low GI diet may be an alternative to conventional diet in the management of Chinese obese adolescents (objective 1, primary/secondary endpoints of the study). We had also examined the changes in insulin sensitivity as measured by homeostasis model assessment (HOMA) from baseline (objective 2 and tertiary endpoints). The results of this randomized controlled trial had been presented as oral or poster presentations in 9 local, regional and international conferences and resulted in 3 full papers (one had been published while two are under preparation). This study had also contributed to the training of 5 postgraduate students, 1 elective student from Singapore and 1 elective student from Canada. In addition, the results of this study facilitated the success of funding support for 3 conference grants (two from Hong Kong Society for the Endocrinology, Metabolism and Reproduction and one from Asian Association for the Study of Diabetes) and 2 research grants (1 from Hong Kong Association for the Study of Obesity and another one from Health and Health Services Reserve Fund mini grant with co-I Prof. Nelson as PI in this mini-grant). This study also forms the basis for potential collaborations with Glycemic Index Research Unit, Temasek Polytechnic, Singapore and The John Hopkins Global Center for Childhood Obesity (www.jhgcco.org).

467410.label: Major findings and research outcome
467410.value: To date, this study is the largest randomized controlled trial with the longest duration of intervention conducted in Hong Kong Chinese obese adolescents to investigate the impact of a low GI diet on body indices and obesity related cardiovascular risk factors and hormonal parameters. At baseline, mean age of the study cohort was 17.2±1.2 years and 17.3 ±1.3 years in low GI and control group respectively. The respective BMI at baseline was 30.7±4.4 kg/m2 in low GI group and 30.8±4.3 kg/m2 in control group. After adjustment for age and sex, subjects in low GI group had significant reduction in obesity indices including BMI, body weight and waist circumference compared to subjects in the control group at 6 month (all p <0.05). After further adjustment with physical activity level, waist circumference remained to be significantly reduced in the low GI group compared to conventional group (p=0.018). The 6-month intervention also resulted in decreased calorie intake and a healthier dietary composition in terms of increased fiber intake and reduced fat intake in obese adolescents. Our results suggested that apart from its quantity, the quality of carbohydrate content in a meal may be an essential element in obesity management with health implications. At 12-month, there was a non-significant trend of reduction of obesity indices (p<0.1 for both BMI and waist circumference). An interesting observation in this study is that we found a very low percentage (1%) of obese adolescents had abnormal fasting plasma glucose levels at the baseline (5.6-6.2 mmol/L) while about 10% of them had impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes which was detected by oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). This highlights the importance of using OGTT to detect early diabetes or pre-diabetes as first phase insulin secretion and post-prandial hyperglycemia are early signs of diabetes in people from Asia. In addition, we found an alarmingly high percentage of fatty liver. Among 176 subjects who had ultrasonography of abdomen done, 51% had fatty liver (31% mild,14%moderate, 2% moderate to severe and 4% severe).

467410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
467410.value: This study provides important information regarding the impact of low GI diet on obesity indices and obesity associated cardiovascular risk factors in local Hong Kong Chinese obese adolescents. These data provided evidence and threw new insights into the emerging attention regarding the role of low GI diet in obesity management. Since the subjects recruited in this cohort had detailed documentation of baseline characteristics including physical activity levels, resting energy expenditure, ultrasound scan of abdomen, etc, this cohort of obese Chinese adolescents forms the basis for future prospective long-term evaluation and a study entitled "Obesity adolescents in Hong Kong-post-trial follow-up after exit from a dietary intervention" is planned for the Summer Undergraduate Research Programme which will be done in summer 2014. In addition, blood aliquots for genetic markers were saved for future use of genetic studies, as well as aliquots for biomarkers were sampled. Therefore, the associations between gene-diet interactions and epigenetic phenomenon can be explored. All these data and samples would be valuable resources for future projects and granting opportunities.

467410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
467410.value: Obesity and its associated diseases in the youth are major public health problems. Most worrying is the lack of effective therapies in the management of childhood and adolescence obesity. There are now emerging data showing that low glycemic index (GI) diet may play a role in obesity management. GI is a measure of how quickly blood sugar levels rise after eating a particular type of food. Here, we conducted a randomized controlled trial which recruited 281 eligible obese Chinese adolescents who were randomized into low GI group (n=139) or control group (n=142) for 12 months. 164 subjects completed 6 months follow-up while the respective figures for subjects completed 12 months and 18 months follow-up were 81 and 37 respectively. We found that subjects in the low GI group had significant reduction in obesity indices including body mass index, body weight and waist circumference compared to subjects in the control group at 6 month of intervention. At 12-month, there was a non-significant trend of reduction of obesity indices. Our results suggested that apart from its quantity, the quality of carbohydrate content in a meal may be an essential element in obesity management with health implications.

467810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
467810.value: 本項目的目的是構建一個香菇的基因組序列註釋數據庫，為理解香菇的生物學特性以及菌種鑑定和繁殖應用提供重要的遺傳信息資源。香菇作為第二大可食用菌，其轉錄組分析以及其對於遺傳育種標記的研究已經受到了廣泛的關注。然而，因為缺少該菌種基因組序列的信息，一些傳統的遺傳分析和菌種改良的分子方法（例如： 微衛星標記）受到了限制。所以我們計劃對香菇進行基因組測序，並對其進行全基因組註釋，同時構建一個用以深入研究香菇生物學特性和遺傳多樣性的分析平台， 最終設計合理的育種和栽培方法。我們（1）首先搭建一個可供搜索的香菇基因組數據庫；（2）然後通過分析香菇的基因組數據，對其進行初步註釋。我們知道多種不同的環境因素能夠誘導香菇子實體的形成，例如在沒有光的環境下，次生菌絲體就不會發展成子實體。但還不清楚光是如何調控基因表達的；（3）通過光信號和子實體形成的轉錄特徵譜，在轉錄水平上對基因進行精確的功能註釋；（4）同時，通過對轉錄特徵譜的分析，來發現有差異表達的光感基因。這些基因標記有助於系統發育樹的構建，遺傳分析和菌種改良；（5）發現一些潛在的遺傳標記，特別是一些微衛星標記並對其在不同栽培品種上進行實驗。香菇的全基因組測序能夠給所有研究香菇以及擔子菌和食用菌的實驗室帶來益處。基於香菇的基因組序列，研究機構能夠對其進行深入研究，包括菌種雜交、子實體的形成和生長、菇類進化以及白腐菌和其他食用菌的遺傳。此外，香菇基因組的研究將會擴展現有的遺傳連鎖圖譜，並驗證前期註釋的功能基因，為育種和園藝提供分子標記。同時也將促進我們理解影響食用菌遺傳和表型差異的因素。

467810.label: Realisation of objectives
467810.value: 1. To construct a searchable database of the genome sequence of Lentinula edodes Using the genome sequence of L. edodes L54A and valuable resources including genome sequences of C. cinerea, L. bicolor, and S. commune, we have built the Comparative Mushroom Genomics Platform (CMGP) for bioinformatics and genome analysis. GBrowse and Ensembl of CMGP enable researchers to easily access L. edodes genome sequence and annotations of various aspects for their research. 2. To analyse the L. edodes genome for initial computer-based annotation at genome level We have predicted 13,382 protein-coding genes from the draft genome sequence of L. edodes. The reference gene set was subject to automated annotation based on the amino acid sequences. Sequence similarity search against NCBI non-redundant protein sequence database (nr), Carbohydrate-Active Enzymes (CAZy) database and Fungal Oxidative Lignin enzymes (FOLy) database were performed. Protein domains and functional sites were predicted by InterProScan. KEGG orthology identifiers were assigned and biological pathways were associated by KEGG Automatic Annotation Server (KAAS). Gene Ontology (GO) terms were assigned to genes by inferring GO terms of assigned Pfam protein domains. 3. To characterize transcript profiles for annotation refinement at transcript level We have sequenced the transcriptome of 9 different developmental stages of L. edodes to capture a wide variety of expressed genes. Sequencing reads were aligned to L54A reference genome to identify precise splice junctions using TopHat. Splice junctions identified from all sampled stages were used to further refine L. edodes gene prediction using AUGUSTUS. 4. To identify light-responsive genes by transcript profiling Comparing the transcript profile of normal light-grown fruiting body and dark-grown white fruiting body, 1701 genes were up-regulated and 1211 genes were down-regulated in dark-grown conditions. Differential expression of genes encoding priA, anthranilate synthase, mitochondrial-processing peptidase subunit beta, laccase 1 and MAP kinase were confirmed by quantitative RT-PCR. 5. To identify potential molecular markers for genetic, breeding, and other horticultural uses A total of 5116 Simple sequence repeat (SSR) motifs of 2 to 6 repeats were identified from the genome sequence. We have developed 63 polymorphic SSR markers. To facilitate rapid molecular determination of A mating type, we developed two intron-length polymorphism (ILP) markers, ILP-Lea1 and ILP-Lea2 based on the two A mating-type genes (Lea1 and Lea2) sequence.

467810.label: Major findings and research outcome
467810.value: For computational analysis of mushroom genomes, we have built the Comparative Mushroom Genomics Platform. It is an Ensembl-based platform, equipped with a battery of genomic analysis tools, including GBrowse, BioMart, Galaxy and BLAST. The platform allows users to browse and compare gene annotations from the 19 fungal genomes covered, particularly mushroom-forming Basidiomycetes. We have annotated the L. edodes genome and compared with other fungal genomes. Comparison of the sets of FOLymes and CAZymes among basidiomycetes revealed the unique lignocellulolytic system of L. edodes. Differential expression of the genes at various developmental stages and different media suggested that different roles of these genes during the development of L. edodes (Wong et al., 2011). Comparative analyses on all available genome sequences of basidiomycetes and ascomycetes revealed genes expanded in genomes of mushroom-forming fungi. The expanded genes included specific types of regulatory proteins, ubiquitin ligases, protein kinases, and transcription factors (Kwan et al., 2013, 2014). Transcriptomic analysis of multiple stages of L. edodes revealed genes differentially expressed during fruiting body initiation and development. Transcriptome age index (TAI) profile and transcriptome divergence index (TDI) profile showed molecular hourglass patterns over the developmental lifecycle of L. edodes (Kwan et al., 2014). Such developmental hourglass patterns were also observed in the model mushroom Coprinopsis cinerea. The findings represented the first evidence that the developmental hourglass concept also applied to the fungal kingdom of life, in addition to animals and plants (Cheng et al., 2015). We identified the A mating-type locus from the first draft genome sequence of L. edodes. Two intron-length polymorphism markers were developed to facilitate rapid molecular determination of A mating-type. L. edodes sequences were compared with those of known tetrapolar and bipolar basidiomycete species revealing the atypical genetic structure of L. edodes A mating-type locus (Au et al., 2014). By mapping the genotype of 20 meiotic spores obtained by resequencing to the reference genome we generated, we have constructed the first high-density sequence-based genetic linkage map of L. edodes. The linkage map spanned a total genetic distance of 637.1 cM and contained 13 linkage groups. Two hundred sequence-based markers were placed on the map, with an average marker spacing of 3.4 cM (Au et al., 2013).

467810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
467810.value: The high-density genetic linkage map can serve as the fundamental genetic resource for understanding the genetic determinants of important phenotypes. With the map, we can map quantitative trait loci (QTL) of selected phenotypic traits, for example growth rate and enzyme activities. We can also map expression QTL for any genes of interest by profiling the expression level of the whole transcriptome of a mapping population. By re-sequencing multiple L. edodes strains and mapping to the reference genome sequence, we can explore the genetic relationship among L. edodes strains in a population. Their morphologies and cultivation characteristics can be investigated to link some phenotypes with the genotypes using a Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) approach. The transcript profile of L. edodes can be used to define transcription start sites and reveal developmentally regulated genes at whole-genome level. The expression profiles along the developmental stages can be further analyzed to generate a comprehensive picture of mushroom development.

467810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
467810.value: To facilitate the omics analyses of mushrooms, we compiled the genome sequences and transcriptome of L. edodes and other fungi into an Ensembl-based platform. The platform is equipped with a battery of genomic analysis tools for comparative mushroom genomics. We analyzed the genome of the L. edodes strains by semi-automated genome annotation and transcript profiling. We identified candidate light-responsive genes which provide insights on the light regulation on the development of L. edodes. We proved that the developmental hourglass concept also applied to the fungi, in addition to animals and plants. We developed genetic markers that are useful for phylogenetics analysis, genetic analysis and strain improvement. Our works have generated rich resources for the analysis of genomics and transcriptomics of mushroom-forming fungi. Our study increased the understanding of the molecular mechanisms of mushroom development and evolution.

467910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
467910.value: Cerebellum is the locomotive coordination center in the brain. Purkinje neurons provide the primary output to motor systems for mediating fine control of motor movements and balance. Disruption of the normal differentiation program of the Purkinje neuronss may result in cerebellar degeneration diseases. Very little is known about the molecular control mechanisms underlying the Purkinje neuron differentiation and maintenance in cerebellum. Foxp4, a member in Forkhead box transcription factor family, has been shown to express highly in Purkinje neurons of different developmental stages in developing and adult cerebellum. However, genetic and functional analyses of Foxp4 during cerebellum development have been limited by the early embryonic lethality in the knock-out mutant mice. To circumvent the embryonic lethality limitation, we employed an ex vivo knockdown approach by siRNA mediated gene-silencing in a cerebellar organotypic slice culture system to study the role of Foxp4 in Purkinje neuron differentiation and maintenance. Our novel data show that there was a dramatic reduction in dendrite arbors of developing Purkinje neurons with Foxp4 knockdown. This suggests that Foxp4 is important in the regulation and/or maintenance of Purkinje neuron differentiation during cerebellum development. Therefore, we propose to address directly the in vivo functional roles of Foxp4 in Purkinje neuron development and maintenance using loss-of-function approach by conditional inactivation of Foxp4 specifically in developing and adult cerebellum. Three different Cre-expressing mouse lines will be used to generate conditional Foxp4 mutant mice at different developmental stages of Purkinje neuron for dissecting the roles of Foxp4 in embryonic, neonatal and adult cerebellum. Confocal fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) microscopy and co-immunoprecipitation technologies will be employed to identify the interacting partners of Foxp4 in order to understand the molecular mechanisms of Foxp4 in controlling the Purkinje neuron differentiation program. 小腦是神經系統中的運動協調中心。小腦中Purkinje神經元提供基本神經信號輸出到運動系統來精細調控身體運動和平衡。Purkinje神經元不正常分化可能會導致小腦退化疾病。Purkinje神經元分化和維持的分子調控機制有很許多未知的。Foxp4是一名叉頭框轉錄因子家族成員，已被證明在Purkinje神經元的不同發育階段和成人小腦有高度表達。但是，Foxp4在小腦發展的遺傳和功能分析一直受限於Foxp4基因敲除突變小鼠的早期胚胎死亡。為了規避胚胎致死的限制，我們運用了體外siRNA介導Foxp4基因沉默的方法,在小鼠小腦器官切片培養系統中研究Foxp4在Purkinje神經元分化和維持的作用。我們的新數據發現，在小腦發展過程中Foxp4基因沉默能導使Purkinje神經元的枝喬木有顯著的減少。這表明Foxp4於調節和/或維持小腦Purkinje神經元分化過程和發展是有著重要的功能。因此，我們建議使用條件性Foxp4基因敲除方法直接研究Foxp4在發展中和成人小腦的Purkinje神經元於發展和維持的體內作用。三種不同的Cre酶表達鼠將被用來生成條件性Foxp4突變小鼠,研究Foxp4在不同發育階段(胚胎，新生兒和成人)小腦Purkinje神經元中的作用。共聚焦熒光共振能量轉移（FRET）顯微技術和免疫共沉澱技術將被用來確定Foxp4的分子合作夥伴，以了解Foxp4於Purkinje神經元分化程序的分子機制。

467910.label: Realisation of objectives
467910.value: In this project, we addressed specifically the roles of a Forkhead-box gene, Foxp4, in development, functioning and/or maintenance of Purkinje cells (PC) in cerebellum of mice. For objective (1), we used ‘loss-of-function’ approach to study and analyze the phenotypic consequence of the loss of Foxp4 function during cerebellum development. To circumvent the problem of embryonic lethality of Foxp4 null mice and investigate the roles of Foxp4 specifically in Purkinje cell, we utilized the Cre/loxP approach to ablate Foxp4 gene function in a tissue and temporal specific manner. In order to achieve conditional inactivation of Foxp4 in cerebellum and PCs specifically during different stages of development, we have established different mouse lines: (1) We successfully generated a novel mouse line with conditional Foxp4 null allele by embryonic stem cell gene targeting strategy, (2) En1-Cre transgenic mouse line, (3) Pcp2-Cre transgenic mouse line, (4) Pcp2-CreERT2 transgenic mouse line. We used the proposed breeding schemes to generate the En1-Cre/Foxp4, Pcp2-Cre/Foxp4 and Pcp2-CreERT2/Foxp4 conditional knockout mutant mice for studying of Foxp4 function in cerebellum. Surprisingly, inactivation of Foxp4 in cerebellar primordium and PCs did not result in any impairment of cerebellum patterning and dendritic development in the mouse. Since Foxp4 proteins were highly conserved in structure and expression among different species suggesting an evolutionarily conserved function of Foxp4 proteins across species. We then investigated the effect of Foxp4 knockdown in zebrafish. The knockdown of foxp4 resulted in brain edema and abnormal hindbrain development in zebrafish. These results suggest that foxp4 is essential for the mid-hindbrain boundary and hindbrain development in the zebrafish but not in mouse. Our findings suggest a non-equivalent importance of Foxp4 in hindbrain development across these species. For objective (2), we identified two LIM-homeobox transcription factors Lhx1 and Lhx5 that can interact specifically with Foxp4 through the homeodomain of Lhx1/5 and forkhead domain of Foxp4. Our previous studies (GRF grant CUHK 467707) revealed that Lhx1/5 are required for the dendritic development of PCs in postnatal mouse cerebellum and they co-expresss with Foxp4 in PCs. Thus, we generated a triple knockout mouse of Lhx1/5 and Foxp4 to examine whether Foxp4 works with Lhx1/5 together in synergistic or antagonistic manner when they regulate PC dendritogenesis. However, there are no observable differences between triple KO mice and control mice in behavioral, histological and molecular levels. This indicates that Foxp4 does not work synergistically or antagonistically with Lhx1/5 in the dendritic development of PCs.

467910.label: Major findings and research outcome
467910.value: The forkhead domain transcription factors play critical roles in many aspects of development. Foxp4 is expressed widely in the developing CNS among different species. Although Foxp4 has been shown to play an important role in neurogenesis within the developing spinal cord, its functional role in the brain remains unclear. Our data showed that Foxp4 is expressed very specifically in Purkinje cells of the cerebellum at different stages of development suggesting that it may play important role in Purkinje cell (PC) development and function. However, to our surprise, our genetic study showed that Foxp4 is not required in vivo for cerebellum and PC development in mouse. Since Foxp4 proteins were highly conserved in structure and expression among different species suggesting an evolutionarily conserved function of Foxp4 proteins across species. We also investigated possible Foxp4 function in CNS in another model. Our data provides evidence showing Foxp4 as critical factor regulating the hindbrain development in zebrafish. Knockdown of Foxp4 in zebrafish resulted in malformation of mid-hindbrain boundary and hindbrain patterning. This is the first report on the expression and functional role of Foxp4 in teleost brain development. Our results suggest a differential requirement of Foxp4 in brain development across species. Thus our findings give new insight into our current understanding of the Foxp transcription factors interactions across species. A manuscript of these findings is written up for submission to Int. J. Dev. Biol. (Part C8 item1). We also identified two LIM-homeobox transcription factors Lhx1 and Lhx5 that can interact specifically with Foxp4 through the homeodomain of Lhx1/5 and forkhead domain of Foxp4. Our previous studies indicate that Lhx1/5 are required for the dendritic development of PCs in postnatal mouse cerebellum so we suggest that Lhx1/5-Foxp4 interaction may play some roles in dendritic development of PCs. Thus, we generated a triple knockout mouse of Lhx1/5 and Foxp4 to examine whether Foxp4 works with Lhx1/5 together in synergistic or antagonistic manner when they regulate PC dendritogenesis. However, there are no observable differences between triple knockout mice and control mice in behavioral, histological and molecular levels. This indicates that Foxp4 does not work synergistically or antagonistically with Lhx1/5 in the dendritic development of PCs. Our findings suggest that Lhx1/5 interact specially with Foxp4 but their interaction does not play role in regulating the dendritic development of PCs. A manuscript of these findings is written up for submission to Neural Development (Part C8 item2).

467910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
467910.value: One of the possible explanations for the lack of observable phenotypes in the Foxp4 conditional knockout mice is the functional redundancy of other forkhead box subfamily P genes in the dendritic development of Purkinje cells. Since Foxp2 is expressed in the cerebellum and Purkinje cells and indeed previous studies have revealed that mutation in Foxp2 gene also disrupt the dendritic development of Purkinje cells, it is very likely that the presence of Foxp2 can compensate the functions of Foxp4 in the conditional Foxp4 knockout mouse cerebellum. Thus, to investigate the functional significance of Foxp4 interaction, we are planning to import the Foxp2 knockout mice line to generate the Foxp2/4 double knockout mutant that would help to resolve if functional compensation by Foxp2 exists during cerebellum and/or Purkinje cell development. This would also give further insight into how different forkhead box P genes interact and regulate the cerebellum and Purkinje cell development.

467910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
467910.value: Neurological disorders and degeneration leads to devastating conditions in those patients and is becoming a global health care concern as the expected longevity of people in the coming future. Understanding of the regulatory control of neural system development and functioning shall benefit the patients in a long term. In order to understand the molecular mechanism of Purkinje neuron developmental program, we investigated the functional role of a transcription factor, Foxp4, expressed in the Purkinje neurons of cerebellum. We found that Foxp4 is important in the teleost hindbrain development, but not in that of mammals. Our findings suggest a non-equivalent importance of Foxp4 in hindbrain development across different species and there may be gene compensation for the function of Foxp4 in mammals. Thus, our study gives new insight into the interaction between similar Foxp genes in the neural system development in different species.

468110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468110.value: Background: Older diabetic people are at greater risk of cognitive decline than non-diabetic people. Vitamin B12 deficiency in older people is associated with cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s disease. Vitamin B12 deficiency may therefore contribute to cognitive decline in older diabetic people. Objective: To determine whether the correction of mild vitamin B12 deficiency in cognitively normal older diabetic people reduces the incidence of cognitive decline. Design: randomized, double blind, placebo controlled trial Subject: 536 cognitively normal diabetic outpatients aged 75 years or older with mild vitamin B12 deficiency (plasma vitamin B12 150-250 pmol/L and serum methylmalonic acid ≥ 0.4 µmol/L), recruited from medical and family medicine/ general outpatient clinics in one health region of Hong Kong. Method: Subjects will be randomly assigned to take either one capsule of vitamin B12 1 mg or one placebo capsule daily for 27 months. Randomization will be stratified by mini mental state examination score (MMSE) of 25. Follow-up will be performed at 9, 18, 27 month. The primary endpoint is the incidence of cognitive impairment or dementia, as indicated by Clinical dementia rating scale. Secondary outcomes include Alzheimer disease assessment scale (cognitive subscale) and Chinese executive interview. Data analysis: Generalized estimating equations (GEE) model will be used to compare the trial groups in the proportions of subjects reaching the primary outcome. Subgroup analysis on subjects with better cognitive function (MMSE >25)will be performed. Background: Older diabetic people are at greater risk of cognitive decline than non-diabetic people. Vitamin B12 deficiency in older people is associated with cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s disease. Vitamin B12 deficiency may therefore contribute to cognitive decline in older diabetic people. Objective: To determine whether the correction of mild vitamin B12 deficiency in cognitively normal older diabetic people reduces the incidence of cognitive decline. Design: randomized, double blind, placebo controlled trial Subject: Cognitively normal diabetic outpatients aged 75 years or older with plasma vitamin B12 150-220 pmol/L in medical and family medicine/ general outpatient clinics in Shatin and Ma On Shan area. Procedure: After excluding those with clinical manifestations of vitamin B12 deficiency and without family member who can reliably inform on cognitive functioning (personal contact at least once a week), eligible patients will be invited to participate in this clinical trial. After obtaining written consent, research assistant (RA) will record demographic and clinical information from the subjects and perform neuropsychological tests – 1. Clinical dementia rating scale (CDR), 2. Chinese Mini mental state examination (MMSE), 3. Geriatric depression scale (GDS). Fasting blood will be taken for serum methylmalonic acid (MMA) and significant comorbidities. Those with cognitive impairment and significant comorbidities will be excluded. 536 eligible subjects will be randomly assigned to take either one capsule containing vitamin B12 one milligram or an identical looking placebo capsule once daily for 27 months. All subjects or family caregivers are reviewed in the research clinic every 12 weeks in which the research assistant performs a pill count and dispenses the trial capsules. At 9 monthly intervals, the subjects will have CDR and MMSE repeated at research clinic. At month 27, fasting serum MMA and vitamin B12 will be repeated. Statistical analyses: Primary outcome is deterioration in CDR, i.e. from 0 to 0.5 or more. The trial will be terminated when subjects develop dementia (CDR 1 or more) at any stage of the trial. The secondary outcomes include the sum of CDR boxes, MMSE and serum MMA. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) model will be employed to adjust age, gender and other possibly confounding variables for comparing the changes on various outcomes across the time points at 0, 9, 18 and 27 months between the two groups. All statistical tests are two-sided and a p-value < 0.05 is considered statistically significant. Subgroup analysis will be performed on those with good cognitive function (MMSE>25). 背景：年長的糖尿病患者是比非糖尿病患者有較高的智能衰退風險，缺乏維他命B12與智能障礙和阿氏痴呆症有關，所以缺乏維他命B12可能引致年長的糖尿病患者智能衰退。 目標：以確定補充維他命B12能否減低智力正常的年長糖尿病患者智能衰退的發生。 設計：安慰劑隨機抽樣對照臨床研究 對象：在沙田及馬鞍山區的內科和家庭醫學/ 普通科門診的75歲或以上的智能正常糖尿病門診病人，及維他命B12血漿水平在150-220 pmol/L。 程序：如有臨床維他命B12缺乏的症狀或沒有家人可以提供關於智力的資料，合資格的病人會被邀請參加這個臨床研究。經參加者書面同意後，研究員會記錄個人資料和病歷，及作以下的心理智能測試：簡短智能測驗(CDR)，癡呆症臨床評估(MMSE) ，老人抑鬱量表，然後抽血檢查甲基丙二酸水平。 536名合適的參加者會被隨機分配每天服用維他命B12一毫克或安慰劑，為期27個月，參加者或家人每12個星期到研究診所領取研究藥物，同時會檢查剩下來的藥丸數目，每9個月患者會和家人接受CDR和MMSE的測試，第27個月參加者會被抽血檢查維他命B12和甲基丙二酸血漿水平。 首要結果是智能衰退的發生：CDR分數由0增加到0.5或以上。如參加者在研究過程中被證實患有痴呆症，研究將被終止。

468110.label: Realisation of objectives
468110.value: The recruitment has been more difficult than expected. After a lot of effort over two years, the proposed number of subjects was recruited. The trial is progressing as planned, and the power of the trial to detect effects of vitamin B12 supplementation has been strengthened by the addition of MRI brain scans which can estimate brain atrophy rate. An interim analysis of cognitive outcomes at month 18 has been performed and the results are encouraging. A paper is being submitted to report our findings and a grant is being sought to support an open label extension trial of 18 months after this randomized trial. This 27 month randomized trial is due to be completed in December 2015. As such, the original objectives can only be fully achieved then. But thanks to the support of this GRF, much has been accomplished. More time for follow-up is required to achieve the stated objectives. (Revised objectives were entered by mistake. They were changes in protocol rather than changes in objectives)

468110.label: Major findings and research outcome
468110.value: Between August 2011 and September 2013, 1534 medical outpatients were screened. Out of these, 272 subjects were randomized into active and placebo treatment groups. As at September 2014, 54 subjects completed the 27 month trial, 40 having dropped out (14.8%; 24 in active treatment group and 16 in placebo group),The reasons for dropout included: Died (N=3), patient withdraw (N=28), prescribe B vitamin (N=4), requested by doctor (N=3), terminal illness (N=1), CVA (N=1). 158 subjects completed follow-up assessment at month 18. Interim analysis showed that the subjects in both trial groups were well matched, without any significant difference in clinical characteristics, vitamin B12 and folate status and neurocognitive scores at baseline. Fasting serum homocysteine at baseline was raised (> 13 umol/L) in 75% of subjects and methylmalonic acid was raised (0.3 umol/L) in 24%. These suggested that the subjects had mild metabolic vitamin B12 deficiency. Repeat serum homocysteine at month 9 showed that methycobalamin was effective in correcting vitamin B12 deficiency (average fell from 16.3 to 11.6 umol/L, P<0.0001), while serum homocysteine was not significantly altered in placebo group. At month 18, 3 out of 80 (3.75%) active treatment group and 6 out of 78 (7.69%) placebo treatment group had cognitive decline as defined by an increase in dementia rating scale global score. The difference was not statistically significant (P=0.285, Pearson Chi square test). Among those with high MMSE (>26), 2 out 49 in active treatment group versus 5 out of 44 in placebo group had cognitive decline (P=0.184) The changes in other neurocognitive test scores were not significantly different between the trial groups at month 9 and 18 follow-up visits. We therefore conclude that vitamin B12 supplementation in mild deficient older diabetic outpatients showed a slight trend of protection against cognitive decline at month 18, especially in those with good cognitive function. The trial is on-going.

468110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
468110.value: A paper to report on the findings of this interim analysis is under preparation. The 27 month trial will be completed in December 2015. With PI’s resources, 178 subjects (92 in active treatment and 86 in placebo treatment) had volumetric MRI brain scan. MRI brain scans will be repeated at month 27. These data will allow the comparison between the trial group subjects in the rate of brain atrophy. In addition, all subjects are started on methycobalamin and will be followed nine monthly for another 18 months. This open label extension trial will address the question if delay in vitamin B12 supplementation may result in higher risk of cognitive decline. A further grant will be sought to fund this extension trial and the follow-up MRI brain scans, so that the effect of delayed supplementation on brain atrophy rate can also be examined.

468110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
468110.value: With a lot of effort, the targeted number of subjects was recruited into the randomized placebo controlled trial of vitamin B12 supplementation to prevent cognitive decline in older diabetic patients with mild vitamin B12 deficiency. The trial subjects were well matched in clinical characteristics. The 27 month trial is on-going. The dropout rate of 14.8% is within expectation. Interim analysis on available data in the first 18 months of follow-up suggested a trend of protection against cognitive decline with vitamin B12 supplementation, especially in those with better cognitive function. In addition to cognitive outcomes, with PI’s other funding resources, volumetric MRI scans of the brain were performed in two thirds of the subjects at baseline and will be repeated at month 27. The analysis of these scans will provide valuable information on the effect of vitamin B12 supplementation on the rate of brain atrophy, which is a more sensitive marker of brain degeneration. A paper to report on this interim analysis is being submitted to an international journal for publication. More papers are expected with the completion of the trial and the MRI scan analysis.

468610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468610.value: Soybean is an important cash crop that is a major source of dietary oil and protein. Due to its symbiotic nitrogen fixation ability, it can be used as a component of most environment friendly and sustainable farming practices. Mapping and identification of loci/genes regulating important agronomic traits will aid the process of marker-assisted breeding and transgenic technology. Previous researches were restricted by the suboptimal marker density of QTL maps, due to the limitation of genotypic and phenotypic diversity in the genetic population employed and lack of complete genomic sequence information. We previously constructed a recombinant inbred population which was resulted from a cross between a wild soybean and a cultivated soybean. A rich biodiversity was observed in the RI lines which are now at F9. In addition, we will soon complete a soybean genomic sequencing project that will provide proprietary genome sequence information of the two parents of the RI population. Using this unique genetic population and genomic sequence information, together with the recent advance in high-throughput sequencing technology, we propose to adopt a new approach of genotyping by whole genome re-sequencing. 468610.label: Realisation of objectives
468610.value: We have successfully completed all objectives. We built a framework of recombination breakpoints of a core panel of 96 RI lines using 983 valid SSR markers (Objective 1). Subsequently, we performed high-throughput genotyping of this core panel by low level whole-genome sequencing. A total of 2577 bin markers were obtained (Objective 2). We recorded 18 agronomic traits from the core panel RI lines and the two parents from different years (Objective 3). We identified 21 major QTLs for 15 agronomic traits (Objective 4), including seed antioxidant content seed anthocyanin content, pod number per plant, seed number per plant, growth period, salt tolerance seed coat color, pod color, trailing growth, leaf length/width ratio, susceptibility to Sinorhizobium, nodule weight, root weight, total weight, and ureides content. However, no major QTLs are found for seed oil content, seed protein content, 100-seed weight, leaf area, plant height, node number and branch number. QTLs related to nitrogen fixation are further studies due to their importance in controlling seed nutrition.

468610.label: Major findings and research outcome
468610.value: Background genomic study: As indicated in the background of our proposal, we were performing whole-genome sequencing research for wild and cultivated soybean germplasms to facilitate this study. This part was finished at the initiation stage of this GRF project (published in Nature Genetics 42:1053-1059; not attached in this report). The major findings include: (1) there is a high allelic diversity in wild soybeans; (2) a high level of linkage disequilibrium exists in soybean genome, 205,614 tag SNPs found may be useful for QTL mapping. Subsequently, we support the high biodiversity of wild soybean genomes by performing whole genome nonreference transposons analysis (Publication #2). To understand the genomic changes under domestication and subsequent breeding program, we identified fixed nucleotides in cultivated and wild soybean and analyzed their impacts during soybean domestication and further improvement (Publication #6). We also reported how whole-genome-sequencing information could expedite the identification of DNA markers in crops, which are important for breeding practice (Publication #7). QTLs, genes and gene families: We identified 21 major QTLs for 15 agronomic traits. Eleven QTLs for 15 traits were reported in Publication #5, including seed antioxidant content seed anthocyanin content, pod number per plant, seed number per plant, growth period, salt tolerance seed coat color, pod color, trailing growth, leaf length/width ratio, and susceptibility to different Sinorhizobium strians. Analyses of QTLs related to the nitrogen fixation process led to another manuscript under review (Publications #9). These QTLs include nodule weight, root weight, total weight, and ureides content. Maturation time is an important trait in soybean production. In relation to a maturation locus we identified, we studied the polymorphism of a maturity gene GmFT2a in soybean. Although GmFT2a is a key flowering gene, GmFT2a polymorphism does not appear to be responsible for maturity diversity in soybean. (Publication #4). Pathogens will cause a stress to soybean, resulting in lowering of seed yield and seed nutrition quality. Making use of our genomic data and other legume genomic data available to us, we investigated the molecular phylogeny ad dynamic evolution of disease resistance genes in the legume family. The data have been used to compose another manuscript (Publication #10). Tools: To facilitate the study and future research, we performed comprehensive surveys on research tools that are available for soybean researches. We covered a wide range of technologies including bioinformatics, genomics, genetic mapping, epigenomic, and proteomics (Publications #1,3,8).

468610.value: We demonstrated that wild soybeans are important genetic resources due to the high diversity of their genomes. We constructed a genetic population using a wild and a cultivation soybean parent. Genotyping and phenotyping of a core panel of this genetic population enables us to identify major quantitative trait loci that regulate important agronomic traits.

468810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468810.value: This study is aimed to identify and characterize the novel glaucoma-associated gene in the GLC1M locus. Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a progressive optic neuropathy that would lead to severe and irreversible visual impairment if not treated early and appropriately. Its occurrence is pan-ethnic. About 2% of the world’s population is affected. The genetics of POAG is known to be complex, with both monogenic and multifactorial etiology. Other risk factors include age and cigarette smoking. However, there is a subset of POAG that appears earlier in life, even at teenage. Such patients are often inherited in an autosomal dominant manner and have more serious clinical conditions. Three genes have been identified for POAG, MYOC, OPTN, and WDR36, but together they account for less than 10% of POAG in the Chinese population. Another 19 loci for POAG are now known without identification of the underlying gene defects. Our whole genome scan and linkage analysis on a juvenile-onset POAG pedigree has led to the identification of the GLC1M locus for POAG at 5q22.1-q32. Involvement of MYOC, OPTN, and WDR36 genes has been ruled out in this family. In this application we propose first to conduct a fine mapping study with microsatellite and SNP markers to further confine the locus to a narrowed region. We shall then carry out positional cloning to identify the gene responsible for glaucoma in the pedigree. Priority will be given to the genes that are expressed in the eye tissues, involved in the possible functional pathways of POAG, and related to glaucoma or other relevant neurodegenerative diseases. When screening the prioritized candidate genes for mutations, we will also analyze the copy numbers of these genes to detect a possibly existing gene dosage effect related to glaucoma. Specific disease-causing mutations in target genes will be explored in POAG families and unrelated POAG patients, all of whom would have been excluded for MYOC, OPTN, and WDR36 gene mutations. Functional analysis will be conducted to characterize the novel glaucoma gene and investigate the impact of mutations on the gene. We should be able to identify and characterize a novel glaucoma gene. Amid the present limited genetic information for POAG and the small proportion of POAG patients with known genetic cause, functions and properties of a new glaucoma gene will give valuable insight into a better understanding of the pathogenesis of glaucoma. 本研究旨在明確位於GLC1M位點一新的青光眼相關基因。原發性開角型青光眼 POAG）是一種進行性視神經病變，如未予及時有效的治療將導致嚴重的不可逆轉 的視覺障礙。該疾病存在于各種族人群，全球約2%的人口罹患此病。POAG的遺傳 特徵複雜，既有單基因遺傳又有多因素遺傳，其他的風險因素包括年齡、吸煙。然 而POAG存在一種亞型，發病年齡較早，甚至出現在青少年時期。這樣的病人通常表 現為常染色體顯性遺傳且具有較為嚴重的臨床特徵。目前已經明確的三個POAG相關 基因，分別是MYOC、 OPTN和 WDR36，但是，在中國人群中，由以上三個基因 導致的POAG所占比例不足10%。此外已知的19個與POAG相關的位點中並未發現潛 在的致病基因。通過對一個青少年發病的POAG家系的全基因組掃描和連鎖分析，我 們發現了一個與POAG相關的基因位點—GLC1M位於5q22.1-q32。在此家系中並未發 現MYOC、OPTN和WDR36基因突變。在本提案中我們擬定首先應用SNP和微衛星標 記進行精細定位研究，以進一步將其限制到一個狹小的區域。接下來進行定位克隆, 以明確該青光眼家系中的致病基因。我們將會優先選擇那些在眼組織中表達，參與 了POAG可能的功能途徑，以及與青光眼或其他神經退行性疾病相關的基因。在篩選 這些候選基因的過程中，我們將進一步分析這些基因的拷貝數以此來測定其與青光 眼可能存在基因劑量效應。對於以上目標基因中發現的特定的致病基因突變，我們 隨後將在其他POAG家系及無關聯的POAG病人中進行檢測，在此之前首先排除 MYOC、OPTN和WDR36的基因突變的可能。我們將採用功能性分析進一步明確這 個新的青光眼基因，並研究此基因突變對青光眼發病的影響。借此我們將可以識別 和發現一種新的青光眼致病基因。目前對於POAG的遺傳信息所知有限，能夠已知遺 傳原因的POAG患者所占比重較小，因此明確一個新的青光眼基因的功能和特點將會 為更好的瞭解青光眼的發病機制提供有價值的見解。

468810.label: Realisation of objectives
468810.value: We have refined the linkage region at GLC1M and showed that the coding sequences, splice sites and CNV of the SPARCgene at the GLC1M locus did not contribute to primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG).To identify new glaucoma gene(s), we have joined an international collaborative genome-wide association study of POAG, and identified the CAV1/CAV2 genes as new associated genes for POAG. Moreover, we found that the minor allele frequency of the CAV1 rs4236601 was much lower than that in the Caucasians, revealing different frequencies of sequence alterations in the new glaucoma genes in local Chinese population. Also, we have performed a mutation screening of the NTF4 gene, and identified two novel missense variants, p.Gly157Ala and p.Ala182Val, in POAG patients, but not in controls, suggesting that they could be disease causing mutations. The frequency of these two variants was less than 0.5%, which was different from the mutation frequency of NTF4 in Caucasians (>1%). Furthermore, we investigated the associations between gene variants in CYP46A1, LMX1B, PLXDC2, TLR4, TMTC2, ZP4, chromosome 2p16.3, and POAG, and revealed different association patterns of these candidate SNPs in the 7 genes/loci with POAG in Chinese. We showed that rs1533428 at 2p16.3 and TLR4 rs7037117 are potential markers of POAG and that rs1533428 is a putative risk variant for late-onset POAG. The identification of an age-specific association between rs1533428 and late-onset POAG highlights a new genotype-phenotype association in POAG. . With all these findings, we have enriched the understanding the POAG genetics and largely addressed the objectives of the granted study. However, due to the complexity of POAG genetics, we have not yet pinpointed the disease-causing gene at the GLC1M locus. Withthe advent of the next-generation sequencing technology, we are planning to perform target sequencing of the GLC1M locus, with an aim to identify all coding variants within the locus, which will allow segregation analysis in the GLC1M-linked family and improve the opportunity of identifying the causative gene in the GLC1M locus.

468810.value: 1. We reported that the coding sequences, splice sites and copy number of theSPARCgene at the GLCM1 locus did not contribute to POAGin Molecular Vision (2010;16:2016-25).In this study, we found no putative SPARC mutation in the GLC1M-linked family. In the cohort of unrelated Chinese participants, we detected 11 sequence variants, two of which were novel: IVS2+8G>T and IVS2+32C>T. For the 9 known SNPs, one was synonymous (rs2304052, p.Glu22Glu) and the others were located in noncoding regions. No individual SNP was associated with POAG. Five of the most common SNPs, i.e., rs2116780, rs1978707, rs7719521, rs729853, and rs1053411, were contained in a linkage disequilibrium block. Haplotype-based analysis showed that no haplotype was associated with the disorder. Copy number analysis revealed that all study subjects had two copies of the gene, suggesting no correlation between the copy number of SPARC and POAG. 2. To identify new glaucoma genes, we joined an international collaborative genome-wide association study of POAG, and identified a common sequence variant at 7q31 (rs4236601[A], odds ratio (OR) = 1.36, P = 5.0 × 10-10) to be strongly associated with POAG. We then replicated the association in 299 POAG cases and 580 unaffected controls from Hong Kong and Shantou, China (combined OR = 5.42, P = 0.0021).The OR was larger in Chinese, but the minor allele frequency of rs4236601 was much lower than that in Caucasian. These findings were reported in Nature Genetics (2010;42(10):906-9). 3.We have performed a mutation screening of the NTF4 gene and identified two novel missense variants, p.Gly157Ala and p.Ala182Val, in POAG patients but not in controls, suggesting they could be disease causing mutations. The frequency of these two variants was less than 0.5%, suggesting a lower mutation frequency of NTF4 in Chinese than in Caucasians (>1%). These findings were reported in Molecular Vision (2012;18:1763-72). 4. We have investigated the associations between POAG and variants in CYP46A1, LMX1B, PLXDC2, TLR4, TMTC2, ZP4, chromosome 2p16.3.We revealed discrepant association patterns of SNPs in the 7 genes/loci with POAG in Chinese, provided positive evidence for POAG markers rs1533428 at 2p16.3 and TLR4 rs7037117, and suggested that rs1533428 is a putative risk variant for late-onset POAG. These findings were reported in Molecular Vision (2012; 18:1629-39).

468810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
468810.value: Primary open angle glaucoma (POAG) is a leading cause of irreversible visual impairment in Hong Kong. Multiple risk factors, including genetic factors, are involved in the pathogenesis of POAG. We had previously identified a gene locus, GLC1M, that may harbor disease-causing genes for POAG. In the present study, we aimed to identify the disease-causinggenes for POAG in local Chinese. We first tested the SPARC gene as causal gene at GLC1M.However, we found that gene variations in SPARC did not contribute to POAG. In another mutation screening study, we identified two new mutations in the NTF4 gene, which account for about 0.5% of POAG in Hong Kong Chinese. We also investigated susceptibility genes for POAG. We have identified a new gene (CAV1/CAV2) for POAG, and found that a variant increased the risk of POAG by about 5 folds in Chinese. In another study, we found genetic markers on chromosomal region 2p16.3 and the TLR4 gene increased the risk of POAG by about 2 folds.These new findings haveenriched our knowledge of the genetic causes of POAG and provided new genetic markers for further investigation of its pathogenesis which would afford new insights into new treatment strategies of glaucoma.
