469110.value: TGF-beta抑制新月體性腎小球腎炎的機制研究:調節性T細胞的作用

469110.label: Project Objectives
469110.value: To determine whether TGF-beta1-induced suppression of crescentic GN is mediated via a Treg-dependent mechanism in TGF-beta1 Tg mice. We have previously shown that latent TGF-beta1 Tg mice (K5.TGF-beta1wt Tg mice) are protected against crescentic GN. In this specific aim, we will test the working hypothesis that TGF-beta1 may induce Treg to suppress crescentic GN by inhibiting Th1 and Th17 immune responses. This will be performed in a mouse model of crescentic GN induced in TGF-beta1 Tg or Wt mice. Adoptive transfer studies will determine whether the Treg population(CD4+CD25+LAP+) in TGF-β Tg mice is responsible for suppression of crescentic GN. The mechanisms underlying suppression of crescentic GN by latent TGF-beta1 and antigen-specific Tregs will be examined. To examine whether a lack of Tregs is a major cause of Th2/Th17-mediated necrotizing GN in Smad3-/- mice. We have recently observed that deletion of Smad3 in mice resulted in a switch from a Th1 to a Th2/Th17-mediated GN characterized by an absence of glomerular crescents while developing severe necrotizing GN. In this specific aim, we will test the working hypothesis that TGF-beta1 may signal through Smad3 to induce Treg, thereby inhibiting Th2/Th17-mediated necrotizing GN. This will be performed in a mouse model of crescentic GN induced in Smad3-/- or Smad3+/+ mice. Role of Smad3 in regulating Treg immune response in GN will be determined by adoptive transfer of Smad3+/+ Tregs. To explore the protective role and therapeutic potential for Tregs in crescentic GN in Foxp3 Tg mice. In this specific aim, we will determine the protective role of Tregs in Th1, Th2, and Th17-mediated crescentic GN induced in Foxp3 Tg mice. Furthermore, the therapeutic role of Tregs will be determined in established crescentic GN by adoptive transfer of different populations of Tregs.

469110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
469110.value: Rapidly progressive crescentic glomerulonephritis is a devastating illness leading to end-stage renal failure within weeks. Biopsy studies and animal models have established a major role for T cell immunity in this disease. However, current therapy is limited due to severe side-effects of immunosuppressive drugs. Thus, there is a critical need to develop more safe, effective, and sepcific therapies. Recent studies have identified three different types of T cells that can cause glomerulonephritis, termed Th1, Th2 and Th17. Crescentic glomerulonephritis is mediated by Th1, while necrotizing glomerulonephritis is caused by Th2, and the precise role of the Th17 has yet to be established. The action of these effector T cells is balanced by regulatory T cells (Tregs) which can suppress T cell functions, thus providing an important control mechanism in T cell-mediated diseases. However, little is known of whether crescent glomerulonephritis results from a failure of Treg function and whether the disease can be suppressed by adoptive transfer of Tregs. Transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) is important for expansion of the Treg population, while directly inhibiting effector T cell function. However, mechanisms of TGF-bete1 in regulating T cell immunity in crescentic glomerulonephritis remains unclear. Our exciting new data has identified that mice overexpressing TGF-beta1 (TGF-beta-Tg mice) are protected from crescentic glomerulonephritis which is associated with an enhanced Tregs while suppressing the Th1 and Th17 immune responses. Furthermore, our preliminary data indicates that deletion of the Smad3 gene (Smad3 KO) in mice results in a switch from a Th1-mediated crescentic glomerulonephritis to a Th2/Th17-mediated necrotizing glomerulonephritis which is associated with a deficiency in Treg function. These novel findings reveal a critical role for TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in T cell-mediated glomerulonephritis. Thus, we hypothesize that TGF-beta1 may induce Treg to suppress crescentic glomerulonephritis via a Smad3-dependent mechanism. This project will test this hypothesis in a mouse model of crescentic glomerulonephritis induced in TGF-beta1-Tg and Smad3 KO mice. Furthermore, the protective role of Tregs in crescentic glomerulonephritis will be examined in Foxp3 Tg mice (higher Tregs) and a novel therapy for crescentic glomerulonephritis will be explored by adoptive transfer of different populations of Tregs. The ultimate significance of this proposal will define novel mechanisms by which TGF-beta acts by stimulating Smad3 to induce Tregs, thereby suppressing Th1, Th2, and Th17-mediated glomerulonephritis and determine the potential for Treg-based immunotherapy for crescentic glomerulonephritis. 新月體性腎小球腎炎是一種伴有嚴重腎功能衰竭的急性進展性腎炎，目前尚無特異性的有效治療措施，主要與其發病機制尚未完全明確有關。因此，研究新月體性腎小球腎炎的發病機制及尋找更為安全，特異，副作用小的治療方法是目前相當緊迫的任務。 近期人體和動物實驗研究結果提示T 細胞免疫是新月體性腎小球腎炎的主要發病機制。研究發現有三種不同類型的T細胞與腎小球腎炎發病有關，其分別為Th1, Th2及Th17。其中，Th1介導新月體性腎小球腎炎發生，而Th2與壞死性腎小球腎炎密切相關，但Th17在腎小球腎炎發病過程中所起具體作用仍不明確，需進一步研究。調節性T細胞（Treg）通過抑制T細胞功能，調節平衡各種效應T細胞作用，是T細胞介導性疾病的重要調控機制。但是，新月體性腎小球腎炎發病是否是由於Treg功能失活導致,以及是否能夠通過轉移Treg抑制疾病過程，目前極少研究報告。轉化生長因數-β1（TGF-β1）直接抑制效應T細胞功能，在Treg增殖中起到重要作用，但其在新月體性腎小球腎炎中調控T細胞免疫的機制仍不明確。 通過本研究組的前期試驗，我們成功的發現， TGF-β1轉基因小鼠(TGFβ1-Tg）能夠抑制Th1及Th17免疫反應活性，增強Tregs活性，從而抑制新月體性腎小球腎炎發病。另外， Smad3 基因敲除小鼠 (Smad3 KO) 從Th1介導的新月體性腎小球腎炎轉換成Th2/Th17介導的壞死性腎小球腎炎，此現象與Treg功能失活有關。上述新發現提示TGF-β/Smad3信號通路在T細胞介導的腎小球腎炎發病過程中起主要作用。基於上述研究結果，我們假設TGF-β1通過依賴Smad3途徑誘導Treg產生，進一步抑制新月體性腎小球腎炎。本研究將通過在TGFβ1-Tg及Smad3 KO小鼠身上建立新月體性腎小球腎炎小鼠模型來驗證此假說。在此基礎上，通過Foxp3 轉基因小鼠（Tregs數量增加）探討Tregs對新月體性腎小球腎炎的保護作用，並且通過轉移療法將不同數量的Tregs輸入動物體內，觀察其治療新月體性腎小球腎炎療效。根據上述研究結果，本項目將闡明TGF-β通過活化Smad3誘導Tregs產生，從而抑制Th1, Th2,及Th17介導的腎小球腎炎發病此重要機制，並為以Treg為基礎免疫治療新月體性腎小球腎炎提供佐證，最終為新月體性腎小球腎炎提供潛在的安全有效特異的治療方法。

469110.label: Realisation of objectives
469110.value: We have completed all three Specific Aims as described above. Results obtained from this study demonstrated that in contrast to active form of TGF-beta1 which is pathogenic in renal fibrosis, latent TGF-beta1 can induce Tregs to suppress crescentic GN by inhibiting Th1 and Th17 immune responses. The induction of Treg by TGF-beta1 is Smad3-dependent since deletion of Smad3 from mice resulted in a loss of Treg and impaired T cell immunity by switching the Th1-mediated crescentic GN to the Th2/Th17-driven necrotizing GN. Thus, Smad3 is a key downstream transcriptional factor of TGF-beta/Smad signaling responsible for the T cell differentiation and functions during GN. Finally, we found that TGF-beta1 induces Foxp3 to negatively regulate T cell-mediated crescentic anti-GBM GN via a Treg-dependent mechanism. Outcomes from this study have resulted in an International Young Nephrologist Award to a PhD student YANG Chen in the World Congress of Nephrology (May 30-June 4, 2014). Because the proposed studies with 3 Specific Aims are very comprehensive involving the generation of three transgenic/knockout mouse models and many cell transfer studies and advanced technologies. However, the budget is small and enough for a full PhD student scholarship with some help from other students/staff. Thus, although all the animal work can be completed as originally scheduled within 3 years, analysis of the huge data base from three-independent animal models takes longer time than the original plan. Nevertheless, we are now in the final stage of data analysis and will submit two additional important manuscripts as soon as possible.

469110.label: Major findings and research outcome
469110.value: We have completed the Specific Aim 1 and found that latent TGF-beta1 induced suppression of crescentic glomerulonephritis (GN) via a Treg-dependent mechanism in a mouse model of anti-GBM crescentic GN induced in TGF-beta1 transgenic (Tg) mice. An increase in Treg immune response in TGF-beta1 Tg mice was associated with suppression of both Th1 and Th17-mediated renal injury. Thus, latent TGF-beta1 may induce Tregs to suppress crescentic GN by inhibiting Th1 and Th17 immune responses. 2. We have also completed the Specific Aim 2 and found that deletion of Smad3 from mice impaired T cell immunity by the switching the Th1-mediated creascentic GN to the Th2/Th17-driven necrotizing GN. Loss of Treg was a major cause of this immune switching. Thus, Smad3 is a key downstream transcriptional factor of TGF-beta/Smad signaling responsible for the T cell differentiation and functions during GN. TGF-beta1 induces Treg via the Smad3-dependent mechanism and Smad3 is an essential regulator in controlling the balance between Th1 versus Th2/Th17 immune responses in anti-GBM GN. 3. As described in Specific Aim 3, we have completed the anti-GBM GN mouse model in Foxp3 Tg mice and found that Foxp3 Tg mice exhibited more than 70-80% of CD4+ T cells being Foxp3 positive Treg cells and were protected against crescentic GN. The protective role of Foxp3 in crescentic GN was associated with a marked inhibition of Th1 , Th2 , and Th17 immune responses. Thus, TGF-beta1 induces Foxp3 to negatively regulate T cell-mediated crescentic anti-GBM GN via a Treg-dependent mechanism. Outcomes from this Specific Aim resulted in an International Young Nephrologist Award to a PhD student YANG Chen in the World Congress of Nephrology 2014. After understanding of the role of TGF-beta/Smad signaling in GN, we decided to extend this project by performing an adoptive transfer of Treg cells into Smad3 KO mice. Interestingly, restored Tregs by transferring 1×106 CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ T cells resulted in a switching of the Th2/Th17-mediated necrotizing GN back to the Th1-mediated crescentic GN. More excitingly, transfer of 2×106 Tregs cells produced a great suppression in all Th1,Th2 and Th17 mediated GN, demonstrating a key regulatory role of Treg and a great therapeutic potential of Treg cells for GN. With the support from this GRF, we also extended the original aims to investigate the role of TGF-beta/Smad signaling in renal inflammation in other forms of kidney diseases. In addition, two PhD students (LIU Zhen and YANG Chen) were trained with this GRF support

469110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
469110.value: Based on the results obtained from this project, we have largely extend this study to other TGF-beta-dependent diseases by proposing two major new research projects: 1) we hypothesize that TGF-beta1 may promote cancer via a Smad3-dependent microenvironments, which has resulted in a new GRF grant funded by RGC in 2013(No:468513). We found that deletion of Smad3 largely enhanced NK activities, thereby protecting against cancer growth, invasion, metastasis, and death. This project has resulted in a patent of a Smad3 inhibitor for treatment of Cancer (WO2014/63659A1) which has licensed to Cancelex (www.cancerlex.com). We also propose that TGF-beta/Smad signaling may play a critical regulatory role in allograft rejection. This proposal has resulted in establishing a collaborative study with a renal transplantation team from Zhejiang University. A Research Agreement between the Chinese University of Hong Kong and Zhejiang University on this project has been signed and research project is undergoing in the PI Lab in CUHK.

469110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
469110.value: Crescentic glomerulonephritis (GN) is a progressive form of kidney disease with poor clinical outcomes because of lacking effective treatment. The mechanisms caused this severe form of kidney damage remain largely unclear. Thus, we proposed in this study to identify a protective mechanism and therapeutic potential for kidney injury by investigating a role of TGF-beta Smad signaling pathway in mouse model of crescenticGN in mice. We found that mice overexpressing human latent TGF-beta1 are protected against crsecentic GN by inducing a good T cell subset called T regulatory T cells (Treg). However, deletion of a downstream TGF-beta signaling mediator called Smad3 results in a loss of Treg and developed necrotizing GN with more severe renal injury and death, which can be rescued by transfer of Treg cells. We also found that TGF-beta1 induces Treg via a gene called Foxp3. Thus, mice transgenically overexpressing Foxp3 are also protected against crescentic GN. Taken together, results from this study demonstrate a key regulatory role of TGF-beta/Smad3 in T cell immune responses and Treg as a great therapeutic potential for GN , which are highly significant both scientifically and clinically.

469210.label: Realisation of objectives
469210.value: The three objectives of this project are achieved. For objective 1, we have identified and validated the functional role of Gemin5 in the formation of snRNP assembly by showing Gemin5 interacts with Sm proteins in an orderly manner. Moreover, the affinity of the snRNA increases when Gemin5 binds to Sm proteins, suggesting that Gemin5 mediates the transfer of the RNA to the Sm proteins. In this study, we also dissect the Sm protein interacting domain of Gemin5 and found that it is located at the C-terminus. Combined with the current findings from other group, we now have a more clear picture of how the snRNP assembly occur. For objective 2, we have finished the biochemical study of Gemin8 in the SMN complex. We mapped the interacting domain of Gemin6/7/8, a subcomplex of the SMN complex, and identified the minimum domain of each other. We further recombinantly expressed and purified the minimum Gemin6/7/8 complex and found that it is a hetero-trimer dimer. For objective 3, we identified and validated the telomerase RNA as the novel binding partner of Gemin5. Moreover, we further mapped the region of hTR that interacts with Gemin5. We also investigated the biological functions of Gemin5 in the context of telomerase biogenesis and found that it plays significant roles in telomerase maturation. Intriguingly and unexpectedly, we found that knockdown of Gemin5 will cause the mis-localization of SMN to the hTR, indicating that Gemin5 is the hTR recognition protein in the SMN complex. In summary, our results in this project provides further understanding of the components of the SMN complex in the context of RNP assembly and protein-protein interactions, in particular the RNA recognition protein Gemin5 and subcomplex Gemin6/7/8.

469210.label: Major findings and research outcome
469210.value: Our major findings of this project is the functional role of the RNA recognition protein, Gemin5, in the SMN complex which is the pathogenic proteins of the spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). We provided the biochemical evidence of how the Gemin5 interacts with Sm proteins in the orderly manner through its C-terminal domain. We also found that the presence of the Sm proteins increases the RNA affinity to the Gemin5. These results suggest that the Gemin5 plays a modulation role in passing the RNA to the Sm proteins. Moreover, we believe that Gemin5 may have another roles to unlock the Sm protein complex in the SMN complex during snRNP assembly. Another significant findings in this project is the novel RNA binding partner of Gemin5. We found that telomerase RNA is the novel RNA binding partner of Gemin5 as well as the SMN complex. Gemin5 binds to the 3'end of hTR where is the scaRNA domain and the interacting sites of other H/ACA RNP proteins. Surprisingly, immunoprecipitation of Gemin5 can bring down the telomerase complex with activity and this indicates that Gemin5 as well as the SMN complex may play role in the maturation of telomerase at the latest stage. In-vivo, up-regulation of Gemin5 will increase the telomerase activity. On the other hand, the knockdown of Gemin5 in cell will reduce the activity of telomerase and also cause the shift of localization of the SMN complex away from hTR. In summary, we have identified and characterized the functional role of Gemin5 in the SMN complex. Moreover, our novel finding in telomerase will open up a new direction for people to study the SMN complex as well as SMA.

469210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
469210.value: SMN is the pathogenic protein of SMA and it plays a significant role in RNA biogenesis such as snRNP assembly. Here, we showed that Gemin5 which is the RNA binding protein in the SMN complex recognizes the telomerase RNA, hTR and further showed that it involves in telomerase biogenesis. For further development of this project, it would be interested to know if there is any link between telomerase and the pathogenicity of SMA because it would open up a new direction to the therapeutic approach.

469210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
469210.value: SMN is the pathogenic protein of SMA and it plays a significant role in RNA biogenesis such as snRNP assembly. Understanding of the functional roles and the mechanistic details of the SMN complex in cell will provide us further information of the pathogenesis of the SMA and may help us to develop therapeutic treatment to the SMA patients. In this project, we found that Gemin5 which is the RNA recognition components of the SMN complex modulates the snRNP assembly by interacting with the Sm proteins in an orderly manner. The results provide further understanding of the mechanism of the SMN complex in handling the RNA and passing to the Sm protein to form the final products. Moreover, we also identified telomerase RNA is the novel binding partner of Gemin5 and it will influence the maturation of telomerase. Since telomerase involves in several important pathways such as genomic stability and aging, the possible linkage between the pathogenesis of SMA may provide further understanding of the SMA disease.

469310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
469310.value: Mast cells are key multifunctional effector cells of the immune system which release and synthesize myriads of chemical mediators, cytokines and angiogenic factors. Osteopontin is an extracellular matrix-associated glycoprotein originally described in bone metabolism which is now also recognised to be an important regulator of various immune responses. Both mast cells and osteopontin have separately been implicated in the mediation of acute and chronic inflammatory reactions that are associated with allergy, innate immune host defence responses, angiogenesis, wound healing and metastasis. However, until recently the effects of osteopontin on mast cell functions have not been investigated. It was demonstrated in mice that osteopontin induced chemotactic migration of mast cells and enhanced IgE mediated degranulation of mast cells through binding to the cell surface receptors CD44 and the v integrin. Furthermore, osteopontin was shown to regulate the magnitude of an IgE-mediated passive cutaneous anaphylaxis reaction through modulation of skin mast cell degranulation. Thus osteopontin is capable of modulating the functions of mast cells which contribute to antimicrobial, inflammatory and angiogenic responses. The discovery is inspiring but required further confirmation. Furthermore, mouse mast cells are known to be different from human mast cells in many aspects. It is hence the aim of the present project to provide an extensive investigation into the regulation of human mast cells by osteopontin. By employing primary human mast cells cultured from progenitors isolated from human buffy coat preparations, the current study will investigate how osteopontin modulates the functions of human mast cells especially when they are activated through different mechanisms that represent innate immune responses (toll like receptor activators) and adaptive immune response (cross-linking of IgE receptors). We will also evaluate if osteopontin can regulate the migration of human mast cells. Since both the level of osteopontin and the number of mast cells are increased in chronic inflammatory conditions, we will investigate the effects of osteopontin on the expression of vascular endothelial growth factors (the most potent inducers of new blood vessels formation) and matrix metalloproteinase 9 (an important factor for matrix degradation) in human mast cells as these factors are important for tissue remodelling and tumorigenesis. This study will be the first to provide clinically relevant and useful information for the better understanding of the role of osteopontin-mast cell interactions in human inflammation. Consequently, the results will facilitate the better design of therapeutic agents for controlling inflammation-associated pathological conditions. 肥大細胞是一種多功能細胞，活化後能夠分泌多種化學介質，細胞因子和血管生成因子，是機體免疫網絡中一種關鍵的效應細胞。骨橋蛋白屬於細胞外基質糖蛋白。骨橋蛋白最初被發現與骨代謝相關。近來研究提示，骨橋蛋白在介導機體多種免疫反應中亦具有重要的調節作用。多個研究分別指出，肥大細胞和骨橋蛋白均能夠參與急性和慢性炎症反應，包括過敏反應、固有免疫反應、血管生成、創傷修復和介導腫瘤轉移。然而，目前關於骨橋蛋白對肥大細胞功能影響的研究卻甚少報導。動物體外實驗發現，骨橋蛋白能夠誘導老鼠肥大細胞趨化性遷移，並通過結合細胞表面CD44受體和v 整合素，增強IgE介導的肥大細胞脫顆粒。另有研究指出，骨橋蛋白通過調節皮膚肥大細胞脫顆粒來調控IgE介導的被動皮膚過敏反應。由此推測，骨橋蛋白能夠通過調節肥大細胞功能進而影響肥大細胞介導的抗菌，抗炎及血管形成。這些關於骨橋蛋白能夠影響肥大細胞功能的初步發現振奮人心，但是需要更深入徹底的研究進一步證實。目前的研究多停留在老鼠肥大細胞上，而老鼠肥大細胞在許多方面與人類肥大細胞的表現存在差異。因此，我們希望以人類肥大細胞為實驗對象，全面而深入地研究骨橋蛋白對人類肥大細胞功能的調控作用。我們已成功在人血中分離並培養出人類原代肥大細胞，並將應用原代培養的人類肥大細胞探索骨橋蛋白如何調節肥大細胞的功能，特別是在不同調控機制參與下，如模擬固有免疫反應（Toll樣受體激動劑的應用）和獲得性免疫反應（IgE受體交聯）啟動下，骨橋蛋白對肥大細胞免疫功能的調控。同時，我們也將觀察骨橋蛋白能否調控肥大細胞的遷移。在慢性炎症條件下，機體內骨橋蛋白水準上升，肥大細胞數量亦增加。我們將探討骨橋蛋白對人類肥大細胞中血管內皮生長因子（新生血管形成的最有力的誘導劑）和 基質金屬蛋白酶9（基質降解的重要因素）表達的影響，因為這兩種因子對組織重構和腫瘤發生均有重要作用。該項研究將首次解答在人類炎症中，骨橋蛋白與肥大細胞的相互作用，為臨床提供有用的信息。因此，本研究將有助於設計針對骨橋蛋白及其相關作用機制的靶向治療方法，用於控制炎症相關疾病。

469310.label: Realisation of objectives
469310.value: Objective 1 This objective has been completed. Mature human cultured mast cells (HCMC) of 12 weeks old in general were found not to demonstrate significant chemotaxis towards osteopontin (OPN) or chemotactic agents such as CCL11 or CXCL12. For immature HCMC that were 6 weeks old, OPN did not induced significant chemotaxis but was able to significantly reduce the chemotaxis induced by CCL11 and CXCL12. Objective 2 This objective has been completed. PGN induced the synthesis of IL-5, IL-8 and TNF-alpha but not degranulation. In general, both soluble and matrix fixed form of OPN failed to demonstrate significant modulation of the PGN induced synthesis of cytokines. Objective 3 This objective has been completed according to the protocols proposed. Initial investigations were delayed by the lack of observable effects with recombinant OPN and this problem was eventually overcome by studying the actions of a range of human OPN preparations. Human OPN isolated from human milk was identified to be most potent and was employed thorough this study instead of the originally proposed recombinant OPN. Furthermore, matrix fixed OPN (mOPN) is more potent that soluble OPN (sOPN). In general OPN enhanced the adhesion of HCMC to extracellular matrix but demonstrated inhibitory action on the IgE receptor mediated synthesis of cytokines in HCMC and had no effect on the degranulation process. Objective 4 The expression of MMP9 and VEGF were investigated with both ELISA and PCR assays as proposed. Both sOPN and mOPN failed to demonstrate any modulatory action to the basal and increased expression of these two cytokines following activation of HCMC with anti-IgE or PGN. Objective 5 This objective has been completed according to the protocols described in the proposal. The cryptic SVVYGLR region was found not to be essential for the observed inhibitory actions of OPN. The employment of immunocytochemistry and neutralizing antibodies revealed that the interaction between HCMC and OPN is mediated through the alphaVbeta3 integrin in HCMC and the arginine-glycine-aspartate (RGD) domain of OPN. Cell signaling molecules of the MAPK and NFB pathways were differentially regulated by mOPN as revealed in immunoblotting studies described in the proposal.

469310.label: Major findings and research outcome
469310.value: This is the first study investigating the effects of osteopontin on human mast cells. The overall inhibitory action on HCMC contradicts with enhancing actions of OPN on murine mast cells and thus further highlights the significance of mast cell heterogeneity among different species such that results from animal studies cannot be directly translated into human equivalence. The lack of activities of recombinant OPN in comparison to OPN isolated from human milk suggested that post-translational modification of nascent OPN is important for the physiological functioning of the peptide. OPN can function as a cytokine in the soluble form or an adhesion molecule when fixed to extracellular matrix. The current study revealed that soluble OPN (sOPN) could only inhibit the release of anti-IgE induced histamine release and only in the presence of manganese which supposed to activate integrins in mast cells. In contrast, significant modulation of HCMC activation was observed with OPN in the adhesion molecule configuration and thus subsequent studies were focused on matrix fixed OPN (mOPN). HCMC adhered to mOPN in a dose dependent manner (0.1-10 ug/ml) and the adhesion was increased following both adaptive and innate activation induced by anti-IgE and PGN respectively. Although mOPN could not suppress anti-IgE induced release of histamine, PGD2 and cys-LTs, it could significantly reduce the synthesis of IL-5, IL-8 and TNF. Further studies with quantitative PCR confirmed the reduction of IL-8 and TNF expression and revealed an increase in the expression of IL-10 while the expressions of Th1/Th/2 cytokines selected (IFN, IL-4, IL-12) were not significantly altered. In contrast, mOPN did not demonstrate significant modulation of cytokine release induced by PGN, suggesting that mOPN differentially regulated the signaling mechanisms involved in anti-IgE and PGN induced mast cell activation. The expression of the angiogenic factors MMP-9 and VEGF were also investigated but both sOPN and mOPN did not demonstrate significant regulation of these factors and thus our hypothesis of OPN might actively promote vascular neogenesis through mast cells was not supported. We further demonstrated that integrin alphaVbeta3 to the receptor for mOPN by a combination of immunocytochemistry and functional studies with antibodies against an array of integrin. Furthermore, the RGD (Arg-Gly-Asp) domain instead of the cryptic SVVYGLR region in OPN was demonstrated to be the integrin interacting sequence. Apart from p38 which activation by anti-IgE was enhanced by mOPN, the anti-IgE induced activation of ERK1/2, JNK and NFkB was suppressed by OPN.

469310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
469310.value: The interaction between osteopontin (OPN) and mast cells in human has been confirmed by our current study. In inflamed tissues, the increased level of OPN will prevent the migration of tissue mast cells from the inflamed site through increased adhesion of activated mast cells to extracellular matrix and suppression of chemotaxis of immature mast cells. In contrast to the original study reporting an activation enhancing action of OPN on murine mast cells, our study observed that OPN suppressed cytokine release from IgE receptor mediated human mast cells. However, cytokine release induced by bacterial peptidoglycan was not affected and thus suggesting that OPN selectively suppressed allergy related inflammation. Since only matrix fixed OPN (mOPN) demonstrated human mast cell modulating activities, it would be interesting to investigate into the differences between the molecular structural conformations of the soluble and matrix fixed form of OPN for better understanding of the structural requirement for the anti-inflammatory actions of OPN. Furthermore, since mOPN produced its effect through interacting with integrin alphaVbeta3, it will also be interesting to investigate the effects of other activators of alphaVbeta3 on human mast cells with the aim of developing new anti-inflammatory agents through regulating integrin functions in inflammatory cells.

469310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
469310.value: Mast cells are key multifunctional effector cells of the immune system which release and synthesize myriads of chemical mediators, cytokines and angiogenic factors. Osteopontin is an extracellular matrix-associated glycoprotein which is an important regulator of various immune responses. In the current study, osteopontin was demonstrated to facilitate the adhesion of activated human mast cells but prevented their movement and thus localized these cells at the site of inflammation. At the same time the capability of human mast cells to synthesis immune modulating proteins following activation by allergic mechanisms was suppressed by osteopontin. However, the activation of human mast cells by bacterial molecules was not affected by OPN. These results thus suggested that OPN suppressed inflammatory reactions associated with allergy. Further studies into the molecular structure of osteopontin and its human cell modulating mechanisms will facilitate the development of a new class of anti-allergic drugs related to osteopontin.

469610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
469610.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia in the elderly. Aggregation of amyloid-β peptide (Aβ), derived from the proteolytic cleavage of amyloid precursor protein (APP), is believed to be central to the pathogenesis of the disease. Additionally, APP intracellular domain (AICD) is also a cleavage product of APP which has been implicated in gene transcription including several AD linked genes. However, the precise mechanisms involved in the regulation of APP processing remain unclear. Accumulating evidence reveals that AICD interacting proteins (AIPs) can influence APP processing as well as APP signaling. There is also evidence to suggest that AIPs work cooperatively and competitively, which may be essential to maintain the normal functions and processing of APP. Hence, the identification of the full complement of AIPs is an important step for improving our understanding of APP processing and signaling. From a therapeutic perspective, targeting AIPs or AIP-APP interactions could lead to the development of effective strategies to combat AD. To this end, we have attempted to identify novel AIPs. We have recently identified engulfment adaptor protein (GULP) as a novel AIP. The primary objective of the proposed study is to investigate the role of the APP-GULP interaction in relation to APP processing and signaling. Preliminary study from our laboratory suggests that GULP can influence APP processing. The proposed study will shed valuable light on the regulatory mechanism(s) of APP processing and signaling, and may provide essential information for the development of more effective therapeutic strategies for AD. 阿爾茨海默氏症是最常見的引發老年痴呆的病因。而由澱粉樣前體蛋白(amyloid precursor protein，APP)切割而產生的β澱粉樣蛋白(β-amyloid, Aβ)在病人腦部的聚積是誘發阿爾茨海默氏症的最重要因素。此外，APP的切割也會產生一胞內片段(APP intracellular domain, AICD),資料顯示AICD會影響某些阿爾茨海默氏症致病基因的基因轉錄。然而，具體調控APP被切割的機制至今仍不為人們所知。但是有越來越多的證據顯示，與 AICD相互作用的蛋白(AICD interacting protein, AIP)會影響APP的切割以及信號的轉導。也有證據表明，這些AIP之間有協同或者競爭的相互關係，而且這些作用對於維持APP正常的水平和功能都是致關重要的。因此，鑑定出全部的AIP無疑會增進我們對於APP切割以及其信號轉導的理解。並且從疾病治療的角度而言，針對於AIP或者AIP-APP相互作用方面，也完全有可能發展出能有效治療阿爾茨海默氏症的新療法。鑑於此，我們研究小組嘗試去尋找新的AIP。而最近我們發現了吞噬接頭蛋白(engulfment adaptor protein, GULP)是一個新的AIP。這個項目的主要目標是研究APP和GULP的相互作用對於APP切割以及信號轉導的影響。而初步研究表明，GULP的確會影響到APP的切割。我們預測，這項研究將會深化人們對於APP胞內切割及信號轉導調控機制的理解，進而為研發更有效治療阿爾茨海默氏症的療法提供重要的資料。

469610.label: Realisation of objectives
469610.value: Objective 1: GULP, also known as GULP1, is a novel APP/APPc interacting protein (AIP) that is found in our laboratory from a yeast two-hybrid screen by using APPc as “bait”. In this project, their interaction was confirmed by various biochemical assays including GST-fusion protein pull-down and co-immunoprecipitation assays. Moreover, their interaction was found to be mediated by GULP PTB domain and APP NPTY motif. Furthermore, in vitro protein binding assay showed that GULP and APP interact directly. These results indicate that APP and GULP interact directly and the interaction is mediated by the NPTY motif of APP and the GULP PTB domain. Objective 2: By using recombinant GULP, we generated a rat anti-GULP antibody. Our characterization work showed that the antibody can detect both transfected and endogenous GULP. Immunofluoresce studies using the GULP antibody revealed that a proportion of both endogenous APP and GULP colocalized in perinuclear regions in embryonic rat cortical neurons. In conjunction with subcellular compartment marker antibodies, we found that GULP and APP were colocalized in ER, Golgi and endosome in neurons. Therefore our findings suggest that a proportion of APP colocalizes with GULP in a variety of subcellular compartments. Objective 3: Since mounting evidence suggests that AIP can alter APP metabolism, we tested if GULP affects APP processing by three different system including APP-Gal4 reporter assay, APP carboxyl terminal fragment analysis and Aβ ELISA. The results of the assays indicated that GULP could enhance both β- and γ-secretase cleavage of APP in different cell types. Moreover, we found that GULP stimulated the secretion of Aβ from CHO stably transfected with APP. In conclusion, GULP is a novel AIP that enhances APP processing. Objective 4: Several AIPs have been shown to participate in APP-mediated gene transcription. Several APP-regulated genes are closely associated with AD. Therefore, we investigated whether GULP is involved in APP-mediated gene transcription by monitoring the transcriptional activity of APP-Gal4 DNA binding domain (APP-Gal4DB) fusion genes using a Gal4-UAS-luciferase reporter. We found that GULP could not stimulate the transcriptional activity of APP-Gal4DB in different cell lines such as CHO, HEK293 and SHSY5Y neuroblastoma. Similarly, RT-PCR analysis showed that GULP did not affect the expressions of mRNA of several APP-regulated genes including GSK-3β and BACE1. Our result is in line with the observation by Wahler et al. (Biochem J. 2013 450(2):333-43) that GULP only mediates LRP1 transactivation but not APP transactivation.

469610.label: Major findings and research outcome
469610.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common fatal neurodegenerative disorder. Accumulating evidence indicates that altered production of amyloid-β peptide (Aβ), derived from the proteolytic cleavage of the amyloid precursor protein (APP), is crucial to AD pathogenesis. It has been shown that APP carboxyl-terminal domain (APPc) interacting proteins can influence APP processing. There is also evidence to suggest that APPc interacting proteins work cooperatively and competitively to maintain normal APP functions and processing. Hence, identification of the full complement of APPc interacting proteins is an important step for improving our understanding of APP processing. In this project, we identified GULP as a novel APPc interacting protein. We found that the GULP-APP interaction is mediated by the NPTY motif of APP and the GULP PTB domain. Confocal microscopy revealed that a proportion of APP and GULP colocalized in neurons. In an APP-Gal4 reporter assay, we demonstrated that GULP altered the processing of APP. Moreover, overexpression of GULP enhanced the generation of APP carboxyl-terminal fragments (CTFs) and Aβ while knockdown of GULP suppressed APP CTFs and Aβ production. Our findings reveal that GULP is a novel APP/APPc interacting protein that influences APP processing and Aβ production. This work has been accepted for publication in Biochemical Journal (publication 1 in part C). In addition to APP, GULP has been reported to interact with a small GTPase named ARF6 which functions as a molecular switch to regulate many intracellular processes including endocytic trafficking and neurite development. Interestingly, we found that ARF6 also interacts with another APP interacting adaptor FE65 from a yeast two-hybrid screen. Therefore, there may have some functional/physical associations between GULP1, APP, FE65 and ARF6. To facilitate our future investigation, we characterized the interaction between FE65 and ARF6. Moreover, FE65-ARF6 interaction was found to regulate neurite outgrowth. This work has been published in FASEB Journal (publication 2 in part C). Since neurite degeneration is another hallmark of AD, this work has laid the foundation for our future investigation to dissect the relationship between GULP1, APP, FE65 and ARF6 in AD.

469610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
469610.value: Since GULP influences APP processing in cultured cells, it is important to confirm the effect in other systems. Creating a transgenic mouse model for GULP will allow the investigation of its effect on APP processing under physiological condition. In our study, GULP-APP interaction is fully characterized. However, the mechanism that regulates the interaction is unknown. As GULP-APP interaction enhances Aβ generation, in depth understanding of the interaction will provide essential insights into how to modulate GULP-APP interaction to lower Aβ production. Both GULP and APP are phosphoproteins with several phosphorylation sites within their interacting regions. As phosphorylation is a common mechanism in regulating protein-protein interaction, it is possible that GULP-APP interaction is regulated by phosphorylation. Investigation of the role of GULP and APP phosphorylation may reveal the mechanism(s) that regulates GULP-APP interaction. Although our study has revealed that GULP-APP interaction is mediated by GULP PTB and APP NPXY motif, the exact interaction interface is still unknown. Therefore, determination of the complex structure of GULP PTB and APP is an important step in revealing how they interact. This is crucial for the development of strategies to block GULP-APP interaction to reduce Aβ generation. Please also see section 6.1 second paragraph

469610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
469610.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common fatal neurodegenerative disorder. Accumulating evidence indicates that over-production of toxic amyloid-β peptide (Aβ), derived from the proteolytic cleavage of the amyloid precursor protein (APP), is an important process for the disease. Recent studies have shown that proteins that bind to APP can affect the production of Aβ. Therefore, it is important to find these APP binding proteins and to evaluate their roles in Aβ generation. In our study, we found that a small protein called engulfment adaptor PTB domain containing 1 (GULP) that binds to APP. Importantly, we demonstrated that GULP can enhance APP cleavage and Aβ production by different assay systems. Therefore, we have identified a new APP interacting protein that modulates Aβ generation. Our findings lay a foundation for exploring the potential of blocking the interaction between GULP and APP as a therapeutic approach for AD.

470110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
470110.value: The rising number of men having sex with men (MSM) reported with HIV infection in Asia and the Pacific is a cause for concern. It is hypothesized that the phenomenon might have arisen from changes in network configuration instead of individual behaviours. The study is founded on the 2-mode principle of the duality of place and people, with MSMs seeking sex partners at specific venues being considered to be closer to one another. The objectives of the study are, using a 2-mode approach, to describe the network configuration of MSM, track changes longitudinally, and differentiate the risk between different venues of sex partnership. The study is planned to be rolled out in 4 phases. Phase I involves MSM sampling and the establishment of a relational database on sex networking. Through a field survey administered through gay saunas and the internet, the sex-partnership pattern of 200 Chinese MSM in Hong Kong would be assessed. An affiliation matrix is constructed to record the frequency of sex partnership in different venues, alongside behavioural and demographic data. Phase II centres on the mapping of MSM networks, their visualization, and the calculation of network measures in terms of density and centrality. Longitudinal data would be collected over a one year period to model the changes of configuration. The influences of regular partnership, alongside the partner-seeking practice at different venues, will be assessed. At Phase III simulation modeling would be conducted to explore differences in infection risk between MSM using different sex partnership venues. Simulation would be pursued on the foundation of the co-evolution model. Results collected from the three phases would then be integrated for the development of analysis, on the advice of people in the community and venue operators, during the final Phase IV. Feedback from MSM and public health authorities would be collected for improving the output generation process. The analysis so obtained would be useful for assessing the HIV risk of MSM in the coming years, and would provide the rationale for appropriate intervention to be designed for preventing HIV transmission in a Chinese community. 在亞太地區，男同性社群當中的愛滋病病毒散播快速增長，情況令人憂慮。這個現象並不一定是個人行為所致，有可能反映了社群網路結構的改變。本研究建基於雙維網絡原則，假設經常到同一地方訪尋性伴的男同性戀者關係比其他人密切。研究目的是以雙維網路方式了解男同性社群的網絡結構、追蹤當中的演變、再分析不同地方的病毒傳播危機。研究工作分四個階段進行：第一階段透過抽樣，招募男同性戀者參與研究，建立關聯資料庫。通過在香港各桑拿及互聯網等調查平台，評估大約200名男同性戀者的訪尋性伴方式，再以關係矩陣紀錄行為、地點和人口統計數據。第二階段的重點是繪制網絡地圖，計算網絡密度和成員的向心性，再通過重複調查了解網絡變化，分析地方和不同伴侶之間的相互影響。第三階級以共同演化為基礎，設立模擬模型，探討訪尋性伴地方和感染危機的關係。第四階段包含綜合分析，並透過吸取社群意見，優化研究的產出。研究結果可望提供理據，設計預防愛滋病病毒在華人男同性社群擴散的有效干預方案。

470110.label: Realisation of objectives
470110.value: OBJECTIVE ONE: To describe the configuration of MSM communities, a 2-mode network was constructed using data derived from survey on 205 sauna-recruited MSM. Three 2-mode centrality measures (degree, closeness, betweenness) were calculated for saunas and MSM respectively. Two saunas and 5 MSM had exceptionally high centrality. The distribution of 2-mode closeness centrality indicates that MSM were closely connected with each other. Geographically, core saunas were identified in urban Kowloon. Multiple regression quadratic assignment procedure was performed to determine the association between individual characteristics and sauna network. In the analyses, MSM similar in age and appearance were more likely to attend the same saunas. Sexual behaviours of MSM were however diverse in terms of the number of non-regular partners and the practice of unprotected anal intercourse (UAI) with these partners. OBJECTIVE TWO: Temporal data were collected through regular internet surveys over a one-year period for respondents recruited at saunas. Separately, 106 respondents were recruited on the Internet for the same surveys. Monthly data from 19 MSM recruited at saunas and 46 internet-recruited MSM were used for assessing temporal changes in network configuration. Assessment has focussed on the pattern of partner-sourcing, derived from the differential use of 9 channels – 5 types of physical venues and 4 major means on internet. For both sauna-recruited and internet-recruited MSM, the 2-mode degree centrality for Smartphone Apps was around 0.15 consistently over the study period. Throughout the survey , higher 2-mode degree centrality was consistently observed in sex-networking venues, where MSM were initially recruited. OBJECTIVE THREE: The baseline sexual behaviour profiles of MSM recruited at venues were compared to those on internet. Some 59.0% of sauna-recruited MSM had non-regular sex partners in the preceding month while only 18.0% of internet-recruited MSM reported having this type of partners. However, the proportion of sauna-recruited MSM using a condom consistently while having anal sex with non-regular partners was similar to that of internet-recruited MSM. A deterministic compartment model was constructed to visualize the HIV transmission pattern in different MSM communities over a one-year period. Three distinctive sex-networking means were identified by 2-mode network configuration and used as the basis for compartments in the model. Sexual behavioural data were obtained from our questionnaire survey to support model development. The model was able to give a comparable number of new HIV cases and suggested a minor role of casual sex partners, as compared to regular partners.

470110.label: Major findings and research outcome
470110.value: Eight core saunas were differentiated from a highly connected sauna network. MSM visiting core saunas were more likely to be younger and users of the Internet for sex networking. They visited 1.7 saunas and had 2.6 sauna partners over 1-month period, which were both significantly higher than those for MSM in peripheral saunas. By conducting multiple regression quadratic assignment procedure, MSM similar in age and appearance were more likely to attend the same saunas. In the sauna, sexual behavior of MSM could be diverse in terms of the number of casual partners and the practice of unprotected anal sex with casual partners. The assessment of temporal changes in network configuration was also made, by using data collected through regular Internet surveys over a 1-year period for respondents recruited at saunas or over a 6-month period for respondents recruited on the Internet. For both sauna-recruited and Internet-recruited MSM, the 2-mode degree centrality for Smartphone Apps was consistently around 0.15 over the study period. As regards other channels for partner-sourcing, higher 2-mode degree centrality was observed in saunas among sauna-recruited MSM whereas 2-mode degree centrality was higher in other virtual venue among Internet-recruited MSM. Methodologically, Internet sampling was efficient in identifying other sex networking venues while Internet recruits gave a high retention rate for updating profiles. Based on the 2-mode network configuration, three distinctive sex-networking means were identified, including network of core saunas, network of peripheral saunas and the Internet, and used as the basis for categorizing MSM communities. A deterministic compartment model suggested that 232 new infections would be observed over a year period (in 2011/2012), which was comparable to the annual number of newly reported HIV cases. Infection rate of MSM using the Internet for sex-networking was substantially higher than those using saunas only. New cases were more likely to be observed among MSM who had regular sex partners and practised receptive anal sex. However, increasing use of the Internet for sex-networking has little impact on raising the number of new HIV cases. For research outcomes, presentations were made at the 8th UK Social Network Conference in Bristol and the 7th IAS Conference on HIV Pathogenesis, Treatment and Prevention in Kuala Lumpur, respectively. An article was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2013, while another article has been accepted for publication in Archives of Sexual Behavior in 2014.

470110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
470110.value: Heterogeneity of the sexual affiliation network of MSM in Hong Kong was observed. Our experiences suggested that sampling strategy of MSM survey must be objective-driven, which may differ for health message dissemination and social marketing, versus HIV surveillance or risk assessment. Prioritization may also be considered so that public health interventions can be targeted at sex-networking venues in denser networks. Due to advancement of technology and changes of preference to some sex-networking venues, network configuration among MSM is ever changing. Surveys at a regular basis, say every 2-3 years, may be useful for evaluating future risk of HIV transmission. Use of condom while having sex with regular partners is particularly important for containing HIV epidemic among MSM in Hong Kong. For effective spread of health messages or behavioral surveillance, the Internet may be an appropriate starting channel. From our analyses, the Internet is shown to be favored by young MSM, who are more likely to have risky sexual behavior and higher connectivity than other sex-networking venues. Given the network configurations revealed from this study, evaluating the effectiveness of social marketing through various sex-networking venues would be important to support the development of health promotion strategies.

470110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
470110.value: Men who have sex with men (MSM) were highly connected through saunas, the Internet and other sex-networking venues. MSM similar in age and appearance were more likely to attend the same saunas. The proportion of MSM using Smartphone Apps for sex-networking was quite consistent over the study period. Through network analyses, clusters of MSM could be identified to assess their different risks of HIV transmission. While MSM attending the same sauna could be diverse in terms of their sexual behaviors, such as practice of unprotected anal sex and number of casual sex partners, the condom usage rate while having sex with casual partners among sauna-linked MSM is generally higher than those of Internet-linked MSM. By categorizing MSM into three bases of network (core saunas, peripheral saunas and the Internet), an epidemic model estimated that 232 new infections would be observed over a year. Rising usage of the Internet for sex-networking has little impact on the increasing number of HIV cases. The model results suggest that HIV transmission has occured mainly between regular partners, whose condom usage was much lower than those with casual partners. Likewise, the frequency of sexual contacts was also higher between regular than casual partners.

470410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
470410.value: Diaphyseal long bone fracture is a common injury in high-energy trauma among young people, where femoral shaft fracture is the one commonly encountered by surgeons. Due to the comminution, displacements and associated severe soft tissue trauma, the nonunion rate is around 2-8% with intramedullary nail fixation. Diaphyseal long bone fractures usually take at least 4-6 months to heal and the functional recovery takes even longer time. Measures to accelerate diaphyseal long bone fracture healing and rehabilitation are main research goals and they will give a high medico-economic impact. Mechanical stimulation plays a critical role in fracture healing. Low-magnitude high-frequency vibration (LMHFV) is a systemic biophysical stimulation that is recently reported to enhance bone mineral density (BMD), circulation and muscular functions, as proven in animal studies and clinical trials on normal postmenopausal subjects. Justified with these characteristic effects on musculoskeletal system, we were the first group to investigate the effect of LMHFV on fracture healing in a rat model. Results showed that LMHFV can accelerate femoral shaft fracture healing by 30%, as confirmed radiologically, densitometrically and with mechanical tests. Callus formation and maturation were enhanced with increased chondrogenesis. Endochondral ossification-related genes (collagen I, II, VEGF and BMP-2) were upregulated at different phases of fracture healing. Application of LMHFV on osteoporotic fracture healing also indicated similar results that prove its high efficacy in fracture repair. Further justified with our clinical applications of LMHFV (35Hz, 0.3g) on normal postmenopausal women which demonstrated an improvement of muscle functions and balancing ability, we therefore hypothesize that LMHFV can enhance femoral shaft fracture healing in humans by enhancing callus formation and maturation, improving micro-circulation, BMD and muscle functions at fracture site. In the present study, we propose to study the efficacy of LMHFV on human femoral shaft fracture healing by conducting a randomized controlled clinical trial and to document the related safety issues on post-operative patients. The patients aged 20-40 of either gender, after surgical fixation of the fractures, will be treated with LMHFV at 35Hz, 0.3g for 20min/day, 5days/week for 6 months. The results will be evaluated by clinical assessments, radiography, densitometry, dynamic MR and functional outcomes at intervals until 12 months postoperatively. Their biochemical bone forming markers will also be assessed. The findings will provide scientific evidences to support the clinical application of LMHFV for long bone fracture patients and promote this biophysical intervention as a routine adjunctive fracture management. 高能量創傷所致長骨幹骨折易發于年輕人，其中臨床常見創傷為股骨幹骨折。由於該類型骨折通常是粉碎性骨折，斷端常見移位且合併有嚴重的軟組織損傷，經髓內釘固定後骨折不癒合率仍高達2-8%。 長骨幹骨折的癒合時間通常至少需要4至6個月，功能恢復則需要更長的時間。如何促進長骨幹骨折癒合及功能康復是當前研究的主要目標，相關措施的實施將帶來良好的醫療經濟學效應。 機械刺激在促進骨折癒合中扮演重要角色。高頻低振幅振動（LMHFV）是一種系統的生物物理學干預方式。近來的動物試驗研究及針對正常絕經後婦女的臨床試驗研究報導都證實LMHFV能提高骨密度（BMD），促進血液迴圈，並改善肌肉功能。根據LMHFV對骨骼肌肉系統的這些作用特性，我們率先通過大鼠模型研究了LMHFV對於骨折癒合的影響。影像學檢查，密度顯像及生物力學測試的研究結果證實，LMHFV能加速股骨幹骨折癒合約30%。LMHFV促進了軟骨發生，加速了骨痂形成及骨痂成熟，增強了軟骨內骨化的相關基因（collagen I, II, VEGF及BMP-2）在骨折癒合不同階段的表達。將LMHFV施加於骨質疏鬆性骨折，得到了類似的結果，顯示了其對骨折修復具有較好效果。進一步研究發現，LMHFV（35Hz, 峰振幅0.3g）能改善正常絕經後婦女的肌肉功能及平衡能力。由此，我們提出假設：LMHFV能通過加速骨痂形成及成熟，改善骨折部位微循環，提高骨密度及增強肌肉功能，促進人股骨幹骨折癒合。 本研究中，我們將應用隨機對照臨床試驗方法，探討LMHFV在人股骨幹骨折癒合中的作用，並為其對術後患者的安全相關問題提供佐證資料。年齡介於20至40歲的股骨幹骨折患者，在骨折固定術後，將接受每天20分鐘，每週5天，共持續6月的LMHFV治療（35Hz, 峰振幅0.3g）。我們將採用臨床評價，影像學檢查，密度顯像，及功能恢復指標等手段，對試驗結果進行連續評估直至術後12月。在整個過程中，同時將檢測成骨的生化標記物。最終的研究結果將為LMHFV在長骨幹骨折患者中的臨床應用提供科學依據，並將推動生物干預手段作為骨折輔助治療方法應用於臨床常規。

470410.label: Realisation of objectives
470410.value: Objective 1: To investigate the efficacy of LMHFV treatment in lower limb long bone diaphyseal fracture healing on the time to radiographic healing by conducting a randomized controlled clinical trial. From 2010 to 2014, a total of 49 patients were recruited to this study from the Prince of Wales Hospital, North District Hospital and Queen Elizabeth Hospital, including 27 patients in the vibration group and 22 patients as the control. Outcome assessments of both groups were performed at the baseline (Week 0), week 2, week 4, week 8, week 12, week 16, week 20, week 26 and week 52 (1 year) post-operation for all subjects. The mean age of subjects was 40±14 years. In the investigation of radiography, the first appearance of bridging callus was week 7.4±5.7 in the vibration group, compared to week 8.3±2.6 in the control (p=0.716). The fracture healing time was not significantly shorter in the vibration group. Objective 2: To assess the multi-factorial effects of LMHFV treatment versus no-treatment control on bone mineral density, blood circulation, functional outcomes including muscle strength, balancing ability, jumping performance and bone-forming biochemical markers. The balancing ability was significantly better in the vibration group, with 20.4% shorter reaction time compared with control group (p=0.026). In 1-year after fracture, vibration group had significantly higher quality of life in terms of physical health (p<0.001), mental health (p=0.017) and total SF-36 score (p=0.008). For the functional recovery, significantly higher Lower Extremity Functional Scale was recorded in vibration group 1-year post-fracture when compared with the control (71.3±8.7 vs 55.4±14.9, p=0.013). Also, the Harris Hip Score of the vibration group was significantly higher than the control in 1-year after fracture (97.3±2.8 vs 88.6±7.2, p=0.006). LMHFV was well accepted by patients with no adverse effects, which is suitable to be introduced to long bone diaphyseal fracture patients.

470410.label: Major findings and research outcome
470410.value: 1. Improvement of balancing ability was found in patients with LMHFV treatment. The vibration group had shown significantly shorter reaction time of 20% in 1 year post-operation with mean between-group difference of -0.38 seconds(p<0.001). Significant enhancement was noted in movement velocity and maximum point excursion, with mean between-group difference of 0.94degree/sec(p<0.001) and 10.72 percentage points(p<0.001) respectively. (Supported by 9.3) 2. Significantly higher Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS) was recorded in the vibration group patients in 1-year post-fracture when compared with the control (71.3±8.7 vs 55.4±14.9, p=0.013). From literature, the minimum clinically important difference (MCID) for the LEFS is 9 points which represents a detectable and clinically meaningful functional change in patients’ condition. Difference of 15.9 points between two groups indicated a significantly better functional recovery of patients with vibration treatment. (Supported by 9.1, 9.2, 9.3) 3. Harris Hip Score of the vibration group was significantly higher than the control in 1-year after fracture (97.3±2.8 vs 88.6±7.2, p=0.006). According to Harris Hip Score, higher score represents better post-surgery recovery in terms of absence of deformity, range of motion, as well as pain, walking distance, limp, support, sit and stand. The above functions are critical to patients’ daily activities and long-term mobility. (Supported by 9.1, 9.2, 9.3) 4. In 1-year after fracture, vibration group patients had significantly higher quality of life. Assessed by SF-36, the physical health of vibration group was 84.7±7.6 out of 100, compared with 67.6±14.8 in the control (p<0.001). The SF-36 mental health component of vibration group patients was also higher than the control group (75.5±7.6 vs 60.5±15, p=0.017). The total SF-36 score of vibration group patients was 81±7.1, which was higher than that of the control group (64.8±13.8, p=0.008). The difference of quality of life may be due to the better functional recovery as stated in 6.1-3 above.(Supported by 9.3)

470410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
470410.value: In this study, the beneficial effects of LMHFV on balancing ability, lower extremity functional score, Harris Hip Score and quality of life among long bone fracture patients were proven. The LMHFV is well accepted by patients from early post-operation phase to rehabilitation phase with negligible adverse effects, which is suitable to be implemented in the long term rehabilitation program for long bone fracture patients. The vibration group patients had shown better functional recovery and quality of life in 1-year post fracture. It would be interesting to see whether the introduction of LMHFV during rehabilitation will benefit patients’ long term functions (2-year post fracture), so assessing the cohorts again 1 year after this study may provide the solid data on this.

470410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
470410.value: Long bone fracture is a common injury caused by high-energy trauma among young people, which usually takes 3-6 months to heal and even years for functional recovery. The non-union rate of long bone fracture is around 2-8% after surgery, and this is a serious complication with fracture failed to heal. Poor recovery of long bone fractures not only brings pain, but also causes loss of mobility and working ability, affecting patients’ quality of life. Therefore it would be useful to explore an intervention that can accelerate the fracture healing and improve the functional recovery of patients. This study is the first randomized clinical trial investigating the effect of daily vibration treatment in accelerating fracture healing. In our results, vibration treatment demonstrated positive effects in improving reaction time, lower extremity functional score, hip joint functions and quality of life. The vibration treatment was also well-tolerated by patients with negligible adverse effects. All these findings were critical in pushing forward the application of LMHFV in accelerating the functional recovery among young patients with long bone fractures.

471010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471010.value: 長期服用類固醇的患者會容易發生繼發性骨質疏松，從而增加骨折的危險．系統性紅斑狼瘡就是一種需要長期服用類固醇治療的疾病．傳統用以診斷骨質疏鬆的技術為雙能X線骨質密度測量儀 (dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry)，但是這項技術有其侷限性。包括其並不能分辨及評價骨密質和骨松質，由於圖像是二維，因此也無法評價三維的幾何立體圖像。另外，該檢查也常常受到偽像，例如骨贅或者動脈鈣化，的影響。因此單靠DXA檢查骨質密度並不能完全預測到骨折的風險，仍然有部分患者雖然骨質密度正常但仍然發生骨折．由此可見，除了骨質密度以外，骨質的三維微結構和硬度韌度等，也是骨質量的重要指標．高分辨CT定量分析技術 (high-resolution quantitative peripheral tomography)是目前最新的可用在人體身上的並且為無創的骨質檢查。該技術採用可耐受的放射量，分辨率可達到80微米，可以分辨骨密質和骨松質，並且可以準確地評價骨頭的密度和結構。 國外已經有研究使用該項技術研究不同性別年齡的人群骨質流失的情況以及骨質微結構。目前，研究發現，使用這項技術來評估停經後患者的遠端橈骨的骨質量，可以準確並且獨立的分辨出患者有無脆弱性骨折．使用這種技術得到的高分辨影響，結合使用有限元分析 (Finite Element Analysis)，用以分析骨頭的強度和韌性，可以得到更完整的骨頭質量的資料，從而更加好的來評價骨折的風險。而這些都是單靠雙能X線骨質密度測量儀所不能做到的． 然而，目前並沒有研究將這種新的檢查技術應用於由於長期服用類固醇導致骨質疏松上面．我們計畫這項研究，評價180名長期服用類固醇的系統性紅伴狼瘡患者和180名健康對照人群的骨密度，骨三維結構和骨強度韌度，從而比較兩組的差異．通過為期2年的觀察，也可以評價兩組人群的骨密度，骨三維結構和骨強度韌度的變化，並且研究這些變化與新發生骨折的關係，從而確定在長期服用類固醇患者中，可以預測到骨折風險的因素．研究的結果可以幫助我們更好的了解骨折發生的成因，從而改善骨折的預防和治療，這些結果更可以應用在其他需要長期服用類固醇的人群中，患者，醫療工作者和研究人員也可以從中受益．

471010.label: Realisation of objectives
471010.value: Objective 1: To compared the differences in cortical and trabecular microarchitecture in SLE patients on chronic GCs and in normal healthy subjects with HR-pQCT. - This objective was fully addressed in our findings from the baseline data. HR-pQCT revealed significant lower cortical volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) and microstructural deficits at the cortical compartment, manifested as lower cortical area, thinner cortices and higher cortical porosity in SLE patients on chronic GCs than in controls. Trabecular microstructure, on the other hand, remained largely maintained in SLE patients. Objective 2: To compare the differences in bone mechanical properties assessed by the finite element analysis based on HR-pQCT images of the distal radius in SLE patients on chronic GCs and in normal healthy subjects. - This objective was also fully addressed in our findings from the baseline data. Compared with controls, SLE patients had significantly lower whole bone stiffness, apparent modulus and failure load. Cortical stress was also lower in SLE patients with stress being more unevenly distributed. Objective 3: To compare the differences in cortical and trabecular microarchitecture and mechnical properties in SLE patients with and without history of vertebral and non-vertebral fracture. - This objective was addressed in our findings from the baseline data. Comparison between patients with and without history of fragility fracture revealed that the majority of the indices obtained from HR-pQCT did not differ significantly between the two groups. This is probably because the number of the patients with history of fracture was rather small (n=23). Therefore, we cannot fully address this objective. Objective 4: To assess changes in BMD, microarchitecture of bone and mechanical properties in SLE patients on GCs and comparing that with healthy controls - This objective was fully addressed in our findings from the prospective cohort. Results showed that during a 24-month period, the major features of structural deficits in SLE patients compared with controls included an accelerated loss of cortical bone area, thickness and an accelerated increase in cortical porosity. Objective 5: To identify the possible factors for incident fracture in patients on long-term GCs - This objective cannot be fully addressed in the prospective study. Preliminary analysis showed that the number of subjects with incidence fragility fracture (n=5) was rather low to allow a reliable analysis of risk factor for fracture. Attempt will be made to re-analyses all X-rays at the spine for incident asymptomatic vertebral fracture.

471010.label: Major findings and research outcome
471010.value: We conducted a two-year case-control prospective study on a cohort of female SLE patients and a cohort of age-matched healthy controls. We obtained areal bone mineral density (aBMD) at multiple skeletal sites using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and indices of volumetric BMD (vBMD) and microarchitecture using HR-pQCT at the distal radius at baseline, 12 and 24 months. Findings from baseline data (Publication #1 & #2) At baseline, In addition to significantly lower aBMD at femoral neck, total hip and lumbar spine, cortical area, average volumetric BMD (vBMD) and cortical vBMD also significantly reduced by 5.3, 5.7, to 1.9 % in SLE patients, respectively. Deteriorations of cortical microarchitecture were pronounced in patients, with 6.3 % reduction in cortical thickness and 13.6 % higher in cortical porosity. Trabecular vBMD and microstructure, on the other, appeared largely maintained in SLE patients. SLE patients had decreased whole bone stiffness, estimated failure load, and apparent modulus, as well as lower and more unevenly distributed cortical stress. We also analyzed the correlations between features of bone quality revealed by HR-pQCT and organ damage in SLE patients. Compared with patients without damage, the prevalence of osteopenia at either total hip or lumbar spine was significantly higher, and there were trends of deterioration of bone geometry, vBMD, microarchitecture, and biomechanical properties in patients with organ damage. Multiple regression analyses showed that higher organ damage was the only clinical variable consistently associated with deterioration of vBMD and microarchitecture. Findings from prospective study (publication #3) In the two-year follow-up study, significant over-time changes were observed in aBMD at the hip and all indices of vBMD, geometry and cortical microstructure at the distal radius. Trabecular vBMD appeared better maintained in patients. However, decrease in cortical area was greater in patients, with significant difference in percentage change seen at 12 months (-2.6% vs. -1.6%, p=0.012). Cortical thickness decreased to a significantly larger extent in patients than in controls at both 12 (-1.7% vs. -0.6%, p<0.0005) and 24 months (-2.7% vs. -1.6%, p=0.037). Increase in cortical porosity index at 24 months was also higher in patients (30% vs. 23%, p=0.049). Concluding remarks We confirmed in cross-sectional and prospective studies that the major features of structural deterioration in SLE patients on GCs were accelerated cortical thinning and cortical porosity. Our results highlight the potential of HR-pQCT to detect longitudinal changes of microstructure that are associated with bone fragility but beyond that provided by aBMD.

471010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471010.value: Our results provide evidence for the utility of HR-pQCT in detecting microstructural changes in SLE patients on long-term GCs who are known to be at risk of fragility fracture. The features revealed by HR-pQCT are beyond the provided by aBMD and they are known to associated with fragility fracture in postmenopausal women. Although we cannot demonstrate further if these features are associated with fracture risk in this group of patients due to the rather small number of subjects with history or incident fracture. Long-term follow-up of these subjects in terms of their clinical feature and their fracture risk using HR-pQCT will be beneficial in further validate the utility of this modality. Furthermore, the seemingly preserved trabecular vBMD and microstructure contrast our current knowledge that GCs predominantly affect trabecular bone particularly at the vertebrae. Despite wide array of adverse effects of GCs on the bone metabolism, these adverse effects may be outweighed by their favorable effect in controlling the active inflammation, especially when used in lower dose. Therefore, the differential effect of GCs on axial and peripheral skeleton, particularly in the context of persistent inflammation such as in a disease like SLE, deserves further investigation.

471010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471010.value: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are known to be at higher risk of fragility fracture, as a result of the active inflammation of the disease and long-term use of glucocorticoids (GCs). However, fracture risk in SLE patients could not be fully explained by the areal bone mineral density (aBMD) provided by traditional dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). In this research, we utilized a novel modality, namely the higher resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography (HR-pQCT), to investigate the volumetric BMD (vBMD) and microstructure at the distal radius in SLE patient relative to healthy controls. While aBMD failed to reveal significant difference at distal radius, HR-pQCT revealed dramatic microstructural decay in SLE patients, manifested as thinner cortices and higher cortical porosity, which are features known to predispose the bone to fracture. Our results highlight the potential of HR-pQCT to characterize bone architecture, to provide information on susceptibility to fracture beyond that provided by DXA and to be used as an outcome measurement for clinical studies. It can be served as a novel tool to improve our current assessment of bone strength in order to more accurately predict fracture risk and its dependence on age, disease and treatment.

471110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
471110.value: 外周血間充質幹細胞功能特點的研究

471110.label: Co - Investigator(s)
471110.value: Prof Chan, Kai-Ming Prof Wan, Chao Prof Zhou, Guang-Qian

471110.label: Project Objectives
471110.value: To improve culture conditions including the use of a bioreactor system for PB-MSCs. To investigate the roles of several selected, novel genes identified from our pilot bioinformatics work by comparing PB-MSCs and BM-MSCs in rats. Five candidate genes will be investigated in their functional roles in PB-MSC and BM-MSC in vitro: (1) Retinol-binding protein 1 (CRBP1); (2) Cadherin 2; (3) SRY-box containing gene 11 (Sox11); (4) Small nuclear ribonucleoparticle-associated protein (snRNP) mRNA, clone Sm51; and (5) Aquaporin 1 (AQP1). Based on the in vitro experimental data, two particular candidate genes will be selected for further functional investigation in vivo. The selected genes will be stably over-expressed or down-regulated in rat BM-MSCs using letiviral gene transfer approaches. The stably transfected rat BM-MSCs will be tested for their in vivo osteogenesis and chondrogenesis potentials in a transplant model. The gene-manipulated cells will also be tested in a rat fracture model by systemic administration to examine if fracture healing is enhanced. In summary, the proposed investigations are divided into 3 series of experiments, addressing mutually independent, yet closely related questions, so that the risk of failure is minimized and research output is maximized. The proposed research will enrich our knowledge of circulating MSCs in general and their novel isolation, enrichment and application in the course of bone repair in particular. The outcomes of this study may lead to a better understanding of the biological mechanisms by which PB-MSCs are released and homed to sites of injury and participate in tissue repair and regeneration. The findings may also lead to novel tissue engineering concepts utilizing PB-MSCs and some of the newly identified genes’ functions.

471110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471110.value: Skeletal tissue healing difficulties cause considerable suffering and pain to the patients following fractures, tendon or cartilage injury, hip replacement, bone tumor resection and metabolic bone diseases such as osteoporosis, which often result in reconstructive surgery. Bone grafting is frequently used, but this procedure has complications and causes further suffering, pain and discomfort to the patients. Synthetic bone materials, culture expansion of skeletal tissue cells, and specific recombinant proteins have been tried, but their use is hampered by difficulty in harvesting and growing skeletal cells, lack of vascularization, long duration of treatment and the associated high costs. Bone marrow cells seeded with synthetic biomaterials have been considered as an alternative to bone, cartilage or tendon grafting, however the requirement of bone marrow aspiration from the patient may cause further pain and morbidity at the donor sites and there is a long duration for culture expansion of these cells and control of their differentiation potentials. Following the recent discovery of a blood-borne cell population that may participate in tissue repair, we have demonstrated that repair cells may be recruited into the peripheral circulation and transported to the sites of skeletal injury to participate in healing, which may be a novel alternative for skeletal tissue repair and regeneration systemically. This project will examine the methods for isolation, culture, and enrichment of these circulating stem cells and the potential key genes that govern their functions and homing capacities. This study will broaden our understanding of how stem cells are mobilized and released into the peripheral circulation and homed to sites where they are needed to heal damaged tissues. The knowledge gained from this study will help us to develop new therapeutic protocols to promote skeletal tissue healing by directing blood-borne stem cells to tissue repair and regeneration, which may reduce the pain and suffer of patients. 幹細胞是近年世界生物學界研究的熱點，而迴圈間充質幹細胞（PBMSCs）相關研究尚少。我們通過前期大量基礎實驗證實，在人、大鼠、兔體內存在PBMSCs，具多向分化潛能；比較研究證實PBMSCs與骨髓來源間充質幹細胞形態功能類似，但在基因表達譜上有差異；在骨折癒合過程中，PBMSCs通過血循環活躍富集於損傷部位，可作為骨組織工程研究中幹細胞的新來源。本專案擬通過旋轉生物反應器建立富集PBMSCs的培養條件和方法；採用基因過表達方法，通過慢病毒載體系統穩定轉染前期已鑒定出的上調最明顯的基因，研究其調節細胞增殖、分化和動員的作用；進行動物體內植入實驗檢測其成骨潛能以及對骨折癒合的影響。通過本項目研究，將進一步拓寬對PBMSCs的認識，建立富集PBMSCs新方法，研究調控間充質幹細胞在組織修復和再生中新的重要功能基因，進而為幹細胞和骨組織工程的應用引入新的細胞或基因治療手段。

471110.label: Major findings and research outcome
471110.value: We have the following major findings through this study: (1) PB-MSCs can be cultured and expanded using bioreactor. (2) CRBP1 (cellular retinol binding protein 1) overexpression promoted osteogenic differentiation of MSCs, while inhibited their adipogenic differentiation. CRBP1 promotes osteogenic differentiation of MSCs by inhibiting RXRα-induced β-catenin degradation, maintaining β-catenin and pERK1/2 at higher levels. (3) N-cadherin overexpression inhibited osteogenic differentiation of MSCs through negatively regulating β-catenin and ERK1/2 signaling pathways. N-cadherin overexpression could promote the migration potential of MSCs. (4) Aquaporin 1 (Aqp1) is a water channel molecule and a regulator of endothelial cell migration. Overexpression of Aqp1 promoted MSCs migration, while depletion of Aqp1 impaired MSCs migration in vitro. When the GFP labeled Aqp1 overexpressing MSCs were systemically injected into rats with a femoral fracture, there were significantly more GFP-MSCs found at the fracture gap in the Aqp1-GFP-MSCs-treated group. β-catenin and focal adhesion kinase (FAK) were upregulated in the Aqp1-MSCs and downregulated in the Aqp1-depleted MSCs. (5) Sox11 overexpression enhanced the tri-lineage differentiation and migration of MSCs. Sox11 could activate BMP/Smad signaling pathway in MSCs. In an open femur fracture model in rats, we found a larger number of MSCs stably expressing Sox11 migrated to the fracture site, and improved bone fracture healing. (6) We have strong pilot data demonstrating a novel role of Sm51 in regulating osteogenic differentiation of MSCs. Sm51 may be an important regulator of osteogenesis in MSCs, probably through directly regulating the expression of Runx2.

471110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471110.value: These findings form the current studies reveal a potential role of CRBP1 in the regulation of β-catenin turnover which can greatly affect the process of osteogenesis and adipogenesis of MSCs. The finding suggests a novel function of Aqp1 in governing MSCs migration, and this may aid MSCs therapeutic applications. Our study also shows that Sox11 is an important regulator of MSCs differentiation and migration, and Sox11-modified MSCs may have clinical implication for accelerating bone fracture healing, which can reduce the delayed unions or non-unions. Finally, we have strong pilot data demonstrating a novel role of Sm51 in regulating osteogenic differentiation of MSCs, which form the basis for future research (RGC) proposal to further explore the functions of Sm51 in regulating MSCs differentiation, bone development and repair.

471110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471110.value: Circulating mesenchymal stem cells is a new cell source for tissue regeneration and tissue engineering. The characteristics of circulating mesenchymal stem cells are similar with bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs), but they exist at a very low level in healthy individuals and have distinct genetic profiles comparing to BM-MSCs. The current study have demonstrated novel roles of some genes and will enrich the basic knowledge of circulating MSCs and their potential clinical applications. The application of MSCs to cure a broad spectrum of diseases is promising, such as spinal cord injury, cardiovascular repair, bone and cartilage repair, etc. The findings from the current study will lead to novel strategies for re-program or genetically modify MSCs for improved clinical therapy applications.
