471210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471210.value: The aim of this research project is to elucidate the causes of childhood obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), in particular to identify the extent to which the disorder is due to genetic factors in order to better develop screening and treatment approaches. OSA is characterized by repeated episodes of complete and or partial upper airway occlusion during sleep, associated with arousals, distorted sleep patterns and physiological abnormalities. Childhood OSA is common in our locality, and it is associated with an extensive array of important complications namely neurocognitive dysfunction as well as cardiovascular and metabolic abnormalities. There is accumulating support that OSA has a strong familial component, however, its magnitude is unclear. Current research suggest the presence of two subtypes of OSA in children with differing clinical characteristics: one associated with lymphoid enlargement in the absence of obesity, and the other “adult-like” entity being primarily associated with obesity. Differential analyses of these two subtypes in childhood OSA research is crucial to the development of treatment strategies. The majority of previous family studies were carried out in Caucasian adults, and limited work with questionable study design has been done to evaluate the role of familial factors in the development childhood OSA. In this proposed genetic-epidemiological study, we will assess the distribution of OSA in families identified to have confirmed childhood OSA and among families in the same community with children without OSA. We aim to determine familial aggregation and risk factors for the development of OSA in Chinese obese and non-obese children. The information obtained will provide a better understanding of ethnic predisposition of childhood OSA, and how anthropometric, facial-skeletal, upper airway size and ventilatory response characteristics interact in each subtype of childhood OSA. We intend to show that first-degree relatives of children with OSA have an increased risk of OSA explained by Mendelian inheritance, and that risk factors for the development of OSA are different for obese and non-obese children. At present the impact of predisposing risk factors on the two subtypes of childhood OSA is unclear. Our research will clarify the genetic link to inheritance of the condition and show that differing risk factors are involved in obese and non-obese children. This research will lead to better screening mechanisms and appropriate treatment regimens for the different subtypes of childhood OSA which will impact on subsequent health care provision. 本研究旨在探討引致兒童阻塞性睡眠呼吸暫停症 [簡稱睡眠窒息症 (OSA)] 之遺傳因素，藉以發展更好的診斷和治療方法。 睡眠窒息症的特點是睡眠時上呼吸道重覆地完全阻塞或部分阻塞，以致覺醒及影響睡眠素質和其他生理問題。兒童睡眠窒息症是本港常見的問題，該症狀與一系列重要併發症有關，包括認知功能障礙，心血管異常及代謝異常。 有越來越多數據支持睡眠窒息症有的家族遺傳性，但其對發病的重要性目前尚不清楚。最近的有關研究建議根據臨床的特徵將兒童睡眠窒息症分成兩型：一型是主要與上呼吸道的軟組織肥大相關；二型是主要與肥胖有關。在研究中這兩種兒童睡眠窒息症必須個別分析，才可發展適當的治療策略。大部分以前的家族性研究都是在白人社區進行，對於遺傳因素在兒童睡眠窒息症發展的角色，現有的理據仍很缺乏。 在此遺傳流行病學研究中，我們將評估及比較睡眠窒息症在兩類家庭當中分佈，一類是有兒童睡眠窒息症的家庭，另一類是沒有兒童睡眠窒息症的家庭。我們的目標是引證兒童睡眠窒息症在中國人社區的家族聚集性，以及探討該病症在肥胖和非肥胖兒童的風險因素。研究中所獲得的資料將對兒童睡眠窒息症的種族傾向提供一個更深入的了解，也可了解更多有關體格、面部骨骼、上呼吸道結構及通氣反應在肥胖和非肥胖兒童睡眠窒息症當中的相互作用及關係。我們預計睡眠窒息症患兒的直系親屬患有睡眠窒息症的風險較高，而肥胖和非肥胖兒童睡眠窒息症的風險因素會有所不同。 目前，各種危險因素對於兩種成因不同的兒童睡眠窒息症的影響仍未清楚。我們的研究將闡明該病症的遺傳性，並找出肥胖和非肥胖兒童不同的風險因。這項研究將改善對於兩種兒童睡眠窒息症的診斷及治療效率，繼而改善日後的健康護理服務。

471310.label: Realisation of objectives
471310.value: All three objectives have been realised. Objective 1: PA-induced hepatotoxicity has been developed in rat model treated with 12 PAs and 6 PA-containing herbal extracts. The results demonstrated that PAs dose-dependently induced hepatotoxicity with significantly varied severity of different PAs. These results proved our hypothesis in that the currently used single toxic dose threshold is not suitable for establishing toxic dosage regulation to all PAs. Furthermore, a novel UHPLC-MS method was developed for qualitatively and quantitatively determining pyrrole-protein adducts in biological specimens obtained from rats dosed with different PAs and PA-containing herbal extracts. The results obtained from Western blot, ELISA, UHPLC-MS, and proteomics all revealed that pyrrole-protein adducts having the identical core pyrrole moiety were generated from metabolic activation of all toxic PAs regardless of their structures. Therefore, it is confirmed for the first time that such pyrrole-protein adducts could be served as a specific mechanism-based biomarker for PA-induced hepatotoxicity. Object 2: Using our developed novel method, pyrrole-protein adducts in biological specimens of rats dosed with PAs and PA-containing herbal extracts were measured. The results further approved our hypotheses in that 1) hepatotoxic severity of different PAs varies significantly; and 2) a single dose is not suitable for the establishment of regulation as a universal toxic dosage threshold for all PAs. The results also demonstrated that both blood and hepatic levels of pyrrole-protein adducts correlated well with 1) PA dosage and 2) severity of PA-induced hepatotoxicity. Therefore, blood level of such adducts can be further developed as the mechanism-based bio-monitoring marker for clinical assessment. Objective 3: Blood samples of 10 PA-induced HSOS patients, who ingested a Chinese medicinal herb ‘Tusanqi’, 3 patients having liver disease with unknown causes, and 10 healthy volunteers from Zhongshan Hospital in Shanghai, China, were tested. All available herbs ingested by HSOS patients were identified as Gynura segetum, and determined to contain toxic PAs (mainly senecionine, seneciphylline and their N-oxides), confirming that PA-containing herbs poisoned all these HSOS patients. Blood pyrrole-protein adducts were determined in all HSOS patients, but not in other liver disease patients or healthy volunteers. Moreover, the results indicated that a median value of pyrrole-protein adducts in severe HSOS patients was significantly higher than that in moderate HSOS patients (14.4 vs 8.5 nM, p<0.05), demonstrating that blood pyrrole-protein adducts level was proportional to the severity of PA-induced hepatotoxicity.

471310.label: Major findings and research outcome
471310.value: The major findings and research outcomes of this project include: 1) The delineation of the toxic mechanism The toxic mechanism was delineated to be metabolic activation mediated by hepatic CYP isozymes to generate reactive metabolites (pyrrolic esters), which rapidly reacts with proteins to form pyrrole-protein adducts leading to hepatotoxicity. We, for the first time, demonstrated the absences of metabolic activation and formation of pyrrole-protein adducts of non-toxic PAs having saturated necine base [4], confirming that metabolic activation only occurred in PAs having unsaturated necine base but not those with saturated necine base. Furthermore, the contributions of structural differences and differential CYPs mediating the metabolic activation to toxic potency of different PAs have also been thoroughly investigated for the first time [5]. 2) The development of a novel mechanism-based bio-monitoring marker The above metioned mechanism study provided a scientific basis for developing pyrrole-protein adducts as the mechanism-based bio-monitoring marker for PA intoxication. We thus developed a novel HPLC-MS analytical method to idnetify and quantidy pyrrole-protein adducts and demonstrated that both blood and hepatic levels of pyrrole-protein adducts correlated well with the severity of PA-induced hepatotoxicity in animal studies. Further application to the patients poisoned by PA-containing herbs confirmed that blood pyrrole-protein adducts can be utilized as specific bio-monitoring marker for the diagnosis and assessment of PA intoxication [1, 6]. 3) The establishment of the fundation for furture development of regulations for safe use of PA-containing natural products Again, based on the toxic mechanims deliniated, we hypothessized that the formation efficency of pyrrole-protein adducts can be used to predict potential hepatotoxicity of PAs. We further developed HPLC-MS analytical methods for the determination of different types PAs and PA N-oxides in herbs [2] to determine identity and quantity of PAs in various herbs, and investigated both in vitro and in vivo toxicities of various of PAs and PA-containing herbs [3, 5]. The hepatotoxicity in animal models was assessed using various methods, including Western blot, ELISA, and proteomics [7]. The results all revealed that pyrrole-protein modifications, especially the formation of pyrrole-protein adducts correlated well with toxic severity and dosage of PAs regardless of their structures. Therefore, it revealed for the first time that toxic dose threshold of different PAs established based on their formation efficiency of pyrrole-protein adducts is more rational for the regulation establishment of quality control of PA-containing/PA-contaminated natural products.

471310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471310.value: Our findings and achievements obtained from this research project provided a solid foundation for the further development of the relevant research into two major areas: 1) the establishment of a suitable regulation, which is based on the toxic meachims of PAs, for the safe use of PA-containing medicinal herbs and natural products; and 2) the translational research for the develoment of specific bio-monitoring marker for clincal diagnosis and assessment of PA intoxication. Consequently, with these sound scientific evidences and rational for the further developed, additional two research projects, which are related to these two areas respectively, were awarded by GRF grants and are currently under progress. The first one (RGC ref. No. 469712) is to develop quantitative method to determine total content of toxic PAs in PA-containing natural products without requiring all PA standards (because most of them are unavailable), and to identify the major factors affecting toxic potency of PAs associated with the metabolic activation. The second one (RGC ref. No. 471013) is to further validate the blood pyrrole-protein adducts as feasible bio-monitoring marker of PA intoxication for future clinical application.

471310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471310.value: Among various phytotoxins, pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are one of the most common causes of natural product poisonings in human, because of their wide distribution in plant with over 6,000 known PA-containing plants to date. PAs cause liver toxicity in human due to the consumption of PA-containing herbs, teas, and vegetables, as well as PA-contaminated foods and dietary products. PAs induce hepatotoxicity via metabolic activation to generate toxic pyrrolic metabolites, which form pyrrole-protein adducts leading to toxicity. In the present study, we systematically investigated the toxic mechanism, particularly pyrrole-protein modifications in laboratory animals treated with different PAs and PA-containing herbs. Based on our findings of the metabolism-induced mechanism, we developed a novel analytical method to determine pyrrole-protein adducts in biological samples and revealed that blood pyrrole-protein adducts correlated well with PA-induced toxicity in animal models. Subsequently, using our developed novel analytical method, we further tested pyrrole-protein adducts in the blood of the patients, who were poisoned by the intake of PA-containing herbs. The results demonstrated that pyrrole-protein adducts were only determined in the patients exposed to PAs, but not in the healthy volunteers. Therefore, we confirmed that blood pyrrole-protein adducts can be utilized as a bio-monitoring marker of PA poisoning.

471310.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
471310.value: We are the first to successfully develop and apply blood pyrrole-protein adducts as bio-monitoring marker for the assessment of PA-induced hepatotoxicity in patients. Our work has been well recognized internationally. In the past two years, we have been invited by US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to collaboratively investigate an outbreak of an unidentified liver disease (ULD) that has affected over 1200 persons with mortality over 30% in Tigray, Ethiopia since 2007. The US CDC has been continuously and financially supporting us for this collaborative project. By the analysis of blood pyrrole-protein adducts in the patients, we have confirmed that this ULD is the PA-induced liver disease due to the consumption of PA-contaminated foodstuffs, which has been subsequently found to be contaminated with PA-containing plants (our unpublished data). Presentation Award: J.Q. Ruan and G. Lin* (2011). Metabolic activation – the hepatotoxicity related metabolism of pyrrolizidine alkaloids. At 2011 ISSX/CSSX Workshop, Guangzhou, China, 2011, 09.

471610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471610.value: Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma (NPC) is endemic in Southern China with an incidence rate of ~25 to 30/100,000 per annum. Targeted interventions represent promising theraputic approaches for this highly malignant cancer, but an understanding on the molecular basis and signaling paths involved is pre-requisite. Aberrant activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, which involved in the control of cell proliferation, apoptosis and oncogenesis, is widely implicated in many human cancers. Recent studies have begun to demonstrate constitutively activated AKT signals in a majority of primary NPCs. However, the precise role of this aberrant PI3K/AKT signaling in the NPC tumorigenesis and the molecular mechanisms by which AKT is constitutively activated remain unclear. Despite there have only few studies describing the genetic alterations of PI3K/AKT signaling constituents in NPC, our group has demonstrated high-level amplification of PIK3CA in 20% of primary tumors. By high-density oligonucleotide microarray, we recently found that expression of INPP4B, a negative regulator of the PI3K/AKT pathway was consistently down-regulated in EBV-positive NPC tumor lines. Furthermore, we showed, for the first time, that INPP4B was transcriptional silenced by promoter hypermethylation and histone modification in NPC. We hypothesize that epigenetic inactivation of INPP4B is one of the key mechanisms in activating PI3K/AKT signaling cascade and thereby contributes to the oncogenesis of EBV-associated NPC. The present study hence proposes to investigate the functional path by which INPP4B exerts its effect on PI3K/AKT pathway in the NPC tumorigenesis and to define the molecular mechanism(s) that underlie the INPP4B inactivation in NPC. Firstly, based on our recent preliminary findings, we will extend our analysis on the genetic and epigenetic changes to INPP4B and other key components of the PI3K/AKT pathway in a large cohort of NPC. Correlative analysis will be carried out to substantiate the significance of these alterations with clinicopathologic outcome of NPC patients. Secondly, the tumor suppressive function of INPP4B and its role in PI3K/AKT signaling pathway will be examined in EBV-positive NPC cells in detail. We will also investigate the effect of INPP4B knockdown on transforming nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Finally, we will determine the potential therapeutic value in targeting the PI3K/AKT pathway, and in combination with chemotherapy, in pre-clinical EBV-positive NPC models. Our proposed studies should provide better understanding on the signaling paths involved in NPC and basis for future development for more efficacious therapies. 鼻咽癌（NPC）為一種中國南方常見癌症，其發病率約為每年25~30/10萬人，因此急需對鼻咽癌進行針對性治療並深入了解該疾病的分子生物學發病機制。在人類癌症發病過程中，細胞增殖，雕亡和癌變都涉及PI3K/AKT信號通路異常活化。我們最新研究證實鼻咽癌標本中激活AKT信號。然而，在這種EB病毒相關上皮癌中PI3K/AKT通路異常活化的分子機制仍有待闡明。儘管少數研究展示鼻咽癌中PI3K/AKT通路發生基因變異，我們發現PIK3CA基因擴增只出現在20％的原發腫瘤中。通過高密度寡核苷酸基因芯片，我們發現在EB病毒陽性鼻咽癌中，PI3K/AKT通路的負調控因子INPP4B表達下調。此外我們首先發現，INPP4B啟動子甲基化令其在多種腫瘤中出現表達下調。我們推測在EB病毒相關鼻咽癌中INPP4B下調為PI3K/AKT信號通路激活的關鍵機制。這項研究旨在探討鼻咽癌中PI3K/AKT信號通路激活的分子機制和研究INPP4B失活在癌變過程中的作用。首先，我們將在大量鼻咽癌樣本中進一步研究PI3K/AKT信號通路的改變機制，及AKT激活和臨床預後之間的關聯。其次我們將研究INPP4B腫瘤抑制功能及其在PI3K/AKT信號通路中的作用，我們亦會研究INPP4B在鼻咽上皮細胞轉化中的作用。最後我們將研究針對PI3K/AKT通路並結合化療作為一種有效治療EB病毒陽性鼻咽癌的方法。這些研究將為今後EB病毒相關鼻咽癌的臨床治療提供研究基礎。

471610.label: Realisation of objectives
471610.value: To elucidate the role of INPP4B and PI3K/AKT signalling pathway in the NPC development, we have comprehensive investigated for the genetic and epigenetic changes of INPP4B and multiple components of PI3K/AKT pathway. We revealed that epigenetic inactivation of INPP4B by promoter methylation and histone modification was common in both NPC tumor lines and primary tumors (37.5%). Using Sanger direct DNA sequencing and massive parallel genome sequencing, we found that somatic genetic changes/mutations of INPP4B, PTEN, AKT1, AKT3 and other components of PI3K/AKT pathway are rare. Notably, missense mutation in the kinase domain of AKT2 was identified in few NPC samples. We also confirmed the frequent PIK3CA amplification (~18%) in the study of a large cohort of primary NPC. In a panel of 10 patients from phase I clinical trial of AKT inhibitor(MK-2206), our preliminary study demonstrated the presence of PIK3CA amplification in 2 patients who showed obviously respond to the treatment. Currently, a new clinical study of AKT inhibitor in a subgroup of NPC patients with PIK3CA alterations is planning. Using a pCMV-INPP4B constructs expressed wild type INPP4B, the effects of ectopic transient expression of INPP4B on suppression of AKT signalling pathway were confirmed in the EBV-positive C666-1 cells. In the INPP4B-expressing HK-1 cells, knockdown of INPP4B by siRNAs resulted in increased p-AKT and p-GSK3b expression. The results imply that INPP4B modulates the activation of PI3K/AKT pathway. The stable INPP4B-expressing C666-1 cells was established for investigation of its effect on cell proliferation, survival and tumor formation. Notably, in vivo study has revealed that the tumor growth was highly reduced in the stable INPP4B-expressing cells when compared with the vector controls. Using the multiple luciferase reporter assays, we have demonstrated that INPP4B also significantly suppresses the NF-kB, Hypoxia and MAPK/ERK signalling pathways in NPC cells. We also discovered the involvement of PI3K/AKT signalling in regulation of multiple novel LMP1 targets (e.g. HVEM) in EBV-associated NPC. The anti-neoplastic activity of multiple inhibitors targeting PI3K (LY294002), AKT (Triciribine) and mTOR (Rapamycin) in NPC cells were examined. The EBV-positive NPC cells were shown to be highly sensitivity to the PI3K inhibitor, LY294002. Furthermore, our recent study has comprehensively characterization of the NPC cancer-stem like cell and sphere-forming cells. Importantly, we showed that the PI3K inhibitor, LY294002 inhibits the growth of the tumor spheres and targets NPC CSCs. In addition to the PI3K/AKT pathway, we also characterized the related AMPK signalling in EBV-associated NPC.

471610.label: Major findings and research outcome
471610.value: In this study, aside from the EBV-encoded LMP1 oncogene, we have demonstrated the activation of PI3K/AKT signalling pathway via genetic (PIK3CA amplification, AKT2 mutation) and epigenetic changes (INPP4B methylation and histone acetylation) in NPC. For INPP4B, we have confirmed its role as negative regulator of PI3K/AKT signalling pathway in this EBV-associated epithelial cancer. The tumor suppressive function of INPP4B was shown in the in vivo nude mice models. (Yuen et al., in preparation and Lo et al, 06/13/Istanbul abstract). We also found that INPP4B also contribute to the inhibition of multiple pathways including NF-KB, Hypoxia and MAPK/ERK. It implies the crosstalk of PI3K/AKT and these pathways in NPC cells. After assessing the antineoplastic effect of multiple inhibitors for PI3K/AKT pathway, we revealed that the PI3K inhibitor, LY294002 with the most efficient growth inhibition of NPC cells. In a collaborated study, we found that inhibition of PI3K/AKT signalling lead to the suppression of sphere-forming cells in C666-1. The finding implies the role of PI3K/AKT pathways in maintenance of cancer stem-like cells in NPC. (Lun et al, PLoS One, 2012; Lo et al, Cancer Lett. 2013). Importantly, our recently studies have further found the associated of PIK3CA amplification with the advance NPC. The presence of PIK3CA amplification in some patients that were responded to the AKT inhibitor (MK-2206) treatment suggested the PI3K/AKT signalling as potential molecular targets for new therapeutic strategies. Our preliminary data led to the redesign of the clinical trial and planning of a new biomarker driven clinical trial of AKT inhibitor is ongoing. The significance of aberrant PI3K/AKT signalling in the development of NPC and its potential role in development of target therapy of this disease were discussed in our recent review articles. (Lun et al, eLS, 2013; Lo et al, Semin Cancer Biol, 2012). Recently, aside from PI3K/AKT pathway, we also characterized the related AMPK signalling in EBV-associated NPC. We demonstrated a novel ability of LMP1 to inhibit the LKB1-AMPK pathway which contributes to the proliferation and transformation of epithelial cells. The findings suggest that AMPK activators could be used to enhance the efficacy of conventional chemotherapeutic agents in the treatment of local and metastatic NPC. (Lo et al, J Pathol, 2013).

471610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471610.value: (1) In this study, we showed that the PI3K inhibitor, LY294002 showed promising growth inhibitory effect on NPC cell line C666-1. We will further evaluate its in vivo antineoplastic effect in a panel of EBV-positive NPC xenografts including xeno-666, xeno-2117, C15 and C17. Similar in vitro and in vivo preclinical study of NPC will be performed using other potential PI3K and AKT inhibitors including MK-2206 . (2) As mentioned in previous lesions, a biomarker driven clinical trials of AKT inhibitor (MK-2206) is planning and INPP4B expression, AKT2 mutation and PIK3CA amplification will be included as potential biomarkers in this study. (3) We will further investigate the role of PI3K/AKT signalling in the development and maintenance of NPC cancer stem-like cells. (4) Identification of novel targets of PI3K/AKT signalling pathways in EBV-associated NPC.

471610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471610.value: The constitutive activation of PI3K/AKT pathway was commonly found in EBV-associated NPC. In addition to LMP1 expression and PIK3CA amplification, we revealed that inactivation of INPP4B by promoter methylation and histone modification is one of the major mechanisms for activation of PI3K/AKT signalling. Suppression of PI3K/AKT signalling by INPP4B was confirmed in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. The tumor suppressive role of INPP4B in NPC cells was also shown in this study. Furthermore, we also demonstrated that targeting PI3K/AKT signalling by PI3K inhibitor suppressed the growth and tumor formation of NPC cells. The novel effect of PI3K/AKT signalling inhibition on targeting NPC cancer stem-like cells was found. Our findings suggest targeting the pathway by PI3K inhibitors is an promising therapeutic strategy for NPC patients.

471810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471810.value: 眾所周知腫瘤細胞會為了生存而調整細胞代謝。新的證據表明“調整細胞代謝”在腫瘤形成中起了關鍵的作用,包括抗凋亡(腫瘤的一個重要的內部特徵)。鼻咽癌是在東南亞非常普遍的一種高侵襲性癌症。抗凋亡會導致失控的腫瘤細胞生長和生存,它是鼻咽癌的一個顯著特徵;但是其潛在的分子機制還未完全清楚。TIGAR（TP53誘導的糖酵解和凋亡調控因子）是一種新的凋亡和細胞代謝雙重調控因子。TIGAR首先被認定是由主要的腫瘤抑制基因p53誘導的,所以也被認為是抑制腫瘤的。然而,最近的證據表明TIGAR表達在腫瘤中可能是失控的(已證實在腫瘤中高表達,包括鼻咽癌),從而通過代謝調整來賦予腫瘤細胞抗凋亡特徵,以此滿足腫瘤快速增殖的高代謝需求,這就將TIGAR被認定的功能從腫瘤抑制切換到了可能致癌。我們相信腫瘤細胞通過一種有待確定的機制導致TIGAR失控或高表達,從而操縱或利用這條抗凋亡通路來實現它們的生存和代謝需求。我們最近的資料證實STAT3,一個已知參與鼻咽癌癌變過程的重要致癌基因和轉錄因子,在鼻咽癌中是TIGAR表達的一個上游調控因子。我們假設STAT3的激活促使了TIGAR在鼻咽癌中的上調或高表達,從而操縱或利用TIGAR來實現它們的生長和代謝需求。在這裡,我們提出了在鼻咽癌中通過STAT3導致TIGAR上調的一個工作模型。我們的目的在於闡明STAT3對 TIGAR的調控機制,同時我們也會觀察這個新的STAT3-TIGAR信號軸在鼻咽癌癌變過程中的生物學相關性和功能性貢獻。這是第一個證實了在癌症中由一個致癌基因 (STAT3) 介導的TIGAR表達調控的研究,這可能是癌症中TIGAR高表達或失控的關鍵驅動機制（因為STAT3在各種人類腫瘤中經常被激活）。我們的研究將會為TIGAR和STAT3在致癌過程中界定新的作用。

471810.label: Realisation of objectives
471810.value: 1. We have demonstrated that TIGAR was overexpressed in 6/6 NPC cell lines and in 27/36 (75%) tumor biopsies from patients with NPC. In NPC, STAT3 is activated by EBV to regulate expression of downstream genes. In this study, we have found that STAT3 silencing results in downregulation of TIGAR expression in 3 NPC cell lines, providing evidence for presence of a novel and biologically relevant STAT3-TIGAR signaling pathway in NPC cells. 2. We have found that activation of the STAT3-TIGAR pathway in NPC cell lines increased cell proliferation (4-fold), NADPH production (2-fold) and cell invasiveness (5-fold). In addition, the expression of the anti-apoptotic protein Mcl-1 (a known STAT3 target gene), and mesenchymal markers fibronectin and vimentin were all upregulated. These results demonstrate that activated STAT3-TIGAR signaling axis contributes to NPC tumorigenesis by promoting cell growth, prohibiting apoptotic cell death and regulating expression of mesenchymal markers. 3. This study has found that downregulation of TIGAR expression in NPC causes growth inhibition, NADPH depletion, reduced cell invasiveness (10-fold) and reduction in expression of mesenchymal markers fibronectin and vimentin. These findings indicate that TIGAR expression is pivotal for NPC tumor growth. 4. It is clear from the above description that the proposed objectives have been achieved to a high degree. We have 1) demonstrated existence of a novel STAT3-TIGAR pathway in NPC by providing proof that STAT3 regulates TIGAR expression, 2) determined the biological relevance of the STAT3-TIGAR pathway towards NPC development (promotion of cell growth, NADPH production, invasiveness and expression of mesenchymal markers essential for EMT) and 3) demonstrated the biological consequence of TIGAR inhibition in NPC cells (inhibition of growth, NADPH production, invasiveness and expression of mesenchymal markers essential for EMT).

471810.label: Major findings and research outcome
471810.value: • Proved existence of a novel and biologically relevant STAT3-TIGAR pathway in NPC cells. • Determined that TIGAR overexpression stimulates cell growth, enhances cellular resistance to damage from reactive oxidant species (ROS) through increased NADPH production, increases cancer cell invasiveness and promotes expression of mesenchymal markers necessary for EMT in NPC cells. • Demonstrated that inhibition of TIGAR expression in NPC results in growth suppression, reduction in NADPH production which renders NPC cells more susceptible to ROS induced cell damage, attenuates cell invasiveness and downregulates expression of proteins required for EMT. • Abstract presented in the 2011 American Association for Cancer Research 102nd Annual Meeting (Title: TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator (TIGAR) induces NADPH production and growth in nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells). • Abstract accepted for presentation in the 2014 American Association for Cancer Research 105th Annual Meeting (Title: Functional significance of TIGAR expression in nasopharyngeal carcinoma). • PhD student graduated with thesis titled “A novel link of Bcl-2 to TIGAR and NADPH regulation reveals the role of TIGAR in tumorigenesis”. • Manuscript is accepted by the Oncology Letters titled “The TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator promotes proliferation and invasiveness of nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells”.

471810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471810.value: • To determine if TIGAR expression correlates with clinical characteristics of NPC patients. TIGAR expression levels could be determined by immunohistochemistry. IHC scores could then be used to investigate whether TIGAR expression levels are correlated with TNM stage, progression free survival, metastasis free survival and overall survival. • TIGAR suppression may be a viable therapeutic option for treatment of NPC patients. To provide further support for this hypothesis, NPC cell lines which have been transfected with either siRNAs targeting TIGAR or negative controls could be grown in mice xenograft models to determine whether TIGAR silenced xenografts do indeed demonstrate reduced growth and invasiveness. • TIGAR overexpression promotes NADPH production in NPC cells. NADPH provides the major source of protection from damage by cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). Since radiotherapy component used in treatment of NPC patients kills cancer cells through generation of ROS, it would be important to determine whether TIGAR overexpression confers radio-resistance to NPC cells and limits treatment efficacy. The effects of radiation on NPC cells could be compared between cells overexpressing TIGAR to those with silenced TIGAR expression to see if TIGAR expression levels affect NPC radiosensitivity.

471810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471810.value: This study has provided evidence demonstrating the biological relevance of a newly identified STAT3-TIGAR signaling pathway in NPC cells. We have found that TIGAR is up-regulated in 75% of NPC biopsies examined and that STAT3 was capable of regulating TIGAR expression in NPC cells. TIGAR overexpression was also found in 6/6 NPC cell lines where it was observed to increase cell proliferation, stimulate NADPH production, promote cell invasiveness and up-regulate expression of mesenchymal proteins necessary for EMT. These findings underscore the importance of TIGAR expression in promoting NPC development. On the contrary, suppression of TIGAR expression was found to be capable of inhibiting NPC cell growth, reducing cellular NADPH levels, suppressing invasiveness and downregulating expression of mesenchymal proteins. These results suggest that TIGAR may have value as a biological target for treatment of NPC patients. All in all, our study has provided a deeper understanding of NPC pathogenesis and laid the foundation for development of a novel therapeutic target for improved treatment and survival of patients with NPC.

471910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471910.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is the 7th most common cancer in Hong Kong where over 50% of patients present with advanced disease requiring cytotoxic chemotherapy. Despite the fact that the high ‘response rate’ (tumor shrinkage) of NPC to chemotherapy, the overall survival of patients with advanced disease remains poor because the benefit of chemotherapy is not durable for most patients. The current method of assessing the efficacy of new drugs for NPC is based mainly on the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (‘RECIST’) criteria which measures uni-dimensional changes in tumor size via radiological imaging, usually following over 3-4 months of empirical therapy. This method is fraught with limitations in NPC because: (a) it is relatively time-consuming since several months of empirical therapy are often needed for detectable changes in tumor dimensions to develop; (b) it does not accurately reflect drug response in bony metastases and some locally recurrent tumors; (c) it has not been directly correlated with patient survival – the key endpoint in cancer drug trials; (d) it is inadequate in assessing target-based drugs that slows/ stop tumor growth but do not shrink tumors. Thus, there is a need to identify a more efficient and accurate way of identifying new drugs that can improve survival in clinical trials of NPC. Plasma levels of Epstein Barr virus DNA (pEBV DNA) reflects tumor burden in NPC, and a single measurement taken at either before or after radiotherapy (RT) is a powerful prognostic marker. It has a half-life of around 4 days following radiotherapy, but the utility of pEBV DNA half-life in predicting drug response in NPC is unclear. Dual 18-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography and CT scan (PET-CT) measures both tumor size and metabolic activity. We therefore hypothesize that the combination of pEBV DNA (half-life) and PET-CT following 1 course of chemotherapy allow earlier and more detection of drug response in advanced NPC than RECIST method, in patients with previously untreated advanced NPC who will receive platinum-based chemotherapy. This study will also determine if this new method can predict survival in these patients. This study may have far-reaching impact on drug development in NPC as it may offer a more optimal way of evaluating drug efficacy in clinical trials and also in clinical management. 鼻咽癌是香港最普遍癌症中排行第七，超過50%病人屬晚期需要接受細胞毒性化療。儘管鼻咽癌對化療的高’反應比率(腫瘤縮小)’，晚期病者的整體存活率偏差，因為大部份病人不能再承受化療的益處。現有評估鼻咽癌新藥方法主要依據放射影像以實體瘤療效評價標準去計算單面腫瘤大小的改變，通常在3-4個經驗性療法之後進行。這方法用於鼻咽癌上有很多限制a) 比較需時,因為需要幾個月經驗性療法，才達腫瘤尺寸可檢測的改變;(b)它不能準確地反映藥物在骨轉移及某些局部復發腫瘤;(c)它不直接與病人生存扯上關係 –癌症藥物試驗;(d)它不足以評估標靶為本藥物只減慢/停止腫瘤生長，但不能縮少腫瘤。再者，有需要找尋一個更有效及準確方法去辨別一些能改善在鼻咽癌臨床試驗中存活率的新藥。EB病毒DNA血漿水平反映鼻咽癌腫瘤負荷，在放射治療或前或後單一量度是有力的前瞻性標誌物。

471910.label: Realisation of objectives
471910.value: (1) Enrollment: From July 2011 to Nov 2015, 111 patients were screened and 69 patients were consented, thus achieving the planned sample of 68 subjects. 11 patients were not eligible due to patient refusal and clinical deterioration before starting chemotherapy. Therefore, 58 patients were eligible for study, of whom 50 (86.2%) completed all study scans. The reasons for not completing all the study scans included withdrawal of consent after the baseline PET-CT, and inability to complete chemotherapy due to clinical deterioration. - Study initiation was delayed due to the PI being on medical leave and enrollment was initially affected by a 20% drop in the number of new NPC cases presenting to the department from 2009 (214 cases) to 2012 (172 cases). Of these new cases, only around 35% were potentially eligible. Several remedial measures were successfully implemented, which included revision of the sample size to 68, increase in the number of investigators, and expansion of the inclusion criteria to patients with locoregionally advanced NPC who needed induction chemotherapy. (2) Realization of objectives: The study aimed to identify a new method of predicting whether a patient may benefit from chemotherapy at the earliest time-point in terms of survival by measuring both metabolic and biomarker response at 4-6 weeks after starting chemotherapy (a dual-endpoint, ‘experimental’ arm), compared with the conventional method of measuring tumor shrinkage on radiological scans by the 'RECIST' criteria (‘control’ arm) at 3 or more months after starting chemotherapy. - Objective 1: This study has met its primary objective of showing that the novel dual-endpoint is a better predictor of progression-free survival (PFS) at a much earlier time-point (4-6 weeks after starting therapy) than the conventional RECIST method (10-12 weeks after starting therapy). - Objective 2 and 4: This study also met its secondary endpoints, in which the dual-endpoint was found to be an independent predictor of PFS than when either modality/ biomarker was analyzed alone. Various cut-off threshold values were investigated in this study, an ‘early PET response’ was best represented by a > 40% drop in the total sum of SUVmax values of all the target tumor lesions, and plasma EBV DNA half-life of < or = 10 days. - Objective 3, Only the dual-endpoint at 4-6 weeks was an independent predictor of the final RECIST-response on multivariate analysis. - Objective 5: The median EBV DNA half-life following chemotherapy is longer than that following radiotherapy.

471910.label: Major findings and research outcome
471910.value: (1) Mean age was 49.2 years (SD+/-9.5), 28 (56%) had metastatic NPC and 22 (44%) had locoregionally advanced NPC. Median plasma EBV DNA half-life during the first 6 weeks of chemotherapy was 9.3 days (range 2.6-322.1). The final objective response at 10-12 weeks after chemotherapy as assessed by CT scan and RECIST (version 1.1) was: 53.1% partial response, 40.8% stable disease. (2) Determination of optimal cut-off values: (a) plasma EBV DNA half-life: Historically, the half-life was 3.8 days after radiotherapy and 6.7 days after surgical resection of locally recurrent NPC. In this study, the plasma EBV DNA half-life values at or around the median of 9.3 days (< or = 8, 10 or 15 days) were evaluated and a cut-off of < or = 10 days was found to be the most optimal in a logistic regression. (b) For metabolic response, the EORTC criteria defined a >15% +/- 25% drop in the sum of SUVmax values of the targeted (cancerous) lesions as clinically meaningful (J Nucl Med 1999: 40;1771). In this study, the cut-off of > 40% drop in the sum of SUVmax value was found to be the most significant. (c) Definition of the 'dual-endpoint' is thus = A value of > 40% SUVmax drop and a EBV DNA half-life of < or =10 days at 4-6 weeks after starting chemotherapy. - Survival data: median follow-up for all patients was 18.2 months (95% C.I, 14.7-22.8m). Median overall survival (OS) for all patients was 25.6 months (95% C.I. 18.7-23.4 m). Median PFS was 12.3 months (95% C.I. 8.2-19.3 m). The primary dual-endpoint was associated with improved PFS with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.172, 95% CI = 0.054-0.542, p = 0.0027). Subjects who achieved this dual-endpoint had median PFS of 19.3 months (95% CI 10.3- not reached), versus 7.9 months (95% CI 7-15.5 months) in those who did not (logrank p < 0.004). None of the prognostic markers correlated with OS. - Correlation with RECIST response: The early dual-endpoint at 4-6 weeks was significantly correlated with RECIST response determined at 10-12 weeks after starting chemotherapy, odds ratio 38.85 (95% CI 4.29-351.98, p=0.0011). - Metastatic subgroup: The dual endpoint was an independent predictor of PFS (HR 0.203, 95% CI 0.062-0.659, p = 0.008). The median PFS for those who achieved this dual-endpoint was 12.4 month (95% CI 6.1-NR), versus 7 months (95% CI 5.3-7.9) in those who did not (logrank p = 0.0049).

471910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471910.value: This study showed that a new dual-endpoint predictor based on both metabolic and biomarker-based response criteria can predict both progression-free survival and subsequent RECIST response at a much earlier time-point during the course of chemotherapy in advanced NPC. Early Metabolic response, plasma EBV DNA half-life during the first 6 weeks of chemotherapy and RECIST response did not predict survival in this study. Validation in a larger subject sample is warranted. If validated, this biomarker has important implications on clinical practice and clinical trial design. This endpoint enables one to get an early indicator if a drug therapy is efficacious or not after just 1 cycle of treatment. This would minimize the chance of over-treating patients with futile therapy, and also provide an early ‘go and no-go’ signal for new drugs in clinical trial. The lack of reliance on detecting changes in tumor dimension makes this endpoint an attractive surrogate marker of survival in early phase clinical trial of targeted therapy, where the predominant mechanism of action is tumor stabilization and not shrinkage. PET scan and plasma EBV DNA are now readily available in developed countries, their results are reproducible and their costs have fallen significantly in recent years.

471910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471910.value: Nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC) is among the top ten most common cancers in Hong Kong and around 35% of patients present with advanced disease which need chemotherapy, which is associated with toxicities. The current method of assessing benefit from chemotherapy relies on the detection of tumor dimensional changes with radiological scans, which are generally performed at least 3 to 4 months after starting treatment. This study has shown that a new response indicator is able to predict progression-free survival and subsequent tumor shrinkage rate as early as 4 weeks after starting chemotherapy in patients with advanced NPC who were undergoing chemotherapy. This endpoint consists of measuring metabolic response using a PET scan, together with measuring blood levels of EBV DNA during the first 4-6 weeks of chemotherapy. These tests are routinely used in clinical practice, and this study has revealed a new way of applying these tests to better predict treatment outcome in patients undergoing chemotherapy in advanced NPC. This promising new predictive biomarker may have far-reaching implications on how doctors and researchers assess drug response in patients with NPC.

473310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473310.value: SR proteins are a family of RNA-binding proteins that play significant roles in constitutive splicing and serve as the key regulators of alternative splicing in mammalian cells. They also play broad roles in post-splicing processes including mRNA export, nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and mRNA translation. SR proteins are so named because of the presence of C-terminal RS domains, characterized by multiple copies of uninterrupted stretches of Ser-Arg (SR) dipeptides, that are essential modules for interacting with proteins and RNA during different stages of mRNA metabolism. The serines within the RS are extensively phosphorylated and their phosphorylation states govern their subcellular localization and activities. The SR protein kinases (SRPKs) have been shown to be one of the key kinase families that phosphorylate the RS domain of SR proteins. Although our previous works on the structural and kinetic studies of SRPK1 have elucidated the phosphorylation mechanism of ASF/SF2, a prototypical SR protein, by the kinase, the precise role of SRPKs in the regulation of SR proteins is still not clear. The link between human diseases and defects in pre-mRNA splicing is well established. Misregulation of splicing factors like the SR proteins can lead to many diseases including cancers. It is therefore essential to study the regulation of SR protein phosphorylation to gain a better understanding of their roles in splicing as well as other cellular functions. The primary focus of our proposal is to understand the molecular basis for substrate specificity and phosphorylation of two important SR proteins, ASF/SF2 and SRp20, by another member of SRPKs, SRPK2. The experiments proposed here will enable us to better understand the biological functions of SRPK2 in the regulation of SR proteins and help to define rules that govern SR protein interaction and phosphorylation by SRPKs. We hope these rules will help us to predict how other members in the family are phosphorylated by SRPKs. 473310.label: Realisation of objectives
473310.value: We have completed object 1 by elucidating the phosphorylation mechanism of SRSF1 (formerly ASF/SF2) by SRPK2. Pull-down assays revealed that a conserved docking groove in SRPK2 is critical for the binding of SRSF1. The equilibrium dissociate constant (Kd) of the interaction between SRPK2 and SRSF1 was measured to be 63 nM using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) spectroscopy. SRPK2 was determined to phosphorylate SRSF1 at ~10-12 sites. Using a start-trap assay, SRPK2 was shown to phosphorylate SRSF1 processively at ~ 6 sites instead of 8-9 sites as seen in the SRPK1 reaction. ATP-dependent phosphorylation mapping experiments demonstrated that SRSF1 was phosphorylated by SRPK2 in a C-terminal to N-terminal direction. Together, our findings suggest that SRPK2 and SRPK1 phosphorylate SRSF1 in similar manner except that SRPK2 is less processive. We have completed objective 2 by studying the molecular mechanisms of SRSF3 (formerly SRp20) recognition and phosphorylation by SRPK2, and the role of their interaction in SRSF3 subcellular localization. SPR analysis revealed that SRSF3 bound SRPK2 with high affinity (Kd = 60 nM). Pull down assays showed that SRPK2 also bound to SRSF3 via its docking groove. While RRM of SRSF3 alone did not bind SRPK2, residues between 106 and 118 of SRSF3 were critical for the interaction with SRPK2. Retention of residues 119 to 128 further enhanced the binding to the same extent as the full length SRSF3. SRPK2 was shown to phosphorylate SRSF3 at nearly 13 sites in a N-to-C direction and about 5 sites are processed in a processive manner. However, attempt to map the phosphorylation sites by MALDI-TOF failed despite multiple proteases have been tried to prepare the samples. One possible explanation is that the amount of arginine within the SRSF3 RS domain is too extensive and the fragments generated are not suitable for MALDI-TOF analysis. Our immunofluorescence studies showed that residues C-terminal to 118 were important for SRSF3 nuclear localization, suggesting that the C-terminal RS domain functions as nuclear localization signal. On the other hand, mutation of all serines C-terminal to residue 118 to alanines did not affect nuclear localization of SRSF3, indicating that phosphorylation of the RS domain may not be required. We have successfully obtained crystals of an active fragment of SRPK2 in complex with a fragment of SRSF1. However, while the crystals clearly showed diffraction, they were highly mosaic. As a result the crystal failed to be indexed to any Bravais lattice. Optimization of the crystals is underway.

473310.label: Major findings and research outcome
473310.value: Serine arginine (SR) proteins are classified into two subclasses based on the presence of one or two RNA recognition motif(s) (RRM(s)). In this study, we have unveiled that SRPK2 utilizes different mechanisms to phosphorylate SRSF3 and SRSF1, which have one and two RRM(s) respectively. One hallmark characteristic of SRPK1 is its ability to phosphorylate SRSF1 in a highly efficient and sequential manner. Here we showed that SRPK2 binds and phosphorylates SRSF1 in a docking groove-dependent manner like SRPK1. However, in contrast to the 8-9 sites seen with SRPK1, SRSF1 was processively phosphorylated at ~6 sites by SRPK2 under similar experimental conditions. This suggests that the molecular mechanism of processive phosphorylation may be different between the two kinases. Some of these findings were published on the peer-reviewed journal Biochemical Journal. We next investigated the recognition and phosphorylation mechanisms of SRSF3 by SRPK2. Our studies showed that SRPK2 utilizes the same conserved docking groove to bind and regulate SRSF3 phosphorylation. We also demonstrated that the region between residues 106 and 118 of SRSF3 is important for interaction with SRPK2. However, since this region contains mostly arginines, it is unclear if it serves as the only docking motif that interacts with the kinase docking groove or other region(s) within the RS domain can also serve the same purpose. Interestingly, we discovered that nearly the entire RS domain of SRSF3 (~13 sites) was phosphorylated by SRPK2 in an N-terminal to C-terminal manner and only 5 sites sites were processed processively. This is different from SRSF1 where the phosphorylation is limited to the N-terminal RS domain and happens in a C-to-N direction. Taken together, our data provides strong evidence that SRPK2 phosphorylates SRSF1 and SRSF3 by distinct mechanisms. Immunofluorescence studies using different truncation constructs of SRSF3 revealed that the RS domain C-terminal to residue 118 is important for SRSF3 nuclear localization, suggesting that the C-terminal region functions as nuclear localization signal. However, when the serines within this C-terminal RS region were mutated to alanines, SRSF3 nuclear localization was not affected. This indicates that, unlike SRSF1, SRSF3 nuclear localization may not depend on RS domain phosphorylation. These findings suggest that the regulatory mechanisms of SRSF1 and SRSF3 subcellular localization are different and may involve post-translational modifications other than phosphorylation.

473310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
473310.value: There are growing evidence that SRPK2 and SRPK1 have distinct biological functions during splicing and other biological processes. The lower processivity of SRPK2 may result in phosphorylated SR proteins that are functionally distinguishable from those produced by SRPK1 and therefore differentiate their functions in vivo. Thus the difference in the processivity of the SRPKs requires further investigation. Recent studies have shown that, in addition to phosphorylation, post-translational modifications like arginine methylation also play a role in the regulation of SR protein subcellular localization. Our studies showed that the nuclear localization of SRSF3 might not depend on RS domain phosphorylation. It is therefore reasonable to speculate that arginine methylation may be important for the regulation of SRSF3. This should be investigated in the future. Finally, we have now obtained complex crystals of SRPK2 and SRSF1. Optimization of the crystallization condition will be performed by varying pH, precipitant concentration, temperature, and addition of different additives. We will also perform various post-crystallization treatments including but not limited to: 1) freezing with different cryoprotectants; 2) annealing; 3) dehydration; 4) soaking with heavy atoms; and 5) crosslinking. This crystal structure will help to understand the difference between the processivity of SRPK1 and SRPK2.

473310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473310.value: This project aimed to study how SRPK2, a protein enzyme involved in pre-mRNA processing, recognizes and modifies its substrates SRSF1 and SRSF3. In brief, this study has successfully identified the determinants on the enzyme and substrates that are important for their interactions and subsequently the modification reactions. We also showed that while the enzyme binds different substrates using similar mechanism, the regulations of the modification processes are very different. These findings can help scientists to better understand the regulation mechanism of gene expression in general. Since the enzyme and substrates being studied play important roles in gene expression and have been found to be misregulated in many diseases including cancers and viral infections, the information obtained in this study may also help scientists to understand the causes of various diseases and aid the development of therapeutic agents that target these proteins.

473410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473410.value: In this application, we aim to characterize the HTRA1 gene in the development of age-related macular degeneration (AMD), which is a leading cause of irreversible visual impairment and blindness in people aged more than 65 years in developed countries, affecting about 50 million people worldwide. Its occurrence is pan-ethnic and its etiology multi-factorial with strong genetic susceptibility. Other major risk factors include age and cigarette smoking. Recently, using the genome-wide association study, we identified an AMD-associated gene, High Temperature Requirement factor A1 (HTRA1). HTRA1 encodes a serine protease. In subsequent studies we found HTRA1 SNPs rs10490924 and rs11200638 both conferred more than 10 times risk to develop AMD. Reported studies of other research groups have established the association of HTRA1 SNPs with exudative AMD in different ethnic populations. An independent study has shown elevated HTRA1 expressions of HtrA1 mRNA and protein had been shown in lymphocytes and retinal pigment epithelium of AMD patients. While the biological roles of the HtrA1 protein in the development of AMD are still under investigation, we propose that HTRA1 is directly linked to AMD pathogenesis. In this proposal, we shall first investigate the HtrA1 protein expression with AMD-associated proteins, CFH, VEGF and PEDF, in vitreous humors of AMD patients and controls. Secondly, we shall carry out two-dimensional proteomics and mass spectrometry analysis to identify HtrA1 molecular substrate targets within the vitreous humor of mice given intravitreal and subretinal injection of recombinant HtrA1. Thirdly, the interactive effect and contribution to AMD by HtrA1, VEGF and identified substrate targets will further be manipulated in the in vitro ocular cell culture system. Results from this study would establish the association of HtrA1 expression in vitreous humor with the disease status of AMD and identify HtrA1 molecular substrate targets in the eye. Valuable information will be provided on the biological effects of HtrA1 and how it affects the development of AMD. Such new knowledge will contribute to advancing the understanding of AMD pathogenesis and provide information for future design of therapeutic treatment. 本研究的目的在於確定HTRA1基因在年齡相關性黃斑變性（age-related macular degeneration, AMD）發展過程中的特徵。在發達國家65歲以上的人群中，年齡 相關性黃斑變性是導致不可逆性視力損傷和失明的一個主要原因。全世界約有5 千萬人患有年齡相關性黃斑變性。該疾病存在於各類種族人種，其發病原因為多 因素性，伴有較強的遺傳易感性。其他的主要危險因素包括年齡和吸煙史。近來， 運用全基因組關聯分析研究，我們發現了一個AMD相關性基因——高溫需要因 子A1基因(High Temperature Requirement factor A1, HTRA1)。HTRA1基因編碼絲 氨酸蛋白酶。在隨後的研究中我們發現攜帶有HTRA1基因單核苷酸多態性 rs11200638的患者比未攜帶此單核苷酸多態性的患者發生AMD的危險性高10 倍。其他科研小組已經報導的研究明確了HTRA1基因單核苷酸多態性與滲出性 AMD在不同種族人群中均有相關性。一個獨立研究發現在AMD患者的淋巴細 胞和視網膜色素上皮中HTRA1基因mRNA和蛋白的表達增加。雖然HtrA1蛋白 在AMD發病過程中的生物學作用仍在研究中，我們認為HTRA1與AMD的發 病機理直接相連。在這個提案中，我們將首先研究AMD患者和正常對照人群的 玻璃體液中HtrA1蛋白表達和AMD相關蛋白，如CFH,VEGF和PEDF。其次， 我們將於小鼠玻璃體腔或視網膜下注射重組HtrA1, 再運用二維蛋白組學和質譜 分析法確定小鼠玻璃體液中HtrA1的分子底物目標。再次，我們將通過體外眼部 細胞培養系統進一步研究HtrA1，VEGF和測定的底物目標間的相互作用和它們 在AMD發病中的作用。該研究的結果將明確玻璃體液中HtrA1表達與AMD疾 病的相關性，並確定眼部HtrA1的分子底物目標。該研究將對HtrA1生物作用 及其如何影響AMD疾病發生提供有價值的資訊。這些新的知識將有助於增進我 們對AMD發病機理的理解並且為未來設計治療方案提供資訊。

473410.label: Realisation of objectives
473410.value: Objective 1: We recruited 55 unrelated Han Chinese patients who underwent ocular surgeries and collected the vitreous humor samples from these patients. Unfortunately, no AMD patient can be recruited since only very few AMD patients need surgery. Instead, the condition of these patients includes vitreous hemorrhage, diabetic retinopathy, central retinal vein occlusion, retinal detachment, epiretinal membrane, macular hole, and intraocular lens reoperation. Still, we revealed that HTRA1 level is positively correlated with VEGF level, but not PEDF level. Vitreous level of HTRA1 is also associated with retinal detachment, which could be an inflammatory condition. Objective 2: Based on the positive association of HTRA1 and VEGF in vitreous humor samples, we speculated that VEGF could interact with HTRA1. Therefore, we induced stress in retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells by tunicamycin and dithiothreitol, and we observed that both HTRA1 and VEGFA are upregulated under stress conditions. When they are overexpressed in RPE cells, their expressions did not change, suggesting that HTRA1 and VEGF do not mutually regulate each other. Moreover, since retinal degeneration is a complex inflammatory condition involving multiple interactive factors, we investigated the genetic interaction of HTRA1 with other AMD-associated genes. We revealed a joint additive effect between HTRA1 gene and other AMD-associated genes, including the inflammatory genes such as the complement factor H (CFH) gene. Although we might not be able to identify the direct molecular substrate of HTRA1 in the eye, we still identified the molecular interactive partners of HTRA1. This also helps us to formulate the pathological mechanism of HTRA1 in AMD development. Objective 3: When we overexpressed HTRA1 in RPE cells, we found that HTRA1 would reduce RPE cell viability, increase cell apoptosis and enhance the responsiveness to anoikis. In addition, we identified a protective HTRA1 variant predominantly presented in control subjects. When this HTRA1 variant is expressed in RPE cells, the cell apoptosis and responsiveness to anoikis are reduced, whereas cell viability is restored. These re-confirm the role of HTRA1 in RPE cell death. From these discoveries, we proposed that oxidative stress and inflammation, the pathological initiators of AMD, could activate HTRA1 and increase expression of HTRA1, in turn induce RPE cell death. Based on this mechanism, we speculated that MG-132, which downregulates HTRA1, could reduce and rescue RPE cell death. Such kinds of treatments would be potential novel therapies for AMD in future.

473410.label: Major findings and research outcome
473410.value: Research outcome from this project can be divided into 2 parts: First area of research findings was generated from the genetic association studies in age-related macular degeneration (AMD). We confirmed the association of the HTRA1 gene with AMD. This association is not only stronger than that in polypoidal choroidal neovascularization (PCV; Liang et al., 2012), but also differentiate these 2 choroidal neovascular diseases by a promoter polymorphism (Liang et al., manuscript in preparation). This would definitely aid the clinical diagnosis of AMD and PCV so as to facilitate the treatments. Moreover, joint additive effect was found between HTRA1 gene and other AMD-associated genes, such as SKIV2L (Liu et al., 2013), ABCA1 (Liu et al., 2014), FPR1 (Liang et al., 2014) and SERPING1 genes (Liu et al., manuscript in preparation). This lays down the foundation for second phase of the research study. Second area of the research findings was come from the molecular biology study. From the vitreous humor collected from the patients with retinal diseases, we revealed that vitreous HTRA1 level is positively correlated with VEGF level, but not PEDF level (Ng et al., 2011). Vitreous level of HTRA1 is also associated with retinal detachment, which could be an inflammatory condition. Upon stress induction, both HTRA1 and VEGFA are upregulated although they do not mutually regulate each other. When HTRA1 is overexpressed in retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells, HTRA1 would reduce RPE cell viability, increase cell apoptosis and enhance the responsiveness to anoikis (Ng et al., manuscript in preparation). In addition, we identified an HTRA1 variant, which has higher frequency in control subjects, indicating that it is a protective variant. When this HTRA1 variant is expressed in RPE cells, the cell apoptosis and responsiveness to anoikis are reduced, whereas cell viability is restored (Ng et al., manuscript in preparation). From functional point of view, these experiments again confirm the protective role of this HTRA1 variant. From these biological discoveries, we proposed that oxidative stress and inflammation, the pathological initiators of AMD, could activate HTRA1 and increase expression of HTRA1, in turn induce RPE cell death (Ng et al., 2013). Based on this mechanism, we speculated that MG-132, which downregulates HTRA1 (Ng et al., 2011), could reduce and rescue RPE cell death (Ng et al., manuscript in preparation). These kinds of treatments are potential novel therapies for AMD.

473410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
473410.value: In this project, we achieved 2 major discoveries. First, we identified and validated the genetic association of HTRA1 gene with AMD. Moreover, joint additive effect was found between HTRA1 gene and other AMD-associated genes, including inflammation genes. This not only provides the foundation for second discovery, but also enables the establishment of molecular diagnosis for AMD to enhance clinical diagnosis (compared to PCV) as well as early monitor and treatment. Second, we revealed that HTRA1 can reduce RPE cell viability, increase RPE apoptosis and enhance the responsiveness to anoikis. In addition, we found that HTRA1 is related to oxidative stress and inflammation. Its expression is highly correlated with the expression of VEGF. From these discoveries, we proposed that oxidative stress and inflammation, the pathological initiators of AMD, activate HTRA1 and increase expression of HTRA1, in turn induce RPE cell death. Based on this mechanism, we postulate that HTRA1 inhibitors, antioxidants and anti-inflammatory agents should reduce the activity of HTRA1, so that RPE cell death could be reduced and rescued. These treatments are potential novel therapies for AMD. Therefore, further studies will focus on the therapeutic modalities rescuing RPE cells by targeting oxidative stress and the HTRA1 pathway.

473410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473410.value: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of severe visual impairment and irreversible blindness in most developed countries, affecting more than 50 million elderly people worldwide. Current treatments, such as intravitreal injection of anti-angiogenic agents, mitigate the effect of advanced AMD, but cannot completely cure the disease. Comprehensive understanding of the AMD pathological mechanisms is important for the development of new therapies. In this research project, we identified the genetic interaction of high temperature requirement factor A1 (HTRA1) gene with other AMD-associated genes. This is the basic foundation for the development of molecular diagnosis for AMD to enhance clinical diagnosis as well as early disease monitor and treatment. Moreover, we also discovered that HTRA1 protein is correlated with another critical AMD-associated protein, VEGF. Their expressions could be related to the oxidative stress and inflammation, the pathological initiators of AMD. In addition, we testified that HTRA1 would cause retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cell death, the causal factor for the development of AMD. Our findings revealed the molecular mechanisms of HTRA1 in the development of AMD. This would promote in-depth research and development of novel therapies for AMD in future.

473710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473710.value: Steroid-associated osteonecrosis (ON) is associated with impaired blood supply in bone and subsequent bone death. Frequent use of steroids is known to associate with ON development. ON occurs mostly in large joints such as hip that results in joint collapse and joint replacement. Core decompression, a surgical technique to remove dead bone and fill with bone substitute, is one of the surgical treatments for preventing joint collapse in early ON stages when the size of dead bone is small. Bone grafts from the same patient are frequently used for core decompression. However, in patients under steroid treatment, bone-forming capability of their marrow-stem-cells (MSCs) is inhibited and MSCs tend to differentiate into fat cells. The treatment strategy is to promote bone forming ability of the MSCs and provide scaffoldings for structural reinforcement of the empathy space in core decompression. The investigators of this proposal have identified a novel and alternative bone forming promotion factor Icaritin derived from herbal Epimedium flavonoids. Our previous findings and those accumulated from our last year’s ‘Fundable but not Funded’ GRF application suggest that Icaritin has estrogenic function and is able to enhance MSCs proliferation and promote bone formation. We also show that Icaritin is able to enhance osteoporotic fracture repair in the ovariectomized mice. One of the co-investigators of our multidisciplinary team with background in material sciences has developed rapid-prototyping technology to produce porous scaffold materials for orthopaedic applications. We have been collaborating for the past years to produce a special porous scaffold material for bone defect repair. Now we have successfully produced a novel composite scaffold material incorporating bone-formation-promoting Icaritin that has been proven to be slow-releasable in vitro after our last year’s submission. The aim of this study is to investigate if the porous composite scaffold incorporating slow-release Icaritin is able to promote bone formation by facilitating proliferation and osteogenic differentiation of host bone MSCs for its better integration with host bone after core decompression using an established steroid-associated ON rabbits model. The findings of this translational research will be able to develop a novel bone-forming promotion composite porous scaffold for potential clinical application for ON management. 473710.label: Realisation of objectives
473710.value: As described in 5.1. we have following two main study objectives as sated above from the original proposal 1 in vitro, to investigate kinetics of Icaritin, i.e. the slow-release patterns of Icaritin from PLGA/TCP/Icaritin composite porous scaffold and its osteopromotive potential for MSCs. 2 in vivo, to evaluate its osteopromotive effect of the composite porous scaffold after core decompression using an established steroid-associated ON model in rabbits. For in vitro part: 1) Fabrication of bioactive PLGA/TCP/icaritin composite scaffold: we used an novel low-temperature 3D rapid prototyping machine for fabrication that was available in our collaborator Prof. Wang’s Department, i.e. Dept. of Materials Science and Engineering of Tsinghua University in Beijing. 2) Testing kinetics of Icaritin, i.e. the slow-release patterns of Icaritin from PLGA/TCP/Icaritin composite porous scaffold: we then immersed the composite scaffold into the physiological saline. The concentration of icaritin released into the saline was measured using high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) at each week using our established protocol. 3) Osteopromotive and anti-adipogenic potential: we tested bioactive PLGA/TCP/icaritin composite scaffold in vitro together with bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and its anti-adipogenic potential using cell culture model with adipocytes. For in vivo part: The PLGA/TCP/icaritin composite material were prepared in a block form and implanted into the muscles of rabbit using a published protocol for testing its potential of osteoinduction and angiogenic effects. SAON model at distal femoral in rabbits was established to test it osteopromotive effects after core-decompression for microCT, histological observation, and mechanical testing. For radiographic and microCT in vivo monitoring, we evaluated new bone formation integration; for histological studies, emphasis was put on local angiography and neovascularization and coupling of new bone formation and scaffold degradation with implantation over time.

473710.label: Major findings and research outcome
473710.value: Our major findings are categorized according to our two study objectives, namely 1 in vitro, to investigate kinetics of Icaritin, i.e. the slow-release patterns of Icaritin from PLGA/TCP/Icaritin composite porous scaffold and its osteopromotive potential for MSCs. As we proposed, our in vitro findings confirmed our pilot studies that formed the basis for our in vitro studies: The major findings are published in leading biomaterial and biomedical journals, including 1) We demonstrated structural and degradation characteristics of our innovative porous PLGA/TCP scaffold incorporated with bioactive molecular icaritin (Xie XH et al. Biomed Mater, 2010 – Appendix I – Paper 1), and 2) The underlying mechanisms on Icaritin, an exogenous phytomolecule, that was able to enhance osteogenesis but not angiogenesis (Yao D et al. PlosOne, 2012 – Appendix I – Paper 3; Appendix II-Conference 2 & 3; Yao D PhD thesis, 2012- Appendix III-Student 2). 2 in vivo, to evaluate its osteopromotive effect of the composite porous scaffold after core decompression using an established steroid-associated ON model in rabbits. Our in vivo efficacy studies were conducted based on our established steroid-associated osteonecrosis (SAON) model in rabbits. The major findings are published in leading orthopaedic journals, including 1) Impaired bone healing in rabbits with SAON that required biological enhancement for bone defect healing after core-decompression (Xie XH, et al. J Bone Joint Surg Br, 2011 – Appendix I – Paper 2); 2) Exogenous phytoestrogenic molecule Icaritin incorporated into a porous scaffold was able to enhance bone defect repair after core-decompression (Wang XL et al. J Orthop Res, 2013 – Appendix I – Paper 4; Appendix II-Conference 1; Xie XH – PhD thesis: Appendix III-Student 1). 473710.value: In order to translate our preclinical study findings into clinically applicable products we need to build up translational R&D platform with installation of hardware, i.e. low temperature 3-D spinning or rapid prototyping machines and GMP facilities to produce our novel scaffold material for clinical applications. In order to realize this goal, Prof. Ling QIN, PI of this project has been appointed as Director of Translational Medicine R&D Center in Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology under Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), a joint unit formed by CAS and CUHK with installation and rapid prototyping machine for producing our designed bioactive scaffold materials (www.siat.cas.cn).

473710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473710.value: The investigators of this proposal identified a novel bone forming factor Icaritin from herb Epimedium. Our previous research showed that Icaritin was able to induce bone marrow stem cells differentiation into bone forming cells. One of the co-investigators with background in material sciences and engineering had developed low-temperature 3D rapid-prototyping technology to produce bone scaffold materials for orthopaedic applications and we together successfully produced a composite scaffold material with potential bone-formation-promoting Icaritin. Our current project successfully confirmed the Icaritin incorporating porous composite scaffold was osteoprmotive as icaritin could be slowly released from the scaffold matrix to induce bone formation and facilitating osteogenic differentiation of host bone marrow stem cells for better integration with host bone after core decompression surgery using an established steroid-associated osteonecrosis rabbit model. Our findings generated from this preclinical research developed a novel bone-forming composite scaffold implant for potential clinical application for osteonecrosis management, a bone metabolic disorders affecting significant number of populations. From both the patients and healthcare perspective, this may preserve the affected joint without replacement surgery and significant reduction of the financial burden to both society and patients.

473810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473810.value: Laboratory confirmed cases of influenza virus in Hong Kong and the USA indicated that about 20% of the infection is due to influenza B virus. This virus also results in morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly in young patients. It is therefore essential to gain more knowledge on this important virus and to compare it to flu A virus, for combating both of them. Nucleoprotein (NP) is the major component of the ribonucleoprotein complex, which mediates the transcription and replication of the flu B genome. In this proposal, we aim at solving the crystal structure of flu B NP and studying the structure-function relationship of this protein, with emphasis on regions that are substantially different from the flu A NP. The proposed studies include: (1) To improve the existing flu B NP crystals for diffracting to high resolution and attempt to crystallize the flu B NP-RNA complex, (2) to find if the extended N-terminal region takes part in oligomerization and the role of selected amino acids in the putative tail loop regions for oligomerization, (3) to find the nuclear localization signals, (4) to characterize the RNA binding property, with emphasis on an RNA binding loop and a selected basic cluster. Through this study, we shall understand the structure of flu B NP, the elements for flu B NP to form oligomers, bind RNA and migrate from the cytoplasm to nucleus. These data in comparison to those of fluA NP will enhance our understanding of this class of proteins and lay the foundation for the design of inhibitors for interfering with both influenza A and B viruses. 473810.value: Objectives 1-3 have been realised. (1) We have elucidated the underlying mechanism of flu B NP homo-oligomerization, clarifying the role of the tail-loop region and the N-terminus. 473810.label: Major findings and research outcome
473810.value: 1. The atomic structure of flu B NP has been determined by x-ray crystallography to a resolution of 3.2 Å. It contains a head, a body domain and a tail loop. Flu B NP forms a crystallographic homo-tetramer by inserting the tail loop into the body domain of the neighboring NP molecule. 2. The role of the tail loop region in the homo-oligomerization of flu B NP has been elucidated by site-directed mutagenesis, luciferase reporter assay and static light scattering. A deeply buried salt bridge R472-E395 and a hydrophobic cluster at F468 were found to be the major driving forces for the process. 3. The essential regions of flu B NP for binding RNA have been identified by site-directed mutagenesis, luciferase reporter assay and surface plasmon resonance assay. The electropositive groove between the head and body domains of influenza B NP was found to be crucial for RNA binding. This groove also contains an extended flexible charged loop (aa. 125-149) and two lysine clusters at the first half of this loop were shown to be crucial for binding RNA. The work of 1-3 are published in Ng et al. (J. Virol. 2012, 86(12):6758). 4. Two nuclear localization signals (NLSs) (aa. 44-47 and aa. 260-274) have been determined by silico prediction, systematic deletion and mutation and fluorescence microscopy analysis. The two NLSs have been proved to be important to the transcription and replication of RNP activities by luciferase reporter assay. 5. The role of the extended N-terminus in the homo-oligomerization of flu B NP has been elucidated by serial truncation, luciferase reporter assay, static light scattering and electron microscopy. This region has been found to help the monomeric flu B NP to associate into higher oligomers in the presence of RNA. It has also been shown to participate in maintaining higher oligomers of flu B NP when RNA is cleaved. These characteristics contribute in the formation and stabilization of RNP structure. The work of 4-5 are being prepared for publication.

473810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
473810.value: We have solved the crystallographic structure of flu B NP. It contains a head, a body domain and a tail loop. It uses the tail loop to insert into the body domain of the neighboring NP molecule to form a homo-tetramer, and an extended flexible charged loop and two lysine clusters in the electropositive groove between the head and body domains. Based on this finding, the X-ray structure of mutants that are defective to form oligomers or to bind RNAs shall be attempted. It will be interesting to compare the monomeric structure of flu B NP and, the RNA binding defective variant with that of the wild-type flu B NP. We have set up the collaboration with Professor Wendy Barclay in Virology Center of Imperial College, UK to generate recombinant viruses carrying truncated N-terminus of NP. It will further show the role of the extended N-terminus in viral life cycle. We have discovered two NLSs in the flu B NP. Follow-up studies will be carried out to screen its interaction with karyopherins (e.g. Importin α, Importin β). Preliminary data have showed that flu B NP interacts with importin α4.

473810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473810.value: Influenza B nucleoprotein (flu B NP) is a major component of the ribonucleoprotein complex (RNP), which plays a vital role in the transcription and replication of the viral genome. We are the first to solve the crystal structure of the flu B NP. We have also found Flu B NP forms homo-oligomer by inserting the tail loop into the body domain of the neighboring NP molecule. We have also shown that an electropositive groove between the head and body domains of influenza B NP is crucial for RNA binding and the extended N-terminal region in Flu B NP plays a role in the formation of homo-oligomers. Flu B NP contains some nuclear localization signals to be transported into the cell nucleus. We have found two NLSs in the sequence of flu B NP and elucidated that they play an important role to the transcription and replication of viral genomes.
