474710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
474710.value: Aberrant epigenetic silencing of various cancer genes including signaling tumor suppressor genes (TSG) by promoter CpG methylation disrupts normal cell signaling, playing a central and critical role in multiple carcinogenesis. Characterizing the epigenome of a tumor, such as the CpG methylation profile of the whole cancer genome, is important for the understanding of its molecular pathogenesis and also the development of biomarkers for cancer molecular diagnosis. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is one of the leading cancers in Hong Kong, and strongly associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). As EBV induces cancer gene methylation in tumor cells, aberrant CpG methylation is assumed to contribute significantly to NPC pathogenesis. Previous work from our Lab and others also showed that NPC generally has more frequent TSG methylation than other carcinomas. Thus, we intend to characterize the NPC methylation epigenome, and identify genome-wide aberrantly methylated cancer genes for this tumor. We will further characterize some identified genes for their epigenetic abnormalities and functions in NPC as well as their potential usage as epigenetic biomarkers. Specifically, by selecting a novel epigenetic master gene CHD5 (chromodomain helicase DNA-binding 5) - an SNF2 protein containing PHD, chromodomains, SNF2-like ATPase/helicase and DNA binding domains critically involved in chromatin remodeling, we will study the functions of epigenetic modifiers in tumor suppression, nuclear/epigenetic signaling and gene regulation. Although frequent deletion/downregulation of CHD5 has been reported in multiple tumors and the mouse Chd5 was recently identified as a tumor suppressor modulating ARF-p53 signaling, its functions in tumorigenesis is not well studied as there is even no full-length human CHD5 cDNA cloned so far. To gain more insight into the molecular functions of CHD5 and related mechanisms, we will study its expression and promoter methylation, its transcriptional modulator function, its impact on NPC cell growth, apoptosis and cell cycle distribution. We will also identify CHD5 target genes through expression profiling, and finally its binding/regulatory complex through immuno-affinity purification and mass spectrometry. 啟動子CpG甲基化介導的抑癌基因表觀遺傳沉默異常可導致細胞信號通路的紊亂，在腫瘤發生發展中發揮著重要的作用。鑒定腫瘤的表觀遺傳組學，如腫瘤全基因組的CpG甲基化圖譜，對我們理解腫瘤發生發展的分子機理和腫瘤早期診斷分子標誌物具有重要的意義。 鼻咽癌是香港常見的腫瘤，與EB病毒的感染密切相關。EB病毒可誘導腫瘤細胞中抑癌基因的甲基化水平異常，由此可見CpG甲基化異常在鼻咽癌變過程中具有重要的作用。我們和其他研究小組前期研究工作表明，與其他腫瘤相比，鼻咽癌通常具有更高頻率的抑癌基因甲基化異常。因此，本項目以期繪製鼻咽癌的表觀遺傳組學圖譜，在基因組範圍內鑒定鼻咽癌特異的甲基化異常基因，同時進一步對已證實的基因進行深入的功能和機制研究，期望發展表觀遺傳分子診斷標誌物。 進一步，我們將以研究小組前期鑒定的表觀遺傳調控基因 - 染色質解旋酶DNA結合蛋白5（chromodomain helicase DNA-binding 5，CHD5）為代表，研究表觀遺傳修飾基因在腫瘤抑制、核/表觀遺傳信號介導和基因調控中的功能。CHD5含有SNF2蛋白結合PHD結構域、染色質結構域、SNF2樣ATP/解旋酶結構域和DNA結合結構域，從而參與染色質重塑。雖然在多種腫瘤中存在CHD5的高頻缺失或下調，且研究表明小鼠Chd5基因作為抑癌基因參與ARF-p53信號通路，但CHD5在人腫瘤發生發展中的作用仍未有報導，特別是全長人源性的CHD5 cDNA至今未被克隆。因此，本項目將以鼻咽癌為模型，研究CHD5的表達、啟動子甲基化，轉錄調節功能；以及對鼻咽癌細胞生長、凋亡和細胞週期分佈的影響；通過表達譜的篩查進一步鑒定CHD5的靶基因，以及通過免疫親和純化發現CHD5的結合蛋白，從而深入瞭解CHD5在鼻咽癌變過程中的生物學功能和分子機制，及其作為腫瘤早期診斷標誌物的潛能。

474710.label: Realisation of objectives
474710.value: In this project, we profiled the whole-genome CpG methylation profiles (methylomes) of NPC cell lines, normal nasopharyngeal epithelial cell lines and primary tumors, using methylated DNA immunoprecipitation (MeDIP-chip). We observed extensive, genome-wide methylation of cellular genes in NPC, with methylation of some selected genes validated. Moreover, epigenetic disruption of key cell signaling pathways (Wnt signaling, MAPK signaling, Hedgehog signaling, TGF-beta signaling and ErbB signaling etc.) were further detected through bioinformatics analysis. We found 1,216 hypermethylated genes with promoter CGIs in NPC cell lines and 2,412 hypermethylated genes with promoter CGIs in NPC tumors. We further validated and characterized several methylated gene discovered, including CHD5 and some cell signaling regulation genes (ROR2, etc). We also studied the disruption of Wnt signaling pathway by methylation of cancer genes in NPC cells. We found that the NPC methylome shows a high CpG methylation epigenotype, indicating a critical role of epigenetic abnormalities in NPC pathogenesis. The methylation of some candidate TSGs identified by this methylome study was found to be potential biomarkers for future NPC diagnosis. In more depth for CHD5, we studied its expression and promoter methylation in NPC as well as other carcinomas, and characterized its tumor suppressive functions and related mechanisms in carcinoma cells. We found that CHD5 is broadly expressed in normal tissues, but frequently silenced or downregulated by promoter methylation in NPC and other carcinoma cell lines. Aberrant CHD5 promoter methylation was also frequently observed in primary NPC tumor samples.CHD5 expression could be restored in methylated and silenced carcinoma cell lines after treated with demethylation reagent Aza. Ectopic CHD5 expression significantly inhibited the clonogenicity, migration and invasion of NPC and other tumor cells. Moreover, we found that CHD5 as a chromatin remodeling factor could downregulate multiple oncogenes (EZH2, etc.), hypoxia-inducible factors (HIF2A etc.), as well as epithelial-mesenchymal transition and stem cell markers (FN1, OCT4, etc.). ChIP assay further confirmed that CHD5 binds to the promoter regions of its target genes. Thus, CHD5 silencing by promoter methylation is a frequent and common event in multiple tumorigenesis. We have reported these findings in international conferences (see below), and the final manuscript is currently in final preparation. All the proposed objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. The results obtained directly from this project have been described in our publications/conference abstracts/manuscripts listed below. Overall, the findings from this project have provided significant molecular understanding on the epigenetic etiology of NPC.

474710.value: Major finding: This study established the detailed genome-wide CpG methylation profiles (epigenomes) of NPC cell lines, primary tumors and normal nasopharyngeal epithelial cell lines as controls, through methyl-CpG DNA immunoprecipitation (MeDIP-chip). 474710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
474710.value: The present work provides us with a detailed in-depth profiling of the methylomes of NPC cell lines and primary tumors. A series of tumor-specific methylated novel genes implicated in the regulation of key signaling pathways have been discovered in NPC. A series of methylated genes with unknown function and mechanisms were newly identified in NPC in this study, which needs further investigations in future. In future, we could extend the work to elucidate the function and mechanisms of more epigenetically-silenced tumor suppressor genes in NPC, and further develop epigenetic biomarkers for NPC detection.

474710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
474710.value: NPC is a leading cancer threat for youth in Hong Kong. As EBV induces cancer gene methylation in tumor cells, aberrant CpG methylation is assumed to contribute significantly to NPC pathogenesis. Previous work from our Lab and others showed that NPC generally has more frequent TSG methylation than other carcinomas, but with no genome-wide DNA methylation of NPC established yet. CHD5 is a methylated novel master gene/epigenetic modifier, with very few studies of its functions in nuclear/epigenetic regulation performed. In this study, we profiled the NPC epigenome, and a series of novel methylated cancer genes were found, which could be potential epigenetic biomarkers for NPC. We also characterized the functions of CHD5 in epigenetic signaling/regulation and tumor suppression. The study provides deep molecular insight into the epigenetic etiology of NPC pathogenesis.

475210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
475210.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is one of the most common carcinomas in Hong Kong. Radiotherapy treatment, although effective in controlling tumour growth, results in swallowing disorder, or dysphagia. As a result, NPC patients suffer from aspiration, meaning food or fluids are misdirected into the airway on oral feeding. The aspirated materials often lead to devastating consequences of chest infections, dehydration and malnutrition. The management of these complications imply spiralling costs to the healthcare system. One way to reduce the burden to the healthcare system is to minimise aspiration with swallowing rehabilitation. Existing swallowing rehabilitation adopted for the NPC patients include traditional swallowing therapy and transcutaneous electrical stimulation. Regrettably, both rehabilitation approaches are not evidence-based for the NPC patients. Without efficacy studies in this unique NPC population, it is impossible to justify all the resources and efforts involved with existing swallowing rehabilitation approaches. Instead of reducing cost to the healthcare system, practising without evidence could mean imposing unnecessary additional cost, on the contrary. The aim of this study is to pioneer an evidence-based NPC swallowing rehabilitation approach. We propose to carry out a single-blinded randomised-controlled trial of swallowing rehabilitation efficacy on dysphagic NPC patients post radiotherapy. In this study, 160 subjects will be randomised into two treatment groups: 1) transcutaneous electrical stimulation and 2) traditional rehabilitation. Immediate and sustained outcomes will be compared using the 1) 8-point Penetration-Aspiration Scale as observed on Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing, 2) a NPC specific quality-of-life questionnaire FACT-NP and 3) Self-rated swallowing score. Results from this study will be the first-ever NPC swallowing rehabilitation evidence in the world. The impact on clinical practice as well as on research contribution is exponential. Clinically, it helps clinicians to make decisions on appropriate treatment approach to NPC patients. The choice of NPC swallowing rehabilitation approach would no longer be dependent upon random preference of individual clinician or patient, but based on scientific data. The results on immediate versus sustained rehabilitation effects also act as guidance on the duration of benefits and optimum assessment interval time. The nature and treatment of NPC has been the study interest of oncologists, radiologists, otorhinolaryngologists and speech-language pathologists. Too little is known about the swallowing mechanism and rehabilitation of the NPC patients. This project will contribute to the emerging evidence bank of diagnosis-specific swallowing rehabilitation that will not only benefit the patients, but also justifies the healthcare resources allocated to swallowing rehabilitation.

475210.label: Realisation of objectives
475210.value: All the objectives as stated in the proposal were addressed. Originally, we planned to recruit 160 subjects in this randomised controlled study. However, only 121 subjects were recruited and 111 of them had performed the FEES at baseline. In order to increase the recruitment rate, we had done the following measures and actions in order to increase the recruitment rate. 1) We had organized several meetings to communicate with related departments from Prince of Wales Hospital and Queen Elizabeth Hospital to enhance the recruitment rate of the study. The related departments included Oncology and ENT. 2) A speech therapist and research assistant were appointed for on-site recruitment of the subjects 3) Application of the extension of the study period in the present study These actions and attempts increased the recruitment rate and sample size in the present study.

475210.label: Major findings and research outcome
475210.value: One hundred and twenty-one patients who fulfilled the inclusion criteria of the study were recruited in the Prince of Wales Hospital and Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Hong Kong. One hundred and eleven subjects had performed FEES at their baseline. Seventy-six subjects completed the swallowing therapy and had their 2nd FEES done. Sixty-five subjects had their 6-month follow-up and 3rd FEES was performed. Fifty-eight subjects had completed a 1-year follow-up. Mean age of the subjects is 52.9 years old (SD=12.01; range 20-81; male = 38; female=20). 29 subjects were recruited in each therapy group. The present study showed that 63.8% NPC patients has aspiration or penetration on at least one or more food consistencies within one year post-radiotherapy. The demographic data, includes gender, time, age, body height and weight, radiation dose to related swallowing muscles and family incomes showed no significant difference between the 2 treatment groups. Objective 1: By using Wilcoxon signed-rank test, it was found that subjects in both group showed a significant improvement in swallowing (reduction of penetration-aspiration score) immediate (p=0.035) and 6-month post-treatment from baseline (p=0.037). It was found that the penetration-aspiration score in the 2 therapy groups showed no statistical significant [F(3,168)=2.241, p=0.085>0.05, partial Eta squared = 0.038)]. The treatment effect in both groups is comparable in alleviating aspiration risks and symptoms immediately post and over a 12-month interval for newly treated NPC patients post radiotherapy. Objective 2: Aspiration risk TG: There was a reduction in the aspiration risk of puree (10ml), mildly thick liquid (10ml) and gastric rice (10ml) in TG. VT: It was not significant in reducing any aspiration risk among different food consistencies. Pharyngeal residue TG: The results showed that there was a statistically significant reduction in the amount of pharyngeal residue after the swallow of puree (10ml), mildly thick liquid (10ml) and gastric rice (10ml). VT: Subjects in the Vitalstim group have a significant reduction in the amount of pharyngeal residue on puree (5ml, 10ml), thin liquid (5ml, 10ml), gastric rice (10ml). When compared with that found in TG, VT seems to have more improvement in reducing the amount of pharyngeal residue than TG. Objective 3: By using binary logistic regression, the staging of disease, comorbidities, cigarette smoking, alcohol consumption, radiotherapy treatment regimen, sex, age, education level and family income do not affect the swallowing rehabilitation outcomes immediate, 6-month and 12-month post-treatment. Others: It was found that there was significant improvement in the quality of life of patients (FACT-NP) as reflected by an increase in the total score of FACT-NP immediate, 6-month and 12-month post-treatment when compared to that of the baseline (F(3,165)=7.417, p=0.001). When within group comparison was performed, it was found that there was also an improvement in the quality of life of NPC patients in the TG and VT group at immediate, 6-month and 12-month post-therapy. Furthermore, a large database of NPC related dysphagia databank consisting of various dysphagia severities, radiation information and swallowing rehabilitation progress was established.

475210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
475210.value: The findings of the present study revealed that the treatment effect of both swallowing groups was comparable. There was a significant swallowing improvement in both treatment groups immediately and 6-month post-treatment. Impact: Swallowing therapy seems to play a role in swallowing rehabilitation of patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma, which in turn improves their quality of life. Early swallowing therapy could enhance the swallowing functions of the NPC patients. It, in turn would indirectly improve their overall quality of life significantly. Future direction: The inclusion of a control group might deem necessary. We might also consider include a subject group with both traditional swallowing therapy and Vitalstim therapy. It is hypothesized that the combined treatment regime of traditional swallowing therapy and Vitalstim therapy would be more effective than the standalone treatment regime of either traditional swallowing therapy or Vitalstim therapy.

475210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
475210.value: The present study is a randomized controlled study to study the treatment effect of two types of swallowing therapies, namely the Traditional swallowing therapy(TG) and the Vitalstim Therapy (VT) in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) within 12-month post-radiotherapy. A total of one hundred and twenty-one subjects were recruited. All of them were randomly assigned to one of the treatment groups (TG or VT). One hundred and eleven of them performed Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES) as baseline measurement. Seventy-six of them had completed the four to five weeks intensive swallowing therapy. Sixty-five subjects were followed up at 6-month from baseline. Fifty-eight of them were followed up at 12-month from baseline. The present study showed that 63.8% of NPC patients had different severity of swallowing impairment. The treatment effect in both groups is comparable in alleviating aspiration risks and symptoms immediately post and over a 12-month interval for newly treated NPC patients post radiotherapy. Both group of subjects demonstrated significant improvement in scores of quality of life (FACT-NP) immediately after treatment, 6-month and 12-month post-treatment. Swallowing therapy seems to play a role in swallowing rehabilitation of patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma within one-year postradiotherapy. There was also an improvement found in the quality of life immediate post-treatment, 6-month and 12-month post-treatment. Early swallowing therapy could enhance the swallowing functions of newly-treated patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

475710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
475710.value: Circulating fetal nucleic acids in the plasma of pregnant women have been intensively studied in recent years. The maternal plasma fetal RNA molecules are of special interest because they offer certain advantages over detection of circulating fetal DNA. For example, they could be utilised in all pregnant cases regardless of fetal gender and polymorphism. Currently, most of the research on circulating fetal RNA has been focused on the diagnostic applications. There are, however, limited investigations on the biological and physiological issues regarding circulating fetal RNA. Previously, we have demonstrated that the placenta is an important source of circulating fetal RNA in maternal plasma. We have further shown that the level of the placental-derived fetal RNA in maternal plasma was positively correlated with the corresponding gene expression level in the placenta. Hence, the detectability of fetal RNA in maternal plasma is largely dependent on the gene expression level in the placenta. Biologically, this observation is concordant with the widely accepted belief that the placenta would non-selectively shed its own mRNA molecules into the maternal circulation, possibly through apoptosis. However, we have recently identified evidence suggesting that for certain transcripts, the plasma placental mRNA level might be governed by additional factors. Thus, in this project, we aim to explore some of these factors. We will first confirm the existence of the regulatory factors by performing a thorough quantitative comparison of the placental-derived mRNA between the placenta and maternal plasma. A panel of transcripts with different placental expression levels will be studied. They will be measured by a digital molecular counting method to ensure a reliable comparison. We will next explore the biological factors which may potentially influence the level of circulating placental mRNA in maternal plasma. In particular, we will study the cell-specific gene expression of the selected mRNA species in different placental cell types, and explore the data for evidence that may suggest the different mRNA releasing mechanisms in these cells. In addition, we will compare if the placental transcripts would show differential clearance kinetics from maternal plasma after delivery. This project would potentially enhance our understanding of the production, release and clearance of circulating placental-derived mRNA in maternal plasma. 475710.label: Realisation of objectives
475710.value: Objective 1 is completed. We demonstrated that the quantitative relationship of the placental-derived transcripts between the placenta and maternal plasma was not tightly held, with placenta-specific 4 (PLAC4) mRNA showing the largest discrepancy. The result confirmed that circulating placental RNA concentration is additionally controlled by other biological factors. Objective 2 is completed. We found that the in vivo localization pattern of PLAC4 mRNA was different to that of the other two studied transcripts. The most distinctive feature was the preferential localization of PLAC4 mRNA molecules around the villous surface. We speculated that this phenomenon might play a role in favoring the release of PLAC4 mRNA molecules from the placenta into maternal plasma, and thus might contribute to its relatively high concentration in maternal plasma. Objective 3 is completed. By studying serial plasma samples collected from women after delivery, we found that the post-delivery clearance half-lives of the studied placental transcripts were not statistically different. Hence, RNA clearance may be a minor factor affecting the differential abundance of the studied placental transcripts in maternal plasma.

475710.label: Major findings and research outcome
475710.value: A manuscript titled “Investigation of biological factors influencing the placental mRNA profile in maternal plasma” was submitted to the PLoS ONE journal. Although the first feedback from the journal was “major revision”, we considered that we had not adequately described the experimental workflow and mathematical calculations in the first version of the manuscript, such that the reviewer might confuse some of the experimental steps. The manuscript has now been revised according to the reviewer’s comments, and was re-submitted to the journal on 19 Aug 2013. We are now waiting for the feedback from the journal. The submitted manuscript and the feedback from the journal are attached in Part C.

475710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
475710.value: In the biological aspect, the function of PLAC4 mRNA and its protein counterpart have not been reported thus far. Based on our observation of the distinctive in vivo localization of PLAC4 mRNA, we speculated that the transcript might be functional extracellularly, such that they might be actively transferred towards the villous surface for extracellular export. To further reveal the releasing process and the potential biological function of PLAC4 mRNA, we plan to refine the spatial localization of PLAC4 mRNA around the placental surface by using high-resolution imaging technology such as electron microscope. In the clinical aspect, our finding may be useful for the more efficient identification and utility of circulating placental mRNA for noninvasive prenatal testing. For example, in preeclampsia, an impaired clearance of circulating fetal DNA and histological changes of placental villous membrane have been reported. Hence, it would be worthwhile to further explore if biological parameters such as clearance kinetics, in vivo placental localization and releasing mechanism of circulating placental RNAs may be altered in preeclampsia. Such information may be useful for the development of noninvasive diagnostic and monitoring strategies for the disease.

475710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
475710.value: Fetal-derived RNA in maternal plasma is valuable for noninvasive prenatal testing. The placenta is believed to be an important source of circulating fetal RNA. Hence, most of the known fetal RNA markers were identified based on their expressions in the placenta. However, it remains unknown if the concentrations of placental-derived transcripts in maternal plasma are solely governed by their expression levels in the placenta. We hypothesized that additional biological factors, such as the release and the clearance of plasma RNA molecules, may affect the circulating fetal RNA profile. We demonstrated here that the maternal plasma profile of placental-derived RNAs was not solely depending on gene expression levels in the placenta. We excluded RNA clearance as a major regulating parameter because the placental transcripts were cleared at similar rates from maternal plasma after delivery. Instead, we postulated that there appears to be differences in the release of different placental transcripts. Transcripts with closer proximity to the placental surface might be more favorable to be released into maternal plasma. This finding may facilitate researchers to understand the turnover dynamics of circulating fetal RNA, and may be useful for the more efficient identification and utility of circulating placental RNA for noninvasive prenatal testing.

475910.label: Project Objectives
475910.value: Examine the effects of inducible conditional deletion of HIF-1α in chondrocytes on cartilaginous callus formation, vessel invasion and bone formation during fracture healing. A femur fracture model will be performed in mice with inducible conditional deletion of Hif-1α in chondrocytes (Col2α1-Cre ER; HIF-1α fl/fl) and control littermates. Targeted deletion of HIF-1α in chondrocytes will be induced upon tamoxifen administration in a defined time window of fracture healing. We will assess expression of the known HIF-1α target genes (VEGF and Glut 1) and chondrogenic marker genes (Ihh, Sox9 and Col2) by in situ hybridization in fracture callus. The impact of this genetic perturbation on fracture healing will be examined at various stages of the healing process by histology, radiology, quantitative cartilage histomorphometry, and immunohistochemistry. Define angiogenic and osteogenic signals that emanate from chondrocytes and the angiogenic-osteogenic coupling events during fracture healing. The environmental queues (mechanical and inflammatory) which are uniquely present in injury site than that seen during development suggest the possibility of different mechanisms in the context of bone repair. We will determine the impact of experimental hypoxia by hypoxic chamber and deletion of Hif-1α by Cre containing adenovirus constructs (Ad-Cre), GFP containing constructs (Ad-GFP) as control, on proliferation, differentiation and maturation of primary mouse chondrocytes. We will further identify the angiogenic and osteogenic signals that emanate from chondrocytes using Affymetrix microarray analysis. Next we will characterize the vascular-bone coupling events using fracture model developed in Aim 1. The osterix-GFP Cre reporter mice will be used to trace osteoblastic lineage cells, pericyte-associated antigen 3G5 will be used to mark the pericytes and CD31 to visualize the endothelial cells. Determine the effects of pharmacologic activation of the HIF-1α pathway on skeletal regeneration. We will examine the effects of local administration of pharmacologic agents (prolyl hydroxylase inhibitors) in a controlled-release pellet to induce HIF-1α on bone regeneration in a bone defect model. Critical sized bone defect model will be performed in mouse femur with or without pharmacologic intervention. Histologic, radiographic and biomechanical evaluation of bone healing will be performed. In addition, activation of the HIF-1α pathway will be evaluated by immunohistochemistry, HIF downstream targets and chondrogenic genes will be detected with in situ hybridization. We anticipate that local application of pharmacologic agents will increase HIF-1α activation and promotes angiogenesis and osteogenesis in the large defect model. We expect that improved angiogenic response and ultimate bone regeneration perform at an optimal rate with pharmacologic intervention.

475910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
475910.value: Bone has a unique ability to regenerate and repair itself postnatally. However, in clinic about 10% of fractures have impaired healing. This results in enormous direct and indirect cost to the individual and society. A hallmark of impaired bone healing is a reduction in vascular supply and nutrient availability at the site of injury, suggesting that impaired blood vessel formation is a major contributor to the pathology. Following injury, disruption of normal circulation in bone leads to hypoxia of adjacent tissues. We reasoned that chondrocytes, the component of the intermediate cartilaginous callus of the healing bone, are ideally positioned to sense and respond to fluctuations in oxygen and nutrient supply during the healing process. The hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) pathway has emerged as the central pathway responding to hypoxia a wide variety of organisms. HIF-1α impinges on gene programs which influence angiogenesis (e.g., VEGF) and cellular metabolism (e.g., glut1). HIF-1α levels are controlled by regulated proteolysis through an oxygen sensitive mechanism. Under normoxic conditions, HIF-1α undergoes prolyl hydroxylation and is ligated by von Hippel-Lindau protein (pVHL), an E3 ubiquitin ligase and then degraded by the proteosome. Under hypoxia, HIF-1α prolyl hydroxylation is inhibited, and HIF-1α accumulates in the nucleus where it forms a dimer with the HIF-1β subunit, and then transactivates HIF responsive genes. Our recent studies have shown that HIF-1α is strongly induced during bone repair, and increased HIF-1α activation in bone in a mouse model increases postnatal bone acquisition. In this proposal, we will test the hypothesis that during fracture healing chondrocytes use the HIF-1α pathway to sense low oxygen tension and transmit signals that regulate the process of angiogenesis and bone healing, and targeting the HIF-1α pathway could be designed as a therapy for improving skeletal regeneration. In aim 1, we will examine the role of Hif-1α in chondrocytes on cartilaginous callus formation during fracture healing using genetic mouse models. In the second aim, we intend to define the angiogenic and osteogenic signals that derive from chondrocytes and visualize the angiogenic and osteogenic events during fracture healing. Finally, we will evaluate the effects of pharmacologic activation of the HIF-1α pathway on skeletal regeneration using a large bone defect model. We expect that the proposed studies will further our understanding on the molecular and cellular mechanisms of skeletal regeneration and lead to novel interventions for patients with impaired bone healing.

475910.label: Realisation of objectives
475910.value: For Aim 1, a femur fracture model was performed in mice with inducible conditional deletion of HIF-1α in chondrocytes and control littermates. Histological analysis indicates that conditional deletion of HIF-1α in chondrocytes impairs cartilaginous callus formation at day 14 and subsequent bone consolidation at day 28 post-surgery. The impaired cartilaginous callus formation is accompanied by down-regulation of chondrogenic markers including Ihh, Sox9 and Col2, as well as the HIF-1α target genes VEGF and Glut 1. Quantitative cartilage histomorphometry analysis indicates that the volume of cartilaginous callus of the healing bone is decreased in mice conditional deletion of HIF-1α in chondrocytes compared with the controls. We also identify that erythropoietin (EPO), the downstream target of HIF-1α, is expressed in chondrocytes of the developing growth plate and the cartilaginous callus during fracture repair. For Aim 2, deletion of HIF-1α in the mesenchyme impairs joint development. Deletion of HIF-1α impairs self-renewal and chondrogenic lineage differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells indexed by colony forming unit assay and reduced expression of chondrogenic marker genes Sox9, Sox5, Sox6, Col2, and aggrecan. In the high through gene profiling analysis, alterations of angiogenic and osteogenic signals that emanate from chondrocytes are identified following deletion of HIF-1α, note that the levels of angiogenic factors VEGF, angiopoietin 1, EPO are down-regulated in chondrogenic cells. This is accompanied by altered expression of osteogenic signals controlling osteoblast differentiation. The key transcription factor osterix is down-regulated following deletion of HIF-1α in the MSCs, the expression of osteogenic markers Runx2, Col1 and osteocalcin is also decreased. Chromatin immunoprecipitation assays confirm the transcriptional control of osterix by HIF-1α. During bone repair, CD31 is identified to be closely located with pericytes which are osterix positive. For Aim 3, the mouse femur bone defect model and tibia distraction osteogenesis model were established. Based on cellular phenotypic screening assays, deferoxamine (DFO) was identified as an HIF-α activator. Local delivery of DFO significantly enhances bone repair in the bone defect and distraction osteogenesis models. The bone volume of the new bone regenerate is increased in the DFO treated group compared with the controls. HIF downstream targets VEGF and EPO is shown to be upregulated in the DFO treated group than the controls. The increased bone formation is associated with increased vascularity in the middle stage of bone healing. We also identify that EPO functions as an agent to promote skeletal repair through enhanced angiogenesis and cartilaginous callus formation.

475910.label: Major findings and research outcome
475910.value: We analyzed the effects of disruption of HIF-1α in chondrogenic cells and the condensing mesenchyme using the Cre/loxp strategy. Our results indicate that HIF-1α serves as a key regulator for chondrogenic cells or MSCs proliferation and differentiation, and to couple angiogenesis to chondrogenesis during skeletal regeneration. Deletion of HIF-1α impairs joint development and formation. Deletion of HIF-1α impaired self-renewal and chondrogenic lineage differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells indexed by colony forming unit assay and reduced expression of chondrogenic marker genes, in accord with our findings in vivo. Conditional deletion of HIF-1α in chondrocytes impairs cartilaginous callus formation at day 14 and subsequent bone consolidation at day 28 post-surgery. The impaired cartilaginous callus formation is accompanied by down-regulation of chondrogenic markers. Activation of HIF-1α using small molecules serves as a novel approach to promote chondrogenesis and skeletal repair. EPO, the downstream target of HIF-1α, functions as an agent to promote skeletal repair through enhanced angiogenesis and cartilaginous callus formation. Hypoxia promotes MSCs expansion for skeletal repair and regeneration. Chromatin immunoprecipitation assays showed direct occupancy of the osterix promoter by HIF-1α. Western blot showed that deletion of HIF-1α affected cyclin D1 levels and its phosphorylation states in MSCs. The results suggest that deletion of HIF-1α impairs MSCs self-renewal and chondrogenic differentiation. Hypoxia condition facilitates MSCs expansion for MSCs-based therapy for skeletal repair. Our results indicate that HIF-1α is required for cartilage development and chondrogenic responses, and also couples chondrogenesis and angiogenesis during bone repair. Three abstracts were accepted for presentations in national and international conferences, and three publications under this project were published in peer reviewed international journals. One PhD student was trained partially under this project with one publication in Plos One as first author.

475910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
475910.value: Based on the results obtained, the PI aims to further develop the project, it is expected that small molecule HIF-α activator serves as an efficient therapy to promote skeletal regeneration for patients with impaired skeletal repair. We propose to further consolidate the results in large size animal models to test the efficacy and safety of the candidate small molecule, and aim to develop a potential drug candidate for promoting skeletal repair and regeneration.

475910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
475910.value: Impaired bone repair (e.g. large bone defects, fracture non-union or delayed union) is a difficult skeletal disorder that causes tremendous suffer and cost to the patients and the society. The pathology of the impaired bone healing is characterized by decreased potential of bone formation associated with less vascularity and oxygen availability, and lacking of reparative stem cells and cartilaginous callus formation. This project identify that deletion of HIF-1α in the chondrogenic cells or MSCs impairs chondrocyte proliferation, MSCs self-renewal and chondrogenic differentiation. HIF-1α is required for cartilaginous callus formation and angiogenesis during bone regeneration. The coordinated regulation between cartilaginous callus formation and angiogenesis is prerequisite for subsequent consolidation of bone repair. Activation of HIF-1α using small molecules or regulation of HIF-1α target may serve as a novel approach to promote skeletal regeneration.

476210.value: 中藥已廣泛應用於緩解多種症狀和治療孕期併發症，卻缺乏系統的評估。到目前為止，還沒有對中藥在孕期使用的安全性和對胚胎發育的益處及不良影響的資料。 在臨床實踐中已經有超過300種中藥在妊娠期間使用。我們的實驗室正在通過懷孕母鼠來篩查最常用的中藥的潛在胚胎毒性。但是，通過在體實驗來檢測所有的中藥的費用昂貴、費時及費力。而胚胎體外實驗方法（包括胚胎幹細胞試驗，胚胎微團培養實驗和全胚胎培養實驗）已經確立並作為替代方法廣泛應用於化工，天然補充劑和藥品，但尚未應用於中藥。所以該研究的目的是檢測每一種體外試驗方法在中藥發育毒性的實用性，並通過體外實驗方法來評估中藥在胚胎發育上的安全性。 在這項研究中，已經被明確描述的中藥以及通過人和/或動物在體實驗所得到的發育毒性的數據會被選擇用於評估。在與香港中醫中藥研究所和德國風險評估研究所的合作中，我們將首先通過體外實驗的方法來確定試驗中藥的潛在胚胎毒性。這種胚胎毒性是通過比較從細胞毒性、分化、胚胎發育、畸形的濃度反應曲線得到的生物和分子數據來確定的。其次，我們會通過比較體外試驗的準確性來預測試驗藥物的潛在毒性的精確分類。預測模型會由體外實驗的線性回歸分析的判別法、敏感性、特異性，預測能力和精度來確定。 檢測中藥的安全性對於本地和國際衛生保健服務以及商業營銷都是迫切的。這個初步的評估可以找出適合研究中藥的胚胎毒性的體外實驗方法，並提供快速的、適當的方法來進行今後的大規模驗證和篩選工作。

476210.value: 1. For EST, the embryotoxic potentials are increased in Safflower, Sanchi, Salvia root, White Peony root, Baical skullcap root, Milkvetch root, Leech, Trichosanthes root, Figwort flower, and then Three-wingnut in ascending orders. For MM test, the embryotoxic potentials are increased in Sanchi, Salvia root, Safflower, Baical skullcap root, White Peony root, Milkvetch root, Leech, Trichosanthes root, Figwort flower, and then Three-wingnut in ascending orders. For WEC test, the embryotoxic potentials are increased in Baical skullcap root, Sanchi, Safflower, White peony root, Salvia root, Figwort flower, Milkvetch root, Leech, Trichosanthes root, and then Three-wingnut in ascending orders. Three-wingnut is the most embryotoxic CHM in all 3 tests. Leech, Trichosanthes root, and Figwort flower have similar high embryotoxic potentials in 3 tests as well. Other CHM has lower but variable embryotoxic potentials however. It suggests that the results of 3 in vitro tests are more consistent in CHM with higher embryotoxic potentials than CHM with lower embryotoxic potentials. The protocol of the study was submitted for a journal publication. The results were presented in a meeting and will be submitted for journal publications and conference presentations very soon. 2. For both EST and WEC, prediction models mistakenly predict Leech and Trichosanthes roots as weakly embryotoxic and White peony root as non-embryotoxic; accuracy rate are about 70%. For MM test, prediction models mistakenly predict Leech and Trichosanthes root as weakly embryotoxic and Figwort flower, Milkvetch root and White peony root as non-embryotoxic; accuracy rate is below 50%. Molecular determinations do not increase the accurate rate. The results indicate that EST and WEC have higher prediction values than MM for the classification of embryotoxic potentials in TCM. The results were presented in a meeting and will be submitted for journal publications and conference presentations very soon.

476210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476210.value: The overall prediction values of EST and WEC for embryotoxicity of CHM are better than MM, but the prediction are still not very good when compared with that for pharmaceuticals (>78%). It suggests that the current prediction models may be not suitable for CHM. There are many difference between CHM and pharmaceuticals. New prediction models specific for CHM is required. According to previous experience for pharmaceuticals, more CHM should be tested to establish a good prediction model. Substantial support is needed.

476210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476210.value: Chinese herbal medicines have been widely used during pregnancy, but safety data is not available. There is an urgent need in testing the safety of Chinese herbal medicines for local and international health care service and also commercial marketing. In this study we tested the usefulness of the in vitro test methods to predict embryotoxicity of Chinese herbal medicines. This evaluation can identify the suitable in vitro embryotoxicity tests for Chinese herbal medicines and provide rapid and reproducible alternative approach for large-scale validating and screening programme in future.

476310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
476310.value: Over the past several years, large-scale analyses of the mouse and human genomes have revealed that a large portion of the mammalian genome is transcribed. However, most transcripts do not seem to encode proteins; rather, they constitute a diverse repertoire of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) emerging as potent regulators of gene expression. Transcripts from Ultra-conserved Regions (T-UCRs) represent a novel class of ncRNAs whose functions in biological processes remain largely unknown. The tissue-specific expression of T-UCRs in skeletal muscle suggests that it may play a role in skeletal muscle development. To explore this possibility, we performed an expression profiling by microarray analysis using RNAs from undifferentiated myoblasts and differentiated myotubes. Our results demonstrated that T-UCRs are differentially expressed in myoblasts and myotubes. A subset of T-UCRs is up-regulated during myoblast fusion into terminally differentiated myotubes. One particular T-UCR, tuc.478+A is among the most significantly up-regulated T-UCRs, leading us to hypothesize that it plays a positive role in skeletal muscle cell differentiation or myogenesis. Further sequence analysis revealed that a possible mechanism through which tuc.478+A stimulates myogenesis is to regulate the splicing of GRIA3 as an antisense transcript. To test above hypothesis, four objectives are proposed which aim to discover a novel mechanism underlying T-UCR’s role in myogenesis. The resultant findings from this study will shed a light on the involvement of T-UCRs in skeletal muscle differentiation and identify a completely novel mechanism of gene regulation by ncRNAs. 近几年的大规模人类和小鼠基因组分析显示很大一部分的基因组都会被转录，但是大部分这样的转录本并不编码蛋白产物，被称为非编码核糖核酸（non-coding RNAs或ncRNAs）。ncRNAs已被证实具有潜在的调控基因表达的功能。来自于基因组超保守区域（Ultra-conserved Regions或UCRs）的ncRNAs被称为T-UCRs（Transcripts from Ultra-conserved Regions）, 代表了一类新的功能未知的ncRNAs。我们在研究中发现一些在骨骼肌中特异表达的T-UCRs可能在骨骼肌发育过程中有重要作用。用微阵列芯片进行的表达谱分析的结果表明许多T-UCRs在未分化和分化的骨骼肌细胞中的表达有差异, 其中一部分在骨骼肌分化过程中表达量增加。在这些表达上调的T-UCRs中，tuc.478+A的表达显著升高，因而我们假设这个T-UCR会促进骨骼肌分化。进一步的序列分析显示tuc.478+A位于Gria3基因的反意义链，因此很可能通过调控Gria3基因表达过程中的选择性剪接来促进肌肉分化。为了验证以上假说，本研究设定了四个研究目标用以揭示T-UCRs在骨骼肌分化过程中的新机理。本课题研究的发现将会加深我们对T-UCRs在骨骼肌分化过程中的功能和ncRNAs调控基因表达机理的认识。

476310.label: Realisation of objectives
476310.value: In the original proposal, we laid out four aims to study the functional role of tuc. 478+A in myogenic differentiation. We have completed most of the proposed work. Results from the first three Aims support our original hypothesis that tuc. 478+A is a functional non-coding RNA in skeletal myogenesis; results from the fourth aim, on the other hand, turned out different from what we originally expected thus prevented us from completing it. Nevertheless, along the way we unexpectedly discovered another long non-coding RNA, Dum that functions as an important regulator of myogenic differentiation and muscle regeneration. Therefore, we expanded our research scope by including the functional study of Dum in skeletal myogenesis, which led to successful cloning and characterization of Dum. The result were submitted for publication on Cell Research and currently under revision. We have also decided to create a computational pipeline, sebnif, for systemic identification of lncRNAs which proves to be instrumental for our current and future study of lncRNAs. Additionally, various projects were started and completed with the aid from this funding, which led to publication of 7 peer-reviewed papers with this project code acknowledged.

476310.label: Major findings and research outcome
476310.value: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are transcriptional units with no protein-coding potential and emerging as potent regulators of gene expression. This study was undertaken to investigate the function of an ncRNA, tuc.478+A in skeletal myogenesis. In the original proposal, we thus hypothesize that tuc.478+A represents an antisense transcript of GRIA3 and it functions to promote skeletal myogenesis through regulating its sense transcript. To test this hypothesis the following four specific aims/objectives are proposed: (1) To determine the expression of tuc.478+A in both in vitro and in vivo myogenesis model. (2) To clone and characterize tuc.478+A gene. (3)To test the positive function of tuc.478+A in skeletal muscle differentiation. (4) To explore the mechanism underlying the function of tuc.478+A in skeletal myogenesis. We have completed majority of the proposed work. Results from the first three Aims support our original hypothesis that tuc. 478+A is a functional non-coding RNA in skeletal myogenesis although results from the fourth aim turned out different from what we originally expected. Nevertheless, along the way we unexpectedly discovered another non-coding RNA, Dum that functions as an important regulator of myogenic differentiation and muscle regeneration. We found that the expression of Dum is dynamically regulated during myogenesis in vitro and in vivo. It is also transcriptionally induced by MyoD binding upon myoblast differentiation. Functional analyses show it promotes myoblast differentiation and damage induced muscle regeneration. Mechanistically Dum was found to silence its neighboring gene, Dppa2 in cis through recruiting Dnmt1, Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b. Furthermore intrachromosomal looping between Dum locus and Dppa2 promoter is necessary for Dum/Dppa2 interaction. This work is currently under revision by Cell Research and expected to be accepted within one months. In addition to the above findings, we have also created a Pipeline, Sebnif, which can be used for identification of novel lncRNAs (PLoS One. 2014). Collectively our studies have identified a novel family of ncRNA, lncRNA, as critical regulators of muscle development and muscle regeneration, which will hopefully lead to future development of therapeutic targets from numerous muscle diseases.

476310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476310.value: Our study has identified long non-coding RNAs as novel family regulators of muscle cell function and muscle regeneration. In the future, to further these findings, two research directions can be explored: (1) To characterize the function of other lncRNAs in skeletal myogenesis and elucidate their importance during muscle regeneration. (2) To further examine the function of Dum in muscle regeneration, we will generate a muscle tissue-specific knock-out mouse model and further explore its functional roles in other aspects of muscle stem cells.

476310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476310.value: Large portion of mammalian genome was thought to be “junk” regions while only ~3% are useful in coding proteins. However, recent efforts in high throughput analyses of the genomes have revealed that these “junk” regions are transcribed into a wide variety of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs). Long ncRNAs (>200nt in length, lncRNAs) are emerging as potent regulators of gene expression. Defects in lncRNAs could lead to the development of many human diseases while the underlying mechanisms are largely unknown. Thus, lncRNAs are considered as the new frontier of biomedical research. Here in this project we for the first time identified and characterized the function role of a novel lncRNA in skeletal muscle cell and muscle regeneration process. In the long run, we hope this will serve as a starting point for the development of new therapeutic approaches for treating muscle related human diseases.

476610.label: Realisation of objectives
476610.value: This was a 2-phases study on patients with REM sleep behaviour disorder (RBD), consisting of a clinical follow-up (Phase-1) study followed by a search of early neurodegenerative markers at Phase-2. Two sub-groups of RBD patients were studied: 1) typical RBD (tRBD)- RBD patients with old age of onset (mean age of onset > 60); 2) atypical/ psychiatric RBD (aRBD)- RBD patients of younger age (mean age ~40) with co-morbid mental illnesses. In this study, our objectives were: 1. To establish the follow-up outcome data on both typical RBD and atypical RBD. (Phase-1) 2. To investigate the neurodegenerative basis of idiopathic typical RBD and atypical RBD by comparing the early neurodegenerative markers in both conditions with controls. (Phase-2) 3. To compare the significance of different early neurodegenerative markers in typical and atypical RBD During the period, we had successfully completed the study. In phase-1 study, we had recruited 91 tRBD and 50 aRBD. Both groups showed favourable responses to clinical treatment with reduction of sleep symptoms and sleep-related injuries. We also found that among tRBD subjects, the estimated 5-year and 9-year risks of development of synucleinopathy-related neurodegenerative disorders were 8.5% and 38.1% respectively. On the other hand, we did not find any incidence of neurodegenerative disorders among aRBD subjects. For phase-2 study, we recruited 50 tRBD and 50 age-, sex- matched community controls; and 40 aRBD and 80 age-, sex- matched controls (2 control arms including a control arm with psychiatric disorders and another one from healthy community subjects) into the phase-2A study. They completed the neurocognitive assessment as listed in the protocol. A further subgroup of these subjects was selected for neuroimaging study. Ten tRBD and 8 age-, sex-matched controls; 10 aRBD, and 20 age-, sex-matched controls (from healthy controls and psychiatric controls) were selected according to the selection criteria for phase-2B PET brain neuroimaging study of dopaminergic transmission. Among various domains of neurocognitive tests (including attention, memory, executive function, olfactory function and color discrimination), both RBD groups (tRBD and aRBD) had poorer performance in olfactory function when comparing with the age-sex matched controls, which is one of the early precursors of neurodegeneration. The neuroimaging study also found that RBD patients (both tRBD and aRBD) had dopamine transmission abnormality as detected by 18F-DOPA scan. The overall findings suggested that early neurodegenerative processes were evident in RBD patients even without overt clinical neurodegenerative features, in both older tRBD and younger aRBD groups.

476610.value: For the tRBD cohort, 91 subjects were recruited with a mean follow-up duration of 5.6 years (mean age of diagnosis was 65.5 years). Nineteen patients (21%) developed clinical neurodegenerative disorders (Parkinson’s disease or dementia), and the estimated 5-year and 9-year risks were 8.5% and 38.1% respectively. In particular, a history of psychiatric disorders would predict an increased risk of PD (Hazard ratio 7.0, 95% CI 1.3-38.3) after adjusting for gender, age and smoking status (Wing et al 2012). Regarding the treatment response, majority of patients were taking clonazepam (96%) and only 4% were prescribed with melatonin. Two third of the patients (67%) reported no more sleep-related injury (SRI) at follow-up. Most patients reported improvement in RBD symptoms including nightmares and dream enactment. The aRBD subjects (n=50, mean age of onset 40.2; mean follow-up duration 3.4 years) had no clinical manifestation of neurodegenerative disorders at follow-up. Various treatment modalities were tried including modification of antidepressant regimes, prescription of clonazepam and melatonin. Most of them showed a parallel improvement in RBD symptoms (nightmares and dream enactment) and reduction of SRI. The study suggested that clinical response were satisfactory in both groups with reduction in both sleep symptoms and SRI. Phase-2 study in search of neurodegenerative markers: We recruited 50 tRBD and 50 age-, sex-matched controls; 40 aRBD, 40 age-, sex- matched healthy control and 40 age-, sex- psychiatric diagnosis matched controls subjects. We had carried out neurocognitive assessment for different domains, including attention, memory, executive functions, olfactory function and visual discrimination ability. Comparing with the age-, sex-matched control subjects, tRBD had poorer performance in olfactory function, (p<0.034) but not in other domains. For aRBD, they also had lower score in the olfactory identification test (p<0.029). No significant differences in other neurocognitive tests were found. Comparing the tRBD with control subjects in the 18F-DOPA PET brain dopamine transmission imaging, tRBD subjects were found to have lower dopamine update (p= 0.028). For the aRBD, they were also found to have lower dopamine update (p= 0.012), when compared to the age and sex matched psychiatric control and healthy control groups. The dopamine transmission abnormalities had significant inverse correlations with clinical RBD symptoms (RBDQ-HK score, r= -0.54, p<0.01), but no correlation with neurocognitive tests were found. The phase-2 results suggested that even among RBD patients without overt clinical neurodegenerative features, early neurodegenerative markers of olfactory abnormalities and abnormal dopamine neurotransmission were detectable in these subjects.

476610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476610.value: While tRBD subjects had definitive risk in the development of neurodegenerative disorders, the young aRBD group, who were at the age of 40s to 50s, may take time to develop. Although they have not yet developed clinical neurodegenerative disorders at follow-up in this study, they had poorer performance in the olfactory function and dopamine transmission abnormalities in the cross-sectional neurocognitive and PET imaging studies. In other words, these findings suggested the presence of early neurodegenerative processes among RBD subjects. However, longer and regular follow-up is needed to detect the ultimate outcome of both tRBD and aRBD subjects. A long-term study especially for both tRBD and especially the young onset aRBD with repeated measurements of clinical, neurocognitive features and dopamine neuroimaging is highly recommended. It is important to determine whether presence of early neurocognitive and dopamine neurotransmission abnormalities may help to predict the future onset of neurodegeneration. From the clinical and prevention perspectives, our data is supporting the prevailing concept that RBD heralded the onset of clinical synucleinopathy-related neurodegeneration for some years. RBD studies provide the ideal model and timing for development of neuroprotective trials to prevent the onset of synucleinopathy-related neurodegeneration.

476610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476610.value: REM sleep behaviour disorder (RBD) is a sleep disorder typically affecting elderly and was found to precede clinical synucleinopathy-related neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson’s disease (PD) and Dementia of Lewy Body. Our Hong Kong cohort data found that the estimated 5-year and 9-year risks of development of neurodegenerative disease were 8.5% and 38.1% respectively. In particular, a past history of psychiatric disorders would predict a 7 fold increased risk of development of PD. RBD showed good clinical response to treatment in terms of control of RBD symptoms and sleep-related injuries. For the young onset RBD co-morbid with psychiatric illnesses (aRBD), they were at much younger age (mean age of 45) than the typical RBD. Although the risk of development of clinical neurodegenerative disorders was not established in this short-term follow-up study, they harboured some early signs of neurodegeneration as demonstrated by the olfactory abnormalities and decrease in dopamine neurotransmission. Further longer term follow-up study of both tRBD and aRBD subjects with prospective monitoring of clinical, neurocognitive and neurotransmission features is indicated. RBD studies provide the ideal model and timing for development of neuroprotective trials to prevent the onset of synucleinopathy-related neurodegeneration.

476710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
476710.value: Current treatments for chronic pain are far from ideal. When the underlying cause of pain is nerve damage (e.g. spinal cord injury, diabetic neuropathy, or amputation), the main focus of attention has been drugs designed to target neuronal systems with an emphasis on blocking neurotransmission. However, potent analgesics such as morphine are surprisingly ineffective in treating neuropathic pain, and the explanation may lie outside the classical idea that morphine regulates pain solely via neuronal opioid receptors. Pain sensations are normally transmitted from the periphery via primary sensory neurons whose cell bodies lie in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG) and are closely enveloped by satellite glial cells. Recent evidence suggests that glial cells contribute to neuroimmune activation in neuropathic pain models and in neurodegeneration due to expression of Toll-like receptors (TLRs). Morphine can stimulate TLR4 and directly activate microglial cells, thus enhancing inflammation and pain and this effect possibly accounts for its failure to treat neuropathic pain syndromes. Until recently, TLRs were thought to be confined to cells of the immune system as sensors of danger signals. Now there is accumulating evidence that TLRs are also expressed by DRG neurons and associated glial cells. TLR4 classically recognizes bacterial products such as lipopolysaccharide, but additionally responds to byproducts of tissue destruction such as heat shock proteins and extracellular matrix proteins which are likely to be present after nerve damage. When stimulated with lipopolysaccharide, isolated DRG neurons generate an opioid-like peptide called nociceptin/orphanin-FQ, whose function may be to inhibit inflammatory cytokine production by DRG glial cells. We propose therefore that activation of TLR4 on neuronal and glial cells within the DRG could influence pain transmission in an autocrine and/or paracrine fashion through nociceptin and cytokine production. Our hypothesis is that disregulation of these systems in the DRG disrupts the acute phase of response to nerve damage and allows progression to a chronic pain state. There are tremendous advantages in designing drug treatments to act in the early stages of nerve damage before irreversible changes are established. Because DRG are axotomized by dissociation, it has been suggested that cultures of dissociated DRG cells represent neuronal cells in a neuropathic pain state. Therefore, we propose to characterize TLR4-dependent responses in DRG neurons and glial cells and examine the crosstalk between these systems. This study of TLR4-dependent neuron-glia responses should help to identify targets for future investigation in the more complex animal models of neuropathic pain. 目前對慢性疼痛的治療是遠不夠理想。當疼痛的主要成因是神經損傷（如脊髓損傷，糖尿病性神經病變，或者截肢）時，主要使用的是能够靶向神經系统，重点用來阻止神經傳導的藥物。然而, 出乎意料的是，强力鎮痛劑例如嗎啡對神經病理性疼痛的治療並没有太大作用，並且這也許不可以用嗎啡僅僅通過神經性阿片受體來調節疼痛的傳統想法來解釋。疼痛感正常是通過初級感覺神經元從外周傳導的,而這些初級神經元的細胞體位於背根神經節（DRG）並且被衛星神經膠質細胞緊緊包圍。最新的證據表明 通過神經膠質細胞Toll樣受體(TLRs)的表達，神經膠質細胞能夠促成在神經病理性疼痛模型和神經退化中的神經免疫激活。嗎啡能夠刺激TLRs，直接去激活微神經膠質細胞，從而能夠增強炎症和疼痛。這一效應可能解釋了嗎啡治療神經病理性疼痛綜合症的失敗。最近，TLRs被認為作為危險信號的感受器，局限於免疫系統的細胞中。現在有越來越多的證據表明TLRs也在DRG神經元及其相關的神經膠質細胞中表達。TLR4 傳統上會識別像脂多糖的細菌代謝物，但是除此之外，TLR4還能够識別由神經損傷造成的組織破壞而產生的副產物，例如熱擊蛋白和細胞外基質蛋白。當被分離的DRG 神經元受到脂多糖的刺激之後，它們會產生一種名叫痛啡肽/孤啡肽-FQ的具有抑制DRG神經膠質細胞炎症細胞因子的產生的阿片樣肽。因此我們提議：位於處在DRG的神經元細胞和神經膠質細胞上的TLR4的激活可能影響疼痛的傳導。這種傳導是通過痛啡肽和細胞因子的產生以一種自分泌和/或者旁分泌的方式進行的。我們的假設是:位於DRG的這些系統失調會破壞對神經損傷反應的急性期，從而會讓其進入到慢性疼痛階段。設計作用於神經損傷在不可逆變化建立之前的早期階段的藥物治療有很多優勢。因為DRG是通過分離被軸索切斷，實驗已經表明分離的DRG細胞的培養表示神經元細胞是處於一種神經病理性疼痛階段。因此，我們提議表徵位於DRG的神經元和神經膠質細胞的TLR4-依賴性反應 以及研究這些體系之間的相互關係。對于TLR-4依賴的神經元-神經膠質細胞反應的研究，應該會為以後確立更複雜的神經病理性疼痛的動物模型的研究目標带來幫助。

476710.label: Realisation of objectives
476710.value: The three principal objectives of this project have been achieved, although some of the more minor components had to be modified as we made new discoveries along the way. For Objective 1, we had intended to immunostain DRG cells for GFAP for non-myelinating glial cells, GS or GLAST as markers for satellite glial cells, and S100β as a marker for Schwann cells. However, satellite glial cells and Schwann cells appear to de-differentiate when put in culture, and markers which are useful in vivo are no longer useful in vitro. The major goals of Objectives 1 and 2 were achieved with regard to TLR4 expression and cell signaling in DRG cells. Regarding Objective 1, we also detected EP4, EPRAP, IP and NOP at the mRNA level, but the antibodies were too poor to pursue more detailed cell-based characterization. For this reason, we also decided not to follow the reports on the opioid-like peptide N/OFQ and rather aimed to concentrate our resources on studying LPS-stimulated TLR4. We selected ultrapure LPS as our TLR4 agonist of choice and found that LPS from R. sphaeroides did not behave as an antagonist in DRG cells, therefore we used CLI-095 to demonstrate TLR4-dependency of LPS-stimulated responses. The goals of Objective 3 became more complicated as we realized that DRG glial cells behaved quite differently to LPS in the presence and absence of neurons, indicating a complex paracrine interaction between these cell types. We established a Ca2+ imaging system to study the acute effects of LPS and look for neuron-glia communication, but have no evidence of LPS-stimulated Ca2+ mobilization. Neither did we find any evidence that TLR4 is preferentially expressed by small diameter neurons, therefore neuropeptide release was not studied. Unfortunately, transfection efficiency of DRG cells intended for Objective 3 proved far too low to consider studying siRNA-based assays, so complete knockdown of TLR4 in a cell type-specific manner remains an elusive goal.

476710.label: Major findings and research outcome
476710.value: At the start of this project, the TLR4 signaling complex had been reported as a non-classical combination of TLR4/CD14/MD-1, but our studies with rat DRG cells suggested that although the cells expressed TLR4, CD14, MD-1, MD-1 and RP105 mRNA and protein, the TLR4 signaling complex was most likely to be the classical receptor complex of TLR4/CD14/MD-2 found on most immune cells. Our next major finding was that TLR4 signaled only through a MyD88-dependent pathway with no evidence for TRIF-dependent cell signaling. Unexpectedly, we discovered that TLR4-dependent expression of IL-1β and TNFα mRNA was entirely dependent on NF-κB, while elevation of COX-2 mRNA could proceed through both NF-κB-dependent and/or EGFR transactivation pathways. Finally, we showed that LPS stimulated COX-2-dependent PGE2 and prostacyclin production while at the same time inhibiting COX-1 expression. All these findings were reported in Tse KH et al (2014) Neuroscience 267:241-251 which represents the first paper to fully characterize TLR4-dependent cell signaling in isolated DRG cells. Next we followed our observation that isolated DRG glial cells expressed TLR4 mRNA but did not express TLR4-ir on their cell surface. DRG neurons prevented the cell surface expression of TLR4 by glial cells, by a cell-cell contact-dependent mechanism, and this has major implications for the regulation of glial cell reactivity following nerve damage. To follow this hypothesis using our in vitro system, we looked at the role of exogenous PGE¬2 and the influence of conditioned medium from damaged neurons on COX-2 and TNFα mRNA expression. In both mixed DRG cells or purified DRG glial cells, exogenous PGE2 increased COX-2 and inhibited TNFα mRNA expression (± LPS). Conditioned medium from control and heat-shocked DRG neuron-enriched cultures also increased COX-2 mRNA expression in DRG glial cells. We hypothesized that conditioned medium from heat-shocked neurons would contain TLR4 ligands but blocking TLR4 had only a small inhibitory effect on this response. (We are currently searching to identify the likely endogenous regulators of TLR4.) All these findings were reported in Tse KH et al (2014) Neuroscience 279:10-22. This paper clearly demonstrates the complexity of neuron-glia interactions and highlights the inhibitory control exerted by DRG neurons over satellite glial cells. It is our hope that neuroscientists studying the astrocytes and microglial cells of the central nervous system consider that these cells may also behave quite differently in the presence of neurons. A third paper on the regulation of inflammatory mediators by PGE2 is in preparation.

476710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476710.value: Because of the similarity in the changes in inflammatory gene expression patterns in response to PGE2 and in response to conditioned medium from DRG neuron-enriched cell cultures, we are currently investigating the role of PGE2 (EP) receptor subtypes in mediating these responses. The literature is in conflict as to the relative roles of EP1, EP2, EP3 and EP4 receptors in inflammatory and neuropathic pain conditions. We hope our continuing studies will go some way to clarifying this matter. Our striking observations that DRG neurons are inhibitory for TLR4 receptor function in associated glial cells supports our previous work showing that DRG neurons are inhibitory to other receptors involved in inflammation, such as CGRP, EP4 and IP receptors. Taken together, these results provide clues as to why satellite glial cells may become activated following nerve injury; circumstances whereby the inhibitory control of neurons may be lost. By implication, nerve damage might remove this inhibitory tone and alter the responsiveness of satellite glial cells in vivo. We have therefore discussed these concepts with a neurosurgeon/neuroscientist colleague in US (Prof. Luc Jasmin) in the hope that he might be able to pursue the in vivo correlate of our in vitro observations.

476710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476710.value: Because current treatments for chronic pain conditions are far from ideal, our goal was to better understand the interactions between the pain-sensing neurons and their associated glial cells which are found in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG). Toll-like receptor-4 (TLR4) is located on glial cells of the spinal cord and is involved in maintaining chronic pain in animal models of nerve injury. We have shown that sensory neurons are the major cell type in the DRG which express TLR4 and are responsive to TLR4 stimuli. Our results suggest that when the sensory neurons lose their intimate contact with their glial cells after nerve injury, these glial cells become super-responsive to TLR4 stimuli. Therefore, any circumstances which release that inhibitory tone normally exerted by healthy neurons will lead to excessive inflammatory reactions within the DRG which will make the neurons even more sensitive to painful stimuli. From this research project, we now have a better understanding of the interactions between DRG neurons and glial cells, and can start to consider how best to manipulate this system to provide improved pain control.

477110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
477110.value: The aim of this project is to determine the prevalence of food allergy and the possible associated risk factors in children from urban and rural areas of China. There have been increasing concerns about the problems of IgE mediated food allergies in many developed countries, especially among patients and their families, schools, food producers, government officials, and policy makers. Food allergy is a disease affecting all age groups and the only preventive treatment is still avoidance of the offending food. Because of the constant fear and anxiety of a severe or even fatal reaction especially when the patients are eating outside of their home, their quality of life is significantly affected. The understanding of the epidemiology and risk factors of food allergy is important in order to develop possible preventive strategies to help sufferers with this condition. Such information is important for clinicians, allergic consumers, policy makers, together with the food industry to effectively manage the problem of food allergies. In the past, we have performed large-scaled epidemiology studies of asthma and allergies using standardized method in Hong Kong and mainland China. Random samples of school children will be recruited from three locations. We propose to determine the prevalence of food allergy in three populations of Chinese schoolchildren using a standardized and internationally accepted protocol. Reliable data of food allergy will be obtained as objective markers of IgE mediated food allergy will be measured. If supported, this will be the first population based study to determine the prevalence of food allergy in Chinese schoolchildren from both the urban and rural settings and to evaluate the possible risk and protective factors of food allergy in Chinese children. The findings will provide directions of future research in the determination of the aetiology of food allergy. 這個項目的目的是確定食物過敏的患病率及可能來自城市兒童和中國農村地區的相關危險因素。食物過敏是一種影響所有年齡組別的疾病，唯一的預防方法仍是避免有問題的食品。由於持續的恐懼和焦慮或嚴重致命的反應，使他們的生活質數有著的明顯影響，尤其是外出膳食。為制定可行的預防方法幫助患者，了解的流行病學和食物過敏危險因素是重要的。這些資料對臨床醫師、患過敏症的消費者、市場策劃者、以及食品工業是非常重要的，能幫助他們有效管理食物過敏的問題。我們建議於中國地區三個年齡組別的學童，使用規範化和國際公認的協議，去確定食物過敏患病率，數據結果將作未來研究的方向，測定食物過敏的原因。

477110.label: Realisation of objectives
477110.value: According to the plan of our research protocol and power calculation, we have successfully recruited adequate random samples of school children from three locations- Hong Kong, Guangzhou (urban) and Shaoguan (rural). A total of 16,875 children aged 6-11 years from these three locations were screening for the presence of possible food allergies as planned. In addition, we have also invite collaboration from investigators in Beijing to screen children from both urban and rural Beijing. A total of 10,672 children from Beijing were screened using the identical internationally validated protocol. The overall response was excellent at 93%. A total of 1866 children have been recruited for the second phase of the study as planned accordingly to our protocol. Skin-prick tests (SPT) and assessment of serum specific IgE have been performed in these children. We were able to achieve the objectives of determining the prevalence of parents' reported food allergy and the prevalence of serum specific IgE against the different foods of the recruited subjects (Objectives # I and #2). The pattern of food allergens in our population was very different from those reported in Caucasians in developed countries. The most common food allergen was shrimp (1.04% in Hong Kong). Peanut allergy was practically non-existent in mainland China. Our results have also confirmed the much higher prevalence of suspected food allergy, allergic sensitization among children recruited from urban environments. Furthermore, we also documented the protective effect associated with previous infection with hepatitis A. Therefore, the most important protective factors against the development of food allergy and allergic sensitization against food allergens were living in the rural environment and past infections of Hepatitis A (Objective #3). Our analysis of children recruited from Hong Kong revealed that one of the major factors affecting the subsequent prevalence of food allergies was the place of birth. Those born and raised in Hong Kong had a prevalence of l.7% while the rate for those born in China and migrate to Hong Kong was much lower at 0.37% (Objective #3). We have established the methods of double-blind placebo-controlled food challenge for possible shrimp allergy according to the standardized Europrevall protocol. All subjects with reported symptoms and evidence of sensitization against shrimp underwent the standardized protocol and our results confirmed that approximately 50% of these children were confirmed to have true shrimp allergy. Therefore, the prevalence of challenge-proven shrimp allergy in the Hong Kong school children was found to be 0.5% while it was less than 0.1% in rural China (objective #4). In summary, we were able to achieve all the 4 objectives as described in our protocol. These results were presented in two international meetings (abstracts attached). In addition, one paper has been published on-line with our date comparing with those from European countries.

477110.label: Major findings and research outcome
477110.value: We have successfully recruited very large random samples of school children from three locations- Hong Kong, Guangzhou (urban) and Shaoguan (rural). In addition, we have also expanded our collaboration with investigators from Beijing to screen children from both urban and rural Beijing. A total of 10,672 children from Beijing were screened using the identical internationally validated protocol. Our results confirmed the marked differences of food allergies and food specific allergic sensitization among the recruited children. In particular, children from the rural regions have much lower prevalence of food allergies. Furthermore, orofecal infections such as Hepatitis A are associated with protection in the Chinese children. The findings have been presented in two meetings and published in one paper (Pediatric Allergy and Immunology, online Dec 2013). Furthermore, our analysis of children recruited from Hong Kong revealed that one of the major factors affecting the subsequent prevalence of food allergies was the place of fifth. Those born and raised in Hong Kong had a prevalence of 1.7% while the rate for those born in China and migrate to Hong Kong was much lower at 0.37%. This finding suggests that exposures in early life have long lasting effects in reducing subsequent development of sensitization and food allergy. With regards to the food challenge test for subjects with possible shrimp allergy, we confirmed that only half of those subjects with the relevant symptoms and evidence of sensitization indeed had true shrimp allergy. This is of great clinical importance as we cannot rely solely on symptoms and sensitization to make the diagnosis. We are currently analyzing the results using component-resolved-diagnostics to evaluate which specific allergens may predict true allergy in these patients. The eventual goal is to reduce the number of challenge test as it is rather expansive and time-consuming.

477110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
477110.value: The findings of our study were of great interest. In particular, we have used a validated and standardized protocol to determine the prevalence of food allergy and allergic sensitization. This will be the baseline set of data for future comparison. Furthermore, it is very clear that the rural environment and past infection with Hepatitis A virus confer protection against the development of food allergy. It is highly likely that there are specific factors in the rural environment which may modulate the early immune system and prevent future development of allergies. Exposure to microbes is likely to be an important factor as we have documented to protective effects of Hepatitis A in China. We have been successful in obtaining another grant from the European Union and National Science Foundation of China to study environmental exposure and determine how these exposures may affect the early immune system. If we are able to identify, the protective exposure and the underlying mechanisms, we will be able to develop primary preventive strategies for the prevention of allergies.

477110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
477110.value: This was the first large-scale comparative study of food allergy in the Chinese population with subjects from both urban and rural environment. The results demonstrated that Chinese children from urban environment had higher prevalence of food allergies and the pattern of food allergies in Chinese is very different from those documented in Caucasians. Environmental exposures in early life are likely to play significant roles as those children born in China with subsequent migration to Hong Kong are protected from the development of food allergies compared to those born and raised in Hong Kong. Furthermore, infections in early life (Hepatitis A) may confer protection against the development of food allergy. As the genetic backgrounds of all recruited subjects are similar, the marked differences in the manifestations of food allergies are likely to be the results of modifiable environmental exposure factors. It is important to understand these factors and the underlying mechanisms of protection. The eventual goal to develop primary preventive strategies by mimicking such exposures.
