477410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
477410.value: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized with breakdown of cartilage. Hypomineralization of subchondral bone plate is also recently shown to involve in pathogenesis of OA. This seriously affects the quality of life of these patients. More than 27 millions people in USA suffered from this disease in 2005. In Hong Kong, 3% of the population was OA patients in 2003. Unfortunately, there is currently no effective clinical treatment to manage OA. Physical activity is an alternative recommended measures for early OA patients to reduce pain and improve functions, with evidence-based support from a few randomized controlled trials. Passive continuous motion was also shown to have superior outcomes for those patients with deep cartilage defects transplanted by autologous periosteum. Low-magnitude high-frequency vibration (LMHFV) treatment is a non-invasive biophysical intervention to provide whole-body vibration stimulation, which can be used as quantifiable physical activities. Its reported biological effects include osteogenicity, blood flow enhancement and muscle gain. Its effects on OA have not been reported yet. Previous studies of vibration on chondrocytes showed the increased proliferation, matrix production and hence resultant biomechanical properties in 3D culture. This proves the direct interaction of vibration on articular cartilage. Our previous studies using LMHFV on fractured rats confirmed the signal transmission to the thigh of rats and the results indicated that LMHFV enhanced cartilage formation with endochondral ossification-related genes upregulated and improved bone mineral density. The application of vibration at 35Hz, 0.3g is now being translated to clinical application. To study mechanical stimulation on OA, we had also applied acoustic mechanical stimulus on OA rabbit model, demonstrating that OA cartilage responded with reparative activity by producing hyaline cartilage while control samples were healed with only fibrocartilage or fibrous tissues. Based on these related studies, we hypothesize that mechanical stimulation by LMHFV enhances and maintains cartilage repair and underlying subchondral bone density for early OA. With our established techniques, we will make use of OA rats to evaluate the effect of LMHFV on the repair of OA cartilage and the changes in subchondral bone plate. To date, this is the first study to evaluate the effect of LMHFV on OA and subchondral bone. The findings of this study will help to understand the response of OA cartilage to mechanical stimulation and to investigate whether LMHFV is beneficial to joints with early OA, which may be a potential clinical treatment for OA patients. 骨關節炎是一種以軟骨破壞為特徵的退行性關節病變。近期研究顯示，軟骨下骨礦質過少參與了其發病機制。該症嚴重影響患者的生活品質。2005年，美國骨關節炎患者逾兩千七百萬人。2003年，香港有3%的人口罹患此症。遺憾的是，針對骨關節炎，臨床上目前尚無有效的治療方案。 一些基於隨機對照試驗的循證研究表明，運動可推薦作為治療早期骨關節炎的一項選擇措施，以減輕疼痛，改善功能。針對自體骨膜移植治療深部軟骨缺損的患者，被動持續運動亦顯示出良好療效。 作為一項非侵入性生物物理干預手段，低振幅高頻率振動(LMHFV)可提供全身振動刺激，用以實現定量化的機體運動。根據現有資料，LMHFV具備骨生成、促進血供、增強肌力等生物效能，然其對骨關節炎的作用至今尚無報道。既往針對軟骨細胞的3D培養顯示，振動可促進軟骨細胞增殖與細胞外基質的生成，從而提高其生物機械性能。該研究證實振動對關節軟骨具有直接影響。我們前期關於骨折大鼠的研究表明，LMHFV可將刺激信號傳遞至大鼠大腿，通過上調軟骨內成骨相關基因的表達，促進軟骨形成，並有效提升骨密度。現今，35Hz、0.3g振動方案已投入臨床應用。為了探討機械刺激對骨關節炎的作用，我們採用相同刺激強度作用於家兔骨關節炎模型，結果顯示，骨關節炎軟骨通過生成透明軟骨產生修復反應，而對照組僅以纖維軟骨或纖維組織的形式癒合。 基於如上相關研究，我們假設：低振幅高頻率振動可促進早期骨關節炎患者的軟骨修復，維持軟骨下骨的骨密度。依據已建立的技術，我們擬採用骨關節炎大鼠模型，來評估LMHFV對骨關節炎軟骨修復及軟骨下骨改變的影響。迄今為止，該項目是首次關於LMHFV對骨關節炎與軟骨下骨作用的研究。其結果將有助於闡明骨關節炎軟骨對機械刺激的反應，並瞭解LMHFV是否利於早期骨關節炎患者關節的康復。這將為骨關節炎的臨床治療提供一項潛在的治療方案。

477410.label: Realisation of objectives
477410.value: Six months old female Sprague Dawley rats received ACLT on right hind knee. They were randomly divided into two groups (Treatment and control) when OA was developed after 12 weeks. The treatment group received LMHFV (35 Hz, 0.3 g) treatment for 20 min/day and 5 days/week, while the rats of control group were placed on the same platform without vibration with the same regime. After 6, 12 and 18 weeks, 6 rats of each group were sacrificed at each time point and the right hind knee was harvested. OA grading score, content of aggrecan and collagen II in cartilage, distal femur cartilage volume (CV), subchondral bone morphology, elastic modulus of cartilage and functional changes between groups were analyzed respectively. For Objective 1: Negative effect of LMHFV on osteoarthritic cartilage repair was observed. LMHFV treatment caused more severe cartilage breakage, as demonstrated by loss of safranin O stained proteoglycan and decrease of cartilage thickness. The histological score of vibration group was significantly higher than control group, indicating more severe OA in vibration group. The pattern of histological score changes between groups over time also showed significant difference, confirming the faster cartilage deterioration in vibration group. For Objective 2: Histological study showed more severe cartilage breakage and faster cartilage deterioration in vibration group. Morphology study by micro-CT showed cartilage volume increased after LMHFV treatment, which may be caused by edema. Immunohistochemistry showed no difference of the aggrecan content and collagen II in cartilage between groups. Elastography study by high-resolution ultrasound microscopy showed no difference of the ultrasound roughness index and integrated reflection coefficient between groups. Elastic modulus by indentation test of cartilage in medial tibia plateau showed an increasing trend without significant difference after vibration treatment, revealing the potential loss of cartilage elasticity. For Objective 3: Morphological study by micro-CT found subchondral bone plate density was significantly increased along with OA progress in both groups. Distal femur epiphyseal bone quality was significantly improved by LMHFV treatment with increased bone fraction, bone number and decreased porosity.

477410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
477410.value: (1) This study demonstrated LMHFV induced cartilage breakage and function deterioration in ACLT induced OA rat model. To better understand the etiology of OA under mechanical loading, detailed mechanism of molecular regulation protein such as transforming growth factor β, insulin-like growth factor, interleukin (IL)-1, IL-6 and prostaglandin E2 translation pathway during this process should be investigated in further study. (2) LMHFV showed positive effects on protecting distal femur epiphyseal bone loss, while the underlying mechanism and its relationship with OA progression should be studied in the future. (3) This study observed LMHFV accelerated OA progress in ACLT induced unstable knee joint. This finding raises our attention on the precautions for clinical application of LMHFV on OA patients with unstable joint. Clinically, most OA patients have stable knee joints and therefore the current data may be restricted to those with unstable joints; in other words, the animal model may not be most suitable to reflect general clinical situation. Future study should focus on the effect of LMHFV on a stable knee joint OA model, such as spontaneous OA animal model, to better know the effects of LMHFV on OA in general elderly.

477410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
477410.value: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a major cause of disability in elderly population but there is no promising treatment clinically. Studies found mechanical stimulation shows some beneficial effects on OA without a solid conclusion. Low-magnitude high-frequency vibration (LMHFV) treatment is a non-invasive biophysical modality to provide a systemic mechanical stimulation to musculoskeletal system. Previous animal and clinical studies of our group found that LMHFV could enhance muscle functions, prevent osteoporosis and promote fracture healing. This study evaluated the effects of LMHFV on cartilage and subchondral bone in anterior cruciate ligament transection-induced OA rat model. Severer cartilage degradation and worse functional results were observed after LMHFV treatment. In contrast, distal femur epiphyseal bone quality was improved by LMHFV treatment with increased bone fraction, bone number and decreased porosity. The findings of this study help us understand the effect of vibration treatment on cartilage and subchondral bone in OA with unstable joints. Although the efficacy of vibration on bone is promising, precautions should be taken for the OA patients with joint instability clinically. Future studies should be focused on those spontaneous OA with stable joints that is more clinically prevalent.

477610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
477610.value: Breaking down of bacterial cells, resulting in releases of dissolved organic materials, is an essential process in water disinfection. These bacterial biomolecules can be potentially hazardous to consumers because they can react with disinfectants to form unwanted chemicals, known as disinfection byproducts (DBPs). Over 600 DBPs have been identified but they only represent less than half of DBPs existed in finished water. Notably, most of them are considered carcinogenic and mutagenic. Adding disinfections is an essential step in modern drinking water treatment in order to inactivate waterborne pathogens. Unfortunately, the optimal disinfection condition that balances the risk between microbial and DBP contaminations for safe drinking water is never defined. Different disinfectants have been tested to maximize bacterial disinfection while to minimize the formation of DBPs in finished water. However, their focuses are on reactions between disinfectants and natural organic matter from terrestrial sources, such as humic and fulvic acids. Few studies have evaluated the DBP formation from the microbiological point of view and have correlated the DBP formation with bacterial disinfection. In particular, bacterial organic matters usually have a low carbon to nitrogen ratio and can be a precursor of highly toxic nitrogenous DBPs found in finished water, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine, chloropicrin, haloacetonitriles, Warm and moist environments in pipeline, water tap, and showerhead in the water distribution system are prone to the formation of biofilms and the growth of microorganisms. Residual disinfectant is usually maintained during water conveyance to the consumers. This effect of residual disinfectants on the biofilm in the distribution is rarely getting attention. The formation of DBPs in the distribution system should not be ignored. We propose a 3-year study, under controlled laboratory environments, to evaluate the contributions of bacteria disinfection on the DBP formation. This pioneering work will examine the kinetics and mechanisms of both bacterial disinfection and DBP formation at the same time and will identify the optimal disinfectant dosage to achieve the most effective bacterial disinfection while minimize reactions of disinfectants with bacterial organic matters to form DBPs. In addition to the commonly used disinfectants, we are particularly interested in water disinfection by photocatalytic oxidation, which is a chemically free and environmental friendly technology. The aim of this proposed project is to identify the optimal disinfection conditions that prevents transmission of infections disease while minimizes the formation of DBPs in finished drinking water. 飲用水處理中，消毒劑氯、氯胺以及臭氧儘管具有滅活水源性病原體的優點，但它們會與水體中某些成分反應形成一類致癌致突變物質即消毒副產物（DBPs）。微生物和DPB威脅飲用水安全之間的風險平衡對水處理工程師和環境微生物學家來說，是一項巨大的挑戰。目前，已有大量關於減少DBP形成的研究，但它們的重點多放在消毒劑與源水中腐植質的反應上。很少有研究從微生物的角度出發來評估DBP的形成並將其與細菌消毒過程聯繫起來。 細胞壁解體導致溶解性有機物的釋放，這是水體消毒的一個重要過程。一般來說，這類細菌類有機物含氮量豐富，分子量比腐殖質小，它們反應形成DBPs的過程卻從未被研究過。這類細胞生物分子對消費者來說具有潛在毒性，能同樣成為與消毒劑反應的消毒副產物前體形成未受管制的含氮消毒副產物，如三硝基甲苯、鹵乙腈及其他未被鑒定的DBPs。重要的是，飲用水布水系統中管道、水龍頭及淋浴花灑裡溫暖濕潤的環境更易於生物膜的形成和促進微生物的生長。因此，我們不能忽視飲用水出水中因細菌消毒過程而形成的含氮DBPs。 我們提出了一個3年的研究計畫，並在控制實驗室環境中評估水處理過程中細胞類物質對DBP形成的貢獻。這項開創新的工作將分析得出細菌消毒和同時形成DBP的動力學機制，並將確定出最適宜的消毒劑劑量，以達到最佳細菌消毒效果並在最大程度上降低消毒劑與細菌類有機物反應形成DBP的可能。除了常見的消毒劑外，我們還對一種化學自由、環境友好的消毒技術：光催化氧化特別感興趣。此項研究的目的是：為水處理工程師和微生物學家提供可借鑒的資料，以找到最有效的消毒工藝，防止傳染性疾病的蔓延，並降低飲用水出水中DBP的形成。

477610.label: Realisation of objectives
477610.value: There are six objectives as stated in Section 5.2. Generally we had completed all the tasks and objectives stated in the proposal. For the formation potential of biomolecules and other precursors of DBPs (Objective 1), we had examined a variety of sources of DBP precursors including terrestrial organic matter (Chow et al., 2011) and bacterial organic materials (Wang et al., 2012) on DBP formation during chlorination. Results showed nitrogen-rich organic matters can cause a greater formation of nitrogenous DBP in finished water. For the toxicity of DBPs (Objective 2), toxicity effects of selected DBPs such as THMs were evaluated using as carcinogen risk assessment in marine animal. Specific results of the study indicate the feed source in addition DOC in water lead to sharp increase of DPBs, which propose unexpected health risk. For the cell lysis under different disinfection processes (Objective 3), we examined bacterial inactivation and DBP formation from different phenotypes (i.e. biofilm at maturation stage and planktonic cell at stationary stage) of bacterial cells. Results were reported in the article published in Water Research (Wang et al., 2013). Regarding the end point (Objective 4) and optimal treatment conditions (Objective 5), our team had examined efficacies of chlorination, chloramination, photo-Fenton reaction, and TiO2/UV photocatalytic oxidation on Escherichia coli K12 and Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 inactivation and DBP formation, and suggested sets of considerations in water treatments in order to achieve most efficient bacterial inactivation while minimize DBP formation. Details of the findings can be found in the M.Sc. thesis at Clemson University, entitled “Comparisons of Bacterial Inactivation Efficiency and DBP formation from Four Different Disinfection Processes” (Li et al., 2014) and an article published in Journal of Photochemistry & Photobiology A: Chemistry (Ng et al., 2014). For the effects of biofilm on DBP formation (Objective 6), biofilms grew on polyvinyl chloride and galvanized zone as two common types of pipeline materials were examined. Results demonstrated that pipeline materials can affect DBP formation during bacterial disinfection. Results were also reported in Water Research (Wang et al. 2013).

477610.label: Major findings and research outcome
477610.value: A total of 7 articles were published in top-tier peer review journals in the field. The HKRGC research grant supported research activities of graduate students from the South China University of Technology of China and the Clemson University of USA. Two graduate stduents from the South China University of Technology, each worked at CUHK for 6 months, while one gradaute student from the Clemson University worked at CUHK for 12 months on this project (see Section 10 for the details). Majoring findings are summarized as follows: (1) Bacterial organic matter as a nitrogenous disinfection byproduct precursor: Chow et al. (2011) & Wang et al (2012) demonstrated that bacterial organic matter could be an important source of disinfection byproducts (DBPs) in finished water, particularly nitrogenous DBPs (N-DBPs). A greater reactivity in forming N-DBP from bacterial organic matter comparing with those of humic acid and fulvic acids. The N-DBP formation is correlated with the C/N ratio of dissolved organic matter (DOM). DOM with low C/N ratio (i.e. greater N content) has a greater reactivity in forming haloacetonitrile during water chlorination. (2) DBP formation from pipeline’s biofilm: Wang et al. (2013) showed planktonic cells formed 7-11 times greater trihalomethanes/carbon than those from biofilms but significantly lower chloral hydrate, highlighting the bacterial phenotype’s impact on the DBP formation from bacterial organic matter. Pipe material appeared to affect the DBP formation when chlorine reacting with biofilm, with 4-28% lower bromine incorporation factor for biofilms on polyvinyl chloride compared to that on galvanized zinc. (3) Dosage and pH effects: Li (2014) on her master thesis demonstrated that an increase of disinfectant dosage generally improves bacterial inactivation efficiency but it could also increase DBP formation. Her research also showed that a higher bacterial inactivation efficacy with lower DBP formation could be achieved in a slightly acidic condition. Results suggested that the risks of DBPs and bacterial contamination in finished water can be reduced through efficient operational conditions. (4) DOM affects bacterial inactivation Ng et al. (2014) observed that DOM could either be a photosensitizer or an inhibitor on bacterial inactivation in photo Fenton treatment, depending on sources and characteristics of DOM. Potential determining factors on the functionality of DOM during water treatment could be carbonyl and carboxyl contents and molecular weight. In addition, Li (2014) showed DOM increased chlorine consumption and protect bacteria from inactivation during water chlorination.

477610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
477610.value: Disinfection byproducts (DBPs) formation during Escherichia coli K12 and Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 inactivation from chlorination, chloramination, photo-Fenton reaction, and TiO2/UV photocatalytic oxidation were examined. Among these 4 disinfection methods, chlorination is the most rapid and effective treatment but it can react with microbial organic matter and generates various DBPs including THM, HAN, and CHD. Chloramination is a good alternative disinfection method with good inactivation efficiency in a relatively short time and limited amounts DPBs formed. However, formation of emerging DBPs such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) could be of health concern in chloramination. Comparing with the conventional disinfection methods, the AOPs (i.e., photo-Fenton reaction and TiO2/UV photocatalytic oxidation) can achieve high efficiency in bacterial inactivation and DBP formation. However, longer reaction times are required in these AOP processes. A higher inactivation efficacy with less DBP formation could be achieved in a slightly acidic condition. Results suggested that the risks of DBPs and bacterial contamination in finished water can be reduced through by slightly lower water pH during water disinfection. Noticeably, AOPs could be promising inactivation methods for drinking water treatments because of their high inactivation efficiencies and no/less DBP formation.

477610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
477610.value: Water treatment efficacy of two conventional disinfection processes (chlorination and chloramination) and two advanced oxidation processes (AOPs, photo-Fenton reaction and TiO2/UV photocatalytic oxidation) were examined in the 42-months project. The major findings are: (1) bacterial organics matters are crucial for DPBs formation in chlorination, (2) less DBPs formed in chlorination process under acidic condition, (3) AOPs are good alternative disinfection process, (4) Pipe materials affect disinfectant interaction with biofilm bacteria, and (5) DOM has dual role in enhancing and inhibiting bacterial inactivation in Photo-Fenton reaction. Based on the above findings, the research team would like to recommend the following conditions for more effective bacterial disinfection and less DPBs formation in microbial disinfection. These conditions are: (1) to balance between efficiency of bacterial inactivation and DPB formation in different process are crucial for effective disinfection, (2) to slight acidify the water sample before conducting chlorination, (3) to replace chlorination/chloramantion by AOPs (photo-Fenton reaction and TiO2/UV photocatalytic oxidation), and (4) to use PVC pipes to replace galvanized zinc pipes for chlorination of biofilm bacteria.

477710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
477710.value: 非酒精性脂肪肝是最常見的慢性肝病之一。在亞洲，約15％至40％的成年人口患有脂肪肝。 脂肪肝可分為單純脂肪肝與非酒精性脂肪肝炎(NASH)，後者的死亡率明顯上升。 NASH可發展到肝硬化，肝衰竭和肝癌。所以，診斷NASH對預後和治療具有重要意義。 目前，肝組織是診斷 NASH的黃金標準。然而，這是一種侵入性程序，不是所有患者都能接受。常規影像學檢查如超聲波掃描可以檢測脂肪肝，但不能判斷肝損傷的程度。所以，我們必須發展脂肪肝炎的無創測試。 磁力共振光譜的是一種非侵入性技術，提供肝臟功能狀態的信息。肝損傷後再生過程中，細胞膜和能量會出現變化。我們試驗了24個病例，發現NASH患者有獨特的光譜特徵。 有NASH的病人有較高 phosphomonoester對無機磷的比例和γ- ATP水平下降。該數據表明，磁力共振光譜有潛質成為非酒精性脂肪肝炎的無創測試。 我們計劃驗證磁力共振光譜分辨單純脂肪肝與NASH的準確性。此外，我們也將比較兩個血清標誌物-細胞角蛋白18片段和脂肪細胞脂肪酸結合蛋白(AFABP)-在單純脂肪肝與NASH的濃度。細胞角蛋白18片段是一個細胞凋亡的標記，AFABP影響脂肪酸代謝及胰島素抵抗。 本研究結果可提供新的非酒精性脂肪肝炎無創測試，以評估脂肪肝患者的風險。

477710.label: Realisation of objectives
477710.value: Objective 1: Phosphorus-magnetic resonance spectroscopy (P-MRS) was performed in 151 subjects. Patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) had increased [PME+PDE]/TP and PDE/TP. Among patients with NAFLD, those with steatohepatitis (NASH) had decreased total ATP/TP and alpha-ATP/TP. The observation is in line with the knowledge that NASH is associated with oxidative stress and cell energy depletion. Overall, the P-MRS parameters had an area under the receiver-operating characteristics curve (AUROC) of around 0.7 in diagnosing NASH. Objective 2: Serum cytokeratin-18 fragments (CK-18) and adipocyte fatty acid-binding protein (AFABP) were measured in 146 NAFLD patients and 74 controls. Since the diagnostic accuracy of AFABP was relatively low, we added testing of fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21), which regulates lipid oxidation and glucose metabolism. A combination of CK-18 and FGF-21 achieved 74% positive predictive value and 82% negative predictive value for diagnosing NASH. CK-18 M30 reflects hepatocyte apoptosis. Recent data suggest that CK-18 M65, a marker of total cell death, may have superior diagnostic accuracy. As such, we performed CK-18 M65 testing on the same group of patients. While the overall diagnostic accuracy of the M30 and M65 assays for NASH was similar, we found that rising M65 level over time was associated with fibrosis progression in 51 patients with paired liver biopsies. Objective 3: 132 NAFLD patients underwent both P-MRS and serum biomarker testing. 95 patients had NASH. Among 20 patients with CK-18 <203 U/L and normal P-MRS features, only 3 had NASH (negative predictive value 85%). In contrast, among 16 patients with CK-18 >670 U/L and abnormal P-MRS features, 14 had NASH (positive predictive value 88%).

477710.label: Major findings and research outcome
477710.value: As highlighted in section 5.3, P-MRS and the serum biomarkers under evaluation all have moderate accuracy in diagnosing NASH, with AUROC of up to 0.7 when used as standalone tests. It is possible to combine 2 biomarkers or 1 biomarker and P-MRS using a 2-step approach. In that case, the main advantage is further improvement in the positive predictive value and negative predictive value for the diagnosis of NASH. When both tests concur with each other, the confidence of the diagnosis is increased. The results of this project led to 3 full papers in peer-reviewed journals and 2 oral presentations in leading conferences in digestive and liver diseases. One PhD candidate was also trained.

477710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
477710.value: The serum biomarkers and P-MRS were validated against liver histology. In the future, the important question is whether these tests may be used to monitor treatment effects and predict hard clinical outcomes such as cirrhotic complications and hepatocellular carcinoma. All patients recruited in this project will be prospectively followed up at the clinic and monitored for liver-related complications. Besides, P-MRS and serum collection have been performed for patients in some of the NAFLD clinical trials at our center. Correlation in patients with paired liver biopsies will be evaluated.

477710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
477710.value: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) currently affects 27% of the Hong Kong adult population. However, only 10-20% of NAFLD patients have steatohepatitis (NASH), the active form of disease that may result in cirrhosis and liver cancer. Previously, the diagnosis of NASH relied mainly on liver biopsy, which is an invasive procedure. In this project, we tested the use of 5 blood tests and magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) as non-invasive tests of NASH. When used alone, the blood test cytokeratin-18 fragment and MRS have the highest accuracy in diagnosing NASH. Combination of blood tests or combination of 1 blood test and MRS can further improve disease prediction. Overall, such test combinations can reduce the need for liver biopsy by around 30%, with a confidence of diagnosis of around 80%. These tests have the potential to be applied at the clinic to streamline the assessment of NAFLD patients.

478110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
478110.value: There is now a global epidemic of diabetes. These silent conditions independently and collectively contribute to 50% of all causes of death mainly due to cardiovascular and renal complications. Fundamental to the development of diabetes is pancreatic  cell secretory failure. Understanding the mechanisms by which  cell function decline within the setting of lipid over-supply, is pivotal to understanding the pathogenesis of diabetes. The incretin effect is defined as enhanced insulin secretion after oral versus intravenous glucose administration due to the insulinotropic effect of the gastrointestinal hormones Glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), which has been extensively studied in type 2 diabetes. In most studies, plasma GIP levels after meals have been found to be normal in type 2 diabetes while GLP-1 levels were modestly reduced. In addition, patients with type 2 diabetes have abnormal responses to action of incretin hormones, particularly GIP, which when infused has almost no effect upon insulin secretion. Although the effects of GLP-1 are partially preserved in type 2 diabetes, which is important for its therapeutic potential, insulin responses are substantially reduced in these subjects compared to normal controls, at comparable plasma glucose levels. Both GLP-1 and GIP receptors are expressed in pancreatic -cells. Thus, it is plausible that impairment of the incretin effect may occur at the receptor level in pancreatic -cells. Apart from sequence variants in the coding region which may alter the structure or expression of these receptors, downregulation by acquired conditions such as gluco- and lipotoxicity are possible explanations for incretin resistance in type 2 diabetes. To date, no genetic variations have been reported for the GLP-1 and GIP receptors, thus it remains plausible that expression of these receptors may be dysregulated especially in the presence of gluco- and lipotoxicity. We recently reported reduced expression of GLP-1 and GIP receptors in -cells in diabetic hyperglycemic rats with impaired insulin secretion capacity. However, it remains uncertain whether similar changes may occur under hyperlipidemia conditions. In this proposal, we aim to explore the role of free fatty acid on the expression of GLP-1 and GIP receptors and functional consequences in terms of insulin secretion using both in vivo and in vitro experiments. 478110.label: Realisation of objectives
478110.value: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is associated with reduced incretin effects. Though previous studies showed that hyperglycemia contributes to the impaired incretin responses in beta cells, how hyperlipidemia, another feature of diabetes, contributes to impaired glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) response is largely unknown. In this study, we investigated the effects of free fatty acids (FFAs) on incretin receptor expression and their signaling. We further examined the glucose-lowering efficacy of incretin-based drugs in combination with the lipid-lowering agent bezafibrate. We found that palmitate treatment decreased GLP-1 receptor (Glp1r) expression in rodent insulinoma cell lines and islets isolated from diabetic db/db mice (specific aim 1, 2). This was associated with impaired GLP-1 stimulated cAMP production, phosphorylation of cAMP-responsive elements binding protein (CREB), and insulin secretion. Expression of exogenous Glp1r restored the cAMP production and the phosphorylation of CREB (specific aim 2 and 3). Treatment with bezafibrate in combination with des-fluorositagliptin or exendin-4 produced more robust glycemic control associated with improved islet morphology and beta cell mass in db/db mice (specific aim 1, 2, 3). We conclude that elevated FFAs contribute to impaired responsiveness to GLP-1 partially through down-regulation of GLP1R expression and its signaling. Improvements in lipid control in diabetic mouse models increases the efficacy of incretin-based therapy. Our studies contributed to the development of incretin-based therapy for the treatment of diabetes.

478110.value: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is associated with reduced incretin effects. Although previous studies have shown that hyperglycaemia contributes to impaired incretin responses in beta cells, it is largely unknown how hyperlipidaemia, another feature of type 2 diabetes, contributes to impaired glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) response. Here, we investigated the effects of NEFA on incretin receptor signalling. We further examined the glucose-lowering efficacy of incretin-based drugs in combination with the lipid-lowering agent bezafibrate. We used db/db mice to examine the in vivo efficacy of the treatment. Beta cell lines and mouse islets were used to examine GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide receptor signalling. Palmitate treatment decreased Glp1r expression in rodent insulinoma cell lines and isolated islets. This was associated with impairment of the following: GLP-1- stimulated cAMP production, phosphorylation of cAMPresponsive elements binding protein (CREB) and insulin secretion. In insulinoma cell lines, the expression of exogenous Glp1r restored cAMP production and the phosphorylation of CREB. Treatment with bezafibrate in combination with des-fluoro-sitagliptin or exendin-4 led to more robust glycaemic control, associated with improved islet morphology and beta cell mass in db/db mice. Conclusions/interpretation Elevated NEFA contributes to impaired responsiveness to GLP-1, partially through downregulation of GLP-1 receptor signalling. Improvements in lipid control in mouse models of obesity and diabetes increase the efficacy of incretin-based therapy.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
478110.value: The incretin hormones glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide are secreted by enteroendocrine cells and augment glucose-induced insulin secretion in response to food ingestion in a glucose dependent manner. This mechanism forms the basis for incretin-based therapies in type 2 diabetes. However, the insulinotropic effect of incretins is diminished in type 2 diabetic patients, due in part to reduced expression of incretin receptors as a consequence of glucotoxicity. In this study, we provide evidence that in addition to glucotoxicity, lipotoxicity also affects incretin receptor expression and signalling in insulin-secreting cells and isolated islets. In animal models of diabetes, we show that co-administration of a lipid-lowering drug with a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor or a glucagonlike peptide-1 agonist improved glucose tolerance and beta cell mass. These novel findings provide convincing support for the notion that restoring normal circulating lipid levels in type 2 diabetes might help improve the efficacy of incretin-based therapies.

478710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
478710.value: TRP channels function as cellular sensors to perceive and respond to many environmental stimuli including temperature, taste, mechanical pressure, osmolarity, pain and pheromones. Several TRP isoforms, including TRPC1, -C5, -C6, -V1, -V2, and -A1, have been suggested to be involved in mechanosensation. In the preliminary studies, we found that TRPC5 forms hypotonicity- and membrane stretch-activated channels in TRPC5-overexpressing human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK) cells and Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells. These data are consistent with the report from another group. We then explored the functional role of TRPC5-related channels in the mechanosensation of aortic arch baroreceptor. Aortic arch baroreceptor is one of key mechanosensors that serve to detect arterial blood pressure. The overall function of aortic arch baroreceptor is to maintain the blood pressure relatively constant. In immunohistochemical studies, it was found that TRPC5 is abundantly expressed in the soma of aortic arch baroreceptor neurons, the axon of baroreceptor nerve, and the sensory terminals of aortic arch baroreceptor. More importantly, we found that hypotonicity-induced Ca2+ influx in the primary cultured aortic arch baroreceptor neurons was markedly reduced by a TRPC5-blocking antibody T5E3 and by a dominant-negative TRPC5 construct TRPC5-DN. Single channel patch clamp also recorded a stretch-activated cation channel in cultured baroreceptor neurons. The activity of the channels was also blocked by T5E3 and TRPC5-DN. These data suggest an important functional role of TRPC5-related channels in baroreceptor mechanosensing. In the present proposal, we plan to further explore the mechanosensitive nature of TRPC5-related channels in aortic arch baroreceptor neurons, to characterize the electrophysiological and pharmacological properties of the channels. We also plan to explore the functional role of TRPC5 in blood pressure sensing and in blood pressure control in living animals. We expect this study to provide crucial information on baroreceptor mechanosensing. The results from this study should fill a key knowledge gap in the basic understanding of blood pressure control in mammals. 瞬时受体电位通道（Transient receptor potential channels, TRP channels)是细胞对外界环境的感受器. 它参与感受温度、渗透压、机械力、味觉等各种刺激。TRP通道含多种亚型. 有些亚型参与机械力的感受, 其中包括TRPC1, -C6, -V1, -V2, and -A1. 在初步实验中, 我们发现TRPC5能参与感受渗透压及细胞膜上的牵张力. 我们也发现TRPC5蛋白大量地表达于胸主动脉中的血压感受器上. 胸主动脉中的血压感受器是人体的主要血压感受器之一. 它的主要功能是维持血压的稳定. 在本项目研究中, 我们会致力于研究TRPC5在主动脉中的血压感受器的功能. 我们也会对在神经细胞中TRPC5做进一步的电生理学和药理学水平的研究. 此项研究对了解血压感受器和血压调控的机理会有重大意义.

478710.label: Realisation of objectives
478710.value: 1. We found that TRPC5 is activated by hypotonicity-induced cell swelling when expressed in HEK293 cells. In nodose baroreceptor neurons, we found a similar hypotonicity-activated current with typical TRPC5 I-V relationship. The current could be inhibited by 2-APB, T5E3 and TRPC5-dominant negative construct. On the other hand, the channel was activated by Gd3+. All above evidence suggests what we saw is "TRPC5 current" in nodose neurons. Ca2+ influx study yielded similar results. We determined the ion selectivity of this component and found that the channel has the permeability profile of PCa:PNa:PK:PCs = 1.5:2.9:1.3:1. 2) We explored the molecular composition of TRPC5-related channels in nodose neurons. This part is not completely finished. Based on ion permeability assay, TRPC5-containing channels in nodose neurons are not homomeric TRPC5 channels. Immunostaining study showed that nodose ganglion neurons express multiple TRP isoforms, which could co-assemble with TRPC5. However, we still have not fully resolved the subunit compositions of TRPC5-containing channels in nodose neurons. We believe that this part is less important compared to objective #3. Therefore, we devoted more effort to the objective #3, which is to confirm the functional importance of TRPC5 in baroreceptor mechanosensing. 3) We have knocked-down TRPC5 using a lenti-viral packed TRPC5 dominant-negative construct (Lenti-TRPC5-DN). We found that the rats treated with lenti-TRPC5-DN have a reduced action potential firing in response to pressure change. Furthermore, the pressure-induced heart rate reduction is impaired in the rats that were treated with Lenti-TRPC5-DN. These data strongly suggest that TRPC5 mediates mechanosensation in aortic arch baroreceptor neurons. Based on reviewers' comment, we have utilized TRPC5 knockout mice to validate the functional importance of TRPC5 in baroreceptor mechanosensing. The main work is currently under revision in the PLOS Biology. We are at the stage of nearly finishing the revision work. The revised manuscript is expected to be resubmitted to PLOS biology in next two months. 4) This project is taken longer than expected, mostly because we have added the data of TRPC5 knockout mice. This part (TRPC5 knockout mice) was not in the original proposal. These new data are added because Reviewers in PLOS Biology requested these data. On the other hand, we do believe that the data from TRPC5 knockout mice should greatly strengthen our main conclusion of "TRPC5 as mechanosensor in baroreceptor neurons". The collected data are positive, we do believe we have addressed all the requests from Reviewers in PLOS Biology and the paper should be published soon in PLOS Biology.

478710.value: The project is still evolving. Now we have TRPC5 knockout mice in our hand. We have observed the deficiency of blood pressure regulation in these knockout mice. We plan to further explore whether TRPC5 dysfunction could contribute to salt-induced hypertension.

478710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
478710.value: Through this project, we demonstrated that TRPC5 is mechanosensitive channels activated by hypotonicity-induced cell swelling and membrane stretch. We characterized the electrophysiological property of TRPC5-containing channels in aortic baroreceptor neurons, that serve to detect blood pressure in our body. More importantly, with the use of TRPC5 knockout mice and lenti-viral packed TRPC5 dominant-negative construct (lenti-TRPC5-DN), we demonstrated that TRPC5 is indeed a mechanosensor in aortic arch baroreceptor neurons and that TRPC5 plays a key role in blood pressure regulation. Our study implicates TRPC5 as a potential therapeutic target for treating diseases that are related to blood pressure dysregulation.

479110.value: Recent epidemiological studies have underscored the rising burden of heart failure with preserved systolic function, or normal ejection fraction (HFNEF) that accounts for approximately half of all heart failure cases with a similar survival to other forms of heart failure. HFNEF is, therefore, a major cause of morbidity and mortality with significant healthcare costs that is inadequately understood and for which effective treatments are lacking. As HF develops, hormones are released that initially improve cardiac output but ultimately contribute to progression of left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. The renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system is an important part of this compensatory response. Aldosterone levels may rise to 20-fold normal levels in HF and aldosterone contributes to the development of myocardial scarring (fibrosis). Spironolactone is a receptor blocker of aldosterone which may prevent cardiac fibrosis. Recent trials have evaluated spironolactone in patients with systolic HF demonstrating significant mortality reduction compared to placebo in addition to usual treatment with an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor and beta-blocker. Two separate US National Institutes of Health-funded, randomized trials, are currently studying the potential benefits of spironolactone over placebo in either hard clinical outcome (aborted cardiac arrest and hospitalization for non-fatal myocardial infarction or stroke), or improved exercise tolerance and quality of life in HFNEF patients. Our proposed study is a randomized clinical trial specifically designed to address the question of whether and how exercise capacity is potentially improved by spironolactone (up to 50mg daily for 12 months) in HFNEF patients using advanced echocardiographic technology. Although spironolactone may reduce myocardial fibrosis it is not known if this will normalize cardiac function especially on exercise. Therefore, we will study the relative contribution of changes of LV mass, geometry and fibrosis, contractile function, twist and untwisting, heart rate response and arterial function during aerobic exercise. Our recently funded GRF project for mechanisms of exercise intolerance in HFNEF will provide groundwork and experience for this study. Advantages of using spironolactone are that it is commercially available, inexpensive, and no longer under patent (therefore this study will not be done by industry). Also, there is a clear physiologic rationale for its use, and the side effect profile is well understood. These results will be important, not only because HFNEF is highly prevalent among the elderly, but also because exercise intolerance is a pivotal outcome that is modifiable, is independent of mortality, and is a critical determinant of quality of life and disability among the elderly. 背景 心力衰竭（心衰）是一個常見而且複雜的心血管綜合征，通常表現為心室擴張，收縮力下降和左心室射血分數（Ejection Fraction）降低。但是約半數患者左心室射血分數正常（高於50％），多為老年女性，患有高血壓。目前，如何治療來改善這部分患者的生存率尚缺乏循證醫學證據。因為運動耐量下降是射血分數正常心衰患者的主要症狀，因此提高這部分患者的運動耐量和生活質量較降低其死亡率可能更有意義。 本研究為隨機臨床試驗，于患者服用螺內酯, Spironolactone,（最大劑量50mg/天）12個月後，通過半臥位次最大量單車運動時所進行先進的超聲心動圖檢查，特異性研究螺內酯是否能夠以及如何改善這部分患者的運動耐量。儘管螺內酯可能減少心肌瘢痕和纖維化，但尚不清楚是否有助於心功能，特別是運動時心功能的恢復。因此我們將研究螺內酯改善參加者運動耐量和生活質量的機制。使用螺內酯的優勢為價廉易得，而且已不在專利保護期內（因此其研發廠商未進行此研究）。同時應用的生理基礎及可能的副作用均已闡明。 研究細節 目標：闡明50mg/天的螺內酯 (Spironolactone) 是否可以改善射血分數正常的心衰患者的運動耐量和生活質量，及其潛在的作用機制。 研究設計：前瞻、隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照試驗，積極治療和安慰劑治療的比例為1:1。最初，我們將進行心肺運動試驗，次最大量(心率最高至120次/分)負荷超聲心動圖檢查，以及生活質量問卷調查及抽血化驗。此後的8周測試期內螺內酯的藥量將逐步增加至50mg/天，並於服藥6個月及12月時，重複上述的檢查。同時我們還會對參加者病情進行額外的5次隨訪（2-3次/年)。 上述研究或可能改善射血分數正常的心力衰竭患者運動耐量及生活質量，而其改善機制正是本研究的主要目的。

479410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
479410.value: The aim of this project is to conduct biochemical and molecular biological research to study the mechanism of vesicle tethering by TRAPP. In eukaryotic cells, the secretion of most hormones and growth factors to the outside of the cells is carried out by small transport vesicles. One important step in the process of vesicle transport is that the vesicles need to be tethered to the correct place. A protein complex called TRAPP (Transport protein particle) has been found to be important for the vesicle tethering between the Endoplasmic Reticulum and the Golgi complex. As TRAPP is one of the important cellular machineries that control the secretion of protein hormones and other important proteins, genetic defects that severely hamper the functions of TRAPP are lethal. Mild defects usually cause a variety of diseases as exemplified by the mutations in TRAPP subunit, Trs20, in patients with recessive X-linked spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia tarda (SEDT). SED related diseases are congenital diseases classified as the skeletal dysplasias, which are bone and cartilages disorders that affect skeletal development, resulting in short statue and dwarfism. The mechanism of how defects in vesicle trafficking translate into skeletal development in SEDT patients is still unknown. Here we propose to study the vesicle tethering mechanism of TRAPP. Specifically, we have previously identified a cytoskeletal element that interacts with TRAPP, and this interaction has provided explanation to our previous results that TRAPP is functionally linked to cytoskeleton regulation. Our recent preliminary discovery on the functional link between TRAPP and the cytoskeletal element will changes the way cell biologists look at the process of vesicle tethering. In this proposal, we will conduct detailed analysis of how the cytoskeleton and motor molecules affect vesicle tethering by TRAPP. 本课题将使用生物化学和分子生物学实验方法研究转运蛋白复合体(TRAPP)拴系(tethering)膜泡(vesicle)的分子机制。 在真核细胞，多数激素和生长素等蛋白质的细胞外分泌要依赖膜泡的参与执行，而目标位置对膜泡的正确识别和捕获即拴系(tethering)是膜泡转运过程一个重要的关键步骤。目前转运蛋白复合体(TRAPP)被认为是拴系膜泡的蛋白质复合体，在内质网和高尔基复合体之间物质转运发挥重要作用，也是细胞内调控激素和生长素等分泌性蛋白质一个重要的分子环节。因此转运蛋白复合体(TRAPP)亚单位的遗传缺陷如果严重阻碍其功能执行，该类缺陷将是致死性的，而轻微的缺陷则表现为各种先天性的疾患。例如转运蛋白复合体(TRAPP)亚单位Trs20突变，病人罹患X-连锁迟发性脊柱骨骺发育不良(SETD)，累及脊椎椎体和身体承重大关节的骨软骨发育障碍，主要临床表现为非对称性矮身材，胸部畸形。至于膜泡转运缺陷是如何发展成为X-连锁迟发性脊柱骨骺发育不良(SETD)的确切分子机制还不明确。 我们一直专注于研究转运蛋白复合体(TRAPP)拴系膜泡的分子机制，而且不久之前我们确认了一个与转运蛋白复合体(TRAPP)相互作用的细胞骨架元件，证实了我们之前认为的转运蛋白复合体(TRAPP)参与细胞骨架结构的功能性调节。我们近期的重大发现将改变生物学者之前对膜泡拴系过程的认识角度。在本课题中，我们将对细胞骨架和动力分子是如何通过转运蛋白复合体(TRAPP)来影响膜泡拴系做具体的分析。

479410.label: Major findings and research outcome
479410.value: So far, the funding support of this project has resulted in two primary research papers and a review article. A manuscript containing data from this project will also be submitted early next year. Scientifically, we have put forth a model that COPII vesicle tether, TRAPP, interacts with motor proteins to facilitate vesicle tethering. This is a novel view in the vesicle tethering field. Second, we have identified a potential involvement of TRAPPC9 at the centrosomes and suggest TRAPPII may function in mitosis and cytokinesis. We have further identified three distinct domains on TRAPPC9 that interact with p150Glued. Two such domains are centrosomal localized and their localization is subjected to the regulation of various kinases.

479410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
479410.value: Future development of the research findings will be focused on the centrosmal function(s) or TRAPPC9. How TRAPPC9 affects the integrity of the centrosomes, particular the abundance of pericentrin at the centrosomes, could provide a novel molecular explanation of the mental retardation and microcephaly related to mutations of TRAPPC9. Mutations of pericentrin cause severe mental retardation and microcephaly.

479410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
479410.value: We have identified a novel protein interaction between vesicle tethering complex, TRAPP and proteins related to organelle movement, p150Glued. The findings from this project provide a novel perspective on the mechanism of vesicle tethering in mammalian cells.

480010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
480010.value: With the increased accessibility of different treatment modalities to the lay public in recent decades, it has become very difficult to predict whether various combinations of all of these medications will lead to unwanted side effects or interactions. Compared with western drugs, there are relatively few studies on herbal components. With a better understanding of the absorption and metabolic pathways of herbal components one can recognize or even predict potential herb-drug interactions and take proper actions to prevent their occurrence. Radix Scutellariae (RS) is a frequently utilized plant ingredient in both traditional prescriptions and modern herbal medications. It has been used for centuries to treat inflammation, cancer, and respiratory and gastrointestinal tract infections. Flavonoids are the most abundant ingredients in RS. The six flavones, namely baicalein (B), baicalin (baicalein-7-glucuronide, BG), wogonin (W), wogonoside (wogonin-7-glucuronide, WG), oroxylin A (OA) and oroxylin A-7-glucuronide (OAG) are the major bioactive components in RS. Herb-herb and Herb-drug interactions of RS have been reported, however, with emphasis on either its impact on the in vivo pharmacokinetics or in vitro pharmacodynamics of western drugs. During the past nine years, with the continuous support of two Earmarked Grants, two ITF Grants and four Direct Grants for both PI and Co-I, we were able to identify the mechanisms of absorption and disposition for a series of active ingredients from herbal medicines including B, BG, W, WG, OA and OAG. In order to translate this basic information on flavonoids to clinical practice, we now propose the current animal-based herb-drug interaction studies between RS and anti-inflammatory drugs. Anti-inflammatory drugs are the e most commonly co-administered western drugs, and they share the same metabolic pathway and possess similar COX-2 inhibition activity with RS components. We plan to 1) in vitro screen for the potential anti-inflammatory agents that may inhibit the metabolism of RS components; and 2) further investigate the potential pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamic interactions between RS and selected anti-inflammatory agent in rats. The current study will not only serve as a pilot study on the potential interactions between a standardized RS extract and its most likely co-administered anti-inflammatory drugs with the simultaneous assessment of the overall impact of pharmacokinetics (on both herbal components and western drug) and pharmacodynamics, but also provide a basis for further prediction of potential herb-drug interactions between herbal components such as flavonoids and western drugs in clinical practice. 近年來，随着公眾更加容易獲得各種各样的药物治療，預測多種合併用藥是否會產生副作用或藥物間相互作用变得更加困難。和西藥相比，對中藥有效成份的研究相對較少。對中藥有效成份的吸收和代謝方面的研究能够让我們識別甚至預測潛在的中西藥間相互作用，以便採取有效的手段預防其發生。黃芩是一種藥用植物，被廣泛應用於傳統及現代中藥。黃芩的應用已經有幾個世紀，它常被用來治療炎癥、癌癥、呼吸系統及胃腸道感染。黃酮是黃芩的主要有效成份。黃芩素(B)、漢黃芩素(W)、千層紙素(OA)、黃芩苷(BG)、漢黃芩苷(WG)及千層紙素苷(OAG)等六個黃酮被認為是黃芩的主要活性成份。虽然有黃芩參與的中藥間及中西藥間相互作用時有報導，然而其側重點在黃芩對於西藥的體內藥動學及體外藥效學的影響。 過去九年，在多项Earmarked及ITF基金的支持下，我們課題組對於一系列中藥活性成份（包括B,W,OA,BG,WG和OAG）的吸收及代謝機制有了清楚的認識。爲了將這些對於黃酮类药物的基礎研究結果更好地應用於臨床，我們將利用動物模型來研究黃芩與抗炎藥間中西藥合用的相互作用。抗炎藥是最經常與黃芩合用的西藥，並且與黃芩的主要活性成份具有相類似的代謝途徑以及環氧合酶-2抑制效應。該課題的主要內容包括：1）用體外模型篩選可能抑制黃芩活性物質代謝的抗炎藥；2）用大鼠模型研究篩選出的抗炎藥與黃芩合用后藥動學及藥效學方面的相互作用。本研究结果不僅對黃芩提取物及與其可能合用的抗炎藥之間的藥動學（包括中藥內活性成份及西藥）和藥效學方面的相互作用進行进一步探讨，並且能夠用来預測臨床應用中可能產生的中藥如黃酮與西藥間相互作用。

480010.label: Realisation of objectives
480010.value: For objective 1, various mechanistic studies were conducted to screen for the potential anti-inflammatory agent that may inhibit the metabolism of Radix Scutellariae components, including: 1. Using hepatic microsomal/cytosolic preparations, the effects of anti-inflammatory agents on the glucuronidation and sulfation of the major bioactive components of Radix Scutellariae were screened; 2. Using Caco-2 cell monolayer and rat intestinal perfusion model, the effects of anti-inflammatory agents on the intestinal metabolism and absorption were evaluated; For objective 2, the potential pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interaction between Radix Scutellariae and mefenamic acid (selected from objective 1) was conducted. Specific experiments included: 1. Assay development for simultaneous determination of Radix Scutellariae components and mefenamic acid in biological samples; 2. Developed and validated an ex vivo method to simultaneously determine the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interaction between Radix Scutellariae and mefenamic acid; 3. Conducted rat experiment for the interaction study.

480010.label: Major findings and research outcome
480010.value: From the initial screening, mefenamic acid was demonstrated to be the most potent inhibitor on the metabolism of Radix Scutellariae components and thus it is selected for further herb-drug interaction study. We successfully developed a novel ex vivo method for the simultaneous evaluation of the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interaction between Radix Scutellariae and mefenamic acid in rats. Our findings indicated that the standardized extract of Radix Scutellariae did not interact with mefenamic acid pharmacokinetically, i.e. did not significantly alter the oral bioavailability and other pharmacokinetic parameters of mefenamic acid; whereas mefenamic acid prolonged the half lives and reduced the clearance of the major components of Radix Scutellariae. Pharmacodynamically, co-administration of Radix Scutellariae extract and mefenamic acid resulted in a significantly prolonged and stronger anti-inflammatory effect than either compound alone. Radix Scutellariae was also found to alleviate the stomach ulcer induced by the long-term administration of mefenamic acid.

480010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
480010.value: Our findings provided insights for the safe combinational use of Radix Scutellariae extract with a selected non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, mefenamic acid with potential benefit in enhancing the therapeutic effect (anti-inflammatory effect) while alleviating the adverse effect (stomach ulcer). Such combinational benefits should be further evaluated in specific disease model such as arthritis or other inflammatory diseases models. Meanwhile, the herb-drug combinational effects could be evaluated in human subjects for a more concrete answer. Furthermore, the combination may also be formulated as a new product to treat inflammatory diseases.

480010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
480010.value: With the increased accessibility of different treatment modalities to the lay public in recent decades, it has become very difficult to predict whether the combinations of all of these medications will lead to unwanted effects. Compared with western drugs, there are relatively few studies on herbal components. Our research dedicated to the understanding of the absorption and metabolic pathways of herbal components, and applied such knowledge to the prediction of potential herb-drug interactions with an aim to prevent adverse outcome while screen for beneficial effects of such combination. In this project, we focused on the interaction between Radix Scutellariae and a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug mefenamic acid based on their similarities in metabolic pathway and therapeutic effects. We used an animal-based study to address the potential interactions between this herb-drug combination through the assessment of the overall impact of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, which could become the. Our findings revealed that co-administration of Radix Scutellariae extract and mefenamic acid did not result in changes in plasma concentration but the anti-inflammatory action was enhanced while the side effect (stomach ulcer) was diminished. Such findings set insightful basis for the development of both clinical usage guidelines and formulation.

500310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
500310.value: In recent years, nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization has become essential in many important engineering and economics applications such as image restoration, signal reconstruction, variable selection, optimal control, robust equilibrium problems and spherical approximation. However, most existing optimization theory and algorithms cannot handle such problems efficiently, because the objective function is often not convex, not differentiable and perhaps not even locally Lipschitz at the solutions. Hence, this project aims to develop effective and innovative methods for nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization. The project consists of three parts. First, we derive new theoretical results on necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization and use these conditions to investigate various important properties, such as the sparsity and stability of stationary points and local and global optimal solutions. Second, we construct efficient algorithms for solving nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization by combining smooth approximation techniques and efficient methods for smooth optimization. Moreover, we will establish error bounds of numerical solutions to the true solutions. Finally, we apply the new theory and algorithms to applications in image restoration, signal reconstruction, variable selection and spherical approximation. The outcomes of this project will have a long-term and significant impact, because nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization problems arise naturally from numerous important applications in engineering and economics. Investigation of the necessary and sufficient optimality conditions will not only contribute to the understanding of the stationary points and local and global optimal solutions of nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization, but is also necessary for developing efficient algorithms. Our results are expected to attract attention from the international scientific community through presentation in leading international journals and conferences, and direct collaboration with world leading scientists from Australia, Germany, Japan and the USA. 近幾年來，非光滑非凸優化問題廣泛地出現在許多重要的工程和經濟應用中，如圖像還原，信號重構，變分選擇，優化控制，健全平衡問題和球面逼近問題。然而，由於目標函數大多是非凸、非可微甚至在優化解附近不滿足局部Lipschitz條件，目前許多優化理論和算法並不令人完全滿意。因此，本項目將針對非光滑非凸優化問題開發有效的，創新的方法。 本項目共包括三部分研究內容。首先，針對非光滑非凸優化問題，推導出關於充分必要最優條件的新理論結果，並應用這些條件研究一些重要的性質，如穩定點，局部和全局最優解的稀疏性和穩定性。其次，結合光滑逼近技術和關於光滑優化的有效方法，設計求解非光滑非凸優化的有效算法。最後，將得到的這些新的理論與算法應用到圖像還原，信號重構，變分選擇和球面逼近等問題中。 由於非光滑非凸優化問題自然地出現在工程和經濟的許多重要應用中，本項目的研究成果將會有一個長期而重要的影響。推導充分必要的優化條件不僅有助於理解非光滑非凸優化問題的穩定點，局部和全局最優解，而且有助於高性能算法的構造。本項目的研究成果將由於在國際著名期刊發表文章，在國際重要的學術會議上做報告，與澳大利亞，德國，日本和美國的前沿科學家直接合作而受到廣泛的關注。

Page 5 uses smoothing approximation and neural network to solve nonsmooth, nonconvex constrained minimization probelms. Paper 6 establishes complexity results of interior point algorithms for nonsmooth, non-Lipschitz minimization problems.

500910.label: Project Objectives
500910.value: To grow epitaxial thin films of perovskite titanates, such as SrTiO3 and Ba1-xSrxTiO3 on III-V semiconductors such as GaAs using laser MBE. To modify the thin film of perovskite titanate from an insulator to an n-type semiconductor having electrical resistivity of 0.01~10 ohm.cm, and to form tailorable heterostructures. To investigate the physical properties of the heterostructures, including dielectric, ferroelectric, electrical transport, optical and p-n heterojunction characteristics. To extend our fundamental studies of the heterostructures to multifunctional device applications ranging from high-frequency agile electronics to p-n heterojunction based electronics and optoelectronics. The performances of the heterostructure devices will be comparable to the current state-of-art results from perovskite titanates grown on oxides or Si wafes. Typically, the dielectric tunability for high-frequency agile electronics would be greater than 30%. Rectifying ratio for the p-n heterojunction would be greater than 1000.

500910.label: Realisation of objectives
500910.value: 1. To achieve objective 1 fully, we have deposited various thin films of perovskite titanates (SrTiO3 (STO), Ba1-xSrxTiO3 (BST), etc.) grown on III-V semiconductor wafers such as GaAs with different resistivity. Laser molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) was used to deposit the thin films. It is known that the structure and chemistry on the GaAs surface are more complex and involves multiple reconstructions. We have successfully overcome the problems and found the optimum conditions for epitaxial thin film grown on GaAs. Briefly, the GaAs substrate was first in situ heated in vacuum. To prevent the GaAs substrate from oxidizing, the chamber was evacuated to a base pressure. The deposition temperature was set around 600 °C for STO thin-film deposition. 2. To achieve objective 2 fully, we have grown oxygen-deficient SrTiO3-δ thin films on p-GaAs substrates to form p–n heterojunctions. The STO films were deposited on GaAs substrates with a resistivity of about 0.01-10 ohm.cm, which is within the proposed resistivity range. To change oxygen stoichiometry, we have controlled the oxygen partial pressure during the growth and post-annealing in order to solve the problem of tailorable heterostructures converting from ferroelectric insulator/GaAs structure to p-n heterojunction. 3. To achieve objective 3 fully, we have investigated the physical properties of the heterostructures, including dielectric, ferroelectric, electrical transport, optical and p-n heterojunction characteristics using a variety of techniques. The in-plane dielectric properties of BST thin film were measured using an HP 4294A impedance analyzer connected to a temperature controlled chamber. The dielectric constant was obtained from the measured capacitances by using Gevorgian model. Optical properties have been performed by optical and luminescent spectrometers, and Raman technique. We have also used advanced piezoresponse force microscopy to show the images and ferroelectric polarization loops as a function of electric field of the films grown on GaAs. 4. To achieve objective 4 fully, we have designed various multifunctional devices. Photolithography technique has been used to make interdigital patterns with Au top layer for fabricating devices. The heterostructure under moderate dc bias field can be tuned by more than 30% and K factor used for frequency agile materials is found to be close to the value of 8. A forward-to-reverse current ratio of p-n junction is measured to be about 1280, which is greater than 1000. All the measured results which have been published in international journals can meet the requirements of the proposed device performance in our proposal.

500910.label: Major findings and research outcome
500910.value: Eight peer-reviewed international journal papers were published from this research project with the RGC GRF Funding acknowledged, including 3 Appl. Phys. Lett., 2 J. Appl. Phys., 1 Angew Chem., 1 Opt. Express., and 1 Scripta Mater.. We have also presented some results in five international conferences, including keynote/invited speech in some conferences. One postgraduate student, Zhibin Yang was trained and authored several journal papers, finally obtained his degree directly supported by the GRF grant. Major findings are as follows: 1. We have successfully developed repeatable growth method based on laser MBE. Key parameters to control the epitaxial growth include GaAs processing temperature, deposition temperature, oxygen pressure and post-annealing conditions. STO buffer layer is found to be important for the subsequent growth of other functional oxides (see: Part C: Journal 5,8, Conference: 2,4) 2. The STO/GaAs p-n junctions present good rectifying behaviors and the thickness dependence of current–voltage properties. The interface of the heteroepitaxial STO/GaAs is sharp, and therefore leads to the temperature and film-thickness-dependent transport properties of the n-STO/p-GaAs junctions. With decreasing STO film thickness, the current mechanism changes from a space charge limited model to strain-assisted tunneling (see: Part C: Journal 3, Conference 3,4). 3 We found that the valence band offset is determined to be 2.6 eV, while the conduction band offset is deduced to be 0.7 eV. The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profile measurement is evident that the interface is free of interfacial compound in our epitaxial STO/GaAs heterostructure fabricated by laser MBE. The above results have been published in Appl. Phys. Lett. (2013) (see: Part C: Journal 8). 4. We have grown perovskite titanate STO buffer layer on GaAs and subsequently grow epitaxial Mn-doped BiFeO3 (MBFO) thin films. Piezoresponse force microscopy images and polarization versus electric field loops indicate that the MBFO films grown on GaAs have an effective ferroelectric switching. This is the first time to show BFO can be grown on GaAs with our developed perovskite/GaAs platform. The MBFO films exhibit good ferroelectric behavior. Ferromagnetic property with saturated magnetization of 6.5 emu/cm3 and coercive field of about 123 Oe is also found in the heterostructure at room temperature. (Part C: Journal 7). 5. We have successfully fabricated ferroelectric titanate tunable thin film devices integrated with GaAs wafer. Butterfly-shaped C-V characteristic curves of BST/STO/GaAs were observed. A relatively large dielectric tunability of 30% was found at 1 MHz. (Part C: Journal 5, Conference 2,3,5).

500910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
500910.value: Our solution to the problem of growing perovskite titanate thin films on III-V semiconductor which is developed in this project can be widely expanded to the growth of various functional oxides in further development of heterostructure research. According to X-ray and ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy investigation of STO/GaAs, we have precisely constructed an energy band diagram of STO/GaAs, showing the energy band discontinuity of heterostructure and a type II band alignment forming at the interface in this project. These findings should be important for further STO/GaAs applications, such as high-k and ferroelectric microwave tunable devices. With our platform by inserting perovskite titanate STO as buffer layer, it is promising to make more types of devices by combining other functional materials with GaAs. For instance, it is hoped that the fabricated multiferroic /STO/III–V semiconductor heterostructure will become an important component in multifunctional devices. Our results also offer the possibility to combine frequency agile electronics of ferroelectric titanate with the high-performance microwave capabilities of GaAs for room temperature tunable device application. It would be interesting to transfer our developed process to microelectronic and information communication industries who are interested in developing high-frequency tunable devices compatible with commercial GaAs microwave circuit.

500910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
500910.value: Perovskite titanates exhibit a broad spectrum of dielectric, ferroelectric, piezoelectric, pyroelectric, and non-linear optical effects. However, the epitaxial growth of titanate thin film on III-V semiconductor represents challenges including structural incompatibility and interdiffusion between GaAs and titanate. In this project, we have achieved controlled heteroepitaxy of perovskite titanates (SrTiO3 (STO), Ba1-xSrxTiO3 (BST), etc.) thin films grown on III-V semiconductor wafer by laser molecular beam epitaxy. Furthermore, two kinds of heterostructures, namely insulating titanate/III-V semiconductor and n-type semiconductor titanate/p-type III-V semiconductor have been designed and fabricated. Some physical properties of perovskite titanate thin films and multifunctional characteristics of the heterostructures have been investigated. Consequently, the developed STO/GaAs can be regarded as a model system and will be extended to other perovskite oxide/III-V’s systems. Our success in fabricating the heterostructures of perovskite titanate thin films/III-V semiconductor will also increase the capabilities of the semiconductor family, allowing not only traditional devices to operate better but also allowing new devices to be conceived. By considering the high-performance microwave capabilities and large-size availability of commercial GaAs, this project exhibits that our developed heterostructure can be processed to be a new component for the applications in tunable high-frequency and multifunctional p-n junction devices.

501010.value: 正倒向滤波，非光滑优化及应用

501010.label: Co - Investigator(s)

501010.label: Project Objectives
501010.value: To introduce and develop the forward-backward filtering theory. To investigate the FBSDE optimization with partial information, based on (1). To investigate the FBSDE optimization with nonsmooth generators using superprocess theory. To investigate the nonsmooth FBSDE optimization with partial information by combining (1)-(3). To investigate some interesting and important real applications using (1)-(4).
rows: To introduce and develop the forward-backward filtering theory.
To investigate the FBSDE optimization with partial information, based on (1).
To investigate the FBSDE optimization with nonsmooth generators using superprocess theory.
To investigate the nonsmooth FBSDE optimization with partial information by combining (1)-(3).
To investigate some interesting and important real applications using (1)-(4).

501010.label: Realisation of objectives
501010.value: (1) We investigate the filtering theory to forward-backward stochastic systems. In partially-coupled case, the related filtering is connected to the classical filtering by separable principle. The associated filter depends on the observation mechanism; In fully-coupled case, the related filtering can be transformed to the combination of standard filtering for forward state and some singular filtering for backward state. Hence, we establish some equivalence to forward-backward martingale problem. To this end, we investigate the regularity properties of a general class of HJB equations with or without obstacles. These equations can be probabilistically interpreted as our stochastic control system with nonlinear (or nonsmooth) cost functional via a backward SDE (BSDE) or a reflected BSDE. (2) We study the FBSDE optimization with partial information structure. By applying the variational analysis and duality relation, the optimal Hamiltonian system is represented by some double-dimensional backward-forward SDE with mean-field type and mixed-initial-terminal conditions. Here, the mean-field structure is due to conditional expectation operator on partial information. In particular, in case the partial information by independent Brownian motion, we derive some backward-forward mean-field Hamiltonian system. Given it, we develop the necessary decoupling in the linear-quadratic case via Riccati equations. This case has very important values in real applications. (3) We also study the FBSDE optimization with non-smooth generator. To this end, we connect it to near-optimal controls and the non-smooth generator can be approximated by its smooth mollifiers. The resulting near-optimal control can be obtained by Ekeland variational analysis. As the special but very important case, we study the optimal control with reflected BSDEs for which the the backward generator is non-smooth and we investigate the limiting behavior of its adjoint equation in maximum principle. We obtain some basic representations in this direction which depends on the local-time process in the first order, and super-process (collision-time) in the second order. (4) We study the nonsmooth optimization based on (1)-(3). Some Hamiltonian system in mean-field type driven by non-smooth generator is introduced and some preliminary results to its wellposedness is established. As the applications, we study some LQ FBSDE control with delayed generators. The underlying state is fully-coupled forward-backward SDE to model the production planning with delay. We also study some mixed optimal-stopping and control problem which is closely related to the control of reflected BSDE. Some mean-field type FBSDE and its wellposedness are obtained. As another application, we discuss the mean-field game with stochastic integral system structure.

501010.label: Major findings and research outcome
501010.value: We find the basic relation between forward-backward filtering to standard forward filtering (FKK or Zakai equation via forward martingale problem) and the possible singular backward filtering (in principle, some back optional projection via four-step scheme of FBSDE). As to the backward singular filter, we find it is necessary to discuss the regularity property of related decoupling function or Feynman-Kac representation. To this end, we discuss the regularity of a general class of HJB equation with nonlinear cost functional which can be applied to our backward filtering setup. As to FBSDE optimization with partial information, we find the related Hamiltonian system becomes some general mean-field backward-forward SDEs with general conditional expectation. We discuss the related LQ case and consider its stability properties to this mean-field system. This includes the case with independent Brownian motion observation. As to the FBSDE with nonsmooth generators, we connect it to the near-optimal control problems by the approximation of smooth mollifiers in FBSDE system. The limiting maximum principle can be obtained through some limiting procedure and Ekeland variation. It can be connected to the local time process in its first order case, and collision-time in its second-order case. As supporting result, we discuss the near-optimal control for a class of linear FBSDE systems with irregular characters. It can be related to our previous results of nonsmooth FBSDE control. As the real applications, we apply our FBSDE optimization results to infinite time horizon of mean-field FBSDE and study its stability properties. We also discuss the FBSDE optimization with delayed generators and obtain related necessary conditions. Some monotonicity method is proposed to show the wellposedness of related Hamiltonian delayed-anticipated system. In addition, some conditional expectation operator is given in this delayed system and it generalizes a series works of Oksendal and Sulem with ``delayed" partial information structure. On the other hand, we also discuss the maximum principle of stochastic control with recursive functional through some reflected BSDE. To this end, some non-smooth BSDE optimization is discussed via smooth-mollifier approximating and some near-optimality necessary and sufficient conditions are derived. As another application, we study the LQ Mean-field games (MFGs) with delayed generators which is related to production-planning with delayed effects. We also study the mixed optimal control and stopping-time problems which is related to the reflected BSDE due to variational inequality. In addition, we discuss the backward LQ MFG with full and partial information.

501010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
501010.value: The potential for further development includes the following parts: (1) One direction is the discussion of FBSDE optimization in more general partial information structure which can be enlarged by the underlying delayed filtration and other hidden process. This will extend our current results to more realistic framework. (2) It is also necessary to study the FBSDE optimization but within the weak formulation framework. Within this framework, it is possible to relax the regularity (smooth) requirements of the underlying coefficients hence potentially, we can get more detailed results of FBSDE with nonsmooth optimization. (3) Another direction is to study the stochastic control with reflected recursive functional which has more economic meanings. It is also interesting to discuss the related numerical computation scheme and discuss the related convergence speed.

501010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
501010.value: The optimization of forward-backward (FB) stochastic system has important values in both theoretical analysis and practical applications. Moreover, it is more realistic to discuss forward-backward dynamic optimization with partial information and nonsmooth coefficients. This project considers the forward-backward stochastic filtering which extends the classical filtering, and also studies the forward-backward dynamic optimization with partial information, non-smooth or irregular coefficients. The related FBSDE nonsmooth optimization is connected to the smooth approximation and near-optimality. Specially, the near-optimality for recursive reflected BSDE functional is considered, and its regularity control property is also analyzed. We discuss the maximum principles to FBSDE with recursive functional, and the relevant near-optimality controls using Ekeland variation. On the other hand, the FBSDE with partial information (say, with delayed filtration) is also discussed by deriving the associated maximum principle. It follows the resulting Hamiltonian system is connected to some general mean-field backward-forward SDE systems. It wellposedness results are discussed. As the supporting research, we systematically discuss the LQ mean-field-type FBSDE optimization in both finite and infinite-time horizon. we also discuss the combination of mean-field control and optimal stopping (which is closely related to reflected BSDE). We also study the related rela applications such as delayed systems.
