514910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
514910.value: In the last three decades, cold-formed steel sections and sheetings have been widely used in building construction as building envelopes and floors. In modern roof systems with cold-formed steel Z-purlin systems, their structural performance depend heavily on various types of restraints offered by various components of the roof systems, namely, i) roof sheetings, ii) bracing members, and iii) lapped Z-sections at purlin-rafter connections. While the first two types of restraints had been known and utilized for structural design for more than 20 years, only few investigations on the third type of restraint had been reported. Currently, owing to the lack of specific experimental and numerical investigations, the effects of these three restraints have not been quantified and itemized individually. Any changes in materials, dimensions and arrangements in these roof components often require expensive and time-consuming full-scale tests to verify and validate the structural performance of the roof systems. A total of 36 bending tests on lapped Z-sections were conducted by the PI between 2002 and 2006, and it was found that owing to the high level of section continuity developed between the lapped Z-sections, their flexural rigidities increased considerably to about 1.4 to 1.6 times of those of single Z-sections. Such beneficial effect of the lapped Z-sections should be properly included in structural design of Z-purlin systems in order to improve the design accuracy. In this proposal, the primary objective is to examine scientifically the structural behaviour of multi-span Z-purlin systems in which the contributions from various types of restraints to their structural behaviour will be quantified and itemized individually. More importantly, the effects of the strength and stiffness enhancement of lapped Z-sections at purlin-rafter connections to the load carrying capacities of Z-purlin systems will be carefully assessed. The study will contribute directly towards new understandings on system behaviour of widely adopted structural systems, and development of effective analysis methods for practical design, enabling a major advancement over the conventional member-based approach. After incorporating the restraining effects of various roof components as system-based structural benefits in multi-span Z-purlin systems, an improvement to the structural efficiency in the usage cold-formed steel materials about 10 % on average will be achieved while a maximum improvement at 15 % is expected in some cases. The findings of the project will be disseminated among the international communities of structural engineering through publications in international journals as definitive references. 在過去三十年，冷彎型鋼及板材已廣泛應用於建築工程以作為建築圍護和樓板結構。在以冷彎 Z 型鋼檁條為支承的現代房蓋系統，其結構性能主要取決於房蓋系統內各組件所提供的約束條件，包括 i) 屋面板，ii) 支撐構件，及 iii) 檁條-椽子連接上的檁條搭接部份。目前，由於缺乏具體明確的實驗和數值分析研究，上述三種約束條件的效能還未能被逐一量化。 此項目主要目的是研究多跨度冷彎鋼檁條系統的結構性能，其中各類約束的影響將被逐一量化。此項目將有助於了解現時廣泛採用的結構體系的系統結構性能，並推動其高效分析方法發展，以作為應用設計的基礎，從而比傳統設計方式作出重大的改善和進步。 此項目的研究結果將於國際結構工程期刊出版，以作為國際結構工程界的權威參考。

515010.value: Review existing HDR imaging techniques for luminance measurement, and then develop a measurement protocol for the spatial and temporal luminance distributions using HDR photography techniques with focus on lighting quality evaluation. Review existing methods of discomfort glare assessment regarding their suitability for electric and natural light sources with nonuniform luminance. Investigate into the effects of nonuniform artificial light sources and windows, as well as the uneven patterns of changing daylight admitted into the low carbon buildings, on visual comfort, using discomfort glare as an assessment parameter aided by HDR photography techniques. 515010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515010.value: Low carbon buildings use innovative daylight harvesting technologies such as smart windows and energy efficient electric lighting installations of next generation, as well as integrated intelligent lighting controls, to minimize carbon emission. The light distribution in such building interiors is often spatially uneven and temporally changing at abundant yet necessary level. This trend has increased the need for simple, quick, and accurate methods for the evaluation of interior lighting performance. Occupants may experience discomfort glare from light sources, windows, or light patterns with overwhelming and non-uniform luminance. Lighting performance across the buildings may be not optimized. Moreover, light outflow through windows to outdoors at night, which may be a potential source of light pollution to the nighttime environment, should be evaluated. These tasks, however, are difficult to accomplish using conventional methods. First, the traditional way of light measurement using luminance and illuminance meters is a tedious point by point manual process, incapable for capturing the entire scenes in short time. Second, existing discomfort glare rating methods, including the widely adopted unified glare rating (UGR) as well as its extensions, and the daylight glare index (DGI), were developed based on the assumption of uniform luminaires or windows. Therefore, technically they cannot be used for non-uniform luminance distributions commonly seen in low carbon buildings. In addition, those discomfort glare indices for electric lighting were found unsuitable for windows. Aided by the emerging high dynamic range (HDR) photography techniques, this research project is aimed to address these issues. It will develop a practical unified discomfort glare index and a quick method for post-occupancy evaluation of interior lighting performance and light outflow through windows to outdoors. A simple, quick, and precise HDR measurement protocol will be developed for measurement of spatial and temporal luminance distribution, followed by laboratory and field experimental studies, based on a comprehensive survey of typical daylit low carbon building interiors found in Hong Kong and mainland China. Case studies will also be carried out for further validation. 低碳建築使用創新技術例如聰明窗口和節能電氣照明設備，並且利用先進的照明控制系統，使碳排放減到最小。低碳大廈的室內光分佈經常是在空間上不均勻和在時間上發生頗大及必要變化。 這個趨向增加了對室內照明表現的簡易、快捷和準確評估方法的需要。大廈居住者也許體驗到從電光源、窗口或巨大和不均勻發光體引起的不舒適眩光。而且，在夜間室內燈光通過窗口溢出到戶外也應該被評估，因爲這也許是一個潛在對夜間環境的光污染源。運用常規方法是很難簡單、快捷和準確地完成室內光環境的評價。 首先，使用傳統亮度和照度計是繁瑣的點對點手動程序，不能快速取得整個場面的數據。 其次，現有的不舒適眩光評價方法，包括被廣泛採用的統一眩光值(UGR) 及採光眩光指數 (DGI)，都是根據均勻發光的燈具或窗口而做的。 所以，它們不能應用於在低碳大廈普遍存在的不均勻亮度分佈室內光環境。這個計劃打算利用高動態範圍 (HDR) 攝影技術研究這些問題，它將開發一個實用的統一不舒適眩光指數和一個簡易、快捷和準確的方法為室內照明表現和光外溢作出評價。繼而在實驗室和典型的香港及內地利用採光照明的低碳大廈內做實地調查及實驗性研究。

515010.label: Realisation of objectives
515010.value: For objective 1, following a literature review, a new measurement method using HDR photography fused with photogrammetry that allows capturing the spatial and temporal luminance distributions was developed. An up-to-date discomfort glare assessment method that can evaluate the lighting quality for electric lighting and windows with non-uniform and ever-changing luminance distributions was suggested. For objective 2, the problems of current discomfort glare assessment methods, namely Unified Glare Rating and Daylight Glare Index, in tackling electric and natural light sources with non-uniform luminance distributions were identified. The necessity of developing a new interior lighting quality assessment method using HDR photography, possibly combined with photogrammetry, was reported for its advantage to obtain pixel luminance across the visual field. For objective 3, using HDR photography to obtain luminance was attempted for examining occupants’ acceptable daylight level in offices. 125 occupants were interviewed and the daylit conditions of their offices were captured using HDR photography for luminance acquisition and conventional illuminance measurements. After successfully managing the technique, the research focus turned back to evaluating discomfort glare. The effects of windows with a non-uniform daylight distribution on visual comfort were firstly studied. Three commonly used metrics for assessing daylight glare (DGI, DGR and DGIN) were examined for their suitability for evaluating discomfort glare from these kinds of windows. The part of objective 3 regarding daylighting quality was successfully achieved. For objective 4, a method for estimating visual acceptance with daylight glare was developed using logistic regression models. The HDR photography, together with user assessment surveys and lighting measurements, were further used to scientifically identify the factors and their controlling parameters that affect occupants to assess the daylighting performance in cellular offices using the analytic hierarchy process. Five factors and their controlling parameters were found. By using these findings and considering the statistically possible sky types in Hong Kong, the probability that a local cellular office with side windows achieves visually acceptable daylighting performance in a year was calculated, a new multi-criteria daylighting quality index (DQI) and associated benchmarking method were developed. Objective 5 about interior daylighting performance was achieved. Work was also carried out on discomfort glare due to interior lighting, light outflow through windows to outdoors and the outdoor lighting environment using computational simulations and HDR photography. The main difficulty in achieving all objectives was due to the difficulty in employing a quality research assistant under the currently prosperous BSE industry in Hong Kong.

515010.label: Major findings and research outcome
515010.value: Shortages of conventional light measurements using a luminance meter were identified; a new luminance measuring technique named high dynamic range photography with photogrammetry was introduced. Five factors for assessing daylighting performance in terms of two criteria: visual comfort and electric lighting energy saving potential for cellular offices were identified; logarithm of average desktop illuminance, logarithm of average surrounding luminance, ratio of minimum to average desktop illuminance, ratio of average luminance of the back half side surfaces of the office to that of the front half side surfaces, and DGIN are the controlling parameters of the factors with regard to the two criteria. A method making use of the values of the controlling parameters of the five factors affecting the amount of saveable lighting energy in visually acceptable daylit cellular offices and the local possible hourly sky types within office hours to estimate the amount of saveable lighting energy throughout a year was introduced. The assessment ability of DGIN on daylight glare was investigated with a series of statistics. The DGIN values of various daylit cellular offices were obtained by HDR photography. DGIN should be lower than 16 in order to allow 80% of the occupants to feel visually acceptable towards the daylight glare. A new multi-criteria daylighting quality index (DQI) using real climatic data and computational simulations was developed. An associated 5-star rating scale was proposed to categorize the daylighting quality of different interiors. Illuminance values conventionally obtained by a calibrated lux meter and those converted by the equation of perfectly diffusely reflecting surface captured by HDR photography at three different angles in a windowless room lit by fluorescent lamps of three different correlated colour temperatures under three different lighting levels. It was found that HDR photography can become a reliable illuminance acquisition tool on a surface covered by grey targets. The UGR values of indoor lighting installations respectively obtained by DIALux simulations and HDR photography were compared with subjective discomfort responses via field measurements and questionnaire surveys. The results showed that HDR photography reflects subjective sensation of discomfort glare caused by electric lighting in an indoor environment in a more accurate manner than what the software shows. A new daylighting performance assessment method with the consideration of the perceived importance of the attributes from occupants using the analytic hierarchy process based on the criteria of visual comfort and electric lighting energy saving potential was developed.

515010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515010.value: Some objectives of the project have not been completely fulfilled during the reporting period. In the future, more studies should be conducted on the electric lighting quality in indoor environments, particularly those with non-uniform light distributions using HDR photography or other simpler and faster but more accurate measurement methods. The next generation of HDR photography is expected to be HDR video. The future lighting research on lighting measurement would be focused on using the feasibility of using HDR video to evaluate a lighting environment. In this way, even the ever-changing daylit conditions in an interior could then be evaluated almost immediately.

515010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515010.value: Energy efficient electric lighting installations and innovative daylighting systems have emerged for building sustainability recently. The light distribution in the interiors with these technologies is however often spatially more uneven and temporally changing at abundant. Occupants may therefore more easily experience discomfort glare from the high luminance contrast between the bright solid state light sources or the bright smart windows and the dark background. Daylight glare index (DGI) and unified glare rating (UGR) were not derived for evaluating glare from non-uniform light distributions. In addition, both metrics involve the luminances of the light source and the background, which are conventionally obtained in a tedious way and may not be appropriate for the new lighting systems. To evaluate the interior lighting quality of the next generation, a simpler, quicker and more reliable method is in great demand. In this project, High Dynamic Range (HDR) photography was tested and applied for luminance acquisition. The results were encouraging that using HDR photography, methods for evaluating the daylighting performance of local sidelit cellular offices and estimating the potential lighting energy that could be saved were developed. It was also proven to give reasonably precise results for accounting for occupants’ discomfort glare from electric lighting.

515110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
515110.value: 智能電網環境下的電力系統安全性和脆弱性評估

515110.label: Co - Investigator(s)
515110.value: Dr Dong, Zhaoyang Prof Wong, Kit Po Prof Xue, Yusheng Dr Zhang, Pei

515110.label: Project Objectives
515110.value: Development of algorithms based on topological analysis using weighted graphs for power system stability and vulnerability assessment, the weights will reflect the underlying power system component characteristics; Development of methodologies for the identification of weak regions of a large scale power system, where external attack/disturbance or internal faults may cause cascading system failure or blackout; Development of complex system theory based methodologies for power system security assessment with consideration of the interaction between the power system and the ICT network under the smart grid environment; Development of power security assessment methods to account for the impacts of increasing renewable generations, especially from wind farms; and Application of the developed methods to real-life large scale power systems so as to derive some general rules of system vulnerability and stability properties with respect to potential attacks (terrorist and extreme nature conditions) to the system. Key Issues and Problems  Power system has become increasingly complex with new developments such as increasing interconnectivities, renewable generations, and interaction with the information and communications networks under the smart grid initiative. Conventional system security and vulnerability analysis techniques are no longer capable of providing timely assessment results.  The topological based system security assessment methods so far cannot handle system dynamics, which requires time domain based methods. This can be time consuming in critical system conditions such as cascading failure.  Power systems are facing continuous threat from malicious attacks from terrorists or natural extreme events. However, how to formulate effective protective and preventive methods remains a challenging problem given the two issues above. How does the proposal address the above issues  In order to give timely information for system security and vulnerability especially during critical states of operation of a power system such as those close to possible cascading failure, new methodologies based on weighted graph theory will be developed for security and vulnerability assessment. This approach will incorporate characteristics of power system to topologically based methods (without any weights on the links of the graphs) for both static and dynamic stability assessment. The findings of this method will provide a new approach for system security assessment and moves the analysis away from time domain approaches, which could be time consuming under such critical conditions.  To fully understand the characteristics of power system during cascading failure and then incorporate them into a general framework, detailed system cascading failure model will be developed and used for the proposed system security and vulnerability assessment framework. Efficient data mining techniques will be used to analyze and extract information from the fault data sets.  In view of system security and vulnerability against malicious attacks and extreme natural conditions, a game theoretic operational approach will be developed. The decision model will fully utilize the results obtained in topological analysis and cascading failure analysis to obtain the most effective and efficient approach for system security and vulnerability enhancement against malicious attacks and extreme natural conditions.

515110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515110.value: Power system security and vulnerability assessment are essential for power system operations and planning worldwide. The primary aim of the power industry is to supply electricity in a secure, reliable and economical manner. In recent years, there have been dramatic changes in the power industry. These changes include rapid growth in electricity demand , especially in China, India, and other rapidly developing countries such as Brazil; increasing penetration of generations from renewable sources such as wind and solar due to corporate responsibility in reducing carbon emission; and increasing use of information, communications technology (ICT) lead to ever growing complexity and interconnectivity of the power systems. Power systems can also fail to operate satisfactorily due to disturbances, which can be caused by unusual combinations of risk factors. In addition to the conventional system disturbances, those factors also include human related factors such as terrorist attacks and interruptions to the power system from extreme natural conditions. Although there are established methodologies for power system security and vulnerability assessment; however, with the recent move toward a smart grid and the increasing human disturbance factors, power system operators and planners are facing new challenges in ensuring its security and reducing its vulnerability to various disturbance sources including malicious attacks. In many countries, the renewable resources are not necessarily located close to the electricity load demand centers. Therefore high voltage transmission over long distance is needed. For smaller power grids like the power systems in Hong Kong, the planned wind power generation and foreseeable increasing connection with South China Power Grid will bring about similar challenges to system operators and planners similar to those of larger power systems. In this project, the highly complex power system with increasing renewable resources and impacts due to smart grid initiatives will be studied, with particular reference to system security and vulnerability. The project will develop complex systems theory, advanced computational methods, and methodologies against malicious attacks to the power systems. A framework of power system security and vulnerability assessment will also be developed in this project. 515110.label: Realisation of objectives
515110.value: The research objectives of this project have been successfully accomplished, and major research outcomes and findings are reported in five top journal publications and two conference publications listed in Part C. A security assessment framework capable of detection of presence of isolated islands and weak regions (Objectives 1&2)based on topological analysis and complex network theory has been established, and details of research findings and outcomes have been reported in two conference publications in part C. Reported in Journal Publication No4 in Part C, the developed framework has also been applied and extended to detect the presence of isolated community in water distribution system, which is a serious security threat in large scale infrastructures like the power grids. With respect to development of power security assessment methods to account for renewable energies (Objective 3), the team has firstly developed a comprehensive fault ride through control strategy for wind turbines to ensure dynamic and voltage stability of power systems with high wind power penetration under grid fault conditions, which is reported in a paper published by IEEE Transactions on Power Systems (Journal No 5 in Part C). Furthermore, security assessment methods that can take wind and other renewable energies into account have been developed and tested using real-life large power system models (objective 4), which are reported in details in Journal publications No 1-3, Part C, including papers published by the IEEE Transactions on Power Systems.

515110.label: Major findings and research outcome
515110.value: This project was initially led by Professor Zhao Yang Dong and later transferred to Dr. Z. Xu as project PI in 2011. Despite the significant change, the project team including Dr. Xu, Prof Dong and others worked closely together in the past three years and fruitful research outcomes have been achieved. The project achieved several major findings and outcomes, including A new grid modeling and security assessment framework for power grids based on topological analysis and complex network theory. This new framework is based on weighted complex network that can be used for power system security and vulnerability analysis, where both topological and physical (electrical) properties of power systems are incorporated. The advantages of the developed framework exist in a simple high level power grid model for rapid and qualitative assessment of large scale power system security and vulnerability that can effectively evaluate security events involving high uncertainties such as cascading outages. Details of the developed framework are reported in the two conference publications as well as the Journal Publication No4 in Part C. It is also interesting to point out that the developed framework can be applied to security analysis (detection of isolated community) for another major infrastructure of similar properties, i.e. water distribution system, which has been reported in a journal Paper published in Chaos (Journal Publication No4 in Part C). Security assessment methods that can take wind and other renewable energies into account. The team firstly developed dynamic simulation model for wind turbines, and then a comprehensive fault ride through control strategy for wind turbines is developed to ensure dynamic and voltage stability of power systems with high wind power penetration under grid fault conditions, which is reported in a paper published by IEEE Transactions on Power Systems (Journal No 5 in Part C). With enhanced stability of wind turbine systems, security assessment methods that can take wind and other renewable energies into account have been developed based on advanced data mining and artificial intelligence techniques and tested using real-life large power system models. These outcomes are published in top journals including IEEE Transactions on Power Systems (Journal publications No 1-3 in Part C).

515110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515110.value: The project has accomplished its preset goals with significant research outcomes and findings resulted. While new models and methods for security and vulnerability analysis have been developed, the team still consider there are plenty of spaces for further research and improvement in this regard. E.g. with respect to security and vulnerability analysis based on topological and physical properties involved complex network based model, a comprehensive security assessment framework has been established in the project that can effectively evaluate security events involving high uncertainties such as cascading outages. Because of incorporation of many uncertainties, the security assessment may somehow involve high computational burdens, resulting in a slow computing speed for security assessment of large scale systems. The team has planned to carry out further research and development to enhance the computing performance of the developed framework in our future scope.

515110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515110.value: The priority of power system operation and control is to prevent power grids from blackouts in events of various security disturbances such as short circuit faults etc. To achieve this, security assessment of power grids against various foreseeable disturbances have to be executed beforehand. Traditional security assessment methods proved to be inadequate as evidenced in many recent blackout events in e.g. North America, India and Europe. To overcome many drawbacks of traditional security methods such as excessive simulation time, high dependency on detailed system model and event based assessment approach, this project proposes a novel network topology and complex network based framework to enable rapid and qualitative security assessment of power grids that presents an alternative yet effective approach for security and vulnerability assessment of power grids with high potentials of practical applications. This proposed framework is especially useful for security assessment of power grids with high renewable penetration against security events of high uncertainties such as cascading outages. With the achievement in this project, further research can be carried out in the future to improve the developed method with respect to the computing efficiency, as well as considering security threats from not only physical domain but also from cyber domain.

515410.label: Realisation of objectives
515410.value: Both of the objectives of the project have been achieved successfully. For Objective 1, the Total Electronic Content (TEC) variations associated with some large seismic events, including the Mw 8.0 Wenchuan earthquake in 2008, the Mw 6.9 Yushu earthquake and the Mw 7.1 Darfield earthquake in 2010 have been mapped with meter-level resolution. It has been found that most of the earthquakes studied were accompanied by severe TEC variations. A number of algorithms have been developed, tested and applied to improve the accuracy of the estimated TEC variations associated with the earthquakes. For instance, a new method has been developed to mitigate the ionopheric effects in the Split Beam Interferometry (SBI) processing with directional filtering and an interpolation procedure. A new method has also been proposed for calculating the integral constant to improve the accuracy of the estimated ionospheric phase screen (IPS) from the SBI measurements. An effective method has been developed to estimate the IPS based on full-polarimetric SAR interferometry, which exploits the fact that ionospheric artifacts on an interferogram can be extracted based on the relationship between the Faraday Rotation (FR) angles and the Vertical Total Electronic Content (VTEC). For the Hong Kong area, the correlation between the SAR derived SBI measurements and the GPS derived the rate of TEC index (ROTI) measurements have been analyzed in both spatial and temporal domains. The SAR and GPS measurements have also been integrated to better map the three-dimensional (3D) TEC variations. For Objective 2, new methods have been developed and tested based on respectively the SBI measurements and FR angles to mitigate the ionospheric effects on InSAR measurements due the ionospheric TEC variations associated with earthquake events or solar activities. The SBI based methods have been tested with SAR data over the Hong Kong area, and areas affected by the Yushu, Darfield and Wenchuan earthquakes. The test results have shown that the long-wavelength ionospheric artifacts in these tested regions can be corrected effectively by using the proposed methods. The FR based method has been tested in an area in Alaska, U.S.A considering the good quality of the SAR data for that region. The test results have shown that the standard deviation of the corrected interferometric phase measurements can be significantly reduced, demonstrating clearly the effectiveness of the developed method.

515410.label: Major findings and research outcome
515410.value: (1) A directional filtering and interpolation method for mitigating the ionospheric effects in the Split Beam Interferometry (SBI) measurements (Hu et al., 2012). Ionospheric effects can be very significant in the SBI measurements. The proposed method exploits the different features between the spatial patterns of the azimuth streaks and the phase fringes due to ground motions in an interferogram. Significant improvements in the accuracy of the estimated azimuth displacements can be achieved with the developed directional filtering and interpolation method. (2) A novel method for calculating the integral constant in estimating and correcting the Ionospheric Phase Screen (IPS) in InSAR measurements. The proposed method is based on InSAR maps of both azimuth and range displacements. At the present, the azimuth displacement field can be generated by offset-tracking or a SBI procedure, but the range displacement field can only be estimated by an offset-tracking procedure. The test results have confirmed that the long-wavelength ionospheric artifacts in the non-coseismic regions could be corrected effectively by using the proposed method. (3) An effective method for estimating and correcting the IPS in InSAR measurements (Hu et al., 2012; Zhu et al., 2015). The proposed method is based on full-polarimetric SAR interferometry. The method exploits the fact that ionospheric artifacts on an SAR interferogram can be extracted based on the relationship between FR angles and the Vertical Total Electronic Content (VTEC). The FR angles and the VTEC maps are estimated first from two SAR images. The ionospheric phase artifacts of full-polarimetric interferograms are then calculated from the VTEC maps. An integrated phase model is finally created to jointly correct the ionospheric and the orbital phase errors. The test results have shown that the standard deviation of the corrected interferometric phase is reduced as much as 8 times, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed method. (4) The TEC variation results associated with the large seismic events and the Hong Kong area (Hu et al., 2012; 2013). The test results have shown that TEC variations are closely related to the studied seismic events, i.e., the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake and the 2010 Yushu and Darfield earthquakes. For the low latitude area such as Hong Kong, it is observed that the ionospheric scintillation can severely contaminate the InSAR measurements. (5) Other related algorithms (Wang et al., 2014a; 2014b; Zhang et al., 2014; Sun et al., 2015a) and some extensive test results (Wang et al., 2012; Hu et al., 2013; 2014a; 2014b; Sun et al., 2015b).

515410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515410.value: The project has made significant progress in estimating and correcting the IPS in InSAR measurements. The TEC variations determined in the project are also very useful to earthquake and ionosphere related research. It will be very useful to further investigate the relationships between the TEC variations and seismic events by carrying out more case studies.

515410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515410.value: Low frequency (e.g., L- and P-band) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data are sensitive to the ionospheric variations in the atmosphere. The ionospheric variations (due to solar activities and also associated with major earthquakes) can cause significant errors in SAR remote sensing, particularly in measuring ground deformation with Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) technique that is widely used for various scientific and practical applications. On the other hand, SAR data can be used to study the spatial-temporal patterns of ionospheric variations in fine scales, especially those associated with large earthquakes that have not been well understood. This project has made significant progress in developing new algorithms for estimating and correcting the ionospheric artifacts in InSAR measurements and in mapping ionospheric variations with SAR data.

515710.value: 用数据挖掘方法对建筑设备进行 使用数据挖掘方法对建筑设备进行故障预测

515710.label: Project Objectives
515710.value: Overall, the research objective is to test the hypothesis that data mining techniques can be applied to analyze, model and predict equipment failures to achieve better results than current approaches in equipment maintenance management. Models will be established from historical data for predicting the failure events and the Remaining Time To Failure (RTTF) for major components/parts in key production equipment, so that the components/parts can be repaired or replaced before failure or at an off-peak season. Different data mining models will be developed for different components/parts based on the equipment groups, maintenance and operational history. Models will possess visualization options to show clearly the decision paths, as well as the ranking of decision variables with respect to RTTF under various conditions. Identify correlated and sequential failures of major components/parts with significant support from equipment failure data series, so that if one failure occurs on one or more components/parts, precautions or corrective actions can be taken on the related components/parts. The research will also explore the effectiveness of the discovered patterns in assisting root-cause analysis on equipment failures. Sharing the same data sources with the current equipment management system, a prototype decision support module incorporating the above data mining models will be developed as a standalone application for failure analysis by an equipment management team. The decision support module will be tested and validated in real life situations.

515710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515710.value: Construction equipment is a key resource, and contractors owning large equipment fleet take all necessary measures to maximize the equipment utilization and minimize the equipment failures. Although most contractors implement scheduled maintenance programs and carry out periodic inspections/repairs on their construction equipment, it is still a difficult task to predict the occurrence of a specific failure of a piece of equipment in the short or long term. According to a survey in the United States, approximately 46% of the major equipment repairs followed upon an unexpected failure. As a result of such breakdowns, the equipment unit has to be pulled out of production and repaired on site, or brought to the shop for repair. In addition to the impact on the project, related problems arise from these unexpected failures, including high costs for emergency repairs on a remote jobsite, and high storage-costs for a large number of spare parts. Although it is not possible to predict all failure events, a slight improvement in their prediction represents a significant saving in time and cost for a large contractor. Currently many contractors take such measures as monitoring and tracking of the condition of equipment to identify signs of failure or near-failure; oil sampling tests; conducting repairs/replacements of some components based on the manufacturer’s recommendations or on industrial benchmarks on the expected life of equipment components. However the effectiveness of such strategies is still unsatisfactory because large numbers of unexpected failures still occur. This research tackles this prediction problem through advanced data analysis of equipment operational and maintenance history. The research is motivated by (1) The contractors have collected large amounts of data on equipment maintenance and failures; (2) failures of construction equipment are closely related to its operational and maintenance history; and (3) advanced computer tools such as data mining can help to extract rules and patterns from large amounts of data on equipment failures. This research will develop predictive and descriptive models of equipment failures by applying data mining techniques to equipment failure events. Questions such as “what is the time remaining until the next major failure for this piece of equipment?”, “what are the failures which occur frequently, what are the patterns of sequential failures, and what are the prevailing conditions associated with these failures?” can perhaps be answered. Models developed and rules discovered from this research will also benefit the whole industry in its management of heavy equipment. 建筑设备是建筑施工的主要资源之一,拥有大量施工设备的承建商尽其所能增加设备使用并减少设备的故障.尽管大部分承包商已经使用了设备维修保养计算机管理系统,并定期检查/维修其设备,对一台设备进行长期或短期的故障预测仍然非常困难.根据一项在美国的调查,46%的主要设备故障为非预见之类.故障发生之后,设备只能停止使用,在现场或送到修理厂维修.除了对工程项目的直接影响之外,其他的后果包括偏远工地紧急维修增加费用,以及备用零件过多带来的存储费用. 尽管不可能预测所有的故障,对设备故障预测准确率的些许提高都会给一个大型承包商带来可观的时间和费用的节省. 当前很多承包商都采取措施控制预测设备故障,包括检测设备的运行状况,油样测试,根据设备手册或行业统计对主部件定期维修更换等.本研究利用当前收集的大量设备运行及维修保养的数据采用先进数据分析的方法解决设备故障预测的问题,研究基于以下之推动因素: (1) 承包商收集了大量设备维修保养和故障的数据;(2)建筑设备故障与它的使用,维修密切相关, 以及(3)先进的计算机工具例如数据挖掘可以帮助我们从大量的设备故障数据里找出规则和规律. 本研究将运用数据挖掘的方法对设备故障建立预测模型.回答诸如”这台设备到下一策故障还有多少时间?”的问题.本研究建立的模型和找到的规律将可推广到整个行业建筑设备的管理.

515710.label: Major findings and research outcome
515710.value: Reliability analysis and failure prediction of construction equipment has been conducted using data mining and time series approach in this research project. The research findings include (1) data mining and time series approach can make better prediction in construction equipment failures in terms of various reliability metrics: remaining time to failure, expected number of failures, availability, system reliability in a forthcoming operational period, etc. in comparison with the classical statistics based approaches; (2) with the proposed data mining approach, analysis of construction equipment reliability can be conducted at the system level and subsystem level to assist decisions in construction equipment operations. Subsystem criticality is defined to identify the most critical subsystems in a piece of construction equipment, so that focused attention can be given to the critical few with planning of management actions ahead of time; (3) the contractor can benefit from the proposed data mining approach for construction equipment reliability analysis with visualized fact-based decision support modules, including optimizing maintenance schedules based on historical and forecasted information, supporting equipment allocations to different sizes of projects, and supporting equipment replacement. With full financial support from the project fund, an MPhil student worked on the project under the supervision of the PI, and was awarded an MPhil degree with the topic “Construction Equipment Reliability Analysis and Failure Prediction”, after 2 years of full time study. The research findings were disseminated in the proceedings of the International Symposium on Automation and Robotics in Construction, June 26, 2012 – June 29, 2012, Eindhoven, Netherlands, and the 5th International Conference on Construction and Project Management (ICCPM2014), 28-30 August, 2014, Taipei, Taiwan (won one of the best paper awards). The PI and the student have two journal publications in the Journal of advanced management science, and Gerontechnology. One journal paper on construction equipment replacement based on failure data analysis is under preparation for submission to Automation in Construction, Elsevier.

515710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515710.value: Through the research works conducted in this project, the PI demonstrated a new methodology for equipment reliability analysis which is only possible with recent advancement of computer science in intelligent data analysis and data modeling, which is based on equipment operational history and facts and a set of machine learning models. The approach has attracted interests from local contractors and international researchers. The PI will further generalize this research area into new but related research areas on asset management, building maintenance management. Research collaborations with professors from the North Carolina state university, university of Toronto, and contractors have been made with joint research proposals submitted or to be submitted to different funding agencies. With large investment of infrastructures in China mainland, the construction equipment industry developed very quickly over the past many years, there is a practical need for research and development in equipment operations and maintenance management, I have been in collaboration and will further work with researchers from China mainland, such as Dalian University of Technology, Dalian, China to further advance research in this area through joint research proposals and consulting projects in the future. Thanks to RGC for providing the funding for exploration and study in this important research area.

515710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515710.value: Construction equipment is a key resource, and contractors owning large equipment fleet take all necessary measures to minimize the equipment failures. In the meantime, the equipment failure, as it occurs, may cause interruption of construction works with collateral consequences. Reliability analysis and failure prediction is conducted using data mining and time series method based on the equipment operational and maintenance history to forecast equipment reliability metrics and mostly likely timing of failure events. The research findings prove that the accuracy of analysis and data mining based forecasting results is much better than the traditional statistics-based approaches, such as power law model. The data mining based forecasting of reliability metrics have significant values to industry practitioners who can rely on the forecasted failure information to make informed decisions on equipment repair, maintenance, allocation, and replacement, therefore reducing the loss of time and productivity related to equipment unavailability in construction projects. The approach to identifying the critical subsystem of construction equipment based on historical data is also proposed in the research to let the equipment managers to focus on the critical few and apply the same data mining approach to subsystem level for reliability analysis and failure prediction.

515810.label: Project Objectives
515810.value: To model heat and mass transport through heterogeneous porous fibrous materials by applying the fractal theory. To develop the theoretical frame work for engineering the fractal-like porous architecture of fibrous materials for different applications.

To develop the theoretical frame work for engineering the fractal-like porous architecture of fibrous materials for different applications.

515810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515810.value: Heat and mass transport properties of porous fibrous materials are extremely important for many different applications such as thermal insulation, fibrous scaffolds for tissue engineering and functional clothing materials. So far, the optimization analysis of the transport properties of fibrous materials is largely based on models in Euclidean geometry. Such method requires huge computational cost and makes it infeasible in optimizing multiple geometric parameters of relatively complex heterogeneous fibrous materials. Although fractal theory, which is advantageous in the optimization analysis as simplified analytical solutions can be derived, has been applied to porous media, existing models are limited to the porous media with homogenously distributed pores or channels. This project is therefore proposed to apply fractal theory to model the heat and mass transport through heterogeneous porous fibrous materials. The improved understanding from the theoretical modeling and analysis will then be applied for engineering heterogeneous fibrous materials with enhanced transport and barrier properties for various applications. 多孔纖維材料的熱和質之傳遞性能对于其許多不同的應用，例如绝熱，生物支架和功能衣物材料，是極端重要的。 到目前為止， 對纖維材料之傳遞性能的優化分析都是根據在歐幾裡德的幾何模型上进行的。 這樣的方法要求巨大的計算成本，并且不能對相對複雜的非均質纖維狀材料實行優化分析。分形理論有利在優化中簡化分析。 雖然分形理論已应用于多孔媒介，現有的模型局限于均質多孔媒介。 因此本項目提議采用分形理論来对非均質纖維狀材料的熱和質傳輸建立理论模型。 通過此理论模型加深对现象的理解，從而对非均質纖維狀材料實施工程設計。

515810.label: Realisation of objectives
515810.value: We have achieved 100% towards the stated project objectives. With regard to the first objective, we have accomplished the following: • Modelled gas and liquid permeation through unsaturated porous fibrous media based on fractal theory and Monte Carlo simulation. We established the expression of relative permeability as a function of porosity, the fractal dimension of tortuous capillaries, the area fractal dimension of pore, saturation and capillary pressure. The model predictions were compared with the available experimental data and past models predictions, and good agreement was found. • Analyzed the effect of structural parameters of fibrous materials, including porosity, tortuosity fractal dimension, pore area fractal dimensions, water phase and gas phase fractal dimensions, on the the water and gas relative permeabilities. It was found that the dimensionless permeability decreases markedly with increasing tortuosity fractal dimension. However, there was only a small decrease in the water and gas relative permeabilities when the tortuosity fractal dimension increased. • Modelled heat transfer through branched structure made of single-walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs). It was found this novel structure can have fast heat transfer and potentially good heat dissipator. • Conducted exploratory theoretical investigation on the formation and transport of liquid water on fibre surface. With regard to the second objective, we have accomplished the following: • Analyzed the optimization of the fractal like architecture of porous fibrous materials for wind/water resistant fabric and thermal insulation & breathable fabrics. • Found that the ratio of dimensionless permeability over dimensionless effective diffusivity of the fractal like architecture of porous fibrous materials decreased with the decrease of porosity and tortuosity fractal dimension, respectively, which implied that lower porosity and tortuosity fractal dimension were beneficial to wind/water resistant fabric. • Found that there is a maximum ratio of dimensionless total effective thermal conductivity over dimensionless effective diffusivity when porosity is 0.92. In addition, it was observed that the ratio of dimensionless total effective thermal conductivity over dimensionless effective diffusivity increased with tortuosity fractal dimension, which implied lower tortuosity fractal dimension was beneficial to clothing insulation, as it reduced the ratio of dimensionless total effective thermal conductivity over dimensionless effective diffusivity. • The optimization results indicated that fabrics with more aligned fibers were preferred for protective clothing, as the low tortuosity fractal dimension implied fibers in the fibrous materials should be more aligned.

515810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515810.value: Based on the research findings and models developed in this study, further investigations may be directed towards (1) optimization of the fractal like architecture of porous fibrous materials for variouys applications such as clothing materials, filters, gas diffusion layers in fuel cells; (2) fabrication of optimized heterogeneous fibrous materials for various applications.

515810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515810.value: Heat and mass transport phenomena exist in fibrous materials for many applications including protective fabrics, clothing insulation, filters, gas diffusion layers in fuel cells. Due to the complexity of the transport processes in porous fibrous media, although they have been studied for many years, the effects of the geometric parameters of the fibrous materials on the heat and mass transport properties of fibrous materials are still not fully elucidated. The understanding and modeling of these processes is significant since it can lead to the optimization and innovation of fibrous materials for various applications. In particular, this study laid the foundation for developing heterogeneous fibrous materials for enhanced performance in various applications.

516510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
516510.value: Three-dimensional (3D) auxetic textile structures are non-conventional fabrics that demonstrate negative Poisson’s ratio (NPR) effect. When properly understood and integrated with the advanced textile fabrication technologies, this phenomenon can be exploited for special applications such as smart protective system and damping materials with high energy absorption capacity. The most important point to the realization of the auxetic or NPR effect of these fabrics is the proper design of the fabric architecture and its manufacturing process. A survey of the literature demonstrated that little work has been done in the study of this important phenomenon of textile materials, especially that of 3D textile structures. Therefore there is a need for a basic understanding of auxetic effect, mechanical performance and manufacturing process of such textile structures. More specifically, the project will deal with fundamental issues of the structure and performance of the 3D auxetic fabrics. Based on previous work done by the applicant, a special textile manufacturing process in the combination of weaving and knitting technologies will be developed to produce the 3D auxetic fabrics. Both theoretical and experimental investigations will be conducted to study their auxetic properties and mechanical performance. The unit-cell model will be established and the multi-scale approach and the finite element method (FEM) will be used to simulate the deformation behaviors and mechanical performance of the 3D auxetic fabrics made of different non-auxetic yarns and structure parameters. As an example, the 3D auxetic fabrics with required auxetic effect will be fabricated for smart protective system. 三維負泊松比紡織結構是具有負泊松比效應的非常規紡織物。通過分析和運用特殊的紡織編織技術，能夠實現編織負泊松比織物並將其運用於特殊領域，如：智能防護系統和高能量吸收性阻尼材料。實現織物的負泊松比效應關鍵在於織物結構的設計和編織工藝技術。通過文獻檢索，可以發現對紡織品的負泊松比性能研究較少，特別是三維負泊松比織物結構。因此，有必要對這類織物的負泊松比效應，機械性能和織造過程進行基礎性研究。 更具體地說， 本項目將研究三維負泊松比織物結構和性能的基礎問題。基於項目申請人的前期工作，一種綜合機織和針織的特殊編織技術將運用於織造三維負泊松比織物。本項目將實驗研究和理論研究並行，研究這類織物的負柏松比效應和力學性能。此外，基於單和多尺度的有限元分析將運用於使用不同紗線和結構編織所成的三維負泊松比織物。最後，作為個案分析，項目所編織的三維負泊松比織物將運用於智能防護系統。

516510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
516510.value: 3D auxetic textile structures are non-conventional fabrics having negative Poisson’s ratio effect. They laterally expand when stretched or laterally shrink when compressed, and have many particular properties such as enhanced shear stiffness, increased indentation resistance and improved energy absorption properties. In this research, a novel kind of 3D auxetic textile structure is firstly designed and fabricated on a prototype developed. Then, the compression deformation behaviors and mechanical properties of 3D fabrics with different structural parameters and yarns are experimentally and theoretically studied. Geometrical, elastic and finite models are proposed to predict their Poisson’s ratios. The significance and value of this research is to provide a basic understanding on the structure characteristic, formation principle, fabrication method and mechanical performance of 3D auxetic fabrics. The investigation will provide direct insights into the design and fabrication of auxetic materials based on 3D textile structures. Thanks to their unusual properties, these auxetic textile structures will enable new applications such as active protective system, damping materials and enhanced performance composites. The investigation will promote the new development of textile products to increase the competitive capacity of the Hong Kong textile and fashion industry.

517010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
517010.value: 高血壓血管組織重構的生物力學

517010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
517010.value: Hypertension, a chronic medical condition in which the blood pressure is elevated, affects many people in Hong Kong. That hypertension leads to ill health is well known, since it will cause stroke, heart attack, heart failure, and other complications. Under high blood pressure, tissue structure and property in blood vessel wall are remodeled. The tissue remodeling of blood vessels in hypertension, such as vessel wall becomes thickening and stiffer, is very important to health because it affects the functions of blood vessels and many organs. In clinical practice, medical doctors prescribe pills for lowering blood pressure. However, it is uncertain whether lowering blood pressure can reverse the vessel wall tissue structure and property. The molecular mechanisms of hypertension have been the central theme in biological investigations. DNA is the molecule that carries genetic information, and makes RNA which makes proteins in tissue remodeling in hypertension. However, the connection between the bio-molecules and the mechanical forces in hypertension, or how genes are responded to the changes of blood pressure, is little known, but can be revealed by determining the Constitutive Equation of the remodeling tissue. The present project has three aims. The first aim is to study the changes of structural and mechanical properties of blood vessels in response to raising or lowering blood pressures in laboratory rats. The second aim is to describe the spatial distribution of each kind of the bio-molecules in the cells and tissues as a tensor. The tensor is a mathematical concept used to describe the geometrical configuration of a system of vectors in a 3-dimentional space and has been used widely. Endothelin-1 (ET-1) and procollagen in the vessel specimen, which are the examples of these proteins that relate to the vascular tissue remodeling, will be labeled with fluorescent markers, and their images will be taken for analysis to determine their geometrical configurations in the vessel. The third step is to determine the relationship between the mechanical stresses acting in the blood vessel wall and the tensors of the bio-molecules in vascular remodeling. This relationship is the Constitutive Equation of the remodeling tissue. The information obtained from this research will serve to link protein synthesis with vascular mechanics and DNA mechanics, which is done with the introduction of the molecular configuration tensor and the relevant constitutive equation. The results of these studies will also help to generate new strategies for the diagnosis and treatment of hypertension. 高血壓是指血管內的血壓持續高於正常標準. 据估計, 香港有超過50萬人患有高血壓. 高血壓.可引致中風、心肌梗死、心腎功能衰竭等致命疾病. 當血壓增高后, 血管壁的结构和特性發生組織重構. 高血壓引致的血管組織重構, 例如血管壁增厚和变硬, 会影響血管的功能从而影響人体內許多器官. 治疗方面, 医生結予高血壓病人物以降低血压. 然而, 尚不清楚降低血压是否可以逆转因高血壓引致的血管壁增厚和变硬. 清楚理解高血壓的分子機制是目前研究的主要方向. 我们的研究重点是通过构建血管組織重構組成方程式去理解力与高血壓的生物分子机制之间的關系, 即基因是如何应对高血壓引致血管內力的改变. 本研究计划有三個研究目標: (1) 升高或降低大白鼠的血压后, 实验测量血管壁结构和特性的改变. (2) 描述生物分子內皮素-1(ET-1)和微晶膠原蛋白(Procollagen)在血管壁的分布成为張量. 張量是一個數學概念用于描述矢量在三度空间的分布. (3) 确定作用在血管壁的力与內皮素-1張量和微晶膠原蛋白張量的關系, 或稱为血管組織重構組成方程式. 從本研究计划获得的新知识將有助于理解高血壓的分子機制和制定新的诊断和治療高血压的方法.

517110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
517110.value: 異位性皮膚炎是一種常見的慢性過敏性皮膚炎症，其病發率在過往數十年間持續上升。異位性皮膚炎最主要特徵是皮膚搔癢，且會反覆發作。搔癢難當確實嚴重影響患者之生活質素[1]。根據澳洲一保健網站 (WrongDiagnosis.com) 於2009年發放之數據指出，每個國家約有5.5%的總人口受此病症困擾，因此預測約有378,000本土人受此病影響。 在過去二十年，一般主張使用相對較安全有效的濕裹衣形式來治療兒童的嚴重及/或頑固性異位性皮膚炎。但由於濕裹衣只能短暫有效地舒緩搔癢情況，暫時緩解嚴重異位性皮膚炎，並只是短期改善使用者的生活質素[5-6]。每件濕裹衣約只能維持一小時之效用。況且有許多有關使用濕裹衣以治療異位性皮膚炎所引致的問題仍有待解決[4]。例如: 穿著濕裹衣會令患者皮膚濕冷而感到不舒適。自2004年，韓與梁共同成功研發使用中藥配方以補充異位性皮膚炎的標準療法，效果亦很顯著[8-10]。 務求改善自願性長時間穿著問題及提供針對異位性皮膚炎持續有效之治療，本研究目的志在設計及研發出一件含傳統中草藥成份並能有效治療異位性皮膚炎而無任何不良效果的衣物。由於使用傳統中草藥以治療異位性皮膚炎能有效地改善生活質素，並能減低敷用皮質激素類藥物，從而減少藥物對患有中度至嚴重異位性皮膚炎的兒童所帶來的不良反應[5-6]。加上近期發展的微粒膠囊技術證實能有效地應用於皮膚護理方面[7]。此方法在於能控制膠囊內藥物逐漸釋出藥理活性成份經由皮膚吸收以解決皮膚相關等問題。故此本研究運用此相關技術將含有用以治療異位性皮膚炎的傳統中草藥精華之微粒膠囊黏附於一般天然衣物纖維的纖維壁上以替代濕裹衣使用。並採用乳膠硬固技術以製造那些含有傳統中草藥之微粒膠囊[7]。 本研究計劃將可達至之成果能讓378,000人受惠，其中包括在香港需要有效治療的兒童和成人。與此同時，亦可減輕患者的父母及其照顧者對患者之料理負擔。再者，本研究所得出的方法成果能應用於其他疾病之有效治療上。

517110.label: Major findings and research outcome
517110.value: In preparation of microcapsules encapsulated Chinese Herbal Medicine (CHM) for treatment of atopic dermatitis, we have successfully designed and developed the efficient method of preparation of microcapsules loaded with CHM. To maximize the herb loading inside the microcaspules and increasing encapsulation efficiency, the optimum conditions (including core-shell ratio =1:2; chitosan concentration = 6% (w/v); agitation speed = 1100 rpm; and cross-linking time = 90 minutes) for microcapsule preparation were determined by using orthogonal array analysis. In addition, relative importance of the preparation parameters is identified in the order: core-shell ratio, agitation speed, chitosan concentration and cross-linking time. Through the analysis of the Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, the CHM has been completely encapsulated into chitosan microcapsules and the in vitro drug release of CHM from the microcapsules in pH5.4 and pH5.0 phosphate buffered saline (PBS) and in 37C temperature is almost completed after the initial 48 hours. To determine if the microcapsules bound on cotton fabric with textile binder had toxic effect on skin, in vitro skin toxicity test was performed. The cytotoxicity test showed that the microcapsules with textile binder had no toxic effect on cells and showed good cellular compatibility. It proves that the microcapsules loaded with CHM bound on cotton fabric are able to use for clinical treatment. (See item 1 and 2 in Part C8 and item 1 in Part C9) To investigate the patient acceptability and efficacy of a garment impregnated with CHM-containing microcapsules for patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD), ten AD patients were recruited and worn the garment with CHM microcapsules each night for two weeks. 40% of AD patients reported that the garment with CHM microcapsules was of good acceptability. This wearer trial result generates important information to help improve AD treatment.

517110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
517110.value: The project deliverables provide a great potential for further development of garments impregnated with CHM-containing microcapsules for clinical treatment. The major problem of current prototype is not able to encapsulate the sufficient amount of CHM inside microcapsules for effective treatment. In addition, the majority of wearer found the garment uncomfortable to wear. The proposed course of action is to develop a natural non-toxic carrier which could hold more CHM and provide similar releasing performance with the microcapsules to human skin. Such carrier bound on garment will provide comfortable to wear.

517110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
517110.value: The project is a mid-stream nature. The significance and the value of the research project are that the method used in this research can be applied to provide the effective treatment of other illnesses using Chinese herbal medicine. In addition, the ultimate deliverable is the wearable garments with Chinese herbal medicine for treatment of atopic dermatitis in patients. More than 10,000 patients with atopic dermatitis that use this garment are beneficial for improvement of their quality of life.

517710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
517710.value: This project is to carry out systematic investigation of a new class of in-line devices and sensors based on mode-coupling in silica optical micro/nanofibers. Optical micro/nanofibers have received significant attention recently for their potential applications in micro/nano-scale photonic systems. Various micro/nanofibers devices and sensors (e.g., evanescent wave couplers and sensors, ring-resonators and lasers, Mach-Zehnder and other type of interferometers), most of them exploit the strong external evanescent field of these thin fibers, have been reported. However, little or no work on micro/nanofiber in-line mode-coupling devices, which are more compact and would add new functionalities to microscale photonic systems, has been reported so far. We will fabricate micro/nanofibers with circular and elliptical (or square-like) cross-sections and inscribe long period gratings (LPGs) and polarization rocking filters (PRFs) in such micro/nanofibers. We will use a femtosecond infrared (IR) laser and/or a CO2 laser to inscribe such LPGs/PRFs. We plan to carry out a series of experimental and theoretical investigations of the mode-coupling induced by refractive index and/or waveguide geometry modulation resulted from femtosecond IR laser/CO2 laser irradiations; and to evaluate the transmission, polarization, and other properties of the in-line gratings (i.e., LPGs and PRFs). We also plan to carry out theoretical and experimental investigation of the possible applications of such in-line gratings (i.e., LPGs and PRFs), including: (1) study of the response of the gratings to external refractive index, temperature, acoustic vibration, bend, twist, and etc.; (2) design and construction of micro/nanofiber in-line modal interferometers/polarimeters based on these gratings, and examination of their possible applications as micro/nanofiber comb-filters and interferometric sensors. The fabrication of grating structures directly on micro/nanofibers would allow for the creation of a novel class of in-line devices and sensors. Possible applications of such micro/nanofiber devices include: micro/nanofiber based wavelength/polarization filters for signal transmission and manipulation, spectrum tailored (e.g., flattened) micro/nanofiber supercontinuum sources, in-fiber interferometric comb filters and sensors, and wavelength-encoded evanescent wave refractive index sensors that would have better performance than the intensity-modulation type sensors made of micro/nanofibers without gratings in them. 此项目的任务是研究基于微/纳米光纤的在线器件和传感器，器件的基本机理是利用微/纳米光纤的光学模式之间的耦合现象。 由于微纳光纤在微纳米级光子系统中具有潜在应用前景，所以微/纳米光纤的研究越来越受重视。目前，大多数已报道的微纳米器件都是利用微纳米光纤的消逝场特性。到目前为止，基本上还没有基于微纳米光纤中光学模式之间耦合的器件研究报道。此类基于模式耦合的器件具有更紧凑的结构，更有利于在微纳米光子系统集成中应用。 我们将制作具有圆形和椭圆型截面的微纳米光纤，并将在这些光纤上制作长周期光栅和偏振摇摆滤波器。我们将利用红外飞秒激光和二氧化碳激光制作此类长周期光栅。 我们将对由红外飞秒激光和二氧化碳激光引起的折射率或者波导结构调制而产生的光学模式耦合进行一系列实验和理论研究，并对微纳米光纤光栅（长周期光栅和偏振摇摆滤波器）的传输、偏振态等光学特性进行研究。 我们将对此类微纳米光纤光栅的潜在实际应用进行理论和实验研究，主要包括：（1）研究微纳米光纤光栅对外界折射率、温度、弯曲、应力等物理量的响应；（2）设计基于这些微纳米光纤的模式干涉仪/偏振干涉仪，以及研究它们在微纳米梳妆滤波器和干涉型传感器中应用前景。 在微纳米光纤上直接实现光栅结构将开启一类新型的在线器件和传感器。此类微纳米器件的潜在应用包括：微纳米光纤波长/偏振态滤波器、光谱整形（如，光谱平坦）、微纳米光纤超连续光源、在线干涉滤波或干涉仪、以及波长调制的消逝场折射率计（此类折射率计比无光栅的基于强度调制的微纳米光纤折射率计具有更好的性能）等。

517710.label: Realisation of objectives
517710.value: Objective 1: The modal characteristics of circular microfibers with diameters from 1 to 10 μm were studied by using finite element method (FEM) and mode couplings were evaluated by using coupled local-mode theory. A pulsed CO2 laser was used to inscribe long period gratings (LPGs) in microfibers with diameters above 5 μm. A femtosecond infrared laser was used to inscribe LPGs in microfibers with smaller diameters, since the grating pitch for such thin fibers becomes significantly smaller than the spot-size of the CO2 laser and it is difficult to write first-order gratings with the CO2 laser. High quality LPGs were made on microfibers with diameters from 1.5 to 7 μm. Objective achieved. Objective 2: Mode-coupling in highly birefringent (Hi-Bi) elliptical microfibers was studied numerically by using FEM and the coupled local-mode theory. The Hi-Bi microfibers were made by firstly“cutting” away the cladding over a short section of a standard single mode fiber (SMF) and then taper-drawn the SMF to wavelength or sub-wavelength scale. The pulsed CO2 laser was used to inscribe high-order LPGs and the femtosecond laser was used to write first and high-order LPGs. High quality LPGs were made in elliptical microfibers with major-diameter from 2.5 to 5 μm and ellipticity from 0.6 to 0.8. Strong polarization dependence resonances were observed in these LPGs. Objective achieved. Objective 3: The responses of both CO2 and femtosecond laser writing LPGs to refractive index (RI) and temperature were investigated. Experimental tests were carried out for both circular and elliptical microfiber-based LPGs and for both naked LPGs and LPGs encapsulated within a glass tube. The variation of refractive index was achieved by using different RI liquids and by heating up the liquid to change its RI. Direct testing of responses to vibration and bend was found difficult because of the very small dimensions of the microfibers. We instead fabricated microfibers suspended and encapsulated within a protective tube, and carried vibration (acceleration) test. Objective achieved. Objective 4: Formations of polarization rocking filters (PRFs) in standard SMFs and Hi-Bi microfibers were studied theoretically with the Jones Matrix method and numerically with a code based on the Full Vectorial Finite Difference Beam Propagation Method and coupled-mode theory. First and higher order PRFs and LPGs were fabricated by use of a point-by-point method that comprises periodic mechanical twisting of the fiber and heating by a scanning CO2 laser beam. Strong resonant polarization conversion was achieved. Objective achieved.

517710.label: Major findings and research outcome
517710.value: Both pulsed CO2 and femtosecond lasers can be used to inscribe high-quality LPGs in microfibers [J6]. It becomes difficult to use CO2-laser to inscribe first-order LPGs in microfibers with diameters <5 μm. Femtosecond infrared lasers can be focused down to very small spot-size and are ideal for LPGs inscription in thin microfibers. LPGs on microfibers generally have small temperature sensitivity and very high sensitivity to RI, and can be made very compact. We have made a 10-period LPG (150-μm long) on a 2.4 μm-diameter microfiber and achieved resonant coupling of 25 dB. Hi-Bi microfibers with diameters from 2.5 to 5 μm and ellipticity from 0.6 to 0.8 were fabricated. Such microfibers can maintain a linear polarization state and have small insertion loss (<0.5dB). The microfibers guide a small number of modes [J6 and C5]. LPGs in the Hi-Bi microfibers were made by pulsed CO2 and femtosecond laser techniques [J6, C4]. A first-order LPG made on a Hi-Bi microfiber with a major-diameter of 2.8 μm demonstrated polarization-dependent resonant couplings of 19.2 and 15.2 dB at resonant wavelengths of 1532.7 and 1614.2 nm; and the device length is only 300 μm. High-order LPGs were also fabricated and the response of a high-order LPG to RI was measured to be 4623 nm/RIU in water [C4]. Analytical and numerical studies show that efficient PRFs or polarization converters can be made on Hi-Bi microfibers [J4, J5 and C3]. PRFs were successfully fabricated by twisting and heating up Hi-Bi microfibers with a CO2 laser. A 3 mm-long PRF made on a microfiber with a major-diameter of 2.8 μm demonstrated a peak-polarization-conversion efficiency of 99% at the resonance wavelength of 1556.4 nm and the spectral bandwidth of the PRF is 74 nm [J4]. This is the first PRFs made on such thin microfibers. Rocking SMFs also produce LPGs with novel characteristics [J2]. An important part of the work that would have significant practical values is the successful encapsulation of microfiber inside a silica capillary [J6] and fabrication of suspended-microfiber by selective pressurization/inflation and tapering a photonic crystal fiber [J3 and C5]. The encapsulation overcomes the problems of contamination and fragility of the non-encapsulated fibers, and makes it possible to develop practical microfiber-based photonic devices. With the encapsulated microfibers, we demonstrated robust high-sensitivity RI sensors [J1, J3, J6, C2 and C5], accelerometers [J3], temperature [J6 and C5] and gas-pressure [J6 and C5] sensors.

517710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
517710.value: The successful encapsulation of microfiber inside a silica capillary and fabrication of suspended-microfiber photonic microcells overcomes the problems of contamination and fragility of the non-encapsulated fibers, and makes it possible to develop a range of practical microfiber-based photonic devices. We plan to make further studies of these microcells for in-fiber amplifiers by filling dye solutions and other materials into the cell and for absorption-based gas and liquid concentration sensors, refractive index sensors, and robust accelerometers. Attempt will be made to attract industrial funds for these studies.

517710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
517710.value: Microfibers with circular and elliptical cross-sections were investigated. Long period gratings (LPGs) and polarization rocking filters (PRFs) were fabricated by use of a femtosecond infrared laser micro-machining system and a CO2 laser heating-and-drawing system. The transmission, polarization and mode-coupling properties of such LPGs and PRFs are studied. The applications of microfibers and microfiber-based LPGs and PRFs for comb-filters and for refractive index, temperature, pressure and acceleration sensors were investigated. Compared with the standard-size fiber devices, the microfiber-based LPGs and PRFs are generally very compact with a device length of hundreds of micrometers, and have smaller sensitivity to temperature and much higher sensitivity to surrounding refractive index. Novel photonic microcells were made by encapsulating microfibers within glass capillaries and by fabricating suspended-microfibers directly from a photonic crystal fiber via a pressurization/inflation and tapering process. The encapsulation overcomes the problems of contamination and fragility of the non-encapsulated fibers, and makes it possible to develop practical microfiber-based photonic devices. With the encapsulated microfibers, we demonstrated robust high-sensitivity refractive index sensors, accelerometers, temperature and gas-pressure sensors. Grating structures have been directly inscribed in the encapsulated microfibers, allowing the creation of a range of robust in-line devices and sensors.

517810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
517810.value: Nonlinear behaviors are ubiquitous in all kinds of engineering systems, physical systems, chemical systems, and bio-physiological systems, and the challenges that these raise are also fundamental in many other disciplines and areas of research such as life sciences, neuroscience, social ecology and economics. Recent advances in life sciences, neurosciences, and space observation by satellites etc have led to a great demand in signal processing of the intriguing nonlinear mechanisms in an explosion of data. Therefore, estimation, modeling and analysis of nonlinear behaviors in complex nonlinear systems have considerable significance both to theoretical research and engineering practice for scientists and engineers to understand and characterize the underlying mechanism of the nonlinear behaviors of interest. Nonlinear systems usually demonstrate complicated dynamic behaviors. How to identify a parsimonious system model and to reveal the core dynamic behaviors and features of the system are key challenges in the literature. The aim of this research is to develop methods for the estimation, modeling and analysis of severely nonlinear systems, to develop complimentary nonlinear frequency domain identification and analysis methods, and to study a considerably large class of nonlinear systems that are frequently encountered in scientific research and engineering practice defined by both time-domain and frequency-domain characteristics. Throughout the research study of this project, the exemplars will be used as case studies, including analysis and design of novel spring-damping systems by exploiting nonlinearities, modeling and analysis of neuronal systems in locusts to reveal the link between motion behaviors and neuronal activity, modeling of spatio-temporal systems such as wave propagation and so on. The objective is to establish a systematic and theoretical framework that can be used to analyze the large quantity of data collected from different sources (e.g., engineering platforms, neuronal activities) and to identify dynamic nonlinear models, and to characterize core dynamic nonlinear behaviors and features of the systems of interest. 非线性行为广泛存在于工程，物理，化学和生物系统之中，非线性问题也同样是生命科学，社会生态和经济学普遍存在的问题。空间科学和生命科学的发展更促使了对非线性行为机理的研究和应用。非线性系统通常具有复杂的动态行为。怎样辨识出一个结构简单的系统模型，怎样去把握，估计和理解一个非线性系统的主导动态特性，是研究的关键问题。本课题针对强非线性系统的信号估计，建模与分析，旨在研究新的有效的系统的辨识和分析方法，尤其是对于其中一类特殊的具有Volterra series展开的非线性系统研究新型的频域分析方法。应用例子研究包括非线性弹簧阻尼系统的分析和设计，神经系统的建模与分析等。预期目标是建立一套有效的系统的信号处理方法，可以应用在不同系统（比如工程系统，神经系统等）的数据处理，建模分析和设计中。

517810.label: Major findings and research outcome
517810.value: (1) A robust control method is proposed for nonlinear system identification, which can make full use of well-developed robust control theories to address nonlinear system identification problems, and would be a general approach to nonlinear system identifcation, neural network learning, classificiation, signal processing and filter design. Refer to Publications [2,10,22]. (2) A robost kernel learning based approach to spatio-tempral nonlinear system identification is developed, which can simultaneously estimate important system physical parameters. Refer to publications [1,16,20]. (3) A systematic frequncy domain method for nonlinear analysis and design with applications to vibration control is established, which provides a significant tool for the analysis, design and optimization of nonlinear systems in terms of output response. Refer to publications [3-9, 11-15, 17]. (4) Novel concepts related to nonlinear system stability and Voterra-type convergence are proposed, which provide the first time a novel insight into understanding of nonlinear dynamics in terms of Volterra series expansion. Refer to publications [14,17]. (5) A X-shape structure is proposed for realization of beneficial nonlinearity in vibration control for desired nonlinear stiffness and damping design. Refer to publications [18,19,21].

517810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
517810.value: (1) The robust control method will be further investigated for complex nonlienar system identification and signal processing, both in theory and practical application such as time-series data prediction and patten recognitation of big data. (2) The frequncy domain method for nonlinear analysis and design with the nCOS approach will be further developed both in theory and applications, targeting at a well developed general theory and analysis tool for analysis, design and optimization of nonlinear data. (3) The X-shape structure will be investigated further from a bio-inspired approach, which potentially provides a powerful and passive solution to many engineering problems for passive vibration isolation and control.

517810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
517810.value: Nonlinear dynamics are existing and involved in everywhere of enginerring practice and our daily life. Therefore, understanding (including analysis and design) of nonlinear phenomenoa is extremely important to increase our knowledge to handle and treat varous engineering problems in a more environmental-friendly and sustainable manner. This project developed several effective and efficient methods for understanding and characterizing nonlinear features and nonlinear dynamics both in the time and frequency domain, which can greatly facilite various engineering practices in the analysis and design of nonlinear systems or nonlinear data.

518710.value: 供应商社会责任发展对供应道德风险的作用：中国食品与飲料制造业研究

518710.label: Project Objectives
518710.value: To test the association between the buyer’s SRSD adoption and the supplier’s CSR adoption. To test the association between the supplier’s CSR adoption and the buyer’s perceived supply ethical risk. To test whether or not such associations are moderated by organizational and environmental factors as shown in Figure 1.
