528510.label: Major findings and research outcome
528510.value: FINDINGS RELATED TO OBJECTIVE 1: The following conclusions were drawn from the push-out tests: (1) the strength of shear studs is governed by stud fracture and can be fully developed; (2) A substantial amount of residual strength remains after fracture of shear studs; (3) The stud height can be greatly reduced without significantly reducing its strength and ductility, so stocky shear studs can be used in DSTBs in the parts with a thin concrete layer; (4) The shear capacity and load-slip behavior of shear studs can be predicted using an existing method developed for use in traditional steel/concrete composite structures. FINDINGS RELATED TO OBJECTIVE 2: The results from large-scale DSTB tests showed that both the DSTBs and the DSTB/deck unit possessed a very ductile response, and that the headed shear studs effectively reduced/eliminated slips between the steel tube and the concrete, leading to enhanced composite action between the two. The test results of FRP-confined SCC showed that the behavior of FRP-confined SCC is generally similar to that of FRP-confined normal concrete although the lateral expansion of the former appears to be a little larger. The axial compression tests on FRP-concrete-steel DSTCs with a circular inner steel tube and a square outer FRP tube showed that the concrete in these square hybrid DSTCs is effectively confined by the two tubes. A 3D finite element (FE) approach for concrete columns under FRP confinement was developed and implemented using ABAQUS, in which the explicit dynamic solution method was used to avoid convergence problems in obtaining the static response using a static solution method (i.e. the explicit approach). This explicit approach was then used to develop a FE model for DSTBs to predict the experimental behavior. The force-based beam element model can predict the behavior of DSTBs well. The simple theoretical model is suitable for use in the flexural design of DSTBs. OTHER RELATED FINDINGS: Axial compression tests on FRP tubes filled with compound concrete containing recycled concrete lumps indicated that with the FRP tube confinement, the ultimate axial stress and the ultimate axial strain of the compound concrete containing recycled concrete lumps can become comparable with those of the fresh concrete, regardless of the strength of the old concrete. In addition, concrete-filled FRP tubes under cyclic axial compression were also studied, with particular attention to the ultimate condition of these tubes.

528510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
528510.value: Follow-on work on the fatigue behavior of DSTBs is in progress. The shear behavior of DSTBs will also be studied in due time.

528510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
528510.value: To overcome the massive infrastructure deterioration problem worldwide, extensive recent research has explored the use of fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites in new construction to achieve corrosion-resistant structures. Against this background, this project has been undertaken to further develop a novel form of hybrid flexural members incorporating FRP which is cost-effective, durable, ductile and easy to construct. This new form of flexural members consists of an inner steel tube, an outer FRP tube and a concrete infill between the two (i.e. hybrid double-skin tubular beams or hybrid DSTBs). Shear studs are provided in DSTBs between the steel tube and the concrete to ensure their composite action and to serve as positioning spacers between them. The research programme included push-out tests to study the behaviour of shear studs, flexural tests on large-scale DSTBs, finite element modelling of confined concrete and DSTBs, and the development of a relatively simple analytical model for use in design. The research outcomes of this project represent an important step forward in understanding and modelling the behaviour of DSTBs and in enabling their practical implementation.

528710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
528710.value: 摘要 超精密銑削加工是一門可用於製造非旋轉對稱自由曲面的技術，利用該技術加工的表面不需要任何的後續拋光就能達到納米級的粗糙度。尤其對於光學、光子、通訊領域等產品或系統，加工表面的品質在其功能表現上起著至關重要的作用。然而，由於複雜的外型和嚴格的品質要求，具有自由曲面的光學元件的加工製作不但困難而且耗時。切削工具的磨損對於加工精度的影響是非常大的，因為刀具的一個微小的磨損就會導致工件的表面粗糙度和形狀精度變差。由於隨著工具的磨損，刀尖圓角半徑與切削深度的比率（R / h）將逐漸增加, 將會發生犁削過程代替切削過程的不利結果，既使是傳統使用的具有極高硬度的單點金剛石工具，加工過程中的刀具磨損對於納米級表面的加工製作仍是一個威脅。 在超精密銑削加工過程中，加工參數設置和加工自由曲面形狀元件所需的時間比常規加工要長許多（從幾小時到幾天)。如果由於刀具磨損致使產品品質無法接受，那麼就會浪費設備所花的時間和先前工件切削的時間， 因此降低了超精密銑削的效率。為了提高產品品質和生產效率，開發一個準確而有效的加工過程刀具磨損監測和補償的方法是超精密銑削的一個關鍵議題。超精密自由曲面銑削是一個非常複雜的加工過程，由於在加工過程中金剛石刀具是繞主軸軸線旋轉而工件是固定的，所以也被稱為飛切加工。眾所周知，在超精密銑削過程中刀具磨損的檢測是非常困難的，在單點金剛石車削方面，研究學者已經做過多項研究，但對於超精密銑削中的刀具磨損，卻很少有文獻報導。 為了評估金剛石刀具的磨損，建立一個新的刀具磨損三維表面重構的自回歸方法用以支持超精密銑削過程中的定位影像處理，該方法運用數位圖像和數位信號處理技術來監測刀具的磨損，並建立刀具磨損和表面完整性的關係。流式圖像將由具有50倍放大鏡頭的CCD相機採集，該相機面向只有幾微米的刀尖半徑。採集後的數位圖像被處理以用於三維表面重構，因此刀具磨損可以得到即時監測。 超精密銑削過程的動態特性將通過測力計和測力感測器進行監測，並通過資料相關系統（DDS）和快速傅裡葉變換(FFT)演算法進行分析。飛刀銑削過程中的切削力變化的研究不僅會有利於更好地瞭解微切削過程，對於刀具磨損的監測也是一個靈敏的工具。該研究將選用可進行熱處理的合金材料，如鋁、銅、鎳銅等，並將在不同切削條件下，採用不同切削策略對其進行一系列的切削實驗。建立一個基於力學和熱學模型的三維有限元模型用以預測超精密銑削過程中刀尖交界面的磨損，該模擬結果將在不同的加工條件下進行實驗驗證。研究的結果及後續的工作將有利於更好地理解超精密銑削的加工過程和提供最優切削策略以降低刀具磨損，而刀具磨損的降低將有助於在生產具有自由曲面的光學元件中更好地控制工件表面的完整性。

528710.label: Realisation of objectives
528710.value: Ultra-precision raster milling (UPRM) is a complex cutting process, in which tool wear certainly affects the surface integrity. Therefore, study on the 3D modelling and measurement of tool wear in UPRM is meaningful. This project aims to provide a reliable method for measuring tool wear both on-line and on-position, so that the effects of tool wear on the surface integrity can be predicted and suppressed. For objective (i) of this project, a series of cutting experiment has been conducted under different machining conditions and tool wear stages. The cutting force and vibration signals were captured online by dynamometer and processed in both time domain and frequency domain. In this way, the signal components of cutting force and vibration in UPRM were studied, and the relationship between tool wear, cutting force and vibration signals were investigated. Based on digital image processing technique, tool wear lands were separated from a tool wear image captured by a CCD camera with a 100X optical system. A traverse search method of arc translation was put forward to eliminate feigned wear lands. A least square polynomial method was adopted to fit inner and outer contours of the wear lands. An auto-regressive calibration method was developed to reconstruct the 3D topographic surface of the wear lands (objective (ii)). Based on the cutting mechanism of UPRM, the generation of tool vibration due to tool wear and its effects on surface integrity were investigated. It is found that tool flank wear enlarges the thrust force during the cutting, which aggravates the effect of tool vibration during the cutting (objective iii). For objective (iv), the widely adopted static 2D/3D FEM models were used to model the steady-state cutting process. The relative tool-workpiece displacement induced by tool-tip vibration is considered in the FEM modelling to study the tool wear in metal cutting. The simulation results of the geometry of worn tools were verified by the experimental data. A group of cutting experiments has been conducted to verify the predictions and modelling results in this project (objective (v)). As a whole, all the objectives of this project have been fully realized. Eight papers have been published in top SCI refereed journals, four papers which published in the A grade Journal such as Journal of Machine Tool & Manufacture and Precision Engineering.

528710.label: Major findings and research outcome
528710.value: In ultra-precision raster milling, a better understanding of tool wear and its relationship with cutting force and chip morphology is of prime importance for better control of the quality of the machined surface. In this project, the tool wear measurement methods have been studied in depth. Major findings and research outcome are summarized as follows: (1) In this project, the cutting force and its relationship with tool wear were investigated in both time domain and frequency domain. In the time domain, the cutting force in UPRM is characterized as a force pulse followed by damping vibration signals which can be modelled by a second order impulse response of the measurement system (To and Zhang, 2014a). In the frequency domain, the power spectrum density at the natural frequency of the dynamometer increases with the progress of tool wear, which can be utilized to monitor the diamond tool wear in UPRM (Zhang et al., 2013). (2) This project investigated the on-position measurement of tool wear, and a novel tool wear image capture system was setup. A program has been developed to process the captured tool wear image. The 3D topographic surfaces of wear lands can be reconstructed by using this program. In addition, the wear area, maximum wear width, average wear width and worn volume can be determined automatically (Zhang et al., 2012). (3) This project explored the effects of the vibrations of spindle and cutting tool on the surface integrity in UPRM. A specialized model of an aerostatic bearing spindle under the impulsive excitations from the intermittent cutting forces in UPRM is developed. The results reveal that the impulsive spindle vibration produces inhomogeneous scallops forming ribbon-stripe patterns and irregular patterns like run-out on the machined surface in UPRM. (Zhang and To, 2013a; Zhang and To, 2013b). (4) This project also investigated the relationship between tool wear and cutting chip formation (Wang and To, 2011) and morphology, and found that tool fracture causes the formation of ridge-like structures on the chip surface (Zhang et al., 2014a) while tool flank wear makes the cutting chip truncated at its both sides (Zhang et al., 2014b). The chip morphologies under different tool wear stages were used to evaluate the tool wear, as well as the surface quality (Zhang et al., 2014a; To and Zhang 2014b). As a whole, the results of this project have been disseminated through publications in top international journals. Eight papers have been published in journals, and one PhD student was trained and graduated.

528710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
528710.value: UPRM is an intermittent cutting process, in which the cutting mechanics, kinematics and dynamics characteristics are significantly different from conventional milling and ultra-precision diamond turning. Due to the existence of background noise in UPRM, the proposed tool wear measurement method is still far from perfect. Currently, this tool wear measurement method can indicate the occurrence of tool wear and roughly identify the tool wear characteristics and their effects on the surface integrity. In the future, the accuracy of the tool wear identification will be improved, which will extend the application of this method. On the other hand, acoustic emission (AE) has been proved as an alternative for on-line monitoring of tool wear in metal cutting. The sensitivity of the AE signal has enabled it as a basic tool for the evaluation of tool wear. In the further study, AE signal will be used to identify tool wear characteristics in UPRM. The relationship between tool wear characteristics and power spectrum density (PSD) of the AE signal will be explored. Based on the analysis of the AE signal in frequency domain, a real time tool wear monitoring method is expected to be developed.

528710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
528710.value: Ultra-precision raster milling (UPRM) is an enabling technology for machining non-rotational symmetric components with sub-micron form accuracy and nanometric surface roughness. However, diamond tool wear during the cutting process can significantly affect the surface finish of machined products. If diamond tool wear makes the machined products unacceptable, the long cutting time and configuration time would be wasted, which would reduce the productivity and effectiveness of UPRM. Therefore, the realization of 3D modelling and measurement of tool wear in UPRM is of great significance. In this project, the tool wear modelling and measurement method in UPRM were explored. Through the realization of tool wear measurement both on-line and on-position, the tool wear characteristics and their effects on the integrity of machined surface can be evaluated during the machining process. Consequently, the deterioration of surface quality can be remedied timely by further actions such as changing cutting strategy and cutting parameters. The proposed research provides a reliable tool wear measurement method for UPRM, which helps to improve the cutting efficiency of UPRM.

529210.label: Project Objectives
529210.value: To develop algorithms for discovering knowledge and extracting intangibles through a 2-tier data filtration by applying Rule-Based Reason(RBR) and Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) as the first and second tier respectively. To develop a new mark-up language as an extensible architecture for intangible assets to enforce uniformity and consistency of intangible knowledge flow through the IC report generation process. 529210.label: Realisation of objectives
529210.value: For Objective 1, an algorithm has been developed for knowledge discovery and extraction of intangibles by applying Rule-based Reasoning (RBR) and Case-based Reasoning (CBR). The algorithm is named Knowledge-based Intellectual Capital Extraction (KBICE) algorithm which incorporates the technologies of computational linguistics and artificial intelligence (AI) for automatic processing of unstructured data and extraction of important IC-related information. Based on the algorithm and guided by a pre-defined IC taxonomy (which was constructed from a manual analysis of all the IC reports available in the banking industry), it is possible to extract commonly referred IC-related information from unstructured data automatically. Therefore an IC information analyst can rely on this method as an additional mean to identify and extract the commonly sought IC information from publicly available financial reports in a fast, systematic and reliable manner. A series of experiments has been conducted for assessing the capability of the algorithm by using publicly available financial reports from the banking industry as the testing batch and encouraging results have been obtained. For Objective 2, the original goal was to develop a markup language to facilitate the generation of IC reports. However, in recent years, both the research community and practitioners have abandoned the use of IC reporting hence it is futile to proceed and develop the markup language. Instead, the prevailing trend is “total reporting” which covers not only IC but also the workplace environment and employee satisfaction and other factors. At the same time, due to the insurgence of social media, a growing volume of user-generated content is being generated in various social channels which can be mined to supplement basic IC information that were extracted from financial reports. Hence, the researchers have turned to develop techniques to perform sentiment analysis by analyzing social media from not only an organization but also from the outside world including customers and consumers. Doing so increases the comprehensiveness and accuracy of IC assessments for an organization as well as extends the work to head towards total reporting. For Objective 3, a semi-automatic Intellectual capital reporting framework has been developed for business core competencies to increase business transparency. A case study has been done to realize the capability of the framework. This framework is customized for IC reporting in the banking industry after a comprehensive analysis of all the words, terms, sentence patterns and writing styles reported in all the IC reports in the banking industry.

529210.label: Major findings and research outcome
529210.value: - From analyzing all the IC reports in the banking industry, researchers identify that there are commonly used words, terms, sentence patterns and writing styles being adopted. Further analyses of these revealed structures help to develop an IC taxonomy. This work has been reported in the first and second conference papers reported in Part C. - An IC taxonomy can help to guide algorithms for intelligent pattern matching and extraction when it comes to processing financial reports for IC-related information. This work is the basis of the first conference paper reported in Part C. - To accomplish IC reporting, a Knowledge-based Intellectual Capital Extraction (KBICE) algorithm which incorporates the technologies of computational linguistics and artificial intelligence (AI) has been developed. - The IC reporting framework has been trialed by processing corpus of texts taken from publicly available financial reports. This work has been published in the journal paper listed in Part C. - Researchers have further carried out work to identify metrics that represent a total IC eco-system and applied action research to validate a model for revealing, representing and validating such information in the IT department of a university. This work is reported in the third conference paper reported in Part C. - The results of the project have been disseminated in one journal paper, three conference papers and one book chapter - A MPhil student has also been trained. She is due to submit her thesis this week. The work on sentiment analysis in IC is reported, among other things, in her thesis.

529210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
529210.value: - Current study is focusing on financial industry. With appropriate customization of the algorithms and framework, it can be further applied to other industries. - Currently, IC reporting is focus on semi-automatic methods of content analysis of existing document. It could be cross check with manual methods in IC auditing so as to investigate further improvement of the methodology. - In this project, sentiment analysis is used for enriching the IC reporting. Further study could be done on correlating the IC indicator with the results of sentiment analysis. - Big Data techniques can be used by analyzing a huge volume of company reports as well as social media and determine if there are indeed patterns of word and term correlations that researchers are unaware of. This is an alternative but can be a ground breaking approach to reveal IC as traditional approach are typically not data-driven but algorithmic-driven. A data-driven approach is especially promising in the Big Data era as IC needs to be tracked and reported closely as well as close approximations rather than exact figures are good enough measurements of IC in any organisation.

529210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
529210.value: Despite living in a knowledge-based economy, metrics for measuring the success of organisations have their roots in the 17th century and have not changed much over time. Today, for-profit organisations are still being measured principally and sometimes solely by their financial performance and compilation of Annual Report is the norm..Intellectual Capital (IC) reporting is an attempt to break this barrier by extending the measurements to cover internal capital, human capital and external capital. However, it is extremely difficult to extract IC information from company reports as they are not written for the purpose of revealing IC information; both manual and automatic content analysis have significant drawbacks. Relying on a prior comprehensive analysis of published IC reports in the banking industry, this research has demonstrated that there are merits in using a human-assisted semi-automatic algorithmic approach to extract and reveal IC. Furthermore, the approach has been extended to cover the analysis of rapidly accumulating user-generated social media which, together with the company published reports, help to track and reveal a more comprehensive IC eco-system (aka Total reporting) for organisations.

529610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
529610.value: The major objective of this project is to assimilate satellite images and real-time field measured sediment concentration into a physics-based numerical model to provide an accurate long-term prediction of sediment transport processes in Deep Bay, Hong Kong. This project is a continuous effort of the Principal Investigator (PI) to strive for better understanding of the sedimentation problem and fate and transport of contaminated sediment in Deep Bay. The improved scientific knowledge can help decision makers to better manage and protect the delicate environment and ecosystem of the bay which is under tremendous threat of human activities in recent years. For instance, during the construction period of the fourth vehicular boundary crossing between Hong Kong and Shenzhen, the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Western Corridor, bored piling and drilling works in the shallow regions of the bay disturbed the sediments in the seabed generating very high suspended sediment concentration (SSC) in the water column. The high SSC has great impact on marine ecology because it will reduce light penetration and the thickness of the euphotic zone and eventually limit primary productivity. The disturbed sediments may also be transported by tidal currents to other shallower regions causing sedimentation problem. In this project, the finite element model developed by the PI and his research team will be used to carry out the sediment transport prediction. The model is equipped with an efficient mass conserved drying-wetting scheme to account for the tidal dynamics in the mudflats of the bay. Kalman filter type data assimilation methods will be used to incorporate satellite images and field observations in the finite element model. Satellite images will be collected in non-cloudy seasons which may be in the summer and in the autumn. Key issues of assimilating data into numerical simulations, such as computational efficiency, uncertainty and inaccuracy of model parameters, optimization strategies, error in field observation, etc. will be addressed in the project. Finally, performance of the proposed method will be evaluated by carrying out 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional synoptic simulations for dry seasons and wet seasons, respectively. Results obtained in this project may offer new insights into what sediment transport processes are governing the short-term and long-term morphological change in the bay. The present approach can provide accurate time varying sediment quality information with high spatial resolution which is useful in implementing the adaptive management skill to protect the delicate aquatic ecosystem in the bay. 這個科研項目的主要目標是集成衛星圖像和即時實地觀測泥沙濃度資料到一個物理數值模型中以提供精確長期預測香港后海灣泥沙的輸移過程。這個科研項目是首席研究員在后海灣泥沙沉積問題和污染物傳輸問題的一項持續性研究。該項研究成果可以帮助政策制定者更好得管理和保護近年來受到人類活動嚴重威脅的后海灣海域環境和生態系統。例如，在香港和深圳的第四條汽車過境通道(香港-深圳西部通道)的建造過程中，在后海灣的淺灘區域進行的打樁和鑽挖工作攪動了海底的泥沙，因此在該水域產生了很高的懸浮泥沙濃度。高的懸浮泥沙濃度對海洋生態系統有著重大的影響，因為它會降低陽光的透射能力和透光層的厚度，進而降低了海洋的初級生產力。這些被攪動的泥沙也可能通過潮汐輸移到更淺海域導致泥沙沉積問題。 這個項目將使用首席研究員及其研究團隊開發的有限元模型進行泥沙輸移預測。該模型採用一種有效的幹濕邊界處理方法來類比海灣泥灘的潮汐動力學過程。另外卡爾曼濾波資料同化方法將會用於把衛星圖像和即時實地測量的泥沙資料同化到有限元模型中。衛星圖像將會選用雲較少的夏季或秋季的圖像資料。一些將觀測資料同化到數值類比中的主要問題，例如計算效率，模型參數的不確定和不准確，優化策略，觀測資料的誤差等將會在該的中詳細闡述。以上提出的方法將會分別用二維和三維的模型在幹季和雨季的類比結果來進行評估。本項目所獲得的成果將對海灣泥沙輸移程序控制短期和長期的地形變化問題提供一些新的見解。項目提出的方法可以提供精確和高分辨力的隨時間變化的泥沙資訊，將有助實施適應性的管理方式來保護海灣內的敏感脆弱生態系統。

529610.label: Realisation of objectives
529610.value: An essential piece of information that plays an important role in the success of this project was provided by the Hong Kong Government and the Shenzhen River Regulation Office of Shenzhen Municipality. The information consists of (1) Shenzhen River Bed Survey Data; (2) Shenzhen Sediment Survey Data; (3) Shenzhen Hydrological Survey Data; (4) Sediment Survey Data under Yuen Long and North District DMP Review Study; and (5) MIKE 21 Model for Shenzhen River. This information was used in this project for Deep Bay numerical model boundary setup, model calibration and simulated result verification as well as satellite imagery comparison. In addition, sediment properties and ecological information upstream of Yuen Long Nullah which discharges into Deep Bay have also been collected. These data and information were used to prescribe the discharge water quality condition at the Deep Bay tributaries in the physical-based numerical model. Current velocity assimilation (CVA) has been developed to improve sediment transport prediction in Deep Bay. One of the data assimilation methods, namely Optimal Interpolation (OI) was employed. OI is under the category of sequential assimilation method which is based on Kalman Filter (KF) that estimates the optimum current model state according to the previous model state estimation as such current measurements and their error statistics are determined by the least square criterion. Similar to KF, the implementation of OI comprises three steps: carrying model simulation forward to the next time step, calculating the Kalman gain and updating the model state according to observations and Kalman gain. For assimilating satellite images and field observations into model simulations, satellite spectra and sediment information including suspended solids concentration and particle size distribution were used. Such information from over 15 field stations in the Pearl River estuary and 8 field stations in Deep Bay were collected for one time satellite passage. The HJ-1A/1B satellite CCD imagery over the Pearl River estuary with spatial resolution of 30m together with field measurements were assimilated into numerical simulations. Five pieces of equipment were used and they were GPS to accurately identify station locations, Ocean Optics HR2000 spectrometer to measure ocean color spectrum, MICROTOPS II sun photometer to measure aerosol optical parameters, LISST 100X to measure suspended sediment concentration as well as particle size distribution and OBS-3A to measure water turbidity. Key issues of assimilating data into numerical simulations, such as computational efficiency, uncertainty and inaccuracy of model parameters, optimization strategies, error in field observation, etc. have been addressed in the project.

529610.label: Major findings and research outcome
529610.value: Sea surface height (SSH) derived from satellite altimetry ENVISAT RA-2 was prescribed in a hydrodynamic model for predicting the tidal flow pattern in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE) which governs the flow and passive substances transport at the sea open boundary of Deep Bay. This virtual tide station concept can extend the spatial and temporal coverage of tidal elevation that traditional tide gauges can provide. (Ref:C(1)). Assimilation methods between remote sensing ocean color and numerical models for the improvement of sediment transport prediction in Deep Bay have been investigated. Two sea surface sediment datasets delineated from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectra-radiometer (MODIS) were assimilated into a coastal ocean model. Model results showed that root mean square errors of forecast sediment concentration with satellite sediment assimilation reduced significantly. (Ref: C(2)). Tidal currents play an important role in sediment dynamics in estuarine regions. Effects of current velocity assimilation (CVA) on sediment transport modeling have also been investigated. Numerical simulation was conducted with in situ current velocity measurements sequentially assimilated into the model using a three-dimensional optimal interpolation scheme. The root-mean-square error of the simulated sediment concentration from the model with CVA decreased by at least 7 %. (Ref:C(3)). An effective method for the retrieval of total suspended sediment (TSS) concentration using HJ-1A/1B satellite images has been proposed. The retrieval method was based on the relationship between the satellite-corrected reflectance band ratio of band 3 and band 2 (Rrs3/Rrs2) and in-situ TSS measurements. Study results show that HJ-1A/1B satellite CCD images can be used to estimate TSS concentrations under different tidal conditions in Deep Bay over synoptic scales without using simultaneous in-situ atmospheric parameters and spectrum data. (Ref:C(4)). Eight years of ocean color collected between 2003 and 2010 by Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) was used to analyze the variation of the total suspended sediment (TSS) concentration in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE). This study provides baseline water quality information in the PRE, and more generally, a remote sensing approach to assess water quality changes in similar water bodies. (Ref:C(5)). Other water quality sampling methods at headwater streams which may discharge into the Bay area have been studied (Ref:C(6)). They are the mesoscale physical habitat (MPH) and cell-in-series (CIS) water quality sampling methods. Correlations between hydroenvironmental and water quality variables have been evaluated for both methods. It is found that habitat dimensions have higher influence in the MPH approach while the substrate condition impacts on the CIS approach.

529610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
529610.value: Multi-platform remote sensing data may be used in the future to narrow the assimilation time in order to achieve a long-term continuous information for numerical forecast and prediction. Moreover, other assimilation schemes may be explored to improve the prediction of suspended sediment concentration in the entire vertical water column. Error correlation of the computed sediment concentration between the surface layer and at the lower levels may be considered in the improved schemes. It is important to note that optimal interpolation is limited to the calculation of time-invariant forecast error covariance. Other data assimilation methods, such as ensemble optimal interpolation and ensemble Kalman filter, may be useful alternatives to increase the scientific perspective as a result of building a more sophisticated operational data assimilation system. Future work could also cover simultaneous assimilation of both flow and sediment concentration measurements. Particular focus could be on the assimilation of suspended sediment concentration derived from remote sensing images into three-dimensional hydrodynamic and sediment transport models. As a result, sediment dynamics in coastal and marine waters could be better determined and understood.

529610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
529610.value: In this project, a finite element model and a finite volume model have been used to carry out the hydrodynamic and sediment transport prediction in Deep Bay and the Pearl River estuary. The models are equipped with drying-wetting schemes to account for the tidal dynamics in the shallow parts of Deep Bay. Satellite images have been collected in non-cloudy seasons during summer and early autumn. Kalman filter type data assimilation methods have been tested to incorporate with satellite images and field observations in the model simulations. Key issues of assimilating data into numerical simulations, such as computational efficiency, uncertainty and inaccuracy of model parameters, optimization strategies, error in field observation, etc. have been addressed in the project. Finally, the assimilation performance of the proposed method has been evaluated by carrying out 3-dimensional synoptic simulations for dry seasons and wet seasons. Results obtained in this project may offer new insights into what sediment transport processes are governing the short-term and long-term morphological change in the bay. The present approach can provide accurate time varying sediment quality information which is useful in implementing the adaptive management skill to protect the delicate aquatic ecosystem in the bay.

529810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
529810.value: Micro/nanofibers (MNFs) are a new class of optical fibers which exhibit many unique and interesting properties such as strong light confinement, large evanescent fields, excellent flexibility and convenient configurability, and enhanced nonlinear effects, because of their extremely small diameter. This opens up new possibilities of fabricating novel optical devices for a wide range of applications. To further enhance the functionalities of the optical devices based on MNFs, it would be desirable if a basic fiber component, fiber Bragg grating (FBG), could be created in the MNF. For instance, an optical fiber sensor based on FBG in MNF can be directly exposed to the surrounding medium, thus possessing high potential to enhance the measurement sensitivity while maintaining superior reliability because of wavelength encoded measurand information. The main objective of the project is to develop novel sensing devices based on FBGs in MNFs. The key issues to be addressed include fabrication of appropriate MNFs, inscription of FBGs in MNFs and test of their responses to refractive index and temperature, and development of efficient optical fiber sensor systems for refractive index measurement and high temperature sensing. The main outcome of the project would be a novel sensing device based on FBG in MNF, which can be effectively utilized to perform refractive index measurement and high temperature sensing with improved performance. The project is expected to have impacts on photonics circuit, chemical and biological sensor, and temperature monitoring in the extreme environment such as aeroengine. 作为一类新型的光纤结构，微纳光纤(MNF)由于自身极小的截面直径，具有诸如较强的光场限制性、较大的瞬逝场、封装应用上的方便和灵活以及非线性效应增强等特点。这些特性可以用来制作具有广泛应用的新型光纤器件。值得注意的是，如果能在MNF上成功制作一类基本的光纤器件——光纤布拉格光栅(FBG)，可以进一步扩展基于MNF的光纤器件功能。例如，基于MNF的FBG传感探头，可直接适用于环境介质的测量，并具有较大的测量灵敏度；同时，该传感探头由于其测量信息的波长编码特性，仍然能保持优秀的测量可靠性。 本项目的主要目标是拓展基于MNF上写入FBG的新型光纤传感器件。该类器件作为传感探头，预计会具有较大的折射率灵敏度以及在高温环境下较快的温度响应时间。需要解决的关键问题包括：拉制具有合适尺寸的MNF；在MNF上写入FBG，并测试其折射率和温度响应；以及研制高效的光纤折射率与高温传感系统。 项目的主要成果为：一类新型的基于MNF上写入FBG的传感器件，该器件可以有效应用于折射率测量和高温传感。该项目预计可以对诸如光学集成链路，生物化学传感，以及极限高温环境下（如航空引擎）的温度监测等多个方面产生影响。

529810.label: Realisation of objectives
529810.value: 1. FBG could be fabricated in MNF and the grating in MNF may have a number of propagation modes in its transmission spectrum and the higher order of modes have higher refractive index sensitivity. 2. The MNFs with different diameters and lengths have been successfully fabricated by use of flame brushing method, where a small flame moves slowly under a single-mode fiber stretched by two moving vacuum absorption holders. The torch flame intensity can be adjusted by controlling the flux of H2, which is optimized at approximately 134 standard cubic centimeters per minute in our experiment, just enough to support the flame to soften the glass without inducing a large loss. The scanning length of the torch is 7 mm, which limits the fiber length. 3. The FBG fabricated has good response to the surrounding refractive index. The maximum sensitivity obtained is 231.4 nm per refractive index unit at the refractive index value of 1.44 when the fiber diameter is 2 µm. 4. A simple, compact and robust refractive index sensor has been developed, which is constructed by twisting a pair of silica micro/nanofibers to form a coupling device. The transmission spectrum of the device is highly sensitive to the surrounding refractive index and the highest sensitivity obtained is -1665nm/RIU (refractive index unit), at the refractive index value of -1.3605, for the fibers with diameter of ~2.1μm, and the sensitivity can be further increased to -2526 nm/RIU for a smaller fiber diameter of ~1.4μm. The developed sensor device is easy to construct, of low cost and compatible with optical fiber system. 5. Efforts have also been made to achieve ultra-compact optical fiber in-line Mach-Zehnder interferometer by creating an inner air-cavity in a section of microfiber. The sandwich structure splits the light propagating in the fiber into two beams: one passes through the inner air-cavity and the other travels along the silica wall of the cavity before recombining at the cavity end, resulting in an interference fringe pattern. Such a device is applied for strain measurement with a high sensitivity of 6.8 pm/μ.

529810.label: Major findings and research outcome
529810.value: The FBG fabricated has good response to the surrounding refractive index. The maximum sensitivity obtained is 231.4 nm per refractive index unit at the refractive index value of 1.44 when the fiber diameter is 2 µm. The characteristics of strong evanescent field of MNF can be used for saturable absorber. When MNF is incorporate with graphene, saturable absorber can be formed and used for passive mode-locked optical fiber laser source. The system can be effectively utilized to directly generate ultra-wide-band doublet pulses for high-capacity wireless communication applications. Moreover, by use of graphene-covered-microfiber and chirped fiber Bragg grating (CFBG), a wavelength-tunable, passively mode-locked fiber laser can be constructed. In such a system, once the mode-locking operation is established, no adjustment of PC is needed even when the peak wavelength of the CFBG is tuned. An ultra-compact optical fiber in-line Mach-Zehnder interferometer can be constructed by creating an inner air-cavity in a section of microfiber. The sandwich structure splits the light propagating in the fiber into two beams: one passes through the inner air-cavity and the other travels along the silica wall of the cavity before recombining at the cavity end, resulting in an interference fringe pattern. Such a device is applied for strain measurement with a high sensitivity of 6.8 pm/μ.

529810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
529810.value: MNF has high potentials in construction of novel photonic devices and for various optical fiber sensing applications. For instance, a MNF loop together with microfiber FBG may form Sagnec interferometer for sensing applications. A simultaneous multiple parameter measurement can also be expected by use of microfiber inscribed with a number of FBGs.

529810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
529810.value: This project aims to investigate the techniques to fabricate fiber gratings on micro/nanofibers, evaluate and improve the grating performance, design and construction of optical fiber sensor based on such micro/nanofiber gratings to implement refractive index measurement. The outcomes of the project include successfully fabricate gratings on micro/nanofiber, test their interesting properties, build up optical fiber sensor system based on this new type of devices and test its responses to refractive index. The novel micro/nanofiber in-line interferometer device for strain sensing has also been developed by creating an inner air-cavity along with a section of microfiber.

531210.label: Project Objectives
531210.value: To investigate the sensor characterizations and develop strict 3D stereo photogrammetric models of lunar orbiter imagery obtained from the CE-1 mission and LRO mission. There are two major concerns to achieve this objective. First, photogrammetric models based on push-broom and frame imaging principles will be investigated and developed to model the imaging geometry of the images from different sensors. Second, jitter affects caused by spacecraft vibrations will be examined and considered in the photogrammetric models for high-precision geometric modeling; To develop an innovative methodology for combined bundle adjustment of multi-source lunar orbiter camera imagery and laser altimeter data from the CE-1 mission and LRO mission to obtain the best possible and consistent ground accuracy. Based on the bundle adjustment model, this project will firstly investigate the integration of multi-source imagery (e.g., the images from different orbits, different sensors, and different missions). Secondly, the integration of multi-source imagery and laser altimeter data will be studied to improve the absolute accuracy of images by incorporating the laser altimeter data as absolute ground control. Specific imagery and laser altimeter data from the CE-1 mission and LRO mission will be selected for processing considering the image resolution and the laser spot size. Effective weighting schemes will be carefully studied and developed in the bundle adjustment system based on extensive experiments; Based on the developed technologies, to produce the highest level of resolution and the most comprehensive topographic models for possible candidate landing sites and other areas of scientific interest to support future lunar landed missions. The topographic models will include detailed 3D digital terrain models, orthophotos, slope maps, 3D surface feature measure, and other special models. Innovated algorithms and software will be developed to process the CE-1 and LRO data for final topographic model production.

531210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
531210.value: In October 2007, China successfully launched its first lunar orbiter Chang'E-1 (CE-1). In June 2009, NASA also launched the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO). Among the science payload instruments on-board both the CE-1 and LRO are orbiter cameras and laser altimeters with different configurations that collect data at various levels of resolution. This provides a chance to use all the available data from multi-sensors and multi-missions for precision lunar topographic mapping which cannot be achieved when only using the data from a single sensor or single mission. This project plans to integrate the orbiter imagery with laser altimeter data obtained from the CE-1 and LRO missions to develop high-precision topographic models to support future lunar landed missions. Project objectives include: (1) To develop strict 3D stereo photogrammetric models of lunar orbiter imagery obtained from the CE-1 and LRO missions; (2) To develop innovative methodology for combined bundle adjustment of multi-source lunar orbiter imagery and laser altimeter data from the CE-1 and LRO missions to obtain the best possible and consistent ground accuracy; and (3) Based on the developed technologies, to produce high-precision topographic models for possible candidate landing sites to support future lunar landed missions. Most of the previous related research is to process orbiter imagery and laser altimeter data separately then do a comparison. This proposed research is an endeavor to integrate the CE-1 and LRO imagery and laser altimeter data in order to reduce their inconsistencies and produce better mapping results. The PI, Dr. Bo Wu, has been working on NASA funded projects in Mars and lunar exploration missions at the Ohio State University (OSU) since 2006. In particular, he worked on a newly funded LRO Participating Scientists Project at OSU focusing on processing of LRO data for near real-time lunar topographic mapping and landing-site assessment. The Department of Land Surveying & Geo-Informatics (LSGI) of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University is an authorized organization of the CE-1 Scientific Application Committee which can access the CE-1 data. LSGI received the CE-1 imagery and laser altimeter data in March 2009. This proposed project will contribute to the advancement of the science and technology of planetary mapping. The multi-source data integration capability enables cross-sensor and cross-mission data correlation that will be very valuable for various scientific investigations in lunar exploration missions and beyond. This project will also enhance the contributions of Hong Kong scientists to support the Chinese space exploration program. 2007年10月，中國成功地發射了第一顆探月衛星嫦娥一號（CE-1）。2009年6月，美國航天局也發射了月球偵察軌道器（LRO）。中國第二顆探月衛星嫦娥二號（CE-2）也將在2010年下半年發射升空。在CE-1、CE-2以及LRO的科學載荷中都有軌道相機和激光高度計，他們具有不同的性能，能夠獲取不同分辨率的月球表面數據。這就為利用來自于多顆月球衛星上的多傳感器數據實現高精度月球地形測繪提供了一個機會，而這可能是利用單一衛星上的單一傳感器的數據所不達到的。本研究項目計劃基於多任務多傳感器數據的集成（如CE-1、CE-2或者LRO上的軌道相機和激光高度計），開發高精度的月球地形測繪方法，以支持未來的月球登陸任務。項目的研究目標包括： （1）對從CE-1和其他月球探測衛星（如CE-2或LRO）獲取的月球影像，開發建立其嚴格的三維立體攝影測量模型; （2）開發一種創新的基於光束法平差的方法，集成處理來自于CE-1和其他月球探測衛星（如CE-2或LRO）的影像和激光測高數據，以獲取最佳的月球地形測繪精度; （3）基於本項目研發的技術，針對若干可能的候選著陸點，生成其高精度的地形模型，以支持未來的月球登陸任務。 以前的相關研究大部分是分開處理月球影像和激光測高數據，然後做一比較。本項目旨在集成處理來自于不同傳感器的數據以消除其中的不一致性，并進而實現更好的測繪成果。本項目的首席研究員吳波博士，自2006年以來一直在美國俄亥俄州立大學從事美國航天局資助的火星和月球項目探測任務的工作。香港理工大學土地測量及地理資訊學是中國嫦娥探月工程的科學應用委員會成員之一，該系已與2009年3月獲取全套CE-1影像和激光測高數據。 本項目將有助於推動月球測繪科學技術的進步。基於多任務多傳感器數據的集成技術可應用于今後的月球探測任務以及其它深空探測任務，它使得跨任務跨傳感器數據的集成和處理成為可能，這將具有重要的科學價值。本項目還將促進香港科學家在中國的太空探索計劃中的貢獻。

531210.label: Realisation of objectives
531210.value: For the first objective, we investigated the sensor characterizations of the CE-1 CCD camera, CE-2 CCD camera, and the LRO narrow angle camera, and developed strict 3D stereo photogrammetric models of lunar imagery collected by these cameras. The CE-1 camera has three CCD lines and is able to obtain three images with 100% overlap (forward, nadir, and backward) of the same area simultaneously. We developed a 3D stereo photogrammetric model based on the co-linearity equations to model the CE-1 imagery. The related results can be found in our publication (Wu et al., 2011, IEEE TGRS). The CE-2 camera has two CCD lines which are assembled on a unique focal plane separately to enable the simultaneously acquisition of forward and backward-looking imagery to create stereo pairs. A similar 3D stereo photogrammetric model was developed for the CE-2 imagery. The related results can be found in the publication (Wu et al., 2014a, EPSL). We also investigated the LRO narrow angle camera and the related results can be found in the publication (Wu et al., 2014b, EPSL). For the second objective, we firstly developed a method for integrating the CE-1 imagery and laser altimeter data for consistent and precision lunar topographic modeling through a combined adjustment model. The participants of the combined adjustment are the laser altimeter points, image exterior orientation parameters, and tie points collected from the stereo images. A weighting scheme is designed for the participants in the adjustment and a local surface constraint is imposed to improve the adjustment performance. The output of the combined adjustment is the refined image orientation parameters and laser ground points, from which the best possible and consistent ground accuracy can be obtained. The related results can be found in our publication (Wu et al., 2011, IEEE TGRS). We further extended this method to a combined block adjustment approach to integrate cross-mission and cross-sensor data (e.g., multiple strips of the CE-2 imagery and LRO Laser Altimeter (LOLA) data) for precision lunar topographic modeling. The results can be found in the publication (Wu et al., 2014a, EPSL). For the third objective, the developed methods were used for the integrated processing of data sets from the Chinese CE-1, CE-2 and NASA’s LRO mission, and high-precision lunar topographic models were generated at the CE-3 landing site to support the CE-3 lunar landing mission. The related results can be found in our recent publication (Wu et al., 2014b, EPSL)

531210.label: Major findings and research outcome
531210.value: We investigated the characteristics of various lunar topographic datasets, and developed calibration and registration methods of multi-source lunar topographic datasets. A surface matching method was developed for the co-registration of lunar topographic models derived from CE-1, SELENE, and LRO laser altimeter data. This method incorporates feature points, lines, and surface patches in surface matching to guarantee robust surface correspondence. A mathematic model was developed for the determination of seven transformation parameters, from which the multiple DTMs could be co-registered. The related results can be found in the publication (Wu et al., 2013, EPSL). We developed innovative and unique approaches for precision lunar topographic modeling by integrating cross-mission and cross-sensor lunar remote sensing data through combined adjustment models. Previous works only focused on processing of lunar imagery and laser altimeter data separately and usually there were inconsistences. Our developments integrate cross-mission and cross-sensor data for consistent and precision lunar topographic mapping. These developments are essential for the proper calibration, registration, and analysis of the multi-source lunar topographic datasets. In turn it allows the full comparative and synergistic use of the datasets, which contributes to the advancement of the science and technology in the planetary mapping and scientific research community. The related results can be found in our publications (Wu et al., 2011, IEEE TGRS; Wu et al., 2014a, EPSL). We investigated the False Topographic Perception Phenomenon (FTPP) problem associated with lunar craters, by using the CE-1 lunar imagery covering the entire lunar surface. The discoveries are important for correct perception and detection of lunar surface features (e.g., craters) suffering FTPP problem. The results can be found in our publication (Wu et al., 2013, PSS). Invited by the China Academy of Space Technology in May 2012, we produced detailed high-precision lunar topographic models of the landing site of the Chinese CE-3 lunar landing mission using the developed methods. From the developments and generated lunar topographic models, terrain analysis including slope analysis and crater distribution analysis in CE-3 landing area were carried out. These topographic modeling and analysis results were extensively used by the CE-3 mission team for strategic planning to identify the landing site for the CE-3, which made a useful contribution to the success of the CE-3 mission. The related results can be found in the publication (Wu et al., 2014b, EPSL). The achievements have been covered by various media locally and internationally. Examples of media coverage are attached in the report.

531210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
531210.value: Invited by the China Academy of Space Technology in February 2014, we are currently working on the topographic mapping and analysis of the landing site of the Chinese CE-5 mission in 2017. We are further developing an integrated software platform with better automation and efficiency based on the developments in this project. After some further developments, the developed methods in this project can be used for related applications in Hong Kong and China mainland such as precision terrain mapping and digital city modeling.

531210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
531210.value: This project developed innovative and unique approaches for precision lunar topographic mapping by integrating cross-mission and cross-sensor lunar remote sensing data (e.g., imagery and laser altimeter data). This development is essential for the proper calibration, registration, and analysis of the multiple source lunar topographic datasets collected from different lunar exploration missions. In turn it allows the full comparative and synergistic use of the datasets, which contributes to the advancement of the science and technology in the planetary mapping and scientific research community. The developments and results from this project were extensively used in the Chinese CE-3 lunar landing mission, for the strategic planning to identify the proper landing site for the CE-3. This innovative work is an important contribution to lunar mapping research in general and the CE-3 mission in particular. The results from this project also contribute to other lunar scientific research objectives, such as study of the lunar topography and morphology, lunar crust and craters, and lunar gravity field.

531610.label: Project Title(Chinese)
531610.value: 具生物粘合性的紡織品染料之合成及應用

531610.label: Project Objectives
531610.value: To design and synthesize catechol-containing colorants by combining DOPA, dopamine, or their derivatives with chromophores that possess a variety colours and cover a relative large colour gamut. To characterize the synthesized catechol-containing colorants in objective 1 using FTIR, HPLC, UV-Vis and other instruments. 531610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
531610.value: 受自然界中蚌類粘性蛋白質極強的水下粘合力的啓示，本研究項目從分子設計著手, 合成具有生物粘合性的染料，用于多種不同的紡織材料。此類新穎染料內含蚌類多邦胺（DOPA）等氨基酸，具粘合及交聯性，也可基于含鄰苯二酚，並引入不同色的發色體。爲增大色域，本研究會先使用黃，紅，藍三色基，之後再擴大到其它色基。此類合成的含鄰苯二酚的染料可溶解于水，因此可用于天然及合成纖維的浸染，其帶液率可用離心及軋機控制。染色後，會試驗不同的後處理方法， 例如空氣接觸，弱鹼處理，氧化及光照處理。這些處理，可使鄰苯二酚基團被氧化成爲醌類低聚物至高聚物，並因此不溶于水及附著于纖維上。其固著原理與還原及硫化染料相同。本項目會仔細研究分子設計及合成，以取得不同顔色，並具有一定的深度，以及水洗牢度。 此類仿生含鄰苯二酚的染料，應能用于不同的纖維，如天然， 合成及混紡纖維，並取得較好色牢度，爲染色工業理想的新型染料。由于這類染料不需要類似還原及硫化染料般的還原過程，可更爲簡單及省時。更者，此類染色過程無須還原劑，有利于環保。此外，鄰苯二酚類成分，有很好的生物相容性及生物降解性。

531610.label: Major findings and research outcome
531610.value: Inspired by the strong and permanent adhesion of marine mussels to almost any surface, bio-adhesive colorants which have high adhesion to different types of textile materials had been designed, synthesized and developed based on dopamine and catechol-containing molecules, together with the method of colouration for this type of colorants. Using the developed adhesive colorants, the colouration of various textile materials, even those that are resistant to traditional colouration, was easily achieved through a simple dip-coating procedure. The colour appearance of the dyed materials could be tuned in a controllable way through the incorporation of various nucleophiles such as amino acids and heterocycle components into the colouration bath. In addition, the colour appearances of the dyed textiles could also be tuned using the oxidants with different oxidization ability. With this new coloration method, textile materials, especially protein based fabrics could be coloured with high colour yields, crocking fastness and wash fastness. For the textile fibres that are resistant to traditional coloration, significant changes in surface wettability and increased surface roughness were observed, which verified the adsorption of the bio-based colorants on the surface of those fibres. In order to enlarge the colour gamut of the new colorants, a catechol-containing colorant was designed and synthesized. The molecular structure of this novel colorant consisted of a catechol group as an adhesive ‘anchor’ and a commercially available colorant as a chromophore. Various textile materials were easily coloured using this novel type of catechol-containing colorant at room temperature via a simple dip-coating procedure. Compared to the control colouration, the obtained results of this novel colorant achieved a deeper colour appearance and was especially suitable for those textile materials that are difficult to be coloured by traditional methods, such as polylactic acid and polypropylene. From the results obtained, it is clear that the new colorants and their coloration method are more environmentally friendly due to the reduced energy consumption and the reduced chemical auxiliaries needed in the coloration process. It truly is an innovative method of colouration of textile materials with high potential for large scale industrial application.

531610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
531610.value: Although the adhesive colorants from dopamine polymerization can dye textile materials easily, the colour gamut was still not large enough. To obtain a large colour gamut, it is feasible as proved by this study to incorporate commercially available colorants as chromophores to the catechol-based structure to form new colorants. In addition, based on the fact that mussels’ adhesive proteins contain high content of DOPA, it is possible to improve the versatility through the increase of catechol content in the catechol-containing colorants so as to achieve good coloration results for all kinds of textile substrates.

531610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
531610.value: By mimicking the adhesive power of marine mussel to all kinds of substrates, the research has developed a novel kind of colorants and these colorants show good dyeability to various kinds of textile fibres including natural, synthetic, and even those fibres that are resistant to normal colouration process. Compared to that of conventional colouration process, the coloration process of the new colorants is achieved at room temperature with much less energy consumption and less dyeing auxiliaries using the simpler dyeing method and shorter dyeing time. The new colorants containing catechol component also have good biocompatibility and biodegradability. With these features, the new colorants and the coloration method developed are clearly more environmental friendly compared to the traditional coloration techniques. The outcomes from the study represent a promising alternative to the traditional colouration techniques. The study not only contributes to the generation of new coloration knowledge, but also creates high impact to the textile industry.

531910.label: Project Objectives
531910.value: To develop an integrated sensor-control device network that can achieve both vibration control and health monitoring objectives for building structures during earthquakes. To develop integrative algorithms by which the semi-active control system can be used to enhance system identification and damage detection, while allowing the health monitoring system’s use to enhance vibration control performance. To conduct a laboratory experiment on a building model subject to earthquake conditions to demonstrate the feasibility of the integrated system and to verify the theoretical and numerical findings.

531910.label: Realisation of objectives
531910.value: (1) The first objective of this project regarding the establishment of an integrated sensor-control device network has been completely achieved. A methodology was proposed for the determination of the minimal number of actuators and sensors at their respective optimal locations to achieve the predetermined control performance. A performance index increment-based method and a response reconstruction-based method were integrated to form the proposed approach. (2) The research for achieving the second objective has been performed much beyond planned. Three types of integrative algorithms in either the frequency-domain or the time-domain have been developed. One method was proposed for damage detection of controlled buildings equipped with semi-active friction dampers through model updating based on frequency response functions (FRFs). By using semi-active friction dampers to create two states of the building, a model updating scheme was presented based on the external excitations and structural responses to identify the time-independent structural parameters. Then, one time-domain approach was developed based on the extended Kalman filter (EKF) for identifying the physical parameters of the controlled buildings without the knowledge of external excitations. A projection matrix was introduced, and the physical parameters and state vectors of the building were then identified and used for determining the optimal control force. Although it is a real-time algorithm without requiring external excitations, the structural parameters are still assumed to be time-independent. Therefore, another time-domain algorithm was proposed for simultaneous identification of time-dependent (time-varying) structural parameters and unknown excitations by using recursive least-squares estimation (RLSE). This real-time algorithm was further extended so that on one hand, the time-varying structural parameters and unknown excitations could be identified and, on the other hand, the excessive structural vibration could be effectively mitigated. (3) It is necessary to investigate the feasibility and accuracy of the aforementioned three types of algorithms through experimental studies. This part of work is related to the third objective of the project. The dynamic tests were firstly conducted to verify the proposed FRF-based approach by using a building complex (12 story main building with a 3 story podium structure). By using an additional stiffness spring to simulate the added stiffness provided by a semi-active friction damper, eight test cases were conducted. However, due to the limited funding for this project, the experiments for validating the two time-domain algorithms could not be conducted.

531910.label: Major findings and research outcome
531910.value: Objective 1: The feasibility of the proposed methodology for establishing an integrated sensor-control device network was investigated numerically through a 20-story shear building structure under earthquake excitations. Results showed that on one hand, the reconstructed responses have good agreement with the actual ones, indicating that they can be employed for damage detection. On the other hand, the predetermined control performance can be achieved with the optimal number and location of sensors and actuators. Although the proposed algorithm has been presented and included in the conference proceedings [2], the journal paper is still under review [6]. Objective 2: The effects of measurement noise and excitation conditions for the proposed FRF-based approach were numerically investigated through a five-story building equipped with semi-active friction dampers [journal 1, conference 1]. Results showed that the FRF-based approach could accurately identify the structural damages even though the noise is considered. The comparative numerical study further exemplified that the FRF-based method is more accurate than the natural frequency and mode shape-based method. The reliability of the proposed EKF-based approach was numerically demonstrated via a five-story shear building equipped with MR dampers under two types of excitations. Results showed that the proposed approach can satisfactorily identify the unknown structural parameters and external excitations, and the structural vibration is significantly attenuated at the same time [journal 3]. The RLSE-based method was first utilized to identify the time-vary structural parameters and unknown excitations [ journal 4]. Numerical results clearly demonstrated that this method can identify both quantities efficiently and accurately. A comparative investigation also showed that the proposed algorithm provides faster convergence and more accurate identification results than the ARLES-UI method. The RLSE-based approach was then extended to demonstrate how health monitoring and vibration control can be integrated in real time [journaal 5]. The numerical example of a five story building equipped with MR dampers showed that the proposed method can not only accurately identify time-varying structural parameters and unknown excitations, but also effectively suppress the excessive structural vibration. (3) Objective 3 The laboratory tests were conducted to verify the proposed FRF-based method by utilizing semi-active friction dampers to create FRF changes of a controlled building complex [journal 2]. The experimental results revealed that FRF curves are more sensitive to connection damage than natural frequencies and mode shapes. In addition, the FRF-based method satisfactorily locates and quantifies damage, even with measurement noise and some uncertainties, if the damage size is more than 5 percent.

531910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
531910.value: The experimental validation of the FRF-based approach in the frequency domain has been completed, but the experimental investigation on the feasibility and accuracy of the remaining two time-domain algorithms (i.e. the EKF-based and RLSE-based integrative algorithms) have not been performed due to limited funding available from this project. The principle investigator recently obtained the limited financial support from the university to continue this investigation. A five story shear building structure equipped with MR dampers is being built in the laboratory. The MR dampers will be placed on the 1st, 2nd, and 5th floor of the building model, and the accelerometers will be employed to obtain the structural responses. A series of silicon oil damper will be designed and installed between each of the two neighboring floor plates to increase the structural damping. The dynamic tests are planned to be carried out on a shaking table.

531910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
531910.value: The aims of health monitoring technology are to monitor the loading conditions and structural responses, assess structural performance, detect structural damage, and guide maintenance. For semi-active control technology, it aims at vibration reduction of building structures during man-made or natural hazards, such as earthquakes. However, although both types of technology require sensors, data acquisition and transmission, processing, and analysis, the two have generally been treated separately which is not cost-effective if building structures require both. In this research project, an integrated sensor-control device network has been built which significantly reduces the number of the sensors and control devices as well as the cost of health monitoring system and vibration control system. The proposed integrative algorithms have provided a promising way for the establishment of an integrated system with synthesis of health monitoring technology and semi-active control technology. The laboratory tests also demonstrated that the proposed integrative algorithms have the potential to be applied for real structures. The research conducted in this project can serve as an essential step on the journey towards the realization of truly smart civil structures.

532010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532010.value: Due to several natural disasters occurring in large scales, great attentions have been drawn on quick distribution of disaster relief. A recent typhoon, Morakot, slammed into Taiwan in August, 2009, and killed about 600 people. The government of Taiwan faced strong criticism over its slow distribution of relief. We therefore propose this project to study vehicle routing problems for relief distribution, where aid-supplies must be delivered to victims by multiple vehicles through humanitarian relief chains as quickly as possible. Under this context, it is critical to minimize the latest completion time of all the deliveries, whose hardness and effective algorithms, however, are almost unknown in literature, as most available works were contributed to minimizing the total transportation cost. In order to fill this niche, we aim to: (1) understand the computational hardness of routing for relief distribution, particularly to prove the best possible relative errors that any polynomial time algorithms can achieve; (2) develop effective algorithms that can produce routing plans close to optimum, particularly to ensure small relative errors in both worst-case analysis and computational analysis. A successful completion of the proposed project would make a significant contribution to the algorithm design and the vehicle routing literature. Findings from will be useful in the long term development of useable heuristic solutions that can be implemented for relief distribution in practice. One such area will be the quick distribution of surgical masks during outbreaks of epidemic diseases, like the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) which affected Hong Kong and most Asian regions severely in 2003. 迅速的救災配送是有效應對大規模自然災害的關鍵，但卻又充滿挑戰。例如，2009年8月的莫拉克颱風在台灣造成逾600人死亡，台灣政府卻因救災的緩慢與低效廣受批評。 本項目將研究救災配送中救災車輛的路線規劃問題，目的是將援助物資盡快地送達到受災地點。雖然路線規劃問題已獲廣泛研究，但現有文獻多是優化運輸的總成本，而少有涉及最晚運送抵達時間的優化。 本項目將著重研究救災配送的兩方面理論問題。一方面，我們將研究救災配送的計算複雜性，並證明多項式時間近似算法所能達到的效率上限。另一方面，我們將為救災配送設計近似算法以提供優質的路線規劃，並驗證其與最優路線的效率差距。 本項目力圖填補關於救災配送問題的算法設計和分析等方面的研究空白。研究成果將對救災配送的實踐具有應用價值和指導意義。

532010.label: Realisation of objectives
532010.value: In this project, we have formulated the vehicle routing problem for relief distribution as a min-max path cover problem. To reflect various practical needs, we have developed different variants of the problem, namely, where the vehicles have either unlimited or limited capacities and start from either a given depot or any depot selected from a given depot set, and where the transportation network is either a general graph or a tree. From our study of these variants, we have achieved all the objectives proposed, with three journal papers published or accepted as a result. For Objective 1, we have followed the idea presented in the proposal to develop a heuristic for the problem under a basic setting, where each vehicle has unlimited capacity and starts from the same depot. The heuristic is based on a novel splitting technique that guarantees a significantly better approximation ratio than the previous best. By extending this technique, we have developed new approximation and heuristic algorithms for other variants of the problem. Moreover, by following a novel dynamic programming approach, we have developed the first fully polynomial approximation algorithms for the problem on a tree-shaped network. For Objectives 2 & 3, we have conducted both worst-case and computational analysis to evaluate the performance of the new algorithms. Worst-case analysis is based on a novel technique that can bound the length of the paths obtained. We have shown that the approximation algorithm for the problem under the basic setting achieves an approximation ratio of 3, which improves on the best known approximation ratio of 4. Extending this analysis shows that approximation ratios of new algorithms for other variants of the problem are also significantly better than the best known ratios. Moreover, we have conducted computational analysis over randomly generated instances, and results show that the new algorithms run fast and provide good initial solutions for local search algorithms to seek out further improvements. For Objective 4, we have followed the preliminary analysis to derive the first approximation hardness result for the problem under the basic setting. The analysis is based on a novel reduction technique that reduces the problem to a 3-dimensional matching problem. We prove that under the basic setting it is unlikely to achieve an approximation ratio of less than 4/3 for the problem. By extending the technique developed, we have further derived new approximation hardness results for other variants of the problem.

532010.label: Major findings and research outcome
532010.value: As the research outcome, three journal papers have been published or accepted: 1. Z. Xu (PI), L. Xu, and C.-L. Li, 2010, "Approximation Results for Min-max Path Cover Problems in Vehicle Routing", Naval Research Logistics, 57(8), 728-748. 2. Z. Xu (PI), D. Xu, and W. Zhu, 2012, "Approximation Results for a Min-max Location-Routing Problem", Discrete Applied Mathematics, 160(3), 306-320. 3. L. Xu, Z. Xu (PI), and D. Xu, 2012, "Exact and Approximation Algorithms for the Min-max k-Traveling Salesman Problem on a Tree", European Journal of Operational Research (EJOR), forthcoming. The major findings are as follows: 1. We have found that the vehicle routing problem for relief distribution can be formulated as a min-max path cover problem, and various practical needs can be taken into account by applying different variants [1-3]; 2. Based on a novel splitting technique [1], we have developed approximation algorithms for four typical variants of the min-max path problem, with the vehicles having either unlimited or limited capacities, or starting from either a given depot or any depot of a given depot set. New approximation algorithms for these variants achieve approximation ratios of max{3−2/k, 2}, 5, max{5−2/k, 4}, and 7, respectively [1], significantly better than the best approximation algorithms known to date in the literature on routing for relief distribution. 3. We have found that the splitting technique is also useful in developing constant approximation algorithms for other min-max optimization problems. By extending the technique, we have developed the first approximation algorithms for a min-max location-routing problem [2], this being an extension of the min-max path cover problem, with decisions on locations of the vehicles' depots being taken into account. 4. Based on a novel dynamic programming approach, we have developed the first fully polynomial approximation scheme for the min-max path cover problem on a tree with a constant number of vehicles [3], which has finally closed a question that has remained open for a decade. 5. Based on a novel reduction technique, we have shown that, unless P = NP, it is impossible to achieve approximation ratios less than 4/3, 3/2, 3/2, 2, and 4/3, respectively, for the four typical variants of the min-max path cover problem and the min-max location routing problem [1,2]. As far as we know, this is the first study that reveals the approximation hardness of routing for relief distribution.

532010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532010.value: Further research and proposed course of action are as follows: 1. One direction for future study is to extend the approximation algorithms to other min-max vehicle routing problems. For example, this study assumes that vehicles can have multiple trips to and from depots. However, in some situations, only a single trip is allowed for each vehicle, for which the split technique cannot be used. For such situations, we are currently trying to show that a new edge-exchange heuristic is a 5-approximation algorithm. 2. Also, the current study investigates problems that use paths for covering, but it would be interesting to study similar problems that use tours, trees, or stars for covering. Under some basic settings, the reduction technique developed in this project can still be used, but we are now working on these problems under more sophisticated settings. 3. For the min-max path cover problem on a tree, we assume that the number of vehicles is a constant, but it would be interesting to develop polynomial time heuristics for the problem with an arbitrary number of vehicles. We are now developing a beam search heuristic, and plan to conduct computational analysis to evaluate its performance.

532010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
532010.value: In this project, we have formulated the vehicle routing problem for relief distribution as a min-max path cover problem. To reflect various practical needs, we have developed different variants of the problem in which the vehicles have either unlimited or limited capacities, start from either a given depot or any depot selected from a given depot set, and where the transportation network is either a general graph or a tree. For several variants of the min-max path cover problem, we have developed approximation algorithms with significantly better approximation ratio guarantees than the best algorithms known in the literature to date. The splitting techniques developed for them can be applied to the development of approximation algorithms for other min-max optimization problems. Also, for the min-max path cover problem on a tree, we have developed the first fully polynomial time approximation scheme, which has finally closed a question that has remained open for a decade. Moreover, we have derived the first approximation hardness results for numerous variants of the min-max path cover problem, and the reduction techniques developed for them can now be applied to the development of approximation hardness results for other min-max vehicle routing problems.

532110.label: Project Objectives
532110.value: The objectives of this research project are to carry out both experimental and analytical investigations of the use of long shank superelastic Nitinol SMA bolts (supplied by SAES Smart Materials) in SEE connections subject to cyclic loading so as to provide information regarding the use of SMAs in the field of steel connections. The test data will be able to illustrate the extent of the self-centring behaviour occurs and the ductility performance of the proposed SEE connection. However, due to the temperature dependence of SMA properties, the results of the proposed research will be limited by the fact that testing will take place at a controlled room temperature. The objectives of this research project can be accomplished by the following tasks: Task I Experimental investigation: Tests of SEE connections with long shank superelastic Nitinol SMA bolts to examine the self-centring behaviour, the ductility performance, the energy dissipating capability, strength, and stiffness of the connections will be conducted. The tests will include a number of parameters such as end-plate thickness, length of SMA bolt shank and size of SMA bolts. Material testing will be conducted for the SMA bolts. In particular, the superelastic and the hysteresis behaviour of the Nitinol SMA bolts will be examined in detail. Tension coupon tests will also be conducted to examine and establish the stress-strain behaviour of all the materials used in the connections. Task II Numerical investigation: Finite element (FE) models will be developed to simulate the structural behaviour of the test specimens. Auricchio’s model will be used for the SMA material in the FE analysis. The FE models will be validated by comparing the finite element results with the test results. The results of the nonlinear finite element analysis will provide further insight into the behaviour of the test specimens. The validated models will then be used to conduct a parametric study of the strength and behaviour of SEE connections with SMA bolts. Task III Develop a preliminary design model: Based on the test results and the FE analysis results, a preliminary design model for SEE connections using Nitinol SMA bolts will be developed. The model will be based on the “thick end-plate” design concept to ensure that the inelastic deformation and plastic rotation of the connection are provided only by the elongation of the Nitinol SMA bolts. Deliverables and Significance: This project will provide important new experimental and analytical data about the behaviour of a novel “smart” stiffened extended end-plate connection which is intended to be suitable for earthquake resistant design of moment resisting frames. The test data will also enhance knowledge of the uses of SMAs as further applications in civil engineering. The research findings will be disseminated to international research communities through journal papers and conference presentations and to local engineering communities through seminars and workshops. In addition, the results of this project will provide the impetus for future experimental research in applying the proposed connection in a moment resisting steel frame subject to seismic loading.
