532110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532110.value: Stiffened extended end-plate (SEE) connections have been recognized as one of the stiff partially restrained (PR) connections that, if properly designed, can be used in steel moment resisting frames subject to seismic loading. To ensure ductile performance of such frames, a strong-column/weak-beam concept is usually employed to ensure the formation of plastic hinges in the connecting beams for earthquake resistant design. Due to the formation of plastic hinges, significant permanent deformation of the beams is expected and it is costly to repair the damage after an earthquake. In addition, the SEE connections used in the frames must be ductile enough to make sure that brittle failure of the connections will not occur prior to the development of plastic hinges in the beams. Recent research in the use of shape memory alloys (SMAs), in particular Nitinol, in steel connection applications provides the alternative whereby plastic hinges form in the connections instead of in the beams. Hence, significant permanent deformation of the beams may be avoided after an earthquake. Shape memory alloys are capable of recovering their undeformed shapes by heating (known as the shape memory effect) or removal of stress (known as the superelastic effect) after experiencing large deformations. With the use of long shank superelastic Nitinol SMA bolts in a SEE connection, the connection is able to develop significant inelastic rotations (a superelastic hinge) at the interface between the column flange and the end-plate and subsequently return to its undeformed shape upon unloading due to the superelastic property of the SMA bolts. In addition, due to the flag-shaped hysteresis behaviour of the SMA bolts, the superelastic hinge developed in the connection is endowed with useful energy dissipating capability. With proper design and detailing the proposed SEE connection is also able to achieve good strength and stiffness. Based on the above discussion, it is believed that the proposed SEE connection with superelastic Nitinol SMA bolts is a good potential candidate for adoption in earthquake resistant design. Therefore, the aim of this study is to investigate experimentally and analytically the use of long shank superelastic Nitinol SMA bolts in place of conventional high strength bolts in stiffened extended end-plate connections subject to cyclic loading.

532110.label: Realisation of objectives
532110.value: In general, all the objectives of the study have been achieved. In total, eight full-scale tests were conducted including seven stiffened extended end-plate connections with shape memory alloys (SMA) bolts and one conventional stiffened extended end-plate connection with normal high strength bolts. In addition, tests were also conducted to examine the behaviour of SMA bars subjected to cyclic direct-shear and uniaxial tension. The SMA connection specimens were shown to have excellent recentring abilities and moderate energy dissipation capability. The stiffness and strength of these connections mainly fell into the semi-rigid and partial-strength categories, respectively. The ductility, which was governed by SMA bolt rupture, was found to be dependent on the net threaded-to-shank area ratio of the bolts, where a lower ratio led to earlier bolt fracture over the net threaded cross-section. The SMA bars with a smaller diameter seem to perform better than those with a larger diameter. For the SMA bar tests, the results show sound recentring and moderate energy dissipation/damping capabilities of the bars under cyclic tension below a strain level of 3%, but beyond this the properties start to degrade. On the contrary, it was observed that the cyclic direct-shear performance of SMA bars is generally unsatisfactory with poor recentring, energy dissipation, and damping characteristics. Therefore, the direct use of SMA bars subject to shear loading is undesirable. The finite element (FE) method was used to analyse the test specimens and the validated FE models were subsequently used to conduct a parametric study to further investigate the structural behaviour and strength of extended end-plate connections with SMA bolts. The FE predictions correlate well with the test results, especially in terms of the deformation mode, strain reading, moment-rotation response, residual deformation, and equivalent viscous damping. The parametric study considered the effects of bolt layout, bolt length/diameter, beam-to-connection strength ratio, end-plate thickness, column web panel deformation, and shear resisting mechanism. Summarizing the results of numerical studies as well as the test observations, a set of design guidance for SMA equipped end-plate connections is proposed. Since the general form of the proposed connection is evolved from the conventional stiffened extended end-plate connections, most of the design rules for the basic connection components, e.g. those considered in the component method specified in Eurocode 3, can still be applicable.

532110.label: Major findings and research outcome
532110.value: A total of eight full-scale stiffened extended end-plate connections, including seven connections with SMA bolts and one connection with high strength (HS) bolts were tested. The SMA connections demonstrated their unique properties, i.e. excellent recentring ability, moderate energy dissipation capability, and moderate ductility. The observed response of the SMA connections agreed well with the initial expectations: the main source of recoverable deformation was offered by the SMA bolts, and thus the remaining structural components were mainly in the elastic state. The excellent recentring ability, along with the moderate energy dissipation capability (up to an equivalent viscous damping (EVD) of 17.5%), clearly demonstrated the feasibility and applicability of the proof-of-concept SMA connections. The lowest ductility found for the SMA connections was 2% drift, while for most specimens, the ductility ranged between 3% and 4% drift. The bolt length and diameter were also observed to affect the connection behaviour, where the SMA connections with ‘slender’ bolts (i.e. long and small diameter bolts) were shown to have higher ductility and better hysteretic stability/repeatability. Typical accumulated residual strains for the SMA bar specimens subject to cyclic tension can range between 1% and 3% when a maximum cyclic strain of 7% is attained. The cyclic properties of SMA bars under direct-shear are relatively poor, thus their application to seismic devices is not recommended. A detailed FE study was conducted to predict the structural behaviour of the SMA connection specimens and to validate a FE model for further parametric study. Good agreements between the FE and test results were observed, especially in terms of the hysteretic moment-plastic rotation curve, energy dissipation property, and recentring ability. While some test specimens experienced early bolt fractures at 2%-3% drift, all the FE analysis in this study have considered a maximum drift level of 5%. The EVDs of the six partial-strength connections ranged between 12.5% and 14.9%, while for the remaining full-strength connection, the EVD achieved 20.1%. Several design rules have been discussed to ensure a reliable recentring connection. A novel HS-SMA hybrid connection which uses the HS bolts to resist the direct shear force together with the SMA bolts and SMA Belleville washers has also been proposed. The research findings have resulted in two conference papers and three journal papers of which two of them are published in the “Journal of Constructional Steel Research” and the other one is published in “Materials and Structures”.

532110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532110.value: Although this study has shed considerable light on the feasibility and design philosophy of SMA based recentring connections, there are still a number of important unsolved issues: 1) pre-training and pre-loading protocols, which were not considered in this study, should be stipulated for the key SMA components; 2) strain rate effect should also be studied for large scale SMA components; 3) more tests should be performed on the influences of screw thread pattern, thread-to-shank diameter ratio, length-to-diameter ratio, and the radius linking the threaded and shank parts on the behaviour of SMA bolts; and 4) it was recognized that shear resistance could be a critical issue for the tested SMA connections, and therefore an improved connection type, namely, an HS-SMA hybrid connection, was proposed. The key idea was to employ the HS bolts to resist the shear force, and the SMA bolts were only used to provide recoverable bending resistance. One of the novel aspects of the new connection was the multi-functional use of the SMA Belleville washer, which was employed to protect the HS bolts, to offer the driving force for recentring, and to provide supplementary energy dissipation. Tests on this proposed HS-SMA hydric connection should be conducted.

532110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
532110.value: The conventional design strategies for seismic resistant building structures normally produce permanent post-earthquake damage either in the beams or in the connections, both of which are costly and difficult to repair. To mitigate the severity of these repairs, research studies have been directed to examine the structural response of self-centring based connection systems, which allow the connection to return to its un-deformed state after experiencing a seismic event. These self-centring connections have the ability to undergo large deformation and dissipate moderate amount of seismic energy without significant permanent damage. Tests were conducted to examine the structural behaviour of a bolted steel connection with the bolts manufactured using a shape memory alloy (SMA) which has the ability to undergo reversible deformations and to dissipate energy when subjected to cyclic loading. The test results showed that the SMA connections have good self-centring ability and moderate energy absorption capability. Computer simulations of the test specimens were also performed. The results of the computer simulations compared well with that of the tests. Preliminary design considerations of this SMA connection were recommended and a novel connection utilizing both high strength steel bolts and SMA bolts was also proposed.

532210.label: Realisation of objectives
532210.value: All of the objectives have been realized. The detailed description is as follows: 1. To fabricate an array of OECTs based on PEDOT:PSS with a device size of about twenty micro-meters by solution process; OECT (5×5) arrays based on poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) were fabricated in poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) microwells by physical delamination. The device has the channel width and length of 22µm and 5µm, respectively. Compared with the OECTs with the channel length/width of 5 mm/0.2 mm, the miniaturized device shows much stable performance and much faster response to application voltages. (See reference: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - General Subjects,1830, 4402-4406 (2013). Adv. Mater. 24, 34–51(2012). ) 2. To integrate a single cancer cell with each OECT. Cancer cells were trapped by PEG walls due to the different surface energy of PEG and PEDOT:PSS in water. Single cell can be localized on the surface of an OECT for sensing applications. (See reference: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - General Subjects,1830, 4402-4406 (2013). Adv. Mater. 24, 34–51(2012).) 3. To continuously monitor single cancer cell activities under the effect of drugs and chemical agents by measuring the characteristics of the OECTs. Cells were monitored by characterizing the device performance of the OECTs. The transfer characteristic of the devices with cells under the effect anticancer drug changes with time. The morphological change of the device can be observed under microscopy as well. (see reference: J. Mater. Chem. 22, 22072-22076 (2012); Adv. Mater. 24, 34 (2012)) 4. To develop a fundamental understanding of the sensing mechanism of the OECTs integrated with single cells. We found that the electrostatic interaction between cells and the active lays of OECTs plays a key role on the sensing performance of the devices. Due to the negative surface charges on cells, holes will be attracted by the negative charges in the active layer and induce the change in the channel current. Under the effect of anti-cancer drug, the surface potential and the adhesion of cells on the devices will changed and thus the devices show obvious response to the anticancer drug. (see reference: J. Mater. Chem. 22, 22072-22076 (2012); Adv. Mater. 24, 34 (2012); Nano Letters, 12, 1404-1409 (2012); BIOSENSORS & BIOELECTRONICS, 26, 4559-4563(2011). ).

532210.label: Major findings and research outcome
532210.value: We find that the performance of OECTs can be dramatically improved by miniaturizing the device size. The response and the stability of the OECTs are greatly enhanced. The devices can be used for cell analysis. We design PEG walls placed around the OECTs, which can trap single or few cells around the devices. The devices were prepared by physical delamination method for the first time and could be used for the fabrication of OECT arrays with high density. (See reference: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - General Subjects,1830, 4402-4406 (2013). ) OECTs can be used for monitoring the cell activities conveniently. The effect of drugs has been successfully tested in our work and the device is promising for drug selection in the future. (see reference: Adv. Mater. 24, 34 (2012); J. Mater. Chem. 22, 22072-22076 (2012)) Besides cell-based sensors, we also find that the device is an idea transducer for glucose, DNA, bacteria (Adv. Mater. 23, 4035-4040 (2011);Adv. Funct. Mater. 21, 2264–2272 (2011); J. Mater. Chem. 22, 22072-22076 (2012)), The sensing mechanism of the device has been studied systematically and the major mechanism is due to interaction between the cells and the active layers of the devices. The finding pave a way to develop other types of cell-based biosensors, such as neuron signal monitoring and cardiac cells testing, by using OECTs. (see reference: Adv. Mater. 24, 34 (2012))

532210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532210.value: The OECTs can be used for many different types of sensors, such as dopamine, glucose, bacteria, uric acid etc. On the other hand, the OECT arrays can be used for multifunctional sensors integrated on a single chip. The devices are flexible, low cost and highly sensitive. Therefore, the OECTs and OECT arrays can be used in many healthcare products, disposal sensors, clinical applications and even wearable electronics in the future.

532210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
532210.value: In this project, OECT arrays were prepared by solution process and used for sensing cells for the first time. To capture the single cells on the top of the devices, PEG walls were patterned by physical delamination. Cells were successfully captured on the devices and the device performance was characterized successfully. The interaction between cells and OECTs has been systematically studied and was found that the electrostatic interaction plays a key role in it. The project demonstrates the successful application of OECTs in cell-based biosensors. Owning to the advantages of the OECTS, including high sensitivity, low cost, biocompatibility and mechanical flexibility, the devices are potentially useful for many biosensing applications besides the detections of cells. More importantly, we found that miniaturized devices show much better stability and faster response speed, which is key to the applications of the devices in monitoring biological signals. Based on the technique developed in the project, the devices can be integrated in biological systems and used for in situ monitoring of carious signals, especially neuron signals and cardiac cell responses.

532810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532810.value: Routing control is a key component in many engineering and service systems. In this project, we consider a system of parallel servers, where an arriving job can be dispatched to any one of the servers. When the arriving job can observe the queue-lengths of all servers, it is natural to apply the well-known join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) policy, which will yield a good performance, and is often optimal, in minimizing the total system workload. However, retrieving such queue-length information may be costly in many situations. For example, when a manager assigns job orders or inquiries to a number of customer service officers in a service center, he may incur excessive communication (cost of retrieving information) if he reviews the number pending jobs of each officer upon each job arrival; for mirror web servers that store the same data at geographically distributed locations, retrieving the state of all servers upon each download request will cause prolonged delay in response and generate overhead traffics. We study a balanced routing control policy that would be an appealing option when it is costly to retrieve queue-length state: upon each job arrival, choose a few servers randomly and then send the job to the one with the shortest queue. As compared with traditional routing policies such as the join-the-shortest-queue, the probabilistic proportional and the round-robin routing policies, the balanced routing policy aims to make a better tradeoff between the cost of waiting (long total queue length) and the cost of retrieving queue length information. Due to the dynamic nature, it is difficult to study the performance and optimality of the policy using traditional methods such as the matrix algebra, which involve high-dimensional Markovian state space and hence intractable computational complexity. To overcome such difficulties, we plan to apply the heavy traffic analysis, which can provide a sound approximation for many complex stochastic system due to its ability to filter out non-essential details of the system. The insight from the proposed research would contribute to the understanding of the basic routing control mechanisms for stochastic processing networks, which arise in many telecommunication, manufacturing and service systems. The control policy is also timely for business and industry when large service and engineering systems are created faster, and the tradeoff between the costs of waiting and information retrieval in such systems become more important than ever. 分派控制是许多工程和服务系统中的重要部分。本项目中，我们考虑一个并行服务系统。新来的顾客服务请求将被分派到系统中的一个服务台。如果刚到的顾客能看到各个服务台前的顾客队长，我们很自然会用“最短队(JSQ)”方法分派顾客，从而使系统总负荷最小。然而，在许多情况下需要一定的成本才能取得队长信息。例如，在一个服务中心，管理人员要把一个工作任务分派給服务员，如果每来一个任务就去查询每个服务员待完成的服务数，就会产生过多的沟通成本；对于一个分布于各地的网页镜像系统，若每来一个下载请求就检查一次各个服务器的状态，也会增加延时和额外的流量。 我们研究一个平衡分派控制方法 -- 当队长信息变得昂贵时，这将是一个有吸引力的选择：当新的任务到达，先随机选取几个服务员，再把该任务送到队长最短的服务员。与传统的分派方法（如JSQ，按比例概率分派，round-robin分派等）相比，平衡分派将在等待成本和队长信息获取成本之间取得平衡。 基于系统的特性，若用传统方法分析，比如矩阵代数，就需要引人高维 Markovian 状态空间并导致难以处理的计算复杂性。我们将应用重流量分析方法克服这些困难。该方法能过滤掉非本质细节，从而对复杂系统给出恰当的近似。 这个研究有助于理解随机处理系统里的基本分派机制，而这些随机系统是在研究实际的通讯，制造和服务系统中提出的。另外，现代工商业里，将会有越来越多大规模的服务和工程系统。在等待成本和信息获取之间取得平衡有助于改善这些系统的性能。故此，本研究是及时的。

532810.label: Realisation of objectives
532810.value: We have developed the diffusion limit for the system under studied. This result can be applied to estimate the system performance in particular when it is heavily loaded. Numerical studies also illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed routing control policy. These studies indicate that under the balanced routing, the cost of waiting can be minimized and the cost information retrieval becomes negligible in a heavily load system. More details are explained in Section 6.1 (Major findings and research outcome). Therefore, the first two objectives in this project are realized. The study related to objective 3 became a complicated part of this project, and developed into two interesting researches. First, we have reported some preliminary results of the comparison between balanced routing and the other policies in the first publication in Part C, and more interestingly the insight from these results give rise to a new and ongoing research in the optimization of the routing control. Second, we find a major difficulty when we tried to characterize the degree of (stationary) performance degradation compared with the join-the-shortest-queue policy, and then we step back to look at the validity of the heavy traffic stationary approximation, which has been developed heuristically so far. This led to a fruitful study (a publication and an ongoing research) in the so-called interchange of limits. Therefore, the objective 3 is essentially fulfilled. Also refer to Section 6.1 below for more details.

532810.label: Major findings and research outcome
532810.value: We have carried out heavy traffic analysis of a network of parallel servers under balanced routing control. It is known that finding a routing policy that minimizes the total workload in the system is a difficult problem in general. Even if the optimal policy is identified, the policy would require the full queue length information at the arrival of each job; for example, the join-the-shortest-queue policy would require comparing the queue lengths of all the servers. Under the balanced routing policy, we derive the fluid limits and diffusion limits of the queue length processes and the workload processes. It is interesting to note that the diffusion limits are the same for these processes regardless the choice of c as long as c >= 2 (where c is the number of randomly chosen servers in our proposed balanced routing policy). We further show that the proposed balanced routing policy for any fixed c >= 2 is asymptotically optimal in the sense that it minimizes the workload over all time in the diffusion limit. We observe through both theoretical and numerical analyses a remarkable feature desirable in many applications; that is the policy helps to distribute works among all the servers evenly. These results are reported in Operations Research (first publication in Part C). In addition, we have also carried out extensive simulation studies to compare the balanced routing with traditional routing control policies as well as new policies. The results have revealed significant rooms for optimizing many of these routing control policies. These observations are striking and point to a new line of research. The PI is exploring this opportunity. The second set of findings concern with the validity of heavy traffic stationary approximation derived in the above, i.e., justifying the interchange of two limits, i.e., letting t and k to infinity in the diffusion limit mentioned above (with t being the time index and k the scaling parameter). We provide such a justification using a moment condition on the primitive data, the interarrival and service times. Indeed, the justification has been worked out for a broader class of stochastic processing networks, including the parallel servers system, the main object in this project. Hence, we have filled a major gap in the heavy traffic approach, which was introduced for the analysis of stochastic systems in 1960's. The findings are reported in the second publication in Part C.

532810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532810.value: We have demonstrated the effectiveness of balanced routing for a system comprising parallel servers. A nature extension in is to investigate the application of this policy in the multiclass queueing networks, which has been an object of broad interest in the past two decades. Moreover, we are also interested in extending the research to the so-called many servers regime (arisen from large-scale service systems like the call center operations), where the number of servers increase as well. Another interesting further research involves the real implementation of the balance routing policy. As mentioned in "major output", we have shown theoretically that our balanced routing control yields the optimal performance when the system is heavily congested. In real implementation of the policy, it is possible to improve the tradeoff between the information retrieval and customer waiting by modifying the policy by retrieving the queue length information after the arrival of several jobs (rather than each arrival). Then, what is the optimal batch size for each retrieval of queue length information? Under what situation and in what sense, the modified policy can achieve the (near) optimal performance?

532810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
532810.value: Limited flexibility is surprisingly powerful, as vigorously demonstrated in this research. We examine a system of parallel servers, in which an arriving job can be dispatched to any one of the servers. When the arriving job can observe the queue-lengths of all servers, the well-known join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) policy is applied, usually with good results. However, retrieving the queue-length information, as required by the JSQ policy, may be costly in many situations. In this project, we propose a so-called balanced routing policy --- under which upon the arrival of each job, a few servers randomly selected with the job being routed to the one with the shortest queue. The flexibility is limited --- only two or a few servers, rather than all in JSQ policy, are selected. Yet, we establish that the balanced routing policy, with the limited flexibility, almost minimizes the system workload in terms of the total number of jobs waiting to be served and can distributes the work among all the servers evenly. This work represents an effort in developing tools and methodologies that support those innovations to tap on the complexity in the changing business environment to achieve competitiveness.

532910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532910.value: The project aims to develop pressure therapy gloves used in the treatment of hypertrophic scars which may cause serious threats to hand function and/or result in a clawed hand. The gloves must fit like a second skin to patients and are engineered to apply adequate pressure to various parts of the hand so as to prevent or reduce the risk of formation of hypertrophic scars and contractures, and must be worn continuously (24 hours a day). Fitting and pressure of the gloves must also be reassessed regularly and adjustments should be made when required. However, the rate of patient compliance of the continuous use of pressure therapy gloves has not been satisfactory. The problems associated with the low rate of compliance are easily identifiable, such as poor air transmission (particularly in summer), discomfort, limited mobility, poor fitting, obsolete functional design and appearance. The project is intended to design and develop pressure therapy gloves with optimum fitting, comfort and functional performance. The dimensions used include physiological and psychological needs of patients, practical use and clinical procedures of the pressure therapy treatment, analysis of the pressure levels and contact conditions of pressure therapy gloves, design of geometry knitting structure of compression materials, development of efficient measuring systems of hand anthropometry, and precise determination of effective pressure that can prevent or reduce the risk of disfigurement and functional disability of hands. To achieve optimum comfort and functional performance, factors such as psychophysical relationship between pressure distribution and subjective sensory comfort perception, non-linear stress-strain and mechanical properties of fabric, deterioration of fabric elasticity that influences comfort, functional performance and efficacy of pressure therapy gloves, are also analysed. Gloves specifications, fabrication, structural features and biomechanical models of pressure simulation when pressure gloves are worn are to be formulated. Prototypes of pressure therapy gloves (e.g. gauntlets for the wrist and hands, gloves for the thumb and fingers, etc.) are to be developed. Based on the clinical wear trial tests, the efficacy of the treatment and patient compliance is to be evaluated. The outcomes of the project will advance our knowledge of a new design or dimension of pressure therapy garments and/or medical clothing by incorporating modern textiles and garment technologies. More importantly, the project can enhance the quality of treatment and care provided for patients.

532910.label: Realisation of objectives
532910.value: During the project period, all of the above 5 objectives has been achieved. A clinical study has been carried out to establish a thorough scientific basis for understanding the needs of patients who wear pressure therapy gloves. Throughout the study, the scar conditions, interfacial pressure, temperature and humidity between gloves and skin are recorded and analysed. In this study, 2D and 3D image analysis methods have been developed as the measuring systems of hand anthropometry by using a domestic colour scanner and 3D laser scanner respectively. Both image analysis methods do not require direct contact with the hand of the subjects throughout the entire process and hence discomfort of patients during measurement taking can be minimized. The anthropometry measurements, morphology and curvatures of the hand, thumbs, fingers and related joints have been analysed. The pressure delivered by pressure gloves made of various fabrics with different reduction factors (RFs) in different locations over the hand, as well as with different hand postures has been evaluated. A mathematical interfacial pressure prediction model based on Laplace’s equation has been formulated. The glove-skin interfacial pressure can be predicted from the fabric tension behavior, strain of glove and hand curvatures. A biomechanical model that simulates the skin pressure in relation to fabric mechanical properties and curvatures of anatomic sites are formulated by using finite element analysis. The effects of glove fabrics and RFs on hands and fingers in terms of dexterity and comfort have been investigated. Physical, mechanical and thermal properties of fabrics, including stress-strain behaviour, bending, surface roughness, air permeability and moisture retention and glove-skin interfacial pressure induced by different combinations of fabrics and RFs are evaluated. To prescribe an optimal pressure therapy glove for hypertrophic scar treatment, the effect of pressure glove RFs on forearm biomechanical and psychophysical responses are evaluated. The changes of forearm muscle activities in performing daily tasks with hands are systematically analysed. New pressure therapy gloves with new fabrication of 3D spacer fabrics and design which improve the physiological comfort of patients and facilitate the flexible and continuous use of the gloves are developed. Laboratory tests and clinical trials on the new glove prototypes are undertaken to evaluate the effectiveness and practical use of the gloves.

532910.label: Major findings and research outcome
532910.value: A new approach of taking hand anthropometry measurements by using 2D and 3D scanning methods was developed and compare against the traditional direct measurement method. A low-cost, portable 3D laser scanner was used and the precise hand measurements can be obtained during clinical practices in various locations in a hospital. A complete 3D image of a plaster hand can be formed from the 3D scanner. Hand data can be accurately and efficiently taken from 2D or 3D image analyses. The effects of fabric mechanical compression on pressure therapy gloves are studied. A new method is proposed to predict the amount of pressure acting on skin induced by pressure therapy gloves on the basis of hand curvatures extracted from three-dimensional hand images. Based on the fabric tensile behaviour and the reduction factor adopted in glove pattern making, the corresponding glove pressure is predicted by the local strain, fabric tension and body curvature. A biomechanical model that simulates the skin pressure in relation to fabric mechanical properties and curvatures of anatomic sites are formulated by using finite element analysis. The effects of glove fabrics and RFs on hands and fingers in terms of dexterity and comfort have been investigated. The use of pressure therapy gloves has considerable impact on hand dexterity and forearm muscle activity in the carrying out of normal daily activities, and this impact is strongly associated with the tightness or RFs of the gloves. To optimise comfort and treatment adherence, fabric choice and anticipated fabric properties should also be taken into consideration. A suitable fabric which can give sufficient interfacial pressure and a lower RF (<15%) should be chosen. New pressure therapy gloves with new fabrication of 3D spacer fabrics and pattern design approach are developed. In this new approach, finger web slants are taken into account in the process of glove pattern design and development. This new approach in pattern development is therefore not only able to improve the fit and comfort of pressure therapy gloves, but also enhances the compliance and effectiveness of hypertrophic scar treatment. The use of spacer fabrics in pressure pads can considerably increases glove pressure, improves the comfort perception and hand motions of the patients. A US patent entitled Pressure Glove (Application NO. 13/433,268) has been filed in March 2012. Four conference papers and five journal papers have been published/submitted.

532910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532910.value: It is recognized that the timeframe of clinical trial in this study is relatively short as the use of pressure garments is generally 12-18 months or until the scar matures in 2 or 3 years. Nonetheless, this study provides preliminary evidence supporting the use of spacer fabrics making up pressure pads and finger web slants in pattern design so as to enhance the interfacial glove-skin pressure and glove fit. Considering the wide range of new innovative textile materials as well as spacer knitting structures and properties, a useful extension would be to evaluate spacer fabricated pads with different pile heights, rigidity and the corresponding deformity after repeated uses. The mechanical and viscoelastic properties of the hypertrophic scar should also be evaluated. Hence, the parametric effects of different interactions, including the hand anthropometry, fabric properties and material plurality of pressure pads, deterioration of fabric elasticity, as well as the condition and elasticity of hypertrophic scars can also be incorporated into the current FE model so as to prescribe the optimal pressure therapy gloves for patients.

533310.label: Project Objectives
533310.value: Development of techniques for computing the shortest path integrity proof. In practice, a queried shortest path spans only a small fraction of the entire road network. We will study the conditions for extracting a concise subgraph from the road network as the integrity proof of the shortest path. Efficient search algorithms and index structures will be developed to facilitate this process. We will also develop efficient client-side techniques for checking the integrity of the reported shortest path against its proof. Development of incremental techniques for maintaining the proof with respect to dynamic traffic updates. As time passes, the shortest path and its integrity proof change dynamically according to the traffic information. However, it is too expensive to recompute the shortest path and its proof whenever the traffic information of a road segment (i.e., edge weight) changes. We will develop communication-efficient techniques for computing and updating the changes in the integrity proof, instead of recomputing the entire integrity proof. Development of techniques for providing integrity proof for advanced path queries. There are other important graph problems such as the maximum flow problem and the traveling salesman problem. We will extend our trustworthy query processing techniques to handle these advanced path queries.

Development of techniques for providing integrity proof for advanced path queries. There are other important graph problems such as the maximum flow problem and the traveling salesman problem. We will extend our trustworthy query processing techniques to handle these advanced path queries.

533310.value: 在此項目，我們研究安全的在線地圖最短路徑查詢。因為在線服務器捕獲最新交通信息， 掌上電腦用戶通常用網上服務器。另一方面，黑客可能入侵服務器，然後篡改服務器的報告路徑。我們的挑戰來自安全的最短路徑查詢。傳統的解決方案，如數字簽名，只幫助核實儲在服務器上路網數據的完整，不可能表明最短路徑的完整。更加複雜問題的是：(i) 道路網絡的數據龐大，及 (ii) 在道路上的交通信息網絡經常更新，所以無法提前預計結果。很多交通規劃需要安全的最短路徑查詢。例如，救護車需要安全的最短路徑到事發地點，以減少生命危險。其他應用包括急運包裹，物流流程規劃等。我們的目標是發展高效率的技術處理安全的最短路徑查詢，應付大型道路網和頻繁交通信息更新。做法是在道路網中提取簡潔子圖，證明最短路徑的完整性。我們發展高效的搜索算法和索引結構配合上述進程。關於交通信息更新，我們發展增量技術保持最短路徑的完整證明，不必重新計算完整的證明。我們還將研究安全的先進查詢，如路徑最大流查詢。

533310.label: Realisation of objectives
533310.value: We have carried out research activities on all project objectives. Two research students (one MPhil and one PhD) were recruited to investigate these issues. For objective 1, we have designed a spatial authentication index (Voronoi MR-tree), developed efficient server-side algorithms to construct concise integrity proof, and developed efficient client-side algorithms to verify the correctness of result against its integrity proof. For objective 2, we have investigated how to update the integrity proof continuously according to position updates of mobile clients. We applied the safe region technique to reduce the communication frequency between the server and mobile clients. Also, we have developed algorithms to compute the integrity proof in an incremental fashion. For objective 3, we have investigated the integrity proof for other queries such as nearest neighbor queries and range queries. We published our research results in a top-tier database journal [ACM TODS 2011] and three top-tier database conferences [IEEE ICDE 2011, ACM CIKM 2012, VLDB 2012].

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
533310.value: In a route planning problem, the user specifies his start and target locations, and then asks for the shortest path between them on a road network. Users prefer online mapping services to offline navigation software because (i) online services capture timely traffic information and require no storage of maps on the user’s mobile device, and (ii) navigation software requires the user to regularly update maps on his mobile device. Nevertheless, those services have some security concerns that remain unresolved. For example, hackers may infiltrate into the server and then actively tamper with the server’s reported result. The outcome of this research project will have substantial impact on many route planning applications. Emergency services receive calls and then dispatch units (e.g., ambulances, fire trucks, police cars) to the incident location using the shortest path. Due to the health, life, and property risks involved in the incident, emergency services demand that the shortest path received from the server must be trustworthy. Similarly, the trustworthy processing of shortest path queries prevents taxi overcharging problems. Every taxi driver could present a proof of the correctness of a route, so the passengers would not be afraid of being overcharged. In another application, delivery companies could show that each urgent parcel is indeed delivered to its recipient along the shortest path.

533910.label: Project Objectives
533910.value: To obtain a good metallurgically bonded HEA-Mg interface that is free from major defects and brittle intermetallics. 533910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
533910.value: In recent years, much interest has been generated in applying magnesium alloys to stress-bearing applications, especially in the aerospace and automotive industries, for it is well known that magnesium alloys have low density and are characterised by high strength-to-weight ratio. However, they are also notorious for their poor corrosion and wear properties. It is generally accepted that it is necessary to apply a surface protective coating to magnesium components or products if they are to survive in a harsh working environment. Indeed, over the years, intensive research efforts have been devoted to developing better coatings in order to meet the challenges demanded by industry. Notwithstanding the advancements that have been made in alloy development, heat treatment and surface engineering, it is still difficult to find a single coating technology capable of providing adequate protection to magnesium alloys from corrosion and abrasion in harsh service environments. Yet the need for lightweight and enduring alloys is becoming more urgent with our growing environmental awareness. The market for a successful material is likely to be very large. Over the past few years, the applicant and other researchers have conducted a series of research studies on laser alloying/cladding of various coatings on magnesium alloys and their composites with the aim of improving their corrosion and wear properties. In spite of the encouraging results that have been obtained so far, the coatings produced are not without weaknesses. The main concerns among these are the weak interfaces and/or low toughness of the coating, which are still not completely resolved. The problems arise mainly due to the formation of brittle intermetallic compounds in the coating. Based on what we have learned from previous studies, the applicant proposes to use High Entropy Alloys (HEAs) as the surface alloying material to overcome these problems. HEAs are based on a new alloy design concept – multi-principle elements – and the alloys consist of five or more principal elements in near equi-molar ratios. They normally have a stable simple solid solution structure resistant to the formation of brittle intermetallics. These alloys possess high as-cast hardness and exhibit excellent wear resistance. It is envisaged that given the unique characteristics of HEAs, and if they can be successfully applied on magnesium alloys, the crucial issues of interface brittleness and low toughness would be resolved. In addition, the high-entropy coatings would meet the demand for good corrosion and wear protection.

533910.label: Realisation of objectives
533910.value: To realise Objectives 1 and 2 To improve the inherent low wear resistance and poor corrosion resistance of Mg alloys, some high entropy alloys (HEAs), such as AlCoCrCuFeNi and Cu0.5NiAlCoCrFeSi, were clad on Mg alloy substrates using the pre-placed powder bed method and the direct blown powder method. Also, a two-step method, involving plasma spray processing and laser re-melting was also employed. It was envisaged that this two-step method should be able to alleviate the compositional dilution problem occurred at the coating interface. In addition to the forming of a pure HEA coating on Mg substrates using laser cladding, the laser melt injection (LMI) technique was also employed for fabricating a HEA particle reinforced composite layer on Mg substrates. The results of these studies showed that the pre-placed and the direct blown methods can produce HEA coatings which are metallurgically bonded to the substrates with no major solidification defects (i.e. cracks and porosity) present at the coating-substrate interface. Moreover, only a small degree of dilution of the HEA composition occurred, and the clad-layer consisted of only bcc and fcc simple solid solution phases without intermetallic compounds. On the other hand, the two-step method can totally eliminate the dilution problem but some porosity was found in the plasma-sprayed layer. The wear resistance of the laser-clad coatings was evaluated using a block-on-ring dry sliding wear tester. Whilst a potentiodynamic polarization test was employed to evaluate the corrosion behaviour of the coatings with the test conducted in a 3.5wt.% NaCl solution. The results showed that both laser cladding and the LMI technique can improve the wear resistance of Mg significantly, whereas the former can also improve the corrosion resistance of the alloy. To realise Objective 3 The microstructure of the HEA coatings was characterised using scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy. In addition, the solidification behaviour of HEA coatings was analysed using the Kurz–Giovanola–Trivedi model, the Gaümann model and Hunt’s criterion with modifications for multi-component alloys. As a result of the above studies, the relationships between microstructure, corrosion properties and wear properties have been realised. The abovementioned work and results demonstrate that the three objectives have been accomplished. The study is now complete and the results have been published in 5 SCI journals and presented in a conference.

533910.label: Major findings and research outcome
533910.value: Laser cladding of HEA coatings has been shown to be a promising method for increasing both the corrosion and wear resistance of magnesium alloys. This research was considered to be a pioneer work in this subject area. The following summarised the major findings of the work: (i) Laser cladding using a pre-placed method is able to fabricate a relatively thick HEA coating on Mg-alloy substrates with low levels of substrate and coating dilution. All the HEA coatings produced only consisted of bcc and/or fcc simple solid solution phases without intermetallic compounds. Moreover, no major defects, such as cracks and porosity, were present in the coating. [reported in Papers 1, 2, 3] (ii) The hardness of the laser-clad HEA coating was some ten times higher than that of the Mg-substrate and was even higher than that of the same HEA produced by arc melting. The coating exhibited good wear resistance, with a wear rate five times lower than that of the substrate material in dry friction wear conditions. [reported in Papers 1 & 2] (iii) The free corrosion potentials of the HEA clad specimens were some 1000 mV more noble than that of the magnesium substrate. The corrosion current densities of the clad specimens were one order of magnitude lower than that of the un-clad magnesium alloy. Moreover, the former displayed a passive region but the latter did not. [reported in Papers 2 & 3] (iv) The solidification behaviours of HEA alloys were, for the first time, analysed using the Kurz–Giovanola–Trivedi model, the Gaümann model and Hunt’s criterion with modifications for multi-component alloys. [reported in Papers 4, 5, 3] (v) The laser melt injection technique was, for the first time, employed to form HEA particle reinforced metal matrix composite coatings on an Mg alloy; the wear volume loss of the coating was only one-seventh of that of the substrate material. [reported in Paper 6]

533910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
533910.value: In this research, a two-step method, involving plasma spray processing and laser re-melting has been shown to be an effective surface engineering technique for fabricating HEA coatings on Mg alloys without encountering the dilution problem. However, porosity was found in the plasma-sprayed layer. More experiments are needed to establish the appropriate processing window. The laser melt injection technique has been shown to be able to form HEA particle reinforced metal matrix composite coatings on Mg alloy substrates for improving wear resistance. This research area is virtually a virgin territory, which deserves further investigation. It is possible to come up with suitable HEAs that are biocompatible in nature and be able to use laser cladding to form protective coatings on implants. Again, this research area is virtually a virgin territory, which deserves exploration and examination. The P.I. may seek internal funding in support of the implementation of these recommendations.

533910.value: In recent years, much interest has been generated in applying magnesium alloys to stress-bearing applications, especially in the aerospace and automotive industries, for it is well known that magnesium alloys have low density and are characterised by high strength-to-weight ratio. However, they are also notorious for their poor corrosion and wear properties. Indeed, over the years, intensive research efforts have been devoted to developing better coatings in order to meet the challenges demanded by industry. However, it is still difficult to find a single coating technology capable of providing adequate protection to magnesium alloys from corrosion and abrasion in harsh service environments. The employment of laser cladding to fabricate High Entropy Alloy (HEA) coatings on magnesium alloys is a new attempt. 534910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
534910.value: The project aims to develop dye and photopolymer co-sensitized solar cells on the basis of novel anodic titanium dioxide (TiO2) with highly-organized nanotube (NT) or nanorod (NR) arrays to obtain significant improvement in photon-to-current conversion efficiency. First, TiO2 NT or NR arrays supported on a titanium substrate will be fabricated by controlled anodic oxidization with a post-calcination process, to obtain the desired architecture and crystalline structure. Second, co-sensitization modification will be conducted by sequential treatments with hybrid sensitizers of carboxylated polypyridyl ruthenium dye and carboxylated polythiophene photopolymer through chemical adsorption and electropolymerization processes, resulting in a composite layer of dye and photopolymer with high bonding strength on TiO2 NT or NR arrays. Accordingly, a feasible electron transfer route can be established by optimizing the TiO2 microstructure of nanotubes and nanorods. More electrons can be transferred from photon-excited dye/photopolymer molecules to the electrode substrate via the TiO2 conduction band for the co-sensitized solar cells by minimizing the photoelectron back-transfer. The optimal TiO2 nanostructure and co-sensitization approach will contribute to enhancing the overall efficiency of these novel solar cells. 本項目旨在研究一種基於陽極氧化製備的新型高度有序納米管或納米線（棒）、使用染料及光聚合物共敏化的、光電轉化效率顯著提高的太陽能電池。首先，通過控制陽極氧化過程製備生長於鈦基體上的二氧化鈦納米管或納米線（棒）並通過後處理過程以得到期望的結構及晶相。其次，依次分別通過化學吸附和電聚合利用釕配合物染料和聚噻吩類光敏聚合物共敏化改性以在二氧化鈦納米管或納米線（棒）表面形成具有高結合強度的染料分子和光敏聚合物的複合層。還通過優化二氧化鈦納米管及納米線（棒）的形貌及晶體結構以改善電子在電極的輸運行為。通過使用染料及光聚合物共敏化改性以降低光生電子復合，更多的電子可以經過二氧化鈦導帶到達電池電極從而提高電池性能。本項目優化的光陽極結構及共敏化改性可以協同提高此類電池的光電轉化性能。

534910.label: Realisation of objectives
534910.value: This project aims to study the TiO2 nanotubes (NTs) based dye sensitized solar cells (DSSCs). To achieve the objectives of the project, the research works were focused on the investigation of the photonic crystal (PC) effects aroused from anodization formed TiO2 PCs, which is expected to be the simplest method to PCs to compete with traditional methods like templating by means of self-assembly of low-refractive-index colloidal microspheres and holographic laser lithography and direct laser writing. In this project, we have developed a single-step approach to the seamless coupling of a PC layer to a TiO2 NT absorbing layer for greatly enhanced photovoltaic performance of DSSCs. The TiO2 NT layers were fabricated by a direct periodic current pulse anodization. The PC effects can be controlled within the visible light region by tuning the period of anodization [1]. We employed the PCs layer to DSSCs with tuning the PC effects within the dye absorption region by forming free-standing open-ended TiO2 NT layers by the two-step anodization method and applied the as growth NT arrays to the photoanode of DSSCs [2]. In order to conquer the challenges in the current technology to couple a DSSC with a PC, we proposed a novel design of PC-based photoanode, composed of a thick TiO2 nanoparticle absorption layer and a thin TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal (TiO2 NT PC) membrane. In this architecture, the bandgap of TiO2 NT PC can be precisely tailored by modulating the anodization parameters using the current-pulse anodization process [8,11]. The relatively low internal surface area of anodized TiO2 nanotube arrays (TNAs) limits dye adsorption and light capturing in TNA-based DSSCs. Therefore, water treatment of as-anodized TNAs at room temperature was used to tailor the geometry of TNA walls in a controllable way, leading to a hybrid tube wall structure with the outer shell in a tubular morphology and the inner surface consisting of small particles. To enable front-side illumination in DSSCs, the TNAs with porous inner walls were transferred to transparent conductive oxide substrates by a selfdetaching and transfer technique [9,16]. In addition to the study of the TiO2 nanotubes (NTs) based DSSCs as energy conversion devices, our research was also extended to study energy materials for carbon based environmental friendly lithium-ion batteries as energy storages [3-7, 10, 12-15, 17, 18] through the creations of the nanostructures on the various electrospun nanofibres.

534910.label: Major findings and research outcome
534910.value: In this project, we developed a single-step approach to the seamless coupling of a PC layer to a TiO2 NT absorbing layer for greatly enhanced photovoltaic performance of DSSCs. The DSSCs equipped with this bi-layer structure showed significantly enhanced power conversion efficiency, increase of over 50% compared with the cells without a PC layer. This improvement is attributed to the enhanced light harvesting of the DSSCs in the spectral range corresponding to the photonic bandgap of the PC and a longer wavelength range. A free-standing open-ended TiO2 NT layer was successfully fabricated by the two-step anodization method and was applied to the photoanode of DSSCs. It was shown that the effective length of the NT layer in the DSSCs was increased in the open-ended NT structure, and the electron lifetime also increased. These two factors contributed to the enhanced photovoltaic performance of the DSSC. A novel design of PC-based photoanode, composed of a thick TiO2 nanoparticle absorption layer and a thin TiO2 nanotube PC membrane was conducted in which the thick TiO2 NP works as the absorbing layer, while the thin TiO2 NT PC provides multi-functionality. Based on the high controllability of current-pulse anodization, the bandgap of TiO2 NT PC can be precisely tailored for maximum PCE. Compared to the normal TiO2 NP based DSSCs, the combined effects of PC and light-scattering yield the maximum enhancement in PCE (39.5%) when the stop band of TiO2 NT PC best matches the absorption maximum of the dye molecules. The water treated TNAs were incorporated into front-side illuminated DSSCs, exhibiting a greatly enhanced solar energy conversion efficiency of 6.06% (improved by _33%). TiO2 and carbon based nano-structured composite fibres were developed as the anode materials for LIBs by using the electrospinning technique. As results, the developed nanomaterials display a high reversible specific gravimetric capacity and volumetric capacity with outstanding rate capability and good cycling stability. Based on the results obtained in this project, 17 journal papers and one book chapter have been published in various high quality journals such as Advanced Materials, Energy & Environmental Science, Journal of the American Chemical Society, Advanced Functional Materials, Scientific Reports, Nanoscale, Journal of Materials Chemistry A, Chempluschem and Journal of Power Sources.

534910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
534910.value: The further development can be focused on the technology transfer and commercialization of research results obtained in this project. The research work can be extended by further development of real dye sensitized solar cells and full sized lithium ion batteries in collaboration with industry. We will try to apply ITF fund for the financial support of the further research activates.

534910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
534910.value: Development of the new materials and devices for energy conversion and storage has been an important issue in the research area of materials, in particular, the nano-materials and nano-technology. This project aims at investigating and developing new nano-structured materials for solar cells and lithium ion batteries. Through the project period, we have developed TiO2 nanotubes based dye sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) by the investigation of the photonic crystal effects aroused from anodization formed TiO2 photonic crystals. In addition to the study of the TiO2 nanotubes based DSSCs as energy conversion devices, our research was also extended to study energy materials for carbon based environmental friendly lithium-ion batteries as energy storages through the creations of the nanostructures on the various electrospun nanofibres. Based on the results obtained in this project, 17 journal papers and one book chapters have been published in various high quality and impact journals such as Advanced Materials, Energy & Environmental Science, Journal of the American Chemical Society, Advanced Functional Materials, Scientific Reports, Nanoscale, Journal of Materials Chemistry A, Chempluschem and Journal of Power Sources.

535010.value: 脉冲式多微射流控制的圆射流

535010.label: Project Objectives
535010.value: Explore further the developed active technique to control the mixing performance of a jet, using pulsed side minijets, specifically, (a) to identify the effects of different configurations such as different numbers and arrangements, each emulating a noncircular jet, of minijets on the control performance and downstream evolution of the main jet; (b) to characterize the dependence of jet mixing on individual control parameters, including the minijet pulsation frequency ratio to the dominant vortex frequency, and mass flow rate ratio to the main jet. Develop a closed-loop or adaptive control for selected configurations of minijets and determine (a) which is the best feedback signal, fluctuating velocities or a passive scalar or their combinations, (b) to what extent the closed-loop control can improve the effectiveness of jet mixing, as compared with the open-loop control as well as the absence of control. Gain a relatively thorough understanding of the flow physics, jet mixing and control mechanisms through measuring and analyzing how the flow (the flow structure, instabilities, turbulence scales, …) is altered under control, as compared with that in the absence of control or under a different control scheme, and connecting the alteration to the observed mixing performance.

535010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
535010.value: The manipulation and optimization of turbulent jet mixing has great potential benefits in various applications such as burners used in process industries, noise suppression, aero and automobile engines, water-jet machining, electronic equipment cooling, printing and drying, most of which are widely seen in the industries of Hong Kong. The next generation of devices to embrace such ability is expected to come from the active control of turbulent jet. Numerous past investigations, albeit with success to different degrees, have identified many issues that have yet to be resolved before a reliable technology emerges. A novel pulsed minijet device, characterized by a very high dynamic response, has been recently developed at PolyU. Preliminary investigation is very encouraging, demonstrating that actuation produced by this device could significantly alter the flow structure and accelerate the jet velocity decay rate by 50%, compared with continuous minijet actuation. Nevertheless, the frequency range over which the actuation is highly effective is found to be narrow. Furthermore, the flow physics and fundamental mechanisms behind the observation have yet to be better understood. This project is a continuation of this investigation, aiming at developing an active jet control technique based on fluidic means and understanding underlying mechanisms and flow physics under control. Specifically, (1) explore further this technique by carrying out a systematic experimental study to establish the controllability of the system, including investigating thoroughly control parameters such as the configuration (the number and geometric arrangement) of minijets, their frequency ratio to the dominant vortex frequency, mass flow rate ratio to the main jet, and blowing angle; (2) expand the existing open-loop control system to a closed-loop or adaptive control system in order to improve further the control performance; (3) conduct a relatively thorough study of the underlying flow physics (turbulence structures, instabilities, spatial correlations, timescales, …) and jet mixing mechanisms under control. The data obtained will also be used for validating and refining numerical simulation that is being conducted in parallel at Peking University. At the completion of the project, we could hopefully address many important issues or scientific questions in fluid mechanics, raised from previous investigations (including ours), and pave the way towards the emergence of a reliable jet-mixing-controllable technology. 射流控制在工程中有广泛的应用。下一代先进射流控制技术应来自射流的主动控制。以往的研究已提出众多的射流主动控制方法，并取得不同程度的成就，但仍有许多尚未解决的问题，因而阻碍了可靠的射流主动控制技术的出现。我们最近发展了一种新颖的、具有很高频响的脉冲式微射流产生器。初步研究表明，该装置产生的脉冲式微射流能有效地改变流动结构并加速射流速度衰减率达50%。不过，有效控制频率范围却很窄；此外，控制的流动机理尚待研究。本项目为该研究的继续，旨在发展基于微射流的射流主动控制技术，并弄清其控制机理。具体为：（1）通过一系列试验，进一步系统地探索脉冲式微射流控制技术；（2）将开环控制拓展到闭环控制，以近一步提高控制效果；（3）系统地研究有效控制下的流动机理，包括湍流结构、不稳定性、时间尺度、及射流混合机理等。

535010.label: Major findings and research outcome
535010.value: 1) The effects of the mass ratio on the control performance can be three types. Type I corresponds to very small mass ratio, and the perturbation excites the natural instability of jet, leading to significantly enhanced vortices, along with vortex pairing. The jet decay or entrainment rate is greatly modified and the control is highly effective. For Type III, the mass ratio is large and the two control jets penetrate deeply into the potential core and even clash with each other, resulting in the transition of laminar vortices to the turbulent in both planes. The jet decay rate increases and approaches an asymptotic state with increasing Cm, though the control may be less efficient than Type I. Type II is a transition between I and III, characterized by a medium mass ratio. 2) The jet decay rate depends strongly on the excitation frequency, showing one pronounced peak and one trough due to greatly enhanced and weakened vortices, respectively. 3) A closed-loop control is also developed and the optimal control performance can be achieved automatically, suggesting the robustness of the technique. A number of papers have been published, including one journal article, one book article. One conference paper out of this project has received The Best Student Paper Award in FSSIC2013. One PhD student working on this project is expected to graduate in 2014.

535010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
535010.value: The jet control technique investigated so far has been proved to be a great success. This work will be continued to examine more minijet configurations and to find an even better control efficiency. Future investigation will also be shifted to examine the mixing improvement in small scale sturbulence. Eventually, it is intended apply the developed technique for industrial applications.

535010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
535010.value: The manipulation of turbulent jet mixing has great potential benefits in various industrial applications. This work is an experimental investigation on the active control of a round air jet using one, two, three, four, five and six unsteady radial microjets. It has been noted that under the control of steady microjets (fe/f0 = 0) the jet centerline velocity decay rate K was first accelerated and then decelerated, after achieving the maximum at mass ratio Cm ≈ 12%, with increasing Cm. Once the steady microjets were replaced by the pulsed, the value of K exhibits a strong dependence on frequency ratio fe/f0, as expected, and another maximum occurs at very small mass ratio Cm = 0.8%. As a matter of fact, the K value was amplified by more than 80% given fe/f0 = 1 and Cm = 0.8%, as compared with the steady microjets of the same Cm, suggesting a significantly improved control efficiency. The flow physics and control mechanisms are also explored based on flow visualization and PIV measurements and are further compared with the natural jet and that under the control of steady microjets. A closed-loop control is also developed and the optimal control performance can be achieved automatically, suggesting the robustness of the technique.

541610.label: Project Objectives
541610.value: To develop and implement a rigorous and innovative survey methodology that integrates migrants and non-migrants in a common sample with equal probability of selection, and to develop panel data that are nationally representative of migration trends in Mainland China over the five-year period 2004-2009 at the societal level. To examine the changing patterns of migration from individual to family and from temporary to permanent; particularly, to document the dynamics of migration decisions of individuals and their families over the five-year period, and to understand the motivations behind the decisions at the individual level for both second-wave migrants and first-wave respondents who have out-migrated since 2004. To assess the degree of integration of migrants according to a range of indicators, including occupational status, family formation, children's education, health status, socio-psychological well-being, participation in urban community activities, and affective integration and long-term commitment to urban life, and to identify how county-level variations in social and economic situations condition individuals' migration experience, settlement pattern, and socio-psychological well-being.

541610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
541610.value: The scope and speed of the internal migration of over 200 million people now underway in China is unprecedented in human history. While the global economic crisis emerging in late 2008 temporarily drove 20 to 30 million migrants back to rural areas, the "migrant labor dearth" of 2004-2006 has re-emerged in September 2009 as this proposal is being drafted. In recent years, the government has introduced a number of initiatives designed to promote urbanization, to increase migrants' access to urban services, and to reduce discrimination against migrants. Comparative migration research generally documents that migrant integration into urban life follows a natural and predictable trend; China-specific studies often reveal policy and structural barriers that result in segregation or malintegration for rural to urban migrants. While we acknowledge the institutional legacy of the existing hukou and other policy constraints, this debate cannot be advanced without an unbiased sample to ascertain the impact of recent economic and policy changes on migrant integration into the various facets of urban life, and whether integration or segregation is the more dominant characteristic of the Chinese migration and urbanization process. We propose to conduct a longitudinal study with a second wave of a national survey of the general population (about 4,000 respondents) and a sub-sample follow-up survey of recent out-migrants (expected sample size about 400), that will detail the social, economic, and political behaviors of migrants and their families, and the ways in which they differ from both rural and urban non-migrants and their families over the five-year period 2004-2009. We will employ Spatial Probability Sampling, which integrates migrants and non-migrants in a common sample with equal probability of selection. Because our data are based on a sample of spaces, they are not biased by the attrition problems that plague existing panel studies at the societal level. The 2004 respondents who are re-interviewed in the 2009 national survey or in the sub-sample out-migrant follow-up survey will provide a basis for analyzing change in migration paths and experiences at the individual level. The study will offer a more comprehensive and sophisticated understanding of the changing patterns and dynamics of migration, the integration of migrants into urban life, and the effects of recent economic and policy changes on migration. It will yield rich material for analyzing the Chinese migration and urbanization process and will also make a valuable contribution to discussions of the existing hukou and other policy issues. 中國國內目前2億人口遷移的規模和速度是人類史無前例的。2008年底出現的全球經濟危機使得2-3千萬的農民工出現返鄉潮尚未明朗，2004-2006年出現的民工荒與2009年又現端倪。近年來，中國政府推出一系列的政策促進城市化的進程，挺高農民工享用城裏的服務，減少對外來人口的歧視。 比較移民研究通常認為移民融入城市生活是一個自然的、可預測的趨勢；中國研究則指出政策和結構的障礙會導致農民工與城市居民的隔離。一方面，我們承認即存的戶口和其他政策的制約；另一方面，我們也意識到，如果沒有一個無偏差的樣本來研究近年來經濟和政策的改變對農民工融入城市生活產生了怎樣的影響，到底整合還是隔離代表了中國人口遷移和城市化進程的趨勢，這樣的爭論是沒有意義的。 我們的研究計畫在2004年一個全國性調查的基礎上，在2009年進行一次跟蹤調查；同時，我們會對2004年和2009年樣本中的外出移民進行跟蹤，以詳細記錄其個人及家庭的社會、經濟、政治等行為，以及這些移民個人及家庭與非移民個人及家庭的差異。在抽樣方法上，我們使用空間概率抽樣法，將移民與非移民以等概率同時抽到研究樣本中。 這項研究會對理解中國人口遷移的模式與動態、移民融入城市生活，以及近年來經濟及政策變化的影響提供更為全面、深入的理解。這項研究的資料、資料對於分析中國移民及城市化的進程以及有關戶口及相關政策的爭論都有重要意義。

541610.label: Realisation of objectives
541610.value: To achieve the project objective #1, i.e., to develop panel data that are nationally representative of migration trends, the second wave of the national household survey Chinese Attitudes toward Inequality and Distributive Injustice was conducted in 2009—five years after the baseline survey in 2004. The survey employed spatial probability sampling technology to achieve a nationally representative sample (N = 2,866), which includes migrants as well as registered residents. In order to better examine the changing patterns of migration as described in the revised project objective #2 and to assess the degree of integration of migrants into urban life as described in the project objective #3, with support from RCCC, we managed to run another wave of national survey in 2011 but within the same primary sampling units (PSUs) in the 2009 national survey. One innovation we made in the 2011 survey was to use the Operational Linescan System nighttime light data provided by the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program to select our secondary sampling units (SSUs), so that we could sample all those people living in an urban area regardless of their hukou status and regardless if the area in which they lived had been official designated as urban. We chose a threshold of 30 at the pixel level to define the sample frame of physical areas deemed “urban” iteratively, which is pretty much in accordance with the definition of urban areas of national standards. From the 26 PSUs and 52 SSUs, spread over 19 provinces, 27 prefectures, and 31 counties or city districts, we sampled 1,906 households and successfully interviewed 1,288 individuals for a response rate of 67.6%. In order to identify how community-level variations condition individuals’ migration experience, settlement pattern, and socio-psychological well-being, as described in project objective #3, we also retrieved numerous provincial-, prefectural-, and county-level variables from local gazetteers, statistical yearbooks, and the 2000 census, and linked them to the survey data. Starting from January 2012, we have been focusing our time and energy on analyzing the multi-level data and writing a series of papers examining issues including the disparities in subjective exposure to environmental hazards and associated health outcomes, the differential experience and consequences of perceived institutional and interpersonal discrimination, and the effects of urbanization on physical and mental health, among others. As of November 2013, we have published five papers in academic journals, presented four papers at professional conferences, and have two manuscripts under review or revision.

541610.label: Major findings and research outcome
541610.value: Since January 2012, we have been focusing on analyzing the multi-level data and have completed a series of papers for conference presentations and journal publications. Our first paper, published in Social Science & Medicine in January 2013, investigates the disparities in subjective exposure to environmental hazards and associated health outcomes. We find that perceived environmental hazards are associated with county-level industrialization and economic development; rural-to-urban migrants are exposed to more water pollution and a higher measure of overall environmental hazard; and the negative effects of perceived environmental hazard on physical health are more detrimental for rural-to-urban migrants than for urban residents. Our second paper, published in Journal of Sociology & Social Welfare in March 2013, investigates the differential experience and consequences of perceived institutional and interpersonal discrimination among rural-to-urban migrants. The results indicate that rural-to-urban migrants perceive institutional discrimination more frequently than interpersonal discrimination; however, perceived interpersonal discrimination has a more detrimental effect than perceived institutional discrimination in the form of self-rated physical health and depressive distress. The third paper we worked on examines the prevalence of chronic conditions and receipt of treatment among urbanized rural residents. The results indicate that urbanized rural residents have similar number or prevalence of chronic conditions with urban residents, but they are less likely to receive treatment particularly for cardiovascular conditions. Urbanized rural residents are more anxious about their potential inability to cover medical expenses than both urban residents and rural-to-urban migrants. The paper appears in BioMed Research International in July 2013. With an innovative use of the nighttime light data from the DMSP-OLS, our fourth paper, forthcoming in China Quarterly, disentangles the process of urbanization and migration and their complex associations with health. We find that while higher absolute level of urbanization at the county level negatively impacted self-reported physical health, faster and accelerating urbanization had a positive impact which could be attributed to the demand-pull effect underlying the healthy migrant phenomenon. By contrast, all three dimensions of urbanization were associated with greater depressive distress and thus had an adverse effect on residents’ mental health. At present, we are revising/preparing two other manuscripts: one examines the neighborhood effects on mental health, and the other will look at urbanization, migration, and citizenship. In addition, the data we collected in the project have been/are being used to analyze the digital divide and e-commerce use (one paper published and one under review) and political trust in China (one paper in preparation).

541610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
541610.value: Our research highlights the importance of encompassing multi-level analyses in studying migration dynamics and migrant integration in the Chinese context. The project also yields rich material for analyzing issues associated with the process of rapid urbanization in China. Particularly, our innovative use of the nighttime light data from the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program Operational Linescan System (DMSP-OLS) demonstrates the huge variations in the urbanization process, which is still ongoing in China. Linking the nighttime light data with the surveys further illustrate more broadly the value of modeling locational parameters in analyses of individual outcomes based on national samples. While continuing to analyze the multi-level datasets and finishing the papers concerning migration dynamics and migrant integration we are currently working on, we also have plans to further look into various measures of urbanization, e.g., different industrial development models, rate of farmland conversion, changes in labor composition and population density, etc., and examine how these different measures of urbanization may affect the degree and process of not only rural-to-urban migrants’ but also in-situ urbanized rural residents’ integration into urban life.

541610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
541610.value: Studies of migration dynamics and migrant integration must encompass multi-level analyses within a longitudinal perspective if they are to provide a complete account. Using the multi-level datasets we constructed based on three national surveys conducted in 2004, 2009, and 2011 and provincial-, prefectural-, and county-level variables extracted from local gazetteers, statistical yearbooks, and the 2000 census, we have examined a number of issues concerning migration and urbanization in China, including: the disparities in subjective exposure to environmental hazards and associated health outcomes, the differential experience and consequences of perceived institutional and interpersonal discrimination, and the effects of urbanization on physical and mental health, among others. Our research highlights the importance of encompassing multi-level analyses in studying migration dynamics and migrant integration in the Chinese context. The project also yields rich material for analyzing issues associated with China’s rapid urbanization. The findings from these studies offer a more comprehensive and sophisticated understanding of the changing patterns and dynamics of migration, the integration of migrants into urban life, and the effects of socio-economic development on migrants’ well-being than previous studies. Based on the research results, we call for a more equitable social environment and equal distribution of resources and opportunities, particularly among the migrant population.
