541810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
541810.value: The primary aim of this research is to investigate whether organisational citizenship behaviours, in-role behaviours, employees’ empowerment and employees’ branding can influence customers’ perceived service quality. A hypothesised model is developed based on three interlinked literature strands that consider human resources management, brand management, and hospitality management. Three separate focus groups will be conducted to gather more information about the evaluation criteria of customers toward service quality in the hotel industry, information about employees’ branding strategies and the typical employees’ in-role, extra-role behaviours and employees’ empowerment found among hotel front line employees in Hong Kong and Mainland China hotels. The survey instruments will be developed based on the results of the focus groups and the previous literature. A cross-sectional survey design with self-administrated questionnaire survey for front office employees, front office supervisors or managers, and hotel guests was adopted to collect the data for this study. A set of relationships among employees’ behaviours, employees’ branding, empowerment and service quality will be examined by structural equation modelling. In addition, the study identified the dimensions of service quality, employees’ in-role behaviours, organizational citizenship behaviours, employees’ empowerment and employees’ branding through principle component factor analysis. The present study aims to make contribution towards a theory of employees’ branding and employees’ behaviours, which has been very limited. This study anticipates the notion that to achieve organisational effectiveness, organisation relies on branding employees, motivating employees’ in-role behaviours, stimulating employees’ extra-role behaviours, empowering employees and ultimately to enhance customers’ perception of quality. The results of the study provide insight into which hotel employee behaviours may directly enhance or cause customers to perceive service quality. To expand the industrial application of the model, a newly incorporated employees’ branding scorecard is design and implement to help hotel managers and employees to understand how performance can be align to branding objectives. The implementation of the scorecard ensures communication and continued learning. Furthermore, the findings could potentially help human resources managers to recruit, select, empower and train employees who can deliver better service to the customers. It gives the marketing manager a deeper understanding of what kind of behaviours needs to be reinforced in the process of branding hotel employees. Ultimately, it would encourage hotels to allocate their company’s resources to improve those critical elements in order to achieve the best results.

541810.label: Realisation of objectives
541810.value: The present study provides an in-depth examination of employees’ perception of brand internalization which can be developed as an employees' branding scorecard. The study identify the factors that affect the brand internalization process. Drawing on the findings of this study, a conceptual model and a measurement scale are developed for hotel brand internalization. The project objectives were successfully achieved in this study. The use of content analysis in this study identified five key themes that coincide with Berry and Parauraman’s (1991) definition of brand internalization. The findings provide evidences to the five steps that reflect brand internalization which are explaining the brand knowledge to employees; associating employees with the desired brand image; communicating the brand messages via various information channels; strengthening employees’ brand awareness; and also rewarding employees’ behavior which support brand delivery. The entire process starts from the first step of providing thorough explanation of the accurate and up-to-date brand knowledge to employees by branded hotels. Employees are likely to associate the acquired brand knowledge with their own belief, personality character, as well as the norms adopted within an organization to picture an image of the brand. Hence, the second step requires hotels to encourage employees to positively associate their understanding of the brand with the desired brand image. Furthermore, hotels attempted to reach employees’ minds in terms of internalizing the brand image by utilizing physical hardware and software to constantly remind employees of the hotel brand. This is the third step of strengthening the brand awareness. The fourth and final step is recognizing and acknowledging employees’ brand delivery performance. The power of rewarding the brand delivery would not only affirm employees’ commitment but also testify the performance of brand internalization process. The step of communicating the brand co-exists with all the four steps. It requires different channels to deliver brand information, to remind brand image, to create brand awareness, and to reward brand delivery. This step penetrates into the whole process and helps hotel brand internalization to take place. The model is the first attempt to describe the hotel brand internalization process, it contributes theoretically to the study of hotel internal branding. To practically utilize the concepts identified, items were constructed in a solid measurement scale in this study.

541810.label: Major findings and research outcome
541810.value: While branding used to be product oriented, there has now been an emerging focus on service as the service industry has become more prominent due to evolution and development. Customer service has been a common practice amongst hotel industries and brand equity could be enhanced by creating customer-based brand initiatives. Whilst attracting and retaining customers are important for a hotel’s success, it would be rather ineffective to only focus on external customers alone as they cannot receive a service or a product if internal customers are not able to deliver good service. Employees are now viewed as brand ambassadors, it is crucial that they internalize the brand in order to encourage the alignment of their actions with the brand promises. The purpose of this study therefore, seeks to explore the dimensions of service brand internalization through the perspectives of hotel employees. This is intended to be a valuable resource for managers and practitioners alike to further their understanding of the concept of internal branding and to improve on the effectiveness of employee branding in hotels. This study uses a qualitative and inductive approach to gain insights about the central theme of brand internalization through in-depth interviews among functional-level hotel employees working in international hotel brands and of different departments. The findings were presented in three dimensions along with several themes emerged after data coding in respect to the internal branding research objectives. They are dimensions of (1) Employee’s orientation of brand which includes brand definition, brand target, brand knowledge, brand choice and personality fit; (2) Influences of internal brand which includes guests, co-workers, management, training, and internal communication; and (3) Delivery of brand promise which includes empowerment, motivation, support systems, and work circumstances. Finally, the study also revealed the significant role of managers as leaders as they have ability to access to hotel resources and the power to initiate brand delivery, thus sought after by employees in guiding them to the direction that is aligned with the brand yet in such a way that does not overlook the concern and needs of employees. While engraining a brand vision into the minds of employees can reap the possibility for brand internalization to happen, the kind of initiative needs to be complimented with the right channels and the right receivers in order to ensure a better success. The contribution of this study lies in the suggestions on how to make brand internalisation works in an international hotel brands.

541810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
541810.value: This study revealed the significance of leaders’ role as they can initiate and facilitate changes to enable brand-supportive behavior. Leaders' attitude and behavior toward brand internalization have exemplary roles which correspondingly affect the attitude and behavior of the subordinates. Thus, it is to the best interests of hotels to explore if senior leadership participation and involvement would be consistent and effective throughout the five steps of the brand internalization process proposed in model of this study. Last but not the least, empowerment, training, recognition and rewards factors have been suggested to motivate employees to be committed to their work along with actions to support the desired brand. However, to what extent should empowerment engage in the brand internalization process? In addition, how should recognition and reward be addressed to employees so to make a difference to their willingness to adopt brand internalization? Finally, based on the study implications to managers lead to generating useful research topics to investigate the field of brand internalization to offer profound theoretical foundation and useful practical solutions.

541810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
541810.value: The present study contributed to the literature to explore the brand internalisation process and the development of branding scorecard. The study confirmed that to achieve organisational effectiveness, organisation relies on branding employees. The findings from this study offer an insight of brand internalization from hotel employees’ perspective. By analyzing, consolidating and integrating the qualitative evidences from the interviews, it is evident to create a clear concept of hotel brand internalization and its components. The findings could help human resources manager to recruit, select,empower and train employees who can deliver better service to the customers. It provided the marketing managers with a deeper understanding of what kind of behaviours needs to be reinforced in the process of branding hotel employees. Ultimately, it would encourage hotels to allocate their companies' resources to improe those critical elements in order to achieve the best results.

542010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
542010.value: 資訊不對稱情形下含多個風險厭惡型零售商的供應鏈協調:理論研究與行為學實驗

542010.label: Project Objectives
542010.value: To explore analytically the format of the incentive alignment contracts and conditions under which a supply chain with a single supplier and multiple risk averse retailers under information asymmetry can be coordinated. To generate insights on how to set the contract parameters in a decentralized manner so that not only the supply chain’s expected profit is maximized, but also the supplier’s utility is maximized. To analytically study: (i) the value of the proposed contracts (under information asymmetry) by comparing the case under coordination with a benchmarking case under a pure wholesale pricing contract, and (ii) the value of perfect information when the retailers share faithfully relevant information with the supplier for setting the supply chain contracts. To explore the issue of whether the retailers have incentives to provide fake private information to the supplier. If so, develop measures for the supplier to avoid this kind of cheating action from happening. To conduct a series of controlled experiments with human subjects to investigate whether the analytical model makes reasonable predictions of rational human behaviors and generates useful insights. To extend the findings by exploring the challenging cases with a higher degree of information asymmetry, heterogeneous retailers, and price-dependent demand functions.

542010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
542010.value: Channel coordination is a core subject of supply chain management. Over the past decade, much research effort has been devoted to exploring the detailed mechanisms (such as incentive alignment schemes) of achieving coordination and many analytical results have been obtained. However, there are two issues under explored: (i) developing a coordination scheme that can achieve coordination for a supply chain with multiple risk averse retailers under information asymmetry, and (ii) obtaining behavioral evidence to support actual application of the proposed mechanisms. In view of this, we propose to conduct both analytical and behavioral studies for a two-echelon information-asymmetric supply chain with a single supplier and multiple risk averse retailers. We use the mean-downside risk approach to model the objectives of the risk averse retailers in which each retailer aims at minimizing the downside risk measure subject to a constraint on achieving an expected profit target threshold. Under information asymmetry, the supplier does not know some important parameter(s) of the retailers (e.g., the profit target threshold or the cost structure). We first study the problem analytically as a Stackelberg game and establish the conditions for equilibrium. We will propose a menu of contracts to help achieve supply chain coordination, as well as maximizing the supplier’s own benefit under information asymmetry. We will develop the expected value of the coordinating menu of contracts, the expected value of perfect information, and other analytical insights. We will explore the issue of whether the retailers have incentives to provide fake information to the supplier. After that, following the behavioral operations literature, we will conduct a sequence of controlled experiments with human subjects to investigate whether the analytical model makes reasonable predictions of rational human behaviors. This will provide behavioral evidence and generate important additional insights. We will also consider several important and challenging extensions, which include exploring the cases with a larger degree of information asymmetry, heterogeneous retailers, and price-dependent demand functions. We believe that this project will not only contribute substantially to the supply chain coordination literature but will also generate useful managerial insights with real-world relevance. 管道協調是供應鏈管理中的核心問題之一。過去十多年來,已有大量研究來探討如何通過一些具體的合作協調機制(例如激勵聯盟計畫)達到協調,並且取得了很多理論成果。然而,該領域有兩個重要問題有待研究: (i) 在資訊不對稱且含有多個風險厭惡型零售商的供應鏈中,構建協調機制達到供應鏈協調; (ii) 通過行為學實驗獲取證據,使所得理論研究成果能夠切實應用於實際管理。有鑑於此,本課題擬對由一位供應商和多位風險厭惡型零售商組成的資訊不對稱的二級供應鏈,進行理論分析和行為學研究。本課題將採用均值—下方風險方法建立風險厭惡型零售商的決策模型,即每位零售商在期望收益目標值的約束下,使得自己的下方風險最小。在資訊不對稱情形下,供應商不知道零售商的某些重要參數(例如收益目標值)。本課題擬通過建立Stackelberg 博弈模型分析該問題,得出均衡解的存在條件,並將給出一個功能表合同,在資訊不對稱情形下最大化供應商利潤的同時,使得供應鏈達到協調。我們還將給出該功能表合同下的期望值,完美資訊下的期望值,以及其它管理啟示。同時,我們將研究零售商是否會有動機給供應商提供錯誤資訊。在此基礎上,本課題將利用行為運作管理的相關研究成果,設計一系列的行為學實驗,來探討所得理論結果能否對理性人的行為進行合理預測。這些實驗結果將為我們的理論分析結果提供行為學上的支援,並產生一些重要的管理啟示。本課題還將就其他幾個重要的富有挑戰性的情形進行深入研究,包括資訊不對稱程度加劇的情形,零售商類別不同的情形,以及需求函數依賴于價格的情形。我們相信,本課題不僅會對供應鏈協調理論的發展產生實質性推動作用,而且對現實管理工作有十分重要的參考價值。

542010.label: Realisation of objectives
542010.value: We basically achieved all the objectives. To be specific, we conducted both analytical and human-subjects based behavioral research on the topic and derived many important results and insights. Some concise details are listed below. For the main objectives of achieving coordination with multiple risk averse retailers under information asymmetry, we analytically studied the topic and also conducted human subjects based behavioral experiments. We published 6 related papers in leading citation journals such as Annals of Operations Research, IEEE Transactions, and Omega; owing to the long review time by many journals, three more papers are still currently under journal review (either the 2nd round or the 3rd round) by European Journal of Operational Research, IEEE Transactions, and Naval Research Logistics. We also (i) published one authored book on Risk Analysis in Stochastic Supply Chains (by Springer's OR/MS series), (ii) organized one related special issue in the journal "Production and Operations Management", and (iii) presented some research results in an international conference.

542010.label: Major findings and research outcome
542010.value: The major findings and research outcome of this project’s findings are listed as follows: First, on analytical research: We investigated the supply chain coordination challenges with (i) multiple risk averse retailers, (ii) information asymmetry, and (iii) risk-averse supplier. We focused our attention on several areas: (1) The channel coordination mechanisms which involve the use of innovative formats of contracts; (2) The real world practice based supply chain coordination problems with the consideration of markdown money; (3) Coordination challenges with some relatively new issues such as carbon tax, and interest rate. Second, on behavioral research: We conducted experiments with human subjects and derived a few important results on how behavioral factors affect supply chain coordination. Two papers were published in which the first paper explicitly revealed that there’re three kinds of human decision makers (playing the role of the supplier) in supply contracting with two heterogeneously risk averse retailers under information asymmetry, and their respective performances were explored and compared. The second paper reported how the self-serving fairness concern (called the minimum profit share ratio (MPSR)) would affect human decision making in supply contract setting with markdown contracts. We found that the presence of MPSR concern would lead to a higher level of supply chain risk. We also observed from the analysis that the supply chain would perform the best when the retailer tends to split the supply chain profit equally with the supplier. Supported by this project, we already published six papers in well-established citation journals such as Annals of Operations Research, IEEE Transactions, and Omega. We also have three more papers under review (either the 2nd round or the 3rd round) by European Journal of Operational Research, IEEE Transactions, and Naval Research Logistics. In addition, we published one book entitled Risk Analysis in Stochastic Supply Chains: A Mean-Risk Approach, Springer, International Series in Operations Research and Management Science. In this book, the mean-risk models are employed to study supply chain problems, including coordination challenges with risk averse agents (Chapter 4). Many discussions of research challenges related to supply chain coordination with risk averse agents under information asymmetry are also presented (Chapter 5). Last but not least, inspired by the multi-methodological study conducted in this project, I have worked with Professor Xiande Zhao and my Co-I Professor T.C.E. Cheng to organize a special issue on Multi-Methodological Research in Production and Operations Management for the journal "Production and Operations Management (POM)". I am the guest department editor and this special issue will be completed by this summer. As a remark, a part of the funding was used to support a PhD student who needed to extend her PhD study duration. This student also helped with the behavioral experiments and was a co-author of one published paper (included in this completion report).

542010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
542010.value: Owing to time limitation, three important papers supported by this project are still under journal review. Thus, we plan to work hard and get them published as soon as possible. Furthermore, more behavioral studies on supply chain coordination can be conducted in the future. For example, we can consider the multiple suppliers multiple retailers supply contracting challenges in which competition and gaming issues would be examined.

542010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
542010.value: Channel coordination is a core subject of modern supply chain management. However, little is known about how to coordinate the supply chain with risk-averse retailers under information asymmetry and how human behaviours would affect the respective coordination mechanism and performance. Based on the existing literature and motivated by the research gaps highlighted above, this project focuses on investigating the corresponding supply chain coordination challenges via analytical and behavioral approaches. This project has generated many important academic and managerial insights. We believe that the findings derived from the analyses not only contribute substantially to the literature but they also help advance our knowledge in how human behavioral factors would affect supply chain coordination mechanism in the real world.

542110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
542110.value: 《明儒學案》整理與明代儒學研究的文本基礎重建

542110.label: Project Objectives
542110.value: To rebuild a dependable textual basis for disinterested research on Confucian learning and intellectual history of Ming China by producing a learned edition of the indispensable source book by Huang Zongxi, the MINGRU XUEAN. To investigate the ways and rationales of textual exploitation and manipulation in the production of source books for philosophical and doctrinal considerations in the sixteenth and seventeenth-century world of Confucian learning, and to compile a volume of recent studies that throw lights on these problems, in particular those reflecting Huang Zongxi's scholarship in the MINGRU XUEAN. To produce a manual for doing textual research on the study of late imperial Chinese thought and intellectual history drawing on the research for the new edition of the MINGRU XUEAN. To train a number of postgraduate students who can do advanced-level textual research for historical and philosophical inquiry and to produce an annotated reader of the MINGRU XUEAN for the general reader, which features the life and thought of eminent Confucians in the Ming.

542110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
542110.value: • 本研究計劃分析及比較包括黃宗羲《明儒學案》在內的五種晚明及清初（約公元1567-1700年間）成書的儒學資料彙編的編纂構思、文字來源以及文本問題，藉以審視儒學資料彙編的編纂原理，明代的思想趨勢，晚明及清初編纂此類書籍的儒者所處理的問題，以及各種成書如何創造其所載儒者的形象，編纂者如何透過編輯操作利用這些儒者被節錄的文字以闡揚編者自己的主張，由此而為瞭解明代及清初的思想世界帶來新知。 • 為求重建客觀研究明代思想及思想文化史的可靠文本基礎，本計劃尤其針對主要資料彙編《明儒學案》的文本作深入細緻的研究，包括以黃宗羲著書時所用的文獻原本校勘此書刊本所見的抄錄文字，且為緣於文字訛誤、字句曲解、傳記訊息不足等原因的問題提出校正和解釋。 • 計劃的預期成果包括（一）製作一本可供研究之用的全新點校本《明儒學案》，（二）製作一本載錄此項研究的研究筆記以及據之講述研究中國近世儒學及其歷史之道的研究手冊，（三）編纂一冊近年研究儒學資料彙編及其編者之學術思想的論文集，以及（四）製作一本能夠反映重要明儒生平學行和思想要旨的《明儒學案》選注本。 • 本計劃同時會訓練從事中國近世歷史與哲學研究的研究生。

542610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
542610.value: An important consequence of the global spread of English in the past four hundred years has been the emergence of a diverse range of nativised varieties of the language in post-colonial societies in Asia and Africa. In the past twenty-five years, these ‘new’ Englishes have been the focus of considerable research and debate in the emerging discipline of World Englishes. Given the numerical ascendancy of Asian users in the Anglophone world, it is perhaps not surprising that much of this scholarly interest has centred on Asian varieties of English, such as those which have evolved in India, the Philippines and Singapore. The proposed study seeks to make a unique contribution to this rapidly developing field by tracing the evolution of English in Hong Kong since the early 1840s. In particular, it seeks to investigate, evaluate and refine Schneider’s (2007) important and much-discussed new theoretical framework, the ‘Dynamic Model’, in the Hong Kong context. Schneider proposes that post-colonial Englishes have evolved by undergoing a single underlying process which can be described as a diachronic sequence of five progressive stages: foundation, exonormative stabilisation, nativisation, endonormative stabilisation and differentiation. Each stage in the evolutionary cycle is characterised by a specific and mutually dependent set of ecological and linguistic factors, which Schneider groups under four headings: extralinguistic background, identity constructions, sociolinguistic conditions and linguistic consequences. At each stage of the process, these four ‘parameters’ are viewed from two perspectives: those of the indigenous population and those of the English-speaking settlers. The objective of the proposed study is to identify the stages in the evolution of English in Hong Kong since the mid-nineteenth century using hitherto unexploited textual data from English-language newspaper archives, Legislative Council proceedings, government records and other printed primary sources. The study builds on ideas presented in a recent article which traces the evolution of the English-language speech community in Hong Kong (Evans, in press). This exploratory article raised doubts as to the applicability of the Dynamic Model to post-colonial societies like Hong Kong which have traditionally attracted few English-speaking settlers. The proposed study will develop a new model to account for the evolution of English in such societies. The study will yield valuable information and insights about a range of issues relating to the nature, acquisition and use of English in colonial and post-colonial Hong Kong and, more generally, will make a significant contribution to theories of language variation and change. 過往四百多年，英語在世界各地的普及化引申出一個很重要的現象，就是在非洲和亞洲後殖民社會裡，湧現一系列經本土化而生的英語。在過往二十五年裡，這些‘新’英語已成為世界英語這個不斷成長的學科裡廣為研究和討論的科題。有鑑於英語世界裡，能使用英語的亞洲人不斷飆升，不難理解，學者們的研究興趣相信早已投放在亞洲例如印度、菲律賓及星加坡等地區的語種上。本研究擬議探討自1840年起，英語在香港的演變，冀能在這個快速成長的研究領域作出貢獻。特別是，本研究致力於探討、檢視及重新定義施耐德(2007)那廣為討論，以香港為處境的湛新重要理論性著述《動態模式》。施耐德提出，不同的後殖民地英語是由一個單一基本發展過程演化成的，是一個縱向及歷時的過程，可以用五個漸進程序概述：奠基期、外規範標準期、本土化期、內規範標準期、和區分期。每個演進期均可以識別出一些特別和相互依靠的語言和生態條件。跟據施耐德，這些條件可以四個標題歸類：語言以外的背境、身份的建構、社會語言的條件、和語言的後果。在每個演進期，以上的四個條件均以兩個層面檢視：原住民的、和以英語為母語之外來定居者的。本研究的目標是通過參考來自迄今尚未予以探討過的英文報刊資料庫存檔、立法局會議過程紀錄、政府紀錄存檔、和其他已赴印的第一身資料，識別出自十九世紀中至今，英語在香港演化的各階段。研究建基於近期一份跟進香港說英語之群體的演進過程的文章(伊文斯，赴印中)。該份探討性文章就《動態模式》在後殖民社區裡例如香港的適用性作出質疑；傳統上，對以英語為母語之外來定居者來說，這些社區的吸引力已今非昔比。本研究將會提出一個新的建構以表述英語在這些社區裡的演化。研究將會就英語在殖民和後殖民的香港裡的本質、掌控和使用等不同範籌提出寶貴信息和卓見。宏觀地，研究亦將會在語言變化和演進等理論上作出重要貢獻。

542610.label: Realisation of objectives
542610.value: The objectives were accomplished by collecting, analysing and synthesising substantial sets of diachronic and synchronic data, which offer complementary perspectives on the evolutionary dynamics of Hong Kong English. These datasets include (1) a 91-million-word corpus of Legislative Council proceedings (1858-2012), which has been used to track changing patterns of language choice in the chamber between 1972 (when the use of Cantonese was first permitted) and 2012, and to trace the evolution of the Hong Kong English lexicon since the 1850s; (2) a corpus of English-language newspapers (1845-2010), which has been used to track the emergence of Hong Kong’s English-using community via an analysis of the authorship of letters to the editor; (3) a database of jury lists (1855-2011), which has also provided important information about the emergence of the English-using community; (4) census and by-census reports (1841-2011), which have been studied to track the ethnic composition of Hong Kong society and patterns of language use; and (5) unpublished primary sources such as memoirs and reminiscences, which provide valuable linguistic, attitudinal and demographic information relevant to the study’s objectives and have been used to illuminate the other sets of data. A large number of secondary sources have also been consulted. The project’s objectives have been addressed in the various publications and presentations recorded in Part C and will be covered in a forthcoming monograph. Given the space/time considerations in journal/conference papers these outputs typically deal with one or two of the objectives, e.g. the articles on the lexicon focus on parameter 4 in the framework. The output in which all four objectives are addressed is the article entitled ‘The evolutionary dynamics of postcolonial Englishes: A Hong Kong case study’ (Journal of Sociolinguistics). This article draws on every set of data collected and analysed in the course of the project and thus offers the reader an overview of the entire investigation. One weakness of the project is that it has failed to yield a satisfactory model for the Outer Circle generally as opposed to Hong Kong. The experience of this project suggests that the reductionism essential to the development of such models is not particularly illuminating and, in any case, the globalisation of English in the past 20 years renders the task of developing a model solely for the Outer Circle virtually impossible. Several of the papers address this issue, notably the key output in the Journal of Sociolinguistics.

542610.label: Major findings and research outcome
542610.value: In terms of scale and scope, this is one of the most substantial studies of the evolution of English in the Outer Circle. The study has not only examined the various facets of Schneider’s (2007) influential Dynamic Model in the Hong Kong context, but has also entailed the collection and analysis of several sets of diachronic data (e.g. relating to the branches of government) which could be used to underpin and illuminate publications in disciplines such as colonial history, public administration and law. Since this study was framed by the Dynamic Model, I understandably targeted journals in areas that are relevant to Model’s parameters, such as world Englishes, sociolinguistics and applied linguistics rather than journals in non-language-related disciplines. In addition to the published and in-press articles, I am currently writing a monograph for Palgrave Macmillan based largely on the findings from the project. This book, which is entitled The English Language in Hong Kong: Diachronic and Synchronic Perspectives, can be regarded as the major outcome of the project. In terms of the journal-based outputs, the 13,700-word lead article in the Journal of Sociolinguistics is the most significant publication, because it is the first attempt to test the Dynamic Model empirically and comprehensively. The article examines all four parameters and draws on evidence from every strand of the investigation, namely, corpora of Legislative Council proceedings and English-language newspapers (including advertisements), census reports, jury lists together with material from private papers, government reports and Colonial Office correspondence. As some of these sets of diachronic data are quantifiable and thus amenable to trend-based analyses, it has been possible to demarcate distinct phases in the use of English in Hong Kong society and the evolution of its community of users. The study has generated a number of presentations at international conferences in Hong Kong and overseas as well as invited talks for the Hong Kong Association of Applied Linguistics (HAAL) and the government’s Official Languages Division. The study’s methods and findings have also been presented and discussed in a range of undergraduate and postgraduate subjects and seminars for research students at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, including English as a Global Lingua Franca (BA), English as an International Language (MA) and Language in Society (Professional Doctorate). The study has also stimulated further questions and issues, which I hope to address in subsequent projects using the rich and varied datasets already collected.

542610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
542610.value: Although this study has focused on the various aspects of Schneider’s framework, as already noted, it has led to the collection of substantial sets of data which can be exploited for other research purposes, including ones not directly related to language studies. One possible direction for future research could be within the relatively new field of the ‘British world’. I believe that the present study provides the basis for a project on the British community in Hong Kong (1842-1940). However, a more likely area for further development would be within the broad field of language studies, particularly in the area of lexicography. Two of the publications generated by the project offer historical perspectives on the lexicon of Hong Kong English. At a recent conference at Oxford University, editors working for the Oxford English Dictionary expressed interest in my research and, recognising the lack of diachronic research on Outer Circle English lexicons, indicated that they would be interested in collaborating with me in future projects in this area. I will be on sabbatical leave at Oxford in 2015 and have arranged to meet the editors to share the results of my lexicographic work and discuss possible directions for future collaborative research.

542610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
542610.value: In the past four decades a range of models have been devised to describe the diverse uses and users of English worldwide and the various processes by which the language has attained its status as the global lingua franca. This project has explored the one of these frameworks: Schneider’s (2007) Dynamic Model, which is the most coherent theory to account for the evolution of postcolonial Englishes. Although the Dynamic Model has been widely discussed and largely accepted by scholars, prior to the present study, it had not been validated by evidence from historical research. This project sought to bridge this gap within the context of Hong Kong by collecting, analysing and synthesising a range of diachronic data, including corpora of Legislative Council proceedings (1858–2012) and English-language newspapers (1845–2010), government census reports (1841– 2011); jury lists from government archives (1855–2011); and miscellaneous accounts of life in colonial Hong Kong, government reports and confidential Colonial Office correspondence. Evidence from these sources was used to depict trends in each of the Dynamic Model’s four parameters. These trends offer an empirically-grounded perspective on the evolutionary dynamics of Hong Kong English between 1842 and 2012.

543210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
543210.value: Nowadays, many public health care systems are suffering from considerable congestion. When more resources are finally allocated into such service systems to create additional capacities, decision makers usually face such a dilemma: should this additional capacity be used to offer the same service by charging a user fee (i.e. creating a two-tier system) or should this additional capacity be simply used to expand the current free service capacity. In this project, we plan to take a comparison study of the two systems, through both a modeling and an empirical approach. Firstly, we plan to build a stylish queueing model and study the optimal price in the two-tier health care system. Based on that, we can then derive the performance measures such as average waiting time. Secondly, we plan to conduct a comparison study of the performance measures for the two systems and find the sufficient condition for the two-tier system to be better than one single free service system. At last, we plan to collect relative data on the two types of health care systems and provide empirical findings. The essential goal of this project is to find a way to maximize the social welfare so that more people can enjoy fast, free, and high quality of health care service. The findings of this project will be insightful for the academic researchers and very helpful for the designers and managers in the health care systems. 世界上很多国家的公立免费医疗系统多处在资金和设施缺乏的窘境。当资金终于被政府拨下来后，医疗系统可能面临两难选择：要么扩大目前免费系统产能；要么建立一个收费系统从而创收，进而资助免费系统。本研究运用排队论和实证分析来比较研究这两种方案，分析各自的优缺点。此研究的终极目标是找到可行的方案来实现社会福利最大化，以便人们用最少的费用享受效用最大的医疗服务。

The pricing decision in such two-tier service system turns out to be very interesting and the results have been published on the prestigious academic journal M&SOM in 2013.

543210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
543210.value: Different countries adopt different health care systems. Countries like Canada mainly adopt pure public ones while countries like the USA adopt private ones. Hong Kong adopt a two-tier system (a hybrid of public and private ones). Through building a queueing system mode, I have identified that two-tier system actually has multiple advantages over pure ones. However, I found that due to customers' self-choice behavior between public and private system, the decision maker shall be very cautious on making pricing decision of the private system as the demand is very sensitive to that. The second main conclusion is that the public capacity is very essential for the self-financing private system. A larger public capacity may make the private system more difficult to survive. Hence when governments consider expanding public system capacity, they shall also consider either to subsidize patients to use private system or directly subsidize private systems.

543310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
543310.value: While organizational investments in complex information systems (IS) have reached a record high, more than half of these initiatives have experienced failure of differing magnitudes. Moreover, once systems progress to the post-acceptance stage, employees rarely use the technologies to their fullest potential, preventing organizations from realizing the promised return. This underachievement is attributable to the underutilization of implemented systems. This proposal aims to address this significant issue by simultaneously investigating the following three major post-acceptance usage behaviors: routine use (RTN), extended use (EXT), and innovative use (INV). In this study, routine use describes users’ utilizing IS in a standardized manner that is consistent with normal work processes. Extended use refers to users’ utilizing more of the available IS functions to support their tasks. Innovative use refers to users’ finding new ways of applying IS to enhance their performance. We conceive RTN, EXT, and INV, in relation to one another, as behaviors with minimum, moderate, and maximum levels of innovativeness and learning, respectively. As such, we postulate that these behaviors will differentially impact users’ job performance. Drawing on motivation theory, we identify extrinsic motivation (EM) and intrinsic motivation (IM) as the antecedents of the three post-acceptance behaviors. Importantly, we propose tri-dimensional intrinsic motivation (3DIM) toward using IS as a richer conceptualization of users’ intrinsic motivation for IS use than the conceptualizations of intrinsic motivations in prior literature. We further theorize the differential effects of EM and 3DIM on post-acceptance behaviors that represent different levels of innovativeness and learning. To test the research framework, we plan to collect data from knowledge workers who use business intelligence systems (BIS) at two retail, two telecom service, and two financial service firms located in China, Hong Kong, and the United States. We have obtained the endorsement from these firms for data access. Having been granted access to multiple data sources by these firms’ top management, we plan to employ a longitudinal, multi-source, and multi-firm research design. In terms of contributions, we expect to develop a richer conceptualization with regard to both post-acceptance usage behaviors and intrinsic motivation toward using IS. In addition, we will theoretically formulate and empirically examine the three post-acceptance behaviors’ differential impacts on job performance and the relative roles of EM and 3DIM in influencing the three post-acceptance behaviors. We also expect to develop insights for managers to formulate effective interventions that will enable organizations to improve their utilization of implemented systems. 儘管現代組織在資訊系統上的投資不斷的上升，超過一半以上的這類投資經歷了不同程度的失敗。再者，一旦到達”採納後階段”，員工很少能充分的使用資訊系統進而實現該系統所能帶來的潛在利益。 為解決此問題，本提案準備同時研究以下三種採納後的系統使用行為，分別為: 例行使用，拓展使用，與創新使用。例行使用描述使用者標準化的使用系統於日常工作中，拓展使用指使用者更廣泛的使用系統中已有的功能以支持其工作，創新使用則是指使用者找尋新穎的使用方法來增進其績效。 概念上，我們分別視例行使用，拓展使用，與創新使用為最小，中等，及最高程度的創新與學習行為。我們並假設此三種使用行為會對使用者的工作績效帶來不同程度的影響。同時，根據動機理論，我們認定外在使用動機與內在使用動機為此三種行為的重要動機因子。為補充以前文獻對資訊系統內在使用動機的不足，我們提出"三維內在使用動機"的概念。我們更進一步的推論外在使用動機與三維內在使用動機會差異化的影響以上三種採納後使用行為。 為測試所提出的研究模型，我們規畫了一個長期跨組織的研究設計。我們計畫分別從位於中國、香港、與美國的兩間零售商、兩間電信服務公司、及兩間財務服務公司的商業智能資訊系統使用者進行蒐集數據。 關於理論上的貢獻，我們期待對"採納後使用行為"以及"資訊系統內在使用動機"進行更豐富的概念化。再者，我們會理論化的推導並實證的測試外在使用動機與三維內在使用動機如何不同的影響三種採納後使用行為，以及這三種使用行為如何差異化的影響使用者的績效。實踐上，我們也期待提出深入的見解以期幫助管理者更有效利用組織中已經實施的資訊系統。

543310.label: Realisation of objectives
543310.value: We have achieved the project objectives to different extents. The findings of this project has deepened our understanding about post-acceptance IT usage behaviors (Output 1), the impacts of technology use at the post-acceptance stage (Outputs 2), the three-dimensional intrinsic motivations toward technology use (Output 1), and the differential influences of different types of motivations on post-acceptance usage behaviors (Output 1). Note that for Objective 1, only 80% was accomplished: although we included all three post-acceptance behaviors in the original manuscript submitted to Information Systems Research, extended use was removed in order to address reviewers’ concerns. Similarly for Objective 2, only 80% was achieved because of we had to modify the manuscript in order to move the paper forward in the review process. We have integrated multiple theoretical lenses – learning theory, innovation theory, motivation theory (Output 1), and economic theory (Output 2) – to attain the research objectives. We have collected multiple data sets to empirically verify the proposed models and hypotheses. Our research findings have informed several research frameworks that can be used by future studies to further investigate post-acceptance IS use from various perspectives.

543310.label: Major findings and research outcome
543310.value: Research Outcomes: Our research project has led to 2 research articles published at major international journals. Major Findings and Research Outcomes: We illustrate our major research findings specific to the questions we proposed to address. Our results show that employees in organizations engage in different types of technology usage behaviors in the post-acceptance stage (Output 1). These post-acceptance usage behaviors are driven by extrinsic motivation and three types of intrinsic motivations toward technology use, including intrinsic motivation toward accomplishment, intrinsic motivation to know, and intrinsic motivation to experience stimulation (Output 1). We also found that these three intrinsic motivations together with extrinsic motivation toward technology use exert differentially impact on distinct types of post-acceptance usage behaviors (Output 1) and that these motivational impacts are contingent upon individual orientation toward technology innovations (Output 1). Our results further show that employees’ voluntary technology use at the post-acceptance stage positively impacts their satisfaction with the implemented technology (user satisfaction) and, more importantly, this positive effect illustrates a diminishing pattern such that system use has less impact on user satisfaction when the system is used more frequently (Output 2).

543310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
543310.value: The post-acceptance stage is an emerging research context that only attracts scholarly attention recently. While this project is one of the first few that pay particular attention to usage behaviors at this stage and has arrived fruitful findings, there are various types of post-acceptance usage behaviors, such as infusion use, customized use, and so on that deserve further scholarly attention. We plan to investigate more variety of post-acceptance usage behaviors to deepen our knowledge for how to further leverage the implemented IS to a fuller extent, thereby extracting more value from such technology investment. Moreover, we plan to examine our research frameworks in other technological, organizational, and cultural contexts to further gauge the generalizability of our findings. When doing so, we will also incorporate the factors that are specific to the investigative contexts in order to achieve a more holistic and nuanced understanding of post-acceptance IS usage behaviors. Finally, although we have shown that IT usage at the post-acceptance stage can generate downstream impact, it is unclear if different types of post-acceptance usage behaviors exert similar or different performance impacts. More research is needed in order to deepen our knowledge in this regard.

543310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
543310.value: Organizations are increasing their investments in sophisticated information systems (IS) to support knowledge workers' work and performance. Unfortunately, while some knowledge workers use the implemented IS in a novel manner and to its fullest potential, most of them only apply the systems in a routine and superficial manner, thereby preventing organizations from realizing the often touted benefits from IS. To address this issue, this study examines why and how knowledge workers use implemented IS differently in the post-acceptance stage and the ensuing impacts. The findings of this research project suggest that while extrinsic motivations for work efficiency and effectiveness drive users' routine use of IS, intrinsic motivations for growth and enjoyment stimulate their innovative use of IS. Moreover, the effect of intrinsic motivations on innovative IS use is stronger/weaker for those who are more/less innovative toward IT innovations. Finally, the results show that knowledge workers’ voluntary IS use at the post-acceptance stage lead to their satisfaction with the implemented IS and this positive effect diminishes when the system is used more frequently.

543810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
543810.value: 雖然原始的情緒表達可能是人類的生存本能，但是我們要能在這高度複雜的社會中獲致成功，卻往往取決於我們如何駕馭自身的情緒以及應對某些特定狀況下的情緒反應。這是Roger Martin的新書 ‘Design of Business: Why Design Thinking the Next Competitive Advantage.’ 的重要前提之一。藉由介紹設計想法，Martin納入了幾項技巧，可用於察覺他人想法以及化解商場上不可或缺的競爭心態。這些設計者所想的方法和情緒乃是息息相關的，每一項設計的目標在於喚起特定的某幾種情緒用以取代其他的情緒。因此，不足為奇的是，2009.08.23的紐約時報的科技章節曾以整頁篇幅報導了有關「情感資訊自動抽取」的發展與應用。透過幾個成功案例的說明，紐約時報揭露了一個事實：情感分析技術已引起了商業界的興趣，而且這方面的興趣在持續增長，尤其是線上資訊擷取應用方面。有幾家公司，例如，Scout Labs、Jodange 和 Newssift，甚至已經提供了此種類型的服務。此外，在商業搜索方面，情感分析不僅影響了特定的領域（例如，電子商務）的搜索市場，而且也開始漸漸影響了大眾搜尋市場。 然而，在情緒計算語言學理論方面，這個領域卻未有應有的積極發展。目前，情感分析已經能夠成功地透過上下文來鑑別文本表達的正面或負面情感，但是這樣的分析並不能可靠地鑑別出諸如生氣、害怕與快樂這樣的特定情緒。同時，目前還比較缺乏一個完善的語言學理論用以指導預測言語表達中的情緒。最關鍵的問題是現有的理論無法將情緒與引發情緒的事件關聯起來。 此計畫書的目標在於提出一個能從句子上下文的語言線索出發預測情緒（emotions）與事件（events）兩者相依性的理論。首先，本研究將給出一個形式理論的表示方法; 然後用該方法開發一個大規模蘊含豐富資訊註解的語料庫（corpus）。最終，該語料庫將應用於檢驗某一質性平台，同時用於構建一個自動識別並分類文句中的情緒與事件類別的隨機模型（stochastic model）。

543810.label: Major findings and research outcome
543810.value: The main findings of the project were presented as a keynote speech (Huang 2013) as well as in an invited paper (Huang and Lee 2012), both underlining the recognized impact and achievements of the project. In these and other related papers (Such as Lee et al. 2013), we proposed a formal framework to present emotion as a complex event, which are linguistically represented. The linguistic representation of the complex event will be anchored by an emotion word either as an adjective (to indicate a state) or as a verb (to represent either the state or the change-of-state). The emotion state typically follows a pre-event, which is the cause or stimulus of the emotion, and represented as either a clause or as a simple noun. However, in the case of a referential noun as the cause, it is coerced to have the meaning of a typical activity that the noun instigates. In addition, the emotion state (or change of state) can be followed by a response as a post-state. By outlining this linguistic framework, we provided the basis for emotion annotation (Tokunaga et al. 2013) and construction of an emotion corpus in both English and Chinese (Lee et al. 2013).The corpus then lends itself to our various computational studies to predict the emotion classes (Li et al. 2013, Wang et al. 2013, Xu et al. 2012) or the cause of emotion (Lee et. al 2013). Based on the model, we also find that it is possible to predict motion in a text, using the annotated data as the training data, and supplement machine learning training with explicit manually constructed rules. Our study showed that the automatic processing of expressive meaning is plausible and could be crucial clues in understanding of underspecified work.

543810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
543810.value: With the creation of our emotion annotated corpus as well as an eventive model for linguistic representation of emotion, there are several possible future directions of future research developments which are either now underway or being discussed with potential partners: 1. First, is to incorporate both the annotated corpus and the linguistic model in affective computing research to do extraction of opinion and attitude. 2. Second, is to develop a more detailed event-based linguistic model for expressive meaning. In particular, linking emotion to event types and to modal and epistemic systems of different languages 3. Third, to explore how language disorder and variations in the development of language competence affects emotion expression and emotion recognition, based on experiments designed and driven by our corpus. 4. Fourth, study language variations from the point view of how emotion is expressed. This same approach can also be applied to study issues involved in cross-cultural communication. 5. Fifth to study the complexity of language in light of the complex representation of emotion. In other words, does the recognition of basic emotion helps to reduce the complexity of language processing?

543810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
543810.value: This project developed a theory predicting the dependencies between emotions and events, based on linguistic cues in context. In particular, we hypothesized that emotion is presented as a complex event with cause as pre-event, emotion state as the main event, and effect of emotion as post-event. This analysis allows us to develop a Generative Lexicon based formal theory of representation, which describes how grammatical cues are used to represent emotion. Based on this theory, we constructed a large corpus annotated with rich information based on this theory. The annotated data provides the basic resources and infrastructure for both linguistic analysis as well as computational automatic analysis of emotion on the web and from other digital texts in the future.

544210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
544210.value: Brand logos, are important components of any company's identity. They are placed on almost every product package, in promotional materials, on company stationery, etc. Despite their wide-scale usage and importance, this important marketing variable has been largely ignored in the consumer research literature. How logos could be designed better still seems to be a mystery to marketing professionals. Of specific relevance to this proposal, the effectiveness of different types of logos hasn’t been examined. We plan to investigate when and how different types of logos influence consumer perceptions of the company and its products. The major variable we will investigate is the shape of the company logo. The questions we will ask include the following: How do logo designers decide on what kind of logo they will design for different companies? Will a round-shaped logo produce different reactions among consumers than an angular-shaped one? What specific consumer responses are influenced by the logo, and what is the underlying process? Can brand logos affect company sales? Our main focus is on the circular vs. angular shape of the logo. We nevertheless extend our research to examine how products that have a circular vs. angular shaped design influence the inferences that consumers draw regarding the performance of the product, and whether purchase intentions are affected as a result. The results of this research should be of direct relevance to both academic consumer researchers and brand managers. 商標是公司形象的重要組成部分，在基本上每個商品的包裝上，宣傳材料上，或者公司文具上你都可以看到商標的存在。雖然商標十分重要且已被廣泛應用，這個重要的營銷工具經常被消費者研究文獻所忽視。不同種類的商標對消費者的不同影響還沒有被系統的研究過。如何能夠設計出更好的商標對大多數營銷人員來說仍然是個不解之謎。在本研究中，我們計划研究何時和如何不同種類的商標影響消費者對於商家及其產品的印象。在研究的前半部分，我們將著眼于商標的形狀。我們將在研究中試圖回答以下問題：商標設計師如何針對不同的商家設計出不同形狀的商標？圓形与方形的商標會否對消費者造成不同的影響？商標的形狀具體會對消費者造成哪些影響，這些影響是如何形成的？商標的形狀是否能真正影響到商家的銷售業績？在研究的後半部分，我們計划將研究目標從商標設計擴展到產品設計。我們將研究圓形和方形的產品設計如何影響消費者對該產品性能的評價。本研究將對消費者行為研究人員和品牌管理營銷人員有直接的幫助。

544210.label: Major findings and research outcome
544210.value: Two major findings are yielded from this project with a general focus of the role of psychological factors in consumer judgment and decision making. One paper, currently under review at JMR, focuses more on the influence of visual stimuli on consumer behavior. Brand logos are important components of any company’s identity. In this paper we examine if the mere circularity/angularity of a brand logo is powerful enough to affect consumer inferences and product attitudes. We found that circular logos communicate “softness,” and angular logos, “hardness.” These associations are found to reliably affect downstream product perceptions and attitudes, e.g., how customer-oriented a service is (Experiment 1), how comfortable and durable a product (i.e., a shoe) is (Experiments 2-4), and how much a brand is liked (Experiments 1 and 3). Logo shape effects were found to enhance product associations and attitudes in an advertising context if, and only if, the logo shape inferences were consistent with the positioning of the product in the ad (Experiment 3). Also, logo shape effects were eliminated when physically-experienced haptic cues were available for judgments (Experiment 4). Our data further suggested that the logo shape effects obtained were unconscious and spontaneous. The second paper, published in 2013 on JCR, investigates more interpersonal determinants of consumer behavior. This paper examines the effects of social exclusion on a critical aspect of consumer behavior, financial decision-making. Specifically, four lab experiments and one field survey uncover how feeling isolated or ostracized causes consumers to pursue riskier but potentially more profitable financial opportunities. These daring proclivities do not appear driven by impaired affect or self-esteem. Rather, inter-personal rejection exacerbates financial risk-taking by heightening the instrumentality of money (as a substitute for popularity) to obtain benefits in life. Invariably, the quest for wealth that ensues tends to adopt a riskier but potentially more lucrative road.

544210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
544210.value: As may be evident from the above section, this project is productive and there is great potential for further development of this research. Our first priority is to work the current under review paper through the review process and hopefully publish it over the course of the next year or so. We also plan to further extend our investigation of shape-induced consumer inferences from simply logo shape to real product shape. That will be an interesting idea to follow up with.

544210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
544210.value: Brand logos are salient and important visual brand elements, and choosing an effective one has become a sophisticated and expensive business. Notwithstanding the importance industry attaches to choosing a brand logo, there is little research on the topic, particularly when it comes to how different features of the shape of a logo influence product and brand judgments. This paper attempts to fill the gap by developing and testing a framework for how the circularity (the extent to which a logo consists of curved lines) vs. angularity (the extent to which a logo consists of straight lines and sharp corners) of the logo might influence product and brand judgments. Our experiments showed that the mere circularity/angularity of a logo could have a powerful enough effect to influence inferences that consumers draw about products and brands, and these inferences affect overall product attitudes. Our research shows that circular and angular logo shapes spontaneously evoke associations of respectively, softness and hardness, which has not been empirically documented. We also extend previous branding research by theorizing about how different logo shapes carry over to influence specific product and brand judgments. Finally, our research should also help managers design and select logos.

544810.label: Realisation of objectives
544810.value: We started this as a very generic project. We had access to the data sets relatively early and expected to do many things that were considered new and important. The project had a good start: (a) to our best knowledge we were the first who successfully matched the custom-firm data sets. (b), after matching the data we quickly finished two preliminary papers with very interesting results and we presented them in a few conferences. We considered them so new and important that we believed we had chances at top journal such as QJE. During the time we tried to polish the papers for publication, however, many many research groups also got access to the same data sets and different working papers came out very quickly. This unexpected development made the field highly competitive and generated unexpected difficulties for us to differentiate our papers. We sent our export price paper (with the most recent title "Multinational Price Premium") to several top journals but got rejections. Nevertheless we tried very hard to make every revision based on valuable feed backs from referees. Fortunately we got a very good response from Journal of Development Economics for an R&R in June 2014. Currently we are closed to finishing the revision for a re-submission. Since both the editor and the referees are very positive about our paper and we can address all their questions, I am very confident about the final outcome. In the meantime, we have used the compiled data on two side projects. Fortunately both projects went very well, we ended up publishing two papers both at World Development. See attache publications, where I acknowledged RGC for the financial support. In addition, we had done a lot more works associated with the compiled data sets. Due to time limitation, however, we will leave them for future completion. I feel that we can conclude this project by claiming the two papers formally published at World Development and one very promising R&R at Journal of Development.

544810.label: Major findings and research outcome
544810.value: - the paper entitled "Multinational Price Premium" (see attachment, an earlier version with a different title "Prices of Chinese Exports: Beyond Productivity"), currently under revision for re-submission at the Journal of Development Economics, is a major paper we targeted for this RGC project. By exploring a rich data set that links international trade transactions to panel data of manufacturing firms from China over the period 2000-2006, in this paper we reveal new patterns of export prices across firms. We find that foreign-owned firms charge about 28 percent higher prices than Chinese exporters even after controls for firm productivity and product-destination-year fixed effects. We provide evidence that the multinational price premium is significantly correlated with the knowledge based intangible assets within multinationals. The multinational price premium is substantially higher for firms with headquarters in more innovative countries and for firms that have technicians and managers sent from their parent companies. The price premium is even higher for foreign wholly owned firms than for joint ventures. - the 2013 World Development paper (see attachment) uses an enterprise-population data set (part of the data originally prepared for this RGC project) to investigate the link between globalization and gender inequality in the Chinese labor market. We find that foreign and exporting firms employ more female workers than domestic non-exporters. Foreign participation and export orientation within the same region and industry significantly encourage female employment and reduce the gender wage gap. - the 2011 World Development (see attachment) provides micro-level evidence on the close link between foreign participation and wage inequality using the the manufacturing firm level data (originally prepared for the project related to this RGC project) . We investigate the wage premium and the wage spillover effect of foreign-invested enterprises in the Chinese manufacturing sectors. The results indicate a significant foreign premium in both wage and non-wage compensation.

544810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
544810.value: - We have finished another paper entitle "Intermediates Import and Gains from Trade Liberalization" in earlier 2011 (see attachment). We show that input tariff reductions encourage the importers to increase the volume of imported inputs and capital goods, to expand product margin and source country margin, to access to more advance countries, and to import more expensive intermediates. Moreover, we find that the import response to trade liberalization significantly improve firm performance. These results provide direct evidences for the learning, variety and quality channels of intermediate imports. We believed the finding was fresh new with great publication potential, since it was the first comprehensive firm-level study on this topic about China (only possible with the matched custom-firm data, while we were the first who finishing the matching). However, the works on this topic evolved very rapidly when many research groups also had the data matched a bit later and similar results on the same topics quickly appeared in working papers format, so it became difficult to differentiate our paper as it stood. And we realized that we needed to find a different angle to re-address the problem. We hope to revise this paper by introducing a new selling point after we finish the JDE paper. We have made a few more findings (though somewhat preliminary) with potentials for further development. I will not describe them here since I believe what have been listed are already sufficient to conclude this project.

544810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
544810.value: In this project we conduct researches on topics related to how firm performance are closely related to trade and foreign firms. We find that firms owned by foreign investors produce higher quality good for exporting and charge significantly higher exporting prices, and this price premium is explained by intangibles owned by foreign firms from more advanced countries; We also find that firms importing technologically more advanced goods as inputs improve the firm performances; And finally, we find exporting and firm ownership have explanatory power on gender inequality and wage inequality in Chinese manufacturing firms, respectively. Thus we identify different channels through which Chinese firms' capability can be improved.

544910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
544910.value: An increasing trend for China-made products entering international markets has been occurring over the past decades. During this internationalization process, Chinese manufacturers encounter various environmentally-oriented institutional forces to mitigate the environmental impact of their products. The trend of increasing internationalization of Chinese manufacturing enterprises is noteworthy because Chinese manufacturers are often found less environmentally conscious as compared to their counterparts in the developed countries. While the Chinese manufacturing export expands, the environmental burdens brought by China-made products will be worsening. Such development highlights the importance of adopting extended producer responsibility (EPR) practices by Chinese manufacturers to meet the growing environmental requirements in international markets while relieving the damages that will cause to the natural environment. This shift of environmental responsibility to upstream manufacturers will accelerate because a growing number of governments including China have incorporated EPR into their environmental policy. Meanwhile, the Chinese government is promoting the development of circular economy so as to alleviate the contradiction between rapid economic growth and shortage of resources. Under this environmental initiative, the manufacturing industry plays an important role in the management of environmental protection and resource issues encountered in China. We propose to investigate how the various environmentally-oriented institutional forces arising from the internationalization of China-made products prompt the adoption of EPR practices in the Chinese manufacturing industry. Based on the institutional theory, we plan to identify the international and domestic pressures that are salient to the growing environmental awareness and responses for these manufacturing enterprises in China. In such case, EPR can be a viable mean for Chinese manufacturers to resolve both the domestic and international pressures for preserving the environment, reaping performance benefits, and aligning with the international expectation and national goal for environmental protection and resource conservation. Through a large scale empirical study with Chinese manufacturers, we will be able to explain the links between internationalization, environmental protection, EPR, and performance outcomes. The results will provide answers on the topical issues relating to the driving forces propelling the adoption of EPR practices by Chinese manufacturers and determine if such adoption is instrumental in improving their environmental and economic performance. On the practical side, a measurement scale for evaluating EPR practices and industrial benchmarking indicators will be part of the study results which are useful references for Chinese manufacturers to assess and develop improvement goals for their EPR practices and performance outcomes. 中國產品在世界市場上的發展，在過去幾十年來呈現不斷上升的趨勢。在這國際化的進程中，各界向中國製造商施壓，提出減輕環境負荷的要求。由於中國製造商的環保意識與發達國家相比還存在很大的差距，中國企業國際化的過程尤其值得關注。 隨著中國製造業的出口量日益擴大，中國製造的產品所帶來的環境負擔也日趨嚴重。以上狀況突顯中國製造商採用 「生產者責任延伸｣ (EPR) 的重要性，以滿足在國際市場上日益增長的環保要求，同時減輕對自然環境造成的傷害。中國與各國地方政府漸把EPR列入國家環保政策，此舉進一步把環境責任推至供應鏈上游的製造商。同時，中國政府正積極推動發展循環經濟，以緩解經濟快速增長和資源短缺兩者之間的制約。在這項環保措施下，製造業在中國環境保護和資源管理中充當重要的角色。此計劃書旨在探討中國產品在國際化過程中所面對的不同體制導向壓力及如何促進中國製造業採用EPR。我們計劃透過體制理論，辨識出中國製造商鑑於環保意識和環保應變的發展而所面對的各種國際和國內對環保有關的要求。在這種情況下，EPR是一個可行的途徑以供中國製造商舒緩國內和國際的環保壓力，提升公司表現，以及達至國際期望和國家環境保護及資源節約的目標。我們通過對中國製造企業進行大型問卷調查，解釋國際化、環境保護、EPR、公司表現，上述四者的關係。研究結果有助解答，「什麼是推動中國製造商採用EPR的驅動力｣，「通過EPR是否有助於改善其環境和經濟表現｣ 以上的熱門話題。研究中的部分成果包括一套評估 EPR的方法和工業基準的指標。這些研究结果將會是有實際應用的相關參考資料，為中國製造商進行評估，並制定及改進他們的EPR做法和表現。

544910.label: Realisation of objectives
544910.value: This study examines the extent to which internationalization of China-made products is related to the environmental awareness of Chinese manufacturing enterprises and hence their adoption of extended producer responsibility (EPR) practices based on institutional theory and environmental management perspectives. A measurement scale for evaluating EPR practices adoption was developed, which was subsequently used to examine the links of the international and domestic environmental pressures encountered by Chinese manufacturers with the extent of their EPR practices adoption and performance outcomes. The empirical results provide managerial and policy actions for enhancing the environmental protection and resource conservation in production activities and promoting the adoption of EPR practices by Chinese manufacturers. In sum, this study is successfully completed with all the five original research objectives achieved. Seven research papers covering the five research objectives of this project with RGC's grant acknowledgement have been published in reputable academic journals.

544910.label: Major findings and research outcome
544910.value: Extended producer responsibility (EPR) is increasingly emphasized by manufacturing enterprises to improve eco-efficiency and to satisfy the growing environmental requirements expected in the market. This trend is salient for export-oriented manufacturers mandated to comply with environmental regulatory requirements before entry is granted for their products in the requisite overseas countries. They need to meet the green barriers to export their products. In sum, this study has achieved the following findings and outcomes: 1) The international environmentalism experienced by Chinese manufacturers positively influences their extent of implementing environmentally-related organizational learning practices; 2) Chinese manufacturers implementing EPR practices more intensively tend to achieve better performance; 3) The positive relationship between implementing EPR practices and the performance outcomes is strengthened when customer integration in the implementation is at a high level; 4) Manufacturers need to pay attention on relationship risk, asset risk, and competence risk in logistics outsourcing; 5) Environmental governance is important for green reputation, which improve a firm's overall corporate reputation and hence economic performance; 6) When the organizational motives for adopting ISO 14001 increase, the performance benefits pertaining to the social, environmental, and market performance from the adoption of environmental management system also increase; 7) Strategic alliance formation is beneficial for the performance of Chinese manufacturing enterprises.

544910.value: A longitudinal analysis of the internationalization pressures, EPR practices, and performance outcomes of Chinese manufacturers is suggested to track the evolution of EPR practices adoption in the Chinese manufacturing industry.

544910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
544910.value: This study examines whether internationalization has led to improved environmental management practices, particularly extended producer responsibility (EPR) practices among Chinese manufacturers. The EPR practices undertaken by export-oriented manufacturers and their market and financial performance outcomes are also investigated. The results show that international institutional pressures positively relate to domestic environmentalism of Chinese manufacturers and their adoption of environmentally-related organizational learning practices including EPR. Environmental learning is a viable method for Chinese manufacturers to ease their environmental burdens by replicating environmental management practices of their foreign counterparts. This study also finds that EPR adoption is beneficial for the performance of Chinese manufacturers. On the policy side, the Chinese government should follow other developed countries efforts to deploy environmental regulations and policies, further motivating environmental awareness and responses in the manufacturing industry. Practically, managers need to understand the performance implications of implementing EPR practices to align with their performance goals and to build their supply chain system capabilities in the age of global complexity.

546710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
546710.value: 香港是一个世界闻名的都市旅游目的地，2008年香港接待了大约3千万国际旅游者，其旅游收入达到1.59亿港元。2006年香港被列为全球五大旅游城市之一。通过利用其独特的历史背景和优越的地理位置，香港政府在过去五十年中利用一系列旅游项目积极发展香港的旅游产业。尽管这些项目对本地旅游业的发展贡献巨大，但是香港仍然面临着来自于亚洲新兴旅游目的地的各种挑战。香港作为都市旅游目的地的一个重要特点是，香港的旅游发展受到其有限的土地资源的制约。这说明了，香港旅游产业的空间分布，相关土地利用问题，以及香港旅游产业能否提供多样化的产品组合的能力等问题都需要学术界的探究。本研究将结合定性与定量研究方法，利用地理信息系统的分析能力，来研究香港主要旅游发展项目对于香港旅游产业及产品组合的空间分布结构的影响。本研究选取了迪士尼乐园作为研究对象。 本研究将在理论及实践两方面对现有文献做出重要贡献。在理论方面，本研究关于旅游产业的空间分布结构和产品组合的分析，以及关于香港迪士尼乐园影响的分析，将从研究主体，研究方法以及研究背景方面扩展人们对于都市旅游的认识。在实践贡献方面，本研究结果将为探索更好的旅游土地利用方案，旅游规划和制定旅游政策提供概念和方法，从而促进香港旅游的可持续发展。

546710.label: Realisation of objectives
546710.value: Objective I: To explore the evolution of the spatial structure of tourism in Hong Kong by documenting the history of tourism development This objective has been fully achieved during the second reporting period. We documented the history of tourism development, as well as the evolution of the spatial structure of tourist attractions, hotels, and other facilities over the time through secondary data. By doing this, we had a better understanding of the overall picture of tourism development in Hong Kong, which laid a foundation for subsequent research work. Objective II: To examine the influence of the Disneyland development on the spatial structure of the Hong Kong tourism industry Objective III: To examine the influence of the Disneyland development on the tourism product mix in Hong Kong and on tourists’ behavior before and during their visits These two objectives have been fully achieved since last reporting period. We used two different analytical methods (the Geographical Weighted Regression and logistic regression) to investigate the changes of tourism spatial structure between 2000 and 2010, i.e. five years before and five years after the Disneyland was open to public. Both studies identified certain pattern of change of spatial structure but it seems that, deviating from the hypothesis, the influence of Disneyland was not that significant. As part of the effort to investigate the influence of consumer behavior, we studied the travel motivation of Mainland Chinese tourists, which were considered as one of the major markets of Disneyland. The influence of cultural values on their motivation was examined. The findings from this part have been accepted on Journal of Hospitality & Tourism Research and International Journal of Tourism Research.

546710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
546710.value: The findings from this project indicate that the influence of Disneyland on the spatial structure and product structure of Hong Kong tourism was not as significant as expected. This insignificance may be partially attributed to its recency. The unexpected results lead me to think about the real attractiveness of urban tourism destination. By reviewing existing literature, I identified the concept of World Tourism City proposed by Maitland and Newman (2009), which is defined as multifunctional and polycentric with the capacity to draw visitors off the beaten track. A proposal conceptualized on this concept has been submitted for the 2014-2015 GRF.

546710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
546710.value: One of the major challenges facing the tourism industry in HK is the limited land resources available and the concomitant failure to provide a diversified range of tourism products. Despite the continuous investment of land and monetary resources in developing tourism, questions such as “are the current land use and spatial distribution patterns of tourism-related phenomena rational?”, “is the existing tourism product mix, including its spatial reflection, suitable for the sustainable development of tourism in HK?”, and “does the current spatial structure of HK tourism fit well with the overall urban fabric?” remain unexplored. The proposed study was designed to answer those questions by investigating the impact of Disneyland on the spatial and product structure of tourism industry in HK. From a theoretical perspective, the proposed study addressed four research gaps identified through a review of the urban tourism literature in general and prior studies on the spatial aspects of urban tourism in particular. Practically, the findings can provide guidance to the government, the local community, and the tourism industry on tourism land use issues and on how to develop, manage, and market HK more effectively as an urban tourism destination in a sustainable manner.

546910.value: 中國環境法規執行的改變：三個城市環保執法官員的追蹤研究

546910.value: Dr Gelder, Jean-Louis van Prof Rooij, van Benjamin Prof Tang, Shui-Yan Dr Zhan, Xueyong

546910.label: Project Objectives
546910.value: To provide a comprehensive view of the changes on enforcement styles among environmental officials in China; To identify various institutional factors, both external and internal to local environmental protection bureaus, that effect such changes; To assess the relative perceived effectiveness of different enforcement styles over a period of time; To evaluate the enforcement gap of regulatory control of industrial pollution from a longitudinal perspective; To identify difficulties these environmental officials face in the enforcement of pollution control rules and regulations; and To identity strategies that can help these local environmental protection bureaus and their environmental officials to develop a stronger enforcement capacity.

To identify various institutional factors, both external and internal to local environmental protection bureaus, that effect such changes;
