546910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
546910.value: In the last three decades, China has adopted a legalistic approach to environmental protection and pollution control, trying to curb the negative side-effects of its tremendous economic growth. During that time, China has gradually established and strengthened a structure of national and local state institutions tasked with implementing and enforcing these environmental regulations. The enforcement of pollution laws in China is one of the best documented cases of regulatory enforcement in a developmental setting and an important case for those seeking to expand existing regulatory theory beyond its current Western confines. There is, however, an important caveat in the literature on Chinese pollution enforcement: there are no serious or organized studies on how enforcement practices at the local level may be changing over time and how such changes are influenced by wider institutional transformations. Institutional developments of the last decade in China force us to question whether the existing picture at the street level, of purportedly informal and weak pollution enforcement is still correct. There has been mounting central government commitment to pollution control, social pressures against pollution have become a stronger force, the Chinese bureaucracy has becoming more professionalized following the introduction of the merit-based civil service system, and most important of all, some local governments, traditionally blamed for the weak enforcement of environmental laws, have shown relatively more commitment to the environment. It would be reasonable to expect that such institutional developments have affected street-level pollution law enforcement. However, the existing literature has yet to capture what changes may have occurred. To address this research gap, this proposed research seeks to perform a longitudinal study of pollution law enforcement in China. Specifically, it intends to answer three important questions: 1) How are regulatory enforcement styles changing in China? 2) What are the institutional factors contributing to these changes? and 3) How have enforcement agents’ perceptions about the effectiveness of different enforcement styles changed? These questions will be addressed by conducting surveys and interviews of environmental enforcement officials. This longitudinal study will build on our earlier study of enforcement styles among enforcement officials in the three Chinese cities of Chengdu, Dalian and Guangzhou conducted in 2000. It will use basically the same set of questions to extend the analysis of cross jurisdiction variation in enforcement styles to that of temporal changes. In this way, this study will advance the boundary of current enforcement research. 中國環境法規執行的改變：三個城市環保執法官員的追蹤研究 在過去三十年，中國以法律形式的方法去保護環境和控制污染，以圖抑制因重大經濟增長所帶來的負面影響。 在此段時期，中國已經逐漸建立和強化一個從中央直達地方的行政體制負責執行這些環保法規。中國污染控制法規的執行是在眾多發展中地區的監管法規執行其中一個記錄最完整的個案，並且是那些尋求將現行的監管理論適用於西方國家以外地區的研究人員的重要個案。可是，現時在中國污染執法的文獻中有一個重大的缺漏：就是沒有對地方執法的實踐因時間而變改和這些改變如何受到宏觀制度變遷的影響的嚴謹或系統性的研究。 中國在過去十年來制度上的發展使我們質疑現時基層故意不規範和不著力去進行污染執法的情況仍然正確。 中央政府對污染控制的強大決心，社會對污染的壓力已經成為一股更強的力量，中國的官僚架構隨著優才公務員制度的推行而變得更專業化，而最重要的是一些傳統上為人詬病對環保法規執行不力的地方政府，已經表現出對環境保護更大的決心。因此，有理由相信這些制度上的發展已經對基層的污染法規的執行產生了影響。可是，現時的研究文獻仍未能掌握這些轉變。 為了填補這個研究遺缺，這個研究建議書致力於對中國污染法規執法進行一個追蹤研究。具體地，它試圖回答三個重要的問題：1. 中國的監管執法方式有何改變？2. 那些制度上的因素促使成了這些改變？以及3. 環保官員對不同執法方式的效果的感覺有何改變？這些問題會透過對環保執法官員進行問卷調查和訪談去回答。這個追蹤研究將以我們較早前在2000年對成都，大連及廣州三個中國城市的環保執法官員所作的執法方式的研究為基礎。是次研究基本上會採用相同的問題去推廣至時空轉變下不同地區執法方式相異的分析。如此，這個研究將會超越現時執法研究的領域。

546910.label: Realisation of objectives
546910.value: As planned, we have completed the interviews of leading officials of individual service organizations in the environmental protection bureau (EPB) of all the three cities of Dalian, Chengdu and Guangzhou. Since the reform of service organizations is a politically sensitive research topic, it took us years to get all interviews arranged and conducted. We encountered difficulties in arranging the interviews in both Dalian and Guangzhou. In Dalian, our research supporting institution there did not have close contact with all service organizations in the Dalian Environmental Protection Bureau and we could only interview a selected number of service organizations. In Guangzhou, the political climate in this period of time did not welcome external researchers to study the institutional changes of Guangzhou Environmental Protection Bureau and we could only complete the interviews of all service organizations in February 2016. In comparison, the arrangements of interviews of service organizations in Chengdu Environmental Bureau were quite smooth and we were able to get all interviews conducted in October 2014. To conduct cross-city comparison of local EPB’s service organizations in these three cities, we used the research method of semi-structured interviews with a set of 10 questions on the following aspects: 1. The establishment and history development of your service organization (贵事业单位成立及发展历史). 2. The reform measures implemented in your service organization (中央推进事业单位分类改革在贵单位实施的具体情况). 3. Major functions and activities of your service organization (主要的业务范围). 4. The management structure and staffing situation (管理体系及人员情况) 5. Work conditions and sources of funding (工作条件及经费来源) 6. The working relationship with municipal environmental protection bureau (与市环保局关系) 7. Major difficulties and problems encountered (面临的主要困难与问题) 8. Future development plan and directions (未来发展计划及方向) 9. Your views and comments on the development and reform of service organizations in your city’s environmental protection bureau (你对贵市在过去十多年环保局属下事业单位的发展和改革情况有什么看法和评价) 10. Give examples to illustrate major changes of services organizations in your city’s environmental protection bureau and identify the reasons (请例举广州市在过去十多年环保属下事业单位的发展重大的转变和原因) Before the interview, we sent the list of these questions to the leading officials of the service organization concerned for information so that they were able to get a clear idea of our research focus and purposes. As a result, many interviewees were quite well-prepared. Each interview last around 60 to 75 minutes. In order to get an accurate picture of the reform situation in each service organization, we insisted to interview either its chief or deputy chief. This also made our study sensitive and increased the difficulties in arranging the interviews. We made all the individual interview records transcribed in April this year and have already conducted preliminary analysis. Based on these interview records, we should be able to identify the general trend of service organization reform in China, to provide an in-depth analysis of the developmental path of all EPB-affiliated service organizations in Guangzhou in the past decade, to compare the practices of service organization reform in the environmental administrative system in different regions in China, to identify various contextual factors, both external and internal to local EPBs, that impact the reform of service organizations in China, and to propose strategies that can help both the central and local governments to reform service organizations in China. In the conclusion of data collection in this project, we judge that we should be able to achieve all the objectives set beforehand. However, we were unable to get the chief/deputy chief of every service organization in each of the three cities’ EPBs interviewed because of various institutional constraints. At the same time, it took us a very long time to arrange interviews in Guangzhou with the latest one completed earlier this year. In order to get an adequate empirical basis for cross-jurisdiction comparisons, we added Tianjin to our study and we conducted interviews of all Tianjin EPB’s service organizations in 2015 with help from the Center of Environmental Publicity and Education of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and additional funding support from PolyU. On the whole, we are satisfied with the results in regard to the interviews conducted. Given the richness of interview data and findings, we will able to produce two different sets of research papers, with one focusing on cross-jurisdiction analysis among these three cities (now, Chengdu, Guangzhou and Tianjin) concerning variations of reform approaches and institutional environments, while the other one focusing on the changes of service organization reform and institutional setting over time in Guangzhou. Two papers are now in the final stage of preparation, with one already presented in an international public management conference. Both will be sent out to top journals for review, with one targeting at Public Administration Review and the other one China Journal. We expect to take another two years to get all major findings published in the form of journal papers. To conclude our research experience in this project, we come to realize that it was far more have expected, particularly to interview officers-in-charge of these service organizations. We were glad to get support from local academic institutions (Tsinghua University for arranging the interviews in Tianjin, Dalian University of Technology for arranging the interviews in Dalian, and Xian Jiaotong University for arranging the interviews in Chengdu) and respective municipal EPBs and their research academies. Finally we would like to thank UGC for their approval for allowing us to use the project funding for obtaining research support from these academic and government institutions in the mainland China.

546910.label: Major findings and research outcome
546910.value: Based on transaction cost considerations, we have developed a conceptual framework of institutional choice in service organization reform in China, arguing that service organizations are more likely to become more independent from their sponsoring government agency if (1) they do not exercise public authority, (2) they provide services that are deemed to be non-essential, (3) there are alternative and reliable vendors, and (4) they have more market opportunities. We also argued that several political and contextual factors may affect the extent to which these transaction cost considerations are applied in actual reform efforts. In this research project, we test the robustness of our institutional choice framework by comparing service organizations reform in Chengdu and Guangzhou. Based on fieldwork and interviews with around ten service organizations in both cities between 2014 and 2016, our analysis shows that some service organizations in Guangzhou have indeed become more independent, following the transaction cost logic; but many have remained tied to the government, driven more by political considerations. In comparison with service organizations in Guangzhou, those in Chengdu have shown less progress toward reform, reflecting the latter’s less open social and political landscapes. Overall, our comparative study shows that the institutional choice framework developed we have developed can be used to explain service organization reform in China, identifies jurisdictional variation in service organization reform, and highlights the contextual constraints for streamlining and rationalizing the Chinese bureaucracy. This same the institutional choice framework has also been adopted to examine the changes of service organization reform in Guangzhou between 2006 and 2015. We found that three service organizations have undergone significant changes. First the enforcement team has been integrated to the administrative framework as part of an enforcement bureau in the provincial government since it exercises the public authority of law enforcement and dispensing penalties on violations. Second the Monitoring Station has now served exclusively for the Guangzhou EPB as its agent for collecting pollution data and monitoring enterprise pollution control performance, stopping from providing paid pollution monitoring services to enterprises since it provides services that are deemed to be essential to EPB. Third, the Guangzhou Academy of Environmental Science has also been asked to support GZEPB’s pollution control planning and research and its EIA (Environmental Impact Assessment) unit has been privatized since it has more market opportunities and at the same time to prevent any conflicts of interest in the EIA process.

546910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
546910.value: This project is one of the rare systematic efforts to conduct the study on the cross-city analysis of service organization reform in China and the reform changes over time. Indeed, the reform of service organizations is an urgent task for Chinese government given its critical impact on shape of government-market and government-society relations. We have developed a conceptual framework that connects contextual factors with institutional choice, based on transaction cost considerations, to capture geographical variations and longitudinal changes in the implementation of service organization reform in the environmental administrative system. Based on the interviews of leading officials of service organizations in the municipal EPBs of Guangzhou, Chengdu, Dalian and Tianjin, we test our framework and the findings suggest the need to contextualize the study of service organization reform in dynamic and diversified institutional settings. As the reform of service organizations in China has from being conclusive, it is strongly desirable to conduct another round of study a few years later on the EPB’s service organizations in these cities in order to provide further empirical support to our theoretical model of contextual changes and service organization reforms.

546910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
546910.value: This project examines the reform of service organizations in China’s environmental protection administration system with the focus on the changes of the reform practices over time at the local level and cross-jurisdiction variations. Specifically, it seeks to answer four questions: 1) How are service organizations changing in the context of broader governance reform? 2) How are service organizations changing in the context of broader governance reform? 3) How are service organizations changing in the context of broader governance reform? 4) How are service organizations changing in the context of broader governance reform? Both the cross-city comparative and longitudinal studies build on our earlier study of service organization reform in the Guangzhou Environmental Protection Bureau in 2007. It uses basically the same set of questions to extend the analysis of cross-sectional study to that of regional variations and temporal changes. In short, our project is the first serious attempt to study how service organization reform practices at the local level may be changing over time and how such changes are influenced by boarder institutional transformation. As a result, this study has advanced the boundary of current research on service organization reform which are predominated case-based and cross-sectional studies.

547110.label: Project Objectives
547110.value: Do local market-supporting institutions (e.g., degree of marketalization, legalization, human capital development, financial depth, levels of corruption, political openness, etc.) affect firms' probability to use the judiciary system? If yes, what is the mechanism of such relationship? Do politically-connected firms in China have advantage in China's judicial system, as evidenced by litigation rates, outcomes and enforcement efficiency?

547110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
547110.value: We study what determines a firm’s decision to litigate rather than reach settlement in China. In particular, we examine the role of local market-supporting institutions and firms’ political connections on their litigation rate, the win rate at trial, and enforcement efficiency. Drawn on China’s provincial level data on institutional development from 1992 to 2009, and the litigation and alternative settlements information of all Chinese listed companies in the same period, our proposition is that better market-supporting institutions increase businesses’ reliance on formal institutions and contracts, and less reliance on guanxi, in structuring economic activities, which increases the probability of litigation to reach settlement in disputes. Moreover, a firm’s political connections, under the present Chinese regime of Party leadership over judiciary, play a significant role in litigation decision and outcome. The effect of political connections is expected to be particularly significant in regions with poor market-supporting institutions and a highly dependent judiciary. This project is significant in that it is, to the applicants’ knowledge, the first work to study Chinese firms’ litigation behavior from the law and economics perspective. It advances the existing theories by extending the litigation selection model (Priest and Klein, 1984; Hylton 1993, 2002) to a relationship based and judicially dependent context. It adds to the prior literature on politically connected firms (Roberts, 1990; Agrawal and Knoeber, 2001; Fisman, 2001; Khwaja and Mian, 2005; Faccio, 2006; Fan et al., 2007) by providing the missing evidence on their link with litigation rates and outcomes (including enforcement). This work also has policy implications on China’s economic reform and judicial capacity building. Though we use China as the country for study, the implication of this project extends to other transitional economies with similar institutional settings to that of China. 本项目研究中国公司遇到纠纷时在使用正式规则（诉讼）与非正式规则（私了）问题上的选择。尤其是地方市场化水平以及公司的政治关联对于公司的诉讼意愿，诉讼胜率，以及执行效率的影响机理。基于对中国1992年至2009年各省的制度环境以及该期间所有上市公司涉及的诉讼以及其它解决方案的实证分析，我们认为不同地区的市场化水平对于该地区的法制环境以及公司使用正式规则保护其财产权利的意愿有积极影响。同时，我们发现在中国司法非独立的政治体系之下公司的政治关联对于其诉讼行为，诉讼结果，以及执行效率都有显著的影响。该等影响在市场化水平较低的省份尤其显著。

547110.label: Major findings and research outcome
547110.value: For the 1st research objective, we do find local market-supporting institutions (e.g., degree of marketalization, legalization, human capital development, financial depth, levels of corruption, political openness, etc.) affect firms' propensity to use the judiciary system. We also find the government has both the stake and capacity to oversee the manner in which disputes arise and are resolved, and court is but one of the many state-sponsored forums to channel social grievances and maintain social stability. On the second research objective, based on our hand-collected dataset of 3323 disclosed commercial lawsuits of listed companies in China. We find robust evidence that Chinese courts favor state owned firms and private firms with personal political ties. This effect is pronounced in litigations but not arbitrations. Local-connected firms are favored in their home courts but not favored when the case is tried outside their home province. We also find the court advantage of connected firms is larger in provinces with weaker legal institutions, but decreases as the case merit becomes complex. Our results cast light on the dispute settlement role of courts in emerging and transitional economies.

547110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
547110.value: This project sets a good 1st empirical step towards uncovering the 'black box' of China's judicial system. It sets a good foundation for subsequent research projects that study firm's litigation strategies, litigation disclosure, and the value of lawyer-directors. The hand-collected dataset (including the institutional environment variables at provincial level, as well as listed firms litigation data) generated from this project has great value to advance the law and finance studies in mainland China.

548210.value: 扶貧的社會中介組織:社會企業支援金字塔底層的角色

548210.label: Project Objectives
548210.value: Understand whether SEs play multiple roles as intermediaries in connecting underdeveloped markets with developed markets? Understand contextual, situational, and contingent variables that govern the existence and success of these different roles?
rows: Understand whether SEs play multiple roles as intermediaries in connecting underdeveloped markets with developed markets?
Understand contextual, situational, and contingent variables that govern the existence and success of these different roles?

548210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
548210.value: Recent estimates suggest that approximately 40% of the world’s population continue to live on less than US$ 2/day (Karnani, 2007; Prahalad, 2006). This lamentable statistic exists despite extensive efforts on the part of governments, non-governmental organizations, and multilateral agencies over the past century. More recently, market-based approaches to poverty alleviation that envisage providing low-income individuals with better access to socially beneficial products and services, as well as linking poor rural producers with new market outlets, have been proposed as complementary solutions to existing charitable endeavors (Prahalad and Hart, 2002). These market-based approaches are most often undertaken by social enterprises (SEs) which are organizations that undertake, “a set of institutional practices combining the pursuit of financial objectives with the pursuit and promotion of substantive and terminal values.” Cho (2006: 36). Thus, these for-profit/nonprofit hybrid forms of organization are able to directly improve the quality of life for people at the base of the global income pyramid (London et al., 2009) while simultaneously providing a reasonable profit to the organization which allows them to sustain and grow their social agenda over time (Akula, 2008; Prahalad, 2006). In previous case studies that we have conducted, we found that SEs engage in base of pyramid (BoP) markets by undertaking a range of intermediation activities. Unfortunately, much of the trade that currently exists within countries plagued by poverty occurs through local middlemen referred to as ‘coyotes’. The lack of competition amongst coyotes represents an extremely inefficient and exploitative trading channel that hinders both producer well-being at an individual level, and economic development at an aggregate level. To rectify this inefficiency, a number of SEs have launched programs in which they, rather than the ‘coyotes,’ act as intermediaries in the buying and selling of products. This intermediation can be transactional or informational in nature, may involve one product or multiple products, and may focus on providing products to the BOP or sourcing products from the BOP. However, very little is known currently about which approach, or combined set of approaches, will lead to greater social and economic success. In this research we propose a mixed-methods approach to understanding the multiple roles SEs play as intermediaries in connecting informal with formal markets. By doing so, we seek to not only uncover broad statistical relationships between variables of interest, but also to decipher the nuanced contextual and contingent variables that influence the success of these different roles.

548310.label: Realisation of objectives
548310.value: The project had six key objectives. It aimed to develop an in-depth understanding of how city users (ordinary people) practiced their everyday lives in public space. It also aimed to explore/review the system of public-space use in a city (i.e. Hong Kong). The project further attempted to provide reference and experience relating to the study of city users’ practices in their everyday spaces. In addition, the project was expected to generate knowledge and experience for future study on similar topics. To meet the objectives, as indicated in the research proposal and progress reports, a case study (qualitative) approach was adopted. We conducted a literature review, a background review, intensive observations and direct interviews. Although many recent studies have claimed to have intensively explored city users’ behaviour, very few have taken seriously the planning and implementation of observation. In contrast, this project (and its researchers) took the matter seriously. For example, disregarding the weather and some practical difficulties, intensive observations of city users’ ways of using different places (e.g. various streets along which different generations congregated, and cross-sections) in Wanchai were conducted over one year: two days a week, at weekends, on special days and during festivals. Although the project was mainly conducted in Wanchai, other districts such as Sham Shui Po and Tin Shui Wai were included as supplementary sites for the study of the ‘reception’ of city users. In addition to Hong Kong residents generally, several specific groups of people were selected for observation, e.g. newly arrived residents (from the Chinese mainland), users of traditional market streets and visitors from the Chinese mainland, to allow a more focused analysis. The project was completed with satisfactory results. As indicated in the section entitled ‘Summary of objectives addressed to date’, all objectives were addressed. The resulting publications and presentations are generating insights and acting as references for urban design researchers and professionals, permitting them to review and consider the importance of ‘users’. As one journal reviewer commented, although user-centred design is not new it is still worthwhile to have further discussion on it and to generate new perspectives to extend reflection on the topic. The project could meet this goal not only by presenting findings but also by raising some critical questions for in-depth review, reflection and further development. Examples of such questions are ‘Is a designer necessary for urban design?’ ‘Are people’s practices continuously changing with the recent ongoing transformation of city space?’ The project also assisted a postgraduate research student and several young researchers to gain experience in the area. The postgraduate student’s thesis will be submitted at the beginning of 2015, and the researchers gained sufficient maturity to be able to join the PI’s research team to work on other projects, or to become researchers at other universities. One researcher also completed his Master’s degree on a similar topic by drawing on his experience in the project. Furthermore, the findings and experience derived through the project were presented at venues with high reputations in the field. For example, the PI was invited to give presentations on the project at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (USA), Tsinghua University, Zhejiang University and the Central Academy of Fine Arts (China). In the newly built Hong Kong Jockey Club Innovation Tower, housing the School of Design, exhibitions of the data analysis (methods and tools) were also presented to professionals and important researchers in the field, and to government departments.

548310.label: Major findings and research outcome
548310.value: The findings of the project show that governments generally consider that professional plans together with government control will inevitably produce a good-quality living environment (see Research Publication Outputs [1-8] in Part C of this report). However, in agreement with some other recent studies, it was also found that a habitable place (with high-quality living) does not result merely from government plans and controls [3, 4, 8]. The outputs of the project include journal publications, presentations and other outputs such as postgraduate research study training and tools for teaching. According to the findings, ‘equilibrium’ in the use of space and the organisation of territory in the urban environment does not result only from the actions of governments and professionals [3, 5, 7, 8]. City users also play an important role in constructing a habitable place [6, 8]. This equilibrium can be understood through using a conventional theory of physics – the three states of equilibrium: stable, unstable and neutral. In other words, city spaces (and urban living environments) are not used exactly as a government anticipates through its planning and controls. However, city users are not free to operate without constraints [4, 6, 8]. Thus, the city space-use system can be better understood as having a three-layered structure: (i) a formal and official urban policy and process of implementation, with codified laws, ordinances and involvement of government departments; (ii) informal ways of operating, with well-established customary, traditional, conventional, local and individual practices; and (iii) an intermediate layer in which city users reconstruct their everyday space to make it habitable through continuous interactions with the government, related bodies and organisations, and other users of the city. Moreover, it is important and essential to shift the focus of ‘design’ from the province of designers to that of the users. Although a designer is necessary to create a design, he/she is not the only factor in a good design [8]. Design professionals should instead adopt a user-centred perspective [3], [5]. Policy-makers and designers should respect the everyday lifestyles of city users, learn how to observe and listen to users, and facilitate an environment that allows and encourages city users to participate in the urban planning and design process [8]. The project also generated some new methods and tools for analysing intensive field studies. Examples of the tools are provided in Part C of this report. Discussion on the tools is included in most of the publications generated from the project [2], [4]-[8]. According to the teaching experience of the PI, these tools (such as a large-scale ‘wall-hanging’ capture of images) are useful to give researchers an overall view of the flow of activities. The tools also make it easy for researchers to conduct comparative studies of user behaviour observed at different times.

548310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
548310.value: Based on user-reception theory, the project generated some new directions for further research. For example, it is necessary to further explore such topics as ‘third-realm’ and ‘neutral equilibrium’. The changing roles of and relationships between policy-makers, professionals and city users are important topics for further study. Comparative studies in different cities are also essential. Regarding the research methods, it would be very worthwhile to conduct in-depth, longitudinal studies on city development and changes in user practices. For example, Hong Kong has undertaken many reclamation projects over more than 100 years, and in-depth studies on not only the changing environment but also changes in the everyday practices and lifestyles of residents could be important. The PI has developed a new research perspective in seeing/reviewing people’s everyday practices in a continuously transforming city and has raised several reflective questions for design researchers and professionals (see Section 5.3). Further studies on these perspectives, areas and questions are necessary. Today, most urban planning journals prefer to accept publications dealing with ‘large-scale’ planning projects and studies. Papers addressing high-quality research on people’s everyday lives and high-quality living spaces are not readily accepted. Although papers from the project have been successfully published, the PI proposes that academic institutes and publishers need to take care to maintain a balance in publishing different perspectives of academic output. This is also a direction of study for future researchers.

548310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
548310.value: In recent years, many people have complained that city people’s quality of life has not improved. Instead, the urban living environment has become a site for modern development rather than everyday living. Through a qualitative study undertaken on several streets with different backgrounds, environmental settings and aspects of life in Hong Kong, this project has brought about a more comprehensive understanding of how ordinary people practice their everyday lives. The project identified and discussed the issues of design and quality of life. It generated insights and references (i.e., publications, presentations) for those involved in policy-making, design and social development, and raised new research questions for further discussion and investigation. A key finding of the project was that the system for use of city space is better understood as a three-layered structure: a formal and official urban policy and process of implementation, with codified laws, ordinances and involvement of government departments; informal ways of operating, with well-established customary, traditional, conventional, local and individual practices; and an intermediate layer in which city users reconstruct their everyday spaces to make them habitable. The project holds that city users’ everyday practices are dynamic to the transformation of the city. A neutral equilibrium arises in city users’ everyday practices that is continually altered by the interactions between policymakers, professionals and users. The findings showed that, instead of designers, city users are the key factors to be taken into consideration in design. The project involved a user-oriented research approach, which is relatively difficult and time-consuming (e.g., involving intensive, long-term field work), and is rarely considered by policymakers and professionals. The new methods and tools generated for carrying out such intensive fieldwork (e.g., a method for capturing field notes, large-scale ‘wall-hanging’ capture of images for data analysis) are useful for exploring city users’ everyday practices.

548810.label: Project Title(Chinese)
548810.value: 什么是价格稳健性？一个实验分析

548810.label: Project Objectives
548810.value: All our objectives pertain to a comparative analysis of four accounting regimes: liquidity, symmetric informativeness, conservatism and aggressive. Objective 1: Determine the comparative effects of the four accounting regimes on stock price volatility Objective 2: Determine the comparative effects of the four accounting regimes on the deviation of stock price from its fundamental value Objective 3: Determine the comparative effects of the four accounting regimes on bid-ask spreads Objective 4: Determine the comparative effects of the four accounting regimes on trading volume Objective 5: Determine the effect of risk aversion and other characteristics on an individual’s trading behavior

548810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
548810.value: Conservative accounting refers to an early recognition of expected losses but deferred recognition of realized gains. Although conservatism has existed for over five centuries, it has recently become an important area of inquiry because of its potential effect on asset prices in the capital market. It is not clear why asymmetric conservatism should be superior to immediate recognition of both expected losses and gains. Protagonists of efficient markets explain conservatism as a mechanism for disciplining managers whereas behaviorists appeal to an inherently asymmetric investor aversion to disappointments. Archival researchers are hampered in resolving this issue due to the lack of a functioning non-conservative benchmark regime whereas analytical researchers depend on unverifiable assumptions. Alternative benchmark accounting regimes, however, can be simulated in an experimental setting. We therefore propose an experiment to investigate the effects of different reporting regimes on stock prices in a controlled laboratory market with repetitive trading. In particular, we compare four regimes in which the periodic earnings are reported in the following ways: (i) current income (liquidity regime); (ii) the average of current income and subsequent period’s expected income (symmetric information regime); (iii) the average of current and subsequent period’s expected income if the subsequent period’s expected income is less than the current income or else the current income (asymmetric conservatism regime); and (iv) the average of current and subsequent period’s expected income if the subsequent period’s expected income is higher than the current income or else the current income (asymmetric aggressiveness regime). All the participants start with equal endowments of cash and the shares in a firm. They are aware of the reporting regime they are in, and receive the earnings report at the beginning of each trading period and engage in trading in a dynamic “virtual” market. They are compensated an amount that is proportional to the sum of their accumulated trading profits, cash holdings and terminal value (computed as the last period income divided by the risk free rate) for the stocks they hold at the end of the experimental session. We examine the comparative effects of the reporting regimes on stock price characteristics such as its deviation from the fundamental value, stock price volatility, bid-ask spread and trading volume. While these results could be interesting per se, they also allow us to ascertain whether a behavioral explanation is essential to explain conservatism. 会计的稳健性是指及时确认预期的损失但是推迟确认预期的收益。尽管会计的稳健性已经存在了50多年，但是直到最近，它才因其在资本市场对资产定价的潜在影响而成为重要的研究领域。目前尚不清楚为什么这种非对称的会计谨慎性应优于对预期收益和损失同时立即确认的会计方法。市场有效的倡导者将会计稳健性解释成约束管理者的一种机制，而行为主义者则呼吁，厌恶失望是投资者的内在特性。由于缺乏可行的非稳健性的会计基准制度，文献研究者无法解决有关会计稳健性的争议问题，而实证分析研究者则依靠无法证实的假设条件试图去解决这个问题。然而，我们可以在实验的情境下模拟出一个替代的基准会计制度。 我们拟在一个可控的重复交易的实验市场中，检验不同报告制度对股票价格的影响。特别地，我们将比较下列四种会计制度，每种制度下，各期会计收益的报告方式如下： （1）当期收益 （流动性制度） （2）当期收益和下一期预期收益的平均值 （信息对称制度） （3）当下一期预期收益小于当期收益时，取二者的平均值作为当期的报告收益；当下一期预期收益大于或等于当期收益时，以当期收益作为当期的报告收益 （非对称的谨慎型制度） （4）当下一期预期收益大于当期收益时，取二者的平均值作为当期的报告收益；当下一期预期收益小于或等于当期收益时，以当期收益作为当期的报告收益 （非对称的激进型制度） 公司的所有参与者在最初时都被赋予同等的现金和股权。他们都知道所在公司的报告制度，并且能在每个交易期间开始前获得收益报告，他们也可以在这个动态的“虚拟”市场中自由进行交易。他们的薪酬与累计交易利润，现金持有量以及实验结束时所持股票的最终价值成正比。其中，股票的最终价值等于最后一期的收益除以无风险利率。 我们检验和比较了不同报告制度对股票价格特性的影响，如股价与基本价值的偏离程度，股票价格的波动程度，买卖价差和交易量。这些结果不仅有趣，也让我们确定了行为主义在解释会计谨慎性的问题上至关重要。

548810.label: Realisation of objectives
548810.value: As we reported in the prior interim reports, we find in all the four reporting regimes, traders appear to be momentum traders and prices deviate from fundamental values. We do not find as we originally proposed conservatism reporting regime curbs the deviations and results in lowest price bubble and volatility. Therefore, we revised our theory and identified a cognitive bias that is a tendency for human being to be overly optimistic when forecasting future events. We use the optimism bias to explain the findings. Specifically, due to the partially recognition of future cash flow news in the reported earnings, especially, only 'bad news' is recognized (as called 'conservatism' in the proposal) , subjects tend to overestimate the extent of good news that is masked by this recognition regime, causing greater price bubbles. We provide evidence support such theory. However, we do not find discernible patterns on the bid-ask spreads or trading volume or earnings response coefficients. We also show that the stock price behavior is consistent with the weights subjects claimed to have placed on past price or reported earnings signals in their trading decisions. Such evidence corroborates with what we observe in their actual trading behavior.

548810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
548810.value: In this paper, we use an experimental approach to examine the effect of reporting regimes on asset prices. The reporting regimes are differentiated based on the recognition of expected future cash flows in the current earnings. We examine four different reporting regimes: the No Recognition regime (NR) where no expected future cash flows are recognized; the Full Recognition regime (FR) where both the expected good news and expected bad news pertaining to the next period cash flows are recognized in current earnings; the Good news Recognition regime (GR) where only the expected good news pertaining to the next period cash flows are recognized in current earnings; and the Bad news Recognition regime (BR) where only the expected bad news pertaining to the next period cash flows are recognized in current earnings. We find that the NR, BR and GR regimes are associated with more intense asset price bubbles than the FR regime. We also find that between the BR and GR regimes, the BR regime is associated with more intense asset price bubbles than the GR regime. We attribute this latter finding to optimism bias among the traders who are overly optimistic when correcting for the negative reporting bias under BR regime. Our findings shed new insights about how biased (non-neutral) reporting regimes could exacerbate behavioral biases in the stock market, and can inform the debate on neutral vs. conservative accounting principles.

549210.label: Project Title(Chinese)
549210.value: 公司特征强度对研发联盟的动态网络和创新实力的影响

549210.label: Project Objectives
549210.value: To examine how social identities affects network dynamics To explore the boundary conditions of the linkage between social identities and network dynamics To investigate how social identities affect firm innovation performance through the mediating role of network dynamics

549210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
549210.value: Although recent studies on identity have examined the impact of identities on social actors’ behaviors and outcomes, sufficient attention has not been paid to the influences of a firm’s identity on a firm’s network dynamics and, in turn, on innovation performance. This study investigates how the strength of a firm’s identity (indicated by identity focus and coherence) can influence how others perceive the firm as a legitimate partner, resulting in changes in the firm’s structural position in its R&D alliance networks, and on the firm’s innovation performance, in the the US biotech industry from 1990 to 2008. We understand identity as being constituted of elements from multiple categories, and its overall feature is influenced by both the distribution and the inter-relationship of those categorical elements. How strong an identity is will thus be influenced by two important characteristics: identity focus (whether the multiple elements are distributed among a limited number of categories) and identity coherence (whether the multiple categorical elements are cognitively close to each other). We will explore whether and how identity focus and coherence influence network dynamics and consequently firm innovation performance. We will examine the dynamics of network centrality and structural holes. We expect that the influence of identity strength will vary for the two network characteristics. Specifically, while a stronger identity will allow a firm to occupy a more central position in its interfirm network, the strong identity will allow the firm to bridge fewer structural holes. Two important moderators will be further identified: the firm’s status and the cohesive level of the network where the firm is embedded. As a high-status actor will be less subject to conformity pressure, status will weaken the relationships between identities and network dynamics. Network cohesion will weaken the main relationships as the signaling role of identity may decrease in a cohesive network. This project will be then extended to the impact of identity strength on firm innovation performance (indicated by both the volume and the quality of innovation activities), based on the mediating role played by network dynamics. 虽然最新研究审查了特征对社会个体行为和结果的影响，但是企业特征对公司的动态网络，也就是，创新实力的影响研究却没有得到足够的重视。本篇文章以1990年至2008年的美国生物技术产业为例，探究了一个公司特征（特性的焦点和一致性）如何影响别人对自身合法合作关系的看待，从而改变公司研发联盟网络和创新实力的结构。我们知道特征由多层元素组成，其整体性受这些元素分布和相互间关系的影响。判断一个特征的强度由两个重要因素组成：特征的焦点（这些多层元素是否分布在有限的层次中）和特征的一致性（这些多层元素是否相互识别）。我们将研究特征的焦点和一致性是否和如何影响动态网络，从而进一步改变公司的创新能力。我们将目光集中在动态网络的中心和结构突破口。我们预测特征的强度会造成两个不同的网络特性。具体来说，较强的特征将会使公司在其内部网络更加集中，同时缩短结构层次间的距离。两个重要的调节因素---公司的地位和嵌入公司的网络凝聚力，将会进行更深入的判断识别。作为一个高地位的社会个体，其一般受到较少的从众压力，其地位也会削弱自身特征和动态网络之间的关系。当特征信号在网络中减弱时，网络的凝聚力也会削弱这种关系。本文章以动态网络的调节性能为基础，进一步探讨特征强度对公司创新能力（以创新活动的数量和质量为标准）的影响。

549210.label: Realisation of objectives
549210.value: The three objectives listed in the original have been successfully achieved. Based on the proposal, we have collected data, conducted analyses, and generated both conceptual and empirical manuscripts. We presented our research in international conferences, including Academy of Management Annual Conferences and Strategic Management Society Annual conferences. Part of our findings have been published in decent international journals, including Strategic Management Journal, Journal of Management, and Strategic Organization. The data collected for this particular project can also be utilized for other on-going follow-up research projects. The key findings from this project have important implications for management practice. I have successfully applied some insights from our research in my executive teaching experiences.

549210.label: Major findings and research outcome
549210.value: In one study generated from this project, we demonstrate that a firm's identity, indicated by the quality of the firm’s board interlocks and the firm’s innovation can serve as signals of its quality as a research and development alliance partner to other firms. The extent of the signaling effects, however, varies under different types of uncertainty. Using research and development alliance, patent and board interlock data from the US biotechnology industry during the period 1990–2003, we find that the board interlock quality as well as the strength and focus of a firm’s inventive capabilities have positive and significant effects on the likelihood of research and development alliance formation. Importantly, we further find that the impact of the strength of a firm’s inventive capabilities is weaker, while the impact of the quality of the firm’s board interlocks is stronger, under both market uncertainty and firm-specific uncertainty. The implications for studies of board interlocks, uncertainty, and research and development alliances are discussed. In another study from this project, we show that firms' identities embedded in networks having denser clustering and shorter path lengths at founding are subsequently more inclined toward exploratory learning. We also demonstrate that subsequent network positions (closeness centrality and structural holes) strengthen the initial small world network imprinting effect. Results based on a sample of US venture capital firms from 1995 to 2003 largely support our hypotheses. Contributions to imprinting theory, the organizational learning literature, and inter-firm network studies are discussed.

549210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
549210.value: Based on the data collected for this project and the key findings so far we obtained, we can move on with some follow-up investigation, such as how a firm's identity strength may influence the firm's innovation performance in a highly uncertain environment. In addition, how will the firm's internal condition, such as resource endowment and slack, may moderate the main-effect relationship. As another research stream, we can also explore how a firm's identity indicated by its network position can interact with the firm's competitive action to affect the firm's innovation performance.

549210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
549210.value: Our findings provide evidence on how firms can manage their identities through the practice of board interlocks which may help make inferences about the focal firm’s quality as an R&D alliance partner and how such a signaling effect may change in light of other signals such as innovation performance from the firm under market and firm-specific uncertainty. The implication may include, for instance, firms in general are more likely to form R&D alliances with firms with higher board interlock quality and stronger as well as more focused inventive capabilities. Firms tend to rely more on cues regarding the focal firm’s interlock quality and less on cues regarding its inventive capability when either market uncertainty or firm specific uncertainty is high. The value of the technological capability becomes highly ambiguous and the cost of verifying this value rises under higher levels of uncertainty.

549310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
549310.value: Cantonese is normally regarded as a language that has an unusually rich repertoire of postverbal elements, many of which cannot be found in Mandarin. The question arises as to the syntactic representation of these functional categories and their preverbal counterparts in clausal structure. This project focuses on the syntax of functional categories in Cantonese, concentrating on the discontinuous constructions of functional categories and their dialectal variation under a parametric framework. In this proposed project, I will investigate systematically how a postverbal element in the discontinuous construction interacts with its preverbal counterpart. The descriptive results can be used as a database for future research in Chinese grammar and Chinese dialectology. To account for the empirical findings observed, this project will formulate a syntactic theory of the discontinuous constructions in Cantonese, and identify parameters from which the dialectal variation emerges. The theoretical part of the project will provide a theory of the discontinuous constructions in Cantonese that is grounded on comparative dialectal consideration. The vision behind this proposal is that the differences between Cantonese and Mandarin with respect to the discontinuous constructions can be all traced back to some 'micro-parameters' that will have predictable consequences in a number of constructions in these two dialects. This is a task that has not been taken before. The results are expected to help in fine-tuning the grammatical knowledge of the discontinuous constructions and to enable us to open up a new horizon in the study of functional categories in Chinese at large, resolving some longstanding disputes and controversies surrounding their syntactic nature in Chinese. It is also hoped that the project could provide a perspective from Chinese dialectal grammar on the understanding of the peripheral positions of a sentence in human language, shedding light on the studies of language acquisition and facilitating language learning of Cantonese and Mandarin/standard Chinese. 粵語擁有比較豐富的後置虛詞成分，出現在動詞之後，而這些後置的虛詞往往不見於普通話語法。我們甚至可以在同一個句子裏為粵語後置虛詞找到相應的前置成分，它們兩者表達相似的意思，形成所謂「框式結構」。尤其可見，如何通過句法學的方式表達它們之間的關係饒有意思。本研究的焦點集中在粵語虛詞的句法分析，尤其是著重從參數理論的角度分析框式結構和它們在漢語方言的差異等問題，系統地調查在粵語框式結構中後置虛詞和前置成分的互動關係。我們所描述的現象可以為日後漢語語法學和漢語方言學研究提供語料的參考。基於所描述的語言現象，我們為粵語框式結構提出句法學的理論分析，並且嘗試從「微觀」的參數解釋粵普的語法差異，找出造成方言語法差異的參數。我們期望本研究的發現將會對漢語虛詞的研究提供一個新的分析角度，解決文獻上一些爭論已久的語法問題。我們也希望通過粵語框式結構的研究讓我們對人類語言句子的邊緣位置有更深入的認識，對粵普學習的研究有一定的啟示作用。

549310.label: Realisation of objectives
549310.value: The discontinuous construction is composed of a preverbal element (such as adverbs) and a postverbal element (such as sentence-final particles or verbal suffixes). In this research project, at least sixty patterns of the discontinuous constructions have been successfully identified. Their grammatical features have been discussed and analyzed. There are more than thirty patterns that are headed by the sentence-final particles and nearly thirty that are headed by the verbal suffixes. This is the first attempt to describe the overall picture of the discontinuous constructions in Cantonese. The descriptive properties of the discontinuous constructions are thoroughly presented in an introductory chapter in a handbook of Chinese linguistics (published by John Wiley & Sons, Inc. in 2014) and a chapter of a reference grammar book of Cantonese (to be published by the Commercial Press) to make them known to more readers and laymen who are interested in Cantonese and general linguistics. To account for the empirical properties of the discontinuous constructions, a formal analysis has been proposed under the cartographic approach. It is argued that the postverbal elements are heads, forming a functional projection in syntax. The distribution of the preverbal elements is subject to locality, in a sense that the preverbal elements and the postverbal elements should be projected within the same clause. Theoretical analyses of the verbal suffixes, sentence-final particles, and other postverbal elements are presented in a number of journal articles and book chapters written by the PI and in a doctoral dissertation supervised by the PI. Cantonese and Mandarin are different with respect to the existence of the discontinuous construction. It is proposed that the lack of the discontinuous constructions is mainly due to the impoverished system of postverbal elements in Mandarin in general.

549310.label: Major findings and research outcome
549310.value: In this research project, at least sixty patterns of the discontinuous constructions have been successfully identified. There are more than thirty patterns that are headed by the sentence-final particles and nearly thirty that are headed by the verbal suffixes. In terms of their semantics, seven types of the discontinuous constructions headed by the sentence-final particles are classified, namely, eventive, temporal, focus, modality, interrogative, imperative, and mood while six types of those headed by the verbal suffixes are classified, namely, aspectual, eventive, degree, telic, quantification, and modality. To account for the empirical properties of the discontinuous constructions, a formal analysis has been proposed under the cartographic approach. It is argued that the postverbal elements are heads, forming a functional projection in syntax. The distribution of the preverbal elements is subject to locality, in a sense that the preverbal elements and the postverbal elements should be projected within the same clause. It is likely that the preverbal elements are adjoined to the projection headed by the same type of postverbal elements. The discontinuous constructions associated with the speech act domain could be projected in a very high position in the clause, perhaps in a layer that connects the core syntax and the pragmatic component. In recent presentations by the PI, it was further proposed that sentence-final particles are phrases or the residues of elided phrases that are conjoined with the main clause, forming a coordinate structure. Preverbal elements of the discontinuous constructions would then be regarded as adjuncts to the coordinate structure. If this new approach is correct, there should be unexpected theoretical implications along these lines. Regarding the dialectal variations, it is proposed that the lack of the discontinuous constructions in the dialects like the northern Mandarin is mainly due to their impoverished system of postverbal elements in general. Similar functions of the sentence-final particles in the discontinuous constructions in Cantonese would largely be realized as intonation in languages like Mandarin and English. Findings of this research project will open a new horizon of understanding the interaction between intonation and preverbal elements like adverbs in natural languages.

549310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
549310.value: Postverbal elements such as sentence-final particles have been examined in detail in this research project. It is challenging if the present analyses could be extended to exclamatives, a subtype of preverbal elements that receive less attention in the literature. The role that intonation plays in the discontinuous constructions would be a new issue that can be worked on particularly in the study of the syntax-phonology interface.

549310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
549310.value: The discontinuous constructions are composed of a preverbal element (such as adverbs) and a postverbal element (such as sentence-final particles or verbal suffixes) on the surface. They are uniquely productive in Cantonese and are not easily found in other Chinese dialects like northern Mandarin. In this research project, at least sixty patterns of the discontinuous constructions have been successfully identified and organized. To account for their empirical properties, a formal analysis has been proposed under the cartographic approach. The descriptive findings of this study definitely shed light on Cantonese grammar and the syntax of natural language in general.

549610.label: Project Title(Chinese)
549610.value: 海外上市对本土市场的影響

549610.label: Project Objectives
549610.value: To see how opening up a stock market (i.e. Hong Kong market) for foreign listing (i.e. China H-shares and redchips) will affect (HK) market growth capital flow, market turnover, and market volatility. To see if opening up a stock market for foreign listing will affect the (HK) market quality in terms of the trading volume, the liquidity, and the bid-ask spread of the local (HK) stocks through either a substitution effect or a complimentary effect. To see how opening up a stock market for foreign listing will affect the information efficiency of the host (HK) market in the following aspects: 1.the host (HK) market synchronicity; 2.the investment sensitivity of the domestic (HK) stocks; 3.the amount of future earnings content incorporated in the current share prices of the domestic (HK) stocks; and 4.the extent of mispricing of the domestic (HK) stocks

549610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
549610.value: Cross-listing studies typically look at how cross-listings affect these firms and their own home markets. Rarely are there studies that examine how such listings affect the host market (i.e., the cross-listed market). We argue that this unexplored area is important and worth investigating. In today’s globalized economy, international capital flows become increasingly frequent and important. Many stock exchanges, large and small, are competing with each other to attract foreign firms to list there. When the number of international stocks cross-listed in a country’s market becomes “large” relative to the country’s own market, cross-listing activities to the host stock market will become a nontrivial issue. The Hong Kong stock market housed with numerous, large Chinese stocks in the form of H-share and Redchips (refer as “China listing” hereafter) provides a natural setting for a systematic investigation on this issue. Specifically, we aim to examine the impacts of the listing of mainland Chinese stocks in Hong Kong on the quality and the development of the Hong Kong equity market. Our study is related to but different from the capital market liberalization literature and the stock investability literature. The former studies the effects on the economy when an emerging market opens up its financial market to international capital. The latter studies look at the effect on individual stocks when an emerging market opens up some of its stocks to international equity capital. Our investigation examines instead the effects on the quality of the host market and its listed stocks as a whole when a relatively small economy opens up its stock market for international listing. Our study hence contributes to the international finance literature by exploring an area not studied before. Other than filling up the void in the international finance literature, our study also has practical relevance and policy implications. Both the Hong Kong government and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong have put a lot of efforts and are quite successful in attracting foreign (mainly mainland Chinese) companies listed in Hong Kong. Important as it is, there has not yet been a systematic and rigorous study on the pros and cons, benefits and problems of such overseas listings on Hong Kong’s domestic stock market. This is what we want to shed light on in this project.

549610.value: All project objectives are achieved except that we did not work on Objective 3.3 and 3.4 because the paper is already quite long and the two "sub-objectives" are only tangential to the main objective of the project.

549610.label: Major findings and research outcome
549610.value: At the macro-level, we find that the increasing presence of mainland Chinese stocks in Hong Kong increases the size, trading volume, and its link wit h the China and world markets but reduces the over all volatility of the Hong Kong stock market. At the firm level, the increase affects the market quality, resulting in lower turnover rate, higher Amihud illiquidi ty ratio, and higher spread for non-mainland Chinese firms. Furthermore, such an increase in presence causes Hong Kong stocks to move in a more synchronized way and reduces these firms investment sensitivity to stock price movement, implying deterioration in the information environment. As a whole, the increasing presence of Chinese companies in Hong Kong brings benefits to the Hong Kong market, yet not without cost.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
549610.value: We study the impact of mainland Chinese listings in Hong Kong on the quality and development of the Hong Kong equity market. In aggregate, the increasing presence of mainland Chinese stocks in Hong Kong increases the size, trading volume, and its link with the China and world markets but reduces the over all volatility of the Hong Kong stock market. For individual stocks on average, the increasing presence of mainland Chinese stocks in Hong Kong reduces the turnover rate, the liquidity, and widens the price spread for non-mainland Chinese firms. Furthermore, Hong Kong stocks tend to move more together and these firms' investment becomes less sensitive to stock price movement. In general, it implies a deterioration in the information environment. As a whole, the increasing presence of Chinese companies in Hong Kong brings benefits to the Hong Kong market, yet not without cost.

550010.value: Build and empirically validate and theoretically integrated model examining the environmental governance mechanisms that can be employed by retailers to instill comment from Chinese manufacturers to implement environmental management practices. 550010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
550010.value: The urgency of combating climate change and conserving the environment has been recognized and has been devoted as one of the key issues in the agenda of the recent United Nations General Assembly 2009 by world leaders. In line with this, there has been rising customer expectation on environmental protection. A study indicated that 87% of customers will accuse or even boycott retailers lacking social responsibility if the upstream apparel manufacturers are convicted of causing environmental damage [15]. Increasingly, apparel retailers are hesitant to source from Chinese garment manufacturers despite their low-priced apparel merchandise. The apparel manufacturing industry in China is notorious for discharging polluted wastewater directly into rivers as well as disposing of untreated toxics to landfill. These environmentally irresponsible conducts have resulted in serious life-threatening social as well as environmental consequences, ranging from acid rain and land desertization to birth defects and premature death, while causing bad reputation to their downstream retailers. Although the importance for Chinese apparel manufacturers to embrace environmental management practices (EMP) is well-acknowledged, retailers seem to lack control over these practices by their upstream manufacturers and access to the accompanying data [10]. There is a dearth of study investigating how retailers can govern their upstream Chinese apparel manufacturers on environmental protection spanning procurement, production, and distribution. Specifically, retailers are uncertain the effect of environmental governance structure that can commit their Chinese manufacturers to environmental protection. Environmental governance structure for improving the environmental performance of apparel retailers is inherently complex with many relational, institutional, as well as transactional aspects involved. Such complexity is obvious because apparel retailers and Chinese apparel manufacturers often experience different institutional pressures due to local environmental regulatory, cultural, competition, and stakeholder expectations. We propose to develop and empirically validate a theoretical model integrating the desirable environmental governance mechanisms from three theoretical perspectives, namely social embeddedness, institutional, and transaction cost economics, acknowledging the complexity on the design of an environmental governance structure. This proposed study will benefit apparel retailers by improving their apparel merchandising in China on both environmental and economic aspects. 顧客對於環境保護的期望不斷上升。研究指出約百分之八十七的顧客向零售商作出指責甚至抵制因其服裝製造商對環境造成破壞 [20]。儘管中國服裝製造商的服裝商品價格低廉，越來越多的服裝零售商都不願意從他們購入產品。有關污染廢水直接排放到河流和棄置未經處理的有毒物質於垃圾填埋地的活動 ，使中國服裝製造業的聲名狼藉。這些不負責任行為對環境造成嚴重的社會威脅和環境後果，包括酸雨和土地沙漠化，甚至出生缺陷和過早死亡。雖然中國服裝製造商對提議環境管理活動(EMP)的重要性是被認同的，但零售商缺乏就原材料製造商有關做法作出控制及評估[12]。他們不肯定EMP是否能使中國製造商對環境保護作出承擔。中國服裝零售商和製造商經常因當地的環境管理、文化和利益相關者的期望而遇到不同體制壓力。我們建議驗證一個綜合三種理論觀點的環境管理機制以確認其設計的複雜性。這個研究將有利於改善服裝零售商的於中國銷售服裝商品所遇上環境和經濟方面的問題。

Objective #2 on the performance implications of suppliers’ environmental management practices is achieved in paper entitled “Green operations and the moderating role of environmental management capability of suppliers on manufacturing firm performance” (Output #3). 550010.label: Major findings and research outcome
550010.value: Recognizing the important role of suppliers in affecting the environmental performance of firms, the findings of this project provides insights into three key aspects. First, the moderating role of environmental management capabilities of suppliers on the performance results of product and process stewardship of firms is empirically proven (Output #3). The paper provides empirical evidence on the performance outcomes of firms collaborating with suppliers with different levels of environmental management capability. Second, the importance of sharing information with supply chain partners through information integration is found (Output #1 and #4). The sharing of information with supply chain partners contributes to environmental management adaptability and innovativeness, which allow firms to cope with the heightening and ever changing environmental regulations. Lastly, the findings of this project indicate that firms cannot rely solely on their own to drive their suppliers in emerging countries to be environmentally responsible in their operations. Environmental regulations also play an important role in driving the suppliers to adopt environmental management practices (Output #3).

550010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
550010.value: This research study has great potential for further development. While the research findings provide theoretical and managerial insights into environmental governance with a focus on the role of suppliers (i.e., Chinese manufacturers) may affect the environmental performance outcomes of firms, future research can be conducted to examine the roles of other stakeholder (e.g., customers, government agency) in environmental management practices. Future research may also be conducted in other emerging countries and developing countries to gain further understanding on how supply chain structure and local regulations may affect the implementation of environmental management practices. This study also provides a foundation for future research in environmental governance by highlighting the importance of information integration in supply chain. Future research may examine what are the optimal information integration structure would lead to desirable environmental performance of a supply chain.

550010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
550010.value: The project findings provide empirical evidence of the environmental governance structure that facilitate environmental management practices of firms to improve environmental performance. Information integration with supply chain partners is an important factor in allow firms to be adaptive and innovative in developing and implementing environmental management practices to achieve performance. Environmental management capability of suppliers is also an important factor to be considered in supplier selection and management. It affects the results of firms in achieving desirable environmental performance. Also, the project findings indicate the importance of local environmental regulations in affecting the performance results of suppliers.

550110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
550110.value: 关于原始设备生产商(OEM)和其具有竞争性的合同承包制造商(CM)之间的市场领导地位的研究

550110.label: Project Objectives
550110.value: Set up competition models in both Cournot and Bertrand settings. Study both simultaneous game and sequential game in each setting. Understand how the product substitution rate affects the OEM’s outsourcing production decision as well as the CM’s production decision. Investigate how the OEM’s outsourcing decision, the unit wholesale price paid to the CM for contract manufacturing, the product substitutability between the OEM and CM’s products and the consumer market size interact and affect the CM’s ability to enter the direct sales channel. Explore the endogenized leadership between the OEM and its competitive CM. If both the OEM and its competitive CM prefer leadership or followership, the game becomes a simultaneous Cournot/Bertrand competition; otherwise, it is a sequential Stackelberg competition where the OEM or the CM takes the leadership. The project will identify the equilibrium outcome of this leader-follower position taken by the OEM and the CM under both price and quantity competition settings. Apply the Pareto and risk dominance selection criteria to study the situations where there coexist two leadership equilibria, and identify which leadership equilibrium will risk-dominate the other and be preferred by the OEM and the competitive CM. Based on the above analysis, provide advice and suggestions to industrial practitioners on outsourcing manufacturing to a competitive CM.

550110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
550110.value: Nowadays, in many industries, the original equipment manufacturers(OEMs) outsources their entire manufacturing of their products to contract manufacturers (CMs). Meanwhile, by handling the production for the OEM, the CMs improve their capabilities such as quality evaluation, production control, and even product design. Some CMs even expanded into direct sales of its own-branded products, which are similar to those of the OEMs. In this project, we explore an outsourcing supply chain in which the contract manufacturer of the OEM is not only a upstream partner but also a downstream competitor of the OEM. That is, the CM produces and sells its own-brand products (“knockoffs”) which are substitutable to those of the OEM. Then we investigate the issue of whether the OEM shall take the market leadership or not under both quantity (Cournot) and price (Bertrand) competition setting. Under both quantity- and price- competition models, the OEM and the competitive CM can move either simultaneously or sequentially. For the sequential move setting, we will consider both cases where the OEM is the leader (such as Hewlett Packard) and the CM is the follower, and where the CM is the leader (such as Flextronics) and the OEM is the follower. Then we want to find out that under both models, whether there exists the fist-mover advantage as well as second-mover advantage for the OEM. We also explore how the wholesale price, the product substitution rate and the production percentage that the OEM outsources to the competitive CM play a role in whether the OEM will take the market leadership and move first. 今天在许多行业,原始设备生产商都把产品的制造功能外包给合同承包制造商.与此同时,通过为原始设备生产商生产产品,有的合同承包制造商提高了它们的生产,设计以及质量控制能力,从而能够生产自己品牌的产品.它们的自我品牌与原始设备生产商的产品常常具有可替代性.我们把这种合同承包制造商称为具有竞争性的合同承包制造商.在这个研究项目中, 我们将探讨原始设备生产商的产品和其具有竞争性的合同承包制造商的产品如何在市场中竞争.我们将用古诺摸型和伯特兰德模型来研究它们谁愿意做市场的领导者.我们还会探讨原始设备生产商的外协决策如何影响其在市场中的领导地位.

550110.label: Major findings and research outcome
550110.value: Under a Cournot (quantity) competition setting, we show that when the outsourcing quantity and wholesale price are exogenously given, either party (the OEM or the CM) may prefer Stackelberg leadership or followership. For example, when the wholesale price or the proportion of production outsourced to the CM is lower than a threshold value, both parties prefer Stackelberg leadership and, consequently, play a simultaneous game in the consumer market. When the outsourcing quantity and wholesale price are decision variables, the competitive CM sets a wholesale price sufficiently low to allow both parties to coexist in the market, and the OEM outsources its entire production to this CM. We also examines the impact of the supply chain parties' bargaining power on contract outcomes by considering a wholesale price that is determined via the generalized Nash bargaining scheme, finding a Stackelberg equilibrium to be sustained when the CM's degree of bargaining power is great and the non-competitive CM's wholesale price is high. Under a Bertrand (price) competition setting, we consider the competitive CM is an original design manufacturer (ODM). We study two market environments: the ODM market and the OEM market. For the ODM market, we show that a sequential pricing game is played between the OEM and its ODM, and moreover, the equilibrium that the OEM prices early risk dominates the one that the ODM prices early. Nevertheless, for the OEM market, the simultaneous pricing game and the sequential pricing game can both arise and be sustained. We also demonstrate that it is in their mutual interest to choose to be friends instead of foes.

550110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
550110.value: Our research shows that once the CM has the capability producing the self-branded product, the OEM actually loses some of its competitive advantage. Due to the special technology/skills that the CM has accumulated over the course of contract manufacturing, often it is difficult for the OEM to replace the competitive CM. This brings us to think another important issue for the OEM, that is, which value-chain functions to outsource and which types of CM to choose. Such decision involves consideration of multiple factors, such as IP leakage, potential competition from the CM, the product cost structure, tax issues, the lead-time for new product development and inventory liabilities. Our current study focuses on the issue of competition and cooperation between an OEM and a CM. It would be interesting in future research to consider a richer model in which some of these other factors are included.

550110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
550110.value: Our study results show that when a competitive CM is able to obtain a reasonable level of profit from contract manufacturing, it has little incentive to develop self-branded products, mitigating the intensity of the competition between it and the OEM. This thus provides another angle from which to view the relationship between OEMs and competitive CMs. This indicates that when the OEM outsources to the CM and engages in price negotiation, a reasonable profit margin shall be allocated to the CM; thus, the CM has less incentive to become the potential competitor of its OEM in the downstream market. Our study also shows that the number of CMs in the upstream supply market affects the price and the competition game between the OEM and its competitive CM. This also indicates that the industry structure and the level of entry barrier have a high impact on the relationship between the OEM and the CM.

A Rational Expectations Approach to Macroeconometrics: Testing Policy Effectiveness and Efficient Market Models]的理性預期研究框架。根據這一框架，我們將會考察非標準審計意見對客戶企業未來財務狀况惡化是否有預測能力，幷檢驗此預測能力與由股票價格行爲推斷出的市場對信息之實際運用是否相符。現有文獻中尚未有此類證據，但此類證據有助于我們評估市場對審計報告之信息含量使用的有效程度。

550910.label: Realisation of objectives
550910.value: All four research objectives have been satisfactorily achieved. To answer the research questions set in our research objectives, we manually collect audit opinion data for the sample period of 1995-2010 and classify modified audit opinions (MAOs) into two categories: GAAP/DISC, i.e., modifications due to the violations of GAAP/disclosure rules, and GC, i.e., modifications due to going-concerns. Overall, the empirical results are pretty strong and adequate to answer our research questions. In addition to the four research objectives originally set in the proposal, we have added a new one during the course of our research. Specifically, we investigate why stocks of MAO firms are mispriced. We hypothesize that MAO and non-MAO firms have distinct “mean-reversion” patterns in financial performance, i.e., it takes longer time for MAO firms to recover from poor performance than comparable firms with clean audit opinions. This difference reflects auditors’ information advantage in assessing clients’ prospects. To the extent that investors fail to recognize this regularity, they may apply non-MAO firms’ reversion rate to MAO firms in forecasting future performance. Such an extrapolation tendency helps to explain why investors over-estimate MAO firms’ future performance and thus over-value MAO stocks. The empirical results also support this new hypothesis. To our knowledge, this finding is new in the literature on the pricing of audit-related information. It also enhances our understanding of investors’ behavior in using financial statement information for valuation.
