rows: To identify the causal role of muscle apoptosis cell death in deep pressure ulcer by examining the effect of apoptosis inhibition on muscle pathology as induced in an established pressure ulcer experimental model.

563210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
563210.value: Pressure ulcer, also named pressure sore, bedsore or decubitus ulcer, is defined as the localized breakdown of soft tissues caused by sustained, unrelieved mechanical pressure. Pressure ulcer represents a considerable healthcare problem which poses significant burdens on patients and caregivers. Deep pressure ulcer, a characterized form of pressure ulcer, is of considerable clinical concern because it results in extremely uncertain prognosis and makes the subsequent treatment very ineffective. Although the clinical importance of deep ulcer has been advocated by the US National Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel (NPUAP), there is no effective treatment available for deep pressure ulcer. The preclusion of the development of novel treatment is primarily due to the lacking of knowledge on the underlying mechanism of deep ulcer. Research has revealed the extrinsic factors of pressure, mechanical insult, and ischemia/reperfusion in the etiology of pressure ulcer. However, the cellular and molecular mechanisms responsible for the development of deep ulcer are not known. Muscle tissue has been suggested to be the initiating site for deep pressure ulcer because of its low tolerance and high susceptibility to respond to external compression. In searching for the molecular target responsible for the development of deep pressure ulcer, we preliminarily demonstrate that muscle apoptosis cell death pathway is activated in a deep pressure ulcer experimental model. Our data further indicate that the activation of apoptotic event occurs prior to the emergence of muscle pathology in response to moderate compression. These preliminary findings support the idea of this proposal hypothesizing that muscle cell death pathway is responsible for the development of deep pressure ulcer. The studies of this proposal are designed to examine the muscle pathology in an established deep pressure ulcer model in which apoptosis will be inhibited. The inhibition of apoptosis will be achieved by adopting multiple approaches including pharmacological inhibitor and genetic deletion. It is our working hypothesis that interference of apoptosis cell death pathway can prevent the pathological development of deep pressure ulcer. Upon completion of the proposed studies, the etiologic role of muscle cell death pathway in deep pressure ulcer will be unraveled and new treatment modalities can be initiated by targeting the muscle cell death pathway. 壓迫性潰瘍，又名褥瘡，壓瘡，是由持續性、非緩解性機械壓力引起的局部軟組織壞死。因給醫患雙方均帶來巨大的負擔，從而成爲一項值得關注的健康護理問題。深部壓迫性潰瘍作爲壓迫性潰瘍的典型表現，由于其預後的難以預測性與後續治療效果的無效性而引起更爲廣泛的臨床關注。盡管美國壓瘡顧問小組(National Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel, NPUAP)申明了防治壓迫性潰瘍的重要臨床意義，但是目前仍沒有有效的治療措施。這主要歸因于缺乏對壓迫性潰瘍的發病機制的了解。已有研究揭示外源性壓迫因素、機械損傷以及缺血/再灌注在壓迫性潰瘍發病機制中的作用。但是，導致其病理性進展的細胞和分子機制仍舊不明。有觀點認爲，由于肌肉組織耐受性低，且對外界壓力高度敏感，故而在深部壓迫性潰瘍的發病中處于首要地位。在探究促進壓迫性潰瘍發病的分子機制的研究中，我們的前期研究結果顯示在深部壓迫性潰瘍的實驗室模型中肌肉細胞凋亡程序受到激活。我們的研究數據進一步顯示，在對中度壓力的反應中凋亡程序的啓動先于肌肉病理變化的發生。這些前期研究結果支持本假說內容，即肌肉細胞凋亡通路在深部壓迫性潰瘍的發病中起決定性作用。本研究擬在現有的深部壓迫性潰瘍模型中探究肌肉細胞凋亡被阻斷的情況下肌肉組織的病理變化。本研究擬通過包括藥理學阻斷劑和基因敲除在內的多重方法達到對肌肉細胞凋亡程序的阻斷，並假設幹擾肌肉細胞凋亡程序可以阻斷深部壓迫性潰瘍的病理進程。上述研究的完成將有助于闡明肌肉細胞凋亡程序在深部壓迫性潰瘍發病中所起的作用，據此可以得到通過靶嚮幹預肌肉細胞凋亡程序來治療壓迫性潰瘍 的新措施。

563210.label: Realisation of objectives
563210.value: The objective of this GRF project was to identify the causal role of muscle apoptosis cell death in deep pressure ulcer by examining the effect of apoptosis inhibition on muscle pathology as induced in an established pressure ulcer experimental model. This project objective has been 100% achieved by successfully completing the two main proposed studies namely the pharmacological caspase inhibitor study and the genetic Bax Bak knockout study. The causal role of systemic apoptosis inhibition in protecting the muscle from compression injury is exhibited in the pharmacological stud. The genetic knockout study further illustrated the specific causal role of skeletal muscle apoptosis in the pathogenesis of compression-induced tissue injury. We did not experience any significant problems throughout the process of the pharmacological study. However, we did encounter considerable problems in the genetic knockout study. As mentioned in our mid-term report, there was a pinworm infection outbreak at the Centralised Animal Facility of PolyU in June 2011. All the Bax Bak offspring produced and the Bax Bak mice purchased from Jackson Lab (USA) were forced to be sacrificed. The Bax Bak mice were re-purchased with the monetary compensation of PolyU but this incident caused a ~6 months delay in the progress of the genetic Bax Bak knockout study. Nonetheless, we had overcome this problem and had successfully completed the study. Another significant problem we have encountered is the problem of unexpected phenotype of the transgenes HSA-rtTA+/+ and TRE-Cre+/+ mice. This strain of Cre mice was originally proposed to be used to crossbreed with the Baxflox/flox Bak-/- mice to generate the HSA-rtTA+/+ TRE-Cre+/+ Baxflox/flox Bak-/- mice in which the deficiency of Bax gene will be achieved by the administration of doxycycline. However, we observed the phenotype of early death (at < 1-month of age) in the HSA-rtTA+/+ TRE-Cre+/+ Baxflox/flox Bak-/- mice that we generated. We suspected that the early death was due to the leakage of the rtTA+/+ TRE-Cre+/+ in the absence of doxycycline administration. To solve the problem, we decided to shift to the system of MerCreMer (i.e., to generate our experimental MerCreMer Baxflox/flox Bak-/- mice by crossbreeding the Baxflox/flox Bak-/- mice with the MerCreMer mice). We successfully produced the MerCreMer Baxflox/flox Bak-/- mice in which the deficiency of Bax is specifically induced in skeletal muscle cells in response to the administration of tamoxifen in addition to the global constitutive deficiency of Bak. By using this tissue-specific conditional double knockout approach, we evidently demonstrated the critical causal role of muscle apoptosis in the compression-induced injury.

563210.label: Major findings and research outcome
563210.value: Pressure ulcer represents a significant health problem as it imposes a heavy burden on sufferers. Most importantly, there are currently no effective therapies for preventing and treating pressure ulcer as the underlying molecular mechanisms of this disorder are largely unknown. This GRF project includes two main studies namely caspase inhibitor study and genetic Bax Bak knockout study. The overall goal of this project was to identify the causal role of muscle apoptosis cell death in deep pressure ulcer by examining the effects of apoptosis inhibition on muscle pathology as induced in an established pressure ulcer experimental model. Both proposed studies have been successfully completed. The caspase inhibitor study has identified the potential causal role of muscle apoptosis cell death in deep pressure ulcer. This study has evidently demonstrated the protective effects of apoptosis inhibition by pharmacological caspase (an essential apoptosis executing enzyme) inhibition on muscle injury induced by our pressure ulcer-mimicking experimental model. This study firstly demonstrated that the pharmacological intervention by blocking caspase activation is effective in alleviating the muscle damage induced by prolonged moderate compression. The findings are of clinical significance as the results suggest that pharmacological regimens targeting caspase/apoptosis inhibition might be of use to treat pressure ulcer. The findings of this caspase inhibitor study have been published in the Journal of Physiology (Impact Factor2011 4.9) with the acknowledgement of the research funding support by GRF RGC. Our next genetic Bax Bak knockout study further demonstrated the specific causal role of muscle apoptosis in the pathogenesis of muscle pathology induced by prolonged moderate compression. We successfully generated MerCreMer Baxflox/flox Bak-/- mice in which the deficiency of Bax (an essential pro-apoptotic gene) is specifically induced in skeletal muscle cells in response to the administration of tamoxifen in addition to the global constitutive deficiency of Bak (another essential pro-apoptotic gene works in a compensatory fashion with Bax). By using this tissue-specific conditional double knockout approach, we evidently demonstrated the critical causal role of muscle apoptosis in the compression-induced injury. The main results of this genetic Bax Bak knockout study are included in this report and the manuscript is in preparation for the submission to scientific journal. The findings of this GRF project were also presented in the following invited talk/keynote lectures: November 2014 (Invited talk) The 5th International Conference on Nutrition and Physical Activity on Aging, Obesity and Cancer (NAPA 2014), Xian, China October 2014 (Invited keynote lecture) 2014 International Conference of Exercise Rehabilitation, Korean Society of Exercise Rehabilitation, Seoul, Korea December 2013 (Invited keynote lecture) 2013 International Conference of Exercise Physiology, Korean Society of Exercise Physiology, Seoul, Korea

563210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
563210.value: The findings of this project overall support the causal role of muscle apoptosis in the pathogenesis of compression-induced tissue injury and pressure ulcer. These results would lead to further investigations in the detailed cellular signaling and molecular mechanisms that are closely related to muscle apoptosis, particularly the Bax Bak and caspase apoptotic signaling pathways in deep pressure ulcer. With these further investigations, it is of hope to fully understand the precise mechanisms of the pathogenesis and development of deep pressure ulcer, which will lead to the development of the novel treatment and prevention regimens for this disorder. Specifically, this project has provided novel data evidently demonstrated that the inhibition of cellular signaling at caspase cascade or pro-apoptotic BCL-2 family protein (Bak and Bak) is effective in protecting muscle from prolonged moderate compression injury. These findings are of important value to support further research to explore potential anti-apoptotic drugs/chemical compounds that can treat or prevent deep pressure ulcer.

563210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
563210.value: Pressure ulcer is defined as the localized breakdown of soft tissues caused by sustained, unrelieved mechanical pressure. Pressure ulcer represents a considerable healthcare problem which poses significant burdens on patients and caregivers. There is no effective treatment available for pressure ulcer. The preclusion of the development of novel treatment is primarily due to the lacking of knowledge on the underlying mechanism of pressure ulcer. In searching for the molecular target responsible for the development of deep pressure ulcer, we have preliminarily demonstrated that muscle apoptosis cell death pathway is activated in a pressure ulcer experimental model. Our data further indicate that the activation of apoptotic event occurs prior to the emergence of muscle pathology in response to moderate compression. The studies of this proposal examined the muscle pathology in an established deep pressure ulcer model in which apoptosis is inhibited. The inhibition of apoptosis achieved by adopting pharmacological inhibitor and genetic deletion consistently demonstrated that interference of apoptosis cell death pathway can prevent the pathological development of deep pressure ulcer. In conclusion, the etiologic role of muscle cell death pathway in deep pressure ulcer is unraveled and new treatment modalities can be initiated by targeting the muscle cell death pathway.

564410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
564410.value: Trypanosoma brucei is a protozoan parasite that causes sleeping sickness in human and Nagana in cattle in southern Africa. T. brucei evades the host immune response by constantly switching its major surface antigen, the Variable Surface Glycoprotein (VSG). The telomere of T. brucei is implicated in this intriguing form of antigenic variation because only one VSG gene out of an archive of over 1000 copies of VSG genes and pseudogenes in the T. brucei genome is expressed from one of ~20 nearly identical transcription units located at the subtelomeric loci. Very recently two telomere-associated proteins in T. brucei have been identified by our collaborator, Dr. Li’s lab, including the TTAGGG Repeat Binding Factor (tbTRF) and the Repressor-activator protein 1 (tbRap1) and shown to be essential for telomere integrity and VSG regulation. Both proteins contain the Myb-type domain that can serve as DNA-binding motif or protein-interacting module. It is not known how the organization of these two proteins on telomere are mediated by their Myb domains, i.e. whether tbTRF and tbRap1 bind to telomeric DNA individually employing their own Myb domain; or tbRap1 is associated with telomere by tethering to the DNA-binding tbTRF. Furthermore it is completely unknown whether loss of DNA-binding as mediated by Myb domain in these two proteins would have any effect on VSG regulation. We propose to address the above questions by carrying out biochemical and structural studies of three Myb-type domains, including the single Myb domain in tbTRF and the tandem Myb and Myb-like domains in tbRap1. Specifically we would first verify the DNA-binding affinity for each Myb domain by in vitro Electrophoretic Mobility Shift Assay (EMSA) and Isothermnal Titration Calorimetry (ITC). Three dimensional structures of these domains will be determined to identify the key residues for telomeric DNA binding; or to delineate structural features incompatible for DNA binding if the Myb-type domain does not interact specifically with duplex telomeric DNA. Lastly Myb domain mutants with weakened or abolished DNA binding capacity will be assessed for their effect on VSG regulation. The outcome of this research will yield valuable information regarding the mechanism of VSG regulation in T. brucei; and provide clues for possible effective treatment to eradicate this parasite. Furthermore it would help our understanding of telomere biology in general. 布氏錐蟲是一種原生動物寄生蟲，主要在南部非洲引起人類的昏睡病和牛类的那加那病。布氏錐蟲通过不斷交換其主要表面抗原，表面糖蛋白變器（VSG）来規避宿主的免疫反應。布氏錐蟲的端粒体与這樣一個有趣的抗原變異形式有关系，因為它的亞端粒体区域含有1000餘份VSG基因和准基因，而每次只有一個VSG基因被调到〜20個轉錄單位中的特定一個单位被轉錄。 最近我們的合作者，李博士的實驗室发现了兩個端粒体相關蛋白，包括TTAGGG重複序列結合因子（tbTRF）和阻遏/激活蛋白1（tbRap1）。这两個蛋白被證明对于端粒完整和VSG調控是必不可少的。這兩種蛋白質均含有MYB型結構域，该結構域可以作為 DNA結合蛋白序列或相互作用的模塊。目前关于tbTRF和 tbRap1這兩種蛋白質如何組織在端粒体上的机理并不清楚。两种可能模式。包括是否tbTRF和tbRap1各自單獨使用自己的MYB型結構域结合到端粒DNA；或tbRap1與端粒的DNA由tbTRF牽引結合有待研究。此外，关于MYB型結構域和端粒的DNA結合对VSG調控有什麼影響是完全不清楚的。 我們计划進行生化和結構研究以解決上述問題。我们将研究三個 Myb型結構域，包括tbTRF Myb型結構域和tbRap1 Myb - Myb like串聯蛋白樣域。具體來說，我們會先通过蛋白電泳遷移率變動分析（EMSA）和等温滴定量熱法（ITC）驗證 每个Myb型結構域与DNA結合的親和力。然后我们计划解析每个Myb型結構域的三維結構，這些结构信息將有助于找出影响端粒DNA結合或者蛋白相互作用的關鍵氨基酸。另外我们会产生一些Myb蛋白域的突變體来削弱或取消它们的DNA結合的能力，并評估其对VSG調控的影響。 本研究的結果將发现与布氏錐蟲抗原變異有價值的信息，以及提供線索找寻可能有效的治療方法，以消除這種寄生蟲。此外，本研究會幫助我們了解端粒体生物學的重要基本原理。

564410.label: Realisation of objectives
564410.value: The project has progressed very well through the 42-month period and it is now completed. We would like to report our activities and results obtained according to the four objectives in the original proposal. Objective 1. Construct optimization for Myb-type domains of tbTRF and tbRap1 This objective has been fully completed at 100%. After extensive screening four optimized constructs have been obtained, including the tbTRF Myb domain, the tbRap1 Myb and Myb-like domain individually plus the fourth construct consisting of tbRap1 Myb and Myb-like domains in tandem. Large amount of purified homogeneous protein for each construct has been obtained to facilitate structural and functional studies. Objective 2. Characterization of DNA binding properties of Myb-type domains in vitro This objective has been fully completed at 100%. In vitro methods of EMSA and ITC have been used to characterize the DNA binding activity of tbTRF and tbRap1 Myb-type domains. The tbTRF Myb domain has been confirmed to bind to both regular (TTAGGG)n telomeric repeats and J-containing (TJAGGG)n repeats with comparable affinity. The tbRap1 Myb domain does not show detectable DNA-binding activity, while the tbRap1 Myb-like domain binds to DNA in non-specific manner. The DNA-binding affinity of the tbRap1 Myb and Myb-like tandem region is not tested but expected to be insignificant based on the results from the individual domains. Objective 3. Structure characterization of the Myb-type domains This objective has been fully completed at 100%. Two structures, i.e. the tbTRF Myb domain and the tbRap1 Myb-like domain, have been determined by NMR. While the tbTRF Myb domain adopts the canonical Myb fold, the tbRap1 Myb-like domain shows an unexpected structure that resembles the RNA Recognition Motif (RRM). The NMR HSQC spectra of tbTRF Myb domain reveal very narrow chemical dispersion pattern that is characteristic of unstructured protein. Structure determination of tbRap1 Myb domain is thus not pursued. Objective 4. Assessment of the functional significance of Myb-type domains in telomere architecture and VSG regulation This objective has been fully completed at 100%. Our structure-based functional studies have focused on tbTRF Myb domain and tbRap1 Myb-like domain. In collaboration with Dr. Bibo Li in Cleveland State University, we have generated a series of tbTRF and tbRap1 mutants with weakened or abolished DNA-binding activity. The impact of such mutations on telomere architecture and VSG regulation has been assessed by in vivo studies such as ChIP and VSG switching assays using mutant T. brucei strains.

564410.label: Major findings and research outcome
564410.value: This project has focused on structural and functional studies of the Myb-type domains in two T. brucei telomeric proteins tbTRF and tbRap1. Our study on tbTRF Myb domain reveals that this region binds specifically to telomeric DNA repeats with regular sequence of (TTAGGG)n or J-containing sequence of (TJAGGG)n. Furthermore the structure of tbTRF Myb domain determined by NMR confirms a canonical helix-turn-helix Myb fold. Mutations of key DNA-binding residues in tbTRF Myb domain weaken or completely abolish its association with telomere but significantly increase VSG switching frequencies, indicating that the telomere DNA binding activity of tbTRF Myb domain is critical for TbTRF’s role in VSG switching regulation. This work has been presented as an invited talk by the PI at an international conference in 2011 (item 9[1] in Research Output). A manuscript reporting this work has been published in Nucleic Acid Research in 2014 (item 8[3] in Research Output). Our study on tbRap1 Myb and Myb-like domains reveal that while the tbRap1 Myb domain is largely unstructured and shows no measurable DNA-binding activity, the tbRap1 Myb-like domain unexpected adopts a structural fold that resembles the RNA Recognition Motif (RRM) although no sequence similarity to RRM could be detected. Furthermore the tbRap1 Myb-like domain shows non-specific interaction with DNA substrates, raising the tempting possibility that the RRM motif could contribute to tbRap1-mediated global suppression on VSG expression by promoting non-specific association of tbRap1 with certain genetic loci. A manuscript reporting this finding is now under preparation (item 8[5] in Research Output). In addition to the T. brucei project the PI and her team have published two papers related to autophagy (item 8[1] and 8[4] in Research Output) and one paper related to antibiotic resistance (item 8[2] in Research Output) within the period of the T. brucei project. Although these papers are not specifically related to T. brucei, they are reported here because they are integral parts of the research program within the PI’s lab and involve the same lab personnel. For example, Dr. Xiaohua Li, the first author of items 8[1] and 8[3] in Research Output, worked on the T. brucei project for her thesis. The training she received from the T. brucei project has been invaluable for her Beclin1 project. Additionally Wu Shuai, a Ph.D. student financially supported by the T. brucei project, worked on both tbTRF protein and the autophagy protein p62, leading to item 8[4] in Research Output.

564410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
564410.value: A novel finding of our study involves the unexpected RNA Recognition Motif (RRM) within the tbRap1 Myb-like domain that was uncovered by our structural studies. RRM is a well-defined structural module that can bind to diverse substrates including single-stranded DNA and RNA molecules as well as protein targets. RRM has been found in many eukaryotic proteins such as the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins (hnRNPs) and proteins that regulate RNA stability and translation. This finding raises the tempting possibility that tbRap1 protein, through its RRM motif within the originally designated Myb-like domain, can associate with a variety of DNA or RNA sites and exert a broader regulatory effect beyond the telomere region of T. brucei. For further development we plan to systematically investigate the binding sites of tbRap1 along the T. brucei chromosomes by whole-genome chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP). In particular we aim to understand the role of RRM in mediating such association by comparing the ChIP association pattern of wild-type tbRap1 and RRM-defective mutants. This work will be done in collaboration with Dr. Bibo Li of Cleveland State University. We plan to apply for future RGC funding for this study after we gather sufficient preliminary data.

564410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
564410.value: Trypanosoma brucei (T. brucei) is a unicellular parasite that causes several infectious diseases including African trypanosomiasis (also known as sleeping sickness) in humans and nagana in animals. Trypanosoma brucei is endemic in sub-Saharan Africa, with up to 450,000 people affected according to the estimation by World Health Organization (WHO). The biggest challenge for African trypanosomiasis therapy is its chronic infection due to antigenic variation. The T. brucei pathogen readily switches the expression of its major surface antigen, Variable Surface Glycoprotein (VSG) to evade the host immune system. Such VSG switching leads to long-term infections and poor prognosis in African trypanosomiasis. Our project focuses on the Myb-type domains of two T. brucei telomeric proteins tbTRF and tbRap1. We have determined the structures of the tbTRF Myb domain and the tbRap1 Myb-like domain respectively. Furthermore our structure-based functional studies have revealed that these two domains have distinct functional roles in VSG regulation. The tbTRF Myb domain specifically binds to telomeric DNA and modulates the VSG switching frequency. The tbRap1 Myb-like domain interacts with DNA in non-specific manner and exerts global suppression on VSG expression. These novel findings can potentially help drug discovery effort to treat African trypanosomiasis in the future.

600110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600110.value: A wide range of intriguing magnetic phenomena that are of fundamental interest and technological importance can occur in nanometer-scale structures due to their small dimensions. Among various possible nanostructures, ultrathin films are model systems for the study of magnetism in reduced dimension. Ultrathin films have attracted significant attention particularly because their magnetic properties can be strongly influenced by the interaction with the supporting substrate. This can occur, for example, through elastic strain, interface anisotropy, or because of the stabilization of unique film structures that do not occur in bulk form. In the proposed research project, we will investigate the growth and magnetic properties of ultrathin Fe films on ordered surface alloys. Practical interest in surface alloys as new materials has been motivated by the fact that their properties can differ substantially from the bulk surfaces of their constituent elements, with attention given overwhelmingly to chemisorption and catalytic behavior in the past. This outlook is encouraged by the prospect of tailoring properties through a careful selection of alloy constituents. Among the numerous surface alloy systems that are known, our investigations will concentrate on the surface-confined c(2×2) ordered alloys that are formed by various noble metals (Cu, Ag, Au, Pt, Pd) on W(100) and Mo(100) refractory metal surfaces. Relevant aspects of electronic structure that affect interface anisotropy through hybridization of electronic states at the interface, namely d-bands at the Fermi level, differ significantly between the noble and refractory metals, and to some extent within the different groups. Therefore, by concentrating on this class of surface alloys, it should be possible to vary interface anisotropy controllably by systematically changing the alloying element and substrate matrix, without otherwise changing other important factors such as elastic strain. The practical effect of these modifications on magnetism will be detected by monitoring macroscopic magnetization behavior. These investigations will be carried out using low energy electron microscopy/diffraction (LEEM/LEED) and spin-polarized LEEM, which are powerful techniques for studying film growth and magnetism, respectively. This research will allow us to evaluate empirically the degree to which interface anisotropy can be varied using surface alloy substrates and may lead to a practical method for exercising control over the magnetic properties of ultrathin films. 由於納米效應，有許多在學術上和科技應用上都俱有深厚研究價值的磁現象都能夠在納米材料的身上發生。就磁特性的探討上，超薄膜的研究是眾多的納米材料當中的模型體系。其中一個原因是因為超薄膜的磁特性會因應超薄膜與其基底之間的強烈相互作用而改變，透過彈性應變、界面各向異性的作用，以及有異於物質正常體性質的特殊薄膜結構，而令其磁特性上產生變化。在這項研究項目之中，我們會對Fe薄膜在不同的有序表面合金上的生長過程和磁性質進行探究。表面合金有別於其原材料，在物理及化學上都有着非常不同的性質，表面合金材料可以透過不同的合金成份組合來改變及設計其特性，俱有很大的可塑性，尤其在化學吸付以及催化應用上更備受了廣泛的關注。在許多已知的表面合金系統當中，我們將會就各種貴金屬(Cu, Ag, Au, Pt, Pd) 於難熔金屬W(100) 與Mo(100) 上所形成的c(2x2) 合金化表面進行研究。由於貴金屬、難熔金屬，以至在某程度上，各個元素族之間，在費米能帶附近的d-能帶的電子態染化情況各異，其電子結構對界面各向異性的作用也有不同的影響。對這一系列的表面合金作深入研究，可以在不影響其他重要條件，例如在彈性應變不變的情况之下，透過系统性地改變基底的合金元素，從而理解控制界面各向異性的本質。實際上，從宏觀磁化現象的觀測可以得知物料在磁性質上的變化。我們會利用低能量電子顯微鏡(LEEM) 與自旋極化低能量電子顯微鏡(SPLEEM)，這些在探討薄膜生長以及磁特性問題上強而有力的工具對以上的系統進行研究。這項研究可以讓我們得知實質上表面合金基底對界面各向異性的影響，進一步更可以取得有效地控制超薄膜的磁特性的方法。

600110.label: Realisation of objectives
600110.value: The project objectives were achieved by performing a combined experimental/theoretical study of Fe thin film growth, thermal stability and magnetism on the clean W(100) surface and the W(100)-M c(2x2) (M=Cu,Ag,Au) surface alloy substrates using spin-polarized low energy electron microscopy and first principles density functional theory calculations. Research began with a comprehensive experimental investigation of Fe on the W(100) surface from continuous films to three-dimensional nanoparticles. The influence of the interface on thin film magnetism was assessed by making a comparative study of Fe on the W(100) surface and surface alloy substrates. These investigations focused on identifying intrinsic interfacial effects in thickness-dependent threshold behavior in magnetic ordering, magnetic domain structure, and magnetization easy axis. We also performed experiments that addressed the role of extrinsic factors that can possibly affect magnetic ordering, including intermixing and segregation of noble metals, surface and interface roughness, and the quality of long-range order in the surface alloys substrates. We identified the influence of atomically stepped substrate morphology on thin film magnetism that interfered with detecting intrinsic interfacial effects. This influence was eventually circumvented by systematically performing measurements on large step-free terraces. Careful procedures were also developed to correct for the variability of the Fe deposition rate, which allowed for accurate film thickness determination. After addressing these two sources of systematic error, we obtained highly reproducible results that facilitated the reliable comparison of behavior on different substrates. A number of other experimental difficulties and their solutions were described in our requests for extension of the project period. Theoretical investigations were carried out for ideal flat films with sharp vacuum and substrate interfaces. Heats of formation were calculated to understand the thermal stability and identify the magnetic ground states for different film thicknesses on the different substrates. Magnetic moments and exchange coupling constants were also determined for the magnetic ground states. The key differences between these microscopic magnetic quantities in films on the clean W(100) surface and surface alloy substrates provide important insight about the nature of the interfacial interaction that guides our understanding of the trends observed experimentally. Theoretical calculations were also performed that addressed the stability of the surface alloy at the buried interface and the energetics and kinetics of intermixing. The combined experimental/theoretical study carried out during this project sheds light on the intrinsic influence of surface alloy substrates on magnetism and the importance of several extrinsic factors on thin film magnetism.

600110.label: Major findings and research outcome
600110.value: Initial experimental investigations provided an overview of the growth, thermal stability and magnetism in Fe/W(100) films [1]. Rough growth of highly-strained pseudomorphic films was observed at room temperature. Kinetically-limited layer-by-layer growth of smooth films up to four monolayers (ML) thick was observed at intermediate temperatures. Growth at higher temperature produced three-dimensional islands on a thermodynamically stable 2ML film. All films are ferromagnetic with in-plane magnetization above a critical thickness that depends upon temperature. Experiments demonstrated that kinetically-limited growth of rough Fe films occurs on the W(100)-M c(2x2) (M=Cu,Ag,Au) surface alloy substrates at room temperature, similar to the growth mode on the clean W(100) surface [1,2]. The onset of ferromagnetic order that occurs with increasing film thickness at room temperature due to finite-size scaling of the Curie temperature varied reproducibly in films on W(100) and the surface alloys [2]. The onset is advanced on the Au-induced alloy (2.76±0.04 ML), marginally advanced on the Cu-induced alloy (2.89±0.03 ML) and delayed on the Au-induced alloy (3.12 ± 0.02 ML) compared to the onset on the W(100) surface (2.93±0.03 ML). The magnetization direction was also dramatically different on the W(100) surface and the surface alloys [3]. Theoretical calculations are being performed by our collaborator, Prof. Y.Miura (Kyoto Institute of Technology), to understand how surface alloys affect the interfacial magnetic anisotropy that causes this difference. These are difficult calculations because the anisotropy energy scale is very small. Theoretical calculations revealed that Fe films should not wet the surface alloy substrates in thermodynamic equilibrium [2]. Magnetic moments and exchange coupling constants were determined for the magnetic ground states of metastable Fe films on the surface alloys that are enhanced compared to their values on the W(100) surface [2]. Therefore, we attribute the reproducible variation of magnetic onset observed experimentally to the competition between the intrinsic enhancement of magnetic ordering expected on the surface alloy substrates due to enhanced magnetic coupling and several extrinsic factors that could suppress magnetic ordering. Supplementary experimental measurements suggest that limited intermixing of noble metals at the interface and the intrinsic roughness of the surface alloy substrates may contribute to the experimental observations. Despite these possible extrinsic effects, it is concluded that the use of the broad class of ordered surface alloys as alternative substrates may offer greater opportunities for manipulating thin film magnetism. 600110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600110.value: In order to develop this research, further investigations are needed to understand and minimize the impact of extrinsic factors on thin film magnetic behavior on surface alloy substrates. Application of spectroscopic or other methods sensitive to intermixing may help to identify its presence during the initial interface formation. The use of different Fe film growth conditions or methods, eg. low temperature or pulsed laser deposition, may also help to suppress intermixing. Improvements in the alloy formation process that lead to a smoother surface alloy substrate morphology may be the key to accessing intrinsic influences of the flat surface alloy interface on magnetism. Our investigations encourage the search for similar effects on macroscopic and microscopic properties in magnetic films on other ordered surface alloys. Similar experiments on noble-metal induced Mo(100)-M c(2x2) surface alloy substrates would reveal the effect of the weaker spin-orbit coupling that is expected at this interface due to the presence of lighter Mo atoms in the surface alloy matrix. A large number of surface alloys are also known to form in other systems. Among these, surface alloys with intrinsically smoother morphology, greater interfacial stability and reduced tendency for intermixing would be good candidates for magnetic thin film substrates.

600110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600110.value: Magnetic nanostructures have attracted sustained interest for many years because of the wide range of fascinating and useful physical phenomena that they exhibit. In the two-dimensional geometry, the fundamental properties of thin film magnetic nanostructures are known to be strongly influenced by the interaction with a supporting substrate. In this project, our combined experimental/theoretical investigations of ultrathin Fe films on the noble metal-induced W(100)-M c(2x2) (M=Cu,Ag,Au) surface alloy substrates revealed the potential as well as possible limitations for controlling magnetic interfaces and thin film magnetism using ordered surface alloys. Experimental investigations found evidence that the surface alloy interfacial structure influences several macroscopic magnetic properties, including sensitive threshold behavior in magnetic ordering, magnetic domain structure, and spontaneous magnetization direction. Theoretical investigations also found that microscopic magnetic parameters – magnetic moments and exchange coupling constants – are significantly influenced by interfacial contact with the surface alloy substrates. Despite the possible extrinsic influence of interfacial roughness and potential for intermixing, these results suggest that the use of the broad class of ordered surface alloys as alternative substrates may offer greater opportunities for manipulating thin film magnetism. This outlook is encouraged by the prospect of tailoring properties through a careful selection of alloy constituents.

600210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600210.value: Recent results have shown that different interesting morphologies, including interspherulitic segregation of one of the blend components of a two-component semi-crystalline miscible polymer blend crystallized from a melt. The arrangement of the lamelliform crystals can be varied from, at the one extreme, spherulitic crystal aggregates of one component in a continuum of crystals of the other, to spherulitic aggregates in which crystals of both components alternate through the spherulite. All intermediate morphologies can likewise be obtained. These different morphologies suggest that materials with a wide range of ultimate properties can be produced. However, there is no systematic study of the relationship between the ultimate mechanical behavior of such blend systems and their morphologies. The goal of the research is to establish the relationship between internal morphology and ultimate mechanical properties of these blends. We will use two blend systems. One of these will be the poly(butylene succinate)/poly(butylene adipate) (PBS/PBA) system whose morphological map, against blend composition and crystallization temperature is already known. We will simultaneously study blends of poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) and poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO). This compatible blend has significant commercial interest, since the PLLA component is biodegradable, but insoluble in water, while PEO is soluble in water but is not biodegradable. This combination of chemical properties suggests utility in medical applications, fostering the study of structure and properties of this blend series. The internal morphology of each preparation of the blends will be carried out using a combination of optical microscopy (OM), scanning electron microscopy, time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) and atomic force microscopy (AFM). Thin-film samples for these experiments will be prepared by spinning the solutions on glass slides and silicon wafers. For low-resolution images, OM will be used. Higher resolution images can be obtained by ToF-SIMS imaging technique, which has a spatial resolution about 0.3 microns. The advantage of using ToF-SIMS is that the samples prepared for the mechanical testing can be directly examined. For even higher resolution images, AFM will be used. The blend component can be easily identified because of their big difference in the melting points. A useful type of outcome of this research is a property map. For instance, one might map failure mechanisms onto a field of strain rate versus temperature. It is anticipated that different types of maps would be created, for instance, fracture energy contours on a field of crystallization temperature and composition. 近期的研究结果展示了各种各样有趣的形貌，例如在二组分半晶高分子均相共混体系的熔融结晶过程中，其中一组分在球晶内部产生了隔离现象。具体而言，通常在球晶的内部，晶片排列方式可以多种多样。在一种极限的情况下，其中一组分的晶粒聚集在另一组分的连续结晶区域里，导致在形成的整体球晶内部出现两组分的交替结晶。这种中间态的形貌都可以按照类似的方式得到。而这些不同的形貌会导致材料在一个很宽的范围内，拥有相应的极限性能。但是迄今为止还没有关于这种共混体系的极限机械性能和形貌关系的系统性研究报道。 本研究的目标是确立半晶高分子共混体系的内部形貌和极限力学性能的关系。在这一研究中，我们将采用两种共混体系，一种是聚丁烯琥珀酸酯/聚丁烯己二酸(PBS/PBA)，该体系的形貌和组分以及结晶温度的关系目前已知。我们同时将研究L型聚乳酸/聚环氧乙烷(PLLA/PEO)共混体系。这一相容体系具有显著的商业前景，因为聚乳酸是可以生物降解的，但是不溶于水，而聚环氧乙烷可溶于水却不能生物降解。二者的化学性质互补使其在医学上的应用意义重大，并能促进这一共混体系结构和性能的研究。 我们在实验中制备的各个共混体系的内形貌将会使用光学显微镜(OM)，扫描电子显微镜(SEM)，飞行时间二级离子质谱(ToF-SIMS)以及原子力显微镜(AFM)进行综合表征。表征中采用的薄膜样品将于载玻片和硅片上通过旋涂共混体系的溶液得到。对于低分辨率的图像，将采用OM表征。较高分辨率的图像可以通过ToF-SIMS成像技术得到，其空间分辨率为0.3微米。使用ToF-SIMS的优点是用于机械性能测试的样品可以直接被检测。而对于更高分辨率的图像，将使用AFM表征。这些共混体系的组分可以很容易被区分开，因为它们的熔点有显著的不同。 展现本研究成果所采用的一个有效方法是绘制性能曲线。例如，为了描述材料的破坏机理，可以以拉伸速率对温度作图。我们预计将要绘制不同类型的曲线，例如，为了描述断裂能，可以结晶温度和共混体系的组成关系来作图。

600210.label: Major findings and research outcome
600210.value: We have determined the critical parameters that controlled the morphology of PLLA and its blends. The formation of ring-banded PLLA spherulites of neat PLLA was promoted by the presence of the low molecular weight fragment on the surface.1 At temperatures above its melting point, the low-Mw component can act as a self-diluent, interacting with the PLLA spherulites to cause interference rings. We also studied PLLA/PEO (80/20) and (50/50) blend thin films to determine the vital parameters that controlled the morphology of the blends.2 The absence and presence of banded structures of the films of PLLA/PEO blends were related to the absence and presence of a coverslip on the surface of the films during crystallization, respectively. This difference in morphology was observed because the PEO component of the blends was oxidized at high temperatures in air without the protection of a coverslip as revealed by XPS results. Ring-banded structures were observed when the blends crystallized in nitrogen without oxidation. Phase images obtained using AFM indicated that the banded structures consisted of valleys and ridges, which were in fact flat-on and edge-on lamellae, respectively. A detailed ToF-SIMS examination suggested that PLLA and PEO were located mainly on the surfaces of the ridges and valleys, respectively. The study on the fracture toughness of PLLA/PEO (80/20) and (50/50) blends was completed,3 The toughness of PLLA, which was significantly improved by blending with PEO, was shown to be closely related to the morphology of the blends and the PEO distribution between the interspherulitic region of the PLLA and the PLLA spherulites. The size of the spherulites which was controlled by annealed temperature determined the distribution of PEO in these two regions. The locus of failure of annealed impact bars containing an arrested crack was examined using a polarized optical microscope. The crack was found to pass through the PLLA spherulites instead of the interspherulitic boundary. The unannealed PLLA/PEO (80/20) blend had the highest impact strength and very small spherulites compared to those of the annealed samples. In this case, a larger interspherulitic region, which contained a higher content of PEO, was the stronger component compared to the PLLA spherulites. For the PLLA/PEO (50/50) blends, the sample annealed at 125 C was the strongest one because of a more even distribution of PEO content between the PLLA spherulites and the interspherulitic boundary as well as a higher PLLA crystallinity. *Papers 1, 2 and 3 are listed in Section C.

600210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600210.value: The study revealed the relationship between processing conditions, morphology and ultimate impact toughness of PLLA /PEO blends. Further investigations are needed in the following areas, including optimization of the annealing process and blend composition. The annealing duration and the annealing temperature should be further investigated to determine the optimal annealing duration and annealing temperature to produce blends with even better mechanical properties. The relationship between the PLLA spherulite size and its impact toughness was established for the PLLA/PEO (80/20) and (50/50) blends. But the PEO contents between 20 and 50 wt% in the PLLA/PEO blends have not been studied. It is expected that a wider range of the mechanical properties of these blends will increase the commercial applications. We also have not done aging experiments of these blends. It is known that PLLA can be degraded via hydrolysis reactions in an environment with high temperature and humidity. Thus aging data of these blends would be very valuable in many applications.

600210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600210.value: In recent years, the usage of biodegradable polymers has become very popular as one of possible solutions to alleviate the solid waste problem and lessen the usage of petroleum-based products. PLLA is showing the highest potential usage among all current biopolymers. It can be degraded in natural environments by enzymatic or non-enzymatic hydrolysis of the ester bonds. PLLA has high strength and modulus; however, the reported sudden fracture during usage has greatly restricted its broader applications due to its intrinsic brittle and low impact resistance properties. Blends of PLLA and PEO show great potential. The mechanical properties of PLLA can be improved significantly by blending it with PEO. Both PLLA and PEO are semi-crystalline polymers and their crystallization temperatures differ significantly. The reported crystallization temperature range of PLLA is from 80 to 130 C. At this temperature, PEO is still in the molten state. Different annealing temperatures will affect the morphology of the blends significantly. The results of this current study indicate the size of the PLLA spherulites and the distribution of PEO between the PLLA spherulites and the interspherulitic region are the two critical factors that control the impact toughness of the blends.

600710.label: Project Objectives
600710.value: Upgrade the current Rb85 2D magneto-optical trap (MOT) cold atom apparatus: improving the optical depth from 45 to about 90. Achieve high efficiency optical storage at high optical depths. We aim to achieve a higher optical storage efficiency in cold atoms than the current experimental limit (<45%) that has been demonstrated in a hot atomic vapor. We are also interested in understanding the dephasing mechanisms and especially their effects on storage efficiency and lifetime at high optical depths. Reduce the ground state two-photon dephasing using optical pumping. If the storage efficiency is indeed limited by the dephasing rate between the two ground states caused by the residual magnetic field fluctuation, we propose to optically pump atoms into a Zeeman state with MF=0 to reduce dephasing. Investigate multi-pulse in series (or pulse sequence) optical storage in cold atoms. We will study how to compress and store at least two optical pulses inside the media, as well as address and manipulate each bit of optical information. Demonstrate simultaneous multi-channel parallel optical storage in cold atoms. We will study how to store and read out multiple optical pulses from different probe beams along different spatial directions. The proposed multi-channel configuration should dramatically increase the storage capacity in a single atomic ensemble.

600710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600710.value: Quantum memory with high efficiency for optical information storage holds the key to long-distance quantum communication, optical quantum information processing, and quantum computation. However, current state-of-the-art quantum optical storage only has a low efficiency of less than 45%. We propose an experimental research plan to achieve higher optical storage efficiency (>70%) in a high dense laser-cooled atomic media with dynamical electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT). We will study time-sequenced multiple pulses and multiple channels in parallel optical storage in a single cold atomic ensemble. The proposed research will also help answer the important question: What is the fundamental limit of storage efficiency and capacity of EIT-based optical memory? 高效率的光信息量子存儲是實現遠距離量子通訊，光量子信息處理和量子計算的關鍵。然而，現有量子光學存儲只有不超過45%的效率。我們在此提出一個實驗研究計劃，運用電磁誘導透明（EIT）技術在一個高密度的冷原子介質中實現更高效率的光信息存儲。我們還將研究如何在一個冷原子係綜裡實現多脈衝串行和並行存儲。我們的研究也將有助於回答一個重要的問題：在電磁誘導透明的介質裡，光信息存儲效率和容量的極限倒底是什麼？

600710.label: Major findings and research outcome
600710.value: We have achieved the following major findings and research outcome: (1) Invention of the dark-line 2D MOT. We invented a dark-line 2D MOT of neutral atoms with high optical depth. For 85Rb atoms, we obtain an optical depth of up to 160 in an electromagnetically induced transparency scheme, which corresponds to an atomic-density-length product of NL=2.05*10^15 m^(-2). In a closed two-state system, the optical depth can become as large as more than 600. Our 2D MOT is ideal for atomic-ensemble-based quantum optical applications, such as EIT, entangled photon pair generation, optical quantum memory, and quantum information processing. Representative Publication: [1] Rev. Sci. Instrum. 83, 073102 (2012); Patent: [1] US Patent Pub. No.: US 2013/0048846 A1 (2013). (2) Highly efficient optical coherent storage (up to 78%) with electromagnetically induced transparency in a dense cold atomic medium We have demonstrated a highly efficient optical coherent storage with electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in a dense cold atomic medium with a high optical depth of more than 100. By carefully minimizing the ground-state depahsing, we achieve a storage efficiency of up to 78% and a fractional delay of 74. This is a world record in EIT systems. Our work signiﬁcantly advances the technology of electromagnetically induced transparency–based optical memory and may ﬁnd practical applications in long-distance quantum communication and optical quantum computation. Representative Publications: [1] Opt. Lett. 36, 4530 (2011). [2] Phys. Rev. Lett. 110, 083601 (2013). (3) Multi-temporal-pulse in-series and multi-channel parallel optical storage We have demonstrated that our EIT cold atom system can be used for multi-temporal pulse in-series and multi-channel parallel optical storage. For the in-series storage, we successfully stored two temporal pulses in the medium, which is limited by the EIT bandwidth. For the parallel optical storage, our result can be extended to many-channel storage because of the system geometry. Representative Publications: [1] PhD Thesis, Shanchao Zhang, 2013

600710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600710.value: Potential for further development of the research and proposed course of action may include: (1) Improve the EIT optical storage efficiency to more than 90%. (2) Apply the cold atoms with high optical depth for other non-EIT optical storage scheme for possible higher storage efficiency. (3) Application in quantum state storage of single photons (4) Application in quantum information processing and quantum communication. (5) Application in quantum network and quantum communication. (6) Application in quantum metrology.

600710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600710.value: Classical optical storage has played a key role in modern information technology, such as compact disc (CD) and digital video disc (DVD). However, using these developed existing techniques we can only store intensity information of light, while we know optical wave has both amplitude and phase information. Coherently storing both amplitude and phase information of optical pulses will lead to revolution of next generation optical memory – a key to quantum information technology. Storage efficiency and time are two important parameters for practical applications. Among the different proposed schemes, electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) is compatible with quantum state operations, but suffers from low storage efficiency (< 45% before our work). In this research project, making use of EIT in cold atoms with a high optical depth (>100), we have demonstrated a coherent optical storage efficiency of up to 78% and a fractional delay of 74, and thus creates a new world record. Our result will lead to important applications in quantum information processing, quantum network and quantum metrology.

601410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601410.value: In this project, we study sub-Riemannian geometry and use it to construct fundamental solutions for sub-Laplacians. We are interested in studying general sub-Riemannian manifolds from the connectivity by sub-Riemannian geodesics point of view. It is known as Chow's connectivity result that any two states can be joined by a smooth integral curve. However, it is generally a difficult problem to find the number and the lengths of geodesics between the origin and the conjugate locus, due to non-commutativities of the vector fields. In this project, we attack these problems by using variational methods like Hamilton-Jacobi theory, partial differential equations and differential geometry techniques and special functions theory. Our work provides a deeper understanding of sub-Riemannian geometry, with many applications ranging from stochastic analysis to clinical magnetic resonance imaging. 本科研項目，我們將研究次黎曼幾何，並利用其結果以構造次拉普拉斯算子的基本解。 我們將會從測地線連接性的觀點，而研究一般的次黎曼流型。 任何兩點都可以用一條光滑積分曲線連接起來，這是眾知的周煒良的連接性定理。 但是，一般地來說，計算連接原點到共軛軌跡的測地線的條數和長度，卻很困難，其主要原因就是向量場的不可交換性。 本科研項目，我們將會利用哈密爾頓－雅可比理論中的變分法，偏微分方程，微分幾何和特殊函數的一些技巧，以解決這些問題。 我們的研究將會對次黎曼幾何提供更進一步的理解，同時也可以應用到從隨機分析到醫療上的核磁共振成像等等許多領域中去。

601410.label: Realisation of objectives
601410.value: We studied the geometry induced by a class of second-order subelliptic operators. Given any two points in the space, the number of geodesics and the lengths of those geodesics are calculated. We found modified complex action functions and showed that the critical values of these functions will recover the lengths of the corresponding geodesics. We found the volume elements by solving transport equations. Then heat kernels for these operators are obtained. We also developed a stochastic method in finding heat kernels by using the probability density of the associated Ito diffusion. The formulas involve an integral of a product between a volume function and an exponential term. We studied the integrability conditions for some sub-elliptic systems and constructed explicit integral representation for the solutions.

601410.label: Major findings and research outcome
601410.value: (1) We studied the geometry induced by a class of second- rder subelliptic operators. This class contains degenerate elliptic and hypoelliptic operators. Given any two points in the space, the number of geodesics and the lengths of those geodesics were calculated. We found modified complex action functions and showed that the critical values of these functions will recover the lengths of the corresponding geodesics. We also found the volume elements by solving transport equations. Then heat kernels for these operators were obtained. (On heat kernels of a class of degenerate elliptic operators, Journal of Nonlinear Convex Analysis, 12(2011), 309-340. ) (2) By using the probability density of the associated Ito diffusion, we were able to find the formulas for the heat kernels for degenerate elliptic operators. The formulas involve an integral of a product between a volume function and an exponential term. ( Heat kernels for a class of degenerate elliptic operators using stochastic method, Complex Variables and Elliptic Equations, 57(2012), 155-168.) (3) We studied the integrability conditions for some sub-elliptic systems and constructed explicit integral representation for the solutions. (Poincaré’s lemma on the Heisenberg group, Advances in Applied Mathematics, 60 (2014) 90–102. )

601410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601410.value: Because the intrinsic difference on geodesics, many facts are known for Riemannian geometry are open for sub-Riemannian geometry. In this project, we have studied some fundamental problems on sub-Riemannian manifolds, in particular on the heat kernels of some sub elliptic operators and integrability conditions. The ultimate goal of the work on the sub-Riemannian manifolds is to establish its general theory in order to provide a framework for quantum mechanics, similar to the role played by the Riemannian manifolds in Classical Mechanics.

601910.value: 高频金融数据的建模与统计推断

601910.label: Project Objectives
601910.value: Estimating the degree of jump activity, i.e., the jump activity index, in high frequency data. There are some studies in the literature on the topic. However, these estimators usually have quite large variance even for high freqency data. There is a desperate need to find more efficent estimators for the jump activity index. Testing for the presense of diffusion or jumps in a discretely observed process. Diffusions have been used for a long time and are found to be inadequate in fanancial data. Jump-diffusions were later proposed. There are also proposals to use jump processes alone to model asset prices. In this project, we attempt to develop statistical tests for testing various models. 601910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601910.value: Since the availability of high-frequency financial data and the observation of jumps in the log-price of securities, there has been tremendous interest in developing a financial model for option pricing and risk management. So far, there has been a bewildering array of models for asset prices in financial econometrics, including Ito's diffusions, pure jump processes, diffusion-jump processes, Levy processes, and the most general Ito's semimartingales. Given a financial time series, one has to choose an appropriate model amongst available ones. Since economic theories usually do not suggest a functional form for continuous-time models, researchers and practitioners alike often use convenient specifications, e.g., for deriving closed-form solutions for various security prices. Since misspecification of a model may lead to erroneous valuation and hedging strategies, it is very important to develop reliable specification tests for continuous-time models. This presents new problems and challenges for probability and statistical researchers. The purpose of this project is to investigate some of the issues in the study of high-frequency financial data. In particular, we wish to develop statistical methods for model selections for financial data and then to conduct statistical inferences for the chosen models. We would also like to investigate the effect of microstructure noise on these models. These are interesting and challenging problems. We believe that the project, once completed, would be of both theoretical and practical value. 近年来，有关高频金融数据的研究越来越受到人们的关注。随之也产生出各式各样的金融模型。例如，伊藤扩散模型，纯跳模型，扩散与跳混合模型等等。在实际中，如果给定一组数据，我们又如何去判定与选择哪一类模型哪？由于错误的模型选择会导致很严重的后果，所以这个问题的研究显得尤其重要。该研究项目就是围绕这一问题展开的。我们想寻找一些简单且实用的统计方法去选择合适的金融模型。 另外，我们还想研究微观结构噪声对这些模型的影响。这些问题的研究不仅有理论上的价值，而且还有实际上的意义。

Secondly, we study the effect of microstructure noise on the asset price models, which has been a hot research topic in recent years. Finally, we investigate the model selection problems for high-frequency data. We have successfully carried out all of our objectives.

602210.value: 邊界問題的高效數值方法

602210.label: Project Objectives
602210.value: Develop a new interface representation which approximates an interface locally and explicitly by piecewise high order polynomials. Design numerical methods for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) and integral equations on an evolving surface represented by these unconnected segments or patches. 602210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602210.value: Accurate modeling of an interface evolution is an important task in many fields in science and engineering. For example, multi-phase flow simulations require a flexible interface representation which can naturally handle topological change in the solution. Or, material scientists numerically model the growth of crystals to study the effects of different background environments on the crystal properties. The boundary between the crystal phase and the liquid phase is separated by an interface. Another example is the interface or surface regularization in image processing or in computer graphics. In this project, we propose to develop novel and flexible numerical methods for efficient modeling of interface evolution. In particular, the goal of this proposal is to develop numerical algorithms, which naturally simulate different topological changes in the evolution according to physics, accurately compute various differential and integral operators defined on the evolving interface, track/capture both Eulerian or global information and Lagrangian information such as an initial parametrization used in the elastic/spring model of an elastic membrane, extend to various types of underlying mesh including an unstructured triangular mesh, achieve better accuracy by adaptivity, and easily incorporate with various well-developed numerical methods for more complex applications. These resulting algorithms will be tested on various interesting applications including multi-phase flows simulations, high order geometrical evolutions of surfaces, and high frequency asymptotic solutions to wave propagations. 如何精確建模邊界的演變是一個在許多科學與工程領域的重要任務。例如，多相流模擬需要一個靈活的邊界表示方法去自然地處理拓撲的變化。或者，材料科學家需要使用數值模型來研究晶體在不同的背景環境生長下對晶體性能的影響。另一個例子是圖像表面正規化處理或電腦動畫。 在這個研究中，我們提出要開發新和靈活的高效數值方法去模擬邊界的演變。這項建議的目的是發展出數值算法 (1) 去根據物理學的進化模擬不同的拓撲變化， (2) 能準確地計算動態界面上各種微分和積分， (3) 能自然地延伸到各類基礎網，包括非結構化的三角網格， (4) 可達到更好的準確性， (5) 能輕鬆地與各種成熟的數值方法一起使用於更複雜的應用。 這些結果將在各種有趣的應用中被測試，包括多相流模擬，高階曲面幾何演化，高頻率波傳播的漸近解。

602210.label: Realisation of objectives
602210.value: As per Objective 1, we have developed a Cell-Based Particle Method (CBPM) which modifies the GBPM. There are several nice features of the proposed algorithm. The new method can significantly improve the distribution of sampling particles on the evolving interface. Moreover, by replacing the grid based discretization using the cell-based discretization, we naturally decompose the interface into segments so that we can easily approximate surface integrals. One peer-reviewed article has been recently published in the journal of computational physics based on this part of the proposal. For the other objectives, we have generalized the GBPM to solve high order geometrical flows including surface diffusion and Willmore flows. The resulting algorithm can be easily implemented. As an interesting application, we study locally inextensible flows governed by energy minimization. We have introduced tension force via a Lagrange multiplier determined by the solution to a Helmholtz equation defined on the evolving interface. Supported by this project, in total of 8 papers have been published. Two graduate students were trained.

602210.label: Major findings and research outcome
602210.value: In Leung, Lowengrub and Zhao (2011), we develop numerical methods for solving partial differential equations (PDE) defined on an evolving interface represented by the grid based particle method (GBPM). We develop implicit time discretization methods for the advection–diffusion equation where the time step is restricted solely by the advection part of the equation. We also generalize the GBPM to solve high order geometrical flows including surface diffusion and Willmore-type flows. In Liu and Leung (2013), we develop a numerical approach to solve variational problems on manifolds represented by the GBPM. We have also developed a new interface representation, named the Cell-Based Particle Method (CBPM), and have successfully tested it on some complicated situations. The final report has been submitted to the J. Comput. Phys. for consideration of publication and is currently under review. We have also studied two new applications of dynamic interface modeling. In Isakov, Leung and Qian (2011), we have proposed a new shape optimization problem for gravimetry. A series of paper has been published on efficient Eulerian methods for approximating the finite-time Lyapunov exponent (FTLE). In Leung (2011), we propose to compute the related flow map using the Level Set Method and the Liouville equation. In Leung (2013), we generalize a recently proposed backward phase flow method which is specially designed for long time level set propagation. Unlike the original phase flow method or the backward phase flow method which is applicable only to autonomous systems, the current approach can also be applied to any time-dependent (periodic or aperiod) flows. In the same direction, we develop an efficient Eulerian numerical approach in You and Leung (2014a) to extract invariant sets in a continuous dynamical system in the extended phase space. We extend the idea of ergodic partition and propose a concept called coherent ergodic partition for visualizing ergodic components in a continuous flow. In You and Leung (2014b), we propose a new Eulerian tool to study complicated dynamical systems based on the average growth in the surface area of a family of level surfaces represented implicitly by a level set function. Since this proposed quantity determines the temporal variation of the averaged surface area of all level surfaces, we name the quantity the Variation of the Integral over Area of Level Surfaces (VIALS). We also prove that the proposed VIALS is closely related to the computation of the FTLE in the LCS extraction.

602210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602210.value: Based on the output from this project, we have recently proposed to further develop some numerical representations of manifolds and computationally efficient approaches to solve elliptic partial differential equations on interfaces represented by the GBPM/CBPM. We have also proposed to apply the developed techniques to various physical applications including seismic and geophysical problems, or nanostructure device modelings.

602210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602210.value: Accurate modeling of an interface evolution is an important task in many fields in science and engineering. In this project, we have successfully developed some novel and flexible numerical methods for efficient modeling of interface evolution. In particular, we have developed numerical algorithms which can naturally simulate different topological changes in the evolution according to physics, accurately compute various differential and integral operators defined on the moving interface, track/capture both Eulerian or global information and Lagrangian information such as an initial parametrization, extend to various types of underlying mesh including an unstructured triangular mesh, and easily incorporate with various well-developed numerical methods for more complex applications. The resulting algorithm is important for multi-phase flows simulations, high order geometrical evolutions of surfaces, and high frequency asymptotic solutions to wave propagations.

602310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602310.value: The chemistry of Ir in +4 or higher oxidation states is not well developed compared with that of Ir(I) and Ir(III). In this project, we propose to synthesize high oxidation state Ir complexes stabilized by sigma-aryl ligands. Of particular interest are Ir oxo complexes due to recent reports that Ir cyclometalated complexes are active, robust catalysts for water oxidation using Ce(IV) as a primary oxidant, in which high valent metal oxo species have been invoked as active intermediates. Very few Ir terminal oxo and nitrido complexes have been isolated to date due in part to the fact that high oxidation states (+5 or above) of Ir are not easily accessible. With a judicious choice of ligand sets (e.g. aryl and nitrogen ligands) and coordination geometry, high valent Ir oxo complexes could be made stable enough for isolation. In this proposed research, high valent Ir sigma-aryl/cyclometalated complexes will be synthesized and their redox properties and organometallic chemistry investigated. These complexes will be used as starting materials for the synthesis of Ir oxo and nitrido complexes. The reactivity of Ir oxo complexes toward nucleophiles will be studied. The atom transfer chemistry of Ir oxo complexes will be explored.

602310.label: Realisation of objectives
602310.value: The objective of this project is to synthesize high valent organoiridum complexes containing oxo and nitrido ligands and to investigate their redox and organometallic chemistry. We have demonstrated that 4,4’-di-tert-butyl-2,2’-bipyridine (dtbpy) and the Kläui oxygen tripodal ligand ([CpCo{P(O)(OEt)2}3]- or LOEt-) can stabilize the +4 oxidation state of iridium. Thus, stable tetravalent iridium(IV) dtbpy trialkyl complexes and LOEtIrCl3 have been synthesized and characterized. These are rare examples of stable organoiridum(IV) complexes that exhibit low Ir(IV/III) reduction potentials. In addition, we have synthesized the first heterobimetallic iridium/ruthenium nitrido complex by reaction of an iridium(III) triaryl complex with a ruthenium(VI) nitride, [LOEtRuNCl2]. The short Ir-N distance is suggestive of the Ir(V)-N-Ru(IV) formulation a with Ir-N multiple bond for the Ir/Ru nitrido complex. This result indicates that electron-rich high-valent organoiridium complexes can form stable multiple bonds with heteroatoms such as nitrogen and oxygen. On the other hand, reaction of tris(mesityl)rhodium(III) with the ruthenium(VI) nitride results in insertion of the ruthenium nitride into the Rh-C bond and formation of a trinuclear Rh(III)/Ru(VI) imido complex. This is a new reaction for a transition metal nitride. Apart from iridium, we have explored the oxo chemistry of lanthanide elements. We have synthesized and structurally characterized a cerium(IV) terminal oxo complex, which is the first lanthanide complex with a genuine metal-oxygen multiple bond. X-ray diffraction and density functional theory studies have shown that this complex possesses a polar Ce-O multiple bond. The reactions of this Ce(IV) oxo with carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide to give Ce(IV) and Ce(III) carbonate, respectively, are relevant to the oxidation functions of ceria-based heterogeneous catalysts. This study demonstrates that like the transition metal analogues, high-valent lanthanide complexes show rich chemistry of metal-ligand multiple bonding.

602310.label: Major findings and research outcome
602310.value: (i) We have synthesized and characterized stable organoiridium(IV) complexes supported by 2,2’-bipyridine and Kläui tripodal ligand. (ii) We have synthesized and characterized a bimetalllic iridium/ruthenium nitrido complex featuring a short Ir-N bond, suggestive of the Ir(V)-N-Ru(IV) formulation. This is a rare example of iridium(V) complex with a nitrido ligand. (iii) We have demonstrated that a ruthenium(VI) nitride can insert into the rhodium-carbon bond to give a trinuclear ruthenium(IV)/rhodium(III) imido complex. This is a new reaction for transition metal nitrido complexes. (iv) We have synthesized and structurally characterized a cerium(IV) terminal oxo complex, [(LOEt)2Ce(O)(OH2)], which is the first example of lanthanide complex with a metal-oxygen multiple bond. The reactivity of this complex toward carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide can provide new insight into the mechanism of the oxidation of carbon monoxide by ceria-based catalysts. (v) We have synthesized and structurally characterized a tetranuclear cerium(IV) oxo cluster, [Ce4(LOEt)4O7H2], which features a unique {Ce4O7} oxo-metallic core. This cluster, which is reactive toward carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide and nitric oxide, can serve as a model for the active site of ceria-based heterogeneous catalysts.

602310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602310.value: This work has demonstrated that high-valent organoiridium complexes with multiply bonded ligands such as nitride and oxide are chemically accessible and display rich reaction chemistry. In particular, high-valent iridium aryl complexes with bridged nitride ligands, which feature Ir-N multiple bonds, have been isolated. Using this methodology, we have very recently synthesized a series of high-valent bimetallic iridium nitrido porphyrins complexes that possess very short Ir-N multiple bonds. The use of these iridium nitrido porphyrins as catalysts for atom transfer reactions (which probably involve ultra-high-valent O=Ir=N=M’ active intermediates) is under investigation. This study can open up a new area of research for high-valent iridium. In the second part of this project, we have synthesized a cerium(IV) complex with a terminal oxo ligand. Knowledge of the pathways of reactions this Ce(IV) oxo complex with small molecules such as carbon monoxide and nitric oxide will provide important insight into the oxidation functions ceria-based catalysts. Therefore, in the future, efforts should be made to elucidate the mechanism of the reactions of cerium oxo complexes with these small molecules. The results of this study can lead to development of efficient metal catalysts for oxidation of carbon monoxide.

602310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602310.value: High oxidation state metal oxo and nitrido complexes are of significance due to their applications in organic synthesis and their important roles in enzymatic processes. Of special interest are iridium oxo complexes that have been implicated as reactive intermediates in the iridium-catalyzed water and organic oxidations using cerium(IV) as the terminal oxidant. However high oxidation state iridium complexes with multiply bonded ligands such as oxo and nitrido are rare. In this project, we have demonstrated that a 2,2’-bipyridine ligand and a tripodal oxygen ligand can stabilize the +4 oxidation state of iridium. Stable bimetallic organoiridium nitrido complexes featuring iridium-nitrido multiple bonds have been synthesized. In addition, we discovered that a ruthenium(VI) nitride can insert into the rhodium-carbon bonds of a rhodium aryl complex to give a ruthenium/rhodium imido species. In the second part of this project, we have synthesized and structurally characterized a cerium(IV) terminal oxo complex, which is the first lanthanide complex with a metal-oxygen multiple bond. The reactivity of this cerium(IV) oxo complex with small molecules such as carbon monoxide has been studied. The results of this study can lead to development of efficient metal catalysts for the oxidation of carbon and nitrogen oxides.

602410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602410.value: The symplectic group (more precisely, its two-fold cover) has a beautiful representation which was immortalized by A. Weil's seminal papers in the early 1960s. In the literature this is called the Weil or oscillator representation. This representation is the foundation of the modern approach to theta series and has diverse applications in representation theory and automorphic forms. We propose to study the refined spectrum theory of the Weil representation. More precisely, we propose to study the restriction of the Weil representation to pairs of reductive subgroups called reductive dual pairs in the sense of Howe. We aim to described the Langlands parameters of all such representations that occur in the spectrum decomposition. Potential applications of this project include the following: (a) Construction of exotic unitary representations. (b) Construction of certain automorphic forms and cohomology classes for locally symmetric manifolds. (c) Properties and formulas for special values of automorphic L-functions. 在1960年代初期，A. Weil 等發現了辛群的一個奇妙表示, 在數學文獻中被稱為 Weil 表示。 這是用現代方法研究 theta 級數的基礎，在表示論和自守型理論中俱有廣泛的應用。 我們計畫研究的是 Weil 表示的譜理論。更確切地說，是將表示限制到所謂的約化對偶對的譜理論。我們的目標是用 Langlands 參數來描述這一確切的譜分解

602410.label: Realisation of objectives
602410.value: In the original proposal we proposed to continue the 30 plus year study of local theta correspondence over archimedean fields. With the ultimate goal of describing all theta correspondences for all reductive dual pairs in mind, our concrete objective was to push research in this direction substantially beyond what is known previously, both in terms of concrete new cases and in terms of new innovations in methods. These concrete objectives have been largely achieved. Together with my students, we have obtained the complete and explicit description of local theta correspondences for the family of dual pairs $(O(p,q), Sp_{2n})$ with $p+q=4$, and several other families including $(O*(4), Sp(p,q))$. Not only are these new and substantial cases, but more importantly, their proof goes beyond the technical limit that seem to have existed in all previous work by myself as well as by others. Thus these new results represent new advances in the general program. One aspect of these advances are several new versions of the induction principle, whose applications go well beyond the specific cases that we have worked out so far.

602410.label: Major findings and research outcome
602410.value: We investigated local theta correspondence for classical reductive dual pairs. Many new cases of explicit correspondence in terms of the Langlands parameters have been obtained. We have also obtained versions of the general inductive principle which pushes beyond the technical limits that existed in all previous works. The Multiplicity One Conjecture is a weaker version of the Howe Duality Conjecture which has been proved by Waldspurger for local fields of residue characteristic different from $2$. In joint work with Sun and Tian, we have obtained a general and completely new proof of the multiplicity one conjecture that covers the residue characteristic 2 case as well. For applications to other fields in mathematics, and particularly to number theory, it is vital to obtain not only the correspondence of abstract representations but also explicit data that come into the global theta lifting. In joint work with Harris and Sun we have made substantial progress on this issue when the two members of the reductive dual pair are of more or less equal size. More precisely, suppose $G,G'$ is a reductive dual pair of similar size. To be definitive, assume both are unitary groups defined over some totally real number field. If $f$ is an automorphic form on $G'$ belonging to some cuspidal automorphic representation $pi=otimes pi_v$, and $ heta(f)$ is its theta lift to $G$ then the inner product of $ heta(f)$ is expressed as a special L-value, modulo local factors at the ramified places. Each local factor (say the place $v$) is essentially an integral of matrix coefficients: the integral of a matrix coefficient of $pi_v$ against a matrix coefficient of the Weil representation at $v$. With a careful choice of data compatible with the global issues at hand, one needs to compute the local integral with almost complete precision. In the archimedean places, by making use of canonical matrix coefficients, the result is expressed as an explicit multiple of the formal degree of $pi_v$. Using the lattice model at the non-archimedean places, we obtain formulas which reflect the principle of theta dichotomy in a most fascinating way. Finally, together with Sun, we have applied results on local theta correspondence to prove that for the unitary group $SU(3,1)$, every unitary representation with non-zero cohomology is automorphic with respect to some arithmetic group.

602410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602410.value: With new versions of the induction principle, we begin to see the general shape of local theta correspondence in terms of Langlands parameters. The key seems to lie in the description at the "first occurrence". There is hope that combination of these new induction principles with Harish-Chandra's results on representation with a given infinitesimal character may reduce the calculation (for each given reductive dual pair) to finitely many cases. As the size of these dual pairs increases, the calculations may become extremely complicated. But the hope remains that at some point, one would be able to see the final and general answer. At that point, the proof of the "final answer" may become quite feasible. In the mean time, even before the most general local results are obtained, we continue to look for interesting applications to automorphic forms and number theory, as we did in some of our recent papers, as well as in a upcoming join work with Eischen, Harris, and Skinner.

602410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602410.value: In this project we studied local theta correspondence over archimedean fields. We obtained the explicit correspondence in some previously unknown cases, and developed new tools which may eventually lead to the complete solution of the general problem, on which mathematicians in this field have been working on for more than 30 years. In addition, we obtained applications of our results to automorphic forms and general representation theory.
