602610.label: Project Title(Chinese)
602610.value: 在均匀贵金属纳米分形上的表面增强超拉曼光谱研究

602610.label: Project Objectives
602610.value: To develop a method for the facile fabrication of well-defined nano-fractals of silver and gold metals. To study surface-enhanced hyper Raman and surface-enhanced Raman scattering of molecules adsorbed onto and/or chemically conjugated to the surface of the noble metal nano-fractals.
rows: To develop a method for the facile fabrication of well-defined nano-fractals of silver and gold metals.
To study surface-enhanced hyper Raman and surface-enhanced Raman scattering of molecules adsorbed onto and/or chemically conjugated to the surface of the noble metal nano-fractals.

602610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602610.value: Hyper Raman scattering (HRS) is a nonlinear optical process in which two photons of either the same or different wavelengths are simultaneously scattered inelastically by molecules or substances under study. HRS is the lowest order nonlinear counterpart of conventional Raman scattering (RS) but provides a set of new information complementary to that from RS about molecules and substances. This is particularly true for molecules or substances with higher than dipolar symmetry and with applications in nonlinear optical processes. Similar to the advantages that a conventional RS can offer with respect to a normal fluorescence process in the study of molecules and substances, HRS is expected to offer the same and even more advantages with respect to the two-photon excited fluorescence technique which has recently found extensive applications in nonlinear optical microscopy and imaging in biology and materials sciences. Therefore, HRS has the potential to become a very powerful technique in nonlinear optical imaging, as well as in ultra-sensitive chemical and biochemical analysis. Due to its nonlinear optical nature, normal HRS is actually a process with very low efficiency which has been the main bottleneck for its development and application. It has been demonstrated that two mechanisms can be employed to boost up or to enhance the efficiency of HRS process. One mechanism is the so-called “resonance enhancement” which takes advantages of the intra-molecular vibronic transitions in resonance with two-photon absorption. Another mechanism is the so-called “surface enhancement” which employs the localized surface plasmon polariton of an external substrate to which the molecules/substances under study are adsorbed to either physically or chemically. The HRS can be drastically enhanced to a level suitable for general purpose applications in chemical and biological analysis when both resonance and surface enhancement mechanisms are employed in a synergetic and constructive manner. The main thrust of this project are (1) to develop a method for the facile fabrication of noble metal nano-fractals as the ultra-active substrates for HRS, and (2) to study HRS of molecules with and without resonance effect on the as fabricated noble metal nano-fractals. The ultimate goal is to develop hyper Raman spectroscopy into a technique for ultra-sensitive chemical and biochemical analysis and for non-linear optical imaging in biology and materials sciences. 超拉曼散射是一个非线性光学过程。 在超拉曼散射中，两个相同或不同波长的光子同时被研究的分子或物质非弹性散射。 超拉曼散射是对应于普通线性拉曼散射的最低阶非线性过程，但它与普通拉曼互补，可以提供被研究分子或物质性质的新信息。对于具有高于偶级对称的分子或物质、或者有非线性光学应用的分子和物质，这点尤其重要。 研究分子和物质时，普通拉曼光谱（双光子分子振动谱）有许多特点 优于普通荧光光谱（双光子电子跃迁谱）。 与此类似，超拉曼散射光谱也有许多特点优于双光子激发荧光光谱技术。而后者最近以非线性光学显微成像的技术在生物科学和材料科学有广泛的应用。所以，超拉曼散射有着极大的潜力发展成一个非常有效的非线性光学成像技术并应用于化学和生物分析的超灵敏检测。 由于其非线性光散射性质， 普通超拉曼散射实际上效率极低。这也是其发展和应用的主要瓶颈。 已有两种机理被证明可以极大增强超拉曼散射效率。一种机理是利用双光子共振激发分子内振电跃迁的“共振增强”。另一种机理是利用被研究的分子吸附在具有局域等离子激子跃迁的外部基底表面。 当共振增强和表面增强被一起互增协同利用时， 超拉曼散射效率可以被极大地增强到可与普通荧光相当的效率，并被广泛应用于分子的化学分析和生物分析中。 本课题的主要特点是 （1）研发一个制备具有高度超拉曼散射活性的贵金属纳米分形的简易方法， （2）选择有或没有双光子共振跃迁的分子，研究其吸附在此贵金属纳米分形上的分子之超拉曼散射光谱。本研究的最终目的是把超拉曼散射光谱研发成一种超灵敏的化学和生化检测技术以及应用于生物科学和材料科学的非线性光学成像技术。

(2) Objective-2 was achieved by having studied surface-enhanced Raman and hyper Raman spectroscopies of selected molecules adsorbed on our as-fabricated Ag fractals and dendritic structures.

602610.label: Major findings and research outcome
602610.value: For achieving objective-1, we have (1) developed a method for fabricating Ag (and Au) fractal structures immobilized in a layer-by-layer assembled ionic polymeric thin film on a conducting substrate; (2) developed a method for fabricating Ag fractals and dendritic structures on a patterned array of templates fabricated by photolithography; (3) developed a method for fabricating a thick film of random Ag fractals by controlling precursor concentration overpotential; (4) developed a method for electrochemically fabricating size/shape-tunable galvanic substrates for pre-shaped Ag aggregates. For achieving objective-2, we have (5) studied surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy of molecules such as 4-MBA, crystal violet, rhodamine dyes adsorbed on above fabricated Ag fractals; (6) studied surface-enhanced hyper Raman spectroscopy of molecules adsorbed in above as-fabricated Ag fractals.

602610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602610.value: We believe that our method has the potential to become a good method for fabricating super-active substrate for applications in portable or hand-held Raman sensors. We plan to extend this study by preparing new RGC grant proposals.

602610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602610.value: For viable applications of surface-enhanced Raman (SERS) and hyper Raman (SEHRS) spectroscopy, it is critically important to develop optically super-active substrates on which the molecules to be studied or detected can adsorb. This project has been conducted with above purpose in mind, and has developed both methods for fabricating the optically super-active substrate with fractal and dendritic structure, and explored their performance in both SERS and SEHRS.

602710.value: 随机交易时间与市场微结构误差下的高频金融数据的统计分析

602710.label: Project Objectives
602710.value: Develop further the theory for the realized volatility when the transaction times are random and when there exists market microstructure noise. Find the main structure of the market microstructure noise based on a more sophisticated model that incorporates rounding and general additive noises. Find a consistent and efficient volatility estimator in the presence of random transaction times and microstructure noise. Provide guidance on how to make corrections to the current volatility estimators which are popularly used but biased due to over-simplification of the assumptions about the transaction times and the microstructure noise.

602710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602710.value: We aim to develop further theory on volatility estimation based on high-frequency financial data, in the presence of random transaction times and market microstructure noise. Most current theory relies on the assumption that the transaction times are non-random or (conditionally) independent of the price process, and also relatively simple assumptions about the market microstructure noise such as pure additive error or pure rounding. In the proposed study we will allow for dependency between the transaction times and the price process. We will also investigate the main structure of the market microstructure noise based on real data and take that into consideration. And finally we will propose a new volatility estimator and provide ways to correct for the bias in the existing popular volatility estimators resulting from over-simplification of the assumptions. 602710.label: Major findings and research outcome
602710.value: We have addressed 100% of the objectives and collected the results in 7 papers. These results have been further presented in many recognized international conferences (please refer to Part C for details). We have developed further the theory for the realized volatility when the transaction times are random and when there exists market microstructure noise (see papers [2] and [4] in Part C). We analyzed the main structure of the market microstructure noise (see papers [5], [6], [7] in Part C) which may involve dependency between the noises, dependency on trading information, or rounding error. We proposed consistent and efficient volatility estimators in the presence of random transaction times and microstructure noise (see papers [4] and [6] in Part C). We provided guidance on how to make corrections to the current volatility estimators which are widely used but biased due to over-simplification of the assumptions on the transaction times and the microstructure noise (see papers [1], [3], [6], [7] in Part C). Our proposed volatility estimators were shown both theoretically and numerically perform substantially better than the existing widely used estimators.

602710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602710.value: (1) We ourselves will probably make further progress and revise the two papers under review and the paper in preparation (papers [5], [6], [7] in Part C), upon receiving referees' comments. (2) It would be valuable to extend results established in this project to higher dimensional cases, where the established results of this project can serve as the fundamental basis and new challenges due to dimensionality should be focused.

602710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602710.value: Before this project, most of the existing methods for volatility estimation relies on the assumption that the transaction times are non-random or (conditionally) independent of the price process and also over-simplified assumptions on the market microstructure noise such as additive white noise or pure rounding. In this project, we allow for dependency between the transaction times and price process, and investigate the main structure of the market microstructure noise with dependency between the noise, other available market trading information, and rounding error taken into account. We propose new volatility estimators which we show both theoretically and empirically perform substantially better than the existing methods. This project leads to significant improvement in the estimation of volatility, which is a key quantity in many financial applications such as risk management, options pricing, portfolio selection, etc.

603010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603010.value: One of the key experiments in the quest of novel high-temperature superconductors are high-pressure experiments. They represent a way to learn how the crystalline structure may change in order to increase Tc. This was demonstrated in the case of LaBaCuO4, where a large positive pressure effect indicated the possibility to further enhance its transition temperature by applying ‘chemical pressure’ [1]. Soon after, the compound YBa2Cu3Ox was found with a maximum transition temperature ranging up to ~94 K [1]. Recently, a new family of high temperature superconductors was found with transition temperatures exceeding 50 K [2,3]. This novel class of high temperature superconductors shows many similarities to the cuprate high temperature superconductors and others unconventional superconductors, such as heavy fermion and organic superconductors [3]. Besides the layered structure, the superconducting phase appears in the vicinity of an antiferromagnetic phase and the antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations are a possible candidate for the superconducting coupling mechanism. It is therefore rather natural to hope that what high pressure has done to cuprate HTS can be repeated in Fe-pnictide superconductors in raising the Tc [4]. At the same time there are clear differences [3], e.g. that the parent compound of the pnictides is a spin density wave semimetal and not a Mott insulator. Experiments on this class of novel high temperature superconductors may therefore lead to new insights into the phenomenon of high temperature superconductivity. It is well known that the leading effect of high pressure on such superconductors is a doping effect due to pressure-induced charge transfer [5,6]. In the present proposal, we would like to use this effect in order to study the phase diagram of the pnictide superconductors by means of specific heat and thermoelectric transport experiments in a Bridgman-type of pressure cell. This allows us to control the charge carrier concentration of pnictide superconductors in a clean way without changing the stochiometry of the samples. The laboratory of the PI is specialized in this kind of experiments in a Bridgman-type of pressure cell and has used this method successfully on cuprate high temperature superconductors [6]. This method is very difficult and only very few laboratories worldwide are able to perform them. The high pressure experiments shall be completed by thermodynamic and thermoelectric transport experiments at ambient pressure for comparison. 高壓實驗是研究高溫超導機制的一個重要手段之一,此類實驗為如何改變超導體的晶格結構而提高超導臨界轉變溫度提供了非常有效的指導。早期高壓實驗研究表明對於銅氧化物高溫超導材料LaBaCuO4，通過“化學加壓”手段可以大大提高其超導轉變溫度。在這個結論的指引下，之後不久，人們就發現轉變溫度高達94 K的同類材料YBa2Cu3O7-d。近來，一族新型的鐵基磷化物被發現擁有高達50 K以上的超導轉變臨界溫度。這類新型高溫超導體顯示出一些與已知的銅氧化物高溫超導材料及其他非常規超導材料（如重費米子超導體及有機超導體）十分類似的性質：具有層狀結構；超導相鄰近反鐵磁相出現；反鐵磁自旋漲落可能是形成超導耦合的途徑。因此我們有充分理由相信，如同對於銅氧化物超導體那樣，高壓實驗研究對提高鐵基磷化物的臨界轉變溫度具有很強的指引作用。另一方面，鐵基磷化物超導體合同氧化物超導材料的不同，例如其母體材料是自旋密度波的半金屬材料而並非Mott絕緣體（銅氧化物超導的母體材料），決定了對此類材料超導機制的研究將會大大拓寬甚至創新高溫超導研究的視野。對此類超導材料加高壓導致的主要效應被公認為由電荷轉移引起的摻雜效應。在本研究計劃中，我們將測量在Bridgman壓砧腔内高壓下比熱及熱電輸運性質，以此研究鐵基磷化物超導體的相圖，高壓強的環境使我們能夠在不改變材料化學成分的前提下用“乾淨”的手段去很好的控制載流子濃度的變化。儘管整個實驗過程極其複雜困難，世界上只有少數幾家實驗室能夠進行此類實驗，但是本課題主要負責人的研究小組在磁方面具有非常高的專業水準並在銅氧化物高溫倡導材料的高也研究中取得了很大成功。高壓實驗得到的數據結果將會用來和常壓下的熱力學及熱電輸運性質一起進行分析比較。

603010.label: Realisation of objectives
603010.value: We have performed various high pressure experiments on CaFe2As2, BaFe2As2, Ba(Fe(1 x)Cox)2As2, Ba1-xKxFe2As2, FeSe and FeTe and we have obtained valuable information on their pressure phase diagram with a detailed set of experimental techniques (specific heat, resistivity, Hall effect, thermopower and Nernst effect). Most of them are rarely performed under pressure and we were pioneering to apply them to Fe-based superconductors. We have obtained precious information on the effect of ions substitution and the condensation energy, and we could explain unknown features in their phase diagram. These high pressure experiments are very difficult. Some experiments extended up to 8 months and not all of them supplied publishable data, which is in the nature of this delicate technique. The data interpretation was required detailed theoretical understanding. Nevertheless, we had very successful experiments and with them we have achieved objective 1, 4 (100%), objective 2 (90 %) and objective 5 (80%). For objectives 2 and 5 we have done all planned experiments, from which we learned a lot about pnictide superconductors, but our hope to contribute significantly to the understanding of the mechanism of high temperature superconductivity was certainly written too enthusiastic at the time of submission, in view that this is still one of the greatest unresolved mysteries in condensed matter physics. We have furthermore successfully addressed objective 3 (100%) with numerous experiments at ambient pressure and have revealed details on the importance of fluctuations in Ba1-xKxFe2As2 over a wide range of the phase diagram, and we have compared the fluctuation behavior to a classical superconductor V3Si. We were able to observe for the first time a vortex melting transition in Fe-based superconductors and we have studied in detail the phase diagrams of K-, P- and Co-doped BaFe2As2. In addition, we have investigated various newly discovered superconductors and contributed to their understanding. Our highlight is that we have discovered with our collaborators a new Fe-based superconductor: We combined the non-superconducting parent compound FeTe with the topological insulator Bi2Te3 and found superconductivity at the interface between the materials. The results are reported in the prestigious journal Nature Communications. Our experiments revealed a particular rich physics in this material. Related to this discovery, we have slightly revised our research focus, which is a further reason, why we consider to have achieved less than 100% for objectives 2 and 5.

603010.label: Major findings and research outcome
603010.value: Ca2Fe2As2 is not superconducting at ambient pressure but moderate pressure drives it superconducting. It was strongly debated whether this superconductivity is of bulk or filamentary nature. With our specific heat experiments we could unambiguously prove the bulk nature of pressure-induced superconductivity and reveal unknown details in the phase diagram with a rich interplay among superconducting, structural and magnetic degrees of freedom. We have performed pressure experiments on undoped, underdoped and optimally Co-doped BaFe2As2 samples with the aim to compare the doping effects of pressure and Co substitution. We found a strong enhancement of the optimal critical temperature and the superconducting condensation energy under pressure, which shows that superconductivity is weakened by Co-doping because of a pair breaking effect of the Co ions within the Fe2As2 layers. The phase diagram of Ba1-xKxFe2As2 differs from other Fe-based superconductors. A new intermediate phase was observed between the orthorhombic stripe-type antiferromagnetic and the superconducting phase. It appears to compete with superconductivity and suppress the critical temperature. With our combination of different experimental techniques under pressure, we could show that the intermediate phase is a phase separated state with re-entrant tetragonal domains that coexist with the orthorhombic stripe-type antiferromagnetic phase and filamentary superconductivity. The effect of critical order parameter fluctuations is generally believed to be negligible in classical superconductors, but has a significant impact on the characteristics of cuprate high temperature superconductors. Fe-based superconductors represent an intermediate case. We have investigated the strength of fluctuations in Ba1-xKxFe2As2 for under- and overdoped samples. We find that strong fluctuations exist in underdoped regime, while a crossover to a BCS behavior is observed in the overdoped regime. In addition, we were able to resolve the tiny fluctuation anomaly in the classical superconductor V3Si, which was for a long time thought to be impossible. We have discovered a new Fe-based superconductor formed at the two-dimensional interface between the non-superconducting material FeTe and the topological superconductor Bi2Te3. While the superconducting origin is still unclear, we have discovered 2D superconductivity, a very large superconducting gap that reveals the potential of high-temperature superconductivity in this heterostructure and a pronounced pseudogap that exists up to 40 K. In addition, we have investigated some newly discovered superconductors: the quasi-1D superconductor Sc3CoC4, ultrathin Pb nanowire arrays and Ca3Ir4Sn13 and have contributed to the understanding of these materials. In Sc3CoC4 we have applied pressure and could show that its transition temperature can be further increased.

603010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603010.value: We have done a lot of development on our pressure technique, with new experimental quantities and a new pressure cell that uses a liquid pressure medium, and feel that we are only at the beginning to apply our techniques to other superconductors and materials with strongly correlated electrons. Some of the pressure experiments in this project would need to be repeated under better hydrostatic conditions, and we aim in particularly at the ‘11’ family of Fe-based superconductors (such as FeSe and FeTe). These materials have the simplest crystalline structure among all Fe-based superconductors, but are promising because of the recent discovery of high temperature superconductivity in a monolayer of FeSe, and our discovery of a large superconducting gap, a pseudogap and topological superconductivity in FeTe/Bi2Te3. For the latter, we have already applied for a new GRF grant. The superconducting mechanism is still unknown and it is likely that the transition temperature could be strongly increased by doping the material, by strain or through application of pressure. In addition, since there is a growing community in Hong Kong interested in Fe-based superconductors, we are considering with our collaborators to apply for a CRF grant on Fe-based superconductivity.

603010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603010.value: Superconductivity was discovered in 1911. It represents a quantum property of a material that occurs typically at very low temperature and causes a vanishing of the electric resistance. With regard of the high application perspective for lossless transport of electrical energy, the quest of finding superconductors with improved characteristics is continuously ongoing, with the ultimate goal of finding a room temperature superconductor. Superconducting characteristics depend on subtle balances of control parameters, such as the electron density or the crystalline structure. Superconductor research focuses mainly on finding new superconductors, understanding their mechanism, trying to improve their characteristics and - most importantly - raising their transition temperature. The application of pressure has been proven to be particularly useful, because it can reveal the potential to superconduct at higher temperature: If a pressure-induced increase of the transition temperature is found, the next step is to replace small atoms in the material by larger ones. This introduces an internal pressure and can lead to a superconductor with higher transition temperature. Our research focuses on a new class of iron-based superconductors. Our experiments aim at unraveling their superconducting mechanism and we want to find out how substitution of atoms or pressure can enhance their characteristics.

603110.value: Understand the classical trajectories of the J-Kepler problems in simple geometric terms. Understand the phase-space of a J-Kepler problem as a co-adjoint orbit of the dynamical symmetry group. Generalize the theory of the Kepler hierarchies from tube domains to symmetric domains.

603110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603110.value: Euclidean Jordan algebras were introduced by Pascual Jordan (1933) in an attempt to reformulate quantum mechanics in a minimal way. A theorem of Jordan, von Neumann and Wigner says that the simple euclidean Jordan algebras consist of four infinity families and one exceptional. Although physicists quickly lost interest in them, the subsequent further explorations taken on by mathematicians turn out to be quite fruitful. The generalized Kepler problems are super integrable quantum models that share the key features of the Kepler/Coulomb model for the hydrogen atom. They can be naturally grouped into hierarchies. A upshot of our recent exploration on the generalized Kepler problems is the realization that these Kepler hierarchies consist of four infinity families and one exceptional and are in a natural one-to-one correspondence with simple euclidean Jordan algebras. Since simple euclidean Jordan algebras are naturally in one-to-one correspondence with symmetric domains of the tube type, we have a natural one-to-one correspondence between the Kepler hierarchies and the tube domains. It is well known among the experts that the mathematics around symmetric domains are beautiful, deep and rich. (Even in the classical upper half plane case we know it involves algebra, geometry, analysis, representation theory, and number theory, etc.). The newly found one-to-one correspondence between the Kepler hierarchies and the tube domains further enriches the mathematics around symmetric domains. There are multiple research fronts on the generalized Kepler problems. The one we chose for this project is to extend our theory to cover all symmetric domains. This extension is very feasible especially because the corresponding extension for the euclidean Jordan algebras, i.e., the hermitian Jordan triple systems, have been well-studied already. 欧氏约旦代数由物理学家约旦（Pascual Jordan）于1933年引入，动机是给量子力学提供新的框架。约旦，冯诺依曼和魏格纳定理给出了单欧氏约旦代数的分类：四个无限族和一个例外。虽然物理学家对欧氏约旦代数很快失去了兴趣，但数学家对约旦代数的进一步探索取得了丰硕的成果。 广义开普勒问题是享有开普勒问题的主要特征的超可积模型。它们可以自然地分成几类。我们近期的探索建立了广义开普勒的类与单欧氏约旦代数的一一对应关系。 单欧氏约旦代数与管状对称域（对称域的子集合）有一一对应关系，很自然我们要把广义开普勒问题继续推广直至得到广义开普勒问题与对称域的一一对应关系。 众所周知，围绕对称域的数学既美丽的又深刻和丰富。 （即使是上半平面这种简单的例子，它已涉及代数，几何，分析，表示论，数论，等等）。所以新的探索会进一步丰富与对称域的相关的数学。

603110.label: Realisation of objectives
603110.value: In the process of carrying out the project in the last few years, two expected discoveries ware made, one is an insight into the Kepler problem itself, the other is the realization that there is a much more general theory under which Kepler problem and oscillator problem are unified under the same umbrella. This general theory is not the same as objective three, but it transcend it in some sense. With the help of the general theory, we were able to introduce the classical magnetized Kepler problem in high odd dimensions, something that was not believed to exist in the past. Consequently we were able to understand the phase-space of these magnetized models, and this serves as a good substitute for objective two. With a hint from the aforementioned first discovery, we were able to completely understand the classical trajectories of magnetized Kepler problem in high odd dimensions. This serves as a good substitute for objective three.

603110.label: Major findings and research outcome
603110.value: In the past few years which is covered by this project, further study of Kepler problem was fruitfully carried out. In this study, two significant discoveries were made: 1. There is an intimate connection between the non-relativistic dynamics of the Kepler problem and the future light cone and Lorentz transformation - the hallmark of the theory of special relativity. 2. There is a general theory for which the Kepler problem (and even the J-kepler problems) and oscillator problems are just special examples, so that a mathematical unity is achieved. Besides that, the higher odd dimensional classical magnetized Kepler problems was constructed and the trajectories were completely understood. In summary, the study transcends the objectives set in the initial proposal in the sense that surprising discoveries rather than anticipated results were made. Indeed, experts such as John Baez called the discoveries remarkable in his internet article on gravity.

603110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603110.value: The research carried out in this project is like filling in missing pieces in a giant jigsaw puzzle game. One can always find a missing piece and put it in before the game is over. However, unlike the real jigsaw puzzle game whose total number of pieces is known before hand, here we don't know where the end is in advance. The history of the Kepler problem repeatedly tells us that it is foolish to declare the end of discovery. Indeed, my own research in the past 10 years started with something which was believed to be impossible, and my recent new discoveries were never anticipated by anyone at all. In fact, my initial motivation of doing research on the Kepler problem was to do a warm-up exercise for something else, but research on that something else never started simply because I have been totally trapped in this giant jigsaw puzzle game.

603110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603110.value: The long term goal of this project and its sequels is to explore the beautiful mathematics behind the Kepler problem, which is the mathematical model for the simplest solar system or simplest atom. We view this as building a powerful "mathematical telescope" so that we can use it to find some clues about fundamental physics. Indeed, a preliminary exploration of some plausible implications to fundamental physics out of our mathematical discoveries has been made, but it is too early and too hard for physicists to accept some of its predications.

603210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603210.value: We propose to design and construct a series of three-dimensional (3D) polyhedral DNA nanostructures out of single DNA strands according to Watson Crick base pairing interactions. The design includes the following aspects: the polyhedral geometry, the optimal sequence, the minimized global energy, and the regulated flexibility and rigidity. The DNA nanostructures to be built consist of tetrahedron, pyrimid, triangle prism, trigonal bipyrimid, and octahedron. On the way of finishing the proposed research objectives, we will also design and build 3D DNA nanostructures with more complexity. The first phase of this proposed research is to construct and amplify the 3D DNA nanostructures. The second phase is to accurately exam these 3D DNA nanostructures by Cyrogenic-Electron Microscopy (cryo-EM). With the financial support of the previous Hong Kong RGC grant to Yongli Mi (RGC 604606; project title: construction of DNA 3-D superstructures by DNA self-assembly; project duration: 30/12/2006 - 29/12/2009) and the USA National Science Fundation (NSF) to H. Yan, we have published an upfront paper in J. Am. Chem. Soc., (131, 13093–13098, 2009). In this article, we reported the design and construction of a DNA tetrahedron out of a single-strand DNA of 286 bases. We also demonstrated that the duplication of the tetrahedron is much more efficient through in vivo replication than the rolling-circle amplification (RCA). Our result was immediately reported as a highlighted story in the PHYSORG.com (http://www.physorg.com/news171624372.html). We have also developed a computer software, Uniquimer 3D, which has been circulated among people worldwide for designing DNA motifs and generating sequences for DNA self-assembly. We will further perfect this software and empower it with more functions, such as global energy minimization and wet-lab simulation for tiling DNA motifs to larger scale assembly. The direct application of this research is in drug delivery, protein crystal templates, medical diagnosis, and DNA computing. The longer term significance of this research is in DNA computing and DNA nanomachines. 本研究方案主要的工作開展包括：對於特殊應用的DNA模板的序列設計，DNA結構的自組裝，DNA組裝結構的表征，DNA納米技術的應用性常識研究。目前DNA納米技術還在二維圖形建立與應用階段。2009年IBM公司投資與加州理工學院聯合開發DNA二維圖形與光刻蝕雜交的方法開發高密度存儲單元。組裝三維DNA模板單元，進而搭建多級結構有重大意義。2009年我和美國Arizona大學合作研究，我們首次報道了用單鏈DNA折疊成正四面體結構，並成功克隆了該結構。最近我已經進一步設計了一系列結構可以由單鏈DNA折疊形成。最近DNA納米結構的三維組裝已經被廣泛的應用。DNA納米技術的亮點是：DNA是完全可編程的以及可控的。迄今為止，種類繁多的一維和二維的DNA納米結構已被成功地設計和組裝。在我們最近的一篇發表在JACS上的文章中，我們成功地設計和組裝了從一個有286個核苷酸長單鏈DNA分子的DNA折疊四面體。並且經酶切，弗格森分析 （Ferguson analysis），原子力顯微鏡（AFM）成像等手段表征其結構。我們的研究報告了一種可用於設計和復制單鏈DNA的三維納米結構。這是第一個三維單鏈DNA的納米結構的報告 如圖一所示。這一研究的應用在醫藥靶向釋放，DNA納米機器，生物分子表征等方面有前景。DNA能夠在生物納米技術上有獨特的應用完全在於其高級結構的可程序化控制性。而序列的生成可以用本人親自開發的DNA程序生成以及DNA三維結構設計的電腦程序來完成。這一程序還考慮到DNA結構的能量最優化，是目前唯一一個可以完成DNA三維設計的電腦程序。用單鏈DNA的好處是（1）不用考慮不同DNA片段的摩爾比，（2）可以在生物體內克隆DNA的三維結構。這兩點在DNA技術上有實際意義。 本人將帶領團隊從事DNA納米技術的分子設計，結構表征，結構克隆等一些列研究。

603210.label: Realisation of objectives
603210.value: Further to the cover story of our JACS paper ofmy Co-I and myself in 2009 by American Physics Society (http://phys.org/news171624372.html), which was the key to form this collaboration with Professor Hao Yan, the Co-I of this project, we carried the objectives 1 to 7 and worked out step by step about how to form DNA 3D objects with flawless structures. We fixed the problem in our 2009 JACS paper in which one of the edges of the tetrahedron consists a loop of the double strand. Objectives 2-7 have demonstrated successful solution. All the objectives were fulfilled. More importantly, we carried the project one big step forward and finished the self-replication of DNA 3D structures and submitted to Science in December 2014. It is now just got accepted on March 15, 2015 by Science with very high reviewers' comments. This is regarded as a big breakthrough in the DNA nano-technology, and, as one of the reviewers commented, revolutionary in self-assembly nanotechnology.

603210.label: Major findings and research outcome
603210.value: The smallest DNA 3D object, a triangular prism with only one turn on each edge, was constructed from a single-stranded DNA. We confirmed its structure using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). This work proves that single-stranded DNA can escape from kinetic traps to form stable topology. We have demonstrated that a DNA triangular prism with an edge-length of even one turn can still be folded from a single-stranded DNA. To the best of our knowledge, this is the smallest structure (each edge of B3.4 nm) of a 3D DNA polyhedron reported so far. It indicates that the DNA backbone can escape from kinetic traps to reach the globally minimized energy state and form a compact 3D DNA polyhedron. This has a significant influence on DNA nanostructure design. Moreover, this is the first report of visualizing 3D DNA nanostructures using a scanning tunneling microscope. The results show that STM imaging can provide more internal information and avoid the enlargement effect, suggesting that STM would be a good technique for the characterization of small DNA nanostructures. Our ssDNA prism is much more compact compared with other DNA nanostructures reported in the literature. Such compact packing, commonly seen only in natural proteins and functional RNA molecules, is a prerequisite for natural biomacromolecules to exert their biological functions.

603210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603210.value: The significance of this research is that this assembling method could be extended to other DNA designs for exploring biological applications. For instance, due to their smaller size and biocompatibility, DNA triangular prisms can be encoded with functional sequence information, or attached with targets (drugs, proteins, etc.), and delivered into cells. Thus, in this way, engineering biological pathways23 and drug delivery in vivo can now become a reality.

603210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603210.value: This work not only use programmable DNA to assemble 3D DNA superstructures which is much desired for the DNA nanotechnology in the applications of drug delivery, protein expression and characterization, DNA computing and artificial intelligence. To carry the project further, we also developed a self-replication mechanism for DNA 3D structures. We have also developed a general process that allows for self-replication, exponential growth and directed evolution of autonomous materials and devices. We demonstrated this process with DNA origami tiles. A seed particle, made from a specific arrangement of these tiles, is placed in a bath of individual tiles. The closed system is then cooled, exposed to ultraviolet illumination, and reheated mimicking the diurnal night/day cycle. In our system the progeny effectively double with each cycle for an amplification of greater than 7 million after 24 cycles. Further we showed that exponential growth can be utilized for selection and directed evolution. There have been quite successful attempts at artificial self-replication of specific molecules and modified enzymes previously. However, our study involves a general process which is illustrated by the use of DNA origamis. There are no enzymes or ribozymes involved, simply the cycling of temperature and light. The work has been submitted to Science on December 20, 2014. It is now just got accepted on March 15, 2015 by Science with very high reviewers' comments. This is regarded as a big breakthrough in the DNA nano-technology, and, as one of the reviewers commented, revolutionary in self-assembly nanotechnology.

We shall study the differences in responses between magnetically ordered states (ferro- and antiferro-magnets) and a few proposed spin-liquid states to these experimental probes.

603410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603410.value: The ability to manipulate spins in electronic devices is an important part of modern technology (spintronics), and an in-depth understanding of how the dynamics of spins could contribute to charge responses of electronic systems is a fundamental issue in this field of study. We propose to study a simple and fundamental problem here – the charge dynamics of simple insulating magnetic systems described by half-filled Hubbard models with large on-site Coulomb repulsion U. We aim at understanding how the spin dynamics could contribute to experimentally observed charge dynamics. The experimental probes we shall consider include AC conductivity (both in the absence and presence of an external magnetic field), Raman spectrum, Acoustic attenuation and thermal conductivity. Attention will be paid to the differences in responses of magnetically ordered states (ferro- and antiferro-magnets) and spin-liquid states to these different experimental probes in energy scales below the charge gap. On the technical side, we propose to study the problems using two approaches: (i) we shall consider the large U limit where the charge gap is large and the problem can be studied in a systematic t/U expansion, where t is the electron hopping matrix element; and (ii) we shall develop a general phenomenological continuum theory to study the problem. The two approaches have their own strengths and weaknesses and are complementary to each other. Our result will provide a general framework to understanding how spins can contribute to charge dynamics of insulating systems in energy scales below the charge gap. In particular, we shall provide theoretical guidance for the experimental distinction between magnetically ordered states and spin-liquid states. The calculation outlined in the project is well defined but technically non-trivial and is a perfect project for training graduate students and young post-docs. 一個現代科技需要的技術是如何利用電磁反應去控制電子器件內的自旋行為，要達到這一目的，我們需要明白一個電子系統內自旋的動力學性質和系統電磁反應的關係。在這裏我們建議研究一個簡單而基礎的課題 - 一個由赫伯模型描述的磁性絕緣體的電磁反應。我們希望明白系統的電子自旋動力行為會如何影響系統的電磁實驗反應，考慮的實驗包括系統的交流電導、拉曼譜、聲子衰減現象及熱導。我們會尤其注意有磁序系統(包括鐵磁態和反鐵磁態)及無磁序系統(自旋液體)在這系列實驗下表現出在低能量區域的不同反應。我們建議用兩個不同的理論方法去分析以上問題：(i) 我們會在大赫伯能隙U極限下進行(t/U)展開，(t是電子的跳躍矩陣元)；(ii) 我們會建構一個普適的現象理論來分析實驗。這兩種不同方法各有優缺點，可以互補另外一方之不足。我們的理論結果會提供一個普適的理論架構去明白自旋如何影響絕緣體在低能量區域的電磁反應，尤其將提供理論依據去判斷系統屬於有磁序系統或是自旋液體。計劃需要的計算明確但相當複雜，是一個訓練研究生或年青博士後的理想題目。

603410.label: Major findings and research outcome
603410.value: The main purpose of the research project is to study the charge responses of Heisenberg model systems to see whether there are charge responses that can distinguish spin liquid states from an ordered magnetic state. A powerful phenomenology for the U(1) spin liquid state is developed for this purpose which can address this question systematically. The major finding of the research is that the U(1) spin-liquid state is in fact a "marginal" Mott insulator state in the sense that the single-particle excitation has a "soft" charge gap. The "soft" charge gap can be seen in, for example, Optical conductivity and photo-emission experiments. We propose that the U(1) spin-liquid state may exists in some organic spin-liquid materials close to Mott transition in a preprint (arXiv:1302.0157) which is submitted for publication to Phys. Rev. Lett. We have also studied the differences in responses between magnetically ordered states and spin-liquid states in a S=3/2 Kagome lattice system in collaboration with Prof. Seunghun Lee from Univerisity of Virginia where neutron scattering experiments were performed on the Kagome lattice system Zn_{x}Co_{4-x}(OD)_{6}Cl_{2}. Our calculated spectrum for magnetically ordered state agrees well with Prof. Seunghun Lee's experimental data.

603410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603410.value: We are investigating other experimental signatures of existence of "soft" charge gap in the U(1) spin-liquid state. In particular, we are studying plausible experimental signature of "soft" charge gap in non-linear I-V measurement now. We are also extending the phenomenology to include spin-orbit coupling in the spin-liquid states.

603410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603410.value: Spin liquid states are new forms of magnetic states absent in the world of classical physics and were proposed to exist because of strong quantum mechanical effects in our microscopic world. These states are interesting because they may generate new particles (called spinons) which do not exist in our "normal" universe. Experimentalists have tried hard to find these states since they were proposed and one important goal of theoretical works is to identify clear experimental signals for these states. This is the main purpose of our work. In this project we have succeeded in proposing a general (phenomenological) framework to calculate the charge responses of a simplest type of spin liquid state called U(1) spin liquid and have identified a unique feature in this kind of spin-liquid state - that they have a so-called "soft" charge gap. We have identified some experimental signatures for the "soft" charge gap in our present work and we are working to identify more experimental signatures for this new state of matter now.

603510.label: Project Objectives
603510.value: To derive the boundary conditions at the fluid-solid interface for the dynamic van der Waals theory developed for one-component fluids of two phases, i.e., liquid-gas systems. The present theory assumes the local equilibrium condition at the solid surface for density. It also assumes the no-slip boundary condition for fluid velocity at the surface. These two conditions will be relaxed by introducing additional dissipative processes at the surface. The positive definiteness of entropy production rate will be the guiding principle for our derivation. To carry out the numerical simulation for our generalized model with the newly derived boundary conditions. To carry out analysis of the theoretical model and the numerical data. This is to investigate the effects of the (newly introduced) surface dissipative processes on contact-line motion. In particular, we plan to investigate the interplay between slip and phase transformation (evaporation/condensation) in the vicinity of the moving contact line. To simulate the contact-line motion in droplet spreading driven by the long-range van der Waals (attractive) interactions between fluid and solid substrate, and to simulate the contact-line motion on patterned surface (with periodically arranged hydrophilic and hydrophobic areas). These two phenomena are of general interest and have been simulated using many different models.

603510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603510.value: The no-slip boundary condition states that there can be no relative motion at the fluid-solid interface. It is generally regarded as a corner stone in continuum hydrodynamics, owing to its proven applicability in diverse fluid-flow problems. In recent years, numerous research efforts have been placed on the Newtonian flows in confined geometries, showing that fluid actually slips at the solid boundary in many circumstances. The magnitude of slip is characterized by a quantity of length unit, referred to as the slip length. For a simple shear flow parallel to the surface, it is the distance below the surface at which the fluid velocity extrapolates to zero (no slip). The slip length usually ranges from a few angstroms to a few nanometers. This explains why the no-slip boundary condition works perfectly well in macroscopic flows, and also why an accurate account of slip is needed for flows of micro/nanoscale. While single-phase flows require the slip effect to be taken into account only at small length scales, the contact-line motion in two-phase flows is incompatible with the no-slip boundary condition even if the system dimension (e.g., the size of a droplet spreading on solid surface) is on macroscopic length scale. In fact, early molecular dynamics simulations have already shown the slip to occur in the vicinity of the moving contact line (MCL). The heart of the MCL problem lies in the boundary condition(s) at the fluid-solid interface. For the MCL in immiscible two-phase flows, a continuum model has been obtained by combining an appropriate slip boundary condition with the continuum hydrodynamic formulation for binary fluids. Its numerical implementation has produced continuum solutions in quantitative agreement with molecular dynamics simulation results. This proposed project intends to study the contact-line motion in one-component two-phase fluids, i.e., liquid-gas systems, by taking into account the slip effect. We will derive the boundary conditions for the existing theory of liquid-gas hydrodynamics and then carry out numerical simulations with them. The liquid-gas systems are noted to be distinguished from the binary fluids by the fact that contact-line motion is accompanied by phase transition, characterized by strong heat transfer and mass transport across the interface. Therefore, we will carry out analysis on the interplay between slip and phase transition (evaporation/condensation) in the vicinity of MCL. These studies will lead to a more complete understanding of the MCL in liquid-gas systems.

603510.label: Realisation of objectives
603510.value: The first objective is to derive the hydrodynamic boundary conditions at the fluid-solid interface for the dynamic van der Waals theory. This has been achieved by applying the principles of continuum mechanics and non-equilibrium thermodynamics. We have derived the boundary conditions which describe a couple of dissipative processes at the fluid-solid interface and can be used to supplement the DVDWT. For details, see Xinpeng Xu and Tiezheng Qian, Contact line motion in confined liquid-gas systems: Slip versus phase transition, J. Chem. Phys. 133, 204704 (2010); Xinpeng Xu, Chun Liu, Tiezheng Qian, Hydrodynamic boundary conditions for one-component liquid-gas flows on non-isothermal solid substrates, Communications in Mathematical Sciences 10, 1027 (2012). The second objective is to carry out numerical simulations for the dynamic van der Waals theory supplemented with the newly derived boundary conditions. This has been achieved by studying the droplet motion driven by wettability gradients and that driven by thermal gradients. In both cases, the boundary conditions play an important role in governing the droplet motion at small (sub-micrometer) scales. Based on the numerical results, we have analyzed the fluid-solid interfacial effects on the droplet migration. For details, see Xinpeng Xu and Tiezheng Qian, Droplet motion in one-component fluids on solid substrates with wettability gradients, Physical Review E 85, 051601 (2012); Xinpeng Xu and Tiezheng Qian, Thermal singularity and droplet motion in one-component fluids on solid substrates with thermal gradients, Physical Review E 85, 061603 (2012). The third objective is to carry out analysis to investigate the effects of fluid-solid interfacial processes on the contact line motion. This has been achieved by carrying out numerical simulations to measure boundary slip and phase transition in the vicinity of moving contact line. For details, see Xinpeng Xu and Tiezheng Qian, Contact line motion in confined liquid-gas systems: Slip versus phase transition, J. Chem. Phys. 133, 204704 (2010). As to the fourth objective, it has been achieved through both theoretical and numerical studies of droplet motion under several different driving mechanisms. For details, see Xinpeng Xu and Tiezheng Qian, Physical Review E 85, 051601 (2012); Xinpeng Xu and Tiezheng Qian, Physical Review E 85, 061603 (2012); Congmin Wu, Xinpeng Xu, and Tiezheng Qian, Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter 25, 195103 (2013); Y. 603510.label: Major findings and research outcome
603510.value: Hydrodynamic boundary conditions. Liquid-gas flows related to droplets, bubbles, and thin films on solid surfaces with thermal and wettability gradients have attracted widespread attention because of the many physical processes involved and their promising potential applications in biology, chemistry, and industry. A continuum model is constructed for simulating the liquid-gas flows on flat and rigid solid surfaces with wettability gradients and thermal gradients. This model is able to describe fluid velocity slip, temperature slip, and mechanical-thermal coupling at fluid-solid interfaces. Major publication: Xinpeng Xu, Chun Liu, Tiezheng Qian, Communications in Mathematical Sciences 10, 1027 (2012). Contact line motion. Based on the dynamic van der Waals theory and the newly derived boundary conditions, numerical simulations have been carried out to investigate the mechanism for contact line motion. We find that the contact line can move through both phase transition and slip, with their relative contributions determined by a competition between the two coexisting mechanisms in terms of entropy production. The observed competition is interpreted by the Onsager principle of minimum entropy production. Major publication: Xinpeng Xu and Tiezheng Qian, J. Chem. Phys. 133, 204704 (2010). Droplet migration at solid surfaces with thermal gradients. Based on the dynamic van der Waals theory and the newly derived boundary conditions, numerical simulations have been carried out to study the droplet migration at solid surfaces with thermal gradients. We find that a thermal singularity occurs at the contact line and leads to a contact angle locally dependent on the substrate temperature. As a thermal gradient is applied on the solid surface, the droplet will move as a result of the capillary pressure gradient caused by contact angle variation. Major publications: Xinpeng Xu and Tiezheng Qian, Physical Review E 85, 061603 (2012); Congmin Wu, Xinpeng Xu, and Tiezheng Qian, Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter 25, 195103 (2013). Other studies of two-phase flows at solid surfaces. These include (i) droplet motion driven by wettability gradients, (ii) two-phase immiscible electro-osmotic flows, (iii) droplet bouncing on patterned surfaces. Major publications: Xinpeng Xu and Tiezheng Qian, Physical Review E 85, 051601 (2012); Sihong Shao and Tiezheng Qian, Communications in Computational Physics 11, 831 (2012); Y. Liu, L. Moevius, X. Xu, T. Qian, J. M. Yeomans, Z. Wang, Nature Physics 10, 515 (2014).

603510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603510.value: Our formulation is based upon the principles of continuum mechanics and non-equilibrium thermodynamics. Therefore, it can be further generalized to more complicated systems. There have been experimental observations that the deformation of solid substrates can affect the wetting properties. To incorporate the solid deformation into a more general continuum model represents a future work to pursue. We would like to point out that the framework presented for modeling two-phase flows at solid surfaces, from bulk equations to boundary conditions, is already in a form that can be used for modeling other fluid-solid interfacial phenomena, e.g., binary alloy solidification with convection and liquid crystals moving on solid surfaces. As to the course of action, we will apply the Onsager principle to describe the non-equilibrium processes in the linear response regime. This requires us to identify the free energy functional and the dissipation functional for the problem first. Then we may develop a variational approach to derive the equations of motion.

603510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603510.value: In order to describe continuum fluid dynamics, we need both the partial differential equations in the bulk region and the boundary conditions at the solid surface. The effects of boundary conditions are expected to be more and more important when the fluid system is approaching smaller and smaller scales. Based on the above general understanding, we have carried out modeling and simulations for one-component liquid-gas flows at solid surfaces. First, we derived the boundary conditions by applying the principles of continuum mechanics and non-equilibrium thermodynamics. We then carried out numerical simulations to investigate a couple of problems that involve one-component liquid-gas flows at solid surfaces, with a focus on droplet motion and moving contact line (where the liquid-gas interface meets the solid wall). These problems are complicated and difficult because they are characterized by the coupling of momentum transfer, heat transfer, liquid-gas transition, and boundary slip. We have revealed the mechanism for contact line motion and investigated the two-phase non-isothermal hydrodynamics for droplet motion under different driving mechanisms. These results not only improve the physical understanding of multi-phase flows at solid surfaces but also are useful in the design of microfluidic devices.

603710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603710.value: Stein's method is a powerful tool for deriving explicit estimates of the accuracy to the approximation of one probability distribution by another. The method is of interest not only because it works for independent random variables, but also because it works well for dependent random variables. The method has been successfully applied to prove uniform and non-uniform Berry-Esseen type error bounds in the normal approximation for sums of independent random variables as well as for dependent random variables. This proposed research focuses on (i) Cram\'er type moderate deviation error bounds for self-normalized sums of independent random variables and other sums of dependent variables; (ii) uniform and non-uniform Berry-Esseen type bounds as well as moderate deviation bounds in non-normal approximation; (iii) applications in different areas such as in statistical physics and number theory. The aim is to identify unknown limiting distributions in some open problems, especially, the limiting distribution of magnetization energy in the Ising model at critical temperature in two and three dimensions, systematically develop Stein's method in normal and non-normal approximation and explore various applications in different subjects. 在处理概率分布逼近问题中，Stein方法为计算逼近精度提供了有力的工具。该方法有趣之处不仅在于从全新的角度处理经典问题，更体现于其在处理相依随机变量时的功效。在对独立以及具有某种依赖关系的随机变量部分和的正态逼近问题中，利用Stein方法人们成功得到了一致与非一致Berry-Esseen型的误差估计。本研究项目则主要针对于以下三方面： (1) 自正则化独立或相依随机变量部分和的Cramer型中偏差误差估计； (2) 一致与非一致Berry-Esseen型上界以及非正态逼近中的中偏差估计； (3) 不同领域中的应用。 本研究项目的主要目标是解决一些未决问题，确定其极限分布，特别是确定在两维和三维的Ising模型中磁化能在临界温度下的极限分布。进一步在正态与非正态逼近问题中系统地发展Stein方法。

603710.label: Realisation of objectives
603710.value: Objectives 1 and 2 are completely realized. A Cramer type moderate deviation theorem is proved under a general Stein's identity and optimal results are obtained for the combinatorial central limit theorem, the binary expansion of a random integer, the anti-voter model on a complete graph and the Curie-Weiss model. A Cramer type moderate deviation is established for self-normalized processes and successfully applied to Studentized U-statistics. Objectives 3 and 4 are 80% achieved. The PI has obtained a general result to identify the limiting distributions, but when the result is applied to the Ising model at the critical temperature case, it involves some difficult calculations of conditional mean and conditional variance. The PI will continue to work on this problem even though the funding for this project ended.

603710.label: Major findings and research outcome
603710.value: In Chen, Fang and Shao (2013), we established Cramer type moderate deviation results under a general framework of Stein's identity and applied the results to the combinatorial central limit theorem, the binary expansion of a random integer, the anti-voter model on a complete graph and the Curie-Weiss model. In Shao and Zhou (2012), we used Stein's method to obtain Cramer type moderate deviation theorems for self-normalized non-linear statistics. The results are new and optimal even for Studentized U-statistics. In Chatterjee and Shao (2011), we developed the Stein's method for non-normal approximation, which not only provides a general result how to identify the limiting density function but also gives a Berry-Esseen type error bound. The paper by Chen and Shao (2012) is the first attempt to establish a sharp Berry-Esseen bound for unbounded exchangeable pairs. In Hu and Shao (2013), we established optimal non-uniform Berry-Essen bounds for weighted U-statistics and generalized L-statistics. The book by Chen, Goldstein and Shao (2011) contains through coverage of the Stein method's fundamentals and includes a large number of recent developments in both theory and applications. Other major finds include: Cramer moderate deviation results for Hotelling's T^2 statistics (Liu and Shao (2013) and for the maximum of self-normalized sums (Liu, Shao and Wang (2013)), necessary and sufficient conditions for the asymptotic distributions of coherence of ultra-high dimensional random matrices (Shao and Zhou (2014)).

603710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603710.value: Stein's method is a powerful tool for the study of the accuracy of normal and non-normal approximation. The method can and should be further explored and can be applied to solve some open problems in statistical physics and spin glass. The PI will continue to work on this topic.

603710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603710.value: Stein's method is a powerful tool for the study of the accuracy of normal and non-normal approximation. It has been proved in this project that the method can not only identify the limiting distribution but also give the bound of approximation error. The research results obtained in this project provide theoretical foundations / justifications for many commonly used statistical practices. The results also reveal theoretical properties form some models in statistical physics.

604210.label: Project Objectives
604210.value: Synthesis of high quality zeolite AEL single crystals with high optical transparency and high perfection in crystal structure. High quality AEL single crystals are crucial for this project in terms of perfect localization of iodine molecules in the nano pores and getting enhanced signal-to-noise ratio of the reference molecular transition frequency by reducing unnecessary light scattering. Incorporation of molecular iodine into the nano pores of the AEL single crystals. Status of dispersion and localization of the iodine molecules in the nano pores might be affected in terms of loading concentration, incorporation pressure and temperature, etc. We will systematically investigate the effects of experimental conditions to the dispersion status of the molecules to get a well-dispersed and perfectly oriented molecular system of I2@AEL crystal. Theoretical simulation of vibration and electronic properties of the localized iodine molecules in the nano pores. To have a better understanding of the confined iodine molecules, we will simulate the physical properties of the localized iodine molecules inside the nano pores, including the properties of vibrations, electronic structures, effect of loading densities, molecular interactions, effect of the pore walls, etc. Study of regular optical properties of the localized iodine molecules. To get information of the status of molecular iodine inside the nano pores, we will study the regular optical properties of the localized iodine molecules, including Raman scattering, light emission and absorption spectra, etc. From Raman scattering, we can get a clear picture of the molecular orientation, molecular motion, molecule-molecule interaction, pore-wall-molecule interaction, etc., from the absorption spectra, we can get information of possible effect of the abovementioned interactions on molecular electronic transitions. Hyperfine spectral structure study of the localized iodine molecules, and demonstration of optical frequency standard and molecular iodine clock. Utilizing the “femtosecond optical frequency comb” technology, we will systematically study the hyperfine structure of the BX transitions of the localized iodine molecules, to see the effects from the confinement on the transition levels. Furthermore, we will use the hyperfine transition near 523 nm as the optical frequency reference to demonstrate a portable version of iodine based optical clock with compact, simple, and less expensive system configurations.

604210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604210.value: In our previous research, molecular iodine has been efficiently frozen at a specific direction of elliptical nano pores of zeolite AlPO-11 (code: AEL) single crystals. Using this unique “solid state” molecular system, in this proposed project, we will investigate the hyperfine spectral structure for perfectly orientated iodine molecules, and demonstrate compact optical molecular clocks by using the hyperfine molecular optical transitions as frequency standard. To diminish the Doppler broadening of the molecular transition lines, in the modern optical atomic / molecular clocks, either the atoms are laser-cooled to the zero-point energy limit, or the Doppler effect of vapor phase molecular motion is reduced by means of pump-probe saturation absorption configuration. In this project research, we will generate a portable version of molecular iodine based optical clock with more compact, simpler and less expensive system configurations by using a molecular iodine dispersed AEL single crystal as the Doppler-free molecule source. To reach the goal, the following issues will be addressed in the project: (1) Synthesis of high quality zeolite AEL single crystals with high optical transparency and high perfection in crystal structure; (2) Incorporation of molecular iodine into the nano pores of the AEL single crystals; (3) Theoretical simulation of vibration and electronic properties of the localized iodine molecules in the nano pores; (4) Study of regular optical properties of the localized iodine molecules; And (5) study of hyperfine spectral structures of the localized iodine molecules, and demonstrate a compact molecular iodine clock. 在前期研究中，我們已成功地將雙原子碘分子鎖定在沸石AEL單晶體的橢圓納米細孔的特定方向上。本課題將利用這種獨特的“固態”分子體系，著重研究在空間和取向上都被局域化的碘分子超精細光譜結構，並將這種分子體系應用到光頻標準元件以及探討在光頻分子鐘領域應用的可能性。在現代光頻原子（或分子）鐘的應用領域，為了消除光學躍遷譜線的多普勒展寬，通常用激光冷卻技術將原子凍結在零能量點的陷阱裡，或者通過pump-probe飽和吸收裝置來抵消運動中的氣相分子之多普勒效應。在本項研究中，我們將研究這種獨特分子體系在小巧、簡便、低造價、可攜式光頻碘分子鐘的潛在應用技術。為達致研究目標，我們將研究內容鎖定在下列幾個主要問題：（1）生長高結晶性和優質光學性能的大尺寸沸石AEL單晶體；（2）完備在AEL晶體納米細孔中組裝碘分子的技術；（3）理論模擬被凍結在納米細孔中的碘分子之振動以及電子能態特性；（4）研究這種“固態“分子體系的常規光學特性；（5）研究這種“固態“分子體系的超精細光譜特性以及探索這種獨特分子體系在光頻分子鐘領域的潛在應用。

604210.label: Realisation of objectives
604210.value: Object 1 --- High quality AEL single crystals are crucial for this project in terms of perfect localization of iodine molecules in the nano pores and reducing unnecessary light scattering. In the initial stage of the project, we have focused our effort in getting optical quality zeolite AEL single crystals. Perfect large AEL single crystals with a typical dimension of 40x80x180 μm3 were synthesized by optimizing the following synthesis conditions: crystallization temperature and duration, molar ratio SiO2/Al2O3, amount of the organic template dipropylamine and HF. (see paper 01). Object 2 --- Iodine molecules are incorporated into the nano pores by means of a physical diffusion process. At low loading level, the incorporated iodine molecules behave as a single molecule, most of them are fixed along the long-axis of the elliptical nano pore. With increasing loading density, the incorporated iodine specimens gradually change their structure from single-molecule like to solid wire like. We systematically investigated the effects of experimental conditions to the dispersion status of the molecules and obtained a well-dispersed and perfectly oriented molecular system of I2@AEL crystal. (see paper 03 -06) Object 3 --- We performed theoretical simulation of possible structures, interactions between molecules, and the affect of adsorbed water molecules to the structural stability of iodine. Structural and dynamical properties of the localized iodine molecules were studied by means of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. It was found that the iodine molecules in the AEL channels are restricted in the (101) planes with only two favorite orientations: lying along the channels and standing along the major axes of the ellipses, well in consistent with experimental observation. The iodine structures are largely dependent on the loading level: with the increase of loading, the iodine specimens change their structures from isolated molecules as in the gas phase to molecular chains. The simulation results show that the standing iodine molecules in the AEL channels are well restricted due to both the appropriate size of ellipses and their alternation throughout the channels. The confined iodine molecules with such structures and properties may be used to improve the accuracy of the frequency standards. (see paper 02 and 05). Object 4 --- We studied regular optical properties of the localized iodine molecules. An iodine molecule trapped in the AEL crystal has an effective internuclear potential close to an ideal harmonic oscillator, while that in the AFI crystal behaves similarly to that in free space. The results are further confirmed by measuring the temperature dependence of Raman spectral width. (see paper 03 and 04). From the Raman scattering study, we developed an interesting and very valuable technique using visible laser light to measure sub-nanometer atomic van de Waals diameter, which is far beyond the optical diffraction limitation. (see papers 06 and 07). Object 5 --- Utilizing the “femtosecond optical frequency comb” technology, we studied the hyperfine structure of the B→X transitions of the localized iodine molecules, to see the effects from the confinement on the transition levels. Because of the mechanical boundary of the channel wall, the vibration energy level in the electronic excitation states are obviously blurred. How to explore quantum information from the blurred vibration states is an interesting topics that need to be further studied.

604210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604210.value: Individual molecules usually exist in a gas phase or in diluted liquid solvents. In both cases, the molecules are keeping motion with random orientation. In these molecular systems, the optical spectral width is broadened and the polarization information can be hardly observed from the motion molecules. In this project, we succeeded in localizing diatomic iodine molecules in nano pores of solid zeolite single crystals with a well-defined orientation. The guest molecule system can be easily handled and accessed optically. The system provided us an ideal plateau to investigate the intrinsic properties in electronic states, binding and vibrations and polarizations. The diatomic iodine molecules are frozen in the elliptical nano pores of zeolite AEL single crystals, which make us possible to measure the atomic radius even using visible laser light beam. The localized molecules have no more thermal translational motion, and thus the electron transition frequency is very narrow in spectrue and very stable against thermal environment, the stable transition frequency could potentially be used as a time standard, e.g., molecular clock.

604310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604310.value: Many cell-signaling events occur at the plasma membrane, where membrane-bound protein receptors acquire extracellular stimuli and trigger the release of intracellular second messengers through a sequence of tightly regulated protein interactions. Acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) are such a kind of protein receptors on the postsynaptic membrane of muscle cells. They receive neurotransmitter stimuli from neuromuscular junctions with nearby presynaptic nerve terminals. Evidently, the lateral motion of AChRs plays an essential role in determining the response of muscle cells to neurotransmitter stimuli. Because of the complex interactions of AChRs with the underlying cytoskeleton and other constituents of the membrane, the motion of AChRs reveals considerable lateral heterogeneity in membrane structure and is not well understood. Several models, including lipid rafts and hop diffusion, have been proposed but they are largely at a qualitative level and no mathematical model is available to quantitatively describe the statistical properties of the interacting proteins. In this proposal we present an experimental program to study the diffusion dynamics of AChRs on the plasma membrane of Xenopus muscle cells in culture. The AChRs will be linked to fluorescent quantum dots and we will track their trajectories with nanometer accuracy over a broad range of times. In one set of experiments, we will study non-equilibrium (active) fluctuations and transport properties of AChRs by measuring their mean-squared displacement and the probability distribution function of the instantaneous displacements with sufficient statistics and under different sampling and cell conditions. In the second set of experiments, we plan to study protein interactions and viscoelastic properties of the plasma membrane using two-particle microrheology. We will measure the mean-squared relative displacement between two AChRs, their pair correlation functions, and the occupation statistics of AChRs on the membrane. The proposed study will contain both the exploration of new physics in non-equilibrium living systems and the investigation of diffusive transport of membrane-bound proteins, which plays an important role in many aspects of cell biology. Such a study is also of current interest in soft matter physics for our general understanding of two-dimensional motion of macromolecules over a complex interaction (energy) landscape. In the experiments, we will investigate universal features of non-equilibrium dynamics in living cells using modern methods of statistical physics, and also explore and characterize special behaviors of AChRs on the plasma membrane. Emphasis will be placed on quantitative characterization and understanding of the dynamic process and physical mechanism of anomalous diffusion in living cells. 大量細胞信號傳導發生在細胞膜上，其中細胞膜附著蛋白可以感受到胞外刺激並通過一系列嚴格調控的蛋白反應引發胞內第二信使的分泌。分佈在肌肉細胞突觸後膜上的乙醯膽鹼受體(AChR) 就是這樣一種細胞膜附著蛋白。這種受體的作用是從附近的神經末端突觸所在的神經肌肉連接處接受神經遞質乙醯膽鹼的刺激。顯然，乙醯膽鹼受體在細胞膜上的橫向運動對肌肉細胞對神經刺激的反應具有決定性的作用。由於AChR同細胞內細胞骨架和膜上其他成分的複雜作用，AChR的運動展示了膜的橫向結構存在具大的差異性。目前人們對AChR的橫向運動還沒有很好的解釋。現有的一些假說模型，包括脂筏和跳躍擴散模型，多從定性方面作描述，而對於蛋白分子動力學反應的定量數學模型還沒有出現。 在這份提案中，我們提出了一個研究非洲爪蟾肌肉細胞膜上乙醯膽鹼受體動態擴散的實驗方案。我們用微小量子點(quantum dot)對AChR作螢光標記，然後在一個很寬的時間範圍內在納米尺放上對它們的運動軌跡作跟蹤。在一組實驗中，我們會通過在不同的樣本和細胞條件下測量統計平均平方位移和即時位移的概率分佈函數並利用足夠統計量來研究AChR的非平衡(主動)漲落和輸運特性。在另一組實驗中，我們計劃利用雙粒子微流變技術來研究蛋白間的相互作用和細胞膜的粘彈性。具體的做法是測量兩個AChR分子之間的相對平均平方位移，它們的相關函數，以及AChR在膜上的位置統計分析。 上述提出的研究包括對非平衡態生命系統中新的物理問題的探索和對在細胞中擔任多重重要角色的膜附著蛋白的生物學問題的研究。這項研究同時也是在軟物質物理研究中有關大分子在複雜二維(能量)曲面下運動的一個研究熱點。在這項實驗中，我們將會用現代物理學方法研究活細胞中非平衡的動態普適特徵，同時也探索細胞膜上AChR運動的特殊性質。我們的研究重點是定量描繪並解釋活細胞中的異常擴散的動態過程及物理機制。

604310.label: Realisation of objectives
604310.value: To fulfill the two research objectives, we have carried out two projects to study lateral motion of proteins and lipids on live cell membrane. In one experiment, we studied the diffusion dynamics of acetylcholine receptors (AChRs), which is a trans-membrane protein, and lipid molecules (GM1s) on the live Xenopus muscle cell membrane. In addition to the measurement of the mean-squared displacement (MSD) of the proteins and lipids, we also measured the probability distribution function (PDF) of the instantaneous displacement with sufficient statistics and other statistical properties of the trajectories of the membrane molecules. Surprisingly, we found that while the measured MSD at long time has the standard diffusion behavior, the PDF of the instantaneous displacement under different cell conditions has a universal non-Gaussian (exponential) form, independent of the duration of time lapse and the origin and cultured days of the cells. The exponential PDF suggests that AChRs and GM1s have a broad distribution in diffusion times or diffusion coefficients (dynamic heterogeneity). In the second experiment, we carried out a parallel study of diffusion dynamics of model colloidal particles over a periodic energy landscape. Here we used an external potential field to mimic the effect of an interaction landscape imposed by the surrounding molecules on the cell membrane and by the underlying cytoskeleton cortex to a tracer protein or lipid. Energy landscape is an important concept in science and its applications can be found in many areas of physics, chemistry and biology. There are few experimental systems in which one can actually visualize the energy landscape, and thus much of the work done so far is through computer simulations. A physical model system in which one can directly measure the energy landscape and track individual particle trajectories would be extremely valuable in testing different theoretical ideas. In this experiment, we developed a two-layer colloidal system to study colloidal diffusion over a periodic energy landscape. This work opens up a whole new realm of investigation at the single-particle level for a range of interesting problems associated with the diffusive and forced barrier-crossing dynamics over complex energy landscapes. An important aspect of this research is the education of PhD students. This grant has supported the research of five PhD students. Among them, the thesis work of Miss Wei He and Mr. Xiaoguang Ma constitutes a major part of the planned research in this grant.

604310.label: Major findings and research outcome
604310.value: (1) Test of the universal scaling law of diffusion in colloidal monolayers. In 1996, Dzugutov (Nature, vol. 381, 137) proposed a universal scaling law for dense liquids, which connects the normalized diffusion coefficient D* with the excess entropy S per molecule relative to an ideal gas, D*=A exp(S), where A is a numerical constant. In this work, we conducted the first experimental test of the scaling law via simultaneous measurements of the diffusion coefficient and pair correlation function in colloidal monolayer suspensions. It was found that the universal scaling law holds well for highly charged polystyrene spheres suspended at an air-water interface, where the strong electrostatic interactions play a dominant role. For monolayer suspensions of hard-sphere-like particles, where the hydrodynamic interactions (HIs) become important, deviations from the universal scaling law are observed. The experiment reveals an interesting way to include the HIs into the universal scaling law of diffusion. This work was published in Physical Review Letters, which is a prime journal in physics. (2) Colloidal diffusion over a periodic energy landscape. In this experiment, a two-layer colloidal system was developed for the study of diffusive barrier-crossing over a periodic energy landscape. The energy landscape is made from the bottom layer of colloidal spheres forming a honey-comb crystalline pattern above a glass substrate. The obtained population probability histogram P(x,y) of the diffusing particles was used to fully characterize the energy landscape U(x,y) via the Boltzmann distribution. The long-time diffusion coefficient D was found to be in good agreement with the theoretic prediction. The experiment demonstrated the applications of the newly constructed colloidal energy landscape. This work was published in Soft Matter and was featured on the cover page of the issue. (3) Dynamic heterogeneity and anomalous diffusion of AChR receptors on live muscle cell membrane. In this experiment, we carried out a systematic study of the diffusion dynamics of acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) on the live muscle cell membrane. The AChRs are linked to fluorescent quantum dots and we track their trajectories with nanometer accuracy over a wide range of times. For the first time, we measured the probability distribution function (PDF) of the instantaneous displacements and found it has a universal exponential form. Furthermore, we showed that the exponential PDF results from an exponential distribution of the diffusion coefficients. A theoretical model was developed to explain the experimental findings. We have finished a manuscript which will be submitted to PNAS shortly.

604310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604310.value: The research discussed above demonstrated the usefulness of having two parallel systems to study the diffusion dynamics of individual molecules in a complex interaction landscape with one system being the actual living cell membrane, which is the target for the research but has many levels of complications and unknowns. The other system is the monolayer suspension of colloidal particles, which serves as a physical analogue of the crowded tow-dimensional membrane with known interactions between the particles but without any active (life) component. For the latter system, one can use different external potentials to mimic the energy landscape in the cell membrane and test different theoretical ideas. These two systems open the door to have a parallel study of a range of interesting phenomena in the cell membrane at the single-particle level. So far we have only studied the effects of simple periodic potentials and it is certainly very interesting to further extend our study to more complex energy landscapes of biological relevance, such as the energy landscape with hierarchy structures. We plan to seek additional funding to support the research in this direction.

604310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604310.value: Many cell-signaling events occur at the cell membrane, where membrane-bound protein receptors acquire extracellular stimuli and trigger the release of intracellular second messengers. Acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) are such a kind of protein receptors on the postsynaptic membrane of muscle cells. Evidently, the lateral motion of AChRs plays an essential role in determining the response of muscle cells to neurotransmitter stimuli. In this research we studied the diffusion dynamics of AChRs at the single-molecule level using the techniques of florescence microscopy and single-quantum-dot tracking. The measured AChR trajectories were found to be quite heterogeneous; some move fast and appear to diffuse randomly and others are transiently confined to small domains on the membrane. This dynamic heterogeneity is best characterized by an exponential distribution of AChR’s instantaneous displacement. Further theoretical modeling and measurements confirmed that this non-Brownian behavior of the AChR’s motion results from a broad exponential distribution of the diffusion coefficients. In addition, a parallel study of diffusion dynamics of colloidal particles was carried out, in which we used an external potential field to mimic the effect of an interaction landscape. Our experiments demonstrated the importance of quantitative characterization and understanding of the physical mechanism of anomalous diffusion in living cells.
