604410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604410.value: There are broad interests in organic semiconductors because of their chemical tenability, low cost, and ease in processing. Many devices such as light emitting diodes, solar cells, photodetectors, and field effect transistors have been fabricated based on organic semiconductors. Recently, the magnetic field effect observed in non-magnetic organic semiconductors started to receive increasing attention. Due to its large value and high sensitivity (up to 10% change in a relatively small magnetic field (~50 mT)) at room temperature, the magnetic field effect in organic semiconductors has a potential to be utilized for developing organic magnetic electronic and optoelectronic devices. In addition, a better understanding of the magnetic field effect can help us to improve our understanding of charge transport, change generation, and charge capture in organic electronic and optoelectronic devices. In our recent research, we found that the magnetic field effect in small molecule semiconductor NPB (N,N′-di(naphthalene-1-yl)-N,N′-diphenyl-benzidine) is sensitive to the device structure, light illumination, and device operation conditions. Therefore, we propose here to carry out a systematic study of the magnetic field effect in organic semiconductors. We will start with commonly used small molecule organic semiconductors and extend our work to semiconducting polymers. We will investigate the influence of the device structure, doping, light illumination, and device operation conditions on the magnetic field effect. We aim to obtain a correlated physical picture of the effect and try to establish a common understanding of the effect. 人们对有机半导体的广泛兴趣起因于它的制作工艺简单、多样、成本低。如今有机发光二极管、有机太阳能电池、有机场效应晶体管均已实现。最近人们对非磁性有机半导体中的磁效应的关注日益增加。因为实验观察到的磁效应对小磁场（~50mT）极为敏感（高达10%的变化）且发生在室温，所以有机半导体中的磁效应有潜力被应用于有机电子和光电子器件中。另一方面对有机半导体中的磁效应产生的物理机理的理解有助于对有机电子和光电子器件中电荷传输、电荷产生、电荷俘获的过程有进一步理解。在最近进行的小分子有机半导体NPB(N,N′-di(naphthalene-1-yl)-N,N′-diphenyl-benzidine)的磁效应研究中我们发现磁效应对器件结构、光照、器件工作条件很敏感，因此我们提出对有机半导体中的磁效应进行系统性的研究。我们将先针对小分子有机半导体进行研究，然后扩展至高分子有机半导体。我们的研究主要集中在器件结构、掺杂、光照、器件工作条件对的磁效应的影响。通过这项研究我们期望能对有机半导体中的磁效应的物理图象和机理有一个全面的理解。

604410.label: Realisation of objectives
604410.value: The magnetic field effect (MFE) is found in both semiconducting small molecule materials and polymers. MFE observed in experiments have some common features such as: (i) they are independent of the magnetic field direction; (ii) their sign can be positive or negative depending on materials and/or operating conditions of the device. MFE can have two distinct origins. One is charge-transport based and the other is excited states, i.e., singlet/triplet intra-molecular excitons and/or inter-molecular electron-hole pairs. We aim to reveal the fundamental mechanisms of magnetic field-dependent excited states and charge transport. As a result, we have carried out experiments on MFE in photoluminescence (MPL), electroluminescence (MEL), and photocurrent (MPC). We have studied the influence of the device structure and operation condition on MPC and the doping effect on MPL and MEL. Based on above correlated experimental results, we can conclude that MPL, MEL and MPC are all resulted from triplet exciton – polaron interactions.

604410.label: Major findings and research outcome
604410.value: 1. The MFEs on PL and the energy transfer processes in a doped OLED, a doped Alq3 and a doped NPB device are investigated. It shows that the magnetic field has no effect on the direct photon absorption and emission process of organic molecules but affect the energy transfer process from NPB and Alq3 to DCJTB. The magnetic field induced change of PL intensity for DCJTB emission is found to be much more prominent in the doped NPB device than that in the doped Alq3 device. We propose that the triplet exciton – polaron interaction is responsible for the observed MFE on DCJTB PL. This work was presented in the 31st International Conference on the Physics of Semiconductors. 2. We investigate the MFE on EL of OLED both without and with fluorescent dopant at room temperature. We observe at high magnetic fields, the EL of doped OLED decreases with increasing magnetic field, while opposite behavior is observed for undoped OLED. The magnetic field induced decrease of triplet-polaron interaction rate might be responsible for the sign change. This work was presented in the 16th International Workshops on Inorganic and Organic Electroluminescence. 3. We investigated MFEs exerted on photocurrents in NPB based devices at room temperature. By varying the layer thickness, applied bias, and interface condition, we achieved interface-exciton/polaron pair-dissociation-dominant and bulk-polaron-detrapping-dominant photocurrent responses. We clearly observed an intermediate MFE (~ 28 mT) that was not reported. A trion model has been proposed and the different zero-filed splitting for triplet-exciton/free-polaron-quenching and triplet-exciton/trapped–polaron-detrapping results in the different characteristic magnetic fields. This work was presented in the 32nd International Conference on the Physics of Semiconductors. 4. We have extended our study to demonstrate a new ZnSe/CdSe/ZnSe nanotube as the sensitizer for photoelectrochemical solar cells and achieve about 6.20% PCE. The TRPL data have supported the superior charge separation and collection in this structure. This work was published in J. Am. Chem. Soc. 5. We have also demonstrated an organic solution process to produce a quasi-QW structure (ZnSe/CdSe/ZnSe) on ZnO nanotetrapods. Single nanorod PL reveals that our quasi-QW has as narrow fwhm and 17 times higher PL intensity than ZnO/HJ. The TRPL study shows that ZnO/QW has a much longer lifetime than ZnO/HJ. The incorporation of 2D geometry on a 1D nanowire brings novel properties desirable for the new generation of bioprobe and photovoltaics. This work was published in ACS Nano.

604410.value: Research on organic semiconducting materials has largely been motivated by device applications such as organic light emitting diodes, field-effect transistors, and organic solar cells. The current project indicates that MFEs are a power tool to experimentally investigate charge generation, charge transport and charge capture in organic light emitting diodes, field-effect transistors, and organic solar cells.

604710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604710.value: Electrorheological (ER) fluid, especially GER (giant electrorheological) fluid, which is considered as a kind of smart material has been applied to the microfluidic systems to achieve active and precise control of fluid by electrical signal, while microfluidics, especially droplet microfluidic attracts more and more researchers from diverse fields, because it requires fewer materials and less time for the experiment, produces less waste and has the potential of highly integrated and computer-controlled activities. In this project, we will employ our recent achievements in microfluidic droplet manipulation and GER fluid droplet digitalization carried out in microfluidic system to realize a complete droplet logic system. A total of 16 logic gates will be designed to one single structure and the droplets would carry on logic by themselves, instead of obeying the electronic logic commands from the outside circuit. This is a first attempt to use GER fluid as the basic operational media for micro fluidic logic manipulation. The successful demonstration of ER fluid-based logic gate would be a very promising event for both ER fluid as well as microfluidic applications. 電流變液體（ERF），是一種智能材料並已被應用到微流體系統實現精確地微流體控制。而微流體，尤其是液滴微流體吸引越來越多的研究興趣，因為它要求較少的材料和較少的時間進行實驗，減少廢物產生而且有高度集成和計算機控制的潛力。在這項目，我們將充分利用我們最近取得的ERF的成就和在微流體液滴操控方法進行數字化流體液滴操控，以實現一個完整的液滴的邏輯系統。共16個邏輯門將被設計為一個單一的結構進行液滴邏輯控制，而不是服從從外部電路的電子邏輯命令。這是第一次嘗試使用電流變液體作為基本的流體媒質的邏輯微流體操控。電流變流體為基礎的邏輯門是一個非常有前途微流體應用器件。

604710.label: Realisation of objectives
604710.value: We successfully achieved simple on-chip logic function IF and NOT, in which electrorheological (ER) droplet can indeed “think” logically. The designed delicate chip structure to realize the first microfluid universal logic device, where all 16 Boolean logic operations (according to two inputs) can be achieved: operating functions are defined only by power supply. Giant electrorheological fluid (GERF), introduced as the computing media, translates fluidic information into electronic and mechanic information back and forth, making this microfluid universal logic gate fully compatible with electronic devices. Our experiment shows that the fabrication is uncomplicated and the equipment required is quite simple. The configuration of on-chip electric circuit makes sure that all 16 logic operations could be achieved in one chip while arranging different voltage inputs. The results also demonstrate one of the logic operations, XOR gate. The results show that the output GER fluid exactly depends on the input signals. Although the GER droplet generation may have a little bit delay, the generated GER droplets could well present the relationship of two input signal droplets. Since the universal logic gate is the most basic component of digitalized computing, this invention promises to become the building block of microfluidic processors. We have also demonstrated two-input microdroplet-based universal logic gates using a liquid-electronic hybrid divider. All 16 Boolean logic functions have been realized by manipulating the applied voltages. Such novel platform consists of a microfluidic chip with integrated microdroplet detectors and external electronic components. The microdroplet detectors perform as the communication media for fluidic and electronic information exchange. Presence or absence of microdroplet at the detector translates into binary signal 1 or 0. The embedded micro-mechanical pneumatically actuated valve (PAV), fabricated using the well-developed multilayer soft lithography technique, offers biocompatibility, flexibility and accuracy for on-chip realization of different logic functions. The microfluidic chip can be scaled up to construct large-scale microfluidic logic computation. On the other hand, the microfluidic chip with specific logic function can be applied to droplet-based chemical reaction for on-demand bio- or chemical analysis. Our experimental results have presented an autonomously driven, precision-controlled microfluidic chip for chemical reaction based on the IF logic function.

604710.label: Major findings and research outcome
604710.value: The important findings of this project are described as following; 1) By using electrorheological fluid, we first designed and fabricated a universal microfluidic logic gate to realize all 16 Boolean logic operations. It is shown that all 16 logic operations could be achieved in one chip while only arranging different voltage inputs. 2) We first observed electrorheological (ER) effect in a single phase ER suspension composed of mono-dispersed dielectric particles from a microgravity experiment. A highly sensitive electro-rheometer is designed for the microgravity measurement and the results show that, in the microgravity environment, the particles can form stable single phase suspension without the suspending liquid which is usually necessary for the conventional ER fluid. It is found from the experiments that the size of the column structures formed by the particles exceeds the theoretical upper bound predicted by the conventional dielectric ER (DER) theory. Finite element method (FEM) is used to evaluate numerically the variation of the electric energy density with respect to the strain, and the results yield a good account of the measured data, especially in low field region. 3) The universal logic gate can be realized by liquid-electronic hybrid divider. Such novel platform consists of a microfluidic chip with integrated micro-droplet detectors and external electronic components. The micro-droplet detectors perform as the communication media for fluidic and electronic information exchange. 4) We first achieved the design and fabrication of the nanofluidic mixer comprising hybrid hydrophobic/hydrophilic micro-patterns on the top and bottom walls of the nanochannel. The unique feature of such mixer is that, without any geometric structure inside the nanochannel, the mixing can be realized solely by the hybrid surfaces. We attribute the mixing achievement to be caused by the convection and chaotic flows of two fluids along the hybrid surface due to the large surface-to-volume ratio of the nanochannel.

604710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604710.value: This universal logic gate could be brought into play in automatic microfluidic chemical reaction investigation, biological reaction and testing and drug screening. The microfluidic chip can be scaled up to construct large-scale microfluidic logic computation. On the other hand, the microfluidic chip with specific logic function can be applied to droplet-based chemical reaction for on-demand bio- or chemical analysis. It is also noted that the potential applications of single phase ER fluids may be used in the outer-space and the adopted experimental method is valuable to study more complex colloidal systems.

604710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604710.value: Electrorheological (ER) fluid has been widely studied on the macroscale as a type of ‘smart’ material. An ER fluid is a fluid which transforms to solid form on application of a sufficiently strong electrical field. More recently, a new type of ER fluid was developed with giant electrorheological (GER) effect. It consists of urea-coated nanoparticles suspended in sunflower oil. Under a sufficiently strong electric field, GER fluid can transform into an anisotropic solid, with a yield stress characterizing its strength. These rheological variations can occur within 10 milliseconds and are reversible when the field is removed. The GER fluid can work as a digital fluid if a coded electrical control signal is provided to control the fluid. Therefore, like electronic logical gate, ER fluid-based logical gate can also realize all logical function which is used for computing and other applications such as preciously chemical reaction and materials fabrications.

604910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604910.value: 在過去的幾年裡，理論物理學家提出了一種全新的材料稱為拓撲絕緣體存在的可能性。這些奇特的材料擁有稀有的特性--他們的內部完全絕緣，但表面是導電的。更重要的是，其載流電子的熱耗散很少和每個電子的流動方向亦決定了它的自旋方向。預計這些屬性即使在室溫下亦存在， 帶出了幾種可實現的應用，包括製造更有效率和更小的晶體管, 其信息傳輸是通過電子的自旋。預計這些材料還擁有實現量子計算功能所必須的特性。 從去年開始，實驗和理論的研究取得了快速的進展，現在有確實的證據顯示Bi1-xSbx 合金, Bi2Se3, Bi2Te3, 和Sb2Te3這些材料的塊狀晶體的確是拓扑绝缘体。在迄今為止所發表的實驗都是用X射線把表面的電子激發出來以研究這些塊狀晶體的表面。但僅僅用這種方法并不足以揭示人們所預計在這些材料的表面存在的所有不尋常的傳輸現象。在這個項目中，我們將會用分子束外延（MBE）技術生長出高純度的和高結構完整性的Bi2M3 (M = Te, Se or S)薄膜。我們將用適當的化學替代以研發出可行的摻雜方案或者用電柵控制的方法把這些材料調整到拓扑傳輸範圍以揭示其拓扑傳輸行為的特徵。 我們提出的研究項目在兩方面具有重要意義。首先，我們可以把在現代電子學已經開發的先進處理技術應用到以薄膜形式存在的拓撲材料上。其次，也許更為重要的是，拓撲薄膜材料是觀測現代理論所預計的有趣現象所必需的平臺。 因為我們過去已經對Bi和Sb的超晶格以及Bi2Te3, Sb2Te3, Bi 0.92Sb0.08外延薄膜的磁傳輸性質進行過研究，所以我們有優勢去開展所建議的項目。此外，我們具有半導體薄膜、量子井和超晶格的分子束外延生長，以及為得到所期望的傳輸性能對其進行摻雜的豐富經驗。尤其是我們最近發現Bi2Te3能夠以原子逐層疊加的方式生長出具有原子平整度表面的薄膜。這一發現對我們的項目非常有意義。 我們正處在一個很好的位置進行擬議的項目，因為我們一直在磁輸運性質的外延薄膜的Bi2Te3，Sb2Te3，畢 0.92Sb0.08，與超晶格的鉍和銻過去。此外，我們還 豐富的經驗，在分子束外延生長半導體薄膜，量子阱與超晶格中摻雜以及他們給所需的運輸特特別是，我們最近發現，Bi2Te3可以生長在一個原子層高產薄膜層模式與原子平面上。這一發現是我們的項目非常有用。

604910.label: Realisation of objectives
604910.value: We have successfully fabricated Bi2Te3-based thin films and heterostructures with very high crystalline quality by the MBE technique. Detailed structural, chemical, electronic transport, lateral and vertical magneto-transport characterizations of these samples have been carried out using high-resolution TEM, EDX, HRXRD, SIMS and low-temperature transport and magneto-transport techniques. We have performed pioneer work on the impurity effects of weak anti-localization of Bi2Te3 topological insulator thin films. A novel Pd/Bi2Te3 was used to study the electron bath effect arising from the topological surface states on the enhancement of surface absorption, The interface effect of of a Bi2Te3 thin film with an array of superconducting Nb strips was studied. We have also fabricated an anti-dot Bi2Te3 structure to study the quantum transport of the surface electrons and a novel Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure using Van der Waals epitaxial growth scheme, which demonstrates a rare two-dimensional superconductivity. An inverted superconducting FeTe/Bi2Te3 heterostructure fabricated by interfacial chemical reaction was realized and studies in terms of the growth mechanism, vortex dynamics and magnetic properties. We have already fabricated Bi2Te3 thin film devices with a top gate and studied the transport properties under a top-gate bias. However, since our as-grown Bi2Te3 is heavily doped n-type, the tuning of the Fermi level is very limited. Thus we were not able to achieve the creation of electrons and holes at the top and bottom surfaces of a thin layer of the topological materials to look for a superconductor-like phase driven by electrostatic binding of electrons and holes as predicted by theorists. We have also fabricated Bi2S3 thin films however the results of their electronic transoport characterizations indicate that they are highly insulating and hamper our further magneto-transport measurements to study whether they are topological insulators. As we have spent most of the time in the project period on the lateral magneto-transport measurements of the Bi2Te3 thin films and heterostructures to further investigate their novel and important physical properties discovered by us, we were not able to carry out any vertical magneto-transport measurements. Overall all the project objectives have been explored and significant results have been achieved and reported.

604910.label: Major findings and research outcome
604910.value: WAL effect in Bi2Te3 thin films was found to have contributions from both 2D surface states as well as from 3D bulk states. The 2D contributions are extracted from MR data obtained in tilted magnetic fields. The 2D WAL effect, which arises as a consequence of the Berry phase, is suppressed by magnetic impurities deposited on the surface of Bi2Te3 thin film, but it is almost unaffected by nonmagnetic impurities. The observed behavior of the magnetoconductance of a 5 nm Bi2Te3 film suggests our system crosses over from symplectic to unitary classes when Fe is deposited on the film surface (Part C: 8(1)). The formation mechanism of an MBE-grown superconducting Fe1+xTe/Bi2Te3 bilayer fabricated on a ZnSe(111)B buffer using chemical reactions between the flux provided by a Bi2Te3 cell and an annealed Fe layer was studied. The results of chemical and microstructural characterization performed on several samples grown with different desired schemes reveal that the formation of the superconducting bilayer structure involves several interfacial chemical reactions that occurred at the Fe/ZnSe interface through the edges of voids created during the annealing of the Fe layer (Part C: 8(4)). Transport measurements on a Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure fabricated via van der Waals epitaxy demonstrate superconductivity at the interface, which is induced by the Bi2Te3 epilayer with thickness even down to one quintuple layer, though there is no clear-cut evidence that the observed superconductivity is induced by the topological surface states. The two-dimensional nature of the observed superconductivity with the highest transition temperature around 12 K was verified by the existence of a Berezinsky–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition and the diverging ratio of in-plane to out-plane upper critical field on approaching the superconducting transition temperature (Part C: 8(5)). The quantum transport experiments on the topological insulator Bi2Te3 thin films with arrayed antidot nanostructures were studied. With increasing density of the antidots, a systematic decrease is observed in the slope of the logarithmic temperature-dependent conductivity curves, indicating the electronelectron interaction can be tuned by the antidots. Meanwhile, the weak antilocalization effect revealed in magnetoconductivity exhibits an enhanced dominance of electronelectron interaction among decoherence mechanisms. The observation can be understood from an antidot-induced reduction of the effective dielectric constant, which controls the interactions between the surface electrons. Our results clarify the indispensable role of the electronelectron interaction in the localization of surface electrons and indicate the localization of surface electrons in an interacting topological insulator (Part C: 8(7)).

604910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604910.value: Our recent discovery of a novel two-dimensional (2D) superconductivity at the interface of a Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure of which the two components are both non-superconducting (Part C:8(5). Our work provides the first example of interface superconductivity between a TI and iron chalcogenide. Due to the possible unconventional pairing symmetry of Fe-based superconductor, the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructures also provide new platforms for creating and studying Majorana fermions in a 2D template. The successful manipulation of Majorana fermions would facilitate a quantum leap in our computational and data storage abilities as these quasi-particles are ideal basic calculation units for a topological quantum computer. So far, the highest on-set superconducting transition temp (Tc) of this heterostructure is only around 12K and the underlying mechanism of the observed 2D superconductivity is still unrevealed. Our research team is planning to submit proposals (GRF and CRF) to perform several novel studies to reveal the physical origin and mechanism of the discovered 2D superconductivity of the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure, including the test of the hypothesis whether the topological surface states of a topological insulator and their magnetic effect or the strain built-in the interface of the heterostructure play a role in inducing the superconductivity.

604910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604910.value: This project targets to fabricate high-quality thin-film topological insulators and reveal their novel topological transport behaviors. Topological insulators have the unusual properties that they are completely insulating in the inside but conducting on the surface and are promising for a number of novel applications in spintronics as well as in quantum computation. Topological materials in thin-film form are essential for practical applications so that the advanced processing technology that has already been developed for modern electronics can be exploited. This project has developed reproducible approaches to fabricate high-quality Bi2Te3-based topological insulator thin films, heterostructures and nanostructures and demonstrated several novel and important topological transport behaviors such as the impurity effect on weak anti-localization in Bi2Te3 thin films and two-dimensional superconductivity at the interface of Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructures, which have shed some light on topological-insulator-based fundamental research and potential applications.

605010.value: 網絡優化中的源點位置問題

605010.label: Project Objectives
605010.value: To elucidate the physical properties of networks with optimal locations of the source nodes when the installation cost of the source nodes relative to the transportation cost of the links varies, and in particular, the dependence of these properties on the different phases with their characteristic cluster configuration of demand nodes, and the regimes of algorithmic hardness. To develop algorithms for optimizing the source locations in networks based on the cavity method, both as a support to the proposed theoretical analysis and as efficient algorithms for practical implementation.
rows: To elucidate the physical properties of networks with optimal locations of the source nodes when the installation cost of the source nodes relative to the transportation cost of the links varies, and in particular, the dependence of these properties on the different phases with their characteristic cluster configuration of demand nodes, and the regimes of algorithmic hardness.

To develop algorithms for optimizing the source locations in networks based on the cavity method, both as a support to the proposed theoretical analysis and as efficient algorithms for practical implementation.

605010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605010.value: Concepts and techniques developed in the statistical physics of magnetic materials have found many applications. In the proposed source location problem in network optimization, one is given a network of nodes and links. All nodes have resource demands, and the task is to locate the source nodes at some of them to provide resources to the others through the links so as to minimize the total cost, which is the sum of the installation cost of the source nodes, and the transportation cost of the resources along the links. This optimization problem is important in many applications, such as the placement of base stations in wireless sensor networks subject to bandwidth limitations in the channels linking the mobile sensors. The tradeoff between the installation cost and transportation cost is similar to the energetic considerations in many systems in physics and computational complexity theory. In these systems, the competition between the energy components leads to the presence of numerous nearly optimal solutions to the problem, rendering the optimization task computationally hard. In this project, we propose to study the properties of networks with optimized locations of the source nodes using the cavity method of statistical physics. We will study the cascades of transitions between phases with different cluster configurations of the demand nodes, when the transportation cost relative to the installation cost varies. The cavity method should enable us to propose optimization algorithms that operate by passing messages among the neighboring nodes. This has the advantages of reducing the computational complexity, and of remaining functional in the absence of global information. Practical algorithms will be tested on realistic networks with generic structures. 從統計物理中發展出的概念和技巧，已經得到廣泛的應用。這裡建議研究的問題，是網絡優化中的源點位置問題。網絡由節點和連線組成，每一節點都有資源上的需求。優化的任務就是要在適當的位置設置源點，使所有節點的資源需求都得到滿足，而總成本達到最小化，這裡總成本包括源點的設置成本，和連線上資源運輸的成本。這優化問題有許多重要的應用，例如在無線感知器網絡中設置基站的問題。問題中設置成本和運輸成本之間的平衡，與很多物理問題和計算複雜性理論中對能量最小化的考慮非常相似。在這些系統中，不同組成部份的競爭，會引致大量亞穩態的出現，使優化問題的計算變得困難。在這建議的研究中，我們將採用統計物理學中的空穴法，探討源點位置優化了的網絡性質。我們將研究當運輸成本與設置成本的比例改變時，系統產生一系列階梯狀的相變行為，其中每一相都有其獨特的源點排列狀態。運用空穴法，我們將提出在相鄰節點之間互相傳遞信息的優化算法，它的優點是降低計算複雜性，在不需要全局信息的情況下仍然順利運作。我們也會在有現實結構的網絡中，測試算法的實用性。

605010.label: Realisation of objectives
605010.value: First objective: a) Entropic effects: We found that the inclusion of entropic information improves the agreement between theoretical and simulation results. b) Locked-unlocked effects: In the color diversity problem, we demonstrated the existence of both paramagnetic and spin glass phases at zero temperature, alternating between networks dominated by even or odd connectivity, when the ratio of the nearest to next nearest neighbor couplings is an integer. c) Entropy gap effects: In the learning of examples in the binary perceptron, we found that an entropy gap exists among solution pairs, while the solution entropy shrinks to zero. This implies that clustering and freezing of solutions coexist, explaining why the solution search is so difficult. d) Frustration effects: We introduced repulsive interactions to optimize the on-off configuration in sensor networks, and observed all-on core effects, antiferromagnetic effects, edge effects, and modulation effects. e) Multi-scale effects: In networks with fast and slow time scales for the nodes and couplings respectively, we discovered that they can generate both static and traveling localized active states, speed up the tracking of external inputs, exhibit slow-decaying plateau behaviors, and temporal modulations. This provides a mechanism for neural systems to shut off short-term memories naturally, and hence might settle a long standing issue in neuroscience. We found a mechanism for a neural system to achieve real-time and anticipatory tracking, in agreement with head-direction experiments in rodents. We further found that temporal modulations enhance resolution of overlapping external stimuli, providing an explanation for transparent motion experiments in humans and monkeys. f) Chaotic effects: We found that ambivalent agents in a competing system exhibit chaotic behaviors. Second objective: a) Optimal source location problem: We derived an entropic message passing method and developed inspired decimation and reinforcement algorithms to identify the optimal location of sources in transportation networks. b) Color diversity problem: We developed exhaustive branch-and-bound search for small systems, extremal optimization for larger systems, and population dynamics for theoretical analysis. We computed the complexity function that describes phase transitions between paramagnetic and glassy phases. c) Path optimization in transportation networks: We employed the physics of interacting polymers and derived a simple, principled, generic and distributive routing algorithm capable of considering simultaneously all individual path choices in networks such as the London underground. d) Network dynamics: We found that the introduction of thresholds on temporally modulated activities in neuronal networks can enhance their information processing performances.

605010.label: Major findings and research outcome
605010.value: In the optimization of source locations in transportation networks, we derived the ground state entropy of network source location problems at both the replica symmetric level and one-step replica symmetry breaking level using the entropic cavity method [9]. The resulting entropic message passing inspired decimation and reinforcement algorithms identify the optimal location of sources in single instances of transportation networks. In the color diversity problem, we demonstrated a periodic variation of free energy, with either the ratio of nearest to next nearest couplings, or the mean number of nearest neighbors [5]. When the coupling ratio is integer, paramagnetic phases can be found at zero temperature. This is shown to be related to the locked or unlocked nature of the interactions. For anti-ferromagnetic couplings, spin glass phases are found at low temperature. We calculated the phase diagram and demonstrated the existence of dynamical transitions at zero temperature. In the study of the solution space for a binary perceptron, we elucidated the entropy landscape from a reference configuration and of solution pairs separated by a given Hamming distance in the solution space. We found an entropy gap, which provides a better understanding for the failure of local search algorithms [3,4,11]. In network dynamics with dynamical couplings, we showed that dynamical synapses with short-term depression in neural systems lead to real-time tracking [1,2]. The behavior of the anticipatory time agrees with head-direction experiments in rodents [6,8]. The parameter regions demonstrate the correlation between tracking performance and the system intrinsic behaviors. When the stimulus moves with the natural speed of the network state, the delay becomes effectively independent of the stimulus amplitude. We further found that temporally modulated activities in neuronal networks can carry information extra to spike rates [10]. They can explain the enhancement of resolution observed in monkey experiments. In traffic optimization in transportation networks, we employed the physics of interacting polymers and disordered systems and derived a simple, principled, generic and distributive routing algorithm capable of considering simultaneously all individual path choices, applicable to networks such as the London underground [7]. In network routing, we introduced a distributive optimization technique by iterating the chemical potentials of the nodes subject to friction on the links. In networks with local cost functions, we found chaotic dynamics. Agents with different resource levels display different degrees of chaos. Chaos diminished the cost savings locally.

605010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605010.value: a) Entropic message passing algorithms: This can be extended to optimization problems with multistable states. b) Color diversity problem: The extremal optimization algorithm can be applied to other hard optimization problems such as the optimization of on-off nodes in sensor networks. c) Distance landscape for the binary perceptron: The entropy gap found in the binary perceptron may be found in other hard optimization problems with discrete variables. d) Network Optimization: We have introduced anti-ferromagnetic couplings to reduce redundant information collection in sensor networks, but this introduces frustrations in sensor networks. We will study the extent of the frustration effects and whether message passing algorithms suffer from convergence problems consequently. Optimization techniques in sensor networks are applicable to robustness optimization of networks such as the power grid, wherein isolated link outages can result in cascade failures. e) Network dynamics with dynamical couplings: The discovery that temporal modulations can enhance the resolution in transparent motion indicates the potential of temporal modulations in encoding information in neural systems. f) Local cost functions on networks: We will consider how pricing policies can be introduced in network traffic to reduce the price of anarchy.

605010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605010.value: In the source location problem, one is given a network of nodes and links. All nodes have resource demands, and the task is to assign nodes at appropriate locations to be source nodes so as to minimize the total cost, which is the sum of the installation cost of the source nodes, and the transportation cost of the resources along the links. This optimization problem is important in many applications, such as the placement of base stations in wireless sensor networks. The tradeoff between the installation cost and transportation cost is similar to the energetic considerations in many systems in physics, where the competition between the energy components leads to numerous nearly optimal solutions, rendering the optimization task computationally hard. Some ambivalent nodes can act as either a source or a consumer. We found that this ambivalence should be taken into account in the solution search. We also made breakthroughs in related network problems, such as maximizing the color diversity on graphs, studying how the separation of solutions affect the hardness in the learning of examples, traffic optimization in transportation networks, the dynamics of neural networks, and chaos in networks of competing agents.

605210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605210.value: 蛋白質和RNA折疊及生物酶催化經常需要多個步驟並且伴隨多個中間物進行,這通常是在微秒時間內發生.快速測量這些過程的動力學是非常重要的;其中最關鍵的是能在一個相當的時間尺度內迅速地改變所研究生物分子的環境(例如,把蛋白質的緩衝液換成變性劑).由於現今計算模擬還太慢,我們仍然大量依賴於實驗測量.雷射技術能達到納秒級解析度,但是生物分子過程很少以這種方式來引發.在各種方法中最誘人的應該是改變生物分子變性劑的濃度--因為該方法可以對大部分生物分子體系產生較大的熱力學擾動;它是引發生物過程最常用的方法.“流動停止”和“流動淬滅”的技術可以在100微秒左右混合溶液,但是它們都要求極高流速(微升/秒)而消耗大量實驗樣品.最近基於微流體而發展的“流體動力聚焦”技術把溶液混合時間縮短到了10微秒,而且實驗樣品的消耗量也極小(皮升/秒).但是它最大缺點是由“預混合”而引起的漫長的“死”混合時間會帶來極大的不準確性. 我們這裡提出一個全新的方法,用電場來快速驅動帶電分子穿過相鄰溶液的介面從一種溶液進入另外一種溶液.不同于以往方法依賴于分子擴散來混合溶液,該方法並不需要把溶液進行混合,它只把感興趣的生物分子轉移了.微通道很窄,使得可以只加很小的電壓來取得很高的電場強度,在該電場下帶電生物分子的電泳速度遠遠大於擴散速度.因此,這些分子能以快於以往基於分子擴散的方法所能得到的速度進行轉移.理論計算表明在一個2微米寬的通道內生物分子可以在1微秒內就被移至新溶液內,比以前的方法快了2-3個數量級.如果加上預聚焦技術能進一步把分子需要移動的距離縮短.脈衝電場使得可以加更高的電壓並且優化條件可以消除分子擴散的幹擾.另外,我們提出的方法只消耗極小量的樣品(皮升/秒). 該計畫將為探測溶液中生物分子在微秒尺度的動態過程提供有力的工具,大大快於以前能達到的尺度.所得到的新資訊將賦予我們以往得不到的寶貴知識並更好地瞭解結構生物學的基本現象.

605210.label: Realisation of objectives
605210.value: For Objective 1, we fabricated and tested an electrically-driven microfluidic platform for rapidly transferring biomolecules among different flow streams in microfluidic channels. We used small molecules of fluorescent dyes as model to test the device and found that the molecules could be switched into a different flow stream when an electrical potential was applied perpendicular to the channel. For Objective 2, we evaluated the microfluidic systems that was tested above, including related electronics and optics, to increase the transferring rate of biomolecules from one flow stream to another. We expected that we could reach into the timescale range between microsecond and sub-microsecond. We increased the electrical potential up to 10 volts; however, any potential above ~4 volts generated gas bubbles rapidly and could foul the experiments because bubble formation would change the local flow of the solutions and also the distribution of electric field. We also tried to narrow the width of the microchannel to 5 micrometers. However, at this dimension, diffusion dominates the mixing process. The fastest mixing time scale we obtained is milliseconds. Because the results are not as good as we expected, we have not published the results yet. For Objective 3, we loaded fluorescently labeled protein molecules into the microfluidic chip; however, we could only obtain the mixing within millisecond timescale. We now change the strategy to trap protein molecules in liposomes (~100nm in diameter) and rapidly break the liposomes to expose the protein molecules to a new environment that is different from the inside of liposomes. We could choose electrical fields or laser to break the liposomes (because laser can heat the solution rapidly into high temperature and affect protein conformation, electric field may be more appropriate).

605210.label: Major findings and research outcome
605210.value: (1) We studied the perturbations of flow in microfluidic channel that is induced by different pumping mechanisms; we also studied its implications on various on-chip applications including on-chip cell culture. This study suggests that different flow-control systems (e.g., pumping and valving mechanisms) can play an important role in flow-related experiments. Although significant, these effects have never been studied previously. Our results are published in Lab Chip. (2) We explored the Y-shaped microchips that we proposed in this project for osmotic fragility test of red blood cells. The results are published in RSC Advances. (3) We used microchips to generate chemical gradients in microchannels for studying cell behaviors. Similar microchips were used to generate chemical gradients in hydrogels for interface tissue engineering of bone/cartilage. These results are published in Advanced Healthcare Materials, and Langmuir. (4) We developed a new composite of gold nanocrystals/polydimethylsiloxane that is optically transparent and can be conveniently heated locally in the channel for controlling the environments of reactions. This well-controlled heating mechanism within the microfluidic channels can be used to change the local temperature of protein solutions in the channel and to cause the conformational change of the proteins. The results are published in Advanced Optical Materials, and Advanced Materials. (5) We fabricated a microchip to conveniently trap nanoparticles and form aggregates in the channel; the adsorption of proteins and other biomolecules onto the surface of the nanoparticle aggregates can change their Raman signals. We developed a rapid, highly sensitive and label-free analytical technique on microchip for determining proteins using SERS. The results are published in Analytical Bioanalytical Chemistry. (6) In order to fabricate complex microfluidic networks for better flow control, we developed a technique that allowed to directly mold 3D printed structures in a single step for truly 3D PDMS microchips. The results are published in Microfluidics and Nanofluidics. (7) In exploration of new researches, we also studied the differentiation of stems cells by controlling the cellular environments such as micropatterns on cell substrates, mechanical strain of the substrates, and chemical embedment in biodegradation materials. These results are published in Advanced Functional Materials, ACS Applied Materials&Interfaces, Advanced Materials, and Biomaterials. (8) we were invited to write review articles on our research results. Three review articles are published in Advanced Materials, Accounts of Chemical Research, and Current Opinion on Biotechnology. (9) We published 18 papers in high-profile, peer-reviewed journals. 4 PhD and 1 MPhil students were partly supported by this project.

605210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605210.value: At the second half of the project, we met some difficulties in the project because the experiment results were not as we expected. We are now changing the strategy to trap protein molecules in liposomes (~100 nm in diameter), which we have already made; we are in the process of finding a proper method to rapidly break the liposomes to expose the protein molecules to a new environment that is different from the inside of liposomes. Following this project for even further development, we would like to apply the developed technique to the following areas. (1) Study the dynamic processes of some important proteins, folding of RNAs, or enzymatic reactions. (2) Collaborate with computational chemists and compare experiment results with computational data. It would also be interesting to genetically modify some amino acids in protein molecules to see the corresponding changes on the dynamic process of the proteins.

605210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605210.value: Rapid kinetic measurements are crucial for understanding protein folding, as well as enzymatic and chemical reactivities; however, these dynamic processes often take place in the microsecond/submicrosecond timescale. To probe these processes it is critical to rapidly switch the molecules of interest from one condition to another at a comparable timescale. Although computational simulations play an important role in our understanding of biomolecular dynamics since, they are currently still of limited value, requiring several months per microsecond of computational time on the fastest supercomputers for most biomolecular dynamical events. Currently, related data heavily rely on experimental measurements. Among all existing techniques, changing denaturant concentration is probably the most attractive method because it can generate a large thermodynamic perturbation on most biomolecular systems. The technique, however, can be difficult to initiate quickly because molecular diffusion of denaturants is typically slow. This proposed work combines flow control with microfluidic devices and electric field to abruptly switch biomolecules’ environment. Its success will provide a powerful tool for probing dynamic processes of biomolecules in solutions at sub-microsecond timescale, much faster than that could be obtained before. It will enable us to extract important information unavailable otherwise and thus to better understand some fundamentals of biology.

605410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
605410.value: 位錯陣和晶界的連續模型

605410.label: Project Objectives
605410.value: To derive continuum models for curved dislocation arrays and grain boundaries with multiple Burgers vectors and in multiple slip planes from the discrete models for dislocation interaction and dynamics. To derive a new dislocation based continuum plasticity theory. To apply the derived continuum models to the energetics and dynamics of general curved grain boundaries.
rows: To derive continuum models for curved dislocation arrays and grain boundaries with multiple Burgers vectors and in multiple slip planes from the discrete models for dislocation interaction and dynamics.
To derive a new dislocation based continuum plasticity theory.
To apply the derived continuum models to the energetics and dynamics of general curved grain boundaries.

605410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605410.value: Dislocations are line defects in crystals. The collective motion and interaction of large numbers of dislocations inside crystalline materials determine their plastic properties. The study of plasticity based on dislocations is very difficult due to the multiscale nature of dislocation modeling: on one hand, the interaction of dislocations is long-range; and on the other hand, there are many short-range interactions such as self-force, reaction, and multiplication that play important roles in the evolution of dislocation microstructures. Direct discrete dislocation dynamics simulations for plasticity are time-consuming and currently are limited only to small systems. Continuum plasticity theories based on continuous distributions of dislocations apply to much larger systems with neglect of many details of the dynamics of dislocations. The accurate incorporation of motion and interactions of dislocations in continuum plasticity theories is still a very challenging task. Dislocation arrays and networks are commonly observed in the course of plastic deformation, and are formed in many structures and processes such as grain boundaries, Frank-Read sources, dislocation pile-ups, and misfit interfaces in epitaxy. Recently, the PI has derived a continuum model from discrete dislocation dynamics model for curved dislocation arrays with single Burgers vector in a slip plane (Xiang, J. Mech. Phys. Solids, 2009). This model incorporates accurately both the long-range interaction and the self-force. In this proposed project, this continuum model will be generalized to dislocation arrays and networks with multiple Burgers vectors and in multiple slip planes, to incorporate accurately the long-range interaction and various short-range interactions for these dislocation structures. The derived continuum models will then be employed to study the energetics, structure, and dynamics of these dislocation arrays and networks. These results will give suggestions and physics for the possible terms and parameters in the framework of currently available continuum plasticity theories, and a new continuum plasticity theory will then be derived. Grain boundaries play important roles in the properties of polycrystalline materials. Low-angle grain boundaries can be modeled as dislocation arrays or networks. The classical dislocation model for grain boundaries applies to equilibrium planar grain boundaries. In dynamical processes, grain boundaries are generally curved due to the interactions with other microstructures or defects such as particles or extrinsic dislocations. The derived continuum models for dislocation arrays and networks from the discrete interaction of dislocations will be employed to study the energetics and dynamics of general curved grain boundaries consisting of curved dislocations. 位錯是晶體中的線性缺陷。晶體材料所含的大量位錯的運動和相互之間的作用確定了材料的塑性性質。由於位錯的多尺度性質，基於位錯的塑性性質的研究是非常困難的。一方面，位錯之間的相互作用是長程的。另一方面，在位錯結構的演化中，很多位錯的短程作用，比如自作用力，相互反應和復制有很重要的影響。基於離散位錯動力學模擬的塑性理論非常耗時，現在只能用於很小的系統。基於連續分佈位錯的連續塑性理論由於忽略了很多位錯運動的細節，則可以用於很大的系統。在連續位錯理論中精確地體現位錯的運動和相互作用是一個很困難的研究課題。 在材料的塑性形變過程中，經常可以觀測到位錯陣和位錯網絡，它們形成於很多微結構和過程中，比如晶界，Frank-Read 源，位錯堆積，和外延附生中的錯配界面等。對於位錯陣包含在一個滑移面並且只具有一個Burgers矢量的特殊情況，本項目主持人已經從離散位錯動力學模型推導出一個連續模型(Xiang, J. 605410.label: Realisation of objectives
605410.value: The three objectives of this project have been fully achieved. Objective 1: We have derived a continuum framework for dislocation structure, energy and dynamics of curved dislocation arrays and grain boundaries. The continuum framework is based on a very simple and accurate representation method for the orientation dependent continuous distribution of dislocations. The continuum formulations incorporate both the long-range dislocation interaction and the local dislocation line energy, and are able to describe dislocation structures with multiple Burgers vectors and different types of dislocation motion including both glide and climb. The continuum models are derived rigorously by asymptotic analysis from the discrete dislocation model. Mathematical properties of the derived continuum models such as their well-posedness are examined. Objective 2: We have developed a dislocation based continuum model for crystal plasticity incorporating the Frank-Read sources. The continuum model is derived accurately from the discrete dislocation dynamics model, and is validated by comparisons of the results with theoretical predictions and discrete dislocation dynamics simulations. We have also derived analytical formulas that generalize the traditional Hal-Petch relation into two dimensions without any adjustable parameters. The derived formulas of the yield stress are examined by direct simulations using our continuum model and discrete dislocation dynamics. Objective 3: We have investigated the following applications using the continuum models for grain boundaries and dislocation arrays. (1) We have studied the Peach-Koehler force on the constituent dislocations of slightly perturbed low-angle tilt boundaries by stability analysis. The dominant regimes of the long-range and local forces are discussed. (2) We have developed a simulation method for the dynamics of dislocation arrays based on the level set representation. The long-range nature of the stress fields of nonplanar dislocation arrays is discussed and is compared with that by a single dislocation. (3) Loss of coherency of the surfaces of misfitting spherical particles and how it influences the dislocation-particle interaction have been discussed using both the discrete dislocation dynamics model and the continuum model. (4) Structure and energy of low angle twist boundaries in fcc metals for all twist angles are studied using atomistic models and continuum models. A new analytical expression for grain boundary energy over the entire twist angle has been obtained.

605410.label: Major findings and research outcome
605410.value: Firstly, we have derived a continuum framework for dislocation structure, energy and dynamics of curved dislocation arrays and grain boundaries (X.H. Zhu, Y. Xiang, Commun. Math. Sci. 2012; J. Mech. Phys. Solids 2014). The continuum framework is based on a very simple and accurate representation method for the orientation dependent continuous distribution of dislocations. The continuum formulations incorporate both the long-range dislocation interaction and the local dislocation line energy, and both glide and climb motion of dislocations. We have developed two methods under this framework for dislocation structures on low angle grain boundaries and misfitting interfaces, including the method based on the Frank's formula and the energy minimization method. We showed that for any low angle grain boundary, the Frank's formula holds if and only if the long-range stress field in the continuum model is canceled out. Secondly, we have developed a dislocation based continuum model for crystal plasticity in a slip plane incorporating the Frank-Read sources. We have also derived analytical formulas that generalize the traditional Hall-Petch relation into two dimensions without any adjustable parameters. It is shown that the yield stress of a rectangular grain depends not only on the grain size, but also on the grain aspect ratio whose exact form is associated with the harmonic mean of the length and width of the rectangle (Y.C. Zhu, H.Q. Wang, X.H. Zhu, Y. Xiang, Int. J. Plasticity 2014). Finally, we have investigated the following applications using the continuum models for grain boundaries and dislocation arrays. (1) We have identified the dominant regimes of the long-range and local forces on the constituent dislocations of perturbed low angle tilt boundaries by stability analysis (X.H. Zhu, Y. Xiang, Scripta Mater. 2011). (2) We have developed a simulation method for the dynamics of dislocation arrays based on the level set representation (X.H. Zhu, S.Y. Dai, Y. Xiang, Int. J. Plasticity 2013). (3) Loss of coherency of the surfaces of misfitting spherical particles has been discussed using both the discrete dislocation dynamics model and the continuum model. (S.S. Quek, Y. Xiang, D.J. Srolovitz, Acta Mater. 2011; X.H. Zhu, Y. Xiang, J. Mech. Phys. Solids 2014). (4) Structure and energy of low angle twist boundaries in fcc metals for all twist angles are studied using atomistic models and continuum models. A new analytical energy expression over the entire twist angle has been obtained. (S.Y. Dai, Y. Xiang, D.J. Srolovitz, Acta Mater. 2013; 2014).

605410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605410.value: The continuum models derived in this project special arrangements of dislocations that lie in a slip plane or a grain boundary. Further development of the research includes generalizations of the continuum models to arbitrary dislocation distributions in three-dimensions, with incorporation of other short-range dislocation interactions in three-dimensions such as correlation of different dislocations, interactions with forest dislocations, and dislocation cross-slip etc.

605410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605410.value: Dislocation arrays and networks are commonly observed and play important roles in the plastic deformation of crystalline materials. Continuum plasticity theories based on continuous distributions of dislocations apply to much larger systems with neglect of many details of the dynamics of dislocations. We have derived a continuum framework for the underlying dislocation structure, energy and dynamics of curved dislocation arrays and grain boundaries. The continuum framework generalizes the classical continuum theory that applies to equilibrium grain boundaries to general nonequilibrium nonplanar ones. The continuum framework is based on a very simple and accurate representation method for the orientation dependent continuous distribution of dislocations, and incorporates both the long-range dislocation interaction and the local dislocation line energy. We have also developed a dislocation based continuum model for crystal plasticity in a slip plane incorporating the Frank-Read sources. These continuum models are derived accurately from the discrete dislocation models. The obtained continuum models have been employed to study the energetics and dynamics of dislocation arrays and networks on general grain boundaries and misfitting interfaces.

605610.label: Project Objectives
605610.value: I will decompose the structure set of multiaxial manifolds into simpler pieces. The decomposition is expected to happen along every two or four strata according to the natural stratification structure. For the special case of multiaxial spheres, I will explicitly compute the individual pieces in the decomposition in the first objective. This gives an explicit decomposition of the structure set and the isotopy classification. I will consider the implication of the computations in the first two objectives on the general properties of the stratified surgery theory such as the periodicity and the replacement property.

605610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605610.value: A manifold is the basic mathematical term that describes mathematical models in the natural and social sciences. The symmetry of manifolds, usually described as group actions on manifolds, plays a very important role in the study of such models. For example, various conservation laws in physics are essentially due to actions by certain types of Lie groups (or quantum groups in the case of quantum physics). The field of geometric topology revolves around the most important problems of analyzing the structures of manifolds, comparing different manifolds (the classification problem), and studying the symmetries of manifolds. Various attempts have been made to use the surgery theory to solve problems involving symmetry. However, the older methods were usually ad-hoc, the symmetries under study were usually described by finite groups or the circle group, and the underlying manifolds were usually smooth. Then Weinberger created the homotopically stratified surgery theory as a more systematic and comprehensive tool for studying the symmetries of topological (as opposed to smooth) manifolds with the symmetry given by finite as well as general compact Lie groups. In earlier works, we have established remarkable theoretical properties about the homotopically stratified surgery theory, such as the periodicity, functoriality and replacement (or decomposition) property. In this project, we will apply the theory to study manifolds with symmetries given by multiaxial actions. Such manifolds have very well behaved stratification structures and serve as a prototypical example of manifolds with symmetries given by positive dimensional groups. Yet not much is known about such manifolds, especially regarding the homotopy classifications. Indeed, compared with the vast knowledge about manifolds with finite symmetries, the literature on symmetries measured by positive dimensional groups (especially noncommutative ones) is rather limited. We expect that the theoretical properties we established about the homotopically stratified surgery theory can be very useful in such a study. Conversely, such a study can also shed more light on these theoretical properties. At the end, the project will substantially enrich our understanding of symmetries specified by positive dimensional groups. 流形是用於描述自然和社會的數學模型中基本和常用的數學概念。流形的對稱性可以由群作用來描述，並往往在對這些模型的分析研究中起了很重要的作用。例如物理中的許多守恆定律本質上來源於某種類型的群的作用。對流形的研究形成了數學中幾何拓撲這門學科，其中心問題是流形的結構，流形的分類，以及流形的對稱性。 隨著龐加萊猜想的解決以及相關工具（高維的換球術，低維的Thurston-Perelman幾何化理論）的建立和完善，流形的分類問題已經基本解決。然而，關於流形的對稱性仍舊有許多需要研究解決的問題。其基本方法是試圖將換球術推廣到具有對稱性的流形，從而解決對稱性問題。Weinberger的同倫分層換球術是其中最系統，最有效的理論。我早期的工作顯示，這種理論具有許多奇妙的性質，比如週期性，函子性，可換性，可分解性。 在新的研究計劃中，我將利用Weinberger的同倫分層換球術去研究帶有多軸作用對稱性的流形。這類流形具有清晰的分層結構，是帶有非離散群作用對稱性的流形的典型例子。然而數學界對這類流形仍然所知寥寥，特別是它們的同倫分類。事實上，與關於離散群作用對稱性的大量文獻相比，關於非離散（特別是非交換的）群作用對稱性的研究非常有限。我相信早期工作中建立的關於Weinberger的同倫分層換球術的奇妙性質可以用來研究多軸作用對稱性。反之，關於多軸作用對稱性的研究可以讓我們對這些性質有更深刻的理解。本計劃將會填補關於非離散群作用對稱性的一些空白。

605610.label: Realisation of objectives
605610.value: For a complex or quaternionic multiaxial manifold, we showed that the structure set decomposes into a direct sum of relative structure sets at every two strata. The decomposition implies the homotopy replacement property for half of strata. For the standard multiaxial sphere, we showed that the structure set is a direct sum of copies of Z and Z_2, and we calculated the exact numbers of copies. The computation implies that the suspension operation induces an injection on the structure sets of multiaxial spheres. In addition to the decomposition of the structure set of complex multiaxial manifolds, we also settled an old conjecture by Conner and Raymond, that the converse to an old theorem of Borel is false. Specifically, we constructed closed aspherical manifolds whose fundamental groups have nontrivial center, yet the manifold does not possess any topological circle actions.

605610.label: Major findings and research outcome
605610.value: For a complex or quaternionic multiaxial manifold, we showed that the structure set decomposes into a direct sum of relative structure sets at every two strata. The decomposition is essentially due to very special structure of the links in the orbit stratified space, for which we have a general decomposition results for the surgery obstructions as well as the structure groups. The decomposition implies the homotopy replacement property for the fixed points of half of the unitary subgroups. The structure set of the standard multiaxial sphere is a direct sum of copies of Z and Z_2. The exact numbers of copies are closely related to the number of schubert cells in the grassmannians. The computation greatly generalizes the classical result on the fake complex projective spaces. The computation of structure set of the standard multiaxial sphere implies that the suspension operation induces an injection on the structure sets. We also settled an old conjecture by Conner and Raymond, that the converse to an old theorem of Borel is false. Specifically, we constructed closed aspherical manifolds whose fundamental groups have nontrivial center, yet the manifold does not possess any topological circle actions.

605610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605610.value: The major remaining problem is the study of real multiaxial manifolds. The links in the orbit stratified spaces are more compacted, and more fundamental research is needed to understand such manifolds.

605610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605610.value: The research makes great advance in the understanding of homotopy classifications of actions on manifolds by positive dimensional and non-abelian groups. The only previous work for such actions were by M. Davis and W.C. Hsiang, under a serious numerical restriction. Our work does not impose such restriction. Moreover, our result has interesting interpretation in terms of the homotopy replacements of fixed points by certain subgroups, while the early replacement results were all about the fixed points of the whole action group. In another direction, we also settled an old conjecture by Conner and Raymond, that the converse to an old theorem of Borel on circle actions is false. Overall, the results we obtained in the project makes us understand much better the actions of positive dimensional groups on topological manifolds, especially the non-abelian groups.

605710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605710.value: TiO2 as potentially the most efficient and environmentally benign photocatalyst can be used for photodegradation of pollutants. Upon absorption of photons with energy higher than its band gap, the excitation from the valence band to the conduction band creats electron-hole pairs. It is these light-induced carriers that migrate to the surface and degrade the surrounding pollutants in contact. The photocatalytic activity is largely controlled by the light absorption, electron reduction and hole oxidation rates on the surface, and the electron-hole recombination rate. A larger surface area with a constant surface density of adsorbents often leads to faster surface photocatalytic reactions. On the other hand, the higher the crystallinity, the slower the recombination, thus the higher the photocatalytic activity. Therefore, photocatalysts with high surface area and good crystallinity in tandem with low cost, low environmental impact, and ability to absorb sunlight is ideal for photodegradation of pollutants. This project focuses on the synthesis as well as photocatalytic properties of ultrathin crystalline nitrogen-doped TiO2 one-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials with diameters ranging from 3 nm down to 4 Å, reaching the regime of atomic wires. As the wire diameter decreases from the nanometer to the angstrom (atomic) scale, the surface to volume ratio increases dramatically. In respect of the atomic wires with a diameter of only about one unit cell, almost all the atoms are on the surface, which will significantly enhance the photocatalytic activities. We will first develop chemical synthesis methods for the ultrathin non-metal-doped TiO2 1D nanomaterials, which emphasize the formation and controlled condensation of precursors. Secondly, we will elucidate the effects of size and doping of the ultrathin wires on their photocatalytic properties in the visible region of the electromagnetic radiation. Finally, to improve the stability and reusability of the photocatalysts, we will use silica mesoporous materials or nafion membranes as a support to disperse the ultrathin wire based photocatalysts. The outcome of this project includes a fundamental understanding of the formation mechanism of extremely thin wires, particularly the atomic wires, of anatase titania, and a roadmap for the application of these new nanomaterials, especially the N-doped TiO2 atomic wires, in photocatalytic degradation of pollutants in water and in air. More generally, the work will also promote exchanges between theory and experiments in fundamental studies of 1D systems and provide unique building blocks to construct high-performance devices in physical, chemical, environmental, and engineering areas. 二氧化钛是可用于光催化降解污染物的潜在最有效和环境友好的光催化剂。当受到能量高于带隙的光子激发时，其价带电子会跃迁到导带从而产生电子－空穴对，即光生载流子。这些光生载流子一旦迁移到表面，可以降解周围与其接触的污染物。 光催化活性主要受控于光的吸收，表面的电子还原率和空穴氧化率，以及电子－空穴复合率。一方面，较大表面积且恒定的吸附剂面密度往往使光催化剂具有更高的活性，从而导致更快的表面光催化反应。另一方面，结晶度越高，电子－空穴复合越慢，光催化活性越高。因此，降解污染物理想的光催化剂应该具有高比表面积，高结晶度，低成本，低污染而且对太阳光有较高的捕获能力。 该项目的重点是合成超细高结晶度的，氮掺杂的，直径在4埃到3纳米之间，达到原子尺寸级别的一维（1D）TiO2纳米材料，以及对其光催化性能研究。由于纳米线的直径从纳米减小到埃（原子）的级别，其比表面积大幅增加。就原子尺寸级别原子线而言，其直径只有单位晶格大小，几乎所有的原子都在表面，这将大幅提高其光催化活性。首先我们将开发一种化学方法合成出超细非金属掺杂的TiO2一维纳米材料，该方法关键点在于前体的形成和受控聚合生长。其次，我们将阐明在可见光区域内，尺寸大小和掺杂对超细纳米线的光催化活性的影响。最后，为了提高光催化剂稳定性和重复使用率，我们将用硅中孔材料或全氟磺酸膜（nafion）作为载体，以分散超细纳米线光催化剂。 这个项目的成果将包括对极细纳米线特别是锐钛型二氧化钛原子线形成机制的基本了解，并将为这些新纳米材料的应用，特别是氮掺杂的二氧化钛原子线对水和空气中的污染物的光催化降解的应用提供路线图。从更广义的层面上讲，该项工作将促进一维材料体系的基础理论和实验研究的交流，并提供独特的结构单元用以建制在物理，化学，环境和工程领域具有高性能的器件。

605710.label: Realisation of objectives
605710.value: Objective 1: We have achieved synthesis of monodisperse, size-tunable N-TiO2 wires by a nonhydrolytic two-step approach consisting of controlled precursor formation involving restricted esterification and precursor condensation. Surface N-doping was shown to be significant for stabilizing the atomically thin wires further because the amine molecules work as both a dopant and a surfactant. Oxygen, water and the ratio of oleylamine to oleic acid are essential to the formation of the N-doped TiO2 atomic wires. Through careful control, titania atomic wires with tunable N-doping levels from 4% to 8% or even higher have been obtained. The N-doping originates from amine oxidation, followed by reaction with the hydrolysis-activated Ti-OH groups, to form Ti-O-NHR species in a way of monodentate coordination on the titania atomic wire surfaces, which complements the bidentate coordination of oleate, snugly capping the TiO2 atomic wires, leading to the N-doping and the stabilization of the atomic wires. Objective 2: The ultrathin wires well as the precursor have been characterized by an extensive series of structural/spectroscopic techniques including TEM, UV-vis, PL, XPS, Raman, ESR and FTIR, which are valuable for understanding the N-doping and the formation mechanisms. We have demonstrated pronounced effects of size and N-doping on the electronic, optical, and phononic properties of the wires. In particular, the extreme size reduction has increased the electronic bandgap by >1 eV, and radically blue-shifted and broadened the phonon spectrum. The N-doping also introduced bandgap states, allowing to absorb the visible light. We also completed a comparative study of the titania wires (2.6 - 0.5 nm) in terms of their optical absorption as well as steady-state and time-resolved photoluminescence and shown the existence of different emissive species responsible for the appearance of high-energetic and low-energetic emission peaks of TiO2 atomic wires and nanorods. Objective 3: We have shown a facile surface doping of N-species on atomically thin TiO2 wires, which turned out to be an effective strategy to enhance visible light absorption for photocatalysis. We have demonstrated photocatalytic activity of the atomic wires for the degradation of methylene blue (MB) as a model reaction under visible light. The N-TiO2 atomic wires show much higher adsorbing and photo-degradation ability of dye molecules than the larger-sized nanowires and the commercial P25 nanoparticles under visible light. This owes to the exceptionally large surface-to-volume ratio and the surface N-doping of the atomic wires. We have also demonstrated the good recyclability of the titania atomic wire photocatalyst.

605710.label: Major findings and research outcome
605710.value: This project has not only realized the intended objectives but also achieved additional outcomes, resulting in a large number of high-quality publications. 1. We have achieved nonhydrolytic synthesis of monodisperse, size-tunable 5-0.4 nm N-TiO2 wires. Oxygen, water and the ratio of oleylamine to oleic acid are essential to the formation of the N-TiO2 wires. Through careful control, titania atomic wires with tunable N-doping levels from 4% to 8% have been obtained. (US patent number 8,840,863 B2, issued 23 Sept. 2014). 2. We completed a comparative study of the titania wires (2.6-0.5 nm) on their optical absorption as well as steady-state and time-resolved photoluminescence and shown the existence of different emissive species responsible for the appearance of high- and low-energetic emission peaks of TiO2 atomic wires and nanorods. (Nanoscale 5, 1465 (2013)). 3. Via surfactant directed self-assembly, we synthesized size-tunable mesoporous TiO2 microspheres (200-600 nm) for quasi-solid state DSSC. The 400 nm microspheres achieved >6.78% PCE due to the balanced light scattering, electrolyte permeation and charge collection. (J. Power Sources 196, 10806 (2011)). 4. Hierarchical WO3 flowers comprising porous single-crystalline nanoplates were synthesized by morphology-conserved transformation from an ammonium tungsten peroxo oxalate precursor. High LIB performance and high visible light photocatalytic activity were demonstrated. (Nano Research 5, 826 (2012)). 5. A 3-step protocol (etching, seed nucleation, and branching) was developed to achieve secondary branching of ZnO nanotetrapods and simultaneous N-doping, yielding an active network for photoelectrochemical water splitting. (Nano Letters 12, 407 (2012)). 6. High efficiency CdS/CdSe sensitized solar cells were demonstrated with a hierarchically branched double layer architecture, a ZnO nanorod array underlayer and a ZnO nanotetrapod top layer. A record PCE of 5.24% was obtained. (ACS Applied Materials & Interface 5, 4000 (2013)). 7. Via controlled synthesis of Co3O4 nanocrystals with different exposed surfaces anchored on graphene, we investigated the effects of surface structure on catalytic activity. The ORR active sites are the surface Co2+ ions, whereas the surface Co3+ ions catalyze CO oxidation. (Scientific Reports, 3: 2300 (2013)). 8. We designed a hierarchical electrode consisting of highly conductive NiCo2S4 single crystalline nanotube arrays branching from a flexible carbon fiber paper, showing high performance in pseudocapacitors. (Nano Letters 14, 831 (2014)). 9. By templating nanoparticle aggregates, we synthesized mesoporous TiO2 single crystals with different shapes, sizes and phases, which show superior photocatalytic performance to the amorphous counterparts. (ACS Applied Materials & Interface 5, 11249 (2013)).

605710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605710.value: This project has studied the formation mechanism of the size-tunable ultrathin titania wires and their special properties. The atomic wires are soluble and easily processable, and their synthesis is simple and scalable. This opens the way to access new material dimensions at the angstrom scale, which is anticipated to exhibit novel properties. Aside from being a new platform for fundamental research, these new materials are anticipated to serve as true 1D building blocks to construct new functional devices. This opens opportunities to explore the physical properties and application of the atomically thin wires. One of the potential further developments is the large-scale synthesis under controlled conditions to facilitate their applications. On the device application side, there is high potential for the ultrathin titania wires in solar energy devices. Initial experiments have already been done on the effective harvesting of visible light by the ultrathin N-TiO2 wires for photocatalytic degradation of organic molecules. The up-coming experiments will show their effectiveness in solar energy conversion.

605710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605710.value: Material properties depend on their sizes and shapes in the nanoscale regime. Titania is one of the most low-cost, environmental friendly, earth-abundant and useful materials for sustainable applications. This project has achieved and mechanistically the synthesis of nearly monodisperse anatase titania wires with sizes tunable between 5 and 0.4 nm, down to the smallest atomic dimension, by a nonhydrolytic two-step approach consisting of controlled precursor formation involving restricted esterification and controlled precursor condensation. Size-dependent and surface N-doping dependent properties have been demonstrated. Most importantly, photocatalytic activities of the ultrathin titania wires have been shown to be size dependent as well, with the atomically thin wires being the most photocatalytically active, indeed much more active than the commercial P25 titania nanoparticles. The proof of concept for designing the size-tunable ultrathin titania wires, dispersible in organic solvents, for sunlight harvesting has been demonstrated, opening the path for the development of the new generation nanostructured solar energy conversion devices with high efficiency and low cost.

606010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
606010.value: 空间随机模型的临界行为

606010.label: Project Objectives
606010.value: Prove phase transition results for the limiting processes of spatial SIR (susceptible /infected /recovered) epidemics in dimensions one, two and three; Prove phase transition results for spatial SIR epidemic models; Establish scaling limit theorems of spatial SIR epidemics and the spread-out percolation in dimensions four and higher; and Establish sharp asymptotics for the critical probabilities for the spread-out percolation in dimensions four and higher.

Prove phase transition results for spatial SIR epidemic models;
Establish scaling limit theorems of spatial SIR epidemics and the spread-out percolation in dimensions four and higher; and
Establish sharp asymptotics for the critical probabilities for the spread-out percolation in dimensions four and higher.

606010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
606010.value: This proposed research aims to study the critical behavior of several widely used stochastic spatial models, including the spatial SIR (susceptible /infected /recovered) epidemic model and the spread-out percolation processes. We will determine whether there are phase transitions for these models, for example, whether an epidemic model will experience extinction-survival transition as certain parameters change from one region to another. We will also establish scaling limit theorems for these models. The scaling limits are continuous (measure-valued) diffusion processes, and are much more tractable than the original models. We will further study the scaling limits, and derive analogous properties for the original models. Our results will allow one to predict macroscopic behavior of these models, like whether an epidemic will become extinct, how the infections are distributed over the space, and how widely the liquid percolates or the information spreads out. 此项目旨在研究几个被广泛应用的空间随机模型的临界行为，其中包括空间传染病SIR模型以及长域渗流模型。我们将研究这些模型是否存在相转移，比如，传染病模型里是否有消亡-生存相转移。我们将证明这些离散模型在尺度变化下会收敛到某些极限过程。它们是连续时间的测度值过程，跟原本的离散模型比较相对容易研究。我们会研究这些极限过程的相关性质，并对原来的离散模型也证明相关性质。这些结果将会揭示这些模型的一些关键性的宏观行为，比如传染病是否会消亡，疫情如何分布，以及它们的扩散范围等等。

606010.label: Realisation of objectives
606010.value: Objective 1 has been fully achieved. As to Objective 2, the work is close to be finished. There are a few technical difficulties which slowed down the progress of the work. The main challenge lies in establishing a uniform regularity property about the spatial distribution of the critical branching random walk. For super-Brownian motions, such a property was obtained in a 1991 paper by Barlow, Evans and Perkins, and further refined in my joint paper with Lalley and Perkins. For branching random walks, some related properties have been obtained in my 2011 paper with Lalley. However, the results therein, as sharp as they are, do not lead to the desired uniform regularity properties. Fortunately, after extensive research, recently I have more clear ideas about how to overcome these difficulties. Objectives 3 and 4 are work-in-progress collaborating with Ed Perkins, and we have made good progress so far. For these two problems, a major challenge is to prove a law of large numbers for the local time process of the branching random walk. We are close to finish the proof, which is unusually technical and difficult.

Establish scaling limit theorems of spatial SIR epidemics and the spread-out percolation in dimensions four and higher; and
Establish sharp asymptotics for the critical probabilities for the spread-out percolation in dimensions four and higher.

606010.label: Major findings and research outcome
606010.value: The PI, together with Steve Lalley and Ed Perkins, studied a process which arises as the scaling limit of the spatial SIR (susceptible /infected /recovered) epidemic model. We show that in dimensions two and three, there is an extinction-survival phase transition, while in dimension one, there is always almost sure extinction. Furthermore, we show that in all dimensions, there is almost sure local extinction. The results are collected in the paper ``A Phase Transition for Measure-valued SIR Epidemic Processes'', see part C. The PI also considered the discrete spatial SIR epidemic model, and is close to establish the analogous phase transition results for this model. As to the four and higher dimensional case, the PI is collaborating with Ed Perkins to study both the spatial SIR epidemics and the spread-out percolation. The four and higher dimensional case is significantly different from the three and lower dimensional case, and the asymptotics of the critical probability of the spread-out percolation is a long standing open problem. We have been making good progress towards solving this difficult problem.

606010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
606010.value: There are many interesting follow-up questions and extensions that are worth studying. One direction that I plan to investigate is the related models in random environments, where the environment is given by, for example, random conductances. The random environment can be used to model the spatially inhomogeneous situation which is closer to the real world.

606010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
606010.value: The models studied in this project are closely connected with many other interacting particle systems and have their own variants, which have wide applications in population biology, physics, information science and marketing. The results allow one to predict macroscopic behavior of these models, like whether an epidemic will become extinct, how the infections are distributed over the space, and how widely the liquid percolates or the information spreads out.
