610110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
610110.value: 解決幾何搜索難題的新方法

610110.label: Project Objectives
610110.value: Investigate the effect of semigroup properties on the computational complexity of (exact) halfspace range searching. Design data structures that offer better space-time tradeoffs for approximate nearest neighbor searching. Design a simple and unified framework for approximate proximity searching.
rows: Investigate the effect of semigroup properties on the computational complexity of (exact) halfspace range searching.
Design data structures that offer better space-time tradeoffs for approximate nearest neighbor searching.
Design a simple and unified framework for approximate proximity searching.

610110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
610110.value: Nearest neighbor and range searching are among the fundamental problems in Computational Geometry, with numerous applications. In both problems, the objective is to preprocess a set P of points in Euclidean space, so that queries can be answered efficiently. In nearest neighbor searching, we need to determine the point of P closest to a given query point, while in range searching, we need to count the points of P lying inside a query region. Both the exact and approximate versions of these search problems have been extensively studied in the past three decades. Despite these efforts, many intriguing questions in this area remain unanswered. In this grant, we propose to tackle these challenging issues with the help of new techniques. In particular, we will (a) investigate the computational complexity of exact halfspace range searching, (b) design data structures that offer better space-time tradeoffs for approximate nearest neighbor searching, and (c) design a simple and unified framework for approximate proximity searching problems. 最近鄰 (nearest neighbor) 和範圍搜索 (range searching) 是計算幾何中最基本的兩個問題，其應用非常廣泛。這兩個問題的目標是對歐式空間內的一個點集P進行預處理，使得一些查詢可以有效地被回答。在最近鄰搜索問題中，我們需要在P中找到和查詢點最接近的點；而在範圍搜索問題中，我們需要對P中位於查詢範圍內部的點進行計數。在過去三十年裏，這兩個問題的精確和近似算法都得到了廣泛的研究，但是仍有很多有趣的問題沒有被解決。在本課題裏我們將利用新技術解決這些具有挑戰性的問題。本課題具體分為以下三個方面：（一）研究精確半空間範圍搜索問題的計算復雜度；（二）為近似最近鄰搜索問題設計數據結構，並提供更好的時間-空間權衡；（三）為近似鄰近搜索問題 (approximate proximity searching) 設計一個簡單而統一的框架。

610110.label: Realisation of objectives
610110.value: Our first goal was to investigate the effect of semigroup properties on the computational complexity of halfspace range searching. In this problem, we are given a set of n points in d dimensions, where each point is associated with a weight from a commutative semigroup, and we need to compute the semigroup sum of the weights of the points lying within any query halfspace. We established new lower bounds for this problem in the semigroup arithmetic model, which nearly resolve the complexity of halfspace range searching in some important settings. Our paper (J1) describing this work has been published in the journal, Discrete and Computational Geometry (DCG). Our second goal was to design data structures that offer better space-time tradeoffs for approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) searching. We showed deep connections between ANN and the polytope membership problem, which resulted in the most efficient data structures for ANN in fixed dimensional Euclidean spaces. Our paper (C1) describing these results has been published in the Proceedings of the Symposium on Discrete Algorithms (SODA). My student Chan Yiu Wai and I applied techniques developed for polytope membership and ANN to the problem of maintaining an approximate Voronoi cell in the data stream model. This work constitutes his MPhil thesis. Finally, we have been working towards designing a simple unified framework for approximate proximity searching. Previous data structures were based on approximate Voronoi diagrams (AVDs), and were rather complcated. We have developed a simple framework based on compressed quadtrees, and used it successfully for fast approximate spherical range searching with both idempotent and integral semigroups. We are writing up these results for journal publication (J2).

610110.label: Major findings and research outcome
610110.value: We elaborate on some of the contributions mentioned in Section 5.3. In J1, we have made substantial progress on settling the computational complexity of exact halfspace range searching. Letting m denote the space requirements, we proved a lower bound for general semigroups of Omega(n^{1-1/(d+1)} / m^{1/(d+1)}) and for integral semigroups of Omega(n / m^{1/d}). Neglecting logarithmic factors, our result for integral semigroups matches the best known upper bounds. For general semigroups, our results nearly resolve the computational complexity of halfspace range searching in the important case of uniformly distributed point sets. In C1, we presented efficient data structures for the approximate polytope membership problem and showed that they lead to immediate improvements to the best space-time tradeoffs for approximate nearest neighbor searching. In the polytope membership problem, we need to preprocess a convex polytope, defined as the intersection of halfspaces, so as to efficiently determine whether a query point lies inside or outside the polytope. Assuming the polytope has constant diameter, the classical approach due to Dudley allows such queries to be solved approximately (error permitted if query point lies within distance eps of the boundary) in O(1/eps^{(d-1)/2}) storage and query time. We showed that, with the same storage bounds, we can improve the query time drastically to O(1/eps^{(d-1)/8}), thus reducing the exponent by a factor of four. Our results arise by replacing the classical approaches to convex approximation by a method that is more locally sensitive to the local geometry of the convex body. Our work on approximating convex polytopes led us to the question of approximating Voronoi cells in data streams. In light of the many applications of Voronoi diagrams to problems such as approximate nearest neighbor searching and motion planning, we believe this is an important issue to study. We showed that it is possible to eps-approximate a Voronoi cell using roughly O(1/eps^{(d-1)/2}) space and update time per insertion. This significantly improves existing results under the data stream model and is optimal in space up to a logarithmic factor. This work constitutes the MPhil thesis of my student Chan Yiu Wai. In J2, we have designed a simple unified framework for approximate proximity searching. The data structure is based on compressed quadtrees and is very simple. It can be used for range searching for smooth convex ranges over both idempotent and integral semigroups. Our data structure leads to nearly optimal space-time tradeoffs and is both simpler and more efficient than previous approaches.

610110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
610110.value: We have nearly resolved the computational complexity of halfspace range searching, designed more efficient data structures for approximate nearest neighbor searching, and designed a simple and unified framework for approximate range searching. Our work suggests a number of open problems for further investigation. In particular, even though we have resolved the complexity of halfspace range searching over idempotent semigroups for uniformly distributed points, there remains a gap for non-uniform data. Despite our improvements, there also remain significant gaps between upper and lower bounds for approximate nearest neighbor searching. It would be interesting to close these gaps in future work.

610110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
610110.value: Our study has helped to establish new lower bounds for halfspace range searching, which nearly settle the computational complexity of this fundamental problem. We have developed novel, more efficient data structures for approximate nearest neighbor searching, based on deep connections with the polytope membership problem. Finally, we designed a simple framework that helps to unify data stuctures for range searching problems in many different contexts.

610210.label: Project Title(Chinese)
610210.value: 关于灵活自由视点电视系统的调查

610210.label: Project Objectives
610210.value: Investigate pre- and post-processing of depth information, which are expected to be very useful to enhance the quality of the virtual view. Investigate correction for illumination and color discrepancy Investigate geometry correction and fast view rendering
rows: Investigate pre- and post-processing of depth information, which are expected to be very useful to enhance the quality of the virtual view.
Investigate correction for illumination and color discrepancy
Investigate geometry correction and fast view rendering

610210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
610210.value: Recent research and convergence of technologies from computer graphics, computer version, multimedia and related fields have enabled the development of new types of multimedia applications, such as 3DTV and free viewpoint TV (FTV). Significantly enhanced viewing experience expands the users’ sensation far beyond what is offered by traditional multimedia data. 3DTV systems provide a 3D depth impression of the observed scenery (also referred to as stereo) by displaying slightly different images to each eye of the viewer. FTV systems, on the other hand, provide the ability for users to interactively navigate and select a viewpoint in the video scene. However, there are tremendous challenges to enable the use of 3DTV and FTV in real-world applications, as the entire processing chain from multiview image capture, 3D scene representation, coding, transmission, rendering, to display has to be considered. In this proposal, we propose to investigate several key technologies enabling a flexible FTV system to achieve good visual quality while serving many users whose displays have very different capabilities. More specifically, we will study the pre- and post-processing of the depth images so that more accurate depth information could be obtained to facilitate high-quality virtual views interpolation. We also will address the illumination correction and color discrepancy problem to make the virtual view more compatible, and thus more realistic and visually pleasing. Furthermore, some low complexity and fast view rendering algorithms will be investigated to meet the real-time requirements for some practical applications. 新兴的3D电视和自由视点电视系统能够为用户提供增强的视觉体验，使用户能够感知深度并具有交互式功能。 3D电视使用特殊的3D显示器/监视器来为左右眼同时显示略有差别的图像，通过双目视差使观众感知深度。自由视点电视系统使用常规的高清显示器为用户同时提供自由视点和观看角度的选择，从而使用户通过运动视差来感知深度。最近，结合这两种技术为用户同时提供深度感知和用户交互成为一种趋势。 在这项提案中，我们计划调查几种能使自由视点电视系统达到良好的视觉质量并且可以运用到不同性能显示器的关键技术。更加具体地说，我们将研究对深度图的前处理和后处理，以使得到更加准确的深度信息来进行高质量的虚拟视点插值。 我们也将研究亮度校准和颜色差异的问题，以获得兼容性更强的虚拟视点，从而使视觉感受更加真实和愉悦。此外，一些低复杂度和快速渲染的算法也将被研究，以满足实际应用中对实时性的要求。

610210.label: Realisation of objectives
610210.value: In texture-plus-depth format of 3D visual data, the texture and depth maps of multiple viewpoints are coded and transmitted. The receiver decodes the texture and depth maps and use them to synthesize desired intermediate view using depth-image-based rendering (DIBR). The quality of the synthesized view is great affected by the depth maps. Our first objective is to find ways to improve/enhance the depth map. Through our research on depth estimation in this project, we understand more in depth the characteristics of depth maps and the difficulty in estimating them accurately. With such insight, we developed a variety of ways to use pre-processing and post-processing means to enhance the depth maps. To remove blocking artifacts in the depth map while preserving depth edges, we find that adaptive depth map postprocessing filter is useful. We find that graph-based transform is a powerful tool for depth image processing. We apply graph-based transform to perform depth map coding and depth map denoising. We also developed a hybrid plane fitting technique to enhance the accuracy of depth maps by taking advantage of the prior knowledge that depth maps should be piecewise planar. Our second objective is to investigate ways to compensate for the difference between adjacent 3D views to that further process such as view synthesis can be performed with high accuracy. We investigated various correction techniques. Rectification is a very important first step for processing of multiview contents. We deveoped some good rectification method using epipolar geometry and constraints. We found that color correction and illumination correction of existing methods were quite good, and our methods were only marginally better than them. We investigated further on camera spacing correction. We managed to model the problem as a convex optimization problem and found the corresponding optimal solution. We found that convex optimization is a very powerful tool for solving 3D problems. Our third objective is to study geometry correction and ways to synthesize views from desired 3D angles using DIBR and corresponding fast algorithms. We developed some effective geometry correction algorithms before DIBR. We developed reliability based rendering to remove contour artifacts in virtual views and temporal hole filling. We model view synthesis as minimization problem by iterative texture projection. We view synthesis and coding jointly and proposed RD-optimized 3D reconstruction from noisy depth maps. We studied quality assessment, 3D saliency model and applied depth map as hints for matting.

610210.label: Major findings and research outcome
610210.value: On Objective (1), we investigated various depth estimation and the pre/post-processing of depth maps. We published 11 papers: [C2] on convex optimization based depth estimation; [C5] on adaptive depth map filtering to remove blocking artifacts; [C6] on depth map superresolution to increase resolution of received depth map; [C8] on depth map coding using graph-based transform; [C10] on hybrid plane fiting to enhance accuracy of depth maps; [C11] to infer depth map from images captured with different aperture; [C12] on cost aggregation with adaptive weight; [C16] to enhance precision of 3D surfaces using multiple depth maps. [C18] on depth map denoising using graph-based transform and group sparity; [J1] on convex optimization based depth estimation (journal paper under review); [J5] on adaptive depth estimation with recursion (journal paper to be submitted) On Objective (2), we investigated various correction techniques for illumination, color, camera spacing and rectification. We found that existing illumination and color correction methods work quite well. Thus we changed our focus slightly to camera spacing correction and rectification. We published 3 papers: [C1] on color image rectification to map epipolar lines into horizontal lines; [C14] on camera spacing correction in ray space; [J2] on convex optimization based camera correction (journal paper). On Objective (3), we did extensive work on geometry correction, view synthesis and fast algorithms. We published 9 papers: [C3] on an overview of image based rendering; [C4] on temporal hole filling; [C7] on view synthesis based error compensation and reliability; [C9] on modeling view synthesis as convex optimization problem; [C13] on 3D visual saliency model guided by 3D motion; [C15] on RD-optimized joint view synthesis and coding; [C17] on quality assessment of 3D depth; [C19] on performing matting on 3D using depth maps as hints; [J3] on optimal view synthesis using iterative projection (journal paper under review); [J4] on 3D motion estimation for visual saliency model (journal paper).

610210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
610210.value: The depth map preprocessing and postprocessing problem is important and difficult. While we have developed some effective ways to refine/enhance problematic depth maps, further research is needed. In particular, the effect of incorrect depth on the human perception is not fully clear to researchers in the world. So further work would be need to study it. We found that graph-based transform and processing is a very powerful image processing tool. However, its mathematical framework is still in development stage. Further research is needed to investigate why and how it really works. The coding of depth map is a hot topic in recent years, though it is not the focus of this project. It would be beneficial to investigate depth coding. View synthesis is a challenging and difficult problem also. Although we have found some effective ways to solve the problem, it is not fully solved. More general problems should be considered. Consistency among synthesized view should be investigated. More work needs to be done on quality assessment as the effect of depth maps on view synthesis is still not very well understood.

610210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
610210.value: In this project, we solve several important fundamental problems in 3D (free-viewpoint) TV. One fundamental element of 3D TV is the correct estimation of object depth (called depth map) and the storage/transmission of it. Knowing that the depth map is often wrong, we develop several ways to correct it. To do so, we study the depth estimation methods and develop some relatively reliable way to do so. Then we develop some methods to repair/refine incorrect depth maps. Distortion on the depth map during transmission is also reduced. We developed a way to do 3D scene generation with good quality. Often users watching 3DTV would change their perspective by moving their head sideway so as to see what is behind the foreground objects. The method to generate the view from the new perspective is called DIBR. We studied many problems of DIBR and proposed several DIBR methods using the inherent property of video and some mathematical optimization techniques leading to high reliability and better visual quality. We also studied ways to perform subjective quality assessment of 3D TV and found some way to identify the portino of a video which is perceptually most important/attractive to the audience.

611310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611310.value: Aerosols deposited on solid surfaces can be resuspended back into the air by turbulent flow and human disturbance. Expiratory aerosols generated from expiration also follow this phenomenon. Yet limited study has investigated the resuspension characteristics and the associated infection risk of these potentially infectious particles comprehensively. With resuspension, indoor surfaces loaded with expiratory aerosols serve as sources of airborne infectious particles. Exposure to airborne infectious particles and the subsequent infection risk will be underestimated by existing models, which often neglect resuspended portion due to lack of resuspension rate data. Resuspension phenomenon may also prolong the exposure, since the lifetime of infectious particles in the premises is lengthened. In addition, resuspended infectious particles are more dangerous than settled ones for diseases such as tuberculosis and influenza. Understanding the infection risk associated with resuspended expiratory aerosol requires knowledge of (1) the adhesive forces binding expiratory aerosols to different indoor surfaces, (2) the resuspension rates of expiratory aerosols from these surfaces, (3) the loss of viability of microorganisms due to the resuspension process, and (4) quantitative prediction of infection risk from the resuspended infectious particles. This research aims at performing experiments to characterize (1) to (3), and developing exposure and infection risk assessment models for (4). Experiments will be performed to characterize the adhesive forces and resuspension rates of expiratory aerosols. Databases of adhesive forces and resuspension rates of expiratory aerosols on different indoor materials and under different conditions will be created. Empirical models describing the adhesive forces and resuspension rates of expiratory aerosols will be constructed. The loss of viability of microorganism due to the resuspension process will also be studied through microbiological air sampling using benign bacteria and bacterial viruses to simulate pathogens. Existing infection risk assessment models will be modified to incorporate the intake of resuspended particles. Based on the experimental data and the new risk model, the performance will be evaluated from the infection control perspectives for different ventilation strategies and indoor materials in various indoor environments The infection risk from resuspended expiratory aerosols will be compared to that from other exposure pathways. This research will reveal the impact of aerosol resuspension, a fluid mechanical phenomenon, on the spread of infectious diseases. The findings will provide additional information for designing and maintaining a healthier built environment. 沉積於固體表面上的氣溶膠會受湍流和人為干擾的影響而被重新懸浮到空氣中。呼氣產生的飛沬氣溶膠也具備這種特性。對於這些存在傳染性的顆粒的重新懸浮特徵及相關感染風險的研究卻非常有限。在重新懸浮現象之下，沉積了呼氣氣溶膠的表面成為了傳染源頭。由於缺乏重新懸浮率數據，現有數學模型往往忽視了重新懸浮部分而低估了傳染性顆粒的暴露劑量和相關的感染風險。重新懸浮的現象也可能延長人群暴露在傳染性顆粒的時間，因為該現象會延長傳染性顆粒在建築物內的傳染壽命。此外，引致某些疾病，如肺結核和流感的傳染性顆粒在懸浮在空氣中的狀態比沉積於固體表面上中的狀態更為危險。要了解飛沬氣溶膠重新懸浮所引致的感染風險需要以下知識:（1）飛沬氣溶膠對不同室內表面的黏附力，（2）飛沬氣溶膠從這些表面上重新懸浮的速率，（3）重新懸浮過程對微生物生存率的影響，（4）定量估測重新懸浮顆粒的感染傳染性風險。本研究的目的是進行實驗去研究（1）至（3），並發展暴露和感染風險評估模型以實現（4）。飛沬氣溶膠的黏附力和重新懸浮率將會以實驗來測定。在不同的室內材料上和不同條件下的黏附力和懸浮率的數據庫將被建立。以經驗為依據的數學模型將被建立以描述飛沬氣溶膠的吸附力和重新懸浮率。利用無害的細菌和細菌病毒配合微生物空氣採樣技術，重新懸浮過程對微生物生存率的影響會被測量。現有的感染風險評估模型將被修改以納入重新懸浮的部分。實驗數據和新的風險評估模型將會被用於對各種室內環境，如醫院，飛機機艙，在不同的室內通風策略和室內材料下，以控制感染的角度作出績效評估。這些結果可讓我們知道重新 懸浮與其他暴露途徑所引致的感染風險的比例。本研究將揭示氣溶膠重新懸浮 (一個流體力學的現象) 對傳播傳染病的影響。研究結果將提供更多的相關信息以助設計和保持一個健康的建築環境。

611310.label: Realisation of objectives
611310.value: The overall project objectives have been achieved. The adhesion together with the resuspension behavior of expiratory aerosols was determined by centrifuge, wind tunnel and vibration experiments. During the research, it was found that due to the ability of deformation of the liquid expiratory aerosols, the resuspension behaviors of liquid aerosols are not necessarily the same as solid particles, and depend on the removal mechanism. As a result, to understand the resuspension of expiratory aerosols, not only the adhesive force, but also the detachment behavior with different removal mechanism should be studied simultaneously. Thus a comprehensive comparison of the resuspension behavior between the two kinds of aerosols was made. A theory was developed to predict the fraction of volume resuspended against force field and it was validated by a precise experiment done by ultracentrifuge and interferometric Mie imaging technique. Different aerosol sizes and various surface materials were also tested. A small-scaled customized wind tunnel was constructed. The resuspension rates of expiratory aerosols were measured under different combinations of air velocity and turbulence intensity. A stochastic model by using the Langevin equation was developed to simulate the resuspension rate and the rolling mechanism in the presence of a turbulent stream. The modeling results obtained using this parameter were found to be in good agreement with experimental data, and the model performed better compared to other models. A vibration experiment was carried out to investigate the resuspension behavior of aerosols due to unsteady force field. The substrate was put inside a substrate holder and installed in a mini-shaker powered by a power amplifier and a function generator. Laboratory and site measurements for different indoor environments were also conducted. Indoor particle resuspension by human activity, e.g. vacuum cleaning was measured. Another experiment was conducted in a real isolation ward of a hospital which was protected by negative pressure. Artificial saliva solution with benign E.coli bacteria was employed to simulate bacterium-laden infectious particles to study the dispersion and the characteristics of microorganism viability. Then a dose–response model was used to assess the infection risks of the occupants in an aircraft cabin. The effect of human movement on airborne disease transmission in an aircraft cabin was analyzed. A likelihood analysis was performed as a hypothesis test on the input parameters and different human movement pattern assumptions. The performance of different ventilation strategies, human activities and materials surface on infection risk were also evaluated.

611310.label: Major findings and research outcome
611310.value: The resuspension behavior between liquid aerosols and solid aerosols was found to be very different and depends on the removal mechanism. A whole solid particle detaches from the surface when the removal force is sufficient, while a portion of a droplet may deform, split and detach even if the removal force is insufficient to detach the whole droplet. Different removal mechanisms, centrifuge, vibration and wind tunnel, which represent a constant force field, an unsteady force field and a force field by turbulent shear flow, respectively, were studied. In the centrifuge experiment, the adhesive force of the solid particles was found to be in the same order of magnitude and generally smaller than that of a droplet in terms of the fraction remaining (i.e. how much volume of the liquid are held by the force). In general, a huge force field (at least hundred times of gravity) is required to detach an aerosol in the size of micron range on a well-treated surface (Leung et al. 2013, Aerosol Science and Technology). For the vibration experiment, the solid particles were resuspended even if the force field was less than that measured in the centrifuge experiment, whereas no resuspension was observed for liquid droplets. The detachment of droplets due to a fully developed turbulent channel flow on different well-treated surfaces of materials was investigated (Fu et al. 2014, Aerosol Science and Technology). Results showed that the detachment behavior was very different for different surfaces. For all cases, the droplet deformed and detached at a critical velocity which is inversely proportional to the square root of the contact diameter. To detach micron size droplets, the required mean velocity exceeds 30m/s. Results indicated the direction that any future research investigating resuspension of liquid aerosols should consider not only the adhesive force, but also the detachment behavior together with the removal mechanism. Results showed that under a single removal mechanism (constant force field or wind flow), common indoor environmental conditions are not likely to resuspend an aerosol in the size of micron range on a clean, smooth and well-treated surface. However, the adhesion decreases on rough and dirty surface. Moreover, as shown in the vibration experiment, resuspension becomes possible at a more complicated removal mechanism which poses the necessity of further investigation. Numerical simulation, laboratory study, site measurements and risk analysis were conducted to show the possible risk due to resuspension of expiratory droplets.

611310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611310.value: This project focuses on expiratory aerosols and future study can be developed on the more general bioaerosols which also pose risk to human health when resuspension occurs. Since this research revealed the very different resuspension behaviors between liquid aerosols and solid aerosols, it is recommended for future research of bioaerosols that liquid and solid aerosols should be distinguished and treated separately. In the current project, some fundamental removal mechanisms have been investigated. In order to understand the risk of resuspension in a daily life more completely, more removal mechanisms can be investigated in the further study. The material surfaces studied in this project were clean, smooth and well-treated. Based on the useful fundamental knowledge obtained, further research efforts can be put on investigating a dust load surface, a multi-layer surface or a geometrical complicated surface, to understand the more complicated aerosol dynamics. Further studies can also be done on the viability characteristics of microorganisms after resuspension. The viability can be affected by resuspension not only due to the shear stress induced, but also the impurity of the droplet or the dust on the surface so as to obtain the more realistic risk assessment information.

611310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611310.value: Coughing and sneezing generate large amount of infectious particles and disperse in the air widely. Over 90% of expiratory aerosols settle onto the floor and other surfaces. Those deposited infectious particles may be resuspended to airborne state again due to air turbulence and human activities. As some pathogens can survive from days to weeks on surfaces, the surfaces with deposited infectious particles would become a new source of airborne infectious particle when resuspension occurs. The actual risk can therefore be higher than predicted if the impact of the spread of infectious respiratory diseases by resuspension is ignored. It is important to know the resuspension behavior of infectious particles so that a better risk analysis of disease transmission can be made. This project studied the physics of the resuspension of infectious particles from a surface. Some theories to predict the relationship between the resuspension rate and the force were developed, and were verified by experiments. A number of scenarios were investigated and demonstrated the risk of resuspension of infectious particles, including different indoor environments (e.g. hospital ward, aircraft cabin, cleanroom), different surface material (e.g. acrylic, glass stainless steel) and human activities. Infection risk assessments were also performed in the project.

611610.value: 在過去十年裏，隨著柵尺寸的快速縮小，矽金屬氧化物半導體場效應電晶體（MOSFET）的運行速度得到了相當的提升。新一代MOSFET的電流增益截止頻率（fT）已經超過了200GHz，而最新的國際半導體技術路線圖顯示其將在25nm節點上達到490GHz。然而，這種顯著的速度提升並非是沒有代價的。由於在發生雪崩擊穿前，器件所能承受的最大電場強度（EBK）是由材料本身的特性所決定，器件物理尺寸的縮小也會同時導致在擊穿前漏所能施加電壓（VBK）的減小。在也被稱為詹森品質因數（JFoM）的fT和EBK的乘積上，矽材料的限制為0.3THz-V。因此，同樣的路線圖也預測了25nm矽MOSFET將只有小於1V的VBK。在數位和特別是要求合理雜訊容限及設計峰值儲備的模擬積體電路中帶來了極大的困難甚而是難以逾越的障礙。 為了迎接這種挑戰，很久以前三五族化合物半導體材料，包括GaAs，InP和GaN，就已經被證實比矽有著顯著的材料優勢。而基於GaAs和InP的器件可以有更高的電子遷移率從而提供更高的JFoM，但又因其禁帶寬度與Si相差不大而難以在VBK上得到明顯的性能提升。寬禁帶氮化鎵作為一種特殊的半導體可以提供高的擊穿電場強度EBK——是矽上測得的結果的7倍。另外GaN的峰值電子速度可以是Si的2.5倍，暗示了在高度縮小的器件上可能獲得最小的狀態切換時間。而雖然GaN的電子遷移率並不如其他三五族材料（如InGaAs等）那樣大，但當器件尺寸減小到一定程度的時候，其更高的飽和電子速度會主導整個器件的性能。進一步地，GaN上可以獲得在二維電子氣（2DEG）中的最大電荷密度也比其他三五族半導體如GaAs，InP或InGaAs高很多。綜上，這些材料特性顯示了GaN及其相關材料有著特殊的潛力以實現高速度，高性能的場效應電晶體器件。 得益於在GaN電子器件及積體電路領域深厚及寬領域的經驗，我們建議發展GaN積體電路技術來開發高速度及高性能的混合信號引用，以利用GaN能達到5THz-V JFoM的傑出材料性質。我們將開發同時具有高fT和高EBK的GaN場效應電晶體。在高密度積體電路中的一些重要問題如平面工藝和工藝一致性也將得到研究以發展相應的解決方案。混合信號積體電路如高採樣率類比數位轉換器（ADC）的原型將被展示。

611610.label: Realisation of objectives
611610.value: All of the four objectives have been achieved with detailed information given as follows: 1. A fluorine plasma ion implantation technique has been developed to realize enhancement-mode HEMTs with positive threshold voltage of +1 V. A thin (nanometer thick) fluorinated surface layer was found to provide additional forward current suppression that helps to increase the forward gate turn-on voltage to ~3 V, creating a 2 V voltage swing for Schottky gate enhancement-mode HEMTs. To further increase the gate swing, attempts have been made in fabricating MIS-HEMT (metal-insulator-semiconductor HEMT) with the additional gate dielectric. In the case of MIS-HEMT, the gate forward turn-on voltage has been increased to ~10 V. Submicron-gate HEMTs with 0.2 um gate length have been successfully fabricated. Maximum power gain cutoff frequency of 180 GHz and maximum current gain frequency of 80 GHz are achieved. 2. A tunnel junction FET with Schottky source contact has been developed. This device features non-alloyed source contact and exhibits enhancement-mode operation. The drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) effect is also investigated and is shown to be insignificant when the gated channel length is larger than 100 nm. The channel confinement has been improved with fluorine implantation to the backside of the channel because fluorine ions are negatively charged in GaN and can raise the local energy band. 3. All the devices and integrated circuits have been tested up to 250 degree Celsius using a high-frequency probe station equipped with a thermal chuck. 4. Key functional mixed-signal blocks have been successfully demonstrated on AlGaN/GaN-on-Si platform. These circuits include temperature sensor, over-temperature protection circuit, 2-bit quantizer, set/reset (S/R) flip-flop, etc.

611610.label: Major findings and research outcome
611610.value: 1. Fluorine implantation was found to be able to create a back barrier in conventional AlGaN/GaN HFET structure, yielding improved electron confinement. The implantation conditions have been optimized for minimum penalties on channel mobility. Detailed device characterizations were completed based on a drain injection measurement technique. 2. A novel metal-2DEG tunnel junction FET (TJ-FET) was successfully demonstrated using a novel Schottky source technique. The devices exhibit positive threshold voltage for enhancement-mode operation, low off-state current for low power consumption. The cut-off frequencies are as good as the conventional HFETs. The TJ-FETs exhibit normally off operation (Vth = +1.35 V) in an otherwise normally on as-grown sample. The unique high-density 2DEG in AlGaN/GaN heterostructures enables the formation of a Schottky tunnel barrier with nanometer-scale barrier thickness even with a large Schottky barrier height (e.g., ∼0.8 eV). In the OFF state, the source Schottky junction provides natural reverse-blocking capability, resulting in significant leakage reduction and low OFF-state current. A drive current of 326 mA/mm, a high ION/IOFF ratio (1E+10), and a low subthreshold swing (89 mV/dec) are obtained. 3. Lateral devices are suitable for high-density integration and thus could be exploited to implement many mixed-signal functional blocks that are indispensable for III-N device/circuit applications. To illustrate the all-GaN solution, a GaN smart power technology platform has been proposed and demonstrated. On a GaN-on-Si substrate, normally-off power HEMTs and high-voltage lateral field-effect rectifiers can be fabricated as the core power components. Meanwhile, peripheral devices such as E/D-mode HEMTs are available to develop direct-coupled FET logic (DCFL) for digital blocks. Many key functional circuit blocks have been demonstrated for the first using GaN devices. These circuits include bootstrapped comparators, 2-bit quantizer, set/reset (S/R) flip-flop, proportional-to-absolute-temperature (PTAT) temperature sensor, etc. All of the GaN integrated circuits demonstrated in this project are capable of operating properly at temperatures as high as 250 degree Celsius, which is the limit of our high-frequency probe station.

611610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611610.value: With the device technology platform established in this project, further development of the research can focus more on advanced design techniques that address the uniqueness of the GaN devices. Device-circuit interactions require further investigation in greater details. A proposal on the development of an all-GaN gate driver is under preparation.

611610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611610.value: Mix Group III-nitride (III-N) wide-bandgap semiconductor devices are especially attractive for high-voltage, high-power, high-frequency and high-temperature electronics, owing to their superior material properties. In particular, high-quality lateral heterostructures (e.g. AlGaN/GaN heterostructures) are readily available and are especially suitable for high-level integration. At present, the lateral III-N heterostructrues are dominating the scene of III-N electron device development for applications in RF/microwave power amplifiers, power switches, as well as high-temperature electronics. In this project, a GaN device technology platform is successfully developed. On this platform, transistors and diodes are seamlessly integrated with robust control over threshold voltage, gate swing and breakdown voltage. Many mixed-signal prototype circuits are successfully demonstrated on GaN device technology platform for the first time. It is now becoming feasible to develop single-chip solutions for many applications of GaN electronics. The technology developed in this project is expected to lead to ultimate system-on-chip (SOC) solutions that promise compact system and enhanced performance.

612210.value: 普適計算中的適應性錯誤測試

612210.label: Project Objectives
612210.value: To identify the patterns of common adaptation faults in context-aware pervasive applications and study their effects on the context-aware ability of these applications. To derive a framework to detect adaptation faults dynamically for context-aware pervasive applications, and locate these detected faults. To implement the proposed framework, and evaluate it based on simulated and real-life context-aware pervasive applications.

To implement the proposed framework, and evaluate it based on simulated and real-life context-aware pervasive applications.

612210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612210.value: Context-aware pervasive applications feature themselves by perceiving changes in their environments and making adaptations to realize seamless integration between users and environments. In such a computing paradigm, contexts play an important role by capturing the characteristics of a continually changing environment, and indicating when an application needs to adapt its behavior accordingly. An application is, however, prone to adaptation faults when there are unexpected context changes not being taken care of at design time. Unfortunately, modeling precisely the variety of contexts and their continual changes and inherent noises is a challenging, sometimes impossible task. The lack of handy and effective tool support for ensuring logic correctness makes adaptation faults common to context-aware pervasive applications. The presence of adaptation faults can have catastrophic effects, making such applications behave unpredictably, and denying their original objective of context awareness. Although adaptation faults can be discovered statically at a design level, such results are usually plagued with false alarms. However, detecting adaptation faults at runtime imposes unique challenges to context-aware pervasive applications. Such applications require high efficiency for reacting to continual context changes in a timely manner, which is inevitably hindered by the complexity of a runtime fault detection mechanism. In this project, we propose to study the following research questions: What are the common patterns of adaptation faults specific to context-aware pervasive applications? What causes the false alarms of adaptation fault detection? Could these false alarms be affected by compounding factors such as variable dependency, physical constraints and runtime behavior in an application? Are there any effective approaches to alleviating or eliminating such false alarms? In addition to the effectiveness of adaptation fault detection, can one make runtime fault detection efficient and scalable for large-scale context-aware pervasive applications? The study of these questions will help us to develop an effective framework for detecting adaptation faults in context-aware pervasive applications that are subject to continual context changes. The framework would enable software engineers to detect adaptation faults automatically and collect analysis results for fault-fixing advice. Prototype tools will be developed to support the proposed framework. To evaluate the applicability of our research results, we will apply our framework to both simulated and real-life pervasive applications. 上下文相關的普適應用持續地感知它們的環境變化，並作出自適應的改變以實現與用戶和環境的無縫結合。在這樣的計算模式下，上下文扮演了很重要的角色，因爲它們描述了環境的特點並指明何時需要作出何種自適應的改變。然而，在設計階段所考慮的上下文可能與實際不符，從而導致應用程序産生錯誤的自適應改變。困難的是，要在設計階段准確地考慮每種可能的上下文，並對它們的變化和內在的噪音進行建模，這具有相當的挑戰性並有可能無法完成。由于缺乏合適的、有效的工具支持，上下文相關的普適應用常常在設計邏輯上有所缺陷。這些缺陷可能會有災難性的後果，使應用程序的行爲不可預測，從而違背設計這些應用最初的目的。盡管這些自適應改變的內在缺陷可以在設計階段用靜態分析的方法予以發現，分析的結果往往包含過多的虛假警報。如果嘗試在運行階段檢測這些缺陷，則需要克服一些特有的困難。比如，普適應用需要對環境上下文的變化作出快速的反應，這可能與在運行階段仔細地檢測自適應改變的缺陷這樣的需求相違背。針對這樣的困難，在本項目中我們計劃研究如下的問題：上下文相關的普適應用具有怎麽樣的自適應缺陷模式？靜態檢測中的虛假警報是如何發生的？這些警報是否與一個應用中的變量相關性、物理規則、和運行時行爲有關聯？是否有有效的方法來減少甚至消除虛假警報？在自適應改變的缺陷檢測方面，能否做到既結果有效又檢測迅速，並對大型應用具有可擴展性？對以上問題的解答將有助于我們開發出普適應用自適應改變缺陷的有效檢測方法。這項工作將幫助軟件開發人員自動地檢測普適應用中的自適應改變缺陷，並提出修複這些缺陷的建議。我們也將提供原型工具以支持該項工作的開展。最後，我們將使用模擬實驗以及真實案例來評估我們工作的實際適用性。

612210.label: Realisation of objectives
612210.value: All three objectives have been successfully accomplished in the project. To pursue the first objective, we conducted an archival study of three active context-aware Android applications, which are capable of adapting their behaviors with respect to changes in environmental contexts. The study involved 80 releases of these applications and 285 reported failures. Three types of faults based on adaptation predictability, adaptation stability and the misperception of environmental changes. These faults arise from non-deterministic adaptive states, auto-cycling among a set of adaptive states, and non-robust handling of noisy sensory data. Patterns of these faults were characterized based on their causes and symptoms. At the end of the project, we started to investigate the issue of non-functional adaptive faults, such as inappropriate use of battery energy. We carried out another archival study of 33 popular Android applications that have been reported to suffer severe battery consumption problems. Patterns of inefficient using of sensor operations were collected and formulated. To achieve the second objective, we proposed a formal model that is capable to precisely express the intended adaptive behavior of a context-aware applications. The model was developed on top of first-order logic, and can be used to detect the adaptive faults. We derived an efficient algorithm and leveraged the intrinsic concurrency support by existing Intel processors to detect adaptation faults. We also proposed a technique to realign an application’s internal adaptive state with its actual environmental state. We also explore a machine learning approach to detect adaptation faults as behavior outliers. To accomplish the third objective, we build an adaptation fault detection tool (ADAM) on top of Java, several robot-cars on top of Cirrus Logic EDB9302 boards with ultrasonic and speed sensors, and a tool (GreenDroid) on top of Java PathFinder to evaluate the effectiveness of using sensor operation. During this project, a PhD student has been trained and has successfully passed his PhD qualifying examination.

612210.label: Major findings and research outcome
612210.value: This project made the following findings and research outcome. - Majority of adaptation faults manifest themselves as non-deterministic adaptive states, auto-cycling among a set of adaptive states, and non-robust handling of noisy sensory data. In our archival study of the 285 reported failures of three popular context-aware applications, the proportion of failures related to adaptation faults ranges from 58.6% to 77.5% [J1]. - A formal model based on first-order logic is proposed to express adaptive behavior of context-aware applications. Our model allows more precise detection of adaptation faults due to the enhanced treatment on the impact of variable dependency and physical constraints [J2]. - Experimental evaluation using robot-cars shows that our fault detection algorithm is able to timely detect 80% of adaptation anomalies within 1.1ms, and 90% of them within 2.3ms [J2]. The robot-cars were built on top of Cirrus Logic EDB9302 board with a TelosB mote for wireless communication. Each car is equipped with ultrasonic and speed sensors that sense their environment every 350ms. - An enhanced version of detection algorithm is proposed to leverage the intrinsic concurrency support of existing processors. Evaluation was conducted on a 24-hour taxi tracking data in Shenzhen city. The data were collected from 760 taxis, which transmit their GPS locations continually to a transportation organization. A speedup of more than two folds can be achieved using a quad-core processor. Theorems are provided to guarantee the soundness of the detected faults [J3]. - As an attempt to relieve users from specifying the intended adaptive behavior, we deployed machine learning to detect anomalies as behavior outliers. We propose a technique to clean data noise based on application-level events, and apply it to sensor motes. Experiments show that our technique can improve the detection speed by 11 times and identify real anomalies within the top three ranked warnings [J4]. - An archival study of 33 popular Android applications suffering from severe energy problems reveals that many applications fail to adapt their energy-consuming sensory operations to changed scenarios. Experiments show that our proposed technique can detect real energy faults. Some of them have not yet been discovered by the application developers. These reports have been readily confirmed by the developers with subsequent fixes [C1]. - A technique is proposed to realign an application’s internal adaptive state with its actual environmental state. Evaluation based on 12 applications on robot-cars show that the technique improves dependability by 30.3% [C2].

612210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612210.value: The project confirms the popularity of adaptation faults in context-aware applications. We found in this project many Android applications need to adapt their non-functional behaviors such as energy consumption to changing scenarios; otherwise scarce battery power can be unnecessarily wasted. A further development of this project is to investigate non-functional anomalies of context-aware applications.

612210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612210.value: Many modern applications are context-aware. They adapt their behavior based on their environmental changes, which are captured by means of environmental contexts. However, programming adaptive behaviors is non-trivial and error-prone. Timely detection of such failures is critical to prevent them from making non-compensable consequences. We made the first archival study of such faults based on real bug reports, and identified these faults commonly arise from the anomalies in adaptation predictability and adaptation stability as well as the misperception of environmental changes. Techniques were proposed with tool supports. Experimental evaluation using real applications shows that our techniques are effective and efficient. New bugs in real applications were found using our tools and confirmed by their developers. Project results were disseminated in four journal and two conference articles.

612310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612310.value: The response time of liquid crystal displays (LCD) is still inferior to the existent competing technologies, such as plasma display panels (PDP) or cathode ray tubes (CRT). The target LC cell response time for a field sequential color (FSC) displays should be less than 1 ms (240 Hz frame frequency) to provide a high resolution, low power consumption and extended color gamut liquid crystal displays (LCD). Fast switching ferroelectric liquid crystal (FLC) displays (FLCD) is a good candidate for the new generation of FSC LCD, which proved to be better in response time, than usually used nematic LC. At the same time ferroelectric LC modules in high speed communication systems(such as switches, attenuators, polarization rotators) are extremely fast, stable, durable, of low losses, operable over a wide temperature range, require small operating voltages and extremely low power consumption especially when using bistable and multi-stable switching with optical memory. The photoalignment technology enables to solve the key problems usually faced in FLCD applications, such as (i) quality of FLC alignment on sufficiently large surface area; (ii) appropriate adjustable anchoring energy and pretilt angle; (iii) low losses in the alignment layers due to their small thickness and etc. The goal of this project is to further development of novel photoaligned fast ferroelectric LCD and Photonics Devices aimed at (i) further fundamental study of the new appropriate electrooptical modes used for switching such as Deformed Helix Ferroelectric (DHF) or Volume Stabilized (VS) FLC mode; (ii) understanding of physical mechanisms of FLC interaction with a photoaligned surface of different photosensitive nature (diffusion, photo-crosslinking, photo-degradation) to produce a stable alignment with a controllable anchoring energy and pretilt angle over sufficiently large surface area; (iii) the development of new fast responding FLC materials with fast switching and a sufficient number of switchable gray levels (V-shape switching); (iv) the implementation of the working prototypes of novel FSC FLC displays; (v)the elaboration of fast response optical FLC elements for Photonics applications, such as switches, attenuators, polarization rotators;(vi)the investigations of regimes of operation to allow efficient addressing of FLCD, and (vii) the development of the software module, taking into account the real FLC parameters with further optimization of FLC optical and electrooptical performance. 液晶顯示器的響應時間仍然不能遜於同現存的其他顯示技術（PDP），如等離子顯示器或者射線管顯示器（CRT）。爲了獲得高解析度，場序彩色電視的目標響應時間應該低於1ms（24 hz 刷新率）。快速響應鐵電液晶顯示器（FLCD）是新一代快速液晶顯示器的技術，並且已經證實其響應速度快於普通的向列液晶顯示器。 同時，鐵電液晶也被應用於快速通訊系統，充當如開關，衰減器，偏振旋轉器等，使用鐵電液晶的雙穩態和多穩態等光學記憶性的工作模式，更可以使其應用到需要滿足諸如，極速，穩定，耐用，廉價，適用于較廣的溫度範圍，低電壓 工作，低耗電此類特性的領域。 光配向技術使我們可以克服鐵電液晶顯示器的一些常見問題，例如（i）大平面鐵電液晶的配向，（ii）可調節的鉚定能和預傾角，（iii）較小的配向層厚度以降低損耗。 此項目的目標在於進一步深入研究光配向快速鐵電液晶顯示器以及光電子器件，主要目標有 （i）進一步研究鐵電液晶新的光電工作模式，例如變形螺旋鐵電模式（DHF）和體穩定鐵電液晶模式（VSFLC）。（ii）研究鐵電液晶材料和不同的配向層接觸的物理化學機理，如（擴散理論，光致交聯，光致降解），以便能夠在大平面上製作穩定的配向層，並且具有鉚定能和預傾角可調的能力。（iii）開發新的鐵電液晶材料，使其具有高的響應速

612310.label: Realisation of objectives
612310.value: New photoaligned materials were developed to with stabilized FLC orientation on the substrates.The photoalignment technology enables to solve the key problems usually faced in FLCD applications, such as (i) quality of FLC alignment on sufficiently large surface area; (ii) appro-priate adjustable anchoring energy and pre-tilt angle; (iii) low losses in the alignment layers due to their small thickness etc. The novel FLC devices include field sequential color (FSC) FLC with a high resolution, low power consumption and extended color gamut, which can be used in the screens of portable PCs, mobile phones, PDAs and micro and pico-projectors. Several electrooptical modes were developed for for the new generation of FLC devices for displays and photonics: (i) deformed helix ferroelectric (DHF) effect; (ii) electrically suppressed helix ferroelectric liquid crystals (ESHFLC); (iii) modulation of light in diffraction FLC grating; and (iv) orientational electro-optic Kerr effect. Fast switching FLCD (in 100 microseconds range) with V-shape gray levels and a low voltage driving (less than 5V) in both transmissive and reflective mode were achieved. FLCD with achromatic (black/white) switching and continuous color gamut with resolution up to VGA and higher and extended color triangle (>130% NTSC) has been obtained. Prototype of FLCD working with a frame frequency of 240Hz and higher for FSC and 3D applications has been demonstrated. FLC switches with diffraction Efficiency about 70% were demonstrated, which is hundred times faster than the existing switchable grating.FLC grating can be operated at high frequency ~ 5KHz with a high contrast ratio. Small electric field is required to switch grating ~ 2V/μm. Good repeatability with low manufacturing cost was obtained. The fibre sensor of a high voltage based on variation of reflectivity of FBG was made based on DHF ferroelectric liquid crystal cell. Switching of DHF FLC cell by harvesting electrical energy from the external electrical field using antenna was proposed and demonstrated enabling to detect electric fields of 100 ~ 400 KV/m. Signal reflected off FBG, when changing external voltage applied to LC cell was varied between 216 and 306 pw. The new sensor can be used as a low cost high accuracy voltage measurement technique for high power distribution systems.

612310.label: Major findings and research outcome
612310.value: We have obtained some good results in studying deformed helix ferroelectric (DHF) effect. Two inherent properties of DHF-FLC have been observed: (i) similar to NLC cells, the electro-optical response is insensitive to the driving voltage polarity, but the response time is two orders faster as compared with NLC, (ii) the response exhibits perfect V-shaped mode obtained for the case of rectangular alternating applied voltage pulses. We have discovered a new electrooptic mode, which we called Electrically Suppressed Helix (ESH) mode. The mode is characterized by a high contrast ratio and very fast electrooptic response and is highly suitable for FSC and 3D applications. The contrast ratio in ESH mode is more than 10000:1 up to 1 kHz at 1.5V and up to 2 kHz at 3V; the light transmission is about of maximum in this case. The electro-optical response manifests evident saturation at 1 kHz and 1.5V with the response time of 130 microseconds. We demonstrate a fast switchable grating based on ferroelectric liquid crystals and orthogonal planar alignment by means of photo alignments. Both 1D and 2D gratings have been constructed. The proposed diffracting element provides fast response time of around 20 microseconds, contrast of 7000:1 and high diffraction efficiency up to 92%, at the electric field of 6V/micron. The saturated electro-optical (EO) states up to very high frequency (5 kHz) are the real advantage of the proposed switchable grating, which finds new applications for projection display and Pico-projectors. A new type of the Kerr-effect has been discovered in FLC with subwavelength helix pitch. In order to systematically examine the pure phase modulation of light that takes place when the selective reflection from the helix is suppressed, we have developed the FLC with the helix pitch p0 = 150 nm. Thus, proposed FLC modulator exhibits continuous, hysteresis free and insensitive to the driving voltage polarity gray scale in electrically controlled phase shift with the operational frequency ranged from 10 Hz to 5 kHz. The very promising possibility to obtain a high contrast ratio and highly uniform LC cell is to use the optimal anchoring energy, which is easy to get by using a photoalignment technology. Our photoaligned FLC can provide a high resolution close to 6000 ppi, as the resolution of photoalignment technology is better than 1 micron , while the typical thickness of FLC layer is less than 2microns.

612310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612310.value: The further development of novel fast ferroelectric LCD aimed at (i) development of new fast responded FLC materials with fast switching and a sufficient number of switchable gray levels (V-shape switching); (ii) implementation of the working prototypes of novel FSC FLC displays, including the 3D version; (iii) investigations of regimes of operation to allow to use efficient addressing of FLCD including TFT drivers enabling a high switching current; (iv) solving the problem of a mechanical stability of FLC layers; (v) mass production of new FLC materials with optimal charateristics. The prototypes of the novel FLC devices include FSC FLC with a high resolution, low power consumption and extended color gamut, which can be used in the screens of portable PCs, mobile phones, PDAs. The switchable goggles and lenses based on new FLC prototypes can be efficiently applied in the new generations of switchable 2D/3D LCD TV. FSC FLC microdisplays, which is now one of the most advanced technologies for pico-projectors can be also made on the basis of new materials and electrooptical modes in FLC.

612310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612310.value: The response time of liquid crystal displays is still inferior to the existing competing technologies, such as plasma display panels (PDP) or organic light emitted diodes (OLED). The target LC cell response time for a field sequential color (FSC) and 3D displays should be less than 1 ms (240 Hz frame frequency) to provide a high resolution, low power consumption and extended color gamut liquid crystal displays (LCD). Fast switching ferroelectric liquid crystal (FLC) displays (FLCD) is a good candidate for the new generation of field sequential color (FSC) LCD, which proved to be better in response time, than usually used nematic LC. Four electrooptic modes in FLC: Deformed Helix Ferroelectric (DHF), Electrically Suppressed Helix (ESH) mode, FLC diffraction mode and FLC orientational electro-optic Kerr effect were proposed for fast FLCD. The photoalignment technology were developed to enable solving the key problems in FLCD applications. FLC is the most advanced technology for a high resolution, field sequential color, advanced color gamut and low power consumption pico-projectors. FLC applications in fiber optics enable production of switches, filters, attenuators, equalizers, polarization controllers, phase emulators and other fiber optical components, using of photo-alignment technique developed by us.

612910.label: Project Objectives
612910.value: To formulate physically-based and thermodynamically-consistent governing equations for transient flows of air-water in drainage systems on the basis of proper averaging of mass, momentum, energy and entropy. To develop a numerical model for the set of governing equations and closure relations developed in objectives 1 and 2. For reasons of efficiency, accuracy and overall robustness, the focus will be on exploring the viability of explicit, second order and conservative finite volume model in which the mass and momentum fluxes are obtained from the Bhatnagar–Gross–Krook (BGK) Boltzmann equation. To address the numerical difficulties associated with (i) the disparity in speeds between waves in air, gravity waves in water and waterhammer waves in surcharged regions; (ii) the large disparity in density difference between air and water and how this disparity induces large error in the pressure of the gas due to small error in water pressure; (iii) the instability when the transition from stratified to slugging flow regime occurs; and (iv) the numerical imbalance in sloping sewers. To validate and verify the model against analytical and semi-analytical solutions, classical KH stability results, existing laboratory data and new laboratory data to be generated at the water resources laboratory at The Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST).

612910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612910.value: Air phase greatly influences the transient flow behavior in urban drainage systems and has led to costly and dangerous failures and to spectacular Geysers in many cities around the world (see http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4aQySL0sKys and the links in http://ihome.ust.hk/~angellam/Background.htm). Despite the importance of air phase dynamics in operation and design of drainage systems, there is no mathematical model that can capture the rich flow physics that result from either an imposed large amplitude perturbation or an inherent hydrodynamic instability to an initially steady flow of a stratified air-water configuration in drainage system by integrating a single set of equations. This research aims at (i) formulating, validating, verifying and applying a two-phase flow model capable of automatically capturing the rich flow patterns in transient flows in drainage systems and (ii) guiding model improvements through experimental as well as three-dimensional (3D) modeling. The transients to be considered include those induced by rapid changes of inflows or outflows and by the Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH) instability at air-water interface. The flow patterns that can result from these transients are complicated and include shock and expansion waves in both water and air, slug flow with air intermittently trapped near the crown of the pipe, and breakdown of surcharging fronts by elevated pressures in air cavities. The one-dimensional (1D) governing equations are to be developed by vertically averaging the principles of mass, momentum, energy and entropy across the water and air layers, respectively. The resulting system of governing equations will then be solved by an explicit, second order and conservative finite volume model in which the mass and momentum fluxes are obtained from the Bhatnagar–Gross–Krook (BGK) Boltzmann equation. The model verification and validation will be made through analytical and semi-analytical solutions, existing experimental data, and laboratory experiments to be conducted in this research. The model will then be used to investigate the rich flow patterns that develop in transient two-phase flows in drainage systems. The nonlinear development of the KH instability and the flow patterns it leads to will be examined using a three-dimensional model that will be developed in this research. The understanding and insights gained from the 3D model will be used to upgrade the 1D model.

612910.label: Realisation of objectives
612910.value: While objective 1 was fully accomplished, objectives 2, 3 and 4 where largely but not fully accomplished. The reason is that the large disparity in density between the two layers (top layer is air and bottom layer is water), the many non-understood hydrodynamic instabilities, and local damping due to spatial non-uniformities along the conduit made meant that we could not develop a stable numerical solution. Therefore, it became clear that we needed to first understand the problem associated with large disparity in density, instabilities and damping. We made excellent progress in this direction. We also found that we need experimental data to better understand the processes, guide the development of the model and verify it. As a result, we applied for another research project to investigate the problem experimentally and were successful. As a result, we have already commenced experiments on the air-water flows at HKUST and are now in the position to develop a stable and convergent numerical for two layer flows and, thus, fully accomplish objectives 2, 3 and 4.

612910.label: Major findings and research outcome
612910.value: A one-dimensional model was developed by vertically averaging the principles of mass, momentum, energy and entropy across the water and air layers, respectively. The resulting system of governing equations was approximated by an explicit, second order and conservative finite volume model in which the mass and momentum fluxes are obtained from the Bhatnagar–Gross–Krook (BGK) Boltzmann equation. The large disparity in density between the two layers, the many non-understood hydrodynamic instabilities, and local damping due to spatial non-uniformities along the conduit made the solution unstable. Therefore, these issues had to be first examined. As a result, the instabilities were investigated in details from their onset to their final state (Journal paper 9; conferences paper 2, 3 & 4). It is found that flow undergoes a sequence of instabilities with distance downstream, where the instability progressively changes to larger modes. Near the upstream end the fundamental mode dominates the ﬂow evolution. This growth of this mode is due to energy production by the base ﬂow. Further downstream, the fundamental mode reaches its saturation amplitude and the dominant mode becomes one with a length scale twice that of the fundamental mode. The transient dynamics investigated the role of unsteady friction and non-uniformities on damping (Journal papers 2 to 8, conference paper 1). Such investigated revealed the role of initial Reynolds number of the transient behavior and showed that non-uniformities shift the oscillations frequency and create a well-defined pattern.

612910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612910.value: The new understanding developed in this research is critical for separating physical instabilities from numerical instabilities and identifying the need for more laboratory data. In fact, we have already commenced experiments on the air-water flows under consideration at HKUST, which is providing badly needed measurements of the velocity, pressure and size distribution of the trapped air pocket in two layer flows. Therefore, we are now in an ideal position to develop a stable and convergent numerical for two layer flows. The numerical model will need to be (i) able to capture a wide range of transient flow patterns including shock and expansion waves in air and water phases, air trapping and slugging, pre-bore motion and interface and KH waves and instabilities, and (ii) well balanced, accurate, efficient and of high order in order to capture KH instabilities, shocks and slugs. The understanding developed in this project of the various instabilities and transient mechanisms and the newly acquired data will be instrumental for our future development.

612910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612910.value: The goal of this project is to understand and model transients in two-phase (air-water) flows in drainage systems. This is because air phase greatly influences the transient flow behavior in urban drainage systems and has led to costly and dangerous failures and to spectacular Geysers in many cities around the world (e.g., http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4aQySL0sKys). Despite the importance of air phase dynamics in operation and design of drainage systems, there is no mathematical model that can capture the rich flow physics that result from either an imposed large amplitude perturbation or an inherent hydrodynamic instability to an initially steady flow of a stratified air-water configuration in drainage system by integrating a single set of equations. This project advances our knowledge of the various physical instabilities that arises in this flow problem and of the role of damping and non-uniformities on rapid flow oscillations.

613410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
613410.value: 光滑扰动分析和Kernel方法之间的关系及其在信用风险管理中的应用

613410.label: Co - Investigator(s)
613410.value: Prof Fu, Michael C. Prof Hu, J.Q.

613410.label: Project Objectives
613410.value: The KM first writes the sensitivity in the form of a conditional expectation and then using kernel function to approximate the conditional expectation. In this research, we propose to apply conditional Monte Carlo approach to directly evaluating the conditional expectation and write the conditional expectation as a regular estimation that can be estimated efficiently. SPA first applies conditional Monte Carlo method to smooth the discontinuous function and then differentiates the expectation of the smooth function, while the KM differentiates the expectation of the discontinuous function first (by applying its own approach) and then applies conditional Monte Carlo method to evaluate the conditional expectation. In this project, we will establish a linkage between the two methods, and show that both methods may lead to the same results under certain conditions. Once we establish the linkage between SPA and the KM, we will apply SPA (or the KM) to existing problems where the KM (or SPA) estimators are available to demonstrate the usefulness of our research. We will further compare the two methods and give guidelines on how to choose between them, and demonstrate our guidelines through some simple but interesting new problems. We will develop sensitivity estimators for measures of portfolio credit loss that can be written as the summation of the losses of all individual obligors if they default. The measures include the probability that the loss is larger than a threshold, and the expected loss when the loss is larger than a threshold. Note that the two measures directly link to two commonly used risk measures: value-at-risk and conditional value-at-risk. We will develop sensitivity estimators for the prices of different credit derivatives, including those whose payoff functions depend on portfolio credit loss, such as collateralized debt obligations (CDO), and derivatives whose payoff functions depend on the order of defaults, such as nth-to-default credit swaps. We will also compare our estimator with existing estimators. We will also consider sensitivity estimation for credit risk under different joint default models, including latent variable models and Bernoulli mixture models that are commonly used in practice and research, and develop efficient estimators based on the knowledge of the models.

613410.label: Major findings and research outcome
613410.value: There are two major findings/research outcomes of this project. First, we have shown that the kernel method (KM) is not only a useful method to develop sensitivity estimators that have n^{-2/5} rate of convergence, it is also a viable tool to develop closed-form expressions that lead to sensitivity estimators that have n^{-1/2} rate of convergence. We have shown that, when both approaches are applicable, the KM and the smooth perturbation analysis (SPA) approach often lead to same estimators. However, in some cases, maybe only one is applicable. This greatly improves the applicability of the SPA approach. Second, we have used sensitivity estimators in optimization of financial risk measures such as value-at-risk (VaR) and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR). In particular, we show that the difficult VaR problem may be solved iteratively by solving relative easier CVaR problems. This outcome was not in the original objective, but it is an natural extension of the original Objective 4, which is on sensitivity analysis of VaRs and CVaRs.

613410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613410.value: I think more should be done on how to take these efficient sensitivity estimators and combine with optimization techniques to solve difficult stochastic optimization problems. With the fast development of computing capability, Monte Carlo method becomes increasingly appealing in solving some of otherwise unsolvable stochastic optimization problems. By utilizing sensitivity estimators (i.e., gradient estimators), we can use powerful gradient-based optimization approach on these problems. As a test of concept, our paper on combining response surface method (a Monte Carlo method) and trust-region method (a gradient and Hessian based nonlinear optimization method) showed that the idea has a lot of potential. This paper was also partly supported by this project.

613410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613410.value: Sensitivity refers to the change of the output with respect to the change of the input. If the sensitivity is high, we say the output is sensitive to the input. Sensitivity plays an important role in financial risk management, because it tells to which risk factors financial risk is sensitive. In the research project we analyzed credit risk, which concerns the financial risk caused by the defaults of loans. We show that these sensitivities may be estimated efficiently through our carefully designed schemes under various models of credit risks. Therefore, these estimators may be employed by financial institutions to monitor, control and manage their credit risks.

613510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613510.value: Psychoacoustic research has had a tremendous impact on audio coding since the 1990s. The exploitation of temporal and spectral masking effects through suitable time-frequency signal processing has created the audio coders and decoders ubiquitous in today’s audio software for personal computers, home and car audio, internet applications, and mobile devices. While audio reproduction is commonplace, new signal processing applications for music are emerging. Analyzing the waveforms of recorded music allows comparing, searching, recognizing, and classifying musical content. Transcription of music, i.e., generating musical scores from recorded waveforms, is a challenging topic. In the future, it may be possible to automatically categorize sounds in terms of various acoustic features and to generate compact sets of rules for sound reproduction from the sounds themselves. The proposed research aims at enlarging knowledge about the perception of musical sounds by evaluating how well listeners can discriminate musical instrument sounds compressed using an MP3 codec. We know that musical instruments are recognizable even when the sound has been substantially altered by a spectrum equalizer or room acoustics. Here, we will determine how detection of MP3-compressed tones varies with bit-rate and instrument. Therefore, the proposal is basic research on human perception of musical tones. We have already conducted previous discrimination studies on linear spectral alterations, including random spectral alteration and spectral interpolation. Both studies found that the detection of linear spectral alterations in musical instrument tones was more difficult in the presence of spectral variations, while spectral “jaggedness” had relatively little effect. Do the same results hold for non-linear spectral alterations such those produced by MP3-compression? Since MP3 encoding uses both temporal and spectral masking through suitable time-frequency signal processing, answering this question is a primary objective of the proposed study. We will also carry out instrument identification tests to generate a matrix showing confusion between sounds as a function of the degree of compression. Finally, we will run dissimilarity tests by having listeners judge the distances between the original and compressed sounds. These tests together will help us determine what listeners are hearing when they distinguish between very similar sounds. Just as earlier basic research on masking effects has paved the way for new ways of audio coding and for new lines of audio products, the proposed research will contribute to the quantitative comparison of musical signals, which may enable new applications, especially in comparing, searching, recognizing, and classifying musical content. 心理聲學的研究自二十世紀九十年代以來對音頻編碼產生了巨大影響。透過效當的時頻信號處理， 時間和頻譜掩蔽效應使音頻編碼器和解碼器無處不在地使用在現今個人電腦上的音頻軟件、家用及汽車音響、互聯網應用和移動設備。 雖然音頻再造已是司空見慣，新的音樂信號處理應用仍然不斷湧現。分析已記錄的音樂波形，容許我們比較、搜索、識別和分類各種音樂內容。音樂的編譯，即從已記錄的音樂波形產生樂譜，是一項具挑戰性的課題。在將來，我們有可能可根據各種聲音的聲學特徵作自動分類，並產生一系列聲音自我生成的規則。

613510.label: Realisation of objectives
613510.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. First, the time-varying spectra of musical instrument tones were data-reduced using MP3 encoding, and then we had listeners discriminate between the original and MP3 tones in formal listening tests, and statistically analyzed the resulting discrimination data. Among the eight instruments, the discrimination scores for horn were lowest. The differences were especially large for low and intermediate bit rates. This suggests that the horn is less sensitive to deterioration caused by MP3 compression. The horn has much less spectral irregularity than the other instruments, and the correlation of spectral irregularity and discrimination leads us to expect lower discrimination scores. Simultaneous masking may be a possible explanation for the correlation of spectral irregularity and discrimination. Then we had listeners identify the musical instrument generating each MP3 tone in formal listening tests, resulting in a matrix showing confusion between instruments as a function of the degree of data reduction. We found that for the saxophone and clarinet, confusion rates were significantly lower than the other instruments due to their high spectral irregularity. As a third test, we had listeners judge dissimilarity in formal listening tests by asking them to judge distances between original and MP3 encoded sounds. The dissimilarity results were significantly correlated to the instrument identification results, and both dissimilarity and identification were more smoothly varying functions than discrimination. We then correlated the discrimination, identification, and dissimilarity results with spectral incoherence, normalized centroid deviation, and spectral irregularity to determine whether these different measures of spectral variation are significantly related. We found that spectral irregularity was significantly corrected to all three, indicating that spectral shape variations have a salient effect on all types of judgments. Spectral incoherence was shown to be correlated with discrimination in randomly altered spectra in previous studies of data reduction. However, the discrimination scores in the current study were not correlated with spectral incoherence. Unlike spectral irregularity, spectral incoherence measures how much a spectrum differs from a coherent version of itself, and therefore how much the spectrum changes between adjacent analysis frames. The bit allocation process in the MP3 psychoacoustic model depends much more on simultaneous masking than on temporal masking. Temporal masking is mainly used to control frequency resolution of subband decomposition. This perhaps explains why spectral incoherence, measuring frame-to-frame spectral variation, was not strongly correlated with the discrimination scores for MP3-compressed tones, while spectral irregularity, measuring harmonic-to-harmonic spectral variation, was strongly correlated.
