613510.label: Major findings and research outcome
613510.value: Among the eight instruments, the discrimination scores for horn were lowest for eight of the ten bit rates, and near lowest for the others. The differences were especially large for low and intermediate bit rates (30, 40, 48, 56, and 64 kbps). This suggests that the horn is less sensitive to deterioration caused by MP3 compression. This makes sense since the horn has much less spectral irregularity than the other instruments, and the correlation of spectral irregularity and discrimination leads us to expect lower discrimination scores. Simultaneous masking may be a possible explanation for the correlation of spectral irregularity and discrimination. Spectral irregularity reflects the jaggedness of the spectra. A more jagged spectrum will therefore tend to have more isolated peaks and valleys. Deviations in weak harmonics will tend to be masked by surrounding strong harmonics. This idea is supported by the strong negative correlation of another measure of spectral jaggedness, the signal-to-mask ratio, with discrimination. Spectral incoherence was previously shown to be correlated with discrimination in randomly altered spectra. However, the discrimination scores in the current study were not correlated with spectral incoherence. Unlike spectral irregularity, spectral incoherence measures how much a spectrum differs from a coherent version of itself, and therefore how much the spectrum changes between adjacent analysis frames. The bit allocation process in the MP3 psychoacoustic model depends much more on simultaneous masking than on temporal masking. Temporal masking is mainly used to control frequency resolution of subband decomposition. This perhaps explains why spectral incoherence, measuring frame-to-frame spectral variation, was not strongly correlated with the discrimination scores for MP3-compressed tones, while spectral irregularity, measuring harmonic-to-harmonic spectral variation, was strongly correlated. Error metrics such as relative spectral error explained 91% of the discrimination variance in previous studies on random spectral alteration. Though its correspondence for MP3 compression was lower, it still achieved a respectable correspondence of 80%. This shows the robustness of relative spectral error as a metric for both linear and nonlinear alteration, and it is an attractive choice for many applications in music synthesis. A new error metric, which captures quantization errors by the zero-crossing rate of the harmonic envelopes’ difference, was investigated. A maximum correspondence of 78.72% was achieved when only the first five harmonics were used. This agrees with the result of the spectral envelope sensitivity study by Gunawan and Sen that distortion is more noticeable on lower harmonics than on higher harmonics.

613510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613510.value: One area for further development of the research is an evaluation of MP3 encoding on not just isolated instrument tones, but monophonic melodies. This will help address the following questions: How much MP3 compression makes the modified melody distinguishable from the original? How much compression can we make and yet retain the identity of the original instrument? Given the same amount of compression, are some melodies more discriminable than others? If so, what makes them more distinguishable? Are some MP3 compressions easier to detect in a musical context as compared to individual isolated tones? Does melodic content make it easier or harder to hear compressions by exposing or hiding the alterations?

613510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613510.value: We have determined how much detail in time-varying spectral data must be preserved to maintain excellent-sounding MP3 compression of music. Our study has found a strong correlation between discrimination and spectral irregularity. Spectral irregularity reflects the jaggedness of the spectra. A more jagged spectrum will therefore tend to have more isolated peaks and valleys. Deviations in weak harmonics will tend to be masked by surrounding strong harmonics. Spectral incoherence was previously shown to be correlated with discrimination in randomly altered spectra. However, the discrimination scores in the current study using MP3 compression were not correlated with spectral incoherence. Unlike spectral irregularity, spectral incoherence measures how much a spectrum differs from a coherent version of itself, and therefore how much the spectrum changes between adjacent analysis frames. The bit allocation process in the MP3 psychoacoustic model depends much more on simultaneous masking than on temporal masking. This perhaps explains why spectral incoherence, measuring frame-to-frame spectral variation, was not strongly correlated with the discrimination scores for MP3-compressed tones, while spectral irregularity, measuring harmonic-to-harmonic spectral variation, was strongly correlated. These results give us valuable insights, and suggest that content-specific data reduction methods, such as future MPEG encoding, can take advantage of these properties.

613810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613810.value: Current commercial DC-DC switching converters are working with a switching frequency (fs) of 1MHz to 4MHz, increased from using 200kHz to 500kHz that was very popular 15 years ago. Higher frequencies help to reduce the sizes of the inductor and the output capacitor, and it is foreseeable that in the next 5 years, the switching frequency of general purpose switching converters will be increased to 10MHz or higher. However, switching converters that have a switching frequency in the VHF (very-high-frequency) range of 30MHz to 300MHz already find applications in powering up computer processors and working as power amplifier supply modulators for polar transmitters. In recent years, there has been active research on switching converters in the 100MHz or even the 1GHz (ultra-high-frequency, UHF) range. For lower frequencies (<100MHz), PWM (pulsewidth modulation) control can be used; but for higher frequencies (>100MHz), variations of hysteretic control are commonly used. To achieve lower output ripple voltages, multi-phase operation has been attempted. In general, designs with lower frequencies and off-chip inductors have higher efficiencies (>80%), and designs with higher frequencies and on-chip inductors have lower efficiencies (<70%). We propose to study and design VHF switching converters that have a switching frequency of over 100MHz and with high efficiency approaching or over 90%. The converters should have very fast line and load transient responses and very fast reference tracking. The loop bandwidth should approach fs/5, as compared to traditional PWM controls that only achieve a bandwidth of around fs/20, whether in voltage-mode or current-mode control. To push for the high loop bandwidth limit, hysteretic control could be considered. Contrary to the established belief that hysteretic converters are unconditionally stable, however, our preliminary study shows that many operating modes are unstable. In this research, we will identify all feasible and infeasible operating conditions. Most hysteretic designs have a variable switching frequency that is undesirable in noise-sensitive applications. Hence, we will explore techniques of hysteretic control with a fixed frequency. All published discussions of switching converters with non-PWM control have failed to discuss their loop gain functions, compensation and stability. In our designs, we will employ state space averaging and loop breaking criterion of signal flow graph to derive the loop gain functions, and discuss stability in details. Many published VHF switching converters employ ad hoc circuit techniques without discussion and/or justification. We will provide design details with justification for others to reproduce our results. 摘要: 現代商用開關穩壓電源轉換器的工作頻率已從15年前的200kHz-500kHz發展至現今的1MHz-4MHz。更高的工作頻率可以減小片外電感和電容的體積。可以預測，在未來5年內，通用開關電源轉換器的工作頻率將增加到10MHz或者更高。並且，工作在甚高頻率（30MHz-300MHz）的開關電源轉換器已經被應用在電腦中央處理芯片以及極座標傳輸器的功率放大器中。近年來，關於100MHz以至1GHz (UHF, 超高頻)的開關電源轉換器已成為熱門的研究。 當頻率小於100MHz時，可以使用脉衝寬度調製來控制開關電源的工作。但當頻率高於100MHz時，控制電路則往往從遲滯控制電路的基礎上衍生出來。爲了減小輸出紋波電壓，有研究人員嘗試採用多相工作模式。總的來說，採用片外電感的低頻開關電源設計的轉換效率可以達到80%以上，而採用片上電感的高頻開關電源的轉換效率則在70%以下。 在此，我們提出開關頻率大於100MHz以及轉換效率接近或大於90%的甚高頻電源轉換器的研究課題。本設計的電源轉換器需要有非常快速的線路瞬態響應，負載瞬態響應以及非常快速的參考電源跟隨能力。傳統脉衝寬度調製控制的電源轉換器的環路響應帶寬為開關頻率（fs）的二十分之一，本設計將基於電壓或電流控制模式，並將環路響應帶寬提升至開關頻率的五分之一。 爲了推高環路帶寬的限制，我們將對遲滯工作模式進行深入研究。一般研究認為遲滯控制模式是無條件穩定的，但在我們的初步研究中發現，遲滯控制在一些工作情況下並不穩定。在本研究中，我們將對遲滯控制模式進行全面的分析并作出結論。遲滯控制的開關頻率是一個變化量，這對於噪聲敏感的應用來說是有影響的。所以，我們希望研究如何將其開關頻率設計成一個固定值。在已發表的文獻中，還沒有人分析過非脉衝寬度調製控制開關電源轉換器的環路增益函數、環路補償和穩定性問題。在本研究中，我們將採用狀態空間平均法、環路斷開準則和信號流圖法來推導環路增益函數，并詳細討論系統穩定性的問題。很多發表的甚高頻開關電源轉換器均採用非常特別的未驗證的電路設計，而在本研究中，我們將提供電路設計的詳細資料，以便開發和應用。

Develop high-speed integrated circuit (IC) functional blocks for VHF switching converters.

Design and document integrated switching converters that work in the VHF range, with a high efficiency as close to, or even higher than, 90%. The converters should have very fast line and load transient responses and very fast reference tracking.

613810.label: Major findings and research outcome
613810.value: In this research, both time-domain and frequency-domain properties of switching converters were thoroughly analyzed, and advanced high-speed IC techniques were developed. The research output can be divided into theoretical study and practical implementation. Theoretical study [J1]: Charge balance analysis and state transition analysis are presented in analyzing hysteretic voltage mode switching converters working in the steady state. The relation between switching frequency and load current of the voltage-mode hysteretic buck converter is accurately predicted, while both boost and buck-boost converters are proved to be infeasible topologies. [J3]: A systematic application of state-space averaging in computing the open-loop and closed-loop transfer functions, namely, the voltage conversion functions, the input impedances and the output impedances of switching converters working in the continuous conduction mode is presented. An accurate circuit-level simulation methodology – the frequency-point spectrum analysis – is introduced to verify the analytical results. [C2]: A comparative study of hysteretic voltage-mode buck converters in achieving high switching frequency and high regulation accuracy is presented. To minimize switching delay single boundary control and ramp generation in-phase with the inductor current should be employed. [C5]: A circuit-oriented geometrical approach based on straightforward graphical analysis of voltage-mode switching converters in predicting subharmonic oscillation is derived. In particular, the critical condition of subharmonic oscillation of the buck converter is derived. Practical Implementation [J2] A 10/30 MHz PWM voltage-mode buck converter with a wide duty-cycle range is presented. A high-accuracy delay-compensated ramp generator using only low-speed comparators but can work up to 70 MHz is proposed. By using a differential difference amplifier (DDA), a new Type-III compensator is proposed to reduce the chip area of the compensator by 60%. Moreover, based on the unique structure of the proposed compensator, an end-point prediction (EPP) scheme is also implemented to achieve fast reference-tracking responses. [C1] A hybrid buck converter that consists of a PWM voltage-mode buck converter with Type III compensation and two auxiliary linear regulators for fast-transient-response is proposed. The auxiliary linear regulators are activated during load transient to achieve small voltage dip and short recovery time; and are deactivated in the steady state to achieve high efficiency. [C3] A 10/30 MHz PWM buck converter with an accuracy-improved ramp generator is proposed. This technique is superseded by the delay-compensated ramp generated that is first presented in [C4], and will be detailed in [J2]. [C4] This is the conference (short) version of [J2]. [PA1] This patent application describes the IC technique proposed in [C1]. [PA2] This patent application describes one of the IC techniques proposed in [J2].

613810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613810.value: In working out this research, several important inventions that we regard as instrumental in the design of VHF switching converters have been made, and two patent applications were sent to the Technology Transfer Center (TTC) of HKUST for consideration. Eventually, one US patent application was filed [PA1], and the other is in the queue [PA2]. Moreover, two techniques, namely the delay-compensated ramp generator and the area-efficient Type III compensator, have been employed in designing a power management integrated circuit (PMIC) that was scheduled to power up a GPS (global positioning system) transceiver developed by Fujitsu Semiconductor. Hence, actual technology transfer is under way. Based on the acquired knowledge through this research, we are planning to work out a 100 MHz switching converter with high efficiency, to pave the way for fully-integrated switching converter (that is, with on-chip inductor and output capacitor).

613810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613810.value: Efficient power transfer (for example, from the battery to the microprocessor) is mostly performed by switching converters, as ideal switching converters are proved to have unity efficiency. The VHF (very-high frequency, from 30 to 300 MHz) range is demonstrated to be a good compromise between increased switching loss and reducing the values as well as the sizes of the inductor and the output capacitor. The objectives of this research project are to develop (1) mathematical techniques in analyzing and (2) integrated circuit (IC) techniques in designing VHF switching converters. We carried out in-depth investigation into the operation of switching converters. Both detailed time-domain analysis and frequency-domain analysis have been worked out, and the results could be used by practicing engineers in analyzing and designing their VHF switching converters. Moreover, advanced IC techniques including a delay-compensated ramp generator that works up to 70 MHz, an area-efficient Type III compensator that built around a differential-difference amplifier, and an end-point prediction scheme for fast reference tracking have been proposed, fabricated, tested and verified. Finally, a 10/30 MHz buck converter that integrated the above IC techniques and achieves accurate and fast transient responses is designed, fabricated and tested with peak efficiency of 91.8%.

614010.label: Project Objectives
614010.value: To develop a novel technique to synthesize graphene sheets for mass production through electrochemical intercalation of natural graphite into fully exfoliated graphite; To apply the layer-by-layer deposition technique to produce graphene/polymer laminate composites that possess exceptional characteristics, such as extremely high transport properties, excellent fracture toughness and barrier resistance.
rows: To develop a novel technique to synthesize graphene sheets for mass production through electrochemical intercalation of natural graphite into fully exfoliated graphite;

To apply the layer-by-layer deposition technique to produce graphene/polymer laminate composites that possess exceptional characteristics, such as extremely high transport properties, excellent fracture toughness and barrier resistance.

614010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
614010.value: Graphene is rapidly emerging as the next-generation 'wonder' material to replace carbon nanotubes in many niche applications. Graphene is a flat monolayer of carbon atoms tightly packed into a honeycomb lattice. The two-dimensional material exhibits a range of unusual properties, such as excellent electrical and thermal conductivities, and extremely high elastic modulus and tensile strength. Graphene is a basic building block for graphitic materials of all other dimensionalities. It can be wrapped up into 0D fullerenes, rolled into 1D carbon nanotubes (CNTs) or stacked into 3D graphite. Thus, these carbon allotropes share many exciting common properties. Graphene can be produced at a fraction of the cost required to synthesize CNTs, making it an attractive alternative to CNTs that are in extensive use in many fields. Amongst the techniques developed to produce graphene sheets, direct exfoliation of graphite in selected solvents is known to be the most promising. However at present, the production scale and quality of graphene still remain a challenge. This project proposes a novel method to synthesize highly conductive graphene sheets with few defects using an electrochemical method. The synthesis process will be optimized by evaluating the effects of several important electrochemical parameters, such as current density, potential value, electrolyte concentration and reaction duration, on the stage index and graphene formation. These graphene sheets will be incorporated into an epoxy to fabricate polymer nanocomposites. To better utilize the unique two dimensional nature of graphene sheets, two new processing techniques will be incorporated, including the application of an electric field and the layer-by-layer deposition of graphene films, so as to produce laminate nanocomposites with well-aligned graphene sheets of high volume contents. These laminate composites will possess exceptional properties, such as extremely high electrical and thermal conductivities, as well as excellent mechanical properties and resistance to fracture and moisture/gas permeation. Hybrid composites containing an additional phase, conductive polymer(s), in the epoxy matrix will also be studied to generate a more isotropic nature to the laminate composites, introducing a desired electrical conductivity along the thickness direction. In summary, the proposed research aims at developing multi-functional laminate nanocomposites incorporating uniform and well-aligned graphene sheets for emerging applications in nanoelectronics, conductive/tough coatings and thin films, and structural composite materials. 石墨烯作為一種迅速出現的下一代新興奇特材料，在許多特定應用領域中有望替代碳納米管。它是由單層碳原子緊密排列而成的蜂窩狀六角平面晶體。這種二維結構的材料具有一系列不同尋常的性質，例如極好的導電和導熱性質，極高的彈性模量和抗張強度。石墨烯是構建其它維數碳材料的基本單元。它可以包裹形成零維的富勒烯，卷曲形成一維的碳納米管，或者堆積形成三維的石墨。因此，這些碳材料具有優良的常見性質。石墨烯的制備成本遠低於已被廣泛應用的碳納米管，從而使之成為一種引人註意的碳納米管的替代品。在制備石墨烯的各種方法中，將石墨在特定溶劑中直接剝離是最可行的方式。但是，批量化生產並且保證石墨烯的質量在目前仍然是一個挑戰。 本項目擬定了一種新型的電化學方法來制備低缺陷並且具有優良導電性的石墨烯。制備流程將會通過評估各種重要電化學參數的影響來優化，這些參數包括電流密度，電壓大小，電解質密度以及在石墨烯形成不同階段的反應時間等。所得到的石墨烯將會被摻入環氧樹脂來制備聚合物基納米復合材料。為了更好的應用石墨烯的獨特二維特性，兩種新型加工技術將會被采用來制備排列整齊並且體積含量高的石墨烯層壓納米復合材料。這兩種加工技術包括利用電場的方法以及利用交替沈積技術來制備石墨烯薄膜。這種層壓復合材料將具有許多獨特的性質，例如極其高的導電和導熱性能，優良的機械性能，以及抗斷裂和抗濕氣/氣體滲透性能等。含有另一相導電聚合物的環氧樹脂基混雜復合材料是另外一個研究重點，通過混雜，復合材料將會具有各向同性的性質，使厚度方向的導電性大為增強。 總之，本研究將專註於開發多功能層壓納米復合材料，此種材料含有均勻分散，排列整齊的石墨烯，在諸多例如納米電子，導電/堅韌塗層和薄膜，結構復合材料等新興領域具有廣闊的應用前景。

614010.label: Major findings and research outcome
614010.value: Objective 1: Synthesis of high quality, monolayer graphene oxide (GO) sheets, liquid crystallinity and transparent conducting films Natural graphite flakes were intercalated to obtain graphite ntercalation compounds which was rapidly heated to produce expanded graphite that was further processed for the production of high quality graphene oxide (GO). (J01) After further oxidation with KMnO4, an aqueous dispersion with well-exfoliated monolayer GO sheets is obtained (J01, J02). The quality of GO sheets was further improved by totally avoiding the use of sonication (J03). A novel technique was developed to sort the as-prepared GO sheets into a few different groups of similar sizes, so that only ultralarge GO sheets were collected for specific use requiring high transparency and excellent transport properties. Four different groups of GO sheets were obtained through three runs of centrifugation. (J04, J05) The ultra large UL-GO sheets were used to identify spontaneous formation of nematic liquid crystals upon the addition in water above a critical concentration of about 0.1wt%. It is the among lowest filler contents ever reported for the formation of liquid crystals due to the ultrahigh aspect ratio of the GO sheets. (J06) Objective 2: Highly transparent, conductive graphene films and highly-oriented multifunctional composites Both the vacuum filtration and Langmuir-Blodgett assembly methods were used to fabricate transparent conducting graphene films on a quartz substrate using GO dispersion. The films were treated using HNO3 and SOBr2 to enhance their functional qualities. (J02, J05). A remarkable sheet resistance of ∼500 Ω/sq at 90% transparency was obtained, which outperformed the graphene films CVD grown on a Ni substrate. (J05) Composites containing highly-aligned graphene sheets were produced via casting of polyurethane (PU) and epoxy resins. The resulting composites based on PU showed excellent electrical conductivity with a low percolation threshold of 0.078 vol%, the lowest value ever reported for graphene/polymer composites. The electrical conductivity of the composites presented significant anisotropy due to the preferential alignment in-plane direction. (J07) The nanocomposites delivered more than 10-fold increases in tensile properties, while the moisture permeability of the composites decreased with increasing graphene content, clearly indicating the impermeable graphene sheets. (J08) The epoxy-based composites combined strong graphene-epoxy interfacial bonds and preferential graphene alignment rendering them unique multi-functional anisotropic properties, including high electrical and mechanical properties and electromagnetic shielding efficiencies. They showed exceptionally high dielectric constants of 14000 with 3wt% of graphene due to the charge accumulation at highly-aligned conductive fillers. (J09, J10)

614010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
614010.value: While developing the synthesis process of GO sheets is more or less saturated, there is still much to do on developing useful graphene-based composites. One potentially attractive most recent development is to fabricate three dimensional (3D) graphene in the form of graphene aerogel and foam. Composites with interconnected graphene fillers can be prepared by infiltrating liquid polymer resins into the porous graphene structure. By virtue of porous nature of these 3D graphene, unique mechanical and transport properties are expected from the composites, and many different processing and materials options can be explored to modify and optimize certain properties depending on end applications.

614010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614010.value: In this project, a new technique has been developed to produce graphene oxide (GO) from natural graphene flakes and sort them into a few groups of different sizes. The large GO sheets produced here are proven to be among the largest according to the literature: they have more than 60 um on average in lateral size, facilitating the fabrication of transparent thin films and polymer-based composites whose intended functional and mechanical properties are much better than those made from ordinary small, low-quality GO. One example is the extremely high transparencies and electrical conductivities of the thin films made from the large GO sheets, which are comparable or even better than those made from synthetic graphene by chemical vapor deposition. These exceptional properties mean a potential substitute of the commercial thin films made from indium tin oxides. Another successful application is the fabrication of highly-aligned GO/polymer composites. These composites delivered very high electrical conductivities with extremely low percolation thresholds, a measure of the filler content to make the composites electrically conductive. They presented very high dielectric constants, along with high electromagnetic shielding efficiencies in a certain direction, making them useful in portable electronic devices like smart phones to block unwanted microwaves.

614410.label: Project Objectives
614410.value: Understand and optimize the method of bilayer alignment of LCD using photoalignment. Investigate the basic mechanism and physics of the inhomogeneous alignment process. Produce a tunable lense based on liquid crystals. Produce an optical beam steering device based on liquid crystals.

Produce an optical beam steering device based on liquid crystals.

614410.label: Realisation of objectives
614410.value: The stated objectives of this project have all been achieved. We were able to make use of our newly invented nanoalignment surfaces to obtain high pretilt angles for a liquid crystal cell. Using a combination of nanoalignment and photoalignment, we could obtain a spatially varying pretilt angle. We investigated theoretically and experimentally such novel alignment mechanisms. It turns out that nanoalignment of liquid crystal is very useful and interesting as well. There is a certain size of the nano-domains for this technique to work. It cannot be too small or else the anchoring energy will be too small and the process window of alignment is too small. It cannot be too large or else the alignment will not be homogeneous. We are able to achieve any pretilt angle routinely using this new method. A patent has been filed. After thoroughly understanding this alignment surface, we combine it with photoalignment to achieve spatially varying pretilt angles across the liquid crystal cell, as proposed in this project. We were able to make a spatial profile mimicking that of a lens. Since the retardation of the liquid crystal cell is dependent on the pretilt angle, thus we are able to achieve spatially varying retardation. Using this property we made a liquid cryatl lens whose focal length can be varied electrically. This tunable lens can be tuned from infinity focal length to 20cm focal length. It should be useful for automatic focussing lens systems and for making zoom lens. We were also able to make a beam steering device using this technique. The beam steering angle is as large as 5 degrees. Unfortunately because of the limited retardation of the liquid crystal material, we could not make the beam steering angle larger. Presumably one can stack several of these beam steering devices to achieve larger steering angles if needed. Thus all the objectives of this project have been achieved. Several conference and journal papers have been published, together with a patent application.

614410.label: Major findings and research outcome
614410.value: We have been able to develop a novel type of alignment surface for liquid crystal molecules. Using a combination of nanostructured domains and photoalignment, we can accomplish a spatially varying pretilt angle with any predesigned spatial variation. Using this technique we fabricated several liquid crystal based optical elements, including a tunable lens and a beam steerer. The technique used is rather unique. A patent application has been filed. By applying our newly developed nanoalignment surfaces, we can produce variable pretilt angles so that the birefringence of the liquid crystal cell can be changed laterally across the cell. Thus we can make a lens as well as a beam steerer. If the spatial variation has a quadratic retardation profile, a lens can be made. We were able to fabricate a lens with a focal length of 20cm. By applying an electric field to reduce the retardation, the focal length can be increased to infinity (no lens action). Thus it is an electrically tunable lens. By making the spatial profile linear, we can achieve a beam steerer. Unfortunate due to the limited retardation value, the beam steering angle is only 5 degrees. Presumably several devices can be stacked together to achieve larger beam steering angles. Using an entirely different approach, we were able to fabricate a beam steering device with more than 10 degrees. This device is a polarization grating. In this device the incoming beam is diffracted to a large angle with high efficiency. But this beam steering is not tunable and is of fixed value. Further development is needed to make this device tunable.

614410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
614410.value: The newly developed technique of spatially varying liquid crystal pretilt angle and hence spatially varying retardation is potentially very useful. In this project we have applied this technique to two optical elements - lens and beam steerer. Presumably more optical elements can be made using this technique. Since the retardation is electrically tunable, hence the optical properties of such devices can be electrically tuned as well. For the polarization grating devices, currently we are using a liquid crystal polymer. Hence the retardation value is not tunable. As a further development, we should try to use ordinary liquid crystal to make this grating. They the diffraction efficiency can be tuned. Unfortunately the diffraction angle will be difficult to vary. Presumably if we use a fine pixel spatial light modulator, we can make the pitch of the grating tunable as well and achieve variable beam steering. Further work should be carried out to make such devices. Electrically tunable optical devices should find applications in many optoelectronic systems.

614410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614410.value: We developed a new technique to align a liquid crystal. Surface alignment of liquid crystal is needed to give it a pretilt angle. We were able to adjust the pretilt angle at will which is heterofore impossible. This is a new development. Furthermore we were able to make the pretilt angle spatially varying by design. This is also impossible to achieve using conventional techniques. In this project we have applied this technique to two optical elements - lens and beam steerer. For the liquid crystal lens, we were able to vary the focal length from 20cm to infinity. For the beam steerer, we were able to steer the optical beam by an angle of 0 to 5 degrees. Presumably more optical elements can be made using this technique. Since the retardation is electrically tunable, hence the optical properties of such devices can be electrically tuned as well.

614910.label: Project Objectives
614910.value: Objective A: Develop a Robust Lattice-Based Interference Alignment Framework Using the high dimensional lattice theory, we will study the benefits and cost of a new interference alignment target, which will result in structured interference that matches the practical finite signal constellation. Objective B: Optimize the constellation design on a MIMO interference network under time-varying and imperfect CSI Using the robust optimization theory, non-linear control, Lyapunov stability theory and the results in (A), we shall study the sensitivity of lattice alignment and optimize the lattice constellation design w.r.t. some practical objectives (such as the SER), taking into account of the imperfect and time-varying CSI knowledge. Objective C: Develop Applications to IMT-Advance and 4G Systems We shall apply the theoretical framework and insights obtained in (A) and (B), and characterize the actual performance gain that could be expected in the next generation wireless systems (such as the IMT-Advance and 4G systems) by performing detail simulations under practical constraints and settings.

614910.label: Realisation of objectives
614910.value: We have successfully developed a robust lattice-based interference alignment framework using high dimensional lattice theory. In contrast to conventional interference alignment where the goal is to reduce the dimension of the common subspace containing interference, our lattice-based method is to align the interference lattice such that the overall interference space has some regular structures. As a result, instead of zero-forcing the interference subspace, the proposed approach utilises all dimensions of the signal space to transmit desired signals over the "gaps" of the structured interference space. We have successfully studied the construction methods as well as the associated DoF analysis using lattice signals as inputs. We have also applied the design framework to finite constellation and IMT-Advanced Systems. We showed that significant performance gains can be achieved compared with conventional approaches.

614910.label: Major findings and research outcome
614910.value: We have thoroughly investigated the feasibility and the advantage of lattice-based interference alignment. The proposed design framework utilises all the available signal space dimension and transmits the desired signals over gaps of the structured interference space. As a result, the proposed scheme achieved substantial performance gains in theory and in practice. We have published six IEEE journal papers (IEEE Transactions in Signal Processing) as well as one IEEE conference paper. Furthermore, the project has supported three Ph.D. students and one postdoc.

614910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
614910.value: There are various items that worth further development. For example, extension of the lattice approach to different network topologies (other than K pairs interference channels) will require careful study. Another important area of extension includes the robustness of the proposed lattice scheme with respect to errors in channel estimation will be crucial for the practical applications of the schemes.

614910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614910.value: Interference is well-known to be a first order bottleneck in many wireless systems such as the cellular network, WiFi. In this project, we have proposed an innovative approach to deal with interference in wireless networks. Using the proposed lattice input signals as well as careful designs of MIMO precoders, we have created structured interference, which is less harmful to random interference. By carefully controlling the transmission of the desired signals over the "gaps" of the interference space, we can achieve significant performance gains over conventional interference mitigation approaches. The proposed method has widespread applications in future wireless communication systems.

615610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
615610.value: 摘要： 商联机构的运动一般由左手子副和右手子副协调完成，两个部分的相对移动决定了此商联机构的运动构型。这种运动构型可能是一个李群、一个子流型或是SE(3)的一个商空间。相较于具有相同运动构型的纯串联和纯并联机构，商联机构具有非常明显的优势，诸如：简单的运动结构、更好的结构刚性、还有更适用于可模块或可重组的设计等等。越来越多的商联机构被广泛应用于高速高精度的工作场合，如半导体封装和高速加工行业。 商联机构的定位精度和系统整体性能不仅取决于各子副的定位精度，还包括两子副间的协调性和兼容性。因此我们需要在拓扑选型、结构设计、标定和控制等各个方面用一系列的指标对系统有一个整体的评估。 本项目将着重研究关节间隙及弹性形变对商联机构定位误差的影响。同时，我们将给出运动构型误差以及型内投影误差构成两个互补子空间的几何和物理解释。在如何高效计算出给定工作空间的运动构型误差的问题解决之后，我们将主要探讨如果将运动构型误差和型内误差应用在拓扑设计、结构优化及机构标定等方面。最后，运动构型误差会被作为主要性能指标进行设计优化，应用到商联LED固晶机之中去。

615610.label: Realisation of objectives
615610.value: 1. Through an extensive study of several mathematically rigorous and engineeringly meaningful models, the quotient space model, we characterize the pose error in a displacement group G and its two projections into a subgroup module H and a quotient module {G/H} of quotient kinematic machines (QKMs). We have resolved the non-uniqueness of projection maps based on two kinematic models: the canonical representation (product of exponential) of {G/H}, and the symmetric (or exponential) submanifolds Exp(m) with m a Lie triple system. Using these two models, we have successfully formulated the QKM optimal design problem with suitable motion type error as the performance index. 2. Based on a convex formulation for typical joint clearances, we have identified the influence on pose error by major error sources in a QKM. The overall pose error is then decomposed into a configuration error (H or Exp(m)) and motion type error ({G/H} or Exp([m,m])). Typical examples for the two cases are: a DELTA robot with rotation pose error, and a uniform rotation parallel wrist with torsion error. On the analysis side, we investigated the measurement of motion type error on a parallel wrist called the omni-wrist under various control schemes. On the design side, we proposed to use “Random Levenberg-Marquardt” algorithm to solve the nonlinear optimization problem involved within. With practical experiments, our algorithm was proved to be efficient and accurate. To deal with configuration error, we proposed an “Adjoint error model” parameterize the joint configuration space, and a calibration algorithm adopting an iterative linearization approach. 3. We have completed the third objective by using our new motion type error formulation in objective 1, and have developed a corresponding algorithm. After rigorous analysis, we found that joint clearance is one of the biggest sources of pose error for parallel manipulators, and finding the bounds of maximal errors is a convex optimization problem. We have applied semi-definite programming and second-order cone programming to solve the maximal error bounds. 4. Based on the study of the three parts mentioned above, we proposed a design that utilized a five-bar mechanism as one module of the QKM for the LED die bonding application. After developing its dynamic equation and a simplified model, we obtained a convex objective function with non-convex constraints. The problem is solved by a differential evolution algorithm and a set of global optimal values have been obtained. The results show that the proposed design approach is effective.

615610.label: Major findings and research outcome
615610.value: 1. We established a complete theory of geometric modeling, analysis and synthesis theory for quotient kinematics machines (QKMs). We studied classifications for canonical representations of {G/H}, and presented an indirect and direct synthesis method for realizations of G/H (Part C.8: Item 1). Besides, a new kinematic model, the symmetric submanifolds, was also developed for modeling motion type error for certain classes of QKMs. The inversion symmetry of SE(3) was systematically exploited and its geometric properties would impact not only the motion type error analysis but also the type synthesis of QKMs (Part C.8: Item 2 and Part C.9: Item 6). 2. A parallel kinematic manipulator (PKM) with proposed motion type may have undesirable (or uncompensated) pose error at the end-effector due to the effect of joint clearance and component flexibility (joint or link). This would cause severe accuracy performance degradation. We proposed a performance index, namely “Motion Type Error”, to evaluate such undesirable errors. A three-step calculation process was developed and formulated, and its application was investigated by case study, in which the comparison of Tsai’s 3UPU, SNU’s 3UPU and Delta robot was carried out (Part C.8: Item 2). Moreover, the end-effector errors of Omni-Wrist V under various control schemes were measured by experiments (Part C.8: Item 7). 3. An accurate kinematic model is one fundamental requirement of high performance manipulators. But due to the existence of tolerance and clearance, calibration should always be carried out first to identify the inaccuracy and further modify the kinematic model. We proposed an innovative “Random Levenberg-Marquardt” algorithm to solve the nonlinear optimization problem. With practical experiments, our algorithm was proved to be efficient and accurate (Part C.8: Item 3). Adopting an iterative linearization approach, the “Adjoint error model” was presented to parameterize the joint configuration space. Based on the error model we derived methods to calibrate the manipulators. Simulations were demonstrated to show its effectiveness. (Part C.8: Item 8-9). 4. The five-bar mechanisms are often used in applications that require high speed and high precision motion control. We proposed a design that utilized the five-bar mechanism as one module of the QKM for the LED die bonding application. After developing its dynamic equation and a simplified model, we obtained a convex function as an objective function with a set of real constraints. We optimized the problem with differential evolution algorithm and got a set of global optimal values. The effectiveness of the proposed design approach is demonstrated by simulation results (Part C.8: Item 4).

615610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615610.value: In comparison to conventional workspace definition and error modeling, motion type error provides a better criterion for prevention of uncompensatable errors. Motion type error serves as a performance criterion for PKM and QKM type selection and dimension optimization. In our future work, we shall consider a more comprehensive motion type error model, taking into consideration unit dependency and coordinate dependency. A comparative study should be conducted between motion type error approach and conventional optimization approach. Besides, experiments on our HKUST PD platform (accuracy within 20μm and precision around ±5μm) shows that performance could be further improved if high-level controller is implemented. Finally, the generalized Jacobian for accuracy, kinetostatic and stiffness modeling, and its extension to rigid body dynamics, will be used to form a complete theoretical package for parametric modeling of the lower mobility manipulators. Further development in prototyping will also be considered in our future work.

615610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615610.value: Mechanisms are designed to have certain degree of freedom and to move within certain subspace of SE(3). However, due to the imperfection of joint clearances and link deflections, machines may have pose errors at the end-effector that are undesirable (or uncompensated) and make the end-effector outside the designed space. Such error is termed “Motion Type error”, which is of vital importance especially to the quotient kinematics machine (QKM). In this project, we developed a complete method of geometric modeling, analysis and synthesis for QKM, and established physical interpretations for the motion type error. The motion type error was then used as a performance index to evaluate different kinds of manipulators by case studies as well as experiments. An accurate kinematic model is one fundamental requirement and calibration should always be conducted before real applications. Formulated as an optimization problem, we came up with the “Random Levenberg-Marquardt” algorithm and “Adjoint error model” to solve the calibration problem. Also we proposed the QKM structure for advance applications such as LED die bonding. Based on this project, we provided theoretical tools to help the mechanical synthesis, the performance index to evaluate different designs and methods to get precise manipulators models.

615710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
615710.value: 高性能電子器件的發展預示半導體器件的臨界尺寸將會小於22納米,並且發熱密度會達到300瓦每平方釐米。這麼高的發熱率對電子工業來說是個大的挑戰。為了有效地耗散電子器件中的廢熱,不同的散熱方法已經被開發出來。這其中包括熱傳導,熱電冷卻器,以及基於流體的散熱系統。在這些方法中,微尺度通道散熱系統或許是最有潛力的一種方法。但是這種方法需要很高的泵壓去驅動流體。同時所需的泵因耗能而會降低電子器件的整體效率。 在本專案中,我們提出一種無泵微/納米流體系統。在這個系統中,流體是被電子器件中的固有溫度梯度所驅動。這個系統中的微/納米通道的表面有著不同的自由能。一邊的表面能很高,另一邊的表面能很低。由於流體-表面作用不同,在表面能高的一邊,流體由低溫向高溫流動;而在表面能低的一邊,流體則由高溫向低溫流動。這樣,如果通道的中間溫度高於兩端的溫度,流體就會被對稱的溫度梯度驅使在通道中不停地流動而並不需要泵(如圖1所示)。雖然我們已經通過分子動力學模擬在納米通道中演示了這個想法,但是這個系統的散熱能力還尚不清楚。在本專案中,我們將製造微/納米通道並且研究流體在有溫度梯度的情況下在通道中的流動。我們還將用分子動力學模擬探討通道表面能和溫度的變化對流體流動的影響。最後,我們將生產這種無泵微/納米流體系統並測試其散熱能力。 本專案中提出的散熱方法設及對流體在微/納米通道中流動的諸多基礎問題的研究。本專案同時將會有利於給香港和珠江三角洲地區的電子工業的發展。

615710.label: Major findings and research outcome
615710.value: We investigated the mechanisms of fluid transport driven by temperature gradients in nanochannels through molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. It is found that the fluid-wall interaction is critical in determining the flow direction. In channels of very low surface energy, where the fluid-wall binding energy is small, the fluid moves from high to low temperature. In high surface energy channels, however, the fluid is pumped from low to high temperature. We explained the mechanisms of the fluid motion in nanochannels induced by temperature gradients through MD simulations. We also studied the effect of channel size on the fluid motion and compared the results with traditional solutions, i.e., the validity of the Navier-Stokes (NS) equations for nanoscale liquid flows through MD simulations. We focused on the role of channel size by considering the fluid-wall interaction. Liquid flows between two planar parallel walls driven by an external force with channel size ranging from 2 to 80 nm were studied. The volumetric flux was computed and the dependence of the volumetric flux on the channel size was explained both qualitatively and quantitatively. Furthermore, we calculated the thermal resistance at the fluid-wall interface in nanochannels and found that the thermal resistance depended on many parameters, such as the flowrate and fluid-wall interaction parameters. In experiments, we conducted water flows in homogeneous nanochannel arrays first and found that the classic fluid mechanics breaks down when the pressure gradient is larger than a critical value. As the pressure gradient is increased, it was found that fluid flows underwent a transition, which is caused by the velocity slip at the fluid-solid interface. In heterogeneous nanochannels, we found that the pressure required to maintain the same flow rate in different directions are different, which offers an opportunity to develop fluidic rectifier without moving parts using nanochannels. Based on our work, we have published 8 journal papers.

615710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615710.value: We will continue the work we have done and try to optimize the cooling capacity of the nanochannel devices. We also plan to develop a fluidic rectification system using heterogeneous nanochannels for flow control.

615710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615710.value: In this project, we studied fluid flows in nanoscale channels and found some new phenomena, which can be employed for ad-hoc applications, including the cooling of micro- and nanoscale devices or chips. Furthermore, heterogeneous nanochannels can be used to control fluid flows without using moving parts, which is important for the biomedical applications of micro/nanofluidic systems.

615810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
615810.value: This proposal proposes a systematic study of magnesium phosphate cement (MPC) based concrete. Unlike conventional concrete that uses Portland cement as a binder, MPC concrete utilizes magnesium phosphate cement as a binding medium. Magnesium phosphate cement is a new kind of cementitious material with chemical bonding formed by an acid-base reaction between magnesia and phosphate. Preliminary research shows that MPC concrete has the advantages of high early strength, low permeability, excellent bonding to Portland cement concrete as well as steel, excellent resistance to chemical attack, excellent strength development at low temperature, and excellent resistance to deicer freezing-thaw scaling. Due to these advantages, magnesium phosphate cement based concrete has been attracting more and more attention. However, MPC concrete sets so fast that it is difficult to apply on site. Besides, the reaction mechanism of MPC concrete has not been clearly understood, nor has its microstructure. To understand the reaction mechanism of MPC concrete, the effects of isothermal behavior, molar ratios, admixtures, and magnesia reactivity will be examined. Molecular dynamics will be firstly used to simulate the possible reaction pattern and products of MPC cement. Then, XRD, NMR, and AFM measurements will be carried out on carefully prepared specimens to clarify the reaction mechanism and identify the microstructural features of the crystalline phases, such as their morphology, crystal habits, grain sizes, and elemental compositions. The systematic microstructural observation of MPC cement will provide essential information for optimizing the crystal structures of the various reaction phases of the cement. The setting behavior will be investigated by Vicat needle penetration and non-contact resistivity measurement to assess the influences of the magnesia particle size, the molar ratio of magnesium to phosphate, and retarder. For application purposes, the surface bonding, compression and flexural strength, and its workability, durability and serviceability will be investigated as well. It is expected that the study will reveal the nature of the MPC concrete’s reactions, build up a model of its microstructure, establish an effective method to control its reaction rate, and provide optimized proportions of the MPC concrete mix for engineering applications.

615810.label: Realisation of objectives
615810.value: By utilizing a dilute suspension made of magnesia powder, potassium dihydrogen phosphate and a large amount of water, together with the measurement of the pH development, the reaction mechanism of magnesium phosphate cement (MPC) has been identified. During the study, the setting control is racialized through the magnesium particle size optimization, addition of suitable amount of borax, and cooling water. The microstructure of the MPC concrete has been characterized by using scanning electron microscopy and XRD, and identified the crystal transferring process from initial product of MgHPO4•7H2O to Mg2KH(PO4)2•15H2O finally to MgKPO4•6H2O. The microstructural observations of the different crystalline phases in MPC are verified by compositional analysis. It provides the base for designing a MPC concrete for practical application, especially for fast repair.

615810.label: Major findings and research outcome
615810.value: The reaction mechanism of magnesium phosphate cement (MPC) has been investigated through a diluted suspension system. The suspension is obtained by adding a mixture of magnesia powder and potassium dihydrogen phosphate to a tenfold mass of water. The pH development of the suspension is monitored and recorded under continuous and moderate stirring. The pH-time curves obtained have a similar shape when different magnesia to phosphate (M/P) molar ratios is used. Several characteristic points can be identified from the curves and used to distinguish different reaction stages of the system. Through phase identification of the residue and ionic concentration analysis of the filtrate at each characteristic point, the reaction process of MPC is realized as follows: after the instant dissolution of phosphate into water, small fraction of magnesia dissociates into solution and forms the initial product of MgHPO4•7H2O. It transfers to Mg2KH(PO4)2•15H2O later on and finally MgKPO4•6H2O. The morphology from SEM observation shows that MgHPO4•7H2O is mainly in hollow bladed shape with various surface textures, Mg2KH(PO4)2•15H2O plank-shape with evident and irregular cleavages on the surface, and MgKPO4•6H2O well-crystallized prismatic crystal with smooth, rigid surface and triangular ends. To further understand the newly developed cementing system, a systematic study of its microstructure is performed, starting from paste design, phase identification, to morphology examination and compositional analysis. The experimental results show that the mechanical properties of MPC pastes may be dictated by the rational formulation, in turn the crystallinity and growth of the principal reaction product of the heterogeneous ternary system. It is found that a poor crystal growth and a significant amount of unreacted raw materials produced in the cement pastes with low M/P ratios, while a better crystal growth associated with high early strength achieved for the pastes with an M/P ratio as high as ten folds of the calculated one. The microstructural observations of the different crystalline phases in MPC are verified by compositional analysis which agrees well with the theoretical values. It provides some base for designing a MPC concrete for practical application.

615810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615810.value: This project has led to a good understanding on the reaction mechanism of MPC and know how on the application of MPC concrete. The potential for further development can be viewed in three aspects. First, the fast setting nature of the MPC makes it perfect candidate for the processing technique of 3-D printing. The study on its application in manufacturing the complicated and functioned MPC-based products using 3-D printing will lead to new research and application area for MPC. Second, the excellent bonding properties of MPC are highly suitable for the coating materials. We will explore the feasibility in developing MPC-based inorganic coating for thermal insulation and decoration purpose. Finally, to be larger applied in practice, more efficient setting time control methods have to be developed.

615810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615810.value: Magnesium phosphate cement (MPC) is a new kind of cementitious binder in which the chemical bonding is formed by a through-solution acid-base reaction between dead burned magnesia and phosphate. One of the advantages of the MPC is fast hardening and high early strength. However, it hardens too fast that does not leave sufficient working time for casting. To control the setting time to suit the need for construction, the reaction mechanism has to be understood. In this project, the dilute suspension system is used to investigate the reaction stages and reaction product at different stages through PH value measurement and chemical analysis on the residual in the solution. It has revealed that MPC reaction can be divided into four stages. The mechanism study provides the theoretical background on how to retard the reaction rate and control the working period, which make it is possible to apply the MPC concrete in large scale project. This project has extended the application of MPC into the reflective coating materials and very good result has been achieved.

616910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616910.value: Wireless ad-hoc networks provide an important technology for a plethora of practical applications, including environmental monitoring, community mesh networks, military and battlefield networks, health and emergency services. This has stimulated a huge research effort over the past few years, aimed at understanding the fundamental capacity limits of wireless ad-hoc networks. Addressing this important problem is very challenging and requires new advanced tools which extend beyond the realm of “classical” information theory. The most common approach so far has been to investigate scaling laws for the so called transport capacity of the network as the number of communicating nodes become large. Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems have also emerged over the past decade as a revolutionary technology for obtaining unprecedented capacity growth. It is now well-known that for a single point-to-point communication link, the capacity of MIMO grows linearly with the number of antennas. In some exciting preliminary work, the Principal Investigator (PI) has shown that MIMO also provides significant advantages for wireless ad-hoc networks, and may be used to successfully overcome some of the key challenges imposed on the higher protocol layers by decentralized and uncoordinated network control. A critical open problem, however, is to determine how to best exploit the advantages of MIMO from an overall network perspective, and what MIMO transceiver algorithms should be employed to maximize performance. In this project, we seek to address these important open problems by developing a powerful new analytical framework for performance evaluation of a generic class of MIMO transmission techniques in decentralized wireless ad-hoc networks, taking into account important network features such as network spatial distributions, network level interference, medium access control, and multi-hop routes, in addition to fading, noise, and path loss effects. In contrast to most existing results, we do not aim to derive fundamental scaling laws, but rather to establish more precise results for practical transmission techniques by employing advanced tools from the powerful mathematical fields of stochastic geometry and random matrix theory. This framework will allow us to establish key insights into the fundamental diversity/multiplexing/interference-cancelation trade-off afforded by multiple antennas in a wireless ad-hoc network setting, and to investigate optimized MIMO transmission strategies which best exploit these degrees of freedom. By providing a fundamental investigation of the use of MIMO technology in wireless ad-hoc networks, the results in this project may play a key role in the design of future-generation wireless networking applications. 无线自组织网络为大量的实际应用提供了一项重要技术，这些应用包括环境监测，社区网状网络，军事战地网络，健康与应急无线电通信业务。在过去几年中，这项技术已经激发了大量的研究工作，旨在理解无线自组织网络的基本容量极限。解决这一重要问题非常具有挑战性，需要用到超越经典信息论领域的新型先进工具。目前为止，最常用的方法就是当网络节点数目变大时，研究所谓的网络传输容量的比例定律。 为获得前所未有的系统容量增长，多输入多输出系统作为一项革命性的技术在过去十年中应运而生。众所周知，对于单个点对点的通信链路，多输入多输出系统的容量随天线数目呈线性增长。在一些振奋人心的初步工作中，主要调查者经研究表明多输入多输出技术也有能力为无线自组织网络提供巨大优势，此技术可以成功克服由于分布式和非协调网络控制方式引发的更高协议层的关键技术难题。然而，目前仍存在一个关键性的公开难题：从整个网络角度考虑，如何最优利用多输入多输出技术优势；为获得最大性能输出，应利用何种多输入多输出系统的收发器算法。 在此项目中，通过开发一套对无线自组织网络中的多输入多输出传输技术进行性能评估的新型有力理论分析框架，我们旨在解决这些重要的却尚未解决的技术难题。此分析框架考虑了重要的网络特征，如网络空间分布，网络干扰，媒体访问控制和多跳路由，以及信道衰落，噪声和路径损耗效应。与多数现有结论相反，我们不以得出基本的比例定律为目标，而是通过运用随机几何和随机矩阵理论等先进有力的数学工具，为实际的传输技术确立更加精确的结果。在无线自组织网络中，分集接收/多路复用/干扰消除技术之间存在一个折衷，此分析框架将有助于我们得到关于这个折衷的关键见解，同时也有助于我们研究如何最优利用这些技术的自由度，使多输入多输出传输机制最有效。 通过提供在无线自组织网络中使用多输入多输出技术的基础研究，此项目的结果将会在下一代无线网络应用的设计中起到关键作用。

616910.label: Realisation of objectives
616910.value: The key objectives have been successfully met, as described below. Objective 1: This substantial objective was aimed at developing a novel analytical framework for characterizing the performance of general MIMO communication strategies under broad ad-hoc networking conditions. This was thoroughly addressed. In particular, [Journal Paper 1] considered a generalized ad-hoc network scenario with arbitrary linear filters at the transmitters and receivers, deriving, for the first time, exact analytical formulae for the network performance. This fundamental result was obtained by employing advanced tools from stochastic geometry and random matrix theory. [Journal Paper 2] and [Conference Paper 2] also provided a novel analytical framework for performance characterization, employing stochastic geometric techniques to derive exact performance measures for large-scale wireless ad-hoc networks considering pilot-based channel estimation effects. Objective 2: This objective aimed at employing the new performance analysis frameworks developed in Objective 1 to present a detailed analysis of existing wireless communication protocols under wide ranging networking conditions. First, the proposed framework in [Journal Paper 1] was employed to study a broad class of generalized MIMO techniques. Exact and asymptotic expressions were presented for the outage probability and network throughput, and a thorough performance evaluation and comparison was given, both analytically and through simulations, demonstrating the strengths and limitations of each MIMO approach. Second, the proposed framework in [Journal Paper 2] and [Conference Paper 2] was employed to characterize the effects of channel estimation and pilot-training lengths under a wide range of different communication scenarios. Various performance measures were studied, including the outage probability, network throughput and transmission capacity Objective 3: This objective aimed to build upon the performance analysis in Objective 2 to design new transmission technologies. In [Journal Paper 1], this was achieved by designing novel methods with optimized number of transmitted data streams, for various linear MIMO transmission methods. These optimized schemes were shown to yield substantially improved network capacities. In [Journal Paper 2] and [Conference Paper 2], novel optimized pilot-training techniques were presented under varying ad-hoc networking conditions, leading to substantially improved network throughput. Objective 4: This objective aimed to give a preliminary investigation into more involved networking configurations, including non-homogeneous networking scenarios. Such a preliminary study was conducted in [Conference Paper 1], considering a stochastic cellular networking scenario with user scheduling. Here, whilst an exact performance characterization seemed intractable, accurate approximations for system performance were provided, yielding key insight into network spectral efficiency and optimal pilot-training.

616910.label: Major findings and research outcome
616910.value: Below is a brief summary of the major findings in each of the journal and conference papers: [Journal Paper 1]: This paper presented a novel performance analysis framework for linear MIMO transmission techniques in general ad-hoc networking scenarios. The results were particularized to important practical transmission schemes including MIMO linear beamforming techniques, transmit antenna selection methods with zero-forcing receivers, and spatial multiplexing methods. A thorough performance evaluation and comparison was given, both analytically and through simulations, demonstrating the strengths and limitations of each approach. Importantly, this analysis also yielded key practical insight into the relative gain of channel feedback under different networking scenarios. In addition, fundamental performance scaling laws were derived, and these were used to design new signaling methodologies with adaptive stream selection. The novel transmission methods where shown to yield substantial performance gains. [Journal Paper 2] and [Conference Paper 2]: These papers provided a novel performance analysis framework which, for the first time, captured the practical effects of pilot-based channel estimation and imperfect CSI. This is a critical practical problem, but one which is extremely challenging, since both the pilot transmission and data transmission phases are subjected to strong multi-user interference, which must be carefully handled. Our novel analysis framework was employed to characterize the effects of channel estimation errors under ad-hoc networking conditions, and was subsequently utilized to design optimized training approaches. Various performance measures were studied, including the outage probability, network throughput and transmission capacity, both theoretically and through simulations, and key connections were made relative to classical single-user and interference-limited scenarios. Moreover, explicit conditions were presented, in terms of the pilot-training length and a target outage level, for which a positive transmission capacity (i.e., a network capacity measure) is achievable. These are fundamental system constraints which must be satisfied in order for a positive transmission rate to be achievable. Scaling laws were also derived, which provided key insight into the optimal training length, and led to new transmission designs with substantially-improved performance. [Conference Paper 1]: This paper considered a stochastic cellular networking scenario with user scheduling. This scheduling mechanism induced complexities in conducting performance evaluation. Here, whilst an exact performance characterization seemed intractable, accurate approximations for system performance were provided, which yielded insight into network spectral efficiency and optimal pilot-training methods.

616910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616910.value: There are numerous avenues for further development. In particular, the novel frameworks introduced in this project did not consider advanced interference cancellation technologies, which could substantially improve performance. In particular, non-linear MIMO transmission methods could be employed, including optimal maximum likelihood receivers. The analysis of such methods is more difficult than the methods considered in the current project, and a thorough study in this direction is likely to be a substantial effort which will be considered as the basis of a major follow-up project. Various other key extensions may also be considered, including more advanced communication setups employing multi-user transmission methods, relaying approaches, massive MIMO or mmWave technologies, advanced scheduling techniques, and so on.

616910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616910.value: Wireless ad-hoc networks are wireless communication technologies which operate without fixed infrastructure. Such networks have a plethora of applications, ranging from environmental monitoring, sensing and health care, through to emergency services. This project has provided an extensive theoretical study of wireless ad-hoc networks, characterizing the ultimate performance limits using concepts from communication theory, signal processing, and information theory. This has led to numerous key insights, and revealed the most appropriate communication structures to employ under various networking configurations (i.e., dense networks, sparse networks, etc). For example, it was revealed how to most appropriately employ multi-antenna technology, how to most effectively learn the communication channels under adverse network interference, and so on. In addition to providing a deep fundamental understanding of ad-hoc network performance limits, new optimized transmission strategies were discovered with impressive theoretical performance gains. Such methods pose attractive technologies for practical wireless network design. Theoretically, the tools introduced in this project are fundamental, and they could potentially be utilized for the design and analysis of many more advanced multi-antenna ad-hoc network communication scenarios.

617010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617010.value: Energy reuse and energy recycling has become an important factor to reduce global warming. The idea of using ambient energy to power up small electronic devices has been attracting a lot of attention in recent years. These energy-autonomous devices self-power themselves over a full lifetime by harvesting the energy coming from the surrounding environment. These devices are particular useful in some unique applications such as wireless remote field sensors which require continuous monitoring of objects in storage or in transit, implantable biomedical devices in which recharging of the batteries needs costly and risky surgery, rescuing devices which determine the locations of disaster survivors in the wilderness. There are basically four main ambient energy sources: solar energy, vibration energy, thermal energy and electromagnetic energy. These energy sources always fluctuate in nature and the power supplied by these energy harvesters also fluctuates and is of low power in nature. Therefore, a power converter is essential to regulate and manage the harvested energy. Current power management circuits consist of several analog building blocks such voltage reference, error amplifier, etc. consume quite a significant amount of power. This power consumption may be higher than the power obtained from the energy harvesting system. As a result, the energy harvesting system will not be able to sustain its own function except under strong ambient energy sources condition such as bright sunlight, extreme temperature difference or strong vibration. In order to have these energy-autonomous devices to be truly self-powered in all conditions, a low-power power management circuit must be developed. The objective of this proposal is to develop an ultra-low-power power management integrated circuit for energy-autonomous electronic device application. This includes the development of new control methods and new circuit topologies of the controller design with ultra-low-power performance. A new series of ultra-low-power analog circuits will also be developed for this application. The focus will be on how to minimize the power management IC such that the energy harvesting system can acquire energy efficiently in all ambient conditions. Other issues related to how to convert the energy from the harvester to a higher voltage for storage and how to control and deliver the energy to the energy-autonomous devices, etc. will also be explored in this project. 能源的重複利用和循環再生是降低全球氣候變暖的重要因素。近年來，採集環境能量爲小型電子設備供電的方法引起了廣泛的關注。這些能量自給設備僅需要採集周圍環境的能量作爲自己的能量來源，使得其在一些特殊的運用環境當中相當有用。例如，需要連續監測目標存儲或傳輸的無線遠程場感應器；電池替換需要高成本高風險手術的可植入生物晶片；為遇害人在荒野中定位的營救設備。目前主要有四種基本的環境能量來源：太陽能，振動能量，熱能和電磁能。然而在自然界中，這些能量來源極不穩定，波動嚴重。能量採集器採集這些能量來源，將提供波動嚴重的微弱電源，這使得用來調制和管理此電源的能量轉換器至關重要。目前，電源管理電路通常由幾個模擬模塊組成，例如電壓基准源和誤差放大器等，這些模塊消耗的能量甚至大于從環境中獲得的能量。因此，除非有足夠強的環境能量來源，例如強光，極大的溫差或強烈的振動等，否則採集系統將不能維持正常工作。爲了確保這些能量自給設備在所有的條件下都能夠實現能量自給，低功耗電源管理器件的研製必不可少。這個項目旨在爲能量自給電子設備研發一款超低功耗的電源管理集成電路。這包括研制新的控制器，用新的控制方法和新的電路結構以實現超低功耗。爲滿足此應用的要求，我們將會設計一系列超低功耗的模擬電路，以優化電源管理集成電路，使得能量採集系統能在不同的環境條件下面有效地獲取能量。除此之外，我們將進一步考察怎樣將採集到的能量轉換成一個更高的電壓以方便存儲，怎樣有效地控制採集到的能量並將其高效地傳遞到能量自給設備等問題。

617010.label: Realisation of objectives
617010.value: This project related to the development of ultra-low-power power management integrated circuit (PMIC) for energy-autonomous electronic device. In order to develop the PMIC for this application, there are four objectives as listed in the report. These objectives are mainly on developing ultra-low-power analogy building blocks to minimize the power consumption of the control circuitries, developing the controller for the booster circuit to step up the terminal voltage of the energy harvesting devices, developing the power regulator to regulate the voltage from the harvesting devices, and developing the PMIC for energy-autonomous electronic devices. All the objectives have been fully achieved. During the project, several building blocks such as voltage reference, current sensor, linear regulators, inductive-based and capacitive-based power converters have been developed, simulated, measured and characterized. Analytical studies and novel ideas on how to improve the performance of the PMIC building blocks have been published in journal and conference papers. In the final stage of the project, several complete PMICs for energy harvesting schemes have been developed. Some of them can achieve a self-startup voltage as low as 21mV with high internal resistance thermoelectric generator.

617010.label: Major findings and research outcome
617010.value: Many novel ideas and novel techniques have been developed in this project. Some of them have been used in the final design of the energy harvesting scheme for energy-autonomous electronic device. In terms of circuit design, several low-power building blocks have been developed in this project. A nano-watt voltage reference has been developed [Conference paper 3] which was used in our PMIC for energy-autonomous electronic device. A digital inductor current sensor has been developed [Journal paper 3] for sensing the inductor current of the inductive-based power converter. The digital approach has great advance of low power consumption over the analog current sensor. This will be very useful for future low-power energy harvesting circuit. Using package bondwire as the inductor of the inductive-based switching converter has been proposed [Journal paper 2 and Conference paper 4]. This has high potential to fully integrate the inductive-based switching converter on a single chip for future energy harvesting single chip solution. Several power converter topologies have been also studies and developed [Conference papers 1, 5]. In particular, the developed 3-state controlled transition mode switching converter can significantly improve the efficiency and lower the ripple voltage at the output of the buck-boost converter. Since the energy and voltage extracted from the energy harvesting devices vary with time, several low-dropout regulators (LDRs) have been developed [Journal paper 1 and Conference papers 2, 9] to regulate the output voltage with minimum output ripple voltage. Inductive-base switching power converters are usually used in PMIC when the voltage extracted from the energy harvesting devices is small. However, when the voltage extracted from the energy harvesting devices is large, e.g. when the solar cells under bright sunlight or a large temperature difference between the thermoelectric generators (TEGs), capacitive-type charge-pump circuit is preferred with higher overall efficiency. Two low-voltage charge-pump circuits have been developed in this project [Conference papers 6, 8] with improved efficiency over the previous approach. Finally, in terms of system design, several energy harvesting systems have been developed [Journal papers 4, 5 and Conference papers 7, 10-12] with different function such as dual mode control and bipolar output. Some of them can achieve a very low self-startup voltage of 21mV which is one of the lowest reported values.

617010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617010.value: In this project, several novel circuits and control schemes have been developed. In most of the designs, thermoelectric generators (TEGs) have been used as the energy harvesting device to verify the designs. TEG has advantages in terms of dimension in mm2 over other energy harvesters such as photovoltaic cell (PVC) and piezoelectric harvester (PEH) in low output power applications of below 100W. On the other hand, the developed techniques in this project can also be extended to PVC and PEH applications with some modifications. Also, although the developed techniques in this project are tailored for low-power applications, some of developed techniques can also be applied to medium to high-power applications.

617010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617010.value: This project related to the development of ultra-low-power power management integrated circuit (PMIC) for energy-autonomous electronic device. The main idea is how to harvest energy from the environment to power up the electronic device without extra battery. The important point is how to design PMIC to harvest energy in not a good enabling environment such as harvesting energy from solar cell in indoor lighting condition and harvesting energy from thermoelectric generator with only a few degrees of temperature difference. In these environment, the energy and voltage available from the harvesters is very small and below tens of W and hundreds of mV, respectively. Typical PMIC cannot harvest energy in this condition or having very low power conversion efficiency. This project has developed several novel circuit techniques and control schemes to improve the power conversion efficiency and the minimum startup voltage of the PMIC. Experimental results show that over 70% efficiency and as low as 21mV self-startup voltage can be achieved.

617410.value: 土及軟岩地基中正交穿越隧道間相互作用的三維離心機試驗研究

617410.label: Project Objectives
617410.value: To investigate and understand the three-dimensional stress transfer and deformation mechanisms of a newly constructed tunnel, which is perpendicularly crossing an existing tunnel in sand and clay. To assess the influence of different tunnelling sequences and alignment angles between tunnels. To study the influence of cover-to-diameter ratio and pillar depth-to-diameter ratio on the three-dimensional tunnel interactions. To provide high quality and comprehensive centrifuge test data for verifying numerical models and modelling procedures. To study and understand the mechanisms of tunnel interactions by carrying out three-dimensional finite element analyses. To develop design charts by carrying out centrifuge model tests and numerical parametric analyses. To provide improved design and construction guidelines for parallel and perpendicularly crossing twin tunnel constructions.

617410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617410.value: To sustain long-term development and growth, and to protect the environment from excessive emissions of carbon dioxide due to traffic jams, underground tunnelling has become the only viable construction technique for many urban cities worldwide such as Hong Kong, London, New York and Beijing. Tunnel construction will cause stress changes in the ground and hence induce ground movements. Uncontrollable ground movements may cause cracks in buildings, gas mains, or even collapse of nearby structures. As the number of tunnels increase, the distance between tunnels is inevitably reduced. Although a considerable amount of research has been carried out to improve and ensure the safe design of tunnels, three-dimensional twin tunnel interactions, between perpendicularly crossing tunnels in particular, and deformation mechanisms are still not fully understood. No systematic centrifuge model tests have been carried out to investigate the interaction effects of perpendicularly crossing twin tunnels in soft ground. In this proposed project, carefully designed three-dimensional centrifuge model tests will be carried out using the-state-of-the-art geotechnical centrifuge at HKUST and three-dimensional numerical simulations will be conducted to investigate and understand the interactions and deformation mechanisms between two perpendicularly crossing tunnels. Governing factors affecting multi-tunnel interaction such as different tunnel alignment angles, construction sequences, cover-to-diameter ratios and pillar depth-to-diameter ratios will be simulated and studied. It is expected to improve existing design guidelines and to develop new design charts. Research findings, design guides and charts developed from this project will certainly benefit the engineering profession directly and also will have major beneficial impacts to the environment and the economy worldwide. 為實現社會長期可持續發展，減小因為交通擁擠而導致的車輛尾氣過度排放對環境造成的不利影響，隧道開挖已經成為香港，倫敦，紐約和北京等世界範圍內許多城市唯一可行的選擇。隧道施工將不可避免的導致土層應力變化及變形。過度的土層變形可能導致建築物、地下管線的開裂，甚至鄰近結構的倒塌。隨著隧道數量的增加，隧道間的間距必然越來越小。雖然曾有學者為改進及保證隧道的設計安全進行了一些研究，但兩隧道間、特別是正交穿越隧道間的相互作用及變形機理目前仍不是十分清楚。在土及軟岩地基中，正交穿越隧道間的相互作用還缺乏系統的離心機試驗研究。 在本項目中，將利用香港科技大學先進的岩土工程離心機進行精心設計的離心機模型試驗，用於研究正交穿越隧道間相互作用以及變形機理。另外，三維數值模擬也將同步進行。本項目將對影響隧道間相互作用的主要因素，如穿越角度、施工順序、埋深與直徑的比例、以及隧道間距與直徑的比例等進行系統的類比研究，以改進現有設計準則和提供新的設計方法。本項目的研究成果、所研製的設計準則和設計方法無疑將可以直接使工程實踐受益，並對社會環境和經濟產生重大有利影響。
