617410.label: Major findings and research outcome
617410.value: A novel device, called “donut”, was developed to simulate both the effects of volume loss and weight loss due to three-dimensional advancement in-flight in centrifuge model tests (refer to the paper by Ng, Boonyarak & Mašín published in Canadian Geotechnical Journal as listed in Part C). This new device was subsequently adopted to investigate various vital actors influencing the interaction of crossing tunnel interactions, namely construction sequence, cover depth, pillar depth, and shielding effects by an existing tunnel. It is found that crossing-tunnel interaction is strongly influenced by the pillar depth-to-diameter ratio (P/D). In the excavation of a new tunnel underneath at P/D of 0.5, the maximum settlement, tensile strain and shear stress induced in the existing tunnel exceeded the permissible limits set in various design standards. For multiple crossing-tunnel interaction involving three tunnels, the settlement of the existing tunnel caused by the vertically stacked tunnel arrangement was smaller than that due to the side-by-side tunnel case. In addition, the shielding effects provided by the upper new tunnel minimized the effects of the new tunnel excavation on the existing tunnel. Regarding the effects of construction sequences of twin perpendicularly crossing tunnels, an existing tunnel was compressed vertically when a new tunnel was excavated underneath. On the contrary, the existing one was elongated vertically when the new tunnel advanced above it. This is because the reduction of stress acting on the existing tunnel in the horizontal direction was larger than that in the vertical direction when the new tunnel was constructed beneath. Details of the findings are reported by Boonyarak and Ng (2014) as listed in Part C. In collaboration with Tongji University, the long-term performance of two oldest metro lines (i.e., Lines 1 and 2) was investigated by element tests, numerical simulations and theoretical calculations. It is revealed that the observed large tunnel settlements in both tunnel lines were mainly caused by the compression of sandy Aquifer IV due to ground water pumping in Shanghai. The measured compression of sandy Aquifer IV accounted for about 65% and 75% of the maximum tunnel settlement of Lines 1 and 2, respectively. The continuing settlement of the tunnel over the 12.5 years of monitoring was the result of secondary compression (creep), which is a common feature of Aquifer IV at various locations in Shanghai. Details of the key findings are reported by Ng, Li & Liu (2011) and Ng, Liu & Li (2013).

617410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617410.value: There are three areas of research worth to be further developed: i.e., (i) the influence of tunnel shape, (ii) effects of joints and (iii) long-term effects on crossing-tunnel interaction. (i) Although considerable understanding has been gained by investigating the interaction between circular tunnels, many tunnels are not circular in reality. Tunnels constructed in rectangular, cart or horseshoe shapes may be more critical (dangerous) and complex when they are excavated nearby. A new GRF may be prepared to carry out the study. (ii) For simplicity, the existing model tunnel used in this project was a continuous pipe without joints. In reality, tunnel linings often have both radial and circumferential joints, which will affect the stiffness of tunnel and opening of joints. To date, no physical model test has been carried out to investigate crossing-tunnel interaction with the presence of joints. For safe design of closely spaced multi-tunnels, it is vital to improve our understanding of the effects of joints on the interaction of crossing tunnels. (iii). For crossing-tunnel interaction in clay, the time dependent behavior of soil that affects the existing tunnel is a factor that is still not fully understood. Due to tunnel excavation, the effects of stress relief and shearing can lead to different excessive pore water pressures in soft and stiff clays, leading to the deformations of clay and tunnel. Thus, long-term behavior of crossing-tunnel interaction should be investigated.

617410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617410.value: A novel device, called “donut”, has been developed to simulate both the effects of volume loss and weight loss due to three-dimensional advancement in-flight in centrifuge model tests. With this new innovative device, a comprehensive and systematic series of centrifuge model tests were carried out to investigate the deformation mechanisms and the interaction effects of perpendicularly crossing twin tunnels. In additional, three-dimensional numerical simulations using a state-of-the-art soil constitutive model have been conducted to improve our understanding the centrifuge model tests and to carry out parametric analyses for the development of calculation charts. Governing factors affecting multi-tunnel interaction such as different construction sequences, cover-to-diameter ratios and pillar depth-to-diameter ratios have been examined. Results from the analyses provide guidelines for engineering designs. Research findings from this project have been disseminated in various international journals and conferences such as those held in Bangkok, Hong Kong, Rome and Perth. These findings will certainly benefit the engineering profession directly and also will have major beneficial impacts to the environment and the economy worldwide.

617610.label: Project Title(Chinese)
617610.value: 供應鏈管理中基於RFID數據查詢及挖掘的標籤移動分析

617610.label: Project Objectives
617610.value: Develop Cleaning Methods and Repairing Mechanisms to Preprocess Multi-Stream Raw RFID Data We plan to develop tactics to clean RFID data in two levels. Physical cleaning is imposed on RFID data streams, in which we remove physical noises on the raw data arising from signal errors. Logical cleaning is imposed at the database level to remove multiple, missing or incorrect data values. We aim to eliminate and repair most of the physical noises and logical noises. For physical noise, we will study a voting method on RFID data streams that are obtained from different smoothing window sizes to eliminate false positive and false negative errors. For logical noise, we will develop inference rules to repair errors and a compression scheme in order to remove data redundancies. Devise an RFID Database Model and Implement an Efficient Storage Scheme We plan to design an RFID database model and implement a scalable storage system for an RFID dataset which supports querying and mining. The RFID database model provides a blueprint to use a relational DBMS to store higher levels of RFID data such as trace records, stay records and other logistic information. We also study various encoding techniques to store the essential information of the SCM system. We will implement the architecture that collects raw RFID data that are pre-processed by the cleaning methods and repair mechanisms. The architecture provides a platform for querying, transforming and carrying out experimentation and demonstration. Develop RFID Manipulation Languages and their Processing Techniques We plan to develop and support various classes of RFID queries such as tracking queries, path-oriented queries, containment queries and many others. To support processing of different classes of queries, we will develop efficient coding and decoding schemes for handling the path information of cleansed RFID datasets. In addition, we will also develop a query template over the storage architecture to translate the RFID language expressions into their corresponding SQL statements executed by the underlying database system. Capture Frequent Tag Movement Trails in Tag Movement Graph We will first establish a graph-theoretic data mining model (TMG) to capture RFID tag movement information. Within the model, we will study various data mining techniques to explore the graph and discover important tag movement trails. We will establish threshold criteria in various abstraction levels such as time duration and location transition. We will carry out experiments on various issues related to the efficiency of the proposed algorithms and effectiveness of the output trails. Discover Logistic Correlated Patterns on Tag Movement Graph and RFID Databases We plan to apply correlation mining techniques on the TMG graph and the RFID database in order to discover some interesting underlying dependencies between the parameters in product flows. We will study the notion of logistic correlated patterns that are able to reveal the underlying dependencies related to logistic attributes and trails. The challenges in discovering logistic correlated patterns are significant due to the fact that the search space involving quantitative and multi-level attributes is often huge. To reduce search space, we will study effective correlation measures to derive bounds of the support of candidate patterns. Build a prototype for Industrial Demonstration and Other Applications We plan to obtain user feedback from industrials. We will build up a simple prototype that demonstrates our querying and mining techniques to our RFID industrial partners that involve SCM businesses. In addition to SCM settings, the prototype can also be adapted to analyze people flow in large exhibition events in general. We will search for opportunities in our university campus such as conference exhibitions and information day for high school students.

In addition, we will also develop a query template over the storage architecture to translate the RFID language expressions into their corresponding SQL statements executed by the underlying database system.

Capture Frequent Tag Movement Trails in Tag Movement Graph We will first establish a graph-theoretic data mining model (TMG) to capture RFID tag movement information. Within the model, we will study various data mining techniques to explore the graph and discover important tag movement trails. We will establish threshold criteria in various abstraction levels such as time duration and location transition. We will carry out experiments on various issues related to the efficiency of the proposed algorithms and effectiveness of the output trails.

Discover Logistic Correlated Patterns on Tag Movement Graph and RFID Databases We plan to apply correlation mining techniques on the TMG graph and the RFID database in order to discover some interesting underlying dependencies between the parameters in product flows. We will study the notion of logistic correlated patterns that are able to reveal the underlying dependencies related to logistic attributes and trails. The challenges in discovering logistic correlated patterns are significant due to the fact that the search space involving quantitative and multi-level attributes is often huge. To reduce search space, we will study effective correlation measures to derive bounds of the support of candidate patterns.

Build a prototype for Industrial Demonstration and Other Applications We plan to obtain user feedback from industrials. We will build up a simple prototype that demonstrates our querying and mining techniques to our RFID industrial partners that involve SCM businesses. In addition to SCM settings, the prototype can also be adapted to analyze people flow in large exhibition events in general. We will search for opportunities in our university campus such as conference exhibitions and information day for high school students.

617610.label: Major findings and research outcome
617610.value: We followed well the objectives defined in the project and the major outcomes related to managing RFID data and, in a more general context, discovering sequential patterns in uncertain data as follows: First, we contributed in developing RFID database models and applied a model-based approach for RFID data stream cleansing as reported in ER2011 and CIKM2012 papers. As RFID data is inherently noisy and are subject to many interference in practice, we contributed in a more general context of (i) mining frequent sequential patterns in large uncertain databases and (ii) finding convex hull over uncertain databases. The above work contributed in algorithmic advancement as well as querying and mining on uncertain data in TKDE2013 and TKDE2014. In particular, Sec7.4 of TKDE2013 paper details a case study of RFID trajectory mining and illustrates the application of our mining algorithms that are able to find probabilistically frequent sequential patterns in an efficient manner. In an RFID indoor positioning and tracking system, RFID readers were deployed at fixed indoor positions. Specifically, if an object moves close to a reader, it is detected by the reader and the system decides that the object is at the location near the reader. However, since the detection range of RFID readers changes continuously with environment factors, the object may also be detected by another reader a little bit farther away, causing location uncertainty. We tackled this problem in a more general context and formulated the problem as finding probabilistic convex hull. Intuitively, the convex hull of a set of two-dimensional points P is the minimal convex polygon that contains all the points in P. We contributed algorithmic advancement and new processing techniques. We illustrated that the approach is efficient as reported in TKDE2014 paper. In order to support RFID applications that involve large flow of queries and require fast response, we made good progress and developed an efficient algorithm to find a high-quality near-optimal meeting point (OMP), which is orders of magnitude faster than the exact OMP algorithms. The project gives inspiration of the development of efficient algorithms for finding OMP on road networks in VLDB2011 paper. In studying the storage schema for supporting RFID tracking, we also contributed fundamental but novel techniques of locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) scheme, which is related to tracking beyond 2D case of RFID object movement. LSH and its variants are well-known methods for solving the c-approximate NN search problem in high-dimensional space.

617610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617610.value: A big challenge of this project is that the read rate for RFID data in the real-world is often in the range of 60-70%, which means over one third of data are missing. This poses a great challenge for mobile data cleansing because sometime; there is no observation of tracking objects in a reader network. We will continue to study the problem of RFID tracking in more dynamic environments with large missing rate via missing value estimation. The intuition for coping with the data missing issue is to make use of historic data of tracking objects. Historic observations are able to provide some evidence to assist the location inference under current timestamp. We will also consider the problem of RFID tracking from the viewpoint of missing value estimation. Given a three order tensor with dimensions on tagged objects, timestamp and location; we could estimate the location of the tagged objects at certain timestamp. Since the locations for tagged objects at certain timestamp are unknown due to the missing data, we could complete the missing entries in the tensor. We may consider that the Bayesian model of the movement as the posterior prior for completing the missing entries in the tensor.

617610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617610.value: RFID (Radio Frequency IDentification) technologies have been widely applied in areas such supply chain and warehouse management owing to its low cost. This project provides effective data analysis of raw datasets obtained from different RFID collection points managed by supply chains. We have achieved this goal successfully by establishing a framework that supports and advances a spectrum of new techniques on uncertain data processed in more general networks. First, we contributed repair mechanisms to preprocess raw RFID data from readers that can generate different kinds of errors such as multiple-reading, miss-reading or incorrect-reading. Second, we established a network model that captures the moving information of tagged objects. We have also developed means to mine frequent tag movement trails and logistic correlated patterns. In a nut shell, frequent tag movement trails are the trace records that are important in SCM and logistic correlated patterns are those relevant tags, temporal attributes and locations that reveal their non-trivial underlying dependencies in SCM. We demonstrated the applicability of our framework by studying real-life RFID datasets. The results are useful in supporting SCM business activities. The work also demonstrates some useful applications of the fundamental research work on mining and path-based querying in sequence databases.

617710.label: Project Objectives
617710.value: Comprehensive understanding of chip error characteristics in IEEE 802.15.4. In the IEEE 802.15.4 protocol, every 4-bit symbol is encoded into a sequence of 32 chips that are actually transmitted over the air. The 32 chips as a whole is also called a pseudo-noise code (PN-Code). Due to complex channel conditions, the transmitted PN-Code will often be received with some PN-Code chips corrupted. In this task, we will conduct a systematical study on these errors occurring at chip-level in different environments. The chip error information will be used to distinguish different channel conditions, such as attenuation, interference, multi-path, and mobility. Achieve simultaneous communications over interference. In traditional wireless communication schemes, a receiver can only receive packets from one single transmitter at a time. This is the main limitation for most algorithm designs and protocol implementations as a receiver in receiving can be considered as “blind”. In this task, we will investigate how to enable simultaneous communications over interference, taking the redundancy in the high redundant coding scheme as an advantage. We will use various kinds of artificial interference to generate different chip error patterns, by which information can be inserted into an existing link. Improve localization. Localization is fundamental for many applications and one widely applied technique is to use RSSI to conduct the localization. However, the RSSI value is not monotonous with the distance. Multipath effect and interference are two major reasons. In existing works, no interference is taken into account which can affect the results significantly. In real situations, however, multipath and interference is unavoidable and is everywhere. In such cases, the RSSI values for localization may be unreliable. How to get the reliable RSSI values for localization will be a challenge. In this part of the work, we aim to improve the accuracy of localization by solving this problem. Build an interference map to improve network throughput. In wireless networks, interference is a challenging issue. This is especially serious in densely deployed networks, in which interference is unavoidable and must be taken into consideration. Most existing works use packet-level metrics like RSSI to build the interference model, which cannot capture the changes of environment in the packet. Moreover, their models need to be trained when the environment changes. Hence, we aim to build an interference map based on the chip error information. In this map, we will quantify the interference level and its frequency which can reflect the interference effect clearly in real time. In addition, our interference map will be more accurate and adaptive to environmental conditions. After getting this information, we will design an effective algorithm to adjust transmission power or bit-rate to improve the throughput of the whole network.

617710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617710.value: Unlike its wired counterpart, a wireless link is easily affected by environment changes and surrounding wireless activities. Determining the instant link conditions (or qualities) is essential for most protocol designs and application developments in wireless communications. In previous studies, link-level metrics are utilized to reflect the link conditions such as Received Signal Strength Indication (RSSI), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and Signal-to-Interference plus Noise-Ratio (SINR). In practice, however, these metrics exhibit many limitations and could be misleading. They are often the statistic measurements over the packet transmission, however, the link conditions may vary dramatically and the packet-level metrics are unable to indicate the instant link condition. Motivated by this, in this research project we propose to use more fine-grained information from the lower layer of the network protocol stack. A chip is an accessible element at the physical layer for many wireless standards such as IEEE 802.15.4 and 802.11b. In these standards, information bits are repackaged as certain sequences of chips before being transmitted over the air. As the chip duration is much shorter, it is more capable of capturing instant channel changes. Analyzing the chip-level error characteristics brings a new measure for the upper-layer network design such as network diagnosis, transmission power control, routing, localization and topology control. To achieve these goals, we will accomplish four critical tasks in this research project. We will first investigate the fundamental characteristics of chip errors, focusing on identifying the different channel conditions at real time in low overhead. For the second task, we will examine the method to allow multiple simultaneous transmissions to a single receiver over interference by using the chip error characteristics, which is impossible by current technologies. For the third task, we will use this chip error information to improve the accuracy of localization. Finally, we will derive the interference map to improve the throughput of the whole network over the existing techniques. 與有線連接有所不同，無線信道很容易受到環境變換和周圍無線活動的影響。確定實時的鏈路狀況（或質量）是無線通信中大部分的拓扑設計和應用所必需的。 在以前的研究中，鏈路層的參數被用來反映鏈路的狀況，例如：接收信號強度，信噪比，信號與干擾及噪音比。然而在實際中，這些參數有著許多的限制並且具有誤導性。 他們一般通過對數據包傳輸過程的靜態測量得到，然而，鏈路的狀況可能變化地非常劇烈同時數據包一層的參數不能反映出實時的鏈路狀況。受到以上的啟發，我們打算在這個研究計劃中利用更細致的來自網絡底層的信息。碼片是許多無線標准中物理層的一個組成單元，例如在IEEE 802.15.4和802.11b中。在這些標准下，信息比特被包裝成碼片流然后傳輸到空氣中。因為碼片的周期非常短，我們相信通過其可以探測出實時的信道變化情況。通過分析碼片層的錯誤信息，給我們帶來了對上層網絡設計，例如：網絡診斷，傳輸能量控制，路由，定位和拓扑控制等的新測量方式。為了達到上述目的，我們首先對碼片錯誤信息的基本性質進行研究，著重在實時，低功耗的分辨出不同的信道狀況。第二個任務我們打算利用碼片錯誤信息，通過干擾來使得一個接收器可以同時接收多個同時傳輸，這是現有的技術所做不到的。第三個任務我們計劃利用碼片錯誤信息來提高定位的精度。最后，我們打算建立一個新的干擾模型來提高整個網絡的吞吐量。

617710.label: Realisation of objectives
617710.value: The objective of this project is to use chip error information to enhance the wireless network performance. It includes four tasks. For task 1, we investigated the fundamental characteristics of chip errors. Wireless links are easily affected by complex channel conditions such as attenuation and interference, where the transmitted PN-Code in the physical layer will often be received with some PN Code chips corrupted. In this work, we conducted a systematic analysis on these errors occurring at chip-level. We found that there are notable error patterns corresponding to different cases. For task 2, we proposed a new communication paradigm which leverages the chip error information. In a typical multi-user environment, coordination among different users is a necessity to avoid severe mutual interference and well utilize the shared medium. Such coordination costs precious communication resource, and leads to a significantly degraded network performance. In this work, we used chip error information that obtained from the lower layer of the network protocol stack to build an extra, free coordination channel. The throughput can be improved up to 250%. For task 3, we used the channel state information which is a fine-grained informaion from physical layer instead of RSSI to improved the indoor localization. We explore the frequency diversity of the subcarriers in OFDM systems and propose a novel approach called FILA, which leverages the channel state information to alleviate multipath effect. We implemented the FILA system on commercial 802.11 NICs, and then evaluated its performance in different typical indoor scenarios. The experimental results showed that the accuracy and latency of distance calculation can be significantly enhanced by using CSI. Moreover, FILA can significantly improve the localization accuracy compared with the corresponding RSSI approach. For task 4, we observed that In RFID systems, the tag randomly selects a slot to send a Random Number (RN) packet to contend for identification. Collision happens when multiple tags select the same slot, which makes the RN packet undecodable. In this task, we redesigned the RN pattern to make the collided RNs decodable. By leveraging the collision slots, the system performance can be dramatically enhanced. This novel scheme is called DDC, which is able to directly decode the collisions without exact knowledge of collided RNs. We implement DDC in GNU Radio and USRP2 based testbed to verify its feasibility. Both theoretical analysis and testbed experiment showed that DDC achieves 40 percent tag read rate gain compared with traditional RFID protocol.

617710.label: Major findings and research outcome
617710.value: In the course of this project, we have published 9 refereed conference papers, including one in ACM MobiCom, and four in IEEE Infocom. We also published 7 IEEE Transaction papers, including 2 IEEE TMC and 5 IEEE TPDS. For achieving simultaneous communications over interference, we designed and implemented an extra coordination free channel. To realize the idea, we proposed a new communication paradigm which leverages the chip error information. It is known that coordination among multiple nodes is a costly operation taking a significant amount of valuable communication resource. In this project, we have an interesting observation that by generating intended patterns, some simultaneous transmissions, i.e., “interference,” can be successfully decoded without degrading the effective throughput in original transmission. As such, an extra and “free” coordination channel can be built. Based on this idea, we propose a DC-MAC to leverage this “free” channel for efficient medium access in a multiple-user wireless network. We theoretically analyze the capacity of this channel under different environments with various modulation schemes. USRP2-based implementation experiments show that compared with the widely adopted CSMA, DC-MAC can improve the channel utilization efficiency by up to 250 percent. For indoor localization, we analyzed multipath effect across the physical layer and account for the undesirable RSSI readings being reported. We explored the frequency diversity of the subcarriers in OFDM systems and propose a novel approach called FILA, which leverages the channel state information (CSI) to alleviate multipath effect at the receiver. We implement the FILA system on commercial 802.11 NICs, and then evaluate its performance in different typical indoor scenarios. The experimental results show that the accuracy and latency of distance calculation can be significantly enhanced by using CSI. Moreover, FILA can significantly improve the localization accuracy compared with the corresponding RSSI approach.

617710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617710.value: Unlike the wired counterpart, a wireless link is easily affected by environment changes and surrounding wireless activities. Determining the instant link conditions (or qualities) is essential for most protocol designs and application developments in wireless communications. In previous studies, link-level metrics are utilized to reflect the link conditions such as Received Signal Strength Indication, Signal-to-Noise Ratio and et.al. In practice, however, these metrics exhibit many limitations and could be misleading. As they are often the statistic measurements over the packet transmission while the link conditions may vary dramatically, the packet-level metrics are unable to indicate the instant link condition. Motivated by this, in this research project we propose to use more fine-grained information from the lower layer of the network protocol stack to improve the wireless network performance. A chip is an accessible element at the physical layer for many wireless standards such as IEEE 802.15.4 and 802.11b. In these standards, information bits are repackaged as certain sequences of chips before being transmitted over the air. As the chip duration is much shorter, it is more capable to capture the instant channel changes.

617810.label: Project Objectives
617810.value: Development of the unified mathematical framework based on VI theory: obtain sufficient conditions guaranteeing the existence/uniqueness of the solution and devise distributed algorithms that are valid for arbitrary payoff functions and strategy sets of the players. Application of the VI framework to multi-antenna multicast cellular systems: formulate a system with several competing multi-antenna base stations, each emitting a different “program” to a number of users within the framework of nondifferentiable VI, and find optimal beamforming strategies. Application of the VI framework to multi-portfolio optimization: formulate the multi-portfolio optimization as Nash equilibrium problems within the framework of VI to characterize the solution together with algorithms. Elaboration of a monograph with VI framework and applications: as a final step, prepare a monograph on the developed framework based on VI and its applications in signal processing, wireless communication systems, networking problems, multicast cellular systems, and financial engineering.

617810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617810.value: The use of convex optimization is ubiquitous in communications and signal processing in the design of single-user and multiuser systems with efficient practical algorithms. Other systems require a different formulation based on the so-called complementary problems. Yet, many other communications and networking problems composed of multiple agents with individual interests are better formulated within the realm of game theory, which is a field of applied mathematics that describes and analyzes scenarios with interactive decisions. Roughly speaking, a game can be represented as a set of coupled optimization problems. Nevertheless, the mathematical tools offered by convex optimization theory, complementary problems, and classical game theory may not be satisfactory to properly study general Nash Equilibrium problems with arbitrary objective functions and strategy sets and to devise distributed algorithms along with their convergence properties. A more general framework suitable for investigating and solving various optimization problems and equilibrium models even when classical game theory may fail, is known to be the Variation Inequality (VI) problem that constitutes a very general class of problems in nonlinear analysis and has been developed in the operation research literature. VI theory is very promising, but so far it has not been properly exploited in practical applications arising in engineering. There is only a handful of papers in the signal processing and wireless communication communities that use VI to solve practical problems. The few existing applications of VI theory in signal processing and communitations are just the tip of the iceberg and it is precisely the aim of this proposal to take VI a step further. In particular, the aim is twofold: 1) to provide a unified framework based on VI theory (for solving arbitrary equilibrium problems with distributed algorithms), and 2) to apply such a framework to an array of different applications in the areas of signal processing, communications, networking, and even finance engineering. 在通信与信号处理领域，凸优化理论及其算法被普遍的应用于设计单用户与多用户系统。还有一些系统能够被抽象阐述成为互补问题。另外，在一个拥有各自利益的多代理通信系统中，需要用博弈论研究其中的问题。博弈论是应用数学的一个分支，是一种处理竞争与合作问题的决策方法。从数学角度讲，一场博弈实际上能被抽象表示为一系列互相耦合的优化问题。 然而，无论是凸优化，互补问题理论，抑或博弈论，都无法很好的研究一般意义上的纳什均衡问题——即拥有任意目标函数与策略集的问题。同时，它们也无法给出收敛性良好的分布式算法。 而变分不等式提供了一个全新的理论体系，它所研究的是一类广泛的非线性问题，能处理传统博弈论无法解决的多种优化问题和均衡模型。在运筹学领域，该理论已被发展起来。 尽管变分不等式理论前景诱人，但在目前的工业界，它并没有被合适发掘与利用。在通信与信号处理领域，变分不等式理论的应用仍相当少，只有少数论文将其应用在解决实际问题中，但这些应用可谓冰山一角。我们这一提案的目的，正是要使变分不等式理论得以更多发展和应用。具体来说，分为两方面：1）提供基于变分不等式的统一的理论体系，使其能解决任意均衡问题并给出分布式算法； 2）将此理论广泛应用于信号处理，通信，网络，甚至金融工程中。

617810.label: Realisation of objectives
617810.value: The main two goals of this project were i) to further develop the theoretical and algorithmic framework of Variational Inequalities, and ii) to apply the framework in different specific applications. Both objectives have been satisfactorily completed and the output consists of seven IEEE journal papers and seven conference papers. Objective 1 was focused on the further development of the framework of Variational Inequalities, both the theory in the sense of characterizing the existence and uniqueness of the solutions as well as in the practice by developing useful algorithms. Several of the papers have completely embraced this objective by developing a complete theory of real and complex monotone communication games, decomposition by partial linearisation, and a universal semidefinite relaxation methodology. Objectives 2 and 3 were on the applications of the Variational Inequality framework. Indeed we have considered several diverse applications ranging from multi-portfolio optimisation, to lifetime maximization in wireless systems, optimization of the electrical smart grid, multiuser communication systems, and maximum likelihood detection. Objective 4 has been accomplished mainly by one of the papers published in IEEE Transactions on Information Theory of 35 dense double-column pages. This paper contains a holistic view and development of the mathematical framework with several applications. It took us several years to complete and we hope to write a more tutorial-like monograph so that the material is more accessible to a wider audience.

617810.label: Major findings and research outcome
617810.value: The major findings of this project are i) the further development of this framework of Variational Inequalities and ii) the application of the framework to different and diverse problems. The framework has been developed in several papers. We have derived conditions simple to check that guarantee existence and even uniqueness of the solution. In addition, we have also considerably advanced the practical aspect, i.e., the development of a family of practical algorithms that can be used in many diverse applications. These algorithms are guaranteed to converge to a solution, are simple to implement, and are naturally distributed methods with low complexity. In a nutshell, we have obtained the best known analytical results and practical methods for many problems of interest in the literature. Regarding the applications of the framework, we have extensibly considered a wide range of applications. One example is multi-portfolio optimization in financial engineering, which can be modeled as a competitive scenario where different clients compete and affect each other. Another example is the optimization of the lifetime of wireless sensor networks that have very limited battery life. An emerging application that we have considerably studied in several papers is the optimization of the electrical smart grid that will become the future in which clients not only can consume electricity but also store and produce it. Of course, more mainstream applications include the optimization of advanced multiuser wireless systems like cognitive radio systems. One last application is on the optimization of the detection process of the information bits transmitted through a multi-antenna wireless communication system. To summarize, I think the objectives have been well achieved and the research outcome has been superb with seven IEEE journal papers and seven conference papers.

617810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617810.value: As mentioned before, we recently published a long IEEE Transactions on Information Theory of 35 dense double-column pages. This paper contains a holistic view and development of the mathematical framework with several applications, but it is extremely dense mathematically. We hope to be able to write a more tutorial-like monograph to make it more accessible to the wider audience.

617810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617810.value: Modern engineering systems rely at the core of their design on some optimization procedure that can make the best out of the existing resources and subject to given constraints. The traditional convex optimization techniques have been very successfully applied during the past two decades. Nevertheless, some of the more advanced and sophisticated systems require a more elaborated formulation of the design that cannot be properly embraced by the traditional convex optimization framework. We have championed the introduction in the signal processing community of a more powerful mathematical framework from operations research called Variational Inequality that has a great potential and has not been exploited yet. Nevertheless, the application of such an existing framework is not direct and we have had to further develop both the theory and the algorithms to make it attractive to the signal processing community. In addition, we have applied the framework to a variety of engineering problems in diverse areas like financial engineering, wireless modern communication systems, the electrical smart grid, etc. We hope other researchers will take over this methodology and apply it to other applications.

617810.value: Thanks to this project, I have supported the training of a PhD student (Yang Yang) and a postdoc (Francisco Rubio). 618010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618010.value: Recent advances in integrated photonics and microfluidics technology have stimulated significant research interests in integrating micro- / nano-scale optical components in microfluidics for optical sensing. Such optofluidic chips offer potentially sensitive, portable, disposable and low-cost sensors that can find applications in chemical/biology sensing. This proposal examines the principle of optical sensing of effective refractive index change using inter-state transition-based pixelized spatial detection in an integrated coupled-microresonator array sensor. The array structure supports periodic transmission bands of the split modes (states) from the coupled microresonators. Each state within the band exhibits a unique spatial field intensity pattern. Thus, upon an effective refractive index change that corresponds to a transition between the states, the array spatial field intensity pattern at a fixed probe wavelength can discretely vary. We propose the optical detection to be in the spatial domain at a single visible-near-infrared (vis-NIR) laser wavelength using a charge-coupled device (CCD) camera. We will detect and integrate the out-of-plane light scattering from each of the coupled microresonators as a pixel. We expect that such pixelized detection enables sufficient details of the array spatial field intensity distribution for digital sensing of the effective refractive index change at a single wavelength while imposing relatively low-spatial-resolution imaging. This is in contrast with the conventional approach of optical sensing in the spectral domain based on sharp resonance wavelength shifts in an integrated microresonator sensor using high-resolution laser wavelength scanning. We will realize the coupled-microresonator array sensors in silicon nitride (SiN) substrates. The SiN thin film deposition and photonic device fabrication are compatible to the conventional silicon microelectronics fabrication processes, thus making the technology potentially mass producible and low-cost. SiN is essentially transparent to vis-NIR wavelengths, enabling the use of silicon CCD camera for imaging-based detection. This is again in contrast with many existing sensor work in the field using silicon-on-insulator technology with 1550-nm telecommunications wavelengths. We will image the out-of-plane light scattering of the array onto a CCD camera. The microfluidic channels in photoresists (e.g. SU-8) will be lithographically patterned on top of the thin silicon nitride photonic layer. We will also aim to develop the proposed sensor as a portable system with disposable optofluidic chips. 近年來，集成光子學和微流體技術的迅速發展，激發了研究集成微米、納米量級的光學器件與微流體學光學傳感器的興趣。 這種微流體光學傳感器具有高靈敏度，便攜，無污染，低成本等優點，在化學和生物學領域有廣泛的應用。 此課題提出了基於模間轉換的像素化空間檢測有效折射率的傳感原理。 傳感芯片由集成的耦合微諧振腔陣列組成。 耦合諧振腔的陣列結構支持了傳輸帶寬內許多分立的模式（態）。 當輸入光波長處於能帶中的任何一個態時，諧振腔中的光場強度展現出獨特的空間分佈模式。 因此，當有效折射率變化引起了態之間的轉換時，在固定波長探測光激發下，陣列傳感器的空間光強分佈也會發生顯著的改變。 我們計劃使用單一波長的可見和紅外波段的激光，以及電荷耦合器件（CCD）相機實現空間探測光學傳感。 從耦合陣列的每一個單元（微諧振腔）散射到外部空間的光被積分、探測為一個像素值。 我們期待這種單一波長、低空間分辨率、像素化的檢測方法能提供充足的空間光場強度分佈信息，用於數字化的傳感有效折射率的改變。 這種新型傳感器的探測原理和結構設計都不同於傳統的（應用高分辨率的可調諧激光器，掃描有效折射率變化引起的諧振峰位置移動）光學微諧振腔傳感器。 我們將在氮化硅基底上構建耦合微諧振腔陣列傳感器。 傳統的硅基微電子加工工藝適用於氮化硅材料的薄膜沉積和光子器件加工。 這為大規模、底成本的生產這種傳感器件提供了潛在的可能性。 氮化硅在可見光和近紅外波段有很高的透射率， 所以硅材料的CCD相機可以應用與此類傳感器。 與此相比，現有的基於絕緣層上硅材料的光學傳感器，大多工作在1550nm的通信波段。 CCD相機對微諧振腔陣列的空間散射光成像。 氮化硅光子器件層上將光刻集成光阻材料（SU-8）的微流體通道。 我們的長期的目標是開發出便攜的光子微流體集成傳感器系統。

618010.label: Realisation of objectives
618010.value: We have successfully realized Objective 1 as per original application. We have systematically investigated the proposed coupled-resonator optical waveguide (CROW) based refractive index (RI) sensors using pixelized spatial detection, both theoretically and experimentally. Specifically, we have designed, modeled, fabricated and characterized CROW-based RI sensors on two silicon-based platforms, including (i) silicon nitride (SiN)-on-silica platform for visible to near-infrared (NIR) light imaging as originally proposed, and (ii) silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform for infrared light (1550 nm) imaging. Instead of limiting our study to only inter-state transitions, we have significantly extended the original proposed sensing principle to using intra-state transitions in our earlier modeling work, and to using a novel correlation method comparing the perturbed pixelized pattern with the characteristic pixelized patterns in our latest approach. The result is a continuous improvement of the CROW-based RI sensing sensitivity from a low sensitivity of 10^-2 refractive index unit (RIU) using inter-state transitions only, to a 10^-3 RIU using intra-state transitions, and to a noise-equivalent level of 10^-5 RIU using correlation analysis. However, we have under-achieved Objective 2, which aims at integrating the SiN-based CROW sensor chip with microfluidic channels, micro-optics for optical interfacing and a silicon CCD camera. Thus far, we have integrated a thin-film polymer (PDMS) based microfluidic channel by bonding on the SOI sensor chip (with a footprint of 10 × 7 mm). Using such a hybrid silicon optofluidic chip, we have successfully injected NaCl solutions of different concentrations (thus of different refractive indices) into the CROW sensors for sensing at a precision of 10^-4 RIU (0.08% concentration by weight). We have yet successfully reproduced such a polymer-bonding process on the SiN CROW sensor chip, which typically has a smaller footprint of 10 × 2.5 mm due to the typically larger SiN waveguide propagation loss in the visible wavelengths than SOI waveguides in the 1550nm wavelengths. We are now making further attempts to bond the polymer-based microfluidic channel onto smaller-sized SiN chips, and also attempting to increase the SiN chip size by trading-off part of the light scattering power available for imaging. We do not consider the above as a fundamental limitation and they can be solved after repeated trials and errors. We believe as soon as the optofluidic chips on SiN substrates can be demonstrated, the rest of the micro-optics and camera integration should be more readily followed.

618010.label: Major findings and research outcome
618010.value: 1. We have theoretically modeled and analyzed CROW-based RI sensors assuming Fabry-Perot (FP) cavities and using transfer-matrix modeling and finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations. Our modeled FP-based CROWs revealed that the mode-field distributions vary upon a RI change at a single wavelength. The corresponding spatial Fourier transform of the CROW mode-field distributions, with each coupled cavity internal-field intensity integrated as a pixel, suggested a shift of the spatial frequency peak. Our modeled 21-element FP-based CROW sensor suggested a theoretical detection limit of 10^−4 RIU. Our FDTD simulations of an 11-element microring-based CROW sensor suggested a sensitivity that is consistent with the FP-based CROW modeling. (Publication 1, Part C) 2. We have designed, modeled, fabricated and characterized CROW-based sensors comprising up to 11-element gaplessly coupled microdisk cavities on the SiN-on-silica platform. The sensors showed strong light scattering signals in the infrared 1550nm wavelengths in the coupling regions between microdisks. Our early experiments revealed wavelength-dependent pixelized mode-field intensity patterns as observed in the light scattering in the far field. (Conference 2, Part C) 3. We have designed, modeled, fabricated and characterized silicon microring CROW-based sensors with pixelized spatial detection in the 1550nm wavelengths using a novel correlation method. The optofluidic sensor chip comprised 8 coupled microracetrack rings, bonded on top with a PDMS microfluidic channel. We analyzed the perturbed pixelized patterns by finding the correlations with the characteristic pixelized patterns. By applying such a correlation analysis, we have successfully confirmed from blind-sensing tests (researchers are not given the solution concentration) a detection of 0.08% (by weight) NaCl solution (a RI change of ~1.4×10^-4 RIU) injected to the CROW sensor chip. We demonstrated the noise-equivalent detection limit to ~1×10^-5 RIU. (Publication 2, Part C) 4. We have designed, modeled, fabricated and characterized SiN microring CROW-based sensors with pixelized spatial detection in the visible wavelengths using the same correlation analysis as mentioned in #3. The sensor chip comprised 8 coupled microracetrack rings. We used a ~680nm laser as the light source and a silicon CCD camera for imaging the light scattering patterns in the far field. We analyzed the perturbed pixelized patterns by finding the correlations with the characteristic pixelized patterns. Our measurements suggested a detection of 0.1% (by weight) NaCl solution (a RI change of ~1.8×10^-4 RIU) covering the CROW sensor chip. We are currently collecting more data to measure the noise-equivalent detection limit and are conducting the blind-sensing tests. (Publication 3, Part C)

618010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618010.value: We need to integrate the demonstrated SiN sensors with optofluidics, micro-optics and a CCD camera. The proposed course of action includes: (i) optimizing the SiN microring CROW sensor design with an optimized coupling between adjacent microrings, (ii) optimizing the SiN material composition in order to minimize the waveguide propagation loss, while allowing sufficient amount of light scattering from the waveguide surfaces for optical imaging in the far field, (iii) designing, fabricating (by soft lithography) and bonding the thin-film polymer-based microlens array on top of the PDMS microfluidic layer, (iv) integrating a relatively large-sized SiN CROW-based sensor with the PDMS microfluidic layer via direct bonding, and (v) imaging the out-of-plane elastic scattering light from the integrated sensor chip using a standard silicon CCD camera. We also plan to further develop the demonstrated CROW-based RI sensor to a label-free biomedical sensor. We will deposit a silica thin film on top of the SiN CROW sensor for the ease of functionalizing the sensor with specific receptors using standard techniques. The SiN CROW-based sensors using pixelized spatial detection can then be applied to specific sensing of targeted small analytes, such as specific DNAs and proteins.

618010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618010.value: Due to the growing demand of healthcare and remote health monitoring, various biochemical sensing technologies have been proposed over the past two decades. Among them, optical microresonator-based sensors have demonstrated as a useful tool to extract information of analytes (such as concentrations of bulk solutions, mass/size of nanoparticles, molecules, viruses or DNAs) interacting on the microresonator surfaces. However, conventional optical microresonator-based sensors often require high-quality-factor microresonators and sophisticated spectral measurements using high-resolution wavelength-tunable lasers. Here, we proposed and successfully demonstrated a paradigm shift of using coupled-resonator optical waveguides (CROWs) as a refractive index sensor by imaging the light scattering patterns from CROW at a fixed laser wavelength. By comparing the perturbed pixelized pattern with the characteristic pixelized patterns, we have demonstrated a minimum change of refractive index in the cladding medium detectable down to 10^-5 in the infrared wavelength. We have also demonstrated CROW-based sensors operating in the visible wavelengths, thus enabling the use of ubiquitous CCD/CMOS cameras that are widely available in smartphones for capturing the light scattering patterns. We therefore envision the technology to be embedded into future smartphones, allowing the sensing data to be transmitted to the cloud and analyzed by experts in a remote site.

618210.label: Realisation of objectives
618210.value: A totally transparent rectangular mini/microchannels with various hydrophobic strips/arrays, microheater and temperature sensor arrays have been developed utilizing recently developed microfabrication techniques. An advanced silicon-based, fast response temperature sensor micro array were integrated into the substrate of rectangular microchannels. An experimental facility for quantitatively measuring the heat flux, temperature, fluid flows and bubble dynamics in microchambers under wettability patterned surfaces and temperatures have been developed. A novel technique for non-invasive liquid temperature measurements in a mini/micro space has been developed. Visualization method is also developed to measure heat transfer and flow conditions under different wall coating and temperatures. Advanced measurement techniques are crucial for the experimental research of this project.Surfaces patterned with multiscale micro/nanostructured surfaces were studied experimentally. This kind of micro/nano structured surfaces improves the capillary capability of the wick, provides more nucleation sites and increases the heat transfer area. It results in a much higher heat transfer coefficient compared with flat surfaces. Multi-bubble generation, oscillating and coalescence in microchambers with different hydrophobic patterns and heating source arrays were studied for predicting the heat and mass transfer characterizing flows and bubble dynamics. The flow velocity, temperature under various heating conditions and Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) heaters were measured using advanced measurement techniques. The wettability pattern induced flow velocity field during the heat and mass transfer process were investigated. The effects of bubble oscillation along a heating source were studied. The effect of fluid flows and the heating pulse power were also investigated. Surface wettability patterns have been used for monitoring and controlling microbubble generation and dynamics. The heterogeneity of the surface, and the heater array arrangement were studied and utilized for microbubble control processes. Bubble size, heat flux, nucleation cites, surface properties and heater dimensions, temperature field, and flow velocity, channel size and aspect ratio have been studied and analyzed using experimental data.

618210.label: Major findings and research outcome
618210.value: In this research, it is found that the dynamics and coalescence of thermal microbubbles are significantly affected by the wettability patterned heterogeneous surfaces (Chen and Qiu 2015). It was found that wettability patterns increase the critical heat flux (CHF) by moderating the Helmholtz instabilities, preventing the formation of an insulating vapor layer. Viewed from beneath the substrate, bubble behavior on the patterned surface was captured and analyzed for better understanding of how hydrophobic islands worked as localized and controlled nucleate sites even with a relatively small heater. Heterogeneous surfaces were performed best compared to the other two homogeneous surfaces by higher CHF and HTC. For the hydrophobic surface, it reached the CHF immediately the liquid started to boil causing poor heat transfer efficiency especially for the relatively small heater in our case. And CHF was enhanced by 90% on the wettability patterned surface in comparison with a hydrophilic surface. Reasons for heat transfer enhancement are presented by bubble dynamics on surfaces with different wettabilities. Supporting phenomenon is found for the heat transfer enhancement from the bubble dynamics point of view. It demonstrated how hydrophobic islands worked as localized and controlled nucleate sites even with a relatively small heater size. The heterogeneous patterns increase the nucleation site density by controlling the bubble size and distance between adjacent bubbles. Wettability perturbation induced by the patterns affects the flow instability which induced local convective microflow surrounding the bubbles. This also affects the bubble departure diameter and departure frequency. The nucleation site density of the biphilic surface was more than 1200% higher, compared to that of the homogeneous surface (72% of hydrophobic islands or 18 of the 25 islands, could be activated simultaneously with heat flux of 206 W/cm2). Experimental observation of the bubble dynamics provided supporting results that hydrophobic islands controlled localized nucleate sites. The latent heat of the trapped droplet under bubbles with unique shapes on the biphilic surface would additionally contribute to the HTC. The departure diameter was about 1/3 of the size on the homogeneous surface. Smaller bubbles grew and departed on the heater quickly, resulting in a higher HTC. Bubble interactions and instability of big bubbles resulted in both a larger CHF and higher HTC. Bubble departure frequency was decreased by the residual bubbles that remained as the boiling nuclei. This further promotes boiling on the biphilic surface which also contributed to the heat transfer efficiency.

618210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618210.value: The newly developed patterned hydrophilic/hydrophobic surfaces can significantly enhance bubble dynamics and heat transfer. The pattern size, pitch distance and pattern shape are three key parameters which need to be optimized. It was found that the bubble contact line was similar to the contour of the hydrophobic islands. The argument is whether a shape with smooth curvature like a circle or with sharp curvature like a triangle confines the nucleate bubble better. The pattern size confines the size of the nucleate bubble and the pitch distance controls the interaction of the adjacent bubbles. Moreover, the integrated size of the two variables controls the nucleation site density. Since the heat transfer efficiency changes with the heat flux, the patterns with different size and pitch distance should have different optimal working conditions. The decrease of bubble departure diameter and the increase of nucleation site density have tradeoff. Optimization of these two variables is a complicated but interesting topic. Systematic research on this topic would provide key parameters for better control of nucleate boiling. Furthermore, hierarchical pattern also has possibilities for heat transfer enhancement.

618210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618210.value: Dynamics and coalescence of thermal microbubbles in microscale is relevant to energy, lab-on-a-chip devices, and analysis, electrokinetic micro pumps, micro heat pipes, micro fuel cells, micro fluidic research and industrial applications. The current project focused on the fundamental phenomena of bubble dynamics and coalescence of thermal microbubbles on wettability patterned surfaces that affect bubble nucleation, growth, detachment and interaction in mini/micro spaces. This is the first time a wettability patterned surface is found to have significant impact on bubble nucleation cite control and break up manipulation which resulted a significant improvement in heat transfer coefficient and critical heat flux. The effects of surface wetting, nucleation cite density, bubble detachment diameter, departure frequency and heat flux on bubble dynamics and heat transfer are investigated. It was crucial to non-invasively measure transient temperatures in mini/micro spaces, especially, in near the interface of micro bubble. A novel visualization technique for a mini/micro space measurement has been developed. Based on our findings, because surface wettability patterns have significant impact on the bubble dynamics, coalescence heat and mass transfer processes, the technique help to better design and optimize the microfluidic cooling devices, such as nuclear power plan cooling, vapor chambers, heat pipes.

618310.label: Project Title(Chinese)
618310.value: 随机及非随机混合不确定性下的强健稳定性

618310.label: Project Objectives
618310.value: To obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for robust stability under mixed deterministic and stochastic uncertainties. It is desired and expected to have such conditions in the form of small-gain theorems. To study the robust controller synthesis problem based on the conditions obtain in Objective 1. This is the secondary objective which will only be addressed if significant progress in Objective 1 is made.

To study the robust controller synthesis problem based on the conditions obtain in Objective 1. This is the secondary objective which will only be addressed if significant progress in Objective 1 is made.

618310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618310.value: Robust stability analysis under deterministic uncertainty has undergone extensive studies in the last forty years. The celebrated small-gain theorem and the structured singular value analysis have had far reaching impact on the development of postmodern control theory. Started at roughly the same time but with less extend, robust stability analysis under stochastic uncertainty has also attracted considerable attention through the years. Nice small-gain theorems in the stochastic setting for both single uncertain parameter case and multiple uncertain parameter case were discovered. Recently, due to the intensive study of networked control systems and financial systems, it is realized that in general a system may contain both deterministic uncertainty and stochastic uncertainty simultaneously. How to analyze the stability robustness and how to design a controller so that the controlled system has strong robustness against such mixed uncertainty are newly emerged theoretic issues. There are some scattered research on-going addressing these issues but the results are still in preliminary stages. In this proposed project, we plan to study the robust stability analysis of LTI systems under mixed deterministic and stochastic uncertainties. Our primary objective is to develop mixed small-gain theorems which generalize both the pure deterministic and pure stochastic small-gain theorems. After achieving this objective, we will then study the optimal control issues which is on how to design optimal controllers so that the stability robustness with respect to the mixed uncertainties is optimized. 在过去的四十年中, 人们对非随机不确定性下的强健稳定性分析作了大量研究. 众所周知的小增益定理及结构奇异值分析对后现代控制理论影响深远. 几乎同时, 人们对随机不确定性下的强健稳定性分析作了一些研究, 发现了随机小增益定理. 其适用于单个不确定参数和多个不确定参数的情形. 近来, 特别是通过对网络化系统和金融系统的研究, 人们认识到系统中通常同时含有随机和非随机的不确定性. 怎样分析此类系统的强健稳定性及怎样控制此类系统来改善强健稳定性自然成为大家关心的新问题. 针对这样的问题, 我们能看到一些零散的但很不完善的结果. 在此项目中, 我们计划研究线性时不变系统在随机及非随机混合不确定性下的强健稳定性. 我们主要的目标是发展出混合型小增益定理, 从而推广纯随机及纯非随机的小增益定理. 然后, 我们也准备研究相关的最优控制问题, 既怎样设计最优控制器使得混合不确定性下强健稳定性得以优化.

618510.label: Project Title(Chinese)
618510.value: 大规模基于图像的三维建筑物重建

618510.label: Project Objectives
618510.value: To develop a proper formulation of a large-scale automatic reconstruction methodology from a very large-scale sequence of systematically captured images. This should take into account the additional constraints and sensors provided in the systematic capturing process, and the whole process is formulated as a constrained optimization. To develop an automatic approach to reconstruct 3D models of buildings from input images captured on ground level. To develop a supervised semantic segmentation of multiple input images into four classes, sky, buildings, ground, trees and the others. To develop a systematic partition scheme to separate buildings into independent blocks using the major man-made line structures of the scene. To develop a facade structure analysis and modeling method to produce visually pleasing building models automatically. To implement the proposed approach and develop pilot applications based on the publically distributed imagery data from Microsoft Virtual Earth and Google Earth.

618510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618510.value: 谷歌数字地球（Google Earth） 与 微软虚拟地球（Microsoft Virtual Earth）项目都包含了城市空间三维模型系统，因此，它们对于基于地面图像的超大规模城市三维重建有着迫切的需求。 针对基于图像的三维重建问题，计算机视觉与图形学领域的许多研究者已经提出了许多不同的方法，但大部分的方法还只能利用较少数量的图像来实现小规模的三维重建。并且，这些方法往往需要人工交互。这些限制使得这些方法不适合于超大规模的城市三维重建，因此针对超大规模的城市三维重建，我们需要一种全自动的更有效的方法。 在本项目中，我们提出了一种利用街景图像的全自动建筑物三维重建技术。首先，我们将会开发一种多视图像的分割方法，该方法将街景图像分割成不同的语意类别，例如天空，建筑物，地面，树以及其它类别。然后，在分割出的建筑物区域中，利用我们提出的街区分解技术，依据街景中的人造结构信息，把建筑群分解为独立的街区。最后，对每个独立的街区，我们运用提出的一种利用物体的正投影平面图的三维重建技术，实现独立街区的三维重建。考虑到三维重建可能会出现部分的缺失或是误差，我们将会利用街景图像的语意分割结果和建筑物结构分析技术来进一步完善三维重建的结果。我们的方法的一个与众不同之处在于，它利用了建筑物特有的规整性先验信息，能够实现逼真的三维重建。我们将会用谷歌数字地球街景（Google Earth Street View）与微软虚拟地球街景（Microsoft Virtual Earth Street side View）中的城市街景数据来验证我们的方法。该项目建立我们以前的研究成果之上，包括大规模半密（quasi-dense）三维点云重建技术和基于图像的半自动建筑物表面，建筑物和树的建模技术。

618510.value: We have developed a formulation of a large-scale automatic reconstruction methodology from a very large-scale sequence of systematically captured images, which takes into account the additional constraints and is formulated as a constrained optimization. We have developed an automatic approach to reconstruct 3D models of buildings from input images captured on ground level, and also have proposed a supervised semantic segmentation of multiple input images into sky, buildings, ground, trees and the others. We have developed a systematic partition scheme to separate buildings into independent blocks using the major man-made line structures of the scene, and also a facade structure analysis and modeling method to produce visually pleasing building models automatically.

618510.label: Major findings and research outcome
618510.value: We have developed a series of façade parsing methods based on the symmetries. In particular, we have presented a novel method for translational symmetry detection, optimization, and symmetry object segmentation in facade images. Unlike most previous methods, our detection algorithm accumulates pixel-level correspondence in translation space. Thus it does not rely on feature point detection and handles patterns with low repetition counts. To improve the robustness with multiple interfering symmetries, we introduce an image-space global optimization, which resolves multiple per-pixel symmetry lattices. We then propose a learning-based method that generates refined segmentation of foreground symmetry objects of arbitrary shapes, with the aid of the per-pixel symmetry information. Our proposed method is accurate, robust and efficient as demonstrated by an extensive evaluation using a large facade image database.

618510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618510.value: This work is now continued for the fusion of the ground level reconstruction and the aerial reconstructions.

618510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618510.value: Google Earth and Microsoft Virtual Earth both proposed a 3D platform for displaying real 3D models of city landscapes and buildings, which drives the demand of reconstructing or modeling very large-scale city environment from images systematically captured on ground level. Computer vision and computer graphics researchers have developed many methods for 3D reconstruction and modeling, but most of the methods can only handle small-scale objects with small-number of input images. More importantly, these methods often require user interactions. This clearly could not satisfy the gigantic scale of reconstruction that requires a fully automatic and efficient approach. In this project, we have proposed an automatic approach to generate 3D representations of buildings from images captured along the streets.

619210.label: Project Objectives
619210.value: The study will, for the first time, extend the previous work of Coutts and Wilkins (a Co-I) et al. (2008) from a flashing checkerboard pattern to a random dot pattern oscillating in yaw and fore-and-aft axes. NIRS responses will be measured at the V3/5/6 cortical areas and selected areas of the distributed vestibular cortex. The study will examine, for the first time, the neural responses associated with two scenarios of eye fixation that are known to produce SIGNIFICANT and OPPOSITE effects on levels of visually induced motion sickness. The first scenario is eye fixation on random dot patterns oscillating in yaw axis and the second is off-axis eye fixation on random dot patterns expanding and contracting along a fore-and-aft axis. NIRS responses will be measured at the V3/5/6 cortical areas and selected areas of the distributed vestibular cortex. The spatial temporal frequency of the stimuli at two eye fixation points will be equalized. The study will identify changes in levels of oxyhaemoglobin in selected areas of the distributed vestibular cortex associated with vection sensations.

619210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619210.value: In 2005, the International Workshop Agreement 3 (IWA3, 2005) concluded that more research on the etiology of visually induced motion sickness (VIMS) is needed. Several hypothetical neural pathways for the development of VIMS (Figure 4, Section 2c) have been presented but remained untested. The proposed study will use near infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) to measure changes in levels of oxyhaemoglobin associated with visual stimuli that are known to produce various levels of VIMS. In particular, two scenarios of eye fixation will be studied: (i) fixation on a random dot pattern oscillating in a yaw axis; and (ii) fixation on an off-axis point in an expanding and contracting random dot pattern. The comparison condition would be watching the same stimuli without eye fixation. Eye fixation has been shown to REDUCE levels of sickness in the former scenario but INCREASE it in the latter. Emphasis will be placed on controlling the spatial and temporal characteristics of the two stimuli. NIRS probes will be placed over the visual cortex (V3, V5, V6) and the hypothetical vestibular cortex (distributed in the superior and medial temporal gyri and parietal cortex). During the collection of NIRS data, time series vection sensation data and finger blood pressure will be collected to provide references for interpreting the temporal changes in the NIRS data. In particular, the study will search for repeatable patterns of NIRS responses related to the presence and absence of vection sensation and the presence and absence of eye-fixation. No such NIRS data have been reported. In 2008, a Co-I of this proposal (Prof. Wilkins) reported repeatable patterns of NIRS responses when watching flashing checkerboard patterns. He used a grey visual background as the baseline condition. A series of experiments will be conducted to establish a suitable baseline condition for this proposed study (see Section 3). Since NIRS systems are scarce resources, the collaboration among the HKUST, the University of Hong Kong, the Centre for Brain Science at University of Essex (UK), and the HK Polytechnic University offers a good opportunity to carry out this proposed study. 在2005年，第3國際研討會協議（IWA3，2005）的結論是需要研究視覺誘發暈浪症狀 (VIMS) 的病因。幾種相關的神經通路已經提交，但仍未經證實。擬議的研究將使用近紅外線光譜（NIRS）測量在視覺神經的氧合血紅蛋白水平變化，已知會產生不同程度的暈浪症狀(VIMS)。研究的重點是: (一）當凝視固定在一個旋轉的隨機圖案所引起的暈浪症狀;及（ii）當凝視固定在一個不斷擴大及減少的隨機圖案所引起的暈浪症狀。重點將放在視覺刺激的空間和時間特徵上。近紅外光譜探測器將被放置在視覺皮層（V3，V5和V6）。這項研究將搜索可重複的NIRS模式。現在沒有這樣的數據。在2008年，我們的合作夥伴 (英國埃塞克斯大學的威爾金斯教授)發現了人類在看棋盤圖案時的NIRS模式。由於近紅外光譜系統是稀缺資源，香港科技大學,香港大學,和香港理工大學之間的合作提供一個良好的機會進行這項建議的研究。

619210.label: Realisation of objectives
619210.value: Objective 1 has been realized. Experiment 1 successfully confirmed the findings of Coutts et al. (2008) and Experiment 3 extended the findings to zooming checkerboard patterns with increased levels of oxygenated haemoglobin (OxHb) in area around V5 (Wang et al., 2011). Experiment 2a used motion illusive stationary patterns to provoke higher OxHb in corical area near V5 but results were not significant. Since the tasks used in Experiment 3 were similar to those in previous heading discrimination studies (e.g., de Winkel et al., 2012), Experiment 2b was conducted to examine whether head discrimination task stimulations would be an alternative stimuli. This experiment disproved a previously reported understanding of how the brain integrates visual and vestibular stimuli. Results were written as a working paper (Bao et al., 2014). Objective 2 has been realized. Experiments 4a, 4b and 4c successfully located and measured significant increases in levels of OxHb at C4 (10/20 system) in respond to exposure to physical motion along lateral, fore-and-aft and sway axes. Results were new (Zhao et al., 2013a,b; 2014). The neural responses associated with two scenarios of eye fixation known to produce opposite effects on VIMS had been studied (Experiments 8a,b - exposure to yaw visual motion with and without eye fixation; Experiments 9a,b – exposure to fore-and-aft visual motion with and with off-axis eye fixation). Results indicated that eye fixation did not cause significant differences in levels of OxHb in cortical regions around C4. Using results of Experiments 6 and 7, we eliminated the possible cofounding effects of finger movements and the presence of background noise. Further investigation indicated that the field-of-view might be another cofounding factor. We increased the field-of-view to 50 degrees x 200 degrees in Experiments 10a,b and found that eye fixation could increase the velocity of image movement projected on the peripheral part of the retina which in turn increase the levels of VIMS (Guo et al., 2014). Objective 3 has been realized. Experiments 5a,b compared the levels of OxHb among viewers of dots moving in random directions verses moving in a coherence roll direction. Although no significant difference was found overall, interesting patterns of OxHb measured at V5, PO(V6) regions, and vestibular areas (C4, 10/20 system) were observed in some individuals and not in others.

619210.label: Major findings and research outcome
619210.value: Due to the physical bulkiness of MRI equipment, previous studies on cortical responses to vestibular stimuli used electric or caloric stimuli to replace physical motion. Such stimuli are not physical motions and could not be directional specific. The current study measured, for the first time, cortical neural responses to physical motions in different directions using a mutli-channel portable near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) system. Results indicated that exposure to 0.5Hz motion in different axes caused significant and different localized changes in levels of oxygenated haemoglobin (OxHb) at cortical regions around T4 and C4 (10/20 system). These results are new and original (Zhao et al., 2013a,b; 2014). The successful determination of cortical neural responses to inertial vestibular stimuli also validates the use of NRIS to study neural integration of visual and vestibular signals. Past studies on neutral integration of visual and vestibular signals suggested a bias towards the vestibular signals and the phenomenon was referred to as the ‘vestibular over-weighting’ (de Winke; et al., 2010). Our study exposed participants to near threshold visual and inertial motion and reported that in the absence of perceivable vestibular stimuli, the ‘vestibular over-weighting’ phenomenon still existed which contradicted the current understanding. Results have been written as a working paper and a new model on the neural integration is proposed (Bao et al., 2014). Eye fixation has been shown to reduce as well as increase levels of visually induced motion sickness (VIMS). Results of the current study suggest that the key to the opposite effects had been the changes in the velocity of image motions projected on the peripheral vision. This velocity has been referred to as the peripheral retinal slip velocity (PRSv). Interacting effects between eye movements and PRSv had been studied and results indicated that while increasing PRSv can increase levels of VIMS, these effects have significant interactions with eye motion velocities. Results are being written as a working paper (Bao et al., 2014a,b). This interesting but inconclusive changes in levels of OxHb during exposure to VIMS provoking stimuli might have been due to the limited penetration depth of NIRS beams. A preliminary proposal to use fMRI to measure the changes of OxHb in deeper cortical regions has been submitted to Collaborative Research Fund (CRF) (HKUST C6012-14G).

619210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619210.value: In this study, although interesting patterns of neural responses were observed among viewers exposing to conflicting visual and vestibular motion cues, the results were not strong enough to be statistically significant. We think this may have been due to the limitations associated with the penetration depth of near-infrared laser. To verify this hypothesis, we have submitted a preliminary proposal to the Collaborative Research Fund (CRF) to conduct a series of functional Magnetic Resonance (fMRI) studies in collaboration with the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong University. Currently, HKUST does not have a MRI facility suitable for the proposed studies.

619210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619210.value: When seated or standing persons watch wide field-of-view moving scenes, they perceived conflicting visual motion cues and vestibular motion cues. About one-third of these viewers would feel sick and report symptoms of visually induced motion sickness (VIMS). Such situations can be commonly found among players of computer games and i-max movie viewers. Understanding how the brains integrate the conflicting visual and vestibular motion cues is an important step to determine the root causes of VIMS. When perceiving moving scenes, the speed of image movements as modulated by the eye motions of the viewers has been shown to significantly affect the levels of VIMS (Guo et al., 2014). This knowledge enables the research team to present controlled conflicting motion cues to study the neural signatures among viewers. Using near-infrared laser beams, the research team successfully measured the localized changes of oxygenated cortical blood flow when participants were exposed to conflicting visual and vestibular cues (Zhao et al., 2013a,b; 2014). A previously report theory on how human integrates visual and vestibular motion cues have been studied and modified (Bao et al., 2014a,b). All in all, the research has enabled us to understand more about how VIMS susceptible viewers integrate the conflicting motion cues.

620010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620010.value: Billions of dollars are lost every year due to telecommunications fraud and credit card forgery, so monitoring, surveillance, and quick detection of fraudulent events and abnormal activities has become critical in a variety of industries that have complex operation systems and process huge amounts of data. Most conventional statistical process control (SPC) techniques cannot effectively handle high-dimensional data monitoring and surveillance in real time. This proposed project focuses on developing SPC techniques for monitoring business processes with large numbers of high-dimensionality transactions and detecting fraudulent records among them. In order to overcome the known disadvantages that other monitoring and surveillance techniques exhibit, three fundamental issues will be studied: (1) an SPC approach that can handle real-time, high-dimensionality data streams with on-line feature extraction and quick fraud detection; (2) a methodology to detect complicated systematic changes from a huge number of data streams that include discrete and non-normal variables; (3) an effective monitoring and surveillance system that can make use of dynamic incoming data streams to update anticipated drifts of the system and at the same time to detect unanticipated shifts for corrective action. The tasks will be carried out with reference to telecommunications. 電信詐欺和信用卡造假造成了每年數十億美元的損失，因此監控並快速檢測欺詐事件和非常態活動已成為許多具有複雜的運行系統、龐大的相關資料的企業關注的重心。大部分傳統的統計過程共治方法不能有效地實現高維資料的即時檢測。本專案著眼於拓展統計程序控制方法，以監控含有大量高維交易資料的商業過程並檢測出其中的虛假記錄。為了克服其他監控和檢測方法顯露出的缺點，三個基本的問題將被著重討論：(1) 可以處理即時、高維的資料流程，實現線上特徵提取和快速欺詐檢測的統計程序控制方法；(2) 可以根據含有離散和非正態變數在內的大量資料流程來檢測複雜的系統變化的方法；(3) 可以利 用動態的輸入資料流程更新預測的系統偏差並同時檢測糾正措施引起的意外變化的有效監控檢測系統。這些任務將通過參照電信相關的事項逐步實現。

620010.label: Realisation of objectives
620010.value: To adapt variable selection and estimation techniques to high-dimensionality on-line monitoring and diagnosis problems, we have developed a variable-selection-based multivariate EWMA chart that has a great potential for process monitoring and diagnosis (Wang, et al., 2012). To characterise and identify relationships among high-dimensionality complex variables on-line, we have applied kernal-distance-based approach and support vector methods (Ning and Tsung, 2013). We have also developed several methods able to effectively monitor high-dimensionality data streams, including Ou et al., 2012; Zou, et al., 2012; Zi, et al., 2012; Li, et al., 2012; Li, et al., 2013; Shen, et al., 2013. Finally, we have developed several approaches for fault diagnosis and isolation making use of false discovery rate (Li and Tsung, 2012), density-based approach (Ning and Tsung, 2012), and applications in multistage processes (Shang, et al., 2013).
