620010.label: Major findings and research outcome
620010.value: We have generated rich research outcomes on all four objectives. In particular, we have spent extensive effort on the real-time monitoring of high-dimensionality data streams. For example, a very efficient spatial rank-based multivariate EWMA scheme has been developed that can be distribution-free and very robust to various data distribution (Zou, et al., 2012; Zi, et al., 2012). For categorical data stream (including binary data), there is usually no efficient way to monitor. We have provided novel solutions with several control schemes, such as in Li, et al., 2012; Li, et al., 2013; Shang, et al., 2013; Shen, et al., 2013. We have published 12 journal papers, mostly in leading journals, and one conference paper. We have also trained two PhD students during the period. One has been an Assistant Professor at the Xian Jiaotong University, and another has got an Assistant Professor offer from the Shanghai University. We have also been invited to present the research results at several international conferences (e.g., INFORMS, etc.).

620010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
620010.value: The high dimensional statistical monitoring and surveillance is a huge and broad problem and has a great potential for further research. The solution may not be limited to variable selection techniques. Our research group at the HKUST Quality Lab will be based on the research outcomes from this project and tackle this research further. Our next focus will go beyond the large data volume and dimension, and be more on the data variety, i.e., the fusion of different forms and heterogeneous sources of data. We have several working papers in preparation and also expect to present our new research ideas and results at various international conferences in the future.

620110.label: Major findings and research outcome
620110.value: Comprehensive review and compilation had been done on the methodologies for modeling dynamic time-space evolution of the rain-field during a single rainstorm event. The review led to the development of a modeling framework to adequately capture the spatio-temporal variation of rain-field characteristics in Hong Kong. In this study, a framework for analyzing the dynamic time-space evolution of the rainfall consistent with 6-min, 1-km by 1-km pixel radar images was developed. Geostatistical approach was employed to analyze the spatial structure of the rain-field. It was found that through the use of indicator variograms of rain-fields the non-Gaussian distribution issue can be adequately handled. The analysis of three heavy rainstorm events that passed through Hong Kong clearly shows that the spatial structure of rain-field is highly anisotropic and such feature must be incorporated in the model to accurately capture time evolution of a rainstorm over a spatial domain. Furthermore, the study developed a model to estimate the rainfall intensity over a spatial domain on the basis of the sample rainfall values and information of the spatial structure (e.g., anisotropic variogram) derived from the radar rainfall data. The cumulative distribution functions at all unsampled locations can be obtained by Indicator Kriging to provide estimations of exceedance probabilities for different rainfall intensity thresholds. A comparison between the observed rain-field and Indicator Kriging-based estimation suggested that the proposed method can produce realistic time-space evolution of rain-field during rainstorm events. In addition, autoregressive integrated moving average models were used to describe the within-storm temporal variations of the rainstorm characteristics describing its spatial structure. This framework could potentially provide useful basis for critical operation and management decisions in agriculture, hydrology, hydraulic structural design and other areas which depend on the reliable estimation and predictions of precipitation. To compliment short-term rainfall forecast as described above, the study also considered rainfall characterization for engineering design purpose by investigating extreme rainfall depth – time scale relationships at automatic raingauges over the territory of Hong Kong. A mechanism was established in the study by using such rainfall depth – time scale relationship to derive at-site short-duration rainfall depth-duration-frequency (DDF) relationships at conventional raingauges at which only daily rainfall information is available.

620110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
620110.value: The time scale based methods for estimating design rainfall DDF should be extended and expanded to ungauged locations in Hong Kong. As the methods involve statistical analysis of finite amount of rainfall data, results of analysis are subject to uncertainty. Hence, appropriate assessment of the uncertainty associated with the estimated design rainfalls should be made and incorporated in the risk-based design of hydrosystem infrastructures.

620110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
620110.value: In Hong Kong, catchments are typically small and highly urbanized. Furthermore, significant part of its territory has hilly terrain. These geographical features result in relatively short flow time and, hence, are indicative that Hong Kong is susceptible to the threat of flash floods and landslides during intense convective thunderstorms and tropical cyclones. An analysis and modeling framework has been developed to capture and describe time-space evolution of storm events passing over the territory of Hong Kong. Such framework could potentially provide useful basis for critical operation and management decisions in agriculture, hydrology, hydraulic structural design and other areas which depend on the reliable estimation and predictions of precipitation. In addition, relationships between extreme rainfall depth and duration in Hong Kong have been investigated to establish a mechanism to estimate reliable short-duration design rainfall DDF relationship at conventional raingauges. This allows engineering design of hydrosystems at many conventional raingauge sites which are otherwise impossible.

620310.value: To identify the initial stress states in sand around a displacement pile before soil creep initiates, i.e., the stress state produced at the end of pile driving or before pile setup develops. To characterize the shaft and base capacity changes of displacement piles in sand during setup and to investigate the associated underlying mechanisms of pile setup for a single pile and a pile group. To investigate how contact creep between sand particles is associated with the development of pile setup and to understand how the initial stress conditions in the surrounding sand produced by pile driving can influence the progress of subsequent pile setup. To gain micromechanical insights into the responses of the surrounding soil during pile installation and subsequent setup, e.g., the evolution of contact forces and contact normals among soil particles and the associated changes in the lateral stress on the piles. To examine the stress, strain, and stiffness changes and the associated stress paths in sand around a displacement pile at different locations during pile installation, setup, and load tests. To characterize the effects of neighboring pile installation and how these effects can change the behavior of subsequent pile setup in a pile group.

620310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620310.value: Displacement piles in sand often demonstrate a significant capacity increase with time after the end of pile driving, i.e., pile setup. This phenomenon has been reported in different places, including Hong Kong where all the high rise buildings are founded on piles. However, in current practice, engineers do not take into account this extra capacity from pile setup in the design. This is because the behavior of pile setup and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In view of this, the main objective of this project is to carry out a comprehensive study to enhance the fundamental understandings on pile setup and to gain new insights into the behavior of surrounding soils. It is expected that findings from this project can ultimately provide an innovative guideline to improve and optimize the current design of pile foundation and therefore may enable considerable reductions both in the cost and time to be involved for pile constructions. In order to achieve the above project goals, a new approach, using well-instrumented centrifuge model tests and advanced numerical simulations by the discrete element method (DEM), will be adopted. It is believed that contact creep between sand particles and subsequent particle rearrangements occur during pile setup, which gradually change the distribution of contact forces and properties in the surrounding soils, and ultimately lead to increases in pile capacity. The development of contact creep, however, depends on the stress condition produced during pile driving. Examining and understanding these issues will be the focus of the centrifuge model tests and DEM simulations in this project. In addition to the use of traditional measurements in the centrifuge model tests, this project will adopt newly developed measurements in the surrounding soils using the wave-based technique, Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) sensors, and flexible force sensors. The MEMS sensors have a miniature size and can be buried into soil samples to characterize particle movements and local stress changes during pile installation and setup. The MEMS sensors can also be used as receivers in wave-based measurements to monitor soil stiffness changes, especially during pile setup. Moreover, since DEM simulations can provide valuable visualization of particle movements and micromechanical insights into the soil responses during pile driving and setup, they can therefore assist in revealing underlying mechanisms of pile setup. Results from centrifuge model tests and the DEM simulations will also be compared and calibrated with published data of field measurements, especially for Hong Kong cases. 排土桩打入砂土地基后，承载力会随时间显著增加，即工程上所讲的桩基歇后效应。很多地方，包括有很多高层建筑的香港，都报道过这种现象。但是，由于桩基歇后效应的特点及其机制还不是很明确，因此在设计施工当中，工程师们很少考虑其产生的额外承载力。鉴于此，本项目的主要目的即是通过全面的研究提高对桩基歇后效应根本理解，以及得到对桩周土特征的新认识，从而为提高和优化桩基设计提供一条新思路，进而减少桩基建设的成本和时间。 研究者认为在桩基歇后效应过程中，砂土颗粒之间会发生接触蠕变，随后颗粒将重新排列。这会逐渐改变接触力的分布和周围土的特点，最终导致桩承载力的增加。但是，接触蠕变的发展取决于桩打入过程中产生的应力状态。为验证和解释这些猜想，本项目将采用配有适当精度仪器的离心机模型试验和离散元数值模拟进行研究验证。 离心机模型试验中，除了常规测量外，还加入了新的测量，采用了波技术，微机电力学系统（MEMS）传感器，以及可弯曲的力传感器。MEMS传感器很微小，能够被埋在土中测量在桩打入以及歇后效应中颗粒的运动和局部应力的变化。在检测土劲度变化时，它还可以作为波量测的接收器，尤其是对歇后效应研究中更有用处。另一方面，由于离散元数值模拟能实现颗粒的运动可视化，提供土反应的微观力学解释，所以其能够帮助揭示桩基歇后效应的潜在力学机制。最后，离心机试验和离散元数值模拟的结果将会同现场试验结果，尤其对香港的案例，进行对比和标定。

620310.label: Realisation of objectives
620310.value: The main objective of this study is to understand the pile setup mechanisms in sand. There are two M.Phil. and two Ph.D. students have been involved to work on this project. There are six objectives that are originally proposed and all of them are successfully achieved. Both experimental characterizations and numerical simulations were used in parallel to achieve the goals, with particular emphasis on revealing the associated micromechanics. In the experiments, innovative sensors and measurement techniques, such as using the tactile pressure sensor, wave-based techniques, and P-wave tomography imaging, are adopted in the laboratory and model pile tests. In the numerical simulations, the discrete element method (DEM) with special designed contact models, were used to help understand the pile-setup mechanism from the micromechanical perspective. All of the findings are summarized in 10 journal papers and 7 conference papers (to be further described in Sec 6.1).

620310.label: Major findings and research outcome
620310.value: The major findings and research outcomes are set out below: (1) The contact models used in the DEM simulations of soil creep during pile setup During the process of pile setup (soil creep or aging), the contact creep between particles occurs. Therefore, the contact models used in the DEM simulations have to be carefully designed in order to reproduce the real soil responses. The relevant finding and outcomes can be found in the attached journal papers [1-4; 6, 7] and conference papers [1-4]. (2) Using the tactile pressure sensor to measure the interparticle force changes during the creep (aging) process Measuring stress in a soil with the conventional load cell is always a challenge because the buried load cell unavoidably influences the stress field in the soil and creates an artificial boundary to promote soil arching. Tactile pressure sensors are ultra-thin and flexible and comprise numerous individual, tiny sensing elements, called sensels. These features resolve the problems associated with the conventional load cells and enable us to accurately measure stress in soils. However, in order to use the tactile pressure sensor, we have to solve the calibration related issues, including sensor drift (see the details in the attached Journal paper [5]). After the calibration related issues are solved, the sensor have been used to successfully characterize the evolution of interparticle forces within soil during the creep (or aging) process that takes place during pile setup. The underlying mechanisms regarding why the creep (or aging) process can continue to improve the soil properties can then be revealed, i.e., the homogenization of contact forces. The relevant findings can be found in the attached journal papers [3,4,6,7] and conference papers [1-4]. (3) Understand the soil responses during pile installation and the mechanisms during subsequent pile setup Both model pile tests and DEM simulations have been used to reveal the responses of soil surrounding the pile during pile installation (see attached journal papers [8, 9] and conference paper [6]), including the mechanism that governs friction fatigue (see attached journal paper [10] and conference paper [7]). It has also been found that pile setup is not caused by the increase in at-rest radial stress. Instead, it is mainly attributed to the increase in radial stress during pile loading, as a result of soil aging (or creep). The relevant findings can be found in the attached journal paper [8] and conference paper [5]).

620310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
620310.value: The practicing engineers always wish to use the capacity gain from the pile setup. Although various hypothesized aging mechanisms have been proposed, promising evidences identifying the underlying mechanisms have not yet been provided. This indeed is the exact reason why pile setup is not considered in the current design practice. In this study, we have provided clear explanations, based on both the numerical simulations and experimental findings, to the pile-setup mechanism. Hence, the further development can focus on how to make a specification to regulate the use of pile setup in the design of pile foundation. In addition, since creep (aging) of soil not only takes place during pile setup but also can be found in various kinds of earth structure, the future research can also looks into how to take the soil properties increases (during the aging process) into the account in the design of geotechnical engineering.

620310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
620310.value: Displacement piles in sand often demonstrate a significant capacity increase with time after the end of pile driving, for which engineers refer as pile setup. This phenomenon has been reported in different places, including Hong Kong where all the high rise buildings are founded on piles. However, in current practice, engineers do not consider this extra capacity simply because the behavior of pile setup has not been well understood and its underlying mechanisms remain unconcluded. Hence, the main objective of this proposal is to carry out a comprehensive study on this issue. It has been found that pile setup is mainly attributed to the increase in radial stress during pile loading, as a result of soil aging (or creep). Pile installation pushes the surrounding soil to the side, thereby imposing additional loading on the soil inside the influence zone. This loading action initiates an associated aging (or creep) process during the setup period; the aging effects, due to contact-force homogenization, ultimately give rise to an increase in pile shaft resistance. All of the findings in this project ultimately can enhance the current design of pile foundations and therefore reduce the construction time and cost.

620410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620410.value: The proposed project focuses on developing theories and technologies for hybrid wireless positioning with applications for the silver population. While GPS/Assisted-GPS is now a matured and accurate positioning technology, it remains an incomplete solution for personal localization and tracking because of its indoor unavailability and because of its relatively heavy battery consumption during each position fix. Cellular network-based positioning, particularly if based on cell ID alone, is inexpensive to implement and undemanding on terminal power, but provides only coarse-grained accuracy. Our project seeks to develop the optimal strategy for combining AGPS and cellular localization techniques to generate location data with sufficient frequency and accuracy to become useful for elderly localization and tracking applications such as emergency assistance, monitoring, cure, prevention, measurement, and lifestyle and social enhancement. These applications may target elderly individuals with different levels of needs, physical capabilities and preferences, and may be used by care professionals, family members, the elderly individuals themselves, and their social peers. Theories and technologies developed will be deployed in a trial network which has been in place since late 2008 in collaboration with a social service organization in Hong Kong. The proposed project will allow us to continue the research and development of this trial system, which currently includes an Assisted-GPS tracker device, Assisted-GPS receiver stations and assistance data server, and web and application servers. 项目的重点在于研究能够应用于老人服务的混合无线定位的理论和技术。虽然全球定位系统GPS和AGPS已经是一个成熟的技术，并能够提供精确的定位精度，但是由于其在室内的不可用性，以及每次定位的高功耗性，GPS/AGPS仍旧未能给个人定位和追踪提供一个完整的解决方案。基于蜂窝网络的定位技术，特别是仅仅使用网络标识来定位的技术，具有实现成本低和对终端电源要求不高的特点，但是它仅能够提供非常粗略的定位精度。我们的项目旨在研究将AGPS和 蜂窝定位技术相结合的最佳策略，以获得具有足够频率和精度的位置数据，从而为诸如紧急援助、监控、治疗、预防、测量以及提高生活方式和社交生活等老人定位 和追踪应用提供帮助。这些应用可能针对具有不同需求、身体素质和个人喜好的老年人，也可能被医护人员、家庭成员，老人自己和他们的社交对象所用。我们将会 在一个试运行网络上部署测试研究出来的理论和技术。该试验网位于香港的一个自2008年底以来和我们有合作关系社会服务机构，目前由一个AGPS追踪设备，AGPS接收基站，辅助数据服务器以及web和应用服务器组成。该项目也将使我们能够继续在该试验网上进行这样的研究和开发。

620410.label: Realisation of objectives
620410.value: Objective 1, which is to enhance the availability and accuracy of location information, has been fully achieved through the techniques published in the papers resulting from this project. A general model for data fusion was presented in journal publication #4. A practical system was described in conference paper #1. Objective 2, which is to enhance the usability of location information through intelligent trajectory tracing and mobility pattern modeling, has also been fully achieved. Journal publication #1, #5, #7 summarize our results in this area. Conference paper #1 and #3 describe how one may build historical mobility model for an individual, make use of such prior knowledge, and switch among different systems for location fixes. Objective 3, which is to develop sample applications for wearable devices, has been achieved to a large extend through the Android Apps that we have developed for cognitive training games for the elderly and for speech and auditory training for children with hearing disability. The first Apps was developed by final year project students and the second was developed with additional funding support. A related location-aware App with messaging capability was developed by an HKUST entrepreneurial company formed by the PI and staffed by graduates of HKUST. This App, named "Rapntok Pro" was developed on a commercial basis for a client and is free for download on Apple Store and Google Play. For measuring wellness, final year project teams have worked on conversation detection through speech/non-speech recognition and mobility detection (through location tracking) to detect social engagement and mobility for elders. Work is not yet complete and an final year project student has become an MPhil student to continue to work on this area. We hope to complete this work in 18 months. Objective 4, which is to develop a greater understanding on the world-wide effort on mobile ehealth, has been largely achieved, through a collaboration project with PCCW, the incumbent telecom operator in Hong Kong, on activity sensing and eHealth. There has also been close collaboration with the Hong Kong Jockey Club Center of Positive Ageing, talk and exchange at the Spatial Data Symposium and with the Hong Kong Institute of Surveyors in 2011.

620410.label: Major findings and research outcome
620410.value: The major research outcomes are: 1) A general model for fusing inputs or results from multiple localization systems. 2) Enhanced particle-filtering techniques for indoor localization and tracking. 3) Use of unlabeled data to reduce the off-line survey effort for Wi-Fi localization. 4) A computationally more efficient method for localization as an optimization problem using regularized least square classification and semi-definite programming. 5) Framework for practical systems for personal mobility pattern modeling and localization using multiple systems including GPS, cellular, and WiFi. Three PhD students and one master student have graduated with support from this project. One PhD graduate is now a post-doc research associate at UCLA. One is employed by Goldman Sach as technology consultant in Hong Kong, and one became a member of the Office of Government Chief Information Officer (OCGIO) of Hong Kong SAR. The master student is employed by Hewlett-Packard's software development team in Hong Kong. The pattern recognition and data processing techniques developed through this project have also enabled the group to extend into problems related to machine vision and automation, and to successfully secure an Innovation and Technology Fund project in the new area.

620410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
620410.value: We have been continuing to work on the problem of indoor localization. Our current focus is on indoor mapping and localization using unlabeled crowd-sourced data, and on personal mobility mapping. Papers which describe our works in these two areas are under review. We believe that a practical indoor localization system must be dynamic and must avoid the tedious effort of manual off-line calibration. We believe also that a localization system should be personalized to take advantage of prior knowledge on mobility and activity patterns of the individuals and to address the problem of device to device variation. We continue to be interested in developing a useful App, and we will develop one when our overall system design is sufficiently mature enough and when we have sufficient resource to do so.

620410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
620410.value: Under this project, we have developed a collection of techniques for fusing multiple systems for localization, for efficient solution of the localization problem as an optimization problem, for indoor localization and tracking, and for using unlabeled data to reduced the off-line setup effort. Our work has contributed to advancing the field of indoor localization and tracking. While we have not developed a localization application with conversation messaging capability as we originally hoped for, we have developed a number of related Apps which have been used in different contexts. The pattern recognition and data processing techniques developed through this project have also enabled the group to extend into problems related to machine vision and automation, and to successfully secure an Innovation and Technology Fund project in the new area.

620910.label: Project Title(Chinese)
620910.value: 减少道路拥堵的道路限行和收费方法

620910.label: Project Objectives
620910.value: To analyze and quantify the efficiency of traffic rationing by bounding the ratio between the system cost under the new user equilibrium and that under the original user equilibrium. To analyze and evaluate the effects of rationing under long-term traffic equilibrium with endogenous car ownership. To examine joint implementation of rationing, pricing or tradable credit schemes, and identify Pareto-improving hybrid strategies to both reduce congestion and make users better off.

To analyze and evaluate the effects of rationing under long-term traffic equilibrium with endogenous car ownership.
To examine joint implementation of rationing, pricing or tradable credit schemes, and identify Pareto-improving hybrid strategies to both reduce congestion and make users better off.

620910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620910.value: Traffic (or road space) rationing is a travel demand management strategy aimed at reducing the negative externalities generated by peak urban travel demand in excess of available supply or road capacity, through artificially restricting demand (vehicle travel) by rationing the scarce common good road capacity during the peak periods. This objective is achieved through restricting access into an urban cordoned off area or city center based on the last digits of the license number on pre-established days and during certain periods, usually, the peak hours. In many cases, road rationing also has the main goal of reduction of air pollution. The practical implementation of this policy is common in Latin America, and has been used in Beijing especially when there are important activities, such as, the 2008 Beijing Summer Olympics. As a possible alternative or supplement to road pricing, traffic rationing has received only very limited attention in transportation research. We propose to develop, model and evaluate rationing cum pricing strategies for urban traffic congestion reduction. The first part of the project will analyze the efficiency of traffic rationing by establishing the upper bound of the ratio between the system cost under the new user equilibrium and that under the original user equilibrium. The second part will analyze the effects of rationing under both short-term and long-term traffic equilibrium. The ‘short-term’ equilibrium describes the situation under which no one has incentive to change car ownership but obeys the rationing rules; the long-term equilibrium under rationing takes into account the travellers’ self-adjustment in car ownership and car disposals and characterizes the situation where no one has incentive to change car ownership. The third part will study joint implementation of rationing and pricing and evaluate the potential benefit derived from it. We shall conduct sensitivity analysis with respect to certain critical system factors such as rationing rate and charging level and develop strategies for the joint implementation of rationing and pricing for system optimization. All the analyses and developments and the policy implementation of the results will be demonstrated with Beijing and Hong Kong's urban network. The proposed study has the potential to help the system planner anticipate users' response to the separate and joint implementation of traffic rationing and road pricing and their effectiveness in improving urban traffic conditions. 为了缓解日趋严重的城市交通拥堵问题，道路限行措施正被越来越多的城市关注和采用。常用的限行措施一般会在高峰期周期性的限制不同尾号的车辆进入城市中心区或指定区域，通过这种方式硬性减少被控区域内的车流量，从而达到缓解拥堵同时减少空气污染的目的。这种限行措施在拉丁美洲被普遍运用，北京奥运会期间的单双号禁行措施更是引起了广泛关注。 尽管在拥堵缓解的实际应用中，道路限行措施已经成为道路收费很好的替代和补充，但是在学术领域，对限行的研究还非常有限。因此，我们首次建立了数学模型来研究限行与收费结合的模式，并对其缓解拥堵的效果进行评估。本研究主要分为三个部分：第一部分将通过找出限行前后交通网络中车辆总行驶时间比值的上限来分析限行的效率；第二部分将分析比较短期限行和长期限行措施下达到的不同的交通均衡状态。在短期限行措施下，用户不改变自己的车辆拥有量，只改变自己的出行方式来严格遵守限行规则；而在长期限行措施下，用户可以通过添置车辆的方式逃避限行，或者因为有限的使用率而放弃车辆来减少支出，故新的均衡下，车辆的出行需求会偏离限行初期的出行需求，均衡时的交通流量也会发生改变。第三部分，我们将研究如何将限行与收费结合起来制定更有效的缓解拥堵措施，并对不同限行比例和收费额度进行灵敏度分析。我们会将以上的模型和研究结果在北京和香港的城市网络中进行模拟应用。 我们相信，对限行措施以及限行和收费措施结合运动的研究将会对改善城市交通状况带来很大的帮助。

620910.label: Realisation of objectives
620910.value: Throughout the three and half years research period; we were able to investigate all the study issues raised originally in the proposal. All aspects of the traffic rationing and pricing for congestion reduction in the original proposal were addressed. Traffic rationing is a travel demand management strategy aimed at reducing the negative externalities generated by peak urban travel demand in excess of available supply or road capacity, through artificially restricting demand by rationing the scarce common good road capacity during the peak periods. This goal is achieved through restricting access into an urban cordoned off area or city center based on the last digits of the license number on pre-established days and during certain periods. This project developed and evaluated rationing cum pricing strategies for urban traffic congestion reduction. Specifically, the project analyzed the efficiency of traffic rationing by establishing the upper bound of the ratio between the system cost under the new user equilibrium and that under the original user equilibrium. The effects of rationing under both short-term and long-term traffic equilibrium are also examined. The 'short-term' equilibrium describes the situation under which no one has incentive to change car ownership but obeys the rationing rules; the 'long-term' equilibrium under rationing takes into account the travelers’ self-adjustment in car ownership and car disposals and characterizes the situation where no one has incentive to change car ownership. The project also investigated joint implementation of rationing, pricing, and tradable credit schemes, identifies Pareto-improving hybrid strategies to both reduce congestion and make users better off.

620910.label: Major findings and research outcome
620910.value: Traffic equilibrium patterns are established under both short- and long-term rationing. It is found that the average daily trip travel time with one car is the essential factor that determines the attainability of Pareto-improvement. Under the same rationing degree, it is found that Pareto-improvement is easier to obtain by short-term rationing than by long-term rationing. Publication: Wang, X.L., Yang, H. and Han D. It is found that Pareto-improving rationing and pricing scheme might be obtained as a combination of the rationing degree and the toll associated with rationing. Cordon pricing and P&R might further help in improving the efficiency of rationing and pricing strategy. Publication: Liu, W., Yang, H. and Yin, Y., 2014. 620910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
620910.value: Through the study, we gained a better command of the economic and operations research approach to tackling the various traffic congestion and mobility management problems. We found that the methodology that we developed can be further extended to deal with the multi-objective optimizations such as congestion mitigation and emission abatement. Further research is being carried out along this line.

620910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
620910.value: Road congestion has become an increasingly serious problem in most urban areas around the world, particularly in many cities of Mainland. Various alternatives and complementary policies such as traffic rationing or traffic rationing cum pricing are considered or implemented to tackle traffic congestion and air pollution problems. Although already in place as both short-term and long-term travel demand management strategies, traffic rationing has received very limited attention in transportation research. This project developed and evaluated rationing and rationing cum pricing strategies for urban traffic congestion control. Apart from having advanced the fundamental theory of traffic network analysis, the study also provided a practical method to analyze advanced rationing and pricing policies, which enables us to compare alternative operative solutions based on solid theoretical background. The study results are also useful for transportation planner to identify when and under what conditions a hybrid between rationing and pricing can be Pareto-improving in a manner that reduces traffic congestion while making no user worse off. It is particularly relevant to the Beijing metropolitan city, where traffic rationing as an appealing strategy is already in implementation and congestion charge is already on the agenda.

621010.label: Project Objectives
621010.value: [Theory on the Relation between Auxiliary and Target Data] We will develop a theory and various distance functions for relating the auxiliary and target collaborative information networks. 621010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621010.value: Collaborative information networks (CIN) are linked collections of users and entities such as products and Web pages. Examples of CINs are social networks, product recommendation systems, social tagging systems (Flickr.com), online product reviews (Amazon.com) and Web search logs from search engine companies (for more on information networks, see: http://dm1.cs.uiuc.edu/projects.html. `Collaborative’ is used here to emphasize the role of users.) A key learning problem is link prediction, which is to predict how one user or entity relates to another user or entity. Link prediction can be used to infer how much a given user likes a certain movie in terms of a user rating. Links can relate users and items by their preferences and shared characteristics. A major difficulty in link-prediction services in CINs is the data sparsity problem. Because each user can only access a limited number of items, and each item may be related to only a small number of other items, the network structure is often very sparse. This is especially true for networks that are newly created, also known as the so-called cold-start problem. When the network is sparse, overfitting can easily occur when we infer new links, causing significant performance degradation. In this project, we focus on how to solve the link-prediction problem for sparse collaborative information networks, by making use of the available auxiliary data sources through transfer learning. Transfer learning addresses a major difficulty in learning when we do not have sufficient knowledge on the target learning task. By recognizing that some auxiliary data sources, which may have different data distributions and features, may be related to the target data, we can transfer their existing useful knowledge to improve the learning performance of the target problem. We note that while our target data are sparse, dense auxiliary data may already exist in some other, more mature applications. For example, as we have demonstrated in our preliminary works, we can transfer some product-rating knowledge from a denser online-book domain to help improve the predictive performance in a sparse movie-rating task. We plan to solve the link prediction problem in sparse CINs by transferring knowledge from auxiliary CINs via a regularization and matrix-factorization based theory. We will investigate distance measures between the CIN data sources to guide the auxiliary-data selection. We consider both transfer learning with and without correspondences between the auxiliary and target data. We will conduct extensive empirical studies on several real-world application domains. 协同信息网络（CIN），例如，Flickr，亚马逊和网络，是联系很多不同用户的网络，如产品和网页的连接等。在这个网络上的链接预测问题是一个很有实际价值的机器学习问题，其目的是预测一个用户或实体如何涉及到其他用户或实体。链接预测可以用来推断多少用户喜欢在一个给定的产品， 也可以用来为用户对电影等产品进行评价，以预测用户的喜好和特点。在CIN链接预测问题上的主要困难是数据稀疏问题。由于每个节点指向其他节点的数量有限，网络结构往往是非常稀疏。在网络稀疏的情况下，机器学习中的过拟合的现象会时有发生，造成严重的性能下降。在这个项目中，我们重点解决稀疏协作信息网络的链路预测问题。 我们的方法是通过迁移现有的辅助数据源，使得迁移的知识，可以用来提高目标问题的学习效果。我们将转移到辅助CIN，通过正规化和矩阵因子分解的基础理论，同时考虑目标和辅助数据之间的两种情况： 有，或者没有，领域对应的学习。我们同时会进行在不同应用领域的实验研究。

621010.label: Realisation of objectives
621010.value: We have now successfully completed all objectives, and established a new framework for transfer learning in composite information networks. Composite information networks are multiple networks of information sources that have certain linkage and overlaps. Examples are social networks that serve different purposes. Often, these networks have knowledge about topology, node and link information, community information and information spreading information to be gained by analysis. Given the linkage and overlap between them, there is an opportunity to learn knowledge in one network and apply to another network. For example, knowledge can be gained from LinkedIn network and apply to authorship network in DBLP, and vice versa. In this aspect, we have developed a number of networks. 621010.label: Major findings and research outcome
621010.value: We have found several interesting insights in the research. First, information networks contains rich information that can be transferred. The knowledge that can be transferred have many angles, including network linkage and structure, user feedback information (ratings), user group behavior and communities. We have developed new algorithms to manage each of these kinds of knowledge transfer. Second, knowledge transfer relies on good distance metric. An important question is how to design good distance metrics that permit positive transfers and avoid negative ones. We have developed new algorithms that allow general forms of distance metrics to be learned (In IJCAI-2011, for example). Third, systems that are able to do knowledge transfer are more effective and general than systems that don't. We demonstrated transfer learning successes in diverse domains, including product recommendation, location reasoning and recommendation, Web search, and user modeling on mobile phones.

621010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621010.value: Following the work on information network transferring, we plan to continue the research in several fronts. First, the Web itself is a huge information network. By making use of the Web, we can find a suitable source domain for all kinds of target domains. Thus, users may not need to provide explicit source domains for transfer. Instead, systems can be designed to automatically find source domains on the Web. Second, large scale transfer learning is possible between vertical domains of application. The important issue is to have a good corresponding distance measure in each domain that can be linked together. Thus, we plan to develop a new research program that allow joint learning of distance metrics in multiple, overlapping composite networks.

621010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621010.value: We live in a world full of networks. We have social networks, professional networks, and even the Web itself is a large network. To build services and applications for users, we need to have lots of knowledge about our networks of interest. For example, we need to know how to fill in the missing and uncertain values when a network is only partially known. We need to know the network community structures. We also need to know how to predict new events in a network. Our research allows knowledge to be gained about a network to be faster, more accurate and involve less human labor. Our approach is to leverage other more established networks, by which we can transfer the knowledge into our target information network. We have demonstrated applications of this approach in several areas, including product recommendation, web search, mobile applications. Our research were published in top conferences and won international awards.

621110.label: Project Objectives
621110.value: Develop fabrication techniques for dual-scaled hybrid nanowicks by growing aligned nanowires on micro-patterned silicon substrates. A two-level structure with well controllable microstructure and nanowire array patterns will be designed and fabricated. Characterize the capillary performance of the nanowicks. We will develop techniques for flow diagnosis including the rising meniscus, liquid spread speed, and flow visualization. Various working solutions and experimental conditions (e.g., temperature, orientation) will be examined, and the effects of surface tension to viscosity ratio, gravity, and nano/micro-pattern configurations will be investigated. Characterize evaporation/nucleate boiling heat transfer of the nanowicks. We will measure the critical heat flux (CHF) and the heat transfer coefficient (HTC), and diagnose bubble dynamics on the heated nanowick surfaces. The heat transfer enhancement will be investigated in terms of the effects of nucleation site density, effective heat transfer surface areas, wettability, and spreadability. Perform multiscale modeling for mass and heat transfer in the nanowicks. To this end, a microscopic model for mass transport at the nano/micro scales of the nanowick structures will be developed, resulting in a wicking limit that can be used to determine the limiting heat flux. At the macroscopic level, the nucleate boiling correlation will be established based on the classical correlations and our experimental data.

621110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621110.value: As microelectronic circuitry reaches unprecedented levels in density, thermal management is becoming a major bottleneck for the advancement of electronics technology. The demand for high heat dissipation (well above 100 w/cm2) has motivated research on innovative cooling technologies. Heat pipes utilize the latent heat of phase change and require no external power, which are superior to their active counterparts. Recirculation of the coolant in a heat pipe is done passively by means of a wick structure that induces capillary flow from the condenser to the evaporator. However, the capillary limit is usually the limiting factor in a heat pipe design. The major challenge for the heat spreading capacity of a heat pipe is to develop an effective wick structure to transport liquid to the heated area. We propose to develop wicking structures by growing nanowire arrays (e.g., ZnO) on patterned silicon substrates using low-cost manufacturing techniques, and investigate the multi-scale two-phase flow and heat transfer through such nanowicks. Compared to conventional wick geometries, the tight packing of nanowire arrays provides a higher capillary action to pump liquid to the evaporator. We will combine top-down and bottom-up approaches to fabricate micro-patterned silicon surfaces coated with aligned nanowire arrays. The ZnO nanowire morphology and density can be controlled by nano/micro-patterns of carbon catalysts in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) synthesis. The resulting dual-scaled surfaces are expected to provide higher wettability and spreadability, both of which are important for enhancing evaporation/boiling heat transfer. We will develop characterization techniques to quantify the wicking and thermal performance of the nanowicks. To validate the merit of nanowicks for use in heat pipes, we will demonstrate the limiting heat flux and the maximum heat transfer coefficient in a testing apparatus of a nanowick based evaporator. We will conduct multiscale modeling and parametric studies to optimize the nanowire configuration and surface pattern that would maximize the capillary flow and heat transfer. The long-term objectives of this effort are to understand the fundamental mechanisms of nanoscale transport and interfacial phenomena in nanostructured materials and to harness these mechanisms to create novel liquid delivery components for thermal management and micro total analysis systems. 隨著微電子電路密度達到前所未有的水平，熱管理正成為電子技術進步的一個主要瓶頸。對高散熱的需求（遠大于100 w/cm2）促進了對於新型冷卻技術的研究。熱管利用相變潛熱，不需要外加電源的特點，使它從眾多競爭者中脫穎而出。冷卻劑在熱管中的流動是通過吸液芯結構實現的，它將毛細管流從冷凝段輸運到蒸發段。然而，毛細極限往往是制約熱管設計的關鍵因素。熱管散熱能力的一個主要挑戰就是開發出高效的吸液芯結構，使其將流體運輸到蒸發段。 我們建議利用低成本製造技術，在具有結構的硅基片上生長納米線陣列的方法來製造吸液芯結構，並探討其多尺度兩相流和傳熱。相對於傳統的吸液芯結構，這種緊密封裝的納米線陣列可以提供更高的毛細作用，從而將液體運輸到蒸發段。我們將結合自上而下和自下而上的方法製造微結構硅表面, 該表面被整齊排列的納米線陣列覆蓋。納米線的形態和密度可以通過化學氣相沉積方法中碳催化劑的微納米結構來控制。預計產生的雙尺度表面能夠提供更高的浸潤性和鋪展性。這兩者對於增強蒸發和沸騰傳熱起到重要作用。我們將發展表徵技術，以量化納米吸液芯的吸液和熱性能。為了驗證在熱管中使用納米吸液芯的優點，我們將利用測試裝置對基於納米吸液芯的蒸發段進行測試，證明放熱端的臨界熱通量和最大傳熱系數。我們將進行多尺度建模並研究其參數，通過優化納米線的分佈和表面結構以優化毛細流和傳熱性能。該研究的長期目標是理解納米結構材料中納米尺度運輸和界面現象的基本機制，並利用這些機制創造一種新的可用於熱管理和微全分析系統的液體輸送組件。

621110.label: Realisation of objectives
621110.value: 1. Objective 1 was fully realized. We developed fabrication techniques for nanostructured surfaces with hierarchical roughness and/or heterogeneous wettability. Using a combined anisotropic wet-etching and/or deep reactive ion etching (DRIE) process, we fabricated aligned nanowires on micro-patterned silicon or copper substrates with well controllable nano/micro roughness and structural patterns. The surface wettability was modified using different deposition methods such as chemical vapor deposition or fluorization. Harnessing the dependence of surface wettability on the roughness, we constructed a) a unique nanograssed micropyramidal architecture that yields global superhydrophobicity and local wettable nucleation sites, both of which contribute to the enhanced phase change. b) non-uniform microstructured surfaces with wettability gradients for investigating droplet impact dynamics, evaporation and boiling phenomena. c) superhydrophobic copper surfaces with nanoribbon structures for studying the influence of surface roughness and chemical properties on the spontaneous motion of condensate drops, promotion or suppression of condensation frosting. 2. Objective 2 was fully realized. We performed static and dynamic wetting diagnosis, visualization and characterization of fluid transport phenomena on the novel nanoengineered surfaces. The experiments were conducted using environmental scanning electron microscopy, high speed imaging in custom-built phase change chamber, high speed imaging with total internal reflection. 3. Objective 3 was fully realized. We have set up a testing facility for phase change heat transfer visualization, characterization, and wetting. We investigated evaporation, boiling, condensation and frosting phenomena on our novel nanoengineered surfaces, measured the critical heat flux (CHF) and the heat transfer coefficient (HTC) and established parametric studies in relation to the nucleation site density, bubble/drop distribution, bubble/drop departure volume, bubble/drop mobility, coalescence size, and surface coverage. 4. Objective 4 was realized based on single drop growth model and drop distribution obtained from experimental data. Using this model, we have predicted the critical features in boiling and condensation (e.g., nucleation) and the thermal performance for simple phase change phenomena with ideal assumptions. However, the model could be extended to more complex scenarios that accounts for bubble/drop coalescence and departure. Currently we are working on a more comprehensive model that could be used for the optimization of surface design and engineering. We will include more coupling effects into the model and perform experiments under more controllable conditions for setting up the correlation.

621110.label: Major findings and research outcome
621110.value: 1. We systematically investigated droplet dynamic wetting, evaporation and boiling on gradient surfaces and found that controlling surface roughness and wettability can be harnessed to precise manipulate liquid or vapor transport. We also developed theoretical models to predict directional motion of evaporating droplets and leidenfrost effect based on the excess free energy and the energy barrier (Applied Physics Letters 2011 2012, Physical Review Letters 2012). 2. We investigated the spontaneous motion of condensate drops on copper surfaces with various nanoribbons and chemical treatments. The results show that spontaneous mobility of condensate drops is related to the surface oxidation and fluorization extent. The enhanced mobility of condensate drops are attributed to two factors: depinning ability and Cassie state of condensate droplets, both of which are determined by the nanostructure morphology and local surface energy (Langmuir 2012, ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 2012). 3. We characterized condensate drop size and mobility, and dropwise condensation heat transfer on patterned nanostructured surfaces. Both microscopic and macroscopic experimental investigations elucidate dropwise condensation dynamics (nucleation, growth, and coalescence). One of the novel surface we developed that is composed of hierarchical (multiscale) nanograssed micropyramid architecture allows for 65% increase in the drop number density and 450% increase in the drop self-removal volume as compared to a superhydrophobic surface with nanostructures alone. Based on theoretical predications, the heat transfer coefficient is expected to enhance by 100-200% (Advanced Functional Materials 2011, Cover Article). 4. We also found the hierarchical morphology not only significantly suppresses the ice nucleation and inter-droplet freezing wave propagation in the condensation frosting process, but also promotes fast frost removal in the defrosting stage (Scientific Reports 2013).

621110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621110.value: Due to the funding and time limit, in the current project, we have not explored the phase change phenomena on the nanoengineered surfaces in a wide range of experimental conditions. The mutliscale modeling is also limited to certain cases with ideal assumptions. For future work, 1. We need to build a testing chamber that can provide more precise and stable control of stage and chamber temperature, partial pressure of the liquid of interest, so that we can expand our experimental capability for the visualization and characterization of phase change phenomena and thermal properties. 2. We will extend our current theoretical model that is based on single drop growth model and drop distribution to more complex scenarios including drop coalescence and departure, and more complex surfaces with hierarchical structures and heterogeneous wettability. 3. We will also explore the coupling of active force such as electric field or acoustic field to the phase change to provide better controllability for fluid manipulation and thermal transport phenomena.

621110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621110.value: The miniaturization of electronic devices demands novel thermal management techniques to efficiently dissipate heat over a small area. Two-phase heat transfer devices such as heat pipes that utilize phase change between an evaporator and a condenser offer superior cooling strategies. In this project, using nanofabrication technology and surface treatment, we have developed bio-inspired nanoengineered surfaces on silicon and copper substrates to control fluid wetting and spreading, nucleation, growth, and departure involved in several phase change phenomena such as evaporation, boiling, condensation, and icing. A combined research through experimental investigation and theoretical modelling provide us the insight of the enhanced interfacial transport and heat transfer mechanism on the micro/nano structured surfaces. The insights learned in this study, especially the elucidation of the role of surface roughness and wettability on fluid spreading and phase change, can further stimulate new theoretical and experimental efforts to probe complex multiphase phenomena. Exploiting multiscale coupling effects will open up novel and exciting vistas in the development of high performance nanomaterials for applications such as electronics cooling, power generation, water desalination, and water harvesting systems.

621310.value: 集成標籤信息的協同推薦系統：一種貝葉斯關係學習方法

621310.label: Project Objectives

To apply the Bayesian relational learning models to collaborative recommendation applications that incorporate social annotations in the form of tagging information and to deliver competitive experimental results with publicly available benchmark data sets.

621310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621310.value: 在萬維網發展的第一個十年，搜索引擎扮演了至關重要的角色。它們允許網絡用戶顯式地搜索他們需要的信息。在使用搜索引擎的時候，一般由用戶來啟動搜索過程：用戶通常會對他們所想要找的信息有一些先驗知識，然後用一些與先驗知識相關的關鍵詞來啟動搜索。由於萬維網上的信息的數量和複雜度均以一種令人震驚的速度在增長，所以搜索引擎自身並不足以幫助用戶找到他們感興趣的信息。近些年來，推薦系統被廣泛使用，並在萬維網搜索中扮演著越來越重要的角色。與需要用戶顯式地搜索感興趣的信息的搜索引擎不同，推薦系統改變了用戶和信息之間關係的方向，使得搜索模式發生了轉變，即以一種非常個性化的方式把信息推薦給合適的用戶。 推薦系統主要分為兩類，基於內容的推薦系統和基於協同過濾的推薦系統。協同過濾系統又可以被進一步分為基於記憶的系統和基於模型的系統兩種。為了進一步改善推薦系統的效用，我們提出研究將一種新的信息源更緊密地集成到推薦系統中。這種新的信息源就是協同標籤，一種在Web2.0持續發展中越來越流行的概念。鑑於基於模型的協同過濾系統被廣泛應用，我們提出將標籤信息集成到其中來產生協同推薦，並將其潛在的機器學習問題形式化為貝葉斯框架下的新的統計關係學習問題。貝葉斯方法不僅非常適合這個計分和標籤信息都非常稀疏的問題，還有效地提供了一個便於進行模型選擇和模型學習的一致的、準確無誤的框架。我們針對關係學習提出了新的層次化貝葉斯模型，這些模型同時具備參數化模型和非參數化模型的特點並且非常靈活、易於解釋和易於擴展。我們將這些模型應用在集成標籤信息的協同推薦系統中，並將在公開的基準數據集上展示該模型的效用。

621310.label: Realisation of objectives
621310.value: We have successfully achieved the project objectives as stated in the project proposal. Specifically, on the first objective, we have developed some novel machine learning models, mostly probabilistic graphical models, to address a range of research issues that often arise when exploiting relational information of various forms. These issues include structured representation of relational information, model and data sparsity, representation and incorporation of prior information, scalability, and latent representation. The graphical model approach also makes the models quite interpretable and flexible for extension. On the second objective, we have conducted extensive empirical studies on collaborative recommendation as well as related applications that involve social interactions. For most empirical studies we have conducted, we make use of publicly available benchmark data sets and compare our proposed models with the state-of-the-art methods. Improvement is often observed in terms of either computational efficiency or prediction accuracy, or even both.

621310.label: Major findings and research outcome
621310.value: This project has led to publications in very respectable venues of several research areas, including machine learning (1 in ICML, 2 in NIPS, 1 in ECMLPKDD), data mining (2 in KDD, 2 in TKDD), artificial intelligence (5 in AAAI, 3 in IJCAI), and computer vision (2 in ICCV, 1 in ECCV). Moreover, for most of these papers, we have made the software implementations of the proposed methods publicly available to facilitate extended work by other researchers and practitioners. To reflect on our project experience, we have found that the promising performance obtained by the proposed models can be attributed to several respects. Of primary importance is to design probabilistic graphical models that can represent the relationships between multiple sources of information effectively in a Bayesian framework on which principled inference algorithms can be developed. This approach is pervasive in many of our papers, particularly in [C1, C2, C5, C7, C11, C16, C17, J1, J2]. Moreover, we have found that it is very important to explicitly deal with sparsity in both the model and the data. The probabilistic graphical model approach adopted by us makes it particularly convenient to design the models appropriately to address the sparsity issue, such as imposing some sparsity-inducing priors under the Bayesian framework. This idea has been exploited in several papers, including [C3, C4, C8, C10, C12, C13, C16, C17].

621310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621310.value: Although the primary focus of this project is on developing novel machine learning models for collaboration recommendation applications, we have noticed that some ideas arisen from the models developed are also applicable to a few applications beyond collaboration recommendation. One of these applications that we have started to extend the ideas is peer grading in massive open online courses (MOOCs), as reported in [C16]. In a typical peer grading setting, each user plays the dual roles of a grader as well as a student. By taking the assumption that a high-performing student is likely to be a competent grader, this subtle relationship can be exploited in a probabilistic graphical model for aggregating the peer grades from multiple peer graders to obtain a more accurate estimate of the true grade of a student. We will continue along this line of research. Another application that can benefit from the ideas developed is visual tracking, which seeks to track the motion of an object as it moves in a video sequence, as reported in [C14, C15]. The subtle connection to visual tracking lies in the fact that many state-of-the-art object trackers regard the online tracking process as an online Bayesian model updating procedure. We have started to address the issue of how to learn a more powerful yet compact latent representation that can be used as the state representation in a state-space model underlying visual tracking.

621310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621310.value: With information explosion on the Web, a key challenge is to bridge the gap between the users and the Web content that they are potentially interested in. Recommender systems have been playing an increasingly important role in helping to address this challenge. This project seeks to develop principled machine learning models that can flexibly incorporate additional sources of information to improve the recommendation accuracy. Specifically, under a probabilistic framework, relational information is incorporated and efficient learning and inference algorithms are developed. We have conducted extensive empirical studies to compare the proposed models with the state of the art based on some publicly available benchmark data sets. Besides collaborative recommendation applications, we have noticed that some ideas from the proposed models are also applicable to a few other applications. We are currently pursuing research to extend the ideas to these new areas.

621510.value: 由大气气溶胶中类腐殖质物质引起的活性氧的产生

621510.label: Project Objectives
621510.value: To quantify ROS production of HULIS from biomass burning particles, polluted urban aerosols, and rural aerosols. To characterize quinone content, a known redox active moiety, in HULIS of various sources. To investigate factors that influence ROS-production in the presence of HULIS.

621510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621510.value: HUmic-LIke Substances (HULIS) have recently been recognized to be an important class of organic compounds in atmospheric particulate matter (PM). HULIS derive the name from their similarities to terrestrial and aquatic humic and fulvic acids in spectroscopic properties. However, their sources and molecular compositions are different from humic substances in aquatic environments and much less understood. Soil-derived humic substance (HS) have been shown to be redox-active substances, but the redox chemistry of HULIS has been little studied. Redox of HULIS could be linked to reactive oxygen species (ROS). PM-mediated ROS generation has been identified to be an important cause for health effects posed by PM. We propose to characterize in vitro ROS production mediated by HULIS of different origins, including biomass burning-derived PM and rural and urban ambient PM. Known redox-active key factors such as the quinone content in HULIS and transition metal concentrations will be quantified in the selected source and ambient PM samples to study their effects on the redox activity of HULIS. Results from this study will provide insights into the underlying cause for the health effects of PM and in turn help to identify PM sources the control of which could provide maximum health benefits. 类腐殖质物质（HULIS）最近被公认为是大气颗粒物中重要的一类有机化合物。 HULIS的名称来自于与陆地和水生腐殖酸和富里酸有相似的光谱性质。不过，其来源和分子组成和水生环境中的腐植质物质不同，我们对其的了解很有限。土源性的腐植物质已被证明是氧化还原活性物质，但HULIS氧化还原的化学还没有被研究过。HULIS的氧化还原可能与活性氧（ROS）的产生有关，另一方面，由大气颗粒物产生的活性氧已被确定为是一个大气颗粒物造成健康影响的重要原因。 我们准备在此研究计划里对不同来源HULIS导致的体外活性氧的产生进行表征，将会考虑从生物质燃烧产生的HULIS，及在农村和城市大气环境中的HULIS。已知的具氧化还原活性的关键成分，例如在HULIS里的醌官能团的含量和过渡金属的含量，将会被定量并研究他们对HULIS的氧化还原活性的影响。这项研究结果将会帮助我们了解大气颗粒物对健康的影响的内在原因，从而帮助确定控制大气颗粒物的哪些源可以达到最大的健康效益。

621510.label: Realisation of objectives
621510.value: Objective 1: Humic-like substances (HULIS) are an unresolved mixture of water-extracted organic compounds from atmospheric aerosol particles. Ambient samples were collected on filters from different types of atmospheric environments (e.g., roadside, urban, suburban, rural). Biomass combustion samples were collected through field burning or obtained from collaborators who collected through their laboratory burning facilities. This wide range of HULIS samples provides experiment materials covering the compositional diversity of atmospheric HULIS for subsequent study of redox properties of HULIS in generating ROS. In this project, we used a cell-free dithiothreitol (DTT) assay to measure ROS production mediated by HULIS. ROS activities by residue metal ions in the HULIS fraction are suppressed by including a strong chelating agent in the DTT assay. The first objective was fully achieved and the related results have been described in Lin and Yu (2011) and reported in two conference presentations. Objective 2: The HULIS samples were characterized using electrospray ionization (ESI) coupled with ultra-high resolution mass spectrometry (UHRMS). The access to this instrument was made possible through our collaboration with Prof. Markus Kalberer at the University of Cambridge. With the remarkable resolving power and mass accuracy of UHRMS, thousands of elemental formulas were identified, including quinone compounds (Lin, Rincon, Kalberer, and Yu, 2012). The UHRMS approach is analytically more powerful than the originally proposed NMR approach in resolving molecular composition of complex organic mixtures. Objective 3: The molecular composition information obtained from UHRMS analysis allows us to hypothesize potential compound classes (based on functional groups) that could influence ROS activities of HULIS. Nitrogen-containing organic bases (e.g., imidazole and its derivatives) have been identified through this approach and found to enhance ROS activities of model quinone compounds as well as ambient and source HULIS (Dou, Lin, Kuang, and Yu, 2014). The impact of HULIS-metal interactions on ROS production was examined by carrying out DTT assays with their separate solutions and mixtures, and also their mixtures in the absence and presence of a metal chelating agent (Lin and Yu, 2011).

621510.label: Major findings and research outcome
621510.value: Through this research, we have revealed that humic-like substances (HULIS) are the major redox active constituents of the water-extractable organic fraction in ambient particulate matter (PM). The ROS activity of the ambient HULIS from rural and suburban atmospheres, on a per unit mass basis, is 2% of the ROS activity by a reference quinone compound, 1,4-naphthoquinone and exceeds that of two aquatic fulvic acids. The ambient HULIS fraction in the ambient samples tested exhibits comparable ROS activities to the organic solvent extractable fraction, which would contain compounds such as quinones, a known organic compound class capable of catalyzing generation of ROS in cells (Lin and Yu, 2011). UHRMS coupled with soft ionization techniques such as electrospray ionization (ESI) allows characterization of complex organic mixtures such as HULIS at the molecular level due to the extremely high resolution and mass accuracy. The application of ESI-UHRMS has led to significant progress in identifying molecular information about HULIS. The identified elemental formulas are a few thousands in number and classified into seven major compound categories, including CHONS-, CHOS-, CHON+, CHON-, CHO+, CHO-, and CHN+ compounds (Lin, Rincon, Kalberer, and Yu, 2012). Among them, organosulfates (i.e., CHONS- and CHOS- formulas) had prominent presence in ESI- spectra and were examined in details. The analysis reveals that biogenic volatile organic compounds are the dominant precursors for organosulfates (Lin, Yu, Engling, Kalberer, 2012). Similar chemical compositional and source information provides valuable basic knowledge for studies of the redox properties of HULIS. Reduced organic nitrogen compounds, such as alkaloids resulting from biomass burning emissions, are found through UHRMS analysis to be among HULIS constituents. We examined the redox activities of pyridine, imidazole and their alkyl derivatives (i.e., 3-methoxypyridine, 4-methylimidazole, 2-methylimidazole, and 2,4-dimethylimidazole) using DTT assay under simulated physiological conditions. These compounds were found to not have redox activity on their own as measured by the DTT assay, but they enhanced ROS generation catalyzed by 1,4-naphthoquinone (as a model quinone compound) and HULIS isolated from multiple aerosol samples. The enhancement effect by the individual nitrogen-containing bases was determined to be proportional to their amount in the assay solutions. It is postulated that the underlying mechanism involves the unprotonated N atom acting as a H-bonding acceptor to facilitate hydrogen-atom transfer in the ROS generation cycle (Dou, Lin, Kuang, and Yu, 2014). We are the first to discover this enhancement effect and suggest the underlying mechanism.

621510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621510.value: This research can be further developed on two fronts. First, the organic compound groups revealed by UHRMS analysis could be scrutinized in related to the newly identified mechanism through forming H-bonding in influencing ROS production. A systematic testing of homologues could be explored to obtain quantitative structure-ROS activities relationships. Second, this research has revealed organic nitrogen-containing bases participate in processes leading to health effects by PM and as such, the quantification of their abundance in atmospheric PM and identification of major sources are worthy work to pursue.

621510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621510.value: Ambient particulate matter (PM) is an important air pollutant known to cause adverse health effects in humans. One of the major toxicological mechanisms is through the induction of oxidative stress derived from PM-mediated generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in cells. Among the numerous constituents of PM, metals and quinoid compounds have been previously established as capable of catalyzing ROS generation in cells, but the knowledge on the range of organic chemical species in PM responsible for ROS generation is very inadequate. Through this project, we found that humic-like substances (HULIS), a complex mixture of water-extractable amphiphilic organic compounds having structural similarities to terrestrial and aquatic humic substances (HS), are major redox-active components in ambient PM. Chemical composition data obtained through ultra-high resolution mass spectrometric analysis have made possible to explore the impact of specific components of HULIS on ROS formation. One such example is the discovery that nitrogen-containing bases, a class of constituent compounds of HULIS and redox inactive on their own, would enhance ROS generation catalyzed by quinones and HULIS. A derived finding from this discovery is that ROS activities of atmospheric PM as a mixture is not simply the sum of ROS activities from individual redox-active constituents.

621810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621810.value: Electrically conductive adhesives (ECAs) are widely used in the electronics industry for applications such as interconnects for integrated circuits, displays, and antenna for radio frequency devices. Silver, which has a superior electrical conductivity, is commonly used as the filler material in ECAs to articulate the electronic flow network. In typical commercial ECAs, silver fillers of up to 75% weight are used to facilitate the building of the conduction path. Recent research of the Principal Investigator has demonstrated that iodine treated silver flakes can substantially reduce the silver content in ECAs to about 27.5 wt% while maintaining an electrical conductivity to a comparable level as commercial counterparts. As silver is the main cost driver in ECAs, this will significantly reduce the cost of an ECA by at least 50%. While the experimental results are highly repeatable, the mechanism behind the conductivity improvement remains obscure. Initial investigation shows that the conductivity improvement is due to the formation of nonstoichiometric Ag/AgI nanostructures on the silver surface which induce a redox reaction inhibiting the formation of silver oxide on the silver flake surface. This enhances contact resistance between the silver fillers and hence improves the overall conductance of the ECA. The proposed investigation is three folded. The first task is to evaluate the iodination process on silver surface, which includes studying the formation and evolution of Ag/AgI nanostructures on silver flakes surface using a range of analytical techniques such as optical analysis, scanning probe and electron microscopy, and surface analysis. This helps to understand the transportation and coalescence process inside the Ag/AgI nanostructures. The second task is to understand the redox reaction process of Ag/AgI nanostructures and its effect on silver oxide formation on the silver surface. The redox reaction at different stages of Ag/AgI nanostructures evolution will be studied using cyclic voltammetry and TOF-SIMS. The focus is to understand the inhibition of oxide formation on silver surface. The third task is to study the conduction path formation during curing of ECAs by evaluating the electrical resistivity of iodine treated silver flakes under different treatment conditions using conductive AFM measurement. The resistivity of ECAs using silver fillers with different iodine treatment conditions will be measured. This proposed study will provide a key understanding to a new reported phenomenon on the effect of formation of nonstoichiometric Ag/AgI nanostructures and its red-ox effect on the conductivity of metal-based, in this case silver-based, ECAs. 導電膠（ECAs）被廣泛應用於電子行業，如集成電路連線，顯示器和無線電天線變頻裝置。銀具有優越的導電性，常用為導電膠填充料以加強導電。業界常用的導電膠，為促進導電，銀填充物含量高達重量 75％。本研究員最近研究成果已證明再用經碘處理銀片可大大減少導電膠的銀含量至 27.5％，而仍可維持導電率在正常運作水平。 由於銀主導導電膠的成本，碘處理銀片將大大降低導電膠成本50％。 雖然實驗結果具有高度重複性，碘處理銀片改善導電的機制仍未清盺。初步調查顯示導電率改善是由於銀表面形成非化學計量的銀/碘化銀納米結構，導致氧化還原反應，抑制銀片表面形成氧化銀。這減少銀片之間的接觸電阻，從而提高填充料整體導電率。 這研究有三大方向。第一項任務是評估銀表面碘化銀的過程，其中包括使用分析方法如 光學分析，掃描探針和電子顯微鏡和表面分析，研究銀片表面上納米銀 /碘化銀的形成和演化範圍分析技術。這有助於了解在銀 /碘化銀納米結構內部的運輸和合併過程。 第二項任務是了解銀 /碘化銀納米結構氧化還原反應過程及其對銀表面上形成氧化銀的影響。氧化還原反應。對不同階段的銀 /碘化銀納米結構的演變，將採用循環伏安法和TOF - SIMS進行研究。重點是了解抑制在銀表面形成氧化銀的成因。 第三項任務是使用導電原子力顯微鏡測量評估在導電膠固化過程中，不同碘處理銀片條件對電傳導路徑形成及電阻率的影響。測量使用不同碘處理銀片導電膠的電阻率。 這個研究將對新發現的非化學計量銀 /碘化銀納米結構的形成和它的碘化銀納米結構氧化還原反應對金屬銀導電膠的電導率提供 關鍵的認識。

621810.label: Realisation of objectives
621810.value: The critical component in the Ag/AgI nanostructures is found to be actually the metal iodide specie (AgI). To achieve this, we simply added AgI into the ECAs instead of doing silver particle iodine treatment. The AgI-treated ECA with 0.7 wt% of AgI crystal has a resistivity of only around 9.5E-5 Ω·cm, which is close to the iodine treated ECAs and also 2 magnitudes lower than the ECAs without treatment. Those results reveal that AgI has the similar effect to iodine treatment on electrical conductivity of ECAs. Furthermore, we extended from AgI to other metal halides or halide compounds, such as KI, CuI, HI, and etc. It is found that those halide species played the role in the conductivity enhancement of the ECAs. With the addition of AgI or iodine treatment, the dynamic percolation curve of the ECAs has a simple exponential decrease of resistance at the very beginning of the isothermal curing (10 s), and reaches rapidly down to the equilibrium value. However, the percolation curves conventional ECAs are relatively complicated, featuring with a two-step growth mode: the first step occurs in the early curing stage and the percolation conductance grew slightly (only by 102 times); the major percolation conductance grew at the following second step, where the percolation conductance typically increased by 104–105 times. The ultra-fast percolation network growth rate from AgI affects the apparent percolation conductivity under the traditional packaging conditions allows ultrahigh efficiency in reaching the volume fraction limiting percolation conductance. Since metal iodide easily reacted with imidazole compound to form imidazolium salts, we simply replaced the common midazole compound with abn imidazolum salts. It is found the ECAs with imidazolum salts as catalyst can percolate with an ultrafast rate comparable to the iodine treated ECAs. Furthermore, by directly extending the polymer matrix from epoxy to silicone rubber system, where immidazolum salts didn’t show any catalytic effect on the polymer matrix, we found that only immidazolum salts can also percolate silver-matrix systems other than epoxy resin. It reveals that the immidazolium salt enhanced the dynamic percolation rate by directly changing the formation of conductive pathways, rather than through the synergistically effect brought by chemical induced polymer curing process

621810.label: Major findings and research outcome
621810.value: The major findings of the project included: (1) We are the first to figure out that there are two different dynamic percolation mechanisms in the percolation of ECAs, i.e., the reaction-limited percolation and physical aging-induced percolation, through our systematically dynamic percolation study. It is understood that the conventional conductive composite has a very low physical aging percolation rate which greatly limits in achieving the high conductivity. By achieving reaction-induced percolation, we can enhance the percolation rate by more than one-magnitude higher and thus the percolation conductivity of the ECAs by more than 2~3 orders of magnitude. We have published those results in Applied Physics Letter. (2) We greatly expanded the applicability of iodine treatment technique in enhancing the percolation conductivity of ECAs, from epoxy to more generic polymer to make the conductive composite, by using immidazolum salts which is intrinsically a room-temperature ionic liquid as the percolation promoter. We further proposed an interlayer phase model to illustrate the difference between the reaction-limited percolation and physical aging-induced percolation. Those results have been published in RSC Advances. (3) We found that the percolation control in the ECAs can not only enhance the electrical conductivity of the ECAs, but also greatly improve their thermal conductivity. Through the percolation control from iodine treatment, we can achieve the 300% enhancement of thermal conductivity with a silver filler loading of 75 wt%. It implies that the iodine treatment and the related revised techniques can be potentially a generic method to control the percolation properties of many other composite systems, such as thermal, thermal-mechanical, dielectric materials, and etc. Some parts of those results were published in Applied Physics Letter.

621810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621810.value: (a) Understand of other conducting material as fillers for ECA. The study has been extended to silver nanowire and graphene as a filler material for ECAs. Silver nanowire has an advantage of forming better pathways. Graphene is an evolving filler material that is much cheaper and lighter than silver. (b) Understand the dynamic behavior of ionic liquid played in changing the dynamic percolation process of the ECAs. There are two courses of action: the directly imaging of filler network formation and evolution brought by the ionic liquid; and the direct correlation between the filler network formation dynamics with the conductive percolation kinetics. The combined use of optical imaging, scanning electron microscopy and X-ray imaging technique plus filler network analysis supported by fractal percolation theory will help in the understanding. (c) Understand the mechanism of ionic liquid played in making the percolation fill network. The critical course of action is to use particle fractal network formation mechanism to investigate the crucial roles of ionic liquid, for example, the interaction force fields brought by the ionic liquid (electrostatic interactions, van der Waals force, hydrodynamic force, etc.). This would lead to the development of more in-depth understanding to percolation control in ECAs.

621810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621810.value: The use of electrically conductive adhesives (ECAs) is widespread in the fabrication of electronic devices. The project is able to provide a deeper understanding on the chemical effect of iodine and immidazolum salts on the conductivity of ECAs. The project also results in a very detailed understanding of the percolation of filler particles in the formation of the conductive pathway in ECAs which requires to the fillers in the pathway to be packed closer than a threshold defined by the tunneling distance. The electrons thus have a high probability to migrate across the fillers facilitating electronic flow. The improvement of electrically conductivity of ECAs is therefore rest on formulating approaches to build such pathway using and combined chemical and mechanical methods. These approaches will be studied in a newly funded GRF project. Percolation is key in control material properties of a composite. Deep scientific understanding in the mechanism control percolation will design and fine-tune composite material properties which will produce a far-reaching effect. Better percolation control will also enable cost reduction in composites as the percentage filler content can be lowered. Application of percolation control extends beyond composite and can be adopted in mixing processes to enhance product performance.
