640410.label: Major findings and research outcome
640410.value: Our study has been accepted by Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, which is one of the top four finance journals. Our main findings include the following. First, consistent with prior studies, after an extensive data collection process, we document that more than 40% of S&P1500 firms are still controlled or managed their founding family shareholders. Next, we show that family and non-family firms in the S&P 1500 differ in their debt maturity and leverage ratios in a manner consistent with the higher expropriation potential of family firms. That is, relatively to non-family firms, family firms reply more on debt financing and they have shorter debt maturity. Moreover, while more transparency causes both family and non-family firms to increase the maturity structure of their debt and reduce leverage ratios, the effects are stronger for family firms. This findings suggests that corporate transparency helps minority (or external) shareholders to monitor family shareholders to mitigate the expropriation risks, and it also enables family firms to reduce the reliance of debt financing and to lengthen the debt maturity. Finally, we also prove that family ownership has incremental effects over typical managerial ownership on corporate transparency and capital structure, suggesting family ownership to be a unique class of blockholders. To conclude, our study has successfully achieved the objevtives stated in the proposal, and the contribtuion has been acknowledged by the referee and the editor during the review process.

640410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
640410.value: We generate some new insights from the research process. Specifically, we realize that there is very limited evidence on how family ownership affects financial firms' information environment. This could be due to the fact that financial firms have very different financial reports from their manufacturing counterparts, so they are found to be difficult to be valued. Based on the preliminary search of banking industry, we find that founding family ownership is not scarce in the financial industry. As such, we plan to do a more comprehensive data collection on family ownership in the banking industry and see whether it can be turned into a meaningful study.

640410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
640410.value: Our study makes the following contributions. First, while various characteristics of family firms have been studied by prior literature, there is little evidence on the association between family ownership and capital structure. Therefore our findings that family firms in the U.S. have shorter debt maturity structures and lower leverage than non-family firms expand existing literature on family firms. In particular, the results seem to suggest family firms are subject to more severe agency problems arising from the conflicts between outside investors and inside controlling shareholders. Second, our paper adds to the literature linking costly external finance to the potential for expropriation of minority shareholders by corporate insiders when control rights and ownership rights diverge, and how this relationship is affected by the opacity of the information environment. Specifically, we show that transparency has larger effects on debt maturity and leverage for family firms as compared to non-family firms, suggesting that the information environment matters more for a company’s financing choice when the potential for conflicts of interest between insiders and outsiders is greater.

640610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640610.value: Our proposed study plans to examine the impacts of simultaneous ownership of different securities of the same company. Holding different securities gives investors multiple claims on the same underlying asset, and this special form of ownership may influence efficiency at the firm level. We focus on the dual holdings of convertible bonds and stocks by hedge funds. Convertible bonds are hybrid securities: they are bonds that can be converted into stocks at the discretion of the holder. As such, a convertible bond is similar to a straight bond plus a warrant (or call option), which provides equity-like payoff when converted. One motivation for investors to hold convertible bonds and stocks at the same time is that they have positive information about the company, and the information is not incorporated into asset prices. We think this motivation is particularly relevant for firms that have convertible bonds, as these bonds are documented to be underpriced within the first few months of issuance. Therefore, buying convertible bonds is a cheap way for existing shareholders to obtain more shares. Investors’ purchases will bid up convertible bond prices, and if asset markets are not perfectly segmented, stock prices may increase also. We will analyze this “information spillover” from one market to the other. This spillover provides a mechanism by which prices in different asset markets remain informationally efficient. Another form of efficiency improvements is the potential mitigation of agency problems that result from leverage in the capital structure. Researchers have shown that there is a conflict between shareholders and bondholders. While shareholders have incentives to increase firm risk to get higher returns, bondholders want to decrease firm risk to minimize the probability of default. By holding both convertible bonds and stocks, investors can protect their bond positions with their equity stake and voting power, reducing the agency conflicts. A related research question is whether the issuance of convertible bonds could also help mitigate agency problems. If shareholders increase equity value at the expense of bondholders, convertible bond investors can convert their stakes into stock. We will study if convertible bond issuance decision, proceeds raised in the market, and pricing are related to agency conflicts. 我們所提出的計劃將會研究投資者同時擁有一家公司的不同證券所帶來的影響。擁有不同證券讓投資者持有對相同基礎資產的多個不同權益，而這種特殊形式的擁有權可能影響企業層面之效率。 我們專注研究對沖基金的可換股債券和股票的雙擁有權。可換股債券是混合型證券：持有人可自由選擇把債券轉換為股票。因此，可換股債券類似普通債券加上認股權證（或認購期權），在轉換後它提供跟股票一樣的收益。投資者同一時間持有可換股債券和股票的其中一個動機是他們對公司有積極的信息，而這信息並不納入資產價格。我們認為這動機是對那些有可換股債券的企業尤其有關，因為文獻指出這些債券的價格在發行的頭幾個月內都是偏低。因此，購買可換股債券是一種能令現有股東以廉價獲得更多股份的方式。投資者的購買將可換股債券價格抬高，如果資產市場不是完全分割的話，股票價格也可能會隨之上升。我們會分析這種從一個市場到另一個的“信息溢出”。這溢出提供了一種機制，讓不同的資產市場價格保持信息上有效。 另一種可能提高效率的形式是緩解資本結構之槓桿所衍生的代理問題。研究人員發現股東和債權人之間存有衝突。一方面股東想藉著增加公司的風險以獲得更高的回報，但另一方面債權人希望降低公司的風險去減少違約的機會。通過同時持有可換股債券和股票，債券投資者可憑股權和投票權保護他們的債權，以減少代理衝突。 一個相關的研究問題是發行可換股債券能否有助減輕代理衝突。當股東犠牲債權人利益去增加自己利益時，可換股債券投資者可以把債券轉換成股票。我們會研究可換股債券的發行、市場上所募集的資金和價格是否與代理衝突有關。

640610.label: Major findings and research outcome
640610.value: We study managers who manage multiple mutual funds. Consistent with the idea that investors infer ability from past returns, flows into a fund are predicted by the past performance in another fund the multi-fund manager manages. The explanatory power of the other fund is stronger when it performed particularly well, when the two funds have similar styles, and when the manager has started managing a fund recently. Nonetheless, past performance in one fund predicts subsequent performance in the other. It is likely due to some investors' insufficient withdrawal of capital from a fund when the other fund performed poorly.

640610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
640610.value: We plan to publish the paper in a top journal. We are now improving the paper based on referees' comments.

640610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
640610.value: Our paper contributes to the understanding of performance-chasing behavior in mutual funds that has attracted enormous attention among academics. Using the unique setting of multi-fund managers, we document results that help distinguish between rational and behavioral explanations. Flow is more sensitive to past performance in the other fund when it is more informative, and we show evidence that the other fund is relevant because skills are transferable between funds. Our findings are consistent with investor sophistication, under which investors infer managerial ability from past returns; behavioral biases are unlikely the cause of such results. Nevertheless, contrary to the prediction by theory models such as Berk and Green (2004), we believe that capital flows do not respond enough to a manager's overall performance. We conclude that investors are generally sophisticated, but may not be up to the level that theory models require.

640910.label: Project Objectives
640910.value: Establish two consumption-based mechanisms for coping with self-esteem threat: product-based and priced-based coping. Predict and test among which consumers and in which consumption contexts each coping strategy will be adopted by invoking the construct product self-relevance. Establish construct validity and robustness of the effects using both situational and individual difference operationalizations of self-relevance. Establish self-esteem repair, i.e., the circumstances wherein trading up or not can either assuage a temporary blow to self-esteem or perpetuate low self-esteem. We predict self-esteem is repaired by trading up (or not) on a product high (low) on self-relevance. Establish self-esteem protection, i.e., establish that possessions can protect self-esteem against otherwise threatening events, thereby mitigating the effect of threat on trading up. Uncover boundary conditions regarding the types of possessions that can serve this self-protective function, and cultural differences between Asians and Westerners that could moderate the extent to which self-esteem is protected by possessions. We also examine the role of conscious awareness and incorporate everyday usage situations. Shed light on the substantive phenomenon of trading up by empirically establishing in which situations and among which consumers self-esteem threat causes trading up or trading down.

640910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640910.value: This proposed research will delve into two broad and inter-related questions: How does self-esteem affect consumption? And, how does consumption, in turn, affect self-esteem? We propose first to explore how events that threaten self-esteem affect spending and the psychological processes mediating this effect. Prior consumer research suggests that people cope with self-esteem threat by behaving more materialistically (Chaplin & John 2007; Kasser 2002; Rindfleisch,Burrows, & Wong 2009). We draw on a rich literature in psychology indicating that self-esteem maintenance is a flexible, adaptive process (e.g., Tesser, Martin, & Cornell, 1996) to posit that consumption-based coping strategies are more diverse than previous findings suggest. We propose two such strategies:(1) acquiring a high-quality product and (2) getting a good deal. Which of these strategies consumers adopt, we argue, should depend on consumers' perceptions of the consumption context at hand. We will focus on one key feature of a consumption context: product category self-relevance. That is, is the consumer making a spending decision in a product category typically used to convey the consumer's self-concept? We posit that threatened consumers shopping in a product category high (versus low) on self-relevance will adopt a quality-focused (versus price-focused) coping strategy. Prior research has highlighted that threatened consumers spend more, but we suggest that threatened consumers spend more in certain consumption contexts and less in others. We also propose to explore when and how consumption can benefit self-esteem. One proposed benefit is self-esteem repair. We will examine circumstances in which quality-focused and price-focused coping can immediately assuage a temporary blow to self-esteem. Another proposed benefit is self-esteem protection. Several experiments will examine moderators, including product importance and culture, to delineate circumstances in which consumers’ possessions become resources that make self-esteem hardy and not easily threatened. By relying on possessions as coping resources, the impact of threat on consumption should be attenuated. Theoretically, we aim to build a richer framework for understanding how consumption is used to cope with self-esteem threat, and how consumption can benefit self-esteem. Substantively, this research should highlight why consumers are willing to pay premium prices for goods and services in some categories and under some circumstances but not others. From a social welfare perspective, this research promises insights into when and why possessions can insulate self-worth and reduce reliance on consumption as a coping strategy. 這論文計畫書主要探討兩項廣泛但互相影響的問題：(一) 消費對自尊的影響 (二) 自尊對消費的影響。首先，研究將探討傷害自尊的情況如何影響個人消費模式和引發這效果的心理過程。過往消費者研究發現， 人們在自尊被受傷害時，會較傾 向於物質主義性的行為 (Chaplin & John 2007; Kasser 2002; Rindfleisch, Burrows, & Wong 2009)。相關的研究也表明，自尊的維護是一個靈活的適應過程 (e.g., Tesser, Martin, & Cornell, 1996)。根據上述的研究觀點，本研究假定，以消費為基礎的應對策略比以前的更多樣化，並提出兩項應對策略：﹝一﹞ 獲得高品質的產品和 ﹝二﹞獲得一個很好的協議。消費者對消費情況的掌握會影響他採取何種策略。是次，我們集中研究消費情況的關鍵元素：產品類別與個人的相關性。消費者在決定選擇產品類別的同時，也是否在建立和定義其自我概念？我們假設，選擇自我相關性高﹝低﹞的產品類別，而同時自尊又感到受威脅的消費者會採取以質量 ﹝價格﹞為中心的對應策略。縱然過往的研究清楚列明自尊感到受威脅的消費者會花費更多，我們卻認為感到他們會因應不同的消費環境而花費更多或更少。 其次，我們將探討消費在何時及如何能對自尊心有正面的影響，其一：如自尊心的修補。我們研究在什麼情況下以質量 (價格)為中心的對應策略能立即緩解對自尊的打擊。其二：如自尊心的保護。過往一些實驗曾指出某些調節變項，如產品的重要性和文化，可以令到擁有該產品的消費者鞏固其自尊心及不易受打擊。消費者把產品擁有權轉化成鞏固自尊心的方法，會減低對其消費的威脅。 本研究的目的是建立一個更完善的理論框架以探討消費如何處理自尊的威脅，和消費對自尊的良好影響。實際上，本研究強調為何消費者在某些情況下願意支付高價商品和服務。在社會福利角度上，本研究也有助了解消費在何時及如何隔離自我價值和減少對零售療法的依賴。

640910.label: Major findings and research outcome
640910.value: The JCR publication that finds support for objective 3 is a series of laboratory experiments that document a phenomenon called motivated forgetting. We draw on research on social identity and psychological threat-based coping to develop a framework that predicts when motivated forgetting occurs, which memories are forgotten, and who is motivated to forget. The framework links motivated forgetting to social identity threat (e.g., negative feedback regarding one’s gender, age, nationality, or race). People cope with social identity threat by suppressing content they associate to the threat, which can include content that is not inherently threatening, like identity-linked sales promotions. The motivation to forget identity-linked promotions depends on one’s sense of connection to the threatened social identity, with strong identifiers forgetting the most. Motivated forgetting does not imply that identity-linked content is truly lost from memory; the content is simply not explicitly retrieved as a defensive response to threat. Accordingly, identity-linked content remains implicitly accessible in the face of threat, and can be explicitly retrieved if a threatened social identity is affirmed, thereby mitigating threat. Finally, motivated forgetting is most successful when the process unfolds nondeliberately. Deliberate attempts to forget threatening memories can backfire because people are prone to accidentally retrieve content that is accessible implicitly, even if not accessible explicitly.

640910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
640910.value: I am working on a direct extension (also relevant to objective 3) with my coauthor (who is a PhD student but left HKUST for a different institution) and another faculty member. This paper explores in more detail some of the effects that were found in the published paper. This extension is about to be submitted for a third round review at JCR (the same journal as the original publication) I am currently writing a manuscript that details evidence for objectives 1 and 4. Lastly, I am in the early stages of a new project on this topic of motivated forgetting. A different PhD student has approached me about the applicability of this phenomenon to dieting goals and we've collected a bit of data that look promising.

640910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
640910.value: Sigmund Freud (1915, Repression) proposed that people can repress, or forget, unwanted memories. Despite its intrigue, this theory has faced numerous challenges. First, Freud’s theory is difficult to test. Second, existing evidence suggests that people dwell on unwanted memories and show good memory for negative events, rather than forgetting negative memories the theory claims. Our paper deals with both types of challenges. In sum, this research identifies situations in which motivated forgetting is likely to occur (i.e., in response to social identity threat), what memories are forgotten (i.e., content that has been tainted by social identity threat), and who is motivated to forget (i.e., consumers who identify strongly with the threatened social group). These findings would be of interest to academics interested in understanding how people cope with threats to social or self-identity. It also has some real-world relevance for marketers. Social-identity-linked marketing is common nowadays and most work on the topic has examined factors like product/brand preference, not memory. This is surprising because memory drives most consumer decisions. Our work is important because it demonstrates factors that cause memory impairment. Imagine that a sports bar offers promotions to fans of a local sports team. If the team is having a bad season, dedicated fans may experience social identity threat and forget about the bar’s promotions.

641010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641010.value: This paper proposes the variable disaster story that has the potential to simultaneously replicate pricing behaviors of variable assets, including stocks, bonds, currencies, and various derivatives. The variable diaster is a rare economic disaster with time-varying arrival intensity that, upon its occurrence, causes severe downward jumps in economic fundamentals. To illustrate the model mechanism, take the model's pricing implications on currency market as the example. There are two prominent puzzles in international finance. First, consumption growth does not co-vary enough to explain the relative smooth movements of the exchange rates (e.g., Brandt, Cochrane and Santa-Clara, 2005), which is sometimes referred to as the "international equity premium puzzle". Second, currency that pays higher interest rates tend to appreciate instead of depreciating (e.g., Fama, 1984), which is called the "forward risk premium puzzle". Variable diaster story provides interpretation for both puzzles. First, even though risks of economic fundamentals are poorly shared, disaster risks tend to be highly shared across borders through investors' common perceptions about the arrivals of disasters. Under the preference that prefer early resolution of uncertainty, i.e., the risk aversion exceeds the reciporal of the elastiicity of substitution (EIS), variable disasters are directly priced which yields the strong comovements of pricing kernels in different countries resulting in the smooth exchange rate process. Second, when domestic disaster is perceived more likely than foreign disasters, domestic interest rate goes down due to precautionary saving and domestic investor demands a higher premium for holding foreign bonds which leads to the depreciation of domestic currency relative to foreign currency. Variable disater story is also likely to explain the pricing features of other assets. First, Watcher (2009) shows that variable disaster can explain the aggregate stock market behavior. Second, an increase in jump intensity decreases bond prices and increases the marginal utility, hence the increase in the bond risk premium. Long term bonds tend to be more sensitive to disasters than short term bonds, hence the increase of term spreads. The positive relation between bond risk premium and term spread is important to replicate the failure of expectation hypothesis in treasury bond pricing. Third, it is well documented that rare disasters are indispensable for explaining derivative prices. By introducing time varying disaster intensity, my model has the potential to replicate the state and time-dependences of options as well. 这篇文章提出灾难的不确定性可以同时解释不同类别资产的定价行为.这些资产包括股票,债券,外汇,以及它们的衍生资产.不确定性的灾难是指很少发生的经济灾难(比如大萧条). 因为它们很少发生,因此在投资者心目中发生的概率应该是变化的: 这一点和文献中通常假定的确定性的发生概率不同. 因为这些灾难一旦发生,会对资产价格发生重大影响(比如,股票和公司债券的价值会跌到零,看跌期权价格会暴涨),市场所估计的发生概率的变化在灾难实际发生之前就会对资产价格产生显著的影响.

641010.label: Major findings and research outcome
641010.value: I find a parsimonious framework featuring unshared variable disaster components goes a long run in capturing various regularities in currency and currency option pricing, such as i) the moderate option-implied volatilities; ii) substantial variations in the risk-neutral skewness of currency returns; iii) the uncovered interest rate parity puzzle, and iv) the first two moments of carry trade returns. 641110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
641110.value: 投資者的短視與首席執行官（CEO）的變更

641110.label: Project Objectives
641110.value: To examine the effect of investor short-termism on both the frequency of CEO turnovers and the sensitivity of turnover to firm performance. To examine the operating performance of firms around CEO changes for firms classified based on their ownership by short-term investors. To examine whether the presence of short-term investors result in new managers to behave more myopically. We expect managerial changes in firms with more short-term investors to increase shareholder payout, conduct fewer equity issues, less external financing, less investment and less R&D financing. We also expect to see less innovation and a greater amount of earnings management.

641110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641110.value: The substantial reduction in Chief Executive Officer (CEO) tenure at major U.S. corporations in the more recent period has attracted considerable attention from both academics and practitioners. The average CEO tenure in the 1970s and the 1980s was about ten years, and it has declined to just over six years in the more recent 1998-2005 period. In addition, the literature on CEO turnover shows that managerial changes have become increasingly sensitive to industry and market returns implying that boards are making systematic attribution errors when assessing performance of CEOs. Many commentators explain the large increase in CEO turnover frequency as a reflection of growing impatience of the markets (and the boards). These commentators argue that shareholders are increasingly focused on short-run performance changes. They are agitating for CEO dismissal even when the short-run performance declines are beyond the CEO’s control. In this project, we propose to examine the extent to which investment horizon of institutional investors affects a firm's CEO replacement decision. Are CEO tenures shorter in firms with a significant ownership by short-term investors? Does the presence of short-term investors affect the sensitivity of CEO turnover to firm performance? To conduct these tests, we will construct several alternative measures of investor myopia and then examine if the presence of myopic investors affects CEO replacements. Second, we examine subsequent firm performance around CEO turnovers and relate that to the investment horizon of the firm’s investors. If CEO dismissal is suboptimal in firms that have myopic investors, the new CEO is unlikely to be an improvement over the outgoing CEO. Thus, we expect to see little change in operating performance subsequent to CEO turnover for firms with myopic investors. Third, we examine the corporate policy decisions of CEOs of firms with myopic investors. CEOs of firms with short-term investors are expected to engage in activities that boost short-term performance at the expense of long-term value. We expect this pressure from shareholders to have a larger impact on the policy decisions of younger CEOs compared to those of older CEOs. 最近一段時間，美國主要公司首席執行官（CEO）任期的大幅度縮短引起了學術界和從業者的廣泛關注。首席執行官的平均任期在上世紀70年代和80年代期间大約為十年，而在1998-2005年期間這一數字已經下降到剛剛超過六年。此外，關於CEO變更的研究文獻表明，管理上的變動對行業和市場回報已變得越來越敏感，這同時也暗示了董事會在評估CEO的績效時所犯的系統性歸因錯誤。許多評論家解釋，CEO變更頻率的大幅提高反映了市場（和董事會）日益增長的不耐情緒。這些評論家認為，股東越來越注重短期績效的變動。他們鼓動對CEO的解雇，哪怕短期業績下滑并不在CEO的控制範圍內。 在此項目中，我們提議考察在何種程度上機構投資者的投資期限可以影響一個公司更換CEO的決定。是否在短期投資者具有顯著所有權的企業中，CEO的任期會更短？短期投資者的存在是否會影響CEO變更對企業業績的敏感程度？為了進行這些檢驗，我們將建立若干衡量投資者短視的可選方法，并考察短視投資者的存在是否會影響CEO的更換。 其次，我們考察CEO更換之後相應的公司業績，並將其與企業投資者的投資期限聯繫起來。如果解僱CEO對擁有短視投資者的企業來說是次優的，新CEO將很難比即將離任的CEO做得更好。因此，我們預計不會看到擁有短視投資者的企業在CEO變更之後經營業績會產生太大變化。 第三，我們要研究擁有短視投資者的企業CEO所做的公司政策決定。擁有短期投資者的企業CEO預計會致力於提高短期業績從而犧牲長期價值。我們預期，與較年長的CEO相比，這種來自股東的壓力對較年輕的CEO的政策決策會產生更大的影響。

641110.label: Realisation of objectives
641110.value: We have completed all three objectives listed in the proposal. First, we examined the effect of investor short-termism on both the frequency of CEO turnovers and the sensitivity of turnover to firm performance. What is the extent to which investment horizon of institutional investors affects a firm’s replacement decisions? To accomplish this objective, we identified CEO turnovers by recording CEO name changes in consecutive years of a firm’s history. We then cross-checked all these names against news searches on Lexis/Nexis and the web to include only those cases where one CEO was replaced by another. The news was used to classify the turnovers as routine or forced. Investor horizon is measured as a weighted average of the turnover rates of institutional investors holding stocks in the firm. We aggregate portfolio churn rates of a firm’s investors to estimate investor horizon. With this data in place, we examined whether CEO turnover is related to investor horizon. We also interacted our investor horizon with measures of firms’ performance to test if turnover is more or less sensitive to performance in firms with short-term investors. Our second objective was to examine the operating performance of firms around CEO turnovers by investor horizon. We estimate size, performance, and industry-adjusted ROA by matching sample firms to a set of control firms in the same two-digit industry, and of similar size and similar ROA in year-1 (within +/- 10% of the sample firm’s size and performance). We then examine how the performance of firms (adjusted for industry, size and pre-turnover ROA) changes following CEO changes for firms with short-term investors compared to firms with long-term investors. Our third objective was to examine if the presence of short-term investors results in new managers behaving more myopically. We examine size, performance, and industry-adjusted measures of both fixed investment (capital expenditures), R&D investment, and number of employees. In addition, we examine how firm risk changes around CEO turnovers and whether the change in risk is greater for firms with short-term investors.

641110.label: Major findings and research outcome
641110.value: We find that firms with a larger fraction of shares owned by short-term institutional investors have a significantly higher likelihood of CEO turnover. At the same time, the presence of short-term investors reduces the sensitivity of CEO turnover to stock returns. These results are consistent with short-term investors pushing for more frequent CEO changes, which are unrelated to changes in firm performance. To establish whether myopia-induced changes in CEOs are inefficient, we examine changes in firm’s operating performance surrounding the turnover and test whether post-turnover performance of firms differs depending on the horizon of investors. We find that indeed firms with short-horizon investors experiencing CEO turnovers experience significantly poor performance relative to other firms experiencing turnovers but investors have longer horizons. All of these pre- and post-earnings comparisons are relative to a control group of firms that are matched on size, industry, and pre-turnover ROA. Finally, we examine if the presence of short-term investors results in new managers behaving more myopically. We focus on investment, operating decisions, and risk of the firm. Theoretically, it is unclear how investor myopia distorts investment. One view is that managers focused on the short-term would underinvest in long-term projects as they are focused on generating higher short-term earnings which will be hurt if the firm increased R&D investments, for example. Alternatively, one could view investment itself as a signal of growth opportunities and managers might distort investor perceptions by overinvesting. Our results show that new managers in firms with more short-term investors significantly reduce R&D, but not capital expenditure. Newly hired CEOs in firms with more myopic investors aggressively invest in physical capital, but at the same time cut-back on long-term investments such as R&D expenditures. In addition, we find a significant increase in idiosyncratic risk of firms when CEOs are replaced in firms with short-term investors. These results are reported in "Investor Myopia and CEO Turnover." In addition, we have worked on two additional papers related to CEO turnovers and incentives. In “Provision of Management Incentives in Bankrupt Firms”, Wei Wang and I examine the use of key employee retention plans in bankrupt firms. We find that these bonus plans are an efficient contracting solution to the problem of retaining and incentivizing key employees in bankruptcy. In another paper, “Top Management Compensation Differences and Merger Outcomes”, Zilong Zhang and I examine if compensation differences between acquirers and targets affect merger outcomes and CEO turnover.

641110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641110.value: Our research has shown that investor adversely affects board’s decisions to replace CEO. Importantly, investor myopia affects decision-making inside firms since newly-hired managers are concerned about the pressure from short-term investors. Future research could examine more on what other CEO decisions are affected by the presence of short-term investors. We have focused on some decisions but have not provided a granular understanding of changes to a firm’s structure of assets and liabilities when managers face short-term investors. More could also be done to examine how corporate governance of firms evolves to restore incentives. Does board composition adopt in response to short-term investor activism? Does it affect management compensation? In general, we would like to know how firms change the incentive structures of managers in the presence of investor myopia.

641110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641110.value: This research examines if the presence of short-term investors results in suboptimal CEO dismissal decisions. CEO tenures have become increasingly shorter. One of the common explanations for the increase in top management turnover is that the markets (and the boards) have become impatient. In this project, we examine if indeed investor short-termism affects a firm’s CEO replacement decisions, and whether these decisions are inefficient. We find that when a firm has more short-term investors, CEOs are replaced more frequently, and the CEO change is less sensitive to firm performance. To test if myopia-induced decisions are suboptimal, we examine operating performance of firms following CEO changes. The results show that CEO changes in firms with myopic investors perform relatively worse compared to performance changes around turnovers in other firms, where performance is always measured relative to a size, industry, and pre-performance matched control sample. We also find some evidence that investor myopia causes managers to also behave myopically. Subsequent to CEO changes, firms with short-term investors reduce R&D investment but increase capital expenditures. Furthermore risk significantly increases around turnovers in firms with myopic investors.

641310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641310.value: Security analysts are important information intermediates who process financial information and provide investment recommendations to market participants. An important product of financial analysts is the analyst report, in which analysts explain the reasoning behind their future earnings forecasts and stock recommendations. The proposed study will examine three questions about analyst reports. The first question is whether the way in which analysts explain their research reasoning (i.e., how they tell their story) varies across analysts and provides additional information beyond the simple future earnings forecast and stock recommendation. The second question is whether the additional information provided by analysts in their reports, if any, affects investment decisions. The third question is whether the readability of analyst reports relates to the underlying characteristics of the firm under analysis, the forecast, recommendation, and analyst characteristics, that is, whether these factors are the determinants of analyst report readability. In the proposed project, we will aim to examine the additional information that investors can extract from financial analysts to help their investment decisions, focusing specifically on the readability of the analyst research report. On the one hand, the readability of an analyst report reflects its information quality, and specifically, the uncertainty of the associated earnings per share (EPS) forecast and stock recommendation. On the other hand, the readability is an indication of the transparency of the analyst's disclosure, and reflects the analyst's willingness and effort to transfer information. Put simply, it is an indication of how good an analyst is at acting as an information intermediary. From the point of view of investors, readability directly influences their understanding of report information, and reflects the credibility of an analyst report. We will perform a large-scale analysis of empirical data, starting with four specific measures of readability, as defined by the complexity and ambiguity of the report. We plan to study the association between these characteristics of analyst reports and future stock returns (over various intervals), controlling for stock recommendations and earnings forecasts. We will then study the association between readability and two categories of determinants of these linguistic characteristics: 1) the underlying characteristics and financial disclosures (i.e., public information) of the firms under analysis, and 2) the characteristics of the analysts and their earnings forecasts and stock recommendations. Our project will add to the financial analyst literature by studying a source of information that is publicly available to investors but poorly understood by researchers. 證券分析師是重要的資訊媒介，他們分析財務資訊並向市場參與者提供投資建議。此一過程中的重要產出即為分析師報告，它說明了分析師對未來盈餘預測及投資建議的理論依據。本研究針對分析師報告探討下列三項問題：（一）分析師報告中的論述是否因分析師而異，以及是否提供了除盈餘預測與股票評級以外的資訊；（二）若分析師報告具有額外的資訊內涵，其是否影響投資者決策；（三）分析師報告的可讀性是否受標的公司、預期盈餘、股票評級、分析師特性等等因素的影響。 本計畫將以分析師研究報告的可讀性為重點，檢視投資者可從報告中得到的有助於投資決策之額外資訊。一方面，報告的可讀性反映了該報告的資訊品質，特別是對預期每股盈餘(EPS)與股票評級的不確定性。另一方面，可讀性還可作為分析師資訊透明度的指標，反映了分析師作為資訊傳播媒介的努力及表現。從投資者的角度來說，可讀性直接影響他們對財務報表的了解程度並反映了該分析師報告的可信度。 我們以四種特定的可讀性指標對實證資料進行大規模的測試，這四種指標是基於分析師報告中的複雜性與模糊程度來定義的。我們首先研究在同一股票評級與預期盈餘水準下，不同特徵的分析師報告與未來各期股票報酬的關聯性。我們接著研究可讀性與下列兩者的關係：（一）該標的公司的屬性與其（公開）財務資訊的品質；（二）分析師本身的特性與其提供的盈餘預測及股票評級。 分析師報告為公開資訊，但相對來說研究人員卻對其少有了解。我們期望藉由研究此一資訊來源，為財務分析師的相關文獻作出貢獻。

641310.label: Realisation of objectives
641310.value: We believe that we have achieved the aforementioned objectives in exploring the nature and effect of analyst report readability. For objectives 1 and 2, we find that higher readability implies lower analyst forecast dispersion, and stock market reactions are significantly positive to the issuance of more readable reports. The positive effect of readability on stock prices is higher when it effectively reduces investors’ uncertainty. For objective 3, we find that the readability of analyst reports varies across analyst and firm. Specifically, we document that analysts with longer experience or follow more firms tend to issue more readable reports. Reports issued with upward forecast revisions are more readable when issued by analysts from smaller brokerage houses or by analysts who have better records of forecast accuracy. Moreover, reports issued immediately after firms’ public disclosures or management forecasts are also more readable. The findings for these objectives provide implications for future research such as the association between analyst quality and readability. We intend to extend these questions further for a more complete understanding about analyst reports.

641310.label: Major findings and research outcome
641310.value: Readability is one important feature of analyst reports that may affect value relevant information. In this project we investigate the association among readability of analyst reports, stock price and expectations of future earnings. We find that readability reduces analyst dispersion but is not associated with revision news, and stock markets reactions are significantly positive to the issuance of more readable reports. We also document that market reacts positively to the predicted component of forecast dispersion reduction due to report readability. Furthermore, the positive effect of readability on stock prices is higher when it effectively reduces investors’ uncertainty, specifically when the uncertainty is higher, when analysts are more experienced, or when forecasts are issued after earnings announcements. This project also explores the questions about whether readability of analyst reports relates to the underlying characteristics of the analysts. The result suggests that readability of analyst report is greatly influenced by analyst characteristics, firms’ disclosure policies and other firm characteristics. Speicifically, we find that analysts with better experience, who follow more firms and have a better forecast accuracy history, write more readable reports containing upward revisions. We also find that analyst reports are more readable when they are issued immediately after public disclosures. Overall, our empirical findings suggest the linguistic features of analysts’ reports reduce uncertainty about future earnings, and investors price that reduction of uncertainty.

641310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641310.value: Based on our results, we intend to further study analyst report in the following aspects. First, as we find that analyst report readability varies with the existence of earnings announcement and management guidance, we plan to further examine whether the quality of companies’ public disclosures (e.g., the readability of management discussion and analysis in annual reports) has any impact on the readability of analyst reports that are issued right after the corporate disclosures. Second, out results show that analyst report readability is associated with analyst characteristics such as experience and forecast accuracy. We intend to explore further whether it can serve as an additional measure of analyst performance. Based on the findings, we conjecture that readability may reflect analyst ability and/or effort, and readability may thus vary with analysts’ later career moves. Third, the promulgation of Regulation Fair Disclosure (Reg FD) in 2000 has largely changed the information advantage that analysts used to have compared to other investors prior to Reg FD. We plan to examine whether the readability of analyst reports has also changed accordingly. This will require that we expand our sample period from post-Reg FD to pre-Reg FD period.

641310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641310.value: This project is one of the first to examine the language and readability of analyst reports, and to establish an important link between the readability of analyst research reports and market pricing. First, this study provides important evidence of how the analysts’ presentations of their research findings have consequences for market pricing beyond the forecast revisions presented in the reports. Second, we provide evidence concerning the aspects of report writing that are most significant. We show that the readability of a report does not depend on the specific news contained in the report. Although many other studies focus on the tone of reports, this study finds that report readability is a cleaner measure of how analyst reports reduce uncertainty about future earnings forecasts. Third, this study improves our understanding of the importance of analysts as information intermediaries. While recent studies suggest that analyst forecasts of risk ratings can predict future return volatilities (Lui, Markov and Tamayo, 2007), the positive association between stock returns and readability suggests that the writing of analyst research reports lowers the discount rate in pricing expected earnings.

641410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641410.value: We predict managers who have experienced short-term forecasting success become overconfident about their ability to forecast future earnings. Importantly, this form of overconfidence is endogenous. In other words, our study will depart from previous research by focusing on time-series properties rather than cross-sectional variations in confidence and study the short-term dynamics behind the forecasts issued by a given manager. We will examine two issues related to the effect of past management earnings forecast accuracy. The first is the effect of a manager’s past forecast accuracy on his or her current earnings forecast. The second issue is the effect of past management forecast accuracy on the extent to which investors and analysts rely on the current management earnings forecast. 我们认为短期盈利预测比较成功的管理者会对自己预测未来盈利的能力过度自信，更为重要的是，这种过度自信是内生的、动态的。换句话说，我们并不是检验文献中常用的横截面差异，而是采用时间序列特性来研究给定管理者的短期盈利预测的动态特征。基于管理者过去的预测准确度，我们主要研究两个问题：第一，管理者历史预测准确度对其当前盈利预测的影响；第二，管理者历史预测准确度对投资者和分析师使用其当前盈利预测的影响。

641410.label: Major findings and research outcome
641410.value: This project leads to one paper published in a top-tier accounting journal (Journal of Accounting and Economics) and two working papers. Please see Part C for the publication information for the first paper. The published paper essentially includes the research findings related to the first three objectives per 5.2 above. The second paper (working paper) reports the findings related to the last two objectives per 5.2 above. Because over-optimism is a phenomenon closely related to over-confidence, to deepen our analysis of our first objective, we also investigate dynamic over-optimism and its implication on firms’ welfare. This results in a third working paper. In the published paper, we examine whether attribution bias leads managers who have experienced short-term forecasting success to become overconfident in their ability to forecast future earnings. Importantly, this form of overconfidence is endogenous and dynamic. We also examine the effect of this cognitive bias on the managerial credibility. Consistent with the existence of dynamic overconfidence, managers who have predicted earnings accurately in the previous four quarters are less accurate in their subsequent earnings predictions. These managers also display greater divergence from the analyst consensus and are more precise. Lastly, investors and analysts react less strongly to forecasts issued by overconfident managers. In the second paper, we examine the effects of CEO characteristics and the sophistication of investors and analysts on dynamic overconfidence in managerial forecasts. We find that managers who have generally been more successful in their careers and managers who were appointed more recently are more strongly affected by dynamic overconfidence. Our results also indicate that investors and analysts are aware of this bias and react less strongly to forecasts issued by overconfident managers. This finding is especially true for sophisticated and experienced market participants. In the third paper, we show that managers of firms that have experienced recent successes are more likely to subsequently issue forecasts that are more optimistic than they would have been absent this bias. Importantly, we also find over-optimism can improve firm’s welfare.

641410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641410.value: We have submitted our third paper to Journal of Accounting and Economics for the first-round review. We plan to submit our second paper to another accounting journal.

641410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641410.value: The research output generated by this project contributes to the accounting and finance literature in at least three ways. First, it investigates whether overconfidence affects the decision-making process of individuals in an important economic setting, that of managerial earnings forecasts. Specially, we consider the influence of past success on current overconfidence/over-optimism. Our analysis diverges from that of most previous empirical research, which primarily considers overconfidence to be a fixed bias and assumes managers are born to be overconfident. We demonstrate that the overconfidence phenomenon emerges from a manager’s behavior and thus should not be treated as a characteristic that is purely fixed. Second, to the best of our knowledge, our study is the first to examine the reaction of market participants to overconfident forecasts. We document that investors and analysts are aware of managers' dynamic overconfidence, and that their ability to detect managerial overconfidence is concentrated in subsamples with sophisticated investors and experienced analysts. Third, our research output suggests that past successes also lead managers to become over-optimistic and that over-optimism can actually improve firm’s welfare.

642010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
642010.value: 中国1959-1961年“大跃进”饥荒的政治经济学：省内死亡率差异的分析

642010.label: Project Objectives
642010.value: 1. To ascertain the size variations in excess mortality at the county level in three provinces. 2. To examine whether variations in excess mortality at the county level in three provinces were due to: a) differences in resource endowments (specifically cropping patterns), and b) differences in political radicalism.
rows: 1. To ascertain the size variations in excess mortality at the county level in three provinces.

2. To examine whether variations in excess mortality at the county level in three provinces were due to: a) differences in resource endowments (specifically cropping patterns), and b) differences in political radicalism.

642010.label: Realisation of objectives
642010.value: To achieve Objectives 1 and 2, I needed to collect data on the key variables of death rates, cropping patterns, and output at the county level for at least three provinces—provinces where both major staple crops—wheat and rice—were cultivated (e.g., Jiangsu, Anhui, Henan, Shandong). To this end, I trained two MPhil students to collect the pertinent data from the offices where the county gazetteers are held. In doing so we encountered two major difficulties, however. The first is that some offices simply did not contain the documents that we were looking for, or perhaps they did not want us to access those materials which they consider politically sensitive. Finally, we overcame this hurdle and obtained most of the materials we needed from the Academy of Science in Beijing. Then came the second problem. In entering the data, my research assistant soon discovered that the quality of the data is rather poor. First there were many missing observations, due in part to the fact that there was not a standardized format required from the counties for reporting the key statistics. An example is that counties in Shandong Province simply contained no statistics on cropping acreage and output. Second, the poor quality of the data is also reflected in the fact that cropping acreage—which should be fairly stable over time—fluctuated enormously from one year to another to the extent that it cannot be credible. Finally, the problem of under-reporting death rates is especially prevalent in counties where the death rates were extraordinarily high. Fortunately, Professor Shuji Cao of Shanghai Jiaotong University has meticulously compiled the data at the prefecture level. While the prefecture is a level above the county, it still qualifies as “sub-provincial”, not to mention that this alternative data source allows me to cover 21 provinces in my analysis. By further constructing a dataset that would allow me to test the hypothesis regarding the channel through which politics or political connections may affect death rates (see Research Outcome), I would consider the revised objectives fully realized. In addition, when evaluated in terms of publications this research has fulfilled two additional objectives, namely: (3) the impact of the Great Leap Famine on the institutional change of agricultural de-collectivization; and (4) the causal effect of political career incentives on the radical behavior of excessive grain procurement (see Research Output).

642010.label: Major findings and research outcome
642010.value: This project has three major findings. With respect to Objective (1), I found that 52 percent of the total variation in the death rate during 1958-61 occurred between provinces, whereas 48 percent occurred within the provinces. This is a novel finding as we only knew previously that the variation in the death rate was high among the provinces; now we know that such variation was also high within a single province, suggesting avenues for further research. With respect to Objective (2), I found that the variations in death rate were insignificantly correlated with differences in resource endowments, or, more specifically, that death rates were not higher in areas specializing in one type of crop vis-à-vis the other (e.g., rice versus wheat), but instead due to politics. This is also a novel finding because variation in the cropping patterns is much likely smaller within a single province than across provinces. In contrast, a strong negative correlation is found between prefectures with a greater presence of the Central Committee (CC) members (measured by their birthplace) and famine severity. Specifically, a one-standard-deviation increase in the density of CC members (1.07) is significantly correlated with a lower excess mortality rate of 0.61‰—about 12 percent when evaluated at mean (the average excess death rate is 4.92‰). For additional outcomes, I used the variation in famine severity to test the effect of an extreme historical incident on farmers’ choice of farming institutions; assuming that higher death rates during the Great Famine would result in stronger preferences for individualized (family-based) farming institution at a time when farmers were allowed to make such a choice (1978-84). We found that, in places where death rates were normal, bad weather at the time of agricultural de-collectivization actually had the effect of strengthening the collective institutions—presumably because they are able to handle weather shocks better than family farm institutions. However, this preference is reversed in provinces where the Great Leap famine severity was high, and where the rural public goods were better provided previously. I also extended my own previous work (Kung and Chen, 2011) by employing the ranking of the Central Committee members at the 8th National Party Congress to identify the causal effect of political career incentives—specifically aspirations for promotion—on radical behavior (measured by excessive grain procurement).

642010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
642010.value: Our next step is to account for this significantly negative relationship between the predominance of Central Committee (CC) members and famine severity. Specifically, I want to measure the more precise channel through which this relationship occurred. One hypothesis is that prefectures with proportionately more CC members originating therefrom may procure less grain from these prefectures during the Great Leap. An alternative hypothesis is that proportionately more “relief grain” may be remitted to those prefectures producing more CC members in times of shortages. In order to test these hypotheses, it is necessary to code the curriculum vitae of the CC members in further details beyond their birthplace, and to collect data on grain procurement and remittance at the prefecture level. For example, we need to be able to tell who was serving in what capacity at the time of the Great Leap; specifically, only those who were serving in Beijing (a relevant position in the central government or party) would be able to authorize to either: procuring less grain from a province (prefecture); or remitting more “relief grain” to a province (prefecture). I have currently appointed someone to perform this particular assignment and I anticipate a completion time early next year.

642010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
642010.value: China’s Great Leap Forward had inadvertently resulted in the worst manmade famine in history: 30 million people are estimated to have died in excess of the normal mortality rate. This project has two main objectives. In light of the enormity of the Chinese provinces and the enormous variations in death rates across provinces, it endeavors to: (1) estimate the extent to which death rate variations occurred within as well as between the provinces, and (2) examine the underlying causes of such variation; specifically whether it was due to nature (cropping suitability-cum-productivity) or politics. Premised upon my previous work, which finds that the excessive procurement of grain from the countryside could be systematically explained by the career incentives embedded in China’s system of personnel control (the “nomenklatura”), this research further confirms the existence of a strong, negative relationship between “political connections” and death rates. Specifically, the prefectures that gave birth to more senior party officials by the time of the 8th Party Congress were systematically spared of excess deaths. Our next step is to identify exactly how that channel operated. This research also finds that the Great Leap Famine has had a lasting impact on the future preferences regarding farming institutions.

642110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642110.value: Volatility measures the variability of returns of an underlying asset, thus providing a measure of the risk of holding that asset. Volatility can be viewed as an asset class in its own right. Holding a long position of volatility may be useful in hedging an equity portfolio. Alternatively, one may exploit the mean-reverting nature of volatility to add alpha to portfolios (buy cheap and sell expensive). Variance swaps are financial instruments that offer investors direct exposure to the volatility of an underlying asset or index, irrespective of the level and path of the underlying asset. Variance swaps have long skews and convexity, and they can be used to trade the variance term structures. Investors can use volatility derivatives to perform (i) directional trading of volatility levels; (ii) trading the spread between realized and implied volatility levels, (iii) hedging implicit volatility exposure. In recent years, new generations of exotic volatility derivatives, like conditional / corridor variance swaps, and VIX derivatives, have gained wider popularity as volatility trading instruments. In this project, I would like to develop analytical / semi-analytical methods and efficient numerical algorithms for pricing and hedging exotic volatility derivatives. First, I would like to explore the more accurate prescription of the dynamics of volatility that reflects various typical behaviors, like fast mean reverting behavior, regime switching, anti-correlation with the underlying asset, and sudden jumps. I also consider how to calibrate the parameter functions in volatility dynamics using the market observed term structure of variance. Next, various analytic / semi-analytic closed form formulas are derived for exotic swap contracts and VIX products under various stochastic volatility models. I also explore the effectiveness of various analytical approximation formulas for pricing derivatives products with exotic volatility payoff structures. For effective numerical pricing of most exotic volatility products, I develop efficient finite difference schemes and the Fast Fourier transform network tree methods that compete with existing numerical algorithms in terms of efficiency, accuracy and reliability. Lastly, I will consider practical hedging and replication procedures for various exotic volatility products using tradeable options and variance instruments. 波幅是量度資產收益的變化，可看成是對持有該資產的風險程度的測量，但同時亦可看成是一種資產性的投資工具。持有波幅的長倉可對資產組合作對冲。波幅性的交換合約，可用作對波幅時限結構的交易。投資者可利用波幅性衍生工具，對波幅的方向性作投資，或對沖波幅方面的風險。 在此研究計劃內，我將推出不同波幅衍生工具的解釋解，並設計相關的計算方法。我將特別考慮使用有限差分法及快速富里叶變換方法。在採用的波幅的動態模型中，將容許有跳躍及範式改變等。還有，我將找出對模型參數函數的求解方法。最後，我考慮如何實踐對沖的手段及如何模擬具有相同結算的投資組合。

642110.label: Realisation of objectives
642110.value: I and my former Phd student, Zheng Wendong, initiated the research project by constructing the stochastic volatility model with simultaneous jumps on both the asset price and volatility for modeling the asset price dynamics of the underlying asset. The price dynamics has included various typical features, like mean reverting feature, sudden jumps, etc. We managed to derive various closed form pricing formulas for discretely monitored generalized variance swaps. The exposure to convexity (volatility of variance) and skew (correlation between the equity returns and variance process) of these third generation variance swaps were examined. We also derived the saddlepoint approximation formulas to price options on discrete realized variance and volatility derivatives. Numerical accuracy of analytic approximation versus Monte Carlo simulation methods and reliability of the analytic approximation approach were examined. Practical hedging properties of these exotic volatility instruments were studied. We also examined the limitations of applicability of the saddlepoint approximation methods, in particular, the pricing of short-maturity derivatives. In the last part of the project, we developed the Fourier time-stepping methods for pricing exotic volatility derivatives under additive processes. We explored various pricing properties of different volatility products and achieved better understanding of risk sensitivities of various variance products. Most of the objectives stated in the proposal have been achieved. We have skipped the construction of finite difference schemes for pricing volatility derivatives since this numerical approach suffers from the curse of dimensionality when we allow for more realistic price dynamics of the asset price process (stochastic volatility with simultaneous jumps). Instead of performing calibration of the model parameters, we mostly rely on earlier published works for the assignment of the model parameter values in our pricing formulas and algorithms.

642110.label: Major findings and research outcome
642110.value: The results of our research findings have been summarized in several research papers and one book chapter. They are either published or accepted for publication in leading journals in quantitative finance, like Mathematical Finance. The research findings have been reported in various international and local conferences and seminars. The part of research performed by Zheng Wendong leads to the phD degree in Mathematics awarded in July, 2012. The major findings and research outcome are summarized as follows: 1. Derivation of closed form pricing formulas for discretely sampled generalized variance swaps. The proposed methodology can be applied to any affine model and other higher order moments swaps. The results are reported in a research paper that has been accepted for publication in Mathematical Finance. 2. We developed and examined numerical accuracy and reliability of various types of the saddlepoint approximation methods for pricing derivatives on discrete realized variance. The results are reported in a research paper that has been accepted for publication in Applied Mathematical Finance. 3. We analyzed the recent trends in the adoption of the fast Fourier transform algorithm for pricing financial derivatives. The results are summarized in one book chapter published by Springer. Later, we developed several types of Fouirer transform algorithms for pricing and hedging discretely sampled exotic variance products and volatility derivatives under additive processes. The results are reported in a research paper that has been accepted for publication in Journal of Computational Finance. Remarks on 2 objectives (Items 2 and 5) that do not achieve 100% completion 1. I have made some preliminary exploration on the calibration and estimation techniques of the stochastic volatility models to tradeable volatility index options and term structure of variances. Their main uses are related to the adoption of model parameter values in our stochastic volatility models. Our research is more focused on pricing and hedging volatility derivatives, less on the development of calibration and estimation techniques. This explains why this item has 30% completion. 2. After some exploration on the finite difference approach, I found that pricing of volatility derivatives using Fourier transform algorithms is more effective than finite difference schemes. Some of the techniques in dealing with the jump conditions in the finite difference schemes are useful in developing the Fourier transform algorithms. The objective of numerical pricing is achieved, though not on the use of finite difference schemes. This item is considered to have 40% completion. a

642110.value: We may extend the pricing methodologies of obtaining closed form price formulas for exotic variance swaps to the class of non-affine stochastic volatility models, like the 3/2 models. Also, we may adopt the convolution type numerical integration method for pricing volatility derivatives under generalized types of payoff structures.

642110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
642110.value: Volatility measures the variability of returns of an underlying asset, thus providing a measure of the risk of holding that asset. Volatility can be viewed as an asset class in its own right. Variance swaps and volatility derivatives are financial instruments that offer investors direct exposure to the volatility of an underlying asset or index, irrespective of the level and path of the underlying asset. In this project, I have developed closed form analytical formulas, saddlepoint approximation methods and numerical algorithms for pricing and hedging exotic volatility derivatives. The availability of better and reliable pricing and hedging methods for volatility derivatives would contribute to more effective trading of these products and improve market efficiency.

642210.label: Project Title(Chinese)
642210.value: 全球化世界中的創新活動，鼓勵政策及國際協調

642210.label: Project Objectives
642210.value: In a closed economy, we seek to understand theoretically the effects of IPR protection in industries where there is on-going process innovation (i.e. innovation is quality-improving in nature), with new innovators replacing incumbents continually. In other words, goods of the same variety are perfect substitutes of each other. We are interested in the effects of strengthening IPR protection on the rate of technological progress and on welfare. Does there exist an innovation-maximizing strength of IPR protection? Does there exist a welfare-maximizing strength of IPR protection? In a global economy with international trade, we seek to understand theoretically the effects of a strengthening of home IPR protection of quality-improvement innovation described above on foreign firms’ incentives to innovate and on foreign welfare. This in turn helps us to analyze a Nash equilibrium in which national governments each sets its strength of IPR protection to maximize its own national welfare given the strengths of IPR protection set by other countries. Then, we shall analyze whether the above Nash equilibrium is globally efficient, and if it is not, then whether it features under-protection or over-protection of IPR. This would have implications on international coordination on IPR protection. Then, we shall compare and contrast the results based on quality-improvement innovation and those based on expanding-variety innovation, i.e. there is on-going product innovation and substitutability between goods is low. We seek to answer the same set of questions as in the above two objectives with regard to other innovation-incentive policies such as anti-trust policy and R&D subsidy. A related and more general question is how in a closed economy product market competition affects the rate of innovation and welfare in industries where there is on-going quality-improving innovation, with new innovators replacing incumbents continually. We seek to understand the impact of increased globalization on the incentive to innovate. In a world where national governments respond to globalization by adjusting their policies, their optimal policy response regarding IPR protection and anti-trust policies would in turn have effects on research intensity and therefore the pace of technological progress. We also analyze whether deeper globalization leads to a greater need for international coordination of innovation-incentive policies.

642210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642210.value: In this project, we study the need for international coordination of innovation-incentive policies, and how the coordination should be carried out if it is needed. By innovation-incentive polices, we mean those that directly influence the incentives to innovate, such as intellectual property rights (IPR) protection, anti-trust policies and R&D subsidies. To fill the gap in the literature, we are especially interested in analyzing the effects of these policies in a setting where there is on-going quality-improvement innovation, with new innovators replacing incumbents continually. We would first analyze the effects of these policies on the rate of innovation and welfare in a closed economy and then the interaction between national policies in a global economy with international trade. In a globalized world, policies such as IPR protection and anti-trust policies of the home country can have cross-border external effects on foreign countries. This would lead to inefficiency of the global Nash equilibrium in the setting of policies by national governments. If the net cross-border externality of a policy is positive (negative), then there is global under-provision (over-provision) of that policy. Thus, international policy coordination can improve global welfare by collectively adjusting policies in the opposite direction. The Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) signed in 1994 as the Final Act of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) is an example of such an international coordination. In this project, we would evaluate TRIPS in the light of the theory that we build in this project. We shall also evaluate whether there is a need for international coordination in other innovation-incentive policies. IPR and anti-trust policies influence the rate of innovation through their effects on product market competition. Therefore, a more general question is: How does product market competition affect the rate of innovation? The answer to this question would help policymakers to set a target for the degree of product market competition they should aim at when different innovation-incentive policies interact in complex ways. The theoretical framework we build can allow us to analyze how deepening of globalization affects innovation and growth when governments respond to globalization by adjusting their policies instead of being totally passive as the literature has been assuming. It also throws light on the important question of whether deeper globalization leads to greater need for international coordination of policies. 在這個項目中，我們將研究國與國之間是否需要就制定鼓勵創新的政策進行國際協商，以及需要協商時應當如何開展的問題。所謂鼓勵創新的政策，我們指的是那些對創新活動有直接影響的政策，比如說知識產權保護，反壟斷以及科研補貼。為了填補現有文獻的空白，我們的興趣主要集中在分析提高產品質量，或者促成行業更新換代的創新行為。在研究的過程中，我們首先會分析這些政策對封閉經濟體中研發速率和福利的影響，接著分析在國際貿易的環境中，國與國之間政策的相互影響。 在全球化的大環境下，一個國家關於保護知識產權或者反壟斷的政策的制定會對其他的國家帶來額外的影響。這種影響會使得各個國家在沒有協商的情況下所制定的政策無法達到最高的全球經濟效益。如果這些額外的影響對其他的國家而言是積極（消極）的，那麽在沒有協商的情況下個別國家的政策會便會顯得不足（過多）。因此，在國際協商的過程中，對各個國家的政策進行調整，可以對全球福利帶來正面的影響。 關稅及貿易總協定（GATT）在1994年所簽訂的《與貿易有關的知識產權協議》（TRIPS）就是一個很好的例子。在這個項目中，我們會基於理論，評估《與貿易有關的知識產權協議》的影響。而且我們還會研究關於其他鼓勵創新的政策的國際協商。 保護知識產權和反壟斷的政策會影響產品市場競爭的激烈程度，從而影響創新的速率。因此，我們可以提出一個更加一般的問題：市場競爭是如何影響創新行為的。而這個問題的答案可以幫助政策制定者擬定一個市場競爭激烈程度的目標，從而在復雜的市場環境中制訂出正確的政策。 由於各國政府面對全球化影響下各自調整政策，我們所建立的理論基礎正好把這些因素包括在經濟模型之中。因此，它可讓我們更好地了解全球化對企業的研發活動及經濟增長的影響。而這些結果亦有助於大家對於全球化的深化是否需要更多的國際政策協商這個重要的問題的理解和思考。

642210.label: Realisation of objectives
642210.value: Objective 1 (100% completed). We build a cumulative-innovation endogenous growth model whereby a new idea strictly improves upon the best existing idea. We found that there exist both an innovation-maximizing patent breadth and a welfare maximizing breadth. The reason for the existence of a welfare-improving breadth is the knowledge spillover from past to future innovation, which creates a positive externality. Objective 2 (50% completed). We find that in a symmetric two-country world, there will be positive cross-border externalities in increasing the patent breadth. The reason is that an increase in patent breadth beyond the welfare-maximizing level always increases the rate of innovation in both countries in a symmetric two-country world. This result implies that there will be global under-provision of patent breadth protection when innovation is quality-improvement in nature. The asymmetric case is a lot harder to analyze. Because of the shortage of time, we leave it to future research. Objective 3 (20% completed). There is an inverted-U shape relationship between patent breadth and rate of innovation in a closed economy. One can interpret the result as saying that a certain level of anti-competitive measures taken by the incumbent against new entrants can improve the rate of innovation and even welfare. Thus, anti-trust laws should not rule all entry-deterrence measures illegal in such kind of industry. Explicitly modeling of anti-trust policies took time, and so we leave it to future research. Objective 4 (70% completed). When innovation is on-going and expanding-variety in nature, we find that decreases in trade and FDI costs lead to greater divergence between the global optimum level of patent strength and the global Nash equilibrium level of patent strength. In other words, there is greater need for international coordination of patent strengths. This is one of the main results in our paper published in Journal of International Economics in January 2013. We made a serious mistake in analyzing the non-cumulative case under the closed economy. Although we fixed the problem, the loss of time prevented us from completing the rest of the objectives in time. Although not all objectives were 100% achieved, the project is still considered quite successful, as we published one paper in Journal of International Economics (a top field journal), completed one paper based on cumulative innovation which will be submitted to a journal soon, and built a non-cumulative innovation model which can be developed into a paper in the near future.

642210.label: Major findings and research outcome
642210.value: Relating to Objective 1, we completed a paper “Cumulative Innovation, Growth and Welfare-improving Patent Policy” based on a cumulative innovation model. It has been presented in many conferences and seminars. It is circulated as a CESifo Working Paper (listed in Part C). We plan to submit the paper to a journal in the summer of 2014. In addition, we also built a non-cumulative-innovation model so as to compare and contrast the results in the two models. The output is a paper titled “Innovation, Patentability Requirement and North-South Integration” (listed in Part C). In this paper, we find that there exists a binding and finite innovation-maximizing patent breadth. However, the welfare-maximizing patent breadth is always a corner solution, i.e. zero patent breadth. In other words, while patent breadth can increase the rate of innovation, it cannot improve welfare. This latter result is a consequence of the fact that there are no knowledge spillovers from past innovation to future innovation. This paper is still in an early stage of development. We plan to revise it and circulate it for comments in the summer of 2014. Relating to Objective 2, based on the closed economy cumulative-innovation model above, we have carried out some extension to the open economy. It is still work in progress. One preliminary result is that in a symmetric two-country world, there will be positive cross-border externalities in increasing the patent breadth. The reason is that for an individual country an increase in patent breadth slightly beyond its own welfare-maximizing level always increases the rate of innovation in both countries in a symmetric two-country world. This result implies that there will be global under-provision of patent breadth protection when innovation is on-going and cumulative in nature. Relating to Objective 3, we conclude that anti-trust laws should be less stringent in industries where competition among firms in the form of quality-improvement innovation is more important. Relating to Objective 4, we carried out analysis assuming that innovation is on-going and expanding-variety in nature. We find that decreases in trade costs lead to greater divergence between the globally-optimal level of patent strength and the global Nash-equilibrium level of patent strength. In other words, there is greater need for international coordination of patent strengths. This result is contained in the paper “Would global patent protection be too weak without international coordination?” published in Journal of International Economics in January 2013 (listed in Part C).

642210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
642210.value: Objective 2. We have carried out some preliminary analysis of the symmetric two-country world, and find that there will be positive cross-border externalities in increasing the patent breadth. In future research, we plan to analyze the asymmetric-country case. Objective 3. Based on our model developed Objective 1, we draw an analogy between the extent of anti-competitive behavior by the incumbent against new entrants that the anti-trust authority can tolerate. Since a certain level of anti-competitive measures taken by the incumbent against new entrants can improve the rate of innovation and even welfare, anti-trust laws should not rule all entry-deterrence measures illegal in such kind of industry. In future research, we plan to formally model the incumbent’s anti-competitive behavior and how the anti-trust authority sets the tolerable extent of such behavior. Objective 4. We have carried out analysis and published a paper in Journal of International Economics based on the assumption that innovation is on-going and expanding-variety in nature. We find that deeper globalization makes international coordination of patent strengths more valuable. In future research, we plan to investigate whether the same conclusion holds when innovation is on-going and cumulative in nature.

642210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
642210.value: We study the need for international coordination of innovation-incentive policies, and how the coordination should be carried out if it is needed. By innovation-incentive polices, we mean those that directly influence the incentives to innovate, such as intellectual property rights (IPR) protection, anti-trust policies and R&D subsidies. In industries where there is on-going quality-improvement innovation, with new innovators replacing incumbents continually, we find that a certain amount of strengthening of patent scope protection can improve the rate of innovation and consumer welfare. This is because innovators carry out too little R&D as they do not capture the benefits of the knowledge that spillovers to other firms. In a globalized world, patent scope protection or anti-trust policy in the home country in industries with on-going quality-improvement innovation have cross-border positive external effects on foreign countries. Thus, there is global under-provision of that policy. Therefore, international policy coordination can improve global welfare by collectively increasing national patent breadth protection and loosening national anti-trust policy. As the world becomes more globalized, the positive cross-border external effects of home country’s patent scope protection on foreign countries get stronger. Therefore, more globalization implies that there is greater need for international coordination concerning innovation-incentive policies.
