643910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
643910.value: Due to the fast growing information technology, researchers nowadays have the advantage of working with large datasets. However, the available tools capable of handling such data are rather limited. Modern factor analysis is able to effectively separate useful information from noise in large datasets. This project will focus on the structural analysis of large dimensional dynamic factor models and will contribute to our understanding by providing an efficient way to analyze large-scale dynamic factor models with micro-foundations. It aims to provide a close link between economic theory and the statistical methods of modern factor analysis. Such a link will help researchers to efficiently utilize the rich information from large datasets and to better identify economic relationships underlying variables of interest. Those relationships are generally implied by the optimal behavior of agents in an economy and are testable within an econometric framework. In normal practice, researchers always focus on such structural models with only several variables included, such as output, inflation, unemployment, consumption, etc. However, in the modern world, decision makers have available datasets covering all sorts of economic sectors over a long time span. For example, when a central bank designs its monetary policy, it looks at hundreds of economic variables. It would be very difficult for researchers to summarize the information that decision makers have using only limited observed series. The methods to be developed in this proposed research will help researchers to construct models with more variables and extract important information through the lens of unobserved factor models. Such large-scale models will also provide a better fit to empirical data than small-scale time-series models. Different from standard time-series econometric models or panel data models, the theory to be developed will be based upon the assumption that both the cross-sectional dimension and the time dimension go to infinity. The methodology to be developed will help researchers better understand the tools available to analyze large dimensional datasets. Beyond statistical techniques, this research may also expand the applicability of modern factor models to the structural analysis of large economic systems. Coupled with dynamic general equilibrium models, this structural method will be able to produce outcome not subject to the Lucas critique. In other words, the model predictions will be robust with respect to policy regime shifts. 摘要 信息技術的高速發展使數據的採集更為方便，研究人員從而獲得更多的機會來研究大型數據。不過現今能有效研究大型數據的方法仍然有限。現代因子分析的方法可以快速地從大型數據中獲取有用的信息，從而將擾動信息分隔開來。此項目將針對高維動態因子模型進行結構分析，研究對象包括具有微觀基礎的大型計量模型。項目的目標是將經濟理論模型同現代高維因子模型緊密聯繫起來。這種聯繫能幫助研究者剔除大型數據中的大量擾動信息從而獲取豐富而有效的信息，從而更好地識別經濟變量之間的關係。此類關係通常由經濟中個體的最優行為導致，並能放在計量框架下進行檢驗。在傳統的結構模型中，一般只有少數幾個經濟變量及其數據被考慮，如產出、通脹、失業率、消費等等。然而在當今社會，決策者手中的數據囊括了經濟社會的各行各業，並且有著相當長的時間跨度。例如央行在制定貨幣政策時考慮的數據超過百種。傳統結構經濟模型很難用少量的經濟變量來總結決策者手中持有的信息。此項目所研究和倡導的方法將有助於研究者在大量經濟變量的基礎上建立經濟模型，利用因子模型來建立模型和數據之間的緊密聯繫。此類大型模型對實際數據的擬合也將優於傳統的小型時間序列模型。不同於傳統時間序列模型和面板數據模型，此項目是針對於雙維漸進理論，一個突出特點是同時具有較長的時間跨度和大量的經濟變量種類。此項目的雙維漸進理論方法同時能幫助研究者更好地理解高維數據的特點。有別於單純的統計模型，此項目中的結構分析模型是由動態一般均衡模型導出，從而避免了盧卡斯批判的問題。換而言之，此模型的預測已經將可能的經濟政策變化及個體的最優反應考慮在內。

643910.label: Realisation of objectives
643910.value: This project has successfully addressed and achieved all six objectives. Motivated by various empirical challenges facing macroeconomics and finance, I have proposed a factor-augmented maximum likelihood estimation method, and have demonstrated that it is both general enough to incorporate structural restrictions and suitable for the study of large scale dynamic systems underlying equilibrium models. In comparison to other candidate estimation methods, such as restricted least squares, the proposed method is able to more effectively handle a rich family of dynamic systems. The estimation method naturally incorporates the large information both across section and over time, which in turn helps the identification of latent factors or the latent state of the dynamic system. I have written computer programs in Matlab so that the complete estimation procedure can be automatically implemented in practice, as long as the dynamic system and the structural restrictions are supplied in the module. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations show that the methodology has good finite sample performance and compares favorably to other candidate estimators in terms of computational cost. I have focused on a long-run risk model throughout the project, which well demonstrates how the method can help to estimate economic latent variables that are of crucial relevance to our further understanding of the economy. Discussions of extensions show a rich pipeline for future research topics.

643910.label: Major findings and research outcome
643910.value: This project concerns identification and estimation of latent factors that drive the dynamics of a large-scale economic system. I find that the factor analysis effectively uncovers the linear space spanned by the latent factors, and the structural restrictions further identify each individual latent factor. Compared to the existing small-scale approach, a huge advantage of the large-scale approach is the ability to consistently estimate the latent factors and to conduct statistical inference of the entire time series of these factors. A highly relevant and important application is to study the risk for the long run in dynamic economic models. The long run risk is a hypothetical persistent but stationary component in macro-finance that can resolve a wide variety of puzzles, although it assumes a very small magnitude. Small scale models conceptually are not suitable for the empirical analysis of the long run risk itself, which has the same dimension as the sample size over time. The estimation problem is further complicated by the low signal-noise ratio due to the possibly small long run risk component. I find that the large scale method can effectively average out the noise and is able to provide consistent estimation of the time series history of long run risk, exploiting the theory-implied factor structure in dividend-price ratios. I provide the confidence band for the long run risk and have used alternative model specifications to demonstrate the robustness of the estimation outcome.

643910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
643910.value: On the theory side, there are lots of further research areas in this topic. For example, it is interesting to study how nonlinearity in the factor representation can be effectively handled. I have already initiated potential collaborations with other researchers. On the application side, it is interesting to further investigate the asset pricing implications of the empirical long run risk model. In the meantime, there are also lots of fields that the methodology can be applied, such as international trade, international macroeconomics, etc. I plan to collaborate with experts in these fields.

643910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
643910.value: People care about the economic health in order to make optimal savings and investment decisions. In reality, the health or state of an economy is not directly observable. However, through the up and downs of economic indicators, such as employment, output, and asset prices, we can make a conjecture whether we are experiencing economic booms or recessions. On the other hand, such a conjecture is contaminated by the fact that there are too many indicators which are similar in one aspect but different in others. This project provides a methodology to summarize the state of an economy based on asset prices as well as the theoretical linkage between asset prices and economic fundamentals. I focus on a special feature of the economic state, namely, the risk of the economic environment far into the future. Learning such a long run risk is challenging due to its possibly small magnitude, but important due to its significant impact on the economy. This project develops an econometric method to uncover such a risk component that provides guide for a better savings and investment decision. The approach has potential applications in other social science and business disciplines such as international trade, international finance, etc.

644010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644010.value: This study will investigate the impact of the recent mandatory adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards (“IFRS”) on bank loans supplied by foreign banks. While many studies have examined how mandatory adoption of IFRS affects the equity markets around the world (e.g., Amiram 2009; DeFond, Hu, Hung and Li 2009; Florou and Pope 2009; Tan, Wang and Welker 2009; Yu 2009), there is not much evidence about how IFRS adoption affects global debt markets. We plan to fill in this gap by focusing on loans offered by foreign banks. We propose that foreign banks and domestic borrowers will benefit from IFRS adoption in the following two ways. First, as IFRS requires more comprehensive disclosures compared to many local accounting standards, foreign creditors face lower monitoring costs, so they are able to offer better loan terms to borrowers. Second, before IFRS adoption, different accounting standards across countries make it difficult for international creditors to understand the financial reports of local business and participate in local debt markets. Thus, converging to a single global set of accounting standards reduces information acquisition costs faced by foreign investors, thereby leading to more cross-border financing arrangements. We hypothesize that IFRS adoption will bring the following changes to banks loans. First, we predict that IFRS adoption is associated with more favorable loan terms offered by foreign banks – that is, domestic borrowers are better able to obtain large loans with longer maturity and lower interest from foreign banks. The improvements in the loan terms subsequent to IFRS adoption are positively associated the extent that local accounting standards differ from IFRS before IFRS adoption. Second, subsequent to IFRS adoption, we expect that more foreign banks will participate in the syndicated loans, and their shares in the syndicated loans would be larger, suggesting lower concentration of syndicates. Third, we postulate that if both borrower’s home country and lender’s home country adopt IFRS at the same time, the increased foreign loans subsequent to IFRS adoption are positively associated with the reduction in accounting standard differences between borrower’s and lender’s home countries. Our study would be important to business corporations, parties involved in financing arrangements and policy-makers. Hong Kong has adopted IFRS since 2005 and bank loans play a significant role in corporate financings. Our proposed study would seem to be especially significant in understanding the importance and impact of converging with global accounting standards for Hong Kong firms. 本项目研究强制采用国际财务报告准则对境外银行贷款的影响。 尽管很多论文已经研究了强制采用国际财务报告准则对股票市场的影响（例如，Amiram 2009; DeFond, Hu, Hung and Li 2009; Florou and Pope 2009; Tan, Wang and Welker 2009; Yu 2009）,当前对该准则在债务市场的影响的研究还非常有限。我们计划通过对境外银行贷款的研究以弥补这一空缺。我们认为采用国际会计准则会从两个不同方面给境外银行和境内公司带来利益。第一：相比很多国家的会计准则， 国际财务报告准则要求更充分详尽的披露，这样可以减少境外银行的监管成本，以便于他们提供给境内公司更优厚的贷款条件。第二，在采用国际财务报告准则以前，由于各国采用不同的会计准则，这使境外贷款人很难理解境内公司的报表，阻碍了境外银行更多的参与海外债务市场。所以， 通过采用国际财务报告准则实现的全球会计一体化有助于减少境外投资者的信息收集成本，以促进国际资本流通。 我们认为采用国际财务报告准则会通过以下渠道影响银行贷款。第一， 我们预测境外银行会提供更优厚的贷款条例给境内公司，例如更大贷款量，更长贷款期，但是较低的利率。而且，如果境内公司本国的会计准则和国际财务报告准则的差异越来，那么境内公司采用国际财务报告准则后获取的上述利益越显著。第二， 我们预测在采用国际财务报告准则之后，更多的境外银行会加入到银团贷款，而且他们在银团贷款中持有更大份额，从而降低了银团贷款的集中度。第三，我们预测如果境内公司所属国和境外银行所属国之间的会计准则差异越大，那么两国同时采用国际财务报告准则而给银行贷款带来的利益也越大。 我们的研究成果会给政策制定者，企业和其他金融市场的参与者带来重要启示。香港在2005年已经采用了国际财务报告准则，而且银行贷款在企业融资中占有重要地位。所以，我们的研究对于理解全球会计一体化如何影响香港公司尤为重要。

644010.label: Realisation of objectives
644010.value: Our study investigates the impact of the mandatory adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) on bank loan contractual terms. Ex ante, the impact of mandatory IFRS adoption on accounting quality and loan contract terms is not obvious. On one hand, IFRS eliminate certain alternative accounting choices, which can reduce both managerial discretion and reporting uncertainty. Moreover, the focus of IFRS on substance over form constrains management from circumventing accounting standards through transaction structuring. This provides an improvement in financial statement informativeness with respect to underlying economics and a reduction in monitoring difficulty. The use of extensive fair value accounting allows for more timely information about economic gains and losses. On the other hand, IFRS change how current earnings and net assets map into future cash flow capacity, lenders thus need to incur additional learning and monitoring costs to determine credit quality and cash flow capacity for borrowers using IFRS. Furthermore, IFRS inherently require more complex and subjective accounting estimates and judgments. This may thus provide managers with greater flexibility and discretion for opportunistic earnings management. Research also suggests that fair value accounting can introduce transitory shocks of expected cash flows into earnings, which weakens earnings persistence as well as the ability of current earnings to predict future cash flows. The subjective nature of asset estimates as well as the opportunities of borrowers to fair value certain liabilities, can reduce the verifiability and reliability of accounting numbers, causing financial covenants to be less effective under IFRS. Base on a treatment sample of 3,968 bank loans issued to 528 borrowers from 18 countries mandating IFRS adoption in 2005, and a benchmark sample of 22,807 bank loans issued to 2,642 borrowers from 16 countries that had not mandated IFRS adoption as of 2005, we find that interest rates increase by about 25 basis points after borrowers adopt IFRS mandatorily. Moreover, IFRS borrowers experience a significant reduction in both the use of accounting-based financial covenants and loan maturity, but a significant increase in collateral provisions as well as the portion of a loan retained by its lead arrangers. Given the impact of mandatory IFRS adoption on loan contract terms, we also explore the channels by which it does so. we find that above changes are more pronounced among borrowers experiencing a greater change in financial reporting standards as well as borrowers suffering a greater deterioration in accounting quality after mandatory IFRS adoption.

644010.label: Major findings and research outcome
644010.value: 1. After controlling for loan- and firm- specific determinants of contract terms, as well as country- and industry- fixed effects, we find that interest rates increase by about 25 basis points after borrowers adopt IFRS mandatorily, representing a 26% increase compared to the pre-IFRS period. By contrast, interest rates to borrowers from benchmark countries decrease by 13 basis points during the same period. Furthermore, we find that, relative to the pre-IFRS period, IFRS borrowers experience a significant reduction in both the use of accounting-based financial covenants and loan maturity, but a significant increase in collateral provisions as well as the portion of a loan retained by its lead arrangers. 2.Given the impact of mandatory IFRS adoption on loan contract terms, we also explore the channels by which it does so. Our cross-sectional analysis yields several interesting findings. First, we find that the reduction in accounting-based financial covenants, the increase in collateral provisions, and the increase in the lead arrangers’ loan portions are all more pronounced for borrowers with local standards deviating from IFRS to a greater extent. Second, we find that mandatory IFRS adoption has an uneven impact on accounting quality, with some firms improving their accounting quality and others reducing their accounting quality. More importantly, we find that borrowers whose accounting quality declines after mandatory IFRS adoption are more likely to face more restrictive loan terms, such as greater increases in interest rates, the collateral provisions and the portions of loans held by lead arrangers, and a greater deduction in the use of accounting-based financial covenants. These findings are consistent with banks adjusting loan contract terms in response to increasing information asymmetry and poorer accounting quality subsequent to mandatory IFRS adoption.

644010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
644010.value: 1. Our study focuses on bank loan contracts, future studies can examine the impact of mandatory IFRS adoption on other debt securities, such as bond, CDS. 2. Our study focuses on the mandatory adoption IFRS, future studies can examine the impact of other financial reporting and disclosure events that change the accounting quality or information environment substantially.

644010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
644010.value: Information asymmetry between lenders and borrowers influences lenders’ perceptions of borrower quality and thus their estimation of post-contract monitoring and renegotiating costs. Lenders subsequently factor these risk and cost estimates into loan contract terms. When information asymmetry is high, lenders will set more restrictive loan contract terms to reduce their risks. For example, lenders tend to charge higher interest rates, offer shorter maturities, ask for a collateral provision, and impose stringent financial covenants. If a loan is syndicated by multiple lenders, the lead arrangers have to commit a greater stake in the loan to signal their efforts to monitor borrowers with high information asymmetry. Accounting quality is found to play a critical role in bank loan contracts by mitigating the information asymmetry and estimation risk. Borrowers with low information opacity and high accounting quality receive more favorable loan contract terms while those with poor accounting quality are penalized for higher borrowing costs and more stringent contract terms. The adoption of IFRS can potentially change the information asymmetry and accounting quality of borrowers, lenders will take this effect into account and adjust loan contracts accordingly.

644310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644310.value: Price momentum as documented by Jegadeesh and Titman (1993) and earnings momentum as originally documented by Ball and Brown (1968) and later confirmed by Bernard and Thomas (1989) and others are the two prominent anomalies that cannot be explained by the Fama and French (1993) three-factor models. A number of explanations have been proposed to explain these two anomalies, including rational models and behavioral models. Rational models argue that recent past winners or firms with recent positive earnings surprises are riskier, and therefore should earn higher returns. Behavioral models suggest that momentum occurs because investors are committed to behavioral biases such as conservatism or overconfidence and biased self attribution. In this proposal, we extend the return decomposition methodology originally developed by Chen and Zhao (2009a; 2009b) to decompose the realized momentum profits into three components: the return attributed to cash flow news, the return attributed to discount rate news, and the expected component of returns. By decomposing momentum profit into these three components, we hope to distinguish between behavioral and rational explanations of momentum profits. The project will be divided into three parts. In the first part, among the three components, we will document which is the major contributor of momentum profits. In the second part, we will investigate return patterns attributed to each of these three components both before and after portfolio formation. The investigations can help us to determine whether the behavioral or rational models are more plausible to explain the profits of momentum strategies. It has been documented that momentum profits are more profound when information is more uncertain. The last part of the proposal will examine whether our results based on this return decomposition are consistent with this prediction. The results of the project will contribute to the literature that considers the major contributors to momentum profits, which, in turn, can help us to distinguish between the behavioral and rational explanations. 價格動量投資策略和盈利動量投資策略是財務學界兩種最重要，無法以三因子模式來解釋的異常報酬現象。目前的解釋大致可分為兩類：理性模式和行為模式，理性模式認為過去股價表現良好和最近盈利有驚喜的公司其風險較高，所以其未來股價報酬亦會較高，行為模式則認為動量投資策略之所以成功是由於投資者過份保守或過渡自信所造成的結果。 夲研究計劃將利用報酬分解法將實現動量報酬分解成三個部份：(1)現金流報酬，(2)折現率報酬，和(3)預期報酬。從而希望能幫助我們分辨動量利潤到底是理性的或行為的解釋較合理。此研究計劃可分三部份：(1) 我們將提供證據到底此三部份中，那一部份對動量利潤的貢獻最大，(2) 同時我們將研究此三部份報酬中，在投資組合形成前後各部份的表現，以瞭解到底是理性模式或是行為模式較能解釋動量利潤，(3)最後我們會探討訊息不對稱是否對我們的結果有所影響。 夲研究計劃對我們瞭解什麼是動量利潤的最大貢獻者將有所助益，從而幫助我們分辨到底動量利潤是由於投資者理性的行為或是非理性的行為造成的。

644310.label: Realisation of objectives
644310.value: The major objective of this project is to examine which explanation is better in explaining the price and earnings momentum profitability (i.e., past winners outperform past losers) using a return decomposition approach. We follow the return decomposition approach suggested by Chen, Da, and Zhao (2013) to decompose the realized return into three components: (i) the expected return component associated with risk, (ii) the cash flow news component associated with earnings surprises, and (iii) the discount rate news component associated with the change in investor risk aversion. We also apply the same return decomposition approach to study which explanation is better in explaining the accrual anomaly (i.e., low accrual firms outperform high accrual firms). We find that the profitability of the momentum strategy and the profitability of the accrual strategy mainly come from the cash flow component, especially for firms with more information uncertainty, while the expected return component does not play important role. The results in both studies tend to support the behavioral mispricing-based explanation and fail to support the rational risk-based explanations. This project has generated two papers: (1) “Price and earnings momentum: An explanation using return decomposition,” and (2) How does the market read information conveyed by accruals? Both papers have been presented in reputable international finance conferences. In addition, both papers have been submitted to journals for publication consideration. Hence, our objectives of the project have been more than achieved.

644310.label: Major findings and research outcome
644310.value: This project has generated the following two papers. The major findings are as follows: 1. Qinghao Mike Mao and K.C. John Wei, 2012, “Price and earnings momentum: An explanation using return decomposition.” We test the rational and behavioral explanations for price and earnings momentum by applying a return decomposition method. We find that momentum profits do not come from the expected return component. Further analysis shows that the cash flow news component is quite persistent, while the discount rate news component dominates the time-series variations of momentum returns. Earnings momentum relies more on past cash flow news than price momentum and does not display a long-term reversal like price momentum does. Overall, our evidence supports the behavioral explanation in that the market incorporates cash flow information too slowly, which drives momentum returns. 2. Qinghao Mike Mao and K.C. John Wei, 2013, “How Does the Market Read Information Conveyed by Accruals?” We use return decomposition to differentiate the earnings fixation explanation from the growth explanations for the accrual anomaly. We show that the underperformance of high-accrual stocks mainly comes from the underperformance in the cash flow news component of returns with the effect being stronger when information uncertainty is high. In addition, stocks with high discretionary accruals experience lower total returns and lower cash flow news returns both before and after portfolio formation. Such a pattern is not observed for stock portfolios sorted by nondiscretionary accruals. A comparison between accruals and other growth proxies suggest that the former has much stronger predictive power for subsequent total returns and cash flow news returns. Overall, the results favor the earnings fixation explanation more than the rational or behavioral growth explanation. The evidence is also consistent with the agency theory of earnings management.

644310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
644310.value: After several years of studies on the cross-sectional return predictability (including the current one) in the U.S. and the international markets, it seems that most of these so-called anomalies associated with the cross-sectional return predictability mainly only exist in the developed markets and not in the emerging markets. So far, there is no integrated theory that can explain this surprising cross-sectional return predictability pattern across countries. Sheridan Titman, Feixue Xie, and I are currently working on a project which is intended to come up with a unified explanation for this phenomenon.

644310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
644310.value: In both papers, we find that, in general, the cross-sectional return predictability based on momentum and accrual trading strategies mainly comes from the earrings surprise component. The results suggest that both analysts and investors tend to underreact to the earnings news, especially for firms being more difficult to evaluate. Our results imply that smart rational investors can profit from the investors and analysts’ underreaction to earnings news. That is, it is more profitable to buy stocks with upward earnings revisions or positive earnings surprises than stocks with downward earnings revisions or negative earnings surprises.

644510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644510.value: While scholars have acknowledged the importance of higher education in social mobility and elite formation in state socialist China (as in elsewhere), most previous studies focused on comparisons between individuals with college educations and individuals without, treating the former as a homogeneous group and their tertiary educational experience as a “black box.” With the rapid expansion of higher education in China since the later 1990s, the increasing inequality in access to college education and decreasing job opportunities for college graduates have led to a heated public debate on the educational policies in China. This project aims to continue the collection of the panel data on college students from 15 universities in Beijing, and to investigate the role of higher education in social stratification and elite formation in contemporary China, focusing on how college students acquire human capital and/or political capital to facilitate their transition from school to work and subsequent career development. Specifically, the PI plans: (1) to examine social inequality in access to different types of higher education among those who have already been able to enter colleges; (2) to analyze the process of the party’s recruitment among college students and of students’ applications for party membership; and (3) to investigate the process of the transition from school to work and the roles of human capital, political capital, and social capital in their subsequent career development and labor market success. Findings from the project will not only provide empirical documentation for the first time on the tertiary schooling process in China but also clarify the mechanisms of inequality generation and elite formation, thus contributing to the theorization on social stratification under China's unique political economy. Such a comprehensive understanding of educational processes and stratification outcomes will also provide a solid basis for policy makers to design appropriate programs to reform higher education and address unemployment issues for college graduates. 摘要 雖然學者早已知道在社會主義國家中，如中國或其他地方，高等教育對社會流動和精英構成起了非常重要的作用，但是大多數的研究只著重比較有沒有接受大學教育的個人差異，這些研究都把所有接受大學教育的人視為同類，也把他們的接受大專教育過程當成一個“黑盒子”。90年代後期，隨著中國高等教育迅速地擴張，升入大學的不平等機會就不斷地增加，同時，大學畢業生就業機會又不斷地下降，這激發了社會上對中國教育政策的激烈地討論。 本研究目的是繼續收集北京巿15所大學學生的緃向數據，並探討高等教育在當代中國社會分層與精英構成的作用，研究重點大學生如何利用人力和/或政治資本，以協助自己從學校過渡到工作和日後的職業發展。具體的研究目標有（1）研究家庭對大學生進入不同類型高等學校的影響；（2）分析黨在學校招募學生和學生申請入黨的過程；（3）瞭解學生從學校到工作的過渡，和人力、政治以及社會資本對學生日後的職業發展和工作成就的影響。 這次研究的結果不僅對中國高等教育提供第一手實證文檔，同時瞭解產生不平等和精英的機制，從而促進當今中國的社會分層理論發展。全面地瞭解中國的教育過程和結果將為政策制定提供強而有力的理論基礎，以提高高等教育和改善大學生就業問題。

644510.label: Realisation of objectives
644510.value: This is mainly a survey data collection project. Working with the National Survey Research Center (NSRC) of Renmin University, we have completed 5 waves of survey of two cohorts of students (admitted in 2006 and 2008) from 15 universities in Beijing, in 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, and 2013, respectively. The benchmark survey based on a multistage stratified probability sample includes 4771 colleges students representative of all students enrolled in public tertiary institutions who were admitted in 2006 and 2008. Through the team collaboration with Renmin University, we have tried different means of data collection and survey technology (e.g., access to administrative records for sampling designs, online survey for the follow-ups), we are able to keep the attribution rates at a minimum level (85% for the first three follow-ups in 2010, 2011, 2012). In the 2013 survey, there are 2603 interviewees still remaining with us. Data collected include basic information, psychological well-being, college admission, academic learning, political/social activities, finance/economics, occupational expectation/career planning, value behavior, family background (2009, 2010, 2011), graduate school choice, marriage and romantic relationship, job search and employment (2012), etc. It is a comprehensive, high-quality data set that will be an important source for the study and understanding of Chinese higher education after the expansion. We have conducted some preliminary analyses of the data and published two volume of reports in Chinese as a team (under the editorship of Prof. Li Lulu). We are working on third volume and also analyze the data for English journal publications and special issues in coming years, and perhaps for more funding to continue the survey. We have also worked on some other related papers, with the funding support from the GRF project.

644510.label: Major findings and research outcome
644510.value: We have completed 5 waves of survey of college students in Beijing, starting from 2009 and continuing to track them over their college life and transition from school to work in 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 (with additional resources from Renmin University). Based on the early waves of the data, we've show that, despite the dramatic expansion of tertiary education in China, social stratification within higher education continues to be observed among national elite, national 211 and local universities), with the national elite school on the top and non-research oriented school on the bottom. Access to different higher education opportunities are highly structured by space (home origin), family background, school tracking. Preferential admission policies provide a way alternative to the entrance examination to get ahead in China’s higher education sector (good school and good major), in which students from better-off families are more likely to take advantage. Merit-based performance are determined only by high school type (key-point school). We also found that students from disadvantaged background are more likely to apply and join in the party, whereas those from better family background will be more likely to choose to continue their investment in human capital by attending graduate schools in China and abroad. The analyses on the graduates who have chosen to work show that, attending the elite school pays off in the labor market. However, the pattern we observed was driven, partly by sample selection on those who can attend the elite school, and also on those who choose to graduate school instead of working after graduation. The project has produced a large-scale, rigorously designed, well-implemented panel data, which will be made available via the National Survey Research Center, Renmin University of China. Two volumes of data reports have been published by Renmin University Press in China (in 2012 and 2014), and the third one is under preparation in 2015. One PhD dissertation (Ye Hua, 2012), one M Phil thesis/Dissertation (Li Zhong Lu, in progress) are based on the analyses of the survey data. Ye, Hua 2012 "College Expansion and School to Work Transition in China.", PhD Dissertation, Division of Social Science, HKUST. Li, Zhonglu 2013 "Can a College Degree Ensure Equal Opportunities?: Family Origin and College Graduates' Outcomes." M Phil thesis, Division of Social Science, HKUST. Several other relevant journal articles, working papers and book chapters are produced with the research support from the project. More are in progress of preparation.

The first wave of national representative survey of middle/high school students were completed in 2014. We plan to continue the collaboration and may jointly apply for the funding in the future.

644810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644810.value: The debate on exchange rate regime has been at the center of international monetary economics for decades. Friedman (1953) and later Mundell (1961) argue that the flexible exchange rate can act as an efficient mechanism for dealing with country-specific productivity shocks when the adjustment of domestic price levels is sluggish. This is because in face of country-specific shocks, although the price is sticky, the adjustment of relative prices between domestic goods and foreign goods can be achieved through the exchange rate fluctuation. Therefore, with flexible exchagne rates, the allocation of resources will be efficient and the same as that under flexible prices. But recent studies of monetary policy in utility-based open economy sticky-price models find that the desirability of flexible exchange rates depends critically on export firms’ pricing behavior. If the export goods prices are set in the producer’s currency, then flexible exchange rates can replicate the flexible price equilibrium. That is, flexible exchagne rates can help to However, if the prices are set in the buyer’s currency (local currency), international relative prices cannot be adjusted by exchange rate changes due to the lack of exchange rate pass-through. Therefore, optimal monetary policy is not able to replicate the flexible price equilibrium. Thus, an interesting question arises; what policies can replace the role of exchange rate to adjust the relative prices between countries in the presence of local currency pricing and thus replicate the flexible price equilibrium. In this project, we will explore the role of fiscal instrument and its implementation for the stabilization policy in an open economy disturbed by country-specific shocks, when the domestic price level is sticky. We will first investigate whether the international tax policy can be used to replace the role of exchange rate and achieve the flexible price allocation under local currency pricing. Then we will explore how to conduct the fiscal policy in open economy when monetary policy is not able to eliminate the inefficiency caused by the nominal rigidity and export pricing. 有關匯率制度的辯論在过去几十年来一直是國際货币经济学这一领域的中心 问题。弗里德曼（1953），和後來蒙代爾（1961）都認為，当國內價格水平的调整是粘性时，靈活的匯率制度可以作為一個有效的機制来应对单个國家的 生產力冲击。這是因為在某个具体國家的生产力受到衝擊时，雖然價格是粘性的，國內商品和國外商品的相對價格调整可以通過 匯率的波動来实现。因此，当汇率可以灵活调整时， 資源分配将和价格可以灵活调整时一樣高效。 但是，以效用函数為基礎的開放型經濟粘性價格模型最近的在对货币政策的研究中發現，靈活的匯率政策是否最优主要取決於出口企業的 定價行為。如果出口貨物的價格是以生產者的貨幣定价，那么 靈活的匯率制度可以複製无价格粘性的那个均衡。但如果價格是以消费者的貨幣（買方/當地貨幣定价，國際相對價格就不能随匯率的變化而调整，因为 匯率变化不能傳遞到消费者面对的价格。因此，最優貨幣政策不 能夠複製靈活價格的那个均衡。因此，一個有趣的問題產生了。在当地货币定价的情况下，什麼政策可以取代灵活的汇率机制的作用，調整国内外商品之間的相對價格，從而複製无价格粘性的均衡。 在這個項目中，我們將探討財政政策工具在开放型经济的稳定政策中的 作用及其启示。我們將首先調查在当地货币定价的情况下， 國際稅收 政策能否否替代灵活匯率机制，实现在靈活價格下的资源 分配。然後我們將探討在一个開放的經濟中， 当貨幣政策無法消除 由於名義剛性和出口價格所导致的低效率时， 如何实施国际財政 政策协调来提高资源分配的效率， 从而实现无价格粘性的均衡。

644810.label: Realisation of objectives
644810.value: We show that a state-contingent tax policy combination with consumption tax (subsidy) and export subsidy (tax) can fully mimic the response of monetary policy to country-specific productivity shocks and achieve the flexible price allocation. This arrangement, however, requires international policy coordination, and it cannot be an equilibrium outcome to international tax game without any restriction. To makes these tax policies effective and also eliminate their externality, some restrictions should be imposed through international coordination. So international coperation between countries in this aspect are important. So we have achieved the twp objectives listed in the orginal application. Our results imply that state-contingent tax policy should be taken into consideration when the economy lack of exchange rate flexibility due to structural frictions or policy constraints. This is extremely important given the zero bound of monetary policies adopted by ECB or Fed after the 2008 financial crisis. It is also relevant for countries in the euro zone since common currency may restrict use of exchange rate or monetary policies.

644810.label: Major findings and research outcome
644810.value: It is well known in international macroeconomics literature that with local currency pricing (LCP), the function of exchange rate to adjust relative prices between countries is limited, then monetary authorities should keep exchange rate fixed, and the welfare under LCP is always lower than that of PCP structure. As an result, the optimal monetary policy cannot replicate the flexible price equilibrium. In this paper, we would like to explore if the fiscal policy can replace the role of exchange rate to adjust the relative prices between countries in the presence of LCP and thus replicate the flexible prices equilibrium. We find that a policy combination of consumption tax (subsidy) and export subsidy (tax) can deliver the economy to the flexible price allocation even in the presence of local currency pricing. Since exchange rate changes have effects on both the consumers and producers sides, to mimic the function of exchange rate, we need two policy instruments. One is used to adjust the price faced by consumers, the other one is used to adjust the preset export prices. Therefore, to respond a positive domestic productivity shock, home country should impose a consumption tax on imported foreign goods, while foreign country gives a same subsidy to its export goods to home market. This policy combination can shift the aggregate goods from foreign goods to home goods in both countries and also make the relative prices between countries completely respond to productivity shocks. In such a case, a flexible price allocation can be replicated even in the economy with a fixed exchange rate. This arrangement, however, cannot be simply achieved in an international tax game. This because that both consumption tax and export subsidy policies have cross-border externality. Therefore, no country can gain from an international tax game with a single consumption tax or export subsidy policy. However, when both policies are considered, one country’s consumption tax can eliminate the externality caused by other country’s export subsidy policy and vice versa. Therefore, in a game with such competition, without any policy restriction, there will be equilibrium outcome for international tax game. To makes these tax policies effective and also eliminate their externality, some restrictions should be imposed through international coordination. Our results imply that state-contingent tax policy should be taken into consideration when the economy lack of exchange rate flexibility due to structural frictions or policy constraints.

644810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
644810.value: Based on these results, the next question I want to explore is that if the set of fiscal instrument matters for the replication of flexible price allocation. As shown by Correia, Nicolini, and Teles (2008), the set of fiscal instrument matters in the closed economy models. They consider both labor income and consumption tax and find the optimal allocation can be replicated, which is in contrast to the conclusion in Benigno and Woodford (2004), Schmitt-Grohe and Uribe (2004), and Siu (2004) where only one kind of tax instrument is used. Adao, Correia, and Teles (2006) also consider both labor income and consumption tax. Nevertheless, in open economy models, another kind of tax instrument one can consider is the export tax/subsidy. So I intend to study if the set of fiscal instrument matters to achieve the flexible price allocation, especially when the international policy coordination problem is taken into consideration. Is labor income tax necessary? Can we simply use consumption taxes and trade policy to replicate the flexible price equilibrium? If we use the labor income tax instead of export tax/subsidy, is international fiscal policy coordination required?

644810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
644810.value: Flexible exchange rates can help to adjust the relative price of home to foreign goods in response to country-specific productivity shocks when prices cannot adjust. Resources will then be allocated efficently towards to places with higher productivity. However, recent studies find that this advantage of flexible exchange will disappear when exporters set export prices in the buyer's/local currency (LCP). This is because with LCP, exchange rate changes cannot adjust the relative price. In this paper we study if other kind of policies can adjust the relative price when prices are set under LCP. It has important policy implications, because LCP becomes more prevalent in the global trade today. For example, in the US, 90% imports are invoiced in dollars. We find that a fiscal combination with consumption tax (subsidy) and export subsidy (tax) can fully adjust the relative price in response to a country-specific shock. Therefore, even with LCP, it is still possible to achieve the efficient resource allocation. This is extremely important given limitation of monetary policies adopted by ECB or Fed after the financial crisis. It is also relevant for countries in the euro zone since common currency may restrict use of exchange rate or monetary policies.

Whether market reacts to opinions of analyst reports, in addition to the information of earnings forecasts and stock recommendations? What are the circumstances where opinions are particularly informative?

645210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645210.value: The proposed project studies the opinions extracted from the qualitative information contained in analyst reports by using a computational opinion classification approach. Specifically, we use a naive Bayesian machine learning approach developed by computer scientists in the area of sentiment analysis, to analyze and extract opinions from the textual information contained in analyst reports. Prior research on financial analysts largely focuses on quantitative information contained in analyst reports, i.e., earnings forecasts, stock recommendations and target prices. Very few papers examine the content of written reports; and they content analyze analyst reports either manually for small samples, or via experimentation (Hirst, Koonce and Simko 1995). Compared with prior work, the automatic opinion classification method used in our study will greatly shorten the time for extracting opinions from textual information, and will enable us to document large sample evidence on the biases of opinions, the association between opinions and earnings forecasts and stock recommendations, and the incremental informativeness of opinions beyond earnings forecasts and stock recommendations. The evidence will shed lights on whether analysts curry favor with management with their report content, and whether affiliated analysts have more incentives to do so than unaffiliated analysts. The study will also provide insights to the literature on the circumstances where opinions in written reports are particularly informative: when analysts are high-ability or independent, or when other elements in reports contain inconsistent, biased, or bold signals. 分析家們是資本市場中最重要的信息中介機構之一。機構和個人投資者認為分析師報告為他們的投資決策提供最有影響的信息（SRI報告，1987）。軼事和研究證據表明，市場對分析家的報告能做出反應（如Schipper，1991年和Ramnath，Rock和Shane，2006）。一個典型的分析報告包含幾個關鍵要素：盈利預測，股票推薦，有時提供目標價格，還有對個股平均長達6.3頁的文字分析。 該項目使用電腦自動化意見分類方法提取和量化分析報告中的文字信息。具體來說，我們使用計算機科學家在情感分析中使用的樸素貝葉斯機器學習方法來分析和提取分析報告中的文字信息（以下簡稱意見）。該意見衡量一個分析師在她的分析報告的文字中是否對公司有正面，負面還是中性的預測，以及她的觀點的強烈程度。我們將研究分析家的意見是否存在偏見，意見和盈利預測和股票推薦之間是否一致，和考慮到盈利預測和股票推薦後意見中包含的資訊。 以前的研究主要集中在金融分析師的報告中的量化信息，即盈利預測，股票推薦和目標價格。只有極少數的論文研究分析報告中的文字內容：他們或手動分析小樣本的分析報告，或通過做實驗來分析文字內容的使用價值（Hirst等人， 1995）。本研究可以成為第一個使用計算機科學和統計中發展完善的樸素貝葉斯機器學習方法來分析大樣本的分析報告的項目。 擬議的研究將會有下列貢獻。首先，它記載大樣本分析報告中意見的屬性和包含的資訊。相較於以前的工作，我們研究中使用的自動分類方法將大大縮短從文本信息提取意見的時間，使我們能記載大樣本裡意見是否存在偏見，意見和報告中其他信息是否一致，和意見裡的資訊。這些證據可以在大樣本裡證實傳聞中所說的，對於投資而言，分析報告中的文字比盈利預測和股票推薦更加有用。其次，我們的證據將能幫助我們理解分析家是否用報告中的文字向企業管理者討好，以及有關聯的分析家是否更有動機這麼做。第三，我們的研究將幫助大家理解什麼時候投資者更加看重分析報告，比如說，是否在分析家能力高時，在分析家更加獨立時，在報告中有不一致信息時，有偏見時，或者有和其他分析師不同的信息時。

645210.label: Realisation of objectives
645210.value: Using a sample of 363,953 equity analyst reports from the US equity market, we extract the opinions from their text with the naive Bayes machine learning approach. We empirically test the hypotheses related to the project objectives and find empirical evidence that answer the questions in the objectives. Specifically, for the first research question, "whether the opinions of analyst reports support or contradict analysts' earnings forecasts and stock recommendations?", we found evidence consistent with textual opinions being consistent with the quantitative summary signals released by analysts contemporaneously, including earnings forecasts, stock recommendations, and target prices. We have found that the textual opinions are not provided to support any one of the quantitative summary signals, but to capture the information content of all the summary signals. We have also found that, however, all the quantitative signals, combined with recent stock performance and firms characteristics, explain only a small portion of the variation in textual opinions, suggesting that textual opinions contain substantial information that is orthogonal to the quantitative summary signals. For the second project objective "whether market reacts to opinions of analyst reports, in addition to the information of earnings forecasts and stock recommendations?", we found that investor reacts to textual opinions, conditional on the quantitative summary measures released contemporaneously. The reactions are also economically significant. In addition, we found that investors attach substantially more weight to negative than to positive statements, suggesting that analysts are especially important in propagating bad news. For the third project objective, "what are the circumstances where opinions are particularly informative?" We found that investors find report text particularly informative in the following situation: when analyst report text places more emphasis on nonfinancial topics, when it is written more assertively and concisely, and when the perceived validity of other information signals in the reports is low.

645210.label: Major findings and research outcome
645210.value: We use the naïve Bayes machine learning approach to extract opinions from the text of 363,952 analyst reports. We show that analyst report text provides information to investors beyond the earnings forecasts, stock recommendations, and target prices released contemporaneously, and helps investors interpret these signals. Cross-sectionally, we find that investors react significantly more strongly to negative text than to positive text, suggesting that analysts are especially important in propagating bad news. In addition, the findings show that analyst report text is more useful when it places more emphasis on nonfinancial topics, when it is written more assertively and concisely, and when the perceived validity of other information signals in the reports is low.

645210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645210.value: We believe that studying the information content of analyst report text is only the starting point of a potentially fruitful research area. There is scope for future research aimed at answering interesting questions, such as how analysts’ incentives affect the way they write up reports and whether corporate decisions are influenced by analysts’ comments in their reports. We plan to develop hypotheses and conduct empirical tests in these research areas.

645210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645210.value: Analyst report text is a means by which analysts provide information to investors, regardless of whether investors agree with their final conclusions. According to II’s annual survey, since 1998, investors consistently rank written reports as a far more important research output from analysts than stock recommendations and earnings forecasts. The emphasis that market participants place on written reports stands in stark contrast to the amount of effort that researchers have made to understand them. Using the naïve Bayes machine learning approach, we extract textual opinions from 363,952 analyst reports issued for S&P 500 firms. This approach enables us to provide large-sample evidence on the information content of analyst report text. We find that, in general, investors react to analyst report text and that the market reaction triggered by text is economically significant. Moreover, investors react to the favorable (unfavorable) quantitative summary measures more strongly when the textual opinion is more positive (negative), indicating that text is also useful in helping investors interpret headlines.We also provide important insights into the cross-sectional variation in the information content of analyst report text.

645510.label: Project Objectives
645510.value: To collect data, ensure their accuracy, and conduct systematic analyses of multifunctional grams in Chinese dialects, including prepositions, conjunctions, adverbs, aspect markers, particles, auxiliary verbs, and pronouns. To collect data, ensure their accuracy, and conduct systematic analyses of multifunctional constructions in Chinese dialects, including the disposal, ditransitive, reduplicative, directional, coordinative & subordinative constructions. To build semantic maps for the multifunctional Chinese grams and constructions analyzed, thereby detailing their semantic and syntactic attributes and revealing relevant synchronic and diachronic implications. To refine and extend the SMM by testing it on Chinese dialects and by dealing with critical methodological issues such as exceptions, loops, the dimensionality of the maps, and suitable mathematical models. To make contributions to Chinese dialectology, historical linguistics (including grammaticalization and language change), typology, language contact, cognitive linguistics and the study of human conceptualization.

645510.label: Realisation of objectives
645510.value: The present project has not realized 100% in every objective for several reasons. First, the original proposal was too ambitious, given that the Semantic Map Model is a new approach, which is also rather complicated in its attempt to conduct cross-language analyses in both diachronic and synchronic studies. Second, the original proposal aimed to include as many multifunctional grammatical forms and Chinese dialects as possible. Third, the PI has been suffering from ill health and unavoidable medication which occasionally made him unfit for any work. However, the PI does intend to continue to work on the semantic map model in the typology and historical studies of Chinese dialects. In fact, he is still supervising a doctoral student whose dissertation is related to the present project. In relation to the first two objectives, the PI and his graduate students have done fieldwork on Chinese dialects in Gansu, Ningxia and Qinghai regions. They have also collected data from the Beijing, Changsha and Chongqing dialects, and from other dialects in Hubei, Shaanxi and Zhejiang Provinces. In relation to the other three objectives, the 2015 collection of papers 漢語多功能語法形式的語義地圖研究 (_The Semantic Map Approach to Multifunctional Grammatical Forms in Chinese_), published in Beijing by the Commercial Press, has been the first major Chinese monograph on the application of the semantic map model in the study of Chinese. It is the best Chinese introduction to the methodology and actual application of the semantic map approach. In particular, there are many original semantic maps in the monograph. For example, a paper written by a Japanese student at the Chinese Department of Peking University has a total of 48 maps on the meaning of _shenme_ (roughly the same as “what” in English) in many languages and Chinese dialects. The most significant impact of the present project is a paradigmatic shift in studying the history and dialects of the Chinese language.

645510.label: Major findings and research outcome
645510.value: Major findings of the present project can be found in (a) two M.Phil. theses and two doctoral dissertations at HKUST, (b) the presentations and publications listed in Part C, (c) the 2015 monograph 漢語多功能語法形式的語義地圖研究 (The Semantic Map Approach to Multifunctional Grammatical Forms in Chinese), published by the Commercial Press. As mentioned in the Preface of the monograph, in September 2007 the first major workshop on semantic maps, entitled “Semantic Maps: Methods and Applications”, took place in Germany. In the following year, the PI of the present project visited Peking University and introduced the new approach to linguists working on the dialects and history of Chinese. Subsequently, their research output, including papers written by the PI and his students, were put together in the 2015 monograph. There are a total of 17 papers, seven of which discuss the methodology of semantic maps, and the other ten are on specific grammatical units in various varieties of Chinese. There is a paper on the benefactive category in _Zuo Zhuan_, a Chinese history book of late 4th century B.C., written by a former student of the PI’s, who is now a professor at the National University of Singapore. The PI himself has devoted his recent research to the unique characteristics of Chinese grammar, including the well-known bǎ construction (a.k.a. the disposal structure), in comparison with languages around the world. He has tried to account for the unique characteristics (as highlighted in the semantic maps model) from the perspective of typology and language contact. In his latest paper of 2016, the PI discusses 16 maps on oblique roles in relation to the merits of two-dimensional vs. three-dimensional maps. The PI puts forward the Interface Hypothesis to deal with three-dimensional maps in a principled way: “On a largely non-vacuous map, if three-dimensionality is unavoidable, the third dimension must occur at the interface nodes linking two separate domains.”

645510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645510.value: The objectives as listed in Section 5.2 can be said to be open-ended. The PI will definitely continue to work on them and to promote the semantic map approach among Chinese dialectologists and grammarians. The PI is still in the process of writing his own monograph, tentatively entitled _Comparative Dialectal Syntax of Chinese on Semantic Maps and Spatial Maps_ 語義地圖和空間地圖上的漢語方言比較語法, to be published by the Shanghai Educational Publishing House. It will be a significant contribution to Chinese linguistics and the development of the semantic maps model.

645510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645510.value: In every language, there are grammatical units having more than one meaning. For example, “to” in English can denote a direction, purpose or recipient, as in “go to Room 246”, “come to see me”, and “give it to John”. The Semantic Map Model is the latest approach in Western linguistics to examine patterns of polysemy in grammatical units across languages. The Chinese language, with a rich variety of regional dialects and a long documented history, would be ideal for testing the SMM. Three tasks have been undertaken: (A) collection and analysis of data, (B) reexamination of existing semantic maps, and (C) building new maps. In Task A, many multifunctional grammatical units from various Chinese dialects have been analyzed. In Task B, existing semantic maps have been revised against Chinese data. In Task C, new maps have been built in a “bottom-up” approach, first exclusively from Chinese data and then compared with other languages. The present project has established a new paradigm that combines humanistic insights with scientific rigor in the field of comparative Chinese dialectal grammar, and that encourages Chinese dialectologists to engage in research beyond mere description, thereby contributing to the typological, cognitive and theoretical studies of world languages.

645710.label: Project Objectives

645710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645710.value: Insider trading erodes the confidence of investors and is antithetical to market fairness and efficiency. Insider trading increases cost of capital and hurts overall economic growth. Despite intensive monitoring and severe punishment, insider trading produces economically significant profits even in well-governed securities markets such as those in the United States. Consequently, the search for an efficient regulation mechanism for insider trading remains one of the most important topics in security market regulation. This study proposes that an effective corporate internal control system helps curtail opportunistic insider trading activities and therefore offers an important alternative to the current insider trading regulation mechanism that relies mostly on outsiders such as regulating agencies or other market participants. We propose an empirical investigation into the relationship between internal control effectiveness and opportunistic insider trading behavior. We plan to investigate not only the cross-sectional variation of insider trading, comparing companies with different levels of internal control effectiveness, but also the time-series changes in insider trading as companies’ internal control effectiveness changes over time. We plan to examine multiple insider trading characteristics including profitability, frequency and timing as well as insider trades’ impact on stock market information asymmetry. This proposed research will be of interest to academics, practitioners and regulators. 内幕交易有损投资者的信心，也对资本市场的公平及效率产生负面影响。同时，内幕交易也会提高资金成本，并影响经济的发展。尽管针对内幕交易有着严格的监控及惩罚措施，但即便在监管严格的美国资本市场，通过内幕交易仍能获得巨大的经济利益。因此，研究出一个高效的内幕交易监管机制始终是资本市场监管领域最重要的课题之一。 这份研究提出有效的公司内部控制机制可以有效抑制内幕交易，所以公司内部控制是可以成为内幕交易监管的一种有效补充。我们将用经验数据来分析公司内部监管机制的效率与公司内幕交易之间的关系。我们将不仅抽样调查代表性的内幕交易，比较不同内部监管等级的公司，也将比较在公司的内部监管机制的效率变化的情况下，内幕交易的变化情况。我们将研究内幕交易的多项特征，包括盈利水平、频率、时间，以及内幕交易对资本市场信息不对称的影响。这份研究将对学术界、从业者及监管人员有所帮助。

645910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645910.value: Economists have long sought to understand mechanisms to sustain social cooperation over time. The prominent results come from the literature of repeated games, which can be summarized as that with suitable monitoring cooperation can be sustained when people are patient. The basic idea is that even though a person obtains some gaining today from misbehaving, he is deterred by a bigger loss that society as a whole imposes to him in the future, provided that his misbehavior can somehow be detected. When the person’s action is only partially monitored, i.e., the action is only observed by some people in society, there is an interesting route to detect. That is, those people can report their observation to society. Indeed, the literature shows that at least for some games, reporting or communication is effective to sustain cooperation under partial monitoring. This is interesting because many real-life interactions are partially monitored and in practice people do sometimes report to others. In this project, we ask whether reporting is effective when people may trade reports. Such a trade is ruled out by assumptions in the literature but it is a concern for the following reason. For reporting to be effective, the person's future payoff must depend on the content of the report made by his observer. But then the misbehaving person desires to "bribe" his observer to misreport. That is, they may trade a report, which may undermine the effectiveness of reporting. We address the question in an environment populated with a large number of people. In each date people are randomly matched in pairs, and in each meeting it is ex ante optimal for two people cooperate to insure each other against some endowment uncertainty, i.e., to transfer some endowment from one to another according the realization of uncertainty. But the transfer is only observed by those two people. So without report no transfer occurs ex post. There are two perceivable report-trading schemes. In one report making and the transfer are determined simultaneously, i.e., the report is directly traded with actions. In another the transfer precedes report making, and the report is traded with some other objects. We suspect that the effectiveness of reporting depends on the trading scheme and on how a trade is reached, and that under the second scheme some means to verify the truthiness of a report may be critical. In this project we shall examine those conjectures thoroughly. 在重複博弈中，當人們有足夠的耐心并有適當的監督，合作能夠持續。文献中一个分支研究溝通或報告在維持合作上的作用。報告能工巧匠防止一個人從事不良行為，該人的未來收益必須要依赖于他的觀察員的報告。鑑於這種依賴，这个人與他的觀察者可能會願意就報告的内容（與其他有价值的對象）進行交易，而就報告内容的交易可能削弱報告的成效。現有的文獻排除了（由假設）这样的交易。在這裡，我們研究兩個模型。在这些模型里，（1）如果沒有報告就沒有合作；（2）如果有報告但沒有報告交易機會，可以很容易地持續合作如故人们有足夠的耐心。我们发现当人們可交易報告的内容时，报告的有效性取决与一系列的因素。

645910.label: Realisation of objectives
645910.value: This project starts with a simple point. When the true history of actions is only observed by a subset of agents, messages created by the observers of actions may enhance cooperation---if you misbehave, your conduct will be revealed by messages and you will be punished in future. But exactly as such, there are incentives to manipulate messages---if you misbehave, you may bribe me not to reveal your conduct by my messages. So the question is how effective messages can be in supporting cooperation when messages can be exchanged with valuable object. This is a rather broad theme and would potentially leads to a few different subjects. In the process to work out the project, we gradually adjust our focus to a specific subject. Specifically, we focus on models with matching in pairs and on pairwise monitoring---actions taken in each pairwise meeting are observed only by the pair of agents in the meeting. We develop a theory for information revelation by maintaining pairwise monitoring as a primitive. Although not necessarily restricted to, our theory is placed on a decentralized risk-sharing model. With pairwise monitoring of risk-sharing actions, our objectives are (a) define an exact sense that a technology reveals information about pairwise monitored actions, (b) figure conditions that ensure full revelation for pairwise monitored actions, and (c) determine the extent of sustainable cooperation in a large population. (Objective (c) pertains to conjectures in the original proposal.) We have achieved all objectives.

645910.label: Major findings and research outcome
645910.value: Objectives (a) and (b) in 5.3 above are more straightforward to address with finite horizon. For objective (a), we inherit an invaluable point made by Townsend in a finite-horizon decentralized risk-sharing model. That is, tokens, a currency-like technology, are a special case of written messages in revealing pairwise monitored risk-sharing actions. We develop Townsend's point in two directions. First, an information revelation technology is a medium of messages such that messages being carried cannot be freely counterfeited after they are generated. Distinguishing factors of the technology are the space of messages it supports, the degree of publicity it permits, and the physical and institutional characteristics it assumes to achieve the non-counterfeit property. Second, the technology is subject to message trading, a generalized version of monetary exchange. In our context, this means that the buyer and seller can exchange messages to be carried by the technology with cake, the present valuable object. For objective (b) in 5.3 above, it renders to a mechanism-design problem in the finite horizon context. We characterize the efficient mechanism. This characterization is non trivial when the agents cannot commit not to renegotiate a Pareto dominated outcome in message trading. The reason is that one party has the surplus-destruction power (he can eat the cake before sharing) in the sense of Dasgupta and Maskin and the initial surplus (i.e., the one before the party destroys the surplus) is endogenous, for it depends on planner's capacities to reward and punish agents, the terms that are chose (and, hence, endogenized) by the planner. We take a novel approach to such a problem. For objective (c) in 5.3 above, we build our results on results obtained from objective (b). As we move to infinite horizon, we are able to clarify issues that can not be addressed with finite horizon.

645910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645910.value: Our contributions to objectives (a) and (b), in the finite-horizon context, provide a unified partial-equilibrium approach to analyzing technologies that resembles payment methods such as currency, checks, and credit cards. Most importantly, such a technology serves a medium of exchange because it is a medium of messages. This point can be much developed in the future research.

645910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645910.value: This project starts with a simple point about the function of messages. If you misbehave and I see you misbehave, your conduct will be revealed by my messages and you will be punished in future, which deters your misbehavior at the first place. But exactly as such, there are incentives to manipulate messages---if you misbehave, you may bribe me not to reveal your conduct by my messages. So the question is how effective messages can be in supporting cooperation when messages can be exchanged with a valuable object. This is a rather broad theme. In this project, we focus to a specific subject. We focus on models with matching in pairs and on pairwise monitoring---actions taken in each pairwise meeting are observed only by the pair of persons in the meeting. We develop a theory for information revelation by maintaining pairwise monitoring as a primitive. Although not necessarily restricted to, our theory is placed on a decentralized risk-sharing model. With pairwise monitoring of risk-sharing actions, our objectives are (a) define an exact sense that a technology reveals information about pairwise monitored actions, (b) figure conditions that ensure full revelation for pairwise monitored actions, and (c) determine the extent of sustainable cooperation in a large population. In achieving objectives (a) and (b), we provide a unified partial-equilibrium approach to analyzing technologies that resembles payment methods such as currency, checks, and credit cards. Most importantly, such a technology serves a medium of exchange because it is a medium of messages. In achieving objective (c), we can address important issues that can not be addressed in partial equilibrium.

646010.label: Project Objectives
646010.value: To model possible responses to China’s “resource diplomacy” at the local, bilateral, and triangular level, in order to assess how China’s rise and resource diplomacy is affecting the international system. To evaluate these relationships using three case studies—Venezuela, Australia, and Nigeria—to see how these countries assess China’s current external behaviour and to see if the U.S. is affecting their bilateral relations, thereby making their bilateral ties triangular. To collect data from secondary sources on six more countries to supplement our detailed case studies. These countries will probably be Canada, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, Angola, Kazakhstan and Iran. We will compare the cases based in part on their ties to the U.S. and the nature of their political systems. To evaluate the level of competition, cooperation and conflict between the U.S. and China on energy and resources, and the perceptions held by elites in both countries towards each other’s behaviour. To create a data base of articles in Chinese and English about China’s resource diplomacy which will be used for our book project and which will be made available to the broader community by posting it on the web.

646010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
646010.value: ABSTRACT China’s foreign policy is driven by resource hunger. Massive urbanization is underway; by 2050, 70 percent of Chinese will live in an urban environment. They want apartments, more cars, and air conditioning. As “factory to the world,” China imports large amounts of minerals, such as nickel, iron, bauxite and copper. This urbanization and production consumes growing amounts of energy, making access to oil, gas and minerals a driving force behind much of China’s foreign policy and its search for national power, with enormous implications for the stability of the CCP-led government. But how does this “resource diplomacy” affect China’s relationship with the world? We propose three models. First, due to the international power structure, where a rising power is challenging a declining hegemon, China’s new or enhanced bilateral relations with resource-rich states (RRS) become “triangular,” as America’s ubiquitous influence means that China’s efforts have strategic or economic implications for U.S. power. Therefore, the U.S. has a strong interest in influencing relations between China and the third country with which the PRC is engaging. Second, some resource rich states advance their national interest by manipulating Sino-US ties, giving the U.S. and China grounds to cooperate. Finally, some resource-rich states see China’s rise negatively; while ready to sell resources to Chinese firms, China’s rise threatens their national security. We further divide the world according to the resource rich state’s ties to the U.S.—"pariahs," "neutrals" (including targets of U.S. influence), and "allies"--assuming that America's relations with the third party will influence China ties with it and with the U.S. In the case of pariahs, China will be pressed to pressure the pariah to conform to international norms. As for America's allies, China may push, but the democratic nature of many of these states--Canada, Australia, Mexico—-let their domestic politics and perceptions of national security influence their response to Chinese policy. Finally, neutral states, with the most freedom of choice, are less predictable. They may manipulate investors to get the best deal, push back against aggressive foreign investors or favour one side, depending on their internal political structure and the nature of the regime. We will visit three energy rich countries--Venezuela, Australia and Nigeria-- as well as Beijing and Washington, to assess these bilateral and triangular relationships, their implications for Sino-American relations and for the world’s response to resource diplomacy. Documentary research will supplement comparisons with six other pariahs, neutrals and U.S. allies. 中国对资源的需求常常影响其外交政策。因国家正借大规模城市化，是以到2050年，百分之七十的中国人将在都市内生活。他们需要房屋；他们将驾驶更多车辆，他们渴求空调设备。此外，作为「世界工厂」，中国必须进口大量矿藏如镍、铁、铝矾土、铜。城市化和工业生产的过程中消耗大量的能源且需求不断增加；石油、天然气及不同矿藏等资源供求遂成为许多中国的外交政策及其追求强大国力、希望成为稳定中共领导政府的推动力。 「资源外交」如何影响中国的对外关系？我们提出了三种模式。首先，根据国际权力结构， 即一股崛起的势力在挑战一个霸权正在减弱的大国时，中国与资源丰富的国家（RRS）建立新的或加强了的双边关系的便成「三角关系」，由于美国的势力触及多国，中国的壮大意味着它对美国会有战略或经济上的威胁。因此，美国有很强的利益去左右中国及资源丰富国家之间的关系。其次，一些资源丰富的国家为争取国家利益而操纵中美关系，使美国和中国有了合作的空间。最后，一些资源丰富的国家可能视中国的崛起为威胁，虽仍会出售各种资源予中国公司，然而他们仍认中国的崛起威胁其国家安全。 我们根据这些资源丰富国家跟美国的关系，细分为敌对国，中立国（包括美国力图施加影响的国家），和盟友国– 我们假设这三种双边关系将影响中国与美国及资源丰富国家的关系。中国与美国的盟友国或敌对国发展关系将挑战美国的全球利益。对前者而言，中国将被施压去协助解决使资源丰富国陷入与美国敌对的危机；对后者来说，美国可以试图去推动，但由于这些国家多是民主国家，如加拿大、澳大利亚、墨西哥等，其本土政治和有关国家安全的民意影响他们对中国政策的反应。最后由于拥有最大的选择自由，中立国的意向变得难测。他们可以操纵的投资者以获得最佳利益，它们到底选择推却有野心的外国投资者或是支持另一方，完全取决于其内部政治结构和政府的管治性质。 我们将考察三个资源源丰富的国家，包括委内瑞拉、澳大利亚和尼日利亚， 以及北京和华盛顿，以评估这些双边和三边关系及其作为中美关系和世界的资源外交反应。研究亦会同时将之比较其他六个敌对国，中立国和盟友国。

646010.label: Realisation of objectives
646010.value: We have fully completed the first four tasks. I designed a model outlining the triangular nature of relationships among China, the U.S., and the Resource Rich States (RRS) in terms of China’s and America’s search for energy security, focusing on whether the U.S. uses it influence to slow China’s growth. We then applied it to 10 case/country studies. We first assessed each RRS’s links to China, to the U.S., and then looked to see if the U.S. intervened in China’s bilateral relations with the 10 countries. The study included papers on Australia, Venezuela, Canada, Nigeria, Angola, Kazakhstan, Sudan, Saudi Arabia, Brazil and Iran. I was involved in writing the theoretical chapter, as well as the chapters on Venezuela, Canada, and supplied information for the chapters on Angola and Australia. The volume that is forthcoming from Routledge also includes studies on America’s energy policy and China’s energy policy. I have also written a new paper for the conclusion of the book, called “China’s Energy Anxiety,” a variation of which I will try to publish in an academic journal. As for our fifth objective, I have compiled an excellent bibliography on my own, and will also draw on the bibliographies from the various chapters in the book, to complete a very comprehensive bibliography in both English and Chinese, which we will post online. Two members of the project abdicated their roles in the project, complicating the completion of the goals of the project. Jiang Wenran left the academic field, forcing me to research more on Canada and basically write a paper myself. Also, without him, I had to turn to other people to help write papers. Prof Xu Nengwu went to the U.S. to study English and basically dropped out of the project after he returned to China. Therefore, we faced more difficulties getting access to Chinese decision makers. In the end, Thomas and I did not travel as much as anticipated. Venezuela descended into chaos, particularly after the death of Hugo Chavez, and I was informed of numerous kidnappings. Similarly, Nigeria is not so safe, with Islamic terrorism in the North and a separatist movement in the South. So, given the loss of Jiang and Xu, I decided that rather than write our own book, I used much of our research to supplement and co-author papers on Canada and Venezuela that went into this edited book.
