646010.label: Major findings and research outcome
646010.value: We found that China’s energy partnerships are triangular in shape, with the U.S. the “third” corner. Nevertheless, America’s interference was rarely driven by concerns over China’s strategic rise. For “pariah” states--Iran and Sudan--the U.S. pressured China to eschew energy ties with them due to their involvement in nuclear proliferation and genocide, respectively. Yet, while Venezuelan presidents have been hostile to the U.S. since 1999, and even though Venezuela remains America’s 4th most important oil supplier, the latter has not objected as Venezuela has dramatically increased its oil exports to China from 1.5% to 6.0% in 2007-2013. The U.S. is wary when its allies get too close to China. Whenever Australian officials suggest that they will not help the U.S. defend Taiwan militarily in a confrontation with China, American diplomats have insisted that Australia maintain its strategic commitment. Nevertheless, the U.S. has not blocked Australian energy sales to China. As for Canada, a U.S. Vice-Presidential report linked Canadian oil supplies to U.S. energy security. But, the U.S. did not oppose the sale of a major Canadian oil company, Nexen, with holdings in the U.S., to a Chinese National Oil Company in 2012. In fact, the U.S. encouraged its ally, Saudi Arabia, to help build China’s strategic reserve to undermine China’s energy dependence on Iran. Among our “neutral” states—Brazil, Angola, Nigeria and Kazakhstan—we found that the U.S. was not the third player only in Kazakhstan; there the Russia-China-Kazakh triangle dominated. Still, all three great powers work hard to insure their own pipelines will run from Kazakhstan to Europe (to supply U.S. allies), China or Russia. The most striking impact of America’s “shale revolution” was the dramatic decline in oil exports from West Africa to the U.S., which enhanced China’s energy security. Finally, while the U.S. and China compete over oil, the U.S. and China have not overlapped so much in terms of energy suppliers. But the key locations for future competition could be Canada and Mexico, new arenas of interest for China and long-term suppliers to the U.S. Second, we found limited cooperation in the Resource Rich States. Instead, significant Sino-U.S. energy cooperation occurs between the two governments through formal agreements, new bilateral organizations, and cooperation in technology transfer. Thus despite Chinese deep concerns that the U.S. cannot but use its hegemonic authority over oil to contain China’s rise, we did not find much proof of such activities.

646010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
646010.value: I intend to continue to work on these energy issues, as this grant has helped increase my visibility on this issue. I will have the opportunity to lecture on China’s energy anxiety and its competition with the U.S. as the book comes online. I also intend to finish the bibliography which we will post online. In terms of China’s energy driven foreign policy, I am particularly interested in keeping up on Canada, Australia and Venezuela.

646010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
646010.value: Some theories suggest that the U.S., as the world’s leading power, should block China’s rise to protect its own dominant position. If true, complicating China’s search for energy would be an excellent strategy. To test this idea, the PI looked at China-US relations and 10 energy rich states. The U.S. did pressure China to cut ties with Iran and Sudan, which the U.S. saw as violating international rules against genocide and nuclear proliferation. The U.S. also pressured its ally, Australia, when Australia’s economic dependence on China led it to suggest that it might not help the US defend Taiwan against China. Yet, the U.S. promoted China’s energy ties with its ally Saudi Arabia, in the hope they could replace China’s dependence on Iran. Similarly, if the U.S. wanted to slow China’s rise, it should have blocked China’s energy ties with Venezuela, which is in its own “backyard.” Yet, it failed to do so. Finally, “neutral” states, such as Brazil, Angola or Nigeria, manipulated China and the U.S. to maximize their own benefits. Thus we could not find that the U.S. used energy to slow China’s rise, despite China’s fears that the U.S. might do so.

660110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
660110.value: Neurons acquire a polarized phenotype during development. The establishment of neuronal polarity is crucial for various neuronal functions, especially the assembly of neural circuits and cognitive functions, and deregulation of neuronal polarization is associated with various neurodegenerative diseases. A number of molecules have been demonstrated to regulate the process of neuronal polarization, including GSK3β (Glycogen synthase kinase 3β) and its substrates, microtubule-binding protein CRMP2 (collapsin response mediator protein-2) and APC (adenomatous polyposis coli). Our preliminary data suggest that a GSK3β substrate and interacting protein, Axin, regulates axon specification and neuronal polarization in cultured hippocampal neurons. Interestingly, we also found that Axin is a potential substrate of Cdk5 (cyclin-dependent kinase 5), a central regulator of neuronal development, raising the intriguing possibility that phosphorylation of Axin by Cdk5 is important for neuronal polarization. The primary objectives of this proposal are to characterize the phosphorylation of Axin by Cdk5 and to investigate the role of Cdk5-dependent phosphorylation of Axin in shaping the polarized morphology of neurons and the underlying signaling mechanisms. Implications of Axin phosphorylation in neurodegenerative diseases will also be investigated. 神經元在發育過程中會逐步向有極性的形態轉變，以此形成維持神經系統各種功能的結構基礎。這種極化過程對於神經回路的形成和認知功能來説顯得尤爲重要。神經元極化過程的失調與多種神經退行性疾病密切相關。許多信號分子都參與了神經元極化的調節過程，比如説糖原合成酶激酶GSK3beta及其底物, 微管結合蛋白CRMP2和APC。Axin蛋白是一個GSK3beta的結合蛋白，也是其底物。我們的初步實驗結果表明，在原代培養海馬神經元中Axin能夠調控軸突特化和神經元極化過程。更重要的是，我們發現Axin是蛋白激酶Cdk5的底物。鑒于Cdk5是調控神經發育的關鍵分子，我們認爲Cdk5依賴性的Axin磷酸化很可能在神經元的極化過程有重要的調節作用。因此，本研究計劃的主要目的就是確認Cdk5對Axin的磷酸化作用並研究這種磷酸化在形成神經元極性結構過程中的功能以及相關的分子生物學機制。我們也將探索Axin磷酸化在神經退行性疾病中的作用。

660110.label: Realisation of objectives
660110.value: This project aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying how cyclin-dependent kinase-5 (Cdk5)-regulated Axin phosphorylation shapes neuronal morphology; this aim was fully realized by addressing the three objectives mentioned above. In order to characterize the phosphorylation of Axin by Cdk5 (Objective 1), we first identified potential phosphorylation sites by searching the consensus sequences for Cdk5 substrates; in vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed that Thr485 was the major phosphorylation site and that Cdk5 was the key kinase in Axin phosphorylation. A rabbit polyclonal antibody that recognizes phospho-Thr485 was generated in house, and its specificity was verified by blocking peptide and gene-silencing methods. The subcellular localization of phosphorylated Axin was examined in developing brains and mature neurons. Accordingly, phosphorylated Axin was enriched in the nuclei of neural progenitors and synapses of mature neurons. In order to investigate whether Axin regulates neuronal polarization and axon formation in a Cdk5-dependent manner (Objective 2), we knocked down Axin expression in utero and confirmed that the Axin phosphorylation at Thr485 is essential for the establishment of polarized neuronal structures and axon formation. Furthermore, the interaction of Axin with glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β), a key polarized signaling molecule in developing neurons, is critical for the polarized distribution of GSK-3β and axon formation in developing neurons. In order to examine the mechanisms by which Axin regulates neuronal polarity (Objective 3), we investigated the regulation of Axin–GSK-3β interaction. We confirmed that Cdk5-mediated Axin phosphorylation enhanced the affinity of Axin for GSK-3β, thus reducing GSK-3β activity; meanwhile, the stability of Axin was not significantly affected by this phosphorylation. More importantly, Axin was phosphorylated in response to polarized extracellular cues (e.g., brain-derived neurotrophic factor [BDNF]) and regulated microtubule cytoskeleton assembly through GSK-3β inhibition and the subsequent dephosphorylation of collapsing response mediator protein-2 (CRMP-2). In addition to fully realizing the proposed research objectives described above, we further examined the role of Axin phosphorylation in the central nervous system. Importantly, we found that the Cdk5-dependent phosphorylation of Axin at Thr485 strictly controls the cytosolic and nuclear localization of Axin, which directs the amplification and differentiation of intermediate progenitors in the developing brain. In addition, Axin is required for the maintenance of dendrites, which are also polarized neuronal structures, and the morphogensis of dendritic spines as well as signal transmission across synapses.

660110.label: Major findings and research outcome
660110.value: In this project, we investigated how Cdk5-dependent Axin phosphorylation regulates the development of neuronal structures. As a result, we unraveled the key molecular basis underlying Axin-regulated neuronal proliferation, differentiation, and plasticity. Cdk5 is a key kinase in the brain that regulates various aspects of neuronal development. We demonstrated that Cdk5 phosphorylates Axin at Thr485 in vivo (Fang et al., J Neurosci., 2011). We further identified Axin as a key determinant of the number of neurons in the developing mouse cerebral cortex by regulating the balance between amplification and differentiation of embryonic neuronal progenitors. Cytoplasmic Axin interacted with GSK-3 to facilitate progenitor amplification, while Cdk5-mediated Axin phosphorylation led to the nuclear enrichment of Axin, resulting in the triggering of differentiation program through β-catenin (Fang et al., Neuron, 2013). Administration of XAV939, a small molecule that inhibits tankyrase activity and stabilizes Axin, resulted in the overproduction of upper-layer neurons and dysregulation of excitatory and inhibitory neuronal transmission, leading to autism-like behavioral abnormalities in mice (Fang et al., Cell Rep, 2014). These findings provide understanding on the molecular basis into the evolutionary expansion of cerebral cortex and the pathological mechanisms underlying neurological disorders such as autism. After the neurons are differentiated, they need to elaborate axons and dendrites, two characteristic polarized structures of neurons. We found that Axin knockdown abolishes the formation of axonal projections in the mouse cerebral cortex and reduces the complexity of the dendritic arbors. Axin’s action in the neuronal morphology is regulated by its phosphorylation by Cdk5. In particular, Cdk5-dependent Axin phosphorylation enhanced Axin–GSK-3β interaction and inhibited GSK-3β activity, leading to the dephosphorylation of microtubule-associated protein CRMP-2. This result suggests a novel regulatory pathway wherein Axin directs axon formation via cytoskeletal dynamics (Fang et al., J Neurosci, 2011; Chen et al., submitted). In addition, we found that Axin is enriched at synapses, the contacting sites between axon and dendrites. Silencing Axin reduced the number of dendritic spines, small protrusions along the dendrites where the excitatory synapses formed. Consistently, stabilizing Axin in neurons increased the dendritic spine number and miniature excitatory postsynaptic potential (mEPSC) frequency. The expression of cytoplasmic-enriched Axin mutant or the small Rho-GTPase Cdc42 restored the defective phenotype in Axin-depleted neurons. These findings demonstrate a new molecular mechanism by which Axin regulates dendritic spine and synapse development via Cdc42 signaling (Chen et al., submitted).

660110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
660110.value: The current project identified the molecular mechanisms by which Axin directs neuronal development. One key issue that should be addressed by future studies is how Axin functions at the level of neural circuit. To this end, we can employ emerging technologies such as optogenetics to manipulate Axin function in specific types of neurons and thus investigate the behavior of input and output neurons as well as changes in excitatory and inhibitory transmission; the results would delineate the precise circuits involved in these processes. Animal models can then be used to evaluate the contributions of Axin-related circuit malfunction to various neurological disorders. Another topic of interest is the association between Axin and human diseases such as autism and neurodegenerative disorders. We can analyze the DNA sequences of normal controls and patients with neurological disorders to identify the potential genetic variations in the exons, introns, and regulatory elements of the related genes. In addition, we can detect changes in the expression and modification of Axin and related signaling partners in body fluids (e.g., cerebrospinal fluid and blood) from patients. The findings will provide novel insights into the disease mechanisms of neurological disorders as well as aid drug development and clinical diagnosis.

660110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
660110.value: Our brains develop through a series of tightly controlled processes, during which proliferating progenitor cells differentiate into neurons with polarized morphology consisting of axons and dendrites. Disturbances to brain development may lead to various diseases, such as autism. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are poorly understood. Our project aimed to better understand these developmental events by investigating how a protein Axin acts as a scaffold for signaling complexes to regulate specific processes during the development and integration of neurons in the cerebral cortex. Interestingly, we found that the phosphorylation of Axin, which is controlled by cyclin-dependent kinase-5, determines the subcellular localization of Axin and hence the balance of the generation and differentiation of neurons in the brain. Alteration of Axin signaling in the cerebral cortex led to the overproduction of neurons, which resulted in autism-like behaviors in mice. In addition, we found that Axin plays a key role in orchestrating cellular signals to direct the development of axons and dendritic spines, which meet at synapses to mediate the communication between neurons, an important process for our cognitive functions. Our findings revealed previously unknown mechanisms of brain development and provide insights into how brain has evolved and how various neurological disorders occur.

660210.value: Cdk5和endophilin B1在柏金遜症病理學中的作用

660210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
660210.value: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the most common neurodegenerative movement disorder that is characterized by selective degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra. Various pathogenic mechanisms have been associated with PD, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, protein aggregation and abnormality with the ubiquitin-proteasome and autophagy pathways. Nonetheless, not only are the precise etiopathological mechanisms of the disease poorly understood, treatments that are effective in halting disease progression are also lacking. Further investigation into the pathogenic mechanisms of PD thus presents an urgent task in the field of PD research. Cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (Cdk5), a multi-faceted serine/threonine kinase, has been recently implicated in the pathophysiology of PD. Earlier studies have revealed that deregulation of Cdk5 activity results in neuronal loss in MPTP toxicity, a well-established model of PD. Interestingly, preliminary findings from our laboratory identified endophilin B1, a lipid-binding protein implicated in the regulation of mitochondrial apoptosis and macroautophagy induction in fibroblasts, as a Cdk5 substrate. Importantly, we found that knock-down of endophilin B1 protected cortical neurons against MPP+, the active toxic molecule in MPTP toxicity. These findings suggest that Cdk5 and endophilin B1 may both contribute to neuronal loss in PD. The aim of our study is therefore to elucidate the involvement of Cdk5 and endophilin B1 in neuronal loss in models of PD. Since excessive activation of macroautophagy can lead to autophagic cell death, it is conceivable that endophilin B1 may contribute to neuronal loss in models of PD through regulating macroautophagy, in addition to controlling mitochondrial apoptosis in neurons. To address this possibility, we will first examine if endophilin B1 also regulates macroautophagy induction and mitochondrial morphology in neurons. We will then consolidate the involvement of endophilin B1, and its phosphorylation by Cdk5, on neuronal loss in PD using two models of PD, namely MPP+ toxicity and overexpression of A53T alpha-synuclein mutant. Finally, whether endophilin B1-dependent regulation of apoptosis and macroautophagy contributes to neuronal loss in models of PD will also be investigated. Our observations will provide essential insights on the molecular players implicated in the pathogenesis of PD, which may aid in the identification of novel drug targets for development of therapeutic treatments against the disorder. 柏金遜症是一種非常普遍的神經退行性運動功能疾病, 其顯著標誌之一就是黑質體的多巴胺能神經元的選擇性退化和死亡。柏金遜症的發病原因有很多，包括氧化應激、綫粒體功能失調、蛋白非正常聚集以及泛素-蛋白酶体通路和細胞自噬功能的異常。然而，我們對導致柏金遜症的確切病理學機制沒有足夠的了解，也缺乏有效的療法去延緩疾病的惡化過程。因此，對柏金遜症的發病機制的研究是一個十分重要的課題。細胞周期依賴性蛋白激酶5 (Cdk5)是一個多功能的絲氨酸/蘇氨酸蛋白激酶。最近的研究表明，Cdk5參與了柏金遜症的病理學過程。MPTP毒性測試是一個廣泛使用的柏金遜症實驗模型。早期研究發現，Cdk5功能失調將導致神經元的死亡。我們通過初步實驗發現一個脂結合蛋白endophilin B1是Cdk5的底物。Endophilin B1在綫粒體介導的細胞凋亡和誘導巨型自噬過程中有重要作用。在MPTP毒性實驗中, 我們發現抑制endophilin B1的表達對神經元具有保護作用, 使它們能夠抵制毒性分子MPP+引起的細胞死亡。這些發現表明Cdk5和endophilin B1都可能參與了柏金遜症中神經元的死亡過程。因此，我們研究的主要目的是利用柏金遜症實驗模型探索Cdk5和endophilin B1在神經元死亡過程中的作用。因爲過度的巨型吞噬將導致細胞死亡，所以我們認爲在柏金遜症實驗模型中, endophilin B1除了調控綫粒體介導的細胞凋亡之外，還可能通過對巨型吞噬作用的調節來控制神經元的死亡過程。爲了證實這種可能性，我們將首先研究endophilin B1是否參與了神經元巨型吞噬的誘導過程，以及endophilin B1對綫粒體形態的影響。之後，我們會用MPTP毒性實驗和過表達alpha-synuclein A53T突變体這兩個實驗模型來研究endophilin B1以及Cdk5依賴性的endophilin B1磷酸化在神經元死亡過程中的作用。最後，我們將探討在柏金遜症實驗模型中, endophilin B1依賴性的細胞凋亡和巨型吞噬作用對神經經元死亡中的影響。我們的研究將進一步揭示柏金遜症的病理學機制，爲尋找合適藥物靶點提供重要的科學依據。

660410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
660410.value: Cellular tissue differentiation and their identity determination are two intricate processes that require good coordination during animal or plant development. Active cellular communication is required to synchronize various cellular molecular activities to ensure a reproducible functional outcome. The study of such event is often complicated in many multicellular organisms by their cellular complexity, which reduces the resolution for observation and obscures the interpretation of the experimentation results. In this proposal, we aim to take advantage of a simply organ structure in C. elegans, the sensory ray consisting of only four tissue-cells each with distinct properties. We aim to evaluate how cellular differentiation of this sensory organ is governed by a network transcription factors impinging on a common target gene mab-22. By characterizing the control of this gene’s expression in terms of its onset timing, duration and maintenance, we try to ascertain how three general neural differentiation factors dictate the differentiation process for all sensory rays via mab-22 gene. Additional regulatory and interacting components will also be isolated through genetic screens to more comprehensively describe the details of developmental regulation. More profoundly, mab-22 is under its own feedback regulatory control so that its expression is brief at the beginning of the differentiation of all rays but is sustained only in three specific rays in adults. Such finding infers ray-specificity of mab-22 function reflective to the organ identities, which must be tightly regulated by the ray identity determining mechanism. Employing different approaches and genetic mutants of the bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) pathway, we will make the first attempt to evaluate how organ identity controlling mechanism converges on the differentiation program where mab-22 serves as a common target to integrate these processes together. The findings resulted from this project will reveal the interplay of known factors and the identification of novel components involved. They will provide insights into the relationship of organ patterning and differentiation controls. The study would advance our understanding of tissue development and manifestation of congenital organ anomaly related to structural or functional deficits. 細胞組織分化和它們的身份確定是在動植物界中兩個複雜的發育過程，需要有良好的協調。細胞間的主動通信是用來使各種細胞能同步分化，確保器官有正常的運作。為了容易觀察和解釋實驗結果，我們通常在較簡單的多細胞生物體做研究。在這項研究建議中，我們利用雄性線蟲一個由四個各具特性的細胞組成的簡單的感覺器官作實驗課題。我們的目標是評估感覺器官細胞分化如何由一個轉錄因子的基因網絡上的協調，影響一個單一目標mab-22。通過描述控制這種基因的表達方案，其啟動時間，持續及其長時間的保持，我們嘗試確定三個神經分化因子在發育過程中如何通過mab-22決定分化結果。其他相關的基因亦會過遺傳篩選方法被隔離，他們性質，怎麼樣調控發育也會被更全面地描述出來。具體來說，我們會集中研究mab-22其自身的反饋調節控制的機理，其在分化初期表達的控制，以及其持續在成蟲的三個特定器官中的表達。運用不同的分子遺傳方法和BMP通路中的不同變種動物，我們將嘗試評估控制機制如何整合各分化流程，以mab-22為目標，改變器官特徵。這一研究將揭示已知基因的相互作用和新元件的識別，一併將模式運作及器官分化的控制提供新的見解，推動我們對組織器官的發育和先天性器官畸形尋找新的認知。

660410.label: Realisation of objectives
660410.value: We have made good progress on all fronts of the investigation. In summary, the objectives (1) and (3) are fully accomplished and the cis-acting elements on the tbx-2 (aka, mab-22) locus were defined (100%). However, objectives (2) and (4) were not fully accomplished due to unexpected mechanism of the gene action. Although extensive characterization was conducted using various reporters and genetic mutants to evaluate the role of the patterning genes on tbx-2 expression, we lacked conclusive evidence to pin point the convergence of the suspected regulators other than hlh-2/lin-32 and ceh-43, i.e., the dbl/sma pathway factors acting on the tbx-2 locus. Through this thorough investigation, the consistent findings not following our initial hypothesis are likely reflective to the actual architecture of the developmental mechanism. We were not able to establish the convergent input on tbx-2 alone, and have to take it as the reality and move on to more promising direction. As a result, in the last one third of the funding period, a major effort was shifted towards molecules being regulated by tbx-2. Expecting the transcriptional cascade would eventually execute the assembly process through modulating cell adhesion properties, we emphasized on the identification of transmembrane proteins controlled by tbx-2 to execute the ray assembly process. A new objective (5), to characterize the downstream trans-membrane proteins as targets of tbx-2/mab-22 during ray assembly, was introduced. The outcome of this part of the project is very promising, and a number of = gap junctional molecules, inx-12 and inx-13 and a tight junction protein, nsy-4 claudin, were identified to be responsible for the ray assembly process. These findings refocus the entire project at the last step of ray assembly, which is also the ultimate objective and long term goal of this proposal. Hence, even though the original objectives (2) and (4) were not 100% fulfilled, relevant novel findings were obtained to help us understand how this sensory organ composed of four cells is put together under the influence of tbx-2. Collectively, we see this project a productive one that yields new insights in the organ assembly mechanism.

660410.label: Major findings and research outcome
660410.value: (1) The onset of the tbx-2 at late L3 stage in the ray precursor cells at the juncture of neuronal / hypodermal asymmetry was confirmed, and the feedback regulation was confirmed by the same reporter assay. (2) Within the tbx-2 coding region, three intronic elements were defined. Two putative palindromic sequences of T-Box binding sites were defined as the negative feedback control elements, which were showed to be bound by bacterially expressed TBX-2 protein with high sequence specificity in in vitro binding assays. The third intronic element 5’ to the two TBX-2 binding sites was shown to be a target of ceh-43, bacterially expressed CEH-43 could bind to it in vitro with good specificity. (3) A composite positive cis-element is also defined in the 3’ non-coding region 1 kb 3’ to the last exon. These elements are targets of hlh-2/lin-32 transcriptional dual factors, as demonstrated by deletion and mutational analysis. (4) We have investigated the feedback positive and negative reporters in diverse mutants affecting the patterning paracrine dbl/sma pathway and combinatorial Hox codes. Repeated checking in mutant alleles did not reveal any change of the patterning profile of reporter genes in specific ray cells. The weaker expression signal, however, eludes to the notion that the dbl-1/sma pathway components act as general positive regulator of tbx-2 but not on differential expression and patterning. (5) cis-acting elements of the ceh-43 locus was localized in the 10 kb locus by serial deletion. The tissue-specific expression control of this transgene was embedded in the 7.4 kb coding region and 3’ end with multiple regulatory elements in control. Two redundant activating elements residing in the first three exons and the 3’ non-coding region were defined, which reflects on the complexity of gene activity control for regulatory genes acting in higher hierarchy. (6) We identified key genes acting downstream of tbx-2 to execute the ray assembly. By genetic and RNAi screens of over 100 candidates, we confidently identified inx-12, inx-13, both encoding gap junction molecules; eff-1 encoding a cell adhesion molecule, frm-5 responsible of membrane cytoskeleton association, nsy-4, hmp-1 and hmp-2 controlling cell adhesion at the tight junctional region. Multiple of them are regulated by ceh-43 and tbx-2 by transcriptional reporter assays, and their expression at the junction complex on the structural cells in a ray was shown to be essential for the assembly process. Cellular role of protein motifs in nsy-4 product is currently under detailed characterization.

660410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
660410.value: This research has two foci on the regulation of organ assembly (1) delineation of multiple factor cross-regulation at gene expression level, and (2) evaluation of patterning and fate controlling genes convergence on a common tbx-2 target. The absence of convincing data in (2) drove us to focus on the identification of a number of execution genes regulated by tbx-2 acting in cellular interaction. Further development of this project can go in two directions, (1) with the regulatory relationship among tbx-2, hlh-2/lin-32, ceh-43 confirmed, the role of additional factors, e.g., irx-1, unc-62 and ceh-20, acting in this process remains elusive. Increased complexity with fine tuning among these factors may be revealed, although the available assays may not be sensitive enough for biological validation. (2) Gap junction and tight junction molecules have been identified as key components for cellular communication and adhesion. The integration of the two in a simple cellular context, e.g., a sensory ray with few cells, is rare. Detailed study of their molecular assembly and intermolecular interactions on the cell surface, at the cell membrane and in the cytoplasm would offer a unique opportunity to uncover the regulation of cell morphology and migration by transmembrane molecules during organ differentiation.

660410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
660410.value: Medical cases are often related to various functional abnormalities caused by genetic and environmental insults, many examples of congenital disorders have been caused by malformation of organ tissues due to cellular function deficits. The elucidation of the underlying mechanisms of these diseases demands high resolution characterization of gene activities and cellular behavior which may not be accomplished easily. This study using nematode sensory organ as a study platform offers a unique opportunity for this interrogation. Upon completion of this project, key cross regulatory events of a handful of transcriptional regulators were elucidated on both the genetic and biochemical levels. While these factors have been implied to be important in neurosensory organ formation in human, the findings provide a rich understanding of their cross talks in embryological sensory organ establishment. The identification of a number of junctional molecules as the validated targets of this transcription factor axis opens up a new venue of studying congenital defects focusing on cellular communication and association, the fundamental regulatory mechanism of which would not be easily revealed using complex organisms such as mice. Hence, this research highlights the potential benefit a simple model system can bring about to the understanding of important human health issues.

660610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
660610.value: Establishing neuronal polarity is essential for various processes throughout the development of the central nervous system (CNS), in particular radial migration of neurons in the developing neocortex. Newborn cortical neurons in the proliferating ventricular zone (VZ) migrate upwards passing through the intermediate zone (IZ) to their proper positions in the cortical plate (CP), where the neurons mature and are integrated into the neuronal circuits. Acquisition of polarized structure is indispensable for migrating neurons to transit from the multi-polar stage in the IZ to the bipolar stage upon their entry into the CP. Defects in neuronal polarization and migration could disrupt the six-layer lamination of the cerebral cortex and thus impair proper neural functions. Interestingly, various signaling proteins that regulate cytoskeletal dynamics have been implicated in neuronal polarization and migration. Mutation of these genes in human brain such as Reelin, Dab1 and doublecortin was found to be associated with various neurological disorders including lissencephaly and autism. Nonetheless, molecular mechanisms underlying the polarization of neurons during radial migration has just begun to be unraveled. Our preliminary findings indicated α2-chimaerin, a Rac GTPase activating protein (GAP) that down-regulates Rac1 activity to induce actin reorganization, is involved in the establishment of neuronal polarization in vitro. Knockdown of α2-chimaerin in dissociated hippocampal neurons disrupted neuronal polarity and promoted the formation of multiple axons. More importantly, silencing of α2-chimaerin in vivo perturbed radial migration of cortical neurons, causing accumulation of neurons in the IZ of the mouse neocortex. These preliminary observations strongly suggest an essential role of α2-chimaerin in neuronal migration and layer organization during cortex development. In this proposal, we will examine the functional roles of α2-chimaerin and its underlying mechanism in neuronal morphogenesis and radial migration of cortical neurons. We will first investigate how α2-chimaerin exerts its action in neuronal polarization in hippocampal neurons. We will then characterize the functional roles of α2-chimaerin in radial migration of cortical neurons. The cellular signaling mechanisms by which α2-chimaerin exerts its biological effects on triggering the migration of cortical neurons will also be dissected. 660610.label: Realisation of objectives
660610.value: 1. To investigate the functional roles of α2-chimaerin in neuronal polarization and migration in the cerebral cortex We found that α2-chimaerin is highly expressed in the intermediate zone of the neocortex, where neurons adopt a polarized morphology. Cortical neurons of mouse embryos at embryonic day 14.5 were electroporated in utero with α2-chimaerin shRNA constructs together with a GFP plasmid, and the brain sections were analyzed at embryonic day 17.5. While the control neurons migrated into the cortical plate, most α2-chimaerin–knockdown neurons remained in the intermediate zone. These α2-chimaerin–knockdown neurons remained stacked in the subcortical region at the later postnatal stages, suggesting that α2-chimaerin knockdown actually arrests neuronal migration instead of merely delaying it. Altered cortical cytostructure can disrupt both local and long-range neuronal connections and is closely associated with epileptic seizures. Thus, abnormally accumulated neurons due to α2-chimaerin knockdown may lead to impaired microcircuitry assembly in the cortex. We performed whole-cell recordings of spontaneous synaptic activity on cortical slices prepared at postnatal days 15–20. The layer II–III neurons overlying the abnormally accumulated neurons exhibited altered cortical excitability. These findings suggest that the balance between circuit excitation and inhibition abnormally shifts towards overexcitation in the upper cortical layers as a result of α2-chimaerin knockdown. Interestingly, α2-chimaerin–knockdown mice exhibited greater susceptibility to convulsant-induced seizures, suggesting an increased risk of seizure in these mice. 2. To explicate the signaling mechanisms by which α2-chimaerin regulates neuronal polarization and radial migration The α2-chimaerin protein possesses different functional domains: a GAP domain for its inhibitory activity towards Rac1, and an SH2 domain to mediate its interaction with tyrosine phosphorylated proteins. To determine how α2-chimaerin regulates cortical development, we re-expressed different α2-chimaerin mutants in α2-chimaerin–knockdown cortices and examined neuronal migration. Interestingly, a GAP-inactive mutant of α2-chimaerin rescued migration to a similar extent as that of wild-type α2-chimaerin. Thus, the GAP activity of α2-chimaerin is dispensable for neuronal migration. On the other hand, re-expression of an SH2 mutant of α2-chimaerin, which exhibited reduced binding affinity for phosphotyrosine residues, failed to rescue the migration defects in the α2-chimaerin–knockdown cortex. This demonstrates that the SH2 domain-mediated interaction between α2-chimaerin and tyrosine phosphorylated proteins is important for directing neuronal migration. Furthermore, depletion of α2-chimaerin deregulated the phosphorylation and activity of a microtubule-associated protein, CRMP-2, suggesting that the function of α2-chimaerin is mediated through the regulation of microtubule dynamics. Re-expression of a specific CRMP-2 mutant rescued neuronal migration in the α2-chimaerin–knockdown cortex, suggesting that α2-chimaerin/CRMP2 is critical for neuronal migration during cerebral cortex formation.

660610.label: Major findings and research outcome
660610.value: During cerebral cortex development, proper neuronal migration is required to ensure newborn neurons arrive at their proper destinations. Abnormal neuronal migration leads to the disruption of cortical circuit assembly. Upon the initiation of migration, cortical neurons need to acquire a polarized cellular morphology. Nonetheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal polarization and radial migration during embryonic cortex development are incompletely understood. α2-chimaerin was originally identified as a signaling protein required for axon pathfinding and motor circuit assembly. The present project shows that α2-chimaerin is essential for radial migration and the formation of functional circuitry in the embryonic cerebral cortex (Ip et al., 2012). Knockdown of α2-chimaerin in utero perturbed the neurons to adopt a polarized structure and, causing them to accumulate in the deeper layers of the cortex. Importantly, α2-chimaerin–knockdown mice exhibited altered cortical excitability and enhanced seizure susceptibility. These results suggest that α2-chimaerin–dependent signaling is critical for the formation of microcircuitry within the cerebral cortex. We also investigated how the function of α2-chimaerin in neuronal migration is mediated. Activation of cell surface receptors by extrinsic signals is considered an important signal for neuronal migration. We found that α2-chimaerin can couple signals from the cell surface receptor TrkB to the intracellular cytoskeletal network upon receptor activation. More importantly, while α2-chimaerin was originally identified to regulate actin cytoskeletal dynamics, we found that it does not affect the actin cytoskeleton in neuronal migration; instead, α2-chimaerin controls neuronal polarization and migration by modulating the microtubule dynamics through regulating the activity of CRMP-2, a microtubule-associated protein. Live imaging analysis showed that α2-chimaerin is important for the establishment and maintenance of the leading processes of the migrating neurons during the locomotion. Moreover, α2-chimaerin knockdown led to the deregulation of the subcellular localization and phosphorylation levels of CRMP-2, resulting in perturbed CRMP-2 activity. In conclusion, our findings suggest that α2-chimaerin–regulated CRMP-2 phosphorylation/activation is a crucial molecular event that controls neuronal migration.

660610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
660610.value: The findings of this project open new avenues for future studies. We showed that impaired neuronal migration caused by α2-chimaerin knockdown perturbs the assembly of cortical microcircuits and causes excitatory/inhibitory imbalance, which is closely associated with epileptic seizures. Furthermore, α2-chimaerin is a critical regulator of neuronal polarity by controlling the stability of the microtubule network and neurite processes. Thus, our results enable us to continue investigating the functional importance of the α2-chimaerin–dependent regulation of the microtubule network in neuronal polarization and migration during cerebral cortex development. Using the α2-chimaerin–knockdown system, we can further characterize how the neurons locally misplaced because of abnormal neuronal migration result in aberrant cortical excitation and epileptic seizures. In addition, by delineating the downstream effectors of α2-chimaerin in microtubule signaling, we can identify and characterize new targets that control neuronal polarization and migration. While this project has established the functional importance of α2-chimaerin/CRMP-2 signaling in cortical circuit formation, it will be interesting to determine whether genetic mutations of α2-chimaerin and its downstream signaling targets are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders related to neuronal migration defects and perturbed cortical circuit connectivity.

660610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
660610.value: The cerebral cortex is composed of discrete layers each containing specific types of neurons that form local or long-range connections. The formation of the cerebral cortex requires that neurons migrate properly; abnormalities in this process are associated with various neurodevelopmental disorders, including epilepsy. Nonetheless, the underlying molecular mechanisms of how abnormal neuron migration lead to neurological problems are poorly understood. In this project, we demonstrated that α2-chimaerin, a signaling protein, is critical for neuron migration and the formation of neural circuitry. Disturbing α2-chimaerin signaling stops newborn neurons from migrating to the upper layers of the cerebral cortex, which disrupts the assembly of neural circuitry. Importantly, mice that express little α2-chimaerin are more susceptible to seizures, suggesting that perturbed α2-chimaerin signaling plays a role in epilepsy. We also showed that α2-chimaerin mediates its functions in neuron migration by establishing and maintaining the polar morphology of neurons. During migration, precise control of microtubule assembly is required for neurons to establish polar morphology. Specifically, blocking α2-chimaerin signaling disrupts the activity of CRMP-2, which binds to microtubules, and thus the stability of the microtubule network; this disrupts the polarization and migration of neurons. These findings open a new avenue for research on neurodevelopmental disorders.

660810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
660810.value: Development of the nervous system is largely influenced by sensory experience, and it is believed that the regulation of gene expression by neuronal activity is crucial to fine-tune synaptic connections between neurons in response to experience. Likewise, consolidation of long-term memory in adult animals, which involves long-lasting modification in synaptic strength, also depends on gene transcription. Firing of action potential and synaptic transmission in neurons must therefore send signals to the nucleus to regulate transcription. Increasing evidence suggests that the regulated nuclear translocation of signaling proteins represents one of the major mechanisms to mediate activity-dependent gene transcription. We and others have demonstrated that the serine/threonine kinase Cdk5 and its activator p35 are crucial for the growth of dendrites and formation of dendritic spines, but the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. In addition, it is not clear if Cdk5 is involved in activity-dependent dendritic growth and spine morphogenesis. Cdk5 and its activators p35 and p39 are localized in both cytoplasm and the nucleus in neurons. In addition, our laboratory and others have identified a number of nuclear proteins as substrates of Cdk5. Intriguingly, preliminary data reveals increased nuclear accumulation of Cdk5 and p35 in primary cortical neurons after neuronal depolarization, and the activity-induced mRNA expression of Bdnf and Arc is greatly attenuated by the Cdk5 inhibitor roscovitine. These observations prompt us to hypothesize that Cdk5 may participate in activity-dependent gene transcription that regulates dendritic growth, spine morphogenesis and synapse development. To test our hypothesis, we will examine the role of nuclear Cdk5 in synapse and spine development by expressing nuclear localization-deficient Cdk5 mutant or nuclear-specific Cdk5 dominant negative construct. We will also determine if neuronal activity triggers nuclear import of Cdk5 and p35 by monitoring nuclear localization of GFP-tagged Cdk5 and p35 in dissociated cultured neurons after neuronal depolarization by KCl. The role of Cdk5 in activity-dependent gene expression will be verified by examining the expression of activity-induced genes after depolarization using real-time PCR. 660810.label: Realisation of objectives
660810.value: 1. Elucidating the roles of nuclear Cdk5 in activity-dependent dendritic growth, and synapse and spine development To determine whether nuclear Cdk5 is important for activity-dependent dendritic growth, we first demonstrated that inhibiting Cdk5 activity by roscovitine significantly attenuated the induction of dendritic growth in response to neuronal depolarization by KCl. We found that KCl treatment did not increase dendritic length in cdk5−/− hippocampal neurons. Furthermore, we used shRNA to knockdown the expression of Cdk5 in hippocampal neurons, which resulted in the reduction of dendritic arborization. Notably, the dendritic impairment of Cdk5-knockdown neurons was rescued by wild-type Cdk5, but not the nuclear localization-deficient Cdk5 . These results indicate that Cdk5 requires localization in the nucleus to promote dendrite development. Activity-induced dendritic growth depends on precise gene transcription control, and bdnf is a well-known activity-induced gene that mediates the dendritic growth. In particular, the transcription of exon IV-containing bdnf transcript is induced by neuronal activity. Hence, to determine if Cdk5 promotes activity-induced dendritic growth via the regulation of gene transcription in the nucleus, the mRNA levels of bdnf (all transcripts) and bdnf exon IV in cdk5+/+ and cdk5−/− neurons after treatment with KCl were examined by real-time PCR. Upon depolarization by KCl, the levels of both transcripts increased dramatically. However, the induction of bdnf exon IV was significantly attenuated in cdk5−/− neurons. The results therefore suggest that Cdk5 regulates activity-induced dendritic development via transcription of genes such as bdnf. 2. Studying the regulation of the nuclear import of Cdk5/p35 by neuronal activity The findings that nuclear Cdk5 is crucial for activity-dependent dendrite development suggest that neuronal activity might regulate the nuclear translocation of Cdk5. To test this hypothesis, we employed time-lapse confocal microscopy to follow the subcellular localization of GFP-Cdk5 in cultured hippocampal neurons. Depolarization by KCl, but not control treatment, triggered the translocation of Cdk5 into the nucleus. Biochemical fractionation and western blot analysis further confirmed the nuclear accumulation of Cdk5 after KCl-induced depolarization. To verify the subcellular localization of Cdk5, cultured hippocampal neurons were stained with the specific antibody against endogenous Cdk5, and we found that nuclear Cdk5 was enriched in cultured hippocampal neurons upon development. To investigate the regulation of nuclear Cdk5 by neuronal activity in vivo, we examined the changes of nuclear Cdk5 levels in the mouse visual cortex before and after eye opening; this is a well-established model for studying activity-dependent gene expression and dendrite development. Mouse visual cortices were collected before (postnatal day 10, P10) and after eye opening (P15), and nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation was performed. Interestingly, Cdk5 levels had increased significantly in the nuclear fractions after eye opening, indicating that Cdk5 is translocated into the nucleus by visual stimulation in vivo. Together with the requirement of the nuclear localization of Cdk5 in dendrite development, our findings suggest that Cdk5 is required for the activity-dependent regulations of neurons through the regulation of gene transcription.

660810.label: Major findings and research outcome
660810.value: The development and maturation of the nervous system are largely influenced by sensory experience. The regulation of gene expression by neuronal activity is crucial for fine-tuning the synaptic connections among neurons in response to experience. Nonetheless, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Our study has identified the nuclear translocation of the serine/threonine kinase Cdk5 is a crucial mechanism to promote the activity-dependent dendritic growth of hippocampal neurons (Liang et al., submitted). Cdk5 protein accumulated in the nuclear fractions of the mouse visual cortex after eye opening, when visual activity refines the neuronal connections of the cortical neurons during brain development. Confocal imaging and biochemical studies further demonstrated that neuronal depolarization by KCl triggered the nuclear translocation of Cdk5 in hippocampal neurons, confirming that neuronal activity regulates the subcellular localization of Cdk5. What are the functional consequences of triggering Cdk5 nuclear translocation in response to neuronal activity? Either inhibition of Cdk5 activity or knockout of Cdk5 impaired dendritic growth of neurons and reduced the dendritic complexity induced by neuronal polarization. Importantly, knockdown of Cdk5 by shRNA inhibited dendritic growth of cultured hippocampal neurons, and the defects could only be rescued by co-expression of wild-type Cdk5 but not its nuclear localization-deficient mutant. These results suggest that the nuclear pool of Cdk5 is critical to activity-dependent dendritic growth. Given that the precise control of gene transcription is essential for dendritic development, we determined whether Cdk5 regulates activity-induced dendritic growth via gene transcription. Microarray analysis was employed to assess whether the loss of Cdk5 would affect activity-induced changes in gene expression. The mRNA was collected in Cdk5+/+ or Cdk5−/− hippocampal neurons after KCl treatment. A specific set of genes (including bdnf, which encodes the neurotrophin BDNF, a key player for activity-dependent dendritic growth) were identified to be differentially regulated by neuronal activity, and the changes in expression of those genes were abolished in Cdk5−/− neurons, suggesting that Cdk5 is required for activity-dependent gene expression. Real-time PCR confirmed the requirement of Cdk5 in regulating activity-induced expression of the exon IV-containing bdnf transcript. Furthermore, Cdk5 regulates the phosphorylation of MeCP2, a key epigenetic regulator of gene transcription. MeCP2 phosphorylation at Ser421 induced by neuronal depolarization is suggested to specifically enhance the transcription of activity-regulated genes such as bdnf. Thus, our results collectively indicate that Cdk5 is important for activity-dependent gene regulation and dendrite development.

660810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
660810.value: The current study demonstrates that Cdk5 plays an important role in activity-dependent dendritic growth and that Cdk5 mediates its functions through the regulation of transcriptional machinery. Importantly, several genes differentially regulated by neuronal activity were found to be dependent on Cdk5. However, it remains unclear how Cdk5 regulates the transcription of these candidate genes. One approach for resolving this question is to determine whether Cdk5 regulates the activity of specific transcriptional regulator(s) involved in activity-dependent dendritic growth. Our results show that neuronal activity increases the phosphorylation of MeCP2, a transcriptional repressor, at Ser421, which is suggested to suppress the transcriptional repressor activity of the protein and therefore enhance transcription. In contrast, Cdk5 inhibition reduces the neuronal activity-induced MeCP2 phosphorylation, consequently perturbing the transcription program. We can advance the study by examining how Cdk5 regulates the phosphorylation and activity of MeCP2 protein. To this end, we will determine if MeCP2 is a direct substrate of Cdk5 by using biochemical analysis together with mass spectrometry. Furthermore, different gene candidates were identified as being regulated by Cdk5 in the microarray analysis, and it would be interesting to examine how Cdk5 regulates expression of these genes. First, we will investigate whether these gene candidates are the downstream targets of MeCP2, if MeCP2 binds to these gene candidates, and if the specific binding is dependent on Cdk5. Understanding the mechanism of activity-dependent gene expression may help to elucidate how the molecular basis of dendritic development and hence proper brain functioning are regulated.

660810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
660810.value: Most synaptic connections are formed on dendrites. Therefore, proper dendrite development is crucial for brain functioning. Dendrite development is regulated by sensory experience through changes in gene expression. Nonetheless, how signals are transmitted to the cell nucleus in response to neuronal activity to regulate gene transcription is unclear. We found that the nuclear expression of a brain protein, cyclin-dependent kinase-5 (Cdk5), is critical for activity-dependent gene transcription and dendrite development. Cdk5 accumulated in the cell nucleus in mouse visual cortex after eye opening, suggesting that neuron activity drives Cdk5 into the nucleus, where it performs various functions by phosphorylating other proteins. While re-expression of Cdk5 reversed the impaired dendrite pattern in neurons upon depletion of Cdk5, a mutant that failed to localize in the nucleus could not rescue the phenotype. Furthermore, Cdk5 is important for the transcription of several activity-induced genes, particularly a variant of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (bdnf) whose induction depends on neuronal activity. Cdk5’s action is mediated by the phosphorylation of MeCP2, a key transcription regulator that modulates bdnf gene transcription through binding to the gene promoter. Our findings identify the nuclear localization of Cdk5 as a novel mechanism during activity-dependent dendrite growth by regulating gene transcription in the nucleus.

661010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
661010.value: Persistent changes in synaptic strength that underlie memory consolidation require de novo protein synthesis for the formation of new synaptic connections. The protein kinase mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) is central to activity-induced protein synthesis, which involves phosphorylation of S6 kinase and subsequently the ribosomal protein S6 for translation initiation. Synaptic activity triggers activation of the mTOR-S6 kinase pathway and induces dendritic protein synthesis required for long-term potentiation (LTP), but the signaling pathways that couple synaptic activity and mRNA translation have only begun to be elucidated. One candidate molecule that mediates the activity-dependent mRNA translation is the neurotrophin BDNF. Activation of NMDA receptor during the induction of LTP increases transcription and translation of the Bdnf mRNA, and BDNF-mediated protein synthesis is required for the maintenance of synaptic plasticity and consolidation of long-term memory. The serine/threonine kinase Cdk5 and its activator p35 are emerging key players in synapse development and synaptic plasticity, but the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Recent studies suggest that phosphorylation of S6 kinase and the translation initiation factor eIF-4E is regulated by Cdk5, suggesting a novel role of Cdk5 in protein synthesis. Preliminary data from our laboratory reveals that phosphorylation of S6 ribosomal protein by BDNF is impaired when p35 expression is knocked-down in dissociated hippocampal neurons. In addition, activation of synaptic NMDA receptor also induces phosphorylation of S6 kinase at the putative Cdk5 phosphorylation site, and that phosphorylation is abolished by the Cdk5 inhibitor roscovitine. These observations therefore prompt us to investigate the potential function of Cdk5 in regulating activity-dependent protein synthesis. To test our hypothesis, we will first determine the synaptic activity and BDNF-induced phosphorylation of signaling proteins involved in translation pathway by Western blot analysis and immunocytochemistry using phospho-specific antibodies. The role of Cdk5 will then be examined by the Cdk5 inhibitor roscovitine, knocking down the expression of Cdk5 or p35 by RNAi, or dissociated primary neurons cultured from Cdk5- or p35-null mice. We will verify the involvement of Cdk5 in mediating activity or BDNF-induced protein synthesis by performing live cell imaging of cultured neurons transfected with a GFP-based reporter. Finally, the significance of Cdk5-mediated phosphorylation of S6 kinase in protein synthesis-dependent synaptic plasticity will be explored. We will examine its role in synaptic scaling in response to chronic blockade of neuronal activity in culture neurons, as well as the structural plasticity of dendritic spines upon activation of synaptic NMDA receptor. 在鞏固記憶的過程中, 突觸強度的持續變化需要細胞重新合成蛋白, 並形成新的突觸連接。哺乳動物雷帕霉素靶蛋白(mTOR) 在神經活性誘導的蛋白合成過程中有關鍵作用。它通過控制S6激酶與核糖體蛋白S6的磷酸化來調節蛋白翻譯的起始過程。突觸活性激活了mTOR-S6激酶信號途徑，並誘導長時程增強(LTP)所需要的樹突蛋白合成。然而，我們對於突觸活性與mRNA翻譯的偶聯機制還缺乏深入了解。其中一個介導神經活性依賴性mRNA翻譯的分子是神經營養蛋白BDNF。在誘導長時程增強的過程中，NMDA受體的激活顯著增加了Bdnf mRNA的轉錄和翻譯，而BDNF誘導的蛋白合成對於維持突觸強度和鞏固長時間記憶是必不可少的。越來越多的證據顯示，絲氨酸/蘇氨酸蛋白激酶Cdk5和它的調節蛋白p35在突觸發育和可塑性過程中有重要的作用，而我們對相關的分子機制還缺乏足夠的了解。最近有研究發現S6激酶和翻譯起始因子eIF-4E的磷酸化受到Cdk5的調控，說明Cdk5在蛋白合成過程中有重要的作用。我們的初步研究表明，在抑制了p35表達的海馬神經元中，BDNF誘導S6核糖體蛋白磷酸化的能力消失了。S6激酶上有一些潛在的Cdk5磷酸化位點。激活突觸的NMDA受體能夠誘導這些位點的磷酸化，而這些磷酸化能夠被Cdk5抑制劑roscovitine所阻斷。這些結果促使我們進一步研究Cdk5在神經活性誘導的蛋白合成過程中的作用。我們首先會用蛋白印記和免疫細胞化學的方法研究突觸活性和BDNF誘導的蛋白翻譯相關信號分子的磷酸化。我們也將利用Cdk5抑制劑roscovitine, shRNA介導的Cdk5或p35基因表達抑制以及Cdk5或p35基因敲除小鼠來確認Cdk5在上述磷酸化過程中的作用。我們會在原代培養的神經元中表達連接了GFP的報告基因，利用活細胞成像技術研究Cdk5在突觸活性或BDNF誘導的蛋白合成中的作用。最後，我們還會探討Cdk5介導的S6激酶磷酸化在蛋白合成依賴性的突觸可塑性中的作用。我們可以激活突觸NMDA受體或者用抑制劑長時間阻斷神經元活性，借此來研究上述磷酸化過程在樹突棘的結構變化以及突觸可塑性的自身調節過程中的作用。

661010.label: Realisation of objectives
661010.value: Objective 1 Phosphorylation of S6 kinase (S6K) and ribosomal protein S6, which are key components of the mTOR pathway and activity-dependent translation initiation, was examined in wild-type and Cdk5 knockout brains by Western blotting. S6K phosphorylation at Ser-411 and S6 phosphorylation was significantly reduced in Cdk5 knockout brains. To confirm the Cdk5-mediated S6K phosphorylation in neurons and to examine its subcellular localization, hippocampal neurons were subjected to immunofluorescence staining. Phospho-Ser-411 immunoreactivity was detected in dendrites of wild-type neurons, and the immunoreactivity was significantly decreased in Cdk5-/- neurons. To directly examine protein synthesis, metabolic labeling based on chemical click reaction was performed to show that newly synthesized proteins were significantly reduced in Cdk5 knockout neurons. We investigated activity-dependent protein synthesis by examining the induction of S6K and S6 phosphorylation by the neurotrophin BDNF and the neurotransmitter glutamate. The BDNF-induced S6K phosphorylation at Ser-411 and S6 phosphorylation was blocked by the Cdk5 inhibitor roscovitine. Activation of synaptic NMDA receptor also induced S6 phosphorylation, which was abolished by roscovitine, the BDNF scavenger TrkB-IgG, and in Cdk5 knockout neurons. To study activity-dependent protein synthesis, we examined the postsynaptic protein PSD-95. Bicuculline and glycine significantly increased PSD-95 expression in a NMDA receptor-dependent manner, and the increase was abolished by the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin, roscovitine, and in Cdk5 knockout neurons, indicating the important role of Cdk5. Objective 2 We found that treatment of hippocampal neurons with rapamycin decreased spine density. To specifically examine the role of S6K, we designed two shRNAs to knockdown S6K expression. Introduction of the shRNAs led to significant reduction of dendritic spine density in hippocampal neurons, which was rescued by co-expression of RNAi-resistant S6K. To examine spine morphogenesis in response to chronic neuronal activity, neurons were either treated with the activity blocker TTX or the neurotrophin BDNF. Depletion of S6K mimicked and occluded the spine loss induced by TTX, as well as abolished the BDNF-induced spine formation. We also investigated the role of Cdk5-mediated S6K phosphorylation by generating phospho-deficient S411A mutant of S6K and performed rescue experiment. Spine loss upon S6K knockdown was rescued by wild-type but not the S411A mutant of S6K. Cdk5-mediated phosphorylation of S6K is therefore required for spine morphogenesis. During homeostatic plasticity, chronic blockade of neuronal activity leads to a compensatory increase in synapse number and miniature excitatory postsynaptic current (mEPSC). The expression of PSD-95 in cortical neurons was increased after 48hr TTX treatment, which was abolished by roscovitine and in Cdk5-/- neurons. Cdk5 is therefore required for homeostatic plasticity in response to TTX. To directly examine the role of Cdk5-mediated S6K phosphorylation in homeostatic plasticity, we measured the mEPSC of transfected hippocampal neurons. Although S6K knockdown significantly reduced spine density, mEPSC frequency or amplitude was not affected. S6K (and its phosphorylation by Cdk5) is therefore required for activity-dependent dendritic spine morphogenesis, but not excitatory synaptic transmission or homeostatic plasticity.

661010.label: Major findings and research outcome
661010.value: The development and plasticity of dendritic spines is influenced by neuronal activity and depends on protein synthesis. Activity-dependent protein synthesis involves the protein kinase mTOR, which phosphorylates S6K at Thr-389. The activated S6K subsequently promotes phosphorylation of S6 ribosomal protein and initiation of mRNA translation. In this study, we hypothesize that Cdk5 might control spine morphogenesis and synaptic function through regulating the mTOR pathway and protein synthesis. S6K can be phosphorylated in vitro at Ser-411 within the C-terminal auto-inhibitory loop by several kinases, including Cdk5, Cdc2 and MAPK. Using phospho-specific antibody to perform Western blotting and immunofluorescence staining on Cdk5 knockout brains and neurons, we found that Cdk5 was the major kinase that phosphorylated S6K at Ser-411 in the distal dendrites of neurons. Ser-411 phosphorylation was induced upon activation of synaptic NMDA receptors. Notably, the NMDA receptor-induced phosphorylation of S6 ribosomal protein and expression of the postsynaptic protein PSD-95 was abolished by the Cdk5 inhibitor roscovitine and in Cdk5 knockout neurons. Metabolic labeling further demonstrated that protein synthesis was reduced in Cdk5 knockout neurons. Together our findings reveal a novel function of Cdk5 in regulating the mTOR pathway/protein synthesis induced by synaptic activity. Some of these findings were published in Nature Neuroscience in 2012. Although Ser-411 phosphorylation of S6K has been known for many years, its regulation and importance remains unclear. We found that Ser-411 phosphorylation was induced by BDNF, but was down-regulated upon chronic blockade of neuronal activity by TTX. Indeed, knockdown of S6K in hippocampal neurons by shRNA led to loss of dendritic spines, which mimicked and completely occluded the effect of TTX. S6K depletion also abolished the effect of BDNF on spine formation. Remarkably, despite extensive loss (~50%) of dendritic spines, excitatory synaptic transmission was not affected in the S6K-shRNA-transfected neurons, since the mEPSC frequency and amplitude was similar to the scrambled RNA control. These findings reveal that excitatory synaptic transmission can be dissociated from dendritic spines. Finally, we found that co-expression of wild-type S6K, but not the phospho-deficient S411A mutant, could rescue the spine defects of S6K knockdown. Together, we conclude that S6K is important in spine morphogenesis driven by BDNF and neuronal activity, but is not required for excitatory synaptic transmission. Moreover, besides the well-established mTOR-mediated phosphorylation at Thr-389, we have demonstrated that S6K function also requires a parallel signaling pathway that involves Cdk5-mediated phosphorylation at Ser-411. Manuscript describing these findings has been submitted and reviewed by the Journal of Biological Chemistry. Currently we are preparing the revised manuscript for resubmission.

661010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
661010.value: The downstream mechanism of how S6K regulates spine morphogenesis requires further investigation. S6K might be required for activity-induced synthesis of specific proteins, such as the kinase LIMK1 and the actin-associated protein Arc. Alternatively, S6K might regulate spine morphogenesis in a protein synthesis-independent manner, such as interaction with neurabin and Tiam1 which can directly regulate spine growth. It will also be important to examine how the Ser-411 phosphorylation modulates S6K functions. We have found that Cdk5 is required for the increase in PSD-95 expression upon chronic TTX treatment. Since depletion of S6K itself does not affect mEPSC frequency or amplitude, it is unlikely that S6K is directly involved in homeostatic plasticity. Investigating the role of other Cdk5 substrates in homeostatic plasticity upon chronic blockade of neuronal activity would be informative. Dendritic spines have long been regarded as the sites of excitatory synaptic transmission. Our findings that mEPSC remains unchanged after S6K knockdown despite the drastic spine loss is intriguing and is consistent with recent study showing similar phenotypes in neurons over-expressing Nr4a1 (Chen et al., 2014 Neuron). This might be explained by a shift of excitatory synapses from spines to dendritic shaft. Mice with S6K knockdown can potentially be used to study the importance of dendritic spines on circuit function and animal behaviors.

661010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
661010.value: Brain cells (neurons) transmit information through the release of chemicals at a specialized structure called synapse. Elucidating the signaling pathways that regulate synapse development is fundamental to our understanding of various brain functions. Dendritic spines are the specialized subcellular compartments of neurons where the majority of excitatory neurotransmission takes place. Abnormality in spine density and morphology is associated with different neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders, underscoring the importance of proper spine maturation in normal brain function. It is generally believed that neuronal activity and the growth factor BDNF are essential for the development of dendritic spines. BDNF activates an enzyme called Cdk5 at the synapse, which in turn modifies the function of a whole repertoire of signaling proteins. One of them is another enzyme called S6K, which we have demonstrated to be essential for maintaining the number of dendritic spines in neurons. Using a combination of biochemical, molecular and cellular approaches, we have further found that the modification of S6K by Cdk5 at one single amino acid (serine 411) is critically involved in the maintenance of dendritic spines. The present study has therefore identified a novel signal transduction pathway that governs the proper development of dendritic spines. It is noteworthy that S6K dysregulation has been linked to Fragile-X syndrome, the most common inherited form of intellectual disability. Our findings reveal a link between S6K and spine morphogenesis, which can potentially explain the cognitive deficits in the neurodevelopmental disorder and might shed new light in identifying potential therapeutic targets.

661110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
661110.value: 中藥的地道藥材因其種植地或生長地符合該品種需要的優良水土及地理環境，一直以來被視作具有特定的種質及獨特的藥效而被廣泛使用。然而由於缺乏科學數據的支持，地道藥材至今仍未得到真正的認同。再加上如今藥材的混偽品和代用品大量充斥市場，因此業界有迫切需要去研究地道藥材及種源的鑒定，從而形成安全及可持續發展的中藥應用。 當歸無疑是一個十分典型的例子。據文獻記載，甘肅的西歸、雲南的雲歸、吉林的東當歸、朝鮮當歸、日本當歸和歐洲的歐當歸分別作為當歸使用。由于當歸品種複雜且市售品多樣化，長期以來這些品種在不同地區混雜使用。為了確保其優良穩定的品質，進一步的品種及規格考証和質控確是克不容緩。 我們過往的研究指出，不同種類的當歸有不同的基因排序和化學成份，因此可推論它們來自不同品種。其他的研究報告亦指出這些不同種類的當歸可發揮不同的藥理作用。再者我們研究隊伍曾發現西歸與雲歸在活血方面的功能有明顯的差異。所以這6種當歸所衍生的問題及其重要性驅使我們繼續作出深入的研究。 在這研究項目中，我們將採用化學和基因組的分析方法研究。將尋找和確定16種化學成份，作為質控指標，同時亦會購入超過6個批次的藥材，以求提高準確性。基因組及動物實驗將用來確實其中當歸的特定藥理功能。整體而言，這項目不但可以促進當歸的正確應用，減少不必要的副作用，而且此方法平台亦可應用在其他中藥質控的研究，從而更進一步保障中藥使用者的健康。

661110.label: Realisation of objectives
661110.value: Angelica root (AR; Danggui; 當歸) is a well-known and commonly used traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) herb, which has been used for more than 2,000 years as a traditional medicine in China, Korea and Japan. AR is widely used to supplement and harmonize the blood, to regulate menstruation, to relieve pain, moisten dryness, and to lubricate the intestines: it can also be used to treat menstrual irregularities, menstrual pain, uterine bleeding, etc. In this study, we have revealed the action mechanism of AR in treating blood deficiency, regulating blood flow and the neuroprotection effect. Firstly, we have established the DNA fingerprinting and chemical profiling metabolomics of authenticate different types of AR water extracts and wine-processed AR from various production areas. In revealing the “blood tonic” function, AR could stimulate a variety of cellular responses in distinct cell models, including: (i) activation of bone differentiation process in cultured osteoblasts; (ii) stimulation of hemoglobin in erythropoietic precursor; (iii) stimulation of erythropoietin (EPO) in cultured liver cells; (iv) activation of nitric oxide (NO) production in rat aorta and cultured endothelial cells; (v) suppression of reactive oxidative species (ROS) in rat aorta and cultured endothelial cells; (vi) inhibition of platelet aggregation in vitro and (vii) neuroprotection in cultured neuron cells. All these biological activities of AR are closely related to the function of AR in treating different diseases. In addition, the AR-induced specific genes/proteins have been identified in different cell models. Therefore, these AR-induced gene/protein repression could be part of the molecular explanation to its clinical usage.

661110.value: [1] The DNA fingerprint and chemical profiling metabolomics of AR from different regions of China, Korea and North Korea were established by 1H-NMR and GC-QQQ-MS/MS, respectively. The chemical profiling of wine-processed AR and AR-containing herbal mixtures were established. These results have been published in international journals. [2] AR from different regions of China, Korea and North Korea showed different chemical and biological assessment of its water extracts; the difference was revealed in Danggui Buexue Tang (DBT). These results have been published in international journals. [3] The level of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) expressed in MG-63 cells, serving as an indicative marker for bone differentiation, was increased by the application of AR, wine-processed AR and AR-containing herbal mixtures. These results suggested that AR might possess the beneficial effect on bone cells which may be used to prevent osteoporosis. These results have been published in international journals. [4] Results showed that AR could inhibit the proliferation of K562 cells and induce the mRNA level of α-globin. These data suggested that AR might induce the erythropoietic differentiation. [5] The application of AR, wine-processed AR and AR-containing herbal mixtures could stimulate EPO gene expression in Hep3B cells, and which could activate pHRE-luc luciferase activity; thus, AR possessed the ability to regulate EPO gene expression in liver by HIF-mediated pathway. These results have been published in international journals. [6] AR, wine-processed AR and AR-containing herbal mixtures possessed the inhibitory effect on platelet aggregation. These data suggested AR might have the ability to facilitate blood circulation. These results have been published in the international journals. [7] The vasodilation effect was observed in rat aorta after the application of AR, wine-processed AR and AR-containing herbal mixtures could stimulate the NO production in cultured HUVECs. These data suggested that AR could facilitate blood circulation. [8] AR, wine-processed AR and AR-containing herbal mixtures possessed the protective effects in rat aorta after injury of the vascular endothelium; furthermore, AR could protect the NO production after the injury of HUVECs. [9] AR possessed the neuroprotective effects in cultured PC12 cells. Also, AR could active the ARE-mediated NQO1 and GSTA2 expressions against cellular oxidation. These results clearly indicated that AR possessed a beneficial effect in protection neurons against oxidative damage. [10] AR-containing herbal mixtures (i.e. DBT) could induce the immune function, the amount of hemoglobin and EPO, the bone marrow density in cyclophosphamide-induced rats. These results have been published in the international journals

661110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
661110.value: In this project, we have provided the DNA fingerprint and chemical profiling metabolomics of AR from different sources and/or species, wine-processed AR and AR composed TCM formulae. We have provided several cellular and molecular evidences to account for the traditional and current usage of AR, wine-processed AR and AR composed TCM formulae in treating different diseases especially for blood systems and protective effects from oxidation in neuronal system. In addition, the AR-mediated specific genes have benn identified. However, most of the results are based on the cell model systems, which may not be sufficient to support the physiological efficacy of AR. Therefore, the next step for AR research should be focused on the animal studies. Also, we would like to search for the active ingredients of AR by revealing the bioactivities of chemical components inside the AR in different cell culture systems.

661110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
661110.value: “Di Dao” (地道) type of the TCM is widely adopted and defined as the best quality of Chinese Material Medica, because of suitable climate, soil and geographical conditions in their production area. However, the current problem of this “Di Dao” concept has no scientific evidence to show how good they are. In addition, undesirable effects were observed due to adulteration and substitution. Therefore, an urgent need for species differentiation and quality assurance is a prerequisite of its sustainable and safe usages. Here, in the current study, we used a commonly used TCM herb, AR, as a model to: [1] set up the DNA fingerprint and chemical profiling; and [2] search for the biomarkers for AR and its related TCM formulae. From the results, we have provided the chemical and biological difference of AR derived from different cultivated regions. In addition, we have determined the biological activities and animal studies of AR, and we have revealed its underlying mechanisms in explaining its function in “Blood tonic”. These evidence could serve as the guidance to understand the meaning of “Di Dao” type of AR and other TCM herbs, which facilitate the international acceptance of TCM.

661610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
661610.value: Following the global trend, harmful algal bloom and red tides have frequently occurred in Hong Kong waters since the 1980s, causing fish kills and beach closures. Among the red tides reported in Hong Kong, Noctiluca scintillans, a large heterotrophic dinoflagellate, is the most frequently occurring red tide species, particularly in the eastern and northeastern waters during winter. Voracious feeding activity on a wide range of food types is suggested to be an important ecological advantage for Noctiluca. Despite its wide spread occurrence, many aspects of its ecophysiology have not been thoroughly studied, especially on subtropical populations. There is only one paper on the seasonal Noctiluca population dynamics in a semi-closed bay of Hong Kong. In this study, I will study: 1) The mechanisms that lead to the high abundance or blooms of Noctiluca in eastern waters in winter and spring; 2) Noctiluca’s feeding behavior and the effect of its selective grazing on other phytoplankton species; 3) Noctiluca’s elemental chemical composition under various conditions and its role in nutrient regeneration. The first topic will be studied through a field survey to be conducted in Port Shelter and its adjacent waters during the NE monsoon period when Noctiluca blooms are most frequent. Our hypothesis is that the NE monsoon causes the intrusion of the nutrient-rich China Coastal Current, which increases the food supply for Noctiluca that is brought into the bay by the wind-induced downwelling conditions. The second and third topics will involve a series of laboratory experiments using Noctiluca isolated from Hong Kong waters. We will first investigate whether Noctiluca prefers certain types of prey. Then we will study whether Noctiluca needs to consume heterotrophic prey in order to meet its nitrogen requirements. Further more, we will study its elemental chemical composition (stoichiometry) and nutrient regeneration under the consumption of N-sufficient and N-deficient prey. The ability of Noctiluca to utilize organic matter to endure long periods of starvation will also be investigated. In addition, through collaboration with Japanese scientists, parallel experiments will be conducted using Noctiluca strains isolated from Hong Kong and Japan to elucidate the difference and similarity in ecophysiological characteristics between the subtropical and temperate Noctiluca populations. Findings from this study will also help us to understand the mechanisms of the formation of Noctiluca red tides in the Hong Kong coastal waters and its role in the microbial food web and biogeochemical process in the sub-tropical coastal marine ecosystems. 如同全球共同的趋势一样，从上世纪80年代以来，有害藻类水华和红潮就经常在香港水域频繁发生并且导致鱼类死亡和海滩被迫关闭。在香港水域报道的红潮中，夜光虫（一种体型较大的异养甲藻）是导致发生红潮最多，特别是在冬季的东部和东北部水域发生最频繁的种类。对于很多食物有较强的捕食能力被认为是夜光虫的一个重要的生态优势。尽管夜光虫分布很广，它很多生理生态特征并没有被充分研究，特别是亚热带种群尤其如此。目前仅有一篇学术文章研究了香港的一个半封闭海湾的夜光虫的季节种群变化。在本研究中，我将研究：1）在冬季和春季东部水域导致夜光虫高密度或者发生水华的机理；2）夜光虫的捕食行为和它对其它浮游植物的选择性摄食；3）夜光虫在各种环境条件下的元素组成以及它在营养盐循环中的作用。 上面第一点将通过在冬季东北季风盛行时夜光虫水华最频繁发生时，在牛尾海以及附近水域的现场调查来研究。我们假设是：东北季风导致了营养盐丰富的中国沿岸流入侵，导致了夜光虫的食物在风引起的下涌流的作用下在湾内富集。第二点和第三点将会通过用香港水域分离的夜光虫的实验室实验来进行研究。我们将先研究夜光虫是否喜欢某些特别的食物。其次我们将调查夜光虫是否需要捕食异样食物来满足它们的氮需求。然后我们将研究在摄食氮丰富和氮贫乏的食物的时候，夜光虫的化学元素组成和营养盐的排泄的变化。我们也会研究夜光虫在长期饥饿情况下利用有机物的能力。我们也会通过跟日本科学家的合作来比较从香港的亚热带夜光虫品系和日本分离的温带品系生态生理特性方面的异同。 此研究的发现将帮助我们理解香港近岸水域夜光虫红潮发生机理以及夜光虫在亚热带近岸海洋微食物环和整个生态系统中的生物地化循环。

661610.label: Realisation of objectives
661610.value: Objective 1 has been achieved by conducting both a field survey and 4 microcosm incubation experiments in Port Shelter during between 4 October 2012 and April 2013. Through the survey and experiments, we found that both biological (plenty of prey due to phytoplankton bloom) and physical (coastal water intrusion due to favorable wind direction) conditions are responsible for the annual Noctiluca bloom during winter and early spring. Objective 2 is achieved by conducting a series lab experiment using 9 mono algal preys and 4 mixed diets to investigate Noctiluca food preference. Selected prey species (T. weissflogii, P. helgolandica and P. dentatum) grown under different nutrient condition (nutrient replete, N-depleted and P-depleted) were also chosen to conduct functional and numerical studies to further elucidate the influence of diet nutritional quality on the growth and grazing of N. stintillans. Experiments designed to study the composition and stoichiometry of nutrient excretion by Noctiluca under nutrient replete, N-limited and P-limited diets suggest that they are the major player in ammonium regeneration in the coast water ecosystems. Nutrient regeneration by Noctilcua under different light level was also studied. Now we are repeating the experiments to confirm our findings. Moreover, we would like to study whether temperature increase could also affect Noctiluca’s nutrient regeneration (and this is actually beyond the objective #3 of this project). For objective #4, we have tried to maintain Noctiluca culture in the yeast extraction, polyamines and glucose, but it was not successful. We observed cyst-like small cells in the cultures after a long period of time without feeding them . We made a great effort to identify that these small cells are the cyst of Noctiluca by molecular approach, but the sequence we obtained does not support that they are related to Noctiluca, so it remains mysterious what are those cyst-like small cells and whether Noctiluca in the starved culture died or formed cysts. We are still trying to study the life cycle of the Noctiluca at this moment.
