700510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
700510.value: Organic photovoltaic (OPV) devices are considered as new generation photovoltaic technology because of their potential as a renewable, alternative source for electrical energy. Encouraging progress with high power conversion efficiency up to 6% has been recently realized via innovative device engineering and development of smart materials. While the observed photocurrent is considerably high, the major obstacle for low power conversion efficiency is the relatively low open-circuit voltage (Voc). Extensive studies have been carried out on the fundamental physics governing the Voc of the devices; particularly, it is well recognized that the Voc is determined by the energy difference between the ionization potential of the donor and the electron affinity of the acceptor. However, the theoretical maximum of Voc is not attainable for most OPV devices at standard operating conditions. It is thus highly desirable to understand the interplays of material properties, device configurations and the Voc of OPV devices, as they are paramount parameters for attaining the theoretical maximum of Voc. Meanwhile, the investigator has recently examined the relation between the Voc and the offset energies at the donor/acceptor interface by using six representative fluorescent dye materials as interfacial layers to form a cascade-type energy band structure. It is found that the device structures and electron energy levels of these interfacial layers have a definite effect on the Voc of the devices. This proposed project aims to have a deep understanding on the origin of Voc of the devices, especially for more complicated device structures with multiple photoactive materials. In particular, this project is designed to i) to carry out systematic studies on how the constituent photoactive materials and device configurations affect the Voc of the devices, ii) to develop feasible approaches for attaining high Voc via post-production thermal annealing and careful control of measurement environment, and iii) to derive design rules for further improving the Voc as well as the power conversion efficiency of small-molecular based OPV devices. It is envisaged that the success of this project would not only provide a more complete understanding on the origin of Voc of the devices, but also permit a fast identification of high potential materials, a performance prediction, and a device structure optimization for creating a new dimension for substantial efficiency improvement of small-molecular based OPV devices. 有機光伏打電池被視為新一代太陽能電池技術，因此種電池有很大潛力提供潔淨再生能源，從而轉為電能。透過創新的器件設計及新材料的研發，目前有機光伏打電池的功率轉換效率已達到6%，其短路電流亦相當高。相反，它們的開路電壓相對較低，大大影響有機光伏打電池的功率轉換效率。近年已有不少學術論文探討有機光伏打電池的光電轉換原理及各項物理條件對開路電壓的影響，其中，廣泛的學術研究認為開路電壓取決於電子提供材料的游離能及電子接受材料的親和力之間的能量差。可是，在標準測試條件下，現時大部份的有機光伏打電池的開路電壓仍遠遠低於此最大理論值，因此深入研究感光材料的光學及電子特性、器件結構和開路電壓的相互影響是非常重要，從而亦可提供一些重要的參數以達到開路電壓的最大理論值。近年，首席研究員透過採用六種具不同電子游離能的螢光材料作電子提供材料及電子接受材料之間的界面層，探討開路電壓與有機物介面的能量偏移的關係，並研究出器件結構及電子能級對開路電壓有著重大的影響。本項目計劃針對一些多層感光材料的複雜器件，深入研究各項影響開路電壓的重要參數。在項目中，我們會一)研究不同的感光材料及器件成份和結構對開路電壓的影響，二)利用不同的測試環境提供可行的方法以提高開路電壓，及三)提出一些設計條件以改善有機光伏打電池的開路電壓和功率轉換效率。預期本項目將不僅提供影響開路電壓的重要參數的全面認識，並提供一些幫助選取高效能材料及器件優化的方法，將大大提高有機小分子光伏打電池的效能表現。

700510.label: Realisation of objectives
700510.value: With regard to this project, all project objectives have been realized and met with success. The roles and influences of electron energy levels of photoactive materials and device architecture on the Voc of the devices (objectives 1 and 2) and the effects of thermal annealing temperature on the performance of OPV devices (objective 3) have been studied. In order to realize the objectives, the influences of different exciton blocking layers (EBLs) and anode buffer layers on the performance of OPV devices with four donor-acceptor combination systems have been studied. The Voc of OPV devices was increased with the incorporation of cathodic EBLs; however, the Voc was increased modestly when an anode buffer layer was inserted. More importantly, the employment of cathodic EBL with higher electron mobility could move the Voc values closer to the theoretical maximum estimated from HOMO-LUMO energy difference. The interplays of the interface offset energy at the donor/acceptor interface and the Voc linearity factor (S1) had also been investigated. In addition to the well-known effects of the interface offset energy, the S1 was found to be dependent on the choice of EBLs. S1 was found to increase with increasing electron mobility in the EBLs; however, a marginal increase in S1 was observed when an anode buffer layer was inserted. A smaller ideality factor and a reduced saturated dark current density were responsible for the performance enhancement for devices with EBL as well as a larger S1 for the Voc. This work demonstrates for the first time the dependence of S1 on the choice of EBLs. The dependence of Voc on the HOMO level of bulk heterojunction OPV devices had also been systematically investigated, in which six non-absorbing hole- and electron-transporting materials were used as donor into C70 acceptor to form bulk heterojunction. The Voc was increased with increasing the HOMO offset and an optimal Voc was reached when HOMO offset was equal to 0.4 eV. Such optimal HOMO offset was higher than that for bilayer OPV devices, explaining why a high Voc could be obtained for bulk heterojunction OPV device. These findings reinforce the importance of the choice of EBLs or non-absorbing donor materials in OPV devices. These findings determine the ideal material parameters and device structures for attaining the theoretical maximum of Voc (objective 4), and provide design guidelines and selection rules for controlling the Voc and for maximizing the performance of OPV devices (objective 5).

700510.label: Major findings and research outcome
700510.value: The influences of different EBLs and anode buffer layers on the performance of OPV devices with four donor-acceptor combination systems had been systematically studied. With the insertion of EBLs, all photovoltaic responses such as Jsc and Voc were dramatically increased, leading to a concomitant increase in the PCE of the OPV devices. In addition, the Voc was linearly increased with the interface offset energy, in which S1 increased with increasing electron mobility in the EBLs; particularly, S1 increased from 0.55 for device without EBL to 0.76 for device with TmPyPB EBL. On the other hand, the insertion of anode buffer layer had a considerably weaker effect on S1 (i.e. S1 ≈ 0.76). This finding suggests that the employment of EBL with higher charge carrier mobility can increase the Voc of OPV devices, pushing the Voc closer to the theoretical maximum value calculated from the HOMO–LUMO energy difference. This work demonstrates for the first time the dependence of S1 on the choice of EBLs and reinforces the importance of the choice of EBLs on the Voc of OPV devices. A manuscript entitled as “Materials selection for an efficient exciton blocking layer for organic photovoltaic devices” has been submitted to Journal of Materials Chemistry C and is under review. The dependence of Voc of bulk heterojunction OPV devices on the energy level of donor materials had also been investigated. Six non-absorbing hole- or electron-transporting organic materials were used as donor doped into C70 acceptor to form bulk heterojunction. The Voc was generally increased from 0.73 V when HOMO level increased and reached its maximum at 0.96 V for HOMO = 5.7 eV, and fell off to 0.68 V for HOMO = 6.6 eV. An optimal Voc was obtained for HOMO offset of ~0.4 eV. It is worth noting that the optimal HOMO energy offset for bulk heterojunction OPV devices was higher than that for bilayer OPV devices. This explains why an extraordinarily high Voc could be observed for the bulk heterojunction OPV devices. A manuscript entitled as “Controlling Factors Governing the Performance of Bulk Heterojunction Organic Photovoltaic Devices with Low Donor Concentration” has been submitted to Organic Electronics and is under review. The present findings provide a complete understanding of the fundamental physics governing the photovoltaic responses, especially the Voc, of OPV devices, as well as provide selection guidelines of EBLs or donor materials in order to achieve theoretical maximum of Voc.

700510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
700510.value: This project has generalized the fundamental factors governing the Voc of bulk heterojunction OPV devices; particularly, the HOMO energy level offset at the donor-acceptor interface plays a crucial role in determining the Voc of the devices. However, the underlying physics governing the Jsc of bulk heterojunction OPV devices are still unclear. On one hand, the spectral responses of the devices were roughly resembled to the absorption spectrum of fullerene, regardless of the donor material employed. On the other hand, the Jsc could be dramatically increased by an order of magnitude upon the incorporation of hole-transporting material as donor. While the concept of a modified bulk heterojunction opens up a new dimension for achieving efficient small molecular-based OPV devices, a deep understanding on the exact mechanisms and physics for the Jsc would be definitely beneficial for the choice of non-absorbing donor materials for boosting up the PCE of the devices. Further studies on the correlation between hole mobilities of non-absorbing donors and the Jsc of bulk heterojunction OPV devices have been carried out. Preliminary results suggest that the Jsc is strongly dependent on hole mobility of donor and more works are needed to provide a complete picture of the underlying mechanisms.

700510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
700510.value: In order to further boost up the PCE of OPV devices, a complete understanding of the fundamental physics governing the photovoltaic responses and their relationship with the physical and energetic properties of the constituent materials are of prime importance. This project has generalized the fundamental factors of the EBLs and the donor materials affecting the photovoltaic responses, especially the Voc, of OPV devices. Particularly, the employment of EBL with higher charge carrier mobility can not only increase the Voc of OPV devices, but also pushing the Voc closer to the theoretical maximum value. Meanwhile, an optimal HOMO energy level offset is necessary for realizing a high Voc. Either too small or too large HOMO energy level offset would inevitably lower the Voc and the power conversion efficiency of the OPV devices. These findings would be technologically useful for improving the performance of OPV devices, and also provide valuable guidelines for material selection in EBLs or donor materials in OPV devices.

700810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
700810.value: Selective and highly efficient oxidation reactions that use environmentally friendly oxidants and /or catalysts from naturally abundant metal ions can resolve many of the problems that are caused by the chemical industries. Practical oxidation reactions with diverse applications in organic chemistry and which use oxygen or hydrogen peroxide as terminal oxidant is a holy grail area. The difficulty lies in lacking means whereby highly reactive oxidants directly generated from oxygen or hydrogen peroxide can be used for chemical reactions as desired. In this proposal, both biomimetic and photochemical approaches are adopted for the research. Light excitation is used to generate highly reactive oxidants including singlet oxygen, which would be harnessed for selective organic oxidation reactions under suitably designed reaction conditions. We propose to develop biomimetic oxidation for organic synthesis using molecular iron-catalysts. This proposal is a new direction of the Principal Investigator’s research in oxidation chemistry and is back up by his recent works on non-osmium catalysed cis-dihydroxylation of alkenes, non-heme iron complexes for organic oxidation, and aerobic organic oxidation reactions. The project involves catalysts design, organic catalysis, and study of reaction intermediates. The keys are: [1] to use high-valent iron-oxo complexes for organic oxidation, [2] to efficiently use air as a terminal oxidant, and [3] to design new ligand systems for highly robust metal catalysts. The proposed research is of fundamental interest in chemical sciences and can lead to novel technologies for chemical industries that are sustainable and environmetally non-hazardous. 使用環境友好的氧化劑和/或源於自然界供應充足金屬的催化劑，有選擇性的高效氧化反應可以解決當前化學工業引起的很多問題。實用型氧化反應在有機化學領域有很多應用，而使用氧氣或過氧化氫作為起始氧化劑，則甚具挑戰性。目前的主要困難是，缺少有效手段使由氧氣或者過氧化氫直接產生的高活性氧化劑可以按照預期設計參與化學反應。在本計畫書，我們採用仿生學和光化學方法研究這一可行性。用光激發的方法產生高活性的氧化劑（包括單線態氧），在合適的反應條件下，可以駕馭並用於選擇性的有機氧化反應。我們計畫開發利用分子型鐵催化劑的仿生氧化反應，用於有機合成。本計畫是主要研究員在氧化反應研究的新分支，他在類似的研究已頗有建樹：比如非-鋨催化的烯烴的順式雙羥基化反應，非-血紅素型鐵配合物的有機氧化反應，和耗氧有機氧化反應等。該專案包括催化劑設計，有機催化，和研究反應中間體。其關鍵幾點如下：【1】使用高價鐵氧配合物做有機氧化反應，【2】有效地使用空氣作為起始氧化劑，和【3】設計新型配體體系來製備穩固的金屬催化劑。本計畫既是重要的化學科學基礎研究，又可以為化學工業開發可持續發展的和環境無害的新型技術。

700810.label: Realisation of objectives
700810.value: We have achieved the stated objectives; 7 papers have been published: Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (1), J. Am. Chem. Soc. (1), Chem. Sci. (1), Chem. Commun. (1) and Chem. Eur. J. (3). 15 presentations were delivered. Objective 1. We prepared a series of palladium(II) porphyrin complexes showing dual emissions with lifetimes up to 473us and robust catalytic activity towards light-induced aerobic oxidation reactions in up to 99% yields. [Chem. Eur. J. 2013, 19, 5654]. Objective 2. We synthesized a series of trans-dioxo-osmium(VI) complexes, which are powerful photo-oxidants with long excited state lifetimes. Their emission quantum yields are highest among the reported luminescent trans-dioxo-osmium(VI) complexes. Upon irradiation with blue LED, they catalyzed photochemical aerobic oxidation of cyclohexane. [Ng, YM; PhD work, unpublished]. Objective 3. We have developed a practical protocol for asymmetric cis-dihydroxylation of alkenes with Oxone using a manganese catalyst to give cis-diols in up to 95% isolated yield and up to 96% ee. ESI-MS analysis of the crude reaction mixture revealed a cationic cis-dioxomanganese(V) intermediate [Chem. Commun. 2011, 47, 11204]. The similar reactions with H2O2 were catalyzed by related iron(III) complexes to give cis-diols in up to 85% yield with excellent ee of 99.8%. [manuscript in preparation] Objectives 4 and 5. Iron(II) oligopyridine catalysts were applied onto practical oxidation with Oxone. Terpy ligand supported on SBA-15 could be recycled for 5 times by in situ reaction with iron(II) salt. The corresponding iron-oxo intermediate was detected by ESI-MS analysis [Chem. Sci. 2011, 2, 2187]. The same catalytic system could applied to nitrene C(sp3)-H bond insertion reactions with PhINR or “PhI(OAc)2 + amine” as the nitrene source. Results from ESI-MS analysis and DFT calculations lends support to reactive iron(IV) or iron(VI) intermediates [J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2013, 135, 7194]. [FeIII(Me3tacn)(Cl-acac)Cl]ClO4 (Fe-1) catalyzed the oxidation of ethane and propane with buffered Oxone at r.t. for 30 min. Oxidation of cyclohexane by “Fe-1 + Oxone” was achieved in 5 min. The reactive oxoiron(IV) ligand-cation-radical intermediate was characterized. [Angew. Chem., Int. Ed. 2014, 53, 798] Objective 6. The previously reported ruthenium- and gold-catalyzed aerobic oxidation reactions were similarly accomplished by singlet oxygen generated by light irradiation of phosphorescent metal complexes - see objective 1. The findings on a panel of light-induced photochemical aerobic oxidation reactions have not been published. A “gold(I) complex + Brønsted acid” protocol was applied to tandem intermolecular hydroamination/transfer hydrogenation of alkynes with secondary amines. [Chem. Eur. J. 2011, 17, 12932]

700810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
700810.value: Oxidation reactions are fundamental important in both Chemistry and Biology. In the development of sustainable catalysis for fine chemicals industry, it is crucial to develop catalysts from earth abundant metals and green oxidants such as air and hydrogen peroxide for selective oxidation reactions that have important practical applications in organic synthesis. The iron catalysts developed in this project have demonstrated important ,practical applications in selective organic oxidations. The iron catalyzed highly enantioselective alkene cis-dihydroxylation reactions using hydrogen peroxide as terminal oxidant is an important finding and further research along this direction should be encouraged. In this project, it has been shown that reactive iron-oxo and iron-imido complexes supported by N-donor ligands display rich oxidation chemistry particularly in C-H functionalization. It is hoped to continue the research so as to develop a protocol “light + oxygen + iron catalyst “ for selective organic oxidation with practical applications.

700810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
700810.value: Although oxidation reaction is a basic transformation in organic synthesis, practical green oxidation reactions with high product selectivity and product yields using oxygen as oxidant and which are performed in water under ambient conditions is not trivial in chemical industry. Advancement in this area will have a profound impact on synthetic chemistry, thereby bringing gigantic social and economic benefits. This project has resulted in a panel of new, inexpensive metal catalysts such as that of iron for highly selective oxidation reactions of importance in fine chemicals industry and practical organic synthesis. In addition, this project has also led to the development of new catalytic oxidation reactions with the use of sunlight and air as terminal oxidant, gold-catalyzed transformations, and manganese-catalyzed highly enantioselective oxidative C-O bond formation reaction. The findings from this project have been published in top international chemistry journals including Journal of the American Chemical Society, Angewandte Chemie International Edition, Chemical Sciences, Chemical Communications and Chemistry-A European Journal. The accomplishments made in this project contribute new, useful synthetic methodologies for fine chemical industry and to put Hong Kong as a world leading research center in homogeneous oxidation catalysis.

701010.label: Project Objectives
701010.value: To develop a theory of the scanning tunneling microscopic study about the Kondo effect in topological insulagors and make prediction or comparison with the expriments based on the theory. To study the Kondo effect in the mesoscopic topological insulators. To deduce the interaction between two Anderson impurities and investigate the Kondo effect for two Anderson impurities.

701010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701010.value: The discovery of the topological insulator is one of the most important progresses in condensed matter physics in recent years. It has attracted lots of attentions because of not only the fundamental importance but also the great potential for practical application. Topological insulator is a nontrivial time reversal invariant insulator with topologically protected gapless boundary states lying in the bulk gap, which is the first example of state of matter with non-trivial topological property besides of the quantum Hall state. The non-trivial topological properties make these boundary states robust against any time reversal invariant perturbation. On the other hand, the spin-orbital interaction plays an important role in the topological insulator systems. Due to the spin-orbital interaction, the spin of the carriers in topological insulators (mainly the boundary states) couples to their momentum. Hence, topological insulator seems to be a rather promising material for developing novel quantum and spintronic devices and has great potential for practical technological application. It is proposed that the surface of topological insulator is a helical metal, where the linear dispersion has been observed experimentally. And the physical properties of those surface states is a very hot topic in condensed matter physics. In this proposal, we would like to investigate the Kondo effect in the topological insulator system with single and two Anderson impurities. We plan to investigate the Kondo effect of a single Anderson impurity on the surface of a mesoscopic topological insulator where the quantum plays an unnegligible role. We will also study the case of two Anderson impurities. We will deduce the interaction between the two impurities mediated by the surface states as an analogous to the RKKY interaction in the conventional metal, and investigate the Kondo effect of two impurites. To make comparison with the experiments, we will study the scanning tunneling spectroscopy experiment, which has been a powerful technique in Kondo effect in normal system, in the topological insulators. With the suitable calculation, we can make prediction on the experiment and test our theoretical calculations. 拓扑绝缘体是凝聚态物理在最近几年最重要的发现之一。拓扑绝缘体对于基础研究和实际应用都有很重要的价值。拓扑绝缘体是指一种时间反演不变且具有受拓扑保护的无能隙的边缘态的绝缘体。拓扑绝缘体是除了量子霍尔效应态以外第一个具有非平庸拓扑性质的物质态。而这种拓扑性质保护了拓扑绝缘体的边缘态使其不受任何时间反演不变扰动的影响。而另一方面，自旋轨道耦合现象在拓扑绝缘体系统中起了很重要的作用。由于自旋轨道，拓扑绝缘体系统（特别是边缘态）中的载流子的自旋和其动量耦合在了一起。因此，拓扑绝缘体在研制新型量子和自旋电子学器件方向上有非常大的应用潜力。有人指出拓扑绝缘体的表面被认为是手征金属，其特性之一的线性色散关系也已经被实验所证实。这样一种表面态是最近凝聚态物理中一个非常重要的问题。我们打算讨论拓扑绝缘体系统里的近藤效应。首先，我们计划研究介观拓扑绝缘体表面上的单个Anderson杂质的近藤效应。然后我们会讨论两个杂质时的情况，并且推导两个杂质之间的类RKKY相互作用。我们还计划针对扫描隧道显微镜等实验给出一些实验预言以便对我们的理论计算进行检测。

701010.label: Realisation of objectives
701010.value: Kondo effect or Anderson magnetic impurity problem is one of the most challenging issues in modern physics because it is related to scaling concept. Recent development of the field in topological insulator has naturally asked the question about the Kondo effect in this new type of matter. This project is to aim to address some of the issues from theoretical point of view. In a series of papers, we have applied variational wave-functions method to study the Kondo effect in the mesoscopic topological insulator, and the spin-spin correlations. We have also used transport theory to predict a giant spin polarization at the edge of a sharp potential when a transverse electric current is applied. Our studies have added new understanding to tis sub-field. The papers are published eithher in Physical Review Letters or Physical Review.

701010.label: Major findings and research outcome
701010.value: * We studied the spin-1/2 Kondo effect of a helical metal on the surface of a three-dimensional topological insulator by using a trial wave function. We found that while the impurity spin is quenched by conduction electrons, the spin-spin correlation of the conduction electron and impurity is strongly anisotropic in both spin and spatial spaces. As a result of strong spin-orbit coupling, the out-of-plane component of the impurity spin is found to be fully screened by the orbital angular momentum of the conduction electrons. (PRB 81, 235411, 2010) * We studied mesoscopic spin Hall effect on the surface of a topological insulator with a step-function potential by using the McMillan method commonly used in the study of superconductor junctions. We predict that, in the ballistic transport regime, a giant spin polarization will be induced by a transverse electric current with parameter suitable to the topological insulator thin film Bi2Se3, the spin polarization oscillates across the potential boundary with no confinement due to the Klein paradox, and should be observable in a spin resolved scanning tunneling microscope. (PRL 106, 057205, 2011) * We studied the spin-1/2 Anderson impurity in a semiconductor quantum well with Rashba and Dresselhaus spin–orbit couplings by using a variational wavefunction method. We found that the local magnetic moment to be quenched at low temperatures, and showed that the spin–spin correlations of the impurity and the conduction electron density show anisotropy in both spatial and spin spaces, which interpolates the Kondo spin screenings of a conventional metal and of a surface of three-dimensional topological insulators. (J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 23, 105602, 2011) * We have done a theoretical analysis on the interlayer couplings in multilayer cuprates using a renormalized mean-field theory, and found that the coexisting uniform antiferromagnetism and d-wave superconductivity reported in multilayer cuprates, when compared to single-layer or bilayer cuprates, should be due to the enhanced screening of random potential modulations in inner layers. The potential for an improved determination of the antiferromagnetic and superconducting order parameters in an ideal single layer from zero-field NMR and infrared Josephson plasma resonances in multilayer cuprates is also suggested. (EPL, 98, 57005, 2012)

701110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
701110.value: 恆星被超大質量黑洞捕獲的後果

701110.label: Co - Investigator(s)
701110.value: Prof Dogiel, Vladimir Prof Liu, Fukun

701110.label: Project Objectives
701110.value: (1)The formation of relativistic jet is very common phenomenon in the accreting black hole systems, ranging from stellar mass black holes, intermediate mass black holes (e.g. microquasars) and supermassive black holes (e.g. active galactic nuclei). When a relativistic jet is emitted during the transient accreting phase after a star is captured by the massive black hole at the center of galaxies. The jet can form shock when it interacts with the interstellar medium and intense broad band radiation will be emitted. We will study the time evolution of the broad band spectrum. In particular we want to know what conditions can make the high energy bands be detected by high energy satellites, e.g. Chandra, Swift and Fermi. Eventually this transient jet becomes non-relativistic, the peak of the emission band should be at radio regime but they may be strong enough to be detected by the ground based telescopes and hence their host galaxies can be identified. (2)Relativistic particles are the key ingredient in the jet, hadronic collisions, which produce pions, are other important processes in this phenomenon. High energy photons and positrons resulting from the decay of neutral and positive charged pions respectively can be important particles to identify this kind of event. In particular annihilation of positrons is a very distinctive signal. We will calculate positron annihilation processes and compare the observed data from COMPTEL and INTEGRAL to set some constraints in the capture process of the Milky Way. (3)We will also study other possible stellar capture related phenomena, which may allow us to understand the stellar capture process and the properties of the galaxies in more detail.

701110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701110.value: It is generally believed that the center of normal galaxies should house a supermassive black hole including the center of Milky Way. Most of these supermassive black holes are not active. However, they can be activated to behave similar to active galactic nuclei after capture and tidally disrupt a star. These phenomena have been observed in nearby galaxies and there are some observational evidences that similar processes have been occurred in the supermassive black hole located at the center of Milky Way too. Conventionally the stellar capture processes are identified by the transient X-ray emission from the accretion disk, which has a characteristic light curve satisfying t^{-5/3}. In this project we will study other observational consequences of these stellar capture processes of various types of stellar objects. The emission of a relativistic jet, which consists of relativistic protons, is a general feature of accreting black hole systems. Therefore after the supermassive black hole capture and disrupt a star, a transient accretion disk is formed and most likely a transient jet is also emitted during the accretion process. The jet contains relativistic particles and it can form shock when it interacts with interstellar medium. A time dependent broad band radiation spectrum will be emitted from the shock region, we will investigate the evolution of this broad band radiation spectrum. If these events occur in nearby galaxies, the X-ray satellites, e.g. Chandra and Swift, should be able to detect them. Eventually the peak of the broad band radiation should shift to radio regime, the ground based telescopes can detect the signal and identify the host galaxies. Also the relativistic particles can collide with the interstellar medium and produce pions. High energy photons produced by decay of neutral pions should be detectable by the gamma-ray satellites, e.g. Fermi, if these events occur in nearby galaxies. Positrons can be produced by the decay of positive charged pions and the annihilation of positrons is one of most clear signature of the stellar capture events. In fact intense annihilation lines have observed in the Center of our Galaxy, which may result from the stellar capture processes. The study of this project not only allow us to probe the quiescent massive black holes located at the center of nearby galaxies but also provide very important information about the formation and evolution of galaxies. 在銀河系中心存在一個幾個百萬太陽質量的大黑洞，叫Sgr A *。 儘管當前的 x 射線觀測表明它處於非活動狀態的階段，我們建議 Sgr A * 過去是活躍的，它是實際的高能量的粒子的能源來源。 我們認為當Sgr A *捕獲一顆恆星時可以成為類似活動星系核的星體。當捕獲恆星的物質傳到星系的黑洞時，會激發包含主要是質子的相對論射流。 許多目前觀察到的高能量的排放現象，即正電子湮沒線、伽瑪射線等，都可能因此相對論射流中發出。 在這一專案中，我們希望進行比較的觀測資料與模型預測的詳細模型計算。 我們亦會研究在我們的星系以及其他如在附近的正常星系的黑洞的恆星捕獲的高能量觀測後果。

701110.label: Realisation of objectives
701110.value: For the first objective, we consider how the magnetic field distribution can affect the injection energy of positrons when they start to annihilate into 0.5MeV photon lines. We next consider the ejection energy produced by the capture process. This energy is carried out by relativistic protons, which can heat the vicinity material and form hot wind. This wind can escape to the galactic halo. Because the wind is supersonic and shock will be formed, the shocked relativistic electrons can emit high energy photons which can be detected by X-rays and gamma-ray satellites. We also consider some other observational phenomena, which may relate to stellar capture events including the transient X-ray emission from some molecular clouds near the galactic center and the evolution of K-shell X-ray lines etc. The Fermi satellite has discovered two gigantic symmetric emission region extended up and down of the galactic center to 10kpc of the galactic halo region called Fermi Bubble, we argue that these two huge gamma-ray emission regions result from the past stellar events. One important mystery of cosmic rays is the origin of cosmic particles with energy higher than 10^15eV, we show that the shocks in the Fermi Bubble may produce these ultra-high energy cosmic particles. For the second objective, we consider the hadronic collisions processes and we show that the decay of pions can produce both gamma-rays as well as high energy neutrinos. In particular the very high energy neutrinos can be detected by the neutrino detected located in south pole called IceCube. For the third objective, we study some events, which may relate to stellar capture processes. One of such possible events is detected by the X-ray satellite Swift and the event is called Swift 1644+57. In this event extremely intense and time varying X-rays are detected. We argue that the properties of the detected X-rays can be explained in terms of some collisions among the discrete ejecta, which are produced after the star is captured by the supermassive black hole.

701110.label: Major findings and research outcome
701110.value: In this project we have published 8 refereed papers in top journals of astronomy and astrophysics. In pub. 1 we consider how the galactic field distribution near the galactic center can affect the injection energy spectrum of positrons, which can put strong constraint on model. In pub. 2 we argue that the event rate of partial stellar capture should be higher than a full capture event. Therefore it is possible that a partial capture event can take place in several hundred years ago. This event can generate an intense X-ray beam for tens of years. The observed transient X-ray emission from the nearby molecular clouds of the galactic center results from the illumination of this past emitted intense X-ray beam. In pub. 3 we suggest that the observed gigantic gamma-ray emission bubbles in the galactic halo called Fermi Bubbles are the consequences of past stellar capture events. In pub. 4 the K-shell X-ray lines emitted from the nearby molecular cloud may result from the excitation of subrelativistic protons which are produced by the past stellar capture. In pub. 5 we study the high energy neutrinos production via hadronic collision processes in the stellar capture event and argue that if these events take place in nearby galaxies, the neutrino detectors, e.g. IceCube in south pole, can be detected. In pub 6, it is known that the origin of cosmic rays with energy lower than 10^15eV is originated from supernovae but the origin of cosmic rays with energy higher than 10^15eV is controversial. We show that given the large spatial scale of shock in Fermi Bubbles it is possible that cosmic rays with energy higher than 10^15eV are generated from this region. In pub. 7 we explain the observed properties of X-rays detected in the extra-galactic stellar capture event in terms of internal shock model. In pub. 8 although the origin of 6.4 KeV iron line emission and the H2 molecular ionization are different, they may still relate to past capture event.

701110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701110.value: Two very important discoveries related to the stellar capture by supermassive black hole events are the Fermi Bubble and Swift J1644+57. In current project we have made some preliminary models for these two events. After their discoveries there are many more data detected in multi-wavebands including radio, X-rays and gamma-rays, it is obviously to carry out more detail studies for these events. We have submitted a new GRF proposal to carry out more detail theoretical calculation to study the detail energy ejection process in the early stage of the stellar capture, which plays very crucial role in explaining the time dependent spectrum of X-rays detected in Swift J1644+57. We will also use Monte Carlo simulation to study the shock formation, shock heating of plasma, propagation of shock front to compare with the detail radio, X-ray and gamma-ray data in Fermi Bubble.

701110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
701110.value: This project mainly studies the consequences and possible observational evidences resulting from the capture of stars by the supermassive black hole (SMBH) located in normal galaxies including the SMBH at the center of our own galaxy Milky Way. We have considered several phenomena around the Galactic Center including positron annihilation lines, time varying X-ray emission, K-shell iron lines etc., we propose that the observed characteristics of these phenomena can be explained by past stellar capture events in Milky Way. Fermi satellite has recently discovered a pair of dump bell shape huge emission region located symmetrically at the top and bottom of the galactic center. We explain the properties of gamma-ray emission bubbles in terms of fast wind injection resulting from the sporadic stellar capture process by the galactic SMBH. Furthermore we calculate the shock acceleration of protons emitted from the Fermi Bubbles and show that these relativistic protons may be the origin of cosmic in the energy range >10^15eV. We also use the stellar capture process to explain the intense transient X-ray emissions produced by other galaxies including Swift J1644+57. The stellar capture process may allow us to probe the properties of SMBH even located in other galaxies.

701510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701510.value: Cocaine is a psychostimulant, and its abuse is responsible for a variety of societal problems and represents a substantial burden on community resources. One way to address the problem of cocaine addiction from a medicinal and therapeutic approach is the development and administration of an effective inhibitor of cocaine. Mimicking the structure of cocaine, which is an 8-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane, a number of analogues have been designed that inhibit the dopamine transporter and could function as antagonists. In addition to the nitrogen-bearing analogues, oxygen and carbon analogues have also been effective. However, the current syntheses of these analogues are unable to afford the desired molecules in high enantiomeric purity efficiently. Based on our recent success in the development of the [4+3] cycloaddition using epoxy enol silanes as oxyallyl cation precursors, we now have in our hands an excellent reaction tool to generate bicyclo[3.2.1]octane systems directly and with high enantioselectivity. This project proposes to further develop the [4+3] cycloaddition for asymmetric synthesis, and then apply the results to construct a number of existing and newly-designed cocaine analogues. The analogues will be screened for dopamine transporter affinity. The assembly of a structure-relationship profile and computer docking experiments will further guide the design of additional inhibitors. The development of the [4+3] cycloaddition using aziridinyl enol silanes and pyrroles as substrates would provide a novel and efficient entry to nitrogen-bearing polycycles which were not previously accessible by this reaction. This could yield a route to novel tropanes as well as nitrogen-containing intermediates toward other pharmacologically significant alkaloids. Ultimately, this project could provide a new and more effective route to molecules which are known inhibitors as well as novel antagonists that could be used therapeutically against cocaine addiction. 可卡因是一種神經興奮劑，它的濫用引發廣泛的社會問題，耗費了大量的社會資源。從醫學和治療學上講，對付可卡因依賴性的一個方法就是開發和應用有效的可卡因抑制劑。通过模擬可卡因的8-氮雜雙環【3.2.1】辛烷結構, 有研究設計了一系列可以抑制多巴胺載體從而可以作為可卡因拮抗剂的類似物。除了這些含氮的類似物外，氮分别被氧和碳替代的類似物也同樣有效。然而現在還缺少對於這些化合物的高效的、高對影選擇性的合成方法。我們最近成功地發展了環氧烯醇硅烷作为氧烯丙基正離子前体的【4+3】環加成反應，該反應為我們提供了雙環【3.2.1】辛烷體系的直接的高對影選擇性的合成方法。該課題的目的就是進一步開發不對稱的【4+3】環加成反應，並將之應用於一些已知或新設計的可卡因類似物的合成中去。我们會对這些類似物的多巴胺載體親和力進行筛選。而構效關係分析和計算機Docking實驗將會為我們後繼的抑制劑設計指明方向。 開發氮丙定烯醇硅烷和吡咯間的【4+3】環加成反應將會我們提供構建氮雜多環類化合物的全新的高效合成方法，這些氮雜多環化合物之前用該方法是得不到的。因此，該研究將會托品烷類似物及其它有重要藥物活性的生物碱的含氮中間體的合成提供一條全新的路線。 最終，該課題將為治療可卡因依賴性的已知抑制剂和全新拮抗剂的合成提供一種新的更有效的合成方法。

701510.label: Realisation of objectives
701510.value: This proposal sought to study the intermolecular (4+3) cycloaddition of epoxy and aziridinyl enolsilanes and its applications. This grant enabled the in-depth study of this intermolecular reaction. We have found the optimized conditions to generate the endo and exo cycloadducts with retained ee and have examined the reaction scope. We have also acquired a good understanding of the mechanism, via computational studies in collaboration with UCLA and with Univ of Queensland. Altogether, the findings of these studies have generated 4 high-impact publications on epoxy enolsilanes and one publication on aziridinyl enolsilanes. Thus Objectives 1 and 5 have been fully realized. The reactions of pyrroles as dienes was extensively studied and just about every technique to realize this reaction has been tried, but so far this difficult diene has not undergone any intermolecular cycloadditions, only alkylations. Thus Objective 6 has been fully addressed although the results are negative. This reaction has been successfully applied to the asymmetric synthesis of an oxabicyclic analogue of cocaine, thus also achieving completely Objective 2. In fact the synthesis of this oxabicyclic analogue is more challenging than the carbocyclic analogue described in Objective 3, and having achieved the oxabicyclic dopamine transporter, to repeat almost the same reactions but to a carbocyclic precursor in order to achieve Objective 3 was expected to be a trivial pursuit. We decided to direct our efforts to study and follow up other findings instead of fully realizing Objective 3. The synthesis of the aryloxy tropane analogues had been studied by Ms. S. Lam as a part of her Ph. D. program. Unfortunately, after a substantial effort, there is still a hurdle to install substituents at the required equatorial position. Therefore Objective 4 was not fully achieved. Other significant findings that we spent time on included mechanistic studies, synthesis and studies of enantiomerically enriched oxabicyclic ketones as catalysts for epoxidations, which constituted two chapters in the Ph.D. thesis of Ms. S. Lam; as well as asymmetric Friedel Crafts reactions that are derived from the same activated epoxide intermediate. This work will be published in due course.

701510.label: Major findings and research outcome
701510.value: 1. The intermolecular (4+3) cycloadditions of enantiomerically pure epoxy enolsilanes are catalyzed by silyl triflates or triflic acid, and are completely diastereoselective to generate optically pure cycloadducts with both furans and cyclopentadienes as dienes. (Publications 1, 2, 3: Publication 2 became a VIP and the cover article of the journal, and publication 3 was selected as a Hot paper. ) 2. That this is an excellent method to afford optically pure bicyclic (4+3) cycloadducts for synthesis is demonstrated by the efficient synthesis of a dopamine transporter inhibitor, which had previously been synthesized with up to 85% ee only; whereas the same product can be obtained from our optically pure adduct in higher yield and with a higher 99% ee. Our method is the best for the synthesis of such compounds in the reported literature. (Publication 3) 3. That this is an excellent method to afford optically pure bicyclic (4+3) cycloadducts enabled the synthesis of a series of optically pure bicyclic ketones for organocatalysis of asymmetric epoxidations via dioxiranes (not yet published). 4. The mechanistic findings both experimentally and computationally that this cycloaddition that does not proceed via oxyallyl cations as intermediates stands in contrast with the common (4+3) cycloaddition paradigm. (Publication 5) 5. The (4+3) cycloaddition of aziridinyl enolsilanes has been realized but used stoichiometric protic acid as the promoter, and shown to also be able to proceed asymmetrically to give cycloadducts with up to 99% ee. (Publication 4)

701510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701510.value: Since the asymmetric cycloaddition of aziridinyl enolsilanes has been achieved, the products could also be explored for use as intermediates for other syntheses. This aziridinyl enolsilane could also be explored further for intramolecular cycloadditions. These aspects will be followed up as projects for future summer students or RPg students. In addition, during the studies on the scope of the cycloaddition, phenyl subsituents were found to react as either Friedel-Crafts aromatics, or as dienes for (4+3) cycoadditions. The asymmetric Friedel-Crafts reaction is being studied by a current RPg. The use of aromatic compounds as dienes is also being pursued.

701510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
701510.value: The (4+3) cycloaddition reaction of enantiomerically enriched epoxy enolsilanes generate bicyclic adducts with high ee. This significant result challenges the current paradigm of the cycloaddition which had been assumed to always proceed via the intermediacy of an oxyallyl cation. Our results show for the first time definitively that oxyallyl cations are not needed as intermediates. In addition to challenging the convention, this reaction is also synthetically useful for the asymmetric synthesis of bicyclic adducts. It has been employed as the key reaction to synthesize a dopamine transporter inhibitor, and is currently the most successful synthesis to date. Aziridinyl enolsilanes have been found to similarly undergo cycloaddition promoted by acids to generate bicyclic adducts that could be used for the synthesis of alkaloids.

We describe the first examples of phosphoserine- and phosphothreonine-containing peptide radical cations formed through a one-electron transfer mechanism during low-energy collision-induced dissociation (CID) of gas phase ternary metal–ligand phosphorylated peptide complexes. The CID of phosphorylated peptide radical cations (pM•+) revealed fascinating gas phase radical chemistry. The extent of neutral H3PO4 loss depended largely on the peptide sequence and the initial sites of the charge and radical. It was followed by a density functional theory study, at the B3LYP 6-311++G(d,p) level of theory to elucidate the factors governing the elimination of neutral phosphoryl groups. Results showed that the dissociation reactions of these two peptide radical cations of the canonical glycylphosphoserinyltryptophan radical cation having its radical located on the side chain of the tryptophan residue ([GpSW]+ ) fragments differently from its tautomer with the radical initially generated on the α-carbon atom of the glycine residue ([GpSW]+).are more efficient than their tautomerization, thereby favoring charge-driven loss of H3PO4; in contrast, radical-driven pathways are more competitive during their fragmentations. 701610.value: Fragmentation of gas-phase peptides and their ion structures in tandem mass spectrometry provide the scientific basis underlying gas phase peptide sequencing by correlating the product ions generated to the original peptide structures. Dissociation of radical peptides is becoming an important emerging bioanalytical technique for proteomics studies. The experimental investigations of radical propagation o was hindered by difficulties in performing experiments for to track the isomerization processes to be computationally tractable. Thus, exploring how the reactivity of peptide radical within the system can help to reveal the fundamental factors governing the isomerization and fragmentation reactions. As part of our ongoing interests toward understanding the fundamental parameters that govern fragmentation chemistry of peptide radical cations, our experimental results and the theoretical construct we have used to allow us to the design of the post-translationally modified peptide radical ion with well-defined initial locations of the radical centers therefore would be important to allow a better understanding over the nature of the isomerization of radical ions and its subsequent dissociation pathways. We believe our findings will enrich the fundamental understanding in the mechanisms for the radical-induced fragmentations in mass spectrometer—the underpinning technology in proteomics and has been routinely used nowadays for protein identification.

701810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701810.value: Raman spectroscopy is a nondestructive spectroscopic technique used to study vibrational, electronic and other low-energy modes in a system. Although persistent interests and remarkable success of vibrational Raman spectroscopy application on single walled Carbon nanotubes (SWNTs) have been achieved for more than a decade, the electronic Raman scattering where the photon is scattered by electrons in SWNTs has rarely addressed if any. The electronic Raman spectroscopy has been proved as a direct probe of carrier (electron) distribution function in conventional bulk semiconductors and 2 dimensional electron gas systems. It is particularly suitable to study the electron transport properties and transient (non-equilibrium) electron distribution in semiconductors. In a one dimensional system such as SWNTs, a direct measure of electron diffusion, electron distribution and electron-electron scattering has been lacking. In this application, the PI proposes methods to explore the application of electronic Raman spectroscopy on SWNTs. The potential application will not only address widespread concerns on electron transport properties of SWNTs but also benefit the study in one dimensional systems. 单壁碳纳米管是一个直径大约在1个纳米量级，自封闭的碳原子管。由于直径接近电子的德布洛伊波长，量子束缚效应非常明显。相比于其他纳米线，碳纳米管可以被认为是真正意义上的量子线。根据结构的不同，碳纳米管可以表现为金属型和半导体型。所以碳纳米管是一个研究一维物理的理想材料。 拉曼散射光谱是一种非损伤的光学手段。它有效广泛的应用于碳纳米管的研究。但是迄今为止，碳纳米管拉曼光谱的研究集中于光子-声子散射。电子拉曼散射光谱还没有涉及。本研究申请计划开展碳纳米管电子拉曼光谱的实验研究。电子拉曼散射光谱将有效的探索一维体系的电子输运性质，电子迁移率，费米速度。

701810.label: Realisation of objectives
701810.value: We have successfully built experimental set-ups for low frequency Raman scattering with high efficiency and observed electronic Raman scattering from individual single walled carbon nanotubes. We collected the single-particle excitation of electronic Raman scattering around 1meV from a semiconducting single walled carbon nanotube with structure index of (14, 13) and extracted the corresponding electronic dispersion with a slope of 5.6~6.3×10^(-7)meV∙cm around the subband edges related with the interband optical transition. This is the first report on single-particle excitation on individual carbon nanotubes. Our finding quantitatively agrees with the present theoretical models and demonstrates the recent advances in experimental approaches towards fine-structured electronic study.

701810.label: Major findings and research outcome
701810.value: We have successfully built experimental set-ups for low frequency Raman scattering with high efficiency, including one dual-stage spectrometer (SPEX1430) with home-build refrided PMT photon-counting system and one single stage spectrometer with a serial of volume Brag grating (VBG) filters. We observed electronic Raman scattering from individual single walled carbon nanotubes. We collected the single-particle excitation of electronic Raman scattering around 1meV from a semiconducting single walled carbon nanotube with structure index of (14, 13) and extracted the corresponding electronic dispersion with a slope of 5.6~6.3×10^(-7)meV∙cm around the subband edges related with the interband optical transition. We also applied our experimental setup to study low frequency Raman mode on 2D crystals. We identified two distinct low-frequency Raman modes, shear mode and layer breathing mode, on atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides.

701810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701810.value: We plan to study the electronic Raman scattering from more individual carbon nanbotubes and therefore to explore new physics in this intrinsic one-dimensional crystals. Owing to the requirement for the resonance excitation and the limitation of laser sources, we only observed electronic Raman signal from one individual carbon nanotube. We plant to work on more samples to explore the new physics. We also plan to apply the established techniques on other emerging low-dimensional materials, particularly 2D materials. Our research emphasizes on the electronic Raman scattering and fundamental excitations, including Single-particle excitation, Plasmon mode, spin-flip mode, etc.

701810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
701810.value: We have successfully built an experimental set-up for low frequency Raman scattering with high efficiency and observed electronic Raman scattering from individual single walled carbon nanotubes, which is a tiny signal reflecting fundamental properties of electronic structures. The experimental setup we developed is a brand new approach to optical study on electronic properties of nanoscale objects. We successfully collected the single-particle excitation of electronic Raman scattering around 1meV from a semiconducting single walled carbon nanotube with structure index of (14, 13) and extracted the corresponding electronic dispersion. To the PI's knowledge, it is the first time to directly measure the dispersion of electronic structures of carbon nanotubes. This approach is a breakthrough in carbon nanotube research.

701910.label: Realisation of objectives
701910.value: LEED measurements have been performed for all SnO2 surfaces. Samples are cleaned by Ar+ sputtering (1 – 1.5 keV) and annealing (600ºC) cycles until sharp LEED pattern are observed. Normal incident LEED IV curves of all the reconstructions are recorded. Surface structures have been analyzed using different models. For example, for SnO2 (110) surface, it was found that the surface may be disordered, due to large R-factors and significant backgrounds in LEED pattern. A mixture of different models (stoichiometric surface, in-plane O mixing, bridging oxygen missing, both in-plane and bridging oxygen missing) was used to lower R-factors, and the possible models (with missing atoms not inside one 1x1 cell in all cases) are: in-plane O missing, Rp=0.380; both bridge O and in-plane O missing, Rp=0.392; and bridge O missing, Rp=0.399. For Cu2O, single crystals were obtained and subjected to surface cleaning with annealing up to 900 K. However, only intense background with no clear LEED patterns was observed. Alternative suppliers of Cu2O single crystals were not available. DFT calculations for SnO2 with and without different adsorbates have also been performed (for the results for water, see J. Phys. Chem. C 115, 19170 (2011)). In comparison with other wide band gap oxide materials, such as ZnO and TiO2, adsorption of O2 and/or H2O does not passivate the gap states. Due to the lack of passivation of gap states, SnO2 is a poor semiconductor and photocatalyst, but it may be of interest for sensing applications. This is in agreement with the experimental results on the possible use of SnO2 as a photocatalyst, where SnO2 nanostructures typically resulted in negligible degradation of organic dyes under UV illumination. We have synthesized different nanostructures of SnO2 and CuxO. For SnO2, comprehensive investigations of properties for different growth conditions and comparison with other wide band gap oxides (In2O3 and ITO) have been performed (Curr. Appl. Phys. 12, 697-706, 2012; Appl. Phys. A 104, 1075-1080, 2011). Surface modifications of SnO2 with different organic molecules have been performed, and two probe AFM measurements have been performed. For CuxO, nanostructured films with different composition were prepared by hydrothermal growth and electrodeposition (Mater. Chem. Phys. 135 (2012) 694-698). Hydrothermal CuO exhibited superior performance for photocatalysis (Mater. Chem. Phys. 135 (2012) 694-698) and catalytic oxidation of CO (in preparation). Excellent LIB performance was obtained for composite anode materials based on SnOx and CuxO (submitted).

701910.label: Major findings and research outcome
701910.value: Surface structures of SnO2 and Cu2O have been investigated experimentally and/or theoretically. It was found that SnO2 behaves very differently compared to other wide band gap oxides, such as ZnO and TiO2. On SnO2 (110) surface, water absorbs dissociatively. The general rule governing water dissociation on metal oxide surfaces was discovered by comparing SnO2 to other metal oxides. Briefly, if the surface O 2p level of an adsorbate-free surface is located high above the valence band, the water will adsorb dissociatively. In addition, the water adsorption does not passivate the defect states in the gap. Consequently, SnO2 is not expected to be a good semiconductor and photocatalyst, which was verified experimentally for dye degradation under UV illumination. The possibility of passivation of surface states with more complex organic molecules was investigated experimentally. It was found that surface modifications with several organic molecules (1,8-octanedithiol, 3-methacryloyloxypropyltrimethoxy silane) significantly increase the conductivity of SnO2 nanowires, indicating passivation of surface states. In addition, different fabrication methods were used to prepare SnO2 and CuxO in different morphologies, and their possible practical applications and the relationship between the material properties and application performance were investigated. For CuxO, it was found that hydrothermally grown CuO exhibits superior photocatalytic performance, as well as catalytic performance for CO oxidation, compared to other nanostructured forms of copper oxides (commercial CuO nanoparticles, electrodeposited CuxO, and/or hydrothermally synthesized Cu2O). For SnO2, applications in dye-sensitized solar cells and lithium ion batteries were explored. For solar cells, photovoltaic performance was strongly dependent on SnO2 nanoparticle properties, and surface coating of SnO2 by TiO2 was essential for dye adsorption and good photovoltaic performance. In addition to the optimization of SnO2 layer and surface coating by TiO2, performance could be further improved by doping SnO2 as well as by the use of plasmonic nanostructures. For battery applications, the best performance was obtained by CuxO/SnOx/carbon nanotube composite materials. High specific capacity and excellent cycling performance can be attributed to the small size of nanoparticles formed and the presence of amorphous SnO2, which appears to perform better in LIB applications compared to crystalline SnO2 possibly due to larger ability of disordered structures to buffer the volume changes upon lithium insertion/extraction.

701910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701910.value: Some of the prepared CuxO and SnO2 nanostructures have great potential for practical applications. For example, hydrothermally synthesized CuO exhibited superior photocatalytic properties for dye degradation as well as CO oxidation compared to CuxO prepared by other methods/having different morphologies and/or composition. These oxides are also of interest for other practical applications. A composite consisting of SnOx, CuxO and carbon nanotubes exhibited excellent performance as an anode for lithium ion batteries, with specific capacity as high as 806 mA h/g at 70th cycle. This electrode also exhibited excellent rate cycle performance, with specific capacity as high as 794 mA h/g was after 120 cycles (at 0.1 A/g, with charge discharge rates during cycling ranging from 0.05 A/g to 1 A/g). Thus, the material is very promising for LIB applications and further work in identifying the properties of the material responsible for superior performance. For example, the role of CuxO phase is not fully clear since in electrochemical data only contributions from Sn and not Cu can be clearly identified. Yet, the presence of CuxO is essential to achieve excellent LIB performance. Future work can include further study of the material properties and development of LIB anodes with improved performance.

701910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
701910.value: The project investigated surface structures of two oxide materials, tin oxide and copper oxide. From the comparison of surface structure of a low energy surface of tin oxide and other wide band gap oxides, a general rule for adsorption of water on metal oxide surfaces was elucidated. In addition, the effect of surface properties on the material properties and performance in practical applications was investigated. In particular, different methods of passivating surface gap states were investigated theoretically and experimentally. Experimental work included synthesis of nanostructured tin oxide and copper oxide with different morphologies and in the case of copper oxide different composition. These nanostructures were evaluated for various practical applications. Several practical applications in which a certain form of SnO2 and/or CuxO exhibited excellent performance were identified, including photocatalysis (hydrothermally grown CuO; possible application in pollutant degradation), catalysis (hydrothermally grown CuO, application in CO oxidation, of interest for catalytic converters for vehicles), and energy storage (CuxO/SnOx@carbon nanotube composite material; application as a lithium ion battery anode). Thus, these materials are promising for a variety of applications concerning energy and environment.

702110.label: Project Objectives
702110.value: To carry out measurements on the positron-induced secondary electron yields in forward (transmission) geometry through C-foils of varying thickness. For the ultimate success of the secondary electron beam based PALS technique it is very important to know the secondary electron yield, the positron transmission coefficient and the energy lost to the positron beam on passage through the C-foil. The objective here is to make a systematic study of these values as a function of C-foil thickness and to publish the results. These measurements while being essential for the success of this project are of great value in their own right since they may be used by theoreticians interested in testing models of electron energy deposition and dispersion in carbon. To construct the prototype of a proposed secondary electron positron beam based PALS system. It is planned to implement a novel needle structure that will insert strong electrostatic radial fields for sweeping secondary electrons away from the beam axis and onto a MCP (Multi-channel plate) detector situated behind the sample that is under investigation. Once the system has been manufactured and tested with its expected high performance the design details and results would be published.

702110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702110.value: The positron beam at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), that uses variable energy monoenergetic positrons, has been used for some time to carry out defect depth profiling studies on surface, interfaces and thin films. These studies have all used the conventional technique employed for obtaining information about the defects, namely that of measuring the Doppler broadened spectral line shape of the gamma photons resulting from the annihilation between the implanted thermalised positron and an electron at a defect site in the sample. For this project, it is proposed to add to the versatility and usefulness of the HKU positron beam by developing the Positron Annihilation Lifetime Spectroscopy (PALS) technique which measures the lifetimes of positrons implanted into the sample. The lifetime data is superior to the conventional observation of the line shape as the former gives more detailed and specific information about the concentration and size of any defects that can be seen by the positron, e.g. vacancies and vacancy related defects. PALS, however, is a notoriously difficult technique to implement on a low energy positron beam as there is no natural “start signal” to indicate the entry of the positron into the sample. Based on a recent discovery, however, made using the HKU positron beam the proposed project will involve the setting up of a new and easier to implement positron beam based PALS system. In this system the low energy positron is allowed to pass through a thin carbon foil thereby creating a number of secondary electrons. The secondary electron, after its detection, is used to start a fast electronic clock which is stopped by the detection of the annihilation gamma photon arising from the positron annihilation with an electron in the sample. In this way, the positron lifetime can be measured as a function of the monoenergetic positron energy, hence the depth of the sample. The successful outcome of this project will greatly increase the versatility, specificity and usefulness of the HKU positron beam and the long term impact will be to provide a versatile and valuable positron research tool for studying defects (especially those in a thin film and the surface layer) in optoelectronic and other materials.

702110.label: Realisation of objectives
702110.value: The two main objectives cited have largely been realised. The study of carbon foil in objective 1 was very successfully executed. For objective 2, the proposed lifetime positron beam was implemented with a high degree of success. The characteristics, efficiency and performance of the new beam were studied and published/reported in a Ph.D. thesis.

702110.label: Major findings and research outcome
702110.value: The very first task was to bring the positron beam to standard by improving the focusing to better than 1 mm diameter. This meant having to make a number of improvements such as replacing a semi-faulty magnetic guidance coil and upgrading the MCP. Before embarking on the carbon foil experiments, we had to make sure that the beam was indeed finely focused with a usable intensity. To this end, we tested the beam by characterising a number of materials such as titanium oxide and zinc oxide. The results were promising [1, 2]. We then proceeded to investigate the properties of secondary electron emission from thin carbon foils. Much time was spent on modifying the hardware of the positron beam not least the mounting of the very fragile and thin carbon films. Upon mastering these techniques, we studied the emission characteristics of secondary electrons induced by positrons going through the C film. Using very thin carbon foils, we measured the yield and other emission properties of the secondary electrons as a function of C coil thickness. The results indicate that the yield was usable and the impact on the positrons upon transmission through the C film was negligible [3]. We further investigated the stopping power and transmission coefficient of positrons by the C film as a function of foil thickness [4]. With these results, it has been possible to conclude that the secondary electron yield is large enough for our upcoming timing experiment and the positrons emerging from the C foil are only very slightly slowed by the C foil. Using the carbon foil results obtained, we implemented the proposed secondary electron positron beam based PALS system. To achieve this, a novel needle structure was employed to insert strong electrostatic radial fields for sweeping secondary electrons away from the beam axis and onto a MCP (Multi-channel plate) detector situated behind the sample under investigation. The system was manufactured and tested for performance. The design details and results were published in [5] and reported in the Ph.D. thesis cited in section 10.

702110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702110.value: Clearly, with the very limited time and resources, the characterisation results of the new lifetime positron beam obtained to-date lack a good signal-to-noise ratio. This also means that the turn-around sample time is much too long for the long spectrum collection time required. To further improve the efficiency and performance of the lifetime beam, a much larger positron source and a better pmt detection system are needed.

702110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702110.value: Prior to this project, the conventional positron beam at The University of Hong Kong using variable energy monoenergetic positrons, was used for materials science research for many years. This equipment had its inherent inadequacies in terms of limitation in both sensitivity and accuracy. This project has succeeded in improving the technique and hardware so as to enhance the sensitivity and accuracy of the equipment. In the improved system the low energy positron is allowed to pass through a thin carbon foil thereby creating a number of secondary electrons. The secondary electrons are used to start a fast electronic clock which is stopped by the detection of the annihilation gamma photon arising from the positron annihilation with an electron in the sample. In this way, the positron lifetime can be measured as a function of the monoenergetic positron energy, hence the depth of the sample. The successful outcome of this project has greatly increased the versatility, specificity and usefulness of the HKU positron beam and the long term impact will be to provide a versatile and valuable positron research tool for studying defects especially those in a thin film and the surface layer in optoelectronic and other materials.

702210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702210.value: Recent proteome research leads to a rapid discovery of protein drugs, biomarkers, tumor markers and various functional proteins. Their clinical analysis requires biosensor for monitoring. Antibodies used in immunosensor are expensive and not available for new proteins discovered. The recent advance of aptamer technology to select specific DNA/RNA sequences with strong binding to target proteins from libraries of 1015 DNA sequences provides a promising method for preparing biosensors, as selected aptamers are stable and can be sequenced and made to sufficient quantities by DNA synthesizers. Although the technology is well recognized, few highly selective aptamers with sufficient sensitivity have been developed. Two directions are proposed to tackle the problem. The first is developing procedures based on microfluidic chip-capillary electrophoresis (microchip CE) device to increase probability for selecting aptamers with strong binding to target proteins. The current method based on SELEX (Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment) to select aptamers gives rise to high dilution factor and undesirable carry-over during collection in each cycle, reducing probability to detect low-abundant, high protein-binding aptamers. The microchip-CE device enables on-chip fraction collection in nL size channels. Coupled with computer-controlled UV detector-aided switching and various sample stacking methods, the dilution factor are expected to be greatly reduced to increase the probability for collecting low-abundant, high target-binding aptamers. The second direction aims to enhance sensitivity of aptamer/PQC biosensor by optimizing sample flow and detection volume, improving coating stability and DNA hybridization efficiency using nano-Ag/TiO2. These methods have been developed in previous RGC projects to enable DNA/PQC biosensor to detect 8 E.coli in drinking water. As aptamers are DNA molecules, same enhancement are expected to enable direct and label free detection of target proteins. Both PQC and microchip CE have been developed by Dr Fung, and aptamers for clinical diagnosis and therapeutics developed by Dr Tanner who will supply purified viral and malarial antigen HRP II proteins for the proposed project. Professor S. Yao is active in aptamer electrochemical sensors. With a combined effort, it will form a critical mass to develop label free aptamer/PQC biosensor for diagnosis of highly infective diseases and clinically significant protein biomarkers. In addition to publishable in high impact journal, the methodology developed provides a general method for preparing other biosensors for clinically significant proteins. The products of the research certainly have huge marketable value for industrial application with the assistance of the Innovation and Technology Fund. 近期迅速發展的蛋白質組學研究發現了眾多的蛋白藥物、生物標誌物、腫瘤標誌物以及各種功能性蛋白質。它們都需要使用生物傳感器進行臨床監測。現時免疫傳感器使用的抗體，不但昂貴，並且對眾多新發現的蛋白質缺少相對可用的抗體。利用核酸適體技術可以從1015 DNA序列庫中篩選出對目標蛋白質具強鍵和力及特異性功能的DNA/RNA序列，從而提供一種制備生物傳感器的有效塗層。選擇出來的核酸適配體很穩定，並且其DNA序列可被準確地測定出來，以便使用DNA 合成器大量制備。雖然這是一項公認可行的技術，但是很少能篩選出具高選擇性和足夠靈敏度的核酸適體。本研究計劃將從兩個方向來解決這個問題。首先是利用微流控芯片-毛細管電泳技術提高對目標蛋白具高鍵和力的核酸適體的篩選成功率。現有方法使用指數富集配體系統進化技術來篩選核酸適體的稀釋率較大，並且會在每周期中收集一些不適當的殘余，因此降低了檢出有用但不多且具高蛋白結合常數的核酸適體的機率。使用微流控芯片-電泳技術能夠在nL級大小的通道中進行芯片在線組分收集。再加上使用電腦控制紫外檢測器輔助的轉換技術和各類堆積技術，稀釋率可被大大降低，從而提高收集有用但不多且具較高蛋白結合常數的核酸適配體的機率。第二個方向是通過優化樣品的流通量和檢測池的體積、以及使用納米銀/二氧化鈦提高塗層的穩定性和增加DNA雜交效率的方法來提昇核酸適體/壓電生物傳感器的靈敏度。這方法在之前的研究資助局資助項目中已經被開發並且能夠用來檢測飲用水中小至8個大腸桿菌。因為核酸適體是DNA分子，所以能夠利用同類技術提昇靈敏度, 以能直接進行無標記目標蛋白質的檢測。馮博士的研究組已經開發了壓電石英晶體和微流控芯片電泳技術；Dr Tanner研究組開發了用於臨床診斷和治療的核酸適體，並且將為本研究項目提供純化的病毒及瘧疾抗原HRP II 蛋白；姚守拙教授在核酸適配體的電化學傳感器方面有突出的成就。三方的合作將有效地開發出無標記核酸適體/壓電石英晶體生物傳感器，以檢測高度傳染性疾病和具臨床重要意義的蛋白質生物標誌物。除了可在高影響因子的雜誌上發表文章外，研究成果將提供一項通用方法以制備其它具臨床重大意義的蛋白質生物傳感器。成果具巨大市場潛力，可向創新科技基金申請資助，推廣研究成果的工業應用價值。

702210.label: Realisation of objectives
702210.value: The objective of the research is by pooling the two lines of research together and in collaboration with biochemistry research group to develop a CE-based method for selection of aptamers from a library for binding with targeted proteins of biomedical significance. A suitable design microfluidic chip-Capillary electrophoresis (MC-CE) device can minimize dilution to enhance detection sensitivity. Thus, the low abundant nucleic acids from the library with high affinity for target proteins can be selected by a specially designed microfluidic chip-capillary electrophoresis device upon enrichment and mixing with target proteins after each selection cycle. The design, assembly and testing of the required device as described in objectives 1 to 2 have been performed and the assessment for their performance as specified in objectives 3 to 4 has been made (J1-2, C2, C4-5, C7-8 and C11). To assess the performance of the system developed for selecting low-abundant, high protein-binding aptamers from DNA libraries using Non-SELEX process (objectives 3 and 6), satisfactory performance have been shown using aptamer coatings selected for detecting two malaria proteins, PfLDH and PfHRP-2, with detection at ng/mL to meet the requirement for their diagnosis. Using magnetic beads for sample cleanup and analyte enrichment, SARS SCoV helicase had been shown to be detected at pg/mL level (J6, J8, C18-20) in a 12 min. assay with a detection limit of 47 picogram µL-1. Under continuous flow, the PQC/DNA-aptamer biosensor was shown to deliver a satisfactory repeatability under FIA operation with 2.7% RSD (n=3) for ScoV spiked to human sera. A new approach for selecting aptamer according to their PQC operation has been developed to provide a simple selection process as compared to the SELEX process. The aptamer selected has shown to deliver sufficient sensitivity to detect microgram quantities of albumin in urine (C20). To enhance the detection sensitivity as described in objective 6 and 7, the use of TiO2 as a catalytic coating does not deliver a better performance as compared to procedures based on sample cleanup and analyte enrichment prior to PQC detection, in particular for dirty samples (urine) and for detecting trace protein biomarkers in high protein samples such as human serum (J3, J5-6, J8, C18 , C21). Attempt has been made by incorporation of high sensitivity microelectrode detector for MC-CE device with promising results shown in the detection of proteins and amino acids in body fluids (C13-14, C21-22).
