702210.label: Major findings and research outcome
702210.value: For developing Piezoelectric Quartz Crystal Biosensor for diagnostic protein biomarkers by aptamers selected via Non-SELEX process using Microfluidic Chip-Capillary Electrophoresis (MC-CE) device, two major techniques are developed with the first on MC-CE devices to assist the selection of aptamers and the second for sensing proteins biomarkers using selected aptamer as sensor coating. The design, assembly and testing of the required device have been made and their technical assessment are successfully completed (J1-2, C2, C4-5, C7-8 and C11). The use of aptamer coatings selected against SARS SCoV helicase has shown satisfactory analytical performance at pg/mL detection level after coupling with magnetic bead for sample cleanup and analyte enrichment (J6, C3, C9-10, C18 and C20). Aptamers against two malaria proteins, PfLDH and PfHRP-2, have been developed with detection at ng/mL to meet the requirement for their diagnosis (J8, .C18). To enhance the detection sensitivity, TiO2 was used as a catalytic coating. However, its performance is not better than procedures based on sample cleanup and analyte enrichment prior to PQC detection, in particular for dirty samples (urine) and for detecting trace protein biomarkers in high protein samples such as human serum (J3, J5-6, J8, C18 , C21). The proteins isolated by MC-CE device have been characterized by the Gas-phase Electrophoretic Mobility Molecular Analyzer (GEMMA) (C5, C8, C12, C15, C17). The device has incorporated transient isotachophoresis (t-ITP) for onchip enrichment of protein prior to separation and quantitation by UV detection (J1, J3, J5, C4, C7 and C11). To enhance the application scope, Flow Injection Analysis (FIA) was incorporated as an automatic high throughput platform for malaria and SARS virus showing improvement in wider working range, higher repeatability in quantitative measurement and rapid to deliver results onsite (J6, J8 and C19-20). A new approach for selecting aptamer according to their PQC operation has been developed to provide a simple selection process as compared to the SELEX process. The aptamer selected has shown to deliver sufficient sensitivity to detect microgram quantities of albumin in urine (C20). The incorporation of high sensitivity microelectrode detector for MC-CE device has found to enhance the detection of proteins and amino acids in body fluids (C13-14, C21-22). Due to the recent rise in interest in the performance and operation of the MC-CE devices, we have invited to write a review on the MC-CE devices developed for determination of proteins and metabolites in urine (J7).

702210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702210.value: For further development, real clinical samples should be used to establish the applicability of devices developed for urine and serum samples in particular for false positive and false negative errors for detecting SARS SCoV helicase and two malaria protein biomarkers, PfLDH and PfHRP-2. Most existing procedures for detecting protein biomarkers for microbial pathogens are focused on qualitative measurement. The procedures we have developed delivers quantitative results to assist medical doctors to follow the effectiveness of new toxic drugs used against new viral pathogens such as SARS to avoid overdose using the toxic viral drugs for treatment and intervention which causes subsequent serious long term health problems for recovered patients as shown in the SARS case. Other developments include the incorporation of portable high sensitivity detector such as the recently developed multi-walled nanocarbon tubes microelectrode detector which offers high potential for clinical application. Another area to be developed is automation of instrumentation to enable operation by clinical staff onsite during the outbreak of infective diseases. The proposed course of action includes the following steps: 1) enhancing detection sensitivity for biosensors, 2) automation of devices for targeted protein biomarkers, and 3) clinical trial using devices developed.

702210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702210.value: In the present research, Piezoelectric Quartz Crystal Biosensors (also known as Quartz Crystal Microbalance) have been developed for determining diagnostic protein biomarkers using DNA selective coating (aptamers) selected from DNA library via Non-SELEX process. The biosensor has been incorporated as a detector in a Flow Injection Analysis (FIA) system as an automatic high throughput platform for the detection of SARS and malaria protein biomarkers. Satisfactory performance have been shown using aptamer coatings selected for detecting two malaria proteins, PfLDH and PfHRP-2, with detection at ng/mL to meet the requirement for their diagnosis. Using magnetic beads for sample cleanup and analyte enrichment, SARS SCoV helicase had been shown to be detected at pg/mL level. The FIA system developed with DNA/Aptamer PQC biosenor as detector offers significant technological advancement to meet the demand for bedside monitoring of target pathogens during the outbreak of infective diseases. It can be used to monitor the administration of newly available toxic drugs against new viral pathogens to avoid the overdose of new drugs used in treatment which causes subsequent serious long term health problems for recovered patients as shown in the SARS case.

702210.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
702210.value: The project starts with collaboration in research between the following three research groups, the research group from Dr Y.S. Fung at the Department of Chemistry for contribution in microchip-capillary electrophoresis devices, Dr J.A. Tanner from Department of Biochemistry, Faculty of Medicine, Hong Kong University for input on biochemistry, and Professor Yao Shouzhuo, Chemical Research Institute Institute, Department of Chemistry, Hunan University for PQC sensor instrumentation. During the course of development for finding sensitive and selective methods for detecting trace proteins in biomedical samples, we have also collaborated with Professor W.S.B. Yeung, Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Faculty of Medicine, Hong Kong University for detecting trace levels of protein in urine. The collaboration leads to the publication of the technique developed on isotachophoresis (ITP) and microfluidic chip-capillary electrophoresis device fabricated for on-chip mixing and fraction collection. The portable MC-CE devices developed for proteins and metabolites in urine have caught attention in metalobomic areas, as the use of 2D t-ITP/CZE for on-chip sample cleanup prior to protein assay greatly improves the detection sensitivity for clinical urinary proteins (J1). It requires less than 10 min for a complete protein assay as compared to 7 hours using existing clinical method based on radio-immunoassay method. It has aroused a high interest that Dr Petr Gebauer, the editor of the regular biannual review entitled "Recent progress in analytical capillary ITP" to be published in the January 2013 as a special issue of ELECTROPHORESIS entitled "CE and CEC Reviews: Methodology and Theory". has decided to use our electropherogram as illustration in the special issue. Due to the recent rise in interest in the performance and operation of the MC-CE devices, we have invited to write a review on the MC-CE devices developed for determination of proteins and metabolites in urine (J7).

702910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702910.value: We plan to carry out computational enzymology study on the catalytic and regulative mechanisms of human class of differentiation 38 (CD38), a multi-function cyclic-ADP ribose hydrolase playing important roles in the cellular calcium messaging processes. As CD38 is an antigen expressed in many different tissues and was found to be broadly associated with physiological processes such as immune responses, metabolic disturbances, and behavioral modifications, understanding the mechanism and regulation of CD38 possess important clinic significance. As a multi-function and promiscuous enzyme, CD38 catalyzes the metabolism (synthesis and hydrolysis) of two distinct Ca2+ messengers, cyclic ADP-ribose (cADPR) and nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NAADP). The catalytic mechanism(s) of CD38 is a highly debate issue due to the complexity of the reactions. It was even proposed that the enzyme might switch between multiple catalytic pathways upon binding of different substrates and/or under different physiological conditions. The key question in the catalysis of CD38 is whether the intermediate state of the substrate is non-covalently bound to enzyme. Previous X-ray crystallographic studies have captured both covalently and non-covalently bound enzyme/ligand complexes, thus did not provide a decisive conclusion. In attempting to resolve this issue, computational enzymology study will be carried out to determine the structure of transition and intermediate states to provide the most direct evidence to the mechanism. Other important issues will also be addressed, including: (1) what is the catalytic role of Glu226; (2) what are the interactions to stabilize the oxocarbenium ion formed in the transition/intermediate state; (3) how does the ribose moiety move during the reaction process; (4) what are the functional significance of those multiple conformational states of the ribose moiety reported in X-ray crystallographic study, and (5) If the domain motions are important to the catalysis as the active site sits in the hinge between two domains. Our research will not only address fundamental questions in enzyme catalysis, but also provide practical and constructive, detailed information to the biological functioning process of CD38. 我们计划对CD38的催化和调节机制进行计算酶学的研究。CD38是一个在细胞钙质信息流程中发挥重要作用的多功能 cyclic-ADP ribose 水解酶。由于CD38是在许多不同的组织中表达的抗原，被发现与广泛的生理过程，如免疫反应，代谢紊乱，行为修改有关联，理解CD38的催化和调控机制具有重要的临床意义。 作为一个多功能和多底物酶，CD38催化两种截然不同的钙代谢的使者，环腺苷二磷酸核糖（cADPR）和烟酸腺嘌呤二核苷酸磷酸（NAADP）的合成和水解反应。CD38的催化机理是一个高度争论的问题。由于该反应的复杂性，有人甚至提出，这种酶在不同底物和/或不同的生理条件下可切换多种催化途径。 CD38的催化关键问题是底物的中间状态是否共价键结合到酶。以前的X射线晶体学研究 已扑获两个共价和非共价键结合酶/配体，因此没有提供决定性的结论。计算酶学研究将会通过确定过渡态和中间态结构以提供最直接的证据的机制来试图解决这个问题。其他重要问题也将得到解决，包括：（1）Glu226的催化作用;（2）什么作用稳定oxocarbenium离子在过渡/中间状态的形成;（3）核糖基在反应过程总如何移动;（4）X射线晶体学研究中发现的核糖的多构象状态的功能意义；（5）因为催化活性部位位于两个结构域之间，结构域运动对反应是否起重要贡献。 我们的研究将不仅解决酶催化反应的基本问题，而且还对CD38的生物学功能的过程提供实用的和建设性的，详细的资料。

702910.value: (1) Covalent catalytic mechanism was favored in our simulations. (2) Glu226 forms covalent connection to the substrate. (3) trans- and cis-ribose form of the substrates seem both to be capable to be catalyzed by CD38, though the binding affinity and catalytic barriers are different. 702910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702910.value: CD38 is an important enzyme in cell signalling processes. Understanding the catalytic mechanism holds the crucial key for designing new ligands to regulate the functions of CD38 and fight against many cancers. One of a long-standing questions in experimental study of CD38 is whether it forms a covalent intermediate state with the substrate, and if so, what interactions are important for the formation of covalent bonds. This question was never determined experimentally due the complexity of the enzyme and the reaction it catalyzes. For this, theoretical and computational studies become an important help to experimentalists. Through our mechanistic simulations, we provided evidence to support the covalent mechanism of the enzyme, and determined important interactions contributing to the formation of this covalent intermediate states. The results will make direct contribution to further experimental and medicinal researches. Through this research progress, we also developed new theoretical methods to address challenging issues in the simulation of complex enzymes like CD38.

703010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703010.value: Relative to aquifers, little research has been directed at low permeability units, known as aquitards, even though in many countries aquitards typically overly aquifers used for drinking water. Excluding shale aquitards, many important aquitards globally are formed of clayey Quaternary deposits. Although the international literature presents comprehensive studies of groundwater flow and hydrochemistry of several aquitards, little pertains to Quaternary aquitards of marine origin. This study is focused on the extensive clayey aquitard, generally 10-30m thick, in the Pearl River Delta (PRD). This aquitard overlies a regional sand aquifer (basal aquifer). The geology of this aquitard has previously been studied in detail indicating that it has two distinct units of marine origin, an upper one of Holocene age and a lower one of Pleistocene age with a thin discontinuous sand aquifer in between. The basal aquifer has spatially variable natural water quality and there has been only minimal aquifer exploitation but this is changing due to pollution of surface water and greater water demand. We hypothesis that the hydraulic, geochemical and solute transport characteristics of the two aquitard units have important influences on the flow and hydrochemistry in the basal aquifer and also that the aquitard has preserved evidence of past geologic process due to extremely slow groundwater flow in some zones. We propose to apply systematically a large number of different but complementary investigative methods to examine the similarities and differences between the two aquitard units and their hydrologic and hydrochemical interactions with the two aquifers. The work will be conducted by an experienced interdisciplinary team with expertise in hydrogeology, hydrogeochemistry, Quaternary geology and numerical modeling using multiple techniques including coring and core hydrochemical analyses, multi-level piezometers, environmental isotope tracers, X-radiography, high-resolution groundwater hydraulic, chemical and temperature profiling, and numerical flow and transport modeling. In addition to providing valuable insights concerning the groundwater resources of the PRD, the findings of this project will have broad scientific importance because this comprehensive combination of investigative techniques has not been used previously in aquitard research and therefore determining the merits of this approach has relevance to many other aquitard investigations, particularly complex marine aquitards in coastal areas. Aquitard units with some similar characteristics to those in the PRD likely also occur in the Yangtze River and Yellow River deltas and elsewhere in Asia. 盡管在許多國家和地區弱透水層（低滲透性的地質單元）往往覆蓋在用于飲用水的含水層之上，然而針對弱透水層的研究卻非常不足，遠不及關于含水層的研究。除去頁岩弱透水層，許多全球性的重要的弱透水層均由富含黏土的第四紀沈積物形成。盡管國際文獻記載了一些弱透水層的地下水流動和水文化學的綜合性研究，卻很難適用于海相起源的第四紀弱透水層。本項目研究對象是珠江三角洲的廣泛含黏土的弱透水層，其厚度通常可達10-30米。該弱透水層覆蓋在一個區域性的砂土含水層（基底含水層）之上。前人對此弱透水層的地質條件進行了詳細的研究，指出此弱透水層有兩層不同的海相生成單元。上層爲全新統，下層爲更新統，中間則夾有一層較薄的非連續的砂土含水層。基底含水層的天然水質在空間上分布有差異。雖然目前只存在極小程度的含水層開采，但隨著地表水的污染以及不斷擴大的用水需求，開采程度也隨之變化。我們假設，這兩個弱透水層水力學、地球化學和溶質運移特征對基底含水層的水流和水文化學有著重要的影響，這些弱透水層由于極低的區域地下水流動速度而保留著過去地質過程的信息。本研究將系統性地采取大量不同的互補的調查方法，以研究這兩個不同的弱透水層單元的相似與不同，及其與兩個含水層的水力和水文化學上的相互作用。這項工作將會由一支經驗豐富的團隊完成。這個團隊由不同學科領域的專家組成，專注于水文地質、水文地球化學、第四紀地質和數值模擬等領域，采用包括鑽取土芯和土芯水化學分析、多層觀測孔監測，環境同位素示蹤，X射線掃描，高分辨率地下水動力學、化學和溫度描述，以及流動和溶質運移的數值模擬等多種方法進行研究。除提供關于珠江三角洲地下水資源的有價值的見解之外，本項目的發現和結果將會具有廣泛的科學重要性，這些研究技術方法在很多其他弱透水層的調查都具有應用價值，尤其是海岸（帶）的複雜海相弱透水層。在長江三角洲，黃河三角洲以及亞洲的其他地區，同樣存在著與珠江三角洲特征相似的弱透水層單元。

703010.label: Major findings and research outcome
703010.value: This study demonstrated that porewater in the aquitard and groundwater in the basal aquifer in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) are mainly composed of paleo-seawater and infiltrated precipitation. The progressively decreasing chloride concentrations in the aquitard towards the ground indicated that the infiltration of local precipitation is gradually driving paleo-seawater down through the aquitard. The spatial distribution of the aquitard thickness is a controlling factor for the high salinity paleo-seawater in the aquifer. Geochemical and isotopic analyses on aquitard sediments and groundwater revealed that the overlying aquitard can significantly control groundwater chemistry in the basal aquifer. This study also found that arsenic concentrations in groundwater in the confined Quaternary basal aquifer ranged from 3.3 to 161.4 μg/L in the study area. Arsenic enriched groundwater was characterized by devoid DO, negative Eh values, slightly alkaline environment, abnormally high ammonium and DOC concentrations, but low nitrate and nitrite concentrations. This study indicated that terrestrial detrital deposits are one of the major sources for solid arsenic of the delta sediments, while correlations between solid arsenic and Ba probably suggested the marine influence on solid arsenic enrichment in the sediments. Reductive dissolution of iron oxyhydroxide was found to be one of the major processes that mobilized solid arsenic. The aquatic arsenic concentrations were significantly controlled by co-precipitation of arsenic with authigenic pyrite occurred in the sediments, causing arsenic concentrations in groundwater closer to the sea to be less elevated than those located further away from the coast. As K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES) was demonstrated to be a very efficient tool to quantitatively determine the oxidation state of arsenic in bulk sediments. Most of As of a reduced form (nominally As(-1)) was likely to be incorporated in arsenical pyrite and this phase generally retained As in a state of low mobility, toxicity and bioavailability. In order to simulate the slug-test data from piezometers installed for this study, equivalent well blocks (EWB) are proposed in numerical modeling of slug test data with MODFLOW. Multi-well slug tests in partially penetrating wells with skin zones can be simulated. Accuracy of the numerical method is demonstrated by benchmarking with analytical solutions. Using this method, the hydraulic conductivity of the aquitards was estimated to be of the order of 10-8 to 10-10 m/s. We also developed a one-dimensional numerical models to integrate the stratigraphy, historical evolution of the geological system during the Holocene, and the processes related to the generation and migration of ammonium.

703010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703010.value: Containing abundant sedimentary organic matter has been identified to be one of the significant geochemical characteristics of the clay-rich aquitad of the PRD. Mineralization of sedimentary organic matter not only generates ammonium, but also releases greenhouse gas, such as CO2 and CH4. For our further research, we are going to study the contribution of sedimentary organic matter mineralization to the atmospheric greenhouse gas. Besides arsenic, geochemical behaviors of other hazard trace elements (eg. Hg) in the PRD aquifer-aquitard system will also be studied.

703010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703010.value: Confined or semi-confined coastal Quaternary aquifers are important sources of groundwater resources, and are also important links between terrestrial and marine biogeochemical cycles. They are often under the protection of low-permeability aquitards and are subject to lower contamination risks of anthropogenic pollutants compared to shallow unconfined aquifers. Our studies demonstrated that clay-rich aquitards can be geochemically active, and are capable of generating and preserving large amounts of chemicals. Geochemical and isotopic analyses in the PRD aquitard sediments revealed that the aquitard is a strong reducing environment, and can significantly control groundwater chemistry in the basal aquifer. Elevated concentrations of arsenic up to 161 µg/L were identified in groundwater samples from the confined basal aquifer. Enriched arsenic (> 10 µg/L) in groundwater has been identified to be serious environmental problems in many parts of the world. Reductive dissolution of iron oxyhydroxide has been identified to be one of the important geochemical processes that mobilized solid arsenic. Mobility, toxicity and bioavailability of arsenic are closely related to its oxidation states. As K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy was demonstrated to be efficient in determining arsenic oxidation states of the bulk sediments. These states were found to be influenced strongly by groundwater activities.

703110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703110.value: 行星狀星雲就是銀河系中大部分的恆星的演化最後階段。雖然行星狀星雲已於二百年前為人所知，但是解釋它們的起源和演化的理論卻只有三十年前才開始出現。從X射線、紫外線、紅外線、亞毫米、和毫米波段觀測，我們知道行星狀星雲在整個電磁波譜都非常活躍。因此行星狀星是研究雲原子和分子過程的最理想實驗室。從哈勃太空望遠鏡拍攝的照片，科學家發現了高速低電離放射區、噴流、弧、環和點對稱等結構。紅外線和毫米/亞毫米波段的光譜讓科學家在行星狀星雲中辨認出許多氣態分子、有機化合物和無機礦物質。銀河系外的行星狀星雲可同時用作測定銀河系外距離的標準燭光，探測暗物質的分布，和研究星系團過去變化的工具。由此可見，現代對行星狀星雲的理解在恆星演化、星際物質、星系結構和演化，和宇宙學方面都非常重要。 在這個項目中，我們將會透過可見光、近紅外線、中紅外線、射電影像，和毫米波段干涉觀測，繪製電離氣體、分子和塵埃在行星狀星雲中的分布。並且利用三維模擬電腦程式來解釋行星狀星雲的內部結構。我們期望通過探索行星狀星雲的形態和靜態結構，重組出它們在形態上演化的經過。

703110.label: Realisation of objectives
703110.value: All the objectives have been achieved. In the process, we have discovered a number of new phenomena (multipolar structures, extended haloes, precessing motions) and raised new questions on the physical origins of these morphological structures. We have demonstrated that multi-wavelength observations are essential for our understanding of the structure of planetary nebulae.

703110.label: Major findings and research outcome
703110.value: We have used a variety of techniques to discover and determine the morphological structure of planetary nebulae. Using the Hubble Space Telescope, we have discovered a number of new multipolar nebulae (Hsia et al. 2014). Using statistical analysis and theoretical simulations, we are able to show that multipolar nebulae are much more common than previously believed (Chong et al. 2012). From infrared imaging observations from both satellite and ground-based observations, we have discovered new morphological structures (e.g., halo in the Helix Nebula, Zhang et al. 2012). From theoretical simulation models, we have shown that a simple universal model can explain many of the observed morphological structures of proto-planetary nebulae (Knoning et al. 2011, 2013). With this model, we can separate what are optical illusions and what are real physical structures. We have also used molecular line submillimeter wave observations to observe the molecular outflows in planetary nebulae and are able to provide a better understanding between the ionized and molecular components of planetary nebulae. The PI was the invited speaker to give the opening lecture "Historical Overview of Planetary Nebulae" at the International Astronomical Union Symposium 283 "Planetary nebulae: an eye to the future" in 2011. A number of papers are also presented by four members of his group at the symposium.

703110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703110.value: Planetary nebulae continues to be a major frontier in modern astronomical research. The PI is one of the co-proposers to the International Astronomical Union to form a new commission on planetary nebulae. We anticipate that new techniques in both ground-based and space-based observations in the X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, millimeter-wave and radio observations will lead to new discoveries and better understanding of planetary nebulae.

703110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703110.value: Planetary nebulae are short-lived (about 20,000 years) phase of stellar evolution just before the death of ordinary Sun-like stars. A host of dynamical processes create beautiful morphological structures which origin are not understood. We made use of state-of-the-art observations from ground-based and space-based telescopes in the visible, infrared, and radio regions to investigate the structures of these nebulae. Through a understanding of the dynamical processes of creation of planetary nebulae, we hope to achieve a better understanding of the death process of stars.

703710.label: Project Objectives
703710.value: Develop a new bootstrap method to check for the unit root non-stationarity of the univariate AR processes. This will include constructing a new generalized bootstrap (GB)-type method, and deriving the corresponding asymptotics. Develop a robust test for unit root non-stationarity of panel AR processes based on the least absolute deviation (LAD) approach. This includes deriving the asymptotic distribution of the constructed test statistic, and constructing a generalized bootstrap (GB) approximation for it. Computer programs will be developed for the tests in Objectives 1 and 2, and applications to the real world data will be considered using economic and financial data. Clearly, the objectives only reflect part of the possible developments with the non-stationarity tests. Many other developments, such as the case with non-stationary volatility, are also possible if time permits.

703710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703710.value: The asymptotic distribution of the test statistics for checking unit root non-statioanrity has a complicated form, and the bootstrap method should be able to play an important role here. However, until recently only a few papers have seriously considered the bootstrap methodology. To fill this gap, this project proposes a powerful generalized bootstrap-typed method to approximate the complicated null distribution in checking unit root non-stationarity for autoregressive processes. On the other hand, a lot of effort has been made in the past decade to study the unit root non-stationarity of the panel data; however, it is still an open problem for the case when these panels exhibit the phenomenon of heavy tails. A non-stationarity test for panel data with cross-sectional dependence estimated by the least absolute deviation approach is also developed. Due to the even more complicated null distribution, the GB-type method offers a feasible and easily implemented solution. 用來檢驗單位根非平穩性的統計量一般來說都會有一個非常複雜的漸近分布。Bootstrap方法正是用來處理這種情況的。但是在這個領域裏，Bootstrap方法並沒有被深入的研究。本項目正好可以填補這個空白。另外，縱向數據的非平穩性的檢驗在過去的十年間被廣泛的研究和討論。但是由于技術性原因，至今仍然沒有人討論過怎樣檢驗厚尾的縱向數據非平穩性。本項目提出了一個基于最小絕對偏差估計的方法來處理這個問題，並且正好利用Bootstrap方法來實施。

704310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704310.value: Flag varieties of reductive algebraic groups and their Schubert subvarieties play important roles in representation theory. The theory of quantum groups gives rise to a natural Poisson structure on each flag variety such that all of its Schubert subvarieties are Poisson subvarieties. We propose to study the Poisson geometry of this Poisson structure such as its equivariant Pfaffians, Poisson divisors and Poisson line bundles. Poisson geometrical aspects of Bott-Samelson resolutions of Schubert varieties will also be studied both for their own sake and as tools to study the Poisson geometry of Schubert varieties. Our project will be the first of its kind to study in great detail an algebraic Poisson structure that is directly related to Lie theory, algebraic geometry, and combinatorics, and it adds to the richness of both Poisson geometry and the theory of flag varieties. We also expect our research to lead to better understanding of connections between Poisson geometry and other areas of mathematics such that quantum groups, Frobenius splittings, and standard monomial theory. 旗族在李群中占重要地位. 我们将从泊松幾何的角度研究旗族和相关的流形. 我们要研究的泊松结构来自量子群. 它的一个重要特点是所有的舒伯特子族都是泊松子族. 我们计划研究它的特殊坐标, 线性化, 及泊松線叢等. 另外我们将研究它和 Bott-Samelson族的关系. 我們的研究直接關係到李群理論，代數幾何， 組合论等, 我們期望我們的研究將導致更好地理解 泊松幾何和这些數學領域的关系,並会推动泊松幾何的发展.

704310.label: Realisation of objectives
704310.value: While concrete objectives were proposed in the original proposal, the project took a somewhat unexpected turn in that half way through the project we realized that we could develop some general theory which would cover the original problems as special case but at the same time open up a new area in Poisson geometry related to group actions. We spent much time in developing the general theory which is being written up in two papers, causing some delay in the writing up of results towards the other objectives. A complete solution to Objective 1 was written in my Mphil student Balazs Elek's thesis 0f 2012 and objective 2 has been written up in a paper under going final revision. Partial results for the other objectives have been written up in various notes and I will continue to work on them. Important results closed related to the proposal, although not listed in the original objectives, were obtained in my PhD student Victor Mouquin's thesis (2014) and he has published a single authored paper in the International Mathematical Research Notices based on the first part of his thesis.

704310.label: Major findings and research outcome
704310.value: Objectives 1 and 2 were more or less completed half way into the project, but the methods used were somewhat ad hoc and depended on lot of computations. Later, my then PhD student Victor Mouquin and I realized that we could develop some general theory which would be applicable to much wider classes of examples and would contain the cases of flag varieties and Bott-Samelson varieties as special cases. We spent quite some time on developing the general theory which is being written up in two papers, one already posted in the archive and the other one still undergoing final revision. The first paper introduces and develops the theory of mixed product Poisson structures, and the second is on Poisson structures defined by quasitriangular r-matrices. The results of these two papers not only set up the frame work for the study of the of Poisson structures proposed in the project, they also lead up to many new research directions such as those related quantization and cluster algebras. As a result of the time spent on developing the general theory in the above mentioned two papers, the actual writing up of the applications to the case of the flag varieties and Bott-Samelson varieties, although already put down in various notes, is a bit delayed. On the other hands, two HKU thesis were written on the subjects of the projects under my supervision and with the partial support of the funding from the project, one by Balasz Elek (Sept. 2010- July 2012, Mphil), who is now a PhD student at Cornell University, and one by Victor Mouquin (Jan. 2009 - July 2013, PhD), who is currently a Postdoc at the University of Toronto. The first part of Mouquin's PhD thesis has been published (single authored) in the journal International Mathematical Research Notices in 2014. The findings of the projects have been presented by myself at the two international conferences, Poisson 2012 and Poisson 2014.

704310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704310.value: Other than direct applications to the case of flag and Bott-Samelson varieties, the theories developed in the two papers mentioned in the previous paragraph open up to many more research directions, notably in relation to quantization, the geometry of elliptic curves, and cluster algebras. Time is also needed in writing up the research results related to the other objectives in the project, which again have already been written up in various notes.

704310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704310.value: The Poisson geometry of flag and Bott-Samelson varieties constitutes an important part of Poisson geometry and Lie theory. Motivated by the study of these Poisson structures, we developed some general theories in the context of mixed product Poisson structures and solutions to Yang-Baxter equations which are applicable to a wide class of Poisson structures. These theories not only are elegant in their applications to the Poisson geometry of flag and Bott-Samelson varieties, they can also be used to study many other problems related to quantization and other areas of geometry.

704510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704510.value: Background: Calciumphosphates and related minerals, such as hydroxyapatite (HAp), are fundamental in understanding saliva chemistry, tooth decay, bone mineralization and related biological systems. However, reported solubilities cannot explain many essential phenomena. Detailed knowledge of exact crystal structures and true solubilities are lacking. The problem lies in the conventional method: addition of large excess of solids is inappropriate (phase transformations occur) and lack of detailed solution equilibria. Published calculations have been based on crudely approximate simplifications; lack of fundamental understanding at the molecular level continues. False equilibria have been used in explanations of many biologically important phenomena for decades. Key issues: An absolute solid-titration (ST) approach (i.e. using tiny amounts of solid) shows excellent reliability and reproducibility, with much greater precision than any other such data. Dissolution and precipitation, which cannot be followed by eye, are monitored by a laser-scattering system. ST is a simple although time-consuming method to obtain equilibrium: it yields thermodynamically-correct results. The true solubility isotherm for HAp has thereby been found to lie substantially lower than previously reported. Contrary to wide belief, dicalciumphosphatedihydrate (DCPD) is not the most stable phase below pH<4.2, where calcium-deficient HAp is indeed less soluble. The discrepancy is due to the unrecognized metastability of DCPD, which nucleates much more easily than HAp at low pH. Such results unambiguously indicate that the Ca-P-system is in need of systematic re-evaluation from the micro- to macro-molecular level. Aims: In this proposal, we will verify the reliability of the solubility isotherms. The solubility surface with respect to pH and Ca:P ratio will be mapped in detail, and the crystallography of the equilibrium solid characterized and refined to relate this to known features of the isothermal surface, features which at present lack explanation. The role and effect of biologically-important ions (e.g. F-, CO32-, Sr2+, Mg2+, Na+) in biological apatite solubility, and thus oral chemistry, will be ascertained. These aims will be complimented by state-of-the-art electronic structure calculations, subsequently aiding in the design of molecular spectroscopy experiments. Significance: A proper understanding of HAp chemistry is critical to understanding biological de- and subsequent re-mineralization. Refinement of the HAp crystal structure will provide reference data for many such studies, while 3-D solubility isotherm mapping will put systems in proper context. The confusion in HAp chemistry will now be resolved. 704510.label: Realisation of objectives
704510.value: 1. The solubility of HAp in H2O- and D2O-KCl system has been determined with the solid titration method (ST). Their isotherms were found to be overlapped to each other. The reliability and reproducibility of solid titration method has been confirmed as well. 2. The ST equilibrium solids (precipitates) in these two systems have been collected at two different pH points, respectively. The physiochemical properties of such precipitates obtained in H2O-KCl system have been examined with SEM, TEM, XRD and FTIR. In comparison to the titrant, precipitates were more uniform crystals with a lower crystallinity, smaller size and lower Ca/P ratio. Neutron diffraction has not been used yet because we lost the contact with one of our co-investigators who was expected to be in charge of it. We are trying to find another equipment available to be used. The characterization of the precipitates collected in D2O-KCl system is still ongoing due to the delayed delivery of D2O. 3. A 3-D solubility isotherm of hydroxyapatite has been obtained. According to the isotherm, the solubility of hydroxyapatite was found to be both pH and Ca/P ratio dependent. 4. The effect of ions, including carbonate, fluoride, phosphate, calcium and strontium on the solubility of hydroxyapatite has been examined, while that of magnesium is still ongoing due to the breakdown of the water purification system in our lab. It is expected to be finished in two months.

704510.label: Major findings and research outcome
704510.value: 1. Upon the solid titration method (ST), the solubility of HAp in H2O- and D2O-KCl system were found to be close to each other, both of which were substantially lower than that obtained with the conventional so-called 'excess solid' method. Meanwhile, the reliability and reproducibility of the solid titration method has been re-confirmed. This is very important. 2. The ST equilibrium solids (precipitates) collected in H2O system at two different pH points were irregular crystals. They were more uniform, with a lower crystallinity, smaller size and lower Ca/P ratio than the titrant used. 3. According to the 3-D solubility isotherm,the solubility of hydroxyapatite is both pH and Ca/P ratio dependent. With the decrease of pH, the solubility increased. A high Ca/P ratio(>1.67) may lead to the decrease of its solubility, while a slightly low Ca/P ratio shows the adverse effect. 4. Carbonate can drive the dissolution of hydroxyapatite and cause the increase of its solubility. 5. The effect of phosphate and strontium on the solubility of hydroxyapatite is concentration-dependent. 6. Fluoride can decrease the dissolution of hydroxyapatite, but the extent was lower than expected. 7. Also 1 mM Ca ion concentration caused the decrease of hydroxyapatite's solubility, while 1.5 mM Mg ion concentration showed no significant effect on the dissolution of hydroxyapatite.

704510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704510.value: The solubility isotherms with/without the existence of all such external ions in the background solution can improve the understanding of hydroxyapatite's dissolution behavior in vivo. It also can be used as the basis for the investigation of the dissolution behavior of biological apatite that is incorporated with various kinds of ions. Calcium apatite with a certain ion or multiple ions incorporated in the crystal lattice can be synthesized and used as the titrant, a simulation model for biological apatite. The concentration and the ratio of different ions can be varied so as to mimic the conditions in vivo. The solubility of such an ion-incorporated calcium apatite can then be determined with the solid titration method so as to investigate the dissolution behavior of biological apatite.

704510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704510.value: As the main inorganic component of human bones, teeth and some bone grafting materials, calcium apatite (which is a mineral) plays a significant role in the formation, remodeling and function of bones, in dental caries as well as in bone reconstruction. The nature of this research project is an investigation of the dissolution of calcium apatite in a condition simulated to the biological environment. The findings in this research have the potential to enhance our scientific knowledge about the biological processes mentioned above. In addition, it has a great potential to provide information for the development of bone grafting materials (biomaterials) so as to improve its clinic performance. All this may significantly affect the well-being of those patients with bone defects, osteoporosis, and dental decay (caries).

704610.label: Project Objectives
704610.value: To characterize totally geodecic subvarieties on finite-volume quotients of bounded symmetric domains in terms of algebraicity (or more generally boundary regularity) of an irreducible component of its inverse image under the uniformization map. To characterize germs of holomorphic maps between bounded symmetric domains preserving an invariant (p,p)-form. To characterize Zariski closures of germs of totally geodesic complex submanfolds on finite-volume quotients of bounded symmetric domains. To develop a differential-geometric method for the study of holomorphic curves into bounded symmetric domains and to determine their asymptotic behavior as the holomorphic curve traverses the boundary with respect to the Harish-Chandra realization.

704610.label: Realisation of objectives
704610.value: We have developed a differential-geometric method for the study of asymptotic behavior of local holomorphic curves traversing the boundary of a bounded symmetric domain in its Harish-Chandra realization. This was first done in [1] in the case where the curve exits the regular boundary with a precise estimate of the boundary behavior, showing in particular that the second fundamental form is asymptotically 0 at a general boundary point. In the general case we proved the asymptotic geodesy in [5] by a method by arguing by contradiction. Assuming that the second fundamental form is not asymptotically totally geodesic, by composing with automorphisms of the bounded symmetric domain we obtain a limiting holomorphic isometry from the Poincare disk D into the domain which behaves more or less like an Aut(D)-equivariant holomorphic isometric embedding. We then prove the impossibility of such an embedding in the case of Hermitian symmetric spaces of the noncompact type by exploiting the Poincare-Lelong equation. This was first done in the case of tube domains (of rank r) and for holomorphic curves where the tangent vectors are of rank r and for the general case where tangent vectors are of rank k we solved the problem of finding a totally geodesic submanifold of rank k and of the tube type containing the curve. In [2] we find new holomorphic isometries from the complex unit ball into an irreducible bounded symmetric domain of rank >= 2 and show that they attain the maximal dimension possible for such maps. These maps were made use of to give in [4] a new solution of the extension problem for Γ-equivariant holomorphic embeddings for irreducible lattices Γ in the automorphism group of a bounded symmetric domain of rank >=2, yielding at the same time rigidity results for the finite-volume quotient varieties. We have developed differential-geometric and complex-analytic method for the study of Zariski closures of images of algebraic subsets of irreducible bounded symmetric domains in their Harish-Chandra realizations under the uniformizing map wrt a lattice, yielding solutions to both Objectives (1) and (3). Since methods relying on arguments in mathematical logic and on representation have now been developed to solve the latter problems in the arithmetic case, in [3] we restrict ourselves to the rank-1 case where there are non-arithmetic lattices, with a method that is applicable both in the arithmetic and non-arithmetic cases.

704610.label: Major findings and research outcome
704610.value: Our research revolving around holomorphic mappings into bounded symmetric domains has demonstrated the vitality of the subject. New existence theorems of holomorphic isometries of the complex unit ball into irreducible bounded symmetric domains of rank >=2 were established in [2] which give a new geometric treatment in [3] of admissible limits of bounded holomorphic functions, implying new rigidity theorems for finite-volume quotients of such domains. In such rigidity theorems we make use of the existence of bounded holomorphic functions on universal covers, making it possible to prove fibration theorems without the usual tool of harmonic maps in Kaehler geometry for the proof of strong rigidity. The existence of holomorphic isometries as given in [2] had been an open problem for some time and the conceptual proof of their existence by means of varieties of minimal rational tangents (VMRTs) and asymptotics for standard complete Kaehler metrics on strictly pseudoconvex domains also gives new links between Kaehler geometry of subvarieties of bounded symmetric domains with the theory of VMRTs which I had developed in other GRF projects with Jun-Muk Hwang. Holomorphic isometries of the complex unit ball also appear in the study of Zariski closures of images of algebraic varieties under the uniformizing map [4]. For the study both of holomorphic isometries and Zariski closures it was deemed important to have a general theory about local holomorphic curves exiting the boundary of the Harish-Chandra realization and this was realized in our project in [1] [5]. It should be noted that while we proved asymptotic total geodesy of local holomorphic curves exiting the boundary of the Harish-Chandra realizations of bounded symmetric domains, the same fails for higher dimensions, as the examples of nonstandard holomorphic isometries of the complex unit ball constructed in [2] are in fact not asymptotically totally geodesic. This contrast illustrates a big difference in the geometry of subvarieties of one and several dimensions with respect to the Bergman metric. Our methods and results demonstrate the importance of methods of Complex Differential Geometry in problems on bounded symmetric domains and their finite-volume quotients, including especially the study of the uniformizing map on such finite-volume quotients, and establish thus an intimate link and interface between Complex Differential Geometry and Functional Transcendence Theory. Especially, our project highlights the importance of asymptotic behavior in differential-geometric terms of intersections of algebraic varieties with bounded symmetric domains in their Harish-Chandra realization.

704610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704610.value: Our research findings demonstrate the importance of transcendental methods in the study of subvarieties of bounded symmetric domains and their finite-volume quotients. Such a perspective can be expanded to the study of fibered spaces over such domains and quotient spaces such as Kuga families of principally polarized Abelian varieties. A GRF grant proposal was written up for the study of such subvarieties, entitled "Geometry on subvarieties of bounded symmetric domains and their quotient manifolds and on fibered spaces over them", which was approved, and research on the grant started in January 2015.

704610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704610.value: Bounded symmetric domains are important objects which furnish the soil upon which many different branches of Mathematics thrive, incluing such diverse subjects as Differential Geometry, Harmonic Analysis, Several Complex Variables, Algebraic Geometry and Number Theory. Our research provides new links and interfaces across such subjects in their interaction in the framework of bounded symmetric domains and their finite-volume quotients, showing the vitality of transcendental methods provided by Complex Differential Geometry, Harmonic Analysis and Several Complex Variables even for the study of algebraic and arithmetic problems. Our research provides important missing links between analytic and algebraic methods and promise to open up new perspectives in future research endeavours on the study of bounded symmetric domains, their finite-volume quotients and fibered spaces over them. Especially, it provides some in-roads into the fascinating subject of Functional Transcendence Theory for which our methods provide new possilibilites for approaching well-known problems and for formulating new arithmetico-geometric problems.

704710.label: Project Objectives

We will train at least 2-3 Mphil/PhD students within the duration of this project. We will build up a good and tight partnership with foreign researchers and institutions to facilitate our scientific and educational activities. We will build up a good educational environment by hiring a senior research assistant, who has skills of radio observations.

704710.label: Major findings and research outcome
704710.value: In this project, we explored the correlation between the properties of known circumstellar maser sources and newly released infrared archival data, and will demonstrate the distribution of each evolutionary class of evolved stars (i.e., AGB, post-AGB, PPNe and PNe) in two-color diagrams of new wavelength-bands. We tried to find new maser sources by observing important unsurveyed samples, so that we could more effectively investigate stellar evolution through the maser properties, and we conducted further follow-up investigations on key objects found in our previous maser surveys, addressing important issues related to the key objects and late-stage stellar evolution. The primary scientific result of this project was that the empirical/observational evolutionary track of evolved stars becomes identified in the two-color diagrams of new wavelength bands, and this information would offer the evolved star community guidelines for constructing theoretical evolutionary-tracks of evolved stars. Another significance was that the distribution of the maser sources on the two-color diagrams offers guidance for selecting samples for further maser surveys, so that we could effectively find new (and scientifically important) stellar maser sources.

704710.value: Based on our findings, potentially we could find more number of evolved stars, of which the evolutionary status is immediately after the AGB phase or on the transition phase between AGB and post-AGB. The potentially increased number of sample would contribute to understand how intermediate-mass stars evolve in their late-evolutionary stage. One important application of our finding would be to observe newly found post-AGB stars using high-resolution radio interferometers like ALMA and CARMA.

704710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704710.value: The stellar evolution of its late-stage is particularly important to understand the chemical evolution of the Universe, because a significant amount of materials are released from stars as a form of molecular gas and dust through the late-phase of the stellar evolution. In particular, since stars are drastically altered both chemically and dynamically in the evolutionary phase immediately after the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) phase, but the number of stars in such the evolutionary phase has been quite limited. In this project, we explored an effective methodology to find new evolved stars immediately after AGB, and found some important criteria to find such stars. Our finding will be useful to find more samples in the transient phase between AGB and post-AGB stars.

705110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705110.value: A topological insulator is a novel topological state of quantum matter which possesses metallic edge or surface states in the bulk energy gap. The edge or surface states consist of an odd number of massless Dirac cones, and result in quantum spin Hall (QSH) effect, which is analogous integer quantum Hall effect. The topological properties of this kind of insulator are unchanged by smooth modifications to their geometry and are robust against non-magnetic impurities and interactions. The prediction of non-zero conductance in QSH effect was already verified experimentally in HgTe/CdTe quantum well, and the surface states in three-dimensional topological insulators have also observed or measured in the materials such as Bi1-xSex, Bi2Se3, and Bi2Se3 by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). While the edge states and surface states are robust against the nonmagnetic impurities because of the time reversal invariance or a Z2 topological invariant, it is found that the disorder effect can even induce a topological insulator from a normal metal in a clean limit. Strong spin-orbital coupling plays crucial role in the formation of topological insulator and the edge and surface states possess a lot of novel quantum transport and magnetoelectric properties. The primary objective of this proposal is to investigate the disorder effect and quantum transport in topological insulator. It will be anticipated to explore the physical mechanism of formation of disorder induced topological insulator and quantum phase transition between the topological insulator and a conventional metal or insulator. A quantum phase diagram of topological insulator will be established in the disorder regime. Quantum transport and magnetic structure will be investigated in various forms of geometry, and novel quantum phenomena are expected to be found for the purpose of application. This project will help us understand the physical properties of topological insulator, enrich the knowledge of condensed matter physics, and explore possible applications of this novel topological state of quantum matter in the future. 拓扑绝缘体是一种新的量子状态, 它在整体能隙间拥有金属性的边缘态或表面态. 边缘态或表面态形成奇数个无能隙的狄拉克圆锥, 在二维可产生量子自旋霍尔效应. 这种绝缘体的拓扑性质在系统的几何形状连续改变下是稳定的, 并且对非磁性杂质和相互作用都是稳定的. 量子自旋霍尔效应中能隙间的非零电导的预言已在碲化汞和碲化镉量子井中得到实验地证实. 三维拓扑绝缘体的表面态也在一系列材料中用角分辨光电子谱观测到. 当边缘态或表面态因为时间反演不变性对非磁性杂质是稳定的, 我们发现杂质效应甚至能从纯净下的正常态产生一个拓扑绝缘态. 强的自旋轨道耦合在拓扑绝缘体的形成中起了决定的作用。 边缘态或表面态拥有一些新的量子输运性和磁电性质. 本项目的基本目的是研究拓扑绝缘体中的无序效应和输运性质. 它将探讨无序引发的拓扑绝缘体的物理形成机制, 和拓扑绝缘体与正常金属或绝缘体间的量子相变. 我们期待建立无序区域内的量子相图. 我们将研究各种几何下的量子输运和磁性结构. 并期待发现新的量子现象. 本项目将帮助我们了解拓扑绝缘体的物理性质, 丰富凝聚态物理知识, 并探讨这种新的量子态在将来可能的应用.

705110.label: Realisation of objectives
705110.value: The proposal aims to investigate the disorder effect of topological insulator, to explore the physical origin of the formation of disordered induced topological insulator or topological Anderson insulator. We have examine the physical origin of this phenomenon. We calculate the topological invariants and density of states of the disordered model in a supercell of a two-dimensional HgTe/CdTe quantum well. The topologically nontrivial phase is triggered by a band touching as the disorder strength increases. The TAI is protected by a mobility gap, in contrast to the band gap in conventional quantum spin Hall systems. The mobility gap in the TAI consists of a cluster of nontrivial subgaps separated by almost flat and localized bands. We also proposed to study the quantum and topological transport properties of topological insulators in disorders and various geometries. We developed theory of weak localisation and weak antilocalization of surface electrons in disordered topological insulator. We successfully obtained a magnetoconductivity formula for the surface states of a magnetically doped topological insulator. It reveals a competing effect of weak localization and weak antilocalization in quantum transport when an energy gap is opened at the Dirac point by magnetic doping. It is found that the gap could induce a crossover from weak antilocalization to weak localization, tunable by the Fermi energy or the gap. This crossover has been observed by several experimental groups. The formula has been applied to analyse experimental data, and resolved some observed puzzles. We further investigated physical properties of an Anderson impurity embedded in the bulk of a topological insulator. Different from the results of a quantum impurity on the surface of a topological insulator, we find for the band-inverted case that a Kondo resonant peak and in-gap bound states can be produced simultaneously. It is shown that the mixed-valence regime is much broader in the band-inverted case, while it shrinks to a very narrow regime in the normal case. We have realized all objectives in this project.

Localization of mobility gap in topological Anderson insulators [6]: Here we examine the physical origin of this phenomenon. We calculate the topological invariants and density of states of the disordered model in a supercell of a two-dimensional HgTe/CdTe quantum well. The topologically nontrivial phase is triggered by a band touching as the disorder strength increases. The TAI is protected by a mobility gap, in contrast to the band gap in conventional quantum spin Hall systems. The mobility gap in the TAI consists of a cluster of nontrivial subgaps separated by almost flat and localized bands. 2. Theory of weak localisation and weak antilocalization of surface electrons in topological insulator. [2][5]: We successfully obtained a magnetoconductivity formula for the surface states of a magnetically doped topological insulator. It reveals a competing effect of weak localization and weak antilocalization in quantum transport when an energy gap is opened at the Dirac point by magnetic doping. It is found that the gap could induce a crossover from weak antilocalization to weak localization, tunable by the Fermi energy or the gap. This crossover has been observed by several experimental groups. The formula has been applied to analyse experimental data, and resolved some observed puzzles. 3. Quantum impurities in topological insulators [10]: We investigate physical properties of an Anderson impurity embedded in the bulk of a topological insulator. Different from the results of a quantum impurity on the surface of a topological insulator, we find for the band-inverted case that a Kondo resonant peak and in-gap bound states can be produced simultaneously. 705110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705110.value: Disorder effect and quantum transport are two of the important topics in topological insulators. Transport properties determine possible application of topological insulators. There are still a lot of issues to be resolved, such as low temperature behaviours of conductivity, and magnetic doped magnetism. Electron-electron interaction may be another important factor to affect the transport properties in topological insulator. PI shall pay more attention along the direction.

705110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705110.value: A topological insulator is a novel material, which is insulating in the bulk but possesses metallic edge or surface electrons. The edge or surface states consist of an odd number of massless Dirac cones, locking the momentum and spin of electrons. The topological properties of this kind of insulator are unchanged by smooth modifications to their geometry and are robust against non-magnetic impurities. Strong spin-orbital coupling plays crucial role in the formation of topological insulator and the edge and surface states possess a lot of novel quantum transport and magnetoelectric properties. The primary objective of this proposal is to investigate the disorder effect and quantum transport in topological insulator. PI has clarified the physical mechanism of formation of topological Anderson insulator. A quantum phase diagram of topological insulator has been established in the disorder regime. PI further developed quantum transport theory for surface electrons in topological insulators, and predicted a crossover from weak anti-localization to weak localization of surface electrons, which has been confirmed experimentally. This project helps us understand the physical properties of topological insulator, and provides theoretical guideline to explore possible applications of the materials in the future.

705310.label: Realisation of objectives
705310.value: The project completed successfully as proposed. We extensively characterized metallodrug (Bi-antiulcer, Pt-anticancer and Ru(anticancer drugs) binding to human transferrin (hTF) at the specific iron site under a variety of techniques. We also carefully examined the effects of anion on metal binding to the proteins and prepared mixed metal transferrin adducts. Moreover we investigated the conformational changes accompanied by metal-binding. We crystallized Fe2-hTF, Fe(C)Bi(N)-hTF as well as Pt- Ru-hTF adducts and analyzed the structures of Fe2-hTF and Fe(C)Bi(N)-hTF with carbonate and malonate as anions. The coordination of ferric iron and Bi(III) was characterized. The preference of four putative binding residues were rationalized with the order of Tyr188> Tyr95> Asp63~ His429. Importantly the metal-induced protein conformational changes were observed, and for the first a partially-opened conformation was observed. The snapshots of the protein conformational changes upon metal-binding were described. All of the objectives were addressed and satisfied results were obtained as proposed. Using transferrin as a template, we developed a simple way to crystallize metal-bound transferrin, and got a variety of Ln-transferrin adducts (Yb(III) and Dy(III)), significantly improving our understanding on the biocoordination chemistry of Ln. Our work clearly demonstrated that the protein can serve as 'carrier' for metallodrug. The slightly poor resolution of Pt- and Ur-transferrin adducts were found which need further optimization due to their different binding. To address this problem, we used vanadium(III) to replace Pu- and Ru, and reasonable resolution was got from X-ray diffration at SSRF (in Shanghai).

705310.label: Major findings and research outcome
705310.value: We extensively characterized metallodrug (Bi-antiulcer, Pt-anticancer and Ru(anticancer drugs) binding to human transferrin (hTF) at the specific iron site under a variety of techniques. We also carefully examined the effects of carbonate and malonate on metal binding to the proteins and prepared mixed metal transferrin adducts (BiFe-hTF). Equally important, we investigated the conformational changes accompanied by metal-binding. The PI and Co-I successfully crystallized Fe2-hTF, Fe(C)Bi(N)-hTF as well as Pt- Ru-hTF adducts and analyzed the X-ray structures of Fe2-hTF and Fe(C)Bi(N)-hTF with carbonate and malonate as anions. The coordination of ferric iron and Bi(III) was characterized. Both Fe(III) and Bi(III) adopted an octahedron coordination geometry. The preference of four putative binding residues were rationalized with the order of Tyr188> Tyr95> Asp63~ His429. Importantly the metal-induced protein conformational changes were observed, and for the first time, a partially-opened conformation was also visualized. Our data clearly indicated that proteins are in breath in solutions (in cells). The snapshots of the dynamics motion of a subdomain of the proteins were described. Our X-ray data provide a molecular basis for understanding the mechanism of metallodrug uptake and release in hTF, as well as protein (and/or enzymes) in motion. Major part of the data was published (in Sci. Rep., 2012; Metallomics, 2013, and a book chapter, 2014). Our Fe2-hTF structure was used as a typical example of transferin immediately in a bioinorganic chemistry textbook (Oxford University Press, 2014). Using transferrin as a template, we developed a simple way to crystallize metal-bound transferrin, and got a variety of Ln-transferrin adducts (Yb(III) and Dy(III)), significantly improving our understanding on the biocoordination chemistry of Ln. Our work further demonstrated that the protein can serve as 'carrier' for metallodrug. A manuscript entitled "transferrin as a template for biocoordination chemistry of lanthanides(III)" was in preparation and will be submitted very soon. The slightly poor resolution of Pt- and Ur-transferrin adducts were found which need further optimization due to their different binding. To address this problem, we used vanadium(III) to replace Pu- and Ru, and reasonable resolution was got from X-ray diffraction at SSRF (in Shanghai).

705310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705310.value: The crystal structure of Bi- and Ln bound hTF represents the first structure of bismuth(III) and Ln(III) with a protein, offering invaluable information on the biocoordination of Bi3+ (and Ln) in view of their importance in medicine. It serves as a good starting point to further examine the use of hTF as a “carrier” for metallodrugs at the molecular level. The data from this project also open new horizons for development of new metallo-agents for human health. A new proposal partially based on this was submitted to ITC (as a Tier 3 application).

705310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705310.value: Human serum transferrin (hTF) binds ferric ion (Fe3+) tightly and reversibly, and delivers it to cells via a receptor-mediated endocytosis. The metal-binding and release result in significant conformational changes of the protein. However, the molecular mechanism of iron uptake and release accompanied by protein conformational changes, is not fully understood. In this project, we characterized the first crystal structures of diferric hTF (Fe2-hTF), bismuth bound hTF (Fe(C)Bi(N)-hTF) at 2.8 and 2.4 Å, and got seval other metal-bound transferrin crystals. Notably, the N-lobe of the protein exhibits an unique “partially-opened” conformation with iron and bismuth only bound to two (Tyr95 and Tyr188) and one (Tyr188) tyrosine residues from one subdomain together with anions. The C-lobe of the protein is fully closed with iron coordinates to four residues and a carbonate (as the synergistic anion). The structures of hTF observed here represent one of the key conformers of the protein, which were “captured” for the first time in this family of proteins. This study provides a molecular basis for understanding the mechanism of metallodrug uptake and release in hTF.

705510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705510.value: In the field of organic chemistry a current area of active research is asymmetric organocatalysis, which revolves around the concept of using small chiral organic molecules to catalyze reactions that result in the selective formation of a single stereoisomer of a product. While this concept was first demonstrated more than thirty years ago, it has only been in the past decade or so that widespread and intense study of it has been undertaken. In the interim the use of chiral metal-based catalysts for stereoselective catalysis became widely investigated and great achievements were made. However, due to the general desire of the chemical and pharmaceutical industries to use non-toxic and non-polluting catalysts free of metals that may end up contaminating the desired product or the environment, the study of organocatalysis has moved to the forefront of asymmetric catalysis research. The two possible sources of chiral organic molecular catalysts are (1) compounds produced by Nature, with or without further modification, and (2) synthetic structures designed by organic chemists. While natural products have the advantage that they are readily available with great structural diversity and complexity, they generally suffer from the fact that both enantiomers of them are not equally available, and this can limit their utility in cases when the most readily available enantiomer of the catalyst produces the undesired stereoisomer of the reaction product. Therefore, despite the labor involved in their production, non-natural organic catalysts can be desirable and advantageous if both enantiomers are equally available. In this regard the 1,1’-binapthyl skeleton has arguably been amongst the most successful platforms for designing organic catalysts, and many notable applications of it have been reported. For example, the vast majority of the research regarding chiral phosphoric acids as organic catalysts has been based upon it. Nevertheless, no matter how useful the 1,1’-binapthyl platform has been, identification of other effective and structurally diverse carbon skeletons that meet the requirements of accessibility should greatly expand the utility of asymmetric organocatalysis by broadening the range of reactions, and their substrate scope, in which it is applicable. Thus, in the present project we attempt to achieve this objective by examining the suitability of a chiral 1,1’-spirobiindane skeleton, known to impart excellent stereoselectivity in metal-based catalysis, as a platform for organocatalyst design. 不對稱有機催化是當前有機化學中活躍的研究領域。其核心發展方向是利用具有手性的有機小分子進行催化, 使反應選擇性地生成單一的立體異構體。這個理念早在三十多年前已被初次肯定, 但是在最近十年才受到普遍的關注和深入的研究。在此期間, 手性金屬催化劑應用於構象選擇催化逐漸得到廣泛的研究並取得了突出的研究成果。然而, 由於金屬可能會對目標產物或者環境帶來污染, 在化工和製藥業, 普遍使用非金屬催化劑, 以確保其無毒性和無污染性。為此, 有機催化已逐步成為不對稱催化研究的前沿。 手性有機小分子催化劑的兩個可能來源是(1)改性或未改性的天然產物，(2)實驗室的合成產物。儘管天然產物大量易得，並且具有復雜多樣的結構，但他們的對映異構體通常並不是同等存在於自然界。而如果其中廣泛存在的對映異構體做催化劑得到的立體異構體產物不是所需的產物，將極大的限制他們的應用。儘管有機催化劑的合成需要投入較多的人力，但如果可以得到等量的對映異構體，將具有顯著的優勢。1,1'-聯萘骨架(1,1'-binapthyl) 結構是目前最成功的有機催化平台之一，在此基礎上發展出大量關於手性磷酸催化劑的研究，擁有很多著名應用。雖然1,1'-聯萘骨架具有較多優點，研究開發其他高效，結構多樣並且易於獲得的催化劑骨架仍是十分必要的。新型催化劑骨架將可能應用於更多不同類型的反應並且擴大反應底物的選擇範圍，從而拓展不對稱有機合成的應用範圍。為實現這個目標，我們在此項目中研究了已知具有高對映選擇性的手性螺環結構(1,1'-spirobiindane) 作為非金屬催化劑設計平台的適用性。

705510.label: Realisation of objectives
705510.value: Despite numerous attempts we were not able to successfully synthesize the ketones of Objective 1. Since the imminium salts of Objective 2 were to be based on the ketones of Objective 1, we were not able to address Objectives 2 and 3. The failure to synthesize the ketones of Objective 1 was perhaps due to their high level of inherent ring strain. We were able to make progress towards Objectives 4-7, but none of this work reached a stage of completeness necessary for publication of our results. Much of the problems with this work was due to the temporary disappearance of the primary research post-graduate student working on the project. She reported having some personal issues that resulted in her repeated and prolonged absence from her research duties. For better or worse, we initially laid out our project objectives in a manner in which they were interconnected. Thus, problems and failures at an early stage really hampered our ability to address many of the things we had hoped to. However, as mentioned in the original proposal, this was envisioned as a high risk/high reward type of project, and unfortunately we were not able to meet our original objectives.

705510.label: Major findings and research outcome
705510.value: During the course of our research several other groups (List, Sasai, etc.) reported conceptually similar research. In light of our difficulties in synthesizing the catalysts to be studied, and our manpower limitations, we shifted the focus of our research to simpler systems which we could make better progress with and publish our results. Specifically we focused our efforts on phosphine and phosphine oxide catalysis. The highlights of our results include developing a one-pot reaction system for making unsymmetrical tertiary amines from a nitrogen equivalent and selective 1,4-reduction of conjugated polyunsaturated ketones. Both of these transformations were unprecedented in the chemical literature prior to our work. Furthermore, we have applied some of the methods developed as part of this project to the synthesis of potentially important flavour components of some common and valuable foods. These compounds may have commercial value because they produce desirable and interesting biological effects.

705510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705510.value: Aspects of the originally proposed research have been published by numerous other research groups early on during our work. This seems to validate our ideas as being important and interesting, and this area of research continues to be active. Regarding our actual results, we are continuing to apply our newly developed methods in new contexts in order to showcase their unique features. This is especially true in the area of food components.

705510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705510.value: We have developed new methods for reduction reactions that allow for the easy synthesis of new classes of compounds. Some o f these compounds have important biological activities and thus may have commercial value. These include components found in the citrus fruit yuzu and Szechuan peppercorns.

705610.label: Project Objectives
705610.value: Prime k-tuples. Let $\Omega (m)$ denote the total number of prime factors of the positive integer $m$. I will try to show that for infinitely many integers $n$, $\Omega \{(n+a_1)(n+a_2) \cdots n+a_k)\}$ is small. As an approximation to the famous prime k-tuples conjecture, there are some previous results of this kind, obtained by different techniques in sieve theory. I intend to improve on these by putting in new ingredients and techniques. Also I will try to obtain results in which $\max_j\{\Omega(n+a_j)\}$ is small. Work will also be carried out in the case that $n+a_1$, say, is constrained to a prime. Sum of squares of primes. I will try to show that all sufficiently large integer $n$, subject to suitable congruence conditions, is the sum of four almost primes $P_r$. Such result was first obtained around 15 years ago, and since then several improvements have emerged. I will try to lower the admissible value of $r$ here. I will also consider the problem of one square of a prime and three squares of almost primes. If time permits, I will also consider the problem of representation by sum of three squares of primes. Waring-Goldbach problems in almost primes. A number of results have been obtained in the last two decades, in which integers solutions to Waring's problem are further constrained to almost primes. I will try to extend the consideration in paragraph 2 above to some higher degree diagonal equations, especially cubic equations.

705610.label: Realisation of objectives
705610.value: Objective 1: On the prime k-tuples conjecture, I and my MPhil. student have used new sieve weights to obtain, at least for 1 < k <6, more precise results on the number of prime factors of each component. These results either equal or improve on those in the literature. Although we have not extended our work to higher values of k due to computational complexity, the new approach we used opens up a new possibility in further research in this area of problems. Objective 2: I and my PhD student successfully attacked the sums of four squares of almost prime problem and have greatly reduced the number of prime factors in each of the four variables. We have also obtained very good result in the case that one of the variables is restricted to a prime. Objective 3: The problem on sums of higher powers of almost primes, especially to the fourth power, has been investigated by my PhD student and he has already published one paper on this problem. His thesis on this area of problems has been awarded the Best Thesis Award of the Hong Kong Mathematical Society in 2014.

705610.label: Major findings and research outcome
705610.value: On the prime k-tuples conjecture, our main results include the following: (i) for any admissible pair (an+b, cn+d), there are infinitely many positive integers n for which an+b is a prime number, and at the same time, cn+d is either a prime, or a product of two primes, or a product of three primes; (ii) for any admissible triplet (an+b, cn+d, en+f), there are infinitely many positive integers n for which (an+b)(cn+d)(en+f) has at most 8 prime factors and each of an+b, cn+d, en+f has no more than 3 prime factors, (iii) similar results for admissible 4-tuples and 5-tuples of linear forms in n are obtained. These form the bulk of the thesis of my MPhil. student Mr. Chan Ching Yin. For Lagrange's four squares of primes problem, the main results include (i) every sufficiently large integer N congruent to 4 mod 24 can be expressed as a sum of four squares of integers, each of which has no more than 4 prime factors; (ii) same type of N as in (i) can be expressed as a sum of four squares of integers in which one is a prime and each of the other three has no more than 5 prime factors. These results are published in a joint paper with my student Zhao Lilu. Investigations on sums of three squares of almost primes and also on sums of twelve biquadrates were carried out by my PhD student Zhao Lilu and the results are included in his thesis.

705610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705610.value: The first part of my project concerns the prime k-tuples conjecture and I tried to devise new sieve weights based on an earlier idea of Selberg. The results produced are encouraging and it suggests that further trials and modifications are worthwhile. However, as already shown in our findings, such approach involves very heavy computational work, and more efficient theoretical arguments are therefore desirable. This can also be compared with the recent work of James Maynard, who also based on the same idea of Selberg has proved that there are infinitely many pairs of prime numbers with gaps less than 600. The seoncd part of my project concerns Lagrange's four squares of primes problem. The results obtained are already very sharp, but there are still some places where we can extract sieve informations more efficiently. The room for further improvements in this problem may be little, but applications of such ideas to similar or higher degree equations are promising and better results can be expected.

705610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705610.value: This project aims at studying linear and higher degree equations in which the variables are restricted to primes and almost primes. Such equations include as particular cases many of the historically important problems in number theory, such as Goldbach's conjecture, prime twins conjecture, Lagrange's four squares of primes conjecture, etc. Although it is still quite impossible to fully solve these famous problems with today's technology, we have successfully found in this project new technical methods to improve certain estimations involving the remainder terms in the sieve methods and also new types of sieve weights. The new results we have produced so far all supersede the best in the literature. On the problem of Lagrange's four squares problem, our results are very sharp and are unlikely to be improved upon in the near future. It is hoped that the technology we have developed in this project will be of use in other similar problems in this area of number theory. In fact, my student Dr. Zhao Lilu has published one more paper in this area as follow up on the investigations in this project. My investigation on the prime k-tuples conjecture uses an idea of Selberg which has never been successfully attempted before. Our results show that this idea should have good potential for further development.

706010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706010.value: In topology, we use various groups (such as homology, cohomology groups) to detect whether two spaces are of the same shape. Sometimes, these invariants are not enough. Torsion is a secondary invariant which can detect spaces that can be continuously deformed to each other but are not the same. In this project, we complete the study of torsion twisted by a flux, which was initiated by the PI and his collaborator. We will study a complex analogue, relate it to generalized geometry, find its property under duality and define a combinatorial counterpart. 在拓撲學中，我們使用各種各樣的群(例如同調群,上同調群)判別二空間是否有同一形狀。有時，這些不變量不足够。扭量是一種二級不變量, 可能判別可以互相連續變形但不相同的空間。在這個研究項目，我們完成由PI和他的合作者創始的被通量扭曲的扭量的研究。我們將研究它的全純類似物，與廣義幾何的關係，發現它在對偶之下的性質, 并且定義組合上的相應概念。

706010.value: The project funded research work on twisted analytic torsion as described in part 5.3. It led to publications in reputable scholarly journals and invited plenary talks at major international conferences. At the time, it opened a new subject area where doing meaningful research was still possible for junior mathematicians, who followed up the work.
