714310.label: Major findings and research outcome
714310.value: Ensuring broadcast efficiency and reliability with low communication overhead is challenging, especially with error-prone links. In [1], we employ erasure coding together with topology-transparent scheduling to combat collisions and channel errors. Topology-transparent scheduling algorithms may be inefficient when the network is static. In [2], we propose to utilize both assigned and unassigned slots efficiently to boost the performance of topology-transparent scheduling algorithms. Topology-dependent scheduling algorithms may depend on the detailed network connectivity information and cannot adapt to dynamic topological changes in mobile networks. In [3], we propose an efficient topology-transparent broadcast scheduling algorithm to provide a guaranteed throughput and achieve a much better average throughput. Recent advances in the physical layer have enabled wireless devices to have multiple packet reception (MPR) capability. In [4], we propose a novel topology-transparent scheduling algorithm that can employ the MPR capability to improve the network performance. Most existing topology-transparent scheduling algorithms are designed for single channel networks and few work have been done in multi-channel networks. In [5], we propose a distributed multi-channel topology-transparent broadcast scheduling algorithm. In [6], we have extended the previous framework on opportunistic scheduling by considering outcome fairness and throughput simultaneously, and developed a testbed to evaluate and demonstrate the proposed algorithms. 714310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714310.value: There are several research directions worth further investigation: 1. Effects of channel error to topology-transparent scheduling: We have assumed that the transmission channel is error free when devising the topology-transparent scheduling algorithms. It would be interesting to investigate the effects of these channel errors to the scheduling performance and devise these scheduling algorithms that can account for channel errors as well. 2. Investigation of topology-transparent broadcasting with multiple packet reception capability: We have investigated that the use of multiple packet reception capability in topology-transparent scheduling can help improve the network performance for the case of unicast communication. It would be interesting to extend the work for broadcasting.

714310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714310.value: Ubiquitous communication is an emerging field providing challenges for fundamental research and opportunities for new technologies. It supports anywhere, anytime communication, which makes our lives safer and more comfortable, and helps organizations manage their resources more efficiently. It thus bears significant military, social, and economical values. To support ubiquitous communication, part of the communication infrastructure must be wireless. The provision of quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees to ubiquitous applications is essential. Scheduling medium access in wireless ad hoc networks is challenging because of node mobility, and the limited availability and variability of wireless bandwidth. Conventional approaches in topology-dependent scheduling require each network node to maintain accurate network connectivity information. This is impractical in wireless ad hoc networks and thus such approaches are not adaptive to changes in network topology. This project develops the efficient, throughput-guaranteed scheduling algorithms which do not need the detailed network connectivity information but can adapt to dynamic topological changes.

714510.label: Project Objectives
714510.value: Devise a novel unified theory of congestion and error control (TCE): We would like to propose TCE to identify, model, and evaluate a set of signals and mechanisms for congestion and error control so that the operating regions and effectiveness of these control mechanisms can be determined. With the support of solid theoretical analysis, we can gain a better understanding on the validity and feasibility of these control mechanisms in the provision of high-speed data transfer for transport layer protocols. Propose a new TCP variant, TCP-TCE: We will design TCP-TCE by employing the findings and the theoretical analysis derived from TCE, rather than simply as ad hoc heuristics, as in many existing TCP variants. As a result, we expect to have substantial performance improvement. We will demonstrate TCP-TCE performance (throughput, fairness, stability, and responsiveness) by computer simulations. Implement a prototype communication system utilizing TCP-TCE: We will implement a prototype communication system utilizing the aforementioned TCP-TCE in a heterogeneous wired/wireless network testbed. We will then evaluate the performance of TCP-TCE on the prototype system in terms of the realized throughput, fairness, stability, responsiveness, computational and storage overheads, power consumption, and so on. We have experience implementing P2P applications in a heterogeneous wired/wireless testbed, and we believe that it is feasible to translate our experience in deploying these P2P applications to TCP-TCE.

In addition, increasingly such traffic is carried on wireless links, which are subject to wireless losses and packet reordering in addition to congestive losses. Compared with most of the existing TCP variants, TCP-TCE is based on sound theoretical analysis, rather than ad hoc heuristics. This project is expected to impact the development of congestion and error control in the next-generation high-speed transport layer protocols. 714510.label: Major findings and research outcome
714510.value: The wireless medium may cause substantial packet losses, rendering Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) inefficient. In [1], we propose a cross-layer solution by combining link-layer retransmission techniques and a solution for TCP packet reordering. The class of additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease (AIMD) algorithms constitutes a key mechanism for congestion control. The algorithmic behaviour may, however, be distorted when wireless links are present. In [2], we develop a framework for AIMD in TCP. The framework enables a systematic analysis of the existing AIMD-based TCP variants and assists in the design of new TCP variants. It further identifies a new approach in enhancing the performance of TCP, known as the compensation scheme. A tax-rebate approach is proposed as an approximation of the compensation scheme. The combination of loss-based TCP and drop-tail routers often results in full buffers, creating large queueing delays. The challenge with parameter tuning and the drastic consequence of improper tuning have discouraged network administrators from enabling AQM even when routers support it. To address this problem, we propose [3] a novel design principle for AQM, called the pricing-link-by-time (PLT) principle. PLT increases the link price as the backlog stays above a threshold, and resets the price once the backlog goes below this threshold. We prove that such a system exhibits cyclic behavior that is robust against changes in network environment and protocol parameters. In [4], we have systematically investigated the consequence of incrementally deploying reordering-robust TCP enhancements. We focus on the impact of enhancing reordering robustness of a flow on competing flows and the whole network. In [5], we described the development of a heterogeneous wired/wireless network testbed, and demonstrated the performance of TCP/NCL. [2] Lai, C., Leung, K.C. and Li, V.O.K., “Design and analysis of TCP AIMD in wireless networks,” Proc. IEEE WCNC, Shanghai, China, April 2013. [3] Lai, C., Low, S., Leung, K.C., and Li, V.O.K., “Pricing link by time,” ACM SIGMETRICS Performance Evaluation Review, Vol. 42, No. 1, pp. 421-433, June 2014. [4] Lai, C., Leung, K.C. and Li, V.O.K., “Does it hurt when others prosper? Exploring the impact of heterogeneous reordering robustness of TCP,” Proc. IEEE INFOCOM, Turin, Italy, April 2013. [5] Lai, C., Leung, K.C. and Li, V.O.K., “A heterogeneous wired/wireless network testbed for Transmission Control Protocol,” Technical Report No. TR-2014-003, Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, The University of Hong Kong.

714510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714510.value: There are several research directions worth further investigation. These include a design theory for general increase/decrease algorithm in TCP and a systematic adaptive AQM. With their simple structure, the additive increase multiplicative decrease (AIMD) algorithms generally exhibit regular behavior that can be well controlled and understood, which facilitates their widespread deployment. However, in order to simultaneously accommodate various possible performance objectives, the general design space of the congestion avoidance algorithm in TCP needs to be expanded beyond AIMD. To consider more general increase and decrease algorithms, we can define generic increment and decrement functions. In this project, we have devised a novel family of AQM algorithms that inherently requires minimal parameter tuning while ensuring robust performance. This gives great incentive for incrementally deploying the AQM algorithms to achieve prompt congestion control. Another approach is to automatically tune the parameters of AQM algorithms, gaining responsiveness and stability without incurring sophisticated manual parameter tuning process.

714510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714510.value: The success of the Internet arises from its capabilities to support robust and reliable end-to-end data transfer services for a myriad of applications running over a set of end-systems, such as PCs and smart phones. The convergence of the computer, communication, entertainment, and consumer electronics industry is driving an explosive growth in Internet traffic, and such growth is expected to continue for some time. With the advancements in wireless technology and the demand for ubiquitous access by users, increasingly such traffic is carried on wireless links, which are subject to wireless losses and packet reordering in addition to congestive losses. For the Internet to function peoperly, it is imporant to correctly identify the occurrence of wireless losses, packet reordering, and congestive losses, and react accordingly. Most existing solutions are rather ad hoc and may not work well. This project develops the theory which will help us identify these events correctly, and provide the foundation on which we have developed some excellent soultions.

714810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714810.value: A quick review on the history of the development of modern science and technology will tell us that many important breakthroughs and innovations are inspired by nature. Just like how pioneers such as Leonardo da Vinci were inspired by how birds fly, engineers are now intrigued by what they can learn by studying biological systems. One such example is the locomotion of biological cells. Although the exact nature is still by and large unknown, cell motility is commonly believed to be driven by actin polymerization. Similar actin-based motility has also been observed in pathogens like Listeria monocytogenes, which have the amazing ability to propel themselves in the cytoplasm by hijacking the actins of the host cell. Since cell motility is essential in so many important biological processes, such as immune response and cancer metastasis, a precise knowledge of how forces, large enough for cellular motions, are generated by actin polymerization will likely provide us clues on finding ways to contain or cure different diseases. In addition, similar to airplanes, we can dream that one day micro or nano-scale actin-driven devices will be invented that can move in our body to deliver drugs or conduct medical procedures. Several lines of evidence have suggested that actin-driven Listeria actually rotate when moving forward. Understanding what cause such rotation is important both fundamentally, as it sheds light on the actual force generation mechanism by polymerization, and practically since it could provide critical information for the design of future actin-driven devices. Unfortunately, no existing theory is capable of explaining or predicting such rotational motions. Furthermore, there are very limited, if any, experimental data on how Listeria, or beads coated with certain proteins and propelled by actin polymerization, rotate under different physical or chemical conditions. This project aims to address these two outstanding issues. Specifically, theoretical models based on different plausible mechanisms will be developed to explain the torque generation by polymerization. In the meantime, carefully designed experiments will be conducted to quantitatively measure the rotation of actin-driven microspheres under various conditions. The experimental results will then be used to compare to the predictions by models based on different mechanisms, from which we hope the real torque generation mechanism can be identified. 一个对现代科学技术发展史的快速回顾告诉我们，许多重要的科技突破和创新的灵感来自大自然，飞机的发明就是一个典型的例子。早在十五世纪八十年代，在达芬奇作出的飞行尝试中，他绘制了超过100张的图纸来说明自己飞行器的设计，以期像鸟儿一样飞行。然而，直到上个世纪，随着空气动力学的进步，人们才终于了解到飞行的秘密。在今天，我们的飞机能够比任何鸟类飞得更快、更高。很多时候，感叹于自然现象的魅力，发掘其背后的基本原理，然后运用获取的知识发明出较自然界对更为先进的东西，这很大程度上说明了科学技术是如何进步的。 就像古代时候着迷于鸟类的飞行一样，现在人们感兴趣的是生物细胞的运动。虽然细胞运动确切的本质仍然是未知的，但它通常被认为是由肌动蛋白的聚合所驱动。通常一个所谓的突出区域会由于肌动蛋白的聚合而在运动细胞的前端形成，这个区域使得细胞可以和外界形成稳定的黏附从而让细胞的运动成为可能。类似的以肌动蛋白为基础的运动在某些病原体上也被观察到，例如李斯特菌，它们有惊人的能力，通过劫持宿主细胞的肌动蛋白，推动自己在细胞质中的运动。由于细胞的运动在许多重要的生物过程（如免疫反应与癌症转移）中是必不可少的，所以，准确地了解肌动蛋白的聚合如何产生足够大的推动力，可能会为我们提供线索以找到新的方法来控制或治疗不同的疾病。此外，像过去对于飞机的梦想一样，我们梦想有一天，可以发明出能够在我们的身体里能借助肌动蛋白而输送药物或施行医疗手术的微纳米尺度设备。 该项目旨在通过对这一领域两个突出问题的研究来增加我们对以肌动蛋白为基础的运动的基本了解。两个问题即：（1）肌动蛋白是如何驱动具有类似李斯特性质蛋白质涂层的小球旋转的；（2）理论上什么原因导致这样的转动。第一个问题可以通过精心设计的实验来回答，而开发聚合反应产生的的扭矩理论模型将解决第二个问题。

714810.label: Major findings and research outcome
714810.value: 1. A theoretical explanation for the torque generation by actin polymerization has been provided. In particular, we showed that interactions between the load surface and the tip of polymerizing filaments, as well as correlation among the orientations of these filaments, play crucial roles in generating moments causing the cargo to rotate and spin (Y. Lin*, V.B. Shenoy, B. Hu and L. Bai. Biophysical Journal, 2010). 2. The force-generation and load-bearing capabilities of realistic actin networks were quantitatively simulated and their dependence on factors like the network architecture have been elucidated. Biological implications/applications of these findings have also been discussed (B. Hu, V.B. Shenoy and Y. Lin*. Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids, 2012; Y. Lin*, X. Wei, J. Qian, K.Y. Sze and V.B. Shenoy. Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids, 2014). 3. Robust protocols have been identified allowing us to generate actin-based motility in vitro (theise by B. Hu, 2011). 4. The twist and curvature distributions of the trajectories of actin-propelled microspheres have, for the first time, been obtained which provide critical inform on how these beads actually spin/rotate when moving as well as for the theoretical modeling in the future (Q. Zhu, A. Liu, and Y. Lin*, to be submitted).

714810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714810.value: 1. It will be interesting to combine the model being developed with proper kinetic description for the crosslinking/branching of individual filaments so that entire structural evolution of the network, as well as its influence on the movement of the cargo, can be simulated. 2. Experimentally, whether non-spherical particles can be fabricated and then be used to generate actin-based motility is an important issue to further pursue as it will provide definite answer to the key question of how surface curvature regulates the force/torque generation capability of polymerizing actin networks. Efforts along these lines are underway in our lab.

714810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714810.value: This study, for the first time, provides a theoretical explanation for the torque generation by polymerization and hence greatly enhances our basic understanding of actin-based motility. The experimental data generated by this project quantitatively demonstrate exactly how actin-propelled microspheres rotate/spin which could be extremely valuable to the development of new theories as well as the design of future micro or nano-scale actin-driven devices.

715110.label: Project Objectives
715110.value: Develop a nonlinear finite element package for structural analysis of RC buildings with transfer structures, based on the 3D hybrid-stress hexahedral element technology. Predict the ultimate drift capacity at member level and model the deformation behavior of RC buildings with transfer structures under extreme loads. Predict the inter-story drift demand of RC buildings with transfer structures, taking into account earthquake magnitude, distance scenarios, site effects and dynamic response behaviors of the building including the torsional response in the inelastic range. 715110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
715110.value: Over the past fifty years, Hong Kong has developed into a financial and commercial hub of the Asia-Pacific region. A significant portion of the urban district is located on reclaimed lands, and it is well-known that landfill material could adversely amplify the local ground shaking. Substantial amount of researches in recent years have indicated that the potential earthquake risk in Hong Kong, due to low-probability high-consequence earthquake events, is no less than that in high seismic zones. Earthquake-resistant design has yet to be specifically required in the current building design codes in Hong Kong. Buildings with significant vertical discontinuities are particularly prone to earthquake damages, for which the transfer plate structures, which are widely constructed in Hong Kong, are the most vulnerable for their massive 2m-thick slabs being connected to relatively weaker structural members. Recently, the applicants have also found out that the exterior walls above the transfer structure are critically loaded structural members under seismic action due to shear concentration effect. Seismic fragility analyses are recent advances in displacement-based techniques to assess general building structures subject to earth-quake loads. However, such an expedient risk assessment tool has not been applied to the more important yet vulnerable transfer structures, which have been widely built in metropolitan cities in China, Shanghai and Beijing, as well as in other major cities such as Singapore, London and New York. Seismic displacement demand and drift capacity of a suite of typical buildings in Hong Kong will first be investigated. Nonlinear pushover analysis will be carried out to assess damage and collapse loads. The risk of damage and collapse of transfer structures will then be evaluated by refined fragility functions specially designed for transfer structures based on displacement demand and drift capacity models. Regarding the computational tool, massive RC structural members, such as shear walls, core walls and thick transfer plates under extreme loads may subject to a combination of intensive shear, bending, twisting and warping, which cannot be accurately modeled by conventional computational techniques. Nevertheless, the new high-performance solid 3D hybrid-stress elements developed by the principal investigator could just be an excellent tool to model the dynamic behaviors of transfer structures. The massive structural members can now be conveniently decomposed into solid brick elements of different shapes and sizes for structural analysis based on the exact geometry without any underlying kinematic assumptions, which is an important attribute to a displacement-based model for seismic assessment.

715110.label: Major findings and research outcome
715110.value: The dynamics of soil and foundation are studied and useful results are obtained and published in four papers. The vibration of fluid and general solid structures are investigated and some interesting results are published in three papers. Various aspects of composite structures have been studied with results published in three papers, these finding will be useful for the design of steel and concrete composite structures. Mesh generation of solid hexahedral elements for reinforced concrete massive structures has been thoroughly studied and nine papers have been published on this topic. Failure mechanism of reinforced concrete members has been investigated and results have been published in four papers.

715110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
715110.value: This project has placed a solid foundation in an efficient and rigorous analysis of massive reinforced concrete structures under the attack of earthquake load. The next step is a practical design procedure of RC buildings subject to earthquake load based on the fragility curves.

715110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
715110.value: The traditional methods are inadequate for the analysis and design of massive reinforced concrete buildings subject to extreme forces. The current project has filled up many of these gaps in providing a convenient and rigorous procedure for the analysis of tall buildings under earthquake loads. The results are especially useful to improve the design of massive concrete buildings with transfer structures.

715510.value: 在有微圖案壁面的微渠道中的電動滑移流動

715510.label: Project Objectives
715510.value: To develop general expressions for the apparent slip as a function of the local surface heterogeneity in potential and slippage, when forced simultaneously by electric field and pressure gradient. To investigate time-oscillatory electrokinetic flow under the effect of boundary slip, and to determine the complex slip coefficients as functions of the frequency parameter for several types of microstructures. To compare the relative performance, in terms of apparent slip, of two-dimensional and one-dimensional patterns as a function of the channel thickness. To derive micromechanics–based constitutive equations relating electrical and mass fluxes to electrical and pressure forcings.

715510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
715510.value: Many chemical and bio-medical tests are now performed on ever-smaller devices so as to reduce the amounts of samples, and to shorten the reaction and analysis time. There is a persistent need to search for effective ways to drive flow through a channel that can be as small as microns in cross-sectional dimensions. Pressure pumping alone may not be satisfactory as its flow-rate drops dramatically with decrease in the channel depth. Electrokinetic phenomena, which are processes involving the interaction between an applied/induced electric field and free charge in the fluid, are important mechanisms that can be utilized to control flow through a miniaturized channel. Also, the channel walls are often engineered to feature mircopatterns that can lead to significant boundary slip, thereby reducing the flow resistance. Electrokinetic phenomena and boundary slip are both interfacial processes, which on the one hand are determined by local microscopic effects near the wall, and on the other hand will affect the global transport through the channel. There lacks sufficient understanding in the existing literature about the effects of microscale wall heterogeneity (in terms of surface potential, intrinsic slippage, roughness pattern) on flow simultaneously driven by electrical and mechanical forcings. Many studies have taken, for example, the slip coefficient simply as a known real constant while grossly overlooking the microscopic effects on it. The slip coefficient can become a complex quantity when the flow is time-oscillating, which is a fundamental issue that has not been thoroughly studied yet. How exactly the electrokinetics and wall slippage will interact with each other, whether positively or negatively, remains much to be determined. It is proposed to develop constitutive equations containing coefficients that are derived based on the microscale electrohydrodynamics. By virtue of the existence of two distinct length-scales (mircoscale for the local features near the wall, and macroscale for the global transport through the channel), an asymptotic method of averaging, known as homogenization, is applied to finding these effective coefficients for several one-dimensional or two-dimensional micropatterns. The deduced equations will then be used to look into some of the unresolved problems, such as (i) the effect of channel thickness on the slip performance exhibited by various micropatterns; (ii) the competition between the electro-retarding and the slip-enhancing effects; (iii) a modified form of boundary slip condition when applied to high-frequency oscillatory flow. 許多化學和生物醫學上執行測試，都在日益縮小的設備進行，以減少樣品的數量，並縮短反應時間和分析。有長期需要尋求有效的途徑，以推動流經一個通道，可以小至微米的截面尺寸。電動現象，這過程涉及感應電場和自由電荷在流體之間的互動，是重要的機制，可以用來控制流過一個微型的渠道。此外，該渠道的牆壁通常設計為模格特徵，可以導致邊界滑移，從而降低了流動阻力。電動現象和邊界滑移都是界面過程，它一方面取決於微觀影響附近的管壁，另一方面影響宏觀的輸流。 現有文獻對影響微尺度的異質性壁（在表面電位、內在滑移、粗糙度模式等），對同時受到電場及壓力場產生的流動，缺少足夠的認識。例如，許多研究採取滑移係數僅僅為已知常數，而真正的嚴重忽視了微觀影響的研究。當流量是時間振盪時，滑移係數可以成為一個複數，這是一個根本問題一直沒有得到深入的研究呢。如何準確的描述電動力學和牆壁滑移相互影響，無論是正面還是負面的，還需要很進深的研究。 這建議目標是制定本構方程，含有的係數是基於微型電水動力學。憑藉存在兩個不同長度的尺度（微觀的是牆壁附近的尺度，和宏觀的是通過通道的尺度），用一個漸進平均方法，被稱為齊性化，用於尋找這些有效係數，包括一維或二維的壁面微圖形。推導出來的方程將被用來研究一些懸而未決的問題，如（i）通道的厚度對滑移性能的影響;（二）電力阻和滑增強之間的競爭影響;（三）適用於高頻振盪流的邊界滑移條件。

715910.label: Project Objectives
715910.value: To investigate the effects of confining dislocations within micron-sized metal crystals on their deformation behaviour, by methods including coating or filling them with a different material, or by introducing grain boundaries inside them. To establish the relationship between dislocation microstructures and the deformation behaviour of micron-size crystals in which dislocations are trapped, by electron microscopy investigation, as well as by theoretical modeling. To investigate the effects introduced by varying the initial dislocation density in micron-sized crystals in which dislocations are trapped, by applying different pre-strains to the bulk materials from which these micro-crystals are made.

715910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
715910.value: Recent compression experiments on metallic micro-pillars revealed that their deformation is, in general, jerky with a stochastic nature. The jerky nature of deformation implies that precise metal forming would be difficult in the micron regime. The jerky flow is believed to be due to the fact that a dislocation avalanche is generated by a source when the stress reaches the source-operating value, but because the crystal is very small, the dislocations zip through the small crystal quickly, leaving the latter in more or less the same source-depleted state as before. Another avalanche is produced when a more difficult source is triggered at a higher stress level. This conjecture is supported by the experimental observation that the residual dislocation density of aluminium micro-pillars after heavy compression does not rise significantly. Confining the dislocations within the small crystal by some means may alleviate the problem of jerky deformation. In this project, a number of methods are proposed to confine dislocations inside micro-sized crystals. First, the crystal can be coated with a thin layer of a second material (e.g. tungsten or platinum) by focused-ion-beam (FIB) induced, chemical-vapour-deposition (CVD) on its free surface. Secondly, a cavity can be milled inside the micro-crystal by FIB, the this can be filled with CVD with tungsten or platinum inside the FIB. The third method involves introducing a grain boundary inside the micro-specimen, i.e. forming a micro-bicrystal. In these cases, the coating, filling, or the grain boundary should hold the dislocations inside the micro-specimen, and so their deformation should be very different. Preliminary work showed that aluminium micro-pillars treated using these methods exhibited much smoother deformation than the untreated state, and that their strain hardening rate was also a lot higher. This project aims at a systematic study into the effects on deformation of micro-crystals by trapping dislocations inside them. 新的壓縮實驗顯示微尺寸材料的塑性變形是急動和隨機的. 急動性的變形代表微尺寸材料的成形將會困難. 而這行為相信是由於晶體位錯在微小材料內運作時太容易橫貫材料的尺寸而消失, 導致材料間歇性地回復到一個缺乏位錯的狀態. 這猜想現已得到充分的實驗結果証明. 上述的猜想同時說明如果位錯能被局限在微小材料內, 材料變形時的急動性便會消失, 可塑性將會大大提高. 這項目將會利用一系列的方法把位錯局限在材料內, 這些方法包括利用聚焦離子束在材料的表面上塗上一層異物, 或將異物填在材料的內部, 又或將一個晶介包含在材料內. 這些異物或晶介應該能有效地把位錯局限在材料內, 達到平滑變形和強化的效果.

715910.label: Realisation of objectives
715910.value: For Objective 1, confining dislocations in small material volumes were investigated by means including involving grain boundaries [2, 3, 12], coating the specimen surface [7] and introducing precipitates [9, 13]. The results have led to a number of publications in good journals, and so this objective is fully achieved. For Objective 2, both TEM investigations [3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13] and theoretical modelling [1, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14] were employed to study the relation between the dislocation microstructures and deformation behaviour of micron-sized materials. Again, the results were published in high quality journals and this objective is fully achieved. For Objective 3, pre-straining was used to study the effects of variations of the initial dislocation density on the deformation of micro-crystals. The results were published in [1, 6, 7, 12]. This objective is fully addressed.

715910.label: Major findings and research outcome
715910.value: The deformation of small crystal volumes was found to be strongly affected by regulation of the dislocation density present, by confinement means including introducing grain boundaries and precipitates and coating the surface, as well as pre-straining [2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 12, 13]. In particular, the size-dependence of strength was found to be significantly affected by the initial dislocation content present, and the power-law exponent of the size dependence was shown to be related to the initial dislocation distribution via a fractal-like model [1, 6]. In addition, the simultaneous application of an oscillatory signal to the mechanical loading was found to result in very significant subgrain formation accompanying softening in different metals [4, 5, 11], and this further illustrates the importance of the dynamical interactions of dislocations in affecting the deformation behaviour. The unusual behaviour of small-scale plasticity was also demonstrated in the sintering of nano-crystals. Under the mutual attractive force between two sintering nano-crystals, MD simulations show that they bombard each other with a high velocity, and this results in peculiar deformation behaviours accompanying the sintering in a dislocation limited context, leading to structural transformations involving twinning [8, 10, 14]. This is a further, yet important example of small-scale plasticity which is the focus of the present project. Apart from journal publications, the PI was also invited to a number of key international conferences on small-scale plasticity, where he presented the findings of this project.

715910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
715910.value: As an extension of the present work, the modeling of nano-structured materials was studied [15, 16]. Furthermore, during the theoretical investigation of the project, we realized the importance of a meso-scale dislocation plasticity simulator that can handle any density of dislocations. Current means of computational dislocation plasticity, including molecular dynamics or discrete dislocation dynamics, are handicapped when the dislocation quantity in the system is high. We are currently developing a novel meso-scale simulator that is based on the dynamics of the dislocation density function, and encouraging results have been obtained so far. The successful development of such a simulator should revolutionalize the field of crystal plasticity, and we plan to seek funding support to pursue this topic.

715910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
715910.value: The mechanical behaviour of small materials usually does not bear similarities with their bulk counterparts, when they are much smaller than the typical microstructural length scale that would determine mechanical properties in the bulk situation. One well-known phenomenon is a strong size dependence of strength, i.e. the strength increases with the reduction in specimen size in a power-law manner. In this project, we have systematically studied how the strength and deformation behaviour of small crystals depend on their dislocation microstructure and loading conditions. In particular, we have shown that using means to confine the dislocation contents in these specimens can have great influence on their properties. One important finding is that the size-dependence of strength can become much milder with dislocations confined in the specimen, and the exponent in the power-law dependence is shown to be a strong, inverse function of the initial dislocation content. Oscillatory mechanical loadings have also been found to be able to significantly reduce the dislocation density stored, leading to enhanced subgrain formation and softening of the material. Unusual plasticity modes were also found in the sintering of nano-crystals, where the difficulty for dislocations to arise leads to peculiar deformation modes involving twinning.

716310.label: Project Title(Chinese)
716310.value: 尖晶石相於回用污泥焚化灰為陶瓷材料的形成作用

716310.label: Co - Investigator(s)
716310.value: Prof Chan, Siu-Wai Prof White, Tim

716310.label: Project Objectives
716310.value: The main purpose of this project is to develop the recycling potential of sludge-incineration ash as a new type of raw material for making ceramics. The main focus is on promoting the formation of ferrite and aluminate spinels in ceramic products. Therefore, spinel incorporation capability with regard to targeted divalent cations will be investigated in great detail, and their metal transformation efficiencies influenced by the sintering scheme (temperature and time) will be provided quantitatively. The crystalline characteristics (lattice parameters, cation distribution, crystal size, etc.) of spinels generated from ash-containing precursors will be quantified by Rietveld refinement using X-ray diffraction (XRD) data to evaluate the crystal properties of spinel-stabilized phases. The effects of clay precursors and other major metal oxides (quartz, feldspars, etc.) in the ceramic matrix will be assessed by monitoring the responses of these crystalline characteristics of spinels. Metal stabilization effects will be analyzed by leaching experiments and examined by surface-sensitive characterization tools, such as atomic force microscopy (AFM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), to elucidate the metal leaching behavior on the surface. With strong expertise in high resolution electron microscopy (SEM and TEM), this research team will characterize the microstructures of ceramic products and identify the nanostructures of the spinel phases, such as the grain boundary features, to facilitate the discussion of a reliable metal incorporation strategy. This project seeks greater international collaboration to provide cutting-edge environmental material research opportunities for staff and students. This is also critical for promoting the role of the local environmental research community within the global movement of interdisciplinary research. One of the Co-Is, Professor Siu-Wai Chan, is a senior materials scientist whose research foci include the characterization of ceramic nanostructures and grain boundaries. She will carry out the identification of boundary features by high resolution electron microscopy to assist us in investigating metal stabilization effects and leaching behavior. The other Co-I, Professor Tim J. White, is a leading scientist in crystallographic analysis of environmental materials, and will concurrently refine our X-ray diffraction data for the discussion of the crystalline characteristics of spinels. Based on the mechanistic understanding of spinel formation initiated by sludge-incineration ash precursors, techniques will be elaborated for fabricating desired nano- and microstructural features for spinel-containing ceramic products. Overall, the results and implementation of this project are targeted to facilitate the goal of developing a sustainable sludge management plan by creating a scientifically sound and experimentally proven waste-to-resource technology for recycling the sludge-incineration ash.

716310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
716310.value: 生活污水处理过程中所产生的污泥对许多地区产生了非常显著的环境影响。在香港本地，污水经过化学强化一级处理（CEPT）过程所产生的脱水污泥高达900吨/天，而填埋是目前的唯一处理方法。根据当地政府相关部门评估，2020年的污泥产生量将会增加到超过2000吨/天，污泥焚化也即将会成为解决这一问题的手段。上述焚化方法可以在有效去除污泥中所含的有机物，并同时产生含大量无机成分的焚化灰。焚化灰中所含的无机成分包括因絮凝剂存在而产生的铁铝氧化物以及视不同污水来源而存在其中的其他金属氧化物。本课题的目的在于将污泥焚化灰研制成瓷砖、绝缘体、颜料以及耐火材料等陶瓷产品的原材料，从而发挥其可循环回收利用的潜能。项目的核心是一方面通过促进重金属铁铝尖晶石（MFe2O4 和 MAl2O4）的形成而在本质上降低尖晶石形成后的重金属渗析力，另一方面通过对研究中形成的尖晶石产品本身微观结构的可靠控制使产品适于不同用途。该项目主持人已经成功研究出通过金属铁铝尖晶石的形成使得含重金属（Ni，Cu）的工业污泥得以稳定化的策略。研究首次阐明了作为主要陶瓷原材料的高岭土在烧结产生金属铝尖晶石的过程中所起到的有效作用。鉴于在尖晶石形成机制上的主要发现，本课题将把富含铁和铝成分的污泥焚化灰废料转化为可作为陶瓷原材料的新资源。基于即将在香港焚化的污泥，本研究组利用其焚化底灰于系统性的陶瓷烧结实验，并利用X射线衍射精修技术将废弃污泥中典型的二价金属离子（Ca2+, Mg2+, Cu2+, Zn2+, Ni2+）形成尖晶石的能力定量化。并且，通过监测尖晶石结构晶胞参数，观察粘土材料的熔融作用，识别晶界特征以及评估材料表面的金属渗析力，上述烧结实验条件将被最优化。最后，不同烧结材料的选择和烧结过程的控制为尖晶石产品的微观结构的设计提供了灵活性，从而使本研究技术在制作陶瓷产品的应用范围达到最大化。

716310.label: Realisation of objectives
716310.value: All the proposed objectives were achieved through this project implementation. The incorporation of different metals were experimentally carried out and constantly repeated throughout the entire project period, and the goal was to compare a wide range of processing parameters and precursor materials. Due to the complexity of sludge-incineration ash and the different precursor materials used in ceramic industry, such systematic work is needed to delineate the different spinel formation behavior and product performance under different reaction conditions. Our unique strength in quantitative X-ray diffraction (QXRD) technique was extensively applied through the fundamental parameter approach in Rietveld refinement analysis and it had quantitatively reported the phase compositions in many products generated in this project. The crystalline characteristics (including lattice parameters, cation distribution, and crystal size of spinels) generated from the targeted ions and different ceramic precursors were also revealed. The changes crystalline characteristics could provide crucial information about the quality of generated crystalline products to assist our assessment of product quality. In addition, the state-of-the-art microscopic tools had largely help the collection of evidence on how the metals were leached from the surfaces generated after the sintering process of ceramic products. The surface sensitive characterization methods used in this project also provided direct evidences in quantifying the chemical and morphological properties of the ash-incorporated ceramic products in this project. The international and inter-institution collaboration had further enhanced depth and width of this project work, particularly on the grain boundary properties, quantitative XRD results and metal leaching behavior topics. The Co-authored papers with our collaborators had demonstrated the synergetic effects in exploring the more complex scientific questions in this field. Finally, the generated material property knowledge and the mechanistic understanding of spinel formation from the targeted metals were applied to the design of sludge ash bearing ceramic products. The control ranges of key processing parameters were reported in the published work, and the high-resolution morphological data had provided us the information on the change trends of nano- and microstructural features for spinel-containing ceramic products. The objects of this project were thus successfully achieved and the outcome has clearly indicated the promising potential in this waste-to-resource strategy by benefitting both the sludge treatment and ceramic fabrication industries.

The influences of precursor materials and sintering conditions on forming ferrite and aluminate spinels have been particularly investigated, which was found important when recycling sludge-incineration ash as a new type of raw material for making ceramics.

The crystalline characteristics, including lattice parameters, cation distribution, and crystal size of spinels generated from the targeted ions (divalent: magnesium, copper, zinc, and nickel; trivalent: aluminum and iron) were already quantified by Rietveld refinement using XRD data generated from different attempts of precursor materials (alumina, clay, feldspars and quartz). The change trends of crystalline characteristics were also analyzed to generate the understanding on how the precursors influence the spinel crystalline characteristics and the strategies of enhancing the robustness of the spinel phases generated in the products.

The metal stabilization effects of the generated spinel phases were tested by the standard leaching procedure and the prolonged leaching experiment invented by us. We also used the high-resolution electron microscopic techniques (SEM and TEM) to compare the surface morphological damage due to the leaching processes. For low-leachable phases, the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and nanoindentation (combined with our atomic force microscopy (AFM) system) were used to examine the leaching effect on the top thin-layer of the targeted metal stabilizing phases and their grain boundary areas. Such findings have suggested the strategies of how to more reliably incorporate the metals in the ceramic products.

We conducted international collaboration with institutes outside of Hong Kong to exchange the research experience and the characteristics information of sludge incineration ash. One of our Co-Is, Professor Chan, visited us at HKU in 2011 summer to discuss our findings on the surface and grain boundary properties of the spinel phases sintered in our experiments. The other Co-I, Professor White, assisted our protocol establishment for XRD refinement work and this has been the most important basis in our quantitative XRD technique. A new inter-institutional research collaboration was built with Dr. P. H. Lee who later helped with the analysis and investigation of metal leachability on the material surfaces. Co-authored papers with our collaborators were published in quality journals in the corresponding fields.

With the mechanistic understanding of spinel formation from the targeted metals, the control ranges of key processing parameters were reported. The high-resolution electron microscopic results also provided us the information on the change trends of nano- and microstructural features for spinel-containing ceramic products. We have used sludge ash materials to successfully create a reliable and experimentally proven technology to recycle the sludge as a new material resource for ceramic industry.

716310.label: Major findings and research outcome
716310.value: This project has generated substantial details in explaining how different types of spinels can be generated from the ash and ceramic precursors, particularly for the major metals in the sludge ash. For example, with copper-bearing ash the copper aluminum spinel (CuAl2O4) can be predominantly incorporated because of widely available aluminum in the ceramic raw materials. On the other hand, the competition from the iron-based spinel (CuFe2O4) should also be a major concern in the design of phase compositions in the products, as well as the micro- and nano-structures of products. The maximum fraction of aluminum-based spinel can reach 98% with alumna precursors and 83% with the clay type precursors. Using iron oxides, iron was transformed into both tetragonal and cubic CuFe2O4, reaching nearly complete copper incorporation. Various colors and microstructures were observed in the fabricated materials and thus such products can be used as pigments, construction materials and ceramic membranes. With zinc-bearing ash, many precursors were also found to be able to crystallochemically incorporate zinc into the zinc aluminum spinel (ZnAl2O4). The incorporation efficiencies through short sintering scheme were first quantitatively determined by quantitative X-ray diffraction data. However, this study also revealed that when using clay and aluminosilicate precursors both zinc aluminate spinel and zinc silicate (Zn2SiO4) phases could be formed during the sintering process. To analyze the details of zinc incorporation reactions, alumina and quartz systems were further used to observe the ZnAl2O4 and Zn2SiO4 formations. The results show different incorporation behavior for clay and aluminosilicate precursors during the formation of ZnAl2O4 and Zn2SiO4 in the system. With a competitive formation between ZnAl2O4 and Zn2SiO4, the ZnAl2O4 spinel phase is predominant at high temperatures. This study also conducted the prolonged leaching test modified from the toxicity characteristic leaching procedure to evaluate the metal stability in the product phases. The results demonstrated the superior acidic resistance of the spinels and confirmed the feasibility of incorporating the toxic metals in sludge ash into the ceramic products. A wide variety of morphological features in the products also provided a potential for different product application opportunities. Overall, the findings of this study suggest a promising technology to beneficially use waste sludge incineration ash as ceramic raw materials. It also provides an economical means to simultaneously reduce the sludge ash environmental hazard and create its beneficial use value.

716310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
716310.value: Further development of this research direction may be targeting at the pilot-scale operation of incorporating the sludge incineration ash into the existing ceramic manufacturing lines. Hong Kong has just completed the largest sludge incineration plant in the world (2000 tpd) and this plant is now in its first stage testing operation. The generation of large quantity sludge ash will soon be the issue in our waste management structure in Hong Kong, but the current plan for managing the generated sludge ash is still toward the landfill disposal after chemical stabilization. The optimal processing parameters derived from this project may need further tuning for applying in the larger scale operations, and the product properties produced from the larger scale processing also require the characterizations for confirmation. Nearly all existing pilot or full size plants in the world for ash beneficial use are solely based on empirical approach. Therefore, the outcome of this project can significantly assist the reliability of such operations and ensure the product safety. On the other hand, the new knowledge and experience obtained from the large scale operations may further reveal the need of new understandings in certain details of the future scientific studies.

716310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
716310.value: A huge amount of sludge is generated from worldwide sewage treatment plants. A fast development of sludge incineration technology has resolved such environmental problem, but its ash residues are mostly buried in landfills, with a huge loss of metal oxides commonly presented in the ash. Moreover, toxic metals can leach out, causing further pollution. This study investigated the feasibility of beneficially incorporating the sludge incineration ash into the ceramic products and focused on the incorporation behavior of metals. The result has revealed that the toxic metals often found in the sludge ash, such as copper and zinc, can largely and reliably incorporated into the ceramic matrix via the spinel formation mechanism. Spinel is a type of minerals often includes aluminum and iron as the trivalent cations to further combine with the other toxic divalent cations. In this project, this scientific finding on spinel formation mechanism was also accompanied by a detail report on the processing parameters to contribute to their industrial applications in the future. The product safety and the physical properties of the products were all further confirmed in this project to ensure a safe and quality new waste-to-resource technology.

716510.label: Project Title(Chinese)
716510.value: 低功耗的FPGA可重構計算編譯器和操作系統支持

716510.label: Project Objectives
716510.value: To develop a high-level compiler techniques that automatically infer different compute architectures for different sections of the program depending on application requirements and the underlying OS and hardware facilities. To develop operating system support that will facilitate run-time reconfiguration of FPGA on a per-application basis and maintain seamless integration with the rest of the computer system. To study power-performance trade-offs of different compute architectures using FPGA-based computing. To study the trade-offs in incorporating FPGAs into tightly-coupled computer core with respect to power-performance of the system.

To develop operating system support that will facilitate run-time reconfiguration of FPGA on a per-application basis and maintain seamless integration with the rest of the computer system.
To study power-performance trade-offs of different compute architectures using FPGA-based computing.
To study the trade-offs in incorporating FPGAs into tightly-coupled computer core with respect to power-performance of the system.

716510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
716510.value: Over the past decade, the performance of computer systems has largely been limited by their power consumption. Sometimes referred as the "power wall," the fact that microprocessor designs can no longer rely solely on the increase in silicon speed for performance improvement has inspired researchers to turn to alternative architectures for computations, such as the use of multi-core processors, general-purpose graphics processing units (GPGPUs), as well as field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Among the three, computing using FPGAs provide researchers unique opportunities to develop highly optimized compute architectures on a per-application basis via post-fabrication reconfigurations. By taking advantage of the flexibilities of these FPGA-assisted reconfigurable computers, researchers have demonstrated that two to three orders of magnitude improvement in performance can be achieved at a fraction of the power consumption when compared to a conventional processor system. As such, FPGAs have provided a new dimension in the power-performance trade-off space that is pressingly needed for the upcoming power-efficient high-performance computing regime. The aim of this project is thus to study systematically the effectiveness of the use of reconfiguration in FPGA-assisted computer systems in providing power-efficient high-performance computing capabilities, with a focus on the interaction between the compiler and the run-time operating system. A new way of computing will be explored in which applications may execute on either a CPU or an FPGA during run-time. Performance alone will not be the only criteria that initiate such FPGA off-loading. Instead, power consumption as well as performance will together form the basis for most compile-time and run-time OS scheduling decisions. High-level compilation techniques required to facilitate such computing paradigm will also be investigated. At the end of the project, we expect that by fully exploiting the use of reconfiguration in high-performance computing, a 10x improvement in power-performance ratio can be achieved when compared to conventional multi-core processor systems. 在過去的十年中，計算機系統性能在很大程度上受到其功耗限制。因此，現代的微處理器已不能再單靠增加芯片速度來改善性能。研究人員正轉向使用其他不同的計算處理器，如使用多核心處理器，通用的圖形處理單元（GPGPUs），以及FPGA。 在三個之中，計算機研究人員利用FPGA提供獨特的機會來開發高度優化的計算架構上的每個應用程序的基礎上通過後製作的重新配置。隨著有CPU和FPGA混合技術的系統日漸成熟，使用FPGA在高性能計算機的情況也在不斷擴大。由於FPGA能透過其靈活性來為每個應用程序提供最適用的計算機設計，FPGA無疑提供了一個計算機耗電控制的新層面。這在未來高性能低功耗的計算機設計上將會起上不可取代的地位。 這個項目的目的是要研究FPGA和CPU之間的相互作用對編譯器(compiler) 和作業系統(operating system)的影響。我們期望通過充分利用FPGA和CPU之間的系統重新配置來達到性能和功耗的最佳平衡。對比於傳統的多核心處理器的系統，我們期望在新的編譯器和作業系統的幫助下性能與功耗比能有最少十倍的進步。

716510.label: Realisation of objectives
716510.value: The project objectives originally set out have generally been met. Power efficiency of FPGA-based systems have been studied and compared against the use of GPUs as accelerators. For objective 1, a high-level FPGA design methodology called QuickDough, which utilizes a coarse-grained reconfigurable array overlay has been developed. The QuickDough compilation framework enables rapid development of accelerators with difference architectural parameters. Taking advantage of this, an extensive study on the relationship between power-efficiency and architecture design has been performed. For objective 2, a run-time system has been developed to allow easy deployment of the compiled overlay and manage the hardware/software communication. It coordinates the execution of the accelerator and synchronizes data in the accelerator buffers with the rest of the system. Furthermore, to facilitate efficient communication between CPU and FPGA, a direct virtual memory system has been developed for the FPGA. This virtual memory system allows FPGA accelerators to access the host virtual memory directly. Operating system kernel running on the CPU, in coordination with a micro-kernel running on the FPGA, facilitates seamless address translations. This system will help future development of QuickDough. Finally, for objective 3 and 4, the earlier work in this project that focuses on medical ultrasound imaging has already laid the foundation of an all-rounded and systematic power-efficiency study. Current implementation of QuickDough has already illustrated the power-efficiency of FPGA compared to a pure CPU-based system in a number of benchmark programs. When combined with the rapid development capability of QuickDough , it is expected that the power-efficiency advantage of FPGAs will eventually enable a new generation of portable, high fidelity medical ultrasound devices.

716510.label: Major findings and research outcome
716510.value: The major outcome of this project is the design and implementation of the QuickDough compilation framework. As part of the early study, an elaborated architectural power-efficiency study using a medical ultrasound application as a driver was conducted. Finally, a virtual memory system for FPGA has also been developed. The developed framework called QuickDough is a rapid compilation for FPGA-based accelerator systems. Given a high level description of a user application, it generates both hardware and software components of the target system automatically. It builds upon the foundation of a previous work developed by the PI to provide seamless integration between software and hardware. A run-time system was developed to manage data communication and execution of FPGA accelerator. By using a soft coarse-grained reconfigurable array SCGRA as an overlay, more than 100x improvement in compilation time as been demonstrated at comparable performance and power consumption as custom-made accelerator. Compared to the software solution, more than 10x improvement in performance has be observed. A manuscript describing the results of QuickDough is in its final stage to be submitted to the ACM transactions on reconfigurable technologies. Furthermore, QuickDough will be available online as an open source compilation framework for FPGAs. To facilitate future expansion of QuickDough, a virtual memory system has been developed in this project. The system includes both OS kernel support and a small hardware micro-kernel on the FPGA that coordinates address translations. A preliminary version of the work has been demonstrated at the 2013 International Conference on Field Programmable Technologies (FPT’13) and published in the corresponding proceeding. Finally, the early design space exploration on medical imaging has opened an exciting avenue for accelerating next-generation ultrasound imaging systems. These works have been published in major periodicals including the IEEE Micro. This work also serves as a foundation for further research collaboration with Dr. Alfred Yu of University of Hong Kong. The work on QuickDough has also lead to further collaboration with Prof. Guy Lemieux of University of British Columbia on rapid overlay synthesis. A book project is also underway that will focus on advanced FPGA design methodologies for software designer.

716510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
716510.value: The QuickDough framework developed in the project has laid an excellent foundation that facilitates future research. One enhancement that will greatly assist users in developing FPGA accelerators is to investigate the use of a fully automatic parameter tuning facility in the framework. This project has exposed the vast design space and power-performance of FPGA accelerators. As a result, a fully automated framework that determines the set of optimal parameters from user’s specification will be an excellent future enhancement. Furthermore, to facilitate acceleration of complex applications with multiple compute intensive sections, another planned future enhancement is to allow the reuse of the SCGRA overlay during run time through in-system reconfiguration. Finally, once the automatic customization framework determines a new overlay configuration, it remains a big challenge to physically implement this overlay on the FPGA. For that, a collaboration work with Prof. Guy Lemieux of UBC, Canada is planned to develop a rapid overlay implementation tool.

716510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
716510.value: Power-efficiency of a system refers to the amount of energy required to perform certain computation. Improving power-efficiency of a system not only reduces the cost of carrying out the computation, but also improves system reliability and helps make the computing systems more sustainable for the environment. FPGAs are devices that perform computation in ways that are different from conventional computers, giving them potentially much more power-efficient than conventional computers. Unfortunately, using FPGAs in combination with conventional systems is non-trivial. They are very difficult to program and the compilation process is tedious and error-prone. Also it is generally unclear how power consumption and performance can easily be trade-off against each other in an FPGA based system. The merit of this project is that the QuickDough compilation framework greatly improves the speed for compilation FPGA accelerators by more than 100 times. The rapid compilation speed and the special overlay architecture makes it possible to quickly explore different implementations of the same design on the FPGA. As a result, it enables a new generation of tools to further enhance power-efficiency of FPGA-based computer systems in the future.

717110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
717110.value: In Hong Kong, the vibration effect of tunnel blasting to slope stability is often limited to an empirical peak particle velocity (PPV). It controls the explosive charge weight and thus the rates of tunnel advancement. The allowable values generally used in Hong Kong are unduly overly conservative as observed in the industry. The 2007-08 Policy Address sets out the blueprint to undertake 10 Major Infrastructure Projects to promote Hong Kong's economic growth in the next decade. One of the major projects, the Lai Chi Kok Transfer Scheme, is to alleviate the flooding by the construction of a drainage tunnel to intercept the surface run-off at the upstream and to discharge them directly to the harbor. The objective of this research is to obtain field vibration data during the blasting of this tunnel. With the use of an advanced finite element program that considers the dynamic properties of the soil material, the attenuation constants of these blasts can be derived reliably so that the vibration effects to nearby slope stability can be determined. Based on the findings of this research, there is a great potential to relax the vibration limits currently adopted for slope in Hong Kong, thus improving the efficiency of blasting and shortening the construction time. 隧道內爆破能引起震動。在香港, 此震動對邊坡的影响往往是用PPV來估算。它控制了炸藥的使用量, 從而影响開挖的進度。工程界一般認為香港爆破炸藥的使用量是過份保守, 拖慢施工進度。 2007-2008年, 香港政府于施政報告中推出十大基建項目的藍圖, 以便促進香港未來十年的經濟發展, 其中一項目是荔枝角雨水轉運計劃, 攔截上游的雨水, 直接排放出大海, 以便緩解水淹的威脅。 本研究項目, 依托于此轉運計劃, 採集爆破引發震動的數據, 結合有限元程序, 對邊坡的影响進行分析。有限元程序將考慮土的震動材料參數和衰減常數等等。 通過此研究, 有可能放寛震動極限, 提高爆破的效率和施工進度。

717110.label: Realisation of objectives
717110.value: A review on papers, reports and design codes on blasting was conducted and completed (Objective 1) The review has identified the state-of-the-art of blasting operations and approaches for predicting ground vibration due to blasting in various types of engineering projects, such as tunneling, building and bridges etc, and helped in formulating the study plan of the subsequent phases of the project (Objective 2). To carry out the second phase of the project, it is necessary to identify a tunnel project site which could be used as the monitoring site so that one can collect first hand information on the ground vibration due to blasting. It is only through the assistance of the Mr Joseph Lo (a Co-investigator of the project) that we were able to identify a suitable site in Lai Chi Kok and we obtained the clearance from various parties; namely the client (Government), contractor and consultant), to carry out the instrumentation and measurement. The time taken for the arrangement was much longer than expected. One of the difficulties is the coordination among the various parties so that the construction of the tunnel will not be affected. Only through the concerted effort of the various parties, we were able to secure over a thousand ground vibration records (Objective 3). To supplement the data collected in the Lai Chi Kok, we were also able to obtain blasting records of the Anderson Quarry with the assistance of Dr Richard Pang (a Co-investigator of the project). These data provided useful information on the transmission of ground vibration in slopes and they, representing open blasting, were analyzed together with those obtained from the Lai Chi Kok site, which was a typical case of confined blasting in tunnel. Based on the collected data, a critical review of the methods that are commonly adopted in the prediction of the ground vibration was carried out. Furthermore, formula taking into account the rock quality was also proposed. Recommendations on the design formula were made. To improve the accuracy and reliability in the prediction, a new probability approach based on the Bayesian method was proposed. Such an approach can not only be used to derive the design parameters for predicting the ground vibration, but it can also quantify the uncertainties in the parameters and the design formula (Objective 4). A spreadsheet programme was developed to assist the engineers in adopting the new design approach (Objective 7). A PhD student, Miss Zhou Jianmei was recruited in 2012 to work on the numerical modeling of the blasting process. She has attempted to use AutoDyn, Oasys-SIREN and FlAC in simulating the ground vibration propagation and attenuation. The effects of the ground vibration on slopes were also studied. The results of her study will be reported in her thesis (Objectives 4 and 5). The findings of the project have led to the publication of two papers in international journals and two conference papers (Objective 6). In conclusion, the objectives of the original applications have been achieved.

717110.label: Major findings and research outcome
717110.value: A comprehensive literature survey of the state-of-the art of the blasting operation, in particular with reference to the current local practice, was conducted and it was reported in the final year project report of Mr Lee Chi Ho and the dissertation of Miss Chan Suet Ying (Section 10). Permission was obtained to carry out the field monitoring of blasting in the Lai Chi Kok Transfer Station (Project A) with the assistance of Mr Lo Joseph Yiu Chung, a Co-investigator. Four geophones (two embedded into the slopes and two mounted on the slope surface) were installed to measure the ground vibration (in blasting engineering practice, vibration is described by the peak particle velocity, that is PPV) during the blasting carried out at the intake shaft and adit. A total of 1386 monitoring records were collected and analyzed. Furthermore, 2477 ground vibration data due to blasting activities at the Anderson Road Quarry (Project B) collected by the Geotechnical Engineering Office were also analyzed so that a comparison of the magnitude of the ground vibration of confined blast (Project A) and open blast (Project B) could be made. In general, the PPV in open blast is higher. Furthermore, the project has also assessed the accuracy of the three commonly adopted methods (square root scaling, cubic root scaling and multiple regression) in predicting the vibration and concluded that the cubic root scaling can fit the data much better than the other two. The findings were reported in Miss Chan’s dissertation. Taking into account the rock quality, an empirical relation in term of the Rock Mass Rating (RMR) was also proposed to predict the ground vibration (Attachement #4). Nevertheless, it is also noted that ground vibration is affected by other site specific parameters such as geology, type of explosive, and delay time. Therefore, it should be more appropriate to determine the site-specific coefficients so that one can predict the ground vibration with higher confidence. However, the vibration records can only be gradually collected in accordance to the progress of the project. In our project, a probabilistic-based design approach using site-specific vibration records was developed to overcome the difficulties of not having sufficient data in the early stage of the project. Reliable confidence level of PPV can be established by using a simple spreadsheet without the needs of any add-on tools. The method can be easily applied to predict the PPV. The findings of the study were reported in Attachment #1, Attachment #2 and Attachment #3. The project has provided the training ground for both undergraduate and postgraduate students. Mr Lee Chi Ho, an undergraduate student, participated in the early stage of the Lai Chi Kok project and he was mainly responsible for the instrumentation and collection of the blasting data. Miss Chan Suet Ying, who is an engineer with the Geotechnical Engineering Office, completed her MSc dissertation on this subject. Another research student, Miss Zhou Jianmei, is carrying out finite element modeling of the ground vibration transmission and the applications of finite element model in predicting ground vibration. She is expected to complete her study in 2015.

717110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
717110.value: Considerable data have been acquired by various parties in our infrastructure projects and they are valuable information for improving our prediction of the ground vibration due to tunneling activities. In addition to the blasting, ground vibration can also be induced by other construction activities (tunneling boring, driving of piles, construction of diaphragm walls and sheetpile walls) and the vibration can be as high as that caused by blasting in tunnels. Unfortunately, most of data are kept confidential. If these data can be made public, a comprehensive study can be carried out and a better model in predicting the level of vibration can then be developed. A survey can also be carried out to find out (1) the effect of the vibration on buildings and other engineering structures; and (2) the acceptance level of vibration of the public. Such a study can help to rationalize our design code which is reckoned as over-conservative. Another area which is worth exploring is the optimization of the blasting process. The optimization parameters include charge weight, delay time, drill hole pattern, construction time as well as the spoil removal process etc.

717110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
717110.value: Blasting is one of the common methods used in tunnel project and vibration induced by it is not only the concern of engineers but also the general public as it will cause nuisance to daily life. Various means have been used to predict the ground vibration but the complexity of the problem have rendered it impossible to have a reasonably accurate prediction. Therefore, rather conservative approaches have been adopted in the design. In this project, the accuracy attained by various commonly adopted approaches in estimating ground vibration have been assessed by using the field data collected in both open as well as confined blasting projects. Furthermore, a probabilistic approach is also proposed to derive the site-specific design parameters using data collected at the early stage of a project. It has demonstrated that the proposed method can resolve the underestimation problem. As a result, the construction cost can be reduced and the efficiency in tunneling can be improved. The proposed approach can be easily conducted using spreadsheet calculation without any additional tools and therefore it is particularly welcome by practicing engineers.

717510.label: Project Title(Chinese)
717510.value: 連續時間編碼放大顯微鏡技術(STEAM)的發展—用於高速生物影像拍攝的新工具

717510.label: Project Objectives
717510.value: High speed optical microscopy has been an important but challenging area to study dynamical processes, especially non-repetitive transient phenomena. Examples are the spatiotemporal study of biochemical waves in cells/tissues [1-2], and high-throughput cell characterization (e.g. flow cytometry [3-4]). However, conventional CCD/CMOS imagers, the major workhorse in microscopy [5-7], are incapable of capturing fast dynamical processes with high sensitivity and resolution. This is mainly due to the fundamental trade-off between sensitivity and frame rate – at high frame rates, fewer photons are collected during each frame – a predicament that affects virtually all optical imaging systems. This project aims to develop a new high-speed imaging tool that is able to overcome this limitation. The proposed imaging system is built on the recent demonstration of an entirely new imaging modality by the PI and co-workers that has established the world record for frame rate (> millions frames per second) and sensitivity (with image amplification in the optical domain) for continuous real-time imaging, called Serial Time-Encoded Amplified Microscopy (STEAM) [8-9]. It encodes the image onto the spectrum of a laser pulse and then converts the spectrum into an optically-amplified time-domain serial data. This allows us to capture images with a single-pixel detector, eliminating the need for the CCD/CMOS imagers and their associated trade-off between imaging sensitivity and speed. Specifically, we aim to: • Develop the amplified dispersive Fourier transform (ADFT) technique in near infra-red (NIR) – Amplified dispersive Fourier transform (ADFT) is a powerful technique which was originally developed for ultrafast real-time spectroscopic measurements with spectral acquisition rate of >MHz, a speed not achievable with conventional spectrometers [10-12]. It is the central element enabling ultrafast imaging in STEAM. ADFT has been demonstrated mainly in the wavelength range of ~1500 nm, we here, in contrast, plan to develop a new ADFT system operating in the shorter wavelength range (~700–900nm). It is well-known to be the preferable working regime, compared with the 1500-nm range, for biomedical applications because of the considerably less optical loss (and the associated sample heat-up/damage) due to water absorption [13-14] and the higher achievable diffraction-limited spatial resolution in microscopy [7]. • Develop the STEAM systems in NIR– Another key feature in STEAM is the mapping of the image into the spectrum of the optical pulse, i.e. spectrally-encoded imaging [15-19]. The spectrum, which is encoded with the image, can thus be measured by ADFT, allowing unprecedented imaging speed. We will design and build the spectrally-encoded imaging system in NIR range. As a result, combining ADFT with this spectrally-encoded imaging technique, we will develop a new STEAM system operating in NIR range with improved image quality in contrast to the prior proof-of-principle demonstration [8-9], and with high-speed (up to MHz) and sensitive imaging (with image amplification in the optical domain) capabilities. • Explore the potential applications of STEAM – The above prototype of STEAM, in its native form, is essentially a type of reflectance confocal microscopy (RCM) which has been extensively used in numerous non-invasive, label-free, in-vivo bio-imaging applications such as diagnosis of skin tumors [20-22]. However, its imaging speed has to compromise the weak detection sensitivity, which is limited by the weak back-scattered light (< few %) from the biological tissue. Hence, STEAM can offer orders-of-magnitude improvement in imaging speed and sensitivity in these applications. We will also investigate the potential of STEAM in other more compelling applications. One example is the combination of STEAM and quantitative phase microscopy (QPM). QPM has been proven to be a powerful technique to provide quantitative evaluation of cellular morphology and function at nanometer scale without the need for any cell preparation or using exogenous labels[23-27]. Hence, such a combined system could impact imaging flow cytometry applications, which demand rapid, high-throughput and quantitative characterization of different cells, e.g. circulating tumor cells [28].

717510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
717510.value: 光學顯微鏡技術是生物醫學上不可或缺的診斷工具，在解開生物組織和細胞複雜性、多樣性和生理過程方面，推動重大進展。儘管目前大部份有關光學顯微鏡技術的研究均過分著重提高空間解析度，但改善時間解析度從而有助研究動態過程（特別是非重複性瞬變現象）亦同樣重要。 然而，顯微鏡技術中的主要元件—傳統電荷耦合元件(CCD)和互補金屬氧化物半導體元件(CMOS)均未能以高敏感度和解析度捕捉快速動力過程，這主要是由於敏感度與幀率之間的取捨，如幀率較高，每個畫面所收集的光能則會較少，差不多所有光學影像系統均陷於這個兩難的情況。 我們的目標是基於首席研究員及其同工最近展示的全新影像技術，開發出一種新型超高速和敏感的影像系統。該全新影像程式名為「連續時間編碼放大顯微鏡技術」(STEAM)，其幀率和敏感度為連續實時影像的全球記錄。這個方向採用光學影像放大技術和其他新發明，克服上述有關影像敏感度與速度之間的取捨問題，透過以單像素偵察器捕捉影像，從此無須再依賴CCD/CMOS影像系統，突破其相關速度限制。在此以其原始形式開發的STEAM原型，可在應用於多種臨床用途的非入侵性活體反射共焦影像技術中發揮重要作用，例如監察對激光手術等治療的快速反應。 我們亦會基於STEAM原型研究將STEAM結合定量相位顯微鏡技術的可能性，旨在提供納米定量細胞資料，而無需任何細胞準備或使用外源標籤。此結合系統將具備高速及高容量（定量）影像拍攝能力，為達到生物醫學中快速、高通量、敏感、定量和免標籤的細胞影像技術和表述（例如流式細胞儀）奠定路向。

717510.label: Major findings and research outcome
717510.value: We have successfully established the first iTEM system which could perform high- resolution and ultrafast quantitative phase imaging for biomedical applications, especially tissue-wide and single-cell imaging applications. We have published over 15 peer-reviewed publications, as well as over 30 international conference publications on the ADFT and iTEM techniques. Also we are the first group enabling ADFT operation in NIR which is significant as it opens up a new opportunity for ADFT to be utilized in a wide range of biophotonic applications. We are also the first demonstrating iTEM which shows sub-cellular resolution. We have established strong collaborations with medical colleagues, notably Prof. Godfrey Chan (Head, Department of Paediatrics & Adolescent Medicine) for working on minimal residual disease detection using our STEAM technology; Prof. George Tsao ( Head, Department of Anatomy) for exploring new high-speed imaging platform for cancer cell biology research.

717510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
717510.value: We will continue to develop the uniquely fast iTEM system and its variant configuration particularly in terms of improving the image resolution, specificity/sensitivity of single-cell analysis based on quantitative phase at such a high imaging speed. We will also explore the multimodal implementation to further advance the quantitative analysis capability, such as incorporating fluorescence detection in the iTEM system. And we will continue to explore the new applications of iTEM where high-throughput imaging or label-free single-cell analysis is critical.

718010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
718010.value: 三维最优Delaunay三角化的研究

718010.label: Project Objectives
718010.value: We will develop optimization methods for computing the ODT that are one order of magnitude faster than the existing method. These include the quasi-Newton method and sub-gradient method. We will study global search strategies for computing improved local minima in ODT computation. These include methods based on simulated annealing and particle swarming optimization. These global strategies will be integrated with local optimization methods for efficient and robust computation of ODT. Parallel implementation of these methods will be studied for further speedup. The ODT method has empirically been observed to deliver better performance in sliver suppression than other optimization-base methods, such as the CVT method. So far, this has only been explained by intuitive interpretations. We will aim to identify specific and definite causes to better explain this observed advantage of the ODT method. We will develop the theory of the general anisotropic ODT that accommodates any Riemannian metric, thus extending the current ODT formulation. In addition, efficient algorithms will be developed for computing high quality 3D anisotropic triangulations based on this new theory.
