718010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718010.value: High quality triangulation of 3D computational domains is highly demanded in numerical simulation and solving partial differential equations. An important and difficult problem in 3D triangulation is suppressing slivers, which are tetrahedral elements having small dihedral angles and thereby causing numerical instabilities. The 3D optimal Delaunay triangulation (ODT), proposed by Long Chen in 2004, has recently been shown in the literature to produce much fewer slivers than other optimization-based methods, such as the Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation method, thus suggesting that the ODT is a promising variational forumulation for computing high-quality 3D triangulation. In this project we will address two major problems that need be resolved for the further development of the ODT method. The first problem is the inefficient computation of the ODT. The existing method for ODT computation converges very slowly. Moreover, poor local minima are often produced due to the fact that the ODT energy function is nonconvex and nonsmooth. We shall explore global optimization methods and Newton-like methods to devise new algorithms for robust and efficient computation of high quality 3D ODT. The second problem is the lack of generality of the current ODT definition, which is limited to the isotropic case with constant vertex density and a special anisotropic case. We will study the theory of the general anisotropic ODT specified by a Riemannian metric and develop efficient methods for efficient computation of anisotropic 3D ODT.

718010.label: Realisation of objectives
718010.value: All the targets have been accomplished. The main results are summarized in our SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing and another paper in SIGGRAPH 2013 (ACM Transactions on Graphics).

718410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
718410.value: 基於策略性路徑選擇的行人流動態宏觀模型

718410.label: Project Objectives
718410.value: The first objective will be to develop a dynamic macroscopic pedestrian flow model with strategic route choice that integrates the exploratory and repetitive behavior of pedestrians in a walking facility. The second objective will be to investigate the analytical properties of the model developed to describe the qualitative behavior of a crowd. The third objective will be to develop efficient numerical schemes that can be used to solve the dynamic macroscopic model.
rows: The first objective will be to develop a dynamic macroscopic pedestrian flow model with strategic route choice that integrates the exploratory and repetitive behavior of pedestrians in a walking facility.
The second objective will be to investigate the analytical properties of the model developed to describe the qualitative behavior of a crowd.
The third objective will be to develop efficient numerical schemes that can be used to solve the dynamic macroscopic model.

718410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718410.value: Walking is a sustainable mode of transportation that is environmentally friendly, highly flexible, and healthy. It also serves as an interface with motorized transportation facilities. Given the importance of crowd management in this context, it is essential to have an understanding of the collective responses of pedestrians in a large crowd to help provide useful inputs for the design and management of walking facilities. The proposed research project will develop a dynamic macroscopic pedestrian flow model that captures the aggregate behavior of pedestrians and describes their movements within walking facilities. We will consider time-varying pedestrian demand and adopt a continuum modeling technique to describe pedestrian movement trajectories in the two-dimensional spatial domain. In a facility with a complicated geometry, it may not be feasible for pedestrians to obtain full information about operating conditions across the entire domain due to physical obstructions, taller neighboring pedestrians, and degrading visibility as they walk through the facility. We therefore expect it to be a challenging, yet rewarding, exercise to model pedestrians’ strategic route choice decisions in a way that captures their exploratory and repetitive behavior in a systematic and coherent framework. The problem will be formulated as an initial value problem with a set of partial differential equations that embed a multi-directional speed-flow-density relationship, which will be coupled with a day-to-day learning mechanism that updates the memory of pedestrians. Efficient numerical schemes will be explored to solve the model. 步行是一種可持續的運輸模式，環保，高度靈活而且健康。同時它還可以作為與機動交通設施的銜接。基於人群管理的重要性，對人流中行人的整體反應的認識，將有助于為行人設施的設計和管理提供有用的指標。擬議的研究項目將研發一個動態的宏觀行人流模型來捕捉行人的行為，并描述他們在行人設施中的運動。我們會考慮到行人需求隨時間的變化，并採用連續的建模方法來描述行人在二維空間中移動的軌跡。在結構複雜的設施中，行人個體因為物理上的障礙，如鄰近的較高的行人和能見度的降低，難以對整個區域的運營獲取全面的信息。因此我們認為，系統并連貫地通過捕捉行人探索性和重複性的行為，從而對行人的策略性路徑選擇建模，是富有挑戰性和研究意義的。首先，我們擬用一組偏微分方程把整個問題表述為一個初值問題。偏微分方程反映多方向的速度，流率及密度的關係，這也涉及到行人對路況不斷更新的認識。最後，我們會探索對模型求解的計算方法。

718410.label: Realisation of objectives
718410.value: To achieve Objective (1), the macroscopic variables of speed, density, and flow were measured to establish the fundamental diagram for pedestrian flows, which provided useful insights to the development of a dynamic macroscopic pedestrian flow model. Bi-directional and multi-directional pedestrian stream models that describe the interactions among pedestrians were constructed based on the Bayesian approach. The effect of visibility on route choice decisions of pedestrian was also studied using experimental approach. The pedestrian flow models with route choice that is based on the exploratory and repetitive behavior in a walking facility were first investigated separately, and then combined into a strategic route choice mechanism to better describe the movement pattern of pedestrians. To achieve Objective (2), the theoretical properties of the models were rigorously studied. Both hexagonal and rectangular cells that govern the pedestrian flow propagation on a two-dimensional surface were exploited. From an experimental dataset, empirical evidence for the look-ahead behavior of pedestrian flows was obtained. The lane formation phenomenon in pedestrian counter flow situation was also investigated based on symmetry breaking, which can be compared with the “optimal self-organization” mechanism in a natural physical system. These findings were used to describe the qualitative behavior of a crowd, and to establish efficient solution algorithms to solve the problem. To achieve Objective (3), computational schemes for the dynamic continuum models were developed. High order schemes based on finite difference method and iterative schemes for the construction of field potential function were established, which were shown to be effective and efficient solution algorithms for the dynamic pedestrian models developed in this study.

718410.label: Major findings and research outcome
718410.value: The macroscopic variables of speed, density, and flow were measured to establish the fundamental diagram for pedestrian flows [C1]. Both bi-directional [J9] and multi-directional [J11] pedestrian stream models were developed. For exploratory route choice behavior of pedestrians in a walking facility, the evacuation patterns were observed under different visibility conditions in experiments [J6], and a macroscopic model that describes the multi-directional movement pattern based on the discretization of the space into regular hexagonal cells was developed [J1]. For repetitive route-choice behavior of pedestrians, the concept of potential field approach was adopted, in which the route choice decisions are governed by a cost potential function based on pedestrians’ experience in the walking facility [J8]. Both exploratory and repetitive behaviors of pedestrians were then combined into a strategic route choice mechanism based on the local cellular automata decision rules in the exploratory context, and the cost potential function based on potential field approach in the repetitive context [J5, J10]. For pedestrian model properties, the collection, spillback and dissipation of a crowd under evacuation condition were investigated [J1]. From an experimental dataset, empirical evidence for the look-ahead behavior of pedestrian flows was obtained [J7], in which the velocity of pedestrians was found to be negatively correlated with not only the densities of the opposite-direction and the identical-direction pedestrians around them, but also the densities of the same-direction pedestrians ahead of them. The lane formation phenomenon in pedestrian counter flow situation was also studied [J3]. It was found that pedestrian lanes could be formed under symmetry breaking, and the underlying physics can be compared with the “optimal self-organization” mechanism, by which driven entities in an open system tend to minimize their interaction to enable them to reach some ordering state. For computational schemes, high order solution algorithms, which are based on the weighted essentially non-oscillatory scheme with a total variation diminishing Runge–Kutta time discretization, and a high-order fast sweeping method, were used to solve the set of partial differential equations. This algorithm was successfully used to solve the coupled system of conservation law and Eikonal equation efficiently for bi-directional pedestrian flow problems [J2, J4]. For the potential field cellular automata models, the solution was obtained by a set of decision rules applied locally, and an iterative scheme to construct the cost potential function [J5, J10]. These solution algorithms were shown to be effective and efficient.

718410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
718410.value: Addressing the need of sustainable transport development, expectations on the knowledge and practices for transportation engineering and planning related to pedestrian have increased remarkably. However, pedestrian is vulnerable road user and constitutes a significant proportion of road casualties in Hong Kong. With a population of 7.1 million and density of 6540 capita per square kilometer, pedestrian-vehicle conflicts are frequent in dense urban road network. In particular, signalized intersections have been the most probable vehicle-pedestrian conflicting spots. A proper account of the relationship between geometric design, road environment, signal timing plan, crossing behavior, and pedestrian accident and injury risk at the signalized intersection is therefore of paramount importance. To address this problem, it is essential to understand the walking behavior of pedestrians, and how they move and interact with pedestrians while crossing the junctions. The pedestrian flow model developed in this project offers a useful tool to simulate pedestrian movements. Together with field observations, we will be able to describe the movement patterns, such as the time required to cross a signalized junction when there are opposing crossing crowd. A research proposal on this subject, based on the preliminary findings of this project, was submitted for the application of the RGC GRF in the 2012-2013 exercise.

Given the importance of crowd management in this context, it is essential to have an understanding of the collective responses of pedestrians in a large crowd to help provide useful inputs for the design and management of walking facilities. The proposed research project develops dynamic macroscopic pedestrian flow models that capture the aggregate behavior of pedestrians and describe their movements within walking facilities. 718710.label: Project Objectives
718710.value: [An Auction-based P2P Microeconomic Framework]: We establish a microeconomic framework to model a typical block exchange based P2P system and investigate auction models that best characterize the content distribution among peers. Our preliminary study has revealed the lack of a well suitable auction model in the literature. We thus seek to develop a new model and design effective auction mechanisms that incentivize peer contribution for their own revenue maximization. [Bidding Strategies]: Based on the new auction mechanism, we design fully distributed buyer bidding strategies, that optimize the usage of individual peer's budget to maximize its perceived quality of experience, while desirably resulting in optimal block scheduling in the entire system. We prove the properties achieved by our strategies by applying techniques from mathematical optimization and mechanism design. [Localization Incentives]: We further design effective incentives to promote local neighbor selection, by which peers voluntarily prefer content exchange with peers within the same AS or ISP. Existing studies investigate locality-aware P2P designs without considering incentives for peers to do so. Our study seeks to provide such an incentive, that effectively reduces inter-ISP traffic without degrading peers' download performance. [Real-world Implementation and Deployment]: We implement the mechanisms in a full-fledged P2P on-demand streaming system. We will first evaluate the system on a high-performance server cluster by replaying traces collected from real-world P2P applications, and then deploy it in large scale onto the Internet.

718710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718710.value: The past decade has witnessed a surge on the number of large-scale peer-to-peer (P2P) applications over the Internet, e.g., BitTorrent, PPLive, Skype. The essence of P2P applications is to use regular users' upload bandwidth to alleviate the server load. As a most important paradigm for Internet applications, P2P will continue to thrive in the coming decades with three important trends: First, novel applications are continuously emerging (e.g., P2P interactive on-demand streaming, P2P 3D virtual environment), in which the rich content to be distributed demands more bandwidth and computational resources, that are too costly to be accommodated all by servers. Second, application designers tend to furnish their P2P client software with increasing end-user control (e.g., the amount of bandwidth to share), in the hope of attracting more users. Third, the large volume of P2P traffic has dramatically increased the traffic-relay cost at the Internet Service Providers (ISPs), leading to ISPs' throttling against P2P traffic; P2P applications are thus urged to localize their traffic within ISP boundaries, using locality-aware overlay designs. These trends are bringing significant challenges to future P2P application design: users may naturally wish to maximize their download but minimize upload contributions if given more control, compromising the foundation of a P2P system; on the other hand, new applications demand more resource contributions from the peers and also intensify the volume of inter-ISP traffic, making localized peering a necessity. Aiming at tackling all three fronts of P2P challenges, this project seeks to establish an auction-based microeconomic framework, to characterize the typical P2P content sharing and to design effective mechanisms such that: (1) peers are automatically willing to contribute their resources; (2) resource utilization in the system is optimized, leading to the best aggregated quality of experience at the peers; (3) peers are incentivized to localize their neighbor selection and the incurred inter-ISP traffic is minimized. Particularly, based on the similarity between commodity trading in a microeconomic system and the content exchange in a P2P application, we model a P2P microeconomic system with autonomous sellers and buyers equipped with budgets, and design a novel auction model with effective mechanisms to achieve the goals simultaneously and in a fully distributed fashion. Our model and mechanisms will be rooted in theories of mathematical optimization and mechanism design. We also seek to develop a full-fledged P2P on-demand streaming system using our mechanisms and deploy it in large scale in real world.

718710.label: Realisation of objectives
718710.value: We have fully achieved Objectives 1-3 in this project to 100%, and achieved Objective 4 to 80%. For Objective 1 and goals 1)-4) in Objective 2, we carefully designed a discriminative second price auction mechanism with seller reservation at the sellers, and a truthful start with iterative price discovery strategy for the bidders, which achieve desirable properties (incentive compatibility, social welfare maximization, Nash equilibrium). The results were reported in our journal publication in ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications and Applications [8(1) in Part C]. For goal 5) in Objective 2, we studied the sustainability of a credit-incentivized P2P content distribution system; the results received the Best Paper Award in HotPOST 2012 [9(1) in Part C]. For goal 6) in Objective 2, we designed optimal P2P VoD caching strategies to optimize content distribution as well as to minimize inter-ISP traffic, with results reported in a journal publication in Springer Peer-to-Peer Networking and Applications Journal [8(4) in Part C]. For goal 7) in Objective 2, we designed effective peer strategies for cross-channel and intra-channel collaborations, and reported results in Elsevier Journal of Tsinghua Science and Technology [8(2) of Part C]. As part of the work to achieve Objective 3, we studied locality-aware P2P living streaming and modeled the relation between streaming performance and traffic locality. Our results were given in a journal publication in Journal of Communications [8(3) in Part C]. As the other part of work to complete Objective 3, we designed an auction-based algorithm to motivate peers' voluntary ISP-aware peer selection, while maximizing the social welfare that considers both peers’ gain and inter-ISP traffic, with results reported in a HotPOST 2014 paper [9(2) of part C]. To achieve Objective 4, we implemented a prototype P2P VoD system with a complete peer client software and a complete tracker server program written in Java, and implemented the auction/bidding mechanisms among peers. We deployed the system onto our server cluster and used the deployment to test our algorithm in the HotPOST 2014 work under realistic settings. We are aware that the prototype software is yet to be further improved to a quality comparable to commercial P2P software, in terms of efficiency and bug-freeness in the parallel threads, to enable its large-scale deployment in the Internet. Due to the exhaustion of the project fund, we were not able to implement this further improvement, and look forward to doing so if additional funds become available.

718710.label: Major findings and research outcome
718710.value: Using P2P VoD streaming applications as examples, we carefully designed a discriminative second price auction mechanism with seller reservation at the sellers, and a truthful start with iterative price discovery strategy for the bidders. We rigorously proved that our design achieves a number of desirable properties: (1) the auction mechanism is incentive compatible, i.e., each seller has the incentive to apply it as its best strategy to maximize revenue, and is also incentivized to maximally contribute its upload capacity; (2) the bidding strategies are equilibrium strategies at the bidders, which can efficiently utilize a bidder’s budget and maximize its aggregate utility; (3) the social welfare is maximized in the equilibrium state, i.e., the aggregate satisfaction of the peers is maximized. The results were reported in journal publication 8(1) in Part C. Through investigation, we found goal 5) in Objective 2 is indeed very intriguing for separate, in-depth investigation: by modeling credit circulation in a credit-incentivized P2P market using a queueing network model, we showed that a stable job circulation state always exists and proved a sufficient and necessary condition for asymptotic budget condensation onto a small number of peers when the system has been running for a long time. This and other results (e.g., on initial budget assignment to avoid budget condensation) appeared in 9(1) in Part C. We designed optimal caching strategies for P2P VoD, that are proven to achieve the best tradeoff between server bandwidth consumption and inter-ISP traffic. The results appeared in journal publication 8(4) in Part C. When multiple P2P overlays are considered in multi-channel P2P VoD, we designed effective, fully distributed strategies for both cross-channel and intra-channel collaborations, such that the server cost can be reduced by up to 25% while high streaming qualities are guaranteed in the entire system. The results were in journal publication 8(2) of Part C. We mathematically characterized the relationship between the inter-ISP traffic and the streaming performance, and obtained the traffic volume when the best streaming performance is achieved and the streaming performance when minimum inter-ISP traffic is incurred. Our models provided intriguing insights on locality-aware P2P protocol design, which were given in journal publication 8(3) in Part C. We also designed an auction algorithm to motivate peer’s voluntary ISP-aware peer selection and implemented a P2P VoD system; its deployment on our server cluster under real scenarios validated the effectiveness of our algorithm (9(2) of part C).

718710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
718710.value: We hope to further improve the prototype P2P VoD software implemented with the microeconomic means (auction/bidding capacity) to a quality comparable to commercial P2P software, and then release it to the public. In this project, the goals on auction mechanism design, theoretical model and analysis have been fully achieved and the part left is Internet-scale deployment, which requires a high-quality software (efficient in large-scale systems, bug free with many parallel threads). We think the main obstacle is the fund to support manpower for this purpose, and are actively looking for additional funds to continue this part of the development.

718710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
718710.value: This project established an auction-based microeconomic framework to characterize typical P2P content sharing and designed effective mechanisms to incentivize peers’ voluntary resource contribution and locality-aware content downloading, to optimize resource utilization in the system and to minimize the incurred inter-ISP traffic, while guaranteeing the best quality of experience at the peers. Particularly, based on the similarity between commodity trading in a microeconomic system and the content exchange in a P2P application, we modeled a P2P microeconomic system with autonomous sellers and buyers equipped with budgets, and designed novel auction mechanisms to achieve the goals simultaneously and in a fully distributed fashion. The framework studied in this project can serve as the foundation to develop high-performance P2P applications, with full peer contribution incentives, optimal resource scheduling, and high network efficiency. In this sense, it is well suitable for implementing next-generation P2P applications with full user control, intense resource demand, and stringent QoS requirement, and can also be applied to enhance the current P2P applications. The P2P on-demand streaming software that we implemented in this project, can serve as a prototype for implementing next-generation, commercial P2P systems equipped with microeconomic means.

719810.value: To determine the concentrations and removal efficiencies of common PCPs in two STPs of Hong Kong: The removal efficiency of a PCP depends highly on the operations and designs of STPs and may be affected by many factors. To investigate the anaerobic biodegradation/biotransformation of the PCP which tend to accumulate in sludge: PCP adsorbed by sludge will eventually enter the anaerobic digester of STPs. In this project, PCP-degraders will be isolated and characterized using DNA-based methods.

719810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719810.value: As a large group of emerging pollutants in various water environments, pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs), which are widely used to protect and improve human health, have recently drawn great attention all over the world. Within PPCP, personal care products (PCPs) have not been studied as frequently as pharmaceuticals. However, after entering the environment, PCP may have either serious long-term ecological effect even at very low concentration levels (ng/L or μg/L) or short-term effect at relative high levels (mg/L). The removal of PCPs in sewage treatment plants (STP) is of particular concern because sewage is one of the main disposal and exposure routes. The elimination of a PCP depends highly on the operating conditions and designs of STPs, and may be affected by many factors. Thus, it is hard to draw solid conclusions about PCP removal efficiencies based on a few samplings, even using composite samples. A few pioneer works using well-controlled laboratory reactors have been conducted to study two major elimination mechanisms in the activated sludge process, i.e. biodegradation/biotransformation and adsorption, of some PCPs at environmental relevant concentrations. PCPs adsorbed by sludge will eventually enter the anaerobic digester of STPs. But, little is known about their behavior and fate in the anaerobic digester. In Hong Kong, our preliminary analytical results showed high concentrations of 6 PCPs, including 3 preservatives (methyl paraben, ethyl paraben and propyl paraben), 2 UV filters (2, 4-dihydroxybenzophenone, benzophenone-3) and 1 antimicrobials (triclosan). Limited information is available about their biodegradation/biotransformation and adsorption in activated sludge and anaerobic digestion processes. In this project, comprehensive research on their removal efficiencies in STPs will be carried out by following a well planned sampling program of influent/effluent of STPs, and using laboratory scale activated sludge and anaerobic digestion reactors. Additionally, the removal mechanisms, i.e. biodegradation/biotransformation and adsorption, will be investigated using laboratory scale reactors (batch and continuous). Degrading microorganisms will be isolated from activated sludge and anaerobic digestion sludge, and characterized using DNA-based molecular techniques. 作为一类新兴污染物，个人护理品近来引起研究者的密切注意。因为污水是此类污染物主要的来源,因此其在污水处理中的去除特别受到关注。这种去除受很多因素影响，包括污水处理厂的设计和运行条件等。因此，很难根据一些随机或复合采样就此类污染物的去除效率得出确凿的结论。一些研究先行者使用受控的实验室反应体系研究了这些化合物在活性污泥过程中的二种主要去除机制，即生物降解转化和吸附。被污泥吸附的个人护理品会最终进入厌氧污泥消化池，目前对它们在厌氧消化过程中的行为和归宿所知甚少。在香港，我们的初步分析结果显示城市污水中至少有六种个人护理品，包括三种防腐剂，两种抗紫外线药剂和一种杀菌剂。对于它们的生物降解转化和吸附，目前的认知十分有限。本项目将利用系统的采样结果调查它们在污水处理过程中的去除效率，在实验室采用批式反应器研究活性污泥和厌氧消化工艺过程中的生物降解和吸附，此外还将分离降解个人护理品的微生物，并利用基于DNA的分子技术鉴定此类微生物。

719810.label: Major findings and research outcome
719810.value: This study firstly developed a rapid and sensitive method for trace analysis of 19 pollutants using solid phase extraction (SPE) and ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS), and detected the concentrations of selected pollutants in Hong Kong municipal wastewater using the established methods. Their concentrations ranged from 5.9 to 1864.9 ng/L in influent and from 2.6 to 1307.4 ng/L in effluent. Additionally, we found suppressive matrix effects in analysis of selected pollutants in three different matrices, i.e. activated sludge, sterile activated sludge and influent. These matrix effects were quantitatively evaluated for more accurate investigation of the removal mechanisms of pollutants in the activated sludge process by batch experiment after correcting matrix effects by post-spiking of selected pollutants. With these established methodologies, this study also conducted laboratory experiments on adsorption and biodegradation/biotransformation of the pollutants in activated sludge treatment process and anaerobic sludge digestion. After correcting the matrix effect by spiking known amount of pollutants, experimental data from batch experiments elucidated that the removal of pollutants in the activated sludge process was mainly by biodegradation while the contribution from the adsorption, hydrolysis and volatilization can be neglected. Three compounds (SDZ, SMX and ROX) were partially biological transformed by ~40%. Higher biodegradation rate (51.9%) was observed on DCF while the other two compounds, TMP and CBZ, showed recalcitrant to the activated sludge treatment. This study also characterized degrading microorganisms using DNA-based molecular methods and isolation approach. Especially, the molecular approaches used in microbial communities study have been optimized, including Biases during DNA extraction of activated sludge samples revealed by high throughput sequencing, 16S regions used in bacterial fingerprint profiling, Taxonomic precision of different hypervariable regions of 16S rRNA gene and annotation methods for functional bacterial groups in biological wastewater treatment, combined metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analysis of microbial structure and functions of activated sludge. Two isolates capable of aerobic degradation of SMX and SDZ were obtained from this system. The biodegradation of SMX/SDZ by acclimated microorganisms and two isolates from this enriched culture indicated that there are some bacteria in the nature which may degrade these pollutants. In addition, some relevant topics, including bulking/foaming bacteria, hydrophobicity of different bacteria and effect of pollutants to bacterial populations in the activated sludge were also studied. The above findings have provided novel insights into fates of pollutants in wastewater treatment plants and the relevant microbial populations in their biodegradation.

719810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
719810.value: The future development could focus constructing a pipeline for identifying unknown degradation products metabolites and further to revealing the pollutant biodegradation pathways, by combining traditional culture methods and in combination with next generation sequencing-based metagenomic/ and metatranscriptomic analyses is the major research technique route. This work can greatly help to characterize the functional degrading microorganism bacteria and profile the functional genes responsible for efficient antibiotics degradation, which will facilitate the establishment and optimization of the bioremediation applications for treating contamination. Degraders could be enriched in laboratory scale reactors and isolated using the culture method established before. Then, the degradation products of the selected pollutants will be characterized and identified using high-resolution liquid-chromatograph quadrupole time-of-flight mass-spectrum. The possible degradation pathways could be speculated and confirmed using the reference compounds. The whole genome of the isolated pure cultures will be sequenced using next generation high-throughput sequencing strategy to search for the genes which are responsible for biodegradation of selected pollutants.

719810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
719810.value: As a large group of emerging pollutants in various water environments, pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs), which are widely used to protect and improve human health, have recently drawn great attention all over the world. Within PPCP, personal care products (PCPs) have not been studied as frequently as pharmaceuticals. However, there is growing concern that PCP pass through sewage treatment plants and enter the environment, and may either have serious long-term ecological effect even at very low concentration levels (ng/L or μg/L) or short-term effect at relative high level (mg/L). In this study, we developed a rapid, sensitive method for trace analysis of 19 pollutants, and detected the concentrations of selected pollutants in Hong Kong municipal wastewater. This study also conducted laboratory experiments on adsorption and biodegradation/biotransformation of these pollutants and further characterized degrading microorganisms using DNA-based molecular methods and isolation approach. Especially, the molecular approaches used in microbial communities study have been optimized. The above findings have provided novel insights into fates of pollutants in wastewater treatment plants and the relevant microbial populations in their biodegradation.

719910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719910.value: With the deregulation of power industry and the development of clean energy based distributed generation (DG) technologies, DG capacities installed in distribution networks could mitigate transmission line congestions and defer the investment of bulk power plants and transmission facilities. As well as the traditional generation expansion and transmission expansion, installation of DGs by the distribution company could be an option to serve load growth. The new challenges in a restructured power industry are 1) how to coordinate the conflicting investment interests of three investors: generation company, transmission company and distribution company; 2) how to consider the investment uncertainties and the impacts of strategic behavior of competing investors. In an electricity market, a high locational marginal price (LMP) indicates an insufficient power supply at the location. Electricity is transported from low LMP regions to high LMP regions (usually load centers), which may cause transmission congestions. The high LMPs at the interface of the transmission network and the distribution network provide investment incentives to the generation company, transmission company and distribution company. However, their investment interests are conflicting. The high LMPs would 1) induce a generation company to set up a power plant; 2) induce a transmission investor to set up a transmission line linking the distribution network with another low LMP node; or 3) induce the distribution company to set up distributed generation units. These three are competing investments and produce products that are “strategic substitutes”. When making its investment decision on capacity expansion, any of the three investment entities needs to consider the impacts of other entities’ strategic behavior. Besides the uncertainties of load growth and highly volatile electricity prices, all three investment entities are disclosed to the uncertainties / risks due to the unknown investment plan of other investors. For example, at the conception of a transmission project, the transmission company may not know the exact scheme of future generation expansion planning or the plan for DG installation. Meanwhile, the generation and DG investors may wish to keep the flexibilities (options) of trading electricity in other markets, or wish to avail of the flexibilities in changing the power plant types / fuels. In the proposed study, we will apply game theory and theory of real options to model the conflicting investment interests of three entities and the uncertainties in power system capacity expansion and investment. 隨著電力市場改革以及清潔能源技術的發展，越來越多的安裝於電力用戶側的分佈式電源和可再生能源將有助於減少輸電阻塞以及推遲大型發電廠和輸電設備的投資。安裝分佈式能源發電可以與傳統的發電容量擴展和輸電容量擴展一起作為應對負荷增長的解決方案。我們面臨的新的挑戰是，如何協調投資者在發電投資、輸電投資和分佈式電源投資中可能出現的利益衝突。 在電力市場中，由於受到輸電容量的約束，投資者會考慮在邊際價格高的地方投資建設發電容量、分佈式電源或者對輸電容量進行擴展。高電價可能導致 1）配電公司投資建分佈式發電容量；2）發電公司投資建新的大型發電廠；3）輸電公司建新的輸電線將低電價地區電力輸送到高電價地區。但是，這三種投資具有競爭關係，並有替代性。 我們的研究將採用博弈論和real options理論對三種投資建立數學模型，並考慮電力系統擴容中的不確定因素，輔助投資者作出最有利的投資決定。

719910.label: Realisation of objectives
719910.value: Capacity expansions in the power system are facing uncertainties / risks not only because of the volatility of electricity prices, but also because of the uncertainties of renewable energy generations and distributed generation installations. On the other hand, polices of carbon emissions and applications of new generation technologies will also affect the decision of capacity investment. To study the capacity expansion issue in power system, we first propose electricity market with renewable energy generations. Both energy market and reserve market are included in the model. By solving the optimization model, electricity prices, which are economic signals for investments, are obtained. On the other hand, the strategic gaming model is applied to simulate the strategic behavior of different market participants. Two-level optimization problems, the mathematical programming with equilibrium constraints (MPEC) are solved. Strategic investors can use the proposed models to obtain the equilibrium of generation and transmission investments, as well as the equilibrium of customers and distributed generations. Capacity investments in power systems are exposed to risks more than other financial investments. For example, uncertainties of renewable energy generations, emission control policies, adoptions of new generation technologies in the future, etc. We have proposed top down strategies for renewable energy investment, and also proposed to use financial instrument hybrid bond to hedge the risk. With regards to carbon emission and its impacts on capacity expansion, we have modeled electricity markets with different carbon reduction policies. The impacts of carbon trading and emission policies on electricity prices are simulated and studied. Capacity investors could refer to the simulation results when considering the uncertainties of emission policies and their risks to the investment. The proposed objectives in the proposal have been implemented. The research work and results have been published (or submitted) to several journals and conferences.

719910.label: Major findings and research outcome
719910.value: In paper [Journal 1], we modeled the electricity market with a significant number of wind producers. A two-stage stochastic programming problem is proposed. The first stage of the problem is the clearing of the market, and the second stage represents the system operation with a number of wind producing realizations. The energy and reserve are co-optimized, and prices are obtained for electricity and reserve. By using this model, the strategic behavior of generators could be considered in the market. The prices obtained could be used as the signal for the strategic gaming between generation and transmission. In paper [Conference 1], we further studied the strategic behavior of a reserve provider in the electricity market to compensate the uncertainties of renewable energy generations. To solve the two-level optimization problem, the mathematical programming with equilibrium constraints (MPEC) is solved. The strategic investors can use the model to obtain the equilibrium of generation and transmission investments considering price volatilities and wind uncertainties. In paper [Conference 2], we added loads and distributed generations in the above market model. The two-level optimization problem is converted to a single-level MPEC problem to obtain analytical results. By doing this, the strategic behavior of customers and distributed generations is taken into account in the equilibrium problem. In paper [Journal 2], a top down strategy is proposed for generation investment. The proposed method is used to identify investment opportunities. Renewable energy, as one of the common distributed generations, has been considered for its investment decisions. To consider the uncertainties of generation and transmission investment, we have discussed financing and risk management issues in paper [Journal 3] using a financing instrument, hybrid bond. In paper [Conference 4], different emission control policies and their applications in power system operations are discussed. The electricity market model including carbon emission trading is proposed and tested in the paper. The impacts of carbon reduction policies on power system operation and capacity investment are discussed and studied. The proposed model could help regulators and investors for decision making in new generation technologies. In paper [Conference 5], impacts of carbon emission polices on electricity markets and market prices are studied based on proposed two models. Market price is one of the important factors for investment decision making. By simulating electricity prices for different emission market mechanisms, the impacts of carbon policies on expansion investments could be estimated and simulated.

719910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
719910.value: The research work of the project could be further studied considering the adoptions of new generation technologies, and new emission trading mechanisms. New generation technologies provide opportunities to power industry. Investors need to study the impacts of new generation technologies on electricity market and prices before making investment decisions. On the other hand, emission reduction of power industry has become an important issue in recent years. New emission reduction policies and emission trading mechanism will affect the profits of generation and transmission expansions. The impacts of new emission control mechanisms on electricity market and capacity expansion need to be studied.

719910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
719910.value: The research work use mathematic models to include investment issues of generation expansion and transmission expansion. For a power system, the cost of facility expansion is high. Investors are facing many risks and uncertainties as power system operation itself is complicated. Optimal decision makings are needed for investors to consider risks caused by electricity price fluctuations, new generation technology adoptions, emission control policies, as well as the strategic behavior between investors. In this project, we use optimization model to model energy market, reserve market, emission policies, and strategic behavior, which are needed for the investor to make investment decisions. The proposed mathematic models will provide tools for the investor to study and simulate investment risks and find the way to hedge the risk.

740610.label: Project Title(Chinese)
740610.value: 電影中的音樂幻想與敍事機制

740610.label: Project Objectives
740610.value: To examine the relationship between narrative agency and music in cinema through the study of a strategic selection of seminal, well known films. To add one important dimension to our understanding of subjective narration in cinema. To suggest that the six chosen films, and many others like them, form a sub-genre defined by their nuanced and ambivalent representation of music listening and its impact on the lives of their characters. To offer one example of a mode of film criticism informed by musical expertise and thus help foster a dialogue between scholars in musicology and film studies. To gather the results of the research in a monograph for advanced students in music and film studies, scholars, and to be published by a university press.

740610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
740610.value: Music in cinema is more than pleasant background filler or entertaining diversion. One of its least recognised roles is to aid the viewer in his or her understanding of narrative agency. Whether told in words or moving images, every story, or narrative, involves an agent doing the telling, or narrator. Sometimes the presence of a narrator recedes in the background and determining who is doing the narrating, how, and why, is of little import for the enjoyment and appreciation of a film. At other times, however, it matters a great deal whether the information we are seeing and hearing, and how this information is presented, is to be ascribed to this or that character or, indeed, whether it can be ascribed to a character at all. My research projects aims to examine a number of films in which such ascription of agency is jeopardised unless one pays heed to the music and how it is used. In the film sequences I aim to examine, music is synchronised to a moment of fantasy, daydreaming or recall on the part of a character. Such music, I would like to argue, elevates him or her to the status of ‘sampler ‘ or ‘composer’ of not just the sounds, but the images of a film themselves. The primary goal of the project, then, is to redefine the nature of subjectivity in cinema so as to encompass a certain kind of use of music as an index of subjective narration. I will take six, strategically chosen case studies as focus, each study envisioned as an instance of film criticism through music. Taken together, the case studies will attempt to develop a mode of film criticism informed by musical expertise and thus galvanise cross-disciplinary dialogue and collaboration across fields of musicology and film studies. 音樂對於電影的作用遠不僅限於增添審美情趣或提升娛樂氛圍。其中，電影音樂 一個鮮爲人知的作用便是促使觀衆理解電影中的敍事機制。無論是以對話臺詞還是影 視畫面，每一個故事或事件，都具有某种元素扮演敍事者，行使敍事功能。在某些情 況下，敍事元素處於隱性狀態，由其它形式的顯性元素完成敍事過程。而敍事過程以 何種方式實現，則不會影響到電影欣賞本身的效果。但在另一种情況下，敍事元素在 極大程度上決定了視聽信息的傳遞，以及這些信息如何與角色對位，甚至從根本上決 定二者能否對位。本人的研究課題將以多部電影為實例，其中音樂的運用對角色對位 具有至關重要的作用。在本人擇取的案例分析中，音樂配置于迷幻的場景，如遐想， 或描摹某人的回憶。本人認爲，這種音樂的功能已超越了聲音概念的範疇，而是以電 影畫面“表現者”或“塑造者”的姿態出現。此項課題的目的為，重塑電影中主觀性 敍述的概念，將音樂的作用囊括于對電影主觀性敍事的研究中。本人將有目的地選取 六部影片片斷作爲案例分析的主體，通過音樂層面的分析，對影片進行研究和評論。 這項研究將重新審視電影評論的形式，以音樂專業性研究的視角對電影進行批判性的 評論，並全方位發展音樂學與電影學領域的交流，開展跨領域的學術對話。

740610.label: Realisation of objectives
740610.value: The project objectives have found realization in a number of articles on Wong Kar Wai's cinema for various anthologies (see items 9, 10 and 12 in my CV attached in Part C), as well as two chapters of my forthcoming monograph, *The Situated Listener* (OUP, 2015). These outcomes spring from and address the main subject of the proposal; they fulfill objectives 1-4; and they expand on some of the proposal's premises by incorporating questions about industry practices, intertextuality, and the study of spectatorship. Objective 5 could not be realized as a monograph on spectatorship and the psychology of attention (mentioned above) took shape in the meantime. While I was able to incorporate some of the research conducted through the grant into it, I resolved that the articles be published as self-standing publications in various anthologies. There are cases, moreover, in which the working out of my ideas, and my focus on certain genres and films, resulted in findings that could not be predicted at the proposal stage. So my work on such directors as Polanski, Lynch, and Fellini, and genres such as the thriller or the opera film, among others, found its way in publications on musical representation and opera, respectively (nos. 8 and 11).

740610.label: Major findings and research outcome
740610.value: The project yielded major insights on the relationship between music and character in cinema; in particular, the sustained study of Wong Kar Wai's films has brought to the fore a demonstrable link between music and a new, media-inspired "aesthetics of the self" in the form of imaginary, narcissistic self-portraits on the part of the characters of his films. This new aesthetics is influenced by all manner of media forms -- MTV, radio and TV advertising, the fashion show, to name a few -- and this has prompted me to suggest that the link between desire and image-making speaks very much to our time. Interspersed in the narrative, such audio-visual portraits complicate narrative agency in new, challenging ways, prompting me to coin the term' diffuse agency' and redefine 'auteurism' as the ability to speak on behalf of, as much as lending one's voice to, a film's characters. Key to the project was also a broader definition of the "image" as encompassing music and sound as much as visual information. In keeping with this premise, my investigation has taken me to examine the relationship between opera and film; for in opera the voice is an essential element of what we might call a composite 'iconography.' Similarly, I have looked at classical Hollywood as well as the film noir revival of the 1970s in search of a link between music and characterization.

740610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
740610.value: A potential area of further development of my ideas lies in a critique of the interactivity afforded by contemporary social media. This project identifies the cinema as one important source of the 'aesthetics of the self' that dominates image-making across the mediascape. The point goes beyond the suggestions of a genealogy. In drawing attention to cinema as a source of new media practices, and a resilient site in the creation and distribution of influential images, I wish to question the difference between so-called passive and interactive forms of leisure. I would like to ask whether much of what passes as the empowering nature of the internet serves, in fact, to reinforce the gulf that separates amateur from professional image-makers. Such a development would entail incorporating in-depth analysis of the difference -- or porousness -- between amateurism and professionalism in image-making today and a thorough analysis of the use of sound and music in social media platforms. Whether the findings will prove my working hypothesis or not, they will open up new avenues for the systematic analysis and interpretation of sound and music in social media.

740610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
740610.value: Knowledge that no one gains access to the images of ourselves we conjure in our daydreaming stimulates the creative instinct, and frees one from inhibitions: the narcissistic impulse toward implausibly flattering self-representations is thus given free rein. In my project, I show how music is often a constitutive element of such fantasizing. This is perhaps most clear in social networking sites, where users’ profiles use popular songs and all manner of musical interventions to boost the appeal of their – often very public – personal profiles. The transmutation of musical sounds into elements of an iconography, and the coalescing of the latter back into the former, is of the essence to self-presentation across the netscape, and points to a long-overdue redefinition of portraiture as a multimedia construct by the savvy media navigator. Yet far from uncovering an invisible, ‘truer’ layer of one’s psyche, the music often partakes of the construction of a cool, cosmopolitan, artsy, and winning self. These are images, to paraphrase Bogart's misremembered quote from 'The Tempest,' as the stuff delusional self-portraits are made of. Taking Wong Kar Wai's films as the main case study, this project locates one important source of this widespread phenomenon in the cinema.

741410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
741410.value: 從社會學分析中醫藥的生存和認受性

741410.label: Project Objectives
741410.value: To examine why medical doctors in China face a legitimacy crisis and how they attempt to sustain their legitimacy to gain social acceptance and credibility. To understand why patients are increasingly distrusting doctors and how their sense of distrust affect their interaction with doctors. To explore how legitimacy and professional authority and the poor doctor-patient relation are constituted by institutional, political, and cultural conditions. To build on existing institutional theories of legitimacy and professional authority to derive theoretical insights into their applicability to Asia in general and to China in particular, and to modify these theories for wider applications.

741410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741410.value: Since the World Trade Organization (WTO) enacted the Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) Agreement in 1995, domestic pharmaceutical companies in developing countries have been hit hard. China, a member of the WTO since 2001, is bound by the TRIPS Agreement and obligated to open its door to foreign pharmaceutical corporations. Without comparable capital and technologies, how are Chinese pharmaceutical businesses able to survive? Applying an institutional approach, this research is based on the premise that organizations require social acceptability and credibility (what sociologists call legitimacy), in addition to material resources and technical information, to survive and thrive. Three major types of legitimacy are identified: normative legitimacy that is based on social obligations; regulative legitimacy that relies on certification or accreditation; and cognitive legitimacy that draws on public and shared culture. The types of legitimacy that organizations bank on largely depend on their social environments. As such, this project asks the following questions: 1) What types of legitimacy do Chinese pharmaceutical businesses strive to establish? Is there a pattern of differences among different types of companies? If so, how do we explain the pattern? 2) What strategies do Chinese drug companies deploy to build their legitimacy? How are their strategies constituted by global, national, and regional institutional, political, and cultural conditions? 3) How and to what extent does legitimacy matter for the survival of Chinese drug companies? How does legitimacy interact with material resources and technical information in exercising its power? I will conduct comparative ethnographic case studies in Beijing and Guangzhou. These cities are chosen for their regional differences in institutional, political, and cultural factors. The studies will include one of each of the following types of company from each city: traditional Chinese medicine companies, large-scale state-run pharmaceutical companies, and recently established private drug companies. Data will be collected through participant observations, interviews, and content analyses of advertisements and company publications. Case-oriented comparative methods will be deployed for theoretical analysis of similarities and differences at both organizational and regional levels. This study contributes to understanding how indigenous industries and companies survive in the face of an influx of multinational industries and corporations. By focusing on the pharmaceutical industry, I hope to offer insights about alternative models for developing countries. Moreover, applying economic sociology to studying the pharmaceutical industry represents a novel theoretical approach. This study will contribute to contextualizing theories of legitimacy in global, national, and regional dynamics. 自1995年世界貿易組織（世貿）通過《與貿易有關的知識產權協議》起，發展中國家的製藥公司受到嚴重的打擊。2001年起加入世貿的中國，亦受條文的約束，必須開放國內市場讓外國藥廠進入。在資本和技術上都較外國藥廠落後的中國本地藥業，應如何在這個充滿競爭的市場下生存呢？ 從社會學角度分析，本研究認為機構要生存甚至成功，所需要的是社會的認受性和本身的可信性（社會學家稱之為正統性），輔以機構擁有的物質資源及資訊科技。本研究會討論三種的認受性，分別是以社會責任為要的規範性認受；依靠證書和驗證而建立的管制性認受；以及因公眾共享文化而成的認知性認受。社會環境是決定機構依賴哪種認受在市場發展的最重要因素。因此，本計劃提出以下的問題： 1）中國藥業建基於哪種認受？不同種類公司的取向有否差異？如有，我們又應該如何去解釋這個不同呢？ 2）中國藥業採用了什麼策略去建立其認受性？國際及國內環境、地區體制，政治及文化氣候如何影響這些公司訂定策略取向？ 3）認受性如何及在何等程度上對中國藥業的生存產生影響？認受性又如何與物質資源及資訊科技產生相互作用的影響力？ 本研究會在北京和廣州進行。这俩个城市在制度、政治和文化上都有差異的地方，適宜進行比較性人種誌個案研究。我會在兩地各取一傳統中藥公司，大型國營藥業及近年成立的私營藥品公司進行個案研究， 透過參觀察、訪問，以及對廣告和公司刊物進行內容分析，收集所需的資料和數據。 這研究旨在探討本土工業如何在跨國集團湧入的時代下生存。透過集中研究藥物工業，我期望能提供一些不同發展模式的方向予發展中國家。而且，以經濟社會學的角度分析藥物工業，是一個新穎的理論方式，有助認受性理論在全球化過程的運用。

741410.label: Realisation of objectives
741410.value: The objectives of this project were revised twice. The revisions were approved by the RGC on August 2012 and January 2014 respectively. As I explained in the Annual Progress Report, the latest revised objectives were to examine factors that constitute the deteriorating relationship between doctors and patients, and how both parties deal with the crisis. The scope of the study has expanded to include all medical practitioners in hospitals in urban areas, regardless whether they were trained in Chinese or Western medicine. The focus of the study has also shifted from doctors’ strategies to the interaction between doctors and patients. With these revisions, I am delighted to report that all of the revised objectives, to a large extent, have been achieved. However, because the research objectives were revised twice, it will take more time for the research outcome to appear in publications. Objective 1: This objective is achieved by papers 2.1 and 2.3 under section 6.1, and paper 1 under section 6.2. My study illustrates that doctors in China face a legitimacy crisis because of the commercialization of public hospitals, which is a result of the cutback of state subsidiaries. The doctors have become the scapegoats of the system and many of them resign themselves to a defensive medical practice, which has further intensified the problem. Objective 2: This objective is achieved by papers 2.1 and 2.2 under section 6.1, and papers 1 and 2 under section 6.2. The commercialization of public hospitals induces doctors to subject patients to unnecessary treatment and diagnostic tests in order to increase hospitals’ revenue. As a result, there is generalized distrust in hospitals and physicians from the public. Patients deal with the distrust problem by largely mobilizing their social networks to gain access to hospital care and by offering cash gifts to surgeons to “buy” better services. Objective 3: This objective is achieved by papers 2.1, 2.3 under section 6.1, and papers 2 and 3 under section 6.2. Doctors’ legitimacy crisis and the poor doctor-patient relation in China can be attributed to both institutional and cultural factors. Institutionally, the concept and practice of professionalism are historically underdeveloped in various professions. Culturally, the intensification of market reform since the 1990s has produced a general distrust societal climate in various aspects of life. Under this context, the corporatization of public hospitals, which structures doctors and patients’ interests into two opposing camps, becomes the immediate cause of the problem. Objective 4: This objective is achieved by papers 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 under section 6.1, and paper 3 under section 6.2. This project contributes to an institutional analysis of how hospital system and non-clinical factors shape doctors’ behaviors, and how patients’ sense of distrust and their cultural practices affect their interaction with doctors. By bringing in the Taiwanese case for comparison, it further contributes to identifying the specificities of the mainland Chinese case and defining the generalizability of the theoretical insights derived from the study.

741410.label: Major findings and research outcome
741410.value: 1. Data Collected: 1.1. From July 2011 to December 2014, a total of 188 face-to-face interviews (lasted for 1-3 hours) were conducted in Guangzhou, Beijing, Shanghai, Xi’an, Guiyang, and Taipei. Among which 105 were conducted by the PI. The interviewees include physicians, patients, patients’ families, medical students, nurses, hospital administrators, and social workers. During the same period, we conducted 86 participant observations in 14 hospitals in the five cities in mainland China. Among which 74 were conducted by the PI. At the same time, we carried out 50 informal chats with relevant informants in the field, and 38 of which were conducted by the PI. 1.2. To roughly assess the popularity of the use of social networks and cash gifts to obtain hospital care, the PI and her research assistant conducted non-random sampling surveys in Guangzhou, Beijing, and Shanghai from October 2012 to June 2013. Self-administered questionnaires were distributed to employees in 70 work units in these cities. We collected a total of 572 valid questionnaires (193 from Guangzhou, 192 from Beijing, and 187 from Shanghai). 2. Papers and Presentations: Three papers have been written to date. Two of the papers have been presented in various international conferences and they are now under final revisions before submitting to top-notch sociology journals for review. These papers include: 2.1 “A Market of Distrust”: It is listed as co-authored in order to acknowledge the contribution of the research assistant who helped to conduct some of the interviews. The paper is entirely written by the PI. I presented the first draft of this paper at an international conference in 2012. It was revised and presented at Yale and Cornell among others in 2013. I substantially revised it in 2014 and presented it in a number of universities in China and Taiwan. This paper is now under revisions and I plan to submit it to American Journal of Sociology (impact factor 4.045 in 2013, ranked No.2 in all sociology journals) for review in August 2015. 2.2 “Strong-Tie Chains and Generalized Exchange”: The first draft of this paper was presented at two international conferences in 2013. It was revised in 2014 by adding in data collected up to August 2013. More data was further collected in 2014 and it is now under final revisions for submitting to American Sociological Review (impact factor 4.266 in 2013, ranked No.1 in all sociology journals) for review in June 2015. 2.3 “Institutional Scapegoat”: The outline of this paper was presented at two international conferences in 2014. The draft was finished in January 2015, and it was accepted to be presented at the international conferences of the American Sociological Association and the European Sociological Association respectively in August 2015. The draft is still very rough at the moment and it will be substantial revised based on the feedback gathered from the upcoming presentations. I plan to submit it to Sociology of Health and Illness (impact factor 2.014 in 2013) for review in 2016.

741410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
741410.value: I just finished the last round of data collection in December 2014. A large dataset is generated. As coding involves analyses, I prefer to do it myself rather than relying on RAs. There are at least three more papers to be produced from this project: 1. Social inequalities in gaining access to hospital care: It will analyze the unequal access to hospital care among the Chinese population. I plan to complete the draft in January 2016 and present it at an international conference. The target for submission: Social Problems (impact factor 1.36). 2. The impacts of gifts for hospital care on patients and doctors: “A Market of Distrust” examines why patients gave cash gifts to doctors but it does not explore the impacts of the gifts. This paper will focus on how gifts affect doctors’ treatment of the patients. I plan to complete the draft in July 2016 and present it at an international conference in 2017. The target for submission: Social Science and Medicine (impact factor 2.558). 3. Guanxi culture in medical care in China and Taiwan. It will utilize the data collected in both China and Taiwan for a comparative analysis of how Chinese guanxi functions differently in helping patients obtain hospital care. I expect to have the draft completed in early 2017 and present it at an international conference. The target for submission: Journal of Contemporary China (impact factor 0.953, ranked No.1 in China studies).

741410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
741410.value: The term “kanbing nan kanbing gui” (medical care is difficult to obtain and expensive) has occurred in everyday conversations in mainland China since the 1990s. At the same time, the tension between doctors and patients has escalated over the past two decades. This project examines the doctor-patient relationship and interaction in China from a sociological perspective. It investigates how the healthcare policies and hospital system negatively affect the frontline doctors’ behaviors and, consequently, generated strong public distrust in hospitals and doctors. The project further studies how the patients deal with the problem of distrust by resorting to the traditional cultural practices of offering gifts and mobilizing social networks to induce preferential treatment and particularism. This project takes a neutral position and strikes a balance on reporting the difficulties faced by both doctors and patients. It analyzes the sources of the conflict of interests between the doctors and patients, how the doctors become the scapegoats of the problematic system, and how the patients are treated unequally. Academically, this project contributes to an understanding of how institutions and cultures shape doctor-patient relationship and interaction. Empirically, it provides implications for policy change and hospital care management.

741810.label: Project Title(Chinese)
741810.value: 研發支出降低的影響與原因

741910.label: Project Objectives
741910.value: We will investigate whether family ownership affects insider trading behavior. To the best of our knowledge, this issue has not been investigated by prior literature. Our findings will suggest that it is essential to consider ownership structure and CEO types when evaluating insider trading information. We complement the existing literature on family businesses. Although some prior studies have argued that strong legal protection in the U.S. prevents controlling shareholders from expropriating minority shareholders (e.g., Burkart et al., 2003), our findings will indicate whether founding families are able to accrue personal benefits in the exploitation of inside information. We will investigate whether corporate governance and transparency mitigate the expropriation of controlling shareholders. In aggregate, our study will identify any costs incurred by family ownership, and will show that whether the costs could be reduced through the enhancement of corporate transparency.

741910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741910.value: Family ownership is considered to be the most prevalent form of corporate governance in the world, and its presence affects agency problems faced by public corporations (Claessens et al., 2000; Morck et al., 2005). Prior research suggests that family control mitigates the classic agency problem that arises from the separation of ownership and management, either by directly appointing a family member as CEO or by monitoring appointed executives more effectively than in non family firms (Demsetz and Lehn, 1985; Anderson and Reeb, 2003a). However, holding substantial ownership may enable family members to seek personal benefits at the expense of minority shareholders. For example, family members can engage in related-party transactions (Anderson and Reeb, 2003a), issue special dividends (DeAngelo and DeAngelo, 2000), freeze out small shareholders (Gilson and Golden, 2003), or entrench the family appointed CEO (Shleifer and Vishny, 1997; Perez-Gonzalez, 2006). Another possibility for controlling shareholders to accrue personal benefits that has not been considered by the prior literature is to reap excess gains from trading their own stocks. Founding families typically invest a large portion of their personal wealth in their company and often hold their shares for very long time (Anderson and Reeb, 2003b). This long-term investment horizons and lengthy tenure give managers who belong to the founding family incentives and means to acquire a more intimate knowledge of the company than professional managers of non-family firms and, of course, than outside investors. In this project we will examine if CEOs who belong to a family controlling the firm (founding CEOs and descendent CEOs) possess better private information than unaffiliated professional CEOs of family firms and CEOs of non-family firms. Specifically we will investigate whether CEOs of family firms engage in more frequent, larger, and more profitable insider trading than other CEOs. Further, we will look at whether firms with good corporate transparency or governance (proxied by institutional ownership) mitigates the information advantage of founding and descendent CEOs. Finally, we will examine whether the presence of a “blackout” period policy is less common in firms that are managed by a founding CEO than in other firms. 家族所有權被認為是世上最普遍的公司治理形式，它的存在影響公司治理所面臨的問題 （Claessens等人，2000; Morck等人，2005）。之前的研究發現，家族企業減輕了所有權和管理權分離的代理問題。無論是由家族成員直接擔任或任命管理人員為執行長比非家族企業有更好的管治成效（Demsetz 和Lehn，1985; Anderson 和Reeb， 2003）。然而，持有主要所有權可能使家族成員為謀取個人利益而犧牲其他少數股東之權益。例如，家族成員可以參與關聯交易（Anderson and Reeb，2003），發行特別股息（DeAngelo和DeAngelo，2000），逼走小股東（Gilson 和Golden，2003），或鞏固家族權利而任命家族成員為執行長（Shleifer 和 Vishny，1997; Perez-Gonzalez，2006）。另一種可能是從內幕交易股票買賣而獲得收益，此題目從前尚未有研究。創立公司之家族通常投資一大部分的個人財富在他們的公司，而且持有該公司股份時間很長（Anderson 和 Reeb，2003）。這種長期投資讓擁有管理權的創始家族比非家族企業及外面的投資者更能深入了解公司的情況。 在此項目中，我們將研究家族企業執行長（創始執行長或當他們的後代為執行長）會否比家族企業的專業執行長和非家族企業執行長具有較優勢的私人信息。具體來說，我們將研究家族企業的執行長比其他的執行長是否進行更頻繁的內幕交易和更有利可圖的交易。此外，我們將研究是否擁有良好的企業透明度和治理的企業可以減輕此信息優勢。最後，我們將研究由創辦者為執行長之家族企業比其他公司是否通常不設立內幕交易限制之“禁售期”的政策。

742510.label: Co - Investigator(s)
742510.value: Prof Imrohoroglu, Ayse Prof Imrohoroglu, Selahattin

742510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742510.value: This project assesses the quantitative importance of population aging and changes in social security policies in explaining the medium term fluctuations in hours worked per person in the U.S. In the U.S., average weekly hours worked per person display a U-shaped pattern, with a downward trend until the early 1980s, and an upward trend since then, especially during the 1990s. Such a change in the trend of hours worked is puzzling from a standard neoclassical model. Mulligan (2001), for example, finds that the aggregate fluctuations in labor are hard to reconcile with simple quantitative models of labor supply and demand. In Ohanian, Raffo and Rogerson (2006), a neoclassical model enhanced by taxes captures some of these changes. However, significant discrepancies between theory and data remain. Recently, McGrattan and Prescott (2007) and Chen, İmrohoroğlu and İmrohoroğlu (2009) find that standard neoclassical models augmented with actual TFP series predict a depression in hours worked in the 1990s, while in fact it boomed. Amongst the factors that may help bridge the gap between theory and data are population aging and changes in social security policies. Specifically, the U.S. has experienced population aging since 1960. In addition, both payroll taxes and the social security benefits feature an increasing pattern until the early 1980s. Intuitively, population aging reduces the aggregate labor supply and, thus, increases the wage rate. A higher wage rate, in turn, encourages more hours of work. Accordingly, demographic transition may contribute to an increase in hours worked since the early 1980s. Increases in payroll taxes, to the opposite, would reduce hours of work via a lower after-tax wage income. Similarly, an increase in social security benefits would put a downward pressure on hours worked by raising the retirement income and, thus, the lifetime wealth. As a result, the observed increase in payroll tax rates and social security benefits before the early 1980s may contribute to the decline in hours worked during the same period by discouraging workers from working long or encouraging early retirement. To explore the quantitative implications of population aging and social security policies for the trends in U.S. hours worked, we construct a life-cycle model that incorporates these two elements. The model is calibrated to U.S. data for the 1960-2006 period. We then conduct deterministic simulations to quantify the effects of these two elements on the observed U-shaped pattern of hours worked. N/A

742810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742810.value: Social support refers to the extent to which individuals’ basic social needs are fulfilled through interaction with others. The online community has emerged as a major source of social support in the Cyber Age. There is a growing literature that examines this phenomenon, but conflicting theoretical views and inconsistent findings have been obtained so far. We formulate a conceptual model to address two of the important but unresolved issues: How and why is online social support beneficial to recipients? We also expand the current conceptualization of online social support by hypothesizing that it comprises both tangible (i.e., actually received) and perceived (i.e., evaluative) facets. To assess this conceptualization, we will construct and validate a new standardized questionnaire and an interview protocol for diverse Chinese samples. An online forum will also be developed for a microanalysis of the process that underlies the actual utilization of online social support. Results from this project may be of theoretical and practical interest to researchers and practitioners. An expanded conceptualization of online social support may foster the construction or refinement of measures with greater explanatory and predictive power. The proposed conceptual model may provide a more sophisticated account of the role of online social support by specifying the conditions in which its benefits are manifested. Findings yielded from this project may be translated into practice for the design of more cost-effective online intervention programs, which demand less time, space, and human resources to run. 社會支持是指透過與他人的互動而滿足個人的基本社會需要。在網絡時代，網上社區已經成為社會支持的一個主要來源，越來越多文獻探討此現象，但至今只獲相互矛盾的理論觀點和不一致的研究結果。我們制訂一個概念模型，以探究兩個重要但尚未解決的問題：網上社會支持如何以及為什麼有益於接受者？我們更擴大現有的網上社會支持概念，假設其包含有形（即實收）和認知（即評價）兩方面。為了評估這個概念，我們將針對不同的華人樣本，建立及驗證一個新的標準化問卷和訪談規約。我們亦將架設一個網上論壇，以對網上社會支持的實際應用過程進行微觀分析。

742810.label: Realisation of objectives
742810.value: Objective 1: We have formulated a new conceptual model that explicates the interplay of social, cognitive, and situational factors in accounting for the benefits of online social support. This conceptual model provides a theoretical framework that states the interrelations among a set of major constructs. The model also orients us towards a specific set of research questions and hypotheses to be tested in various studies (see Objectives 2 to 4 below). Objective 2: We have conducted an elicitation study using the focus-group method, and used the results derived from several focus-group sessions for constructing two new measures. Specifically, we have developed a new self-report questionnaire and a semi-structured interview protocol that assess online social support in different samples and contexts. We have also designed another study to evaluate the psychometric properties of the newly developed questionnaire. Results showed that the new questionnaire has adequate internal consistency, criterion-related validity, construct validity, and discriminant validity. Objective 3: We have collaborated with the Hong Kong PHAB Association to discuss the setting up of an online forum, and we have developed the online forum that has been successfully launched on their website. An evaluation study has been carried out that assessed the use of online social support via the website and its impact on the users’ psychological well-being over time. Objective 4: We have studied online social support and its impact on psychological adjustment among different cultural samples using a multimethod approach to provide a comprehensive assessment of this psychological phenomenon. Both questionnaire and experimental studies provided convergence evidence on the beneficial role of online social support across diverse cultural groups in the present cyber age.

742810.label: Major findings and research outcome
742810.value: In our project, we have constructed a new measure for accessing online social support and to employ this new measure to scrutinize the use of online social support as a coping strategy. Participants completed the new self-report questionnaire of online social support as well as some personality and criterion measures. Results revealed that new measure displayed good test-retest reliability and adequate internal consistencies. Online tangible support and online socio-emotional support were related to a different set of psychological variables, thus demonstrating criterion-related validity. Specifically, there were relationships of online tangible support with Internet addiction, computer efficacy, and interpersonal anxiety. The conceptual model upon which this study was based have been presented in an international conference (see Section C9 #1), and the findings of this study have been presented in another international conference (see Section C9 #2). A manuscript has been submitted to a refereed international journal for possible publication (see Section C8 #1). In another cross-cultural study, we compared findings between a sample of Caucasians from a North American university and a sample of Chinese from a Hong Kong university. It was hypothesized that Facebook renders a kind of online social support that could buffer the adverse effects of stress by providing users with a reminder of their social support networks. An experimental study of priming was conducted using a 2 (culture: European-American vs. Hong Kong Chinese) x 2 (Facebook: exposure vs. non-exposure) design; participants wrote about a stressful experience and then were told to find information about their close friends on Facebook (priming them to activate their potential support networks) in the experimental condition to see if being on the social networking site would elicit psychological benefits (social support) versus those who viewed a less social networking site (Wikipedia). Results showed that European Americans intended to seek out others for social support more to cope with stressful events in the Wikipedia condition than the Facebook condition, suggesting that Facebook provides online social support that reduces the need to actively seek offline social support from others. However, this was not the case for Hong Kong Chinese, suggesting that Facebook does not provide online social support in the way that it does for European Americans. The findings of this study have been presented in an international conference (see Section C9 #3) and a manuscript is now under preparation for possible publication.

742810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
742810.value: Findings yielded from this project have revealed the psychological benefits of online social support, suggesting that seeking online social support is a potentially new way of coping with life stress among young adults in the present cyber age. Our findings have expanded the scope of the coping literature by identifying new coping strategies (e.g., seeking online information support, seeking online emotional support, seeking online companionship, seeking online tangible aids etc.) that are of potential relevance and significance for coping research and counseling. Specifically, our studies have opened up a new arena for coping researchers by expanding current conceptual frameworks of coping, which were formulated by psychologists in the 1960’s and 1970’s. The expanded framework of coping functions to enhance the explanatory and predictive power of the salutary role of coping on psychological well-being and adjustment among youngsters in the cyber age. The findings may also benefit practitioners, especially those who work with youngsters because many of whom, if not all, are Internet users. As online resources are accessible free of geographical and time constraints, utilizing online resources may be more convenient and effective for young Web users in boosting their self-esteem and subjective well-being.
