743010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743010.value: Since the 20th century, information technology has fundamentally changed our society. As never before, we are confronted with massive flow of information, offering not only unprecedented opportunities but also challenges in this newly established network and knowledge society that we are living in. In particular, we bear witness to the vexing dichotomy between protecting personal information on the one hand, and allowing free access to information on the other hand. While different legal regimes have endeavoured to resolve the above problem, a harmonized legal framework is yet to emerge in this era of Internet and globalization. Adding to the complexity, despite various efforts, legal protection of personal information is seriously lagging behind technological advancements, making it necessary to rely as much on technological instruments as on law for effective realization of data security. In light of the above, the proposed project examines both potential technological as well as legal measures that could improve the safeguard of information on the Internet. This research project’s results shall finally help policy makers in enhancing the protection of personal data both on- and offline. 自二十世紀以來，資訊科技徹底改變了我們的社會：規模空前的資訊流通帶來了新生網路和知識社會從未有過的機遇，同時也帶來料所不及的挑戰。尤其是，我們正面臨著個人資訊保護與自由獲取資訊兩者之間帶來的衝擊和矛盾。 > 雖然不同的法律制度都一直努力地解決這衝擊和矛盾，但是一個能協調一致而又能適用於這個互聯網和全球化時代的法律管治模式卻遙不可及。況且，儘管人們多方努力，個人資訊的法律保護仍嚴重落後於科技的發展。因此，要有效保障資料安全，不能單靠法律，還有賴科技本身對互聯網資訊安全保障設施的發展。有鑑於此，本計劃將同時硏究如何改善互聯網資訊安全保障的技術措施和相關的法律。本研究計劃的成果，將有助決策者增強對「在線」和「離線」個人資訊的保護。

743010.label: Realisation of objectives
743010.value: All the six objectives have been realized. • Concerning the first objective, we have developed a techno-legal approach for the better protection of personal information: by examining privacy challenges posed by advancing information technologies that bring about huge economic benefits and social influence, examining inadequacies in privacy law responses both domestically and comparatively, reflecting on the conceptual basis of the legislation in relation to the technologies, and proposing reforms or measures from doctrinal, legislative, regulatory and technical perspectives respectively but with reference to each other. This approach enhances the traditional techno-legal approaches which focused one-sidedly on either embedding law in technological development or embedding technology in law formulation. To facilitate the use of this approach, we have brought together academics, legal professionals, representatives of the industry and regulatory authorities of personal data protection to explore the complex privacy challenges and reflect on solutions through informed discussion at two conferences held for this purpose. The most significant output of this approach was the publication of ‘Privacy and Legal Issues in Cloud Computing’ (see Research Output No.3). • Concerning Objective 2, we have provided extensive and in-depth review of law and policies relating to data protection in the use of advanced ITs including Internet of things, mobile geo-location tracking, social networking sites, and cloud computing. More importantly, we have revisited the certain critical concepts on which the current legal framework of privacy is based but which compatibility with the advancing technologies are insufficiently explored, including the concept of personal data per se and the right to be forgotten. Such theoretical reflections provide insights for the reforms in legislation and regulation. • Concerning Object 3, we have compared two major legal models (EU and US) which are both general frameworks for data protection in the context of globalized data flow, and studied privacy regulation and Internet governance in different jurisdictions, including UK, Australia, Canada, Germany, and China. Based on these observations, we have suggested an improved model or harmonized framework with respect to the privacy challenges identified above, and also suggested reform to Hong Kong’s personal data protection legislation. • Concerning Objective 4, in the light of or in relation to the aforementioned legal analysis and theoretical reflections, we have formulated practical rules and guidelines regarding data security in cloud computing, computer forensic examination and digital evidence acquisition. • Concerning Objective 5, special procedures and techniques were devised for better protection of personal data in computer forensic examination and digital evidence acquisition. Contributors to our book on cloud computing have recommended practical methods of data protection concerning the digitization of health information, cross-border sharing of genomic data, and general licensing in cloud computing. • Concerning Objective 6, apart from the publication of research results and holding of two conferences which can be accessed by the civil society, a database was established to include all laws and regulations on privacy and personal data protection in Hong Kong, mainland China, Macau and Taiwan, which provides a one-stop portal for the civil society to learn about legal obligations concerning the use of different ITs in the Greater China region.

743010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
743010.value: The research approach can be further developed and applied on an important emerging technology, i.e. big data, which will heavily influence the future of the technologies studied in this project. The project's empirical findings about privacy risks, normative suggestions about legislative and regulatory reform, and practical techniques about privacy protection in deploying technologies can be revisited in the context of big data. And the theoretical reflections of this project are good basis to review the privacy impacts of big data which questions the operablility of the current legal model's founding principles, including the concept of identifiable personal data and consent of data subjects.

743010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743010.value: This project examined alternative solution to tackle privacy challenges brought by information technologies, including popular technologies affecting each individuals, such as social networking sites and mobile location tracking, as well as cutting-edges technologies that are subtly but profoundly transforming the global economy, such as the Internet of things and cloud computing. Different from traditional research that relied only on improving technologies or reforming laws, this project has combined legal research and technological research, and make the two research illuminate each other. Its outputs will not only help legislators and authorities better understand the privacy risks posed by the most influential technologies, but also make practical suggestions about legislative reforms, regulation improvements and technological enhancements that are more consistent with each other and in a timelier manner. The project also contributes to the harmonization of different legal models, and sheds new light on the values and concepts on which these legal models are based. The edited volume resulting from the project is one of the first legal-techno handbook for privacy protection in cloud computing and welcomed by both the academy and the industry.

743110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
743110.value: 創意, 危機與日常生活: 香港城市文化文本研究

743110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743110.value: Referring to contemporary Hong Kong urban cultural texts, this project explores the intricate relationship between creativity, ethics of otherness, crisis, and everyday life. Being a cosmopolitan city, Hong Kong and its people have to face various crises over the decades, including tidal waves of globalization and capitalism and political tensions caused by the 1997 handover. The subtle changes that take place in the ordinary, everyday spaces of the city during such crises reflect transformations on a global scale. This project deals with cultural texts that revolve around the everyday life of ordinary people. On the one hand, the realm of everyday life is a crowded space regulated by familiar, repeated actions. On the other hand, the fictional worlds of everyday life created by the selected artists in this project become ground for aesthetic experimentations. A study of everyday life in contemporary Hong Kong cultural texts will bring new insights to the understanding of the city’s transformation through a spatial perspective. However, little research has been done on this topic. This project will be the first study of Hong Kong literature and film to develop a theoretical framework for analyzing urban cultural texts through the perspective of crisis and spatial transformation. It will provide an interdisciplinary, cross-media, and cross-genre model for the study of Hong Kong culture. The project will look at contemporary Hong Kong films and literature from the late 1970s/early 1980s onwards. This particular historical scope has been chosen as it marks the emergence of creative works with a sharp Hong Kong focus, internationally respected filmmakers of the “New Hong Kong Cinema” being cases in point. The project will examine how the power of creativity is liberated in everyday life experiences and moments of crisis. It will explore how the ethics of otherness is generated through the representations of urbane and grassroots communities and realms. To achieve these aims, subtle mutations in urban space will be examined through three inter-related topics: (i) how the mutating city demonstrates the perpetual process of demolition and construction; (ii) how everyday practices construct petite narratives of ordinary people; and (iii) how encounters with strangers generate an ethics of otherness. 計劃摘要 本研究計劃參照當代香港的城市文化文本，探討創意和倫理政治與日常生活錯綜複雜的關係。香港是國際都會，幾十年來居民面對種種的危機，尤其全球化和資本主義的浪潮、「九七」回歸帶來的政治緊迫氣氛。這些危機潛伏於庶民的生活空間，產生種種的微妙轉變，以香港這全球化的城市來說，可顯微知著。本計劃集中分析庶民的日常生活如何以兩種面貌呈現：一方面既是眾人習以為常、週而復始的體驗；另一方面於本土的文學與藝術工作者而言，那是一個想像與虛構的世界，是他們實驗美學和創意之源。 研究當代香港文化書寫的庶民生活，透過空間的剖析，更能了解此城的轉變。同樣題目的研究文獻甚少，此計劃是學術界首次以香港文學和電影為本，發展一個理論框架──從社會危機及城市蛻變的角度，分析都市文化文本；同時為研究香港文化提供一個跨學科、跨媒介及跨類型的模式。 本計劃集中討論上世紀七、八十年代迄今的香港電影和文學，選擇這一段時期的文本，是因為期間以香港本土文化為根的文學及電影大量冒起，尤以「香港新浪潮」一批電影人最為特出，不少新浪潮的導演及作品享譽國際。本計劃會審視日常生活的經驗、面對危機的時刻，文學與藝術工作者的創作力量如何回應此變遷；都市的草根社群，如何誘發涉及「他者」的倫理政治。計劃的目標是探討三個相關的題目： (一) 城市的變化如何在破壞與建設的過程中展現； (二) 庶民如何透過日常生活的體驗書寫他們的「小故事」； (三) 涉及「他者」的倫理政治如何產生。

743510.label: Project Title(Chinese)
743510.value: 通過Web 2.0工具作探究式學習，以發展資訊素養

743510.label: Co - Investigator(s)
743510.value: Dr Van Aalst, Jan Cornelis Wouterus
rows: Dr Van Aalst, Jan Cornelis Wouterus

743510.label: Project Objectives
743510.value: To develop an evidence-based theoretical model of the development of information literacy among secondary students through inquiry learning with the use of Web 2.0. To design, implement, develop, and evaluate a supportive learning environment using Web 2.0 applications in the implementation of IES for senior secondary students. Formative assessments with each iteration will provide the bases for design revisions.
rows: To develop an evidence-based theoretical model of the development of information literacy among secondary students through inquiry learning with the use of Web 2.0.

To design, implement, develop, and evaluate a supportive learning environment using Web 2.0 applications in the implementation of IES for senior secondary students. Formative assessments with each iteration will provide the bases for design revisions.

743510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743510.value: The rapid development of information technology, especially the Internet, has led to an overwhelming flow of information in societies. However, evidence indicates that our students do not possess effective information literacy skills to deal with the problem of information overload. Information literacy has been defined as the ability to access, evaluate, and creatively use information. Since the 1970s, research on information literacy continues to evolve with the advancement of information technology. Recent research findings in this area recommend the development of students’ information literacy through inquiry learning in curricular contexts. Inquiry learning is an approach that uses active questioning to involve students in their own learning. This study examines the development of information literacy through inquiry learning with the use of Web 2.0 applications. Web 2.0 represents a range of web applications that promotes collaboration among users, and has been suggested to be beneficial for information literacy education. However, the usefulness of Web 2.0 in the development of information literacy is yet to be substantiated with empirical evidence. This study will contribute to the understanding of information literacy development among secondary students, formulating an evidence-based theoretical model for teaching. Through the process of research, this study will also address the problem of inadequate information literacy skills for inquiry learning in senior secondary schools in Hong Kong. Using a design-based research approach, this study will design, implement, and evaluate a supportive online learning environment that fosters development of information literacy through an extensive inquiry project among secondary students. An iterative process of formative evaluations is proposed to integrate various Web 2.0 applications for the Independent Enquiry Studies (IES) of local senior secondary students enrolled in the Liberal Studies course over a three-year period. Using the Information Literacy Framework for Hong Kong Students as proposed by the Education Bureau as a basis for design and analysis, a wiki-like platform, a social bookmarking tool, and a reference citation manager will be adopted to support the conduct of IES. Measurements and evaluations will be done using a mix of quantitative and qualitative methods and analysis, involving form 4 and form 5 students, teachers of Liberal Studies and Information Technology, and librarians. Two major outcomes are expected: (1) a theoretical model that explains the development of students’ information literacy through inquiry learning with Web 2.0 applications, and (2) a learning environment that promotes students’ development in information literacy through engaging in IES. 資訊科技急速發展，當中以互聯網為甚，這導致各種資訊在社會急劇湧現。可是，有證據顯示學生並沒有足夠的資訊素養能力去面對資訊泛濫的問題。資訊素養被定義為蒐集、評估及具創意地使用資訊的能力。自七十年代起，資訊科技不斷發展，相關研究漸多。近年的研究結果都建議學生通過參與探究式學習的課程來發展資訊素養能力。探究式學習鼓勵學生積極提出疑問，從中自我學習。本研究將探討如何通過Web 2.0工具作探究式學習，以發展資訊素養。Web 2.0包括一系列促進用戶協作的網絡工具，這些工具已被認為有助資訊素養教育。然而，Web 2.0在資訊素養發展的效用仍需驗證。本研究將有助了解中學生發展資訊素養發展的過程，並制定以論證為基礎的教學理論模型供教學之用。此研究亦會談及到香港高中學生缺乏資訊素養能力進行探究式學習的問題。 本研究採用設計為本的研究基礎來設計、實施和評估一個網上學習環境，以支援中學生通過探究式專題研習來發展資訊素養。在三年的研究中，研究人員將進行一連串的進展式評估來整合各種Web 2.0工具，以協助本地高中學生在通識課作獨立專題研習。研究將採用由教育局提倡的香港學生資訊素養架構，讓學生在獨立專題研習中利用維基平台、社會書籤工具及文獻管理工具來協助研習的設計及分析。本研究將結合量性和質性的量度和評估方式，對中四和中五學生、通識科老師、電腦科老師和圖書館主任作綜合分析，並預期有以下兩大研究成果：一、發展一套理論模式用以解釋如何通過Web 2.0工具來協助探究式學習，以發展資訊素養；二、建構一個學習環境讓學生作獨立專題研習，以促進學生發展資訊素養。

743510.label: Realisation of objectives
743510.value: Both of the project objectives have been achieved. For the first objective, an evidence-based theoretical model has been developed. It shows how teachers can provide scaffolded support in their students’ development of information literacy by first providing them with an information literacy training workshop. It then followed by offering students practice of the knowledge learned through doing an individual assignment on information literacy (Siu, Chan, & Chu, 2014). At the same time, teachers can engage their students in an inquiry group project work facilitated by Web 2.0 technologies such as wiki (Chu, Cheng & King, 2012) and social bookmarking tools (Chu, Cheng, Lee & Feng, 2014). Teachers can also assess whether students have actually improved on their knowledge and abilities in information literacy by testing them with a pre and post information literacy assessment test (Chu, Yeung & Chu, 2012). Regarding the second objective, various Web 2.0 applications (a social bookmarking tool called Delicious and two wiki tools [Google Sites and PBworks] ) have been used to set up online working environment to facilitate secondary students’ Liberal Studies project work (Chu, Capio & Cheng, 2014; Chu, Cheng, Lee & Feng, 2014; Chu, Cheng & King, 2012). Both formative and summative assessments have been conducted with each iteration and this has provided the bases for design revisions with the Web 2.0 applications throughout this project. 743510.label: Major findings and research outcome
743510.value: Through the theoretical model described in section “5.3 Realisation of objectives”, students’ information literacy can be effectively developed through the use of 3 intervention strategies: training workshop on information literacy, individual assignment on information literacy and inquiry group project work facilitated by an online wiki platform that allows group members to co-construct their project work anytime and anywhere they want (Chu, Cheng & King, 2012; Siu, Chan, & Chu, 2014). This project survey 347 secondary school students in Hong Kong with a questionnaire on their perceptions of Google Sites in five areas: learning/pedagogy, motivation, group interaction, technology and knowledge management. Overall, students were positive about all 5 areas. Students found that Use of Google Sites enhanced their interest in working on the project and it also enhanced their motivation to conduct the project. Use of Google Sites promoted students’ collaborative learning and Students found Google Sites easy to use. Finally, students opined that Google Sites facilitated knowledge sharing (Chu, Chin, Wong, Chan, Lee, Wu & Pun, 2011). The project also investigated the value of Google Sites in support of collaborative group writing among the students. Four groups from a secondary school were engaged in group writing projects that used the Google Sites as an online platform. Data were gathered from the revision tracking history, questionnaire on the perceived pedagogical value of wiki, and group interviews. Findings showed that students who produced the best writing output as evaluated by their teachers used the wiki to engage in collaborative group writing, while those who produced poor quality output had limited online engagement. Overall, students reported a moderately positive perception of the pedagogical value of wiki across different categories. The functionalities offered by the wiki appear capable of promoting collaborative writing, but students need to be prepared and encouraged to use them (Chu, Capio & Cheng, 2014). References: See “Part C”.

743510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
743510.value: One “unexpected” finding from this project is the seriousness of plagiarism in secondary students’ group project work. Yeung, Chu, Chu & Fung (2014) found that 75% of junior secondary students in an academically strong Hong Kong local school plagiarized in varying degrees. This “surprised” study result has prompted me to draft a GRF proposal on the topic in this academic year. The proposed project aims to develop an instructional strategy to scaffold upper-primary (ages 9-11) and junior-secondary (ages 12-14) students’ understanding of plagiarism and to develop their capacity for plagiarism-free inquiry learning. The upper-primary and junior-secondary levels are selected because students in Hong Kong generally begin learning to access, evaluate and use information for project work at the former level in General Studies (GS) and at the latter in Liberal Studies (LS). Teaching students to be mindful of the risk of plagiarism right from the start can help them develop good, ethical writing habits that will be beneficial in the long run. References: Yeung, A.H.W., Chu, C.B.L., Chu, S.K.W. & Fung, C. (2014). Exploring Junior Secondary Students’ Plagiarism Behavior. Paper will be submitted to Library & Information Science Research.

743510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743510.value: This project tries to help secondary students develop their information literacy through inquiry group project work with the use of Web 2.0 tools. The results showed students’ information literacy can be developed through training workshop, individual assignment and inquiry group work facilitated by wiki (the tool behind Wikipedia) that allows group members to work on their project anytime and anywhere they want. This project survey 347 students on their ideas of Google Sites (a wiki) in five areas: learning/pedagogy, motivation, group interaction, technology and knowledge management. Overall, students were positive in all 5 areas. Students found that using Google Sites enhanced their interest and motivation in working on the project. Use of Google Sites promoted students’ collaborative learning and they found Google Sites easy to use. Students also believed that Google Sites facilitated knowledge sharing. Four groups of students were engaged in collaborative group writing projects that used the wiki. Findings showed students who produced the best writing output used the wiki to engage in collaborative group writing, while those who produced poor quality output had limited online engagement on wiki. Overall, students reported a moderately positive perception of the pedagogical value of wiki across different categories.

743910.label: Project Objectives
743910.value: To design and carry out cross-cultural and cross-linguistic surveys, formulated in both English and Chinese, on philosophical intuitions. To critically examine the assumptions (1) that intuitions are important philosophical evidence and (2) that cultural variability in intuitions would present a significant challenge to traditional philosophical method. To explore the ways in which cultural variability in intuitions would be philosophically and scientifically significant. To improve on the experimental design of extant studies in experimental philosophy.

743910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743910.value: This research will attempt to determine (1) whether there are cross-cultural differences in a range of philosophical intuitions between Hong Kong Chinese, mainland Chinese, and North Americans, and (2) if so, the kind and degree of philosophical impact such differences ought to have. It can seem as though philosophical theories are evaluated according to whether they are compatible with intuitions, i.e. non-inferential judgments about what is true or false in some (usually hypothetical) scenario. But whose intuitions matter? Usually, philosophers ask only other philosophers for their intuitions. What results will we get if we ask large groups of non-philosophers? Will significant cross-cultural differences emerge? Using a survey methodology familiar from the social sciences, the project will investigate these issues. The PI will develop surveys in both English and Chinese, presenting scenarios from recent philosophical literature on language, knowledge, mind, and morality. Data from surveys using Hong Kong subjects will be compared with data from mainland Chinese and North American subject groups. This empirical side of the project will contribute to the burgeoning “experimental philosophy” movement, whose practitioners conduct intuition surveys to assess claims about intuitions in philosophy. On the whole, experimental philosophy has been confined to intra-cultural studies in the USA; only a handful of cross-cultural studies have been carried out, and none using Chinese language formulations of survey questions. The proposed research will thus produce an important new range of data for experimental philosophers to consider. However, the PI is skeptical about a particular use to which results in experimental philosophy have sometimes been put. Some experimental philosophers maintain that their empirical results challenge philosophy’s reliance on intuitions as a source of evidence. The PI’s view is that this challenge is misconceived. Arguments in philosophy do not in fact, and need not in principle, rely on treating intuitions as a source of evidence. The theoretical side of the project will involve developing this objection to this use of experimental philosophy. The PI’s position is that a narrow focus on experimental philosophy as a challenge to traditional philosophical method obscures experimental philosophy’s true philosophical and scientific significance. The project promises to shed light on the methodology of philosophy and to foster East-West cultural understanding. Cross-cultural differences in intuitive reactions to philosophical cases would be an important finding, one of potential use to social scientists in explaining other, higher-level cultural differences. 本研究将试图确定（1）是否有在中国香港之间，大陆中国哲学的直觉范围的跨文化的差异，北美，和（2）如果是这样，哲学的种类和影响程度等差异应该有。 它看起来好像哲学理论进行评估，根据他们是否是兼容的直觉，什么是真正的或在某些（通常是假设性的）情景假即非推理判断。但他们的直觉呢？通常情况下，哲学家只要求他们的直觉其他哲学家。我们将会得到什么结果，如果我们要求非哲学家的大集团？将重要的跨文化差异出现吗？ 利用统计调查方法从社会科学熟悉，该项目将调查这些问题。将开发的PI中英文和中文的调查，展示从最近对语言，知识，思想，道德哲学文学场景。从调查的数据对象将利用香港与内地相比中国和北美主题组的数据。 这个项目的经验方将有助于新兴，Äúexperimental 哲学，金运动，他们的从业者进行调查，以评估有关的直觉，在哲学的直觉索赔。整体而言，实验哲学一直局限于在美国内部文化研究，只有跨文化研究已经开展了一些，没有采用调查问卷中文配方。因此，建议的研究将产生一个哲学家对实验数据的新的重要考虑范围。 不过，首席研究员是关于一个特定的用途表示怀疑这会导致实验 哲学有时被付诸表决。一些哲学家坚持说，他们的实验研究结果挑战作为证据来源直觉理念，星光大道的依赖。在有价证券投资，政务主任的看法是，这一挑战是错误的。在哲学论据并不在事实，需要在原则不是，当作证据来源依靠直觉。该项目的理论方面将涉及发展中国家这一反对使用这种实验哲学。 PI的，星光大道上的立场是，作为一个传统的哲学方法的挑战实验哲学的狭隘关注掩盖实验哲学，星光大道真正的哲学和科学意义。 该项目有望揭示光的哲学方法论，促进东西方文化的理解。以哲学的情况下直观的反应跨文化差异是一个重要的发现，对社会的潜在用途之一 科学家在解释其他，更高层次的文化差异。

743910.label: Major findings and research outcome
743910.value: The hypothesis that intuitions about the reference of proper names is influenced by the speaker's reference/semantic reference distinction was tested and the influence found to be minimal. The hypothesis that intuitions about the incompatibility between free will and determinism are due to distorting beliefs about a phenomenon known as "bypassing" was tested and evidence suggests the hypothesis is unlikely. The PI's monograph makes a case for thinking that intuitions are far less philosophically significant than ordinarily supposed.

743910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
743910.value: The research outcomes can be developed in several ways, including: (1) Using the methodology of these studies to improve work in experimental philosophy and (2) Arriving at a more accurate description and assessment of philosophical methods as actually practiced.

743910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743910.value: How do philosophers acquire knowledge of abstract truths about knowledge, justice, beauty, freedom, etc.? According to a pervasive conception of philosophy, intuitions about hypothetical examples and "thought experiments" play a fundamental role. But this conception can and should be challenged. The question is how to challenge it. One way is to conduct empirical studies of people's intuitions about philosophical examples. The recent trend towards "experimental philosophy" represents this way of challenging the conception. Another way to challenge the conception is argue that it is simply a misconception of the character of philosophy. The research project pursued both of these strands of criticism at once.

744310.label: Project Objectives
744310.value: Produce 150-210 pages of high-quality articles to be published in law journals with an international reputation. Demonstrate how different branches of public international law simultaneously complement and conflict with each other, thus adding a sophisticated middle-ground approach to the unified-versus-fragmented debate over the nature of public international law. Design nuanced secondary rules to help reconcile the instances when specialized branches of public international law directly conflict, thereby bringing greater coherences to the whole. Examine some of the ways that international human rights law and international humanitarian law interact during an armed conflict, and recommend ways to reconcile these bodies of law when they directly conflict. Debate the unified or fragmented nature of the law of international organizations, and determine what exactly in public international law is responsible for its overall cohesion, since many international organizations can be seen as self-contained regimes established by their constitutive treaties. Differentiate between integral and interdependent treaty obligations in the context of disarmament law and international humanitarian law, and evaluate whether certain disarmament obligations can be classified as integral obligations because of their humanitarian-law nature, thereby avoiding the need for state consent and removing the ability to withdraw from these obligations.

744310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744310.value: The field of public international law – or the law regulating the activities of states and international organizations – often is taught and thought of as a group of disconnected substantive subfields. These specialized subfields range from international human rights law to the law of the sea, from international economic law to collective security law. Considerable energy and ink has been spent in the past decade trying to comprehensively define the field’s nature as either united or fragmented. Even the UN’s International Law Commission established a study group to explore this topic, which concluded after four years of study that international law is more fragmented than united due, in part, to the collision of different specialized bodies of international law. The project being proposed here will not attempt to resolve this perennial debate over the nature of public international law in such an all-or-nothing fashion. Rather, this project will take a more nuanced, middle-ground approach by exploring how various specialized subfields might simultaneously conflict with and complement each other. If forced to choose one word to capture the essence of this dynamic within public international law, it would be “cleaving,” which concurrently can mean “to join together” and “to break apart.” After identifying ways that various subfields conflict with and complement each other, this project will develop secondary rules to reconcile those conflicts, thus bringing a greater degree of coherence to the overall field. This project will be housed in the HKU Centre for Comparative and Public Law, which has a proven track record since 1995 in managing and ensuring the successful completion of RGC-funded research projects. 國際公法的領域——或規範國家和國際組織活動的法律——往往被視為是由一組獨立而又互不相關的子領域組成，教學時亦然。這些專門的子領域，由國際人權法到海洋法、由國際經濟法到集體安全法，都有涵蓋。過去十年來，業界花上不少精力及墨水，嘗試廣泛地為國際公法的領域下定義——有人認為是統一的，亦有人認為是相互割離的。聯合國的國際法委員會，更為了探索這個議題，成立研究小組，經過四年研究，小組的結論，是國際公法傾向是相互割離，而不是統一的，部分原因是不同的國際公法司法機構，會出現衝突。 有關國際公法定義這個爭論不休的議題，本計劃不試圖以非黑即白的方式去化解。反之，本計劃會以較微小、中立的角度，去探究國際公法各種特定的子領域，為何有機會產生衝突之餘，又同時互相補足。在識別出各子領域，如何出現衝突而又互相補足之後，本計劃會發展出一套輔助規則，去調和這些衝突，令整個國際公法領域，更具連貫性。

744310.label: Realisation of objectives
744310.value: I have realized the objectives of this project, and even far surpassed them: (1) one book Legal Resolution of Nuclear Non-Proliferation Disputes of 504 pages (200,688 words), published by Cambridge University Press, which has been awarded an A by the SENSE Ranking of Academic Publishers. This book addresses the simultaneous interaction of nuclear non-proliferation law, the law relating to international dispute settlement and UN law. This publication fulfills objectives 1 and 2. (2) one significant peer-reviewed article “Towards an Agreement on Investment in Mercosur” (41 pages or 16,940 words), which was published by the Journal of World Investment and Trade, a law journal that received an “A” ranking by the 2009 law journal rankings of the Australian Research Council. This publication fulfills objectives 1 and 2. An additional book currently is under review with Cambridge University Press following revision after initial submission in December 2012. Incorporating all of the feedback after initial submission has been the main reason for the delay in submitting this final report. This book is entitled Cleaved International Law and is 562 pages (or 239,782 words). This book reflects the general theory of “cleaved” international law that I have developed, as well as eight case studies. I will submit the published work to the RGC once it comes out in print. This publication fulfills objectives 1, 2 and 3. Finally, there is one other article currently under review with the International & Comparative Law Quarterly, which is entitled “Termination of Secretaries General and the Law of International Organizations”. This article is 96 pages (or 42,605 words). The article addresses whether there is a law of international organizations, as opposed to laws of international organizations, which fits into the “cleaved” debate. Despite my best efforts, this article has not been published by the deadline because it took an exceptionally long time to gather all of the constitutive instruments of the hundreds of international organizations, then to analyze them and then to write the article, which has been another cause of delay. I will submit the published work to the RGC once it comes out in print. This publication fulfills objectives 1, 2 and 4. In short, this project produced 1,203 pages (or 500,015 words) of top-quality material, which equates to 3.57 words per HK dollar of the grant. I doubt if any other grant has led to this level of productivity per dollar in the past.

744310.label: Major findings and research outcome
744310.value: The notion of “cleaved” international law represents a more accurate depiction of the international legal system than the models presenting in the traditional unity-versus-fragmentation debate, which typically are too simplistic. The ten case studies of this project support the thesis that the branches of public international law simultaneously conflict with and complement each other. By comparing these branches and studying how they interact in certain contexts, it becomes clear how the relationship between branches is complex, and this project encourages embracing the complexity, as opposed to ignoring it, as some commentators appear inclined to do. In terms of tangible research outcomes, there obviously are the research outputs listed in Part C, which speak for themselves. In terms of observed impact of this work, the book Legal Resolution of Nuclear Non-Proliferation Disputes has had the greatest impact so far. For examples, an abbreviated version of this work was a finalist for the 2011 Doreen & Jim McElvany Nonproliferation Challenge, which is an annual competition to identify “the most outstanding new thinking in the nonproliferation field”. This work also received 6th place for the 2012 Innovating Justice Award, which is an annual competition run by the Hague Institute for the Internationalisation of Law to find the most “[p]romising, new, breakthrough solutions to Rule of Law challenges”. This work has been nominated by Cambridge University Press and colleagues for a host of book awards, including the prestigious Paul Guggenheim Prize in International Law and the Grawemeyer Award for Ideas Improving World Order. Finally, I am aware of two book reviews currently being written by high-level academics about this book, and I suspect the book reviews will appear in top international law journals and will acknowledge the significant contribution that this work has made to the field and to international society. I suspect the other research outputs associated with this project also eventually will have similar impact on the field of public international law and on international society, although more time is needs in order to assess that impact.

744310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
744310.value: This research is easily expandable to include more case studies. This project only looked at 10 case studies, but there are a limitless number of case studies that could be done to support the underlying theory of “cleaved” international law. For example, most of the leading public international law textbooks list around 11 different branches in the field on average. This leads to 48 different pairings, assuming the influence between branches is bidirectional. Each branch has a large number of rules, each of which has the potential to conflict with or complement the rules and principles of the others, which leads to an inordinate number of possible permutations and pairings, all of which could be explored and could lead to some interesting observations and conclusions. However, I believe 10 case studies are enough to support this new approach to the unity-versus-fragmentation debate, and so I believe it is time to pursue other research paths in the future. Nevertheless, I am sure I will return to this general research topic in the future, whether as part of my main research area or as my secondary research area or to update the work I have done in relation to this project.

744310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
744310.value: The field of public international law – or the rules and principles relating to the relations of states – often is taught and thought of as a group of disconnected substantive subfields. These specialized subfields range from international human rights law to the law of the sea, from international trade law to collective security law. While compartmentalization can give the appearance of order to a field that often is criticized for its lack of order, superficial compartmentalization in this case is potentially counterproductive inasmuch as it oversimplifies reality and distracts one from looking for sophisticated solutions to common problems throughout. This project has presented the theory that the subfields of public international law simultaneously conflict with and complement each other, thereby presenting a new approach to understanding the nature of the international legal system. This project also has shown how the interaction of many subfields reflects this type of dynamic relationship, thereby supporting the underlying theory.

744410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744410.value: 世界衛生組織估計，2020年抑鬱症將成為第二個最主要的疾病負擔成因，未來數十年更會是公共健康的重要威脅，該組織亦曾提出多項預防措施。不過，這些措施往往因普遍人不願向專業人士求助而未能發揮最大效用。 據文獻和我們過往的研究所知，增強精神健康的求助意識會遇上多方面因難：一）抑鬱人士會因精神病的污名感而對求助卻步；二）不少抑鬱人士會傾向選擇媒體或上網找資料；三）研究指媒體上的資料往往正是污名感的源頭，令媒體用戶更不願求助；四）男姓和年青的抑鬱人士更抗拒求助。 世界衛生組織認為推廣精神健康有助預防抑鬱症。不過，目前學界仍缺乏以理論及文化因素為依據、以提高求助意識來推廣精神健康的研究。 本研究的目標是回應上述的挑戰，以計劃行為理論(Theory of Planned Behavior)為基礎，概念化、開發並實施能提高個人求助意向和行為的模式，同時考慮多項因素，包括尋求資訊的意向和行為、污名感、改善健康的自我效能、健康知識、對精神健康的態度、精神健康水平和個人背景。 本研究共分四部份：一）透過10至20人立意抽樣的深入訪談，找出個人求助態度的環境、傾向及文化等因素；二）按第一部份資料制作相關量表，並確立量表的信效度；三）按第一部份資料開發推廣訊息及活動內容；四）採用前測後測的隨機控制實驗方式來評估活動成效。

744410.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a theory-driven model for help-seeking for depression (Stage 1), tested, and validated the model empirically (Stage 2). Based on the results of the Stage 1 and 2, mental health promotion material and campaign were developed (Stage 3) and the campaign outcome effectiveness was evaluated (Stage 4). In the papers of research findings, evidence-based best practice and user-centered policy guidance were suggested and discussed. Major findings are reported in free open access journals for public dissemination. All three stated objectives have been completely achieved.

744410.label: Major findings and research outcome
744410.value: Drawing on the theory of planned behavior, we deployed the illness narrative approach and in-depth interviewed 18 participants in Hong Kong. With the diverse results we gathered, a behavioral model was built to conceptualize the interplays of various factors in shaping one’s help-seeking intention and behavior for depression. Participants appeared to have a limited view of treatment options and had diverse views of the symptoms of depression, both of which profoundly affected their motivation to seek help. The role of family and friends and a holistic approach to mental health education were found to be particularly important for encouraging help-seeking behavior in future campaigns concerning depression. (Hui, A., Wong, P., & Fu, K.W. (2014). Building a model for encouraging help-seeking for depression: a qualitative study in a Chinese society. BMC Psychology, 2(1), 9.) We evaluate the effectiveness of an online depression awareness campaign in encouraging help-seeking intention, intention for depression, and mental health literacy, which is informed by the findings of the first stage. Participants were recruited through the Facebook advertisements, either through a “happy face” or a “sad face” pictorial advertisement. Volunteered participants registered to the study through clicking on the advertisement and invited to leave their personal e-mails for receiving the information about depression. They were then randomly assigned into two groups with one receiving the campaign material and the control group receiving official information from the Hospital Authority in Hong Kong in four consecutive weeks. Pre-test and post-test were conducted before and after the campaign to measure the differences in help-seeking intention and mental health literacy. 199 registered and completed the pre-test and 116 (campaign = 55 and control = 62) of them completed the campaign and the post-test. At the post test, we found no significant changes of help-seeking intention between the campaign and the control groups; but the campaign group participants demonstrated a significant higher improvement in mental health literacy than the control group (p=.03). This study demonstrates the practicality and effectiveness of an online depression awareness campaigns using Facebook recruitment and Email content distribution. It is important for future studies to take advantage of the popularity of online media and conduct evaluative research on these campaigns. (Hui, A., Wong, P., & Fu, K.W. (under review) Evaluation of an online campaign for promoting help-seeking for depression using Facebook advisement: Online Randomized Controlled Experiment, Journal of Medical Internet Research)

744410.value: Through 18 in-depth interviews in Hong Kong, we found some important but largely overlooked factors in shaping one’s help-seeking intention and behavior for depression. Participants appeared to have a limited view of treatment options and had diverse views of the symptoms of depression, both of which profoundly affected their motivation to seek help. The role of family and friends and a holistic approach to mental health education were found to be particularly important for encouraging help-seeking behavior in future campaigns concerning depression. Online media can help to reach large numbers of participants and get help-seeking messages across to a population. This study demonstrates the possibility of delivering a mental health campaign through the Internet. Participants were recruited through the Facebook advertisements. Volunteered participants registered to the study through clicking on the advertisement and invited to leave their personal e-mails for receiving the information about depression. They were then randomly assigned into two groups with one receiving the campaign material and the control group receiving official information. Finally, we found no significant changes of help-seeking intention between the campaign and the control groups; but the campaign group participants demonstrated a higher improvement in mental health literacy than the control group.

744610.label: Project Title(Chinese)
744610.value: 投资者情绪与非系统性风险：对于预期市场收益的含义

744610.label: Co - Investigator(s)
744610.value: Dr Yu, Jianfeng Dr Yuan, Yu

744610.label: Project Objectives
744610.value: Our first objective is to apply and compare different conditional variance models on the expected idiosyncratic risk. These models have been used in previous studies. In particular, we want to look at the rolling window method in Ang, Hodrick, Xing, and Zhang (2006), the EGARCH models in Fu (2009), and an AR(6) model, the realized variance model. We want to make sure that our empirical results are robust amongst these models. Our second objective is to study the relation between idiosyncratic risk and stock return during high and low sentiment periods. We expect to find that such relation change during different time periods. In particular, in a high sentiment period, sentiment investors tend to have a large impact on stock prices. Therefore, high idiosyncratic risk stocks are more likely to be over priced, which leads to lower subsequent returns. During a low sentiment period, sentiment investors have much less impact on stock prices, so we would observe a weaker or no negative idiosyncratic risk and return relation.

744610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744610.value: This project aims to address the influence of investor sentiment on the relation between idiosyncratic risk and stock return. Finance theory predicts a positive or no relation between cross-sectional idiosyncratic risk and return, but previous empirical studies document mixed results on this relation. We want to show that investor sentiment plays a key role in the idiosyncratic risk and return relation, both the time series and the cross section relation. Our focus on investor sentiment is motivated by Baker and Wurgler (2006). They document that investor sentiment has significant effects on the cross-section of stock returns. We expect that high idiosyncratic risk stocks are likely to be more affected by shifts in investor sentiment. Therefore, the idiosyncratic risk and return relation should be different during low and high sentiment periods. If sentiment is high, high idiosyncratic risk stocks are more likely to be over priced and such mispricing is more difficult to arbitrage. This would lead to lower returns on high idiosyncratic risk stocks in the subsequent period. During the low sentiment period, the negative premium on high idiosyncratic risk stocks should weaken and even disappear. And if investors are compensated for not being able to diversify risk, then a positive premium on high idiosyncratic risk stocks should be discovered during the low sentiment period. We also expect our results to be robust among different conditional variance models, so that we can explain the contradictory results in previous empirical studies. In our preliminary results, we found supporting evidence that investor sentiment has significant impact on the relation between idiosyncratic risk and stock returns. With further work, we expect the empirical results to be consistent with our theory. Such results would make two important contributions. First, it would confirm the important role of investor sentiment, and suggest that future models of prices and expected returns should incorporate investor sentiment. Second, during high sentiment periods, the high idiosyncratic risk stocks carry a negative premium. Since investors usually cannot short sell such stocks due to high costs or high price volatility, they should avoid these stocks during high sentiment periods. 本研究旨在探讨投资者情绪对非系统性风险与股票收益之间关系的影响。金融理论认为这两者之间存在着正向关系，或不存在什么关系，然而之前的经验研究对此给出了模糊不清的证据。 我们想要表明，不论从横截面还是时间序列的角度，投资者情绪对非系统性风险与股票收益之间关系起到了关键作用。我们的这一研究最初来自于Baker与Wurlger（2006）的启发，他们的研究表明投资者情绪对股票收益有着显著的影响。我们则猜想较高的股票非系统性风险更有可能是投资者情绪改变的影响结果。 那么，非系统性风险与股票收益之间的关系在投资者情绪高低不同的时期应当有所不同。当投资者情绪较高时，具有较高非系统性风险的股票常常会被过高的定价而难以套利，这就导致了此类股票随之而来的较低收益率。当投资者情绪较低时，较高非系统性风险引起的溢价则会减弱甚至消失。如果投资者能够因无法分散风险而获得补偿，那么在投资者情绪较低的时期，较高非系统性风险带来的正的溢价就应当显现。我们希望这一结论在不同的条件方差模型中都应当是稳健的，这样我们就能够解释之前的经验研究中的一些看上去相互矛盾的结果。 在我们最初的结果中，我们发现投资者情绪对非系统性风险与股票收益之间关系存在显著影响的证据，进一步的研究则表明经验结果与我们的理论相一致。这一结果在两个方面具有重要的意义。第一，本研究证实了投资者情绪的重要作用，说明未来有关股票价格与预期收益的有关模型构建应当将投资者情绪包括进来。第二，在投资者情绪较高的时期，非系统性风险较高的股票具有负的溢价，而投资者由于高成本或高价格波动，常常难以做空此类股票，因此，在投资者情绪较高的时期，应当避免持有此类股票。

744610.label: Realisation of objectives
744610.value: We accomplish both objectives. First, we are able to apply and compare different conditional variance models on the expected idiosyncratic risk. Second, we are able to find that in both cross-sectional and time-series analysis, investor sentiment plays a crucial role in reconciling the relation between idiosyncratic volatility and expected stock returns. During high-sentiment periods, the return of high idiosyncratic volatility portfolio is significantly lower than that of low idiosyncratic volatility in the cross-sectional analysis. Furthermore, the market return is negatively associated with the aggregate idiosyncratic volatility in the time-series. In low-sentiment periods, there is no discernible relation between idiosyncratic volatility and expected stock returns. These results appear consistent with our hypothesis that during high-sentiment periods, sentiment traders overprice stocks with high idiosyncratic volatility, leading to lower subsequent stock returns.

745110.label: Project Objectives
745110.value: The proposed research primarily aims to study the effect of a Dance/movement-based psychotherapy program on Chinese breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy. Primary objectives examine the effect of the program on: (1) reducing symptom cluster (fatigue, distress, pain and sleep disturbance), (2) improving quality of life, in Chinese breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy. Primary objectives examine the effect of the program on: (1) reducing symptom cluster (fatigue, distress, pain and sleep disturbance), (2) improving quality of life, in Chinese breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy.

745110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745110.value: Cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy usually experience a cluster of overlapping physical and psychological symptoms such as fatigue, distress, sleep disturbance, and pain. These symptoms significantly affect patients’ daily functioning and quality of life during treatment, with long-term repercussions on health and illness prognosis. Though the need for psychosocial support for patients receiving treatment has been well-documented, intervention outcome research was underdeveloped compared to those for post-treatment survivors. Documented treatment programs were mostly either physical or psychological in nature. Given the multidimensional nature of the symptoms affecting patients physically and psychologically, an integrated therapeutic approach which intrinsically has both components is worth studying. There is also growing interest in the study of the relationship between symptom clusters and the Hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis functioning. Besides helping understand the etiology of the symptoms and their management, this line of research also has significant impact on the scientific inquiry of the mind-body interaction in health and illness. The present study is a randomized control trial. The primary aim is to study the impact of a dance/movement-based psychotherapy program on the symptom cluster and quality of life in Chinese breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy. The second aim is to investigate the effect of the intervention on cortisol rhythm, as well as the relationship between cortisol rhythm and the symptom cluster. 150 breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy will be recruited and randomized into the intervention and the waitlist control group. A 90-minute dance/movement-based psychotherapy program will be offered to the treatment group twice weekly for 3 weeks. Participants will be assessed before and after treatment in psychological and physiological domains including fatigue, stress, anxiety, depression, sleep quality, pain, and salivary cortisol level. The intervention program encompasses a physical component (gentle movement, dances, games, and improvisation), with a psychotherapeutic component based on the humanistic client-centered approach with problem solving and insight orientation. Emphasis is put on mutual support, self-care, stress managment, self-understanding and cultivation of a peaceful mind. The intervention is expected to reduce the symptoms and improve patients’ quality of life. The relationship between the symptom cluster and diurnal cortisol rhythm and the effect of the intervention on this biomarker will be examined. These results can inform the future design of treatment programs for cancer or non-cancer patients with similar symptoms and introduce the adoption of biomarkers for symptom management. Study findings also lay the groundwork for future research in mind-body medicine for the Chinese population.

745110.label: Realisation of objectives
745110.value: The primary objective of this study is to investigate the effectiveness of a dance/movement-based psychotherapy program on reducing symptom cluster (fatigue, stress, pain and sleep disturbance) and improving quality of life in Chinese breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy; while the secondary objective is to examine the relationships between symptom cluster and cortisol pattern, and the effects of the intervention on cortisol pattern. In order to achieve the mentioned objectives, we successfully recruited 147 breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy and had them randomized into treatment group (n=72) and control group (n=75). We analyzed all the data collected in this study which include quantitative psychosocial (questionnaires) and physiological (cortisol) data as well as qualitative verbal (verbal feedback and focus group) and non-verbal (drawings of body shapes) data collected at baseline and/or after the intervention. Since the data is very rich in content, within the limited time, we have tried our best to look at the major outcomes as well as other outcomes which are all related to this study. We looked at the baseline characteristics of this group of breast cancer women, and found that they had higher perceived stress, anxiety and pain severity compared with US breast cancer patients. Fatigue related to most of the symptoms. Participants with more server side effects (greater psychological distress, poorer perceived health and greater perceived stress) were associated with flatter diurnal cortisol slopes. Cortisol patterns and their symptom cluster were inter-related. When comparing the pre and post data in both groups, both quantitative and qualitative data indicated the Dance/ movement-based psychotherapy program was effective on reducing radiotherapy-related symptom cluster (i.e. fatigue, distress and pain) and improving the quality of life (better sleep, psychosocial improvements and regaining life control). Effects of the program on cortisol have been analyzed preliminarily. Due to the nested and complicated nature of cortisol data, we are currently working on more advanced statistical method for better understanding and reporting. Moreover, exploration on the participants' experiences, especially on specific body movement elements (body shapes, postures, personal space and rhythm) using focus group and verbal feedback demonstrated an awareness of transition and growth in the women. As a whole, we achieve the objectives of demonstrating the Dance/ movement-based program can help reduce symptom cluster and improve quality of life in breast cancer patients. We will continue to work on the data, in particular the cortisol data and qualitative data obtained in this study.

745110.value: Our findings suggest that Dance/movement-based psychotherapy program can help Chinese breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy on both physical symptoms (fatigue, pain and poor sleep) and psychological symptoms (stress, anxious and depression). It also helps them achieve better social connections and quality of life (Item 8.3, 8.5, 9.1, 9.5, 9.7, 9.10, 9.12, 9.13, 9.15, 9.19, &9.24). On investigating the interrelationships among symptom cluster, we found that breast cancer patient’s perceived stress, anxiety and pain severity were associated with severity of cancer related fatigue (Item 8.1); and fatigue also related to pain and quality of life (Item 9.6, 9.16). On examining the neuroendocrine function and its relationships with psychosocial variables, we demonstrated that fatigue level was associated with abnormal cortisol pattern in a preliminary analysis (Item 9.3). Sleep quality, negative emotions and anxiety related to cortisol level (Item 9.4, 9.8). Poorer psychological distress and poorer perceived health linked with flatter diurnal cortisol slope (Item 9.21&9.26). Dysregulation of Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal (HPA) axis functioning was suspected in this sample. Findings from this study also contribute to other areas in psycho-oncology. We demonstrated that majority of Chinese breast cancer women had dilemma in dietary restrictions during treatment (Item 9.2) and had used complementary therapy including Chinese herbs during Western cancer treatment (Item 9.9). Unmarried patients had more negative psychological reactions toward the treatment which affected their quality of life more (Item 9.17) than married women. The meanings attribute to recovery could also affect breast cancer patient’s physical and emotional functioning (Item 9.23). Since radiotherapy is the end stage of active treatment for most breast cancer patients, we also examined the experiences of cancer patients in this transitional period. We innovatively used a movement based focus group study. Results indicated that through moving and reflecting, participants regained the connection between the body and the emotions. Some of them found new insights and meaning (spiritual benefits) from their cancer experiences (Item 9.10, 9.11, 9.14, 9.18, 9.22). Finally, this study also contributes to scale development and validation. The psychometric properties of the Chinese Brief Fatigue Inventory (BFI) had been evaluated (Item 9.20). Based on this, using a factor mixture analysis, we suggested that cancer patients can be classified into specific clinically significant classes based on fatigue symptoms which might help make better clinical decisions and predictions (Item 8.4). Moreover, we also examined the Chinese Pittsburg Sleep Disturbance Index (PSQI) and demonstrated the satisfactory psychometric properties of the Chinese PSQI in this population (Item 8.2&9.25).

745110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745110.value: The immediate therapeutic effects of Dance/ movement-based program had been shown in this study on Chinese breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy. Though the side effects of radiotherapy will diminish after the end of treatment, long-term effects of the intervention program on participants’ psychosocial variables are worthy to study. A longitudinal follow up can be conducted on participants who had joined the treatment. Moreover, our study demonstrates the relationships between symptoms cluster, psychosocial variables and neuroendocrine function. Further investigation on which specific symptom, e.g. sleep patterns, pain, or depressed mood relates in what extent to neuroendocrine function and even immune function can contribute to better care for cancer patients. Both cross-sectional and longitudinal studies with immune and inflammatory markers can potentially achieve this purpose. Lastly, examining the effects of this intervention in samples other than breast cancer and women is also important. Given the beneficial effects on both physical and psychosocial aspects and enjoyable experiences as reflected by the participants in this study, the Dance/movement-based program can potentially be applied to other healthy and diseased populations. Its preventive effects on physical and mental are also warranted to study. We have already prepared a proposal on using dance/movement program on elderly population.

745110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
745110.value: Radiotherapy often leads to a series of physical side effects (fatigue, stress, anxiety, depression, pain and sleep disturbances) and affects patient’s quality of life. Better understanding on the inter-relationships among these symptoms, psychosocial factors, and endocrine function may help better planning on clinical care for patients in this period. This study demonstrates a close relationship between symptoms and abnormal cortisol pattern. It also shows a Dance/ movement-based psychotherapy can provide beneficial effects on reducing cancer-related symptoms, in particular fatigue and pain, as well as helps improve quality of life in Chinese breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy. With a focus on movement (non-verbal expression) and reflection (verbal expression and sharing), participants have a chance to reconnect the body and emotions, as well as re-examine their connections with others. Participants have increased awareness towards their bodies, inner feelings and even able to find meanings in their breast cancer experiences. Dance/ movement-based psychotherapy can bring about physical, psychosocial and spiritual benefits.

745210.label: Project Objectives
745210.value: To examine how different visual-to-auditory mapping tasks modulate the development of visual expertise through a combination of different methodologies. In particular we examine: - Logographic language reading, where word stimulus maps to syllables in pronunciation. - Alphabetic language reading, where word stimulus consists of letters that map to phonemes in pronunciation. - Music notation reading, where the vertical locations of stimuli (as opposed to the appearance) map to pitches in a systematic order. To use neurocomputational models that take into account known observations of visual anatomy to address processing differences among the three visual-to-auditory mapping tasks under examination, aiming to establish the link between cognitive processes and brain functions. To investigate the shift from LH to bilateral visual processing in the development of music reading expertise through both computational modeling and behavioral studies.

745210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745210.value: Many real-life visual tasks require us to link a visual input with an auditory (sound) output, such as reading words and music notes. These tasks usually have different demands. For example, reading English words (an alphabetic language) requires us to map letters to corresponding phonemes (consonants and vowels) in pronunciation: stimulus parts map to components in pronunciation. In contrast, reading Chinese characters (a logographic language) does not involve this letter-sound mapping; each character corresponds to a syllable in pronunciation. Music notation reading represents another type of mapping task: the locations of notes (as opposed to the appearance of stimuli) map to pitches in a systematic order. Recent research suggests that learning different visual tasks, even if with the same visual stimuli, can lead to qualitatively different visual processing in the brain. Here we examine the differences in visual processing among these different visual-to-auditory mapping tasks, in order to understand which brain areas are recruited and why, and how they differ for each task. We first examine the processing differences between alphabetic and logographic language reading and test the hypothesis that, given the same visual stimuli, the learning task alone (i.e. alphabetic vs. logographic mapping from visual word form to pronunciation) can lead to qualitatively different visual processing. Specifically, compared with logographic mapping, alphabetic mapping may require finer-grained visual processing that involves less holistic pattern recognition and more reliance on visual details (left hemisphere). We examine processing differences between the two mapping tasks through a human training study with psychophysical, eye tracking, and electrophysiological measures, and a corresponding computational modeling study. We then examine music notation reading. A recent brain imaging study showed that musicians use both left hemisphere (LH) and right hemisphere (RH) visual processing when reading music notes whereas non-musicians use the LH more. We test the hypothesis that this difference is due to a musician’s efficient use of the relative locations of notes on the staff to identify them and estimate the corresponding pitch changes; this distance (coordinate) judgment may require more RH visual processing compared with note location (categorical) judgments adopted by non-musicians. We first examine corresponding behavioral differences between musicians and non-musicians, and then test the hypothesis through both computational modeling and psychophysical studies. This research will contribute to our understanding of the link between cognitive processes and brain functions. It also has important educational implications for how to facilitate learning in single or multiple tasks. 在現實生活中，許多的視覺作業（例如閱讀文字和音符）要求我們將所接收的視覺資訊與相關的聽覺資訊（聲音）聯繫起來。這些作業通常有不同的要求。例如，閱讀英語（拼音語言）單詞時我們需要於發音前先將字母配對相應的音位（子音和母音）：將視覺刺激的部分對應發音的組件。相比之下，閱讀漢字（語素語言）並不需要對應字母與音位︰發音時，每個漢字對應一個音節。樂譜閱讀則表現了另一類的對應作業：音符的位置（而非刺激的外觀）有系統地對應不同的音高。最近的研究顯示，基於相同的視覺刺激，學習不同的視覺作業能夠導致大腦中不同性質的視覺加工。在這項研究中，我們研究由不同的視覺聲音對應作業與其導致的視覺加工的關係，從而了解有關腦區的作業，以及這些腦區引致作業上差異的原因和方法。 首先，我們測試在閱讀拼音及語素語言時視覺加工上的差異，從而檢驗以下的假設︰給予同樣的視覺刺激，光是不同的學習作業（即拼音及語素語言於文字與讀音之對應上的差異）便能導致不同性質的視覺加工。具體來說，相比起語素文字的對應，拼音文字的對應可能需要較細微的視覺加工，從而依賴較多視覺上的細節（左腦）並牽涉較少整體樣式的識別。我們用真人訓練研究來瞭解兩種對應作業於視覺加工上的差異，包括眼動追踪，心理物理學和電生理學方法，以及相應的計算機模擬研究。 然後，我們研究樂譜閱讀。最近的一項大腦成像研究顯示，音樂家閱讀音符時同時使用左腦和右腦作視覺加工，而非音樂家則較多使用左腦。我們檢驗以下的的假設︰閱讀音符時，音樂家與非音樂家之所以使用不同的腦區是由於音樂家高效地運用五線譜上音符的相對位置，以確認音符並估計其相應的音高變化﹔這個距離的判斷（坐標式）與非音樂家對音符位置的判斷（歸類式）相比，可能需要更多的右腦視覺加工。我們首先研究上述於音樂家與非音樂家間的行為差異，然後通過計算機模擬和心理物理學研究檢驗假設。 這項研究將有助於加深我們對認知加工過程與大腦功能關係的理解，而且這研究亦對促進學習單個或多個作業具有重要的教育意義。

745210.label: Realisation of objectives
745210.value: Objective 1. We have examined how different visual-to-auditory mapping tasks modulate the development of visual expertise through a combination of different methodologies, including computational modeling, behavioral studies (including both behavioral measures and eye tracking data), and EEG examinations. In particular, we have examined logographic language reading, alphabetic language reading, music notation reading, and face recognition. Most of the results have been published in peer-reviewed journals, conference proceedings, or conference abstracts. Two related manuscripts are under review, and three are currently in preparation for journal publication. Objective 2. We have used neurocomputational models that take into account known observations of visual anatomy to address processing differences among different visual-to-auditory mapping tasks, including logographic word reading, alphabetic word reading, music notation reading, and face recognition. Most of the results have been published in several peer-reviewed journals, conference proceedings, and conference abstract. One manuscript about computational modeling is currently under review for journal publication, and another one is in preparation. These findings were able to establish the link between cognitive processes and brain functions. Objective 3. We have investigated the shift from left hemisphere to bilateral visual processing in the development of music reading expertise through both computational modeling and behavioral studies. Some of the results have been published in peer-reviewed conference proceedings/conference abstracts. One manuscript is currently under revision for journal publication.

745210.label: Major findings and research outcome
745210.value: Through computational modeling and behavioral experiments, we found that hemispheric lateralization in visual word recognition can be influenced by: (1) visual similarity among words in a lexicon. (2) Whether word reading involves consistent letter-sound mapping (Hsiao & Lam, 2013). These two factors can explain why different Chinese character types involve different lateralization (Hsiao & Cheung, in press; APCV 2011 & CogSci 2011), why Chinese and English word reading involve different lateralization, and why European-English bilinguals showed stronger left hemisphere lateralization in processing English words as compared with Chinese-English bilinguals (Lam & Hsiao, 2014; CogSci 2011 & APCV 2011). We further examined the difference between logographic (e.g., Chinese) and alphabetic reading (e.g., English). We found that (1) Chinese character recognition involves more visuospatial processing whereas English word recognition involves more phonological processing (Fernandes, Wammes, & Hsiao, 2013). (2) Alphabetic and logographic reading training leads to different holistic processing and hemispheric lateralization effects (CogSci 2015). (4) Experience with alphabetic vs. logographic reading can also modulate holistic processing in speech perception (CogSci 2014 & 2015). We also examined the relationship between holistic processing and hemispheric lateralization and factors that can influence the two effects in different visual recognition tasks, through computational modeling, behavioral, and EEG examinations. We found that (1) the relationship between holistic processing and hemispheric lateralization depends on whether the recognition task relied on featural or configural information (CogSci 2011 and ICONIP 2013; one manuscript under review). (2) Sensorimotor experience can influence holistic processing and lateralization effects differently (Tso, Au, & Hsiao, 2014; CogSci 2011, VSS 2012, CogSci 2012, HKPS 2013, CogSci 2013, VSS 2014, CogSci 2015). (3) The two hemispheres can be equally holistic depending on the task requirements and perceivers’ experience (APCV 2013 & CogSci 2015; one manuscript under review). (4) Simplified and traditional Chinese readers showed asymmetric transfer effects in holistic processing, but similar transfer effects in hemispheric lateralization (CogSci 2012, VSS 2012, APCV 2013, VSS 2014; two manuscripts under review). (5) The right hemisphere may play a dominant role in unconscious processing (CogSci 2013, APCV 2013, & VSS 2014). (6) Analytic eye movement patterns in face recognition are associated with better performance than holistic patterns (Chuk, Chan, & Hsiao, 2014; CogSci 2013, CICEM 2014, VSS 2014) (7) Reading direction alone can account for some perceptual asymmetry effects (CogSci 2012, VSS 2012, & VSS 2014). (8) Music reading expertise selectively improves categorical judgment with musical notations (APCV 2011).

745210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745210.value: Future work may further develop the research in the following directions: 1. Neural correlates of the development of expertise in music reading: Electrophysiological examinations can be used to further examine the shift from left hemisphere to bilateral processing in music notation reading expertise. We have planned a related pilot EEG study. 2. Influence from sensorimotor experiences: Further studies can be conducted to examine how writing/drawing experiences influences perceptual expertise development in different visual-to-auditory mapping tasks. We have had some preliminary results and will continue this line of research. 3. The relationship between perceptual expertise effects (such as holistic processing and hemispheric lateralization effects) and eye movement strategies: Future work may examine the association between different eye movement patterns and various perceptual expertise effects. We have started some preliminary examinations along this line of research.

745210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
745210.value: Through behavioral, computational, and electrophysiological examinations, here we show that learning different real-life visual-to-auditory mapping/recognition tasks, such as reading words or music notations, involves different cognitive processes and brain regions. More specifically, reading words in English, an alphabetic language in which individual letters map to individual phonemes/sounds, involves more left hemisphere processing than reading Chinese characters, which does not involve this letter-sound mapping. In contrast, music reading, which involves locations of notes (as opposed to the appearance of stimuli) mapping to pitches in a systematic order, seemed to involve a transition from left hemisphere to bilateral brain processing. We also examined the relationship between hemispheric lateralization and holistic processing effects in visual recognition tasks. We found that although right hemisphere lateralization has been associated with holistic processing in the literature, these two processes do not always go together; it depends on task requirements and perceivers’ experiences. In addition, we found that sensorimotor experience may play an important role in shaping the cognitive processes involved in visual recognition expertise. These findings have contributed significantly to our understanding of the link between cognitive processes and brain functions and provided important educational implications for how to facilitate learning in real-life visual recognition tasks.

745310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745310.value: There are over one million of Taiwanese businesspeople (Taishang台商) living in China. From Beijing’s perspective, Taishang could be a useful leverage for advancing its policy in Taiwan. The political leverage, however, is based on the assumption that Taishang can exercise influence and are willing to do in favor of Beijing’s policy. But tough questions are: Are Taishang willing to do so? Have Taishang identified themselves more with Beijing after years of living in the mainland? This project seeks to understand Taishang’s political identification through opinion survey and content analysis. Taishang’s identity is complex, fluid, and elusive, and the research on their political attitudes and identity from polling and surveying is very thin, due to the difficulty of conducting survey in China and the time consumed to win over Taishang trust. To better understand them, we plan to use in-depth interview, combining with opinion survey, to look into their political mind. This study is a two-step process. The first step is a survey of Taishang’s political identity before going to the mainland. We use the professional support and database at Election Study Center, National Chengchi University for focused analysis. The second step is fieldwork on whether and how Taishang’s mainland experiences have changed their identity choice. Most Taishang do not want to be PRC citizens. But, on the other hand, the longer they live in the mainland, the more they become estranged with the Taiwanese society. That put them in an awkward position of choosing political identity (政治身份). This project proposes to examine multiple dimensions and levels of political identification among Taishang. First, we differentiate Taishang by their ethnic background (省籍), political orientation and personal attributes. Second, we use the level of social contacts, adaptation, interest calculus, the effect of socialization, and personal life impacts as independent variables to explain their political identity choices. Third, we will use logistic regression models to construct cognitive mapping of Taishang’s identity preferences and factors that contributing to the formation of such preferences. This project benefits and builds on my previous GRF research on Taishang (HKU 7692/06H). Since 2006, we have accumulated over 220 cases of Taishang opinions survey and interviews. With further GRF support, we can enlarge the scale of opiniond survey and interview up to 1,000-1,200 cases. We are confident our research team, with years of experiences and the trust we have developed with Taishang, can deliver state-of-the-art research on Taishang’s political identity. 目前大約有近一百萬台商及其家屬在中國大陸居住和工作，他們主要分佈於珠三角﹑長三角和福建省，並有逐漸向大陸其他省份擴散的趨勢。隨著近年兩岸“大三通”的實現，兩岸之間的經商和交流更加便利，越來越多的臺灣人選擇到大陸發展。臺灣人在大陸居住的經歷會不會影響他們對大陸社會和兩岸關係的看法和態度呢？他們的政治認同會不會由此發生變化呢？如此眾多的台商在大陸居住，會不會成為北京的對台政策的政治杠杆呢？至今為止，我們對台商政治態度和身分認同的研究仍然十分薄弱，可以引用的文獻和資料鳳毛麟角。這一方面是由於此類調查和研究受到諸多限制，到目前為止未有學者進行大規模的調查研究。另一方面是由於台商本身的自我防範，一般問卷調查很難掌握第一手可靠資料。本專案將通過問卷調查和深入訪談相結合的方式，對在珠三角﹑長三角和福建居住的台商進行田野調查，重點研究他們在大陸的生活和工作經歷對他們的身份認同有何影響，哪些因素影響了他們對大陸社會和兩岸關係的看法，這種看法改變會不會影響他們政治認同的選擇，以及這種改變對今後兩岸關係有何意義。

745310.label: Realisation of objectives
745310.value: This project has largely achieved its research goals. The central research questions of the project is whether there is an identity shift among Taiwanese businessmen (Taishang) after years of experiences working and living in the mainland, and, if any, how and to what extent it has happened. The research team has collected over 550 samples of opinion survey and in-depth interview with the Taiwanese business people who have at least worked and lived in the mainland for six months. The dataset we have built through this project is unprecedented and largest ever in the field. The process of our data collection over the last three years was challenging, but we have managed to collect a set of high-quality data. Since Taishang have a strong sense of self-protection, we did everything we could to ensure the quality and reliability of the data. We were fortunate in recruiting a team of Taiwanese postgraduate students from National Chengchi University to conduct the survey. From 2011 to 2013, we surveyed in Dongguan and the Greater Shanghai region (including Kunshan), two areas of the largest clusters of Taishang. Our interviews were conducted in a way comfortable to Taishang. In addition to questionnaire, our interviewers (2 each time) also conducted in-depth interview to follow up on the issues in the questionnaire. Each interview resulted in a written note of 1000-1500 Chinese characters. With such a rich dataset and written interview notes, we are proud and confident to say that we did a superb job in our empirical research, and with this dataset we will be able to produce first-class academic publication in the Taishang study. Did we solve all the puzzles we had? The answer is no. The issue of Taishang’s identity change is an extremely complicated issue. The literature tends to define Taiwanese identity either in terms of Taiwan identity (臺灣認同) or China identity (中國認同). Although most Taiwanese see their identity in a negative term of being“not Chinese,” our research found this dichotomized definition does not work. There is identity change but it is a matter of degree. Another complication is their identity shift taking place in the context of their assimilation and adaptation to the mainland society. Since they belong to the same cultural roots, their identity transformation is not an “either-or” issue. Most of Taishang have well adapted to the mainland society, but have managed to maintain their Taiwanese political identity.
