745310.label: Major findings and research outcome
745310.value: Our survey included a questionnaire of 55 questions and in-depth interview that measure whether and how Taishang’s identify has changed. One of major findings is our empirical data suggests evidence of identity change among Taishang. Taiwanese identity is a very complex issue. It is shaped by their ethnic background (省籍), political orientation, and other personal attributes. Taishang are no different. Yet given their shared “national identity,” we found there are factors causing Taishang identify shift and this change varies by their primordial ties and other personal attributes. Our survey use the level of social contacts and adaptation, interest calculus, the effect of socialization, personal life impacts as independent variables to study the identity change. Although the majority of Taishang have found comfort in adapting to life in the mainland society, a small number of them remain linguistically and culturally distinct from the local society. Taishang’s social identity sometimes takes the form of “club membership” as well as “we-group.” Another major finding concerns dimension and level of identity change among Taishang. Our survey finds there are behavioral changes among Taishang in terms of local contacts, socialization, perception of interests, life planning, and child education. But there is little change in terms of political identity. Our data also shows that most Taishang’s political attitudes are not rooted in a parochial ethnic nationalism, rather, in a more nuanced rationality of belongings. This nuanced rationality involves their “politically-correct” views of “Taiwan” and preferred views of cross-Strait relations. Most Taishang don’t see China as ‘enemy’ and are more open-minded about future cross-Strait relations. They see no contradiction between making money in the mainland and retaining their Taiwanese identity. They can culturally and socially identify and even assimilate into the mainland society, but still retain a strong psychological attachment to Taiwan. They view themselves culturally Chinese and politically Taiwanese. This tells us Taishang's concept of political identity is no longer a nativist appeals (being ethnic Taiwanese), rather, it is more “civic.” Taishang increasingly realize Taiwan is not differentiated from the mainland so much by language, culture or livelihood, but more by the values and beliefs concerning socio-political system. There is variance among age and partisan groups. The older and more established business-oriented people are more “rational” than the younger and less established people. But even the younger people are no longer “anti-China” as they used to.

745310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745310.value: The Taishang study is an emerging inter-disciplinary field of academic enquiry, cutting cross into political science, sociology, psychology, economics, and humanities. They have moved to the mainland, largely driven by economic opportunities and business incentives. Yet, are they interest-driven and political indifferent? They travel across political boundaries, and they maintain primordial ties with Taiwan on one hand, and attempt to adapt to the mainland society on the other hand. Although the majority of Taishang do not want to be brainwashed by the “patriotic education” in the mainland, the longer they live in the mainland, the more they become estranged with the Taiwanese society. So that is an important question for scholarly inquiry on political identification. German philosopher Hans-Georg Gadamer argues that people have "historically effected consciousness" embedded in particular history, culture, and political boundary that shaped them. In future research we need to design better ways of measuring how Taishang’s consciousness is transformed in context of their China experience. We need to further explore how Taishang socialize in the mainland society, how government policies and citizenship politics in the mainland shape their views of cross-Strait relations, and how identity politics and partisan politics in Taiwan shape their political identity.

745310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
745310.value: This study is about identity change among Taiwanese businessmen (Taishang) living in the China mainland. Taishang share the same culture and civilization with the mainland people but have different political ideology and orientation. Our research attempts to find any identity shift among them and, if any, how and to what extent it has happened. The research project has collected over 550 samples of opinion survey and in-depth interview with Taishang. The dataset we have built is unprecedented and largest ever in the field. Our survey used the level of social contacts and adaptation, interest calculus, the effect of socialization, personal life impacts as independent variables to measure the identity change among Taishang. We found they can socially identify with the local society but still retain a strong psychological attachment to Taiwan, a political community they consider different from the mainland. They are culturally Chinese and politically Taiwanese. We also found that Taishang’s concept of political identity is no longer just a nativist appeals (being ethnic Taiwanese), rather, it is more “civic.” They increasingly realize Taiwan is not differentiated from the mainland so much by language or culture, but more by political values and beliefs.

745410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
745410.value: 跨文化中的特质交易: 作为内部人士有用嗎?

745410.label: Co - Investigator(s)
745410.value: Prof Lee, Cynthia Dr Liu, Jun

745410.label: Project Objectives
745410.value: Develop a cross-cultural conceptual model relating perceived insider status to i-deals and employee contribution by applying and extending the social-identity theory. Develop and validate a group-reference measure of perceived insider status. Develop and refine a measure of ex post i-deals (i-deals that are negotiated after an employee has been at work). Develop and validate a social identity based measure of collectivism. Examine longitudinally the relationship between perceived insider status, i-deals, collectivism and employee contribution.

745410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745410.value: The present proposal is an attempt to examine the functionality of idiosyncratic deals (i-deals: Rousseau, 2001) in cross-cultural settings. I-deals are personalized employment arrangements that can be unique for each employee and are, supposedly, beneficial to both employees and employers (Rousseau, 2005). I-deals are frequently observed in both the academia and the business world. Research on i-deals, however, can benefit from more systematic analyses of the foundation of i-deals and the generalization of the theories of i-deals to cross-cultural contexts. We propose that when employees perceive themselves as insiders of their organizations, they would likely seek and receive i-deals. In return, they would take on exceptional responsibilities. We used social identity (cf. Mael &Ashforth, 1992) as a construct to link theoretically employees’ perception of their insider status within an organization, i-deals, employee contribution and cross-cultural considerations. We further consider the contents of “social identity” in cross-cultural contexts. People from varies cultures have been found to differ in how they relate to bigger groups or collectives. Following Brewer and Chen’s conceptualization of collectivism (2007), we propose that employees who base their social identity on relationships to significant members of an ingroup (relational collectivism) would differ from employees who base their social identity on categorical group membership (group collectivism) in how they respond to perceived insider status. For relational collective employees, they will more likely seek and receive i-deals if their perceptions of insider status are based on relationships with important members of the ingroup. For group collective employees, they will more likely seek and receive i-deals if their perceptions of insider status are based on being a member of an important or high status in-group. The present proposal contributes theoretically to understandings of relationships between perceived insider status, i-deals, cultural values and employee contributions using social identity theory The present proposal also contributes to the management of i-deals by highlighting how i-deals can be functional. 此建议书尝试着研究“特质交易”在跨文化背景中的功能（简称i-deals: Rousseau, 2001）。特质交易是具化到个人的雇佣安排，对每个员工来说可以是独一无二的，并且被认为会对雇员和雇主都有利（Rousseau, 2005）。在学术界和商界我们都经常可以观察到特质交易这一现象。 关于特质交易的研究，可以进一步从系统的关于特质交易的基础的分析和在跨文化背景中的运用中受益。我们提出当员工认为自己在公司里是内部人士，他们更加倾向于去寻找或者接受特质交易。作为回报，他们也会承担额外的责任。我们使用社会认同 （查阅Mael &Ashforth, 1992）作为一个构念去从理论上连接员工关于自己是否是公司内部人士的感知以及特质交易，员工贡献和跨文化因素。 我们同时进一步考量在跨文化背景中“社会认同”的内容。来自不同文化背景的人们会以不同的方式与更大的社会体联系起来。引用Brewer和Chen关于集体主义的概念（2007），我们提出将自己的社会身份建立于与一个团体里面一些重要成员的关系之上的员工（关系集体主义）和另一些将自己的社会身份建立与所在团体的类别之上的员工（团体集体主义）将会有不同方式去感知自己是不是公司内部人士。对于具有关系集体主义的员工来说，如果关于自己是不是内部人士的认知是建立在和一些团体内重要成员的关系上，他们会寻找或接受特质交易。对于具有团体集体主义的员工来说，如果关于自己是不是内部人士的认知是建立在拥有重要或者较高层的在团体内的地位上，他们会寻找或接受特质交易。 此建议书引用社会认同理论丰富了关于对内部人士感知，特质交易，文化价值员工贡献的关系的理解。并且突出了特质交易的功能性从而对特质交易的管理也作出了贡献。

745410.label: Realisation of objectives
745410.value: We have developed a cross-cultural conceptual model relating perceived insider status to i-deals and employee contribution by applying and extending the social-identity theory. We have developed and validated a group-reference measure of perceived insider status. We have developed and refined a measure of ex post i-deals (i-deals that are negotiated after an employee has been at work). We have developed and validated a social identity based measure of collectivism. We have examined longitudinally the relationship between perceived insider status, i-deals, collectivism and employee contribution. Based on our findings, we developed an alternate conceptual model that included idiosyncratic deals, self-enhancement (conceptually based on the self-identity theory) and individualism (conceptually the other end of the dimension of individualism-collectivism). We published this conceptual model in the Journal of Applied Psychology, a top-tier journal in management.

745410.label: Major findings and research outcome
745410.value: We developed our grant proposal based on a social-identity approach to conceptualizing effects of i-deals. When we collected the data, we included also self-enhancement (related to the self-identity approach) as a comparative construct to social-identity. We found that self-enhancement theory, a theory that is conceptually related to self-identity theory, was more powerful than social-identity theory in explaining the effects of i-deals. In our paper to be published in the Journal of Applied Psychology (published in e-form already), we used a 3-wave lagged design that involved a multisource sample including 230 employees and 102 supervisors from 2 Chinese companies. In this study, we compared the mediating roles of social exchange and self-enhancement and the moderating role of individualism in the relationships between i-deals and employee outcomes, as indicated by proactive behaviors and affective commitment. The results of bootstrapping analyses confirm the mediating effects of social exchange and self-enhancement. In addition, employees with high levels of individualism are more receptive to self-enhancement effects; in contrast, employees with low levels of individualism are more receptive to social exchange effects. We suggested that self-enhancement in specific and a self-oriented approach in general would be fruitful for conceptualizing effects of i-deals. We have also examined the effects of constructs that are pertinent to employees’ self-concepts on employee PIS. Specifically, we propose that employees’ past accomplishments and future prospects are important determinants of their sense of self-worth and perceived worth to their organizations, and are important predictors of perceived insider status and employee contributions. In a sample of 298 employee-supervisor dyads from 17 Chinese companies, we found support for this proposition. We found further that the possession of social skills would strengthen the effects of past accomplishment and future prospect on employee outcomes.

745410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745410.value: It is interesting to note that in our multiple data sets and papers (including conference papers and the Journal of Applied Psychology paper), we found self-enhancement and individualism to be more powerful explanations of i-deals and perceived insider status than social-identity and collectivism are. Even though some theorists have projected social- versus self-identity and individualism versus collectivism as polar dimensions, we did not find symmetric effects of the two ends of the dimensions. We further found that employees’ sense of self-worth based on their past accomplishments and future prospects with their employers are powerful predictors of PIS. These findings led us to consider the importance of teasing out when self-based versus social-based identity would explain employees’ relation to the organization and their contributions. We have collected four waves of data that included variables like insider status, relational/group collectivism, past accomplishments, future prospects, desire for upward mobility and employee outcomes like innovative behavior and taking-charge behaviors. We are hoping to finalize a conceptual model that would provide insights into when self-based versus social-based constructs would explain employee perceptions and behaviors.

745410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
745410.value: We found that idiosyncratic-deals (I-deals), work arrangements that are tailor-made for individual employees, are powerful in cultivating employees’ emotional ties, as well as behavioral contributions, to their employers. One important explanation for the effects of I-deals focuses on the importance of the sense of self-identity of employees. Employees work to enhance their sense of self-esteem and worth. When they perceive that they are special to and valued by the employer, as evident by the granting of I-deals, their sense of self-esteem and self-worth would be enhanced. They are more likely to perceive themselves as having special status within the organization. Consequently, they would make more significant contributions to the employer. We also found that employees who are individualistic were more responsive to self-enhancing initiatives. Overall, the findings suggest the importance of treating employees with respect and offering opportunities to employees to enhance their self-concepts. We suggested that I-deals, past accomplishment and future prospects are things that employers can leverage to enhance self-concepts of employees.

745610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745610.value: This proposal focuses on an issue of major importance to learning in Hong Kong higher education: the feedback second language students receive on their written assignments – both from subject tutors and language instructors. Feedback is a particularly significant aspect of learning as it offers the kind of individualized attention that is otherwise rarely possible under normal classroom conditions. With the expansion of university provision in recent years and the impending widening of access to greater numbers of students through the implementation of the 4-year curriculum, this aspect of teaching and learning assumes even greater importance. Students receive various types of response to their writing, all carrying different messages about university values and beliefs, about the role of writing in learning, about their identity as students, about their competence as writers, and about their induction into disciplinary epistemologies. The rationale for this study is that it is important to discover what these messages are, what tutors intend to achieve with them, how students understand them, and what they contribute to learning. The proposed study therefore seeks to illuminate the attention tutors give to matters of literacy in their written feedback and what their comments communicate to students about their writing, their learning, and how their disciplines use language to construct knowledge. The study will adopt a case study methodology by focusing on six undergraduate students (ten will be followed as a precaution against mishap or dropouts) who speak English as a Second Language in each of four subject areas selected to represent a broad cross-section of academic practice: Business studies, Biology, Engineering, and History. It will examine the perceptions of both the student subjects and each of their tutors concerning the feedback given and received on written assignments, the feedback itself, and the student responses to this feedback in subsequent work. A methodology which employs student and tutor interviews and text analyses of tutor written comments and student text responses will help illuminate what readers intend to convey in their feedback, how receivers understand and respond to it, and what this means for teaching and learning. This research will therefore have important outcomes: for our understanding of feedback and its relationship to learning, for providing insights into the ways practitioners and students see the literacy practices of the disciplines studied, and for the practical applications of improving teaching and learning. 這項建議書集中研究一項在香港高等教育學習的重要議題：以英語為第二語言學生從學科教師和語言導師所獲得對他們書寫作業的反饋。 這項研究將採個案考查方法，重點放在六個以英語作為第二語言的本科生上（十個學生將被跟隨作為閃失或退出的一項預防措施）。那些學生是從四個有廣泛代表性的學科領域中挑選的, 它們是商學，生物學，工程學及歷史。本項目會研究學生及導師對反饋有關的看法：範圍包括導師給予書寫作業的反饋及學生書寫作業獲得的反饋，反饋本身及學生對其收到的反饋的應對與跟進工作。研究方法是採用學生和導師訪問，文本分析導師的書面意見和學生的應對。這方法有助說明讀者在他們的反饋所打算轉達的意思，接收者對反饋的理解和應對，以及反饋對教與學的意義。因此，本研究將具有重要的成果：會有助我們理解反饋和其與學習的關係，對參加者和學生對所學學科的文字運用的看法給予洞察，以及有助改善教與學的實際應用。

745610.label: Realisation of objectives
745610.value: This proposal focuses on an issue of major importance to learning in Hong Kong higher education: the feedback second language students receive on their written assignments – both from subject tutors and language instructors. All the objectives were achieved. Interviews were conducted with twenty four first and second year undergraduate students, six from each of four faculties (Business, Science, Engineering and Arts) and with twenty academics form the same fields and fifteen English language teachers. Overall about 120 hours of interview data were recorded, transcribed and analysed using NVivo. Samples of students' written work which had received feedback from tutors on both their content and language course were also collected and analysed to provide triangulated support for conclusions. The analysis involved moving from individual perceptions to common elements. The student responses were categorised into various themes and checked by a graduate research assistant and myself with an inter-rater agreement of kappa 0.8. Several themes emerged relating largely to how teachers gave feedback, what they commented on, and how much they wrote, identifying recurring, developing and significant patterns and themes. The results have been presented in a number of peer-reviewed journals and in conference presentations and professional development seminars.

745610.label: Major findings and research outcome
745610.value: The interviews also showed that students come to notice discernible messages in this feedback that told them about the discipline they are studying, about its communicative practices, and about how they should engage with texts and lecturers. These messages do not always correspond with the intentions of tose giving the feedback. It was possible to identify five broad themes in these messages, relating to: 1. the importance of language accuracy in academic writing 2. the role of writing in disciplinary communication 3. the role of writing in learning 4. the value of feedback in developing knowledge and skills 5. the nature of the teacher-student relationship For many students the absence of any focus on writing in their tutor's feedback suggests that conventions are things to be picked up rather than learned and that writing is simply a means of assessment rather than a part of learning disciplinary forms of argument. The delayed nature of much feedback also conveyed the idea that written work was unimportant to their tutors. The reluctance of many subject tutors to engage with students’ ideas and understandings in their writing to foster such learning is also apparent in the student interviews. For many learners it is difficult to sustain a view that feedback is a potentially useful learning resource when their subject tutors give the impression that feedback has little value in the development of their subject knowledge or of a disciplinary-appropriate rhetorical competence. Finally, at the same time students are acquiring impressions of how their teachers might understand writing and their attitudes to teaching and learning from feedback, they also glean information about the nature of the teacher-student relationship itself. Embedded in tutors’ feedback practices are messages concerning relative power-distance dynamics and how teacher-student interactions should be conducted. Providing an unadorned grade, delaying the return of papers and failing to discuss comments with students suggest to students that their teachers believe it is not worth engaging in a dialogue with them on their writing. It signals what appears as an aloof and uninterested stance towards them. These results have provided the basis for 3 ISI papers ad one book chapter together with several presentations at major conferences.

745610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745610.value: There are two main ways forward. First, to conduct the research with a larger sample of students and tutors, in more universities and in more disciplines. This would help to flesh out the baseline results provided by this study. It would also be advantageous to focus more closely on the relationship between the feedback providers and the feedback they give as this may offer insights into any connections between individuals (their training, experience, backgrounds, etc.) and styles of feedback The second way forward is to develop workshop materials to raise tutors' awareness of these messages and how they might make them more positive and productive.

745610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
745610.value: While feedback research has largely addressed the practices of teachers, this project has shifted attention to the meanings students take from these practices. Where feedback is perceived as timely, individualised and focused it conveys encouragement and a sense of the importance of writing, but where it is seen as perfunctory, delayed and unrelated to their individual needs, these messages are negative and fail to support students’ efforts to master academic writing practices. Quality feedback supports learning by revealing any gap between students’ current performance and expected levels of achievement and assisting them to narrow that gap. But because these students are rarely provided with feedback which helps them to conceptualize how disciplinary communication expresses epistemological beliefs. This study suggests that the overriding message students take from their tutors’ feedback is that academic literacy is an abstract and self-evident style of writing unrelated to particular academic communities. They come to believe that they simply have to master a set of grammar rules to write accurately rather than understanding the argument practices of their fields. Teachers should be encourage to reflect on their feedback and consider its use to better scaffold learning in formal mentoring schemes and CPD workshops.

746010.label: Realisation of objectives
746010.value: All project objectives have been achieved or are still being achieved on the basis of the data sets collected and analyzed. The gathering of data for the project was affected by several factors (1) change of PI which requires establishing a new set of relationships in Gansu (2) more focus placed on senior secondary three gaosan students as China entered a stage of mass secondary schooling (3) having to await approval from RGC to hire research assistance (incl. HKU grads) in Chinese mainland (4) schools were only willing to engage students in our surveys at certain times of the school year due to preparation for the national college and entrance examination (5) more focus on ethnic minority schools due to the background of the PI in ethnic minority studies and the decision for surveys in ethnic minority counties to constitute half of the survey data. The data sets include 10 counties (incl. the five ethnic minority autonomous counties) in which nearly 3,000 final year senior high school students (the majority were between 16-21 years old) and nearly 500 teachers were surveyed. Also, I have been able to acquire the gaokao scores on the national college and university entrance examination of the students we surveyed. This was unanticipated and is unprecedented in past research. Much more analysis and dissemination is expected in the year ahead with two book contracts in play (one with Routledge by the PI&2Cs), and one with Johns Hopkins University Press by the PI with a focus on how China balances increased demands for educational equality with aspirations to go global. In short, this is a long term endeavor and we will be working more with the data sets, including another field visit by the PI in January 2016.

746010.label: Major findings and research outcome
746010.value: 1. Rural families have become increasingly involved in their children’s education at all levels, and increasingly in senior secondary level education (Xie&Postiglione 2014). This is due to the increased demand beyond nine-years of schooling, the rapid expansion of higher education, parents increased access to information about education through popular media, and rural to urban migration. Nevertheless, there is increased stratification among rural and minority families in the household resources. See finding 4 below. 2. Students who are most successful in their gaokao scores and their access to higher education are those whose families have the time and household resources to engage with their children at home, but also outside of the home (Sargent, Kong, Zhang 2014) . Some families provide more of an enabling environment for the fostering of cultural cultivation that helps their children succeed in school (Xie&Postiglione 2015). Cultural cultivation includes parent participation at home with study related issues, as well as guidance and communication. Materials resources contributing to cultural cultivation included books as well as payment for private tutoring. 3. Successful parent strategies include providing their children with sufficient food, nutritional support (especially when children board ta school), as well as time spent and interest in their well-being. It also includes interacting with school teachers, including gifting. Again, materials resources matter (Postiglone, Kong, Hannum (in press). See outcome 4 below. 4. While opportunities to enter tertiary education have increased, the proportion of poor rural and minority students going entering top tier universities has decreased, despite quota increases for students from poor areas, as well as traditional policies for ethnic minorities (Postiglione, forthcoming). In this context, parent socio-economic status has come to have a strong influence involvement on success in taking the gaokao, gaining access to higher education in general and top-tier universities in particular (Postiglione 2015). Cadre families continue to have an advantage. Market forces have created new economic elite whose household resources support their children’s educational success. The case of ethnic minorities is more complex. 5. This is especially relevant in the case of ethnic minorities because they tend to drop out of school earlier than Han Chinese students. Moreover, if they gate to senior secondary school and take the gaokao exam, their scores differ. For example, the average Han Chinese students score is 409. For Hui Muslims it is 369. For Tibetans, it is 336. For Dongxiang Muslims, it is 329.

746010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746010.value: Opportunities abound for further development: (1) PI and PDF received a research grant from the Ford Foundation to examine rural student experience at top-tier universities.(2) PI is supported by Asian Development Bank to examine the employment of college and university graduates in China, especially those who attend second and third tier institutions, most from rural areas.(3) Longitudinal data will be gathered.

746010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746010.value: While opportunities for student, including from poor rural and ethnic minority areas of western China to access higher education have increased, they still score below the national average on the national college and entrance examination, despite the increased efforts and strategies of their parents to support their educational success. Moreover, opportunities have become increasingly stratified as cadre families maintain their advantage over traditional farming families and new economic elite brings their social capital and material resources to bear on fostering an enabling environment of cultural cultivation that improved their children’s educational future.

746110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
746110.value: 學生需要什麼樣的知識和技能才能積極有效地使用技術輔助外語學習？

746110.label: Co - Investigator(s)
746110.value: Dr Ki, Wing Wah Dr Mishra, Punya Dr SHUM, Mark Shiu Kee Prof Zhao, Yong

746110.label: Project Objectives
746110.value: To understand the relative significance of MTACK in fostering active and effective use of common ICTs for foreign language learning To explore its potential association with gains in foreign language learning To unravel the support learners need in developing such knowledge and skills
rows: To understand the relative significance of MTACK in fostering active and effective use of common ICTs for foreign language learning
To explore its potential association with gains in foreign language learning
To unravel the support learners need in developing such knowledge and skills

746110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
746110.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research to understand what knowledge and skills students need in order to make active and effective use of common information and communication technologies (ICTs) for foreign language learning. It proposes that a crucial but largely neglected component is the meta-cognitive understanding and skills on the effective use of various common ICTs for various language learning needs (MTACK). The project tests this claim through a quasi-experimental design that compares the quantity and quality of autonomous use of common ICTs for foreign language learning between the learners who are equipped with such knowledge and skills and those who are not. Actively engaging in autonomous learning with common ICTs is an essential 21st century learning skill. However, learners are found not using ICTs for learning despite the accumulating literature on the educational potential of various technologies. Thus supporting learners to develop such capacity becomes a pressing issue, and identifying the required knowledge and skills is the first and foremost step. Current literature has conceptualized this knowledge and skills set as autonomous learning skills and digital literacies. However, digital literacies are still too generic to ensure effective application of ICTs for specific learning needs. We propose that a more contextualized approach that focuses on MTACK would be more effective. We hypothesize that MTACK is more facilitative of active and effective use of common ICTs for foreign language learning, and will test this claim through a quasi-experimental research. To help students harness the educational power of technologies, we have to foremost understand what knowledge and skills students need to possess. A quasi-experimental study on the effectiveness of two different conceptualizations will greatly enhance our understanding. It will push the field of technology and language education forward to focus on turning the potentials into reality, namely to support learners to actually use technologies actively and effectively for foreign language learning. Key terms: Meta-cognitive technological content knowledge (MTACK): the meta-cognitive knowledge about what technologies to use for what learning contents and purposes, about the cognitive and socio-affective factors and processes involved in using particular technolog(ies) for specified learning needs, and about the strategies in making effective use of such technologies for the specified purpose. Common information communication technologies (ICT): the technologies that surround the learners in their everyday life and that they frequently use for personal and entertainment purposes (e.g., the Internet, digital games, mobile phones, and MP3 players). 该研究项目旨在了解学生积极有效使用技术辅助外语学习所需的知识和技能。该研究提出当前的文献忽略了一个重要的元素，即对有效使用各类技术满足不同语言学习需求的元认知知识和技能（MTACK）。该项目将测试该元素的重要性，了解有效使用技术辅助外语学习所需的各项知识和技能，并揭示学生发展这些知识和技能所需的支持和帮助。 积极使用技术进行自主性学习是21世纪的一个重要的学习技能。然而，当前的研究发现尽管技术在教育方面有着种种优势，学生并没有主动将技术用于学习。因此，必须帮助学生发展使用技术辅助学习的能力，而了解学生要发展该能力所应具备的知识和技能是首要的。当前的研究普遍认为自主学习能力和数位素养是该能力的核心。然而，具有数位素养并不能保证学生能有效地使用技术来满足具体的学习需求。我们提议MTACK是辅助学生积极有效使用技术辅助语言学习的关键，并在该研究中测试这一假设。 要帮助学生利用技术的学习优势，我们必须得知道学生应具备哪些相关的知识和技能，以及如何很好地帮助他们获取这些知识和技能。只有帮助学生掌握相关的知识和技能，才能真正实现技术在语言教学方面的优势。 关键词： 技术学科元认知知识（MTACK）：关于哪些技术可用于满足语言学习哪些方面的需求及在使用某个具体技术满足某个具体的学习需求时所涉及的认知和情感因素及过程的认知，和有效使用技术来辅助语言学习的相关策略。 信息交流技术（ICT）：学生在日常生活中经常用作个人和娱乐目的的技术（如：网络、电子游戏、手机、MP3播放器等）

746110.label: Realisation of objectives
746110.value: The project aimed at fulfilling two objectives: 1) to understand the significance of MTACK in fostering active and effective use of common ICTs for foreign language learning and 2) to unravel the support learners need in developing such knowledge and skills. To achieve the research objectives, an online website that aimed at training MTACK has been built and implemented at schools. Around 400 students from three schools were involved in the study. Students’ uses of common ICTs for foreign language learning were assessed before and after the training. The project found that MTACK is important in fostering active and effective use of common ICTs for foreign language learning. This project further identified some internal and external factors that are critical in supporting learners to developing such knowledge and skills. Thus, both the two objectives have been achieved.

746110.label: Major findings and research outcome
746110.value: Finding 1: MTACK is a critical factor in facilitating active self-directed use of technology for language learning, affecting technology use through enhancing students’ perceived compatibility between technology use and learning expectancies. Facilitating conditions in terms of the availabilities of the support from teachers and peers and learners’ self regulation skills affect students’ MTACK. The findings were reported in a paper published in Language Learning & Technology. Finding 2: Student training on MTACK can enhance students’ frequency of self-directed use of technology for language learning and promote a greater willingness and stronger knowledge and skill base in support of such learning behaviors. It further found that to support learners in developing MTACK, the training component needs to include both general and skill specific pedagogical training, technical training and strategy training for matching particular technologies with particular strategic moves in skill development, and specific guidance on suing particular technologies effectively for language learning purposes. The findings were reported in a paper currently under second round review on minor revisions in Computer Assisted Language Learning.

746110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746110.value: There is a potential for further developing the research to examine the effects of MTACK training on and the support needed for different groups of students population and in different sociocultural contexts. To develop further understanding on this issue, we plan to conduct training comparison studies between K-12 students and university students and across different cultural contexts.

746110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746110.value: This research project aimed at understanding whether students’ knowledge and skills in effective use of technology for language learning is critical in facilitating greater quantity and quality of technology use for language learning among the language learners. The research project found that students’ knowledge and skills in effective use of technology for language learning is a critical factor in affecting students’ frequency of technology use. It further found that training students on such knowledge and skills can enhance students’ frequency of technology use for language learning and promote a greater willingness and stronger knowledge and skill base in support of such learning behaviors. It further identified that to support students develop such knowledge and skills, students need to be given both general and skill specific pedagogical training, technical training and strategy training for matching particular technologies with particular strategic moves in skill development, and specific guidance on suing particular technologies effectively for language learning purposes. This research project is significant in that it enhances our understanding on how to foster autonomous foreign language learning with common technologies, an important 21st century learning skills.

746210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
746210.value: The research aims at developing a short-range forecast system of daily ambulance demand by geographic areas. The system is founded on historical patterns of spatial and temporal variability of weather and its effects on the daily ambulance demand in Hong Kong. Adverse weather conditions (especially in intense heat, cold, or air pollution) have been known to trigger health-related emergencies in the elderly population. Given the ageing population of Hong Kong and the rising demand for emergency ambulance services, it is prudent to devise ways to dispatch more effectively limited resources by targeting the needy population according to where they live. Weather data, patient records, and census demographic information for 2006 to 2009 inclusive will be analyzed by geographic areas. The locational relationships between weather conditions and daily ambulance demand will be extracted through a series of geostatistical, spatial econometric and time series analyses. Specifically, we shall look for weather and locational characteristics as well as observable seasonal patterns that yield a high demand for emergency ambulances. These spatio-temporal models will guide the development of a short-range forecast system to predict daily ambulance demand for the next 2-3 days using data from 5-day weather forecasts in concurrent consideration of the current population characteristics and their spatial concentration. This research will contribute towards the formulation of weather-related priority dispatch systems to mobilize manpower and improve vehicle logistics under the constraints of existing resources. With the elderly population of Hong Kong on the rise and an increase in the frequency of extreme weather conditions, our research will enable strategic assignment and timely dispatch of ambulance and paramedic care to the needed. Our results will also add to a better understanding of the location-allocation heuristics of our ambulance services and enable assessments on whether the present locations of our ambulance depots are optimal and whether these facilities are adequate for residents within their designated service areas. A secondary research outcome is a projected average daily ambulance demand in 2036. The Census and Statistics Department of Hong Kong (2007) anticipated that the 2036 population of Hong Kong aged 65 and over would increase around 2.5 times while the remaining population would stay constant. Knowing the effects of adverse weather conditions on the elderly population, our research would estimate in advance potential areas in demand of ambulance services to instigate appropriate policy measures and assess resource implications. 本項研究旨在設計一個依據地理區域需求而建立的日常救護車需求的測報系統。天氣變化（特別是在極熱、極冷、或極污染的時候）對老年人的健康會有不利影響，這已經是不爭的事實。為預測天氣驟變對救護車需求的影響, 尤其是針對香港人口老化和不斷增長的情況，本研究從地理信息系統(GIS)角度切入，利用醫院救護車的事故資料，對事故發生地點的欄位進行定位，建置具備時空模式資料庫的GIS，提供使用者進行救護車日常需求的查詢、統計與分析。 本研究所蒐集的2006至2009年的資料，主要包括:(1)救護車事故現場資料、緊急救醫途中資料、醫生診斷及後續醫療資料;(2) 傷者的病歷;(3)氣象資料及空氣污染指數; (4)普查人口資料。通過一系列的提取統計，空間計量和時間序列的具體分析，本研究所產生的GIS時空模式的平台，將同時根據當前的氣象變化、居住地區的人口特徵和空間集聚，來預測未來 2-3天日常救護車的使用率。另外，資料庫和預報系統的設計，亦兼顧到未來內容的擴充、其他部門共享資料的可能性和應用功能的可持續性。 香港政府統計處於2007年預計本港年齡65歲及以上的人口將在2036年增加約 2.5倍，而其餘的人口將保持不變。隨著老年人口迅速增加和極端氣象日益頻發，我們的研究不僅有助於了解緊急救護服務的區域範圍、設備的分配和資源的善用，而且還能提供對潛在需求的評估，從而採取恰當的政策措施，提升救護車的調配運作和服務效率。

746210.label: Realisation of objectives
746210.value: This research has addressed, in varying degrees of success, research questions and objectives presented on the outset. This research is also the first study to establish possible relationships between the daily ambulance demand and weather factors of Hong Kong. The stratified analysis by socio-demographic characteristics not only revealed the weather sensitivity of people with different backgrounds, but also gave hints to the existence of first order spatial effects on ambulance demand. In addition, the stratified analysis by income group and triage level produced new knowledge. Income group was considered a rare variable which had not been analysed in previous international studies while the triage level, in our case, helped to clarify that weather effects on people was mainly a physiological impact but not a psychological impact. The stratified analysis by gender also recalled the importance of weather effects on gynaecological sources which was generally overlooked. Regarding the short-term forecasts, it has a major contribution on validating the effectiveness of meteorological forecast data in predicting the daily ambulance demand. The use of meteorological forecast data had been neglected surprisingly by researchers of the past who tended to use meteorological data in retrospective analyses. The research asserted that temperature and the change of age-gender population structure were two of the most important parameters for estimating demand for ambulance service. It has demonstrated the need to account for weather effects and population demographics in deriving more accurate projections of the long-term demand for emergency ambulance services in Hong Kong. The projection offers a piece of scientific and objective evidence to support or rethink procurement decisions and policy changes to sustain emergency ambulance services. This evidence alerts the needs to re-evaluate funding deployment and consider alternatives such as the user-pay principle to curb the rising demand. As a quick response ambulance service can save lives, a reliable estimate of ambulance demand is of paramount importance. Although all seven areas had certain underestimation, ranging from 5% to 23.1% due to different degrees of ageing, this was much better than the 38% underestimation in 2036. The longer-term projection on the ambulance demand considering the weather effects not only demonstrated potential problems in the future, but also provided the necessary objective evidence for supporting the launch of timely preventive policies.

746210.label: Major findings and research outcome
746210.value: The relationships between weather and daily ambulance demand were established by socio-demographic factors and patients’ condition (Part C 8.3). Results showed that the elderly, women, low income groups, more severe patients, and patients admitted to a hospital were more sensitive to weather factors. The relation between triage level and weather factors was another strong relationship demonstrated in the study. Together with the strong relationship observed between hospital admissions and weather factors, we concluded that severe patients were relatively sensitive to weather conditions. Although the gender difference was not large enough for making a conclusion, the stronger relationship obtained on female patients was consistent with that of previous findings (Part C 10.1). We assessed the effectiveness of using the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) 7-day weather forecast data and the characteristics of population structure differences of different spatial units to improve the short-term ambulance demand forecast. The success of improving the ambulance demand forecast by using the HKO 7-day weather forecast data not only meant more accurate forecasts could be made, but also demonstrated that improvement was feasible and could be made without additional resource because the weather forecast data was already available on the HKO website (Part C 8.1). Regarding the use of characteristic differences of population structure of individual spatial units to improve the ambulance demand forecasts, the results were a little bit disappointing. Mild improvement could only be observed on the 3-areas-combined forecast, but significant deterioration was observed on the 18-areas-combined forecast. Even though the consideration of population structure differences at the 18-district level did not seem to improve the short-term ambulance demand forecast in this study, the results of 3-areas-combined forecasts did suggest that the effects of population structure differences on ambulance demand was significant (Part C 10.1). The longer-term projection for the whole territory paints a truthful albeit painful picture about future service provision of the ambulance systems of Hong Kong (Part C 8.2; 10.2). The surging demand beyond normal expectation must be considered in light of local demographic and global climate changes. Effects of these factors have been grossly understated and overlooked as their impacts today are still marginal and practically insignificant.

746210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746210.value: More accurate data about the service/incident locations of ambulances not only can improve the spatial accuracy, but also can help identify cases which did not arrive at the hospital (e.g. false alarm, death before arrival, multi-patient cases). They could also allow the analysis of spatial-temporal hot spots which are sensitive to adverse weather conditions (e.g. elderly homes). The 10% yearly rate of emergency move-ups of ambulances could also be analysed at the ambulance depot level so that more focused arrangement to service high demand areas could be made. Moreover and without having to ask patients for these data, additional socio-demographic characteristics could be derived from the locational detail by means of address geocoding and matching against Census data to further stratify patient groups. Such information is rarely available for research studies because it is not always feasible during an emergency situation to obtain answers to socio-demographic questions. The ARIMA model developed from this study could be extended to investigate the effects of imposing ambulance usage fee to address the problems of ambulance misuse. Besides, the proposed ambulance demand forecast system could be extended to forecast user demand for the Personal Emergency Link services to cut down on unnecessary expenditures.

746210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746210.value: Our research establishes a few significant causal relationships between weather factors and the daily total of ambulance cases by different target groups. We conclude that weather factors can reasonably predict the demand for emergency ambulance services for older people, more severe patients, hospital admitted cases and welfare recipients. Although the world has begun to face weather changes more seriously, actions against climate change have been slow in forthcoming. Our study has demonstrated the need to account for weather effects and population demographics in deriving more accurate projections of the long-term demand for emergency ambulance services in Hong Kong. There are few studies about the joint decision-making processes of forecasters and emergency managers during severe weather events. Due to a lack of standardization and the complex nature of interagency cooperation, much time is wasted at the beginning on liaison and coordination. Given that the present day emergency services do not provide forecasts of daily ambulance demand, our forecasting model is helpful for the agency or the managing authority to know beforehand and be better prepared for the expected rise in the daily demand for emergency ambulances arising from changing weather conditions.

746710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
746710.value: Breast cancer is the second most common cancer worldwide, presenting a major global health burden. Among women in Hong Kong, breast cancer is the most common cancer and the third leading cause of cancer death. About thirty percent of women with breast cancer will face disseminated breast cancer, an incurable disease, at some point in their illness trajectory. As treatments progressively prolong life, and women with advanced disseminated breast cancer now often survive 5-10 years longer than a decade ago, advanced breast cancer has become a chronic disease. Living with this disease presents a significant emotional and psychological challenge to the patient and her family. For example, the impact of being diagnosed with advanced breast cancer will challenge many women’s goal-directed activities, such as continuing a normal daily routine, pursuing career development, and performance of valued social and other roles. Studies in other populations suggest that individual differences in general goal adjustment tendencies (goal adjustment flexibility) can influence psychological well-being. Goal adjustment tendencies may also partially modulate women’s adjustment to the disease progression though this question has never been explored in women with disseminated breast cancer. Also, nothing is currently known about the interaction of goal adjustment flexibility with established markers of resilience. We aim to (1) examine if goal adjustment tendencies (defined as disengagement from unattainable goals and reengagement in alternative goals) affect psychological well-being among women with advanced breast cancer, (2) examine how goal disengagement tendencies and goal reengagement tendencies interact with psychological well-being over time, (3) determine if dispositional hope and dispositional optimism moderate effects of goal adjustment on change of psychological well-being. A longitudinal study addresses the proposed objectives. Eligible participants are Chinese women recently diagnosed with advanced breast cancer. Approximately 200 women will be recruited. Women will be approached while waiting for outpatient oncology consultation. Those agreeing to participate complete an interview (baseline), and follow-up at 3 (FU1), 6 (FU2) and 12 months later (FU3). At baseline women’s goal adjustment tendencies, dispositional hope, dispositional optimism, and indicators of psychological well-being are assessed; follow-ups assess indices of psychological well-being. Linear mixed effects (LME) models will be used to examine (1) changes in indicators of psychological well-being over time, (2) interactions between goal disengagement, goal reengagement and psychological well-being, (3) moderating role of dispositional hope between goal adjustment and psychological well-being, and (4) moderation role of dispositional optimism in the relationship between goal reengagement and psychological well-being. 現時，乳癌是全球第二普遍之癌症，為人類帶來沈重的健康負擔。在香港，乳癌是婦女中最常見的癌症，死亡率則是婦女所患癌症中排行第三。約百分之三十的乳癌病患者會在她們治療的過程中被診斷為晚期乳癌，可是現時醫學界對晚期乳癌還未有完全根治的方案。現今的治療不斷地延長了患上晚期乳癌婦女的生命。較十年前相比，晚期乳癌的病患者往往可以延長多五至十年的壽命。因此，晚期乳癌被視為一種長期病患。對於病人及其家人，要與乳癌共存是她們在情緒上和心理上最大的挑戰。譬如說，婦女被診斷出晚期乳癌將會對她們實踐自我目標上造成了深遠的影響，好像在她們繼續如常生活，追求事業發展，以及她們在演繹社會及其他重要角色的表現上都成為她們生活中的挑戰。在其他國家的研究中表示，病人在對於調整目標上不同的傾向（如：目標調整的靈活性）可以影響心理健康。調整目標的能力亦有可能部分地影響了她們的適應力，然而這個問題從未在晚期乳癌病患者身上進行探討。再者，現時對於有關目標調整的靈活性和心理復原力之間的相互關係並沒有任何資料。所以我們的研究主要針對於（１）驗證目標調整的傾向（將使用對於放開不能達成之目標和重新追求另一目標兩方面的傾向來評核）會否影響晚期乳癌婦女的心理健康，（２）調查她們對於如何放開未能達成之目標以及重新追求另一新目標的傾向會怎樣互相影響患上晚期乳癌婦女的心理健康狀況，（３）測定患者對於希望和樂觀兩方面的個人取向會否影響目標的調整和心理健康上的關係。我們會使用長期研究的方法以完成我們的研究目標。 這次研究會邀請大約二百位剛被診斷出患上晚期乳癌的婦女參與。我們會於病患者等候診症的時間跟她們接觸。研究員會跟同意參與研究的婦女先進行一次訪問（作為研究的基線），再於其後的三個月（第一次跟進），六個月（第二次跟進）和十二個月（第三次跟進）進行總共三次的個案跟進。在第一次訪問時，研究員會問及她們對目標調整的傾向，對於希望和樂觀兩方面的個人取向，以及評估她們心理健康。而於其後的跟進都會就於她們的心理健康作出調查。這次研究會使用等級線性模型（Linear mixed effect models） 方法驗證（１）心理健康指標隨著不同時間的轉變，（２）對於如何放開不能達成的目標和重新追求另一新目標的傾向，以及心理健康三者之間的相互關係，（３）就患者對於希望的個人取向對於目標調整和心理健康之間的影響，和（４）她們對於樂觀的個人取向對於重新追求另一新目標及心理健康之間的影響。

746710.label: Realisation of objectives
746710.value: From October 2010 to November 2012, we identified 228 women who met the inclusion criteria and 193 (85%) agreed to participate in the study. A total of 21 (11%) participants died during the study period. This comprehensive recruitment and follow-up (between 67%-80%) enabled us to address the four study objectives exploring the impact of goal adjustment tendencies on change of psychological well-being. We used latent growth curve modeling (LGM) to initially examine the trajectories of psychological well-being (Anxiety, Depression, and Positive Affect). We then examined if goal adjustment tendencies influenced initial psychological well-being scores, and its growth change, adjusting for the effect of resilience (operationalized as optimism and hope), distress (operationalized as negative cancer-related rumination and physical symptom distress), and demographic and clinical factors. Finally, we examined if resilience (optimism and hope) moderate the effects of goal adjustment tendencies and goal disengagement and reengagement on psychological well-being. For each model, the comparative fit index (CFI) and root mean square error approximation (RMSEA) were used to determine the fit of the model. The LGRM employs a robust full-information maximum-likelihood estimation procedure for handling missing data. We were able to recruit an adequate sample, robustly measure and follow-up the sample, and analyse the data according to our original plan. Thus we completed all proposed tasks and achieved the study aims.

746710.label: Major findings and research outcome
746710.value: Anxiety Goal disengagement (p=0.009), reengagement (p=0.04), optimism (p<0.001), and negative cancer-related rumination (p<0.001) were significantly associated with initial anxiety scores. Goal disengagement (p=0.041) and negative cancer-related rumination (p=0.007) significantly predicted the rate of change in anxiety scores. Hope did not associate with initial levels of anxiety or predict anxiety change over time. Patients with lower goal disengagement, lower optimism, but higher goal reengagement and negative cancer-related rumination had a significant higher anxiety scores at baseline. Moreover, optimism (p=0.029) moderated the effect of goal disengagement on initial anxiety scores at baseline. Women with low goal disengagement experienced higher initial anxiety scores regardless of their level of optimism, whereas women with high goal disengagement reported a lower initial anxiety scores if they were high in optimism. Depression Goal disengagement, goal reengagement and hope did not associate with initial depression scores or predict change of depression over time. Optimism (p<0.001) and negative cancer-related rumination (p<0.001) significantly predicted initial depression scores at baseline. Optimism (p=0.010) and negative cancer-related rumination (p<0.001) also significantly predicted the rate of change in depression scores. Patients with lower optimism, but higher negative cancer-related rumination had a significantly higher depression scores at baseline. Positive affect Goal reengagement (p<0.001), optimism (p=0.013), and hope (p<0.001) were significantly associated initial positive affect scores. Goal disengagement did not predict positive affect. Only optimism (p=0.032) significantly predicted rate of change in positive affect scores. Patients with higher goal reengagement, higher optimism, and higher hope had a significant higher positive affect scores at baseline. Furthermore, hope (p<0.001) moderated the effect of goal reengagement on initial positive affect scores at baseline Women with low goal reengagement reported a lower initial positive affect score if they reported low hope, whereas women with high goal reengagement reported a higher initial positive affect scores if they reported high hope. Hence, our findings showed that goal disengagement and reengagement were two relatively independent processes influencing psychological well-being. Goal disengagement mostly influenced anxiety, suggesting successful disengagement from unattainable goals minimizes anxiety in response to the diagnosis of advanced breast cancer. In contrast, goal reengagement mostly influenced positive affect, suggesting goal reengagement tendencies play an important role in stabilizing psychological well-being. Interestingly, optimism moderated the effect of goal disengagement on anxiety, whereas hope moderated the effect of goal reengagement on positive affect.

746710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746710.value: To our knowledge, this is the first study to examine the interaction of goal adjustment and established markers of resilience (optimism and hope) on psychological well-being. Our findings suggest that optimism with goal disengagement, and hope with goal reengagement are two distinct processes influencing psychological outcomes among women diagnosed with advanced breast cancer. Hence, health care professionals helping women with advanced breast cancer to manage the anxiety should focus on assisting patients to let go of their unattainable goals. To enhance women’s positive adjustment, interventions should focus on assisting patients in finding new meaningful goals. The present study conceptualized goal adjustment as a dispositional characteristic and did not examine situational goal adjustment. Future studies should examine if situation goal adjustment plays a distinct role on psychological adjustment. Furthermore, the present study only examined the change of psychological well-being over the first year after the diagnosis of advanced breast cancer. Future studies should explore the effect of goal adjustment on long-term psychological well-being.

746710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746710.value: It is recognized that some people report experiencing a burst of personal growth following a cancer diagnosis, while others struggle and experience high distress. We tried to understand what might explain these differences. We looked at how women with advanced breast cancer differed in terms of being able to “let go” of goals that were increasingly unattainable since their diagnosis, and their relative abilities to switch to new more-attainable goals. Women who generally expect more good than bad things to happen in the future, and who are also able to let go of unattainable goals are likely to experience less anxiety in response to a diagnosis of advanced breast cancer. Moreover, women who demonstrate hopeful goal-directed behavior together with the ability to find new meaningful goals are likely to show positive adjustment (“growth” or “resilience”) in response to the diagnosis of advanced breast cancer. This suggests that resilience and or growth has at least two distinct features. Whether these processes are sequential, or concurrent and complementary remains unknown. These findings will help clinicians to tailor specific interventions to help women coping with the diagnosis of advanced breast cancer.

747910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
747910.value: Spirituality, which encompasses both religious and non-religious meaning and values of an individual, has been increasingly recognized as a central component of holistic well-being at end of life. There is growing evidence indicates that terminal patients want help in finding hope, meaning and spiritual resources. Yet, most literature on spirituality in palliative care reflects the opinions of health care professionals with very little information on the perspective of patients and families. Spirituality involves subjective experience and perception of the individuals; understanding the concept of spirituality from the vantage point of patients becomes paramount important. Moreover, because of their collectivist and relational orientation, Chinese patients’ spirituality may be closely related to familial aspects of their lives and their daily interaction with the families. It is thus important to understand the perspectives of both the patients and the families. To date, spirituality among Hong Kong Chinese palliative care patients has not been empirically examined. The few studies done with the Chinese population focused only on patients. This not only constitutes a significant knowledge gap but also greatly limits the development of effective policy and practical guides on quality holistic palliative care. This proposed study is the first to investigate spirituality in end of life from the perspectives of both Chinese patients and their families receiving palliative care in Hong Kong. It addresses patients’ spirituality regarding their concerns, hope, purpose, and meaning as well as the factors that contribute to their spiritual well-being in the context of death and dying. Adopting a qualitative constructivist paradigm, semi-structured interviews will be conducted with twenty patients and their family caregivers recruited from the palliative care units of a hospital in Hong Kong. An innovative interview technique integrating life review with narrative story-telling will provide in-depth and contextual understanding of the meaning of spirituality of patients and their families. This is a timely study when there is an increasing demand, globally and locally, for holistic and patient-oriented palliative care that takes into account the full range of the needs of patients and their families, from physical, psychosocial to spiritual. The expected findings will generate new knowledge contributing to advancement in both theories and practices in palliative care. Moreover, Chinese people are one of the largest migrant populations in all major cities, so the findings will greatly benefit practitioners and researchers on a global scale.

747910.label: Realisation of objectives
747910.value: This research successfully generated findings that address the objectives of the study. It expands our understanding of the range of spiritual experiences (from spiritual distress to spiritual peace) of patients at the end-of-life and the processes involved (creating meaning, making connections, and transcending death) (Objectives 1 and 2). Relational dynamic is revealed as a salient theme in Chinese patients’ coping when death approaches. When the patient is harmoniously connected with others, social support serves to enhance patients’ spirituality. However, regrets of unfulfilled filial responsibilities can be a cultural barrier for reconciliation and contentment at life’s final stage (Objectives 3). Moreover, the conception of spirituality is found to be highly related to the notion of dignity in the Chinese context, with one complements the other to promote well-being at the end-of-life. Meaning, connectedness, and transcendence are found to be important components of patients’ spirituality. Culturally-specific conceptions of spirituality such as moral transcendence, enduring pain, living with the Mandate of Heaven are revealed to be factors that enhance spiritual well-being of Chinese patients. (Objectives 2 and 3). The above findings were generated after the data collection and analysis procedures following a constructivist research paradigm. Based on the notion of data saturation, a total of twenty-two adult patients having diverse cancer diagnoses and their key family caregivers were recruited (N=44) from the palliative care unit of Shatin Hospital in Hong Kong. Some participants attended a follow-up interview which provided the opportunity to validate and expand the information gathered in previous interviews. A total of 49 interviews with 30 to 90 minutes durations were conducted by the trained interviewers of the research team. The interviews focused on the participants’ conception of spirituality, their experience in confronting death and dying, and caring for their dying relatives (for carers). All interviews were digitally-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using the grounded theory approach and framework analysis. Two researchers of the project conducted coding independently. Discussion was made in the research team to scrutinize the plausibility of the themes observed and to agree on the final coding. Most emergent themes of this study are evidently culturally-specified, pinpointing the paramount importance of cultural competence and awareness for working with ethnically diverse groups. The findings are published in peer-reviewed academic journal, book chapters and disseminated through local and international conferences, as well as educational programs at the University and in the community.

747910.label: Major findings and research outcome
747910.value: Spiritual experience of Chinese palliative care patients: Findings reveal that spiritual experience of Chinese patients at the end-of-life encompasses a spectrum from spiritual distress (loss of self, anguish, hopelessness) to spiritual peace (self-integrity, interpersonal harmony, equanimity). The patients’ process from distress to peace includes (1) creating meaning, which involves actualization of a moral self, fulfillment of familial responsibilities, and appreciating strengths in self; (2) making connection, which includes reconciliation with self and others, giving and receiving love, and passing on one’s life values; and (3) transcending death, which is achieved through accepting the Mandate of Heaven and living in the moment (see Part C9). Chinese patients’ conception of spirituality: Meaning, connectedness, and transcendence are found to be important components of patients’ spirituality. Findings reveal that there are culturally-specific conceptions of spirituality in the Chinese content - moral transcendence, enduring pain, and living with the Mandate of Heaven. A salient theme is relational dynamic. On the part of the patients, “the desire of not to be a burden”, “feeling grateful toward the family members” and “taking pride in achievement of one’s offspring” are factors that support one’s spirituality, motivating individuals towards transcendence in confronting the suffering with terminal illness. On the other hand, “being a burden”, “feeling indebted toward the family members”, “interpersonal discord/unforgiveness” are related to a sense of guilt and shame which compromise patients’ spirituality. Social support is found to be a double-edge sword, serving as either a source of distress or a spiritual capital, depending on whether the patient can be harmoniously connected with others and one’s moral principles (see Part C8: Wan, Leung and Fong, 2013, Ho, et al. 2013 and Part C9). The dynamics of caregiving: Analysis reveals that family caregivers derived meaning from “witnessing and appreciating the patients’ resilience”, “being able to fulfill filial responsibilities” and “returning of care received in the past”. Caregiving can be a spiritually rewarding experience. However, emotional distance between patients and the family caregivers are created when regrets of unfulfilled filial responsibilities exist. This acts as a cultural barrier for reconciliation and contentment at the end-of-life (see Part C8: Wan, Leung and Fong, 2013, and Part C9). The above findings have been disseminated in 1 journal article, 3 book chapters and 6 conference presentations. It has also served to train 2 PhD students, with one received the Student Cross-Cultural Paper Award in an international conference.

747910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
747910.value: In collaboration with the Hong Kong Sheng Kung Hui Welfare Council, some of the findings of the study have developed into the hospice care programs of its Nursing Home for its elderly residents and their family members. A study entitled “Evaluation Study of Integrative Body-Mind-Spirit Hospice Care for Older Adults in Hong Kong Sheng Kung Hui Nursing Home” was successfully completed in November 2012 with encouraging results. The findings of the study were disseminated through a public forum held in December 14, 2012 and through press coverage (See Appendix III). Discussion on further research on a pioneer spiritually-oriented intervention program for physically weak and cognitively impaired elderly is underway.

747910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
747910.value: This study investigates spirituality at the end-of-life from the perspectives of both Chinese patients and their families receiving palliative care in Hong Kong. It addresses patients’ spirituality regarding their needs, concerns, and experiences as well as the factors that contribute to their spiritual well-being in the context of death and dying. A total of 49 interviews were conducted with twenty-two patients having diverse cancer diagnoses and their family caregivers. The findings of this study expand our understanding of the range of spiritual experiences of terminally ill patients. It highlights the possibility of shifts from spiritual distress to well-being when an individual is able to go through the necessary spiritual process. In particular, this study sheds light on how Chinese patients use culturally specific ways to enhance their spiritual well-being. Relational dynamic, familial obligations and harmony with self, others and cultural principles are found to be core components of Chinese spirituality. The findings of this study illuminate how cultural values interact with the experience of dying, and they inform culturally respectful palliative care practice at the end-of-life care.

747910.value: a. Award Received A paper presentation entitled “The Blessings and the Curses of Filial Piety on Dignity at the end-of-Life: Lived Experience of Hong Kong Chinese Adult Children Caregivers” has received the Student Cross-Cultural Paper Award from the 35th Annual Conference of the Association for Death Education and Counseling to be held in Hollywood, California, April 24-27, 2013 (see Appendix I). b. Knowledge Transfer The findings of this study have been used in the training of hospice care professionals and volunteers, locally and in Mainland China. On April 16, 2011, a training organized by the Li Ka Shing Foundation on Spirituality-enhancing Life Stories Intervention was presented to more than 700 medical doctors, nurses, social workers and volunteers who came from more than 30 cities in Mainland China. It successfully trained up more than 700 participants to use the life story intervention in serving terminal patients in different parts of China. Successful hospice life story projects were produced into VCDs for further dissemination among the hospice care communities in Mainland China. The projects have also been widely disseminated through the Foundation’s hospice website at http://www.hospice.com.cn/love_present/index.aspx, arousing more awareness on provision of quality palliative care in China. More recently, our research team has also been invited to present the findings of this study in the “8th Chinese National Congress on Cancer Rehabilitation and Palliative Medicine” organized by the Rehabilitation and Palliative Care Committee of Chinese Association Against Cancer held on 12-14 October in Qingdao, China (See Part C9). The presentation was published in the professional newsletter “Oncology” of the Association (in Chinese). This widely disseminates the key findings on spiritual care for cancer patients and their family among hospice care community in China (See Appendix II). Locally, the study attracted collaboration with a charity organization, “Togetherness”, in developing volunteer community services for terminal patients. Adopting the findings of the study, the organization launched projects in helping the patients to work on life integration and reconciliation. A successful case story of the collaboration was disseminated in the 8th Palliative Care Symposium held on August 20, 2011 in Hong Kong (See Part C9). As iterated in section 6.2, the findings from this study have formed the basis of a new research initiative entitled, “Evaluation Study of Integrative Body-Mind-Spirit Hospice Care for Older Adults in Hong Kong Sheng Kung Hui Nursing Home”. This study is also a knowledge-transfer activity. The findings of this new initiative are widely disseminated to the non-academic audience via press coverage (see Appendix III), pushing forth the idea of holistic palliative care for individuals and families in Hong Kong. Furthermore, this body of work has also been incorporated into undergraduate and post-graduate courses offered in the University of Hong Kong. These include the Common Core Curriculum “CCHU9024 – The Last Dance: Understanding Death and Dying” and the course “SOWK0020-6035 – Psycho-social Oncology, Palliative and Hospice Care” in the Department of Social Work and Social Administration. The former has approximately 100 students registered per year while the latter with approximately 30 students registered per year.

748010.label: Project Title(Chinese)
748010.value: 运动方向和运动路线关系之研究

748010.label: Project Objectives
748010.value: • Examine how conflicting path trajectories influence heading perception, and whether humans combine path and motion cues from optic flow for heading estimation in a statistically optimal way. • Examine whether people use extended motion streamlines of environmental points (flow lines) in retinal flow for direct path perception without recovering heading, and investigate the added contribution of heading perception and acceleration information in the flow field to path perception. We hope to find empirical evidence in support of the mathematical model that uses vertical flow lines in retinal flow for path recovery (see Wann & Swapp, 2000). • Show distinct patterns of cortical activation using BOLD fMRI signal for heading and path perception and examine how the cortical activation for these two perceptual processes can be modulated by related path and optic flow cues.

• Examine whether people use extended motion streamlines of environmental points (flow lines) in retinal flow for direct path perception without recovering heading, and investigate the added contribution of heading perception and acceleration information in the flow field to path perception. We hope to find empirical evidence in support of the mathematical model that uses vertical flow lines in retinal flow for path recovery (see Wann & Swapp, 2000).
