748010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748010.value: Accurate perception and control of self-motion is essential for humans to successfully move around in the world. Two defining features of human locomotion are one’s instantaneous direction of self-motion (heading) and one’s future trajectory of self-motion (path). They coincide when travelling on a straight path but diverge when travelling on a curved path, as in the latter case, heading is the tangent to one’s current curved path. Research over the last two decades has focused on how to recover heading from optic flow and how heading is used in the control of self-motion. More recently, researchers have started to question whether it is necessary to recover heading, and whether people can directly perceive path from optic flow and use path for the control of self-motion. Even more recent brain-imaging studies have shown that path features activate cortical areas different from those involved in heading perception, suggesting that heading and path perception are two separate perceptual processes. In the current project, by examining (1) in what manner heading perception is influenced by conflicting path trajectories, and (2) whether people can directly perceive path using flow lines in retinal flow without recovering heading, we aim to determine whether heading and path perception are two parallel perceptual processes or the perception of one is necessary to enable the perception of the other. Furthermore, by conducting brain-imaging studies based on the results from the behavioral studies, we plan to pinpoint the brain areas sensitive to optic flow and path cues for heading and path judgment. The findings from the current project will facilitate understanding of the relationship between heading and path perception and the neural mechanisms responsible for these two perceptual processes, which will greatly facilitate the development of new theories accounting for the visual cues used in the control of locomotion. The findings will also be applicable in the design of effective navigational interfaces, and biomimetic mobile robots and unmanned vehicles. 正确的本体运动知觉与控制是人类生存的关键。运动方向和运动路线是定义人类运动的两大变量。当运动路线是直线时这两个变量相等同，而当运动路线是曲线时这两个变量是完全不同的，此时运动方向乃是运动路线在每一个时刻的切线方向。以往三十年来的研究集中于回答运动者如何从光流信息中获取当前的运动方向以及此运动方向如何被用于控制本体运动。近些年来研究者开始对获取当前运动方向是否必要以及人们能否能够直接从光流信息中提取运动路线的信息并将其用于控制本体运动有所质疑。更近期的脑成像研究发现运动方向和运动路线这两个变量的知觉各自涉及不同的脑区，从而提出运动方向以及运动路线知觉乃是两个完全分离的知觉加工过程。我们当前的研究计划于解决（1）当运动路线信息与运动方向信息相冲突时运动路线如何影响运动方向的知觉， 以及（2）人们能否不借助于运动方向知觉而直接从投射于视网膜上的光流模式中获取运动路线的信息。此计划目的在于回答运动方向与运动路线知觉是否为两个平行的知觉过程或是否知觉一方乃为知觉另一方之必不可少的条件。此外，通过基于行为研究结果的脑成像研究手段我们期望能够定位在运动方向以及运动路线判断任务中所涉及到的被光流信息和运动路线信息所激活的脑区。此研究的结果将会促使人们对运动方向和运动路线知觉之间的关系以及这两种知觉过程所涉及的神经机制有更进一步理解，从而极大地推动有关本体运动控制所涉及视觉信息的新理论发展，对于高效的导航人机界面，仿生机器人以及无人驾驶车辆的设计也具有应用价值。

748010.label: Realisation of objectives
748010.value: Regarding Objective 1, we have achieved it 100% by conducting a series of experiments to examine how conflicting path trajectory information influences heading perception. Specifically, we have examined whether human heading perception solely depends on motion information from optic flow, whether heading perception is affected by path-related form information, and whether humans combine motion cues from optic flow and path-related form information in a statistically optimal way for heading judgment. Regarding Objective 2, we have achieved it 100% by conducting a series of experiments to examine how people perceive their path of forward traveling from optic flow. Specifically, we examined whether people can perceive their path directly from optic flow without recovering heading and how extra-retinal signals about eye movements contributes to perceiving path from optic flow. Furthermore, we have also examined what visual strategies people use for the control of self-motion, and when steering/walking toward a goal, whether people align one’s heading specified by optic flow (Gibson, 1950) or their future path (Wann & Swapp, 2000) with the target. Regarding Objective 3, we have achieved it 100% by conducting a series of brain-imaging experiments to examine whether there are distinct patterns of cortical activation for heading and path perception and the control of self-motion, and how the cortical activation can be modulated by related optic flow cues.

748010.label: Major findings and research outcome
748010.value: Regarding Objective 1, we have found that humans combine motion cues from optic flow and path-related form information in a statistically optimal way for heading judgment. Furthermore, path-like form information heavily biases heading perception but has no effect on the perception of object motion during self-motion (Niehorster & Li, 2012 July & August, 2014). Furthermore, we have found that discrepant optic flow generated during walking overwrites path perception and biases both the perceived visual and proprioceptive straight ahead in egocentric space (Chen, He, Wei, & Li, 2014). Regarding Objective 2, we have found that contrary to the idea that looking where you want to go provides accurate path perception (Wann & Swapp, 2000), people use the rotation in the retinal velocity field for path curvature estimation and recover their path of forward travel relative to their perceived heading (Li & Cheng, 2011). Furthermore, extra-retinal signals about eye movements support accurate path perception only for the natural case of self-motion when the body orientation is aligned with heading such that pursuit compensation helps to stabilize the heading in the body-centric coordinate system (Cheng & Li, 2012; Li, Niehorster, Liston, Siu, & Stone, 2013; Niehorster, Siu, & Li, 2013). We have also found that when steering/driving toward a goal, people steer to align their heading but not future path trajectory with the target (Li & Cheng, 2011). When target egocentric direction cues are available, people still use the heading strategy for the control of locomotion (Li & Cheng, 2013; Chen, Niehorster, & Li, 2013; Li & Niehorster, 2014; Li, Niehorster, Warren, Bolte, Wieland, & Lappe, 2014; Chen & Li, 2014). Last, we found that the visuomotor component of the steering/driving task used in the above mentioned studies can improve through action video game play (Li, Chen, & Chen, 2012). Regarding Objective 3, we have found that rather than a single visuomotor region, the posterior cingulate contains adjacent but separate motor (CMA) and visual (CSv) regions. A surprising and novel finding is that activity in CSv is suppressed during a self-motion control task, despite the visual stimulus being identical to that used to localize the region. This provides an important clue to the specific role played by this region in the utilization of optic flow for heading and path perception and the control of self-motion (Field, Inman, & Li, under review; Li, Inman, & Field, 2013).

748010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748010.value: The findings of the current research project show that there are in fact quite large individual differences in the task performance, which, when used together with the brain-imaging techniques, can identify the underlying neural mechanism responsible for the control of locomotion in humans. Indeed, we have conducted some pilot studies to systemically examine the strategies that people use to steer/walk toward a goal and written up a GRF grant proposal on the investigation of neural bases for the visual control of locomotion in humans, which has just been awarded.

748010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748010.value: Accurate perception and control of self-motion is essential for humans to successfully move around in the world. Two defining features of human locomotion are one’s instantaneous direction of self-motion (heading) and one’s future trajectory of self-motion (path). In the current project, we examined in what manner heading perception is influenced by conflicting path trajectories, and whether people can directly perceive path using information from optic flow without recovering heading. Furthermore, by conducting brain-imaging studies based on the results from the behavioral studies, we pinpointed the brain areas sensitive to optic flow and path cues for heading and path judgment, and how these brain areas are involved in the control of self-motion. The findings from the current project increase our understanding of the relationship between the perception of heading and path from optic flow and the underlying neural mechanisms sensitive to the visual cues for heading and path judgment. The findings can assist design engineers in the development of effective user interfaces for navigation and training-effectiveness evaluation, and roboticists in the design of biomimetic (neurophysiologically plausible processes) mobile robots and unmanned vehicles.

748410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
748410.value: 民间信仰的根源:对中国村庙捐款的研究

748410.label: Co - Investigator(s)
748410.value: Prof Dean, Kenneth Prof ZHENG, Zhenman

748410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748410.value: Believing in religion (inner faith) and belonging to a religious group (attendance) are two distinct aspects of religiosity. Weber (1930) argued that both have important consequences for economic development, and Barro (2003) has used country-level data to show that they affect the economy in different ways. The proposed research will shed new light on these two elements utilizing the first-ever micro-level data set on actual temple contributions in rural China. Specifically, we propose a new methodology that will (1) quantify the relative importance of believing versus belonging and (2) further decompose the motives for belonging into secular and non-secular components. Our approach will hinge on the forms of contribution that members choose, which vary by visibility and voluntariness. We will develop a model to show how the choice of contribution form may be driven by underlying motives: individual faith, status-seeking, or the secular rewards of religious activities (e.g. social capital). We will then estimate the model using a large data set on temple contributions in Fujian province. This data seet contains over 30,000 complete records of contributions to more than 3,000 temples since the early 1990s (see attachment for an example). Preliminary analysis of a sub-sample (from 50 temples in three villages during 2005) shows that around 70 percent of the contributions were publicly visible and of mandated contribution amounts. This could imply that secular social rewards, rather than private faith, are the primary force behind religious participation in Fujian. The project has two objectives. The first objective is to digitize the raw contribution data and merge them with data on local socio-economic conditions, such as local family trees and economics statistics, to build a database than can be used to study important questions about religiosity and human society. The second objective is to deploy the data in a rigorous examination of the importance of pure faith and the secular causes of religious participation, and how they interact with human society and economic activities. 在经济发展的同时,中国的地方民间信仰的规模也快速增长.本项研究的目的在于探究这个现象的驱动因素.我们的数据来源是福建莆田地区的村庙的捐款榜文.榜文里有每次信仰活动的具体捐献数额.捐献的数额和结构因不同的村庙有很大的不同.这项研究计划的目的之一是把这些榜文的信息电子化以利后续的研究(一共有超过1000间村庙过去十五年间的30000多张榜文).另一个目的是对这个资料做初步的分析.希望能了解民间信仰在农村生活的重要性,和探求为什么村民愿意参加民间信仰的活动.

748710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748710.value: We provide a new perspective on the analysis of two of the most popular technical trading rules, involving so-called resistance and support price barriers. The barriers are either formed by a recent high or low price, or by a special round number like 10, 20, 30. Unlike existing literature, we (i) exploit changes in the second moments, i.e. variance and covariance of stock price, to detect the barriers and (ii) analyze stock price dynamics both before and after breaking through the barrier. Using NYSE and AMEX listed stocks, our preliminary analyses show that the systematic risk measured by the beta of Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), total return variance, and idiosyncratic return variance all significantly decrease prior to breaking through a historical high or low price. After the breakthrough of a resistance level at a historical maximum, the one-day change in the risk-adjusted return measured by the CAPM alpha is highly significant at an annualized value of 35%. The analyses for barriers at special round numbers are more mixed. After detecting the price barriers and their effect, we intend to explore the relationship between the limits of arbitrage and the barrier effect in the next step of our analysis. To be more precise, we are going to look at whether the barrier effect is confined within the stock market or it also spread to the option market. We are also going to investigate whether short sales help to mitigate this temporary price deviation from the fundamentals. 我們對包括壓力或支撐等價格壁壘在內的技術分析等問題提供新的研究角度。這些壁壘由歷史高價或低價形成，又或者為 10，20，30等等特別整數形成。本文與既有文獻不同的是，一、我們透過二階動差的變動來確認價格壁壘的存在；二、我們分析了在突破價格壁壘前后的股價變動情況。本文資料包含紐約證券交易所及美國證劵交易所全部上市股票。我們的最初分析發現，在突破歷史價格上的高位與低位時，資本資產定價模型中的beta，總風險和非系统性風險都顯著降低。在突破歷史價位高點时，資本資產定價模型中的alpha的日收益達到換約35%的年率，且高度显著。在整數價格壁壘上的结果則是沒有定論的。我們將進一步研究套利限制和價格壁壘之间的關係。

748710.label: Realisation of objectives
748710.value: In this project, we propose a new way of studying price irregularities when stock prices are close to or breaking through a 52-week high or low price. Instead of focusing on noisy measurements of abnormal returns, we focus on stock-option implied volatilities and second moments of stock returns (beta, idiosyncratic volatility). In addition, while existing work mainly focuses on price behavior after breaking through the 52-week high or low, we study both the stock price behavior when current prices are close to the 52-week high or low, and the behavior after a breakthrough. This provides new insights into the validity of theories that have been put forward to explain the effect of a 52-week high and low. In particular, we find strong evidence that beta, idiosyncratic volatility and option-implied volatility decrease when stock price are close to their 52-week high or low. This is in line with the anchoring hypothesis of Tversky and Kahneman (1974). After breaking through the 52-week high or low, we find a strong increase in stock return volatility and implied volatility, consistent with both anchoring and the investor attention hypothesis of Barber and Odean (2008). An interesting question is whether it is possible to develop a trading strategy that exploits the predictive patterns documented in this paper. The evidence shows that option implied volatilities respond more strongly to approaching and breaking through the 52-week high or low than the underlying return volatility does. This would imply that options are cheap when approaching a 52-week high or low, and expensive just after a breakthrough of the 52-week high or low. Economically, these effects are large, between 0.40 and 1.16 volatility points in absolute terms. A trader could potentially exploit this by buying options when the stock price approaches the 52-week high or low, and selling these options after a breakthrough, while delta-hedging with the underlying stock. Of course, transaction costs in option markets are substantial (Mayhew (2002)), hence such a trading strategy may only be profitable for the subset of liquid options. Finally, even though we focus in this paper on the 52-week high and low, our approach of analyzing implied volatilities and second moments of returns around specific events can be applied whenever a researcher is investigating short-term price irregularities.

748710.label: Major findings and research outcome
748710.value: Our key findings are as follows. First, we observe a strong decrease in implied volatilities when approaching 52-week highs or lows. The implied stock volatility decreases by about 1 volatility point when approaching the 52-week high (the average implied volatility for stocks in our sample is 43 volatility points), and about 0.4 volatility point when approaching the 52-week low. We find similar effects in the underlying stock returns: approaching the 52-week high or low has a strong effect on volatility. The idiosyncratic stock return variance decreases significantly when approaching the 52-week high or low, controlling for the usual determinants of return variance. In addition, a stock's beta decreases by about 0.12 (0.05) when the stock price is within 3% from the 52-week high (low). Finally, we find that trading volume of stocks increases significantly when approaching a high or low. All these results are statistically significant and robust to changing the setting in several dimensions. Second, we find a strong and significant increase in option-implied volatility after breaking through the 52-week high or low. Implied stock-option volatilities increase by more than 1 volatility point when stock prices break through the 52-week high or low. Consistent with this finding, the underlying stock return variance increases by about 19% on the day after breaking through the 52-week high and 43% after breaking through the 52-week low. The after-breakthrough variance effects last for a few days. The effect of breakthroughs on the stock's beta is smaller. Finally, stock trading volume increases by a large amount after breakthroughs, in line with findings of Huddart et al. (2008). We implement a simple option pricing model with stochastic volatility to assess whether the variance effects in the underlying stock returns are quantitatively consistent with the observed effect on option-implied volatilities. Overall, we find that the effects on implied volatilities seem to be somewhat larger than the effects on the underlying return variances. In addition, we find some evidence that option traders do not anticipate the huge increase in variance after a potential breakthrough when the stock price is close to the low but has not (yet) crossed it.

748710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748710.value: Even though we focus in this paper on the 52-week high and low, our approach of analyzing implied volatilities and second moments of returns around specific events can be applied whenever a researcher is investigating short-term price irregularities.

748710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748710.value: We provide a new perspective on option and stock price behavior around 52-week highs and lows. We analyze whether option-implied volatilities change when stock prices approach or break through their 52-week high or low. We also study the effects of highs and lows on a stock's beta and return volatility. We find that implied volatilities and stock betas decrease when approaching a high or low, and that volatilities increase after breakthroughs. The effects are economically large and significant. The approach results can be explained by the anchoring theory. The breakthrough results are consistent with anchoring and the investor attention hypothesis.

749210.label: Project Objectives

749210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
749210.value: The proposed research project examines the activity space and mobility patterns of the elderly in an urban context and sheds light on the ways of preserving and enhancing their outdoor mobility, which is highly valued in an ageing society. Many high-income cities and countries worldwide are facing ageing population. The provision of an accessible and safe transport system in an ageing society is on the agenda of local and national governments, as well as international organizations. For community-dwelling elderly, the ability to “get out and about” is not only beneficial to their physical but also mental health. Walking is a form of physical exercise that has proven health benefits. Moreover, making regular trips outside homes enables the elderly to engage in interactions with other people and is a form of socialization which helps to prevent depressive symptoms and maintain their self-esteem. In ageing societies, the nature of traffic safety problems also changed. In particular, older people are much more likely to be pedestrians. Even controlling for the higher exposure, elderly pedestrians are still at higher risks of being involved in vehicle-pedestrian crashes. To make things worse, elderly pedestrian casualties were having higher chances of dying and suffering from serious injury. The proposed project is also a pioneer research analyzing the elderly pedestrians’ traffic judgements in detail. The relationships of unsafe traffic judgements with the characteristics of the road-crossing environment, and the elderly’s age, gender, walking speed, travel behaviour characteristics, level of physical activities, and cognitive ability are examined. The guiding philosophy is to ensure the safety of the elderly without jeopardizing their mobility. Hence, this research aims to identify not only the more vulnerable groups of elderly pedestrians but also the more risky road locations and environment for elderly pedestrians. With the information gathered, it is possible to develop more effective countermeasures, which may vary from lengthening the pedestrian crossing time at signalized crossings, shortening the standards for providing pedestrian-crossing facilities, encouraging vulnerable elderly to travel accompanied or simply alerting them about the key elements of safe road crossing. The long-term objective is to facilitate the formulation of a road safety strategy in an ageing society. 這個研究項目是要調查在城市範圍內長者的活動空間和流動形態以維護和加強他們的戶外流動性。全球許多高收入的城市和國家都面臨人口老齡化。在一個老齡化社會，為長者提供方便和安全的交通運輸系統是眾多地方和國家政府以及國際組織的主要議題。對於社區長者，有能力“走到户外”不僅有利於他們的身體健康，對其心理健康也有益處。步行是一種形式的體育鍛煉。此外，進行定期户外活動能讓老年人參與人際互動和融入社會，有助於防止抑鬱症狀以及維護他們的自我形象。在老齡化社會，交通安全問題的性質也產生了變化。老年人十分依賴步行為交通工具。在惕除高使用率的因素下，長者仍比其他年齡的行人更容易涉及行人受傷的交通事故中。更糟糕的是，年長行人有較高機會在交通事故中死亡和嚴重受傷。這個研究項目分析年長行人的交通判決及其細節。研究會對長者過路的判斷，道路環境，年齡，性別，步行速度，行為特徵，身體活動水平和認知能力進行調查。研究的主導原則是要在不影響長者流動性的前題下，增加長者步行的安全性。因此，研究的目的不僅是要識別容易受到交通事故傷害的長者群體，還要找出各種相關的因素。根據所收集的數據，我們能提出更有效的對策，如延長行人過路信號的時間，縮短提供行人過路設施的標準，鼓勵長者結伴同行或提醒他們有關安全過馬路的關鍵要素。本研究的長期目標是要在一個老齡化社會中促進和制定有效的道路安全策略。

749210.label: Realisation of objectives
749210.value: The PI and CoI are very pleased that all objectives as per the original application have been fully achieved. The first objective was fully achieved. The relevant research publications are 1) Lam, Loo and Yao (2013), which maps out the actual activity space and mobility patterns of the elderly pedestrians and takes a further step to use the information as an exposure measure to analyse traffic collisions involving elderly pedestrians in Hong Kong; 2) Yao and Loo (2012), which compares the collision-based (often used in the literature) with the person-based approach (advocated in this project) to examine pedestrian safety in Kwun Tong of Hong Kong; and 3) Loo and Yao (2013), which compares the different methods of identifying hazardous road locations from a methodological point of view. It is a technical paper arising directly from our work in this project to identify dangerous road locations in road safety analysis. The second objective was fully achieved. The relevant research publication is 1) Loo and Tsui (under review), which summarizes the main results of the questionnaire survey and the computer-simulated experiment. The paper was prepared at the beginning of 2014 but it was rejected by Injury Prevention recently. We have taken the comments positively to improve the paper. The journal paper now is under review for consideration of publication in Accident Analysis & Prevention. The third objective was also fully achieved with the relevant research publication of Loo and Lam (2012), which directly addresses the activity patterns and the needs of the elderly by focusing on the elderly’s needs of visiting health care facilities and the walkability of the built environment. The fourth objective was fully achieved. The relevant research publications are Loo et al (2013), which summarises an effort to move from the place-based to person-based safety analysis through working with a multidisciplinary team; and 2) Wong et al (2012), which was a joint paper involving many researchers working on road safety in Hong Kong. The work was jointly supported by five different grants. In addition, this project partially supported the training of Linna Li (PhD), Frederic Du Verle (MPhil) and Samantha Nichols (MPhil), together with the continual research training of two recent PhD graduates, Dr. Winnie Lam and Dr. Ada Yao. They are all working on social sustainability and/or safety issues, especially those involving neighbourhood walkability and the elderly.

749210.label: Major findings and research outcome
749210.value: Elderly pedestrians are vulnerable. However, protecting the elderly by reducing their mobility can adversely affect their quality of life. Understanding the reasons for critically wrong road-crossing decisions is extremely important so that targeted measures can be made. Loo and Tsui (under review) found that, without considering vehicle speed, a judgment based on distance alone is highly dangerous. Elderly pedestrians are also not good at making road-crossing decisions when the oncoming vehicle is travelling on the far-side lane. On physical variables, age group is the most significant but younger age groups among the elderly actually made more critically wrong judgements. Lastly, elderly pedestrians with mild and moderate cognitive impairment were more likely to make critically wrong judgements. In this project, we also found that the methods of analysing road safety problems for the elderly pedestrians should be multi-disciplinary (Loo et al, 2013), network-constrained (Loo and Yao, 2013) and person-based (Loo et al, 2013; Yao and Loo, 2012). In particular, Loo et al (2013) integrated the crash and hospital databases, and used a public health and people-based approach in analysing crash patterns. Loo and Yao (2013) compared the hot zone results using the link-attribute approach and the network-constrained event-based approach to identify crash clusters. Yao and Loo (2012) calculated the crash intensity by a casualty-weighted method, which assigns different weights to different injury severity types, to identify dangerous road locations for pedestrians in Hong Kong. This project also found that the spatial patterns of elderly pedestrian crashes should be analysed by taking into consideration the actual volume of elderly pedestrian traffic (exposure) (Lam, Loo and Yao, 2013). In the paper, a disaggregate Geographical Information Systems (GIS)-based three-dimensional (3D) time-space framework was used to relate individual travel activities with crash patterns. In an attempt to integrate the activity-based and spatial crash analysis models, the paper combined three relational databases to better describe elderly pedestrian behaviour in a road network. The most hazardous locations and time for elderly pedestrians were found to be different when the exposure factor is considered. Last but not least, we found that the walkability of the built environment has to be systematically evaluated and enhanced to encourage the elderly to walk safely, conveniently and comfortably (Loo and Lam, 2012). The paper highlighted the need to assess and provide a walkable pedestrian environment for promoting active ageing.

749210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
749210.value: This project has great potential for further development because active transportation can be promoted to most people of all walks of life. The association among walking, the built environment and road safety is complex. One major potential is to extend the analysis to other vulnerable road users, such as school children. Another major potential is to further examine the relationships among walking, its potential health benefits (both physical and mental) to the elderly, and the built environment that they are living in. For the first potential, the PI and Co-I have submitted a RGC General Research Fund application in 2013 on “Understanding child pedestrians and re-thinking about independent mobility: Factors associated with ability to cross road safety”. Even without the research funding, the PI has started to conduct some meaningful research in the area. For the second potential, the PI, Dr Lam (the recent PhD graduate trained with the financial support of this grant), Dr Katagiri and Dr Mahendran have successfully applied for a major external research grant on “Promoting Active Transportation for the Elderly: A Comparative Study of Three Asian Cities” by the National University of Singapore. The project is now underway and is having satisfactory progress.

749410.label: Project Title(Chinese)
749410.value: 香港新高中英文科老師如何融合流行文化及語文教育

749410.label: Co - Investigator(s)
749410.value: Prof Canagarajah, Suresh Dr Hui, Diane Dr Lin, Angel

749410.label: Project Objectives
749410.value: To investigate existing perceptions and practices of a group of native-speaker (NETs) and local English teachers (LETs) towards integrating culture and English language education (ELE) through popular cultural texts; To examine any changes in the teachers’ perceptions and practices as a result of (1) increased understanding of methods to read texts critically; and (2) NET-LET collaboration; and To analyze the impact of culture-integrated text-mediated ELE on students’ intercultural literacies practices and sense of global identities.
rows: To investigate existing perceptions and practices of a group of native-speaker (NETs) and local English teachers (LETs) towards integrating culture and English language education (ELE) through popular cultural texts;
To examine any changes in the teachers’ perceptions and practices as a result of (1) increased understanding of methods to read texts critically; and (2) NET-LET collaboration; and
To analyze the impact of culture-integrated text-mediated ELE on students’ intercultural literacies practices and sense of global identities.

749410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
749410.value: The present proposal aims to investigate how teachers in Hong Kong integrate culture and English language education (ELE) at senior secondary level through engaging students in “reading” a variety of popular cultural texts in multimodal formats. The intertwining relationship between foreign language learning, culture, and global citizenship education has gained increasing attention worldwide particularly in overseas contexts such as North America and Europe (see Byram, 1989; Guilherme, 2002; Kramsch, 1995). It is stated in the 2007 Hong Kong Senior Secondary English Language Curriculum and Assessment Guide that a major aim for learning English is to enable students to extend their knowledge and experience of the other cultures. However, systematic empirical studies based in Hong Kong on what and how to integrate culture and language learning are scanty. In the present proposal, we particularly focus on examining whether and how teachers would perceive and practice culture-integrated ELE differently with increased understanding of critical text reading, and whether and how teachers from different sociocultural backgrounds such as the NETs (or native English teachers recruited under the current native English-speaking teachers’ scheme), and LETs (or local English-Chinese bilingual teachers) would perceive and practice culture and ELE differently with collaboration. NETs and LETs are believed to possess different culture-related resources as well as display different orientations to culture-integrated language teaching. This study will employ a qualitative case study methodology in three schools representing different student ability levels and with involvement of both NETs and LETs. Data from in-depth interviews, lesson observations, and documentary analyses of teaching materials and student work will be collected in three phases. In Phase 1, we explore the teacher participants’ existing perceptions and practices on culture and ELE. The next two phases take the form of an action research with researcher input and collaborations to investigate the impacts of adopting a critical textual analysis approach to reading popular cultural texts (Phase 2) and LET-NET collaboration (Phase 3) on the teachers’ pedagogical perceptions and practices. The impacts of different approaches on students’ intercultural literacies practices will also be explored. Findings from this project would contribute to a theory informing local and international foreign language educators and policy-makers of how popular cultural texts can be used in English lessons through a critical textual analysis approach and native-local teacher collaboration, and their impacts on students’ intercultural literacies and global identities in an Asian context. 本研究項目旨在研究新高中英文科老師如何透過多媒體流行文化素材以達至融合流行文化及語文教育的目的。近年，有關外語學習、文化和全球公民意識間的相互關係在北美和歐洲等海外國家已引起廣泛關注。由香港教育局製訂的新高中課程及評核指引(2007年版)內亦明確訂定有關透過英語學習以擴闊學生對不同文化的認識的主耍目的。然而，有糸統性地於香港進行有關如何融合流行文化及英語教育的學術研究卻絕無僅有。於此研究項目，我們特別關注老師會否和如何因為增加了對批判性閱讀的認識而改變他們對融合流行文化及英語教育的看法和實踐方法。此外，本研究項目亦會研究以廣東話為母語和以英語為母語的老師會否和如何通過協作而改變他們對融合流行文化及英語教育的看法和實踐方法。一般認為，以廣東話為母語和以英語為母語的老師擁有不同的文化資源，因而他們對融合流行文化及英語教育也會有不同的傾向。 此研究將於三所取錄不同組別學生的中學進行「定性個案研究」，每所學校均有一位以廣東話為母語和一位以英語為母語的老師被邀參與研究。數据採集將分三個階段進行，方法包括深入訪探、課堂觀察、教材及學生作業分析等。首階段集中採納老師對融合流行文化及英語教育的現存看法和實踐方法；第二及第三階段會以「行動研究」形式進行，通過研究人員的協助，老師將會於第二階段運用由研究人員提供的「批判性閱讀模式」引導學生分析流行文化素材。於第三階段以廣東話為母語和以英語為母語的老師將會相互協作教學。研究人員會通過分析三個階段的數据，而找出兩組老師對融合流行文化及英語教育的看法和實踐方法有否改變和如何改變，亦會找出兩組老師的教學模式如何影響相關學生的跨文化學習。 研究成果將有助建立一套理論，揭示如何在亞洲地區有效地融合流行文化及英語教育，以達至提升學生的跨文化學習及全球公民身份的建立和意識，為本地及國際語言教育學者及教育政策製訂官員提供寶貴的資料。

749410.label: Realisation of objectives
749410.value: We have fully achieved project objectives (PO for short) 1 and 2. PO1 has been achieved through three in-depth interviews with the project teachers, with one conducted before and after data collection and one conducted in the middle. Six senior secondary teachers (3 native English-speaking, or NETs, and 3 local teachers) from three schools were involved in the project. Due to practical constraints (see paragraph 3 below), two teachers from one school were unable to do all three interviews, and the NET teacher was only available to do one background interview. Despite repeated efforts from the Principal Investigator to arrange an end-of-project interview either face-to-face or via email, the NET teacher concerned did not respond positively. We stopped pursuing after making efforts for three to four months and we had to interpret the teacher’s responses as voluntary withdrawal. PO3 was achieved through three in-depth interviews with 33 students from the project schools (6 students from each of the two classes nominated by the school, but in one class, only three students agreed to join). One was a background interview, and two interviews including a popular culture text reading activity were conducted in the middle and at the end of the project. PO2 was achieved for 80% mainly because we had problems identifying a high band school. The school we originally identified had to withdraw due to manpower changes, and we were only able to obtain a replacement school after one year of the project. The two teachers were, however, unable to conduct two phases of teaching due to tight teaching schedule, and the constraints from the school-based common curriculum requirements under which all teachers at the same year level needed to implement. Nevertheless, the two teachers agreed to conduct one collaborative planning meeting for one lesson based on our project framework (the teachers originally agreed to do two lessons but due to their tight exam preparation schedule, both only did one lesson for the project). As for the other two schools, three of the four teachers contributed lessons to all three phases of the project, but one NET was not able to conduct the lessons collaboratively planned with his local colleague in Phase III due to personal issues and curriculum constraints.

749410.label: Major findings and research outcome
749410.value: Teachers’ perceptions of culture-integrated English teaching have been documented in a peer-reviewed journal article (item 8.1 in Part C). As for practices, the classroom teaching data collected from different phases revealed that the project teachers were able to change their pedagogical orientations from a knowledge transmission approach to a critical cultural text reading approach based on the framework introduced in the workshop, which seeks to engage students in exploring and discussing the cultural implications behind certain words and expressions in a popular cultural text. It was observed that students had made more attempts to express critical opinions towards cultural issues (e.g gender and social class) in the project lessons than in the baseline lessons. Most of the project teachers, particularly two of the NET teachers, had expressed a novel understanding of their students’ ability to conduct higher-order thinking. The study, however, also reveals concerns about the performance gaps between students’ L1 cognitive maturity and L2 language resources. Discussion and analysis of this cognition-language gap issue will appear in another journal article (item 8.2, Part C). Students’ intercultural literacies development was evaluated through two popular culture small group reading tasks conducted in Chinese. Most students were able to identify critical intercultural elements (e.g. related to gender stereotypes and social class) with prompts from the researchers. their reading of an authentic English advertisement based on principles from the critical text reading framework. It was also found that students with lower English proficiency tended to rely on the visual images of the text and their everyday knowledge in their reading analysis. While all students welcomed the inclusion of popular culture in the school curriculum, most seemed unable to identify learning points beyond vocabulary items. Most also reported a lack of confidence in expressing complex ideas in English. Relevant data and analysis will be presented in an international conference (item 9.4, Part C). In terms of NET-LET collaboration, each pair of native-speaking (NET) and local (LET) teachers had conducted one joint teaching planning meeting. Based on the data, we found that the meeting has afforded the teachers an opportunity to exchange resources pertinent to their cultural backgrounds, and be exposed to cultural resources that they were not aware of. However, findings from one pair of teachers also showed non-reciprocal exchange patterns probably due to perceived power relationship and the English proficiency gaps between the NET and LET.

749410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
749410.value: The findings of the project call for the need to further research on the impacts of English language proficiencies on students’ ability to conduct critical cultural exploration through reading and discussing popular cultural texts. Such abilities can be compared to similar abilities in Chinese, or the students’ first language. The PI of the project had developed a GRF proposal for 2013-14, and succeeded in obtaining the funding to conduct the research between Nov 2013-Oct 2015 to investigate the role of the first and second languages in the discursive construction of critical thinking. The new GRF will also investigate whether and how the interrelationships between critical thinking (as a form of higher-order thinking) and language resources are acknowledged and developed in different disciplines including Chinese, English, and Liberal Studies.

749410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
749410.value: This project investigated how a group of senior secondary teachers in Hong Kong integrated culture into English language teaching through engaging students in reading popular cultural texts, focusing on whether and how this pedagogical initiative would enable senior secondary students to develop their creativity, critical thinking skills, and intercultural awareness. We also examined whether and how teachers from different sociocultural backgrounds such as the native-English teachers and local English-Chinese bilingual teachers could collaborate in the pedagogical preparation and exchange distinct linguistic and cultural resources to the development of their own intercultural awareness as well as that of their students. Six teachers from three schools took part in this three-year project. The project is significant in showing how popular culture can be utilized to promote critical thinking and intercultural literacies of adolescent students in addition to bringing fun and laughter. Most students reported feeling more engaged in expressing own opinions in the project lessons, even though they also felt inadequate in their command of English to express complicated ideas. It also shows the desirability for teachers from diverse backgrounds to complement each other in the deployment of cross-linguistic and cross-cultural resources to jointly help students develop their intercultural literacies.

749510.value: 小型开放经济中的模型错误,消费波动,和当前帐户.

749510.label: Co - Investigator(s)
749510.value: Dr Nie, Jun Prof Young, Eric

749510.label: Project Objectives
749510.value: The main objective is to examine the effects on consumption and the current account of two types of information frictions: model misspecification and rational inattention in an otherwise standard ICA model. Solve and simulate a robust control and filtering problem of a typical information-constrained consumer who does not trust his model in small open economies. Use the Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) to estimate the model and use the detection error probability to calibrate the preference for robustness. Show how the interactions of robustness and RI can make the model better explain the data in the following aspects: (i) The joint dynamics of the current account and income; (ii) the difference in the relative volatility of consumption to income in developed and emerging economies; (iii) the persistence and volatility of the current account; (iv) the positive relationship between uncertainty and the current account.

Show how the interactions of robustness and RI can make the model better explain the data in the following aspects: (i) The joint dynamics of the current account and income; (ii) the difference in the relative volatility of consumption to income in developed and emerging economies; (iii) the persistence and volatility of the current account; (iv) the positive relationship between uncertainty and the current account.

749510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
749510.value: Many empirical studies show that the stylized intertemporal current account (ICA) models based on the permanent income hypothesis are often rejected in the post-war data. Specifically, the main problems with the standard ICA models are three-fold. First, it cannot capture the actual dynamic responses of the current account to income shocks. If income is a unit root or a persistent AR(1) process, the current account is constant or procyclical, whereas in the data it is countercyclical. Second, it cannot explain why consumption is more volatile than output in emerging economies, whereas the reverse is the case in developed economies. Third, it cannot generate large enough volatility in the predicted current account relative to the volatility in the actual current account data. In addition, these models ignore some important channels through which income uncertainty affects the current account. Hansen and Sargent (1995, 2007) first introduced robustness (a concern for model misspecification) into economic models. Agents with this preference are concerned about the possibility that their model is misspecified in a manner that is difficult to detect statistically; consequently, they choose their decisions as if the subjective distribution over shocks was chosen by a malevolent nature in order to minimize their expected utility. As shown in Luo and Young (2009), the stronger preference for robustness, the more consumption responds initially to income shocks. Since the main problem in the stylized ICA model is that given income processes, the model leads to unrealistic procyclical current accounts, the sensitive consumption reaction under robustness could possibly improve the model's prediction on the current account. In addition, the preference for robustness is context specific, i.e., agents in emerging economies could be more concerned about model misspecification than agents in developed economies, which might be helpful to explain the difference in the relative volatility of consumption in the two economies. However, robustness itself cannot provide a strong propagation mechanism that is essential to generate persistent current accounts. We then consider another important information friction: Rational Inattention (RI). Sims (2003) first introduced RI into economics and argued that it is a plausible method for introducing sluggishness, randomness, and delay into economic models. Given these features of robustness and RI, we plan to examine how the combination of the two types of information frictions is capable of producing the right consumption dynamics, a countercyclical and volatile current account, and a positive association between uncertainty and the current account. 我们在一个小型开放经济模型中研究两种信息不完备: 模型错误和有限信息处理能力, 对消费波动和当前帐户的影响. 我们证明两种信息不完备的的互相作用会改善模型对收入,消费,和当前帐户的动态行为. 具体来说, 它们能改善模型对以下几个方面的解释能力: (i) 当期收入和当前帐户的相关性, (ii) 新兴国家和发达国家当前帐户的不同持续性和波动, (iii) 相对消费波动和消费对收入变化的反应.

749510.label: Realisation of objectives
749510.value: All of the objectives proposed for this project are realized. The project has generated two papers. The major paper generated from this project has been published in a top economics journal: The Journal of International Economics. In this JIE paper, we addressed the objectives we proposed in this project and fully explored how the two important informational frictions: model uncertainty due to robustness and state uncertainty due to rational inattention affect the joint dynamics of income, consumption, and the current account in small-open economies including developed and emerging countries within an otherwise standard international current account model.

749510.label: Major findings and research outcome
749510.value: We first build up international current account models with the two informational frictions. We then solve the models explicitly. Using the explicit solutions, we carefully calibrate the key model parameters using the detection error probability approach and show that the model with both informational frictions can quantitatively explain what we observed in the data. Specifically, we find that the interactions of the two informational frictions can improve the model's predictions on the following key stochastic properties: (i) The correlation between the current account and income; (ii) the persistence and volatility of the current account; (iii) the positive relationship between uncertainty and the current account; (iv) the difference in the relative volatility of consumption to income in developed and emerging economies.

749510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
749510.value: This paper examines the importance of the two informational frictions in explaining the observed joint behavior of consumption, income, and the current account in small open economies. In the future, it is promising to apply this idea in another important international macroeconomic setting: the two-country general equilibrium setting. Once we can successfully incorporate the informational frictions into that setting, we can address some very interesting issues in international macroeconomics. For example, the comovements of key macroeconomic variables in the two countries and the observed low international consumption correlations. In addition, we can also address how they can affect the dynamics of the exchange rates.

749510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
749510.value: In the major paper generated from this project, we examine the effects of two types of "induced uncertainty", model uncertainty due to robustness (RB) and state uncertainty due to finite information–processing capacity (called rational inattention or RI), on the observed behavior of consumption and the current account. We show that the combination of RB and RI improves the model's predictions for (i) the contemporaneous correlation between the current account and income and (ii) the volatility and persistence of the current account in small open emerging and developed economies. In addition, we show that the two informational frictions improve the model's ability to match the impulse response of consumption to income and the relative volatility of consumption to income growth.

750210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
750210.value: The rise of the knowledge economy has generated new global infrastructures with information technology playing an increasingly important role. The popularity and prominence of information technology not only changes the nature of knowledge but also restructures higher education, research and learning. It is in such a wider context that an increasing number of institutions of higher learning are being established with new missions. In addition to the missions in improving their research and teaching performance, the expansion of mission opens up new opportunities for universities to establish linkages with the industry and the society at large, but it also poses new challenges for which they may not be prepared. The intense pressure on universities to be more entrepreneurial and innovative is most evident in their efforts to engage in revenue enhancing activities and in their efforts to improve their positions in global ranking of universities. Universities have embarked on massive restructuring exercises along the line of “marketization”, “corporatization”, “privatization” and “commercialization”. Universities’ quest for becoming entrepreneurial has inevitably changed the role of the university sector and its relationship with the state, market, and society. A Triple Helix network system has evolved which opens a window that generates a set of coordinates transcending the points of reference of discourses that previously took place within separate institutional spheres. This research project sets out in the socio-economic context outlined above to examine the major policies and strategies that governments in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Singapore, South Korea, Japan and Mainland China have adopted in driving their university systems to become more entrepreneurial and innovative. More specifically, this study will focus on how universities in these selected Asian societies have become more proactive and entrepreneurial in engaging with business for enhancing innovation. Central research questions to be addressed include: What major strategies have these university systems adopted to reach out to business for enhancing innovation? What measures have universities employed in commercializing their research products and promoting knowledge transfer? With the objective of critically examining the changing relationship between the state, university and business, this research project will develop a new conceptual framework for analyzing the changing roles and relationships. The conclusions drawn will assist local public administrators in Hong Kong to make better decisions about future policies and strategies in enhancing Hong Kong’s global competitiveness in the context of the rise of Asia and China Mainland. 這項研究計劃旨在探索近年東亞區內大學在推動大學創新及企業發展的策略，以求使大學變得更有活力來面對急劇的社會及經濟變遷。本研究計劃集中比較東亞區內大學如何推動大學創新及發展企業精神來使大學教學及研究變得更適合時代需要，特別以對比角度來探索東亞地區內大學創新能力和推動知識轉移的策略。

750210.label: Major findings and research outcome
750210.value: When comparing how Hong Kong has promoted knowledge transfer and innovation advancement with other three East Asian economies Singapore, Taiwan and Korea, we must admit that all other three East Asian economies have taken a more proactive approach in promoting university-industry-business cooperation. In particular, the governments of Singapore and Korea have adopted a more directive role in shaping innovation and research policy, while Taiwan government has started encouraging university-industry-business cooperation earlier than the other three East Asian Tigers. Hong Kong, in comparing with the other three East Asian Tigers and even with the most recent strategies and initiatives adopted by the Chinese government in the mainland, is far more slow in policy response. One of the reasons accounting for this approach is closely related to Hong Kong's liberal stance in directing innovation, research and development. In terms of state funding support in promoting innovation, research and development, Hong Kong is far behind when compare with other East Asian economies, let alone the role of the state in driving such an endeavour. Facing intensified global and regional competition, the Hong Kong government should rethink and search for new governance model in shaping / directing innovation, research and development in Hong Kong in order to maintain the global and regional competitiveness of the city-state. During the last few years when conducting the present research project, the research team has tried to publish different internationally refereed outputs. Based upon the findings, the PI and his team has been able to produce a single-authored book, an edited volume and a few journal articles and book chapters in disseminating the findings. The PI has also made use of different invitations to speak at a number of international conferences / symposium to publicize the findings. Through presenting the findings of the present research, the PI and his team has attracted more international research cooperation opportunities as the PI has been invited to join two international research platforms, namely, Asia Pacific Higher Education Research Partnership (APHGRP) as a core member and a newly developed ESRC Centre for Engaged Global Higher Education based at the Institute of Education, the University of London in the UK as a core member directing a research theme related to promoting of innovation and internationalization in higher education and its impacts on East Asian students / graduates' career development and social mobility after educated in the UK. Locally in Hong Kong, the PI has been interviewed by local media to comment on innovation policy adopted by HK government and his comparative work has indeed enriched the local discussions.

750210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
750210.value: The present research project is completed but further work can be done in extending the research scope to examine how the Chinese government in general and universities in the mainland in particular have transformed their policies and practices in promoting innovation, research and development, as well as entrepreneurship. The proposed research would provide useful insights for Hong Kong universities to search for appropriate ways in working / cooperating with research institutions or universities in China mainland, identifying both strengths and weaknesses of Hong Kong when engaging with her Chinese counterparts in research cooperation. As a recent international review reports that despite Hong Kong still maintaining a relatively high ranking in terms of global competitiveness, the competitiveness of its higher education and research / innovation is declining. The proposed research would provide new insights and perspectives for universities / research institutes in Hong Kong to develop deep cooperation with institutions in China mainland and even in Taiwan to further enhance regional cooperation in research, innovation promotion and technological advancement. Such a proposal would enhance research productivity and development in the Greater China region. A public policy research grant could be developed along this line of research activities.

750210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
750210.value: Hong Kong has successfully relied upon “four traditional economic pillars”, including financial services, trade & logistics, tourism, and professional & other producer services in the last few decades. Yet these industries are facing ever-mounting challenges from regional competitors like Shenzhen, Shanghai and Singapore in recent years. The strive for a knowledge economy has become even more acute after the 1997 handover and the Asian Financial Crisis in 1997-98, when Hong Kong’s finance-centered economy was questioned. This research is set out against this context to critically examine how the four Asian Tiger economies like Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea and Taiwan have tried to transform the roles of universities in engaging with the industry and business to enhance innovation and entrepreneurship. This comparative studies has clearly suggested these Asian tigers have confronted intensified pressures to enhance their global competitiveness by promoting university-industry-business cooperation in enhancing innovation and creativity. More specifically, this studies compares and contrasts different strategies that these Asian governments have adopted in responding to changing social and economic challenges and how the role of universities has transformed adapting to changes. This project shows Hong Kong is behind the other East Asian economies in promoting innovation, research and development and the HKSAR Government should adopt a more proactive approach in promoting innovation, investing in research and technology and knowledge transfer activities to enhance Hong Kong's global and regional competitiveness.

750610.label: Project Objectives
750610.value: To carry out a thorough genealogical study on the evolution of the urban planning system in Hong Kong, paying special attention to the relationships among urban planning, urban development and urban form, and the implications on citizens’ right to the city. To analyse through a synthesised framework of Healey’s institutional perspective (2007a, 2007b) and Flyvbjerg’s phronetic (practical wisdom) research guidelines the genesis of the 1991 Comprehensive Review of the TPO, the 1996 Town Planning White Bill, the failed enactment of the 2000 Town Planning Bill and the eventual partial amendment of the Ordinance in 2004 and to assess their implications on place governance over time. To evaluate if the delay of the amendment of the outdated TPO had led to the rise of ‘walled buildings’ and when and how this ‘urban form’ has become ‘problematised’ as a society-wide concern and its implications on the place governance processes. Through a detailed case study of civil society’s attempt to stop the planning approval of ‘walled’ buildings in an old neighbourhood, examine the effectiveness of the 2004 amended TPO in guaranteeing citizens’ right to the city. To make appropriate recommendations to the planning system and, among others, the TPO, with a view to developing a mode of place governance that embraces people’s right to planning a socially just city with quality places.

750610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
750610.value: With the mushrooming of massive ‘walled buildings’ in Hong Kong in the past two decades, critics have condemned the planning system for turning Hong Kong, Asia’s World City, into Asia’s ‘walled’ city. Those living in the old neighbourhoods behind the ‘walled buildings’ have suffered from blocked views and ventilation, ‘heat island effect’ and deteriorated air quality. They are angry in face of a planning system that seems to deny their ‘right to the city’ (Brenner, 2000; Harvey, 2003; Lefebvre, 1968, 1991), a right to reshape cities into socially just, economically vibrant and environmental sustainable spaces. In fact, the government had undertaken a comprehensive review of the then outdated Town Planning Ordinance (TPO) in 1991 with a view to making the planning system more open, fair and accountable to the public. A Town Planning White Bill was published for consultation in 1996 and a comprehensive Town Planning Bill was introduced in the Legislative Council in 2000 but it was not until 2004 that the TPO was partially amended. Has such a delay led to the emergence of ‘walled buildings’? This study would like to use Healey’s institutional perspective (2006, 2007a, 2007b) and Flyvbjerg’s phronetic (practical wisdom) social science research guidelines to analyse why it took Hong Kong 13 years to enact a partially amended TPO. It will investigate the relationships of this delay with the growth of ‘walled buildings’, people’s ‘right to the city’ and the mode of place governance. The study will first review the historical relationships among urban planning, urban development and urban form to provide the contextual background for three thick TPO and ‘walled buildings’ related case studies. The first one is a review of the genesis and evolution of the TPO reform to examine the politics involved in the rhetoric and practices of various stakeholders for or against it. The second one concerns the emergence of ‘walled buildings’ and its relationship with the delayed amendment of the TPO. It will also examine how and when such ‘walled buildings’ became a social concern that eventually changed the routinised planning practices. The third case zoomed into a ‘failed’ case of ‘walled building’ development as a result of strong local objections in order to evaluate the effectiveness of the 2004 amended TPO. Finally, the research will put forward recommendations for a better mode of place governance that will guarantee people’s right to a socially just city with quality places.

750610.label: Realisation of objectives
750610.value: Almost all the objectives have been achieved. The project had successfully reviewed the evolution of the urban planning system in Hong Kong (Objective 1). The constraints and limitations of the system have much to do with its original attachment to the Buildings and Works Departments within the bureaucracy. This historical association also explains the difficulties urban planners encountered in reforming the Town Planning Ordinance (TPO) to resume the power of development control from other rules and regulations (Objective 2). Hence, the delay of the amendment of the TPO did not directly lead to the rise of ‘walled buildings’. Yet, if the TPO were amended more comprehensively earlier on to allow for more involvements by citizens in the planning process, limitations of the overall development control framework in Hong Kong might then be identified at an earlier time and that might check the spread of ‘walled buildings’ (Objective 3). Detailed case studies of development projects proved that a plethora of factors had led to the civil society’s efforts in stopping the growth of ‘walled’ buildings and the protection of people’s right to the city (Objective 4). Recommendations have been made to improve the system in various publications (Objective 5). We did encounter some difficulties in the detailed case study, that is, the mega tower (now Hopewell Centre II): the developer had declined multiple invitations for interviews; and the absence of new land leases with the presence of new buildings on the Hopewell sites in Wanchai is another puzzle that the project fails to resolve and this has affected the completion of a paper on this case.

750610.label: Major findings and research outcome
750610.value: The Government’s heavy reliance on land-relate revenue (about 1/3 of all revenue) accounts for a pro-development governance regime that emphasizes on the production of spaces for exchange (market) values rather than use values that treasure ‘history, culture and heritage’ (papers 2, 4&6). The resultant urban forms shape people’s social interactions and sometimes cause controversial debates (papers 1,4&8). Yet case studies show that citizen’s right to the city movements have also led to changes in urban form, thus highlighting the importance of people’s right to city planning (papers 1,3,7&8 and conference paper 4). The pro-development regime is characterized by development control mechanisms that grant development rights to land owners through a set of relatively simple planning and building regulations. The corollary of this is confined control of development by urban planners and limited rights to city planning by the lay public (papers 3,6&8). The Town Planning Ordinance (TPO) is inadequate not only in engaging the general public but also ineffective in protecting the natural and cultural heritage and environmental qualities (papers 3,4,6,7&8). As planning owes its institutional origin in the buildings and works sections of the colonial bureaucracy, some of the planning power is embedded in the buildings related regulations. Planners face a lot of obstacles and objections from the pro-development forces in reforming the planning system to regain the right to regulate development (papers 3,6&8). Nevertheless, the awakening civil society and green groups have been instrumental in problematizing the ‘walled buildings’ and forced limited institutional changes (papers 3, 4&8). In particular, intellectuals have played a ‘system-transforming’ role within and outside the administrative system to counteract top-down technical discourses through synthesizing and mobilizing connaissance (contextual and personal) knowledge to initiate changes in planning regulations, processes and the eventual urban form (papers 1,6&8). It is therefore important to employ different types of knowledge through the (antagonistic) interactions among different stakeholders in formal or informal institutions to negotiate the eventual development of urban forms (Conference papers 6&7). The study points to the merit of using the concept of planning rights to guide the establishment of planning-related institutions (paper 3&8). It calls for a new breed of planners that are capable of navigating through different disciplines, invoking various analytical and prescriptive insights, integrating different types of knowledge, building environmentally friendly sustainable communities through capacity building processes and efforts to develop consensus amidst conflicts and arguments (papers 2,3,5,6&8).

750610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
750610.value: Further research work can be identified as follows: 1. Review the Buildings Ordinance and evaluate the effectiveness of the current development control mechanisms to identify avenues to reforms that would grant more rights to citizens in urban development and planning. 2. To theorize the relationships among the government, the private sector and the civil society in the making of urban forms via institutionalized processes that have been modified and changed over time. 3. Investigate further how the planning and development regimes shape the urban spaces to produce exchange values and how such processes affect the use values of the urban realm to existing citizens. 4. Applying the concept of the right to the city in the specific context of Hong Kong. Efforts need to be made to understand the impacts of the current development and planning regimes on the building of communities and pros and cons for the long-term sustainable development of Hong Kong. Another GRF grant has been obtained to work on point 4 above. A proposal on point 3 has been submitted to compare and contrast the development and planning regimes in producing spaces for exchange and use values in Hong Kong, Shenzhen and Xian.

750610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
750610.value: The government’s heavy reliance on land-related revenue has produced a pro-development regime that privileges the production of spaces for exchange (market) rather than use values. A set of relatively simple planning and building regulations, developed long time ago when planning was subsumed in the works section, has given rise to bulky ‘walled buildings’ along the waterfront, impacting negatively on the environment of old urban areas. Given the presence of strong pro-development camps, planners have failed to revamp fundamentally the outdated Town Planning Ordinance (TPO) to grant the lay public more rights to city planning. Nevertheless, the awakening civil society has succeeded in ‘problematizing’ the ‘walled building’ phenomenon and mobilizing synthesized contextual and personal knowledge to counteract the trend. The study advocates the use of the right to the city concept to guide the restructuring of the planning-related institutions such as further amendment of the outdated TPO, the review of the Building (Planning) Regulations and the nurturing of a new breed of urban planners who are capable of navigating through different disciplines, invoking various analytical and prescriptive insights, integrating different types of knowledge, building environmentally friendly sustainable communities through capacity building processes and efforts to develop consensus amidst conflicts and arguments.

750710.label: Project Title(Chinese)
750710.value: 工作嵌入: 東西方文化的比較

750710.label: Project Objectives
750710.value: The present study clarifies the nature of the construct of job embeddedness, and in particular, whether it is perceived positively or negatively by employees. The present study extends our understanding of the impact of job embeddedness beyond its current focus on turnover. Specifically, we examine in-role performance, citizenship behavior, and counterproductive work behavior as well. The present study addresses when and why job embeddedness is associated with positive versus negative organizational outcomes. To resolve conflicting perspectives, we examine how factors such as employee organizational trust and amount of external social networking activity help explain the relationship between job embeddedness and various important work outcomes. The present study addresses cross-cultural differences in the nomological network of job embeddedness, which have been neglected in the existent literature.

750710.label: Realisation of objectives
750710.value: 1) Clarifying the nature of the construct of job embeddedness, and in particular, whether it is perceived positively or negatively by employees. Outcomes: We have found that, unlike many previous studies on job embeddedness have shown, employees tend to view job embeddedness negatively, particularly seeing it as a stressor that will upset work-family balance. Thus, the first objective is fully achieved. 2) Extending our understanding of the impact of job embeddedness beyond its current focus on turnover. Outcomes: In this project, we have examined various consequence variables of job embeddedness (e.g., citizenship behavior, innovative behavior). Interestingly, we observed that job embeddedness also affects such personal outcomes as work-to-family conflict and family-to-work conflict quite strongly, which have not been examined before by other embeddedness researchers. Thus, the second objective is fully achieved. 3) Examining when and why job embeddedness is associated with positive versus negative organizational outcomes. Outcomes: In this project, we have examined several moderators, such as trust and social relationships. One moderator which was found to have particularly interesting results is individualism vs. collectivism. Our data show that, compared to collectivists, individualists are more likely to see job embeddedness as negatively affecting their work-family balance. Collectivists, on the other hand, are less likely to view and react to it in a negative way. Thus, the third objective is fully achieved. 4) Addressing cross-cultural differences in the nomological network of job embeddedness, which have been neglected in the existent literature. Outcomes: We have shown that there are cultural differences (between the U.S. and China) in respondents’ reactions to job embeddedness. The U.S. respondents reacted more strongly to job embeddedness. Thus, the fourth objective is fully achieved.

750710.label: Major findings and research outcome
750710.value: Across the various consequence variables of job embeddedness we had measured in our field studies, we observed that the relationship between job embeddedness and work-family balance is particularly strong. Therefore, we have focused our first publication on this issue (Part C, 1st publication). In that manuscript, we offered competing hypotheses regarding the relationships of changes in organizational and community embeddedness with changes in work-to-family and family-to-work conflict. Data were collected from 250 U.S. and 165 Chinese managers and professionals, all of whom were married, at three points in time over a ten-month period. Results suggest that increases in perceptions of organizational and community embeddedness are associated with increases in work-to-family conflict and family-to-work conflict over time. Further, we found that these effects were even stronger for employees with highly individualistic values. Thus, while much of the previous research has focused on the positive effects of employee embeddedness for individuals’ work lives, the present study provides some evidence of the potentially negative effects of employee embeddedness for individuals’ family lives. Our second project was not related to job embeddedness. However, because we had extra space on our field surveys for including more measurement items, we measured several additional constructs that were of interest to us more broadly. With those data, we generated another manuscript which examined whether and how employees reciprocate to their organizations for the idiosyncratic deals (i-deals) they receive (Part C, 2nd publication). Specifically, in that project, we examined whether i-deals (in scheduling flexibility and professional development) are related to employees’ flexible work role orientation, social networking behavior, and organizational trust over time. In turn, we hypothesized that these mediating variables would be positively related to employees’ use of constructive voice. Data were collected from 466 managers and professionals in the U.S. and China at three points in time over a ten-month period (this dataset is independent of the dataset used in the first project described above). The analyses revealed that flexible work role orientation, social networking behavior, and organizational trust all mediated the relationship between i-deals and voice behavior. Further, the mediating effects were generally stronger for professional development i-deals than for scheduling flexibility i-deals and were generally stronger in the China sample than in the U.S. sample.

750710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
750710.value: Extending the first project described above, researchers should collect data from dual wage-earning couples to further examine the effects of organizational and community embeddedness on employees. Specifically, when the core research question is whether organizational and community embeddedness is positively or negatively related to work-to-family and family-to-work conflicts, it is important to examine that question in a sample where such conflicts are likely to be both prevalent and relevant. In the first study described above, we investigate married employees. However, the case of dual wage-earning couples is even more interesting in this regard because, when both partners have jobs, the totality of embedding forces keeping them attached to their organizations and communities is likely to be greater. Furthermore, when both partners have jobs, they are even more vulnerable to experiencing conflicts between their work and family domains. For dual wage-earning couples, then, both the embedding forces and the likelihood of experiencing conflicts between work and family domains are likely to be stronger. As such, they provide an especially rich context for studying the effects of embeddedness on the work-family interface for employees. Thus, this line of investigation represents a logical extension of the first project described earlier.

750710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
750710.value: 1st publication: By embedding employees in their organizations (e.g., providing them with more perks) and in their communities (e.g., encouraging more involvement in volunteer and philanthropic activities), senior management hopes to make employees less likely to leave their jobs. However, we found that increases in organizational and community embeddedness are also associated with greater conflict between work and family. Consequently, our study suggests that adopting an “embeddedness human resource strategy” cannot be viewed as a positive end in and of itself, and cannot be seen as effective remedies for lowering turnover across all cultures. 2nd publication: The current study demonstrates to managers that i-deals are related to one important component of performance (namely, constructive voice behavior). In addition, the results here suggest that granting of i-deals contributes to employees taking a more flexible orientation to their work, a greater interest in internal networking, and a greater appreciation of the organization’s efforts on their behalf. Taken together, the results here suggest that i-deals can serve an “unfreezing” function in how employees approach their jobs, their colleagues, and their employers more broadly. In addition, this study shows that i-deals will have the greatest positive impact when they are consistent with cultural norms.

751110.label: Project Objectives
751110.value: Sketch the historical and institutional development of volunteering in mainland China, and compare it with the existing data on Hong Kong, Taiwan and elsewhere. Describe and analyse the public discourse on volunteering as it appears in the Chinese press, internet and official documents. Collect and analyse the biographies and narratives of active volunteers involved with four cases of organizations involved in promoting volunteering: Communist Party Youth League, Yidan xuetang Confucian movement, Dongjingyuan Buddhist/popular religious movement, and secular post-quake relief NGOs. Investigate the history, internal organization, ideology, moral discourse, social action and legitimation strategies of the four organizations. Observe acts of service by volunteers in the four organizations, and the social roles and relationships they constitute; establish typologies of volunteers, volunteer roles and volunteer actions; and describe the social spaces constituted by volunteering. Identify and compare any correlations between the social spaces and the moral discourses of the four organizations.
