751110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
751110.value: Following the Sichuan earthquake of 12 May 2008, tens of thousands of volunteers spontaneously joined the relief effort – an unorganized grassroots movement which caught both the Chinese government and international observers by surprise. A few months later, at the Beijing Olympic games, thousands of well-organized volunteers efficiently catered to the needs of visitors. With these two events, volunteerism became visible as a mass phenomenon in China, as many Chinese seek to “do something good” for others and something “meaningful” for themselves. Volunteering represents a new form of civic engagement with profound implications for the development of Chinese civil society. But the status of the volunteer remains contested and weakly institutionalized. The self-understanding and public legitimation of volunteers is often couched in a moral discourse concerning motivations and obligations, appropriate behaviour and social ideals – a discourse which resonates strongly with traditional discourses of virtue and merit, as well as with the socialist state’s rhetoric of citizenship and nation-building. Such discourses are invoked and deployed by volunteers involved in a wide array of groups, including the Communist Youth League; Confucian, Buddhist and Christian movements; and secular NGOs aligning themselves to global progressive ideals. A moral discourse posits ideal models for both self-transformation through good deeds, and the transformation of social relationships through service to others. But it is not clear to what extent volunteers in groups drawing on vastly different traditions of social engagement deploy different moral discourses, and to what extent such differences contribute to variations in social and political outcomes. The purpose of this study is to answer the following question: how does moral discourse structure the trajectories and social spaces of volunteers in contemporary mainland China? The inquiry will be framed within three levels of social context: the discourse, organization and actions of specific groups which recruit and deploy volunteers; the general discourse on volunteering in the broader culture, as it appears in the Chinese press; and the ideological, institutional and political norms and boundaries imposed by the state. Focusing on four types of volunteer organization and using media analysis, focus groups, interviews and participant observation, the study will assess what kinds of social spaces are created through volunteer action within the complex political constraints on civic engagement which exist in China, and whether different moral discourses lead to the formation of different types of social spaces. 當代中國的志願者運動：道德話語與社會空間 本課題將用人類學的視角研究最近在中國出現的志願者文化。從5－12地震和北京奧運會后，在中國的志願者運動逐漸普及。本課題將考察不同志願者文化的 形成及演變。 關注志願者的內部範疇、準則和道德話語；通過志願者活動所形成的社會關係模式、互助模式及社會空間；個體、機構及社區之間的互動；傳統文化中志願者的前身及當代志願者浪潮作為中國現代性的表現。

751110.value: Over 80 individual and group interviews of over 200 persons were conducted. The objectives were surpassed, with more than four organizations being studied. Research was conducted in Guangzhou, Chengdu, Beijing and Shanghai, as well as in rural Sichuan, in Hong Kong and Taiwan.

751110.label: Major findings and research outcome
751110.value: The phenomenon of volunteering in contemporary China forces us to reconsider the dynamics of civil society in socialist China. Millions of volunteers constitute the active base of civic engagement at the grassroots, dedicating their time and energy to the needs of an abstracted society that extends beyond their particularistic interests and networks. In this sense, they are the foundation of a society of active citizens. However, volunteers' motivation tends to be self-expression and personal development, rather than social engagement or transformation. As a spontaneous movement, the transformational potential of volunteerism is thus limited. Religious and political organizations, however, are creating structures for the systematic and sustained articulation of personal yearnings and social concern. Some of them, such as the Communist Party Youth League, do so with the express goal of channelling the energies of volunteers toward the goals of the state. Religious groups, on the other hand, have a variety of ideological and practical objectives. Ultimately, a tension always exists between volunteering as an expression of modern individualization, the social and ideological goals of the organizations that attempt to mobilize them, and the aims of the state. Individualization and Civic Engagement in China’s Middle Class Chapter 3: Constructing a Moral Self: Public and Private Narratives of Volunteers Chapter 4: Searching for a Purpose: Volunteers at a School for Migrant Children Chapter 5: Connecting Through Suffering: Religious Volunteers after the Sichuan Earthquake Chapter 6: Recovering the Nation: A Confucian Volunteer Movement Chapter 7: Civilizing the Natives: Han Volunteers in the Yi Minority Region Chapter 8: Training for Leadership: Youth League Volunteers in Rural West China Chapter 9: Regional Comparisons: Hong Kong, Taiwan and Japan Chapter 10: Contested Motives: The Politics of Public Altruism in China

751510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
751510.value: With Asia emerging from the economic crisis that struck the region in late 2008, this is an opportune time for beginning to assess the social impacts of the crisis and the performance of social protection programs against them. It is within this context that the study proposes to examine social protection and economic crisis in four middle and high income countries in Asia: Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand. The four are remarkably similar yet significantly different, making them excellent cases for comparative study. The central questions the proposed study will address are: What are the social impacts of the 2008/09 economic crisis? What social protection arrangements exist to protect residents against them? How do the arrangements perform in face of the crisis? What are the factors that have shaped the arrangements and their performance? Towards understanding the social effects of the current economic crisis, the study will collect and analyse data on a comprehensive range of employment, income, expenditure, health, and education indicators. To understand the social protection programs, the study will delineate the programs’ key design features and analyse their implications, including the timing and circumstances of their establishment, eligibility for receiving benefits, sources of financing, and governance. The social safety nets to be covered by the study include non-contributory programs directly targeting the poor or those vulnerable to poverty. To assess the programs’ performance, the study will examine: public expenditure, coverage, poverty-targeting, impact on the poor’s income/expenditure, school enrolment, and healthcare utilization. Finally, the project will study the social, political, and economic factors that have shaped the social protection programs and their performance, as these are choices made by policymakers guided by a mixture of interests, institutions, and ideas. The information needs for completing the study are vast. To meet the challenge, the project proposes to conduct subejctive survey research and focus group discussion, in addition to combing through published policy papers, statistical data and annual reports of relevant agencies,. The proposed study will be, when completed, the first systematic assessment of the social protection arrangements in Asia and their performance during economic crisis. It expected to make a vital contribution to empirical appraisal and theoretical debates on social protection in Asia. The findings will also be of practical significance in that they will relate directly to improving the programs and thus improving the lives of people affected by future economic crises. 隨著亞洲擺脫經濟危機襲擊該地區在2008年年底，這是一個時機，開始評估社會影響的危機，表現社會對他們的保護方案。正是在這一背景下，研究提出研究社會保障和經濟危機在四中，高收入國家在亞洲：香港，新加坡，馬來西亞和泰國。四個非常相似但顯著不同，使它們優秀的案件進行比較研究。 建議的核心問題研究會地址：什麼是社會影響 2008/09經濟危機？存在什麼樣的社會保障安排，以保障居民的反對呢？怎麼安排的執行中面臨的危機？有哪些因素塑造的安排和他們的表現呢？ 走向理解的社會影響當前的經濟危機，這項研究將收集和分析數據，一個全面的就業，收入，支出，健康和教育指標。為了了解社會保護方案，這項研究將劃定方案的關鍵設計特點並分析其影響，包括他們的時間和情況下成立，領取福利的資格，資金來源和治理。社會安全網所涵蓋的研究包括非供款的方案直接針對窮人或那些容易陷入貧困。為了評估計劃的表現，本研究將探討：公共開支，覆蓋面，貧困為目標，對窮人的影響的收入/支出，入學，醫療保健和利用。最後，該項目將研究社會，政治和經濟因素已形成了社會保護方案和他們的表現，因為這些都是由決策者選擇指導混合物利益，觀念和體制。 該信息需要完成的研究是巨大的。為了迎接挑戰，該項目建議進行調查研究和焦點小組討論，除精梳通過發表政策文件，統計數據和年度報告有關機構。 擬議研究會，建成後，第一次系統評估的社會保障安排在亞洲，其業績在經濟危機。它預計將作出重大貢獻的實證評價和關於社會保障的理論辯論在亞洲。調查結果也將是實際意義，他們將直接涉及改善方案，從而改善人民生活的影響，未來的經濟危機。 (translated from English by www.translate.google.com)

751510.label: Realisation of objectives
751510.value: Objective 1. A thorough review of the secondary literature on the subject and interview with key players in the social protection sector were conducted to ascertain information on the historical evolution of social safety net programs in the four countries. Objective 2. Information on the safety net programs in Hong Kong and Singapore were relatively easy to collect. In contrast, the programs in Malaysia and, especially, Thailand are highly decentralized which made identifying the programs and their features difficult to identify. Although collection of information on the different programs has been completed, follow-up enquiries have been sent to relevant contacts to double-check facts. Objective 3. Data on public expenditures on social protection programs and the population coverage have been compiled. However, other aspects of this component of the proposed research encountered unexpected difficulties. By the time the research started towards the end of 2010, the financial crisis that research proposed to study was already on the wane and the programs that had been announced earlier were never formally implemented and in many instances not even enacted or budgeted. As such, the research has focussed unavoidably on regular social protection programs and their performance in assisting households to cope with decline or interruption in income. Fortunately, population census were conducted in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand in 2010 and in Hong King in 2011. Household income and/or expenditure surveys were also conducted in these countries in the years 2009-11. The data from the surveys have begun to be published and are being analysed to gain insight into the vulnerable population’s behaviour in terms of consumption expenditures, educational enrolment and health care utilization. Objective 4. Comparison of the social safety nets in the four countries have been completed. Census and household expenditures data, which are still in the process of being published, are being analysed to enhance the comparison. Objective 5. Analysis of the different factors that have shaped social protection arrangements in the four countries has been completed. The 2008 financial crisis in Asia occurred in the shadows of the 1997 economic crisis. Drawing on the lessons from the previous crisis, governments responded decisively and promptly. The scope and depth of the response was commensurate with their experience of the previous crisis and the ruling party’s political vulnerability. Social and ideational factors played a relatively small role in shaping the social safety nets. Objective 6. Preliminary conclusions based on the findings of the study have been drawn. Final conclusions will be prepared after research on #3 and # 4 above have been completed.

751510.label: Major findings and research outcome
751510.value: The research set out to understand the social repercussions of the 2008/2009 financial crisis in Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore and Thailand, and the respective governments’ policy responses to the crisis. The research proposal was prepared at the height of the crisis in mid-2009 and it was expected that tracking the crisis and response to it offered unique opportunities for understanding what at the time was billed as the deepest economic crisis since the Great Depression. But by the time the research project launched in late 2010, the crisis in Asia was largely over, limiting opportunity for studying the dynamics of the crisis in real time. Some research components (such as survey of households adversely affected by the crisis) became unviable but, on the other hand, new opportunities for focussed retrospective study became available. Materials collected during the course of the research show that governments in the region continue to be hesitant towards establishing long-term social protection programs that will protect the vulnerable population on a continuing basis. They also continue to rely on fiscal and monetary policy measures targeted at businesses rather than social protection for households. Finally, social protection programs suffer from design flaws that are compounded by lack of adequate household level data. The variations in policies are explained by the particular political and institutional conditions that exist in each country.

751510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
751510.value: The research highlights an opportunity for extending the comparison of social protection programs to other countries in Asia. In fact, China, Indonesia, and Philippines have undertaken significant social policy reforms in recent years that offer immense opportunities for empirical and theoretical research.

751510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
751510.value: The objective of the research was to understand social protection against the adverse effects of economic crisis in Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand. The research found that governments in the region are still reluctant to establish long-term social protection programs despite increase in frequency and intensity of economic crisis and the ensuing social repercussions. Instead, they deal with social effects of economic crisis in an ad hoc and piecemeal basis. There is also a tendency to respond to crisis through fiscal and monetary policy interventions targeted at businesses rather than direct assistance for those affected by the crisis. The social protection programs that do exist suffer from design flaws. Both exclusion and inclusion errors are large in Malaysia and Thailand whereas the strict eligibility criteria for benefits in Singapore contribute to large exclusion errors. Hong Kong has the longest standing social protection programs in the region that are reasonably robust in offering protection to those adversely affected by changes in economic conditions. The variations in policy responses to the crisis are explained by the particular political and institutional conditions that exist in each country.

752010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
752010.value: The human visual system is able to use a wide range of cues to perceive the 3D structure of our environment. These include not only stereoscopic 3D cues, but also pictorial cues like linear perspective. Studying how the visual system integrates multiple sources of 3D information is an active area of current psychological research. Although many depth cues can produce perception of 3D, the amount of depth perceived is often not accurate. For example, the image in figure 1 appears to be a surface slanted in depth because of linear perspective cues. However, the apparent slant of the surface is much less than a geometrically accurate interpretation of the image. Such perceptual biases are the focus of this research. One possible explanation for perceptual underestimation of depth is that the visual system has a prior expectation of uniform depth, which must be counteracted by sensory information to perceive 3D variations. Weak or ambiguous cues would then produce only limited perception of depth. This explanation can be naturally modeled in a Bayesian theoretical framework. Bayesian estimation has been successfully applied to modeling the relative contributions of different 3D cues, use of implicit assumptions about the world, and other aspects of 3D cue integration. A Bayesian model of perceptual underestimation of depth has not yet been fully formulated or rigorously tested. The question of whether a Bayesian model with a uniform depth prior can account for perceptual biases is theoretically important. Bayesian models have recently been criticized for being unable to account for the relationship between perceptual bias and cue reliability, and for unrealistically assuming that sensory estimates are unbiased. This research will test a model of 3D slant perception that combines slant information from sensory cues with a prior that is biased toward uniform depth. The proposed studies will manipulate the reliability of available sensory information, and the strength of the prior assumption, to test whether perceived slant changes in the predicted manner. 人類視覺系統能夠利用多方面的資訊去感知環境的三維結構. 這不單包含體視的三維資訊, 還有圖象資訊, 例如線性透視. 研究視覺系統怎樣將不同來源的三維資料整合是本心理學研究的主要部分. 雖然很多深度資訊可以產生三維感知, 但感知到的深度大小很多時侯並不準確. 例如, 在圖一看到的圖象看似一塊有深度的斜面是因為斜面上有線性透視 的資訊, 但看上去的斜度是遠遠少於準確幾何分析所得到的結果. 這個感知的偏差是本研究的重點. 其中一個低估斜度可能成立的解釋是人類視覺系統對於平面有均一深度的預設期望, 而這個預設一定要被知覺資料抵消去感知三維的變化. 微弱或含混的資訊可能會因而產生有限的深度感知. 這個解釋可以利用貝葉斯理論的架構去模擬. 貝葉斯評估一直被成功利用去模擬不同三維資訊的相對使用性 , 四周環境非明確假設的使用和其他方面的三維資訊整合. 低估感知深度的貝葉斯模型到目前為止並沒有被完全被制定或嚴格地測試. 一個以均一深度作為預設的貝葉斯模型能否解釋感知上的偏差在理論的層面上是重要. 貝葉斯模型近來一直被批評沒能解釋感知偏差和資訊可靠性的關係, 和非現實地假設知覺的評估是沒有偏差. 本研究會測試一個感知三維斜面的模型. 這個模型會結合由知覺資訊來的斜度資料和偏向均一深度的預設. 這個擬議的研究會操控可用的知覺資訊的可靠性和預設的強度, 藉此去測試究竟感知到的斜度會否隨預測的方式而變化.

752010.label: Major findings and research outcome
752010.value: The general goal of the project is to test whether a Bayesian model could account for systematic biases in perception of 3D slant. The key idea was to measure both perceptual biases and perceptual cue weights in conditions with multiple cues. A Bayesian model predicts relationships between these measures, which allows this model to be differentiated from other explanations. The project proposed a main experiment using this paradigm and a number of follow-up experiments that varied either the quality of slant information or the prior expectations. The main experiment has been performed and the results are reported in a manuscript currently under review at Journal of Vision. The results were consistent with a Bayesian model, and inconsistent with some other proposed explanations for perceptual underestimation of slant. This directly addresses Aims 1 and 2. We have also performed follow-up experiments varying texture information and field of view. These manipulations affected both perceptual biases and cue weights in a consistent manner, consistent with a Bayesian model. Two manuscripts reporting these results are currently in preparation. We have not yet performed experiments that varied the prior expectations. The main experiment took longer than anticipated because we had to refine our method. I initially proposed using a 2D gauge figure to assess slant perception. However, we found that this method did not yield sufficiently reliable results, and showed idiosyncratic individual differences. We tested some alternatives, and eventually settled on a 3D hand alignment task, which has produced more consistent and reliable results. This task required using a motion tracking system to record the 3D orientation of the freely moving hand. During the grant period, we performed some additional studies that were not part of the original research proposal. Dr. Young Lee, a postdoc that joined our lab, conducted a set of studies on how different 3D cues facilitate shape discrimination across changes in viewpoint. This is related to the topic of perception biases in 3D perception, but was not one of the specific projects proposed in the grant. This line of research has resulted in two publications, and another manuscript is in preparation. Another related study has looked at perceptual underestimation of depth from motion parallax. This is closely related to Aims 1 and 2, but studying motion as a depth cue rather than stereo or texture. This work has been presented at a conference, and a manuscript is in preparation.

752010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
752010.value: Our results are consistent with a model that combines 3D slant cues with some additional factor or factors that bias perceived slant toward frontal. The current experiments cannot distinguish whether this additional frontal influence is due to conflicting visual cues, such as lack of accommodative gradient, or a general Bayesian prior. These could be distinguished by varying the orientation of the projection surface, which is a natural direction for further research. The original proposal included manipulations of the prior expectations, which remains a promising direction. We were not able to complete these studies during the grant period, but the methods have been developed and we plan to conducting such studies in the future. Another promising direction for further research is perceptual learning. Some previous research has found that the relative weighting of perceptual cues can be adapted from experiment. Our results reveal a relationship between perceptual biases and cue weights, consistent with an underlying Bayesian model of cue integration. One might expect perceptual biases to be adaptable in an analogous manner.

752010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
752010.value: Perception of 3D depth is based on multiple visual cues that must be integrated into a coherent percept. Recent models of depth cue integration have used a framework of Bayesian estimation. A Bayesian model of cue integration predicts that different cues should be "weighted" according to their reliability, which has been confirmed in many previous studies. If sensory cues were integrated with a Bayesian prior, the contribution of the prior would similarly depend on cue reliability. I tested whether such a model could explain the phenomena of perceptual underestimation of depth. Judgments of the 3D slant of surfaces often show large biases toward the frontal plane, particularly when depth information is limited. This might reflect inaccurate interpretation of visual cues. However, an alternative explanation is that cues are accurately processed but too weak to counteract a frontal prior. This Bayesian model predicts a relationship between perceptual bias and the relative weighting of cues, which was tested here. Across multiple experiments, we found that perceptual biases were consistent with reliability of slant cues as predicted by a Bayesian model, and inconsistent with other proposed explanations. These results provide further support for Bayesian models of sensory cue integration.

752710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
752710.value: Building on my past work, in this project I will examine under which conditions killing in self-defence is morally permissible, argue that self-defence (broadly conceived) is the best model for justifying killing in war and then apply my model of self-defence to the much debated question of “the moral (in)equality of combatants”. This question concerns whether the combatants on both the “just” and the unjust side have an equal liberty-right to kill each other. I will try to show, against many recent and past dissenting voices, that in most wars they do. In addition, I will argue that virtually no real war (at least none that comes to my mind) has ever actually been justified. This, however, does not lead me to a pacifist position, since I argue – again against many dissenting voices not only in the present but in past centuries – that participation in an unjust and unjustified war can be justified (no paradox is involved here). Soldiers (and other militants) bear responsibility for their own actions, not for the war (or the militant campaign) as such. 建基於本人早前研究，本文意在審視於何種情況下，自衛殺人為道德所允許；我將先論證在戰爭中要合理殺人，最佳依據為出於（廣義上的）自衛，接著再以我所論述的「自衛」回應一常見議題：「各方參戰者在道德意義上是否平等」。 這關乎參戰者是否不論在「正義」或「不義」一方都有同等自由互相撕殺〔即同樣無義務不殺對方〕。 異於一般反對聲音，我將闡明在大部分戰爭中，他們的確有同等自由互相殺害。 而且，我將論証現實中幾乎沒有一場戰爭能真正稱得上義戰。 雖然如此，這並不等同支持和平主義，因為我認為一個人們可合理地參與一場不公義及不合理的戰爭，而這立場亦非自相矛盾。 軍人（或其他武裝人員）要為自己的行動負責，而非為戰爭（或其他武裝活動）負責。

752710.label: Realisation of objectives
752710.value: The project’s objectives have been completely achieved. In fact, during the runtime of the project I had certain spin offs of the project that while not pertaining to its core still pertained to questions of war more generally speaking. In other words, I overachieved: I did finish the project and already went beyond it. In particular: My forthcoming book (with State University of New York Press) "On the Ethics of Torture" contains a detailed theory of self-defense (incidentally, Stephen Kershnar, an expert on the ethics of torture, has in his review for the publisher said about my book: “The book is the single best discussion of the moral status of torture. It is outstanding.”). Further special issues and problems in the theory of self-defense are dealt with in several published, accepted or submitted articles I have attached here. Three of these articles directly deal with the applicability of self-defense theory to war, and they also cover the further objectives mentioned (as will already be clear from the titles of the articles and papers). One of the articles will appear with two replies by commentators. The spin-offs concern my work on terrorism, guerrillas, mercenaries and of course also the application of self-defense theory to torture.

752710.label: Major findings and research outcome
752710.value: 1. I have developed a comprehensive theory of self-defense. This theory explains the right to self-defense in a way that can deal with the difficult issues of the so-called innocent attacker and of the non-responsible threat, and it deals with these cases in a way that avoids, unlike a number of competing theories, counter-intuitive implications and unmotivated ad-hoc-assumptions. 2. The theory is applicable to the issue of war and to the issue of torture. I have demonstrated that torture can in rare cases be justified under appeal to self-defense; and I have shown that many soldiers in war, even those on the “just” side, become liable to attack because they participate in relevant ways in unjust attacks. Thereby this theory also shows that in many wars there is a certain moral equality of combatants (something that has been denied by a large part of the just war tradition and by many present-day just war theorists); on the other hand, however, I also demonstrate that not all soldiers can be liable to attack under an appeal to self-defense. Thus, I demonstrate both the scope and the limits of self-defense as a justification for killing in war. 3. I have shown that if one takes just war theory seriously, hardly any real war will ever be justified. However, this does not lead me to downright pacifist conclusions, for a) in principle war can sometimes be justified, and b) an individual can often be justified to participate even in an unjustified war, since individual participation in unjustified collective acts is not necessarily unjustified itself, in fact, it can sometimes be commendable. I have thus developed a highly original and sophisticated theory of justified war and of individual combat that takes a mediating and differentiated position between pacifism on the one hand and some over-confident just war theories on the other.

752710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
752710.value: In an earlier book of mine I had pointed out a difference between self-defense and what German law calls justifying defensive emergency. This distinction does not exist in Anglo-Saxon law (it is not the same as the distinction between self-defense and necessity!); however, the moral criteria governing self-defense are not the same as the ones governing justifying emergency. In my further research I will compare the self-defense justification with the justifying emergency justification and other justifications of killing and apply these justifications to war and to killing in war. I will also further deal with the question of terrorism and with humanitarian intervention. I will then publish the articles already produced in the course of this project together with the additional material in a book to be entitled “Self-Defense, War, and Terrorism”; probably with Oxford University Press. I will acknowledge the GRF grant I received in that publication. (I did not do this in the articles because I was not aware that I should do so; once I became aware of it, however, I saw to it that the grant will be acknowledged in my book on torture. Thus, in the end the grant will be acknowledged in TWO BOOKS).

752710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
752710.value: In this project I explain under which conditions killing in self-defense is morally permissible. I then show how, and to which extent, self-defense can work as a justification for war and for killing in war. A particular focus here is on the much debated question of “the moral (in)equality of combatants”. This question concerns whether the combatants on both the “just” and the unjust side of a war have an equal liberty-right to kill each other. I explain, against many dissenting voices, why in most wars they do. Nevertheless, I also show that virtually no real war has ever actually been justified, since the demanding requirements of just war theory are actually difficult to meet. Yet, I further also argue that participation in an unjust and unjustified war can nevertheless be justified (no paradox is involved here). Soldiers (and other militants) bear responsibility for their own actions, not for the war (or the militant campaign) as such. Thus, while my theory is rooted in the just war tradition, it nevertheless takes on a mediating role between this tradition and pacifism and offers an original, more differentiated and more adequate understanding of the ethics of killing and war.

752810.label: Project Objectives
752810.value: This study aims to develop, a multi-dimensional, standardized, comprehensive measurement tool for assessment of media pluralism in Asian countries. The study will produce a composite of indicators known as the Media Pluralism Monitor for Transition Societies. The measurement tool has been developed in Europe under the auspices of the European Union but not necessarily useful in the same form in Asia. The study will generate original data and gather existing data in a systematic and transparent way on media pluralism in Hong Kong and mainland China. The study aims to create a scheme for regular, longitudinal monitoring of the status of media pluralism in Hong Kong and mainland China. Such a scheme should entail sufficient flexibility to reflect nuances and specific features of particular indicators as well as ongoing trends of changes. The study will create opportunities for comparative studies of media pluralism in Asian and mainland China for Asian and global comparative perspectives on media pluralism, comparing Hong Kong and mainland China to other states in the region and the world, including Western democracies as well as transition countries. The project provides policy makers in the area of media, communication, and information society, with systematic data on media pluralism in Hong Kong and mainland China as well as with scientific tools of their analysis and interpretation. The measurement will lay the ground work for further comparative, longitudinal research on media pluralism regarding Hong Kong, China and other Asian countries including a) democratic systems including India or Japan, and b) transition countries including Indonesia, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, and other countries

752810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
752810.value: 媒體多元化監測系統(Media Pluralism Monitor，簡稱MPM)是一套目前最全面的研究工具，以系統性、高透明度及多角度的方式來量度媒體的多元化程度。MPM是透過約五十位來自多個國家的媒體研究人員的合作，以及三位主要研究人員的協調﹝包括本項目的首席研究員及兩位副研究員﹞後得來的成果。MPM包括166項已全面發展和標準化的媒體多元化特定指標及一套使用者指引。本計劃由香港大學的香港及中國媒體專家團隊組成，並與幾位領導MPM發展的專家合作，量度香港和中國的媒體多元化程度。 計劃包括以下的重要科學化革新和長遠影響： - 將MPM首次應用在國際媒體研究上，用以量度香港和中國的媒體多元化； - 以媒體多元化的概念﹝一個廣泛應用於民主體系的概念﹞，應用到中國近期的媒體發展化上﹝媒體的商業化、市場化、地理多樣化及新媒體發展的型式和類別﹞； - 以全面、系統化及高透明度的方式來收集有關香港和中國﹝廣東省和北京市的個案研究﹞媒體多元化的實況。 至於香港，研究員將以系統化及高透明度的方式來整理數據，作為量度香港媒體多元化的指標，從而建立一個持續和長遠的體制來監察香港的媒體多元化情況。與此同時，這計劃亦為政策制訂者提供有關媒體、傳訊及資訊社會等範疇的系統性數據，以及用作分析和闡述的科學化工具。 而在中國的研究，研究員將建造一個適用於轉變型社會的媒體多元化監測系統﹝建基於MPM﹞，以系統化及高透明度方式整理有關廣州及北京的媒體多元化數據，從而建立一個持續和長遠的體制來監察中國的媒體多元化情況，同時提供足夠的靈活來反映細微差別、獨特指標的特徵以及持續的轉變趨勢。 量度亞洲媒體的多元化：中國廣東的個案研究 摘要 媒體多元化監測系統(Media Pluralism Monitor，簡稱MPM)是一套目前最全面的研究工具，以系統性、高透明度及多角度的方式來量度媒體的多元化程度。MPM是透過約五十位來自多個國家的媒體研究人員的合作，以及三位主要研究人員的協調﹝包括本項目的首席研究員及兩位副研究員﹞後得來的成果。MPM包括166項已全面發展和標準化的媒體多元化特定指標及一套使用者指引。 本計劃由香港大學的中國媒體專家團隊組成，並與幾位領導MPM發展的專家合作，量度中國的媒體多元化程度。 計劃包括以下的重要科學化革新和長遠影響： - 將MPM首次應用在媒體研究上，用以量度中國的媒體多元化； - 以媒體多元化的概念﹝一個廣泛應用於民主體系的概念﹞，應用到中國近期的媒體發展化上﹝媒體的商業化、市場化、地理多樣化及新媒體發展的型式和類別﹞； - 以全面、系統化及高透明度的方式來收集有關中國﹝廣東省的個案研究﹞媒體多元化的實況。 在中國的研究，研究員將建造一個適用於轉變型社會的媒體多元化監測系統﹝建基於MPM﹞，以系統化及高透明度方式整理有關廣東省的媒體多元化數據，從而建立一個持續和長遠的體制來監察中國的媒體多元化情況，同時提供足夠的靈活來反映細微差別、獨特指標的特徵以及持續的轉變趨勢。

752810.label: Realisation of objectives
752810.value: The project objectives have been achieved fully achieved in most areas and largely achieved in two areas. The study created a scheme for regular, longitudinal monitoring of the status of media pluralisation in China (Objective 2). Particular indicators with specific features were developed in 6 areas: 1) the basic domain: party control and economic reform in the media sector 2) diversification of media ownership and/or control 3) diversification of media types and genres 4) geographic diversification of the media 5) cultural pluralisation in the media 6) political pluralisation of the media. In all areas of media diversification/pluralisation, historical trends were analyzed and data gathered (Objective 3). Specific papers targeted pluralisation of content in online media (especially weibo) and the differences from traditional media in several content and framing areas (such as the coverage of environmental conflicts, or relatively sensitive public affairs). Access to empirical data in China was limited in some areas due to political sensitivities (e.g., ethnic diversity of media workforce). Conceptual and empirical opportunities were created for comparative studies of media pluralism in Asian countries, global comparative perspectives on media pluralism, comparing China to other states in the region and the world, including Western democracies as well as transition countries (Objective 4). The project outcomes focusing on media and internet policies provided policy makers in the area of media, communication, and information society, with concepts and data on media pluralisation in China as well as with scientific tools of their analysis and interpretation. (Objective 5). Regarding an general Asian media pluralism monitor, the differences between countries with non-democratic vs. non-democratic government presented some challenges (Objective 1). 752810.label: Major findings and research outcome
752810.value: The key finding is that media pluralisation in China results from the dynamic interplay between the party-state, media professionals, and the audience/media users. First, as a result of economic reforms, media organizations engage in increasingly fierce market competition and are given more managerial power. Official media diversification opens up multiple, competitive spaces, including novel, diverse forms of media ownership and managerial control, mushrooming media types, genres and platforms, and leads to tremendous geographic diversification of media in China. As these multiple media spaces become contested by media professionals and audiences/users, the planned, top-down, controlled process of diversification (of media ownership and control; diversification of media types and genres; geographic diversification of media) spills over into unplanned struggles that give a chance to genuine pluralisation of political and cultural content. While diversification remains selective and incomplete, it provides media professionals (media managers, editors, journalists) with space for innovative agency. Media professionals, especially at leading provincial- and municipal level commercial media outlets, manage to offer viable alternatives to the party media, hence widening the spectrum of voices in the Chinese media. Third, both the propaganda-oriented party media and market-oriented commercial media face the challenge of engaging audiences. Audiences put pressure on professionals at both the party and commercial media – that is, it prompts the party media to refine their propaganda skills while stimulating commercial media to offer niche content. Finally, interactive digital media technologies such as micro-blogging and other social media have turned passive audiences into active users. This offered new channels of political and social expression and had an impact on traditional media. The project developed specific indicators to explore and measure media diversification/pluralization in six areas: 1) the basic domain: party control and economic reform in the media sector; 2) diversification of media ownership and/or control; 3) diversification of media types and genres; 4) geographic diversification of the media; 5) cultural pluralisation in the media; 6) political pluralisation of the media. The project also created research tools for sampling political content in online as well as traditional media. The results indicate de facto political pluralisation among different media types: online media is freer, market papers are more controlled and party papers are the most controlled. The project also prove that there exists a degree of political pluralisation in ideological terms (more reform-oriented vs. more official communist vs. more nationalist) among different newspapers in the PRC.

752810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
752810.value: There are potentials for further development of the research in three fields. 1. The project developed conceptual tools and developed indicators to measure media diversification/pluralisation in six areas: 1) party control and economic reform in the media sector 2) diversification of media ownership and/or control 3) diversification of media types and genres 4) geographic diversification of the media 5) cultural pluralisation in the media 6) political pluralisation of the media. There are plenty of opportunities for further empirical work in all areas, including content/framing analysis as well as fieldwork/interviews with media professionals in China. 2. In the area of political pluralisation, the project developed two methodologies that could be utilised in further content and framing analysis of media content: A) quantitative framing analysis could be further used to compare how different media types (e.g., weibo vs. market papers vs. party papers) cover moderately sensitive issues and how their coverage differs. B) the political keyword/slogan method could be further used to show systematic differences of ideological orientation of traditional media in China. 3. International comparative perspectives. Further work on the role of government policies, actors (including media professionals and audiences/users), social-political dynamics and technologies in media pluralisation could be conducted. (In fields 2 and 3, research is still conducted.)

752810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
752810.value: This project examined media change in China in terms of media pluralisation, a concept that had been applied mostly in the context of democratic countries. The project found that the media system in China is becoming more diversified along several lines. The project developed concepts and indicators to explore 1) the media policies of the CCP: how party control and censorship coexist with media competition and economic reform 2) diversification of media ownership and/or control: how some private media ownership become possible and how media managers and editors are becoming more important in decision making 3) diversification of media types and genres: from party newspapers to market papers and magazines, from propaganda to entertainment genres, from traditional to online media like weibo and blogs 4) geographic diversification: how audiences shift from central national media like CCTV to provincial television and radio stations and metropolitan papers, 5) cultural pluralisation: how gender and ethnicity are represented in the media 6) political pluralisation: how moderately sensitive issues are presented differently by weibo vs. market papers vs. party papers, and how some newspapers differ ideologically (some are more reform-oriented, others follow a more official communist line, yet others have a more nationalist orientation).

753010.label: Project Objectives
753010.value: Our first objective is to provide a systematic account of CDO collateral asset management. We would like to derive new insights from the CDO market on delegated portfolio management. There is a large literature from mutual funds and hedge funds, but CDOs could provide a different setting. For example, unlike mutual funds or hedge funds, CDOs are subject to credit ratings. Related, CDO investors resemble debt holders more than equity holders. Further, a CDO manager is responsible for different tranches, which creates an incentive problem. We distinguish several alternative theories. These hypotheses regarding why CDOs select certain collaterals include risk premium, liquidity premium, rating arbitrage, agency conflicts, herding, etc. More than one of these hypotheses are potentially in effect, in which case we will conduct decomposition. We will draw implications from this study of (i) the risk and risk premium of the structured products; (ii) the future design of structured finance products; (iii) the regulation of rating agencies.

753310.label: Project Objectives
753310.value: To conduct a theoretically informed empirical study of Post Cold War Japanese diplomacy in the Middle East and produce four research articles for publication. To understand the different conceptual interpretations of the "normalisation" of Japan and identify the factors impeding and facilitating this process in Japanese foreign policy in general. To delineate the role of the United States and China in Japanese policy in the Middle East. To demarcate any possible divergence of Japanese foreign policy from the US position with regards to Iran and the Arab-Israeli conflict, and the reaction of the United States to this perceived or real (if any) divergence in Japanese policy in the Middle East.

753310.label: Realisation of objectives
753310.value: The objectives of the research project have been largely achieved. The project aimed to produce a theoretically informed empirical study of Post Cold War Japanese diplomacy in the Middle East. The conceptual lens that the project has utilized and focused upon is the idea of “Normalization” and its meanings for both Japanese policy and scholarly community. A large amount of time and effort has been spent on analyzing writings in both English and Japanese on how the scholarly and policy community in Japan and elsewhere thought of and operationalize the various different ideas behind “Normalization”. Beyond this, the project has also tried to find out in what ways (empirically) the “Normalization” of Japan has been carried out militarily, politically, constitutionally and also in terms of the prevailing norms in Japan. The theoretical part of the component has benefitted many of the PI’s other projects and writings, lending to the achieving of the objectives through the series of outputs. Due to the unforeseen circumstances in Middle East politics (the Arab Spring), there were tremendous difficulties faced in terms of travelling to the Middle East. This was due to difficulties in obtaining the visas and travelling logistics for each of the Spring/Summer period that coincided with the fieldwork periods. The governments of Libya, Egypt, Tunisia and Yemen were overthrown with major protests happening in Algeria, Sudan, Iraq, Jordan, Morocco, Bahrain and Oman over three years from 2010 to 2013. During this period, many flights to the region were cancelled. This is completely unforeseen at the time of submitting the proposal. Consequently, the Principal Investigator (the ‘PI’) could not go to the American University in Cairo and Hebrew University in Jerusalem as expected within the timeframe as stipulated in the proposal. In mitigation, the emphasis was shifted to focus on Middle East scholars and policymakers as well as experts who studied the countries concerned based outside of the Middle East such as those in Asia and American Universities such as Stanford, Berkeley, the LSE, Oxford and Capetown University. The PI also travelled to conferences and workshops, some in Islamic Countries (such as Malaysia) in order to speak to scholars and officials from the region. The PI also made four extended research trips to speak to officials and scholars based in Japan, and held numerous discussions with Chinese colleagues in working on the Middle East. This mitigated the difficulties faced by the project to a large extent.

753310.label: Major findings and research outcome
753310.value: In this study, the PI focused on four principal empirical issues, examined through the conceptual notion of “Normalization”, namely Japan’s (i) participation in the International Coalition to Fight Piracy in the Gulf of Aden; (ii) relationship with one of the Pariah of International Relations – the Islamic Republic of Iran (and its principal rival – Saudi Arabia); (iii) role in the Arab-Israeli Peace Process and (iv) Japanese diplomatic efforts in relation to the US and China. The project’s main findings are as follow: the idea of “Normalization” is still a relatively amorphous concept in Japan itself. A majority of the Japanese scholars and policymakers all feel that Japan should actively continue to strive to play a bigger role in international affairs and global security, but nonetheless, most do not have a common idea as to what Japan could possibly do to effect this notion of normalization i.e. even amongst right-wing groups. There exists a spectrum of ideas and beliefs over the question of Constitutional Amendment, the dispatch of troops overseas, and collective defence. Most interlocutors however are of the view that Japan should do all she can in terms of anti-piracy deployments and assist in Middle East Peacekeeping efforts, whilst many are ambivalent over the unconditional support of US military operations in the region. Most Japanese interlocutors perceive the prioritization of Japan’s domestic problems as well as contention with Japan’s neighbors such as China and the Koreas as a priority, thereby drawing Tokyo’s attention away from the Middle East. Conversely, interlocutors from the Middle East however do not perceive Japan as a heavy weight player in regional affairs. This is largely a result of history, but more so because of Japan’s alliance with the United States. Most Middle East countries – ranging from Iran to United States’ allies such as Saudi Arabia and Israel all privilege building better relations with China rather than Japan. . Japan’s alliance with the United States thus weighs heavily on Japanese diplomacy. The Middle East issues, such as Japan’s response to Iran and her eagerness to participate in the Peace process are causing a rethink in Tokyo over Japan’s alliance with the United States. Unfortunately, due to the challenges in the Asia-Pacific and the contentious nature of Japanese politics, there is little political will or clout to redefine how US-Japan alliance could enhance rather than detract Japan’s diplomacy in the Middle East.

753310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
753310.value: Not much has been written on the topic. With the materials collected, the PI feels that a platform for further research would be to take on a comparative approach and consider further in depth Japan’s interaction with other powers in the region. Another tack potential line of enquiry would be to examine Japan’s interactions with the United States and China in other regions. Using this as a framework, the PI has actually made preliminary surveys on the topic. This has resulted in two further research proposals. One such proposal was submitted twice to the Hong Kong RGC, and both times, the proposals were returned with scores of 3.5. The PI intends to pursue the research after the completion of the writing of this project. Additionally, there could be further research done on the tenacity and resilience of the Japan-US Security partnership. This research has identified the stress points of the alliance, and it would be interesting to see how far either Japan and the United States are willing affirm the alliance in the face of diverging interests and competing priorities.

753310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
753310.value: This project is a timely project to understand the evolvement of Japanese domestic political orientation away from Pacifism that Japan is so famous for since the 1950s. The Middle East is an important test case for Japanese diplomacy because as Japan’s aspirations evolve, Japanese policymakers are pushing for greater involvement in global affairs. Yet, even as Japan ventures into the region, the implications of how Japan’s alliance with the United States and her strategic competition with China are becoming clearer. Japan’s diplomacy with states like Saudi Arabia, Iran and Sudan are all indirectly affected by her affinity with the United States. Even though Japan has an urge to become more assertive and to depart from her past policies (e.g. over Iran), Japan is circumscribed by the fact that her primary interests in the Asia-Pacific region is still reliant on the United States. This is only so much Japan can do without offending the United States. China on the other hand does not face such constraints. This research has important implications for how we conceptualise the relationship between powers in global affairs, especially in terms of how we situate the normalization of Japan versus the rise of China.

753510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
753510.value: Although post-traumatic stress disorder and depression have been identified as the two most common consequences of intimate partner violence, research has generally not differentiated the effects of different types of intimate partner violence on victim’s mental health. With intimate partner violence treated as a single phenomenon rather than having different types, abused women are unlikely to receive the most appropriate interventions. Johnson’s typology of control has been used increasingly to classify intimate partner violence based on physical assault and controlling behavior. Two distinct types of the violence, Intimate Terrorism and Situational Couple Violence, have received much attention. The two differ not only in the cause and trajectory of the violence but also in the effects including mental health outcomes. Although control is a critical factor in distinguishing intimate terrorism from situational couple violence, there is no consensus on what constitutes high or low control in physically violent intimate relationships. Partly, this may be due to the sole reliance on quantitative measures to determine the levels of control. By understanding the context in which control tactics are used, qualitatively different phenomena between violent relationships with high control and those with low control may be more apparent. Thus, there is a need to collect both quantitative and qualitative data on the use of controlling behaviors. It has also been hypothesized that intimate terrorism and situational couple violence have different mental health outcomes but few studies have examined this empirically and none has studied women’s experiences of the negative psychological consequences as victims of these two types of violence. The purpose of this study is to extend the extant work on the typology of intimate partner violence by employing mixed methods to collect quantitative and qualitative data. Using a sample of 600 physically abused Chinese women, with 300 from the community setting and 300 from the shelter setting in Hong Kong, we seek to identify intimate terrorism and situational couple violence using the Revised Conflict Tactics Scales and Revised Controlling Behaviors Scale. Post-traumatic stress disorder and depression symptoms are measured using the Impact of Event Scale-Revised and Beck Depression Inventory version II, respectively. Individual interviews will be conducted with 200 of the women (100 from each setting) to explore the context within which controlling behaviors are used and to elicit the women’s experiences of the mental health effects. The findings of this study have the potential to inform practice, theory and policy. 儘管創傷後壓力症及抑鬱症已被確認為親密伴侶暴力行為的兩種最常見後果，但是，研究一般並無分辨不同類型的親密伴侶暴力行為對受害者精神健康所造成的影響。當親密伴侶暴力行為被視為一種單一現象，而並無劃分為不同類別時，被虐婦女難以獲得最合適的治療方式。 Johnson對控制行為的分類已日漸被採納，以根據對身體的虐待及控制的行為，對親密伴侶暴力行為進行分類。其中兩種較明顯的暴力行為 － 蓄意性與觸發性伴侶暴力已受到廣泛關注。這兩種暴力行為不單止在導致暴力行為的原因及軌跡方面有所不同，所造成的結果（包括對精神健康的影響）亦截然不同。雖然控制程度是分辨蓄意性與觸發性伴侶暴力的主要因素，但是有關出現身體暴力的親密關係中，有哪些因素會導致控制程度較高或較低，現時尚未有達成共識。在某程度上，這是由於目前只倚賴量化量度方式來釐定控制水平所致。透過瞭解使用控制手段的背景，控制程度不同高低的暴力關係之間在性質上的不同現象或可更顯而易見。因此，進行分類時需要收集有關作出控制行為的量化及質化數據。 蓄意性與觸發性伴侶暴力亦已被假定導致不同精神健康後果，然而，對這項假設進行實驗的研究少之又少，亦無研究對婦女作為這兩種暴力行為受害人所出現的負面心理影響進行研究。 本研究旨在透過運用混合性方法收集量化及質化數據，擴展現存有關親密關係的分類學工作。透過對香港600名遭受身體虐待的中國女性樣本（當中300個樣本來自社區，另外300個則來自庇護中心）進行分析，我們嘗試利用經修訂衝突處理量表及經修訂控制行為量表，分辨蓄意性與觸發性伴侶暴力。創傷後壓力症及抑鬱症狀分別以事件影響量表 － 修訂版及貝克抑鬱量表第二版量度。本研究將會與200名女性（社區及庇護中心設定各100名）進行個別訪問，以探究有關控制行為被使用的背景，及發掘有關婦女曾出現的精神健康影響。本研究的研究結果可能會為有關醫務工作、理論及政策帶來新資訊。

753510.label: Realisation of objectives
753510.value: The following explains how 100% of the six objectives have been achieved: For Objective #1: By recruiting 600 abused Chinese women from community and shelter settings as planned and assessing (i) whether intimate partner violence (IPV) was accompanied by a pattern of coercive control (based on the Revised Controlling Behaviors Scale, CBS-R) and (ii) whether the woman and/or the intimate partner was/were violent and controlling, the IPV reported was classified into Intimate Terrorism (IT) or Situational Couple Violence (SCV)using Johnson's Typology of Domestic Violence. Specifically, in IT, the partner is violent and controlling but the woman is not. In SCV, the partner is violent but not controlling and the woman is neither violent nor controlling. For Objective #2: Quantitative data on the use of controlling behaviors in physically violent intimate relationships were collected from 600 abused Chinese women using the Chinese version of the CBS-R. Similarly, qualitative data were elicited from 200 of the afore-mentioned 600 women using individual interviews based on open-ended questions covering the use of controlling behaviors and the mental health effects. Audio-taped records of individual interviews were analyzed using content analysis to determine if there was a pattern of coercive control by the woman and/or her partner. Those individuals (women and their partners) with or without a pattern of control were matched with the quantitative CBS-R scores (which were differentiated into “high” or “low” level of control based on a cut-off score) of the same participants. A receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate the accuracy of the cut-off score to identify whether or not the (qualitatively derived) pattern of control was being used. For Objective #3: The Impact of Event Scale – Revised (IES-R) and Beck Depression Inventory version II (BDI-II) were used to assess PTSD and depressive symptoms among the 600 abused Chinese women recruited from community and shelter settings in Hong Kong. For Objective #4: After distinguishing the reported IPV into IT and SCV, independent t-tests were used to differentiate the mental health effects (reported as PTSD and depressive symptoms) between IT and SCV survivors. For Objective #5: Types of IPV and mental health effects of shelter women were compared to those of community-dwelling women using t-test analysis. For Objective #6: The differential mental health effects of IT and SCV as experienced by community-dwelling and shelter women were analyzed.

rows: Among the 600 community-dwelling and shelter Chinese women in this study, we have identified 228 (38%) IT and 356 (59.3%) SCV survivors. A further breakdown of the findings according to community and shelter samples has revealed that 24% and 73.2% of the community sample were IT and SCV survivors respectively whereas 64.4% and 33.2% of the shelter sample were IT and SCV survivors respectively.

A pattern of coercive control was identified through content analysis of the 200 qualitative interviews, with the following characteristics: (i) restricting women's capacity, (ii) restricting her contact with relatives and friends, (iii) monitoring her activities, (iv) trying not to provoke violence from the partner, (v) expressing fear, powerlessness and helplessness, (vi) resisting is futile, (vii) controlling is worse than violence, (viii) adverse impact on women's health, and (ix) possessive partners who believe they have the right to control their "women". In addition, a cut-off score of 1.145 on the CBS-R was found to distinguish between individuals using patterns of coercive control and those who do not based on the ROC curve analysis, with satisfactory correct classification rate (93% (95% CI = 89.3% to 96.7%)) and Kappa value (0.8).

With reference to the PTSD symptoms, the mean total score of the IES-R was 4.10 (SD = 4.04) in the community-dwelling abused women and 6.82 (SD = 3.89) in the shelter women. For the depressive symptoms, the mean total score of the BDI-II was 19.93 (SD = 16.40) in the community-dwelling abused women and 28.07 (SD = 17.97) in the shelter women.

We have found that IT and SCV have differential effects on abused Chinese women’s mental health. For PTSD symptoms, survivors of IT reported significantly higher IES-R scores than SCV survivors (IT mean = 8.19 vs. SCV mean = 2.97; p <.0001). For depressive symptoms, IT survivors were found to have significantly higher BDI-II scores than SCV survivors (IT mean = 34.68 vs. SCV mean = 14.91; p <.0001).

Compared to community-dwelling women, more shelter women were found to be IT survivors (shelter = 64.4% vs. community = 24%) and they also reported significantly higher PTSD symptoms (shelter mean = 6.82 vs. community mean = 4.10; p <.0001) as well as significantly higher depressive symptoms (shelter mean = 28.07 vs. community mean = 19.93; p < .0001).

Regardless of settings, IT survivors reported significantly higher PTSD symptoms as measured by the IES-R (IT mean = 8.19 vs. SCV mean = 2.97; p <.0001) as well as significantly higher depressive symptoms as measured by the BDI-II (IT mean = 34.68 vs. SCV mean = 14.91; p <.0001), compared with SCV survivors. Also, shelter women reported significantly higher PTSD and depressive symptoms than community-dwelling abused women (shelter IES-R mean = 6.82 vs. community IES-R mean = 4.10; p <.0001; shelter BDI-II mean = 28.07 vs. community BDI-II mean = 19.93; p < .0001). Given that there were more IT survivors among shelter women (shelter = 64.4% vs. community = 24%), the higher PTSD and depressive symptoms can be explained.

753510.label: Major findings and research outcome
753510.value: 1. Using a mixed method design to collect quantitative and qualitative data from 600 abused Chinese women from shelter and community settings in Hong Kong, and classifying the reported IPV by (i) whether the violence in an intimate relationship took place in a context of coercive control, and (ii) whether one or both in the relationship was/were violent and controlling, we have found different types of IPV (IT and SCV being the two major types) with each differing in etiology, trajectory and outcomes. Our study is the second reported study on the differential mental health effects of IT and SCV globally (after Johnson & Leone, 2005) and the first for Chinese populations. As there is sparse empirical evidence for the Typology, ahead of the write-up of the final findings, we have already presented our findings as they emerged at different points of the study (9.1, 9.2) and drawn much attention to our project including personal communication from Michael Johnson, the originator of the Typology. 2. The few studies on the classification of IPV into IT and SCV used cluster analysis to dichotomize individuals as either high and low control, with inherent risks of misclassification. In our study, using pairs of qualitative and quantitative data on controlling behaviors, a cut-off mean score of the Chinese CBS-R (i.e. 1.145) was identified to distinguish high and low control and evaluated to have satisfactory ability to identify individuals using a pattern of coercive control. Not only does the cut-off score found in this study provide an extra option for researchers to differentiate between “high” and “low” level of control, it is also much easier to manipulate than cluster analysis in clinical practice and hence the potential for clinical application, as reported in 9.2. 3. The 200 qualitative interviews conducted with abused Chinese women have yielded rich information about the context in which IPV takes place in Chinese intimate relationships and the revelation of a pattern of coercive control, with implications for practice including the development of culturally appropriate interventions. 4. We have developed specific strategies, with pleasing results, for interviewing abused Chinese women from whom we had to elicit private information often considered as taboo subjects. In response to the calls for us to share our strategies for research and practice purposes, we have presented our findings in international conferences (9.3, 9.4).

753510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
753510.value: The differential health effects of IT and SCV, as revealed by Chinese women’s self-reports in this study, provide important information for early detection of those at high risk of health declines and informing the choice of interventions. This is an important development of the Typology of Domestic Violence, from a theoretical framework to clinical application. Further development of the Typology should consider combining self-reports with quantitative indicators of health so that a more comprehensive assessment of IPV survivors’ health status can be made. This is because self-reports may be influenced by the negative affect associated with the traumatic stress of IPV, thus reducing their reliability. Recently, telomere shortening, as a quantitative indicator of health, has been found to be associated with IPV and postulated to be the result of chronic stress. We plan to build on our completed study by comparing telomere length between abused (differentiated into different types based on the Typology) and never abused women. We have already conducted a pilot study and found significantly shorter telomere length in abused Chinese women using a novel molecular cytogenetic technique. We are preparing a proposal for developing the pilot study into a full-scale study.

753510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
753510.value: To investigate the types of violence that occurred in Chinese intimate relationships and the context in which the violence took place, we conducted 200 individual interviews with and administered 600 questionnaires to abused Chinese women recruited from shelter and community settings. By finding a cut-off mean score on the Revised Controlling Behaviors Scale, we have found a valid and easier way to differentiate between “high” and “low” level of control in intimate relationships. This is important for the present and future research as, by assessing whether intimate partner violence (IPV) was accompanied by high or low level of control, we were able to identify different types of IPV with reference to Johnson’s Typology of Domestic Violence. Intimate Terrorism (IT) and Situational Couple Violence (SCV), the two main types found in our study, demonstrated differential effects on survivors’ mental health with significantly higher posttraumatic stress disorder and depressive symptoms reported by IT survivors. Our study provides empirical evidence for Johnson’s Typology as well as moves it from a theoretical framework to clinical application. Specifically, early detection of those at high risk for health declines (IT survivors) can be made and appropriate interventions provided to ameliorate the adverse health effects.

753610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
753610.value: Specific-language-impairment (SLI) is defined as a significant disorder in language development, which affects one’s daily functioning, but not attributable to sensory, intellectual or neuropsychological deficit. Children with SLI make up one of the largest subgroups of students with special educational needs (SEN) in Hong Kong. Without appropriate intervention, SLI may persist into adolescence and lead to long-term literacy difficulties and social rejection, which were found to be associated with societal problems like unemployment and crime commitment. Among the language domains, syntax/grammar has been viewed as a core deficit in these children. Speech-Language-Pathologists (SLPs) often provide intervention on this aspect for them. However, very few intervention efficacy studies could be identified. Without pertinent research evidence, clinical-decision-making in treatment approach selection may be dubious. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of two procedures for syntax intervention, namely the Sentence-Combining (SC) and Narrative-Based (NAR) procedures using a randomized-controlled-trial (RCT) design. These two procedures have been indicated to be effective in previous case reports and expert opinions. By using the rigorous study-design of RCT, this study provides stronger evidence to support clinicians in determining the most effective treatment procedure. To achieve sufficient statistical power to detect the treatment difference, 52 children with SLI will be recruited and randomly assigned to one of the treatment groups. The primary outcome will be measured by the Hong Kong Cantonese Oral Language Assessment Scale (HKCOLAS), a standardized language assessment which provides a comprehensive profile of school children. Language skills ratings by teachers will also be collected via questionnaires. Intention-to-treat analysis will be employed. Pre- and post-treatment scores on the outcomes will be subject to analyses of covariance with the pre-treatment scores as the covariate. Moreover, subgroup analysis based on children’s grammar abilities in the sentential grammar subtest and the syntactic complexity scores in the narrative subtest of HKCOLAS will be conducted using multiple regression analyses. This aims to compare the outcomes of children with different pre-treatment grammar profiles in the two subtests to investigate if children with a specific profile respond better to one procedure than the other. This project will result in strong research evidence that supports clinical-decision-making which can eventually improve the clinical management of children with SLI. Such evidence will assume increasing clinical importance, in view of the rise of evidence-based-practice (EBP) in the field. This project will also give rise to a series of treatment resources that are appropriate for the Chinese population. 特殊語言障礙是語言發展過程中一項值得注意的病癥，它影響人們的日常生活，但並非感官，智力或神經心理方面的缺陷。特殊語言障礙兒童是香港有特殊教育需要的學生中人數最多的群體之一。 如不進行適當的治療，語言障礙會持續影響兒童的青少年階段，并導致長期的讀寫困難和社會性拒絕，這與失業，犯罪等社會問題息息相關。在語言領域，句法或語法被看作是這類孩子所存在的核心缺陷。言語治療師常為他們提供針對這些方面的治療。然而，極少有治療功效方向的研究。缺乏相關研究依據，在治療方法選擇中臨床決策也有待質疑。此項研究旨在評估兩種句法干涉方法的效力，即通過臨床隨機控制試驗的形式進行句子結合及故事敘述。以往的病例報告及專家意見已確認上述兩種方法的有效性。採用嚴格的臨床隨機控制試驗，此項研究可提供更有力的依據幫助治療師確定最有效的治療方案。 為獲得足夠的統計數據以檢測治療差異，本計劃將招募52名語言障礙兒童，並將他們隨機分配到各治療小組。初期結果將以香港兒童口語（粵語）能力量錶為標準進行評估，該量錶為標準語言測試，可提供學童的全面情況。教師對學童的語言能力評定也將通過問卷進行收集。該研究還會採用目的治療分析（意向分析）。治療前後結果評估將進行協方差分析，以治療前的分數為協變量。此外，在香港兒童口語（粵語）能力量錶中的敘述分測試包括句法分測試及合成句子複雜性分測試，基於兒童語法能力的人群分析將以上述測試為基準，進行多元回歸分析。上述分析的目的在於對比治療前語法情況有差異的兒童在兩項分測試中的表現，從而研究具體特定兒童在其中一項測試中的反應是否好於另一項，該計劃將得出強有力的研究依據以支持臨床決策，并最終改善語言障礙兒童的臨床管理。鑒於該領域中實證執業地位的提升，這些依據預期會產生日益增長的臨床重要性。該計劃也會產生一系列適合漢語語障兒童的治療資源。

753610.label: Realisation of objectives
753610.value: The two revised objectives have been achieved. 52 students with language impairment were recruited. We have invited the Speech Therapy Section of the Education Bureau to collaborate in the project and invited three school-based SLPs to participate. Pre-test assessments were carried out in January 2012. Each participant was assessed individually by the research staff using a comprehensive test in the child’s school. All the subtests for each child were carried out according to the order described in the test user’s manual. The whole assessment lasted for about 1 hour and 15 minutes and was divided into two sessions within the same week. Seven of the students did not join the treatment phase while all 52 were followed up. Treatment protocol and materials were developed and provided to school-based SLPs to deliver the treatment. The intervention phase commenced in late January 2012, after the pre-test. Each child received direct and individual treatment delivered by the school-based SLP according to their allocated arm. Eight 35-minute intervention sessions were provided to the participants on a fortnightly basis over a 4-month period. Four syntactic structures were targeted, which were common to both treatment approaches. These included (1) relative clauses in noun phrase expansion, (2) connectives conjoining clauses with different semantic relations, (3) verb phrase modification with prepositional phrases, and (4) embedded clauses in the form of clausal complements. These four syntactic structures were developmentally sensitive to school-age Cantonese-speaking children during their narrative production. Intervention was provided to the children in their schools, and take-home exercises were given to the children in both treatment arms after each session. Post-test was conducted on all 52 students in July 2012.

753610.label: Major findings and research outcome
753610.value: The present study compared the efficacy of NAR and SC intervention approaches in facilitating the acquisition of complex syntax in school-age children with language impairment using a RCT design. Children received 8 sessions of individual therapy with the school SLPs over a period of four months offered by school SLPs according to the protocol. Seven out of 52 children recruited did not join the treatment phase but they were followed up. Both treatment arms appeared to be equally efficacious in facilitating syntactic growth as measured by the standardized grammar subtest and the syntactic complexity measure in the narrative subtest. That there was greater improvement in the two primary syntactic measures than in the indirect measures is evidence for the specificity of the two treatments to syntactic difficulties in school-age children. Post-hoc subgroup analyses were conducted, with children having no treatment being excluded. Similar patterns were observed with reference to the effectiveness of the two treatment approaches. That is, no one approach was more effective than the other. The No-treatment group demonstrated minimal growth in the two primary outcome measures when compared to those who received treatment. The more robust and specific discrepancy in the change of and the effect size of the intervention between the two treatment groups (NAR-R and SC-R) and the No-treatment group provided some evidence that the syntactic growth in the two treatment arms was likely to be an intervention-induced effect. However, it must be cautious that the number of participants in the No-treatment group was only seven. The small sample size may not provide adequate statistical power for significant difference to be detected. The gains observed in the two treatment groups were generally specific to the treatment target, that is, syntax. Some gains were also observed in both treatment arms for expressive vocabulary, which assessed a child’s ability to name single words. Effect sizes, however, indicated that this gain was smaller than that observed for the primary outcome measures, particularly in the case of the SC treatment arm. This simultaneous improvement in the semantic domain was not a priori planned as the treatment was devised with syntax as the primary target. The growth might have been due to the fact that when the children were requested to formulate complex syntactic structures, complex ideas were involved and higher-level vocabulary was used. As a result, changes in the semantic domain might also have been induced. The findings were written in a manuscript, which was still under review in Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research after the first revision. When the manuscript is finally accepted, the paper along with the treatment protocol and materials developed will be shared with SLPs and teachers via the platform of www.hkedcity.net.

753610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
753610.value: This study evaluated the efficacy of Sentence-Combining (SC) and Narrative- Based (NAR) intervention approaches to syntax intervention using a randomizedcontrolled-trial (RCT) design. Fifty-two Cantonese-speaking school-age children with language impairment were assigned randomly to either the SC or the NAR treatment arm. Seven children did not receive treatment as assigned. Intervention in both arms targeted the same complex syntactical structures. The SC group focused on sentence combining training, whereas the NAR group made use of narratives in which the target structures were embedded. Pre-test and post-test performances measured using a standardised language assessment were subjected to mixed effect model ANOVAs. Children in both treatment arms demonstrated significant growth after four months of intervention. The interaction effect between treatment arms and time was not significant, suggesting that both treatment approaches showed similar effects. This study provided evidence to support language intervention in the school years. However, no one approach was shown to be more efficacious than the other. The comparable treatment outcome may indicate that both approaches contain the active ingredients of language intervention, functional tasks, focused input, and specific targets. Future research could examine the effects of a longer treatment period and include the functional outcome measures.

754110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
754110.value: Learning is an important and fundamental process that allows us to respond adaptively to our fast-changing environment. Recent studies in psychology have shown that even adults readily improve their perceptual ability after learning in a wide range of attention specific laboratory tasks, and that this enhancement can last for a long time. This suggests that our neural system is constantly adjusting itself to stimulation in the environment. But we know very little about how this learning unfolds, and how new learning generates and sustains behavior change. This link between attention, learning and behavior change is at the heart of education and is relevant to enhancing the effects of education. In this research, we propose to carry out four experimental studies and develop a computer model to understand the connections between attention, learning, and behavior change. A mathematical model will be developed as a first step in automating these processes so that it will make it possible to more effectively harness learning principles in the process of education. Our proposed research is based upon a discovery made by the PI and colleagues that prolonged learning in a visual search task can alter one’s sensitivity to a targeted color (Tseng, Gobell, & Sperling, 2004). The long-lasting effect suggests there is a structural change in our neural system, and learning transfer within the whole target color category also implies that higher-level categorical learning is involved. We want to utilize our novel paradigm to further investigate the following questions: (1) What is the nature of learning when attention is selective within a specific context? (2) Is this a different kind of learning mechanism from learning in situations in which persistent and intensive attention is not required? (3) What is the most efficient way to establish learning effects in relation to our visual perception? (4) What are the restrictions or prerequisites for generalizing from a learned stimulus to an unlearned one? (5) How can we represent our behavioral observations with a physiologically-plausible computer model? Our research results is a necessary first step in understanding how attention, learning, and behavior change can be enhanced and what is the best environment in which to promote the occurrence and generalization of such learning. Our model will provide a “blueprint” for applications of this new model to virtual computer expert systems, as well as to applications for real world training and education. 學習是一個基本和重要的過程， 使我們能夠有效地回應身邊在迅速變化的環境．最近有心理學研究發現， 一些成年人的知覺能力，在實驗室經過與注意力相關訓練後得到持續提升． 這結果代表我們的神經系統會因應身邊環境的刺激而作出長期性的改進和自我調整． 科學界對於這個學習程序，和它對我們行為上的實際影響了解甚少‧ 專注力，學習，和行為變化的聯繫， 正是教育的核心，並且對於提升現有的教育水平非常重要‧ 在本研究中, 我們將進行4個實驗研究，最終目的在以製造一個用來了解專注力， 學習和行為變化相關聯繫的電腦模型． 我們這項研究是根據以前的一項發現 - 長時間的視覺搜尋訓練， 能夠改變一個人對某些目標顏色的敏感度 (Tseng, Gobell, & Sperling, 2004)．這個效應能持續一段時間，顯示我們的神經系統組織上產生了變化，使得與目標同類別的顏色都受到相同的效應轉移，也暗示這牽涉到關於高階段的類別學習．我們希望透過新穎的實驗方式去進一步探討以下問題：１）當選擇性專注力在一個特定的範圍內, 學習的性質是什麼？ 2) 這種學習機制和其他不需要持久和深入地投放專注力的學習情況,有什麼不同？ 3)建立學習效果與我們的視覺感知最有效的方式是什麼？ 4) 要從一個學到的刺激概括到沒有學到的刺激，到底有什麼限制或先決條件？ 5) 如何利用一個生理可信的電腦模型去代表我們的行為觀察？ 我們的研究結果對於提高專注力， 學習和行為變化的了解踏出重要的第一步‧數據可以使我們更理解哪些環境可以促進和推廣這種學習方式‧ 我們所製造的電腦模型將會為應用虛擬電腦系統提供一個藍圖‧ 而且更加會有助於社會上的培訓和教育‧
