754110.label: Major findings and research outcome
754110.value: The sensitization of a visual feature through learning will provoke a change in its saliency in relative to other visual features. This change can be characterized with psychophysical behavioral measurements, and also a learning model that takes account of previous trials of performance. Our results provide a way to connect our attentional system and learning. Specifically, here are a few key features we have concluded from our studies: 1. Observers’ attention toward a particular visual feature is a pre-requisite to provoke measurable salience change. The saliency does not change if the visual feature is simply presented, but not attended. (Exp 1) 2. The establishment of salience change between competing features is through both sensitization and desensitization. Attentional system simultaneously enhances the features observers learned to attend to and reduces the ones they learned to ignore. Further, there is notable individual difference in which strategy (i.e. enhancing or suppression) to adopt. Overnight sleep is important to see observable change. (Exp 2) 3. Learning is flexible, and it occurs within or between categories. The transfer effect suggests that observers can have flexible representation of how and what to learn. It is likely learning and attention interacts at multiple sites at the same time, and the measuring tool may benefit the reveal of some stages only. (Exp 3) 4. Our implementation of Bayesian sequential learning model is promising, and its output from enters the third-order computation for motion processing. We are able to use it to do trial-by-trial behavioral prediction on an individual basis with satisfactory accountability (Exp 4). In addition, we also observe an unexpected factor (target spatial outlay) to modulate visual search in the process, and extend the learning studies to younger infant population. These two lines, although not the central research topics, can become separate research topics. The main findings are concluded in the following publications: Tseng, C.H. (under review). Learning in visual search: top-down or bottom-up? Evidence from psychophysical studies. Yang, LX and Tseng, C.H. (under revision). Trial-by-trial estimation of visual salience calibration in visual search: an individual approach. Tseng, C.H., & Jingling, L. (2012). Collinearity distractor impairs local visual search. Journal of Vision, 12(9), article 1348. Tseng, C.H., Vidnyánszky, Z., Papathomas T.V., & Sperling, G. (2010) Attention-based long-lasting sensitization and suppression of colors. Vision Research, 50, 416-423. Tseng, C. H., Lam, H. T. (2010). "The Suppression Component of Attentional Selection in Long-term Visual Search Learning". Vision: the Journal of the Vision Society of Japan, 2010

754110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
754110.value: In the course, we also discover visual search learning is heavily modulated by element organization (i.e. perceptual grouping). In particular, background collinear structures heavily affect our detection and discrimination of local elements. This has huge impact on attentional and learning theory development and it could be developed further into the attention/learning model. We also take another developmental approach to examine how younger group of subjects require similar abstract form of learning. We do so by habituation pre-verbal infants to the same fundamental rules in various formats of stimuli. Then we use the eye movement to infer their preference and their learned effect. The developmental approach allows us to conclude that generalized learning is limited by age maturity, and it is heavily impacted by the nature of stimuli types. How the developmental trajectory of learning capacity will provide valuable assets for early education.

754110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
754110.value: Visual search is an integral part of our daily lives, and our experience in selective items modulates how we process relevant information. In this study, we investigated how learning modulated attentional system and proposed possible neural computations to account for the long-term behavioral change. Our results showed that our attention connects to our perceptual system, and if we direct our attention on a particular color continuously, a learning system will be activated and the consequence of learning is our re-interpretation of this attended color. This is similar to the video-game playing experience that players usually become very sensitive to the looked-for targets after prolonged practice. Our experiments use simple and well-designed stimuli which allow us to go beyond the general observation, but quantitatively describe the amount of perceptual change in the system. The learning model we proposes is a good candidate to explain how attention-modulated learning occurs.

754510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
754510.value: This is the first project to interpret the most famous court cases involving controversial novels and their authors from an interdisciplinary perspective; it covers six cases from the Madame Bovary trial in France (1857) to the Ulysses trials in the United States (1920/1933). It will make a contribution to the study of modern fiction, ‘law and literature’ studies, and gender studies. Previous studies of literary trials have either presented them as historical background for contextualising literature (the traditional literary approach) or as stages in the evolution of obscenity law or norms of censorship (the traditional legal approach). This study provides a new, interdisciplinary approach to the trials in two ways. From a theoretical perspective, it interprets the trials as scenes of reading which problematise the disciplinary boundaries between ‘literature’ and ‘law’. From a historicist perspective, it interprets literature as a discourse which contested the normative masculinity of the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, a gender construct which the law sought to uphold. As someone trained in both legal analysis and literary criticism, I aim to combine literary and legal modes of interpretation by posing the following epistemological question: ‘what do the most famous literary trials in Western history tell us about the relationship between literature and the law?’. This study demonstrates that the trials can be read as interdisciplinary encounters which destabilise the boundaries between literary and legal discourses by revealing the themes and tropes which migrate between them. Moreover, the period under examination was one in which the hegemonic middle-class masculine identity inherited from the first half of the nineteenth century came under severe pressure. This study interprets the literary works as representations of deviant sexualities which challenged this identity, and the trials to which they gave rise as the law’s response to this challenge. This project builds on my journal articles on literary trials and on my recently-completed PhD dissertation from the University of Cambridge. It proposes to examine six literary trials in detail: the Madame Bovary trial (1857) and the Charlot s’amuse trial (1884) in France, the Henry Vizetelly trials (1888), the Oscar Wilde trials (1895) and the Well of Loneliness trials (1928) in England, and the Ulysses trials in the United States (1920/1933). The project outcome will be a monograph on the subject. 小說受審之研究，1857至1933年 過去多個著名案例，都涉及具爭議性的小說及其作家，本計劃將會首次以跨學科的角度，去詮譯這些案例，當中包括法國的《包法利夫人》案（1857）、及美國的《尤利西斯》案（1920/1933）等六宗案件。是項研究，對研究現代小說、「法律和文學」研究及兩性研究，都會有所貢獻。 以往研究涉及文學的審訊，往往會將之演譯為語境化文學的歷史背景（傳統文學方式），或者是淫褻法例或規範審查的演化階段（傳統法律方式）。本研究將會由兩個方面，提供全新及跨學科的研究角度。以理論層面來看，這些審訊會被詮釋為一種讀本，令「文學」和「法律」之間的懲處界限，變得難以劃分。從歷史主義的角度來看，這些審訊就會被理解為一種論述文學，對十九至二十世紀初的男子氣慨定義，提出爭議，而這種男子氣慨定義，是獲法律維護的一種性別構建。 本研究將會說明，這些案件可以被理解為跨學科衝突，在揭示案件之間的主旨及比喻之後，文學與法律之間的分界就會被顛覆。此外，審訊這些案件的時期，正值承傳自前十九世紀的那種霸權中產男子氣慨身份，承受著巨大壓力的時期。本研究會將這些文學作品，理解為挑戰霸權中產男子氣慨身份的不正常性別表述，而這些文學作品引發的審訊，就是法律對這項挑戰的回應。 本研究建議詳細審視以下六宗案例：法國的《包法利夫人》案（1857）及《夏洛特的樂趣》（Charlot s’amuse）案（1884）；英國的《亨利韋茨特利》案（1888）、《奧斯卡王爾德》案（1895）及《寂寞之井》案（1928）；美國的《尤利西斯》案（1920/1933）。有關議題會撰寫成專題論文，成為本計劃的結果。

754510.label: Realisation of objectives
754510.value: The objectives outlined above have all been achieved. The GRF project has resulted in a manuscript for a monograph entitled 'Masculinity and the Trials of Modern Fiction'. The manuscript is now under consideration by Cambridge University Press (Objective 1). The study examines a number of literary trials sparked by the publication of novels (in English and French) from the mid-nineteenth to the early-twentieth century. Each chapter approaches the trials as encounters between legal and literary discourses. The chapters cumulatively demonstrate that law and literature, far from being distinct disciplines, repeated each other's tropes and structures of representation during this period (Objective 2). This study provides theoretically-informed and historically-situated close readings of the trial transcripts and judgments to demonstrate the ways in which legal material is underpinned by literary and linguistic structures (Objective 3). Despite its pretensions to disciplinary specificity, the fact that law is a linguistic product means that it shares many properties with literature, a fact which it often disavows in an attempt to maintain a distinct disciplinary identity. In terms of the role of gender, this study shows that notions of obscenity and indecency of the time were defined in relation to normative gender constructions, such that works of fiction which were deemed legally obscene or indecent were often those that presented sexed identities which challenged, problematised or subverted such constructions (Objectives 4 and 5). It concludes that literature, as a forum which enabled alternative identities to be imagined and given form, was often brought to the dock because of the unconventional ideas about gender which it presented to its readers (Objective 6). Finally, the study of the relationship between law, literature and gender presented in this study shows that our current thinking about accepted, and acceptable, forms of masculinity can be traced to the middle of the nineteenth-century, when notions of bourgeois domesticity were consolidated. This study therefore informs our current understanding of licit and illicit masculine behaviour in literary and cultural production (Objective 7).

754510.label: Major findings and research outcome
754510.value: The major findings are as follows: 1) From the middle of the nineteenth century to the first decades of the twentieth century, the confrontation between 'law' and 'literature' in the courtroom revealed the two discourses to be intertwined. Literature and the law repeated each other's tropes and structures of representation, such that the law encapsulated the very problems in the literary texts which it sought to condemn. 2) The censorship and repression of fiction in this period were tied to conceptions of middle-class masculinity. Specifically, literary works which presented sexed identities that challenged, problematized or subverted normative masculinity were often the subject of legal censure. 3) Literature, as a form of writing which provided a forum for the imagination and creation of alternative identities, often gave rise to obscenity trials through which the government sought to curb the dissemination of ideas about such identities. In turn, the trials ironically helped to cement the status of these works as part of the literary canon. 4) Our current thinking about masculinity, with its still prevalent assumption that 'proper' men should form their own families, become fathers, and provide for their household, can be traced to the middle of the nineteenth-century. A study of the formation and transformation of ideologies about male identity and the family at that time can therefore shed light on twenty-first conceptions of sexed identity.

754510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
754510.value: The manuscript which is the product of the GRF project is currently under consideration by Cambridge University Press. The study's focus on the inter-relationship between law, literature and masculinity, as revealed by the literary trials it discusses, can be extended further into the twentieth century to include later literary-legal events such as the Lady Chatterley's Lover trial. The Principal Investigator is contemplating a further GRF application for extending the study to the remaining decades of the twentieth century.

754510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
754510.value: This project examines a number of literary trials from the middle of the nineteenth century to the first decades of the twentieth century. It approaches these trials as moments of encounter between 'law' and 'literature', a scene of reading in which the boundaries between the two disciplines can be reconfigured and reconceptualized. Specifically, this study shows that literary and legal discourses repeated each other's modes of representation during this period, and that the law often embodied the very problems of representation which it purported to condemn in its literary counterpart. This study further examines the centrality of gender to the confrontation between literature and law. It argues that literary works often came under legal censure because it posited constructions of sexed identity which challenged or interrogated the dominant conception of masculinity. A study of the ways in which different masculinities were problematized and defended can shed light on the ways in which we think about what it means to be a man in our own time.

754910.label: Project Title(Chinese)
754910.value: 從僧侶與商人的流動性看越洋世界的構成 ─ 佛學傳教者在亞洲海域 (約由1650年至1750年)

754910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
754910.value: During the seventeenth century, Chan Buddhist masters from South China led missions to Asian seaports, where they built temples. Religious revival, commercial revolution, weak states, and maritime conflict in the sixteenth and seventeenth century helped to motivate this expansion. The agency for this expansion came from an unlikely cast of monks, patrons, and lay followers that included sea merchants, literati, officials, and overlords—some Chinese, some not. Together, this inter-patronage surrounding these missionary communities anchored a key institutional pillar that stabilized a new kind of transoceanic Chinese society across the maritime sphere. Yet, missions migrated into host societies, too, whenever elite patronage provided opportunity. This expanded circulation of people, objects, ideas, and influences integrated earthbound societies into a dynamic, multi-ethnic region centered in the social ecology of the sea. Conventional models have long misunderstood this phenomenon. They reinforce a state-centered, landlubber perspective that perceives ocean as lacking the kind of geographical definition that influences human movement. This reinforces perceptions of Asia that stress categorical difference over relational connectivity. Regions become inert, bounded constructs, leaving the “Overseas Chinese” a static network marginal to China and other societies. The interactive, cosmopolitan societies that fostered this missionary phenomenon are overlooked. The significance of the sea is lost. This project will explore a missing and important moment of complex network expansion, the transoceanic society it created, and the maritime region that grew from it. It will focus on the period of most intense temple-building activity in the late seventeenth century, and the interactions of the resulting monastic networks that facilitated interactions within the maritime region I have reconstructed. I will trace missions from monastic centers in southern China to Chinese enclaves overseas. This study ends by analyzing the effect of this expanded religious circulation on overseas Chinese, host societies, and the places in China where these missions began, to understand their contribution to the development of an integrated maritime region. My data will be primarily archival, but also rely on visits to temples created by these monks, to collect data from inscribed artifacts such as inscriptions and bronzes. By highlighting a fluid maritime space, with such culturally and politically ambiguous characters, this study hopes to contribute to the conceptualization of an intra-Asian region, made possible by an intertwining of economic, political, and religious networks. By doing this, I hope to challenge analytical frameworks that had been very conventionally land-based and state centered. 早於17世紀，南中國的禪宗佛教大師帶領傳教團進入亞洲海港興建佛寺。16至17世紀，宗教復興、商業改革、弱勢國家 及海事糾紛等問題，促使了這方面的擴展。促成這局面的亦包括不太起眼的僧侶、贊助人和一羣追隨者，當中不乏海上商人、文人、政府官員和土豪劣紳等。他們有部分是中國人，有些則不是。這班圍繞著傳教社區的跨界別贊助者，不僅扎根成為機構的重要支柱，亦穩定了跨越海事范圍的新越洋中國社會。然而，有權勢的贊助者提供機會，傳教者相繼遷移至主要社羣。愈來愈多流轉的人、物與意念，促使俗世社會演變成一個富動力的多種族地域，位於社會生態海洋的中心。 傳統模式令我們長期誤解此現象。他們既加強了一個以國家為中心和不懂航海，視海洋為缺乏某種地理定義而影響人類活動的視野，同時亦加強了在連接關系之上，強調類別分野的亞洲視野。地域之間因建立了界限而變得停滯不前，令「海外華人」成為僅次於中國和其它社會的靜態網絡。這個互動和多元文化的社會，令這個傳教現象被忽略，海洋的重要性亦消失。 是次的研究計劃，會探索一個在復雜擴展網絡中而被忽視的重要時刻﹔亦會探索越洋社會的形成和隨著成長的海事領域。此外，計劃會集中分析於17世紀末繁盛的寺廟興建活動，與及由筆者重構，促進海事領域的僧侶網絡。與此同時，筆者會追蹤位於南中國傳教中心在中國以外的一些傳教活動。是次的研究，會分析海外華人在擴展中的宗教流傳影響下、主要社會及傳教活動在中國開始的地方的作結，從而加深對綜合海事領域發展的了解。筆者的資料主要以檔案為主，但亦會透過考察由這些僧侶所創造的寺廟、附有雕刻的文物、碑文和銅器等收集相關資料。 通過強調流暢的海事空間，包含文代和政治上的模糊角色﹔透過互相依存的經濟、政治和宗教網絡，是次研究旨在概念化跨亞洲地域 。為了達到研究目的，本人希望突破以傳統地域和國家為中心的分析框架。

755110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
755110.value: In the United States, about 40% of five-year-old children with specific language impairment (SLI) subsequently demonstrates reading disabilities (RD) at school age. This percentage is much higher than the overall prevalence of RD of 10% to 18%. SLI is a pervasive impairment of oral language, affecting vocabulary, grammar, and discourse. Reading builds on oral language skills, and therefore children with SLI are at high risk for RD. To date, research on the connections between SLI and RD has focused primarily on alphabetic languages, despite the enormous number of children worldwide learning to speak and read Chinese—a non-alphabetic language. RD refers to deficits in word reading (dyslexia) and/or reading comprehension. Our on-going longitudinal RGC-funded project was the first to test five-year-old kindergarten (K3) Cantonese-Chinese children with SLI for dyslexia subsequently in Primary 1 (P1). To predict dyslexia in P1, we tested the children on reading-related cognitive skills that are important across languages (e.g., phonological processing, rapid automatic naming) as well as those that are manifested differently in Chinese (e.g., morphological awareness and orthographic processing). In this proposed project, we aim to extend our on-going work and ask how well K3 and P1 oral language, word reading, and cognitive skills predict reading comprehension in P3 children with and without SLI. We also ask whether P3 verbal working memory improves the prediction. Evidence from children learning alphabetic languages suggests that vocabulary, grammar and discourse are more important than phonological processing for reading comprehension. Little is known about how different oral language and cognitive skills may be related to reading comprehension in Cantonese-Chinese children. Our proposed project will fill this major research gap. At P3, we will test our current longitudinal sample of children on reading comprehension, verbal working memory, word reading and oral language. Our other research questions are: 1) are children with SLI more likely to have reading comprehension deficits in P3? 2) how are oral language, word reading and verbal working memory associated with reading comprehension at P3? 3) how do children with and without comprehension deficits differ in oral language, word reading and cognitive skills? The findings can potentially help 1) predict word reading and reading comprehension outcomes as early as kindergarten in children with SLI and 2) inform the design of effective and proactive interventions and bring about changes that can help minimize the long-term negative impact of language and reading difficulties for children in Hong Kong.

755110.label: Realisation of objectives
755110.value: Children who struggle with sounding out the words when reading (children with dyslexia) have problems understanding written text. So do children who have problems with speaking and understanding oral language (children with specific language impairment (SLI)). In the research literature on children with poor comprehension (poor comprehenders), children with dyslexia were often excluded. Many poor comprehenders were found to have problems with oral language and some met criteria for specific language impairment (SLI). Little is known about reading comprehension difficulties in children with dyslexia and how their underlying deficits are the same or different from children with SLI. This study is a longitudinal follow up of an earlier GRF-funded project. 125 children were first recruited at the final year of kindergarten and 94 children returned at Grade 2 for this study. Twelve children were excluded as they did not maintain their language status as being SLI or normal language. The 82 children fell into four groups: the normal language group (n=34), the dyslexia group (N = 8), the SLI group (n = 18) and the comorbid SLI-dyslexia (N= 22) group. Data were collected to address the three objectives. There were two outputs, a conference presentation in July 2014 and a manuscript submitted. These two outputs examined how the groups, the SLI and the Dyslexia group in particular, differed from the normal group on reading comprehension, working memory, comprehension monitoring, inferencing and word reading. We are now examining the data again to address issues about how kindergarten oral language and word reading abilities can predict reading comprehension at Grade 2.

755110.label: Major findings and research outcome
755110.value: The SLI-only, the Dyslexia-only and the SLI-Dyslexia group performed worse than the Normal group in reading comprehension. The SLI-only and the Dyslexia-only group showed a different profile of deficits in skills associated with reading comprehension. The SLI-only group performed worse than the normal group in comprehension monitoring, inference making, working memory, while the Dyslexia-only group was only weak in comprehension monitoring. Both groups also scored lower than the normal group on written Chinese grammar. These findings suggest different intervention approaches for the remediation of reading comprehension difficulties in children with SLI and children with dyslexia.

755110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
755110.value: Given the different underlying deficits, the approach to intervention to the two groups of children should be different. For the children with SLI, it will be important to structure the reading task in order to lighten their working memory load, for example first through identifying the challenging words and phrases before reading the text. For children with dyslexia, it will be good to use prompt question to heighten their awareness of the need to integrate information in a situation model and identify inconsistencies. A follow up study is being done to examine if comic illustrations can facilitate reading comprehension in the children with dyslexia and children with SLI.

755110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
755110.value: Reading is important for academic success. The ability to comprehend written text gives students access to knowledge. Reading comprehension is a complex task as it requires the integration of meaning from different sources, the ability to infer meanings from information provided, and to keep information in working memory when these processes take place. Children with dyslexia and children with oral language difficulties, particularly those with specific language impairment (SLI) are at risk for reading comprehension difficulties. The underlying causes of their difficulties were different, however. Obviously the difficulty with the children with dyslexia was word reading. In addition, they also have problems with monitoring the success or problems in reading comprehension. The SLI group showed more pervasive difficulties with problems in both comprehension monitoring and inferencing. Inferencing refers to the ability to infer new meanings from what is written explicitly. The different deficits suggest different intervention goals and foci for the children with dyslexia and children with SLI.

755210.label: Project Title(Chinese)
755210.value: 逆向選擇與房地產市場流動性

755210.label: Co - Investigator(s)
755210.value: Prof Chau, Kwong Wing Dr Yiu, Chung-yim Edward

755210.label: Project Objectives
755210.value: To explain real estate liquidity by the theory of adverse selection To test the explanation using second-hand real estate transactions
rows: To explain real estate liquidity by the theory of adverse selection
To test the explanation using second-hand real estate transactions

755210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
755210.value: George Akerlof, a Nobel laureate in 2001, shows that when used car sellers know more than buyers about the car quality, an adverse selection of low quality cars would occur. Yet, second-hand real estate is actively traded (e.g. in Hong Kong), apparently contradicting his prediction. This study aims to extend Akerlof’s insight to explain real estate liquidity and test several new implications using second-hand housing transactions. Our idea is to treat information on real estate quality as partly symmetric and partly asymmetric. In Hong Kong, for instance, while information on building defects (e.g. water seepage and blocked drains) could be highly asymmetric between buyers and sellers, land attributes (e.g. land use and the surrounding environment) is generally much more symmetric. The symmetric part, as we argue, would provide a natural counteracting force against adverse selection. Three hypotheses related to real estate liquidity are proposed: 1) real estate liquidity depends on the relative importance of land and building value; 2) real estate price and trading volume bear a positive relationship; and 3) the positive relationship is weakened for real estate with relatively high land value. These hypotheses will be tested with panel data from the second-hand housing market. Some data are not readily available and have to be compiled from district-level price indices and location price gradients. This study is the first application of Akerlof’s (1970) idea in the real estate market. It offers a new explanation for spatial variations in real estate liquidity, as well as for the price-volume relationship commonly found in the real estate literature. Practically, a better understanding of real estate liquidity across districts allows better management of investment risk, particularly with regard to geographic diversification. 2001年的諾貝爾得獎者喬治•阿克洛夫提出，如果二手車銷售者比購買者更清楚汽車的品質，就會出現低品質汽車的逆向選擇。然而，二手房的交易仍能很活躍（例如香港市場），此現象似乎並不符合阿克洛夫的預測。 本研究旨在通過拓展阿克洛夫的見解來解釋房地產市場流動性，並用二手房交易實例來驗證一些新的推斷。二手房品質的信息可看作部份對稱及部份不對稱。例如，在香港，購房者與售房者之間有可能對樓宇缺損（例如漏水及排水堵塞）方面的信息高度不對稱，而對土地屬性（例如土地用途及周邊環境）的信息一般會比較對稱。本研究認為對稱的部份會對逆向選擇產生一種自然的反作用力，並提出三個關於房地產市場流動性的假說：1）房地產市場流動性取決於土地價值與建築價值的相對重要性；2）房價及成交量呈正向關係；3）房地產的相對土地價值愈高，這種正向關係愈小。這些假說將用二手房市場的追蹤數據來驗證，當中需估算出各區的樓價指數和地價梯度。 本研究是阿克洛夫理念在房地產市場的一次應用，為房地產流動性的地區差異提供了一種新的解釋，亦為文獻中經常提及的價格-成交量關係提供了一種新見解。在實踐方面，加深對房地產市場流動性的瞭解，有助於更有效地管理投資風險，尤其對於在不同地域的房地產投资項目。

755210.label: Realisation of objectives
755210.value: The first objective has been achieved by 1) a comprehensive review of the literature on adverse selection and liquidity and 2) developing a theoretical information model with testable implications on the relationship between liquidity and the land-to-structure value ratio. The second objective has been achieved by 1) background research on the asymmetric information problems in trading second-hand real estate in Hong Kong and 2) testing the theory empirically by using new district-level data in Hong Kong. The new data came from a set of repeat-sales property price indices constructed specifically for this project.

755210.label: Major findings and research outcome
755210.value: Four testable implications were generated from the theory, and they are all empirically confirmed using data from Hong Kong’s housing market. Specifically, based on housing transactions from 1992 to 2008 across 50 districts in Hong Kong, the research finds that: 1) the liquidity of real estate increases with the share of its land value; 2) there is a positive relationship between real estate prices and turnover rates when land supply is more inelastic than the supply of structures; 3) the positive relationship is stronger when the land value component gets smaller; and 4) while the availability of first-hand real estate may divert demand away from the second-hand market, such a substitution effect is weaker when the land value component is large. The findings have been reported in our paper published in Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics.

755210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
755210.value: There is a potential to further develop the theory proposed in this research to explain the financing decisions (e.g. listing locations) of real estate companies. We are working on this and will apply for another research grant or write another paper when the idea is more fully developed.

755210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
755210.value: This research is an innovative application of Akerlof’s (1970) prize-winning lemon theory in the real estate market. By allowing product quality information to be partly symmetric and partly asymmetric, cross-sectional variations in real estate liquidity, as well as the price-volume relationship commonly found in the real estate literature, are jointly explained. The results reveal the importance of the land-to-structure value ratio in real estate investment, especially for investors with a great concern on liquidity.

755910.label: Project Objectives
755910.value: Study how a type of inter-agent interaction affects the equilibrium efforts and contracts. Study how a type of inter-agent interaction affects the welfare and how this effect varies with important exogenous parameters. Study the implications of contract forms (linear or non-linear) in this setting. Study the implication of the restriction that one principal can only contract with a subset of the agents whose actions affect this principal's payoff. Study the incentive of disclosing or hiding the incentive contracts between a principal and her agent when inter-agent interaction is possible.

Study how a type of inter-agent interaction affects the welfare and how this effect varies with important exogenous parameters.
Study the implications of contract forms (linear or non-linear) in this setting.
Study the implication of the restriction that one principal can only contract with a subset of the agents whose actions affect this principal's payoff.

755910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
755910.value: This is an applied microeconomic theory project, mostly related to organizational economics and contract theory. Often an agent is hired to create a suitable outcome for a principal. For example, a headhunter is hired to find potential candidates for a company and a talent agent is hired to look for suitable opportunities for an artist. Since the suitability of the outcome is not completely determined by the agent's effort and different principals have different characteristics, the agents have incentive to get together and potentially exchange their outcomes to create better fits with their respective principals if their pay depends on the suitability of the outcome delivered. In the process, the agents share commissions with each other. In such a setting, it is interesting to understand the effect of the inter-agent interaction. Particularly, I want to know how it influences the equilibrium efforts exerted by the agents and the incentive contracts offered by the principals. Therefore, the main benchmark here is the case when inter-agent interaction is not allowed. I also use the first-best contracts with trading allowed as a secondary benchmark to better understand the results. Preliminary research has shown that the inter-agent interaction introduces a public-good-provision (or free-rider) problem among the principals as each wants to keep a bigger share of the surplus from inter-agent trading. This effect pushes down the equilibrium piece-rate when only linear contract is considered. However, depending on the form of the effort (whether it is an "un-targeted" effort that increases the vertical quality valued by both principals or it is a "targeted" effort that increases the fit with only one principal), there can be other countervailing effects. For example, a principal would also want to increase the piece-rate of a linear contract to reduce the targeted effort of the non-contracted agents so that other agents' outcomes are also potentially good for her. I also want to investigate the welfare implication of allowing such inter-agent interaction, which is not ex ante obvious. Allowing interaction increases the chance of a good fit, which is welfare-improving, but at the same time causes contracts to be less-powered, which can be welfare-improving or -decreasing depending on the type of effort. Further research is also needed to ascertain the optimality of linear contracts among general form contracts under inter-agent interaction, even though linear contract is known to be optimal in this setting if interaction is not allowed.

755910.label: Realisation of objectives
755910.value: The "type of inter-agent interaction" in Objective 1 and 2 refers to an ex post trading of the outcomes of the agents' efforts to improve the matching of outcomes to principals. Objective 1 and 2 are achieved by comparing to a benchmark where trading is not allowed. Objective 4 is dealt with in section 6.1 of the paper by comparing to a benchmark where the principals can contract with two agents. Objective 5 was dealt with in earlier versions of the paper, but since the answer is simple and does not add much value, it is omitted in the newest version. (When the contract is hidden, the "cross-motivating incentive" is absent.) Objective 3 was not accomplished due to the complicity of the model, but the restriction to linear contract is widely accepted in the literature.

755910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
755910.value: When one person hires another to perform a task by designing an incentive contract, the former is called a principal and the latter is called an agent. This paper studies the externality that arrives between principals when their agents can engage in trading of the outcomes of their efforts (after they have exerted efforts) to improve the matching of outcomes to principals. It shows that each principal has an incentive to use her contract with her own agent to reduce the transfers to the outside agent with whom a principal does not directly contract. This causes each principal to offer an inefficiently low piece-rate (commission rate) that is also lower than that in a benchmark where trading is not allowed. Even though trading reduces an agent's effort and increases his outside option, a principal still gains from allowing trading because of the better match of outcomes to tastes.

756910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
756910.value: This research project puts emphasis on the history of Ci-Fu （辭賦）, a special Chinese literary style with rhythm, in the Tang Dynasty (618–906). A candidate must write a Fu （賦） to pass the imperial officials’ examination in the Tang Dynasty. In order to obtain profound understanding of the Tang Dynasty, we have to study Ci-Fu. The main aim of the research is to evaluate the status of Ci-Fu in the Tang Dynasty and the value of Ci-Fu in classical Chinese literature. Based on an exploration of the development and function of Ci-Fu, this research will be organized to conduct a comprehensive study and a systematic analysis in order to reveal the objective developmental rules of Ci-Fu and the mutual relationship between Ci-Fu and the officials’ examination in the Tang Dynasty. The interpretation and demonstration of the research will be grounded firmly in describing the developmental track of Ci-Fu in the Tang Dynasty to achieve the research goal with a comprehensive consideration of the politics, ideology, culture and art in the Tang Dynasty. This project has various academic values. It would not only enrich and renew the literary history of the Tang Dynasty but also serve as a reference for contemporary officials’ examination. 唐代辭賦通史研究計劃簡介 唐代辭賦與唐詩同樣發達，傳世作品尚存1500篇以上，但到目前爲止，國內外尚未出現一部獨立的唐代辭賦通史性質的專著，這與唐代辭賦自身的歷史存在狀況和學術研究價值是不相稱的。 本研究計畫以唐代（618—711）辭賦作品與理論爲研究對象，以撰寫《唐代辭賦通史》爲基本目標，立足于唐代辭賦之發展軌跡的描繪，包括該文體的創作實踐和理論批評，通過政治、思想、文化、藝術等各方面的綜合觀照，展開系統的分析論證，揭示唐代辭賦發展的基本規律，論定其在文學史上真正的地位和價值。 研究中需要解決的核心問題主要有以下幾點： 1、研究唐代辭賦所處的思想文化背景，特別注意古、今賦體演化過程中轉折階段的政治、經濟、文化狀況，將研究對象置入唐代儒、釋、道思想文化語境下，顯現其發展變化中蘊藏的特殊規律。 2、考察和探究有唐一代辭賦創作在各個發展階段的不同面貌，分析不同賦體形成的原因，在此基礎之上，把握唐代辭賦發展的真正脈動。根據唐代辭賦的創作實際，努力將零落雜散的賦家賦作的個體研究整合爲有規模的、有層次的整體研究。 3、唐代律賦是用於科舉考試的文體，在前期與中期，它與科舉考試緊密結合；在後期，它與科舉考試有所偏離。本研究將對律賦與唐朝科舉制度之間的關係作仔細地考察與梳理，嘗試揭示其對後代公務員考試的啟迪作用。 4、本研究將依據各賦體自身的藝術特徵，從結構、句式、聲韻等方面設立考察標準——賦體因數，細化統計相關數據，依此討論各種賦體在唐代的演進情況嗎，並儘量嘗試將辭賦與西方某些文類作比較文學研究。 5、辭賦創作和批評理論之間存在著相互影響與促進的關係，本研究將對唐代辭賦理論作全面的闡釋，並揭示創作與理論的互動。並將辭賦與其他文學樣式如詩、文、小說的發展聯繫起來，揭示其間的互動關係。 6、本研究將就唐代的賦對宋代以後的賦創作的影響作出切實的分析。 本研究計畫是對唐代辭賦史的綜合性宏觀研究，可以彌補當前文學史研究中還未有唐代辭賦通史的缺憾，在對各種賦體演變規律可作出科學性的總結的同時，完善對律賦與科舉考試關係的理性認識，對唐代文學史的架構更新作出有益的補充，為當代辭賦創作提供精緻的範本。

In today’s China, the current administrative servant examination system learns a lot from western countries. It’s necessary for authorities in China to learn from both western advanced systems and valuable civilization in ancient China, in particular, the regulations of imperial examination in Tang dynasty. It is the idea of making the past serve the present which highlights this project.

757810.label: Project Title(Chinese)
757810.value: 信任与合约在中国角色的演变：对外方采购商和本地供应商交易的长期研究

757810.label: Project Objectives
757810.value: To understand whether foreign firms rely more on trust or contracts in response to exchange hazards in their transactions with local suppliers in China as the market develops. To investigate the evolving role of trust and contracts on exchange performance over time. To examine how legal and cultural institutions moderate the formation and performance implications of trust/contracts. To provide important managerial implications for multinational companies, including Hong Kong firms, to understand how to use trust and contracts to safeguard exchange hazards and achieve better performance in China.

To investigate the evolving role of trust and contracts on exchange performance over time.
To examine how legal and cultural institutions moderate the formation and performance implications of trust/contracts.

To provide important managerial implications for multinational companies, including Hong Kong firms, to understand how to use trust and contracts to safeguard exchange hazards and achieve better performance in China.

757810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
757810.value: During China’s transition towards a market economy, the unprecedented changes that have occurred in its social, legal, and economic institutions pose serious strategic concerns for enterprises operating there. As foreign companies increasingly invest in the Chinese emerging market and outsource from local suppliers, a particular challenge is how to overcome potentially deleterious exchange hazards and achieve superior performance. The conventional wisdom is that firms must build informal relationships with their business partners, such as trust or guanxi, to substitute for institutional voids and coordinate transactions. However, the market-efficiency logic of new institutional economics suggests that as the transition towards a market economy progresses, the role of informal mechanisms, such as trust, will decline, whereas the role of formal governance, such as contracts, will increase. Despite this significant debate, no study has taken a comparative governance approach to examine the roles of trust and contracts over time, leaving this question of strategic choice largely unexplored. Central to the debate is whether the role of trust or contracts decline or increase over time. However, the extant literature has mainly taken a cross-sectional design, which prevents theoretical completeness and limits understanding of the dynamic roles of alternative strategic choices. In this study, we employ a longitudinal study to investigate the role of trust and contracts in foreign buyer-local supplier relationships in China, with four specific research questions: (1) How do foreign firms respond to exchange hazards in their relationships with local suppliers in China as the market develops, building a strong level of trust or signing a detailed contract? (2) What are the effects of trust and contracts on exchange performance over time? (3) How does the development of legal institutions moderate the formation and performance implications of trust and contracts? (4) How does the cultural distance moderate the formation and performance implications of trust and contracts? By addressing these questions, our results will not only enrich the literature on strategic choices in emerging economies, but will also provide important managerial implications for companies to understand how to safeguard exchange hazards and achieve better performance in China. 在中国市场化的进程中，巨大的制度性变化对企业运营产生极大挑战。对外方采购商而言，怎样应对与本地供应商的交易风险尤其重要。传统观点认为公司必须与本地供应商建立信任等非正式关系，而新制度经济学建议在市场化的进程中，信任的作用将会减弱，正式合约的作用将会增强。 在这些不同观点中的核心问题是：在市场化的进程中，信任与合同的角色是增强还是减弱？在这个项目里，我们将采用长期研究的方法来分析信任与合同在中国角色的演变。具体的四个问题是： 1． 在中国市场化的进程中，外方采购商如何去应对与本地供应商的交易风险？是建立更强的信任关系，还是签订更详尽的合约？ 2． 随着时间的变化，信任和合约对交易绩效的影响有何变化？ 3． 法律制度的变化对信任和合约的形成和绩效有何影响？ 4． 中外的文化差异对信任和合约的形成和绩效有何影响？

757810.label: Major findings and research outcome
757810.value: Major findings: 1) When facing exchange hazards, companies in China draft detailed contracts with their suppliers. 757810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
757810.value: This project advances a framework to study the effects of trust and contracts in China. In particular, we have the following major findings: 1) When facing exchange hazards, companies in China draft detailed contracts with their suppliers. Moreover, perceived fairness mediates the effects of contracting on exchange performance. 2) Trust has a decreasing yet contracting has an increasing effect on exchange performance over time. 3) The development of legal system significantly affects the efficacy of trust and contracts on exchange performance. 4) In situations where cultural distance is high, contracts are an effective mechanism to deter local supplier opportunism only when relational trust exists. The findings of this project not only enrich our understanding of the effects of trust and contracts in China, but also provide important managerial implications for foreign companies to understand how to employ trust and contracts to build better supplier relationships in China.

757910.value: 企业的并购、分拆与行业竞争

757910.label: Project Objectives
757910.value: Analyze the incentive to divest and relate it to the incentive to merge. Relate the two incentives to underlying economic conditions. Study the interaction between these two activities: how does a merger or divestiture alter other firms’ incentives to merge and to divest? How does the anticipation of such an alteration in turn change firms’ restructuring incentives in the first place? Characterize the industry equilibrium: how does the interaction between firms’ restructuring activities affect market competition? Will the market become more or less concentrated? Derive policy recommendations: what should the antitrust authority do to promote social welfare? What kind of mergers or divestitures should be blocked? Are divestitures effective as a structural remedy for mergers? Empirically test the theoretical findings.

757910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
757910.value: In the U.S. and European Union, antitrust policies have been an important force in maintaining market competition and shaping business strategies. More than half of antitrust resources have been spent on merger controls. In the past, merger control was mainly through the scrutiny of merger proposals and the blocking of mergers thought to be harmful to competition. Recently, however, the focus has shifted to structural remedies: Merging parties are frequently required to divest part of their businesses before a merger can be approved. Apart from involuntary divestitures imposed by the antitrust authority when firms attempt to merge, many companies engage in voluntary divestitures as a major vehicle for corporate restructuring. Understanding the incentives of divestitures and their impact on market competition is thus of ultimate importance for effective antitrust policy and enforcement. This is particularly relevant for Hong Kong and China, as both regions have recently drafted competition laws. The high profile acquisition of Huiyuan Juice by Coca-Cola and its subsequent rejection by the Chinese Ministry of Commerce highlight the importance of understanding the impact of mergers and divestitures on competition. While there is a large body of research on mergers, very few have studied divestitures, especially in relation to mergers and as merger remedies. This project aims to fill the gap by studying the interaction between divestitures and mergers and its impact on market competition. I have found a novel way to model divestitures as reverse mergers, and intend to continue the successful approach of my previous studies of mergers, which have been supported by RGC grants. I plan to investigate the incentive to divest and its relation to underlying economic conditions, the strategic interaction between divestitures and mergers, and the optimal policy of merger control, especially that of structural remedies through divestitures. The findings of this project will contribute to theoretical research, public policies and business strategies. For economic theory, the project will further our understanding of the forces behind divestitures and mergers, and the interaction between the two activities in shaping market competition. For government officials and regulators, the research will provide guidelines for merger controls. For practitioners, it will highlight divestitures and mergers as competitive tools by showing how companies may gain competitive advantage through carefully planned restructuring of their production facilities, what to expect of rivals as a result of their restructuring, and how to act strategically to induce favorable restructuring from rival firms. 反托拉斯是国际上重要的维持竞争的手段，主要通过对企业并购的审核，近年来重点移向结构性处理，也就是要求参与并购的企业分拆一部分资产。 许多企业自己有时候也希望进行分拆，对于反托拉斯来说，分析企业分拆的动机和后果就显得很重要。中国和香港最近都在加强反托拉斯的立法和执行，例如中国商务部阻止了可口可乐收购汇源。 经济学上有很多关于并购的研究，但对分拆的研究很少。这个项目旨在研究并购与分拆之间的关系及其对行业竞争的影响。我会继续利用上一个成功项目的研究方法探讨各种相关问题。 本项目的研究对一下几个方面都可有所贡献：对经济学理论，我们可以加深对分拆与并购的认识，尤其是两者之间的互动。对公共政策，它可以指导反托拉斯的执行。对企业家，它凸显并购和分拆作为竞争策略的作用，以及自身企业重组会怎样影响其他竞争者的企业重组。

757910.label: Realisation of objectives
757910.value: 1. Achieved completely. I confirmed that the incentive to divest is exactly the opposite of the incentive to merge. A merger reduces competition between the merging firms, but non-merging firms take the opportunity to expand, which hurts the merging firms. Conversely, a divestiture creates internal competition, but it forces competitors to be less aggressive. I showed that a merger is profitable if and only if the products are sufficiently differentiated; the opposite is true for divestitures. 2. Achieved completely. I found that each type of restructuring is a complement of a second restructuring of the same type. In particular, a merger encourages further mergers, while a divestiture encourages further divestitures. Moreover, firms may restructure strategically in order to encourage mergers and/or discourage divestitures among the remaining firms. 3. Achieved completely. I found that all firms merge when products are either very different or very similar. A striking feature is that the interaction between restructurings can completely alter the influence of the underlying economic conditions. When restructuring is done in isolation, product substitution hinders mergers, but when mergers and divestitures are considered together, product substitution leads firms to merge. 4. Achieved completely. I concluded that mergers may happen for strategic reasons: an unprofitable merger may be carried out to precipitate another merger or prevent a divestiture. This means the antitrust authorities should take a more active and more dynamic view in dealing with merger applications. 5. Achieved partly. I have spent quite some time thinking about the empirical test and have hired a research assistant to help me read through a merger database and collect a lot of relevant data, but I did the empirical test only partly. Data collection proved harder than I thought despite my effort. Also, my own training is analytical, and I had hoped to admit a PhD student to help me with the empirical work. Two years in a row, I made offers to PhD applicants but they both declined the offer and it was too late to admit another one.

757910.label: Major findings and research outcome
757910.value: In this project I study firms’ corporate restructuring choices where each firm may either merge or divest and where multiple restructuring may take place. Unlike most game-theoretical studies examining corporate restructuring issues, which models merger and divestiture separately, I take a more realistic approach. As merger and divestiture represent the two ends of the same spectrum for corporate restructuring, and they are often no stand-alone phenomena, I consider these two corporate restructuring activities together as two intrinsically related strategic options in an integrated model. Empirical studies also call for such joint consideration as it adequately captures the strategic interactions among participating firms and therefore facilitates better understanding of corporate restructuring efforts. I show that a merger reduces competition between the merging firms, but also makes them less competitive, while a divestiture has the opposite effect. Therefore, firms tend to merge when products are differentiated and to divest when products are close substitutes when these two actives are treated in isolation. However, when merger and divestiture are considered together, firms will merge in order to preempt divestiture. In other words, a firm may try to influence other firms’ restructuring, giving rise to strategic incentives in its own restructuring effort. Therefore, a merger can be strategic because it preempts a more damaging outcome in which all firms divest. Consequently, there is a tendency for firms to merge at all levels of product differentiation, leading the multi-product firms. This prediction is also consistent with observations in real life that merger is very common while divestiture is much rarer. The finding is important because academic research and casual observation both indicate that M&A activities far exceed divestiture in both volume and value. This comes as a surprise as both M&A and divestiture are strategic alternatives along a continuum of governance modes and corporate restructuring efforts. Furthermore, compelling evidence indicate that M&A do not create value for shareholders. Although there are some theories explaining these puzzles, they are not satisfactory. In this research I provide a new explanation to show that firms merge to pre-empt divestiture as the latter would lead to an even worse situation. In other words, I argue that firms may be well aware of the difficulties and the possible negative consequences of mergers, and yet they still decide to merge because it intends to achieve a particular strategic objective, that is, to prevent divestiture of rival firms.

757910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
757910.value: There could be several routes to further develop the research conducted in this project. One is to carry out empirical tests. The paper has generated some predictions that can be tested. For example, the merger intensity is U-shaped in the degree of product differentiation; divestitures will be more likely when mergers become less profitable due to increased internal substitution, and mergers will be more likely when divestitures are more profitable due to smaller fixed costs of divestiture. A second route is to model firms’ restructuring behavior using cooperative games. This project has used non-cooperative games. In order to reach a unique equilibrium, I have assumed that firms restructure sequentially. Given symmetric firms, sequential move may be OK, but people may still ask where the order of move comes from and how a restructured firm can commit to not restructure again, as assumed by the model. There could be two solutions. One is to look at asymmetric firms and endogenize the order of move. The second is to use cooperative games. Both will require a completely different model.

757910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
757910.value: Academic research and casual observation both indicate that M&A activities far exceed divestiture in both volume and value. This comes as a surprise as both M&A and divestiture are strategic alternatives along a continuum of governance modes and corporate restructuring efforts. Both are important and valuable boundary adjustment activities to achieve different strategic objectives. Furthermore, compelling evidence indicate that M&A do not create value for shareholders. To explain these puzzles, I offer a new theory to explain why firms merge despite negative consequences, i.e., firms merge to pre-empt divestiture as the latter would lead to an even worse situation. I demonstrate that modeling merger and divestiture simultaneously is important because these two activities are interdependent; any study that treats them in isolation is likely to produce erroneous findings. Finally, the research resolves two long standing paradoxes in the area of corporate restructuring, namely, the merger and divestiture paradox, which argues that merger will never be profitable while divestiture is always profitable. These two related paradoxes would predict the proliferation of divestiture and disappearance of merger, which is the opposite of the reality. My findings demonstrate that the so called paradoxes are essentially an artifact of an overly simplified model.

758010.label: Project Objectives
758010.value: Empirically examine the effects of servant leadership on team performance and shared psychological safety perceptions. Test whether the team members’ perception of psychological safety mediates the relationship between servant leadership and team performance. Test whether the team members’ perception of psychological safety mediates the relationship between servant leadership and team performance.

758010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
758010.value: Today, there is a growing interest in developing servant leaders who set aside self-interest for the betterment of their followers and organizations (Spears, 2002). This emerging leadership approach is one strongly based on ethical and caring behavior, and one that is attempting to enhance the personal growth of workers while improving the caring and quality of our community (Greenleaf, 1977). However, despite the assumed prominence of servant leadership behavior in organizations, little theoretical or empirical work has studied the claimed strength of servant leadership and the mechanism through which it fulfills individuals and energizes teams (Barbuto & Wheeler, 2006; Liden, Wayne, Zhao, & Henderson, 2008). This study examines the effects of servant leadership behavior on team performance across matched financial services teams in Hong Kong and the United States. The model predicts that servant leadership influences team performance through the mediating effect of team psychological safety—shared beliefs among team members that the team is safe to engage in interpersonal risk taking (Edmondson, 1999) across both sub-samples. In addition, these effects are moderated by the cultural value (power distance and collectivism). These two cultural value moderators are proposed to explain why stronger effects of servant leadership on team performance are observed among the Chinese participants (characterized by high power distance and collectivism) than among the American participants (characterized by low power distance and individualism). This study contributes not only to research on servant leadership and team functioning but also to emerging research on leadership and values by demonstrating how two types of follower values moderate the impact of servant leadership on follower performance. rows: Servant leadership was found to be significantly related to team psychological safety and team psychological safety was also significantly related to team performance.

When both servant leadership and team psychological safety were included as predictors of team performance, only team psychological safety demonstrated a statistically significant effect (β = .38, p < .001). The beta coefficient for servant leadership regressing on team performance was no longer significant when controlling for team psychological safety. These results indicate that team psychological safety mediated the relationship between servant leadership and team performance.

The moderation tests showed that the positive effect of servant leadership on team psychological safety was stronger among branches with higher collectivism and among branches with higher power distance.

758010.label: Major findings and research outcome
758010.value: The results based on both Hong Kong and U.S. samples demonstrated that team level servant leadership ratings were related to superior team performance, and this relationship was mediated by team psychological safety. Furthermore, team cultural values were found to moderate the effects of followers’ perceptions of servant leadership on psychological safety and team performance. Specifically, servant leadership had a stronger positive influence on team psychological safety and subsequent team performance among teams that endorsed high power distance and, separately, high collectivism.

758010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
758010.value: In this study, we chose to focus on the overall impact of servant leadership and accordingly, data analyses were conducted by using a composite servant leadership index. However, different dimensions involved in servant leadership may exert different effects on people. Future research that theorizes and tests the unique functions associated with specific servant leadership dimensions will enhance understanding of social influence processes associated with servant leadership. In addition, it would be useful if future studies incorporated processes associated with other leadership models (e.g., initiating structure, LMX, and transformational leadership, among others) and seek to identify the unique contributions of servant leadership.

758010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
758010.value: The findings of the current provide some practical implications for how managers might attempt to create a psychologically safe climate and improve team performance. First, the behaviors associated with servant-leadership can be particularly useful for managers who are interested in building team psychological safety. By behaving ethically, empowering team members, helping them grow and succeed, and showing emotional support, members feel free to share ideas and opinions without negative repercussions. Hence fears, afflictions, and doubts begin to recede within the team, thus facilitating more open and collaborative group processes. In both HK and U.S. settings, servant leadership was found to have strong positive influences on team psychological safety and team performance. However, the effect is stronger in the Chinese culture of Hong Kong, because of the higher modal levels of power distance and collectivism in that culture. Thus, leaders and organizations should consider the fact that certain team contexts may be more favorable for servant leadership when designing their approaches to enhance leadership in different settings.

758110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
758110.value: 顧客滿意程度的導因：公司層面產品質量-顧客滿意度擴充模型研究

758110.label: Project Objectives
758110.value: Our proposed research addresses the following questions: 1) How does the management of a product and its associated service jointly influence customer satisfaction? 2) Are the effects of a product and the associated service activities on satisfaction additive or multiplicative? 3) Do pre- and post-sale services play different roles in affecting customer satisfaction? 4) Does the joint effect of the product and service on customer satisfaction vary with firms’ inter-functional coordination? 5) How does a firm optimize resources allocation between the management of a product and its associated services to maximize the return on investment? Our project aims to make the following contributions: 1) This project applies the consumer level satisfaction theory in the domain of the firm strategic management, and translates the consumer understanding to the firm strategic decision. 2) This research takes a unique view to unveil the cumulative nature of customer satisfaction. It reaches beyond the conventional boundary between a product and service, and demonstrates how firms can improve customer satisfaction by jointly managing the product and service. 3) Drawing from the conceptual framework at the consumer level, this project captures consumers’ shift of emphasis on product quality evaluation. It further addresses the differences between pre- and post-sale services in converting investment in product management to customer satisfaction. This extends our understanding on the quality satisfaction relationship. 4) The quantified outcomes of the firm level model allow managers to measure, calculate, and compare different alternatives in strategic management. Therefore, our empirical findings at the firm level will provide important implication for businesses to optimize resource allocation between the product and service management in achieving the superior return on investment.

758110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
758110.value: Customer satisfaction is a cumulative evaluation of the firm offerings evolving from the dynamic flow of interaction with both products and services through the consumption period. However, the existing literature largely ignores the joint effects of products and the associated pre- and post-sale services on customer satisfaction. Furthermore, there has been little attempt to model how firms strategically manage their products and services to improve the aggregated firm level customer satisfaction. Aiming to fill these gaps, our proposed project develops a firm level augmented quality-satisfaction model that recognizes the cumulative consumption experience. We use survey data to empirically test the joint impact of firms’ product and service management on customer satisfaction. We further investigate the influences of pre- and post-sale services on the conversion of product management to customer satisfaction. Lastly, we examine the moderating effect of inter-functional collaboration on our proposed mechanism. This research will provide important implications for firms’ strategic management in resource allocation optimization among different functional units. 顧客滿意程度的導因：公司層面產品質量-顧客滿意度擴充模型研究 顧客滿意程度是於消費時透過公司所提供的產品及服務的互動所累積的評價。然而，現有的文獻都忽視產品及售前售後服務對顧客滿意程度的影響。再者，現時並無太多研究關於公司如何策略地管理他們的產品及服務，以提升顧客滿意程度。為填補這方面不足，我們計劃開發一個有關公司質量滿意的擴充模型，以識別累積的消費經驗。我們會用調查數據來測試公司管理的產品及服務對顧客滿意程度的影響。我們亦會深入研究售前售後服務對顧客滿意程度的影響。最後，我們會調查公司職能部門協調對我們所提倡的模型如何影響。這個研究將為資源分配的策略管理提供重要的應用。

758110.value: We have finished the following objectives: 1, 2 and 3 We have collected a comprehensive data set of 250 firms with 570 specially selected and constructed variables/measures. We are in the process of analyzing the data, testing different hypotheses and work toward an output of a research paper. Therefore, we haven't fully achieved the following objectives. 4,5, and 6 The project was delayed due to the comprehensive nature of our firm level study. We have spent great efforts and time to compile the question list and translated the material into Chinese. We used double translators to guarantee the accuracy of translation to finalize the question list. The next barrier was the implementation of data collection. For the comprehensiveness of the data collection, we felt that it would be difficult for us to use research assistant(s) to conduct the surveys from Hong Kong. Instead, we searched and hired professional marketing research firm to carry out the survey for us for the reasons of: 1) the location of target, i.e. firms potentially widely spread over mainland China 2) the wide coverage of the business concepts included in the survey list; 3) the requirement of the comprehensiveness of the business operations for the firm, specifically the management of product and service simultaneously; 4) the wide coverage of the business, i.e. potentially from any sectors, and for both C2B and B2B business; 5) the senior level of the management to be interviewed, i.e. potentially multiple director or general manager from each firm. However, due to the budget constraint (the approved budget was almost 50% short of the applied amount), the contracted firm took longer time to collect the trial data before fully carried out data collection. We used both personal interview and online survey to collect data, which added the turnaround time. It was not until the late 2nd half of 2014 did we finally received the complete data set. This left us insufficient time to fully mine the data and finish all planned work. However, due to the newness of the data (collected in 2014), it won't affect the quality and timeliness of our research. We have adjusted our time table to push forward the project as follows: Now to June, 2015 Data analysis and paper write-up June, 2015-March, 2016 Paper submission, review process and paper publication

758110.label: Major findings and research outcome
758110.value: Drawing from the literature of New Product Innovation (NPI), Total Quality Management (TQM), Just-in-Time (JIT) and Total Productive Management (TPM), we developed the consumer-level augmented quality-satisfaction (CLAQS) framework. We conjecture that product management and service management positively impact customer satisfaction, and that service management accelerates the conversion of product management to customer satisfaction. We also theorize that the associated services have stronger positive impact on product-satisfaction relationship in firms with strong inter-functional coordination. Due to the delay of our data collection, we are still in the process of finalizing our data analysis and empirically substantiate our theory. We have planned the completion of our first research paper with regard to the above framework in the coming months.

758110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
758110.value: During the further development of our framework, we have added new constructs such as innovation, service cocreation, IT capability, social responsibility, etc. to our data collection. In this sense, our data are very comprehensive (with 570 variables for 250 firms from different industries over China, which both manufacture and handle the service for their products), and therefore there are many alternative ways for us to expand our framework. In other words, we are able to develop other projects with possible combinations of different constructs we measured. Our plan is to develop multiple follow-up projects after we finalize the first paper based on our framework in this research proposal. To implement the follow-up projects will be relatively quick and efficient because we have already collected the data needed for these future research.

758110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
758110.value: This project develops a firm level augmented quality-satisfaction model that recognizes the cumulative consumption experience. Upon completion, we are able to empirically demonstrate the joint impact of firms’ product and service management on customer satisfaction. We further investigate the influences of pre- and post-sale services on the conversion of product management to customer satisfaction. Lastly, we examine how inter-functional collaboration moderates the proposed effects. This research will provide important implications for firms which manage both manufacturing and serving customers with their products at the same time. It sheds lights on how firm can design strategic management in resource allocation optimization among different functional units to achieve customer satisfaction and market/financial performance.

760410.label: Realisation of objectives
760410.value: The aim of this project was to identify cross-reactive antigens on the surface of human renal proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTEC) that mediate anti-dsDNA antibody binding, and the mechanism(s) involved in translocation of anti-dsDNA antibodies to the nucleus to mediate downstream inflammatory and fibrotic processes. Having identified the cross-reactive antigens, further studies were undertaken to investigate their expression in renal specimens, and to determine serum immunoglobulins and anti-dsDNA antibody binding to these cross-reactive antigens using ELISAs. Although our preliminary studies for this research proposal implicated myosin and tropomyosin in anti-dsDNA antibody binding to PTEC, using more sensitive and advanced methodologies, further analysis demonstrated that other proteins played a more prominent role. In total 4 proteins were identified in the plasma membrane, cytosolic and nuclear fractions that bound to anti-dsDNA antibodies, namely Ku70, Ku80, major vault protein and calreticulin. In order to investigate serum immunoglobulins and anti-dsDNA antibody binding to these cross-reactive antigens, sufficient purified proteins from HK-2 cells (human PTEC immortalized by transduction with the human papilloma virus), was required. We initially encountered some difficulties in the over-expression of these proteins in HK-2 cells, since yields were low and some proteins underwent degradation during the purification steps despite taking precautionary steps. The technical procedures were repeated in new cells, and so far, we have not encountered further degradation. We hope to complete the procedures to purify these proteins in the coming months to complete the ELISAs for this study. The other objectives of this research project have been completed.

760410.label: Major findings and research outcome
760410.value: In this study, we demonstrated that human polyclonal anti-dsDNA antibodies bound directly to human PTEC through a mechanism independent of chromatin material. This was followed by their rapid internalization and translocation to the cytosol and nucleus. Using biochemical and proteomic approaches, we demonstrated that anti-dsDNA antibodies bound to Ku70 in plasma membrane extracts isolated from PTEC, and to Ku70, Ku80, major vault protein and calreticulin in cytosolic and nuclear fractions. Anti-dsDNA antibodies increased Ku70, Ku80 and major vault protein synthesis in a time-dependent manner. Expression of these proteins was localized to proximal tubules particularly those undergoing atrophy, and their staining was more prominent in renal tissue from patients with active diffuse proliferative lupus nephritis compared to non-lupus renal disease or control specimens. Binding of anti-dsDNA antibodies to PTEC increased of ERK, p38 MAPK, PKC-alpha, PKC-betaII and AKT/PI3K phosphorylation, which was accompanied by a concomitant increase in IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1, TNF-alpha and TGF-beta1 secretion, and synthesis of fibroblast specific protein-1, fibronectin, collagen type I and laminin - proteins that play critical roles in kidney inflammation and fibrosis. Further analysis showed distinct regulatory mechanisms of each protein, with ERK, p38 MAPK, PKC and AKT/PI3K regulating IL-6, IL-8, TGF-beta1, fibroblast specific-1 protein, fibronectin and collagen type I synthesis, and p38 MAPK regulating MCP-1 and TNF-alpha secretion. One of the first extracellular matrix proteins deposited during tubulo-interstitial fibrosis is fibronectin. Anti-dsDNA antibodies induced both soluble and cell-associated fibronectin in a time-dependent manner. Cell-associated fibronectin was predominantly localized to the extracellular matrix, whereas soluble fibronectin contributed to tubular fibrogenesis by increasing TGF-beta1 secretion and collagen type I synthesis - both key mediators of tissue fibrosis. Although it is well established that IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 and TNF-alpha are pro-inflammatory mediators, their induction in PTEC by anti-dsDNA antibodies also resulted in a significant increase in soluble fibronectin and highlights their role in kidney fibrogenesis in the setting of lupus nephritis. Data generated from this research project have been presented at 3 international meetings. A manuscript detailing the contributing role of anti-dsDNA antibodies in tubular fibrogenesis has been submitted to the Journal of Autoimmunity (impact factor: 7.018) and is currently under review. Part of the data has also been included in two invited reviews. We are currently preparing two further manuscripts detailing (1) the identification of cross-reactive antigens that mediate anti-dsDNA antibody binding and translocation in PTEC, and (2) the role of anti-dsDNA antibodies in tubular inflammation.

760410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
760410.value: Having identified Ku70 as the predominant antigen in plasma membrane extracts that cross-react with anti-dsDNA antibodies, we would like to further develop this area of research and investigate in-depth the functional role of Ku70 in PTEC in the setting of lupus nephritis. Published data indicate that under physiological conditions, Ku70 is predominantly localized in the nuclei of cells in the form of heterodimers comprising two subunits each of Ku70 and Ku80, and play critical roles in DNA double strand break recognition and repair, growth regulation and transcription. Ku70 may also exist in its monomeric form in the cytosol and plasma membrane, where it contributes to inflammation, apoptosis and cell-matrix adhesion. These processes are aberrant during progressive lupus nephritis. It is possible that increased Ku70 synthesis in PTEC following anti-dsDNA antibody stimulation may amplify inflammatory and fibrotic processes in the kidney during lupus nephritis. A research proposal submitted to the RGC General Research Fund 2014-15 entitled “The role of Ku70 and Ku80 in the pathogenesis of lupus nephritis” was recently funded, which will allow us to further investigate whether changes to Ku70 synthesis and their sub-cellular localization plays an important role in tubular inflammation and fibrosis.

760410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
760410.value: Kidney involvement, termed lupus nephritis, is one of the most severe organ manifestations of systemic lupus erythematosus. Anti-dsDNA antibodies have been implicated in disease pathogenesis. The mechanism through which anti-dsDNA antibodies bind to renal proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTEC) to mediate their detrimental effect is currently unknown. In this research project, we demonstrated that binding of anti-dsDNA antibodies to PTEC is independent of double-stranded DNA but reliant on its interaction with Ku70. Following binding to Ku70, anti-dsDNA antibodies are internalized and enter the nucleus where they induce inflammation and fibrogenesis in PTEC through activation of the protein kinase C and mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling pathways. Fibronectin is an extracellular matrix protein that is synthesized in low quantities by PTEC under normal conditions, and its expression is increased under pathological conditions. Anti-dsDNA antibodies increased both soluble and cellular fibronectin in PTEC. Whereas cellular fibronectin accumulates in the extracellular matrix, soluble fibronectin also contributed to fibrotic processes by increasing TGF-beta1 secretion and collagen type I synthesis. Taken together, our data show that anti-dsDNA antibodies contribute to tubulo-interstitial inflammation and fibrosis during lupus nephritis through its interaction with Ku70.
