761210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
761210.value: The high lethality of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 disease in humans, especially in the context of its continued pandemic potential, makes it important to explore the underlying disease mechanisms. Such understanding will underpin the development of novel therapeutic interventions for this disease. These are urgently needed in view of the poor clinical response to current therapeutic options. Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), the most severe form of acute lung injury (ALI), has been the cause of severe illness and death in patients with disease caused by influenza H5N1 virus infection. ARDS was also a cause of death during the 1918 influenza pandemic and is also seen in those rare instances of fatal infection with the current pandemic swine-origin influenza H1N1 virus. Recent in vivo and in vitro studies indicate that allogeneic multi-potent mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) may have a therapeutic effect on acute lung injury through their immunomodulatory and pluripotent properties. However, whether MSC will have beneficial effect on lung injury induced by HPAI H5N1 virus infection has not been investigated. In this research proposal, I propose to establish an in vitro model to study alveolar fluid clearance following influenza H5N1 virus infection and to investigate the beneficial effect of cell-based therapy with allogeneic human MSC on the severity of lung injury and edema formation and on accelerating the resolution of lung edema in a physiological and clinically relevant model of in vitro primary human alveolar epithelial cells. I hypothesize that treatment with MSC will alter the course of ALI by reducing edema formation and enhancing edema clearance. Investigation of these mechanisms will offer new insights and lead to the development of new treatment options for patients suffering from ARDS caused by influenza H5N1 virus infection and also other pathogens that cause severe lung injury including, albeit rarely, the current pandemic swine-origin influenza H1N1 virus. 高致病性禽流感（HPAI）H5N1病毒對人類有很高的致命性，由於它仍具有導致流感大流行的潛力，因此了解它的疾病機制尤其重要。由於現有的治療方法，在臨床應用的成效不理想，因此我們對於能有助研發能預防和治療這種疾病的方法及藥物的資料實在有急切的需要，也正是這個研究項目的預計成果。急性呼吸窘迫綜合徵（ARDS）是最嚴重的急性肺功能受損（ALI），也是導致感染H5N1流感病毒患者病況嚴重和死亡的原因之一。急性呼吸窘迫綜合徵也是在1918年大流感導致死亡的原因，它亦出現在目前豬流感H1N1病毒罕見的致命病毒感染個案。最近在試管和動物實驗的研究指出，同種異體骨髓間質幹細胞（MSC）能對急性肺損傷的免疫調節和多能性性質起治療作用。本研究建議採用一個以肺泡上皮細胞和同種異體骨髓間質幹細胞的試管實驗模型，作測試在H5N1病毒感染下，導致因肺泡液體清除失衡而產生肺水腫的機制。這個研究項目更會探討使用MSC對肺損傷的治療功效。我們將以MSC對肺泡上皮細胞傷害（肺損傷）的嚴重程度和肺水腫的形成及清除速度，來評估MSC細胞治療的成效。研究會假設在MSC細胞治療能有效減少肺水腫的形成和加強清除水腫現象，從而防止ALI的發生。預料研究將對治療嚴重肺功能受損提供新的見解，並可因提供新的治療方法，使感染H5N1流感及其他能引致嚴重肺功能受損的病原體包括絕少會出現的現時流行源自豬隻的H1N1流感病毒而引致ARDS的病得到有效的醫治。

761210.value: Objective 1 to 4: The in vitro lung injury model is fully established and successfully optimized in this GRF proposal. We showed that influenza H5N1 (and the novel H7N9 virus), but not seasonal H1N1 (H9N2, H3N2 and H7N8) influenza virus increased the epithelial protein permeability and impaired alveolar fluid clearance (AFC). Besides, we showed that H5N1 virus significantly up-regulated the pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine expression and down-regulated the expression of ENaC, Na-K-ATPase and CFTR, which suggested their critical role in H5N1 associated acute lung injury. Whilst, the treatment of selective inhibitors of the major sodium/chloride transporters in alveolar epithelial cells infected with H5N1 virus can reverse the impairment of AFC and protein permeability by up-regulated the degraded Na-K-ATPase and CFTR, suggests the potential therapeutic options in H5N1 associated lung edema using specific inhibitor to epithelial transporters. Furthermore, in the study on the role of MSC-secreted soluble proteins, we demonstrated that the MSC-mediated reversal of AFC and protein permeability impairment was mediated in part through the secretion of Ang1 and KGF, however, other soluble factors likely play a synergistic role in the beneficial effects provided by MSC. 761210.label: Major findings and research outcome
761210.value: The in vitro lung injury model is fully established and successfully applied in this GRF proposal. Lung injury index (the impairment in AFC and protein permeability) of influenza virus infected alveolar epithelial cells can be used as a risk assessment tools for influenza virus. We showed that influenza H5N1 (and the novel H7N9 virus), but not seasonal H1N1 (H9N2, H3N2 and H7N8) influenza virus increased alveolar epithelial protein permeability and impaired AFC. Furthermore, by using virus-free conditioned medium obtained from virus-infected alveolar epithelial cells, we showed similar effects on AFC and protein permeability. This result reflected the effects of soluble mediators released from H5N1 virus infected cells. Furthermore, we showed that H5N1 virus significantly up-regulated cytokine and chemokine mRNA and protein expression which play an important role in impairment in AFC and permeability. Besides, the major sodium/chloride transporters, ENaC, Na-K-ATPase and CFTR expression are significantly down-regulated after H5N1 virus infection. On the other hand, selective inhibitors of sodium/chloride transporters have been used to treat alveolar epithelial cells with H5N1 infection. We showed that these inhibitors reverse the impairment of AFC and protein permeability by up-regulated the degraded Na-K-ATPase and CFTR. Besides, we showed that co-culture of MSC with H5N1 virus infected alveolar epithelial cells significantly reversed the H5N1 virus impaired AFC and protein permeability of alveolar epithelial cells. In addition. co-culture of MSC with H5N1 virus infected alveolar epithelial cells led to a significant suppression of IL-1β, RANTES, IL6, IL8 and IP10 expression; whilst up-regulated the sodium/chloride transporter protein expression in H5N1-infected alveolar epithelial cells. Finally, we showed that selectively knocked down Ang1 and/or KGF protein secretion in MSC using Ang1 siRNA and KGF siRNA separately or co-transfected together. The beneficial effect of MSC was reduced in Ang1 and KGF siRNA pre-treated MSC by 49% and 38% respectively, compared to control MSC. MSC with siRNA knock-down of both Ang1 and KGF had 58% reduction in their ability to restore AFC compared to treatment with control MSC co-culture. Similarly, no further protection was observed in MSC with plasmid over-expressing Ang1 and KGF. These results indicated that the MSC-mediated reversal of AFC and protein permeability impairment was mediated in part through the secretion of Ang1 and KGF, other soluble factors likely play a synergistic role in the beneficial effects provided by MSC.

761210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
761210.value: The lung injury model established in this proposal can use to study alveolar fluid clearance following influenza H5N1 virus infection and to investigate the beneficial effect of cell-based therapy with allogeneic human MSC on the severity of lung injury and edema formation and on accelerating the resolution of lung edema in a physiological and clinically relevant model. The results can propose the novel therapeutic treatment of human H5N1 diseases with MSC which effectively alter the course of ALI by reducing edema formation and enhancing edema clearance. Investigation of these mechanisms will offer new insights and lead to (1) future animal and clinical study on the use of MSC in the treatment of influenza associated lung injury; (2) the development of new treatment options for patients suffering from ARDS caused by H5N1 virus infection and other pathogens that cause severe lung injury including, the novel H7N9, SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV. Furthermore, the lung injury index (the measurement of the impairment of AFC and protein permeability) generated by the established in vitro lung injury model can be used as an important risk assessment tools for human disease severity of influenza virus, as well as other emerging respiratory viruses, e.g., SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV.

761210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
761210.value: This research project has established experimental model to study the effects of influenza H5N1 viruses on how it induced lung edema and damage, the key factors that pertain to the pathogenesis of ARDS and death. MSC due to their specific nature and their ability to secret multiple paracrine factors such as KGF and Angioprotein-1, can potentially redress the major abnormalities of alveolar epithelial function that lead to the often fatal consequences of human H5N1 disease. This research project also provides new information on the mechanisms underlying the development of acute lung injury and will possibly lead to potentially novel therapeutic options. We will learn how MSC reverse the impairment of alveolar fluid clearance, protein permeability and modulates our host pro-inflammatory response after highly pathogenic influenza H5N1 virus infection. I envision future clinical trials and studies building on these results to study further the effect of MSC on the mechanism of alveolar fluid transport in an injured alveolus infected with influenza H5N1 virus.

761710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
761710.value: 我們研究發現空間行為認知的出現，決定於發育期間，前庭核(VN)神經元胞膜上谷胺酸亞受體的插入。另外，我們亦首次發現初生老鼠在腦部內跟重力相關的三維空間圖譜之形成，具有可被改變的關鍵時期。雖然我們已知腦源性神經營養因子(BDNF)能夠調控海馬體及大腦皮層神經細胞的突觸可塑性，但BDNF對於調控前庭系統發育的可塑性，以及其對前庭行為於發育時出現所扮演的角色仍然未知。 我們假設，在發育時可以透過BDNF/TrkB來調節突觸可塑性，並進一步改變腦部空間行為認知之建立。我們首先利用細胞膜片箝制技術來判斷BDNF如何調控刺激性突觸及抑制性突觸，以及由此探索其於發育期間誘發VN突觸可塑性之角色。我們亦會將BDNF或其抑制劑放到初生老鼠的VN內，以確定BDNF及TrkB受體在前庭系統內建立三維空間圖譜的角色及其對空間定位學習的影響。 我們繼而假設BDNF具有對成年前庭系統可塑性之重現產生作用。基於我們發現在初生老鼠VN內，減低抑制性突觸的主導作用能夠改變空間圖譜及前庭行為，我們將證明這現象能否透過增強BDNF水平，在成年老鼠身上重新啟動。 總括而言，我們這項研究的結果將會讓我們更了解BDNF調控腦部空間圖譜及前庭行為認知的機制。此外，這項研究亦將揭示在成年前庭系統重啟可塑性的運作機制。

761710.label: Realisation of objectives
761710.value: Whole-cell patch-clamp experiments conducted in rat brainstem slices documented the maturation profile of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) synapses in the vestibular nucleus (VN) of postnatal rats. Gramicidin-perforated patch-clamp data showed that GABA receptor-mediated postsynaptic currents (PSCs) were excitatory in neonatal VN but switched from depolarization to hyperpolarization between postnatal day (P) 9 and 12. Furthermore, theta burst stimulation, a protocol that is known to trigger long-term synaptic plasticity, delivered to vestibular afferents induced long-term depression (LTD) and long-term potentiation (LTP) of GABA receptor-mediated evoked PSCs. GABAergic input to VN neurons exhibited an age-dependent shift from LTD to LTP. Notably, the efficacy of GABAergic transmission in the postnatal VN could be modulated by brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). Such effect of BDNF on GABAergic synaptic plasticity could also be modulated by retrograde signaling via endocannabinoid receptor. Taken together, our results indicate that BDNF plays an important role in modulating the maturation of GABAergic transmission and activity-dependent synaptic plasticity within the VN during the first two postnatal weeks. Due to time limitation of the project, the effect of BDNF on glutamatergic transmission within the VN was not investigated. Using the expression of immediate early gene c-fos as an indicator for functionally activated neurons, we demonstrated that topographic maps representing head movements in three dimensions are established in the brainstem during postnatal maturation. This provides an internal neural representation for spatial perception in three-dimension. Notably, this map in adult rats could be deranged using an intervention approach that perturbed GABAergic transmission within the neonatal VN. That central vestibular neurons also expressed BDNF receptor TrkB suggests that BDNF signaling via modulating GABAergic transmission plays a dominant role in tuning VN neurons for postnatal coding of head movements. Using a unique paradigm that allows slow release of BDNF to the neonatal VN, we were able to advance the emergence of negative geotaxis, an otolith-related orientation reflex, in postnatal rats. That no change was observed in adult rats that were pretreated with BDNF after P14 enabled us to identify a critical period of susceptibility for the refinement of neural network that contributes to the acquisition of graviceptive behavior.

761710.label: Major findings and research outcome
761710.value: We documented the maturation profile of GABA receptor-mediated inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSC) in neurons within the VN of rats. During the first two postnatal weeks, the frequency of miniature-IPSCs increased progressively whereas their rise time and decay time decreased by 2-fold. GABA receptor-mediated PSCs were excitatory in neonatal VN and that these currents switched from depolarization to hyperpolarization between P9 and P12. Furthermore, LTD of evoked-PSCs was observed at P4. At P14, the probability of inducing inhibitory LTD decreased but the same stimulus induced LTP. After pre-incubation with BDNF, LTDs were recorded both in P4 and P14 neurons while LTP could no longer be induced at P14. These effects of BDNF were mimicked with the application of TrkB receptor agonist. With blockade of endocannabinoid (eCB) receptor that mediates retrograde signaling and presynaptic release of GABA, BDNF changed the efficacy of GABAergic VN synapses (P4 and P7) from LTD to LTP. Altogether, our findings demonstrate that eCB receptor modulates BDNF-induced change in efficacy of GABAergic transmission in the VN. We revealed that spatial maps that encode rotation- and gravity-related cues emerged in the brainstem during postnatal development. Functionally activated VN neurons co-expressing Fos and TrkB receptors were detected from P7 onward. The number of these neurons increased with age, reaching 90% of the total Fos-labeled VN neurons in adult rats. Neonatal infusion of GABA receptor antagonist to the VN perturbed formation of the spatial map. Our results suggest that TrkB/ neurotrophin signaling plays a dominant role in modulating VN neurons for postnatal coding of head movements. We further used negative geotaxis, a gravity-detection innate response in which animals move head-up against gravity, to attest the effects of BDNF in developmental acquisition of vestibular reflex. Young rats placed either side-down or nose-down on a tilted platform in the dark could re-orient to nose-up position as early as P7 and P9, respectively. Rats implanted at P1 with BDNF-impregnated Elvax slice (a biocompatible polymer that allows sustainable delivery of drug) over the brainstem surface on the VN were able to re-orient themselves at 2 days earlier than the controls. In adult rats that were implanted with BDNF-impregnated Elvax at P14, no behavorial change in negative geotaxis was observed. We have therefore revealed a critical period during which BDNF regulates the expression of vestibular-related behaviors.

761710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
761710.value: We are the first group to demonstrate that maturation of GABAergic circuitry in the brainstem vestibular nucleus is regulated by BDNF. Furthermore, BDNF modifies experience-dependent synaptic plasticity of the developing vestibular network and behavioral expression of vestibular function. Our findings open up a novel research direction about the developmental role of neuromodulator BDNF in governing pre-/postsynaptic plasticity within a functional vestibular network, thereby contributing to downstream behavioral modification. Research in these directions will shed light on the design of drugs for strategies that could rescue synaptic disorders for restoration of balance function. Furthermore, our findings provide the reference framework to assess the contribution of BDNF in functional establishment of the vestibulo-thalamic pathway that serves as the gateway to the cerebral cortex. Data made available will unveil our understanding on the transformation of sensory cues of balance into head-direction signals during maturation of the central vestibular circuitry, and in turn its contribution to the realization of spatial navigation.

761710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
761710.value: Refinement and consolidation of synaptic inputs at single cell level is known to orchestrate the establishment of neural circuitry during brain development. Plasticity of these networks is governed by both pre- and postsynaptic mechanisms. We demonstrated for the first time that brain-derived neurotrophic factor modifies experience-dependent synaptic plasticity of the developing vestibular network and behavioral expression of gravity-detection behavior. Postnatal development of sensory function for spatial recognition therefore requires tuning of neural networks in the descending vestibulospinal circuitry. We further identified a neonatal period of susceptibility during which brain-derived neurotrophic factor modulates the expression of such innate behavior. Our results have also provided insights for the development of therapeutic strategy that enhances brain plasticity for restoration of motor function.

761910.label: Realisation of objectives
761910.value: The role of Sox2 in development of otic sensory neuron precursors In Sox2 mutant Lcc/Lcc, neuroblasts were specified but the differentiated sensory neurons failed to be maintained. We found levels of otic SOX2 in Lcc/Lcc was reduced to 40% early (at 13sp) but by 25sp was only 7%. To address the role of SOX2 in specifying otic neuroblasts, we ablated Sox2 in the otic vesicle using Pax2Cre mice that leads to loss of Sox2 expression in the “pre-otic field” in the otic vesicle. We found a temporal and dose-dependent requirement for Sox2 in the specification of otic neuroblasts during neurogenesis. Therefore SOX2 controls specification of progenitors for all three cell types: sensory neurons, hair cells and supporting cells in the inner ear. Genes and genetic pathways regulated by SOX2 in otic development To understand the impact of loss of Sox2 expression on cell fate and key pathways in otic development, RNA-seq was performed on the FACS GFP+ve cells of Sox2EGFP/+ and Sox2EGFP/Lcc E9.5 otic vesicles. We found the BMP/TGFβ pathway was significantly affected in the Sox2 mutants. To gain insight into the role of BMP/TGFβ signaling in sensory specification we inactivated this pathway specifically in the otocysts of mice by conditional gene ablation of Smad4. Loss of BMP/TGFβ signaling resulted in severe inner ear abnormalities, including the loss of vestibular semicircular canals, vestigial cochlea. Within the mutant inner ears we found expanded Sox2 expressing prosensory patches that give rise to ectopic sensory organs with hair cells and supporting cells. The opposing phenotypes associated with reduced SOX2, and resulting enhanced expression of several downstream targets of BMP/TGFβ signaling, versus expansion of prosensory development when Smad4 is inactivated, implicate an antagonistic relationship between these two transcription factors. We therefore hypothesise that Sox2 and BMP/TGFβ signaling function antagonistically to coordinate development of sensory and non-sensory structures in the correct location in the inner ear. Identification of otic specific enhancer(s) controlling Sox2 expression in the inner ear We had determined that the Lcc breakpoint and pAA2 insertion in Ysb lie 166 kb and 616 kb respectively 3’ to Sox2 coding sequence. We further found that sequences spanning 213 kb to 583 kb 3’ of Sox2, could drive otic expression in E10.5. In collaboration with Prof. Hisato Kondoh we tested screened conserved sequences (CNSs) for enhancer activity using chicken embryo electroporation. We identified 2 CNSs as potential otic enhancers able to direct otic expression in chick and transgenic mice.

761910.label: Major findings and research outcome
761910.value: Development of the inner ear requires coordination of early specification, in the correct location, of specific cell types: sensory hair cells, non-sensory supporting cells and sensory neurons that innervate the hair cells. These cells are essential for hearing and balance, acting as mechanosensors for the detection of sound (cochlear region), gravity and acceleration (vestibular region) which are transmitted to the central nervous system. Sensory and non-sensory structures in the functional inner ear are specified early in development, before any overt structure can be seen, according to the spatial location of progenitors within the epithelium of an initial sphere of cells (otocyst). It is thought that the six sensory organs in the inner ear develop from common progenitors in the otic epithelium. We previously discovered that Sox2 is essential for hearing and balance through studying two allelic mouse mutants with recessive deafness and balance-impairment, Light coat and circling (Lcc/Lcc, completely deaf) and Yellow submarine (Ysb/Ysb, severely hearing impaired). We showed that Sox2 is essential for the prosensory and sensory precursors in the inner ear starting from the otocyst stage. In Lcc/Lcc inner ears, all six sensory regions were absent, neither hair cells nor supporting cells differentiate, while the sensory epithelium was severely disrupted in Ysb/Ysb. These phenotypes are due to the severely reduced (Lcc/Lcc) or reduced (Ysb/Ysb) expression of Sox2, specifically within the developing inner ear. We asked whether Sox2 is also essential for specifying the progenitors for the sensory neurons that innervate the hair cells. We found a temporal and dose-dependent requirement for Sox2 in the specification of and/or maintenance of the otic neuroblasts during neurogenesis. Our studies implicate Sox2 as the master specifier for progenitors of the three lineages (sensory neurons, hair cells and supporting cells). How is sensory versus non-sensory fate was controlled in the inner ear? We found showed upregulation of BMP/TGFβ signaling with loss of Sox2 function. By contrast loss of BMP/TGFβ signaling results in ectopic sensory development. Our data imply Sox2 and BMP/TGFβ signaling function antagonistically to coordinate development of sensory and non-sensory structures in the inner ear. How is the otic expression of Sox2 regulated? We found that sequences spanning 213 kb to 583 kb 3’ of Sox2, could drive otic expression in E10.5 transgenic embryos. In collaboration with Hisato Kondoh (Osaka University) we identified 3 conserved elements within this region that could drive transgene expression that recapitulated the endogenous otic Sox2 expression.

761910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
761910.value: Our results lead us to hypothesise that Sox2 and BMP/TGFβ signaling function antagonistically to coordinate development of sensory and non-sensory structures in the correct location in the inner ear. This antagonism is regulated at transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels. This discovery forms the basis of further research to address the hypotheses and obtain mechanistic insights into the molecular link between Sox2 and BMP/TGFβ signaling in controlling sensory versus non-sensory cell fate in the developing inner ear.

761910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
761910.value: One child out of 800 is born with hearing impairment and 60% of people over 70yrs suffer some hearing loss, often caused by the permanent loss of hair cells in the inner ear. Our study identified a master gene regulator, SOX2, that ensures the proper development of the stem cells responsible for the formation of sensory cells in the inner ear that are responsible for hearing and balance. We further provided insight into how expression of SOX2 is controlled and implicate another regulator, SMAD4 that acts to antagonistically to control the precise location of sensory cells in the inner ear. These discoveries are fundamental to long term strategies aimed at regenerative or reparative therapies for building a functional ear.

762010.label: Project Objectives
762010.value: 1. To define the mechanism by which NF90 regulates influenza virus replication. We have identified a physical interaction between NF90 and NP and have established that this interaction does not affect the interaction between NP and PB2. The present study will further investigate whether NF90 associates with the RNP complex through NP or if it interacts only with free NP molecules. 2. To conduct further mapping of the molecular domain of NP that interacts with NF90. We previously found that interaction with NF90 may involve the C-terminal of NP, using site mutagenesis. This study will map the region of NP which is targeted by NF90 in more detail. 3. To further characterize whether NF90 has a different effect on avian versus human influenza virus replication. NP has been suggested to play a role in host range restriction and it will be important to understand if host factors interact differentially with NP from viruses of different host origins. 4. To determine if the interaction between NF90 and NS1 is involved in the regulation of virus replication associated with the interaction of NF90 with NP.

762010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
762010.value: 核蛋白NF90调节流感病毒复制的分子基础 动物病毒通过病毒的适应性变异或重组形成大流行流感病毒。2009年的大流行流感H1N1病毒由人，猪和禽流感病毒重组产生。近年来，禽流感H5N1, H7N7 和H9N2病毒跨种传播引发人类感染也在一些国家发现。2009年的大流行H1N1流感病毒能在人群中有效传播但毒性不高，相反的，H5N1病毒传播力低但毒性很高。不同流感病毒的不同性质说明病毒与宿主之间的相互作用关系很复杂。病毒受体特异性并不能完全决定宿主的限制性，比如H9N2病毒已经具有人类细胞的受体结合能力，但H9N2病毒感染人并不经常发生。我们现在还不知道2009年的大流感病毒是否已经在人群流行了一段时间才发生大流行，因为猪流感病毒也不经常感染人。所以，宿主对病毒其它功能的障碍也很大程度限制了流感病毒的跨种传播。 我们知道宿主因子与流感病毒复制的作用在病毒的适应性和致病性有紧密的关系。利用蛋白组学技术，我们的研究发现和鉴定了一些同流感病毒不同功能相互作用的蛋白，其中的一个蛋白，NF90，直接与病毒的核糖蛋白，NP，直接作用，并通过干扰病毒的复制体系抑制病毒繁殖。然而，NF90如何通过与NP的作用调节病毒繁殖和病毒如何逃逸细胞的抑制还不清楚。另外，我们的研究还发现NF90与病毒的NS1蛋白相互作用。所以，我们提出这样的一个假设，尽管细胞通过NF90限制流感病毒繁殖，病毒的NS1可能通过与NF90的作用拮抗这种抑制。我们的结果还发现NF90对不同宿主来源的流感病毒有不同的抑制效果。因为NP被认为具有决定病毒宿主的作用，所以确定NF90的宿主决定性也意义重大。综上所述，本研究将鉴定NF90调节流感病毒繁殖的分子基础并提供理解病毒与宿主限制作用新视野。

762010.label: Major findings and research outcome
762010.value: PKR plays an essential role for the innate immunity to viral infectin. Phosphorylation of PKR is required for activation of its function and can be regulated by other host RNA binding proteins besides dsRNA. We confirmed interaction between NF90 and PKR and found that low concentrations of NF90 restore some PKR activity in response to poly(I:C) induction in NF90 stably knocked-down cells. However, when high concentrations of NF90 were introduced by transfection, PKR phosphorylation was inhibited in these cells. Furthermore, the results showed that the inhibitory effect is exerted by the dsRNA binding domain, presumably through competition with PKR for dsRNA ligand in an RNA binding dependent manner. Our results suggest that a physiological concentration of NF90 is required for optimal activation of PKR in response to stimuli such as cellular dsRNA or intermediate dsRNA products generated during virus replication. Because PKR phosphorylation can activate downstream antiviral cascades including NF-kB and inflammasomes, it is postulated that NF90 may serve as a regulator for PKR activation in response to cellular dsRNA stimuli or virus infection. Our findings suggest a mechanism in which NF90 may act to regulate PKR activity in cells through balancing PKR phosphorylation in response to dsRNA via its N- and C-terminal functions. The PKR activation function of NF90 lies in the N-terminal region. On the other hand, interaction between NF90 and PKR may also modulate the activation of PKR through competition with dsRNA via its C-terminal RNA binding domain; this was also reported previously in an in vitro study. Activation of PKR is required for the formation of stress granules in response to virus infection. We found that NF90 and Rap55 are regularly associated with stress granules formed in response to treatments with oxidative substances (arsenite) or dsRNA mimics. It was further demonstrated that NF90 may be required for the formation of stress granules in the dsRNA induced host response, as there is a significant reduction in the levels of stress granules formed in response to ds-RNA treatment in NF90 stably knocked-down cells. We proved that NF90’s association with stress granules is coupled with its ability to interact with PKR and regulate its activation. To further verify the linkage between NF90 and PKR signaling in the host antiviral response we generated an influenza A virus specifically mutated in the NS1 gene which is attenuated in its ability to inhibit PKR activation, but otherwise functions normally. We found that NP of this mutant is targeted to stress granules, presumably through interaction with NF90 and/or other NP interacting proteins. Using this PKR specific virus model, this study clearly demonstrated that this mutant virus is able to replicate to a similar level to wild type virus in NF90 knockdown cells, but not in scrambled control cells or in Vero cells, which are deficient in expression of IFN-b. Our experiments also showed that this specific mutant virus is able to inhibit interferon-β expression just as wild type virus does, but that the R38A mutant which has lost RNA binding ability is attenuated in terms of suppression of interferon. These lines of evidence strongly support the hypothesis that NF90 antiviral function is signaled through the PKR pathway. Details please find in research output file 2 (Mok B et al., 2012) and 4 (Wen X et al., 2014).

762010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762010.value: Further studies are needed to unveil the molecular details of regulatory loop of the NF90-PKR pathway. Host innate immunity relies on pattern recognition receptors (PRRs), which reside mostly in the cytosol or cellular membranes, to recognize pathogen associated molecule patterns (PAMPs) which are usually intermediate products generated from the viral replication process. Because NF90 predominantly resides in the nucleus, it would be important to examine if NF90 is a yet to be defined nuclear pattern recognition receptor (PRR), like IFI16.

762010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762010.value: The double stranded RNA (dsRNA)-dependent protein kinase PKR plays an essential role in the innate immunity to viral infection. How PKR is activated is not fully understood. This study identified NF90 as key factor in the regulation of PKR activation. We found that activation of PKR leads to the phosphorylation of eIF2 and subsequently triggers formation of stress granules which involve both NF90 and PKR. We further characterized that physiological level of NF90 is essential required for PKR activation in response to virus infection and phosphorylation of NF90 by PKR is required for NF90-PKR signaling to induce antiviral stress granules. NF90 is a nuclear protein and we found that NF90 is phosphorylated by PKR and retained in the cytoplasm during the NF90-PKR interaction. Our finding concluded that NF90 and PKR are mutually regulated to maintain the balance of antiviral state in cells. We presented a novel model for the regulation of PKR innate immunity. In that, an accumulation of NF90 in the cytoplasm may subsequently compete with PKR for dsRNA binding and thereby form a feedback loop to restore PKR back to its latent form and, similarly, NF90 would then be recycled back to the nucleus after the stimuli dissipates.

762610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
762610.value: 食管癌是一種世界範圍內廣泛分佈的癌症，並具有高發病率（世界第八位）和高死亡率（世界第六位）的特點。而食管鱗狀上皮細胞癌，作爲食管癌的主要組織學類型之一，其發病率在亞洲地區包括中國大陸和香港等地尤其高。儘管現代醫療技術有了很大進步，但是食管癌的致死率依然居高不下。對於惡性程度高和轉移性的食管癌，依然缺乏有效的治療手段。所以，深入了解對食管癌的發生和發展過程起關鍵作用的基因以及信號通路，對新的治療藥物和方法至關重要。 近期一個受到關注的觀點認爲，腫瘤細胞分泌的生長因子和細胞因子通過自分泌、旁分泌以及內分泌的方式，影響腫瘤微環境和身體內部環境，最終對腫瘤的發生和發展起到重要的調控作用；尤其是腫瘤發展後期，當腫瘤細胞廣泛轉移，自分泌方式更是起到了主導作用。磷脂酰肌醇3 激酶(phosphatidylinositol 3 kinase , PI3K) / 蛋白激酶B (Akt) 作爲一個重要的信號通路，廣泛調節腫瘤細胞的增值、存活、血管生成、浸潤和轉移。我們之前報道過，在食管癌中過量表達的致癌基因 Id1 (分化因子1）可以激活這個信號通路，從而促進了食管癌細胞的生長和轉移。我們通過初步實驗證明，腫瘤細胞分泌的IGF2 (胰島素樣生長因子2) 在這個激活過程起了重要的介導作用。Id1，IGF2 以及IGF2的受體 IGF1R (胰島素生長因子1受體) 的表達水平和食管癌的分期，轉移以及預後相關。根據現有的文獻和初步實驗數據，我們認爲：食管癌細胞産生的IGF2能通過自分泌和內分泌系統激活磷脂酰肌醇3 激酶/蛋白激酶B，從而促進腫瘤的生長和轉移；而阻斷這個信號通路或可以抑制腫瘤的發展。爲了驗證我們的假說，我們將會用過量表達Id1 的食管癌細胞作爲實驗模型，去研究腫瘤細胞産生的 IGF2對磷脂酰肌醇3 激酶/蛋白激酶B信號通路的調節作用，以及對腫瘤的生長、存活和浸潤的影響。我們計劃通過體外和體內實驗研究Id1調控IGF2的機制，並最終證實腫瘤細胞分泌的IGF2在食管癌的發生和發展中的重要性。阻斷這一信號通路可能爲食管癌的臨床治療提供更多的用藥選擇。

762610.label: Realisation of objectives
762610.value: Objective 1: Using a combination of ChIP and bioinformatics methodologies, we confirmed that the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway is indeed involved in the regulation of IGF2 by Id1, but in a more intricate manner than we originally hypothesized. Instead of Id1 competing with IGF2 for interaction with proteasome subunit S5A, we found that important cell cycle regulators including E2F1 and Cdc20 were involved in this regulatory network. Our results showed that there are interactions among Id1, Cdc20 and E2F1, and that competitive binding between Id1 and Cdc20 induces E2F1 and transcriptional activation of IGF2. This objective has been achieved, but we are waiting for in vivo data (which will increase the impact) to be included in a manuscript (entitled “Id1 confers chemoresistance and cancer cell stemness by competitive binding with Cdc20 to release E2F1 for transcriptional activation of IGF2”) describing this novel mechanism and its biological significance in the context of chemoresistance and cancer stem cells (see attached). The target journal is Journal of Clinical Investigation. Objective 2: This objective was successfully achieved. Conditioned media from ESCC cell lines with ectopic expression of Id1, co-expression of Id1 and shIGF2, or empty vector were used to treat untransfected ESCC cells. Then MTT, wound healing and cell invasion assays were carried out to study the effect of Id1-induced IGF2 on cell proliferation, survival, migration and invasion potentials. Objective 3: This objective was accomplished using in vivo models. To study the effect of Id1-induced IGF2 on tumorigenicity, subcutaneous ESCC xenografts with Id1 overexpression, co-expression of Id1 and shIGF2, or empty vectors were compared for their ability to instigate tumor formation from parental ESCC cells injected into the contralateral flank of nude mice. To study the effect of Id1-induced IGF2 on metastasis, the ability of these subcutaneous tumors to promote metastasis of intravenously injected parental ESCC cells were compared. Lung metastasis was monitored using bioluminescent imaging. Objective 4: This objective was accomplished using Cixutumumab (developed by ImClone Systems) which is a fully human antibody targeting the IGF1R receptor. The in vivo tumorigenicity and experimental metastasis assays described in Objective 3 above were used to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of the antibody on tumor growth and metastasis of ESCC cells, as proposed in original research plan. In addition, we tested the efficacy of Cixutumumab in sensitizing human ESCC tumors to conventional chemotherapeutics 5-fluoruracil (5-FU) and cisplatin.

762610.label: Major findings and research outcome
762610.value: (i) Id1 induces IGF2 expression and secretion in human cancer: Stable and transient transfection experiments showed that Id1 induced the production and secretion of IGF2 in a variety of human cancer cells. Immunohistochemical study of human ESCC tissue microarray showed upregulation of Id1 and IGF2 in a high percentage of ESCC and a positive correlation between IGF2 and Id1 expression. (ii) IGF2 is a crucial autocrine and endocrine factor that mediates the activation of PI3K/AKT by Id1 in ESCC: Our results showed that Id-induced IGF2 secreted from ESCC cells could enhance the ability of ESCC cells to proliferate, migrate and survive. In vivo, IGF2 secreted by Id1-expressing tumors exerted endocrine influence to instigate the growth of less aggressive tumors at a distant site through activation of PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, and to facilitate metastatic colonization of disseminated cancer cells. (iii) Blockade of IGF2/IGF1R signaling has therapeutic potential in the management of esophageal cancer: We proved that targeting IGF2 and IGF1R with neutralizing antibodies had significant suppressive effects on tumor growth and metastasis in mice. Treatment with IGF1R antibody, Cixutumumab, enhanced the chemosensitivity of tumor xenografts to fluorouracil and cisplatin. The findings under points (i) to (iii) were reported in Clinical Cancer Research (see Part C). (iv) Id1 confers 5-FU chemoresistance through E2F1-dependent induction of thymidylate synthase (TS) expression in ESCC cells: We found that ectopic Id1 expression significantly increased TS expression and enhanced the resistance of ESCC cells to 5-FU, whereas knockdown of Id1 reduced TS and restored the sensitivity of chemoresistant cells to 5-FU. These effects were abrogated by E2F1 knockdown and overexpression, respectively. (v) IGF2 plays an important role in acquired chemoresistance and maintenance of stem cell properties: Our in vitro and in vivo experiments showed that IGF2-knockdown not only markedly enhanced sensitivity of ESCC cells and tumor xenografts to 5-FU treatment, but also significantly inhibited sphere-formation, self-renewal, expression of stemness markers, and tumor-initiating abilities of ESCC cells. (vi) Id1 increases IGF2 transcription by competitive binding with Cdc20 to protect E2F1 from protein degradation: Immunoprecipitation experiments showed that excessive Id1-Cdc20 interaction prevented Cdc20 from binding to E2F1, thus protecting E2F1 protein from degradation. Bioinformatics analysis, ChIP, dual luciferase reporter assay, and Western blot experiments convincingly established that E2F1, induced by Id1, could directly activate IGF2 transcription. The findings under points (iv) to (vi) are included in a manuscript in preparation for submission to Journal of Clinical Investigation (see Part C).

762610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762610.value: (i) We extended our study to investigate the paracrine effects of Id1-induced IGF2 in the tumor microenvironment, and successfully obtained a RGC GRF grant in 2011-12. (ii) Having confirmed that Id1 has important roles in esophageal cancer progression and chemoresistance, we have applied for RGC GRF in 2014-15 to study the mechanisms of its upregulation, in particular in terms of microRNAs that target Id1. (iii) In the course of this study, we established several 5-FU-resistant cell lines which can serve as cell models for identification of important genes/pathways involved in the mechanisms of chemoresistance. We have obtained seed funding from HKU to generate a database of chemoresistance-associated genes through genome-wide gene profiling of 5-FU-resistant cells. Genes of interest will be selected for further study We have obtained useful preliminary data and have applied for a NSFC grant this year. (iv) Having established that IGF2 plays an important role in maintenance of cancer cell stemness, we proceeded to study its effect on CD133, a marker commonly used to identify cancer stem cells. We found that IGF2 induced CD133 expression through regulation of miR-377. A manuscript incorporating these results is in preparation for submission to Cancer Research (see Part C).

762610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762610.value: Esophageal cancer ranks as the 6th most frequent cause of cancer death in the world. Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is the predominant form of esophageal cancer in Hong Kong, mainland China and throughout the Asia-Pacific region. There is an urgent need for a better understanding of the underlying mechanisms to develop more effective therapeutic strategies for this highly lethal disease. This study uncovers an autocrine/endocrine link between Id1 and the PI3K/AKT pathway involving insulin-like growth factor 2 (IGF2) and its receptor IGF1R, which promotes esophageal cancer growth, metastasis, and chemoresistance. We found that systemic treatment with cixutumumab, an IGF1R neutralizing antibody, can significantly inhibit esophageal cancer growth and metastasis, as well as sensitize tumor xenografts to fluorouracil and cisplatin treatment in animal models. Cixutumumab is currently investigated in clinical trials for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma. Our study therefore provides important preclinical data supporting the clinical application of cixutumumab therapy both as a single agent and in combination with conventional chemotherapeutic drugs. We have also unraveled a novel mechanism in which Id1 protects the E2F1 transcription factor from degradation, thus enabling it to bind directly to IGF2 gene promoter and increase IGF2 expression.

763310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
763310.value: Underdevelopment of the mandible, or lower jaw, can result in a misaligned bite, airway obstruction, and aesthetic problems, which have a negative psychological impact on the patient. Surgical advancement of the mandible by sagittal split osteotomy is the traditional technique of choice, but it can result in a high incidence of neurosensory deficit, as well as relapse in cases of moderate to large mandibular advancement. An alternative procedure - distraction osteogenesis - is to move the lower jaw gradually by 1 mm per day using a special mechanical traction device attached to the bone. Since 1992, this technique has been applied with clinical success in the treatment of severely recessed mandibles that require moderate to large advancement. So far, however, no prospective clinical studies have been done to compare the two types of surgery. The aim of this study will thus be to conduct a prospective randomized controlled trial comparing the treatment outcomes of the current standard method of sagittal split osteotomy with those of distraction osteogenesis. Sixty patients with moderate to severe mandibular underdevelopment will be selected and randomly divided into two groups for treatment. One group will receive bilateral sagittal split osteotomy and the other will receive bilateral mandibular distraction osteogenesis. The investigation will focus on the following outcome measures: morbidity, psychological impact, and quality of life, as assessed by questionnaires; stability of the advancement, as assessed by radiographic analyses; neurosensory function, as assessed by objective and subjective neurosensory tests; biting function in terms of changes in maximum bite force, biting contact area, jaw movement, and muscle activity; airway changes, via cone-beam computed tomography; and jawbone changes, via cone-beam computed tomography and the Helkimo index. In addition, the aesthetic outcome will be assessed photographically using 3-dimensional digital photogrammetry. The results of this study will clarify several current dilemmas in decision-making when clinicians consider which of the two treatments to use when managing moderate to severe mandibular recession. Furthermore, patients will be better informed on the pros and cons of each treatment method during the consent procedure. 下颌骨发育不足引起的下颌后缩畸形可导致咬合紊乱和气道阻塞，并且影响外形，从而对患者造成不良的心理影响。 通过矢状劈开截骨前徙下颌骨是矫正下颌后缩畸形的传统手术方法，但其具有较高的下齿槽神经损伤风险，而且对于一些下颌前徙距离较大的患者容易出现术后复发。牵引成骨是利用一种特殊的机械装置，每天1mm缓慢移动骨块而前徙下颌骨，这是治疗下颌后缩畸形的另一方法。1992年以来，牵引成骨技术临床治疗中度和重度下颌后缩畸形已获得成功。但迄今为止，尚未有前瞻性研究对牵引成骨和矢状劈开截骨两种术式进行比较。 本研究的目的是通过前瞻性随机分组临床试验比较矢状劈开截骨和牵引成骨两种术式的治疗效果。将60例中度和重度的下颌后缩畸形患者随机分为两组，一组接受双侧下颌骨矢状劈开截骨术，另一组接受双侧下颌骨牵引成骨术。研究的主要评价指标包括：手术并发症；心理影响；问卷分析生存质量；影像学分析下颌骨前徙的稳定性；主观及客观评价下齿槽神经功能；最大合力变化、咬合接触面积和肌肉运动情况分析咬合功能；CT分析气道改变情况；CT及Helkimo指数分析术后颞下颌关节改变情况。此外还应用三维数码成像技术分析术后外形。 本研究结果将为如何选择牵引成骨和矢状劈开截骨治疗中度和重度下颌后缩畸形提供依据，而且也有利于患者在知情同意过程中更好地理解两种术式的利与弊。

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
763310.value: This is the first randomized controlled trial (RCT) to compare distraction osteogenesis and orthognathic surgery in the treatment of mandibular retrognathia for patients with Class II dentofacial deformity. The results of the study will have important clinical implications, especially in helping to elucidate differences in these two surgical techniques, which are currently of great concern to both surgeons and patients. The study will also provide insight into the long-term success of both surgical techniques.

763410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
763410.value: 神经嵴(NC)细胞源于背神经管上皮细胞是一种短暂出现的多功能干细胞，它会成为间叶细胞然后和周围的细胞分层以游离向边缘，在那里它们有助于颅面结构以及周围神经系统的形成.因此成功的分层是一个重要的步骤对于神经嵴(NC)细胞去获得运动性能和随后的分化过程.在分层的过程中, 神经嵴(NC)细胞经历了一个上皮间质转化（EMT），失去了它上皮细胞的结构特征和于周围细胞的黏附能力成为了具有移动能力的间叶细胞.根据基因突变在上皮间质转化（EMT）过程当中经常会导致相应的先天性缺失, 因此在神经嵴(NC)细胞形态转换过程中适当的遗传调控必须到位. 神经嵴(NC)细胞在经历分层过程中需要协调信号分子和转录因子. 先前的证据说明BMP和Wnt信号参与了调控神经嵴(NC)细胞的起始分层过程. 抑制这些信号(BMP和Wnt)会削弱神经嵴(NC)细胞分层但是不会影响能赋予神经嵴(NC)细胞性质的基因Sox9和Snail2的表达,这表明了这些因子(Sox9 和Snail2)和神经嵴(NC)细胞分层无关.这一概念和我们之前的报告表明Sox9协同Snail2调节神经嵴(NC)细胞的诱导和分层是矛盾的. 我们最近的调查结果提出了一个可能性去解释这个问题.我们发现了小泛蛋白样修饰蛋白(small ubiquitin-like modifier, SUMO)修饰和PKA磷酸化Sox9基因似乎是协调和赋予其能力与Snail2合作从而管理神经嵴(NC)细胞的分层. 这些数据提出一种可能性，即BMP或Wnt信号的失活可能抑制磷酸化和小泛蛋白样修饰蛋白修饰Sox9基因, 从而使Sox9失去了和Snail2合作开启神经嵴(NC)细胞的分层的能力.在这个项目中,我们的目标是探讨翻译后修饰Sox9基因在调控神经嵴(NC)细胞的分层中的作用，其重点是：(1)是否小泛蛋白样修饰蛋白修饰和磷酸化Sox9基因是协调的而且足够去开启神经嵴(NC)细胞的分层; (2)这些基因修饰怎样赋予Sox9能力去促进神经嵴(NC)细胞的分层; (3)是否BMP和Wnt信号参与了Sox9基因的翻译后修饰. 我们所提出的研究将提供一种新的见解关于Sox9基因的翻译后修饰促成神经嵴(NC)细胞的分层以及这些基因修饰怎样协同和结合信号网络导致神经嵴(NC)细胞的分层.

763410.label: Realisation of objectives
763410.value: We have addressed objectives 1.1 and 1.2 by showing that ectopic expression of constitutive SUMOylated form of Sox9 or phosphomimetic mutant (Sox9S64D,S181D) is able to induce neural crest delamination like wild-type (WT) Sox9, suggesting that SUMOylation or phosphorylation of Sox9 is sufficient for promoting neural crest delamination. Moreover, we also found that phosphorylation of both S64 and S181 resides are required for Sox9 SUMOylation but not vice versa. To investigate whether protein kinase A (PKA) is involved in this process, we examined the phosphorylation and SUMOylation levels of Sox9 in the presence of a constitutive active PKA (CA-PKA) or a dominant negative form of PKA (DN-PKA). We found Sox9 SUMOylation was enhanced by CA-PKA and substantially reduced by DN-PKA without significantly altering the levels of Sox9 phosphorylation, suggesting that PKA is not required for Sox9 phosphorylation but it does enhance SUMOylation. We have also completed objective 2.1 by showing that both phosphorylation and to a lesser extent SUMOylation, confer the ability of Sox9 protein to initiate neural crest delamination. We further demonstrated that phosphorylation of Sox9 is required to interact with Snail2 in vivo and cooperate with it to trigger delamination. However, we still failed to address objective 2.2 using in ovo Snail2-promoter driven luciferase reporter as a readout to examine the transcriptional capacity of various SUMO- and/or phospho-mutant and mimic versions of Sox9 either alone or with Snail2. We consistently obtained low reporter reading with large variation between samples and replicates. We made another reporter consisting of a concatemer of four Snail2 promoters in order to enhance the sensitivity but still failed to obtain robust activation response. Nevertheless, all point mutant constructs are capable of inducing robust ectopic HNK-1 expression upon misexpression. In objective 2.3, by candidate approach, we identified Nedd9 and DLC1 as the potential downstream targets of Sox9 and work is underway to investigate how they mediate Sox9 function (please see 6.2 for details). We have completed objective 3 by showing that the ability of Sox9 to be phosphorylated and SUMOylated were abolished upon inhibition of BMP and canonical Wnt signaling by Smad6 and β-cantenin-engrailed repressor (β-cat-EnR) respectively, whereas activation of BMP or canonical Wnt signaling pathway using a constitutively active BMP receptor 1A (CA-BMPR-1A) or TCF-VP16 increased the phosphorylation and SUMOylation of Sox9. These data suggest that BMP and canonical Wnt signaling are both sufficient and required for Sox9 phosphorylation and SUMOylation.

763410.label: Major findings and research outcome
763410.value: In this study, we established that, in the developing chick neural tube, both endogenous and ectopic expression of Sox9 can be phosphorylated and SUMOylated and phosphorylation of Sox9 on S64 and S181 residues facilitates its SUMOylation partly due to its capability to interact with a SUMO-conjugation enzyme, UBC9. By in ovo electroporation, we demonstrated that ectopic Sox9 protein lacking phosphorylation and/or SUMOylation is able to induce neural crest cell fate at the expense of neural progenitor specification but non-phosphorylatable version of Sox9 (Sox9S64A,S181A) fail to initiate efficient trunk neural crest delamination. Both phosphorylation, and to a lesser extent SUMOylation, of Sox9 results in a physical interaction between Snail2 and Sox9, and Sox9 phosphorylation is necessary to cooperate with Snail2 to trigger neural crest delamination. Moreover, both BMP and canonical Wnt signaling are sufficient and required for Sox9 phosphorylation and SUMOylation thereby connecting extracellular signals with the delamination of neural crest cells. Altogether, these data indicate that BMP and canonical Wnt signaling initiate neural crest cell delamination by inducing the phosphorylation of Sox9 and its cooperation with Snail2. Our findings were presented both in the local and international conferences and published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America in Feb 2013. Please refer to Part C for details.

763410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
763410.value: Our findings have led us to address the next key issue of how the transcriptional outcome of phosphorylated form of Sox9 result in initiating neural crest delamination and migration. By candidate approach, we found Nedd9 (neural precursor cell expressed, developmentally downregulated 9), an intracellular scaffolding protein of the Cas family, is expressed in the premigratory and delaminating neural crest cells and can be induced by Sox9 regardless of its phosphorylation status, and Sox9 depends on Nedd9 to mediate the transition of neural crest cells from delamination to migration via switching from RhoA to Rac1 GTPase activities. This switching appears to be mediated by a Rho GTPase activating protein (RhoGAP), DLC1 (Deleted in liver cancer 1), which is also expressed in the premigratory and delaminating neural crest cells and induced by Sox9 but not Sox9S64A,S181A. In addition, the RhoGAP activity of DLC1 depends on Nedd9 function. These preliminary data have been submitted for the current round of early career scheme grant application aiming to further characterize the mode of action of DLC1 in neural crest development. Our proposed studies will reveal a novel molecular network linking the transcriptional outcome of phosphorylated form of Sox9 and neural crest migratory capacity.

763410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
763410.value: Cell migration is crucial to the formation of organs and tissues in distinct location during embryonic development. The neural crest is among the best-studied embryonic migrations. These cells arise from the top of the neural tube, detach and migrate to various locations of the embryo to form bone, cartilage, neurons, glia and pigment cells. Proper genetic control to initiate neural crest detachment and migration is therefore essential for the generation of various tissues. Consequently, defective regulation of cell migration results in developmental disorders. In this study, we extended our previous findings of a developmental regulator, Sox9, in conferring neural crest cells with migratory capacity by showing that two signaling molecules, BMP and Wnt, regulate the addition of two phosphate residues to Sox9 protein essential for cooperating with another regulator, Snail2, to initiate efficient detachment of neural crest cells from the neural tube. Considering this detachment occurs in a manner similar to the spread of tumor cells in which Sox9 and Snail2 are also essential, our data suggest that Sox9 and Snail2 may play a conserved role in regulating cell motility in both normal and pathological conditions.

763710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
763710.value: 法樂氏四聯症是最常見的紫紺型先天性心臟病。目前，無論在香港還是其他地方，幾乎所有伴有這種畸形出生的嬰兒都可以存活至成年。因此，修復手術後的法樂氏四聯症的青少年和成年患者的人數逐年增加。心室間的相互作用伴隨著雙心室功能不全，與發病率和死亡率有密切關係，而成為焦點問題。因術後肺動脈返流而出現的右心室擴張和功能障礙已經被充分證明了，而左心室功能障礙作為一個可惡化長期結局的風險因素的重要性，最近被越來越多的意識到。然而，心室間相互作用的機制尚不明。已知兩個心室的心肌間存在相互影響而且共用一個室間隔，因此，右心室容量負荷過重可能通過改變左室心肌的線性和扭轉的變形方式，來損傷左心室的功能。我們假設，外科手術修復後的法樂氏四聯症患者的心室的相互作用，是因右室容量超負荷導致異常左室線性和扭轉變形。新近的三維斑點追蹤超聲心動圖，可以以三維向量方向同時成像並追蹤左心室所有節段的斑點運動，為我們提供了一個機會從全新的視角來審視心室間相互作用的機械力學原理。該研究的目的是檢驗這一假設：外科手術修復後的法樂氏四聯症患者的心室的相互作用，是右室容量超負荷導致異常左室線性和扭轉變形，而且左室心肌變形能力的改變可以影響運動能力及左室整體功能。我們嘗試解決的主要問題包括：i) 右心室容量負荷過重對左室三維收縮形變和扭轉的影響；ii) 改變了的左室三維應變和扭轉對運動能力和左室整體功能的影響；iii) 手術修復後的法樂氏四聯症患者的肺動脈瓣置換對左室變形能力的影響。就我們所知，本研究是首次量化左室心肌的三維形變，並有助於瞭解伴有或未有肺動脈瓣置換的法樂氏四聯症患者修復術後心室間相互作用的力學機制，及幫助出現了繼發於術後肺動脈瓣返流的右心室輕度擴張的無症狀病人選擇手術方式、決定肺動脈瓣置換的時機。

763710.label: Realisation of objectives
763710.value: Using novel three-dimensional (3D) speckle tracking echocardiography, we evaluated comprehensively the true 3D deformation and torsional mechanics of the left ventricle in a relatively large cohort of patients (n=76) after surgical repair of tetralogy of Fallot. The repaired tetralogy of Fallot patients comprised two groups: i) those without additional pulmonary valve replacement, and ii) those with pulmonary valve replacement to ameliorate pulmonary regurgitation. The inclusion of these two subgroups allowed us to answer further the question of whether pulmonary valve replacement has an impact on the altered LV mechanics in the long-term. The possible mechanism of abnormal ventricular-ventricular interaction through the ventricular septum was explored by evaluating the influence of altered septal curvature, secondary to right ventricular volume overload, on LV mechanics and global LV ejection fraction. Exercise capacity of patients were evaluated by formal cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Based on the aforementioned, both of the objectives of the study were achieved. The findings led to the conclusion, as described in our paper accepted for publication (see part C), that adverse 3D LV mechanics characterized by impaired global and regional 3D systolic strain, mechanical dyssynchrony, and reduced twist is related to reduced septal curvature in repaired tetralogy of Fallot patients with and without pulmonary valve replacement.

763710.label: Major findings and research outcome
763710.value: This is the first study to interrogate left ventricular (LV) mechanics in repaired tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) patients with and without pulmonary valve replacement using new 3D speckle tracking echocardiography. Novel findings of the present study include 1) adverse 3D LV mechanics as characterized by impaired global and regional 3D systolic strain, mechanical dyssynchrony, and reduced twist adjusted for LV length in repaired TOF patients with significant pulmonary regurgitation and even in those after PVR, 2) strong associations between septal curvature and 3D indices of LV mechanics, and 3) potential usefulness of a newly proposed 3D global performance index in the comprehensive evaluation of LV dysfunction in patients.

763710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
763710.value: There are two important areas for further development: i) The proposed new 3D global performance index that incorporates the three important parameters of left ventricular (LV) mechanics, i.e. peak global 3D strain, LV twist gradient, and LV mechanical dyssynchrony may supercede previously used indices of LV global function. Indeed, based on the results of this study, we had extrapolated the use of this index in childhood cancer survivors and reported its high sensitivity in detection of impaired LV function (Yu et al. J Am Soc Echocardiogr. 2013;26:846-852). Further applications of this index in patients at risk of subclinical LV dysfunction are expected. ii) Longitudinal monitoring of indices of 3D mechanics in a larger patient cohort to track the changes of LV performance before and after implantation of the pulmonary valve may help to shed more light on the still controversial question of optimal timing for pulmonary valve replacement.

763710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
763710.value: This research project aims to answer the question of why the left and right hearts interact abnormally and the effect of abnormal left heart function in patients after repair of a common type of congenital heart disease called tetralogy of Fallot. The right heart usually enlarges after operation due to backflow of blood from the lung with loss of pulmonary valve integrity. We found that right heart enlargement may also affect left heart function through distortion of the ventricular septum, the wall separating the left and right hearts. As a result, shortening and twisting of muscles of the left heart are affected and their contraction also becomes asynchronous. This is significant as global function of the left heart and the exercise capacity of the patients would be affected. Furthermore, this provides a basis for the need to replace the pulmonary valve to prevent backflow of blood from the lung and to normalize the size of the right heart. Additionally, a new index of global left heart function that takes into account of three important aspects, namely heart muscle shortening, twisting, and degree of coordinated contraction, has been proposed for future assessment of subtle heart dysfunction in other at-risk patient populations.

764510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
764510.value: Body fluid and salt balance is meticulously regulated by neural and endocrine systems. When there is a change in the volume or content of the extracellular fluid, these control systems enact immediate responses to counteract changes in order to bring the values back to within the physiological limits. As a consequence, an appropriate blood volume and blood pressure sufficient for optimal tissue perfusion by the heart was maintianed. Water/salt homeostasis is therefore one of the three fundamental issues, in addition to reproduction and growth/metabolism, in the study of life sciences. With previous supports from GRF, we found that secretin (SCT) can stimulate vasopressin (VP) synthesis and release in the hypothalamus, is a pituitary hormone, and after release, it can function in a concerted manner with VP to conserve water in the kidney. These observations not only confirmed the potential of SCT as a novel pituitary hormone released into circulation under water deprivation, but also provide explanations to abnormalities underlying certain types of diabetes insipidus in which VP release is normal but the kidney is not responsive to circulatory VP. Hence, SCT could be the long-sought VP-independent mechanism to solve the riddle that has puzzled clinicians and physiologists for decades. Future studies of SCT should provide a new target for prevention or therapeutic intervention for these disorders. Knowing that angiotensin II (ANGII) plays a pivotal role in initiating upstream osmoregulatory responses, the next key issue that remains unresolved is the neural mechanisms that mediate the functions of ANGII in the brain. Our preliminary data clearly showed that functional SCT and its receptor are indispensible in mediating actions of ANGII. In this proposal, we hypothesize that SCT is the missing link that connects ANGII with its central effects in the network of sites in higher brain to control downstream effects. Besides, in the past, little is understood regarding the regulation of sodium intake/appetite. The current proposal is therefore designed to investigate the potential role of SCT in regulating salt appetite in specific brain regions. This project may therefore be relevant to conditions associated with abnormal sodium appetite. For example, marked increases in sodium appetite are often observed in certain subsets of patients with hypertension and adrenal insufficiency, thus, identifying the mechanisms through which SCT modulate salt intake should contribute to a better understanding of the pathophysiology of hypertension. SCT antagonist and SCTR blocker should warrant further investigation as potential anti-hypertensive agents. 體液和鹽類平衡是通過神經及內分泌系統進行精密調節的。當細胞外液容量或成分發生改變時，這些調節系統發揮即時作用以抵消之前的變化，從而保持細胞外液容量及成分在生理限度內。為實現這一調節，需要維持適當的血壓及血容量，從而使外周組織得到來自心臟的適當血流灌注。水鹽體內平衡，同生殖，發育與新陳代謝一起，是生命科學研究的三個基本問題。在GRF支持下，我們的既往研究發現，促胰泌素(SCT)屬於垂體激素，它可以刺激下丘腦內血管加壓素(VP)的合成與分泌，還可以和血管加壓素協同促進腎臟的保水作用。這些發現不但證實了促胰泌素作為一種新的垂體激素，會在缺水狀態下釋放到循環中，而且可以解釋在特定類型糖尿病中出現的腎臟對循環中正常分泌的血管加壓素缺乏反應的異常現象。因此，促胰泌素可能是醫學和生理學家長期尋找的獨立於血管加壓素之外的另一調控機制。未來對促胰泌素的研究將提供預防或治療水鹽平衡失調的新目標。目前已知血管緊張素II(ANGII)在激發上游的滲透調節中起著關鍵作用，下一個未解決的關鍵問題是控制血管緊張素II腦部功能的神經調節機制。 我們的初步研究資料清楚顯示促胰泌素及其受體對調節血管緊張素-II的功能具有不可或缺的作用。在這份建議書中，我們假定促胰泌素是連接血管緊張素II在高等腦部的功能和其下游調控作用之間的紐帶。在過去，我們對於鈉鹽攝入調節機制知之甚少。故而當前研究著重於促胰泌素在特定腦部區域對鹽類攝入的潛在調控機制。這一項目將可能同鹽類攝入異常相關。例如，在特定類型高血壓並伴有腎上腺機能不全的病人中，經常可以觀察到鈉鹽攝入量的顯著增長。因此，研究促胰泌素調節鹽分攝入機制將有助於更好理解高血壓的病理生理學。促胰泌素拮抗劑和促胰泌素受體阻斷劑，作為潛在抗高血壓新藥，值得進一步研究。

764510.label: Realisation of objectives
764510.value: In objective 1, we confirmed the involvement of SCT in lamina terminalis in response to dehydration and/or ANGII by: 1) i.c.v. ANGII stimulated cFos expression in all sites of the lamina terminals in wild-type (WT) animals, but the activated cFos expression was reduced in SCT-/- and SCTR-/- mice; 2) immunohistochemical and in situ hybridization demonstrated the expression SCT and SCTR in the lamina terminalis; 3) Using LCM-qPCR technique, we found that SCT and SCTR expression were significantly increased in SFO, OVLT and PVN under saline drinking, dehydration or i.c.v. ANGII treatments. These data strongly suggest SCT play indispensable functions in regulating ANGII-mediated drinking behavior in rodents. More importantly, we demonstrated that the ANGII induced drinking was almost abolished in SFO-specific SCT knock-out mice. This further suggests that drinking behavior is mainly regulated by the release of SCT from SFO. In addition, by the overexpression, silencing, and binding assay (ChIP and EMSA), we confirmed the transcription factor, ERRα, is the important upstream regulator of the SCT gene in response to ANGII and hypertonic stimulations. In objective 2, we investigated the role of SCT in mediated VP expression and release. Our data suggested that salt loading and overnight dehydration significantly increased the expression of SCT and SCTR in the PVN as well as plasma SCT concentrations. The relationship between SCT and VP under dehydration was studied by (1) overnight water deprivation (dehydration) and (2) saline drinking experiments. As expected, after dehydration or saline drinking, drastically elevated VP expression in PVN and increased VP release from the neurohypophysis were observed in WT animals, but in contrast, no significant effect can be observed in SCT-/- and SCTR-/- mice. Taken together, this evidence supported our hypothesis that SCT is responsible for stimulating VP expression and VP release upon dehydration. In objective 3, our preliminary result shown that SCT-/- mice consumed less saline after dehydration. To further investigate the linkage between SCT and salt appetite, salt consumption were measured in mice after i.c.v. SCT. However, our result suggests that there is no significant different in salt appetite in i.c.v. SCT mice when compare to the control (i.c.v. PBS). This data confirms that the reduction of saline drinking in our preliminary results is not a direct effect of the central SCT.

764510.label: Major findings and research outcome
764510.value: As suggested in our proposal, secretin plays a key role in the ANG II-mediated control of drinking behavior. The knock-out of SCT/SCTR axis in mice abolished ANGII stimulated osmoregulatory function, including drinking, cFos expression in lamina terminals, and VP release from hypothalamus. We also found that SCT and SCTR expression were significantly increased in SFO, OVLT and PVN under saline drinking, dehydration or i.c.v. ANGII treatments. Therefore, our data suggested the role of SCT as the link between ANGII and its downstream effects. In addition, we provide evidence that estrogen-related receptor α (ERRα) acts as an upstream activator of the SCT gene. In vitro studies using mouse hypothalamic cell line N-42 show that ERRα upregulates SCT promoter and gene expression. More importantly, knockdown of endogenous ERRα abolishes SCT promoter activation in response to hypertonic and ANGII stimulations. In mouse brain, ERRα coexpresses with SCT in various osmoregulatory brain regions, including the lamina terminalis and the PVN of the hypothalamus, and its expression is induced by hyperosmotic and ANGII treatments. The results from this project were published in several publications (refer Part C).

764510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
764510.value: As shown in objective 3 of this project, central SCT is not involved in salt appetite control. The decrease of saline drinking in SCT-/- mice may be due to the indirect, peripheral action of SCT. For salt homeostasis, rennin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) has been studied for decades as one of the rapid regulating mechanisms. In this system, the salt homeostasis was well controlled by aldosterone from the adrenal glands, which regulate both the abundance and activity of epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) to increase sodium retention at the price of potassium excretion. In this project, we demonstrated the tight relationship between ANGII and SCT on drinking behavior and VP release mechanism. Based on this information, we speculate there are certain connections among ANGII, SCT and aldosterone. Therefore, we propose to study the role of SCT/SCTR axis on aldosterone secretion and possibly regulate sodium homeostasis through RAAS.

764510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
764510.value: Our body uses a complex neural and endocrine system to maintain the balance of water and salt. When there is a change in the volume or content of the extracellular fluid, these control systems enact immediate responses to counteract changes in order to bring the values back to within the physiological limits. Two hormones, angiotensin II (ANGII) and vasopressin (VP), are well known factors that regulate the body fluid and salt balance by controlling the drinking behavior and salt conservation. Recently, our research group demonstrated that another hormone, secretin (SCT), can stimulate VP production and release in brain. Therefore, in this project, we focused on the studies about the functional relationship between SCT and ANGII in regulating the drinking and VP production. Our data strongly suggest SCT play indispensable functions in regulating ANGII-mediated drinking behavior. We also confirmed the transcription mechanism that governs the expression of SCT after ANGII and hypertonic stimulations. We also provided evidence that SCT is responsible for stimulating VP production and release upon dehydration. Therefore, the present study, combining both neuroanatomical and functional approaches, provides useful information to demonstrate the role of SCT in the behavioral and physiological control systems for fluid balance maintenance.

765510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
765510.value: Population declines and extinctions of amphibians occurring at a global scale have complex local and regional causes. The Hong Kong newt (Paramesotriton hongkongensis) is currently categorized as globally Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List of endangered species and populations are considered to be declining. Given that only 14 breeding sites are known for this species in Hong Kong and not all of these sites occur on protected lands, there is significant potential for the loss of populations unless a conservation plan is developed and implemented. Unfortunately, fundamental information on the life history and population ecology of P. hongkongensis is lacking, thereby limiting our ability to protect this species. Our objectives are to study the life history, movements, and population ecology of P. hongkongensis in Hong Kong. We will: (1) characterize aquatic and terrestrial habitats, as well as breeding phenology,(2) use radio telemetry to track movements of newts and estimate home range sizes, (3) use mark-recapture techniques to estimate demographic vital rates and population sizes,(4) use geographic information systems to quantify core terrestrial habitats surrounding breeding sites, and (5) develop a demographic model to evaluate population-level effects of upland habitat loss on P. hongkongensis. Our findings will identify priority populations and critical habitats in order to provide a basis for conservation management action that will protect populations of P. hongkongensis in Hong Kong. 全球兩棲動物種群下降及滅絕，受複雜的本地及區域性因素所影響。香港瘰螈(Paramesotriton hongkongensis)已於國際自然保護聯盟瀕危種物種紅色名錄(IUCN)中被列為近危，其種群數目很可能正不斷下降。香港瘰螈於本港的已知繁殖地僅有十四個，而並非所有都位處於保護區內。除非有一個有效的保育計劃，否則其種群數量將有嚴重下降的可能。不幸地，我們對香港瘰螈之生活史及種群生態仍缺乏認識，以致我們不懂如何有效地保護此物種。本研究旨在了解本地的香港蠑螈之生活史、活動模式及其種群生態。我們將會(1) 描述其水中及陸上棲息地的特點，與其繁殖物候學 (Breeding Phenology)，(2) 利用無線電追蹤香港瘰螈的移動估算其活動範圍，(3) 利用標誌重捕法來估算香港瘰螈種群生存比率(Demographic Vital Rate)及種群大小，(4) 利用地理資訊系統 (GIS)來量化其繁殖地周邊的陸上生境，及(5) 開發一個種群模型以評估高地生境的破壞對香港瘰螈種群之影響。我們的研究將會識別需優先保護的危急種群及生境，作為對香港瘰螈未來的保育管理計劃之基礎。

765510.label: Realisation of objectives
765510.value: This study has been completed and all objectives have been achieved. Objective 1: We documented terrestrial and aquatic habitat use and movements for P. hongkongensis using transect searches and radio-telemetry. We estimated survival for each age class of P. hongkongensis using mesocosm studies, mark-recapture techniques, and demographic modeling. We determined sex and age class structure of populations. We estimated sizes of each population. Objective 2: Using geographic information systems and land cover data, we quantified habitat types and land use at the watershed-scale surrounding P. hongkongensis breeding sites. These data have been summarized for each site. Objective 3: Using data collected and demographic parameters estimated in objectives 1 (movements, demography) and 2 (habitat types and land use), we conducted population viability analyses to model a series of scenarios that reduced percent forest and shrub cover around new breeding sites to predict impacts of forest loss to P. hongkongensis populations. Objective 4: Based on the results of objective 4, we have developed a set of conservation recommendations for P. hongkongensis for the Hong Kong SAR Government. These recommendations focus on protection of forested habitats around P. hongkongensis breeding streams. Their submission to Government will need to await completion of the PhD thesis by RPG Anthony Lau, due later this year. Once all the results have been synthesized in that thesis, the specific recommendations will be forwarded to the Agriculture, Fisheries, and Conservation Department (AFCD) of HKSAR Government. Such action will be timely, as AFCD have the responsibility of formulating and implementing species action plans (e.g. for the Hong Kong newt) under the territory-wide Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan which is part of HK's international obligations as a signatory to the global Convention on Biodiversity (it should be added here that the PI is a member of the BSAP Steering Committee). It should also be noted that although Objectives 1-4 appear to be equivalent, we devoted most time to Objective 1, as it involved a multi-year study of newt population dynamics, following the fate (movement, survival, growth) of marked individuals over the course of several years. The results of some of that research was published by Fu et al. (2013), and a copy of that paper is attached in Section 8 of Part C of this report. Also addressing Objective 1, we used radio-tagging to assess habitat use of individual newts that were followed in the field during two years. This was extremely onerous and time-consuming work.

765510.label: Major findings and research outcome
765510.value: To investigate habitat use and movement pattern of P. hongkongensis (hereafter ‘newts’) during the terrestrial(non-breeding) phase, we conducted a radio telemetry study at three sites in Hong Kong and line transect surveys at two sites (Figure 1 – refers to Figures and Tables included as supplementary material in Section 11 of Part C). Fifty-four adults newts were implanted with VHF radio-transmitters and tracked for 2-77 days (mean = 18 days) in the wet seasons (April to July) of 2013 and 2014. Radio-tagged newts predominantly used forested macrohabitat with high canopy coverage. Microhabitats used by newts were characterized by high percentage cover of coarse woody debris, litter, and rocky substrate, where newts tended to occur beneath ground cover (e.g. leaf litter, branches, or Pandanus tectorius fronds) but never underground. Radio-tagged newts also never entered streams during the non-breeding period. The maximum distance in which a radio-tagged newt was detected from a stream was 480 m - substantially higher than previously supposed. However, the core terrestrial habitat of adult newts was estimated to average 61.2 m from water (Figure 2). Newt population demography was investigated by a multi-year mark-release-recapture study at four breeding sites representing four distinct populations (Figure 1 map). Population demographic parameters (annual survival rate, annual recruitment rate, population growth rate, population size, and sex ratio) were estimated using the multistate open robust design model in MARK software (Table 1). Three of four populations experienced population growth from 2007-2012, whereas one declined. A female-skewed sex ratio appeared to be linked to low recruitment rates, and consequently an overall decline in a population. This is surprising since egg supply, rather than proportions of males, might be expected to constrain recruitment. Eleven landscape-scale habitat features of 16 known breeding sites and 30 randomly selected non-breeding sites were quantified using a geographic information system to determine what features influence breeding site selection. The best approximating logistic regression model demonstrated that probability of a site being used for breeding by newts increases as percentage forest cover within 480 m increases (Table 2, Figure 3). This clearly indicates that maintaining forest cover is a prerequisite for newt conservation; preservation of riparian forest around Hong Kong streams is of critical importance. Population viability models confirmed that deforestation reduces the long-term viability of newt populations (Figure 5), and demonstrate that maintaining a 60-m buffer of intact riparian forest along streams where newts breed reduces extinction risk of populations.

765510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
765510.value: The relationship between percentage forest cover around breeding sites and annual survivorship of P. hongkongensis appears to be scale-dependent and warrants further investigation. At the core terrestrial habitat scale (within 60 m of streams or thereabouts), annual survivorship appears to decrease as percentage forest cover increases. However, at the landscape- or whole-population scale (within 480 m), the relationship appears hump-shaped, indicating that there is an intermediate amount of forest cover that maximizes survivorship. Our sample size must be expanded before this relationship is confirmed, although it implies that newts may do better in a mosaic landscape that includes forest rather than one that is forested entirely. The apparent absence of newts in Sai Kung and their relatively low abundance in Lautau Island, despite ample suitable habitat is intriguing. Our population genetic analyses demonstrate that the newts on Lantau Island are genetically distinct compared to the rest of Hong Kong. A thorough survey (possibly using environmental-DNA methods) should be carried out in Sai Kung and Lantau to better resolve the distribution and status of P. hongkongensis. Should vacant habitat be available for newts, translocation could be considered as a strategy for establishing new populations of this species of conservation concern.

765510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
765510.value: The Hong Kong newt occurs only in Hong Kong and Guangdong Province, and is a species of conservation concern. It breeds in streams during the dry season, spending the wet season in adjacent forest. We documented its habitat use, movements, and population dynamics, both in water and on land. We found that the newt is long lived (>8 years), returning year after year to breed in the same stream pools. Newts in Hong Kong have a highly fragmented distribution, and populations tend to be genetically isolated with some undergoing steep declines. Although the newt requires both streams and forest to complete its life cycle, we do not know how much forest the animals need. To find that out, we conducted statistical analyses to simulate how different levels of forest loss might impact populations, and related this to data on the movement of radio-tracked individuals. Newts spend most of their time in forest within about 60 m of streams and preferred areas that had >80% forest cover. However some newts moved almost 500 m from streams. We recommend that a protective buffer of at least 60 m of forest is needed around breeding streams to maintain newt populations.
