765810.label: Project Objectives
765810.value: Specific Aim 1: Study the single and combined effects of Fusarium toxins on the enterocyte-mediated defence responses. To evaluate the individual and combined effects of mycotoxins on the enterocytes –mediated defence mechanisms, we will study in vitro the effects of single and combined doses of these mycotoxins on a set of end points representing the main components of the enterocytes-mediated defence mechanisms that might be influenced by these toxins and are also a potential target for probiotics beneficial effects as demonstrated in figure 1. These endpoints include: A. Expression and localization of tight junction proteins (ZO-1, claudin1), transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) and transepithelial permeability as markers for the functionality of the intestinal barrier. B. Mucin secretion and MUC2 mRNA expression, expression of human β-defensin-2 (hBD-2), and expression of mRNA encoding for pro-inflammatory cytokines (including IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-12, IFN-γ and TNF-β) as markers for the modulatory effects on both innate and adaptive immunity. C. Activation of mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPK) as markers for the effects on signal transduction pathways of relevance to mycotoxins toxicity. Specific Aim 2: Assess association of pathogenic bacteria to the compromised enterocytes. We will investigate whether the modulation of barrier function, innate and adaptive immunity and signal transduction by the studied mycotoxins will interfere with the association of Salmonella typhimurium (S. typhimurium) to enterocytes. This study will provide useful information on whether these mycotoxins have additive or synergistic toxicity on these enterocytes. Specific Aim 3: Assess the ability of probiotics to beneficially modulate the unwanted effects induced by Fusarium toxins on the enterocyte-mediated defence responses. We will assess which specific probiotics and their microbial products can alter the toxicity of Fusarium toxin/s using the endpoints listed in Objective 1. The bacteria to be tested will initially include established probiotic strains selected to represent a wide array of species and genera and on the basis of their previously documented ability to modulate the local defence mechanisms of enterocytes.

765810.label: Realisation of objectives
765810.value: Despite the significant challenges faced during the term of this project, we have been able to realize all the objectives as listed in section 5.1. There are key findings from this project that may impact the future expansion of the current project. For example, our data clearly demonstrated individual and combined effects of four common Fusarium mycotoxins, DON, NIV, ZEA and FB1 on immunological defense mechanisms of intestinal epithelial cells using pro-inflammatory cytokine synthesis (IL1α, IL1β, IL6, IL8, TNFα and MCP-1), antimicrobial peptide (pBD-1 and pBD-2) synthesis and secretion on porcine intestinal epithelial IPEC-J2 cells, as well as secretory mucin (MUC5AC and MUC5B) synthesis and secretion on human intestinal epithelial cells (Caco-2) and mucin-producing cells (HT29-MTX) co-cultures as end-point measures. These Fusarium mycotoxins differentially modulated the synthesis and secretion of IL1α, IL1β, IL6, IL8, TNFα and MCP-1, pBD-1, pBD-2, as well as MUC5AC and MUC5B. Statistical analyses showed significant interactions between treatments would indicate that the addition of more than one mycotoxin has a non-additive effect (i.e. antagonism or synergy), whereas an observed lack of interaction would indicate additive effects. Results showed that additive effects were noted in most of the toxin mixtures. Therefore, these results provide evidence demonstrating that Fusarium toxins, individually and in mixtures, expressed different responses on intestinal immunological defense mechanism. Additionally, we demonstrated that spent culture supernatants of certain strains of probiotic bacteria, for example Lactobacillus GG (LGG) and E.coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) differently regulated secretory mucins MUC2, MUC5AC and MUC5B, as well as trefoil factor 3 in HT29-MTX cells. Metabolic products of LGG and EcN also modulated differently both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines profiles (IL1α, IL1β, IL4, IL5, IL6, IL8, IL10, IL13, TGF-α, IFN-γ, GM-CSF, MCP-1 and TNF-α secreted by HT29-MTX cells. These changes in mucins, trefoil factors and cytokines could be efficient in the management of the negative effects induced by Fusarium toxins on enterocyte-mediated defence responses.

765810.label: Major findings and research outcome
765810.value: Data from this project were utilized to the write up of 6 original manuscript (4 accepted and 2 under review) in addition to one review article (under review). Data from objectives 1 and 2 highlighting the individual and combined effects of DON, NIV, ZEA and FB1 on endpoints including cytotoxicity, antimicrobial peptides, proinflammatory cytokines and mucus, were submitted and accepted for publication in top tier journal (Q1) in the field of toxicology and microbiology namely; Toxicological Sciences, Toxicology Letters, and Food and Chemical Toxicology and Applied and Environmental Microbiology. Moreover, our data from objective 3 where the effect of spent culture supernatants of certain strains of probiotic bacteria, for example Lactobacillus GG (LGG) and E.coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) on secretory mucins MUC2, MUC5AC and MUC5B, as well as trefoil factor 3 in HT29-MTX cells, contributed to the write-up of two manuscripts, which are currently under review in Applied and Environmental Microbiology. We have also submitted a review article (currently under review) to the prestigious journal Critical reviews in food science and nutrition. Additionally, data were presented (both oral and poster) in international meeting as listed in part C.

765810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
765810.value: Collectively, our in vitro findings demonstrate that ingestion of Fusarium toxins may compromise enterocyte-mediated defence responses, which may lead to an increase in the susceptibility of the intestinal mucosa to experimental or natural infections. This warrants further investigation on the effect of mycotoxins on the enterocyte-mediated defence responses and confirm the “protective capacity” of probiotics in animal models (e.g mice) utilizing the best candidate probiotic strain from our in vitro studies. Currently, we have submitted another GRF grant (Ref no. 17106614) which is an extension of this research grant which aims to investigate whether Fusarium toxins compromised mucus synthesis and secretion, which is a potential target for probiotic intervention. An exposure regimen to stimulate the human exposure experience will be designed. Two different protocols that vary the time-points of oral administration of probiotic bacteria to determine whether probiotic bacteria could prevent and treat the unwanted effects induced by Fusarium toxins will be used. Various components of the enterocyte-mediated defence responses such as mucin dynamics, intestinal bacterial populations, mucosal permeability and bacterial translocation induced by Fusarium toxins, parameters connected with mucin secretion and turnover, intestinal morphology, intestinal permeability, intestinal bacterial population levels and bacterial translocation will be examined.

765810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
765810.value: The contamination of foods and feeds with mycotoxins is a serious problem worldwide and there is an increasing concern over the adverse effects of mycotoxins on animal and/or human health. However, research on the effects of multiple mycotoxins on animal and/ or human intestinal health is limited. Therefore, the results from this research project allowed the identification and characterization of the combined effects of Fusarium toxins on the immunological defence mechanisms of the enterocytes, which is of significant relevance to the "risk assessment" process. Additionally, since biological decontamination of mycotoxins using microorganisms, for example probiotic bacteria, is one of the well known strategies for the management of mycotoxins in foods and feeds, data so generated from this research project provided very valuable and essential information to be known before proceeding with the design of intervention studies on the protective capacity of probiotic bacteria against mycotoxicosis either in human or farm animals. These provide a greater understanding of potential novel nutritional modalities to reduce exposure to mycotoxins and their combinations.

766110.label: Project Title(Chinese)
766110.value: 在頸動脈體中的促炎細胞因子在間歇性低氧的病理生理作用

766110.label: Project Objectives
766110.value: Specific aim 1: to determine the effect of IH on the gene expression of interleukin (IL)-1b, IL-6, IL-10, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-a and their receptors, and the local inflammation in the CB. Specific hypothesis 1: the increased expressions of cytokines and their receptors play roles in the CB inflammation. Blood pressures, hematocrit, serum and tissue oxidative markers will be obtained from rats treated with IH or CH. The mRNA levels of the genes encoding the cytokines and receptors in the CB collected from the IH rats will be compared to the CH and normoxic control using real-time PCR and in-situ hybridization methods. The protein levels will be confirmed by Western-blot analysis. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) will be performed to localize the proteins in the CB with double-labeling of the cellular marker for the chemosensitive (glomus) cells. Local inflammation will be examined by the expression of inflammatory mediators, cyclooxygenases (COX) and chemokines, and macrophage infiltration with IHC using macrophage markers. Superior cervical ganglion will be a control tissue. It is speculated that levels of oxidative stress, local inflammation and the expressions of cytokines and receptors are significantly increased in the CB of IH rats. Specific aim 2: to examine how cytokines influence the chemoreception and lead to CB functional changes in IH. Specific hypothesis 2: the cytokines alter potassium currents and intracellular calcium ([Ca++]i) responses to acute hypoxia in the chemosensitive glomus cells, leading to the CB hyperexcitability and increased local expressions of signaling mediators of inflammation (NF-kb activity, IKK phosphorylation, MAPKs) in the CB. The effects of cytokine ligands on the chemoreceptor afferent activity, [Ca2+]i response and potassium current in the glomus cells in normoxia and acute hypoxia will be studied in the presence or absence of cytokine receptor antagonists or antibodies. Electrophysiological study of the afferent nerve activity of the chemoreceptor will be performed on isolated CB. Patch-clamp study and spectrofluorimetric [Ca++]i measurement will be performed on dissociated glomus cells. The DNA-binding activity of NF-kb will be evaluated by EMSA. Western-blot will be performed to measure the total and phosphorylated levels of IKK and MAPKs. Results obtained from the IH groups will be compared with those of the CH and normoxic controls. It is speculated that the afferent, potassium current and [Ca++]i responses to acute hypoxia; the activation of NF-kb activity and the signaling mediators, are significantly increased in the IH group, which could be antagonized by the receptor blockers. Specific aim 3: to determine the effect of anti-inflammatory drugs and anti-oxidants on the blood pressures and the expression and function of cytokines in the CB or cultured PC12 cells in IH. Specific hypothesis 3: blood pressures and the expressions of cytokines and their receptors, and the inflammatory responses are attenuated by anti-inflammatory drugs or antioxidants. Arterial pressures and the expression and function of the cytokines and their receptors, and the local inflammatory markers and signaling mediators in the CB will be obtained in the IH rats concurrently treated with dexamethasone or ibuprofen. Results will be compared with the CH and normoxic groups. Additionally, the CB cytokine expression could be confirmed by studies using the wild-type and COX-knockout mice treated with IH. In cultured PC12 cells as an oxygen-sensitive model, studies will be performed on the IH-induced cytokine expression, activation of NF-kb and signaling mediators in the presence of vehicles, antioxidants, COX inhibitors and cytokine receptor antagonists. The hyperexcitability will be evaluated by functional studies measuring the catecholamine secretion, [Ca++]i elevation in responding to acute hypoxia.

766110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766110.value: 頸動脈體是一對位於頸動脈分叉感覺動脈血氧分壓，二氧化碳和酸度的化學敏感器官。在頸動脈體的化學敏感細胞轉導化學信號和傳入神經纖維到大腦增加心肺功能的表現。因此，頸動脈體是對缺乏氧氣（缺氧）的生理反應的主要器官。長期缺氧（連續或間歇性缺氧）常見於慢性疾病，如心功能不全，肺疾病或睡眠呼吸暫停，在頸動脈體產生的功能變化在病理生理後果中起著重要作用。具體來說，我們的初步研究表明：（1）慢性缺氧 (CH) 顯著增加了大鼠頸動脈體的炎性細胞因子介素（IL）-1b，白細胞介素-6，腫瘤壞死因子（TNF） - a）的mRNA表達;（2）表達的細胞因子及其受體定位於小葉球含有酪氨酸羥化酶的化學敏感細胞，（3）細胞因子濃度依賴地提高分離化學敏感細胞內對嚴重缺氧的鈣離子反應，（4）慢性缺氧會增加頸動脈體中炎症介質的基因轉錄。這些數據表明，在頸動脈體中增加表達的促炎細胞因子對調製頸動脈化學感受器活動和局部炎症反應中起著積極的作用。在此建議，我們推測在大鼠頸動脈體的促炎症細胞因子在間歇性缺氧發揮了重要調製頸動脈化學感受器的功能和局部炎症的作用。我們特別感興趣是因為在臨床間歇低氧條件下許多缺氧發作是不連續的，間歇性的，而造成一組唯一的致病性活動，包括系統性高血壓。我們提出分子分析研究，細胞內鈣離子的測量，電生理和在體內的評估來審查在頸動脈體中促炎細胞因子的局部表達在間歇缺氧的病理生理作用。新的發現將提供對在間歇缺氧的頸動脈體的基礎分子和細胞病理生理機制的新見解。新的信息基礎將更好地了解發展中的病理生理和新的治療，如使用消炎藥治療間歇性缺氧/低氧血症有關的疾病與慢性心肺疾病及睡眠呼吸暫停的病人。

766110.label: Realisation of objectives
766110.value: Three specific aims were proposed in the project objectives, which have been fully achieved by experimental studies performed in the project duration. For the specific aim 1, studies were performed to examine the effect of chronic intermittent hypoxia on the expression of cytokines and their receptors in the carotid body (CB); also, the pathogenic mechanism underlying the effect of intermittent hypoxia on oxidative stress and inflammation in the CB. For specific aim 2, studies were conducted to investigate the effect of cytokines on the intracellular calcium responses to acute hypoxia in the chemosensitive glomus cells. For specific aim 3, studies were set to evaluate the effect of anti-inflammatory drugs or antioxidants on the CB inflammation mediated by the cytokines.

Specific hypothesis 1: the increased expressions of cytokines and their receptors play roles in the CB inflammation. Blood pressures, hematocrit, serum and tissue oxidative markers will be obtained from rats treated with IH or CH. The mRNA levels of the genes encoding the cytokines and receptors in the CB collected from the IH rats will be compared to the CH and normoxic control using real-time PCR and in-situ hybridization methods. The protein levels will be confirmed by Western-blot analysis. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) will be performed to localize the proteins in the CB with double-labeling of the cellular marker for the chemosensitive (glomus) cells. Local inflammation will be examined by the expression of inflammatory mediators, cyclooxygenases (COX) and chemokines, and macrophage infiltration with IHC using macrophage markers. Superior cervical ganglion will be a control tissue.
Specific aim 2: to examine how cytokines influence the chemoreception and lead to CB functional changes in IH.

Specific hypothesis 2: the cytokines alter potassium currents and intracellular calcium ([Ca++]i) responses to acute hypoxia in the chemosensitive glomus cells, leading to the CB hyperexcitability and increased local expressions of signaling mediators of inflammation (NF-kb activity, IKK phosphorylation, MAPKs) in the CB. The effects of cytokine ligands on the chemoreceptor afferent activity, [Ca2+]i response and potassium current in the glomus cells in normoxia and acute hypoxia will be studied in the presence or absence of cytokine receptor antagonists or antibodies. Electrophysiological study of the afferent nerve activity of the chemoreceptor will be performed on isolated CB. Patch-clamp study and spectrofluorimetric [Ca++]i measurement will be performed on dissociated glomus cells. The DNA-binding activity of NF-kb will be evaluated by EMSA. Western-blot will be performed to measure the total and phosphorylated levels of IKK and MAPKs.
Specific aim 3: to determine the effect of anti-inflammatory drugs and anti-oxidants on the blood pressures and the expression and function of cytokines in the CB or cultured PC12 cells in IH.

Specific hypothesis 3: blood pressures and the expressions of cytokines and their receptors, and the inflammatory responses are attenuated by anti-inflammatory drugs or antioxidants. Arterial pressures and the expression and function of the cytokines and their receptors, and the local inflammatory markers and signaling mediators in the CB will be obtained in the IH rats concurrently treated with dexamethasone or ibuprofen. Results will be compared with the CH and normoxic groups. Additionally, the CB cytokine expression could be confirmed by studies using the wild-type and COX-knockout mice treated with IH. In cultured PC12 cells as an oxygen-sensitive model, studies will be performed on the IH-induced cytokine expression, activation of NF-kb and signaling mediators in the presence of vehicles, antioxidants, COX inhibitors and cytokine receptor antagonists. The hyperexcitability will be evaluated by functional studies measuring the catecholamine secretion, [Ca++]i elevation in responding to acute hypoxia.

766110.label: Major findings and research outcome
766110.value: Major experimental results showed increased levels of oxidative stress in the carotid body (CB) of rats with 7-day-IH treatment resembling recurrent apneic conditions when compared with the normoxic control. Local inflammation shown by the amount of ED1-containing cells (macrophage infiltration) and the gene transcripts of NADPH oxidase subunitsand chemokines in the CB were significantly more in the hypoxic group than the control. In addition, the cytokines and receptors were expressed in the lobules of chemosensitive glomus cells containing tyrosine hydroxylase and the levels of expressions were significantly increased in the hypoxic group. For the signaling mechanism, experimental findings showed that exogenous cytokines elevated the intracellular calcium ([Ca2+]i) response to acute hypoxia in the dissociated glomus cells. The effect of cytokines on the [Ca2+]i response was significantly greater in the hypoxic than that of the normoxic group. For the effect of anti-inflammatory mechanisms, results showed that daily treatment of the hypoxic rats with anti-inflammatory drugs (dexamethasone or ibuprofen) attenuated the levels of oxidative stress, gp91phox expression and macrophage infiltration in the CB. In addition, levels of the mRNA expression of angiotensin receptor (AT) subtypes AT1a receptors was significantly increased in the carotid body of the hypoxic rat. Daily treatment of IH rats with losartan, an AT1 receptor antagonist, attenuated the levels of oxidative stress, gp91phox and cytokine expression as well as macrophage infiltration in the carotid body. Hence, these results suggest that a mechanistic involvement of the up-regulated expression of the AT receptors in the augmented carotid body activity and local inflammation via AT1 receptor activation under intermittent hypoxia conditions in patients with sleep-disordered breathing.

766110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
766110.value: Our studies have shown anti-inflammatory drugs could significantly lower the CB inflammation and the elevated chemoreceptor activity induced by intermittent hypoxia. As for the treatment of patients with sleep apnea, pharmacological intervention might be proposed to alleviate the pathophysiological impact on the cardiovascular morbidities and mortalities. Thus, anti-inflammatory drugs may be implicative according to the results of our experimental study. Also it is well known that oxidative stress induced by intermittent hypoxia exerts a systemic impact on multiple physiological systems and organs, leading to significant levels of systemic and chronic inflammation in patients with sleep apnea. Thus, it might be proposed that the anti-inflammatory drugs could have significant effect not only targeting the locally upregulated cytokine pathways in the carotid body, but also on the systemic inflammation in other systems and organs as well. Future studies in this direction warrant further investigations regarding the effective of the treatment with anti-inflammatory drugs in patients with sleep apnea.

766110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766110.value: The expression of proinflammatory cytokines and inflammatory mediators in the carotid body play a pathogenic role in sleep apnea. The cytokine signaling pathway is part of the mechanistic cascade involved in the augmented carotid chemoreceptor activity because of the local upregulation of the proinflammatory cytokines and cytokine receptors and inflammatory mediators in the carotid body. This in effect could significantly contribute to the increase chemosensory activity and the afferent activity of the chemoreflex, causing breathing instability in sleep apnea. Anti-inflammatory drugs could significantly attenuate the inflammation of the carotid body and the augmented carotid chemoreceptor activity induced by chronic intermittent hypoxia. Since the involvement of oxiditive stress in the pathogenic mechanism, it is proposed that the anti-inflammatory drugs could have significant effect not only targeting the locally upregulated cytokine pathways in the carotid body, but also on the systemic inflammation in other systems and organs as well.

766510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766510.value: Sirtuins, a class of enzymes with NAD-dependent deacetylase and putative ADP-ribosyltransferase activities, have increasingly been shown to have fundamental roles in regulating life span, transcription, cell survival, and metabolism. Small molecules that can regulate the activity of sirtuins are reported to have potentials to promote life span extension and to treat cancer, neurodegeneration diseases (Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases), and metabolic diseases (such as diabetes). Mammals have 7 sirtuins, SIRT1-7. Understanding the molecular structure and biological function of all the seven sirtuins in humans is required to fully realize the therapeutic potential of targeting sirtuins. Of the seven human sirtuins, only three of them, SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT3, have robust deacetylation activity in vitro and in vivo. The other sirtuins have either no detectable or very weak deacetylation activity in vitro. Here we propose that the sirtuins with no or very weak deacetylation activity catalyze the hydrolysis of other acyl groups from acylated lysine residues. The hypothesis is based on our preliminary results on SIRT5, which we have shown to have robust demalonylation and desuccinylation activity in vitro. The specific aims of this proposal are: (1) To further understand the structural basis of SIRT5’s preference for malonyl and succinyl peptides as substrates; (2) To develop specific inhibitors for SIRT5; (3) To probe the structure and function of Class II (SIRT4) and Class IV (SIRT6 and SIRT7) sirtuins that have no or weak deacetylation activity. Addressing these specific aims will significantly improve our understanding about the biological functions of sirtuins and help to explore the therapeutic potential for treating sirtuin-related diseases. Sirtuins蛋白质家族是一组酶，并且具有依赖NAD的去乙酰化酶活性和潜在的核糖转移酶活性。因为其在哺乳动物细胞中参与调节细胞寿命，同时在核酸转录，细胞存活，以及新陈代谢中都发挥的重要的作用，引起了包括结构生物学家在内的广泛兴趣，并越来越受到各国医学研究的广泛关注。其中，那些能直接调控Sirtuins 蛋白质家族功能的化学小分子则被认为是能延长人类寿命，治疗癌症，神经系统退变性疾病（如阿尔茨海默症和帕金森氏综合症），以及新城代谢疾病（如糖尿病）的潜力药物。研究发现，哺乳动物sirtuins蛋白酶家族有七个成员，即SIRT1-7。 对此sirtuins家族的七个成员的分子结构和生理功能的破译无疑是找到以sirtuins蛋白酶家族为治疗靶点先决条件。研究发现，在sirtuins家族的七个成员中，只有SIRT1， SIRT2和SIRT3在细胞内具有非常强的蛋白质去乙酰化活性，而其他的家族成员有的没有此去乙酰化的活性，有的则非常低。然而，根据我们的研究结果推测，那些没有乙酰化活性或是活性较低的sirtuins家族成员具有去其他酰基化的能力，可以水解被酰基化的赖氨酸上的酰基。通过我们对SIRT5的研究发现，SIRT5具有非常强的去丙二酰化和去琥珀酰化活性。所以我们的研究目标是1）对SIRT5以丙二酰基去琥珀酰基为亲和底物的结构生物学研究来了解其酶活机制。2）基于SIRT5的蛋白质三维结构，筛选对SIRT5的专一抑制剂。3）研究该家族没有去乙酰化活性的其余成员（如SIRT4, SIRT6 和SIRT7）的蛋白质三维结构和生物学功能。解决上述问题能加深和提高我们对sirtuins家族生物学功能的了解，更重要的是将来可以研发以sirtuins蛋白酶家族为治疗靶点的药物，从而能治疗与sirtuins蛋白酶家族相关的疾病。

766510.label: Realisation of objectives
766510.value: We have full achieved the goals that we set out in the proposal. (1) Using structural and biochemical data we have discovered that SIRT5 is an efficient desuccinylase and demalonylase in vitro, catalyzing the hydrolysis of succinyl and malonyl lysine residues. Furthermore, deletion of SIRT5 in mice increase the level of succinylation on carbamoyl phosphate synthase 1 (CPS1), a known target of Sirt5. Our work establishes that protein lysine malonylation is a previously unrecognized protein posttranslational modification and SIRT5 can reverse these modifications. SIRT5 is the first sirtuin demonstrated to prefer an acyl group other than acetyl, suggesting that other sirtuins showing little or no deacetylation activity may prefer to hydrolyze different acyl groups too. (2) The unique activity of SIRT5 enabled us to develop thiosuccinyl peptides as mechanism-based inhibitors specific for SIRT5. We have determined two new crystal structures: a binary complex of SIRT5 with an H3K9 succinyl peptide and a binary complex of SIRT5 with a bicyclic reaction intermediate after incubating with NAD and an H3K9 thiosuccinyl peptide. This is the first time that a bicyclic intermediate in the sirtuin-catalyzed deacylation reaction has been captured in a crystal structure, thus providing insights into the reaction mechanism. This intermediate structure also explains the mechanism that thiosuccinyl peptide is an efficient and specific inhibitor of SIRT5 with an IC50 of 5 μM, mainly because the bicyclic intermediate is stalled at the active site . (3) By using chemical and structural biology techniques, we revealed that SIRT6 can in fact remove long chain fatty acyl groups from protein lysine amino acids. We then assessed the physiologic relevance of their findings by examining the secretion state of TNFα, a protein messenger essential for many immune responses. We demonstrated that Sirt6 promotes the secretion of TNFα by removing the fatty acyl modification on the protein.

766510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
766510.value: SIRT6 was the first human sirtuin known to recognize long chain fatty acid groups. However, a recent study reports that SIRT1, SIRT2, SIRT3 and SIRT4 can remove lipoic acid. Our own preliminary data also show demyristoylation activity of SIRT1-3. We will develop mechanism-based inhibitors that inhibit sirtuin enzymatic activity to remove long chain fatty acyl groups.

766510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766510.value: Enzymes can modulate the activity of target proteins by appending and removing different chemical groups at specific amino acids. For example, a family of enzymes known as sirtuins regulates a host of cellular functions by specifically removing acetyl chemical groups from modified proteins. Not all mammalian sirtuins participate in this process, however, and we have uncovered an unexpected function for one sirtuin. Human sirtuin SIRT5 has very weak deacetylation activity, so we compared its structure with other sirtuins to find out why. Based on differences at the enzyme’s binding site, we predicted that SIRT5 was more likely to bind to proteins that have been modified via addition of succinyl or malonyl chemical groups at a lysine amino acid. This was surprising, because such succinyl protein modifications have only been observed in bacteria, while lysine-malonyl modifications have never been observed at all. We were able to isolate multiple proteins involved in cellular metabolism that are apparently modified with succinyl or malonyl, and we identified at least one protein that is desuccinylated by SIRT5 in vivo. These modifications therefore appear to represent a previously undiscovered mode of regulation in mammalian cells.

767110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
767110.value: Muscle fibers consist of macromolecules such as myosin and actin assembled in a highly ordered manner. The relative sliding of actin and myosin causes muscle contraction during which chemical energy is converted to mechanic movement. The generation of myofibril is a masterpiece of bioengineering by nature. However, how such a complex structure of muscle fiber is generated remains as a mystery to scientists. Myofibril components must be delivered to the appropriate sites of assembly before and during the myofibril assembly process. In our preliminary studies, we show that kinesin-1, the earliest discovered microtubule-based motor protein, serves as an intracellular “truck” for the delivery of a subset of myofibril components to the assembly sites. Mice with Kif5b (the heavy chain of kinesin-1) conditionally knocked out in skeletal muscles died quickly after birth with severe muscle dystrophy. In cultured Kif5b mutant myoblast cells, the myofibril component α-sarcomeric actin and intermediate filament protein desmin accumulated around the nuclei rather than in the polar regions of differentiating myoblasts where myofibril assembly occurs. Expression of Kif5b in mutant cells could rescue their localization and myofibril assembly. Furthermore, α-sarcomeric actin could be immunoprecipated by an anti-kinesin-1 antibody. These results uncover novel functions of kinesin-1 in myogenesis and strongly suggest that kinesin-1 delivers α-sarcomeric actin to the myofibril assembly sites. However, the exact mechanism how kinesin-1 delivers myofibril components in differentiating myoblast remains exclusive. Building on our extensive experience in working with genetics and function of intracellular motor molecules in mammalian cells, we propose to investigate the nature of kinesin-1-dependent delivery of myofibril components in differentiating myoblast. We are particularly interested in (i) identifying the subunits and domains of kinesin-1 protein complex responsible for the delivery of myofibril components in differentiating myoblast; (ii) elucidating whether kinesin-1 delivers myofibril components by directly binding to the myofibril components or through mediator proteins. We also intent to study the possibility that myofibril components are packed in membranous vesicles delivered by kinesin-1; (iii) identifying potential mediators of kinesin-1-dependent delivery in differentiating myoblast if kinesin-1 interacts with myofibril components indirectly. Completion of this proposed project will give us insight into how one of the most fascinating structures of living organisms, the muscle fiber is built. 767110.label: Realisation of objectives
767110.value: 1. Identify the subunits and domains of kinesin-1 responsible for the delivery of myofibril components in differentiating myoblast: We constructed a series of Kif5b truncations and subjected them to rescue experiment. While Kif5b without KLC binding domain (788-854 aa) or the globular tail (919-963 aa) was still functional in bipolar transportation of the myofibril components, lacking the 64 aa α-helix domain (855-918 aa) totally abolished Kif5b’s function. These results indicated that kinesin-1 heavy chain functioned independently of KLC, and the 64 aa domain in the tail region of Kif5b was crucial for transporting these myofibril components. These results has been published in Development (2013). Interestingly, we also found that the KLC binding domain and the autoinhibitory peptide in the globular tail region were both indispensable for the kinesin-1-mediated myonuclear positioning, indicating that different domains of Kif5b participated in delivering different cargos. This result has been published in Biochem Biophys Res Commun (2013). 2. Elucidate whether kinesin-1 delivers myofibril components by directly binding to the myofibril components or through mediator proteins: We first tested whether the Kif5b tail domain had the capacity to bind to these cargo proteins by GST pull-down. The full length tail domain GST-Kif850-963, but not the head, stalk, or light chain binding domain of Kif5b, could bind to desmin, α-sarcomeric actin and NMIIB from the lysate of wild-type cells. Within the tail domain, the 64-aa functional domain (855-918 aa), but not other fragments, had a similar binding capacity to the full-length tail, indicating that Kif5b may form a complex with its cargo proteins through this 64-aa domain. We next tried using mutant myoblast cell lysate in the GST pulldown assays. In this circumstance, only desmin can bind to GSTKif855-918, but not α-sarcomeric actin or NMIIB, suggesting that there should be other linker proteins, which were missing or abnormally functioning in mutant cells, bridged Kif5b tail and actin/NMIIB. We then tried to test whether Kif5b and desmin had a direct interaction. Data showed that 855-918 aa of Kif5b could bind to His-tagged desmin, whereas 919-963 aa could not, indicating that Kif5b directly interacts with desmin through the α-helix domain in the tail. Since desmin and nestin can form heteropolymers in muscle, and desmin can associated with actin through a giant actin-interacting protein nebulin, we proposed that desmin may act as a direct linker of Kif5b to bind to the intermediate filaments and actin-associated myofibril components. These results have been published in “Development”.

767110.label: Major findings and research outcome
767110.value: Controlled delivery of myofibril components to the appropriate sites of assembly is crucial for myofibrillogenesis. In this project, we generated mice with kinesin-1 heavy chain Kif5b conditionally knocked out in skeletal muscles, which revealed important roles of kinesin-1 in myonuclei positioning, myofibril assembly and their linkage to the myotendinous junctions (MTJ). The in vitro differentiated myoblasts with Kif5b deficiency reproduced the in vivo phenotypes, and demonstrated a role of Kif5b in anterograde transport of myofibril components α-sarcomeric actin and NMIIB, together with the intermediate filament proteins desmin and nestin to the growing tips of the elongating myotubes. We identified the subunits and domains of kinesin-1 responsible for the delivery of myofibril components in differentiating myoblasts. While Kif5b without KLC binding domain (788-854 aa) or the globular tail (919-963 aa) was still functional in bipolar transportation of the myofibril components, lacking the 64 aa α-helix domain (855-918 aa) totally abolished Kif5b’s function. These results indicated that kinesin-1 heavy chain functioned independently of KLC, and the 64 aa domain in the heavy chain tail region was crucial for transporting these myofibril cargos. We demonstrated that the Kif5b tail domain could bind to desmin, α-sarcomeric actin and NMIIB from the wild-type myoblasts, it only bound to desmin from the mutant cell lysate, suggesting that there should be other linker proteins, which were missing or abnormally functioning in mutant cells, bridged Kif5b tail and actin/NMIIB. We then demonstrated that 855-918 aa of Kif5b expressed in E. coli could bind to His-tagged desmin, indicating that Kif5b directly interacts with desmin through the α-helix domain in the tail region. Since desmin and nestin can form heteropolymers in muscle, and desmin can associated with actin through a giant actin-interacting protein nebulin, we proposed that desmin may act as a direct linker of Kif5b to bind to the intermediate filaments and actin-associated myofibril components (Development). KLC binding domain and the autoinhibitory peptide in the globular tail region were both indispensable for the kinesin-1-mediated myonuclear positioning, indicating that different domains of Kif5b participated in transportation of different cargos (BBRC). Moreover, we noticed that the transportation of EGFP-tagged desmin was bipolar-regulated in elongating myotubes in FRAP experiment. Domain mapping of desmin showed that the N- or C-terminus was dispensable for its anterograde transportation, while the N-terminal globular domain of desmin confers signal for its retrograde transportation, which may be mediated by cytoplasmic dynein complex (Journal of China-Japan Friendship Hospital).

767110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
767110.value: We proposed two possible directions for the further development of the research: 1. We used LC/MS/MS to identify other potential binding partners for Kif5b 855-918 aa. Among the identified proteins, Arhgef2 and Murc, which are both regulators in Rho/ROCK signaling pathway, may affect actin dynamics and myofibrillogenesis. Therefore, the interaction of these proteins and Kif5b need to be verified both in vitro and in vivo. Functionally, the impact of Kif5b deficiency on actin dynamics would be investigated. 2. Since the mutant myoblasts with Kif5b deficiency reproduced the in vivo phenotypes to a great extent, it may serve as an ideal model to study other potential intracellular transport process mediated by kinesin-1. Besides myofibril filaments, Kif5b may also participate in specific membrane protein targeting, including ion channels, glucose transporter, receptors of signaling molecules and so on. One feasible method to identify these membrane cargo proteins is to label the total membrane proteins of wildtype and mutant cells with biotin, purify these proteins by affinity purification, and then subject them to proteomics and search for differentially existed membrane proteins from wildtype and mutant cells. This information would enrich our understanding on kinesin-1-mediated transportation in muscle cells.

767110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
767110.value: Skeletal muscle contains highly ordered cytoskeleton systems mainly composed of myofibrils. Controlled delivery of myofibril components to the appropriate sites of assembly is crucial for generating functional contraction units. Here we discovered novel functions of a microtubule motor kinesin-1 in transportation of myofibril components and intermediate filaments in differentiating myoblast cells using mouse model and primarily cultured myoblast cells. Loss of kinesin-1 in mice muscles affected myofibril assembly and their linkage to the myotendinous junctions, and lack of this motor protein in differentiating myoblast cells abolished the bipolar transportation of the myofibril components and the intermediate filament proteins for assembly and their potential linkage to the myotendinous junctions. We verified that the light chain of kinesin-1 was dispensable in transporting these cargo proteins, while the heavy chain, especially a 64 amino acid α-helix region in the tail, played an important role in interacting with the myofibril components. Among the cargo proteins, desmin directly bind to kinesin-1 heavy chain, which may bridge other myofibril cargos to this kinesin motor. These findings provided new directions in studies of molecular mechanisms of myofibrils assembly and myotendinous junction-related myopathy.

767510.label: Realisation of objectives
767510.value: All four objectives were realized using a genetic association study with a candidate gene approach based on two large randomized placebo-controlled trials on influenza vaccination. In the first trial (T1), 915 children aged 6-15 had been randomized to receive either an inactivated trivalent seasonal influenza vaccine (TIV) (Vaxigrip, Sanofi Pasteur) or placebo in phases from 2009-2010. In the second trial (T2) 703 children aged 6-11 had been randomized to receive either a live attenuated influenza vaccine (FluMist MedImmune Inc.) or a saline nasal spray for either or both of seasonal influenza (trivalent vaccine) and pandemic A/H1N1 (monovalent vaccine) in 2009-2010. Randomized subjects were followed-up together with their household contacts (2545 in T1, 1854 in T2) for study outcomes. Vaccine response was defined by a post-vaccination antibody titer of 1:40 or ≥4-fold rise in all TIV components. Adverse vaccine responder was defined by an aggregated symptom score ≥2 on day 1 post-vaccination, basing on 10 symptoms each on a scale of 0(absent)/1(mild)/2(moderate/3(severe), thus having at least 2 mild or 1 moderate symptoms. Influenza infection was confirmed in T1 with a post-season antibody titer of ≥1:40 and ≥4-fold increase, and in both trials by RT-PCR on nasal and throat swabs collected during illness episodes. All participants kept a daily symptom dairy. Individuals having serological evidence of infection reporting fever plus ≥4 other symptoms in any illness episode were classified as a more serious case of infection. Whole blood samples from 2593 participants (T1) and buccal swab samples from 1603 participants (T2) were collected for genetic analysis in this study. DNA was extracted and genotyped for single nucleotide polymorphisms for IL-1B -511G>A (rs16944), IL-6 -5843A/G (rs1818879), IL-8 -251T/A (rs4073), IL-10 -1082A/G (rs1800896), -819T/C (rs1800871), -592A/C (rs1800872), MBL-2 -5232G>A, (rs1800451). -221C/G (rs7096206), -34C>T (rs5030737). -550G>C (rs11003125), MxA-88G/T (rs2071430), OSA1 -347A/G (rs2660), RIG1 G/C (rs9695310), TLR3 -1377T/G (rs3755290), -7G/T (rs3775296), TLR4 G/A (rs5030718), Asp299Gly (rs4986790), TLR7 Gln11Leu (rs179008), 1817G/T (rs5741880), TLR8 -129G/C (rs3764879), Met1Val (rs3764880), and (rs11003131)G/T. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate the relationship of polymorphisms with various outcomes and compute the ORs and 95% confidence interval (CIs) in relation to vaccination response, adverse effects, disease incidence and severity respectively when compared to the wild type genotype. The heterozygous genotype was also grouped with either of the two homozygous genotypes to analyze in a dominant or recessive model. Two-sided P values were reported and p≤0.05 was considered to indicate statistical significance.

767510.label: Major findings and research outcome
767510.value: Among 535 subjects receiving TIV, 295 were classified as vaccine responders. Polymorphisms RIG1 rs9695310 CA (OR=1.917, CI=1.148-3.202), and combined CC/CA (OR=1.672, CI=1.012-2.755) in a dominant model, IL-6 rs1818879 AG (OR=1.667, CI=1.109-2.504), and combined AG/GG (OR=1.637, CI=1.093-2.454) were associated with increased odds of response. TLR7 rs5741880 GT (OR=0.161, CI=0.046-0.566), combined GT/TT (OR=0.371, CI=0.159-0.866) in a dominant model, and TLR3 rs3755290 GG (OR=0.572, CI=0.335-0.976) in a recessive model comparing with GT/TT were associated with lower odds of response. No serious vaccine response including anaphylaxis or shock had been reported by any recipient. With a symptom score ≥2, 26.1%, 8.5%, and 36.2% were being classified as adverse responders for TIV, seasonal FluMist, or pandemic FluMist respectively. For TIV, IL-6 rs1818879 AG (OR=1.833, CI=1.14-2.945) and combined AG/GG (OR=1.778, CI=1.108-2.854) were associated with a higher risk, while CCL1 rs2282691 AT (OR=0.578, CI=0.347-0.963) with a lower risk of adverse response. For seasonal FluMist, no significant association was found between polymorphism and adverse response. For pandemic FluMist, RIG-1 rs9695310 combined CC/CG (OR=6.369, CI=0.759-52.632), and OSA-1 rs2660 combined GA/GG (OR=1.66, CI=1.023-2.692) were associated with an increased risk of adverse response. MxA rs2071430 TT (OR=0.332, CI=0.134-0.821), combined GT/TT (OR=0.539, CI=0.334-0.87), IL-10 rs1800871 CC (OR=0.399, CI=0.158-1.0), CT (OR=0.529, CI=0.305-0.917), combined CC/CT (OR=0.497,CI=0.298-0.831), rs1800872 CA (OR=0.579, CI=0.351-0.955), combined CA/CC (OR=0.548, CI=0.34-0.883), and IL-8 rs4073 combined AA/TA (OR=0.594, CI=0.362-0.976) were associated with lower risk of adverse response. Serologically and RT-PCR confirmed influenza were reported in 23.7% and 4.55% of participants respectively. TLR4 rs5030718 GA (OR=4.207, CI=1.377-12.853), TLR8 rs3764879 CG (OR=1.309, CI=1.01-1.695) and rs3764880 GA (OR= 1.338, CI=1.035-1.731), TLR3 rs3775296 GT (OR=1.263, CI=1.034-1.542) and combined GT/TT (OR=1.211, CI=1-1.466) were associated with increased susceptibility. OSA-1 rs2660 GG (OR=0.613, CI=0.364-01.031) in a recessive model comparing to GA/AA was associated with reduced susceptibility for serological infection. TLR7 rs5741880 GT (OR=0.214, CI=0.051-0.89), combined GT/TT (OR=0.23, CI=0.071-0.741), TLR3 rs3775296 TT (OR=0.432, CI=0.185-1.0) and combined GT/TT (OR=0.071, CI=0.52-0.97), were associated with reduced susceptibility for RT-PCR confirmed infection. Only 2 hospitalizations and no mortality were reported among all participants with serological confirmation of influenza. A more serious clinical picture occurred in 19.2%. RIG-1 rs9695310 CC (OR=0.198, CI=0.043-0.905) and CCL1 rs2282691 combined AA/AT (OR=0.546, CI=0.302-0.985) were associated with lower odds of having a more serious clinical picture. All these effects of polymorphisms in relation to susceptibility or vaccination response are compatible to the current understanding regarding the role played by those genes in either the pathogenesis or immunological response to influenza infection.

767510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
767510.value: These results are exciting in identifying genetic determinants affecting the response to vaccination and susceptibility to influenza infection in human. Manuscripts for publication are currently in preparation and should be of interest to high impact general scientific journals. Further exploration to include other SNPs, including those that could not be accommodated in the initial Sequonom assay design, and other SNPs recently reported to affect disease severity (rs12252-C IFITM3) will be performed as a next step. Exploration of other SNPs currently not examined in the IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TLR3, TLR4, TLR7, TLR8, MBL-2, RIG1, CCL1 and OSA1 genes will also allow for the study of different haplotypes and potential interacting effects of different SNPs. Further refinement of analysis and adjustment of potential effect of familial clustering will also be done. We are currently seeking funding to further investigate genetic determinants of risk of infection in other ongoing studies including household transmission studies. We are also considering the idea of a case-control study to further investigate the host genetic effect on severe vaccine side-effects and severe infection outcomes to cater for the problem of paucity of these rare outcomes in our current study.

767510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
767510.value: The susceptibility to influenza infection in an individual is dependent on the interplay of host immunity and viral pathogenicity. This study has examined the relationship between variation in the host genetic make-up and the risk in relation to influenza infection based on a sample of 6017 individuals that participated in two large-scale clinical trials of influenza vaccination. The result from this study has demonstrated the importance of host genetic variation in affecting the response to influenza vaccination and also in susceptibility to influenza infection. Our findings may help to explain the great variability in the protection achieved by influenza vaccination and the susceptibility to influenza infection upon exposure in different individuals. A number of genetic variations conferring significant increases in risk of infection have been identified, which are important in improving our understanding on the pathogenetic mechanism of and immunological response to influenza infection. The identification of genetic variations associated with poor response and adverse effect on receiving influenza vaccination also enhanced our understanding in the area and could contribute to the development of better vaccines that may offer improved protection to all recipients.

767710.label: Realisation of objectives
767710.value: 1) We have validated the interaction between PACT and RIG-I. Importantly, we performed co-immunoprecipitation, biochemical co-fractionation and FRET imaging to demonstrate that endogenous PACT interacts with endogenous RIG-I in Sendai virus-infected cells. Our GST pull-down analysis with truncated GST-RIG-I mutants revealed that the C-terminal repression domain (CTD) of RIG-I was sufficient for binding with PACT in vitro, whereas the CARD and helicase domains were dispensable for this interaction. In addition, we mapped the RIG-I-binding domain to dsRBD1 of PACT. We also found that the interaction between PACT and RIG-I does not require dsRNA. However, the presence of dsRNA might enhance PACT-RIG-I interaction. 2) We have almost completed the mechanistic study on PACT-induced activation of RIG-I. Co-expression of RIG-I and PACT resulted in substantial enhancement of RIG-I activity. The helicase activity of RIG-I was seemingly required for the activation of RIG-I by PACT, since the helicase-dead K270A mutant of RIG-I was not activated by PACT. We further demonstrated the cooperation between RIG-I and PACT in the activation of innate antiviral response in the context of Sendai virus infection. In addition, we found that TBK1 and CARD9 were differentially recruited to the MAVS complex in cells expressing PACT and RIG-I. Direct measurement of the steady-state amounts of IFN-beta and ISG15 transcripts in PACT-compromised A549 and MEF cells by quantitative RT-PCR confirmed an inhibition of viral activation of IFN- and ISG15. Moreover, we also provided evidence that PACT activation of RIG-I does not required Dicer or PKR and that PACT stimulates the ATPase activity of RIG-I. Finally, our results indicated that PACT further facilitate the activation of RIG-I by intermediate-length poly(I:C) of ~500bp, but not by 5'-ppp short dsRNA. 3) We demonstrated the role of PACT in facilitating the activation of RIG-I by intermediate-length poly(I:C). We also found that IFN-beta production was significantly activated only in IFN-beta-treated 293PACT cells, but not in IFN-beta-treated HEK293 cells. Our findings reveal PACT as a novel and important component in initiating and sustaining the RIG-I-dependent antiviral response. A new model for PACT and RIG-I function has been proposed based on these findings and this has gained support from recent papers published by other groups including one leading group from Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. We further identified and characterized two viral antagonists of PACT function: herpes simplex virus 1 Us11 protein and Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus 4a protein. We showed that these proteins interact directly with PACT but not RIG-I and prevent PACT from activating RIG-I. Our findings reveal PACT targeting as a new mechanism in viral suppression of innate antiviral response. 4) We also found that PACT interacts with and potently activates MDA5. The activation of MDA5 by dsRNA or encephalomyocarditis virus (EMCV) was substantially potentiated when PACT was overexpressed. On the contrary, the activation of MDA5 by dsRNA or EMCV was abrogated in PACT-/- murine embryonic fibroblasts (MEF). The interaction between PACT and MDA5 is dsRNA-independent. Mechanistically, PACT activates MDA5 by enhancing its homodimerization and potentiating its ATPase and RNA helicase activity. Hence, PACT is a protein activator of both RIG-I and MDA5.

767710.label: Major findings and research outcome
767710.value: Essential role of PACT as a cellular activator of RIG-I-dependent antiviral response – RIG-I, a virus sensor that triggers innate antiviral response, is a DExD/H-box RNA helicase bearing structural similarity with Dicer, an RNase III-type nuclease that mediates RNA interference. Dicer requires double-stranded RNA binding protein partners, such as PACT, for optimal activity. We show that PACT physically binds to the C-terminal repression domain of RIG-I and potently stimulates RIG-I-induced type I interferon production. PACT potentiates the activation of RIG-I by poly (I:C) of intermediate length. PACT also cooperates with RIG-I to sustain the activation of antiviral defense. Depletion of PACT substantially attenuates viral induction of interferons. The activation of RIG-I by PACT does not require double-stranded RNA-dependent protein kinase or Dicer, but is mediated by a direct interaction that leads to stimulation of its ATPase activity. Our findings reveal PACT as an important component in initiating and sustaining the RIG-I-dependent antiviral response (Kok et al., 2011). Suppression of PACT- and RIG-I-dependent innate antiviral response by herpes simplex virus 1 Us11 protein – Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) Us11 protein is a double-stranded RNA-binding protein that suppresses type I interferon production through the inhibition of cytoplasmic RNA sensor RIG-I. Whether additional cellular mediators are involved in this suppression remains to be determined. In this study we report on the requirement of cellular double-stranded RNA-binding protein PACT for Us11-mediated perturbation of innate antiviral response. US11 associates with PACT tightly to prevent it from binding with and activating RIG-I. The Us11-deficient HSV-1 was indistinguishable from the Us11-proficient virus in the suppression of interferon production when PACT was compromised. More importantly, HSV-1-induced activation of interferon production was abrogated in PACT-knockout murine embryonic fibroblasts. Our findings suggest a new mechanism for viral evasion of innate immunity through which a viral double-stranded RNA-binding protein interacts with PACT to circumvent type I interferon production. This mechanism might also be used by other PACT-binding viral interferon-antagonizing proteins such as Ebola virus VP35 and influenza A virus NS1 (Kew et al., 2013). Suppression of PACT-induced activation of RIG-I and MDA5 in innate antiviral response by Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus 4a protein – Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) is an emerging pathogen that causes severe disease in human. MERS-CoV is closely related to bat coronaviruses HKU4 and HKU5. Evasion of innate antiviral response might contribute significantly to MERS-CoV pathogenesis, but the mechanism is poorly understood. In this study we characterized MERS-CoV 4a protein as a novel immunosuppressive factor that antagonizes type I interferon production. MERS-CoV 4a protein contains a double-stranded RNA-binding domain capable of interacting with poly(I:C). Expression of MERS-CoV 4a protein suppressed interferon production induced by poly(I:C) or Sendai virus. RNA binding of MERS-CoV 4a protein was required for IFN antagonism, a property shared by 4a protein of bat coronavirus HKU5, but not by the counterpart in bat coronavirus HKU4. MERS-CoV 4a protein interacted with PACT in an RNA-dependent manner, but not with RIG-I or MDA5. It inhibited PACT-induced activation of RIG-I and MDA5, but did not affect the activity of downstream effectors such as RIG-I, MDA5, MAVS, TBK1 and IRF3. Taken together, our findings suggest a new mechanism through which MERS-CoV employs a viral double-stranded RNA binding protein to circumvent innate antiviral response by perturbing the function of cellular double-stranded RNA binding protein PACT. PACT targeting might be a common strategy used by different viruses including Ebola virus and herpes simplex virus 1 to counteract innate immunity (Siu et al., 2014).

767710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
767710.value: We have published one major paper on PACT activation of RIG-I in Cell Host Microbe, the best international journal in the broad field of microbiology. Two related papers documenting the suppression of PACT activation of RIG-I and MDA5 by HSV-1 Us11 and MERS-CoV Us11 have also been published by Journal of Virology, a well-respected international speciality journal. We are preparing another paper on PACT activation of MDA5 and we are confident that this will also be published in a decent international journal. In addition, we are invited to publish a preview in Cell Host Microbe when our findings on PACT and RIG-I were independently confirmed by a leading group led by Dr. Christopher Basler at Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai in the context of Ebola virus-encoded interferon-antagonizing VP35 protein. Our achievements obtained in the study of PACT supported by this GRF grant have allowed us to compete for and obtain another CRF grant (HKU1/CRF/11G). With the support from CRF and from SK Yee Medical Research Foundation in 2012, our continuing study on PACT and RIG-I-like receptors has been accelerated and enhanced. We have expand our analyses and are carrying out protein analysis and animal work to shed light on the mechanism and biological function of PACT-mediated activation of RIG-I and MDA5. Our further studies will derive new knowledge and have a significant impact on molecular immunology and virology. Our findings also have implications in vaccine and drug development.

767710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
767710.value: Innate immunity is the first-line defense against invading viruses. The activation of innate immunity is triggered by the sensing of viral components such as RNA by specialized cellular proteins. One of these specialized proteins named RIG-I is a major virus sensor. We found that RIG-I does not work alone in virus sensing but partners with another cellular protein PACT which directly binds with viral RNA. In support of our finding that PACT is important in virus sensing, we discovered that two pathogenic human viruses use viral proteins that can also bind with RNA to block PACT function. Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) Us11 protein is one example. Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) 4a protein is another. HSV-1 and MERS-CoV are important human pathogens. Why they cause disease in human is unclear and one possibility is that they are particularly efficient in counteracting innate immunity. It will therefore be critical to clarify how HSV-1 and MERS-CoV cripple cellular proteins that sense viruses. Our work not only provides a new understanding of the abilities of HSV-1 and MERS-CoV to subvert virus sensing, but might also prove useful in revealing new strategies for the development of vaccines and antivirals.

768010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768010.value: Our recent success in identification of bioactive small-molecule inhibitors of SARS-CoV by chemical genetics using an automated high-throughput screening (HTS) platform has prompted us to search for small-molecule compounds that would interfere with influenza A virus infection. Applying the concept of chemical genetics, we have identified from a chemical library with 50,240 structurally diverse compounds more than 1,000 small-molecule inhibitors that would inhibit the infectivity of the viruses in Madin-Darby canine kidney (MDCK) cell-based HTS assay. After secondary screening of 950 selected hits with more stringent conditions, we have identified 39 compounds that are potent antagonists of influenza A infection. We further identified 5 compounds perturbing intracellular trafficking of the viral nucleoprotein (NP). To illustrate that our approach is effective in identifying new druggable targets in influenza A infection, we have isolated an escaped mutant with elevated resistance to a selected compound (nucleozin). Whole genome sequencing of the resistant mutant has confirmed a single amino acid substitution in the NP. The compound that we termed nucleozin stops the temporal nuclear localization of NP at sub-micromolar concentrations and abolishes the replication of the virus in MDCK cells. Preliminary animal studies using H5N1 influenza A virus infection model in mice indicated that nucleozin is also effective in vivo. We will elucidate the antiviral mechanisms of nucleozin by investigating the RNA binding properties, host factor interactions, and replication efficiency of NP in the presence or absence of nucleozin. We will also investigate the structure-activity relationship of the derivatives of nucleozin by plaque reduction assay (PRA), biochemical and biophysical assays employing isothermal titration calorimeter (ITC) and differential scanning calorimeter (DSC), and molecular modeling analysis. Our successful identification of nucleozin as a new anti-flu compound and influenza A NP as a novel druggable target clearly demonstrate that chemical genetics is an effective approach to identify new druggable targets and potential drug candidates simultaneously. We therefore also propose to elucidate the molecular targets of the identified bioactive compounds interfering with viral NP trafficking and other biological processes crucial to influenza infections. Abstract 摘要 之前我們成功採用化學遺傳學方法，通過自動化高通量篩選平臺鑒定出一些具有生物活性的小分子可以抑制SARS冠狀病毒（SARS-CoV），這一發現促使我們去尋找一些可以阻止A型流感病毒感染的小分子化合物。應用化學遺傳學這一概念，通過高通量平臺篩選實驗我們從含有50240個結構不同的化合物庫找到了超過1000個小分子抑製劑可以抑制病毒感染MDCK細胞。我們從這1000多個化合物中選取了950個化合物進行第二輪更嚴格的篩選，確定了39個化合物是A型流感病毒的感染強有力的拮抗劑并進一步確定了5種化合物可以干擾細胞內核蛋白（NP）的運輸。爲了說明我們的試驗方法可以有效鑒定A型流感病毒感染過程中新的藥物靶點，我們分離出一個突變的病毒對選定化合物Nucleozin有高耐藥性。通過對這個抗性突變的全基因組測序進一步確定了在核蛋白上只有單一氨基酸被替換。 這個被命名為Nucleozin的化合物可以在亞微摩濃度下阻止核蛋白在核內的定位以及破壞病毒在MDCK 細胞中的複製，在H5N1 A型流感病毒感染的小鼠模型中進行的研究也初步說明了Nucleozin在體內同樣有效。因此我們將通過化合物nucleozin 對RNA結合的能力，宿主因子的相互結合以及核蛋白複製效率的影響來闡明nucleozin 的抗病毒機制。我們也將通過採用空斑抑制實驗（PRA）,以及等溫滴定量熱法（ITC）,示差掃描量熱法（DSC），分子圖形分析等生物物理及生物化學的實驗來研究Nucleozin的衍生物的構效關係。我們成功的鑒定Nucleozin 是一種新的抗流感化合物，而A型流感病毒核蛋白也成為一個新的藥物靶點，這一發現表明化學遺傳學手段在用於尋找新的藥物靶點以及篩選新的有潛力的藥物時非常有效。因此我們也建議可以闡釋已經找出的影響病毒NP蛋白運輸的具有生物活性化合物的分子靶標以及其他一些對於流感病毒感染十分重要的生物過程。

768010.label: Realisation of objectives
768010.value: This projects aims at understanding the mechanisms of the newly identified anti-influenza A compound nucleozin and to further explore NP as a target for antiviral therapeutics. Objective 1: Mode of action of nucelozin on influenza A nucleoprotein trafficking: In order to understand the mode of action of nucleozin, we have commenced experiments to examine the in vitro cell-free and cellular activities of nucleozin on influenza A nucleoprotein (NP). The recombinant NP has been purified and in vitro assays employing dynamic light scattering and molecular modeling. We showed that nucleozin acts on purified recombinant NP to causing massive aggregation of the protein and the presence of RNA molecules will enhance the aggregation properties of nucleozin-NP interaction. Furthermore, we were able to show that the ribonucleoprotein (RNP) is also a direct target of nulceozin, explaining why the inhibitory effects of nucleozin are spanning through the whole course of cellular infection. In influenza A infected cells, the action of nucleozin on RNP is almost instant – the addition of nucleozin to replicating viruses leads to rapid aggregation of RNP and the whole process of NP trafficking is halted. Without the proper involvement of NP/RNP, the infection cycle of the virus stopped and no infectious viral particles are produced, leading to very restricted infection in few cells. Objective 2: Identification of the molecular targets of the bioactive compounds perturbing influenza A nucleoprotein trafficking: In order to define the molecular targeting site of NP-inhibiting compounds, we have commenced mutant-raising of compounds interfering with NP activities and were able to identify Y289 and Y52 as the major amino acid residues critical for compound-NP interaction leading to aggregation. The mutations at these positions have rendered nucleozin become less effective in inhibiting viral replication. In addition, we have identified several novel inhibitors inhibiting the inward movement of NP indirectly by interfering with the HA molecule. These new compounds greatly slow down the replication of the virus by targeting the fusion of the virus with host cells leading to the delayed migration of RNP into the nucleus. The NP and RNP are excellent markers for monitoring the replication and maturation of the infecting viruses and their inhibitors may have great potential for therapeutic uses. Our study results in two publications “Nucleozin targets cytoplasmic trafficking of vRNP-Rab11 complexes in influenza A virus infection (2013, JVI)” and “Identification of Novel Fusion Inhibitors of Influenza A Virus by Chemical Genetics (submitted to JVI)”

768010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
768010.value: We have identified a new compound nucleozin that will cause the clumping of a viral component known as nucleoprotein (NP). We are also the first one to show that NP is a possible target for drug treatment. Our study further defines how nucleozin works and how it can stop the NP from moving around in the infected cell. We discovered that the addition of nucelozin in cells infected with influenza A virus will stop the virus replication rapidly. Our study also has identified new compounds that interacts with the hemagglutinin (HA) and slows down the entering of the infecting influenza A virus to the nucleus. The compounds and drug targets we have identified and validated will be of great value for antiviral drug discovery and drug development.

768110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768110.value: In this project, using a combination of photographic-identification mark-recapture and genetic techniques, we will study population parameters of Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins, locally known as Chinese White Dolphins, that inhabit the Pearl River Estuary. Among the parameters investigated, we will estimate the population size, how far the individual dolphins travel within and between regions of the Estuary, what is their network of social interactions, broader social structure and genetic structure across the Estuary; and how each of the parameters interacts with one another. This study will enable us to determine whether there are different environmental pressures across the estuary and how they affect the pattern of dolphin group formation and the intra- and inter-group relationships; and whether the Pearl River estuary acts as a barrier to gene flow between dolphin groups. By comparison with similar study of humpback dolphins off southern Africa, we will also examine how social behaviour of these animals and their broader population structure vary (or perhaps how similar it is) across distant habitats and ocean basins. With this comparative component, this study will contribute to the growing understanding of the influence of environments on the demographic and behavioural processes of group living mammals such as dolphins. Furthermore, this study will also deliver information that is important for the conservation and management of humpback dolphins in Hong Kong. Through our genetic analyses we will determine how interconnected and how genetically diverse is the dolphin population in the Pearl River Estuary, which will be highly informative for the assessment of stock vulnerability. 珠江口中華白海豚(Sousa chinensis)之群落結構及社交行為動態: 沿海棲海豚的模型系統 此計劃將一併利用相片辨認及標誌重現技術(photographic-identification mark-recapture)以及基因技術，以研究棲息於珠江口之印太洋駝海豚(本地稱中華白海豚)之族群變數。 變數包括族群數目估算，個體於珠江口不同區域內及區域之間的移動，社交互動網絡，廣泛社交結構，及珠江口內族群之基因結構等，以及變數間之關係。此研究能使研究員判斷珠江口內各種環境壓力的存在與否， 環境壓力對白海豚群落形成之影響，群落內及群落間之互動關係，以及珠江口作為白海豚群落間基因交流之障礙與否。此研究亦透過與研究非洲南部駝海豚的相似項目之比較， 讓研究員了解存在於不同生境或海域的駝海豚社交行為及廣泛族群結構之相異性(或相似性)。通過此類形的比較模式，此研究將提高對於如海豚般之群居哺乳類動物之族群及行為過程，受環境影響的了解。另外，此研究亦能提供香港白海豚保育及管理的重要資訊。 通過基因分析，研究員將可判斷珠江口白海豚族群間的基因關連及基因多樣性，而此分析將能對珠江口白海豚族群脆弱性的評估提供重要及極具參考性的資訊。

768110.label: Realisation of objectives
768110.value: Population Parameters -- This objective have been achieved to the fullest and beyond the initial expectations. A manuscript that quantifies the population parameters in Hong Kong waters is currently in preparation (target journal: Animal Conservation); the data summary is presented in Part C (attachment 8.6). Owing to our intensity of field effort, large sample size, and thoroughness of photo-ID capture-recapture events, our dataset is robust and generated high quality estimates. A follow-up manuscript will consolidate the data collected in Hong Kong and Mainland waters and will quantify population parameters across east/central PRE. Such analyses, covering a substantially larger area, will benefit from an additional field season and therefore this manuscript is intended to follow-up in late 2015. Meanwhile, demographic projection of population trends has already been published in 2012 (attachment 8.2), while our recent quantification of thresholds of the species long-term survival in PRE ready for journal submission (Part C, attachment 8.5; target journal: Biological Conservation). Movement/Ranging Pattern -- This objective has been fully achieved within the anticipated extent, including the uncertainty surrounding the spatial models. As the individual re-capture rates are moderate-to-low (which on its own serves for a valuable indicator of population structure), we anticipate a minimum of one more field seasons is needed to reliably quantify spatial and temporal movement, and two more sampling seasons for modelling diffusion rates and the individual displacement over time. Meanwhile, spatial data describing utilization distribution in Hong Kong waters have already been quantified with Local Convex Hull (LoCoH) models and relevant manuscript is intended for journal submission by mid-2015 (target journal: Animal Conservation). Socio-Behavioural Dynamics -- Similarly as above, this objective has been achieved in full anticipated extent and preliminary results have been tabulated. However, as socio-ecological models based on mark-recapture analyses are immensely 'data-hungry' and especially so when the individual re-capture rates are not high, further two seasons of data collection are required for a sufficiently robust dataset that can deliver high-ranking research output. Meanwhile, however, the comparative component of this project progressed well beyond the initial expectations. A comparative study, co-supervised by the PI, quantified reproductive parameters of the species off Taiwan (manuscript In Review; see attachment 8.7) which provides means for comparative analyses when a similar dataset becomes available for PRE. Genetic Structure/Connectivity -- This objective is well achievable and the framework has been well in place; however, the work was obstructed solely by an unresolved bureaucratic hurdle, which is a holdup of AFCD research permit. Despite several applications and many discussions, the permit has not been issued (it remains pending) and, consequently, the genetic sampling could not be initiated. An alternative approach, using samples from stranded animals, has been investigated and produced encouraging initial results. This work will be continued further under a separate research funding.

768110.label: Major findings and research outcome
768110.value: This project provides quantitative mark-recapture estimates of the population parameters and size of Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins in Hong Kong (Part C, Output 8.6) and across a larger spatial scale of the Pearl River Estuary (PRE) (manuscript to follow in 2015). These estimates come along with quantitative models of the population demography and structure (analyses partially completed), spatiotemporal movements of individuals (analyses underway), and patterns of geographic fidelity (completed). Demographic analyses of the population trends (Output 8.2) are now coupled with quantitative models of the demographic and ecological thresholds (Minimum Viable Population and Minimum Area of Critical Habitat, respectively) of this species in PRE (Output 8.5) and comparative assessment of other populations in a broader geographic range of the species (Output 8.3). Even though some of the analytical work is still underway and will take several more months to complete, this overall work is already setting a benchmark for this type of research in Southeast Asia. It is a first time that such a concerted and thorough population-level research has been performed in the PRE region and in fact anywhere in coastal China; and it is not common internationally. Contrary to what is frequently cited by activists and local media, the population figures of humpback dolphins in Hong Kong waters and across PRE substantially differ. There are at least ca. 450 dolphins that inhabit Hong Kong waters, and ca. 320 of them can be seen in Hong Kong each year. However, this group of animals does not represent a distinct population. Even though some of them display notable site fidelity in Hong Kong waters, they are not resident in Hong Kong but rather "frequent visitors" that interact with one another along a wide range social spectrum that includes "frequent companionships" as well as "casual acquaintances." Although a community sub-division can be discerned on a larger spatiotemporal scale, individual long-term associations are not the norm for these animals and their social structure follows a fluid fission-fusion pattern. It has to be noted, however, that as socio-behavioural analyses require long-term datasets, at present our 3-year project cannot deliver the complete story. Further work, including both field data collection and analytical model construction is needed, and is currently underway (independently funded). Our demographic analyses of population status and trend (Output 8.2) provide a strong quantitative evidence of continuous rate of population decline of 2.5% per annum, which, if remains constant, may lead to the current population numbers diminished by ca. 74% within three generations of these animals (<60 years), which under IUCN criteria classifies the PRE humpback dolphins as Endangered. This is a first-time that such complex demographic models have been constructed for this species, and is among few similar approaches in the field of cetacean studies. Our spatial analyses of area/habitat use pattern indicate that dolphin core areas are located along natural coastline where foraging represents the predominant behaviour. The range of transit travel extends further beyond that of other behaviours, connecting core foraging and milling grounds. The majority of core areas of biologically critical behaviours are unprotected and currently not prioritised for future conservation in Hong Kong, which is a cause of concern (manuscript in preparation, intended for submission in mid-2015). On a broader range-wide scale, our collaboration with a large international research team helped to refine the current understanding of the evolutionary divergence of humpback dolphins along their entire distribution range and proposed a new taxonomic classification of the genus Sousa (paper published in 2013).

768110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
768110.value: Our recent work suggests that the extreme west of PRE harbours far greater population of humpback dolphins than previously thought; and these animals remained undiscovered to science until literally two years ago thanks to this RGC-funded project. Current data from across PRE, although still preliminary, suggests a sophisticated population structure with three apparent "communities" that maybe socio-behaviourally discreet and correspond to three regions of PRE, eastern, middle, and western; with a unique phenotype (abnormal pigmentation) restricted only to Middle-PRE. However, as socio-behavioural analyses of the complexities of social structures of long-lived animals require long-term datasets, our 3-year project could not deliver the complete story. Further research effort is currently underway (RGC grant HKU-768913M). An important next step in research should address the issue of how cumulative effects of coastal degradation and habitat destruction may compromise the ecological requirements of humpback dolphins in PRE and other comparable coastal systems. Habitat integrity is essential in ensuring survival of free-ranging populations; yet, facing many present-day anthropogenic impacts, this integrity is increasingly degraded at scales seldom anticipated and even less measured or monitored. A study that would focus on the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin, a species with highly restricted inshore shallow-water distribution and narrow habitat selectivity (hence highly susceptible to adverse effects of human activities and the degradation of inshore habitats) would be an important contribution to the emerging field of global-change-ecology. Such project would be especially timely in PRE and much needed in Hong Kong, in the face of ongoing and soon-to-be-initiated major coastal constructions. Such project is currently submitted to RGC for funding consideration.

768110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
768110.value: This research project significantly advanced our knowledge of the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins, locally in China and Taiwan known as Chinese White Dolphins, inhabiting Hong Kong waters and Pearl River Estuary (PRE). With the application of modern analytical and quantitative research techniques, we have deciphered the population parameters and structure, and discovered that they markedly differ from what is a common Layman's perception in Hong Kong. The dolphins, counted in several hundred, are not resident in Hong Kong but rather "frequent visitors" that interact with one another along a wide range of social spectrum that includes "frequent companionships" as well as "casual acquaintances." Individual long-term associations are not common for these animals and their social structure follows a fluid fission-fusion pattern. Dolphin core areas are located along natural coastline where foraging represents the predominant behaviour. However, the majority of core areas of biologically critical behaviours are unprotected and currently not prioritised for conservation in Hong Kong, which is a cause of major concern. Our demographic analyses indicate that the dolphin population in PRE and Hong Kong is declining at an alarming rate of 2.5% annually. If nothing is done to slow down this trend, the population will decline by over 70% in a lifespan of just three generations of these animals (less than 60 years). Under the IUCN criteria, such population projection classifies it as Endangered. This is a first-time that such detailed ecological, behavioural and demographic studies have been conducted on this species in the PRE region, and in fact anywhere in coastal China; and it is among few similar approaches elsewhere in the field of cetacean studies. The outcome of this project carries major implications to the understanding of the current status and viability of the dolphin population inhabiting the Pearl River Delta system.
