768110.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
768110.value: This project provided research training and partial research support for three PhD students at HKU, furnishing a substantial part of their postgraduate thesis. However, all the student projects are still ongoing; one of the students is expected to submit her thesis at the end of 2015; while the other two will do so in Aug 2016 and Aug 2017. A research collaboration has been established with (i) the Institute of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at National Taiwan University (NTU), Taipei, Taiwan; (ii) Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Marine Resources and Coastal Engineering, School of Marine Sciences at Sun Yat-Sen University (SYSU), Guangzhou; (iii) Guangdong Pearl River Estuary Chinese White Dolphin National Nature Reserve in Zhuhai; and (iv) Coastal and Marine Research Institute at Nelson Mandela Metropolitan University in Port Elizabeth, South Africa. The academic collaboration involved the PI's co-supervision of two PhD students at SYSU and 1 PhD and 1 Master student at NTU, and advising one PhD student on comparative research conducted in South Africa. A postdoctoral associate at NTU (Dr. S-L Huang) recently joined the PI's research team at HKU as post-doctoral fellow supported through a separate funding. This project provided a major source of data used during the recent regional marine mammal Red List Assessment (species status and trends) conducted within the framework of the Biodiversity Strategy Action Plan of the currently ongoing in Hong Kong implementation of the Convention of Biological Diversity. The comparative component of this project progressed well beyond our initial expectations, on both regional and range-wide scale. A joint undertaking with a large international research team resulted with two high-profile publications. The first, in 2011, merges together applications of population genetics with remote sensing, providing a novel approach to investigating ecology and population structure of mobile marine vertebrates. The second, in 2013, refines the evolutionary divergence of humpback dolphins along their entire distribution range and proposes new taxonomic classification of the genus Sousa. The large amount of mark-recapture material and associated geographically referenced data collected during this project provided impetus to the development of an earlier prototype of computer software DISCOVERY - a photo-identification data-management system for individually recognisable animals (©2012 G. Gailey & L. Karczmarski). The DISCOVERY software is designed to provide a comprehensive approach to process, store, manage, and analyze photo-identification and other associated information. Analytical tools are incorporated to provide summary of data and export them into Excel, Access, SOCPROG, Mark, and GIS software for further processing and mark-recapture analyses. The DISCOVERY system can be particularly useful for maintaining a centralized database for projects involving multiple-species and large geographic scales with multiple research teams. It was designed to be highly customizable and applicable to any photo-identification project. Consequently, DISCOVERY has a broad multi-species application which has already been recognised internationally by research working with diverse species, both marine and terrestrial. One measure of such recognition was invited Keynote Lecture delivered on 5 November 2014 by both developers, G. Gailey and L. Karczmarski, to an international audience at the 1st symposium of the Photo-ID Wildlife Network held during 3-6 Nov 2014 at the University of Eastern Finland. The lecture is available on You Tube at: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CqQOIrURbtM&index=1&list=PLaNfvlZd-a3UarXVi4RqDxNIbo71Kxl7G DISCOVERY along with its comprehensive Manual is freely available online at http://www.biosch.hku.hk/ecology/staffhp/lk/Discovery/index.html where the contribution of RGC's support is prominently acknowledged.

768310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768310.value: The aim of this proposal is to apply chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) for assessing the detection of early degeneration in human lumbar intervertebral discs (IVD) in a non-invasive manner using 3 Tesla (3T) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) system. Disc degeneration is an irreversible process of an aberrant, cell-mediated response to progressive structure failure, which has been assumed to be a factor strongly associated with low back pain, one of the biggest global concerns with tremendous socioeconomic implications. Such pain may severely diminish functional activity, decrease quality of life, lead to loss of wages, and increase health-care costs. Currently, there is considerable interest in biological motion preservation, whereby growth factors or stem cells are introduced into the IVD to attempt to regenerate it. However, all available evidence would suggest that treatment is most efficacious in early degeneration as such approaches can only stop disc degeneration but not reverse it. Therefore, detecting early disc degeneration is of vital importance in order to identify subjects that are most suitable for these new therapies. Disc degeneration results in loss of glycosaminoglycan (GAG) and the reduction of the osmotic pressure. As a consequence the strength of the disc is weakened and shrinkage of the disc height is observed. Thus, it is essential to diagnose early degenerative changes at the stage of GAG loss in structurally sound disc by non-invasive quantification of the GAG content using a standard clinical MRI scanner. In an effort to improve the capability of MR techniques to quantitatively assess disc degeneration, relaxation times and water diffusivity are being studied with limitation to measures of only tissue hydration. In this proposal, we suggest two novel MRI techniques that can potentially provide more specific information. Firstly, we propose to use CEST imaging which is sensitive to changes in GAG content. Recently, detection of GAG content by using CEST imaging was successfully demonstrated in cartilage, however it has never been tried on human lumbar IVD. Secondly, we propose to apply DTI for assessing integrity of the extracellular matrix of the discs and to test whether DTI indices are sensitive to early disc degeneration. We have already conducted pilot studies using CEST and DTI which suggested that in vivo quantification of both methods is feasible in human lumbar IVD and may potentially be a clinical tool in identifying early degenerative changes, providing complementary information to conventional techniques. 該研究項目的目標是在3T磁力共振 (MRI) 系統中應用化學交換飽和轉移 (CEST) 和彌散張量影像 (DTI) 技術，以無創傷方式實現人體腰椎間盤退化的早期診斷。椎間盤退化是一種由漸進性組織損傷誘發的異常細胞反應，而此過程是不可逆轉的。研究認為椎間盤退化是導致腰痛疾病的一個重要因素。腰痛是全球性疾病之一，會嚴重損害人體組織功能，降低生活質素，減少工作收入並增加醫療衛生開支，對社會經濟產生巨大的影響。目前，新型的脊柱運動功能保留治療技術受到廣泛關注，該項技術通過將生長因子或幹細胞注入椎間盤來復原椎間盤細胞組織。不过，現有證據都反映出該治療只在椎間盤退化早期階段實施最為有效，因為它只能阻止椎間盤退化的過程，並不能逆轉退化。因此，椎間盤退化早期的檢查診斷變得非常重要，它能讓患者於椎間盤退化早期及時接受新型技術的治療。椎間盤的退化會導致其內部的糖胺聚糖 (GAG) 物質減少及組織的滲透壓力降低，這些變化造成椎間盤強度減弱，形體萎縮。在退化的初期，椎間盤細胞組織結構正常，但GAG已經開始流失，所以利用臨床磁力共振系統以無創傷的方式進行GAG定量分析成為早期診斷的重要一環。傳統上，利用MRI定量分析椎間盤退化的研究中，弛豫時間和水分子擴散係數是主要的研究指標，但這種研究的局限之處在於它們只能測量組織的水合程度。在這份研究計劃中，我們提出兩種新型的MRI技術，它們可能會提供更具體的組織信息。首先，我們建議使用CEST影像技術，它可以靈敏探測到GAG的變化。雖然人體腰椎間盤的CEST影像尚未經試驗，不過最新研究表明，CEST在軟骨組織中能成功探測到GAG。第二項技術是DTI，此技術可用以評估細胞外基質結構的完整性，並可檢測DTI各指標是否能靈敏探測到早期椎間盤退化。我們已經完成相關的CEST和DTI試驗，實驗結果顯示，利用這兩種方法進行體內腰椎間盤的定量分析是可行的，有可能成為臨床診斷早期腰椎間盤退化的一種重要技術，並與傳統影像技術相輔相承，提供全面的診斷信息。

768310.label: Realisation of objectives
768310.value: We conducted glycosaminoglycan chemical exchange saturation transfer (gagCEST) imaging for intervertebral discs (IVDs) of asymptomatic human volunteers (objectives #1, 2, 4). As with all CEST methods, especially for analysis, B0 field inhomogeneity can be of great concern as small shifts in frequency lead to large effects on the results. Although higher order shimming was used in our study, artifacts were apparent in IVDs. This suggest that even very small shifts (a few Hz) can have detrimental effects because the slope of the Z-spectrum is very steep due to the direct water saturation around 0 ppm. In our study, the B0 variations in IVDs and across the entire abdomen were measured by using a recently developed WASSR correction method, a new absolute water frequency mapping approach which was demonstrated in glycogen CEST application. Advantages of using WASSR over B0 field map or frequency correction approaches by centering of CEST Z-spectrum with polynomial fitting include relatively short scan time, sub-Hz accuracy and identical field reference condition with CEST due to same acquisition scheme. Our results show substantial improvement in spatial homogeneity of gagCEST maps in combination with WASSR correction. We examined DTI in healthy human lumbar IVDs to investigate difference in tissue microstructure of various IVD components (objectives #3-4). FA, one of the DTI-derived measures is especially sensitive to SNR. Thus, we have performed lumbar IVD imaging with multiple averaging which is known to provide higher SNR and subsequently allowed for better spatial resolution imaging in an acceptable time frame. However, one drawback using 3T is increased susceptibility induced distortion artifacts which require additional care. We therefore reduced distortion artifacts by rFOV using OVS presaturation pulses while maintaining relatively reasonable SNR and spatial resolution of images. In order to minimize rater-dependent bias for the quantitative analysis of DTI-derived indices while sustaining objectivity, histogram analysis was utilized in our study. Only the NP was examined for analysis due to poor SNR of the AF which stems from naturally lower water content compared with the NP. While SNR of the NP was around 15:1 which met generally accepted criteria for DTI analysis, SNR in the AF was considerably lower and therefore produced erroneous and unreliable indices. Although it has been proved possible to successfully map the lamellar architecture of the AF using DTI, this involved microimaging with small excised portions of the AF which is not feasible for in vivo human disc imaging.

768310.label: Major findings and research outcome
768310.value: We conducted glycosaminoglycan chemical exchange saturation transfer (gagCEST) imaging for intervertebral discs (IVDs) of asymptomatic human volunteers. This study demonstrates the feasibility of performing in vivo gagCEST quantification in lumbar IVDs. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report on CEST measurement for in vivo human IVDs. Several interesting observations were made; First, the mean CEST value of the nucleus pulposus (NP) was significantly greater than that of the annulus fibrosus (AF) throughout all disc levels, which is attributed to the differences in biochemical composition of the two regions and particularly to the fact that the NP has a greater concentration of proteoglycan (PG). Second, a trend of decreasing CEST values from L3/L4 to L4/L5 to L5/S1 was evident in the NP. This is in agreement with previous reports which indicated the higher prevalence of disc degeneration of the lower lumbar region due to the increased mechanical stress that may affect the synthesis and turnover of the disc’s matrix. Third, CEST signal was heterogeneous across the NP region in the surface and contour maps., in agreement with histological reports in the literature suggesting that PG content is not uniform across the NP (published in NMR in Biomedicine, 2011). Next, we examined diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) in healthy human lumbar IVDs to investigate difference in tissue microstructure of various IVD components, and to quantitatively assess age-related degenerative changes. Fractional anisotropy (FA) increased during the transition from young to elderly age groups, consistent with the developing fibrous nature and an overall increased microstructural complexity of the IVD. In the elderly group, the FA tended to increase more rapidly with age, possibly reflecting that the ongoing process of disc degeneration becomes accelerated during this age range, which is in agreement with postmortem studies. Meanwhile, mean diffusivity (MD) decreased with aging, consistent with a previous study, which is probably associated with the changes in the disc water content and shrinkage of the disc volume. Taking into account a primary role of PGs to retain water, it can be inferred that the loss of PG in the NP will accompany a significant drop in water content with aging. Interestingly, larger differences between young and elderly groups were observed in lower rather than upper disc levels. This agrees with histology reports in the literature suggesting that lumbar discs of lower levels experience more degeneration than upper levels. (published in Magnetic Resonance Imaging, 2012).

768310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
768310.value: As diagnosis with PG related changes of IVDs is particularly suited for early and subtle degenerative stages which conventional imaging techniques are not sensitive enough to, future longitudinal studies investigating larger cohorts of patients with CEST measures in addition to conventional MRI are needed to investigate whether CEST can be clinically used as a marker of disc degeneration. Moreover, further study using extracted disc samples is needed to validate the relationship between degenerative grade evaluated by DTI and the actual degenerative status of an individual IVD. In current studies, the relationship between quantitative DTI metrics and clinical symptoms such as lower back pain is unresolved because only healthy asymptomatic volunteers were included. Therefore, additional studies in patients with clinical symptoms, especially with disc-related pain, are necessary to investigate correlations between DTI metrics and the presence/severity of clinical symptoms. This will lead to validation of the clinical usefulness and relevance of DTI.

768310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
768310.value: Low back pain is a global concern with tremendous socioeconomic implications. Such pain may severely diminish functional activity, decrease quality of life, lead to loss of wages, and increase health-care costs. Although it has been assumed that IVD degeneration is a factor strongly associated with low back pain, the relationship between disc degeneration, MRI, and low back pain remains undefined. All available evidence suggests that treatment is most efficacious in early degeneration. Therefore methods of detecting early disc degeneration are of vital importance in order to identify subjects most suitable for therapies. As the depletion of macromolecules such as GAG in the matrix of IVD may be an initiating factor in degenerative disc disease, diagnostics of early degenerative changes at the stage of GAG loss in structurally healthy disc is essential, especially by using an in vivo imaging technique that quantitatively reflects GAG content. In addition, monitoring disc matrix integrity by using advanced in vivo MRI technique would enable further investigation on its pathological mechanism. Therefore, CEST MRI and DTI that are suggested in our proposal may be potential tools for the early detection of degenerative lumbar discs as they are more specific to chemical changes than conventional MR imaging.

768510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768510.value: During an infection by influenza A virus, RIG-I is a protein in mammalian cells responsible for recognising the presence of viral RNA that has invaded the cells and initiates a signalling pathway to trigger the innate immune response, the first line of defence against such infection, to produce cytokines. Upon detection and recognition of influenza A viral RNA (vRNA), RIG-I is activated and recruits the adaptor protein, IPS-1, thereby initiating the cascade of type-1 IFN response. Among patients infected with influenza A virus, patients with H5N1 infection have higher serum concentrations of cytokines and chemokines than patients with seasonal influenza. We have also observed that at a similar viral replication level, influenza A H5N1 but not H1N1 virus resulted in the hyperactivation of the RIG-I signalling pathway and knocking down RIG-I expression with siRNA rendered the pathway inactive. We therefore postulate RIG-I and vRNA recognition by RIG-I may play an important role in this hyperactivation. The present proposal aims to decipher the underlying reasons of hyperactivation of the pathway by the H5N1 virus and not the H1N1 virus by looking at the recognition and discrimination of the vRNA of the 2 influenza A subtypes by RIG-I and difference in activation of RIG-I, and in turn, the RIG-I signalling pathway upon binding of vRNA by these two influenza A subtypes. 在流感病毒A感染哺乳動物細胞的過程中，病毒的核糖核酸侵入了哺乳細胞後會激活機體天然免疫應答的信號通路。在此信號通路產生的細胞因子，通常是抵抗此類病毒感染的第一道防線。蛋白質RIG-I則在此信號通路中扮演重要的角色，因為它負責識別入侵病毒的核糖核酸。當流感病毒A的核糖核酸侵入細胞後，RIG-I被激活，並激活免疫應答的信號通路，同時招募在通路中傳遞其信號的其他接頭蛋白質，比如，IPS-1。 IPS-1再將信號繼續傳遞，從而開始了以此方式的級聯放大的信號傳遞過程。根據研究發現，在感染流感病毒A的病人體內，細胞因子和趨化因子的含量明顯的比感染普通季節性流感病毒的病人要高出許多。我們同時又發現，在相似的病毒復製水平上，RIG-I激活的信號通路在感染流感病毒A亞種H5N1的細胞較流感病毒A的另一亞種H1N1病毒為顯著。而且，如果用核糖核酸干擾技術將蛋白質RIG-I的功能在感染流感病毒A H5N1的細胞內失活，此信號通路將會被阻斷。所以我們推測，RIG-I以及在由其介導的核糖核酸和RIG-I識別的過程在細胞活化扮演著重要的角色。所以，我們目前的目的是通過結構生物學的研究對1) RIG-I識別兩種流感病毒A亞種（H5N1，H1N1) 核糖核酸的相互作用機制的比較, 2) RIG-I被激活的機制的比較，以及3）由通過RIG-I與核糖核酸結合所介導的信號通路的比較，來解碼H5N1病毒信號通路導致的細胞活化機制，並同時區分與H1N1病毒機制的不同。

768510.label: Realisation of objectives
768510.value: Objective 1 As reported, we previously expressed and purified two truncated constructs of human RIG-I (hRIG-I) (a.a. 243-796 and 263-796) and obtained preliminary crystallisation hits for construct a.a 243-796 in the presence of dsRNA and AMP.PNP (an analogue of ATP). However, the structures of hRIG-I 243-769 were published by Luo et al. (Luo et al. (2011) Cell 147:409-22), the structural studies of these constructs were terminated. Objective 2 We have cloned the DNA fragment encoding full length hRIG-I into the pET SUMO vector (Invitrogen) and the resulting plasmid was transformed into E. coli expression strain BL21(DE3)-Rosetta II (Novagen) for large scale expression of hRIG-I. Recombinant hRIG-I was purified to homogeneity by Ni affinity chromatography, sumo protease cleavage, followed by size exclusion chromatography on Superdex s200. Full length RIG-I was crystallised in 2 separate forms: apo and co-crystallizing with dsRNA. The apo RIG-I crystals diffracted to a resolution of 2.85Å at 1.0M sodium malonate pH 5.5. The dataset was collected and processed. The asymmetric unit was estimated to contain one copy of RIG-I. The phase was yet to be solved. Co-crystallizing hRIG-I with dsRNA formed long needle clusters at 1.0 M Imidazole pH 7.5 and 0.3M Tris pH 8.8, 18% ethanol. The crystal clusters were taken for x-ray diffraction and the maximum resolution was >20Å. Objective 3 As previously reported, IPS-1 CARD domain was expressed as a MBP fusion protein and purified by amylose resin followed by size exclusion chromatography. Pull-down assays were performed between purified IPS-1 CARD and hRIG-1 at various buffers and salt conditions, with or without dsRNA and/or AMPPNP or ATP. In all conditions tested, RIG-I and IPS-1 was eluted at separate fractions showing that the interaction was very weak. Nonetheless. high throughput crystallization trials were set up for co-crystallizing RIG-I and IPS-1 CARD. ~400 conditions were screened with the proteins mixed in 1:1 ratio, and in the presence of AMPPNP, MgCl2 and dsRNA. Unfortunately, no crystallization conditions have been identified to date. Objective 4 We have constructed yellow fluorescent protein or cyan fluorescent protein tagged full-length hRIG-I expression constructs and double fluorescent protein tagged full-length hRIG-I expression constructs. These constructs were being used to transfect mammalian cells and the effects of activation human RIG-I of RNAs will be studied by looking at the FRET signals.

768510.label: Major findings and research outcome
768510.value: 1) Expression, purification and crystallization of RIG-I Full length RIG-1 (925 residues) was successful expressed in recombinant with His tagged SUMO protein and purified. RIG-I was crystallized into 2 separate forms: apo and co-crystallizing with dsRNA. The apo RIG-I crystallized in 0.8-1.4M Na Malonate pH 5.5 -5.8. All crystals exhibit a bipyrimidal shape with a dimension of 0.05 × 0.05 × 0.05 mm The crystal was best diffracted to a resolution of 2.85Å at 1.0M sodium malonate pH 5.5. The dataset was collected and processed in a space group F23 with a unit cell parameters a= b= c= 216.43 Å , α= β= γ= 90°. The asymmetric unit was estimated to contain one copy of RIG-I, with a calculated crystal volume per unit molecular weight VM of 2.01 Å3 Da-1, corresponding to a solvent content of 38.8%. The results of the expression, purification and crystallization of apo RIG-I has been published in Acta Crystallographica Section F: Structural Biology Communications in 2014 (please refer to Part C Item 8). Co-crystallizing hRIG-I with dsRNA formed long needle clusters at 1.0 M Imidazole pH 7.5 and 0.3M Tris pH 8.8, 18% ethanol. The crystal clusters were taken for x-ray diffraction and the maximum resolution was >20Å. The crystallization conditions are still being optimized. 2) RIG-I and MDA-5 interaction with IPS-1 Pull-down assays were performed between RIG-I and IPS-1 CARD in the presence of dsRNA, with or without ATP/ AMPPNP. All pull-down assays showed that RIG-I did not bind with IPS-1 CARD as these two proteins were eluted in separate fractions. ITC further indicated that the binding between RIGI and IPS-1 were almost zero and equivalent to background heat exchange. Recent publications had reported K63 linked polyubiquitin chains by TRIM25, an E3 ligase were essential for RIG-I downstream signaling. Thus, the negative pulldown results for RIG-I and IPS-1 CARD were justified as no polyubiquitin chains were added in the in vitro experiment. We also performed pull-down assay of MDA-5, another member of the RIG-I like receptor family, which shared the same downstream signaling molecule IPS-1 for innate immune response but does not require ubiquitination to elicit the interaction. The pull-down of MDA-5 CARD and IPS-1 CARD showed strong binding and both proteins elute together. The ratio between IPS-1 and MDA-5 CARD was not in 1:1. All of the above experimental results are included the thesis of Miss Jane Kwok (see Part C item 10).

768510.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
768510.value: 1) RIG-1 phase problem At present, we were trying to soak apo RIG-I crystal with I3C solution to locate the iodide heavy atom. Iodine can give high anomalous signal to help solve the phase problem. The best dataset we have currently collected diffracted up to 4Å and we are actively trying to locate the iodine atoms in order to solve the structure of the apo RIG-I. Optimization of RIG-I co-crystallizing crystals was very challenging as the crystal size gave little improvements and is still in progress. The eventual solution of both structures would allow us to understand the conformational changes that would occur during the activation of RIG-I for binding to IPS-CARD and elicitation of the innate immune response upon invasion of RNA viruses. 2) RIG-I interactions with IPS-1 CARD In vitro ubiquitination of RIG-I CARD is underway to modify RIG-I CARD to facilitate interaction with IPS-1 CARD. Then, ITC could be applied to quantify binding parameters such as Kd. Once the stable complex can be obtained, we can proceed for crystal screening. Structures of intermolecular CARD-CARD had not been presented and could help to illuminate the homotypic interaction between CARDs of RIG-I and IPS-1, which was critical for triggering anti-viral response.

768510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
768510.value: The H5N1 avian strain of the influenza virus A causes severe threat worldwide. Upon viral infection our body is able to recognize the influenza virus and fight it off via the RIG-I stimulated innate immune response. RIG-I is able to recognize the influenza virus RNA and trigger downstream events by releasing its CARD domains to bind to and to stimulate an adaptor protein named IPS-1, triggering downstream events to fight off the virus. Being such an integral component in the innate defense against the influenza virus, there serves a major importance in understanding the mechanism on how the RIG-I triggers the downstream pathway upon recognition of the virus. Having obtained crystals of the inactivated form of RIG-I, we can now solve the structure of this form to examine the conformational changes between activated and inactivated forms RIG-I and how this conformational change stimulates downstream events. Moreover, we have determined that the interaction of CARD domains of RIG-I to the CARD domain of the adaptor IPS-1 protein requires modifications of RIG-I. Further studies can then be continued to obtain structures of the modified RIG_I bound to IPS-1 to fully understand the how these proteins interact to trigger the downstream immune response.

768610.value: 鑑定骨質疏鬆症全基因組研究中發現的候選基因的功能位點

768610.label: Project Objectives
768610.value: To detect the potential causal variant(s) of ten candidate genes identified by genome-wide association study of osteoporosis in 1,520 Hong Kong Southern Chinese subjects with extreme BMD phenotypes by massively parallel targeted sequencing. To study the genotype and phenotype correlation between the variant loci and osteoporosis phenotypes (including bone mineral density, bone geometry and osteoporotic fractures).

To study the genotype and phenotype correlation between the variant loci and osteoporosis phenotypes (including bone mineral density, bone geometry and osteoporotic fractures).

768610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768610.value: 骨質疏鬆症是一個常見的與年齡有關的疾病，主要特徵是低骨密度（bone mineral density, BMD）、骨微結構的退化和骨折風險的增加。本研究組之前在對骨質疏鬆症的遺傳和環境因子的鑑定研究中已經發現了一些新的疾病相關位點和驗證了一些骨質疏鬆症和骨折風險的重要因子。本研究組最近在1,520個有極值骨密度的中國南方人群中進行了全基因組關聯掃描研究（genome-wide association study, GWAS），發現了一些新的與骨密度和骨折相關的基因和變異位點。並且這些研究結果在其它的中國人群和高加索人群得到了驗證。為了找到這些基因中的真正的致病位點，本研究組將採用大規模平行靶標深測序（massively parallel targeted sequencing）的方法來對這些基因進行測序研究。鑑定到的與基因功能相關的致病位點將在體外的成骨細胞系和破骨細胞系模型中採用轉染/誘導沉默和基因表達的方法進行研究。最後，功能位點和骨質疏鬆症表型（包括骨密度、骨幾何結構和骨質疏鬆性骨折）之間的基因型和表型的相關性將在人類骨源細胞和外周血單核細胞中進行驗證。

768610.label: Realisation of objectives
768610.value: The original PI (Prof Annie Kung) and the new PI (Prof PC Sham) have worked together and published a number of peer-reviewed articles, including 2 that are high impact and have resulted from international collaboration. As an independent initiative, we have identified periostin as a novel susceptibility gene for osteoporosis and fracture. We have also successfully completed DNA sequencing of candidate genes identified by GWAS, identified 2 genes that may harbor rare susceptibility variants, and completed the validation of these results by SNP genotyping.

768810.value: 接受血液析離治療青光眼及非青光眼病人視神經損壞之評估

768810.label: Project Objectives
768810.value: To evaluate the IOP changes in glaucoma and non-glaucoma subjects during hemodialysis To find out if there is a real damage to the optic nerve as a consequence of long-term hemodialysis in non-glaucoma and glaucoma subjects
rows: To evaluate the IOP changes in glaucoma and non-glaucoma subjects during hemodialysis
To find out if there is a real damage to the optic nerve as a consequence of long-term hemodialysis in non-glaucoma and glaucoma subjects

768810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768810.value: Glaucoma means irreversible damage of the optic nerve usually due to high intraocular pressure (IOP) and/or unstable blood perfusion. The unstable blood perfusion theory has gained support from animal studies but large scale clinical study on human is lacking. We see a similar unstable perfusion setting in patients who are on hemodialysis, where systemic blood pressure is transiently reduced in a cyclical fashion throughout each hemodialysis session. These patients serve as an excellent clinical human model for the study of unstable perfusion in the pathogenesis of glaucoma. Studies on the long-term effect of hemodialysis on optic nerve function are lacking. Glaucoma patients undergoing hemodialysis have not been studied either. The aims of this study are i) to evaluate the IOP changes in glaucoma and non-glaucoma subjects during hemodialysis, ii) to find out if there is a real damage to the optic nerve as a consequence of long-term hemodialysis in non-glaucoma and glaucoma subjects. Results of this study should be able to 1) provide more evidence to support the unstable perfusion theory in the pathogenesis of normal tension glaucoma (a type of glaucoma related to perfusion problem); 2) provide important information on whether it is necessary to take preventative measures against the development and progression of glaucoma in patients undergoing hemodialysis; 3) provide a clinical human model for the future studies of neuroprotection in glaucoma. Thirty non-glaucoma and 30 glaucoma subjects requiring hemodialysis will be recruited and followed up for a period of 2 years. Fifty non-glaucoma patients on peritoneal dialysis will be recruited as control. Ophthalmological assessment will include documentation of IOP and optic disc morphology. The IOP will be measured at 30 minutes before, 1 hour after starting and 1 hour after completion of the hemodialysis. The cup-disc ratio (a marker of glaucomatous optic nerve damage) will be documented regularly in the follow-up period. Ophthalmic investigations on the function and structure of the optic nerve fibers will include visual field tests and retinal nerve fiber layer analysis using the Optical coherence tomography. Both tests will include a baseline measurement and will be repeated yearly for 2 years. Other systemic hemodynamic parameters including systemic blood pressure before, during and after hemodialysis will also be measured. The data will be gathered into a database and the results will be compared with various statistical analysis using the SPSS. Sub-group analysis will include types of glaucoma, types of hemodialysis and duration of hemodialysis. 青光眼是因高眼壓或不穩定血液供應導致視神經永久損壞. 不穩定血液供應理論從動物實中得到證實但大型臨床研究則缺乏. 我們見到在接受血液析離治療的病人可能有不穩定血液供應的類似情况-上血壓出現循環性的下降. 這些病人正適合成為不穩定血液供應導致青光眼的人類臨床研究模式. 現今暫未有血液析離治療對視神經功能影响的長期研究報告. 青光眼病人接受血液析離治療的研究亦未有. 此研究之目的為: 1) 評估青光眼及非青光眼病人接受血液析離治療時眼壓的變化; 2) 找出長期接受血液析離治療的病人其視神經是否受到破壞 研究報告可以: 1) 提供更多醫學證據持不穩定血液供應理論導致正常眼壓青光眼; 2) 提供重要資料讓我們決定是否需要對接受血液析離治療青光眼的病人提供預防視神經損壞措施; 3) 為將來提供一個青光眼保護視神經研究的人類臨床研究模式 研究會徵募大概六十名接受血液析離治療的病人. 在他們接受治療之前, 之中和之後量度眼壓,角膜厚度, 視神經頭/杯比例, 視野視和神經纖維層厚度. 他們會被跟進三年. 上述檢查除了量度眼壓外其餘都是非接觸和非創傷性的. 研究得出的數據會用统計學去分析.

768910.label: Realisation of objectives
768910.value: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the most common glomerulonephritis worldwide and an important cause of kidney failure. The disease is characterized by the deposition of "pathogenetic" polymeric immunoglobulin A1 (pIgA) in the glomerular mesangium followed by proliferation of the mesangial cell (HMC) and cellular infiltration. Podocytes hold a strategic position in the regulation of trafficking between the mesangial and tubulointerstitial compartments of the nephron. Injury to podocytes leads to heavy proteinuria, glomerulosclerosis, and loss of kidney function. While there is no direct binding of pathogenetic IgA to the podocytes in IgAN, mediators released from mesangial cells following IgA deposition could alter the expression of podocyte proteins and result in their dysregulation and apoptosis. In the present study, we have investigated in-depth the roles played by the podocytes in the disease progression of IgAN. We first elucidated the expression of various components of the podocytic renin-angiotensin system (RAS) under the impact of pIgA-activated HMC; followed by investigating the podocytic apoptosis following the alteration of RAS within the podocytes in IgAN. The mechanism and the related signaling pathways associated with the RAS-induced podocytic apoptosis in IgAN were also examined. Finally, we have also attempted to explore novel therapeutic approaches for IgAN by blocking the deleterious effect of altered RAS within the podocytes using prorenin receptor (PRR) blocker in addition to blockade by angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB). We have also defined the pathogenic role of RAS within podocytes using our in vitro cell culture model. Our data showed that humoral mediators released from the glomerular mesangium following pIgA deposition induced TNF-α synthesis by the podocytes. TNF-α up-regulated the expression of podocytic TNFR1 and AT1R. This TNF-α/TNFR1/AT1R axis leads to loss of cellular integrity and apoptosis in podocytes. Humoral mediators released from the glomerular mesangium following pIgA deposition also lead to enhanced PRR expression and CTGF production by the podocytes. This PRR/CTGF axis leads to podocytic injury through the activation of notch1 signaling pathway. Furthermore, AT1R activation also triggers the CTGF production by podocytes and forming a link between the two axes of podocytic apoptosis induction. We suggest that dual blockade of activation of NFκB and notch1 is essential to abolish the podocytic damage following mesangial pIgA deposition. However it would be very important to test the protective role of dual blockade of AT1R and PRR using an appropriate animal model, which is not yet examined in the present study and warrants further investigation.

768910.label: Major findings and research outcome
768910.value: In this study, we have shown that although podocytes do not bind pathogenic pIgA, humoral factors, particularly AngII, TNF-α released following pIgA binding to mesangial cells activated synthesis of TNF-α and CTGF by podocytes; these two key effectors promote apoptosis in podocytes. We used a conditionally immortalized human podocyte cell line as a model to examine the role of RAS in the pathogenesis of IgAN. Podocytes express a functional intrinsic RAS. The mesangial-podocytic crosstalk triggered by mesangial IgA deposition induced the overexpression of AT1R and PRR in podocytes, and these two receptors utilize different signal mechanism contributing to the podocytic apoptosis. [RAS in podocyte and the podocytic crosstalk have been written as reviews and was published in Contrib Nephrol. 2011;170:135-44 and Contrib Nephrol. 2014, vol 183, pp 54–63. Part of the data were published in Apoptosis, 2015, DOI: 10.1007/s10495-015-1117-1.] Glomerulo-podocytic communication plays an important role in the podocytic injury in IgAN. We examined the role of AT1R and PRR in podocytic apoptosis in IgAN. IgA-HMC media had no effect on AngII release by podocytes. IgA-HMC media significantly up-regulated the expression of AT1R and PRR, down-regulated nephrin expression and induced apoptosis in podocytes. Mono-blockade of AT1R, PRR, TNF-α or CTGF partially reduced podocytic apoptosis. IgA-HMC media activated NFκB, notch1 and HEY1 expression by podocytes and dual blockade of AT1R with PRR, or anti-TNF-α with anti-CTGF, effectively rescued the podocytic apoptosis induced by IgA-HMC media. Our data suggest that activation of podocytic NFκB and notch signaling pathways play an essential role in the podocytic apoptosis induced by glomerulo podocytic communication in IgAN. Simultaneously targeting the AT1R and PRR could be a potential therapeutic option to reduce the podocytic injury in IgAN. To translate our in vitro data to the bedside, glomerular apoptosis and the expression of TNF-α, TNFR1, AT1R, PRR and CTGF in renal biopsies from IgAN patients were examined by immunohistochemical staining. Up-regulated glomerular expression of TNF-α, TNFR1, AT1R, PRR and CTGF were observed in IgAN patients. Increased number of glomerular apoptotic cells was also visualized in IgAN patients. Of particular note, these up-regulated glomerular TNF-α, TNFR1, AT1R, PRR or CTGF expression and apoptotic events were much more profound in IgAN patients with severe proteinuria. [The data were presented at ISN Forefronts Symposium 2011 (Aarhus, Denmark) & ASN Kidney Week 2012 Annual Meeting (San Diego, USA). The results was published in Apoptosis, 2015, DOI: 10.1007/s10495-015-1117-1.]

768910.value: Our data have revealed that humoral mediators released from the glomerular mesangium following pIgA deposition activate the TNF-α/TNFR1/AT1R and the PRR/CTGF axis, leading to loss of cellular integrity and apoptosis in podocytes. We suggest that dual blockade of activation of NFκB and notch1 is essential to abolish the podocytic damage following mesangial pIgA deposition. However, clinical evidences demonstrating how the dysregulated expression of TNF-α, TNFR1, AT1R, PRR, and CTGF lead to podocytic apoptosis in IgAN patients are lacking. Furthermore, it would be very important to confirm the protective role of dual blockade of AT1R and PRR using an appropriate animal model, and warrants further investigations. Progressive dysfunction in podocytes is a common phenomenon in IgAN. Recent studies have focused on dissecting the dynamic interaction between podocytes and other glomerular resident cells including mesangial and endothelial cells. Our present study addressed the podocytic apoptosis induced by glomerulo-podocytic communication in IgAN, nonetheless, the possible communication or crosstalk between tubular epithelial cells and podocytes, which is also an important determinant of the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), however, is less investigated. Bridging this gap will facilitate the invention of more mechanism-oriented and targeted therapeutics for proteinuric glomerular or tubular diseases.

768910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
768910.value: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the major cause of end-stage renal disease in Hong Kong. The disease is characterized by deposition of "pathogenetic" polymeric immunoglobulin A1 (pIgA) in the kidney mesangium followed by proliferation of the mesangial cells (HMC). This will eventually lead to injury of the podocytes, damage of the glomerular filtration barrier and cause proteinuria. In this study, we have shown that although podocytes do not bind pathogenic pIgA, soluble factors, particularly angiotensin II, TNF-α released following pIgA binding to kidney HMC activated synthesis of TNF-α and CTGF by podocytes. We have further shown that these two key effectors were able to promote apoptosis in podocytes. The role of podocytic renin-angiotensin system (RAS) in the pathogenesis of IgAN was also studied. We revealed that podocytes express a functional RAS. The communication between HMC and podocytes, or the so-called mesangial-podocytic crosstalk, triggered by mesangial IgA deposition induced the overexpression of angiotensin II receptor subtype 1 (AT1R) and prorenin receptor (PRR) in podocytes, and these two receptors utilize different signal mechanisms contributing to the podocytic apoptosis. We suggested that simultaneously targeting the AT1R and PRR could be a potential therapeutic option to reduce the podocytic injury in IgAN.

769410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
769410.value: The obesity epidemic, seen in many parts of the world including China, is associated with increased death and suffering due to the atherosclerotic diseases, coronary heart disease and stroke. Inflammation of the fat tissues may be one mechanism whereby obesity leads to enhanced atherosclerosis. Recent research findings suggest that obesity-related nutrition overload and metabolic stress in fat cells lead to excess burdens to the cellular machineries, in turn resulting in the activation of various inflammatory pathways, including the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) pathway. We have shown that JNK activation in the fat cells enhances the production of various pro-inflammatory cell products, or cytokines, and the infiltration of fat tissues by inflammatory cells called macrophages. These cytokines, also produced by the macrophages, can accelerate the development of atherosclerosis by promoting insulin resistance and its related cardiovascular risk factors including hyperglycaemia, hypertension and hypertension, by increasing the macrophage infiltration of the vascular tress, and by reducing the production of adiponectin, an insulin-sensitizing, anti-inflammatory and anti-atherogenic hormone. It is now recognized that atherosclerosis is an inflammatory disease characterized by the infiltration of inflammatory cells and the presence of foam cells or cholesterol-filled macrophages. We have recently shown that adiponectin can increase circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPC) in obese diabetic db/db mice which have impaired EPC-mediated vascular repair. Reduced circulating EPC number is also found in humans with cardiovascular disease and/or various cardiovascular risk factors including diabetes and hyperlipidaemia, and predicts cardiovascular outcome, suggesting the importance of EPC in vascular integrity and protection from atherosclerotic diseases. EPC survival, differentiation and function can be adversely affected by inflammatory mediators. JNK activation, by impairing vascular response to insulin, can also reduce the production of nitric oxide, a molecule of crucial importance in EPC-mediated vascular repair. The above findings have prompted us to hypothesize that JNK activation in fat tissues may play a central role in linking obesity with atherosclerosis. We will test this hypothesis in the db/db mice and the hypercholesterolaemic, atherosclerosis-prone apo E deficient mice, by selectively blocking JNK activation in their fat tissues using transgenic technologies. We will investigate the effects on vascular repair and whether they are consequent to changes in EPC mobilization or function. The development of atherosclerotic lesions will also be assessed. In addition to improving our understanding of how obesity can lead to atherosclerotic diseases, this project may potentially lead to a new therapeutic approach to obesity-related atherosclerosis. 在現今世界，包括中國在內，肥胖症正日益流行，此與動脈粥樣硬化、冠心病和中風導致的死亡和病痛的增加有密切相關。最近的研究結果表明，與肥胖有關的營養過剩和脂肪細胞代謝會激使細胞機器負擔過重，從而激活了各種炎症反應的信號通路，包括JNK路徑。我們已經證實，在脂肪細胞內，JNK的激活導致了各種炎症免疫蛋白因子或細胞因子的產生，以及脂肪組織內巨噬細胞的浸潤。這些由巨噬細胞產生的細胞因子，通過進一步增加巨噬細胞浸潤和減少脂聯素（一種有胰島素增敏，抗炎和抗動脈粥樣硬化作用的激素）的生產，從而促進胰島素抵抗以及其相關的心血管疾病的危險因素，包括高血糖、高血壓和高血脂的發生，進而加速了動脈粥樣硬化的發展。現在我們已經認識到，動脈粥樣硬化實際上是一種炎症性疾病，它是以炎性細胞浸潤和泡沫細胞或膽固醇填充的巨噬細胞的存在為特點。最近，我們的實驗證實，脂聯素可以增加db/db肥胖糖尿病小鼠血循環中的內皮祖細胞（EPC）的數量，從而改善肥胖db/db小鼠本身的EPC介導的血管內皮的修復機能。同時，我們已經注意到，在一些患有心血管疾病和/或有各種心血管疾病危險因素（包括糖尿病和高血糖狀態）的人群，在外周血循環中也存在EPC減少的現象，而這種循環中EPC的減少可以預測心血管疾病的結果。這就表明，循環中的EPC在維持血管的完整以及粥樣硬化的防護方面有很重要的作用。炎症介質對EPC的生存，分化和功能有著廣泛的影響。JNK的活化導致血管對胰島素的反應受損，同時還可以減少一氧化氮的產生，而一氧化氮對EPC介導的血管修復至關重要。上述研究結果促使我們提出這樣的假設：在脂肪組織中JNK的活化可能在肥胖導致動脈粥樣硬化的過程中起著關鍵的作用。為了進一步的探索以上的假說，我們將在db/db小鼠和高膽固醇血合併動脈粥樣硬化的載脂蛋白E基因缺陷小鼠中，應用轉基因技術，有選擇性的阻斷脂肪組織中JNK的激活，進一步研究這種JNK活性的阻斷對血管修復的影響，以及是否因此而轉變EPC動員或功能。同時，我們還將評估動脈粥樣硬化病變的發展。這個項目，除了可以幫助我們進一步了解肥胖是如何導致動脈粥樣硬化性疾病的，同時也提出了一個潛在的針對肥胖有關的動脈粥樣硬化的治療靶向。

769410.label: Realisation of objectives
769410.value: For Objective 1, while cross-breeding ApoE-/- mice with transgenic mice with adipose-specific expression of a dominant negative form of JNK (dnJNK) to generate ApoE-/-/dnJNK (ADJ) mice, we first characterized whether diet-induced obesity and hypercholesterolaemia per se in wildtype (WT) mice could lead to impaired re-endothelialization, using a carotid artery injury model. HFHC diet treatment for 8 weeks significantly enhanced the body weight and % fat without affecting fasting and feeding blood glucose. However, these obese mice exhibited glucose intolerance compared to the lean control as evidenced by glucose intolerance test (GTT). Interestingly, these mice revealed no significant change in reendothelialization upon vascular injury compared with the lean control mice. Both lean and obese mice attained approximately 40% of vascular reendothelialization 3 days after the wire-induced injury in the carotid arteries (see appendices at end of report). These data suggest that obesity and hypercholesterolaemia per se do not result in vascular reendothlialization upon vascular injury. In view of these findings, we concluded that further investigating the role of tissue-specific deletion of JNK on vascular repair in ADJ mice and ApoE-/- mice with diet-induced obesity would not be justified. On the other hand we continued to address the remaining part of Objective 1 and investigated whether adipose-specific inactivation of JNK could protect against atherosclerosis development in hypercholesterolaemic mice on HFHC diet. Our subsequent studies in the ADJ mice showed that selective adipose tissue suppression of JNK activity could indeed protect against atherosclerosis. For Objective 2, to confirmatively demonstrate a long-distance communication between inflamed adipose tissue and the vasculature, we generated an atherogenic mouse model with the locally inflamed adipose tissue residing in the periphery, by transplanting epidermal white adipose tissue (eWAT) isolated from obese donor mice (WT or dn-JNK) into ApoE-/- recipients subcutaneously. We had modified the initially proposed protocol by transplanting the fat from dn-JNK and WT mice fed on HFHC diet, instead of standard diet-fed mice, for 12 weeks, to speed up the development of the atherosclerosis in the recipients. Compared to sham-operated mice, recipient ApoE-/- mice which received eWAT graft from obese WT mice (trans-WT) demonstrated increased atherosclerotic changes and systemic inflammation as evidenced by elevated serum levels of soluble tumour necrosis factor receptor 2 (sTNFR2) and adipocyte fatty acid binding protein (A-FABP). eWAT graft from dnJNK donors displayed significantly reduced inflammation compared to that from WT donors, even after 4 weeks of transplantation. The transplantation of eWAT from dnJNK donors largely reversed the accelerated atherogenesis observed in ApoE-/- recipients of eWAT from WT donors. Thus we have successfully established the visceral fat transplant model and demonstrated the role of JNK in the cross-talk between visceral fat inflammation and atherosclerosis. Because we previously found that A-FABP interacts with JNK via a positive feedback loop to modulate inflammatory responses (Hui X et al, J Biol Chem 2010), we proceeded beyond our original proposal to investigate the effect of continuous infusion of A-FABP into Apo-E-/- recipients of dnJNK donors, to levels comparable to those in recipients of obese wild-type donors. This additional study had provided further mechanistic insight on the JNK-mediated cross-talk between visceral fat and the vasculature.

769410.label: Major findings and research outcome
769410.value: After 10 weeks of high-fat-high-cholesterol diet treatment, ApoE deficient mice (ApoE-/-) with adipose-specific JNK inactivation, ApoE-/-/dnJNK (ADJ), had significantly reduced atherosclerotic plaques, macrophage accumulation, and smooth muscle cell proliferation in the aortic root region when compared with ApoE-/- mice. A reduced macrophage infiltration was also observed in the epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) in ADJ mice, as shown by histology, and the expression levels of pro-inflammatory markers including macrophage chemoattractant protein 1 (MCP-1), tumour necrosis factor α (TNF-α), interleukin 1β (IL-1β), and adipocyte fatty acid binding protein (A-FABP) were significantly lower in eWAT in ADJ mice than in ApoE-/- mice. There was a significant reduction in systemic inflammation in ADJ mice, as evidenced by reduced levels of serum MCP-1 and A-FABP. These significant reductions in visceral fat and systemic inflammation in the ADJ mice, conferred by adipose-specific JNK inactivation, were not associated with significant changes in lipid or glucose metabolism, but were sufficient to provide protection against atherosclerosis in these ApoE deficient mice. Using the visceral fat transplant model, we found that lean ApoE-/- mice that received transplantation of visceral fat from obese wild-type donor mice for 4 weeks showed exacerbated systemic inflammation and atherosclerotic plaque formation. Conversely, lean ApoE-/- recipients carrying visceral fat graft from obese dnJNK donors were protected against increased systemic inflammation, as reflected by circulating levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines including adipocyte fatty acid binding protein (A-FABP), and accelerated atherogenesis. The beneficial effects of adipose-specific JNK inactivation on atherogenesis in ApoE-/- recipients could be significantly abrogated by continuous infusion of recombinant A-FABP to levels comparable to those in recipients of obese wild-type mice. We concluded therefore that enhanced atherosclerosis in obesity can be attributed, at least in part, to a distant cross-talk between visceral fat and the vasculature, mediated by the release of pro-inflammatory adipokines, such as A-FABP, from the inflamed visceral adipose tissue with JNK activation. The above data have been included in a manuscript submitted to Circulation and several abstracts presented at international meetings.

769410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
769410.value: A recent publication (Cao H et al, Cell Metabolism 2013) has reported that, in mice, recombinant A-FABP can stimulate hepatic gluconeogenesis whereas treatment with a neutralizing antibody for 2 weeks reduces hepatic glucose production. It should be noted that monoclonal antibodies directed against therapeutic target molecules or receptors are increasingly used in targeted therapy for treating various diseases, including cancers, immunological diseases and severe hypercholesterolaemia. Our findings in the current project would suggest that monoclonal antibodies against A-FABP may be explored for the prevention and treatment of atherosclerotic diseases, such as coronary artery diseases and stroke. On the other hand, we and others have found that obesity (Zhang X et al, Diabetes 2008) and various obesity-related disorders, including diabetes (Chen C et al, Diabetes Care 2011), non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (Dushay J et al,Gastroenterology 2010) and atherosclerosis (Chow WS et al, ATVB 2013), are associated with increased levels of fibroblastic growth factor 21 (FGF21), a metabolic hormone being actively investigated in preclinical and clinical studies for the treatment of diabetes and hyperlipidaemia (Woo YC et al, Clin Endocrinol 2013). The possible presence of FGF21 resistance was demonstrated in obese mice in which impaired FGF21 signaling consequent to JNK-mediated TNF-α activation in the inflamed adipose tissue was observed (Diaz-Defin J et al, Endocrinol 2012). Our ADJ mice can potentially be employed to investigate whether and how adipose tissue FGF21 resistance is involved in the pathogenesis of obesity-related atherosclerotic diseases.

769410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
769410.value: Obesity is associated with increased risk of atherosclerotic diseases, such as heart disease and stroke. In this study, we have demonstrated the importance of fat tissue inflammation in the development of atherosclerosis. It has been observed that individuals with central obesity or excessive fat in their abdomen (so-called visceral fat), have a greater risk of dying from atherosclerotic diseases, than those who cumulate fat tissue mainly under the skin. In this study, we have identified an underlying mechanism for this observation. We have demonstrated that the inflamed visceral fat from obese mice, when transplanted under the skin into lean mice which are prone to atherosclerosis, can accelerate the development of atherosclerosis in these lean mice. This accelerated atherosclerosis can be blocked if the visceral fat from the donor mice is genetically suppressed. Our studies also demonstrate that the distant inter-talk between visceral fat and the blood vessels is mediated by the increased release of inflammatory factors from the visceral fat, such as adipocyte fatty acid binding protein. Therefore, strategies which block the action of these inflammatory factors can potentially be explored for the prevention of coronary artery diseases and stroke, common causes of death in our aging population.

769610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
769610.value: The differentiation of B cells into antibody-secreting plasma cells, or plasmacytic differentiation, is crucial for the humoral immune response. Tight regulation of this process is important for providing adequate immune defence while avoiding pathogenic development of malignancies or autoimmunity. Although the overall transcription regulation for plasmacytic differentiation has been identified, the mechanisms regulating Blimp-1, the master regulator of plasmacytic differentiation, remain incompletely understood. Blimp-1 is required for plasmacytic differentiation, immunoglobulin secretion and plasma cell survival. Elevated levels of Blimp-1 are frequently found in human multiple myeloma, the second most common hematological cancer that is formed by malignant plasma cells. In addition, Blimp-1 has been shown to be required for the survival of multiple myeloma and formation of plasmacytoma in mice. Recently, altered microRNA expression in plasmacytic differentiation and plasma cell malignancies has been observed. Therefore, further studies to explore the regulatory mechanisms of Blimp-1 expression mediated by the microRNA pathway will provide a fuller understanding of the humoral immunity as well as pathophysiology of B cell development. Recent studies including ours have shown that leptin plays an important role in both innate and adaptive immunity. While evidence exists for its involvement in humoral immunity, it remains largely unclear how leptin affects plasmacytic differentiation and the survival of plasma cells. Elevated leptin serum levels have been found in patients with multiple myeloma, and aberrant expression of leptin receptor was observed in their cancer cells. In our pilot studies, we found that leptin induced Blimp-1 expression and suppressed microRNAs that can potentially target the putative sites in the 3’ untranslated region of Blimp-1 RNA. Importantly, we also found that leptin promoted plasmacytic differentiation and the survival of both plasma cells and plasmacytoma cells, indicating a role for leptin signaling in regulating plasmacytic differentiation and survival of both normal and malignant plasma cells. In this proposal we aim to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which leptin regulates Blimp-1 expression during plasmacytic differentiation and plasma cell maintenance via the microRNA pathway. Moreover, we will perform a series of studies to assess the function of leptin in enhancing the growth of malignant plasma cells in vitro and in vivo. These findings will facilitate the potential design of new therapeutic strategies for targeting malignant plasma cells. N/A

769710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
769710.value: Cardiovascular disease is a widely recognized public health problem. In China rapid economic development has driven the attendant epidemiologic transition to a high burden pattern of chronic conditions. Sex-steroids are increasingly seen as relevant to these conditions in men as well as women. A growing number of observational studies suggest that low testosterone is associated with cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in men, and hence that testosterone therapy might be beneficial in older men. However, trials of hormone replacement therapy in women did not show the same benefits as observational studies, indicating the need for caution and to triangulate the evidence. Moreover, we have developed and substantiated a novel, physiologically-based hypothesis suggesting that nutritionally and inter-generationally driven changes to the gonadotrophic axis may underlie the epidemic of ischemic heart disease in men that occurs with economic development. However, large scale trials to test the life-time role of testosterone in cardiovascular disease are neither feasible nor ethical. In this proposal, building on two complementary existing studies from Southern China, we will take advantage of recent advances in genetics to test whether genetic bio-markers of pubertal sex-steroids are associated with later life cardiovascular disease risk factors. Using genetic polymorphisms as bio-markers of endogenous exposures has the potential to provide the same level of evidence concerning causality as a trial. We will use a sample of 600 adolescents from our large (n=8,327) birth cohort “Children of 1997” to identify a parsimonious set of genetic polymorphisms associated with pubertal sex-steroids, from which we will derive and validate genetic prediction equations for pubertal sex-steroids. We will then use a sample of 5,040 older adults from the Guangzhou Biobank Cohort Study to assess the associations of both these genetic polymorphisms and estimated pubertal sex-steroids with existing data on cardiovascular disease risk factors. This proposal has the unique potential to provide a timely answer to a question relevant to the cardiovascular health of the growing number of older men worldwide, and hence inform interventions. Simultaneously, it will extend the state of the science by confirming (or refuting) a novel, physiologically-based hypothesis concerning the etiology of ischemic heart disease. As such it may also identify, as targets for intervention, groups particularly vulnerable to cardiovascular disease in Hong Kong and mainland China or other countries currently undergoing rapid economic development. 心血管病是非常重要的公共衛生問題，中國的快速經濟發展引致流行病轉移至大量的慢性病負擔。在男女性，性類固醇與慢性病有關。越來越多研究顯示低睪酮與男性心血管病和死亡有關。但激素補充治療測試在女性中未能像觀察的研究般顯示效益。因此，我們發展一個創新和基於生理學的假設，就是營養和跨代因素引致促性腺軸變化是男性缺血性心臟病隨經濟發展增加的原因。但是大型測試生命過程中睪酮對心血管病的影響並不可行和不道德。 本研究基於兩個在南中國現存的研究，我們利用遺傳學去研究青春期性類固醇的基因標記是否與生命稍後期的心血管病危險因素有關。利用基因多態性作為內在暴露的生物標記可提供與測試相等的因果證據。我們會用97的兒女香港出生隊列(8,327人)中的600青少年樣本去找出一系列與性類固醇有關的基因多態性，從而獲得和檢測基因預測青春期性類固醇的方程式。然後用廣州生物庫隊列5,040較年長成人的樣本去評估這些基因多態性與青春期性類固醇的估值和現有的心血危險因素的關係。 此研究有獨特的潛質去及時提供有關世界上較年長的男性的心血管病為什麼不住增加的答案，從而協助設計干預方法。同時可以測試一個新的建基於生理學關於心血管病成因的假設，擴展科學研究範疇，並為香港、中國大陸和其他經濟急速發展的國家的干預方法和對象提供依據。

769710.label: Realisation of objectives
769710.value: To set the scene in this study we first implemented a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to summarize the effects of testosterone therapy on cardiovascular-related event. We used a separate-sample two-stage Mendelian randomization analysis to obtain an unbiased estimate for causal inference concerning the association of testosterone and other sex-steroids with cardiovascular risk factors in older people, using a step-by-step process. a) First, genetic scores for predicting serum testosterone and estradiol were developed in 290 young Southern Chinese men and 237 young women from Hong Kong based on a parsimonious set of genetic polymorphisms from selected related SNPs. We selected the candidate SNPs from a literature review and then tested Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium and Linkage disequilibrium. Then stepwise linear regression with bootstrapping internal validation was used to find a parsimonious set of SNPs which best predicted log testosterone and log estradiol, because the distribution of sex hormones was skewed. b) In older adults we assessed the associations of these genetic polymorphisms and estimated sex-steroids with cardiovascular disease risk factors. Specifically, we examined the association of genetically predicted testosterone and estrogen with CVD risk factors (SBP, DBP, LDL-cholesterol, HDL cholesterol and fasting glucose), Framingham score and systemic inflammation (white blood cell, lymphocyte, granulocyte count and hs-CRP) among 4,212 older men and 3,096 older women from the Guangzhou Biobank Cohort Study, using multivariable linear regression. c) We also tested the hypothesis that pubertal sex-steroids, i.e., genetically predicted serum testosterone and estrogen, have long-term sex specific effects on body shape, i.e., waist-hip ratio. d) Finally, we also tested the hypothesis that pubertal sex-steroids, i.e., genetically predicted serum testosterone and estrogen, have long-term sex specific effects on body shape, i.e., waist-hip ratio fasting glucose and diabetes in men and women. We have finished the analysis above and submitted 5 papers. Our most important findings concern the role of testosterone among men, where we found that genetically predicted endogenous testosterone was associated with higher LDL-cholesterol and lower HDL-cholesterol. Moreover, genetically predicted testosterone was also associated with higher Framingham score, although the confidence intervals included no effect. Our findings are consistent with our published meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials showing that testosterone therapy raises the risk of a cardiovascular event. As such, our study adds to the serious public health concern of cardiovascular risk from the widespread use of testosterone replacement therapy in older men.

769710.label: Major findings and research outcome
769710.value: Our scene setting systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found that exogenous testosterone therapy increased the risk of cardiovascular-related events, with considerable publication bias and a higher risk among trials not funded by the pharmaceutical industry. From our first study in young people, we were able to develop genetic prediction rules successfully for peak serum testosterone and estrogen. In young men, three SNPs (rs10046, rs1008805, rs1256031) were selected for the genetic prediction of log testosterone as -0.07×rs1008805+0.07×rs10046-0.07×rs1256031+3.0. In young women, two SNPs, rs1008805 in CYP19A1 and rs2175898 in ESR1 were selected for the genetic prediction of log 17β-estradiol as 0.1×rs1008805-0.1×rs2175898+4.7. As expected, genetically predicted testosterone and estradiol were not associated with socioeconomic position or lifestyle, including age, education, smoking status and use of alcohol. We then projected these predictions onto a study of older people where we had obtained these SNPs, so as to assess the key relations of genetically predicted testosterone and estrogen with CVD risk factors, Framingham score and diabetes. Our key findings were that in older men, predicted testosterone was unrelated to blood pressure, fasting glucose or Framingham score but was associated with higher LDL-cholesterol (0.02 mmol/L, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.04) and lower HDL-cholesterol (-0.01 mmol/L, 95% CI -0.02 to -0.001). (Presented at Society of Epidemiology, June 2013, Boston, USA and paper revised and resubmitted to International Journal of Epidemiology) Using a Mendelian randomization analysis with an SSIV estimator to minimize reverse causality in southern Chinese men, we found no indication that endogenous testosterone was associated with healthier CVD risk factors. On the contrary it was associated with an unhealthier lipid profile. Our novel study provides no support for protective effects of endogenous testosterone on cardiovascular risk factors or Framingham score. Testosterone should be used cautiously considering the detrimental effects on exogenous testosterone on cardiovascular related events, and of endogenous testosterone on LDL- and HDL-cholesterol.

769710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
769710.value: This project has been very successful in generating unbiased estimates of the effects of testosterone on cardiovascular disease risk factors, we have extended it to use the same approach to assess a) the effect endogenous testosterone on systemic inflammation, where we found little clear effect. The resulting paper is now under review at Epidemiology. b) the effect of endogenous estrogen on systemic inflammation where, we found estrogen negatively associated with systemic inflammation. The resulting paper has been submitted to the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health. c) the effect of endogenous testosterone on cognition, where we found no association. The resulting paper is to be submitted to American Journal of Epidemiology (AJE). We also compared testosterone and estrogen in young Chinese men with US men. Testosterone and estrogen were lower among young men in Hong Kong than the US. The resulting papers are at the American Journal of Human Biology and AJE. Finally, since this project was designed, work on prostate cancer has shown testosterone is not a complete indicator of androgen activity. We are planning to use the same study design (SSIV) in the same studies to assess the role of androgen activity in cardiovascular disease and its risk of androgen.

769710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
769710.value: With socio-economic development, non-communicable disease, especially cardiovascular disease has become the leading cause of morbidity globally. Observationally testosterone among men is negatively correlated with cardiovascular disease and its risk factors, but these correlations could be due to many other factors, such as testosterone falling with ill-health. Large-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of testosterone replacement are not ethical because of the potential risks of prostate cancer. We used a novel study design to examine the causal association of testosterone with cardiovascular risk factors without any potentially harmful interventions. Our study, comparing people with genetically different levels of testosterone, did not support any protective effects of endogenous testosterone on cardiovascular risk factors. Instead, we found testosterone associated with unhealthy lipid profile, consist with a meta-analysis of RCTs showing that testosterone causes cardiovascular-related events. This study indicates that androgens may be a modifiable causal factor underlying men’s greater vulnerability to cardiovascular disease, with corresponding implications for developing new effective treatment and prevention strategies. In contrast, testosterone therapy needs to be used very cautiously, as it could be harmful.

769810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
769810.value: 最近由結核分枝桿菌（MTB）所引起的肺結核病例在全球有大量增加, 而這些病例和愛滋病毒(HIV)在全世界的廣泛傳播是息息相關的. 現時, 我們對於肺結核病的發病機制仍未完全了解, 而在愛滋病毒如何加強結核分枝桿菌感染和傳播這方面更是未知數。過往的研究顯示促炎性細胞因子，包括干擾素伽瑪和腫瘤壞死因子-α能刺激免疫系統去形成肉芽腫來控制結核分枝桿菌、鳥分枝桿菌複合群或卡介苗等分枝桿菌的擴散。 在已往香港研究資助局(研資局)撥款的研究項目中, 我們發現分枝桿菌能利用細胞內作為抗菌的信號轉導通路去幫助它們生存。 同時, 愛滋病毒或分支桿菌都可以通過絲裂原活化蛋白激酶和細胞因子如白細胞介素-10的失調來逃避免疫系統的殺菌作用。在進行中的研資局資助研究項目中（GRF＃768507，2007-2010），我們報告了愛滋病毒Tat蛋白能在巨噬細胞中增加SOCS2 的表達, 從而壓制由干擾素伽瑪引起主要組織相容性複合體第二型的基因表達。由此可見, 我們可以透過了解細胞因子失調的病因和病機中，尋找更多線索去發展新的療法。 最近的研究報告顯示當細胞受到血清、細胞因子或生長因子的剌激後，c-Jun氨基末端激酶會通過一個負責調控細胞命運的轉錄因子 — ATF3，去作出應激反應。ATF3是致癌基因 — c-Myc的下游因子，它的作用是調控c-Myc的功能。而且，在我們的初步實驗結果中, 分枝桿菌能上調c-Myc來誘導干擾素伽瑪的表達。因此，我們假設結核分枝桿菌能通過特定的信號激酶去激活c-Myc和相關致癌基因在人類巨噬細胞中的表達，從而誘導促炎細胞因子而達致抗菌的效果。 我們特定的研究目標是：1）被卡介苗/鳥分枝桿菌複合群感染時會否影響c-Myc基因的表達；2）探究卡介苗/鳥分枝桿菌複合群是通過那一些信號通路和細胞因子來引起c-Myc基因表達；3）證明那一些重要的轉錄因子和促炎細胞因子是被c-Myc蛋白所調控；以及4）研究c-Myc蛋白所調控的細胞信號通路和細胞因子對消滅分枝桿菌的功效。 我們的研究結果將對分支桿菌與巨噬細胞的相互作用，以及和致癌基因與它們相關的轉錄因子在細胞信號通路及細胞反應的作用提供新的見解。研究結果將有助於為免疫功能失調的患者設計新和有效的療法去對付結核分枝桿菌的感染。

769810.label: Realisation of objectives
769810.value: Tuberculosis (TB) caused by the infection of mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) is the second leading cause of death from an infectious diseases of the world. Many fundamental questions regarding MTB pathogenesis remain unanswered. At the beginning of the project, we observed mycobacteria Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) could specifically induce the expression of the oncogene c-Myc. As c-Myc could regulate about 15% of the genes, we hypothesize that c-Myc may play a role in the immune responses against mycobacterial infection. Our first objective was to examine whether mycobacteria could induce c-Myc expression. In order to examine this, primary human blood macrophages (PBMac) were treated with mycobacteria including Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) and M. avium (MAC). The results showed that the c-Myc protein levels and its mRNA levels were increased by these mycobacteria in a dose and time-dependent manner. Next, we delineated the signaling pathways in mycobacteria induced c-Myc expression. We treated the primary macrophages with different kinases specific inhibitors followed by BCG stimulation. The results showed that inhibition of ERK1/2 and JNK1/2, but not p38 MAPK and NF-κB, suppressed BCG induced c-Myc expression. We also examined the effect of an anti-inflammatory cytokine, IL-10 on BCG induced c-Myc expression. It showed that IL-10 did not suppress the BCG induced c-Myc expression. In addition to IL-10, we also pretreated Epidermal growth factor (EGF) prior to BCG challenge. Similar to IL-10, EGF also could not suppress BCG induced c-Myc expression. For objective 3, we first knocked down the c-Myc expression by si-RNA targets the coding region of Myc mRNA in macrophage. We then added the BCG or MAC to the c-Myc si-RNA or control si-RNA treated primary macrophage and examined the cytokine expression profile. The results showed that mycobacteria induced TNF-α and IL-6 were suppressed in c-Myc siRNA treated macrophage but not in the control si-RNA treated macrophages. We further delineated c-Myc specifically enhanced mycobacteria-activation of IRAK1 as well as the downstream kinases including ERK1/2 and p38 kinases and NF-kB activation. These results demonstrated c-Myc plays a role in mycobacteria induced cytokine production by enhancing the activities of IRAK1, ERK1/2, p38 MAPK and NF-kB. Furthermore, our experiments for last objective illustrated that the intracellular growth of mycobacteria was enhanced in c-Myc siRNA treated macrophage. In summary, c-Myc could be induced by mycobacterial infection. The induced c-Myc participated in the mycobacteria induced cytokine production and affects the intracellular survival of the mycobacteria in the macrophage.

769810.label: Major findings and research outcome
769810.value: Major findings Our findings indicated that an oncogene c-Myc plays a role in the immune response against mycobacterial infection. Previously, the studies on c-Myc are mainly on its role in oncogenesis. It is showed that c-Myc, as a transcription factor regulates about 15% of the total genes in whole genome, but its role in immune responses against infection is unknown. Our results demonstrated that in normal human primary macrophages, mycobacterial infection induced c-Myc expression was through the ERK1/2 and JNK activation. The induced c-Myc was located at the cytoplasm, rather than in the nucleus normally in cancer cells. In order to examine the role of the induced c-Myc, we used siRNA to knock down the c-Myc expression and examine the immune response after mycobacterial infection. Our results showed that mycobacteria induced proinflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-alpha could be suppressed by the knock down of c-Myc expression, via the suppression of MAPK activation. As proinflammtory cytokines are to induce inflammation and leading to the tissue damage, inhibition of the overproduction of proinflammatory cytokines could reduce the development of chronic inflammation. Since the production of anti-inflammatory cytokines is another way to inhibit the inflammation, we also examined whether c-Myc also induce the production of anti-inflammatory cytokine, IL-10. Our data showed mycobacteria induced IL-10 production was not regulated by c-Myc, also IL-10 cannot affect the induction of c-Myc induced by mycobacteria. Therefore, c-Myc was specifically affected the production of proinflammatory cytokines and its regulatory pathways. We also investigated the intracellular growth of the mycobacteria in the macrophages. This is a critical step to limit the further dissemination of the pathogens and hence resolve the infection. Our results demonstrated the growth of mycobacteria BCG or MAC was enhanced when c-Myc expression was knocked down. In summary, c-Myc potentiates the immune responses against mycobacterial infection by suppressing the proinflammatory cytokines production and the intracellular growth of the mycobacteria. Research outcomes The results of this study were published in PNAS, which is a well-known journal in the field of general science. We also presented this study in different local and international conferences with presentation awards. Part of the results were also filed for US patent application and is currently under review. The Ph.D student working on this project is recruited by Monash Institute of Medical Research in Australia as post-doctoral fellow.

769810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
769810.value: Results from this study showed that c-Myc plays a role in mycobacterial infection. Therefore, we established another project and funded by HMRF to further study the role c-Myc in mycobacteria induced T-cell responses, which is critical to develop tuberculosis. We also started the in vivo experiments as stated in our proposal to confirm the findings obtained in the in vitro experiments. We would like to use different c-Myc chemical inhibitors such as 10058-F4 for the in vivo study. Since the inhibition of c-Myc is one of the therapeutic targets for cancer treatment, our findings may provide an insight on the side effects of the future use of c-Myc inhibitors. Apart from mycobacterial infection, we will also investigate the role of c-Myc in other infectious diseases such as MRSA, influenza, HPV and EBV. If the pathogens could induce the c-Myc expression and action, this may be one of the reasons for the development of viral related cancer.

769810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
769810.value: Tuberculosis (TB) caused by the infection of mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) is the second leading cause of death from an infectious diseases of the world. In 2013, there is about one-third of the world’s population infected with Mtb, resulting in 1.2–1.5 million deaths annually. In Hong Kong, there are about 6000 new cases of tuberculosis each year. Mtb usually infect patient’s lung (pulmonary TB) and sometimes it will disseminate to other tissues (extrapulmonary TB). There are about 10% of people infected with Mtb will develop into active TB. Therefore, we have to delineate the mechanisms of mycobacterial infection and identify the key modulators for the development of specific and effective treatment. The results from this study illustrated our immune system could make use of an oncogene, c-Myc to fight against the mycobacterial infection, by controlling the overwhelmed immune responses and suppressed the survival of the mycobacteria in the cells. Therefore, the mycobacteria infection can be stopped. Our findings would provide new insights into mycobacterial pathogenesis and potential means for developing novel therapeutics.
