770010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
770010.value: Many emerging infectious diseases are zoonoses that cause epidemics in humans after overcoming the inter-species barrier, best exemplified by SARS coronavirus (SARS-CoV) and the latest swine-origin H1N1 pandemic. Therefore, identifying possible animal origins or counterparts of emerging viruses is important in understanding their epidemiology, evolution and potential for re-emergence. Several novel human parvoviruses have been discovered in the past few years. Recently, we have also discovered novel porcine and bovine parvoviruses closely related to one of these novel human parvoviruses, human parvovirus 4 (PARV4), and described a novel genus Hokovirus to describe this group of novel parvoviruses. Apart from PARV4, a previously undescribed parvovirus, human bocavirus (HBoV) belonging to the genus Bocavirus, was identified in 2005 and subsequently confirmed to be associated with respiratory diseases in children worldwide. Soon after its discovery, we have performed the first study to describe its clinical epidemiology in children in Hong Kong and discovered an association between HBoV and gastroenteritis in children. Subsequently HBoV has been reported in feces of children from different countries, supporting that HBoV is not only a respiratory virus. At the moment, at least three different genotypes of HBoV have been identified. However, the molecular evolution of HBoV in relation to related animal bocaviruses and the possible animal origin of these emerging parvoviruses are unknown. In this project, we aim at identifying possible animal origin of HBoV and novel animal bocaviruses, and characterizing the molecular evolution and epidemiology of these emerging parvovirueses. For identifying the animal bocaviruses, we propose to carry out a study on various animal specimens to detect the presence of bocaviruses by PCR. The full-length genome sequence of the novel bocaviruses identified will be determined for molecular characterization and their evolution and epidemiology will be studied. The feasibility of the current project is supported by our preliminary results on the existence of previously unidentified bocaviruses from porcine samples and our previous success in the study of other novel viruses and animal origins of emerging human viruses.

770010.label: Realisation of objectives
770010.value: For the first objective, we have carried out experiments to detect bocaviruses in a variety of animal species including cats, dogs, bats, birds, rodents, chicken and rodents, using PCR with conserved primers specifically designed to target bocaviruses. During the process, we have identified several novel animal bocaviruses, including two novel porcine bocaviruses from swine, a novel feline bocavirus from domestic cat and a novel genogroup of canine bocavirus from dogs in Hong Kong. Although no direct animal ancestor of HBoV can be identified, our results expand the understanding of the diversity and evolution of bocaviruses, and the existence of bocaviruses in cats and dogs which are the commonest domestic pets that share close habitat with humans. For the second objective, we have performed complete genome sequencing and genetic diversity studies on the novel animal bocaviruses discovered. For the porcine bocaviruses, since marked nucleotide polymorphisms were observed in the partial VP1 sequences, complete VP1 genes from three fecal and one nasopharyngeal specimens were cloned and sequenced, which suggested the presence of two different bocaviruses and demonstrated significant intra- and inter-host genetic diversity. Complete genome sequences revealed the presence of two novel bocaviruses, PBoV3 and PBoV4, in a fecal and nasopharyngeal specimen respectively, with two genotypes, PBoV4-1 and PBoV4-2, in the latter. Phylogenetic analysis showed that they were distantly to other bocaviruses, forming a distinct cluster within the genus. Recombination analysis showed possible recombination events among VP1 sequences of PBoV4 strains from a fecal specimen, with two (68-bp and 71-bp) breakpoints identified, suggesting that different strains/variants within the same host could have arisen from recombination. Three genomes of feline bocavirus and four genomes of canine bocavirus were also sequenced. Partial VP1/VP2 sequence analysis of 23 FBoV and 25 CBoV strains demonstrated inter-host genetic diversity, with two potential genetic groups of FBoV and a novel CBoV group, CBoV-HK, distinct from the three groups, CBoV-A to C, found in USA. For the third objective, we have examined the epidemiology of these novel animal bocaviruses by PCR. For the porcine bocaviruses, they were present in 16.5 % (55/333) of porcine samples (including lymph nodes, serum, nasopharyngeal and fecal samples). For the feline bocavirus, it was detected in 7.2%, 0.3%, 1.6%, 2% and 0.8% of fecal, nasal, urine, kidney and blood samples from 364 cats. For the canine bocavirus, it was detected in 4.6%, 5.1%, 6.3% and 0.3% of fecal, nasal, urine and blood samples from 351 dogs. Our study represents the first to describe the existence of bocaviruses in domestic cats. Moreover, a novel genetic group of CBoVs was identified among the present dogs, suggesting that diverse CBoVs may be distributed in different geographical areas.

770010.label: Major findings and research outcome
770010.value: In this project, several novel animal bocaviruses, including two novel porcine bocaviruses, a novel feline bocavirus and a novel genogroup of canine bocavirus, were identified and characterized. For the porcine bocaviruses, they were detected by PCR among 16.5 % (55/333) of porcine samples (including lymph nodes, serum, nasopharyngeal and fecal samples) Since marked nucleotide polymorphisms were observed in the partial VP1 sequences, complete VP1 genes from three fecal and one nasopharyngeal specimens were cloned and sequenced, which suggested the presence of two different bocaviruses and demonstrated significant intra- and inter-host genetic diversity. Complete genome sequences revealed the presence of two novel bocaviruses, PBoV3 and PBoV4, in a fecal and nasopharyngeal specimen respectively, with two genotypes, PBoV4-1 and PBoV4-2, in the latter. Their genomes encode three ORFs, characteristic of bocaviruses. Phylogenetic analysis showed that they were distantly to other bocaviruses, forming a distinct cluster within the genus. Recombination analysis showed possible recombination events among VP1 sequences of PBoV4 strains from a fecal specimen, with two (68-bp and 71-bp) breakpoints identified, suggesting that different strains/variants within the same host could have arisen from recombination. This represents the first report describing marked sequence diversity and co-existence of two viruses of the Parvoviridae within the same host, which may be originated from and, in turn, facilitated recombination. The results have been published in the Journal of General Virology (see part C). Based on the above experience, we have further carried out experiments to detect bocaviruses in a variety of animal species including cats, dogs, bats, birds, rodents, chicken and rodents, using PCR with conserved primers specifically designed to target bocaviruses. Among these specimens, we discovered a novel bocavirus, feline bocavirus (FBoV), and novel bocaviruses closely related to canine bocavirus (CBoV) strain Con-161 in stray cats and dogs in Hong Kong respectively. FBoV was detected in 7.2%, 0.3%, 1.6%, 2% and 0.8% of fecal, nasal, urine, kidney and blood samples from 364 cats, while CBoV was detected in 4.6%, 5.1%, 6.3% and 0.3% of fecal, nasal, urine and blood samples from 351 dogs by PCR respectively. Three FBoV genomes sequenced revealed the presence of three ORFs, characteristic of bocaviruses. Phylogenetic analysis showed that FBoVs were only distantly related to other bocaviruses, forming a distinct cluster within the genus. The four CBoV genomes sequenced shared 87.4% to 89.2% nucleotide identities to that of CBoV strain Con-161. In addition to the three bocavirus ORFs, they encoded an additional ORF, ORF4, immediately downstream to NS1, which was not found in other bocaviruses including CBoV strain Con-161. Partial VP1/VP2 sequence analysis of 23 FBoV and 25 CBoV strains demonstrated inter-host genetic diversity, with two potential genetic groups of FBoV and a novel CBoV group, CBoV-HK, distinct from the three groups, CBoV-A to C, found in USA. Our study represents the first to describe the existence of bocaviruses in domestic cats. Moreover, a novel genetic group of CBoVs was identified among the present dogs, suggesting that diverse CBoVs may be distributed in different geographical areas. These results have been published in the Journal of General Virology (see part C).

770010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
770010.value: The present results expand the understanding of the diversity and evolution of bocaviruses, and the existence of bocaviruses in cats and dogs which are the commonest domestic pets that share close habitat with humans. Although the pathogenicity of these novel animal bocaviruses remains to be determined, their presence in different host tissues suggested wide tissue tropism. Further studies are being carried out by our research group on viral cultures, seroepidemiology studies to better understand their epidemiology and pathogenicity. These results will in turn benefit studies on the pathogenicity of human bocaviruses, which is still poorly understood. Moreover, the success of this project has formed a basis for identification of more bocaivruses in other animals in our population, which has generated promising results that are yet to be published.

770010.value: In this project, we have carried out experiments to detect bocaviruses in a variety of animal species including cats, dogs, bats, birds, rodents, chicken and rodents. During the process, we have identified several novel animal bocaviruses, including two novel porcine bocaviruses from swine, a novel feline bocavirus from domestic cat and a novel genogroup of canine bocavirus from dogs in Hong Kong. To better understand these novel animal bocaviruses, we have further performed complete genome sequencing and genetic diversity studies. For the porcine bocaviruses, the results showed the presence of two different bocaviruses and demonstrated significant intra- and inter-host genetic diversity. For feline and canine bocavruses, inter-host genetic diversity were also demonstrated, with two potential genetic groups of FBoV and a novel CBoV group, CBoV-HK, distinct from those found in USA. Our results expand the understanding of the diversity and evolution of bocaviruses, and the existence of bocaviruses in cats and dogs which are the commonest domestic pets that share close habitat with humans.

770610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
770610.value: Cyclic ADP-ribose (cADPR) is a novel cyclic nucleotide derived from NAD. Results accumulate in the past decade establish that it is a universal Ca2+ messenger for store-mobilization in a wide range of cellular systems spanning three biological kingdoms. The functions that cADPR regulates are equally diverse and range from mediating the stress responses of abscisic acid-signaling in plants and sponges to social behavior in mice through modulation of oxyntocin secretion. This proposal is to elucidate the mechanism of regulating the cADPR levels in cells. Specific aims are: Aim 1. To develop methods for modulating intracellular cADPR Levels. Aim 2. To elucidate the mechanism of regulation of the cADPR synthesizing enzyme. Aim 3. To develop mouse models with inducible elements. 環二磷酸腺苷核糖（cADPR）是来自于煙酰胺腺嘌呤核苷酸的一種新型的環核苷酸。過去10多年研究證明，cADPR是一個普遍的動員細胞內鈣庫的鈣離子信使，其調節範圍廣泛，廊括3種生物王國细胞系統。 cADPR調節功能也多种多樣，包括從調解植物和海綿脫落酸信號的應激反應，到小鼠通過調控催產素分泌的社交行為。本研究方案是為了闡明調節細胞的cADPR水平機制。具體研究目標是制定調節細胞內cADPR水平的方法。

770610.label: Realisation of objectives
770610.value: We have succeeded in developing a method for modulating intracellular cADPR levels. The method involved engineering a soluble form of CD38 that is directed to express in the cytosol. CD38, once expressed in the cytosol, uses the cytosolic NAD and produce cADPR in the cells. The process can be controlled by putting the expression under the regulation of the tetracycline responsive element. Two additional methods have also been devised, by mutating the positive residues and the serine residues in the N-terminal of CD38. The Aim is thus completed. Left HKU on March 27, 2013 before the project completion date of 31-12-2013.

770610.value: We have succeeded in developing a method for modulating intracellular cADPR levels. The method involved engineering a soluble form of CD38 that is directed to express in the cytosol. CD38, once expressed in the cytosol, uses the cytosolic NAD and produce cADPR in the cells. The process can be controlled by puting the expression under the regulation of the tetracycline responsive element. Aim is thus completed. Using a similar approach, we have mutated the charges at the N-terminal of CD38 and succeeded in changing its membrane orientation, putting the catalytic domain inside the cytosol. The mutated CD38 is effective in raising cellular cADPR. Methods were designed and developed, using the engineered CD38, to measure the endogenous concentration of intracellular Ca2+ messengers, cADPR and NAADP. In collaboration with Kim's group in Korea, we show that NAADP is a messenger functioning in an auto/paracrine manner to regulate glucose homeostasis. Most recently, a study has been completed to further engineer CD38 by mutating the N-terminal serines and use as tool for manipulating intracellular cADPR. A manuscript has been submitted to the J. 771110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
771110.value: Background. In vertebrates, hematopoiesis occurs in successive waves during development. Definitive hematopoiesis occurs at different embryonic sites and constitutes life-long hematopoiesis after birth. Zebrafish has emerged as a unique model for the study of these processes. In this organism, definitive hematopoiesis arises successively at the ventral wall of dorsal aorta, pronephric duct, posterior blood island, and lastly the kidney and thymus. Methionine aminopeptidase 2 (MetAP-2) is the target of an anti-angiogenesis compound Fumagillin and has been investigated for its robust expression in human cancers and tumor angiogenesis. MetAP-2 removes the initiator NH2-terminal methionine from the nascent peptides during protein translation. The process is an important determinant for protein stability, function and cellular localization. MetAP-2 has also been implicated in the regulation of non-canonical Wnt pathway as well as eIF2 and ERK1/2 phosphorylation. Despite its significance in cancers, the physiological role of MetAP-2, particularly in hematopoiesis, has remained unclear. In an initial screening of fumagillin analogues for their anti-angiogenic effects in zebrafish embryos, we observed a hitherto unexpected effect on hematopoiesis. Preliminary studies demonstrated expression of metap-2 in the pronephric duct. Knock down of metap-2 with morpholino (4.5 ng) targeting at the splice-site junction resulted in a characteristic phenotype with kinked tail and altered somitic patterning. Both c-myb and runx1 genes, which denote HSC in definitive hematopoiesis, were significantly increased in the ventral wall of dorsal aorta. Molecular targeting and specificity of metap-2 knock-down were confirmed by RT-PCR and phenotypic rescue by metap-2 mRNA. Objective. In this proposal, we will make use of the zebrafish model and investigate: 1. The functions of MetAP-2 in definitive hematopoiesis; 2. What is/are the mechanisms of action? Methodology. We will accomplish these objectives by examining in detail the spatial relationship of metap-2 expression in relation to the pronephric duct and HSC. Knock-down of MetAP-2 function will be accomplished by morpholino and fumagillin treatment. Functional redundancy of MetAPs will be evaluated by gene expression and knock-down studies of MetAP-1 and MetAP-2like genes in zebrafish. Furthermore, the mechanisms of action of MetAP-2 during definitive hematopoiesis will be evaluated with particular reference to its aminopeptidase activity and its potential role(s) in the regulation of non-canonical Wnt pathway, eIF2 and ERK1/2 phosphorylation. We will also perform proteomic and microarray studies with a view to identify novel targets of MetAP-2. Summary. The proposal will shed novel insights to the regulation of definitive hematopoiesis by MetAP-2 and its mechanisms of action. 摘要： 研究背景：在脊椎动物成长过程中，造血是持续进行的。永久造血发生在胚胎阶段的不同部位，并且在胎儿出生后依然维持着终生的造血。斑马鱼是研究造血过程的独特模型，在斑马鱼中，永久造血相继发生于背主动脉腹侧壁，原肾管，尾部血岛，最后是肾脏和胸腺。 甲硫氨酸氨基肽酶（MetAP-2）是抑制血管新生药物烟曲霉素（Fumagillin）的靶基因，目前对其在人类癌细胞中的大量表达和在肿瘤血管新生中的作用均有相关研究。在蛋白翻译过程中，MetAP-2可以从新生肽中移除氨基末端蛋氨酸，而此过程对于蛋白质的稳定性，功能和在蛋白质在细胞中的定位有重要的决定作用。另外，MetAP-2也参与了调节非经典Wnt通路及eIF-2和ERK1/2磷酸化。除了其在癌症中的重要作用，MetAP-2的其他生理功能，尤其是在造血中的作用目前尚不明确。 在最初的筛选试验中，我们对烟曲霉素类似物在斑马鱼胚胎中抗血管新生的作用进行了研究，意外地发现MetAP-2可能对造血过程有影响。早期的研究显示MetAP-2在原肾管中表达，Morpholino的作用靶点是剪切位点结合处，用Morpholino（45ng）抑制MetAP-2的表达，可以导致斑马鱼胚胎发生特征性的体型改变，并出现尾巴卷曲，而代表永久造血的C-myb和RUNX1基因在背主动脉腹侧壁的表达显著提高。MetAP-2靶向及特异性抑制试验可以用MetAP-2 mRNA解救试验证实。 目的：在这个研究计划中，我们将利用斑马鱼作为模型进行以下研究： 1. MetAP-2在永久造血中的作用。 2. MetAP-2作用机制是什么？ 方法：首先，我们将深入研究MetAP-2在斑马鱼胚胎不同部位的表达，特别是在原肾管和血液干细胞中的表达情况。用烟曲霉素或morpholino抑制基因表达的方法研究MetAP-1, MetAP-2类似基因在斑马鱼中功能的重复性。继之，基于MetAP-2的氨肽酶功能和其对非经典Wnt通路及eIF-2和ERK1/2磷酸化的调节功能，我们将从该角度对MetAP-2在永久造血中的作用机制进行深入的研究。我们还将运用蛋白组学技术和基因芯片技术寻找MetAP-2的新的靶向基因。 总结：该研究计划将有利于对MetAP-2在永久造血过程中的调节作用及其作用机制作出新的解释。

Furthermore, we evaluated the translational potential of these studies and performed a set of new experiments in which we examined the effects of MetAP-2 inhibitor in human leukemia. 771110.label: Major findings and research outcome
771110.value: In this proposal, we investigated the role of MetAP2 in hematopoiesis by using zebrafish embryo and human umbilical cord blood models. We demonstrated that zebrafish metap2 was expressed ubiquitously during early embryogenesis and later in the somitic region, the caudal hematopoietic tissue, and pronephric duct. metap2 was knocked down by morpholino and inhibited by fumagillin treatment, resulting in increased mpo expression at 18 hours postfertilization and reduced c-myb expression along the ventral wall of dorsal aorta at 36 hours postfertilization. It also disrupted intersegmental vessels in Tg(fli1:gfp) embryos without affecting development of major axial vasculatures. Inhibition of MetAP2 in CB CD34(+) cells by fumagillin had no effect on overall clonogenic activity but significantly reduced their engraftment into immunodeficient nonobese diabetes/severe combined immunodeficiency mice. metap2 knock-down in zebrafish and inhibition by fumagillin in zebrafish and human CB CD34(+) cells inhibited Calmodulin Kinase II activity and induced ERK phosphorylation. The study demonstrated a hitherto-undescribed role of MetAP2 in definitive hematopoiesis and a possible link to noncanonical Wnt and ERK signaling.

771110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
771110.value: The proposal has provided us with important ground for the study of MetAP-2 and its role in leukemogenesis. The research has also provided a traning opportunity for a MMedSc student who has successfully completed her study and graduated in 2013. We have since then initiated a new set of studies evaluating the effects of protein translation inhibition on leukemia growth. The research will have significant potential in opening up a new avenue for therapeutic internvention in acute leukemia.

771110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
771110.value: In thist study, we have first evaluated the expression and functional role of an enzyme methionine aminopeptidase II (MetAtP-2) in the embryonic hematopoiesis (blood formation). The results have resulted in new knowledge in this hitherto unexploited area in hematopoiesis. Now we understand that MetAP-2 plays an important role in zebafish and human cord blood hematopoiesis. The proposal has proven to be a productive one. Based on these original findings, we have further exploited the use of drugs to inhibit the enzyme with a view to discover new agents that may be useful for the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia. These new experiments have now become the new focus of research in our laboratory. Furthermore, an original article was published in BLOOD (a top tier journal in the field of haematology) and thesis focusing on the use of fumgaillin (inhibitor of MetAP-2) in acute leukemia was also completed in 2013.

771310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
771310.value: Infectious bursal disease virus (IBDV) causes a highly contagious disease in young chicks and leads to significant economic losses in the worldwide poultry industry. By infecting B lymphocytes in the Bursa of Fabricius, IBDV causes severe immunodeficiency and mortality in young chicks. Cell culture adaptation of wild type IBDV (wtIBDV) has been widely reported to generate cell culture adapted IBDV (caIBDV) with mutations found in the capsid protein VP2. After cell culture adaptation, IBDV infects non-lymphoid cell lines and becomes attenuated to the chicken B lymphocytes. Recently, the cell entry mechanism of IBDV was characterized by several studies on receptor identification, viral uncoating and membrane penetration. Chicken heat shock protein 90 (cHSP90α) and mouse integrin α4β1 were identified as putative receptors for caIBDV. Low concentration of calcium ion in endosome was suspected to stimulate dissociation of viral particle and induce membrane perforation. The suspected involvement of endosome suggested IBDV internalizes into host cell by endocytosis. This project aims to confirm the occurrence of endocytosis during caIBDV entry and to characterize the specific endocytic pathway. Moreover, the limiting factor for wtIBDV to infect cell lines was demonstrated at the cellular entry step, which involves receptor attachment and internalization. As we previously demonstrated wtIBDV can attach to cell lines without adaptation, the role of internalization pathway for wtIBDV adaptation will be investigated. In response to these objectives, a susceptible chicken cell line DF-1 will be infected by purified caIBDV to reveal the internalization kinetics of IBDV, determined by flow cytometric and confocal microscopic analyses. Chemical inhibiting endocytosis such as sodium azide will be used to determine the occurrence of viral endocytosis. Chemicals inhibiting macropinocytosis, clathrin-dependent endocytosis, caveolin-dependent endocytosis and specific factors involved in endocytosis will be utilized to identify the endocytic pathways that IBDV employed. After estimating the pathway involved, dominant negative mutants and siRNAs targeted to knock-down corresponding genes essential to the endocytic pathway will be introduced into DF-1 followed by IBDV internalization. Purified wtIBDV will be incubated with DF-1 to investigate its capability of internalization, in comparison with caIBDV. This study is expected to provide valuable information on the endocytic pathways hijacked by IBDV and unveil the potential discrimination between wtIBDV and caIBDV. As viral entry is a determining factor for infection, a thorough understanding of the entry mechanism of IBDV may bring new insights to the mechanism of cell culture adaptation and anti-viral strategy.

771310.label: Realisation of objectives
771310.value: Realization of objectives: We have performed experiments to fulfill all the stated 3 out of the 4 objectives. The main reason that we cannot fulfill objective 3 is that we have tried but unsuccessfully obtain DT40 cell line. The stock cells I brought back from US was too old to revive back in culture. Since Df-1 has been the avian cell line of choice for researchers in the field, we believe that our work is directly relevant. Virus entry into host cells has been the “black box” of virology research. For IBDV, the primary receptor for IBDV infection has not been confirmed, several putative receptors have been identified to at least support cell surface attachment. These putative receptors include chicken heat shock protein 90 (cHSP90a) identified from DF-1 chicken embryonic fibroblasts, integrin alpha4beta1 from a murine BALB/c 3T3 cell line and surface IgM identified from a chicken bursal lymphoma-derived DT40 cell line. On the other hand, the uncoating and penetration of IBDV was hypothesized to be mediated by depletion of calcium ion. Calcium ion has been suggested to maintain the structure of the IBDV capsid by stabilizing the interaction within the VP2 trimer and between the trimmers. We have clearly demonstrated the role of endocytosis during the entry of caIBDV into DF-1 was demonstrated, based on the observation that uncoating of caIBDV required vesicular dissipation of Ca2+ regulated by vacuolar H+-ATPase (V-ATPase). By comparing the viral content during the early replication cycle of caIBDV under the treatment of selected inhibitors, the involvement of various components and regulators of endocytosis was determined where lipid raft, tyrosine kinase, dynamin and actin polymerization play essential role in caIBDV-mediated endocytosis. In addition, we have performed RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) to unveil the transcriptional profile of a chicken embryonic fibroblast cell line DF-1 at the early stage of cell-adapted IBDV (caIBDV) infection. The differential expression landscape demonstrated with RNA-Seq provides a more comprehensive picture on the molecular interactions between host cells and virus at the early stage of caIBDV infection.

771410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
771410.value: It has been well established that endothelial function is impaired in diabetes, resulting in a number of pathophysiological processes in cardiovascular diseases. A considerable body of evidence implicates generation of reactive oxygen species as an important pathogenic factor in diabetic endothelial dysfunction. Acute administration of antioxidants that includes glutathione, vitamin C, vitamin E, flavonoids, and polyphenols are known to improve the abnormal endothelium-dependent responses resulted from diabetes. However, their long-term benefits on human are still under investigation. Ergothioneine, a chemical rich in mushroom, has been proposed to possess potent antioxidant activities, involving the removal of cell toxic radical species or chelating of metal ions. However, the biological relevance of these findings is unclear because most of the preceding studies were performed in cell-free systems. It is not known whether ergothioneine can protect endothelial cells from oxidative stress. However, our preliminary data demonstrates that ergothioneine can be taken up by endothelial cells. Ergothioneine also preserves the viability of endothelial cells and restore the endothelium-dependent relaxation of arteries in high glucose condition. Most importantly, our data shows that the endothelial protective effect of ergothioneine is stronger than that of other antioxidants such as vitamin C and vitamin E. Three key issues will be addressed in this project. First, the transport system by which ergothioneine is taken up into endothelial cells will be characterized. Second, the antioxidant and anti-apoptotic effects of ergothioneine on endothelial cells will be studied. Third, we will strengthen our preliminary study that ergothioneine can protect endothelial functions from damage by diabetes. It is generally accepted that protection of endothelial cells against oxidative stress may prevent diabetes-related cardiovascular events. We hope that the findings in this study could advance our knowledge on the cardiovascular drug development, particularly those associated with diabetes.

771410.label: Realisation of objectives
771410.value: 1) We have successfully used radiolabelled ergothioneine as a tool to study how ergothioneine is taken up by the endothelial cells. We have also used siRNA to find up the major transporter responsible for the ergothioneine uptake. 2) Pyrogallol, hypoxanthine plus xanthine oxidase and high concentration of glucose were used to induced oxidative stress in endothelial cells. We have used fluorescence dye to study the effect of ergothioneine on the generation of reactive oxygen species in endothelial cells. 3) The cytoprotective effect of ergothioneine was studied using the MTT assay. 4) animal studies have also been carried out to investigate whether ergothioneine could reverse the impaired relaxation of blood vessels under oxidative stress and under diabetic conditions.

771410.label: Major findings and research outcome
771410.value: RT-PCR and Western blotting demonstrated transcription and translation of an ergothioneine transporter in human brain microvascular endothelial cells (HBMECs). Uptake of [3H]ergothioneine occurred by the organic cation transporter novel type-1 (OCTN-1), was sodium-dependent and was reduced when expression of OCTN-1 was silenced by siRNA. The effect of ergothioneine on the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in HBMECs was measured using dichlorodihydrofluorescin and lucigenin, and the effect on cell viability was studied using the 3-(4,5-Dimethylthgiazol-2-yl)-2, 5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assay. ROS production and cell death induced by pyrogallol, xanthine oxidase plus xanthine and high glucose were suppressed by ergothioneine. The expression of NADPH oxidase was decreased, and those of glutathione reductase, catalase and superoxide dismutase enhanced by the compound. Ergothioneine attenuated the reduction in relaxation of isolated rat basilar arteries to the endothelium-dependent vasodilator acetylcholine caused by pyrogallol, xanthine oxidase plus xanthine or incubation in high glucose. Chronic treatment with the compound improved the response to acetylcholine in arteries of rats with streptozotocin-induced diabetes. In summary, ergothioneine is taken up by endothelial cells via OCTN-1, where the compound then protects against oxidative stress, curtailing endothelial dysfunction. The research findings have been written as an manuscript and submitted to Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics.

771410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
771410.value: Ergothioneine shows good antioxidant and protective effect to blood vessels. The absence of toxicity, high potency, and broad spectrum antioxidant properties, together with the high water solubility and stability at physiological pH, make ergothioneine, especially when compared with existing conventional antioxidants, a very attractive candidate for protecting endothelial cells against oxidative stress and thus for the treatment and/or prevention of oxidative stress-associated cardiovascular diseases. For further development, it will be interested if we can find out a cheaper source of ergothioneine. The synthetic ergothioneine is very expansive. It is known that ergothinoeine is abundant in food, especially mushroom. Our preliminary study has shown that mushroom extract, which is a much cheaper source of ergothioneine, can produce a comparable antioxidant and protective effect on endothelial cells. It is worthwhile further studying.

771410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
771410.value: Oxidative stress is harmful to our body, especially the cardiovascular system because it can impair the function of endothelial cells in blood vessels. Previous animal studies have shown that antioxidants such as N-acetylcysteine, vitamin C and vitamin E can prevent the deterioration of endothelial functions. Unfortunately, these agents usually fail to improve endothelial function in human. One of the possibilities is the dose of antioxidants used. For instance, the effect of vitamin C has been assessed in humans with Type 2 diabetes but up to 1 mM had to be administered directly into the blood vessels. Such high local concentrations of vitamin C cannot be achieved by oral administration. Ergothioneine is an amino acid that humans consume with plant food, especially mushroom. Our study shows that ergothioneine can protect the integrity and functions of endothelial cells against oxidative stress. It is known that ergothioneine is highly retained in our body. The absence of toxicity, the high potency of its antioxidant properties, its high water solubility and stability make ergothioneine a very attractive antioxidant over other conventional antioxidants, in protecting endothelial cells from oxidative stress. Our study has explored the possibility of using ergothioneine or any source of ergothioneine (e.g. mushroom) in the treatment and/or prevention of cardiovascular diseases.

771910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
771910.value: Hong Kong has experienced an alarming increase in colon cancer incidence in recent decades, now amongst world’s top 10 highest incidence areas. Understanding the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of tumour suppressor gene (TSG) inactivation could lead to new treatment strategies. Specifically epigenetic therapy is emerging as a new modality for cancer treatment. Cancer is characterised by frequent chromosomal aberrations, which may contribute to the inactivation of TSGs through intragenic mutation or deletion. Recently, we (Nature Genetics 2009) and others have illustrated a novel mechanism of TSG gene silencing in the germline, involving the deletion of 3’ exons and abrogation of polyadenylation signal of a neighbouring gene. Consequently, transcriptional read-through into the disease genes in either sense or antisense direction leads to promoter methylation and transcriptional silencing, causing hereditary diseases including hereditary colon cancer and alpha-thalassaemia. Based on the high frequency of random somatic chromosomal aberrations observed in cancers, we hypothesised that such events could also lead to aberrant transcriptional read-through into neighbouring or translocated TSGs in either sense or anti-sense direction, inducing their methylation and silencing. Here we propose to use the new generation Solexa DNA sequencing platform to perform a systematic and comprehensive survey of the colon cancer transcriptomes in search of fusion transcripts. Whereas previous studies on fusion transcripts tend to focus on those resulted in aberrant activation of oncogenes, we hereby propose to study fusion transcripts arising from genes with 3’exons or polyadenylation sites deletion or genomic translocations that could induce aberrant transcriptional read-through into TSGs. Fusion transcripts with which the 3’ ends correspond to recurrent aberrant transcription into known or putative TSGs in either the sense or antisense direction will be identified for further study. Such candidate TSGs will be investigated in detail for the presence of silencing via promoter methylation induction, using the high-throughput targeted bisulphite-DNA sequencing technology. The current study endows marked potential in expanding the list of TSGs documented in colorectal cancer and advancing our understanding of the mechanisms for TSG silencing and methylation induction. 近幾十年來，香港地區結腸癌發病率錄得驚人增長，現已居全世界前十位。對腫瘤抑制基因失活的遺傳及表觀遺傳機制的研究有助於開發新的治療手段。特別是針對表觀遺傳學的治療已開始顯現。頻發染色體異常可導致腫瘤抑制基因的突變或缺失，是腫瘤的重要特徵之一。最近，我們(Nature Genetics 2009)和其他研究人員闡述了胚系腫瘤抑制基因沉默的新機制，即相鄰基因3’端外顯子和多聚腺苷酸信號缺失引起上游基因轉錄通讀至疾病基因，誘導啟動子甲基化和轉錄沉默，導致遺傳性結腸癌、α-地中海貧血等遺傳性疾病。我們推斷這種轉錄沉默不僅發生於胚系，也可能發生於體系染色體異常，而隨機的體系染色體異常在腫瘤中發生率很高。因此，我們計劃利用新一代Solexa DNA 測序平臺，通過全面系統地篩查結腸癌轉錄組，尋找融合的轉錄子。此前關於轉錄融合的研究多集中在致癌基因的異常啟動，我們於此提議研究可導致腫瘤抑制基因失活之轉錄融合。那些3’端為已知或推定的腫瘤抑制基因的融合轉錄子，將被選作進一步研究。我們將利用高通量針對性亞硫酸氫DNA測序技術詳細研究這些候選腫瘤抑制基因是否因啟動子甲基化而沉默。這項研究將擁有極大潛力增添結直腸癌腫瘤抑制基因數量，並且加深我們對腫瘤抑制基因沉默和甲基化誘導機制的理解。

771910.label: Realisation of objectives
771910.value: The project aims to undercover candidate tumour suppressor genes(TSG) silenced by promoter methylation in a genome wide scale and to examine whether transcriptional interference due to deletion of the 3’-end of genes could constitutes an important mechanism for methylation induction, using gastrointestinal tract cancer such as colorectal cancer as a model. The method involves finding genomic breakpoints in a genome-wide scale to identify those that remove the 3’ end of genes. In parallel, examination for promoter methylation in a genome wide scale and then matching with the breakpoints to look for specific association of 3’-end deletion of upstream genes and methylation induction, and matching to gene expression data to look for candidate TSGs silenced by promoter methylation. We have attempted to address these basic mechanisms of methylation induction using a closely related cancer of the gastrointestinal tract, gastric cancer, which shares many common molecular pathways of alteration with colorectal cancer, specifically in terms of genes deregulated by methylation, such as MLH1 or p16. This is because of the unique opportunity of availability of whole genome sequencing data in an expanded cohort of 100 gastric cancer patients, which is substantially bigger than the original cohort of 50 patients proposed in the grant. We thus performed Illumina Infinium Human Methylation450 BeadChip to interrogate the methylation status of 450,000 methylation sites, with genome wide coverage in these 100 cases. In parallel, we performed gene expression profiling. Integrative analysis of these three sets of comprehensive genomics data thus enabled us to achieve the project goal. We identified large number of structural variants, some of these removed the 3’ end of genes. Whilst we do observed specific association of deletion of 3’-end of genes and corresponding promoter methylation in the downstream genes in some cancers involving specific genomic loci, these are scattered all over the genome and non-recurrent, due to extreme degree and random nature of chromosomal aberrations. Although we did not find genes recurrently methylated due to deletion of 3’-end of upstream genes, we have detected in a genome-wide scale, many novel genes recurrently silenced by promoter methylation as well as many genes up-regulated by demethylation. Furthermore, we found association of aberrant gene methylation with specific molecular subtype of cancer, which underlies novel mechanisms of de-regulated methylation. Thus overall, the project achieves its aims of discovery of TSGs silenced by promoter methylation in a genome-wide scale and uncovering potential underlying mechanisms.

771910.label: Major findings and research outcome
771910.value: Based on whole genome sequencing in 100 cancers, we identified 1753 interchromosomal translocations, 2468 intrachromosomal translocations and 4917 large insertions or deletions; many of these were found to remove the 3’ end of genes. The results revealed an extreme degree of chromosomal instability in some subgroups of cancer. Analysis of the methylation array show extensive hypermethylation and demethylation events scattered across the genome. Integrative analysis with gene expression data identified 89 genes with concordant promoter methylation and downregulated expression, affecting 4 to 48% of cancer samples. These include well-known TSG silenced by methylation such as MLH1, MGMT, and also many novel candidate TSGs such as PARP6, which was shown to modulate cell cycle, and TP73-AS1, which was shown to regulate apoptosis. Unexpectedly, we also detected 92 putative oncogenes up-regulated by demethylation, affecting 3 to 60% of cancers, including genes inducing intestinal metaplasia (CDX1), genes affecting stem cell function (ASCL2) or cancer signaling pathway (CDH17). Overall our analysis generated a complete catalogue of methylation deregulated genes, many of which could be important for gastrointestinal carcinogenesis. Whilst most of these genes recurrently de-regulated by methylation are not closely associated with 3’-end deletion of upstream gene, because of the dramatically random nature of the chromosomal aberrations, we observed novel association of methylation pattern with molecular subtypes of cancer, revealing new dimension of methylation regulation. Specifically, the EBV-associated cancer is associated with extremely high level of genome-wide methylation, affecting around 25% of all CpG sites assessed. This extremely high level of methylation could be related to the process of virus-induced carcinogenesis. The MSI cancers alternatively, have a moderate level of hypermethylation, but also an extensive degree of genome-wide demethylation. The diffuse type cancers have significant elevated methylation in promoter CpG islands, whereas the intestinal type cancer have extensive genome-wide demethylation. We also observed a significant association of extent of genome-wide demethylation with chromosomal instability and presence of TP53 mutation. Analysis of the transcription factor binding sites underlying the hypermethylated and demethylated region revealed enrichment of polycomb complex in the hypermethylated region and AP-1 complex in the demethylated region, revealing potential underlying mechanism for methylation and demethylation induction. Overall, our project have achieved the goal of identifying potential novel tumour suppressor genes or oncogene deregulated by methylation, and identified potential novel underlying mechanisms of methylation induction through association with specific molecular subgroups or deregulated activity of transcription factors linked to the polycomb or AP-1 complexes.

771910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
771910.value: We have identified many novel putative TSGs and oncogenes deregulated by methylation. We will further study the functional roles of these genes in the process of carcinogenesis, using organoid culture of normal and cancer tissue, with transfection or knockdown of these genes, to examine effect on cell growth behavior and tumorigenicity in nude mice. Treatment with demethylating agent including 5-Aza will be performed to validate the importance of methylation in regulation of gene expression. Molecular subgroups of cancer with differing methylation level will be examined in relation to their sensitivity to therapeutic agents modulating methylation level. We are currently performing intensive bioinformatics analysis to understand the relationship of hypermethylated and demethylated region with regional genomic architecture, so as to identify novel mechanism of methylation regulation and to find ways to reverse such changes. These studies will lead to candidate therapeutic development to reverse genes deregulated by methylation as a means for cancer treatment.

771910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
771910.value: Cancers of the gastrointestinal tract constitutes the most common cancer types worldwide. Apart from gene mutations, epigenetic dysregulation of genes caused by abnormal methylation of gene promoters can also cause cancer. Knowing which genes are deregulated by methylation and understanding its underlying mechanism of deregulation can lead to development of new treatment strategy adapted to specific subgroup of patients. The current study has used the most advanced next-generation sequencing and methylation profiling technology to comprehensively decipher in a genome-wide scale, genes that are deregulated by methylation in a large cohort of cancer patients. We have discovered large number of genes deregulated by methylation, and identified different pattern of methylation abnormality in different subgroups of patients. We have also identified potential mechanism of methylation induction linked to specific group of transcription factors. In some subgroups of cancer patients, de-regulated methylation constitutes the key abnormalities in the cancer tissue. This raises possibility of increased responsiveness to epigenetic therapy in specific patient subtypes. Further study of the novel candidate oncogenes or tumour suppressor genes discovered could lead to development of new treatment strategy for these common and deadly cancers.

772110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
772110.value: Fifteen percent of Hong Kong adults suffer from moderate to advanced chronic periodontitis. This condition is caused by infection with opportunistic pathogenic bacteria. The severity of chronic periodontitis is associated with factors that are involved in the negative modulation of the host immune response, such as smoking, diabetes mellitus, and inadequate stress-coping skills. Periodontitis causes tooth mobility and tooth loss, and significantly affects the oral health-related quality of life (OH-QoL) of those with the disease. Although traditional therapist-centered treatment of chronic periodontitis, including non-surgical or surgical therapy followed by supportive periodontal therapy (SPT), can initially successfully manage the disease, a considerable proportion of treated individuals develop recurrent periodontitis, especially if they fail to comply fully with the recommended SPT. One possible reason for treatment failure could be that no patient-centered approaches to therapy were delivered and that patients do not assume their responsibility in homecare and SPT. How patients psychologically respond to stress may also be a contributing factor to poor healing and disease recurrence. Patient-centered treatment for periodontitis with adjunction behavioral therapy could offer an alternative approach to management by taking into account how patients cope with stress and enhancing coping mechanisms if these are deficient. There is a lack of research in the literature on the relevance and effects of patient-centered treatment in enhancing compliance to supportive periodontal therapy and hence long-term OH-QoL in periodontitis patients. Our proposed study aims (1) to prospectively characterize the clinical healing responses and OH-QoL changes, if any, after non-surgical mechanical periodontal therapy in a group of patients with chronic periodontitis who have been categorized as either adequate or inadequate stress-copers, and (2) among patients with recurrent periodontitis, to prospectively assess the effects of standardized cognitive-behavioral therapy, as an adjunct to non-surgical therapy, on periodontal healing response and perceived OH-QoL. The significance of this proposed investigation is the promotion of a patient centered, rather than the current operator centered, approach to long term chornic periodontitis care. 百份之15本港成人患有重度牙周炎，其成因謂為牙周細菌感染。牙周病之嚴重性可受吸煙，糖尿及心理壓力等因素影响，左右。牙周病導致牙齒鬆動及脫落，亦嚴重影响口腔生活質素。傳統之醫護為中心牙周治療，雖能治愈牙周病，患者每每因疏於牙周維護及防治致牙周病復發。這情況於不服從之牙周病友尤為常見。其原因可能由於牙周治療過程並非以病患為中心，故令病友們忽略了口腔日常清潔及到牙醫診所進行定期維護。他們的壓力及情緒反應亦可影响牙周復原以及牙周病復發。患者為本及行為療法可增強患者對牙周病療程及適當口腔衞生行為之適應。本研究旨在(1)縱向記錄牙周病復原過程於口腔生活質素之改變，及(2)運用認知及行為方法協助牙周病人復原。盼日後以牙周病患者為本治療可帶來更多，更好的治療成果。

772110.label: Major findings and research outcome
772110.value: Chronic periodontitis adversely affects oral health related quality of life (OHRQoL) of those suffered the disease, in particular pain, functional and psychosocial aspects. Periodontal disease treatment however could only help alleviate the pain and psychosocial aspects. The Functional limitations and physical disabilities does not benefit from successful periodontal treatment. Problem focused coping unfortunately, does not appeared able to assist better healing responses/outcomes for those who process the favorable trait. The group also discovered that non-surgical periodontal treatment discomfort perception of patient relates with their prior dental experience, gum inflammation and adequacy of the pain control while the treatment would lead to dentine sensitivity and hence lower OHRQoL up to an extended period. This study however discovered for the first time that subjects affected with systemic diseases, e.g. type 2 diabetes mellitus may experience different pattern of OHRQoL recovery which is possibly a result of the dynamic construct of the latter’s change in people with systemic diseases. Such concept would be very important for clinicians, dental or medical alike, handling someone affected by chronic non-communicable disease(s) and periodontitis.

772110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
772110.value: The dynamic construct of OHRQoL influenced by chronic non-communicable disease in an aging population like Hong Kong needs further investigations.

772110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
772110.value: Advanced chronic periodontitis affect up to 30% of the Hong Kong population. Those unfortunate ones experience pain/discomfort, loss of oral functions etc., in particular in those with high dental anxiety. Periodontal disease does not appear to affect social life of the periodontitis patients and render them feeling handicapped, however, the psychological impacts seemed significant. Fortunately the latter conditions shall improve with appropriate periodontal therapy. On the other hand, oral functional issues require special attention even after therapy. Subjects with periodontitis associating concurrent medical condition like diabetes (DM) display a different oral health related quality of life (OHRQoL) profile which does not seemed to response in the same way after regular periodontal therapy. That shall remain a challenge for therapists interested to improve OHRQoL of DM patients with periodontitis. This study failed to detect any benefit of particular coping style or coping training in terms of periodontal healing response and OHRQoL improvement. Nevertheless, we also discovered the importance of effective pain control on subsequent periodontal treatment. The impact of post-treatment root surface sensitivities was also considered. Ongoing researches are being conducted to further characterize the relationship between periodontal therapy and OHRQoL especially on those who are with chronic non-communicable diseases.

772410.label: Project Objectives
772410.value: The OVERALL goal is to evaluate and dissect the roles of specific non-cell autonomous, environmental cues in the structural and functional maturation of otherwise developmentally arrested ventricular hESC-CMs. To this end, three independent but complementary specific experimental objectives will be pursued: OBJECTIVE 1:To test the hypothesis that electrical conditioning that mimics endogenous fetal heart pacing is an environmental factor that triggers global maturation of ventricular hESC-CMs at the single-cell level. The following functional and structural properties will be measured and compared to control ventricular hESC-CMs and adult ventricular CMs. • Electrophysiological maturation of action potential profile and key ventricular ionic currents (e.g., INa, ICaL, IKr, INCX, If, Ito, IK1, IKs). • Ca2+-handling and contractile properties. • Structural maturation of t-tubules, alignment of sarcomeres, physiological hypertrophy (cell size/membrane capacitance) will be assessed. OBJECTIVE 2: To dissect the effects of electrical conditioning and their mechanistic basis, followed by fine-tuning for optimal facilitated maturation of hESC-CMs. • To explore the dependency of electrical conditioning on stimulating frequency, voltage, pulse duration, cell age, etc, by systematically varying these parameters to explore their inter-correlations. • To study the role of electrical stimulation alone in facilitated maturation by decoupling excitation-contraction coupling. OBJECTIVE 3: To test the hypothesis that global maturation of hESC-CMs at the multi-cellular level can be achieved via systematic cell alignment to mimic the highly organized arrangement in the native heart. • To generate a monolayer of “strip” of uni-directionally aligned ventricular hESC-CMs using a microgroove technology. • To measure the conduction properties (transverse and longitudinal velocities, anisotropy, connexin (Cx) expression and localization). • To evaluate the frequency of occurrence of reentrant arrhythmias of cardiac strips with or without electrical conditioning. • To evaluate the electrophysiological, Ca2+-handling and contractile properties as well as other maturation signs. • To combine with 2) to generate an anisotropic mature “cardiac strip” that mimics the native ventricle.

772410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
772410.value: Heart diseases have been a major cause of death worldwide, including developed countries. Indeed, loss of non-regenerative heart cells due to aging or diseases is irreversible. Current therapeutic regimes are palliative in nature, and in the case of end-stage heart failure, transplantation remains the last and only resort. Unfortunately, there is a severe shortage of donor cells and organs, leading to substantial mortality and morbidity as well as socio-economical costs. Recent advances in the isolation and identification of pluripotent or multipotent stem cells have enabled clinicians and scientists to pursue the revolutionary paradigm of Regenerative Medicine. Human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) can propagate indefinitely while maintaining their ability to become all cell types of the body, including heart cells. Therefore, hESCs may serve as an unlimited factory of heart cells for transplantation therapies, alleviating the need for donor organs. To this end, we have identified a major gap in the field: heart cells derived from hESCs are immature, and if anything, are most similar to heart cells isolated from heart failure patients. As such, they have a high likelihood to cause lethal heart rhythms disturbances (arrhythmias). Thus, there is an urgent need to develop protocols to rescue the developmentally arrested behaviors of derived CMs for their eventual clinical and other applications. For instance, how can hESC/iPSC-CMs serve as excellent in vitro models for cardiotoxicity screening and heart disease models to accurately reflect the adult heart when they are both functionally and structurally immature and dissimilar to the adult counterpart? This proposal aims to build on our expertise and existing knowledge in the field to address this major gap: to develop an effective and reproducible method for driving maturation of otherwise developmentally arrested hESC/iPSC-CMs. Not only does the proposal promise to deliver pragmatic tools that will be useful for the field of cardiac regeneration but the knowledge gained is also anticipated to improve our understanding of the processes of human cardiogenesis and maturation that are otherwise difficult to study due to various ethical and practical concerns involved in obtaining healthy human hearts. 在全球很多國家中，心臟疾病都是主要的致命疾病。事實上，因老化或疾病而壞死的心臟細胞都是不能再生的。 現存的心臟病治療方案都是緩和性質為主，而針對末期心臟衰竭患者，心臟移植是目前唯一的治療方法。可惜社會上嚴重缺乏器官捐贈，致令死亡率高企及對社會造成沉重的損失。 再生醫學的興起，迅速掀起一股研究萬能幹細胞/多能幹細胞修補受損器官的熱潮。人類胚胎幹細胞可以無限繁殖，並轉化為包括心臟細胞在內的人體組織和器官細胞。 有見及此，人類胚胎幹細胞可成為可無限生產心臟細胞供移植用的工廠，緩和對器官捐贈的需求。至目前為止，我們發現由人類胚胎幹細胞培殖的心臟細胞不夠成熟，與心臟衰竭的病人細胞相似。因此，由人類胚胎幹細胞培殖的心臟細胞或會導致致命的心律失常及心律不整毛病。 所以，專家有急切需要研究如何挽救發育停滯的心肌細胞。例如，針對人類胚胎幹細胞或由人工多能幹細胞轉化的心肌細胞作體外研究，以發展心臟檢查和心臟疾病模型，準確地探討這些細胞在功能和結構上是否成熟，及與人體內的細胞有何不同。 此研究項目旨在利用我們的專業知識，針對上述問題作研究，找出有效提升這些由人類胚胎幹細胞或由人工多能幹細胞轉化的心肌細胞成熟度並可培殖的方法。 此研究不單是心肌再生範疇中的實用工具，而且當中獲得的知識，預料能為我們對現時因受道德和實際考慮，而難以進行研究的人造人類心臟細胞及其成熟過程，增進認識。

772410.label: Major findings and research outcome
772410.value: Human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) can be efficiently and reproducibly directed into cardiomyocytes (CMs) using stage-specific induction protocols. However, their functional properties and suitability for clinical and other applications have not been evaluated. 1) Our results showed that hESC/iPSC-CMs commonly displayed immature, proarrhythmic action potential properties. Among the panoply of sarcolemmal ionic currents investigated, we pinpointed the lack of the Kir2.1-encoded inwardly rectifying K(+) current (IK1) as the single mechanistic contributor, providing the first link of a complex developmentally arrested phenotype to a major effector gene. By providing the environmental cues that are missing in conventional culturing method, this approach did not require any genetic or pharmacological interventions. 2) As a fundamental property of working CMs, Ca2+ signaling and its role in excitation-contraction (EC) coupling are well described. However, the biology of these processes in hESC-CMs is just becoming understood. By meticulously examining the immature Ca2+-handling properties of hESC-CMs, at the levels of global transients and sparks, we provided the first direct evidence of functional EC coupling, facilitating the development of various in vitro approaches to drive their maturation. 3) Epigenetic regulation is implicated in embryonic development and the control of gene expression in a cell-specific manner. However, little is known about the role of histone methylation changes on human cardiac differentiation and maturation. We found that the epigenetic state of hESC-VCMs is dynamic and primed to promote growth and developmental maturation, but that proper environmental stimuli with chromatin remodeling will be required to synergistically trigger global CM maturation to a more adult-like state. 4) Although the electrophysiology of single hESC-CMs is now better defined, their multi-cellular arrhythmogenicity has not been thoroughly assessed due to the lack of a suitable experimental platform. Indeed, the generation of ventricular (V) fibrillation requires single-cell triggers as well as sustained multi-cellular reentrant events. Although native VCMs are aligned in a highly organized fashion such that electrical conduction is anisotropic for coordinated contractions, hESC-derived CM (hESC-CM) clusters are heterogenous and randomly organized, and therefore not representative of native conditions. Here, we reported that engineered alignment of hESC-VCMs on biomimetic grooves uniquely led to physiologically relevant responses. Not only do functional anisotropic hESC-VCMs engineered by multi-scale topography represent a more accurate model for efficacious drug discovery and development as well as arrhythmogenicity screening (of pharmacological and genetic factors), but our approach may also lead to future transplantable prototypes with improved efficacy and safety against arrhythmias.

772410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
772410.value: We are currently translating these findings into practicable applications: engineering of human cardiac tissues as well as "mini-hearts" with properties that are more similar to the native heart. These can be used for drug discovery and cardiotoxicity screening with higher sensitivity and accuracy, as well as to serve as future transplantation prototypes.

772410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
772410.value: Heart diseases are a major cause of death worldwide. Loss of cardiomyocytes (CMs) due to aging or diseases is irreversible. Current therapeutic regimes are palliative; in end-stage heart failure, transplantation remains the last resort but is significantly hampered by a severe shortage of donors. Human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) can self-renew while maintaining their pluripotency to differentiate into all cell types, including CMs. Direct reprogramming of adult somatic cells to induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) has been achieved. The availability of hESC/iPSCs has enabled researchers to gain novel biological insights and to pursue heart regeneration. Despite these promises, substantial hurdles remain for translating into cell-based therapies and other applications (e.g., disease modeling, cardiotoxicity and drug screening). Based on our team's own work in the past decade, we identified major gaps: hESC-CMs have immature properties. In this project, we have overcome some of these hurdles. We are currently in the process translating these findings into practicable applications, by merging with some of the latest state-of-art technologies i.e. engineering of human cardiac tissues as well as "mini-hearts". These tools can be used for drug discovery and cardiotoxicity screening with higher sensitivity and accuracy, as well as to serve as future transplantation prototypes.

772510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
772510.value: 尽管近年来在心血管疾病的诊断和预防上取得了很大的进展，但冠状动脉疾病（CAD）在香港乃至整个世界范围内，发病率和死亡率仍居高不下。现在的治疗方法，例如冠状动脉血管重建术（coronary revascularization）仍然无法避免心肌损伤，在20-37%的病人中并发了心肌梗死，逐渐出现心脏功能衰竭症状。最近的研究发现，骨髓间充质干细胞（MSC）疗法可改善心梗后发生的心肌损伤及心脏功能衰竭。而骨髓间充质干细胞分泌的一系列营养因子及免疫因子可保护心肌细胞，招募心肌干细胞（cardiac progenitor cells,CPC），可能是其作用的主要机制之一。因此，鉴定这些MSC旁分泌因子对心脏的保护作用，将有重要的科研及临床意义。 近来，我们发现在低氧培养后，MSC分泌的培养基可延缓低氧条件下Kit+/Lin-心肌干细胞的衰老。在这些不同的旁分泌因子中，我们发现低氧培养后的MSC培养基中高表达基质细胞衍生因子-1（Stromal cell-derived factor-1，SDF-1）及神经调节素-1（Neuregulin，NRG-1）。SDF-1及NRG-1分别通过各自的受体CXCR4及ERbB4，促进心肌细胞存活及生长。而我们也证实了，CXCR4及ERbB4的过表达可提高心肌干细胞的低氧环境下的存活率。然而，SDF-1/ CXCR4和NRG-1/ ERbB4在缺血损伤后，影响心肌干细胞增殖及分化的潜在机制还未阐明。在低氧条件下，CXCR4仅在最初的24小时内瞬时表达，而ERbB则表达缺失。在本研究中，我们假设SDF-1和NRG-1可产生协同效应，在缺血损伤后，对成熟的心肌细胞及未分化的心肌干细胞都发挥保护作用。为证实这个假设，我们设定了一系列实验目标： 目标1. SDF-1及NRG-1对低氧损伤后的Kit+/Lin-心肌干细胞特性的影响 目标2. SDF-1及NRG-1延缓低氧损伤后的心肌干细胞发生衰老的主要机制 目标3. 在缺血小鼠模型上，证实激活心肌干细胞的SDF-1/ CXCR4和NRG-1/ ERbB4轴对心肌的作用 本研究可阐明MSC移植后发挥积极作用的机制，SDF-1和/或NRG-1在心肌梗死后对心脏的保护作用，可能作为潜在的新的治疗手段。

772510.label: Major findings and research outcome
772510.value: We found ERBB4 expressed MSC display stronger survival and mobilization potentials associated with a NRG1-ERBB4/ ligand-receptor manner against serum depletion or hypoxia. Second, through western blotting, ELISA and FACS assays, it revealed that MSC with ERBB4 overexpression in turn increased NRG1 synthesis and secretion, forming a novel NRG1-ERBB4-NRG1 autocrine loop. Further studies showed the activation of NRG1-ERBB4-NRG1 autocrine loop is regulated through a PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. Third, in vitro transwell culture assay disclosed enhanced functional NRG1 secretion protects neonatal cardiomyocytes against hypoxia stress. In addition, ERBB4 overexpressed MSC also increased secretion of stem cell factor (SCF) to mobilize Ckitpos progenitor cells. Fourth, transplantation of autocrine loop activated MSC significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction, reduced heart infarction size and preserved MSC and host cell survival post-heart infarction , compared with controls and naïve BM-MSC transplant(P<0.001).

772510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
772510.value: Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy can limit myocardial injury and cardiac dysfunction after heart infarction. The secretion of a variety of trophic and immunomodulatory factors by MSC to prevent cell death and recruit endogenous cardiac progenitor cells (CPC) have been postulated as one of the major mechanism of their beneficial effects. In this study, we identified that activation of a novel NRG1-ERBB4-NRG1 autocrine loop potentiates MSCs-mediated heart protection associated with increasing NRG1 concentration, preserving cardiac progenitor cells and mature cardiomyocytes. Compared with naïve bone marrow MSC transplantation, activation of NRG1-ERBB4-NRG1 signaling pathway in MSC transplant provides superior myocardial protections. These findings provide a novel strategy to enhance therapeutic efficacy of MSC-based transplantation in ischemic heart disease by pre-activating NRG1-ERBB4-NRG1 signaling pathway in MSC.

772710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
772710.value: The researches of our group have been focused on plant and microbial purple acid phosphatases (Phytochemistry, 2008; Gene 2009; Plant Physiology, 2009a; Plant Physiology, 2009b.). The subject of this study is AtPAP2, one of the 29 PAPs in Arabidopsis genome. We have generated overexpression lines, T-DNA line and complementation lines of AtPAP2 in Arabidopsis. The overexpression lines of AtPAP2 exhibited significant phenotypes when it is compared to the wild-type plants: (i) Earlier flowering and faster growth rate; (ii) Higher sucrose and glucose levels at the end of day. (iii) Higher seed yield (+38-57%) and siliques numbers (+38-57%) during maturity. (iv) Higher recovery rate under prolonged darkness treatment; (v) Higher activity of sucrose phosphate synthase; and (vi) Greater resistant to sucrose- and glucose-induced anthocyanin synthesis. Microarray studies showed that a number of key genes involved in K uptake and nitrogen assimilation were also altered in both independent overexpression lines (p<0.05). All of these phenotypes pointed to a dramatic shift of metabolism in the overexpression lines. Our hypothesis is that AtPAP2 might counteract the functions of SnRK1 or its upstream activating kinases and shift the carbon and nitrogen resources from catabolism to anabolism. SnRK1s in plants are the key switches of energy flow in living organisms. Under energy deficiency, SnRK1 is activated by phosphorylation at Thr175, which in turn phosphorylates a number of substrates, including sucrose phosphatase synthesis, nitrate reductase, 6-phosphofructose-2-kinase/ phosphofructose-2,6-bisphosphatase and HMG-CoA reductase. The phosphorylated forms of these proteins then bind to 14-3-3 proteins and become inactivated. Inactivation of SPS and NR channels the carbon and nitrogen resources from anabolism to catabolism. Overexpression of SnRK1.1 and 1.2 resulted in retarded growth, which is opposite to the phenotypes of the AtPAP2 overexpression lines in. Two kinases GRIKs were reported to phosphorylate both SnRK1.1 and 1.2 at the T-loop and enhance their kinase activities. Non-specific phosphatases like PP2C and PP2A had been reported to dephosphorylate SnRK1 in vitro. However, a phosphatase that specifically dephosphorylates SnRK1 in vivo has not yet been identified. A specific phosphatase that counteracts with SnRK or its upstream kinases should, theoretically, have higher SPS and NR activities, changes in 14-3-3 binding profiles, higher sucrose content, higher anabolism rates, and possibly higher growth rate and seed yield. Based on our current data, AtPAP2 might be a phosphatase that specifically dephosphorylates SnRK1 or its upstream kinases in vivo and the objective of this proposal to find out the answers. 我們組的科研目標主要集中在植物和微生物的紫色酸性磷酸酶。(Phytochemistry, 2008; Gene 2009; Plant Physiology, 2009a; Plant Physiology, 2009b.).本研究的主題是AtPAP2，是擬南芥基因組PAPs29個家族成員之一。我們已經在擬南芥中完成了這種PAP基因的過表達，T-DNA插入轉基因株系，以及回交系擬南芥。結果表明AtPAP2過表達的轉基因株系相對於野生型植株，顯出了顯著的表型差異。（一）早開花和更快的增長速度;（二）高蔗糖和葡萄糖含量，（三）成熟時有更高的種子產量高（增加了38-57％）和角果數（增加38-57％），（四）在黑暗長期處理後有更高的恢復率，（五）蔗糖磷酸合成酶有更高活性，及（六）對蔗糖和葡萄糖誘導花青素的合成有更大的抵制作用。 基因晶片的研究表明，許多關鍵的涉及到鉀離子吸收和氮同化的基因表達水準也在各個過表達株系過程發生了改變（P <0.05）。這些表型都表明在過表達株系中的新成代謝發生了很大變化。 我們的假設是，AtPAP2可能抵消SnRK1或者它的上游啟動激酶的活性，並且把碳和氮代謝的資源從分解代謝轉移到合成代謝。植物SnRK1是生物體能量流的關鍵開關。在能源缺乏時，SnRK1能通過Thr175位點的磷酸化被啟動，從而磷酸化很多下游底物，包括蔗糖磷酸合成酶，硝酸還原酶，6-phosphofructose-2-激酶/phosphofructose-2,6-二磷酸酶和HMG-CoA還原酶。這些被磷酸化的蛋白隨後綁定到14-3-3蛋白從而失去活性。失活的蔗糖磷酸合成酶和硝酸還原酶能把碳和氮代謝的資源從合成代謝轉換到分解代謝。過表達SnRK1.1和1.2導致了生長遲緩，這是與 AtPAP2過表達株系的表型是相反的。 據報導，兩種GRIKs激酶磷酸都能磷酸化SnRK1.1和1.2並加強其激酶活性。一些非特異性針對PP2C and PP2A的磷酸酶已經被報導過能在體外去磷酸化SnRK1。然而，能在體外特定去磷酸化SnRK1的磷酸酶還沒有被找到。理論上一個特定的能抵消SnRK或其上游激酶應該具有較高的蔗糖磷酸合成酶和硝酸還原酶活性，能改變14-3-3的結合模式，具有高蔗糖含量，較高的分解代謝率，可能較高的生長速度和種子產量。基於我們目前的資料，AtPAP2可能是一個能在植物體內特異性針對SnRK1或者其上游激酶的去磷酸磷酸酶。因此我們的目標和計畫就是找出這個答案。

772710.label: Realisation of objectives
772710.value: Objective 1, to find out the physiological roles of AtPAP2 in plant, is the main goal of this study. Two articles (Sun et al., 2012a, 2012b) were published to describe its subcellular localization and biological effects. We have further delineated its biological roles (see 6.1) and a manuscript is under preparation. Objectives 2, 3 and 4 are to study the metabolome, phosphoproteome and transcriptome of the fast-grow lines. We have achieved these objectives except that proteome instead of phosphoproteome were examined. Data on metabolome (sugars, organic acids, amino acids) was published in Sun et al., 2012a and data on ATP/ADP/NADPH/NADP was published in Liang et al., 2013. The microarray data (objective 4) was also published in Liang et al., 2013. A manuscript is being prepared to integrate the Omics data (transcriptome, proteome and metabolome). Objective 5: We found that AtPAP2 is a protein phosphatase. It is responsible for protein dephosphorylation. Objective 6: We only examined the rate of K updates in the transgenic lines. Objective 7: We achieved this goal and the results were published in Zhang et al., 2012.

772710.label: Major findings and research outcome
772710.value: Overexpression (OE) of AtPAP2 in Arabidopsis led to faster plant growth, elevated sucrose content and high seed yield (Sun et al., 2012a). The transgenic lines also contained elevated level of ATP but the level of NADPH remained similar to the wild-type (WT) (Liang et al., 2013). We showed that AtPAP2 is the only known plant protein that is dual-targeted to chloroplasts and mitochondria by a C-terminal targeting signal. Using in vitro organelle import and green fluorescence protein (GFP) localization assays, we showed that AtPAP2 is located on, but not imported across the outer membrane (Sun et al., 2012b). Similar to AtPAP2, several protein receptors (Toc33/34 and Tom20), which are responsible for chloroplast and mitochondrial imports, are also anchored on the outer membranes by their C-termini (Sun et al., 2012b). By yeast-two hybrid and BIFC experiments, we showed that AtPAP2 interacted with the transit peptides of a number of nuclear-encoded proteins that are targeted to chloroplasts (small subunit of Rubisco, pMORF2, etc) and mitochondria (pMORF3,5,6). Import experiments showed that the speed of import into these organelles were different between the OE and WT lines (unpublished results). Hence, our results indicate that AtPAP2 is likely to be a protein phosphatase anchored on the outer membranes of chloroplasts and mitochondria and is responsible for selective import of certain proteins into chloroplasts (photosynthesis) and mitochondria (pMORFs, responsible for RNA editing). By using sucrose density gradient, the thylakoid membrane protein complexes (e.g. PSII-LHCII and PSI-LHCI-LHCII) were fractionated. Western blot analysis showed that some thylakoid membrane proteins exhibited differential protein expression between WT and OE fractions. We hypothesize that the overexpression of AtPAP2 leads to selective import of proteins into chloroplasts and causes substantial changes in the macrostructure of photosystem complexes. As a consequence, the energy capturing capacity of chloroplasts may be enhanced and thus results in higher ATP, higher sugar and seed yield in the OE lines. In additional to the publications listed in Part C, two manuscripts are under preparation to report the major findings described above. Overexpression of AtPAP2 in a Brassica, Camelina sativa, also led to faster growth and high seed yield (Zhang et al., 2012). The findings from this study may help to improve crop production in the future.

772710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
772710.value: 1. We hypothesize that cyclic electron flow (CEF), where electron is transferred from photosystem I (PSI) back to plastoquinone (PQ), might be enhanced in the OE lines. CEF generates ATP-generating proton gradient without NADPH production and thus conforms to our metabolomics data. We shall verify this by carrying out chlorophyll fluorescence measurement and oxygen evolving assays. 2. How overexpression of AtPAP2 affects the physiology of mitochondria is still unclear. We also generated AtPAP2 overexpression lines which only targeted AtPAP2 to mitochondria. These OE lines still contained high ATP levels but exhibited early senescence. We shall compare the mitochondrial complexes isolated from the OE (dual-targeted and single-targeted) and WT lines by 2D BN-PAGE DIGE and compare their mitochondrial proteomes by iTRAQ LC-MS-MS. The physiology of mitochondria will be examined by oxygen evolving assays and activity assays. 3. Our studies showed that AtPAP2 interacted with a number of pMORF proteins which are targeted to chloroplasts or mitochondria. pMORF proteins were shown to involve in RNA editing in these two organelles. We obtained RNA-seq data of the OE and WT lines, including organellar transcripts. Bioinformatics analysis will be carried out to examine if overexpression of AtPAP2 affect the extent of RNA editing in these two organelles.

772710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
772710.value: AtPAP2 is the only protein known to be dually targeted to the outer membranes of both energy-generating organelles (chloroplasts and mitochondria) in plants. Overexpression of AtPAP2 in Arabidopsis results in fast-growth, high energy (ATP), high sugars and high seed yield (+50%) in transgenic plants. Our studies delineate the biological roles of AtPAP2 in plants and partially explain how its overexpression leads to the above phenotypes. The AtPAP OE lines are unique. To date, our lines are the only transgenic lines that exhibited significantly higher ATP contents in both dark (no photosynthesis) and light conditions. Energy is the driving force of all anabolic processes. Our lines will provide an unique model for the plant science community to study the impact of high energy supply on plant physiology. Fast-growth and high seed yields are the goals of agrobiotechnology. The discovery from this project may contribute to yield improvement in agriculture in a long run.

772810.value: 視網膜會發生多種遺傳性或後天性的退行性病變,“老年性黃斑變性”和“視網膜色素變性”是其中兩大類最主要的疾病，它們的共同特征是，在疾病早期，患者先出現逐漸加重的夜盲癥狀，隨著疾病的發展，患者的日間視力也逐漸減弱，直至完全失明。這是由於視網膜中對光敏感的的“感光細胞”死亡造成的，不幸的是，死亡的感光細胞無法自行修復或再生。時至今日，對這兩種視網膜病變，我們仍舊顯得有些束手無策。 我們計劃用一種新近發現的感光色素——“黑視素”（melanopsin）來取代已死亡的感光細胞色素來建立新的感光細胞。之前，我們通過基因工程的方法，把黑視素轉染到因感光細胞死亡而失明的小鼠的“視網膜神經節細胞“中，以求恢復它的視覺。我們發現新表達的黑視素，可以幫助失明的眼睛恢復對光的基本反應和簡單的視覺導向行為。可是，這種僅依賴於神經節細胞重構視覺的方法，跳過了視網膜內部的必要而復雜的信號處理過程，因此，恢復的視覺可能有所欠缺。下一步，我們將把黑視素轉染到神經節細胞的上一級細胞"雙極細胞"，以期待取得較高的空間分辨率和光線敏感性，實現更精確的視覺反應。 我們的假設基於視覺信息在視網膜的處理過程通過“明”和“暗”兩條平行的路徑：光線增加時，“明”路徑激活，而光線減少時，“暗”路徑激活。在神經節細胞上表達黑視素只激活了對”明”反應的一條通路。而讓雙極細胞人工表達黑視素，可以同時激活“明”“暗”兩條通路，恢復的視覺將更接近正常。此外，轉染黑視素進入雙極細胞的另一個優勢是，它可能對保護視網膜內部結構也有所幫助，可謂一舉兩得。 總之，通過基因工程方法，人工建立感光細胞，可以為治療視網膜變性創造機會。盡管我們的基因療法，可能受光線強度影響，或因轉染細胞對光的反應遲緩而欠完善；但要記住，我們現階段研究的初衷是給因病致盲的患者提供日常生活最基本的視覺輔助，像具備對周圍方位識別能力和緩慢離床步行能力；而恢復更具挑戰性的高級別的視覺，像面部識別，顏色分辨等將是我們未來研究的目標。

772810.label: Major findings and research outcome
772810.value: We used an adeno-associated viral vector (AAV) or in vivo electroporation to produce widespread expression of melanopsin in bipolar cells in the rd10 mouse model of human retinitis pigmentosa (RP). We investigated the morphological and functional properties of bipolar cells, using a combination of immunohistochemistry, patch-clamp recordings, electroretinographic (ERG) analysis and optokinetic tracking. We found that polysaccharides provided functional rescue of photoreceptors and improved visual behaviors in rd10 mice. Ectopic expression of melanopsin in bipolar cells conferred light sensitivity to the ON pathways of the retina, and improved ERG responses. The treatment also allowed the animals to respond to light and dark and to successfully restore optomotor behavioral performance.

772810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
772810.value: We will continue to use different promoters to drive the expression of melanopsin in a specific population of bipolar cells, and investigate animal behavioral performance for understanding how the brain decode signals from different signaling pathways.

772810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
772810.value: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is caused by a large number of mutations that result in the loss of photoreceptors and subsequent partial or complete blindness. At present, no effective treatment is available for restoring vision to RP patients once photoreceptors have been lost. To restore photosensitivity to the photoreceptor degenerated retinas, we genetically targeted photosensitive pigment melanopsin to the surviving bipolar cells, the second-order neurons, to convert them into photosensitive photoreceptors in a mouse model of RP. We used an adeno-associated viral vector (AAV) to produce widespread expression of melanopsin in bipolar cells in rd10 mice. We found that ectopic expression of melanopsin in bipolar cells restored light responses in the retina. The treatment also allowed the animals to respond to light and dark and to successfully restore optomotor behavioral performance. The melanopsin-based gene therapy thus has great potential to restore light perception in humans suffering from photoreceptor degenerations.
