772910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
772910.value: Angiogenesis plays an important role in many diseases including cancer. Although antiangiogenic agents targeting vascular endothelial growth factor are already in clinical use and can effectively treat various cancers, there is a continued need for the development of new angiogenesis inhibitors to circumvent resistance or reduce toxicity. A recombinant polypeptide, NC1 domain of the α chain of type VIII collagen (vastatin), has previously been shown to inhibit bovine aortic endothelial cell proliferation, revealing its potential antiangiogenic activity. We first investigated the in vivo efficacy of recombinant adeno-associated virus carrying human vastatin (rAAV-vastatin) for treating hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in a rat orthotopic model. Recently, we evaluated its effect for treating glioblastoma in a human glioblatoma U87 cell nude mouse xenograft model, and compared its efficacy with other anti-angiogenic genes. Our results showed that rAAV-vastatin significantly prolongs median survival time and inhibits tumor growth in both HCC-bearing rats and U87 glioblastoma-bearing mice. No toxicity was observed, even when a high dose of rAAV-vastatin was administered. Importantly, we discovered that vastatin is particularly effective for the treatment of glioblastoma. As the molecular mechanisms and the therapeutic benefits associated with vastatin-mediated therapy are not fully understood, we propose here to further evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of vastatin in a clinically relevant intracranial glioblastoma animal model, and examine the mechanisms by which vastatin inhibits angiogenesis and glioblastoma proliferation. We will identify the downstream targets and signaling pathways for vastatin-mediated anti-angiogenic and anti-glioblastoma therapies. Understanding these mechanisms should lead to future advances in the clinical use of vastatin and in the development of novel, promising treatments for glioblastoma, HCC and other cancers. 血管生成在包括腫瘤在內的許多疾病裡面起著非常重要的作用。 儘管針對血管內皮為靶點的抗血管生成藥物在臨床上已經應用，並且可以有效地治療各種腫瘤，為了克服藥物抗性或者降低現有藥物的毒性，仍舊需要開發新型的血管生成抑制劑。重組多肽，IIIV型膠原蛋白（伐他汀）的α鏈的NC1結構域,已經被試驗證明可以抑制牛主動脈內皮細胞的增殖，顯示了其具有潛在抗血管生成的性質。應用大鼠原位肝細胞癌模型，我們首次在體內研究了帶有人源的伐他汀基因的重組腺相關病毒治療肝癌的效果。 最近我們又研究了它對人腦膠質瘤裸鼠移植瘤的治療效果，並和其他抗血管生成基因的治療效果做了比較。我們的研究結果表明，帶有人源的伐他汀基因的重組腺相關病毒可以顯著地抑制肝細胞癌和人腦膠質瘤細胞在大鼠和裸鼠身上的生長，並顯著延長大鼠和裸鼠的中位生存期。即使給予大鼠和裸鼠高劑量的帶有人源的伐他汀基因的重組腺相關病毒，仍然沒觀察到任何的毒副作用。更重要的是，我們發現伐他汀治療腦膠質瘤特別有效。至於伐他汀的治療效果及其相關的機理還不完全清楚，所以，我們在此提出進一步評價伐他汀在顱腦內的膠質瘤腫瘤的動物模型上的治療效果，並研究伐他汀通過什麼機理抑制腦膠質瘤的血管生成，因為顱腦內膠質瘤腫瘤的動物模型和臨床上膠質瘤腫瘤更加相似。我們將鑒定伐他汀下游的靶點和參與其抗血管生成和抗腦膠質瘤生長的具體信號通路。對其分子機理的研究，將會進一步促進伐他汀在臨床上的應用，並且促進開發新型、充滿前景的治療腦膠質瘤、肝細胞癌及其他癌症的方法。

772910.label: Realisation of objectives
772910.value: To evaluate the therapeutic effect of vastatin as compared to endostatin, the leading anti-angiogenic gene, in mice intracranially transplanted with U87 glioblastoma cells. 1.1 We established a murine model of intracranial GBM and showed that this model well represents the human GBM tumour in terms of the high vascularity, necrosis, mitosis, haemorrhage and angiogenesis. Treatment of vastatin was delivered by a nanoparticle Folate-PEI600-CyD (H1) mediated gene therapy. Enhanced local expression of vastatin was confirmed after intratumoural injection of H1/vastatin. H1/vastatin significantly prolonged the survival of GBM-bearing mice. Histologic staining showed that vastatin decreased the vessel density in tumours and caused a more defined margin, both of which indicated reduced malignancy. H1/Endostatin also prolonged the survival of animals. There was no significant difference in animal survivals between vastatin and endostatin treated groups. No obvious mortality or behavioural disorder was caused by the treatment. We demonstrated that H1/vastatin gene therapy is of therapeutic potential for GBM. 1.2 To achieve maximal therapeutic effect, we combined vastatin with chemotherapy for the treatment of intracranially xenografted glioblastoma. We first generated chemoresistant GBM cells U87-ATR by chronic exposure of GBM U87 cells to TMZ in culture. Then we successfully used these cells to established a TMZ resistant GBM model by intracranial inoculation. Treatment of H1/vastatin not only prolonged the survival of the animals alone, but also enhanced the therapeutic efficiency of TMZ. Thus we suggested vastatin has synergistic effect with TMZ chemotherapy. 2. To elucidate the mechanisms of action underlying the antiangiogenic effects of vastatin. 2.1 To investigate the mechanisms of vastatin induced antiangiogenesis, we showed that AAV-Vastatin infection inhibited the proliferation, tube formation and migration of microvascular endothelial cells (MEC) in vitro. 2.2 We have conducted cDNA microarray study to identified the effect of AAV-Vastatin on global gene expression profile of microvascular endothelial cells. Vastatin down regulated the pathways involved in MECs proliferation, metabolism, cell adhesion and Notch signaling activity, suggesting a broad spectrum antiangiogenic effect. The results were confirmed by western blot.

772910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
772910.value: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a very deadly cancer which is still in lack of effective treatment. Antiangiogenesis is a therapeutic strategy that aims to kill tumours by blocking new vessel formation and suspending nutrient supplement. We previously found that vastatin, an fragment of collagen VIII, had antiangiogenic activities on cell level and in animal model of liver cancer. We hoped that vastatin could also be used for treating GBM. In this study we established a mouse GBM model and tried to test the therapeutic potential of vastatin. These results suggested that vastatin could be used for future drug development and bring hopes to GBM patients.

773210.label: Realisation of objectives
773210.value: In the current proposal, we first aimed to identify the anti-oxidative effect of lutein and its underlying mechanism in cerebral and retinal ischemia/reperfusion injury. We successfully demonstrated that lutein treatment increased neuronal viability and decreased oxidative stress induced after ischemic injury reflected by reducing apoptotic neurons and decreasing the expression of nitrotyrosine and poly(ADP-ribose), respectively in neurons in both the brain and the retina. Through these studies, we have successfully achieved our first aim. Secondly, we aimed to elucidate lutein-mediated protection in relation to post-ischemic inflammation as well as activation of NF-κB and its target genes. Again, we demonstrated that lutein displayed anti-inflammatory effects by decreasing nuclear translocation of NFκB as well as modulating MAPK/ERK and NFκB signaling pathways in the neurons in both the brain and the retina. These results clearly demonstrated that lutein is neuroprotective and can reduce most of the detrimental damages (both morphologically and functionally) caused by ischemic injury by its anti-apoptotic, anti-oxidative and anti-inflammatory effects. We have been trying to further delineate and distinguish the effect of lutein on neurons and glia using a more homogeneous population of cells. We have chosen to use cell culture for this purpose. In the studies relating to retinal ischemic injury, we are successful with the Muller cells as a cell line is available (results published). Yet, there is none for retinal ganglion cells. We have tried to isolate these cells ourselves following published protocol but in vain. We have sought for advice from experts in the field; yet, the purity and yield await further optimization. We have therefore requested for an extension of 6 months. Recently, with advice from other vision researchers in international conferences, we started to work on a retinal cell line, R28, which is claimed to carry characteristics of retinal neurons. Studies using this cell line are on-going.

773210.label: Major findings and research outcome
773210.value: We investigated the effect of lutein treatment in experimental stroke in a murine model of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury using unilateral middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Higher survival rate, better neurological scores and smaller infarct size were observed in lutein-treated mice. Lutein could effectively reduce oxidative stress by inhibiting expression of nitrotyrosine, poly(ADP-ribose) and nuclear translocation of NFκB as well as modulating MAPK/ERK and NFκB signaling pathways. These findings showed the neuroptotective role of lutein in experimental stroke for the first time and were published as research article and book chapter (Part C Section 8 #1,7) and presented (oral and poster) in international conferences (Part C Section 9 #2,3,10). Following on our previous reports on beneficial effects of lutein in retinal I/R injury (Li et al Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci[2009]50:836-43; Li and Lo* Int J Mol Sci[2010]11:2109-17), we further showed that lutein treatment minimized deterioration of retinal function and reduced gliosis in retinal I/R injury. In cultured Muller cells, lutein treatment increased cell viability and reduced level of nuclear NFκB, IL-1β and Cox-2, suggesting an anti-inflammatory role of lutein, which is a novel finding. These results were published as book chapter, research article and review (Part C section 8 #3,4,7) as well as presented in international conferences (Part C Section 9 #1,5,6,8,10-12). They are also well received and were presented as an invited talk in Special Interest Group (SIG) on “Anti-oxidants and AMD: into the mechanisms” in 2013 (Part C Section 11). Based on our report on anti-apoptotic properties of lutein, we further extended our investigations into its role in retinal detachment using rats. Lutein could salvage photoreceptors, with a therapeutic window of at least 36h. These novel findings were published as review and research article (Part C Section 8 #2,6) as well as presented in a conference (Part C Section 9 #4). Moreover, a MBBS student was awarded MRes[Med] and received Young Investigator Award in 2011 (Part C Section 10-11) with this project. Using the same I/R model, we also expanded our investigations to study the neuroprotective role of other naturally occurring compounds, namely Lycium barbarum polysaccharides (LBP). A PhD student (YANG Di) who was trained in the lutein project confirmed that LBP is neuroprotective based on its anti-oxidative properties. Her studies were published as review and research article (Part C section 8 #5,7) as well as presented in a conference (Part C Section 9 #7,9).

773210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
773210.value: We have established and confirmed the neuroprotective role of lutein in cerebral and retinal ischemic injury, a novel information on lutein. Lutein mediates its neuroprotective effects by its anti-oxidative, anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory properties, which is reported by our team for the first time. Yet, further experiments are necessary to distinguish lutein’s effects on the neurons and glia. As described in Section 5.3, we have requested for a 6-month extension. During this period, we have characterized a retinal neuronal cell line. We have also discovered another novel property of lutein, its involvement with the autophagy pathway, which is a novel finding and has not been reported before. Together with the studies using retinal neuronal cell line, this data will considerably provide more information on the mechanism of lutein-mediated neuroprotection, which will significantly increase the therapeutic potential for the clinical use of lutein in ischemic stroke and retinal ischemic injury, in which neuroprotective interventions are lacking. These results will provide us with preliminary data for the coming GRF exercise.

773210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
773210.value: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death worldwide, bringing about serious lasting disability and considerable social burden. Vision impairment can also occur due to ischemic injury in the retina. There have been diverse therapeutic interventions, based on general success in pre-clinical animal studies involving various neuroprotective candidates. However, these have been unsuccessful clinically. Using various animal and cell culture models of cerebral and retinal ischemic injury as well as retinal detachment, we identified and confirmed for the first time the neuroprotective role of lutein with its anti-oxidative, anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory properties. Lutein is a safe dietary carotenoid and has been used as a functional nutrient. Our results help to recognize, establish, strengthen, and verify another important role of lutein as a potential therapeutic agent that is effective and safe in ischemic stroke and retinal ischemic injury, adding significant predictive value in selecting lutein for translation into human clinical trials.

773310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
773310.value: 在拟南芥裡大約有3500花藥特定基因﹐了解它們的功能除了可以增進我們對植物繁殖的知識外﹐也可在育種和農業上控制雄蕊的繁殖力。 最近我們報告了一個在拟南芥雄蕊繁殖中不可缺少的一個DFR相關基因(DRL1)。 DRL1不是一個典型的DFR酵素, 但它跟很多在苯基丙酸代謝中需要NADPH的酵素有一定程度的同源性。拟南芥drl1突變體的花粉壁形成是有缺陷的﹐ 而且DRL1是在被子植物(包括單子葉和雙子葉)中有高度保留性﹐所以在不同植物裡很有可都是由一條與DRL1相關的代謝途徑來生產花粉壁的分子成份。本計劃將以重組蛋白酵素的催化效力測試跟突變體和轉基因體的代謝分析來了解DRL1的生化功能﹐並探討DRL1在水稻和煙草的雄蕊繁殖力上的作用。我們的研究有助於發現一條生產花粉壁的進化保守代謝途徑﹐並提供出一個可以用作調控經濟作物雄蕊不育的分子目標。 (詳情以英語版本為準)

773310.label: Realisation of objectives
773310.value: Objective 1: As the anther-specific AtDRL1 was initially annotated as a flavonoid enzyme (dihydroflavonol 4-reductase), recombinant protein was expressed in E coli and first tested for its activities toward different phenylpropanoid and flavonoid substrates. We demonstrated that it does not utilize these substrates, thus it is not likely to be involved in flavonoid and phenylpropanoid metabolism in developing anther. A few months after this project was started, the role of AtDRL1 as a tetraketide α-pyrone reductase (TKPR) was reported (Plant Cell 22:4667-4083). We quickly switched our focus to investigate whether the biochemical steps involving TKPR and other enzymes are conserved in different flowering plants. In tobacco, we isolated anther-specific cDNAs encoding acyl-CoA synthetase (NtACOS1), polyketide synthase (NtPKS1), and NtTKPR1. A range of fatty acid substrates (C6 – C18) with different hydroxylation patterns (in-chain and terminal) were used as substrates for NtACOS1. The reaction mixtures were then incubated with NtPKS1, following by further incubation with NtTKPR1. The reaction steps were optimized for the best pH and temperature conditions. LC-MS/MS analysis was used to analyze the reaction product at each step. Finally, the production of reduced α-tetraketide pyrone was detected after the three reactions. Hence the sequential ACOS-, PKS-, and TKPR-catalyzed reactions are conserved in tobacco. We further isolated rice anther-specific OsPKS1 and OsTKPR1 and demonstrated they have similar catalytic activities as the tobacco and Arabidopsis orthologs. Objective 2– In addition to DRL1 (now TKPR1), we examined the possible conservation of ACOS and PKS for male fertility in rice and tobacco. We performed in-situ hybridization to confirm the tapetum-specific expression of the tobacco ACOS1, PKS1, and TKPR1 genes. Suppression lines for each gene were generated using the RNAi approach. In each case, the endogenous promoter was used to drive the target dsRNA expression in transgenic tobacco lines. Successful gene suppression was achieved and three lines for each gene were selected for phenotypic analysis. As the anther-specific expression of OsPKS1 and OsTKPR1 was reported previously, we focused on the characterization of T-DNA insertion mutants available from the public domain. PCR genotyping were performed to identify homozygous insertion lines. A combination of morphological, histological, electron microscopy investigations were employed to investigate the anther developmental defects in the tobacco and rice mutants which were found to have different degrees of male sterility and seed yield reduction. Normal seed formation was observed when the different mutants were pollinated by wild-type plants, confirming that their female gametophytes were functional.

773310.label: Major findings and research outcome
773310.value: The metabolic steps catalyzed by the anther-specific ACOS, PKS, and TKPR were investigated. Using fatty acids as starting substrates, sequential activities of heterologously expressed tobacco NtACOS1, NtPKS1, NtTKPR1 resulted in the production of reduced tetraketide α-pyrones. Transgenic RNA interference lines were generated for the different tobacco genes which were demonstrated to be indispensable for normal pollen development and seed formation. In all cases, complete sterility with non-viable and highly distorted or malformed exine structures was observed. Apparently the reaction steps catalyzed by the enzymes encoded by these tobacco tapetum-specific genes are essential for exine formation and male fertility. Furthermore, recombinant rice OsPKS1 and OsTKPR1 were shown to function as downstream enzymes of NtACOS1. The mature anthers of Ostkpr1 mutants were completely empty and there were no seed formation. On the other hand, Ospks1 mutants showed partial sterility with significantly reduced seed formation. Blast search analysis of the rice genome identified an ACOS-like gene which is annotated to show strongest expression in pre-emergence inflorescences. Hence, it is highly likely that the encoded protein participates along the same pathway together with OsPKS1 and OsTKPR1, although no insertion lines are readily available for phenotypic analysis. The major findings described above were accepted for publication in Physiologia Plantarum (in press). The work was contributed by Wang Yanbing (tobacco and rice TKPR1; rice PKS1), Lin Ying-Chen (tobacco PKS1), and So Joan (tobacco ACOS). Most of Wang Yanbing’s PhD work was described in the above paper. A poster was presented at the 23rd International Conference on Arabidopsis Research in Vienna by Lin Ying-Chen in July 2002. In addition to the enzyme assay results, Lin presented our complementation analysis in Arabidopsis pks1 mutants by the transgenic expression of NtPKS1 under the control of the endogenous AtPKS1 promoters. The transgenic mutants were found to be fully male fertile with the formation of normal siliques and seeds. In Lin’s MPhil thesis, she also described the work on a second PKS gene, NtPKS2, in tobacco and it showed similar expression pattern as NtPKS2. In So Joan’ FYP project, she also described the full complementation of Arabidopsis acos5 mutant by NtACOS5 under the control of the AtACOS5 promoter. Thus, the PKS and ACOS genes are interchangeable between tobacco and Arabidopsis, further illustrating the conservation of these tapetum-specific genes between different flowering plants.

773310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
773310.value: While we demonstrated the anther-specific ACOS, PKS, and TKPR1 enzymes function sequentially in a conserved biochemical pathway in diverse plant species, the involvement of other related homologs cannot be excluded. For example, tobacco contains two anther-specific PKS genes with highly degree of identity (Lin’s thesis). Elucidation of the physiological and biochemical roles of NtPKS2 may reveal additional and novel biochemical pathways that are essential for pollen wall formation. There may also be considerable differences between the functional roles of anther-specific PKS enzymes in different species. While NtPKS1 is indispensable for pollen formation in tobacco, PKS single mutations only resulted in partial sterility in Arabidopsis and rice. Furthermore, we have constructed complementation vectors using either OsTKPR1 or NtTKPR1 driven by the native promoter of AtTKPR1. The vectors were then transformed into Arabidopsis tkpr1 mutants. However, neither OsTKPR1 nor NtTKPR1 was able to restore the male fertility and seed formation in the Arabidopsis mutant, suggesting that the different TKPR1 orthologs may function in a species-specific manner. Further investigations of PKS and TKPR genes/enzyme in different plants may reveal species-specific metabolic pathways essential for pollen wall formation and anther development. Preliminary data will needed to be generated for preparing a new GRF proposal.

773310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
773310.value: The development of pollen wall with proper sporopollenin formation is essential for pollen viability and male fertility in flowering plants. Sporopollenin is a complex biopolymer synthesized from fatty acid and phenolic acid derivatives. The existence of ancient biochemical pathways for sporopollenin biosynthesis has been widely proposed based on the widespread occurrence of a number of anther- and tapetum-specific homologous sequences encoding metabolic enzymes in monocot and dicot species. However, experimental evidence from plant species other than the experimental model plant Arabidopsis is not extensively available. Our study demonstrated that the metabolic steps catalyzed by ACOS, PKS, TKPR1 are evolutionarily and functionally conserved in taxonomically distinct species including plants in the mustard, grass, and nightshade families. Sequential activities of these enzymes resulted in the formation of reduced tetraketide α-pyrones, potentially representing essential building blocks for pollen wall formation in flowering plants. Hence, the above anther-specific enzymes may be exploited as molecular targets for manipulation of male sterility in economic crops. Male sterility in plants is a useful trait for different agricultural applications, such as extension of flower shelf-life and production of hybrid seeds.

773710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
773710.value: During spermatogenesis, spermatogonia (diploid) undergo a series of cell divisions including mitosis and meiosis and further differentiate into mature elongated spermatozoa (haploid) in the seminiferous epithelium. At the same time, these developing germ cells initially situated at the basal compartment must traverse the blood-testis barrier (BTB) constituted by tight junctions (TJ) and adherens junctions (AJ) to enter the adluminal compartment of the seminiferous epithelium for further development. Therefore, a timely disassembly of cell junctions including TJ and AJ between adjacent Sertoli cells and AJ between Sertoli and germ cells should be implemented to allow the translocation of germ cells along the epithelium. Following the movement of germ cells, cell junctions must be immediately reassembled to maintain the integrity of the BTB to avoid the development of auto-immunity and to ensure the developing germ cells remain attached to Sertoli cells for nutritional and physical support. Thus, the precise regulation of cell junctions is important in spermatogenesis. The integrity of cell junctions is maintained by an array of transmembrane proteins including occludin, claudin-11, junctional adhesion molecule (JAM) and nectin. Each of the protein components indeed plays an indispensable role in the junction dynamics as single knockout of the gene encoding junction proteins could result in male infertility. Recently, nectin-like molecules (necl) have been identified as new components of epithelial adherens junction. Several necl members are present in the testis and knockout of necl-2 resulted in male infertility. In this proposal, the P.I. will focus on the regulation of necl-based AJs between Sertoli cell and germ cells. Specifically, the project aims to (i) investigate the effect of cytokines, TGF-βs, on the expression of necls in Sertoli cells and germ cells, and (ii) identify necl-associating partners in the testis. The results of this study will make a crucial contribution to the understanding of germ cell development and AJ restructuring during spermatogenesis.

773710.label: Realisation of objectives
773710.value: The objectives stated in the proposal have been extensively studied during the grant period. An array of techniques including cell culture, transfection, siRNA knockdown, immunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence, endocytosis assay, ChIP assay and promoter assay has been employed to address the stated objective. The function and regulation of necl proteins have been investigated during the grant period

773710.label: Major findings and research outcome
773710.value: In the whole grant period, the mechanisms on cytokine-mediated regulation of necl and the identification of necl-interacting proteins have been studied. We have investigated the mechanism on how TGF-β1 regulates Necl-2 expression to achieve timely junction restructuring in the seminiferous epithelium during spermatogenesis. We have demonstrated that TGF-β1 reduces Necl-2 mRNA and protein levels at both transcriptional and post-translational levels. Using inhibitor and clathrin shRNA, we have revealed that TGF-β1 induces Necl-2 protein degradation via clathrin-dependent endocytosis. Endocytosis assays further confirmed that TGF-β1 accelerates the internalization of Necl-2 protein to cytosol. Immunofluorescence staining also revealed that TGF-β1 effectively removes Necl-2 from cell-cell interface. In addition, TGF-β1 reduces Necl-2 mRNA via downregulating Necl-2 promoter activity. Mutational studies coupled with knockdown experiments have shown that TGF-β1-induced Necl-2 repression requires activation of Smad proteins. EMSA and ChIP assays further confirmed that TGF-β1 promotes the binding of Smad proteins onto MyoD and CCAATa motifs in vitro and in vivo. Taken together, TGF-β1 is a potent cytokine that provides an effective mechanism in controlling Necl-2 expression in the testis via Smad-dependent gene repression and clathrin-mediated endocytosis. (Cheng et al. 2011 Histology and Histopathology 26:1465-1474; Gao et al. 2013 PLOS one 8:e64316) We have also examined the necl-interacting partners and how TNF affects Necl expression by altering the interaction of Necl-4 with polarity protein and GTPases. We have demonstrated that Necl-4 protein level was significantly reduced by ~40% in TNFα-treated group when compared to vehicle control in the presence of cycloheximide, suggesting that TNFα promotes Necl protein turnover via post-translational regulation. Addition of nystatin (an inhibitor for caveolin-dependent endocytosis) or lactacystin (a proteasome inhibitor) significantly abolished the effect of TNFα on Necl expression, suggesting that caveolin-dependent endocytosis and proteasome might be involved in TNFα-induced Necl-4 reduction. Co-immunoprecipitation assay further confirmed that TNFα induced ubiquitin-conjugated Necl-4 in the presence of lactacystin. These results suggest that TNFα promotes Necl-4 turnover via caveolin-dependent endocytosis, as well as ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. By immunoprecipitation, we found that Necl-4 interacts with Par3 and Par6 to form a functional junction complex. TNFα promoted the binding of active cdc42 and aPKC to Necl-4, which alters the interaction of Par proteins with Necl-4. It is believed that the alteration of protein binding with Necl-4 causes destabilization of Necl-4 functional complex and trigger the degradation of Necl-4 through caveolin-dependent endocytosis and ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. (Li et al. 2011 Spermatogenesis 1:123-136; and some unpublished data are submitted to Biology of Reproduction).

773710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
773710.value: Our current studies have clearly shown that several cytokines play important role in regulating necl expression in testicular cells and the interaction of necl with other proteins is modulating the junction restructuring in the testis. In order to precisely facilitate the movement of developing germ cells along the seminiferous epithelium, restructuring of cell junctions constituted by different junction proteins must be crucially coordinated. A thorough understanding on how these cytokines and each junction proteins are involved in cell junction restructuring during spermatogenesis is of great importance. Data obtained from the testicular cell culture model enable us to design the in vivo models such as knockout model to further elucidate the potential function of necl proteins in the testis. We further extend our study in understanding the relationship between cytokine-mediated necl expression and male infertility and its underlying mechanisms. Further detailed investigation in the area is warranted and it definitely will shed new light in understanding unexplained male infertility.

773710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
773710.value: In this study, the expression and regulation of necl-2 in the testis and the interaction of necl with other junction proteins have been examined. We have identified the cytokines such as TGF-1 and TNF and respective signaling pathways involved in regulating the expression of necls so as to regulate the junction restructuring in the seminiferous epithelium required for germ cell development. The results obtained from this study make crucial contribution to the understanding of germ cell development and AJ restructuring during spermatogenesis. In fact, the findings are not be limited to testicular physiology since Necls are junction proteins that can be found in other tissues. Our studies serve as blueprints for other tissue models. This study provides a novel piece of information that Necls are in fact important transmembrane protein that facilitates cell adhesion and its timely regulation are of importance in germ cell development.

774110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
774110.value: Voice problems, or dysphonia, are common in children. High prevalence figures of voice disorders have been reported in this population with at a rate of at least 6% (McNamara & Perry, 1994). Children with voice problems suffer from significant functional limitations in their daily and social voice activities. They are also being negatively stereotyped by listeners (Connor et al., 2008). An accurate assessment of children with voice problems is an important first step for voice therapy planning and provision. Voice assessment includes examining the voice impairment severity as well as the patient's self-perceived functional impacts due to the voice problems. Currently, there is a lack of pediatric normative database on how Cantonese dysphonic children manifest differently from vocally healthy Cantonese children in terms of voice impairment and functional impacts. Therefore, basic-but-crucial clinical question namely "whether a given voice sample is normal or pathologic, and if pathologic, how severe" is not readily solved. Voice normative data are available in the Cantonese adult population. However, such data from adults cannot be applied in children because of the substantial structural and physiological differences between adult and children larynx. Data reported in the literature on English children cannot be directly applied in Cantonese children. Cantonese is a dialect of Chinese and is a tonal language whereas English is a non-tonal language. Studies have revealed that voice measures manifest differently between tonal and non-tonal languages (Chen, 2005; Yamazawa & Hollien, 1992). Therefore, applying those database established from English-speaking individuals in Cantonese children can be problematic as they may not be able to accurately reflect Cantonese children's voice impairment and functioning. This project is an extension of the previous work by the applicants, who have developed voice assessment protocols for clinical voice evaluation in Cantonese adults (Chan & Yiu, 2002; Ma, 2003; Ma & Yiu, 2001; Ma & Yiu, 2006). The study aims to develop and validate a protocol for assessing voice impairment and functional impacts of voice problems in Cantonese children. The World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF, World Health Organization, 2001) will be adopted as the overarching framework of the protocol. The project will provide a much-needed empirical basis for identifying and assessing Cantonese children with voice problems. 兒童聲線問題十分普遍，有研究顯示最少百份之六的兒童患有聲線問題。兒童的聲線健康與其身心及學術發展有極密切關係，有外國文獻指出聲線健康的兒童被視為較患聲線問題的兒童聰明、冷靜及有信心。 聲線評估結果有助於定立合適的治療，因此一套準確的聲線評估工具極為重要。然而，現今大部份為兒童設計的聲線評估工具源於西方國家，基於語言和文化上之不同，那些聲線評估工具並不能直接運用於香港學童上。要準確地評估香港（粵語）學童的聲線狀況，一套有效並合適香港（粵語）學童的聲線評估工具是十分重要的。 此研究目的為建立一套有效度的聲線評估工具以量度學童的聲線狀況，評估工具運用了世界衛生組織的國際功能，殘疾和健康分類 (International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health; World Health Organization, 2001) 作為概念，就聲線問題的：1)嚴重程度及 2)生活質素作出評估，此研究之結果將對於日後香港學童聲線研究及發展有極大的貢獻。

774110.label: Realisation of objectives
774110.value: The project was carried out in three stages achieving four objectives: OBJECTIVE ONE (Stage One): In Stage One, two studies were carried out. 1) The Pediatric Voice Handicap Index (pVHI, Zur et al., 2007) was translated from its original English version into Cantonese. The translated pVHI was trialed with 10 speech therapists and 10 parents to ensure face and content validity. 2) The selection and preparation of passage stimulus for connected speech sample recording was completed. The passage was trialed with 56 school-age children of various age groups (primary one to primary six) to evaluate its reliability and to ensure age-appropriate linguistic level for young children. OBJECTIVE TWO (Stage Two): In Stage Two, two studies were carried out. 1) A pilot study to examine parents' and teachers' ability to detect voice problems in children for appropriate referrals. Parents and teachers of 64 Primary One students in Hong Kong completed a screening questionnaire for each of their own child or student. They were asked to rate the overall voice severity rating of the child's voice on a 6-point equal appearing interval scale as well as decision of referral for follow-up of the child's voice conditions. Their judgements were compared against the judgements made by four speech therapists. Results revealed that parents and teachers were not as sensitive as speech therapists in identify children with voice problems. 2) A total of 1334 children recruited from 10 local primary schools in Hong Kong attended voice screening sessions conducted by speech therapists. At the screening sessions, students with either i) suspected voice problems associated with vocal pathologies or ii) healthy voice were invited to attend a full voice assessment at the HKU Voice Research Laboratory. A total of 57 voice-disordered children and 72 vocally healthy children completed the full voice assessment protocol. The voice assessment protocol involved evaluation of acoustic, aerodynamic and voice range profile characteristics. The child's self-perceived severity of voice problems, and their care-givers' perception of the child's voice problems were also assessed. A database which characterised the patterns of voice impairment and voice-related functional impacts in vocally healthy and voice-disordered children was established. OBJECTIVE THREE & FOUR (Stage Three): Stage Three involved determining the minimal set of voice measures for voice assessments in young children. Both objectives were addressed based on statistical analysis of the voice database established in Stage Two.

774110.label: Major findings and research outcome
774110.value: OUTCOMES OF OBJECTIVE ONE: 1) The translated paediatric Voice Handicap Index demonstrated good face and content validity. It was used to capture parent's perceived voice-related functional impacts in their children with voice problems. 2) A Cantonese passage was selected and was trialed with 56 school-age children from Primary One to Six. Results revealed that all children could read aloud the passage easily and fluently, suggesting the passage was at age-appropriate expressive level for school-age children. Also, highest within-trial and between-day reliabilities were obtained from passage reading than sustained vowel prolongation and sentence reading, suggesting that the passage was a reliable task to be included in the voice assessment protocol. The findings were presented at the 41st Annual Voice Foundation Symposium (Lee, Ma, & Lam, 2012). OUTCOMES OF OBJECTIVE TWO: 1) In the pilot study which examined parents' and teachers' ability to detect voice problems in children. Results revealed that parents and teachers were not as sensitive as speech therapists in identifying children with voice problems and normal voices, suggesting the important roles of speech therapists in voice screenings. The results were presented at the 10th Pan-European Voice Conference (Ma & Cheung, 2013); and also submitted to journal for publication (Cheung & Ma, submitted). 2) In the main study, 1334 children from 10 local primary schools in Hong Kong attended voice screening sessions. At the screening sessions, students with either i) suspected voice problems associated with vocal pathologies or ii) healthy voice were invited to attend a full voice assessment at the HKU Voice Research Laboratory. A total of 57 voice-disordered children and 72 vocally healthy children completed the full voice assessment. Presence of vocal pathology in dysphonic children was evaluated by endoscopic examination. A voice database of the children's acoustic, aerodynamic and voice range profile characteristics was established. The database also comprised the child's self-perceived severity of voice problems, and also their care-givers' perception of the child's voice problems. OUTCOMES OF OBJECTIVE THREE & FOUR: A minimal set of instrumental voice parameters was identified based on the predictive power of voice parameter in distinguishing children with vocal pathology from children without vocal pathology, and in distinguishing children with different voice severity levels. Results showed that the two groups of children (dysphonic versus vocally healthy) performed significantly different in six voice parameters, including the relative average perturbation, shimmer percentage, maximum phonation time, mean airflow rate, intensity range and profile area in maximum voice range profile. The combination of shimmer percentage and maximum phonation time correctly predicted 93.3% of the presence of vocal pathologies. The findings were reported at three conferences including the Summerfest 2013 The Multilingual Academy - Communication Disorders in a Multilingual World (Lam & Ma, 2013), the 10th Pan-European Voice Conference (Ma & Lam, 2013), and the 9th Asia Pacific Conference of Speech, Language and Hearing (Ma & Lam, 2013).

774110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774110.value: Based on the minimal set of voice measures that can best distinguish children with voice problems from vocally healthy children, further development of the research include developing a computerised programme (iOS and Android Apps) for teachers and parents to do a quick screening of their children's voice. This facilitates early identification of voice problems in children.

774110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774110.value: Currently, there is a lack of paediatric normative database on how Cantonese children with voice problem manifest differently from those with normal voices. The present study aimed to develop and validate a voice assessment protocol for assessing voice impairment and functional impacts due to voice problems in Cantonese children. Such voice assessment protocol represented the first of its kind for studying voice problems in Cantonese children. The norm gathered encompasses information on voice impairments and functional impacts of voice problems in Cantonese children. The database will serve as an invaluable resource for various professions including teachers, parents and healthcare workers to assess children who have developed some forms of voice problems.

774410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
774410.value: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a disease state characterized by airflow limitation that is not fully reversible. It consists of chronic bronchitis and emphysema. Cigarette smoking is the single most important cause of the disease. Exposure to passive smoking is also associated with an increased prevalence of COPD and respiratory symptoms. COPD has been estimated to be the third leading cause of mortality by 2020 worldwide. COPD is usually diagnosed in the later stages of its course with no specific treatment available for stopping the progression, other than smoking cessation. Recently, studies have suggested that adiponectin can influence the development of airway inflammation. Adiponectin, a member of the adipokine family secreted mainly by adipocytes, acts by binding to two cell membrane receptors, adiponectin receptor 1 (AdipoR1) and AdipoR2. AdipoR1 is a high-affinity receptor for globular adiponectin generated by proteolytic cleavage of adiponectin whereas AdipoR2 is for full-length adiponectin. Expression of adiponectin and functional adiponectin receptor 1 has been reported in airway epithelial cells. Cigarette smoke (CS) has been found to cause a decline in human serum adiponectin levels. However, links between adiponectin and CS-induced lung diseases are not well defined. Our preliminary data showed a decline in circulating and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) levels of adiponectin, and airspace enlargement in rat distal lung architecture after 56-day CS exposure. We hypothesize that the expression of adiponectin and its receptors will be modulated by CS exposure over time leading to airway cell injury. To verify the hypothesis, we will first characterize the cigarette smoke medium (CSM)-induced alterations in airway epithelial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, expression of proinflammatory cytokines and apoptosis induction in relation to adiponectin and its receptors in vitro. We will then clarify whether poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase-1 (PARP-1) activation resulting from CS-induced DNA damage plays a role in their regulation. The particular signaling pathways will be elucidated using selective inhibitors or activators to identify the potential therapeutic targets. We will further examine the in vivo effects of CS-exposed rats to compare lung injury development before and after the proposed therapeutic treatments through examination of serological indicators and morphological changes in the airways and lung parachyma by biochemical, histological and immunohistchemical techniques. This study will provide important insights into the understanding of the underlying pathophysiological pathways of COPD, and may identify therapeutic targets to arrest or slow down the progression of airway damage before the development of extensive airway destruction. 慢性阻塞性肺病是以肺部氣流阻塞且並不完全可逆為特徵的疾病。包括〝慢性支氣管炎〞和〝肺氣腫〞。吸煙為最重要的致病因素。吸二手煙與慢性阻塞性肺病之患病率的增加及呼吸道症狀也有關係。預計到二零二零年慢性阻塞性肺病將成為全球第三大致死疾病。此病通常在後期才被確診，除戒煙外尚無可用的特效療法以阻止病情的惡化。近期研究顯示脂聯素可以影響呼吸道炎症的形成。脂聯素是脂肪細胞因子之一，主要是由脂肪細胞分泌的。脂聯素通過與兩個細胞膜受體結合而發揮作用。脂聯素受體1是脂聯素蛋白裂解產物，與球形脂聯素具有高度親和性，而脂聯素受體2則與全長型脂聯素有親和力。已有報導指呼吸道上皮細胞有脂聯素和功能性脂聯素受體1的表達。目前已發現香煙煙霧能引起人血清中脂聯素的水平下降。但是脂聯素與香煙煙霧所促發的肺疾病之間的關係並不明確。我們的初步研究數據顯示，大鼠在接觸香煙煙霧56天之後，其循環和支氣管肺泡灌洗液中的脂聯素水平下降，及肺末梢組織氣腔擴張。我們假設脂聯素及其受體的表達會受持續接觸香煙煙霧所影響，以導致呼吸道細胞受損。為了驗證這一假說，我們將首先查找香煙煙霧引致的呼吸道上皮活性氧生成的變化，促炎性細胞因子的表達和誘導凋亡與脂聯素及其受體在體外的關係。然後弄清聚腺苷酸二磷酸核糖轉移酶-1活化對它們是否起調控作用。而該酶的活化是由香煙煙霧引發的脫氧核糖核酸損傷的結果。選用不同的聚腺苷酸二磷酸核糖轉移酶-1抑製劑或激活劑來闡明特定的信號傳導途徑，以尋找可能的治療目標。然後用接觸過香煙煙霧的大鼠做進一步研究，用生物化學，病理和免疫組織化學技術檢測血清指標，呼吸道形態及肺實質的改變來比較用建議的方法治療前後肺損傷的進展狀況。這項研究將對認識慢性阻塞性肺病的病理生理基本途徑提供重要的啟示，並可能找出治療目標，在氣道廣泛受損之前阻止或減緩其損傷的進展。

774410.label: Realisation of objectives
774410.value: Objective 1: Due to undetectable levels of secreted adiponectin in the supernatants of BEAS-2B cells using the commercially available ELISA kits, we have now successfully detected the intracellular adiponectin levels in cell lysates using Western blots after exposure to cigarette smoke medium (CSM) for 24 hours, in relation to the inflammatory marker, interleukin (IL)-8 in the cell supernatants using ELISA. We have accomplished the localization of adiponectin receptor (AdipoR) 1 and AdipoR2 after 24-hour CSM exposure in BEAS-2B cells using immunofluorescent microscopy and the lung sections from the in vivo cigarette smoke (CS)-exposed rat model using immunohistochemistry. Objective 2: For the in vivo model, we have evaluated the lipid profiles using biochemical assays and their regulating enzymes involving influx and efflux of cholesterol using Western blot analyses in relation to cigarette smoke (CS)-induced morphological damage using histological staining. Objective 3: For the in vitro model, we have studied the functional role of AdipoR1 in BEAS-2B cells by incubating recombinant full-length (from R & D System) or globular adiponectin (AdipoGen) in the absence and presence of CSM for 24 hours before assaying for inflammatory marker IL-8 release in the supernatants. Due to the unavailability of pharmacological tool, i.e. selective adiponectin receptor antagonist, we haven’t taken this part further. Objective 4: We have successfully investigated the intravenous administration of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) from two sources, i.e. human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived MSCs (iPSC-MSCs) and adult bone marrow-MSCs (BM-MSCs) as well as oral gavage of an antioxidant, epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) in the in vivo cigarette smoke (CS)-exposed rat model. We have measured various systemic and local oxidative and inflammatory markers using biochemical assays, ELISA and Western blots in the lung and heart homogenates.

774410.label: Major findings and research outcome
774410.value: 1. Cigarette smoke (CS)-exposed rats exhibited severe alveolar destruction that was attenuated in the presence of induced pluripotent stem cell derived-mesenchymal stem cells (iPSC-MSCs) or bone marrow (BM) derived-MSCs. This might be contributed to the novel observation of mitochondrial transfer from MSCs to rat airway epithelial cells in lung sections exposed to CS. In vitro studies further revealed that transfer of mitochondria from iPSC-MSCs to bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B) with preservation of adenosine triphosphate contents. This distinct mitochondrial transfer occurred via the formation of tunneling nanotubes (TNT). Inhibition of TNT formation blocked mitochondrial transfer. Our findings indicate a higher mitochondrial transfer capacity of iPSC-MSCs than BM-MSCs to rescue CS-induced mitochondrial damage. Submitted to American Journal of Respiratory Cell and Molecular Biology (under review). 2. Furthermore, both treatments shared similar efficacy to attenuate CS-induced lung cell apoptosis and to alleviate CS-induced elevation of systemic cytokine-induced neutrophil chemoattractant (CINC)-1 (an analog to human IL-8) and transforming growth factor (TGF)-1 but not in lung. Both CS-induced elevation of systemic 8-isoprostane (a marker of oxidative stress) and CS-induced reduction of lung adiponectin were abolished by iPSC-MSCs and not BM-MSCs. However, both treatments abolished CS-induced elevation of lung cholesterol with no effect on serum cholesterol. We found significant CS-induced reduction of ATP-binding cassette transporter (ABCA1; an enzyme controlling cholesterol efflux) and elevation of low density lipoprotein (LDL) receptor (LDL-R; an enzyme mediating cholesterol influx) in lung expression. We also observed reduced lung expression of cluster of differentiation 36 (CD36; an enzyme mediating fatty acid uptake and oxidation) after CS exposure. The full manuscript is being prepared for submission. 3. In parallel, oral administration of EGCG in the presence of CS exposure had no effect on systemic and lung adiponectin. EGCG abolished CS-induced systemic oxidative stress and inflammation but not local inflammation. 4. Cigarette smoke medium (CSM) did not cause secreted adiponectin in BEAS-2B supernatants but led to upregulation of AdipoR1 on the cell membranes. Both recombinant full-length (from R & D System) and globular adiponectin (AdipoGen) alone cause no elevation of IL-8 in the supernatants. However, recombinant full-length adiponectin potentiated CSM-induced elevation of IL-8 in the supernatants. We also observed upregulation of AdipoR1 over airway epithelial cells of lung sections after CS exposure. These data will be submitted as an abstract to the European Respiratory Congress to be held in September 2014.

774410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774410.value: • We did not perform pulmonary function assessment in rats despite observed lung damage. Further studies should be performed to directly examine the effect of cigarette smoking in the absence and presence of stem cell or drug treatment on lung function as we have recently bought and set up the unrestrained whole-body plethysmography in the department. • Interventional studies using specific siRNA for adiponectin receptors are warranted to explore the complex interplay of adiponectin between anti-inflammation and pro-inflammation in the development of lung damage. • The contractile properties of tracheal or bronchial rings should be tested in the ex-vivo setting to reflect the early structural changes using organ chambers, in collaboration with the Department of Pharmacology and Pharmacy. • BEAS-2B is a cell line, originally developed by immortalization of normal human bronchial epithelial cells using AD12-SV40 virus. To be certain that the present in vitro results are not unique to this cell line, there is a need to carry out studies in primary human normal tracheal, bronchial and small airway epithelial cells. • In order to obtain more physiological model, BEAS-2B cells or primary human airway epithelial cells may be cultured at air-liquid interface (ALI).

774410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774410.value: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a common airway condition that is characterized by losing lung function at an accelerated rate, which is probably due, at least in part, to accelerated apoptosis of alveolar capillaries caused by cigarette smoking. COPD is not only a smokers’ disease, but one that worsens with age. The airways lesions are inflammatory and bronchospastic, but alveolar lesions with destruction of airway sacs are ischemic. Using a rat model exposed to cigarette smoke to simulate COPD, we demonstrated a cascade of events involving systemic and lung oxidative stress, inflammatory process and cholesterol homeostasis with accelerated programmed cell death resulting in lung damage. In this study, cigarette smoke-exposed rats tend to have lower levels of adiponectin in the blood and lung than sham air-exposed rats. Adiponectin is a protein hormone produced mainly in the fat cells of the body. Our studies futher found that cigarette smoking led to upregulation of functional adiponectin receptor 1 (AdipoR1) in the airway epithelium, which might mediate chronic inflammation in COPD. Our findings allow better understanding the link between adiponectin and lung function, and provide further insights into strategies for slowing down the disease progression after cigarette smoking.

774610.label: Project Objectives
774610.value: To elucidate the mechanism(s) through which calcitriol acutely reduces the release of EDCF in SHR aorta. Our previous findings suggest that this acute vascular effect of calcitriol is related to calcium signaling in response to acetylcholine and ATP the receptor-mediated agonists [Wong et al., 2008]. Therefore, the present proposal will focus on examining the acute effect of calcitriol on capacitative calcium entry and/or calcium release from intracellular stores that are involved in EDCF production in SHR aorta. To investigate the signaling pathways involved in the improvement of endothelial functions by chronic treatment of calcitriol in SHR aorta. Our preliminary studies suggest that continuous administration of calcitriol (1.875 x 10-8 g/hr) to SHR for 6 weeks increases endothelium-dependent relaxation and reduces endothelium-dependent contractions in aorta, and these effects of calcitriol are mediated through mechanism(s) that are downstream of calcium signaling, unlike the acute vascular actions of calcitriol. Since classical vitamin D receptors are known to affect gene expression and transcription, the present study will examine the gene and protein expressions of endothelial cells, which determine the progression of endothelial senescene hence dysfunction [Maier et al., 1990; Comi et al., 1995; Shelton et al., 1999; Ha et al., 2004; Lee et al., 2007], following chronic treatment with calcitriol. To evaluate the potentials of calcitriol as a preventive measures against the development of hypertension. Endothelial dysfunction is known to play a role in the development of hypertension [Vita et al., 2002; Vanhoutte et al., 2005; Taddei et al., 2006]. As our previous published and unpublished findings suggest that calcitriol has beneficial effects on endothelial function in hypertension, it will be reasonable to study whether or not supplementation of calcitriol at early stages of hypertension may prevent the progression of high blood pressure in SHR. To investigate whether or not the beneficial vascular effects of calcitriol is affected by the plasma level of gonadal hormones, testosterone and/or estrogen. Our previous studies demonstrate that gender, in particular the gonadal hormones, affects vascular reactivities [Teoh et al., 1999; 2000; Keung et al., 2005a]. , it is important to identify whether or not the beneficial vascular effects of calcitriol in hypertension are not affected by gender.

774610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
774610.value: 維生素D 對高血壓中內皮細胞功能異常的保護作用 維生素D 被認為是人體必需營養成分之一。研究發現它具有內固醇結構。受光線中的B型紫外線照射後，維生素D3（cholecalciferol）在人體皮膚中合成。維生素D3是活性代謝物1α,25(OH)2-D3（又稱為1,25-二羥維生素D或鈣三醇）的前體物。維生素D的其中一個重要作用是通過調節甲狀旁腺激素（PTH）的水準調節體內鈣平衡。近期研究表明維生素D能影響心腦血管功能。大鼠餵食缺乏維生素D的飼料後，其血管收縮壓明顯上升。長期居住于高海拔的人們比較容易得高血壓，通過補充維生素D後血壓歸於正常水準。與白人相比，非裔美國人高血壓和心臟病發病率較高，可歸咎為體內較低的維生素D水準。短期補充維生素D後能降低這些病人的血壓。 跟其它的類固醇激素一樣，鈣三醇作用于基因水準。維生素D的受體位於細胞的膠質溶漿中。當其與鈣三醇結合後，該受體結合物移動至細胞核，從而調節基因功能。然而，近期也有發現表明維生素D的部分作用非常迅速（從幾秒至幾分鐘不等），由此推論此作用並非基因水準的調節。 在一個項目資金的支持下，我們開展了對維生素D的活性代謝物鈣三醇的非基因水準作用的研究，研究其對雄性高血壓大鼠SHR及正常血壓大鼠WKY的主動脈中的內皮細胞源性反應的作用。鈣三醇對於乙醯膽鹼引導的舒張反應影響不明顯。當用一氧化氮合酶抑制劑阻斷了一氧化氮的產生後，乙醯膽鹼、三磷酸腺苷（ATP）或鈣離子載體A23187增加濃度可觸發內皮細胞源性收縮作用。鈣三醇可顯著抑制乙醯膽鹼或ATP引起的內皮細胞源性收縮作用，但對於A23187的作用不明顯。短期給予鈣三醇可明顯降低由乙醯膽鹼而非A23187引起的類前列腺素（被認為是內皮細胞源性收縮因數）的釋放。從共聚焦顯微鏡下觀察到在血管內皮細胞中，鈣三醇可降低由乙醯膽鹼而非A23187引起的細胞質內游離鈣離子濃度的增加。通過免疫組織化學的方法可觀察到維生素D受體主要分佈于內皮細胞。關於鈣三醇短期體外給藥對於降低細胞源性收縮因數的良性效果的報導已經發表。鈣三醇在體長期給藥的前期試驗結果表明，經過六星期長期給藥後，鈣三醇可減低SHR主動脈中內皮細胞源性收縮因數的產生，但不改變細胞質中鈣離子濃度。 對於調節高血壓大鼠的內皮細胞功能，特別是調節內皮細胞源性收縮因數的產生，維生素D的作用非常顯著。本課題主要目的為繼續研究維生素D對於高血壓中血管內皮細胞功能異常的保護作用，特別是維生素D在血管作用（對鈣離子通道的作用）的信號通道及作用機制。我們會研究長期給予維生素D對高血壓大鼠SHR及正常血壓大鼠WKY在血壓及血管功能方面的作用，並研究鈣三醇對血管內皮細胞功能異常的保護作用是否存在性別差異。因此雄性及雌性SHR作為主要試驗對象，並以WKY作為正常對照。

774610.label: Realisation of objectives
774610.value: In order to examine whether or not calcitriol produced beneficial vascular actions in hypertension, endothelium-dependent relaxations and contractions were examined, using organ chamber technique, in aorta of spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) and the normotensive counterparts, Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rats. As part of our objectives was to identify whether or not there are differences between the acute and chronic vascular effects of calcitriol, experiments were conducted on aortae incubated with calcitriol acutely (30 minutes) and those isolated from SHR treated with vitamin D chronically (for 6 weeks, by means of mini-osmotic pump implanted subcutaneously in the rat), in the absence and presence of different pharmacological inhibitors. The findings indicate that both acute and chronic administrations of calcitriol inhibit endothelium-dependent contractions in SHR aorta (a characteristic of endothelial dysfunction). Furthermore, biochemical assays including Western immunoblotting and enzyme immunoassay and confocal microscopy were performed to determine the site of actions of calcitriol. Plasma level of calcitriol in SHR following chronic administration was also measured and was compared with that found in human to determine the relevance of the doses used in the chronic study. The antihypertensive potential of calcitriol was also investigated by measuring the blood pressure of SHR treated with calcitriol or its vehicle for six weeks. As our finding suggests that calcitriol did not affect capacitative calcium entry and the activity of iPLA2 (in Objective 1), we proceeded instead to examine the role of PKC in the inhibitory effect of calcitriol on EDCF production (please refer to item 4 in Section 6.1). During our studies for Objectives 2 and 3, there is a shortage of supply of SHR, and so some of the mRNA and protein expressions were not measured as proposed in Objective 2, and the responses to endothelium-independent vasoactive agents were not studied (but the vascular responses were studied in arteries with and without endothelium) in Objective 3. Therefore, we are confident that the omission of these experiments would not affect the outcome of our study. After establishing the mechanisms of the vascular effects of calcitriol, experiments were conducted to study whether or not the vascular effects of calcitriol were affected by gender. As such, aortic rings of male SHR were incubated with the major female sex hormone, 17β-estradiol. The data did not suggest that the beneficial vascular effect of calcitriol in hypertensive animals were affected by the female sex hormone.

774610.label: Major findings and research outcome
774610.value: The major findings from the present study are 1. The major active metabolite of vitamin D, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (also known as calcitriol), significantly reduced endothelium-dependent contractions to acetylcholine in the aorta of male spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) of age 36-40 week old. This finding suggests that supplementation of vitamin D may help to alleviate endothelial dysfunction that is associated with hypertension and that contributes to vascular complications in this pathological condition. 2. As calcitriol produces this vascular effect acutely (30 minutes incubation in the organ chamber), its effect unlikely involves the modulation of gene expression that is typical of a classic nuclear vitamin D receptor. 3. Previous studies have indicated that acetylcholine induced endothelium-dependent contractions through activation of cyclooxygenase and the resultant release of prostanoids, mainly prostacyclin, acting on thromboxane-prostanoid (TP) receptors is responsible for the endothelium-dependent contraction. The present data indicate that acetylcholine-induced release of prostacyclin was reduced by the acute administration (30 minutes) of calcitriol. Exposure to calcitriol reduced the increase in cytosolic free calcium concentration caused by acetylcholine in the endothelial cells as determined by confocal microscopy. Therefore, calcitriol likely affects the intracellular concentration of calcium thereby reducing the release of endothelium-derived contracting factor (prostacyclin). 4. The inhibitory effect of calcitriol on endothelium-dependent contractions in SHR aorta was mimicked by protein kinase C (PKC) inhibitor, GF 109203X (5 μM). Moreover, in SHR aorta incubated with GF 10203X, calcitriol no longer inhibited endothelium-dependent contractions to acetylcholine. Therefore, our finding suggests that calcitriol inhibits PKC to suppress the production of endothelium-derived contracting factor (prostacyclin). 5. Chronic treatment with calcitriol (6 weeks delivered by Alzet® mini-osmotic pump, 1.25  10-4 g/ml or its vehicle at 0.15 µl/hr, starting at an age of 36 weeks) reduced arterial blood pressure in SHR but not in its normotensive counterparts, Wistar Kyoto rats (WKY). Using enzyme immunoassay, it was found that the plasma level of calcitriol following the chronic treatment increased by two-fold in both SHR and WKY rats (control versus calcitriol treatment: 20.9 ± 1.3 versus 54.9 ± 11.7 pg/ml in SHR and 23.8 ± 2.3 versus 48.4 ± 9.8 pg/ml in WKY). In aorta isolated from SHR treated with calcitriol for six weeks, endothelium-dependent contractions to acetylcholine were reduced, but endothelium-independent contractions to TP receptor agonist, U46619, were not different from SHR without calcitriol treatment. Unlike with acute treatment, the increases in cytosolic free calcium concentration caused by acetylcholine in the endothelial cells were not different between SHR treated with and without calcitriol. On the other hand, the reduced endothelium-dependent contractions were associated with reduced mRNA and protein expressions of cyclooxygenase-1, but not of prostacyclin or thromboxane synthases. Together with the findings from the acute study, it appears that the genomic and non-genomic mechanisms of the vascular effects of calcitriol in hypertensive animals are different. 6. Chronic treatment with calcitriol also reduced the level of reactive oxygen species in arotic endothelial cells, as determined by confocal microscopy. Therefore, the reduced endothelial dysfunction in SHR by chronic calcitriol treatment is likely mediated by reduced oxidative stress. 7. Physiological concentration (1 nM) of 17β-estradiol did not affect the vascular effect of calcitriol in SHR aorta.

774610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774610.value: The findings from the present study suggest that vitamin D produces both genomic (reduction of cyclooxygenase-1 protein expression) and non-genomic (reduction in the agonist-induced increases in intracellular calcium concentration and inhibition of protein kinase C) to inhibit endothelium-dependent contractions in SHR aortae. While the mechanism through which vitamin D produces beneficial vascular effect in hypertension has been studied in the present study, whether or not the vascular effects of calcitriol are the same in male and female remains to be examined. Therefore, function studies with organ chamber techniques and/or biochemical assays with immunoassays [as reported in the present study] can be utilized to examine the vascular effects of calcitriol in female SHR, and of male SHR in the presence of female sex hormones. The role of classical vitamin D receptors in the vascular effects of calcitriol shown in the present study can be further investigated, e.g. by examining whether or not calcitriol induces the translocation of vitamin D receptor from nucleus to plasma membrane for its acute vascular effects. Moreover, the effects of other vitamin D analogues, for example inecalcitol, on endothelium-dependent contractions in SHR aorta will be investigated. A paper will be prepared for submission for publication after we have a chance to finalize some of the data and complete the analysis of the results.

774610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774610.value: It is now recognized that responses to vitamin D can be very rapid (seconds to minutes) and do not involve genomic modulation. Therefore, the present studies explore both the acute (non-genomic) and chronic (genomic) effect(s) of vitamin D on endothelial dysfunction in hypertension, using spontaneously hypertensive rat as the experimental model of essential hypertension. Our data suggests that both acute and chronic administration of the active metabolite of vitamin D, calcitriol, reduces endothelium-dependent contractions (a characteristic of endothelial dysfunction in SHR aorta). While this effect is due to reduced release of endothelium-dependent contracting factor, the mechanisms underlying this effect are different between acute and chronic treatment, with the former being non-genomic while the latter involving modification of protein expression. Moreover, chronic administration of calcitriol also results in reduced oxidative stress, and reduces the blood pressure in SHR. As such, calcitriol may be used as a health supplement not only for vascular protection, but also for blood pressure control.

774710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
774710.value: Schizophrenia is a neurodevelopmental disorder manifest by early adulthood. This proposal addresses 2 critical questions : i) what predicts onset of schizophrenia in an ‘at-risk’ group, and ii) how might it be prevented? The initial neurodevelopmental insult in schizophrenia is probably during fetal life, long before clinical presentation. We have shown significant brain structural changes in brain already apparent at first presentation, indicating prior maldevelopment. Establishing early diagnostic markers is crucial because long duration of untreated illness worsens outcome. However, not all people at risk go on to develop the disorder and unnecessary antipsychotic drug treatment carries potentially serious side-effects. In order to establish brain markers predictive of schizophrenia we plan to “compress” its protracted time course in an innovative prospective study in rodents. One rodent year is equivalent to almost the full human life span, making longitudinal follow-up during the clinically ‘silent’ period of schizophrenia practical in a rodent model. The objective is to identify brain markers predicting full-blown disease using MRI and to test potential prevention strategies in the maternal immune activation (MIA) mouse model of schizophrenia. The MIA model of schizophrenia is based on convincing evidence that exposure to immune challenge during prenatal life, which increases inflammatory cytokines especially interleukin (IL)6, also increases risk of schizophrenia. Indeed, chronic immune system deregulation is a consistent feature of schizophrenia. We and others have shown the MIA model closely simulates the neuranatomical, neurochemical and behavioural features of schizophrenia and follows a very similar trajectory to man, with impairments not fully evident until adulthood. Recent advances in small animal in-vivo MRI afford a unique opportunity to repeatedly examine detailed longitudinal changes in brain anatomy. We have developed methodology to analyse grey matter, white matter and CSF across each volume-element (voxel) of whole brain in the living mouse. This can be applied to compare model mice to controls in adolescence, prior to full expression of phenotype, and again during adulthood. Given the pivotal role of inflammation in pathophysiology of schizophrenia, we propose an experimental investigation of complementary anti-inflammatory treatment in the MIA model. (n-3) polyunsaturated fatty-acids (PUFA) have robust anti-inflammatory action, inhibit production of IL6, and may be beneficial in schizophrenia. PUFA during pregnancy may generally benefit child development. Therefore we will examine whether PUFA supplementation during either adolescence or prenatal life, attenuates development of schizophrenia-like brain phenotype in the MIA mouse model.

774710.label: Major findings and research outcome
774710.value: 1. Maternal immune activation (MIA) in the mouse causes an overall reduced average genome-wide level of hypomethylation in the hypothalamus. 2. MIA in the mouse causes hypomethylation of the MECP2 gene promoter region in the hypothalamus. The MECP2 gene was previously associated with schizophrenia in a genome-wide association study. 3. The above effects were more prominent in female animals 4. Lists of MIA exposure induced hyper-methylated and hypo-methylated genes were obtained by reduced-representation bisuphite sequencing. 5. Genes involved in symaptic plasticity were enriched in these gene lists. 6. In over 80% of the genes, change in methylation in response to MIA exposure was stabilized by dietary omega-3 supplementation. 7. MIA expsosure in mouse also causes altered brain biochemistry as measured by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), as well as behavioural changes. 8. These MRS and behavioral changes are stabilized by dietary omega-3 supplementation

774710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774710.value: The results support the promise of the MIA in the mouse as a model system to system the aetiology and mechanisms of neurodevelopmental disorders such as schizophrenia. In particular, we demonstrated that epigenetic changes in the form of altered DNA methylation may play a crucial role in mediating the effects of immune activation. Remarkably we were able to show that dietary omega-3 supplementation may offer protection to some of the effects of MIA exposure. Further research is underway to study the downstream mechanims of the MIA model, by transcriptome sequencing of MIA-exposed fetal mice.

774710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774710.value: Because of the ethical and practical difficulties in accessing studying human brains, this study uses a mouse model of neurodevelopmental disorders to study diseases mechanisms processes. This mouse model involves the activation of the immune system of a pregnant animal, which has been shown in previous studies to produce behavioral and brain structural changes similar to those of patients with schizophrenia and autism. In this project, we have further shown that the adult brains of animals exposed to immune activation in the uterus had altered DNA methylation, which can potentially change the pattern of gene expression and therefore neuronal function and development. Remarkable, we found that most of these changes were stablized by increasing the amount of omega-3 fatty acids in the diets of the mouse during development. Finally, we showed that brain biochemical and behavioral changes in the immune-activation exposed mice were also stablized by omega-3 dietary enrichment. These findings point to changes in DNA methylation as a possible mechanism that leads abnormal brain development, and suggest the potential benefits of childhood omega-3 supplementation in preventing this processes.

775110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775110.value: 肝癌（肝細胞癌，HCC）是世界範圍內的主要惡性腫瘤，亦是第二種最常見於東南亞、中國內地和香港，由廣範流行的B型肝炎病毒感染而引起的致命癌症。儘管對於肝癌病人的治療方法及效果已經有了長足的進步，但總體而言，由於較晚發現癌症以及頻繁的術後復發，肝癌的預後仍欠滿意。人們期待已久肝癌的新輔助療法。在這方面，有關肝癌的發生、發展潛在的細胞和分子靶點的研究是非常重要，因為這方面的知識可以為肝癌的干預治療提供新發展。從我們對肝癌缺失基因1和2（DLC1 和 DLC2）以及肝癌 tensin2 在內的粘附蛋白基因的長期研究中，我們發現cten可以通過一種不依賴於磷酸酪氨酸結合（PTB）區域的方式與 DLC1 相結合。此外，根據我們的初步結果表明，相對於非腫瘤性肝癌，cten在肝癌中的表達通常為上調狀態，亦在高轉移性肝癌細胞株中的表達水平也較原發性肝癌組織或低轉移性肝癌細胞株中為低。過度表達 cten 也大大提高了肝癌細胞的轉移能力和侵襲性。Cten 在肝癌中表達上調表明其在肝癌中的失調和肝癌的形成以及轉移有關。然而，有關 cten 在肝癌中的表達譜圖，致瘤潛力以及功能特徵的信息卻很少甚至沒有。在這項研究計劃裏，我們將確立 cten 在肝癌中的作用以及其發揮自身作用的分子通路。我們計劃 1）評估 cten 在人類肝癌樣品及肝癌細胞中的基因表達譜、基因變異及臨床意義; 2）從體內和體外兩方面來表征 cten 肝癌中的致瘤性; 3）從體內和體外兩方面來表証 cten 在肝癌中增強癌癥轉移的能力; 以及 4）描繪 cten 在肝癌中參與的細胞信號通路。我們對肝癌中 cten 功能作用的表証是原創性的，並會對肝癌的發病機理提供新的見解。鑒於肝癌對於香港的重要性以及我們研究團隊現有的實力，我們的研究很可能會為建立肝癌治療的新策略以及有效的治療方法提供更深入的見解。

775110.label: Realisation of objectives
775110.value: We have comprehensively addressed the proposed objectives by performing the following experiments. We have documented the Tensin4 expression in both HCC cell line and human clinical samples by means of real time qPCR, immunoblotting and immunohistochemistry. Our study provided good evidence that Tensin4 is overexpressed in human HCCs (see attached manuscript). We linked up Tensin4 with HCC growth and potentially metastatic functions by showing tight regulation under the MAPK pathways, its intrinsic localization control to focal adhesions, and its potential role in triggering actin cytoskeleton remodeling and controlling cell shape (see manuscript). Our data clearly demonstrated the signaling requirement of ERK kinase activation in Tensin4 expression by mitogen stimulation. We established stable Tensin4 knockdown HCC cell model to demonstrate its pro-oncogenic role in supporting cell growth and mitogen-induced cell migration (see manuscript). The role of Tensin4 is well associated with cell migration. Besides mitogen-induced cell migration, Tensin4 knockdown cells also showed reduced cell migration rate in serum-induced migration in SMMC and BEL7402 cells (data not included in manuscript). We have demonstrated that transiently overexpressed Tensin4 can stimulate cell invasion in PLC cells. In vivo cell model demonstrating the role of Tensin4 in HCC metastasis was limited. Our laboratory utilizes orthotopic liver implantation/injection mouse model to illustrate the ability of implanted HCC cells to metastasize e.g. to the lungs. Unfortunately, the cell line models with Tensin4 knockdown in our study were not able to form primary tumor in the liver when directly implanted into the liver, making subsequent tracing of lung metastasis not possible. On the other hand, the generation of Tensin4-overexpressing model can serve to complement our loss-of-function data. We tried but it was technically challenging to generate Tensin4-overexpressing models in different HCC cell lines. In BEL7402 cells with relatively low Tensin4 expression, by classical chemical transfection followed by antibiotics selection, we were able to obtain several individual stable clones with Tensin4 overexpression but at a low successfully rate. However, preliminary functional assay using these overexpressing clones showed consistent results when compared with the migratory ability among the clones (data not included in manuscript). To minimize the potential artifacts due to clonal effects, we had also tried to utilize retroviral based Tensin4 transduction. However, so far, this approach is not successful. To our knowledge, report of the establishment Tensin4 overexpressing stable cell or animal model is rare; probably this approach is not favorable relating to the intrinsic biological properties of Tensin4.

775110.label: Major findings and research outcome
775110.value: The focal adhesion protein Tensin4, also known as cten (c-terminal tensin like), is structurally distinct from the three other members in the Tensin family. Its expression and potential functions in cancers including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are not well understood. With immunohistochemistry, 43% (10/30) of our human HCC cases showed up-regulation of Tensin4 as compared with their non-tumorous livers. In HCC cells, treatment with epidermal growth factor (EGF) significantly induced Tensin4 protein expression, while treatment with pharmacological inhibitors against the kinases in the MAPK signaling cascade abolished such induction, suggesting that Tensin4 expression was dependent on Ras/MAPK signaling. With immunofluorescence microscopy, the focal adhesion localization of Tensin4 was confirmed in HCC cells. Significantly, detailed examination using a panel of Tensin4 deletion constructs revealed the requirement of the N-terminal region and, to a much less extent, the C-terminal SH2 and PTB domains for this specific localization. Up-regulating of ERK signaling by EGF also resulted in a change of the HCC cells to a mesenchymal cell-like morphology through modulation of the actin cytoskeleton. Functionally, stable Tensin4 knockdown in SMMC cells, which had a high basal expression of Tensin4, resulted in reduced cell proliferation and migration in vitro. Taken together, our data suggest that Tensin4 may play a pro-oncogenic role in HCC, possibly functioning as a downstream effector of Ras/MAPK signaling.

775110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775110.value: In this study, we found that Tensin4 was a downstream target of the Ras/MAPK signaling. It plays pro-oncogenic role in promoting HCC cell migration and is responsive to mitogen stimulation. The data generated by HCC cell lines are encouraging. To further confirm the functional significance of Tensin4 in HCC cells, the use of model resembling the clinical HCC would be highly relevant. Recently, a number of patient-derived HCC xenograft model (PTDX) in immunodeficient mice are under development in our laboratory. It would be interesting to investigate and explore Tensin4 expression and MAPK activation in these HCC xenograft models. By stratifying the HCC PTDX model with or without Tensin4 overexpression, it would provide a useful model for comparing their drug sensitivity towards e.g. Sorafenib or other potential kinase inhibitors, which has been shown to prolong HCC patient survival by blocking kinase activity including the upstream Raf kinase in the MAPK signaling cascade. Tensin4 expression may serve as a prognostic marker to predict the kinase activation in the MAPK signaling and predict the HCC cell sensitivity to kinase inhibitor treatment.
