775510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775510.value: The first cell differentiation event in mammalian embryo development is the formation of trophoectoderm (TE) and inner cell mass (ICM). It is now clear that the diversity of cell differentiation and the corresponding gene expression pattern is mediated by means of epigenetic mechanisms, such as DNA methylation and covalent histone modifications. With a global comparison of promoter DNA methylation patterns between mouse embryonic stem (mES) cell and mouse trophoblast stem (mTS) cell, we have identified a transcription factor, Elf5, which regulates the determination of trophoblast cell fate through its DNA methylation status. However, the mechanism which directs the set up of differential Elf5 methylation in embryonic precursor cells remains to be elucidated. Recent studies demonstrated that both H3K9 methylation and DNA methylation can be established at the same loci by a repressor protein complex. Although the role of H3K9 methylation in ICM and TE lineage specification is largely unknown, we hypothesize that H3K9 methylation can mediate DNA methylation at Elf5 promoter in ICM precursor cells of early blastocysts, hence proposing that H3K9 methylation also plays a role in trophoblast determination and interacts with other mechanisms of epigenetic regulation. In addition, we aim to study the role of a recently identified histone H3K9 demethylase Jmjd2 family in the differentiation of mES cell to trophoblast lineages. Studying the crucial Jmjd2 member using our established mES cell differentiation system thus enables us to unveil the details of epigenetic mechanism as well as identify novel lineage determination genes in trophoblast development. On the other hand, the conserved epigenetic regulations of trophoblast development in mouse embryo provides a novel approach in understanding the determination of human trophoblast and hence facilitates the derivation of human TS cell line, which can serve as an excellent model to study human pregnancy disorders, such as pre-eclampsia and fetal intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR). Taken together, studies on the epigenetic regulation in trophoblast differentiation can provide valuable information on the formation of the placenta, which is crucial for the survival and normal development of an embryo. This study therefore sheds light on the mammalian developmental strategy and ultimately helps in understanding the proper development of human embryos. 在哺乳動物的胚胎發育中，最早的細胞分化發生在滋養層和內細胞團的形成過程中。現在的研究已經清楚地揭示了不同的細胞分化過程和其相應的基因表達模式是通過表觀遺傳的機制來調控的，例如：DNA 的甲基化和組蛋白的共價修飾。通過對小鼠胚胎幹細胞和滋養層幹細胞 啟動子DNA甲基化的全局比對分析，我們發現一個叫做Elf5的轉錄因子基因。通過調節這個基因的DNA甲基化水平可以決定滋養層細胞的命運。然而目前還不清楚在胚胎前體細胞中Elf5甲基化水平是通過何種機制來調節的。最近的研究證實，通過一種阻抑蛋白複合體可以同時對同一基因位點進行組蛋白H3K9和DNA的甲基化。儘管組蛋白H3K9甲基化在內細胞團和滋養層譜系分化中的作用還不是很清楚，但是我們推測早期胚泡中的內細胞團前體細胞是通過對Elf5位點組蛋白H3K9的甲基化來誘導其對啟動子DNA甲基化的。因此我們也認為組蛋白H3K9的甲基化在滋養層細胞決定中發揮重要功能並且與其他表觀遺傳機制有相互作用。此外，我們也致力於研究一個最近新發現的組蛋白H3K9去甲基化酶家族Jmjd2在小鼠胚胎幹細胞分化成滋養層細胞過程中的作用。通過我們建立的小鼠胚胎幹細胞分化系統來研究Jmjd2家族中的重要蛋白可以令我們更深入的瞭解表觀遺傳的具體機制並且有機會發現決定滋養層細胞發育的關鍵基因。另一方面，通過研究影響小鼠胚胎滋養層發育的表觀遺傳機制可以為我們提供一個全新的角度來瞭解人類滋養層的發育，而且有助於我們誘導分離人類滋養層細胞系。分離得到的人類滋養層細胞系是研究諸如先兆子癇和宮內遲緩發育癥等人類妊娠疾病絕佳模型。綜上所述，對滋養層分化過程中表觀遺傳調節機制的研究可以為我們提供胎盤形成的重要信息。這些信息對胚胎的生長發育至關重要。因此這項研究將更加清晰地揭示哺乳動物的發育模式並且最終有助於我們瞭解人類的胚胎發育。

775710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775710.value: Hirschsprung (HSCR) disease is attributed to a failure of the enteric neural crest cells (NCCs) to form enteric ganglia in the hindgut. Aside from proper migration and proliferation, development of the enteric nervous system (ENS) also relies on the synchronization and balance of neurogenesis and gliogenesis of NCCs. Imbalance of these processes may lead to premature gliogenesis, resulting in intestinal aganglionosis as seen in HSCR. To date, numerous HSCR genes and pathways have been identified. Nevertheless, how different signaling pathways are integrated to coordinate neuronal and glial differentiation, and whether any of these pathway components are involved in HSCR are yet to be elucidated. Hedgehog and Notch are known signaling pathways implicated in ENS development. We have previously reported that Sonic hedgehog (Shh) maintains the enteric progenitor pool by promoting proliferation of enteric NCCs and inhibiting its neuronal differentiation. Strikingly, our preliminary data showed that constitutive activation of hedgehog signaling by conditional knockout of Patched (Ptch) in enteric NCCs results in hypoganglionosis of the mouse bowel. Furthermore, we showed that the Notch pathway is activated in Ptch-deficient NCCs, which exhibit premature gliogenesis. These results suggest that improper glial cell differentiation during ENS development may lead to HSCR disease. In line with these observations, our genome-wide association study (GWAS) on HSCR demonstrated that the neuregulin-1 gene (NRG1), which modulates gliogenesis, is a susceptibility gene for HSCR disease. Importantly, through epistasis analysis of our GWAS data, we identified a specific allelic distribution of SNPs in the SHH and NOTCH signaling pathway genes in HSCR patients, suggesting that these pathways may contribute to disease development. Nevertheless, the coordination mechanism between the Shh and Notch pathways in ENS development has yet not been fully elucidated. Therefore, we propose to determine how hedgehog signaling causes pre-mature gliogenesis by 1) elucidating the global and spatial effects of the Shh-Notch pathway in balancing the population sizes of the neuronal and glial precursors; 2) delineating the underlying molecular mechanism to help identify the HSCR susceptibility genes; and 3) studying the capacity of Shh-Notch to induce gliogenesis of NCCs in the diseased environment in order to assess their therapeutic potential for improving differentiation capacity of transplanted precursor cells in the diseased bowel. In summary, this work will gain significant insights into human biology as a way to better understand disease states, with the long-term goal of improving treatments. 先天性巨結腸病（HSCR）的病因是在腸壁的自主神經叢缺乏神經節細胞。在正常情況下，發育中的神經節細胞會在腸壁有秩序地擴散及分化，並形成腸神經系統。分化失衡會導致過早產生神經膠質原細胞，因而引致HSCR。迄今為止，HSCR相信是一種多原遺傳性疾病，不少有關基因及信號通路已經確定。然而，這些信號通路是如何整合，協調神經元和膠質原細胞分化，還有待了解。 Sonic Hedgehog和Notch信號通路對腸神經系統的發展非常重要。我們早前已發現，Sonic Hedgehog對維持神經節細胞擴散和抑制其神經元分化尤其重要。引人注目的是，我們的初步數據顯示，條件性敲除鼠腸道Ptch1基因能有效地激活Hedgehog信號，並減少腸道神經節細胞。此研究同時發現，缺少Ptch1 的鼠神經細胞會過度激活Notch信號通路， 並促使神經膠質原細胞過早形成。所以，我們相信，不當的膠質細胞分化可能是引致HSCR的誘因。此外，這些結果跟我們早前對HSCR作出的全基因組關聯研究（GWAS）吻合，顯示其中一種能調節膠質原細胞分化的基因，稱為神經調節蛋白1基因（NRG1），是一個HSCR易感基因。其後數據分析，更確定了HSCR病人帶有特定的SHH及Notch信號通路基因變化，這表明這些信號通路變化可能是HSCR的元兇。可是，對於SHH及Notch信號通路失衡是如何影響腸神經系統發展，我們尚未充分了解。因此，我們建議，用以下方法加深了解Hedgehog信號通路是如何引致經膠質原細胞過早出現：1）SHH及Notch是怎樣平衡神經元和神經膠質前體的規模; 2）劃定引致神經膠質原細胞過早出現的基本分子機制，從而查明HSCR易感性基因; 3）研究SHH及Notch是否能促使已移植於腸道的幹細胞分化成膠質原細胞，籍此評估其治療潛力。總括來說，這項研究工作所取得的成果，會加深我們對人類生物學及HSCR病理的了解，而改進治療方法更是我們的長遠目標。

775710.label: Realisation of objectives
775710.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. Objective 1: We have defined PTCH1 from HH pathway and DLL3 from NOTCH pathway are susceptibility genes for HSCR disease. Aberrant activation of Hh pathway prone NCCs to glial lineage differentiation, leading to reduced progenitor pool size that may result in lack of nerve cells in the colon as observed in HSCR patient. Our study highlights that the premature glial differentiation of enteric NCCs may represent a new disease mechanism for HSCR. 775710.label: Major findings and research outcome
775710.value: Hirschsprung’s (HSCR) disease is a complex genetic disorder attributed to a failure of the enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs) to form ganglia in the hindgut. Hedgehog and Notch are implicated in mediating proliferation and differentiation of ENCCs. Nevertheless, how these signaling molecules may interact to mediate gut colonization by ENCCs and contribute to a primary etiology for HSCR are not known. In this study, we performed a pathway-based epistasis analysis of data generated by a genome-wide association study on Hirschsprung’s disease and demonstrated that specific genotype constellations of Patched (PTCH1) (which encodes a receptor for Hedgehog) and Delta-like 3 (DLL3) (which encodes a receptor for Notch) SNPs confer higher risk to HSCR. Importantly, deletion of Ptch1 in mouse ENCCs induced robust Dll1 expression and activation of the Notch pathway, leading to premature gliogenesis and reduction of ENCC progenitors in mutant bowels. Dll1 integrated Hedgehog and Notch pathways to coordinate neuronal and glial cell differentiation during enteric nervous system development. Moreover, Hedgehog-mediated gliogenesis was found to be highly conserved, such that Hedgehog was consistently able to promote gliogenesis of human neural crest-related precursors (JCI 2011; NeuroSignal 2013, Mol Syndrom 2013, Ip’s MPhil thesis). Subsequently, we also demonstrated that the balance between neurogenesis and gliogenesis is critical for ENS development. When ENCCs were dedicated to glial lineage by Nrg1, the neurogenic propensity of ENCCs was reduced. The neurotropic factor (Gdnf), on the other hand, negatively regulated the expression of Nrg1 receptor (ErbB2) to balance the neurogenesis and gliogenesis of ENCCs (Hum Genet, 2013). In addition to understand the etiology of HSCR, we also established a transplantation model for developing an effective transplantation strategy for HSCR. In particular, we elucidated the therapeutic potential of skin-derived precursor cells (SKPs) and induced pluriopotent stem cells (iPSC) derived NCCs for replenishing absent ganglia in HSCR bowel. We showed that both mouse and human SKPs and human iPSCs retain high differentiation capacities to form enteric neurons, and glia (Exp Cell Research, 2013). Importantly, we also revealed that SKPs and iPSC-NCCs can effectively differentiate into neurons and glia in the Retk/k aganglionic hindgut explants (JPS 2012) and in vivo chick embryos (Kwok’s MPhil thesis), respectively. Collectively, we defined PTCH1 and DLL3 as HSCR susceptibility genes and that aberrant gliogenesis may represent a new disease mechanism for HSCR. We also established two transplantation models for assessing in vivo differentiation potentials of NCCs.

775710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775710.value: In this study, we demonstrated the relevance of Hh pathway in HSCR pathogenesis. We then further elucidate the underlying molecular and cellular events. In particular, we sequenced the three HH effector genes, namely GLI1, GLI2 and GLI3 in HSCR patients who do not carry any RET mutation. Our initial screen revealed several deleterious mutations that residing in the functional domains of GLI protein, suggesting that perturbed HH-GLI signal transduction cascade may contribute to HSCR. Further functional studies will be performed to delineate the roles of GLI in ENS development and HSCR pathogenesis using mouse and human embryonic stem cell models. A GRF research proposal was submitted for consideration of new research funding.

775710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775710.value: Hirschsprung’s (HSCR) disease (congenital megacolon) is a birth defect affecting 1 in 3000 babies in Asia. These babies suffer from severe constipation and intestinal obstruction because nerve cells which co-ordinate bowel movement are absent. The reasons for the absence of nerve cells in the bowel are unclear, and therefore treatment remains unsatisfactory. We have conducted a study that integrates genetics, statistics and bioinformatics with experimental biology to investigate the mechanisms by which a small number of genes interact with each other to cause HSCR disease. With the mouse models, the study identified that specific DNA changes in Patched (PTCH1) and Delta-like 3 (DLL3) genes (genes that work coordinately to control the sequential waves of neural differentiation and formation of the nerve cells in bowel) will lead to premature development of nerve-supporting cells, thus increase the risk of having HSCR by 278%. In addition, we established two transplantation platforms for developing an effective transplant strategy for HSCR. The novel finding provides important breakthrough for understanding the pathology of this genetic disease and pave way to establish cell-based therapy for HSCR disease.

776110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776110.value: Acute respiratory viral infections remain a major cause of morbidity worldwide and of mortality in the developing world. The impact of emerging respiratory viruses such as SARS, avian influenza H5N1 and pandemic H1N1 caused major impact on societies and economies in many countries. The innate immune system is the first line of host defense and is central to a patient’s effort to combat such emerging infections as well as more mundane and common respiratory virus diseases. Toll-like receptors (TLR) are an integral part of this front-line of host defense and they sense the presence of a microbe and activate host defenses to contain such infection. Sometimes they also contribute to disease pathogenesis. Of the 10 human TLRs, the function of TLR10 is still poorly understood. We have preliminary experimental data that suggests that TLR10 is important in the host response to influenza A. We hypothesize that it may be a yet unrecognized but key component of our immune defense against many viruses. It this project, we plan to investigate the role of TLR10 in coronavirus and influenza infections as an initial step in unraveling the role of this receptor in overall host defenses. Such information would provide novel insights into host defense and disease pathogenesis of respiratory infections in particular and virus infections in general. 急性呼吸道病毒感染仍然在全球及發展中國家引起很高的發病及死亡率。新發的呼吸道病毒如SARS，禽流感H5N1和2009 甲型H1N1在許多國家對社會及經濟造成了重大的影響。先天免疫系統是機體防禦的第一個屏障，在病人對抗這些新發性感染及常見的呼吸道病毒疾病中起了重大作用。其中， Toll樣受體（TLR）是這個機體防禦屏障中不可或缺的部份，它們識別微生物並且激活機體防禦以對抗其感染。但，有時它們也在疾病的發病機制中擔演角色。在人的十個Toll樣受體中，我們對Toll樣受體十的功能仍然知之甚少。我們的初步實驗數據表明，Toll樣受體十在機體對抗甲型流感中起了重要的作用。我們推測，它可能是一個未知但重要的對抗病毒感染的機體防禦部份。在這個項目中，我們計劃研究Toll樣受體十在冠狀病毒及流感病毒感染中的角色， 從而作為解開這個受體 在整體機體防禦中的第一步。這些資料將對機體防禦及呼吸道感染疾病的發病機理提供新的見解。

776110.label: Major findings and research outcome
776110.value: TLR10 mRNA and protein were detected in human macrophages and epithelial cells in relatively low expression level. TLR10 protein was predominantly expressed intracellularly with only very little detection on the surface of the intact cells. TLR10 expression was markedly upregulated in response to influenza virus but not to Co-V (SARS Co-V and Co-V 229E) infection. The intensity of TLR10 expression varied among different influenza virus strains (H5N1 > H7N9 > H1N1) and it seems that the extent of TLR10 induction was correlated with the pathogenicity of the viruses. We next investigated whether the expression of cytokines which are typically up-regulated following influenza A virus infection is TLR10-dependent. Compared to non-targeting control small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), TLR10 siRNA knockdown significantly reduced the expression of TLR10 mRNA. H5N1 induced IL8 and IL6 mRNA expression was significantly suppressed in TLR10 siRNA knockdown cells compared to control. TLR10 siRNA treatment also significantly suppressed IFNβ and IL29 mRNA induction. Therefore the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines as well as type I and type III IFNs induced by H5N1 virus infection was, at least partially, mediated via TLR10. In order to understand if dsRNA for activating TLR10, we challenged the TLR10 siRNA knock down cells and controls with poly IC (synthetic analog of viral dsRNA) and LPS (major component of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria) as a control. However no conclusions could be drawn at the moment as challenging cells (both TLR10 siRNA knock down and control non-targeting siRNA transfected cells) using poly IC added to culture medium resulted in only marginal IFN mRNA levels. The low IFN expression level (either with or without poly IC treatment) makes the data impossible to interpret. TLR10 knock down did not affect the expression of the above mentioned cytokines and IFNs tested following LPS challenge. In consideration of our data that TLR10 was predominately expressed intracellularly, we then transfected poly IC directly into the siRNA knock down or control cells. However, the transfection with poly IC led to significant cell death in TLR10 siRNA knock down cells and no conclusions could be drawn. As an alternative to poly IC, we therefore investigated the effect of the whole viral RNP complex (including the vRNA and viral proteins) to determine whether this viral-RNA complex induced cytokine expression was TLR10-dependent. We performed a virus RNP reconstitution assay. Viral RNP complex genes (PB2, PB1, PA and NP) of A/Vietnam/1203/04 (H5N1) virus were transfected into 293T cells to mimic viral replication. A pPOLI-NS-Luc reporter that expresses vRNA-like luciferase RNA was used to monitor the activity of viral polymerases. Human TLR10 expression plasmid was co-transfected into 293T cells to examine the effect of its expression on viral replication. At 20 h post transfection, cytokine expression was only increased by 5 fold in RNP-transfected cells, while its expression was greatly increased in RNP/TLR10-transfected cells. The data suggest that TLR10 substantially enhanced vRNP induced activation of cytokine expression. The viral components that trigger TLR10 activation and cytokine expression could be viral proteins, viral RNA or the whole RNP complex TLR10 and trigger downstream signaling. Further dissection of the relevant ligand is planned in future studies.

776110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776110.value: Up to now, TLR10 has remained an orphan receptor without known agonist or function. Data arising from this study suggested for the first time that TLR10 is a novel innate immune sensor of viral infection and thus opens up a new field in innate immunity. Understanding influenza virus in relationship to their hosts and how this receptor is related to pathogenicity is novel. Further work on ligand identification, signaling and functional study of TLR10 will be extremely important.

776110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776110.value: TLRs play key roles in innate immune recognition of pathogens leading to the activation of innate host defenses and sometimes to immunopathology. In humans, there are ten identified TLR members, designated TLR1-10. Of those, TLR10 remains the only one without a defined ligand or function. We now provide the first evidence that TLR10 plays a role in innate immune responses following influenza viral infection. Compared to seasonal influenza virus H1N1, the highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses H7N9 and H5N1 are a more potent inducer of TLR10 and activator of TLR10 to trigger cytokine expression, suggesting that the differential expression of TLR10 in response to different viruses may be related to disease pathogenicity. Further work including ligand identification, signaling and functional study of TLR10 will be of great importance in order to understand influenza virus in relationships to their hosts and how this receptor related to pathogenicity.

776710.value: DNA甲基化和组蛋白后转移修饰作为表观遗传调控机制的两个主要类别，相互影响，相互协作，通过调节染色质结构，进而影响基因表达。 UHRF1可以作为一个很好的模板在分子水平上来研究DNA甲基化和组蛋白后转移修饰的相互关联： UHRF1上的SRA区域能够识别包含hemimethylated CpG 的DNA，同时UHRF1的 double Tudor 区域能够识别组蛋白H3K9me3，我们最近发现其另一段PHD finger区域能够识别组蛋白H3K4me0。到目前为止UHRF1是第一个已表征的蛋白能同时识别 hemimethylated DNA 和组蛋白H3K4me0K9me3。以前的研究证实UHRF1与DNA甲基酶DNMT1 有直接的结合， 这有助于DNMT1在DNA复制过程中更有效的甲基化其底物hemimethylated DNA，从而保证了DNA甲基化模式在细胞分裂过程中的延续性。 UHRF1还与其他组蛋白修饰酶如G9a，HDAC1等有相互作用，并抑制重要的抗肿瘤基因如 p16INK4A、p14ARF和p21的基因转录，所以在多种癌症UHRF1被检测出过量表达。 尽管近来对于UHRF1的研究进展很快，但仍有很多议题留待阐明。在这个项目我们将结合结构生物学与细胞生物学的手段进一步研究UHRF1的运作机理：(1) 确定UHRF1识别组合表观遗传修饰的分子基础。 (2) 阐释UHRF1与其结合的其它染色质修饰酶的相互作用 。 我们期望我们获得的新的结构信息能够进一步确定UHRF1在基因表达调控以及DNA复制过程中的分子机理， 能够有助我们在更深层次理解不同的表观遗传修饰如何协作共同去调控基因转录，以及染色质修饰酶如何协同特定染色质修饰的识别蛋白去保持表观遗传模式在细胞分裂过程中的一致性

776710.label: Realisation of objectives
776710.value: Human UHRF1 has recently been extensively characterized as a key epigenetic regulator for maintaining DNA methylation patterns. UHRF1 SRA domain preferentially binds to hemimethylated CpG sites, and tandem Tudor domain has been implicated in recognizing H3K9me3 mark, but the role of the adjacent PHD finger was not unclear. Over the funding period, (1) We identified that UHRF1 PHD finger preferentially binds to unmodified histone H3 N-terminal tail. (2) We found the preceding zinc-Cys4 knuckle is indispensable for UHRF1 PHD finger to recognize histone H3 N-terminal tail. This is very unique compared with all of those published PHD fingers. (3) We determined the high-resolution crystal structure of UHRF1 PHD finger (including the preceding zinc-Cys4 knuckle) in complex with N-terminal tail of histone H3. Notably, this interaction is severely impaired by methylation on H3R2, while methylation on H3K4 has less significant effect. (4) Our in vitro binding analyses indicated that UHRF1 tandem Tudor domain (TTD) is required but not sufficient for histone H3K9me3 recognition. In fact UHRF1 PHD finger acts together with the adjacent TTD to specifically recognize the H3K9me3 mark. We further propose a model that combinatorial recognition of H3K9me3-containing histone H3 tail by UHRF1 PHD finger and TTD may play a role in establishing and maintaining both DNA methylation and histone H3K9 methylation patterns during the cell cycle. (5) We explored the interaction between UHRF1 and DNMT1. In contrast to the observations of several recent published literatures, we did not observe the physical interaction between UHRF1 SRA domain and DNMT1 replication focus targeting sequence (RFTS) domain, even though we tried multiple approaches including ITC and NMR titration to detect the possible interaction. (6) A recent study has demonstrated that UHRF1 can specifically ubiquitinate histone H3K23, and DNMT1 RFTS domain has been shown to bind to ubiquitinated H3K23, which promotes DNMT1 association with the chromatin. Interestingly, we found that DNMT1 RFTS domain tightly associate with ubiquitin. The structure-based analysis of the interaction is currently underway. (7) Except the N-terminal ubiquitin-like domain, the function and structure of other UHRF1 individual domain have been extensively explored. In collaboration with Dr. Zhongjun Zhou, we are exploring UHRF1 UBL domain binding protein partner and studying the functional relevance (by generating UHRF1ΔUBL mice).

776710.label: Major findings and research outcome
776710.value: (i) By using fluorescence polarization assay, we identified that UHRF1 PHD finger preferentially binds to unmodified histone H3 N-terminal tail. (ii) We further characterized the functional organization of UHRF1 PHD finger. We found that the zinc-Cys4 knuckle preceding the canonical PHD finger of UHRF1 is required for histone H3 binding. The UHRF1 canonical PHD finger is well-folded, but it does not show any binding to histone H3 peptide, as demonstrated by fluorescence polarization assay, isothermal titration calorimetry and nuclear magnetic resonance titration. This is very unique compared with all of those published PHD fingers from other proteins. (iii) We determined the crystal structure of UHRF1 atypical PHD finger in complex with histone H3 N-terminal 7-amino-acid peptide at 1.95Å resolution. Interestingly, the side chain of histone H3 Arg2 (H3R2) forms an extensive hydrogen bonds network with UHRF1 PHD finger, implying that histone binding may be sensitive to H3R2 methylation. This is further supported by mutagenesis analyses. (iv) By using isothermal titration calorimetry and NMR titration, we observed that PHD finger is required for UHRF1 tandem Tudor domain to specifically recognize histone H3K9me3 mark. UHRF1 tandem Tudor domain is required but not sufficient for H3K9me3 binding. (v) We proposed a model of UHRF1-mediated propagation of DNA methylation and histone H3K9me3 during cell division (Xie S et al. JMB 2012). The model is consistent with the results from several more recent cell-based studies. (vi) UHRF1 serves as an E3 ubiquitin ligase to target histone H3K23, and DNMT1 RFTS domain has been shown to bind to ubiquitinated H3K23 that helps DNMT1 associate with the chromatin. We provided strong evidence that DNMT1 replication focus targeting sequence (RFTS) domain binds tightly to ubiquitin. The structural analysis is underway(Li T et al. Manuscript in preparation). (vii) To investigate the interaction of UHRF1 with associating chromatin modifying enzymes, we first cloned DNMT1 fragments including replication focus targeting sequence (RFTS) domain and the catalytic domain, we further applied isothermal titration carorimetry and nuclear magnetic resonance titration to monitor the binding between UHRF1 SRA domain and DNMT1 which has been observed by several cell biology groups, while we did not observe obvious interaction between UHRF1 SRA domain and DNMT1 in vitro.

776710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776710.value: Based on a recent finding that UHRF1 can ubiquitinate histone H3K23, H3K23 ubiquitination further promotes DNMT1 association with the chromatin. We have verified that DNMT1 fragments including RFTS domain binds strongly to ubiquitin in vitro. The structure-based analysis of this interaction is underway. We speculate that the interaction not only promotes DNMT1 association with chromatin, but also stimulates DNMT1 enzymatic activity, because several lines of evidence indicate that DNMT1 RFTS domain naturally inhibits its enzymatic activity by blocking DNA from accessing to DNMT1 enzymatic active site, probably DNMT1 requires other binding proteins to release the inhibitory RFTS domain from the active site and allow DNA binding. Currently the exact function of UHRF1 N-terminal ubiquitin-like domain (UBL) remains elusive. Recent extensive studies on many other UBL domains strongly imply that UHRF1 UBL domain modulate UHRF1 interaction with other proteins. In collaboration with my colleague Dr. Zhongjun Zhou, we are using TAP and mass spectrometry to fish out proteins that may have direct interaction with UHRF1 UBL domain. At the same time, we are generating UHRF1ΔUBL mice to examine the phenotype caused by this domain deletion.

776710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776710.value: The regulation and transduction of genetic information of the human genome is governed not only by the information encoded in the DNA sequence, but also by the epigenetic information that is heritable through cell divisions. Accumulating evidence shows that DNA methylation and histone post-translational modifications play an important role in controlling of the capacity of the human genome to store, release and inherit biological information. However, the interplay between these two epigenetic alternations in mammals is yet to be fully understood. Human protein UHRF1 plays a critical role in maintaining DNA methylation patterns during cell division. As we know now, global DNA hypomethylation is a hallmark of human cancer cells. UHRF1 has also been shown to cooperate with other chromatin enzymes to regulate gene expression of several tumor suppressors such as p16INK4A, p14ARF and p21. It is not surprising that UHRF1 has been found to be over-expressed in many different forms of human cancers, including breast, cervical, prostate and bladder cancer. Our proposed studies should gain new structural insights into UHRF1-mediated epigenetic crosstalk and transcriptional regulation, and provide a platform for the development of highly selective therapeutic agents that enable investigation of biological functions of UHRF1 under physiological conditions.

776810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776810.value: 背景 二零零九年H1N1甲型流感病毒已蔓延全球,這很可能是大流行病毒品種已取代以前的H1N1病毒與 H3N2病毒。 第一波之大流行比初時預期小，有大部人都有沒有受感染。因此我們還未清楚未來的感染力度及疾病對醫療系統帶來多少的負擔。 這研究讓我們有機會了解年和年之間甲型流感傳播動力。二零零九年八月我們於基線調查獲得約一千名香港市民血清， 其中百分之九十五之血清於流感蔓延開始之前收集到的。我們相信不容易在其他地方有這樣一套有代表性的基線血清收集。 二零零九年十一月，我們會就此受資項目作跟進調查。我們期待這兩個血清配對能準確地提供流行病學的大流行的描述。 當前的建議的主旨 從原有的參與者作多三輪的血清收集，若有參與者不再參與 ，我們會再找新的參與者作替代 ，並增加這個項目的參與人數。 設計和對象 我們使用隨機撥號招募大部分參與者，額外的家庭將以同樣的方式作招募，其中至少一名成員會被邀請參與被要求提供血清樣本。 家庭所有成員需填寫症狀記錄冊。我們建議將分開三次血清收集(時期為二零一一年一月，二零一一年十一月及二零一二年十一月)。期間，研究對象及家庭成員將持症狀記錄冊和生病時報告流感症狀。我們的醫生將免費提供諮詢或進行家訪，並會安排收集鼻子和咽喉拭子，從而得到其鼻水及口水樣本。 研究工具 一個四倍或更大的病毒中和檢測將被視為一個指標去檢視參與者於研究期間對某類病毒之暴露。我們將所有的血清樣本對本地流行的三個流感病毒品種作測試。在二零一年（已受資之第二輪項目），二零一一年和二零一二年，參與者和家庭成員將被要求保留症狀記錄冊，並於生病時讓我們收集其鼻子和咽喉的鼻水及口水樣本，從而去確認是否實驗室確診感染流感。血清測試結果將與臨床和實驗室確診的流感個案作比較。利用簡單年齡結構我們更能特顯按年傳播動力 主要的研究的結果 血清確診流感感染對象之比例-這比例讓我們準確地估計每年不同年齡流感染住院率和死亡率。 分析 我們將估計年齡發病率和症狀發病率並使用簡單的數學模型來估計有效再生數及之前受感染個體的相對感受性易係數。

Serological detection of infections with (H1N1)pdm09 and H3N2 were conducted by haemagglutination inhibition assays on the sera collected during the first two rounds, and the testing results of the last round are pending and should be available shortly. 776810.label: Major findings and research outcome
776810.value: Our most important findings related to the incidence and severity of H1N1pdm09 compared to H3N2 are as follows *Incidence* During the period that included three influenza virus epidemics between 2009 and 2011, there was a change in age distribution of infections with A(H1N1)pdm09 across two separate epidemics, with a similar age pattern of infections in the second wave of A(H1N1)pdm and the epidemic of A(H3N2) that occurred between the two waves of H1N1pdm09. Interestingly, despite a very high incidence of infection in children in 2009, the A(H1N1)pdm09 virus returned within a year to cause a second epidemic with substantial impact, implying that herd immunity among children may not be sufficient to prevent large epidemics. This has particular relevance for the assessment of the potential cost-effectiveness of vaccinating children against influenza. *Severity* The ‘severity’ of influenza virus infection can be defined as the risk of more serious disease, or death, conditional on infection. There is no single best measure of severity, but we have recently proposed the “infection fatality risk” as a good measure of severity – the IFR is defined as the risk of death for a person who is infected with influenza virus (Wong et al. 2013 Am J Epidemiol). The IFR can be compared for different influenza types/subtypes and strains. To our knowledge, there is no previous estimate of the IFR of H3N2, and only a small number of published estimates of the IFR of H1N1pdm09 (Wong et al. 2013 Epidemiol). In the present study, we estimated that the IFR of H3N2 was around 2 times higher than H1N1pdm09, which is a novel and extremely valuable finding. In addition we estimated that H3N2 infections were twice as likely as H1N1 infections to require medical attention. It is well- known that H3N2 epidemics have had greater impact than H1N1 epidemics in the preceding 10 years (Wu et al. 2012 J Infect Dis), but it has not been clear whether this greater impact was due to greater incidence (i.e. more infections) versus greater severity. Our results demonstrate that greater impact of H3N2 is likely to be due to greater severity, while we found similar incidence in the post-pandemic H3N2 and H1N1pdm09 epidemics during our study period. Please also see part (C)

776810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776810.value: The present funded project has now finished, but there are areas with potential for further development of the research: 1. We have received further funding from another source to extend our serological study through to February 2015. We will expand our study estimate the age specific attack rates of influenza A and B in a representative group of households using three sets of paired serology between November 2012 and February 2015. 2. We will continue to analyze the data collected as part of this study, using a mathematical model to estimate the attack rates across the entire population allowing for household structure (the present analysis does not take household structure into account although this is unlikely to have a major effect on the results). The mathematical model will also allow us to estimate and characterize the underlying transmission dynamics of influenza. 3. We will to analyze the data collected as part of this study to evaluate the risk factors of infections for influenza virus infection including age, vaccination status and geographic location.

776810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776810.value: It is not known how many people are infected with influenza virus every year, although it is known that the burden of influenza is considerable. In this study we were able to estimate that 19% of the population were infected with the new H1N1 virus during the first wave of the pandemic in 2009-10, including approximately 50% of school-age children, and the same virus caused another epidemic in 2011 infecting 16% of the population. In an H3N2 epidemic in late 2010, 7% of the population were infected. However, a greater number of deaths associated with influenza occurred during the H3N2 epidemic, and we estimated that H3N2 infections were twice as likely to lead to death (and twice as likely to require medical attention) compared to H1N1 infections. This is the first estimate of the comparative severity of H3N2 compared to H1N1. Our results can be further used to estimate the dynamics of influenza transmission, and thereby to inform potential policies for control such as increasing the coverage of influenza vaccination

777210.label: Project Objectives
777210.value: To reconstruct multiple parallel phylogenies of Annonaceae lineages that show African-Asian disjunctions, using maximum parsimony (MP), maximum likelihood (ML) and Bayesian inference (BI) methods. To determine ancestral geographical areas at internal nodes in the phylogenies (and hence the direction of African-Asian migration events) using dispersal-vicariance analysis based on the results of Bayesian phylogenetic analysis. To estimate the dates of the migration events in different lineages using uncorrelated lognormal distributed relaxed clock (UCLD) methods, as implemented in the program BEAST. To correlate the age of the migration events with geological and palaeoclimatic data, and hence identify parallel migrations in different lineages that are likely to be correlated with common geological and climatic events. To assess the various alternative migration routes that have been postulated, and identify which migration route is most probable during specific geological periods. To develop bioclimatic models that can be interpreted phylogenetically to determine whether climate preferences are conservative over phylogenetic timescales, thereby giving an insight into current and potential future changes in distribution, speciation and extinction associated with global warming.

777210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777210.value: Research into the evolutionary diversification of flowering plants is greatly facilitated by the study of early-diverging lineages as this enables the ancestral condition of features to be inferred. The basal angiosperm family Annonaceae is of particular importance due to its large size, broad geographical distribution and comparative morphological specialization. Considerable advances have been made in recent years to reconstruct the phylogeny of the Annonaceae and a broad consensus of the topology has now been reached, although many clades remain inadequately sampled or poorly resolved. The discovery of the sequence of past migration and dispersal events is an integral component of our broader understanding of evolutionary patterns and processes. Historical biogeographical research has undergone a revolution over the past two decades with the development of new analytical techniques and the availability of new data. Although several studies of the biogeography of the Annonaceae have previously been undertaken, many important questions remain unresolved. The availability of revised tectonic, palaeogeographic and plaeoclimatic models, new fossil calibration points, new methodologies for estimating divergence times, and a broader range of taxa that have been sequenced, collectively presents an ideal opportunity for reassessing current knowledge of the biogeography of the family. This study focuses on African-Asian biogeographical connections in the Annonaceae, with the aim of using the family as a paradigm for not only other basal angiosperms but also other components of palaeotropical lowland forest ecosystems. The phylogenies of selected lineages that show African-Asian disjunctions will be reconstructed, and the most probable ancestral areas determined for all internal nodes within the trees, thereby enabling the direction of migration events to be inferred. Relaxed molecular clock methods will be used to estimate divergence times, enabling the putative migration events to be correlated with geological and palaeoclimatic data. It is likely that dispersals between Africa and Asia occurred via different routes during different “windows of opportunity”, as determined by geological and climatic conditions (which influenced sea-levels). The relative importance of alternative dispersal routes will be evaluated by reference to the geological and climatic data. Species distribution data will be correlated with available climatic data to generate optimized climatic preferences for each species; this will then be mapped onto the phylogenies to determine whether such preferences are conservative over phylogenetic timescales, and to give an insight into current and potential future changes associated with global warming.

777210.label: Realisation of objectives
777210.value: We were able to successfully address all the main objectives of the project. We successfully reconstructed the phylogeny of the species-rich genus Uvaria, which shows a clear African-Asian disjunction, and then expanded the study significantly to accommodate a much broader taxonomic sampling across the entire family. This latter study included representatives of c. 75% of all Annonaceae genera. The phylogenies obtained during this research were largely well-resolved and strongly supported, enabling continued study and biogeographical interpretation. In each of the two main studies we were able to successfully determine ancestral areas for internal nodes in the phylogenies using statistical dispersal-vicariance analysis and/or likelihood reconstructions. We furthermore used uncorrelated lognormal distributed (UCLD) relaxed molecular clock methods to infer divergence ages of lineages with reference to fossils of known age and phylogenetic position. We were successfully able to correlate these results with geological and palaeoclimatic data as well as known patterns of frugivory and seed dispersal in extant species. Using this data we were able to infer the most likely explanations for the African-Asian disjunctions, and, in the second, broader study, assess how general these dispersal or vicariance events were. We encountered some problems with the application of phyloclimatic modeling, largely because of limitations of taxon selection. I have indicated 100% achieved, below, for this objective, however, because the knowledge gained in phyloclimatic modeling as a result of this funding has now been successfully applied to another intercontinental disjunction in the Annonaceae (the Asimina-Disepalum disjunction); this research is about to be submitted to Journal of Biogeography within the next few months, but is not listed here as output from this grant as it does not focus specifically on African-Asian disjunction, but rather Neotropical-Asian disjunction.

777210.label: Major findings and research outcome
777210.value: The early stages of the project focused on an evaluation of the historical biogeography of the genus Uvaria, a member of the early-divergent angiosperm family Annonaceae. As well as being comparatively species-rich (c. 230 species), Uvaria exhibits a clear African-Asian disjunction, and is an ideal candidate genus for testing the three competing biogeographical hypotheses to explain this disjunction: (1) ‘rafting’ on the Indian tectonic plate, enabling Africa-to-Asia dispersal; (2) migration via Eocene boreotropical forests; and (3) transoceanic long-distance dispersal. We generated an extensive dataset of chloroplast DNA sequences (matK, psbA-trnH spacer, rbcL and trnL-F) for 59 Uvaria species, including 20 from Africa-Madagascar, and 39 from Asia-Australasia. This dataset was supplemented with corresponding data for 77 outgroup taxa, derived from GenBank. We used this data to generate a molecular phylogeny using Bayesian inference methods, which was time-calibrated using fossil taxa of known age and phylogenetic position. We were therefore able to determine the diversification age of all lineages within the phylogeny, and showed that the genus originated c. 31.6 Ma. We also used software to determine the most likely ancestral areas for all internal nodes within the phylogeny. This revealed that the genus originated in Africa, with two main migration events: dispersal into Madagascar around 17.0 Ma; and dispersal into Asia between 21.4 and 16.1 Ma. We were not only able to correlate these deduction with known geological and palaeoclimatic changes, but also with patterns of frugivory and seed dispersal observed in extant species. Our results were not congruent with the geological dates required for hypotheses (1) and (2), above. Uvaria fruits are widely reported to be consumed by primates, and are therefore unlikely candidates for successful long-distance transoceanic dispersal (hypothesis 3, above). We suggested an alternative scenario, involving dispersal during the late Middle Miocene thermal maximum (17-15 Ma), associated with the ‘out-of-Africa’ dispersal of primates. We subsequently expanded the study to include a much broader sampling of Annonaceae species to determine whether other African-Asian disjunctions could be similarly explained. We accumulated extensive DNA sequence data for representatives of c. 75% of genera in the family, and used statistical dispersal-vicariance analysis and likelihood reconstructions to identify 12 intercontinental dispersal events between Africa and Asia. Although migration through the Eocene boreotropics are undoubtedly of great significance, our results highlighted the importance of post-boreotropical processes, with overland connections between Africa and Asia possible via the Arabian Peninsula during the Miocene.

777410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777410.value: The enteric nervous system (ENS) is a part of peripheral nervous system which controls the motility, secretions and immune response in the intestinal tract. The ENS is derived from vagal neural crest cells during embryogenesis, abnormal development of enteric neural crest cells leads to intestinal aganglionosis, a condition known as Hirschprung’s disease in humans. The primary pathology of Hirschprung’s disease is the absence of neurons and ganglia in the distal colon, resulting in considerable morbidity and mortality. The Sox10 gene encodes a transcription factor which plays an important role in maintaining the potency of neural crest stem cells. A reduction of the stem and progenitor cell pool is one of the factors leading to the deficiency of ganglion cells in the distal colon. However, it is not known whether Sox10 affects the intrinsic migration ability of neural crest cells, or affects the neural crest cell-gut microenvironment interaction, which will also lead to the absence of ganglion cells in the distal colon. We have generated a Sox10-NGFP mutant mouse model in our laboratory, in the mutant mice all the enteric neural crest cells are marked by GFP. The Sox10-NGFP mutants displayed varied degree of intestinal aganglionosis. Our pilot experiments suggest that Sox10 mutant cells display abnormal cell-matrix interactions, which will impair the motility of the mutant neural crest cells in the gut. In this project, using ex vivo gut explant co-culture assays, we propose to investigate the migration behaviour and motility of the enteric neural crest cells in wildtype and mutant guts by time-lapse confocal live-imaging analyses. To understand the molecular basis for the cell autonomous and non-cell autonomous migratory defects of the Sox10-NGFP mutant neural crest cells, the expression of candidate signalling molecules including PKCα, GTPase RhoA, β1-integrin will be investigated. The molecular and cellular basis underlying enteric neural crest cell migration in vivo is not known. This project will be one of the first studies in elucidating the mechanisms for the abnormal enteric neural crest cell migration behaviour in the developing mammalian gut. 腸道神經系統屬於週邊神經系統的一部分。它的功能主要是調控腸道的能動性，腸分泌及其免疫反應。腸道神經系統起源於胚胎期的迷走神經脊細胞。不正常的腸神經脊細胞發育會導致腸道神經節缺失，也就是所謂先天性巨結腸症。先天性巨結腸症的基本病理是遠端结腸的神經元和神經節缺失， 因而導致發病和死亡。 Sox10是一種轉錄因子。它對於維持神經脊幹細胞的各種潛能性有非常重要的作用。神經脊幹細胞和前體細胞數量的減少是導致遠端結腸神經節缺乏的一個非常重要的原因。但是，到目前為止還不知道Sox10是否可以影響神經脊細胞的自主遷移能力，或者影響神經脊細胞與腸道微環境的相互作用，因此而導致遠端结腸神經節的缺失。 我們實驗室構建了一種Sox10-NGFP突變鼠，在這種突變鼠體內，突變的腸道神經脊細胞被綠色熒光蛋白（GFP）所標誌。Sox10-NGFP突變鼠表現出一系列不同程度的腸道神經節缺失。我們的前期實驗表明Sox10突變細胞與細胞基質的相互作用不正常，因而損傷了突變神經脊細胞的運動性能。在這個課題中，我們運用了體外腸組織培養和即時活體顯微影像分析來研究原生型和突變型神經脊細胞的遷移行為和運動性能。為了了解有關Sox10-NGFP 突變細胞的細胞自主性和非細胞自主性的運動缺陷的分子機理，我們將要分析相關的信號分子的表達，包括PKCα, GTPase RhoA, β1-integrin。活體內有關腸道神經脊細胞遷移的細胞分子機理到目前還不清楚。我們的研究將會是第一個闡明有關腸道神經脊細胞在發育期腸道中的遷移的機理的研究。

777410.label: Realisation of objectives
777410.value: Objective 1. By time lapse live-cell imaging analyses using normal and Sox10-NGFP mutant mouse embryos, we have examined the abnormal cell migration behavior of the Sox10 mutant cells. To investigate whether there are cell-autonomous defect in the Sox10-NGFP mutant enteric neural crest cells which impair their motility in the gut, organotypic co-culture experiments with combinations of donor gut and aganglionic recipient gut were carried out, using Wnt1-cre;Z/EG mice as normal conrol. We concluded that the Sox10-NGFP mutant enteric neural crest cells displayed cell-autonomous defect in cell migration. We have achieved Objective 1 as planned. Objective 2. We investigated the interaction of Sox10 mutant cells with gut extracellular matrix components by culturing gut explants on different extracellular matrix molecules including fibronectin, laminin, vironectin and tenascin-C in different combinations. Furthermore, we performed live-cell imaging experiments and analysed the single cell movements of Sox10 mutant gut explaints. We have analysed the motility of Sox10 mutant and normal control cells using available software as well as mathematical modeling. Therefore, we have fully achieved Objective 2. Objective 3. The interaction of enteric neural crest cells with extracellular matrix molecules is mediated by the integrin family of cell-surface receptors and other cell adhesion molecules. To investigate the expression of these cell adhesion family of genes, we purified Sox10 mutant enteric neural crest cells by FACS, and examined the expression profiles of candidate genes by qRT-PCR. We have also investigated the changes in expression of intracellular signaling molecules involved in cell migration, such as PDGFRa and FAK, by immunohistochemistry. In this study, we have obtained novel insights on the molecular mechanism and signalling pathways underlying the defects in cell motility and cell migration of the Sox10 mutant. We have achieved Objective 3 as planned.

777410.label: Major findings and research outcome
777410.value: Using the Sox10-NGFP mouse model where EGFP is fused to the N-terminal domain of Sox10, we have been able to visualize the migration behaviour of mutant enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs). We examined Sox10-NGFP/+ intestines from E10.5 to E16.5, and measured the migration speed of ENCCs using time-lapse imaging on ex vivo gut explant cultures. In Sox10NGFP/+ intestines, the migration speed of the ENCCs was significantly slower when compared with Wnt1-Cre/ZEG control cells at all time points. To address whether delay of gult colonization could be due to abnormal interaction of ENCCs with specific extracellular matrix molecules (ECM) dynamically expressed along the rostrocaudal axis of the gut, we cultured E12.5 Sox10-NGFP/+ gut explants on various ECM substrata – vitronectin, laminin-1, fibronectin, and tenascin-C. Wildtype cells were well-dispersed outside the explants, but mutant cells were found to be tightly packed. Cell aggregation was observed for mutant Sox10-NGFP/+ ENCCs on all matrices tested, especially on fibronectin substrate. In further study the motility of mutant ENCCs, we examined ex vivo gut explants culture on fibronectin. Movements of cells from the explants were recorded for 24 hours by confocal time-lapse live-cell imaging. While the Sox10-NGFP/+ cells displayed active movements on fibronectin-coated dish, their persistence was 43% lower than control cells, giving a significant 26% reduction in final displacement. Furthermore, by western blot analysis using protein extracts of mutant and normal midguts, the level of phospho-FAK397, the activated form of focal adhesion kinase required for cell motility, was reduced in Sox10-NGFP/+ mutants. To determine whether adhesion molecules could be involved in the altered migration behaviour observed in the mutant gut, we analyzed the gene expression of selected cell adhesion molecules by qPCR, using ENCCs purified by FACS. qPCR results showed no significant changes in the expression of α4, α5, α6, αV, β1, β5 integrins, suggesting that integrins are not likely to contribute to altered motility of ENCCs in the Sox10 mutants. We further analyzed selected cadherin genes, and found altered expression of the type II cadherins cdh10 and cdh11, which suggests changes in cell-cell adhesion strength. Changes in cadherin expression profile could likely contribute to reduced motility observed in Sox10NGFP/+ guts. Our results indicated that Sox10 is required for controlling the locomotion of enteric neural crest cells. We have identified specific cadherin molecules which are affected in the Sox10 mutant cells, providing a novel mechanism underlying the abnormal neural crest colonization in the developing gut.

777410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777410.value: In this project, we have discovered that the expression profile of cell adhesion molecules of the enteric neural crest cells have a profound effect on cell-cell and cell-matrix interaction, thereby affecting their migration behavior and contribute to the phenotypes observed in the Sox10 mutant mice. Further development of the current project will include the following: 1. It is not clear whether the changes in cadherin gene expressions are resulted from direct transcriptional regulation by the Sox10 gene, or indirect consequence of cellular behavior. Further studies will be necessary to distinguish these possibilities. 2. This study opens up a new family of candidate genes involved in cell adhesion which could be novel disease causing genes for intestinal aganglionosis. This will have an impact on further studies on disease gene identification for Waardenburg-Shah syndrome and Hirschprung disease. 3. The Sox10-NGFP mice we generated provide a platform for purified cell source via cell sorting, allowing future transcriptome or large scale genomic based studies on different cell types which express the Sox10 gene. In view of these possible project development, future research grant proposals will be developed and submitted to the RGC for further funding and continuation of the study.

777410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777410.value: Mutations of the transcription factor gene Sox10 in human and mice lead to deficiency of ganglion cells in the colon. We investigated the roles of Sox10 in controlling the migration of enteric neural crest cells in the developing gut. By time-lapse live-cell imaging using the Sox10-NGFP mutant mice we generated, we found that the Sox10 mutant enteric neural crest cells displayed reduced migration speed and altered trajectories. This behaviour was cell-autonomous, as shown by organotypic grafting of mutant gut segments onto control guts. To investigate the interactions of Sox10 mutant cells on extracellular matrix molecules (ECM), we cultured gut explants on various ECMs and found that Sox10 mutant cells formed aggregates, particularly on fibronectin. Single cell time-lapse imaging analysis indicated that the tightly-packed Sox10 mutant cells displayed increased cell adhesiveness. We examined the expression profile of adhesion molecule families by qPCR using FACS-sorted Sox10 mutant cells, and found that expression of specific cadherins were altered, suggesting that Sox10 mutation affects cell adhesion properties of enteric neural crest cells. Our findings identify a de novo role of Sox10 in regulating cell adhesion and the migration behaviour of enteric neural crest cells, which has important implications for the treatment of Hirschsprung disease.

777610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777610.value: Stroke is a leading cause of disability in human diseases. Current therapies are seldom successful in improving the recovery of neurological deficits of stroke victims. Recent progress suggests that neural stem/progenitor cells can potentially develop into new functional neurons in the injured area, offering hope for regeneration therapies for post-stroke patients. Developing new drug target for promoting neurogenesis is an attractive strategy for brain repair, which relies on the understanding of the signal mechanisms of adult neurogenesis. Both vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and Notch1 play critical roles in regulating neurogenesis. VEGF is showed to stimulate proliferation and differentiation of adult neural stem/progenitor cells and improve recovery of neurological deficits after stroke. Notch signaling can modulate the maintenance, proliferation and differentiation of neural stem/progenitor cells. The activation of the Notch1 signaling is associated with the enhanced proliferation of neural stem/progenitor cells and the inhibited neural differentiation after transient focal cerebral ischemia. However, there is a gap in current knowledge regarding how VEGF and Notch1 signaling are modulated in the NSCs. Our pilot studies have suggested that a plasma membrane signal molecule named caveolin-1 could be a key player in controlling proliferation and differentiation of NSCs after stroke. Caveolin-1 is found in the NSCs but its function has not been defined. Our preliminary results showed that (1) the down-regulated caveolin-1 was coincident with the enhanced VEGF and VEGF receptor Flk1 and cell proliferation in post-stroke brains at early stage whereas the up-regulated caveolin-1 was coincident with the enhanced Notch1 signaling, decreased VEGF signaling and inhibited neural differentiation at late stage; (2) manipulations of caveolin-1 remarkably affected the VEGF and Notch1 signaling and neural differentiation in the neural stem/progenitor cells. The experimental evidence leads us to hypothesize that caveolin-1 can regulate neurogenesis by inhibiting VEGF and VEGF receptor and activating Notch1 signaling. To verify the hypothesis, we will address following questions: (1) Does caveolin-1 modulate the proliferation and differentiation of neural stem/progenitor cells ? (2) Are VEGF and its receptor Flk-1 the targets of caveolin-1 in controlling the proliferation and differentiation of neural stem/progenitor cells? (3) Does caveolin-1 regulate Notch1 signaling in neural stem/progenitor cells? The proposed study will advance current knowledge about the mechanisms of neurogenesis after stroke. Importantly, if our hypothesis can be verified, caveolin-1 can be potentially used as a novel target protein for drug discovery, which will open a new therapeutic window for stroke and other neurodegenerative diseases. 中風是人類疾病中的第三位殺手﹐目前無有效的促進神經損傷修復的有效方法。近年來的研究發現﹐中風後損傷區域的神經幹細胞具有向新生功能性神經發展的潛能﹐為神經再生治療帶來了希望。研究成年神經幹細胞的信號調節機製﹐是發展促進神經再生的新標靶和神經修復治療的有效途徑。血管內皮細胞生長因子(VEGF)和Notch是神經再生的重要調控因子﹐ VEGF能刺激成年神經幹細胞增殖和分化﹐促進中風後神經功能的修復。Notch信號能調節神經幹細胞增殖和分化﹐ 但是他們是怎樣影響神經幹細胞增殖和分化還不清楚。我們先前的研究證明細胞膜上的小凹蛋白可能是中風後神經幹細胞增殖和神經分化的重要調節蛋白。我們基於已有的實驗證據﹐進一步提出新的假說﹐小凹蛋白通過與血管內皮細胞生長因子(VEGF)和Notch信號相互作用﹐從而抑制缺血後腦組織神經幹細胞增殖和神經分化。為證明本假說﹐我們將研究以下幾個問題﹕(1)是否小凹蛋白能抑制缺血後腦組織神經幹細胞增殖和神經分化﹖(2)是否小凹蛋白通過抑制VEGF和它的受體﹐達到抑制神經幹細胞增殖和神經分化的﹖(3) 小凹蛋白是否影響Notch信號通路﹐從而抑制神經幹細胞增殖和神經分化﹖ 本研究將為促進中風後神經再生提供的新標靶﹐以促進神經幹細胞向新生功能性神經發展﹐為發展中風後遺症神經再生治療的新藥打下基礎。

777610.label: Realisation of objectives
777610.value: We conducted a series of experiments and have achieved all of the goals designed in our original proposal. Objective 1. (1)We used primary cultured NPCs and investigated the proliferation and differentiation of NPCs under both normoxic and hypoxic conditions. Both siRNA and cav-1 peptides were used to verify the roles of cav-1 in the regulation of neuronal differentiation, oligodendroglial differentiation and astroglial differentiation under normoxic and hypoxic conditions. (2)We conducted in vivo animal experiments by using wild-type and Cav-1 knockout (KO) mice to compare the differences of neuronal differentiation under normal condition and the conditions of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO)-induced cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Objective 2. (1) We investigated the mechanisms of cav-1 in regulation of neuronal differentiation in NPCs. In addition to the VEGF signaling and Flk receptor. We also investigated other signaling pathways including enhanced phosphorylations of p44/42MAPK, Akt and Stat3. Both in vitro cultured NPCs and in vivo MCAO cerebral ischemia-reperfusion animal models were used in the experiments. Both wild type and cav-1 KO mice were used in the study. (2) We further studied the mechanisms of cav-1 in modulating oligodendroglial differentiation of NPCs. For in vivo experiments, we investigated oligodendroglial differentiation by detecting the expressions of 20,30-cyclic nucleotide 30-phosphodiesterase (CNPase) and beta-catenin in the brains of wild type mice and Cav-1 knockout mice. For in vitro experiments, we observed the potential roles of Cav-1 in modulating beta-catenin expression and oligodendroglial differentiation in isolated cultured NPCs by manipulating Cav-1 expression with Cav-1 scaffolding domain peptide and Cav-1 RNA silencing approach. (3) To understand the effects of microenvironment niche regulation of neurogenesis, we used co-cultured system with brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMVECs) and NPCs in vitro. In the meantime, we investigated the roles of endothelial cav-1 in regulating neurogenesis in MCAO animal model with WT can cav-1 KO mice. Objective 3 (1) We investigated the roles of cav-1 in modulating astroglial differentiation and explored the mechanisms related to Notch signaling pathway. The expressions of S100β, GFAP, VEGF, NICD and hairy enhancer of split 1 (Hes1) were detected in the brains of wild-type and cav-1 KO mice in vivo. (2) We also studied the effects of cav-1 in regulating Notch signaling pathway with in vitro cultured differentiating NPCs. Others realted research activities: We further explore the potential application of cav-1 as new drug targets and investigated the changes of cav-1 in the plasma of ischemic stroke patients.

777610.label: Major findings and research outcome
777610.value: 1. Caveolin-1 plays a crucial role in inhibiting neuronal differentiation of neural stem/progenitor cells via VEGF signaling-dependent pathway The study proves that Cav-1 can inhibit neuronal differentiation via down-regulations of VEGF, p44/42MAPK, Akt and Stat3 signaling pathways, and that VEGF signaling is a crucial target of Cav-1. The hypoxia-induced down-regulation of Cav-1 contributes to enhanced neuronal differentiation in NPCs. The results have been published in PLoS One 2011; 6(8):e22901. 2. Caveolin-1 could inhibit oligodendroglial differentiation of NPCs through modulating beta-catenin expression in vivo and in vitro. The study prove that cav-1 can inhibit oligodendroglial differentiation of NPCs through modulating beta-catenin expression. The results have been published in Neurochemistry International 59(2):114-121, 2011 3. Caveolin-1 could promote astroglial differentiation of NPCs through modulating Notch1/NICD and Hes1 expressions in vivo and in vitro. The study suggests that cav-1 can promote astroglial differentiation of NPCs through modulating Notch1/NICD and Hes1 expressions. The results have been published in Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications 407(3):517-524, 2011 4. Caveolin-1 derived from endothelial cells impacts on neuronal differentiation of NPCs in post-ischemic brains Cav-1 was found to mainly distribute in brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMVECs).Using co-cultured system with BMVECs and NPCs, we found that cav-1 and VEGF, secreted from BMVECs, could influence neuronal differentiation of NPCs through modulating NeuroD1, and p44/42MAPK phosphorylation. Animal experiments revealed that cav-1 derived from BMVECs negatively modulated neural regeneration of NPCs by targeting VEGF signaling. Down-regulation of cav-1 in the microvascular niche contributes to enhanced neuronal differentiation in NPCs. The manuscript is in preparing. 5. Drug discovery for promoting neurogenesis by targeting cav-1 and its down-stream signaling pathways We used cav-1 and its downstream signaling as targets for drug screening to promote neurogenesis. Baicalin, a flavonoid compound isolated from Scutellaria baicalensis G, is a promoting candidate for regulating its down–stream signaling and promoting neurogenesis. The results indicate that baicalin promotes the neural differentiation but inhibit glial formation and its mechanisms are associated with the modulations of stat3 and bHLH. These results has published in Brain Research 1429:36-42; 2012 We also studied the changes of cav-1 in plasma samples of ischemic stroke patients. Twenty-one patients with ischemic stroke were included in the study. Pearson analysis showed that plasma cav-1 was negatively correlated with the neurological deficit scores. Cav-1 could be an important bio-marker for stroke patients. We are planning to collect more pilot data for our next research proposal for clinical study.

777610.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777610.value: Based on the achievement of our studies, we expect following potential directions for further studies: (1) To further explore the molecular mechanisms of cav-1 in regulating proliferation and differentiation of NPCs. In particular, how cav-1 regulates Notch1/NICD, Hes1 signaling pathways and beta-catenin signaling pathway are valuable to be further studied. (2) Using cav-1 as a molecular target for drug screening to develop new therapeutic approaches for regeneration therapy. More extensive studies can be conducted in this aspect. (3) To further investigate the relationship between plasma cav-1 level and neurological dysfunction in both stroke animal model and stroke human subjects. Due to the limitation of funding and research period, we could not achieve the goals. We plan to seek for more funds from RGC GRF grants or other funding sources to continue our studies in this direction.

777610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777610.value: Stroke is a leading cause of disability in human diseases. The prevalence of stroke becomes one of the major disease burdens worldwide. Current therapeutic approaches fail to prove their efficacy in the improvement of neurological dysfunction. Targeting neural stem cells is a promising strategy for regeneration therapy in post-stroke treatment. Thus, seeking for new molecular targets for regeneration therapy is timely important. With the support of RGC GRF grant, we conducted a series of experiments to test our hypothesis that caveolin-1, a plasma membrane signaling molecule, plays important roles in the regulation of the growth of neural stem cells. We demonstrate that caveolin-1 plays a crucial role in inhibiting neuronal and oligodendroglial differentiation but promoting astroglial differentiation through modulating different cellular signaling pathways. Caveolin-1 could be a crucial protein for cell fate decision during neurogenesis. Hypoxia or ischemia reduces caveolin-1 level in brain and blood. The decrease of cav-1 can trigger the program of adult neurogenesis in the ischemic brain. Therefore, cav-1 is an important molecular target for drug discovery in the regeneration therapy for post-stroke treatment. This project yields 4 original articles, 1 article in preparation, 3 review article and trained 5 postgraduate students.

777810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777810.value: Our ultimate goal of in vitro derivation of Schwann cells from adult tissues is such that they may be used autologously in nerve guidance channels to assist post-traumatic nerve regeneration in both PNS and CNS. Protocols for transdifferentiation of bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs) to Schwann cell-like cells fall short in stability of the acquired phenotype and functional capacity of the derived cells to myelinate axons. The present study will address these issues by (1) selecting and expanding neuro-ectodermal stem/progenitor cells among the BMSCs, (2) inducing differentiation of the neuro-ectodermal derivatives to early Schwann cell-like cells, and (3) specifying commitment to the Schwann cell lineage. The BMSC-derived Schwann cells will be tested for stable commitment in subcultures and for functional capacity to myelinate both in vitro and in vivo. This work not only advances the know-how for directed differentiation of BMSCs to stable Schwann cells in vitro prior to use in transplantation and cell-mediated therapy, but also promises new knowledge on key molecules in neuron-glia interactions that specify commitment to the Schwann cell fate. 我們研究成年組織在體外衍生為雪旺氏細胞的最終目標是這些細胞可能被自體用於神經導管內協助損傷後的外周和中樞的神經再生。從骨髓基質幹細胞（BMSCs）到雪旺氏樣細胞的轉分化實驗在細胞獲得性表型和衍生細胞使軸突髓鞘化的功能性上尚有不足之處。我們目前的研究將通過（1）選擇和擴充BMSCs以外的神經外胚層神經幹細胞/前体细胞；（2） 將神經外胚層細胞分化為早期雪旺氏樣細胞；及（3）將雪旺氏樣細胞特定分化為雪旺氏細胞， 針對性地解決以上問題。傳代培養實驗檢測了BMSC-源性雪旺細胞的定型穩定性，及在體離體實驗檢測了其形成髓鞘的功能性。這項研究不僅推進了BMSCs在用於移植和細胞介導治療前，定向分化為雪旺氏細胞的方法，還揭示了在神經細胞-膠質細胞相互作用中决定雪旺氏细胞定向分化的关键分子。

777810.label: Realisation of objectives
777810.value: Objective 1: to consolidate the Schwann cell derivation protocol and to test for functional capacity of the derived cells to guide axonal regrowth and remyelination of axons in an in vivo model • We addressed planned experiments under Objective 1. We exploited sphere cultures to expand neural crest derivatives at the expense of mesenchymal and haematopoietic cells among bone marrow cells collected from adult rats. Commitment to the Schwann cell fate was achieved by coculture of these neural crest derivatives with dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons. Efforts were made to translate this protocol to the in vitro derivation human Schwann cells from bone marrow cells and human donors. • The bone marrow-derived Schwann cells demonstrated capacity for myelination both in a cell culture model and in a guidance channel that bridged a critical gap between stumps of a transected sciatic nerve (in vivo model). Objective 2: to identify neuron-associated Nrg-1 type III as a key effector that specifies commitment of Schwann cell-like cells to the Schwann cell fate • We addressed planned experiments in 2.1: DRG neurons in culture were immunopositive for Nrg-1 type III in both soma and neurites. Expression of the cognate receptors of Nrg-1 type III, ErbB2 and ErbB3, were not detectable (by RTPCR, immunocytochemistry and Western blot analysis) among bone marrow-derived Schwann cell-like cells (SCLCs) until these derived cells had been cocultured with the DRG neurons. • We addressed 2.2 and 2.3: The switch of SCLCs to fate commitment could not be achieved with either soluble isoforms of Nrg-1 or coculture with non-neuronal HEK293T-NRG1 type III cells, suggesting the importance of neuronal contact with SCLCs to accomplish Nrg-1 type III signaling for the switch. • We took an alternative strategy to address 2.2 and 2.4: By identifying Notch signaling that mediates the expression of ErbB2 and ErbB3 in SCLCs, we found the key that turns on the SCLC response to Nrg-1 type III signaling en route to the Schwann cell fate. DRG neurons therefore play dual roles in presenting: (1) surface Notch ligands, Dll-1 and Jagged-1 for effecting Notch signaling that leads to upregulation of ErbB2 and ErbB3 in Schwann cell-like cells and (2) surface Nrg-1 type III for effecting ErbB2/3 signaling for the Schwann cell fate. • We have yet to find if Schwann cell fate commitment is an early target of PI 3-kinase activation by Nrg-1 type III.

777810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777810.value: Our ultimate goal of in vitro derivation of Schwann cells from adult tissues is such that they may be used autologously in nerve guidance channels to assist post-traumatic nerve regeneration in both the peripheral and central nervous systems. The bone marrow harbours renewable progenitor cells that can be tapped for directed differentiation in vitro. Existing protocols for derivation of Schwann cell-like cells (SCLCs) from bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs) fall short in stability of the acquired phenotype and the functional capacity to myelinate axons. In the current project, we successfully directed the differentiation of neuro-ectodermal progenitor cells among the BMSCs such that they accomplish commitment to the Schwann cell fate. These derived Schwann cells when transplanted into the injured environment of the rat sciatic nerve switched on an axon-supportive program that improved nerve regeneration and functional recovery. The dorsal root ganglia neurons play key roles in presenting signaling ligands: (1) Notch ligand-receptor pair and (2) neuregulin-ErbB2/3 to BMSC-derived glial cells such that they commit to the Schwann cell fate.

777910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777910.value: 心臟肌肉細胞是心臟發揮其收縮功能功不可沒的功臣。鑑於心肌只擁有有限的再生功能，在一些刺激如心肌壞死的情況下，心肌缺失幾乎是不可逆的。在這個時候，往往能比較理想地治療末期心臟衰竭的是同種異體移植。但是這依舊收到移植源短缺問題的牽制。故此，嶄新的細胞水平研究已逐漸發展成一個應對心肌細胞再生障礙的策略。眾所周知的，胚胎幹細胞擁有心肌細胞分化的巨大潛能。和其他科學家們一樣，我們屢次在實驗室裡的心肌壞死模型中成功地證實它確實可以修補受損傷的心臟肌肉。儘管如此，在“概念證明”上，胚胎幹細胞的再生能力還是被保留的，一些有待突破的胚胎幹細胞研究障礙至今依然存在。舉例：自發的胚胎幹細胞分化是極為罕見的，這使得胚胎幹細胞在臨床上的實際使用受挫。 雖然掌握胚胎期心臟的發展被扼要地顯示能促進胚胎幹細胞的心肌分化，我們最近的發現卻證實胚胎幹細胞分化的心肌細胞有着不成熟的顯型。這包括了：對於鈣離子的處理。這處理與心臟興奮-收縮耦聯有着密切關係。這些不成熟度，不但會形成移植物和宿主在心臟電生理學上的不協調還有可能導致宿主在移植後爆發致死性心律失常。 不能大面積地培養成熟、穩定的心肌分化-胚胎幹細胞這方面研究的一大絆腳石。我們的實驗已經不成熟胚胎幹細胞分化的心肌對鈣離子的處理是與它們的分化程度和對特定鈣離子的處理以及調控蛋白有莫大關係。利用腺病毒成為基因載體，我們成功地提高胚胎幹細胞分化--心肌細胞對鈣離子的處理性質，使得它們有更接近於成熟心肌細胞的成熟顯型。儘管這理念是極具吸引力，但腺病毒載體的使用以及其偶發性是仍然是成功基因轉錄的羈絆。另一方面，生理學上的刺激可以促進後天的細胞肥大和改變細胞對鈣離子的處置告訴我們給予合適的刺激或者干預，讓胚胎幹細胞分化的心肌細胞穩定並不是遙不可及的。事實上，很多的刺激包括生理壓力的壓力和體積改變；神經-內分泌上的調變：哇巴因和甲狀腺原的相聚能最終激活絲裂原活化蛋白激酶的信號級聯並決定心臟細胞的顯型。我們知道，這些能使胚胎幹細胞分化的心肌細胞穩定的措施並還沒有在被系統地探索。 故此，我們提議探索所有能促進胚胎幹細胞分化成心肌細胞的策略，應用一系列生理上的刺激使分化後的心肌細胞趨向穩定、成為有再生能力的心肌。這研究的實用性以及安全性將在胚胎幹細胞分化的心肌細胞研究上為我們開拓更多未知的領域、提高我們在這方面的認識。而這一些將能進一步地加強基因轉錄的在心臟衰竭上的實際應用。

777910.label: Realisation of objectives
777910.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) represent an attractive ex-vivo cell source for cardiac regenerative therapy. However, spontaneous differentiation of ESCs toward cardiac lineage is nonetheless inefficient, and the resultant cardiomyocytes display immature electrophysiological and calcium handling properties. The overall aim of this RCG project is to enhance cardiogenesis of ESCs and improve maturity of the resultant cardiac derivatives using various endogenous signals including triidothyronine (T3) and ouabain. In our study, we have first tested the effects of endogenous signals triidothyronine and ouabain on cardiogenesis in ESCs. Both T3 and ouabain result in enhanced cardiogenesis (~2 folded and 4-folded increase respectively). We have attempted to increase the dosage of these compounds in order to increase cardiogenesis, but this resulted in increase in apoptosis. Although the improvement in the efficacy of enhancing cardiogenesis (increase in number of cardiomyocytes) is rather modest, we have identified the downstream signaling pathway that leads to cardiogenesis: ERK1/2 pathway for ouabain and the classical genomic pathway for T3. This allows further exploitation of these pathways in enhancing ESC cardiogenesis. More importantly, we have demonstrated that T3 can significantly mature the electrical phenotypes and calcium handling properties of ESC derived cardiomyocytes. The immature electrical phenotypes including more positive resting membrane potential and prolonged action potential duration are the principle determinants of arrhythmogenesis when transplanted into the myocardium. T3 treatment shortens the action potential duration and generats more negative resting membrane potential. Both T3 and ouabain improve the calcium handling properties of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes, which is the key process of excitation contraction coupling. These results provide important clues for future steps in preparation of cardiomyocytes for regenerative medicine.

777910.label: Major findings and research outcome
777910.value: Objective 1: To test the hypothesis that endogenous signals: (A) Triidothyronine (T3) and (B) ouabain can enhance the cardiomyocyte differentiation of ESCs. In this regard, we have first demonstrated the T3 promotes cardiogenesis and myofibrillogenesis of ESCs. T3-treated embryoid bodies from ESCs exhibit an increase in differentiation into cardiomyocytes (in terms of the percentage of beating outgrowths and troponin-positive cardiomyocytes). T3 supplementation during cardiac differentiation from ESCs increases gene expression of cardiogenesis (Nkx2.5) and myofibrillogenesis (MLC-2v, α- and β-MHC). This T3-enhanced cardiogeneis of ESCs works through the classical genomic pathway of Thyroid hormone, which can be blocked by bisphenol-A, but not the Akt- and MAPK-signaling cascades. In addition, we tested also the effect of ouabain on cardiogenesis of ESCs. Resembling T3, ouabain-treated EBs showed an increased differentiation into cardiomyocytes (in terms of the percentages of beating outgrowths and troponin-positive cardiomyocytes) and increased gene expression of cardiogenesis (α-MHC and β-MHC). The enhanced cardiogenesis appears to be working through ERK1/2. Objective 2: To test the hypothesis that embryonic calcium handling phenotypes of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes can be matured for safer transplantation with (a) T3 and (b) ouabain. In addition to the enhanced cardiogenesis, we have demonstrated both T3 and ouabain can facilitate the maturation of the electrical phenotypes as well as the calcium handling properties of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes, which can be pro-arrhythmic. Specifically, electrophysiological properties of T3 treated ESC-derived cardiomyocytes were adult-like with significantly more negative resting membrane potential and much shorter action potential duration, which were both important determinants of arrhythmogenesis. In addition, using confocal calcium imaging, the calcium transient, the key process underlying the excitation contraction coupling is much improved in T3-treated ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. Specifically, T3-treated ESC-derived cardiomyocytes generated a significantly larger maximal upstroke velocity and a higher maximal decay velocity, which were associated with upregulation of SERCA-2a and RyR-2. Likewise, ouabain treated ESC-derived cardiomyocytes also exhibited more mature calcium handling properties with larger calcium transients, higher maximal and decay velocity, and a more mature SR as evidenced by large surges of caffeine induced calcium release.

777910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777910.value: Given the promising effects of the individual endogeneous signals for cardiac differentiation, we have been developing protocols combining T3 and ouabain in order to facilitate cardiac differention. In addition, the protocol will be tested in induced pluripotent stem cells which is similar to ESC but without the potential ethical issue of the use of human embryo.

777910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777910.value: In this research project, we have successfully improved the process of generation of heart muscle cells from stem cells and maturate their functional properties by using our bodily signal system. This represents important ground works for realization of stem cell therapy in regeneration of human heart.

778610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
778610.value: 複雜疾病的遺傳結構包括共同變異（Common Variances, CVs；發生頻率5％）和稀有變異（Rare Variances, RVs；發生頻率<3％; 更可能是功能性變異而具有更大風險）。 CVs和RVs的存在不是相互排斥的，問題是要確定其各自對疾病的相對貢獻。全基因組測序對於疾病充分的了解在此十分重要，但它目前尚不能廣泛實行，而在我們研究範圍內的成本效益也並不理想。由於蛋白編碼外顯子往往富於功能性變異，另一種方法是對疾病相關信號通路的關聯基因的編碼序列（Coding Sequences, CDS）進行深入測序。目前數據已顯示與對照組相比缺失型RVs在疾病組大量出現。我們建議把這種候選基因的測序方法用於先天性巨結腸（Hirschsprung's disease ，HSCR，散發性或家族性神經節細胞缺失），一種由於腸道中的神經元前體細胞遷移異常致病的複雜遺傳性疾病。利用454測序技術，我們將深入測序涵蓋腸道神經系統 (ENS) 發育的相關通路中的62個基因的CDS，剪接位點，和5' - 3'非翻譯區（Un-Translated Regions, UTRs）, 此研究包括600個散發性HSCR病例 ，和600個對照。 HSCR被認為是ENS發育相關基因的CVs和RVs相互作用所致。因為具備成熟的資源條件包括專業人才和與本大學基因組研究中心 (GRC) 的長期合作, 我們現處於一個獨厚的位置來論證這個假設。作為對此申請的支持, 此前小規模候選基因研究結果顯示：i) 因為目前尚無對候選基因的有系統篩查, 所以有可能存在尚未發現的缺失型RVs; ii）一些HSCR患者隱藏ENS發育相關基因的RVs; iii）CVs和RVs對HSCR的關聯在其主要相關基因RET以及NRG1（NRG1是本團隊在全基因組關聯研究中發現的一個新的HSCR相關基因）已經被認同。然而，這些基因的變異只存在於一小部分病人，說明可能有其他基因變異的存在。由於HSCR已成為其他復雜疾病的研究模範，我們的研究將成為此類疾病研究的新依據，也將有助於了解HSCR。 HSCR在本地區的特殊性也值得注意, 因為中國是世界上其中一個HSCR發病率最高的國家。

Thus, we screened 62 genes in some HSCR patients and the whole exome in others. We feel that in the end, we have got much more information on the genetic architecture of HSCR and this can be seen in the research output.
