779210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
779210.value: In some epidemiological, public health and social studies, it is often needed to acquire sensitive information on sexual behavior, abortion, HIV, AIDs, illegal drug usage, child abuse, employee theft, social security fraud, tax evasion, and cheating. When being directly asked sensitive questions, some respondents may refuse to answer or provide wrong answers in order to protect their privacy. To overcome the difficulty, Warner (1965) proposed a randomized response (RR) approach to encourage truthful answers. Since the introduction of the Warner model, voluminous work related to the RR technique have been developed in various directions. Despite of their popularity, the RR models have long been criticized by their (a) lack of reproducibility; (b) lack of trust from the interviewers; (c) higher cost due to introducing randomized devices (RDs); (d) difficulty of understanding RR techniques; (e) narrow range of application; and (f) lower relative efficiency. To overcome some of these difficulties, the PI and his collaborators have developed non-randomized response (NRR) techniques without using any RDs. However, when the response variable Y is a sensitive binary variable (e.g., the status of HIV), no studies have been conducted to investigate the relationship of Y with other covariates (e.g., age, education, and so on). Next, sample size formulae and corresponding regression analysis for the multi-category non-randomized design are not yet available. Further, new and more efficient NRR models need to be further explored. In this proposal, we plan to (1. Hidden Logistic Regression with L1 Penalty) develop hidden logistic regression for the NRR triangular model and identify significant risk factors; (2. Multi-category Non-randomized Model) develop sample size formulae for this model and develop hidden multinomial logistic regression using regularized L1 penalty; (3. The Non-randomized Parallel Model) develop a new parallel model which may be more efficient than the triangular model and determine its sample size formulae; (4. Association Between One Sensitive Question and One Non-sensitive Question) develop a new NRR design and statistical methods for measuring association between one sensitive binary variable (e.g., whether or not takes drug) and one non-sensitive binary variable (e.g., health status); (5. Availability of Free Computer Codes for Practitioners) implement these methods in computer programs and make them available freely to practitioners. Upon completion of the aims, We are confident that the new designs/algorithms will provide fruitful complement to existing NRR techniques and can further benefit surveys involving sensitive questions in epidemiological, public health, behavioral and social society broadly. 摘要: 在某些流行病、公共卫生和社会研究中，我们经常需要收集带敏感性问题的信息。例如：性行为、流产、艾滋病、吸毒、虐孩、偷窃、骗领社会福利、偷税和考试作弊等。如果直接对应答者问这些敏感问题，出于保护隐私，应答者可能会拒绝回答或者提供不真实的答案。 为了克服这些困难，Warner(1965)提出了一个随机化应答方法来鼓励真实的回答。之后，有许多文献进一步地发展了随机化应答技术。然而，随机化应答技术有几个缺点：(a)缺乏再生性；(b) 应答者不信任随机化装置；(c) 由于引入随机化装置，费用大；(d) 要完全地理解该技术，困难大；(e) 应用范围窄；(f) 相对效率低。为了克服这些缺点，本课题负责人及他的合作者提出了不需要使用任何随机化装置的非随机化应答技术。然而，当响应变量Y是一个敏感的二值变量(例如: HIV状态)，如何调查Y与其他协变量(例如：年龄、教育、婚姻状况等)的关系，到目前为止，我们未见到这样的研究文章。其次，相应于多值非随机设计，样本大小计算或回归分析研究也是一个空白。最后，我们需要研究新的和更加有效的非随机化应答模型。 在此课题中，我们有五个目标。 1. 对非随机化的三角模型，发展隐藏的logistic回归并选择显著的风险因子； 2. 用正则化的L1惩罚技术，对多值非随机化应答模型，导出样本大小公式并发展隐藏 的多项式logistic回归技术； 3. 提出并发展一个新的，比存在的三角模型更加有效的非随机化的平行模型并导出它 的样本大小公式； 4. 发展一个新的非随机化设计及相应的统计分析方法来测量一个敏感的二值变量与 另一个非敏感的二值变量之间的关联度； 5. 提出免费使用的计算机编程供使用者。

779210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
779210.value: We could further develop a Poisson item count technique (ICT) and a negative-binomial ICT which replace several independent non-sensitive Bernoulli variables in the original version of ICT by a single non-sensitive random variable following a Poisson distribution or a negative binomial distribution, respectively. Next we can introduce a new Poisson-Poisson ICT for estimating the Poisson mean associated with a sensitive qualitative variable. This Poisson-Poisson ICT can be used to collect and analyze sensitive qualitative data, where an independent non-sensitive Poisson random variable is introduced to facilitate the data collection.

779210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
779210.value: (1) In this project, I provided a systematic research on several important non-randomized response models/techniques for sensitive questions in surveys. (2) I hope that the systematic research will stimulate the application of the non-randomized response approach in surveys and new non-randomized response designs. (3) In particular, I anticipate that these non-randomized response approaches would be useful to a wide range of audiences including government agents, academic researchers, and sample survey practitioners.

779810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
779810.value: NF-κB信號途徑在永生化鼻咽上皮細胞中的激活 鼻咽癌高發于華南地區，由於缺乏合適的細胞模型，使人們對於早期鼻咽癌發生的分子和細胞機制的研究受到限制。永生化屬於癌細胞的固有特性，癌癥發生早期就已開始顯現出這一特徵。我們研究團隊以永生化鼻咽上皮細胞為細胞模型，致力于鼻咽癌早期形成機制的研究，對於其分子和細胞機制的探討和闡釋，有助於人們對於鼻咽癌發病機理的理解。傳統的知識告訴我們，單一依靠端粒酶的方式不能有效地對細胞永生化，需要其他因素的進一步參與。然而，我們實驗室報導了第一個通過端粒酶方式永生化的鼻咽上皮細胞系NP460hTert。隨著不斷地努力，我們最近又建立了三個永生化的細胞系NP361hTert、NP446hTert和NP550hTert，這些細胞系都是單一依靠端粒酶永生化方式獲得的。通過對這些細胞系遺傳學特性的分析研究，我們發現NF-κB的激活廣泛存在于所有這些永生化的鼻咽上皮細胞系中，進一步研究確認，阻斷NF-κB的激活能夠明顯抑制這些端粒酶永生化的鼻咽上皮細胞生長。值得注意的是，EB病毒與鼻咽癌的發病有著緊密的聯繫，而EB病毒編碼的癌基因LMP1又是NF-κB信號途徑強有力的激活子。在LMP1促細胞轉化過程中，活化的NF-κB信號途徑介導許多途徑，參與細胞惡性轉化。所有的這些研究都支持一個重要概念，NF-κB信號途徑的激活在永生化細胞和鼻咽癌細胞中都扮演中重要的角色。然而，在永生化的鼻咽上皮細胞中，目前我們仍然不清楚持續激活NF-κB的機制，以及NF-κB活化后的功能。我們將致力于闡釋特異的NF-κB激活途徑以及對NF-κB激活的調節機制。尤其是，我們將在永生化的鼻咽上皮細胞中，明確p16和EGFR蛋白與NF-κB的相互作用機理。綜上所述，我們實驗室的端粒酶永生化的鼻咽上皮細胞系，為我們提供了一個獨特的優勢來探討和研究NF-κB信號途徑在鼻咽癌發生早期的作用。

779810.label: Realisation of objectives
779810.value: Objective 1: We have demonstrated canonical activation of NF-kB signaling in three out of three nasopharyngeal epithelial cell lines (NP361, NP460, NP550) immortalized by telomerase (hTert) alone. In contrast, NF-kB signaling was not detected in primary culture of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Activation of NF-kB signaling was demonstrated by phosphorylation of IkB (the NF-kB inhibitor) and nuclear translocation of NF-kB subunits ( p65 and p50). Activation of NF-kB was observed at early stage of immortalization but is independent of telomerase activation. The common constitutive activation of NF-kB activation in immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells suggests that it facilitates the immortalization action of telomerase. Objective 2: We examined the effects of inhibition of NF-kB activation on growth and survival of immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells by (a) over expression of the NF-kB inhibitor, IkB and (b) silencing the p65 subunit by shRNA approach; both of which effectively inhibited the proliferation properties of all the three immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cell lines examined as indicated by the inhibition of thymidine uptake (a reflection of inhibition of DNA synthesis and cell proliferation). Hence NF-kB activation is required to maintain the proliferative properties of telomerase immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. We also observed several of the downstream events of NF-kB activation including IL6, cyclin D1 and c-myc were also down-regulated upon inhibition of NF-kB activation. Objective 3. We activate NF-kB by expressing the EBV-encoded LMP1 and telomerase (hTert) which resulted in the immortalization of a primary nasopharyngeal epithelial cell line (NP44). Examination of signaling pathways revealed activation of NF-kB in the LMP1/hTert-immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Inhibition of NF-kB suppressed the growth of LMP1/hTert immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Interestingly, EGFR receptor is over expressed in LMP1/hTert immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. We also observed strong activation of mTOR by LMP1 in the immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Objective 4. We observed that EGFR over expression in the immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells is the major driving force of NF-kB activation. EGFR activation and its downstream events, including activation MEK and ERK drive mTOR activation. Inhibition of EGFR by antibody against EGFR and specific inhibitor against EGFR signaling as well as inhibition of mTOR by Rapamycin completely inhibited NFkB signaling and cell proliferation. Hence, an activation of EGFR/IKK/mTOR pathwaymay drive constitutive activation of NF-kB in immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. A manuscript about the significance of activation of NF-kB in immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells have been submitted to Internal Journal of Cancer and has received positive review. The Editor has invited resubmission of the manuscript with some revisions recommended.

779810.label: Major findings and research outcome
779810.value: Major findings: This is the first report of constitutive activation of NF-kB involved in immortalization of human epithelial cells. The involvement of NF-kB activation in immortalized human nasopharyngeal epithelial cells is particularly relevant to the pathogenesis of nasopharyngeal carcinoma which is closely associated with EBV infection. The EBV-encoded LMP1 is a potent activator of NF-kB. Expression of this viral oncogene will facilitate immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Incidentally, LMP1 expression extends the life span and facilitate immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells which support a role of EBV infection in development of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. In this study, we showed that EGFR over expression and its downstream activation of IKK which in turn activates mTOR will lead to activation of NF-kB in immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. In contrary, inhibition of EGFR, mTOR or NF-kB inhibited growth of immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Findings from Objective 1, 2 and 4 are related to the role of NFkB in immortalization and have been submitted for publication to International Journal of Cancer. It has been favorably reviewed and resubmission is invited with some revision recommended. We intend to resubmit the revised manuscript in June, 2015 and will update the RGC for the final status of this manuscript. The submitted manuscript and the decision letter plus reviewer's comments are attached in this report. Immortalization is a pre-requisite of malignant transformation. Defining the early events involved in immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells may reveal early events involved in development of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. In this study, we showed that activation of NF-kB through EGFR over expression and mTOR activation plays an important role in immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Activation of EGFR by the EBV-encoded LMP1 has been well documented. We were able to demonstrate that EGFR over expression was induced by LMP1 in the immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Furthermore, we observed LMP could also activate mTOR. Interestingly, we found that many malignant properties LMP1 expressed which is mediated by NF-kb could be effectively blocked by mTOR inhibitor. Our findings indicate the involvement of mTOR in mediating the pathologic role of EBV infection through activation of NF-kB in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Another manuscript on how LMP1 activates mTOR is under preparation for submission to Journal of Virology ( manuscript draft is attached in this report).

779810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
779810.value: The establishment of immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells have provided valuable tools for understanding events involved in EBV infection and its role in pathogenesis of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The characterization of these underlying events contributed to our understanding of disease mechanisms of NPC. In NPC, expression of LMP1 encoded in premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cells by EBV contributes to activation NF-kB. Many pathogenic properties of LMP1 are mediated via NF-kB activation. Our study showed the mTOR may be the key signaling pathway mediating the myriad pathogenic properties of LMP1. The involvement of mTOR in mediating the pathogenic property of EBV has not been previously reported and is under active pursue in our laboratory. The important role of mTOR in immortalization and activation of NF-kB in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells may suggest a novel target for control of growth and metastatic property of nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

779810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
779810.value: Immortalization is a pre-requisite property of cancer cells. Events leading to immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells may reveal early events involved in the development of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is 100% associated with EBV infection. The LMP1 is encoded by EBV in infected nasopharyngeal carcinoma and has been shown to have oncogenic property. Many of LMP1 properties are mediated by NF-kB activation. Our study showed that NF-kB activation supports immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells which is concordant with our earlier findings that LMP1 could immortalize nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. We identify that NF-kB activation in immortalized nasopharyngeal requires mTOR activation which is mediated by over expression of EGFR. Interestingly, both mTOR activation and EGFR over expression are induced by LMP1. Our study suggested that nasopharyngeal epithelial cells are susceptible to the action of mTOR and EGFR activation which support growth and proliferation. Our findings support the involvement of EBV infection in the development of NPC, particularly at its early stage of pathogenesis. The dependency of immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells on NF-kB, EGFR and mTOR activation may reveal novel targets for NPC treatment and prevention.

780110.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780110.value: 儘管最新的藥物治療和冠脈血運重建術能減少急性心肌梗死（MI）患者的死亡率，但是多達三分之一存活下來的心肌梗死患者存在心力衰竭，極大的影響了患者的生存品質。祖幹細胞（progenitor stem cell）是目前急性心肌梗死後心力衰竭心臟修復治療重要的研究方向，在這方面，我們臨床研究小組和其他研究團隊最新的研究結果表明，不同類型的幹細胞，特別是骨髓衍生的幹細胞能改善心肌梗死後心力衰竭患者的心功能。然而，自體成體幹細胞不但來源受限，獲得的數量少，而且分化成新的心肌組織和修復損傷心肌能力有限, 人體胚胎幹細胞（ESC）具有多向分化成多種組織和修復多種組織的潛能，但是ESC分化的倫理問題和產生的免疫排斥反應是需要解決的障礙。 Yamanaka等在誘導多能幹細胞(iPSc)取得了重大技術突破，通過一種創新的方法無限提供患者需要的特異性幹細胞進行心臟修復。人體iPSc可以從體細胞獲取，例如將一種高表達ESC的轉錄因數導入分化的皮膚成纖維細胞，獲得類似於ESC的iPSc細胞。iPSc功能上難於與ESC辨別，能夠分化成心肌細胞（CMs）。最新研究表明，自體成纖維細胞衍生的iPSc移植到有免疫活性的小鼠，可以實現原位心臟，平滑肌和內皮細胞組織的再生，改善心肌梗死後的心臟功能 。然而，這種自體iPSc導入的重組技術的治療的主要優勢至今並沒有報導。 我們研究小組最新報導了採用一種心臟大小、解剖和生理學都類似於人類，能複製出人類臨床疾病模型的特殊的豬的iPSc移植分化的研究結果，這是一個重要的發現，因為雖然經過了長期的實驗，但是以前並未真正成功的在豬身上進行ESC的分化。豬的iPSc的分化像我們以前觀察到鼠的iPSc的分化，有標準的多向分化性，有沿著向多種組織系統分化的能力。這種個性化的豬進行iPSc細胞移植治療與人類患者進行細胞移植治療的作用過程相似，可以用來進行細胞移植治療的試驗。iPSc與ESC細胞相似，iPSc的多向分化存在形成畸胎瘤的風險，這個過程可以通過iPSc向心肌細胞分化的過程中抑制多能基因來降低畸胎瘤形成, 但是由此卻可能增加由於分化未成熟表型心肌細胞導致的心律失常發生的危險。人的iPSc的移植治療也存在同樣的風險，優秀的豬的動物模型的建立應該消除那些風險因素的存在。值得注意的是，至今在心肌梗死和心力衰竭的大動物模型中沒有個性化iPSc的細胞移植和iPSc分化心肌細胞對功能影響和心律失常風險性（安全性）評價。這裏，我們建議調查與臨床相關的心肌梗死和心力衰竭的大型動物模型在移植iPSc和 iPSc分化心肌細胞的作用過程中的有效性和安全性，評價個性化幹細胞移植的優勢，利用我們已經具有的領先的人類胚胎幹細胞和心臟分化的研究經驗，進行基於iPS細胞移植為治療手段，進行心力衰竭治療的應用研究。

780110.label: Realisation of objectives
780110.value: To address Objective 1 and 2, we have successful generated porcine mode of ischemic heart failure (HF) and porcine induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) line. However, the major hurdle in this project was the differentiation of porcine iPSC line into cardiomyocytes. We have attempted to differentiate the cardiomyocytes from 2 porcine iPSC lines using lentivirus vectors generated from one farm pig and one minipig, respectively. While those porcine iPSC lines showed similar characteristics as human iPSC, we failed to differentiate them into beating cardiomyocytes (CMs) using established methods (handing drop method, co-culture with END2 and small molecule) for cardiac differentiation in human embryonic stem cells (ESC) or iPSC. Then we further explored the cardiac differentiation from two other reported established iPSC lines obtained from Prof. MA Estaban lab (GIBH, CAS, China) and Prof. JC Wu lab (Stanford, USA) in which they were created by using retrovirus and lentivirus vectors, respectively (Figure 1). Unfortunately, we also failed to induce cardiac differentiation in both of these porcine iPSC lines, and thus our proposed experiment on the use of porcine iPSC-CMs in ischemic cardiomyopathy is not feasible. Next, we attempted to the transplantation of autologous iPSC created from 4 pigs after induction of myocardial infarction (MI) and HF. Unfortunately, all four animals died suddenly shortly after the transplantation. Therefore, we suspected that transplantation of autologous iPSC is associated with early mortality, likely due to cardiac arrhythmias in ischemic cardiomyopathy, and thus further experiment on the use of autologous iPSC was not tested. These findings showed that pig is not an ideal large animal model to investigate the therapeutic effect of iPSC-CM due to the difficulty to induce cardiac differentiation from porcine iPSC. As a result, we have focused to explore the therapeutic effects and safety of human iPSC derived mesenchymal stem cells (iPSC-MSC, n=6) and human ESC derived cardiomyocytes (ESC-CM, n=6) versus control (n=8) on treatment of ischemic cardiomyopathy in this project.

780110.label: Major findings and research outcome
780110.value: We first established a porcine model of post-MI HF in 8 pigs by rapid ventricular pacing and MI induction. Serial echocardiogram showed that LVEF decreased from 66.5±1.7% at baseline to 33.8±1.8% with induction of MI+HF (P<0.001), confirming the establishment of an animal model of HF (see Publication 2). This group of animal will serve as control. In another group animals (2 farm pigs and 2 minipig), we obtained skin fibroblast from ear biopsy and those cells were expanded in vitro. Cells at an early passage were transduced with lentiviruses vector encoding the Sox2, Klf4, Oct4, and c-Myc factors using a modified protocol using ROCK inhibition in serum-free medium (Figure 2). Colonies were picked and expanded. Alkaline phosphatase staining and immunofluorescence microscopy for ESC markers (Nanog, Rex1, SSEA-4, TRA-1-61 and TRA-1-81) were used as the initial screening to determine which iPSc colonies are fully reprogrammed (Figure 3A and 3B). Those iPSC lines formed teratoma after injection into immunodeficient mice (Figure 4). Unfortunately, we failed to differentiate functional CMs from porcine iPSC from our lab or others (See above), and further testing of porcine iPSC-CM transplantation is not feasible. Next, we studied the safety and efficacy of undifferentiated iPSC transplantation in porcine model of MI+HF (n=4). Unfortunately, all four animals died suddenly shortly (<1 week) after the transplantation, and thus further experiment on the use of autologous iPSC was not tested. To further explore the therapeutic potential of different cell sources derived from iPSC and ESC (See Publication 3), we sought to compare the effects of human iPSC-MSC (n=6) and ESC-CMs (n=6) versus control (n=8) on treatment of ischemic cardiomyopathy in this project. At 8-10 weeks after transplantation,serial cardiac assessment with LV dP/dt showed significant improvement in LV systolic function in iPSC-MSC treated animals versus control, but not in ESC-CM treated animals (Figure 5). Despite the use of immunosuppression agents with steroid and cyclosporine A, very limited (<1%) transplanted iPSC-MSC or ESC-CM could be detected in the myocardium. Nevertheless, transplantation of human iPSC-MSC and human ESC-CM did not result in teratoma formation or spontaneous ventricular arrhythmias. Moreover, there was no significant difference in the proportion of animals with inducible ventricular arrhythmias between controls versus those treated with iPSC-MSC and ESC-CMs. Therefore, we concluded that transplantation of iPSC-MSC was more effective than ESC-CM in improving cardiac function in ischemic cardiomyopathy. (Final publication in preparation).

780110.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780110.value: 1. As discussed above, the major issue in this project is failure to induce cardiac differentiation from porcine iPSC. To our knowledge, there is currently no report on successful differentiation of cardiomyocytes from porcine iPSC. Interestingly, it is also well know that porcine ESC lines are also much more difficult to establish. In the future, we need to explore different culture conditions or factors, such as physical method (Publication 1) to induce the cardiac differentiation of porcine iPSC. 2. The other major hurdle with stem cell therapy for heart disease is the poor engraftment and survival of the transplanted cells. Therefore, we are investigating different strategies eg induction therapy with MSC infusion, and biological scaffold to enhance cell survival after transplantation.

780110.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780110.value: Despite recent advances in treatment to reduce mortality of acute myocardial infarction (MI), up to 1/3 of patients surviving a MI develop heart failure (HF). This increased burden of post-MI HF has created interest in developing progenitor stem cell therapies for cardiac repair. Human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) can be generated from somatic cells, such as skin fibroblasts using a combination of defined transcription factors that is highly expressed in embryonic stem cell (ESC). iPSc are functionally indistinguishable from ESC, and have been shown to be able to differentiate into cardiomyocytes (CMs). Recent proof-of-principle studies have demonstrated that transplantation of allogeneic fibroblast-derived iPSc into immunocompetent mice can achieve in-situ cardiac regeneration and improve cardiac function post-MI. Nevertheless, the major therapeutic advantage of this reprogramming technology for autologous iPSC-based intervention has yet to be documented. In this project, we explored the safety and therapeutic effects of different cell sources derived from human iPSC and ESC in a large animal model of HF after MI. Our results showed that iPSC derived mesenchymal stem cells and ESC derived CMs are both safe for transplantation but iPSC- mesenchymal stem cell is more effective for improving heart function in HF after MI.

780210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780210.value: The modern world, characterized by food abundance and sedentary lifestyle, is witnessing a rapid rise in the prevalence of obesity. Obesity is a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, including coronary artery disease, peripheral vascular disease and stroke, which are leading causes of disability and death in Hong Kong. The metabolic syndrome describes the clustering of multiple cardiometabolic risk factors frequently found in obese individuals, including abdominal obesity, high glucose level, high blood pressure and abnormal lipid profile. Together, these contribute to the increased risk of cardiovascular diseases. There is a need to identify biomarkers, whether biochemical or genetic, that may allow early identification of individuals at-risk for the metabolic syndrome and eventual cardiovascular diseases, for targeting of preventive therapy. As obesity is a key component of the metabolic syndrome, serum protein markers or genetic variants that are associated with obesity are potential candidates as biomarkers for the metabolic syndrome and cardiovascular diseases. Obesity is characterized by the accumulation of excess fat mass. Fat cells actively secrete many factors, known as adipokines, that have effects on metabolism and inflammation and may play a role linking obesity, the metabolic syndrome and cardiovascular disease. There is also genetic influence on the development of obesity and recent genome-wide association studies have identified several obesity-susceptibility genes. Our previous work suggest that some of these genes are also associated with obesity in our population. In this study, we will explore the role of circulating levels of three adipokines (resistin, lipocalin-2 and zinc-alpha-2-glycoprotein), variants of their genes and three obesity-susceptibility genes identified from genome-wide association studies (glucosamine-6-phosphate deaminase-2 gene, fat mass and obesity-related gene and melanocortin-4 receptor gene) in the prediction of the metabolic syndrome in Chinese. We shall be utilizing the available database and samples collected from the Hong Kong Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence Study (CRISPS), the longest prospective population-based study with comprehensive cardiovascular risk factor assessment conducted amongst Southern Chinese. We shall also conduct the long-term 15-year follow-up of these subjects for assessment of the development of cardiovascular diseases and examine the role of the above adipokines and genetic variants as biomarkers of cardiovascular disease in our population.

780210.label: Realisation of objectives
780210.value: Altogether, 1618 subjects have returned for follow-up. There were 748 men (age, mean±SD, 59.1±11.1 yrs) and 870 women (age, 58.5±9.9 yrs). In the whole cohort (n=2895) that started in 1995, there had been 258 deaths; 278 subjects who refused to return; 85 subjects who changed their telephone numbers and 656 subjects who could not be contacted. We have analysed the clinical data, stored DNA and blood samples of these subjects. We have succeeded in attaining the four objectives: 1. We have investigated whether the circulating levels of various hormones such as lipocalin-2 predict MetS over 6 years in Chinese (CRISPS-2 to CRISPS-3). Lipocalin-2 plasma concentrations have been measured in 1925 subjects. We found that plasma lipocalin-2 concentration is related to blood pressure. We also investigated two other circulating factors, adiponectin and tumor necrosis factor-alpha receptor 2, and found that they could predict the development of diabetes. For ZAG (zinc-alpha-2-glycoprotein), we found that neither its serum protein level at CRISP2 nor its SNPs were predictive of MetS. 2. We have investigated the association of obesity-related genes, including GNPDA2, FTO and MC4R, with cardiometabolic risk factors and MetS in cross-sectional analyses (CRISPS-3) and prospectively over 12 years (CRISPS-1 to CRISPS-3). We studied single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the three obesity-susceptibility genes, rs10938397 (GNPDA2), rs8050136 (FTO) and rs17782313 (MC4R), in i) 354 subjects with and 994 subjects without central obesity at both baseline and a 12-year follow-up, ii) 2214 subjects (816 cases and 1398 controls) in an MetS cross-sectional case–control study and iii) 225 subjects with and 1221 subjects without MetS at both baseline and the 12-year follow-up. We demonstrated that FTO and GNPDA2 variants predicted persistent central obesity, and contributed to the risk of persistent MetS, in the Chinese population, further supporting their importance as obesity-susceptible genes. 3. Using Death Registry and Hong Kong Hospital Authority computerized records, we have been able to estimate the prevalence and cumulative incidence of CVD, including coronary artery disease, heart failure, stroke, peripheral vascular disease and cardiovascular mortality in the CRISPS cohort. We found that elevated circulating adipocyte-fatty acid binding protein levels predicted incident cardiovascular events at the 12-year follow-up. 4. We found that the combined use of serum interleukin-6 and C-reactive protein was better than either alone in predicting cardiovascular events in our cohort. Neither lipocalin 2 nor ZAG was an independent predictor of cardiovascular events, as protein or genetic biomarker.

780210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780210.value: We found that genetic SNPs often influence the plasma level of a hormone. This is useful for performing Mendelian randomization experiments, and the knowledge of the genotype helps in the interpretation of the plasma level of the hormone in individuals. We have confirmed the usefulness of C-reactive protein and interleukin-6 in predicting the development of cardiovascular disease, but importantly, we have identified lipocalin-2 and adipocyte-fatty acid binding protein as important players as well as novel markers in the development of cardiovascular disease.

780210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780210.value: Obesity is associated with hypertension, diabetes and abnormal lipid levels, which are components of the metabolic syndrome and risk factors for cardiovascular diseases including coronary artery disease and stroke. There is a need to identify biomarkers, whether biochemical or genetic, that may allow early identification of individuals at risk. In our long term follow up study of people in the general population in Hong Kong, we have found that certain hormones that can be measured in the blood (including adiponectin and adipocyte-fatty acid binding protein), and certain genetic markers (single nucleotide polymorphisms in the FTO and GNPDA2 genes) that can be detected in the DNA, allow the prediction of aspects of the metabolic syndrome and the occurrence of cardiovascular disease. In particular, we found that plasma level of lipocalin-2 was related to hypertension and its development, while plasma levels of adiponectin and tumour necrosis factor-alpha receptor 2 were related to diabetes and its development. We found that circulating adipocyte-fatty acid binding protein levels in the blood predicted cardiovascular disease at the 12-year follow-up. Our work further confirms the importance of obesity as a precursor to the long term development of the metabolic syndrome and cardiovascular disease.

780410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780410.value: The endothelium is a crucial regulator of vascular homeostasis, producing under healthy conditions a balanced array of substances with potent vasodilator, anti-aggregatory, anti-atherosclerotic and anti-inflammatory properties. Nitric oxide (NO) is the main endothelium-derived relaxing (EDRF) and protective factor. However, under pathological conditions, in particular spontaneous hypertension, endothelial cells become also a source of endothelium-derived contracting factors (EDCFs), prostanoids and reactive oxygen species. The occurrence of endothelial dysfunction, characterized by impaired endothelium-dependent vasodilatation, precedes and contributes to the development of vascular diseases such as diabetes and atherosclerosis and predicts the occurrence of cardiovascular events. Obesity is a major risk factor for endothelial dysfunction. Adipokines [bio-active molecules secreted by fat cells] play a critical role in obesity-related vascular disorders, but it is uncertain how the aberrant production of adipokines affects endothelial function. Lipocalin-2 is a pro-inflammatory adipokine which is up-regulated in obese subjects. Its plasma levels are closely correlated with various metabolic and inflammatory parameters [e.g. insulin resistance, hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia, and high sensitive C-reactive protein]. Mice with deletion of the lipocalin-2 gene (Lcn2-KO) show improved systemic insulin sensitivity, decreased inflammatory cytokine production and attenuated inflammation in adipose tissue. Replenishment with lipocalin-2 in Lcn2-KO mice increases circulating blood glucose and insulin levels, and causes insulin resistance, suggesting that lipocalin-2 acts as an inflammatory adipokine causally involved in the development of obesity-associated insulin resistance and the ensuing metabolic abnormalities. Recent findings suggest that both aging- and obesity-associated endothelial dysfunctions are prevented by lipocalin-2 deficiency. Lcn2-KO mice show better responses to insulin- and acetylcholine-induced vasodilatation in the aorta, but reduced EDCF-mediated contractions in carotid arteries. Based on this information, the present proposal is designed to further investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the vasoprotective effects of lipocalin-2 deficiency and to evaluate whether or not, and, if so, how lipocalin-2 participates in the development of endothelial dysfunction by affecting the balance between the release of NO and EDCF[s] 血管内皮是调节心血管动态平衡的关键。血管内皮细胞产生内皮舒张和收缩因子，抵抗动脉粥样硬化和发炎。在病理条件下，如糖尿病和动脉粥样硬化, 内皮功能障碍可以使得血管舒张功能受损。脂肪因子[由脂肪细胞分泌的生物活性分子]在血管疾病中发挥重要作用。Lipocalin-2是一种最新發現的促炎脂肪因子。它的血浆水平与各代谢和炎症参数[如胰岛素抵抗，高血糖，高血脂，高敏C -反应蛋白] 密切相关。Lipocalin-2基因缺失（Lcn2-KO）可改善小鼠全身胰岛素敏感性，降低脂肪组织生产的炎症细胞因子和减輕发炎。补给小鼠Llipocalin-2增加血糖和胰岛素水平，并导致胰岛素抵抗。最近的研究结果表明，Lcn2-KO小鼠对老龄与肥胖相关的内皮功能障碍有保護功能。本課題的目的是进一步探讨lipocalin-2调节血管内皮功能动态平衡的细胞和分子机制。

780410.label: Realisation of objectives
780410.value: All objectives have been completed. Mice models with wild-type (WT) or null lipocalin-2 alleles (Lcn2-KO) were subjected to either standard chow or high fat diet . Endothelial functions were evaluated using a Halpern-Mulvany myograph system. Blood pressure was measured by an implantable radio-telemetry. For Objective 1, we found that enhanced eNOS/NO bioactivity and decreased ROS were responsible for the improved vasodilatory activity of arteries in mice without lipocalin-2. The results were published in British Journal of Pharmacology, 2012 (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/21740414) and details included in the mid-term report. For Objective 2, the metabolism of arachidonic acid and the production of downstream metabolites were evaluated using solid phase extraction-coupled with HPLC separation and fluorescent detection, and validated by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. The results demonstrated that lipocalin-2 deficiency significantly up-regulated the level of 20-HETE but reduced that of 11,12-diHETE. Incubation with 20-HETE reduced the contractions induced by U46619, a TP receptor agonist, in aortae of both WT and Lcn2-KO mice. Furthermore, 20-HETE inhibited acetylcholine-evoked contractions in aortae and carotid arteries of eNOS deficient mice, and significantly reduced the prostacyclin production in arteries of WT mice under basal conditions and during exposure to acetylcholine. The anti-contractile activity of 20-HETE was prevented by the IP receptor antagonist, CAY10441, and by removal of the endothelium. These findings demonstrate that the increased production of 20-HETE explains the improved endothelial function in lipocalin-2 deficient mice. The results are currently in submission to British Journal of Pharmacology. For Objective 3, the molecular transformation and the pathogenic role of lipocalin-2 in causing hypertension were investigated. Mass spectrometry analysis revealed that human and murine lipocalin-2 were modified by polyamination. Polyaminated lipocalin-2 was rapidly cleared from the circulation. Adipose tissue was a major site for lipocalin-2 deamidation. The circulating levels and the arterial accumulation of deamidated lipocalin-2 were significantly enhanced by treatment with linoleic acid, which bound to lipocalin-2 with high affinity and prevented its interactions with matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9). Combined-administration of linoleic acid with lipocalin-2 caused vascular inflammation and endothelial dysfunction, and raised the blood pressure of mice receiving standard chow. A human lipocalin-2 mutant with cysteine 87 replaced by alanine contained less polyamines and exhibited a reduced capacity to form heterodimeric complexes with MMP9. Thus, polyamination facilitates the clearance of lipocalin-2, whereas the accumulation of deamidated lipocalin-2 in arteries causes vascular inflammation, endothelial dysfunction and hypertension. The results were accepted for publication in JAHA: Journal of The American Heart Association.

780410.label: Major findings and research outcome
780410.value: Main findings of the study are: 1. Lipocalin-2 is a hormonal factor causatively involved in obesity-associated cardiovascular dysfunctions; 2. Lipocalin-2 is polyaminated, and activated by deamidation; 3. Deamidated lipocalin-2 alters lipid metabolism and eNOS activity in the arteries of obese mice; 4. Upregulation and activation of lipocalin-2 is closely associated with adipose tissue dysfunction. Main Research Outcomes: 1. Five original research reports and two invited review articles published in internationally peer-reviewed journals, including the high profile journal JAHA; 2. Training of four PhD students (see Part C); 3. A number of oral/poster presentations in international conferences/meetings (see part C); 4. International collaborations with academic institutes as well as industrial companies for developing lipocalin-2-based therapeutics.

780410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780410.value: Obesity is a common risk factor for a cluster of inter-related cardiovascular and metabolic disorders [dyslipidemia, insulin resistance, hypertension, accelerated atherosclerosis and type 2 diabetes]. Lipocalin-2 is a blood-borne adipokine involved in the pathogenesis of these obesity-associated chronic diseases. In addition, lipocalin-2 is also a bacteriostatic agent that acts at the crossroad of host innate immune system and microbiota homeostasis. Little is known about the mechanisms underlying lipocalin-2 up-regulation in obese conditions. Our results demonstrate that human and murine lipocalin-2 protein are modified by polyamines. Polyamination of lipocalin-2 facilitates its clearance from the mice circulation, whereas deamidated (polyamine groups removed) lipocalin-2 displays a longer half-life in circulation than the polyaminated species and is accumulated in the walls of arteries to cause endothelial dysfunction and hypertension. Apparently, the pro-inflammatory function of lipocalin-2 is enhanced by deamidation. However, it is not clear whether this modification also alters the anti-bacterial function of lipocalin-2. Host innate immune system off-and-on is regulated by microbiota homeostasis. The presence or absence of certain types of bacteria may feedback on or directly modulate the polyamination/deamidation status of lipocalin-2. Thus, future study will focus on the elucidation of these interactions at cellular, molecular and animal physiological levels, which will provide valuable information on how the balance is achieved between host immune function and microbiota infection by timely controlling the inter-conversion of polyaminated/deamidated lipocalin-2. In a long term, since obesity and the associated medical complications, especially cardiovascular diseases, are imposing an enormous burden to our healthcare system, the study will shed new lights on the practical strategies of targeting lipocalin-2 as a potential therapy. We are actively seeking further funding supports from RGC for the continued research and development on this project.

780410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780410.value: Endothelial dysfunction is a major culprit for obesity- and ageing-associated cardiovascular diseases. Due to the earlier onset, endothelial dysfunction represents a robust diagnostic marker and a promising therapeutic target for cardiovascular abnormalities. The present research demonstrates that in obese and aged human subjects, the production and activation of lipocalin-2 [a molecule produced by fat tissue] is significantly enhanced. Disrupting lipocalin-2 gene expression prevents the development of endothelial dysfunction, hypertension and ischemic heart diseases. Thus, lipocalin-2 is a potential therapeutic drug target. Furthermore, the study reveals that the activation of lipocalin-2 mainly occurs in adipose tissues of obese animals. Activated lipocalin-2 cannot be efficiently removed from the blood circulation and is accumulated in arteries, in turn causing endothelial dysfunction and hypertension. The study has established a causal role of lipocalin-2 in obesity- and ageing-related cardiovascular diseases via modulating endothelial functions. Next, we will address how lipocalin-2 is activated and how to prevent its activation. Answering these questions will allow us to define a suitable path towards drug design and development by targeting the abnormal activation of lipocalin-2.

780510.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780510.value: 牡蠣是一種重要生態學和商業貝類資源。 他們有複雜生命週期，在期間游泳(遠洋)幼蟲選擇一個適當的基體，附有(定居)它，然後變形入水底成人。 這卓越的轉折從遠洋與水底生活迅速地發生以回應環境化工暗示并且有一高死亡率─經常歸因於惡劣的不僅當前影響他們的水產養殖生產全球性地，而且他們的資源管理的基體挑選─。 驚人地，幼蟲也交換他們的碳酸鈣殼biomineral從aragonite到方解石在這轉折期間。 最近，自然環境變動和人類活動導致可能影響這個轉折過程的一個動搖的和易變的碳酸鹽化學政權，它的作用和所有可能的幼蟲反饋機制依然是「黑箱子」。 當前，我們定量anthropogenically被駕駛的變化的作用在碳酸鹽化學(海洋酸化)上的在幼蟲發展和成長。 潮間帶的有機體幼蟲(牡蠣和眼鏡)看上去非常寬容對大範圍碳酸鹽化學可變性，即。 生長率和發展樣式是未受影響的。 然而，我們的最近的工作建議生理質量、解決幾新陳代謝的酵素率、表示和變形成功在碳酸鹽政權減少在或在aragonite飽和水平(<Ωarag)之下附近。 在這樣情景，被注重的幼蟲趨向到舉起更多碳酸鈣，也許強加重大費用。 我們，因此，假設在變形期間， <Ωarag將影響幼蟲解決行為和biomineralization，可能通過得出精力充沛地昂貴的生物化學和生理反應。 具體地，我們預言越來越少的Ωarag將減少蛋白質綜合性容量和生物化學的能量可利用為幼蟲解決，并且可能因而削弱他們的選擇能力正確的基體為解決。 我們也預言被列出的作用以上也許歸結於幼蟲努力維護相對地自然aragonite和方解石降水率以增加的努力應付減少Ωarag。 在這個提案，我們使用商業牡蠣(巨蠣屬hongkongensis)在香港的牡蠣文化區域的將檢驗這些假設通過暴露他們的幼蟲在各種各樣的治療仿造自然和計劃的碳酸鹽化學政權。 幼蟲從每種治療將使用到(1)使用挑選生物鑒定審查他們的有差別解決行為， (2)探針他們的biomineral構成和動力學通過定量碳酸鈣多形體使用X-射線衍射計(XRD)和(3)研究他們的生化，即。 RNA/DNA比率、精力充沛的方面、酶活性和選擇的biomineralization蛋白質的表示水平使用proteomic和immunoblot技術。 這學科(幼蟲生物和biomineralogy)合作將幫助我們審查機制，藉以改變的港灣碳酸鹽化學能影響當前下降趨勢牡蠣幼蟲解決(種子生產)在中國南方沿海水域。 它在當地商業牡蠣也將使我們，第一次，學習幼蟲變形和biomineralization在自然以及給他們強加的計劃的情況由全球性環境變動和二氧化碳排放。

780510.label: Realisation of objectives
780510.value: We have successfully addressed all the three goals of this proposal. Importantly, we have trained 3 PhD students and a post doc, established a strong interdisciplinary collaborative platform for ocean acidification (OA) studies, published 7 papers (4 published and 3 under review) and presented the results in >15 international conferences (including 6 invited talks by the PI and rest by the students). Results obtained have also helped us to secure three more GRF grants and couple of HKU grants. There are three distinct goals in this project: oyster larval metamorphosis, biomineralization and biochemistry responses to OA. These three goals have been addressed through interdisciplinary collaboration as set in the proposal. To achieve our goals, we have 1) used the larvae of the Hong Kong native and commercially important species C. hongkongensis as model to investigate OA impact on targeted response variables. The response variables measured using standard procedures and importantly we have intensively used biomineralization and proteomics tools to understand mechanisms behind the observed OA responses (e.g. metamorphosis and growth). During this project we successfully used for the first time the materials science tool, X-ray diffraction patterns to understand OA impact (Chan et al 2013). Additionally, we have also employed several advanced engineering tools such as FTIR, ICP, nanoindentation, micro CT and Raman spectroscopy (Ko et al 2013). Similarly, for the first time, we have used both gel based and gel-free proteomics tools such as two dimensional electrophoresis and 2D nano LC/MS (i-TRAQ labeled) based quantitative proteomics (Dinesh et al 2013) in OA research. As proposed, we have also used immunoblot techniques to study the expression pattern of selected proteins to some extent, and identified protein expression signatures for OA stress. Nevertheless, we could not use the immunoblot techniques to trace the expression pattern of biomineralization specific proteins because there were no commercially available antibiotics for oyster proteins. However, this difficulty was overcome by using transcriptome and RT-PCR approaches (Dinesh et al 2014 under review). Thus, our experimental approaches have helped us to achieve all the three goals of this project in time.

780510.label: Major findings and research outcome
780510.value: Oysters have an incredibly complex life-cycle with metamorphic process that transforms swimming larva to sessile adult in minutes. This transition is perhaps the most challenging step because larva must simultaneously choose the right place, switch their molecular machinery to suit sessile life and to build calcite shells instead of aragonite larval shells through sophisticated calcification mechanisms. Therefore, this project specifically addressed how oyster larvae can cope with OA stress. Our series of experiments have led to the following findings: 1. Proved that OA will affect larval settlement behavior and biomineralization during metamorphosis, possibly through eliciting energetically costly biochemical and physiological responses, 2. Against our speculation, OA have not decreased the protein synthetic capacity and biochemical energy available for larval metamorphosis, and consequently could not impair their ability to select the right substrate for settlement, 3. Series of proteomics experiments demonstrated that the oyster larval proteome was significantly altered by OA, i.e. the number of expressed proteins and their phosphorylation level decreased, proteins involved in larval energy metabolism and calcification were down-regulated, and cell motility and production of cytoskeletal proteins were increased, 4. Our results supported the hypothesis that the oyster larvae are vulnerable to the interactions of OA with reduced salinity and warming in coastal waters now and in the future, 5. The pre-adapted ability to resist a wide range of OA conditions may provide some oyster species with the necessary tolerance levels to withstand rapid OA changes over the coming century. 6. We hypothesized that under OA, the larvae produce an impaired and mechanically weaker shell. However, contrary to our hypothesis, larvae produced 4-fold harder and stiffer shells at OA. It seems that larvae physiologically overreact to OA by producing harder shells, 7. Using the newly annotated complete genome information of the Pacific oyster and the quantitative proteomics approach (iTRAQ labeling followed by LC-MS analysis with LTQ-Orbitrap), the interactive effects of OA, warming and freshening on proteome of the oyster larvae was examined, 8. Comparative proteome analysis indicated that elevations of metabolic process and stress-related proteins are essential for acclimation to OA. Although the expressions of cytoskeletal and signal transduction proteins were down-regulated in response to OA, there were no marked alternations in developmental pattern and importantly in larval metamorphic success. These results suggest that the C. hongkongensis possess an acclimation mechanism at proteome level to tolerate near-future OA scenarios.

The primary aim of this symposium is to form a multidisciplinary group involving scientists, seafood consumers and oyster growers to conserve edible oysters through scientific approaches. 2. 780510.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780510.value: Oyster consumption is expected to rise with the increasing human population. However, ocean acidification (OA) is threatening oyster survival, e.g., the collapse of oyster production in the United States. This is a serious warning to China, which produces >80% of the world’s oysters. The invasive oysters (Pacific and Portuguese) appear to be winners and they may have the capacity to invade and replace the native Hong Kong oyster. A mechanistic understanding gained from this project on the effect of OA on Hong Kong oyster is a pressing issue for oyster farmers in South China and policy makers of Asia. OA altered oyster physiology to cope with OA through adjusting protein expression. Such proteome wide stress related alterations could have provided Hong Kong oyster necessary physiological plasticity to deal with OA. We have successfully used the high-resolution shotgun proteomics technology to understand how the oyster larval proteome was altered to cope with OA. We have identified thousands of proteins with high confidence and also quantitatively mapped molecular pathways used by them to tackle OA. Thus this project answered some of the challenging questions through integrating the rapidly advancing proteomics with larval biology in this era of multidisciplinary collaboration.

781410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
781410.value: 生长激素（GH）是垂体前叶分泌的一种非常重要的激素，它可以通过调控肝脏中类胰岛素增长因子I（IGF-I）的生成量来影响生物体的生长和代谢，GH调节IGF-I的机理构成了“生长调节素”假说的基础。肝脏是GH的主要靶器官，同时也是胰腺激素如胰高血糖素的靶器官，这一现象说明生长轴可能与调节体内能量平衡的胰腺激素存在一定的关联。我们最近以草鱼肝细胞为模型的研究发现，在肝脏中胰高血糖素能够通过直接作用来提升GH诱导的IGF-I的表达量。另外，我们还发现经过胰高血糖素处理后，GH受体（GHR）的基因和蛋白的表达量都有所增加。在利用GH或胰高血糖素单独处理的初始阶段，细胞因子信号传导抑制蛋白3 (SOCS3)的转录水平表现出短暂的增加，并且在胰高血糖素和GH协同处理下SOCS3基因的表达量也出现了显著的升高。因为SOCS3能够负反馈调节JAK2/STAT5信号通路，所以我们的发现显示在草鱼肝脏中胰高血糖素能对GH功能进行双重影响：（1）利用GHR表达量的上调来增加GH的影响；（2）增加SOCS3表达量来阻止过多的GH信号传递。基于初步的研究，我们认为在草鱼肝脏中胰高血糖素诱导的GHR表达与它对GH诱导SOCS3表达量的加强影响均是通过cAMP通路及下游MAPK和PI3K进行调控。在本课题中，我们将做如下两项工作：（1）检验cAMP/PKA及其次级MAPK 和 PI3K通路和后续的CREB磷酸化在胰高血糖素激活GHR启动子，以及GHR转录表达和蛋白合成方面的作用；（2）阐明草鱼肝细胞中与胰高血糖素受体相连的cAMP通路和与GHR相连的JAK2/MAPK 和 JAK2/PI3K通路在胰高血糖素增强GH诱导SOCS3表达方面的协同作用。根据已有文献，胰高血糖素刺激GHR表达以及它与GH增强SOCS3表达的协同作用尚未被报道过，所以我们的研究将在体内能量平衡和生长轴之间的功能交流方面提出一些崭新的观点。另外根据最新的报道，SOCS蛋白具有肿瘤抑制剂的作用，所以我们在肝脏SOCS3表达调节机理方面的研究也可能会为临床治疗肝癌提供一些启示。

781410.label: Realisation of objectives
781410.value: Objective (1) For our study on functional interactions between glucagon and growth hormone (GH) in the carp liver, we showed that glucagon could markedly enhance GH-induced IGF-I gene expression in carp hepatocytes and this potentiating effect occurred with concurrent rises in GH receptor (GHR) mRNA and protein expression. Apparently, glucagon treatment could elevate GHR expression through activation of AC/cAMP/PKA and MEK1/2/ERK1/2 cascades followed by rapid phosphorylation of the transcription factor CREB. The MEK1/2/ERK1/2 pathway was confirmed to be working downstream of cAMP-dependent cascades and functionally coupled to PKA but not Epac activation. Furthermore, glucagon-induced GHR expression did not involve PLC/IP3/PKC and PI3K/Akt pathways nor other MAPK components (e.g., P38 & JNK). Objective (2) In carp hepatocytes, the half-life of GHR transcript was not altered by glucagon treatment, implying that glucagon-induced elevation of GHR mRNA levels might be caused by GHR gene transcription rather than modifications in its transcript stability. This idea is supported by our findings in alphaT3 cells with glucagon receptor expression and transfected with a luciferase-expressing reporter carrying the carp GHR promoter. In this case, GHR promoter activity could be induced by glucagon and this stimulatory action was mediated by functional coupling of AC/cAMP/PKA and MEK1/2/ERK1/2 cascades and subsequent CREB phosphorylation similar to carp hepatocytes. Glucagon-induced GHR promoter activity could be mimicked by CREB over-expression and inhibited by the dominant negative CREB mutant or gene silencing using CREB siRNA. These results confirm that CREB activation caused by cAMP- and MAPK-dependent mechanisms plays a key role in glucagon-induced GHR gene expression in carp species. Objective (3) At the hepatocyte level, glucagon not only could induce GHR expression but also trigger a transient rise in transcript expression of SOCS3, which is an intracellular repressor for GHR signaling through JAK/STAT pathway. In carp hepatocytes, glucagon-induced SOCS3 mRNA expression was mediated by AC/cAMP/PKA, PI3K/Akt/mTOR and P38 MAPK but not MEK1/2/ERK1/2 cascades. Interestingly, glucagon-induced SOCS3 gene expression could also be potentiated by GH co-treatment. This synergistic effect was dependent on JAK2/STAT5 signaling and AC/cAMP/PKA, PI3K/Akt and P38 MAPK cascades. Besides, GH co-treatment was also effective in enhancing glucagon-induced cAMP production, PKA enzyme activity, Akt & ERK1/2 activation, and CREB phosphorylation. These results, as a whole, suggest that glucagon may have a dual role in the carp liver, including a stimulatory role by increasing GH sensitivity via GHR expression and an inhibitory role via SOCS3 expression to trigger down-regulation of GHR signaling.

781410.label: Major findings and research outcome
781410.value: In this study, we have cloned and expressed grass carp GHR for antiserum production. With the new tools in hand (including real-time PCR and GHR Western blot), we have elucidated the mechanisms for glucagon potentiation of GH-induced IGF-I gene expression in the carp liver. The process involves up-regulation of GHR expression via functional coupling of AC/cAMP/PKA and MEK1/2/ERK1/2 cascades and subsequent induction of CREB phosphorylation to activate GHR gene transcription. Although Epac is known to be a key mediator for cross-talk between cAMP- and MAPK-dependent pathways, our data reveal that the cross-talk of the two pathways in carp hepatocytes is mediated by PKA but not Epac activation. To my knowledge, our study represents the first to demonstrate that (i) increasing GH sensitivity by up-regulation of GHR expression may contribute to glucagon potentiation of GH-induced IGF-I gene expression at the hepatic level, and (ii) functional crosstalk between cAMP- and MAPK-dependent cascades can stimulate GHR promoter activity & gene transcription via CREB activation in fish model. Apparently, glucagon-induced GHR expression also has an inhibitory component via SOCS3 expression. SOCS3 is a member of type II SOCS, which are feedback repressors for cytokine signaling through JAK/STAT pathway. Its functional role as an intracellular inhibitor for GHR signaling in mammals has been reported in recent years. In our study, we have cloned SOCS3 in grass carp and confirmed that SOCS3 over-expression could inhibit GHR signaling via JAK2 & STAT5 and block GH-induced IGF-I promoter activity. In carp hepatocytes, we have shown that a rise in SOCS3 mRNA level also occurred with glucagon-induced GHR expression. Interestingly, this stimulatory effect could be notably enhanced by GH co-treatment. Using a pharmacological approach, we have elucidated the signaling mechanisms for glucagon-induced SOCS3 gene expression through cAMP/PKA, PI3K/Akt and P38 MAPK cascades. Regarding the synergistic effect with GH treatment, signal enhancement through JAK2/STAT5 pathway and potentiation through cAMP/PKA, Akt & MAPK have been confirmed. Our findings, taken together, indicate that glucagon may have a dual role in the carp liver. On one hand, glucagon can enhance GH-induced IGF-I expression by up-regulation of GHR expression through MEK1/2/ERK1/2 coupling with the cAMP/PKA pathway. Meanwhile, glucagon can act with GH to induce SOCS3 expression in a synergistic manner via functional crosstalk of cAMP/PKA, PI3K/Akt & MAPK cascades, which may serve as an intracellular feedback for signal termination of GH-induced IGF-I expression.

781410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
781410.value: To shed light on the functional role of SOCS in fish model, we have also cloned the other members of type II SOCS in grass carp, including SOCS1, SOCS2 & CISH. Similar to SOCS3, all of these SOCS members could be induced by GH in carp hepatocytes, although no potentiating/synergistic effects could be noted with glucagon co-treatment. Functional expression of these newly cloned SOCS members revealed that they could all suppress GHR signaling via JAK/STAT and inhibit GH-induced IGF-I promoter activity. These findings indicate that GHR activation at the hepatic level can trigger intracellular feedback for signal termination via up-regulation of various SOCS members. This inhibitory component may also serve as the site of regulation/modulation by other endocrine factors (e.g., glucagon) or even immune signals (e.g., local production of cytokines). In our recent studies, we have a novel finding that pituitary expression of SOCS1-3 & CISH could be induced by somatolactin treatment. In grass carp, we have recently reported the presence of a local feed-forward loop for somatolactin-induced somatolactin gene expression at the pituitary level. Further studies are clearly warranted to investigate the functional role of SOCS as a feedback repressor for signal termination of somatolactin actions within the pituitary.

781410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781410.value: Similar to mammals, body growth in bony fish is controlled by the somatotropic axis with GH-induced IGF-I expression in the liver as a major component. In our study, we have the novel findings that (i) glucagon can potentiate GH-induced IGF-I gene expression in carp hepatocytes via up-regulation of GHR expression, (ii) the stimulatory effect of glucagon on GHR expression is mediated by functional cross-talk between cAMP- and MAPK-dependent cascades and subsequent activation of the transcription factor CREB, and (iii) glucagon enhancement of GHR expression & signaling also has a feedback component with synergistic interactions with GH to trigger hepatic expression of SOCS3, which is an intracellular repressor for GHR signaling via JAK/STAT. Our studies have provided new insights on the functional communication between energy homeostasis (via glucagon secretion) and somatotropic axis (via IGF-I expression). Since carp polyculture represents a major source of animal protein in Asian countries, our study on the functional components involved in glucagon potentiation of GH-induced IGF-I expression will help to establish a conceptual framework for future development of growth-promoting strategy/biotechnology in fish farming. Recently, SOCS proteins have been reported to have tumor-suppressing activity, new information on SOCS regulation may also have clinical implications in cancer treatment.

782610.value: 左心室結構和功能磁共振成像研究

782610.label: Co - Investigator(s)
782610.value: Prof Chow, Kwok Wing Prof Tse, Hung-Fat

782610.label: Project Objectives
782610.value: Establish DTI techniques to characterize myocardial fiber and sheet structure in isolated working hearts: We will develop and validate a diffusion-encoding, stimulated-echo pulse sequence in an electrically paced, perfused working rat heart model. This new technique will allow delineation of myocardial architecture in actively contracting hearts, permitting direct evaluation of dynamic changes in myocardial structure. Elucidate the structure-function relationship in isolated working heart under normal loading condition: DTI images will be acquired at end-diastole and different stages of systole to delineate dynamic changes in 3D fiber and sheet structure. Regional and global ventricular function will be measured with MRI tagging. Functional changes will be correlated with structural changes. Evaluate the changes in cardiac structure and function in postinfarct hearts: We will examine (i) whether postinfarct hearts (after LAD ligation) manifest limited changes in fiber and sheet orientation at systole in the infarct borderzone and (ii) whether this reduced capacity of reorientation is responsible for decreased contraction in borderzone. We will also evaluate changes in remote areas to examine whether heterogeneous structural remodeling is responsible for the differential functional changes in postinfarct hearts.

782610.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
782610.value: 早期的組織學研究顯示，左心室組成，不僅週向和縱向纖維，也間接地運行纖維。了解這個三維結構和收縮功能的複雜關係是重要和必要的。心臟疾病的進展往往伴隨著在心肌纖維結構破壞。這些變化常常會導致心功能異常。擬議項目旨在開發一個綜合磁共振成像方法，闡明左心功能的結構基礎。最近，磁共振擴散張量成像（DTI）已成為一個強大的和非破壞性檢查組織微觀結構的方法。我們的初步研究成功地實施DTI分析心肌纖維結構。擬議的項目將開發新技術，探討正常心臟生理和postinfarct重塑。首先，我們將開發新DTI方法表徵心肌纖維和負債結構的動態變化。其次，結合功能性磁共振成像評估標註，我們將運用這些MRI方法來闡明正常和梗死大鼠心模型中結構與功能的關係。心臟衰竭仍然是最昂貴的和普遍的醫療問題。擬議的研究，旨在提供基礎科學家新的探索心臟功能結構工具，並受益臨床科學家更好地理解和診斷心肌功能障礙。

782610.label: Realisation of objectives
782610.value: Objective #1 has been mostly achieved (95%) through careful formulation of MR data acquisition and analysis procedures, which are incrementally and experimentally optimized during the project period. These technical accomplishments have been published in mainstream imaging journals and leading MRI conference. These contributions have laid the technical foundation for the presently emerging clinical use of cardiac diffusion tensor imaging to investigate various types cardiovascular diseases. Objective #2 has been largely achieved (75%), with publications documenting the 3D laminar structures of myocardium in normal hearts arrested in systole and diastole and their functional correlation with strain findings from MR tagging analysis. However, diffusion MR imaging of isolated hearts was not very successful (i.e., not to publishable standards) due to the extremely fast rodent heart motion that was found to severely interfere with diffusion encoding process, despite our persistent efforts over last two years. These attempts include: (i) setting up an MRI-compatible heart isolation apparatus; (ii) optimizing the beating heart triggering with respect to MR acquisition; (iii) developing more rapid MR acquisition protocol; (iv) using post-acquisiton processing to recover signal loss that arises from the heart motion during diffusion encoding; and (iv) developing rudimentary gradient coil hardware to shorten the diffusion encoding duration during the heart beating. The last approach above presents the ultimate solution to this problem. Yet its correct implementation requires major system engineering of the MRI system, which cannot be realistically and successfully achieved during the project period due to large amount of funding required. It is noteworthy that this hardware based approach has been recently adapted by the research group at Martinos Imaging Center of Harvard University to tackle the diffusion MR imaging of beating rodent hearts. Objective #3 has been mostly achieved (85%) despite the difficulties associated with rapid heart motion as outlined above. In brief, the microstructural alterations in infarcted hearts have been documented and systematically examined. These published results laid solid foundation for future diffusion MR investigation of human patients with ischemic hearts, which are emerging. In addition, the optimal MR protocol parameters for detecting and characterizing myocardium infraction have been investigated and reported, directly yielding insights for future optimization of human cardiac diffusion MR. Lastly, our efforts in pursuing the technically challenging cardiac diffusion MR have lead to a number of diffusion MR methodology developments and applications in non-heart organs. In particular, our efforts have directly impacted the liver, brain and intracellular lipid diffusion MR imaging methodology.

782610.label: Major findings and research outcome
782610.value: 1. Objective #1: Successful formulation of MR data acquisition and analysis procedures to probe and quantify the laminar myocardium structure in 3D domain (X, Y, Z and time), as directly reported in journal publications 4, 6, 11, 12 and conference presentations 2, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16 in Section C. These contributions have laid the technical foundation for the presently emerging clinical use of cardiac diffusion tensor imaging to investigate various types cardiovascular diseases. 2. Objective #2: 3D laminar structure of rodent heart was documented and published, detailing the potentially close coupling between structures and functions at both local and global level, directly yielding insights into fundamental and complex heart physiology (as reported in publications 4, 11, 12 and conference publications 5, 10 and 11). Our research findings have contributed to our basic understanding of heart functions and structures. Furthermore, our results have motivated a number of leading MRI groups in several top academic institutions to pursue cardiac MR for functional and structural relationship in basic heart physiology. In addition, through our experimental efforts (including these unpublished efforts as outlined in Section 5.3 above), we have identified the gradient hardware improvement as the key solution to perform isolated heart diffusion imaging. This position has led to the development of high performance gradient subsystem for cardiac diffusion imaging at other leading institutions. 3. Objective #3: We have examined and reported the microstructural alterations in infarcted hearts in a systematic manner (journal publications 4, 11 and conference publications 5, 6, 10, 11, 12, 14 and 16). These published results laid solid foundation for future diffusion MR investigation of human patients with ischemic hearts, which are emerging. In addition, the optimal MR protocol parameters for detecting and characterizing myocardium infraction have been investigated and reported, directly yielding insights for future optimization of human cardiac diffusion MR. 4. Resulting from our pursuit of rapid diffusion MR imaging methodology, we have adapted our cardiac diffusion MR method for diffusion investigation in non-heart organs. These technical and scientific contributiosn have impacted the liver (journal publications 1, 8, 9, 13 and conference publications 1, 3, 8, 9, 19, 20), kidney (journal publication 3), brain (journal publications 7, 10, 18), and intervertebral disc (conference publication 17). Arising from this project, new research directions are being developed to investigate the diffusion of intramyocellular lipids in myocardium and skeletal muscles.

782610.value: 1. Diffusion investigation of intracellular lipids in myocardium: This new research direction opens up the possibility of directly probing the heart lipid metabolism in both normal and diseased heart in a noninvasive and longitudinal manner. 2. Improvement of current diffusion investigation/imaging of liver and brain: Fast diffusion MR acquisition and analysis have benefited and will continue to impact the ongoing optimization of diffusion MR protocols for clinical liver and brain imaging. 3. 782610.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
782610.value: Myocardial architecture in mammalian hearts is both hierarchical and heterogeneous. Understanding the relationship between this complex 3D architecture and the contractile function of the heart is essential to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of ventricular dysfunction and to identify optimal strategies for restorative interventions. To date, our understanding of the fundamental relationship between cardiac structure and function is incomplete due to the lack of appropriate methodologies for both functional and structural assessment. In this project, we developed an integrated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) methodology to elucidate the structural basis of left ventricular function in both normal and diseased rodent hearts. Using MR diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), we analyzed the myocardial fiber architecture in rat hearts under normal and infarcted conditions. We also documented the relationship of DTI-determined architecture with local cardiac function assessed by MRI tagging analysis of wall motion, providing insights into the complex heart physiology and improving our understanding and diagnosis of myocardial dysfunction.

782710.label: Project Objectives
782710.value: To develop practical sampling schemes and estimate the associated logistical requirement (in terms of surveillance capacity) for accurately estimating age-specific seroprevalence over the course of an influenza pandemic. To demonstrate (using simulations) that seroprevalence data can enhance the statistical robustness of transmission parameters when combined with more standard epidemic curve data (e.g. daily number of new cases) in the parameter estimation process. To determine how the optimal age-based vaccination strategy changes over time as population immunity builds up from natural infection over the course of the epidemic. To demonstrate that accurate real-time estimates of age-specific seroprevalence is an important determinant for the optimization of age-based vaccination strategies.

782710.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
782710.value: Surveillance of pandemic influenza has generally focused on measures such as daily number of new cases, hospitalizations and deaths. In contrast, very few resources have been invested in real-time surveillance of seroprevalence. Age-specific seroprevalence data can provide very useful information in several aspects of pandemic situational awareness. First, seroprevalence directly reflects the level of pre-existing immunity in the population at the start of an epidemic and the degree of spread of the disease (i.e. the attack rate) as the epidemic unfolds. Second, seroprevalence data are not affected by non-transmission confounding factors such as underreporting and laboratory capacities (as in daily number of new confirmed cases) and can enhance the statistical robustness of transmission parameter estimates (e.g. basic reproductive number) when combined with more standard epidemic curve data in the parameter estimation process. Finally, seroprevalence is a cornerstone for optimizing vaccination strategy because the latter obviously has a strong dependence on the level of population immunity that has been built at the time of vaccination. We propose to use mathematical modeling to quantify the potential benefits (e.g. the gain in accuracy of transmission parameter estimates and prediction of the outcomes associated with different vaccination strategies) and logistical requirement (e.g. the sample size, manpower and laboratory resources required for an accurate weekly estimate of age-specific seroprevalence) of real-time seroprevalence surveillance during an influenza pandemic. 流感大流行期間的監測通常只集中於每日的新增確診個案，住院和死亡個案。相反，很少的資源被運用於流感抗體的監測。 流感抗體的數據可以提供幾方面有關流感大流行疫情的重要信息。第一，抗體數據能夠直接反映流感大流行初期人口中的免疫力。隨著疾病蔓延，抗體數據能夠反映疾病蔓延的程度（例如，罹患率）。 第二，抗體數據不受與傳染無關因素的影響，例如確診率和監測資源限制。除此之外，將抗體數據融入流感大流行監測中能夠提高疫情監測和預測的準確性。 最後，疫苗接種對控制疫情的成效顯然和人口中的免疫力有密切關係。因此，抗體數據有助制訂疫苗接種策略。 我們提議使用數學模型來估計在流感大流行期間進行抗體監測所帶來的好處（如對傳播率的準確估計）以及對資源的需求（如每週抗體監測所需的樣本數量，人力和實驗室資源）。

782710.label: Realisation of objectives
782710.value: We demonstrated the potential utility and logistical requirement of serial cross-sectional serosurveillance using a Susceptible-Infectious-Recovered (SIR) model for a population of 7 million with 2 equally-sized age groups where the basic reproductive number R0 was 1.8 and the mean infectious duration was 3 days (which corresponded to an epidemic doubling time of 6 days). Age group 1 and 2 represented the high-transmission and high-severity group, respectively. Age group 1 was twice as susceptible to infection whereas age group 2 had an infection-hospitalization probability (IHP) that was 2-10 times higher. We assumed that that the time from infection to seropositivity was 10 days on average and the sensitivity and specificity of serologic testing were both 100%, respectively. We assumed that vaccination was 80% efficacious against infection. We used a convolution-based method for obtaining real-time estimates of incidence/IHP from serial cross-sectional serologic data and hospitalization data. Objective 1: We compared two schemes for allocating sero-surveillance capacity among the age groups: (i) uniform allocation and (ii) dynamic allocation by allocating higher capacity to groups with less reliable incidence/IHP estimates. We found that the two schemes had nearly identical performance and hence adopted uniform allocation for serosurveillance in the remaining objectives. Objective 2: With 100 serum specimens per week per age group, reliable estimates of incidence/IHP could be obtained 2 weeks before the epidemic peak. In contrast, reliable estimates could not be obtained from the epidemic curve data alone until weeks after the peak. Objective 3: If the objective was to minimize the reproductive number or final overall infection attack rate (IAR), then the importance-leveling scheme developed by Wallinga et al (PNAS, 2010), under which the age group that had the highest product of incidence and force of infection had higher priority to vaccination, was nearly optimal. If the objective was to prioritize high-risk individuals for vaccination, then the high-severity group should be completely vaccinated first before vaccinating any members of the high-transmission group. Objective 4: Incidence/IHP estimates obtained from sero-surveillance can directly be used to inform optimal vaccine allocation by (i) using the incidence estimates to implement importance-leveling scheme when the objective is to minimize the reproductive number and (ii) using IHP estimates to identify the high-severity group when the objective is to prioritize high-risk individuals for vaccination.

782710.label: Major findings and research outcome
782710.value: Incidence/IHP was estimated by (i) obtaining the shape of the incidence curve from the hospitalization (epidemic curve) data using deconvolution (accounting for the time between infection and hospitalization); and (ii) obtaining the magnitude of the resulting unscaled incidence curve by fitting the associated unscaled seroprevalence curve (accounting for the time between infection and seropositivity) to the serosurveillance data. Objective 1: Uniform allocation of serologic testing capacity among age groups was nearly optimal. We compared uniform allocation with dynamic strategies that allocated more testing capacity to age groups with less precise IHP estimates (see manuscript in part C). All strategies had similar performance in terms of the timeliness of reliable incidence/IHP estimates, hence we adopted uniform allocation in the other objectives. In general, confidence intervals of IHP estimates ranged from 0 to 1 (i.e. not informative) before the first seropositive sample was registered. The first age group to register a seropositive sample was typically the one with the highest IAR but not necessarily so because of statistical variance associated with small sample sizes in each cross-section of serologic data. Once seropositive samples were registered on consecutive days, the IHP estimate quickly zoomed to the correct order of magnitude with sharply narrowed confidence intervals. Objective 2: Using only epidemic curve data, reliable estimates of incidence/IHP could not be obtained until after the epidemic peak and, more importantly, depended critically on knowing the relative susceptibility and mixing matrix. With the addition of seroprevalence data, reliable estimates became available 2-3 weeks before the peak and, more importantly, did not need require knowledge on transmission dynamics for input. Objective 3 and 4: Importance-leveling scheme required two parameters. parameterized by the incidence/IHP estimates from serosurveillance resulted in reproductive number and final IAR that were much closer to their optimal values (obtained by assuming complete knowledge of the transmission model and optimizing vaccine allocation) compared to random/pro-rata allocation. When the objective is to prioritize high-risk individuals for vaccination, the group with higher IHP could be quickly identified within a few days once seropositive samples had been detected by serosurveillance in both age groups. Conclusions were not sensitive to assumptions regarding vaccine efficacy and sensitivity of serologic testing within their plausible ranges. Conclusions depended critically on 100% specificity for serologic testing which could be achieved by rising the seropositivity threshold at the expense of lowering the test sensitivity which had relatively little impact on the performance of serosurveillance.

782710.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
782710.value: We have not considered optimizing vaccine allocation to minimize the total number of hospitalizations, which depends both on the nonlinearity of transmission dynamics (as in minimization of incidence) as well as differential severity among age groups. Importance-leveling scheme will no longer be nearly optimal if the relative severity of high-risk individuals is high. Development of a novel and efficient allocation scheme for minimization of total number of hospitalizations will be a potentially fruitful direction for further development of the work done here.

782710.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
782710.value: We performed computer simulations to demonstrate that serial cross-sectional serosurveillance had the potential to provide reliable real-time estimates of the number of infections (incidence) and disease severity in an emerging pandemic. With 100 specimens per week per age group, accurate estimates could be obtained up to 2-3 weeks before the epidemic peak if the epidemic doubling time was longer than 5-6 days. We found that the simple strategy of uniformly allocating serologic testing capacity across subgroups was nearly optimal. The resulting estimates of incidence and severity could be directly used to determine what proportion of the vaccine stockpile should be given to different age groups under different objectives, including minimizing epidemic growth rate or final epidemic size, or prioritizing high-severity groups for vaccination. In conclusion, we have shown how to integrate serial cross-sectional serosurveillance with optimization of vaccine allocation by parameterizing the vaccine allocation scheme with incidence/severity estimates inferred from serosurveillance and epidemic curve data.
