782910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
782910.value: Myocardial reperfusion is the restoration of blood flow to an ischemic heart, which is necessary to salvage the ischemic myocardium. However, reperfusion after a prolonged period of ischemia such as after myocardial infarction results in oxidative stress and is a known causative factor of injury to cardiac muscle .Myocardial reperfusion injury is also seen after the use of primary percutaneous coronary intervention following myocardial infarction and this may account for significant morbidity. Consequently the prevention of this has recently been suggested to be an important therapeutic target. Brief episodes of ischemia and reperfusion given before prolonged ischemia protect the myocardium and is termed ischemic preconditioning (IPC). Although effective, IPC requires access to the coronary vessels which is not feasible in the majority of cases. Subsequently, attention has focused on modifying events occurring at the time of myocardial reperfusion (i.e., postconditioning). The concept of postconditioning (PTC) was introduced in 2003 by Zhao et al. (ref 8). They demonstrated that in vivo application of three 30-second episodes of alternating left anterior descending artery reocclusion and reperfusion, immediately following sustained occlusion, reduced infarct size. This effect is comparable to IPC. However, numerous experimental studies reveal that the cardioprotective effects of IPC and PTC are suppressed in the presence of some pathological conditions such as in patients with diabetes and obesity. In other words, the sensitivity of the diabetic heart to postconditioning is impaired and the mechanism for this is unknown. The release of nitric oxide (NO) represents one of the most important defense mechanism against myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury. NO is also one of the major mediators of PTC cardioproteciton. Unfortunately, the NO bioavailability in the myocardium of diabetes is reduced. Paradoxically, hyperglycemia-induced over expression of a NO synthase (NOS) enzyme called inducible NOS (iNOS) has been shown to lead to the reduced NO bioavailability in the myocardium of diabetic subjects. We postulate that iNOS over expression is responsible for the loss of postconditioning cardioprotective effect in diabetes. If this proves to be true, we will see if chronic inhibition of iNOS may restore the sensitivity of the diabetic heart to postconditioning. The proposed research aims, therefore, to identify the reasons why diabetics have this particular problem and strategies that could be used to restore this sensitivity. The proposed studies will facilitate the development of novel and optimal therapies. 心肌再灌注是对缺血心肌血流恢复的过程，而长时间缺血后的再灌注（如心梗后）往往导致氧化应激，此时的再灌注也被认为是心肌细胞损伤的促成因素和重要的发病因素，这在心肌梗死后的经皮冠状动脉介入干预研究中得到证实。因此对心肌缺血再灌注时期的干预成为心肌保护的重要治疗靶点。反复多次的短暂心肌缺血对随后更长时间的心肌缺血/再灌注损伤有保护作用，亦即缺血预处理(IPC)。但IPC需通过结扎冠状动脉手段发挥心肌保护作用，这在接诊的绝大多数临床心肌梗死案例中并不实用，随后人们把心肌保护的重点集中在再灌注阶段，如缺血后处理(PTC)。2003年Zhao等人首次提出这一概念，即对缺血心脏实施供血重建之前进行3个30秒为一循环的短暂缺血/再灌注,可减轻供血重建的再灌注引起的心肌损伤。PTC可产生类似于IPC的保护效果。然而，大量研究发现IPC、PTC的心肌保护效果在病态患者（如糖尿病和肥胖病人）中作用减弱，即糖尿病心肌对缺血后处理敏感性降低，而此作用机制尚不清楚。一氧化氮(Nitric oxide, NO)释放是对抗心肌缺血再灌注损伤保护机制中最重要的途径之一，也是PTC发挥心肌保护作用机制中起调节作用的重要介质之一，然而高血糖介导的诱导型NO合酶（iNOS）过度表达被认为是导致糖尿病心肌NO生物利用度降低的因素。我们假设iNOS过度表达是后处理对糖尿病心肌保护作用消失的原因，如果此假设成立，我们将进一步观察对iNOS长期抑制是否可以修复后处理对糖尿病心肌保护作用的敏感性。本课题研究目的是确定糖尿病心肌对后处理失去敏感性的原因以及提供修复此敏感性的方法策略，并为临床应用提供理想的治疗方法。

782910.label: Major findings and research outcome
782910.value: We have found that excessive iNOS activation (especially in diabetic status) plays an important role in excerbating myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury both in man and in rats (published) and that moderate iNOS activation (or reduding the degree of iNOS activation) may be helpful in diabetes. Further, we identified that protein kinase C (PKC) beta overexpression is a major mechanism responsible for myocardial iNOS overexpression and increase if myocardial peroxynitrite over production in diabetic rats (published). Based on these findings, we conducted further experiment and find that inhibition of either PKC-beta or iNOS can restore diabetic heart responsiveness to ischemic postconditioning cardioprotection (paper to be published). Current research outcome includes the publication of two original research articles respectively in: Clinical Science, Diabetes; and two conference abstracts, which are highly related to the original project objectives. Futher, we extend the study to explore the mechanism regarding the interplay between HO-1 (a major antioxidant and cardioprotective enzyme) and STAT3 (a key molecular in ischemic postconditioning) in diabetic rats with cardiac hypertrophy and dysfunction, which has led to related publicaiton in Crit Care Med (2014) and one publication in J Diabetes and Metabolism.

783010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783010.value: Insulin is the principal hormone that controls blood glucose levels through its multiple metabolic actions in the peripheral targets. Insulin resistance, which is defined as a failure of the major metabolic organs to respond to normal concentrations of circulating insulin, is the early event of diabetes, a costly disease currently afflicting over 250 million people worldwide. Since the skeletal muscle accounts for approximately 75% of whole body insulin-stimulated glucose disposal, insulin resistance in this tissue is one of the main contributors to hyperglycemia in diabetic patients. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of the insulin signaling pathways in skeletal muscle might help identify new therapeutic targets to develop drugs for treating diabetes and other insulin resistance-related diseases. APPL1 and APPL2 are a pair of closely-related intracellular adaptor protein with a similar structural organization. APPL1 has recently been shown to be a critical player in insulin signal transduction. We have demonstrated that APPL1 prevents insulin resistance and diabetes in mice by potentiating insulin-stimulated activation of the protein kinase Akt. However, despite their structural similarity, emerging evidence suggests that the function of APPL2 in regulating insulin actions might be opposite to APPL1. In diet-induced obese mice, we found that the expression of APPL2, but not APPL1, is selectively increased in skeletal muscle. Transgenic overexpression of APPL2 in mice impairs insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in skeletal muscle, whereas reducing APPL2 expression in muscle cells potentiates the metabolic actions of insulin. Based on these findings, we propose that APPL1 and APPL2 act as a “Yin-and-Yang” pair that tightly controls insulin responses and glucose metabolism. APPL2 is a negative regulator of insulin signal transduction, and its elevated expression in skeletal muscle contributes to insulin resistance and impaired glucose homeostasis. In this study, we will test this hypothesis by characterizing the metabolic changes in a muscle-selective APPL2 knockout mouse model established in our laboratory. In addition, we will study in great details the cellular mechanisms and structural basis whereby APPL2 impairs insulin actions in muscle cells. The results will expand our knowledge on the metabolic regulation of insulin in its largest target tissue skeletal muscle, and will uncover a new pathological pathway leading to insulin resistance and diabetes. The unique animal model established in this study might serve as a useful tool for in vivo validation of new drug candidates to combat the aforementioned diseases. 胰島素作為調控血糖水平的重要激素，在其靶組織內行使著多種調控代謝的功能。胰島素抵抗，其定義為主要代謝器官不能對正常循環濃度的胰島素做出相應的代謝反應，是糖尿病發病的一個早期事件，目前困擾著全球超過2.5億人的健康。由於骨骼肌組織大約承擔著全身75％的胰島素刺激的葡萄糖攝取，所以發生在這個組織的胰島素抵抗成為了糖尿病患者高血糖性狀的主要因素。因此，全面了解胰島素在骨骼肌細胞內的信號通路可能有助於確定新的治療靶點以及開發新的藥物來治療糖尿病和其他胰島素抵抗相關的疾病。 APPL1和APPL2是一對密切相關的且具有類似二級結構的細胞內接頭蛋白。 APPL1最近被證明是一個在胰島素信號轉導過程中起關鍵作用的分子。而且我們的研究結果也表明，APPL1能通過增強胰島素刺激蛋白激酶Akt的活化以防止小鼠產生胰島素抵抗和糖尿病的病癥。儘管二者的結構非常相似，然而新的證據卻表明， APPL2調節胰島素的功能很可能是與 APPL1相反的。我們發現，在飲食誘導的肥胖小鼠的骨骼肌細胞中, APPL2而不是APPL1的基因表達水平被選擇性的上調了。轉基因表達APPL2的小鼠表現出減弱了的胰島素刺激骨骼肌細胞的葡萄糖攝取，而減少 APPL2表達的肌肉細胞則會加強胰島素的代謝功能。基於這些發現，我們預測APPL1和APPL2充當一對“陰和陽”的調控因子來牢牢控制機體的胰島素反應和糖代謝平衡。其中 APPL2作為一個胰島素的負性調節信號傳導分子，其在骨骼肌中基因表達的升高，促進了胰島素抵抗的產生和糖耐受的降低。在這項研究中，我們將用我們實驗室產生的肌肉選擇性APPL2基因敲除的小鼠為模型，來驗證此假說預測的機體特異性的代謝變化。此外，我們會很詳細地研究骨骼肌細胞中APPL2損害胰島素代謝功能的分子機制和結構基礎。這些結果將擴大我們對胰島素在其最大的靶組織--骨骼肌中代謝調節功能的瞭解，將揭示一個新的導致胰島素抵抗和糖尿病發病的病理途徑。此中所建立的獨特的動物模型很可能成為一個特別有用的工具，用以在體內驗證新的候選藥物，以求治疗上述疾病。

783010.label: Realisation of objectives
783010.value: Objective-1: We have generated skeletal muscle-selective APPL2 knockout mice (APPL2-mKO, and comprehensively characterized the metabolic phenotypes of the mice on high fat diet (HFD) or standard chow (STC). Glucose tolerance, insulin tolerance and glucose-clamping tests were employed to measure the changes in systemic and local insulin sensitivity. Our results showed that APPL2-mKO mice on HFD had significantly lower fed glucose and insulin levels. Glucose tolerance and insulin tolerance tests showed a mild enhancement in glucose disposal and insulin sensitivity in STC fed-APPL2-mKO mice. Glucose-clamping test also demonstrated a selective elevation of insulin sensitivity in skeletal muscle of APPL2-mKO mice. Furthermore, we investigated the impact of transgenic overexpression of APPL2 in mice. Our results showed that the APPL2-transgenic mice display impaired glucose tolerance and impaired insulin sensitivity, further supporting the notion that APPL2 is a negative regulator of insulin signaling. Objective-2: We isolated both soleus and extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles from APPL2-mKO mice, APPL2 transgenic mice and and their Wt littermates for ex vivo studies. Our results showed that in APPL2-mKO mice on STC, insulin-evoked phosphorylation of Akt and glucose uptake was enhanced. Genetic ablation of APPL2 prevented the HFD-induced impairment in insulin-stimulated Akt activation and glucose uptake, whereas both muscles with transgenic expression of APPL2 exhibit impaired insulin-stimulated glucose uptake. Objective-3: We generated recombinant adenoviruses expressing FLAG-tagged full-length APPL2, BAR-APPL2 and PH-PTB of APPL2, and found that the cells overexpressing the full-length or BAR domain of APPL2, but not the PH-PTB domain, suppressed insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of Akt and subsequent glucose uptake. Subcellular fractionation experiment revealed that knockdown of APPL2 abolishes insulin-stimulated activation and membrane recruitment of Akt. Furthermore, we discovered a novel mechanism by which APPL1 and APPL2 modulates Akt activation by regulating ubiquitination-dependent plasma membrane translocation. Objective-4: We identified the Rab-GTPase-activating protein TBC1D1 as an interacting partner of APPL2. By using co-immunoprecipitation and mutagenesis, we mapped the linker region of TBC1D1 as the minimal binding motif. Proteomic analysis identified Serine-235 in the linker region as a phospho-Akt substrate (PAS) residue. Using an in-house anti-phospho-Ser235 antibody, we found that Serine-235 is phosphorylated in response to insulin in a PI3K-dependent manner. Using a TBC1D1 mutant in which Serine-235 was mutated to non-phosphorylatble alanine (S235A), we showed that S235A impairs APPL2-TBC1D1 interaction. Furthermore, by using advanced imaging techniques, we showed that APPL2 overexpression prevents insulin-stimulated membrane translocation of GLUT4, and such an effect is abrogated by overexpressing an APPL2-binding-deficient mutant TBC1D1.

783010.label: Major findings and research outcome
783010.value: This project allows us to identify the adaptor protein APPL2 as a physiological suppressor of insulin actions in skeletal muscle, which is a principal organ responsible for insulin-stimulated glucose disposal and a major site of insulin resistance in type 2 diabetic patients. The major findings were published in in Diabetes, PNAS and one paper in Biochemical Journal, as summarized below: 1. Unlike its homolog APPL1, APPL2 suppresses insulin-stimulated signaling and glucose uptake in skeletal muscle. Mice with muscle-selective knockout of APPL2 are resistance to high fat diet-induced insulin resistance in skeletal muscle, and exhibit improved glycemic control, whereas transgenic overexpression of APPL2 is sufficient to induce glucose intolerance and insulin resistance even when fed with standard chow. 2. APPL2 inhibits insulin-stimulated Akt activation by forming a heterodimer with APPL1. While APPL1 promotes the translocation of Akt from cytosol to plasma membrane via competition with tribble-3 (an endogenous inhibitor of Akt), APPL2 prevents such an action of APPL1 by forming a stable heterodimer. The interaction of APPL1 and APPL2 is mediated by their BAR domains. 3. APPL1 promotes the translocation of APPL1-Akt complex to plasma membrane via TRAF6-mediated ubiquitination. Lys160 located within the BAR (Bin/amphiphysin/Rvs) domain of APPL1 is the major site for its ubiquitination, which is catalyzed by TRAF6 (tumour-necrosis-factor-receptor-associated factor 6). Replacement of Lys160 with arginine abolishes insulin-dependent ubiquitination and membrane localization of APPL1, and also diminishes membrane recruitment and activation of Akt, thereby abrogating the effects of APPL1 on alleviation of insulin resistance and glucose intolerance in obese mice. Suppression of TRAF6 expression attenuates insulin-mediated ubiquitination and membrane targeting of APPL1, leading to an impairment of insulin-stimulated Akt activation. On the other hand, APPL2 blocks insulin-stimulated ubiquitination of APPL2. 4. APPL2 suppresses insulin-stimulated glucose uptake by inhibition of the plasma membrane translocation of the insulin-responsive glucose transporter GLUT4 via phosphorylation-dependent interaction with the Rab-GTPase-activating protein TBC1D1. Insulin stimulated TBC1D1 phosphorylation on serine-235, leading to enhanced interaction with the BAR domain of APPL2, which in turn suppressed insulin-evoked TBC1D1 phosphorylation on threonine-596 in cultured myotubes and skeletal muscle. 5. Substitution of serine-235 with alanine diminished APPL2-mediated inhibition on insulin-dependent TBC1D1 phosphorylation on threonine-596 and the suppressive effects of TBC1D1 on insulin-induced glucose uptake and GLUT4 translocation to the plasma membrane in cultured myotubes. Therefore, the APPL2-TBC1D1 interaction serves as a key step to fine-tune insulin-stimulated glucose uptake by regulating the membrane recruitment of GLUT4 in skeletal muscle.

783010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783010.value: With the support of this GRF and several other external grants, we have discovered APPL1 and APPL2, as a pair of “Yin-and-Yang” molecule that control insulin sensitivity and energy metabolism. The findings were published in Cell Metabolism (Cheng KK, 2009), PNAS (Cheng KK, 2012), Diabetes (Cheng KK and Wang Y, 2007, 2011 and 2014), Biochemical Journal (Cheng KK, 2013), and other journals. In the future, we will continue to use the floxed APPL2 mice generated from this study to explore the roles of APPL2 in regulating insulin secretion in pancreatic β cells and in controlling energy expenditure via its brain actions. To this end, we have already generated β cells- and hypothalamus-selective APPL2 knockout mice, and we already obtained funding support from Hong Kong HMRF and Mainland NSFC to support the studies. In addition, Dr. Kenneth CHENG from our group will apply for 2015/2016 GRF grant to explore how APPL1 and APPL2 modulate adipose tissue inflammation via its actions in macrophages. We will also collaborate with structural biologists to elucidate the structural basis whereby the APPL2 and TBC1D1 interaction leads to inhibition of GLUT4 translocation.

783010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783010.value: Insulin resistance is the primary cause of type 2 diabetes, which is currently affecting 380 million people worldwide. However, there is currently no cure available for this disease, in part due to our incomplete understanding of insulin actions and insulin resistance. This project allows us to identify the adaptor of APPL2 as a novel suppressor of insulin actions in skeletal muscle, which is the largest organ for glucose disposal in our body. Furthermore, we have uncovered a new mechanism by which the interplay between APPL2 and its binding partners APPL1 and TBC1D1 fine tune insulin actions and elucidated the molecular basis underlying their interactions. These findings will shed new light on the metabolic actions of insulin, and will be useful for the future development of more effective anti-diabetic drugs by targeting insulin resistance.

To characterize the functional effect of Cav1-mediated Met activation in HCC metastasis.
To evaluate the clinicopathological relevance and prognostic significance of Cav1 and Met expressions in HCC clinical tissues.

783310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783310.value: 肝細胞癌（HCC）是一種在東南亞特別普遍的癌病，在香港HCC所引致的死亡率更位列第二。由於HCC的復發率和癌細胞轉移較高，預後比較困難。因此，鑑定有效的生物標記不單能提昇臨床管理的效果，也可協助發展新的療法。小窩蛋白-1（Cav1）的命名是基於它作為細胞膜小窩的基本結構及功能元件。在焦點粘聯中能發現非細胞膜小窩Cav1，在其中參與焦點粘聯動力和細胞遷移。新的證據顯示Cav1與人類癌細胞的轉移有極強的關係。事實上，我們的研究結果顯示Cav1在轉移的HCC細胞株中的表達顯著增高。在生理方面，我們觀察到Cav1在人類臨床樣本中的非腫瘤肝組織，原位腫瘤和轉移的肝癌組織中的表達逐步增加。Cav1在轉移癌細胞中的顯著表達說明Cav1與肝癌轉移有關。從功能上來看，提高Cav1在HCC細胞株中的表達能促進細胞的生長，遷移和侵襲，也能促進腫瘤在小鼠模型中的生長，而抑制HCC細胞株中Cav1的表達則能妨礙腫瘤在裸鼠體內形成。我們的初步證據表示，Cav1調節肝細胞生長因子（HGF）誘導的遷移和入侵，並增強肝細胞生長因子受體 (Met) 在肝癌細胞中的表達。異常的HGF-Met信號通路在癌細胞轉移中扮演著關鍵角色，過度Met的表達更是一個肝癌轉移的預後指標。我們猜測Cav1在肝癌轉移中激活Met和其下游信號通路有著極其重要的作用。在這項研究中，我們目的是闡明Cav1在肝癌轉移中介導Met活化的分子學基礎及功能。我們建議 1）在肝癌細胞中劃定Cav1和Met信號通路的相互作用，2）利用體外活化實驗和原位移植模型，描繪Cav1介導Met活化的功能，以及 3）評估在臨床肝癌組織中的Cav1和Met表達的臨床及預後意義。據我們了解，這研究是首次探討Cav1在肝癌轉移中調節HGF-Met信號的作用。這項研究也將為Cav1在肝癌轉移的功能提供有力的論證。此外，臨床病理分析Cav1介導Met激活有可能產生深遠的預後價值以供臨床剖析之用。

783310.label: Realisation of objectives
783310.value: 1. To delineate the molecular interaction of Cav1 and Met signaling pathways in HCC Both Cav1 and Met were profoundly expressed in metastatic HCC cells. Using PLC cells as a working model, the protein and mRNA expressions of the Met were upregulated in PLC Cav1 overexpressing (PLC/Cav1) cells. With hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) stimulation, Met-ERK1/2 signaling cascade was transactivated. A notable increase and higher level of pMet was detected in PLC/Cav1 cells as compared to the control. The capacity for Cav1 to interact with Met was illustrated by their colocalization at perinuclear and cytoplasmic regions. Their colocalization in the early endosomes suggested that Cav1 might affect the endosomal dynamics and the subcellular localization of Met. 2. To characterize the functional effect of Cav1-mediated Met activation in HCC Cav1 overexpressing and knockdown stable clones were established and subjected to different functional assays. Collectively, our data demonstrated the salient contribution of Cav1 in promoting in vitro cell growth, anchorage independent growth, motility and invasiveness, as well as the in vivo tumorgenicity and metastasis of HCC cells. Extensive cell scattering was observed in PLC/Cav1 overexpressing cells upon HGF stimulation. The number of scattered colonies under HGF stimulation was increased remarkably. Such de-compacted colonies were not observed in control. To manifest the involvement of HGF/Met signaling in Cav1 promoted motility and invasiveness, we perturbed the HGF/Met signaling pathway by suppressing the Met expression and activity. Suppression of Met expression by siRNA against Met or inhibition of Met activity using Met kinase inhibitor SU11274 in PLC/Cav1 overexpressing cells largely suppressed HGF-induced migration and invasiveness of PLC/Cav1 cells. The number of scattered colonies formed under HGF stimulation was also substantially reduced. 3. To evaluate the clinicopathological relevance and prognostic significance of Cav1 and Met expressions in HCC clinical tissues Immunohistochemistry was performed in 106 paired non-tumorous and tumorous liver tissues and 31 sets of samples comprising non-tumorous livers, primary HCCs and extrahepatic metastatic tumors from the same patients. Cav1 was not detected in non-tumorous liver but exclusively expressed in tumorous liver. Cav1 overexpression was observed in 36% of primary tumors and significantly associated with venous invasion. Increase in cav1 expression was also detected in 35.5% of metastatic tumors when compared to the primary tumors. These observations suggested the promoting role of Cav1 in HCC tumorigenesis and metastasis. Met was also found to be overexpressed in HCC. However, significant association between Cav1 and Met was not found.

783310.label: Major findings and research outcome
783310.value: Clinical significance of Cav1 in HCC Cav1 expression was upregulated in non-metastatic HCC cell lines as compared to the non-tumourigenic liver cell line, and dramatically overexpressed in metastatic cell lines. The observation in human HCC tissues was in accordance with that observed in cell line panel. Cav1 was not expressed in non-tumourous liver but overexpressed in primary and extrahepatic tumours. We demonstrated for the first time the progressive increase of Cav1 along with cancer progression. Clinicopathological analysis further revealed a significant association of Cav1 expression with venous invasion. These findings collectively suggest the significance of Cav1 as a prognostic marker in HCC. (J Pathology 2012, AACR annual meeting abstract 2009) Oncogenic properties of Cav1 in HCC tumorigenesis and metastasis Overexpression and knockdown approaches were performed to characterize the functions of Cav1 in HCC. The promoting role of Cav1 in in vitro cell growth, motility and invasiveness was demonstrated. Moreover, Cav1 overexpression dramatically augmented the in vivo tumorgenicity and metastasis of HCC cells. Collectively, our data demonstrated the undisputable role of Cav1 as a promoter in HCC tumorigenesis and metastasis. (J Pathology 2012). Mechanisms underlying the oncogenic capacity of Cav1 To provide mechanistic insights, we examined the involvement of the HGF/Met signaling pathway in Cav1 mediated tumourigenesis. Our data demonstrated clearly the transactivation of HGF/Met-ERK1/2 signaling cascade in Cav1 overexpressing cells. Ectopic expression of Cav1 upregulated the mRNA and protein expression of Met receptor, thus sensitizing the HCC cells to HGF-induced cell growth, motility and invasiveness. We further pinpointed the ERK1/2 signaling to be the downstream of Cav1-mediated HGF/Met transactivation. Such unprecedented observation explained in part the oncogenic function of Cav1 in HCC and elucidated the signaling pathways involved. (Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver conference abstract 2010, Days of Molecular Medicine conference abstract 2010) Role of hypoxia-induced Cav1 expression in HCC metastasis Similar to Met surfact receptor, Cav1 was found to be induced by hypoxia. It was found that Cav1 was upregulated at both the transcriptional and translational levels. Its expression was also enhanced in the hypoxic region of tumor mass. The hypoxia-induced upregulation of Cav1 was found to be regulated by HIF1alpha. Functionally, upregulation of Cav1 promoted HCC cell migration and invasiveness. Using cDNA expression profiling, S100P was found to be the downstream target of Cav1. Hypoxia upregulated the expressions of Cav1 and S100P. Silencing of Cav1 abolished the upregulation of S100P under hypoxia indicating that Cav1 is the upstream regulator of S100P. Functional study also revealed that Cav1 augmented cell migration and invasiveness through S100P. (AACR annual meeting abstract 2011)

783310.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783310.value: The novel findings of our study provided a comprehensive understanding regarding the functional implications and mechanistic nature of Cav1 in HCC tumorigenesis and metastasis. Mechanistic study also provided evidence about the Cav1-mediated activation of Met pathway as the underlying basis of the oncogenic property of Cav1. Our data also suggested the capacity for Cav1 to interact with Met as illustrated by their colocalization at perinuclear and cytoplasmic regions. In addition, we identified the perinuclear region, where Cav1 and Met colocalize, to be the early endosomes. Colocalization of Met and EEA1 endosomal marker was revealed in our study and this finding has implicated the endosomal dynamics of Met regulated by Cav1. Endocytosis and endosomal sorting have been shown to be involved in the nuclear entry of surface receptor. The role of Cav1 in the internalization of Met thus warrants further investigation. Indeed, our data also revealed the presence of nuclear Met (nMet) in the nucleus of HCC cells. Emerging evidence has shown that the localization of Met is not restricted to the cell membrane and cytoplasm. Nuclear Met has been detected in different cell types. The functional role and clinical implications of nMet are awaited to be further investigated.

783310.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783310.value: In this study, we elucidated the functions and molecular mechanism of Cav1-mediated Met activation in HCC metastasis. Metastasis is a key event at the advanced stage of hepatocarcinogenesis. In light of the emergence of Cav1 as a new master of cancer metastasis in various cancer types and its undefined role in HCC metastasis, it is important to unveil the role of Cav1 in HCC. The current understanding about the molecular mechanisms of Cav1 in cancer metastasis is conflicting. Also, the underlying basis of Cav1 in HCC metastasis has never been addressed. Our work on dissecting the interplay of Cav1 and Met signaling pathways in HCC metastasis is original. To our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate the effect of Cav1 overexpression on Met signaling cascades in HCC metastasis. This study has deciphered novel molecular pathways contributing to the invasiveness and metastasis of HCC. The functional data obtained from animal work has provided the first in vivo evidence about the functional effect of Cav1 in HCC metastasis. In addition, the clinicopathological data obtained in this study has determined the significance of Cav1 as a prognostic marker and a potential therapeutic target for advanced HCC.

783810.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783810.value: Influenza infection in human may lead to mild to severe clinical manifestations. Infection with seasonal influenza and the newly emerged pandemic H1N1 influenza currently show 0.05-0.2% case fatality ratio. However, a 60% case fatality ratio has been reported for the H5N1 influenza virus, which has infected ~450 humans since its emergence in 1996. While H5N1 infection is characterized by severe pneumonia which may progress to acute respiratory distress syndrome; the detailed mechanism that leads to a fatal outcome after infection is not fully characterized. Clinical evidence suggests that despite of high level of pro-inflammatory cytokine response, high viral loads and lymphopenia were detected in H5N1 fatal cases, suggesting failure of host immune response in controlling viral replication. Pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) that identify pathogen-associated molecular patterns play an important role in sensing infection and triggering signaling cascades that induce inflammatory and immune responses. The hyper-induction of pro-inflammatory cytokines triggered after H5N1 infection may be a result of significant higher viral replication, differential recognition by PRRs, or both. PRRs including toll-like receptors 3 and 7, retinoic acid-inducible gene I, as well as nucleotide-binding and nod-like receptors have been reported to recognize influenza viral RNA at different forms. In addition to viral RNA, viral surface glycoproteins have been reported to interact with toll-like receptors and C-type lectin receptors (CLR). H5N1 influenza hemagglutinin has recently been shown to interact with dendritic cells-specific intracellular adhesion molecule (ICAM)-3 grabbing non-integrin (DC-SIGN), one of the major CLR expressed on dendritic cells (DC). DCs are professional antigen-presenting cells equipped with various PRR for antigen sensing and uptake. Immature DCs express a large variety of CLRs that not only facilitate antigen capture of immature DC and also serve as receptors for internalizing glycosylated antigens. As DCs play an important role in initiating innate and modulating adaptive immune responses, we propose to (1) systemically evaluate the potential interaction between influenza HA glycoproteins and major CLRs expressed by human conventional DCs, (2) to investigate if the surface glycoproteins of non-lethal and lethal influenza viruses trigger differential DC activation and maturation through distinct CLR signaling, and (3) to understand if the HA-CLR interaction will lead to downstream signaling and if it will modulate the TLR3 or RIG-I signaling pathway triggered by viral RNA. Identify crucial DC response for induction of effective adaptive immunity will help to improve our current therapeutic and vaccination strategies. 流感病毒感染可以在人類引發輕微到嚴重的臨床表現。 季節性流感與新興的 H1N1 流感感染約造成 0.05% 到 0.2%的病死率， 而H5N1 流感病毒自1996年起至今已經在全球感染超過450案例並引起約60%的病死率。H5N1 型病毒感染的特點是重症肺炎並可引發急性呼吸窘迫綜合症，然而導致患者於感染後致命的詳細的機制仍然並不明確。過去的研究顯示H5N1感染後的病患可以測得炎症細胞因子增高，病毒量增加，及淋巴細胞減少，這些臨床數據顯示宿主免疫反應在控制病毒複製的反應上失效。模式識別受體 (PRRs) 負責辨識與病原相關的分子模式 (PAMPs)，於偵測病原感染與引導信息傳遞以引發炎症和免疫反應上發揮重要作用。臨床上所見H5N1病患所表現出的高量的炎症細胞因子，可能是由於大量病毒複製所導致，然而H5N1病毒亦可能差異性的激活模式識別受體 ，因而誘發高量的炎症細胞因子。模式識別受體 包括 Toll-like 受體 3 和 7 ，視黃酸誘導基因 (RIG-I)，以及 Nod-like 受體，均以偵測流感病毒的 RNA作為感應病毒感染的機制。除了病毒 RNA之外，過去研究發現一些病毒的表面醣蛋白亦可與 Toll-like 受體和 C-型凝集素受體 (C-type lectin receptors) 進行交互作用。近期研究顯示H5N1病毒表面的血凝素醣蛋白可以與樹突細胞表面的一種主要的C-型凝集素受體DC-SIGN進行交互作用。樹突細胞是專業抗原遞呈細胞，因此樹突細胞具有多種不同的模式識別受體以感應並捕捉不同的病原。未激活的樹突細胞表面帶有許多的C-型凝集素受體，它們的功能不僅於感應並捕捉不同的病原，它們亦可以作為病原進入細胞內部所使用的受體。由於樹突細胞在激活先天免疫 (innate immunity) 與後天免疫 (adaptive immunity) 反應上均扮演重要的角色，本研究目的為 (1) 系統性評估流感病毒表面血凝素與人類樹突細胞之C-型凝集素受體之間的可能交互作用，(2) 探討非致命性和致命的流感病毒的表面醣蛋白藉由與人類C-型凝集素受體作用而激活樹突細胞的能力，(3) 調查病毒的表面醣蛋白與人類C-型凝集素受體作用後所引發的細胞信息傳道對誘發高量的炎症細胞因子的可能機制。研究結果將有助了解激活樹突細胞後天性免疫的有效方法，未來可應用於治療及疫苗的研發。

783810.label: Realisation of objectives
783810.value: The proposed research aimed to study the potential interaction between CLR and influenza HA glycoprotein. The first objective “Evaluate interaction between a panel of 17 expressed human CLRs and with noninfectious virus-like particles (VLPs) expressing HA derived from different H1N1 and H5N1 influenza viruses” was achieved by 100%. In brief, lentiviral-based pseudoparticles expressing the HA derived from seasonal H1N1(A/HK/54/98) or highly pathogenic H5N1 (A/VN/1203/04) influenza viruses were generated and were screened against a panel of recombinant soluble human CLR [CLEC1 (DCAL-1), CLEC2C (CD69), CLEC4A (DCIR), CLEC4C (BDCA-2), CLEC4E (Mincle), CLEC4K (Langerin), CLEC4L (DC-SIGN), CLEC4M (DC-SIGNR), CLEC5A (MDL-1), CLEC6A (Dectin-2), CLEC7A (Dectin-1), CLEC8A (LOX1), CLEC10A (ML2), CLEC12A (CCL-1), CLEC13A (BIMLEC), CLEC13B (DEC205), CLEC13E (ENDO180)]. Significant binding was observed for CLEC1, CLEC4C, CLEC4E, CLEC4K, CLEC4L, CLEC4M, CLEC5A, CLEC13A, CLEC13B, CLEC13E, among which only the CLEC5A showed significantly higher binding to H5 over the H1 pseudoparticles and was selected for further investigation. The second objective “Apply H1N1 and H5N1 recombinant influenza viruses with common internal genes but differed in HA and NA glycoproteins to study their effect on DC antigen uptake, activation, and maturation through CLRs” was achieved by 100%. We generated recombinant viruses of identical internal genes but differed by the surface HA and NA glycoproteins: A/PR/8/34 x A/VN/1203/04HA,NA (H5N1) (VN1203) and A/PR/8/34 x A/HK/54/98HA,NA (H1N1) (HK5498). To investigate if over-expression of CLEC5A would lead to increased viral internalization, we infected conventional CHO cells and the CLEC5A overly-expressed CHO cells and did not observe a significantly increased viral entry of either VN1203 or HK5498 recombinant viruses, confirming previous observation that CLEC5A would not facilitate Dengue virus entry. Since CLEC5A is not expressed on dendritic cells but on human monocytic U937 and PBMC-derived M-CSF-differentiated macrophages, recombinant viruses were applied to monitor potential host response after infection. VN1203 virus showed higher infectivity than HK5498 virus in both U937 and M-CSF-differentiated macrophages and induced higher level of chemokines and pro-inflammtory cytokines after infection. The third objective “Study the downstream signaling upon HA-CLR activation” has been partially addressed. Specifically, we have performed gene silencing of CLEC5A in U937 cells followed by infection with VN1203 virus. Down-regulation of CLEC5A using siRNA leads to a significant reduction of IP-10 and MCP-1 after infection with VN1203 virus comparing to the cells transfected with non-targeting siRNA controls. The signaling pathway is currently investigated by using specific pathway inhibitors by the PhD student whose thesis is due by August 2014.

783810.label: Major findings and research outcome
783810.value: Pattern recognition receptors including TLR 3 and 7, RIG-I, and NALP3 recognize influenza viral RNA to trigger innate immune response. In addition, viral surface glycoproteins have been reported to interact with C-type lectin receptors (CLR), which may also affect the host response after infection. The project aimed to screen for potential interaction between CLR and the influenza HA glycoprotein. Lentiviral-based psuedoparticles expressing HA derived from seasonal H1N1 or highly pathogenic H5N1 influenza viruses were generated to screen against a panel of recombinant soluble human CLR. While both H1 and H5 pseudoparticles showed binding to previously reported DC-SIGN and DC-SIGNR, we observed an increased binding of H5 pseudoparticles to MDL-1(CLEC5A), a type II transmembrane protein with a short cytoplasmic tail that binds to the adaptor protein DAP12 to rely downstream signaling upon activation. Binding of Dengue virus to CLEC5A was shown to amplify pro-inflammatory cytokine response leading to increased inflammation and vascular permeability. Western blot or FACS analyses identified high level of CLEC5A expression in the human monocytic U937 cells or M-CSF differentiated PBMC-derived macrophages. To investigate the potential effect between HA-CLEC5A interaction, we generated recombinant influenza virus of identical internal genes but differed by the surface HA and NA glycoproteins: A/PR/8/34 x A/VN/1203/04HA,NA (H5N1) (VN1203) and A/PR/8/34 x A/HK/54/98HA,NA (H1N1) (HK5498). We first observed that over-expression of CLEC5A in CHO cells did not significantly increased viral entry. U937 cells with high CLEC5A expression were infected with VN1203 or HK5498 viruses to evaluate if CLEC5A-HA interaction would lead to increased chemokine/ cytokine induction. VN1203 recombinant virus showed higher infectivity in U937 cells than that of the HK5498 virus, leading to increased cell death and higher level of cytokine (TNF-, IL-6) and chemokine (MCP-1, IP-10, IL-8) induction at 24 h post infection. Gene silencing of CLEC5A in U937 cells leads to a significant reduction of chemokines (IP-10 and MCP-1) after infection with recombinant VN1203 virus while compared to the U937 cells transfected with non-targeting siRNA controls. Overall, our results support a potential interaction between CLEC5A and the HA derived from H5N1 influenza virus, which could modulate cytokine/chemokine responses following infection with the highly pathogenic H5N1 influenza virus. The funding support has provided the opportunity to train one 4-year PhD student (PhD expected in August 2014) and the research findings were presented at the 17th Research Postgraduate Student Symposium at HKU.

783810.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783810.value: The interaction between CLEC5A and the H5 HA could potentially leads to improved control over host response after infection with H5N1 influenza virus. Previous studies demonstrated the effect of CLEC5A antagonizing antibody in blocking the interaction between Dengue virus and CLEC5A, leading to reduced inflammation and vascular permeability as well as increased survival in a mouse model. As human infections with H5N1 influenza virus often exhibit severe pneumonia with increased pro-inflammatory cytokines, termed cytokine storm, developing compounds that specifically block the CLEC5A-DAP12 signaling pathway may help to control the host response after infection with the highly pathogenic H5N1 influenza virus.

783810.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783810.value: Human infection with influenza virus may lead to mild to severe clinical symptoms due to differential viral –host interaction. H5N1 infected patients often exhibit severe clinical symptoms and hyper-induction of pro-inflammatory cytokines, termed cytokine storm. While viral replication efficiency and tissue tropism play major roles in determining the host response, we hypothesize that specific viral determinants may interact with host innate sensing network and affect host response after infection. Here, we applied lentivirus based pseudoparticles expressing the HA derived from H1N1 or H5N1 viruses, which were applied to screen for potential interaction between HA and C-type lectin receptors (CLR), a member of pattern recognition receptors responsible for pathogen detection and induction of innate immune response. We identified CLEC5A which interact specifically with H5 HA but not H1 HA, and observed by gene silencing that this specific interaction would lead to increased induction of chemokines including IP-10 and MCP-1. The results provide new insights for the potential mechanisms of hyper-induced host innate response followed by H5N1 infection. Identification of specific downstream signaling pathway leading to increased chemokine induction may reveal druggable targets for the development of novel therapeutic agents.

783910.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783910.value: Infertility affects 15% of couples worldwide. Assisted reproduction can partially overcome the problem. However, the success rate remains low partly because of our incomplete knowledge on reproductive events. Implantation is the most critical first step of reproduction in mammals. It involves apposition of the embryo at the blastocyst stage and subsequently its attachment onto the uterine endometrium. This is followed by invasion of the blastocyst into the endometrium. Each of these steps involves coordinated interaction between the embryo, the endometrium and its extracellular matrix. Our knowledge on human implantation is limited because of obvious ethical concerns. Mouse implantation model is therefore used in this project. MicroRNAs are a group of small ribonucleic acids (RNAs) that do not produce proteins but suppress the expression of other genes (target genes). Although microRNAs are known to be involved in many developmental events, knowledge on their roles in embryos before implantation (the preimplantation period) is scarce. We and others have demonstrated that microRNAs are differentially expressed in different developmental stages of preimplantation mouse embryos. One family of miRNAs termed let-7 shows preferential expression in oocytes and zygotes, but not in the blastocysts. Experimentally, blastocysts can be induced to become dormant without implantation potential (delayed implantation). Interestingly, dormant blastocysts have high level of let-7 and, when they regain their implantation potential, let-7 expression decreases to a level similar to those found in normal blastocysts. Importantly, the restrict requirement of a low level of let-7 at the blastocyst stage is also illustrated by our preliminary data that forced-expression of let-7 in normal blastocysts reduces their ability to attach and grow onto the extracellular matrix of the endometrium in an in vitro model of implantation as well as to implant in uterus after transfer into female mice. The hypothesis of this project is that a reduction of let-7 expression in blastocysts is critical for implantation. Specifically, this project proposes to study the involvement of three let-7 target genes, namely Dicer, Integrin beta3 and Vav-3, in mediating the actions of let-7 in the regulation of other miRNAs, attachment, and outgrowth of mouse blastocysts, respectively. The outcome of the project will enhance our understanding on the role of miRNA in blastocyst activation and implantation. The knowledge generated from the proposed study should provide useful insight for developing new strategy to enhance the implantation potential of cultured embryos and to increase the success rate of clinical assisted reproduction. 不育症在全世界影響15%的夫婦，輔助生殖能部分克服這一難題。然而，由於對生殖機理不十分瞭解，輔助生殖成功率還比較低。胚胎植入是哺乳動物生殖最關鍵的第一步，包括胚泡緊貼，粘附及侵入三個階段，每一步都涉及胚胎，子宮內膜及細胞外基質的協調相互作用。因為倫理方面的問題，我們在人類胚胎植入方面的知識非常有限。所以本課題將使用小鼠胚胎植入模型作為研究。 MicroRNA是一類非編碼小RNA，其功能主要是抑制靶基因的翻譯。儘管microRNA被證實在胚胎發育方面有重要的功能，但在胚胎圍植入期的作用卻少有報導。我們和其他研究人員的資料顯示在植入前胚胎中miRNA差異表達，其中一個miRNA家族，let-7家族，在卵子及受精卵中高表達，但在囊胚中低表達。囊胚能被誘導失去植入潛能，變成休眠的囊胚。令人興奮的是let-7在休眠囊胚中高表達，當休眠囊胚被啟動而獲得植入潛能時，let-7的表達降低到與正常囊胚相似的水準。更重要的是我們的資料也顯示正常囊胚超表達let-7後，其在細胞外基質上粘附及生長能力均降低，利用體內胚胎移植模型研究發現，超表達let-7的囊胚植入率也降低。這些體內，外資料顯示let-7在囊胚階段的低表達對成功胚胎植入有重要的意義。 本課題的假說是囊胚let-7的降低對胚胎成功植入起關鍵性的作用。主要研究let-7的三個靶基因dicer, 整合素β3及Vav-3在小鼠胚泡粘附及擴展中的作用。研究結果將增加我們對microRNA在囊胚啟動及植入中作用的理解，也會對臨床輔助生殖成功率及體外培養胚胎植入潛能的提高提供新的思路。

783910.label: Realisation of objectives
783910.value: In this project, we used the mouse delayed implantation model to study the role of microRNA (miRNA) let-7 on implantation. Delayed implantation is a phenomenon in which embryos become dormant for days/months before implantation, in order to allow the offspring to be born in a favorable environment for survival. The phenomenon can be induced in mice, and a single dose of estradiol can activate the dormant blastocysts to resume implantation. We used the model to time the initiation of implantation. By comparing the miRNA profile of dormant and estradiol-activated mouse blastocysts, we identified up-regulation of let-7 family members in the dormant blastocysts. The results were confirmed by direct determination of the expression of let-7a and let-7e using qPCR (Liu et al., 2012). This project hypothesized that a reduction of let-7 expression in blastocysts was critical for implantation. In silico analysis identified dicer, integrin-beta3 (Itgb3) and vav3 as targets of let-7a. The four objectives of the project aimed to investigate how these targets mediated the action of let-7a on implantation. Four approaches were used to address the objectives. 1. Dual luciferase reporter assay was used to determine whether let-7a bound to the 3’ untranslated region (3’UTR) of the targets in a human trophoblast cell line. Transfection of let-7a precursor or inhibitors decreased and increased the luciferase signal, respectively in the assay. The results were confirmed by qRT-PCR and immunostaining analyses of the targets in the trophoblast and mouse blastocysts. 2. An electroporation protocol was developed to modulate the expression of let-7a and its targets in mouse preimplantation embryos, and to investigate how these genes affected implantation The method could introduce exogenous RNA efficiently into mouse embryos, and 82% of the electroporated embryos developed to blastocysts (Liu et al., 2012). 3. qRT-PCR and immunostaining and/or western blotting were used to demonstrate a reciprocal relationship between let-7a and its targets in normal blastocysts, dormant blastocysts and estradiol-activated blastocysts. 4. Various endpoints were used to determine the role of the target genes in mediating the suppressive action of let-7a force-expression on implantation. Blastocyst attachment and spreading were used for the study of Itgb3. A novel blastocyst invasion assay was developed to determine the invasiveness of blastocysts with force-expression of let-7a or siRNA of vav3. Epidermal growth factor (EGF) binding assay was used to determine the activation status of blastocysts. Embryo transfer was used to demonstrate that the observations in vitro also affected implantation in vivo.

783910.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783910.value: Results from this study are based on in vitro and in vivo mouse models. The effect of let-7 on human embryos remains unknown. Our unpublished miRNA profiling data showed similar down-regulation of let-7 family members in human embryos during preimplantation development. Therefore, it is likely similar molecular regulation exits in human embryos. Moreover, other miRNA clusters including miR-17~92, 15a/16 and 290-295 were also differentially expressed between dormant and estradiol-activated embryos. These miRNA clusters could be potential targets for future studies. Recent study demonstrated that human blastocysts from infertile women had dysregulated expression of miRNAs. Further studies should confirm these initial observations and determine how the dysregulated miRNAs affect implantation. In future, it may be possible to help infertile couples by correcting the miRNA expression of embryos. Let-7 is estradiol-regulated in the mouse uterus. Higher expression of let-7 is observed in the delayed implanting mouse uterus after activation, and in the implantation site relative to inter-implantation site. The functions of let-7 in the endometrium are unknown. Itgb3, a well-known endometrial receptivity marker, is also expressed in the uterine luminal epithelium. How does let-7 modulate the expression of Itgb3 and affect uterine receptivity is a worthwhile area for future study.

783910.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783910.value: Implantation starts with a developmental competent blastocyst attaching and invading a receptive endometrium. The underlying molecular mechanism leading to implantation remains largely unknown. In this proposal, we studied the role of microRNA let-7a in regulating implantation in a mouse delayed implantation model. The results showed that blastocysts had low level of let-7 family members, which increased after experimental-induced dormancy. The level of let-7 in the dormant blastocysts decreased upon estradiol-induced activation. The change in let-7a expression was associated with opposite change in the expression of its target molecules dicer, vav3 and integrin-beta3. The inverse relationship of let-7a with its targets was reproduced by artificial force-expression of let-7a in mouse embryos. Upon force-expression of let-7, the mouse blastocysts had reduced attachment, outgrowth and invasive ability resulting in lower implantation potential. Evidence was obtained showing that dicer, integrin-beta3 and vav3 mediated these suppressive effects of let-7 on embryo implantation, trophoblast outgrowth and invasion. In summary, estradiol-activation of dormant mouse blastocysts reduced let-7a expression, which in turn increased dicer, integrin-beta3 and vav3 expression for embryo implantation. The results allow us to better understand the underlying mechanism of implantation. Recent evidence suggest that dysregulation of microRNAs in embryos may be a cause of infertility

784010.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784010.value: In the conventional clinical trial paradigm, we evaluate treatment toxicity, efficacy, and confirmatory long-term benefit in three separate and successive phases. Phase I trials focus on dose finding based on toxicity alone, and are typically characterized by a binary toxicity outcome. Phase II trials evaluate anti-disease effects or any beneficial drug activity in terms of an early binary efficacy outcome variable. Phase III randomized trials compare treatments based on overall survival or disease-free survival times. Limited resources, new treatment methods, and enormous demands to increase the pace of drug discovery have exposed the shortcomings of the clinical trial designs that are currently available. This has resulted in urgent calls for innovative statistical methods and accompanying software to use in the conduct and analysis of clinical trials. With a focus on the problems faced by clinical researchers in different settings of phase I, phase II, phase I/II and phase III trials, we propose to develop new Bayesian clinical trial designs, more efficient and innovative statistical methods, and trial conduct software that is user-friendly and freely available. The research we propose will provide solid methodological basis and novel analysis tools for a variety of different clinical settings, including dose-finding trials, dose-response studies, adaptive randomization in clinical trials, multiple-agent therapies, single-arm and multiple-arm phase I/II trials, and personalized medicine studies. In particular, we will propose statistical methods to address issues for robust dose finding, late-onset toxicity or missing data modeling, phase II designs with Bayesian adaptive randomization and predictive probability, phase II designs by jointly modeling efficacy and toxicity, and targeted therapy studies to identify prognostic or predictive biomarkers. These issues are very serious while not yet adequately addressed in the literature. Bayesian adaptive designs are efficient which often results in a smaller expected sample size; flexible by appropriately stopping the trial earlier under certain circumstances such as safety, futility or superiority; and ethical by using response-adaptive randomization to assign more patients to better treatments. We will develop computer programs and user-friendly software for each of the proposed statistical designs, and will incorporate these methods into routine clinical trial designs. We will closely work with researchers at M.D. Anderson Cancer Center and also develop collaborations with medical researchers at the University of Hong Kong. We will share the scientific knowledge and software we develop with the broader research community through publications, presentations in conferences, in our teaching and on our web site.

784010.label: Realisation of objectives
784010.value: We have rigorously investigated and completed all the four projects in the original research proposal. During the investigation, we have also come up with some new relevant ideas and developed new methods related to the proposal. All the four objectives have been fully achieved, and some of the ideas and methods have been further developed and expanded to other related areas, such as two-stage clinical trial designs, censored quantile regression, multiple change-points, and cure rate models. In particular, objective 1 is related to late-onset toxicities, and we incorporated the times to observing toxicity events using the Kaplan-Meier estimator (or the alternative approach by redistributing censored data to the right). Furthermore, we integrated the missing data theory and survival analysis techniques including multiple imputation and data augmentation to develop the continual reassessment method in phase I clinical trials. We found that by casting delayed toxicity or other unobserved outcomes in the missing data framework, the trial design can nicely incorporate missing information and thus fully utilize all the trial data and resources for a better design. In objective 2, we utilized the missing data idea in a multiple-arm randomized phase II clinical trial, when the response cannot be observed quickly. When treating unobserved data as censoring, we also extended our work to cure rate modeling as patients could be insusceptible to the event of interest. As to objective 3, we studied the outcome adaptive randomization and made comparison with other methods in phase II clinical trials. This work also leads to more theoretical development in survival data analysis. When there is a change-point or multiple change-points in the survival or hazard curves, the usual proportional hazards assumption may not hold, which motivated us for further research and development in change-points detection problems. Regarding objective 4, we developed a two-stage Lasso screening method to select prognostic or predictive biomarkers. This idea is also related to subgroup analysis, which is currently being investigated extensively. How to identify a sensitive subgroup is a very important question, so that a specifically tailored treatment strategy can be formulated to induce better response.

784010.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
784010.value: To provide more solid methodological basis and more innovative analysis tools for a variety of clinical trials, further development in dose-finding studies may involve information from pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modeling, which would offer more insights into dose-response relationships. Adaptive randomization in clinical trials may adjust for covariates as well as response, which would lead to more ethical trial design and yet maintain desirable power at the same time. Multiple-agent therapies or drug combinations pose enormous new challenges in design and analysis of clinical trials. More extensive research with multiple drug interactions is warranted, particularly for modeling dose-response surfaces. Personalized medicine studies mainly involve identification of prognostic or predictive biomarkers, which are therapeutically useful for determining specific treatments for different subgroups of patients. These issues are very serious and challenging, while not yet adequately addressed in the literature. Bayesian adaptive designs may offer a viable approach to alleviating the difficulties involved in these more complex trial settings.

784010.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
784010.value: Clinical trials and drug development in cancer have become increasingly challenging due to limited resources and enormous demands in terms of trial planning, conduct, analysis and infrastructures. This urgent situation calls for innovative statistical methods in the conduct and analysis of clinical trials. Cancer clinical trials involve extensive collaborative efforts from many different aspects. From statistical perspectives, we have developed several novel Bayesian adaptive designs and analysis methods. Our approaches are more flexible by accommodating various sources of data and information. In the proposed methods, we evaluate treatment toxicity and efficacy jointly, model the time to event data using novel statistical methods, develop more efficient two-stage designs for trial monitoring, extract information from missing data as much as possible for better dose finding, and develop new methods for subgroup analysis and biomarker identification for tailored treatment strategies.

784210.label: Project Objectives
784210.value: Use spatial analytic and time series statistics to identify the temporal and geographic clustering of suicide deaths within the mortality databases of Hong Kong and Taiwan; We hypothesize that statistically significant time/space defined clusters of suicides will be identified. Describe the decedents in each cluster identified by geospatial mapping using demographic, mental health service and socio-economic related data. We hypothesize that cluster decedents share similar demographic, mental health and social environment features, and that cluster participation is more common amongst youth. We will explore associations between indices of social deprivation and/or social fragmentation and suicide clusters. We hypothesize that clusters are more likely to occur in regions of social deprivation or disadvantage. Identify trends in suicide clusters. 784210.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784210.value: The aims of this study are to conduct an observational epidemiolgical investigation of the prevalence, characteristics and trends in suicide clusters in Hong Kong and Taiwan using temporal and geospatial methods. The project is timely, relevant and potentially saving lives. Suicide rates in Hong Kong and Taiwan have experienced significant changes in the past decade 1997-2007. Hong Kong suicide rate has increasd more than 50% from 12.6 per 100,000 in 1997 to a historical high 18.6 per 100,000 in 2003. Taiwan has experienced a simlar trend, from 10.0 per 100,000 to 14.2 per 100,000 in 2003 and is continuing increasing up to 19.0 per 100,000 in 2008. There is increasing concern about allegedly rising number of suicide clusters, particular in some disadvantegous districts in Hong Kong and in the urban areas in Taiwan. If significant clusters are detected using these methods, we shall determine their characteristics and the extent to which cluster in time and locality (i.e. hot spots) can be explained by known or suspected risk factors including seasonal factors (sesaonlity of suicides), demographic factors (age, gender, socioeconomic status, urbanicity/rurality), mental health factors (substance abuse, previous suicide attempts, mental health service provision), macro-level contextual influences, income inequality, economic activities, employment condition, population density, availability and lethality of suicide methods, overall suicide rate and media coverage. The recent advent of geospatial mapping techniques provides an opportunity to move from anecdotal and statistically unverified reports of clusters to scientific analysis of spatial patterns of clustering, including hypothesis testing, multi-level modeling and multivariate analysis. Spatial analytic techniques and geographic information systems (GIS) are used increasingly in epidemiological and public health research, but have been rarely applied to suicide-related issues. We propose to explore the utility of geospatial mapping techniques to systematically identify suicide clusters in Hong Kong and Taiwan for suicide prevention. We anticipate that our study will provide an evidence-based for developing cluster prevention and intervention strategies as part of integrated suicide prevention programs, specifically by estimating the prevalence of clusters, describing the characteristics of decedents in clusters, exploring current trends, and identifying at-risk sites and populations which require specialized prevention efforts. Then evidence-based suicide prevention programs can be developed in Taiwan and Hong Kong to reduce the number of suicides which could produce psycho-socio and economic benefits to both region and internationally as well. 最近被廣泛使用的地理空間定位技術提供了我們一個機會，擺脫以往傳統和統計上未經證實的地區組群報告以致使用科學方法分析地區群組的空間格局，包括假設驗證，多層式模組和多元因素分析等的研究報告。我們更發現越來越多空間分析技術和全球定位系統（GIS）使用於流行病學和公共衛生的研究，但用於自殺有關的問題研究卻很貧乏。 我們建議探究地理空間定位技術的實用性，再有系統地識別香港和台灣的自殺群組而作穩固預防自殺的基礎。研究將提供以實證為本，綜合發展地區群組的預防和阻截式的策略作為我們的預防自殺的計劃，特別是透過估計地區群組的流行率，描述地區群組中死者的特徵，探索目前的趨勢，並在找出高危場所和組群要求特定性的預防工作。因此台灣和香港便能發展出以實證為本的預防自殺方案從而減少自殺人數。

784210.label: Realisation of objectives
784210.value: We have successfully achieved all the 5 stated project objectives. Re objective 1, we have applied advanced statistical models i.e. scan statistics to identify suicide clusters in Hong Kong and Taipei city, and found evidence for statistically significant time-space clusters in the two cities, in particular amongst the youngest group. Re objective 2, we have found that the suicide clusters did not necessarily occur in the most socioeconomically deprived or socially fragmented areas. This finding suggests that other factors, e.g. media reporting, may have contributed to the occurrence of suicide clusters. Re objective 3, we found that suicide clusters were relatively a rare occurrence, when we used the exact points where the residential addresses were located in the analysis. However, when using the area where the residential addresses were located in the analysis, this tended to yield multiple clusters with relatively a large number of cases. This suggest that future time trend analysis of suicide clusters using area-based data, rather than point data, should take into account false positives. Re objective 4, we found only some evidence for the media effect on suicide clusters in Hong Kong, but not in Taipei. The only Hong Kong suicide cluster that was robust to a series of sensitivity analyses received extensive and often sensational media coverage, whilst the Taiwan cluster was not covered by the media. . Re objective 5, we found some evidence of identification amongst suicides to celebrity suicide, e.g. some similarities in demographic characteristics.

784210.label: Major findings and research outcome
784210.value: The major findings of this project includes that there were marked variations in suicide rates across different areas in Hong Kong, mostly in densely populated and socioeconomically deprived areas. Such variations could be as large as a two-fold difference in local suicide rates between the most deprived quintile and the least deprived quintile. Variations in local suicide rates were associated with some socioeconomic deprivation and social fragmentation indices, with the median household income showing the strongest association. There was a prominent socioeconomic gradient in suicide rates in Hong Kong, in particular non-elderly men. Thus men aged 10-64 living in deprived areas are a high risk group and need to be targeted in suicide prevention efforts Time-space suicide cluster was a relatively rare occurrence, in both Hong Kong and Taipei, and this finding depended on the characteristics of data, i.e. point data versus area-based data. The area-based data analysed using Poisson model tended to yield false signals of suicide clusters, and point data tended to lead to more consistent and robust results. One important findings of our suicide cluster analysis is that, in parallel to previous studies, suicide cluster appeared to occur more commonly in the youngest group than other age groups, suggesting vulnerability to copycat or identification effect in the particular group. This will have implications for public health approaches to suicide prevention in young people. Also we have established the mutual causation of suicide reporting and suicide incidence which provide the evidence to work with the media for promoting responsible reporting.

784210.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
784210.value: Our results pave ways to future further studies of suicide clusters. For example, further analysis of the phenomenon of suicide cluster should be based on robust statistical models and careful choice of data format. The area-based data were easier to obtain and most previous studies of suicide cluster were based on such data, perhaps leading to many false positive results and exaggerated estimates of the frequency of suicide cluster. We will try to identify other point-based data for suicide or suicide attempt to verify our findings in future projects. We are working with media in promoting responsible suicide reporting too,

784210.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
784210.value: Suicide cluster, i.e. unusually clustered suicide incidences within a short period of time and a geographic area, has attracted substantial attention from the media, the public, and researchers worldwide. However, previous empirical investigations into suicide cluster are limited, and are mostly based on case reports which could not take into account the baseline suicide rates. This may lead to false alarm and anxiety in the communities. In this study we have applied advanced and methodologically sound statistical models to study suicide clusters in two cities, Hong Kong and Taipei. The results show that suicide cluster is a relatively rare phenomenon, and in the few clusters identified in our analyses they are mostly amongst the youngest group (aged 10-24 years). The identified suicide cluster in Hong Kong received wide and sensational media coverage, but Taipei’s suicide cluster was not covered by the media, suggesting different mechanisms underlying the occurrence of suicide clusters. Also, the relationship between suicide reporting and incidence has been established and we shall make use of the results for promoting responsible reporting among media professionals. Our findings have important implications for future research and suicide prevention strategies.

784310.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784310.value: Plant hormone ethylene controls many aspects of plant growth and development ranging from seed germination to organ senescence such as fruit ripening. In certain detached climacteric fruits such as apple and pear when undergo the ripening process, large amount of ethylene is synthesized (2-5 nmol/g/h) to drive the biochemical changes associated with fruit softening and fruit flesh starch to sugar conversion. These high rates of ethylene could last a few days to a few weeks. During this ripening ethylene biosynthesis, co-product cyanide needed to be detoxified by beta-cyanoalanine synthase (CAS); and cysteine, the substrate for the CAS would also need to be regenerated by the cysteine synthase (CS) complex. The proposed experiments in this project attempt to sort out some of unsolved problems associated with ethylene biosynthesis. As stated above, there have close relationships among ethylene biosynthesis, cyanide detoxification and cysteine regeneration (or sulfide recycling) in plant tissues. Recent results from my laboratory confirmed that cyanide detoxification would take place in mitochondria while cysteine regeneration would mainly occur in cytoplasm. This implies that a continuous import of cysteine from cytosol to mitochondria in order to sustain cyanide detoxification during high rates of ethylene biosynthesis. The proposed experiments are designed firstly to elucidate the nature of this transport system; and secondly proceed to the molecular cloning of putative genes coding for such transporter protein(s); and thirdly verify the functions of these gene encoding proteins by employing various molecular and cellular biology techniques. 植物激素乙烯可以控制從種子萌發到器官衰老等植物生長和發育的很多方面，比如果實的成熟。在一些摘下的正在成熟中的呼吸躍變型果實，比如蘋果和梨中，有大量的乙烯被合成了出來（2~5納摩爾/克/小時），誘導了果實的軟化及果肉澱粉轉化為糖等生化改變。這麼大量的乙烯可以維持幾天到幾個星期。在這個乙烯生物合成的過程中，副產物氰化物需要由β-氰丙氨酸合成酶（CAS）解毒；而β-氰丙氨酸合成酶（CAS）的底物半胱氨酸則需要由半胱氨酸合成酶（CS）複合物再生出來。 這個項目的建議實驗嘗試解決在乙烯生物合成過程中遇到的一些未解問題。正如上述，在植物組織中，乙烯的生物合成，氰化物解毒及半胱氨酸再生（或稱硫化物再循環）三者之間存在著密切的關係。我們實驗室最近的研究結果確認了氰化物的解毒是在線粒體中進行的，而半胱氨酸的再生則主要在胞質中進行。這個結果說明在大量的乙烯生物合成過程中，爲了維持氰化物的解毒，半胱氨酸會不停地從胞質進入到線粒體。建議的實驗首先是設計用來闡明這種轉運系統的性質；其次會對可能編碼這個（些）轉運蛋白質的基因進行分子克隆；第三是用各種分子和細胞生物技術來驗證這些基因編碼蛋白的功能。

784410.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784410.value: Background The advent of dentin adhesives has greatly revolutionized the practice of restorative dentistry. The bonding of composite restorations to coronal dentin, fiber posts and lately root filling materials to root canal dentin can now be achieved via dentin adhesives. Despite the popularity of dentin adhesives, the durability of resin-dentin bonds is still a serious clinical problem. The decline in bond strength with time has been attributed to degradation of the "hybrid layer", which consists of adhesive resin and dentin collagen at the bonded interface. Key issues Traditionally, hydrophilic "water-loving" resin monomers are used in dentin adhesives to facilitate bonding to wet dentin, via "water wet-bonding" that prevents collapse of unsupported collagen fibrils and enhances complete penetration of adhesive monomers into demineralized dentin. However, the presence of water in this technique creates a potential for phase separation of hydrophobic "water-hating" and hydrophilic resin monomers, thereby yielding a less than optimum hybrid layer. Under such conditions, resin penetration into demineralized dentin is incomplete and results in exposed collagen fibrils within the hybrid layer, which are prone to attack by the naturally occurring enzymes, matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) 2, 8 and 9 in dentin. Increased water sorption by hydrophilic resin monomers alters the chemistry of the polymer chains (plasticization) and decreases the mechanical properties of dentin adhesives over time. To extend the longevity of resin-dentin bond, future dentin adhesives should be rendered less hydrophilic. A recently developed “ethanol-wet-bonding” technique allows better infiltration of hydrophobic resin and encapsulation of collagen fibrils. Recent studies have shown that this protocol improves bond durability of hydrophobic adhesives. Alternatively, chlorhexidine (CHX), a potent MMP inhibitor against MMP 2, 8 and 9, can be applied before the dentin adhesives to prevent collagen degradation in the hybrid layer. Therefore, the adjunctive use of ethanol-wet-bonding with CHX for hydrophobic adhesives should be a promising solution to improve the durability of the bonded interface by reducing resin and collagen degradation simultaneously. Aims and significance The proposed project aims to evaluate the effect of ethanol-wet-bonding and CHX in arresting bond degradation. We plan to use this novel bonding technique in two different dentin substrates: coronal and root canal dentin. The effectiveness of the new technique will be evaluated quantitatively using bond strength testing and nanoleakage, and qualitatively using transmission electron microscopy. Our findings will improve adhesion and restoration technology, as well as the longevity of a wide spectrum of esthetic bonded dental restorations. 牙本質粘接劑的出現徹底改變牙科修復技術. 可是,樹脂牙本質粘接的耐用性仍然是一個大問題. 為了延長樹脂牙本質粘結的壽命，未來牙本質粘合劑應用少親水性樹脂.“乙醇濕粘結”技術已被證明可以更好地滲透疏水性樹脂和包蓋混合層的膠原蛋白. 洗必泰（放線菌酮）是一種有效的蛋白酶抑製劑, 在牙本質粘合劑應用前使用洗必泰, 已被證明可以防止混合層的膠原蛋白分解.因此,放線菌酮的應用加“乙醇濕粘結”技術應可以減少膠原的降解, 提高結合界面的耐久性. 擬議項目的目的是評估“乙醇濕粘結”技術與放線菌酮停止破壞牙本質粘結界面成效.

784410.label: Realisation of objectives
784410.value: Objective 1: To evaluate the effect of ethanol-wet bonding (EWB) with or without chlorhexidine (CHX) on the bond durability of hydrophobic adhesives to normal and caries-affected dentin The first objective is 100% completed. Dentine surfaces of molars were etched after caries removal and randomly allocated to four groups. In Groups 1 and 2, dentine surfaces were saturated with either 2 ml of 100% ethanol or 2 ml of ethanol with 2% CHX for 60 s. In Groups 3 and 4, dentine surfaces were saturated with either 15 µL of distilled water or 15 µL of distilled water with 2% CHX for 60 s. Two coats of primer, followed by neat resin were applied and light-cured for 40 s. Resin composite build-ups were placed and bonded specimens were sectioned for bond strength testing after 24 h and 12 months’ storage in artificial saliva. Bond strength data were analyzed using 3-way ANOVA and SNK tests. Interfacial nanoleakage was evaluated using a field-emission scanning electron microscopy and data were analyzed using Kruskal-Wallis test. Objective 2: To examine the effect of EWB with or without CHX on the bond durability of fiber post luted to intra-radicular dentin with hydrophobic adhesives The second objective is 100% completed. Ninety-six extracted human teeth with a single root and root canal were prepared for post placement after endodontic treatment. The teeth were randomly divided into four groups after etching and rinsing for rewetting: Group 1: water-wet bonding, Group 2: water-wet bonding with CHX, Group 3: ethanol-wet bonding and Group 4: ethanol-wet bonding with CHX. Teeth in Groups 1 and 2 were treated with either distilled water or distilled water with 2% CHX for 60 s; while teeth in Groups 3 and 4 were treated with either 100% ethanol or 100% ethanol with 2% CHX. Two coats of primer, followed by neat resin were applied and light-cured for 40 s. Fiber posts were luted to bonded root dentine using dual-cure resin cement. Bonded roots were subjected to push-out bond strength testing and interfacial nanoleakage evaluation after 24 h, 6 and 12 months’ of storage. Data were analyzed using 3-way ANOVA and SNK tests.

784410.label: Major findings and research outcome
784410.value: Objective 1 (1) Adjunctive application of chlorhexidine (CHX) and ethanol-wet bonding (EWB) on durability of bonds to sound and caries-affected dentine. Major research outcome: After 12 months of ageing in artificial saliva, the adjunctive application of CHX with EWB preserved the bond strength of hydrophobic adhesive to both sound dentine (SD) and caries-affected dentine (CAD). Conversely, the adjunctive application of CHX with water-wet bonding (WWB) similarly preserved the bond strength of hydrophobic adhesive to SD after 12 months. Incorporation of CHX to EWB with hydrophobic adhesive enhances the success rate of aesthetic bonded restorations. Research output: A manuscript has been provisionally accepted for publication at Journal of Dentistry and a revised version has been submitted (Part C 8 No.1). Conferences abstract: Three abstracts presented (Part C 9 No. 1, 2, 7, 8). 1 Faculty Research Seminar delivered 17 Oct 2011. (2) A new method of evaluation of fracture patterns following microtensile bond strength testing using polarized light microscopy Major research outcome: The results of EDX mapping and SEM observation showed that the use of polarized light microscopy is a simple, viable method for differentiation between the resin-covered and dentin surfaces for determining fracture pattern analysis after bond testing. Research output: A manuscript has been accepted for publication at Journal of Adhesive Dentistry (Part C item 3). (3) Effect of solvent on the inhibition of matrix metalloproteinases (MMP) by chlorhexidine Major findings and research outcome: CHX solvated in ethanol and acetone had greater inhibitory effect on soluble and matrix-bound MMPs than in water. Conferences abstract: One abstract presented (Part C 9 No. 6). For Objective 2 (1) Effect of chlorhexidine and ethanol-wet bonding with hydrophobic adhesive to intraradicular dentine Major research outcome: After 12 months of ageing in artificial saliva, EWB groups showed significantly higher bond strength than WWB groups for all three root regions tested. The bond strengths of the EWB groups were not affected by ageing in artificial saliva. However, the addition of CHX to EWB did not further improve the bond strength of fiber post to intraradicular dentine, when compared to EWB alone. EWB with a hydrophobic adhesive alone could improve the bond durability of fiber post to intraradicular dentine and therefore would increase the success rate of post and core restorations of endodontically treated teeth. Research output: A manuscript has been published at Journal of Dentistry (Part C item 2). Conference abstract: Three abstracts presented (Part C 9 No.3, 4 & 5).

784410.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
784410.value: It has been shown in our in vitro study that ethanol-wet bonding (EWB) + chlorhexidine (CHX) improved resin-dentin bond durability in both sound and caries-affected coronal dentin, while EWB alone could improve the bond durability of fiber post to intraradicular dentine. Future studies should investigate the effects of EWB with or without CHX on vital pulp so that this beneficial bonding technique can be applied clinically to enhance the longevity of esthetic tooth colored restorations as well as post and core restorations of endodontically treated teeth. Because of the electrostatic binding nature of CHX, another possible direction of research will be to prolong the action of MMP inhibitor in the hybrid layer. Further studies should investigate the effect of incorporation of methacrylate-based, matrix metalloproteinases inhibitory monomers into experimental adhesives on preventing bond degradation.

784410.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
784410.value: Despite the popular usage of dentin adhesives, durability of resin-dentin bonds is still a major clinical problem. To extend the longevity of resin-dentin bond, future dentin adhesives should be rendered less hydrophilic as increased water sorption by hydrophilic resin monomers causes plasticization of the polymer chains and decreases the mechanical properties of dentin adhesives over time. The ethanol wet bonding (EWB) technique allowed better infiltration of hydrophobic resin and encapsulation of collagen fibrils. Conversely, chlorhexidine (CHX), a potent matrix metalloproteinases inhibitor, has been shown to prevent collagen degradation in the hybrid layer. Hence, the adjunctive application of EWB and CHX with hydrophobic adhesives should be a promising solution to improve the durability of the bonded interface by reducing collagen and resin degradation simultaneously. Findings of our study showed that EWB + CHX improved the stability resin-dentin bond over time in both sound and caries-affected coronal dentin, while EWB alone could improve the bond durability of fiber post to intraradicular dentine. The results of our project established a solid foundation for further in vivo investigation of this beneficial bonding technique clinically to improve the longevity of a wide spectrum of bonded restorations for our patients.
